groups.name: Undergo State Change · 转变与质变 (Change, Transform, Convert)
groups.tip: 状态或性质发生改变

items.def_zh: 改变，发生改变；更换；兑换
items.def_en: 1. to become different, or make someone or something different. 2. to exchange or replace something with another.
items.ex_en: The weather began to change rapidly as dark clouds rolled over the hills.
items.ex_zh: 乌云翻滚越过山头，天气开始迅速发生变化。
items.ex2_en: You can change your password anytime by accessing your account settings.
items.ex2_zh: 你可以随时通过访问账户设置来更改密码。

items.def_en: 1. to begin to be or grow into; to come to be. 2. to suit or look attractive on someone.
items.ex_en: Over the past few months, the quiet neighborhood has become increasingly lively.
items.ex_zh: 在过去的几个月里，这个安静的街区变得越来越热闹。

items.def_en: to become green, or make something green or environmentally friendly.
items.ex_en: The municipal council launched ambitious projects to green the city center this year.
items.ex_zh: 市议会今年启动了雄心勃勃的项目来绿化市中心。
items.ex2_en: The barren hills green quickly after the warm spring rains arrive.
items.ex2_zh: 暖春的雨水降临后，光秃秃的群山迅速变绿。

items.def_zh: 转变，改变；转换，交换；开/关（电器）
items.def_en: 1. to change or turn from one thing to another; exchange. 2. to turn an electrical device on or off using a switch.
items.ex_en: Many consumers decided to switch to energy-efficient appliances to lower their bills.
items.ex_zh: 许多消费者决定转用节能家电以降低账单开支。
items.ex2_en: Please switch the living room lights off before you go to bed.
items.ex2_zh: 上床睡觉前请把客厅的灯关掉。

items.def_zh: 变化，改变；（使）不同，呈现差异
items.def_en: to be different or change according to conditions; to make changes in something so it is not always the same.
items.ex_en: Prices of fresh produce can vary significantly depending on seasonal supply shortages.
items.ex_zh: 新鲜农产品的价格可能会因季节性供应短缺而出现很大差异。
items.ex2_en: Experienced chefs often vary their special menus according to the season.
items.ex2_zh: 经验丰富的大厨经常根据季节变换他们的特色菜单。

items.def_zh: （使）转变，转化；（使）改变信仰，皈依；兑换
items.def_en: 1. to change from one form, system, or state to another, or cause something to do so. 2. to change one's religion or beliefs.
items.ex_en: The engineers plan to convert the old warehouse into a modern research facility.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们计划将旧仓库改造成现代化的科研设施。
items.ex2_en: Solar energy will convert into electricity through these efficient rooftop panels.
items.ex2_zh: 太阳能将通过这些屋顶高效电池板转化为电能。

items.def_en: to change or transition from one state, condition, or style to another.
items.ex_en: The manufacturing plant must transition from fossil fuels to sustainable energy sources.
items.ex_zh: 该制造工厂必须从化石燃料过渡到可持续能源。
items.ex2_en: The company hired consultants to transition the workforce toward automated digital systems.
items.ex2_zh: 公司聘请了顾问来引导员工向自动化数字化系统转型。

items.def_zh: 使彻底改变，使改观，转化
items.def_en: to change markedly the form, appearance, or character of something.
items.ex_en: A fresh coat of vibrant paint can completely transform an otherwise dull room.
items.ex_zh: 一层鲜艳的新油漆能让原本沉闷的房间彻底改观。
items.ex2_en: Caterpillars transform into delicate butterflies during their quiet cocoon stage.
items.ex2_zh: 毛毛虫在安静的茧期蜕变成精致的蝴蝶。

items.def_zh: 改变，更改；改动（衣服使其合身）
items.def_en: to change or make someone or something different; to adjust the fit of clothing.
items.ex_en: The tailor offered to alter the jacket to ensure a much better fit.
items.ex_zh: 裁缝主动提出修改这件夹克，以确保它更加合身。
items.ex2_en: His deep voice seemed to alter slightly whenever he spoke under pressure.
items.ex2_zh: 每当他在压力下说话时，他低沉的嗓音似乎都会略有改变。

items.def_en: [I/T] to change or cause someone/something to change completely into another entity
items.ex_en: Without proper maintenance, this small misunderstanding could easily turn into a bitter conflict.
items.ex_zh: 如果不妥善处理，这件小小的误会很容易演变成激烈的冲突。
items.ex2_en: A sudden drop in temperature can turn water into solid crystal ice.
items.ex2_zh: 气温骤降会把水变成坚硬的冰晶。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to stop being one thing and become another, or make sth do this
items.ex_en: With the first frost of autumn, delicate green leaves change into vibrant gold.
items.ex_zh: 随着秋天初霜降临，娇嫩的绿叶转变成了灿烂的金黄色。
items.ex2_en: The fairy godmother waved her magic wand to change pumpkins into carriages.
items.ex2_zh: 仙女教母挥动魔杖，将南瓜变成了马车。

items.def_en: (+ to sth) to change from one system, method, or state to another
items.ex_en: The hospital will switch over to a completely digital record system next month.
items.ex_zh: 下个月该医院将全面切换至数字化病历系统。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to completely transform the appearance or structure of sb/sth
items.ex_en: The design team worked tirelessly to make over the dilapidated public library.
items.ex_zh: 设计团队不知疲倦地工作，对这座破旧的公共图书馆进行了彻底改造。

items.def_en: to make bitter in taste; to make someone resentful or cynical.
items.ex_en: Years of relentless hardship and deceit had begun to bitter his tender soul.
items.ex_zh: 多年的艰难困苦与欺骗开始让他温柔的心灵变得痛苦而怨恨。

items.def_zh: 给……镀青铜；使晒成古铜色；变成青铜色
items.def_en: to give the color or appearance of bronze to something; to become or make sun-tanned or bronze in color.
items.ex_en: A week spent sailing across the bay served to bronze their fair skin.
items.ex_zh: 在海湾航行的一周时间让她们白皙的皮肤晒成了古铜色。
items.ex2_en: Her pale skin will bronze quickly after several sunny afternoons outdoors.
items.ex2_zh: 在户外度过几个阳光明媚的下午后，她苍白的皮肤很快就会晒成古铜色。

items.def_en: to convert coal into coke by heating it in the absence of air, or to undergo this process.
items.ex_en: The massive industrial ovens coke bituminous coal under strictly controlled, oxygen-free conditions.
items.ex_zh: 巨型工业炉在严格受控的无氧条件下将烟煤炼成焦炭。
items.ex2_en: Special grades of coal coke efficiently when heated in modern closed retorts.
items.ex2_zh: 特殊等级的煤在现代密闭蒸馏釜中受热时能高效结焦。

items.def_zh: 使复杂化；使变得世故，使精明；篡改
items.def_en: to make more complex, refined, or worldly; to alter or adulterate deceptively.
items.ex_en: Recent technological innovations serve to sophisticate the analytical methods used by researchers.
items.ex_zh: 近期的技术创新使研究人员采用的分析方法更加复杂精细。

items.def_en: to use machines or computers to control or perform a process automatically.
items.ex_en: The company decided to automate its assembly line to enhance overall production efficiency.
items.ex_zh: 公司决定使其装配线自动化，以提高整体生产效率。

items.def_zh: 改变……的形状或结构，重塑；翻新，改造
items.def_en: to change the structure, layout, or appearance of a building, room, or system.
items.ex_en: They hired an experienced contractor to remodel their outdated kitchen this summer.
items.ex_zh: 他们今年夏天聘请了一位经验丰富的承包商来改造过时的厨房。

items.def_zh: 使成麦芽，用麦芽处理；发麦芽
items.def_en: to convert barley or other grain into malt by steeping and germinating, or to treat with malt.
items.ex_en: Artisanal distillers carefully malt locally grown barley to develop rich, complex flavors.
items.ex_zh: 手工酿酒商精心将当地种植的大麦制成麦芽，以酝酿出丰富醇厚的风味。
items.ex2_en: Harvested barley will malt naturally once placed in warm, moist germination chambers.
items.ex2_zh: 收获的大麦一旦放入温暖湿润的发芽室，便会自然发芽制成麦芽。

items.def_zh: （使）图像平滑变换；逐步演变成，变化
items.def_en: to change smoothly and gradually from one image, shape, or state into another.
items.ex_en: Over just a few years, his hobby morphed into a lucrative business.
items.ex_zh: 短短几年之内，他的业余爱好就演变成了一门赚钱的生意。
items.ex2_en: The graphic software can morph your portrait photo into an artistic cartoon.
items.ex2_zh: 该图形软件可以将你的肖像照片渐变成艺术卡通形象。

items.def_en: to undergo genetic mutation, or cause a gene or organism to develop new characteristics; to change into a different form.
items.ex_en: Scientists monitored how the virus could mutate under selective environmental pressures.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们密切监测该病毒在选择性环境压力下可能发生的突变。
items.ex2_en: Ultraviolet radiation can mutate cellular DNA and increase cancer risk substantially.
items.ex2_zh: 紫外线辐射会使细胞DNA发生突变，并大幅增加患癌风险。

items.def_en: to shape again or give a new form, structure, or direction to something.
items.ex_en: The new policy seeks to reshape the national economy toward long-term sustainability.
items.ex_zh: 新政策旨在重塑国家经济结构，实现长期可持续发展。

items.def_zh: 彻底变革，使发生革命性剧变
items.def_en: to completely change the way that something is done, thought about, or made.
items.ex_en: Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence will radically revolutionize several key economic sectors.
items.ex_zh: 人工智能领域的突破将彻底变革数个关键经济部门。

items.def_zh: 用硫酸（盐）处理；使硫酸盐化
items.def_en: to treat or combine with sulfuric acid or a sulfate, or coat with lead sulfate.
items.ex_en: Over time, harsh acid rain may sulfate exposed limestone surfaces across the city.
items.ex_zh: 随着时间的推移，强酸雨可能会使城市中裸露的石灰石表面发生硫酸盐化。

items.def_zh: 使计算机化，用电脑处理
items.def_en: to equip with computers or convert a process or system to automatic computer operation.
items.ex_en: The clinic spent several months striving to computerize all patient medical records.
items.ex_zh: 该诊所花费了数月时间，努力将所有病人的医疗记录计算机化。

items.def_zh: （动词）列出词形变化；（使）结合，配对
items.def_en: 1. (grammar) to list or change the different forms of a verb according to tense, person, etc. 2. to join together or unite.
items.ex_en: Ancient languages often conjugate regular verbs across dozens of intricate mood forms.
items.ex_zh: 古代语言通常会根据数十种复杂的语气形式对规则动词进行曲折变化。
items.ex2_en: These irregular verbs conjugate unpredictably in both past and present tenses.
items.ex2_zh: 这些不规则动词在过去时和现在时中的变位都难以预测。

items.def_en: to convert pictures, sound, or information into a digital form that can be processed by a computer.
items.ex_en: The university library launched a major project to digitize historic manuscripts securely.
items.ex_zh: 大学图书馆启动了一项重大项目，旨在安全地将历史手稿数字化。

items.def_en: to convert an atom or molecule into an ion, or become converted into ions.
items.ex_en: Cosmic rays easily ionize gas atoms present in the upper atmosphere layers.
items.ex_zh: 宇宙射线极易使高层大气中存在的气体原子发生电离。
items.ex2_en: Gas particles ionize rapidly when exposed to extremely high thermal radiation.
items.ex2_zh: 气体粒子在暴露于极高热辐射时会迅速电离。

items.def_en: to change completely into something very different, or cause someone or something to do so.
items.ex_en: Over centuries, the sleepy medieval hamlet would metamorphose into an industrial metropolis.
items.ex_zh: 几个世纪以来，这个沉睡的中世纪村落蜕变成了一座工业大都市。
items.ex2_en: Intense underground heat and pressure metamorphose limestone into smooth marble.
items.ex2_zh: 地下的高热和高压将石灰岩转变成光滑的大理石。

items.def_zh: 使发酵；使生动，给……增添趣味
items.def_en: 1. to add yeast or a leavening agent to dough so it rises. 2. to make something less serious or more enjoyable by adding humor or variety.
items.ex_en: His gentle, witty remarks often served to leaven an otherwise tense conversation.
items.ex_zh: 他温和而风趣的话语往往能给原本紧张的谈话增添一丝生动幽默。

items.def_en: to make an area or population more urban in character, infrastructure, or lifestyle.
items.ex_en: Rapid industrial expansion continues to urbanize once-remote rural valleys in the province.
items.ex_zh: 快速的工业扩张继续使该省曾经偏远的山区乡村走向城市化。
items.ex2_en: Coastal fishing villages urbanized quickly during the post-war industrial construction boom.
items.ex2_zh: 战后工业建设繁荣时期，沿海渔村迅速实现了城镇化。

items.def_zh: 使磁化，使带磁性；吸引，强烈吸引
items.def_en: 1. to make something magnetic. 2. to attract or fascinate people strongly.
items.ex_en: High electric currents can rapidly magnetize the iron core inside the device.
items.ex_zh: 强电流可以迅速使设备内部的铁芯发生磁化。

items.def_zh: （词）发生曲折变化，改变词尾；使弯曲；改变音调
items.def_en: 1. (grammar) to change the form of a word, typically the ending, to show tense, person, or number. 2. to alter the tone or pitch of the voice.
items.ex_en: The poet carefully learned to inflect each subtle phrase with lingering sorrow.
items.ex_zh: 诗人精心地学会让每一个微妙的词句都带有一抹挥之不去的哀伤。
items.ex2_en: English verbs inflect very little compared to ancient Latin grammatical forms.
items.ex2_zh: 与古拉丁语的语法形式相比，英语动词的词形屈折变化很少。

items.def_zh: 使多样化；使成杂色，使斑驳
items.def_en: to make varied or diverse; to mark with different colors or patches.
items.ex_en: Morning sunbeams broke through the canopy to variegate the damp forest floor.
items.ex_zh: 晨曦穿透树冠，使潮湿的林地地面显得斑驳陆离。

items.def_en: to heat sugar or food containing sugar until it turns brown and sweet, or to undergo this change.
items.ex_en: Cook the sliced onions slowly over low heat until they thoroughly caramelize.
items.ex_zh: 用小火慢炒切好的洋葱，直到它们完全焦糖化。
items.ex2_en: The pastry chef gently caramelizes white sugar to top the dessert.
items.ex2_zh: 西点师轻轻将白糖熬焦以点缀甜点。

items.def_en: to change completely, or change something, into a different form, substance, or state.
items.ex_en: Ancient alchemists constantly sought secret methods to transmute base metals into gold.
items.ex_zh: 古代炼金术士不断寻求能将贱金属彻底转化为黄金的秘密方法。
items.ex2_en: Ancient folklore claimed that sorrow could transmute into enduring spiritual strength.
items.ex2_zh: 古老的民间传说称，悲伤可以转化为持久的精神力量。

items.def_en: to treat or combine an organic substance (such as liquid vegetable oil) with hydrogen.
items.ex_en: Food manufacturers hydrogenate liquid vegetable oils to create solid, shelf-stable shortening products.
items.ex_zh: 食品制造商将液体植物油氢化，以制造固体且耐储存的起酥油产品。

items.def_zh: 重塑了，改造了（remodel 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (chiefly British English) past tense and past participle of remodel; altered the structure or appearance of.
items.ex_en: The architect remodelled the old Victorian townhouse into bright, contemporary studio flats.
items.ex_zh: 建筑师将这栋古老的维多利亚风格联排别墅改造成了明亮现代的单间公寓。

items.def_en: to adopt or cause to adopt the customs, ideas, or culture of Western countries.
items.ex_en: The ruling government pushed wide reforms to westernize legal and educational institutions.
items.ex_zh: 执政政府推进广泛改革，以使法律和教育机构西方化。
items.ex2_en: Traditional societies westernize gradually through increased exposure to global media entertainment.
items.ex2_zh: 传统社会通过越来越多地接触全球媒体娱乐而逐渐西方化。

items.def_zh: 使变性（改变天然性质）；使（酒精等）变性以不可饮用
items.def_en: 1. to alter the natural qualities or structure of a protein or other molecule. 2. to add a toxic or foul-tasting substance to alcohol so it is unfit to drink.
items.ex_en: Extreme heat will denature cellular proteins, preventing them from functioning normally anymore.
items.ex_zh: 极度高温会使细胞蛋白质变性，使其无法再正常发挥功能。
items.ex2_en: Fragile enzyme proteins denature instantly when chemical solution temperatures rise excessively.
items.ex2_zh: 当化学溶液温度过度升高时，脆弱的酶蛋白会瞬间变性。

items.def_zh: （使）升华；使高尚化，净化（本能冲动）
items.def_en: 1. (physics / chemistry) to change directly from a solid to a gas or vice versa without becoming liquid. 2. (psychology) to redirect primal or unacceptable impulses into socially constructive activities.
items.ex_en: Under low atmospheric pressure, dry ice will sublimate directly into gaseous carbon.
items.ex_zh: 在低气压环境下，干冰会直接升华为气态碳化合物。
items.ex2_en: The laboratory technician used high vacuum equipment to sublimate pure iodine.
items.ex2_zh: 实验技术人员使用高真空设备使纯碘升华。

items.def_en: to make or become feminine or more suitable for or typical of women.
items.ex_en: Some analysts argue that expanding healthcare services tends to feminize the workforce.
items.ex_zh: 一些分析师认为，医疗服务体系的扩大往往会使劳动力队伍呈现女性化。
items.ex2_en: The primary teaching profession feminized steadily over the past few decades.
items.ex2_zh: 在过去的几十年里，小学教师行业逐渐女性化。

items.def_en: to convert or be converted into a mineral substance; to impregnate with minerals.
items.ex_en: Subterranean waters rich in silica slowly mineralize ancient buried timber over millennia.
items.ex_zh: 富含二氧化硅的地下水在数千年间慢慢使掩埋的古木矿化。
items.ex2_en: Organic bone matter will mineralize thoroughly over several million geological years.
items.ex2_zh: 有机骨骼物质在经历数百万地质年后会彻底矿化。

items.def_zh: 使具有性色彩，使性感化
items.def_en: (British English) to make something sexual in character or quality, or view someone primarily in sexual terms.
items.ex_en: Critics argued that modern advertising campaigns tend to sexualise young female performers.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士指出，现代广告宣传往往倾向于将年轻的女演员过度性感化。

items.def_en: to transfer from religious to civil ownership or control; make secular.
items.ex_en: The new republican regime sought to secularize public education across the nation.
items.ex_zh: 新成立的共和国政权试图在全国范围内实现公共教育的世俗化。

items.def_en: to transform into something more beautiful, spiritual, or elevated.
items.ex_en: The radiant evening sunset seemed to transfigure the bleak, wind-swept moorland landscape.
items.ex_zh: 绚烂的晚霞似乎让荒凉、饱经风霜的荒原景色焕发出了神圣的美感。

items.def_en: to make or become English in form, pronunciation, character, or customs.
items.ex_en: Many immigrant families chose to anglicize their surnames upon arriving in Britain.
items.ex_zh: 许多移民家庭在抵达英国后选择将自己的姓氏英文化。
items.ex2_en: Foreign loanwords often anglicize quickly in spelling after widespread daily usage.
items.ex2_zh: 外来借词在日常广泛使用后，拼写往往会很快英文化。

items.def_en: to introduce a carboxyl group (-COOH) into a chemical compound.
items.ex_en: Specialized enzymes readily carboxylate the organic substrate during the essential metabolic pathway.
items.ex_zh: 在关键的代谢途径中，专门的酶很容易使有机底物羧化。

items.def_zh: （使）恢复原状，（使）再转变；（使）重新皈依
items.def_en: to convert back to a previous state, use, or religion.
items.ex_en: City planners decided to reconvert the vacant railway terminal into a museum.
items.ex_zh: 城市规划者决定将闲置的火车站终点站重新改造成博物馆。
items.ex2_en: The synthetic compound reconverts back to its original liquid state rapidly.
items.ex2_zh: 这种合成化合物迅速重新转化回其原始的液体状态。

items.def_zh: 使成复数形式；使多元化
items.def_en: 1. (grammar) to make a word plural, or become plural. 2. to make a system or society more diverse.
items.ex_en: Demographic shifts inevitably pluralize modern urban societies across various cultural dimensions.
items.ex_zh: 人口结构的变化不可避免地使现代城市社会在各个文化维度上更加多元化。
items.ex2_en: Most regular nouns in modern English pluralize simply by adding an s.
items.ex2_zh: 现代英语中大多数规则名词只需加s即可变为复数。

items.def_en: to remove the magnetic properties from an object or material.
items.ex_en: Careful annealing at elevated temperatures will quickly demagnetize the hardened steel rod.
items.ex_zh: 在高温下进行精细退火可以使硬化钢棒迅速退磁。

items.def_zh: 使失去个性，使非人化；使客观化
items.def_en: to deprive of personal qualities or individuality; to make cold or impersonal.
items.ex_en: Excessive bureaucratic paperwork threatens to depersonalize essential healthcare relationships between doctors and patients.
items.ex_zh: 繁琐的官僚程序可能使医患之间原本重要的人际关怀变得冰冷而机械化。

items.def_en: to give male physical traits or masculine characteristics to someone or something, or develop them.
items.ex_en: Elevated hormone levels during development can significantly masculinize certain juvenile anatomical structures.
items.ex_zh: 发育期升高的激素水平会显著促进幼体某些解剖结构的雄性化。
items.ex2_en: The adolescent boy's vocal cords masculinize naturally during puberty stages.
items.ex2_zh: 青春期男孩的声带在发育阶段会自然男性化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe an entity undergoing or being subjected to a transition in physical nature, internal form, function, or status (often taking prepositions like 'into' or 'to'). They range from basic general shifts to deep structural, mechanical, or biochemical transmutation.
groups.summary_zh: 描述事物形态、性质、功能或状态发生实质性转变与重塑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes transitioning from one state, nature, or function into another, contrasting with static continuity or simple surface alteration by emphasizing a distinct phase shift or structural reconfiguration.
groups.desc_zh: 指事物从一种状态、性质或功能跨入另一种形态的转变，与静态持存或表面微调不同，侧重阶段更迭或结构性重塑。
groups.nuance_en: change: neutral generic shift in condition (mind / plan / direction) · transform: marked complete metamorphosis in form or character (economy / landscape / life) · convert: purposeful structural or functional adaptation into a new system (energy / currency / building) · transition: smooth managed passage between phases (regime / phase / role) · switch: sudden binary swap from one alternative to another (track / sides / allegiance)
groups.nuance_zh: change: 最通用的中性状态更替 (mind / plan / direction) · transform: 形态、性质或外貌上的彻底蜕变 (economy / landscape / life) · convert: 目的明确的系统性、功能性改造或信仰皈依 (energy / currency / building) · transition: 阶段间平稳有序的过渡转化 (regime / phase / role) · switch: 两者间迅速明确的二选一切换 (track / sides / allegiance)

groups.name: Visual Gaze & Scrutiny · 凝视与审视 (Look, Gaze, Stare)
groups.tip: 目光投向目标的多样方式

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to look quickly at sb/sth and then look away
items.ex_en: She could only glance at her wristwatch before answering the urgent telephone.
items.ex_zh: 在接听紧急电话之前，她只能匆匆看了一眼手表。

items.def_zh: 匆匆一瞥，扫视；掠过，擦过
items.def_en: 1. to look quickly and briefly at someone or something. 2. to bounce off a surface at an angle.
items.ex_en: He paused briefly to glance across the crowded hallway for familiar faces.
items.ex_zh: 他停顿了一下，迅速扫视拥挤的走廊以寻找熟悉的面孔。

items.def_en: to see someone or something very briefly or only partially.
items.ex_en: Through the thick fog, the sailors could only glimpse the distant lighthouse.
items.ex_zh: 穿过浓厚的大雾，水手们只能隐约瞥见远处的灯塔。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to look closely or with difficulty into sth
items.ex_en: The detective leaned forward to peer into the dark, abandoned basement stairway.
items.ex_zh: 侦探探身向前，费力地端详着漆黑、废弃的地下室楼梯。

items.def_zh: 看见，看到；理解，明白；查明；经历
items.def_en: 1. to perceive with the eyes. 2. to understand, realize, or find out.
items.ex_en: Turn on the lamp so that you can see your reading properly.
items.ex_zh: 把台灯打开，这样你才能看清阅读的内容。

items.def_zh: 看，注视；寻找；显得，看起来
items.def_en: 1. to direct one's gaze towards someone or something. 2. to appear or seem.
items.ex_en: Please look toward the camera and smile naturally for this family portrait.
items.ex_zh: 请面向镜头自然微笑，来拍这张全家福照片。

items.def_en: 1. to look at or inspect something carefully. 2. to regard or consider something in a particular way.
items.ex_en: Potential buyers came early yesterday morning to view the historic countryside estate.
items.ex_zh: 潜在买家昨天一早就赶来参观审视这处历史悠久的乡村庄园。

items.def_zh: 看见，发现；用瞄准器对准
items.def_en: 1. to manage to see or catch sight of something, especially from a distance. 2. to aim a weapon or telescope at something.
items.ex_en: After weeks adrift, the weary crew finally managed to sight coastal land.
items.ex_zh: 在海上漂流数周后，疲惫的船员们终于远远望见了海岸陆地。

items.def_en: 1. to look at something with eyes partly closed, such as in bright light. 2. to have an eye that turns inward or outward.
items.ex_en: He had to squint at the tiny print on the medicine bottle without his glasses.
items.ex_zh: 没戴眼镜，他不得不眯起眼睛看药瓶上的小字。

items.def_zh: 凝望星空，眺望星辰；遐想，做白日梦
items.def_en: 1. to look at or observe the stars. 2. to daydream or engage in aimless contemplation.
items.ex_en: We often lay outside on the grass at night to stargaze quietly.
items.ex_zh: 夜里我们常常躺在外面的草地上，静静地凝望星空。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to look steadily at sb/sth for a long time, often in wonder or thought
items.ex_en: Visitors stood in awe to gaze at the magnificent alpine mountain scenery.
items.ex_zh: 游客们满怀敬畏地驻足，凝视着壮丽的高山景致。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to look directly at sb/sth for a long time with wide open eyes
items.ex_en: It is considered impolite to stare at strangers in public.
items.ex_zh: 在公共场合盯着陌生人看被认为是不礼貌的。

items.def_zh: 观看，注视；看守，监视；注意，留心
items.def_en: to look at someone or something attentively over a period of time; to observe, guard, or monitor.
items.ex_en: Curious tourists gathered along the harbour railings to watch the evening ferry dock.
items.ex_zh: 好奇的游客聚集在海港栏杆旁，注视着夜班轮渡靠岸。

items.def_en: to look at someone or something closely, attentively, or with suspicion.
items.ex_en: The detective continued to eye the nervous suspect during the entire interrogation.
items.ex_zh: 在整个审讯过程中，侦探一直疑窦丛生地注视着那名紧张的嫌疑人。

items.def_en: (+ at/into) to look narrowly or searchingly, as if trying to see clearly
items.ex_en: She had to peer into the dense fog to locate the road signs.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不费力地凝视浓雾，以看清路标。

items.def_en: to look steadily and intently at someone or something for a long time, often in admiration, wonder, or thought.
items.ex_en: They stood on the cliff to gaze at the sunset in sheer wonder.
items.ex_zh: 他们伫立在悬崖边，满怀惊叹地凝视着落日。

items.def_en: (literary or archaic) to see, view, or look attentively at someone or something.
items.ex_en: Travelers stopped in solemn silence to behold the ancient temple in the valley.
items.ex_zh: 旅人们在肃穆的寂静中驻足，瞻仰山谷中的古老神庙。

items.def_en: 1. (informal) to look closely or stare directly at someone or something. 2. to estimate without measuring tools.
items.ex_en: The mechanic began to eyeball the engine before picking up his diagnostic tools.
items.ex_zh: 技工在拿起诊断工具前，先用眼睛仔细打量了一番发动机。

items.def_en: to stare openly and stupidly or rudely at someone or something.
items.ex_en: Tourists gathered to gawk stupidly at the bizarre street performer in the square.
items.ex_zh: 游客们聚集在广场上，呆头呆脑地盯着那个古怪的街头艺人。

items.def_zh: 看见了，注视了（behold 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (literary) past tense and past participle of behold; saw or observed.
items.ex_en: Upon ascending the summit, the weary pilgrims beheld a vista of boundless beauty.
items.ex_zh: 登上顶峰之后，疲惫的朝圣者们目睹了一幅辽阔无垠的壮美风光。

items.def_zh: 目瞪口呆地凝视，张着嘴看
items.def_en: (chiefly British informal) to stare openly and stupidly, often with the mouth open.
items.ex_en: Don't just stand there and gawp at the accident like an idiot.
items.ex_zh: 别傻愣愣地站在那儿张着嘴看车祸，像个白痴似的。

items.def_en: to look directly and continuously at someone or something with eyes wide open.
items.ex_en: It is considered rude to stare at people in public places like trains.
items.ex_zh: 在火车等公共场所盯着别人看被认为是不礼貌的。

items.def_zh: 瞪大眼睛看，惊愕地注视
items.def_en: to look at something with wide, staring eyes, often in surprise, disbelief, or admiration.
items.ex_en: Children began to goggle in disbelief as the magician pulled out living rabbits.
items.ex_zh: 当魔术师变出活生生的兔子时，孩子们难以置信地瞪大了眼睛。

items.def_en: [I/T] to stare at someone in an overtly amorous, lustful, or intrusive manner
items.ex_en: The drunk man continued to ogle every woman who walked past his table.
items.ex_zh: 那个醉汉不断色迷迷地打量着每一个走过他桌旁的女人。

items.def_zh: 目瞪口呆地凝视；张开，裂开
items.def_en: 1. to stare at someone or something with an open mouth, usually in surprise or shock. 2. to be or become wide open.
items.ex_en: Passersby stopped to gape in shock at the deep sinkhole on the street.
items.ex_zh: 路人们停下脚步，惊恐地目瞪口呆看着街道上的巨大深坑。

items.def_zh: 怒目而视，恶狠狠地瞪着
items.def_en: to look at someone in an angry, sullen, or threatening way.
items.ex_en: The captured outlaw sat bound in chains and continued to glower at everyone.
items.ex_zh: 被俘的歹徒被铁链捆绑着，依旧恶狠狠地怒视着所有人。

items.def_zh: 怒目而视，怒瞪；发出刺眼的强光
items.def_en: 1. to look at someone in a very angry or fierce way. 2. to shine with a very bright, uncomfortable light.
items.ex_en: The librarian turned around to glare angrily at the noisy students in back.
items.ex_zh: 图书管理员转过身，愤怒地瞪着后排吵闹的学生。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express directed visual attention, characterized by duration, openness of eyes, and underlying emotional states (such as wonder, shock, hostility, or curiosity). They distinguish brief casual glances from prolonged, fixed, or socially intrusive stares.
groups.summary_zh: 以特定眼神、时长及情绪状态对目标进行注视、打量或审视。
groups.desc_en: Covers visual engagement directed intentionally at a target, differing from passive reception (mere seeing) by indexing duration, investigative intensity, and perceptual intent.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖朝向目标的刻意视觉投射，与被动感知（单纯看见）不同，它通过注视时长、探究深度与观察意图形成区隔。
groups.nuance_en: glance: brief hurried directional dart of the eyes (watch / clock / mirror) · glimpse: momentary incomplete sighting caught in passing (fugitive / view / future) · peer into: strained squinting search through obscurity or tight spaces (darkness / mist / room) · gaze: sustained contemplative or wonder-filled stare (stars / distance / horizon) · sight: deliberate visual acquisition of a sought target (land / enemy / bird)
groups.nuance_zh: glance: 短暂匆促的扫视或一瞥 (watch / clock / mirror) · glimpse: 刹那间捕捉到的残缺视象 (fugitive / view / future) · peer into: 穿透昏暗或狭窄处费力地窥探 (darkness / mist / room) · gaze: 凝神沉思或带赞叹的长久注视 (stars / distance / horizon) · sight: 经过搜寻后终于锁定辨识出目标 (land / enemy / bird)

groups.name: Physical Impact & Striking · 殴击与猛击 (Hit, Strike, Batter)
groups.tip: 各种力度的物理击打

items.def_zh: 急敲，急击；严厉斥责；说唱
items.def_en: 1. to strike sharply and quickly, producing a knocking sound. 2. to criticize sharply. 3. to perform rap music.
items.ex_en: She used the heavy brass knocker to rap sharply on the wooden door.
items.ex_zh: 她用沉重的黄铜门环急促地敲击着木门。

items.def_en: to hit something, especially an insect, with a sharp, flat blow.
items.ex_en: He rolled up a magazine and tried to swat the persistent mosquito away.
items.ex_zh: 他卷起一本杂志，试图将那只纠缠不休的蚊子猛拍下去。

items.def_en: (+ at sb/sth) to hit or try to hit sb/sth with force
items.ex_en: The frightened traveler used his cane to strike out at the growling stray.
items.ex_zh: 受到惊吓的旅人拿起手杖，猛力挥向那只咆哮的流浪狗。

items.def_zh: 击打，碰撞；击中；袭击，造成严重不良影响
items.def_en: 1. to bring a hand, object, etc. forcefully against someone or something. 2. to affect adversely.
items.ex_en: A falling tree branch threatened to hit his car during the severe storm.
items.ex_zh: 在猛烈的风暴中，一根掉落的树枝险些砸中他的汽车。

items.def_zh: 连续击打，敲打；战胜，打败；（心脏等）跳动；搅拌
items.def_en: 1. to strike repeatedly with a hand, stick, or implement. 2. to defeat in a game or contest. 3. to throb or pulsate. 4. to mix vigorously.
items.ex_en: The fierce tribal warriors began to beat their hollow drums to signal battle.
items.ex_zh: 凶悍的部落战士们开始敲响空心鼓，以此发出战斗信号。

items.def_zh: 击打，碰撞；罢工；侵袭；给……以特定印象
items.def_en: 1. to hit someone or something forcefully. 2. to refuse to work as a form of protest. 3. to affect suddenly or give a particular impression to someone.
items.ex_en: A massive tidal wave threatened to strike the fragile coastline with devastating force.
items.ex_zh: 一场巨大的海啸恐将以毁灭性的力量冲击脆弱的海岸线。

items.def_en: 1. to strike a surface noisily, especially to attract attention. 2. to collide with or hit someone or something forcefully.
items.ex_en: Please knock firmly on the principal's office door before you enter the room.
items.ex_zh: 进屋前，请用力敲一下校长办公室的门。

items.def_zh: 击打，撞击（strike 的过去式和过去分词）；给……留下印象
items.def_en: past tense and past participle of strike; hit forcefully, or impressed/affected deeply.
items.ex_en: A falling piece of masonry struck the worker on his protective safety helmet.
items.ex_zh: 一块坠落的砖石砸中了这名工人的安全帽。

items.def_en: (informal) to hit someone on the head, especially with a thrown ball.
items.ex_en: The erratic pitcher managed to accidentally bean the opposing batter with a fastball.
items.ex_zh: 那个失控的投手不慎用快球砸中了对方击球手的脑袋。

items.def_zh: 掌掴，猛击；使劲撞；有……意味
items.def_en: 1. to hit someone or something forcefully with a flat hand or object, making a loud, sharp noise. 2. (smack of) to suggest or have a trace of something bad.
items.ex_en: The frustrated mother threatened to smack the counter to get their divided attention.
items.ex_zh: 心烦意乱的母亲猛击柜台，以吸引他们分散的注意力。

items.def_en: [I/T] to hit heavily, producing a dull, resonant thud
items.ex_en: The furious guard began to thump the reinforced wooden door with his fists.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的守卫开始用拳头砰砰重击加固的木门。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to hurt sb badly by hitting and kicking them repeatedly
items.ex_en: Don't beat yourself up over an honest mistake.
items.ex_zh: 不要因为一次无心之失而过度自责。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack sb violently with physical blows
items.ex_en: The enraged brawler began to lay into his rival with heavy, repeated blows.
items.ex_zh: 怒火中烧的格斗者开始痛击对手，挥拳连连猛打。

items.def_zh: 用拳猛击；按（键），打（孔）；冲压
items.def_en: 1. To hit someone or something hard with a clenched fist. 2. To make a hole or pattern in something using a tool. 3. To press a button or key.
items.ex_en: He stepped forward to punch the padded boxing bag with all his might.
items.ex_zh: 他跨步上前，用尽全力猛击装有软垫的沙袋。

items.def_zh: 猛击，痛击；撞坏；严厉批评
items.def_en: 1. (+ against/into) (informal) To hit someone or something hard and violently. 2. (informal) To criticize someone or a group harshly.
items.ex_en: The angry vandal tried to bash the vandalized car door with a crowbar.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的破坏分子试图用撬棍猛击那扇已被损坏的车门。

items.def_zh: 连续猛击，殴打；使受损，使受重创
items.def_en: (+ at/on) To hit someone or something repeatedly and violently with heavy blows; to damage or affect severely.
items.ex_en: Fierce gale-force winds continue to batter against the weathered coastal stone structures.
items.ex_zh: 狂风肆虐，持续猛烈地拍打着历经风雨的沿海石制建筑。

items.def_zh: （用能量、激光等）击打，摧毁；快速击中；快速移动
items.def_en: (informal) To hit, destroy, or attack someone or something suddenly using a weapon, electric current, or laser; to move very fast.
items.ex_en: The electronic flyswatter allowed him to zap annoying bugs with a quick spark.
items.ex_zh: 电蚊拍让他能用瞬间电火花快速击毙恼人的飞虫。

items.def_en: (+ into/against) (informal) To hit or crash into something violently with a loud, dull impact.
items.ex_en: The speeding vehicle swerved sharply and went wham into the concrete highway barrier.
items.ex_zh: 那辆超速行驶的车辆猛然转向，砰地一声撞上了公路混凝土护栏。

items.def_zh: 重击，猛打；彻底击溃，大胜
items.def_en: (informal) To hit someone or something very hard; to defeat an opponent decisively.
items.ex_en: The heavyweight champion used his powerful left hook to wallop the weary challenger.
items.ex_zh: 这位重量级拳王用有力的左勾拳狠狠重击了疲倦的挑战者。

items.def_en: to strike repeatedly and violently; hit very hard
items.ex_en: The burly bouncer threatened to clobber any unruly patrons causing trouble inside.
items.ex_zh: 身材魁梧的保镖威胁要狠狠收拾里面任何闹事的不规矩顾客。

items.def_zh: 猛击，重击（smite的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (archaic) Past tense and past participle of smite; struck heavily.
items.ex_en: The ancient hero was smit down by a treacherous arrow from behind.
items.ex_zh: 那位古代英雄被一记来自背后的冷箭击倒重创。

items.def_zh: 猛击，重打；重创（smite的过去式）
items.def_en: (archaic / literary) Past tense of smite; struck heavily or afflicted severely.
items.ex_en: With righteous fury, the legendary warrior smote his mortal enemy upon the battlefield.
items.ex_zh: 带着义愤，这位传奇勇士在战场上重创了他的宿敌。

items.def_en: (informal) To hit someone very hard on the head.
items.ex_en: The burglar threatened to brain the homeowner with a heavy brass candelabra.
items.ex_zh: 窃贼威胁要用沉重的黄铜烛台猛击房主的头部。

items.def_en: to hit repeatedly with a heavy club or blunt instrument
items.ex_en: The ruthless attacker tried to bludgeon the defenseless night guard with an iron pipe.
items.ex_zh: 凶狠的袭击者试图用铁管痛殴毫无防备的夜班守卫。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote an agent forcefully delivering an impact against a person or surface, varying from light, sharp raps to brutal, bludgeoning blows. Register ranges from casual/colloquial smacks to formal or literary strikes and sustained beatings.
groups.summary_zh: 施加物理外力进行击打、猛击或连续殴打。
groups.desc_en: Involves delivering a forceful contact or blow to a surface, distinguished from steady mechanical pressure or friction by kinetic abruptness and tactile shock.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过动能骤然施加于物体表面的撞击力，与持续机械压力或摩擦相斥，强调突发性碰撞与物理震荡。
groups.nuance_en: hit: direct kinetic collision or blow with force (target / ball / wall) · strike: decisive sharp contact delivered with sudden impact (clock / blow / terror) · rap: quick sharp percussive tap (knuckles / gavel / window) · swat: brisk sweeping slap aimed at flattening a pest or flying object (fly / mosquito / hand) · beat: repetitive punishing rhythmic blows (drum / victim / wings)
groups.nuance_zh: hit: 最基础直接的强力撞击或击打 (target / ball / wall) · strike: 决绝突发且具冲击性的打击 (clock / blow / terror) · rap: 快速清脆的轻敲或叩击 (knuckles / gavel / window) · swat: 挥动式猛拍扁平物体或飞虫 (fly / mosquito / hand) · beat: 连续节律性的惩罚性殴打或拍击 (drum / victim / wings)

groups.name: Expansion & Proliferation · 暴增与膨胀 (Grow, Surge, Skyrocket)
groups.tip: 从平缓生长到急速膨胀剧增

items.def_en: (+ sth) to increase in amount, size, or strength over time
items.ex_en: The athlete worked patiently to build up her stamina before the grueling marathon.
items.ex_zh: 在艰苦的马拉松开赛前，这名运动员耐心地逐渐积蓄耐力。
items.ex2_en: Dangerous water pressure will build up behind the old wooden dam.
items.ex2_zh: 老木坝后会逐渐积聚起危险的水压。

items.def_zh: 增长，扩大；生长，成长；逐渐变得；种植
items.def_en: 1. To increase in size, amount, degree, or power. 2. To develop or mature naturally as a plant or animal. 3. To become gradually. 4. To cultivate plants.
items.ex_en: The local tech company continues to grow steadily despite difficult economic market conditions.
items.ex_zh: 尽管经济市场环境艰难，这家本土科技公司仍在稳步扩张。
items.ex2_en: Local farmers grow sweet organic strawberries along the fertile river bank.
items.ex2_zh: 当地农民在肥沃的河岸边种植甜美的有机草莓。

items.def_zh: （月亮）渐圆，渐满；变大，增大；给……上蜡
items.def_en: 1. (literary) When the moon waxes, it appears to become larger and rounder. 2. To increase in size, strength, or degree. 3. To polish or coat with wax.
items.ex_en: Astronomers gathered atop the remote hill to observe the celestial crescent moon wax.
items.ex_zh: 天文学家们聚集在偏僻的山顶上，观察那轮弦月逐渐渐盈。

items.def_en: To become larger or greater in number, amount, size, or degree; to make something become larger or greater.
items.ex_en: The firm planned to increase production capacity significantly to meet growing global demand.
items.ex_zh: 该公司计划大幅提高产能，以满足日益增长的全球需求。
items.ex2_en: Demand for electric vehicles will increase significantly over the next decade.
items.ex2_zh: 对电动汽车的需求在未来十年将显著增加。

items.def_zh: 膨胀，增大；（健身）增肌；使变大
items.def_en: (also 'bulk up') To become larger, thicker, or heavier, especially by gaining muscle mass.
items.ex_en: He consumes protein shakes daily to bulk up before the regional bodybuilding competition.
items.ex_zh: 他每天喝蛋白粉奶昔，以便在地区健美赛前有效增肌。
items.ex2_en: The distribution company bulks smaller parcels into large shipping containers daily.
items.ex2_zh: 这家分销公司每天将小包裹集装成大型集装箱。

items.def_zh: 膨胀，肿胀；（数量或体积）增加，扩大
items.def_en: 1. To become larger and rounder than normal, often due to injury, fluid, or pressure. 2. To increase in size, number, or volume.
items.ex_en: His sprained ankle began to swell visibly within an hour of the injury.
items.ex_zh: 受伤后不到一小时，他扭伤的脚踝就开始明显肿胀起来。
items.ex2_en: Heavy monsoon rains quickly swell mountain streams into raging muddy torrents.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的季风降雨很快使山涧涨成汹涌的泥泞洪流。

items.def_en: [I/T] to increase or intensify by rapid stages
items.ex_en: Border disputes can escalate rapidly into armed international conflicts if left entirely unchecked.
items.ex_zh: 如果完全不加遏制，边界争端可能会迅速升级为武装国际冲突。
items.ex2_en: Both nations tried not to escalate diplomatic tensions into violent warfare.
items.ex2_zh: 两国都尽量不使外交紧张局势升级为暴力冲突。

items.def_zh: 长得过大而不适于；长得比……快（或高、大）；因长大而改掉
items.def_en: 1. To grow too big for clothes or an environment. 2. To grow bigger or faster than someone or something else. 3. To stop doing or needing something as you become more mature.
items.ex_en: The child will outgrow his winter clothes before the cold season finally ends.
items.ex_zh: 在寒季彻底结束之前，这个孩子就会长得穿不下他的冬衣了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to increase sharply or make sth increase significantly in amount, speed, or size
items.ex_en: The factory had to ramp up medical supply output during the health emergency.
items.ex_zh: 在卫生紧急状态期间，该工厂不得不大幅提高医疗用品的产量。
items.ex2_en: Automobile production will ramp up considerably once chip shipments arrive safely.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦芯片货物安全送达，汽车产量将大幅增加。

items.def_zh: 猛增，急升；刺穿，扎破；在（饮料）中掺烈酒（或毒药）
items.def_en: 1. To rise sharply and suddenly to a high peak. 2. To pierce or fasten with a sharp spike. 3. To secretly add alcohol or a drug to a drink.
items.ex_en: Electricity consumption tends to spike dramatically during exceptionally hot summer afternoon hours.
items.ex_zh: 在异常炎热的夏日午后，用电量往往会急剧猛增。
items.ex2_en: Unexpected economic news can spike interest rates throughout global financial markets.
items.ex2_zh: 出人意料的经济消息可能会使全球金融市场的利率猛增。

items.def_zh: 急剧增加，激增；膨胀如气球
items.def_en: 1. To increase very rapidly in amount, degree, or size. 2. To swell out like a balloon.
items.ex_en: Unchecked public spending caused the small municipal budget deficit to balloon beyond control.
items.ex_zh: 未受约束的公共支出导致这座小城市的预算赤字急剧膨胀失控。

items.def_zh: （使）急剧增长，（使）大幅提升（尤与up连用）；狂暴地冲撞
items.def_en: (also 'ramp up') To increase the level, speed, or amount of something sharply.
items.ex_en: The company decided to ramp marketing spending ahead of the critical product release.
items.ex_zh: 该公司决定在重要产品发布前大幅增加营销支出。
items.ex2_en: Passenger traffic ramps considerably during the festive holiday travel travel rush.
items.ex2_zh: 在节日旅游高峰期间，客流量会大幅飙升。

items.def_zh: 剧增，急升；汹涌奔腾，急冲
items.def_en: 1. To increase suddenly and strongly in level, value, or intensity. 2. To move suddenly and powerfully in a particular direction.
items.ex_en: Investor confidence helped corporate share prices surge abruptly to new historic record heights.
items.ex_zh: 投资者的信心促使公司股价骤增，创下历史新高。

items.def_zh: 迅速增长，雨后春笋般涌现
items.def_en: To increase, spread, or develop at an extremely rapid rate.
items.ex_en: New software startups continue to mushroom throughout the thriving metropolitan technology district.
items.ex_zh: 新兴软件初创公司在欣欣向荣的大都市科技园区内如雨后春笋般涌现。

items.def_zh: 成金字塔式递增，急剧增加；使呈金字塔状堆叠
items.def_en: To increase rapidly in amount, size, or stages; to arrange or pile up in the shape of a pyramid.
items.ex_en: Unpaid credit card interest charges quickly pyramid into an overwhelming financial disaster.
items.ex_zh: 未偿还的信用卡利息费用会如金字塔般急剧滚存为灭顶之灾。
items.ex2_en: The aggressive investor pyramid loans across multiple properties to maximize returns.
items.ex2_zh: 这位激进的投资者通过在多处房产上滚动加码贷款来追求最大收益。

items.def_en: 1. To rise very quickly to a high level or amount. 2. To fly or glide high in the air.
items.ex_en: Severe geopolitical tensions caused world crude petroleum prices to soar almost overnight.
items.ex_zh: 严峻的地缘政治紧张局势导致全球原油价格几乎一夜暴涨。

items.def_zh: 滚雪球般迅速增长，急剧扩大；掷雪球
items.def_en: 1. To grow rapidly larger, more serious, or more intense at an accelerating pace. 2. To throw snowballs at.
items.ex_en: A minor minor clerical error can snowball quickly into a catastrophic corporate auditing crisis.
items.ex_zh: 一个微小的文书错误也能像滚雪球般迅速扩大为灾难性的企业审计危机。

items.def_zh: 迅速生长，繁荣发展；萌芽
items.def_en: (formal) To grow, expand, or develop rapidly and successfully.
items.ex_en: International trade partnerships began to burgeon across the flourishing newly unified economic bloc.
items.ex_zh: 国际贸易伙伴关系在欣欣向荣的新统一经济区内蓬勃发展。

items.def_en: To increase, multiply, or spread rapidly in number or quantity.
items.ex_en: Toxic algae blooms proliferate rapidly whenever agricultural fertilizer runoff contaminates freshwater lakes.
items.ex_zh: 每当农业化肥流失污染淡水湖泊时，有毒藻华就会迅速繁殖泛滥。

items.def_en: to increase or rise very suddenly and rapidly
items.ex_en: Local home prices shoot up sharply whenever new transit hubs are publicly announced.
items.ex_zh: 每当新的交通枢纽方案公布时，当地房价都会暴涨猛升。

items.def_en: to increase suddenly, dramatically, and precipitously in quantity
items.ex_en: Subscriptions to the innovative streaming platform explode following the viral documentary release.
items.ex_zh: 在那部引发热议的纪录片播出后，这款创新流媒体平台的订阅量骤然激增。

items.def_en: To increase extremely fast to a very high level.
items.ex_en: Ticket prices skyrocket as diehard sports fans scramble to attend the championship game.
items.ex_zh: 随着狂热体育迷争相抢购决赛门票，票价一路飙升。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail an escalation in size, volume, price, or quantity, progressing from steady organic increases to sudden, explosive, vertical spikes. Nuances distinguish continuous accretion, physical swelling, and explosive exponential multiplying.
groups.summary_zh: 数量、规模或程度由缓步扩增至剧烈爆发式膨胀暴涨。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an upward or outward magnification in volume, degree, or extent, differing from baseline accumulation by an accelerated or critical-mass momentum.
groups.desc_zh: 指体量、程度或范围向上或向外的急剧扩增，与平缓积累不同，带有一种加速累积或突破临界点的迸发态势。
groups.nuance_en: grow: natural organic increase in maturity or size (business / plant / confidence) · swell: outward distension or surging volume near bursting (crowd / ranks / waves) · escalate: sharp upward spiral in intensity or gravity (conflict / tension / dispute) · build up: gradual strategic accumulation toward a peak (reserves / pressure / momentum) · outgrow: expand beyond the capacity or suitability of an earlier state (clothes / premises / fear)
groups.nuance_zh: grow: 自然有机地发育变大或增长 (business / plant / confidence) · swell: 鼓胀膨胀或体量汹涌暴增至几近饱和 (crowd / ranks / waves) · escalate: 冲突或危机急剧升级螺旋恶化 (conflict / tension / dispute) · build up: 循序渐进地积累汇聚以蓄势 (reserves / pressure / momentum) · outgrow: 因体量过度增长而脱离或不再适宜原有容器 (clothes / premises / fear)

groups.name: Defeat & Overpower · 战胜与溃败 (Defeat, Overcome, Rout)
groups.tip: 战胜压制并征服对手

items.def_en: to defeat an opponent by a very narrow margin
items.ex_en: The reigning champion managed to edge out his determined challenger by two points.
items.ex_zh: 卫冕冠军仅以两分的微弱优势险胜他那斗志昂扬的挑战者。

items.def_zh: （在最后一刻以微弱优势）险胜，击败；破壳而出；唧唧叫
items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British informal) To defeat someone by a very narrow margin, especially at the last moment. 2. To peck through an eggshell; to chirp.
items.ex_en: The talented young British sprinter managed to pip the veteran at the tape.
items.ex_zh: 那位天赋出众的年轻英国短跑手在终点线前险胜老将。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to defeat a challenger or opponent in a contest or fight
items.ex_en: The experienced grandmaster managed to see off his aggressive opponent in forty moves.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的特级大师在四十回合内彻底击溃了攻势凌厉的对手。

items.def_en: to succeed or prevail after a prolonged contest or struggle
items.ex_en: Despite all the political interference, common sense eventually won out.
items.ex_zh: 尽管受到重重政治干扰，常识和理性最终还是占了上风。

items.def_zh: （在体育比赛中）封杀，使对手一分未得；使模糊，抹去
items.def_en: 1. (North American sports) To prevent an opposing team or player from scoring any points. 2. To become blank or cause something to become blank.
items.ex_en: The dominant hockey defense managed to blank their fierce traditional rivals completely tonight.
items.ex_zh: 今晚，占统治地位的冰球队防线成功将凶悍的宿敌彻底零封。

items.def_zh: 以多数票击败，以票数胜过
items.def_en: To defeat someone or a proposal by winning a greater number of votes.
items.ex_en: Shareholders gathered yesterday to decisively outvote the board's proposed controversial corporate restructuring.
items.ex_zh: 股东们昨天集会，以多数票否决了董事会提出的充满争议的公司重组方案。

items.def_en: 1. To be successful or victorious in a game, fight, or competition; to defeat an opponent. 2. To achieve or gain something through effort.
items.ex_en: Our talented debate team worked tirelessly to win the difficult regional interscholastic championship.
items.ex_zh: 我们才华横溢的辩论队不知疲倦地奋战，最终赢得了艰难的地区校际锦标赛。

items.def_zh: 击败，胜过；出王牌赢过；优先于
items.def_en: 1. To beat someone or something by doing or saying something better, or by having a stronger advantage. 2. To play a trump card that beats another card.
items.ex_en: Her extensive practical experience ultimately trumped his impressive academic qualifications during the final interview.
items.ex_zh: 在最终面试中，她丰富的实践经验最终胜过了他那亮眼的学历背景。

items.def_en: (formal) To defeat someone completely in a fight, argument, or competition.
items.ex_en: The veteran barrister thoroughly worsted the inexperienced prosecutor during yesterday's intense cross-examination.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的大律师在昨天激烈的分辨盘问中彻底击败了初出茅庐的检察官。

items.def_en: 1. To win a victory over someone in a battle, contest, or competition. 2. To prevent a plan, aim, or proposal from succeeding.
items.ex_en: The alliance successfully defeated the rebel forces after a decisive three-day engagement.
items.ex_zh: 经过为期三天的决定性交战，盟军成功击溃了叛乱部队。

items.def_en: to overwhelm, subdue, or defeat utterly and decisively
items.ex_en: The championship favorites crushed their underprepared opponents with an overwhelming offensive barrage.
items.ex_zh: 夺冠热门队伍以势不可挡的攻势彻底击溃了准备不足的对手。

items.def_zh: 战胜，征服；克服（困难等）；受到……强烈压倒（或影响）
items.def_en: 1. To defeat an opponent or enemy. 2. To succeed in dealing with a problem, emotion, or difficulty. 3. (usually passive) To affect someone deeply or overpower them.
items.ex_en: The national team fought tenaciously to overcome their fierce regional rivals last night.
items.ex_zh: 国家队昨晚奋力拼搏，最终战胜了劲敌。

items.def_en: (North American informal) To defeat an opponent completely in a game without allowing them to score any points.
items.ex_en: Our softball team skunked the reigning league champions seven to zero this afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 今天下午，我们垒球队以七比零的比分把卫冕冠军剃了个光头。

items.def_zh: 在谋略上胜过，智胜；侧翼包抄（敌军）
items.def_en: 1. To gain an advantage over a rival by using cleverer tactics. 2. (military) To move around the side of an enemy army.
items.ex_en: The chief executive cleverly outflanked the hostile takeover bid through decisive boardroom diplomacy.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官通过果断的董事会斡旋手段，在策略上巧妙击溃了敌意收购。

items.def_zh: 以谋略击败，在策略上胜过
items.def_en: To defeat or gain an advantage over an opponent by using superior tactics or cleverness.
items.ex_en: The nimble startup outmaneuvered established corporate giants through rapid software deployment and agility.
items.ex_zh: 这家充满活力的初创企业凭借敏捷性与快速的软件迭代，在策略上击败了老牌巨头。

items.def_en: To be much better, stronger, or more capable than an opponent.
items.ex_en: The challenger's impressive technique gradually outmatched the reigning champion's raw fighting power.
items.ex_zh: 挑战者精湛的战术技巧逐渐压制并战胜了卫冕冠军纯粹的蛮力。

items.def_en: To conquer and take back land or control from an enemy.
items.ex_en: Imperial forces launched a massive spring offensive to reconquer the disputed border province.
items.ex_zh: 帝国军队发起了一场大规模的春季攻势，以重新夺回那座争议边界省份。

items.def_zh: 以谋略击败，在策略上胜过
items.def_en: (British English spelling of outmaneuver) To defeat or gain an advantage over an opponent by using superior tactics.
items.ex_en: The minister adroitly outmanoeuvred his political rivals during the heated parliamentary committee debate.
items.ex_zh: 在激烈的议会委员会辩论中，那位部长巧妙运筹，在策略上压倒了政敌。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to completely destroy or overwhelmingly defeat an opponent
items.ex_en: Our squad completely wiped out the opposing team before the first round ended.
items.ex_zh: 第一轮比赛还没结束，我们战队就把对手全部歼灭了。

items.def_en: To defeat an army or opponent completely and force them to flee in disorder.
items.ex_en: The coalition forces decisively routed the defending army, precipitating a chaotic general retreat.
items.ex_zh: 联军以压倒性优势彻底击溃守军，引发了对方混乱的全线溃败。

items.def_en: to thoroughly defeat in battle, contest, or conflict
items.ex_en: The heroic knight vowed to vanquish the treacherous usurper and restore lawful peace.
items.ex_zh: 英勇的骑士立誓彻底铲除奸诈的篡位者，重铸正义与和平。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe prevailing over an opponent, competitor, or obstacle, graded by the margin and decisiveness of victory. They span from narrowly edging past someone or tactical outmaneuvering to overwhelming subjugation and complete, chaotic destruction.
groups.summary_zh: 在竞争或冲突中战胜对手，从险胜智取到全面溃败征服。
groups.desc_en: Encapsulates prevailing over an opponent in a competitive, martial, or strategic trial, contrasting with mere survival by leaving the adversary definitively vanquished or subordinated.
groups.desc_zh: 概括在竞争、战斗或博弈中压制对手，与单纯自保不同，侧重彻底确立胜势并使对手屈居下风或遭淘汰。
groups.nuance_en: defeat: conclusive mastery over an opponent in contest (army / champion / bill) · edge out: prevail by the narrowest of fractional margins (rival / competitor / incumbent) · pip: defeat narrowly right at the finish line (opponent / rival / favorite) · see off: repel or outlast a challenger until safely eliminated (threat / challenge / rivals) · trump: override decisively using superior force or authority (argument / ace / card)
groups.nuance_zh: defeat: 正式而决定性地击溃对手 (army / champion / bill) · edge out: 以极其微弱的优势险胜挤掉 (rival / competitor / incumbent) · pip: 在终点线前一刻极微优势反超胜出 (opponent / rival / favorite) · see off: 顽强顶住挑战并将其彻底赶跑清除 (threat / challenge / rivals) · trump: 凭绝对优势王牌直接压倒碾压 (argument / ace / card)

groups.name: Locomotion & Rapid Striding · 奔跑与疾行 (Run, Sprint, Gallop)
groups.tip: 步伐加快的高速奔跑

items.def_zh: 慢跑，缓步跑；轻推；唤起（记忆）
items.def_en: 1. To run slowly and steadily, especially for exercise. 2. To nudge or push gently. 3. ('jog someone's memory') To cause someone to remember something.
items.ex_en: David likes to jog around the peaceful suburban reservoir early every morning.
items.ex_zh: 戴维喜欢每天清晨绕着宁静的郊区水库慢跑。

items.def_en: When a horse canters, it moves at a smooth, easy running pace between a trot and a gallop; to ride a horse at this pace.
items.ex_en: The sleek mare began to canter smoothly across the wide grassy meadow.
items.ex_zh: 那匹健美温顺的母马开始在广阔的草地上平稳地慢步奔跑。
items.ex2_en: The skilled jockey cantered the nervous horse around the dirt track.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的骑师策马在泥地跑道上慢跑。

items.def_en: 1. To walk around while asleep. 2. (figurative) To act in a way that risks danger without realizing it.
items.ex_en: The worried mother watched her young son sleepwalk quietly down the darkened hallway.
items.ex_zh: 忧心忡忡的母亲看着年幼的儿子在昏暗的走廊里悄悄梦游。

items.def_en: To walk or travel across deep snow wearing snowshoes.
items.ex_en: We had to snowshoe across the frozen valley after the heavy overnight blizzard.
items.ex_zh: 昨夜暴风雪过后，我们不得不踩着雪鞋穿过冰封的山谷。

items.def_zh: 沉重缓慢地走；吃力苦干
items.def_en: (+ along/through/on) To walk slowly with heavy, tired steps; to work steadily and unexcitingly at a boring task.
items.ex_en: Exhausted travelers continued to plod along the muddy track toward the distant village.
items.ex_zh: 筋疲力竭的旅人沿着泥泞的小路，步履沉重地朝远方的村庄蹒跚前行。

items.def_zh: 踩，踏，行走（tread的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of tread; walked, stepped on, or pressed down with feet.
items.ex_en: The lone pilgrim trod the stony mountain path under the fading evening light.
items.ex_zh: 孤独的朝圣者在日暮残阳中踏过崎岖不平的碎石山径。

items.def_zh: 徐徐前行，行进（通常用 wend one's way）
items.def_en: ('wend one's way') (literary) To travel or walk slowly in a specified direction.
items.ex_en: Weary pilgrims slowly wended their way toward the ancient sanctuary atop the hill.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的朝圣者们沿着山路徐徐前行，走向山顶那座古老的圣所。

items.def_en: to leave a place very quickly on foot
items.ex_en: He had to dash off immediately to catch the final outbound commuter train.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不飞奔离开，去赶最后一班开往郊区的通勤列车。

items.def_zh: 奔跑，疾行；运转，运行；经营，管理
items.def_en: 1. To move swiftly on foot with both feet leaving the ground simultaneously at each stride. 2. To operate or function. 3. To manage or oversee.
items.ex_en: The excited children run across the wide playground whenever the recess bell rings.
items.ex_zh: 每当下课铃声响起，兴奋的孩子们就会飞奔穿过宽敞的操场。
items.ex2_en: She runs an efficient logistics company that delivers goods across Europe.
items.ex2_zh: 她经营着一家高效的物流公司，向全欧洲运送货物。

items.def_zh: 匆忙赶路，急忙疾行；催促
items.def_en: 1. To move or act very quickly or fast. 2. To urge someone to act or move faster.
items.ex_en: Commuters hurry through the crowded terminal every morning to catch connecting train services.
items.ex_zh: 每天早晨，通勤族都急匆匆地穿过拥挤的航站楼去赶换乘列车。
items.ex2_en: The urgent phone call hurried the weary detective out of bed.
items.ex2_zh: 一通紧急电话催促着疲惫的侦探匆忙起床。

items.def_zh: 大步快走，阔步行进；跨过
items.def_en: 1. (+ across/into/along) To walk quickly with long, confident, decisive steps. 2. To step across or over.
items.ex_en: The director strode purposefully across the bustling studio to greet the distinguished visitors.
items.ex_zh: 总监迈着自信的大步穿过繁忙的演播室，去迎接尊贵的访客。

items.def_zh: 疾跑，急步走（常作 hoof it）；踢
items.def_en: (also 'hoof it') (informal) To run or walk briskly somewhere.
items.ex_en: Since our car broke down unexpectedly, we had to hoof it five miles.
items.ex_zh: 既然车子半路抛锚了，我们只得硬着头皮徒步急行五英里。

items.def_en: to run away at maximum speed over a short distance
items.ex_en: The guilty suspect panicked and sprinted off through the crowded subway station.
items.ex_zh: 心虚的嫌疑人慌了神，拔腿全速冲刺逃穿过拥挤的地跌站。

items.def_en: to move or run somewhere very quickly and excitedly
items.ex_en: Two mischievous boys tore along the narrow corridor, ignoring repeated warnings from teachers.
items.ex_zh: 两个调皮的男孩在狭窄的走廊里疯跑狂奔，全然不顾老师们的屡次警告。

items.def_zh: 疾行，狂奔；赛跑，竞赛；使飞速运转
items.def_en: 1. To run or move very fast in a hurry. 2. To compete against someone in a speed contest. 3. To operate or cause to operate at high speed.
items.ex_en: Panicked shoppers raced toward the emergency exits when the loud fire alarm sounded.
items.ex_zh: 刺耳的火警响起时，惊慌失措的顾客们拔腿向紧急出口狂奔。
items.ex2_en: The millionaire driver will race his classic sports car this weekend.
items.ex2_zh: 这位百万富翁车手将于本周末驾驶他的经典跑车参加比赛。

items.def_en: (+ to/into) to run or move suddenly and rapidly over a short distance
items.ex_en: She had to dash into the nearby grocery store before the downpour started.
items.ex_zh: 暴雨倾盆而下之前，她不得不猛冲进附近的杂货店躲避。

items.def_en: (+ across/out) to move rapidly and suddenly like a projectile
items.ex_en: A frightened squirrel darted across the busy suburban driveway toward the protective bushes.
items.ex_zh: 一只受惊的松鼠敏捷地疾冲穿过繁忙的私家车道，窜向有遮蔽的灌木丛。

items.def_en: (+ off/away) (chiefly British informal) To run very fast, like a hare.
items.ex_en: The startled rabbit hared away across the open lawn into the thick undergrowth.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的野兔像脱缰般飞奔穿过开阔的草坪，窜入了密林灌木丛中。

items.def_en: to run away with sudden, uncontrolled speed, often in alarm
items.ex_en: The frightened horse suddenly bolted down the dusty country lane, tossing its rider.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的马匹突然脱缰般狂奔下尘土飞扬的乡间小道，把骑手甩了下来。

items.def_en: To run or move at maximum speed over a short distance.
items.ex_en: Athletes sprint toward the finish line with every ounce of their remaining energy.
items.ex_zh: 运动员们使出浑身最后一点力气，全速向终点线冲刺。

items.def_zh: （马）飞奔，全速跑；疾驰，急速前进
items.def_en: When a horse gallops, it runs at its fastest pace; to move or progress very quickly.
items.ex_en: Wild stallions gallop freely across the rugged plains under the clear morning sky.
items.ex_zh: 在晴朗的晨空下，野马群在起伏辽阔的荒原上肆意飞奔。
items.ex2_en: The young rider galloped her horse through the muddy forest path.
items.ex2_zh: 年轻的骑手策马疾驰穿过泥泞的森林小道。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate self-propelled terrestrial locomotion, graded by gait, velocity, and exertion. They separate slow, heavy plodding from rhythmic jogging, sustained long running, and full-effort, high-speed sprinting.
groups.summary_zh: 以不同步态、速度与发力程度进行地面奔跑或疾速行进。
groups.desc_en: Signifies purposeful terrestrial movement across space, departing from generic displacement by highlighting cadence, physical gait, and specific kinematic resistance.
groups.desc_zh: 指具有明确动作特性的地面位移，脱离单纯的空间移动概念，强调步频、体态及特定动力学阻力特征。
groups.nuance_en: jog: steady rhythmic low-impact conditioning trot (memory / park / pace) · canter: smooth easy three-beat bound between trot and gallop (horse / pace / trail) · plod: heavy laboured footstep dragging under fatigue or load (mud / way / footsteps) · dash off: sudden sprint departing in high haste (note / scene / errand) · wend: slow leisurely progress along an indirect path (way / home / road)
groups.nuance_zh: jog: 匀速规律的慢跑锻炼或适度触发 (memory / park / pace) · canter: 介于快步与疾驰之间从容优雅的慢跳跑 (horse / pace / trail) · plod: 负重或疲惫下沉重费力地蹒跚前行 (mud / way / footsteps) · dash off: 极度匆忙下骤然狂奔离开或草草挥就 (note / scene / errand) · wend: 沿着曲折路径缓慢从容地行进 (way / home / road)

groups.name: Settle & Disburse Funds · 支付与费用结算 (Pay, Remit, Defray)
groups.tip: 付款买单结清账目

items.def_zh: 支付，付款；偿还；付代价；值得，带来收益
items.def_en: To give money for goods, services, or debts; to yield a return or benefit.
items.ex_en: Customers must pay for their selected groceries before leaving the checkout counter.
items.ex_zh: 顾客在离开结账柜台之前必须为所选购的食品杂货付款。

items.def_zh: 给……开账单，向……收费；把……宣传为，将……列入节目单
items.def_en: To send a bill or charge an amount to someone; to advertise or promote in a specified way.
items.ex_en: The hospital will bill your insurance provider directly for all inpatient medical expenses.
items.ex_zh: 医院会就全部住院医疗费用直接向您的保险公司寄送账单结算。

items.def_zh: （pay的过去式及过去分词）支付，付款；偿还
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of pay: to give money for goods, services, or debts.
items.ex_en: She promptly paid all outstanding household utility invoices using the mobile banking application.
items.ex_zh: 她使用手机银行应用程序迅速结清了所有未付的家庭水电公用账单。

items.def_zh: 支付，负担（费用，尤用于 foot the bill）；步行
items.def_en: To pay for something, especially a bill or expenses (most commonly in 'foot the bill'); to walk.
items.ex_en: Taxpayers inevitably have to foot the exorbitant bill for repeated infrastructure cost overruns.
items.ex_zh: 纳税人不可避免地要为基础设施建设的一再超支承担高昂账单。

items.def_zh: 付酬金给；出资聘用（尤指专业人士）
items.def_en: To pay a fee to someone (especially a lawyer, doctor, or agent) for their services.
items.ex_en: The multinational corporation feely retained elite patent counsel to handle the contentious dispute.
items.ex_zh: 该跨国公司出资聘请了精英专利律师来处理这起充满争议的纠纷。

items.def_en: (+ with) to pay what is owed so that debts between parties are cleared
items.ex_en: If you pay for the groceries now, we can settle up when we get home.
items.ex_zh: 要是你现在先付食材的钱，我们到家后再结清。

items.def_en: to reluctantly provide or pay an amount of money demanded
items.ex_en: The stubborn tenant finally coughed up the overdue rent after receiving another eviction warning.
items.ex_zh: 收到又一封驱逐警告信后，顽固的租客终于不情愿地掏出了拖欠的租金。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to finish paying all the money that you owe for sth
items.ex_en: It took them fifteen arduous years of disciplined saving to pay off their mortgage.
items.ex_zh: 他们经过了十五年省吃俭用的艰苦积蓄，才终于还清了房屋抵押贷款。

items.def_zh: 结清欠款；全额付款（尤指勉强）
items.def_en: to give sb the money that you owe them, especially when unwilling
items.ex_en: After several legal warnings, the tenant finally paid up the overdue rent.
items.ex_zh: 经过几次法律警告后，租客终于结清了拖欠的房租。

items.def_zh: 支付；掏腰包（尤指迫不得已）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to spend a lot of money on sth, especially reluctantly
items.ex_en: We had to fork out hundreds of dollars for sudden unexpected automobile repairs.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不自掏腰包数几百美元，用来支付突如其来的汽车维修费。

items.def_en: (British English variant of check) To pay by writing a cheque.
items.ex_en: The retired solicitor preferred to cheque all substantial maintenance payments directly to contractors.
items.ex_zh: 这位退休的事务律师更习惯于直接向承包商开具支票支付大额维修款项。

items.def_en: to repay money that someone has spent on official business or services
items.ex_en: The agency will promptly reimburse authorized business expenses upon submission of valid receipts.
items.ex_zh: 办事机构将在提交有效收据后，立即报销经过核准的公务支出费用。

items.def_zh: 下赌注；付款，出资（尤用于 ante up）
items.def_en: (+ up) (gambling / informal) To put money into the pot before cards are dealt; to pay an amount of money required.
items.ex_en: Every participant had to ante up twenty dollars before joining the holiday gift pool.
items.ex_zh: 每位参与者在加入节日礼品互赠池之前，都必须交纳二十美元。

items.def_zh: （prepay的过去式及过去分词）预付，先付
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of prepay: to pay for in advance.
items.ex_en: The organizers prepaid the auditorium rental fees well before the international symposium commenced.
items.ex_zh: 组织者在国际研讨会开幕之前，早就提前结清了礼堂的租赁费用。

items.def_zh: 汇出，汇寄（款项）；免除，赦免（债务、惩罚）；提交，下呈（审理）
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) (finance) To send money in payment or transfer funds. 2. (formal) To cancel a debt, penalty, or prison sentence.
items.ex_en: Please remit the total balance due to our overseas treasury account within thirty days.
items.ex_zh: 请在三十日内将应付全额款项汇入我方的海外资金账户。

items.def_zh: （underpay的过去式及过去分词）少付……报酬，付给……过低的工资
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of underpay: to pay too little money for work done.
items.ex_en: The garment factory underpaid vulnerable migrant workers for months until state regulators intervened.
items.ex_zh: 这家服装厂少付了弱势外来劳工数月的薪酬，直至政府监管机构介入。

items.def_zh: 划拨，支付（官方/基金款项）
items.def_en: to pay out money from an official fund or institutional account
items.ex_en: The financial committee authorized the treasurer to disburse emergency grant funds immediately.
items.ex_zh: 财务委员会正式授权财务官立即划拨并支付紧急援助赠款。

items.def_en: (formal) To pay or contribute money toward the cost or expenses of something.
items.ex_en: A generous bequest helped defray the substantial publishing costs of the historical manuscript.
items.ex_zh: 一笔慷慨的遗产捐赠帮助支付了这部历史手稿出版所需的大笔费用。

items.def_en: (formal) To pay someone money for work, services, or expenses provided.
items.ex_en: The university pledges to remunerate visiting fellows in accordance with standard international guidelines.
items.ex_zh: 校方承诺按照现行国际标准规程，向各位访问学者支付相应劳务报酬。

items.def_en: To pay for goods, services, or postage in advance before receiving or using them.
items.ex_en: Clients must prepay shipping charges before our warehouse releases international bulk orders.
items.ex_zh: 在仓库放行国际大宗货单之前，客户必须先行预付运费。

items.def_zh: 少付……报酬，付给……过低的工资
items.def_en: To pay a worker less money than they deserve or less than the statutory rate.
items.ex_en: Unscrupulous contractors often underpay temporary seasonal laborers during heavy harvesting periods.
items.ex_zh: 不道德的承包商往往在繁重的秋收农忙期间少付临时季节工的工资。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail transferring monetary compensation in satisfaction of a debt, invoice, service, or shared cost. Distinct scenario variants encompass advance payment ('prepay'), legal reimbursement/coverage ('defray'), transmitting institutional remittances ('remit'), or footing the entire bill.
groups.summary_zh: 就商品、服务或债务结算款项，包括垫付、汇付及结清。
groups.desc_en: Relates to the financial discharge of liabilities or expenditures, contrasting with generic gifting or wealth exchange by adhering to formal billing, compensatory duty, or grudging settlement.
groups.desc_zh: 指财务债务、开销的清偿与结算，与泛化的赠予或财产流转不同，强调依循账单清结、补偿性义务或被迫买单。
groups.nuance_en: pay: direct generic handover of currency for debts or goods (bill / price / rent) · foot: bear the full and often unwelcome cost of an undertaking (bill / expense / tab) · settle up: clear remaining balance to square mutual accounts (tab / balance / debt) · cough up: reluctantly part with demanded money under duress (cash / ransom / fine) · pay off: fully liquidate a long-term debt or illicitly bribe (mortgage / official / loan)
groups.nuance_zh: pay: 最通用的按值支付货币清还费用 (bill / price / rent) · foot: 承担全部且往往令人无奈的昂贵账单 (bill / expense / tab) · settle up: 与对方核对并彻底结清余账债务 (tab / balance / debt) · cough up: 被迫勉强掏钱认账或吐出赃款 (cash / ransom / fine) · pay off: 彻底还清长期贷款或行贿封口 (mortgage / official / loan)

groups.name: Deceive & Mislead · 欺骗与误导 (Dupe, Swindle, Delude)
groups.tip: 虚假陈述或故意误导他人

items.def_en: (+ into) To deceive someone, often in order to get them to do something foolish
items.ex_en: The imposter managed to trick the gullible clerk into revealing confidential office passwords.
items.ex_zh: 冒名顶替者设法诱骗轻信的职员透露了机密的办公室密码。

items.def_en: (informal) To confuse, baffle, or trick someone.
items.ex_en: The subtle logical loophole completely foxed the defense attorney during cross-examination yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 那个微妙的逻辑漏洞在昨天的交叉质证中彻底难住了辩护律师。

items.def_en: (+ into/out of) To trick somebody, especially to gain money or a dishonest advantage
items.ex_en: The smooth-talking salesman conned naive tourists into purchasing cheap imitation jewelry at inflated prices.
items.ex_zh: 花言巧语的推销员诱骗天真的游客以高价购买廉价的仿冒珠宝。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to deceive or trick sb into believing sth false
items.ex_en: Many inexperienced retail investors were completely taken in by the fraudulent cryptocurrency prospectus.
items.ex_zh: 许多缺乏经验的散户投资者完全被那份欺诈性的加密货币招股说明书给蒙骗了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to mislead sb or encourage them to believe sth that is not true
items.ex_en: He deliberately led the prospective buyers on despite knowing the property had severe defects.
items.ex_zh: 尽管明知房产存在严重缺陷，他还是故意诱导买家，让他们抱有错误幻想。

items.def_en: (+ sb out of sth) to trick sb into giving you money or property
items.ex_en: The predatory telemarketer conned the elderly widow out of her hard-earned retirement savings.
items.ex_zh: 那名不怀好意的电话推销员骗走了这位年迈寡妇辛苦攒下的全部养老金。

items.def_en: To cause someone to believe something that is not true, especially by giving false or incomplete information.
items.ex_en: Misleading advertising claims can easily mislead vulnerable consumers into making poor dietary choices.
items.ex_zh: 虚假的广告宣传极易误导易受影响的消费者做出不健康的饮食抉择。

items.def_en: (+ into) To deliberately make someone believe something that is false, often to gain an advantage.
items.ex_en: The crooked accountant attempted to deceive auditors by creating falsified quarterly financial reports.
items.ex_zh: 心术不正的会计企图通过伪造季度财务报表来欺骗审计人员。

items.def_zh: 虚张声势，虚张声势地吓唬，蒙骗
items.def_en: To deceive or mislead someone by pretending to be stronger, more confident, or better prepared than you really are.
items.ex_en: He had no actual evidence but tried to bluff his way through questioning.
items.ex_zh: 他手头没有任何实际证据，却试图靠虚张声势来蒙混过关接受质询。

items.def_zh: 哄骗，戏弄，搞恶作剧欺骗
items.def_en: To trick or deceive someone into believing something false, especially as a practical joke or public fraud.
items.ex_en: The mischievous teenager managed to hoax the local radio station with a fabricated disaster.
items.ex_zh: 那个调皮的少年编造了一起虚构的灾难，成功戏弄了当地广播电台。

items.def_zh: 使误入歧途，不当地指引，错误地引导
items.def_en: To lead someone into making wrong judgments, unwise choices, or mistaken actions.
items.ex_en: Unqualified online advisors often misguide desperate job seekers into enrolling in worthless accreditation programs.
items.ex_zh: 不合格的网络顾问经常错误引导走投无路的求职者去报名毫无价值的认证课程。

items.def_en: (+ into) To deceive or trick someone, especially someone who is naive or unsuspecting
items.ex_en: The clever scammer managed to dupe the naive tourist into surrendering her passport.
items.ex_zh: 那个狡诈的骗子设法蒙骗了天真的游客，让她交出了护照。

items.def_en: (literary or dated) To fool, cheat, or deceive someone easily.
items.ex_en: The wily courtier easily gulled the naive young prince with hollow flatteries.
items.ex_zh: 诡计多端的廷臣用虚妄的奉承轻易愚弄了天真的年轻王子。

items.def_zh: 欺骗，迷惑，哄骗（使产生错觉）
items.def_en: To trick or mislead someone or oneself into believing something that is not true.
items.ex_en: We must not delude ourselves into thinking that this crisis has passed.
items.ex_zh: 我们绝不能自欺欺人地认为这场危机已经过去了。

items.def_zh: 欺骗，蒙混（尤用于 fob off：用假货或托辞打发）
items.def_en: (chiefly British informal) To deceive someone into accepting something inferior, or to get rid of someone with an excuse (usually in 'fob off').
items.ex_en: The dishonest shopkeeper tried to fob me off with a cheap plastic imitation.
items.ex_zh: 那个不老实的店主试图用廉价的塑料仿制品糊弄我。

items.def_en: (+ out of) To cheat someone out of money or property using deceit
items.ex_en: The crooked accountant swindled the elderly couple out of their life savings.
items.ex_zh: 那个黑心会计诈骗了这对老夫妇毕生的积蓄。

items.def_en: To give someone false or inaccurate information, causing them to be mistaken.
items.ex_en: The spokesperson misinformed the public regarding the actual severity of the chemical spill.
items.ex_zh: 发言人在化学品泄漏的实际严重程度上向公众提供了错误信息。

items.def_en: (+ into) (informal) To confuse, cheat, or deceive someone completely so they do not realize what is happening.
items.ex_en: The salesman bamboozled the elderly woman into signing an expensive maintenance contract.
items.ex_zh: 销售员把老妇人彻底搞糊涂了，哄骗她签下了一份昂贵的维保合同。

items.def_en: (+ into) To deceive or trick someone, especially by hiding your true intentions.
items.ex_en: Corrupt promoters hoodwinked investors into financing a completely nonexistent housing project.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的发起人蒙骗投资者，让他们为一个完全不存在的住房项目注资。

items.def_en: (+ into/out of) (literary or archaic) To trick, deceive, or swindle someone into doing or giving something.
items.ex_en: The sly rogue cozened the traveler out of his remaining gold coins.
items.ex_zh: 那个狡黠的恶棍诓骗走了旅人身上仅剩的金币。

groups.summary_en: Communicative verbs where a speaker or actor deliberately misinforms, tricks, or misguides an agent into false beliefs or poor decisions. Register spans informal swindling to literary craftiness.
groups.summary_zh: 蓄意隐瞒真相、欺诈或误导他人使其受骗上当。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the deliberate subversion of another's judgment through false pretense or misdirection, contrasting with truthful error by harboring deceptive intentionality.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过虚假表象或蓄意误导来扭曲他人判断，与无心之失相斥，以主观欺诈意图与操纵性为核心特征。
groups.nuance_en: deceive: formal comprehensive concealment or distortion of truth (public / partner / senses) · mislead: direct toward an erroneous conclusion through biased cues (investigators / public / voters) · trick: outwit someone via clever contrivance or illusion (buyer / opponent / mind) · con: swindle systematically by winning illicit confidence (victim / tourist / investor) · lead on: entice falsely with encouraging pretenses over time (suitor / investor / follower)
groups.nuance_zh: deceive: 庄重书面语，指系统性隐瞒或歪曲真相以蒙骗 (public / partner / senses) · mislead: 通过诱导性线索使对方误入歧途得出错误判断 (investigators / public / voters) · trick: 用狡黠的花招、诡计或幻术戏弄诱骗 (buyer / opponent / mind) · con: 利用骗取信任实施精心策划的欺诈洗劫 (victim / tourist / investor) · lead on: 虚情假意释放假信号引诱拖延对方 (suitor / investor / follower)

groups.name: Acquire to Forcibly Seize · 获取与夺取 (Get, Obtain, Wrest)
groups.tip: 从普通获取到强行夺取

items.def_zh: 获得，得到；取得，拿到；变成；到达
items.def_en: 1. To obtain, receive, or acquire something. 2. To become. 3. To arrive at a place.
items.ex_en: She managed to get a rare scholarship after months of intense preparation.
items.ex_zh: 经过数月的紧张准备，她成功获得了一笔难得的奖学金。

items.def_zh: 侵吞，私吞；将……收入囊中；装入衣袋
items.def_en: 1. To take or steal money or valuables dishonestly. 2. To win or earn an amount of money. 3. To put something into a pocket.
items.ex_en: The corrupt official pocketed millions in kickbacks from public infrastructure contracts.
items.ex_zh: 那个贪官从公共基础设施工程合同中私吞了数百万回扣。

items.def_zh: 继承（财产等）；经遗传获得
items.def_en: 1. To receive property, money, or a title from someone after they die. 2. To derive a characteristic from parents or predecessors.
items.ex_en: She will inherit a grand historic estate from her late grandfather next month.
items.ex_zh: 下个月她将从已故祖父那里继承一座宏伟的历史庄园。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to seize or gather sth suddenly and eagerly
items.ex_en: Shoppers rushed into the store to grab up all the discounted electronics.
items.ex_zh: 顾客们冲进店内，争先恐后地将所有打折电子产品抢购一空。

items.def_zh: 夺取，占领；拿取，获取；接受；乘坐
items.def_en: 1. To seize, capture, or gain possession of something by force or authority. 2. To reach out and grasp or obtain something. 3. To accept or receive.
items.ex_en: Elite military troops moved swiftly under cover of darkness to take the port.
items.ex_zh: 精锐部队借着夜色迅速行动，攻占了该港口。

items.def_en: 1. To obtain something useful, advantageous, or necessary, especially through effort. 2. To increase in amount or value.
items.ex_en: The determined athlete gained valuable experience during the grueling international tournament.
items.ex_zh: 这位意志坚定的运动员在那场艰苦的国际锦标赛中积累了宝贵的经验。

items.def_zh: （经过努力）争取到，获得；固定；使安全
items.def_en: 1. To obtain or achieve something, especially after a lot of effort. 2. To fasten or attach firmly. 3. To protect against danger.
items.ex_en: The diplomat worked tirelessly to secure a permanent peace agreement for the region.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官不知疲倦地工作，为该地区争取到了一项永久和平协议。

items.def_zh: （通过努力或购买）获得，赢得；存在，流行
items.def_en: 1. To get or acquire something, especially through effort, planning, or request. 2. (formal) To exist, be established, or apply as a custom or rule.
items.ex_en: Applicants must obtain written authorization from the ministry before commencing field research.
items.ex_zh: 申请人必须在开展实地研究前获得该部委的书面批准。

items.def_zh: 取得，获得；购得，收购；学到
items.def_en: 1. To gain possession of something, especially by buying or being given it. 2. To learn, develop, or master a skill or habit.
items.ex_en: The corporate conglomerate acquired a promising technology startup for forty million dollars.
items.ex_zh: 该大型企业集团斥资四千万美元收购了一家很有前景的科技初创公司。

items.def_zh: 重新获得，收复，夺回；重返
items.def_en: To obtain possession or control of something again after losing it; to reach a place again.
items.ex_en: The dedicated runner fought hard to regain her lead in the final lap.
items.ex_zh: 这位专注的跑者在最后一圈拼尽全力夺回了领先优势。

items.def_en: (formal) To obtain something, especially with care or special effort; to buy or acquire goods.
items.ex_en: The research team struggled to procure rare medical supplies during the severe embargo.
items.ex_zh: 在严酷的禁运期间，研究团队竭尽全力采购稀缺的医疗物资。

items.def_zh: 夺取，抢去；抓住，拿走（常与 onto 连用）；偷
items.def_en: (North American slang) ('glom onto') To seize, grab, or steal something; to latch onto.
items.ex_en: Opportunistic developers quickly glomed onto the prime waterfront property before prices spiked.
items.ex_zh: 投机开发商在价格暴涨前迅速抢占了这块黄金水滨地产。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to take sth violently, abruptly, or by surprise
items.ex_en: The thief snatched away the tourist's handbag and vanished into the crowded alley.
items.ex_zh: 小偷一把抢走游客的手提包，随即消失在拥挤的小巷中。

items.def_en: to take hold of suddenly and forcefully; confiscate by legal or physical force
items.ex_en: Federal agents moved swiftly to seize counterfeit goods valued at millions of dollars.
items.ex_zh: 联邦执法人员迅速采取行动，查封了价值数百万美元的假冒伪劣商品。

items.def_en: to grasp or seize hastily, eagerly, or violently
items.ex_en: He snatched the burning letter from the fireplace before it turned to ash.
items.ex_zh: 他在燃烧的信件化为灰烬前一把从壁炉中将其夺了出来。

items.def_zh: 抢夺，夺取；费力取得；猛扭
items.def_en: (+ from) To take power, control, or an object away from someone violently or with great effort.
items.ex_en: The courageous rebels fought bitterly to wrest independence from the oppressive empire.
items.ex_zh: 英勇的反抗军奋力拼杀，誓从压迫帝国手中夺取独立。

items.def_zh: 收回，强制收回（抵押品、未付款财产等）
items.def_en: When a lender or landlord repossesses property, they take it back legally because payments were not made.
items.ex_en: The commercial bank had to repossess the luxury car after months of default.
items.ex_zh: 在拖欠数月款项后，商业银行不得不依法收回了那辆豪华轿车。

items.def_en: (+ sth from sb) to take sth away from sb with a violent twist or heavy struggle
items.ex_en: She wrestled desperately to wrest the kitchen knife from the violent intruder's grip.
items.ex_zh: 她拼死扭打，硬从那名暴力入侵者的手中夺下了菜刀。

items.def_zh: 篡夺，强行霸占（权力/职位）
items.def_en: to take a position of power, right, or property illegally or by force
items.ex_en: The ambitious general conspired with conspirators to usurp the emperor's legitimate throne.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的将军与同谋密谋，企图篡夺皇帝的合法王位。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail obtaining possession of a physical or abstract asset, arranged along an intensity continuum from neutral receipt or standard acquisition to assertive securing, forceful wresting, and violent expropriation.
groups.summary_zh: 占有所有权或控制权，从常规获取递进至强行夺取与霸占。
groups.desc_en: Spans the spectrum of coming into possession of an asset, varying along an axis from passive entitlement and lawful procurement to aggressive appropriation and forceful seizure.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖获取某项资源或权益的过程，在谱系上从合法的程序性取得、被动继承，一直延伸至强行夺取与擅自占有。
groups.nuance_en: get: plain colloquial acquisition of an object (job / ticket / chance) · obtain: formal achievement of possession through diligent effort (permit / results / evidence) · secure: anchor firm control over a contested or scarce resource (funding / contract / border) · pocket: illicitly or quietly appropriate funds or winnings (bribe / profits / change) · grab up: eagerly and opportunistically snatch available assets (tickets / shares / bargain)
groups.nuance_zh: get: 最通俗口语化的获得或拿到 (job / ticket / chance) · obtain: 经过正式程序或付出努力而合法获取 (permit / results / evidence) · secure: 在竞争中锁定、保全稀缺资源或稳固成果 (funding / contract / border) · pocket: 悄悄私吞公款落袋为安或将收益收入囊中 (bribe / profits / change) · grab up: 见机行事、迫不及待地争抢一空 (tickets / shares / bargain)

groups.name: Curtail & Diminish · 缩减与削减 (Reduce, Decrease, Deplete)
groups.tip: 指标数量由多变少逐步下调

items.def_en: 1. To reduce in amount, price, degree, or value. 2. To move something down to a lower position.
items.ex_en: The central bank decided to lower interest rates to stimulate economic growth.
items.ex_zh: 中央银行决定降低利率以刺激经济增长。
items.ex2_en: Blood pressure may lower naturally following consistent daily aerobic physical exercise.
items.ex2_zh: 持续进行每日有氧体育锻炼后，血压可能会自然降低。

items.def_en: 1. To make something smaller or less in size, amount, degree, or price; to become smaller or less. 2. To force into a particular condition.
items.ex_en: The factory introduced automation to reduce operational costs and eliminate manufacturing waste.
items.ex_zh: 工厂引入了自动化以缩减运营成本并消除生产浪费。
items.ex2_en: The hot sauce will reduce into a thick glaze after simmering.
items.ex2_zh: 辣酱在慢炖后会收浓成浓稠的调味汁。

items.def_zh: 下降，减少，衰落；婉拒，谢绝
items.def_en: 1. To gradually become less, smaller, or weaker in number, amount, or quality. 2. (formal) To politely refuse an offer or invitation.
items.ex_en: Profits began to decline steadily after the government introduced stricter environmental regulations.
items.ex_zh: 在政府出台更严格的环保法规后，利润开始稳步下滑。

items.def_en: To become less or smaller in size, amount, degree, or number; to make something less.
items.ex_en: Public transit authorities agreed to decrease ticket prices during off-peak morning hours.
items.ex_zh: 公共交通部门同意在早晨非高峰时段下调车票价格。
items.ex2_en: Crime rates decrease steadily when community investment and education standards improve.
items.ex2_zh: 当社区投资和教育水平提高时，犯罪率会稳步下降。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce the number, size, or amount of sth
items.ex_en: The doctor advised him to cut down his consumption of processed sugars.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议他减少加工糖分的摄入量。
