items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce the size, scope, or extent of an operation or plan
items.ex_en: The aerospace company decided to scale down its lunar exploration project drastically.
items.ex_zh: 这家航空航天公司决定大幅缩减其月球探测项目的规模。

items.def_en: to gradually decrease in amount, rate, or intensity
items.ex_en: Rainfall should gradually taper off as the storm system moves farther east.
items.ex_zh: 随着风暴系统进一步向东移动，降雨应该会逐渐减少。

items.def_zh: 将……减到最低程度，降低；贬低，低估
items.def_en: 1. To reduce something to the lowest possible level, amount, or degree. 2. To make something seem less important than it really is.
items.ex_en: Careful strategic planning will minimize the financial risks associated with the merger.
items.ex_zh: 周密的战略规划将把与此次合并相关的财务风险降到最低。

items.def_zh: 大幅削减，腰斩（价格/开支）
items.def_en: to reduce drastically, violently, or sharply
items.ex_en: The struggling department store slashed retail prices to clear its unsold inventory.
items.ex_zh: 那家陷入困境的百货商店大幅削减零售价格以清仓滞销库存。

items.def_zh: 减弱，抑制；减小（振动），阻尼
items.def_en: To suppress or reduce the intensity of something active, such as unrest, speculation, or flames.
items.ex_en: Heavy police presence helped damp down rising civil unrest across the capital.
items.ex_zh: 大批警力的进驻有助于平息首都各地日益升温的骚乱。

items.def_zh: 逐渐减少，逐渐变小（常与 off 连用）；（使）逐渐变细
items.def_en: (+ off) To become gradually smaller in amount, degree, or intensity; to become narrower at one end.
items.ex_en: The trail begins to taper into a narrow rocky ridge near the summit.
items.ex_zh: 小径在靠近山顶处逐渐收窄为一条狭窄的岩石山脊。
items.ex2_en: The skilled barber will taper your hair neatly around the neck.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的理发师会把你的颈部头发修剪得齐整渐薄。

items.def_en: To become smaller, less, or weaker; to make something smaller, less, or less severe.
items.ex_en: The prescribed medicine helped lessen the severe pain caused by the fracture.
items.ex_zh: 开具的药物帮助缓解了骨折引起的剧烈疼痛。
items.ex2_en: Rainfall began to lessen gradually as the morning storm moved eastward.
items.ex2_zh: 随着清晨的风暴向东移动，降雨开始逐渐减少。

items.def_en: To reduce something, especially supplies, energy, or money, by a large amount.
items.ex_en: Decades of severe drought have depleted the region's primary underground water reserves.
items.ex_zh: 数十年的严重干旱消耗殆尽了该地区的主要地下水储备。

items.def_en: (+ from) To take away an amount or part from a total sum.
items.ex_en: The payroll department will deduct mandatory taxes directly from your monthly paycheck.
items.ex_zh: 财务部将从你的月薪中直接扣除法定税费。

items.def_zh: 削减，缩短（开支/权利/活动）
items.def_en: to cut short, diminish, or reduce in extent or duration
items.ex_en: The city council voted to curtail late-night entertainment hours across downtown venues.
items.ex_zh: 市议会投票决定缩短市中心各娱乐场所的深夜营业时间。

items.def_en: To reduce an amount by fifty percent, or divide something into two equal parts.
items.ex_en: New technological innovations can halve the total production time of electric vehicles.
items.ex_zh: 新技术创新可以将电动汽车的总生产时间缩减一半。
items.ex2_en: Operating costs halve rapidly when companies switch toward renewable energy solutions.
items.ex2_zh: 当公司转向可再生能源方案时，运营成本会迅速减半。

items.def_zh: （使）裁员；（使）缩小规模；换搬到较小的住宅
items.def_en: To reduce the number of employees or operations in an organization to cut costs; to move to a smaller home.
items.ex_en: Facing severe economic headwinds, the corporation was forced to downsize its workforce.
items.ex_zh: 面对严峻的经济逆境，该企业被迫缩减员工规模以求生存。
items.ex2_en: The firm downsized significantly during the harsh national economic recession period.
items.ex2_zh: 在全国经济严峻萧条时期，这家公司进行了大幅裁员缩减。

items.def_zh: （shrink的过去式及过去分词）变小，缩小；退缩
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of shrink: to become or make smaller; to move back from fear.
items.ex_en: Her favorite wool sweater shrunk considerably after being washed in hot water.
items.ex_zh: 她最喜欢的羊毛衫在用热水洗涤后严重缩水了。
items.ex2_en: The dry cleaning staff accidentally shrunk the expensive silk jacket during washing.
items.ex2_zh: 干洗店员工在洗涤过程中不小心洗缩了这件昂贵的丝绸夹克。

items.def_en: [I/T] to become less intense, or cause something to diminish in degree
items.ex_en: The fierce maritime storm showed no signs that it would soon abate.
items.ex_zh: 这场猛烈的海上风暴丝毫没有很快缓和下来的迹象。
items.ex2_en: The government took emergency measures to abate harmful industrial noise pollution.
items.ex2_zh: 政府采取紧急措施以减轻有害的工业噪音污染。

items.def_zh: 抑制，减弱，浇灭（热情、需求或势头）
items.def_en: To make feelings, enthusiasm, demand, or an effect less strong or intense.
items.ex_en: Rising borrowing costs have begun to dampen consumer demand across the housing market.
items.ex_zh: 不断上升的借贷成本已开始抑制整个房地产市场的消费需求。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express causing a quantity, magnitude, level, or extent to become smaller, or the process of decreasing autonomously. Nuances range from standard arithmetic/volume reduction to strategic downsizing, depletion of reserves, or gradual tapering off.
groups.summary_zh: 指数量、幅度、规模或储备的降低、压缩或耗竭削减。
groups.desc_en: Signifies reducing the quantity, magnitude, or intensity of a target, differing from complete elimination by keeping a reduced base or guiding it toward a lower ceiling.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动调减或自发回落数量、规模与强度，与彻底清零不同，是在保留底数的前提下压缩基数或逐步趋向低位。
groups.nuance_en: reduce: universal lowering of amount, size, or severity (costs / emissions / risk) · cut down: deliberately slash or prune volume by direct action (consumption / spending / trees) · scale down: proportionally downsize the scope of an operation (project / ambitions / operations) · taper off: gradually diminish to a narrow end or lull (production / rain / interest) · minimize: keep down to the absolute smallest feasible limit (damage / risk / disruption)
groups.nuance_zh: reduce: 最通用的压低指标、数量或烈度 (costs / emissions / risk) · cut down: 采取直接行动砍减用量或开支 (consumption / spending / trees) · scale down: 按比例全局收缩项目规模与预算 (project / ambitions / operations) · taper off: 呈锥形逐渐微弱、放缓直至止歇 (production / rain / interest) · minimize: 将负面影响或风险抑制在最低极限量 (damage / risk / disruption)

groups.name: Fasten & Secure · 固定与系紧 (Anchor, Moor, Tether)
groups.tip: 纽扣、拉链或绳缆等固定方式

items.def_en: 1. To attach a bell to an animal or object.
items.ex_en: The shepherd decided to bell the lead sheep to locate the flock.
items.ex_zh: 牧羊人决定给领头羊系上铃铛，以便找寻羊群。

items.def_zh: 扣上纽扣，系紧纽扣；用纽扣扣住
items.def_en: 1. (+ up) To fasten a garment with buttons.
items.ex_en: He quickly buttoned up his thick overcoat against the bitter winter wind.
items.ex_zh: 他迅速系紧厚大衣的纽扣，以抵御刺骨的寒风。
items.ex2_en: This stylish vintage jacket buttons up easily along the front seam.
items.ex2_zh: 这件时尚的复古夹克沿着前缝很容易扣上纽扣。

items.def_zh: 拉上拉链，用拉链扣紧；飞速移动，疾驰
items.def_en: 1. (+ up) To fasten a garment or bag with a zipper. 2. (informal) To move very quickly or briskly.
items.ex_en: Zip up your backpack tightly before running so your books do not spill.
items.ex_zh: 跑步前把背包拉链拉严，免得书本掉出来。
items.ex2_en: The tight leather boots zipped up smoothly without any painful friction.
items.ex2_zh: 这双紧身皮靴拉链拉得很顺畅，没有任何费劲的摩擦。

items.def_zh: 用胸针别住，用别针固定；佩戴胸针装饰
items.def_en: 1. (archaic) To fasten or adorn a garment with an ornamental brooch or pin.
items.ex_en: She brooched the rich velvet mantle at her shoulder with an emerald pin.
items.ex_zh: 她用一枚祖母绿别针将华丽的丝绒斗篷固定在肩头。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To fasten or secure hatches or objects firmly with battens or ropes
items.ex_en: Sailors worked furiously to batten down the cargo hatches before the hurricane struck.
items.ex_zh: 水手们在飓风来袭前拼命把货舱舱盖钉紧封牢。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To secure something tightly in place with ropes or chains
items.ex_en: Workers used heavy steel chains to lash down the machinery during transport.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在运输途中用沉重的钢链将机械设备紧紧捆绑固定。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To fasten or secure an object firmly to a structure using ropes or cords
items.ex_en: He didn't want to buy a house because he hated being tied down to one location.
items.ex_zh: 他不想买房，因为讨厌被束缚在同一个地方。

items.def_en: (+ to) To attach or fix something firmly so that it cannot move or fall
items.ex_en: Please secure the safety harness to the metal railing before beginning work.
items.ex_zh: 开始作业前，请将安全带牢固地系在金属栏杆上。

items.def_zh: 用钩子钩住，扣紧；钩住，捕获；吸引
items.def_en: 1. (+ up/onto) To fasten or secure something with a hook. 2. To catch or hold something with or as if with a hook.
items.ex_en: She took a moment to hook the heavy brass latch onto the doorframe.
items.ex_zh: 她花了一会儿工夫把沉重的黄铜锁扣钩在门框上。

items.def_zh: 用钉子钉牢，把……钉住；抓获，逮住；圆满完成
items.def_en: 1. (+ down/to) To attach or fasten something somewhere by means of nails. 2. (informal) To catch someone or succeed completely at something.
items.ex_en: The carpenter managed to nail down the loose wooden boards onto the patio.
items.ex_zh: 木匠设法用钉子将露台上松动的木板牢牢钉住。

items.def_zh: 用别针/大头针别住，钉住；按住，压住使不能动弹；把（希望、过错等）归咎于
items.def_en: 1. (+ to/onto) To fasten or attach something with a pin. 2. (+ down/against) To hold someone firmly so that they cannot move.
items.ex_en: Please pin this identification badge to your jacket lapel before entering the building.
items.ex_zh: 进入大楼前，请将这张身份胸牌别在你的西装翻领上。

items.def_zh: 抛锚，使固定；紧紧固定，使稳固；主持（电视或广播节目）
items.def_en: 1. To lower an anchor to hold a ship firmly in place, or to fix something firmly and stably to a support. 2. To host a television or radio programme.
items.ex_en: Crew members prepared to anchor the vessel securely in the sheltered coastal bay.
items.ex_zh: 船员们准备将船只稳稳地抛锚固定在避风的海湾中。
items.ex2_en: The fishing boat anchors safely inside the calm natural harbor bay.
items.ex2_zh: 这艘渔船在风平浪静的天然港湾内安全地下锚停泊。

items.def_zh: 用绳索捆绑，拴紧；用套索抓捕（牲口）
items.def_en: 1. (+ in/up/off) To tie, bind, or secure something firmly with ropes. 2. To catch an animal using a lasso.
items.ex_en: Police officers moved in to rope off the crime scene from curious bystanders.
items.ex_zh: 警官们上前用绳索将犯罪现场隔离起来，挡住好奇的围观群众。

items.def_zh: （用缆绳等）系泊，固定（船只）；泊船
items.def_en: 1. (+ to/at) To secure a boat or ship in place using ropes, cables, or an anchor.
items.ex_en: The captain decided to moor the yacht to the wooden pier overnight.
items.ex_zh: 船长决定将游艇系泊在木码头上过夜。
items.ex2_en: The luxury cruise ship moors alongside the bustling commercial harbor dock.
items.ex2_zh: 这艘豪华邮轮系泊在繁华的商业海港码头旁。

items.def_zh: 扎紧，扣紧，系紧；使固定，固定住；把（目光等）集中于
items.def_en: 1. (+ to/on/up) To close or attach something firmly with a button, zip, belt, or lock. 2. To fix firmly or become fixed in position.
items.ex_en: Passengers are respectfully requested to fasten their seatbelts before the aircraft takes off.
items.ex_zh: 飞机起飞前，请乘客系好安全带。
items.ex2_en: This durable safety harness fastens tightly with a solid metal buckle.
items.ex2_zh: 这条耐用的安全背带通过坚固的金属搭扣系得紧紧的。

items.def_en: (+ to) To tie an animal or object with a rope or chain to a fixed point to restrict movement
items.ex_en: The farmer used a sturdy leather cord to tether the goat to the post.
items.ex_zh: 农夫用一根结实的皮绳将山羊拴在木桩上。

items.def_zh: （登山中）用安全绳系牢，保护；（航海中）把缆绳拴在系索栓上
items.def_en: 1. (climbing / nautical) To secure a climbing rope or ship's line around a pin or device to hold someone or something safely.
items.ex_en: The experienced mountaineer prepared to belay his partner up the sheer ice wall.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的登山者准备用安全绳为同伴提供保护，助其攀上陡峭冰壁。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To fasten something firmly to the floor or a surface using bolts
items.ex_en: Technicians must bolt down the heavy industrial generator onto the concrete floor.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员必须用螺栓将沉重的大型工业发电机牢牢固定在混凝土地面上。

items.def_en: (+ to/together) To tie something firmly with a rope or cord
items.ex_en: They had to lash the timber logs together firmly to build the raft.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须用绳索把原木紧紧绑在一起，以便搭建木筏。

groups.summary_en: Physical manipulation verbs where an agent attaches, anchors, or immobilizes an object or vessel to a fixed structure using fasteners, lines, or mechanical hardware.
groups.summary_zh: 使用绳索、扣具或硬件将物体固定在某处防脱移。
groups.desc_en: Involves restraining an object in place against displacement or hazard, distinguished from loose holding by the structural rigidity, binding material, or tension applied.
groups.desc_zh: 指施加张力或闭锁结构将物体牢牢限定在原位以防晃动或位移，区别于松散支撑，侧重机械紧固或抗险防护。
groups.nuance_en: secure: make firmly steadfast and proof against dislodgment (door / load / perimeter) · batten down: brace and seal hatches or barriers against storm forces (hatches / equipment / shutters) · tie down: immobilize with ropes or constrictive obligations (cargo / rules / commitments) · lash down: bind tightly to a deck or frame using heavy cordage (freight / canvas / deck) · zip: close or fasten together via interlocking teeth (jacket / bag / fly)
groups.nuance_zh: secure: 确保物件或场地牢固稳固无被撬松松脱风险 (door / load / perimeter) · batten down: 用压条封牢舱口护栏以严阵以待狂风暴雨 (hatches / equipment / shutters) · tie down: 用绳索牢固捆绑以固定，或指受契约束缚 (cargo / rules / commitments) · lash down: 用粗绳缆紧紧绑系固定在甲板或支架上 (freight / canvas / deck) · zip: 通过拉链齿扣迅速拉合紧固 (jacket / bag / fly)

groups.name: Reprove to Fiercely Condemn · 谴责与痛斥 (Criticize, Censure, Excoriate)
groups.tip: 从口头挑错升级为严厉谴责

items.def_zh: 发啧啧声（表示不满、责备或遗憾）
items.def_en: (+ at) (chiefly British) To make a clicking sound with your tongue against your teeth to express disapproval or annoyance.
items.ex_en: The elderly woman tutted at the teenagers who were blocking the narrow aisle.
items.ex_zh: 那位老妇人对挡在狭窄过道上的青少年们发出了不满的啧啧声。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to scold or reprimand sb severely and formally
items.ex_en: On Fridays, staff are allowed to dress down.
items.ex_zh: 每周五，员工可以穿便服上班。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to speak angrily to sb because they have done sth wrong
items.ex_en: The teacher told him off for chatting during the exam.
items.ex_zh: 老师因为他在考试中聊天而严厉训斥了他。

items.def_en: To express disapproval of someone or something based on perceived faults; to analyze and evaluate a work.
items.ex_en: Many art reviewers criticized the latest exhibition for its lack of originality.
items.ex_zh: 许多艺术评论家批评最新的展览缺乏独创性。

items.def_en: to express sharp, stern disapproval directly to someone
items.ex_en: The director severely rebuked the manager for breaching company confidentiality protocols yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 主管昨天因经理违反公司保密规定而对其进行了严厉斥责。

items.def_en: to rebuke someone formally or officially for a wrongdoing
items.ex_en: The commanding officer reprimanded the young soldier for neglecting his basic duties.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官因那名年轻士兵疏忽基本职责而对其进行了正式申斥。

items.def_en: (informal) To criticize someone severely or say unkind, damaging things about them behind their back.
items.ex_en: He constantly badmouths his colleagues whenever the department manager leaves the room.
items.ex_zh: 只要部门经理离开房间，他就总是说同事的坏话。

items.def_en: (+ at sb/sth) to criticize sb/sth suddenly and very angrily
items.ex_en: Under intense pressure, the politician lashed out at reporters questioning his integrity.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大压力之下，这位政客愤然痛斥质疑他诚信的记者。

items.def_zh: 贬低，把……说得一文不值，猛烈抨击
items.def_en: (chiefly British & Australian informal) To criticize someone or something severely as worthless or completely wrong.
items.ex_en: Local film critics rubbished his ambitious new screenplay as utterly unwatchable nonsense.
items.ex_zh: 当地影评人痛批他雄心勃勃的新剧本，称其为不可卒读的废话。

items.def_zh: 公开谴责，强烈反对，抨击
items.def_en: (formal) To publicly state that you strongly oppose or disapprove of something.
items.ex_en: Human rights advocates decried the violent crackdown against peaceful student demonstrators yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 人权倡导者昨天公开谴责了针对和平学生示威者的暴力镇压。

items.def_en: (formal) To criticize or condemn someone officially and severely for bad behavior.
items.ex_en: The ethics committee voted overwhelmingly to censure the senator for financial misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 道德委员会以压倒性多数投票决定就财务不当行为对参议员予以正式谴责。

items.def_en: (+ for) To criticize or scold someone angrily and at length.
items.ex_en: She berated her assistant for misplacing the confidential legal documents during trial.
items.ex_zh: 她因助手在庭审期间放错机密法律文件而将其狠狠痛骂了一通。

items.def_zh: 严厉批评，痛斥；体罚，惩罚
items.def_en: (formal) To criticize someone severely for bad behavior; to punish someone physically.
items.ex_en: The headmaster chastised the unruly boys for their disrespectful behavior towards teachers.
items.ex_zh: 校长严厉批评了那些不服管教的男孩对老师无礼的行为。

items.def_en: (formal or archaic) To condemn, reject, or express strong disapproval of someone or something.
items.ex_en: The orthodox elders reprobated the radical doctrines preached by the visiting scholar.
items.ex_zh: 正统的长者们对那位访问学者传授的激进学说予以强烈谴责。

items.def_zh: 玷污，使蒙受耻辱，给……贴上耻辱的标签
items.def_en: (British English spelling of stigmatize) To treat or mark someone or something as socially unacceptable or shameful.
items.ex_en: Society often stigmatises individuals who struggle openly with severe chronic mental illnesses.
items.ex_zh: 社会往往给公开与严重慢性心理疾病作斗争的人贴上耻辱标签。

items.def_zh: 痛斥，公然谴责；告发，检举
items.def_en: (+ as/for) To criticize someone or something publicly and strongly; to accuse someone publicly of illegal or evil acts.
items.ex_en: The ambassador publicly denounced the sudden military invasion as an unlawful aggression.
items.ex_zh: 大使公开谴责这起突如其来的军事入侵是非法的侵略行为。

items.def_en: to criticize, reprimand, or punish someone severely
items.ex_en: The editorial castigated local authorities for failing to protect vulnerable urban citizens.
items.ex_zh: 这篇社论严厉谴责地方当局未能保护弱势城市市民。

items.def_zh: 严厉指责，痛斥；擦破，损伤（皮肤）
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To criticize someone or something severely and mercilessly. 2. (medical) To scratch or scrape off skin.
items.ex_en: The legal scholar excoriated the flawed judicial ruling in a scathing review.
items.ex_zh: 这位法学学者在一篇言辞尖锐的评论中痛斥了那项有缺陷的司法裁决。

items.def_en: (+ against) (formal) To speak, protest, or write angrily and fiercely against someone or something.
items.ex_en: The opposition leader fulminated against the unfair tax increases during his speech.
items.ex_zh: 反对党领袖在演讲中猛烈抨击了不公正的增税措施。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame signify evaluating someone or something negatively and expressing disapproval, ranging from quiet scoffing ('tut') and formal institutional reprimands ('censure') to blistering, vehement moral assaults and blistering public denunciations ('fulminate', 'excoriate').
groups.summary_zh: 表达不满与批判，从口头轻责递进至严厉谴责与公开痛斥。
groups.desc_en: Captures the expression of severe verbal censure or hostility toward wrongdoing, varying in intensity from mild disapproving vocalizations to scorched-earth rhetorical assaults.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖对过失或不端行为的言语问责与批判，烈度从轻微咂舌不悦，延伸至正式申斥乃至暴风雨般的失控痛斥。
groups.nuance_en: criticize: analytical generic fault-finding of flaws or conduct (decision / policy / performance) · reprimand: formal official disciplinary censure by a superior (officer / subordinate / pupil) · tell off: sharply scold an offender to their face in anger (colleague / child / driver) · dress down: severely and humiliatingly berate a subordinate (staff / troops / team) · lash out: erupt in sudden violent verbal or physical attack (critics / press / fury)
groups.nuance_zh: criticize: 最具普遍性的指出过错与分析性针砭 (decision / policy / performance) · reprimand: 上级对下属或机构依照规程给予的正式诫勉申斥 (officer / subordinate / pupil) · tell off: 当面怒气冲冲地严厉训斥数落 (colleague / child / driver) · dress down: 居高临下毫不留情地当众痛批贬损下属 (staff / troops / team) · lash out: 在受挫或激怒下突然爆发凶狠的言语反扑或击打 (critics / press / fury)

groups.name: Ring & Clatter · 鸣响与叮当声 (Tinkle, Clink, Toll)
groups.tip: 大钟沉重悠远敲响报时

items.def_zh: （钟表等）发滴答声；给……打勾，打钩标出；起作用，运转
items.def_en: 1. When a clock or watch ticks, it makes a regular, soft clicking sound every second. 2. (chiefly British) To put a checkmark (✓) beside an item.
items.ex_en: The antique clock ticked softly on the mantelpiece through the quiet evening.
items.ex_zh: 在寂静的傍晚，壁炉架上的古董钟轻轻地发出滴答声。

items.def_zh: （使）发出叮叮声，发出清脆的金属声
items.def_en: 1. To make a high, clear metallic ringing sound like a small bell or glass.
items.ex_en: The spoon tinged sharply against the fine porcelain cup during the ceremony.
items.ex_zh: 仪式期间，汤匙碰到精致的瓷杯，发出清脆的叮当响声。
items.ex2_en: The host tinged his crystal glass to catch everyone's attention.
items.ex2_zh: 主持人轻敲水晶杯以引起大家的注意。

items.def_zh: 叮咚作响；发出清脆的细响
items.def_en: [I/T] To make a light, clear, delicate ringing sound
items.ex_en: Wind chimes tinkled outside the bedroom window whenever a gentle breeze blew.
items.ex_zh: 每当微风吹拂，卧室窗外的风铃就会叮咚作响。
items.ex2_en: The street musician tinkled the triangle bell to introduce his performance.
items.ex2_zh: 街头乐手轻敲三角铁以拉开表演的序幕。

items.def_en: to produce a resonant musical ringing sound together or in sequence
items.ex_en: The distant bell towers chimed in to mark the arrival of midnight.
items.ex_zh: 远处的座座钟楼伴随鸣响，一同报响午夜的降临。

items.def_en: to make a continuous series of short, sharp, percussive noises
items.ex_en: The vintage tram rattled along the cobblestone tracks towards the historic square.
items.ex_zh: 那辆老式电车在通往历史广场的鹅卵石轨道上咔嗒咔嗒前行。

items.def_zh: （使）发砰/乒的尖锐脆响，发叮当声；（向……）发送简讯或提示音；（计算机）发送ping测试信号
items.def_en: 1. To make a short, sharp, high-pitched ringing sound. 2. (computing / informal) To send a quick message or network signal to check a connection.
items.ex_en: My smartphone pinged with a sudden notification in the middle of dinner.
items.ex_zh: 在晚餐正中，我的智能手机突然发出一声提示音。
items.ex2_en: A submerged submarine pinged the distant ocean floor with sonar pulses.
items.ex2_zh: 一艘水下潜艇用声纳脉冲探测遥远的海底。

items.def_zh: （使）发叮当声，发出金属撞击声；（口语）轻微撞凹；惩罚，扣除
items.def_en: 1. To make a clear metallic ringing sound like a small bell. 2. (informal) To dent something slightly, or to penalize or criticize someone.
items.ex_en: The brass counter bell dinged sharply as each customer entered the boutique.
items.ex_zh: 每当有顾客走进这家精品店，黄铜柜台铃就会清脆地叮当一响。
items.ex2_en: A stray flying pebble dinged the shiny door of my car.
items.ex2_zh: 一颗飞溅的小石子砸凹了我汽车锃亮的车门。

items.def_zh: （使）发出哔哔声，嘟嘟响；按（汽车喇叭）
items.def_en: 1. When a horn, alarm, or electronic device beeps, it makes a short, high-pitched sound.
items.ex_en: The kitchen microwave beeped three times to indicate that soup was ready.
items.ex_zh: 厨房里的微波炉哔哔响了三声，提示汤已经热好了。
items.ex2_en: Angry drivers constantly beep their loud horns during heavy rush-hour traffic.
items.ex2_zh: 愤怒的司机在高峰拥堵时不断按响他们嘈杂的喇叭。

items.def_zh: （钟等）鸣响，敲出和谐的乐声；（钟表）打钟报时；插话，附和 (chime in)
items.def_en: 1. When bells or a clock chime, they make a clear, musical ringing sound. 2. (of a clock) To indicate the hour by ringing musical strokes.
items.ex_en: The grandfather clock chimed eight deep notes across the silent living room.
items.ex_zh: 老式落地钟在静悄悄的客厅里敲响了八下深沉的钟声。
items.ex2_en: The tower bell chimes twelve heavy strokes at the stroke of midnight.
items.ex2_zh: 钟楼的钟在午夜时分敲响了十二声沉重的钟声。

items.def_zh: （使）发出叮当声；（诗歌等）押韵工整
items.def_en: 1. When keys, coins, or small bells jingle, or when you jingle them, they make a light, pleasant metallic ringing sound.
items.ex_en: He jingled his car keys nervously while waiting for the elevator doors.
items.ex_zh: 他在等电梯门打开时，紧张地把车钥匙摇得叮当响。
items.ex2_en: Small silver bells jingle brightly in the gentle morning mountain breeze.
items.ex2_zh: 小银铃在清晨温和的山风中清脆作响。

items.def_zh: （油煎等时）发出嘶嘶声；（情感、气氛等）极具吸引力，非常热烈
items.def_en: 1. When food sizzles in a hot pan, it makes a sharp hissing sound; (informal) to be extremely hot, exciting, or passionate.
items.ex_en: Thick cuts of seasoned bacon sizzled loudly in the hot cast-iron skillet.
items.ex_zh: 厚切腌培根在滚烫的铸铁煎锅里滋滋作响。

items.def_zh: 发出哔哔声；（在广播电视中用哔哔声）遮蔽敏感词
items.def_en: 1. To make a short, high-pitched electronic sound, or censor a swear word on television or radio with a tone.
items.ex_en: The broadcaster bleeped out the offensive profanities during the live radio interview.
items.ex_zh: 广播电台在现场直播采访中用哔哔声遮蔽了令人反感的粗话。
items.ex2_en: The kitchen timer bleeped insistently until she turned the heat off.
items.ex2_zh: 厨房定时器哔哔叫个不停，直到她关掉火。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ against/together) To make a short, light, sharp ringing sound like glassware or metal touching
items.ex_en: The celebratory guests clinked their champagne glasses together in a joyful toast.
items.ex_zh: 欢庆的宾客们把香槟杯轻碰在一起，愉快地举杯祝酒。
items.ex2_en: Crystal glasses clink gently together when guests make an affectionate toast.
items.ex2_zh: 当客人们亲切祝酒时，水晶杯轻轻碰撞发脆响。

items.def_en: to make a clear, resonant, and loud sound
items.ex_en: A single gunshot rang out through the foggy stillness of the night.
items.ex_zh: 一声清脆响亮的枪声划破了夜色中弥漫大雾的寂静。

items.def_zh: （缓迎慢送地）敲（钟），鸣（钟）；（钟）沉重缓慢地鸣响；征收（通行税等）
items.def_en: 1. When a large bell tolls, or someone tolls it, it rings slowly with deep, solemn strokes. 2. To collect a toll or fee from.
items.ex_en: The cathedral bell tolled slowly for the late monarch's solemn funeral procession.
items.ex_zh: 大教堂的钟声缓缓敲响，为已故君主庄严的葬礼队伍送行。
items.ex2_en: The church bellringer tolled the heavy bronze bell during the ceremony.
items.ex2_zh: 教堂司钟人在仪式期间敲响了沉重的青铜大钟。

items.def_zh: （使）发出咯咯声/咔嗒声；使慌乱，使紧张；喋喋不休地说
items.def_en: 1. To make a rapid series of short, sharp knocking sounds, or shake something so it makes this noise. 2. (informal) To make someone nervous, frightened, or upset.
items.ex_en: The loose windowpane rattled violently against the frame during the winter storm.
items.ex_zh: 在冬季暴风雨中，松动的窗玻璃对着窗框剧烈地咔嗒作响。
items.ex2_en: The playful toddler rattled his plastic toys excitedly against the floor.
items.ex2_zh: 顽皮的幼儿兴奋地把塑料玩具在地上敲得咔哒作响。

items.def_zh: （大钟等）发咚咚声，沉重地鸣响
items.def_en: 1. When a large heavy bell dongs, it makes a deep, resonant ringing sound.
items.ex_en: The giant bronze temple bell donged sonorously across the tranquil morning valley.
items.ex_zh: 寺庙那口巨大的青铜钟在宁静的清晨山谷中咚咚作响，余音袅袅。

items.def_zh: （大钟或锣等）咚咚地响，发出低沉悠长的撞击声
items.def_en: 1. When a large bell or gong bongs, it makes a deep, resonant booming sound.
items.ex_en: The heavy brass gong bonged loudly, announcing the start of the performance.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的铜锣咚地发出一声浑厚巨响，宣告演出正式开始。

items.def_en: [I/T] To ring loudly and resonantly, especially a set of church bells
items.ex_en: The church bells pealed joyfully across the town after the royal wedding.
items.ex_zh: 王室婚礼结束后，教堂的钟声在整个城镇上空欢快齐鸣。
items.ex2_en: The proud town band pealed trumpets loudly to celebrate the victory.
items.ex2_zh: 自豪的小镇乐队高声吹响小号以庆祝胜利。

groups.summary_en: Auditory perception verbs depicting the production of metallic, high-frequency, or percussive ringing and striking sounds, differing by resonance, sharpness, and duration.
groups.summary_zh: 发出清脆、金属撞击或深沉悠扬的敲击鸣响声。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the production of crisp metallic, resonant, or mechanical auditory signals, distinct from dull thuds or muffled sounds by their acoustic high frequency and sharp clarity.
groups.desc_zh: 指敲击或电子设备发出的清脆金石之声、共振声或机械蜂鸣，以高频通透与利落发声区别于沉闷钝响。
groups.nuance_en: tinkle: light delicate ringing of fine glass or bells (bell / glass / laughter) · ting: single clear high-pitched metallic ping (glass / fork / bell) · ding: resonant ringing chime of a service bell or impact (bell / fender / elevator) · ping: sharp electronic notification or high-velocity deflection (radar / bullet / message) · beep: short electronic monotone alert (horn / monitor / scanner)
groups.nuance_zh: tinkle: 纤巧玻璃或小铃铛相互碰撞发出的连续清脆丁冬声 (bell / glass / laughter) · ting: 单次极清澈的高频金属碰击声 (glass / fork / bell) · ding: 具有余韵的门铃、铜钟振鸣或轻微磕碰声 (bell / fender / elevator) · ping: 尖锐短促的电子声响、雷达声或子弹反弹跳飞声 (radar / bullet / message) · beep: 警告性质的单调电子提示短鸣或喇叭按鸣 (horn / monitor / scanner)

groups.name: Slide & Glide · 滑动与滑行 (Slide, Slip, Glide)
groups.tip: 表面平滑无阻前行

items.def_en: to move smoothly and effortlessly across a surface or through the air
items.ex_en: The sleek swan glided along the glassy surface of the tranquil lake.
items.ex_zh: 那只优雅的天鹅在平静如镜的湖面上顺畅滑行。

items.def_en: To glide smoothly across an icy or slick surface
items.ex_en: The graceful figure skaters skated over the polished ice with remarkable agility.
items.ex_zh: 优美的花样滑冰选手以惊人的敏捷身姿在光滑的冰面上一滑而过。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to move smoothly down a slippery or inclined surface
items.ex_en: Excited children loved to slide down the snowy bank behind the cabin.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的孩子们喜欢从小木屋后面的积雪斜坡上滑落下去。
items.ex2_en: Workers slide down the heavy steel pipes using sturdy safety ropes.
items.ex2_zh: 工人们用结实的安全绳将沉重的钢管滑放下去。

items.def_en: to slide smoothly or accidentally away from a surface or position
items.ex_en: The damp silk scarf slipped off her shoulders into the mud below.
items.ex_zh: 那条湿润的丝巾从她的肩头滑落，掉进了下方的泥潭里。

items.def_zh: （车辆等）滑行，惯性前行；轻易成功，得过且过
items.def_en: To move effortlessly without using power or pedaling; to succeed or make progress with little effort.
items.ex_en: He stopped pedaling and allowed his bicycle to coast down the hill.
items.ex_zh: 他停下踩踏，任由自行车顺着山坡顺势滑行下去。

items.def_en: (+ on/across) To slide accidentally for a short distance, often losing one's balance
items.ex_en: Careful pedestrians slipped frequently on the icy pavement outside the train station.
items.ex_zh: 火车站外结冰的人行道上，小心翼翼的行人们仍频繁滑倒。

items.def_zh: （使）滑行，（使）滑动；悄悄移动；滑落，下跌
items.def_en: To move smoothly along a surface, or to make something do this; to move quietly or drop gradually.
items.ex_en: She gently slid the wooden drawer shut before leaving the quiet study.
items.ex_zh: 离开安静的书房前，她轻轻地把木抽屉滑上推拢。
items.ex2_en: Pebbles slide easily down the wet mud bank after heavy rain.
items.ex2_zh: 暴雨过后，小石子很容易沿着湿润的泥坡滑下。

items.def_en: To glide smoothly over ice on ice skates, or over a hard surface on roller skates or a skateboard.
items.ex_en: Local teenagers often skate at the newly built concrete park after school.
items.ex_zh: 当地的青少年放学后经常在新建的水泥滑板公园溜冰滑板。

items.def_en: To move smoothly over snow or water on a pair of skis.
items.ex_en: They planned to ski down the challenging Alpine slopes every single afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 他们计划每天下午都去阿尔卑斯山那些极富挑战性的雪道滑雪。

items.def_zh: 滑行，滑翔；轻快平稳地移动
items.def_en: (+ across/through/down) To move smoothly, quietly, and effortlessly; to fly without engine power.
items.ex_en: The eagle spread its enormous wings to glide effortlessly through mountain thermals.
items.ex_zh: 那只雄鹰展开巨翅，借助山间热气流毫不费力地平稳滑翔。

items.def_zh: （slide的过去式及过去分词）（使）滑动，（使）滑行；滑落
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of slide: to move smoothly along a surface; to decline gradually.
items.ex_en: The heavy cargo slid across the polished metal deck during the squall.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨期间，沉重的货物在光滑的金属甲板上滑移开来。
items.ex2_en: The skilled bartender slid a cold glass of beer across counter.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的调酒师沿着吧台滑过去一杯冰镇啤酒。

items.def_zh: 乘雪橇滑行；用雪橇运送
items.def_en: (chiefly North American) To ride down snow on a sled, or transport loads using a sled.
items.ex_en: The neighborhood kids loved to sled down the steep hill all afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 附近的孩童们喜欢整个下午都在那个陡峭的山坡上坐雪橇滑雪。

items.def_zh: 乘雪橇滑行；用雪橇运送
items.def_en: (chiefly British) To slide or travel over snow on a sledge; to carry loads on a sledge.
items.ex_en: During winter holidays, tourists sledge down the designated snowy trails in groups.
items.ex_zh: 在寒假期间，游客们成群结队地乘雪橇沿着指定雪道滑下。

items.def_zh: （自行车等）滑行，不用脚踩骑行；随心所欲，不受拘束地行事
items.def_en: To travel downhill or forward on a bicycle without pedaling; to live or act freely without strict controls.
items.ex_en: The cyclist could freewheel for miles along the smooth mountain downhill road.
items.ex_zh: 骑手可以顺着平坦的山间下坡路不用脚踩连续滑行数英里。

items.def_en: To slide uncontrollably across a wet road surface on a thin film of water
items.ex_en: Worn car tires are much more likely to hydroplane on rain-soaked highways.
items.ex_zh: 磨损严重的汽车轮胎在暴雨倾盆的高速公路上更容易发生水上打滑。

items.def_en: (of a vehicle or wheel) To slide uncontrollably sideways on a wet, icy, or loose surface.
items.ex_en: The speeding delivery van skidded dangerously across the patch of black ice.
items.ex_zh: 超速行驶的货车在那片暗冰上极其危险地侧滑了过去。

items.def_en: To glide down snow-covered slopes while standing on a snowboard.
items.ex_en: Enthusiastic winter athletes snowboard down the powdery mountain trail with daring style.
items.ex_zh: 充满激情的冬季运动健儿以大胆的姿态在粉雪山道上单板滑行。

items.def_zh: （蛇般）蜿蜒滑行，滑动；不稳地滑动
items.def_en: (+ across/into/down) To slide smoothly along a surface with a twisting, sinuous motion; to slip or slide unsteadily.
items.ex_en: A green garden snake slithered quickly across the sunny stone patio pathway.
items.ex_zh: 一条翠绿的游蛇快速蜿蜒滑过洒满阳光的石头露台小径。

items.def_zh: 坐平底雪橇滑行；暴跌，骤降
items.def_en: To slide down a snow-covered hill on a toboggan; to fall or drop sharply.
items.ex_en: Families gathered to toboggan down the pristine snowy slopes of the resort.
items.ex_zh: 许多家庭聚集在度假村纯净的积雪斜坡上坐平底雪橇滑雪。

groups.summary_en: Manner-of-motion verbs where an entity moves smoothly, continuously, or involuntarily over a low-friction surface without taking steps. Distinctions relate to friction control, equipment used, and surface type.
groups.summary_zh: 沿光滑表面平稳、低阻力或失控地滑动前行。
groups.desc_en: Refers to continuous low-friction traversal across a smooth surface, contrasting with stepped walking or tumbling rolling by the unbroken tangential contact maintained.
groups.desc_zh: 指物体与光滑介质表面保持不脱离切线接触的低阻力滑行，与抬脚行进或翻滚截然不同，侧重摩擦极小化与连贯流动性。
groups.nuance_en: slide: continuous linear travel over a low-friction surface (ice / base / slide) · slip: sudden accidental loss of traction or discrete sliding away (grip / floor / away) · glide: graceful effortless drift carried by momentum or air currents (dancer / skater / bird) · coast: effortless movement powered only by leftover momentum without power (downhill / victory / finish) · skate over: skim swiftly across a surface or treat a sensitive issue superficially (ice / details / problem)
groups.nuance_zh: slide: 沿低摩擦表面顺滑平稳地直线滑动 (ice / base / slide) · slip: 突然失去抓地力导致的意外打滑，或悄悄滑脱溜走 (grip / floor / away) · glide: 借助气流或惯性优雅、无声且毫无费力感的滑行 (dancer / skater / bird) · coast: 切断动力仅凭惯性轻松前行，亦指毫不费力吃老本胜出 (downhill / victory / finish) · skate over: 在冰面高速掠过，引申为轻描淡写地回避敏感关键问题 (ice / details / problem)

groups.name: Surpass & Exceed · 超越与胜过 (Outdo, Eclipse, Surpass)
groups.tip: 在数量能力或地位上凌驾压制

items.def_en: (+ to sb/sth) to be as good as expected or reach a necessary level or competitor
items.ex_en: The candidate simply did not measure up to the board's high expectations.
items.ex_zh: 这位候选人根本没有达到董事会的高期望。

items.def_en: (+ of sb/sth) to overtake and establish a lead over competitors
items.ex_en: The marathon runner pulled ahead of her rivals in the final stretch.
items.ex_zh: 那位马拉松跑者在最后的冲刺路段赶超对手并确立了领先地位。

items.def_en: To surpass or do better than someone or something; to improve upon a previous standard or record.
items.ex_en: She worked diligently to better her rival's impressive world record this season.
items.ex_zh: 本赛季她勤勉训练，旨在打破并超越竞争对手那令人瞩目的世界纪录。

items.def_en: To win more points, goals, or marks than an opponent in a game or contest.
items.ex_en: The home team completely outscored their rivals during the dramatic final quarter.
items.ex_zh: 主队在激动人心的第四节比赛中得分完全压制了对手。

items.def_en: To be more successful or do something better than someone else
items.ex_en: The young chef tried to outdo his master with an inventive menu.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻厨师试图用富有创意的菜单来胜过他的师父。

items.def_zh: 在军衔、地位或级别上高于
items.def_en: To hold a higher official rank, position, or status than someone else.
items.ex_en: Senior naval captains easily outrank junior lieutenants on military naval vessels.
items.ex_zh: 在军舰上，高级海军上校的军衔显然高于初级初级中尉。

items.def_zh: 高于，高耸于……之上；超越，胜过
items.def_en: (literary) To rise higher than or tower above something else; to surpass.
items.ex_en: Magnificent ancient redwoods overtop every other tree in this secluded virgin forest.
items.ex_zh: 雄伟的古红杉高耸于这片幽僻原始森林中的所有其他树木之上。

items.def_zh: 做得比预期更好，超水平发挥，取得超出预期的成就
items.def_en: To perform better or achieve greater success than expected from past ability or standards.
items.ex_en: The underdog team managed to overachieve and reached the national tournament finals.
items.ex_zh: 那支不被看好的队伍超水平发挥，成功杀入了全国锦标赛决赛。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to be vastly superior to or far surpass others in quality or achievement
items.ex_en: His groundbreaking theoretical contributions tower above those of contemporary economic scholars.
items.ex_zh: 他在理论方面的开创性贡献远远超越了当代其他经济学学者。

items.def_zh: 超过，胜过，优于；位居……之首；给……加顶
items.def_en: To surpass or be superior to someone or something; to be at the top of a list or rank.
items.ex_en: Her latest novel managed to top all national bestseller lists this summer.
items.ex_zh: 她的最新小说在今年夏天成功位居全国所有畅销书榜单之首。

items.def_en: To be greater than a particular number, amount, or limit; to surpass expectations.
items.ex_en: Total quarterly production costs must never exceed the strictly approved operating budget.
items.ex_zh: 季度的总生产成本绝对不可超出严格核准的运营预算。

items.def_en: To be better or greater than someone or something; to exceed a record, expectation, or standard.
items.ex_en: The quarterly profits of the corporation easily surpassed all previous financial records.
items.ex_zh: 该公司的季度利润轻松超过了以往所有的财务纪录。

items.def_en: To be exceptionally good at doing something; to perform better than others.
items.ex_en: She always managed to excel at mathematics without showing much outward effort.
items.ex_zh: 她总是能够在数学方面表现优异，而且表面上毫不费力。

items.def_zh: 使显得矮小，使相形见绌
items.def_en: To make someone or something seem very small or insignificant by comparison.
items.ex_en: The modern skyscraper completely dwarfs the historic church standing right beside it.
items.ex_zh: 现代化的摩天大楼让伫立在它正旁边的那座历史悠久的教堂相形见绌。

items.def_zh: 超越，超出（通常界限、范围或经验）
items.def_en: (formal) To go beyond the usual limits, boundaries, or human understanding of something.
items.ex_en: Great works of art often transcend cultural differences and the passage of time.
items.ex_zh: 伟大的艺术作品往往能够超越文化差异和时间的流逝。

items.def_en: To be so prominent or remarkable as to diminish the apparent importance of another
items.ex_en: Her remarkable breakthrough threatened to overshadow the efforts of the rest of the team.
items.ex_zh: 她非凡的突破可能会让团队其他成员的努力显得黯然失色。

items.def_zh: 占优势，占主导地位；数量上占多数
items.def_en: (+ over/in) To be the largest in number, most noticeable, or most powerful element in a group or situation.
items.ex_en: Conservative economic views still predominate in the newly formed governing coalition.
items.ex_zh: 保守派的经济观点在刚成立的执政联盟中依然占据主导地位。

items.def_en: To grow, develop, or improve much faster and surpass another completely
items.ex_en: Consumer demand quickly outstripped the factory's limited capacity to supply new devices.
items.ex_zh: 消费者需求迅速超过了工厂供应新设备的有限产能。

items.def_zh: 使黯然失色，使相形见绌；遮蔽，掩盖；（天体）形成日食/月食于
items.def_en: 1. To make someone or something seem far less important, successful, or impressive by comparison. 2. (astronomy) To block the light from a celestial body.
items.ex_en: The young prodigy's brilliance threatened to eclipse the achievements of her mentor.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻神童的才华让其导师的成就相形见绌。

groups.summary_en: Gradable verbs indicating one entity being greater than another in quality, number, or achievement. Nuances scale from simply topping a threshold to utterly outclassing and overshadowing rivals.
groups.summary_zh: 在数量、程度、能力或声望上高出并超越对手。
groups.desc_en: Signifies rising above a competitor, benchmark, or expectation in stature, metric, or performance, differing from plain winning by introducing a vertical hierarchy of excellence.
groups.desc_zh: 指在体量、层级、指标或成就上凌驾于对手、旧有标杆或预期之上，与单纯胜出不同，强调等级阶差与卓异性超越。
groups.nuance_en: outdo: surpass someone in ingenuity, performance, or extravagance (rival / expectations / peers) · outrank: hold seniority or higher tier in an explicit institutional hierarchy (officer / competitor / peer) · pull ahead: break clear and widen lead in an ongoing race (poll / race / competition) · better: improve upon a previous standard or record (record / performance / time) · outscore: defeat an opponent specifically by compiling more numerical points (opponent / rival / team)
groups.nuance_zh: outdo: 在表现、能力或手笔上更胜一筹超过对手 (rival / expectations / peers) · outrank: 在建制化军衔、官阶或既定排名榜上地位更高 (officer / competitor / peer) · pull ahead: 在拉锯战或竞速中突然拉开身位建立领跑优势 (poll / race / competition) · better: 打破既有纪录，做出更优越的成绩 (record / performance / time) · outscore: 在赛事或评分机制中单凭积分多于对手而获胜 (opponent / rival / team)

groups.name: Think & Deduce · 沉思与推断 (Ponder, Deduce, Conclude)
groups.tip: 动用脑力进行逻辑推理

items.def_en: (dated) To have only a superficial knowledge of something, or to speak or think superficially about it.
items.ex_en: He loved to smatter of philosophy without comprehending any of its core tenets.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢浅薄地谈论哲学，却对其任何核心教条一无所知。

items.def_zh: 思考，考虑；认为，以为；料想
items.def_en: To use the mind to consider, reason, or solve problems; to hold an opinion or belief.
items.ex_en: I need a few quiet moments to think carefully about this complex problem.
items.ex_zh: 我需要安静片刻，好好思考一下这个复杂的问题。

items.def_zh: 仔细考虑，斟酌；认为，看作；顾及
items.def_en: To think carefully about something, especially before deciding; to regard in a specified way.
items.ex_en: The committee will carefully consider your proposal during the upcoming executive session.
items.ex_zh: 委员会将在即将召开的执行会议上仔细考虑你的提议。

items.def_zh: 想知道，纳闷，琢磨；感到惊奇，惊叹
items.def_en: To think about something with curiosity or doubt and try to understand it; to feel surprise and admiration.
items.ex_en: I often wonder how migratory birds navigate across such vast, unfamiliar oceans.
items.ex_zh: 我常常纳闷，候鸟究竟是如何飞越如此辽阔陌生的大洋的。

items.def_zh: 认为，料想，猜想；计算，估计
items.def_en: (+ that) (informal) To think, believe, or expect that something is true; to calculate or estimate.
items.ex_en: I reckon that we should probably leave now before the traffic gets terrible.
items.ex_zh: 我想我们大概现在就得动身，免得路上堵得一塌糊涂。

items.def_en: To understand or solve something through sustained thought or trial
items.ex_en: Scientists are trying to figure out why the virus mutated so rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们正试图弄明白这种病毒为何变异得如此之快。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to consider all the possible details and consequences of sth carefully
items.ex_en: They clearly hadn't thought the consequences through before acting.
items.ex_zh: 他们行动前显然没有把后果通盘考虑清楚。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to solve or deduce the answer to a problem by thinking
items.ex_en: The detective finally worked out the cipher hidden within the victim's journal.
items.ex_zh: 侦探终于破解了隐藏在受害者日记中的密码。

items.def_zh: 推论，推断；逻辑思考，讲理；劝说
items.def_en: To form conclusions or judgments through logical thought; to persuade someone using rational arguments.
items.ex_en: He tried to reason with the angry crowd, but nobody would listen.
items.ex_zh: 他试图跟愤怒的人群讲道理，但根本没人愿意听。

items.def_zh: 抽象地考虑，把……抽象出来；提炼，提取；作摘要
items.def_en: To consider something theoretically or separately from concrete realities; to extract or remove; to summarize.
items.ex_en: The philosopher attempted to abstract general moral rules from everyday human interactions.
items.ex_zh: 这位哲学家试图从日常的人际互动中提炼出普遍的道德法则。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on/over) To think about something carefully and deeply, especially before making a decision
items.ex_en: The judge sat silently to ponder over the conflicting testimony presented in court.
items.ex_zh: 法官静静地坐着，仔细掂量法庭上呈现的相互矛盾的证词。

items.def_zh: 忧思，沉思，焦虑地思索；孵（蛋）
items.def_en: 1. (+ over/about/on) To think deeply and unhappily about something for a long time. 2. (of a bird) To sit on eggs to hatch them.
items.ex_en: It is unhealthy to brood over past mistakes that you cannot change anyway.
items.ex_zh: 对自己无论如何也无法改变的过错耿耿于怀是于事无补的。

items.def_en: (+ from) To form an opinion or deduce a conclusion based on evidence and reasoning.
items.ex_en: Scientists can infer the climate of ancient eras from deep ice core samples.
items.ex_zh: 科学家可以根据深层冰芯样本推断出远古时代的气候状况。

items.def_zh: 建立理论，推测，提出假说
items.def_en: (+ about/that) To develop or propose a theory or explanation to account for something.
items.ex_en: Physicists continue to theorize that multiple hidden dimensions exist alongside our own universe.
items.ex_zh: 物理学家继续提出假说，认为我们的宇宙同时存在着多个隐藏维度。

items.def_zh: （依据已知事实）推断，推知；外推
items.def_en: (+ from) To estimate or predict unknown facts or values by extending known information and data.
items.ex_en: Analysts extrapolated future sales figures directly from the strong third-quarter revenue data.
items.ex_zh: 分析师直接根据强劲的第三季度营收数据推断出未来的销售额。

items.def_zh: 重新解释，作出新理解，重新诠释
items.def_en: To understand or explain a text, concept, or event in a new or different way.
items.ex_en: Historians recently began to reinterpret the diplomatic documents in a radically different light.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家最近开始从一个截然不同的角度重新解读这些外交文件。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to find an answer or solution by logical thought and deduction
items.ex_en: She sat quietly until she could reason out the logical flaw in his argument.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐着，直到推理出他论点中的逻辑漏洞。

items.def_en: (+ that) To form an opinion or decide something after considering all available evidence
items.ex_en: The jury concluded that the defendant was not guilty beyond any reasonable doubt.
items.ex_zh: 陪审团断定被告在无可置疑的合理范围内罪名不成立。

items.def_zh: 演绎推导出；根据已知推断出
items.def_en: (+ from) To reach an inescapable conclusion using logical reasoning based on known facts
items.ex_en: Sherlock Holmes was able to deduce the traveler's profession from his muddy boots.
items.ex_zh: 夏洛克·福尔摩斯能够从旅客沾满泥巴的靴子推断出其职业。

groups.summary_en: Cognitive verbs where an agent applies deliberate mental effort to process facts, weigh possibilities, and draw inferences. Nuances range from casual pondering and deep brooding to formal logical deduction.
groups.summary_zh: 运用心智思考、考量并依据线索推导出结论。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses internal cognitive processing to synthesize information, hypothesize, or resolve confusion, distinguished from passive perception by active mental labor.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖通过内在认知加工来梳理信息、建立假设或解构疑难的过程，区别于被动感官吸收，强调脑力的主动沉潜运作。
groups.nuance_en: think: fundamental broad cognitive pondering and deliberation (future / deeply / twice) · consider: weigh various factors carefully before deciding (options / proposal / consequences) · reckon: intuitive or dialectal estimation and calculated hunch (chance / cost / value) · figure out: decipher an intricate puzzle or solve a mystery through reasoning (solution / problem / motive) · think through: systematically examine all consequences and branches of a plan (plan / implications / scenario)
groups.nuance_zh: think: 最普适的基础思维活动、主观斟酌与考量 (future / deeply / twice) · consider: 在做决定前周全权衡利弊与情境 (options / proposal / consequences) · reckon: 带有直觉感、地方色彩的心中估算或算计 (chance / cost / value) · figure out: 经过逻辑推导逐步解开谜团或摸透门道 (solution / problem / motive) · think through: 从头到尾系统性预演推敲方案的每一处细微后果 (plan / implications / scenario)

groups.name: Annoy & Provoke · 激怒与惹恼 (Irritate, Exasperate, Enrage)
groups.tip: 从小事烦扰逐步升级到怒火中烧

items.def_en: (informal) to deliberately annoy, tease, or provoke someone, especially with repeated remarks.
items.ex_en: Stop trying to needle your brother about his terrible performance in yesterday's game.
items.ex_zh: 别再拿你弟弟在昨天比赛中的糟糕表现去故意刺激他了。

items.def_en: to annoy, irritate, or provoke someone slightly.
items.ex_en: Her dismissive tone clearly nettled him, though he attempted to remain courteous.
items.ex_zh: 她那轻蔑的语气显然惹恼了他，尽管他极力保持礼貌。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To annoy or exasperate someone
items.ex_en: His constant interruptions during the briefing really began to tick off the manager.
items.ex_zh: 他在简报过程中不断的打断真的开始惹恼经理了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To deliberately say or do things to tease, irritate, or anger someone
items.ex_en: He only said those harsh words to wind you up, so ignore him.
items.ex_zh: 他说了那些难听的话只是故意想惹你生气，别理他就是。

items.def_zh: 烦扰，惹恼；在……安装窃听器
items.def_en: 1. (informal) to annoy or irritate someone persistently. 2. to place a hidden listening device in a room or phone.
items.ex_en: That persistent flickering light overhead is starting to bug me immensely.
items.ex_zh: 头顶那盏老是不停闪烁的灯真快把我给烦死了。

items.def_zh: 惹恼，折磨，戏弄；用辛辣调料烹制
items.def_en: 1. to cause annoyance in or harass someone with petty irritations. 2. to coat or cook food with hot, pungent seasonings.
items.ex_en: Cruel schoolyard bullies loved to devil the quiet new boy with constant pranks.
items.ex_zh: 校园里恶毒的恶霸们喜欢用接连不断的恶作剧来戏弄那个安静的新生。

items.def_zh: 使烦躁，激怒；刺激（身体部位，引起疼痛或发炎）
items.def_en: 1. to annoy someone or make them impatient. 2. to make a part of the body sore, red, or inflamed.
items.ex_en: The harsh synthetic fabric began to irritate his sensitive skin within minutes.
items.ex_zh: 这种粗糙的合成纤维面料在几分钟内就刺激得他敏感的皮肤发红。

items.def_en: To annoy somebody intensely, often worsening an already strained situation
items.ex_en: His dismissive remarks did nothing but aggravate an already tense boardroom confrontation.
items.ex_zh: 他不屑一顾的言辞只会进一步激化董事会本就紧张的对峙局面。

items.def_zh: 使恼怒，激怒；磨伤，擦破（皮肤）
items.def_en: 1. to make someone feel very annoyed, bitter, or resentful. 2. to make skin raw or sore by rubbing.
items.ex_en: It galled him deeply to see his incompetent rival receive the coveted promotion.
items.ex_zh: 看到那个无能的对手获得梦寐以求的晋升，这让他感到极其恼火与不甘。

items.def_zh: 使耿耿于怀，使怨恨，令人生怨；化脓
items.def_en: to cause continued anger, annoyance, or resentment over a long period.
items.ex_en: The unfair criticism continued to rankle in his mind for many months afterward.
items.ex_zh: 那番不公的批评在随后的许多个月里依然让他久久难以释怀。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To annoy, infuriate, or make someone very angry
items.ex_en: His arrogant behavior at the meeting really pissed off the entire department.
items.ex_zh: 他在会议上的傲慢举动彻底惹毛了整个部门。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To stir someone up to intense irritation, agitation, or anger
items.ex_en: The provocative political speech was clearly designed to rile up the crowd.
items.ex_zh: 那篇煽动性的政治演说显然旨在激起人群的愤怒。

items.def_en: 1. to deliberately annoy or anger someone so that they react aggressively. 2. to cause a particular reaction, feeling, or situation.
items.ex_en: Do not provoke that sleeping dog unless you are fully prepared to run.
items.ex_zh: 别去招惹那只睡着的狗，除非你做好了随时逃跑的准备。

items.def_en: To annoy and irritate somebody intensely, especially through persistent friction
items.ex_en: The airline's endless delays and bureaucratic excuses completely exasperated the weary travelers.
items.ex_zh: 航空公司无休止的延误和官僚式的借口彻底惹恼了疲惫不堪的旅客。

items.def_zh: 激怒，使极度愤慨；触犯，违犯
items.def_en: to make someone extremely angry and shocked, especially through an unjust, cruel, or offensive action.
items.ex_en: The dictator's blatant human rights abuses outraged the international community.
items.ex_zh: 该独裁者公然践踏人权的行径激怒了国际社会。

items.def_en: To make someone extremely angry or furious
items.ex_en: The referee's controversial penalty call enraged the thousands of passionate fans present.
items.ex_zh: 裁判极具争议的罚球判决激怒了在场的数千名热血球迷。

items.def_zh: 激怒，使大怒；焚香，用香熏
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) to make someone extremely angry and indignant. 2. to perfume or burn with incense.
items.ex_en: The arrogant diplomat's remarks incensed the foreign ministers attending the peace summit.
items.ex_zh: 那位傲慢的外交官的言论激怒了出席和平峰会的外长们。

items.def_en: to make someone extremely angry.
items.ex_en: It infuriates me whenever someone cuts in front of me in line.
items.ex_zh: 只要有人在我前面插队，我就气得火冒三丈。

groups.summary_en: Emotion-induction verbs describing acts that stimulate negative affective responses, scaling from minor prickling irritation to unbearable provocation and blind fury.
groups.summary_zh: 引发不快情绪，从轻度烦躁惹恼递进至怒不可遏。
groups.desc_en: Describes inducing emotional exasperation or anger in another, contrasting with physical injury by targeting psychological equilibrium via repetitive or deliberate friction.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过重复性摩擦或蓄意冒犯去侵扰他人的心理平衡，与肉体创伤相斥，侧重激发烦躁、激愤等情绪应激。
groups.nuance_en: irritate: cause chafing impatient frustration through nagging annoyance (skin / audience / senses) · aggravate: exacerbate an already inflamed, fragile, or tense condition (injury / problem / tension) · needle: deliberately prick someone with sarcastic teasing or persistent jabs (opponent / colleague / rival) · nettle: provoke sharp fleeting stinging resentment or pique (pride / critic / conscience) · bug: persistently bother or pester like an unavoidable insect (parents / conscience / teacher)
groups.nuance_zh: irritate: 像受擦伤般令人心烦意乱、失去耐性 (skin / audience / senses) · aggravate: 使业已恶化、脆弱的局势或伤情进一步雪上加霜 (injury / problem / tension) · needle: 用冷嘲热讽或微小挑衅持续扎人痛处 (opponent / colleague / rival) · nettle: 刺痛对方自尊心使其顿生微愠或反感 (pride / critic / conscience) · bug: 如飞虫绕头般在耳边烦扰纠缠让人不胜其烦 (parents / conscience / teacher)

groups.name: Decorate & Adorn · 装饰与美化 (Embellish, Bedeck, Garnish)
groups.tip: 添置饰物装点以增加美观

items.def_zh: 为……增色，使优美，装饰；使荣耀，赏光
items.def_en: 1. to make something more attractive or pleasing; adorn. 2. to bring honor or dignity to someone or something by being present.
items.ex_en: Magnificent oil paintings from the Renaissance grace the walls of the grand gallery.
items.ex_zh: 宏伟画廊的墙壁上装饰着文艺复兴时期的壮丽油画。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To make someone or something look neater, cleaner, or more attractive
items.ex_en: We decided to spruce up the guest bedroom before our visiting relatives arrived.
items.ex_zh: 我们决定在亲戚来访之前，把客房好好收拾美化一番。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To decorate or dress someone or something in a very elaborate or festive way
items.ex_en: The organizers decked out the grand ballroom with silver ribbons for the gala.
items.ex_zh: 组织者用银色缎带把宴会大厅装点一新，以迎接晚会。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To furnish, equip, or decorate something elaborately or attractively
items.ex_en: He spent thousands of dollars to trick out his vintage motorcycle with chrome.
items.ex_zh: 他花了几千美元给自己的复古摩托车镀上铬件，精心改装了一番。

items.def_zh: 收拾美化；整理得焕然一新
items.def_en: (+ sth) To improve the appearance of something by cleaning or decorating it
items.ex_en: A fresh coat of paint will quickly smarten up this dull kitchen.
items.ex_zh: 刷上一层新油漆会很快让这间昏暗的厨房显得焕然一新。
items.ex2_en: The scruffy puppy will smarten up noticeably after a thorough bath and grooming.
items.ex2_zh: 彻底洗澡和修剪毛发后，这只脏兮兮的小狗会明显变精神。

items.def_zh: 装饰，装点；粉刷，装修；授予勋章
items.def_en: 1. to make something more attractive by adding ornament, paint, or details. 2. to paint or paper the interior of a room or building. 3. to award a medal or decoration to someone.
items.ex_en: The children helped decorate the living room with colorful paper lanterns and flowers.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们帮忙用五颜六色的纸灯笼和鲜花装点客厅。

items.def_zh: 用羽毛装饰；长羽毛；（划船等中）转桨（以减少阻力）
items.def_en: 1. to cover, line, or decorate something with feathers. 2. to turn an oar blade or propeller edgewise to reduce air or water resistance.
items.ex_en: The artisan used soft down to feather the interior of the winter coat.
items.ex_zh: 工匠用柔软的羽绒衬裹冬衣内部以作装饰和保温。

items.def_en: to decorate or embellish something to make it look more attractive.
items.ex_en: Delicate carvings of mythical creatures ornament the massive wooden pillars of the temple.
items.ex_zh: 神庙粗大的木柱上雕刻着神话生物的精美图案作为点缀。

items.def_en: to decorate or embellish someone or something with attractive objects or features.
items.ex_en: Garlands of fresh jasmine flowers adorned the bride's long, dark braided hair.
items.ex_zh: 新鲜的茉莉花环装点着新娘乌黑修长的发辫。

items.def_en: (+ with) To make something more beautiful by adding decorative features or details
items.ex_en: The calligrapher embellished the borders of the ancient parchment with intricate golden vines.
items.ex_zh: 书法家在古羊皮纸的边缘用错综复杂的金色藤蔓加以装点润色。

items.def_en: (+ with) To add a decorative embellishment, especially a small piece of food to a dish
items.ex_en: The chef garnished the roasted lamb chop with a sprig of fresh rosemary.
items.ex_zh: 大厨用一枝新鲜的迷迭香装点了烤羊排。

items.def_zh: 以杂色斑纹装饰，给……饰以菱形花纹
items.def_en: to decorate or variegate with a pattern of bright, contrasting diamond shapes or patches.
items.ex_en: Autumn leaves fell to harlequin the paved garden pathway with brilliant, contrasting hues.
items.ex_zh: 秋叶飘落，为花园的石板小径铺上了斑驳绚丽、色彩鲜明的杂色斑纹。

items.def_zh: 用闪烁的小饰物装饰，点缀；（使）闪烁
items.def_en: (often passive) to decorate or cover something with small sparkling objects, lights, or spots.
items.ex_en: Millions of brilliant stars spangled the midnight sky over the vast, quiet desert.
items.ex_zh: 数以百万计的璀璨繁星点缀着广袤寂静的沙漠上空的午夜苍穹。

items.def_zh: 镶嵌，嵌饰（inlay的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (past and past participle of inlay) to decorate a surface by embedding pieces of wood, metal, or stone into it.
items.ex_en: Master craftsmen inlaid the antique tabletop with precious ivory and mother-of-pearl patterns.
items.ex_zh: 能工巧匠在古董桌面上镶嵌了珍贵的象牙和珍珠母贝图案。

items.def_zh: 用纹章（或图案、文字）装饰；醒目地展示；赞美
items.def_en: 1. to decorate something with a coat of arms, crest, or vivid pattern. 2. to display a design, name, or symbol conspicuously.
items.ex_en: The royal guard carried shields emblazoned with a golden roaring lion emblem.
items.ex_zh: 皇家卫队携带着绘有金色咆哮雄狮纹章的盾牌。

items.def_zh: 使显现斑驳光影，使缀满斑点（或斑纹）
items.def_en: (often passive) to mark or decorate a surface with spots of light, shadow, or color.
items.ex_en: Afternoon sunlight filtered through the leaves to dapple the quiet forest floor.
items.ex_zh: 午后的阳光穿透树叶，在静谧的林地上投下斑驳的光影。

items.def_zh: 以彩带（或花环等）装点，张灯结彩
items.def_en: (often passive) to decorate a place with hanging chains or garlands of ribbons, flowers, or lights.
items.ex_en: The villagers festooned the town square with bright banners for the annual carnival.
items.ex_zh: 村民们用鲜艳的彩旗装点市镇广场，迎接一年一度的狂欢节。

items.def_en: (+ with/in) To decorate or clothe somebody/something in a showy, lavish way
items.ex_en: She arrived at the royal ceremony bedecked in sparkling diamonds and emeralds.
items.ex_zh: 她全身缀满闪烁的钻石和祖母绿，盛装出席了皇家典礼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs of surface enhancement and decorative design, where an agent adds artistic ornaments, colors, or materials to improve visual appeal. Nuances differ by formality and aesthetic style.
groups.summary_zh: 通过增设饰品、花纹或点缀物使事物更加美观华贵。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on bestowing aesthetic enhancement upon an object, person, or space, contrasting with functional assembly by subordinating utility to visual embellishment or celebratory display.
groups.desc_zh: 指对物体、人或空间施加美学增色，与单纯的功能性装配不同，它将实用性退居次席，侧重视觉修饰与典雅陈设。
groups.nuance_en: decorate: universal furnishing or adorning with color, ornaments, or paint (room / cake / hall) · ornament: embellish an existing structure with intricate artistic additions (building / manuscript / surface) · spruce up: briskly tidy, freshen, and groom for an improved appearance (house / image / self) · deck out: lavishly or flamboyantly dress up in full festive array (hall / costume / ship) · grace: confer prestige, elegance, or dignity simply by present beauty (presence / table / cover)
groups.nuance_zh: decorate: 最通用的通过上漆、挂饰进行空间或物体的美化布置 (room / cake / hall) · ornament: 在既有构造上雕琢附加精巧典雅的装饰物 (building / manuscript / surface) · spruce up: 快速打扫收拾、修饰仪容以焕然一新 (house / image / self) · deck out: 盛装打扮或披红挂彩般华丽铺张地盛大装点 (hall / costume / ship) · grace: 纯粹凭借自身雅致的风度、美态使环境或版面增光添彩 (presence / table / cover)

groups.name: Apportion & Distribute · 划分、分配与拨给
groups.tip: 把物资分发配给各方

items.def_en: to distribute something to people, often in large amounts or in a casual manner
items.ex_en: The unsolicited advisor loved to dish out unwanted advice to everyone around him.
items.ex_zh: 那个不请自来的顾问总喜欢随意向身边的每个人大肆兜售建议。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To share or divide something up among several people
items.ex_en: The partners met privately to divvy up the massive profits from their venture.
items.ex_zh: 合伙人们私下会面，以瓜分他们合资企业带来的巨额利润。

items.def_en: to give out something in small amounts, often reluctantly or charity-style
items.ex_en: The frugal manager chose to dole out office supplies only upon strict request.
items.ex_zh: 节俭的经理选择仅在严格申请下才少量配发办公用品。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To distribute things by hand to each member of a group
items.ex_en: The teacher asked two volunteers to hand out the exam papers quickly.
items.ex_zh: 老师请了两位志愿者迅速把试卷分发下去。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To divide something into parts or portions and distribute them
items.ex_en: The committee decided to parcel out the remaining grant money among local charities.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定将剩余的拨款分派给当地的几家慈善机构。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To divide something into specified amounts or shares and distribute them
items.ex_en: The chef carefully portioned out the stew so that every guest received equal amounts.
items.ex_zh: 主厨仔细地将炖菜按份分配，确保每位客人都分到等量。

items.def_zh: 分摊，分配；分享，共享；共有
items.def_en: 1. To divide something into parts and distribute them among several people. 2. To have, use, or experience something together with others.
items.ex_en: The roommates agreed to share the monthly utility bills equally between themselves.
items.ex_zh: 室友们同意彼此平均分摊每月的公用事业费用。

items.def_en: To put someone on a fixed allowance, or supply goods in limited, regular rations.
items.ex_en: During the prolonged siege, the commander had to allowance each soldier to one biscuit daily.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的围城期间，指挥官不得不严格定量配给，每名士兵每天仅发一块饼干。

items.def_zh: 分发，分配（parcel out）；打包，裹好（parcel up）
items.def_en: 1. (parcel out) To divide land, money, or work into shares and distribute them. 2. (parcel up) To wrap something into a package.
items.ex_en: The council will parcel the newly acquired estate into affordable residential development plots.
items.ex_zh: 市议会将把新购置的地产分割为经济适用住宅用地进行分配。

items.def_zh: 给予；分发（处罚、正义或份额）
items.def_en: to dispense or apportion justice, punishment, or harsh treatment
items.ex_en: The ancient gods would ruthlessly mete out harsh punishment to deceitful mortals.
items.ex_zh: 古诸神会对欺诈的凡人施以毫不留情的严酷惩罚。

items.def_en: To divide into lots or parcels, especially of land or goods for distribution or sale.
items.ex_en: The surveyor was hired to lot the farmland into five separate commercial parcels.
items.ex_zh: 这位测绘员受雇将那片农田划分成五个独立的商业地块。

items.def_zh: 分发，分配；分销；散布，分布
items.def_en: To give or share something out to a number of people, or supply goods over an area.
items.ex_en: Volunteers gathered at dawn to distribute warm meals to displaced families across town.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者清晨聚集起来，向全镇流离失所的家庭分发热饭。

items.def_en: To officially assign or distribute resources, money, or tasks for a specific purpose or person.
items.ex_en: The board voted to allocate substantial funding to modern renewable energy projects.
items.ex_zh: 董事会投票决定拨出大笔资金用于现代可再生能源项目。

items.def_en: (+ to) to give a particular amount of time, money, space, etc. to someone or something as a share
items.ex_en: The manager will allot ten minutes to each team member for their presentation.
items.ex_zh: 经理将给每位团队成员分配十分钟的陈述时间。

items.def_en: To share or distribute wealth, land, goods, or responsibilities again in a different or fairer way.
items.ex_en: The new administration promised to redistribute national tax revenues to rural hospitals.
items.ex_zh: 新一届政府承诺将国家税收重新分配给乡村医院。

items.def_en: To divide and share out money, resources, or responsibilities fairly among people or groups.
items.ex_en: The partners agreed to apportion all unexpected financial losses according to their investments.
items.ex_zh: 合伙人们同意按照各自的出资比例合理分摊所有意外的经济损失。

items.def_en: To distribute money, resources, or duties again in a different way or to different people.
items.ex_en: The ministry decided to reallocate emergency relief supplies to the hardest-hit district.
items.ex_zh: 该部决定将紧急救灾物资重新调配到受灾最严重的地区。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to dividing up a finite quantity of goods, funds, or responsibilities and dispensing parts to different recipients or destinations. Distinctions center on whether the division is formal and budgeted (allocate, apportion), shared mutually (share), or parcelled out in discrete physical shares (parcel, lot).
groups.summary_zh: 将资金、份额、土地或责任依特定原则或份额分派与拨付给各方。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves dividing a finite whole into shares and dispensing them among recipients, contrasting with simple 'giving' by emphasizing allocation, entitlement, or rationing.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及将有限的整体分割为若干份额并分发给受众，与单纯的“给予”不同，它侧重份额划分、配给机制或定额分配。
groups.nuance_en: dish out: lavish or indiscriminate dispersal (punishment / advice / criticism) · divvy up: casual split among partners (profits / spoils / chores) · dole out: measured, stingy dispersal of scarce reserves (rations / cash / relief) · hand out: routine gratuitous distribution (flyers / leaflets / samples) · parcel out: deliberate fragmentation into discrete tracts or quotas (land / resources / territories)
groups.nuance_zh: dish out: 随性大方或不加节制地分派 (punishment / advice / criticism) · divvy up: 伙伴间随意分账或瓜分 (profits / spoils / chores) · dole out: 吝啬或微量配给紧缺物资 (rations / cash / relief) · hand out: 常规无偿分发 (flyers / leaflets / samples) · parcel out: 刻意切块或划分额度 (land / resources / territories)

groups.name: Cut, Snip & Sever · 切割、修剪与劈削
groups.tip: 借助刀锯切割分段或修边

items.def_en: (+ sth) To remove something with a quick, short cut using scissors or shears
items.ex_en: The gardener used shears to snip off the dead leaves from the rosebushes.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用大剪刀剪掉了玫瑰丛上的枯叶。

items.def_zh: 割伤；划出缺口，刻痕于；偷窃
items.def_en: 1. To make a small, shallow cut in something or someone. 2. (informal) To steal something.
items.ex_en: He accidentally nicked his chin with an old razor while shaving in a hurry.
items.ex_zh: 他匆忙刮胡子时不小心用旧剃须刀划破了下巴。

items.def_zh: 修剪，剪下；夹住，扣牢；轻撞
items.def_en: 1. To cut short or trim something with shears or scissors. 2. To fasten something with a clip or clamp.
items.ex_en: She carefully clipped the stray branches from the hedge along the garden walkway.
items.ex_zh: 她仔细修剪掉了花园小径旁树篱上杂乱横生的枝条。

items.def_zh: 剪短，修剪；裁剪（照片）；收获，种植
items.def_en: 1. To cut or trim something very short. 2. To cut off the edges of a picture or photograph.
items.ex_en: He went to the barber to crop his overgrown hair short for the military.
items.ex_zh: 他去理发店把过长的头发剪得很短，以备入伍。

items.def_en: to cut away irregular or unwanted parts to make something neat and tidy
items.ex_en: You need to trim the jagged edges of the paper before framing the drawing.
items.ex_zh: 在给画装框之前，你需要修剪掉纸张参差不齐的毛边。

items.def_zh: 用剪刀剪；（使双腿等）像剪刀般开合移动
items.def_en: 1. To cut something with scissors. 2. To move, or move your legs, in a sharp crossing motion like scissor blades.
items.ex_en: The tailor carefully scissored along the chalk mark on the dark wool cloth.
items.ex_zh: 裁缝用剪刀沿着深色呢料上的粉笔标记仔细裁剪。

items.def_en: To cut something quickly with small, short strokes using scissors.
items.ex_en: The nurse took small scissors and snipped the loose threads off the bandage.
items.ex_zh: 护士拿小剪刀剪断了绷带上松脱的线头。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To remove or sever a piece of something using a sharp instrument
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_zh: 切，割，剪，砍；削减，降低；中断
items.def_en: 1. To divide, trim, or make an opening in something using a sharp instrument. 2. To reduce the amount, size, or number of something.
items.ex_en: The chef used a sharp knife to cut the ripe watermelon into equal wedges.
items.ex_zh: 厨师用锋利的刀将成熟的西瓜切成大小相等的块。

items.def_zh: 锯，锯开；拉锯般来回移动
items.def_en: To cut something using a saw, or make a back-and-forth cutting movement.
items.ex_en: The carpenter carefully sawed through the thick oak plank to make a tabletop.
items.ex_zh: 木匠仔细锯开厚厚的橡木板以制作桌面。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cut something into pieces with repeated downward strokes of an axe, heavy knife, etc.
items.ex_en: He spent the cold morning chopping firewood behind the cabin with an axe.
items.ex_zh: 他花了一上午的寒冷时间在小木屋后用斧头劈柴。

items.def_en: to cut the wool off a sheep, or cut hair or foliage using large scissors or shears
items.ex_en: Farmers will shear the thick wool off the sheep before summer arrives.
items.ex_zh: 农夫们会在入夏之前剪去羊身上厚厚的羊毛。

items.def_zh: 用长柄大镰刀割；扫除，迅猛穿过
items.def_en: To cut grass, grain, or weeds with a scythe, or sweep through something rapidly and powerfully.
items.ex_en: The reaper scythed through the golden wheat under the blazing midday sun.
items.ex_zh: 割麦人在正午烈日下挥动大镰刀迅猛割过金色的麦田。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To sever or detach something with a forceful blow using a blade or axe
items.ex_en: The butcher used a heavy cleaver to chop off the pig's feet cleanly.
items.ex_zh: 屠夫用一把沉重的剁肉刀利落地砍下了猪蹄。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To sever something roughly and violently with repeated clumsy chops
items.ex_en: He angrily hacked off the thick branches with a rusty machete in the woods.
items.ex_zh: 他在树林里用生锈的开山刀胡乱砍下了那些粗树枝。

items.def_zh: 劈，砍；非法侵入（计算机系统）；应付，搞定
items.def_en: 1. To cut or chop something roughly or violently with heavy blows. 2. To gain unauthorized access to a computer system.
items.ex_en: They had to hack a path through the dense, tangled jungle brush.
items.ex_zh: 他们不得不在茂密杂乱的丛林灌木中劈出一条小道。

items.def_en: to cut completely through something, dividing it cleanly into separate parts
items.ex_en: The sharp blade managed to sever the thick marine rope with one stroke.
items.ex_zh: 锋利的刀刃一刀彻底切断了粗大的船用缆绳。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe dividing, incising, or removing portions of a physical entity using a sharp-edged tool. Nuances depend heavily on tool type and kinetic force: light quick snips with scissors (snip, scissor, clip), agricultural swinging strokes (scythe, sickle), toothed abrasions (saw), or rough, forceful chops (hack).
groups.summary_zh: 使用利器或刀刃实施切开、剪短、劈削或锯断等动作。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema entails detaching or shaping physical material with sharp blades or shearing force, contrasting with rough 'breaking' by requiring directional incision or tidy edge-reduction.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及通过利刃或剪切力使物理材料分离或成形，与粗暴的“折断”不同，它强调沿边缘的定向切除、修剪或缩减截断。
groups.nuance_en: snip: light quick shear with small scissors (thread / coupon / herbs) · nick: incidental shallow notch or cut (skin / rim / edge) · crop: severe truncation of excess height or perimeter (image / hair / plant) · trim: neat cosmetic reduction of margins (beard / hedge / budget) · cut off: complete severance of distal part or flow (limb / connection / supply)
groups.nuance_zh: snip: 用小剪刀轻快剪断 (thread / coupon / herbs) · nick: 意外划出微小浅口 (skin / rim / edge) · crop: 大幅截除顶部或多余外缘 (image / hair / plant) · trim: 精细修齐边缘以求美观 (beard / hedge / budget) · cut off: 彻底截断末端或阻隔供给 (limb / connection / supply)

groups.name: Damage to Annihilate · 破坏、毁损与彻底湮灭
groups.tip: 毁坏并使之彻底瓦解消亡

items.def_zh: 毁灭，摧毁；撤销，使归于乌有（unmake的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: (past and past participle of unmake) To undo, destroy, or reverse something that has been made or established.
items.ex_en: Decades of political strife completely unmade the once-flourishing kingdom into ruin.
items.ex_zh: 数十年的政治纷争彻底摧毁了这个昔日繁荣的王国，使其化为乌有。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To violently and severely damage or destroy something by hitting it
items.ex_en: Vandals broke into the shop and smashed up all the glass display cabinets.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子闯入商店，把所有的玻璃陈列柜砸得粉碎。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To deliberately demolish or take apart a building or structure
items.ex_en: The old factory was torn down to make way for a modern shopping mall.
items.ex_zh: 那座旧工厂被拆除，以便改建现代化的购物中心。

items.def_en: (slang) To murder or kill someone intentionally.
items.ex_en: The mob boss hired a ruthless hitman to off his former business partner.
items.ex_zh: 黑帮头目雇佣了一名冷酷的杀手去干掉他以前的商业伙伴。

items.def_en: To damage something so severely that it no longer exists or cannot be repaired; to ruin or put an end to something.
items.ex_en: The massive earthquake threatened to destroy entire neighborhoods across the capital city.
items.ex_zh: 这场大地震有彻底毁灭首都整个街区的危险。

items.def_zh: 破坏，毁掉；使（船只、车辆等）失事
items.def_en: To severely damage or destroy something; to cause a ship or vehicle to be wrecked in an accident.
items.ex_en: The drunk driver managed to wreck both luxury cars in the midnight crash.
items.ex_zh: 那个醉驾司机在午夜的车祸中彻底毁掉了两辆豪车。

items.def_zh: 毁坏（建筑物等）的内部；取出……的内脏
items.def_en: 1. To destroy the inside or contents of a building, especially by fire. 2. To remove the internal organs of a person, animal, or fish.
items.ex_en: The intense fire rapidly gutted the entire interior of the historic Victorian mansion.
items.ex_zh: 大火迅速将那座具有历史意义的维多利亚式豪宅内部焚烧殆尽。

items.def_en: to cause extensive damage or utter destruction across a wide area
items.ex_en: The Category 5 hurricane threatened to devastate coastal towns throughout the entire region.
items.ex_zh: 这场五级飓风极可能严重摧毁整个地区的沿海城镇。

items.def_en: to completely pull down or knock down a building or large structure
items.ex_en: Construction crews used heavy wrecking balls to demolish the abandoned apartment block.
items.ex_zh: 施工队使用重型铁球彻底拆除了那座废弃的公寓楼。

items.def_en: To destroy or be destroyed deliberately, especially a rocket or missile for safety reasons.
items.ex_en: Engineers had to destruct the malfunctioning experimental rocket safely over the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 工程师不得不让出现故障的实验火箭在开阔洋面上空安全自毁。
items.ex2_en: The malfunctioning space missile had to destruct high in the upper atmosphere.
items.ex2_zh: 故障的太空导弹不得不在高空自毁。

items.def_zh: 采伐……的森林，砍光……的树木
items.def_en: To clear an area of trees or forests.
items.ex_en: Logging companies threaten to deforest thousands of acres of ancient woodland every year.
items.ex_zh: 伐木公司每年都可能砍光数千英亩古老林地的树木。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To destroy something or be destroyed completely by an explosion
items.ex_en: Terrorists conspired to blow up the historic suspension bridge during peak rush hour.
items.ex_zh: 恐怖分子密谋在早晚高峰期间炸毁这座历史悠久的悬索桥。
items.ex2_en: The abandoned fireworks warehouse blew up suddenly, shaking windows miles away.
items.ex2_zh: 废弃的烟花仓库突然爆炸，震碎了数英里外的窗户。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To destroy, eliminate, or eradicate completely
items.ex_en: The harsh winter blizzard threatened to wipe out the small isolated mountain village.
items.ex_zh: 严酷的冬日暴风雪几乎要彻底抹除那个与世隔绝的高山村落。

items.def_en: To spoil or destroy something completely; to cause someone to lose all their money, power, or status.
items.ex_en: Heavy sudden downpours threatened to ruin the farmer's unharvested fields of barley.
items.ex_zh: 突降的暴雨有彻底毁掉农夫尚未收割的大麦田的危险。

items.def_en: to remove all signs of something, totally destroying its existence
items.ex_en: The fierce coastal storm threatened to obliterate every trace of the small settlement.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的沿海风暴几乎要将这个小定居点的一切痕迹抹除殆尽。

items.def_en: to destroy something or someone completely so that nothing remains
items.ex_en: The overwhelming military offensive was designed to completely annihilate enemy fortifications overnight.
items.ex_zh: 压倒性的军事进攻旨在连夜将敌方防御工事彻底歼灭殆尽。

items.def_zh: 切开……的肚子取出内脏，开膛；彻底破坏……的内部
items.def_en: To cut open a body and remove its internal organs; (figurative) to remove the essential contents of something.
items.ex_en: The brutal conqueror ordered his men to disembowel the captured palace guards.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的征服者命令部下将俘获的宫廷卫兵开膛破肚。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scale frame denote causing structural impairment, catastrophic ruin, or total elimination of an entity. They progress in severity from spoiling or breaking functionality (unmade, ruin), to severe physical wrecking (gut, wreck, disembowel), up to absolute total annihilation (destroy, destruct, off).
groups.summary_zh: 从使之失效、局部毁坏，递增至开膛破坏与彻底摧毁消灭。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves structural dismantling or violent eradication that reduces an entity to ruin, contrasting with mere 'damaging' by carrying catastrophic finality.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及以破坏性力量拆解或彻底毁灭实体结构，与轻微的“损伤”不同，它带有不可逆的灾难性与终结性。
groups.nuance_en: tear down: deliberate physical demolition of edifices (building / wall / monument) · smash up: violent chaotic mechanical battering (car / furniture / storefront) · gut: complete internal hollow-out by fire or reform (building / reform / ship) · devastate: overwhelming sweeping ruin of vast scope (region / economy / lives) · destroy: total functional or physical nullification (evidence / bridge / city)
groups.nuance_zh: tear down: 蓄意拆毁既有建筑物 (building / wall / monument) · smash up: 暴力猛烈地砸碎捣毁 (car / furniture / storefront) · gut: 内部全被焚毁或掏空 (building / reform / ship) · devastate: 大范围毁灭性破坏或重创 (region / economy / lives) · destroy: 物理或功能上的彻底湮灭 (evidence / bridge / city)

groups.name: Insert & Embed · 插入与嵌入 (Incorporate, Imbed, Lodge)
groups.tip: 将物体塞入、穿插或嵌入缝隙

items.def_en: (+ sth) To insert or place something quickly and easily into a small space or opening
items.ex_en: I'll pop in for a quick cup of coffee on my way home.
items.ex_zh: 我在回家路上顺便进去喝杯咖啡。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To slide or fit neatly into a narrow opening, groove, or space
items.ex_en: He managed to slot in the memory card securely into the tiny digital camera.
items.ex_zh: 他成功将存储卡妥帖地插入了数码相机的窄槽中。
items.ex2_en: The puzzle piece slotted in smoothly without needing any force at all.
items.ex2_zh: 这块拼图严丝合缝地滑了进去，完全不需要用力。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To push or fold the edges of something neatly into an opening or under something
items.ex_en: She carefully tucked in the corners of the white sheets under the mattress.
items.ex_zh: 她仔细地将白色床单的边角整齐地折进了床垫底下。

items.def_en: (+ into) To put or position something neatly and securely into a specific place
items.ex_en: The technician tried to fit the new graphics card into the tight computer case.
items.ex_zh: 技术员试图把新的显卡装入狭小的电脑机箱内。
items.ex2_en: The small spare tire fits easily into the shallow trunk compartment.
items.ex2_zh: 这个小型备胎能轻松装进较浅的后备箱隔层里。

items.def_zh: 把……塞进，塞入；卷起，收拢；缝褶裥
items.def_en: 1. (+ into/under/away) To push loose edges neatly into a space, or insert something snugly to keep it tidy or secure.
items.ex_en: She decided to tuck the folded letter into the secret pocket of her coat.
items.ex_zh: 她决定把折叠好的信件塞进外套的暗袋里。

items.def_zh: 在……中插入（页、层或数据块）；交错排列
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To insert blank or different pages, layers, or data blocks alternately between existing ones.
items.ex_en: The printer will interleave the manuscript pages with blank sheets of protective parchment.
items.ex_zh: 打印人员会在手稿各页之间交错插入空白的羊皮保护纸。

items.def_zh: （在历法中）插入闰日/闰月；插入，嵌入（地层等）
items.def_en: 1. (calendar / geology) To insert an extra day or month into a calendar, or insert a layer between existing rock strata.
items.ex_en: Astronomers had to intercalate an extra month to reconcile lunar cycles with seasons.
items.ex_zh: 天文学家必须插入一个闰月，以使阴历周期与四季相吻合。

items.def_en: (+ in) To set or place an object firmly into a ground or substance
items.ex_en: The climber managed to plant the iron spike deeply into the solid rock face.
items.ex_zh: 登山者成功将铁岩钉牢牢打入了坚固的岩壁之中。

items.def_zh: 夹入，把……夹在两物之间；挤在狭小空间或时间中
items.def_en: 1. (+ between) To fit or squeeze someone or something tightly between two other things or people.
items.ex_en: I was sandwiched between two tall passengers on the crowded downtown morning bus.
items.ex_zh: 在早晨拥挤的市区公交车上，我被夹在两名身材高大的乘客中间。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ in) To become firmly fixed, embedded, or stuck in a narrow or solid space
items.ex_en: A sharp piece of shrapnel managed to lodge in the soldier's left shoulder.
items.ex_zh: 一片尖锐的弹片卡入了那名士兵的左肩深处。
items.ex2_en: The archer managed to lodge a deadly arrow deep into the target trunk.
items.ex2_zh: 弓箭手成功将一支致命的箭深深射入了靶木中。

items.def_en: 1. (+ into/between) To put or introduce something into something else.
items.ex_en: Please insert your plastic keycard into the electronic lock to open the door.
items.ex_zh: 请将塑料钥匙卡插入电子锁以打开房门。

items.def_zh: 嵌入，插入；深深刻入，使铭记
items.def_en: 1. (+ in) To fix an object, idea, or code firmly and deeply into a surrounding mass or system.
items.ex_en: Engineers plan to embed tiny microchips in the concrete pillars for structural monitoring.
items.ex_zh: 工程师计划将微型芯片嵌入混凝土立柱中，以便监测结构状况。

items.def_zh: （给……）注射；注入，灌注（资金、想法等）；引入
items.def_en: 1. (+ into/with) To put a drug or liquid into a body using a needle and syringe. 2. To introduce or add a new quality, idea, or money into something.
items.ex_en: The doctor had to inject the emergency antidote directly into the patient's bloodstream.
items.ex_zh: 医生不得不将急救解毒剂直接注射进患者的血液中。

items.def_zh: 置于……之间，插入；介入，干预；插嘴
items.def_en: 1. (+ between) (formal) To place something between two things or people. 2. To interrupt a conversation with a remark, or intervene in a dispute.
items.ex_en: The bodyguard tried to interpose his own body between the diplomat and the gunman.
items.ex_zh: 保镖试图将自己的身体挡在外交官和持枪者之间。

items.def_zh: 嵌入，插入；深深刻入（同 embed）
items.def_en: 1. (+ in) (variant spelling of embed) To fix an object, idea, or code firmly and deeply into a surrounding mass or system.
items.ex_en: The craftsman decided to imbed delicate pearl ornaments in the polished wooden chest.
items.ex_zh: 工匠决定将精致的珍珠饰物牢牢镶嵌在光滑的木箱上。

items.def_zh: 给……插管，将导管插入（气管或体内）
items.def_en: 1. (medicine) To insert a breathing or feeding tube into a patient's windpipe or stomach.
items.ex_en: The emergency physician had to intubate the unconscious patient to secure his airway.
items.ex_zh: 急诊科医生不得不为昏迷的病人插管以确保其呼吸道畅通。

items.def_en: 1. to insert something, especially an affix into the middle of a word. 2. to implant or fix firmly in the mind.
items.ex_en: The wise teacher sought to infix strong moral values deeply into her students' minds.
items.ex_zh: 这位睿智的老师试图将崇高的道德观念深植于学生们的心中。

groups.summary_en: Spatial manipulation verbs where an agent introduces, slides, or firmly nests an object into an opening, tight container, or surrounding solid matrix.
groups.summary_zh: 将物品置入间隙、夹层或紧紧嵌进外部实体之中。
