groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves positioning an object snugly inside a pre-existing enclosure or receptive matrix, contrasting with general 'putting' by emphasizing dimensional fit and secure envelopment.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及将物体紧密安置于已有凹槽、缝隙或母体结构中，与宽泛的“放置”不同，它强调契合度、嵌入性与包覆感。
groups.nuance_en: pop in: casual swift insertion into a space (disc / battery / mouth) · slot in: exact alignment into a dedicated groove (aperture / schedule / token) · tuck: neat folding or stashing into a tight fold (corner / blanket / shirt) · plant: deliberate subterranean or surreptitious fixing (bug / bomb / seed) · interleave: alternating insertion between sheet layers (pages / memory / sheets)
groups.nuance_zh: pop in: 轻松随手滑入或塞入 (disc / battery / mouth) · slot in: 精准滑入卡槽或严丝合缝插入 (aperture / schedule / token) · tuck: 塞入褶皱或边角以保齐整 (corner / blanket / shirt) · plant: 牢固植入地下或隐秘安放 (bug / bomb / seed) · interleave: 隔页穿插或交错插入 (pages / memory / sheets)

groups.name: Join, Fasten & Interlock · 物理连接与嵌合
groups.tip: 采用铰接或联轴结为复合体

items.def_en: (+ sth) To connect or fasten mechanical or electrical components together
items.ex_en: Can you help me hook up the sound system to my laptop?
items.ex_zh: 你能帮我把音响系统连接到笔记本电脑上吗？

items.def_en: (+ sth) To join various parts or fragments together to create a single complete entity
items.ex_en: The forensic detectives tried to piece together the shattered porcelain vase from tiny shards.
items.ex_zh: 法医侦探们试图用细小的碎片拼合那只破碎的瓷花瓶。

items.def_en: (+ to/together) to connect two or more things physically or mechanically
items.ex_en: The new suspension bridge will link the small peninsula to the mainland highway.
items.ex_zh: 这座新悬索桥将把这个小半岛与大陆公路物理连接起来。

items.def_en: To join, link, or combine two things, vehicles, or concepts together.
items.ex_en: The railway workers will couple the freight cars to the heavy diesel engine.
items.ex_zh: 铁路工人们将把货运车厢连接到重型柴油机车头上。
items.ex2_en: The train cars couple smoothly whenever they meet at the central junction.
items.ex2_zh: 列车车厢在中央交叉口交会时总能顺畅地挂接在一起。

items.def_en: To connect two words or parts of a word with a hyphen.
items.ex_en: The copy editor had to hyphenate the compound adjective before the main noun.
items.ex_zh: 文字编辑必须在主要名词前的复合形容词中使用连字符连接。

items.def_en: To fit or interlock closely together so as to form a rigid whole
items.ex_en: The wooden floorboards lock together tightly to create a completely seamless, durable surface.
items.ex_zh: 这些木质地板紧密咬合在一起，形成了完全无缝且耐磨的表面。
items.ex2_en: The worker quickly locked the metal scaffold pieces together for safety.
items.ex2_zh: 为了安全起见，工人迅速将金属脚手架部件紧锁在一起。

items.def_zh: 连接，接合；联合，结合；加入，参加
items.def_en: 1. To connect, fasten, or link two or more things together. 2. To become a member of a group or participate in an activity.
items.ex_en: A wide concrete bridge was constructed to join the island to the mainland.
items.ex_zh: 修建了一座宽阔的混凝土大桥，将岛屿与大陆连接起来。
items.ex2_en: The two mountain rivers join together before emptying into the vast ocean.
items.ex2_zh: 这两条山涧在注入浩瀚的大海之前汇合在一起。

items.def_zh: 连接，联结；接通（电话、网络）；使产生联系
items.def_en: To join or link two or more things together; to establish a relationship or communication channel.
items.ex_en: This new high-speed rail line will connect the capital with the southern provinces.
items.ex_zh: 这条新的高铁线路将把首都与南部各省连接起来。
items.ex2_en: The printer connects quickly to your laptop through the local wireless network.
items.ex2_zh: 打印机通过本地无线网络迅速与你的笔记本电脑连接。

items.def_zh: 绞接，拼接（绳索、电线、胶片等）；使结合
items.def_en: To join the ends of two ropes, wires, or pieces of film together so that they form one continuous piece.
items.ex_en: The technician carefully spliced the broken fiber-optic cables to restore the internet connection.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员小心翼翼地拼接断开的光缆，以恢复网络连接。

items.def_en: To fit or lock firmly together so that the movement of one part affects the other.
items.ex_en: The safety mechanisms interlock precisely to prevent accidental operation of the heavy machinery.
items.ex_zh: 安全机构精密地相互联锁，以防止重型机械意外启动。
items.ex2_en: You must interlock the two steel brackets firmly before tightening the screws.
items.ex2_zh: 在拧紧螺丝之前，你必须先把这两个钢制支架牢牢咬合在一起。

items.def_zh: 给（牲畜）套上轭；连接，使紧密结合
items.def_en: To join two animals together with a yoke, or link two things closely together.
items.ex_en: The farmer prepared to yoke the two oxen together before plowing the field.
items.ex_zh: 农夫准备在耕田前给两头公牛套上牛轭。

items.def_zh: 以鸠尾榫接合；严密嵌合
items.def_en: [I/T] to join two pieces of wood with interlocking tenons; to fit together closely and neatly
items.ex_en: The cabinet maker took great care to dovetail the corners of the drawer.
items.ex_zh: 木工十分用心地用鸠尾榫接合抽屉的转角。
items.ex2_en: Our strategic goals dovetail perfectly with their long-term economic development plans.
items.ex2_zh: 我们的战略目标与他们的长期经济发展规划完美契合。

items.def_en: To connect or link two or more things closely together so they depend on or relate to each other.
items.ex_en: Complex financial regulations interlink the global banking networks across several major continents.
items.ex_zh: 复杂的金融法规将跨越数大洲的全球银行网络紧密相连。
items.ex2_en: All the computer networks interlink across the campus via high-speed fiber cables.
items.ex2_zh: 所有计算机网络通过高速光纤在整个校园内紧密互联。

items.def_en: To join two pieces of wood or molding at an angle, usually a 45-degree bevel, to form a corner.
items.ex_en: The master carpenter carefully mitered the decorative moldings to form crisp corners.
items.ex_zh: 木工大师小心翼翼地将装饰线条斜接，形成利落的拐角。

items.def_zh: （使）连锁，连结成串；（计算机）连接（字符串或数据）
items.def_en: To link things, such as strings of text, data, or events, together in a continuous chain or series.
items.ex_en: Fate seemed to concatenate these disparate tragedies into an unbroken chain of sorrow.
items.ex_zh: 命运似乎将这些零星的悲剧串联成一条连绵不断的悲伤锁链。

items.def_en: [I/T] to join together physically by melting, blending, or heating
items.ex_en: Intense thermal energy caused the adjacent metal plates to fuse into one block.
items.ex_zh: 强烈的热能导致相邻的金属板熔合为一个整体。
items.ex2_en: Extreme heat will fuse the two copper wires into a single solid piece.
items.ex2_zh: 极度高温会将这两根铜线熔合成一个坚固的整体。

items.def_en: (+ together/to) to join pieces of metal or plastic by heating them until soft or liquid and hammering or pressing them
items.ex_en: Workers must weld the steel beams securely to the foundation of the bridge.
items.ex_zh: 工人们必须将钢梁牢固地焊接到桥梁的地基上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the mechanical or physical union of two or more entities into a continuous whole. The manner varies from simple adjacency (join, connect) to mechanical harnessing (yoke, couple), structural overlapping (splice, miter), and interlocking configurations (interlock, interlink, concatenate).
groups.summary_zh: 通过机械、嵌合、拼接等物理方式将两物连接或合为一体。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves creating a functional or physical continuity between separate components, contrasting with mere 'gathering' by requiring mechanical union, linkage, or interlock.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及在分离构件之间建立物理连接或咬合连续体，与单纯的“聚集”不同，它强调机械接合、链环联动或精密锁固。
groups.nuance_en: hook up: connecting utility lines or electronic rigs (sound system / trailer / water) · piece together: reconstructive assembly of fragmented parts (clues / mosaic / evidence) · lock together: rigid reciprocal latching (gears / puzzle / joints) · couple: linked pairing for force transmission (railcars / concepts / engines) · link: relational or articulated connection (stations / databases / networks)
groups.nuance_zh: hook up: 联通管线、设备或接驳拖挂 (sound system / trailer / water) · piece together: 拼合碎片以还原整体 (clues / mosaic / evidence) · lock together: 刚性互锁或嵌合咬合 (gears / puzzle / joints) · couple: 成对机械挂接或连结传动 (railcars / concepts / engines) · link: 节点相连或枢纽连通 (stations / databases / networks)

groups.name: Assess & Evaluate · 评估、估算与再评价
groups.tip: 对价值或状况全面估量

items.def_en: to form an approximate judgment or calculation concerning the size, value, or cost of something
items.ex_en: Contractors estimate that repairing the collapsed tunnel will take at least six months.
items.ex_zh: 承包商估算，修复坍塌的隧道至少需要六个月时间。

items.def_en: To evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, ability, or value of someone or something.
items.ex_en: Independent inspectors arrived on site to assess the structural integrity of the dam.
items.ex_zh: 独立质检员到达现场，评估大坝的结构完整性。

items.def_en: To judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something.
items.ex_en: The admissions committee will evaluate every applicant based on academic merit and leadership.
items.ex_zh: 招生委员会将根据学术水平和领导能力对每位申请者进行评估。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To carefully examine and form a judgment or appraisal of someone or something
items.ex_en: The two boxers paced around the ring, sizing each other up.
items.ex_zh: 两位拳手在拳台上踱步，审视打量着对方。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To evaluate the pros and cons or relative worth of something before deciding
items.ex_en: We must carefully weigh up the financial risks before accepting this lucrative offer.
items.ex_zh: 在接受这份丰厚的报价之前，我们必须仔细权衡财务风险。

items.def_zh: 判定；估算；判断（态度或反应）
items.def_en: to make a judgment about people's feelings, opinions, or a complex situation
items.ex_en: Surveys were conducted across several cities to gauge public reaction to the policy.
items.ex_zh: 在多个城市展开调查，以判定公众对该政策的反应。

items.def_en: to fail to recognize the true quality, value, or importance of someone or something
items.ex_en: Critics often underrate his quiet leadership, mistaking his reserved nature for extreme weakness.
items.ex_zh: 批评者常常低估他内敛的领导力，将他的沉默寡言误认为极度软弱。

items.def_en: To think or judge that someone or something is better, stronger, or more important than they really are.
items.ex_en: Audiences tended to overrate the film simply because of its star-studded celebrity cast.
items.ex_zh: 仅仅因为全明星阵容，观众往往对这部电影评价过高。

items.def_en: To calculate or estimate an amount, value, size, or person's ability too high.
items.ex_en: Financial analysts warn that the retail company might overestimate holiday sales this quarter.
items.ex_zh: 财务分析师警告称，该零售公司可能会高估本季度的假日销售额。

items.def_en: to judge the value, quality, or condition of someone or something, often in an official or professional capacity
items.ex_en: An independent expert was hired to appraise the rare diamonds before the auction.
items.ex_zh: 拍卖前聘请了一位独立专家对这些稀有钻石进行估价鉴定。

items.def_en: To examine and judge the value, quality, or importance of something again.
items.ex_en: The board decided to reevaluate its expansion plan in light of recent losses.
items.ex_zh: 鉴于最近的亏损，董事会决定重新评估其扩张计划。

items.def_zh: 重新评估，重新审视；重新核定
items.def_en: To think carefully again about a situation, value, or person in order to decide if your opinion or plan should change.
items.ex_en: Military commanders were forced to reassess their overall strategy after the sudden ambush.
items.ex_zh: 突遭埋伏后，军事指挥官们被迫重新审视他们的整体战略。

items.def_zh: 高估（价值、重要性）；对……估价过高
items.def_en: To think or decide that something is worth more money or importance than it actually is.
items.ex_en: Eager buyers frequently overvalue properties located near newly developed commercial districts.
items.ex_zh: 急切的买家经常过高估计新开发商业区附近房产的价值。

items.def_zh: 预先判断，先入为主地评判
items.def_en: To form an opinion or judgment about someone or something before knowing all the facts.
items.ex_en: The defense attorney cautioned the jury not to prejudge the defendant before hearing.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师告诫陪审团，在听证之前不要先入为主地评判被告。

items.def_zh: 重新评估（财产或资产价值）；使（货币）升值
items.def_en: To assess the worth of an asset or property again, or officially raise the exchange value of a currency.
items.ex_en: The municipal government intends to revalue commercial real estate for taxation purposes.
items.ex_zh: 市政府打算重新评估商业地产价值以用于税收目的。

items.def_en: To examine and judge the value, quality, or situation of someone or something again.
items.ex_en: Scholars gathered at the conference to reappraise the literary legacy of the poet.
items.ex_zh: 学者们齐聚研讨会，重新评价这位诗人的文学遗产。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the cognitive act of judging the quality, importance, value, or performance of something or someone. They range from neutral, objective appraisal (assess, evaluate) to subjective misjudgment or bias (prejudge, overrate, overestimate) and formal revisitation (reassess, reevaluate).
groups.summary_zh: 对事物或人的价值、能力、质量进行考量、估测或二次评价。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves cognitive appraisal to determine magnitude, worth, or character against an internalized standard, contrasting with 'knowing' by emphasizing deliberate subjective judgment.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及依据内在标准对客体的量级、价值或性质进行评定与权衡，与直接“获知”不同，它强调主观裁量与推求考量。
groups.nuance_en: estimate: tentative approximation of numerical metrics (cost / distance / damage) · assess: systematic evaluative judgment for taxation or policy (risk / impact / property) · size up: intuitive rapid scanning of an opponent or challenge (rival / situation / problem) · gauge: calibrated sensing of fluid variables (reaction / mood / pressure) · weigh up: deliberative balancing of competing facets (options / pros and cons / risks)
groups.nuance_zh: estimate: 对数值或规模的粗略预估 (cost / distance / damage) · assess: 为决策或定损进行系统评估 (risk / impact / property) · size up: 直觉性快速打量或摸底 (rival / situation / problem) · gauge: 敏锐测量或揣摩动态变量 (reaction / mood / pressure) · weigh up: 权衡比较利弊与风险 (options / pros and cons / risks)

groups.name: Bind, Tether & Restrain · 绑缚、栓系与物理束缚
groups.tip: 打结穿带紧紧系在一起

items.def_zh: 用系带束紧，系紧；使交织；在……中添加（烈酒、毒药等）
items.def_en: 1. To fasten or tighten shoes or clothing by pulling strings or cords through eyelets. 2. To add a small amount of alcohol, drug, or poison to food or drink.
items.ex_en: He sat on the bench to lace his running shoes before the marathon.
items.ex_zh: 他在长椅上坐下，在马拉松开跑前系紧了跑鞋的鞋带。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To tie or wrap tightly with cloth, rope, or bandages
items.ex_en: The paramedic carefully bound up the deep wound to stem the bleeding.
items.ex_zh: 医护人员小心地包扎好深伤口以止血。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To bind someone or something tightly with ropes or cords so they cannot move
items.ex_en: Most of his capital is tied up in long-term real estate investments.
items.ex_zh: 他的大部分资金都被长期房地产投资套住了。

items.def_en: (+ with/to) to tie someone or something tightly with rope, string, or tape
items.ex_en: The warehouse workers used heavy twine to bind the cardboard boxes securely together.
items.ex_zh: 仓库工人用粗麻绳将这些纸箱紧紧地捆绑在一起。

items.def_zh: 把……打结，绑紧；（使）纠缠成结；（肌肉等）痉挛紧绷
items.def_en: 1. To tie string, rope, or ribbon into a knot, or become tangled. 2. To become tight and painful from tension, or make muscles do so.
items.ex_en: The sailor showed the young recruit how to knot the thick anchor rope.
items.ex_zh: 水手向新兵演示了如何给粗重的锚绳打结。
items.ex2_en: His shoulder muscles knotted painfully under the immense stress of the exam.
items.ex2_zh: 在考试的巨大压力下，他的肩部肌肉痛苦地紧缩成疙瘩。

items.def_zh: 用皮带（或绳子）拴住；束缚，控制
items.def_en: To restrain and control an animal with a leash, or curb something tightly.
items.ex_en: Park regulations require owners to leash their dogs at all times during visits.
items.ex_zh: 公园管理规定要求游客在游园期间必须始终用绳子拴住爱犬。

items.def_zh: 捆绑，绑紧；扎紧（待烹饪的禽类的翅膀和腿）
items.def_en: To tie someone's arms and legs, or a bird's legs and wings before cooking, tightly with string or rope.
items.ex_en: The chef demonstrated how to truss the chicken with kitchen twine before roasting.
items.ex_zh: 厨师演示了在烘烤前如何用厨房用线扎紧整鸡。

items.def_zh: （用绳或链）拴住，系住；束缚，限制
items.def_en: To tie an animal or object with a rope or chain to a fixed point so it cannot move far.
items.ex_en: She decided to tether the restless horse to a wooden post outside the stable.
items.ex_zh: 她决定将躁动不安的马拴在马厩外的木桩上。

items.def_zh: 用紧身胸衣束紧；严格限制，约束
items.def_en: 1. To dress or bind someone tightly in a supporting corset. 2. To restrict or constrain someone or something strictly.
items.ex_en: Bureaucratic rules corset the innovation of creative researchers within the conservative institute.
items.ex_zh: 官僚主义的条条框框严重束缚了该保守机构内富有创意的研究人员的创新。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To tie up someone's limbs or an animal tightly and securely
items.ex_en: The masked bandits used thick electrical cords to truss up the wealthy merchant.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面强盗用粗电线将这位富商五花大绑起来。

items.def_en: To put handcuffs on someone to restrain them; (figurative) to restrict someone's freedom of action.
items.ex_en: Police officers moved swiftly through the crowd to handcuff the fleeing burglary suspect.
items.ex_zh: 警察迅速穿过人群，给那名逃跑的入室盗窃嫌疑人戴上了手铐。

items.def_en: to put handcuffs, fetters, or chains on someone to prevent free movement
items.ex_en: Guards were ordered to shackle the violent inmate before moving him across facilities.
items.ex_zh: 警卫接到命令，在跨设施转移这名暴力囚犯前必须给他戴上镣铐。

items.def_zh: 捆绑（两臂）；绑住，压住；剪去（鸟的）飞羽
items.def_en: To tie or hold someone's arms tightly to stop them from moving; to cut off the wing tips of a bird to prevent flight.
items.ex_en: Two burly guards managed to pinion the struggling captive against the stone wall.
items.ex_zh: 两名健壮的守卫合力将挣扎的俘虏压在石墙上，紧紧制伏了他的双臂。

items.def_en: to tie someone's feet together with chains; to heavily restrict freedom
items.ex_en: Oppressive medieval traditions fetter the young princess, denying her any personal freedom.
items.ex_zh: 压抑的中世纪传统束缚着年轻的公主，剥夺了她的一切个人自由。

items.def_zh: 使不能移动，使固定；使瘫痪，使丧失机动性
items.def_en: To prevent someone or something from moving or functioning normally.
items.ex_en: Paramedics applied a rigid splint to immobilise the patient's fractured leg completely.
items.ex_zh: 急救人员使用刚性夹板将患者骨折的腿部完全固定住。

items.def_en: to bind someone's hands or legs with metal manacles
items.ex_en: Cruel jailers chose to manacle the helpless prisoner to the damp dungeon wall.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的狱卒把无助的囚犯用手铐脚镣锁在阴湿的地牢墙上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to restricting the physical movement or freedom of a person or animal using ropes, chains, cords, or mechanical restraints. Differences hinge on the restraining device (handcuff, leash, tether, lace), binding complexity (knot, truss), or targeted limb restriction (pinion).
groups.summary_zh: 使用绳索、系带、手铐等用具使对象固定或剥夺其行动自由。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves constricting an entity's mobility using cords, chains, or ties wrapped around it, contrasting with static 'holding' by enforcing mechanical constraint.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及利用绳索、链条等卷绕捆扎以剥夺实体的自由活动能力，与静态的“握持”不同，它强调机械拘束与强行束缚。
groups.nuance_en: knot: interlacing cords into an interlocking tangle (rope / tie / shoelace) · lace: crisscross threading to draw edges closed (boots / corset / football) · tether: flexible mooring restricting radius of movement (horse / drone / goat) · truss: immobilizing limbs snugly with rope (fowl / prisoner / culprit) · bind: circumferential wrapping under tension (wounds / hands / sheaves)
groups.nuance_zh: knot: 打结锁闭绳带 (rope / tie / shoelace) · lace: 交叉穿带拉紧收口 (boots / corset / football) · tether: 系绳拴锁以限定活动半径 (horse / drone / goat) · truss: 五花大绑束缚肢体 (fowl / prisoner / culprit) · bind: 张力包裹紧固捆绑 (wounds / hands / sheaves)

groups.name: Harden, Congeal & Solidify · 硬化、凝结与固化
groups.tip: 物理结壳或化学交联变硬

items.def_en: to change from a liquid or soft state into a firm, solid state
items.ex_en: Leave the freshly poured concrete alone overnight so that it can set properly.
items.ex_zh: 让刚浇筑的混凝土静置一夜，以便它能够完全凝固。

items.def_en: To form or become covered with a hard outer layer or crust.
items.ex_en: The fresh snow began to crust after hours of exposure to freezing winds.
items.ex_zh: 经过数小时刺骨寒风的吹拂，新雪表面开始结出一层硬皮。
items.ex2_en: Baking heat will quickly crust the outer dough of the fresh bread.
items.ex2_zh: 烘烤的热力会很快使新鲜面包的外皮结成一层硬壳。

items.def_en: To become firm, rigid, or solid, or make something do so
items.ex_en: The soft clay will quickly harden up when left under the afternoon sun.
items.ex_zh: 柔软的黏土在午后的阳光照射下会很快硬化。
items.ex2_en: Special chemical sealants harden up the porous concrete surface within a few hours.
items.ex2_zh: 特殊的化学密封剂能在数小时内使多孔混凝土表面硬化。

items.def_en: To gradually become rigid, stiff, or less pliable
items.ex_en: His joints tend to stiffen up significantly after prolonged periods of physical inactivity.
items.ex_zh: 长时间缺乏身体活动后，他的关节往往会明显变得僵硬。

items.def_en: [I/T] to become solid or firm, or to cause a liquid or gas to do so
items.ex_en: The melted chocolate will slowly solidify once you place it in the refrigerator.
items.ex_zh: 熔化的巧克力一旦放入冰箱就会慢慢凝固。
items.ex2_en: Freezing winter temperatures solidify the shallow water inside the exposed garden pipe.
items.ex2_zh: 严冬的低温使裸露在花园管道里的浅水凝结成冰。

items.def_zh: （使）变硬，（使）僵硬；（使）变坚定，增强
items.def_en: To become firm, hard, or rigid, or to make something firm, hard, or rigid; to become or make more determined.
items.ex_en: A dose of starch was added to the wash to stiffen the collars.
items.ex_zh: 洗涤时加入了一剂淀粉，以使衣领变得挺括硬实。
items.ex2_en: His joints stiffen visibly whenever the temperature drops drastically in the winter.
items.ex2_zh: 每当冬天气温骤降时，他的关节就会明显僵硬。

items.def_en: (often callus over) To form or cause to form thick, hardened patches of skin.
items.ex_en: Years of hard manual labor caused his weathered hands to callus over heavily.
items.ex_zh: 多年的重体力劳动使他历经风霜的双手结满了厚厚的老茧。
items.ex2_en: Constant friction from hard hiking boots will quickly callus your bare heels.
items.ex2_zh: 硬质登山靴的持续摩擦会很快让你赤裸的脚后跟磨出老茧。

items.def_zh: （对金属、玻璃等）进行退火处理；锻炼，磨炼
items.def_en: To heat metal or glass and allow it to cool slowly to make it harder, tougher, or less brittle; (figurative) to strengthen or temper.
items.ex_en: The blacksmith will carefully anneal the forged steel to eliminate internal structural stresses.
items.ex_zh: 铁匠将仔细对锻造的钢材进行退火，以消除内部结构应力。

items.def_zh: （使）钙化，（使）硬化；（态度、制度等）僵化
items.def_en: 1. To become or cause to become hard by the deposition of calcium salts. 2. (figurative) (of attitudes, beliefs, or institutions) to become rigid and unchanging.
items.ex_en: Over decades, archaic organizational dogmas began to calcify into completely unchangeable rules.
items.ex_zh: 数十年来，陈旧的组织教条开始僵化为完全不可动摇的死规矩。
items.ex2_en: Aging tissues calcify internal arteries, reducing the flexibility of critical blood vessels.
items.ex2_zh: 衰老组织会使内部动脉钙化，降低关键血管的弹性。

items.def_en: To become thick or solid, or cause a liquid to thicken into a solid or semi-solid state, especially upon cooling.
items.ex_en: The gravy began to congeal on the cold plate as dinner ended.
items.ex_zh: 晚餐结束时，肉汁开始在冰冷的盘子里凝结。
items.ex2_en: Sudden cold temperature will congeal the warm beef soup within thirty minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 骤降的低温会在三十分钟内使温热的牛肉汤凝固。

items.def_en: (especially of blood or liquids) To change from a liquid into a thick, semi-solid mass.
items.ex_en: Certain medications are prescribed specifically to prevent circulating blood from starting to coagulate.
items.ex_zh: 某些药物是专门为了防止循环中的血液发生凝固而开具的。
items.ex2_en: The laboratory technician used a specialized enzyme to coagulate the blood samples.
items.ex2_zh: 实验室技术人员使用一种专用酶使血液样本凝结。

items.def_en: To become completely solid or immobilized through freezing
items.ex_en: Whenever she stepped onto the stage, her mind completely froze up.
items.ex_zh: 每当她走上舞台，她的大脑就一片空白、彻底卡壳。

items.def_en: [I/T] to become hard like bone, or turn into bone tissue
items.ex_en: In elderly patients, softer cartilage around the joints can sometimes ossify into bone.
items.ex_zh: 在老年患者中，关节周围较软的软骨有时会骨化成骨组织。
items.ex2_en: Rigid corporate bureaucracy can quickly ossify creative ideas into dull standard procedures.
items.ex2_zh: 死板的企业官僚作风能很快将创意僵化成枯燥的标准流程。

items.def_zh: （使）玻璃化，（使）变成玻璃状物质
items.def_en: To convert or be converted into glass or a glassy substance, especially by extreme heat.
items.ex_en: Volcanic lightning possesses enough intense heat to vitrify surrounding desert sand instantly.
items.ex_zh: 火山闪电蕴含着极高的热量，能使周围的沙漠细沙瞬间玻璃化。
items.ex2_en: Clay pots vitrify easily inside the intense kiln fire during pottery firing.
items.ex2_zh: 陶罐在窑炉的高温烈火中烧制时很容易玻璃化。

items.def_en: To treat rubber with sulfur at high temperatures to increase its strength, elasticity, and durability.
items.ex_en: Industrial manufacturers vulcanize raw rubber to produce durable tires for heavy trucks.
items.ex_zh: 工业制造商对生胶进行硫化处理，以生产适用于重型卡车的耐用轮胎。

items.def_en: [I/T] to change into stone or a stony substance by chemical mineral replacement
items.ex_en: Rich mineral deposits seep into fallen trees and petrify the organic wood.
items.ex_zh: 富含矿物质的沉积物渗入倒伏的树木中，使有机木质石化。
items.ex2_en: Ancient fallen trees petrify naturally under deep volcanic ash over millions of years.
items.ex2_zh: 古老的倒木在深厚的火山灰下历经数百万年会自然石化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the phase change or physical transformation of a substance from soft, liquid, or malleable into a firm, rigid, or glass-like solid. The process may be biological (callus, calcify), chemical/thermal (anneal, vulcanize, vitrify), or colloidal/viscous (coagulate, congeal, stiffen).
groups.summary_zh: 物质由软变硬、由液体或可塑态转化为坚硬固体或凝胶态。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema entails phase transformation from fluid/supple to unyielding/compact through chemical, thermal, or aging actions, contrasting with mere 'cooling' by producing structural rigidity.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及通过化学、物理或老化作用使实体由流质、柔软状态转变为坚硬刚体，与单纯“冷却”不同，它强调结构固化与抗形变性。
groups.nuance_en: set: planned chemical cural transition into solid state (gelatin / concrete / glue) · crust: outer boundary hardening into a dry mantle (snow / bread / wound) · stiffen: loss of mechanical flexibility (muscles / fabric / resolve) · solidify: macroscopic transition to cohesive solid body (lava / grease / position) · anneal: thermal tempering to toughen microstructure (glass / steel / metal)
groups.nuance_zh: set: 化学固化或凝结定型 (gelatin / concrete / glue) · crust: 表层硬化结壳 (snow / bread / wound) · stiffen: 失去柔韧性而僵化紧绷 (muscles / fabric / resolve) · solidify: 凝聚凝固成坚固整体 (lava / grease / position) · anneal: 退火热处理以韧化硬化 (glass / steel / metal)

groups.name: Increase & Expand · 增加与扩大 (Enlarge, Augment, Amplify)
groups.tip: 通过添加扩充或倍增扩大规模

items.def_zh: 增加，添加；做加法；补充说
items.def_en: 1. to put something together with something else to increase the size, number, or amount. 2. to calculate the total of two or more numbers. 3. to say something further.
items.ex_en: The pastry chef decided to add fresh blueberries to enhance the cake's flavor.
items.ex_zh: 糕点师决定添加新鲜蓝莓以提升蛋糕的口感。

items.def_en: to add something extra to an existing thing in order to improve or complete it.
items.ex_en: Doctors usually recommend athletes supplement their daily diet with extra vitamins and minerals.
items.ex_zh: 医生通常建议运动员在日常饮食中增补额外的维生素和矿物质。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To gradually increase in amount, size, or strength over time
items.ex_en: Regular strength training helps patients gradually build up muscle mass after severe surgery.
items.ex_zh: 定期力量训练有助于患者在重大手术后逐渐增强肌肉量。
items.ex2_en: Toxic exhaust fumes build up dangerously inside the poorly ventilated car repair garage.
items.ex2_zh: 有毒废气在通风不良的汽车修理厂内危险地积聚起来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To sharply increase the rate, volume, or intensity of something
items.ex_en: Automakers plan to ramp up electric vehicle production to meet surging consumer demand.
items.ex_zh: 汽车制造商计划大幅提升电动汽车产量，以满足激增的消费者需求。
items.ex2_en: Military training operations ramp up noticeably as international tensions mount around the border.
items.ex2_zh: 随着边境周边国际局势加剧，军事训练行动显著升级。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To increase the size, amount, or extent of something proportionally
items.ex_en: The successful startup must scale up its customer support team to handle growth.
items.ex_zh: 这家成功的初创公司必须按比例扩大其客户支持团队，以应对业务增长。
items.ex2_en: Server workloads scale up automatically whenever holiday traffic spikes on the website.
items.ex2_zh: 每当网站上的节日流量激增时，服务器负载就会自动扩展。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To boost or increase the speed, intensity, or level of an activity
items.ex_en: The hospital had to step up security measures following the recent incident.
items.ex_zh: 在最近的事件发生后，医院不得不加强安保措施。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ into/by) To become greater or make something greater in size, scope, or extent
items.ex_en: The ambitious technology firm intends to expand its operations into several Asian markets.
items.ex_zh: 这家雄心勃勃的科技公司打算将其业务拓展至数个亚洲市场。
items.ex2_en: The warm air expands rapidly inside the colorful hot air balloon envelope.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖的空气在五彩斑斓的热气球气囊内迅速膨胀。

items.def_en: To make something increase, become better, or be more successful
items.ex_en: Lower interest rates usually boost consumer spending across the domestic retail sector significantly.
items.ex_zh: 较低的利率通常会显著推动国内零售业的消费者支出增长。

items.def_zh: 扩大，扩展；放大（照片等）；详述，阐述
items.def_en: 1. to make something bigger or to become bigger. 2. to produce a larger print of a photograph. 3. (+ on/upon) to speak or write about something in greater detail.
items.ex_en: The growing family decided to enlarge their suburban house by adding two bedrooms.
items.ex_zh: 随着家庭人口增加，这家人决定通过增建两间卧室来扩建郊区住宅。
items.ex2_en: The pupils of your eyes naturally enlarge when walking into a dark room.
items.ex2_zh: 当你走进黑暗的房间时，你的瞳孔会自然放大。

items.def_en: to increase the size, amount, value, or strength of something by adding to it.
items.ex_en: The charity received generous philanthropic donations to augment its community relief fund.
items.ex_zh: 该慈善机构获得了慷慨的慈善捐助，以充实其社区救济基金。

items.def_zh: 变宽，变阔；扩大，拓宽（范围、经验、知识等）
items.def_en: to become wider, or to expand the scope, range, or variety of something.
items.ex_en: Traveling abroad helped broaden his perspective on different cultural traditions and values.
items.ex_zh: 去国外旅行有助于拓宽他对不同文化传统和价值观的视野。
items.ex2_en: The narrow mountain road broadens steadily as it descends toward the fertile valley.
items.ex2_zh: 狭窄的山路在向肥沃的山谷延伸时逐渐变宽。

items.def_zh: （使）加倍，（使）增加一倍；兼任；折叠
items.def_en: 1. to become twice as much or as many, or to make something twice as large. 2. (+ as) to have a second role, purpose, or job. 3. to bend or fold something over.
items.ex_en: The company expects to double its annual revenue within the next two years.
items.ex_zh: 该公司预计在未来两年内将其年营业收入翻一番。
items.ex2_en: The city's urban population will double over the next several decades of growth.
items.ex2_zh: 该市的城市人口在未来几十年的增长中将会翻倍。

items.def_en: to become three times as much or as many, or to make something three times as big.
items.ex_en: Online sales began to triple as holiday demand surged across the country.
items.ex_zh: 随着全国假日需求的激增，线上销售额开始增至三倍。
items.ex2_en: The aggressive marketing campaign managed to triple the small bakery's monthly revenue.
items.ex2_zh: 激进的营销活动使这家小面包店的月收入增加了两倍。

items.def_zh: 增加，成倍增加；乘，使相乘；繁殖
items.def_en: 1. to increase greatly in number or amount, or to make something do this. 2. to calculate the product of two numbers. 3. to reproduce or cause organisms to reproduce.
items.ex_en: Administrative problems began to multiply rapidly after the sudden resignation of key managers.
items.ex_zh: 在关键管理人员突然辞职后，行政管理上的问题开始急剧增多。
items.ex2_en: Warm humid conditions multiply harmful bacteria inside raw poultry within a few hours.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖潮湿的环境会在几小时内使生禽肉中的有害细菌成倍增加。

items.def_en: To increase the strength, volume, or significance of something
items.ex_en: Sensational media reports only served to amplify public anxiety about the economic crisis.
items.ex_zh: 耸人听闻的媒体报道只会进一步放大公众对经济危机的焦虑。

items.def_zh: 使增加到最大限度，最大化；充分利用
items.def_en: 1. to increase something to the greatest possible amount or degree. 2. to make the best or most effective use of something.
items.ex_en: The logistics team redesigned the delivery routes to maximize daily operational efficiency.
items.ex_zh: 物流团队重新设计了配送路线，以最大限度提高日常运营效率。

groups.summary_en: Quantity and scale transformation verbs where an agent or process boosts the number, volume, dimension, or extent of an entity, ranging from simple arithmetic addition to strategic scaling.
groups.summary_zh: 使规模、尺寸、数量或范围在原有基础上扩张放大。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves augmenting the volume, reach, or scale of an extant entity, contrasting with 'creating' by operating as a dimensional accretion on an existing base.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及在现有基础上扩展实体在规模、容量或空间上的体量，与凭空“创造”不同，它表现为既有实体的外延扩充或蓄积增量。
groups.nuance_en: supplement: adding an auxiliary part to remedy a deficit (income / diet / vitamins) · build up: progressive cumulative accretion over time (reserves / strength / pressure) · ramp up: planned steep acceleration of output (production / marketing / volume) · scale up: proportional systemic magnification (operation / infrastructure / trial) · expand: broad outward geometric enlargement (footprint / universe / empire)
groups.nuance_zh: supplement: 填补不足的辅助性追加 (income / diet / vitamins) · build up: 渐进积累与蓄积壮大 (reserves / strength / pressure) · ramp up: 有计划的大幅拉升提速 (production / marketing / volume) · scale up: 按比例成倍放大系统规模 (operation / infrastructure / trial) · expand: 几何级向外扩张或伸展 (footprint / universe / empire)

groups.name: Weave, Knit & Sew · 纺织、针织与缝纫
groups.tip: 穿针引线编结织物成衣

items.def_en: (+ sth) To join or interloop threads or elements closely together
items.ex_en: A shared sense of purpose helped knit together the diverse volunteer groups.
items.ex_zh: 共同的目标感帮助将各个多元的志愿者团队紧密交织在一起。
items.ex2_en: His broken leg bones knit together completely after six quiet weeks in a cast.
items.ex2_zh: 他骨折的腿骨在打了六周安静的石膏后完全愈合在了一起。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To fasten pieces of textile or material together using stitches
items.ex_en: She carefully began to sew together the patchwork pieces for the quilt.
items.ex_zh: 她开始细心地将缝制被子的碎布块拼接缝合在一起。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To join or mend fabric or wounds using a needle and thread
items.ex_en: The doctor had to stitch up the deep cut on his forearm.
items.ex_zh: 医生不得不把他前臂上的那道很深的伤口缝合好。

items.def_zh: 织入金银丝；织成（花纹织物）
items.def_en: to weave, especially with gold or silver threads, into rich decorative fabric.
items.ex_en: The royal weaver would tissue the velvet mantle with shimmering silver filaments.
items.ex_zh: 皇家织工将闪烁的银丝织入这件华丽的天鹅绒斗篷中。

items.def_en: [I/T] to join, fasten, or repair something using a needle and thread
items.ex_en: She used fine black silk thread to stitch the hem of the dress.
items.ex_zh: 她用精细的黑丝线将那件连衣裙的下摆仔细缝缀好。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make clothes, blankets, etc. by looping yarn with a hooked needle
items.ex_en: Grandmother loves to crochet delicate wool blankets for the upcoming winter evenings.
items.ex_zh: 祖母喜欢在即将到来的冬夜里用钩针编织精致的羊毛毯。

items.def_en: to join three or more strands of hair, straw, or fabric by interlacing them
items.ex_en: The mother gently began to plait her daughter's thick hair into braids.
items.ex_zh: 母亲温柔地开始将女儿浓密的头发编成整齐的辫子。

items.def_zh: 在（织物）上缝打褶花边，绣蜂巢形褶裥；给……穿上罩衫
items.def_en: 1. to gather fabric into close decorative folds with embroidered stitching. 2. to dress someone in a smock.
items.ex_en: Artisans labored for hours to smock the delicate linen bodice with geometric embroidery.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们辛苦劳作数小时，在精致的亚麻紧身胸衣上绣出蜂巢褶裥。

items.def_zh: 织反针，织反缝；（溪流等）潺潺流动
items.def_en: 1. To knit with a reverse stitch that creates a raised horizontal ridge. 2. (of a shallow stream) To flow with a gentle, murmuring sound.
items.ex_en: The pattern instructed the knitter to purl three stitches across the row.
items.ex_zh: 图解说明指示编织者在这一行中织出三个反针线圈。

items.def_zh: 编织；使紧密结合；（断骨）愈合；皱（眉）
items.def_en: 1. To make clothes or fabric from yarn using long needles or a machine. 2. To join together closely and firmly; (of broken bones) to heal and grow together.
items.ex_en: She plans to knit a warm wool cardigan before the cold weather arrives.
items.ex_zh: 她计划在寒冷天气到来之前编织一件暖和的羊毛开衫。
items.ex2_en: The fractured arm bones will knit naturally if kept in a tight plaster cast.
items.ex2_zh: 如果固定在紧绷的石膏托里，骨折的手臂骨骼会自然愈合。

items.def_en: To join, repair, or make clothes and fabric items using a needle and thread or a sewing machine.
items.ex_en: He learned how to sew torn seams using a basic handheld needle.
items.ex_zh: 他学会了如何用一把普通的手缝针缝补撕裂的接缝。

items.def_zh: 织，编织；编造，虚构；穿梭，迂回行进
items.def_en: 1. To make cloth, a basket, or a pattern by crossing threads or strips over and under each other. 2. To move along by turning and dodging around obstacles.
items.ex_en: Local artisans still weave traditional patterns into these colorful tapestries by hand.
items.ex_zh: 当地手艺人仍然手工将传统图案编织进这些色彩绚丽的挂毯中。

items.def_en: [I/T] to decorate fabric with patterns sewn with colored thread
items.ex_en: She spent weeks attempting to embroider delicate floral patterns onto the silk pillowcases.
items.ex_zh: 她花了好几个星期尝试在真丝枕套上刺绣精致的花卉图案。

items.def_en: [I/T] to join threads, fibers, or strips by weaving them under and over one another
items.ex_en: The artisan began to interlace flexible bamboo strips to form a durable basket.
items.ex_zh: 工匠开始将柔韧的竹篾互相交错编织，做成一个耐用的篮子。
items.ex2_en: Their delicate fingers interlace tenderly while walking through the peaceful autumn woods together.
items.ex2_zh: 一起漫步在宁静的秋日树林中时，他们纤细的手指温柔地交缠在一起。

items.def_zh: 织入锦缎花纹，在……上织出凸纹花样
items.def_en: To weave rich, raised decorative patterns—often with gold or silver thread—into heavy fabric.
items.ex_en: Weavers would brocade gold thread into the heavy silk to fashion imperial robes.
items.ex_zh: 织工们会将金线织入厚重的真丝中，制成凸纹华丽的帝王袍服。

items.def_en: To divide, form, or mark into a fine network of intersecting lines or veins.
items.ex_en: Intricate veins reticulate the translucent surface of the delicate autumn leaf.
items.ex_zh: 错综复杂的叶脉在纤细的秋叶透明表面上交织成网状。
items.ex2_en: Delicate red capillary vessels reticulate throughout the surface of the human eyeball.
items.ex2_zh: 纤细的红色毛细血管在人类眼球表面交织成网状。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the interlocking, interlacing, or stitching of yarn, thread, or fabric to construct or decorate textiles. Nuances range from basic joining with needle and thread (sew, stitch) to structured looping (knit, crochet) and perpendicular interlacing on a loom (weave).
groups.summary_zh: 用针线或纱线交错、环套成布或进行缝合加固。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves intertwining supple threads, yarns, or structural strands to fabricate or mend a flexible textile, contrasting with rigid 'assembling' through pliable interlacing.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及将柔软的纱线、线缕等按规则经纬交织，以制成或修补柔性织物，与刚性“组装”不同，它依托纤维的柔韧套结与缝纳。
groups.nuance_en: stitch: passing needle and thread through substrate (wound / hem / leather) · crochet: interlocking loops with a hooked needle (blanket / lace / cardigan) · plait: interbraiding three or more flexible strands (hair / straw / ribbons) · knit together: interlocking looped yarns into cohesive fabric (sweater / community / bones) · smock: decorative tight gathering of cloth with embroidery (blouse / fabric / bodice)
groups.nuance_zh: stitch: 针线穿刺缝合 (wound / hem / leather) · crochet: 用钩针编织镂空线圈 (blanket / lace / cardigan) · plait: 三股或多股交错编辫 (hair / straw / ribbons) · knit together: 环扣交织连结成片 (sweater / community / bones) · smock: 抽褶密缝刺绣装饰 (blouse / fabric / bodice)

groups.name: Affection & Veneration · 喜爱与崇敬 (Like, Love, Adore, Revere)
groups.tip: 从单纯喜欢到顶礼膜拜的情感递进

items.def_en: To feel a mild attraction toward or liking for someone or something
items.ex_en: I think he really began to fancy her after the office party.
items.ex_zh: 我觉得在办公室派对之后，他真的有点看中她了。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) feel affection, fondness, or liking toward someone
items.ex_en: He clearly continued to care for her deeply despite their many differences.
items.ex_zh: 尽管他们之间有诸多分歧，他显然依然深深钟情于她。

items.def_en: To find someone or something pleasant, attractive, or enjoyable; to prefer or wish for.
items.ex_en: Most students seem to like the new history teacher and her engaging lessons.
items.ex_zh: 大多数学生似乎都很喜欢那位新来的历史老师以及她生动有趣的课。

items.def_en: (+ sb) have a great deal of respect and admiration for someone
items.ex_en: Young athletes around the world look up to her as an inspirational leader.
items.ex_zh: 全世界的年轻运动员都视她为鼓舞人心的榜样并敬佩她。

items.def_zh: 爱，热爱；非常喜欢，倾心于
items.def_en: To feel deep affection, passion, or fondness for someone or something.
items.ex_en: They promised to love each other through all of life's unpredictable challenges.
items.ex_zh: 他们承诺无论生活面临怎样不可预测的挑战，都将彼此深爱。

items.def_en: To admire someone deeply for their abilities, qualities, or achievements; to treat with consideration or regard.
items.ex_en: Colleagues widely respect her professional integrity and dedication to sound ethical principles.
items.ex_zh: 同事们普遍非常敬重她的职业操守以及对崇高道德原则的坚守。

items.def_en: To regard someone or something with respect, wonder, or approval.
items.ex_en: Many young scientists admire her groundbreaking research and relentless pursuit of truth.
items.ex_zh: 许多年轻科学家都钦佩她开创性的研究成果以及对真理的不懈追求。

items.def_en: To hold someone or something dear and protect or care for them tenderly
items.ex_en: He will always cherish the memories of summer afternoons spent with his grandfather.
items.ex_zh: 他将永远珍视那些与祖父一同度过的夏日午后记忆。

items.def_en: To cause someone or something to be loved or liked (usually followed by 'to').
items.ex_en: Her humble kindness and gentle humor helped endear her to the community.
items.ex_zh: 她谦逊的善意和温和的幽默感使她深受社区居民的喜爱。

items.def_en: (+ sb) feel lavish, excessive, or uncritical love and adoration for someone
items.ex_en: The proud grandparents continue to dote on their only grandson without restraint.
items.ex_zh: 这对引以为傲的祖父母依然毫无节制地溺爱着他们唯一的孙子。

items.def_en: (+ sb) develop strong romantic affection or infatuation for someone
items.ex_en: It did not take long for him to fall for her charming personality.
items.ex_zh: 没过多久，他就彻底迷恋上了她那极具魅力的个性。

items.def_en: To love someone very much and feel great admiration or affection for them; to like very much.
items.ex_en: The children adore their new golden retriever puppy and play with it daily.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们非常喜欢他们新养的金毛幼犬，每天都和它一起玩。

items.def_en: To admire or love someone or something to an excessive, uncritical degree
items.ex_en: Teenage fans often idolize pop stars without seeing their normal human flaws.
items.ex_zh: 十几岁的狂热粉丝往往会盲目崇拜流行歌星，却看不到他们普通人的缺点。

items.def_en: (formal) To feel deep respect, admiration, and awe for someone or something.
items.ex_en: Villagers deeply revere the ancient spiritual traditions handed down by their ancestors.
items.ex_zh: 村民们深深崇敬祖先流传下来的古老精神传统。

items.def_en: To regard with deep religious, moral, or historical respect and awe
items.ex_en: Scholars still venerate the master philosopher whose writings shaped early democratic thought.
items.ex_zh: 学者们依然崇奉那位著作塑造了早期民主思想的哲学大师。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe experiencing or directing positive emotional regard toward someone or something, scaling from mild personal preference to deep devotion and sacred awe.
groups.summary_zh: 表达对人或事物的好感与崇敬，程度由浅喜至深爱与顶礼膜拜。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves an internal scalar posture ranging from mild personal attraction to profound moral exaltation, contrasting with neutral 'judging' by centering on affectionate or reverent emotional bias.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式表现为从浅层个人倾慕到深层道德敬畏的情感梯度，与中立的“评判”不同，它侧重于饱含主观爱慕或敬仰的价值肯定。
groups.nuance_en: fancy: ephemeral superficial liking or attraction (someone / chances / dessert) · care for: tender solicitude or mild fondness (patient / elder / painting) · look up to: aspiring deference toward a role model (mentor / sibling / hero) · admire: objective esteem for exceptional qualities (courage / skill / honesty) · cherish: vigilant emotional treasuring with protectiveness (memory / freedom / heirloom)
groups.nuance_zh: fancy: 浅层的爱慕或一时兴起的中意 (someone / chances / dessert) · care for: 关切体贴或温和的好感 (patient / elder / painting) · look up to: 对榜样由衷的仰慕与效仿 (mentor / sibling / hero) · admire: 对卓越品质的钦佩赞赏 (courage / skill / honesty) · cherish: 悉心守护与深切珍视 (memory / freedom / heirloom)

groups.name: Dash & Hurtle · 疾驰与疾射 (Hurtle, Whizz, Scud)
groups.tip: 极快速度冲刺奔跑或掠过

items.def_en: to move suddenly and rapidly in a specific direction
items.ex_en: A startled deer suddenly began to dart across the busy mountain highway.
items.ex_zh: 一只受惊的鹿突然飞奔穿过繁忙的高山公路。

items.def_en: run or move away suddenly and swiftly
items.ex_en: The frightened kitten saw the open door and chose to dart off.
items.ex_zh: 那只受惊的小猫看到敞开的门，便猛冲逃走了。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) rush past very rapidly, often making a buzzing or whistling sound
items.ex_en: Speeding sports cars seemed to whizz by our small bicycle every minute.
items.ex_zh: 超速的跑车似乎每分钟都会呼啸着从我们的小自行车旁飞掠而过。

items.def_zh: （小孩或小动物）欢快地奔跑，蹦蹦跳跳地跑
items.def_en: 1. (+ away/off/around) When small animals or children scamper, they run quickly with light, playful steps.
items.ex_en: The energetic squirrels scamper through the courtyard trees every crisp autumn morning.
items.ex_zh: 充满活力的小松鼠每个清凉的秋晨都在院落的树间欢快蹦跳。

items.def_zh: 轻快敏捷地跑，飞掠；使掠过水面
items.def_en: 1. (+ across/along/away) To move quickly and lightly across a surface with rapid, darting steps.
items.ex_en: Tiny sand crabs skitter rapidly across the wet shore when waves crash.
items.ex_zh: 当海浪拍岸时，小沙蟹在湿润的海滩上轻快敏捷地飞掠跑开。

items.def_zh: （发飒飒声或嗖嗖声）飞快掠过
items.def_en: 1. (+ past/through) To move very quickly with a soft, rushing, hissing sound.
items.ex_en: The raven's wings whish past the ancient tower in the twilight calm.
items.ex_zh: 暮色的宁静中，乌鸦的翅膀伴着微弱的破空声掠过古塔。

items.def_zh: （使）呼呼疾驰，（使）嗖地飞快移动
items.def_en: 1. (variant spelling of whoosh) To move very rapidly with a soft rushing sound.
items.ex_en: The express train seemed to woosh along the platform without stopping once.
items.ex_zh: 那列特快列车呼呼疾驰穿过站台，中途没有一丝停留。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) dart or fly by with exceptional velocity
items.ex_en: The bright green racing car seemed to shoot past us with unbelievable speed.
items.ex_zh: 那辆翠绿色的赛车以令人难以置信的速度飞速掠过我们身旁。

items.def_en: move or travel at dangerously high speed
items.ex_en: Reckless young drivers often tear along the narrow country lanes after dark.
items.ex_zh: 天黑之后，轻率的年轻司机常常在狭窄的乡间小道上狂奔疾驰。

items.def_en: to move exceptionally fast, leaving a blurred visual impression
items.ex_en: A silver meteor seemed to streak across the dark northern sky tonight.
items.ex_zh: 今晚，一颗银白色的流星飞速掠过漆黑的北方夜空。

items.def_en: 1. (+ across) When clouds or a boat scud, they move rapidly and smoothly driven by the wind.
items.ex_en: Dark rainclouds scud across the gray horizon ahead of the oncoming gale.
items.ex_zh: 在即将来临的大风暴前，乌黑的雨云疾驶掠过灰蒙蒙的天际线。

items.def_en: (also 'hie oneself') (archaic / humorous) To go quickly or hurry to a place.
items.ex_en: The weary messenger had to hie himself to the king's palace immediately.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的信使不得不立刻匆忙赶往国王的宫殿。

items.def_zh: 疾驰，飞驰，呼啸而过；（使）发出飕飕声
items.def_en: To move very quickly, often making a buzzing or whistling sound through the air.
items.ex_en: Stray bullets began to whizz dangerously overhead during the chaotic night battle.
items.ex_zh: 在混乱的夜战中，流弹开始危险地在头顶呼啸掠过。

items.def_en: (+ through/down) to drive or move fast and often heedlessly or destructively
items.ex_en: The heavy truck continued to barrel down the steep road despite failing brakes.
items.ex_zh: 尽管刹车失灵，那辆重型卡车依然在陡峭的公路上疯狂疾驰而下。

items.def_en: To move very fast in a particular direction, often in a violent or uncontrolled way.
items.ex_en: Enormous boulders hurtle violently down the sheer mountain cliff after the blast.
items.ex_zh: 爆炸过后，巨大的圆石从险峻的山崖上猛冲飞落而下。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote moving rapidly across or through an area, distinguishing between light, skittering foot movements and high-velocity rushes that produce audible rushing or whipping sounds.
groups.summary_zh: 指高速穿行或冲刺，涵盖轻捷掠行与带风声呼啸的猛冲。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves ballistic or erratic high-velocity linear movement, contrasting with ordinary 'running' through explosive acceleration, diminutive agility, or audible wind-shear.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及如弹道发射或瞬息骤变的高速直线位移，与普通的“奔跑”不同，它伴随着爆发性加速、灵巧变向或带风呼啸感。
groups.nuance_en: dart: instantaneous abrupt burst in a new vector (glance / tongue / fish) · scamper: frantic scampering gait of small entities (mice / squirrels / children) · skitter: light hurried sliding across a surface (pebble / beetle / leaves) · whizz by: high-speed transit producing sharp air friction (bullet / car / drone) · shoot past: sudden linear bypass at blinding velocity (meteor / train / racer)
groups.nuance_zh: dart: 瞬时离弦般疾射或转向 (glance / tongue / fish) · scamper: 小型实体仓皇碎步奔逃 (mice / squirrels / children) · skitter: 沿表面轻快掠过或滑窜 (pebble / beetle / leaves) · whizz by: 高速掠过并发出破空声 (bullet / car / drone) · shoot past: 如箭矢般极速超前疾驰 (meteor / train / racer)

groups.name: Fasten & Secure · 绑扎与紧固 (Fasten, Secure, Cinch)
groups.tip: 绳带绑扎系牢紧固

items.def_en: (dated) To fasten or support a stocking or sock with a garter.
items.ex_en: The courtier bent down to garter his silk stockings before the ball.
items.ex_zh: 那位侍臣在舞会前弯下腰，用袜带系紧自己的丝绸长袜。

items.def_zh: 用魔术贴粘紧，用搭扣带固定
items.def_en: To fasten or attach something using hook-and-loop Velcro tape.
items.ex_en: Be sure to velcro the protective elbow pads securely before skating outdoors.
items.ex_zh: 在去户外滑冰之前，务必用魔术贴粘紧护肘以确保安全。

items.def_en: (+ sth) fasten tarpaulins or hatches securely with battens or fittings to withstand rough weather
items.ex_en: Sailors worked quickly to batten down the ship's hatches before the storm arrived.
items.ex_zh: 水手们在风暴来临前迅速行动，用压条把船舱盖彻底封牢。

items.def_en: (+ sth) fasten and immobilize securely using one or more straps
items.ex_en: The movers used heavy cords to strap down the furniture onto the truck.
items.ex_zh: 搬家工人用结实的绳索把家具牢牢绑紧固定在卡车上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) secure an object firmly in place using ropes, cords, or straps
items.ex_en: He didn't want to buy a house because he hated being tied down to one location.
items.ex_zh: 他不想买房，因为讨厌被束缚在同一个地方。

items.def_en: (+ down/to) To fasten, secure, or hold in place using a strap or belt.
items.ex_en: Please strap the child securely into the car safety seat before driving.
items.ex_zh: 开车前请务必用安全带把孩子稳稳固定在儿童安全座椅上。

items.def_en: (+ down/to) To tie or secure something firmly in position with cord or rope.
items.ex_en: The deckhands began to lash the remaining timber to the cargo deck.
items.ex_zh: 水手们开始用粗绳索把剩余的木材紧紧捆绑固定在货舱甲板上。

items.def_en: (carpentry) To fasten two pieces of timber together by driving nails in obliquely.
items.ex_en: The carpenter decided to toenail the upright studs to the bottom plate.
items.ex_zh: 木工决定用斜钉把直立的龙骨柱牢牢固定在底板上。

items.def_zh: 用系缆栓系牢（绳索）；给……加固夹板
items.def_en: To secure a rope to a cleat, or to strengthen something with cleats.
items.ex_en: The sailor paused to cleat the halyard securely to the wooden dock.
items.ex_zh: 水手停下脚步，用系缆栓把升降绳稳稳系紧在木码头上。

items.def_zh: （用夹板）固定（骨折或受伤部位）
items.def_en: To support and immobilize an injured bone or limb with a splint.
items.ex_en: Paramedics moved rapidly to splint his fractured leg before moving the stretcher.
items.ex_zh: 急救人员在移动担架前迅速用夹板固定住他骨折的腿部。

items.def_zh: 用挂锁锁上，用挂锁扣紧
items.def_en: To fasten or secure something firmly using a padlock.
items.ex_en: Remember to padlock the storage shed before leaving the farm for the weekend.
items.ex_zh: 周末离开农场之前，记得一定要用挂锁把储物棚牢牢锁好。

items.def_zh: 用压条（木条）固定；（尤指风暴来临前）钉牢，紧固（舱门等）
items.def_en: To fasten or secure something firmly with wooden or metal strips, especially against bad weather.
items.ex_en: The crew hurried to batten the open windows as the hurricane approached.
items.ex_zh: 随着飓风逼近，船员们急忙用压条紧固敞开的窗户。

items.def_zh: 用肚带（或带子）系紧，勒紧；确保获得，稳操胜券
items.def_en: 1. To fasten or tighten a saddle or belt securely. 2. (informal) To make certain of achieving or winning something.
items.ex_en: The cowboy stepped forward to cinch the heavy leather saddle onto his horse.
items.ex_zh: 牛仔上前一步，用肚带把沉重的皮鞍紧紧勒在马背上。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) hold or fasten an object tightly against a surface using a clamp
items.ex_en: He had to clamp down the uneven wooden board before starting the saw.
items.ex_zh: 他在启动电锯之前，必须先用夹具把不平整的木板牢牢夹紧固定。

items.def_en: (+ down/on) To hold, fix, or secure tightly with a mechanical clamp.
items.ex_en: You need to clamp the glued joints together until the adhesive dries completely.
items.ex_zh: 在胶水完全干透之前，你需要用夹具把涂了胶的接缝紧紧固定住。

groups.summary_en: Verbs detailing specialized physical interventions used to bind, clamp, tie, or anchor objects firmly to prevent movement, loosening, or detachment.
groups.summary_zh: 指使用特定工具或构件固定、系牢、锁死或稳固物体的机械/手工紧固行为。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves immobilizing structural elements against external strain (e.g. storm, transit) via anchor ropes, clamps, or binders, contrasting with 'joining' by prioritizing stability under duress.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及使用系带、绳索或扣具将物体死死锚定以抗击外界晃动或风暴，与单纯“连接”不同，它强调受力时的抗倾覆与安全锁止。
groups.nuance_en: batten down: secure deck hatches or doors against tempests (hatches / tarp / house) · strap down: immobilize payload with high-tension webbings (cargo / luggage / crate) · lash: tightly bind objects to spars using multiple cord winds (helm / mast / spar) · toenail: secure framing studs by driving nails at an angle (rafter / stud / post) · velcro: quickly fasten via micro-hook-and-loop fabric (shoes / patch / cuff)
groups.nuance_zh: batten down: 封堵舱盖扣紧防风门窗 (hatches / tarp / house) · strap down: 用高张力压紧带固定货物 (cargo / luggage / crate) · lash: 用绳索层层捆扎缚牢于立柱 (helm / mast / spar) · toenail: 建筑中斜向打钉固定梁柱 (rafter / stud / post) · velcro: 用魔术贴快速黏扣紧固 (shoes / patch / cuff)

groups.name: Give & Bestow · 给予与恩赐 (Give, Accord, Bestow)
groups.tip: 从一般给到隆重赠与

items.def_en: (+ sth) present something freely as a gift or charitable donation
items.ex_en: The bakery decided to give away unsold loaves of bread to the community shelter.
items.ex_zh: 面包店决定把未售出的面包无偿捐赠给社区收容所。

items.def_en: (+ sth) distribute items or money freely to a group of people
items.ex_en: Volunteers gathered at dawn to hand out warm meals to the displaced flood victims.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们破晓时分集合，向流离失所的洪灾灾民分发热餐。

items.def_zh: 递上，端上；提出，提供（建议等）
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) (formal) To hold out or offer something—such as advice, help, or an object—for someone to accept.
items.ex_en: The diplomat chose to proffer valuable counsel to the prime minister during the crisis.
items.ex_zh: 危机期间，这位外交官选择向首相提出宝贵的建议。

items.def_en: (+ sth) distribute or dispense things lavishly or freely
items.ex_en: The candidate loved to dish out lavish promises to everyone during his town tour.
items.ex_zh: 该候选人在小镇巡回期间，喜欢向大家大肆开出空头支票。

items.def_zh: 正式签署让渡；过户转赠
items.def_en: (+ sth) legally transfer ownership of property or rights to another person
items.ex_en: The elderly gentleman decided to sign over the family estate to his eldest daughter.
items.ex_zh: 那位老绅士决定正式签署协议，将家族庄园过户给他的长女。

items.def_zh: 给，送给；提供；交给；让步，变松
items.def_en: 1. To freely transfer possession of something to someone, or hand something over. 2. To produce, yield, or provide. 3. To bend or yield under pressure.
items.ex_en: She decided to give her vintage acoustic guitar to her most dedicated music student.
items.ex_zh: 她决定把自己的复古原声吉他送给她最专注的音乐学生。

items.def_zh: 给予，授予；与……相符合，一致
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To give or grant someone power, status, or recognition. 2. (+ with) To be consistent or in agreement with something.
items.ex_en: The committee decided to accord full diplomatic status to the visiting foreign envoy.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定授予来访的外国特使完全的外交地位。

items.def_en: 1. Past tense of give.
items.ex_en: The generous benefactor gave a massive collection of rare manuscripts to the university.
items.ex_zh: 那位慷慨的赞助人将大批珍贵手稿捐赠给了这所大学。

items.def_en: to formally give, allow, or bestow something requested or earned
items.ex_en: The municipal council agreed to grant permission for the historic library expansion project.
items.ex_zh: 市议会同意准予该历史图书馆扩建项目的施工许可。

items.def_en: 1. (+ to) (law / formal) To leave money, property, or a legacy to someone in a will after death.
items.ex_en: The scholar chose to bequeath his extensive personal library to the local university.
items.ex_zh: 这位学者选择在遗嘱中将他藏书丰富的私人图书馆遗赠给当地大学。

items.def_zh: 授予（神职人员）圣职及俸禄
items.def_en: 1. (historical / ecclesiastical) To grant a church office and its endowed income to a clergyman.
items.ex_en: The bishop decided to benefice the devoted parish priest with a substantial rural parish.
items.ex_zh: 主教决定授予这位忠诚的教区神父一处附带丰厚俸禄的乡村教区圣职。

items.def_zh: 授予；赐予（头衔、学位或荣誉）
items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to grant an honor, title, right, or favor to someone formally
items.ex_en: The university senate voted to confer an honorary doctorate upon the distinguished novelist.
items.ex_zh: 大学学术委员会投票决定授予这位著名小说家荣誉博士学位。

items.def_en: 1. (+ on/upon) (formal) To give an honor, title, gift, or right formally to someone.
items.ex_en: The monarch chose to bestow a royal knighthood upon the courageous young captain.
items.ex_zh: 君主决定将皇家骑士爵位赐予那位英勇的年轻上尉。

items.def_zh: 慷慨给予，过多地给予；过分挥霍
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/upon) To give someone a huge amount of money, praise, care, or attention generously.
items.ex_en: The doting grandmother continued to lavish excessive praise and presents upon the child.
items.ex_zh: 溺爱孩子的祖母继续对那个小孩慷慨施予过度的赞美与礼物。

items.def_en: (+ with) to provide with a permanent fund or establish through a generous bequest
items.ex_en: The wealthy entrepreneur resolved to endow the research laboratory with a substantial fund.
items.ex_zh: 那位富有的企业家决定为该研究实验室资助一笔数额可观的永久基金。

groups.summary_en: This frame spans the continuum of giving or transferring assets, privileges, or honors, escalating from neutral baseline transfers to formal bestowals and lavish endowments.
groups.summary_zh: 表示交付、赋予或赠予所有权与荣誉，程度由普通移转升至盛大恩赐。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves transferring title or possession across a social hierarchy, contrasting with plain 'giving' through status disparities, ceremonial protocol, or non-negotiable deed transfer.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及在社会等级或正式契约框架下转让财物所有权或权力，与平级“赠与”不同，它彰显身份层级、礼仪规范或法定割让。
groups.nuance_en: give away: uncompensated surrender of property or secrets (prizes / secret / assets) · proffer: courteous tentative offering for acceptance (resignation / apology / hand) · sign over: formal legal conveyance of deed or ownership (rights / deed / estate) · accord: formal institutional granting of status or privilege (praise / rights / respect) · bestow: dignified confersion of an honor from above (title / medal / blessing)
groups.nuance_zh: give away: 无偿出让财产或不慎泄露 (prizes / secret / assets) · proffer: 谦逊恭敬地呈递以待接纳 (resignation / apology / hand) · sign over: 签署法律契约正式割让权益 (rights / deed / estate) · accord: 依礼遇或规范正式给予 (praise / rights / respect) · bestow: 居高临下地赐予殊荣或祝福 (title / medal / blessing)

groups.name: Permit to Compel · 许可、规约与强制
groups.tip: 从规劝到硬性强制

items.def_en: (+ sth) To officially approve or grant formal permission for something
items.ex_en: The regional director will finally sign off on the revised budget proposal tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 区域主管明天终于会正式签署批准这份修订后的预算方案。

items.def_en: to allow someone to do something, especially by an official rule or law
items.ex_en: The strict park regulations do not permit visitors to kindle fires after sundown.
items.ex_zh: 严格的公园管理条例不准许游客在日落之后生火。

items.def_zh: 可以（表示许可）；可能，也许；祝愿
items.def_en: 1. Used to ask for or give permission to do something. 2. Used to express possibility or likelihood.
items.ex_en: Registered participants may leave their luggage in the conference hall overnight without charge.
items.ex_zh: 注册参会人员可以将行李免费存放在会议厅过夜。

items.def_en: 1. To allow or permit someone to do something. 2. To rent out a house, room, or piece of land.
items.ex_en: The strict librarian refused to let the noisy students enter the study hall.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的图书管理员拒绝允许喧闹的学生进入自习厅。

items.def_zh: 允许，准许；使成为可能；留出，拨出
items.def_en: 1. To give permission for someone to do something. 2. To make it possible for something to happen or be done.
items.ex_en: The museum guards do not allow guests to touch any ancient ceramic artifacts.
items.ex_zh: 博物馆保安不允许游客触摸任何古代陶瓷文物。

items.def_zh: 应该，应当；可能，按理会；如果，万一
items.def_en: 1. Used to state what is proper, advisable, or morally required. 2. Used to express that something is probable or expected.
items.ex_en: All employees should review the updated safety protocol before starting their morning shift.
items.ex_zh: 所有员工在开始早班工作前都应当温习最新的安全规程。

items.def_en: to demand that something must be done according to a law, rule, or contract
items.ex_en: Federal labor regulations strictly require companies to provide adequate protective gear to workers.
items.ex_zh: 联邦劳动法规严格规定企业必须向工人提供充足的防护装备。

items.def_zh: 迫使，强迫；使感激；施惠，帮忙
items.def_en: 1. To force someone to do something because of a law, duty, or necessity. 2. To help or do a favor for someone.
items.ex_en: Urgent financial difficulties now oblige the municipal council to suspend the bridge project.
items.ex_zh: 紧迫的财政困难如今迫使市议会暂停这项大桥工程。

items.def_en: (+ sb into sth) To compel or coerce someone into performing a duty or service
items.ex_en: The military regime sought to press rural villagers into compulsory road construction labor.
items.ex_zh: 军政权企图强行迫使农村村民加入强制性的筑路劳役。

items.def_en: 1. Used to express that something is necessary or required by rule, law, or duty. 2. Used to express that something is logically certain.
items.ex_en: All international travelers must present a valid passport before boarding the transatlantic flight.
items.ex_zh: 所有国际旅客在登上跨大西洋航班之前必须出示有效护照。

items.def_zh: 强迫，迫使；用力推开，强行打开
items.def_en: 1. To compel someone to do something against their will using physical strength, authority, or pressure. 2. To push or move something using physical effort.
items.ex_en: Severe floodwaters began to force residents from their homes in the lower valley.
items.ex_zh: 汹涌的洪水开始迫使低洼山谷的居民撤离家园。

items.def_en: 1. To force or oblige someone to do something. 2. To evoke or bring about a particular reaction or feeling by having strong authority or quality.
items.ex_en: Overwhelming circumstantial evidence will compel the corrupt official to resign from his post.
items.ex_zh: 压倒性的旁证将迫使这名腐败官员从其职位上辞职。

items.def_zh: 使承担义务，迫使；施恩惠于
items.def_en: To bind someone legally, morally, or socially to do something.
items.ex_en: The binding contractual terms obligate the developer to finish the complex by December.
items.ex_zh: 具有约束力的合同条款迫使开发商必须在十二月前完工该建筑群。

items.def_en: (+ sb into sth) To pressure or coerce someone into doing something hastily or against their will
items.ex_en: Aggressive investors tried to railroad the timid board into approving the risky takeover.
items.ex_zh: 激进的投资者试图仓促逼迫胆小的董事会就范，批准那项高风险收购。

items.def_en: (+ into) to force someone to do something that they do not want to do, through threats or pressure
items.ex_en: The extortion syndicate attempted to coerce the small business owner into paying protection.
items.ex_zh: 敲诈勒索团伙企图胁迫这位小企业主交纳保护费。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scale frame express degrees of deontic pressure and authority imposed upon an agent. They scale upwards from granting permission (may, allow, let), to normative recommendation (should), to legal/moral obligation (obligate, oblige, must), and finally to inescapable coercion (compel, force).
groups.summary_zh: 从给予许可、道义建议，递增至法定规约与绝对强迫。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema charts the deontic continuum governing an agent's agency—from negative non-interference up to coercive mandate, contrasting with descriptive statements by dictating normative bounds.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式勾勒出规范性约束的道义阶梯——从消极的不干预、准许直至强制性施压，与纯粹的陈述事实不同，它施加行为准则与义务规范。
groups.nuance_en: sign off on: formal bureaucratic ratification of an action (budget / plan / proposal) · allow: permissive tolerance by non-intervention (entry / variation / pet) · require: strict imperative precondition set by rule (qualification / permit / license) · oblige: imposing an inescapable moral or legal duty (party / debtor / host) · compel: overwhelming overpowering force driving compliance (witness / surrender / reform)
groups.nuance_zh: sign off on: 官僚流程上的正式签字核准 (budget / plan / proposal) · allow: 消极不干预式的许可或容忍 (entry / variation / pet) · require: 规则设定的必要前置条件 (qualification / permit / license) · oblige: 施加不可推卸的法律或道义职责 (party / debtor / host) · compel: 强力压迫下迫使就范 (witness / surrender / reform)

groups.name: Resound & Sound Out · 物件发声与鸣响
groups.tip: 各种声响与发声方式

items.def_zh: 发出飒飒声，发出沙沙声，呜呜作响
items.def_en: (literary) To make a soft, moaning, or rustling sound, like wind blowing through trees or waves on a shore.
items.ex_en: A melancholic autumn wind began to sough softly through the barren pine branches.
items.ex_zh: 凄凉的秋风开始在光秃秃的松树枝间发出飒飒的低鸣。

items.def_en: (of a clock or bells) ring together or strike to mark the hour
items.ex_en: Across the courtyard, three grandfather clocks chime in together to strike midnight precisely.
items.ex_zh: 院子对面，三座落地大钟齐鸣，准确地报出午夜钟声。

items.def_zh: 发声，鸣响；使发声，鸣响；听起来；试探
items.def_en: 1. To make a noise, or cause something to produce a sound. 2. To give a specified impression when heard.
items.ex_en: The vigilant sentry hastened to sound the brass horn as the cavalry approached.
items.ex_zh: 随着骑兵的逼近，警惕的哨兵急忙吹响铜号。
items.ex2_en: The loud fire alarm sounded across the school building during the morning drill.
items.ex2_zh: 在早间演习期间，刺耳的火警警报响彻了整栋教学楼。

items.def_zh: 格格作响；发出连串撞击声
items.def_en: [I/T] to make a series of short, sharp knocking sounds when shaken or moved
items.ex_en: Strong gusts of wind began to rattle the loose metal shutters outside continuously.
items.ex_zh: 强劲的阵风开始让室外松动的金属百叶窗连续格格作响。
items.ex2_en: The old wooden windowpanes rattle loudly whenever a heavy truck passes outside.
items.ex2_zh: 每当重型卡车从外面开过时，老旧的木窗玻璃就会哗啦啦作响。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a clear, ringing sound when struck, like a set of bells or clock
items.ex_en: The tall brass clock will chime melodiously on the hour throughout the day.
items.ex_zh: 那座高大的黄铜钟会在整点发出悦耳的鸣响，贯穿一整天。
items.ex2_en: The playful wind chimed the hanging bells softly under the roof eaves.
items.ex2_zh: 调皮的微风在屋檐下轻轻敲响了悬挂的铃铛。

items.def_zh: 发出劈啪声，发出咔啦声
items.def_en: To make a series of short, sharp, snapping or popping noises, like dry wood burning.
items.ex_en: Dry pine logs began to crackle brightly inside the stone fireplace all evening.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的松木柴整个晚上都在石头壁炉里欢快地发出劈啪声。

items.def_zh: 发出嗒嗒声，发出马蹄得得声；嗒嗒作响地走
items.def_en: To make the hollow knocking sound of a horse's hoof hitting a hard road, or move with this sound.
items.ex_en: The steady hooves began to clop along the cobblestones under the dim lamplight.
items.ex_zh: 稳健的马蹄在昏暗的街灯下沿鹅卵石路面发出得得的声响。

items.def_zh: （渡鸦或野鹅）发出低沉粗厉的叫声，呱呱叫
items.def_en: (especially of a raven or wild goose) To utter a deep, hoarse, croaking cry.
items.ex_en: A lone black raven perched high upon the gallows to cronk its mournful cry.
items.ex_zh: 一只孤独的黑渡鸦高栖在绞刑架上，发出低沉粗厉的哀鸣。

items.def_zh: 响亮地响起；发出清脆回响
items.def_en: sound loudly, clearly, or resoundingly across an area
items.ex_en: A single gunshot seemed to ring out sharply across the desolate snowy valley.
items.ex_zh: 一声清脆的枪响似乎在荒凉的雪谷中尖锐地回荡开来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to sound with slow, solemn, regular strokes, especially of a large funeral or church bell
items.ex_en: The cathedral bell began to toll slowly for the fallen soldiers at dusk.
items.ex_zh: 黄昏时分，大教堂的沉重钟声开始为阵亡将士缓慢哀鸣。
items.ex2_en: The sad village priest tolled the heavy bronze bell for the solemn funeral.
items.ex2_zh: 悲伤的乡村神父为庄严的葬礼敲响了沉重的铜钟。

items.def_zh: 咔嗒咔嗒作响；使哐当乱响；喧闹地移动
items.def_en: To make a continuous loud, rattling sound by striking against something, or cause objects to make this noise.
items.ex_en: The nervous waiter caused the porcelain plates to clatter loudly on the tray.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的服务员让托盘上的瓷盘发出一连串刺耳的咔嗒碰撞声。
items.ex2_en: The plastic storage boxes clattered down the wooden stairs during the sudden earthquake.
items.ex2_zh: 在突如其来的地震中，塑料收纳箱哗啦啦地滚下了木楼梯。

items.def_zh: （风笛等）发出尖厉响亮的声音；高声鸣响
items.def_en: (especially of bagpipes) To make a shrill, piercing musical sound.
items.ex_en: The highland bagpipes began to skirl proudly as the Scottish regiment marched past.
items.ex_zh: 苏格兰军团行进经过时，高地风笛骄傲地发出了尖厉嘹亮的鸣响。

items.def_en: (of bells or thunder) ring out loudly and solemnly
items.ex_en: Ancient cathedral chimes peal out across the misty harbor to welcome the dawn.
items.ex_zh: 古老大教堂的钟声在薄雾笼罩的港口上空大声轰鸣，迎接黎明。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a loud, resonant metallic sound
items.ex_en: The heavy iron gates would clang shut behind every arriving prisoner each night.
items.ex_zh: 每天夜里，沉重的铁门都会在每位新到的囚犯身后哐啷一声关上。
items.ex2_en: The angry chef clanged the heavy metal pot down on the steel counter.
items.ex2_zh: 愤怒的厨师把沉重的金属锅哐当一声砸在不锈钢操作台上。

items.def_zh: 洪亮地鸣响，震响；使大声鸣响
items.def_en: To ring or sound loudly and resonantly, as of bells, thunder, or laughter.
items.ex_en: Great bells peal from the gothic tower, echoing through the empty city squares.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的钟声从哥特式塔楼中洪亮地震响，回荡在空旷的城市广场。
items.ex2_en: The energetic church bellringer pealed the massive bronze chimes to mark the victory.
items.ex2_zh: 精力充沛的教堂敲钟人敲响了巨大的铜钟以庆祝胜利。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent inchoative or continuous auditory emissions produced by natural phenomena, metal, bells, or hard surfaces. Nuances distinguish between harsh repetitive clicks (clatter, clop, crackle), wind whispers (sough), bell rings (peal, ring), and high-pitched piping (skirl).
groups.summary_zh: 物体撞击、风声刮拂或器物钟乐所发出特有节奏与质地的声响。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema entails inanimate physical entities generating characteristic acoustic vibrations via impact, resonance, or friction, contrasting with biological 'vocalizing' by stemming from material acoustics.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及非生物材料受撞击、共振或摩擦作用而产生特有的声学振动，与生物“发声”不同，它体现为材质特有的物理鸣响与谐振。
groups.nuance_en: clop: hollow muffled impact of hooves on firm ground (hooves / pony / horse) · crackle: rapid train of sharp dry snapping micro-explosions (fire / radio / twigs) · chime: clear resonant metallic pinging of tuned bells (clock / bell / glasses) · rattle: rapid succession of loose dry impacts inside a casing (bones / windows / engine) · sough: deep murmuring moan of wind through branches (pines / wind / boughs)
groups.nuance_zh: clop: 马蹄踏在硬地上发出的沉闷笃笃声 (hooves / pony / horse) · crackle: 噼啪碎裂或无线电杂音 (fire / radio / twigs) · chime: 悦耳清脆的金属撞钟鸣音 (clock / bell / glasses) · rattle: 松动部件碰撞发出的格格作响 (bones / windows / engine) · sough: 风过林莽发出的低沉飒飒呼啸 (pines / wind / boughs)

groups.name: Scare & Terrify · 惊吓与威慑 (Scare, Frighten, Terrify, Petrify)
groups.tip: 主动施加恐惧或吓唬他人的动作

items.def_en: To cause a sudden shock or alarm that makes someone jump or twitch
items.ex_en: The sudden thunderclap did not fail to startle the sleeping infant in the cradle.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的雷声顿时让摇篮里熟睡的婴儿吓了一跳。

items.def_en: (informal) To frighten a person or animal, making them skittish or nervous
items.ex_en: Sudden flashing camera lights would easily spook the nervous mare inside the stall.
items.ex_zh: 照相机突然闪烁的强光很容易吓坏马厩里那匹神经质的母马。
items.ex2_en: Skittish deer spook easily at the sudden snapping sound of dry twigs nearby.
items.ex2_zh: 胆小的鹿听到附近干树枝断裂的猝发声很容易受惊。

items.def_zh: 使毛骨悚然；吓得起鸡皮疙瘩
items.def_en: (+ sb) cause someone to feel nervous, repulsed, or uneasy through creepiness
items.ex_en: The way that abandoned house looks at dusk really creeps me out.
items.ex_zh: 那栋废弃房屋在黄昏时的模样真让我心里发毛。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) cause someone or something to leave or stay away through fear
items.ex_en: The loud alarm system was installed to scare off any opportunistic nocturnal burglars.
items.ex_zh: 安装高分贝警报系统是为了吓跑任何伺机作案的夜间窃贼。

items.def_en: (+ sb) fill someone with an unsettling, eerie sense of fear
items.ex_en: Those bizarre creaking sounds in the attic really spook out the younger children.
items.ex_zh: 阁楼里那些离奇的吱嘎怪声真把年幼的孩子们吓得毛骨悚然。

items.def_en: To make someone feel afraid, anxious, or shocked.
items.ex_en: Sudden loud bangs can easily frighten the rescue dogs during their outdoor training.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的巨响在户外训练中很容易使这些搜救犬受到惊吓。

items.def_en: To make someone feel frightened or nervous; to become frightened.
items.ex_en: Ghost stories told around the campfire never fail to scare the younger scouts.
items.ex_zh: 营火旁讲述的鬼故事总能把年幼的童子军吓得提心吊胆。
items.ex2_en: Young horses scare easily whenever unfamiliar shadows move along the forest trail.
items.ex2_zh: 每当陌生的阴影沿着林间小径移动时，年轻的马匹就很容易受惊。

items.def_en: To frighten or overawe someone, especially in order to make them do what one wants
items.ex_en: The ruthless prosecutor tried to intimidate the key witness during the intense cross-examination.
items.ex_zh: 无情的检察官在激烈的交叉质询中企图恫吓关键证人。

items.raw_cluster: 恐吓与使恐惧 Frighten & Terrify
items.def_zh: 使慌乱，使胆怯，使丧失勇气
items.def_en: To make someone lose confidence, courage, or emotional composure.
items.ex_en: The ominous silence of the abandoned mansion served to unnerve the fearless explorers.
items.ex_zh: 废弃大宅那令人不安的死寂让那些无畏的探险家们阵脚大乱。

items.def_en: (+ sb) make someone extremely frightened, panicky, or agitated
items.ex_en: The eerie whispers in the corridor will freak out anyone exploring the ruins alone.
items.ex_zh: 走廊里怪异的低语声会让任何单独探索遗迹的人吓得魂飞魄散。
items.ex2_en: Nervous first-time drivers freak out easily during heavy thunderstorm downpours on highways.
items.ex2_zh: 新手司机在高速公路上遭遇暴风雨倾盆时很容易惊慌失措。

items.def_en: (archaic or literary) To frighten, terrify, or alarm someone suddenly.
items.ex_en: The ghostly apparition did sorely affright the lone sentry standing guard at night.
items.ex_zh: 那幽灵般的幻影使夜间站岗的孤独哨兵大受惊吓。

items.def_zh: 使极度恐惧，恐吓，使极其害怕
items.def_en: To fill someone with extreme fear; to frighten severely.
items.ex_en: The sudden engine explosion above the ocean began to terrify all the passengers.
items.ex_zh: 大洋上空突发的引擎爆炸让所有乘客陷入极度恐慌之中。

items.def_en: To render someone unable to move or act due to overwhelming fear
items.ex_en: Sudden sheer dread seemed to paralyze the trapped mountain climber on the ledge.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的极度恐惧似乎让困在悬崖岩架上的登山者吓呆了。

items.def_zh: 恐吓，威胁；实行恐怖统治
items.def_en: To fill people with extreme fear by using violence or threats of violence.
items.ex_en: Ruthless armed cartels continue to terrorize rural farming communities across the northern province.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的武装贩毒集团继续在北部各省恐吓并威胁农村农业社区。

items.raw_cluster: 恐吓与使恐惧 Frighten & Terrify
items.def_zh: 使吓呆，使吓得动弹不得；（使）石化，（使）僵化
items.def_en: 1. To frighten someone so severely that they are unable to move or think. 2. (geology) To change organic matter into stone or a stony substance.
items.ex_en: The terrifying roar of the hidden predator seemed to petrify the weary traveler.
items.ex_zh: 潜藏猛兽那惊心动魄的咆哮声似乎让疲惫的旅人吓得动弹不得。
items.ex2_en: Shy wild deer petrify instantly when sudden bright headlights shine across the road.
items.ex2_zh: 当刺目的车前灯突然照亮马路时，害羞的野鹿立刻吓得动弹不得。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe inducing varying degrees of acute fear, dread, or shock in a sentient experiencer, from sudden alarm to paralyzing dread.
groups.summary_zh: 通过不同方式引起对方剧烈惊惧，从乍现的心慌到令人僵化的极度恐慌。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves an external stimulus provoking defensive terror or disarming an agent's confidence, contrasting with generic 'displeasing' by activating visceral threat instincts.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及外部危险刺激引发受试者的防卫性惊骇或瓦解其行动勇气，与一般的“惹恼”不同，它直接触发本能的危机警觉与应激恐惧。
groups.nuance_en: startle: sudden reflexive reflex from unexpected sensory spike (deer / bystander / driver) · spook: triggering nervous jumpiness or bolting in skittish agents (horse / markets / cattle) · creep out: slow unease born of uncanny or repulsive stimuli (doll / stranger / silence) · intimidate: deliberate deterrence via display of power or menace (witness / rival / debtor) · terrify: paralyzing saturation with sheer existential dread (hostage / victim / child)
groups.nuance_zh: startle: 突发刺激导致的惊跳反射 (deer / bystander / driver) · spook: 受惊炸窝或令敏感者神经紧绷 (horse / markets / cattle) · creep out: 诡异反常事物令人心头发毛 (doll / stranger / silence) · intimidate: 施展权威或凶相进行威慑压制 (witness / rival / debtor) · terrify: 令人惊骇欲绝或吓到瘫痪 (hostage / victim / child)

groups.name: Boost & Amplify · 提升与增强 (Raise, Enhance, Boost, Amplify)
groups.tip: 把数值强度或高度往上拉升

items.def_en: To raise something to a higher position, level, or moral standard
items.ex_en: The ambitious director sought to elevate theatrical production standards across the entire country.
items.ex_zh: 雄心勃勃的导演力图将全国范围内的戏剧制作水平提升到新高度。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make something stronger, larger, or more effective
items.ex_en: The border agency plans to beef up border security checks before the holidays.
items.ex_zh: 边境管理部门计划在节前加强边境安检力度。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to increase the level, volume, or intensity of something
items.ex_en: The campaign manager wanted to crank up advertising efforts before the final election.
items.ex_zh: 竞选经理希望在最终选举前大幅加大广告宣传攻势。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to increase the speed, intensity, or rate of effort of something
items.ex_en: The hospital had to step up security measures following the recent incident.
items.ex_zh: 在最近的事件发生后，医院不得不加强安保措施。

items.def_zh: 提高，增加；举起，抬高；筹集；抚养
items.def_en: 1. To increase the level, amount, or strength of something. 2. To lift or move something to a higher position.
items.ex_en: The central bank decided to raise benchmark lending rates to combat stubborn inflation.
items.ex_zh: 中央银行决定提高基准贷款利率以应对居高不下的通货膨胀。

items.def_en: To help something increase, improve, or become more successful.
items.ex_en: The clever tax incentive program will boost small business investments in depressed areas.
items.ex_zh: 这一巧妙的税收激励计划将促进对萧条地区小型企业的投资。

items.def_zh: 提高，增强，增进（质量、价值或吸引力）
items.def_en: To increase or further improve the good quality, value, or status of someone or something.
items.ex_en: The innovative digital filters definitely enhance the visual clarity of the satellite imagery.
items.ex_zh: 这种创新的数字滤镜无疑提高了该卫星图像的视觉清晰度。

items.def_zh: 大幅提高，猛增（价格、利率等）；徒步旅行
items.def_en: 1. To increase a price, rate, or tax sharply. 2. To go for a long walk, especially in the countryside.
items.ex_en: The greedy landlord decided to hike our rent by another twenty percent this month.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的房东决定这个月把我们的房租猛涨百分之二十。

items.def_en: To become or make something stronger, more intense, or higher (such as feelings, tension, or contrast).
items.ex_en: Recent border skirmishes have heightened diplomatic tensions between the two neighboring states.
items.ex_zh: 近期的边境冲突加剧了这两个邻国之间的外交紧张局势。
items.ex2_en: Tensions heighten noticeably as both rival factions prepare for the upcoming national vote.
items.ex2_zh: 随着两个对立派系为即将到来的全国投票做准备，紧张局势显著加剧。

items.def_zh: 放大，增强；（用透镜等）放大；夸大
items.def_en: 1. To make a sound, effect, or problem greater, stronger, or more serious. 2. To make something look larger than it really is, especially by using a lens or microscope.
items.ex_en: Inadequate communication will only magnify existing operational difficulties across all departments.
items.ex_zh: 沟通不力只会加剧所有部门现有的运转困难。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to substantially increase or expand the volume, rate, or level of something
items.ex_en: The factory will ramp up output next week to meet holiday demand.
items.ex_zh: 工厂下周将大幅提升产量，以满足假日期间的需求。
items.ex2_en: Emergency medical operations ramp up dramatically across the city during the flu season.
items.ex2_zh: 在流感季节，全市的紧急医疗救助行动大幅增加。

items.def_en: To increase or cause to increase rapidly in intensity or extent
items.ex_en: Officials feared that minor border disputes might escalate into a full-scale armed conflict.
items.ex_zh: 官员们担心微小的边境争端可能会逐步升级为全面的武装冲突。
items.ex2_en: Irresponsible media coverage could escalate local civil protests into dangerous violent riots.
items.ex2_zh: 不负责任的媒体报道可能会使当地民间抗议升级为危险的暴力骚乱。

items.def_en: To become or make something greater, stronger, or more extreme
items.ex_en: Authorities anticipate that the fierce winter storms will intensify over the coming days.
items.ex_zh: 当局预计这场猛烈的冬季暴风雪在未来数日内还会加剧。
items.ex2_en: The political debate will intensify public discussion about environmental protection across the country.
items.ex2_zh: 这场政治辩论将在全国范围内激化关于环境保护的公众讨论。

items.def_zh: 放大（声音、信号等）；增强，扩大；阐述，详述
items.def_en: 1. To make a sound, electrical signal, or effect louder or stronger. 2. To explain, expand on, or add details to a statement or idea.
items.ex_en: The newly installed auditorium speakers amplify acoustic guitars with exceptional clarity.
items.ex_zh: 礼堂新安装的扬声器能以极佳的清晰度放大原声吉他的声音。

groups.summary_en: Verbs depicting an upward scaling in degree, volume, value, or efficacy, ascending from simple elevation to intense qualitative or acoustic magnification.
groups.summary_zh: 描述数量、品质、强度或声量的级联上升，从简单调高至倍数级放大。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves driving an operating parameter, intensity, or magnitude upward beyond standard operating thresholds, contrasting with neutral 'moving' by aiming for heightened vigor or output.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及强力拉升运行参数、强度或量级，使其超越常规基准，与中立的“移动”不同，它追求输出效能的显著增益与强化。
