groups.nuance_en: puzzle: inducing mental labor to resolve an ambiguous or illogical problem (detectives / observers / scholars) · baffle: utterly defeating comprehension through inexplicability (experts / doctors / scientists) · mystify: confounding completely by presenting what appears magical or impossible (audiences / critics / onlookers) · bemuse: generating mild, detached, and often amused bewilderment (visitors / listeners / public) · throw off: suddenly breaking someone's concentration, rhythm, or cognitive trajectory (timing / balance / pursuers)
groups.nuance_zh: puzzle: 因疑难或反常让人费解琢磨 (detectives / observers / scholars) · baffle: 极度不可理喻以致彻底难倒行家 (experts / doctors / scientists) · mystify: 如魔术般神秘莫测让人摸不着头脑 (audiences / critics / onlookers) · bemuse: 使人陷入略带困惑与迷茫的出神状态 (visitors / listeners / public) · throw off: 突然打乱人的思绪、步调或节奏 (timing / balance / pursuers)

groups.name: Convey & Haul Goods · 载运与货运 (Transport, Truck, Freight)
groups.tip: 车辆船只运送物流

items.def_en: [I/T] to send or transport goods by sea, road, rail, or air
items.ex_en: Our warehouse will ship your order within three business days of purchase.
items.ex_zh: 我们的仓库将在您购买后的三个工作日内发运商品。

items.def_zh: 用公共汽车运送；乘公共汽车出行
items.def_en: To transport passengers by bus, or to travel by bus.
items.ex_en: The municipal district arranged to bus the school children across town safely.
items.ex_zh: 市政学区安排用公共汽车将这些学童安全运送到城市另一端。

items.def_en: To carry or convey people or goods from one place to another by vehicle, ship, or aircraft.
items.ex_en: Heavy cargo planes transport vital medical supplies to remote disaster zones daily.
items.ex_zh: 大型货运飞机每天向偏远的灾区运送重要的医疗物资。

items.def_zh: 用卡车运送；驾驶卡车；以物易物
items.def_en: To convey goods by truck, or to drive a truck.
items.ex_en: Local distributors truck fresh dairy produce from regional farms to supermarkets daily.
items.ex_zh: 当地分销商每天用卡车将新鲜乳制品从本地农场运往超市。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to transport or take someone or something away, especially roughly or in large quantities
items.ex_en: Armed police arrived promptly to cart off all the confiscated counterfeit merchandise.
items.ex_zh: 武装警察迅速赶到，将所有没收的假冒商品悉数拉走。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to transport a heavy load or bulk goods away from a place
items.ex_en: Contractors used heavy flatbed trucks to haul away broken concrete and debris.
items.ex_zh: 承包商使用重型平板卡车运走了破碎的混凝土和建筑垃圾。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to send cargo or goods away to another destination
items.ex_en: The distribution center will ship out all backordered items early tomorrow morning.
items.ex_zh: 配送中心将于明早发运所有先前缺货积压的商品。

items.def_en: to carry or move a heavy load or bulk goods in a vehicle over a long distance
items.ex_en: Freight trains haul immense loads of iron ore across the arid continent.
items.ex_zh: 货运列车穿越干旱的大陆，长途运输巨量的铁矿石。

items.def_en: to transport people or goods by boat, aircraft, or vehicle over a short regular route
items.ex_en: Small water taxis ferry daily commuters across the busy harbor every morning.
items.ex_zh: 小型水上出租车每天早晨在繁忙的港口间往返摆渡通勤旅客。

items.def_zh: 用大车运送；费力搬运，运载
items.def_en: To carry or transport something heavy or cumbersome in a cart or with effort.
items.ex_en: Volunteers had to cart heavy bags of donated clothes into the hall.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们不得不费力地把沉重的捐赠衣物袋运进大厅里。

items.def_zh: 以货运运输；给（车辆、船只等）装货
items.def_en: To transport goods by cargo ship, aircraft, train, or truck.
items.ex_en: Global logistics agencies freight valuable electronic equipment overseas by dedicated air transports.
items.ex_zh: 全球物流机构通过专用航空货运将贵重的电子设备运往海外。

items.def_en: To ship or transport cargo again, or forward goods to another destination.
items.ex_en: The damaged parcel returned to the depot before we could reship it.
items.ex_zh: 在我们能够重新发运之前，受损的包裹又被退回了仓库。

items.def_zh: 转运，换装（从一种运输工具转到另一种）
items.def_en: To transfer cargo from one ship, vehicle, or conveyance to another for onward transit.
items.ex_en: Port workers must transship the container freight onto river barges for inland transit.
items.ex_zh: 港口工人必须将集装箱货物转运到内河驳船上进行内地运输。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the commercial or physical conveyance of freight, cargo, or passengers via specialized vehicular modes and handling stages.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过汽车、卡车或船舶等工具对货物与旅客进行专业承运与中转。
groups.desc_en: Physically shifting bulk cargo, freight, or people across distances via heavy commercial vehicles or organized logistics, distinct from manual personal carrying.
groups.desc_zh: 依托重型车辆或物流通道跨距离批量调度转运货物或人员，区别于轻便的人力手提携行。
groups.nuance_en: transport: broad, generic conveyance of items or persons from one location to another (goods / passengers / troops) · haul: moving heavy, bulky loads over road or rail with sustained mechanical effort (timber / coal / freight) · ship: dispatching cargo via commercial maritime, air, or postal freight networks (orders / containers / goods) · truck: conveying loads overland primarily by commercial road lorry (produce / supplies / gravel) · haul away: dragging off discarded waste or cleared debris from a site (debris / wreckage / trash)
groups.nuance_zh: transport: 最通用的运输货品、人员或物资 (goods / passengers / troops) · haul: 动用重载工具吃力拖运大宗重工业物资或重物 (timber / coal / freight) · ship: 通过集装箱海运、空运或快递网络发货 (orders / containers / goods) · truck: 采用公路卡车长途或短途货运 (produce / supplies / gravel) · haul away: 将现场清理出的废料、残骸运离拉走 (debris / wreckage / trash)

groups.name: Cut & Slice · 切割与修剖 (Slit, Carve, Julienne)
groups.tip: 用刀刃切片、修剪或开切缺口

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut something into smaller pieces using a knife or sharp blade
items.ex_en: The sous chef used a heavy cleaver to cut up beef flank.
items.ex_zh: 副厨师长用一把沉重的剁刀把牛腩切成了小块。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to slice something completely into thin pieces or portions
items.ex_en: Please slice up those ripe red tomatoes before dressing the garden salad.
items.ex_zh: 在给田园沙拉浇调料汁之前，请把那些熟透的红西红柿切成薄片。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove the edges or unwanted parts of something by cutting
items.ex_en: Carefully trim off any excess fat from the pork chops before seasoning.
items.ex_zh: 调味之前，请仔细将猪排上多余的肥肉修剪掉。

items.def_en: To cut something into thin, flat pieces, or to cut cleanly through something with a sharp blade.
items.ex_en: Use a sharp serrated knife to slice the freshly baked sourdough bread.
items.ex_zh: 用一把锋利的锯齿刀将新鲜出炉的酸面团面包切片。

items.def_zh: 将（肉、鱼或虾等）从中间切开摊平（成蝶状）
items.def_en: (cooking) To split a piece of meat, fish, or shrimp almost completely in half and spread it flat before cooking.
items.ex_en: The cook demonstrated how to butterfly the raw chicken breast before grilling.
items.ex_zh: 厨师示范了如何在烧烤前将生鸡胸肉纵向切开摊平。

items.def_en: 1. To make something neat or tidy by cutting away unwanted or irregular parts. 2. To reduce the amount, number, or size of something.
items.ex_en: The diligent gardener decided to trim the overgrown boxwood hedge this weekend.
items.ex_zh: 勤劳的园丁决定在这个周末修剪过度生长的黄杨绿篱。

items.def_en: to make a long, narrow cut or opening in something
items.ex_en: The warehouse clerk used a sharp utility knife to slit the tape.
items.ex_zh: 仓库管理员用一把锋利的美工刀划开了封箱胶带。

items.def_zh: 切成薄片（或细长条）；分裂成细碎片
items.def_en: To cut or split something into small, thin, narrow pieces.
items.ex_en: Delicate moonbeams slivered the quiet water into shards of shimmering bright silver.
items.ex_zh: 皎洁的月光将平静的水面割裂成片片微光闪烁的银鳞。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut a large piece of meat or material into portions or slices
items.ex_en: Dad picked up the carving knife to carve up the roasted turkey.
items.ex_zh: 爸爸拿起切肉刀，将烤火鸡分切成一块块肉片。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cut cooked meat into slices, or to shape an object by cutting away material
items.ex_en: He learned how to carve tender roast beef into uniformly thin slices.
items.ex_zh: 他学会了如何将鲜嫩的烤牛肉切成厚薄均匀的薄片。

items.def_en: to cut or tear something into narrow, ragged strips
items.ex_en: The cook told the kitchen assistant to shred the iceberg lettuce finely.
items.ex_zh: 厨师吩咐厨房助手把卷心莴苣细细地切成菜丝。

items.def_en: to cut food (especially vegetables) into thin, matchstick-like strips
items.ex_en: Her delicate fingers julienned crisp carrots into exceedingly thin ribbons of orange.
items.ex_zh: 她纤巧的手指将爽脆的胡萝卜切成细若发丝的橙色细条。

items.def_en: (formal) To cut into a surface, especially with a sharp surgical instrument; to carve or engrave words or designs.
items.ex_en: The skilled surgeon prepared to incise the tissue along the marked guideline.
items.ex_zh: 技艺精湛的外科医生准备沿着标记好的划线切开组织。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote specific techniques of cutting, dividing, or trimming food or materials using sharp blades, defined by the geometry, thinness, or purpose of the cut.
groups.summary_zh: 指用锋利刃具按特定几何厚度、剖开方式或目的对食材或材料进行裁切剖理。
groups.desc_en: Penetrating or parting material into portions using a bladed edge along a path, distinct from tearing, snapping, or blunt crushing.
groups.desc_zh: 以利刃沿特定走向割开或分离物质，区别于撕裂、折断或钝击粉碎。
groups.nuance_en: cut: general division or penetration with an edged instrument (paper / rope / finger) · slice: drawing a blade smoothly across to yield broad, even, flat portions (bread / ham / pie) · slit: making a narrow, clean, linear incision through a thin membrane or surface (throat / envelope / fabric) · trim: neatly shaving or clipping edges to tidy, shape, or reduce excess (fat / hedges / hair) · butterfly: splitting meat or fish horizontally almost in half and unfolding it flat (chops / shrimp / chicken breast)
groups.nuance_zh: cut: 最通用的刀刃切断、割开或裁切 (paper / rope / finger) · slice: 平稳下刀切出整齐均匀的薄片 (bread / ham / pie) · slit: 在薄膜或表面上划开一条窄长口子 (throat / envelope / fabric) · trim: 修剪边缘多余部分以使之整洁 (fat / hedges / hair) · butterfly: 将肉类从中间横剖留边展开成蝶翼状 (chops / shrimp / chicken breast)

groups.name: Discolor & Blanch · 变色与褪色 (Discolor, Whiten, Blacken)
groups.tip: 光照岁月让光彩渐失泛白褪色

items.def_en: to gradually lose brightness, vividness of color, or visual distinctness
items.ex_en: The vibrant colors of the antique watercolor will fade away under sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 这幅古董水彩画鲜艳的色彩在阳光曝晒下会逐渐褪色。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to lose color, or cause fabric or a surface to fade and become pale through washing or exposure
items.ex_en: The outdoor music festival was completely washed out by the downpour.
items.ex_zh: 室外音乐节因倾盆大雨而被迫彻底取消。
items.ex2_en: Frequent machine washing will cause bright summer fabric dyes to wash out completely.
items.ex2_zh: 频繁的机洗会导致鲜艳的夏季面料染料彻底褪色。

items.def_en: to turn yellowish and discolored through aging or chemical deterioration
items.ex_en: Cheap pulp paper will quickly yellow out when exposed to excessive atmospheric moisture.
items.ex_zh: 廉价纸浆纸暴露在过量空气水分中时会很快发黄变质。

items.def_en: To become yellow, or make something turn yellow, especially because of age.
items.ex_en: Old library books inevitably yellow when stored inside humid, poorly ventilated basements.
items.ex_zh: 存放在潮湿、通风不良的地下室里的老旧图书不可避免地会发黄。
items.ex2_en: Excessive exposure to sunlight will yellow the white finish on the furniture.
items.ex2_zh: 过度暴晒在阳光下会使家具上的白色漆面变黄。

items.def_zh: （使头发等）变灰白；（使）变成灰色
items.def_en: To become grey, especially of hair as one ages, or to make something grey.
items.ex_en: Years of severe professional stress began to grey his dark hair prematurely.
items.ex_zh: 多年的重大工作压力使他的黑发过早地变得灰白起来。
items.ex2_en: His neatly trimmed beard began to grey naturally as he reached his fifties.
items.ex2_zh: 步入五十岁时，他修剪整齐的胡子开始自然变白。

items.def_zh: （使头发等）变灰白；（使）变成灰色
items.def_en: (US spelling of grey) To become grey, especially of hair as one ages, or to make something grey.
items.ex_en: Her temples began to gray noticeably after she turned forty-five years old.
items.ex_zh: 年满四十五岁之后，她的两鬓开始明显地泛出白发。
items.ex2_en: Endless anxiety over company finances rapidly grayed his once pitch-black hair.
items.ex2_zh: 对公司财务无休止的焦虑迅速让他曾经乌黑的头发变白了。

items.def_en: [I/T] To lose brightness, vividness, or color gradually over time.
items.ex_en: Constant exposure to harsh afternoon sunlight will fade the bright velvet curtains.
items.ex_zh: 经常暴露在强烈的午后阳光下会使鲜艳的天鹅绒窗帘褪色。
items.ex2_en: The vibrant morning colors slowly faded from the western horizon as dusk fell.
items.ex2_zh: 黄昏降临时，西边地平线上鲜艳的晨光慢慢褪去。

items.def_en: To become white or paler, or make something whiter.
items.ex_en: Soaking the stained cotton shirts in diluted bleach will quickly whiten them.
items.ex_zh: 将沾有污渍的纯棉衬衫浸泡在稀释漂白水中能使它们迅速变白。
items.ex2_en: His pale knuckles whitened noticeably as he tightly gripped the heavy iron steering wheel.
items.ex2_zh: 当他紧紧握住沉重的铁质方向盘时，苍白的指节明显发白。

items.def_en: (US spelling of discolour) To change color or become stained, faded, or spoiled in appearance.
items.ex_en: Acidic industrial pollutants gradually discolor the white marble facade of the cathedral.
items.ex_zh: 酸性工业污染物逐渐使大教堂正面的白色大理石变色褪泽。
items.ex2_en: Old white paper will gradually discolor if left directly exposed to sunlight.
items.ex2_zh: 老旧的白纸如果直接暴露在阳光下，就会逐渐变色。

items.def_en: To become red or make something red, especially of the face due to embarrassment, anger, or heat.
items.ex_en: Her fair cheeks began to redden with sudden embarrassment before the assembly.
items.ex_zh: 在全场人员面前，她白皙的脸颊因突如其来的羞窘而泛起红晕。
items.ex2_en: The fierce afternoon heat quickly reddened the fair skin of the swimmers.
items.ex2_zh: 下午酷烈的暑热很快让游泳者白皙的皮肤泛红。

items.def_en: [I/T] To lose lustre or discolor as a result of exposure to air or moisture.
items.ex_en: Airborne sulfur compounds will readily tarnish fine sterling silver utensils over time.
items.ex_zh: 空气中的硫化物久而久之很容易使精美的纯银器具失去光泽。
items.ex2_en: The shiny copper pots naturally tarnish when left exposed in the moist kitchen.
items.ex2_zh: 光亮的铜锅放在潮湿的厨房里暴露着会自然失去光泽。

items.def_en: 1. To become black or dark, or make something black. 2. To damage someone's reputation or good name.
items.ex_en: Thick billowing smoke from the foundry began to blacken the limestone cliffs.
items.ex_zh: 铸造厂滚滚冒出的浓烟开始将石灰岩悬崖熏得漆黑一片。
items.ex2_en: The pale sky began to blacken rapidly as the terrible storm approached.
items.ex2_zh: 随着可怕的风暴临近，苍白的天空开始迅速变黑。

items.def_en: [I/T] To turn pale or make something white from fear, illness, or lack of light.
items.ex_en: His pale face blanched visibly upon witnessing the horrific carriage accident unfolding.
items.ex_zh: 目睹可怕的马车事故发生时，他苍白的脸瞬间吓得煞白。
items.ex2_en: The chef quickly blanched the fresh spinach in boiling salted water for dinner.
items.ex2_zh: 大厨迅速将新鲜菠菜放入加盐的沸水中焯烫以备晚餐。

groups.summary_en: Inchoative and causative verbs denoting a gradual or involuntary change in hue, pallor, or surface coloration due to aging, weathering, emotion, or chemical exposure.
groups.summary_zh: 指物体或肤色因衰老、风化、光照或情绪等自然/病理性变色、褪色或暗淡化。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an intrinsic alteration or loss of a surface's chromatic vibrancy, contrasting with superficial staining or intentional painting by emphasizing natural aging, exposure, or wear.
groups.desc_zh: 指物体表面因光照、老化或磨损等自然过程发生的色泽减退或变异，区别于外在的人工染色或偶发弄脏。
groups.nuance_en: fade: gradual loss of chromatic brightness or intensity (color / memory / daylight) · wash out: bleaching or leaching of pigment by water or exposure (fabric / complexion / print) · yellow: gradual shift toward amber tones via chemical aging (paper / teeth / varnish) · whiten: lightening toward stark white via age, fear, or chemical action (hair / face / teeth) · grey: progressive dulling into neutrality, typically through age or neglect (hair / skies / skin)
groups.nuance_zh: fade: 色彩或明度随时间逐渐淡化 (color / memory / daylight) · wash out: 因水浸或暴晒导致色素流失褪白 (fabric / complexion / print) · yellow: 因氧化变质或岁月沉淀泛黄 (paper / teeth / varnish) · whiten: 因衰老、惊吓或漂白变白 (hair / face / teeth) · grey: 色泽转灰变暗，尤指衰老或萧瑟 (hair / skies / skin)

groups.name: Don & Doff · 穿戴与脱卸 (Don, Doff, Disrobe)
groups.tip: 穿上或脱下衣帽的动作

items.def_en: (+ sth) to place a piece of clothing, headwear, or jewelry onto your body
items.ex_en: Remember to put on your warm wool coat before stepping outdoors tonight.
items.ex_zh: 今晚出门前，请记得穿上你那件保暖的羊毛大衣。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove a piece of clothing or footwear from your body
items.ex_en: Please take off your muddy work boots before entering the clean living room.
items.ex_zh: 进入干净的客厅之前，请脱掉你沾满泥巴的工装靴。

items.def_en: to put on a piece of clothing quickly and easily
items.ex_en: She hurried home from work to slip into a comfortable cotton bathrobe.
items.ex_zh: 她下班后匆匆赶回家，迅速换上了一件舒服的纯棉浴袍。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to put on a piece of clothing quickly and carelessly
items.ex_en: I just threw on an old hoodie and dashed out to grab some milk.
items.ex_zh: 我随手套上一件旧连帽衫，便冲出门去买牛奶。

items.def_zh: 给……戴上帽子；为……提供帽子
items.def_en: To put a hat on someone; to supply or cover with a hat.
items.ex_en: She hatted the shivering toddler before letting him play outside in the snow.
items.ex_zh: 她给瑟瑟发抖的幼儿戴上帽子，才让他到外面的雪地里玩耍。

items.def_en: (formal) To put on an item of clothing, a hat, or glasses.
items.ex_en: The surgeon donned sterile gloves and a mask before entering the operating theatre.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生在进入手术室前戴上了无菌手套和口罩。

items.def_en: To take off your clothes, or to remove someone else's clothes.
items.ex_en: The nurse gently undressed the patient to prepare him for the routine physical examination.
items.ex_zh: 护士轻柔地帮病人脱掉衣服，为常规体检做准备。

items.def_en: to remove an item of clothing, especially to take off or raise one's hat as a greeting
items.ex_en: The gentleman smiled politely and doffed his velvet cap to the passing ladies.
items.ex_zh: 那位绅士礼貌地微笑着，向路过的女士们脱帽致意。

items.def_zh: 穿得过于随便；穿得不够保暖
items.def_en: To wear clothes that are too casual or not warm enough for an occasion or weather.
items.ex_en: I underdressed for the chilly evening and shivered throughout the entire outdoor concert.
items.ex_zh: 我为了微凉的傍晚穿得太单薄，整场户外音乐会都在发抖。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to take off all or most of your clothes, especially quickly
items.ex_en: After the muddy hike, he stripped off his soaked boots and filthy jeans.
items.ex_zh: 泥泞的远足结束后，他迅速脱下了湿透的靴子和脏兮兮的牛仔裤。

items.def_en: [I/T] to remove all or most of one's clothing, or take the clothes off another person
items.ex_en: The doctor asked the injured athlete to strip to his waist for evaluation.
items.ex_zh: 医生让受伤的运动员脱掉上衣以便进行检查评估。

items.def_zh: 脱去……的衣服；脱去外皮，剥光；揭开
items.def_en: (formal or literary) To remove clothes from someone; to strip off an outer covering.
items.ex_en: The cold autumn winds unclothed the ancient weeping willows along the tranquil riverbank.
items.ex_zh: 萧瑟的秋风剥落了静谧河畔古老垂柳的枝叶。

items.def_zh: 脱衣；脱去（尤指礼服、长袍）
items.def_en: (formal or humorous) To take off your clothes, especially formal or ceremonial robes; to undress someone.
items.ex_en: The high court judge disrobed privately in his chambers after delivering the verdict.
items.ex_zh: 高等法院法官宣判完毕后，在法官室内私下脱去了法袍。

groups.summary_en: An agent performs the physical act of putting on or taking off garments, headwear, or footwear. Verbs range from neutral everyday dressing/undressing to formal, literary, or ritualized acts of clothing and stripping.
groups.summary_zh: 动作行为层面特异性地穿上、摘下或脱卸衣物饰物。
groups.desc_en: Covers intentional bodily attachment or removal of garments and accessories, contrasting with mere physical carrying or uncoupling by framing the item as personal attire.
groups.desc_zh: 指穿戴或脱卸衣物饰品的身体化动作，区别于一般的机械携带或卸载物品。
groups.nuance_en: don: formal or deliberate vesting of apparel (uniform / mantle / armor) · doff: formal or deferential tipping or removal (hat / cap / gloves) · slip into: effortless, fluid dressing in comfortable garments (dress / robe / slippers) · throw on: hurried, casual putting on of clothes (jacket / shirt / coat) · undress: comprehensive shedding of personal attire (patient / child / model)
groups.nuance_zh: don: 庄重或特意地穿戴 (uniform / mantle / armor) · doff: 敬意或脱卸帽饰手套 (hat / cap / gloves) · slip into: 轻松利落地换上轻便衣物 (dress / robe / slippers) · throw on: 匆忙随意地披套衣服 (jacket / shirt / coat) · undress: 全面脱除身上衣物 (patient / child / model)

groups.name: Existence & Occurrence · 存在与发生 (Exist, Occur, Happen, Transpire)
groups.tip: 事物存在或事件发生

items.def_en: To exist, live, or have reality; to take place or occur.
items.ex_en: Scientists still ponder whether intelligent life can be found elsewhere in our vast universe.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们仍在思考在我们广袤的宇宙中是否还存在着地外智慧生命。

items.def_en: To take place or occur, especially by chance or without being planned.
items.ex_en: The minor traffic accident happened on the slippery road during the morning rush.
items.ex_zh: 那起轻微的交通事故发生在早高峰湿滑的路面上。

items.def_en: To have actual being or objective reality; to live or remain alive.
items.ex_en: Ancient organisms continued to exist in deep ocean trenches despite the extreme hydrostatic pressure.
items.ex_zh: 尽管承受着极高的水压，古老的生物仍继续存在于深海海沟中。

items.def_zh: 发生；存在，出现；（想法等）浮现于脑中
items.def_en: 1. To happen or take place. 2. To exist or be found. 3. (of an idea or thought) To come into a person's mind.
items.ex_en: Significant seismic activity occurred along the tectonic fault line early yesterday morning.
items.ex_zh: 昨天清晨，地质断裂带沿线发生了显著的地震活动。

items.def_en: (of a problem or situation) To come into existence or become noticeable
items.ex_en: Unforeseen technical difficulties might arise during the preliminary phase of the major project.
items.ex_zh: 在重大项目的初期阶段可能会出现未曾预料的技术难题。

items.def_en: To occur, especially according to an arrangement or plan
items.ex_en: The annual international summit will take place in Geneva over the coming weekend.
items.ex_zh: 年度国际峰会将于即将到来的周末在日内瓦举行。

items.def_en: to happen or occur, especially through an unforeseen chain of circumstances
items.ex_en: Historians frequently debate how such dramatic social transformations actually came about so quickly.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们经常争论如此剧烈的社会变革究竟是如何迅速产生的。

items.def_en: to happen unexpectedly or arise as an issue requiring attention
items.ex_en: I must reschedule our lunch because an urgent business matter has just come up.
items.ex_zh: 我必须重新安排我们的午餐，因为刚才突然冒出一件紧急公务。

items.def_en: to appear or happen suddenly and unexpectedly
items.ex_en: Several unexpected software bugs cropped up right before the scheduled system deployment today.
items.ex_zh: 就在今天预定的系统部署之前，突然冒出了几个意想不到的软件漏洞。

items.def_zh: （尤指不好的事）复发，重现；再次浮现
items.def_en: To happen again periodically or repeatedly; to come back to mind.
items.ex_en: Doctors warned that the dangerous symptoms might recur if the therapy was discontinued.
items.ex_zh: 医生警告说，如果停止治疗，那些危险的症状可能会再次复发。

items.def_zh: 发生；为人所知，透露；（植物）蒸腾，散发水分
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To happen or occur. 2. (formal) To become known or be revealed. 3. (biology) To give off water vapor through pores or stomata.
items.ex_en: Nobody knows exactly what transpired behind closed doors during that tense emergency meeting.
items.ex_zh: 没有人确切知道在那场紧张的紧急闭门会议中究竟发生了什么。

items.def_zh: 出现，发生；起床，站起（arise 的过去分词）
items.def_en: (past participle of arise) Having emerged, come into being, or occurred.
items.ex_en: A serious conflict has arisen between the two rival factions regarding resource allocation.
items.ex_zh: 两个敌对派系之间在资源分配方面已经产生了严重的冲突。

items.def_en: (literary) To happen to someone, typically of something bad or unexpected
items.ex_en: A terrible misfortune befell the quiet seaside hamlet during that bitter winter storm.
items.ex_zh: 在那场严酷的冬季风暴中，一场可怕的灾难降临到了宁静的临海小村。

groups.summary_en: Intransitive predicates describing an entity's being in reality or an event taking place in time, ranging from neutral ontological state to sudden or formally reported occurrence.
groups.summary_zh: 描述实体在时空中的客观存在或事件的发生与显现。
groups.desc_en: Conceptualizes reality transitioning from latent potentiality into actualized presence or spatiotemporal manifestation, contrasting with static non-being or artificial manufacturing.
groups.desc_zh: 概念化现实从潜伏状态到现实显现的过程，区别于静态的无或人为制造。
groups.nuance_en: exist: static ontological reality or presence (entity / doubt / species) · occur: factual, localized instantiation in time (incident / phenomenon / thought) · arise: emergence out of underlying conditions or disputes (problem / question / conflict) · take place: premeditated or structured event unfolding (meeting / ceremony / election) · transpire: revelation or subsequent realization of what secretly happened (events / truth / secret)
groups.nuance_zh: exist: 静态的本体存在或实体具有 (entity / doubt / species) · occur: 偶发性事件在特定时空的发生 (incident / phenomenon / thought) · arise: 由特定温床或矛盾中冒出 (problem / question / conflict) · take place: 依计划或程序安排发生 (meeting / ceremony / election) · transpire: 隐秘事态的显露或后续证实 (events / truth / secret)

groups.name: Flee & Abscond · 逃跑与潜逃 (Decamp, Abscond, Bolting)
groups.tip: 脱离险境仓皇奔逃

items.def_en: to leave a place quickly, especially when told to do so
items.ex_en: The angry landlord ordered the noisy tenants to clear out by sunrise tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的房东命令那些吵闹的房客在明天日出之前彻底搬走离开。

items.def_en: to depart quietly or secretly without being noticed
items.ex_en: Don't let this incredible opportunity slip away.
items.ex_zh: 别让这个绝佳的机会悄悄溜走。

items.def_en: (informal) to run away or leave quickly, especially in panic
items.ex_en: When the angry guard dog barked loudly, the mischievous kids decided to skedaddle.
items.ex_zh: 当凶猛的看门狗大声吠叫时，那群淘气的孩子决定溜之大吉。

items.def_en: to leave quickly, usually in order to escape or after committing a crime
items.ex_en: The burglar made off as soon as the burglar alarm went off.
items.ex_zh: 防盗警报一响，窃贼就仓皇逃窜了。

items.def_en: (+ from sb/sth) to secretly or abruptly leave a place or escape from danger
items.ex_en: The frightened little boy tried to run away from the barking street dog.
items.ex_zh: 那个受惊的小男孩试图从狂吠的流浪狗面前逃跑。

items.def_zh: 逃跑，逃脱，逃走；避免，避开；被遗忘
items.def_en: 1. To run away or break free from confinement, danger, or a bad situation. 2. To avoid an unpleasant fate, punishment, or harm.
items.ex_en: Two dangerous convicts managed to escape from the high-security prison last night.
items.ex_zh: 两名危险的重刑犯昨夜设法从那座高度设防的监狱中逃脱了。

items.def_en: to suddenly run away very fast, often because of fright
items.ex_en: The frightened horse suddenly bolted across the open pasture toward the dark forest.
items.ex_zh: 那匹受惊的马突然狂奔着穿过开阔的牧场，冲向黑暗的森林。

items.def_zh: 私奔（尤指未经父母同意秘密结婚）；逃跑，潜逃
items.def_en: (+ with) To run away secretly in order to get married, especially without parental consent.
items.ex_en: The young couple decided to elope to Las Vegas without telling their parents.
items.ex_zh: 这对年轻情侣决定背着父母悄悄私奔去拉斯维加斯结婚。

items.def_en: (+ with/from) To leave secretly and suddenly, especially to avoid arrest or escape custody, often taking stolen money.
items.ex_en: The corrupt accountant absconded with five million dollars from the company pension fund.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败的会计携带着公司养老基金中的五百万美元潜逃了。

items.def_en: to leave suddenly and secretly, often with money or goods that do not belong to you
items.ex_en: The fraudulent promoters decamped before dawn, leaving hundreds of investors completely penniless.
items.ex_zh: 那些诈骗发起人在黎明前悄然溜走，令数百名投资者倾家荡产。

items.def_en: (British informal) To run away or leave quickly, especially to avoid trouble or arrest.
items.ex_en: As soon as the police sirens wailed nearby, the young vandals scarpered quickly.
items.ex_zh: 附近的警笛一响，那些年轻的破坏分子便仓皇逃窜了。

items.def_en: To run away quickly from a dangerous, frightening, or unpleasant place or situation.
items.ex_en: Thousands of terrified villagers were forced to flee across the heavily guarded border.
items.ex_zh: 数以千计惊恐的村民被迫逃离家园，穿过重兵把守的边境。

items.def_zh: 逃跑，仓皇出逃；（过时）痛打，猛击
items.def_en: (slang) To run away or flee hurriedly, especially from the police; (dated, transitive) to strike or hit hard.
items.ex_en: After escaping custody, the notorious bank robber went on the lam for months.
items.ex_zh: 脱离看管后，那名臭名昭著的银行劫匪四处逃窜流亡了数月。

groups.summary_en: An agent departs abruptly, furtively, or illicitly from confinement, legal custody, obligations, or danger. Nuances contrast panic-stricken running with clandestine embezzlement flight and colloquial vanishing acts.
groups.summary_zh: 逃避抓捕、危险或法定义务而仓皇逃遁、私奔或秘密潜逃。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an urgent, covert, or sudden departure to evade restraint, danger, or social obligation, distinguishing itself from neutral leaving by its evasive motive.
groups.desc_zh: 指为规避危险、拘禁或责任而发生的紧急、隐蔽或突然离去，区别于普通中性的离场。
groups.nuance_en: bolt: abrupt, frantic dash out of sudden panic (horse / suspect / rabbit) · slip away: quiet, surreptitious withdrawal without notice (guest / fugitive / patient) · abscond: illicit flight with stolen assets or to skip bail (banker / trustee / debtor) · run away: complete abandonment of domestic custody or peril (child / dog / refugee) · elope: secret flight to wed without parental or community sanction (couple / lovers / daughter)
groups.nuance_zh: bolt: 惊慌之下猛然拔腿窜逃 (horse / suspect / rabbit) · slip away: 悄然无声地溜走或抽身 (guest / fugitive / patient) · abscond: 携款潜逃或畏罪潜匿 (banker / trustee / debtor) · run away: 逃离家庭管束或险境 (child / dog / refugee) · elope: 瞒着家庭秘密私奔结合 (couple / lovers / daughter)

groups.name: Impede & Foil · 阻挠与削弱 (Hamstring, Undercut, Preempt)
groups.tip: 暗中使绊削弱根基

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to preemptively obstruct, intercept, or isolate an opponent or their line of movement
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to ward off, neutralize, or push back an antagonistic threat or attack
items.ex_en: The experienced diplomat skillfully fended off aggressive questions from the persistent reporters.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的外交官巧妙地化解了咄咄逼人的记者们提出的挑衅性问题。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to anticipate an opponent or problem and intercept them to prevent action
items.ex_en: Management acted immediately to head off a damaging nationwide strike by rail workers.
items.ex_zh: 管理层立即采取行动，以防止铁路工人发起破坏性的全国罢工。

items.def_en: to prevent someone from accomplishing something planned or intended
items.ex_en: Alert border guards successfully thwarted an attempt to smuggle contraband into the country.
items.ex_zh: 警惕的边防警卫成功挫败了一起企图将违禁品走私入境的图谋。

items.def_en: to prevent something from happening, being accomplished, or continuing
items.ex_en: A lack of corporate funding has completely stymied our ongoing scientific research efforts.
items.ex_zh: 缺乏企业资金彻底妨碍了我们正在进行的各项科研工作。

items.def_zh: 暗中破坏，削弱（地位、效力等）；廉价出售（以抢生意）
items.def_en: 1. To undermine, weaken, or damage the effectiveness or authority of someone or something. 2. To sell goods or services at a lower price than a competitor.
items.ex_en: Constant public criticism can easily undercut the authority of the newly appointed chairman.
items.ex_zh: 持续不断的公众批评很容易削弱新任董事长的权威。

items.def_zh: 使陷入僵局；（国际象棋中）使走投无路成和棋
items.def_en: To bring a dispute, negotiation, or contest to an impasse where no action can be taken or progress made.
items.ex_en: Uncompromising demands from both sides stalemated the critical international peace negotiations indefinitely.
items.ex_zh: 双方互不妥协的要求使这场关键的国际和平谈判无限期陷入了僵局。

items.def_zh: 使陷入困境，阻碍；在斯诺克台球中使进球困难
items.def_en: (informal) To thwart, hinder, or place someone in a situation where they cannot act effectively.
items.ex_en: A flat tire right before the interview completely snookered his career prospects.
items.ex_zh: 面试前车胎突然漏气，彻底把他逼入绝境并毁了他的前程。

items.def_zh: 预先阻止；先发制人，先一步行动
items.def_en: To prevent, hinder, or thwart an anticipated event or action by taking early measures beforehand.
items.ex_en: The central bank raised interest rates preemptively to forestall an impending inflationary spiral.
items.ex_zh: 中央银行先发制人地上调了利率，以遏制即将到来的通胀螺旋。

items.def_zh: 妨碍，阻碍；拖累，加重负担
items.def_en: To burden, weigh down, or impede the free movement, progress, or activity of someone or something.
items.ex_en: Heavy debt obligations continue to encumber the small business during its restructuring phase.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的债务负担在重组阶段继续拖累着这家小型企业的发展。

items.def_en: to damage someone or something so severely that they cannot function normally
items.ex_en: The devastating transport strike could cripple the nation's fragile manufacturing supply chain.
items.ex_zh: 破坏性的交通大罢工可能会重创该国脆弱的制造业供应链。

items.def_zh: 妨碍，使陷入瘫痪，削弱……的效力；割断……的腿腱
items.def_en: 1. to prevent a person, plan, or organization from operating effectively or successfully. 2. to cripple a person or animal by cutting the hamstring tendon.
items.ex_en: Severe budgetary constraints have severely hamstrung the agency's ability to enforce basic regulations.
items.ex_zh: 严峻的预算限制极大地削弱了该机构执行基本法规的能力。

items.def_zh: 先发制人以阻止，抢先采取行动；取代，替代
items.def_en: 1. to take action in order to prevent an anticipated event or to stop someone from doing something. 2. to replace or take the place of something.
items.ex_en: The technology giant bought the small startup to preempt any emerging market competition.
items.ex_zh: 这家科技巨头收购了那家初创公司，以抢先消除潜在的市场竞争。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote deliberate tactical actions taken to obstruct, weaken, or anticipate and neutralize an opponent's operational capability or momentum.
groups.summary_zh: 指采取战术手段暗中掣肘、设局阻滞、削弱能力或先发制人以破坏计划。
groups.desc_en: Signifies intentional intervention that disrupts, blocks, or disables an adversary's operational momentum, contrasting with general passive opposition or mere disagreement.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动干预、挫败或削弱对手的推进动能与预定计划，区别于消极的反对或言辞异议。
groups.nuance_en: thwart: decisive frustration of an active scheme or ambition (plot / attempt / ambition) · stymie: presenting an intractable obstacle that stalls progress (investigation / progress / negotiators) · undercut: covert erosion of standing, price, or authority (credibility / authority / rival) · head off: preemptive intervention before a crisis materializes (crisis / conflict / strike) · snooker: placing into a blocked, helpless tactical dilemma (opponent / government / player)
groups.nuance_zh: thwart: 彻底挫败谋划或野心 (plot / attempt / ambition) · stymie: 设下难以逾越的障碍使其停滞 (investigation / progress / negotiators) · undercut: 暗中削弱根基、底价或权威 (credibility / authority / rival) · head off: 在事态恶化前迎头拦截 (crisis / conflict / strike) · snooker: 制造死局令对手陷入困境 (opponent / government / player)

groups.name: Initiation & Commencement · 开始与启动 (Start, Begin, Commence, Initiate)
groups.tip: 事件或进程的开端

items.def_zh: 开始，着手；开动，启动；创办，建立；使惊起
items.def_en: 1. To begin doing something or to begin to happen. 2. To set in motion or cause to operate.
items.ex_en: The anxious technician pressed the green button to start the massive backup generator.
items.ex_zh: 焦虑的技术员按下了绿色按钮，以启动巨大的备用发电机。
items.ex2_en: The grand musical festival will start promptly at seven o'clock this evening.
items.ex2_zh: 盛大的音乐节将于今晚七点准时开始。

items.def_en: To start to happen or exist; to start doing something.
items.ex_en: The audience settled into their seats as the symphony orchestra began to play.
items.ex_zh: 当交响乐团开始演奏时，观众们纷纷在各自的座位上坐定。
items.ex2_en: The ambitious team will begin their extensive laboratory research early next Monday.
items.ex2_zh: 雄心勃勃的团队将于下周一清晨开始他们广泛的实验室研究。

items.def_zh: 开始；着手（begin 的过去式）
items.def_en: (past tense of begin) Started to happen or exist; started doing something.
items.ex_en: Dark thunderclouds gathered overhead and heavy rain began to fall upon the city.
items.ex_zh: 乌黑的雷雨云在头顶聚集，大雨开始倾盆落向整座城市。
items.ex2_en: The director began the rehearsal by giving notes to the lead actors.
items.ex2_zh: 导演通过给主演们提出意见开始了这次排练。

items.def_en: To start an activity, campaign, or product with enthusiasm or publicity
items.ex_en: The innovative company plans to launch a new electric vehicle model this autumn.
items.ex_zh: 这家创新型公司计划在今年秋天推出一款全新的电动车型。
items.ex2_en: The nationwide environmental initiative launched smoothly across several major universities last week.
items.ex2_zh: 上周，这项全国性环保倡议在几所主要大学顺利展开。

items.def_zh: 开始；着手（begin 的过去分词）
items.def_en: (past participle of begin) Having started to happen, exist, or do something.
items.ex_en: Construction on the new suspension bridge has already begun ahead of original schedule.
items.ex_zh: 新悬索桥的施工已经提前于原定进度正式展开了。
items.ex2_en: The energetic committee has already begun the elaborate preparations for the festival.
items.ex2_zh: 充满活力的委员会已经开始了为节日准备的精细工作。

items.def_en: To cause an important process or action to begin
items.ex_en: The progressive government decided to initiate a comprehensive review of existing labor laws.
items.ex_zh: 开明政府决定对现行的劳动法规启动一次全面的审查。

items.def_en: (informal) To start an event or proceedings energetically
items.ex_en: A lively brass band kicked off the annual community summer festival in style.
items.ex_zh: 一支充满活力的铜管乐队热闹非凡地为年度社区夏季节拉开了序幕。
items.ex2_en: The international trade conference kicked off with an inspiring keynote address yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 国际贸易会议昨天在一场鼓舞人心的主题演讲中拉开序幕。

items.def_en: to embark on a journey, process, career, or sequence of actions
items.ex_en: She started out as an unpaid intern before eventually becoming the managing director.
items.ex_zh: 她最初起步时是一名无薪实习生，最终晋升为了常务董事。

items.def_en: (+ sth/doing sth) to begin an active task or endeavor with purpose
items.ex_en: After breakfast, the meticulous gardener set about pruning the overgrown rose bushes outside.
items.ex_zh: 吃过早饭后，细心的园丁便着手修剪室外过度生长的玫瑰丛。

items.def_zh: 开始认真对待；着手进行
items.def_en: (+ sth) to begin giving serious, focused attention or effort to an activity
items.ex_en: Now that the introductions are done, let's get down to business.
items.ex_zh: 既然介绍完毕，我们就言归正传、开始谈正事吧。

items.def_en: (formal) To begin or start an activity, event, or process.
items.ex_en: The solemn university graduation ceremony will commence promptly at ten tomorrow morning.
items.ex_zh: 庄严的大学毕业典礼将于明天上午十点整准时开始。
items.ex2_en: The judge will commence the high-profile court hearing early tomorrow morning.
items.ex2_zh: 法官将于明天清晨开庭审理这起备受瞩目的案件。

items.def_en: (computing) To set a computer program, system, or variable to its starting state or initial value.
items.ex_en: The embedded software script must initialize every hardware register prior to system boot.
items.ex_zh: 嵌入式软件脚本必须在系统启动前对每一个硬件寄存器赋初值。

items.def_en: (formal) To begin again after an interruption or pause.
items.ex_en: Both diplomatic delegations agreed to recommence peace talks after a brief holiday recess.
items.ex_zh: 双方外交代表团均同意在简短的假期休会后重新启动和平谈判。
items.ex2_en: Classes recommenced promptly at eight o'clock following the pleasant winter vacation.
items.ex2_zh: 度过愉快的寒假后，课程于早晨八点准时恢复。

groups.summary_en: Verbs denoting the initial point of an action, process, or state, spanning informal everyday speech, mechanical activation, and formal ceremonial inception.
groups.summary_zh: 指示动作、过程或状态的最初起点，涵盖日常起步至正式典礼启动。
groups.desc_en: Captures the pivotal threshold where an operation, enterprise, or state of being transitions from void to momentum, contrasting with ongoing continuation.
groups.desc_zh: 聚焦项目、行动或状态从无到有破土而出的临界启动点，区别于持续推进。
groups.nuance_en: initiate: setting a complex official process or reform into motion (inquiry / proceedings / reform) · launch: high-profile or explosive release into public space (campaign / product / missile) · kick off: energetic, ritualized, or celebratory commencement (match / festivities / debate) · commence: formal, solemn start of an institutional event (ceremony / proceedings / sentence) · begin: broad, foundational inception of any temporal span (year / journey / work)
groups.nuance_zh: initiate: 正式启动复杂程序或制度改革 (inquiry / proceedings / reform) · launch: 高调推出新产品或发起攻势 (campaign / product / missile) · kick off: 充满活力或仪式性地揭开序幕 (match / festivities / debate) · commence: 庄严正式地开启官方事务 (ceremony / proceedings / sentence) · begin: 最基础广泛地进入某一时段 (year / journey / work)

groups.name: Inspire & Uplift · 激励与振奋 (Hearten, Enliven, Embolden)
groups.tip: 注入活力使人精神振作

items.def_en: to make someone feel happier or more hopeful
items.ex_en: The optimistic news from the doctor cheered the worried family immensely that afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 那天下午，来自医生的乐观消息极大地鼓舞了忧心忡忡的家属。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to become more cheerful, or to make someone feel happier and more hopeful
items.ex_en: A warm cup of hot cocoa helped cheer up the lonely child instantly.
items.ex_zh: 一杯热腾腾的可可立刻让那个孤独的孩子心情好转起来。
items.ex2_en: The weeping child began to cheer up after seeing her favorite toy.
items.ex2_zh: 看到自己最喜爱的玩具后，哭泣的孩子开始高兴起来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to regain energy, enthusiasm, or high spirits, or to instill vitality into someone
items.ex_en: A strong espresso and a brisk walk quickly perked up the exhausted researcher.
items.ex_zh: 一杯浓缩咖啡和一趟快走让精疲力竭的研究员迅速恢复了活力。
items.ex2_en: The wilting garden flowers perked up visibly after the refreshing morning rain.
items.ex2_zh: 在清爽的晨雨之后，花园里枯萎的花朵明显振作精神恢复了生机。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to become more lively and animated, or to infuse excitement into a person or event
items.ex_en: Upbeat jazz music and colorful party lights livened up the otherwise quiet living room.
items.ex_zh: 轻快的爵士乐和五彩斑斓的派对彩灯让原本沉寂的客厅活跃了起来。
items.ex2_en: The quiet reception suddenly livened up when the upbeat brass band arrived.
items.ex2_zh: 当欢快的铜管乐队到来时，原本安静的招待会突然活跃起来。

items.def_en: (often buoy up) to support someone emotionally and make them feel more cheerful or confident
items.ex_en: Strong community support buoyed the grieving family throughout their most challenging personal ordeal.
items.ex_zh: 强有力的社区支持在悲伤的一家人度过最艰难的煎熬时给予了心理支撑。

items.def_zh: 使精神振作；使精力充沛
items.def_en: to give fresh life, energy, and strength to someone
items.ex_en: A brisk swim in the cool ocean water will invigorate your weary body.
items.ex_zh: 在清凉的海水中欢快地游上一圈会让你疲惫的身躯重新充满活力。

items.def_en: to give someone the courage or confidence to do something or to behave in a certain way.
items.ex_en: Their early electoral success emboldened the opposition leaders to demand sweeping political reforms.
items.ex_zh: 初期的选举胜利给反对派领导人壮了胆，使他们提出更全面的政治改革要求。

items.def_zh: 使更有生气，使生动，使活跃
items.def_en: to make something more interesting, lively, or cheerful.
items.ex_en: The speaker used witty anecdotes to enliven an otherwise dry academic symposium.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者用风趣的轶事使原本枯燥的学术研讨会活跃起来。

items.def_en: to make someone feel happier, more hopeful, or more confident.
items.ex_en: The encouraging quarterly sales report heartened investors after months of severe market turmoil.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了数月剧烈的市场动荡后，令人鼓舞的季度销售报告提振了投资者的信心。

items.def_en: (also 'liven up') To become more lively or energetic, or to make something or someone more lively.
items.ex_en: A splash of bright paint will quickly liven up this dreary living room.
items.ex_zh: 添上一抹鲜艳的油漆能让这间沉闷的客厅立刻活跃起来。
items.ex2_en: The dull party finally began to liven up as more guests arrived.
items.ex2_zh: 随着更多客人的到来，沉闷的派对终于开始热闹起来。

items.def_zh: 挑逗，激起……的兴趣（尤指带有性刺激）；刺激
items.def_en: to excite or stimulate someone pleasantly, especially in a sexual or intriguing way.
items.ex_en: The tabloid published scandalous rumors designed solely to titillate curious readers.
items.ex_zh: 该小报刊登了丑闻流言，纯粹是为了激起猎奇读者的窥探欲。

items.def_en: (also 'chirk up') (informal) to cheer up or make someone cheer up.
items.ex_en: Drink some hot cocoa and chirk up before the guests arrive for dinner.
items.ex_zh: 在客人来吃晚饭前，喝点热可可让自己振作起来吧。
items.ex2_en: A cup of warm chamomile tea might chirk up the stressed student.
items.ex2_zh: 一杯温暖的洋甘菊茶也许能让压力沉重的学生振作起来。

items.def_en: (formal or literary) to fill someone with spirit, courage, or enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: The general's impassioned speech served to inspirit the weary troops before dawn.
items.ex_zh: 将军慷慨激昂的演说在黎明前鼓舞了疲惫的军队士气。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe infusing a person with courage, high spirits, or mental vitality, differing predominantly in literary register and specific affective outcome.
groups.summary_zh: 指激发他人勇气、生机与精神振奋，各词在书面语体与触动深度上存在差异。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the external psychological stimulation of an agent's spirit, mood, or fortitude, contrasting with physical nourishment or mere verbal praise.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过精神力量激发、提振主体的士气、活力或胆识，区别于物理滋养或表面称赞。
groups.nuance_en: buoy: keeping sinking spirits afloat against adversity (spirits / market / hopes) · embolden: imparting daring courage to act audaciously (rebels / critics / heart) · invigorate: injecting vigorous energy and physical-mental vitality (economy / body / debate) · enliven: injecting spark, color, and cheerfulness into a dull setting (party / discussion / scene) · cheer: direct dispelling of gloom through overt warmth (crowd / team / patient)
groups.nuance_zh: buoy: 托起即将下沉的情绪或信心 (spirits / market / hopes) · embolden: 壮人胆魄使其勇于采取行动 (rebels / critics / heart) · invigorate: 注入充沛生机与活力 (economy / body / debate) · enliven: 为沉闷场景增添生趣与光彩 (party / discussion / scene) · cheer: 用热忱欢呼直接驱散阴霾 (crowd / team / patient)

groups.name: Join & Interlock · 物理连接与接合 (Fasten, Splice, Mortise)
groups.tip: 将分散部件接合为一体

items.def_en: (+ with/up) To join together in pairs, or to bring two people or things together to work or form a unit.
items.ex_en: The teacher paired each foreign student with a native speaker for conversation practice.
items.ex_zh: 老师将每位留学生与一名母语者配对进行会话练习。
items.ex2_en: The two eager dance partners paired up naturally for the upcoming waltz.
items.ex2_zh: 两位热切的舞蹈搭档自然地结成一对，准备迎接接下来的华尔兹。

items.def_zh: 在……上架桥，连接；消除（分歧、鸿沟），弥合
items.def_en: To build or form a bridge over something; (figurative) to connect or reduce the distance or difference between two things.
items.ex_en: The committee introduced practical measures to bridge the deep economic divide between regions.
items.ex_zh: 委员会出台了切实措施以消除区域之间巨大的经济鸿沟。

items.def_zh: （使）牢固黏合，结合；（使）建立亲密关系
items.def_en: 1. To join or stick firmly together, often using heat, glue, or pressure. 2. To form a close, affectionate, or trusting relationship with someone.
items.ex_en: This waterproof epoxy resin will bond the two ceramic surfaces together permanently.
items.ex_zh: 这种防水环氧树脂会将两块陶瓷表面永久地黏合在一起。
items.ex2_en: The specialized metal plates bond securely under intense heat and pressure.
items.ex2_zh: 这种专用金属板在高温高压下能够牢固结合。

items.def_zh: 用榫接等连接，接合；（在关节处）切开（肉）
items.def_en: 1. To fit, fasten, or join parts together, especially with a joint. 2. To divide or cut meat into pieces at the joints.
items.ex_en: The carpenter carefully jointed the wooden boards to create a seamless tabletop.
items.ex_zh: 木匠将这些木板仔细榫接在一起，制成了一张无缝的桌面。

items.def_zh: 连接，系上，贴上；赋予，重视
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) To fasten, join, or connect one thing to another. 2. (+ to) To attribute importance, value, or meaning to something.
items.ex_en: Please attach the metal bracket securely to the timber frame with bolts.
items.ex_zh: 请用螺栓将金属支架牢牢固定在木构架上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to connect or link mechanical parts, components, or devices together
items.ex_en: Can you help me hook up the sound system to my laptop?
items.ex_zh: 你能帮我把音响系统连接到笔记本电脑上吗？

items.def_en: (+ sth) to assemble or join separate parts to form a whole structural entity
items.ex_en: The conservator painstakingly pieced together the ancient shattered porcelain vase using resin.
items.ex_zh: 文物修复师用树脂费尽心思地将破损的古代瓷瓶拼凑复原。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fit or join securely together so that parts interlock and cannot move independently
items.ex_en: The gear teeth must lock together smoothly to prevent mechanical damage under pressure.
items.ex_zh: 齿轮的齿距必须顺畅啮合，以防在高压下发生机械损坏。
items.ex2_en: The technician locked the metal panels together using sturdy industrial screws.
items.ex2_zh: 技术人员用坚固的工业螺丝将金属面板紧锁在一起。

items.def_en: to attach or fix two parts or objects firmly together using a clip, screw, or strap
items.ex_en: Workers used stainless steel straps to fasten the industrial conduit to the girder.
items.ex_zh: 工人们用不锈钢带将工业导管牢固地固定在大梁上。
items.ex2_en: The vintage metal suitcase fastens easily with two sturdy brass side latches.
items.ex2_zh: 这个老式金属手提箱通过两侧坚固的黄铜锁扣轻松扣紧。

items.def_en: to join the ends of two ropes, wires, or timbers by weaving or overlapping them
items.ex_en: The experienced sailor skillfully spliced the broken mooring lines before high tide.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的水手在涨潮前熟练地将断裂的系泊缆绳绞接在一起。

items.def_en: to fit or mesh tightly together by reciprocal parts
items.ex_en: The modular paving stones interlock perfectly without requiring any mortar between them.
items.ex_zh: 这些模块化铺路石严丝合缝地相互咬合，缝隙间无需任何灰浆。
items.ex2_en: The builder carefully interlocked the wooden timber joints to ensure maximum stability.
items.ex2_zh: 建筑工小心地将木梁榫接在一起以确保最大的稳定性。

items.def_zh: 以鸠尾榫接合，紧密吻合
items.def_en: to join two pieces of wood with interlocking wedge-shaped tenons, or fit together neatly
items.ex_en: The master craftsman dovetailed the walnut drawer corners with extraordinary historical precision.
items.ex_zh: 这位高级工匠以极高的传统精度用鸠尾榫接合了胡桃木抽屉的角部。
items.ex2_en: Our departmental project goals dovetail perfectly with the firm's overall corporate vision.
items.ex2_zh: 我们部门的项目目标与公司的整体企业愿景完美契合。

items.def_en: (carpentry) To cut a hole (mortise) into a piece of wood or stone, or to join parts together using a mortise and tenon.
items.ex_en: He mortised the heavy oak beam to receive the corresponding vertical post.
items.ex_zh: 他在沉重的橡木梁上凿出榫眼，以接合相应的立柱。

groups.summary_en: An agent secures two or more physical parts, materials, or structural elements together using fasteners, structural joints, adhesive bonds, or interlocking woodworking methods. Register spans general workshop assembly to precise joinery and structural engineering.
groups.summary_zh: 通过紧固件、咬合槽口或粘合剂将构件在物理结构上连接固定。
groups.desc_en: Applies to the physical, chemical, or structural union of discrete components into an integrated functional whole, contrasting with mere proximity or juxtaposition.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过物理、化学或结构衔接将分离构件结合为功能一体，区别于空间上的邻近并列。
groups.nuance_en: bond: fusion via adhesive or cohesive molecular force (surfaces / brick / polymers) · attach: fastening a secondary accessory onto a primary body (file / tag / lead) · lock together: rigid interlocking of matching structural parts (teeth / panels / mechanisms) · bridge: spanning a physical or conceptual gap (chasm / divide / cultures) · pair: coupling two complementary entities for coordinated function (devices / socks / dancers)
groups.nuance_zh: bond: 借助粘剂或分子力实现胶合牢接 (surfaces / brick / polymers) · attach: 将附属构件系于主构件上 (file / tag / lead) · lock together: 匹配构件的咬合与卡死 (teeth / panels / mechanisms) · bridge: 架设跨接以弥合沟壑鸿沟 (chasm / divide / cultures) · pair: 将相称的两物配对协同 (devices / socks / dancers)

groups.name: Leap & Gambol · 腾跃与雀跃 (Hop, Spring, Bound)
groups.tip: 离开地面的弹跳动作

items.def_en: to move forward by repeated hopping or skipping bounds
items.ex_en: The injured robin began to hop along the garden path toward shelter.
items.ex_zh: 那只受伤的知更鸟顺着花园小径一路蹦跳着寻找庇护所。

items.def_zh: 单脚跳；（鸟或昆虫）双足跳跃；快速跳上（或跳下）
items.def_en: 1. To move by jumping on one foot, or (of an animal or bird) to spring with both feet together. 2. To move quickly or board a vehicle.
items.ex_en: The little bird hopped rapidly along the brick wall chasing tiny insects.
items.ex_zh: 小鸟沿着砖墙飞快地跳跃着追逐细小的昆虫。

items.def_en: to move along quickly by hopping lightly on each foot in turn
items.ex_en: The happy child began to skip playfully down the sunlit sidewalk alone.
items.ex_zh: 快乐的孩子开始独自在洒满阳光的人行道上轻快地蹦跳向前。

items.def_en: to run and jump around playfully and happily, like lambs
items.ex_en: Young lambs gamboled across the lush meadow beneath the gentle spring sun.
items.ex_zh: 小羊羔在温暖柔和的春阳下穿过郁郁葱葱的草地欢腾雀跃。

items.def_en: To dance energetically or move rhythmically, especially to pop or jazz music.
items.ex_en: The teenagers started to bop energetically to the infectious rhythm across town.
items.ex_zh: 青少年们随着动感的节拍在城里各地充满活力地欢跳起舞。

items.def_en: to move forward with lively, expansive, buoyant leaps or strides
items.ex_en: The excited puppy bound along the sandy beach toward the rolling ocean waves.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的小狗沿着沙滩大步雀跃，迎着翻滚的海浪奔去。

items.def_en: to leap or jump suddenly into the air from a resting position
items.ex_en: The startled deer sprang up from the tall grass and dashed away.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的鹿从高草丛中猛然跃起，疾驰而去。

items.def_en: 1. To leap, skip, or move quickly and lightly. 2. To move the body rhythmically to music.
items.ex_en: Specks of golden dust danced lightly in the beam of warm sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 金色的微尘在温暖的阳光束中轻快地上下舞动。

items.def_en: 1. To move suddenly and quickly upward or forward in a leap. 2. To cause something to spring or trigger suddenly.
items.ex_en: The athletic cat sprang gracefully over the wooden garden fence without hesitation.
items.ex_zh: 矫健的猫毫不犹豫地轻盈跃过了花园的木栅栏。

items.def_zh: 跳跃着前进，弹跳；形成……的界线，限制
items.def_en: To move forward with leaps or long, energetic steps; to bounce.
items.ex_en: The spirited dog bounded across the open meadow chasing the bright ball.
items.ex_zh: 那只精力充沛的狗在开阔的草地上雀跃飞奔，追逐着彩球。

items.def_en: [I/T] to jump high or a long distance into the air across an obstacle
items.ex_en: The champion horse leaped over the wide wooden hurdle with immense power.
items.ex_zh: 冠军骏马以极其充沛的力量一跃跨过了宽阔的木制跨栏。

items.def_zh: 跳，跃起（spring的过去式与过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of spring; to move or leap forward suddenly.
items.ex_en: The tiger sprung from the dense foliage toward its unsuspecting prey instantly.
items.ex_zh: 老虎瞬间从茂密的树叶中纵身跃出，扑向毫无防备的猎物。

items.def_en: To skip, jump, or dance about in a lively, playful, and energetic way.
items.ex_en: The young goats capered playfully around the rocky hillside in early morning.
items.ex_zh: 小山羊清晨在岩石密布的山坡上欢蹦乱跳地四处嬉戏。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote self-propelled aerial locomotion off the ground, varying by foot action, distance, rhythm, and emotional playfulness.
groups.summary_zh: 表现以脚蹬地腾空的各种跳跃姿态，区分起跳方式、动作幅度与欢跃神态。
groups.desc_en: Characterizes explosive, buoyant, or playful upward/forward ballistic locomotion driven by leg strength, contrasting with grounded steady walking or continuous running.
groups.desc_zh: 指由腿部爆发力驱动的向上、腾跃或欢快弹跳移动，区别于脚踏实地的连续跑走。
groups.nuance_en: gambol: lighthearted, frolicsome skipping typical of young animals (lambs / children / calves) · bound: powerful, long-striding leaps displaying muscular grace (deer / athlete / dog) · spring: explosive, coiled upward or outward launch (trap / panther / gymnast) · hop: short, jerky jumps off one foot or two together (bird / frog / child) · skip: rhythmic, alternating light-footed hopping steps (child / pedestrian / dancer)
groups.nuance_zh: gambol: 幼兽或孩童般欢快的雀跃嬉闹 (lambs / children / calves) · bound: 矫健有力的大步腾跃奔跃 (deer / athlete / dog) · spring: 像发条蓄力后突发弹跳 (trap / panther / gymnast) · hop: 单脚或双足的短促跳跃 (bird / frog / child) · skip: 欢畅有韵律地垫步跳行 (child / pedestrian / dancer)

groups.name: Place & Juxtapose · 放置与并置 (Stow, Juxtapose, Superimpose, Plunk)
groups.tip: 规整收纳妥当存放起物件

items.def_en: (+ sth) to place something onto a flat surface or resting spot
items.ex_en: He put down his heavy tools on the workbench after work finished.
items.ex_zh: 工作结束后，他把沉重的工具放在了工作台上。

items.def_en: To put something carefully onto a flat surface
items.ex_en: The waitress set down the fragile crystal goblet carefully upon the table.
items.ex_zh: 女服务员小心翼翼地把易碎的水晶高脚杯放在桌子上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to place objects side by side or spread them carefully across an area
items.ex_en: The CEO laid out an ambitious five-year growth strategy.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官详细阐述了一项雄心勃勃的五年增长战略。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to stow an object into a designated storage space or container
items.ex_en: We packed away the winter clothes into plastic storage bins yesterday afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 昨天下午，我们把冬装妥善收纳进塑料储物箱里。

items.def_zh: 妥善收纳，妥善放置，收藏
items.def_en: 1. To pack, place, or store luggage, equipment, or goods neatly in a safe space.
items.ex_en: The flight attendant instructed passengers to stow their baggage in overhead compartments.
items.ex_zh: 乘务员指导乘客将行李妥善放置在头顶的行李舱内。

items.def_zh: 改变……的位置，重新放置；改变（产品、形象等的）市场定位
items.def_en: 1. To move someone or something into a different position or angle. 2. To change the way a product, service, or brand is marketed to the public.
items.ex_en: The medical technician had to reposition the patient to obtain clearer radiological images.
items.ex_zh: 医技人员不得不重新调整病人的体位以获取更清晰的影像。

items.def_zh: 把……并列，把……并置（以形成对照）
items.def_en: 1. To place two or more things, images, or ideas side by side, especially to highlight a contrast.
items.ex_en: The exhibition juxtaposes classical stone sculptures with vibrant contemporary abstract paintings effectively.
items.ex_zh: 该展览将古典石雕与生动的当代抽象画并列展出，形成鲜明对照。

items.def_zh: 噗通放下，重重坐下/掷下
items.def_en: To put down or drop something with a dull, sudden sound
items.ex_en: Exhausted after hiking, she plopped her heavy backpack down onto the floor.
items.ex_zh: 徒步后精疲力竭的她把沉重的背包噗通一声扔在地上。
items.ex2_en: Heavy fat raindrops plopped noisily onto the tin roof during the storm.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨中，大滴沉重的雨点扑通扑通响亮地落在铁皮屋顶上。

items.def_en: 1. To place a layer, pad, or support underneath something.
items.ex_en: The workers underlaid the hardwood floor with a thick foam insulation pad.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在实木地板下面铺垫了一层厚厚的泡沫隔音隔热垫。

items.def_en: 1. To place one geometric figure, wave, or layer directly on top of another so that they coincide.
items.ex_en: The cartographer superposed the historical boundary map directly over the modern satellite imagery.
items.ex_zh: 制图师将历史疆界地图直接重叠在现代卫星图像之上。

items.def_en: To drop or place down roughly, abruptly, or carelessly
items.ex_en: The courier dumped the parcel carelessly on the doorstep before driving away.
items.ex_zh: 快递员把包裹随手扔在门阶上，随后便开车离开了。

items.def_zh: 将（图像、文字、特征等）叠加于……之上；使重叠
items.def_en: 1. To place or lay one image, text, or layer on top of another so that both can be seen.
items.ex_en: The editor superimposed bold subtitles across the opening scene of the documentary.
items.ex_zh: 剪辑师在纪录片的开场画面上叠加了粗体字幕。

items.def_zh: 重重地放下，随便扔下；弹拨（琴弦）
items.def_en: 1. To drop, set, or place something down heavily or carelessly. 2. To pluck or twang the strings of a musical instrument.
items.ex_en: He plunked his muddy boots down right by the polished front door.
items.ex_zh: 他把满是泥巴的靴子随手重重扔在光亮的大门旁。

groups.summary_en: Verbs specifying the spatial manner, relative positioning, or casual/careful attitude involved in situating one object onto, next to, or beneath another.
groups.summary_zh: 指将物体置于特定相对位置或以特定动作姿态搁放、并列与叠置。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the spatial arrangement, deposition, or relational positioning of concrete objects in a designated site, contrasting with haphazard discarding or mere carrying.
groups.desc_zh: 强调对实体物品在特定空间中的安置、摆放或对照定位，区别于胡乱丢弃或单纯搬移。
groups.nuance_en: juxtapose: deliberate side-by-side placement for thematic contrast (images / styles / eras) · stow: compact, orderly caching of gear away from view (luggage / gear / supplies) · lay out: methodical planar spreading or conceptual blueprinting (plans / tools / map) · plop: heavy, careless, or unceremonious dropping (book / bag / infant) · reposition: adjusting existing spatial coordinates to optimize placement (furniture / troops / camera)
groups.nuance_zh: juxtapose: 刻意并列以构成艺术或意义对照 (images / styles / eras) · stow: 紧凑有序地收入储藏空间 (luggage / gear / supplies) · lay out: 展开铺平或条理清晰地规划 (plans / tools / map) · plop: 沉重沉闷、不拘小节地扑通放下 (book / bag / infant) · reposition: 调整方位以优化布局态势 (furniture / troops / camera)

groups.name: Solidify & Coagulate · 凝固与硬化 (Solidify, Congeal, Fossilize)
groups.tip: 由流体变凝胶进而坚硬成型

items.def_en: lose all moisture and become hard or brittle
items.ex_en: Without regular watering, the moist potting clay will dry out and crack.
items.ex_zh: 若不按时浇水，湿润的盆栽黏土就会干硬开裂。
items.ex2_en: Strong desert winds will dry out the exposed skin in just minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的沙漠狂风会在短短几分钟内吹干裸露的皮肤水分。

items.def_en: become hard, solid, or rigid through drying, cooling, or chemical action
items.ex_en: The wet cement needs at least twenty-four hours to set up properly.
items.ex_zh: 湿水泥至少需要二十四小时才能完全凝固硬化。
items.ex2_en: The cold temperature sets up the liquid gelatin much faster in winter.
items.ex2_zh: 在冬天，寒冷的温度能使液体明胶凝固得快得多。

items.def_zh: （使）凝结成胶状；（想法或计划）定型，变得明确
items.def_en: 1. To set and become firm or jelly-like. 2. (of ideas, plans, or relationships) To take a definite, workable form.
items.ex_en: Leave the freshly prepared fruit gelatin in the refrigerator until it jells.
items.ex_zh: 把刚调好的水果明胶留在冰箱里，直到它凝结成冻。
items.ex2_en: The calm discussion helped jell our vague team ideas into concrete plans.
items.ex2_zh: 平静的讨论有助于将我们团队模糊的想法凝聚成具体的计划。

items.def_en: become completely covered with a solid layer of ice
items.ex_en: The lake usually freezes over by late December.
items.ex_zh: 这个湖通常在十二月下旬完全封冻。
items.ex2_en: Arctic cold snaps often freeze over the broad surface of northern rivers.
items.ex2_zh: 北极寒潮经常将北方河流开阔的水面完全冻结封冻。

items.def_zh: （使）结块，（使）凝结成硬块；厚厚地覆盖
items.def_en: To form into a compact, hard mass, or to cover something with a thick, hard crust.
items.ex_en: Wet river mud began to cake firmly around the hiker's heavy leather boots.
items.ex_zh: 潮湿的河泥开始在这位徒步者的厚皮靴周围凝结成硬块。
items.ex2_en: Blowing desert sand quickly caked the dusty windshield of our rental car.
items.ex2_zh: 狂风吹起的沙漠沙尘很快在我们租来的汽车挡风玻璃上结成了厚块。

items.def_en: To set or cause liquid to set into a firm, trembling jelly.
items.ex_en: Boiling the fruit peels helps the natural pectin jelly into thick preserves.
items.ex_zh: 水煮果皮有助于其中的天然果胶凝结成浓稠的果冻。
items.ex2_en: The pastry chef jellied the rich fruit juice with organic powdered gelatin.
items.ex2_zh: 面点师用有机明胶粉将浓郁的果汁凝结成果冻。

items.def_en: [I/T] to form into a thick, semi-solid mass, characteristic of blood or milk
items.ex_en: The doctor administered anticoagulants to prevent the patient's blood from clotting dangerously.
items.ex_zh: 医生注射了抗凝剂，以防患者体内的血液发生危险的凝固。
items.ex2_en: The cold temperature clotted the fresh milk into thick creamy curds overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 寒冷的温度在一夜之间把新鲜牛奶凝结成了厚厚的凝乳。

items.def_en: 1. To become solid or hard, or to make a liquid or soft substance so. 2. To become definite, firm, or established, or to make something so.
items.ex_en: Molten volcanic lava begins to solidify rapidly as it enters the cold ocean.
items.ex_zh: 熔融的火山岩浆在进入冰冷的海水时迅速凝固变硬。
items.ex2_en: Freezing winter temperatures solidify the shallow mountain ponds into solid ice blocks.
items.ex2_zh: 严寒的冬日气温把浅浅的山塘冻结成坚固的冰块。

items.def_zh: （使）凝结，（使）凝固成乳块；（使）变质；使毛骨悚然
items.def_en: 1. (of a liquid, especially milk) To separate into thick solid lumps and watery liquid, or cause to do so. 2. (in 'curdle one's blood') To fill someone with extreme horror.
items.ex_en: Adding acidic lemon juice will curdle the warm milk almost instantly into curds.
items.ex_zh: 加入酸性的柠檬汁几乎会瞬间让温牛奶凝结成乳块。
items.ex2_en: The fresh milk began to curdle after sitting in the warm sun.
items.ex2_zh: 在温暖的阳光下放置后，鲜奶开始凝结成乳酪状。

items.def_zh: 烧结；（使）经高温压结硬化
items.def_en: To cause powdered metal or ceramic particles to coalesce into a solid mass through heat or pressure without complete melting.
items.ex_en: The furnace operates at high temperatures to sinter ceramic powder into dense components.
items.ex_zh: 炉子在高温下运转，将陶瓷粉末烧结成致密坚硬的构件。
items.ex2_en: Fine metallic particles sinter together into solid masses under extremely high temperatures.
items.ex2_zh: 在极高温度下，微细的金属颗粒会烧结凝聚成坚固的块体。

items.def_en: [I/T] to change from a liquid to a solid or semi-solid state, especially upon cooling
items.ex_en: Left untouched overnight on the counter, the rich gravy began to congeal.
items.ex_zh: 在料理台上放置一整夜未动后，浓稠的肉汁开始凝结成胶状。
items.ex2_en: The bitter arctic cold quickly congealed the fatty soup inside the pot.
items.ex2_zh: 严酷的北极严寒迅速把锅里油腻的汤凝结成了半固体。

items.def_en: 1. To turn into a fossil, or cause an organism to become preserved as a fossil. 2. To become rigid, outmoded, or unchangeable, or to make something so.
items.ex_en: Over countless millennia, ancient tree trunks fossilized into stone under massive sedimentary pressure.
items.ex_zh: 历经千百万年，古树树干在巨大的沉积压力下石化成了化石。
items.ex2_en: Intense mineral pressures fossilized the prehistoric marine creatures over hundreds of millennia.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的矿物压力在几十万年间将史前海洋生物石化成了化石。

items.def_en: [I/T] to turn organic matter into stone by mineral deposition
items.ex_en: Mineral-rich spring water slowly petrified the buried plant matter over centuries.
items.ex_zh: 富含矿物质的泉水在几个世纪间慢慢将掩埋的植物遗骸石化。
items.ex2_en: Organic wooden branches slowly petrified under mineralized sedimentary layers over million years.
items.ex2_zh: 数百万年间，有机树枝在矿化沉积层下逐渐石化变硬。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail phase changes and transitions wherein liquids, gels, or loose particulates turn dense, firm, crusty, or petrified through cooling, chemical reaction, or mineral deposition.
groups.summary_zh: 指液体、胶体或粉末经冷却或化学作用凝结、结块并变硬。
groups.desc_en: Depicts fluid or malleable matter transitioning into a dense, unyielding, or cohesive solid via cooling, chemical reaction, or drying, contrasting with melting or dissolving.
groups.desc_zh: 指流体或柔韧物质因冷却、化学反应或脱水而变为坚硬致密固体，区别于融化或溶解。
groups.nuance_en: solidify: broad transition into rigid, durable structure (concrete / lava / alliance) · clot: biochemical aggregation of organic liquid into viscous lumps (blood / cream / milk) · congeal: viscous thickening of gelatinous or fatty liquid upon cooling (gravy / blood / grease) · jell: setting into an elastic, coherent semi-solid gel (jam / plans / mixture) · cake: crusting or hardening into a brittle, compact dry layer (mud / blood / powder)
groups.nuance_zh: solidify: 广泛意义上的转为坚硬实体或稳固形态 (concrete / lava / alliance) · clot: 生化液体凝结成稠块 (blood / cream / milk) · congeal: 油脂或明胶遇冷后凝结成冻状 (gravy / blood / grease) · jell: 凝成弹性质地的胶体，或想法成形 (jam / plans / mixture) · cake: 泥浆粉末干涸板结成硬块 (mud / blood / powder)

groups.name: Specialized Civil Construction · 筑建与特种工程 (Roof, Causeway, Canal)
groups.tip: 堆叠构件施工筑起建筑物

items.def_en: (+ sth) build a barrier or obstruction across an opening, channel, or way
items.ex_en: Engineers blocked off the damaged water tunnel with steel plates and concrete.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们用钢板和混凝土封死了受损的输水隧道。

items.def_en: To cover a building or structure with a roof.
items.ex_en: The builders decided to roof the new municipal sports arena with curved steel.
items.ex_zh: 建筑施工队决定用曲面钢板给新的市政体育馆盖上屋顶。

items.def_en: (+ with) to cover ground with flat stones, asphalt, or concrete to create a firm surface
items.ex_en: The municipal crew worked all night to pave the broad avenue with asphalt.
items.ex_zh: 市政施工队整夜施工，用沥青铺设这条宽阔的大道。

items.def_zh: 筑坝拦住，截断（河流或水流）
items.def_en: (+ sth) build a barrier across a river or stream to hold back its flow
items.ex_en: Fallen trees and rockslides dammed up the mountain creek after the storm.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨过后，倒下的树木和滑坡的山石筑坝堵死了山溪。

items.def_en: (+ sth) support or strengthen a wall, trench, or structure with props or beams
items.ex_en: Workers used heavy timber beams to shore up the collapsing brick wall safely.
items.ex_zh: 工人们用厚重的木梁稳妥地支撑并加固那堵快要倒塌的砖墙。

items.def_en: to build or form a bridge across an obstacle, gap, or watercourse
items.ex_en: The provincial government bridged the turbulent river to connect two isolated mountain towns.
items.ex_zh: 省政府在这条汹涌的河流上架设桥梁，连接了两个偏僻的山镇。

items.def_en: To build a canal through an area, or to provide an area with canals.
items.ex_en: Nineteenth-century engineers canaled the valley to transport coal straight to the coast.
items.ex_zh: 十九世纪的工程师们在该流域开凿运河，将煤炭直接运往沿海地区。

items.def_en: (+ up) to construct an embankment across a river or stream to hold back water
items.ex_en: The authority planned to dam the river to generate clean hydroelectric power.
items.ex_zh: 当局计划在这条河上筑坝，以生产清洁的水力电能。

items.def_en: 1. To fit together the parts of something to construct it. 2. To gather together in a single place.
items.ex_en: Technicians assembled the prefabricated steel frame of the bridge in just forty-eight hours.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员仅用四十八小时就组装好了大桥的预制钢构架。
items.ex2_en: A large crowd of eager citizens assembled peacefully in the city plaza.
items.ex2_zh: 大批热切的市民平静地聚集在城市广场上。

items.def_zh: 重建，重修；恢复，重新建立
items.def_en: 1. To build something again after it has been damaged or destroyed. 2. To restore or reorganize something such as a life, system, or organization.
items.ex_en: The residents worked tirelessly together to rebuild their destroyed homes after the flood.
items.ex_zh: 洪水过后，居民们不知疲倦地齐心协力重建他们被毁的家园。

items.def_zh: 重建，重修（rebuild 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of rebuild: to construct something again after damage or destruction.
items.ex_en: Engineers completely rebuilt the collapsed canal embankment before the rainy season arrived.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们在雨季到来之前彻底重建了坍塌的运河堤岸。

items.def_zh: 修筑堤道跨越；为……筑堤道
items.def_en: To build a raised road or embankment across wet ground or water.
items.ex_en: The monarch sought to causeway the treacherous marsh to unite his divided provinces.
items.ex_zh: 君主试图在这片凶险的沼泽上筑起堤道，以联通他分隔的省份。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ through/under) to excavate an underground or underwater passage
items.ex_en: The construction crew will tunnel through solid granite to build the highway bypass.
items.ex_zh: 施工队将打穿坚硬的花岗岩，开凿一条公路分流隧道。

groups.summary_en: Builders execute specific civil or structural engineering works by erecting or outfitting particular infrastructural elements (roofs, channels, embankments, or assembled systems). Verbs emphasize the specific architectural component or civil modification involved.
groups.summary_zh: 针对水渠、堤道、顶棚等特定基建构件实施铺设、架筑或系统组装。
groups.desc_en: Covers heavy civil and geotechnical engineering designed to alter topography, bridge infrastructure, or contain natural elements, contrasting with light modular carpentry.
groups.desc_zh: 指改造地形水文、构筑交通跨越或拦水护土的重型土木工程，区别于轻量木工装配。
groups.nuance_en: dam: hydraulic construction to impound, retain, or choke water flow (river / stream / floodwaters) · shore up: underpinning structural weaknesses with timber, stone, or props (embankment / wall / economy) · pave: sealing ground surfaces with rigid stones, asphalt, or tiles (road / street / courtyard) · roof: spanning and shielding a structure overhead with weatherproofing (building / house / stadium) · canal: excavating an artificial inland waterway for navigation (isthmus / valley / territory)
groups.nuance_zh: dam: 筑坝截断、截留水流 (river / stream / floodwaters) · shore up: 用支柱斜撑加固濒塌结构或经济 (embankment / wall / economy) · pave: 用石料沥青铺砌硬化路面 (road / street / courtyard) · roof: 为建筑物封顶盖设屋面 (building / house / stadium) · canal: 开凿人造人工运河水系 (isthmus / valley / territory)

groups.name: Strike & Batter · 痛击与殴打 (Clout, Smite, Pummel, Bludgeon)
groups.tip: 从寻常击打到重创猛击

items.def_en: To hit someone heavily, especially with a fist, causing a dull thud
items.ex_en: He thumped his rival squarely in the chest, knocking him completely off balance.
items.ex_zh: 他狠狠一拳砸在对手胸口，打得对方彻底失去了平衡。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) strike sb or sth repeatedly and forcefully with the fists or a blunt object
items.ex_en: The furious customer began to pound on the counter, demanding an immediate refund.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的顾客开始猛砸柜台，要求立刻退款。

items.def_en: To beat someone repeatedly and violently with a stick, whip, or fists
items.ex_en: The cruel guard threatened to thrash any prisoner caught trying to smuggle contraband.
items.ex_zh: 残酷的守卫威胁要痛打任何企图走私违禁品的囚犯。

items.def_zh: 猛击，重击（人用手或重物）
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To hit someone hard with the hand or a heavy object.
items.ex_en: The bouncer suddenly clouted the rowdy patron across the jaw with his fist.
items.ex_zh: 保镖突然挥拳狠狠打在那个闹事顾客的下巴上。

items.def_zh: 击倒，打倒；迅速击溃（对手）
items.def_en: 1. To knock down quickly; (cricket) to defeat or bowl out opposing batsmen rapidly.
items.ex_en: The star fast bowler managed to skittle the opposing batting order before lunch.
items.ex_zh: 这位明星快速球手在午餐前便迅速击溃了对手的击球阵容。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack sb violently by hitting them repeatedly with heavy blows
items.ex_en: Don't beat yourself up over an honest mistake.
items.ex_zh: 不要因为一次无心之失而过度自责。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack someone with sudden, violent physical blows
items.ex_en: The enraged boxer suddenly laid into his sparring partner with relentless heavy punches.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的拳击手突然对陪练展开猛攻，连续挥出重拳。

items.def_en: To strike repeatedly with hard blows so as to inflict severe injury
items.ex_en: The assailant proceeded to batter the defenseless victim with a heavy metal wrench.
items.ex_zh: 袭击者随即用一把沉重的金属扳手接连猛击毫无防备的受害者。

items.def_en: 1. (informal) To hit or beat someone heavily and violently. 2. (informal) To defeat an opponent decisively.
items.ex_en: He whopped the intruder over the head with a heavy cast-iron frying pan.
items.ex_zh: 他用沉重的铸铁煎锅狠狠砸向入侵者的头部。

items.def_zh: 重击，猛打；惩罚，使遭灾祸；深深打动
items.def_en: 1. (literary or archaic) To hit someone or something with a powerful blow. 2. To defeat, afflict, or severely punish. 3. [T, usually passive] To affect deeply with a strong feeling, especially love.
items.ex_en: The ancient hero raised his enchanted hammer and smote the beast with fury.
items.ex_zh: 古老的英雄举起附魔战锤，愤怒地将凶兽击倒。

items.def_zh: 用重棒击打，猛击；强迫，恐吓
items.def_en: 1. To hit someone repeatedly with a heavy club or similar object. 2. To force or bully someone into doing something.
items.ex_en: The robbers attempted to bludgeon the security guard into submission with heavy clubs.
items.ex_zh: 劫匪试图用沉重的棍棒反复殴打保安，逼他就范。

items.def_en: 1. To hit someone or something repeatedly and forcefully, especially with the fists.
items.ex_en: The champion continued to pummel his exhausted opponent against the corner turnbuckle.
items.ex_zh: 卫冕冠军在擂台角落里继续用双拳连续猛击精疲力竭的对手。

items.def_en: 1. To hit someone violently in the face or body with the top of one's head.
items.ex_en: The drunken hooligan unexpectedly headbutted the police officer during the heated street brawl.
items.ex_zh: 那个醉酒的流氓在激烈的街头斗殴中突然用头猛撞了警官。

groups.summary_en: Physical violence frame describing striking someone with heavy blows, blunt implements, or repeated physical impacts, escalating from a sharp slap to savage bludgeoning.
groups.summary_zh: 以拳头、钝器或头部实施身体打击，从一记掌掴升级为连续重击与乱棒殴打。
groups.desc_en: Signifies repeated, brutal, or punishing blunt-force kinetic impacts intended to crush, shatter, or beat down a target, contrasting with light tapping or single surgical incisions.
groups.desc_zh: 指旨在彻底摧垮、打碎目标的反复沉重顿挫性暴击，区别于轻微拍打或外科手术式切割。
groups.nuance_en: batter: relentless, damaging blunt-force pummeling (coastline / door / suspect) · beat up: aggressive physical assault inflicting bodily harm (victim / prisoner / rival) · pound on: rhythmic, thunderous beating against an unyielding barrier (door / piano / drum) · thrash: violent flailing or severe disciplinary whipping (opponent / child / water) · clout: delivering a heavy, swinging blow with fist or hand (head / opponent / ear)
groups.nuance_zh: batter: 持续猛烈的钝力摧折与狂轰滥炸 (coastline / door / suspect) · beat up: 带有恶意的人身拳脚殴打 (victim / prisoner / rival) · pound on: 沉重有节律地猛捶猛敲 (door / piano / drum) · thrash: 痛笞严惩或在水中剧烈扑打 (opponent / child / water) · clout: 用手或重器抡出的一记重击 (head / opponent / ear)

groups.name: Strike & Lash · 击打与抽打 (Slap, Whip, Flagellate)
groups.tip: 使用鞭绳皮具抽打惩罚

items.def_zh: 用巴掌轻打，掌掴；给……戴上手铐
items.def_en: 1. To hit someone lightly, especially with an open hand. 2. (informal) To put handcuffs on someone.
items.ex_en: He playfully cuffed his younger brother on the cheek after the good news.
items.ex_zh: 听到好消息后，他开玩笑地用手掌轻拍了弟弟的脸颊一下。

items.def_zh: 猛踢，挥拳痛打；猛烈抽打
items.def_en: (+ at sb) hit out violently and suddenly with a limb, weapon, or whip
items.ex_en: Cornered by the alley thugs, he began to lash out wildly with fists.
items.ex_zh: 被小巷里的暴徒逼入绝境后，他挥拳猛烈反击。

items.def_en: (+ at sb) attempt to hit sb with a sudden blow of the fist
items.ex_en: Panicking in the dark, the startled guard struck out at his mysterious assailant.
items.ex_zh: 在黑暗中惊慌失措的守卫突然出拳，打向神秘的袭击者。

items.def_en: (+ sth) swing or strike sth with a quick, lash-like snapping motion
items.ex_en: The trainer whipped around the leather cord to drive the wild stallion back.
items.ex_zh: 训马师猛地甩动皮绳，将那匹野马赶了回去。

items.def_zh: 掌掴，拍击；啪地放下（或撞上）；施加（处罚等）
items.def_en: 1. To hit someone or something quickly with the palm of the hand or a flat object. 2. To place or put something down quickly, forcefully, or noisily.
items.ex_en: She angrily slapped the rude customer across the face before walking away abruptly.
items.ex_zh: 在愤怒地扇了那个无礼顾客一记耳光后，她随即转身离去。

items.def_en: to hit someone hard with a hand or heavy implement
items.ex_en: I watched the angry barman clout the unruly patron right across the ear.
items.ex_zh: 我看到愤怒的酒吧侍者狠狠一耳光打在那个闹事顾客的耳朵上。

items.def_zh: （用皮带等）抽打，鞭打；用皮革覆盖
items.def_en: 1. To beat or thrash someone severely, especially with a leather strap. 2. To cover or furnish something with leather.
items.ex_en: The strict headmaster used to leather disobedient boys with a heavy strap.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的校长过去常用一根厚皮带狠抽不听话的男生。

items.def_zh: 鞭打，抽打；搅打（奶油等）；迅速拿取；猛冲
items.def_en: 1. To hit a person or animal with a whip or strap. 2. To beat cream, eggs, etc. until light and firm. 3. To move or take something quickly and suddenly.
items.ex_en: The cruel carriage driver began to whip the tired horse to make it run.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的马车夫开始抽打那匹疲惫的马，逼它快跑。

items.def_zh: 痛打，猛击（常与 on/into 连用）；捕鲸
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To hit or thrash someone or something hard and repeatedly (often followed by 'on' or 'into'). 2. To hunt whales.
items.ex_en: The heavyweight champion began to whale on his challenger against the ropes mercilessly.
items.ex_zh: 重量级拳王靠着围绳毫不留情地猛打挑战者。

items.def_en: (informal) To hit someone or something very hard, especially with a closed fist.
items.ex_en: The furious defender socked the rival striker right in the jaw during halftime.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的后卫在中场休息时一拳狠狠捣在对方前锋的下巴上。

items.def_zh: 鞭笞，鞭打（尤指作为宗教忏悔或惩罚）；严厉谴责
items.def_en: To whip or flog someone, especially oneself as a religious discipline or as a severe punishment.
items.ex_en: Devout ascetics would flagellate themselves with cords as an act of solemn penance.
items.ex_zh: 虔诚的苦修者会用绳鞭抽打自己，以此作为庄严的赎罪之举。

items.def_en: to beat severely with a whip or stick as an official or extreme punishment
items.ex_en: The court ordered the rogue soldier flogged publicly for committing severe insubordination.
items.ex_zh: 军事法庭下令对这名严重抗命的叛逆士兵处以公开鞭笞。

items.def_en: to whip someone severely using a multi-thonged lash
items.ex_en: The ruthless inquisitor scourged the chained captive without showing any hint of mercy.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的审讯官用皮鞭严刑拷打戴着铁链的俘虏，毫无慈悲之意。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe delivering blunt or stinging physical impacts, differentiating flat-handed cuffs, fist blows, and repetitive, punitive flogging with straps or flexible scourges.
groups.summary_zh: 指用手掌、拳头或皮鞭等对人体进行抽打、痛击或笞刑惩罚。
groups.desc_en: Denotes sharp, whipping, or whiplash-like strikes delivered with a flexible implement, palm, or sudden kinetic snapping motion, contrasting with blunt crushing blows.
groups.desc_zh: 指用柔性器具、巴掌或突然抽动施加的清脆鞭打，区别于重物钝击。
groups.nuance_en: whip: rapid stinging strike delivered with a cord, rod, or lash (horse / wind / branches) · slap: flat-palmed, stinging open-handed strike (face / cheek / table) · lash out: explosive, sudden defensive or angry strike (tail / critics / tongue) · cuff: quick, light clipping blow with open hand or fist (ear / child / dog) · leather: punishing severe thrashing with leather straps (hide / belt / boy)
groups.nuance_zh: whip: 绳鞭破空带出的灼热抽打 (horse / wind / branches) · slap: 手掌正面脆响的掌掴 (face / cheek / table) · lash out: 突发性暴怒反扑或甩打 (tail / critics / tongue) · cuff: 带有训诫意味的侧掌轻削或刮打 (ear / child / dog) · leather: 用皮带沉重狠厉地体罚痛抽 (hide / belt / boy)

groups.name: Torment & Victimize · 虐待与侵害 (Abuse, Victimize, Terrorise)
groups.tip: 恶意施暴欺凌与威吓

items.def_en: to annoy or bother someone continually and repeatedly in an unpleasant way
items.ex_en: The unscrupulous debt collection agency continued to harass the family with threatening calls.
items.ex_zh: 这家无良的讨债机构继续用恐吓电话骚扰这家人。

items.def_en: (+ on sb) join together as a group to harass, intimidate, or bully sb
items.ex_en: The older school bullies liked to gang up on smaller children during recess.
items.ex_zh: 高年级的校园恶霸喜欢在课间休息时结伙欺负身材矮小的孩子。

items.def_en: (+ sb) treat sb badly, unfairly, or unkindly through repetitive harassment
items.ex_en: Why do the older kids always pick on him during recess?
items.ex_zh: 为什么大孩子们课间总爱找他茬、欺负他？

items.def_en: (+ sb) take cruel advantage of, exploit, or victimize vulnerable individuals
items.ex_en: Dishonest telemarketers often prey on vulnerable elderly residents with deceptive investment schemes.
items.ex_zh: 不诚实的电话推销员经常利用欺诈性的投资骗局侵害易受骗的老年人。

items.def_zh: 用毒气毒害，用毒气杀死
items.def_en: To kill, injure, or attack someone with poisonous gas.
items.ex_en: Authoritarian forces threatened to gas the barricaded protestors hiding inside the underground complex.
items.ex_zh: 独裁势力威胁要用毒气袭击躲藏在地下设施内的设障抗议者。

items.def_zh: 用九尾鞭抽打（惩处或虐待）
items.def_en: To flog or whip someone with a cat-o'-nine-tails.
items.ex_en: The cruel naval commander ordered the boatswain to cat the mutinous sailor severely.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的海军指挥官命令水手长用九尾鞭狠狠抽打叛变的水手。
