items.def_en: 1. To treat a person or animal with cruelty or violence. 2. To speak rudely or insultingly to someone. 3. To use something improperly or excessively.
items.ex_en: The investigation revealed that the corrupt supervisor continued to abuse his subordinates systematically.
items.ex_zh: 调查显示，这位腐败的主管一直在系统性地虐待下属。

items.def_zh: 持续骚扰，不断折磨；反复袭击
items.def_en: To persistently harass, distress, or launch repeated attacks on someone.
items.ex_en: Mounted raiders continued to harry the remote border settlements throughout the harsh winter.
items.ex_zh: 骑兵劫掠者在整个严冬里不断骚扰边境偏远的定居点。

items.def_en: to cause severe physical or mental suffering to someone repeatedly
items.ex_en: Guilt and regret continued to torment the retired detective long after the trial.
items.ex_zh: 审判过去很久之后，内疚与懊悔依然在折磨着这位退休侦探。

items.def_en: to treat someone cruelly and unfairly over a long period, especially for beliefs or identity
items.ex_en: The totalitarian regime sought to persecute political dissidents and suppress all public dissent.
items.ex_zh: 极权政权试图迫害持不同政见者并压制所有公开的异议。

items.def_zh: 使受害，迫害，不公地对待；欺骗
items.def_en: To single someone out for cruel, unfair, or abusive treatment; to make a victim of.
items.ex_en: Corrupt managers sought to victimize the brave whistleblower by denying her earned promotion.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的管理层企图通过拒绝给予应得的晋升来打击报复这位勇敢的举报人。

items.def_zh: 强奸，强暴；肆意蹂躏，破坏
items.def_en: To force someone to have sexual intercourse against their will; to despoil or violate.
items.ex_en: Invading armies sought to rape the fallen city and plunder its sacred treasures.
items.ex_zh: 入侵的军队企图肆意蹂躏这座陷落的城市，并掠夺其神圣的宝藏。

items.def_zh: 恐吓，使惊恐，以暴力威胁；实行恐怖统治
items.def_en: To intimidate, severely frighten, or coerce someone through threats or violence.
items.ex_en: Armed cartels used brutal violence to terrorise local villagers into complete submission.
items.ex_zh: 武装贩毒集团利用残暴手段恐吓当地村民，逼迫他们彻底顺从。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe inflicting persistent physical, psychological, or sexual suffering upon victims, scaling from harassment to catastrophic violence.
groups.summary_zh: 描述对弱势受害者施加身体、精神或性侵犯，体现程度从骚扰到摧残的加剧。
groups.desc_en: Conceptualizes the systematic, malicious, or asymmetrical infliction of mental or physical suffering upon a vulnerable victim, contrasting with fair, balanced adversarial combat.
groups.desc_zh: 指强者凭借不对等地位对弱势方进行的系统性残酷折磨与侵害，区别于公平博弈。
groups.nuance_en: abuse: chronic physical, verbal, or emotional maltreatment exploiting power (child / power / trust) · prey on: predatory exploitation of weakness or innocence (elderly / vulnerable / fears) · harass: unrelenting, tormenting irritation and intrusive pressure (employee / minority / debtor) · harry: constant badgering, raiding, and wearing down (retreating troops / borders / enemy) · gang up: collective pooling of force to bully a lone target (critics / bullies / competitors)
groups.nuance_zh: abuse: 滥用权力施加的长期身心摧残 (child / power / trust) · prey on: 弱肉强食式的寻猎压榨 (elderly / vulnerable / fears) · harass: 持续侵扰逼迫令人不堪其扰 (employee / minority / debtor) · harry: 不断袭扰耗竭敌方心力 (retreating troops / borders / enemy) · gang up: 结伙合谋围攻孤立无援者 (critics / bullies / competitors)

groups.name: Walk & Amble · 漫步与徐行 (Walk, Stroll, Amble)
groups.tip: 闲适缓慢的步行

items.def_en: walk at a slow, relaxed, leisurely pace
items.ex_en: Couples frequently stroll along the historic waterfront promenade on warm summer evenings.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖的夏夜，情侣们经常沿着历史悠久的海滨漫步前行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) walk slowly around an area without any clear purpose or haste
items.ex_en: Foreign tourists often wander around the historic downtown district admiring the colorful architecture.
items.ex_zh: 外国游客经常在历史悠久的市中心街区漫步，欣赏色彩斑斓的建筑。

items.def_en: To walk somewhere in a slow, relaxed, and unhurried way.
items.ex_en: The retired couple likes to stroll through the botanical garden every Sunday morning.
items.ex_zh: 这对退休夫妇喜欢在每个周日早晨漫步穿过植物园。

items.def_zh: 踮着脚尖走，蹑手蹑脚地走
items.def_en: To walk quietly and carefully on the tips of one's toes to avoid making noise.
items.ex_en: She had to tiptoe past the nursery so she would not disturb him.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不蹑手蹑脚地走过育儿室，以免吵醒他。

items.def_zh: 蹑手蹑脚地走动，悄悄潜行
items.def_en: walk very quietly and cautiously, trying not to attract attention
items.ex_en: Suspicious figures were spotted trying to creep around the darkened museum compound late.
items.ex_zh: 有人发现可疑人物深夜在漆黑的博物馆大院周围悄悄潜行。

items.def_zh: 步行，走；散步；遛（狗等）；护送……走
items.def_en: 1. To move forward on foot by taking steps. 2. To take a pet out for exercise; to escort someone on foot.
items.ex_en: Doctors advised the recovering patient to walk thirty minutes every single afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议正在康复的病人每天下午步行三十分钟。

items.def_en: To lift one's foot and place it down in a different position, or to walk a short distance.
items.ex_en: Be careful when you step onto the frozen pond near the edge.
items.ex_zh: 当你踏上靠近岸边的结冰池塘时，一定要小心。

items.def_en: To walk slowly without any clear direction or purpose.
items.ex_en: Visitors often meander through the quiet cobblestone alleys of the ancient village.
items.ex_zh: 游客们经常漫步穿行在古村幽静的鹅卵石小巷中。

items.def_zh: （在公共场所或海滨）漫步，散步
items.def_en: (formal or dated) To walk slowly in a public place, especially for pleasure or to see and be seen by others.
items.ex_en: Wealthy Victorian aristocrats loved to promenade along the seaside pier before high tea.
items.ex_zh: 维多利亚时代的富裕贵族喜欢在下午茶前沿着海滨码头从容漫步。

items.def_en: To walk at a slow, relaxed, and unhurried pace.
items.ex_en: Elderly villagers often amble down to the town square for their morning coffee.
items.ex_zh: 村里的老人经常从容漫步到城镇广场享用他们的早间咖啡。

items.def_en: To walk in a slow, relaxed, confident manner without hurry.
items.ex_en: He liked to saunter into the trendy café with an air of confidence.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢神态自若地漫步走进那家时髦的咖啡馆。

items.def_zh: 进行太空行走，进行舱外活动
items.def_en: To move or perform tasks outside a spacecraft in outer space.
items.ex_en: Trained astronauts had to spacewalk outside the orbital station to replace faulty batteries.
items.ex_zh: 训练有素的宇航员必须在轨道空间站外进行太空行走，以更换故障电池。

items.def_zh: 疲惫地走，拖着步子走；漫游，闲逛
items.def_en: (informal) To walk somewhere slowly, wearily, or reluctantly, often over a long distance.
items.ex_en: Shoppers had to traipse across the rainy city center to find open pharmacies.
items.ex_zh: 购物者不得不冒雨拖着沉重的步子穿过市中心，寻找营业的药店。

groups.summary_en: Manner-of-locomotion verbs characterizing unhurried, leisurely, or stealthy pedestrian movement on foot without intense urgency or aggressive pace.
groups.summary_zh: 指步行移动方式中的悠闲漫步、轻声缓步或游逛行进，不含紧迫狂奔意涵。
groups.desc_en: Delineates unhurried, exploratory, or low-urgency pedestrian movement guided by leisure, observation, or stealth, contrasting with purposeful, hurried marching.
groups.desc_zh: 指无紧迫目的、受闲适心境或隐秘动机驱使的从容徒步，区别于急促坚决的行军赶路。
groups.nuance_en: stroll: leisurely, dignified, and relaxed recreational promenade (park / boulevard / beach) · meander: aimless wandering along a winding, circuitous path (river / tourist / thoughts) · tiptoe: silent, stealthy stepping on the balls of the feet (nursery / corridor / bedroom) · amble: easy, unhurried, and comfortable pacing (path / gardens / lane) · wander: walking without set destination, driven by impulse (streets / wilderness / countryside)
groups.nuance_zh: stroll: 仪态安适的闲庭信步 (park / boulevard / beach) · meander: 蜿蜒曲折、漫无指向的迂回缓行 (river / tourist / thoughts) · tiptoe: 蹑手蹑脚、垫起脚尖的潜行 (nursery / corridor / bedroom) · amble: 从容不迫、缓步徐行的走动 (path / gardens / lane) · wander: 毫无定规的漫游浪荡 (streets / wilderness / countryside)

groups.name: Aimless Rambling & Idle Chatter · 漫谈与闲扯 (Maunder, Natter, Palaver)
groups.tip: 没完没了地说些琐碎废话

items.def_en: to engage in light, informal, sociable conversation about trivial matters
items.ex_en: Colleagues love to chitchat over hot morning coffee before opening their laptops daily.
items.ex_zh: 同事们喜欢在每天打开笔记本电脑前，一边喝着热咖啡一边闲聊家常。

items.def_en: Continue talking about trivial or unimportant things at tedious length
items.ex_en: My talkative neighbor will rabbit on about her stubborn prize cats for hours.
items.ex_zh: 我那个健谈的邻居能没完没了地唠叨她那些倔强的获奖名猫好几个小时。

items.def_zh: 漫无边际地长篇大论，啰嗦不停
items.def_en: Talk or write in a confused or inconsequential way for a long time
items.ex_en: The speaker tended to ramble on about unrelated personal memories during his lecture.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者在讲座中往往会东拉西扯，大谈无关的个人回忆。

items.def_zh: 胡扯，喋喋不休地说废话
items.def_en: Talk foolishly, vaguely, or without purpose for a lengthy period
items.ex_en: The evasive politician began to waffle on about vague reforms without providing details.
items.ex_zh: 那位闪烁其词的政客开始胡扯些空洞的改革，却没给出任何细节。

items.def_en: (+ on/about) to talk at length without staying on topic or reaching a clear point
items.ex_en: The nervous candidate began to ramble about trivial childhood incidents during the interview.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的求职者在面试中开始漫无边际地东拉西扯起童年琐事。

items.def_zh: 空谈，闲聊，没完没了地唠叨；讨价还价，交涉
items.def_en: (dated / informal) To talk at length unnecessarily or engage in idle, complicated chatter.
items.ex_en: We do not have time to palaver over petty office gossip this afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 今天下午我们可没工夫为了微不足道的办公室八卦没完没了地闲扯。

items.def_zh: 闲聊，喋喋不休，漫谈琐事
items.def_en: (British informal) To chat casually and continuously about unimportant things.
items.ex_en: The two old friends loved to natter about gardening over cups of tea.
items.ex_zh: 这两位老朋友喜欢一边喝茶，一边漫谈园艺琐事。

items.raw_cluster: 喋喋不休与闲聊 Chatter & Babble
items.def_en: (dated informal) To talk nonsense or chatter trivially.
items.ex_en: Stop trying to piffle about trivial nonsense and focus on finishing the report.
items.ex_zh: 别再扯那些无聊的废话了，专心把报告完成吧。

items.raw_cluster: 喋喋不休与闲聊 Chatter & Babble
items.def_zh: 啰嗦，胡扯，东拉西扯；漫无目的地游荡
items.def_en: 1. To talk in a rambling, confused, or boring way. 2. To move or wander aimlessly.
items.ex_en: The lonely peddler would often maunder about his vanished youth to completely indifferent strangers.
items.ex_zh: 那位孤独的小贩常向漠不关心的陌生人絮絮叨叨地追忆自己逝去的青春。

items.def_zh: 滔滔不绝地絮叨，单调乏味地讲个不停
items.def_en: Talk for a long time in a monotonous and boring tone
items.ex_en: The boring lecturer seemed to drone on endlessly about outdated nineteenth-century economic theories.
items.ex_zh: 那个乏味的讲师似乎在没完没了、单调乏味地念叨十九世纪过时的经济理论。

items.def_en: (chiefly British) to talk or write redundantly, evasively, and at length without saying anything useful
items.ex_en: The unprepared spokesperson continued to waffle rather than answer the reporter's direct question.
items.ex_zh: 毫无准备的发言人继续废话连篇，而不是回答记者的直接提问。

items.raw_cluster: 闲聊与喋喋不休 Chatter & Babble
items.def_zh: 急促含糊地说话，喋喋不休；急促含糊地说出
items.def_en: To talk very fast and indistinctly so that others cannot easily understand you.
items.ex_en: The terrified witness began to gabble so rapidly that the detectives understood nothing.
items.ex_zh: 受到惊吓的目击者开始急促含糊地说话，以至于侦探们什么也没听懂。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey informal, digressive, time-wasting, or tedious talk—meandering speech that lacks discipline, urgency, or point.
groups.summary_zh: 漫无边际、漫谈闲聊或言不及义地消磨时间的口头闲扯。
groups.desc_en: Captures unstructured, repetitive, or vacuous verbal output that drifts away from logical focus into trivia, contrasting with concise, disciplined discourse.
groups.desc_zh: 指脱离逻辑中心、在琐碎微末处打转的空洞絮叨，区别于精炼清晰的正式表述。
groups.nuance_en: ramble: wandering disjointedly far away from the main point (speech / lecture / speaker) · waffle: evasive, wordy equivocation lacking decisive substance (politician / spokesperson / report) · natter: cozy, informal, continuous social chattering over trivia (neighbors / friends / tea) · palaver: unnecessarily prolonged, fussy negotiation or empty fuss (bureaucrats / meeting / diplomacy) · rabbit on: irritating, endless droning about trivial topics (caller / bore / colleague)
groups.nuance_zh: ramble: 思维涣散、信马由缰地跑题漫扯 (speech / lecture / speaker) · waffle: 语言空洞含糊、回避核心实质 (politician / spokesperson / report) · natter: 亲近随和但没完没了的扯闲篇 (neighbors / friends / tea) · palaver: 徒费口舌的冗长空谈或虚礼交涉 (bureaucrats / meeting / diplomacy) · rabbit on: 令人烦躁地就琐事喋喋不休 (caller / bore / colleague)

groups.name: Annoy, Anger & Drive Mad · 激怒与逼疯 (Annoy, Offend, Enrage, Craze)
groups.tip: 从轻度惹恼到怒不可遏的愤怒升级

items.def_en: 1. To make someone slightly angry or irritated, especially by minor disturbances.
items.ex_en: His constant tapping on the desk began to annoy everyone sitting nearby.
items.ex_zh: 他不停地敲击桌子，开始让坐在附近的每个人都感到烦躁。

items.def_en: to make someone feel impatient, annoyed, or slightly agitated
items.ex_en: The harsh fluorescent lighting seemed to irritate her tired eyes during work.
items.ex_zh: 刺眼的荧光灯似乎在她工作时刺激到了她疲惫的双眼。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Annoy, anger, or irritate someone
items.ex_en: His dismissive attitude during the meeting will definitely tick off the team.
items.ex_zh: 他在会议上轻蔑的态度肯定会惹恼整个团队。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Deliberately tease, irritate, or provoke someone to make them angry
items.ex_en: Stop mocking his accent just to wind him up before the presentation.
items.ex_zh: 别为了在演讲前故意惹火他而嘲笑他的口音了。

items.def_en: 1. To make someone angry. 2. To become angry.
items.ex_en: The manager's unfair criticism will certainly anger the hardworking staff members.
items.ex_zh: 经理不公的批评必定会激怒那些勤奋工作的员工。
items.ex2_en: The proud old warrior angered easily whenever his past courage was questioned.
items.ex2_zh: 每当有人质疑他过去的勇气时，这位骄傲的老战士很容易发怒。

items.def_zh: 冒犯，得罪；触犯（法律、规章）
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel upset, annoyed, or insulted. 2. To commit an illegal act or break a rule.
items.ex_en: He did not mean to offend anyone with his blunt and honest comment.
items.ex_zh: 他那直率坦白的评论并非有意要冒犯任何人。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Cause someone to become extremely agitated, distraught, or wildly irrational
items.ex_en: The terrifying roar of thunder suddenly began to freak out the young children.
items.ex_zh: 可怕的雷声突然开始让这群小孩子吓得极度抓狂。
items.ex2_en: She began to freak out when her apartment lights suddenly went out.
items.ex2_zh: 当公寓里的灯突然熄灭时，她开始吓得六神无主。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Annoy, irritate, or infuriate someone greatly
items.ex_en: Losing my house keys for the third time this week really pissed me off.
items.ex_zh: 这周第三次弄丢房门钥匙真让我火冒三丈。

items.raw_cluster: 使发狂与激怒 Madden & Craze
items.def_zh: 使发狂，使狂热；（使陶瓷等表面）产生细裂纹
items.def_en: 1. (literary) To make someone wildly excited or mentally deranged. 2. (of ceramics or glazed surfaces) To develop a network of fine cracks, or cause to do so.
items.ex_en: Prolonged isolation and gnawing hunger threatened to craze the stranded explorer completely.
items.ex_zh: 长期的孤立与噬骨的饥饿几欲使这位受困的探险家完全发狂。
items.ex2_en: The delicate porcelain glaze crazed naturally after decades of temperature fluctuations.
items.ex2_zh: 经过数十年的温度波动，精致的瓷器釉面自然产生了开裂细纹。

items.def_en: to make someone extremely angry, furious, and indignant
items.ex_en: The sudden delay of our connecting flight will infuriate all the tired passengers.
items.ex_zh: 我们中转航班的突然延误会让所有疲惫的乘客怒火中烧。

items.def_en: to exasperate someone to the brink of insanity or total loss of self-control
items.ex_en: The neighbor's barking dog is going to drive me completely mad today.
items.ex_zh: 邻居家那只吠叫不止的狗今天真要把我逼疯了。

items.def_en: to fill someone with vehement fury and violent rage
items.ex_en: The scandalous corruption revelations enrage citizens across the entire beleaguered nation.
items.ex_zh: 骇人听闻的腐败丑闻曝光，激怒了整个陷入困境的国家的人民。

groups.summary_en: Causing increasing levels of displeasure, anger, and loss of composure in another person, ascending from mild irritation and wounded dignity to blinding fury and mental derangement.
groups.summary_zh: 从轻微恼人、冒犯尊严递进至狂暴震怒乃至发疯
groups.desc_en: Depicts psychological agitation progressing from mild friction and exasperation to explosive fury or mental derangement, contrasting with calm composure.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘情绪从微小的摩擦不适向极度狂暴或失智状态不断升级的激化过程，区别于平和宁静。
groups.nuance_en: irritate: persistent minor friction producing raw chafing impatience (skin / habit / tone) · offend: wounding moral sensibilities, self-esteem, or propriety (dignity / values / host) · enrage: inciting incandescent, blind fury and violent anger (mob / populace / rival) · wind up: deliberate teasing or baiting to provoke a reaction (opponent / sibling / player) · freak out: plunging into sudden hysteria, panic, or mental destabilization (passengers / crowd / parents)
groups.nuance_zh: irritate: 琐屑言行带来的持续刺痛与毛躁 (skin / habit / tone) · offend: 触犯自尊、冒犯道德或礼数底线 (dignity / values / host) · enrage: 激起暴跳如雷的滔天怒火 (mob / populace / rival) · wind up: 故意撩拨设套挑动其情绪失控 (opponent / sibling / player) · freak out: 陷入骤然的恐慌失常或精神崩溃 (passengers / crowd / parents)

groups.name: Appear & Emerge · 出现与显露 (Loom, Surface, Crop up)
groups.tip: 从隐蔽中浮现或露面

items.def_en: to appear or occur unexpectedly or unexpectedly frequently
items.ex_en: Unexpected financial emergencies always seem to crop up at the worst possible times.
items.ex_zh: 意想不到的财务紧急状况似乎总是在最糟糕的时刻突然冒出来。

items.def_en: Appear or occur suddenly and unexpectedly
items.ex_en: These error messages keep popping up on my screen.
items.ex_zh: 这些错误提示一直在我的屏幕上弹出来。

items.def_en: Arrive or make an appearance at an event or place
items.ex_en: He promised to attend the party, but failed to show up at all.
items.ex_zh: 他答应过会来参加聚会，但结果根本没有露面。

items.def_en: Appear, develop, or come into existence quickly and suddenly
items.ex_en: Dozens of trendy coffee shops spring up along the vibrant downtown avenue.
items.ex_zh: 数十家时髦的咖啡馆在这条充满活力的市中心大道上迅速涌现。

items.def_en: Appear or be found, often unexpectedly or after a search
items.ex_en: My lost passport might turn up somewhere inside the messy office drawers.
items.ex_zh: 我丢失的护照可能会在凌乱的办公室抽屉里的某个地方冒出来。
items.ex2_en: Please turn up the central heating thermostat because this basement room feels chilly.
items.ex2_zh: 请把中央暖气温控器调高一些，因为这间地下室感觉挺冷的。

items.def_zh: 出现，显现；显得，看来；出庭，出场
items.def_en: 1. To become visible or come into sight. 2. To seem or give a particular impression. 3. To present oneself publicly or in court.
items.ex_en: Dark rain clouds appear on the eastern horizon just before sunset today.
items.ex_zh: 今天日落前夕，乌黑的雨云出现在了东边的地平线上。

items.def_en: to rise to the surface of water, or to become visible after being hidden
items.ex_en: Fresh allegations of corporate fraud surface during the ongoing federal investigation.
items.ex_zh: 在持续进行的联邦调查中，关于企业欺诈的新指控浮出了水面。

items.def_en: 1. (+ in/from/with) To come into existence, start, or arise from a specific source. 2. To create, invent, or initiate something new.
items.ex_en: Many ancient cultural traditions originate from primitive rituals celebrating agricultural harvests.
items.ex_zh: 许多古老的文化传统起源于庆祝农业丰收的原始仪式。

items.def_zh: 显现，出现（hove into sight/view，heave的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: (nautical / literary) Past tense and past participle of heave; used in 'hove into sight/view' meaning to come into view or appear gradually.
items.ex_en: Through the dense sea mist, a massive ghost ship hove into sight.
items.ex_zh: 透过浓重的大海迷雾，一艘巨大的幽灵船赫然显现在眼前。

items.def_zh: 浮现，显露，出现；（事实等）暴露
items.def_en: 1. (+ from) To come out of an enclosed, dark, or hidden place into view. 2. (of facts or ideas) To become known or apparent.
items.ex_en: Startling details emerge from the recently declassified government intelligence report.
items.ex_zh: 令人震惊的细节从最近解密的政府情报报告中显露出来。

items.def_en: to appear as a shadowy form, especially one that is large or threatening
items.ex_en: Dark storm clouds loom menacingly over the ancient mountain peaks tonight.
items.ex_zh: 今夜，黑压压的暴风雨云阴森可怖地笼罩在古老山峰之上。

items.def_zh: 突然显现，出现；实现，成为现实
items.def_en: 1. (British English spelling of materialize) To appear suddenly, often in an unexpected or magical way. 2. To actually happen or become a reality.
items.ex_en: A mysterious figure seemed to materialise out of the swirling grey fog.
items.ex_zh: 一个神秘的身影仿佛从翻滚的灰雾中凭空幻化显现。
items.ex2_en: The director worked hard to materialise his abstract artistic vision on film.
items.ex2_zh: 导演努力工作，将他抽象的艺术构想在电影中具象化展现出来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify how an entity enters perception or existence—whether coming into view gradually, rising to the surface, showing up unexpectedly, or looming ominously.
groups.summary_zh: 指主体以某种特定方式进入视野或显露存在（如浮现、逼近隐现或突现）。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the manner, speed, and sudden perceptibility with which an entity manifests into sight or awareness, contrasting with static existence or gradual development.
groups.desc_zh: 聚焦事物显露于视野或意识中的方式、突发性与可见度，与静态的存在或渐进的发展相对。
groups.nuance_en: crop up: arise unexpectedly as an annoyance or impediment (problems / complications / questions) · pop up: appear suddenly, briefly, or ubiquitously (ads / notifications / windows) · surface: rise to the level of public awareness or visibility from concealment (rumors / allegations / tensions) · spring up: proliferate or emerge rapidly in great numbers (buildings / businesses / trends) · turn up: arrive or be recovered unexpectedly after absence (lost keys / evidence / missing person)
groups.nuance_zh: crop up: 突然冒出并带来困扰 (problems / complications / questions) · pop up: 突兀、短暂或遍地弹出显现 (ads / notifications / windows) · surface: 潜伏后浮出水面为人所知 (rumors / allegations / tensions) · spring up: 迅速大量涌现或拔地而起 (buildings / businesses / trends) · turn up: 失踪或寻觅后意外露面或被找回 (lost keys / evidence / missing person)

groups.name: Attack & Assault · 袭击与进攻 (Attack, Charge, Assault)
groups.tip: 发起攻击与突袭侵入

items.def_en: [I/T] to carry out a sudden military attack or offensive action against a target
items.ex_en: Allied fighter jets prepare to strike key strategic enemy positions at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 盟军战斗机准备在破晓时分对敌军的关键战略阵地发起打击。

items.def_en: to attack someone by surprise from a concealed position
items.ex_en: Rebel forces hide in the dense jungle to ambush the passing convoy.
items.ex_zh: 叛军潜伏在茂密的丛林中，企图伏击途经的车队。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack an enemy or victim suddenly, catching them by surprise
items.ex_en: The fierce predators fall on the unsuspecting herd under cover of darkness.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的掠食者借着夜色的掩护突袭了毫无防备的兽群。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack sb suddenly and violently
items.ex_en: The rogue bandits set upon the weary travelers in the dark alley.
items.ex_zh: 流窜的匪徒在黑暗的小巷中猛然扑向了疲惫的旅人。

items.def_en: (+ on sb/sth) descend suddenly and swiftly in an unexpected raid or attack
items.ex_en: The giant eagle prepares to swoop down on its unsuspecting small prey.
items.ex_zh: 巨鹰准备俯冲突袭毫无防备的小型猎物。

items.def_en: 1. To use violence to try to hurt, defeat, or destroy someone or something. 2. To criticize someone or something strongly.
items.ex_en: Hostile military troops attack the fortified border outpost without any warning.
items.ex_zh: 敌对部队在未发出任何警告的情况下攻击了坚固的边境哨所。

items.def_zh: 冲锋，猛冲；收费；指控；充电
items.def_en: 1. To rush forward in a sudden, violent attack. 2. To ask an amount of money for goods or a service. 3. To officially accuse someone of a crime.
items.ex_en: Frightened soldiers watch the enemy cavalry charge across the muddy open battlefield.
items.ex_zh: 惊恐的士兵们看着敌军骑兵猛冲过泥泞开阔的战场。

items.def_en: to attack and enter a fortified place suddenly and with overwhelming force
items.ex_en: Elite special forces storm the terrorist stronghold to rescue the trapped hostages.
items.ex_zh: 特种精英部队强攻恐怖分子的据点，以营救被困人质。

items.def_en: To attack someone violently and physically.
items.ex_en: The masked suspects attempt to assault the security guards outside the bank.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面嫌疑人企图在银行外暴力袭击保安人员。

items.def_en: To make a sudden surprise attack on a place, or enter a place unexpectedly to arrest people or seize illegal goods.
items.ex_en: Federal agents raid the abandoned warehouse in search of illegal counterfeit weapons.
items.ex_zh: 联邦探员突击搜查了那座废弃仓库，以搜查非法的违禁武器。

items.def_zh: （动物等）凶猛攻击，撕咬；猛烈抨击
items.def_en: 1. (especially of an animal) To attack someone violently and cause severe injuries. 2. To criticize something or someone very harshly.
items.ex_en: A stray dog managed to savage the postman during his morning deliveries.
items.ex_zh: 一只流浪狗在邮递员早间送信时凶猛地撕咬了他。

items.def_zh: 武力入侵，侵略；涌入；侵扰
items.def_en: 1. To enter a country or territory by military force to conquer or occupy it. 2. To enter a place in large numbers, often in an unwelcome or disruptive way.
items.ex_en: Foreign troops cross the disputed river boundary to invade the sovereign nation.
items.ex_zh: 外国军队越过有争议的界河，入侵了这个主权国家。

groups.summary_en: An agent launches hostile, violent physical action against an opponent or territory to inflict injury, defeat, or capture. Verbs vary in tactical manner—from sudden localized raids and rapid rushes to brutal physical beatings or massive territorial invasions.
groups.summary_zh: 描述以武力对敌方目标或地盘发起进攻、突袭或猛攻。
groups.desc_en: Denotes violent, offensive kinetic movement directed against an adversary, differing from mere verbal confrontation or sustained military campaigning.
groups.desc_zh: 强调针对敌对目标的突发、剧烈动能攻势，与单纯的口头冲突或持久的战役运作相对。
groups.nuance_en: strike: deliver a sudden, decisive kinetic blow (target / enemy base / infrastructure) · ambush: launch a surprise assault from concealed positions (patrol / convoy / troops) · charge: rush forward directly and aggressively in force (cavalry / barricades / lines) · storm: violently capture a fortified place by overwhelming frontal assault (fortress / building / citadel) · swoop down: descend rapidly from above in a predatory pounce (aircraft / raptor / invaders)
groups.nuance_zh: strike: 实施迅雷不及掩耳的决定性打击 (target / enemy base / infrastructure) · ambush: 设伏伏击毫无防备之敌 (patrol / convoy / troops) · charge: 集中力量正面猛烈冲锋 (cavalry / barricades / lines) · storm: 强行强攻并攻陷坚固堡垒 (fortress / building / citadel) · swoop down: 如猛禽俯冲般从高处突袭掠杀 (aircraft / raptor / invaders)

groups.name: Attest & Corroborate · 证实与证明 (Confirm, Verify, Certify)
groups.tip: 提供证据以证实说法属实

items.def_en: (formal) to give evidence of or serve as proof of something
items.ex_en: These archaeological discoveries evidence the presence of advanced civilization in this valley.
items.ex_zh: 这些考古发现证实了该山谷中曾存在过高度发达的文明。

items.def_en: to state or prove that something is true, correct, or definite
items.ex_en: Subsequent genetic laboratory results confirm the doctor's initial diagnosis of the rare illness.
items.ex_zh: 随后的基因实验室结果证实了医生对该罕见病症的初步诊断。

items.def_zh: （出具文件）证明，证实；给……颁发合格证书
items.def_en: to state or declare officially in writing that something is true, accurate, or of a high standard
items.ex_en: Authorized civil medical inspectors certify the newly renovated hospital facilities as sterile.
items.ex_zh: 官方授权的民事医疗检查员出具文件证明翻新后的医院设施符合无菌标准。

items.def_en: to check or prove that something is true or accurate
items.ex_en: The banking software will verify your identity before processing the overseas transfer.
items.ex_zh: 银行软件将在处理海外转账前核实您的身份。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Assert or confirm the truth, accuracy, or good character of someone or something
items.ex_en: Several respected senior colleagues will gladly vouch for his honesty and reliability.
items.ex_zh: 几位受人尊敬的资深同事很乐意为他的诚实和可靠作保。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Support or confirm the truth of an assertion, prediction, or hypothesis
items.ex_en: The final audit results bore out all our initial suspicions about financial mismanagement.
items.ex_zh: 最终的审计结果证实了我们最初对财务管理不善的所有怀疑。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Provide clear evidence or formal testimony of the truth of something
items.ex_en: Numerous impressive customer reviews attest to the remarkable durability of this product.
items.ex_zh: 众多令人印象深刻的客户评价证实了该产品卓越的耐用性。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Serve as evidence or proof of a fact or condition
items.ex_en: These remarkably preserved historic documents testify to the harsh realities of wartime life.
items.ex_zh: 这些保存完好的历史文件有力证明了战时生活的残酷现实。

items.def_en: to check or formally prove the accuracy, validity, or sound basis of something
items.ex_en: Further rigorous scientific experiments are required to validate the novel biochemical hypothesis.
items.ex_zh: 需要进行更严格的科学实验来验证这一新颖的生物化学假说。

items.def_zh: 证实，确证（提供补充证据）
items.def_en: to support or confirm a statement, theory, or finding with additional evidence
items.ex_en: Recent independent witness testimonies corroborate the complex timeline provided by the detective.
items.ex_zh: 最新的独立证人证词证实了侦探所提供的复杂时间线。

items.def_zh: 担保，证明属实（常与 for 连用）
items.def_en: (+ for) to state that you believe someone or something is good, true, or reliable
items.ex_en: My former employer is completely willing to vouch for my professional capabilities.
items.ex_zh: 我的前雇主完全愿意为我的专业能力担保。

items.def_en: to provide concrete facts or proof to demonstrate the truth of a claim or allegation
items.ex_en: The defense attorney failed to substantiate the controversial claim with physical evidence.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师未能用实物证据来证实这一备受争议的主张。

groups.summary_en: An agent, document, or piece of evidence establishes the truth, accuracy, or authenticity of a statement, claim, or official status. Nuances vary from institutional certification to factual corroboration or personal endorsement.
groups.summary_zh: 依凭凭据、权威审查或担保来确立事实真实性。
groups.desc_en: Involves supplying confirmatory evidence, formal authority, or testimony to substantiate truth, differing from mere subjective belief or unsubstantiated assertion.
groups.desc_zh: 通过呈递确凿证据、权威背书或证言来证实真实性，与主观信念或无根据的断言相对。
groups.nuance_en: verify: ascertain or test factual accuracy through empirical checking (identity / calculations / facts) · attest to: affirm under oath or provide authentic evidence of existence (character / validity / signature) · corroborate: strengthen or support existing claims with independent data (alibi / testimony / findings) · certify: guarantee officially and formally in writing (documents / competence / products) · bear out: validate or confirm an earlier prediction or hypothesis through reality (theory / suspicion / prediction)
groups.nuance_zh: verify: 经核查或比对求证真实性 (identity / calculations / facts) · attest to: 宣誓确认或作为凭证以证明 (character / validity / signature) · corroborate: 以旁证或独立数据印证支持现有说法 (alibi / testimony / findings) · certify: 官方出具正式文书予以认定认证 (documents / competence / products) · bear out: 事实印证前情预测或假说 (theory / suspicion / prediction)

groups.name: Beautify & Embellish · 美化与装饰
groups.tip: 通过修饰提升外观

items.def_zh: 在（糕点等）上涂糖霜；冰镇；使结冰；结冰
items.def_en: 1. To decorate a cake or pastry with icing or frosting. 2. To cool or chill food or drinks with ice. 3. (often ice over/up) To cover with ice or freeze.
items.ex_en: The talented pastry chef plans to ice the layered wedding cake beautifully.
items.ex_zh: 这位才华横溢的点心师计划给多层婚礼蛋糕涂上精美的糖霜。
items.ex2_en: The shallow puddle iced quickly as temperatures plunged well below freezing overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 夜间气温骤降至冰点以下，浅浅的水坑很快结上了冰。

items.def_zh: 对……进行景观美化，美化（环境等）；做景观美化工作
items.def_en: To improve the appearance of a piece of land or garden by planting trees, shrubs, or adding decorative features.
items.ex_en: They hired skilled local gardeners to landscape the neglected backyard area properly.
items.ex_zh: 他们聘请了经验丰富的当地园丁，对荒废的后院进行妥善的景观美化。

items.def_en: make someone or something look clean, neat, and smart
items.ex_en: We should spruce up the living room before our dinner guests arrive.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该在晚餐客人到达之前把客厅收拾整洁漂亮。

items.def_en: make something appear more attractive, often cosmetically or superficially
items.ex_en: A fresh coat of paint will quickly pretty up this dingy hallway.
items.ex_zh: 刷上一层新油漆能很快把这条昏暗的走廊修饰得更好看。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Decorate or dress someone or something in an elaborate or festive manner
items.ex_en: The excited organizers deck out the grand banquet hall in shimmering silver.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的组织者们用闪亮的银饰把大宴会厅盛装装点起来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Dress someone or oneself in very attractive or fancy clothing and makeup
items.ex_en: She took hours to doll herself up for the prestigious annual gala.
items.ex_zh: 她花了数小时把自己盛装打扮，去参加盛大的年度晚会。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Enhance, decorate, or dress something in a showy or attractive way
items.ex_en: They decided to gussy up the plain venue with elaborate floral arrangements.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定用繁复的花艺布置来把朴素的场地精心修饰一番。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Repair, decorate, or improve the appearance of a room or building
items.ex_en: The young couple bought an old cottage intending to do it up.
items.ex_zh: 这对年轻夫妇买下了一间老旧农舍，打算好好翻新装饰一番。

items.def_en: make something look more attractive by putting things on it or painting it
items.ex_en: The children love to decorate the fragrant pine tree with colorful ornaments.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们喜欢用彩色的饰物来装点散发着香气的松树。

items.def_en: make more beautiful or attractive by adding ornaments, jewels, or features
items.ex_en: Delicate pearl necklaces and sparkling emeralds adorn the regal queen's slender neck.
items.ex_zh: 精致的珍珠项链和璀璨的祖母绿佩饰在端庄王后的纤细颈项上。

items.def_en: make something more attractive by the addition of decorative details or features
items.ex_en: Artisans embellish the sacred wooden temple doors with intricate golden floral carvings.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们用精细的金色花卉雕刻来美化神圣的木制庙门。

items.def_en: To make someone or something more beautiful, appealing, or attractive.
items.ex_en: The municipal committee launched a civic initiative to beautify the urban parks.
items.ex_zh: 市政委员会发起了一项旨在美化城市公园的市民倡议。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to enhancing the aesthetic appeal of an object, surface, space, or person through alteration, adornment, or specialized decorative treatment.
groups.summary_zh: 通过添加装饰、整修或特殊工艺使人、物体或环境显得更加美观。
groups.desc_en: Depicts informal, cosmetic, or scenario-specific enhancements of appearance, contrasting with fundamental structural renovation or permanent artistic creation.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘非正式、表面化或特定场景下的修饰与打扮，与本质上的结构改造或恒久艺术创作相对。
groups.nuance_en: spruce up: tidy, clean, or refresh an existing space or person smartly (room / garden / image) · deck out: dress or festoon elaborately for special celebration (hall / float / guests) · doll up: groom and dress a person up glamorously, often ostentatiously (outfit / oneself / date) · landscape: redesign an outdoor terrain for aesthetic appeal (grounds / backyard / campus) · ice: coat confectionery smoothly with decorative sugary icing (cake / cupcakes / cookies)
groups.nuance_zh: spruce up: 整理刷洗使焕然一新 (room / garden / image) · deck out: 为庆典华丽盛装或披红挂彩 (hall / float / guests) · doll up: 浓妆艳抹、花哨打扮 (outfit / oneself / date) · landscape: 营建或改造户外园林景观 (grounds / backyard / campus) · ice: 涂抹糖霜以装饰甜点 (cake / cupcakes / cookies)

groups.name: Beg & Cadge · 乞求与蹭取 (Obtaining by Importunity)
groups.tip: 靠软磨硬泡讨要或蹭得利益

items.def_en: (+ sb) Ask for and obtain small items or money from someone for free
items.ex_en: He managed to bum ten dollars off his wealthy classmate for lunch.
items.ex_zh: 他设法从阔绰的同班同学那里蹭讨到了十美元去吃午饭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Manage to collect or obtain something needed by begging or foraging
items.ex_en: We barely managed to scrounge up enough change to pay the fare.
items.ex_zh: 我们好不容易才东拼西凑凑齐了足够的零钱来付车费。

items.def_en: (informal) to ask for and obtain a cigarette, a ride, or petty money from someone
items.ex_en: The penniless student asked to bum a cigarette from the friendly stranger.
items.ex_zh: 那个身无分文的学生向那位友善的陌生人讨要了一支香烟。

items.def_zh: 乞求，蹭取（钱或食物）；四处寻觅，搜找
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To obtain food, money, or goods by begging or taking advantage of others. 2. To search around in order to find something useful.
items.ex_en: He relies on good friends to scrounge a meal whenever funds vanish.
items.ex_zh: 每当资金告罄时，他便依赖好友去蹭口饭吃。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Get food, money, or favors from someone without paying or reciprocating
items.ex_en: The lazy roommate continues to mooch food off us without contributing anything.
items.ex_zh: 那个懒惰的室友继续蹭吃蹭喝我们的食物，却没做任何贡献。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Obtain money, food, or shelter from someone parasitically without paying
items.ex_en: He continues to sponge off his aging grandparents instead of seeking work.
items.ex_zh: 他不但不去找工作，反而继续向年迈的祖父母蹭吃蹭喝白占便宜。

items.def_en: (+ off/on) to repeatedly get money, food, or shelter from others without giving back
items.ex_en: The lazy relative intends to sponge off generous family members every summer.
items.ex_zh: 那个懒惰的亲戚每年夏天都打算在慷慨的家人身上揩油白吃白喝。

items.def_en: (+ off) to ask for and get things for free from acquaintances rather than paying
items.ex_en: He always tries to mooch cigarettes off his coworkers during lunch breaks.
items.ex_zh: 他午休时总是试图向同事蹭烟抽。

items.def_en: (informal, disapproving) (often followed by 'off' or 'on') To rely on others for free food, money, or accommodation without giving anything in return.
items.ex_en: Her brother continued to freeload off their aging parents well into his thirties.
items.ex_zh: 她弟弟三十好几了还继续在年迈的父母那里白吃白喝。

items.def_en: (informal, chiefly North American) To beg, cadge, or freeload money, food, or favors from others.
items.ex_en: He managed to schnorr a free dinner from his wealthy college roommate.
items.ex_zh: 他设法从富有的大学室友那里蹭到了一顿免费晚餐。

items.def_zh: 讨要，白讨，蹭取（烟、钱或食物）
items.def_en: (informal) (often followed by 'off' or 'from') To ask for and obtain something, such as money, food, or cigarettes, for free without intending to pay back.
items.ex_en: Can I cadge a couple of dollars from you for bus fare?
items.ex_zh: 我能向你讨几块钱坐公交车吗？

items.def_en: to stop people in public places and ask them directly for spare money
items.ex_en: He spent the cold afternoon trying to panhandle spare change outside the station.
items.ex_zh: 他在寒冷的下午守在车站外，试图向路人乞讨零钱。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe getting food, money, or favors from others through petty begging, sponging, or opportunistic pleading without paying or contributing.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过乞求、占便宜、吃软饭或蹭取方式无偿获取钱物或食宿。
groups.desc_en: Refers to acquiring small items, money, or favors through persistent importunity, parasitic coaxing, or scavenging rather than earning, trade, or overt force.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过软磨硬泡、寄生揩油或四处淘弄来索取微小物品或好处，与诚实赚取、交易或强取豪夺相对。
groups.nuance_en: bum: extract small consumable favors casually with shameless familiarity (cigarette / ride / buck) · mooch: habitually live off or solicit unearned benefits parasitically (meals / money / couch) · scrounge: forage around persistently to scrape together scarce items (supplies / tickets / cash) · sponge off: exploit someone's hospitality or wealth continuously as a deadbeat (parents / friends / relatives)
groups.nuance_zh: bum: 随手讨要、蹭用小零碎 (cigarette / ride / buck) · mooch: 习惯性白嫖、蹭吃蹭喝 (meals / money / couch) · scrounge: 四处搜寻凑齐急缺物品 (supplies / tickets / cash) · sponge off: 寄生吸血般占熟人便宜度日 (parents / friends / relatives)

groups.name: Beg & Plead · 乞求与恳求 (Entreat, Implore, Beseech)
groups.tip: 从虔诚祈告递进到苦苦乞求

items.def_en: ask politely or plead to be excused from an obligation, invitation, or duty
items.ex_en: She had to beg off the committee meeting due to a sudden migraine.
items.ex_zh: 由于突发偏头痛，她不得不告假推脱了委员会会议。

items.def_en: (+ sb to do sth) appeal formally or urgently to sb to take action
items.ex_en: The ambassador called on both nations to respect the established ceasefire agreement immediately.
items.ex_zh: 大使郑重呼吁两国立即遵守既定的停火协议。

items.def_en: 1. To beg or plead with someone earnestly. 2. To speak to a god in order to give thanks or ask for help.
items.ex_en: We pray that you reconsider your harsh decision before taking formal action.
items.ex_zh: 我们恳求你在采取正式行动前重新考虑你那严厉的决定。

items.def_en: To make a formal request to an authority, a court, or someone in power, especially by submitting a written petition.
items.ex_en: Local residents decided to petition the municipal council for improved street lighting.
items.ex_zh: 当地居民决定向市议会递交请愿书，正式请求改善街道照明。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ with/for) to make an urgent, emotional statement asking for something
items.ex_en: The desperate mother pleaded with the judge for leniency regarding her son.
items.ex_zh: 这位绝望的母亲向法官苦苦恳求，希望对她的儿子从轻发落。

items.def_en: to ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something
items.ex_en: The captive entreated the guards to grant him a single cup of water.
items.ex_zh: 俘虏恳请守卫赐给他一杯水。

items.def_en: (+ for sth) make an urgent, desperate plea or appeal for help or relief
items.ex_en: The famine-stricken villagers cried out for urgent humanitarian assistance from the international community.
items.ex_zh: 饱受饥荒折磨的村民们大声呼吁国际社会提供紧急人道主义援助。

items.def_en: 1. To ask someone very anxiously or earnestly for something. 2. To ask people for money or food, especially in a public place.
items.ex_en: She begged her manager for another chance to prove her professional capabilities.
items.ex_zh: 她恳求经理再给她一次证明自身专业能力的机会。

items.def_en: to beg someone urgently or desperately to do something
items.ex_en: The defense attorney implored the jury not to convict an innocent young man.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师哀求陪审团切勿给一个无辜的年轻人定罪。

items.def_en: to ask someone urgently and fervently to do something, typically in a formal or literary register
items.ex_en: I beseech your majesty to spare the lives of these loyal fallen soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 臣跪求陛下饶恕这些忠诚战败士兵的性命。

items.def_en: To ask or beg humbly and earnestly for something, especially from someone in authority or from God.
items.ex_en: The penitent knelt before the altar to supplicate the Almighty for divine forgiveness.
items.ex_zh: 忏悔者跪在祭坛前，谦卑地祈求全能的上帝赐予宽恕。

items.def_zh: 强求，纠缠，没完没了地恳求
items.def_en: To ask someone persistently and urgently for something, often to the point of annoyance.
items.ex_en: Creditors continued to importune the bankrupt merchant with daily demands for immediate repayment.
items.ex_zh: 债权人每天没完没了地纠缠这位破产商人，强求其立即还债。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe an agent urgently, humbly, or desperately asking someone for mercy, help, or a favor, ranging from formal petitions to desperate emotional begging.
groups.summary_zh: 表示主体出于卑微、迫切或绝望的情绪向他人恳求、求情或告贷，依语气急迫度递增。
groups.desc_en: Encapsulates earnest, deferential, or desperate appeals for mercy, aid, or favors, distinguished by an explicit hierarchy or vulnerability from neutral demanding or requesting.
groups.desc_zh: 体现向对方卑微、急迫或极度恳求宽恕、援助的情感张力，以显性权力差或脆弱地位区别于中性要求或请求。
groups.nuance_en: plead: appeal desperately based on emotion, helplessness, or formal defense (innocence / mercy / cause) · entreat: appeal earnestly and solicitously with grave respect (ruler / mentor / captor) · beseech: beg with desperate, urgent anguish (aid / forgiveness / protection) · petition: formally request through an official collective appeal (court / government / parliament) · beg off: ask politely to be excused from a commitment (invitation / duty / obligation)
groups.nuance_zh: plead: 绝望且动之以情地哀求或辩解 (innocence / mercy / cause) · entreat: 郑重谦恭、苦口婆心地恳求 (ruler / mentor / captor) · beseech: 焦灼凄切地央告乞援 (aid / forgiveness / protection) · petition: 呈递正式请愿书向当局申诉 (court / government / parliament) · beg off: 委婉求免除既定义务或活动 (invitation / duty / obligation)

groups.name: Biological Reproduction & Calving · 生育与繁殖 (Fertilize, Calve, Farrow, Pup)
groups.tip: 新生命的孕育与生产

items.def_en: (of a female dog or carnivorous mammal) To give birth to puppies or offspring
items.ex_en: The solitary hound whelped six healthy pups deep inside the sheltered cave.
items.ex_zh: 那只孤零零的猎犬在隐蔽的山洞深处产下了六只健壮的幼崽。

items.def_en: produce and bring forth young or offspring from the body
items.ex_en: The mare gave birth to a healthy black foal early yesterday morning.
items.ex_zh: 那匹母马昨天清晨产下了一匹健康的小黑马。

items.def_en: (of livestock or female animals) give birth to a young animal
items.ex_en: I can drop you off at the station on my way to work.
items.ex_zh: 我上班顺路可以把你送到车站下车。

items.def_en: 1. (of a wild animal such as a fox, bear, or lion) To give birth to young.
items.ex_en: The mother bear cubbed two tiny offspring within her secluded winter den.
items.ex_zh: 母熊在隐蔽的冬眠巢穴里产下了两只幼崽。

items.def_en: (of fish, frogs, or mollusks) To release or deposit eggs
items.ex_en: Every autumn, adult salmon swim upstream against strong currents to spawn their eggs.
items.ex_zh: 每年秋天，成年鲑鱼都会逆流而上产卵。

items.def_en: 1. (of a female cat) To give birth to kittens.
items.ex_en: The pampered tabby cat kittened four ginger babies beneath the bedroom wardrobe.
items.ex_zh: 那只受宠的虎斑猫在卧室衣柜下产下了四只黄色小猫。

items.def_en: 1. (of an animal such as a dog, fox, or seal) To give birth to pups.
items.ex_en: The female seal pupped quietly upon the vast, windswept Arctic ice floe.
items.ex_zh: 母海豹在狂风呼啸的北极浮冰上悄然产下了幼崽。

items.def_zh: 使受精，使受粉；施肥于，使肥沃
items.def_en: 1. To join sperm or pollen with an egg or plant cell so that young or seeds can develop. 2. To add nutrients or fertilizer to soil to make plants grow well.
items.ex_en: A single vigorous sperm cell must penetrate the protective membrane to fertilize the egg.
items.ex_zh: 单个充满活力的精子必须穿透保护膜才能使卵子受精。

items.def_en: (of a mare or female donkey) To give birth to a foal
items.ex_en: The champion thoroughbred foaled without any complications under the veterinarian’s watchful care.
items.ex_zh: 在兽医的精心照料下，那匹纯种冠军母马顺利产下幼驹。

items.def_en: 1. (of a sow) To give birth to a litter of piglets.
items.ex_en: The prize-winning Berkshire sow farrowed ten vigorous piglets in the clean straw.
items.ex_zh: 那头获奖的伯克希尔母猪在干净的稻草堆上产下了十头健壮的小猪。

items.def_zh: （牛、鲸等）产崽；（冰川、冰山）崩解，脱落
items.def_en: 1. (of a cow, whale, or elephant) To give birth to a calf. 2. (of a glacier or iceberg) To break off a mass of ice.
items.ex_en: The pregnant dairy cow is expected to calve sometime before next Thursday.
items.ex_zh: 预计那头怀孕的奶牛将在下周四之前产崽。

items.def_en: 1. (of a female mammal) To produce and discharge a mature egg from an ovary.
items.ex_en: Hormonal shifts indicate that the patient will likely ovulate within twenty-four hours.
items.ex_zh: 激素变化表明该患者很可能在二十四小时内排卵。

groups.summary_en: Terms situated in biological and animal husbandry contexts depicting the physiological stages of conception, gamete release, and the birth of specific animal litters or young.
groups.summary_zh: 农牧与生物繁衍语境中，指受精、排卵或特定兽类分娩产仔的生理过程。
groups.desc_en: Specifies biological parturition or offspring delivery tailored to specific zoological species, contrasting with generic mammalian birth or clinical delivery.
groups.desc_zh: 专指特定动物物种的分娩与繁衍产仔方式，与泛指的人类或通用哺乳动物生育概念相对。
groups.nuance_en: spawn: release vast clusters of eggs or milt in water (salmon / amphibians / coral) · whelp: give birth specifically as a carnivore, especially a dog (puppies / litter / bitch) · pup: give birth specifically to seals, dogs, or small canines (colony / seal / pups) · kitten: give birth specifically to cats (queen / litter / kittens) · fertilize: introduce sperm or pollen into an egg to initiate development (egg / ovum / soil)
groups.nuance_zh: spawn: 水生生物产卵或排精繁衍 (salmon / amphibians / coral) · whelp: 犬科或肉食动物产下幼仔 (puppies / litter / bitch) · pup: 海豹、海狗等产崽 (colony / seal / pups) · kitten: 母猫产下一窝猫崽 (queen / litter / kittens) · fertilize: 授精、授粉以触发受精发育 (egg / ovum / soil)

groups.name: Blab & Leak · 泄密与不慎吐露 (Manner of Divulging Secrets)
groups.tip: 将隐秘或机密信息透露公开

items.def_en: (+ on) to reveal minor misdeeds or childish secrets to an authority figure
items.ex_en: The younger brother threatened to tattle on his sister for breaking the vase.
items.ex_zh: 弟弟威胁说要把姐姐打碎花瓶的事向大人打小报告。

items.def_en: Become known publicly despite efforts to keep the information secret
items.ex_en: News of the planned corporate merger began to leak out across financial markets.
items.ex_zh: 企业计划合并的消息开始在金融市场上泄露出去。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Reveal a secret or confidential piece of information inadvertently
items.ex_en: During dinner, he accidentally let slip that a surprise party was planned.
items.ex_zh: 吃晚饭时，他无意中说漏嘴透露了筹划惊喜派对的事。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ the beans/secrets) to reveal confidential information, often indiscreetly
items.ex_en: Under intense questioning from his friends, Mark finally spilled the beans about everything.
items.ex_zh: 在朋友们的严厉盘问下，马克终于将一切托盘而出。
items.ex2_en: Hot coffee spilled everywhere when she tripped over the messy extension cord.
items.ex2_zh: 当她被杂乱的延长线绊倒时，热咖啡洒得到处都是。

items.def_zh: 脱口而出，不假思索地说漏嘴
items.def_en: (+ sth) Say something suddenly and without thinking, especially a secret
items.ex_en: She suddenly blurted out the confidential password before she could stop herself.
items.ex_zh: 她还没来得及克制自己，就猛然把绝密密码脱口而出了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Reveal or disclose secret information spontaneously or recklessly
items.ex_en: His deepest childhood secrets began to spill out after drinking several cocktails.
items.ex_zh: 几杯鸡尾酒下肚后，他内心最深处的童年秘密开始倾吐而出。
items.ex2_en: The emotional speaker spilled out her painful family memories to the audience.
items.ex2_zh: 情绪激动的演讲者向听众倾吐了她痛苦的家庭回忆。

items.def_en: [I/T] to deliberately disclose secret or private information unofficially to the public
items.ex_en: An anonymous official leaked classified documents regarding the scandal to the press.
items.ex_zh: 一名匿名官员将有关该丑闻的机密文件泄露给了媒体。
items.ex2_en: Confidential government files leaked onto social media platforms during the busy afternoon.
items.ex2_zh: 政府机密文件在繁忙的下午被泄露到了社交媒体平台上。

items.def_en: To make known private, secret, or sensitive information to others.
items.ex_en: The contract forbids former employees to divulge proprietary technological secrets to rivals.
items.ex_zh: 合同明令禁止前员工向竞争对手泄露专有技术机密。

items.def_zh: 告密，告发；违背诺言，变节
items.def_en: (informal) To inform on someone to the police or authorities (usually 'fink on'); to back out of an agreement.
items.ex_en: The thief chose to fink on his accomplices in exchange for immunity.
items.ex_zh: 该窃贼选择向警方告发同伙以换取豁免权。

items.def_en: To say something suddenly and impulsively without thinking, especially a secret (often 'blurt out').
items.ex_en: He did not intend to blurt that damaging secret during the meeting.
items.ex_zh: 他并非故意在会议期间冲口说出那个极具破坏性的秘密。

items.def_zh: 解密（机密文件），从保密级别中降除
items.def_en: To officially declare that government or military secrets are no longer confidential or restricted.
items.ex_en: The military decided to declassify historic reconnaissance photographs taken during the cold war.
items.ex_zh: 军方决定解密冷战期间拍摄的历史侦察照片。

items.def_zh: 泄密，走漏风声；大嘴巴多嘴
items.def_en: To reveal a secret carelessly or indiscreetly by talking too much.
items.ex_en: Don't tell Sarah about the promotion because she will surely blab immediately.
items.ex_zh: 别告诉萨拉升职的事，因为她肯定会立刻大嘴巴走漏风声。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the disclosure of confidential data, ranging from careless, impulsive blabbering and informers spilling info, to formal administrative release of declassified documents.
groups.summary_zh: 呈现泄露隐秘的典型方式，涵盖口无遮拦失言、暗中告密及官方正式解密。
groups.desc_en: Delineates the indiscreet, careless, or malicious disclosure of private information, contrasting with controlled, official public announcements.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘无心失言、轻率口风不严或恶意背叛导致的隐秘外泄，与官方正式受控发布相对。
groups.nuance_en: blurt out: utter precipitously without thinking under emotional pressure (secret / answer / confession) · let slip: reveal inadvertently through a momentary lapse of discretion (detail / clue / identity) · divulge: disclose sensitive or private information knowingly to someone (confidential source / plot / data) · tattle: report petty misdeeds to an authority figure spitefully (misconduct / sibling / classmate) · leak: release unauthorized classified intelligence covertly to the press (memo / audiotape / document)
groups.nuance_zh: blurt out: 情绪激动或未加思索冲口而出 (secret / answer / confession) · let slip: 一时口疏不慎走漏蛛丝马迹 (detail / clue / identity) · divulge: 故意向特定对象透露隐情或机密 (confidential source / plot / data) · tattle: 恶意向长辈或上级打小报告告密 (misconduct / sibling / classmate) · leak: 蓄意私下向外界媒体泄露密件 (memo / audiotape / document)

groups.name: Boast & Vaunt · 吹嘘与自夸 (Boast, Brag, Crow)
groups.tip: 洋洋得意地夸耀自身或吹嘘

items.def_en: to talk boastfully about one's own achievements or skills
items.ex_en: He never misses an opportunity to blow his own horn about investments.
items.ex_zh: 他从不错过任何在投资方面自吹自擂的机会。

items.def_en: (+ sth) behave boastfully to draw admiring attention to one's possessions or abilities
items.ex_en: The young millionaire loved to show off his collection of expensive sports cars.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻的百万富翁喜欢炫耀他收藏的昂贵跑车。

items.def_en: (+ sth) describe sb or sth in glowing or exaggerated terms to impress others
items.ex_en: The company talked up the new phone, but users found it quite ordinary.
items.ex_zh: 公司对那款新手机大加吹捧，但用户发现它其实平平无奇。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) praise or speak boastfully about sb or sth to others
items.ex_en: Proud parents often brag on their children's athletic accomplishments to every neighbor.
items.ex_zh: 自豪的父母常常向每一位邻居大肆夸耀自己孩子的体育成就。

items.def_zh: 吹嘘，自夸；拥有（引以为豪的事物）
items.def_en: 1. (+ about/of) To talk with too much pride about your achievements, abilities, or possessions. 2. (formal) To possess something desirable that is a source of pride.
items.ex_en: The prestigious university boasts five Nobel laureates among its current faculty members.
items.ex_zh: 这所著名学府引以为豪的是其现任教职员工中拥有五位诺贝尔奖得主。

items.def_zh: （尤指得意忘形地）自鸣得意，幸灾乐祸地夸耀；（公鸡）啼叫
items.def_en: 1. (+ over/about) To boast or gloat loudly about a success or victory. 2. (of a rooster) To make a loud, proud crying sound at dawn.
items.ex_en: The champion continued to crow about his victory long after the match.
items.ex_zh: 比赛结束很久之后，这位冠军仍在为自己的胜利自鸣得意。

items.def_en: 1. To describe something as larger, better, worse, or more important than it really is.
items.ex_en: Fishermen frequently exaggerate the true size of the fish that escaped them.
items.ex_zh: 钓客常常会夸大脱钩游走的鱼的实际尺寸。

items.def_en: 1. (+ about/of) To talk too proudly and boastfully about what you own or have achieved.
items.ex_en: He kept bragging about his high test scores to all his classmates.
items.ex_zh: 他不停地向所有同班同学吹嘘自己的高考试分数。

items.def_zh: （为……）自鸣得意，自我吹嘘（plume oneself on）；（鸟）整理羽毛
items.def_en: 1. ('plume oneself on') (formal) To feel proud and boastful about an achievement or quality. 2. (of a bird) To clean and arrange its feathers.
items.ex_en: The author tended to plume himself on his remarkably sophisticated literary style.
items.ex_zh: 该作家往往对自己那极其典雅高超的文学风格自鸣得意。

items.def_en: to behave or talk in an arrogant, overly confident manner
items.ex_en: He swaggered into the boardroom and boasted arrogantly about doubling quarterly revenue.
items.ex_zh: 他大摇大摆地走进会议室，傲慢地吹嘘季度收入翻了一番。

items.def_en: (+ over/about) to dwell on one's own success or another's misfortune with smug pleasure
items.ex_en: It is quite unsportsmanlike to gloat over your defeated opponent's bitter misfortune.
items.ex_zh: 对落败对手的不幸遭遇幸灾乐祸地自鸣得意是极缺乏风度的。

items.def_en: 1. (formal / literary) To boast or brag proudly about one's achievements or qualities.
items.ex_en: The proud general vaunted his military prowess before the assembled royal court.
items.ex_zh: 骄傲的将军在聚集的朝廷百官面前大肆夸耀自己的赫赫武功。

groups.summary_en: A speaker talks with excessive pride or self-satisfaction about their achievements, possessions, or capabilities. Verbs vary from conversational self-praise to formal, ostentatious, or gloating celebration.
groups.summary_zh: 言谈中带着过度的自得或优越感，大肆炫耀自身成就或优势。
groups.desc_en: Expresses excessive self-praise, hubris, or ostentatious display of one's assets or deeds, contrasted with modest self-expression or objective reporting.
groups.desc_zh: 表达对自身资本、功绩的过分吹嘘、洋洋自得或招摇炫耀，与谦逊自陈或客观陈述相对。
groups.nuance_en: brag: boast crudely and noisily about possessions or accomplishments (exploits / wealth / scores) · crow: gloat loudly and exultantly over another's defeat or one's triumph (victory / success / rivals) · show off: display one's abilities, possessions, or body ostentatiously for admiration (skills / sports car / physique) · talk up: promote or exaggerate the qualities of something eagerly (prospects / product / candidate) · blow one's own horn: unabashedly promote one's own merits to self-aggrandize (achievements / talent / resume)
groups.nuance_zh: brag: 粗鲁喧闹地自吹自擂 (exploits / wealth / scores) · crow: 胜券在握后得意忘形地幸灾乐祸 (victory / success / rivals) · show off: 卖弄展现本领或财富以求喝彩 (skills / sports car / physique) · talk up: 大力吹捧宣传某事物以抬高声价 (prospects / product / candidate) · blow one's own horn: 恬不知耻地为自己评功摆好 (achievements / talent / resume)

groups.name: Classify & Compartmentalize · 分类与归类 (Classify, Categorize, Pigeonhole)
groups.tip: 按特征将事物分门别类

items.def_en: (+ sth) divide or classify information or items into smaller constituent categories
items.ex_en: The analyst will break down the complex data into three manageable categories.
items.ex_zh: 分析师将把复杂的数据细分分解为三个易于处理的类别。
items.ex2_en: The antique delivery truck broke down completely right in the city center.
items.ex2_zh: 那辆老旧送货卡车在市中心正中央彻底抛锚损坏了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) arrange things into different categories according to type or quality
items.ex_en: Volunteers helped sort out the donated clothes into adult and children sizes.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们协助将捐赠的衣物分拣归类为成人和儿童尺码。

items.def_en: (+ into) to arrange things systematically in groups according to type or character
items.ex_en: The postal workers sort letters into distinct regional bins for prompt delivery.
items.ex_zh: 邮政工人将信件按不同地区分拣归类，以便迅速投递。

items.def_en: (+ with/together) to group people or things together as being similar or equal
items.ex_en: Critics often bracket his early novels together with works of classic realism.
items.ex_zh: 评论家们经常将他的早期小说与经典现实主义作品归为一类。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) put different people or things into the same group without distinction
items.ex_en: You shouldn't lump all modern politicians together as corrupt without solid evidence.
items.ex_zh: 在没有确凿证据的情况下，你不该把所有现代政客混为一谈视作腐败。

items.def_en: To assign someone or something to a particular class, rank, or category.
items.ex_en: Sociologists typically class these suburban families as middle-income household units.
items.ex_zh: 社会学家通常把这些郊区家庭归类为中等收入家庭单元。

items.def_en: 1. To arrange or group people or things into categories according to shared characteristics. 2. To designate official documents or information as secret.
items.ex_en: Biologists classify organisms according to their specific evolutionary relationships and genetic traits.
items.ex_zh: 生物学家根据生物特定的进化关系和遗传特征对其进行归类。

items.def_en: To put people or things into specific groups or classes according to their shared features or type.
items.ex_en: The software automatically categorizes incoming emails based on their subject and sender.
items.ex_zh: 该软件会根据主题和发件人自动将收到的电子邮件分类。

items.def_en: To assign someone or something to a different category, rank, or official classification.
items.ex_en: Customs officials decided to reclassify the imported components under a different tariff.
items.ex_zh: 海关官员决定将进口零部件重新归入另一税则类别。

items.def_zh: 把……不合理地分类，贴标签；把……搁置，束之高阁
items.def_en: 1. To unfairly classify someone or something into a narrow or rigid category. 2. To put aside or postpone action on something indefinitely.
items.ex_en: She resented how casting directors attempted to pigeonhole her into comedic roles.
items.ex_zh: 她很反感选角导演试图把她模式化归类进喜剧角色的做法。

items.def_zh: 划分，把……分隔成独立部分；（心理上）隔绝
items.def_en: To divide something into separate, discrete sections or categories so that they do not influence or interfere with one another.
items.ex_en: He learned to compartmentalize his demanding corporate duties from his personal life.
items.ex_zh: 他学会了将繁重的公司职责与个人生活在心理上隔绝开来。

items.def_zh: 给（演员）定型，分配千篇一律的角色；把……模式化归类
items.def_en: 1. To repeatedly assign an actor to the same type of role based on appearance or past success. 2. To identify or treat someone according to a rigid stereotype.
items.ex_en: The talented actor feared the studio would typecast him as a villain.
items.ex_zh: 这位才华横溢的演员担心制片厂会把他模式化定型为反派角色。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe sorting items, ideas, or people into systematic conceptual groups, escalating from objective taxonomic arrangement to overly rigid, restrictive labeling.
groups.summary_zh: 指按属性划分类别，由客观分门别类至僵化定型或分流限制。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the intellectual or administrative act of sorting disparate items into defined rubrics, contrasting with unsystematic hoarding or blending.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据特定标准将杂乱事物归整入不同栏目或范畴的心智与行政操作，与杂乱堆砌或融合相对。
groups.nuance_en: categorize: assign systematically to predetermined scientific or conceptual groups (data / species / risks) · pigeonhole: rigidly and unfairly restrict someone or something to a narrow label (actor / genre / concept) · lump together: inappropriately combine distinct entities into an undifferentiated mass (disparate groups / ideas / symptoms) · sort out: disentangle, organize, and resolve disordered items logically (papers / mess / logistics) · bracket: group entities together as sharing a common range or condition (income levels / ages / contenders)
groups.nuance_zh: categorize: 系统性归纳分入既定类别 (data / species / risks) · pigeonhole: 僵化死板地贴标签或划入固定框框 (actor / genre / concept) · lump together: 抹杀差异、一刀切地胡乱混为一谈 (disparate groups / ideas / symptoms) · sort out: 理清并分拣杂乱无章之物 (papers / mess / logistics) · bracket: 视同等梯队或置于同一区间归并 (income levels / ages / contenders)

groups.name: Clear & Scrape Residue Off Surfaces · 清理与揩刮 (Mop, Scrape, Hoover)
groups.tip: 用工具清除污垢灰尘

items.def_en: (+ sth) clean up dust or debris from a floor or surface using a vacuum cleaner
items.ex_en: She used the portable vacuum to hoover up crumbs beneath the sofa.
items.ex_zh: 她用便携式吸尘器吸净了沙发下方的碎屑。

items.def_en: (+ sth) remove liquid or dirt from a surface using a mop or cloth
items.ex_en: The janitor quickly grabbed a rag to mop up the spilled juice.
items.ex_zh: 清洁工快速拿来一块抹布，将洒出来的果汁擦拭拖净。

items.def_en: to clear dirt or debris from a floor using a brush or broom
items.ex_en: She grabbed the kitchen broom to sweep the broken glass off the floor.
items.ex_zh: 她拿起厨房扫帚，把地上的碎玻璃扫除干净。

items.def_en: 1. To clean or wash a floor or surface using a mop; wipe away sweat or liquid.
items.ex_en: After finishing dinner, he helped mop the sticky kitchen floor with hot water.
items.ex_zh: 吃完晚餐后，他帮忙用热水把发黏的厨房地面拖洗干净。

items.def_en: 1. (dated / regional) To sweep a floor or area clean with a broom.
items.ex_en: The elderly caretaker rose before dawn to broom the fallen leaves from the flagstones.
items.ex_zh: 年迈的看管人拂晓前便已起身，用扫帚清扫石板路上的落叶。

items.def_en: to clean or dry a wet surface, especially glass, using a rubber-bladed scraping tool
items.ex_en: The window washer used a rubber blade to squeegee soapy water from the glass.
items.ex_zh: 擦窗工用橡胶刮板刮除玻璃上的肥皂水。

items.def_zh: 刮除，擦掉；刮擦出刺耳声；擦伤
items.def_en: 1. To remove dirt, paint, or ice from a surface using a sharp or hard edge. 2. To rub roughly against something, making a harsh sound; scratch or graze.
items.ex_en: He took a small putty knife to scrape the dried paint from the pane.
items.ex_zh: 他拿了一把小刮刀，把窗玻璃上干掉的油漆刮掉。

items.def_en: (+ sth) remove an unwanted substance or encrusted layer from a surface with a hard edge
items.ex_en: You need to scrape off the thick rust before repainting the garden gate.
items.ex_zh: 在重新粉刷花园大门之前，你需要刮掉上面厚厚的铁锈。

items.def_zh: 彻底擦洗，用力刷洗（表面）
items.def_en: (+ sth) clean a large surface thoroughly by rubbing it hard with a stiff brush and water
items.ex_en: The sailors had to scrub down the wooden deck with stiff bristle brushes.
items.ex_zh: 水手们不得不拿硬毛刷用力刷洗整个木质甲板。

items.def_en: to clean a carpet or floor with an electrical suction apparatus
items.ex_en: I try to vacuum the bedroom carpet at least twice a week to remove dust.
items.ex_zh: 我尽量每周至少吸两次卧室地毯，以清除积尘。

items.def_en: 1. (+ up) (British English) To clean a floor or carpet using a vacuum cleaner.
items.ex_en: Could you hoover the living room rug before the guests arrive this afternoon?
items.ex_zh: 下午客人来之前，你能用吸尘器把客厅地毯吸一下吗？

items.def_en: to rub hard with a stiff brush, cloth, and water to remove deeply embedded dirt
items.ex_en: She had to scrub the stained tile grout vigorously with a small brush.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不拿一把小刷子用力擦洗变脏的瓷砖缝隙。

groups.summary_en: Removing dirt, dust, grime, or encrusted residue from a surface using a specialized handheld implement (broom, scraper, wet mop, or suction machine). Emphasizes mechanical action and contact surface.
groups.summary_zh: 利用专用工具通过刷、拖、刮或吸除清洁表面
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the mechanical removal of liquid, dust, or clinging residues from hard surfaces via friction or suction tools, contrasting with washing or mere chemical dissolving.
groups.desc_zh: 强调借助摩擦或吸力工具物理清除硬表面上的积水、灰尘或附着残留物，与浸泡洗涤或单纯化学溶解相对。
groups.nuance_en: scrape: dislodge stubbornly adhering solid substance using a hard blade (paint / ice / burnt food) · mop up: absorb and remove standing liquid using an absorbent head (spill / mess / puddle) · squeegee: wipe water swiftly off smooth surfaces using a flat rubber blade (windshield / floor / glass) · hoover up: suck up dry dust and loose dirt mechanically with a vacuum (crumbs / carpet / mess) · sweep: clear loose debris across a dry floor using a brush broom (debris / floor / leaves)
groups.nuance_zh: scrape: 用硬刃刮除附着极牢的固态污垢 (paint / ice / burnt food) · mop up: 用吸水拖把吸收并清除滩水 (spill / mess / puddle) · squeegee: 用橡胶刮板刮除光滑平面积水 (windshield / floor / glass) · hoover up: 机械吸尘器强力吸走浮尘残渣 (crumbs / carpet / mess) · sweep: 用扫帚推拂清扫干燥杂物 (debris / floor / leaves)

groups.name: Coat & Plate · 涂覆与电镀 (Japan, Plate, Plaster)
groups.tip: 在物体表面涂抹或镀层

items.def_en: (+ sth) spread a thick, sticky, or wet substance coarsely over a surface
items.ex_en: He used a broad knife to daub on the thick waterproof sealant roughly.
items.ex_zh: 他用一把宽刀粗糙地把厚厚的防水密封胶涂抹在表面。

items.def_en: (+ sth) apply a layer of paint, plaster, or coating to a surface
items.ex_en: The mason began to lay on a fresh layer of plaster over the bricks.
items.ex_zh: 泥瓦匠开始在砖墙上厚厚地抹上一层新鲜的石膏灰泥。

items.def_en: To coat a surface with a hard, glossy black lacquer.
items.ex_en: The artisan chose to japan the wooden chest with successive coats of glossy lacquer.
items.ex_zh: 工匠决定给这个木箱逐层涂上光亮的黑漆。

items.def_en: 1. To coat or plate an object with silver or a silvery substance. 2. To turn silver or silvery-white, or cause to do so.
items.ex_en: The craftsman took great care to silver the delicate glass ornament for the cathedral.
items.ex_zh: 工匠精心为这座大教堂精致的玻璃饰品镀上一层银。
items.ex2_en: The calm surface of the mountain lake silvered under bright moonlight.
items.ex2_zh: 明亮的月光下，平静的山间湖面泛出银白色的光芒。

items.def_en: To coat food with breadcrumbs before cooking.
items.ex_en: Dip the chicken cutlets in whisked egg and then bread them before frying.
items.ex_zh: 先将鸡排浸入打匀的蛋液，再裹上面包屑，然后下锅油炸。

items.def_en: To coat or plate a metal object with nickel.
items.ex_en: The master metalworker intended to nickel the iron fittings against the damp sea air.
items.ex_zh: 金属大师打算给这些铁质构件镀镍，以抵御潮湿的海风侵蚀。

items.def_en: (+ sth) apply or spread a thick layer of a substance onto a surface
items.ex_en: The nurse began to plaster on a soothing herbal poultice across the wound.
items.ex_zh: 护士开始在伤口上厚厚地敷上一层舒缓的草药膏。

items.def_zh: 在……上抹灰泥；厚厚地涂抹；贴满
items.def_en: 1. To cover a wall or ceiling with wet plaster. 2. (+ with) To cover a surface thickly or completely with a substance, posters, or pictures.
items.ex_en: The workers prepared to plaster the exterior wall before the autumn rains set in.
items.ex_zh: 工人们准备赶在秋雨来临前给外墙抹上灰泥。

items.def_en: to coat or decorate a metallic or ceramic surface with a glossy glassy substance
items.ex_en: Specialist artisans carefully enamel the copper surface using powdered glass melted under intense heat.
items.ex_zh: 专业工匠通过高温融化玻璃粉末，细致地给铜制表面上珐琅。

items.def_en: to cover a surface with a thin layer of gold leaf or gold paint
items.ex_en: The artisan began to gild the ornate wooden frame with gossamer sheets of gold.
items.ex_zh: 工匠开始用薄如蝉翼的金箔给华丽的木框贴金。

items.def_en: (+ with) to coat a metal object with a thin layer of another metal using electrolysis
items.ex_en: The silversmith chose to electroplate the brass chalice with a lustrous sheen of platinum.
items.ex_zh: 银匠决定用电镀法给铜圣杯镀上一层光泽夺目的铂金。

items.def_en: To coat a metal object with a thin layer of silver, typically by electroplating.
items.ex_en: He vowed to silverplate the heirloom candlesticks until their burnished glory returned.
items.ex_zh: 他发誓要给传家宝烛台重新镀银，直到它们恢复昔日光辉。

groups.summary_en: An artisan or industrial process applies an adhesive, protective, decorative, or metallic layer onto an underlying surface via electrolytic deposition, chemical lacquering, or thick physical spreading.
groups.summary_zh: 通过电解附着、上漆或刮抹在物体表面覆盖防护、装饰或金属层。
groups.desc_en: Involves applying a protective, aesthetic, or functional outer layer of material onto a substrate, differing from impregnating or carving.
groups.desc_zh: 指在基底表面均匀附着一层保护性、装饰性或功能性外层介质，与浸渍渗透或雕刻减材相对。
groups.nuance_en: plaster: coat thick wet mortar heavily across a rough wall (wall / ceiling / surface) · plate: deposit a thin adhering metallic film electrochemically or mechanically (gold / chrome / copper) · silver: apply a reflective metallic coating of silver onto a glass backing (mirror / glass / optics) · bread: press crumbs over moistened food before frying (cutlet / fish / chicken) · japan: coat with a hard, glossy black lacquer (metal / furniture / clock face)
groups.nuance_zh: plaster: 大面积厚厚糊抹石膏灰浆 (wall / ceiling / surface) · plate: 电解或化学沉积金属覆层 (gold / chrome / copper) · silver: 在玻璃背面镀银制镜 (mirror / glass / optics) · bread: 烹炸前在食材外表包裹一层面包糠 (cutlet / fish / chicken) · japan: 涂覆硬质乌黑亮漆 (metal / furniture / clock face)

groups.name: Construct & Erect · 建造与构筑 (Build, Construct, Erect)
groups.tip: 施工搭建建筑物或实体

items.def_zh: 建造，修筑，构筑；逐步建立，树立
items.def_en: 1. To construct something by putting parts or materials together. 2. To gradually develop, establish, or strengthen something.
items.ex_en: The volunteers worked together to build a safe shelter for the homeless community.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们齐心协力为无家可归者社区建造了一座安全的避难所。
items.ex2_en: Heavy storm clouds continue to build menacingly along the southern coastal mountains.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨的阴云继续在南部沿海山区险恶地聚集堆积。

items.def_zh: 建造，构筑（build 的过去式与过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of build: to construct something by assembling parts or materials.
items.ex_en: They proudly inspected the stone cottage they had built with their own hands.
items.ex_zh: 他们自豪地审视着自己亲手建造的那座石砌小屋。
items.ex2_en: Tension built noticeably in the crowded boardroom as deadline talks completely stalled.
items.ex2_zh: 随着截止日期谈判陷入僵局，拥挤的会议室里紧张气氛明显聚集。

items.def_en: To plan, arrange, or organize the parts of something in a systematic way.
items.ex_en: The committee decided to structure the new curriculum around practical hands-on experience.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定围绕实际动手经验来构建这门新课程体系。

items.def_zh: 建造，构筑；构建，构想（理论、体系）
items.def_en: 1. To build or make something large, such as a building, bridge, or machine. 2. To form or create an idea, system, or theory.
items.ex_en: Engineers plan to construct a high-speed railway connecting the two remote industrial cities.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们计划修建一条连接这两座偏远工业城市的高速铁路。

items.def_en: to erect or assemble a building, fence, or temporary structure
items.ex_en: The neighbors helped him put up a sturdy wooden fence around his backyard.
items.ex_zh: 邻居们帮他在后院四周搭起了一圈结实的木栅栏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to create, develop, or construct something gradually over time
items.ex_en: Over twenty years, she managed to build up an internationally respected design firm.
items.ex_zh: 历经二十载，她成功建立起一家备受国际赞誉的设计事务所。
items.ex2_en: Thick black storm clouds built up rapidly along the distant rocky horizon.
items.ex2_zh: 厚重的黑色风暴云在遥远的岩石地平线上迅速积聚。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to assemble or construct something by joining separate parts or pieces
items.ex_en: The archeologists managed to piece together the shattered pieces of the ancient mosaic.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家们设法将古老马赛克的破碎碎片拼凑复原。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to build or erect a structure hurriedly or carelessly
items.ex_en: The investigation threw up some unexpected problems for the company.
items.ex_zh: 调查给公司暴露出了一些意想不到的问题。

items.def_en: to build or put up a vertical structure such as a wall, monument, or building
items.ex_en: The city council plans to erect a bronze monument honoring the fallen soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 市议会计划兴建一座青铜纪念碑以缅怀牺牲的士兵。

items.def_en: to construct or manufacture an industrial product or building from standardized components
items.ex_en: The company was hired to fabricate the heavy steel girders for the bridge.
items.ex_zh: 该公司受聘为大桥装配制造沉重的钢梁构件。

items.def_zh: 重建，重修；重现，再现（事件经过）
items.def_en: 1. To build something again that has been damaged or destroyed. 2. To piece together how a past event happened from available evidence.
items.ex_en: Historians worked diligently to reconstruct the temple according to original fifteenth-century blueprints.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们一丝不苟地根据十五世纪的原始图纸重建了这座神庙。

items.def_zh: 筑交叉拱顶于；为……修筑防波堤
items.def_en: 1. (architecture) To build or form intersecting arches (groins) in a ceiling. 2. To protect a shoreline or riverbank with groins.
items.ex_en: The royal architects laboured to groin the lofty nave of the new abbey.
items.ex_zh: 皇家建筑师们倾力为新建修道院高耸的中殿修筑交叉拱顶。

groups.summary_en: An agent puts parts, structural materials, or conceptual frameworks together to form a standing, coherent edifice or system. Verbs span basic physical construction to deliberate architectural or systemic design.
groups.summary_zh: 将材料、部件或要素系统性地搭建组合成实体建筑或宏观体系。
groups.desc_en: Depicts assembling materials or prefabricated units to assemble a physical structure, contrasting with natural organic growth or mere assembling of small mechanisms.
groups.desc_zh: 强调按工程规程把建材或构件自下而上拼装竖立为建筑实体，与自然生长或小物件拼装相对。
groups.nuance_en: construct: assemble an engineered, complex physical edifice according to plan (bridge / highway / skyscraper) · put up: erect quickly a modular, temporary, or functional structure (tent / fence / scaffold) · throw up: build shoddy, hurried, or unsightly structures hastily (tenements / shacks / barriers) · piece together: patiently assemble fragmented elements into a cohesive whole (puzzle / narrative / evidence) · build up: progressively accumulate, fortify, or expand over time (reserves / strength / defenses)
groups.nuance_zh: construct: 依图纸精密规划构筑大型工程 (bridge / highway / skyscraper) · put up: 迅速竖立模块化或临时性设施 (tent / fence / scaffold) · throw up: 粗制滥造、仓促搭建简陋建筑物 (tenements / shacks / barriers) · piece together: 耐心拼合零碎线索或部件 (puzzle / narrative / evidence) · build up: 渐进积累、增筑壮大规模 (reserves / strength / defenses)

groups.name: Cover & Panel Surfaces · 覆层与铺面 (Tile, Clad, Cap)
groups.tip: 在外表覆上一层遮蔽物

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cover a window, door, or architectural opening with wooden boards
items.ex_en: Shopkeepers boarded up their storefronts before the hurricane arrived.
items.ex_zh: 店主们在飓风来临前用木板封住了店铺临街的门窗。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to enclose or encase a physical perimeter with protective panels or fencing
items.ex_en: They had to fence in the pasture to keep the sheep from wandering.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须用栅栏把牧场围起来，以防羊群走失。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cover or encase a surface with protective sheets or plastic covering
items.ex_en: We should sheet over the lumber pile before the heavy rainstorm begins tonight.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该在今晚暴雨来临前用防水布把木料堆遮盖好。

items.def_zh: 给……装玻璃；给……安装玻璃罩
items.def_en: To fit or encase something with glass; to glaze.
items.ex_en: The botanist sought to glass the veranda to safeguard his fragile tropical ferns.
items.ex_zh: 植物学家试图给走廊装上玻璃外罩，以庇护他那些娇弱的热带蕨类。

items.def_en: To pave, surface, or repair a road with crushed stone or gravel.
items.ex_en: The estate workers worked through the spring to metal the carriage drive with flint.
items.ex_zh: 庄园工人们整个春天都在劳作，用坚硬的燧石铺砌马车道。

items.def_zh: 覆盖……的顶部；盖住；给……戴帽子；限制（数量或金额）
items.def_en: 1. To cover or form the top of something. 2. To put a limit on the amount of money that can be charged, spent, or borrowed.
items.ex_en: Heavy snow began to cap the high mountain peaks as winter approached rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 随着冬日迅猛来临，皑皑白雪开始覆盖高耸的山峰顶部。

items.def_en: to cover or decorate a wall or ceiling with flat rectangular boards or sheets
items.ex_en: The interior designers decided to panel the study walls with polished dark oak.
items.ex_zh: 室内设计师决定用打磨光滑的深色橡木板嵌装书房墙面。

items.def_zh: 像树冠（或华盖）般覆盖；遮蔽
items.def_en: (literary) To cover, shelter, or form a canopy over something.
items.ex_en: Ancient banyan trees canopy the secluded stone path with their vast sprawling branches.
items.ex_zh: 古老的榕树以其舒展庞大的枝丫如华盖般遮蔽着幽静的石径。

items.def_zh: 用瓷砖（或瓦片）铺设，盖瓦于
items.def_en: To cover a floor, wall, or roof with tiles.
items.ex_en: They hired a professional contractor to tile the master bathroom from floor to ceiling.
items.ex_zh: 他们雇了一名专业承包商，把主卧浴室从地板到天花板贴满瓷砖。

items.def_en: to cover a ground or floor surface with flat stones, bricks, or concrete blocks
items.ex_en: The town council decided to pave the market square with decorative red cobblestones.
items.ex_zh: 镇议会决定用红色的装饰性鹅卵石铺砌集市广场。

items.def_zh: （给墙壁、建筑等）覆层，包层；（clothe 的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive) To cover a building, wall, or structure with a protective or decorative outer layer. 2. Past tense and past participle of clothe: dressed or covered.
items.ex_en: Architects decided to clad the modern skyscraper in shimmering panels of treated copper.
items.ex_zh: 建筑师们决定用闪闪发光的特制铜板为这座现代摩天大楼作外墙包层。

items.def_en: to encase or cover something in a protective outer layer or casing
items.ex_en: The shipwrights chose to sheathe the wooden hull in heavy plates of beaten copper.
items.ex_zh: 造船匠们选择用厚重的锻铜板包裹木制船体以作防护。

groups.summary_en: An agent or structural element covers, lines, or encases an architectural or physical surface with protective, structural, or finishing panels. Verbs are distinguished by the specific material or spatial placement used (tiles, metal sheets, glass, or crowns).
groups.summary_zh: 以特定建筑材料或构件（如瓦片、金属、玻璃）对表面进行封盖与包覆。
groups.desc_en: Refers to securing panels, sheets, or protective rigid shells across structural openings or boundaries, contrasting with flexible textile draping or fluid painting.
groups.desc_zh: 指用硬质板材、护壳或围障来封闭孔洞、保护断面或界定边界，与柔性织物垂挂或流质涂抹相对。
groups.nuance_en: board up: seal windows or doorways securely with wooden planks against damage (windows / storefront / house) · panel: line interior walls with decorative or insulating rigid sheets (wood / oak / interior) · cap: seal the upper end or top surface with a protective barrier (well / summit / bottle) · fence in: enclose an open boundary securely with a palisade or wire perimeter (yard / livestock / perimeter) · sheet over: enclose broadly under a planar layer of ice, plastic, or metal (pond / framework / scaffold)
groups.nuance_zh: board up: 钉木板严密封堵门窗以防破损 (windows / storefront / house) · panel: 用硬质护墙板装饰或隔热护壁 (wood / oak / interior) · cap: 给顶部加装保护性封口或封顶 (well / summit / bottle) · fence in: 用篱笆栅栏划界圈禁 (yard / livestock / perimeter) · sheet over: 铺设或冻结出一整层薄板或薄膜覆层 (pond / framework / scaffold)

groups.name: Create & Originate · 发明与开创 (Invent, Devise, Pioneer)
groups.tip: 凭独创性提出新概念或事物

items.def_zh: 创造（新词语或表达）；杜撰；铸造（硬币）
items.def_en: 1. To invent or devise a new word or phrase. 2. To manufacture coins from metal.
items.ex_en: The linguist had to coin a brand new phrase to describe the online phenomenon.
items.ex_zh: 这位语言学家不得不创造一个全新的词组来描述这种网络现象。

items.def_en: 1. To design or make something that has never existed before. 2. To fabricate or make up a story, excuse, or lie.
items.ex_en: The curious engineer set out to invent a machine that cleans ocean plastic.
items.ex_zh: 这位充满求知欲的工程师着手发明一种清理海洋塑料垃圾的机器。

items.def_zh: 想出；构思出（点子或计划）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to produce, invent, or devise an original idea, design, or solution
items.ex_en: Our creative team managed to come up with an innovative solution to the dilemma.
items.ex_zh: 我们的创意团队设法想出了一个应对这一困境的创新解决方案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to invent or concoct an unusual, clever, or fanciful idea or scheme
items.ex_en: I wonder who managed to dream up such an outrageous and silly excuse.
items.ex_zh: 真不知道是谁凭空编造出如此离谱又荒唐的借口。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to invent or fabricate a story, plan, or excuse, especially a deceptive one
items.ex_en: He had to cook up an excuse for being late to the morning briefing.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不编造一个早会迟到的借口。

items.def_en: To be the first to develop, introduce, or use a new method, area of study, or technology.
items.ex_en: Dr. Miller helped pioneer minimally invasive surgical techniques throughout the early nineteen nineties.
items.ex_zh: 米勒医生在二十世纪九十年代初开创了微创手术技术。

items.def_en: [I/T] to bring into being or initiate a completely new idea, practice, or thing
items.ex_en: Scholars believe the unique decorative tradition did originate within remote mountain monasteries.
items.ex_zh: 学者们认为这一独特的装饰传统确实首创于偏远的山地寺院。

items.def_zh: 设计，发明，想出；遗赠（房产等）
items.def_en: 1. To invent, plan, or design a system, method, or machine by using intelligence and imagination. 2. (law) To leave real property to someone by will.
items.ex_en: The research team worked overnight to devise an effective algorithm for processing data.
items.ex_zh: 研究团队通宵达旦地设计出一种用于处理数据的有效算法。
