items.ex_zh: 几条山间细流逐渐汇入蜿蜒穿过山谷的较宽河流中。

items.def_en: to intertwine threads or diverse strands closely together into one complex fabric
items.ex_en: Ancient tapestries interweave shimmering strands of gold with rich crimson and azure silk.
items.ex_zh: 古老的挂毯将微光粼粼的金线与浓郁的绯红及天蓝丝线紧密交织。
items.ex2_en: Traditional melodies and modern jazz chords interweave seamlessly throughout this captivating musical composition.
items.ex2_zh: 传统旋律与现代爵士和弦在这部迷人的音乐作品中交织得天衣无缝。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Merge or dissolve so thoroughly into something as to become indistinguishable
items.ex_en: The retreating stag seemed to melt into the misty shadows of the woodland.
items.ex_zh: 撤退的雄鹿似乎悄然融进了林间雾气弥漫的阴影之中。

items.def_zh: 混合，调和；（使）融合，融为一体
items.def_en: 1. To mix different substances, qualities, or styles together smoothly. 2. (+ in/with) To harmonize or fit in well with surroundings.
items.ex_en: The chef managed to blend local spices smoothly into the traditional French sauce.
items.ex_zh: 厨师成功地将当地香料顺畅地融入传统的法式酱汁中。
items.ex2_en: The smooth watercolor paints blend effortlessly on the wet textured paper during painting.
items.ex2_zh: 作画时，光滑的水彩颜料在潮湿的纹理纸上毫不费力地融为一体。

items.def_en: to combine two or more things gradually so that the boundary between them disappears
items.ex_en: The two competing financial entities decided to merge into one corporate powerhouse smoothly.
items.ex_zh: 这两家相互竞争的金融实体决定平稳合并为一个强大的联合企业。
items.ex2_en: The two corporate giants merged the two competing departments to improve administrative efficiency.
items.ex2_zh: 两家企业巨头合并了两个相互竞争的部门，以提高行政效率。

items.def_en: to combine diverse elements, groups, or businesses into one unified body
items.ex_en: The board resolved to amalgamate three regional subsidiaries into one comprehensive administrative division.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定将三家区域子公司合并为一个综合性行政部门。
items.ex2_en: The distinct local cultures amalgamated naturally over several generations of peaceful trade interaction.
items.ex2_zh: 经过几代和平的贸易往来，不同的本土文化自然而然地融合在了一起。

items.def_en: (+ into/with) To come together to form one larger group, substance, or mass.
items.ex_en: Divergent grassroots movements began to coalesce into a formidable nationwide political campaign recently.
items.ex_zh: 形形色色的草根运动最近开始凝聚成一场强大的全国性政治运动。

items.def_en: (+ with) To mix or mingle together, or to combine two or more things closely.
items.ex_en: Rich scents of jasmine and damp earth intermingle sweetly in the nocturnal breeze.
items.ex_zh: 茉莉的馥郁与湿土的气息在夜风中甜美地交融在一起。
items.ex2_en: The chef intermingled fresh aromatic herbs into the creamy garlic pasta sauce carefully.
items.ex2_zh: 厨师小心翼翼地将新鲜的芳香草本植物混入奶油大蒜意面酱中。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (formal) To mix or blend two or more things, funds, or groups together.
items.ex_en: Attorneys warned the executor never to commingle personal capital with estate trust assets.
items.ex_zh: 律师告诫执行人切勿将个人资金与遗产信托资产混合在一起。
items.ex2_en: Public finances and private corporate funds commingled unlawfully during the disputed development project.
items.ex2_zh: 在有争议的开发项目中，公共财政资金与私营企业资金非法混杂在一起。

items.def_en: to join or become combined into a single, indivisible entity, often under intense conditions
items.ex_en: Intense thermal energy causes the individual alloy components to fuse into solid compound.
items.ex_zh: 剧烈的高温促使各个合金组分熔合成为坚固的复合物。
items.ex2_en: The technician applied intense electric heat to fuse the two thick plastic pipes.
items.ex2_zh: 技术人员施加了强烈的电热，把两根粗塑料管熔接在一起。

groups.summary_en: Distinct elements, substances, or groups combining into an integrated whole. Distinctions turn on whether components remain identifiable when intermixed or lose their separate identities through seamless fusion and organic coalescing.
groups.summary_zh: 多样成分交错混合或融合成统一的无缝整体
groups.desc_en: Describes the coming together of distinct entities, ingredients, or ideas into a unified, harmonious, or indivisible whole, contrasting with 'attach' by entailing the loss of distinct original boundaries.
groups.desc_zh: 指多个离散实体、成分或思想融汇为高度统一、调和或不可分割的整体，区别于机械拼接 (attach)，伴随着原有分明边界的消融与重构。
groups.nuance_en: blend: mix smoothly to produce an agreeable homogeneous composite (flavors / colors / spices) · merge: unite separate legal or physical streams into one (companies / traffic / lanes) · coalesce: gradually draw together into a coherent body or consensus (ideas / factions / clouds) · amalgamate: combine organizations or elements into a structured unity (unions / firms / societies) · interweave: braid distinct strands together intricately (stories / threads / themes)
groups.nuance_zh: blend: 调和混匀呈现和谐整体 (flavors / colors / spices) · merge: 合并组织或车流汇聚为一 (companies / traffic / lanes) · coalesce: 凝聚融合成为合力或共识 (ideas / factions / clouds) · amalgamate: 兼并整合成正式实体 (unions / firms / societies) · interweave: 错综交织在一起 (stories / threads / themes)

groups.name: Clean & Purify · 清洁与净化 (Cleanse, Sanitize, Disinfect)
groups.tip: 除菌消毒恢复无菌洁净

items.def_zh: 彻底清扫，清除内部脏物
items.def_en: (+ sth) Clean the interior of a space or container thoroughly, removing unwanted dirt or contents
items.ex_en: We should clean out the cluttered attic before bringing in the new furniture.
items.ex_zh: 在把新家具搬进来之前，我们该彻底清理一下杂乱的阁楼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Clean a large surface thoroughly by spraying or splashing water over it
items.ex_en: He washed down the spicy tacos with a cold glass of lemonade.
items.ex_zh: 他喝了一大口冰柠檬水，咽下了辛辣的墨西哥卷饼。

items.def_zh: （用布等全面）擦拭清洁，擦洗消毒
items.def_en: (+ sth) Clean the entire surface of something thoroughly using a damp or disinfectant cloth
items.ex_en: Cafeteria staff wipe down every tabletop thoroughly with disinfectant spray after the lunch.
items.ex_zh: 午餐过后，食堂员工会用消毒喷雾把每张桌面彻底擦拭干净。

items.def_zh: 清洗，清洁（皮肤、伤口等）；净化，清洗（罪孽）
items.def_en: 1. To make skin, a wound, or an area thoroughly clean. 2. (formal) To free someone from guilt, sin, or bad feelings.
items.ex_en: The attending surgeon used saline solution to cleanse the contaminated laceration prior to surgery.
items.ex_zh: 主治医生在手术前使用生理盐水彻底清洗了受污染的伤口。

items.def_zh: 清洗净化，彻底清除杂质
items.def_en: to rid an enclosed space, conduit, or system completely of impure substances or residues
items.ex_en: Engineers must purge the pipeline completely of flammable residue before commencing high-temperature maintenance.
items.ex_zh: 工程师在开始高温维护作业前，必须彻底清除管道内的易燃残留物。

items.def_en: 1. To clean a surface, wound, or room with a chemical substance to destroy harmful bacteria and viruses.
items.ex_en: Nurses routinely disinfect all clinic examination rooms to curb the transmission of viruses.
items.ex_zh: 护士们按惯例对所有诊室进行消毒，以遏制病毒传播。

items.def_zh: 给……消毒，实施卫生处理；净化，粉饰（删去令人不快的信息）
items.def_en: 1. To clean and disinfect something thoroughly to remove germs. 2. To alter a report or story to remove offensive, unpleasant, or controversial details.
items.ex_en: Hospital protocol requires technicians to sanitize surgical instruments thoroughly before every major procedure.
items.ex_zh: 医院规程要求技术人员在每次大手术前对器械进行彻底卫生消毒。

items.def_zh: （用巴氏灭菌法）对……进行消毒灭菌
items.def_en: 1. To heat milk, juice, or wine to a specific temperature to kill harmful bacteria without altering its flavor.
items.ex_en: Dairy processors pasteurize raw milk to destroy hazardous pathogens while preserving nutritional integrity.
items.ex_zh: 乳品加工厂对生牛奶进行巴氏灭菌，以杀灭有害病原体并保留营养成分。

items.def_en: to make completely free from live bacteria, viruses, and other microorganisms
items.ex_en: Specialized laboratory personnel sterilize glassware in high heat to eradicate all microbial life.
items.ex_zh: 专门的实验室人员在高温下对玻璃器皿进行彻底灭菌，以杀灭所有微生物。

items.def_en: 1. To disinfect or clear a building, room, or crops using chemical smoke or gas to kill pests and germs.
items.ex_en: Authorities had to fumigate the entire grain warehouse to eradicate an aggressive weevil infestation.
items.ex_zh: 当局不得不对整座粮仓实施烟熏消毒，以彻底消灭猖獗的象鼻虫害。

items.def_en: to sterilize medical or laboratory equipment using high-pressure superheated steam
items.ex_en: Technicians routinely autoclave surgical instruments to guarantee absolute sterility before delicate neurological procedures.
items.ex_zh: 在精细的神经外科手术前，技术人员按例对器械进行高压蒸汽灭菌以确保绝对无菌。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame identify specialized decontamination and purification methods aimed at neutralizing microbes, pathogens, or pests through specific chemical or thermal protocols.
groups.summary_zh: 通过化学药剂、热力或物理熏蒸等特化手段消杀病原体与污垢。
groups.desc_en: Signifies eradicating contamination, pathogens, or undesirable elements from surfaces, substances, or populations, surpassing mundane 'clean' by demanding biological sterility or moral/doctrinal purification.
groups.desc_zh: 指清除表层病原体、污物杂质或思想异端，区别于日常表面洗洁 (clean)，侧重生物学灭菌消毒或体制性/精神性的深度净化。
groups.nuance_en: cleanse: deeply free from moral guilt or physical impurities (skin / soul / wound) · disinfect: chemically destroy bacteria on inanimate surfaces (countertops / tools / equipment) · sanitize: reduce microorganisms to public health safety levels (hands / kitchen / restrooms) · purge: ruthlessly eliminate unwanted elements or rivals (party / ranks / system) · pasteurize: heat-treat food to neutralize harmful microbes (milk / juice / cheese)
groups.nuance_zh: cleanse: 深层洁净、净化灵魂或创口 (skin / soul / wound) · disinfect: 用药剂杀灭表面病菌消毒 (countertops / tools / equipment) · sanitize: 卫生消毒使符合公共标准 (hands / kitchen / restrooms) · purge: 严厉清洗整肃异己分子 (party / ranks / system) · pasteurize: 巴氏杀菌法高温消毒 (milk / juice / cheese)

groups.name: Coat & Smear Viscous Substances · 涂抹与厚敷 (Daub, Smear, Bedirection)
groups.tip: 随手涂抹泥浆漆料

items.def_en: (+ sth) spread a thick, sticky substance crudely or clumsily onto something
items.ex_en: The clumsy apprentice managed to daub on uneven patches of paste across the canvas.
items.ex_zh: 笨手笨脚的学徒在画布上胡乱涂抹出一块块不均匀的浆糊。

items.def_zh: 涂抹，胡乱涂抹；弄脏，蹭污；诽谤，玷污
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/over/with) To spread a soft, greasy, or sticky substance carelessly over a surface. 2. To damage someone's reputation by making false accusations.
items.ex_en: The mechanic accidentally managed to smear black grease right across his clean uniform.
items.ex_zh: 机械师不小心把黑乎乎的机油蹭到了自己干净的制服上。

items.def_zh: 用棉棒或拭子涂敷（药液等）
items.def_en: (+ on/over) to apply a liquid or antiseptic generously to an area with an absorbent pad
items.ex_en: The nurse used a sterile cotton pad to swab cool antiseptic over the scratch.
items.ex_zh: 护士用无菌棉球在抓伤处仔细涂敷了一层清凉的消毒液。

items.def_en: (+ on/with) To spread or smear a thick, wet substance such as paint, plaster, or mud coarsely or clumsily onto a surface.
items.ex_en: The children proceeded to daub wet river mud over the wooden playhouse walls.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们动手把湿漉漉的河泥胡乱涂抹在木制游戏房的墙上。

items.def_zh: 在…上涂厚厚一层；抹上膏/泥覆盖
items.def_en: (+ sth) cover a surface heavily with a thick, sticky, or paste-like substance
items.ex_en: The mason will plaster over the cracked bricks with a thick mortar coating.
items.ex_zh: 泥瓦匠将用厚厚的一层砂浆泥抹平开裂的砖块表面。

items.def_en: (+ sth) spread a thick layer of a substance thickly or lavishly onto a surface
items.ex_en: You ought to slather on waterproof sunscreen generously before stepping outside into intense sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 步入烈日之前，你真应该在身上厚厚地涂上一层防水防晒霜。

items.def_en: 1. To cover or coat a surface with tar. 2. To characterize or damage someone's reputation unfairly.
items.ex_en: Workers labored under the hot summer sun to tar the newly laid road.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在夏日酷暑下辛勤劳作，给新铺就的道路浇涂焦油。

items.def_en: to cover or smear all over with a greasy, muddy, or staining substance
items.ex_en: Mischievous youths did besmear the ancient stone memorial with soot from the chimney.
items.ex_zh: 淘气的年轻人们用烟囱里的煤烟把古老的石头纪念碑抹得脏污不堪。

items.def_zh: 用杂酚油涂抹（木材等），用防腐油处理
items.def_en: To treat or coat wood with creosote to protect it from rot.
items.ex_en: The railway company hired contractors to creosote newly laid wooden ties along the line.
items.ex_zh: 铁路公司雇佣承包商用杂酚油涂抹沿线新铺设的木质枕木以防腐烂。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) to cover a surface thickly with a sticky or wet paste
items.ex_en: The decorators will plaster the uneven stone wall with smooth white gypsum today.
items.ex_zh: 装修工人今天将用平滑的白色石膏厚厚地糊平不平整的石墙。

items.def_zh: 大量涂抹；厚厚敷上一层
items.def_en: (+ on/with) to spread a thick layer of a substance lavishly over a surface
items.ex_en: The children love to slather sweet strawberry jam lavishly over warm breakfast toast.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们喜欢在热腾腾的早餐吐司上厚厚地抹上一大层甜草莓酱。

groups.summary_en: Spreading, layering, or plastering thick, sticky, or viscous substances (paint, grease, tar, preservative) onto a surface. Nuances range from crude, messy slathering to heavy, protective chemical coating.
groups.summary_zh: 将粘稠或油性物质涂敷、涂抹或糊于表面
groups.desc_en: Involves spreading, wiping, or caking viscous, oily, or messy substances across a surface in an uneven or thick layer, differing from fine 'paint' by emphasizing viscosity, tactile wetness, and crude coverage.
groups.desc_zh: 指将粘稠、膏状或油腻物质粗厚、不均或湿答答地涂敷在物体表面，区别于精细涂刷 (paint)，突出物料的高粘度、粗糙度与厚重感。
groups.nuance_en: smear: spread a messy, oily substance blurrily or dirtying (butter / grease / lipstick) · daub: apply paste or paint crudely with clumsy strokes (clay / ointment / paint) · slather on: lavishly and thickly coat with rich viscous matter (sunscreen / butter / sauce) · plaster over: heavily conceal cracks or flaws with a thick paste (wall / cracks / scandal) · tar: coat defensively or punitively with sticky black pitch (roof / feathers / road)
groups.nuance_zh: smear: 糊乱涂抹蹭脏 (butter / grease / lipstick) · daub: 乱涂乱抹药膏或颜料 (clay / ointment / paint) · slather on: 慷慨厚厚敷上一层 (sunscreen / butter / sauce) · plaster over: 糊上厚厚灰泥以掩饰瑕疵 (wall / cracks / scandal) · tar: 涂抹沥青柏油 (roof / feathers / road)

groups.name: Coat & Treat Surfaces · 表面涂覆与处理 (Tin, Electroplate, Anodize)
groups.tip: 在物体表面镀层或覆盖

items.def_en: (+ sth) lightly cover a surface with a powdery substance
items.ex_en: The baker will dust on powdered sugar over the fresh pastries before serving.
items.ex_zh: 烘焙师在上桌前会在新鲜糕点表面轻轻洒上一层糖粉。

items.def_en: (+ sth) sprinkle a fine layer of flour across the surface of sth
items.ex_en: She told her assistant to flour over the rolling board before kneading the dough.
items.ex_zh: 她吩咐助手在揉面之前先在擀面板表面薄薄撒上一层面粉。

items.def_zh: 镀锡于；（尤指英）将（食品）装罐保存
items.def_en: 1. To coat a metal surface with a thin layer of tin. 2. (chiefly British) To preserve food by putting it into a tin or can.
items.ex_en: Craftsmen carefully tin the interior surface of copper saucepans to prevent toxic contamination.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们仔细地给铜质平底锅内壁镀锡，以防止发生毒性析出。

items.def_zh: 使布满脉纹（或叶脉状条纹）
items.def_en: (usually passive) To cover, streak, or mark a surface with lines or veins like those in marble, wood, or leaves.
items.ex_en: Delicate green mineral deposits vein the polished surface of the luxurious Italian marble table.
items.ex_zh: 细腻的绿色矿物沉积物如脉络般遍布在这张奢华的意大利大理石桌面上。

items.def_zh: 用帆布覆盖；用帆布装备
items.def_en: To cover, line, or equip something with canvas.
items.ex_en: Sailors decided to canvas the open freight compartments against the imminent driving rains.
items.ex_zh: 水手们决定用帆布将敞开的货舱严密覆盖起来，以防大雨浇淋。

items.def_en: To sprinkle or coat food or a cooking surface with flour.
items.ex_en: Make sure you flour the baking tin lightly so the cake releases easily.
items.ex_zh: 确保在烤模上轻轻撒上一层面粉，这样蛋糕就能轻松脱模。

items.def_en: to cover a metal object with a thin coating of another metal, especially gold or silver
items.ex_en: The manufacturing jewelers intend to plate brass decorative fixtures with pure gleaming gold.
items.ex_zh: 这家珠宝制造商打算在黄铜装饰配件表面电镀上一层纯净闪亮的黄金。

items.def_en: to cover thinly with gold leaf or gold paint
items.ex_en: Artisans used fine leaf to gild the elaborate wooden carvings of the altar.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们用精致的金箔给圣坛上繁复的木雕作品细细镀金。

items.def_en: to coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc
items.ex_en: Industrial facilities galvanize structural steel components with molten zinc to resist corrosive marine environments.
items.ex_zh: 工业设施用熔融锌为结构钢构件镀锌，以抵御海洋腐蚀环境。

items.def_en: To coat a metal object with a thin layer of another metal using an electric current.
items.ex_en: Modern factories electroplate steel automotive components with chromium to provide an exceptionally lustrous finish.
items.ex_zh: 现代工厂利用电流在钢制汽车零部件上电镀铬层，以提供极其光亮的饰面。

items.def_zh: 阳极氧化处理（对金属表面进行电解氧化以防腐）
items.def_en: (metallurgy) To coat a metal, especially aluminum, with a protective or decorative oxide layer by electrolysis.
items.ex_en: Specialists electrochemically anodize aluminum bicycle frames to establish exceptional resistance against environmental corrosion.
items.ex_zh: 专业技术人员对铝制自行车架进行电化学阳极氧化处理，以建立起优异的耐腐蚀性。

groups.summary_en: An agent applies a protective, decorative, or culinary layer onto an object's surface through industrial treatment, chemical deposition, or cooking preparation. Verbs are distinguished by the specific material applied (e.g., flour, tin, oxide layer).
groups.summary_zh: 通过化学电镀、机械覆盖或烹饪裹粉在物体表面加覆图层。
groups.desc_en: Applies a substance or thin layer onto a substrate to protect, finish, or decorate it, differing from generic 'cover' by implying specialized surface-altering treatments or culinary/metallurgical coatings.
groups.desc_zh: 指在基底表面涂覆、镀覆或撒敷薄层以起保护、修饰或加工作用，区别于一般'遮盖'在于强调工艺化或料理性的表面改性处理。
groups.nuance_en: flour: dusting a surface lightly with powder (tin / board / meat) · tin: coating metal with a protective layer of molten tin (copper pan / sheet metal) · plate: depositing a thin bonded layer of metal by electrolysis or dipping (silver / nickel / chrome) · gild: applying gold leaf or golden pigment for ornamentation (frame / dome / lettering)
groups.nuance_zh: flour: 撒上薄粉以防粘或调理 (tin / board / meat) · tin: 挂锡或镀锡以防腐 (copper pan / sheet metal) · plate: 电镀或沉浸金属防护层 (silver / nickel / chrome) · gild: 贴金箔或涂金色以修饰 (frame / dome / lettering)

groups.name: Collate & Systematize · 编目与版式排布 (Arranging by Order or System)
groups.tip: 依序排列或重新规划次序

items.def_zh: 起草，编订（清单、表格或文书）
items.def_en: (+ sth) prepare and write out a structured list, plan, or formal document
items.ex_en: The legal team drew up a comprehensive contract for the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队为此次收购拟定了一份详尽的合同。

items.def_en: (+ sth) arrange text, illustrations, or items in a structured, systematic design
items.ex_en: The CEO laid out an ambitious five-year growth strategy.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官详细阐述了一项雄心勃勃的五年增长战略。

items.def_en: (+ sth) arrange a group of things systematically into order or into different categories
items.ex_en: Volunteers helped to sort out the donated clothes into distinct sizes and seasons.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们帮忙将捐赠的衣物按不同尺寸和季节系统地分类整理。

items.def_en: to compile an alphabetized or classified pointer list for information
items.ex_en: Librarians worked diligently to index the historical collection of regional municipal archives systematically.
items.ex_zh: 图书管理员们努力工作，系统地为这批地方市政历史档案编制索引。

items.def_en: to collect and combine texts or pages in proper logical sequence
items.ex_en: Clerks gathered to collate the scattered manuscript pages into their appropriate numerical order.
items.ex_zh: 文员们聚集在一起，把散落的手稿页面按正确的数字顺序整理校对。

items.def_en: to list items individually and systematically
items.ex_en: Accountants must itemize each travel expenditure clearly before submitting the annual reimbursement claim.
items.ex_zh: 会计人员在提交年度报销申请之前，必须将每笔差旅支出逐项列清。

items.def_zh: 按字母顺序排列；用字母表示
items.def_en: to arrange words, names, or items in alphabetical order.
items.ex_en: Please alphabetize the patient files carefully so we can retrieve them without delay.
items.ex_zh: 请将这些病历档案仔细按字母顺序排列，以便我们能毫不迟延地检索。

items.def_zh: 重新排列，重新整理；重新安排（时间等）
items.def_en: to change the position, order, or time of something.
items.ex_en: The manager decided to rearrange the seating layout to encourage better departmental communication.
items.ex_zh: 经理决定重新调整座位布局，以促进部门之间更顺畅的沟通。

items.def_zh: 重新排列，调整顺序；再次订购
items.def_en: 1. to arrange things in a different order or sequence. 2. to order a fresh supply of something.
items.ex_en: The editor asked the writer to reorder several introductory paragraphs for better coherence.
items.ex_zh: 编辑要求作者重新调整开头几个段落的顺序，以提高连贯性。

items.def_en: to set or arrange written text and characters into type ready for printing.
items.ex_en: The historic publisher still hires skilled craftspeople to typeset poetry collections by hand.
items.ex_zh: 这家历史悠久的出版社仍聘请技艺精湛的手艺人来手工排版诗集。

items.def_zh: 将……列成表格，把……制成表格
items.def_en: to arrange data, numbers, or facts systematically in a table with columns and rows.
items.ex_en: Researchers must tabulate the survey responses systematically before performing any advanced statistical analysis.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员在进行任何高级统计分析之前，必须将问卷调查结果系统地列成表格。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the systematic manipulation and structured ordering of items, text, or data into specific sequences, tables, or publication formats.
groups.summary_zh: 指依据字母、数据、逻辑或出版规制对文本和物件进行精细结构化排布。
groups.desc_en: Organizes, categorizes, and formats discrete items or text into a coherent, navigable system, unlike mere 'gather' or 'put' which lack methodical ordering.
groups.desc_zh: 将分散的条目或文本依特定次序与规范整理、编排并定稿，区别于普通的'收集'或'放置'在于其具有严密的系统性与版式结构。
groups.nuance_en: collate: gathering and verifying pages or data in strict sequential order (documents / records / manuscripts) · index: creating a structured alphabetical key to facilitate retrieval (book / archive / database) · itemize: setting down piece by piece in an analytical list (expenses / deductions / damages) · alphabetize: arranging strictly according to the letters of the alphabet (names / files / entries) · lay out: designing the spatial arrangement or schema of elements (page / floor plan / exhibition)
groups.nuance_zh: collate: 按顺序核对并装订整理 (documents / records / manuscripts) · index: 编制索引以便检索 (book / archive / database) · itemize: 逐项列明清单 (expenses / deductions / damages) · alphabetize: 按字母顺序排列 (names / files / entries) · lay out: 规划版面排布或空间布局 (page / floor plan / exhibition)

groups.name: Combust, Scorch & Incinerate · 燃烧、灼烧与焦化 (Burn, Scorch & Char)
groups.tip: 受火热侵蚀发焦燃烧

items.def_zh: 闷烧，阴燃；（情绪）郁积，潜伏
items.def_en: 1. To burn slowly with smoke but without flames. 2. (of feelings) To exist and linger in a hidden or suppressed state.
items.ex_en: Damp fallen leaves continued to smoulder slowly long after the autumn bonfire died.
items.ex_zh: 秋季篝火熄灭良久之后，潮湿的落叶依然在缓缓地冒烟阴燃。

items.def_en: to burn slightly or superficially, especially at the edges, tips, or surface fibers
items.ex_en: A stray flame happened to singe the loose fringes of her knitted scarf.
items.ex_zh: 一记乱溅的火苗不小心燎焦了她针织围巾上松散的流苏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) blacken or become blackened on the surface by intense heat
items.ex_en: Intense heat from the grill will char up the outer surface of steaks.
items.ex_zh: 烤架上的高温很快就会把牛排的外表面烤焦。
items.ex2_en: The dry wooden fence began to char up quickly near the blazing bonfire.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的木栅栏在熊熊燃烧的篝火旁开始迅速烧焦发黑。

items.def_zh: 燃烧；烧毁，灼伤；消耗（能量或燃料）
items.def_en: 1. To be on fire or to catch fire; to destroy, damage, or injure by heat or flames. 2. To consume or be consumed as fuel for energy.
items.ex_en: Dry leaves burn quickly if sparks from the campfire drift into the brush.
items.ex_zh: 如果营火的火星飘进灌木丛，干树叶很快就会燃烧起来。
items.ex2_en: The careless camper burned the dry wooden logs until only gray ash remained.
items.ex2_zh: 粗心的露营者把干木头烧光了，直到只剩下灰白色的灰烬。

items.def_en: 1. To burn or become burned until the surface is blackened. 2. (British, dated) To work as a cleaning woman.
items.ex_en: The intense heat began to char the wooden fence near the outdoor grill.
items.ex_zh: 高温开始将户外烤架附近的木篱笆烤焦发黑。
items.ex2_en: The leftover bread slices charred quickly under the blazing heat of the broiler.
items.ex2_zh: 剩下的面包片在烤箱炙烤档的烈火下很快就烧焦了。

items.def_en: to burn or discolor the surface of something by heat or flame without consuming it entirely
items.ex_en: A careless moment with the hot iron can easily scorch your delicate silk shirt.
items.ex_zh: 用热熨斗稍不留神就会把你娇贵的丝绸衬衫烫焦。
items.ex2_en: The green lawn grass scorched badly during the severe summer drought across the region.
items.ex2_zh: 在全区严重的夏季干旱期间，绿色的草坪被严重晒焦。

items.def_en: (+ sth) be completely consumed by fire or heat, or destroy something totally by burning
items.ex_en: He threw the old letters into the fireplace and watched them burn up completely.
items.ex_zh: 他把旧信件扔进壁炉，看着它们彻底烧成了灰烬。

items.def_zh: 烧焦，灼伤；（烹饪中）高温快煎
items.def_en: 1. To burn or scorch the surface of something with sudden, intense heat. 2. (cooking) To brown the surface of meat quickly at high temperature.
items.ex_en: The chef used a screaming hot cast-iron skillet to sear the fresh tuna steak.
items.ex_zh: 厨师用滚烫的铸铁煎锅高温快煎这块新鲜的金枪鱼排。

items.def_en: 1. To catch fire and burn, or to cause something to burn.
items.ex_en: Certain chemical mixtures may spontaneously combust under conditions of extreme heat and pressure.
items.ex_zh: 某些化学混合物在极度高温高压的条件下可能会发生自燃。
items.ex2_en: Excessive electrical friction can combust dry engine materials inside the damaged industrial machine.
items.ex2_zh: 过度的电摩擦会引燃受损工业机器内部干燥的发动机部件材料。

items.def_en: (+ sth) be completely destroyed by fire, or destroy a building completely with flame
items.ex_en: Faulty wiring caused the historic timber barn to burn down in minutes.
items.ex_zh: 电线故障导致那座历史悠久的木结构谷仓在几分钟内被彻底烧毁。
items.ex2_en: The arsonist used gasoline to burn down the abandoned warehouse late last night.
items.ex2_zh: 纵火犯昨晚深夜用汽油烧毁了那座废弃的仓库。

items.def_en: to burn something completely until it is reduced to ash
items.ex_en: Hospitals operate specialized facilities to incinerate hazardous biological waste safely and completely.
items.ex_zh: 医院运行着专业设施，以安全且彻底地焚化危险的生物废弃物。

groups.summary_en: This frame specifies the chemical reaction of burning and thermal surface degradation caused by intense heat or flame. Verbs distinguish between low-oxygen slow smouldering, generic combustion, surface blackening (charring/searing), and complete destructive burning.
groups.summary_zh: 高温引起的缓慢阴燃、明火燃烧、表面焦化或剧烈灼烧。
groups.desc_en: Transforms or destroys material through high thermal exposure and oxidation, spanning the spectrum from surface singeing to total ash reduction, distinct from generic 'heat'.
groups.desc_zh: 通过热力和氧化作用使物质发生表面灼损直至彻底烧毁的化学物理质变，区别于单纯的'加热'在于伴随焦化、炭化或灰化。
groups.nuance_en: smoulder: burning slowly with smoke but no flame (embers / ruins / turf) · singe: burning superficially or scorching the very tips/edges (eyebrows / feathers / fabric) · scorch: discoloring or drying out a surface with brief intense heat (ironed shirt / grass / earth) · sear: rapidly browning or sealing a surface with extreme high heat (steak / tuna / flesh) · char: blackening and partially reducing to carbon through fire (wood / toast / bone)
groups.nuance_zh: smoulder: 无火闷烧并散发烟雾 (embers / ruins / turf) · singe: 微灼或燎焦表面边缘 (eyebrows / feathers / fabric) · scorch: 烤焦或烘黄表面 (ironed shirt / grass / earth) · sear: 高温骤然炙烤使外表硬脆 (steak / tuna / flesh) · char: 烧焦使其炭化发黑 (wood / toast / bone)

groups.name: Common Animal Calls & Onomatopoeia · 常见动物拟声叫声 (Meow, Moo, Chirp)
groups.tip: 各种动物发出的叫声

items.def_en: (of a cat) to make a continuous low, vibrating sound expressing contentment
items.ex_en: The contented cat began to purr softly as soon as I stroked its chin.
items.ex_zh: 我一抚摸那只满足的猫的下巴，它便轻柔地打起呼噜来。

items.def_en: begin to speak or emit a high-pitched cry or chirp
items.ex_en: The shy boy suddenly decided to pipe up during the tense family discussion.
items.ex_zh: 那个害羞的男孩在紧张的家庭讨论中突然尖声插话了。

items.def_en: (of a pig) to make its quintessential grunting sound
items.ex_en: The hungry piglets began to oink loudly when the farmer approached with feed.
items.ex_zh: 当农夫带着饲料走近时，饥饿的小猪们开始大声哼叫起来。

items.def_en: (of a cat) To make its characteristic crying sound.
items.ex_en: Every morning at dawn, the calico cat would meow outside my bedroom door.
items.ex_zh: 每天清晨拂晓时，那只花猫都会在我的卧室门外喵喵叫。

items.def_zh: 发出吱吱声（或尖叫声）；侥幸通过，勉强胜出
items.def_en: 1. To make a short, high-pitched cry or sound. 2. ('squeak by/through') To succeed or get through with difficulty by a narrow margin.
items.ex_en: The mice would squeak and scurry beneath the floorboards whenever darkness fell.
items.ex_zh: 每当夜幕降临，老鼠就会在地板下吱吱叫着四处乱窜。

items.def_en: (of a cow) To make a long, deep, low sound.
items.ex_en: Across the misty pasture, the dairy cows began to moo for their morning milking.
items.ex_zh: 在薄雾笼罩的牧场对面，奶牛们开始哞哞叫着等待晨间挤奶。

items.def_zh: （小鸟或昆虫）唧唧喳喳叫；轻松愉快地说
items.def_en: 1. (of a small bird or insect) To make short, sharp, high-pitched sounds. 2. To speak in a lively, cheerful way.
items.ex_en: Small sparrows chirp merrily among the leafy branches outside my open window.
items.ex_zh: 小麻雀在我打开的窗外茂密的树枝间欢快地唧唧喳喳叫着。

items.def_en: (of a duck) To make its characteristic harsh, flat sound.
items.ex_en: The ducks continue to quack loudly whenever visitors toss breadcrumbs into the pond.
items.ex_zh: 每当游客往池塘里扔面包屑，鸭子们就会不停地大声嘎嘎叫。

items.def_en: to make the short, sharp, loud explosive sound typical of a dog
items.ex_en: The guard dogs bark fiercely at any stranger approaching the heavy perimeter gate.
items.ex_zh: 看门狗对任何靠近外围大门的陌生人都会猛烈吠叫。

items.def_en: (of a horse) to utter a characteristic high, prolonged whinnying cry
items.ex_en: The startled stallion reared back and began to neigh loudly across the quiet stable.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的种马向后扬起前蹄，在安静的马厩里大声嘶鸣起来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) emit a sharp, abrupt, bark-like sound or cry
items.ex_en: The drill sergeant would constantly bark out fierce commands across the training field.
items.ex_zh: 训练军士经常在训练场上厉声咆哮着下达严厉的指令。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent standard, species-defining onomatopoeic cries of domestic animals, songbirds, and small creatures.
groups.summary_zh: 常见家禽、家畜及小动物的特征性拟声鸣叫与呼唤。
groups.desc_en: Emits characteristic, biologically innate vocalizations by animals, often functioning onomatopoeically and distinguished by the specific species, acoustic pitch, and emotional state.
groups.desc_zh: 动物发出具有物种特异性的本能鸣叫拟声词，依物种类型、声调频率及生理/情绪状态而区分，区别于一般泛指的'发声'。
groups.nuance_en: purr: producing a low, continuous vibrating drone denoting feline contentment (cat / kitten) · squeak: emitting a short, high-pitched shrill cry (mouse / bat) · quack: making a harsh, flat guttural call characteristic of ducks (duck / mallard) · chirp: producing short, sharp, cheerful high notes (bird / cricket / sparrow) · moo: uttering a deep, prolonged lowing sound (cow / cattle / calf)
groups.nuance_zh: purr: 满足时发出低沉持续的咕噜呼噜声 (cat / kitten) · squeak: 发出短促高频的吱吱尖叫 (mouse / bat) · quack: 发出扁平粗嘎的嘎嘎声 (duck / mallard) · chirp: 发出清脆悦耳的啁啾细鸣 (bird / cricket / sparrow) · moo: 发出低沉延长的哞哞叫声 (cow / cattle / calf)

groups.name: Complain & Protest · 申诉至愤抗 (Complain to Remonstrate by Intensity)
groups.tip: 从喋喋不休碎碎念到当面抗议

items.def_en: to make weak, low sounds of complaint or unhappiness
items.ex_en: The exhausted toddler began to whimper softly after dropping her favorite ice cream cone.
items.ex_zh: 掉落了心爱的冰淇淋甜筒后，精疲力竭的小女孩轻声啜泣抱怨起来。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) complain repeatedly in an irritated or whining manner
items.ex_en: He will always moan about the chilly weather whenever winter arrives in town.
items.ex_zh: 每当冬天降临这座小镇，他总会不停地抱怨寒冷的天气。

items.def_en: (archaic or literary) to complain, lament, or express sorrow and dissatisfaction.
items.ex_en: The wounded knight did softly plain of his bitter fate beneath the ancient oaks.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的骑士在古老的橡树下，轻声哀诉着自己凄惨的命运。

items.def_zh: 大声抗议；表达强烈不满
items.def_en: protest loudly or make a vehement public complaint against an injustice
items.ex_en: Local residents cry out against the unfair municipal tax increases outside city hall.
items.ex_zh: 当地居民在市政厅外大声抗议不公的市政税费上涨。

items.def_en: to express discontent, displeasure, pain, or resentment; make a formal complaint.
items.ex_en: Frustrated commuters gathered to complain about the constant train delays during morning rush.
items.ex_zh: 沮丧的通勤者聚在一起，投诉早高峰期间列车的频繁延误。

items.def_zh: 发牢骚，哭诉，抱怨；发出哀鸣，发出尖锐刺耳声
items.def_en: 1. to complain in an annoying, petulant, or tearful voice. [I] 2. to make a long, high-pitched, complaining sound.
items.ex_en: Spoiled children often whine loudly when they are denied sweets before dinner.
items.ex_zh: 被宠坏的孩子在晚饭前吃不到糖果时，常常会刺耳地哭闹抱怨。

items.def_zh: 抱怨，喋喋不休地发牢骚；大声喧嚷
items.def_en: (informal) to talk loudly and continuously, or whine and complain repeatedly.
items.ex_en: Stop your constant yammer about small inconveniences and help me finish this project.
items.ex_zh: 别再为你那点不便絮絮叨叨地发牢骚了，快帮我把这个项目做完。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) complain or protest loudly, bitterly, and forcefully against something
items.ex_en: Activists regularly rail against systemic corruption that harms vulnerable working-class communities.
items.ex_zh: 活动家们经常激烈抗议伤害弱势工人阶级社区的体制性腐败。

items.def_zh: 喧嚷抱怨；大声抗议要求
items.def_en: (+ for/against) to make an insistent, noisy demand or protest
items.ex_en: The angry citizens clamor for justice before the palace gates as tensions escalate.
items.ex_zh: 随着紧张局势升级，愤怒的市民在宫殿门前大声喧嚷要求正义。

items.def_en: (formal) to argue, protest, or make a forcefully reproachful objection against an action or decision.
items.ex_en: The senior diplomat ventured to remonstrate against the dangerous newly proposed foreign policy.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深外交官斗胆就新提出的危险外交政策提出异议与抗议。

items.def_en: (+ against/at) to complain passionately and furiously using abusive language
items.ex_en: The deposed monarch would bitter rail against the treacherous courtiers who betrayed him.
items.ex_zh: 被废黜的君王痛切地怒斥那些背叛了他的奸诈朝臣。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame scale in intensity from ordinary expressions of grievance and petulant whining up to loud, repetitive clamoring and forceful, formal remonstration.
groups.summary_zh: 按不满程度递增，从日常表达委屈、哭丧哀鸣，逐步升级至高声喧嚣乃至正式抗议反驳。
groups.desc_en: Vocalizes dissatisfaction, grievance, or distress across an escalating gradient of loudness, pettiness, and moral indignation, differing from neutral 'say' or 'report'.
groups.desc_zh: 通过言辞或呜咽表达不满、怨怼或愤慨，依委屈呻吟至激烈痛斥的强度递增，区别于中性的'陈述'或'汇报'。
groups.nuance_en: whine: complaining in a high-pitched, childish, or self-pitying tone (child / defeatist) · moan about: grumbling chronically or lugubriously about trivial hardships (taxes / weather / workload) · complain: stating a formal or everyday dissatisfaction directly (customer / patient / neighbor) · rail against: denouncing passionately and angrily with harsh rhetoric (injustice / establishment / fate)
groups.nuance_zh: whine: 带有自怜或幼稚腔调的哭腔抱怨 (child / defeatist) · moan about: 没完没了地低沉牢骚与抱怨琐事 (taxes / weather / workload) · complain: 直接提出常规或正式的不满与申诉 (customer / patient / neighbor) · rail against: 义愤填膺地激烈痛斥或抨击 (injustice / establishment / fate)

groups.name: Congregate & Swarm · 聚集与汇合
groups.tip: 从四处聚到一起

items.def_en: come together or assemble in one place around a common focal point
items.ex_en: Curious villagers gather near the town square whenever important announcements are made.
items.ex_zh: 每当有重大公告发布时，好奇的村民们就会聚集在城镇广场附近。
items.ex2_en: The eager professor gathered his graduate students around the laboratory bench for instructions.
items.ex2_zh: 热切的教授把他的研究生召集在实验台周围听取指导。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) gather closely together in large numbers around a person or point
items.ex_en: Eager fans quickly crowd around the famous actor as he exits the theater.
items.ex_zh: 热切的影迷们在著名演员走出剧场时迅速围拢了上去。

items.def_en: congregate or gather in large numbers in one place
items.ex_en: Migratory geese flock together in massive formations before their long southward autumn journey.
items.ex_zh: 候鸟大雁在秋季漫长的南飞旅程开始前，成群聚集结成庞大阵列。

items.def_en: (+ sth) enter and fill a space in very large, tightly packed numbers
items.ex_en: Hundreds of excited commuters pack into the subway car during the morning rush hour.
items.ex_zh: 早高峰期间，数百名步履匆忙的通勤者挤进了这节地铁车厢。

items.def_zh: 聚集，群集；使成簇，使聚集
items.def_en: To form or gather into a small, close group, or cause things or people to do this.
items.ex_en: Shivering tourists cluster under the small awning to escape the sudden torrential downpour.
items.ex_zh: 瑟瑟发抖的游客们挤在狭小的雨篷下，以躲避突如其来的暴雨。
items.ex2_en: The shepherd used trained sheepdogs to cluster the wandering sheep into a pen.
items.ex2_zh: 牧羊人用训练有素的牧羊犬把散落的羊群聚集到一个羊圈里。

items.def_en: come together as a organized group in one place for a definite purpose
items.ex_en: The delegates will assemble in the main conference hall precisely at nine o'clock.
items.ex_zh: 代表们将于整整九点在主会议大厅正式集合。
items.ex2_en: The director assembled all staff members in the auditorium for an urgent announcement.
items.ex2_zh: 主管将所有员工召集在礼堂里，准备宣布紧急事项。

items.def_en: (+ to) move or come together rapidly in large numbers like a flock of birds
items.ex_en: Thousands of eager shoppers flock to the downtown department stores every holiday season.
items.ex_zh: 每个假日季，数以千计热切的购物者都会蜂拥前往市中心的百货大楼。

items.def_zh: 成群移动，涌往；挤满，群集
items.def_en: (+ into/around/with) When insects, birds, or crowds swarm, they move together in large, dense numbers.
items.ex_en: Aggressive hornets swarm around anyone who ventures too close to their hidden nest.
items.ex_zh: 只要有人靠得离隐蔽的蜂巢太近，凶猛的黄蜂就会群起围攻。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) move toward and meet at a shared point or destination from differing directions
items.ex_en: Scholars from across the globe converge upon the ancient university for the symposium.
items.ex_zh: 来自全球各地的学者们汇聚到这所古老大学参加学术研讨会。

items.def_en: To gather together in a crowd or large group in one place.
items.ex_en: The devout worshippers congregate inside the historic cathedral every Sunday for morning prayer.
items.ex_zh: 虔诚的信徒们每周日都会聚集在这座历史悠久的大教堂内做晨祷。

items.def_en: flock together or pack tightly into a place in overwhelming numbers
items.ex_en: Vast crowds throng the narrow illuminated streets during the annual midsummer lantern festival.
items.ex_zh: 在一年一度的仲夏灯节期间，庞大的人群挤满了狭窄而明亮的街道。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe animate entities or people drawing together from different points to form a dense crowd, mass, or group in a single location.
groups.summary_zh: 人或动物自发地从各处汇集、聚集到一处形成密集群体。
groups.desc_en: Draws multiple animate entities together into a dense spatial grouping, distinguished by movement trajectory, intentionality, and aggregate density compared to generic 'meet'.
groups.desc_zh: 多数生命体向同一空间汇聚聚拢成群，依聚集意图、流动轨迹与聚集密度相区别，不同于普通的'相遇'或'开会'。
groups.nuance_en: gather: coming together naturally or purposefully in one spot (crowd / family / supporters) · assemble: congregating formally in response to a plan or summons (delegates / troops / committee) · flock: moving together in large, eager masses like birds (tourists / pilgrims / shoppers) · swarm: moving or clustering in vast, disordered, buzzing multitudes (bees / children / spectators) · cluster: grouping tightly into small, localized knots (islands / stars / spectators)
groups.nuance_zh: gather: 自然或自发性地聚拢到一处 (crowd / family / supporters) · assemble: 应召集或按计划正式集合 (delegates / troops / committee) · flock: 如群鸟般成群结队蜂拥而至 (tourists / pilgrims / shoppers) · swarm: 密密麻麻如蜂蚁般纷乱涌聚 (bees / children / spectators) · cluster: 紧密聚集成小团或簇 (islands / stars / spectators)

groups.name: Copulate & Mate · 交配与交媾 (Mate, Breed, Mount)
groups.tip: 两性发生性交与交媾行为

items.def_en: (of a male animal) to climb onto a female animal to mate
items.ex_en: The dominant bull prepared to mount the receptive cow during the breeding season.
items.ex_zh: 在繁殖季节，占主导地位的公牛准备爬跨发情的母牛进行交配。

items.def_en: [I/T] (of animals) to pair up and engage in copulation to produce offspring
items.ex_en: Many solitary avian species only mate once each spring to produce new offspring.
items.ex_zh: 许多独居鸟类每年春季只交配一次来繁衍后代。
items.ex2_en: The researcher mated the two prize pigeons to study their inherited feather patterns.
items.ex2_zh: 研究员让这两只特等鸽子交配，以研究它们羽毛图案的遗传。

items.def_en: [I/T] to mate and produce offspring, or to keep animals for reproduction
items.ex_en: Certain rare amphibians will only breed under specific environmental temperature and humidity conditions.
items.ex_zh: 某些稀有两栖动物只有在特定的环境温湿度条件下才会交配繁殖。
items.ex2_en: Local farmers breed sturdy sheep on the windswept hills throughout the winter months.
items.ex2_zh: 当地农民整个冬季都在迎风的山坡上繁育耐寒的羊群。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) engage in sexual activity or intercourse with someone
items.ex_en: Can you help me hook up the sound system to my laptop?
items.ex_zh: 你能帮我把音响系统连接到笔记本电脑上吗？

items.def_en: (+ sb) have sexual intercourse with someone
items.ex_en: She discovered that her partner had decided to sleep with someone else secretly.
items.ex_zh: 她发现自己的伴侣私下里竟然决定与别人发生性关系。

items.def_en: form a romantic or mating partnership with another individual
items.ex_en: The penguins pair off each autumn before embarking on their grueling nesting rituals.
items.ex_zh: 企鹅在每年秋季开始艰苦的筑巢繁殖前都会成对结合。

items.def_en: 1. (British taboo slang) To have sexual intercourse with someone. 2. (baseball) To chase and catch fly balls during practice.
items.ex_en: He bragged constantly about how he managed to shag someone after the party.
items.ex_zh: 他不停吹嘘自己在派对结束后如何搞定并与人睡了一觉。

items.def_en: 1. (taboo slang) To perform anal intercourse on someone. 2. (informal, offensive) To ruin, break, or exhaust someone or something.
items.ex_en: The ruthless prisoners threatened to bugger the newcomer if he did not comply.
items.ex_zh: 那些残忍的囚犯威胁说，如果那个新人不顺从就要对他实施鸡奸。

items.def_en: (+ with) (formal or biology) To have sexual intercourse, especially for reproduction.
items.ex_en: Entomologists observed how the male beetles copulate with females during warm summer nights.
items.ex_zh: 昆虫学家观察了雄性甲虫在炎热夏夜与雌性交配的过程。

items.def_en: (biology / medicine) To introduce semen into a female human or animal to cause pregnancy.
items.ex_en: Veterinarians use advanced techniques to inseminate pedigree livestock with high genetic precision.
items.ex_zh: 兽医利用先进技术对纯种牲畜进行人工授精，以实现极高的基因精准度。

items.def_en: (formal / law) To engage in anal intercourse with someone, especially by force.
items.ex_en: The court found the defendant guilty of attempts to sodomize the vulnerable victim.
items.ex_zh: 法庭裁定被告企图对弱势受害者实施鸡奸性侵的罪名成立。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to sexual intercourse or biological reproduction, spanning clinical biology, zoological pairing, and vulgar or colloquial descriptions of the physical act.
groups.summary_zh: 描述生物配种繁殖或人类性行为的动作，涵盖生物学中性、粗鄙口语及特定方式。
groups.desc_en: Engages in sexual union, spanning biological procreation in animals, formal reproductive pairing, and colloquial human sexual relations, unlike non-sexual 'embrace'.
groups.desc_zh: 指生命体之间的交媾与交配行为，涵盖动物的繁衍骑跨、良种繁育到人类口语化的性行为，区别于非性关系的'拥抱'或'相处'。
groups.nuance_en: mate: pairing of animals for sexual reproduction (birds / wolves / pandas) · mount: assuming the male position on top of the female to copulate (stallion / bull / dog) · breed: systematically mating animals to produce specific offspring (horses / dogs / livestock) · hook up: entering into an informal or casual sexual encounter (students / strangers / exes)
groups.nuance_zh: mate: 动物为繁衍后代而进行交配 (birds / wolves / pandas) · mount: 雄性动物爬跨雌性进行交配 (stallion / bull / dog) · breed: 人工饲养或配种以育种 (horses / dogs / livestock) · hook up: 随意或非正式的发生性关系 (students / strangers / exes)

groups.name: Cover & Conceal · 隐藏与遮盖 (Hide, Mask, Occult)
groups.tip: 将物体藏起避开视线

items.def_en: to hide, protect, or shelter someone or something by interposing a partition or barrier
items.ex_en: Tall evergreen hedges screen the private backyard patio from the busy neighborhood street.
items.ex_zh: 高大的常绿树篱将私密的后院露台与繁忙的社区街道隔挡开来。

items.def_zh: 把……藏起来，遮掩，隐瞒；躲藏，隐蔽
items.def_en: 1. To put or keep something or someone in a place where they cannot be seen or found. 2. To conceal an emotion, secret, or truth.
items.ex_en: The secretive fugitive attempted to hide the stolen diamonds inside an old mattress.
items.ex_zh: 那个行踪隐秘的逃犯试图把偷来的钻石藏在一张旧床垫里。

items.def_en: To put or keep something out of sight; to conceal from view or discovery.
items.ex_en: The dense underbrush had hidden the entrance to the forgotten cave for decades.
items.ex_zh: 几十年来，茂密的灌木丛一直隐匿着那个被遗忘的洞穴入口。

items.def_en: To cover or conceal something so that it cannot easily be seen, heard, or noticed; to hide a feeling, fact, etc. under a false appearance.
items.ex_en: She wore a cheerful smile to mask the deep sorrow burdening her heart.
items.ex_zh: 她脸上带着欢快的微笑，以此掩饰压在心头的深深悲伤。

items.def_en: (+ sth) place something over an object to hide it from view, or conceal wrongdoing
items.ex_en: Corrupt officials conspired desperately to cover up their extensive financial crimes before audit.
items.ex_zh: 腐败官员在审计之前极力串通，企图掩盖他们庞大的经济罪行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) stop light from entering or obscure something from view by standing in front of it
items.ex_en: Heavy velvet drapes block out the bright morning sunshine effectively in the bedroom.
items.ex_zh: 厚重的丝绒窗帘在卧室里有效地遮挡住了清晨刺眼的阳光。

items.def_en: (+ sth) separate and conceal an area or object from sight using a barrier or screen
items.ex_en: The nurses used portable dividers to screen off the patient during emergency examination.
items.ex_zh: 护士们在紧急检查期间用移动隔板将患者遮蔽开来。

items.def_en: to conceal or enclose something with or as if with a hanging curtain
items.ex_en: Thick climbing ivy rose to curtain the crumbling stone walls of the mansion.
items.ex_zh: 浓密的攀缘常春藤生长蔓延，宛如帘幕般遮蔽了庄园残破的石墙。

items.def_en: to prevent something from being seen or heard clearly by dimming or obstructing it
items.ex_en: Thick maritime fog rolled inland to obscure the tall lighthouse from passing ships.
items.ex_zh: 浓重的海雾向内陆蔓延，模糊了过往船只望向高大灯塔的视线。

items.def_en: To hide or block something from view; (in astronomy) to cut off light from a celestial body by passing in front of it.
items.ex_en: During the solar eclipse, the passing moon will completely occult the radiant sun.
items.ex_zh: 在日食期间，经过的月球将会完全掩食光芒四射的太阳。

items.def_en: To cover someone's eyes with a piece of cloth so that they cannot see.
items.ex_en: The kidnappers chose to blindfold the hostage tightly before transporting him anywhere else.
items.ex_zh: 绑匪在将人质转移到别处之前，选择将他的双眼紧紧蒙住。

groups.summary_en: An agent or object places something out of visual or cognitive reach by interposing a covering, barrier, or blind. Verbs range from basic everyday concealment to specialized sensory blocking and astronomical/technical obscuration.
groups.summary_zh: 通过覆盖物、眼罩或物理阻隔将目标置于视线之外或隐蔽。
groups.desc_en: Interposes a barrier between an object and an observer to make it unseen, undetectable, or confidential, differing from 'protect' by focusing strictly on visual or cognitive obscurity.
groups.desc_zh: 在客体与观察者之间设立物理或信息屏障以遮蔽视线或隐匿真相，侧重视线认知阻隔而非实质保护。
groups.nuance_en: hide: placing out of sight to prevent detection (weapon / evidence / feelings) · mask: disguising the real nature or odor of something with a deceptive exterior (symptoms / pain / smell) · screen: shielding from sight or wind using a barrier or partition (porch / view / eyes) · cover up: actively and deceitfully concealing a scandal or misdeed (affair / scandal / crime) · curtain: enclosing or obscuring with hanging fabrics (window / bed / stage)
groups.nuance_zh: hide: 藏匿使脱离视线或不被发现 (weapon / evidence / feelings) · mask: 伪装遮蔽以掩盖本来面貌或气味 (symptoms / pain / smell) · screen: 用屏风或遮挡物遮蔽视线 (porch / view / eyes) · cover up: 恶意蓄意掩盖劣迹或丑闻 (affair / scandal / crime) · curtain: 用挂帘遮掩隔绝 (window / bed / stage)

groups.name: Cover & Envelop · 遮盖与涂覆 (Coat, Blanket, Encase)
groups.tip: 给物体蒙上罩布或涂覆保护层

items.def_en: (+ sth) enclose or cover something completely in paper, cloth, or protective material
items.ex_en: Let's wrap up this meeting so everyone can catch their flights.
items.ex_zh: 我们结束这次会议吧，这样大家都能赶上航班。

items.def_en: To cover or coat something with a layer of copper.
items.ex_en: Shipbuilders would copper the wooden hull beneath the waterline to deter marine borers.
items.ex_zh: 造船工人会用铜包裹吃水线以下的木质船体，以抵御海洋蛀虫。

items.def_en: To coat or treat something with rubber.
items.ex_en: The manufacturer decided to rubber the heavy steel handles for better worker grip.
items.ex_zh: 制造商决定在沉重的钢手柄上包一层橡胶，以便工人抓握。

items.def_en: to cover the surface of an object with a thin decorative or protective coating
items.ex_en: Craftsmen overlay the plain mahogany base with exquisite patterns of shimmering mother-of-pearl.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们在普通的红木底座表面铺贴上一层流光溢彩的精致珍珠母贝图案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) cover an entire area or surface heavily with a thick layer of something
items.ex_en: A thick morning fog blanketed the quiet mountain village in total silence.
items.ex_zh: 清晨浓重的大雾将寂静的山村完全笼罩在一片死寂之中。

items.def_zh: 把…装入硬壳中；密封包裹
items.def_en: (+ sth) enclose something entirely in a protective shell, frame, or container
items.ex_en: The final step in making a hardcover book is to case in the sewn text block.
items.ex_zh: 制作精装书的最后一步是将缝合好的书芯套壳装订。

items.def_zh: 罩上，覆盖；给……戴上风帽（或头巾）
items.def_en: To cover something with or as if with a hood.
items.ex_en: She hooded the lens to protect it from sudden bursts of direct sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 她给镜头罩上遮光罩，以防止刺眼的阳光直射。

items.def_zh: 厚厚地覆盖；在……上铺地毯；严厉训斥
items.def_en: 1. To cover something completely with a thick layer, like a carpet. 2. (informal) To severely reprimand or scold someone.
items.ex_en: The boss carpeted Tom for missing another critical project deadline this morning.
items.ex_zh: 老板今天早上严厉训斥了汤姆，因为他又错过了关键的项目截止日期。

items.def_en: To cover something completely with a thick, dense layer of something.
items.ex_en: Heavy overnight snow blanketed the entire city, bringing all morning traffic to a halt.
items.ex_zh: 昨夜的大雪完全覆盖了整座城市，致使早晨的交通全部瘫痪。

items.def_en: to encase or cover something in a protective outer layer of metal, plastic, or wood
items.ex_en: The ancient artisans sheathed the magnificent wooden temple pillars in gleaming bronze plates.
items.ex_zh: 古代工匠用闪亮的青铜薄板包裹起宏伟的木制庙宇立柱。

items.def_en: to surround or completely enclose something within a hard or protective layer
items.ex_en: Specialists encase the delicate reactor core in thick layers of reinforced concrete.
items.ex_zh: 专家们用厚厚的钢筋混凝土层将脆弱的反应堆堆芯完全包围起来。

groups.summary_en: An agent or substance forms an extensive protective, industrial, or insulating layer over an underlying surface or object. The verbs differ primarily in the mechanical manner, medium, or material thickness (e.g., metals, rubber, textile covers, or atmospheric drifts).
groups.summary_zh: 以特定材质或厚重表层对物体进行紧密包裹或涂覆。
groups.desc_en: Spreads a continuous protective or enveloping material completely over an area or object, emphasizing physical encapsulation or surface-wide carpeting rather than concealment.
groups.desc_zh: 在物体外表铺展或包裹一层连续的材料以形成全面包覆或铺垫，强调物理包封与全域铺设而非刻意隐瞒。
groups.nuance_en: blanket in: covering completely with a thick, unbroken, muffling layer (snow / smoke / fog) · carpet: spreading across a horizontal surface like a woven floor-covering (leaves / flowers / debris) · encase: enclosing securely inside a rigid or form-fitting protective case (concrete / armor / glass) · wrap up: bundling tightly in flexible folds of paper or fabric (package / baby / scarf) · overlay: laying an ornamental or finishing film smoothly atop a surface (veneer / gold leaf / tile)
groups.nuance_zh: blanket in: 密不透风地厚厚裹覆覆盖 (snow / smoke / fog) · carpet: 像地毯般平铺覆盖地面 (leaves / flowers / debris) · encase: 严密嵌装在坚固的外壳内 (concrete / armor / glass) · wrap up: 用柔软纸布等紧密包裹包裹 (package / baby / scarf) · overlay: 平铺覆贴装饰或保护外层 (veneer / gold leaf / tile)

groups.name: Damage & Disfigure · 毁损与残损 (Blight, Disfigure, Mangle)
groups.tip: 从外观损毁到功能丧失

items.def_en: to impair the appearance, quality, or perfection of something
items.ex_en: A persistent, bitter feud marred the serenity of their ancestral home for decades.
items.ex_zh: 一场旷日持久的宿怨数十年来玷污了他们祖宅的宁静。

items.def_en: (+ sth) spoil the appearance, condition, or proper functioning of something
items.ex_en: He accidentally messed up the complex wiring while trying to fix the old amplifier.
items.ex_zh: 他试图修理那台旧功放时，不小心弄乱了复杂的线路。

items.def_en: to spoil the surface or appearance of something, especially by writing or drawing on it
items.ex_en: Vandals defaced the historic marble monument with bright red spray paint overnight.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子在一夜之间用鲜红色的喷漆涂损了这座历史悠久的大理石纪念碑。

items.def_zh: 击穿（船底），使（船底）破损漏水；（船底）破裂
items.def_en: (nautical) To break or stave in the bottom of a ship, causing it to take on water; to suffer such damage.
items.ex_en: The jagged reef bilged the wooden schooner during the violent midnight gale.
items.ex_zh: 锯齿状的暗礁在午夜狂风中击穿了木质帆船的船底。
items.ex2_en: The old fishing vessel bilged on the rocky reef during the storm.
items.ex2_zh: 那艘旧渔船在暴风雨中撞击暗礁导致船底破裂。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) hurt someone badly or batter an object by repeatedly striking them violently
items.ex_en: Don't beat yourself up over an honest mistake.
items.ex_zh: 不要因为一次无心之失而过度自责。

items.def_en: (+ sth) damage or mutilate something severely by ripping it violently into pieces
items.ex_en: He tore up the draft agreement in frustration and walked out of the room.
items.ex_zh: 他沮丧地撕毁了协议草案，甩门而去。

items.def_zh: 破坏，毁害；使染上枯萎病
items.def_en: 1. To spoil, damage, or severely impair something. 2. (of plant diseases) To infect crops or plants with blight.
items.ex_en: Persistent poverty and corruption blighted the economic hopes of the entire rural province.
items.ex_zh: 持续的贫困与腐败毁掉了整个农业省份的经济希望。

items.def_zh: 严重损毁，压碎，撕碎；乱改，糟蹋（文句或音乐等）
items.def_en: 1. To damage something severely by crushing, tearing, or twisting it out of shape. 2. To ruin or spoil something, such as speech or music, by performing or rendering it badly.
items.ex_en: The heavy hydraulic press mangled the steel frame beyond any possible repair.
items.ex_zh: 重型液压机将钢制框架压得严重变形，根本无法修复。

items.def_zh: 毁容，破损……的外貌，损害……的外观
items.def_en: To spoil or permanently damage the appearance of someone or something.
items.ex_en: The explosion disfigured the historic facade of the ancient stone cathedral.
items.ex_zh: 爆炸严重损毁了那座古老石质大教堂的历史外立面。

items.def_zh: 肆意破坏，蓄意毁坏（公私财物）
items.def_en: To deliberately destroy or damage public or private property.
items.ex_en: Rowdy teenagers vandalized the neighborhood park, breaking benches and smashing streetlamps.
items.ex_zh: 吵闹的青少年蓄意破坏了社区公园，砸碎了长凳，击毁了路灯。

items.def_en: to inflict severe, dismembering, or permanent damage that ruins the structure or form
items.ex_en: The violent blast mutilated the priceless statue beyond all recognition.
items.ex_zh: 剧烈的爆炸严重毁损了那尊珍贵的雕像，使其变得面目全非。

groups.summary_en: An agent, disease, or external force causes severe structural, functional, or aesthetic harm to a surface, entity, or human body. Verbs vary in intensity from marring aesthetic value or spoiling growth to violently mutilating physical integrity.
groups.summary_zh: 描述对外观、结构或整体完好性造成破坏、残损与损毁。
groups.desc_en: Inflicts physical, aesthetic, or functional impairment upon an entity, ranging from superficial surface blemish to catastrophic structural mangling, contrasting with total 'destroy'.
groups.desc_zh: 对实体造成外观、美感或结构功能上的残损破坏，从表层瑕疵至剧烈碎裂不等，区别于彻底抹除的'毁灭'。
groups.nuance_en: mar: spoiling the perfection, smoothness, or beauty of something (surface / reputation / occasion) · deface: intentionally spoiling or vandalizing the visible exterior (monument / building / poster) · blight: withering, ruining, or casting an enduring curse upon (crop / landscape / prospects) · mangle: violently crushing, tearing, or twisting out of recognizable shape (limb / vehicle / body)
groups.nuance_zh: mar: 损伤完好外貌或美感造成微瑕 (surface / reputation / occasion) · deface: 蓄意涂鸦乱刻毁坏外貌 (monument / building / poster) · blight: 枯萎、毁坏或长期投下阴影 (crop / landscape / prospects) · mangle: 猛烈碾压扯碎使其面目全非 (limb / vehicle / body)

groups.name: Defeat & Prevail · 击败与战胜 (Vanquish, Overcome, Crush)
groups.tip: 击溃对手并彻底征服占领

items.def_en: (+ sb) defeat an opponent or rival who challenges you, forcing them away
items.ex_en: The defending champion easily saw off his aggressive young challenger in straight sets.
items.ex_zh: 卫冕冠军直落数盘，轻松击败了年轻气盛的挑战者。

items.def_en: succeed after facing strong opposition or competition; prevail ultimately
items.ex_en: Despite all the political interference, common sense eventually won out.
items.ex_zh: 尽管受到重重政治干扰，常识和理性最终还是占了上风。

items.def_en: to succeed in dealing with or gaining control over an opponent, obstacle, or feeling
items.ex_en: Through relentless determination, she overcame severe stage fright before her major concert debut.
items.ex_zh: 凭借顽强的毅力，她在大型音乐会首演前克服了严重的怯场心理。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) defeat an opponent completely or destroy their remaining resistance
items.ex_en: A glass of warm milk helped finish off the night.
items.ex_zh: 一杯热牛奶为这个夜晚画上了圆满的句号。

items.def_en: 1. To take control of a country or territory by military force. 2. To successfully overcome a fear, problem, or difficulty.
items.ex_en: The emperor led seasoned legions across arid plains to conquer neighboring kingdoms.
items.ex_zh: 皇帝率领身经百战的军团穿过干旱平原，征服了邻近的王国。

items.def_en: (+ over) To gain a great victory or achieve success after a struggle or contest.
items.ex_en: Justice will ultimately triumph over oppression after this long and bitter struggle.
items.ex_zh: 在这场漫长而艰苦的抗争之后，正义终将战胜压迫。

items.def_zh: 战胜，击败，获胜；流行，盛行
items.def_en: 1. (+ against/over) To defeat an opponent or succeed after a difficult struggle. 2. To be widespread, dominant, or commonly accepted.
items.ex_en: Courageous villagers prevailed against the invading army despite suffering overwhelming odds.
items.ex_zh: 尽管敌众我寡，勇敢的村民们最终还是击败了侵略军。

items.def_en: to defeat an enemy or opposing team completely and force them to flee in disorder
items.ex_en: Allied forces routed the enemy division, forcing survivors to flee in total panic.
items.ex_zh: 盟军彻底击溃了敌方师团，迫使残部惊慌失措地四散逃窜。

items.def_en: (literary) To defeat an enemy, opponent, or fear completely.
items.ex_en: The legendary warrior vanquished the shadowy beast that haunted the quiet woodland realm.
items.ex_zh: 传奇勇士彻底斩杀了盘踞在寂静林地王国中的幽暗巨兽。

items.def_en: (informal) To defeat an opponent completely and by a wide margin.
items.ex_en: Our hometown basketball team trounced their bitter rivals by thirty points last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚我们的家乡篮球队以三十分的巨大优势痛宰了死敌。

items.def_en: to defeat or suppress someone or something decisively and completely
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime crushed the sudden civilian uprising with overwhelming military force.
items.ex_zh: 该威权政权以压倒性的军事力量彻底粉碎了突如其来的平民起义。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate overcoming an opponent or obstacle in contest or combat, progressing from winning or asserting dominance to crushing and utterly obliterating an adversary.
groups.summary_zh: 指在竞争、冲突或战争中战胜敌手，由最终占优升华至彻底毁灭性击溃。
groups.desc_en: Gains decisive mastery over an adversary, obstacle, or difficulty through exertion, ranging from outlasting resistance to complete physical rout, contrasting with passive 'win'.
groups.desc_zh: 通过力量或意志压倒对手、阻碍或逆境以确立胜局，从艰难耐受胜出到彻底击溃驱逐，区别于中性的单纯'获胜'。
groups.nuance_en: overcome: mastering a challenge, handicap, or emotional hurdle through effort (fear / adversity / deficit) · prevail: emerging victorious after a protracted contest or enduring struggle (justice / logic / team) · rout: defeating overwhelmingly and driving into chaotic, disorganized retreat (army / opponent / enemy) · see off: decisively confronting and repelling an incoming challenger (rival / threat / intruder) · conquer: subjecting by military might or fully subordinating an arduous obstacle (territory / mountain / addiction)
groups.nuance_zh: overcome: 克服阻力、情绪或弱点 (fear / adversity / deficit) · prevail: 经漫长较量最终占得上风 (justice / logic / team) · rout: 彻底击溃并迫使敌方狼狈溃逃 (army / opponent / enemy) · see off: 成功击退并解决外来挑战者 (rival / threat / intruder) · conquer: 彻底征服领土或攻克艰巨难关 (territory / mountain / addiction)

groups.name: Defiance & Insurrection · 反抗与叛乱 (Oppose, Resist, Revolt)
groups.tip: 从被动抵制到公然叛变

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) oppose, resist, or actively disagree with an authority's plan or demand
items.ex_en: Discontented employees pushed back against the sudden mandate demanding five days in office.
items.ex_zh: 不满的员工强烈抵制要求每周五天在办公室办公的突发规定。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) resist or confront a powerful authority or bully courageously without flinching
items.ex_en: These materials are designed to stand up to extreme weather conditions.
items.ex_zh: 这些材料旨在经受住极端天气的考验。

items.def_en: To disagree strongly with a plan or policy and try to prevent it; to fight, resist, or compete against someone.
items.ex_en: Environmental groups fiercely oppose the sudden construction of a sprawling chemical plant.
items.ex_zh: 环保团体强烈反对突如其来建造大型化工厂的计划。

items.def_zh: 反抗，抵制，违抗；（马等）猛然弓背跃起
items.def_en: 1. To resist, oppose, or refuse to comply with a trend, system, or authority. 2. (of a horse) To jump vertically with an arched back to throw off a rider.
items.ex_en: The small startup bucked industry standards by offering completely transparent product pricing.
items.ex_zh: 这家小型初创公司逆行业常规而行，推出了完全透明的产品定价。

items.def_zh: 反抗，抵制；忍住，克制；抗拒（疾病、外力等）
items.def_en: 1. To fight against or oppose someone or something. 2. To stop yourself from doing or having something you want.
items.ex_en: Disciplined soldiers managed to resist fierce enemy artillery assaults throughout the cold night.
items.ex_zh: 训练有素的士兵在寒冷的夜里成功抵挡住了敌人猛烈的炮击。

items.def_en: to openly resist or refuse to obey an authority, rule, or expectation
items.ex_en: Brazen demonstrators defied the curfew, staging mass rallies across the capital's central square.
items.ex_zh: 无畏的示威者公然藐视宵禁，在首都中心广场举行了大规模集会。

items.def_en: rebel against an oppressive government or authority, often using violent insurrection
items.ex_en: The citizens rose up against the corrupt military regime.
items.ex_zh: 市民们揭竿而起，反抗腐败的军事政权。

items.def_en: To oppose or fight against people in authority or a government; to take part in a rebellion.
items.ex_en: Oppressed workers finally rebelled against the corrupt management after months of unpaid wages.
items.ex_zh: 被拖欠数月薪水后，受压迫的工人们终于奋起反抗腐败的管理层。

items.def_zh: 反叛，起义，反抗；（使）反感，（使）恶心
items.def_en: 1. To take violent action against a government or authority; to rebel. 2. To feel or cause to feel strong disgust or shock.
items.ex_en: Impoverished citizens revolted against the ruthless tyrant, storming state armories across town.
items.ex_zh: 贫困的百姓奋起反抗残酷的暴君，冲进了全城的多处国立军械库。

items.def_en: to rise up in active, armed rebellion against recognized authority
items.ex_en: Oppressed highland clans insurged against the imperial throne to reclaim their ancestral rights.
items.ex_zh: 受压迫的高原部族揭竿而起反抗帝国皇权，以夺回祖传的权益。

items.def_en: (especially of soldiers or sailors) to openly rebel against military commanders
items.ex_en: Starving crew members mutinied against the tyrannical captain, seizing control of the vessel.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的船员们哗变反抗残暴的船长，夺取了货船的控制权。

groups.summary_en: Verbs tracking escalation in defiance against an authority, policy, or regime—from passive or political disagreement to armed insurrection.
groups.summary_zh: 从政策抵制、公然违抗升级至武装叛乱或暴力颠覆政权。
groups.desc_en: Refuses compliance and actively confronts an authority, norm, or coercive force across an escalating spectrum from tacit pushback to armed uprising, differing from passive 'disagree'.
groups.desc_zh: 拒绝服从并公开对抗权威、法规或压迫力量，涵盖从隐忍顶撞到武装叛乱的对抗强度，区别于消极的'不同意'。
groups.nuance_en: resist: exerting counterforce to withstand pressure or encroachment (arrest / temptation / invasion) · defy: openly and audaciously flouting an order, law, or authority (court / ban / odds) · buck: kicking against or refusing to conform to an established norm (trend / system / convention) · rise up: mobilizing en masse in armed or collective revolt (citizens / peasants / proletariat) · rebel: actively renouncing allegiance and taking up arms against governance (insurgents / colonies / youth)
groups.nuance_zh: resist: 抵受外力施压或侵害 (arrest / temptation / invasion) · defy: 公开挑衅并蔑视权威或禁令 (court / ban / odds) · buck: 顶撞或逆反既定规则与趋势 (trend / system / convention) · rise up: 掀起集体或武装起义 (citizens / peasants / proletariat) · rebel: 彻底背叛并反抗既定政权或秩序 (insurgents / colonies / youth)

groups.name: Derision & Open Contempt · 嘲弄与讥诮 (Mock, Ridicule, Jeer)
groups.tip: 以挖苦模仿方式取笑他人

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) tease or mock someone, exposing them to ridicule
items.ex_en: Classmates poked fun at his mismatched neon socks throughout the entire morning assembly.
items.ex_zh: 在整个早会上，同学们都在拿他那双不配对的荧光色袜子打趣。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) make fun of or deride someone in an unkind, mocking way
items.ex_en: Cruel bullies laughed at his clumsy attempt to jump across the wide stream.
items.ex_zh: 恶劣的霸凌者嘲笑他试图跳过宽阔溪流时的笨拙动作。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) treat someone or an idea with spoken scorn, disbelief, and open contempt
items.ex_en: Skeptical scientists scoffed at his bizarre theory regarding instantaneous time travel across galaxies.
items.ex_zh: 持怀疑态度的科学家们对他关于星系间瞬间穿越的离奇理论嗤之以鼻。

items.def_en: tease or laugh at in a scornful or contemptuous manner, often by imitating
items.ex_en: Rude spectators mocked the stammering speaker by mimicking his nervous hand gestures repeatedly.
items.ex_zh: 粗鲁的观众反复模仿发言人紧张的手势，以此嘲弄结结巴巴的他。

items.def_zh: 嘲笑，讥讽，嘲弄；狼吞虎咽地吃
items.def_en: 1. (+ at) To speak about someone or something in a scornful, mocking way. 2. (informal) To eat food quickly and greedily.
items.ex_en: Critics scoffed when the rookie politician claimed he could end corruption within weeks.
items.ex_zh: 当那位政坛新手声称能在数周内消除腐败时，批评人士纷纷讥讽嘲笑。

items.def_en: express contempt for or dismiss someone or something as completely worthless
items.ex_en: Arrogant elites derided the ambitious young inventor's prototype as childish nonsense.
items.ex_zh: 傲慢的精英阶层嘲笑那位雄心勃勃的年轻发明家的原型机是幼稚的胡闹。

items.def_en: (informal, especially US) To tease, mock, or heckle someone playfully or derisively.
items.ex_en: Teammates razzed the quarterback endlessly after he threw three interceptions in one half.
items.ex_zh: 四分卫在一个半场内送出三次抄截后，队友们无情地戏弄起他来。

items.def_en: To make fun of someone or something in an unkind or mocking way.
items.ex_en: Cynical commentators ridiculed the prime minister's ambitious new economic strategy on national television.
items.ex_zh: 愤世嫉俗的评论员在国家电视台节目中嘲弄了首相雄心勃勃的新经济战略。

items.def_en: provoke or challenge someone with insulting, hurtful remarks
items.ex_en: Rival fans taunted the distraught striker as he missed the crucial penalty kick.
items.ex_zh: 当失落的前锋罚丢关键点球时，对手的球迷大声奚落挑衅他。

items.def_en: interrupt a public speaker or performer with aggressive, derisive comments
items.ex_en: Angry protestors heckled the cabinet minister throughout his speech on pension reforms.
items.ex_zh: 在内阁部长就养老金改革发表演讲时，愤怒的抗议者不断起哄喝倒彩。

items.def_en: To laugh at or shout rude, mocking remarks at someone.
items.ex_en: Disappointed fans jeered loudly when their star player missed the easy open net.
items.ex_zh: 当当家球星面对空门却将球打飞时，失望的球迷们大声起哄嘲弄。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent aggressive speech acts intended to belittle, humiliate, or laugh at a target, ranging from spoken scornful dismissiveness (scoff), playful teasing to harsh teasing (razz), direct exposure to laughing absurdity (ridicule), to loud vocal hostility (jeer).
groups.summary_zh: 通过言辞或叫嚣嘲笑、贬低或公开羞辱他人，流露不屑与敌意。
groups.desc_en: Subjects someone or something to malicious laughter, parody, or contemptuous dismissiveness, distinguished from harmless humor by its belittling and hurtful intent.
groups.desc_zh: 以言辞、笑声或模仿对人事物进行轻蔑排挤与贬抑，区别于无恶意的'幽默'在于其蓄意贬低与不敬伤害。
groups.nuance_en: mock: mimicking or parodying contemptuously to expose absurdity (accent / victim / gestures) · ridicule: exposing someone to harsh collective laughter or absurd characterization (proposal / beliefs / theory) · deride: treating with disdainful, intellectual scorn as utterly worthless (claims / efforts / critics) · scoff at: expressing derisive incredulity or dismissing as absurdly improbable (idea / warning / suggestion) · razz: teasing loudly and good-naturedly or heckling boisterously (player / teammate / speaker)
groups.nuance_zh: mock: 恶毒模仿或嘲讽以揭示荒唐 (accent / victim / gestures) · ridicule: 将其作为笑柄大加取笑讽刺 (proposal / beliefs / theory) · deride: 视其毫无价值而冷酷贬损嘲弄 (claims / efforts / critics) · scoff at: 不屑一顾地轻蔑嘲笑怀疑 (idea / warning / suggestion) · razz: 起哄戏弄或喝倒彩嘲弄 (player / teammate / speaker)

groups.name: Deteriorate & Worsen · 恶化与退化 (Exacerbate, Decay, Devolve)
groups.tip: 不良状况加剧恶化

items.def_en: [I/T] to become of poorer quality or make an existing problem more severe
items.ex_en: Torrential rain worsened already hazardous driving conditions along the narrow mountain pass.
items.ex_zh: 倾盆大雨让狭窄山口原本就危险的驾驶条件变得更加恶劣。
items.ex2_en: His chronic health conditions worsened rapidly after he moved to the humid city.
items.ex2_zh: 搬到潮湿的城市后，他的慢性健康状况迅速恶化。

items.def_en: gradually deteriorate in quality, health, or condition
items.ex_en: His fragile health went downhill rapidly after contracting a severe viral infection last winter.
items.ex_zh: 自去年冬天感染严重病毒后，他本就虚弱的健康状况急转直下。

items.def_en: [I/T] to undergo progressive structural, moral, or biological decline
items.ex_en: Forgotten fruit trees slowly decayed under the suffocating grip of wild toxic weeds.
items.ex_zh: 无人照料的果树在野生毒草的窒息性缠绕下慢慢衰亡腐烂。
items.ex2_en: Excessive moisture and airborne bacteria quickly decayed the unprotected wood on the porch.
items.ex2_zh: 过多的湿气和空气中的细菌迅速腐蚀了门廊上未受保护的木材。

items.def_zh: （病情）复发；重新陷入（恶习或不良状态）
items.def_en: To become ill again after an apparent improvement, or to return to bad behavior or an undesirable condition.
items.ex_en: The recovering patient relapsed into clinical depression following the sudden loss of employment.
items.ex_zh: 在突然失去工作后，这位康复中的患者抑郁症复发。

items.def_zh: 倒退，退化，退回到（较差状态）
items.def_en: To return to an earlier, less advanced, or worse state of development, behavior, or condition.
items.ex_en: Under intense academic pressure, the traumatized toddler regressed to bedwetting and thumb-sucking behaviors.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大的学业压力下，受到创伤的幼童退化出了尿床和吮吸手指的行为。

items.def_en: disintegrate or break down completely in structure or condition
items.ex_en: The coalition government fell apart completely after months of bitter internal ideological clashes.
items.ex_zh: 经过数月激烈的内部意识形态冲突，联合政府彻底瓦解崩溃。

items.def_en: become completely broken, disorganized, or mentally incapacitated
items.ex_en: She went to pieces completely when police delivered the tragic news about her brother.
items.ex_zh: 当警察带来有关她兄弟的悲惨噩耗时，她整个人彻底崩溃了。

items.def_zh: 加重，使加剧，使恶化；激怒
items.def_en: 1. To make an injury, illness, or bad situation worse. 2. (informal) To annoy or exasperate someone.
items.ex_en: Carrying heavy boxes will aggravate your acute back strain and delay your recovery.
items.ex_zh: 搬运重箱子会加重你背部的急性拉伤，并延缓康复进程。

items.def_en: To become worse in quality, condition, health, or moral standards over time.
items.ex_en: The peaceful protest quickly degenerated into chaotic street brawls and widespread looting.
items.ex_zh: 这场和平抗议迅速恶化演变成了混乱的街头群殴和大范围抢劫。

items.def_en: to make a problem, disease, or bad situation significantly worse
items.ex_en: The sudden interest rate hike exacerbated the struggles of heavily indebted young homeowners.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的加息进一步加剧了负债累累的年轻业主的困境。

items.def_en: (+ into) to degenerate progressively into a lower or disordered state
items.ex_en: The peaceful demonstration devolved into violent riots after police fired tear gas canisters.
items.ex_zh: 在警方发射催泪瓦斯罐后，和平示威迅速蜕变成暴力骚乱。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey the decline of a condition, health, or structure toward a lower, more broken, or more severe state, progressing from setback and regression to compounding decay and acute aggravation.
groups.summary_zh: 指状态、健康或局势向下退化变劣，从复发倒退升级至严重恶化崩塌。
groups.desc_en: Undergoes progressive loss of health, order, functional integrity, or moral quality along a negative trajectory, contrasting with stationary 'fail' or deliberate 'ruin'.
groups.desc_zh: 沿着负面轨迹发生机能退化、结构瓦解或病势加重，体现动态退化过程，区别于瞬间发生的'失败'或人为的'破坏'。
groups.nuance_en: worsen: becoming more severe, critical, or unfavorable (condition / economy / relations) · decay: decomposing organically or undergoing steady cultural/structural decline (teeth / corpse / empire) · regress: slipping backward into an earlier, less developed, or primitive state (behavior / patient / society) · fall apart: losing structural cohesion or emotional composure entirely (structure / marriage / person) · aggravate: intensifying the severity, pain, or vexation of an already bad state (injury / conflict / symptoms)
groups.nuance_zh: worsen: 情况、病情或关系进一步恶化加剧 (condition / economy / relations) · decay: 发生有机腐朽或文明制度衰亡 (teeth / corpse / empire) · regress: 倒退退化至早期原始状态 (behavior / patient / society) · fall apart: 彻底瓦解崩溃或分崩离析 (structure / marriage / person) · aggravate: 使既有的伤痛或恶局更形恶化 (injury / conflict / symptoms)

groups.name: Dig & Excavate · 挖掘与开凿铲挖 (Dig, Spade, Gouge)
groups.tip: 从浅层翻土到深层凿坑

items.def_en: (+ sth) create a cavity or remove material with a curved tool or hands
items.ex_en: The baker scooped out the ripe pumpkin flesh to prepare fragrant autumn pies.
items.ex_zh: 面包师舀出了熟南瓜的果肉，用来制作香气四溢的秋季馅饼。

items.def_en: [I/T] to dig a hole or tunnel into the ground, as an animal does
items.ex_en: Frightened rabbits burrow deep underground to escape aggressive predators during harsh daylight hours.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的兔子在严酷的白昼深掘地下打洞，以躲避凶猛的捕食者。

items.def_zh: 挖空成洞穴状；将……置于洞穴中
items.def_en: (literary) To hollow out like a cave; to enclose or place in a cavern.
items.ex_en: Rushing underground torrents cavern the ancient limestone hills over tens of thousands of years.
items.ex_zh: 奔腾的地下激流在数万年间将古老的石灰岩山丘淘蚀成幽深洞穴。

items.def_en: (+ sth) make a hole or passage in the earth, or excavate something buried
items.ex_en: I dug out an old photo album from the attic.
items.ex_zh: 我从阁楼里翻出了一本旧相册。

items.def_en: (+ sth) break ground and remove something from the earth by digging
items.ex_en: The media managed to dig up some scandalous details about his past.
items.ex_zh: 媒体设法翻出了他过去的一些丑闻细节。

items.def_en: to make an empty space inside something by digging or scooping material out
items.ex_en: Skilled woodworkers hollow out solid cedar logs to construct traditional handcrafted tribal canoes.
items.ex_zh: 熟练的木工挖空实心雪松原木，以打造传统的手工部落独木舟。
items.ex2_en: The ancient tree trunk hollowed out naturally over several decades of severe weathering.
items.ex2_zh: 经过几十年的严重风化，这根古老的树干自然镂空了。

items.def_en: To break up, turn over, or remove soil or earth with a tool, hands, or a machine.
items.ex_en: The enthusiastic gardener dug deep trenches into the moist soil to plant potatoes.
items.ex_zh: 热情饱满的园丁在湿润的泥土中挖出深沟，准备种植土豆。

items.def_en: [I/T] to dig long, narrow ditches or trenches into the earth
items.ex_en: Soldiers trenched the muddy defensive perimeter beneath a dark sky of falling mortar shells.
items.ex_zh: 士兵们在迫击炮弹落下的昏暗天空下，沿泥泞的防御线开挖壕沟。

items.def_en: To dig, cut, or turn over earth using a spade.
items.ex_en: He spaded the rich garden soil diligently, preparing expansive flowerbeds for spring bulbs.
items.ex_zh: 他勤奋地用铁锹翻动肥沃的花园土壤，为春季球茎准备宽阔的花坛。

items.def_en: [I/T] to dig out materials systematically or uncover archaeological remains
items.ex_en: Archaeologists excavated the ancient burial mound, uncovering bronze spearheads and intact pottery urns.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家发掘了古老土冢，出土了青铜矛头和完好的陶罐。

items.def_zh: （用利器等）挖出，凿出；敲诈，漫天要价
items.def_en: 1. To make a groove or hole in something roughly or with a sharp tool; 2. (informal) to overcharge someone unfairly.
items.ex_en: The sharp screwdriver slipped suddenly, gouging a deep splintered groove into the mahogany table.
items.ex_zh: 锋利的螺丝刀突然滑脱，在红木桌面上凿出了一道深深的裂痕。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame focus on the physical methods, tools, and actions used to break into, scoop out, or hollow subterranean or solid ground, from standard manual spade work to sharp gouging.
groups.summary_zh: 使用工具或手力对地面、固态表层进行挖土、开凿或掏空。
groups.desc_en: Displaces earth or solid material using implements, hands, or claws to create a hollow or extract buried objects, differing from generic 'cut' by creating concave depth.
groups.desc_zh: 使用工具或爪足铲开土壤以形成凹陷深坑或掘出地下埋藏物，区别于平面的'切割'在于形成了凹陷的三维空间。
groups.nuance_en: dig: breaking up and turning over earth with a tool or paws (ground / hole / garden) · burrow: tunneling underground or into soft material to create a shelter (rabbit / mole / parasite) · scoop out: clearing material from a cavity using a curved utensil or stroke (melon / earth / ice cream) · hollow out: removing the interior volume of an object to leave an empty shell (tree trunk / log / stone) · trench: excavating long, narrow, straight ditches for drainage or warfare (battlefield / pipe / cables)
groups.nuance_zh: dig: 翻土或掘坑 (ground / hole / garden) · burrow: 穿土打洞构筑地道或庇护所 (rabbit / mole / parasite) · scoop out: 用弧状铲勺掏空挖出 (melon / earth / ice cream) · hollow out: 掏空实体内部使成空壳 (tree trunk / log / stone) · trench: 开凿狭长的壕沟或沟渠 (battlefield / pipe / cables)

groups.name: Disturb & Agitate · 扰乱与心绪不宁 (Unsettle, Perturb, Fluster)
groups.tip: 打破心绪平衡、给人添堵的打扰动作

items.def_zh: 使心神不宁，使不安；扰乱
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel anxious, nervous, or uncertain. 2. To disturb the stability or established order of something.
items.ex_en: The sudden midnight phone call unsettled her calm nerves throughout the entire morning.
items.ex_zh: 半夜突如其来的电话让她一整个早上都心神不宁、忐忑不安。

items.def_en: to disturb the composure or self-possession of someone
items.ex_en: The stranger's piercing gaze seemed to discompose the proud diplomat's usual serenity.
items.ex_zh: 陌生人锐利的目光似乎打乱了那位傲慢外交官一贯的从容。

items.def_en: (+ sb) shock or upset someone emotionally and disrupt their composure
items.ex_en: The new CEO plans to shake up the entire management structure.
items.ex_zh: 新任首席执行官计划对整个管理架构进行大洗牌。

items.def_en: (+ sth) provoke strong, unsettled, or troubled emotions
items.ex_en: The sudden announcement served only to stir up bitter resentment among the staff.
items.ex_zh: 这一突如其来的通知只会在员工中激起强烈的怨恨情绪。

items.def_zh: 使极度激动，使心烦意乱
items.def_en: (+ sb) agitate someone or make them highly nervous and upset
items.ex_en: Sensational news reports will easily work up vulnerable citizens into an irrational panic.
items.ex_zh: 耸人听闻的新闻报道很容易让脆弱的市民极度惊慌失措。

items.def_en: 1. To cause someone worry, distress, or physical pain; bother someone to do something.
items.ex_en: A persistent backache continued to trouble him throughout the long winter months.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的冬季里，持续的背痛一直困扰着他。

items.def_zh: 使心烦意乱，使苦恼；扰乱，打乱；打翻
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel unhappy, worried, or angry. 2. To disturb the normal order, balance, or progress of something. 3. To knock something over accidentally.
items.ex_en: The unexpected flight delay threatened to upset our carefully planned vacation schedule completely.
items.ex_zh: 意外的航班延误可能会彻底打乱我们精心策划的假期行程。

items.def_en: 1. To disturb the normal order, function, or peaceful state of something; throw into confusion.
items.ex_en: Violent civil unrest threatened to disorder the peaceful civic administration of the province.
items.ex_zh: 暴力的内乱恐将破坏该省和平的市政管理秩序。

items.def_en: to make someone nervous, confused, or agitated by putting them in a rushed or awkward state
items.ex_en: The rapid barrage of unexpected questions began to fluster the inexperienced young spokesperson.
items.ex_zh: 一连串突如其来的尖锐提问让那位缺乏经验的年轻发言人慌了手脚。

items.def_en: to cause someone to feel anxious, agitated, or deeply unsettled
items.ex_en: The sudden drop in quarterly profits deeply perturbed the board of senior directors.
items.ex_zh: 季度利润的骤降让资深董事会成员们感到极为不安。

items.def_en: to worry or excite someone emotionally so that they cannot rest easily
items.ex_en: Rumors of imminent job cuts continued to agitate the factory workers throughout yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 即将裁员的谣言昨天一整天都让工厂的工人们坐立不安。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe external events, news, or behaviors disrupting a person's inner equilibrium, emotional composure, or mental order. While 'trouble' denotes mild persistent concern, 'unsettle' and 'perturb' shake one's confidence or peace of mind, and 'discompose' implies a loss of visible poise.
groups.summary_zh: 指外界事物打破人的内心平静、从容神态或安稳状态，使其心神不定。
groups.desc_en: Upsets the calm, stability, or emotional equilibrium of a person or system, spanning cognitive disquiet to active physical turbulence, distinct from mere 'anger'.
groups.desc_zh: 打破人身心理或系统局面的安宁秩序与平衡，引发心绪不安或局势骚乱，区别于直接的'激怒'。
groups.nuance_en: unsettle: undermining security, certainty, or peace of mind with creeping doubt (revelation / silence / news) · discompose: disturbing one's dignified composure, self-control, or serene facade (criticism / glance / presence) · stir up: deliberately provoking unrest, strife, or dormant passions (trouble / resentment / crowd) · shake up: drastically reorganizing or shocking out of complacency (management / system / industry) · fluster: making agitated, nervous, and confused by rushing or unexpected demands (witness / speaker / host)
