groups.nuance_zh: unsettle: 动摇心神安定使人忐忑不安 (revelation / silence / news) · discompose: 扰乱从容泰然的风度自持 (criticism / glance / presence) · stir up: 蓄意煽动骚乱、风波或宿怨 (trouble / resentment / crowd) · shake up: 大刀阔斧洗牌重组以打破沉滞 (management / system / industry) · fluster: 仓促或措手不及导致慌乱心急 (witness / speaker / host)

groups.name: Drive & Steer · 驾驶与操控 (Operating Vehicles)
groups.tip: 操纵载具行进

items.def_zh: 驾驶，开（车）；驱使，促使；推动
items.def_en: 1. To operate and control the direction and speed of a motor vehicle. 2. To force or compel someone or something into a particular state or action.
items.ex_en: She learned to drive a manual transmission car along steep, winding mountain roads.
items.ex_zh: 她学会了在陡峭蜿蜒的山路上驾驶手动挡汽车。

items.def_zh: （驾车）闲逛，兜风；用工具加工（或装备）
items.def_en: 1. (informal) (often followed by 'around' or 'along') To drive or travel in a vehicle, especially casually or leisurely. 2. To shape, ornament, or equip something with a tool.
items.ex_en: We spent Sunday afternoon tooling along the scenic coastal highway in an old convertible.
items.ex_zh: 周日下午，我们开着一辆旧敞篷车在风景优美的沿海公路上兜风。

items.def_zh: 驾驶（飞机或船只）；领航，引导；试行，试验
items.def_en: 1. To act as a pilot of an aircraft or ship; to navigate or guide. 2. To test a new scheme, project, or product before introducing it more widely.
items.ex_en: The captain carefully piloted the massive cargo vessel through the narrow, shallow channel.
items.ex_zh: 船长小心翼翼地驾驶着这艘庞大的货轮穿过狭窄浅窄的航道。

items.def_zh: 单独飞行；单飞，独自表演
items.def_en: To fly an aircraft alone without an instructor or co-pilot; to perform a piece of music or an act alone.
items.ex_en: After twenty hours of dual instruction, she was finally permitted to solo safely.
items.ex_zh: 在接受了二十个小时的双人指导后，她终于获准安全单飞。

items.def_en: steer a vehicle into the flow of traffic or move into another lane
items.ex_en: The multinational corporation decided to pull out of the unprofitable market.
items.ex_zh: 该跨国公司决定退出这一无利可图的市场。

items.def_en: steer a vehicle to the side of the road and stop
items.ex_en: The police officer signaled the speeding driver to pull over.
items.ex_zh: 警察打手势示意超速司机靠边停车。
items.ex2_en: The highway patrolman pulled over a reckless driver on the busy interstate.
items.ex2_zh: 高速公路巡警在繁忙的州际公路上拦停了一名鲁莽驾驶的司机。

items.def_en: maneuver a vehicle in reverse out of an enclosed space
items.ex_en: He carefully checked his mirrors before backing out of the narrow driveway slowly.
items.ex_zh: 他在慢慢倒车驶出狭窄的车道前仔细检查了后视镜。
items.ex2_en: She carefully backed the delivery van out of the congested warehouse loading dock.
items.ex2_zh: 她小心翼翼地把送货货车从拥挤的仓库装卸区倒了出来。

items.def_en: to control the direction in which a vehicle or boat moves using a wheel or rudder
items.ex_en: The helmsman fought hard against the strong currents to steer the boat shoreward.
items.ex_zh: 舵手竭力抗击强劲的水流，操舵将船驶向岸边。
items.ex2_en: The yacht steers easily even through turbulent coastal waters and heavy winds.
items.ex2_zh: 即使在汹涌的沿海水域和强风中，这艘游艇操纵起来也十分容易。

items.def_en: to direct and plan the course of a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle
items.ex_en: Early Polynesian sailors successfully navigated open oceans by observing stars and ocean swells.
items.ex_zh: 早期的波利尼西亚水手通过观察星象和海浪，成功在大洋上导航。

items.def_en: to steer or move a vehicle carefully and with skill in a tight space
items.ex_en: She managed to maneuver the large delivery truck deftly into a tiny loading bay.
items.ex_zh: 她巧妙地将那辆大型送货卡车倒入了一个极其狭小的装卸泊位。
items.ex2_en: The compact electric vehicle maneuvers smoothly through narrow downtown streets and alleys.
items.ex2_zh: 这辆紧凑型电动汽车在狭窄的市中心街道和小巷中操纵平稳自如。

items.def_en: to drive someone around as a passenger in a motor car
items.ex_en: He spent the entire weekend chauffeuring his demanding in-laws around the historic city.
items.ex_zh: 他整个周末都开车带着要求苛刻的岳父母在这座历史名城四处游览。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scenario cover the physical operation, navigation, and maneuvering of wheeled conveyances, aircraft, or marine vessels, ranging from everyday driving to technical piloting.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及机动车、飞机或船只的操控、驾驶与领航等场景动作。
groups.desc_en: Operates and directs the course, speed, and maneuvers of a land, sea, or air vehicle, differing from passive 'ride' by requiring deliberate mechanical navigation.
groups.desc_zh: 操控机动运载工具的速度、路线与特定规避停靠动作，区别于被动的'乘车'在于必须施加自主机械操控。
groups.nuance_en: drive: operating and controlling the locomotion of a motor vehicle (car / truck / vehicle) · steer: guiding the directional heading of a vehicle or vessel (wheel / ship / course) · pilot: navigating a craft through complex airspace or narrow waterways (aircraft / vessel / drone) · pull over: maneuvering a vehicle to the side of the road and stopping (curb / shoulder / vehicle) · back out: reversing a vehicle out of an enclosed space or parking spot (driveway / garage / space)
groups.nuance_zh: drive: 操纵汽车等机动车行驶 (car / truck / vehicle) · steer: 控制方向盘掌握航向走向 (wheel / ship / course) · pilot: 驾驶飞行器或引领船舶穿行水道 (aircraft / vessel / drone) · pull over: 将车辆驶至路边停靠 (curb / shoulder / vehicle) · back out: 将车辆从狭窄空间倒出 (driveway / garage / space)

groups.name: Dry & Dehydrate · 干燥与脱水 (Desiccate, Scorch, Wither)
groups.tip: 蒸发或吸除水分至干燥状态

items.def_en: To become dry, or to make something dry by removing moisture or liquid.
items.ex_en: Hang the wet wool coats outside so they dry quickly in the breeze.
items.ex_zh: 把湿羊毛大衣挂在外面，好让它们在微风中快点晾干。
items.ex2_en: The warm morning breeze quickly dried the freshly washed linen on the line.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖的晨风很快吹干了晾在绳上的新洗亚麻布。

items.def_en: become completely dry or cause something to lose all moisture
items.ex_en: The continuous dry heat will soon dry out the newly poured concrete foundation.
items.ex_zh: 持续的干热天气很快就会让新浇筑的混凝土基底完全干透。
items.ex2_en: The soggy football field dried out quickly under the intense afternoon sun.
items.ex2_zh: 湿漉漉的足球场在午后强烈的阳光下很快变干了。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ away/up) to become dry and limp from lack of water (especially of plants)
items.ex_en: Without regular rainfall, the delicate potted flowers began to wither and droop mournfully.
items.ex_zh: 由于缺乏定期降水，娇嫩的盆栽花卉开始枯萎凋零。
items.ex2_en: The intense summer heat withered the green leaves across the vast valley.
items.ex2_zh: 炎热的夏日酷暑枯萎了整个辽阔山谷中的绿叶。

items.def_en: To lose a large amount of water from the body, or to remove all water from food or other substances.
items.ex_en: Athletes can quickly dehydrate if they train vigorously under the scorching midday sun.
items.ex_zh: 运动员在烈日下进行高强度训练可能会迅速脱水。
items.ex2_en: Specialized commercial machines dehydrate fresh sliced apples for long shelf life storage.
items.ex2_zh: 专用商业机器将新鲜苹果片脱水，以便长期保存。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ up) to shrink, wrinkle, and become dry through intense heat, cold, or age
items.ex_en: Left forgotten in the sun, the juicy plums began to shrivel and darken.
items.ex_zh: 多汁的李子被遗忘在阳光下，开始枯萎起皱并变黑。
items.ex2_en: The fierce autumn frost shriveled the tender petals of the backyard roses.
items.ex2_zh: 凛冽的秋霜让后院玫瑰娇嫩的花瓣萎缩了。

items.def_en: To remove moisture or humidity from indoor air; dehumidify.
items.ex_en: The modern climate system works constantly to dehumidifier the damp museum storage rooms.
items.ex_zh: 先进的环境调控系统持续运转，为潮湿的博物馆储藏室除湿。

items.def_en: lose all water or moisture completely, especially through evaporation
items.ex_en: During prolonged summer droughts, local streams frequently dry up into dusty gravel beds.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的夏旱期间，当地溪流往往会彻底干涸，沦为布满碎石的河床。
items.ex2_en: Weeks of blazing sunshine dried up the muddy irrigation ditches completely.
items.ex2_zh: 数周强烈的日晒彻底晒干了泥泞的灌溉水渠。

items.def_en: become dry, wrinkled, and smaller from acute loss of moisture
items.ex_en: The green leaves shrivel up rapidly under the scorching heat of the wildfire.
items.ex_zh: 在野火的高温炙烤下，绿叶迅速枯萎皱缩。
items.ex2_en: Intense thermal radiation shriveled up the delicate seedlings inside the greenhouse.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的热辐射使温室里娇嫩的幼苗干瘪枯萎了。

items.def_en: to dry out or burn the surface of something with intense, sudden heat
items.ex_en: The chef quickly seared the tuna steak on both sides in high heat.
items.ex_zh: 厨师用高温迅速将金枪鱼排的两面略微煎烤灼干。

items.def_zh: 使干透，使极度干渴；烤干
items.def_en: To make something extremely dry, hot, or thirsty, especially through heat or exposure to the sun.
items.ex_en: Blistering desert winds threatened to parch the land and exhaust the weary travelers.
items.ex_zh: 灼热的沙漠干风恐将烤干大地，使疲惫的旅人极度干渴。

items.def_en: [I/T] to remove the moisture completely from something, typically for preservation
items.ex_en: Industrial food processors often desiccate sliced fruits before packing them for long journeys.
items.ex_zh: 工业食品加工厂通常会在包装水果片进行长途运输前将其彻底脱水。
items.ex2_en: Fallen autumn leaves desiccated rapidly under the dry desert winds.
items.ex2_zh: 飘落的秋叶在干燥的沙漠风中迅速变干枯竭。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the removal or loss of moisture from an entity, varying in mechanism from natural evaporation and ambient heating to extreme botanical or biological desiccation.
groups.summary_zh: 指脱除物体或机体水分的过程，涉及日晒风干、抽湿及极度枯竭。
groups.desc_en: Removes or loses moisture from an organic or inorganic entity, resulting in dryness, shrinkage, or withered vitality, differing from 'drain' by involving evaporation or desiccation.
groups.desc_zh: 通过蒸发或脱水剥离有机或无机物的水分，导致干燥、萎缩或生机干涸，区别于液态流淌的'排干'。
groups.nuance_en: dry out: losing all moisture gradually until brittle or cured (wood / soil / mouth) · wither: losing sap and moisture, resulting in limpness, shriveling, or dying away (leaves / plant / hopes) · dehydrate: removing bound water artificially or suffering systemic loss of bodily hydration (fruit / body / runner) · shrivel: shrinking and wrinkling drastically through intense loss of moisture (raisin / skin / prune) · desiccate: draining moisture completely to a state of absolute, preservative dryness (specimen / soil / corpse)
groups.nuance_zh: dry out: 水分流失渐尽变得干脆 (wood / soil / mouth) · wither: 枯萎下垂并丧失生命力 (leaves / plant / hopes) · dehydrate: 机器烘干脱水或机体严重缺水 (fruit / body / runner) · shrivel: 因极度失水而起皱干瘪萎缩 (raisin / skin / prune) · desiccate: 极度抽干水分制成干粉或标本 (specimen / soil / corpse)

groups.name: Dwell & Reside · 居住与定居 (Reside, Inhabit, Lodge)
groups.tip: 安家落户或长期居住生活

items.def_en: (+ in/down) to establish a permanent residence in a new community or area
items.ex_en: After years of traveling abroad, they finally decided to settle in a quiet village.
items.ex_zh: 在国外漂泊多年后，他们最终决定在一个安静的村庄定居下来。

items.def_en: reside at the place where one works or studies
items.ex_en: They are looking for a reliable live-in nanny for their twins.
items.ex_zh: 他们正在为双胞胎物色一位可靠的住家保姆。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) live together as sexual partners without being married
items.ex_en: They decided to shack up together in a downtown loft to save rent.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定在市中心的一处阁楼里同居，以节省房租。

items.def_en: stay or hide in a safe, secluded dwelling for a period
items.ex_en: The wanted fugitives managed to hole up inside a deserted cabin for weeks.
items.ex_zh: 那些被通缉的逃犯在荒废的小木屋里藏匿隐居了数周。

items.def_en: (+ in/at) to live permanently or habitually in a specific place (formal)
items.ex_en: The elderly foreign ambassador will reside in the capital until his official retirement.
items.ex_zh: 这位年迈的外国大使将一直在首都居住，直至正式退休。

items.def_zh: 居住，栖息；老是想着，唠叨（与 on/upon 连用）
items.def_en: 1. (+ in/at) (formal or literary) To live or reside in a particular place. 2. ('dwell on/upon') To think, speak, or write at length about something, especially something unpleasant.
items.ex_en: Ancient nomadic tribes used to dwell peacefully along the fertile banks of this river.
items.ex_zh: 古代游牧部落曾经平静地栖居在这条河流两岸肥沃的土地上。

items.def_en: (+ in/at) to stay or dwell in a place (archaic or literary)
items.ex_en: The hermit was content to abide in his mountain sanctuary away from mankind.
items.ex_zh: 那位隐士心满意足地居住在远离尘嚣的深山庇护所中。

items.def_en: to live in or occupy a specific territory, environment, or house
items.ex_en: Diverse species of colorful birds inhabit the dense canopy of this tropical rainforest.
items.ex_zh: 多种多样的色彩斑斓的鸟类栖居在这片热带雨林茂密的树冠层中。

items.def_zh: 开拓定居，建立家园（在政府分配的土地上）
items.def_en: (historical) To settle on and cultivate public land granted by the government.
items.ex_en: Pioneering settlers worked tirelessly to homestead vast tracts of untamed western prairie land.
items.ex_zh: 拓荒者们不知疲倦地在广袤无垠的西部大草原上开拓土地、安家立业。

items.def_zh: 寄居，暂住；（常与up连用）同居
items.def_en: (informal, usually 'shack up') To live or stay in a place; to live together as romantic partners without being married.
items.ex_en: He had to shack in an inexpensive motel while looking for a permanent apartment.
items.ex_zh: 他在寻找长期公寓期间，不得不暂时寄居在一间廉价汽车旅馆里。

items.def_zh: 居住，栖身（dwell的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of dwell; lived or resided in a specified place.
items.ex_en: The reclusive poet dwelt in a remote seaside cottage for over forty quiet years.
items.ex_zh: 这位避世的诗人曾在一座偏远的海滨小屋里平静地居住了四十多年。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the state or ongoing act of living continuously in a particular home, territory, or condition, ranging from informal living setups to legal and formal residency.
groups.summary_zh: 指在某处持续生活、落户或安居的状态，涵盖非正式寄宿到法定定居。
groups.desc_en: Denotes establishing physical or legal presence in a habitat, ranging from permanent legal domicile to temporary illicit sheltering, contrasting with transient visiting or mere physical presence.
groups.desc_zh: 表示在特定空间建立物理或法律上的居留状态，涵盖法定定居至临时匿居，区别于短暂停留或单纯身处某地。
groups.nuance_en: reside: formal or legal permanent occupancy (city / jurisdiction / address) · dwell: literary or contemplative sustained habitation (forest / realms / past) · inhabit: ecological or demographic populating of a space (island / ruins / continent) · settle: establishing a lasting homestead or community (frontier / valley / region) · hole up: taking defensive or illicit shelter (hideout / cabin / hotel)
groups.nuance_zh: reside: 正式或法律意义上的定居 (city / jurisdiction / address) · dwell: 文学或沉思性的栖居与盘桓 (forest / realms / past) · inhabit: 生态或人口学意义上的栖息与居住 (island / ruins / continent) · settle: 开拓性的安家与落户 (frontier / valley / region) · hole up: 隐匿性或防御性的潜伏躲藏 (hideout / cabin / hotel)

groups.name: Eat & Partake · 进食与进餐 (Eat, Dine, Feast)
groups.tip: 日常餐饮与聚餐场景

items.def_en: To eat an early morning meal.
items.ex_en: The visiting delegates will breakfast in the private salon before the summit begins.
items.ex_zh: 来访的代表们将在峰会开始前在私人宴会厅享用早餐。

items.def_zh: 在餐馆就餐，在外面吃饭
items.def_en: have a meal in a restaurant rather than at home
items.ex_en: With their busy work schedules, they tend to eat out several times a week.
items.ex_zh: 由于工作繁忙，他们每周往往会在外就餐好几次。

items.def_en: eat an evening meal away from home, especially at a restaurant
items.ex_en: We usually dine out on Friday evenings to celebrate the end of the workweek.
items.ex_zh: 我们通常在周五晚上去餐馆吃饭，庆祝一周工作的结束。

items.def_zh: 津津有味地大吃，开怀畅饮
items.def_en: (+ sth) start eating food enthusiastically and in large quantities
items.ex_en: The hungry children eagerly tucked into their hot bowls of creamy potato soup.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的孩子们热火朝天地大口喝起热气腾腾的土豆浓汤。

items.def_zh: 尽情享用（美食），大吃大喝；参加宴会；款待
items.def_en: To eat a large amount of food with great pleasure; (feast on) to consume or view something with deep enjoyment.
items.ex_en: The victorious warriors would feast on roasted venison late into the stormy night.
items.ex_zh: 凯旋的勇士们尽情享用烤鹿肉大餐，一直狂欢到风雨交加的深夜。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽地吃；贪婪地捕食；掠夺
items.def_en: To eat voraciously or hungrily; to hunt greedily for prey or plunder.
items.ex_en: Starving beasts raven across the frozen tundra in desperate search of small rodents.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的野兽在冰冻的苔原上贪婪觅食，绝望地搜寻着小型啮齿动物。

items.def_en: To have or take part in a picnic.
items.ex_en: We love to picnic by the tranquil lake whenever the spring weather warms.
items.ex_zh: 每当春日回暖，我们便喜欢去宁静的湖畔野餐。

items.def_en: to attend or partake in an elaborate, formal celebratory meal with many guests
items.ex_en: The royal guests will banquet in the grand hall beneath magnificent crystal chandeliers.
items.ex_zh: 王室宾客们将在璀璨的水晶吊灯下齐聚大厅参加盛大宴会。

items.def_en: to eat an evening meal, typically in a relaxed or traditional context
items.ex_en: They sat quietly together to sup on simple crusty bread and hearty stew.
items.ex_zh: 他们静静地坐在一起，用简单的脆皮面包和丰盛的炖菜进晚餐。

items.def_en: [I/T] to eat large quantities of food greedily and to excess, stuffing oneself
items.ex_en: The excited guests continued to gorge themselves on delicious seafood throughout the festival.
items.ex_zh: 兴高采烈的客人们在整个节日期间狼吞虎咽，大口享用美味的海鲜。

items.def_en: To eat dinner or have a formal meal.
items.ex_en: The distinguished couple intends to dine at an exclusive rooftop restaurant this evening.
items.ex_zh: 那对尊贵的夫妇今晚打算在一处高档屋顶餐厅用正餐。

groups.summary_en: People consume food under distinct social, temporal, or behavioral circumstances, ranging from everyday domestic meals (breakfast, picnic) to formal evening repasts, communal banqueting, or voracious animal feeding.
groups.summary_zh: 在不同社交场景、时间或食欲驱动下进餐消费食物。
groups.desc_en: Specifies culturally or physically contextualized eating rituals, contrasting with generic metabolic consumption by foregrounding venue, sociality, or consumption posture.
groups.desc_zh: 强调具特定社交、空间或进食姿态的就餐场景，区别于中性的生理进食，突出就餐仪式与情境。
groups.nuance_en: dine out: eating commercially prepared meals outside the home (restaurant / bistro) · tuck into: hearty, eager physical indulgence in food (meal / hearty breakfast / steak) · feast: celebratory, abundant ceremonial gorging (delicacies / roasted meats / banquet) · picnic: open-air leisure dining (park / meadow / beach) · raven: rapacious, predatory devouring driven by extreme hunger (prey / leftovers)
groups.nuance_zh: dine out: 在外商业化就餐 (restaurant / bistro) · tuck into: 痛快大嚼、大快朵颐 (meal / hearty breakfast / steak) · feast: 节庆式的丰盛宴饮 (delicacies / roasted meats / banquet) · picnic: 户外休闲野餐 (park / meadow / beach) · raven: 饥不择食的贪婪吞食 (prey / leftovers)

groups.name: Emphasize & Highlight · 强调与突出 (Underscore, Foreground, Stress)
groups.tip: 用斜体、聚光灯等手法加重语气

items.def_en: (+ sth) draw attention to a fact or detail so it is noticed
items.ex_en: The auditor took care to point out several glaring discrepancies in the ledgers.
items.ex_zh: 审计员特意指出了账目中几处极为显眼的差异。

items.def_zh: 凸显，衬托出（特征或品质）
items.def_en: (+ sth) make a particular quality or feature clearly noticeable
items.ex_en: The dark velvet background helped bring out the brilliant sparkle of the diamond.
items.ex_zh: 深色丝绒背景完美衬托出了那颗钻石的璀璨光芒。

items.def_en: (+ sth) enhance or emphasize the appearance of something by contrast
items.ex_en: A crisp white collar can nicely set off the deep blue wool blazer.
items.ex_zh: 挺括的白领能极好地衬托出深蓝色羊毛西装的质感。

items.def_en: to give special importance or verbal emphasis to a point or syllable
items.ex_en: The keynote speaker took extra time to stress the importance of personal integrity.
items.ex_zh: 主讲人特意多花了时间来强调个人诚信的重要性。

items.def_zh: 突出，强调；用醒目颜色标出
items.def_en: 1. To emphasize something or draw special attention to it. 2. To mark text with a bright colour to make it prominent.
items.ex_en: Recent corporate scandals highlight the urgent necessity for stricter environmental regulations and oversight.
items.ex_zh: 最近的企业丑闻凸显了实行更严格的环境法规和监管的紧迫性。

items.def_en: to draw a line under text, or symbolically emphasize a key factor
items.ex_en: These alarming statistics clearly underline the severe economic disparity in rural communities.
items.ex_zh: 这些令人担忧的统计数据清楚地突显了农村社区严重的经济差距。

items.def_en: to emphasize the importance or truth of something, as if drawing a line beneath it
items.ex_en: The ongoing trade conflict serves to underscore the vulnerability of global supply chains.
items.ex_zh: 持续的贸易冲突进一步凸显了全球供应链的脆弱性。

items.def_zh: 用斜体书写（或印刷）（以示强调等）
items.def_en: To print or format words in italic type, typically to emphasize them or indicate a title.
items.ex_en: Please italicize all foreign words and book titles within your final research paper.
items.ex_zh: 请在你的最终研究论文中将所有外来词汇和书籍名称用斜体书写。

items.def_zh: 突出，使受到瞩目；用聚光灯照亮
items.def_en: 1. To direct widespread public attention to a particular person, issue, or event. 2. To illuminate someone or something with a spotlight.
items.ex_en: The investigative documentary will spotlight systemic corruption within the municipal government system.
items.ex_zh: 这部调查纪录片将把公众焦点引向市政府内部的体制性腐败。

items.def_en: to make something the most prominent or important feature in an analysis or depiction
items.ex_en: The newly published history text seeks to foreground the voices of marginalized workers.
items.ex_zh: 这本新出版的史学著作力图将边缘化劳工的声音置于最突出的地位。

items.def_en: To emphasize something or make a feature, detail, or contrast much more noticeable.
items.ex_en: The tailored cut of the formal suit served to accentuate his broad shoulders.
items.ex_zh: 这套正装合身的剪裁进一步突显了他宽阔的肩膀。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe communicative or visual techniques used to draw special attention to an element, contrasting rhetorical stress with typographic or compositional foregrounding.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过修辞强调、版式字体或视觉构图来格外突出某项要点。
groups.desc_en: Employs optical, graphic, or positioning devices to make an element visually or intellectually prominent against a background, contrasting with substantive addition of evidence.
groups.desc_zh: 通过视觉、版式或空间衬托手段使对象在背景中格外凸显，区别于提供论据的实质性论证。
groups.nuance_en: highlight: drawing focal attention using visual or thematic contrast (discrepancy / risk / achievement) · underline: adding graphic or rhetorical gravity to mark significance (importance / urgency / need) · underscore: authoritative, emphatic verification of an underlying truth (point / vulnerability / irony) · set off: enhancing prominence through aesthetic contrast (features / brilliance / colors) · bring out: drawing forth an obscured latent quality (flavor / meaning / best)
groups.nuance_zh: highlight: 运用视觉或主题反差凸显焦点 (discrepancy / risk / achievement) · underline: 如下划线般强调迫切重要性 (importance / urgency / need) · underscore: 权威性地印证并强化某一事实 (point / vulnerability / irony) · set off: 依靠审美或反差映衬衬托 (features / brilliance / colors) · bring out: 诱发并显现潜藏特质 (flavor / meaning / best)

groups.name: Emphasize & Underscore · 强调与着重 (Emphasize, Stress, Underscore)
groups.tip: 着重凸显核心要点

items.def_en: (+ that) to give special importance or verbal emphasis to a point or fact
items.ex_en: The seasoned manager made sure to stress that strict punctuality remained entirely mandatory.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的经理特意着重强调，严格遵守时间仍然是完全强制性的。

items.def_en: to draw special attention to an essential fact, detail, or situation
items.ex_en: The newly released report serves to highlight serious deficiencies in local emergency preparedness.
items.ex_zh: 新发布的报告突出了地方应急防灾准备中存在的严重不足。

items.def_en: 1. To emphasize or make something more noticeable. 2. To pronounce a syllable, word, or note with special stress.
items.ex_en: Strategic golden trim was used to accent the rich architectural details inside.
items.ex_zh: 巧妙点缀的金色饰边被用来突出室内丰富的建筑细节。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to highlight or accentuate an important fact or condition to make it clearly noticeable
items.ex_en: The crisis pointed up the urgent need for structural reform.
items.ex_zh: 这场危机凸显了进行结构性改革的紧迫性。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a particular quality, feature, or detail more prominent and easily noticed
items.ex_en: The clever contrast of lighting helps bring out the subtle textures of painting.
items.ex_zh: 巧妙的光影对比有助于突出这幅画作微妙的质感细节。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to emphasize or exaggerate the importance or value of something deliberately
items.ex_en: Political advisors always try to play up minor successes during tight election campaigns.
items.ex_zh: 在选情胶着的竞选中，政治顾问们总是极力大肆渲染微小的胜利。

items.def_en: To give special importance or prominence to something in speaking or writing.
items.ex_en: The medical instructor consistently emphasized the critical role of rigorous hand hygiene protocols.
items.ex_zh: 医学讲师一贯强调严格执行手部卫生规程的关键作用。

items.def_en: to underline or clearly emphasize the importance of something
items.ex_en: The recent financial report underscores the urgent need for structural economic reforms.
items.ex_zh: 最近的财务报告突显了进行结构性经济改革的紧迫性。

items.def_zh: 强调，突出，使置于突出地位
items.def_en: To give prominence or special emphasis to a particular feature or issue.
items.ex_en: Her new exhibition foregrounds the harsh social realities faced by working-class families.
items.ex_zh: 她的新展览突出了工薪阶层家庭所面临的残酷社会现实。

items.def_zh: 喋喋不休地阐述，过分强调；痛打，抨击
items.def_en: 1. To explain or insist on something to an excessive and tedious degree. 2. To attack physically or verbally.
items.ex_en: There is no need to belabor the point since everyone already understands.
items.ex_zh: 既然大家都已经明白了，就没必要再喋喋不休地强调这一点了。

items.def_en: To give too much importance or attention to something.
items.ex_en: We should not overemphasize short-term profits at the expense of long-term sustainable growth.
items.ex_zh: 我们不应以牺牲长期可持续增长为代价而过分强调短期利润。

groups.summary_en: A communicator highlights a key fact, idea, or detail to draw distinct focus, attach greater importance, or make something unmistakable. Verbs range from typographical and phonetic accents to vehement reiteration or excessive laboring.
groups.summary_zh: 通过言辞、重音或论证突出某一要点，以引起高度注意或明确其权重。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on rhetorical weight, force, and strategic prioritization in discourse, contrasting with merely mentioning or neutrally presenting information.
groups.desc_zh: 强调话语体系中的修辞分量、施压度与主次排序，区别于客观陈述或轻描淡写地提及。
groups.nuance_en: emphasize: conscious allocation of rhetorical weight and importance (necessity / point / value) · stress: urgent insistence driven by pressure or gravity (danger / need / urgency) · accent: stylistically inflecting or tinting a specific element (difference / rhythm / positive) · play up: strategically amplifying a feature for persuasive gain (success / rivalry / benefits) · point up: sharply exposing structural flaws or contrasts (inequalities / contradictions / limitations)
groups.nuance_zh: emphasize: 有意识地赋予修辞分量与权重 (necessity / point / value) · stress: 基于紧迫感或压力施加着重力道 (danger / need / urgency) · accent: 在风格或节奏上有意赋予重音与色彩 (difference / rhythm / positive) · play up: 出于策略考量刻意大肆渲染 (success / rivalry / benefits) · point up: 尖锐指明并暴露出结构性反差或缺陷 (inequalities / contradictions / limitations)

groups.name: Enchant & Cast a Spell · 蛊惑与迷醉 (Beguile, Bewitch, Enthrall)
groups.tip: 散发魅力令人神魂颠倒

items.def_zh: 令（某人）神魂颠倒；使完全陶醉
items.def_en: (+ sb) to overwhelm someone with intense emotion, wonder, or fascination
items.ex_en: The floodwaters swept away cars and makeshift bridges within minutes.
items.ex_zh: 洪水在几分钟内冲走了汽车和简易桥梁。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to overwhelm or captivate someone completely with beauty, charm, or astonishment
items.ex_en: Her breathtaking smile and effortless charm completely bowled him over last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚她迷人的微笑与由内而外的魅力彻底让他倾倒迷醉。

items.def_zh: 使冲昏头脑；使沉醉入迷
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone to lose self-control through overwhelming excitement or fascination
items.ex_en: He was easily carried away by the euphoric cheers of the stadium.
items.ex_zh: 体育场内狂热的欢呼声轻易便让他沉醉入迷，不能自已。

items.def_en: fill someone with great delight or hold them as if under a spell
items.ex_en: The melodic whisper of the ancient forest enchanted the weary wandering poet.
items.ex_zh: 古老森林中悠扬的低吟让身心俱疲的流浪诗人为之陶醉。

items.def_en: attract and hold the interest and affection of someone completely
items.ex_en: The speaker captivated the audience with her poignant stories of personal resilience.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者用她坚韧不拔的动人故事彻底吸引了全场观众。

items.def_en: hold the complete attention of someone almost to the point of hypnosis
items.ex_en: The rhythmic movements of the dancers mesmerized everyone in the crowded theater.
items.ex_zh: 舞者极富节奏感的动作让拥挤剧场里的所有人都看得如痴如醉。

items.def_en: capture the fascinated attention of someone, rendering them transfixed
items.ex_en: The flickering flames hypnotized the exhausted hikers into a peaceful, unbroken silence.
items.ex_zh: 摇曳的火焰让筋疲力尽的徒步者们完全看呆了，陷入一片安详的沉寂。

items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British English spelling of enthrall) To capture the fascinated attention and imagination of someone completely. 2. (archaic) To enslave.
items.ex_en: Her wondrous tales of forgotten realms enthralled the wide-eyed children around her.
items.ex_zh: 她口中关于失落国度的奇妙故事深深吸引了周围睁大双眼的孩子们。

items.def_en: 1. To attract, delight, and captivate someone so intensely that they lose judgment. 2. To put a magic spell on someone.
items.ex_en: The mysterious traveler bewitched the entire royal court with strange exotic melodies.
items.ex_zh: 神秘的旅人用奇异的异域曲调蛊惑了整个宫廷的心神。

items.def_zh: 使迷恋，使神魂颠倒；使糊涂
items.def_en: (usually passive) To inspire someone with an extravagant, foolish, or short-lived passion or admiration.
items.ex_en: He was so thoroughly infatuated with her that he ignored all rational advice.
items.ex_zh: 他彻底为她神魂颠倒，以至于不顾所有理性的劝告。

items.def_en: 1. To charm, enchant, or fascinate someone, sometimes in an enticing way. 2. (+ into) To trick or deceive someone into doing something.
items.ex_en: The charismatic stranger beguiled the lonely heiress with grand promises of romance.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有魅力的陌生人用宏大的浪漫许诺迷住了孤独的女继承人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve exerting an almost magical, deceptive, or intoxicating power of attraction over someone, completely captivating their senses, lowering their defenses, or clouding their judgment through charm or allure.
groups.summary_zh: 借助迷人魅力、魔力或欺骗性手段使人神魂颠倒、丧失防备。
groups.desc_en: Metaphorizes captivating sensory or emotional attraction as magical subjugation or hypnotic sensory paralysis, contrasting with ordinary persuasion or mild liking.
groups.desc_zh: 将强烈的感官或情感吸引隐喻为施法蛊惑与催眠般的意志剥夺，区别于理性的说服或温和的喜爱。
groups.nuance_en: enchant: casting a delightful, fairy-tale magical thrall (audience / visitor / heart) · captivate: seizing irresistible, sustained emotional or intellectual hold (crowd / imagination / reader) · mesmerize: transfixing into a motionless, trance-like fascination (onlookers / spectator / gaze) · enthral: holding completely spellbound as if spiritually bonded (theatergoers / listener / mind) · hypnotize: inducing an altered, helpless state of suspended critical faculty (prey / subject / crowd)
groups.nuance_zh: enchant: 施展梦幻迷人般的魔法吸引 (audience / visitor / heart) · captivate: 捕获不可抗拒的情感与注意投入 (crowd / imagination / reader) · mesmerize: 令人如入催眠般目不转睛、呆滞神往 (onlookers / spectator / gaze) · enthral: 彻底俘获并牢牢扣住全副心神 (theatergoers / listener / mind) · hypnotize: 剥夺自主判断力般令其恍惚顺从 (prey / subject / crowd)

groups.name: Enclose & Shield · 围蔽与掩蔽 (Curtain, Rim, Capsule)
groups.tip: 拉帘遮掩以阻隔视线

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround an area or object with a fence or barrier to confine or enclose it
items.ex_en: The ranchers decided to fence in the northern pasture before winter arrived.
items.ex_zh: 牧场主们决定在冬天到来之前用栅栏将北部牧场围起来。

items.def_zh: 用屏风或帷幕隔开/遮蔽
items.def_en: (+ sth) to divide or hide an area or object using a screen, partition, or curtain
items.ex_en: Hospital staff used mobile partitions to screen off the emergency treatment area.
items.ex_zh: 医院工作人员用移动隔板将急诊处置区域隔开遮挡。

items.def_zh: 用帘子遮蔽，给……装帘子（常与off连用隔开）
items.def_en: 1. (+ off) To cover a window or divide an area using a curtain or hanging cloth.
items.ex_en: Heavy velvet drapes curtained the high windows against the bitter winter chill.
items.ex_zh: 厚重的丝绒帘子遮蔽了高窗，阻挡了刺骨的冬日寒意。

items.def_en: 1. To form or serve as an outer edge or border around something.
items.ex_en: A ring of towering pine trees rimmed the serene mountain lake completely.
items.ex_zh: 一圈高耸的松树严密地环绕着这座宁静高山湖泊的边缘。

items.def_zh: 装入胶囊，封装；简要概括
items.def_en: 1. To enclose something in a capsule; to summarize or condense.
items.ex_en: The concise report aims to capsule the primary findings of the survey.
items.ex_zh: 这份简明报告旨在概括该项调查的主要研究结果。

items.def_en: to surround something in a circle
items.ex_en: Ancient stone walls and deep defensive moats encircle the historic imperial capital.
items.ex_zh: 古老的石墙与幽深的防御护城河环绕包围着这座历史悠久的皇城。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to close off an area by placing a barrier of ropes, tapes, or police lines around it
items.ex_en: Police officers quickly cordoned off the entire street to secure the evidence.
items.ex_zh: 警察迅速拉起警戒线将整条街道封锁隔离，以保护现场证据。

items.def_en: to surround someone or something closely so that movement is restricted
items.ex_en: Hostile cavalry units managed to hem in the retreating soldiers on all sides.
items.ex_zh: 敌方的骑兵部队从四面围住了撤退的士兵，限制其行动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to enclose, separate, or isolate an area by building a wall around or across it
items.ex_en: Part of the courtyard was walled off to create a private garden.
items.ex_zh: 院子的一部分被砌墙隔开，改造成了一个私人花园。

items.def_zh: 用屏风或障壁遮挡避光或遮丑
items.def_en: (+ from/off) to shelter, protect, or conceal someone or something with a partition or barrier
items.ex_en: Dense bamboo bushes screen the private swimming pool from curious neighboring eyes.
items.ex_zh: 茂密的竹丛遮挡住私人泳池，避免了邻居好奇的目光。

items.def_zh: 用覆盖物完全遮掩或笼罩
items.def_en: to cover or hide something completely, preventing it from being seen
items.ex_en: A thick blanket of early morning mist shrouded the sleeping hillside village.
items.ex_zh: 一层厚厚的晨雾完全笼罩了沉睡中的山坡村庄。

groups.summary_en: An agent or barrier places a border, wall, or hanging covering around an object to seal, hide, or frame it. Verbs in this frame evoke specific structural shapes such as hanging folds, raised perimeters, or protective hulls.
groups.summary_zh: 以帷幔、边框或密闭外壳将目标环绕遮蔽或框定。
groups.desc_en: Envelops, walls off, or creates physical or fabric barriers to isolate, protect, or confine a space, contrasting with open, unobstructed boundary demarcation.
groups.desc_zh: 借助实体屏障、织物或围构体进行物理包围与掩蔽隔绝，区别于单纯划定无阻碍的抽象边界。
groups.nuance_en: cordon off: setting up security perimeters to restrict access (area / street / crime scene) · screen off: shielding from sight or draft using a movable divider (bed / alcove / view) · curtain: veiling or draping with hanging fabrics to conceal (window / bed / stage) · hem in: constricting and restricting freedom of movement closely (crowd / troops / traveler) · encircle: forming a complete ring around an entity (city / compound / prey)
groups.nuance_zh: cordon off: 设置警戒线实施安全封锁与阻隔 (area / street / crime scene) · screen off: 用屏风或遮挡物隔断视线或气流 (bed / alcove / view) · curtain: 悬垂帷幔以遮蔽掩映 (window / bed / stage) · hem in: 密不透风地围堵以剥夺活动空间 (crowd / troops / traveler) · encircle: 形成闭合环形包围圈 (city / compound / prey)

groups.name: End & Terminate · 结束与终止 (Cease, Terminate, Abort)
groups.tip: 由自然结束到主动终止

items.def_en: [I/T] To halt an action, motion, or operation either temporarily or permanently
items.ex_en: The train conductor had to stop the locomotive when warning signals flashed red.
items.ex_zh: 当警报信号闪烁红光时，火车司机不得不紧急刹车停下车头。
items.ex2_en: The fast passenger train stopped abruptly outside the signal box.
items.ex2_zh: 那列快速客车在信号楼外突然停了下来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to bring an activity, business, or speech to a planned or final close
items.ex_en: Let us quickly wind up today's meeting so everyone can go home.
items.ex_zh: 我们赶快把今天的会议结束掉，好让大家早点回家。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to complete or conclude an event, meeting, or process successfully
items.ex_en: Let's wrap up this meeting so everyone can catch their flights.
items.ex_zh: 我们结束这次会议吧，这样大家都能赶上航班。

items.def_en: To finish or stop, or to bring something to a finish or stop.
items.ex_en: The negotiations finally ended when both sides signed the formal peace agreement.
items.ex_zh: 双方签署了正式和平协议后，谈判终于宣告结束。
items.ex2_en: The referee ended the intense championship soccer match after extra time expired.
items.ex2_zh: 加时赛结束后，裁判结束了这场激烈的冠军足球赛。

items.def_en: [I/T] To bring an event, transaction, or speech to a formal or structured close
items.ex_en: The ambassador concluded his keynote speech with a call for international cooperation.
items.ex_zh: 大使以呼吁国际合作为这篇主题演讲画上了圆满句号。

items.def_en: To stop happening or existing, or to stop doing something.
items.ex_en: Fighting along the contested border must cease immediately to prevent further bloodshed.
items.ex_zh: 争议边界上的交火必须立即停止，以防止进一步的流血事件。
items.ex2_en: The factory manager ceased production of obsolete models due to low market demand.
items.ex2_zh: 由于市场需求低迷，工厂经理停止了过时型号的生产。

items.def_en: [I/T] To bring or come to an abrupt or decisive standstill
items.ex_en: The sudden outbreak of unrest threatened to halt the peace negotiations entirely.
items.ex_zh: 突发的动乱有可能使和平谈判彻底陷入停顿。
items.ex2_en: The long convoy halted beside the riverbank for a brief rest.
items.ex2_zh: 长长的车队在河岸边停下来稍作休整。

items.def_en: To cancel an event or operation before or while it is underway
items.ex_en: Officials were forced to call off the outdoor festival due to torrential rain.
items.ex_zh: 由于暴雨倾盆，官员们被迫取消了那场户外节日庆典。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to bring an abrupt or premature halt to a supply, process, or continuity
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: 1. To come to an end, or to bring something to an end. 2. (formal) To end someone's employment.
items.ex_en: The company decided to terminate his employment contract following repeated misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 在屡次违纪之后，公司决定正式解除与他的雇佣合同。
items.ex2_en: His lucrative employment contract terminates automatically at the end of the year.
items.ex2_zh: 他那份收益丰厚的雇佣合同将在年底自动终止。

items.def_zh: 中途终止，夭折；使流产，堕胎
items.def_en: 1. To stop a process, plan, or mission before it is completed. 2. To end a pregnancy before the fetus can survive.
items.ex_en: Ground control ordered the engineers to abort the rocket launch immediately.
items.ex_zh: 地面控制中心命令工程师立即中止火箭发射任务。
items.ex2_en: The dangerous space mission aborted automatically when critical flight systems failed unexpectedly.
items.ex2_zh: 当关键飞行系统意外发生故障时，这项危险的太空任务自动中止了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe bringing an activity, state, or process to a halt, ranging from standard natural stops to deliberate legal expirations or abrupt, premature cuts.
groups.summary_zh: 指使活动或进程停止，由自然结束递进至法定终止与强制腰斩。
groups.desc_en: Brings an activity, state, or continuum to a definitive halt, contrasting with gradual drifting dissolution or mere momentary pausing.
groups.desc_zh: 使活动、状态或进程走向最终终结或人为掐断，区别于过程的自然淡出或短暂中顿。
groups.nuance_en: terminate: legal or decisive administrative bringing to a hard end (contract / pregnancy / employment) · cease: formal, complete cessation of action or motion (fire / hostilities / operations) · wrap up: informal, tidy packaging of a concluded event or session (meeting / deal / filming) · call off: cancelling a planned or ongoing operation before completion (search / strike / wedding) · halt: abrupt, arresting interruption of kinetic progression (advance / production / proceedings)
groups.nuance_zh: terminate: 依程序或法理予以硬性彻底终止 (contract / pregnancy / employment) · cease: 正式、完全地停息或休止行动 (fire / hostilities / operations) · wrap up: 圆满且利落地打包装箱、收尾了结 (meeting / deal / filming) · call off: 临机取消或撤销既定行动 (search / strike / wedding) · halt: 强行遏止动力学意义上的行进与运转 (advance / production / proceedings)

groups.name: Eradicate & Wipe Out Entirely · 消除与根除 (Dispel, Eradicate, Obliterate)
groups.tip: 连根拔除，使其彻底不存

items.def_zh: 驱散，消除（疑虑、恐惧、谣言等）
items.def_en: To make a doubt, feeling, or belief disappear.
items.ex_en: The CEO held a press conference to dispel rumors regarding possible bankruptcy.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官举行了新闻发布会，以消除关于可能破产的谣言。

items.def_zh: 彻底抹去；抹杀（记忆、痕迹）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to obscure completely or wipe away all traces of a memory, sight, or existence
items.ex_en: She deliberately tried to blot out the painful memories of the accident.
items.ex_zh: 她刻意尝试彻底抹去关于那场事故的痛苦记忆。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to find and completely eliminate a source of trouble, evil, or corruption
items.ex_en: The government launched a sweeping campaign to root out corruption among officials.
items.ex_zh: 政府发起了一场雷厉风行的运动，以彻底根除官员内部的腐败。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to suppress or eradicate something bad or dangerous by forceful measures
items.ex_en: Health authorities acted swiftly to stamp out the potential outbreak of disease.
items.ex_zh: 卫生部门迅速采取行动，以扑灭可能爆发的疫情。

items.def_en: to destroy, remove, or kill everyone or everything in a target group completely
items.ex_en: A single unexpected frost could wipe out the entire season's fruit crop.
items.ex_zh: 一场突如其来的霜冻就可能彻底毁掉整季的水果收成。

items.def_en: to destroy or get rid of something bad completely so that it cannot return
items.ex_en: International medical teams have worked tirelessly to eradicate polio across developing nations.
items.ex_zh: 国际医疗队孜孜不倦地工作，以期在发展中国家彻底根除脊髓灰质炎。

items.def_zh: 连根拔起，根除；使背井离乡
items.def_en: 1. To pull a plant entirely out of the ground, including its roots; eradicate completely. 2. To force someone to leave their home or familiar environment.
items.ex_en: Fierce gale-force winds threatened to uproot ancient trees in the town square.
items.ex_zh: 强劲的烈风险些将镇广场上的古树连根拔起。

items.def_en: to pull up by the roots or completely destroy something noxious or unwanted
items.ex_en: The tyrant sought to extirpate every vestige of democratic thought from society.
items.ex_zh: 暴君企图从社会中彻底拔除一切民主思想的遗迹。

items.def_zh: 彻底消灭，毁灭；抹去，擦去（痕迹、记忆等）
items.def_en: To destroy something completely so that nothing remains; wipe out or erase.
items.ex_en: The violent explosion threatened to obliterate the entire block in seconds.
items.ex_zh: 剧烈的爆炸几秒钟内便有将整个街区完全抹杀毁灭的危险。

items.def_en: to reduce an enemy, structure, or object to complete nonexistence or ruin
items.ex_en: The army used advanced artillery to annihilate the fortified enemy stronghold completely.
items.ex_zh: 该部队动用先进火炮彻底摧毁歼灭了设防的敌军据点。

items.def_zh: 根除，消灭，灭绝（害虫、群体等）
items.def_en: To kill or destroy all individuals of a group of animals, pests, or people completely.
items.ex_en: Specialists were hired to exterminate the aggressive termites infesting the wooden foundation.
items.ex_zh: 房主聘请了专业人员，以彻底灭绝侵蚀木质地基的凶猛白蚁。

groups.summary_en: Causing an entity, population, abstract condition, or trace to cease to exist, ranging from dispelling insubstantial doubts to tearing up deep roots and violently wiping out all visible remnants.
groups.summary_zh: 从驱散虚妄疑虑到连根拔起、彻底抹除灭绝
groups.desc_en: Eliminates threats, evils, or traces with absolute thoroughness down to the origin, contrasting with surface-level mitigation, concealment, or containment.
groups.desc_zh: 将威胁、弊端或残迹连根拔起并从源头彻底消灭，区别于浮于表面的压制、掩盖或缓和。
groups.nuance_en: eradicate: completely tearing out by the metaphorical roots to prevent resurgence (disease / poverty / corruption) · extirpate: surgically or violently destroying dangerous entities entirely (heresy / weeds / vermin) · stamp out: forcefully crushing an incipient flare-up through physical suppression (fire / rebellion / dissent) · blot out: utterly obliterating from vision, memory, or existence (sun / memory / stain) · dispel: scattering and dissolving intangible fears or illusions like mist (doubts / myths / fears)
groups.nuance_zh: eradicate: 连根拔起以绝后患 (disease / poverty / corruption) · extirpate: 外科手术或毁灭性地彻底根绝 (heresy / weeds / vermin) · stamp out: 铁腕踏灭刚露头的火星或乱苗 (fire / rebellion / dissent) · blot out: 涂抹覆盖以彻底湮灭痕迹或视线 (sun / memory / stain) · dispel: 如风驱雾般驱散疑虑与虚妄 (doubts / myths / fears)

groups.name: Excrete & Void · 生理排泄与腺体分泌 (Discharge of Bodily Waste/Fluids)
groups.tip: 生理代谢废物的排泄

items.def_en: (+ sth) to eject food or bile from the stomach through the mouth
items.ex_en: The investigation threw up some unexpected problems for the company.
items.ex_zh: 调查给公司暴露出了一些意想不到的问题。

items.def_zh: 通过出汗排出（毒素、水分等）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to eliminate toxins or fluid from the body through heavy perspiration
items.ex_en: After intense training, athletes often hit the sauna to sweat out toxins.
items.ex_zh: 高强度训练后，运动员常常去蒸桑拿以通过排汗排出毒素。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to expel phlegm or fluid from the respiratory tract by coughing
items.ex_en: The chronic smoker began to cough up thick mucus every single morning.
items.ex_zh: 这位老烟民每天清晨都开始咳出浓稠的黏痰。

items.def_en: [I/T] (formal/medical) to discharge waste material such as urine or feces from the body
items.ex_en: The nurse instructed the post-surgery patient to void his bladder before discharge.
items.ex_zh: 护士嘱咐刚做完手术的病人在出院前先排空膀胱。

items.def_en: (informal, impolite) to release intestinal gas through the anus.
items.ex_en: He accidentally farted during the quiet yoga class, causing immense personal embarrassment.
items.ex_zh: 他在安静的瑜伽课上不小心放了个屁，感到尴尬至极。

items.def_en: 1. to let saliva trickle or drip out of the mouth. 2. (informal) to express excessive delight, enthusiasm, or craving for something.
items.ex_en: The hungry puppy began to drool uncontrollably upon smelling the roasted meat.
items.ex_zh: 闻到烤肉的香味后，饥饿的小狗开始止不住地流口水。

items.def_en: 1. (of a cell, gland, or plant) To produce and discharge a substance. 2. To hide or conceal something secretly.
items.ex_en: Specialized endocrine glands secrete essential hormones directly into the human bloodstream.
items.ex_zh: 特化的内分泌腺体直接将必需的激素分泌进入人体血液。

items.def_en: To discharge urine from the body.
items.ex_en: The patient struggled to urinate without experiencing severe, sharp abdominal pain.
items.ex_zh: 病人排尿时极度痛苦，伴随着腹部尖锐剧烈的疼痛。

items.def_en: to produce and discharge saliva in the mouth
items.ex_en: Pavlov observed that the dogs would salivate whenever a bell was rung.
items.ex_zh: 巴甫洛夫观察到，只要铃声一响，那些狗就会分泌唾液。

items.def_en: To discharge solid waste from the bowels through the anus.
items.ex_en: Patients suffering from severe food poisoning frequently need to defecate painfully.
items.ex_zh: 严重食物中毒的患者常常需要频繁且痛苦地排便。

items.def_en: to excrete sweat through the pores of the skin (formal)
items.ex_en: Anxious candidates began to perspire profusely under the bright studio lights.
items.ex_zh: 焦虑的候选人们在演播室明亮的灯光下开始大汗淋漓。

groups.summary_en: This scenario covers the physiological expulsion of metabolic waste products, gland emissions, and natural secretions from human or animal bodies, varying by anatomical pathway and formality.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖人体或生物体经由特定生理器官将代谢废弃物或体液排出体外的过程。
groups.desc_en: Expels biological wastes, secretions, or ingested matter from the body cavities or glandular surfaces, contrasting with passive chemical weeping or mechanical leakage.
groups.desc_zh: 自机体腔孔或腺体向外排出代谢废物、分泌物或胃内容物，区别于无生命的渗漏或被动析出。
groups.nuance_en: urinate: physiologically discharging liquid waste from the bladder (urine) · void: clinical, complete evacuation of bladder or bowels (bladder / bowels) · secrete: biological synthesis and deliberate release of functional fluids (hormone / venom / mucus) · drool: involuntary, slack-mouthed leaking of saliva (saliva / spit) · throw up: violent, retrograde gastric expulsion through the mouth (food / stomach contents / blood)
groups.nuance_zh: urinate: 生理排尿 (urine) · void: 临床术语指排空体液或腔囊 (bladder / bowels) · secrete: 腺体自主生成并分泌活性液体 (hormone / venom / mucus) · drool: 失控性的涎水流淌 (saliva / spit) · throw up: 剧烈的胃反流呕吐 (food / stomach contents / blood)

groups.name: Fasten by Mechanical Means · 机械扣合与销夹固定 (Clamp, Latch, Buckle, Peg)
groups.tip: 用夹具栓销牢牢固定

items.def_zh: 系紧安全带；用搭扣扣牢
items.def_en: (+ sth) to fasten securely with a buckle, especially a vehicle seatbelt
items.ex_en: All passengers must buckle up securely before the airplane taxis onto runway.
items.ex_zh: 所有乘客在飞机滑行进入跑道之前都必须牢牢系好安全带。
items.ex2_en: The careful mother buckled up her toddler in the rear car seat.
items.ex2_zh: 细心的母亲把幼儿系好在汽车后排座椅的安全带中。

items.def_zh: 用门闩闩牢，上闩；抓住，理解（latch onto）
items.def_en: 1. To fasten a door, gate, or window with a latch, or to be fastened in this way. 2. ('latch onto') To attach oneself to someone, or to grasp an idea eagerly.
items.ex_en: Make sure you latch the front gate properly so the dog stays inside.
items.ex_zh: 请务必把前门闩好，免得狗跑出去。
items.ex2_en: The wooden storm door latches securely whenever it closes shut.
items.ex2_zh: 这扇木制防风门关严时总会牢牢插住。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to bind, tighten, or secure firmly using a strap, belt, or mechanical tie
items.ex_en: The movers used heavy ratchet straps to cinch down the wooden furniture.
items.ex_zh: 搬家工人用结实的棘轮绑带将木质家具紧紧拉牢扎好。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fasten or press an object securely in place using a mechanical clamp
items.ex_en: The carpenter carefully clamped down the glued wooden planks to ensure stability.
items.ex_zh: 木工小心地用夹具将涂好胶的木板夹紧固定，以确保牢固。

items.def_zh: 用木栓（或钉子、衣夹）固定；使（工资、物价等）与……挂钩，限定
items.def_en: 1. To fasten or secure something with pegs. 2. To fix a price, currency, or rate at a particular level.
items.ex_en: They had to peg the tent securely into the rocky mountain soil.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须用桩子把帐篷牢固地钉入多石的山地土壤中。

items.def_zh: 夹紧，固定；强行固定；严厉打击，取缔（clamp down）
items.def_en: 1. To hold or fasten something tightly in place using a clamp. 2. ('clamp down on') To take strict official action to stop or prevent something.
items.ex_en: Please clamp the metal pipe firmly before you begin sawing through it.
items.ex_zh: 在你开始锯断金属管之前，请先用夹具将它紧紧夹住固定。

items.def_zh: 用搭扣扣紧，系紧；（使）弯曲，压垮；屈服
items.def_en: 1. To fasten something with a buckle, or to be fastened with a buckle. 2. To bend or collapse under pressure or heat; to give in.
items.ex_en: He quickly buckled his leather belt before running out the front door.
items.ex_zh: 他在冲出前门之前迅速扣紧了自己的皮带。
items.ex2_en: The sturdy steel bridge buckled under the tremendous weight of the vehicles.
items.ex2_zh: 坚固的钢桥在车辆的重压下发生了变形弯曲。

items.def_zh: 系紧于系缆栓上；用夹板固定
items.def_en: to secure or fasten a rope or object around a cleat
items.ex_en: The seasoned sailor expertly cleated the main halyard to prevent slipping.
items.ex_zh: 老练的水手熟练地将主升降索系紧在系缆栓上以防滑脱。

items.def_en: to secure a belt, strap, or girth firmly around something
items.ex_en: He had to cinch his belt another notch after losing significant weight.
items.ex_zh: 在体重明显下降后，他不得不将腰带又勒紧了一个扣眼。

items.def_en: to fasten or bind tightly using metal loops or shackles
items.ex_en: The guards were ordered to shackle the dangerous prisoner by his ankles.
items.ex_zh: 警卫接到命令，要用金属脚镣把这个危险的囚犯锁住。

items.def_en: to bind or fasten the arms, legs, or mechanical parts firmly to immobilize them
items.ex_en: The captors ruthlessly pinioned his arms behind his back with thick rope.
items.ex_zh: 捕手们残忍地用粗绳将他的双臂紧紧反绑在身后限制其行动。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe securing an object in place by employing a dedicated mechanical catch, strap, pin, or gripping device. They differentiate through the mechanical mechanism involved: spring/screw compression ('clamp'), pivoting bars ('latch'), interlocking prongs ('buckle'), or dowel pins ('peg').
groups.summary_zh: 运用门闩、卡扣、夹具或插销等机械结构紧固或扣牢物体。
groups.desc_en: Fastens, locks, or secures physical elements using rigid mechanical hardware, lever principles, or interlocking components, contrasting with adhesive bonding, chemical welding, or soft tying.
groups.desc_zh: 利用刚性五金配件、杠杆传动或扣合构件实现坚固锁定，区别于胶合粘接、焊接或软性绳结捆扎。
groups.nuance_en: clamp: applying dual-sided mechanical pressure using a screw-tightened vice (wood / pipe / workpiece) · latch: engaging a catch or lever into a strike plate to secure a closure (door / gate / lid) · buckle: interlocking two strap ends via an articulated tongue-and-frame fitting (belt / harness / shoes) · peg: securing or fastening into a fixed hole with an inserted pin (stake / tent / plank) · cinch down: tightening webbing or straps relentlessly through a friction buckle (load / saddle / cargo)
groups.nuance_zh: clamp: 旋紧夹具实施双面机械施压夹紧 (wood / pipe / workpiece) · latch: 拨入卡栓或锁舌使门扇扣合 (door / gate / lid) · buckle: 扣牢带扣以固定约束带 (belt / harness / shoes) · peg: 钉入木销或地钉进行定位销紧 (stake / tent / plank) · cinch down: 穿过摩擦扣强力勒紧并绑扎 (load / saddle / cargo)

groups.name: Fear & Terrify · 恐惧与惊骇 (Intimidate, Frighten, Petrify)
groups.tip: 从普通害怕递进至极度惊骇

items.def_en: (+ sb) to induce an unsettling feeling of fear, revulsion, or unease in someone
items.ex_en: The way that abandoned house looks at dusk really creeps me out.
items.ex_zh: 那栋废弃房屋在黄昏时的模样真让我心里发毛。

items.def_en: to make someone feel sudden fear or anxiety
items.ex_en: The sudden clap of thunder frightened the children sleeping quietly upstairs.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的雷声吓醒了在楼上安静睡觉的孩子们。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ away/off) to cause sudden fright or nervousness in someone
items.ex_en: Don't shout like that; you will scare the baby into crying.
items.ex_zh: 别那样大喊大叫，你会把小宝宝吓哭的。
items.ex2_en: Feral cats usually scare easily when strangers approach them too quickly.
items.ex2_zh: 当陌生人靠得太快时，野猫通常很容易受惊吓。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to drive an intruder, animal, or person away by frightening them
items.ex_en: The farmer set up a tall scarecrow to scare off hungry birds.
items.ex_zh: 农夫立起一个高大的稻草人来吓跑饥饿的鸟雀。

items.def_en: To make someone feel frightened, anxious, or worried that something dangerous might happen.
items.ex_en: Recent reports of burglaries in the neighborhood deeply alarmed the elderly residents.
items.ex_zh: 该街区近期的盗窃案报道让年长的居民们深感恐慌不安。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to experience or cause an episode of sudden, intense fear or panic
items.ex_en: She totally freaked out when she saw a huge hairy spider inside.
items.ex_zh: 当她看到里面有一只巨大的多毛蜘蛛时，彻底吓坏了。
items.ex2_en: The eerie unexplained noises in the dark attic freaked out the children.
items.ex2_zh: 黑暗阁楼里怪异莫名的响动吓坏了孩子们。

items.def_zh: 非常害怕，畏惧，极度担心
items.def_en: To feel great fear, anxiety, or apprehension about something that is going to or might happen.
items.ex_en: He dreaded giving the opening keynote address before such a massive audience.
items.ex_zh: 他非常畏惧在如此庞大的听众面前发表开幕主题演讲。

items.def_zh: 使极度惊恐，使震惊，使厌恶
items.def_en: To shock and frighten someone deeply with something terrible, appalling, or sickening.
items.ex_en: The gory details of the crime horrified everyone present in the courtroom.
items.ex_zh: 这桩罪案血腥可怖的细节让法庭上的每一个人都深感震惊和厌恶。

items.def_en: To suddenly feel so frightened or anxious that you cannot think or act sensibly, or to cause someone to do so.
items.ex_en: Flames leaped up the curtains, causing several theater guests to panic immediately.
items.ex_zh: 火苗窜上了窗帘，导致剧院的几名客人立刻惊慌失措。
items.ex2_en: Sudden false alarm warnings panicked the crowd inside the shopping mall.
items.ex2_zh: 突然的虚假警报让商场内的人群陷入恐慌。

items.def_en: to fill someone with acute, overwhelming terror
items.ex_en: Violent turbulence during the flight terrified passengers aboard the small charter plane.
items.ex_zh: 飞行途中的剧烈颠簸令这架小型包机上的乘客们极度惊骇。

items.def_en: to paralyze someone with fear so that they cannot move or think
items.ex_en: The sight of the approaching beast petrified the traveler into absolute immobility.
items.ex_zh: 逼近的猛兽让行者吓得呆若木鸡，全然无法动弹。
items.ex2_en: The frightened little boy petrified with fear upon hearing the loud thunder.
items.ex2_zh: 听到巨大的雷声，受惊的小男孩吓得动弹不得。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate states of emotional distress caused by perceived threat or impending danger, scaling from sudden unease and anticipatory dread to paralyzing terror.
groups.summary_zh: 指因感知危险或威胁引发的惧怕情绪，从警觉不安递进至极度惊骇僵死。
groups.desc_en: Instills intense psychic dread, visceral panic, or paralyzing apprehension, contrasting with rational caution, analytical worry, or mild surprise.
groups.desc_zh: 向心理灌注强烈的恐惧、生理性恐慌或惊骇瘫痪感，区别于理性的防备、单纯的担忧或轻度吃惊。
groups.nuance_en: terrify: striking utter, debilitating panic and horror into the psyche (victim / population / child) · horrify: inducing sickening shock blended with visceral disgust or moral recoil (onlookers / public / conscience) · scare off: repelling an unwanted actor through an intimidating deterrent display (intruders / birds / competitors) · alarm: triggering an urgent, alerting realization of imminent danger (citizens / neighbors / market) · creep out: evoking subtle, uncanny revulsion and skin-crawling discomfort (listener / guest / observer)
groups.nuance_zh: terrify: 剥夺反抗能力的剧烈惊吓与震慑 (victim / population / child) · horrify: 令人毛骨悚然、道德反胃与骇然惊愕 (onlookers / public / conscience) · scare off: 施加威慑以骇退不速之客 (intruders / birds / competitors) · alarm: 触动警报使人猛醒意识到危局 (citizens / neighbors / market) · creep out: 诱发诡异不适、起鸡皮疙瘩的阴森感 (listener / guest / observer)

groups.name: Fill & Overflow · 充溢与过载 (Inundate, Satiate, Swamp)
groups.tip: 从充盈满溢发展至过载泛滥

items.def_en: to enter or crowd into an enclosed space or vehicle rapidly in large, overwhelming numbers
items.ex_en: Dozens of eager concertgoers piled in as soon as the doors opened.
items.ex_zh: 大门一开，数十名急切的音乐会观众便蜂拥挤了进去。

items.def_en: to flow over the edge of a container, or spread uncontrollably beyond normal boundaries due to excess
items.ex_en: Simmering anger over high taxes began to spill over into violent protests.
items.ex_zh: 对高额税收酝酿已久的愤怒开始外溢扩散为暴力抗议。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to clog or completely fill a passage or space so movement is obstructed
items.ex_en: Narrow streets were choked with stranded vehicles following the sudden torrential downpour.
items.ex_zh: 突降暴雨之后，狭窄的街道被抛锚的车辆堵得水泄不通。

items.def_en: to overwhelm someone or something with an excess of things to deal with
items.ex_en: The small support team was swamped with hundreds of urgent customer complaints.
items.ex_zh: 这个小型支持团队被数百起紧急客户投诉搞得应接不暇。

items.def_en: to spread over or occupy a place in large, excessive numbers
items.ex_en: Abandoned city alleys were completely overrun by hundreds of aggressive stray cats.
items.ex_zh: 废弃的城市小巷彻底被数百只极具攻击性的流浪猫所占据肆虐。

items.def_zh: 使过度拥挤，容纳过多的人
items.def_en: (often passive) To fill a place or vehicle with too many people or things.
items.ex_en: Commuters complained that railway operators constantly overcrowded the early morning passenger cars.
items.ex_zh: 通勤人员抱怨铁路运营商总是让清晨的客车车厢过度拥挤。

items.def_zh: 使充斥，使过量供应；使吃得过饱
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To supply a market with far more goods than can be bought or sold. 2. To satisfy an appetite or desire to the point of excess.
items.ex_en: Cheap imports threatened to glut the domestic market with excess steel inventory.
items.ex_zh: 廉价进口产品有可能使国内市场充斥过剩的钢铁库存。

items.def_en: (+ with) To give someone or something too much work, worry, or physical load to handle.
items.ex_en: Do not overburden young employees with excessive administrative duties and unrealistic deadlines.
items.ex_zh: 不要用过多的行政事务和不切实际的截止日期让年轻员工负担过重。

items.def_en: To fill a container or space with too much of something so that it overflows.
items.ex_en: Be careful not to overfill the oil tank during routine vehicle maintenance.
items.ex_zh: 在进行日常车辆保养时，小心不要把油箱加得太满而溢出。

items.def_zh: 淹没；使应接不暇，使充满
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive, + with) To overwhelm someone with a huge number of things, requests, or questions. 2. To flood an area with water.
items.ex_en: The agency was deluged with calls after broadcasting the dramatic public announcement.
items.ex_zh: 在播送了那则引人注目的公众通告后，该机构接到了海量来电。

items.def_en: to overwhelm with a huge flood of things, requests, or information
items.ex_en: The editor was inundated with hundreds of manuscripts from ambitious new authors.
items.ex_zh: 这位编辑被野心勃勃的新人作者们铺天盖地寄来的数百份稿件淹没了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe supplying, filling, or burdening a container, system, or entity with people, goods, or input beyond its capacity, escalating from overfilling to overwhelming inundation.
groups.summary_zh: 指填充、供给或施加负担超出受体的承载极限，由单纯装得过满升级为泛滥压垮。
groups.desc_en: Floods a receptacle, space, or cognitive capacity beyond its structural capacity until it spills or chokes, contrasting with controlled, orderly containment.
groups.desc_zh: 涌入之物远超容器、空间或承载力的物理极限，导致漫溢、窒息或瘫痪，区别于受控的饱满容纳。
groups.nuance_en: swamp: overwhelming like a wave and rendering helpless by sheer volume (inbox / system / market) · overrun: invasive, unstoppable spilling over of numbers occupying a domain (territory / lawn / field) · glut: saturating a market or pipeline far beyond absorption capacity (market / commodity / shelves) · overburden: crushing structural integrity under excessive mechanical or mental weight (infrastructure / system / staff) · choke with: clogging a narrow channel until flow ceases entirely (debris / weeds / traffic)
groups.nuance_zh: swamp: 巨浪般灌入并使系统无力瘫痪 (inbox / system / market) · overrun: 侵略性超员漫溢并攻陷地盘 (territory / lawn / field) · glut: 过度倾销导致消化不良与供过于求 (market / commodity / shelves) · overburden: 施加超负荷使支撑结构濒临崩解 (infrastructure / system / staff) · choke with: 杂物积塞咽喉通道致使流体阻绝 (debris / weeds / traffic)

groups.name: Foretell & Portend · 预言与预示 (Prophesy, Augur, Presage)
groups.tip: 预先预告并昭示将来吉凶

items.def_zh: 预示；表明…很有可能发生
items.def_en: (+ sth) to indicate that a particular future event or situation is likely to happen
items.ex_en: Current economic indicators point to an inevitable rise in national unemployment rates.
items.ex_zh: 目前的经济指标表明全国失业率很有可能会出现上升。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to be a sign that a major change or new period is beginning
items.ex_en: The dawn of quantum mechanics heralded in a magnificent era of physics.
items.ex_zh: 量子力学的拂晓预告了一个辉煌物理学时代的到来。

items.def_en: to act as an advance indication or suggestion of what is to come
items.ex_en: Gloomy storm clouds in chapter one foreshadow the tragic fate of lovers.
items.ex_zh: 第一章中阴沉的暴风云为这对恋人的悲剧命运埋下了伏笔。

items.def_en: (+ well/ill) to be a sign of a particular good or bad outcome in the future
items.ex_en: These falling export figures bode ill for the nation's fragile economic recovery.
items.ex_zh: 这些不断下滑的出口数据对于该国脆弱的经济复苏而言是不祥之兆。

items.def_zh: 预言，预告；（受神启）说预言
items.def_en: To predict or say what will happen in the future, especially through religious or mystical inspiration.
items.ex_en: Ancient oracles prophesied that a mighty king would rise from humble ashes.
items.ex_zh: 古代神谕预言一位伟大的君王将从卑微的灰烬中崛起。

items.def_en: To announce, signal, or foreshadow the approach or arrival of something.
items.ex_en: Golden autumn leaves harbinger the quiet arrival of a harsh northern winter.
items.ex_zh: 金黄的秋叶预示着严酷北方冬日的悄然来临。

items.def_zh: 预言，预告，预示（foretell的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of foretell; to predict or announce beforehand.
items.ex_en: The astrologer foretold a great calamity that would soon engulf the kingdom.
items.ex_zh: 占星师预言了一场即将吞噬整个王国的巨大灾难。

items.def_zh: 预示，是……的征兆；占卜，预言
items.def_en: 1. To be a sign of a good or bad outcome in the future (especially in 'augur well/ill'). 2. To foretell or predict the future from signs or omens.
items.ex_en: Recent positive negotiations augur well for long-term peace in the troubled region.
items.ex_zh: 近期的积极谈判兆示着该动荡地区有望迎来长期的和平。

items.def_en: To predict or say what will happen in the future, especially by using magic or intuition.
items.ex_en: Wise village elders claimed they could foretell coming droughts by watching birds.
items.ex_zh: 村里睿智的长老们声称通过观察鸟类就能预知即将到来的旱灾。

items.def_en: to act as an omen or warning of something, typically bad, that is about to happen
items.ex_en: Heavy rolling thunderclouds presaged a violent tempest that would batter coastal towns.
items.ex_zh: 翻滚的沉重雷云预示着一场将重创沿海城镇的狂暴风暴。

items.def_en: To be a sign or warning that something momentous, usually unpleasant, is going to happen.
items.ex_en: Mysterious sudden bird die-offs portend an ecological disaster for the remote marshlands.
items.ex_zh: 鸟类神秘的突然大批死亡预示着偏远沼泽地的一场生态灾难。

groups.summary_en: A sign, omen, or human seer indicates future events before they happen. Verbs span divine/supernatural utterances, interpretive omen readings, literary foreshadowing, and symbolic precursor roles.
groups.summary_zh: 通过神谕宣称、卜测征兆或天然迹象在事前预言并预示吉凶。
groups.desc_en: Reads present omens, signs, or causal indicators to forecast future events, contrasting with retrospective historical analysis or spontaneous guessing.
groups.desc_zh: 通过现存征兆、预兆或早期迹象对未来事态进行预示，区别于事后溯源分析或凭空盲目揣测。
groups.nuance_en: foreshadow: artistic or historical dropping of ominous, structural clues (tragedy / climax / future) · augur: divining or prognosticating favorable or dire systemic outcomes (success / disaster / change) · presage: serving as an intrinsic, shuddering somatic or atmospheric omen (doom / storm / decline) · harbinger: actively announcing or ushering in the arrival of a new era or trend (spring / collapse / revolution) · bode: carrying a relational valence of good or ill fortune (ill / well / omen)
groups.nuance_zh: foreshadow: 文艺或历史脉络中埋设结构性伏笔 (tragedy / climax / future) · augur: 占卜或研判系统性结局吉凶 (success / disaster / change) · presage: 本身构成灾变即将来临的实质前兆 (doom / storm / decline) · harbinger: 充当先声先锋以揭示新时代的降临 (spring / collapse / revolution) · bode: 带有关系性地预兆吉凶祸福 (ill / well / omen)

groups.name: Fortify & Arm · 设防与武装 (Fortify, Arm, Entrench)
groups.tip: 修筑工事与装备武器

items.def_zh: 武装，配备武器；装备，提供防御；备战
items.def_en: 1. To provide weapons or defensive equipment to someone, or to supply oneself with weapons. 2. To provide someone with useful skills, information, or equipment. 3. To make a bomb, weapon, or security device ready to explode or operate.
items.ex_en: The commander ordered officers to arm all recruits with modern assault rifles.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官命令军官用现代突击步枪武装所有新兵。

items.def_zh: 设要塞防守；筑堡设防；（fort up）退入城堡固守
items.def_en: 1. To protect or fortify with a fort; ('fort up') to take refuge in or as if in a fort for protection.
items.ex_en: Settlers decided to fort up inside the stockade until reinforcements arrived safely.
items.ex_zh: 定居者们决定退入栅栏堡垒固守，直到援军安全抵达。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to support, strengthen, or reinforce a weak structure or defensive position
items.ex_en: Engineers worked desperately to shore up the weakened dam before nightfall came.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们在夜幕降临前拼命抢修加固受损脆弱的大坝。

items.def_en: to dig protective trenches or entrench defensive positions in preparation for enemy attack
items.ex_en: Infantry units were ordered to dig in before heavy enemy artillery struck.
items.ex_zh: 步兵部队接到命令，在敌方重炮轰击前掘壕固守阵地。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to block an entrance or confine someone securely behind erected fortifications
items.ex_en: Guards managed to barricade the protesters in the inner courtyard without violence.
items.ex_zh: 警卫设法设路障将抗议者们封堵在内院，未发生暴力冲突。

items.def_zh: 派兵驻守；防守（城镇、要塞）
items.def_en: to station troops in a town or fortress to defend it
items.ex_en: The crown decided to garrison five hundred soldiers inside the frontier citadel.
items.ex_zh: 王室决定派驻五百名士兵驻守边境城堡以加强防卫。

items.def_zh: 筑防御工事保卫，加强防卫；增强，强化；（给食品）添加营养素
items.def_en: 1. To strengthen a place with defenses or fortifications against attack. 2. To make someone feel physically or mentally stronger. 3. (+ with) To enrich food or drink by adding vitamins or minerals.
items.ex_en: Troops labored all night to fortify their hill outpost against incoming assaults.
items.ex_zh: 部队整夜劳作，修筑防御工事以抵御即将到来的攻击。

items.def_en: to block or defend an entrance, street, or building with an improvised barrier
items.ex_en: Rebels used abandoned vehicles and wooden crates to barricade the main boulevard.
items.ex_zh: 叛乱分子用废弃车辆和木箱在主干道上设置路障进行阻挡。

items.def_zh: 供给军需品；为……装备武器弹药
items.def_en: To supply an army, fort, or ship with weapons and ammunition.
items.ex_en: Government arsenals worked day and night to munition distant forward military bases.
items.ex_zh: 政府军工厂日夜赶工，为远方的陆前军事基地供给武器弹药。

items.def_zh: 掘壕固守；牢固确立防线
items.def_en: to dig trenches or defensive earthworks to secure a position against attack
items.ex_en: Soldiers entrenched themselves along the ridge to repel any impending counterattack effectively.
items.ex_zh: 士兵们沿着山脊掘壕固守，以有效击退任何即将到来的反击。

items.def_zh: 使武器化；改造为攻防武器
items.def_en: to adapt or equip something for use as a weapon in combat or conflict
items.ex_en: Extremists sought to weaponize common industrial chemicals for their deadly covert operations.
items.ex_zh: 极端分子企图将普通工业化学品武器化，用于其致命的秘密行动。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe preparing a location, military unit, or person for defensive or offensive conflict by installing fortifications, weapons, or protective obstacles. They range from physical reinforcement of a site to supplying weaponry or digging in defensive positions.
groups.summary_zh: 通过构筑防御工事、提供武器弹药或挖壕固守以增强战斗防御准备。
groups.desc_en: Converts an open or vulnerable position into a defensible military stronghold through engineering or weaponry, contrasting with passive hiding or retreat.
groups.desc_zh: 通过工程筑垒或军事武装将脆弱暴露据点改造成防御要塞，区别于消极藏匿或被动撤退。
groups.nuance_en: fortify: reinforcing civil or military structures with walls, earthworks, or stamina (castle / border / resolve) · garrison: occupying and holding a military outpost with stationed troops (town / outpost / fort) · barricade: erecting impromptu physical obstructions across an opening (street / entrance / door) · dig in: excavating entrenchments for prolonged, stubborn holding of ground (troops / defenders / position) · shore up: providing structural timber bracing or external support against collapse (defenses / banks / confidence)
groups.nuance_zh: fortify: 构筑坚壁工事或注入精神支撑以御敌 (castle / border / resolve) · garrison: 派驻守备部队以控制要塞城关 (town / outpost / fort) · barricade: 临时搭建路障或障碍物以堵死通路 (street / entrance / door) · dig in: 挖掘散兵壕深壕以誓死固守 (troops / defenders / position) · shore up: 架设斜撑木支柱以防阵线崩解 (defenses / banks / confidence)

groups.name: Groom, Style & Adorn Hair/Appearance · 理容、修饰与梳理装扮 (Groom & Preen)
groups.tip: 梳理毛发修剪整饰外表

items.def_en: (+ sth) to style or arrange hair neatly, or dress someone attractively
items.ex_en: She spent two full hours doing up her hair for the gala.
items.ex_zh: 她花了整整两个小时精心盘梳头发，准备参加盛会。

items.def_zh: 抹平；把（头发）梳得油光水滑
items.def_en: (+ sth) to flatten and smooth hair down using water, pomade, or oil
items.ex_en: The boy used scented pomade to slick down his stubborn unruly hair.
items.ex_zh: 那个男孩用芳香发膏把他顽固不顺的头发抹平理顺。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to tidy and groom personal appearance to look neat and stylish
items.ex_en: He went to the washroom to spruce up before his dinner date.
items.ex_zh: 他在赴晚餐约会前去洗手间拾掇了一下仪容。

items.def_zh: （给动物）梳刷毛皮；修整（外表），打扮；培养，培训
items.def_en: 1. To clean and brush the coat of an animal, especially a horse or dog. 2. To make your appearance neat and tidy. 3. To prepare or train someone for a special purpose or career.
items.ex_en: Stable hands wash and groom prize horses every morning before the races.
items.ex_zh: 马房工人每天清晨在比赛前都会清洗并梳刷名贵赛马的毛皮。

items.def_zh: 为……理发（或修面）；当理发师
items.def_en: 1. To cut the hair of or shave someone; to work as a barber.
items.ex_en: The elderly gentleman went downtown every Friday morning to barber his beard.
items.ex_zh: 那位老绅士每周五早晨都会去市中心修剪修整胡须。

items.def_zh: 梳理（头发或毛发）；彻底搜查，全面搜寻
items.def_en: 1. To untangle, tidy, or arrange hair or fur with a comb. 2. To search a place or an area thoroughly.
items.ex_en: She sat before the mirror to comb out tangles from long hair.
items.ex_zh: 她坐在镜子前，用梳子梳顺长发中的缠结。

items.def_en: 1. To apply lipstick to the lips.
items.ex_en: She hurriedly lipsticked her mouth red before rushing out to the party.
items.ex_zh: 在匆忙出门去参加聚会之前，她赶紧给嘴唇涂上了红色口红。

items.def_en: to apply pomade or scented ointment to hair to give it a sleek, styled look
items.ex_en: Dancers pomaded their hair backwards to achieve a sleek and polished appearance.
items.ex_zh: 舞者们用发膏将头发往后抹平定型，以呈现出光滑利落的仪容。

items.def_en: 1. To make hair curly or wavy by treating it with chemicals.
items.ex_en: She decided to perm her naturally straight hair for an upcoming wedding.
items.ex_zh: 为了即将到来的婚礼，她决定把自己天生的直发烫卷。

items.def_en: to spend time making oneself look neat, attractive, and well-groomed
items.ex_en: The actor paused before each hallway mirror to preen his neat suit.
items.ex_zh: 演员在走廊的每面镜子前停下脚步，精心整理他整洁的西装。

items.def_en: to style or arrange someone's hair in an elaborate or neat fashion
items.ex_en: The celebrity stylist coiffed the bride's locks into an elegant bridal bun.
items.ex_zh: 明星发型师将新娘的秀发打造成一个优雅的新娘发髻。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote tending to, styling, cosmeticizing, or maintaining one's personal hygiene, hair, or physical appearance. They vary from basic hair combing and professional barbering to cosmetic application and chemical hair styling.
groups.summary_zh: 梳理毛发、理发修面、化妆修饰或化学美发等外形打理行为。
groups.desc_en: Cleans, trims, oils, and styles hair, fur, or physical appearance to project hygienic order or dapper elegance, contrasting with basic washing or deep surgical alterations.
groups.desc_zh: 对毛发、面容或体表进行修剪、梳理、敷油与拾掇，以彰显利落仪表或精致姿容，区别于基础沐浴或侵入性手术整形。
groups.nuance_en: groom: systematic brushing, tidying, and maintenance of hair or fur (coat / mane / whiskers) · spruce up: briskly freshening and smartening one's appearance or clothes (wardrobe / image / room) · comb: drawing a toothed instrument to untangle hair or fleece (hair / locks / fleece) · pomade: applying perfumed wax or scented grease to sleek down the coiffure (hair / curls / mustache) · barber: professional cutting, trimming, and shaving of masculine hair (hair / beard / patrons)
groups.nuance_zh: groom: 细致打理、清洁与修剪毛发外表 (coat / mane / whiskers) · spruce up: 快速收拾利落以焕然一新 (wardrobe / image / room) · comb: 用梳齿梳通纠结发丝 (hair / locks / fleece) · pomade: 涂抹发油发蜡使发型油亮服帖 (hair / curls / mustache) · barber: 职业理发匠式的修剪、刮脸与刮剃 (hair / beard / patrons)

groups.name: Hew & Sever · 削砍与截切 (Hew, Lop, Bevel)
groups.tip: 斧锯刃具劈砍成形

items.def_en: to shape pieces of wood by carving off thin slices with a knife
items.ex_en: The old carpenter sat outside whittling small pine figurines with his penknife.
items.ex_zh: 老木匠坐在屋外，用他的小折刀削出小小的松木人像。

items.def_zh: 把……切成斜角（或斜边），斜削
items.def_en: To cut, grind, or shape an edge or surface at a sloping angle rather than a right angle.
items.ex_en: The stone mason carefully beveled the sharp corners of the marble slab.
items.ex_zh: 石匠仔细地将大理石板的锋利棱角削磨成倾斜的边角。

items.def_zh: 使成锯齿状；在……边缘切出齿纹
items.def_en: To cut, notch, or form sharp, saw-like teeth along the edge of something.
items.ex_en: Craftsmen serrate the steel blade edge to cut coarse rope more effectively.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们在钢制刀刃边缘切出锯齿纹，以便更高效地割断粗绳。

items.def_en: to cut away a right-angled edge on a block of wood or stone to make a symmetrical sloping edge
items.ex_en: Workers chamfered every exterior timber beam to prevent painful splinters during handling.
items.ex_zh: 工人们将所有外露木梁削出倒角，以防搬运时被刺扎伤。

items.def_zh: 砍掉，修剪（树枝等）；大幅削减
items.def_en: 1. To cut or chop off parts of something, especially branches of a tree, with a heavy stroke. 2. (informal) To reduce or eliminate a large amount from something.
items.ex_en: The board decided to lop several million dollars from the annual budget.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定从年度预算中大幅削减数百万美元。

items.def_zh: （用斧等）砍，劈，砍伐；凿出，劈出；坚守，遵循 (hew to)
items.def_en: 1. To chop or cut something heavily using an axe, sword, or other tool. 2. To shape or carve something out of wood or stone. 3. (hew to) To adhere or conform strictly to something.
items.ex_en: Pioneers had to hew heavy logs to build warm shelters before winter.
items.ex_zh: 先驱者们必须砍伐粗重的原木，以便在入冬前建造温暖的庇护所。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to sever an object or protruding part completely using heavy blows of an ax or blade
items.ex_en: The butcher used a cleaver to chop off thick bone joints cleanly.
items.ex_zh: 屠夫用剁肉刀利落地将粗大的骨关节彻底砍断。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to sever or cut something off roughly and unevenly using repeated blade strikes
items.ex_en: He had to hack off the rusted metal bracket with dull shears.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不费力地用钝剪刀粗暴乱砍，卸下生锈的金属支架。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut off or sever an unwanted branch or limb with a single sharp stroke
items.ex_en: The gardener lop off rotten thick branches with a heavy curved pruning saw.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用一把厚重的弯刃修枝锯利落地砍下了腐烂的粗树枝。

items.def_en: to cut something roughly or violently with heavy, repeated blows of an ax or knife
items.ex_en: Explorers had to hack through dense jungle vegetation with heavy steel machetes.
items.ex_zh: 探险家们必须用沉重的钢制开山刀在茂密的丛林植被中劈斩出一条路。

items.def_en: to cut through something completely, separating one part from another with a sharp instrument
items.ex_en: The surgeon worked delicately to sever the diseased tissue without harming nearby nerves.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生精细操作，在不伤及临近神经的情况下切除了病变组织。

groups.summary_en: An agent shapes, severs, or bevels a piece of wood, stone, or plant using a sharp cutting blade, ax, or tool, either creating specific angled profiles or severing protruding parts.
groups.summary_zh: 使用利刃、斧具对木料、石材或枝干进行成型削边或斩断截落。
groups.desc_en: Executes forceful or angled blade strikes to shave, sculpt, or amputate solid woody or bony matter, contrasting with thin incision, puncture, or tearing.
groups.desc_zh: 借助刃器挥砍、切削或倒角以剥除、修整或截断固体木石肢体，区别于线状浅割、穿刺或撕裂拽断。
groups.nuance_en: hew: heavy, rhythmic axe-strikes carving massive timber or stone (logs / timber / path) · lop: cleanly severing dangling or sprawling limbs and branches with a sweeping cut (branch / limb / bough) · bevel: cutting or planing an edge to a sloping, non-orthogonal angle (edge / glass / woodwork) · chamfer: cutting away the sharp right-angled corner of a timber or stone beam (corner / edge / plank) · whittle: peeling repetitive small slivers from wood using a handheld pocketknife (stick / wood / figure)
groups.nuance_zh: hew: 运斧重力劈砍原木或在乱石中凿辟 (logs / timber / path) · lop: 一刀挥断多余枝杈或外凸肉体 (branch / limb / bough) · bevel: 将垂直立面切削成斜角斜面 (edge / glass / woodwork) · chamfer: 刨去石木棱角削成倒角过渡面 (corner / edge / plank) · whittle: 用小刀从容削下薄片雕琢木器 (stick / wood / figure)

groups.name: Illuminate & Bathe in Light · 照亮、照射与投光 (Illuminate & Irradiate)
groups.tip: 强光或辐射光芒投射照亮

items.def_en: to provide light to an area or make an object bright enough to see
items.ex_en: A single oil lamp was enough to light the small wooden cabin.
items.ex_zh: 一盏油灯就足以照亮这座小木屋。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to brighten a space completely or bathe an object in sudden light
items.ex_en: Sudden flashes of lightning began to light up the dark night sky.
items.ex_zh: 道道闪电突然开始照亮漆黑的夜空。
items.ex2_en: The children's faces lit up with joy upon receiving their gifts.
items.ex2_zh: 收到礼物时，孩子们脸上洋溢出喜悦的光芒。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to direct rays of luminous light onto a person or surface
items.ex_en: The midday sun continued to shine on the quiet courtyard below.
items.ex_zh: 正午的阳光继续照射着下方宁静的院子。

items.def_en: to cast intense or focused rays of light downward onto an area
items.ex_en: Searchlights beam down from the helicopters patrolling the dark coastline.
items.ex_zh: 探照灯从巡逻黑暗海岸线的直升机上向下方投射强光。

items.def_en: to supply a place or object with light, making it clearly visible
items.ex_en: Rows of vintage streetlamps illuminate the historic avenue each evening.
items.ex_zh: 成排的复古街灯每晚都会照亮这条历史悠久的大道。

items.def_en: to make an area or object lighter, more luminous, or brighter
items.ex_en: Adding another mirror helped brighten the narrow and dimly lit hallway.
items.ex_zh: 增添一面镜子有助于使狭窄昏暗的走廊变得明亮。
items.ex2_en: The gloomy sky brightened gradually as the morning storm clouds dispersed.
items.ex2_zh: 随着清晨的风暴云散去，阴沉的天空逐渐亮堂起来。

items.def_zh: 照射，照亮；（使）生辉；放射，以射线照射
items.def_en: 1. To illuminate something brightly; make radiant. 2. (physics, medical) To expose something to radiation.
items.ex_en: Powerful floodlights irradiate the ancient stone cathedral during evening celebrations.
items.ex_zh: 强力的泛光灯在晚间庆典期间照亮了这座古老的石头大教堂。

items.def_en: 1. To illuminate a building, sports field, or open area with powerful floodlights.
items.ex_en: Officials decided to floodlight the football stadium for the evening championship match.
items.ex_zh: 官员们决定用泛光灯照亮足球场，以举行晚间冠军赛。

items.def_zh: 用泛光灯照亮（floodlight 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. (past tense and past participle of floodlight) To illuminate an outdoor area or building with floodlights.
items.ex_en: Bright lamps floodlit the castle walls throughout the festive night.
items.ex_zh: 明亮的灯光在整个节日之夜照亮了城堡的墙壁。

items.def_en: 1. (literary) To light up or brighten something. 2. To enlighten spiritually or intellectually.
items.ex_en: Gentle moonlight rose to illumine the silent paths of the garden.
items.ex_zh: 温柔的月色升起，照耀着花园寂静的小径。

items.def_en: 1. (poetic) To light up, brighten, or illuminate.
items.ex_en: Pale morning rays illume the distant mountains as dawn breaks.
items.ex_zh: 破晓时分，淡淡的晨曦照亮了远方的群山。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe casting light upon or penetrating an object or area with luminous rays. Nuances span from practical physical illumination (spotlights, floodlights) and scientific ray exposure to literary and poetic lighting of scenes.
groups.summary_zh: 向物体或区域投射光线、人工大面积打光或用射线照亮/照射。
groups.desc_en: Projects active photonic energy or rays onto an obscure target to dispel darkness and reveal physical details, contrasting with radiating heat or passive chemical luminescence.
groups.desc_zh: 向幽暗目标投射主动光波或光束以驱散晦暗并清晰成像，区别于单纯热辐射散热或自发性荧光弱光。
