groups.summary_en: Verbs describing an agent attaining an endpoint, destination, or milestone after traversing distance. 'Arrive' focuses intransitively on reaching the termination point, while 'reach' transitively captures the span crossed to touch that terminus.
groups.summary_zh: 描述行程结束到达终点或触及某一空间或时间节点的动作。
groups.desc_en: Attaining a destination or terminus through intentional motion, effort, or transit schedules, contrasting with neutral motion (moving, traveling) by focusing squarely on the endpoint completion.
groups.desc_zh: 经由位移、努力或既定班次最终抵达终点，聚焦于行程终结的达成，区别于中性的行进或移动。
groups.nuance_en: arrive: formal or scheduled reaching of an endpoint (train / flight / delegation) · reach: achieving an endpoint after deliberate distance or exertion (summit / consensus / shore) · make it: overcoming barriers or time constraints to arrive safely (party / deadline / border) · pull in: vehicular entry and slowing to a halt at a stop (train / bus / ferry) · hit: informal, dynamic landing upon a venue or milestone (town / club / milestone)
groups.nuance_zh: arrive: 按计划或正式抵达终点 (train / flight / delegation) · reach: 克服距离或阻力后触及终点 (summit / consensus / shore) · make it: 战胜困难或赶在时限前幸存/赶到 (party / deadline / border) · pull in: 车辆进站停靠或靠岸 (train / bus / ferry) · hit: 口语中动态且迅猛地落脚某地或触及里程碑 (town / club / milestone)

groups.name: Assault & Ambush · 突袭与武装打击 (Ambush, Firebomb, Blitz)
groups.tip: 发起猛烈突袭猛攻目标

items.def_zh: 半路拦截突袭；埋伏守候
items.def_en: to wait in hiding to surprise, ambush, and attack someone on their way
items.ex_en: Armed bandits planned to waylay the royal courier in the shadowed mountain pass.
items.ex_zh: 武装强盗密谋在阴暗的山隘中半路截杀皇家信使。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack someone by jumping or pouncing without warning
items.ex_en: The alley mugger jumped on the unsuspecting tourist from behind the dumpster.
items.ex_zh: 小巷里的劫匪从垃圾桶后突然扑向毫无防备的游客。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to attack someone or something suddenly and with fierce violence
items.ex_en: Fierce raiders fell upon the sleeping encampment under cover of total darkness.
items.ex_zh: 凶悍的袭击者在浓重夜色的掩护下猛扑向沉睡的营地。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack someone physically with great force and aggression
items.ex_en: The bouncer suddenly laid into the unruly patron with a flurry of punches.
items.ex_zh: 保镖突然对那名闹事的顾客大打出手，拳头如雨点般砸下。

items.def_en: To attack someone suddenly from a hidden position.
items.ex_en: Rebel soldiers ambushed the military supply convoy along the narrow forest road.
items.ex_zh: 叛军士兵在狭窄的林间小路上伏击了军用补给车队。

items.def_en: to attack, damage, or sink a vessel using one or more underwater torpedoes
items.ex_en: A hostile submarine torpedoed the lone cargo freighter in the deep channel.
items.ex_zh: 一艘敌对潜艇在深水道中用鱼雷击沉了那艘落单的货船。

items.def_en: to launch a rapid, concentrated, and devastating military attack on an objective
items.ex_en: Enemy bombers blitzed the industrial district in a devastating coordinated nighttime assault.
items.ex_zh: 敌方轰炸机在一次毁灭性的夜间协同突袭中猛烈轰炸了工业区。

items.def_zh: 用马刀砍杀，用军刀袭击
items.def_en: To cut, strike, or wound someone with a sabre.
items.ex_en: Charging cavalrymen ruthlessly sabred the retreating infantry across the bloody battlefield.
items.ex_zh: 冲锋的骑兵在血腥的战场上用马刀无情砍杀溃退的步兵。

items.def_zh: 扫射突袭（低空用机枪或炮火扫射）
items.def_en: to attack ground troops or locations repeatedly with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft
items.ex_en: Fighter jets strafed the enemy trenches with continuous, devastating heavy machine-gun fire.
items.ex_zh: 战斗机用持续且极具破坏力的重机枪火力俯冲扫射敌方战壕。

items.def_zh: 用燃烧弹袭击，投掷燃烧弹攻击
items.def_en: To attack and damage or destroy a building, vehicle, or area using incendiary bombs.
items.ex_en: Rioters firebombed several commercial storefronts during the violent clashes downtown last night.
items.ex_zh: 暴徒在昨晚市中心的激烈冲突中用燃烧弹袭击了数家商铺。

groups.summary_en: An aggressor strikes a target suddenly using concealed surprise, explosive/incendiary weaponry, or overwhelming armed violence, intended to devastate or catch off-guard.
groups.summary_zh: 通过埋伏突击、纵火轰炸或冷兵器劈砍发起剧烈武力袭击。
groups.desc_en: Executing a sudden, aggressive, and often concealed or overwhelming military or physical strike, contrasting with symmetrical combat or gradual confrontation.
groups.desc_zh: 实施突然、隐蔽且往往具压倒性的武力突袭或猛烈打击，区别于对称作战或渐进式对抗。
groups.nuance_en: ambush: concealed surprise attack from cover (patrol / convoy / prey) · waylay: intercepting and accosting someone unexpectedly en route (traveler / courier / minister) · blitz: rapid, concentrated, devastating onslaught (city / defenses / sector) · torpedo: destructive underwater or metaphorical subversive strike (vessel / career / bill) · lay into: sudden, vicious physical or verbal assault (opponent / critic / attacker)
groups.nuance_zh: ambush: 设伏伏击毫无防备的目标 (patrol / convoy / prey) · waylay: 半路截击拦路盘问或劫掠 (traveler / courier / minister) · blitz: 迅猛集中的毁灭性闪电式打击 (city / defenses / sector) · torpedo: 发射鱼雷摧毁或暗中颠覆破坏 (vessel / career / bill) · lay into: 突然施加凶狠的肉体攻击或痛骂 (opponent / critic / attacker)

groups.name: Attention to Obsessive Focus · 注意至全神贯注 (Heed, Engross, Rivet)
groups.tip: 从留心注意到全神贯注

items.def_en: (+ to) Pay conscious attention or give careful heed to what is said or observed
items.ex_en: The delegates were urged to attend closely to the nuances of the treaty.
items.ex_zh: 代表们被敦促密切注意条约中的细微措辞。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to think, speak, or worry persistently about something for an excessive period
items.ex_en: She tends to dwell on minor mistakes instead of celebrating her achievements.
items.ex_zh: 她总是对微小的过失念念不忘，而不是庆祝自己的成就。

items.def_en: Take up someone's full mental attention and interest completely
items.ex_en: The complex historical mystery completely absorbed his attention for the entire weekend.
items.ex_zh: 那个复杂的历史谜团在整个周末彻底吸引了他的全部注意力。

items.def_zh: 留心，注意，听从（建议或警告）
items.def_en: (formal) To pay close, serious attention to advice, a warning, or a rule.
items.ex_en: The captain failed to heed the severe weather warnings issued by coastal authorities.
items.ex_zh: 船长未能听从沿海当局发布的恶劣天气警告。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to focus one's attention or gaze unwaveringly on someone or something
items.ex_en: The detective locked onto the suspect the moment he entered the lobby.
items.ex_zh: 嫌疑人刚走进大厅，侦探的目光就紧紧锁定了对方。

items.def_zh: 把注意力完全集中于，锁定
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to direct all one's attention, focus, or aim closely toward a specific target
items.ex_en: Auditors zeroed in on the unusual wire transfers during the preliminary inquiry.
items.ex_zh: 审计员在初步调查期间把全部注意力锁定在那些异常的电汇上。

items.def_en: Hold someone's attention, eyes, or mental focus completely and firmly
items.ex_en: The tragic monologue riveted the silent theater audience to their seats completely.
items.ex_zh: 那段悲怆的独白深深吸引住剧场内静默的观众，令他们目不转睛。

items.def_zh: 使全神贯注，吸引；正式誊写（公文等）
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To hold someone's attention completely so they notice nothing else. 2. (law) To write out an official document in large, clear handwriting.
items.ex_en: The intricate philosophical debate engrossed the visiting scholars for many quiet hours.
items.ex_zh: 这场深奥的哲学辩论让来访的学者们全神贯注地沉浸了数小时。

items.def_zh: 全神贯注于，念念不忘；凝视，注视；使固定
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/upon) To focus your attention or obsession exclusively on one person, idea, or object. 2. To direct your eyes steadily toward something. 3. To make something fixed or stable.
items.ex_en: The troubled youth began to fixate upon the bizarre symbol on the wall.
items.ex_zh: 那个心神不宁的年轻人开始对墙上奇异的符号念念不忘。
items.ex2_en: Deep-seated childhood trauma can easily fixate a person's emotional development at an early stage.
items.ex2_zh: 根深蒂固的童年创伤很容易使一个人的情感发展停滞在早期阶段。

items.def_en: [T/I] Continually preoccupy or intrude upon the mind abnormally to the exclusion of other thoughts
items.ex_en: Dark premonitions of impending failure obsessed the young composer throughout the night.
items.ex_zh: 对即将到来的失败的灰暗预感整夜折磨着这位年轻的作曲家。
items.ex2_en: Many perfectionists obsess over minor details when preparing their final research presentations.
items.ex2_zh: 许多完美主义者在准备最终的研究展示时会对微小的细节过度纠结。

groups.summary_en: This intensity gradient traces mental focus from paying attentive heed to external advice, up to total absorption, and ultimately pathological fixation or unshakeable obsession where all other stimuli are blocked out.
groups.summary_zh: 体现从留意听取、全神贯注到陷入极端执念或牢牢吸引的注意力强度阶梯。
groups.desc_en: Directing cognitive resources toward a specific stimulus along an ascending scale from polite mindfulness to total cognitive capture, contrasting with passive perception (seeing, hearing).
groups.desc_zh: 将认知资源投射于特定刺激，呈现从礼貌留意到彻底入迷的强度递增，区别于被动的无意感知。
groups.nuance_en: heed: prudent, cautionary attentiveness to advice or warnings (warning / advice / counsel) · attend: formal mental application or active listening (lecture / detail / patient) · zero in on: sharp, converging focus onto a specific point or problem (target / flaw / issue) · engross: absorbing one's attention fully to the exclusion of surroundings (reader / thinker / mind) · rivet: paralyzing or locking gaze/attention through sheer fascination or terror (audience / eyes / attention)
groups.nuance_zh: heed: 警惕、审慎地听从劝告或警示 (warning / advice / counsel) · attend: 专注倾听或处理细节 (lecture / detail / patient) · zero in on: 视线或思路高度收敛聚焦于单一点 (target / flaw / issue) · engross: 深度吸引使之完全沉浸其中 (reader / thinker / mind) · rivet: 因极度着迷或震惊而牢牢钉死注意力 (audience / eyes / attention)

groups.name: Attire & Clothe · 穿戴与盛装 (Attire, Tog, Bonnet)
groups.tip: 穿戴衣物盛装打扮的过程

items.def_en: (+ sb) to dress someone or oneself warmly in layers of clothing
items.ex_en: Mother told the kids to bundle up warmly before venturing into the blizzard.
items.ex_zh: 母亲嘱咐孩子们在踏入暴风雪之前先把自己裹得严严实实。
items.ex2_en: The mother bundled up her shivering child in a thick woolen blanket.
items.ex2_zh: 母亲用厚厚的毛毯把颤抖的孩子紧紧裹好。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to put on formal, fancy, or special clothing
items.ex_en: You don't need to dress up; casual clothes are fine for the party.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要盛装打扮，去参加聚会穿便装就行。
items.ex2_en: She decided to dress up the plain dining table with colorful flowers.
items.ex2_zh: 她决定用色彩斑斓的鲜花将朴素的餐桌装饰一番。

items.def_zh: 穿上套装或特定防护服/队服
items.def_en: to put on a business suit, uniform, or special gear suited for an activity
items.ex_en: The firefighters quickly suited up in heavy protective gear before entering the blaze.
items.ex_zh: 消防员在冲入火海前迅速穿上了厚重的专用防护服。

items.def_en: 1. (dated) To put a bonnet or hat on someone's head.
items.ex_en: The nurse gently bonneted the fragile infant before taking her into the courtyard.
items.ex_zh: 护士在把虚弱的婴儿抱进庭院前，轻柔地为她戴上了小童帽。

items.def_zh: 给……穿上衣服，装扮（常与out或up连用）
items.def_en: (also 'tog out') (informal) To dress someone or oneself in particular or smart clothes.
items.ex_en: They tog out in their finest velvet suits for the annual gala dinner.
items.ex_zh: 他们穿上最精致的丝绒西装，精心装扮前往参加年度盛宴。

items.def_en: (+ in) to fit or equip someone with a complete set of distinctive clothes
items.ex_en: The theatrical costumer rigged out the actors in elaborate eighteenth-century period costumes.
items.ex_zh: 剧团服装师给演员们换上了精致考究的十八世纪成套戏服。

items.def_en: to put on a piece of clothing, hat, or coat (formal or literary)
items.ex_en: The magistrate solemnly donned his ceremonial black robes before entering the courtroom.
items.ex_zh: 法官在步入法庭前庄重地穿上了仪典黑色长袍。

items.def_zh: 使穿衣，打扮（通常用于被动语态）
items.def_en: 1. (often passive, 'be attired') (formal) To dress someone in a particular, especially fine or formal, style of clothes.
items.ex_en: The royal ambassador was attired in sumptuous silk garments for the reception.
items.ex_zh: 皇家大使身着华丽的丝绸服饰出席了这场招待会。

items.def_zh: 盛装打扮；打扮得花枝招展
items.def_en: (+ in/with) to dress or decorate someone or oneself in a very striking, festive manner
items.ex_en: The townspeople decked themselves out in bright ribbons for the summer carnival parade.
items.ex_zh: 镇民们系上鲜艳的丝带，盛装打扮以参加夏季嘉年华游行。

items.def_en: (+ in) to dress someone in fine, elaborate, or regal clothing (archaic/literary)
items.ex_en: The proud monarch stood magnificently arrayed in purple velvet and shimmering gold.
items.ex_zh: 那位威严的君主身着紫丝绒与闪亮金饰的华服，气度不凡地站立着。

groups.summary_en: An agent puts clothes, hats, or specific ceremonial finery on themselves or another person, typically indicating stylistic distinction, archaic register, or dressing for an occasion.
groups.summary_zh: 给自身或他人穿戴衣冠，多侧重正式穿戴、特定服饰或特殊打扮风格。
groups.desc_en: Putting on garments or dressing someone, often with an emphasis on decorative, formal, or specialized outerwear, contrasting with the basic physiological act of donning everyday clothes.
groups.desc_zh: 穿戴衣物或为他人更衣，多强调外饰性、庄重性或特定仪式装备，区别于日常中性的穿衣动作。
groups.nuance_en: don: formal or literary act of putting on an item (coat / hat / mantle) · attire: dressing elegantly or officially in elaborate clothing (guests / monarch / corpse) · bundle up: wrapping thickly in warm layers against the cold (children / commuter / baby) · rig out: outfitting in unusual, specialized, or conspicuous costume (crew / performer / ship) · suit up: donning specialized uniform or protective gear for action (athlete / astronaut / soldier)
groups.nuance_zh: don: 文雅正式地穿上特定服饰或披风 (coat / hat / mantle) · attire: 盛装打扮或给某人穿上正式礼服 (guests / monarch / corpse) · bundle up: 严密包裹厚重御寒衣物 (children / commuter / baby) · rig out: 配备奇特、特殊或引人注目的服饰装备 (crew / performer / ship) · suit up: 为执行任务而穿戴专业制服或防护服 (athlete / astronaut / soldier)

groups.name: Attribute Fault & Accuse · 归咎与指控 (Blame, Reproach, Accuse)
groups.tip: 追究责任与严厉批评指责

items.def_en: (+ sth + on sb) to attribute fault, blame, or an accusation to a specific person
items.ex_en: The manager attempted to lay the blame for the blunder on interns.
items.ex_zh: 经理企图把这次疏失的责任推到实习生身上。

items.def_en: (+ sth + on sb) to attribute blame, responsibility, or a crime to someone
items.ex_en: The corrupt officer tried to pin the botched robbery on an innocent bystander.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败的警官企图把那起拙劣的抢劫罪名栽赃给无辜的路人。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to accuse someone publicly of being responsible for a fault or wrongdoing
items.ex_en: Frustrated residents pointed the finger at the mayor for the worsening transit crisis.
items.ex_zh: 沮丧的居民公开把日益恶化的交通危机归咎于市长。

items.def_en: To hold someone or something responsible for a fault, failure, or negative outcome; to criticize.
items.ex_en: Many economists blame deregulation for the unprecedented collapse of the local housing market.
items.ex_zh: 许多经济学家将当地房地产市场的空前崩溃归咎于放松管制。

items.def_en: To state that someone has done something wrong, improper, or illegal.
items.ex_en: The prosecutor formally accused the rogue executive of embezzling millions in company funds.
items.ex_zh: 检察官正式指控这位变节的高管侵吞了数百万公司的资金。

items.def_en: to express sharp, stern disapproval or criticism of someone's actions
items.ex_en: The board chairman sternly rebuked the director for leaking proprietary financial data.
items.ex_zh: 董事会主席因主管泄露专有财务数据而严厉训斥了他。

items.def_en: To criticize or express disappointment to someone for failing to do something or doing something wrong.
items.ex_en: She reproached her careless brother for forgetting their elderly mother's milestone birthday.
items.ex_zh: 她责备粗心的弟弟忘记了年迈母亲的重要生日。

items.def_en: (+ with) to publicly or legally state that someone has committed a crime
items.ex_en: Federal agents charged the rogue financier with multiple counts of wire fraud yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 联邦特工昨天以多项电汇欺诈罪名正式指控了这名不法金融家。

items.def_en: to criticize someone or something severely in a formal, official statement
items.ex_en: The ethics committee voted unanimously to censure the lawmaker for improper behavior.
items.ex_zh: 道德委员会一致投票决定正式谴责该立法者的不当行为。

items.def_en: to formally charge a public official with high crimes or misconduct
items.ex_en: Parliament prepared to impeach the corrupt president for high crimes against the state.
items.ex_zh: 议会准备就危害国家的重罪弹劾这位腐败的总统。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate holding someone accountable for a wrong, error, or offense, graduating from attribution of fault (blame), moral disappointment (reproach), to formal adversarial accusation (accuse, charge).
groups.summary_zh: 将过错或罪责归于某人，由责任推诿渐升至当面责备与正式指控。
groups.desc_en: Ascribing moral, administrative, or legal culpability for a fault to a person along an intensifying scale of gravity and formality, contrasting with objective causal attribution.
groups.desc_zh: 将过失的道德、行政或法律责任归咎于特定主体，具有层级渐增的正式性与严重性，区别于客观的因果解释。
groups.nuance_en: blame: holding responsible internally or interpersonally for an error (driver / victim / weather) · reproach: rebuking someone sorrowfully for failing moral/emotional expectations (friend / partner / colleague) · accuse: direct, overt declaration that someone has committed a wrong (suspect / rival / cheat) · charge: formal, institutional allegation of legal or systemic offense (suspect / official / defendant) · pin on: transferring blame unfairly or manipulatively onto a scapegoat (subordinate / crime / rap)
groups.nuance_zh: blame: 认知或人际上把过错归咎于某人 (driver / victim / weather) · reproach: 带着失望或委屈责备某人未尽道义 (friend / partner / colleague) · accuse: 当面公开指认某人有过错或罪行 (suspect / rival / cheat) · charge: 司法或机构层面正式提起公诉或指控 (suspect / official / defendant) · pin on: 嫁祸、栽赃或强加罪名于替罪羊 (subordinate / crime / rap)

groups.name: Awkward Fall & Loss of Balance · 失足与跌倒 (Stumble, Flop, Tumble)
groups.tip: 失去平衡倒下或翻滚摔落

items.def_en: to lose balance accidentally and collapse or drop to the ground
items.ex_en: The tired skater slipped on the wet patch and fell down heavily.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的滑冰者踩在湿滑的水迹上，重重地摔倒在地。

items.def_en: to slide unintentionally and lose one's footing
items.ex_en: Someone in the accounting department must have slipped up.
items.ex_zh: 财务部肯定有人粗心犯了错。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to catch one's foot on something and stumble or fall awkwardly
items.ex_en: The courier tripped over a stray electrical cable stretched across the busy corridor.
items.ex_zh: 信使被横拉在繁忙走廊里的一根杂乱电线给绊倒了。

items.def_en: (+ over/on) to catch one's foot on something and stumble or fall
items.ex_en: She tripped on the uneven stone stairs and scraped her right knee.
items.ex_zh: 她在凹凸不平的石阶上失足绊倒，擦伤了右膝盖。
items.ex2_en: A loose wire across the busy corridor tripped several unsuspecting office workers today.
items.ex2_zh: 穿过繁忙走廊的一根松动电线今天绊倒了好几位毫无防备的办公室员工。

items.def_zh: 绊倒，跌跌撞撞地走；结巴，犯错
items.def_en: 1. to trip and almost fall while walking or running; walk unsteadily 2. to make mistakes or pause hesitantly in speaking
items.ex_en: He stumbled over the hidden tree root while running through the dark forest.
items.ex_zh: 他在穿过幽暗森林奔跑时被隐藏的树根绊得跌跌撞撞。

items.def_zh: 沉重地落下，笨拙地下跌（或坐下、躺下）；彻底失败，砸锅
items.def_en: 1. to fall, drop, or sit down heavily and awkwardly 2. (informal) to fail completely
items.ex_en: Exhausted after the marathon, she flopped into the nearest armchair without speaking.
items.ex_zh: 跑完马拉松精疲力竭的她一言不发，扑通瘫坐在最近的扶手椅里。

items.def_zh: 跌倒，翻滚摔下；暴跌，骤降
items.def_en: 1. to fall quickly and without control; roll or topple downward 2. to drop rapidly in amount, value, or rate
items.ex_en: Loose boulders tumbled down the steep hillside after the sudden torrential rainstorm.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的暴风雨过后，松动的巨石从陡峭的山坡上滚落下来。

items.def_en: to become unsteady and fall down from a standing or upright position
items.ex_en: The tall stack of delicate porcelain bowls toppled onto the tiled floor.
items.ex_zh: 那一高摞精致的瓷碗摇晃着倾覆倒在瓷砖地板上。
items.ex2_en: A sudden gust of wind toppled the precarious ladder against the wooden fence.
items.ex2_zh: 一阵突如其来的狂风吹倒了靠在木栅栏上的不稳固梯子。

items.def_en: (+ down) to sit down or drop heavily and suddenly, usually from fatigue
items.ex_en: She plumped down on the sofa with a heavy sigh after work.
items.ex_zh: 下班后，她带着沉重的叹息扑通一声瘫坐在沙发上。

items.def_en: to fall down suddenly because of a loss of strength, support, or consciousness
items.ex_en: The dehydrated runner suddenly collapsed onto the track just yards from the finish.
items.ex_zh: 脱水的赛跑选手在离终点仅几米远的地方突然瘫倒在跑道上。
items.ex2_en: The demolition crew collapsed the abandoned warehouse using several controlled explosive charges.
items.ex2_zh: 拆除队使用几处定向爆破炸药放倒了那座废弃仓库。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict people or things losing balance and descending clumsily, rolling headlong, or dropping heavily without physical grace.
groups.summary_zh: 描述身体失衡后踉跄失控、跌滚或沉重瘫倒的笨拙下坠动作。
groups.desc_en: Losing physical equilibrium involuntarily through foot obstructions, slick surfaces, or muscle failure, contrasting with deliberate lowering or graceful diving.
groups.desc_zh: 因脚步受阻、地面湿滑或身体脱力而被迫失去平衡倒地，区别于有意的伏低或优雅下潜。
groups.nuance_en: trip: catching one's foot on an obstacle and pitching forward (wire / root / step) · stumble: striking the foot and taking clumsy, faltering recovery steps (drunkard / hiker / horse) · tumble: chaotic rolling, somersaulting fall down an incline or height (acrobat / child / climber) · topple: losing vertical stability and falling over from the top (statue / tower / regime) · flop: collapsing limply and clumsily from exhaustion or dead weight (exhausted runner / dog / doll)
groups.nuance_zh: trip: 绊到障碍物而前倾失衡 (wire / root / step) · stumble: 磕绊后踉跄蹒跚、险些跌倒 (drunkard / hiker / horse) · tumble: 混乱翻滚着从高处或斜坡跌落 (acrobat / child / climber) · topple: 失去竖直重心而头重脚轻地倾覆 (statue / tower / regime) · flop: 脱力或沉重地噗通瘫倒在地 (exhausted runner / dog / doll)

groups.name: Bar & Expel · 资格剥夺与社交除名 (Exclusion from Groups or Status)
groups.tip: 取消资格、除名或孤立排挤

items.def_en: (+ sb) to exclude someone from a group or social activity through deliberate coldness or hostility
items.ex_en: Clingy colleagues deliberately froze out the newcomer by omitting him from group luncheons.
items.ex_zh: 抱团的同事们在集体午餐时故意不带那个新人，从而排挤他。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to force someone to leave an organization, group, or premises permanently
items.ex_en: He was kicked out of the university for repeatedly cheating on exams.
items.ex_zh: 他因多次考试作弊被大学开除。

items.def_zh: 将……除名，把……从名单中划掉；使（股票等）退市
items.def_en: 1. to remove from a list, register, or category. 2. (finance) to remove the shares of a company from a stock exchange so they can no longer be traded there.
items.ex_en: The ancient scribe delisted the disgraced general from the imperial army registry forever.
items.ex_zh: 古老的抄写官将那位蒙羞的将军从帝国军名册中永久除名。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to banish or completely exclude someone from a community or society
items.ex_en: The village elders cast out the treacherous traitor into the desolate barren wilderness.
items.ex_zh: 村里的长老们将那个背信弃义的叛徒放逐到了凄凉荒芜的旷野。

items.def_zh: 剥夺神职资格；开除教籍
items.def_en: to officially deprive a priest or religious minister of ecclesiastical status
items.ex_en: The ecclesiastical council voted decisively to defrock the corrupt bishop for grave heresy.
items.ex_zh: 教会理事会果断投票，因严重的异端行为剥夺了该腐败主教的神职资格。

items.def_en: to remove an authority figure suddenly and forcefully from high office
items.ex_en: Rebel military officers swiftly deposed the despotic ruler in a bloodless midnight coup.
items.ex_zh: 叛军军官在一场不流血的午夜政变中迅速罢黜了专制统治者。

items.def_en: to deliberately exclude, avoid, or banish someone from a group, society, or community.
items.ex_en: The insular community chose to ostracize the whistleblower after the scandal broke out.
items.ex_zh: 丑闻曝光后，这个封闭的社群选择孤立并排斥那名告密者。

items.def_zh: 取消……的律师资格，开除……的律师会会籍
items.def_en: (law) to officially expel a lawyer from the legal profession so they are no longer permitted to practice law.
items.ex_en: The supreme court decided to disbar the attorney following his felony fraud conviction.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院在该律师因重罪欺诈被定罪后，决定取消其律师执业资格。

items.def_zh: 投反对票排挤；拒绝……入会，排斥
items.def_en: to reject or exclude someone from membership in an organization or social club by voting against them.
items.ex_en: Prejudiced board members conspired to blackball the progressive applicant from the prestigious club.
items.ex_zh: 抱有偏见的董事会成员密谋投反对票，将那位思想进步的申请人拒之门外。

items.def_en: to officially exclude someone from participating in the sacraments and services of a religious group
items.ex_en: The bishop declared that the unrepentant heretic would be excommunicated from the church.
items.ex_zh: 主教宣布，这名执迷不悟的异端分子将被逐出教会。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent exclusionary mechanisms whereby a professional body, club, exchange, or community revokes membership or systematically banishes an individual from social participation.
groups.summary_zh: 强调社会共同体、行业协会或交易场所通过投票或法定程序予以除名与联合排斥。
groups.desc_en: Formally or socially expelling an individual from an institution, profession, or community by revoking legitimate status, contrasting with simple physical eviction.
groups.desc_zh: 通过剥夺合法资质或社交断绝，正式或群体性地将某人逐出机构、行业或社群，区别于单纯的物理驱逐。
groups.nuance_en: disbar: legally stripping an attorney of their license to practice (lawyer / attorney / prosecutor) · defrock: canonically stripping a cleric of their priestly credentials (priest / bishop / minister) · ostracize: collective social exclusion, shunning, and cold-shouldering (dissident / pariah / newcomer) · delist: removing a security or entity from an official exchange or register (company / stock / species) · freeze out: systematically isolating someone socially or commercially to force departure (colleague / partner / competitor)
groups.nuance_zh: disbar: 吊销律师执业资格 (lawyer / attorney / prosecutor) · defrock: 剥夺教士的神职身份或圣职 (priest / bishop / minister) · ostracize: 群体性排挤、孤立并切断社交往来 (dissident / pariah / newcomer) · delist: 官方取消上市公司交易资格或除名名录 (company / stock / species) · freeze out: 采用冷遇或排挤手段迫使某人退出 (colleague / partner / competitor)

groups.name: Belittle & Disparage · 贬低与轻视 (Belittle, Disparage, Demean)
groups.tip: 故意压低评价，轻视他人价值与成果

items.def_en: (+ from) to disparage or detract from a person's character, merits, or authority
items.ex_en: Nothing in these subsequent findings can derogate from her established reputation as an upright judge.
items.ex_zh: 随后的这些调查发现丝毫无损于她作为正直法官的既有声誉。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to criticize someone in a way that makes them feel small, foolish, or unimportant
items.ex_en: He constantly put down his colleagues during meetings just to inflate his own ego.
items.ex_zh: 他开会时总是贬低同事，仅仅是为了满足自己的虚荣心。

items.def_zh: 用居高临下的口气对……说话
items.def_en: (+ sb) to speak to someone condescendingly as though they are inferior or less intelligent
items.ex_en: Stop talking down to me as if I know nothing about this computer system.
items.ex_zh: 别用居高临下的语气跟我说话，好像我对这套电脑系统一无所知似的。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to criticize, belittle, or disparage someone or something persistently
items.ex_en: She spends half her workday running down her rivals behind their backs.
items.ex_zh: 她大半个工作日都在背后说竞争对手的坏话。

items.def_en: To make something seem less important, serious, or valuable than it really is.
items.ex_en: The spokesperson attempted to downplay the severity of the financial crisis during the briefing.
items.ex_zh: 发言人在简报会上试图淡化这场金融危机的严重性。

items.def_en: To make someone or their achievements seem unimportant, small, or worthless.
items.ex_en: A good manager should never belittle the honest efforts of their team members.
items.ex_zh: 一名优秀的管理者绝不应贬低团队成员所付出的真诚努力。

items.def_en: To lower someone's dignity, respect, or standing; to demean oneself by acting beneath one's dignity.
items.ex_en: The politician refused to demean himself by engaging in petty personal attacks.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客拒绝通过参与琐碎的人身攻击来贬低自己的身份。

items.def_en: To speak of someone or something in a disrespectful or critical way that suggests they have little value.
items.ex_en: Critics unfairly disparaged the author's latest novel as derivative and utterly unoriginal.
items.ex_zh: 评论家们不公地贬损这位作家的最新小说，称其毫无新意且完全抄袭。

items.def_zh: 诋毁；恶意贬低（名誉或价值）
items.def_en: to criticize unfairly or disparage someone's reputation, value, or achievements
items.ex_en: Slanderous campaigns were orchestrated specifically to denigrate the minister's distinguished military career.
items.ex_zh: 有人精心策划了诽谤行动，专门诋毁部长卓越的军旅生涯。

items.def_zh: 贬低；轻视（功劳或重要性）
items.def_en: to represent something as being of little worth or importance; to belittle
items.ex_en: He tended to depreciate his own contributions, attributing the company's success entirely to luck.
items.ex_zh: 他倾向于贬低自己的贡献，将公司的成功完全归功于运气。
items.ex2_en: New luxury vehicles depreciate rapidly in resale value during their first three years.
items.ex2_zh: 新的豪华汽车在头三年内转售价值贬值非常迅速。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey expressing a low opinion of someone or something, minimizing their merit, or degrading their dignity. They range from public rhetorical disparagement and minimizing achievements to degrading personal worth and formal censure.
groups.summary_zh: 通过言辞压低他人或事物的价值、地位或重要性，伴有贬损侮慢色彩。
groups.desc_en: Representing a person, effort, or idea as insignificant, defective, or beneath respect, contrasting with objective criticism or neutral critique.
groups.desc_zh: 将人、成就或观点描绘为微不足道、有缺陷或不齿，旨在矮化贬损，区别于客观批评或公允评估。
groups.nuance_en: belittle: dismissing achievements or traits to make them seem minor (achievement / effort / contribution) · disparage: casting slighting remarks to erode reputation or worth (rival / work / talent) · demean: lowering someone's dignity or status dishonorably (character / office / self) · derogate: formally detracting from or impairing authority, merit, or standing (reputation / right / authority) · talk down to: adopting a patronizing, condescending tone toward someone (employee / audience / child)
groups.nuance_zh: belittle: 刻意把功劳或成就贬为微不足道 (achievement / effort / contribution) · disparage: 用轻蔑言辞贬损声誉或价值 (rival / work / talent) · demean: 玷污人格、拉低身段或尊严 (character / office / self) · derogate: 正式克扣、削损权威或合法价值 (reputation / right / authority) · talk down to: 居高临下、自以为是地训话 (employee / audience / child)

groups.name: Bilateral Consultation & Terms Negotiation · 商讨与条件谈判 (Consult, Negotiate, Renegotiate)
groups.tip: 遇事征询专业意见或共同商定

items.def_zh: 商议，商讨；咨询，请教；查阅，参考
items.def_en: 1. To discuss something with someone in order to reach a decision. 2. To seek information or advice from an expert or reference source.
items.ex_en: The board must consult legal counsel before executing such a high-risk commercial merger.
items.ex_zh: 董事会在执行如此高风险的商业合并前，必须咨询法律顾问。

items.def_zh: 谈判，协商；商定；顺利通过（障碍）
items.def_en: 1. To discuss something formally in order to reach an agreement. 2. To successfully deal with or get past a difficult obstacle or route.
items.ex_en: Diplomats worked tirelessly through the night to negotiate a comprehensive ceasefire agreement.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们通宵达旦地不知疲倦地工作，以协商达成全面的停火协议。

items.def_en: (+ with) to hold talks with an opposing side, especially in warfare, over terms of armistice
items.ex_en: The besieged garrison dispatched an envoy to parley with the enemy commanders.
items.ex_zh: 被围困的守军派出特使与敌方指挥官进行媾和交涉。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to negotiate and reach an agreement or solution after extensive discussion
items.ex_en: Both parties managed to hammer out an acceptable compromise after grueling overnight talks.
items.ex_zh: 经过艰苦的通宵谈判，双方终于敲定了一个双方都能接受的折中方案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to resolve minor problems, disagreements, or details through discussion
items.ex_en: The committee met yesterday afternoon to iron out the remaining contractual details.
items.ex_zh: 委员会于昨天下午开会，以解决合同中剩余的细节问题。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to discuss something thoroughly and passionately until a mutual settlement is reached
items.ex_en: We sat together for hours trying to hash out our ideological differences.
items.ex_zh: 我们坐在一起谈了几个小时，试图充分协商解决我们意识形态上的分歧。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) to discuss prices, conditions, or concessions in order to reach a deal
items.ex_en: Shoppers often bargain with street vendors over antique trinkets in the flea market.
items.ex_zh: 在跳蚤市场里，顾客经常就古玩小饰品与街头摊贩讨价还价。

items.def_en: (+ with) to have formal discussions to exchange opinions or seek advice before deciding
items.ex_en: The chief executive convened to confer with senior advisers about restructuring plans.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官召集会议，就重组计划与高级顾问进行切磋商议。

items.def_en: To discuss the terms of an agreement, contract, or debt again in order to change them.
items.ex_en: The bankrupt company sought to renegotiate repayment terms with its primary creditors.
items.ex_zh: 破产的公司试图与主要债权人重新谈判债务偿还条款。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) to dispute or argue persistently over cost or petty terms
items.ex_en: He wasted twenty minutes haggling over fifty cents at the local fruit stand.
items.ex_zh: 他在当地水果摊上为了五毛钱锱铢必较地讲了二十分钟的价。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures bilateral or multilateral communication aimed at exchanging expert guidance or bargaining toward mutually acceptable contractual terms.
groups.summary_zh: 指双边或多边就协议、条款及专业意见进行磋商博弈与谈判。
groups.desc_en: Engaging in structured or adversarial discourse between opposing parties to resolve discrepancies and secure mutually binding terms, contrasting with unilateral decree or casual talk.
groups.desc_zh: 多方之间进行结构化或博弈性磋商务求弥合分歧并敲定约束性条款，区别于单方面决断或闲聊。
groups.nuance_en: negotiate: formal, strategic bargaining toward a formal agreement (treaty / contract / terms) · hammer out: reaching agreement through arduous, contentious, prolonged effort (deal / compromise / text) · hash out: talking through heated differences candidly until settled (differences / plan / details) · iron out: smoothing over minor remaining hitches or discrepancies (discrepancies / kinks / wrinkles) · confer: exchanging views and pooling counsel before deciding (advisers / attorneys / doctors)
groups.nuance_zh: negotiate: 正式且具策略性地就条款展开谈判 (treaty / contract / terms) · hammer out: 历经艰辛、反复争执后敲定协议 (deal / compromise / text) · hash out: 坦诚且热烈地逐条讨论解决分歧 (differences / plan / details) · iron out: 消除、抹平最后残留的细微摩擦或瑕疵 (discrepancies / kinks / wrinkles) · confer: 协商、碰头、共商对策以交换意见 (advisers / attorneys / doctors)

groups.name: Bind & Bundle · 捆扎与包扎 (Bundle & Fasten with Flexible Material)
groups.tip: 用绳带束紧包裹并固定成捆

items.def_en: (+ sth) to gather items together and tie or wrap them into a compact bundle
items.ex_en: She bundled up the old newspapers and carried them to the recycling bin.
items.ex_zh: 她把旧报纸捆成一包，然后搬到了回收桶旁。
items.ex2_en: We must bundle up warmly before going outside into the freezing winter blizzard.
items.ex2_zh: 在走入严寒的冬日暴风雪之前，我们必须把自己穿得暖和厚实。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to bind or secure objects tightly together using cord, rope, or string
items.ex_en: Most of his capital is tied up in long-term real estate investments.
items.ex_zh: 他的大部分资金都被长期房地产投资套住了。

items.def_zh: 捆扎，扎成包；把……匆忙打发走
items.def_en: 1. (+ up/together) To tie or wrap multiple items tightly together into a bundle. 2. (+ into/off) To push or hurry someone quickly somewhere.
items.ex_en: The workers bundled several wooden stakes together before loading them onto the truck.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在把几根木桩装上卡车之前将它们紧紧捆扎在一起。

items.def_zh: 用绳索捆扎；将（木柴）堆扎成考得
items.def_en: To tie or fasten something securely with a cord; to stack cut firewood in measured cords.
items.ex_en: The lumberjack helped cord the freshly split oak neatly beside the shed.
items.ex_zh: 伐木工人帮忙把新劈开的橡木整齐地堆扎在棚屋旁。

items.def_en: to wrap someone, especially a baby, tightly in garments or cloths
items.ex_en: The nurse gently swaddled the newborn infant in a soft cotton blanket.
items.ex_zh: 护士用柔软的棉毯轻轻地将新生婴儿包裹严实。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to wrap tightly or secure firmly with bandages, cords, or strips
items.ex_en: The paramedic carefully bound up the deep wound to stem the bleeding.
items.ex_zh: 医护人员小心地包扎好深伤口以止血。

items.def_en: to tie or wrap something securely with rope, wire, or ribbon
items.ex_en: He used sturdy twine to bind the heavy packages securely for overseas shipment.
items.ex_zh: 他用结实的麻绳将沉重的包裹牢固捆扎好，以便海外运输。

items.def_zh: 用带子捆扎，束牢；用绷带包扎
items.def_en: (+ to/down/into) To fasten, secure, or bind someone or something in place with a strap or belt.
items.ex_en: Please ensure you strap the heavy generator down securely before driving off.
items.ex_zh: 开车离开前，请务必用带子把那台笨重的发电机牢牢束牢。

items.def_en: to press and bind materials (such as hay, cotton, or paper) into a tight, rectangular block
items.ex_en: Modern machinery allows farmers to bale cut alfalfa within just a few hours.
items.ex_zh: 现代机械使农民能够在短短几个小时内将割下的苜蓿打包成捆。

items.def_en: to tie up the wings and legs of a fowl before cooking, or to bind someone tightly so they cannot move
items.ex_en: The chef demonstrated how to truss the turkey with kitchen twine before roasting.
items.ex_zh: 大厨演示了在烘烤前如何用厨房用线紧紧绑住火鸡。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote gathering items together and securing or wrapping them into a cohesive unit using flexible materials like rope, cords, straps, or bands. They contrast in the type of fastening medium used and the neatness or purpose of the packaging.
groups.summary_zh: 用绳、带或包材将散物聚拢并紧固成包或束。
groups.desc_en: Constricting, wrapping, or grouping objects into a compact unit using flexible binders like cord, cloth, or straps, contrasting with rigid fastening (bolting, nailing).
groups.desc_zh: 使用绳索、布匹或绑带等柔性材料将物体包缠或聚集固定为紧凑单元，区别于刚性机械紧固（如螺栓连接）。
groups.nuance_en: bind: constricting or holding firmly with a encircling band or cord (wound / prisoner / package) · swaddle: wrapping infants snugly in bands of cloth for warmth/restraint (baby / newborn / limbs) · bundle: collecting separate items loosely together into a parcel (sticks / documents / clothes) · strap: securing firmly in place using heavy flexible webbing or leather belts (luggage / gurney / pack) · cord: binding securely with rough string or cordage (bundle / wood / box)
groups.nuance_zh: bind: 用绳带紧紧捆住或包扎 (wound / prisoner / package) · swaddle: 用布条紧裹婴儿以保暖或限动 (baby / newborn / limbs) · bundle: 将散碎物杂凑捆扎或打成一包 (sticks / documents / clothes) · strap: 用皮革或织带将物品勒紧固定 (luggage / gurney / pack) · cord: 用粗绳线捆绑结实 (bundle / wood / box)

groups.name: Bind & Fasten · 捆绑与固定 (Fasten, Lash & Tape)
groups.tip: 用绳索或束带绑牢固定

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fasten or secure something flatly against a surface using adhesive tape
items.ex_en: Technicians taped down loose electrical cables across the auditorium floor to prevent tripping.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员用胶带将礼堂地面上松散的电缆粘住固定，以防绊倒人。

items.def_en: to fasten, join, or seal something using adhesive tape
items.ex_en: She taped the cardboard parcel thoroughly so nothing would fall out during transit.
items.ex_zh: 她用胶带把纸板包裹封得严严实实，以免运输过程中掉出东西。

items.def_en: To bind branches, sticks, or twigs tightly into a bundle.
items.ex_en: Foresters fagoted dry twigs into dense bundles to provide fuel for winter hearths.
items.ex_zh: 林务员将干燥的细枝紧紧扎成柴捆，为冬日的壁炉提供燃料。

items.def_zh: 用透明胶带粘住，用胶带封贴
items.def_en: (chiefly British) To stick, fasten, or mend something using clear adhesive tape.
items.ex_en: He quickly sellotaped the torn page back into his reference manual before class.
items.ex_zh: 上课前，他赶紧用透明胶带把被撕破的那页粘回了参考手册中。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to secure or immobilize an object firmly in place using straps
items.ex_en: We strapped down the rooftop cargo carefully to withstand strong highway winds.
items.ex_zh: 我们用绑带小心地系紧车顶货物，以抵御高速公路上的强风。

items.def_en: to tie an animal or object with a rope or chain to restrict its movement within a certain area
items.ex_en: The farmer tethered his restless goat to a sturdy fence post in the meadow.
items.ex_zh: 农夫把躁动不安的山羊拴在草地上一根坚固的栅栏柱上。

items.def_zh: 把绳索拴在系绳木上；保护系牢
items.def_en: [I/T] to secure a rope around a pin or cleat, or to secure a climber with a rope
items.ex_en: The experienced mountaineer carefully belayed his partner as she traversed the sheer cliff.
items.ex_zh: 当女搭档横穿陡峭的悬崖时，经验丰富的老登山员小心地为她打绳保护系牢。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to tie something down tightly and securely using heavy ropes or cables
items.ex_en: Sailors worked hurriedly to lash down loose deck gear before the gale hit.
items.ex_zh: 在大风暴来临之前，水手们匆忙用绳索将甲板上松散的器械牢牢系紧。

items.def_en: to fasten or secure something firmly with a rope, cord, or chain, especially on a ship or vehicle
items.ex_en: Crew members lashed the shipping container to the vessel frame with steel cables.
items.ex_zh: 船员们用钢缆将集装箱牢牢绑系在船体框架上。

items.def_en: (nautical) To bind, lash, or wrap ropes tightly around something to secure or strengthen it.
items.ex_en: The crew frapped heavy cables around the damaged hull to prevent catastrophic flooding.
items.ex_zh: 船员们用粗缆紧扎受损的船体四周，以防发生灾难性进水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify specialized mechanical techniques for securing, immobilizing, or joining objects using adhesive strips, tightly wound nautical ropes, or binding twigs/faggots together. They differ markedly by technical domain and binding instrument.
groups.summary_zh: 采用胶带粘贴、绳缆盘紧或扎捆等特定手段固定物品。
groups.desc_en: Securing an object firmly to an anchor or surface using adhesive tape, ropes, or anchors to prevent displacement, contrasting with free coupling or loose joining.
groups.desc_zh: 利用胶带、索具或系绳将物体牢牢固定在基底或锚点上以防位移，区别于松散连接或自由挂靠。
groups.nuance_en: lash down: securing cargo or tarps firmly to a deck with crisscrossed rope (cargo / boat / equipment) · tether: tying an animal or vessel to a central fixed anchor with limited range (horse / balloon / goat) · tape down: sticking an object flat to a surface using adhesive strips (cables / edges / flaps) · belay: securing a climber or boat by looping rope around a pin/rock (climber / rope / vessel) · strap down: immobilizing an object firmly onto a bed or rack using ratchet belts (freight / patient / load)
groups.nuance_zh: lash down: 用绳索纵横交错地将物资紧绑在甲板或台架上 (cargo / boat / equipment) · tether: 拴系牲口或器物并保留有限活动范围 (horse / balloon / goat) · tape down: 用胶布将物件平整粘贴固定在地面或表面上 (cables / edges / flaps) · belay: 攀岩或航海中利用绳索环绕支点设保护固定 (climber / rope / vessel) · strap down: 用捆绑带牢牢勒紧固定在运输托盘或车床 (freight / patient / load)

groups.name: Botch, Ruin & Mutilate · 弄糟、毁损与残破 (Botch, Goof, Mutilate)
groups.tip: 结构松散或遭外力毁损

items.def_en: (chiefly British) to develop a vertical line of unraveled stitches in tights or stockings, or cause this to happen.
items.ex_en: She cursed under her breath when she noticed her brand-new silk stockings laddered.
items.ex_zh: 当发现崭新的丝袜抽丝脱线时，她忍不住低声咒骂了一句。
items.ex2_en: Rough wooden benches quickly laddered her delicate sheer tights during the afternoon lecture.
items.ex2_zh: 下午听讲座时，粗糙的木凳很快把她轻薄精致的连裤袜刮脱丝了。

items.def_zh: 弄糟，搞砸；出差错；混日子，闲荡
items.def_en: (informal) (often goof up) to make a silly mistake or ruin something; (goof off/around) to waste time lazily.
items.ex_en: The inexperienced clerk goofed and sent confidential tax files to the wrong client.
items.ex_zh: 缺乏经验的办事员出了大差错，把机密税务文件寄错了客户。

items.def_en: (+ sth) bungle or ruin something through incompetence or a mistake
items.ex_en: A sudden software glitch fouled up the entire inventory tracking system yesterday morning.
items.ex_zh: 昨天上午，突发的软件故障把整个库存追踪系统彻底搞砸了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) bungle, ruin, or spoil a situation, plan, or physical object
items.ex_en: Careless scheduling will completely mess up the filming itinerary for the whole crew.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的排期安排会彻底打乱并搞砸全剧组的拍摄行程。

items.def_en: (+ sth) completely spoil, bungle, or make a severe mistake in something
items.ex_en: He really screwed up that critical sales pitch by forgetting the key figures.
items.ex_zh: 他把那场至关重要的销售推介彻底搞砸了，因为他把关键数据忘了个精光。

items.def_en: (often botch up) to ruin or spoil a task, job, or piece of work through clumsiness or carelessness.
items.ex_en: An amateur builder botched the bathroom renovation, leaving pipes that leaked immediately.
items.ex_zh: 一个外行施工人员把浴室装修搞砸了，留下的水管随即发生漏水。

items.def_en: to carry out a task clumsily, incompetently, or carelessly, leading to complete failure
items.ex_en: The local authorities bungled the rescue operation through terrible miscommunication and delays.
items.ex_zh: 由于极度糟糕的沟通不畅和拖延，地方当局拙劣地搞砸了救援行动。

items.def_en: to spoil, demolish, or reduce an object, project, or state to an unusable condition
items.ex_en: Unseasonal frost threatened to ruin the entire apple harvest across the valley.
items.ex_zh: 不合时令的霜冻极有可能毁掉整座山谷的苹果收成。

items.def_zh: 严重损毁，毁损；残害，使残废；使残缺不全
items.def_en: to damage an object, body, or text severely by cutting, tearing, or destroying essential parts.
items.ex_en: Vandals entered the historic chapel overnight and mutilated several irreplaceable marble statues.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子连夜潜入这座历史悠久的小教堂，严重损毁了几尊无可替代的大理石雕像。

items.def_zh: 撕扯得血肉模糊，压碎损坏
items.def_en: to sever, twist, or tear severe portions off an object or limb so it is unrecognizable
items.ex_en: The high-speed collision mangled both vehicles beyond any possibility of immediate repair.
items.ex_zh: 那场高速碰撞将两辆车压撞得严重损毁变形，毫无现场修复的可能。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this intensity-graded frame characterize human failure that ruins an endeavor, material, or organism—scaling from minor blunders and unraveling textures (e.g., runs in tights) to catastrophic bungling and violent physical disfigurement of living bodies or texts.
groups.summary_zh: 从工作失误弄砸递增至严重残害、割损肢体或整体毁坏。
groups.desc_en: Ruining an undertaking, object, or mechanism through gross incompetence, clumsy execution, or destructive blundering, contrasting with planned dismantling or honest error.
groups.desc_zh: 因手法粗劣、愚笨笨拙或严重失职而把任务、器物弄糟毁损，区别于依规拆解或诚实过失。
groups.nuance_en: botch: ruining a task or item through shoddy, clumsy execution (repair / job / surgery) · bungle: mishandling a complex operation through ineptitude and confusion (investigation / heist / rollout) · goof: informal slip-up or blunder caused by carelessness (cue / line / chance) · ruin: causing irreversible loss of function, beauty, or viability (reputation / painting / chance) · mess up: colloquially throwing order or success into disarray (schedule / relationship / project)
groups.nuance_zh: botch: 因手艺粗糙拙劣而把活计搞砸 (repair / job / surgery) · bungle: 因愚笨笨拙而搞乱重大行动或调查 (investigation / heist / rollout) · goof: 因马虎大意而犯下愚蠢小错或搞砸机会 (cue / line / chance) · ruin: 彻底破坏毁损使之丧失原有价值或机能 (reputation / painting / chance) · mess up: 口语中把秩序、方案或关系搞得一团糟 (schedule / relationship / project)

groups.name: Breed, Procreate & Cross-Fertilize · 生育、交配与杂交繁衍 (Breed & Procreate)
groups.tip: 杂交繁育与孵化繁衍后代

items.def_zh: 通过选择育种消除（某特征）
items.def_en: (+ sth) Eliminate an undesirable trait in animals or plants through selective breeding
items.ex_en: Agronomists have successfully bred out susceptibility to fungal blight in modern wheat.
items.ex_zh: 农学家已通过选择育种成功消除了现代小麦对真菌枯萎病的易感性。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Breed or hybridize an animal or plant with another variety or species
items.ex_en: Botanists crossed the wild orchid with a hardy cultivar to enhance frost resistance.
items.ex_zh: 植物学家将野生兰花与一种耐寒品种杂交，以增强其抗霜冻能力。

items.def_en: to reproduce sexually or produce offspring through controlled selection
items.ex_en: Many specialized ranchers breed thoroughbred horses specifically for competitive championship racing.
items.ex_zh: 许多专业牧场主专门培育纯种马，用于参加锦标赛竞速。
items.ex2_en: Many migratory birds breed along these coastal marshes during the warm spring months.
items.ex2_zh: 许多候鸟在温暖的春季月份里沿着这些沿海沼泽繁衍后代。

items.def_zh: 孵出，孵化；密谋，策划（计划或阴谋）
items.def_en: 1. To break out of an egg, or to cause an egg to break open and produce young. 2. To secretly invent and plan a plot or scheme.
items.ex_en: Conspirators met in secret cellars to hatch a daring rebellion against the crown.
items.ex_zh: 密谋者在秘密地下室碰头，策划一场反抗王权的惊人叛乱。

items.def_en: to multiply or reproduce organisms, especially plants, through seeds or cuttings
items.ex_en: Horticulturists propagate delicate tropical shrubs primarily through stem cuttings in specialized greenhouses.
items.ex_zh: 园艺学家主要在专用温室中通过茎扦插繁殖娇贵的温带灌木。
items.ex2_en: Sound waves propagate through water much faster than they do through ambient air.
items.ex2_zh: 声波在水中的传播速度远快于在周围空气中的传播速度。

items.def_en: to breed or cause to breed with an animal or plant of another species or variety
items.ex_en: These two distinct bird species rarely interbreed when their native habitats overlap.
items.ex_zh: 当原生栖息地重叠时，这两种不同的鸟类也极少发生异种交配。
items.ex2_en: Botanists deliberately interbreed wild orchids with greenhouse varieties to produce hardier blossoms.
items.ex2_zh: 植物学家特意将野生兰花与温室品种进行杂交，以培育出更耐寒的花朵。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To reproduce and produce biological offspring.
items.ex_en: Certain rare mammalian species struggle to procreate successfully while kept in prolonged captivity.
items.ex_zh: 某些稀有哺乳动物在长期圈养环境中往往难以成功繁殖后代。

items.def_en: to produce or cause to produce hybrids by crossbreeding; to combine different elements
items.ex_en: Agricultural scientists hybridize domestic grain varieties to create strains capable of resisting drought.
items.ex_zh: 农业科学家将国内谷物品种杂交，培育出能够耐受干旱的品系。
items.ex2_en: These two closely related frog populations readily hybridize along the river valley boundary.
items.ex2_zh: 这两个亲缘关系密切的青蛙种群在河谷交界处极易发生杂交。

items.def_en: to breed or cause to breed with a different species or variety of animal or plant
items.ex_en: Livestock farmers frequently crossbreed beef cattle to optimize meat quality and heat tolerance.
items.ex_zh: 畜牧农民经常将肉牛杂交培育，以优化肉质和耐热性能。
items.ex2_en: Different subspecies of wolves sometimes crossbreed when territories overlap during harsh winters.
items.ex2_zh: 在严冬领地重叠时，不同亚种的狼有时会进行杂交。

items.def_en: (formal/archaic) to father or produce offspring by sexual reproduction
items.ex_en: The elderly patriarch hoped to beget a worthy male heir to inherit his vast estate.
items.ex_zh: 这位年迈的族长希望能生得一名合格的男性子嗣来继承其庞大家业。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses biological reproduction, mating, cross-fertilization, and embryonic emergence. It covers formal procreation, inter-strain and cross-species hybridization, selective breeding, and the hatching of offspring from eggs.
groups.summary_zh: 生物界繁衍后代、卵生孵化、两性交配及品种间杂交繁育。
groups.desc_en: Facilitating, directing, or engaging in biological reproduction, genetic mixing, or deliberate cultivar propagation, contrasting with asexual splitting or generic growth.
groups.desc_zh: 参与、引导或进行生物繁衍、杂交育种或人工培育，区别于无性裂变或通常的生理生长。
groups.nuance_en: breed: selectively mating animals to reproduce and cultivate traits (horses / dogs / livestock) · procreate: biological act of conceiving and producing offspring (human / animals / species) · hybridize: crossing two distinct species or varieties to yield a crossbred organism (plants / strains / roses) · propagate: multiplying plants via cuttings, seeds, or tissue culture (succulent / flora / lineage) · hatch: emerging from an egg or incubating an embryo to emergence (chicks / eggs / conspiracy)
groups.nuance_zh: breed: 人工选择性繁育特定性状的牲畜 (horses / dogs / livestock) · procreate: 生物学意义上的生育、繁衍后代 (human / animals / species) · hybridize: 使不同物种或品系杂交 (plants / strains / roses) · propagate: 扦插、播种或组织培养繁育植物种群 (succulent / flora / lineage) · hatch: 孵化出壳，或雏鸟破壳而出 (chicks / eggs / conspiracy)

groups.name: Bring into Being & Produce · 创造与生成 (Create, Produce, Generate)
groups.tip: 从无到有创造制造出事物

items.def_zh: 制造，做；创造，产生；使成为；迫使
items.def_en: 1. To create, construct, or produce something by combining materials or putting parts together. 2. To cause something to exist, happen, or appear.
items.ex_en: Skilled local artisans make beautiful wooden furniture using traditional hand-carving techniques.
items.ex_zh: 技艺娴熟的当地工匠运用传统手雕技艺制作精美的木制家具。

items.def_zh: 形成，产生；组建，建立；塑造
items.def_en: 1. To begin to exist or cause something to begin to exist or develop. 2. To organize, set up, or establish an organization, committee, or group.
items.ex_en: Volunteers decided to form an independent relief committee following the destructive typhoon.
items.ex_zh: 破坏性台风过后，志愿者们决定组建一个独立的救灾委员会。
items.ex2_en: Thick ice crystals began to form on the cold windowpane overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 厚厚的冰晶一夜之间开始在冰冷的窗玻璃上形成。

items.def_zh: 创造，创作；建立，设立；引起，造成
items.def_en: 1. To bring something new into existence through skill, imagination, or design. 2. To cause a specific situation, feeling, or problem to occur.
items.ex_en: The innovative architect sought to create a completely carbon-neutral office skyscraper.
items.ex_zh: 这位极具创新精神的建筑师试图打造一座完全碳中和的办公摩天大楼。

items.def_en: to bring something into existence through a process, effort, or natural growth
items.ex_en: The newly upgraded assembly line can produce hundreds of electric vehicles every day.
items.ex_zh: 新升级的装配流水线每天能够生产出数百辆电动汽车。

items.def_zh: 产生，创造（利益、结果等）；发电，产生（能量）；引起
items.def_en: 1. To produce or create something, such as ideas, wealth, or power. 2. To cause a particular feeling, reaction, or situation to develop.
items.ex_en: The innovative offshore wind project will generate clean electricity for millions of households.
items.ex_zh: 这个创新的海上风电项目将为数百万家庭产生清洁电力。

items.def_en: (+ sth) cause something to happen or bring a new condition into existence
items.ex_en: The widespread adoption of AI is likely to bring about major changes in the job market.
items.ex_zh: 人工智能的广泛应用可能会给就业市场带来重大变革。

items.def_en: (+ sth) produce or manufacture a quantity of goods or creative works
items.ex_en: The local garment factory can turn out thousands of winter coats each week.
items.ex_zh: 当地那家服装厂每周能够生产出数千件冬装大衣。

items.def_zh: 大量炮制；粗制滥造地生产
items.def_en: (+ sth) produce large quantities of something rapidly and automatically, often with little regard for quality
items.ex_en: The studio continues to churn out cheap romantic comedies every single summer.
items.ex_zh: 这家电影制片厂每年夏天都继续大量炮制廉价的爱情喜剧。

items.def_en: [T/I] to initiate or bring something completely new into being; to start from a particular source
items.ex_en: The innovative curriculum originated from a small educational initiative in rural Scotland.
items.ex_zh: 这一创新课程源自苏格兰农村地区发起的一项微小教育计划。

items.def_zh: 产生，引起（特定状况或感受）
items.def_en: (formal) to cause or give rise to a feeling, situation, or condition
items.ex_en: The controversial tax reform engendered widespread hostility among middle-class taxpayers across the nation.
items.ex_zh: 这项饱受争议的税改在全国中产阶级纳税人中引发了广泛的敌意。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to bringing something new into existence, whether physical, conceptual, or energetic, ranging from general making to systematic generation.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过创造、塑造或系统转化使某事物从无到有地生成。
groups.desc_en: Causing an entity to exist, function, or emerge from raw materials, ideas, or systemic processes, contrasting with merely modifying or moving an existing entity.
groups.desc_zh: 通过原材料、创意构思或系统机制促成新实体的诞生或生成，区别于对既有物体的单纯挪动或修改。
groups.nuance_en: create: originating something unique, original, or aesthetic from nothing (art / world / opportunities) · produce: bringing forth products or media through deliberate fabrication or natural yield (goods / crops / film) · generate: causing an abstract output, energy, or revenue via a systemic engine (power / revenue / interest) · bring about: initiating chains of causality to effect a historical or social change (reform / downfall / peace) · churn out: producing large quantities rapidly, mechanically, and without quality care (novels / content / graduates)
groups.nuance_zh: create: 从无到有地独创出具有审美或独创性的事物 (art / world / opportunities) · produce: 经由加工制造或自然产出产品、作物及作品 (goods / crops / film) · generate: 系统性运转促生能量、收益或数据 (power / revenue / interest) · bring about: 引发因果链条促成社会变革或历史后果 (reform / downfall / peace) · churn out: 机械化、流水线式粗制滥造大批产出 (novels / content / graduates)

groups.name: Bubble & Foam · 起泡与泛沫 (Bubble, Fizz, Froth, Effervesce)
groups.tip: 产生气体或泡沫翻腾

items.def_en: Rise to the surface in or as bubbles
items.ex_en: Tiny air bubbles bubbled up from the mud at the river's edge.
items.ex_zh: 微小的气泡从河边的泥泞中不断冒了出来。

items.def_en: Produce hissing bubbles and become effervescent rapidly
items.ex_en: The cold soda began to fizz up as soon as I added ice.
items.ex_zh: 我一加入冰块，冰凉的汽水就立刻嘶嘶作响地泛起泡沫。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Form or cause to form a mass of small bubbles on the surface of a liquid
items.ex_en: The barista used the steam wand to froth up the warm oat milk.
items.ex_zh: 咖啡师用蒸汽棒使温热的燕麦奶泛起一层细腻的泡沫。
items.ex2_en: Fresh soap suds froth up instantly whenever hot tap water pours forcefully.
items.ex2_zh: 每当热水用力冲下时，新鲜的肥皂泡沫就会瞬间泛起。

items.def_en: (+ with/up) to form or rise in spheres of gas in a liquid
items.ex_en: The aromatic stew started to bubble gently in the heavy cast-iron pot.
items.ex_zh: 香气扑鼻的炖菜在沉重的铸铁锅里开始轻轻冒泡翻滚。

items.def_zh: 起泡并嘶嘶作响；充满活力
items.def_en: (of a liquid) To produce lots of tiny bubbles and make a hissing sound; to effervesce.
items.ex_en: The freshly poured mineral water continued to fizz vigorously inside the crystal flute.
items.ex_zh: 刚倒入的水晶香槟杯里的矿泉水依然激烈地泛着嘶嘶细泡。

items.def_en: to give off small bubbles of gas rapidly and hiss softly, as carbonated liquids do
items.ex_en: The chemical mixture began to effervesce vigorously when hydrochloric acid was introduced.
items.ex_zh: 当加入盐酸时，这种化学混合物便开始剧烈冒泡翻腾。

items.def_en: Produce so many bubbles that the liquid rises and overflows its container
items.ex_en: The boiling strawberry jam will bubble over if you do not lower heat.
items.ex_zh: 如果你不把火调小，滚沸的草莓酱就会冒泡溢出锅外。

items.def_zh: （使）起泡沫，（使）泛起泡沫；充满愤怒
items.def_en: To form or cause a liquid to form a mass of small white bubbles on its surface.
items.ex_en: The agitated sea water began to froth around the jagged offshore rocks.
items.ex_zh: 汹涌的海水在近海嶙峋的礁石周围泛起了一片层层白沫。
items.ex2_en: The energetic cook frothed the egg whites until stiff white peaks appeared.
items.ex2_zh: 精力充沛的厨师打发蛋清，直到出现坚硬的白色泡沫尖角。

items.def_en: to produce a mass of small white bubbles on the surface of a liquid
items.ex_en: The detergent caused the soapy wastewater to foam all over the laundry floor.
items.ex_zh: 洗涤剂导致满含肥皂水的气泡在洗衣房地板上泛起了厚厚一层泡沫。

items.def_en: to create or discharge frothy foam or froth, especially waves or agitated water
items.ex_en: Fierce breakers spumed relentlessly against the ancient granite walls of the harbor.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的巨浪在港口古老的花岗岩防波堤上不断碎成漫天飞沫。

groups.summary_en: Liquids produce, trap, or release gas bubbles, differentiating in physical manifestation from steady internal bubbling ('bubble'), light acoustic carbonation ('fizz', 'effervesce'), to dense surface spume formation ('froth', 'foam').
groups.summary_zh: 液体释放气体或形成泡沫的物理状态，由细微滋滋作响递增至涌出厚重泡沫。
groups.desc_en: Generating and releasing gas vesicles within a liquid or liquid-like medium, manifesting surface turbulence, foam, or audible hiss, contrasting with quiescent boiling or smooth liquid flow.
groups.desc_zh: 在液体内部产生并释放气泡，在表面泛起泡沫或发出嘶嘶声，区别于中性的平稳流动或纯粹静止沸腾。
groups.nuance_en: bubble: forming and bursting gas spheres in a liquid or boiling mass (tar / soup / spring) · fizz: producing a steady, hissing hiss of micro-bubbles (soda / champagne / tablet) · froth: churning into a dense, creamy mass of small surface foam (milk / beer / mouth) · effervesce: vigorous, sparkling escape of gas bubbles from carbonated liquid (mineral water / wine / fluid) · bubble over: overflowing the brim with bubbles or metaphorical excitement (pot / joy / enthusiasm)
groups.nuance_zh: bubble: 液体内冒出并破裂大个气泡 (tar / soup / spring) · fizz: 碳酸液体嘶嘶作响冒出细密微气泡 (soda / champagne / tablet) · froth: 液体剧烈搅动泛起浓密泡沫或白沫 (milk / beer / mouth) · effervesce: 液体剧烈翻腾起泡并欢腾逸散 (mineral water / wine / fluid) · bubble over: 泡沫溢出容器边界，或热情溢于言表 (pot / joy / enthusiasm)

groups.name: Calm & Soothe · 平息与舒缓
groups.tip: 平复情绪或紧绷状态

items.def_zh: 使平静，平息，抚平；使静止
items.def_en: To make someone or something calm, quiet, or motionless.
items.ex_en: A soft evening breeze descended upon the meadow and stilled the rustling leaves.
items.ex_zh: 一阵柔和的晚风拂过草地，抚平了沙沙作响的树叶。
items.ex2_en: The chaotic commotion in the grand hall gradually stilled as midnight approached quietly.
items.ex2_zh: 随着午夜悄然临近，大厅里混乱的嘈杂声渐渐平息下来。

items.def_en: (+ down) to cause someone or something to become quiet, relaxed, and undisturbed
items.ex_en: The flight attendant took deep breaths to calm her racing heart during turbulence.
items.ex_zh: 在颠簸期间，乘务员深吸了几口气以让自己狂跳的心平静下来。
items.ex2_en: The restless ocean waters began to calm as the severe storm drifted eastward.
items.ex2_zh: 随着猛烈的风暴向东漂移，躁动不安的海水开始平静下来。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) become or make someone or something less agitated, angry, or emotional
items.ex_en: He went outside for a smoke to calm down after the heated meeting.
items.ex_zh: 开完激烈的会议后，他走到外面抽根烟让自己平静下来。
items.ex2_en: The gentle schoolteacher tried to calm down the frightened children after the alarm.
items.ex2_zh: 警报响过之后，温柔的老师试图安抚受惊的孩子们。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) become or make someone or an environment quieter, less noisy, or less agitated
items.ex_en: The excited schoolchildren took several minutes to quiet down after the recess bell.
items.ex_zh: 课间铃声响起后，兴奋的小学生们花了好几分钟才安静下来。
items.ex2_en: The librarian asked the noisy teenagers to quiet down their animated group conversation.
items.ex2_zh: 图书管理员要求喧闹的青少年们压低他们热烈的群体交谈声。

items.def_en: relax and unwind after a period of work, activity, or stress
items.ex_en: I love to wind down on Friday nights with a warm bubble bath.
items.ex_zh: 我喜欢在周五晚上泡个热水澡来彻底放松一下。
items.ex2_en: The multinational corporation decided to wind down its unprofitable consumer electronics division gradually.
items.ex2_zh: 这家跨国公司决定逐步压缩并停办其无利可图的消费电子部门。

items.def_en: to gently relieve someone's distress, irritation, or emotional upset
items.ex_en: She sang a gentle lullaby to soothe her crying child back to sleep.
items.ex_zh: 她唱起温柔的摇篮曲，以安抚啼哭的孩子重新入睡。

items.def_zh: 放松，释怀，平复情绪；解开，展开（卷绕之物）
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To relax and stop feeling anxious or tense after a period of work or worry. 2. To unroll, uncoil, or untwist something that has been wound, or to become unwound.
items.ex_en: A quiet walk along the beach helped him unwind after the grueling shift.
items.ex_zh: 沿着海滩漫步片刻，帮助他在辛苦繁重的轮班之后放松了下来。
items.ex2_en: She carefully unwound the long spool of thread before sewing the torn hem.
items.ex2_zh: 在缝补破损的下摆之前，她小心地解开了长长的一轴线。

items.def_en: to suppress or subdue strong unpleasant feelings, unrest, or anxieties
items.ex_en: The prime minister appeared on television to quell public anxiety about the currency collapse.
items.ex_zh: 首相出现在电视上，以平息公众对货币暴跌的焦虑情绪。

items.def_en: to quell anger, agitation, or hostile discontent in a person or population
items.ex_en: The regional governor offered immediate food aid to pacify the starving and mutinous villagers.
items.ex_zh: 地方长官立即提供粮食援助，以平息饥饿且蠢蠢欲动的村民们的愤怒。

items.def_zh: （使）平静下来，（使）安静，平息；抚慰
items.def_en: (+ down) (chiefly British) To become quieter, calmer, or less active, or to make someone or something calm.
items.ex_en: The stormy winds began to quieten down as the ship entered the bay.
items.ex_zh: 当船驶入海湾时，狂暴的狂风终于开始平静了下来。
items.ex2_en: The experienced nurse quietened the crying toddler with a gentle lullaby and milk.
items.ex2_zh: 经验丰富的护士用轻柔的摇篮曲和牛奶让哭闹的蹒跚学步幼儿安静下来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe reducing agitation, noise, stress, or excitement in a person, environment, or feeling, returning things to a peaceful or relaxed state. They encompass physical relaxing ('unwind'), calming motion or storm ('still'), and lowering vocal or mental agitation ('quieten', 'soothe', 'quell').
groups.summary_zh: 消除喧嚣、焦虑或动荡，使身心或局势恢复平静。
groups.desc_en: Mitigating agitation, turbulence, or emotional distress, restoring a system or mind to tranquil equilibrium, contrasting with passive dormancy or suppression by blunt force.
groups.desc_zh: 平抑躁动、动荡或心理应激，恢复平静和谐的稳态，区别于被动休眠或暴力的强行镇压。
groups.nuance_en: soothe: gently relieving pain, irritability, or raw emotion (baby / burn / nerves) · calm: bringing an agitated person or sea into a steady, composed state (waters / mind / patient) · quell: firmly extinguishing rebellion, intense fear, or civil disorder (unrest / riot / fear) · wind down: gradually decelerating activity or tension toward rest (business / evening / tension) · still: causing all physical motion or acoustic disturbance to cease entirely (wind / heart / chatter)
groups.nuance_zh: soothe: 柔和地抚平痛楚、伤痛或受刺激的神经 (baby / burn / nerves) · calm: 使激动的心绪或汹涌的风浪平伏沉着 (waters / mind / patient) · quell: 果断强力地压制平息叛乱、恐慌或骚乱 (unrest / riot / fear) · wind down: 紧绷状态后逐渐放松减速或收尾 (business / evening / tension) · still: 使所有的物理运动或喧哗完全静止平息 (wind / heart / chatter)

groups.name: Censure & Denounce · 申斥与痛批 (Reprimand, Berate, Slag)
groups.tip: 指出过失与错误，严厉斥责与追究责任

items.def_en: to speak to someone severely about something wrong they have done, often warning them not to repeat it
items.ex_en: The supervisor gently admonished the new intern for missing the important safety briefing.
items.ex_zh: 主管因新实习生错过了重要的安全简报会而轻声规劝了他。

items.def_en: to speak to someone in a disapproving way about minor misbehavior
items.ex_en: She chided him with a gentle smile for forgetting their dinner reservations again.
items.ex_zh: 她带着温柔的微笑轻声责备他再次忘记了晚餐预订。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Speak angrily to someone for doing something wrong or unacceptable
items.ex_en: The teacher told him off for chatting during the exam.
items.ex_zh: 老师因为他在考试中聊天而严厉训斥了他。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Scold someone thoroughly and vigorously for a failure or mistake
items.ex_en: The drill sergeant chewed out the recruit for dropping his rifle in mud.
items.ex_zh: 教官把那名将步枪掉进泥里的新兵狠狠臭骂了一顿。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Reprimand someone severely and formally for misconduct
items.ex_en: On Fridays, staff are allowed to dress down.
items.ex_zh: 每周五，员工可以穿便服上班。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Attack or criticize someone harshly with angry words
items.ex_en: The manager laid into the kitchen staff for serving raw poultry to guests.
items.ex_zh: 经理严厉痛斥后厨员工向客人端上未煮熟的禽肉。

items.def_en: (formal) To tell someone officially and severely that they have done something wrong.
items.ex_en: The committee reprimanded the director for gross negligence in overseeing the hospital finances.
items.ex_zh: 委员会因该董事在监督医院财务方面的重大过失而对其予以严肃训斥。

items.def_zh: 严厉批评，痛骂（slag off）；变成炉渣
items.def_en: 1. (slag off) (British informal) To criticize someone or something harshly and rudely. 2. (metallurgy) To convert into or form slag.
items.ex_en: The anonymous critic loved to slag off young novelists on his internet blog.
items.ex_zh: 那位匿名评论家总喜欢在他的网络博客上对年轻小说家大加痛骂。

items.def_en: to criticize or speak angrily to someone at length
items.ex_en: The furious customer berated the frightened cashier over an expired discount coupon.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的顾客因一张过期的优惠券对受惊的收银员进行了长时间的痛斥。

items.def_en: to criticize someone or something publicly and vehemently
items.ex_en: The editorial fiercely lambasted the mayor's reckless decision to cut the public transport budget.
items.ex_zh: 社论严厉抨击了市长削减公共交通预算的鲁莽决定。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote verbally rebuking, scolding, or aggressively attacking someone for faults or misconduct, scaling from formal institutional reprimands to vitriolic colloquial abuse.
groups.summary_zh: 对某人的过错进行严正训诫、斥责，直至恶言恶语的猛烈抨击。
groups.desc_en: Verbally castigating, reprimanding, or condemning an individual with varying degrees of institutional authority and linguistic violence, contrasting with gentle counsel or polite correction.
groups.desc_zh: 以不同层级的制度威权或激烈言辞对失职者进行痛斥、训诫或谴责，区别于温和劝告或礼貌纠错。
groups.nuance_en: admonish: mildly but earnestly warning or correcting against an error (child / student / disciple) · reprimand: formally and officially censuring someone for misconduct (employee / officer / subordinate) · dress down: severely scolding a subordinate face-to-face (troops / junior / offender) · chew out: aggressively and loudly blasting an inferior with verbal wrath (recruit / team / driver) · slag: publicly and maliciously disparaging or verbally trashing someone's reputation (celebrity / rival / politician)
groups.nuance_zh: admonish: 恳切、温和地告诫劝勉以防重犯 (child / student / disciple) · reprimand: 制度层面正式而严肃地通报批评或申斥 (employee / officer / subordinate) · dress down: 当面厉声训斥下属使其下不来台 (troops / junior / offender) · chew out: 暴跳如雷、粗暴大声地痛骂下级 (recruit / team / driver) · slag: 公开且刻薄下流地痛骂或抨击名誉 (celebrity / rival / politician)

groups.name: Coat & Smear · 涂抹与涂覆 (Coat, Lacquer, Enamel)
groups.tip: 在物体表面涂上保护层

items.def_en: (+ sth) cover an object or surface with a thin, glossy protective or decorative layer
items.ex_en: The potter prepared to glaze over the decorative bowls before the final firing.
items.ex_zh: 陶艺师准备在最后一次烧制前给这些装饰碗表面上一层釉。
items.ex2_en: His eyes began to glaze over as the boring speaker droned continuously.
items.ex2_zh: 当乏味的演讲者不停嗡嗡念叨时，他的眼神开始变得呆滞迷离。

items.def_zh: 涂上一层（油漆、釉或薄膜）
items.def_en: (+ sth) apply a thin liquid, glaze, or coating to a surface using a brush
items.ex_en: The craftsman used a badger brush to paint on the protective liquid varnish.
items.ex_zh: 工匠用獾毛刷在表面小心翼翼地涂上一层透明保护光油。

items.def_en: to fit or cover with a smooth, glossy coating or vitreous substance
items.ex_en: The baker used sweet apricot syrup to glaze the top of the fruit tart.
items.ex_zh: 面包师用香甜的杏子糖浆在水果挞表面刷上了一层光亮浆。
items.ex2_en: The wet highway glazed with treacherous black ice during the freezing overnight drop.
items.ex2_zh: 在夜间刺骨的降温中，潮湿的公路结上了一层危险的黑冰。

items.def_zh: 涂以瓷釉，上搪瓷；给……施彩饰
items.def_en: 1. To coat metal, pottery, or a surface with smooth, glossy protective enamel.
items.ex_en: The artisan will enamel the copper pendant with vibrant shades of powdered cobalt blue.
items.ex_zh: 工匠将用鲜艳的钴蓝釉粉在这只紫铜吊坠表面烧制上一层瓷釉。

items.def_zh: 涂亮漆，喷漆（或定型发胶）于
items.def_en: 1. To coat wood, metal, or hair with glossy protective lacquer or hairspray.
items.ex_en: Carpenters patiently applied four separate coats to lacquer the antique mahogany dining table.
items.ex_zh: 木工们耐心地涂了四道清漆，为这张仿古红木餐桌上了漆。

items.def_zh: 用喷枪喷绘；用气刷修饰（照片）；粉饰，掩饰
items.def_en: 1. To paint or retouch a photograph or surface using an airbrush to improve its appearance. 2. (figurative) To alter a situation or history to remove undesirable facts.
items.ex_en: The graphic designer spent an hour to airbrush the model's facial blemishes away.
items.ex_zh: 平面设计师花了一个小时用数码气刷修饰掉了模特的脸部瑕疵。

items.def_zh: 用蜂蜡涂抹，用蜂蜡上光
items.def_en: 1. To polish and protect furniture or leather using beeswax.
items.ex_en: The antique restorer decided to beeswax the oak cabinet to enrich its golden luster.
items.ex_zh: 古董修复师决定用蜂蜡涂抹橡木柜，以使其散发出丰润的金色光泽。

items.def_en: 1. To cover or smear something with thick, slippery mucus or slime.
items.ex_en: The oversized garden slugs managed to slime the entire stone patio overnight.
items.ex_zh: 那些硕大的花园鼻涕虫一夜之间把整个石板露台涂满了恶心的黏液。

items.def_en: to apply a transparent hard protective resin coating onto wood or metal
items.ex_en: We must varnish the wooden deck before the heavy winter rains arrive next week.
items.ex_zh: 我们必须赶在下周冬季暴雨来临前给木质甲板涂上一层清漆。

items.def_en: to apply a thick, sticky, or greasy substance crudely or unevenly over a surface
items.ex_en: He carelessly daubed thick yellow paint across the lower edge of the fence.
items.ex_zh: 他胡乱将厚厚的黄油漆粗劣地涂抹在篱笆的下沿。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail the application of a thin protective, decorative, or viscous film/layer over a surface, classified by substance, equipment, and finish.
groups.summary_zh: 使用特定介质、工艺或工具在物体表面涂覆保护层或装饰层。
groups.desc_en: Applies a liquid, viscous, or protective substance across a substrate to alter its surface texture, shine, or resilience, contrasting with simple permeating or staining.
groups.desc_zh: 将液体、粘性物或保护剂涂敷于基底表面以改变质感、光泽或防护力，区别于单纯的浸润或染色。
groups.nuance_en: glaze: apply a vitreous or shiny coating (pottery / pastry / eyes) · enamel: coat with a hard, glossy, heat-fused protective layer (metal / jewelry / cookware) · lacquer: seal with a hard, high-gloss resinous varnish (wood / furniture / nails) · airbrush: apply a fine mist for smooth, flawless coverage (photo / skin / illustration)
groups.nuance_zh: glaze: 涂敷光亮釉质或糖浆 (pottery / pastry / eyes) · enamel: 搪瓷或上珐琅硬质涂层 (metal / jewelry / cookware) · lacquer: 涂刷高光树脂清漆 (wood / furniture / nails) · airbrush: 气刷细密喷涂以除瑕修饰 (photo / skin / illustration)

groups.name: Coax & Wheedle · 诱导与哄骗 (Coax, Wheedle, Inveigle)
groups.tip: 用甜言蜜语巧妙劝诱哄劝

items.def_en: to persuade someone gently and patiently to do something or go somewhere
items.ex_en: She managed to coax the frightened stray kitten out from under the porch.
items.ex_zh: 她耐心地把受惊的流浪小猫从门廊底下哄劝了出来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) praise or flatter someone excessively to gain their favor or wheedle something out of them
items.ex_en: The junior accountant tried to butter up his demanding boss with expensive pastries.
items.ex_zh: 初级会计试图用昂贵的糕点巴结哄劝他那位苛刻的老板。

items.def_en: (+ into) to talk to someone nicely and charmingly in order to persuade them to do something
items.ex_en: He managed to sweet-talk the suspicious landlord into waiving the late rent fee.
items.ex_zh: 他凭着三寸不烂之舌说甜言蜜语，哄得心存怀疑的房东免去了滞纳金。

items.def_en: (+ sb) persuade or coax someone into doing something through persuasive conversation
items.ex_en: Her persistent friends finally talked her into joining the weekend mountain hiking expedition.
items.ex_zh: 在朋友们不依不饶的劝导下，她最终被说动去参加周末的登山探险。

items.def_en: to coax or cajole someone with gentle flattery or ingratiating speech
items.ex_en: The ambitious courtier attempted to blandish the queen into granting him tax exemptions.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的廷臣企图用谄媚的甜言蜜语哄劝女王赦免他的赋税。

items.def_en: (+ into/out of) to persuade someone to do something by sustained flattery or soothing words
items.ex_en: The detective deftly cajoled the reluctant witness into signing the written formal confession.
items.ex_zh: 侦探巧妙地以柔和的话语劝诱不情愿的目击证人签下了正式供状。

items.def_zh: 哄骗，用甜言蜜语劝诱（以获取某物）
items.def_en: To persuade someone to do something or give you something by using flattery, praise, or pleasing words.
items.ex_en: The spoilt teenager tried to wheedle extra allowance out of her indulgent grandmother.
items.ex_zh: 那个被宠坏的少女试图用甜言蜜语从放任她的祖母那里多骗取些零花钱。

items.def_en: To persuade someone to do something or give you something by using clever talk, flattery, or deception.
items.ex_en: The shrewd promoter managed to inveigle several prominent investors into the risky venture.
items.ex_zh: 精明的发起人通过巧言令色成功诱骗了几位知名投资人注资这项风险投资。

items.def_en: (+ sb) trick or coax someone into doing something through artful deception
items.ex_en: The dishonest salesman conned the elderly widow into purchasing an overpriced heating system.
items.ex_zh: 奸诈的推销员诱骗那位年迈的寡妇高价购买了一套根本不值这个钱的供暖系统。

items.def_en: (+ into) to fool, cheat, or persuade someone into doing something by obscure or tricky means
items.ex_en: The fraudulent scheme bamboozled hundreds of retirees into handing over their life savings.
items.ex_zh: 这起欺诈阴谋耍花招蒙骗了数百名退休人员，使他们交出了毕生积蓄。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe persuading or manipulating someone into doing something or giving something up through gentle flattery, artful deception, or persistent charm. They typically take an object followed by a prepositional phrase like 'into doing something' or 'out of something'.
groups.summary_zh: 通过巧言令色、谄媚或诱骗等手段说服他人行事或交出财物。
groups.desc_en: Influences or manipulates someone toward compliance through persistent flattery, gentle persuasion, or charm, unlike direct ordering or rational debate.
groups.desc_zh: 通过持续奉承、温和劝说或魅力诱导他人顺从，区别于直接施令或理性辩论。
groups.nuance_en: coax: gentle, patient persuasion (child / engine / smile) · wheedle: whining or fawning coaxing to extract a favor (money / permission / secrets) · cajole: persistent, charming flattery to overcome reluctance (donors / reluctant witness / colleague) · inveigle: cunning entrapment or deception into an action (heiress / signature / consent)
groups.nuance_zh: coax: 耐心温和地诱导哄劝 (child / engine / smile) · wheedle: 甜言蜜语或摇尾乞怜式讨要 (money / permission / secrets) · cajole: 软磨硬泡的花言巧语奉承 (donors / reluctant witness / colleague) · inveigle: 设局诱骗或巧取豪夺 (heiress / signature / consent)

groups.name: Convey & Transport · 运送与携运 (Convey, Transport, Haul)
groups.tip: 随身或借助工具携带

items.def_en: 1. To take or carry someone or something to a place or person. 2. To cause something to happen or exist.
items.ex_en: Please remember to bring your passport to the airport counter tomorrow morning early.
items.ex_zh: 请记住明早务必将您的护照带到机场柜台。

items.def_zh: 携带，提，扛；运送，输送；承担，承受
items.def_en: 1. To hold and support someone or something while moving from one place to another. 2. To transport or transmit something. 3. To bear or accept a responsibility or burden.
items.ex_en: The strong porter will carry these heavy travel trunks up the steep stairs.
items.ex_zh: 那位强壮的搬运工会把这些沉重的旅行箱提上陡峭的楼梯。

items.def_zh: 携带，带来；引起（bring 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of bring; to have taken, carried, or caused something.
items.ex_en: The friendly courier brought three large packages directly to our front entrance yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 那位友好的快递员昨天直接将三个大包裹送到了我们前门处。

items.def_en: to take or carry people or goods from one place to another by vehicle
items.ex_en: Specially refrigerated trucks transport fresh seafood from the coastal docks to inland supermarkets.
items.ex_zh: 特制的冷藏车负责将新鲜海鲜从沿海码头运送到内陆各大超市。

items.def_en: to carry something heavy or cumbersome around with you
items.ex_en: The tired commuter had to tote a bulky laptop briefcase through rush-hour crowds.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的通勤者不得不拎着一个笨重的笔记本电脑公文包挤过早高峰人群。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to convey or transport someone or something away, often forcefully or clumsily in a vehicle
items.ex_en: The municipal bailiffs came to cart off the debtor's seized office equipment yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 市政法警昨天过来拉走了债务人被查封的办公设备。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to transport people or goods frequently from one place to another
items.ex_en: She spent the whole sunny afternoon ferrying around children to their sports games.
items.ex_zh: 她把整个晴朗的下午都花在四处接送孩子们去参加各种体育比赛上。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to send someone or transport goods away to another destination
items.ex_en: Her desperate parents decided to pack off the unruly boy to boarding school.
items.ex_zh: 绝望的父母决定把这个任性叛逆的男孩打发到寄宿学校去。

items.def_en: to pull or transport something heavy over a distance, often in a truck
items.ex_en: Two powerful diesel trucks hauled the giant wind turbine blades across the desert.
items.ex_zh: 两辆强劲的柴油货车拖拉着巨大的风力涡轮机叶片穿过了沙漠。

items.def_en: to carry or transport someone or something from one place to another
items.ex_en: An underground automated pipeline will convey petroleum from the seaport to the refinery.
items.ex_zh: 一条地下自动化管道将负责把石油从海港安全运送到炼油厂。

groups.summary_en: Carriers move objects or passengers from an origin to a destination across space. Nuances distinguish between manual, person-borne carriage and mechanized, bulk, or heavy-duty logistical transport.
groups.summary_zh: 人或载具承受负重，将货物或人从一处转移运送到另一处。
groups.desc_en: Shifts physical items or persons over distance using vehicles, vessels, or sustained manual effort, contrasting with stationary handling or mere passing.
groups.desc_zh: 借助载具、容器或持续体力将人或物位移至远方，区别于原位搬弄或随手递交。
groups.nuance_en: transport: systemic movement across distances via infrastructure (freight / troops / goods) · haul: drag or convey heavy loads with sustained effort (timber / coal / luggage) · ferry: shuttle back and forth across a short route (commuters / supplies / refugees) · cart off: convey away abruptly or forcibly (debris / suspects / rubbish)
groups.nuance_zh: transport: 依托系统与运输工具的规程化运送 (freight / troops / goods) · haul: 耗费重力拖运大宗重物 (timber / coal / luggage) · ferry: 穿梭往返于定点短途摆渡 (commuters / supplies / refugees) · cart off: 强行或仓促拉走清运 (debris / suspects / rubbish)

groups.name: Critique & Denounce · 批评与谴责 (Chide, Lambast, Castigate)
groups.tip: 由温和责备逐渐升级至严厉训诫

items.def_en: (+ for) To scold or rebuke someone mildly or affectionately for behaving badly.
items.ex_en: The grandmother chided the little boy for spilling fresh milk on her rug.
items.ex_zh: 祖母因小男孩把鲜牛奶洒在地毯上而轻声训诫了他几句。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to challenge, criticize, or denounce someone openly for bad behavior or wrongdoing
items.ex_en: The student council president called out the board for ignoring environmental campus concerns.
items.ex_zh: 学生会主席在大会上公开指责校董事会忽视校园环境问题。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
items.ex_en: The teacher told him off for chatting during the exam.
items.ex_zh: 老师因为他在考试中聊天而严厉训斥了他。

items.def_en: to express sharp, stern disapproval or criticism directly to someone
items.ex_en: The commander delivered a harsh rebuke to the sentry for sleeping on duty.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官对当值睡觉的哨兵予以了严厉的指责与训斥。

items.def_en: to express severe, official disapproval of someone's actions
items.ex_en: The medical licensing board reprimanded the physician for violating strict patient confidentiality rules.
items.ex_zh: 医疗执业管理委员会因该医生违反严格的患者保密规定而对其予以正式申斥。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to reprimand or verbally denounce someone with great severity
items.ex_en: Dad really laid into me when he saw the dent on his car.
items.ex_zh: 爸爸看到车上的凹痕时，把我狠狠地痛骂了一顿。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to criticize, attack, or scold someone in a very angry and aggressive manner
items.ex_en: The coach tore into the players for their lazy defense after the match.
items.ex_zh: 赛后，教练因防守懒散而把队员们痛斥了一番。

items.def_zh: 严厉谴责，痛斥；猛打，痛打
items.def_en: (+ for) 1. To criticize someone or something harshly, angrily, and publicly. 2. To beat or strike violently.
