items.ex_en: Editorials lambasted the mayor for his reckless handling of the municipal budget crisis.
items.ex_zh: 社论严厉谴责了市长对市政预算危机的草率处理。

items.def_zh: 严厉批评，严加申斥；严罚
items.def_en: (+ for) (formal) To criticize or punish someone or something severely, usually in public.
items.ex_en: The committee castigated the executive for withholding crucial evidence during the investigation.
items.ex_zh: 委员会因该高管在调查期间隐瞒关键证据而对其进行了严厉斥责。

items.def_en: (formal) to criticize someone or something with blistering, scathing severity
items.ex_en: The report excoriated the agency for its catastrophic regulatory failures and negligence.
items.ex_zh: 该报告严厉抨击了该机构灾难性的监管失职与疏忽。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve communicating harsh disapproval, reprimand, or moral condemnation toward a person or act. The scale progresses from mild or scolding remonstrance ('chide') to severe public excoriation ('lambast', 'castigate', 'excoriate').
groups.summary_zh: 指表达指责、训诫与严厉谴责，由温和轻责递进至严正斥责。
groups.desc_en: Utters sharp, explicit disapproval or condemnation targeting misconduct or errors, ranging from gentle correction to blistering censure.
groups.desc_zh: 对过失或不端行为进行明确的责备或严厉谴责，从轻度微词递增至狂暴轰击。
groups.nuance_en: chide: scold gently with mild admonition (child / friend / impatience) · reprimand: formal, authoritative disciplinary censure (officer / employee / subordinate) · rebuke: sharp, stern corrective reprimand (critic / minister / behavior) · lambast: violently and publicly attack or criticize (critics / opponent / policy)
groups.nuance_zh: chide: 轻声嗔怪或温和责备 (child / friend / impatience) · reprimand: 具权威性或正式行政规诫 (officer / employee / subordinate) · rebuke: 疾言厉色的当面痛斥 (critic / minister / behavior) · lambast: 狂风暴雨式的公然痛批 (critics / opponent / policy)

groups.name: Curtail & Retrench · 削减、紧缩与减少 (Curtail, Retrench, Dwindle)
groups.tip: 数量削减或规模由大变小

items.def_en: to reduce the amount, size, or cost of something, especially financial expenditure
items.ex_en: We must cut back our marketing expenditures before the end of this quarter.
items.ex_zh: 在本季度结束之前，我们必须削减营销开支。

items.def_en: to gradually diminish, become smaller or weaker, and then stop completely
items.ex_en: The lively protest gradually petered out as the heavy rain began to fall.
items.ex_zh: 随着大雨倾盆而下，原本热烈的抗议活动渐渐平息了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce the size, scope, budget, or extent of an activity or project
items.ex_en: The studio had to scale down the film's production budget significantly this year.
items.ex_zh: 制片厂今年不得不大幅按比例削减该电影的制作预算。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to gradually reduce an activity, production, or operation before ending it
items.ex_en: The factory plans to wind down operations over the next three months.
items.ex_zh: 该工厂计划在接下来的三个月内逐步收束运营业务。
items.ex2_en: The lively evening party wound down quietly as exhausted guests drifted toward home.
items.ex2_zh: 随着疲惫的客人们纷纷回家，热闹的晚会渐渐平静落幕。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce spending, staff, or resources gradually to a bare minimum
items.ex_en: The hospital was forced to pare back non-essential services due to funding deficits.
items.ex_zh: 由于资金短缺，该医院被迫将非必要服务精简至最低限度。

items.def_en: 1. To become gradually smaller, fewer, or weaker in size, quantity, or strength.
items.ex_en: Our remaining water supplies began to dwindle under the scorching desert sun.
items.ex_zh: 在沙漠灼热的阳光下，我们剩余的水储备开始逐渐减少。

items.def_en: 1. To reduce or limit something, especially spending, rights, or the duration of an activity.
items.ex_en: New regulations will curtail public gatherings during the declared state of emergency.
items.ex_zh: 新规定将在宣布的紧急状态期间限制公众集会。

items.def_en: to gradually reduce something, such as expenses or numbers, to an essential minimum (+ down)
items.ex_en: Management must pare down administrative overhead to ensure the company's long-term survival.
items.ex_zh: 管理层必须逐步削减行政开支，以确保公司的长期生存。

items.def_zh: 减弱，降低；抑止（呼吸，多用于 with bated breath）
items.def_en: 1. (archaic) To lessen, diminish, or moderate; to hold back or suppress (force or breath).
items.ex_en: The captive crowd bated their breath as the daring trapeze artist leapt.
items.ex_zh: 当那位勇敢的高空杂技演员跃起时，全场观众都屏住了呼吸。

items.def_zh: 紧缩开支，削减费用；裁员，缩减业务
items.def_en: 1. To reduce expenses, cut costs, or scale back operations during difficult economic times.
items.ex_en: Faced with falling profits, the corporation chose to retrench by laying off contractors.
items.ex_zh: 面对利润下滑，该企业选择通过解雇承包商来紧缩开支。

groups.summary_en: A quantity, budget, activity, or resource diminishes over time or is deliberately cut back by an entity seeking restraint or facing exhaustion.
groups.summary_zh: 开支、规模或活动等被有意削减、紧缩，或资源自行缩减消退。
groups.desc_en: Deliberately diminishes, trims, or phases out scale, expenditure, or activity, contrasting with sudden termination or natural decay.
groups.desc_zh: 主动压缩、裁减或逐步削减规模、支出及活动，区别于骤然终止或被动耗竭。
groups.nuance_en: curtail: restrict or cut short before completion (spending / civil liberties / trip) · pare: trim off excess or reduce by small increments (costs / budget / workforce) · retrench: reduce expenses in response to economic stringency (business / expenditure / operations) · wind down: gradually reduce operations toward closure (business / production / campaign)
groups.nuance_zh: curtail: 强制截短或限制剥夺 (spending / civil liberties / trip) · pare: 层层剥除冗余或精简开支 (costs / budget / workforce) · retrench: 紧缩开支以应对财务萧条 (business / expenditure / operations) · wind down: 有步骤地收尾或逐步降温 (business / production / campaign)

groups.name: Cut & Cleave · 切开与劈裂 (Slit, Cleave, Rive)
groups.tip: 利器劈斩开劈分两半

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut cleanly and effortlessly into or through something using a sharp blade
items.ex_en: The chef's razor-sharp knife sliced cleanly through the fresh tuna fillet.
items.ex_zh: 厨师锋利的刀利落地切穿了新鲜的金枪鱼柳。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a straight, sharp incision to open something such as an envelope or bag
items.ex_en: She grabbed the letter opener and slit open the mysterious envelope instantly.
items.ex_zh: 她拿起拆信刀，瞬间划开了那个神秘的信封。

items.def_en: to cut with a wide, sweeping violent stroke of a blade
items.ex_en: The robber slashed the canvas bag with a wide stroke of his blade.
items.ex_zh: 劫匪猛挥刀刃，一刀划开了帆布包。

items.def_en: To make a long, narrow cut or opening in something with a sharp instrument.
items.ex_en: He carefully slit the taped seam of the cardboard box with a utility knife.
items.ex_zh: 他用美工刀小心地在纸箱的封胶处切开了一条缝。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to split or slice cleanly and forcefully through a solid physical object
items.ex_en: The broadsword cleaved cleanly through the wooden shield, splitting it in two.
items.ex_zh: 重剑利落地劈开了木盾，将其一分为二。

items.def_zh: 劈开，劈裂；坚持，黏附（cleave to）
items.def_en: 1. To split or cut something apart, especially with a heavy blow from a sharp weapon or tool. 2. ('cleave to') To stick firmly or adhere to something.
items.ex_en: With one mighty swing of his axe, the woodsman cleaved the thick log.
items.ex_zh: 樵夫挥起斧头猛力一劈，将粗大的原木劈裂开来。
items.ex2_en: The brittle geological formation cleaved cleanly under the immense subterranean pressure over centuries.
items.ex2_zh: 在几个世纪巨大的地下压力下，脆弱的地质岩层整齐地裂开了。

items.def_en: to split or tear apart violently or along natural grain
items.ex_en: A sudden flash of lightning rived the ancient oak tree straight down the middle.
items.ex_zh: 一道突如其来的闪电将那棵古老的橡树从正中劈开。
items.ex2_en: The dry slate rock rived easily under intense temperature changes throughout winter.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的板岩在整个冬季剧烈的气温变化下很容易裂开。

items.def_zh: 劈开，分裂（cleave 的过去分词）；劈成两半的
items.def_en: (archaic) Past participle of cleave; to split or divide into distinct parts.
items.ex_en: The mighty quake had cloven the bedrock into two gaping chasms.
items.ex_zh: 强烈的地震将基岩劈裂成了两道巨大的深渊。
items.ex2_en: Ancient volcanic boulders had cloven over centuries from relentless cycles of freezing water.
items.ex2_zh: 数百年间，古老的火山巨石在冷水反复冻融的作用下开裂了。

items.def_en: to tear or split something apart with violent force
items.ex_en: Fierce gale winds rend the sails into ragged shreds during the ferocious storm.
items.ex_zh: 在狂暴的风暴中，强烈的狂风将船帆撕成了碎片。

items.def_en: to break or wrench apart forcefully into two or more pieces
items.ex_en: The devastating civil war sundered the historic nation into bitter rival factions.
items.ex_zh: 毁灭性的内战使这个历史悠久的国家分裂为势不两立的敌对派系。
items.ex2_en: Ancient trade alliances sundered abruptly when prolonged severe drought sparked territorial border disputes.
items.ex2_zh: 当长期的严重干旱引发领土边界争端时，古老的贸易同盟骤然破裂。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe parting a physical object cleanly or forcefully along a line or natural grain using a sharp blade or heavy wedge. 'Slit' denotes a precise, shallow or linear incision, while 'cleave' and related terms imply forceful, deep splitting into two parts.
groups.summary_zh: 强调沿纹理或线条利落切开、劈成两半的动作。
groups.desc_en: Divides or pierces a solid body using a sharp edge or wedge under force, separating parts along a plane or natural grain.
groups.desc_zh: 以锋利刀刃或楔状外力沿切面或纹理劈开并割裂实体，区别于无方向的粉碎。
groups.nuance_en: slit: cut a narrow, straight incision (throat / envelope / fabric) · slash: cut with sweeping, violent, erratic strokes (tires / prices / throat) · cleave: split firmly along a natural line or divide solidly (rock / air / wood) · rive: violently tear apart or splinter with immense stress (heart / timber / oak)
groups.nuance_zh: slit: 细长而利落地切开狭缝 (throat / envelope / fabric) · slash: 挥舞刀刃凶狠劈砍或狂削 (tires / prices / throat) · cleave: 沿纹理利落劈裂或穿透破浪 (rock / air / wood) · rive: 巨大应力下的撕裂或劈碎 (heart / timber / oak)

groups.name: Damage & Break · 损坏与破坏 (Impair, Blemish, & Break)
groups.tip: 破坏外观或损害原本功用

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a shallow cut or mark on the surface of something with a sharp object
items.ex_en: Be careful not to scratch the polished wooden tabletop with that key.
items.ex_zh: 小心别用那把钥匙划伤抛光的木质桌面。
items.ex2_en: Soft plastic phone screens scratch easily if stored alongside sharp metallic house keys.
items.ex2_zh: 柔软的塑料手机屏幕如果与锋利的金属家门钥匙放在一起很容易刮花。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to break a small piece off the surface or edge of a hard object
items.ex_en: He accidentally chipped off a corner of the expensive marble kitchen counter.
items.ex_zh: 他不小心磕掉了昂贵的大理石厨房台面的一角。

items.def_en: [I/T] to break off a small piece from the edge or surface of a hard object
items.ex_en: I accidentally chipped the edge of my favorite ceramic mug this morning.
items.ex_zh: 今天早上我不小心把我最喜欢的陶瓷杯边缘磕掉了一块。
items.ex2_en: Cheap glass dinnerware chips easily when stacked haphazardly inside a crowded metal rack.
items.ex2_zh: 廉价的玻璃餐具在拥挤的金属架上随意堆放时很容易碎裂磕碰掉角。

items.def_en: To cause something to have a defect, blemish, or weakness, thereby ruining its perfection or efficacy.
items.ex_en: A single careless crack flawed the structural integrity of the delicate porcelain vase.
items.ex_zh: 一道不经意的裂缝破坏了这件精致瓷瓶的结构完整性。
items.ex2_en: The brittle diamond flawed internally under the uneven pressure of the faulty cutter.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的钻石在有缺陷的切割机不均匀的压力下内部产生了瑕疵。

items.def_en: To spoil or damage the appearance, quality, or perfection of something.
items.ex_en: Deep tire tracks marred the pristine perfection of the freshly manicured lawn.
items.ex_zh: 深深的车辙破坏了修剪整齐的新草坪的完美外观。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to break or smash physical objects violently
items.ex_en: The drunken patrons bust up several chairs during the violent tavern brawl.
items.ex_zh: 醉酒的顾客在酒馆的激烈斗殴中砸坏了好几把椅子。

items.def_zh: 打破，弄坏；突击搜捕；（使）破产
items.def_en: 1. To break, smash, or ruin something completely. 2. To arrest someone or raid a place.
items.ex_en: He managed to bust the heavy padlock open using an iron crowbar.
items.ex_zh: 他用铁撬棍设法砸烂了那把沉重的挂锁。
items.ex2_en: The pressurized copper water pipe busted completely during the sudden subzero winter freeze.
items.ex2_zh: 承压的铜水管在突如其来的零下严冬冰冻中彻底破裂了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to crack, split, or break a hard object, bone, or structural surface
items.ex_en: The heavy impact fractured the athlete's tibia during the championship match.
items.ex_zh: 在锦标赛中，剧烈的撞击导致该运动员的胫骨骨折。
items.ex2_en: The brittle foundation wall fractured slowly under the weight of shifting underground soil.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的地基墙在移动的地下土壤重量挤压下慢慢开裂了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to destroy or severely damage something by violently breaking it into pieces
items.ex_en: Vandals broke into the boutique overnight and smashed up all the glass display cases.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子连夜闯入精品店，砸烂了所有的玻璃展示柜。

items.def_en: [I/T] to break violently into many small pieces
items.ex_en: The dropped crystal bowl shattered into hundreds of pieces on the stone floor.
items.ex_zh: 掉落的水晶碗在石质地板上摔得粉碎成数百块碎片。
items.ex2_en: The violent blast shattered several heavy storefront windows along the commercial downtown street.
items.ex2_zh: 剧烈的爆炸震碎了市中心商业街上的几面厚实临街橱窗。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate impairing the integrity, functionality, or surface perfection of an entity. They scale along an intensity gradient from subtle aesthetic blemish or internal flaw to complete physical breakage or destruction.
groups.summary_zh: 损伤实体完好度，从轻微外表瑕疵到彻底破损断裂。
groups.desc_en: Inflicts physical harm, structural failure, or cosmetic degradation on an entity, diminishing its utility, value, or wholeness.
groups.desc_zh: 对实体施加机械或外观损伤致使其破损、断裂或贬值，区别于单纯的化学腐蚀。
groups.nuance_en: mar: impair the perfect appearance or quality without destroying it (surface / reputation / beauty) · chip: detach a small edge fragment by impact (paint / mug / tooth) · fracture: break or crack hard material or structural continuity (bone / skull / skull) · bust: break, smash, or rupture completely and violently (lock / door / knuckles)
groups.nuance_zh: mar: 损毁外观完整性或大煞风景 (surface / reputation / beauty) · chip: 磕碰掉边缘碎片或漆皮 (paint / mug / tooth) · fracture: 硬质结构的骨折、开裂或断裂 (bone / skull / skull) · bust: 暴力砸碎、搞烂或冲破 (lock / door / knuckles)

groups.name: Deceive & Scam · 坑害与诱骗 (Con, Scam, Dupe)
groups.tip: 设下圈套隐瞒真相来行骗

items.def_en: To trick or cheat someone, especially to persuade them to give you money or something valuable.
items.ex_en: The smooth salesman conned the elderly widow out of her life savings.
items.ex_zh: 那个巧舌如簧的推销员骗走了那位年迈寡妇一生的积蓄。

items.def_zh: 欺诈，诈骗，通过欺诈手段获取
items.def_en: To practice fraud or trickery to obtain money or advantage; cheat someone.
items.ex_en: Shady loan brokers shark vulnerable homeowners by charging exorbitant hidden service fees.
items.ex_zh: 不法贷款中介通过收取高额隐形服务费来坑骗脆弱的房主。

items.def_en: to cheat someone, especially by charging them too much money or selling poor goods
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to maliciously manipulate a situation to falsely incriminate or victimize someone
items.ex_en: He claimed the corrupt detectives stitched him up by planting false evidence.
items.ex_zh: 他声称是那些腐败的侦探栽赃伪造证据陷害了他。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to deliberately deceive someone over a period of time by giving them false hope
items.ex_en: The dishonest manager strung him along with empty promises of a promotion.
items.ex_zh: 那个不诚实的经理用晋升的虚假希望一直吊着他、愚弄他。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to successfully trick, deceive, or perpetrate a scam on someone
items.ex_en: You cannot pull one on me because I know all your little tricks.
items.ex_zh: 你休想蒙我，因为你的那些小把戏我一清二楚。

items.def_en: (informal) To cheat or trick someone out of money or property through a dishonest scheme.
items.ex_en: An offshore syndicate scammed thousands of investors with a bogus cryptocurrency project.
items.ex_zh: 一个境外犯罪团伙利用虚假的加密货币项目诈骗了数千名投资者。

items.def_en: (informal) To treat someone unfairly or cheat them out of something.
items.ex_en: The greedy contractor shafted the subcontractor by refusing to pay for finished labor.
items.ex_zh: 那个贪婪的总包商拒绝支付完工的人工费，狠狠坑了分包商一把。

items.def_en: to trick or cheat someone into believing an untruth or doing something foolish
items.ex_en: He duped unsuspecting tourists into buying fake antique coins near the ruins.
items.ex_zh: 他在废墟附近诱骗毫无戒心的游客购买假的古董硬币。

items.def_en: to deceive or trick someone, especially by concealing one's true intentions
items.ex_en: The cunning politician hoodwinked the voters with promises he never intended to keep.
items.ex_zh: 那个狡猾的政客用从未打算兑现的诺言蒙蔽了选民。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this informal frame describe tricking, manipulating, or unfairly taking advantage of a victim through deceptive schemes, exploitation, or harsh betrayal.
groups.summary_zh: 用圈套骗局引诱受害者上当，或在利益关系中苛待、坑害他人。
groups.desc_en: Swindles or defrauds a victim through calculated trickery, predatory schemes, or bad faith, contrasting with straightforward theft.
groups.desc_zh: 通过预谋的圈套、诈术或背信弃义诱使受害人上当以谋取不义之财，区别于直接偷盗。
groups.nuance_en: con: manipulate someone into handing over assets via confidence tricks (investor / marks / victim) · scam: execute a fraudulent scheme to defraud online or commercially (seniors / taxpayers / buyers) · rip off: cheat blatantly or grossly overcharge (tourists / consumers / customers) · string along: mislead deceitfully by sustaining false hopes over time (suitor / client / investors)
groups.nuance_zh: con: 设局博取信任的经典诈骗 (investor / marks / victim) · scam: 针对群体的系统化欺诈骗局 (seniors / taxpayers / buyers) · rip off: 宰客、漫天要价或直接敲竹杠 (tourists / consumers / customers) · string along: 虚假许诺并长期吊人胃口 (suitor / client / investors)

groups.name: Decelerate & Halt · 减缓与停止 (Slow, Halt, Cease)
groups.tip: 由放慢节奏到完全终止

items.def_en: to gradually decrease in speed, vigor, or intensity
items.ex_en: The strong wind finally began to slack off as the storm system moved inland.
items.ex_zh: 随着风暴系统移向内陆，强风终于开始减弱放缓。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to reduce speed, velocity, or the rate of physical movement
items.ex_en: Drivers must slow down when approaching this dangerous curve on the mountain road.
items.ex_zh: 驾驶员在接近这条山路上的危险弯道时必须减速。
items.ex2_en: Heavy police patrols on the highway slowed down reckless drivers during the evening.
items.ex2_zh: 高速公路上密集的警车巡逻在傍晚时分让鲁莽驾驶的司机减慢了车速。

items.def_en: 1. (+ down/up) To reduce speed or move more slowly, or cause someone or something to do so.
items.ex_en: Dense morning fog slowed traffic to a crawl along the coastal expressway.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的大雾使得沿海高速公路上的交通慢如蜗行。
items.ex2_en: The speeding train slowed noticeably as it approached the steep mountain railway curve.
items.ex2_zh: 飞驰的列车在接近险峻的山区铁路弯道时明显慢了下来。

items.def_en: 1. To stop speaking or doing something for a short time before continuing.
items.ex_en: The lecturer paused for a moment to take a sip of cold water.
items.ex_zh: 讲师停顿了片刻，喝了一小口凉水。

items.def_en: [I/T] to reduce speed gradually or cause a moving vehicle or process to slow down
items.ex_en: The high-speed train began to decelerate smoothly as it approached the central station.
items.ex_zh: 高铁在接近中心车站时开始平稳减速。
items.ex2_en: The careful pilot decelerated the passenger jet gradually before touching the tarmac runway.
items.ex2_zh: 细心的飞行员在接触停机坪跑道前逐步降低了客机的滑行速度。

items.def_zh: 停止，中断；停下；阻止，阻拦；堵塞
items.def_en: 1. To come to a halt, or prevent someone or something from moving or continuing. 2. To prevent someone from doing something or keep something from happening. 3. (+ up) To block or plug an opening.
items.ex_en: The red traffic signal stopped the flow of cross-town traffic during rush hour.
items.ex_zh: 红色的交通信号灯在高峰期阻止了穿城车流的前行。
items.ex2_en: The tired marathon runner stopped abruptly to catch his breath beside the bench.
items.ex2_zh: 疲惫的马拉松选手突然停下脚步，在长凳旁喘了口气。

items.def_en: to bring a vehicle or oneself to a complete stop
items.ex_en: The black limousine pulled up smoothly right outside the hotel's grand entrance.
items.ex_zh: 那辆黑色豪华轿车平稳地停在了酒店大门外。

items.def_en: [I/T] to bring or come to an abrupt or decisive stop, especially in motion or progress
items.ex_en: A nationwide rail strike abruptly halted public transit across the entire country.
items.ex_zh: 全国性的铁路罢工使得整个国家的公共交通骤然停摆。
items.ex2_en: The tired infantry soldiers halted abruptly when the commanding officer raised his hand.
items.ex2_zh: 当下达命令的军官举起手时，疲惫的步兵士兵们立刻停下了脚步。

items.def_zh: 嘎吱作响地停下；陷入停滞
items.def_en: (+ a halt) to decelerate gradually with friction until coming to a complete stop
items.ex_en: Factory production ground to a halt following the unexpected catastrophic power grid failure.
items.ex_zh: 在电网突发灾难性故障之后，工厂的生产陷入了停滞。

items.def_en: [I/T] to come or bring to a complete, final end; discontinue entirely
items.ex_en: Both nations agreed to cease all military hostilities along the contested border.
items.ex_zh: 两国均同意完全停止在有争议边界上的所有军事敌对行动。
items.ex2_en: The heavy monsoon rains finally ceased as warm morning sunlight pierced the clouds.
items.ex2_zh: 随着温暖的晨光穿透云层，猛烈的季风降雨终于停歇了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote a progressive reduction in velocity or motion culminating in total cessation, ranging from a slight deceleration or temporary suspension to an absolute, permanent standstill.
groups.summary_zh: 描述运动或过程由减速、暂歇到完全停止的递进过程。
groups.desc_en: Reduces velocity or terminates ongoing motion, progress, or operation, progressing from mild deceleration to an absolute standstill.
groups.desc_zh: 降低运动、进度或运转的速度直至绝对静止，覆盖从渐缓减速到猝然制动。
groups.nuance_en: decelerate: mathematically or mechanically reduce velocity (vehicle / growth / pace) · slack off: lose momentum, intensity, or diligence (effort / trade / rain) · halt: bring or come to an abrupt, definite stop (production / traffic / advance) · pull up: bring a moving vehicle or oneself to a controlled stop (car / horse / curb)
groups.nuance_zh: decelerate: 机械或数学意义上的降速与减速 (vehicle / growth / pace) · slack off: 势头减退、变缓或松懈懈怠 (effort / trade / rain) · halt: 猝然逼停或下令全面中止 (production / traffic / advance) · pull up: 驾驶载具或止步勒马平稳停靠 (car / horse / curb)

groups.name: Decompose & Spoil Chemically · 腐烂与质变败坏 (Decay, Rot, Spoil)
groups.tip: 有机物自然腐烂分解

items.def_en: to become unfit for consumption due to natural breakdown, or render food stale
items.ex_en: Leaving fresh dairy milk outside the refrigerator will quickly cause it to spoil.
items.ex_zh: 把新鲜牛奶留在冰箱外面很快就会导致它变质变馊。
items.ex2_en: Excessive exposure to warm ambient temperatures will spoil freshly prepared potato salad quickly.
items.ex2_zh: 过多暴露在温暖的室温下会很快让新鲜制作的土豆沙拉变质。

items.def_en: to decompose organically or chemically into simpler substances
items.ex_en: Fallen leaves gradually break down into nutrient-rich organic soil over several months.
items.ex_zh: 落叶在几个月内逐渐分解成富含有机养分的土壤。
items.ex2_en: Specialized digestive enzymes quickly break down complex dietary carbohydrates into absorbable simple sugars.
items.ex2_zh: 专门的消化酶迅速将复杂的膳食碳水化合物分解为可吸收的单糖。

items.def_en: to become stale, sour, or unfit to eat or drink
items.ex_en: Smell this opened carton of milk to check if it has gone off.
items.ex_zh: 闻闻这盒开封的牛奶，看看它是不是已经变酸变质了。

items.def_en: 1. To rot or cause something to rot through natural organic decomposition. 2. To gradually become bad or deteriorate in quality, strength, or condition.
items.ex_en: Without regular brushing and flossing, your teeth will rapidly decay from bacteria.
items.ex_zh: 如果不定期刷牙和使用牙线，你的牙齿很快就会因细菌而腐蚀蛀烂。
items.ex2_en: Damp acidic rainwater decays the exposed wooden facade of historic buildings over time.
items.ex2_zh: 潮湿的酸雨随着时间的推移腐蚀破坏着历史建筑裸露的木质立面。

items.def_zh: （使）变酸，（使）变馊；（使关系或心情）变糟，恶化
items.def_en: 1. To make or become sour or acidic, especially as a result of fermentation or spoilage. 2. To make or become unfriendly, unpleasant, or bitter.
items.ex_en: Leaving the opened fruit juice in the sun will quickly sour its taste.
items.ex_zh: 把开封的果汁放在太阳底下很快就会让其发酵变酸。
items.ex2_en: Unpasteurized milk sours rapidly when kept on the kitchen counter in hot weather.
items.ex2_zh: 未灭菌的牛奶在炎热天气下放在厨房台面上很快就会变酸。

items.def_en: To decay, or make something decay, naturally and gradually through the action of bacteria or fungi.
items.ex_en: Untreated wooden fence posts will quickly rot in this damp, swampy soil.
items.ex_zh: 未经处理的木制篱笆桩在这片潮湿泥泞的土壤中很快就会腐烂。
items.ex2_en: Excessive ground moisture and fungal spores rot the roots of sensitive potted plants.
items.ex2_zh: 过多的土壤水分和真菌孢子会使敏感盆栽植物的根系腐烂。

items.def_zh: 逐渐腐烂殆尽；完全腐化
items.def_en: to decay progressively until little or nothing remains
items.ex_en: The abandoned wooden pier slowly rotted away under the relentless ocean surf.
items.ex_zh: 废弃的木制码头在无休止的海浪冲刷下慢慢腐烂殆尽。

items.def_en: to decay and break down organically into simpler chemical parts
items.ex_en: Bacteria and fungi help decompose fallen trees on the moist forest floor.
items.ex_zh: 细菌和真菌有助于分解潮湿森林地面上的倒伏树木。
items.ex2_en: Organic kitchen scraps decompose naturally inside the aerated outdoor compost bin over weeks.
items.ex2_zh: 有机厨房残渣在通风的室外堆肥桶内经数周时间自然分解。

items.def_en: to become septic, producing pus, rot, or advancing putrid inflammation
items.ex_en: Without prompt antiseptic cleaning, the open wound will quickly fester and swell.
items.ex_zh: 如果不及时进行消毒清理，开放性伤口很快就会化脓溃烂。

items.def_zh: 腐烂化脓；散发恶臭变质
items.def_en: to decompose with the emission of a foul, fetid odor through bacterial action
items.ex_en: The discarded organic waste began to putrefy in the sweltering summer heat.
items.ex_zh: 被丢弃的有机废弃物在酷热的夏日暑气中开始腐烂发臭。
items.ex2_en: Intense summer heat and bacteria putrefy uncovered butcher scraps within a single afternoon.
items.ex2_zh: 酷烈的夏日暑气和细菌在短短一个下午内就使裸露的屠宰残渣腐烂发臭。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate biological and organic breakdown, progressive tissue putrefaction, or chemical degradation of perishables from edible freshness into stench, acidity, or decomposed matter.
groups.summary_zh: 指有机物因菌类或化学作用由新鲜变为酸败、腐坏及分解分解。
groups.desc_en: Undergoes biochemical or organic breakdown, leading to structural rot, foulness, and loss of original freshness or integrity.
groups.desc_zh: 发生生物化学层面的分解变质，导致有机物腐败、发酸或丧失原始完好性。
groups.nuance_en: spoil: deteriorate and become unfit for use or consumption (food / fruit / milk) · sour: spoil biochemically through acid fermentation (milk / wine / relations) · rot: decay naturally through fungal/bacterial action (wood / corpse / teeth) · decompose: break down fundamentally into constituent elemental parts (corpse / matter / leaves)
groups.nuance_zh: spoil: 变质走味至不可食用 (food / fruit / milk) · sour: 酸败发酵或变酸变劣 (milk / wine / relations) · rot: 细菌真菌侵蚀的生化溃烂腐烂 (wood / corpse / teeth) · decompose: 动植物残骸彻底化解为基质组分 (corpse / matter / leaves)

groups.name: Deep Aversion & Hate · 厌恶与憎恨 (Dislike, Loathe, Abhor)
groups.tip: 从轻微反感到切齿痛恨的负面情感

items.def_en: to experience a feeling of aversion or lack of liking for someone or something
items.ex_en: Most cats genuinely dislike taking wet baths with soap and warm water.
items.ex_zh: 大多数猫打心底里不喜欢用肥皂和温水泡澡。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) stop liking someone and become hostile, antagonistic, or resentful toward them
items.ex_en: The voters began to turn against the mayor after the recent corruption scandal.
items.ex_zh: 最近的腐败丑闻爆出后，选民们开始转而敌视市长。

items.def_en: to look down on with disdain and intense, contemptuous dislike
items.ex_en: He earned everyone's contempt because he openly despised those less fortunate than himself.
items.ex_zh: 他公开鄙视那些境遇不如自己的人，因而招致了所有人的蔑视。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) experience a feeling of intense physical disgust or strong moral repulsion toward something
items.ex_en: Her moral conscience revolted against the cruel methods used by the interrogation team.
items.ex_zh: 审讯团队所使用的残忍手段让她在道德良知上感到极度反感。

items.def_en: To feel intense dislike, hostility, or aversion toward someone or something.
items.ex_en: They deeply hate each other after years of bitter legal disputes over property.
items.ex_zh: 经过多年关于财产的痛苦法律争端，他们彼此深恶痛绝。

items.def_en: To hate or dislike someone or something very intensely.
items.ex_en: The principled diplomat detests hypocrisy and dishonesty in all international negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 这位有原则的外交官在所有国际谈判中都痛恨虚伪与欺诈。

items.def_zh: 极其厌恶，憎恨，极其反感
items.def_en: To feel intense hatred and disgust for someone or something.
items.ex_en: I loathe dishonest politicians who make empty promises just to win votes.
items.ex_zh: 我极其厌恶那些只为赢得选票而许下空头承诺的不诚实政客。

items.def_en: to detest vehemently and view with profound moral hatred
items.ex_en: The pious puritan truly abominates all forms of cruelty and wicked deceit.
items.ex_zh: 这位虔诚的清教徒由衷地痛恨一切形式的残酷与邪恶欺骗。

items.def_zh: 深恶痛绝，痛恨，强烈反感
items.def_en: (formal) To hate a way of behaving or thinking deeply, especially because it seems morally wrong.
items.ex_en: Civilized societies abhor all forms of torture and arbitrary detention of citizens.
items.ex_zh: 文明社会对针对公民的任何形式的酷刑和任意拘押都深恶痛绝。

items.def_en: (formal) To feel or express extreme hatred or loathing for someone or something; to curse.
items.ex_en: The citizens gathered to execrate the brutal tyrant responsible for their suffering.
items.ex_zh: 市民们聚集在一起，谴责并诅咒导致他们受苦的残暴暴君。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey intense emotional repulsion, ranging from conscious strong aversion to moral disgust and vehement denunciation.
groups.summary_zh: 表达从强烈的个人反感、极度厌恶到道德唾弃的情感阶梯。
groups.desc_en: Harbors extreme, visceral antipathy or moral revulsion toward an object or person, far beyond mild disapproval or non-preference.
groups.desc_zh: 对客体产生极度生理性厌恶或道德层面的唾弃憎恨，远甚于寻常的偏好不合。
groups.nuance_en: detest: feel intense, active dislike combined with contempt (hypocrisy / violence / arrogance) · loathe: feel deep, sickened physical or visceral revulsion (liars / injustice / sight) · despise: look down on with sheer disdain and complete lack of respect (cowardice / weakness / traitor) · abominate: view with ultimate moral or religious abhorrence (cruelty / sin / tyranny)
groups.nuance_zh: detest: 带有强烈反感与鄙弃的深恶痛绝 (hypocrisy / violence / arrogance) · loathe: 生理性的胃部翻涌与作呕反感 (liars / injustice / sight) · despise: 认定其卑贱可鄙而不屑一顾 (cowardice / weakness / traitor) · abominate: 视若亵渎或道德极恶的痛恨 (cruelty / sin / tyranny)

groups.name: Deflect & Tilt · 偏离与倾斜 (Deviate, Veer, Bank)
groups.tip: 角度倾斜偏转或偏离原定轨道

items.def_en: (+ sth) to hit a surface and deflect away at an angle
items.ex_en: The rubber ball bounced off the brick wall and rolled into the bushes.
items.ex_zh: 橡胶球从砖墙上反弹偏折，滚进了灌木丛中。

items.def_en: [I/T] to tilt sideways when turning, especially of an aircraft
items.ex_en: The pilot banked the aircraft steeply to line up with the narrow runway.
items.ex_zh: 飞行员让飞机大幅侧倾，以对准狭窄的跑道。
items.ex2_en: The agile fighter jet banked sharply to avoid incoming radar detection over mountains.
items.ex2_zh: 敏捷的战斗机急剧倾斜机身飞行，以避开山峦上空的雷达探测。

items.def_zh: 倾斜，使倾斜；说黑话，讲行话
items.def_en: 1. To tilt, slant, or lean to one side; to set or turn something at an angle. 2. To use hypocritical, pious, or specialized jargon.
items.ex_en: The old timber shed canted dangerously toward the overgrown garden after the storm.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨过后，那座旧木棚危险地朝向杂草丛生的花园倾斜。
items.ex2_en: The reckless driver canted the heavy trailer sharply onto two wheels during turns.
items.ex2_zh: 鲁莽的司机在转弯时将沉重的拖车猛烈倾斜，仅剩两轮着地。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cause something to turn aside from a straight path, or to bounce off at an angle
items.ex_en: The metal shield was designed to deflect incoming shrapnel away from soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 这面金属护盾旨在使飞来的弹片偏斜，保护士兵。
items.ex2_en: The fast ball deflected off the stone post and missed the open goal.
items.ex2_zh: 疾速飞来的球撞在石柱上偏离了方向，错失了空门。

items.def_en: (physics) (of waves, particles, or radiation) To scatter or reflect back toward the direction of origin; to cause this to happen.
items.ex_en: Dense atmospheric clouds backscatter solar radiation directly into the darkness of space.
items.ex_zh: 浓密的大气云层将太阳辐射直接反向散射回黑暗的太空中。
items.ex2_en: Incoming laser pulses backscatter predictably from dense microscopic aerosol particles in cloud layers.
items.ex2_zh: 射入的激光脉冲可预见地从云层中密集的微小气溶胶颗粒上发生后向散射。

items.def_zh: 偏离直行方向；突然转向
items.def_en: to deviate sharply from an established course or alignment
items.ex_en: The speeding vehicle suddenly sheared off from the marked lane into the ditch.
items.ex_zh: 超速行驶的车辆突然偏离标线车道，冲进了水沟。

items.def_en: to abruptly change direction and move away from an intended course
items.ex_en: The distracted driver veered off the icy road and struck a wooden post.
items.ex_zh: 分心的司机偏离了结冰的道路，撞上了一根木桩。

items.def_zh: 突然改变方向；猛然转向
items.def_en: (+ off/away) to change direction or course suddenly
items.ex_en: The sailboat veered sharply to the left to avoid a submerged rock.
items.ex_zh: 帆船猛然向左转向，以避开一处暗礁。

items.def_zh: 急转弯；突然转向以避开
items.def_en: [I/T] to change direction abruptly, especially to avoid an obstacle
items.ex_en: She swerved the car onto the gravel shoulder to avoid the falling rock.
items.ex_zh: 她猛打方向盘将车拐到碎石路肩上，以避开坠落的巨石。
items.ex2_en: The overloaded transport truck swerved violently to avoid colliding with an oncoming vehicle.
items.ex2_zh: 超载的运输卡车猛然急转方向，以避免与迎面而来的车辆相撞。

items.def_zh: 降落在（跑道）近侧，落后于（目标）；射击脱靶，未达到
items.def_en: 1. (aviation) To land an aircraft short of the runway. 2. To fall short of a target, goal, or expected amount.
items.ex_en: Due to poor visibility, the cargo flight undershot the runway during landing.
items.ex_zh: 由于能见度低，这架货运航班在着陆时降落在了跑道近侧外。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe physical entities or trajectories departing from an intended straight path, horizontal level, or direct alignment, either through mechanical tilting, aerodynamic banking, or physical scattering.
groups.summary_zh: 描述物体或运动轨迹发生角度倾斜、偏离直线路线或散射的动作与状态。
groups.desc_en: Alters direction or angular alignment away from an original straight trajectory or level plane, either through impact or steered divergence.
groups.desc_zh: 因撞击反弹或主动偏转而脱离原定直线轨迹或水平基准，区别于单纯的原地旋转。
groups.nuance_en: deflect: cause to turn aside from a straight course upon impact (bullet / blow / blame) · veer: change direction suddenly or erratically (car / wind / conversation) · bank: tilt laterally when rounding a curve (aircraft / cyclist / turn) · cant: tilt or slant to an oblique angle away from vertical/horizontal (deck / hull / wheel)
groups.nuance_zh: deflect: 受到击打或格挡后受力偏斜 (bullet / blow / blame) · veer: 骤然急转或偏离航向轨道 (car / wind / conversation) · bank: 飞行器或车辆转弯时的外侧倾斜 (aircraft / cyclist / turn) · cant: 倾斜并歪向一侧偏离水平或垂直轴 (deck / hull / wheel)

groups.name: Deform, Pulp & Crush Soft Matter · 挤压、捏柔与捣碎 (Squish, Knead, Puree)
groups.tip: 用力挤压使其变形碎裂

items.def_en: (+ sth) to crush food or other soft matter into a soft, pulpy mass
items.ex_en: Use a fork to mash up the ripe bananas before adding flour.
items.ex_zh: 在加入面粉之前，先用叉子把熟透的香蕉捣烂成糊。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to press or flatten something soft or flexible into a smaller or flatter shape
items.ex_en: He squashed down the overflowing trash bag to make room for more waste.
items.ex_zh: 他把装得过满的垃圾袋压扁，以便腾出空间装更多垃圾。

items.def_en: to crush soft food or matter into a soft, uniform mass using pressure
items.ex_en: She patiently mashed the boiled potatoes until they reached a creamy consistency.
items.ex_zh: 她耐心地把煮熟的土豆捣烂，直到它们达到细腻的糊状。

items.def_en: [I/T] to crush or squeeze something flat, soft, or out of shape through heavy pressure
items.ex_en: Someone accidentally squashed the soft loaf of bread under a heavy carton.
items.ex_zh: 有人不小心在重纸箱下把柔软的面包压扁了。
items.ex2_en: Overripe bananas squash easily if packed underneath heavy canned food in grocery bags.
items.ex2_zh: 过熟的香蕉如果在杂货袋里被压在沉重的罐头食品下面很容易被压扁烂。

items.def_en: To crush or squeeze something soft into a flat shape; to make a soft, wet squeezing sound.
items.ex_en: The child accidentally squished the ripe strawberry between his sticky little fingers.
items.ex_zh: 孩子不小心用黏糊糊的小手把熟透的草莓捏烂了。
items.ex2_en: Wet coastal mud squished loudly under our heavy hiking boots during the hike.
items.ex2_zh: 徒步旅行时，潮湿的海滨泥浆在我们沉重的登山靴下发出咯吱的挤压声。

items.def_zh: 把（蔬菜、水果等）捣成泥，压成糊
items.def_en: To crush, mash, or blend food into a smooth, thick liquid paste.
items.ex_en: The chef carefully pureed the cooked carrots into a smooth, savory soup.
items.ex_zh: 主厨把煮熟的胡萝卜细心捣成泥，做成了顺滑可口的浓汤。

items.def_zh: 揉，捏（面团、黏土等）；按摩，推拿
items.def_en: To press, stretch, and fold dough or clay with the hands; to massage muscles firmly.
items.ex_en: He kneaded the sourdough firmly on the wooden board for ten minutes.
items.ex_zh: 他在木板上用力揉了十分钟酸面团。

items.def_zh: 揉皱，压扁，挤压；缩紧；发出嘎吱声
items.def_en: to crush or squeeze something into a tight or compact shape; to make a loud crunching sound.
items.ex_en: Frustrated with the draft, she scrunched the paper into a tight ball.
items.ex_zh: 因为对草稿感到沮丧，她把纸揉皱成了一个紧实的纸团。
items.ex2_en: Dry autumn leaves scrunch noisily underfoot whenever joggers run through the city park.
items.ex2_zh: 每当慢跑者跑过城市公园时，脚下干燥的秋叶就会发出咯吱咯吱的碎裂声。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to crush or reduce pliable matter completely into a wet pulp
items.ex_en: The heavy rain pulped up the cardboard boxes left on the back porch.
items.ex_zh: 大雨把留在后门廊上的硬纸板箱彻底浇成了一团烂浆。

items.def_en: [I/T] to press something with extreme force so that it breaks down into small particles or pulp
items.ex_en: The heavy industrial roller crushed the discarded plastic bottles into flat sheets.
items.ex_zh: 重型工业压路机将废弃的塑料瓶压碎成了平整的薄片。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe forcefully compressing, mashing, or manipulating soft, yielding, or pliable substances until their internal structure collapses, softens, or blends into a pulp. They differ by physical outcome, ranging from gentle working of dough to total liquifying or wet crushing.
groups.summary_zh: 施力挤压、揉捏或捣碎柔软易变形物体使其变扁或成糊状。
groups.desc_en: Applies compressive, kneading, or crushing force to malleable or soft materials to flatten, pulp, or distort their physical form.
groups.desc_zh: 对柔软或塑性物料施加挤压、捏揉或捣碾，迫使其形变并化为泥团，区别于对硬物的击碎。
groups.nuance_en: squash: compress flat or out of shape with heavy downward force (bug / tin / fruit) · mash: crush into a uniform soft pulp or mass (potatoes / bananas / grain) · puree: process cooked food into a velvety, creamy paste (vegetables / soup / fruit) · knead: repeatedly press, fold, and stretch a pliable mass (dough / clay / muscles)
groups.nuance_zh: squash: 垂直重压导致压扁或压烂 (bug / tin / fruit) · mash: 捣碾成粗泥块状 (potatoes / bananas / grain) · puree: 料理搅打成细腻膏状或幼滑浓汤 (vegetables / soup / fruit) · knead: 反复按压推揉面团或舒展肌肉 (dough / clay / muscles)

groups.name: Defraud & Fleece · 欺诈与剥夺 (Defraud, Swindle, Fleece)
groups.tip: 巧取豪夺榨取他人钱财

items.def_zh: (+ sb + out of sth) 骗取（某人的财物）
items.def_en: (+ sb + out of sth) to trick someone into giving away money or property by deceit
items.ex_en: The slick salesman conned the elderly widow out of her retirement savings.
items.ex_zh: 那个油嘴滑舌的推销员骗走了那位老年寡妇的退休积蓄。

items.def_zh: (+ sb + out of sth) 诈取；骗走
items.def_en: (+ sb + out of sth) to cheat someone out of what is rightfully theirs through petty swindling
items.ex_en: The dishonest mechanic tried to diddle him out of twenty extra dollars.
items.ex_zh: 那个不老实的汽修工试图多讹他二十美元。

items.def_en: 1. (informal) To obtain a lot of money from someone by overcharging or tricking them. 2. To shear the wool from a sheep.
items.ex_en: The unscrupulous taxi driver fleeced the confused tourists for a short ride.
items.ex_zh: 无良出租车司机向晕头转向的游客漫天要价，狠敲了一笔竹杠。

items.def_en: (informal) To cheat or defraud someone of money; to overcharge someone.
items.ex_en: The corrupt card dealer rooked inexperienced gamblers out of their entire stakes.
items.ex_zh: 那个腐败的发牌员把毫无经验的赌徒们的所有赌注都诈骗一空。

items.def_en: To cheat someone in order to get money, goods, or possessions from them.
items.ex_en: He organized a fake charity to swindle generous donors out of money.
items.ex_zh: 他组织了一个虚假慈善机构，以骗取慷慨捐赠者的钱财。

items.def_en: to cheat someone out of what is due to them, especially money
items.ex_en: The contractor bilked several vulnerable subcontractors out of their rightful project payments.
items.ex_zh: 该承包商赖掉了几家弱势分包商应得的工程款。

items.def_en: to trick or deceive someone in order to take something from them
items.ex_en: The cunning imposter managed to cozen the naive lord of his family fortune.
items.ex_zh: 狡猾的冒牌货设法哄骗了天真的贵族，卷走了他的家族财产。

items.def_zh: (+ sb) 敲诈；狠狠坑骗（钱财）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cheat someone by overcharging them or stealing their money
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_zh: 以不正当手段骗取或勒索（金钱）
items.def_en: (+ of) to obtain money from someone by deceit, extortion, or harsh exaction
items.ex_en: Corrupt tax collectors mulcted the poor villagers of their hard-earned autumn grain.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的税吏以苛捐杂税勒索了贫苦村民辛苦换来的秋粮。

items.def_en: (+ of) To trick someone in order to get money, property, or rights from them illegally.
items.ex_en: The rogue accountant defrauded the charitable foundation of millions of development dollars.
items.ex_zh: 那名劣迹斑斑的会计诈骗了慈善基金会数百万美元的发展资金。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe illicitly depriving a person or organization of money or property through calculated misrepresentation, deceit, or exorbitant overcharging.
groups.summary_zh: 以蓄意虚假陈述、骗术或敲竹杠手段非法牟取受害者财物。
groups.desc_en: Strikes specifically at someone's financial or material assets through predatory swindles, extortionate margins, or sharp practice.
groups.desc_zh: 专门针对他人资财，运用欺罔、宰割或敲骨吸髓手段进行巧取豪夺，强调财产剥夺。
groups.nuance_en: swindle: deprive of money through deliberate, calculated deceit (pensioners / investors / company) · fleece: strip someone mercilessly of excessive money or assets (tourists / victims / consumers) · bilk: evade paying debts or cheat out of expected funds (creditors / government / charity) · cozen: beguile or subtly trick out of property through artifice (estate / funds / master)
groups.nuance_zh: swindle: 设局吞没巨额款项或资产 (pensioners / investors / company) · fleece: 如剪羊毛般剥光搜刮其资财 (tourists / victims / consumers) · bilk: 赖账逃债或克扣骗走应付钱财 (creditors / government / charity) · cozen: 甜言巧语使阴招套取钱物 (estate / funds / master)

groups.name: Demolish & Level · 夷平与摧毁 (Flatten, Demolish, Level)
groups.tip: 彻底扫平建筑夷为平地

items.def_en: (+ sth) to demolish a building or structure so that it falls to the ground
items.ex_en: The old factory was knocked down to make way for a modern shopping center.
items.ex_zh: 旧工厂被拆除，为一座现代化的购物中心腾出了空间。

items.def_en: to level or knock down a structure flat to the ground
items.ex_en: The powerful tornado flattened several historic farmhouses in less than five minutes.
items.ex_zh: 强烈的龙卷风在不到五分钟内将几座历史悠久的农舍夷为平地。
items.ex2_en: The heavy corrugated cardboard box flattened under the weight of stacked moving crates.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的瓦楞纸箱在堆叠的搬家木箱重量下被压得扁平。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 彻底拆毁（大型结构）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to deliberately demolish a building or large structure
items.ex_en: The city council decided to pull down the derelict textile mill yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 市议会昨天决定拆毁那座废弃的纺织厂。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to demolish or dismantle a building, wall, or structure completely
items.ex_en: The old factory was torn down to make way for a modern shopping mall.
items.ex_zh: 那座旧工厂被拆除，以便改建现代化的购物中心。

items.def_en: to completely flatten a building or area of land
items.ex_en: Heavy artillery barrages leveled the entire downtown quarter during the fierce battle.
items.ex_zh: 在激战中，沉重的炮火轰击将整个市中心街区夷为平地。

items.def_en: to pull or knock down a building or structure completely
items.ex_en: The construction crew will demolish the unsafe pedestrian bridge tomorrow at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 施工队将于明天拂晓彻底拆除那座危险的人行天桥。

items.def_en: to destroy something or someone completely so that nothing remains
items.ex_en: The devastating tsunami annihilated the coastal village, leaving only scattered debris behind.
items.ex_zh: 毁灭性的海啸彻底摧毁了沿海村庄，只留下散落的瓦砾。

items.def_zh: 夷平，彻底摧毁，把……夷为平地
items.def_en: To completely destroy or knock down a building, town, or settlement to the ground.
items.ex_en: Invading forces razed the ancient fortress to the ground after a siege.
items.ex_zh: 入侵的军队在围城之后将那座古老的要塞彻底夷为平地。

items.def_zh: 彻底粉碎，摧毁；将……磨成粉
items.def_en: 1. To crush or grind something into a fine powder. 2. (informal) To defeat or destroy someone or something completely.
items.ex_en: Our home team pulverized the defending champions with a decisive blowout victory.
items.ex_zh: 我们的主队以一场决定性的大胜彻底击溃了卫冕冠军。

items.def_zh: 夷平，彻底摧毁（raze 的变体写法）；擦掉，抹去
items.def_en: (archaic or variant of raze) To completely destroy or level a building or settlement to the ground.
items.ex_en: The relentless conqueror commanded his troops to rase every monument of rebellion.
items.ex_zh: 残酷的征服者命令他的军队夷平所有叛乱纪念碑。

groups.summary_en: Destructive agents systematically or cataclysmically tear down, shatter, or flatten structures, settlements, or physical substances into ground level or fine dust. Intensity escalates from structural flattening to total molecular pulverization.
groups.summary_zh: 对建筑物或物体施加极强破坏力，使其倒塌、平毁或化为碎末。
groups.desc_en: Uses overwhelming structural violence or mechanical force to tear down built structures completely to ground level, contrasting with partial damaging.
groups.desc_zh: 运用巨大机械力或破坏力将建构物彻底拆毁瓦解至地表，区别于局部破损。
groups.nuance_en: demolish: methodically or explosively pull down a structure (building / stadium / wall) · raze: level completely and smoothly to the ground (city / village / fortress) · tear down: physically dismantle and rip apart a structure (shack / monument / fence) · flatten: knock down completely flat by sheer impact or blast (forest / homes / defenses)
groups.nuance_zh: demolish: 爆破或工程化全面拆毁建筑 (building / stadium / wall) · raze: 斩草除根式彻底夷为平地 (city / village / fortress) · tear down: 人工或机械扒倒、拆除 (shack / monument / fence) · flatten: 冲击波或重力碾压致使其整体扁平贴地 (forest / homes / defenses)

groups.name: Depart & Exit · 离开与出发 (Leave, Depart, Scram)
groups.tip: 从某处起步动身

items.def_zh: 离开，动身；留下，剩下；委托，交托
items.def_en: 1. To go away from a person, place, or situation. 2. To let something remain behind or remain in a particular condition. 3. To deliver or entrust something to someone.
items.ex_en: She decided to leave the crowded party early because of a headache.
items.ex_zh: 由于头痛，她决定提早离开拥挤的聚会。

items.def_en: [I/T] to go out of or leave a building, stage, or enclosed space
items.ex_en: Please ensure you exit the auditorium through the marked emergency doors quickly.
items.ex_zh: 请务必通过有标记的应急门迅速离开礼堂。

items.def_en: (+ for/on) to begin a journey or expedition
items.ex_en: The adventurous mountaineers set off for the icy summit before the sunrise.
items.ex_zh: 富有冒险精神的登山者在日出前启程前往冰封的山顶。

items.def_en: to leave a place quickly or permanently, often upon command
items.ex_en: The furious landlord ordered the noisy tenants to pack up and clear out.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的房东命令吵闹的租客打包行李赶紧搬离。

items.def_en: to depart, especially in an informal or slightly rude directive
items.ex_en: The gruff guard told the loitering youths to shove off immediately.
items.ex_zh: 粗暴的守卫叫那些闲荡的年轻人立刻滚开。

items.def_zh: 离开；动身（尤指匆忙或突然）
items.def_en: to leave or depart, especially abruptly or quickly
items.ex_en: He took off without saying goodbye as soon as the police arrived.
items.ex_zh: 警察一到，他连招呼都没打就匆匆溜走了。

items.def_en: to start a journey or leave a place to go somewhere else
items.ex_en: We should head out early to avoid the morning traffic.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该早点出发，避开早高峰。

items.def_en: to begin moving away from a stationary starting point
items.ex_en: The ceremonial procession finally began to move off toward the city hall.
items.ex_zh: 典礼游行队伍终于起步，朝着市政厅的方向前行。

items.def_zh: 离开，启程；偏离，背离（常规等）
items.def_en: 1. (+ from/for) (formal) To leave a place, especially to start a journey. 2. (+ from) To deviate or stray from an established rule, practice, or standard.
items.ex_en: The express train is scheduled to depart from platform nine at noon.
items.ex_zh: 这趟特快列车定于中午从九号站台启程出发。

items.def_en: 1. (informal, chiefly imperative) To leave immediately and quickly.
items.ex_en: The angry shopkeeper shouted at the trespassers to scram off his property.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的店主冲着侵入者大喊，叫他们滚出自己的地盘。

groups.summary_en: An agent moves away from a place or starting point, spanning neutral daily departures, formal timetabled embarkations, and colloquial abrupt or hurried departures.
groups.summary_zh: 离开某处或动身启程，涵盖日常表达、正式班次出发及口语急促离开。
groups.desc_en: Initiates motion to quit a location or embark on a journey, ranging from formal departure to urgent, informal absconding.
groups.desc_zh: 采取行动脱离某处空间或启程出发，涵盖正式起步、撤离至口语化的溜走。
groups.nuance_en: depart: set out or leave formally according to schedule (train / delegation / life) · set off: embark actively on an expedition or journey (trail / sunrise / quest) · shove off: push off a shore or take one's leave casually/curtly (boat / crowd / visitors) · clear out: vacate a room or premises completely and hurriedly (tenants / squatters / office)
groups.nuance_zh: depart: 循时刻表或正规仪轨起程离去 (train / delegation / life) · set off: 整装启程奔赴旅程或任务 (trail / sunrise / quest) · shove off: 划桨撑船离岸或粗鲁打发离场 (boat / crowd / visitors) · clear out: 迅速清场并彻底腾空搬离 (tenants / squatters / office)

groups.name: Depletion of Energy & Physical Exhaustion · 疲劳与虚脱 (Tire, Fatigue, Exhaust)
groups.tip: 精力从困倦到彻底耗尽

items.def_en: gradually lose strength, momentum, or stamina until coming to a stop
items.ex_en: Her initial burst of energy petered out during the final marathon miles.
items.ex_zh: 在马拉松最后的几英里中，她最初的充沛精力逐渐衰竭殆尽。

items.def_en: 1. To become tired or make someone feel tired. 2. (+ of) To become bored with or lose interest in something.
items.ex_en: The uphill march quickly tired the inexperienced hikers after only three miles.
items.ex_zh: 仅仅走了三英里，上坡行军就迅速让毫无经验的徒步者感到劳累。
items.ex2_en: The young marathon runner tired visibly toward the final two miles of competition.
items.ex2_zh: 年轻的马拉松选手在比赛最后两英里时明显露出了疲惫之态。

items.def_en: (+ sb) reduce someone's health, vitality, or physical energy through strain or overwork
items.ex_en: Months of relentless night shifts had run down his immune system terribly.
items.ex_zh: 数月不休的夜班彻底搞垮了他的身体，使他精疲力竭。

items.def_en: (+ sb) tire someone out thoroughly so they lack energy
items.ex_en: A long afternoon chasing energetic puppies completely tuckered out the young boy.
items.ex_zh: 追着精力旺盛的小狗玩了一整个下午，把小男孩累得精疲力竭。

items.def_zh: 使筋疲力尽，使极度疲劳；疲劳；（材料）产生疲劳破坏
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel extremely tired, or to become exhausted. 2. (technical) To weaken or become weakened from repeated stress (of materials).
items.ex_en: The grueling trek across the desolate dunes fatigued the weary desert travelers.
items.ex_zh: 穿过荒凉沙丘的艰苦跋涉使疲惫的沙漠旅行者极度劳累。
items.ex2_en: Repeated mechanical stress causes metal components to fatigue and eventually crack under pressure.
items.ex2_zh: 反复的机械应力会导致金属部件发生疲劳并在受压下最终开裂。

items.def_zh: （使）精疲力竭，（使）疲惫不堪；（因过度接触等而使）厌倦
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To make someone tired, exhausted, or bored through overwork or excess.
items.ex_en: Decades of superficial high-society chatter had jaded the once enthusiastic playwright.
items.ex_zh: 数十年上流社会的虚浮客套让这位曾经热情洋溢的剧作家心力交瘁、深感厌倦。

items.def_en: become completely exhausted through prolonged overwork or intense effort
items.ex_en: She risked burning out if she continued working seventy hours every week.
items.ex_zh: 如果每周继续工作七十个小时，她就有可能彻底累垮。

items.def_zh: 使筋疲力尽，使疲惫不堪
items.def_en: to exhaust someone's stamina completely through hard labor or exertion
items.ex_en: Running after toddlers all afternoon completely wore me out.
items.ex_zh: 整个下午跟在幼儿屁股后面跑让我筋疲力尽。

items.def_en: to drain someone completely of energy, strength, or vitality
items.ex_en: The rigorous training drills exhausted the new recruits within just two hours.
items.ex_zh: 严格的训练演习在短短两个小时内就耗尽了新兵的所有体力。

items.def_zh: 使力竭倒地；使虚脱卧床
items.def_en: to reduce someone to extreme physical weakness, helplessness, or collapse
items.ex_en: A sudden bout of severe fever prostrated the explorer in his tent.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的剧烈高烧使探险家虚脱倒在帐篷里。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scale frame denote progressive loss of strength, vitality, or endurance in living beings through exertion or stress. They scale from mild loss of freshness (tire), through sustained clinical wearying (fatigue, jade), to ultimate depletion and collapse (exhaust, prostrate).
groups.summary_zh: 描述体力或精力从轻度发困乏力、持久劳损，到完全衰竭力竭的递进状态。
groups.desc_en: Depletes physiological, mental, or mechanical vigor under sustained stress, descending toward utter exhaustion or burnout.
groups.desc_zh: 在持续应力或劳碌下载荷耗尽，经历从初现倦意至全面虚脱、衰竭。
groups.nuance_en: tire: begin to feel weary and lose physical freshness (legs / eyes / patient) · fatigue: suffer deep, systemic physiological or material exhaustion (muscles / metal / troops) · tucker out: thoroughly fatigue to the point of collapse (toddler / puppy / runners) · burn out: completely exhaust mental/physical reserves through chronic overwork (employees / doctor / teachers)
groups.nuance_zh: tire: 活力初现疲惫与精力衰减 (legs / eyes / patient) · fatigue: 全身系统性劳损或金属疲劳 (muscles / metal / troops) · tucker out: 彻底耗尽体力瘫软无力 (toddler / puppy / runners) · burn out: 长期压力导致身心枯竭崩溃 (employees / doctor / teachers)

groups.name: Descend & Submerge · 下沉与沉没 (Sediment, Sink, Submerge)
groups.tip: 由降落沉降直至完全没入

items.def_en: to sink down gradually to the bottom of a liquid
items.ex_en: The muddy sediment took several silent hours to settle to the lakebed.
items.ex_zh: 浑浊的沉积物过了几个安静的小时才逐渐沉降到湖底。

items.def_en: (of suspended particles) separate and sink to the bottom of a liquid
items.ex_en: Leave the cloudy mixture undisturbed until the heavy particles settle out completely.
items.ex_zh: 将浑浊的混合液静置，直到沉重的颗粒完全沉淀析出。

items.def_en: to settle to the bottom of a liquid, or to cause solid particles to settle.
items.ex_en: The suspended minerals began to sediment along the bottom of the beaker.
items.ex_zh: 悬浮的矿物质开始在烧杯底部沉降。
items.ex2_en: Industrial centrifuges sediment heavy colloidal impurities from chemical solutions rapidly within minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 工业离心机在数分钟内就能迅速使化学溶液中的重胶体杂质沉降下来。

items.def_en: sink beneath the surface of the water
items.ex_en: The damaged fishing boat started to go down after hitting the reef.
items.ex_zh: 触礁之后，受损的渔船开始沉入水下。

items.def_zh: （使）下沉，（使）沉没；沉降，下陷；下降，衰退
items.def_en: 1. to go down below the surface of water or liquid, or to make something do this. 2. to move downward or fall to a lower level.
items.ex_en: Heavy iron anchors will sink rapidly once they are dropped into the ocean.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的铁锚一旦抛入海中，便会迅速下沉。
items.ex2_en: The fierce maritime storm sank three commercial fishing boats near the rocky shoreline.
items.ex2_zh: 凶猛的海洋风暴在岩石海岸附近击沉了三艘商用渔船。

items.def_zh: （使）下沉，（使）沉没（sink 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: past tense and past participle of sink: to go down below the surface of liquid, or cause to do so.
items.ex_en: The torpedo struck the freighter, which sunk within a matter of minutes.
items.ex_zh: 鱼雷击中了货轮，货轮在短短几分钟内就沉没了。
items.ex2_en: The pirate vessel fired explosive cannonballs and sunk the merchant galleon without mercy.
items.ex2_zh: 海盗船发射了爆炸性加农炮弹，毫不留情地击沉了商用大帆船。

items.def_en: to go completely under the surface of water or liquid, or to put something completely under water.
items.ex_en: The high tide threatened to submerge the coastal road beneath deep saltwater.
items.ex_zh: 涨潮眼看就要将沿海公路完全淹没在深海水中。
items.ex2_en: The research submarine submerged quietly into the dark depths of the Pacific Ocean.
items.ex2_zh: 科考潜艇悄无声息地潜入了太平洋黑暗的深水之中。

items.def_zh: （使）下沉，（使）沉没（sink 的过去分词，现多作形容词）
items.def_en: (archaic) past participle of sink: to go down below the surface of liquid.
items.ex_en: The ancient galleon had sunken deep beneath the dark, unforgiving waves.
items.ex_zh: 那艘古老的大帆船已深深沉入昏暗而无情的海浪之下。

items.def_en: (of a ship) to fill with water and sink completely beneath the surface
items.ex_en: Battered by massive waves, the old cargo vessel began to founder rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 在巨浪的撞击下，这艘旧货船开始迅速沉没。

items.def_en: [I/T] to submerge and perish in water, or flood completely
items.ex_en: Torrents of river water rushed into the basement and threatened to drown everything.
items.ex_zh: 湍急的河水涌入地下室，眼看就要将一切彻底淹没。
items.ex2_en: Inexperienced swimmers can easily drown in violent rip currents along unguarded ocean beaches.
items.ex2_zh: 没有经验的游泳者在无巡视的海滩上极易溺亡于凶猛的离岸流中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame track the physical progression of downward motion into or beneath a liquid or sediment, scaling from slow particulate settling to complete underwater engulfment.
groups.summary_zh: 描绘物体在液体中下落、沉积直至被彻底没顶吞噬的沉溺程度递进。
groups.desc_en: Moves downward beneath a fluid surface or deposits down through a suspension under gravity, contrasting with upward floating.
groups.desc_zh: 在重力作用下沉入流体表面之下或从悬浮介质中沉积到底部，区别于浮起漂流。
groups.nuance_en: sink: descend beneath the surface of water or soft ground (ship / stone / sun) · submerge: go or place completely under the liquid level (submarine / coastal land / diver) · settle: gradually drop down and come to rest at the bottom (dust / sediment / silt) · sediment: precipitate and accumulate solid particulate layers (matter / wine / mud)
groups.nuance_zh: sink: 自身因重量沉底没入水中或软泥 (ship / stone / sun) · submerge: 整体覆没于水面之下 (submarine / coastal land / diver) · settle: 微粒在悬浮液中渐趋沉淀落定 (dust / sediment / silt) · sediment: 形成沉淀层析出或沉积 (matter / wine / mud)

groups.name: Devastate & Demolish · 摧毁与夷平 (Ravage, Bulldoze, Nuke)
groups.tip: 施加暴力使其倾覆解体

items.def_en: (+ sth) to completely destroy a building or structure by fire, or be destroyed in this way
items.ex_en: Arsonists managed to burn down the abandoned warehouse in the dead of night.
items.ex_zh: 纵火犯在深夜将那座废弃仓库彻底烧毁。
items.ex2_en: The old wooden barn burned down completely before local firefighters arrived with equipment.
items.ex2_zh: 在当地消防员带着装备赶到之前，老旧的木制谷仓就已经彻底烧毁了。

items.def_en: to level a building or area completely to the ground
items.ex_en: The violent tornado managed to flatten the small village within a few minutes.
items.ex_zh: 狂暴的龙卷风在几分钟内就将这个小村庄夷为了平地。
items.ex2_en: The steep sand dunes flattened gradually under continuous coastal winds across the desert.
items.ex2_zh: 在穿越沙漠的持续海岸风吹拂下，陡峭的沙丘逐渐变得平缓。

items.def_en: (often passive) To cause severe and widespread damage or destruction to something.
items.ex_en: Fierce wildfires continue to ravage thousands of acres of untouched woodland.
items.ex_zh: 肆虐的野火继续摧毁着数千英亩未开发的林地。

items.def_zh: 使（船只）失事，使遭海难；彻底毁灭，破坏
items.def_en: (usually passive) To destroy or ruin a ship at sea; to ruin or destroy completely.
items.ex_en: Violent squalls threatened to shipwreck the small wooden vessel against the jagged rocks.
items.ex_zh: 猛烈的狂风眼看就要将那艘小木船拍碎在礁石上导致海难。

items.def_en: to completely destroy a town or building so nothing remains standing
items.ex_en: Invading forces moved quickly to raze the historic fortress to the ground.
items.ex_zh: 侵略军迅速行动，将这座历史悠久的要塞彻底夷为平地。

items.def_zh: 用推土机推倒，夷平；强推，强迫执行
items.def_en: 1. To demolish buildings or clear land using a bulldozer. 2. To force someone into doing something or push a decision through aggressively.
items.ex_en: The construction crew will bulldoze the old tenements to build modern luxury apartments.
items.ex_zh: 施工队将用推土机推平旧公寓楼，以建造现代奢华公寓。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) （用炸弹、重武器）炸碎；彻底摧毁
items.def_en: (+ sth) to utterly destroy or pulverize something with explosive force
items.ex_en: The heavy artillery strike threatened to blow away the enemy bunker completely.
items.ex_zh: 重炮轰击眼看就要把敌军的掩体彻底炸个粉碎。

items.def_zh: (+ sb/sth) 彻底消灭；全歼；夷为平地
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to destroy, eliminate, or eradicate something completely
items.ex_en: The devastating tsunami managed to wipe out an entire cluster of coastal villages.
items.ex_zh: 毁灭性的海啸将沿海的一整片村落彻底抹去。

items.def_zh: 用核武器摧毁，彻底消灭；用微波炉加热
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To attack or completely destroy something with nuclear weapons. 2. (informal) To heat or cook food in a microwave oven.
items.ex_en: Military strategists threatened to nuke the enemy base if talks collapsed completely.
items.ex_zh: 军方战略家威胁称，如果谈判彻底破裂，就用核武器摧毁敌军基地。

items.def_en: to wipe out completely leaving no trace whatsoever
items.ex_en: The incoming artillery shells threatened to obliterate the remaining defensive fortifications entirely.
items.ex_zh: 袭来的炮弹眼看就要将残存的防御工事彻底抹去。

groups.summary_en: These verbs describe total, catastrophic obliteration or systematic clearing of structures, landscapes, or entities. They contrast widespread natural or military pillaging and mechanical leveling with absolute, extreme annihilation.
groups.summary_zh: 描述对建筑、地形或实体实施彻底破坏、夷平或毁灭性打击。
groups.desc_en: Denotes violent, wholesale reduction of standing structures or landscapes to ground-level ruin, differing from generic 'destroy' by emphasizing total physical leveling or catastrophic sweeping devastation.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过暴力手段将建筑物或地貌彻底夷为平地或全面摧毁，与一般“破坏/毁灭”相比，强调彻底扫平、荡然无存的平面化与灭绝性破坏。
groups.nuance_en: raze: level completely to the ground, especially by deliberate order (city / village / fortress) · bulldoze: flatten with heavy machinery or overwhelming force (building / shantytown / opposition) · ravage: wreak pervasive, catastrophic damage across an area (countryside / coastline / economy) · wipe out: eradicate entirely leaving no trace (settlement / population / savings) · burn down: consume totally by fire until reduced to ashes (house / barn / warehouse)
groups.nuance_zh: raze: 彻底夷平至地表，多含蓄意命令 (city / village / fortress) · bulldoze: 用推土机或强横力量硬性铲平 (building / shantytown / opposition) · ravage: 大面积肆虐并造成灾难性破坏 (countryside / coastline / economy) · wipe out: 彻底抹去消灭且不留痕迹 (settlement / population / savings) · burn down: 完全焚毁至仅剩灰烬 (house / barn / warehouse)

groups.name: Devour & Ingest Hastily · 狼吞虎咽与急吞 (Gulp, Gobble, Wolf)
groups.tip: 大口吞下或急迫吞食的吃相

items.def_zh: 匆忙吞下（未咀嚼直接咽下）
items.def_en: (+ down) to swallow food hurriedly with little or no chewing
items.ex_en: He had to bolt down his morning toast before sprinting to catch the bus.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不狼吞虎咽地咽下早餐吐司，然后拼命跑去赶公交车。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽地吃光（通常作 scarf down）
items.def_en: (+ down) to consume food rapidly, hungrily, and in quantity
items.ex_en: Hungry teenagers can easily scarf down three large pizzas in ten minutes.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的青少年能在十分钟内轻轻松松狼吞虎咽地吃光三张大披萨。

items.def_en: to swallow a drink completely without stopping for breath
items.ex_en: The exhausted marathon runner began to chug cold water without taking a breath.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的马拉松选手开始不喘气地大口灌下冰水。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 咕咚咽下；大口吞下
items.def_en: (+ sth) to swallow food or drink rapidly and in large amounts
items.ex_en: He paused briefly to gulp down a tall glass of icy lemonade.
items.ex_zh: 他停顿了一下，咕咚咽下一大杯冰柠檬水。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 飞快吞下；风卷残云般吃完
items.def_en: (+ sth) to eat something voraciously and in a hurry
items.ex_en: The starving hiker proceeded to scarf down the entire burger in seconds.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的徒步者在几秒钟内就风卷残云般吃完了整个汉堡。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to eat food very quickly and greedily in large mouthfuls
items.ex_en: The ravenous stray dog proceeded to wolf down the bowl of meat greedily.
items.ex_zh: 那只极度饥饿的流浪狗贪婪地把整碗肉狼吞虎咽地吃了个精光。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽地吃完（常与 down 连用）
items.def_en: (+ down) to eat food very quickly and greedily in large amounts
items.ex_en: Late for practice, Mark proceeded to wolf down his remaining sandwich quickly.
items.ex_zh: 训练要迟到了，马克赶紧狼吞虎咽地吃完了剩下的三明治。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽，大口吞食；（火鸡）咯咯叫
items.def_en: 1. To eat something quickly and greedily (often 'gobble up/down'). 2. (of a turkey) To make a characteristic gurgling sound.
items.ex_en: The starving children began to gobble up the warm freshly baked bread.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的孩子们开始狼吞虎咽地大口吞吃刚出炉的热面包。

items.def_zh: 大口吞下，吞咽；倒抽气，深吸一口气；哽住
items.def_en: 1. To swallow food or drink quickly in large mouthfuls. 2. To take a quick, deep breath, especially from surprise or shock.
items.ex_en: He paused to gulp the scalding black coffee before rushing out the door.
items.ex_zh: 他停下来猛灌了一大口滚烫的黑咖啡，然后冲出了门。

items.def_en: [I/T] to drink or eat greedily, noisily, and in large quantities
items.ex_en: Thirsty fans proceeded to guzzle pints of cold beer throughout the match.
items.ex_zh: 口渴的球迷们在整场比赛中大口狂饮着一杯杯冰啤酒。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify the hasty, noisy, or voracious ingestion of food or drink, characterized by taking excessively large mouthfuls, minimal chewing, and rapid swallowing.
groups.summary_zh: 指大口急吞、不加细嚼、贪婪快速地进食或咽下。
groups.desc_en: Denotes consuming food or drink with rapacious, urgent haste, differing from ordinary 'eat' or 'drink' by the conspicuous absence of chewing, table manners, or restraint.
groups.desc_zh: 指极其急促、贪婪地吞咽食物或饮料，与普通“吃/喝”相比，强调全无咀嚼、不顾吃相或毫无节制的狼吞虎咽。
groups.nuance_en: wolf down: consume voraciously in large, barely chewed chunks (meal / burger / steak) · gobble: swallow hurriedly with noisy greed (food / dessert / turkey) · scarf: polish off eagerly and at high speed, colloquial (pizza / fries / lunch) · gulp down: force large liquid or solid mouthfuls down the throat hastily (medicine / coffee / bite) · chug: drink down an entire liquid vessel without pausing for breath (beer / water / pint)
groups.nuance_zh: wolf down: 像狼一样不加咀嚼大块猛吞 (meal / burger / steak) · gobble: 贪婪且急促地大口吞下 (food / dessert / turkey) · scarf: 口语中极速吃光一扫而空 (pizza / fries / lunch) · gulp down: 喉头大口猛咽液体或固体 (medicine / coffee / bite) · chug: 不换气一口气灌完整容器液体 (beer / water / pint)

groups.name: Dig & Excavate · 挖掘与开采 (Extract from the Earth)
groups.tip: 破土取物挖出地下资源

items.def_en: 1. To dig into the earth to extract valuable minerals, coal, or ores. 2. To lay explosive mines in an area.
items.ex_en: Local companies continue to mine rich deposits of copper deep underground.
items.ex_zh: 当地公司继续在地下深处开采储量丰富的铜矿。

items.def_en: To prepare and cultivate land for growing crops by plowing, harrowing, or hoeing.
items.ex_en: Farmers will till the fertile soil thoroughly before sowing the spring wheat.
items.ex_zh: 在播种春小麦之前，农民们会彻底犁翻肥沃的土地。

items.def_en: [I/T] to break up and move earth with a tool, machine, or hands
items.ex_en: The workers had to dig a deep drainage trench across the muddy field.
items.ex_zh: 工人们不得不在泥泞的田野上挖出一条深排水沟。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 掘出；发掘；翻掘（泥土）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove earth or extract something buried beneath the ground by digging
items.ex_en: The media managed to dig up some scandalous details about his past.
items.ex_zh: 媒体设法翻出了他过去的一些丑闻细节。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to locate and remove something buried or stuck in the earth
items.ex_en: I dug out an old photo album from the attic.
items.ex_zh: 我从阁楼里翻出了一本旧相册。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to hollow out earth or remove loose soil with a shovel, scoop, or heavy equipment
items.ex_en: The giant mechanical backhoe began to scoop out huge loads of loose dirt.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的机械挖掘机开始挖出一大铲一大铲松散的泥土。

items.def_en: to extract stone, slate, or other materials from an open pit
items.ex_en: Local builders continue to quarry granite from the mountainside for modern projects.
items.ex_zh: 当地建筑商继续从山腰采掘花岗岩以用于现代工程。

items.def_en: [I/T] to clear the bed of a harbor, river, or body of water by scooping out mud and debris
items.ex_en: Crews will dredge the shallow river channel to allow large cargo ships passage.
items.ex_zh: 工作人员将疏浚浅水河道，以便让大型货船通行。

items.def_en: [I/T] to dig out earth systematically to reveal buried remains or create a foundation
items.ex_en: Archaeologists arrived early to excavate the ancient Roman ruins beneath the square.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家早早赶来，对广场下方的古罗马遗址进行发掘。

items.def_en: 1. To dig up something buried in the ground. 2. To uncover or bring to light something hidden or forgotten.
items.ex_en: Construction workers managed to unearth several ceramic artifacts beneath the old foundation.
items.ex_zh: 建筑工人在旧地基下方发掘出了几件陶器文物。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe breaking, overturning, or penetrating ground or earth to obtain minerals, reveal buried items, or prepare soil for cultivation. They range from everyday manual digging and agricultural tilling to industrial extraction and archaeological uncovering.
groups.summary_zh: 破开、翻动地表以开采矿藏、培土或掘出埋藏物。
groups.desc_en: Denotes systematic subterranean excavation or extraction of earth and natural resources, contrasting with shallow 'scratching' by its depth, industrial scale, and intent to harvest hidden materials.
groups.desc_zh: 指对地下土地或自然资源进行系统性开采与挖掘，与表层浅扒相比，强调挖掘深度、产业规模以及获取深埋资源的明确意图。
groups.nuance_en: mine: extract valuable minerals or ores beneath the surface (coal / gold / data) · quarry: cut stone or minerals out of open-pit surface workings (marble / granite / limestone) · dredge: scoop or suck up silt and sediment from submerged beds (harbor / riverbed / channel) · till: plow and turn earth to prepare for cultivation (soil / land / field) · dig up: unearth by breaking ground systematically (fossils / roots / remains)
groups.nuance_zh: mine: 深入地下开采矿产或数据资源 (coal / gold / data) · quarry: 从露天矿坑中凿切采掘石材 (marble / granite / limestone) · dredge: 从水下泥床中疏浚吸捞淤泥 (harbor / riverbed / channel) · till: 翻耕土地以备耕作播种 (soil / land / field) · dig up: 破土掘出埋藏之物 (fossils / roots / remains)

groups.name: Dig & Extract Material · 挖掘与铲掘 (Quarry, Shovel, Spade)
groups.tip: 开掘泥土采石挖掘

items.def_en: (+ sth) lift or remove aggregate material with a shovel, scoop, or cupped hands
items.ex_en: The gardener used a metal trowel to scoop up the fresh potting soil.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用一把金属泥铲铲起了新鲜的盆栽土。

items.def_en: to dig, cut, or turn over earth using a spade
items.ex_en: You need to spade the flowerbed deeply before planting the delicate bulbs.
items.ex_zh: 在种植娇嫩的球茎之前，你需要用铁锹把花坛深翻一遍。

items.def_en: (+ into) to dig into the ground with a tool; to search deeply into an area
items.ex_en: The archaeologist began to delve into the mound with a small trowel.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家开始用一把小铲子深入挖掘土丘。

items.def_en: (+ sth) excavate and extract something deeply embedded in the earth or snow
items.ex_en: I dug out an old photo album from the attic.
items.ex_zh: 我从阁楼里翻出了一本旧相册。

items.def_en: (+ sth) break up earth and remove an object or material from beneath the ground
items.ex_en: The media managed to dig up some scandalous details about his past.
items.ex_zh: 媒体设法翻出了他过去的一些丑闻细节。

items.def_en: (+ sth) clear or extract large quantities of earth, coal, or rubble using a shovel
items.ex_en: Volunteers arrived with heavy tools to shovel out the mud from basements.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们带着重型工具赶来，铲出地下室里的淤泥。

items.def_zh: 开采，采掘（石料等）；努力搜寻（资料）
items.def_en: 1. To dig or extract stone, slate, or other materials from a quarry. 2. To search deeply to extract information.
items.ex_en: Workers continue to quarry massive limestone blocks for the historic restoration project.
items.ex_zh: 工人们继续采掘巨大的石灰石块，用于历史建筑的修复工程。

items.def_zh: 用铲子铲；狼吞虎咽地把（食物）送进嘴里
items.def_en: 1. To lift, clear, or move earth, snow, or other loose material with a shovel. 2. To put large amounts of food into your mouth quickly.
items.ex_en: The laborers had to shovel loose gravel onto the roadbed all morning.
items.ex_zh: 劳工们整个上午都得用铲子把碎石铲到路基上。

items.def_en: [I/T] to extract coal, minerals, or metals from the earth by digging pits or shafts
items.ex_en: They plan to mine anthracite coal from the newly opened vertical shaft.
items.ex_zh: 他们计划从新开辟的立井中开采无烟煤。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ up) to clean out or scoop up silt, mud, and material from the bed of a body of water
items.ex_en: The heavy machinery will dredge up thick mud from the harbor bed.
items.ex_zh: 重型机械将从港底挖捞起厚厚的淤泥。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame center on using implements or machinery to dig up, extract, or move aggregates, soil, ore, or stone from the ground. The semantic focus is on the manual or mechanical act of displacing and harvesting raw earth/minerals.
groups.summary_zh: 使用工具或器械铲除、挖掘并提取泥土、矿石等物料。
groups.desc_en: Denotes manipulating tools to hollow out, scoop, or dislodge particulate or dense earth, differing from broad 'mining' by focusing on the physical mechanics of using spades, scoops, or blades.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用铲、勺等工具切削、挖出或移开松散土壤与颗粒物料，与广义“开采”相比，更聚焦于工具切土与铲拨的实体机械动作。
groups.nuance_en: shovel: lift and move bulk material using a broad blade (snow / dirt / gravel) · spade: cut and turn firm earth using a sharp, flat tool (garden / plot / bed) · scoop up: gather loose contents in a curved, lifting motion (earth / sand / debris) · delve: dig deeply into the ground, or metaphorically into records (earth / archive / mystery) · dig out: clear passages or extract trapped objects by hollowing surrounding earth (tunnel / trench / car)
groups.nuance_zh: shovel: 用宽铲大量铲除搬运物料 (snow / dirt / gravel) · spade: 用锋利扁锹深翻切削紧实土壤 (garden / plot / bed) · scoop up: 用弧状工具舀起或兜起松散物 (earth / sand / debris) · delve: 深入土壤深挖，引申为深入钻研查考 (earth / archive / mystery) · dig out: 挖开周围泥土以清理通路或掘出受困物 (tunnel / trench / car)

groups.name: Direct Retailing & Hawking · 叫卖与分销 (Hawk, Peddle, Vend)
groups.tip: 多种方式沿街推销货品

items.def_zh: 征订，招募预订；认购（股份）；定期订购，订阅；赞同
items.def_en: 1. To take advance orders for a forthcoming publication, or agree to buy shares in a company. 2. To pay money regularly to receive a service, product, or publication.
items.ex_en: Investors rushed to subscribe for shares before the public offering closed yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 投资者赶在昨天公开发行结束前争先恐后地认购股份。

items.def_en: (formal) To sell small items, food, or goods, especially from a street stall, cart, or machine.
items.ex_en: Street vendors gather in the plaza to vend hot snacks to tourists.
items.ex_zh: 街头小贩聚集在广场上，向游客兜售热小吃。

items.def_zh: 沿街叫卖，到处兜售；传播，散播（观念、谎言）
items.def_en: To travel from place to place selling small goods; to spread or promote ideas or illegal items.
items.ex_en: He traveled from town to town to peddle cheap handmade wooden trinkets.
items.ex_zh: 他从一个城镇走到另一个城镇，沿街兜售廉价的手工木制小饰品。

items.def_en: to solicit orders, subscriptions, or votes door-to-door
items.ex_en: Volunteers agreed to canvass the neighborhood to gather signatures for the petition.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们同意挨家挨户游说邻里，为请愿书征集签名。

items.def_zh: 廉价抛售，兜售（尤指劣质或多余物品）
items.def_en: (+ sth) sell something quickly, cheaply, or aggressively to get rid of it
items.ex_en: The bankrupt retailer tried to flog off its damaged surplus stock cheaply.
items.ex_zh: 破产的零售商试图以低廉的价格抛售其受损的过剩库存。

items.def_zh: 以次充好兜售；硬塞给（某人）
items.def_en: (+ sth on sb) get rid of an inferior or unwanted item by deceitful selling
items.ex_en: The dishonest dealer tried to palm off a counterfeit painting on buyers.
items.ex_zh: 那个不诚实的商人试图将一幅赝品画作以次充好卖给买家。

items.def_zh: 沿街叫卖，兜售；咳出（痰等），清嗓；放鹰捕猎
items.def_en: 1. To travel around selling goods, usually shouting loudly to attract customers. 2. To clear your throat noisily and bring up phlegm.
items.ex_en: Peddlers shout at the top of their lungs to hawk fresh produce.
items.ex_zh: 小贩们扯开嗓子大声叫卖新鲜的农产品。

items.def_en: to solicit patronage or trade importunately or aggressively
items.ex_en: Aggressive vendors stood outside the arena to tout overpriced tickets to fans.
items.ex_zh: 激进的小贩站在场馆外，向球迷强行兜售高价门票。

items.def_en: to sell goods aggressively or dishonestly, especially cheap wares
items.ex_en: Dishonest peddlers continue to huckster fake designer watches on busy street corners.
items.ex_zh: 不法商贩继续在繁华的街角强行兜售仿冒名牌手表。

items.def_en: To conduct an auction and sell items to the highest bidder.
items.ex_en: The estate invited an expert to auctioneer the valuable antique collection today.
items.ex_zh: 遗产管理方今天邀请了一位专家来主持拍卖这批贵重古董。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the manner of selling goods directly to customers, typically on the street, door-to-door, or through public bids and soliciting.
groups.summary_zh: 走街串巷、兜售摆摊或公开叫价拍卖等直接面向客户的推销分销行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the aggressive, direct, or itinerant promotion and sale of goods, differing from institutional 'selling' by its emphasis on persistent solicitation, mobile peddling, or intrusive self-pitching.
groups.desc_zh: 指直接走街串巷、主动招揽或兜售货品，与正规被动零售相比，强调流动巡回、高声叫卖、死缠烂打或带欺诈诱导的推销方式。
groups.nuance_en: hawk: shout or advertise goods aggressively in public spaces (wares / souvenirs / papers) · peddle: travel around selling small items, or spread illicit ideas (goods / trinkets / lies) · tout: solicit business or praise items aggressively and pushily (tickets / services / credentials) · vend: dispense products routinely, often via machines or stalls (merchandise / snacks / newspapers) · palm off: dispose of worthless goods or duties deceptively onto another (fake / responsibility / imitation)
groups.nuance_zh: hawk: 在公共场合大声叫卖或强行推销 (wares / souvenirs / papers) · peddle: 沿街走访兜售零星杂物或兜售劣质观点 (goods / trinkets / lies) · tout: 极力吹捧招徕以倒手倒卖 (tickets / services / credentials) · vend: 通过摊位或自动贩卖机例行销售 (merchandise / snacks / newspapers) · palm off: 欺诈性地将劣质假货或烫手山芋转嫁他人 (fake / responsibility / imitation)

groups.name: Disavow & Recant Statements · 撤回与收回言论 (Retract, Disclaim, Recant)
groups.tip: 否认权利主张并收回前言

items.def_en: to withdraw or admit to be untrue a remark, insult, or assertion
items.ex_en: The angry politician was forced to take back his insulting remarks publicly.
items.ex_zh: 那位愤怒的政客被迫当众收回了他侮辱性的言论。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 撤回（言论）；收回（声明）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to retreat from or modify a prior public statement, claim, or promise
items.ex_en: The press secretary attempted to walk back the president's controversial remarks yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 新闻秘书昨天试图收回总统此前发表的争议性言论。

items.def_zh: 退让；放弃（原有立场或要求）
items.def_en: to withdraw a demand, claim, or assertion in the face of opposition
items.ex_en: Faced with widespread public outrage, the mayor chose to back down quickly.
items.ex_zh: 面对公众的普遍愤怒，市长迅速选择了退让。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 反悔；收回（承诺、协议）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to withdraw from a prior commitment, statement, or agreement
items.ex_en: The contractor tried to back out of his formal agreement without penalty.
items.ex_zh: 承包商试图在不受处罚的情况下反悔并撤回正式协议。

items.def_zh: 撤回，收回（言论、承诺等）；缩回，缩进
items.def_en: 1. To officially withdraw or take back a statement, promise, or accusation. 2. To pull or move back inside, or become drawn back inside.
items.ex_en: The newspaper was legally required to retract the false claims against him.
items.ex_zh: 报社被法律要求撤回对他的虚假指控。
items.ex2_en: The cat's sharp claws retract smoothly into protective sheaths when it feels relaxed.
items.ex2_zh: 当猫感到放松时，其锋利的爪子会平滑地缩回保护鞘中。

items.def_en: to state publicly that one has no connection with, knowledge of, or responsibility for something
items.ex_en: The senator moved swiftly to disavow any connection to the extremist group.
items.ex_zh: 参议员迅速采取行动，宣布与该极端组织断绝一切关系。

items.def_zh: 否认，拒不承认；放弃（权利、所有权等）
items.def_en: 1. To state publicly that you have no responsibility for, knowledge of, or connection with something. 2. (law) To formally renounce or surrender a legal right or claim.
items.ex_en: The official statement sought to disclaim all legal responsibility for the accident.
items.ex_zh: 该官方声明试图否认对这起事故负有任何法律责任。

items.def_zh: 公开撤回，放弃（先前的信仰、言论或主张）
items.def_en: (formal) To publicly announce that you no longer hold or support a previously stated belief or opinion.
items.ex_en: Under intense political pressure, the scholar was forced to recant his heresy.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大的政治压力下，这位学者被迫公开放弃了自己的异端观点。

items.def_zh: 发誓放弃（信仰、权利或主张）
items.def_en: (formal) to formally reject or renounce a belief, cause, or claim under oath
items.ex_en: The prisoner was commanded to abjure his allegiance to the rebel cause.
items.ex_zh: 囚犯被勒令发誓放弃对叛乱事业的效忠。

items.def_en: (formal or literary) To take back or retract words that you have already spoken.
items.ex_en: Once an unforgivable insult has been uttered, no apology can unsay it.
items.ex_zh: 一旦不可饶恕的侮辱之言已说出口，任何道歉都无法将其收回。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote repudiating, annulling, or withdrawing a prior statement, belief, confession, or legal claim.
groups.summary_zh: 指公开撤回前言、否认关联、收回指控或正式放弃既有信仰与主张。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formally or publicly withdrawing a previous statement, allegiance, or position under pressure, contrasting with mere 'denial' through the explicit act of reversal or repudiation.
groups.desc_zh: 指在压力下正式或公开撤回、放弃先前的言论、立场或从属关系，与单纯“否认”相比，强调原话的收回或反悔性切割。
groups.nuance_en: recant: formally and publicly renounce a previously held religious or philosophical belief (heresy / testimony / confession) · retract: formally draw back an untrue or defamatory claim (statement / allegation / confession) · disavow: deny any connection with or responsibility for an act or agent (knowledge / statement / relationship) · walk back: partially retreat from or reframe an overextended remark to limit fallout (comments / claim / threat) · disclaim: explicitly renounce legal claim or ownership of liability (responsibility / title / copyright)
groups.nuance_zh: recant: 正式且公开声明放弃过去的宗教信仰或政治立场 (heresy / testimony / confession) · retract: 官方撤回此前不实或具诽谤性的陈述 (statement / allegation / confession) · disavow: 彻底否认与某人某事的关联以划清界限 (knowledge / statement / relationship) · walk back: 策略性软化或局部收回失当言论以平息争议 (comments / claim / threat) · disclaim: 法律上明确声明免除责任或放弃权益 (responsibility / title / copyright)

groups.name: Discard & Dump · 抛弃与倾倒 (Get Rid of Waste Carelessly or Decisively)
groups.tip: 视作垃圾扔掉或毁弃

items.def_zh: 报废；取消，废弃（计划或物件）
items.def_en: to discard or abandon a plan, system, or object as useless
