items.ex_en: The committee decided to scrap the costly project after facing widespread community backlash.
items.ex_zh: 面对社区广泛的反对，委员会决定废弃这个耗资巨大的项目。

items.def_zh: 丢弃，甩掉（不再需要的人或物）
items.def_en: to informally abandon or get rid of something or someone no longer wanted
items.ex_en: She decided to ditch her old gasoline car and rely solely on public transit.
items.ex_zh: 她决定抛弃自己的旧燃油车，完全依靠公共交通出行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) discard an unwanted item or rubbish decisively into the trash
items.ex_en: You shouldn't throw away such a wonderful job opportunity.
items.ex_zh: 你不应该白白浪费这么好的工作机会。

items.def_en: (+ sth) get rid of something no longer useful or needed
items.ex_en: The judge threw out the lawsuit due to lack of evidence.
items.ex_zh: 法官因证据不足驳回了该起诉讼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) casually or unceremoniously dispose of something unwanted
items.ex_en: He decided to toss out a stack of outdated magazines cluttering the desk.
items.ex_zh: 他决定把桌上堆得乱七八糟的一叠过期杂志随手扔掉。

items.def_zh: 丢弃，扔掉；损坏，捣毁；痛斥
items.def_en: (informal) 1. To throw away something that is no longer needed. 2. To damage or destroy something severely. 3. To criticize severely.
items.ex_en: I need to trash these broken plastic chairs before the movers arrive tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 在搬家工人明天到来之前，我得把这些坏掉的塑料椅扔掉。

items.def_zh: 倾倒，丢弃；倾销；甩掉（恋人）
items.def_en: 1. To get rid of waste, rubbish, or unwanted things, especially carelessly or in an illegal place. 2. To sell goods in another country at an unfairly low price.
items.ex_en: Irresponsible contractors continued to dump hazardous chemical waste into the abandoned quarry illegally.
items.ex_zh: 不负责任的承包商继续非法向废弃的采石场倾倒危险化学废料。

items.def_en: to throw something away casually or carelessly
items.ex_en: Just chuck those empty takeout containers into the recycling bin behind the door.
items.ex_zh: 直接把那些空外卖盒随手扔到门后面的回收桶里就行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) discard or deliberately divest oneself of an unwanted burden, garment, or tie
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_zh: 投弃（货物以减重）；放弃（包袱）
items.def_en: to throw cargo overboard to lighten a craft; to decisively drop ideas or burdens
items.ex_en: The captain ordered the crew to jettison heavy cargo during the violent storm.
items.ex_zh: 在猛烈的风暴中，船长命令船员投弃沉重的货物以减轻负荷。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe getting rid of unwanted items, refuse, or burdens, ranging from unceremonious disposal to careless, bulk unloading.
groups.summary_zh: 强调随意、果断或成批抛弃无用之物与垃圾的动作方式。
groups.desc_en: Denotes unceremoniously getting rid of unwanted physical waste or surplus possessions, differing from systematic 'disposing' by its casual, hasty, or disrespectful treatment of the item.
groups.desc_zh: 指随手或干脆利落地甩弃无用废弃物或剩余物品，与规范的“处理/处置”相比，强调动作的随意、草率、弃置如敝屣的轻蔑感。
groups.nuance_en: dump: unload heavily or abandon carelessly in an unauthorized spot (waste / trash / partner) · ditch: abruptly abandon or get rid of someone or something inconvenient (car / plan / escort) · scrap: discard or break down as useless junk (metal / project / proposal) · chuck: toss away casually and without ceremony (wrapper / clothes / junk) · trash: discard into the bin, or physically ruin (receipt / file / room)
groups.nuance_zh: dump: 粗暴卸下倾倒废料，或绝情甩掉伴侣 (waste / trash / partner) · ditch: 果断甩掉或抛弃累赘之物或人 (car / plan / escort) · scrap: 将无用之物当废料报废或彻底叫停 (metal / project / proposal) · chuck: 随手扔掉或抛掷进垃圾桶 (wrapper / clothes / junk) · trash: 把物品扔进垃圾堆，或彻底捣毁砸烂 (receipt / file / room)

groups.name: Discard & Purge · 消除与废弃 (Delete, Scrap, Eradicate)
groups.tip: 清除抹去痕迹或丢弃不用

items.def_en: to get rid of something that is regarded as useless or no longer required
items.ex_en: Laboratory staff must carefully discard contaminated materials in clearly marked biohazard containers.
items.ex_zh: 实验室人员必须将受污染的材料小心丢弃在标有生物危害的专用容器中。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 扔掉；废弃；否决（提议）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to discard something unwanted or officially reject a plan or proposal
items.ex_en: The judge threw out the lawsuit due to lack of evidence.
items.ex_zh: 法官因证据不足驳回了该起诉讼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to discard or get rid of something that is no longer needed
items.ex_en: We should toss out these leftover vegetables before they turn completely bad.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该在这些剩菜彻底变质之前把它们扔掉。

items.def_en: To remove or erase written, printed, or computer-stored text, files, or information.
items.ex_en: Please delete the sensitive customer data permanently from your personal computer right now.
items.ex_zh: 请立即从你的个人电脑中永久删除那些敏感的客户数据。

items.def_zh: 废弃，取消，抛弃；报废（旧物）；打架，吵架
items.def_en: 1. To cancel, abandon, or discard a plan, system, or object no longer needed. 2. (informal) To have a fight or argument.
items.ex_en: The automobile company chose to scrap the flawed engine prototype after numerous failures.
items.ex_zh: 经历多次失败后，汽车公司决定报废那个有缺陷的发动机原型。

items.def_zh: 丢弃，断然舍弃（计划或负荷）
items.def_en: to throw goods overboard, or decisively abandon a plan, idea, or burden
items.ex_en: To survive the market downturn, the firm had to jettison unprofitable subsidiaries.
items.ex_zh: 为了度过市场低迷期，该企业不得不果断放弃亏损的子公司。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to formally stop using, eradicate, or abolish a practice, rule, or system
items.ex_en: The new administration pledged to do away with outdated bureaucratic regulations very quickly.
items.ex_zh: 新一届政府承诺将迅速废除那些过时的官僚规章制度。

items.def_en: 1. To completely remove or get rid of something unwanted. 2. To defeat someone so that they can no longer take part in a competition.
items.ex_en: Health authorities launched a national campaign to eliminate infectious diseases from rural areas.
items.ex_zh: 卫生部门发起了一项全国性运动，以消除农村地区的传染性疾病。

items.def_en: to completely destroy or put an end to something undesirable, removing it root and branch
items.ex_en: Global health initiatives strive tirelessly to eradicate extreme poverty and endemic viruses worldwide.
items.ex_zh: 全球卫生倡议不知疲倦地努力，旨在全世界范围内彻底根除赤贫和地方性病毒。

items.def_en: to wipe out entirely so that no trace or memory remains
items.ex_en: The relentless artillery fire threatened to obliterate the ancient city without leaving any traces.
items.ex_zh: 持续不断的炮火几乎要彻底抹灭这座古城，不留任何痕迹。

groups.summary_en: An agent removes, discards, or utterly destroys an entity, record, policy, or project so that it no longer exists or functions. Verbs range in destructive force from routine administrative removal (delete) and programmatic abandonment (scrap) to total annihilation (eradicate, obliterate).
groups.summary_zh: 从常规删除、彻底放弃项目到完全消灭。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the systematic elimination, expunging, or discarding of obsolete, redundant, or unwanted entities, contrasting with basic 'throw away' by its administrative, technical, or permanent finality.
groups.desc_zh: 指系统性、永久性地清除、剔除或废弃冗余过时之物，与日常“扔掉”相比，强调制度化、不可逆的清理与彻底根绝。
groups.nuance_en: jettison: deliberately discard unwanted weight or baggage to survive or streamline (cargo / fuel / policy) · eliminate: remove completely so as to leave no remainder (deficit / risk / competitors) · do away with: abolish or formally discontinue a custom or rule (tax / regulation / slavery) · delete: erase recorded data or text irrevocably (file / record / comment) · scrap: abandon an entire framework, scheme, or machine decisively (plan / program / deal)
groups.nuance_zh: jettison: 为轻装减负或求生而果断舍弃包袱政策 (cargo / fuel / policy) · eliminate: 彻底铲除消灭以绝后患 (deficit / risk / competitors) · do away with: 废除或废止旧有规章制度习俗 (tax / regulation / slavery) · delete: 彻底擦除电子数据或文本记录 (file / record / comment) · scrap: 断然中止废止大型计划方案或协议 (plan / program / deal)

groups.name: Discontinue & Terminate · 中止与终止 (Discontinue, Terminate, Cease)
groups.tip: 叫停运转或终止原流程

items.def_en: [I/T] to stop happening or to bring an activity to an end (formal)
items.ex_en: Hostilities must cease immediately so humanitarian aid convoys can safely enter the conflict zone.
items.ex_zh: 敌对行动必须立即停止，人道主义救援车队才能安全进入冲突地区。
items.ex2_en: The university decided to cease all outdoor athletic activities during the hazardous storm.
items.ex2_zh: 在危险的风暴期间，大学决定停止所有室外体育活动。

items.def_zh: 清算；结束；了结（业务或活动）
items.def_en: to bring a business, meeting, or activity to a planned conclusion
items.ex_en: Let us wind up this lengthy department meeting before lunchtime begins today.
items.ex_zh: 我们赶在今天午饭时间开始前把这个冗长的部门会议结束了吧。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cancel an event, operation, or planned activity
items.ex_en: Officials were forced to call off the outdoor festival due to severe flooding.
items.ex_zh: 由于严重的水灾，官员们被迫取消了那场户外节日活动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to stop operating or cause a business, service, or machine to cease operating
items.ex_en: The aging manufacturing plant will permanently shut down its operations by next month.
items.ex_zh: 那座老旧的制造工厂将在下个月前永久停止其运营。
items.ex2_en: The nuclear reactor will shut down automatically if sensor temperatures exceed safe limits.
items.ex2_zh: 如果传感器温度超过安全极限，核反应堆将自动停机关闭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to abruptly end a relationship, agreement, or formal negotiation
items.ex_en: The rebel faction decided to break off peace talks following the border skirmish.
items.ex_zh: 边境发生小规模冲突后，叛乱派系决定中止和平谈判。
items.ex2_en: Dry pine branches break off easily when burdened by thick, heavy winter snowfall.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的松树枝在承受厚重冬雪的重压时很容易折断。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to stop using or producing something gradually over a period of time
items.ex_en: The government plans to phase out single-use plastics over the next three years.
items.ex_zh: 政府计划在未来三年内逐步淘汰一次性塑料制品。

items.def_zh: 终止；使终结；解除（合同/雇佣）
items.def_en: [I/T] to bring an agreement, employment, or ongoing operation to an official end
items.ex_en: The company exercised its legal right to terminate the vendor contract without penalty.
items.ex_zh: 该公司行使其合法权利，免责终止了与该供应商的合同。
items.ex2_en: The long-distance passenger train terminates at the newly renovated southern grand terminal.
items.ex2_zh: 这趟长途客运列车终点停靠在刚翻新好的南部宏伟总站。

items.def_zh: 中止，中断，停止；停产，终止提供
items.def_en: to stop doing, producing, or providing something that was previously regular or ongoing.
items.ex_en: The pharmaceutical giant decided to discontinue production of the drug due to low demand.
items.ex_zh: 由于需求低迷，这家制药巨头决定停止生产该药物。

items.def_zh: 中止；夭折；叫停（任务/计划）
items.def_en: [I/T] to terminate a process, project, or mission before completion due to a problem
items.ex_en: Engineers were instructed to abort the rocket launch after detecting a critical sensor failure.
items.ex_zh: 在探测到关键传感器故障后，工程师接到指令叫停火箭发射。
items.ex2_en: The scheduled space mission aborted automatically when unexpected system errors occurred.
items.ex2_zh: 当发生意外系统错误时，预定的太空任务自动中止了。

items.def_zh: 最后确定，定稿，完成；使定局
items.def_en: to complete and agree on the final details of a plan, deal, or document.
items.ex_en: Both legal teams met early this morning to finalize the terms of the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 双方的法律团队今天一早就碰头敲定收购协议的最终条款。

groups.summary_en: An authority, institution, or agent puts an end to an ongoing activity, production line, contract, or service before or upon its completion. Verbs vary in formality from formal business cancellation ('discontinue') to legal or definitive nullification ('terminate', 'sever').
groups.summary_zh: 使正在进行的生产、业务、合同或项目正式停止或终结。
groups.desc_en: Denotes bringing an ongoing activity, enterprise, or state to a definitive stop, differing from natural 'ending' by implying deliberate administrative agency, contract expiration, or stepwise closure.
groups.desc_zh: 指人为、主动或依规终止一项持续中的活动、业务或合作，与自发“结束”相比，强调行政裁定、契约到期或步骤化的强制截停。
groups.nuance_en: terminate: end decisively through formal, contractual, or physical intervention (contract / employment / pregnancy) · discontinue: cease producing, providing, or practicing routinely (service / medication / line) · phase out: withdraw or terminate gradually in planned stages (subsidy / chemical / product) · wind up: conclude affairs systematically leading to final closure (business / meeting / estate) · shut down: halt operational machinery or business activities entirely (factory / plant / government)
groups.nuance_zh: terminate: 依合同、法律或人为干预正式硬性终止 (contract / employment / pregnancy) · discontinue: 停止常规生产、供应或服用 (service / medication / line) · phase out: 按计划分阶段逐步淘汰取缔 (subsidy / chemical / product) · wind up: 系统清算资产事务以圆满收尾结业 (business / meeting / estate) · shut down: 关闭停运工厂或中止机构运营 (factory / plant / government)

groups.name: Discourage & Deject · 沮丧与消沉 (Discourage, Dishearten, Deject)
groups.tip: 从泄气失落到心如死灰

items.def_en: to cause someone to lose confidence, hope, or enthusiasm for an endeavor
items.ex_en: Repeated rejections can easily discourage young writers from pursuing their literary dreams further.
items.ex_zh: 接二连三的拒绝很容易使年轻作家气馁，不敢继续追寻文学梦想。

items.def_en: to cause someone to feel extremely sad, downcast, or low in spirits
items.ex_en: The unexpected exam results seemed to cast down his normally cheerful spirits entirely.
items.ex_zh: 出人意料的考试成绩似乎让他平时开朗的精神彻底消沉了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) cause someone to feel depressed, disheartened, or unhappy
items.ex_en: Dark and gloomy winter days often get me down if I stay inside.
items.ex_zh: 如果一直呆在室内，阴暗沉闷的冬日往往会让我感到沮丧抑郁。

items.def_zh: 使心事重重，使消沉压抑
items.def_en: (+ sb) burden someone with anxiety, sorrow, or despair
items.ex_en: She felt weighed down by domestic responsibilities and work pressures.
items.ex_zh: 她感到家庭责任和工作压力压得自己喘不过气来。

items.def_zh: 使沮丧，使气馁，使失去信心
items.def_en: 1. To make someone lose hope, confidence, or enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: A series of critical setbacks did not dishearten the determined research team at all.
items.ex_zh: 一连串重大的挫折丝毫没有使这支坚定的研究团队灰心丧气。

items.def_zh: 使士气低落，使沮丧泄气；使道德败坏
items.def_en: 1. To destroy the morale, confidence, or enthusiasm of someone. 2. (formal) To corrupt the morals or principles of.
items.ex_en: Constant pay cuts and harsh conditions served to demoralize the entire workforce thoroughly.
items.ex_zh: 不断降薪和恶劣条件彻底瓦解了全体员工的士气。

items.raw_cluster: 使沮丧与使悲伤 Depress & Deject
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive) To make someone feel sad, depressed, or dispirited.
items.ex_en: The continuous bad news from abroad seemed to deject everyone in the office.
items.ex_zh: 来自国外的连续坏消息似乎让办公室里的每一个人都倍感沮丧。

items.raw_cluster: 使沮丧与使气馁 Discourage & Dispirit
items.def_zh: 使气馁，使沮丧，使萎靡不振
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive) To make someone lose enthusiasm, energy, or hope.
items.ex_en: Persistent rainy weather and isolation tended to dispirit the remote research station crew.
items.ex_zh: 持续的阴雨天气和隔绝状态往往会使偏远科考站的队员们萎靡不振。

items.def_zh: 丧气，垂头丧气，失去希望
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To become disheartened or discouraged; to lose all hope.
items.ex_en: Even amidst crushing defeat, the stoic general refused to despond or surrender prematurely.
items.ex_zh: 即使身处惨败之中，那位坚毅的将军也拒绝丧气或过早投降。

items.def_zh: 击溃，彻底粉碎（士气或希望）
items.def_en: to overwhelm and completely destroy someone's spirit, confidence, or morale
items.ex_en: The sudden financial audit seemed to crush his remaining optimism about the company.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的财务审计似乎彻底粉碎了他对公司仅存的乐观心态。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate the emotional deflation and loss of confidence or hope inflicted on an agent, stepping from mild loss of enthusiasm to paralyzing despair.
groups.summary_zh: 打击士气、剥夺希望，导致人由泄气退缩滑向彻底绝望消沉。
groups.desc_en: Denotes causing a loss of morale, confidence, or optimism through adversity, differing from general 'sadden' by specifically undermining one's motivation and spirit to pursue an objective.
groups.desc_zh: 指因受挫或逆境而销蚀信心与锐气，与单纯“使悲伤”相比，强调特异性地削弱行动意愿、抹杀斗志与意志力。
groups.nuance_en: demoralize: destroy discipline, confidence, and fighting spirit completely (troops / workforce / team) · dishearten: dampen hope and enthusiasm after setbacks (student / investor / crew) · dispirit: rob of vitality, zest, and resolution, producing listlessness (defeat / weather / silence) · deject: cast into low, subdued spirits, usually manifesting posture-wise (applicant / suitor / candidate) · cast down: deeply depress or humiliate the spirit (soul / face / heart)
groups.nuance_zh: demoralize: 彻底瓦解团队的士气、纪律与必胜信念 (troops / workforce / team) · dishearten: 因受挫而浇灭希望热情使其丧气 (student / investor / crew) · dispirit: 抽空活力与锐气使其意兴阑珊 (defeat / weather / silence) · deject: 使情绪低落垂头丧气 (applicant / suitor / candidate) · cast down: 使心灵极度消沉沮丧或受辱沉沦 (soul / face / heart)

groups.name: Disfigure, Corrupt & Spoil · 玷污、损毁与败坏 (Deface, Blotch, Vitiate, Bollix)
groups.tip: 涂抹损毁物品破坏外观

items.def_en: [I/T] to dull the sheen of metal or diminish the purity and respect of a reputation
items.ex_en: The bribery scandal will surely tarnish the minister's previously unblemished political reputation.
items.ex_zh: 这桩受贿丑闻必将玷污这位部长此前无可指摘的政治声誉。
items.ex2_en: Polished silver cutlery tends to tarnish quickly when exposed to humid air.
items.ex2_zh: 抛光的银质餐具暴露在潮湿空气中时往往容易失去光泽。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to spoil, disfigure, or bungle the condition, appearance, or smooth working of something
items.ex_en: His careless typing managed to mess up the entire accounting spreadsheet within minutes.
items.ex_zh: 他粗心的键入在几分钟内就把整张会计电子表格搞得一团糟。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to ruin, damage, or bungle an arrangement, object, or situation
items.ex_en: One minor misunderstanding could completely screw up the fragile negotiations between both parties.
items.ex_zh: 一个小小的误会就可能彻底搞砸双方之间脆弱的谈判。

items.def_zh: 损毁，破坏……的美观或完整
items.def_en: to ruin or diminish the perfection, appearance, or enjoyment of something
items.ex_en: A sudden violent thunderstorm threatened to mar the beauty of the outdoor wedding.
items.ex_zh: 一场突如其来的猛烈雷暴眼看就要破坏这场户外婚礼的美好氛围。

items.def_en: to deliberately spoil or damage the surface or appearance of something, especially by writing, carving, or spraying graffiti on it.
items.ex_en: Vandals used bright spray paint to deface the historic marble fountain overnight.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子一夜之间用鲜艳的喷漆涂污了这座历史悠久的大理石喷泉。

items.def_en: (often passive) to mark or cover a surface with irregular spots or patches of color.
items.ex_en: Age and water damage began to blotch the surface of the antique mirror.
items.ex_zh: 岁月的侵蚀与水汽的损害使那面古董镜子的表面开始斑驳变色。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make something dirty, damaged, or hopelessly disorganized
items.ex_en: A faulty software update can easily foul up the airport's delicate flight scheduling system.
items.ex_zh: 一个有缺陷的软件更新很容易搞乱机场精细的航班调度系统。

items.def_en: to spoil the attractive appearance of a person, monument, or surface severely
items.ex_en: The severe chemical burns threatened to disfigure her facial features permanently without surgery.
items.ex_zh: 如果不做手术，严重的化学灼伤可能会永久损毁她的面部容貌。

items.def_zh: 损害，破坏，削弱；使变质；使在法律上失效
items.def_en: (formal) to spoil, weaken, or reduce the quality or effectiveness of something; to make legally invalid.
items.ex_en: Any procedural error in gathering evidence might vitiate the integrity of the prosecution.
items.ex_zh: 搜集证据过程中的任何程序性失误都可能损害检方指控的法律效力。

items.def_en: (informal) (often bollix up) to mess up, ruin, or bungle something completely.
items.ex_en: His terrible mismanagement threatened to bollix the entire multi-million dollar construction deal.
items.ex_zh: 他糟糕的经营管理险些把那笔数百万美元的建筑大单彻底搞砸。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on the specific manner in which value, beauty, validity, or smooth function is compromised—ranging from visual vandalism and staining (defacing, blotching) to formal-legal corruption (vitiating an argument or contract) and chaotic informal messing-up (bollixing).
groups.summary_zh: 通过涂抹损毁外观、从法律实质上败坏或彻底搞乱。
groups.desc_en: Denotes ruining the beauty, integrity, or flawless execution of an object or project, differing from plain 'destroy' by leaving the damaged entity intact but scarred, botched, or vitiated.
groups.desc_zh: 指破坏事物原有的外观完美度、纯洁性或运作有效性，与直接“摧毁”相比，受害者仍存留但已伤痕累累、丑化或漏洞百出。
groups.nuance_en: deface: spoil the surface appearance of something intentionally, often via graffiti (statue / wall / monument) · disfigure: permanently spoil the shape or aesthetic beauty of a face or form (scar / burns / architecture) · mar: impair the perfection, smooth finish, or enjoyment of (surface / record / reputation) · tarnish: dull the bright luster of metal, or soil honor (reputation / silver / legacy) · screw up: botch or blunder an operation through incompetence (plan / interview / chances)
groups.nuance_zh: deface: 故意涂鸦刻画以毁损外表形象 (statue / wall / monument) · disfigure: 留下永久性伤疤严重毁损容貌或形体美观 (scar / burns / architecture) · mar: 出现瑕疵破坏了整体的完美或愉悦 (surface / record / reputation) · tarnish: 使金属失去光泽，或玷污名誉声誉 (reputation / silver / legacy) · screw up: 因笨拙失误而把事情彻底搞砸 (plan / interview / chances)

groups.name: Disguise & Enshroud · 伪装与遮蔽 (Camouflage, Cloak, Shroud)
groups.tip: 如面纱般掩起真实面貌

items.def_en: (+ sth) disguise or hide problems superficiality without solving them
items.ex_en: The joint statement merely papered over deep disagreements between the two leaders.
items.ex_zh: 这份联合声明只是粉饰了两位领导人之间的深刻分歧。

items.def_en: (+ sth) conceal something completely from view or public knowledge
items.ex_en: Corrupt officials conspired secretly to cover up the financial fraud from federal auditors.
items.ex_zh: 腐败官员密谋向联邦审计人员掩盖这起财务欺诈的真相。

items.def_en: to cover something completely with a thick layer of snow, smoke, or cloud
items.ex_en: Heavy morning snow began to blanket the quiet suburban streets in white silence.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的大雪开始将安静的郊区街道厚厚地覆盖在一片洁白的寂静中。

items.def_en: To hide someone or something carefully so that they cannot be seen, or to prevent something from being known.
items.ex_en: He tried his best to conceal his mounting anxiety behind an easy smile.
items.ex_zh: 他竭尽全力用轻松的微笑来掩饰自己内心与日俱增的焦虑。

items.def_en: 1. To change someone's appearance or voice so that people cannot recognize them. 2. To hide a true feeling, intention, or fact so that others do not notice it.
items.ex_en: The spy wore an elaborate costume to disguise himself as a simple peasant.
items.ex_zh: 那名间谍穿戴精细的服饰，将自己伪装成一个普通的农夫。

items.def_en: To cover something with a veil; to hide, mask, or disguise feelings, intentions, or facts.
items.ex_en: Diplomats often veil their mutual distrust behind polished smiles and formal courtesies.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们往往在优雅的微笑和正式礼节后掩饰彼此间的猜忌。

items.def_en: To cover, hide, or disguise something, especially so that it remains secret or unknown.
items.ex_en: Dense morning fog served to cloak the enemy warship from defensive coastal lookouts.
items.ex_zh: 清晨浓密的迷雾遮蔽了敌方战舰，使其未被海岸防御瞭望哨发现。

items.def_en: (literary) to envelop or cover something as if with a loose sleeveless garment
items.ex_en: Thick velvet shadows began to mantle the ancient ruins as twilight faded away.
items.ex_zh: 随着暮色渐褪，厚重的如天鹅绒般的阴影开始笼罩这处古老废墟。

items.def_en: 1. To hide an animal, soldier, or vehicle by coloring or covering it to blend in with its surroundings. 2. To disguise a fact, feeling, or intention to prevent it from being noticed.
items.ex_en: Soldiers attached leaves and netting to camouflage their military vehicle in dense foliage.
items.ex_zh: 士兵们挂上树叶和伪装网，将他们的军车隐藏在浓密的枝叶中。

items.def_zh: 遮蔽，隐藏，笼罩；裹以裹尸布
items.def_en: 1. To cover, hide, or surround something so that it is not clearly seen or understood. 2. To wrap a dead body in cloth for burial.
items.ex_en: A pervasive quiet seemed to shroud the desolate valley after the fierce storm passed.
items.ex_zh: 猛烈的风暴过去后，一片无所不在的死寂似乎笼罩了那座荒凉的山谷。

groups.summary_en: An agent deliberately obscures the identity, appearance, or existence of something through active concealment strategies such as military camouflage, misleading disguises, heavy enveloping wraps, or metaphorical shrouds.
groups.summary_zh: 采用伪装、斗篷包裹或厚重织物笼罩以彻底掩饰真实面目。
groups.desc_en: Denotes placing a deceptive or obscuring layer over something to hide its true shape, identity, or defects, contrasting with mere 'hiding' by creating a simulated or impenetrable exterior barrier.
groups.desc_zh: 指在事物表面覆盖遮挡层或伪装以掩盖其真实形态或瑕疵，与普通“隐藏”相比，强调营造出假象或严密的包裹遮蔽屏障。
groups.nuance_en: camouflage: disguise by blending seamlessly into surrounding patterns (troops / vehicles / intention) · cloak: wrap in an impenetrable mantle of secrecy or darkness (operation / mystery / identity) · shroud: envelop completely so as to make invisible or ominous (mountain / body / secrecy) · veil: partially conceal behind a semi-transparent filter or pretext (threat / face / meaning) · paper over: superficially patch up cracks or disputes without resolving the underlying issue (differences / cracks / problems)
groups.nuance_zh: camouflage: 通过与背景融为一体实现军事或意图伪装 (troops / vehicles / intention) · cloak: 用严密的外衣或夜色笼罩隐匿真相 (operation / mystery / identity) · shroud: 如裹尸布般全面遮罩使其陷入阴郁或未知 (mountain / body / secrecy) · veil: 半遮半掩或以借口托词含蓄遮蔽 (threat / face / meaning) · paper over: 敷衍粉饰分歧裂痕而不触及根本矛盾 (differences / cracks / problems)

groups.name: Dishearten & Deject · 使沮丧与挫伤 (Dishearten, Dismay, Crush)
groups.tip: 大受打击导致信心丧失殆尽

items.def_en: cause someone to lose determination, confidence, or enthusiasm
items.ex_en: The critical review failed to dishearten the young and ambitious theater director completely.
items.ex_zh: 苛刻的剧评未能彻底使这位雄心勃勃的年轻话剧导演灰心丧气。

items.def_en: make someone feel unhappy, dispirited, and downcast
items.ex_en: The prolonged isolation caused by illness did deject him far more than expected.
items.ex_zh: 因病导致的长期隔离使他感到的沮丧情绪远超原本的预期。

items.def_zh: (+ sb) 使情绪低落；拖垮（心智）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to lower someone's spirits or cause them to feel depressed
items.ex_en: Rising energy costs could drag down the entire manufacturing sector.
items.ex_zh: 不断上涨的能源成本可能会拖垮整个制造业。

items.def_zh: (+ sb) 使心事重重；压抑（情绪）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to burden someone mentally with worries or sadness
items.ex_en: She felt weighed down by domestic responsibilities and work pressures.
items.ex_zh: 她感到家庭责任和工作压力压得自己喘不过气来。

items.raw_cluster: 使沮丧与使惊愕 Dismay & Dishearten
items.def_en: To make someone feel deeply worried, disappointed, or disheartened by something unexpected.
items.ex_en: The sudden cancellation of government funding will dismay many grassroots community organizers.
items.ex_zh: 政府资助的突然撤销将使许多基层社区组织者深感沮丧与惊愕。

items.raw_cluster: 使气馁与使沮丧 Discourage & Deject
items.def_zh: 使幻灭，使幻想破灭，使醒悟
items.def_en: (often passive) To destroy someone's illusions, making them realize that something they admired is not as good as they thought.
items.ex_en: The revelations of corruption will disillusion voters who placed great trust in him.
items.ex_zh: 腐败丑闻的曝光将使那些曾对他寄予厚望的选民幻想破灭。

items.def_en: dampen someone's enthusiasm or high spirits
items.ex_en: Repeated technical failures threatened to dispirit the dedicated team of young engineers.
items.ex_zh: 接连发生的技术故障眼看就要挫伤那支敬业的年轻工程师团队的斗志。

items.def_zh: (+ sb) 使沮丧；使意志消沉
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone to feel extremely dejected or disheartened
items.ex_en: Unfavorable economic forecasts continue to cast down business owners throughout the entire region.
items.ex_zh: 不利的经济预测持续使整个地区的私营企业主们感到沮丧与消沉。

items.raw_cluster: 使气馁与使沮丧 Discourage & Deject
items.def_zh: 使气馁，使沮丧崩溃；使失去男子气概
items.def_en: (dated or literary) To deprive someone of courage, confidence, or fortitude; to cause to break down emotionally.
items.ex_en: The horrific sight of the battlefield threatened to unman the seasoned warrior completely.
items.ex_zh: 战场上恐怖可怖的惨状险些让那位身经百战的勇士彻底丧失胆气。

items.def_en: overwhelm someone emotionally so completely that their spirit is destroyed
items.ex_en: Losing the championship final in the final minute would crush any athlete emotionally.
items.ex_zh: 在最后一分钟输掉决赛冠军，足以在情感上彻底摧毁任何一名运动员。

groups.summary_en: Events, revelations, or hardships sap someone's spirits, courage, or confidence, ranging from mild disenchantment to total psychological paralysis.
groups.summary_zh: 外界打击使人丧失信心、热情或勇气，程度由气馁递增至崩溃绝望。
groups.desc_en: Denotes inflicting profound psychological despondency or crushing disappointment, contrasting with milder 'unsettle' through the heavy, downward emotional sinkhole it plunges the subject into.
groups.desc_zh: 指给人的精神带来深重沉重的沮丧、幻灭或挫败感，与轻微的“烦扰”相比，强调情绪被沉重下坠感所吞噬。
groups.nuance_en: dismay: fill with shocking distress mixed with bewildered discouragement (news / reaction / supporters) · disillusion: shatter cherished naive ideals or trust by revealing harsh realities (idealists / public / youth) · weigh down: oppress mentally with overwhelming sorrow or heavy burdens (conscience / heart / worries) · deject: push down into gloom and downcast listlessness (spirits / mood / countenance) · drag down: progressively pull another into lower spirits or despair (family / morale / team)
groups.nuance_zh: dismay: 震惊、惶恐与失望交织使其手足无措 (news / reaction / supporters) · disillusion: 刺破美好幻想让其面对现实而大失所望 (idealists / public / youth) · weigh down: 沉重心事或负罪感压得人喘不过气 (conscience / heart / worries) · deject: 使神采颓丧情绪消沉 (spirits / mood / countenance) · drag down: 拖累情绪使其不断沉沦消极 (family / morale / team)

groups.name: Dismiss & Minimize Significance · 轻蔑与轻忽贬抑 (Overlook, Disregard, Trivialize)
groups.tip: 粗心疏漏乃至刻意漠视

items.def_zh: 对……不以为意；耸肩置之度外
items.def_en: (+ sth) to treat something serious or unpleasant as trivial and unimportant
items.ex_en: The seasoned politician chose to shrug off the personal attacks from the media.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的政客选择对媒体的人身攻击耸耸肩不以为意。

items.def_zh: 忽视，忽略；不予理会；俯瞰；宽恕
items.def_en: 1. To fail to notice or consider something; to choose to ignore a fault or offense. 2. To have a view of a place from above.
items.ex_en: Managers must not overlook minor workplace safety violations that could lead to accidents.
items.ex_zh: 管理者绝不能忽视工作场所中那些可能引发事故的轻微安全违规行为。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to dismiss or ignore an objection, argument, or person casually
items.ex_en: He tried to brush off the criticism as petty jealousy.
items.ex_zh: 他试图对这些批评不予理会，将其归咎于小人的嫉妒。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to treat an embarrassing, serious, or critical situation lightly through laughter
items.ex_en: He tried to laugh off the criticism, but it clearly bothered him.
items.ex_zh: 他试图对批评一笑了之，但显然心里很介意。

items.def_zh: 挥手打发；轻描淡写地排除
items.def_en: (+ sth) to dismiss an objection or opinion without giving it serious consideration
items.ex_en: The arrogant director attempted to wave aside all legitimate concerns raised by staff.
items.ex_zh: 那位傲慢的管理者试图挥手打发员工们提出的所有合情合理的担忧。

items.def_en: to decide that something or someone is not worthy of serious consideration or belief
items.ex_en: The manager dismissed her valid concerns about workplace safety as mere exaggerations.
items.ex_zh: 经理把她对工作场所安全的合理担忧轻蔑地当作单纯的夸大其词而不予考虑。

items.def_en: to treat someone with disrespect or deliberate neglect
items.ex_en: He felt slighted when his colleagues organized a celebratory dinner without inviting him.
items.ex_zh: 同事们组织庆祝晚宴却没有邀请他，这让他觉得自己受到了怠慢。

items.def_en: To ignore something or treat it as unimportant and unworthy of attention.
items.ex_en: The driver blatantly disregarded the warning signs and sped through the red light.
items.ex_zh: 这名司机公然无视警告标志，闯红灯超速驶过。

items.def_zh: 使显得微不足道，轻视，贬低
items.def_en: To make something seem unimportant, less serious, or less significant than it really is.
items.ex_en: Critics argued that the sensational news coverage trivialized the serious humanitarian crisis.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士认为，耸人听闻的新闻报道贬低了这场严重人道主义危机的分量。

items.def_en: to represent or treat something as being of far less value, size, or importance than it really is
items.ex_en: The company attempted to minimize the financial losses caused by the recent data breach.
items.ex_zh: 该公司试图淡化最近数据泄露事件所造成的经济损失。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame range along an intensity continuum of treating matters as unimportant, starting from unmindful omission, advancing through deliberate refusal to respect, to active verbal or cognitive trivialization.
groups.summary_zh: 从无心漏看、故意视若无睹到积极贬损、将问题微不足道化。
groups.desc_en: Denotes treating an objection, claim, or entity as trivial, unworthy of serious consideration, or completely negligible, contrasting with 'arguing' by refusing to even engage with its merits.
groups.desc_zh: 指将某项异议、指控或人物视作微不足道而不予理会，与“争辩反驳”相比，强调根本不屑于正面应对或将其当场扫地出门。
groups.nuance_en: brush off: rebuff or dismiss casually and without consideration (question / critic / complaint) · shrug off: treat an injury, criticism, or setback as trivial and unworthy of care (criticism / injury / setback) · wave aside: haughtily gesture away an objection or concern as irrelevant (concern / protest / objection) · laugh off: deflect a serious threat or awkward blunder by treating it as a joke (rumor / accusation / blunder) · slight: treat someone with disdainful neglect or deliberate insult (guest / contribution / host)
groups.nuance_zh: brush off: 漫不经心地随手打发或回绝 (question / critic / complaint) · shrug off: 耸耸肩对批评或伤痛毫不在意一笑了之 (criticism / injury / setback) · wave aside: 傲慢摆手将抗议或顾虑撇在一边 (concern / protest / objection) · laugh off: 嘻嘻哈哈将严肃指控当作玩笑来化解 (rumor / accusation / blunder) · slight: 居高临下地轻视、怠慢或侮辱他人 (guest / contribution / host)

groups.name: Distinguish & Differentiate · 区分与辨别 (Distinguish, Differentiate, Individuate)
groups.tip: 观察细节以挑出差异

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to identify or distinguish someone or something from a surrounding group or background
items.ex_en: The victim was able to pick out the attacker from a lineup of suspects.
items.ex_zh: 受害者能够从一排嫌疑人中指认出袭击者。

items.def_en: to perceive the difference between two or more similar people or things
items.ex_en: The twins look so similar that even their teachers can hardly tell them apart.
items.ex_zh: 这对双胞胎长得太像了，连他们的老师都很难分清。

items.def_zh: 使显出特色，使与众不同
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to show that someone or something is different from others or has distinct qualities
items.ex_en: Her exceptional leadership skills marked her out for early promotion.
items.ex_zh: 她出众的领导能力注定了她会早早获得晋升。

items.def_zh: 挑出，单独挑选出（以便特别对待或区分）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to choose or identify one person or thing from a group for special attention, praise, or criticism
items.ex_en: It is unfair to single out one player when the whole team performed poorly.
items.ex_zh: 在全队表现都很差的情况下，单单挑出一名球员来责备是不公平的。

items.def_zh: 区分，辨别；认出，看清；使出众，使显赫
items.def_en: 1. To recognize or understand the difference between people or things. 2. To see, hear, or recognize something clearly.
items.ex_en: It was difficult to distinguish between the two identical twins in dim lighting.
items.ex_zh: 在昏暗的光线下，很难分清那一对长相相同的双胞胎。

items.def_zh: 区分，辨别；构成……的区别，使有别于
items.def_en: 1. (+ between) To recognize or show the differences between people or things. 2. To make someone or something different or distinct.
items.ex_en: Specialized features differentiate this professional software tool from cheaper consumer alternatives on sale.
items.ex_zh: 专业的特性使这款专业软件工具有别于市面上更便宜的消费级替代品。

items.def_zh: 区分辨明两者间的异同
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ between/from) to recognize or point out the difference between two things
items.ex_en: Trained experts can easily discriminate authentic antique pottery from modern factory reproductions.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的专家能够轻松区分真正的古代陶器与现代工厂仿制品。

items.def_en: to detect, recognize, or discriminate subtle differences by careful perception
items.ex_en: The seasoned perfumer could discern subtle hints of vanilla hidden in the fragrance.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的调香师能够敏锐洞察出香水中隐藏的一丝微妙香草气息。

items.def_zh: 使个体化，赋予个性；区分，使具备独特性
items.def_en: 1. To distinguish an individual person or thing from others of the same kind; give individuality to.
items.ex_en: Unique architectural details individuate each historic townhome from the modern surrounding apartments.
items.ex_zh: 独特的建筑细节使每栋历史悠久的联排别墅与周围的现代公寓明显区分开来。

items.def_en: to establish the clear boundaries, limits, or distinct categories of something
items.ex_en: The committee established clear policies to demarcate managerial roles from staff responsibilities.
items.ex_zh: 委员会制定了明确的政策，以清晰划分管理职责与员工职责的界限。

groups.summary_en: A cognizer recognizes, separates, or highlights the characteristic traits that set one entity apart from another or render it singular.
groups.summary_zh: 认知主体审视特征以分辨差异，或赋予事物独特个体性。
groups.desc_en: Denotes intellectually or visually perceiving boundaries, differences, and unique marks among similar items, contrasting with vague 'noticing' through its comparative, analytical precision.
groups.desc_zh: 指在智识或视觉上辨明同类事物之间的细微边界与特有标志，与粗略的“看到/注意”相比，强调比较分析性的精确辨识能力。
groups.nuance_en: discern: perceive subtle or obscure details through keen insight or sight (pattern / motive / shape) · discriminate: make fine, critical distinctions between qualities or categories (flavor / nuances / right and wrong) · differentiate: identify or constitute the specific boundary that sets one apart from another (species / product / symptom) · distinguish: recognize clear markers separating things, or confer special prestige (features / twins / self) · tell apart: distinguish visually between two near-identical items (twins / counterfeits / accents)
groups.nuance_zh: discern: 凭借敏锐洞察力看透模糊隐晦的细节 (pattern / motive / shape) · discriminate: 对细微品质品位进行批判性辨别 (flavor / nuances / right and wrong) · differentiate: 确立使两者截然不同的本质特征或边界 (species / product / symptom) · distinguish: 辨明显著区别特征，或使自己出类拔萃 (features / twins / self) · tell apart: 从肉眼或直观上分清两个极相似之物 (twins / counterfeits / accents)

groups.name: Draft & Publish Content · 撰写与出版发售 (Draft, Serialize, Ghostwrite)
groups.tip: 以连载方式公开发行刊物

items.def_en: [I/T] to prepare and issue a book, journal, or piece of music for public sale
items.ex_en: The university press will publish his new historical research paper next spring.
items.ex_zh: 大学出版社将于明年春天出版他的最新历史研究论文。

items.def_en: to write or compose a letter, article, or literary work
items.ex_en: The lonely poet penned an exquisite tribute to his distant, forgotten homeland.
items.ex_zh: 孤独的诗人亲笔撰写了一首优美的颂歌，献给他遥远而遗忘的故土。

items.def_en: to write a book, report, or paper jointly with another person
items.ex_en: Two prominent climate scientists co-authored the comprehensive report on rising sea levels.
items.ex_zh: 两位著名的气候学家合著了这份关于海平面上升的综合报告。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to publish, release, or produce something for the public
items.ex_en: The independent record label will put out her highly anticipated debut album tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 这家独立唱片厂牌将于明天发行她备受期待的首张专辑。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to publish or release a new book, album, or other product
items.ex_en: The renowned publisher plans to bring out an illustrated edition of the classic novel.
items.ex_zh: 著名出版社计划推出这部经典小说的精美插图版。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to write or draw something very quickly and effortlessly
items.ex_en: She had to dash off a quick thank-you note before catching her flight.
items.ex_zh: 在赶飞机之前，她不得不匆匆草拟了一封简短的感谢信。

items.def_en: to produce a book or report by bringing together material from various sources
items.ex_en: The research team spent months compiling data from hundreds of academic field surveys.
items.ex_zh: 研究小组花费数月时间汇编了来自数百份学术实地调查的数据。

items.def_zh: 连载，分期发表；（计算机）序列化
items.def_en: 1. To publish or broadcast a story, book, or show in regular installments; (computing) to convert data into a sequential format.
items.ex_en: The literary magazine chose to serialize the gripping novel over six consecutive issues.
items.ex_zh: 这家文学杂志决定在连续六期杂志上连载这部扣人心弦的小说。

items.def_en: 1. To rewrite in a different code or assign new classification codes to data.
items.ex_en: The software engineer had to recode the legacy database script for better security.
items.ex_zh: 软件工程师不得不重写旧版数据库脚本以提升系统安全性。

items.def_en: 1. To write a book, speech, or article for another person who takes official credit as the author.
items.ex_en: A seasoned political journalist was hired to ghostwrite the retired senator's memoirs.
items.ex_zh: 一位经验丰富的政治记者受聘为这位退休参议员代笔撰写回忆录。

groups.summary_en: Professional creative workflow verbs covering the composition, adaptation, and segmented release of written texts for public distribution, ranging from unauthorized/proxy drafting to episodic publication.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖文本起草、代笔编写、分期连载及付印发行等职业出版全流程动作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the professional production and dissemination of written materials into the public sphere, differing from private 'writing' by including compilation, collaborative authorship, and formal publication pipelines.
groups.desc_zh: 指将文字内容进行专业化撰写、编纂并推向公共领域发行，与私密“书写”相比，涵盖了文稿起草、合著及正规出版发行的全流程。
groups.nuance_en: pen: write or compose formally with an authorial voice (letter / novel / memoir) · co-author: collaborate equally with another in writing a text (paper / report / study) · serialize: publish a literary work sequentially in successive installments (novel / story / column) · compile: assemble gathered material from diverse sources into a collective work (anthology / dictionary / list) · bring out: produce and issue a book or album into commercial release (edition / album / volume)
groups.nuance_zh: pen: 亲自执笔撰写正式书信或文学著作 (letter / novel / memoir) · co-author: 与他人作为共同作者合写学术论文或著作 (paper / report / study) · serialize: 在报刊或媒介上分期连载作品 (novel / story / column) · compile: 搜集多方素材汇编成集 (anthology / dictionary / list) · bring out: 出版发行新版书籍或专辑 (edition / album / volume)

groups.name: Dress & Clothe · 穿衣与着装 (Costume, Clothe, Attire)
groups.tip: 穿戴日常衣物或穿上特定服装

items.def_en: to provide with or put garments on someone
items.ex_en: The caring matron clothed the shivering orphans in warm hand-knitted woolen coats.
items.ex_zh: 慈爱的护士长给瑟瑟发抖的孤儿们穿上了温暖的手工针织大衣。

items.def_zh: 给……穿上衣服；使着特定服装（尤指修道士服等）
items.def_en: (archaic or literary) To clothe or dress someone, especially in a particular costume or habit.
items.ex_en: The solemn ceremony habited the devout novitiates in traditional dark monastic robes.
items.ex_zh: 庄严的仪式为虔诚的见习修士们穿上了传统的深色修道士袍。

items.def_zh: 给（演员等）穿上戏服；为……提供服装
items.def_en: To dress someone in a costume, or to provide actors or performers with suitable costumes.
items.ex_en: The wardrobe department costumed the entire cast in colorful Victorian era attire.
items.ex_zh: 服装部门为全体演员穿上了色彩斑斓的维多利亚时代戏服。

items.def_en: (informal) to dress someone in a special or conspicuous outfit
items.ex_en: She decided to rig out her young son in a charming pirate outfit.
items.ex_zh: 她决定把年幼的儿子装扮成可爱的海盗模样。

items.def_en: to put on formal, fancy, or specialized costume clothing
items.ex_en: You don't need to dress up; casual clothes are fine for the party.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要盛装打扮，去参加聚会穿便装就行。
items.ex2_en: She decided to dress up the plain dining table with colorful flowers.
items.ex2_zh: 她决定用色彩斑斓的鲜花将朴素的餐桌装饰一番。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to dress or decorate someone or something in a very attractive or elaborate manner
items.ex_en: They deck out the reception hall with fairy lights and fresh winter pine.
items.ex_zh: 他们用小彩灯和新鲜冬松把接待大厅精心装扮了一番。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to provide someone with the necessary clothes or equipment
items.ex_en: The school will kit out every member of the football squad with new gear.
items.ex_zh: 学校将为足球队的每位成员配备崭新的运动装备。

items.def_zh: 穿上特定服装（如西装、运动服或制服）
items.def_en: to put on a special suit of clothes, uniform, or athletic gear
items.ex_en: The players rushed into the locker room to suit up before the championship game.
items.ex_zh: 球员们冲进更衣室穿上比赛球服，准备迎接冠军争夺战。

items.def_en: (formal/literary) to dress someone in formal or elaborate clothing
items.ex_en: The royal servants attired the young monarch in velvet robes for the coronation.
items.ex_zh: 皇家仆从为年轻的君主穿上天鹅绒长袍，以迎接加冕典礼。

items.def_en: (formal/passive) to dress someone in a distinctive style or uniform
items.ex_en: The palace guards were garbed in ceremonial scarlet tunics and tall bearskin hats.
items.ex_zh: 宫廷卫士们身穿猩红色仪仗制服，头戴高耸的熊皮帽。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe outfitting a person in clothing, garments, or specialized regalia, ranging from literary dressing to dressing up in theatrical costume.
groups.summary_zh: 指为某人穿上特定衣物、制服或舞台戏服等装扮行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes donning garments or outfitting a person in specialized, decorative, or situational attire, contrasting with functional 'wear' by foregrounding the deliberate act of styling, costuming, or equipping.
groups.desc_zh: 指为人穿上特定风格、装饰性或功能性的整套服饰，与单纯功能性的“穿着”相比，强调造型装扮、盛装打扮或披挂整齐的仪式化动作。
groups.nuance_en: clothe: provide with essential garments, or cover the bare body (poor / child / nudist) · deck out: dress or adorn showily and festively for display (costume / finery / jewels) · rig out: furnish with a distinctive, elaborate, or unusual outfit (sailors / wedding party / kids) · costume: dress someone up deliberately in historical or theatrical disguise (actors / performers / cast) · dress up: put on formal or fancy clothing exceeding normal daywear (evening / party / interview)
groups.nuance_zh: clothe: 为其提供蔽体衣物或穿戴整齐 (poor / child / nudist) · deck out: 盛装打扮打扮得花枝招展以供展示 (costume / finery / jewels) · rig out: 为特定场合为其整饬配备全套独特行头 (sailors / wedding party / kids) · costume: 为演员穿戴戏剧道具服装以实现角色扮演 (actors / performers / cast) · dress up: 穿上超出日常标准的高级礼服盛装出席 (evening / party / interview)

groups.name: Drink & Swallow · 饮用与吞饮 (Ingesting Liquids)
groups.tip: 大口吞下或畅快痛饮

items.def_en: To drink a liquid slowly by taking only a small amount at a time.
items.ex_en: She sat quietly on the veranda, slowly sipping hot chamomile tea from a porcelain mug.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐在阳台上，从小瓷杯里细细啜饮着热洋甘菊茶。

items.def_zh: 一饮而尽，大口吞下（尤指酒）
items.def_en: (+ sth) drink an alcoholic beverage quickly or in large gulps
items.ex_en: He quickly knocked back a glass of cold beer after finishing the yard work.
items.ex_zh: 干完庭院里的活后，他迅速大口喝下了一杯冰凉的啤酒。

items.def_en: (+ sth) quickly drain or drink down a glass of liquid in one draft
items.ex_en: The exhausted traveler tossed off the remaining water and asked for another fresh glass.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的旅人仰脖喝尽了杯底剩下的水，又要了一杯新鲜的。

items.def_en: 1. To take liquid into your mouth and swallow it. 2. To consume alcoholic beverages, especially regularly or in large quantities.
items.ex_en: Doctors advise that every healthy adult should drink plenty of fresh water daily.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议每个健康的成年人每天都应当饮用充足的新鲜水分。

items.def_en: to drink deeply and heartily, especially alcoholic beverages
items.ex_en: The merry sailors quaffed mug after mug of spiced ale by the fire.
items.ex_zh: 欢闹的水手们围坐在火炉旁，痛饮了一杯又一杯加香料的麦芽酒。

items.def_en: to take a quick, hearty drink directly from a bottle or container
items.ex_en: He paused during his run to swig some cold water from his bottle.
items.ex_zh: 他在跑步中途停下来，直接对准水壶大口豪饮了几口凉水。

items.def_zh: 一口吞下，一饮而尽；击倒，击落
items.def_en: To swallow or drink something quickly, especially in one gulp; to bring or knock down.
items.ex_en: Thirsty after the race, she downed the whole glass of lemonade in one gulp.
items.ex_zh: 比赛后口渴难耐，她一口气喝光了整整一杯柠檬水。

items.def_zh: 大口吞下；狼吞虎咽地喝
items.def_en: to swallow large mouthfuls of liquid quickly and noisily
items.ex_en: He gulped down the lukewarm coffee in a rush before sprinting toward the train.
items.ex_zh: 在冲向火车前，他匆匆忙忙地大口咽下了温温的咖啡。

items.def_en: To drink large quantities of alcohol or liquid greedily; to rinse or flush something with water.
items.ex_en: The rowdy crowd sat in the back tavern, swilling cheap lager until midnight.
items.ex_zh: 那帮吵闹的酒客坐在酒馆后座，大口畅饮着廉价拉格啤酒直至深夜。

items.def_en: to drink all of a beverage quickly without stopping to breathe
items.ex_en: His college friends dared him to chug an entire bottle of sparkling soda.
items.ex_zh: 大学朋友们向他打赌，让他一口气喝光整整一瓶苏打汽水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the physical intake of liquids into the mouth and stomach, differentiating between delicate tasting, steady ingestion, and greedy or rapid gulping.
groups.summary_zh: 描述将液体摄入口中并咽下的动作，涵盖从浅抿啜饮到大口狂饮。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the physical act of taking liquids into the mouth and swallowing them, differentiated internally by pacing, volume per draw, and degree of leisure or urgency.
groups.desc_zh: 指将液体摄入口中并下咽的生理动作，其内部通过饮用速度、单次吸入体量以及是慢品还是牛饮来区分微差。
groups.nuance_en: sip: drink in tiny, measured measures to savor or test temperature (tea / wine / soup) · quaff: drink heartily, thirstily, and with exuberant enjoyment (ale / goblet / draft) · swig: take large, uncouth drafts directly from a bottle or flask (whiskey / water / beer) · knock back: swallow a strong alcoholic shot rapidly in one go (shots / vodka / espresso) · gulp: swallow large mouthfuls audibly or in great haste (water / air / drink)
groups.nuance_zh: sip: 小口细啜以品尝风味或试探温度 (tea / wine / soup) · quaff: 痛快淋漓地大口畅饮美酒 (ale / goblet / draft) · swig: 仰头对着瓶口大口猛灌烈酒或水 (whiskey / water / beer) · knock back: 一饮而尽一口闷掉高浓度烈酒 (shots / vodka / espresso) · gulp: 喉头发声、大口急促地猛灌吞下 (water / air / drink)

groups.name: Dwell & Reside · 居住与栖宿
groups.tip: 定居常住或短期借宿

items.def_en: (+ at/with) to stay in a place on a temporary basis, often paying for accommodation
items.ex_en: During his college semester abroad, he lodged with a friendly local host family.
items.ex_zh: 在大学出国留学期间，他寄宿在一个友好的当地寄宿家庭。
items.ex2_en: The university agreed to lodge international exchange students in newly renovated dormitories.
items.ex2_zh: 大学同意将国际交换生安置在刚翻修的宿舍里住宿。

items.def_en: (+ at/in) to stay in a location temporarily as a guest or traveler
items.ex_en: The weary diplomat chose to sojourn in the peaceful mountain village for a month.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的外交官选择在这个宁静的山村暂住逗留一个月。

items.def_en: to stay or hide in a safe, secluded, or secret place
items.ex_en: The stranded hikers had to hole up in an abandoned cabin until dawn.
items.ex_zh: 滞留的徒步旅行者不得不在一间废弃的小木屋里蛰居栖身直到黎明。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) to start living with someone, especially as romantic partners without being married
items.ex_en: He decided to shack up with his girlfriend in a small downtown apartment.
items.ex_zh: 他决定和女朋友一起在市中心的一套小公寓里同居。

items.def_en: to go to sleep or find a temporary place to sleep, often in makeshift accommodations
items.ex_en: The exhausted soldiers bunked down on simple cots set up inside the gymnasium.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的士兵们在体育馆内搭建的简易折叠床上搭铺过夜。

items.def_zh: 扎营，宿营，在帐篷中居住
items.def_en: (dated) To camp out or dwell in a tent.
items.ex_en: The adventurous travelers tented near the quiet lake under the vast starry sky.
items.ex_zh: 富有冒险精神的旅行者们在浩瀚星空下，靠近宁静的湖畔扎营宿夜。

items.def_en: 1. To live or have one's home in a particular place permanently or for a long period. 2. (+ in) (of rights, power, or qualities) To belong to or be inherent in someone or something.
items.ex_en: The retired diplomat intends to reside permanently in the peaceful countryside near Florence.
items.ex_zh: 这位退休外交官打算在佛罗伦萨附近宁静的乡间永久定居。

items.def_en: (formal) To occupy a building, land, or property as a rent-paying tenant.
items.ex_en: Several innovative tech startups currently tenant the renovated brick warehouse on waterfront avenue.
items.ex_zh: 目前有数家创新科技初创企业租借了滨水大道上改建的砖砌仓库。

items.def_en: (+ in/at) to live as a permanent or settled inhabitant in a particular place
items.ex_en: Solitary hermits dwelt among the remote northern hills far from noisy modern cities.
items.ex_zh: 孤独的隐士栖居在远离喧嚣现代城市的偏远北方群山之中。

items.def_en: to occupy a territory, building, or habitat continuously as a resident
items.ex_en: Numerous rare species of tropical birds inhabit the dense equatorial rainforest reserve.
items.ex_zh: 许多珍稀热带鸟类栖息并居住在这片茂密的赤道雨林保护区内。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote having one's ongoing home, domicile, or temporary lodging in a specific place. They range from formal civil habitation ('reside') and tenancy ('tenant') to transient lodging in tents ('tent') or staying temporarily as an occupant ('sojourn', 'lodge').
groups.summary_zh: 指在某处安居、定居、租住或作为宿处临时栖留。
groups.desc_en: Denotes establishing temporary or formal physical habitation in a space, differing from generic 'living' or 'staying' by emphasizing legal tenure, transience, or provisional shelter.
groups.desc_zh: 指在特定物理空间内建立长期或临时的栖居状态，与单纯的“居住/停留”相比，更凸显法定居留权、过渡寄宿或简陋庇护的色彩。
groups.nuance_en: reside: formal or legal permanent dwelling (citizen / territory / country) · lodge: rented or temporary accommodation (guest / tourist / tenant) · sojourn: literary temporary stay in a foreign place (traveler / scholar / exile) · hole up: secretive or defensive confinement (gang / fugitive / rebel) · shack up: informal cohabitation without marriage (partner / couple)
groups.nuance_zh: reside: 正式或法律意义上的定居 (citizen / territory / country) · lodge: 寄宿或租住临时寓所 (guest / tourist / tenant) · sojourn: 旅居或客居异乡 (traveler / scholar / exile) · hole up: 隐匿避险或藏匿闭门不出 (gang / fugitive / rebel) · shack up: 非婚同居或搭伙暂住 (partner / couple)

groups.name: Elect & Appoint · 选举与任免 (Elect, Appoint, Commission)
groups.tip: 民主表决推举干部

items.def_zh: 投票，选举；表决，投票决定
items.def_en: 1. To express a choice in an election or referendum by casting a ballot or raising a hand. 2. To decide, approve, or grant something by a formal vote.
items.ex_en: Over eighty percent of eligible citizens cast their ballots to vote on Tuesday.
items.ex_zh: 超过百分之八十的合资格公民在周二投出了选票参与表决。

items.def_zh: 任命，委任（为军官）；委托制作；使（军舰等）服役
items.def_en: 1. To officially appoint someone to the rank of officer in the armed forces. 2. To officially order or ask someone to create or do something. 3. To put a ship, plane, or facility into active military service.
items.ex_en: The prestigious military academy commissioned twenty exemplary young graduates as naval officers yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 这所著名的军事学院昨日正式任命了二十名优秀的年轻毕业生为海军军官。

items.def_en: 1. To choose someone for a position by voting. 2. To choose to do something.
items.ex_en: The town residents gathered together to elect a trustworthy new mayor this November.
items.ex_zh: 全镇居民齐聚一堂，准备在今年十一月选举一位值得信赖的新市长。

items.def_zh: 任命，委派；约定，确定（时间、地点）
items.def_en: 1. To officially choose someone for a job or responsibility. 2. To arrange or decide on a time or place for something.
items.ex_en: The governing board decided to appoint her as the company's chief operating officer.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定任命她担任公司的首席运营官职务。

items.def_en: to officially choose someone to hold a specific office or perform a duty
items.ex_en: The president designated a seasoned special envoy to lead the critical peace negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 总统指派了一位经验丰富的特使来主导至关重要的和平谈判。

items.def_zh: 提名（作为候选人或任职者）
items.def_en: to formally propose someone as a candidate for election, honor, or public appointment
items.ex_en: Senior party delegates agreed to nominate the respected governor for the upcoming election.
items.ex_zh: 党内资深代表一致同意提名受人尊敬的州长参加即将举行的大选。

items.def_en: (+ sb) elect someone to an official position or into government
items.ex_en: Citizens voted in a reform-minded mayor during the recent election.
items.ex_zh: 市民在最近的选举中选出了一位具有改革思想的新市长。

items.def_en: (+ sb) officially induct someone into public office by administering an oath
items.ex_en: The new president will be sworn in on January 20th.
items.ex_zh: 新总统将于1月20日宣誓就职。

items.def_en: to place someone formally in an official office or rank with customary ceremony
items.ex_en: The university installed the distinguished foreign scholar as its new chancellor yesterday afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 昨天下午，该大学为这位杰出的外国学者举行仪式，使其正式就任新校长。

items.def_en: to authorize or appoint someone to act as a representative or deputy
items.ex_en: The director deputed his senior assistant to sign the international contract on his behalf.
items.ex_zh: 主任授权其高级助理代表他签署该项国际合同。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the institutional mechanisms of selecting, authorizing, and designating individuals for public offices, official committees, military ranks, or administrative posts through formal ballots or executive decree.
groups.summary_zh: 通过投票表决或行政委任赋予个体特定公职、军阶或法定权力。
groups.desc_en: Covers the formal procedural vesting of authority, office, or status in an individual, contrasting with mere hiring or choosing through its institutional legitimation.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过既定程序授予个体公职、权力或法定身份，与普通“雇佣/挑选”相比，具有体制化的程序性与合法性授权特征。
groups.nuance_en: elect: selection by collective balloting (president / official / council) · appoint: unilateral designation by executive authority (judge / committee / envoy) · nominate: formal proposal as candidate (candidate / successor / justice) · commission: formal conferral of rank or creative mandate (officer / artist / inquiry) · swear in: ceremonial induction into office (governor / president / witness)
groups.nuance_zh: elect: 民主投票选举 (president / official / council) · appoint: 行政任命或委任 (judge / committee / envoy) · nominate: 提名候选人 (candidate / successor / justice) · commission: 正式授予军衔或委托专项创作 (officer / artist / inquiry) · swear in: 宣誓就职仪式 (governor / president / witness)

groups.name: Emit Intermittent or Reflected Light · 闪烁与闪光 (Flash, Sparkle, Gleam)
groups.tip: 忽明忽暗的短促光亮

items.def_en: to shine faintly with a soft, wavering, or unsteady light
items.ex_en: Distantly through the dense coastal mist, lonely lighthouse lanterns glimmered across dark waters.
items.ex_zh: 透过浓密的沿海迷雾，远处孤单灯塔的微光在漆黑的水面上隐约闪烁。

items.def_en: (+ sth) emit or transmit bright rays of light in a specific direction
items.ex_en: The powerful automated lighthouse began to beam out strong white signals across waves.
items.ex_zh: 功能强大的自动化灯塔开始向翻涌的海浪发出强烈的白色光束信号。

items.def_en: to shine with an unsteady or wavering light that goes on and off rapidly
items.ex_en: The dying campfire flickered gently in the cold night breeze before going out.
items.ex_zh: 即将熄灭的营火在寒冷的夜风中微微闪烁，随后彻底熄灭。

items.def_zh: 闪烁，微光闪现；（眼睛等因情绪而）发亮
items.def_en: 1. To shine with a soft or gentle light. 2. (of eyes) To show a particular feeling or emotion brightly.
items.ex_en: Polished silver cutlery gleamed under the warm crystal chandeliers during the formal banquet.
items.ex_zh: 在正式宴会上，擦拭得发亮的银质餐具在温暖的水晶吊灯下熠熠生辉。

items.def_en: to give out or reflect small, bright flashes of light momentarily
items.ex_en: The bright morning sunlight glinted sharply off the surface of the calm lake.
items.ex_zh: 明媚的晨光在平静的湖面上反射出点点耀眼的微光。

items.def_en: suddenly emit a brief burst of bright or flickering light
items.ex_en: The dry firewood flared up suddenly when dry kindling caught the hot spark.
items.ex_zh: 当干燥的引火柴接住炙热的火花时，干木柴猛然腾起刺眼的火光。

items.def_en: 1. To shine, or make something shine, suddenly and brightly for a short time. 2. To move, pass, or appear very quickly.
items.ex_en: Bright lightning flashed across the midnight sky, illuminating the quiet landscape beneath momentarily.
items.ex_zh: 明亮的闪电划过午夜的夜空，刹那间照亮了下方沉寂的大地景致。
items.ex2_en: The observant driver flashed his headlights to warn approaching traffic of danger.
items.ex2_zh: 细心的司机闪烁车灯，以提醒对向车辆注意危险。

items.def_zh: 闪耀，闪烁；焕发活力，才华横溢
items.def_en: 1. To shine brightly with many small flashes of light. 2. To be lively, witty, or full of enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: The clear morning dew began to sparkle brightly on the fresh green leaves.
items.ex_zh: 清晨清澈的露珠在鲜绿的叶片上开始闪闪发光。

items.def_zh: 像灯塔般发光照亮；照亮指引
items.def_en: To shine brightly like a beacon; to illuminate or guide as with a beacon.
items.ex_en: The lighthouse beaconed brightly across the dark, turbulent waters to guide lost ships.
items.ex_zh: 灯塔在黑暗汹涌的水面上熠熠生辉，为迷失的船只指引方向。

items.def_en: to shine brightly with many small points of flashing light
items.ex_en: Her diamond necklace glittered brightly under the brilliant lights of the grand ballroom.
items.ex_zh: 她的钻石项链在豪华宴会厅明亮的灯光下闪闪生辉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe sources or surfaces emitting brief bursts of intense light, flickering rapidly, or softly reflecting luminescence.
groups.summary_zh: 光度不恒定地闪现、微弱反光或明亮短促地发光。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to transient, unsteady, or reflected visual luminance, distinguished from steady 'shining' by fluctuation in frequency, origin, or optical sharpness.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘不稳定、断续或反射性的光芒释放，与恒定“照耀(shine)”相比，侧重光线的跳动频率、反射质感或突发性闪烁。
groups.nuance_en: flicker: wavering, unsteady luminescence (candle / shadow / screen) · gleam: steady subdued glow from polished surfaces (teeth / polished wood / eye) · glint: brief, hard flash of reflected light (dagger / coin / spectacle) · sparkle: lively dispersion of multiple bright points (diamond / jewel / wine) · flash: sudden, brief burst of intense radiance (lightning / camera / signal)
groups.nuance_zh: flicker: 微弱摇曳不定的闪烁 (candle / shadow / screen) · gleam: 抛光表面泛出的柔和反光 (teeth / polished wood / eye) · glint: 硬质反光体瞬现的尖锐微光 (dagger / coin / spectacle) · sparkle: 多角度晶莹闪烁或迸发星光 (diamond / jewel / wine) · flash: 突发性强光一闪 (lightning / camera / signal)

groups.name: Encroach & Infringe · 蚕食与越界侵犯 (Encroach, Impinge, Trespass)
groups.tip: 步步渗透侵犯界限权益

items.def_zh: 悄悄潜入，慢慢挤进（他人领域）
items.def_en: (+ on sb/sth) to advance or encroach gradually and cautiously into another's space or domain
items.ex_en: The new manager attempted to edge in on her colleague's prestigious client portfolio.
items.ex_zh: 新经理企图悄悄蚕食同事手头优质的客户资源。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) to intrude or encroach uninvited upon something belonging to or involving others
items.ex_en: He had no right to horn in on their private conversation without invitation.
items.ex_zh: 他毫无权利未经邀请就硬插手他们的私下谈话。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on/upon) to advance beyond the usual limit and restrict or violate someone's rights
items.ex_en: The proposed security surveillance laws directly infringe on fundamental civil liberties of citizens.
items.ex_zh: 拟议的安全监控法案直接侵犯了公民的基本自由。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to enter land without permission, or unlawfully intrude upon rights
items.ex_en: Hikers must be careful not to trespass on private property in the countryside.
items.ex_zh: 徒步旅行者必须小心，不要在乡间非法闯入私人领地。

items.def_en: (+ on/into/upon) to enter a place or situation uninvited where one is unwelcome
items.ex_en: Paparazzi constantly intrude upon the private lives of prominent political figures and celebrities.
items.ex_zh: 狗仔队不断强行介入知名政治人物和名流的私生活。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To gradually take over someone else's territory, rights, time, or privacy.
items.ex_en: Commercial real estate developers continue to encroach upon the protected wetland nature reserve.
items.ex_zh: 商业地产开发商继续蚕食受保护的湿地自然保护区。

items.def_zh: 侵害，侵犯；产生不利影响
items.def_en: (+ on/upon) (formal) To interfere with or limit someone's rights or freedoms, or to have a noticeable negative effect on something.
items.ex_en: The stringent curfew will inevitably impinge upon the ordinary freedoms of local citizens.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的宵禁将不可避免地侵害当地公民的正常自由。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon/into) (formal) To force yourself, your opinions, or something unwelcome on someone without being invited.
items.ex_en: He hesitated to obtrude his personal opinions upon the somber grieving family members.
items.ex_zh: 他犹豫着不愿将个人观点强加于悲伤肃穆的家属身上。

items.def_en: (+ on sb/sth) to involve oneself aggressively or intrusively in someone else's affairs or territory
items.ex_en: Rival gangs attempted to muscle in on the lucrative downtown entertainment district quickly.
items.ex_zh: 敌对帮派企图迅速蛮横插足利润丰厚的市中心娱乐区。

items.def_zh: 侵占；越界偷猎（客户、资源）
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on) to encroach on another's territory or rights to take resources illicitly
items.ex_en: A rival tech startup tried to poach top clients from our sales team.
items.ex_zh: 一家竞争对手初创公司试图从我们销售团队手中抢夺顶级客户。

groups.summary_en: An agent, rule, or expanding influence gradually, surreptitiously, or intrusively crosses into someone else's territory, privacy, rights, or autonomy. Typically patterns with prepositions like 'on' or 'upon'.
groups.summary_zh: 以渐进、逾矩或强加的方式侵犯他人的领地、权利、时间或界限。
groups.desc_en: Involves gradually, stealthily, or forcefully crossing physical, legal, or normative boundaries into another's domain, contrasting with overt 'invading' by its incremental or rights-violating nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指循序渐进、隐蔽或越界侵入他人的物理界限、权益或私人领地，与全面“侵略”相比，侧重渐进蚕食或法理越权。
groups.nuance_en: encroach: gradual creeping advance beyond legitimate limits (sea / suburb / power) · infringe: legal violation of established rights or rules (copyright / patent / liberty) · trespass: unlawful physical entry onto private land (land / property / boundary) · impinge: disruptive impact or interference on another's sphere (autonomy / privacy / freedom) · intrude: unwelcome physical or social thrusting of oneself (privacy / conversation / room)
groups.nuance_zh: encroach: 步步蚕食或渐进侵占 (sea / suburb / power) · infringe: 法律意义上的侵权或违例 (copyright / patent / liberty) · trespass: 非法侵入私人领地 (land / property / boundary) · impinge: 冲击并妨碍他人权益 (autonomy / privacy / freedom) · intrude: 冒昧闯入或硬性插足 (privacy / conversation / room)

groups.name: Engender & Summon Into Being · 孕育与唤出 (Beget, Conjure, Spawn)
groups.tip: 从无到有，催生新生命或事物

items.def_en: to cause something to develop or accumulate over time (e.g. discontent)
items.ex_en: Widespread government corruption will inevitably breed intense public resentment and social unrest.
items.ex_zh: 广泛的政府腐败必然会孕育强烈的民愤与社会动荡。
items.ex2_en: Bitter resentment began to breed silently within the neglected urban community.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的怨恨情绪开始在被忽视的城市社区中悄然滋生。

items.def_zh: 凭空变出，变戏法般唤出
items.def_en: (+ sth) to create, bring into existence, or make something appear as if by magic
items.ex_en: The talented chef managed to conjure up an exquisite feast from basic ingredients.
items.ex_zh: 这位才华横溢的大厨设法用基础食材凭空变出一桌精致盛宴。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cause something to come into being, occur, or be produced
items.ex_en: The charismatic leader's passionate speech called forth great courage from the weary soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有魅力的领袖发表的热情演讲唤起了疲惫士兵的巨大勇气。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to invent or concoct something unusual, creative, or fanciful
items.ex_en: They managed to dream up an ingenious marketing strategy for the new gadget.
items.ex_zh: 他们为这款新设备凭空想出了一个绝妙的营销策略。

items.def_en: to produce offspring in large numbers or generate widespread outcomes rapidly
items.ex_en: The sudden viral video spawned thousands of creative imitations across social media platforms.
items.ex_zh: 这段意外走红的视频在社交媒体平台上引发了成千上万的创意模仿。

items.def_en: to call forth an image, spirit, or emotional reaction through words or ritual
items.ex_en: The ancient ballad invokes deep feelings of nostalgia among the elderly village residents.
items.ex_zh: 这首古老的民谣唤起了村里长者内心深处的怀旧情怀。

items.def_zh: 变出，神奇般地创造出（常后接 up）；用魔法变出；令人联想起
items.def_en: 1. (often + up) To make something appear or create something as if by magic. 2. To evoke or bring an image or feeling to mind. 3. To perform magic tricks.
items.ex_en: The magician managed to conjure white doves out of an apparently empty wooden box.
items.ex_zh: 魔术师竟从一个看似空无一物的木盒里神奇地变出了白鸽。

items.def_zh: （材料学中）生成晶须，长出须状结晶
items.def_en: To form or grow microscopic hair-like crystal filaments on a material.
items.ex_en: Under intense stress, the pure tin coating began to whisker inside the electronics.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大应力下，电子元件内部的纯锡镀层开始长出晶须。

items.def_en: to cause or give rise to a feeling, situation, or condition
items.ex_en: The ambiguous contract clause engendered profound mistrust between the two negotiating corporate partners.
items.ex_zh: 含糊不清的合同条款在两个谈判合作方之间引起了极大的不信任。

items.def_zh: 导致，引起；成为……的父亲，生育
items.def_en: 1. (formal or literary) To cause something to happen or exist. 2. (archaic) To father a child.
items.ex_en: Violent oppression will always beget bitter resentment among the subjugated population.
items.ex_zh: 暴虐的压迫必将在受征服的人民心中催生刺骨的怨恨。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate generating, fathering, or bringing complex outcomes or entities into existence seemingly out of nothing or by procreation/causation. 'Beget' carries an archaic/biblical lineage tone, whereas 'conjure' implies magical or mental evocation.
groups.summary_zh: 指催生、繁衍或仿佛凭空召唤出某物或某种后果。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the mystical, mental, or biological generation of entities or consequences, distinguishing itself from deliberate 'creating' through elements of proliferation, magic, or unintended progeny.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过心理构想、神秘召唤或繁衍使事物降生/显现，与普通“创造”相比，带有魔法降现、滋生繁衍或无心催生的意味。
groups.nuance_en: spawn: prolific or sudden generation of multiple offspring/effects (movement / industry / panic) · breed: biological propagation or systematic cultivation of traits (discontent / familiarity / cattle) · conjure up: evoking vividly through imagination or magic (memory / image / spirit) · invoke: calling upon an authority or spirit for aid/validation (spirit / deity / law) · call forth: eliciting a latent reaction or dormant power (response / emotion / energy)
groups.nuance_zh: spawn: 大量催生或迅速繁殖派生 (movement / industry / panic) · breed: 繁衍培育或孕育不良后果 (discontent / familiarity / cattle) · conjure up: 施法召唤或凭空唤起想象 (memory / image / spirit) · invoke: 祈请神灵庇佑或援引权威依据 (spirit / deity / law) · call forth: 唤醒内在潜能或引发响应 (response / emotion / energy)

groups.name: Enrich & Enhance · 丰富与赋能 (Enrich, Spice, Optimise)
groups.tip: 提升品质使其更具价值

items.def_zh: 使更有活力，使更花哨出彩
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make something more lively, colorful, or exciting
items.ex_en: Bright throw pillows can easily jazz up a bland and boring living room.
items.ex_zh: 鲜艳的抱枕可以轻易让平淡无奇的客厅显得更有活力。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to add excitement, interest, or piquancy to something
items.ex_en: They decided to spice up their dull weekend routine with an impromptu road trip.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定通过一场说走就走的公路旅行，给枯燥的周末增添趣味。

items.def_en: to add salt, herbs, or zest to bring out flavor and character
items.ex_en: The chef carefully seasoned the braised lamb shank with fresh rosemary and sea salt.
items.ex_zh: 厨师用新鲜迷迭香和海盐精心为炖羊小腿调味。

items.def_zh: 给……增添趣味，使更精彩；在……中加香料
items.def_en: (also 'spice up') To make a talk, event, or relationship more interesting, lively, or exciting.
items.ex_en: The keynote speaker spiced his presentation with humorous anecdotes about his early career failures.
items.ex_zh: 主讲人分享了早年职业挫折的幽默轶事，为演讲增添了趣味。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make something stronger, more substantial, or more effective by adding resources or substance
items.ex_en: The security company hired extra guards to beef up airport defenses before holidays.
items.ex_zh: 安保公司在节前增派警卫，以切实加强机场防御力量。

items.def_en: to increase or further improve the good quality, value, or strength of something
items.ex_en: The new software update will significantly enhance the overall processing speed and system security.
items.ex_zh: 新的软件更新将显著提升系统的整体运行速度与安全性。

items.def_zh: 充实，丰富；改善，提高（品质）；使富裕
items.def_en: 1. To improve the quality, depth, or value of something by adding good elements to it. 2. To make someone wealthy.
items.ex_en: Studying classic literature will greatly enrich your understanding of different human cultures and values.
items.ex_zh: 研读古典文学将极大地丰富你对不同人类文化与价值观的理解。

items.def_zh: 加固；充实；添加营养成分
items.def_en: to make something stronger or more effective by adding nutrients or support
items.ex_en: The manufacturer fortifies its breakfast cereals with essential vitamins to boost nutritional value.
items.ex_zh: 该制造商在早餐麦片中添加必需维生素，以增强其营养价值。

items.def_zh: （使地区）中产阶层化，改善改造（gentrify的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of gentrify: upgraded and renovated an area to make it suitable for middle-class people.
items.ex_en: Wealthy investors quickly gentrified the historic warehouse district into trendy upscale apartment complexes.
items.ex_zh: 富有的投资者迅速对历史悠久的仓储区进行中产阶层化改造，建成了高档公寓群。

items.def_zh: 使最优化，使尽可能有效（optimize的英式拼写）
items.def_en: (British English) To make something as good, efficient, or effective as possible.
items.ex_en: Engineers analysed the industrial workflow carefully to optimise overall factory productivity and resource efficiency.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们仔细分析了工业流程，以使工厂的整体生产力和资源利用率最优化。

groups.summary_en: These verbs denote upgrading the quality, flavor, social status, or functioning of a system or resource by adding potent elements or systematically refining components. Nuances range from culinary zest to systemic fine-tuning and socioeconomic upgrading.
groups.summary_zh: 通过增添精粹成分、优化机制或改良结构来提高质量或档次。
groups.desc_en: Depicts adding complementary qualities, substance, or vibrancy to an existing substrate, contrasting with raw 'improving' by focusing on sensory zest, nutritional depth, or systemic fortification.
groups.desc_zh: 指向既有主体添加成分、风味或能量以提升其品质，与普通“改良”相比，侧重风味增色、养分富集或结构性补强。
groups.nuance_en: enrich: adding nutritional, cultural, or intellectual value (soil / vocabulary / life) · enhance: augmenting attractiveness, quality, or functionality (reputation / performance / flavor) · spice up: adding pungent excitement or variety (presentation / relationship / party) · beef up: reinforcing strength, substance, or numbers (security / army / proposal) · fortify: strengthening defensively or nutritionally (city / food / resolve)
groups.nuance_zh: enrich: 充实内涵、滋养或使丰富 (soil / vocabulary / life) · enhance: 增进功能、提升吸引力或表现 (reputation / performance / flavor) · spice up: 增添趣味、刺激或活力 (presentation / relationship / party) · beef up: 充实人力、加固力量或内容 (security / army / proposal) · fortify: 构筑工事防守或强化营养 (city / food / resolve)

groups.name: Entrap & Seize Prey · 设伏猎获与捕套 (Snare, Harpoon, Ensnare)
groups.tip: 利用器械设伏擒获猎物

items.def_en: to capture an animal, fish, or fugitive using a mesh net or coordinated sweep
items.ex_en: The local police managed to net the escaped convict after a massive coordinated manhunt.
items.ex_zh: 经过大规模协同搜捕，当地警方终于抓获了这名逃犯。

items.def_en: to catch an animal or quarry in a mechanical enclosure or deceptive contrivance
items.ex_en: The wildlife ranger used a humane cage to trap the injured wild coyote safely.
items.ex_zh: 野生动物巡逻员用人道陷阱笼安全地捕获了那只受伤的野郊狼。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to catch with a lasso, or persuade/entrap someone into participating in a scheme
items.ex_en: My persuasive neighbor tried to rope me in to organize the neighborhood block party.
items.ex_zh: 我那能说会道的邻居试图拉我入局，一起组织社区街区派对。

items.def_zh: 困住，使陷于重围动弹不得
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround and trap someone or something so that escape or free movement is impossible
items.ex_en: My car was boxed in by two huge delivery trucks, and I couldn't pull out.
items.ex_zh: 我的车被两辆大卡车死死卡在中间，根本开不出来。

items.def_zh: 收线拉上（猎物），诱捕抓获
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to pull in a captured fish or animal on a line, or effectively trap and capture someone
items.ex_en: The experienced angler fought hard to reel in the massive bluefin marlin successfully.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的钓手奋力收线，成功把巨大的蓝枪鱼拉了上来。

items.def_zh: 重新捕获，收复，夺回；重现，再体验
items.def_en: to capture a person, animal, or territory again after losing control; to experience or bring back a past feeling or memory.
items.ex_en: The dedicated police task force successfully recaptured the fugitive near the northern border.
items.ex_zh: 专案警察小队在北部边境附近成功重新捕获了那名逃犯。

items.def_zh: 用罗网（或陷阱）捕捉；诱捕，使落入圈套
items.def_en: to catch an animal in a snare or trap; to trick or trap someone into a difficult situation.
items.ex_en: The cunning poacher set wire loops to snare wild rabbits in the dense forest.
items.ex_zh: 狡猾的盗猎者在茂密的森林中设置钢丝圈套诱捕野兔。

items.def_en: to catch or hold an animal or target fast in a net, cords, or complex obstacle
items.ex_en: The discarded plastic fishing net tragically entangled several endangered sea turtles near the shore.
items.ex_zh: 遗弃在海岸附近的塑料渔网不幸缠住了几只濒危海龟。

items.def_en: to strike, spear, or catch a whale or large fish with a harpoon.
items.ex_en: Early whalers used heavy iron spears to harpoon massive whales in frigid waters.
items.ex_zh: 早期的捕鲸人在寒冷的水域中使用沉重的铁矛来叉捕巨鲸。

items.def_zh: 诱捕，用陷阱捕捉；使落入圈套
items.def_en: to catch an animal in a trap; to trick or entangle someone in an unpleasant or dangerous situation.
items.ex_en: The spider spun an intricate web designed to ensnare unsuspecting insects in the dark.
items.ex_zh: 蜘蛛织成了一张错综复杂的网，专为在暗中捕获毫无防备的昆虫。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scenario frame detail the mechanical or tactical trapping, spearing, and capture of animals or human targets through devices or calculated ambushes. They range from using specialized physical gear (snares, harpoons) to retaking an escaped target or catching someone metaphorically in a trap.
groups.summary_zh: 使用陷阱、器械或战术圈套捕获、猎杀或重新缉捕目标。
groups.desc_en: Constitutes confining or capturing targets through deceptive devices, cordons, or snares, distinct from direct physical 'catching' by reliance on traps, lines, or strategic cornering.
groups.desc_zh: 指借助器械陷阱、圈套或策略性合围捕获猎物或对手，与直接“抓住”相比，强调机械机关、设局围困或缠绕致擒。
groups.nuance_en: snare: catching with a loop trap or treacherous scheme (rabbit / bird / victim) · net: capturing with a woven mesh or securing wide gains (fish / criminal / profit) · trap: confining securely within an unavoidable enclosure (prey / animal / miner) · entangle: incapacitating by snarls, loops, or complex ties (feet / wire / alliance) · reel in: drawing in captured quarry via a line or systematic effort (fish / investor / client)
groups.nuance_zh: snare: 设套捕获或诱入圈套 (rabbit / bird / victim) · net: 张网网罗或一网打尽 (fish / criminal / profit) · trap: 设陷阱诱捕或困于绝境 (prey / animal / miner) · entangle: 缠绕使丧失行动力或卷入复杂纠葛 (feet / wire / alliance) · reel in: 收线拉近猎物或逐步争取到手 (fish / investor / client)

groups.name: Establish & Institutionalize · 确立与制度化 (Institute, Codify, Enshrine)
groups.tip: 创立制度并载入法典奉为规范

items.def_zh: 设立；制定实行（规则、体系或调查）
items.def_en: to officially introduce, set up, or initiate a system, law, or process
items.ex_en: The hospital board resolved to institute strict new sanitation guidelines for all operating theaters.
items.ex_zh: 医院董事会决定为所有手术室制定并推行严格的新卫生准则。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to formally establish, institute, or organize a system, company, or set of rules
items.ex_en: The government aims to set up a new regulatory body for artificial intelligence oversight.
items.ex_zh: 政府旨在设立一个新的监管机构，以负责人工智能的监督工作。
items.ex2_en: A spontaneous demonstration set up outside city hall as anger mounted rapidly.
items.ex2_zh: 随着愤怒迅速升温，市政厅外自发形成了一场抗议示威。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to introduce or establish a new law, policy, or system officially
items.ex_en: Parliament voted decisively to bring in tough new environmental protection legislation this year.
items.ex_zh: 议会果断投票决定在今年出台严厉的新环保法规。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to establish or implement a system, rule, or mechanism so that it operates
items.ex_en: The administration put in place comprehensive emergency procedures before the severe storm hit.
items.ex_zh: 在强风暴来袭之前，政府落实了一套完备的应急处置程序。

items.def_zh: 牢固确立；使（权利或地位）难以撼动
items.def_en: to firmly establish something, especially a right or attitude, so that change is very difficult
items.ex_en: The constitutional reform serves to entrench equal voting rights firmly for every single citizen.
items.ex_zh: 这项宪法改革旨在牢固确立每位公民平等的投票权，使之不可动摇。

items.def_zh: 重新确立，重新施行（法律、制度等）；重新引入（物种、产品等）
items.def_en: 1. To bring a law, product, or animal species back into use or its former habitat.
items.ex_en: Conservationists worked tirelessly to reintroduce native river otters into their historical wetland habitats.
items.ex_zh: 环保人士不知疲倦地工作，将本土水獭重新引入其历史湿地栖息地。

items.def_zh: 使制度化；确立为常规体制
items.def_en: to make a practice, value, or convention standard and established within an institution or society
items.ex_en: The university sought to institutionalize collaborative interdisciplinary research programs across all scientific departments.
items.ex_zh: 该大学力求在所有科学系所中将跨学科合作研究项目制度化。

items.def_zh: 庄严载入（法律或宪法等），奉为神圣；把……置于神龛内供奉
items.def_en: 1. (+ in) To preserve a right, principle, or tradition in a law or constitution, or keep something sacred in a shrine.
items.ex_en: The nation's foundational constitution enshrines universal freedom of speech as an inalienable right.
items.ex_zh: 该国的根本宪法将普遍的言论自由庄严载入条文，作为一项不可剥夺的权利。

items.def_zh: 编纂（法典）；使（规则或惯例）成文法典化
items.def_en: to arrange laws, rules, or principles into a systematic written code
items.ex_en: Legal scholars worked for decades to codify ancient customary laws into modern statutes.
items.ex_zh: 法学学者们耗费数十载，将古老的习惯法编纂成现代成文法规。

items.def_zh: 使正式化，以制度形式确立；拘泥于形式
items.def_en: 1. To make a plan, agreement, or relationship official, structured, and legally recognized.
items.ex_en: Both nations agreed to formalize their long diplomatic alliance through a comprehensive bilateral treaty.
items.ex_zh: 两国同意通过一项全面的双边条约，将其长期的外交同盟关系正式化。

groups.summary_en: Authorities or governing bodies officially implement policies, laws, or traditions into an enduring, legally binding, or standardized system. Verbs range from general procedural formalization to deeply safeguarding core principles in constitutional law.
groups.summary_zh: 官方或权威机构将规则、惯例或原则正式确立并载入体制或法律。
groups.desc_en: Covers cementing laws, practices, or bodies into permanent societal fabric, differing from initial 'founding' by embedding into enduring legal or cultural architecture.
groups.desc_zh: 将法律、规程或组织固定并内嵌于社会长期结构中，与最初的“创立”相比，强调规范化、法定化与制度性固化。
