groups.nuance_en: institute: formally initiating and establishing a policy or system (reform / inquiry / proceeding) · institutionalize: embedding an ethos or rule into systemic culture (practice / behavior / corruption) · enshrine: securing a right or value as sacred and inviolable (right / principle / freedom) · entrench: deeply rooting an attitude or privilege against change (habit / privilege / power) · codify: compiling unwritten customs into formal statutes (law / rule / principle)
groups.nuance_zh: institute: 确立制度或正式启动程序 (reform / inquiry / proceeding) · institutionalize: 使习惯或规约体制化/内生化 (practice / behavior / corruption) · enshrine: 将原则或权利奉为神圣法令予以铭刻 (right / principle / freedom) · entrench: 使特权或观念根深蒂固难以撼动 (habit / privilege / power) · codify: 将惯例法典化或体系化编纂 (law / rule / principle)

groups.name: Exceed & Surpass · 超越与胜过 (Surpass, Exceed, Outstrip)
groups.tip: 在数量、速度或权重上胜过他人

items.def_en: to be greater in number, degree, or extent than an established limit or quantity
items.ex_en: Vehicle exhaust emissions must never exceed the strict limits permitted by municipal environmental regulations.
items.ex_zh: 车辆尾气排放绝不能超出市政环保法规所允许的严格限度。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to exceed an expected limit, scope, or normal degree of something
items.ex_en: His exceptional dedication and selflessness clearly go beyond the normal duties of his job.
items.ex_zh: 他非凡的奉献精神和无私品质显然超越了他本职工作的普通要求。

items.def_zh: 超时；超过（预定数量或限制）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to go beyond an allotted limit, budget, or timeframe
items.ex_en: The keynote address was so engaging that it ran over the allotted time slot.
items.ex_zh: 主旨演讲非常引人入胜，以至于超出了预定分配的时间。

items.def_zh: 超过，超越（在品质或成就上）
items.def_en: to be greater, better, or stronger than another in capability or achievement
items.ex_en: Her innovative research outputs far surpass the modest academic goals originally anticipated by faculty.
items.ex_zh: 她的创新研究成果远远超过了院系最初预期的谦逊学术目标。

items.def_en: (formal or archaic) to go beyond or surpass someone or something
items.ex_en: The artist's astonishing creative vision seemed to outgo all established conventions of his era.
items.ex_zh: 这位艺术家的惊人创作视野似乎超越了他所处时代的所有既定惯例。

items.def_zh: （在重量、重要性或价值上）超过，重于
items.def_en: to be greater or more important than something else
items.ex_en: The substantial long-term economic advantages will clearly outweigh the minimal initial setup costs.
items.ex_zh: 可观的长期经济效益显然会超过微不足道的初期启动成本。

items.def_zh: 超过，赶超（跑得更快或发展更迅猛）
items.def_en: to become much more successful, faster, or greater in quantity than a competitor
items.ex_en: Demand for clean renewable energy will soon outstrip the current capacity of traditional grids.
items.ex_zh: 对清洁可再生能源的需求很快将超过传统电网目前的承载能力。

items.def_zh: 使承担过多任务（或债务）；过度扩展，使延伸过长
items.def_en: to take on more work, debt, or responsibility than one can handle; to extend something too far
items.ex_en: The regional developer overextended its finances by starting multiple luxury hotel projects simultaneously.
items.ex_zh: 该区域开发商因同时启动多个豪华酒店项目而使其财务过度扩张。

items.def_en: to be sold in greater quantities than something else
items.ex_en: The author's latest thrilling mystery novel quickly outsold every other book on the shelf.
items.ex_zh: 这位作家最新的惊悚推理小说销量迅速超过了书架上的所有其他书籍。

items.def_zh: 超出，越过（overshoot 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: past tense and past participle of overshoot; to have gone beyond a target, limit, or intended destination
items.ex_en: The speeding passenger train overshot the designated platform stop by nearly one hundred meters.
items.ex_zh: 超速行驶的客运列车冲过了指定的站台停车点近一百米。

groups.summary_en: A subject goes beyond another entity or standard in extent, speed, quantity, or competitive performance. Verbs range from general quantitative excess to domain-specific superiority such as commercial sales or physical range.
groups.summary_zh: 在数量、尺度、表现或商业效益上超过对比目标。
groups.desc_en: Marks surpassing defined boundaries, standards, or rivals along a continuum, diverging from neutral 'passing' through comparative superiority or quantitative overshoot.
groups.desc_zh: 指在量级、质量或竞争中超越预设限度或竞争对手，与中性“经过/超过”相比，侧重量化超限、性能压倒或胜过同侪。
groups.nuance_en: exceed: crossing an explicit quantitative limit or mandate (speed limit / quota / authority) · surpass: excelling above rivals or benchmarks in excellence (expectation / record / predecessor) · outstrip: moving faster and leaving behind in race or growth (competitor / demand / capacity) · outweigh: prevailing over another in importance or substance (benefit / cost / risk) · overextend: stretching resources or commitments beyond safe limits (army / resource / credit)
groups.nuance_zh: exceed: 超越法定/设定的数值界限 (speed limit / quota / authority) · surpass: 在品质、成就或预期上优于对照物 (expectation / record / predecessor) · outstrip: 发展速度或规模甩开对手 (competitor / demand / capacity) · outweigh: 份量、重要性压倒另一方 (benefit / cost / risk) · overextend: 战线拉得过长或资源透支过度 (army / resource / credit)

groups.name: Exclamations & Emotional Vocal Outcries · 欢呼与情态呼喊 (Whoop, Howl, Ooh)
groups.tip: 兴奋欢呼或高声大喊宣泄情绪

items.def_zh: 尖声插话，突然发声嚷嚷
items.def_en: to suddenly start speaking or shouting, often in a high-pitched or shrill voice
items.ex_en: The timid student suddenly piped up with an insightful answer during the tense debate.
items.ex_zh: 在紧张的辩论中，那个胆怯的学生突然尖声说出了一个富有见解的答案。

items.def_zh: 发出“哦”的惊叹声，发出赞叹声
items.def_en: To make a long 'ooh' sound to express wonder, pleasure, surprise, or admiration.
items.ex_en: Spectators began to ooh and cheer as the dazzling fireworks lit the night sky.
items.ex_zh: 当耀眼的烟花照亮夜空时，观众们开始发出阵阵惊叹并欢呼起来。

items.def_en: to shout or speak loudly to attract attention or express an emotional outcry
items.ex_en: The trapped miner desperately called out for help in the dark, collapsed shaft tunnel.
items.ex_zh: 被困的矿工在黑暗坍塌的矿井巷道里绝望地高声呼救。

items.def_en: to shout approval, praise, or encouragement warmly and loudly
items.ex_en: The enthusiastic crowd began to cheer loudly as the marathon runners crossed the finish line.
items.ex_zh: 当马拉松选手冲过终点线时，热情的观众开始大声欢呼喝彩。

items.def_en: to give a loud, informal, full-throated shout or call
items.ex_en: Dad stepped out onto the porch to holler at the kids to come inside.
items.ex_zh: 爸爸走到门廊上，扯着嗓子喊孩子们赶紧进屋。

items.def_en: to make a sudden, loud sound or shout due to pain, fright, or strong emotion
items.ex_en: The injured hiker could only cry out in agony when he twisted his swollen ankle.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的徒步者扭伤了肿胀的脚踝，疼得忍不住失声痛叫。

items.def_zh: 高声欢呼，兴奋大叫；欢呼着说出
items.def_en: To shout loudly and excitedly with joy, triumph, or enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: The fans began to whoop wildly when their underdog team scored the winning goal.
items.ex_zh: 当弱旅球队踢进决胜球时，球迷们兴奋得高声欢呼大叫起来。

items.def_zh: 长嚎，狂吠；咆哮，大声哭喊；呼啸
items.def_en: To make a long, loud, mournful sound like a wolf or dog; to cry, shout, or laugh loudly.
items.ex_en: The winter gale seemed to howl through the narrow mountain pass all night long.
items.ex_zh: 整整一夜，冬日的狂风似乎都在狭窄的山口中呼啸咆哮。

items.def_en: to produce a prolonged, high-pitched vocal cry of grief, fear, or pain
items.ex_en: The grief-stricken mother began to wail inconsolably beside the damaged wreckage of the car.
items.ex_zh: 悲痛欲绝的母亲在损毁的车旁凄声哀号，无法自抑。

items.def_en: to emit a deep, loud, roaring shout typical of extreme rage or distress
items.ex_en: The furious drill sergeant began to bellow orders at the recruits across the field.
items.ex_zh: 狂怒的教官隔着操场如雷般咆哮着，向新兵们发出命令。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on non-verbalized or interjectional outcries expressing intense emotional states like delight, surprise, mockery, or physical anguish.
groups.summary_zh: 指表达惊叹、欢呼狂喜、痛楚或起哄等情绪的特异拟声呼喊。
groups.desc_en: Involves uttering sudden, uninhibited vocalizations driven by visceral joy, alarm, or excitement, differing from articulate 'shouting' by raw emotional inflection.
groups.desc_zh: 由狂喜、惊愕或亢奋引发的本能情态呼喊，与常规“喊叫”相比，侧重声音的情绪喷发、粗粝质感或非词义叫嚣。
groups.nuance_en: whoop: sudden high-pitched cry of triumphant joy (crowd / victor / fan) · cheer: unified vocal outburst of public acclaim (crowd / audience / spectator) · howl: prolonged wailing cry of anguish, wind, or mirth (mob / dog / grief) · holler: loud vernacular shout to summon or complain (boy / worker / driver) · pipe up: unexpectedly speaking or crying out in a thin voice (child / critic / dissenter)
groups.nuance_zh: whoop: 欢呼雀跃的高声欢叫 (crowd / victor / fan) · cheer: 齐声喝彩与声援欢呼 (crowd / audience / spectator) · howl: 痛苦长嚎或哄堂大笑 (mob / dog / grief) · holler: 粗声粗气的呼喊或抱怨 (boy / worker / driver) · pipe up: 尖声突兀地开口说话 (child / critic / dissenter)

groups.name: Exhilarate & Elate · 振奋与欢欣 (Uplift & Exhilarate)
groups.tip: 精神抖擞重新焕发活力

items.def_en: (+ sb) to make or become more cheerful, positive, and full of spirits
items.ex_en: A bouquet of fresh flowers and some chocolate helped to cheer up the sick patient.
items.ex_zh: 一束鲜花和一些巧克力让生病的患者精神振作、高兴了起来。
items.ex2_en: Her mood visibly cheered up after receiving encouraging words from her mentor.
items.ex2_zh: 在得到导师的鼓励后，她的心情明显振作了起来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to become or make someone more lively, cheerful, or energetic
items.ex_en: A hot cup of strong black coffee helped the exhausted driver perk up quickly.
items.ex_zh: 一杯热腾腾的浓黑咖啡让筋疲力尽的司机很快打起了精神。
items.ex2_en: The cheerful morning greeting perked up everyone in the gloomy office.
items.ex2_zh: 欢快的早晨问候让阴沉沉的办公室里的每个人都振作了精神。

items.def_en: to give comfort, hope, or lighthearted happiness to someone
items.ex_en: The unexpected arrival of old friends helped cheer her through the long, dreary winter.
items.ex_zh: 老朋友们的意外造访，给她在漫长沉闷的冬日里带来了安慰与欢欣。

items.def_zh: （使）振作起来，（使）精神抖擞；竖起
items.def_en: (also 'perk up') To become or make someone more cheerful, lively, or energetic after feeling tired or sad.
items.ex_en: After taking a quick nap, the tired puppy began to perk visibly and play.
items.ex_zh: 小睡片刻后，疲倦的小狗明显精神抖擞起来，开始玩耍。
items.ex2_en: The refreshing morning breeze perked the exhausted runners after the race.
items.ex2_zh: 清爽的晨风让赛后筋疲力尽的跑步者们恢复了活力。

items.def_en: to fill someone with renewed physical or mental energy and vitality
items.ex_en: A brisk walk along the windy coastline will invigorate your body and clear your thoughts.
items.ex_zh: 沿着多风的海岸线快步行走，会让你的身体充满活力，思绪清晰。

items.def_zh: 点燃热情，使斗志昂扬/极度兴奋
items.def_en: (+ sb) to fill someone with intense enthusiasm, excitement, or determination
items.ex_en: The coach's speech fired up the team before the final match.
items.ex_zh: 决赛前，教练的演讲彻底点燃了全队的斗志。

items.def_zh: 使振奋，使极度兴奋，使高兴
items.def_en: (often passive) To make someone feel extremely happy, excited, and energized.
items.ex_en: She felt completely exhilarated by the rapid descent down the steep, snow-covered mountain slope.
items.ex_zh: 从白雪皑皑的陡峭山坡上飞速滑下，让她感到极度兴奋与振奋。

items.def_zh: 使兴高采烈，使欢欣鼓舞
items.def_en: (usually passive) To make someone feel extraordinarily proud, joyful, and excited.
items.ex_en: The prestigious award seemed to elate the young scientist beyond all realistic expectations.
items.ex_zh: 这项享有盛誉的奖项让这位年轻科学家备受鼓舞，欣喜若狂。

items.def_en: to excite or elate someone to the point of losing self-control or critical awareness
items.ex_en: The sudden taste of immense political power seemed to intoxicate the ambitious young senator.
items.ex_zh: 初尝巨大政治权力的滋味，似乎让这位野心勃勃的年轻参议员彻底陶醉忘形。

items.def_en: to fill someone with intense pleasure, delight, or reverent joy
items.ex_en: The haunting melody of the solitary cello managed to enrapture the entire silent audience.
items.ex_zh: 那凄美悠扬的大提琴独奏声，令在场所有的听众都听得如痴如醉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe instilling positive energy, high spirits, or euphoric joy in someone. They range from a mild boost in alertness or cheerfulness to soaring, overwhelming excitement and pride.
groups.summary_zh: 使某人振奋精神、心情舒畅乃至陷入极度兴奋自豪。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to infusing the psyche with exuberant energy, high spirits, or euphoric pride, contrasting with soothing 'comforting' by dynamic emotional elevation.
groups.desc_zh: 指将心境从低落引向高昂、狂喜或精力充沛的状态，与“安抚”相比，侧重情绪的动力激发与欣喜飞扬。
groups.nuance_en: exhilarate: thrilling and invigorating the senses intensely (speed / victory / sport) · elate: filling with profound, uplifting pride or triumph (success / victory / news) · invigorate: restoring physical vitality and sharp alertness (breeze / walk / drink) · perk up: reviving spontaneously from lethargy or gloom (patient / market / flower) · fire up: igniting passionate enthusiasm or battle readiness (team / crowd / audience)
groups.nuance_zh: exhilarate: 令人极其兴奋、心旷神怡 (speed / victory / sport) · elate: 因大捷或成功而喜不自胜 (success / victory / news) · invigorate: 注入充沛体力与精力 (breeze / walk / drink) · perk up: 精神由委顿转为振作 (patient / market / flower) · fire up: 煽动激情或斗志 (team / crowd / audience)

groups.name: Express Clearly & Expound · 阐述与系统表达 (Articulate, Discourse, Expound)
groups.tip: 通过图表或言语清晰说明

items.def_en: (+ sth) to explain or present ideas, facts, or plans clearly and systematically
items.ex_en: The CEO laid out an ambitious five-year growth strategy.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官详细阐述了一项雄心勃勃的五年增长战略。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to state, arrange, or explain facts, arguments, or intentions clearly in speech or writing
items.ex_en: The comprehensive white paper aims to set out our core diplomatic objectives for next year.
items.ex_zh: 这篇全面的白皮书旨在明确陈述我们明年的核心外交目标。

items.def_zh: 用图解法表示；绘制……的图表
items.def_en: To represent, explain, or show the arrangement of something using a diagram.
items.ex_en: The engineer took out a notepad to diagram the flow of cooling water precisely.
items.ex_zh: 工程师拿出一个笔记本，精确地绘制了冷却水流动的图解。

items.def_zh: 为（图片、插图等）加文字说明或标题
items.def_en: To provide an illustration, photograph, or video with a title or explanatory caption.
items.ex_en: The museum curator took time to caption each historical photograph with great historical detail.
items.ex_zh: 博物馆馆长花时间为每张历史照片附上了详尽的文字说明。

items.def_zh: 详加说明，极其明白地阐述
items.def_en: (+ sth) to explain something in full, explicit, and painstaking detail
items.ex_en: You don't need to spell out every detail; we get the general idea.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要把每个细节都阐释得那么细，我们明白大意。

items.def_en: To speak or write authoritatively and at length about a particular subject.
items.ex_en: The visiting scholar began to discourse at length on the economic implications of artificial intelligence.
items.ex_zh: 访问学者开始就人工智能对经济的影响进行长篇权威论述。

items.def_zh: 清晰明确地表达；清晰发音；关节连接
items.def_en: 1. To express an idea or feeling clearly and effectively in words. 2. To pronounce words or sounds clearly. 3. To connect parts together with a joint.
items.ex_en: The skilled diplomat was able to articulate the complex treaty provisions with remarkable precision.
items.ex_zh: 这位干练的外交官能够以非凡的准确性清晰阐明复杂的条约条款。

items.def_en: to describe, outline, or represent something precisely in speech or diagrammatic detail
items.ex_en: The architectural blueprints delineate the exact boundaries and load-bearing structures of the facility.
items.ex_zh: 这份建筑蓝图精确勾画出了该设施的确切边界与承重结构。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to explain a theory, belief, or concept thoroughly in systematic detail
items.ex_en: The renowned professor agreed to expound upon his controversial new theory of economic growth.
items.ex_zh: 这位知名教授同意深入系统地阐述其备受争议的经济增长新理论。

items.def_en: to make something clear and easy to understand by careful explanation
items.ex_en: The expert witness was asked to elucidate the technical evidence for the confused jury.
items.ex_zh: 专家证人被要求向困惑的陪审团阐明那些专业技术证据。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote formulating ideas with precision, speaking or writing in structured detail, or illustrating concepts systematically.
groups.summary_zh: 清晰严密地阐明见解，或通过详述与图注进行系统说明。
groups.desc_en: Covers formulating thoughts into structured, lucid, and systematic discourse, contrasting with basic 'speaking' through rigorous conceptual clarity and rhetorical architecture.
groups.desc_zh: 指将思维转化为条理清晰、层次分明的言辞或蓝图，与普通“说/讲”相比，强调逻辑严密、详尽剖析与系统性展开。
groups.nuance_en: articulate: expressing subtle ideas fluently and distinctly (vision / thought / argument) · expound: setting forth detailed theoretical explanations (doctrine / theory / view) · spell out: making terms clear and unmistakable without ambiguity (rule / detail / implication) · lay out: presenting an ordered plan, case, or design (plan / argument / option) · delineate: outlining precise boundaries or conceptual profiles (boundary / role / principle)
groups.nuance_zh: articulate: 清晰流利地表达微妙理念 (vision / thought / argument) · expound: 详尽系统地阐发义理或学说 (doctrine / theory / view) · spell out: 逐一明确解说、直白道破细节 (rule / detail / implication) · lay out: 层次分明地陈述方案或论点 (plan / argument / option) · delineate: 精准勾勒轮廓、边界或权责 (boundary / role / principle)

groups.name: Extinguish & Put Out · 熄灭与扑灭 (Extinguish, Put out, Quench)
groups.tip: 扑灭火焰或压制火光

items.def_en: to make a fire, cigarette, or light stop burning or shining
items.ex_en: The brave firefighter worked quickly through the smoke to put out the raging blaze.
items.ex_zh: 英勇的消防员在浓烟中迅速行动，扑灭了熊熊大火。

items.def_en: to extinguish a small flame by blowing air onto it
items.ex_en: The young birthday girl closed her eyes to blow out all seven scented candles.
items.ex_zh: 过生日的小女孩闭上双眼，一口气吹灭了全部七支香薰蜡烛。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to extinguish a flame or candle by covering it or pinching it
items.ex_en: Before leaving the study, he used a metal snuffer to snuff out the candle.
items.ex_zh: 离开书房前，他用金属灭烛罩掐灭了那根蜡烛。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to extinguish a small fire by treading heavily upon it
items.ex_en: The alert scout rushed forward to stamp out the stray sparks from the campfire.
items.ex_zh: 警觉的童子军冲上前去，踩灭了营火溅出的余烬火星。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to extinguish a flame or fire thoroughly by pouring water or liquid over it
items.ex_en: The campers used several buckets of lake water to douse out their dying bonfire.
items.ex_zh: 露营者们用几桶湖水泼倒在将熄的营火上，将其彻底浇灭。

items.def_en: 1. To put out a fire, flame, or light so it stops burning. 2. To completely destroy or end a feeling, hope, or idea.
items.ex_en: The automated emergency sprinkler system activated instantly to extinguish the chemical warehouse fire.
items.ex_zh: 自动紧急喷淋系统瞬间启动，扑灭了化学品仓库的火灾。

items.def_zh: 厚闷熄灭；隔绝空气闷灭
items.def_en: to extinguish a fire by covering it tightly to deprive it of oxygen
items.ex_en: She grabbed a heavy wool blanket to smother the kitchen grease fire safely.
items.ex_zh: 她抓起一条厚重的羊毛毯，安全地将厨房的油火隔绝空气闷灭。

items.def_zh: 掐灭，熄灭（烛火等）；扼杀，消灭；用鼻子闻，吸入
items.def_en: 1. To extinguish a candle flame or light (often 'snuff out'). 2. To put an end to something suddenly. 3. To sniff or inhale something.
items.ex_en: He paused beside the mantelpiece to snuff the solitary flame with wet fingers.
items.ex_zh: 他停在壁炉架旁，用湿润的手指掐灭了那簇孤零零的火苗。

items.def_en: to extinguish a fire or flame, especially by pouring water or liquid over it
items.ex_en: The forestry team pumped cold mountain water to quench the spreading brush fire effectively.
items.ex_zh: 林业队抽取冰凉的山泉水，有效地浇灭了蔓延的丛林大火。

items.def_en: to extinguish a fire by throwing a large amount of liquid over it
items.ex_en: The watchful camper poured a bucket of cold water to douse the burning embers.
items.ex_zh: 警惕的露营者倒了一桶冷水，将燃烧的余烬猛浇扑灭。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe causing a fire, flame, or light source to cease burning or shining by depriving it of oxygen, cooling it, or using a physical barrier. They range from everyday phrasal verbs to formal or literary terms.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过隔绝氧气、降温或覆盖使火焰、烛光熄灭或扑灭。
groups.desc_en: Constitutes terminating combustion, illumination, or metaphorical desires through direct physical suppression, distinguished from natural 'dying down' by deliberate active intervention.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过直接物理干涉阻断燃烧、熄灭光亮或掐灭抽象苗头，与火势自然“熄灭”相比，凸显人为主动扑灭与压制。
groups.nuance_en: extinguish: formal complete quelling of flame, light, or hope (fire / blaze / hope) · put out: everyday manual extinguishing of combustion (candle / cigarette / campfire) · smother: choking fire by cutting off oxygen supply (flame / fire / revolt) · snuff out: abruptly pinching off flame or crushing existence (candle / life / revolution) · douse: rapidly soaking or swamping a fire with liquid (flame / campfire / deck)
groups.nuance_zh: extinguish: 正式而彻底地扑灭烈火或希望 (fire / blaze / hope) · put out: 日常熄灭明火或香烟 (candle / cigarette / campfire) · smother: 窒息法灭火或扼杀苗头 (flame / fire / revolt) · snuff out: 掐灭烛火或迅速扼杀生命/反抗 (candle / life / revolution) · douse: 泼水大举浇灭 (flame / campfire / deck)

groups.name: Fabricate & Craft Materially · 锻造与人工制造 (Forge, Mint, Synthesise)
groups.tip: 从无到有锻造与生产

items.def_en: to shape molten metal or other material by pouring it into a mold
items.ex_en: The master artisan prepared the clay mold to cast an ornate bronze commemorative bell.
items.ex_zh: 工艺大师备好黏土模具，准备浇铸一口华丽的青铜纪念钟。

items.def_en: to make up a substance or drug by combining two or more ingredients
items.ex_en: The licensed pharmacist worked in the laboratory to compound the customized topical dermatological ointment.
items.ex_zh: 持证药剂师在实验室里配制这种定制的皮肤外用软膏。

items.def_zh: 匆匆敲定，粗略拼装制作出
items.def_en: (+ sth) to assemble or fabricate something roughly or hurriedly from material parts
items.ex_en: We managed to knock together a temporary bookshelf using some discarded wooden shipping pallets.
items.ex_zh: 我们用几块废弃的木质运输托盘，匆匆拼装制作出了一个简易书架。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to assemble or create a physical object by joining separate parts or pieces
items.ex_en: The boy spent hours in his room to piece together the complex model airplane.
items.ex_zh: 男孩在房间里花了数小时，将那架复杂的飞机模型拼装起来。

items.def_zh: 粗制滥造，临时拼凑制作
items.def_en: (+ sth) to put together or fabricate something quickly and roughly from whatever materials are available
items.ex_en: The stranded survivors managed to cobble together a makeshift raft from driftwood and vines.
items.ex_zh: 受困的幸存者们用浮木和藤蔓临时拼凑制作出一只简易木筏。

items.def_zh: 打制，锻造；缔造，开创；伪造，假冒
items.def_en: 1. To shape metal by heating it in a fire and beating it with a hammer. 2. To build or form something strong, such as an alliance, relationship, or agreement. 3. To make an illegal copy of something to deceive people.
items.ex_en: The traditional blacksmith used an iron hammer to forge a sturdy plowshare from iron.
items.ex_zh: 传统铁匠用铁锤将铁块敲打锻造成一把坚固的犁铧。

items.def_zh: 铸造（硬币）；创造，发明（新词语等）
items.def_en: 1. To make coins from metal, especially officially for a government. 2. To invent or coin a new word or phrase.
items.ex_en: The official treasury was commissioned to mint silver commemorative coins for the royal jubilee.
items.ex_zh: 官方造币局受命为王室禧庆铸造银质纪念币。

items.def_en: to construct or manufacture an industrial product or structure from raw materials
items.ex_en: The specialized engineering plant was contracted to fabricate heavy steel trusses for the suspension bridge.
items.ex_zh: 这家专业工程厂受托为悬索桥加工制造重型钢桁架。

items.def_zh: 重制，重新制作（remake 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of remake; to produce, make, or shape something again, often in a new or different way.
items.ex_en: The skilled jeweler remade the vintage gold ring into an exquisite, contemporary pendant necklace.
items.ex_zh: 技艺精湛的珠宝匠将那枚复古金戒重新制作成了一条精美的现代吊坠项链。

items.def_en: 1. (chemistry / biology) To produce a substance by chemical or biological synthesis. 2. To combine various separate ideas, styles, or concepts into a unified whole.
items.ex_en: The research team developed a novel catalytic process to synthesise the critical antibiotic molecule.
items.ex_zh: 该研究团队开发了一种新颖的催化工艺来人工合成这种关键的抗生素分子。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe specialized, often technical or physical processes of fabricating, shaping, or compounding material items such as metal, currency, or chemicals.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过熔铸、压印、化学合成等专门工艺或人工技术制造实物。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on assembling, forging, or constructing tangible objects through manual craft, industrial metallurgy, or improvised piecing together, contrasting with purely intellectual 'inventing'.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过手工工艺、工业铸造或拼装拼接等实体手段制造器物，与纯粹智力层面的“构思”相比，强调物质成型与工艺操作。
groups.nuance_en: forge: shaping metal through heating and hammering; forming sturdy bonds (metal / weapon / alliance) · cast: shaping liquid material into a rigid mold (bronze / statue / ingot) · mint: stamping official metal currency into existence (coin / medallion / money) · cobble together: assembling hastily from makeshift components (coalition / plan / agreement) · fabricate: manufacturing complex physical components industrial-style (steel / structure / device)
groups.nuance_zh: forge: 锻造金属或锤炼坚实同盟 (metal / weapon / alliance) · cast: 浇铸熔液入模定型 (bronze / statue / ingot) · mint: 官方铸币厂冲压铸币 (coin / medallion / money) · cobble together: 仓促拼凑、粗制搭成 (coalition / plan / agreement) · fabricate: 工业化装配制作构件 (steel / structure / device)

groups.name: Fabricate & Forge · 仿造与伪造 (Counterfeit, Forge, Fake)
groups.tip: 仿照原作进行复刻或造假

items.def_en: (+ sth) Produce an unauthorized, illicit, or cheap copy of a design or product
items.ex_en: Let's knock off for the day and grab some dinner together.
items.ex_zh: 我们今天就收工吧，一起去吃顿晚餐。

items.def_en: To make a photographic or printed copy of a document using a photocopier.
items.ex_en: Could you please photocopy this ten-page legal contract before the afternoon board meeting starts?
items.ex_zh: 你能赶在下午董事会开始前，把这份十页的法律合同复印一份吗？

items.def_zh: 捏造；伪造（故事、证据或借口）
items.def_en: (+ sth) Fabricate, invent, or concoct a false story, plan, or excuse
items.ex_en: He had to cook up an excuse for being late to the morning briefing.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不编造一个早会迟到的借口。

items.def_zh: 以假乱真地推销或冒充
items.def_en: (+ sth as sth) Falsely represent a fake or replica item as genuine
items.ex_en: The crooked street vendor tried to pass off cheap plastic jewelry as genuine emeralds.
items.ex_zh: 这个奸诈的街头摊贩企图将廉价的塑料饰品冒充成天然祖母绿推销。

items.def_en: 1. To make an exact copy of something in order to deceive people; forge. 2. To pretend to have a feeling, illness, etc.
items.ex_en: The cunning con artist used specialized vintage printing plates to fake priceless antique banknotes.
items.ex_zh: 那个狡猾的骗子使用特制的复古印版来伪造价值连城的古董纸币。

items.def_zh: 复制，仿制；再现，重现；繁殖，生殖
items.def_en: 1. To make a copy of a text, picture, sound, etc. 2. To make something happen or exist again in the same way. 3. (of humans, animals, or plants) To produce young or offspring.
items.ex_en: The high-end museum gift shop was authorized to reproduce rare seventeenth-century Dutch landscape paintings.
items.ex_zh: 这家高端博物馆礼品店获权仿制十七世纪珍稀的荷兰风景画作。
items.ex2_en: Microscopic bacteria reproduce rapidly under warm and excessively moist laboratory conditions.
items.ex2_zh: 微小的细菌在温暖且极其潮湿的实验室条件下迅速繁殖。

items.def_zh: 克隆，无性繁殖；复制，仿造
items.def_en: 1. (biology) To produce an exact genetic copy of an animal, plant, or gene. 2. To make an exact copy of a computer system, digital file, or product.
items.ex_en: The rogue technician secretly stole the source code to clone the entire proprietary operating system.
items.ex_zh: 叛逃的技术人员窃取了源代码，以全盘仿制该专有操作系统。

items.def_zh: 篡改，伪造（账目、记录或数据）
items.def_en: to alter records, reports, or accounts fraudulently so as to mislead
items.ex_en: The corrupt accountant conspired with senior executives to falsify internal corporate financial audit records.
items.ex_zh: 这名贪腐的会计与高管合谋，蓄意篡改公司内部的财务审计记录。

items.def_zh: 伪造，假冒（签名、画作或文件）
items.def_en: to fraudulently make or alter a document, signature, or work of art in order to deceive
items.ex_en: The dishonest clerk used black ink to forge the executive director's signature on the check.
items.ex_zh: 心术不正的办事员用黑墨水在支票上伪造了执行董事的签名。

items.def_en: to make an exact fraudulent imitation of something valuable, especially banknotes or official documents
items.ex_en: The criminal syndicate set up an underground press to counterfeit foreign currency banknotes systematically.
items.ex_zh: 该犯罪团伙设立地下印刷厂，有系统地伪造外国货币纸钞。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe producing a replica, imitation, or counterfeit version of an original object, document, or organism, often with intent to deceive or bypass authentic creation. The manner ranges from standard mechanical duplication (photocopy, reproduce) to fraudulent imitation (fake, forge, counterfeit).
groups.summary_zh: 仿制或伪造原件与真品，涵盖技术克隆及意在欺诈的假造。
groups.desc_en: Depicts manufacturing illicit duplicates, spurious narratives, or manipulated documents to deceive, contrasting with genuine 'copying' through its fraudulent intent and simulated authenticity.
groups.desc_zh: 指出于欺诈目的制作冒牌物品、虚假档案或编造不实之词，与合法的“复制”相比，具有伪造欺骗与以假乱真的定性。
groups.nuance_en: forge: fraudulent copying of handwriting, art, or official seals (signature / passport / painting) · fake: simulating appearance or symptoms deceptive-style (illness / document / death) · falsify: altering authentic records to misrepresent facts (record / account / datum) · counterfeit: unlawfully replicating currency, goods, or marks to pass off as real (currency / money / ticket) · cook up: inventing a false excuse, story, or pretext (story / excuse / scheme)
groups.nuance_zh: forge: 伪造笔迹、护照、艺术品以牟利 (signature / passport / painting) · fake: 假造外表、伪装病症以瞒骗 (illness / document / death) · falsify: 篡改账目、捏造数据 (record / account / datum) · counterfeit: 非法仿造货币或品牌商品 (currency / money / ticket) · cook up: 凭空捏造托词或荒唐借口 (story / excuse / scheme)

groups.name: Face & Confront · 迎面正视与正面硬抗 (Brave, Confront, Beard)
groups.tip: 由勇敢直面升级为正面交锋

items.def_en: to accept and deal directly with a difficult situation or opponent
items.ex_en: The newly elected mayor must soon face the mounting public anger over property taxes.
items.ex_zh: 新当选的市长很快就必须正视公众对房产税日益高涨的愤怒情绪。

items.def_zh: 勇敢面对；正视（现实或困境）
items.def_en: (+ sth) Accept and confront an unpleasant truth, difficult situation, or consequence squarely
items.ex_en: He has to face up to the fact that his business is failing.
items.ex_zh: 他必须正视自己的生意正在走向失败这一现实。

items.def_zh: 勇于面对；摆好架势迎战
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Face and deal resolutely with a challenger, threat, or hard reality
items.ex_en: It is finally time for the government to square up to the looming energy crisis.
items.ex_zh: 政府终于到了必须鼓起勇气、正视迫在眉睫的能源危机的时候了。

items.def_en: to resist or confront someone powerful courageously and refusing to yield
items.ex_en: These materials are designed to stand up to extreme weather conditions.
items.ex_zh: 这些材料旨在经受住极端天气的考验。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Confront, challenge, or oppose an adversary or formidable problem directly
items.ex_en: The courageous local community banded together to take on the predatory real estate developers.
items.ex_zh: 勇敢的当地社区团结一致，正面抗衡那些唯利是图的房地产开发商。

items.def_zh: 使竞争，使对抗，使相斗；在……上留下凹痕；去（果）核
items.def_en: 1. (+ against) To set someone or something in competition or conflict with another. 2. To make small marks or depressions on a surface. 3. To remove the stone or pit from fruit.
items.ex_en: The intense championship match will pit the defending champion against an ambitious teenage prodigy.
items.ex_zh: 这场激烈的冠军争夺战将使卫冕冠军与一位雄心勃勃的少年天才展开较量。

items.def_zh: 公然对抗，勇斗，当面顶撞
items.def_en: 1. (literary) To openly confront, oppose, or defy someone in a bold and fearless way.
items.ex_en: The fearless knight marched boldly into the imperial throne room to beard the despotic tyrant.
items.ex_zh: 无畏的骑士大步走进皇宫大殿，当面顶撞对抗那位专横的暴君。

items.def_en: 1. To face and withstand a dangerous, difficult, or unpleasant situation with courage.
items.ex_en: The rescue workers had to brave freezing blizzards to reach the stranded alpine climbers.
items.ex_zh: 救援人员不得不顶着严寒暴风雪，前去营救受困的高山攀登者。

items.def_zh: 正视，勇敢面对；当面对质，对抗
items.def_en: 1. To face, meet, or deal with a difficult situation or problem directly. 2. To face someone with hostile or challenging intent, or confront them with evidence.
items.ex_en: She decided to confront her aggressive business partner directly about the missing offshore funds.
items.ex_zh: 她决定就离岸资金下落不明一事，当面与咄咄逼人的商业合伙人对质。

items.def_en: to openly resist or refuse to submit to an authority or formidable force
items.ex_en: The fearless activist chose to publicly defy the unjust military censorship law yesterday afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 那位无畏的活动人士昨天下午选择公开藐视并违抗不公的军事审查法。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail an agent stepping directly into the path of an adversary, hazard, or unpleasant truth instead of flinching or retreating. Nuances range from stoic endurance ('brave') to assertive, unblinking opposition ('confront') and defiant, up-close audacity ('beard the lion').
groups.summary_zh: 指主动迎面正视、毫不避让地抗衡危险、敌手或严峻现实，强调勇气与正面交锋。
groups.desc_en: Denotes positioning oneself directly opposite an adversary, threat, or painful reality with deliberate defiance, differing from mere 'meeting' through conscious resistance and bravery.
groups.desc_zh: 指在强敌、危机或严酷现实面前正面相对并不退让，与普通的“遭遇”相比，强调充满决心的正视、硬抗与主动对峙。
groups.nuance_en: confront: meeting face-to-face in direct opposition or challenge (accuser / crisis / reality) · face up to: accepting and addressing an unpleasant reality squarely (truth / fact / failure) · brave: enduring perilous or harsh conditions unflinchingly (storm / danger / weather) · stand up to: resisting a dominant oppressor or bully courageously (bully / tyrant / pressure) · beard: audaciously defying someone in their own stronghold (lion / enemy / minister)
groups.nuance_zh: confront: 当面正面对质或直面危机 (accuser / crisis / reality) · face up to: 鼓起勇气正视无可回避的现实 (truth / fact / failure) · brave: 顶风冒雪勇对险恶环境 (storm / danger / weather) · stand up to: 挺身抗击强权或霸凌 (bully / tyrant / pressure) · beard: 深入险境捋虎须、当面叫板 (lion / enemy / minister)

groups.name: Familiarize & Acquaint · 熟悉与了解 (Acquaint, Familiarize, Orient)
groups.tip: 从初次接触到全面掌握知晓

items.def_en: (+ sb on) to give someone essential practical information or instructions in advance
items.ex_en: The operations commander took thirty minutes to brief the special task force on their mission.
items.ex_zh: 作战指挥官花了三十分钟向特派部队简要介绍了他们的行动任务。

items.def_en: (+ sb on/about sth) Provide someone with key information or context to make them informed
items.ex_en: Could you please clue me in on what happened during this morning's strategy meeting?
items.ex_zh: 你能给我讲讲今天上午战略会议上都发生了些什么，让我知情吗？

items.def_en: (+ sb on sth) Give someone the details or background information necessary to understand a matter
items.ex_en: My helpful colleague offered to fill me in on the latest project budget adjustments.
items.ex_zh: 我热心的同事主动向我详细介绍了最新的项目预算调整情况。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Familiarize someone with the latest developments or necessary working knowledge
items.ex_en: The team lead scheduled a meeting to bring the new developers up to speed quickly.
items.ex_zh: 团队负责人安排了一次会议，以便让新开发人员迅速熟悉最新工作情况。

items.def_zh: 使适应；使熟悉（新环境或情况）
items.def_en: (+ oneself/sb to/towards) to direct or accustom someone to new surroundings or facts
items.ex_en: The introductory workshop is designed to orient new international graduate students to university life.
items.ex_zh: 这场入门讲座旨在帮助新入学的国际研究生适应并熟悉大学生活。

items.def_en: (+ oneself/sb to) to make someone familiar with something through repeated exposure or habit
items.ex_en: New diplomats must accustom themselves to the demanding protocols of state dinners.
items.ex_zh: 新任外交官必须使自己习惯国宴上严苛的礼节。

items.def_zh: 使知悉；使了解（与 with 连用）
items.def_en: (+ oneself/sb with) to make someone familiar with or aware of facts, conditions, or rules
items.ex_en: The manager took time to acquaint the newly hired staff with office procedures.
items.ex_zh: 经理花时间让新入职的员工熟悉了办公室的办事流程。

items.def_zh: 使熟悉，使了解；使普及，使通俗化
items.def_en: To make someone or oneself familiar with or knowledgeable about something.
items.ex_en: All employees must familiarize themselves with the updated workplace safety regulations immediately.
items.ex_zh: 所有雇员必须立即熟悉更新后的工作场所安全规章。

items.def_en: (+ sb of) to inform or notify someone about a development or state of affairs
items.ex_en: The director will apprise the board of the recent financial setbacks tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 主管将于明天向董事会通报近期的财务受挫情况。

items.def_zh: 使重新熟悉，使重新结识
items.def_en: To make someone or oneself familiar again with someone or something.
items.ex_en: She returned home briefly to reacquaint herself with old friends and neighbors.
items.ex_zh: 她短暂地回了趟老家，与昔日的朋友和邻居重新熟络起来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote causing oneself or another person to gain knowledge, understanding, or habitual competence regarding a subject, environment, or process, typically followed by 'with'.
groups.summary_zh: 指使自己或他人知悉、习惯并掌握某项事物或环境。
groups.desc_en: Involves imparting foundational knowledge, procedural updates, or environmental awareness, distinguishing itself from deep 'teaching' through its orientation towards operational readiness.
groups.desc_zh: 向个体输入背景知识、操作规程或环境信息使其适应状况，与深度的“讲授”相比，侧重适应环境与通晓实操信息。
groups.nuance_en: familiarize: acquiring practical conversance with a system or place (user / student / employee) · acquaint: introducing to basic facts, contexts, or people (visitor / newcomer / reader) · brief: giving concise, directive operational intelligence (minister / team / soldier) · orient: aligning someone to spatial, cultural, or institutional surroundings (new recruit / student / traveler) · bring up to speed: updating someone with latest omitted information (colleague / partner / newcomer)
groups.nuance_zh: familiarize: 通过接触使熟悉掌握系统或环境 (user / student / employee) · acquaint: 介绍初步概况使其有所了解 (visitor / newcomer / reader) · brief: 执行任务前提供简要情报指示 (minister / team / soldier) · orient: 使在空间、方向或文化体制上建立定位 (new recruit / student / traveler) · bring up to speed: 补充最新进展使其步调一致 (colleague / partner / newcomer)

groups.name: Fascination & Absolute Charm · 吸引与神魂颠倒 (Captivate, Fascinate, Enthrall)
groups.tip: 从产生兴趣到深深沉醉着迷

items.def_zh: 激起……的好奇心；引起极大兴趣
items.def_en: arouse the curiosity or interest of someone by being unusual or mysterious
items.ex_en: The mysterious coded letter seemed to intrigue the seasoned detective immensely.
items.ex_zh: 那封神秘的密码信似乎极大地激起了这位老练侦探的好奇心。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Gain someone's affection, admiration, or favorable approval through charm or persuasion
items.ex_en: His witty presentation helped win over even the most skeptical investors.
items.ex_zh: 他机智风趣的演说赢得了哪怕是最持怀疑态度的投资者的支持。

items.def_en: delight greatly and attract through pleasing personality or appearance
items.ex_en: Her warm smile and effortless wit never failed to charm dinner guests.
items.ex_zh: 她温和的微笑与自如的风趣总能轻易迷住晚宴的宾客。

items.def_zh: 使惊叹不已；使为之倾倒
items.def_en: (+ sb) Overwhelm someone with surprise, admiration, or delight
items.ex_en: Her stunning vocal performance on stage totally bowled over the entire audience.
items.ex_zh: 她在舞台上惊艳的歌唱表演彻底让全场观众为之倾倒。

items.def_zh: 使神魂颠倒（尤指 sweep sb off their feet）
items.def_en: (+ sb off sb's feet) Completely captivate or infatuate someone, sweeping away resistance
items.ex_en: His romantic gestures managed to sweep her off her feet completely that evening.
items.ex_zh: 那个晚上，他浪漫的举动彻底让她神魂颠倒。

items.def_en: To hold someone's complete interest, attention, and curiosity by being very interesting or delightful.
items.ex_en: Ancient Egyptian architecture continues to fascinate historians and tourists from everywhere.
items.ex_zh: 古埃及建筑依然深深吸引着来自各地的历史学家和游客。

items.def_en: hold the complete attention of someone as if bound by a spell
items.ex_en: The ancient storyteller's wondrous voice seemed to spellbind the silent gathering.
items.ex_zh: 这位年迈说书人奇妙的嗓音仿佛施了魔法，使沉寂的人群听得入迷。

items.def_en: To attract and hold the attention and affection of someone completely by being charming, beautiful, or delightful.
items.ex_en: Her effortless grace on stage continued to captivate audiences throughout the tour.
items.ex_zh: 她在舞台上毫不费力的优雅姿态在整个巡演中始终深深吸引着观众。

items.def_en: 1. To hold someone's fascination and attention completely. 2. (archaic) To enslave.
items.ex_en: Her luminous stage presence continued to enthrall the silent, appreciative audience.
items.ex_zh: 她在舞台上光芒四射的魅力持续迷住了全场静默而沉醉的观众。

items.def_en: cause someone to become motionless with horror, wonder, or astonishment
items.ex_en: The terrifying sight of the approaching beast seemed to transfix the hunter.
items.ex_zh: 那头猛兽逼近的可怖景象仿佛让猎人吓得呆在原地，动弹不得。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame mark an ascending scale of mental and emotional capture, from arousing intense intellectual curiosity and interest (fascinate), to holding total aesthetic or personal absorption (captivate, enthrall), to being completely struck or overwhelmed by infatuation (smite/smitten).
groups.summary_zh: 从引起强烈兴趣与好奇，到牢牢吸引全部心神，直至彻底坠入爱河。
groups.desc_en: Marks exerting an irresistible hold over someone's attention, curiosity, or desire, differing from mild 'attracting' through the almost hypnotic paralysis of critical distance.
groups.desc_zh: 指施加不可抗拒的吸引力使人神魂颠倒或专注凝滞，与轻度“吸引”相比，强调几乎如同中邪般剥夺注意力的深度陶醉与着魔。
groups.nuance_en: captivate: holding attention totally through exquisite charm or beauty (audience / reader / admirer) · fascinate: intensely gripping intellectual or sensory curiosity (scientist / child / onlooker) · enthrall: holding spellbound as though under a magical thrall (crowd / spectator / listener) · spellbind: arresting speech and motion through wondrous performance (audience / child / listener) · bowl over: completely stunning or overwhelming with sudden delight/surprise (critic / audience / crowd)
groups.nuance_zh: captivate: 凭借美貌或魅力倾倒观众、捕获芳心 (audience / reader / admirer) · fascinate: 激发极强烈的好奇心与研究迷恋 (scientist / child / onlooker) · enthrall: 令人如痴如醉、全神贯注 (crowd / spectator / listener) · spellbind: 令人屏息凝神、如中定身法 (audience / child / listener) · bowl over: 惊喜或震撼得目瞪口呆 (critic / audience / crowd)

groups.name: Fashion & Construct · 构筑与匠造 (Fashion, Carpenter, Fabricate)
groups.tip: 动手打造打磨自制物品

items.def_en: to put together roughly or quickly using whatever materials are at hand
items.ex_en: They managed to cobble together a decent presentation using leftover slides.
items.ex_zh: 他们用剩下的幻灯片东拼西凑，总算赶制出了一份像样的演示文稿。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Construct or assemble something rapidly or roughly from available materials
items.ex_en: We can knock together a temporary garden shed using these scrap boards.
items.ex_zh: 我们可以用这些废弃木板匆匆拼凑出一个临时的花园棚屋。

items.def_en: to assemble a complete whole by joining separate components carefully
items.ex_en: The archaeologists carefully tried to piece together the shattered pieces of pottery.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家们小心翼翼地试图将破碎的陶器碎片拼凑复原。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Assemble, build, or synthesize parts into a coherent physical or conceptual whole
items.ex_en: It took the engineers several weeks to put together the complex machine.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们花了好几周时间才把这台复杂的机器组装完成。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Erect, assemble, or construct something quickly or makeshift fashion using whatever is at hand
items.ex_en: They had to rig up a makeshift tent before the heavy rain.
items.ex_zh: 他们不得不在大雨来临前用手头的材料草草搭起一个简易帐篷。

items.def_zh: 做木工活；打造，制作（木制品）；精巧地装配
items.def_en: To make, fit, or repair wooden structures and objects; to construct or assemble skillfully.
items.ex_en: The artisan skillfully carpentered a sturdy dining table out of reclaimed oak.
items.ex_zh: 工匠用回收的橡木精巧地打造了一张结实的餐桌。

items.def_zh: 手工制作，打造，塑造（使成形）
items.def_en: To shape, make, or form something skillfully, especially with hands or simple tools.
items.ex_en: The artisan slowly fashioned a delicate pendant out of raw river clay.
items.ex_zh: 手艺人用河底的原生黏土，缓缓捏制出一枚精致的坠饰。

items.def_zh: 重新制作，重造；翻拍（电影等）
items.def_en: To make something again in a different or improved way; to produce a new version of an existing film or song.
items.ex_en: The studio announced plans to remake the classic sci-fi film next summer.
items.ex_zh: 该制片厂宣布计划于明年夏天翻拍这部经典科幻电影。

items.def_en: to construct or manufacture an industrial or structural product from raw parts
items.ex_en: Specialized factories fabricate high-precision components required for commercial aviation engines.
items.ex_zh: 专业化工厂制造商用航空发动机所需的高精度部件。

items.def_en: to shape metal by heating and hammering, or to build a durable relationship/result
items.ex_en: The blacksmith worked through the night to forge a sharp ceremonial blade.
items.ex_zh: 铁匠通宵达旦地劳作，锻造出一把锋利的仪式用剑。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe skillful, deliberate shaping and manual construction of physical or figurative artifacts from raw components or pre-existing material, emphasizing craftsmanship, structural assembly, or adaptive rework.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过手工技艺或精巧工艺构筑、制作或改制物品。
groups.desc_en: Denotes assembling or shaping physical or conceptual structures from disparate materials, contrasting with standardized manufacturing by emphasizing ad-hoc improvisation, artisanal shaping, or patchwork integration.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用零散部件或原材料进行拼凑、构筑或塑形，与标准化工业制造相比，更凸显临时拼凑、手艺打磨或拼贴重构的工艺色彩。
groups.nuance_en: cobble together: hasty assembly from ill-fitting scraps (coalition / compromise / plan) · knock together: quick rough construction with minimal care (shed / meal / prototype) · piece together: meticulous investigative reconstruction (clues / narrative / puzzle) · rig up: makeshift improvisation using available gear (shelter / contraption / antenna) · fashion: artisanal shaping out of raw substance (garment / tool / identity)
groups.nuance_zh: cobble together: 仓促将不配套材料勉强拼凑成一体 (coalition / compromise / plan) · knock together: 草率粗糙地快速搭建 (shed / meal / prototype) · piece together: 抽丝剥茧般重组零散线索 (clues / narrative / puzzle) · rig up: 利用手头简陋物件临时拼装改装 (shelter / contraption / antenna) · fashion: 匠心打磨并赋予特定形式 (garment / tool / identity)

groups.name: Fasten, Secure & Enclose Barriers · 关锁与门禁启闭 (Shut, Unlock, Latch)
groups.tip: 开合通道或施加锁闭

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Enclose or confine someone or something by closing doors, gates, or barriers
items.ex_en: The blizzard had shut in the villagers inside their remote mountain cabins.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雪把村民们关在了偏远的深山小木屋里。

items.def_zh: 给……装大门；用闸门关住，关门限制……出入
items.def_en: To furnish or close off with a gate; to restrict or confine within gates.
items.ex_en: The estate managers decided to gate the rear courtyard to ensure security.
items.ex_zh: 庄园管理者决定给后院装上大门，以确保安全。

items.def_en: To open the lock of a door, container, or device; to make something accessible or revealed.
items.ex_en: He inserted the brass key into the old door to unlock it.
items.ex_zh: 他把黄铜钥匙插进旧门锁里，将其打开。

items.def_en: to fasten a door or gate with a latch so it stays closed
items.ex_en: Please ensure you latch the garden gate properly so the dog stays inside.
items.ex_zh: 请务必把花园门栓扣好，别让狗跑出去。
items.ex2_en: The heavy wooden gate latched securely as soon as it swung shut.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的木门一关上就稳稳地上闩锁住了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Secure, fasten, or obstruct an entrance or window firmly with wooden or metal bars
items.ex_en: Shopkeepers rushed to bar up their windows before the violent hurricane arrived.
items.ex_zh: 店主们赶在强飓风来临之前匆忙用横木封堵了门窗。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Fasten boards over doors or windows to enclose, barricade, or secure an opening
items.ex_en: Shopkeepers boarded up their storefronts before the hurricane arrived.
items.ex_zh: 店主们在飓风来临前用木板封住了店铺临街的门窗。

items.def_en: To close an entrance, container, or opening so that passage is obstructed; to cease operations.
items.ex_en: She stepped outside into the cold air and quickly shut the heavy door.
items.ex_zh: 她走到室外的冷空气中，迅速关上了那扇沉重的大门。
items.ex2_en: The automated metal gates shut tightly whenever the alarm system is activated.
items.ex2_zh: 只要警报系统启动，自动化金属门就会紧紧关闭。

items.def_en: to secure all doors, gates, and windows of a building or room with locks
items.ex_en: The shop owner made sure to lock up the store before leaving.
items.ex_zh: 店主在离开之前确保将店铺的所有门窗都锁好了。

items.def_en: to secure an entrance or barrier firmly by placing a heavy bar across it
items.ex_en: The guards decided to bar the castle gates firmly against incoming intruders.
items.ex_zh: 卫兵们决定用横木将城堡大门牢牢挡住，抵御来犯的入侵者。

items.def_en: to fasten a door or window firmly with a sliding metal bar
items.ex_en: Remember to bolt the back door securely before you go to sleep.
items.ex_zh: 睡觉前记得把后门插上门栓锁牢。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote manipulating doors, gates, and movable barriers to secure, fasten, or unfasten access to an enclosed space.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过门栓、锁具或门栏对通道与出入口进行闭合、上锁或开启。
groups.desc_en: Denotes physically blocking, securing, or liberating boundaries and portals, contrasting with general 'closing' or 'opening' through specific mechanical restraints, fortifying barriers, or punitive containment.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过机械锁闭、加固屏障或实体隔断来封闭、封死或解封出入口，与宽泛的‘开关’相比，强调安防锁定、物理封堵与禁锢属性。
groups.nuance_en: latch: engage a mechanical catch without full locking (door / gate / window) · lock up: secure firmly with a key or mechanism to prevent escape/entry (store / valuables / prisoner) · bar up: secure a portal with rigid crossbars (windows / entrance / shutters) · board up: seal openings with nailed timber against threat or abandonment (storefront / broken window / house) · gate: regulate or restrict access through an official perimeter (access / entry / community)
groups.nuance_zh: latch: 碰上门闩锁扣但未彻底上锁 (door / gate / window) · lock up: 用钥匙或机械锁死以绝内外 (store / valuables / prisoner) · bar up: 用金属或木制横条强行封死 (windows / entrance / shutters) · board up: 用木板钉死门窗以防风暴或废弃 (storefront / broken window / house) · gate: 设卡门禁以控制进出流动 (access / entry / community)

groups.name: Fight & Clash · 纠缠交战与肢体扭打 (Skirmish, Scuffle, Grapple)
groups.tip: 不同规模的武力冲突

items.def_en: (+ sb) Engage in a short, messy, informal physical fight or scuffle
items.ex_en: The hotheaded boy began to scrap with his classmates over petty playground insults.
items.ex_zh: 那个急性子的男孩因为操场上的微小辱骂而与同学扭打起来。

items.def_zh: 发生小冲突，进行小规模交火；发生小争吵
items.def_en: To engage in a minor, brief fight or dispute, especially between small military groups.
items.ex_en: Border patrols began to skirmish along the disputed demarcation line yesterday morning.
items.ex_zh: 边境巡逻队昨天上午开始在争议分界线沿线发生小规模交火。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) to struggle or fight roughly and disorderly, especially to obtain possession of something
items.ex_en: The two determined players continued to tussle over the loose ball fiercely.
items.ex_zh: 两名志在必得的球员继续激烈地缠抢那个失去控制的球。

items.def_en: Engage in a heated physical fight or aggressive scuffle
items.ex_en: The rival gang members stepped outside the crowded tavern to mix it up.
items.ex_zh: 敌对帮派的成员走出拥挤的酒馆，在外面大打出手。

items.def_zh: 摆好架势对打；对峙决斗
items.def_en: (+ with sb) Adopt a fighting stance or prepare to engage directly in a combat clash
items.ex_en: The two rival boxers began to square off in the ring's center.
items.ex_zh: 两位宿敌拳手开始在擂台中央摆好架势准备交锋。

items.def_en: to fight noisily and roughly in a public place
items.ex_en: Drunken patrons began to brawl in the street outside the noisy tavern.
items.ex_zh: 喝醉的顾客开始在嘈杂小酒馆外的街头上聚众斗殴。

items.def_en: (+ with) to engage in a close-quarters fight or struggle without weapons by clutching and wrestling
items.ex_en: The two wrestlers continued to grapple fiercely on the canvas for dominance.
items.ex_zh: 两名摔跤手继续在垫子上激烈缠斗，争夺主动权。

items.def_en: To fight briefly and confusedly at close quarters; to shuffle feet noisily.
items.ex_en: Several angry protesters began to scuffle with the line of riot police.
items.ex_zh: 几名愤怒的抗议者开始与防暴警察防线扭打混战在一起。

items.def_zh: （中世纪骑士）骑马持矛比武；激烈交锋，展开竞争
items.def_en: To fight on horseback with lances in a medieval tournament; to engage in a fierce competition or contest.
items.ex_en: The two ambitious candidates prepared to joust fiercely in the televised debate.
items.ex_zh: 两位野心勃勃的候选人准备在电视辩论中展开激烈的唇枪舌剑。

items.def_zh: （战斗机）进行近距空中缠斗；激烈争夺
items.def_en: (of fighter aircraft) To engage in close-range combat in the air; to engage in a fierce struggle.
items.ex_en: Hostile jet fighters continued to dogfight aggressively high above the contested airspace.
items.ex_zh: 敌对的喷气式战斗机在争议领空高处继续进行激烈的空中近距缠斗。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote dynamic, specialized physical combat or chaotic clashes, emphasizing the physical manner of engagement such as tangled wrestling, brief border fighting, or rapid aerial dogfighting.
groups.summary_zh: 描述具体方式的肢体打斗、混乱扭打或小规模交火冲突。
groups.desc_en: Denotes engaging in disorderly, impromptu, or close-quarters combat, contrasting with organized 'warfare' through chaotic physical tangling, minor skirmishing, or street-level violence.
groups.desc_zh: 指爆发非正规、即兴或贴身的肉搏缠斗与短兵相接，与正规‘战争/交战’相比，强调混乱扭打、摩擦冲突与市井格斗色彩。
groups.nuance_en: scuffle: brief, disorganized physical tussle without deadly intent (crowd / protesters / guards) · brawl: noisy, uncontrolled free-for-all fight in public (drunks / patrons / rivals) · grapple: seize and struggle in close wrestling grip (assailant / opponent / problem) · skirmish: minor clash on the periphery of a larger conflict (patrols / factions / troops) · scrap with: informal gritty fight or sparring (siblings / rivals / competitors)
groups.nuance_zh: scuffle: 偶发的短暂混乱推搡扭打 (crowd / protesters / guards) · brawl: 喧闹失控的群体性公开斗殴 (drunks / patrons / rivals) · grapple: 贴身紧抓死斗或角力抱摔 (assailant / opponent / problem) · skirmish: 边缘性、小规模试探性交火 (patrols / factions / troops) · scrap with: 非正式且充满火药味的小打小闹 (siblings / rivals / competitors)

groups.name: Flee & Depart Secretly · 仓促逃离与溜走 (Decamp, Hightail, Skedaddle)
groups.tip: 摆脱束缚或仓皇逃跑逃离

items.def_en: (+ with) to escape hurriedly, especially after doing something illegal
items.ex_en: The burglar made off as soon as the burglar alarm went off.
items.ex_zh: 防盗警报一响，窃贼就仓皇逃窜了。

items.def_en: Leave or depart quietly, unobtrusively, and without drawing attention
items.ex_en: She decided to slip off during the noisy reception without saying goodbye.
items.ex_zh: 她决定趁着嘈杂的酒会悄悄溜走，没有跟任何人道别。

items.def_en: Depart furtively and secretly, often to avoid detection or duty
items.ex_en: The tired apprentice tried to sneak off early while the master rested.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的学徒趁着师傅休息，试图偷偷早点溜走。

items.def_en: Depart or evacuate a place rapidly, abruptly, or under pressure
items.ex_en: The landlord gave the unruly tenants two hours to clear out completely.
items.ex_zh: 房东限令那些不守规矩的房客在两小时内彻底滚蛋撤走。

items.def_en: (+ for/from) to suddenly and rapidly run away out of fear or an urge to escape
items.ex_en: The frightened deer suddenly decided to bolt for the safety of dense trees.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的鹿突然拔腿飞奔，逃向安全的密林之中。

items.def_en: (+ with/from) to depart secretly and hide, typically to avoid arrest or prosecution, often taking money
items.ex_en: The corrupt accountant managed to abscond with millions of dollars from the vault.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败的会计卷走了金库里数百万美元潜逃了。

items.def_zh: （尤指秘密或匆忙地）逃走，溜走；拔营，撤营
items.def_en: 1. (often + to/with) To leave a place suddenly and secretly, often to escape or with stolen goods. 2. To pack up and leave a camp.
items.ex_en: The tenants decided to decamp in the night without paying overdue rent.
items.ex_zh: 租客们决定在夜色中悄悄溜走，分文未付逾期的房租。

items.def_en: to leave in a great hurry, frequently used in imperative commands
items.ex_en: He angrily told the trespassing youngsters to scram from his private property.
items.ex_zh: 他愤怒地呵斥那些擅自闯入的年轻人们赶紧从他的私有领地上滚开。

items.def_zh: 仓促逃走，飞快逃离（常用于hightail it）
items.def_en: (also 'hightail it') (informal) To run away or leave a place as quickly as possible.
items.ex_en: When sirens wailed nearby, the vandals decided to hightail it down the alley.
items.ex_zh: 警报声在附近响起时，破坏分子决定沿着小巷飞快逃离。

items.def_en: (informal) To run away or leave quickly, especially in a hurry or panic.
items.ex_en: When the guard dog barked loudly, the trespassers decided to skedaddle immediately.
items.ex_zh: 当看门狗大声吠叫时，擅闯者们决定立刻仓皇逃走。

groups.summary_en: Informal and literary verbs denoting rapid, sudden, or evasive departures to avoid detection, pursuit, or impending consequences, typically used intransitively.
groups.summary_zh: 指为躲避追踪、麻烦或职责而突然、仓促地逃离或溜走。
groups.desc_en: Denotes sudden, evasive, or clandestine departure to evade capture, reckoning, or responsibility, contrasting with neutral 'leaving' via panic, stealth, or unlawful flight.
groups.desc_zh: 指为躲避追捕、问责或责任而突发、隐秘或惊慌地脱逃离去，与中性‘离开’相比，带有畏罪潜逃、溜之大吉或仓皇遁匿色彩。
groups.nuance_en: bolt: sudden panicked dash away from confinement or danger (horse / suspect / prisoner) · abscond: illicit flight to escape legal prosecution or debt, often taking assets (treasurer / fugitive / trustee) · decamp: abrupt and secretive departure, often leaving debts behind (debtor / army / tenant) · sneak off: stealthy departure without attracting notice (employee / guest / child) · scram: urgent, hurried exit, often under orders (trespasser / intruder / kids)
groups.nuance_zh: bolt: 因受惊或企图脱身而突然拔腿狂奔 (horse / suspect / prisoner) · abscond: 携款或畏罪秘密潜逃 (treasurer / fugitive / trustee) · decamp: 连夜撤离或溜之大吉以规避债务与困局 (debtor / army / tenant) · sneak off: 蹑手蹑脚、不为人知地溜走 (employee / guest / child) · scram: 被呵斥或紧急情势下的仓皇滚蛋 (trespasser / intruder / kids)

groups.name: Float, Suggest & Formalize Proposals · 试探、提议与郑重提出 (Suggest, Moot, Propose, Proposition)
groups.tip: 提出建设性建议或正式提案

items.def_en: (+ sth) Introduce a topic, matter, or proposal into conversation or consideration
items.ex_en: She was hesitant to bring up the budget deficit during the staff meeting.
items.ex_zh: 在全体员工会议上，她对是否提出预算赤字问题犹豫不决。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Produce or suggest an idea, scheme, or proposal for consideration
items.ex_en: The marketing team worked hard to come up with a creative advertising slogan.
items.ex_zh: 营销团队努力想出了一个富有创意的广告宣传标语。

items.def_en: to offer an idea, theory, or candidate for general consideration and evaluation
items.ex_en: The committee decided to put forward several proposals regarding sustainable municipal transport.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定就可持续的城市交通提出几项方案以供考虑。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Offer or mention an idea or suggestion casually for discussion
items.ex_en: During the initial brainstorming session, they casually tossed out various branding ideas.
items.ex_zh: 在最初的头脑风暴会议中，他们随口抛出了各种品牌推广构想。

items.def_en: to propose an idea, plan, or course of action; to imply or indicate something indirectly.
items.ex_en: The doctor decided to suggest a change of diet rather than prescribing medication.
items.ex_zh: 医生决定建议改变饮食习惯，而不是直接开具药物处方。

items.def_zh: 提出（计划或建议）供讨论；讨论
items.def_en: (often passive) (chiefly British) to suggest or bring up an idea or plan for consideration and discussion.
items.ex_en: A radical tax reform proposal was recently mooted by the finance ministry.
items.ex_zh: 一项激进的税收改革方案最近由财政部提出以供审议讨论。

items.def_en: (chiefly BrE) to officially submit a motion, proposal, or topic for formal debate
items.ex_en: The member of parliament plans to table a new motion regarding healthcare.
items.ex_zh: 这位国会议员计划就医疗保健问题正式提交一项新动议。

items.def_zh: 提议，建议，提出（计划等）；求婚；打算
items.def_en: 1. To put forward a plan, idea, or offer for consideration. 2. (+ to) To ask someone to marry you.
items.ex_en: The committee chairman will propose several substantial amendments to the existing bylaws.
items.ex_zh: 委员会主席将就现行规章提出几项实质性的修正建议。

items.def_zh: 向（某人）提议；向（某人）提出性要求
items.def_en: To make a suggestion or offer to someone, especially a business proposal or an invitation to have sex.
items.ex_en: A strange man brazenly decided to proposition the young woman at the bar.
items.ex_zh: 一个陌生男子厚颜无耻地在酒吧向那位年轻女子提出了不正当的要求。

items.def_en: to present a formal written bid, resignation, or proposition formally to an authority
items.ex_en: The minister decided to tender his formal resignation to the prime minister.
items.ex_zh: 该部长决定向首相正式呈交他的书面辞呈。

groups.summary_en: This frame spans speech acts that put an idea, course of action, or offer before an interlocutor for consideration—escalating from tentative hint or open brainstorming (moot, suggest) to formal institutional presentation (propose) and blunt, often improper personal solicitations (proposition).
groups.summary_zh: 从试探性推敲、委婉建议递进至正式提呈乃至直白利诱。
groups.desc_en: Denotes introducing ideas, theories, or proposals along an axis from tentative conversational floating to formal procedural tabling, contrasting with general 'speaking' by its focus on soliciting consideration.
groups.desc_zh: 指将想法、案卷或提议公之于众以供审议，沿‘随口试探—正式立案’的强度演进，与普通‘交谈’相比具有明确的提案与征询意图。
groups.nuance_en: toss out: casually offer an unvetted idea without commitment (ideas / suggestions / numbers) · moot: put forward an idea for open debate or speculation (merger / proposal / hypothesis) · put forward: earnestly offer a reasoned candidate or thesis for serious review (candidate / theory / plan) · table: formally submit for legislative/official consideration (in UK) or postpone (in US) (motion / bill / amendment) · propose: deliberately and formally present an actionable plan or alliance (solution / partnership / toast)
groups.nuance_zh: toss out: 随口抛出不加修饰的灵感或粗略想法 (ideas / suggestions / numbers) · moot: 提出议题以供公开辩论或假设探讨 (merger / proposal / hypothesis) · put forward: 郑重提出成熟候选人或理论假说 (candidate / theory / plan) · table: 议会/机构层面正式提请审议（英）或延缓搁置（美） (motion / bill / amendment) · propose: 正式提出具有行动约束力的计划或婚盟 (solution / partnership / toast)

groups.name: Fly & Soar · 飞行与翱翔 (Airborne Motion)
groups.tip: 在空中振翅或滑翔

items.def_en: Make contact with the ground at the conclusion of flight
items.ex_en: The commercial airliner managed to touch down safely despite the heavy rainstorm.
items.ex_zh: 尽管遭遇大暴雨，这架商用客机仍设法安全降落着陆。

items.def_en: to stay in the air in one place, flapping wings or rotors rapidly
items.ex_en: The rescue helicopter had to hover steadily above the rough mountain ridge.
items.ex_zh: 救援直升机不得不在崎岖的山脊上方平稳地悬停。

items.def_en: to fly smoothly through the air without power or engine noise
items.ex_en: The majestic eagle began to glide effortlessly over the deep forested canyon.
items.ex_zh: 那只雄鹰开始轻松惬意地在深邃的森林峡谷上空滑翔。

items.def_en: Fly downwards rapidly and smoothly through the air, often toward prey
items.ex_en: The sharp-eyed hawk swooped down through the trees to snatch the unsuspecting mouse.
items.ex_zh: 那只目光敏锐的鹰俯冲穿过树丛，抓住了毫无防备的老鼠。

items.def_en: Leave the ground and begin airborne flight
items.ex_en: The passenger jet took off smoothly into the clear morning sky without delay.
items.ex_zh: 客机平稳地升空，准时飞入了清朗的晨空。

items.def_zh: 飞，飞翔；驾驶（飞机）；飞越；疾驰
items.def_en: 1. To move through the air using wings or an aircraft. 2. To operate an aircraft; to transport someone or something by aircraft.
items.ex_en: Migratory geese fly thousands of miles south every autumn in a V formation.
items.ex_zh: 每年秋天，候鸟大雁都会排成V字形向南飞行数千英里。
items.ex2_en: The experienced pilot flew the cargo plane across the turbulent ocean safely.
items.ex2_zh: 经验丰富的飞行员安全地驾驶货机穿过了波涛汹涌的海洋。

items.def_zh: 飞翔，飞行；飞越；击中（人或鸟的）侧翼或翅膀
items.def_en: 1. (literary) To travel through the air using wings; to fly. 2. To wound a bird or person in the wing or arm.
items.ex_en: A solitary heron winged its silent way across the twilight sky toward home.
items.ex_zh: 一只孤鹭展翅穿过暮色苍茫的天空，静静地飞向巢穴。

items.def_en: to fly high in the air without moving wings much, carried by air currents
items.ex_en: The majestic eagles soar effortlessly high above the rugged peaks on thermal currents.
items.ex_zh: 雄伟的雕群乘着热气流，在巍峨的山巅上方轻松地翱翔。

items.def_en: To fly directly over a particular place or territory in an aircraft.
items.ex_en: Foreign military aircraft are strictly prohibited from overflying the disputed border territory.
items.ex_zh: 外国军用飞机被严禁飞越该争议边境领空。

items.def_en: to move rapidly downward through the air, especially to attack or land
items.ex_en: A hungry seagull swooped swiftly toward the harbor to steal a fish discard.
items.ex_zh: 一只饥饿的海鸥迅速向海港俯冲而去，去抢夺丢弃的杂鱼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe self-propelled or winged movement through the air, ranging from basic transit aloft to effortless gliding, high climbing, and swooping.
groups.summary_zh: 描述在空中展翅飞行、翱翔滑翔或俯冲巡航的各种空中运动方式。
groups.desc_en: Denotes dynamic airborne traversal and altitude maneuvering, contrasting with static 'floating' or passive 'falling' through self-directed aerodynamic control, predatory descent, or expansive ascent.
groups.desc_zh: 指凭借空气动力掌控在空中穿梭与升降，与静态‘漂浮’或被动‘下坠’相比，强调有意识的滑翔、俯冲或展翅冲霄。
groups.nuance_en: soar: rise high into the air effortlessly on thermal currents (eagle / glider / spirits) · glide: smooth continuous motion without motor power or flapping (plane / bird / skater) · swoop down: sudden swift diving attack or descent through the air (hawk / predator / jet) · hover: remain suspended stably in one airborne spot (helicopter / hummingbird / hawk) · wing: travel swiftly by purposeful flight (flock / migratory birds / way)
groups.nuance_zh: soar: 借气流不费力地直冲云霄或高空翱翔 (eagle / glider / spirits) · glide: 不借动力或不振翅地平稳滑翔 (plane / bird / skater) · swoop down: 居高临下猛禽捕食般急骤俯冲 (hawk / predator / jet) · hover: 在半空定点悬停滞空 (helicopter / hummingbird / hawk) · wing: 振翅奋飞、定标远航 (flock / migratory birds / way)

groups.name: Forage & Prey on Specific Fauna · 特类动植物捕猎与采集 (Prey, Fowl, Frog, Oyster)
groups.tip: 野外追捕并猎取动物

items.def_en: (+ sth) Consume or forage specific plants or animals as a primary food source
items.ex_en: Owls feed primarily on small rodents at night.
items.ex_zh: 猫头鹰主要在夜间捕食小型啮齿动物。

items.def_en: [I/T] to try to catch fish or seafood in a body of water using nets, lines, or traps
items.ex_en: The elderly brothers fish along the quiet mountain stream every Sunday at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 这对年迈的兄弟每逢周日拂晓都会在幽静的山间溪流旁钓鱼。

items.def_en: to hunt or catch frogs.
items.ex_en: Local boys often frog along the murky bayou banks using long wooden spears.
items.ex_zh: 当地男孩经常拿着长木矛，沿着昏暗的河涌岸边抓青蛙。

items.def_en: to search for and catch crabs as a livelihood or recreational activity
items.ex_en: We used to crab off the wooden pier using chicken necks for bait.
items.ex_zh: 我们过去常在木码头上用鸡脖子当诱饵抓螃蟹。

items.def_en: to gather, dredge, or fish for oysters.
items.ex_en: Generations of local watermen have oystered in the shallow waters of the bay.
items.ex_zh: 世世代代的当地渔民都在海湾的浅水区采捞牡蛎。

items.def_en: (+ for) to dig for or gather edible clams from coastal sands or mudflats
items.ex_en: The family loves to clam for sweet quahogs along the muddy tidal flats.
items.ex_zh: 一家人喜欢沿着泥泞的潮滩挖掘美味的硬壳蛤。

items.def_en: to hunt, shoot, or catch wild birds.
items.ex_en: Nobles would fowl among the autumn marshes with trained falcons and loyal hounds.
items.ex_zh: 贵族们常带着训练有素的猎鹰和忠诚的猎犬在秋日沼泽中打鸟。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Track, pursue, and capture wild prey after targeted pursuit
items.ex_en: Detectives worked around the clock to hunt down the suspect.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们夜以继日地工作，力求将嫌疑人缉拿归案。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Hunt, capture, and feed upon another creature
items.ex_en: Large predatory owls routinely prey on field mice and other small nocturnal rodents.
items.ex_zh: 体型庞大的食肉鸮类经常捕食田鼠和其他小型夜行啮齿动物。

items.def_zh: 捕食，猎食；侵害，欺凌；折磨，使苦恼
items.def_en: (prey on/upon) to hunt and eat another animal; to exploit, harm, or deceive vulnerable people.
items.ex_en: Ruthless online fraudsters frequently prey upon lonely elderly people with deceptive lottery schemes.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的网上骗子经常用虚假的中奖骗局侵害孤独的老人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this specialized frame describe engaging in the targeted hunting, gathering, or predatory harvest of specific wild creatures or preying upon other living organisms in nature. They typically function intransitively, often derived denominally from the quarry itself.
groups.summary_zh: 针对特定物种开展捕猎、采集或本能捕食活动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes harvesting or hunting specific aquatic or avian wild species, contrasting with generic 'hunting' or 'gathering' through target-specialized extraction techniques and habitats.
groups.desc_zh: 指在特定水域或沼泽荒野中采捕特定物种的生计活动，与宽泛的‘捕猎/采集’相比，具名指代物种专属的抓捕习性与工具手法。
groups.nuance_en: fowl: hunt wild birds for sport or food (marsh / wetland / game) · frog: capture edible bullfrogs typically by gigs or spotlights (swamp / pond / bayou) · crab: catch crabs using pots, nets, or trotlines (bay / shoreline / pier) · oyster: dredge or gather oysters from aquatic beds (reefs / coastal beds / estuary) · feed on: systematically consume specific flora/fauna as staple prey (carcasses / insects / algae)
groups.nuance_zh: fowl: 在沼泽水网猎捕野禽野鸭 (marsh / wetland / game) · frog: 夜间用刺叉或照明灯捕捉食用蛙 (swamp / pond / bayou) · crab: 下笼捕捞海蟹或淡水蟹 (bay / shoreline / pier) · oyster: 在滩涂或礁床拖网撬采牡蛎 (reefs / coastal beds / estuary) · feed on: 生物以特定猎物为食进行常态捕食 (carcasses / insects / algae)

groups.name: Forbid & Prohibit · 严禁与法令取缔 (Ban, Prohibit, Outlaw)
groups.tip: 法令或规矩明文不许

items.def_en: to officially or legally prevent something from being done, read, or used
items.ex_en: The city council voted unanimously to ban single-use plastics across all supermarkets.
items.ex_zh: 市议会一致投票决定在所有超市明令禁止使用一次性塑料制品。

items.def_en: 1. To officially forbid something by law, rule, or other authority; make something impossible.
items.ex_en: Federal regulations strictly prohibit unauthorized personnel from entering the nuclear testing facility.
items.ex_zh: 联邦法规严禁未经授权的人员进入核试验设施。

items.def_en: to prohibit or forbid authoritatively, especially by an authoritative or ecclesiastical order
items.ex_en: The papal decree sought to interdict all unsanctioned trade with heretical factions.
items.ex_zh: 教皇法令试图下令封禁与异端派系的一切未经许可的贸易往来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Impose strict measures or an outright ban to suppress an illegal or unwanted practice
items.ex_en: Maritime authorities are moving swiftly to clamp down on illegal smuggling along coastlines.
items.ex_zh: 海事部门正迅速采取行动，严厉打击沿海的非法走私活动。

items.def_zh: 明令排除；判定不可行/不允许
items.def_en: (+ sth) Exclude or formally disallow an action, candidate, or possibility
items.ex_en: Investigators cannot entirely rule out deliberate arson as the cause of the blaze.
items.ex_zh: 调查人员无法完全排除蓄意纵火作为起火原因的可能性。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Take severe, decisive legal or institutional action against prohibited activities
items.ex_en: The police announced a new campaign to crack down on reckless driving.
items.ex_zh: 警方宣布开展一项新行动，严厉打击危险驾驶行为。

items.def_zh: 禁止，不准（forbid 的过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past participle of forbid; to officially disallow or order not to do something.
items.ex_en: Visitors were expressly forbidden to touch the fragile ancient artifacts inside the museum.
items.ex_zh: 游客被明确禁止触摸博物馆内脆弱的古代文物。

items.def_en: To order someone not to do something, or to officially disallow something.
items.ex_en: Rigid school rules strictly forbid students from using smartphones inside the classroom.
items.ex_zh: 严格的校规明令禁止学生在教室内部使用智能手机。

items.def_en: to make something totally illegal by passing a statute or governmental decree
items.ex_en: The newly elected parliament quickly moved to outlaw unfair workplace hiring practices.
items.ex_zh: 新当选的议会迅速采取行动，立法取缔不公正的职场招聘行为。

items.def_en: to denounce or forbid a practice or organization formally as dangerous or unlawful
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime sought to proscribe rival political groups and independent newspapers.
items.ex_zh: 该威权政权企图明令取缔竞争对手政团和独立报纸。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent authoritative, legal, or institutional acts that decree an activity unlawful or inadmissible. 'Forbid' spans interpersonal and general injunctions, whereas 'prohibit' and 'ban' carry official and statutory gravity, and 'outlaw' formally places a practice outside legal protection.
groups.summary_zh: 依法律、权威或规章明令禁止某项行为或剥夺其合法地位。
groups.desc_en: Denotes exercising authoritative, statutory, or physical power to disallow actions or suppress practices, contrasting with informal 'discouragement' through institutional interdiction and punitive finality.
groups.desc_zh: 指凭借法律、行政或强制权威明令封杀某项行为或活动，与私下‘劝阻’相比，带有官方取缔、制度阻断和强制惩处的效力。
groups.nuance_en: ban: impose an official or legal prohibition across a jurisdiction (weapons / books / imports) · prohibit: strictly disallow through statute, regulation, or formal rule (smoking / entry / discrimination) · interdict: legally or militarily intercept and nullify flow or commerce (contraband / shipments / airspace) · crack down on: enforce punitive severity against illicit conduct (corruption / dissent / cartel) · forbid: express direct personal, moral, or authoritative veto (access / contact / marriage)
groups.nuance_zh: ban: 官方颁布全面禁令或永久封禁 (weapons / books / imports) · prohibit: 依据法条、规章严加禁止 (smoking / entry / discrimination) · interdict: 军警或法定层面的阻断截击与干预 (contraband / shipments / airspace) · crack down on: 严打整肃违法乱纪行为 (corruption / dissent / cartel) · forbid: 凭借长辈或上位者威权下达直接禁令 (access / contact / marriage)

groups.name: Fracture to Destruction · 裂碎至分子化粉碎 (Chip, Grind, Smash, Atomize)
groups.tip: 施加外力击碎碾压成微粒

items.def_zh: （使）掉碎片，（使）磕碰破损；凿，切削
items.def_en: To break a small piece off something by knocking or hitting it, or to be broken in this way.
items.ex_en: I accidentally chipped the delicate antique porcelain saucer while washing the dishes.
items.ex_zh: 我在洗碗时不小心把那只精致的古董瓷碟磕掉了一小块。
items.ex2_en: The fragile ceramic mug chipped easily when it knocked against the granite.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的陶瓷马克杯撞到花岗岩时很容易就磕掉了碎片。

items.def_en: to break or cause to break into small, thin, sharp pieces
items.ex_en: The heavy wooden bat splintered into several sharp fragments upon striking the pitch.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的木质球棒在击中投球的瞬间崩裂成了数根尖锐的木刺。
items.ex2_en: The forceful impact splintered the dry wooden beam into numerous sharp pieces.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的撞击将干燥的木梁震裂成许多锋利的碎片。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Disintegrate or cause to fracture into distinct smaller fragments
items.ex_en: Road crews used heavy hydraulic machinery to break up the damaged concrete pavement.
items.ex_zh: 修路工人使用重型液压机械将受损的混凝土路面碎裂成块。
items.ex2_en: The massive ice shelf broke up rapidly during the unusually warm summer.
items.ex2_zh: 巨大的冰架在异常温暖的夏季迅速解体崩裂。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Reduce something solid to small particles or fine powder by friction or crushing
items.ex_en: The pharmacist used a stone mortar to grind down the mineral crystals.
items.ex_zh: 药剂师用石臼将矿物结晶研磨成了细腻的粉末。

items.def_en: to break violently into numerous tiny pieces upon impact
items.ex_en: The crystal vase shattered into hundreds of sparkling fragments upon the tiled floor.
items.ex_zh: 水晶花瓶掉在瓷砖地板上，瞬间粉碎成了成百上千块闪烁的碎片。
items.ex2_en: The angry protestor shattered the plate glass window with a heavy hammer.
items.ex2_zh: 愤怒的抗议者用一把重锤砸碎了厚平板玻璃窗。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Break something violently into small pieces; destroy by shattering
items.ex_en: Angry rioters broke through the heavy doors and smashed up the entire lobby.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的暴徒冲破沉重的大门，把整个大堂彻底砸了个稀烂。

items.def_en: To break violently into many pieces, or to cause something to do this; to hit or collide with great force.
items.ex_en: The vandal deliberately threw a heavy brick to smash the storefront glass display.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子故意扔了一块沉重的砖头砸烂了临街橱窗玻璃。
items.ex2_en: The runaway delivery truck smashed violently against the concrete highway divider barrier.
items.ex2_zh: 失控的送货卡车猛烈撞击在公路混凝土隔离护栏上。

items.def_zh: 磨碎，碾碎；摩擦，磨光；折磨
items.def_en: To break or crush something into small pieces or powder; to rub two hard surfaces together.
items.ex_en: The barista will grind whole roasted beans just before brewing your morning espresso.
items.ex_zh: 咖啡师会在冲煮早晨的浓缩咖啡前现场磨碎整颗烘焙豆。

items.def_en: to reduce completely to fine dust or powder by crushing or beating
items.ex_en: Our home football team completely pulverized the visiting rivals in a lopsided victory.
items.ex_zh: 我们主场足球队在一场一边倒的胜利中彻底粉碎了客场对手。

items.def_zh: 使粉碎成微粒；使雾化，使喷成雾状；使分裂，使瓦解
items.def_en: 1. To reduce something to tiny particles or spray; to turn a liquid into a fine mist. 2. To divide or break something into separate, isolated units.
items.ex_en: The immense blast seemed to atomize the old stone wall into thick mist.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的爆炸声似乎把古老的石墙彻底粉碎成了漫天的浓尘。
items.ex2_en: Liquid fuel tends to atomize instantly inside the high-pressure combustion chamber.
items.ex2_zh: 液体燃料在高压燃烧室内部往往会瞬间雾化。

groups.summary_en: This frame spans the physical reduction of brittle or solid structures into smaller fragments, powder, or ultimate constituents. It progresses in destructive intensity from small superficial fractures ('chip') to violent shattering ('smash'), crushing reduction ('grind'), down to absolute micro-level disintegration ('atomize').
groups.summary_zh: 由表层剥落、暴力破碎到研磨碾烂，直至彻底粉碎或化为微粒的破坏过程。
groups.desc_en: Denotes progressive mechanical breakdown of a solid body into fragments, powder, or ruins, contrasting with clean 'cutting' or 'snapping' through sheer pulverizing violence or microscopic wear.
groups.desc_zh: 指固体受外力或研磨而逐步瓦解为碎片、齑粉或废墟的过程，与整齐的‘切割/折断’相比，体现粉碎性破坏、残损与微粒化。
groups.nuance_en: chip: break off tiny surface fragments or flakes (paint / tooth / china) · splinter: shatter along grain into sharp, jagged needle-like shards (bone / wood / windshield) · shatter: burst violently into countless unrecoverable pieces (glass / silence / illusions) · smash: violently destroy with direct crushing or concussive force (window / barrier / records) · grind down: wear away into fine powder or exhaustion through persistent abrasion (wheat / tools / resistance)
groups.nuance_zh: chip: 边角微损脱落或磕出小口 (paint / tooth / china) · splinter: 顺着纹理裂成尖锐刺状残片 (bone / wood / windshield) · shatter: 脆性材料遭遇重击炸裂成碎渣 (glass / silence / illusions) · smash: 强力砸烂或猛力撞成稀烂 (window / barrier / records) · grind down: 经年累月研磨成粉，或在持续消耗战中磨灭 (wheat / tools / resistance)

groups.name: Frame & Word Communication · 措辞与表达形式 (Phrase, Couch, Formulate)
groups.tip: 斟酌字句将思想转化为言辞

items.def_en: (+ adv./prep.) to express something in a specified manner or words
items.ex_en: To put it simply, our department cannot afford such an expensive software upgrade.
items.ex_zh: 简单来说，我们部门无法承担如此昂贵的软件升级费用。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Communicate or express thoughts and messages clearly and effectively
items.ex_en: He used simple analogies to put across complex scientific concepts.
items.ex_zh: 他运用简单的打比方，将复杂的科学概念表达得清晰易懂。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Formulate or state something in clear, unambiguous, and explicit detail
items.ex_en: You don't need to spell out every detail; we get the general idea.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要把每个细节都阐释得那么细，我们明白大意。

items.def_en: to select and arrange words carefully to communicate a thought
items.ex_en: The lawyer carefully worded the formal statement to avoid any legal misinterpretation.
items.ex_zh: 律师字斟句酌地措辞这份正式声明，以避免任何法律上的误解。

items.def_zh: 用言语表达，措辞；划分乐句
items.def_en: 1. To express something in words, especially in a particular style. 2. (music) To divide or group musical notes into melodic units.
items.ex_en: She phrased her polite criticism very gently so as not to offend anyone.
items.ex_zh: 她非常委婉地措辞了自己礼貌的批评，以免冒犯到任何人。

items.def_zh: 用……方式表达，以……措辞；低放（长矛等）；蹲伏
items.def_en: To express or state something in a specified style or manner of words.
items.ex_en: The diplomat couched the stern ultimatum in polite and carefully measured bureaucratic language.
items.ex_zh: 外交官用礼貌而极有分寸的官样辞令表达了严正的最后通牒。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Frame or present words, facts, or ideas attractively to disguise an unpleasant truth
items.ex_en: You don't need to dress up; casual clothes are fine for the party.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要盛装打扮，去参加聚会穿便装就行。
items.ex2_en: She decided to dress up the plain dining table with colorful flowers.
items.ex2_zh: 她决定用色彩斑斓的鲜花将朴素的餐桌装饰一番。

items.def_zh: （以特定视角或方式）构思表达
items.def_en: to express or present an idea, statement, or question in a specific way
items.ex_en: The campaign manager framed the controversial economic policy as an investment in families.
items.ex_zh: 竞选经理将这项颇具争议的经济政策构思表述为对家庭的投资。

items.def_zh: 重新阐述，改换措辞表达；重构，改制
items.def_en: To express or state a plan, idea, or theory again in a different or clearer way.
items.ex_en: The professor asked the confused student to reformulate his original thesis question clearly.
items.ex_zh: 教授让那位困惑的学生把最初的论文问题重新清晰地阐述一遍。

items.def_en: 1. To express thoughts, feelings, or opinions in words. 2. To utter sounds or sing with the voice.
items.ex_en: The employees finally gathered enough courage to vocalize their serious safety concerns aloud.
items.ex_zh: 员工们终于鼓起足够的勇气，大声说出了他们对安全的严重担忧。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame focus on the deliberate selection, packaging, or stylistic styling of words to convey a specific sentiment or tone, ranging from neutral articulation to highly cautious or evasive phrasing.
groups.summary_zh: 强调刻意选择特定言辞、语气或结构来包装与阐述想法。
groups.desc_en: Denotes shaping linguistic content through strategic tone, rhetorical packaging, or structural clarity, contrasting with raw 'saying' through calculated rhetorical design.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过特定的措辞语气、修辞包装或逻辑结构来塑造表达效果，与随口‘说话’相比，强调有心机的语言修饰与框架搭建。
