items.ex_zh: 每当微风拂过，门廊上精致的玻璃风铃便会发出清脆的鸣响。
items.ex2_en: The clocktower chimes the exact hour every morning across the quiet square.
items.ex2_zh: 钟楼每天早晨都会在寂静的广场上敲响准点报时。

items.def_zh: 发出呼呼声，发出嗡嗡声
items.def_en: To make a continuous, low, rapid buzzing or humming sound.
items.ex_en: The computer's internal cooling fan began to whir loudly under the heavy load.
items.ex_zh: 在高负荷运转下，电脑的内部散热风扇开始大声呼呼作响。

items.def_en: to sound loudly and resonantly, especially of bells or chimes
items.ex_en: Joyous cathedral bells peal out across the tranquil valley to announce the royal wedding.
items.ex_zh: 欢快的大教堂钟声在宁静的山谷中回荡响起，宣告皇室婚礼的举行。

items.def_en: to emit a loud, clear, resonant metallic or bell-like sound that carries through an area
items.ex_en: A single gunshot rang out through the frosty morning mist, startling the birds.
items.ex_zh: 一声清脆的枪响划破清晨的霜雾，惊飞了群鸟。

items.def_en: to sound a large bell slowly and regularly, typically for a funeral or disaster
items.ex_en: The bronze church bell continued to toll mournfully for the fallen village elder.
items.ex_zh: 青铜教堂钟沉重而哀伤地长鸣，悼念逝去的村中长者。
items.ex2_en: The monk tolled the heavy iron bell to signal the morning prayers.
items.ex2_zh: 僧侣敲响沉重的铁钟以宣告晨祷的开始。

items.def_zh: （使）发出叮当刺耳声；激怒，使烦躁
items.def_en: 1. To make, or cause to make, an unpleasant, ringing metallic sound. 2. To make someone feel nervous, anxious, or irritated.
items.ex_en: The prison guard's heavy metal keys jangle loudly at his hip with every step.
items.ex_zh: 狱警腰间沉重的金属钥匙随着他每迈出一步都发出刺耳的叮当声。
items.ex2_en: She jangled her metal bracelets impatiently while waiting for the elevator.
items.ex2_zh: 她在等电梯时不耐烦地晃动着金属手镯叮当作响。

items.def_zh: 鸣丧钟；敲响（缓慢低沉的钟声）；预示灭亡
items.def_en: To ring slowly and solemnly, especially for a funeral; to sound as an omen of death or disaster.
items.ex_en: The distant bell began to knell across the darkened moor, foreboding inevitable doom.
items.ex_zh: 远方的丧钟在昏暗的荒原上空凄凉敲响，预示着无法逃脱的厄运。

items.def_zh: （使）发出拨弦声，（使）发出嘣的震颤声；带鼻音讲话
items.def_en: 1. To make, or cause something to make, a sharp vibrating metallic or string-like sound. 2. To speak with a strong nasal sound.
items.ex_en: The archer released his bowstring, letting it twang sharply in the crisp air.
items.ex_zh: 弓箭手松开弓弦，在清冽的空气中发出一声尖锐的嘣响。
items.ex2_en: He twanged the loose guitar string to test its acoustic pitch.
items.ex2_zh: 他拨弄了一下松弛的吉他弦，测试其声音音高。

items.def_zh: 叮当响；发出高亢金属声
items.def_en: to make a loud, resonant metallic sound like that of hard metal hitting metal
items.ex_en: Heavy iron pipes clang violently against each other during the sudden warehouse collapse.
items.ex_zh: 在仓库突发的坍塌中，沉重的铁管猛烈相撞，发出巨响。
items.ex2_en: The angry chef clanged the heavy copper pots against the stove.
items.ex2_zh: 愤怒的厨师把沉重的铜锅撞在炉灶上发出当啷声。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the emission of resonant, plucking, clashing, or solemn acoustic vibrations, typical of bells, metallic objects, or vibrating cords.
groups.summary_zh: 发出琴弦拨动声、金属碰撞的刺耳脆响或沉重钟鸣声。
groups.desc_en: Denotes emitting or producing clear, reverberating acoustic vibrations characteristic of struck metal or bells, contrasting with dull thuds or continuous noise by emphasizing tonal resonance, metallic crispness, or solemn persistence.
groups.desc_zh: 指发出敲击金属或钟体时特有的清脆、回荡声响，与沉闷撞击声或杂乱噪音相比，强调音色清透、金属质感与鸣响回荡。
groups.nuance_en: chime: emit clear, harmonious, bell-like musical strokes (clock / bells / melody) · peal out: ring forth in loud, glorious, joyous reverberations (church bells / laughter / thunder) · toll: strike a heavy bell slowly and rhythmically for mourning or warning (death / bell / hour) · jangle: produce an unpleasantly harsh, clashing metallic rattle (keys / harness / nerves) · knell: sound solemnly as a harbinger of death, disaster, or extinction (bell / doom / era)
groups.nuance_zh: chime: 发出清脆悦耳、和弦般的钟乐报时声 (clock / bells / melody) · peal out: 洪亮欢腾、连贯回荡地敲响 (church bells / laughter / thunder) · toll: 缓慢而沉重地规律鸣响以志哀或警示 (death / bell / hour) · jangle: 发出散碎刺耳的金属碰擦碰撞声 (keys / harness / nerves) · knell: 敲响象征死亡、灾劫或终结的丧钟 (bell / doom / era)

groups.name: Restrain & Fetter · 束缚与禁锢 (Fetter, Shackle, Trammel)
groups.tip: 具象化锁链缰绳捆绑与限制自由

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround closely and restrict freedom of movement, action, or growth
items.ex_en: Tall concrete high-rises hem in the historic neighborhood, blocking out most natural sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的混凝土高楼紧紧包围着这片历史街区，挡住了大部分自然阳光。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to restrict someone's freedom of movement, development, or choice through obligations or constraints
items.ex_en: He didn't want to buy a house because he hated being tied down to one location.
items.ex_zh: 他不想买房，因为讨厌被束缚在同一个地方。

items.def_en: to limit or restrict someone's freedom or ability to develop freely
items.ex_en: Archaic regulations continue to trammel the creative freedom of young independent artists.
items.ex_zh: 陈旧过时的规章制度仍在束缚年轻独立艺术家的创作自由。

items.def_zh: 给（马）套上辔头；控制，约束；（因受冒犯而）动怒，昂首表示不悦（bridle at）
items.def_en: 1. To put a bridle on a horse; to control or restrain something. 2. (+ at) to show sudden anger or resentment.
items.ex_en: The seasoned diplomat struggled to bridle his surging indignation during the tense negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的外交官在紧张的谈判中极力克制自己翻腾的怒火。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to fasten securely with chains or restrain tightly so as to prevent movement
items.ex_en: Workers chain down the heavy machinery onto the flatbed truck before highway transport.
items.ex_zh: 在公路运输前，工人们用铁链将重型机械紧紧锁在平板卡车上。

items.def_en: to fasten or confine someone or something securely with a metal chain
items.ex_en: The owner had to chain the vicious guard dog near the warehouse gate.
items.ex_zh: 主人不得不把那只凶狠的看门狗用铁链拴在仓库大门旁。

items.def_zh: 给……戴上手铐（或脚镣）；束缚，阻碍
items.def_en: 1. To fasten someone's hands or feet with shackles. 2. To severely restrict someone's freedom or prevent them from acting freely.
items.ex_en: Excessive bureaucratic paperwork threatens to shackle the startup's ability to innovate quickly.
items.ex_zh: 繁冗的官僚程序势必会严重束缚该初创公司快速创新的能力。

items.def_zh: 以契约束缚（做学徒或仆役）
items.def_en: (historical) To bind someone by a signed contract to work for another person as an apprentice or servant.
items.ex_en: In seventeenth-century England, impoverished families would often indenture their sons to blacksmiths.
items.ex_zh: 在十七世纪的英格兰，贫困家庭经常以契约形式将儿子送给铁匠做学徒。

items.def_en: 1. To restrict someone's movement by chaining their feet. 2. To restrict someone's freedom, choice, or development.
items.ex_en: Rigid dogmas should never fetter the human intellect in its pursuit of truth.
items.ex_zh: 僵化的教条绝不应当束缚人类探索真理的心智。

items.def_en: to put handcuffs on someone, or severely restrict their freedom to act
items.ex_en: Strict financial penalties will severely manacle the administration's capacity to execute vital reforms.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的财政惩罚将极大地束缚当局推行关键改革的能力。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe restricting a person's liberty, action, or development through physical bonds, legal contracts, or figurative constraints.
groups.summary_zh: 通过实体枷锁、契约或抽象障碍剥夺自由并限制行动。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame evoke the physical or legal imposition of bonds, chains, or confining perimeters, contrasting with neutral 'restrict' by emphasizing oppressive, movement-crippling encumbrance.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架根植于链条锁具、刑具或狭窄围栏的具象压制意象，与中性的“限制/阻止”相比，极力强调使行动力彻底瘫痪或自由度严重受缚的压迫感。
groups.nuance_en: shackle: heavy mechanical or legal immobilization (suspects / industry / growth) · trammel: subtle systemic or procedural impediment (freedom / progress / innovation) · hem in: spatial or strategic confinement on all sides (troops / choices / development) · bridle: exerting rein-like control or curbing impulses (passions / spending / ambition) · tie down: anchoring or overcommitting resources so they lack mobility (capital / forces / time)
groups.nuance_zh: shackle: 沉重机械或法律维度的硬性锁闭与桎梏 (suspects / industry / growth) · trammel: 规则、制度或细碎程序造成的束缚牵绊 (freedom / progress / innovation) · hem in: 空间或战略态势上的四面合围逼仄 (troops / choices / development) · bridle: 勒马收缰般的节制与遏抑 (passions / spending / ambition) · tie down: 牵制、锚定资源使其丧失调动灵活度 (capital / forces / time)

groups.name: Retreat & Fall Back · 撤退与后撤 (Retreat, Withdraw, Fall back)
groups.tip: 脱离交战主动向后撤离

items.def_en: to move away from an enemy, danger, or difficult situation
items.ex_en: The infantry received urgent orders to retreat before the bridge was destroyed.
items.ex_zh: 步兵部队接到紧急命令，在大桥被摧毁之前迅速后撤。

items.def_en: to retreat or move back to a safer or secondary defensive position
items.ex_en: The troops were ordered to fall back to fortified positions.
items.ex_zh: 部队接到命令，撤退到坚固的防御阵地。

items.def_en: [I/T] to withdraw troops or forces from a forward position, or to move backward
items.ex_en: The commanding general decided to pull back his frontline divisions to regroup safely.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官决定撤回前线部队，以便安全地重整旗鼓。
items.ex2_en: The frightened kitten pulled back into the corner when footsteps approached.
items.ex2_zh: 当脚步声临近时，受惊的小猫缩回了角落。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ of) to evacuate or completely withdraw forces, personnel, or support from an area
items.ex_en: The multinational corporation decided to pull out of the unprofitable market.
items.ex_zh: 该跨国公司决定退出这一无利可图的市场。

items.def_en: to retreat backwards slowly away from a person, threat, or dangerous situation
items.ex_en: The frightened hiker began to back away slowly from the aggressive black bear.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的徒步者开始慢慢向后退，远离那只具有攻击性的黑熊。

items.def_en: to retreat from an active confrontation, dangerous encounter, or position
items.ex_en: The bouncer warned the aggressive customer to back off before trouble started.
items.ex_zh: 保镖警告那名挑衅的顾客在事态恶化前赶紧退后。

items.def_en: to move back or withdraw from a position or engagement gradually
items.ex_en: The weary defenders began to fall away as the enemy breach widened rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 随着敌方的突破口迅速扩大，疲惫的守军开始逐渐向后溃退。

items.def_zh: 撤退，撤离，离开；撤回，撤销；取款
items.def_en: 1. To pull back, retreat, or move away from an area or conflict. 2. To take back, remove, or retract something. 3. To take money out of a bank account.
items.ex_en: The diplomat chose to withdraw his controversial proposal after intense international criticism.
items.ex_zh: 在遭受强烈的国际批评后，该外交官选择撤回这项争议性提案。
items.ex2_en: The exhausted soldiers withdrew slowly behind the secure defensive stone barricades.
items.ex2_zh: 疲惫的士兵们慢慢撤退到坚固的石质防御路障后面。

items.def_zh: 撤回，撤退；退出；提（款）（withdraw的过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past participle of withdraw; to move back or away from a place or situation, remove, or take money out.
items.ex_en: The ambassador was withdrawn from his post following the sudden diplomatic breakdown.
items.ex_zh: 由于外交关系的突发破裂，该大使已被从驻地召回。
items.ex2_en: The retreat order having arrived, the infantry had withdrawn before dawn break.
items.ex2_zh: 撤退命令下达后，步兵在破晓前就已撤退。

items.def_zh: 撤回，撤退；退出；提（款）（withdraw的过去式）
items.def_en: 1. Past tense of withdraw; to move back or away from a place or situation, remove, or take money out.
items.ex_en: The armored division withdrew twenty miles to establish a fortified defensive perimeter.
items.ex_zh: 装甲师向后撤离了二十英里，以建立坚固的防御圈。
items.ex2_en: The anxious bank customer withdrew five hundred dollars from the automated teller.
items.ex2_zh: 焦虑的银行客户从自动取款机里取出了五百美元。

groups.summary_en: An agent deliberately moves backward or departs from an active area of engagement, danger, or social participation. 'Withdraw' serves as the formal baseline, whereas 'retreat' conveys forced movement under threat.
groups.summary_zh: 指从危险前线、战场或特定场所主动或被迫向后撤离离开。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame designate deliberate backward locomotion to disengage from danger, confrontation, or untenable ground, contrasting with accidental 'stumble' or neutral 'leave' via its defensive tactical logic.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架表达从危险、冲突或不利阵地主动向后撤离以图保全的战术行为，与单纯的“离开”相比，强调面对敌意或高压时的防御性规避与空间回退。
groups.nuance_en: retreat: formal tactical or psychological backward movement under pressure (troops / army / glacier) · withdraw: orderly, often institutional disengagement or recall (ambassador / forces / funding) · fall back: defensive retrograde step to secondary positions (defenders / lines / squad) · pull out: complete extraction of an entire unit or commitment (contingent / investor / sponsor) · back off: psychological or interpersonal de-escalation by stepping away (critics / police / bully)
groups.nuance_zh: retreat: 承受压力时的战术后撤或心理退缩 (troops / army / glacier) · withdraw: 有秩序的、制度化的撤出或召回 (ambassador / forces / funding) · fall back: 遭遇强阻时退守次级防线的渐进后撤 (defenders / lines / squad) · pull out: 整体性拔出、撤资或全面脱离干预 (contingent / investor / sponsor) · back off: 人际交涉或对抗中的主动示弱、让步与降温 (critics / police / bully)

groups.name: Reveal & Uncover · 揭露与展露 (Disclose, Reveal, Unveil)
groups.tip: 展现公开隐藏的事物

items.def_en: to make known something that was previously secret or unknown
items.ex_en: The newly released audit will reveal massive financial discrepancies within the organization.
items.ex_zh: 最新发布的审计报告将揭示该机构内部存在的巨额财务出入。

items.def_en: to uncover harmful secrets, dishonest acts, or scandalous behavior
items.ex_en: Investigative journalists worked tirelessly to expose the corrupt practices of corporate executives.
items.ex_zh: 调查记者们孜孜不倦地工作，以曝光企业高管的腐败行径。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make qualities, hidden details, or obscured facts visible or clearly noticed
items.ex_en: Clever questioning helped the prosecutor bring out crucial contradictions in the suspect's testimony.
items.ex_zh: 巧妙的盘问帮助检察官揭示出嫌疑人证词中至关重要的矛盾。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to disclose a secret, true identity, or confidential information carelessly or unintentionally
items.ex_en: His nervous glance almost gave away their hidden location to the searchers.
items.ex_zh: 他紧张的一瞥差点向搜寻者暴露了他们的隐蔽地点。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reveal or disclose a piece of confidential information or news
items.ex_en: A careless employee accidentally let out confidential details about the upcoming merger.
items.ex_zh: 一名粗心的员工不慎泄露了关于即将进行的合并的机密细节。

items.def_en: To make secret, new, or private information known publicly; to reveal.
items.ex_en: The pharmaceutical company is legally obligated to disclose all known side effects.
items.ex_zh: 制药公司在法律上有义务向公众披露所有已知的副作用。

items.def_zh: 公布，推出；揭幕，揭开面纱
items.def_en: To show or introduce a new plan, product, or system to the public for the first time; to remove a cover or veil from something.
items.ex_en: The tech giant will unveil its next flagship smartphone at tomorrow's conference.
items.ex_zh: 这家科技巨头将在明天的发布会上推出其下一代旗舰智能手机。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To show something clearly through signs or actions. 2. (often 'manifest itself') To appear or become evident.
items.ex_en: Severe economic distress will often manifest through widespread civil unrest and strikes.
items.ex_zh: 严重的经济危机往往会通过广泛的民众骚乱和罢工显现出来。

items.def_en: to give away private or secret information to others
items.ex_en: The former employee refused to divulge proprietary trade secrets to competing firms.
items.ex_zh: 这名前雇员拒绝向竞争对手公司泄露专有商业机密。

items.def_en: to reveal the true character or identity of someone or something hidden
items.ex_en: A covert investigation finally helped unmask the mastermind behind the fraudulent scheme.
items.ex_zh: 一项秘密调查最终帮助识破了这起诈骗阴谋幕后黑手的真面目。

groups.summary_en: Agents make previously hidden, confidential, or obscure information, facts, or objects visible and known to the public. Differences lie primarily in formality, ceremony, and whether tangible items or abstract secrets are revealed.
groups.summary_zh: 将隐藏、保密的信息或遮蔽的实物公布于众或显露出来。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame invoke the removal of physical coverings, veils, or confidentiality seals to bring covert reality into sight, contrasting with accidental 'display' through intentional lifting of secrecy.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架以掀开遮蔽物、面纱或解除保密机制为隐喻，与一般的“展现/陈列”相比，强调消除人工掩盖或未知状态，使隐秘真相大白于天下。
groups.nuance_en: reveal: dynamic uncovering of previously hidden truths or features (identity / secret / plot) · disclose: formal release of proprietary or regulated facts (records / assets / information) · unveil: ceremonial or staged first-time public presentation (monument / prototype / plan) · expose: unmasking corruption, danger, or vulnerability (fraud / scandal / corruption) · manifest: tangible physical or behavioral outward emergence of an inward state (symptoms / discontent / power)
groups.nuance_zh: reveal: 揭示、展现原本不为人知的真相或神貌 (identity / secret / plot) · disclose: 依规、正式向公众或受众披露保密事实 (records / assets / information) · unveil: 仪式性或阶段性地隆重初次展示 (monument / prototype / plan) · expose: 撕去伪装以曝光丑闻、黑幕或脆弱点 (fraud / scandal / corruption) · manifest: 内在潜伏状态或情绪在外部显性流露 (symptoms / discontent / power)

groups.name: Roll & Wheel Around · 翻滚与转向 (Turn, Roll, Round)
groups.tip: 绕轴或向不同方向转

items.def_en: to move forward smoothly on wheels or by continuous rolling rotation
items.ex_en: The heavily loaded freight cars roll along the rusted railway tracks steadily.
items.ex_zh: 满载货物的车厢在生锈的铁轨上平稳地滚滚向前行驶。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to turn over completely onto one's side, back, or face by rotational movement
items.ex_en: The tired dog decided to roll over onto its back for belly rubs.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的小狗翻了个身仰面躺着，想要让人给它揉肚子。

items.def_zh: 绕过，拐过；使成圆形；（使）变圆；四舍五入
items.def_en: 1. To go or pass around a corner, curve, or obstacle. 2. To make something round or become round. 3. (math) To round up or down to the nearest whole number or unit.
items.ex_en: The sleek racing car rounded the sharp hairpin corner with breathtaking speed.
items.ex_zh: 那辆流线型赛车以惊人的速度绕过了那个陡峭的发卡弯。

items.def_en: to pivot or turn around suddenly and sharply in a curving arc
items.ex_en: Hearing footsteps behind him, the guard wheeled around with his weapon drawn.
items.ex_zh: 听到身后传来的脚步声，守卫猛然转身并拔出了武器。
items.ex2_en: The driver quickly wheeled the heavy cart around to dodge oncoming pedestrians.
items.ex2_zh: 司机迅速转动沉重的手推车以避开迎面走来的行人。

items.def_zh: 旋转，转动；转弯，转向；转变，变成
items.def_en: 1. To move in a circular motion around an axis, or cause something to do so. 2. To change direction or orientation. 3. To change state or condition.
items.ex_en: The massive water wheel continues to turn slowly under the rushing mountain stream.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的水车在湍急的山溪冲刷下继续缓缓旋转。
items.ex2_en: She slowly turned the ornate brass key inside the rusty old lock.
items.ex2_zh: 她慢慢转动生锈旧锁里的华丽黄铜钥匙。

items.def_zh: 翻滚，滚动；使滚动；卷起；摇摆
items.def_en: 1. To move by turning over and over on an axis or along a surface, or cause to do so. 2. To curl or wrap into a tube or ball shape.
items.ex_en: Giant granite boulders roll down the steep mountain slope after the landslide.
items.ex_zh: 山体滑坡发生后，巨大的花岗岩巨石沿着陡峭的山坡翻滚而下。
items.ex2_en: The excited children roll the giant snowball across the snowy park lawn.
items.ex2_zh: 兴奋的孩子们在覆雪的公园草坪上滚着巨大的雪球。

items.def_en: [I/T] To turn around quickly or fly in wide sweeping circles
items.ex_en: A flock of startled seagulls wheeled gracefully against the stormy evening sky.
items.ex_zh: 一群受惊的海鸥在暴风雨来临前的夜空中优美地盘旋转向。
items.ex2_en: The nurse wheeled the hospital stretcher down the long sterile corridor carefully.
items.ex2_zh: 护士小心翼翼地把医院担架床推过漫长无菌的走廊。

items.def_en: To change direction suddenly or deviate from a straight course
items.ex_en: The reckless driver suddenly veered into oncoming traffic to avoid the fallen tree.
items.ex_zh: 那名鲁莽的司机为了避开倒下的树木，猛然变向驶入逆行车道。

items.def_en: [I/T] To change direction abruptly, especially in order to avoid an obstacle
items.ex_en: She had to swerve hard to the right to miss a stray dog.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不猛地向右急打方向盘，以避开一只流浪狗。
items.ex2_en: The panicked motorist swerved his pickup truck across three empty traffic lanes.
items.ex2_zh: 惊慌失措的车主将皮卡车猛然转向横跨了三条空车道。

items.def_en: To perform a rolling movement turning heel over head
items.ex_en: The agile gymnast managed to somersault across the mat with remarkable precision.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的体操运动员精准利落地在垫子上完成了连续空翻动作。

groups.summary_en: An entity changes bodily facing, curves along an arc, or translates forward across a surface by continuous rolling rotation.
groups.summary_zh: 自身翻滚、绕弯转向或沿表面转动前行。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote rotational, curvilinear, or swiveling kinetic motion, contrasting with linear 'move' through continuous angular displacement or revolution on an axis.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描述物体围绕自身轴心滚动、旋转或在前进中划出弧形轨迹的运动，与单纯的“直线移动”相比，凸显角度转换与圆周/滚翻动力学特征。
groups.nuance_en: roll: continuous axial tumbling or revolving over a surface (boulder / dice / carriage) · wheel: swift pivoting or arcing turn by a massed body or wheeled object (birds / horses / chariot) · veer: sudden erratic deviation from a heading (vehicle / wind / policy) · round: executing a smooth sweep along a curved corner or perimeter (cape / bend / corner) · turn: fundamental rotational change of posture or trajectory (doorknob / head / key)
groups.nuance_zh: roll: 沿表面连续翻滚或轴向旋转前进 (boulder / dice / carriage) · wheel: 群体或车辆整齐迅疾地绕轴回旋、盘旋打转 (birds / horses / chariot) · veer: 偏航、突然改变原定路线或风向/策略转向 (vehicle / wind / policy) · round: 紧贴弧形边缘绕行拐过 (cape / bend / corner) · turn: 最基础的转向、改变朝向或扭动机构 (doorknob / head / key)

groups.name: Rule & Dominate · 统治与控制 (Govern, Control, Monopolize)
groups.tip: 国家治理与强权统辖

items.def_en: To control or maintain the rate or operation of a system by rules
items.ex_en: The federal agency exists to regulate interstate commerce and ensure fair competition.
items.ex_zh: 该联邦机构的存在旨在监管州际商业活动并确保公平竞争。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to be in formal control of or exercise dominant authority over an organization, state, or proceeding
items.ex_en: The senior justice was appointed to preside over the complex antitrust trial.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深法官被指派主持这场复杂的反垄断案件审理。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to exercise sovereign authority, dominion, or administrative control over people or a country
items.ex_en: The monarch sought to rule over the fractured realm with an iron fist.
items.ex_zh: 这位君主企图以铁腕手段统辖这个分崩离析的王国。

items.def_zh: 统治，统辖，控制；操纵；抑制
items.def_en: To exercise authoritative power or dominance over an area or group; to manage, direct, or restrain something.
items.ex_en: Rebel forces fought fiercely to control the strategic seaport and its supply routes.
items.ex_zh: 叛军激烈交战，试图控制该战略性海港及其补给线。

items.def_en: 1. To conduct the policy and affairs of a state or organization. 2. To control or directly influence something.
items.ex_en: Strict constitutional principles must govern every major policy decision made by parliament.
items.ex_zh: 严格的宪法原则必须支配和指导议会做出的每一项重大政策决定。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to act in an arrogant and domineering manner toward someone
items.ex_en: He loved to lord it over his junior colleagues whenever management was away.
items.ex_zh: 每当管理层不在时，他就喜欢在初级同事面前作威作福。

items.def_zh: 统治，治理；裁定，判定；支配
items.def_en: 1. To exercise authority or control over a country, people, or group. 2. To make an authoritative or legal decision.
items.ex_en: The high court is expected to rule on the constitutionality of the ban.
items.ex_zh: 预计最高法院将对该禁令是否符合宪法做出裁定。

items.def_en: [I/T] To exert a commanding, preeminent, or overbearing influence over others
items.ex_en: Two major supermarket chains continue to dominate the country's entire retail sector.
items.ex_zh: 两家大型连锁超市继续主宰着整个国家的零售行业。

items.def_en: To have or take exclusive control over a trade, market, conversation, or activity so that others cannot share.
items.ex_en: The state-owned enterprise was accused of trying to monopolize the national telecommunications industry.
items.ex_zh: 这家国有企业被指控企图垄断全国的电信产业。

items.def_en: To bring completely under domination or control, especially by military conquest
items.ex_en: The ruthless warlord invaded the neighboring valleys to subjugate the local tribes.
items.ex_zh: 这位残暴的军阀入侵邻近山谷，意图彻底征服当地部落。

groups.summary_en: Actors exercise institutional power, regulatory direction, or overwhelming hegemony over subjects, states, or markets, escalating from standard administration to absolute subjugation.
groups.summary_zh: 行使治理、支配或垄断性权力，由制度监管升级至绝对主宰。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote the exercise of sovereign command, administrative oversight, or asymmetric power over subjects, contrasting with 'influence' by its enforceable structural hierarchy.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架聚焦掌握最高支配权、管辖权或非对称控制力的施权行为，与温和的“影响/建议”相比，强调强制性的层级管辖、指令服从与垄断主导地位。
groups.nuance_en: govern: structured, legitimate institutional administration (nation / province / affairs) · rule: sovereign command or sustained hegemony (empire / people / kingdom) · dominate: overwhelming competitive or psychological preeminence (market / conversation / scene) · preside over: formal ceremonial or procedural chairmanship over an era or body (meeting / transition / tribunal) · lord it over: arrogant, patronizing assertion of petty superiority (peers / siblings / subordinates)
groups.nuance_zh: govern: 依法、有建制地良性治理与行使政权 (nation / province / affairs) · rule: 君临天下式的最高主权统治或长久霸权 (empire / people / kingdom) · dominate: 在竞争或心理场域占据压倒性主导与垄断优势 (market / conversation / scene) · preside over: 居于主导主持地位以把控全场或见证变迁 (meeting / transition / tribunal) · lord it over: 趾高气扬、作威作福地向他人耍官威或摆架子 (peers / siblings / subordinates)

groups.name: Rumble & Resonate · 轰鸣与共振 (Rumble, Drone, Thunder)
groups.tip: 低沉震颤激起空气共鸣

items.def_zh: 发嗡嗡声；发出低沉轻微的哼鸣
items.def_en: to make a low, steady, continuous sound like that of a bee or electrical transformer
items.ex_en: The large electrical generator continued to hum steadily in the quiet basement.
items.ex_zh: 大型发电机在寂静的地下室里持续发出低沉而平稳的嗡鸣声。

items.def_en: to emit a continuous, monotonous, low-frequency buzzing or humming sound
items.ex_en: Old ceiling fans drone on overhead, doing little to ease the suffocating heat.
items.ex_zh: 老旧的吊扇在头顶上持续单调地嗡嗡响着，对缓解闷热无济于事。

items.def_en: to make a steady, resonant, low-pitched mechanical vibration or acoustic hum
items.ex_en: The massive factory turbines hum along smoothly throughout the uninterrupted night shift.
items.ex_zh: 庞大的工厂涡轮机在整个无休的夜班中平稳低沉地运转嗡鸣。

items.def_zh: 发出嗡嗡声，作轰鸣声；忙乱，充满喧闹声；按蜂鸣器呼叫
items.def_en: 1. To make a continuous low humming or vibrating sound like a bee or machinery. 2. To be filled with excitement, activity, or continuous chatter. 3. To signal or call someone with a buzzer.
items.ex_en: Scores of worker bees buzz noisily around the hive in the midday heat.
items.ex_zh: 成群的工蜂在正午的酷热中围着蜂箱嗡嗡作响。

items.def_zh: 发出低沉的嗡嗡声，轰鸣；单调低沉地讲，喋喋不休
items.def_en: 1. To make a continuous low, dull humming or vibrating sound. 2. (+ on) To speak for a long time in a monotonous, boring voice.
items.ex_en: High-voltage transmission lines drone softly over the deserted rural fields at dusk.
items.ex_zh: 高压输电线在黄昏荒芜的田野上空持续发出低沉微弱的轰鸣声。

items.def_zh: 发出隆隆声，发轰鸣声；缓缓低沉地移动
items.def_en: To make a continuous, deep, low rolling sound like thunder or heavy vehicles.
items.ex_en: Massive military trucks rumble down the unpaved road, shaking the nearby cottages.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的军用卡车在未铺砌的道路上轰隆驶过，震颤着附近的村舍。

items.def_en: to produce a deep, loud, resonant reverberating sound that travels widely
items.ex_en: The church bells boomed out across the valley, signaling the start of the festival.
items.ex_zh: 教堂的钟声在山谷间轰响回荡，宣告着节日的开始。

items.def_zh: 发出低沉有力的隆隆声；巨响
items.def_en: to emit a deep, hollow, resonant and prolonged sound
items.ex_en: Thunder began to boom in the distance as the dark storm clouds gathered overhead.
items.ex_zh: 当头顶阴暗的暴风云聚拢时，远处开始传来低沉的隆隆雷声。

items.def_zh: 轰隆作响；打雷；雷鸣般呼喊，怒斥
items.def_en: 1. To make a loud, deep rumbling sound like thunder. 2. (impersonal) To produce thunder during a storm. 3. To speak, shout, or move with great noise and force.
items.ex_en: Heavy artillery thundered across the plains, rattling windows in the nearby abandoned village.
items.ex_zh: 重炮在平原上轰隆作响，震得附近废弃村庄的窗户直晃。

items.def_en: to echo back or resonate repeatedly through a physical space or medium
items.ex_en: His deep voice reverberated through the vaulted corridors of the ancient stone cathedral.
items.ex_zh: 他低沉的嗓音在古老石制大教堂的穹顶走廊中久久激荡回旋。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe producing or reverberating with a continuous, low-pitched, vibratory sound. They vary along the auditory spectrum from monotonous low-frequency hums and mechanical buzzing to earth-shaking, reverberating low-frequency thunder.
groups.summary_zh: 发出或伴随低沉、连续且具振动感的轰鸣声或嗡嗡声。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame evoke sustained low-frequency acoustic vibrations and resonant deep noises, contrasting with sharp 'bang' by their continuous, visceral, or reverberating quality.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描摹低频震颤、沉闷回响或持续共振的声学特征，与清脆突兀的“爆响”不同，强调声音的厚重、绵延不绝以及穿透肉体的震荡感。
groups.nuance_en: rumble: deep, heavy rolling acoustic vibration (thunder / stomach / artillery) · drone: flat, hypnotic, mechanical continuous hum (engine / bagpipe / speaker) · boom: resonant, explosive, highly authoritative blast of sound (cannon / voice / surf) · buzz: rapid, high-frequency vibratory friction or social murmur (bees / neon / crowd) · hum: steady, gentle low-pitch harmonic vibration (generator / wires / bee)
groups.nuance_zh: rumble: 沉重沉闷、连绵滚动的低频声浪 (thunder / stomach / artillery) · drone: 机械、单调、催眠般的连续嗡鸣 (engine / bagpipe / speaker) · boom: 洪亮深邃、极具穿透力与威严的轰鸣回响 (cannon / voice / surf) · buzz: 高频短促的颤动杂音或沸沸扬扬的人声低语 (bees / neon / crowd) · hum: 平稳轻柔的工频微震或闭嘴沉吟嗡嗡声 (generator / wires / bee)

groups.name: Rupture & Explode · 爆裂与爆炸 (Burst, Rupture, Explode, Blast)
groups.tip: 压力骤增引发猛烈爆炸破裂

items.def_zh: 发出砰声爆裂；啪地爆开
items.def_en: [I/T] to make a light explosive sound, or to burst with a sharp popping noise
items.ex_en: The child watched the bubble drift upward until it popped with a tiny sound.
items.ex_zh: 孩子看着泡泡往上飘，直到它啪的一声轻响爆开了。
items.ex2_en: The mischievous boy popped the red party balloon with a sharp pin.
items.ex2_zh: 淘气的男孩用一根锋利的别针刺破了红色的派对气球。

items.def_en: [I/T] to break apart or burst open under internal pressure or physical stress
items.ex_en: Extreme water pressure caused the main underground pipe to rupture without warning yesterday morning.
items.ex_zh: 极大的水压导致地下主管道在昨天清晨毫无预警地破裂了。
items.ex2_en: Excessive hydraulic pressure ruptured the heavy steel pipeline during structural stress testing.
items.ex2_zh: 在结构压力测试中，过大的液压冲破了厚重的钢管。

items.def_en: [I/T] to break violently into many small pieces through explosive force or sharp impact
items.ex_en: The shockwave from the detonation shattered every glass window on the entire street.
items.ex_zh: 爆炸产生的冲击波震碎了整条街上的每一扇玻璃窗。
items.ex2_en: The delicate crystal vase shattered into tiny shards upon hitting the floor.
items.ex2_zh: 精致的水晶花瓶掉在地上碎成了细小的碎片。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to explode violently or be destroyed by an explosive concussive detonation
items.ex_en: Terrorists attempted to blow up the railway bridge using heavy homemade explosive devices.
items.ex_zh: 恐怖分子企图使用重型自制爆炸装置炸毁那座铁路桥。
items.ex2_en: The pressurized industrial boiler blew up violently, shaking the nearby buildings.
items.ex2_zh: 加压工业锅炉发生剧烈爆炸，震动了附近的建筑物。

items.def_en: to detonate, burst, or explode suddenly with great force
items.ex_en: The old generator suddenly went off with a deafening blast during the storm.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨中，那台老旧发电机突然发出震耳欲聋的巨响爆炸了。

items.def_zh: （使）爆炸，（使）破裂；猛冲，突然出现；突然发作
items.def_en: 1. To break open or apart suddenly and violently, especially from internal pressure. 2. To move or enter somewhere suddenly and with great force.
items.ex_en: The overinflated tire suddenly burst while the truck was speeding down the highway.
items.ex_zh: 卡车在公路上疾驰时，充气过度的轮胎突然爆裂了。
items.ex2_en: The sudden surge of electrical power burst several fluorescent light bulbs.
items.ex2_zh: 突然涌来的电流击爆了几个荧光灯泡。

items.def_en: [I/T] to burst violently and noisily into pieces as a result of chemical reaction or pressure
items.ex_en: Leaking gas caused the entire upper floor of the apartment building to explode.
items.ex_zh: 煤气泄漏导致这栋公寓楼的整个顶层发生了剧烈爆炸。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to shatter or violently disintegrate into pieces by explosive detonation
items.ex_en: The powerful dynamite blast apart the solid rock barrier blocking the tunnel entrance.
items.ex_zh: 威力巨大的炸药炸碎了阻挡隧道入口的坚硬岩壁。
items.ex2_en: The abandoned masonry chimney blasted apart under the powerful lightning strike.
items.ex2_zh: 废弃的砖石烟囱在强烈的雷击下炸成了碎片。

items.def_zh: 炸毁，爆破；发出尖锐强音，轰鸣；猛烈抨击
items.def_en: 1. To blow up or destroy something with explosives. 2. To make a loud, harsh sound or play music very loudly. 3. To criticize someone or something severely.
items.ex_en: Demolition crews plan to blast the dilapidated concrete tower early on Sunday morning.
items.ex_zh: 拆除队计划在周日清晨爆破炸毁那座破旧的混凝土高塔。

items.def_en: [I/T] to trigger or undergo a sudden, extremely violent supersonic shockwave explosion
items.ex_en: Engineers carefully detonated the controlled explosive charge inside the deep mining shaft today.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们今天在深矿井内部小心翼翼地引爆了定向爆破药包。
items.ex2_en: The volatile chemicals detonated unexpectedly under the intense afternoon factory heat.
items.ex2_zh: 易挥发的化学物质在工厂午后的酷热中意外爆炸。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures violent mechanical or explosive disintegration, progressing from internal pressure breaking open a container or skin to high-energy concussive detonations that shatter surroundings.
groups.summary_zh: 从内部压力胀破、开裂递进到剧烈爆炸与强力爆破摧毁。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame capture sudden violent structural failure driven by internal pressure or concussive energy, contrasting with gradual 'crack' through explosive volumetric shattering.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架聚焦由于内压过载或猛烈冲击波导致容器/结构瞬间分崩离析的力学过程，与渐进的“裂开”相比，强调不可逆的爆破性毁伤与空间炸碎。
groups.nuance_en: explode: violent energetic outward blast producing blast waves (bomb / volcano / boiler) · burst: structural failure of skin or container under internal pressure (bubble / balloon / pipe) · rupture: biological or geological structural split and breach (appendix / pipeline / fault) · shatter: violent disintegration of brittle matter into countless shards (glass / mirror / silence) · blow up: high-yield destructive detonation or inflation to destruction (bridge / depot / vehicle)
groups.nuance_zh: explode: 剧烈能量瞬间向外炸开并产生冲击波 (bomb / volcano / boiler) · burst: 容器或薄膜因内压充盈失控而爆裂张开 (bubble / balloon / pipe) · rupture: 生理器官、管道或地壳断层发生裂断破溃 (appendix / pipeline / fault) · shatter: 硬脆材质遭受震荡粉碎性破裂成碎屑 (glass / mirror / silence) · blow up: 使用炸药将实体彻底炸毁摧毁 (bridge / depot / vehicle)

groups.name: Sail & Steam · 航行与游弋
groups.tip: 驾船或依动力在水面行驶

items.def_zh: （轮船等）靠蒸汽动力航行，驶过；蒸（食物）；冒热气
items.def_en: 1. To move or travel across water by means of steam power. 2. To cook food using steam. 3. To give off steam.
items.ex_en: The heavy cargo vessel steamed steadily across the misty bay toward the harbor.
items.ex_zh: 那艘重型货轮借着蒸汽动力稳稳地驶过雾气蒙蒙的海湾，向港口开去。

items.def_en: To travel on water in a boat or ship, or control and direct a boat across water.
items.ex_en: They decided to sail their small wooden sloop around the rugged northern coast.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定驾驶他们的小型木制单桅帆船环绕崎岖的北部海岸航行。

items.def_en: travel smoothly at an unhurried speed by boat or ship, often for pleasure
items.ex_en: The luxury yacht cruised gracefully along the sunlit coast during the afternoon hours.
items.ex_zh: 午后时分，这艘豪华游艇在阳光明媚的海岸边优雅地巡航。

items.def_en: to depart or begin a sea voyage across open water
items.ex_en: The white brigantine sailed off into the horizon as the morning fog lifted.
items.ex_zh: 晨雾散去，那艘白色双桅帆船扬帆启航，消失在天际线上。

items.def_zh: 开足马力前行，全速航行
items.def_en: to travel forward steadily and continuously under engine power across waterways
items.ex_en: Despite the supply chain hiccups, the construction project is steaming ahead.
items.ex_zh: 尽管供应链出现小波折，该建筑工程仍在全力推进。

items.def_en: to leave a port, harbor, or coastal shore and head out to sea
items.ex_en: The brave fishing trawlers put out before sunrise to catch the morning tide.
items.ex_zh: 勇敢的渔船在日出前离港出海，以赶上清晨的潮汐。

items.def_en: go on a long journey, especially by sea or into unfamiliar waters
items.ex_en: The fearless explorers voyaged across uncharted polar seas in search of new lands.
items.ex_zh: 无畏的探险家们远涉重洋穿过未知的极地水域，寻找新的大陆。

items.def_en: direct, steer, or travel through a stretch of water along a planned course
items.ex_en: The experienced captain navigated the narrow channel despite the dense fog and reefs.
items.ex_zh: 尽管有浓雾和暗礁，经验丰富的船长依然顺利穿航了这条狭窄航道。

items.def_zh: 乘汽船航行；以蒸汽机车行进
items.def_en: (dated) To travel or move by means of a steamship.
items.ex_en: The weary travelers opted to steamer down the wide river toward the capital.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的旅人们选择搭乘轮船顺着宽阔的大河航向首都。

items.def_en: (+ between/along) travel regularly over a route, water body, or commercial line
items.ex_en: Ferry boats have plied between the two bustling port cities for over centuries.
items.ex_zh: 数个世纪以来，渡轮一直规律地往返穿梭于这两座繁华港口城市之间。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe large motorized or wind-powered marine vessels traveling over the sea, waterways, or coastal waters, often evoking steady commercial, naval, or passenger passage.
groups.summary_zh: 轮船、帆船等中大型水面船只在江海水域平稳航行、游弋或穿梭。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame portray powered or wind-driven transit across maritime expanses, contrasting with general 'travel' through distinct hydro-navigational mechanics and open-water passage.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描摹利用风帆或引擎动力在水域中长途破浪前行的航道运动，与普通“旅行/移动”相比，凸显鲜明的航海操纵、水体介质与巡洋离岸场景。
groups.nuance_en: sail: wind-propelled or general fluid marine skimming (yacht / ship / fleet) · steam: engine-powered heavy industrial propulsion through water (liner / battleship / tug) · cruise: smooth, unhurried recreational or patrolling passage (liner / warship / yacht) · navigate: tactical charting and guiding through tricky waterways (channel / reefs / river) · voyage: epic, extended passage across immense oceanic distances (oceans / seas / globe)
groups.nuance_zh: sail: 扬帆出海或通用泛指水上乘舟漂移航行 (yacht / ship / fleet) · steam: 依靠蒸汽/内燃重型动力冒烟破浪稳步推进 (liner / battleship / tug) · cruise: 巡航、漫无压力或以巡弋戒备状态在海面游弋 (liner / warship / yacht) · navigate: 观测水情海况、精准辨别方位以引导航路 (channel / reefs / river) · voyage: 史诗般的远洋跨洲长途探险性航海 (oceans / seas / globe)

groups.name: Sap Strength & Undermine · 削弱与损耗 (Weaken, Undermine, Emasculate)
groups.tip: 力量减弱走向衰落

items.def_en: (+ at sth) to gradually diminish, weaken, or undermine an entity's strength, authority, or stability
items.ex_en: Relentless media scandals slowly chipped away at the prime minister's political authority this year.
items.ex_zh: 接连不断的媒体丑闻今年正在逐渐削弱这位首相的政治权威。

items.def_en: [I/T] to gradually destroy or diminish power, confidence, or value over time
items.ex_en: Persistent inflation continues to erode consumer purchasing power across the fragile national economy.
items.ex_zh: 持续的通货膨胀继续在脆弱的国民经济中逐步侵蚀消费者的购买力。
items.ex2_en: The soft sandstone cliffs erode quickly against the crashing ocean waves.
items.ex2_zh: 柔软的砂岩悬崖在海浪的冲击下迅速被侵蚀。

items.def_en: (+ at sth) to gradually destroy, erode, or undermine the integrity or substance of something
items.ex_en: Corrosive saltwater slowly ate away at the steel support beams of the dock.
items.ex_zh: 具有腐蚀性的盐水慢慢侵蚀着码头的钢制支撑梁。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to gradually weaken someone's physical strength, resistance, or structural firmness through sustained pressure
items.ex_en: Persistent negotiations finally wore down the opposition's resistance.
items.ex_zh: 旷日持久的谈判最终瓦解了反对派的抵抗意志。
items.ex2_en: The rubber soles will wear down quickly from running on rough asphalt.
items.ex2_zh: 在粗糙的沥青路面上跑步会导致橡胶鞋底迅速磨损变薄。

items.def_en: To become less strong, powerful, or determined, or to make someone or something less strong.
items.ex_en: Prolonged illness had weakened his physical stamina significantly over the past three months.
items.ex_zh: 长期的疾病在过去三个月里显著削弱了他的体力和精力。
items.ex2_en: Her fragile resolve weakened noticeably as the harsh winter storm dragged on.
items.ex2_zh: 随着严酷的冬季风暴持续蔓延，她脆弱的决心明显动摇了。

items.def_zh: 逐渐削弱，暗中破坏；从根基处破坏
items.def_en: To gradually weaken or damage someone's authority, confidence, or a system.
items.ex_en: Leaked official documents severely undermined the government's credibility regarding the controversial reform policies.
items.ex_zh: 泄露的官方文件严重损害了政府在争议性改革政策方面的公信力。

items.def_zh: 消耗，暗中削弱（精力/力量）
items.def_en: to slowly exhaust or deplete someone's strength, vitality, or resolve
items.ex_en: The sweltering afternoon heat sapped all the construction workers' energy before midday passed.
items.ex_zh: 午后闷热的天气在正午刚过时就耗尽了所有建筑工人的精力。

items.def_en: to severely impair the strength, health, or functioning of an entity
items.ex_en: The sudden economic sanctions rapidly debilitated the small nation's key manufacturing industries.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的经济制裁迅速重创了该小国关键制造业的正常运转。

items.def_zh: 削弱……的力量（或效力）；使丧失男子气概；阉割
items.def_en: (formal) To make a system, law, or idea less effective or powerful; to deprive a man of his male role or identity.
items.ex_en: The proposed legislative amendments effectively emasculate the original environmental protection regulations entirely.
items.ex_zh: 拟议的立法修正案实质上彻底削弱了原环境保护法规的效力。

items.def_zh: 使极度衰弱，使软弱无力
items.def_en: to make someone or something extremely weak, frail, or devoid of energy
items.ex_en: Years of severe malnutrition had enfeebled the destitute refugees in the remote camp.
items.ex_zh: 多年的严重营养不良使偏远难民营中赤贫的难民们极度虚弱无力。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe reducing the physical strength, structural integrity, authority, or effectiveness of something, ranging from gradual erosion to total psychological or systemic evisceration.
groups.summary_zh: 指力量、根基、权威或效能的减弱、暗中侵蚀乃至彻底废除。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote the slow, parasitic, or attrition-based depletion of vigor, structural integrity, or authority, contrasting with 'break' through unseen, incremental erosion.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架体现寄生虫般抽吸元气、日削月朘式的损耗机制，与剧烈而突发的“击碎”相对，强调无形中步步削蚀目标的根基、力量与元气。
groups.nuance_en: sap: silent draining of vitality or fluid sustenance from within (strength / morale / confidence) · undermine: clandestine digging away of foundations to collapse authority (credibility / position / trust) · erode: natural friction or chemical weathering eating away mass (cliff / margins / authority) · debilitate: rendering severely incapacitated or functionally helpless (disease / strike / heat) · wear down: relentless attrition exhausting an opponent's reserves (patience / defense / enemy)
groups.nuance_zh: sap: 悄然抽干内在元气 (strength / morale) · undermine: 挖墙脚动摇根基 (credibility / trust) · erode: 渐进冲刷剥蚀 (margins / authority) · debilitate: 使虚弱瘫痪 (body / economy) · wear down: 持续消耗磨损 (patience / defense)

groups.name: Satisfy & Gratify · 满足与取悦 (Content, Please, Satisfy)
groups.tip: 迎合心意并使人感到满足高兴

items.raw_cluster: 取悦与使满足 Please & Gratify
items.def_zh: 使满意，取悦，使高兴；（用于礼貌请求）请；愿意，喜欢
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel happy, satisfied, or content. 2. To choose or wish to do something. 3. Used as a polite word when asking for something.
items.ex_en: The talented young pianist played several classical encores to please the enthusiastic audience.
items.ex_zh: 这位才华横溢的年轻钢琴家加演了数首古典名曲，以取悦热情的观众。

items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel happy, satisfied, or willing to accept a situation.
items.ex_en: A modest pension could content the retired clerk during his peaceful final years.
items.ex_zh: 微薄的退休金就能让这位退休办事员在平静的晚年感到知足常乐。

items.def_en: to be acceptable, convenient, or pleasing to someone
items.ex_en: This flexible meeting schedule will suit all team members across different time zones.
items.ex_zh: 这种灵活的会议时间安排将合乎不同时区所有团队成员的心意。

items.def_zh: 使满意，使高兴；满足，符合（需求、条件）
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel pleased by giving them what they want or need. 2. To fulfill or meet a need, condition, or requirement.
items.ex_en: The rich hot broth quickly satisfied our gnawing hunger on that freezing night.
items.ex_zh: 在那个寒冷的冬夜，热腾腾的浓汤迅速抚慰了我们饥肠辘辘的肚子。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to provide the things that a particular person or situation needs or wants, often in order to satisfy or please them
items.ex_en: The seaside resort built new amenities to cater to the needs of families.
items.ex_zh: 该海滨度假胜地增建了新设施，以迎合各家庭群体的度假需求。

items.def_zh: 迎合，纵容（不良嗜好或低级趣味）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to do or say what someone wants in order to please them, especially when it is unreasonable or wrong
items.ex_en: Sensational tabloid newspapers often pander to the public's appetite for scandalous gossip stories.
items.ex_zh: 耸人听闻的小报往往迎合大众对丑闻八卦的低俗趣味。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to be very nice or flatter someone so that they will do what you want or be pleased with you
items.ex_en: He brought expensive chocolates to butter up his strict supervisor before asking permission.
items.ex_zh: 他在提出请求前带了高档巧克力来巴结讨好他严厉的主管。

items.def_zh: 姑息，平息，满足（要求/胃口）
items.def_en: to satisfy a hunger or pacify an adversary by agreeing to their demands
items.ex_en: The government made minor tax concessions to appease the furious striking transport workers.
items.ex_zh: 政府在税收上作出了微小让步，以平息怒不可遏的罢工运输工人的怨气。

items.def_en: to give pleasure or satisfaction to a person by fulfilling a desire or ambition
items.ex_en: Winning the prestigious architecture award deeply gratified the hardworking designer after years of effort.
items.ex_zh: 经过多年的努力，荣获著名的建筑大奖令这位勤勉的设计师倍感欣慰。

items.def_en: to make an angry or hostile person feel less dissatisfied or hostile by concessions
items.ex_en: Management offered free vouchers to placate the passengers delayed by the flight cancellation.
items.ex_zh: 管理层提供了免费消费券，以抚慰因航班取消而受延误的乘客们的不满情绪。

groups.summary_en: A stimulus, person, or outcome meets the desires, expectations, or emotional needs of an experiencer. Verbs vary from bringing adequate peace of mind without demand for more (content) to active delight and appeasement (please, gratify) and meeting stringent formal requirements (satisfy).
groups.summary_zh: 达到心理期望、使人心满意足或迎合取悦。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame designate the fulfillment of demands, appetites, or emotional conditions, contrasting with mere 'feed' or 'aid' by focusing on reaching subjective contentment or placating expectations.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架表达精准对应欲望、诉求或心理标准，使其达到饱和与愉悦，与中性的“提供/辅助”相比，强调主观满足感、取悦心理或息事宁人的调和。
groups.nuance_en: satisfy: meeting exact minimum criteria, legal conditions, or physical cravings (hunger / requirements / curiosity) · please: producing positive emotional gratification or delight (critics / audience / eye) · cater to: tailoring services or compromises to specific, often base tastes (demands / elite / clientele) · pander to: debasing standards to gratify vulgar or illicit desires (fears / tastes / instincts) · appease: concessions surrendered to calm an aggressive or aggrieved party (dictator / anger / gods)
groups.nuance_zh: satisfy: 满足严苛的标准、要求或填补生理欲求 (hunger / requirements / curiosity) · please: 使人发自内心地喜悦、称心如意 (critics / audience / eye) · cater to: 投其所好、量身定制地迎合特定人群偏好 (demands / elite / clientele) · pander to: 丧失底线原则地迎合庸俗、恶劣的低级趣味 (fears / tastes / instincts) · appease: 割肉妥协、姑息让步以抚平暴怒或平息争端 (dictator / anger / gods)

groups.name: Scold & Rebuke · 训斥与斥责 (Express Sharp Disapproval)
groups.tip: 由责怪批评上升为严厉训斥

items.def_en: (+ for/about) to speak to someone in mild disapproval, gently scolding them for minor errors
items.ex_en: She gently chided her little brother for leaving his muddy boots inside yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 她昨天轻声责怪她的小弟弟把沾满泥巴的靴子留在了屋里。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Severely reprimand or scold someone in authority
items.ex_en: On Fridays, staff are allowed to dress down.
items.ex_zh: 每周五，员工可以穿便服上班。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong
items.ex_en: The teacher told him off for chatting during the exam.
items.ex_zh: 老师因为他在考试中聊天而严厉训斥了他。

items.def_en: To speak angrily and critically to someone, especially a child, because they have done something wrong.
items.ex_en: The mother scolded her reckless son for crossing the busy avenue without looking.
items.ex_zh: 母亲严厉训斥了鲁莽的儿子，因为他不看路就横穿繁忙的大马路。

items.def_en: (+ for) to express sharp, official, or authoritative disapproval of someone's behavior
items.ex_en: The board formally reprimanded the chief officer for violating company ethical conduct standards.
items.ex_zh: 董事会因首席主管违反公司职业道德准则而对他予以正式申诫。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Reprimand someone harshly and loudly
items.ex_en: The furious sergeant chewed out the careless recruit for dropping his unloaded weapon.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的中士把那个弄掉了未上膛枪支的粗心新兵狠狠训斥了一通。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Attack someone verbally with great force and anger
items.ex_en: The opposition party leader laid into the minister regarding the failed housing program.
items.ex_zh: 反对党领袖针对失败的住房项目，把该部门部长狠狠痛斥了一顿。

items.def_en: To speak angrily or critically to someone because they have done something wrong or unacceptable; to reprimand.
items.ex_en: The committee chairman publicly rebuked the delegate for his rude and disruptive remarks.
items.ex_zh: 委员会主席公开斥责了该代表粗鲁且极具破坏性的发言。

items.def_en: (+ for) to criticize or scold someone angrily, harshly, and at length
items.ex_en: The angry coach berated his players for their sluggish defense during the match.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的教练在比赛期间严厉呵斥了队员们迟缓松懈的防守表现。

items.def_en: (+ for) to reprimand or criticize someone severely and publicly
items.ex_en: The independent investigation castigated senior management for ignoring repeated internal safety warnings entirely.
items.ex_zh: 独立调查严厉责难了高层管理人员完全忽视多次内部安全警告的行径。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe expressing sharp, direct disapproval or anger toward someone for their misconduct, ranging from domestic fault-finding to formal, authoritative censure.
groups.summary_zh: 因过错或不当言行而对当事人进行严厉责备、训诫或谴责。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame describe the vocal delivery of sharp, authoritative, or aggressive moral reprimand, contrasting with mild 'advise' by its punitive emotional force.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架表达以上对下或因道德义愤而发出的严厉训斥与声讨，与客观平缓的“劝告/纠正”不同，蕴含强烈的惩戒意图、情绪威慑与言语打击。
groups.nuance_en: reprimand: formal, official institutional rebuke from authority (officer / employee / student) · scold: nagging or irritable vocal censure, typically parental (children / puppy / boy) · rebuke: sharp, righteous, cutting moral correction delivered directly (subordinate / peer / critic) · chew out: intensely aggressive, vulgar, or loud tongue-lashing (cadet / team / recruit) · chide: mild, gentle, or teasing admonition for a minor fault (friend / sister / partner)
groups.nuance_zh: reprimand: 官方、体制内或职场层级上正式的申诫处分 (officer / employee / student) · scold: 家长式絮叨、恼怒且声调偏高的呵斥怪罪 (children / puppy / boy) · rebuke: 针对道义过失给予义正词严的当头棒喝 (subordinate / peer / critic) · chew out: 极具攻击性、唾沫横飞的狗血淋头痛骂 (cadet / team / recruit) · chide: 轻声嗔怪、带着善意或微愠的委婉点拨 (friend / sister / partner)

groups.name: Seasonal Sheltering & Temporary Habitation · 栖居与越冬 (Winter, Camp, Cohabit)
groups.tip: 同居栖息共同生活度日

items.def_en: (+ in/at) Spend the winter in a specified place or sheltered sanctuary
items.ex_en: Flocks of migrating waterfowl winter in the warm southern wetlands every single year.
items.ex_zh: 成群的候鸟水禽每年都在温暖的南部湿地越冬栖息。

items.def_en: Sleep outdoors in a tent or temporary shelter, especially for recreation or necessity
items.ex_en: We chose to camp out in the sheltered pine forest near the lake.
items.ex_zh: 我们选择在湖泊附近背风的松树林里搭帐篷露营过夜。

items.def_en: (Of animals) Retreat into a lair or den to seek protection during cold months
items.ex_en: Black bears typically den up under fallen tree hollows before the first snowfall.
items.ex_zh: 在初雪来临之前，黑熊通常会躲进倒木空心处归巢越冬。

items.def_en: to go to sleep in a temporary, makeshift, or shared bed or place
items.ex_en: The stranded hikers decided to bunk down on the barn floor for tonight.
items.ex_zh: 受困的徒步旅行者们决定今晚就在谷仓的地板上临时搭铺睡下。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) to start living together in the same dwelling, often without being formally married
items.ex_en: After dating for two months, they quickly decided to shack up together downtown.
items.ex_zh: 交往仅两个月后，他们便迅速决定在市区同居搭伙生活。

items.def_en: to hide or stay sheltered in a secure, secluded, or hidden place for an extended period
items.ex_en: The fugitive gang decided to hole up in an abandoned cabin deep inside.
items.ex_zh: 逃犯团伙决定深藏在森林深处的一间废弃小屋里避风头。

items.def_en: Spend the winter in a dormant, inactive state resembling deep sleep
items.ex_en: Many small woodland rodents hibernate in underground burrows throughout the harsh frozen months.
items.ex_zh: 许多林地小啮齿动物在整个严酷寒冷的冬日里都会在地下洞穴冬眠。

items.def_zh: 同居，共同生活；（动植物）共栖，共同存活
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (formal) To live together in a sexual relationship without being legally married. 2. (biology) To exist or live together in the same habitat.
items.ex_en: The unmarried couple decided to cohabit peacefully in their newly purchased suburban condominium.
items.ex_zh: 这对未婚情侣决定在他们新买的郊区公寓里一起同居生活。

items.def_en: 1. (biology) To spend or survive the winter season in a specific place or condition; to keep plants or animals alive through the winter.
items.ex_en: Fragile flowering potted shrubs must overwinter in a heated greenhouse against frost damage.
items.ex_zh: 娇嫩的盆栽开花灌木必须在有暖气的温室中越冬，以防霜冻危害。

items.def_en: 1. (military / mountaineering) To camp temporarily outdoors in the open without tents or with minimal shelter.
items.ex_en: The weary mountain infantry soldiers bivouacked along the rocky ridge beneath the stars.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的山地步兵战士们在星空下的岩石山脊上露宿过夜。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe living, dwelling, or making temporary encampments under specific environmental conditions, seasonal shifts, or domestic arrangements. They range from organisms surviving cold seasons to humans setting up temporary quarters outdoors or co-residing.
groups.summary_zh: 指在特定季节、极端环境或临时条件下栖居、扎营越冬或同住。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame designate seasonal or survival retreat into sheltering redoubts, contrasting with permanent 'inhabit' via their temporal, adaptive, or defensive contingency.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架以季节节律、规避严寒或躲避战乱危险为导向的阶段性避难驻扎，与持久稳定的“定居”相比，凸显高度的临时性、自保性与自然适时性。
groups.nuance_en: winter: spending the cold season in a sheltered climate or port (cattle / birds / fleet) · hibernate: physiological dormancy or prolonged total metabolic retreat (bears / economy / virus) · hole up: barricading oneself in a covert, fortified hideout (fugitives / robbers / sniper) · camp out: sleeping outdoors in temporary improvised shelters (protesters / hikers / fans) · shack up: informal, often illicit or casual cohabitation under one roof (couple / partner / lover)
groups.nuance_zh: winter: 候鸟迁徙或舰队牲畜在安全暖和处熬冬度过冬季 (cattle / birds / fleet) · hibernate: 生理深度冬眠，或产业/系统长久休眠蛰伏 (bears / economy / virus) · hole up: 如困兽藏入洞穴般闭门潜伏躲避搜捕或风头 (fugitives / robbers / sniper) · camp out: 在野外或街头安营扎寨露宿 (protesters / hikers / fans) · shack up: 未婚同居、搭伙厮混于逼仄住所 (couple / partner / lover)

groups.name: Seat & Lodge · 安放与入位 (Seat, Lay, Hole)
groups.tip: 将物体或人置于特定位置

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to place or become comfortably, stably, and firmly positioned in a seat, recess, or resting spot
items.ex_en: She carefully settled in the fragile porcelain vase upon the polished mantelpiece shelf.
items.ex_zh: 她小心翼翼地把脆弱的瓷花瓶稳妥地安放在光滑的壁炉架上。
items.ex2_en: The exhausted traveler settled in for a long, quiet night of rest.
items.ex2_zh: 筋疲力尽的旅行者安顿下来，享受漫长而安静的夜晚休息。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to draw or push the edges of something securely into a narrow space, recess, or fold
items.ex_en: He gently tucked in the corners of the heavy woolen blanket around her.
items.ex_zh: 他温柔地将厚羊毛毯的边角严严实实地掖在她身遭各处。

items.def_zh: 使就座，安排……坐下；安置，使安放于特定位置；容纳……坐下
items.def_en: 1. To lead or show someone to a seat, or assign a place to sit. 2. To fit or position something securely in a specified place. 3. To have enough seats for a certain number of people.
items.ex_en: The polite usher seated the foreign dignitaries in the front row of seats.
items.ex_zh: 礼貌的引座员安排外国贵宾在第一排座位上稳妥就座。

items.def_en: 1. To put someone or something down carefully or in a flat position. 2. (of a bird or insect) to produce an egg.
items.ex_en: Please lay the fragile glass panels flat on the carpet to prevent cracking.
items.ex_zh: 请将脆弱的玻璃板平放在地毯上，以防止碎裂。

items.def_zh: 放置，平放（lay 的过去式和过去分词）；铺设；产（卵）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of lay; to have put something down flat or carefully.
items.ex_en: She gently laid her sleeping infant in the cradle beside the warm hearth.
items.ex_zh: 她轻轻地将睡着了的婴儿平放在温暖壁炉旁的摇篮里。

items.def_zh: 使安卧；半隐半现地置于
items.def_en: [I/T] to place or settle comfortably, snugly, or securely within a recess
items.ex_en: The secluded stone cottage nestled quietly in the hollow of the mist-shrouded mountain.
items.ex_zh: 幽静的石屋静静地安卧在云雾缭绕的山坳之中。
items.ex2_en: She nestled her sleepy newborn baby gently against her warm shoulder.
items.ex2_zh: 她轻轻地将昏昏欲睡的新生儿依偎在温暖的肩膀上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to pack, squeeze, or seat an object tightly into a narrow opening or cavity
items.ex_en: He wedged the thick wooden block in the narrow opening to secure the heavy door.
items.ex_zh: 他把厚木块卡入狭窄的缝隙中，以固定住沉重的门。

items.def_zh: （高尔夫球中）击（球）入洞；进洞；在……上打洞
items.def_en: 1. (golf) To hit a ball into a hole. 2. to make a hole in something, especially a ship.
items.ex_en: With an effortless swing, she holed the ball from twenty feet across the green.
items.ex_zh: 她轻松挥杆，便把二十英尺外的球推入了果岭洞中。

items.def_en: [I/T] to fix, force, or deposit firmly into a position or receptacle
items.ex_en: A sharp piece of gravel lodged firmly inside the tread of his running shoe.
items.ex_zh: 一颗尖锐的碎石牢固地卡进了他跑鞋的底纹里。
items.ex2_en: The archer lodged a sharp hunting arrow right inside the bullseye circle.
items.ex2_zh: 弓箭手把一支锋利的猎箭牢牢射入了靶心圈内。

items.def_en: to fix firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass
items.ex_en: The surgeon will embed a tiny microchip beneath the patient's dense muscular tissue.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生将把一枚微型芯片植入患者厚实的肌肉组织深处。

groups.summary_en: These verbs designate placing an object or person into a stable, recessed, or designated resting recess, surface, or cavity. They emphasize positioning something horizontally or seating it securely into its designated resting base or enclosure.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重将物体横放、深置或安顿至凹槽、底座与承重位置。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote the careful, deliberate mechanical insertion or positioning of an object into a stable resting niche, contrasting with loose 'put' through spatial snugness and secure stability.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架聚焦将人或物体妥帖、稳固地嵌放进凹槽、基座或安全窝巢的动作，与随手“放置”相比，强调空间上的严丝合缝、受托支撑与归位安顿。
groups.nuance_en: seat: securing firmly into an intended mechanical socket or formal chair (guest / bolt / valve) · lay: setting horizontally and deliberately flat on a plane (foundation / floorboards / corpse) · nestle: settling snugly and affectionately into a warm, sheltered hollow (cabin / child / kitten) · wedge in: forcing tightly into an undersized slot by heavy compression (books / car / foot) · tuck in: folding neat borders inward to stow compact and cozy (sheets / blanket / edges)
groups.nuance_zh: seat: 使严整稳固地就座或机械部件严密落座卡紧 (guest / bolt / valve) · lay: 郑重平稳地水平铺设或横放陈列 (foundation / floorboards / corpse) · nestle: 依偎、温存且半隐半蔽地嵌坐于温暖凹处 (cabin / child / kitten) · wedge in: 强行将物体死死硬塞挤进狭窄缝隙 (books / car / foot) · tuck in: 掖好被角衣边，规整包裹以求紧凑安适 (sheets / blanket / edges)

groups.name: Seep & Exude Slowly · 渗漏与滴流 (Ooze, Seep, Trickle)
groups.tip: 液体缓慢渗出或滴落过程

items.def_zh: 滴下，流淌；流口水；（球类）运球，带球
items.def_en: 1. When liquid or saliva dribbles, it flows slowly in thin drops or a small trickle. 2. (sports) To move a ball forward with repeated short kicks, bounces, or touches.
items.ex_en: Cold tea continued to dribble slowly from the cracked spout onto the clean counter.
items.ex_zh: 冷茶继续从破损的壶嘴缓慢滴落到干净的台面上。
items.ex2_en: The nervous child dribbled cold water down his new cotton shirt.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的孩子把冷水滴洒在自己的新棉质衬衫上。

items.def_en: to flow or leak out very slowly through small cracks or porous material
items.ex_en: Dark motor oil began to seep out through the cracked seal beneath the engine.
items.ex_zh: 黑色的机油开始从发动机下方开裂的密封圈处渗出。

items.def_en: to emerge or flow out slowly in a thin stream, intermittent drops, or small amounts
items.ex_en: Clear spring water trickled out from the mossy rocks in a steady, thin stream.
items.ex_zh: 清澈的泉水从覆满苔藓的岩石间缓缓细流而出。

items.def_en: to flow slowly in a very thin, continuous or broken stream
items.ex_en: Melting snow trickled down the cold glass pane in thin, winding streams all afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 整个下午，融化的雪水顺着冰冷的玻璃窗细细流淌而下。
items.ex2_en: The gardener trickled liquid fertilizer around the roots of the roses.
items.ex2_zh: 园丁将液体肥料缓缓浇灌在玫瑰花根部的周围。

items.def_en: 1. (+ out/from/with) When a thick liquid oozes, it flows out slowly through small openings. 2. To show or express a particular quality or emotion strongly.
items.ex_en: Sticky yellow resin began to ooze from the freshly severed bark of the pine.
items.ex_zh: 黏稠的黄色树脂开始从松树新被切开的树皮处冒出。
items.ex2_en: The old pipe oozed oily black slime onto the clean concrete floor.
items.ex2_zh: 老旧的水管把黑色的油滑黏液渗漏到了干净的混凝土地面上。

items.def_en: (+ into/through/out) When water, oil, or gas seeps, it flows slowly through small cracks or porous materials.
items.ex_en: Contaminated rainwater gradually seeped into the underground reservoir through porous foundation walls.
items.ex_zh: 受污染的雨水通过多孔的地基墙壁逐渐渗入地下水库。

items.def_en: to filter gradually through a porous surface, membrane, or granular medium
items.ex_en: Boiling water must percolate slowly through the finely ground coffee beans for optimal extraction.
items.ex_zh: 沸水必须缓慢滤过多孔的细咖啡粉，以达到最佳萃取效果。
items.ex2_en: The chemist percolated the organic solvent through the powdered mineral mixture.
items.ex2_zh: 化学家将有机溶剂缓慢过滤渗透过粉末状矿物混合物。

items.def_zh: 缓缓渗出；淌出（浓稠液体）
items.def_en: to discharge or escape slowly and sluggishly from an opening, wound, or surface
items.ex_en: Thick black syrup oozed out from the punctured container onto the cold kitchen floor.
items.ex_zh: 浓稠的黑糖浆从破损的容器中缓缓淌到冰冷的厨房地板上。

items.def_en: (+ through/into) to seep or spread into an adjacent surface, as dye, ink, or sap
items.ex_en: The red fountain pen ink quickly bled through the thin parchment paper upon contact.
items.ex_zh: 红色的钢笔墨水一接触到薄羊皮纸就迅速渗透开来。

items.def_en: to discharge moisture, resin, or smell slowly and steadily through pores or cuts
items.ex_en: Certain desert shrubs exude a fragrant resin to protect themselves from intense sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 某些沙漠灌木会分泌出一种芳香的树脂，以抵御强烈的日晒。

groups.summary_en: A liquid moves through a porous barrier, crack, or wound in small, slow, or viscous amounts rather than a rapid gush. Verbs contrast thick sluggish discharge (ooze), capillary absorption through pores (seep), and intermittent thin dripping (trickle, dribble).
groups.summary_zh: 微量液体经孔隙或狭缝缓慢渗析或细细滴淌。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame capture the sluggish, capillary, or gravitational filtration of liquid through tiny pores or narrow channels, contrasting with voluminous 'pour' by its slow, stealthy emission.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描摹液体受毛细作用或重力驱使，极缓慢地经由微孔缝隙溢出滴淌的动态，与奔涌“倾泻”相反，凸显不易察觉、潜滋暗长的微量流失。
groups.nuance_en: seep: capillary infiltration through fine porous barriers or cracks (water / oil / poison) · ooze: sluggish, viscous discharge of thick liquid (slime / blood / mud) · trickle: narrow, intermittent dripping stream of thin fluid (tears / sweat / stream) · percolate: slow downward filtration through porous media or cultural dissemination (coffee / rainwater / ideas) · dribble: uncontrolled, clumsy leaking of small intermittent drops (saliva / liquid / soup)
groups.nuance_zh: seep: 穿透细小孔隙或缝隙的隐秘毛细渗漏 (water / oil / poison) · ooze: 浓稠黏液极其缓慢恶心地翻涌溢出 (slime / blood / mud) · trickle: 细细弱弱、断断续续地成线滴流淌落 (tears / sweat / stream) · percolate: 经由过滤介质缓缓下渗，或思潮下沉发酵 (coffee / rainwater / ideas) · dribble: 沿下颌边缘稀稀拉拉、失控滴落挂垂 (saliva / liquid / soup)

groups.name: Shape & Inscribe Rigid Material · 雕刻与塑形 (Carve, Sculpt, Chisel)
groups.tip: 雕琢打磨使原材料成型

items.def_en: (+ away/down) to carve wood into an object by repeatedly cutting small slices off it
items.ex_en: The grandfather sat on the porch and whittled small wooden figures for his grandchildren.
items.ex_zh: 祖父坐在门廊上，为孙辈们削着小木雕像。

items.def_en: (+ on/with) to cut words or designs into a hard surface such as metal, glass, or stone
items.ex_en: The jeweler will engrave your initials on the polished surface of the golden watch.
items.ex_zh: 珠宝匠会将你的名字首字母镌刻在这块打磨光滑的金表表面。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to shape an artistic figure, hollow, or dimensional form by cutting into hard material
items.ex_en: The artisan carved out a smooth hollow from the solid block of polished marble.
items.ex_zh: 工匠从整块光滑的大理石中雕刻出了一个规整的凹陷。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut, carve, or hollow out a shape, cavity, or relief from stone or wood with a chisel
items.ex_en: The stonemason chiseled out a fine ornamental rosette from the limestone wall.
items.ex_zh: 石匠用凿子在石灰岩墙面上凿出了一朵精美的装饰性玫瑰花结。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to carve or shave thin slices away from wood or rigid material to reduce its size or form a shape
items.ex_en: He whittled down the thick branch until it perfectly fit the socket.
items.ex_zh: 他把粗树枝逐渐削小，直到它完全契合插孔。

items.def_en: To carve, sculpt, or engrave words or designs into a hard surface.
items.ex_en: Ancient masons graved solemn prayers into the granite monument for future generations.
items.ex_zh: 古老的石匠将庄严的祷词铭刻在花岗岩纪念碑上，以昭示后人。

items.def_zh: 雕刻，雕琢；把（熟肉等）切成薄片
items.def_en: 1. To cut wood, stone, or another hard material into a specific shape or pattern. 2. To slice cooked meat into pieces.
items.ex_en: The skilled craftsman carved intricate floral patterns directly into the solid oak panel.
items.ex_zh: 熟练的工匠直接在坚硬的橡木板上雕刻出复杂的花卉图案。

items.def_en: To carve, cast, or shape a material into a three-dimensional work of art.
items.ex_en: She spent several months using local clay to sculpture a lifelike human figure.
items.ex_zh: 她花数月时间用当地的黏土雕塑了一尊栩栩如生的人物像。

items.def_zh: 塑形，浇铸；塑造（性格等）；发霉
items.def_en: 1. To shape a soft substance into a particular form by pouring or pressing it into a container. 2. To strongly influence the development or character of someone. 3. To decay and become covered with mould.
items.ex_en: The artisan poured liquid bronze into the sand cast to mould the commemorative medal.
items.ex_zh: 工匠将青铜液倒入沙模中，浇铸出纪念奖章。

items.def_en: (+ out/into) to cut or shape stone, wood, or metal with a chisel
items.ex_en: The master artist chiseled delicate facial details into the rugged block of granite.
items.ex_zh: 这位艺术大师在粗糙的花岗岩石块上凿刻出精致的面部细节。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe cutting away hard materials like stone or wood, or shaping malleable materials into dimensional figures or artistic forms.
groups.summary_zh: 通过切割、凿刻坚硬材质或模塑可塑材料来塑造立体形象。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote the subtractive removal or incision of hard resistant materials using edged tools to render forms or text, contrasting with additive 'build' through reductive shaping.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指使用利刃或硬质工具对坚硬原材料实施减法式的切割、凿削与铭刻，与堆叠的“建造”不同，凸显剥除多余实体以赋形铸意的雕琢工匠性。
groups.nuance_en: carve: broad sculpturing of figure or relief by cutting away mass (meat / statue / wood) · engrave: fine incisive cutting of lines or letters onto hard plates (metal / ring / plaque) · chisel: sharp, heavy chipping away with an angled blade (marble / stone / features) · whittle: folk, leisurely shaving off thin shavings from wood (stick / figurine / away) · sculpt: high-art volumetric modeling of three-dimensional form (clay / marble / masterpiece)
groups.nuance_zh: carve: 大开大合地剔除料胚切出具象轮廓或肉片 (meat / statue / wood) · engrave: 用锐利刻刀在硬质板面上凹刻精细文字或图纹 (metal / ring / plaque) · chisel: 用凿子与手锤敲击，凿击出硬石棱角与深痕 (marble / stone / features) · whittle: 闲坐时用小刀削木片，指一层层削减减损 (stick / figurine / away) · sculpt: 融通各种造型手法的整体性三维高雅艺术雕塑 (clay / marble / masterpiece)

groups.name: Shed & Molt · 蜕皮与生物脱落 (Shed, Molt, Desquamate)
groups.tip: 表皮或组织脱落与蜕变

items.def_en: to come off in flakes, scales, or thin layers from an outer skin or surface
items.ex_en: The dry skin on his sunburned nose began to peel off in messy flakes.
items.ex_zh: 他晒伤的鼻梁上的干皮开始碎屑般地脱落。
items.ex2_en: The decorator carefully peeled off the old faded wallpaper from the bedroom.
items.ex2_zh: 装修工小心翼翼地把卧室里褪色的旧壁纸撕下来。

items.def_en: (+ off) to slough off or discard skin, horn, or cuticle naturally
items.ex_en: In the warmth of spring, the serpent cast off its faded, weathered skin.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖的春日里，那条蛇蜕下了它褪色干瘪的旧皮。

items.def_en: to naturally drop or cast off hair, fur, skin, or leaves as part of a biological cycle
items.ex_en: During the transition into summer, our golden retriever sheds its thick winter coat.
items.ex_zh: 在转入夏季的这段时间，我们的金毛猎犬会蜕掉厚重的冬毛。

items.def_en: [I/T] of sunburned or diseased skin, to separate and flake off in thin strips
items.ex_en: After spending all day on the beach, his shoulders started to peel uncomfortably.
items.ex_zh: 在海滩上待了一整天之后，他的肩膀开始难受地脱皮。
items.ex2_en: The chef peeled the ripe golden potatoes before boiling them for dinner.
items.ex2_zh: 厨师在把成熟的黄土豆煮作晚餐前先削去了它们的皮。

items.def_en: (US spelling of moult) When an animal or bird molts, it sheds old feathers, skin, hair, or a shell so new ones can grow.
items.ex_en: Young birds molt their fluffy juvenile down before growing their true flight feathers.
items.ex_zh: 幼鸟在长出真正的飞羽之前，会先蜕掉毛茸茸的雏羽。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to shed or molt a naturally discarded outer covering, such as a skin, shell, or cuticle
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to shed, cast off, or peel away dead biological tissue, outer skin, or scales
items.ex_en: The chemical peel caused the patient to slough off damaged outer layers of skin.
items.ex_zh: 化学换肤疗程使患者蜕去了受损的表层死皮组织。
items.ex2_en: Dead skin cells slough off naturally during the body's daily regeneration.
items.ex2_zh: 死皮细胞在身体的日常新陈代谢过程中会自然脱落。

items.def_en: [I/T] (often + off) to drop off or cause dead tissue or outer skin to be shed
items.ex_en: The necrotic tissue will naturally slough away as the healthy wound begins healing.
items.ex_zh: 随着健康的伤口开始愈合，坏死组织会自然脱落。
items.ex2_en: A snake regularly sloughs its scaly outer skin to accommodate rapid growth.
items.ex2_zh: 蛇会定期蜕去带鳞的外皮以适应快速生长。

items.def_zh: 去除（角质）；片状脱落，剥落
items.def_en: To shed dead skin or bark in thin layers, or to remove dead skin cells using a cosmetic scrub.
items.ex_en: Dermatologists recommend that you gently exfoliate dry skin cells once or twice a week.
items.ex_zh: 皮肤科医生建议每周温和去除一到两次干燥的死皮角质。
items.ex2_en: Old birch bark exfoliates naturally during dry periods in late autumn.
items.ex2_zh: 深秋干旱季节，老桦树皮会自然分层脱落。

items.def_en: (British English spelling of molt) When an animal or bird moults, it sheds old feathers, skin, hair, or a shell.
items.ex_en: The adult eagle moults its worn flight feathers every autumn before migration starts.
items.ex_zh: 成年雕每年秋季迁徙开始前都会换掉磨损的飞羽。

groups.summary_en: An animal, human, or skin surface periodically casts off outer biological layers such as skin, feathers, shells, or cuticle dead cells naturally or through scrubbed peeling.
groups.summary_zh: 动物或生物表皮自然脱去旧毛羽、外皮或蜕落角质细胞。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame evoke the natural biological or physical discarding of an obsolete outer layer or dead cuticle, contrasting with deliberate 'strip' by its autonomous, organic detachment.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架源于生物换羽蜕壳或组织自然角质化脱落的机理，与外部粗暴的“剥离”相对，强调衰亡外壳周期性、自发性抛弃以实现更新新生。
groups.nuance_en: shed: natural casting off of outer coats, leaves, or tears (fur / skin / tears) · molt: periodic, seasonal biological shedding of feathers, hair, or exoskeleton (snake / bird / crab) · slough off: discarding a dead, necrotic, or useless epidermal layer (dead skin / habit / burden) · peel: separating and coming away in strips or thin skin (paint / skin / bark) · cast off: decisive, autonomous shedding of an unwanted shell or garment (restraints / old ways / moorings)
groups.nuance_zh: shed: 自主甩掉、散落外皮毛发，或洒下泪水 (fur / skin / tears) · molt: 动物受生理节律支配的定期换羽蜕壳 (snake / bird / crab) · slough off: 坏死角质层或陈腐负担的大块结痂脱落 (dead skin / habit / burden) · peel: 枯干表面呈长条状卷翘裂开剥离 (paint / skin / bark) · cast off: 毅然决然地解开系留、丢弃外壳旧羁绊 (restraints / old ways / moorings)

groups.name: Shine & Glow · 发光照耀与温润生辉 (Shine, Glow, Radiate)
groups.tip: 持久而温暖地发出光泽

items.def_zh: 发光，发出微光；容光焕发，喜形于色
items.def_en: 1. To produce a dull, steady light, especially without flames. 2. To look healthy, warm, or happy with color in your face.
items.ex_en: The dying coals continued to glow dimly in the dark hearth until dawn arrived.
items.ex_zh: 将熄的余炭在黑暗的壁炉里微弱地发着红光，直到破晓。

items.def_zh: 透出柔和或反射的微光
items.def_en: to shine with a gentle, smooth, or reflected brightness
items.ex_en: Polished silver cutlery gleamed softly under the ambient light of the dining room chandelier.
items.ex_zh: 打磨光滑的银餐具在餐厅吊灯的光晕下泛着柔和的光泽。

items.def_en: to shine brightly, warmly, and continuously downwards onto a place or person
items.ex_en: The brilliant tropical sun beamed down on the crowded white sands of the resort.
items.ex_zh: 热带明艳的阳光温暖地普照在度假村拥挤的白色沙滩上。

items.def_en: to send a clear, steady, luminous ray of light through a translucent opening or medium
items.ex_en: Despite her nervousness, her deep knowledge of the subject shone through.
items.ex_zh: 尽管她有些紧张，但她扎实的专业素养依然表露无遗。

items.def_en: 1. To produce or reflect light; be bright. 2. To point light in a particular direction.
items.ex_en: The full moon will shine brightly over the calm surface of the lake tonight.
items.ex_zh: 今晚满月将在平静的湖面上投射出明亮皎洁的光芒。

items.def_en: [I/T] to emit rays of light or heat in all directions
items.ex_en: The central heating element radiated intense heat outward across the entire laboratory chamber.
items.ex_zh: 中央加热元件向整个实验室舱室四周辐射出强烈的热量。

items.def_zh: 发光，照耀（shine的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past tense and past participle of shine; to give off or reflect bright light.
items.ex_en: Morning sunlight shone through the stained glass windows, illuminating the old church hall.
items.ex_zh: 晨光透过彩色玻璃窗照耀进来，照亮了古老的教堂大厅。

items.def_zh: 烈日暴晒；强光炙烤照射
items.def_en: to shine with intense heat and powerful, unyielding brightness from above
items.ex_en: The midday sun blazed down relentlessly on the workers paving the highway.
items.ex_zh: 正午的烈日无情地暴晒着铺设公路的工人们。

items.def_en: to transmit or cast a bright, focused ray of light
items.ex_en: The lighthouses along the coast beam powerful warning signals across the foggy sea.
items.ex_zh: 沿海的灯塔穿过大雾弥漫的洋面投射出强烈的警示光柱。

items.def_en: to shine with a very bright, intense, and hot light
items.ex_en: The emergency flares blazed brightly against the dark expanse of the night sky.
items.ex_zh: 求救信号弹在漆黑夜空的映衬下爆发出极其炽烈的强光。

groups.summary_en: An emitter gives off a steady, warm, or broad beam of continuous light, distinguishing sustained luminescence from brief flickering bursts.
groups.summary_zh: 持续散发稳定、温热或普照的明亮光辉。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame describe the continuous emission or reflection of luminous optical radiance, contrasting with explosive 'flash' through sustained, steady, or glowing luminescence.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描述光源自体向外散发光波或表面平稳折射明朗光晕的物理视觉现象，与一闪即逝的“闪烁”相比，着眼于光泽的持久性、温暖感与照射质地。
groups.nuance_en: shine: bright, radiant, unimpeded emission of luminous rays (sun / star / light) · glow: warm, incandescence without open flame or diffused soft warmth (embers / cheeks / screen) · gleam: brief or subdued flash of light reflected off polished dark planes (metal / eyes / sword) · radiate: sending out energy, light, or joy evenly in all radial directions (heat / warmth / confidence) · blaze: blinding, ferocious, high-intensity furnace-like illumination (sun / fire / diamond)
groups.nuance_zh: shine: 核心明亮且无所遮蔽的光辉直接照射 (sun / star / light) · glow: 无明火的炽热红光、温润柔和的暗处透光或脸色绯红 (embers / cheeks / screen) · gleam: 抛光深色表面所反射出的一缕幽冷微光或眼神狡黠 (metal / eyes / sword) · radiate: 从中心向四面八方全方位辐射光热或欢欣魅力 (heat / warmth / confidence) · blaze: 如熔炉烈火般炫目炽热、极具灼目威力的逼人强光 (sun / fire / diamond)

groups.name: Skim, Glide & Surf across Surfaces · 滑行与冲浪 (Taxi, Surf, Skim)
groups.tip: 顺势在表面平稳移动

items.def_en: to move forward smoothly on a surface through existing momentum without applying active force
items.ex_en: He stopped pedaling and let the bicycle coast along the flat asphalt road.
items.ex_zh: 他停下踩踏，任由自行车在平坦的柏油路上顺势滑行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to move smoothly, effortlessly, and quietly over a flat surface or across water
items.ex_en: The graceful white swan glided across the glassy surface of the tranquil lake.
items.ex_zh: 优雅的白天鹅平静地滑过宁静湖面那如镜般的表面。

items.def_en: 1. (of an aircraft) To move slowly along the ground before taking off or after landing. 2. (informal) To travel in a taxi.
items.ex_en: Let's just taxi to the airport instead of dragging these heavy bags onto transit.
items.ex_zh: 咱们干脆乘出租车去机场吧，别拖着这些沉重的行李去挤公交了。

items.def_en: to move smoothly, quietly, and continuously along a surface without noticeable effort
items.ex_en: The experienced skater glided effortlessly along the frozen surface of the winter canal.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的滑冰者在冬日运河结冰的表面上毫不费力地平稳滑行。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to pass or move quickly and lightly across the surface of water or ground, barely touching it
items.ex_en: The flat pebble skimmed across the calm water before sinking into the lake.
items.ex_zh: 扁平的鹅卵石轻快地掠过平静的水面，然后沉入了湖中。

items.def_en: 1. To ride toward the shore on ocean waves using a surfboard. 2. To spend time browsing different websites or TV channels.
items.ex_en: Adventurous tourists surf the magnificent ocean swells along the rocky Hawaiian coastline every morning.
items.ex_zh: 充满冒险精神的游客每天清晨都会在夏威夷多石的海岸边迎浪冲浪。

items.def_en: to move quickly and lightly just above or along the surface of water or land
items.ex_en: The low-flying pelican skimmed the crests of the ocean waves with extraordinary precision.
items.ex_zh: 低飞的鹈鹕以极高的精准度紧贴着海浪的波峰飞掠而过。

items.def_en: to ride incoming waves while lying prone on a specialized short foam board
items.ex_en: Local teenagers often bodyboard along the gentle breaking surf on warm summer afternoons.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖的夏日午后，当地青少年经常在平缓的碎浪中趴板冲浪。

items.def_zh: 进行冲浪板运动，用冲浪板冲浪
items.def_en: To ride ocean waves standing or lying on a surfboard.
items.ex_en: Professional athletes surfboard across high Pacific breakers during the annual summer competition.
items.ex_zh: 在一年一度的夏季赛事中，专业运动员踩着冲浪板飞驰在太平洋的高浪之间。

items.def_en: to skim across a surface of water, or uncontrollably slide across a wet road on a film of water
items.ex_en: Driving too fast through deep standing water caused the vehicle to hydroplane dangerously.
items.ex_zh: 在深积水中车速过快导致车辆危险地发生了水面滑移。

groups.summary_en: An agent, vessel, or aircraft moves smoothly across a surface—such as water, runway tarmac, or waves—utilizing hydrodynamic or aerodynamic lift without fully taking flight or sinking. Verbs contrast ground navigation of aircraft (taxi) with hydroplaning over waves (surf, skim).
groups.summary_zh: 顺着地表或波浪表面顺滑滑行而不脱离支撑。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame designate frictionless, continuous kinetic travel barely touching or skimming across fluid or land surfaces, contrasting with heavy 'trudge' through hydrodynamic grace and effortless momentum.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架描绘贴着水面、冰面或跑道，凭借流体升力与极小摩擦进行的悬浮感贴面运动，与笨重的“涉行/拖步”相比，强调轻盈、借势滑掠的高速顺畅性。
groups.nuance_en: glide: smooth, effortless, frictionless motion across air or ice (eagle / skater / dancer) · skim: rapid horizontal passage just grazing the uppermost surface (stones / water / waves) · surf: riding forward dynamically on the crest of rolling liquid energy (waves / board / internet) · coast: moving smoothly onward solely by residual momentum without power input (bicycle / car / along) · taxi: slow ground navigation of an aircraft rolling on runways (airplane / jet / runway)
groups.nuance_zh: glide: 几乎零阻力、优雅流畅的无动力长途滑翔滑行 (eagle / skater / dancer) · skim: 飞快掠过水面或地表最上层，指尖仅轻触表皮 (stones / water / waves) · surf: 借助海浪推力冲浪起乘，或在网络数据浪潮冲浪 (waves / board / internet) · coast: 完全不费力踏踩、单凭惯性在坡道或表面顺势滑走 (bicycle / car / along) · taxi: 飞机在起飞前后于停机坪或跑道上自行动力慢速地面滑行 (airplane / jet / runway)

groups.name: Spill & Splatter · 倾倒、飞溅与泼洒 (Spill, Slop, Splatter)
groups.tip: 液体倾泻奔涌而出

items.def_en: move around noisily and splash within a container or on a surface
items.ex_en: The leftover milk sloshed around inside the plastic jug as she walked quickly.
items.ex_zh: 当她快步行走时，塑料壶里剩下的牛奶不停地来回晃荡拍溅。
items.ex2_en: The clumsy waiter sloshed the iced tea around in the pitcher.
items.ex2_zh: 笨拙的服务员端水时把水罐里的冰茶晃得直晃荡。

items.def_en: 1. To flow, run, or fall over the edge of a container accidentally, or to cause a liquid to do this. 2. To pour or move out in large numbers.
items.ex_en: Be careful carrying that brimming mug so you do not spill hot coffee everywhere.
items.ex_zh: 端那只装得太满的马克杯时小心点，别把热咖啡泼得到处都是。
items.ex2_en: The bubbly soapy water spilled over the brim of the bathtub.
items.ex2_zh: 冒泡的肥皂水从浴缸边缘溢了出来。

items.def_zh: （使）溢出，（使）泼洒（spill的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British) Past tense and past participle of spill: to flow or cause to flow over the edge of a container.
