items.ex_en: He accidentally spilt half a bowl of hot soup over his clean apron.
items.ex_zh: 他不小心将半碗热汤洒在了自己干净的围裙上。
items.ex2_en: Cold milk spilt across the kitchen counter when the glass tipped over.
items.ex2_zh: 玻璃杯翻倒时，冰牛奶洒了满厨房的操作台。

items.def_en: 1. To spill or splash over the edge of a container carelessly, or to cause liquid to do so.
items.ex_en: Dirty soapy water slopped over the rim of the bucket during the vigorous cleaning.
items.ex_zh: 在用力擦洗的过程中，脏肥皂水从水桶边缘晃荡溅了出来。
items.ex2_en: The careless cleaner slopped soapy dishwater across the slippery cafeteria floor.
items.ex2_zh: 粗心的清洁工将带有肥皂的洗碗水泼洒在湿滑的食堂地板上。

items.def_en: pour or splash out of a container in an uncontrolled manner
items.ex_en: Red paint spilled out across the garage floor when the shelf suddenly collapsed.
items.ex_zh: 架子突然倒塌时，红油漆泼洒了一车库的地板。
items.ex2_en: The sudden impact spilled out all the loose coins from her purse.
items.ex2_zh: 突如其来的撞击把她钱包里所有的零钱都震洒了出来。

items.def_en: flow or slosh over the rim or edge of a container
items.ex_en: Foam began to spill over the top of the glass as he poured hastily.
items.ex_zh: 由于他倒得太急，泡沫开始从玻璃杯顶端漫溢出来。

items.def_en: to hit or cover something in large drops or messy patches with a wet, splashing sound
items.ex_en: Heavy raindrops splattered against the bedroom window pane throughout the noisy stormy night.
items.ex_zh: 在嘈杂的风雨之夜，豆大的雨点整夜啪啪地溅落在卧室的窗玻璃上。
items.ex2_en: The muddy truck splattered dirty water over all the waiting sidewalk commuters.
items.ex2_zh: 满是泥泞的卡车将脏水溅到了所有在人行道上等候的通勤者身上。

items.def_en: to move around noisily in a container, or cause a liquid to splash clumsily over the edge
items.ex_en: The bucket was too full, causing muddy water to slosh over his boots.
items.ex_zh: 水桶装得太满了，导致泥水晃出来泼溅到了他的靴子上。
items.ex2_en: He carelessly sloshed red wine over the pristine white linen tablecloth.
items.ex2_zh: 他粗心地把红酒泼洒在了洁白如新的亚麻桌布上。

items.def_zh: 大雨倾盆（尤与 down 连用）；用桶提（舀）水
items.def_en: 1. (informal, especially 'bucket down') To rain very heavily and in large amounts. 2. To carry, pour, or scoop something in a bucket.
items.ex_en: It began to bucket down just as the outdoor wedding ceremony was starting.
items.ex_zh: 户外婚礼仪式刚一开始，天空就倾盆大雨地下了起来。

items.def_en: (of rain) to pour down heavily and rapidly against a surface
items.ex_en: Freezing rain pelted down against our jackets as we hurried toward the subway entrance.
items.ex_zh: 当我们匆匆赶向地铁入口时，冰冷的雨水暴降倾泻在我们的夹克上。

groups.summary_en: A liquid moves or is made to move out of its container or path in an uncontrolled, messy, or torrential manner, varying from accidental overflow to vigorous sloshing or pouring in sheets.
groups.summary_zh: 液体失控地漫出、颠簸泼洒或如桶倾般倾泻落下。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the uncontrolled, accidental escape or messy projection of liquids over containment boundaries, contrasting with purposeful pouring or sprinkling.
groups.desc_zh: 指液体不受控、意外溢出容器边界或凌乱飞溅的动态，区别于有意的倾倒或洒水。
groups.nuance_en: spill: general accidental overflow or tipping over (milk / beans / secrets) · slop: clumsy, sloppy spilling of thick or messy liquid (pigswill / soup / water) · slosh: liquid splashing or surging vigorously within or out of a container (water / fuel / drink) · splatter: forceful scattering into small flying drops upon impact (mud / blood / sauce)
groups.nuance_zh: spill: 最通用的失手溢出或倾覆 (milk / beans / secrets) · slop: 粗鲁晃荡导致稠浊液体溅出 (pigswill / soup / water) · slosh: 液体在容器内剧烈晃荡并涌出 (water / fuel / drink) · splatter: 液体受冲击而四处飞溅出斑点 (mud / blood / sauce)

groups.name: Spin & Rotate · 旋转与转动 (Rotate, Spin, Whirl)
groups.tip: 极速旋转眼花缭乱

items.def_en: (+ sth) rotate lightly and rapidly, like in a dance
items.ex_en: The cheerful toddler twirled around the living room until she fell onto the carpet.
items.ex_zh: 那个快乐的蹒跚学步的小孩在客厅里打转圈，直到跌坐在地毯上。
items.ex2_en: The delighted girl twirled her colorful parasol around in the sunny garden.
items.ex2_zh: 高兴的女孩在阳光明媚的花园里轻轻转动着她五颜六色的阳伞。

items.def_en: [I/T] to turn around a fixed central point or axis in a continuous, controlled manner
items.ex_en: The mechanical turntable rotates steadily on its central axis at thirty-three revolutions each minute.
items.ex_zh: 机械转盘绕着其中央轴平稳旋转，速度为每分钟三十三转。
items.ex2_en: The radar technician rotates the satellite dish toward the northern horizon.
items.ex2_zh: 雷达技术员将卫星天线转向北方地平线。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move in a circular orbit around a central point, or turn on an axis
items.ex_en: The Earth and other planets revolve around the sun in predictable elliptical orbits.
items.ex_zh: 地球和其他行星沿着可预测的椭圆轨道围绕太阳公转。
items.ex2_en: The clever engineer revolves the mechanical turntable using an electric gear system.
items.ex2_zh: 聪明的工程师利用电动齿轮系统转动机械转盘。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) turn or cause to turn rapidly around a central axis
items.ex_en: The coach told the young skater to spin around quickly on one blade.
items.ex_zh: 教练让年轻的花滑选手单脚冰刀快速旋转。
items.ex2_en: The dizzy carousel spins around rapidly as joyful carnival music plays.
items.ex2_zh: 伴着欢快的狂欢节音乐，旋转木马快速旋转着。

items.def_en: 1. To turn around and around quickly, or make something do this. 2. To twist fibers into thread.
items.ex_en: He watched the colorful wheel spin until it gradually stopped on the grand prize.
items.ex_zh: 他看着彩色的轮盘飞速旋转，直到缓缓停在大奖上。
items.ex2_en: The magician spun the shiny silver coin across the smooth tabletop.
items.ex2_zh: 魔术师让闪亮的银币在光滑的桌面上飞速旋转。

items.def_zh: （使）飞旋，疾转；急转（身）；（头脑）发晕
items.def_en: To turn or spin around very quickly, or cause something to do so.
items.ex_en: Autumn leaves whirl through the empty streets whenever strong gusts of wind blow.
items.ex_zh: 每当阵阵强风吹过，秋天的落叶便在空旷的街道上飞旋。
items.ex2_en: The dancer whirled his light wooden partner across the crowded ballroom floor.
items.ex2_zh: 舞者带着轻盈的女舞伴在拥挤的舞池地面上飞旋。

items.def_en: To turn round and round quickly and lightly, or make something do so.
items.ex_en: She began to twirl playfully across the wooden floor in her new dress.
items.ex_zh: 她穿着新裙子，轻快地在木地板上旋转起舞。
items.ex2_en: The baton twirler twirled her baton skillfully before the cheering crowd.
items.ex2_zh: 指挥棒表演者在欢呼的观众面前熟练地旋转着手杖。

items.def_en: rotate or spin around very quickly, often creating dizziness
items.ex_en: Startled by the sudden noise, he had to whirl around to face the darkness.
items.ex_zh: 被突如其来的声音吓了一跳，他猛地转过身面对黑暗。

items.def_zh: （使）快速旋转（spin 的过去式和过去分词）；纺（纱）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of spin; to have turned around rapidly, or twisted fibers into thread.
items.ex_en: The dancer spun smoothly on his toes before finishing the dramatic performance.
items.ex_zh: 舞者用脚尖轻盈地快速旋转，随后结束了这段精彩的表演。
items.ex2_en: The playful boy spun his plastic top across the smooth tile floor.
items.ex2_zh: 顽皮的男孩让塑料陀螺在光滑的瓷砖地板上飞快旋转。

items.def_zh: 飞速回旋；作螺旋形晃转
items.def_en: to turn around quickly in circles or spirals, often with unsteady motion
items.ex_en: The mechanical apparatus began to gyrate with violent, erratic motions during testing.
items.ex_zh: 该机械装置在测试过程中开始剧烈且不规则地高速旋转晃动。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe circular motion around an axis or center point, ranging from steady mechanical rotation to rapid, dizzying, or violent spinning.
groups.summary_zh: 描述绕轴心或中心旋转，从平稳转动到急遽飞旋。
groups.desc_en: Denotes circular or pivoting motion around an axis, distinguished from linear progression or simple curved turning by continuous angular velocity and centripetal orientation.
groups.desc_zh: 指围绕轴心进行持续的角速度旋转运动，区别于直线位移或单纯的转弯改变方向。
groups.nuance_en: rotate: regular, systematic turning around a fixed internal axis (wheel / planet / crops) · revolve: orbiting an external center or smooth cyclical pivoting (Earth / cylinder / door) · spin: rapid, continuous whirling around an axis (top / coin / propeller) · whirl: dizzying, turbulent rotational or swirling rush (dancers / dust / wind) · twirl: light, nimble, and playful rotational movement (baton / moustache / umbrella)
groups.nuance_zh: rotate: 绕内部固定轴心规则、系统地转动 (wheel / planet / crops) · revolve: 绕外部中心公转或平稳周期性转动 (Earth / cylinder / door) · spin: 绕轴心高速飞转 (top / coin / propeller) · whirl: 令人眩晕的湍急狂转或卷动 (dancers / dust / wind) · twirl: 轻盈、灵活且带玩味地转动 (baton / moustache / umbrella)

groups.name: Sprout & Germinate · 萌芽与初生生长 (Germinate, Sprout, Shoot)
groups.tip: 植物破土抽芽并生出分蘖

items.def_en: (+ sth) produce or develop new shoots, buds, or leaves
items.ex_en: After the gentle spring rains, the rose bushes put out tender green shoots.
items.ex_zh: 春雨过后，这些玫瑰丛长出了嫩绿的新芽。

items.def_en: emerge and begin growing upward quickly as a shoot or seedling
items.ex_en: Green seedlings began to sprout up rapidly through the fertile garden soil.
items.ex_zh: 绿色的幼苗开始透过肥沃的花园土壤迅速萌发生长。

items.def_en: [I/T] to develop roots and establish biological anchorage for growth
items.ex_en: These plant cuttings should root properly if you keep the soil moist enough.
items.ex_zh: 如果保持土壤足够湿润，这些植物插条应该能好好生根。
items.ex2_en: The gardener rooted the fresh rose cuttings in well-drained organic compost.
items.ex2_zh: 园丁把新鲜的玫瑰插条扦插生根在排水良好的有机堆肥中。

items.def_en: to produce or develop vegetative buds or nascent flowers
items.ex_en: The cherry trees along the pathway start to bud when warmer days arrive.
items.ex_zh: 随着天气转暖，小路两旁的樱花树开始打苞萌蕾。

items.def_zh: （树桩或植物）萌发新枝，分蘖；排便
items.def_en: 1. (botany) When a plant or stump stools, it sends up new shoots from the base or roots. 2. (medical) To pass solid bodily waste from the bowels.
items.ex_en: After the harsh coppicing, the ancient chestnut trunk began to stool vigorously.
items.ex_zh: 经过重度修剪后，那株古老的栗树树桩基部开始强健地分蘖抽枝。

items.def_en: 1. When plants or seeds sprout, they begin to grow and produce new shoots or buds. 2. To appear or develop suddenly and in large numbers.
items.ex_en: Tiny vegetable seeds will sprout within a few days under warm, moist conditions.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖湿润的环境下，微小的蔬菜种子几天内就会发芽。
items.ex2_en: The spring sunshine sprouted tender green buds on the dormant apple trees.
items.ex2_zh: 春日阳光让休眠的苹果树抽出了嫩绿的幼芽。

items.def_zh: 发芽，萌芽；（想法等）开始酝酿
items.def_en: When a seed or plant germinates, it begins to grow; when an idea germinates, it starts to develop.
items.ex_en: The rare seeds will not germinate unless the environmental conditions remain optimal.
items.ex_zh: 除非环境条件保持最佳，否则这些珍稀种子不会发芽。
items.ex2_en: Warm spring rains quickly germinate the tiny wildflower seeds buried in the garden soil.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖的春雨迅速使埋在花园土壤里的野花种子发芽。

items.def_zh: 拔节长高；迅速长出幼茎
items.def_en: grow rapidly taller from a shoot or stem
items.ex_en: Those sunflower plants shoot up so fast once summer temperatures rise.
items.ex_zh: 一到入夏气温升高，那些向日葵就拔节疯长起来。

items.def_en: (often + up) to grow rapidly upwards from the ground or a plant stem
items.ex_en: Fresh asparagus stems shoot above the ground during early morning hours.
items.ex_zh: 清晨时分，新鲜的芦笋嫩茎便会破土冒出。

items.def_zh: 萌发新芽；迅速抽芽生长
items.def_en: to begin to grow buds or young leaves; to rapidly develop and expand
items.ex_en: In early May, the orchard trees burgeon with countless pale blossoms and leaves.
items.ex_zh: 五月初，果园的树木萌发出无数淡雅的花朵与嫩叶。

groups.summary_en: A seed, spore, or botanical organism initiates growth and produces preliminary vegetative parts such as buds, roots, or shoots. Often used intransitively, or transitively when causing seeds to put out shoots.
groups.summary_zh: 种子或植物打破休眠萌发生长，抽芽生根或迅速冒出幼苗。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the initial emergence and emergence-driven expansion of new plant tissue from seeds or dormancy, contrasting with mature vegetative flourishing or sheer height growth.
groups.desc_zh: 指植物种子萌发或休眠组织初生破土的生命力爆发，区别于成熟期植物的繁茂或单纯的高度增长。
groups.nuance_en: germinate: internal activation and initial emergence from a seed or spore (seed / idea / spore) · sprout: outward emergence of tender green shoots or buds (wheat / seed / hair) · bud: formation of immature unopened shoots or flowers (rose / tree / talent) · shoot up: rapid, vigorous vertical growth spurt (weeds / bamboo / child)
groups.nuance_zh: germinate: 种子或孢子在微观上萌动、生根发芽 (seed / idea / spore) · sprout: 嫩芽破土或毛发初生破出 (wheat / seed / hair) · bud: 植物打苞、孕育未绽的花芽 (rose / tree / talent) · shoot up: 迅猛垂直蹿高或爆发式抽穗 (weeds / bamboo / child)

groups.name: Strike with Rod or Strap · 抽打与鞭笞 (Whip, Lash, Flog)
groups.tip: 用皮鞭或长物猛烈抽击

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) strike suddenly and violently towards someone with or as with a whip
items.ex_en: The angry driver raised his whip and began to lash out at the runaway horse.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的马车夫扬起鞭子，猛烈抽打那匹受惊奔跑的马。

items.def_en: (+ sth) swing or strike violently using a flexible lash or strap
items.ex_en: The trainer had to whip around his flexible leather strap to drive off the beast.
items.ex_zh: 驯兽师不得不挥动柔软的皮鞭抽打，以驱离那头猛兽。

items.def_en: to hit a person or animal repeatedly with a whip or strap
items.ex_en: The cruel master threatened to whip the stray dog if it approached the porch.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的主人威胁说，如果流浪狗靠近门廊，就要用鞭子狠狠抽它。

items.def_en: to punish someone by striking them with a slender cane
items.ex_en: The strict headmaster would cane misbehaving students across the palms as punishment.
items.ex_zh: 这位严厉的校长会用藤条击打调皮学生的手掌以示惩罚。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack someone forcefully with severe physical blows or strokes
items.ex_en: He grabbed a thick belt and began to lay into the intruder without hesitation.
items.ex_zh: 他操起一根粗皮带，毫不犹豫地猛抽痛打那个闯入者。

items.def_zh: 抽打，鞭打；猛烈冲击；严厉指责；捆绑
items.def_en: 1. To hit someone or something violently with a whip, strap, or rope. 2. To beat or strike forcefully against something (like wind or rain). 3. To tie or fasten securely with a cord or rope.
items.ex_en: The cruel guard proceeded to lash the exhausted prisoner across the back.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的守卫接着用鞭子抽打那名筋疲力尽的囚犯的后背。

items.def_en: To flog or whip someone with a bundle of birch twigs as a formal physical punishment.
items.ex_en: In colonial schools, authorities would birch unruly youths to enforce strict classroom discipline.
items.ex_zh: 在殖民时期的学校里，当局会用桦条鞭笞不守规矩的青年以严格维持课堂纪律。

items.def_zh: 鞭打，痛打；彻底击败；剧烈扭动，翻腾
items.def_en: 1. To hit or beat a person or animal repeatedly with a stick or whip. 2. To decisively defeat an opponent. 3. To flail or move limbs violently and wildly.
items.ex_en: The farmer grabbed a stout stick and began to thrash the attacking stray dog.
items.ex_zh: 农夫抓起一根粗木棍，对着扑上来的流浪狗一顿痛打。

items.def_en: to beat someone harshly as a formal or severe physical punishment
items.ex_en: The naval tribunal ordered the officer to flog the deserter before the crew.
items.ex_zh: 海军法庭命令军官在全体船员面前公开严惩并鞭笞这名逃兵。

items.def_en: to whip severely using a multi-thonged lash; inflict painful punishment
items.ex_en: The fanatical penitents chose to scourge their bare flesh with knotted cords.
items.ex_zh: 狂热的忏悔者选择用带结的绳索残酷笞责自己赤裸的皮肉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail striking a person or animal forcefully with an implement such as a whip, birch rod, or belt, distinguished by the physical instrument, repetition, and severity of punishment.
groups.summary_zh: 用鞭子、藤条或棍棒反复猛烈抽打、鞭笞或实施体罚。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the punitive or disciplinary delivery of sharp, flexible kinetic blows via an implement, contrasting with blunt bludgeoning or bare-knuckle striking.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用柔性或长条形器具（鞭、杖、条）进行的惩罚性或抽击性打击，区别于钝器重击或赤手挥拳。
groups.nuance_en: whip: striking with a flexible lash with rapid stinging snaps (horse / cream / tail) · lash: delivering forceful, sweeping, punitive strokes (prisoner / sail / rain) · flog: heavy, repeated judicial or systematic scourging (soldier / convict / back) · cane: disciplinary striking using a stiff slender rod (pupil / offender / hand) · birch: formal corporal punishment with a bundle of birch twigs (criminal / boy / buttocks) · thrash: violent, unrestrained physical beating (opponent / bully / crops)
groups.nuance_zh: whip: 用软鞭等轻快抽打或带破风声地劈打 (horse / cream / tail) · lash: 猛烈、横扫式的抽打或风雨扑打 (prisoner / sail / rain) · flog: 严酷、成套的司法或惩罚性笞刑 (soldier / convict / back) · cane: 用藤条、教鞭进行的纪律性体罚 (pupil / offender / hand) · birch: 用白桦枝条束施加的传统笞刑 (criminal / boy / buttocks) · thrash: 痛打、狂暴地暴揍一顿 (opponent / bully / crops)

groups.name: Suggest Indirectly & Convey · 暗示与体现 (Imply, Insinuate, Bespeak)
groups.tip: 言在此而意在彼，含蓄传递深层内涵

items.def_en: to suggest that something is true without saying it directly
items.ex_en: The financial audit seemed to imply that public funds had been severely mismanaged.
items.ex_zh: 财务审计似乎暗指公共资金遭到了严重的管理不善。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ at) to suggest something indirectly or provide a subtle clue
items.ex_en: The manager chose to hint subtly rather than reveal the upcoming promotions directly.
items.ex_zh: 经理选择委婉地透露口风，而不是直接宣布即将进行的晋升。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to suggest or refer to something indirectly
items.ex_en: Her mysterious remarks seemed to hint at an unexpected secret within the family.
items.ex_zh: 她那神秘的话语似乎在暗示着这个家族内部的一个意外秘密。

items.def_en: (+ sth/sb) to mention someone or something in an indirect or casual way
items.ex_en: During his scholarly lecture, the professor did not allude to the ongoing scandal.
items.ex_zh: 在学术讲座中，教授并未间接提及那起正在发酵的丑闻。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to suggest that something is true, likely, or exists
items.ex_en: All available forensic clues point to deliberate sabotage at the chemical processing facility.
items.ex_zh: 所有现存的法医线索都表明该化工厂遭遇了蓄意破坏。

items.def_en: to state or make known subtly, delicately, or indirectly
items.ex_en: The diplomat managed to intimate his dissatisfaction without speaking any harsh words.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官并未说出任何严厉之词，却委婉示意了自己的不满。

items.def_zh: 显示，表明（bespeak 的过去式和过去分词）；预订
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of bespeak; to have shown, signaled, or suggested something.
items.ex_en: Her measured tone bespoke deep sorrow despite the polite smile on her face.
items.ex_zh: 尽管她脸上带着礼貌的微笑，她沉稳的语调却流露出深深的悲伤。

items.def_zh: 暗指，暗示（不快或不光彩的事）；讨好，巴结（insinuate oneself into）
items.def_en: 1. To suggest something bad or unpleasant in an indirect way. 2. (insinuate oneself into) to gain favor or acceptance by subtle manipulation.
items.ex_en: He tried to insinuate that his competitor achieved success through fraudulent business practices.
items.ex_zh: 他试图暗指他的竞争对手是通过欺诈性的商业手段取得成功的。

items.def_en: (of a word or idea) To suggest a feeling or meaning in addition to its literal meaning.
items.ex_en: For many people, the word home will connote warmth, security, and familial love.
items.ex_zh: 对许多人来说，“家”这个词意味着温暖、安全感与亲情。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To suggest or be a clear sign of something. 2. (formal/archaic) to order or reserve something in advance.
items.ex_en: His refined manners and extensive knowledge bespeak a privileged and cultured upbringing.
items.ex_zh: 他优雅的举止和渊博的知识表明他出身优渥且受过良好教养。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe conveying an idea, attitude, or quality indirectly rather than stating it plainly, ranging from subtle insinuation to formal evidence inherent in someone's actions.
groups.summary_zh: 非直接明说地表达想法或流露特征，含含蓄暗示或显露迹象。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the indirect conveyance of meaning through contextual inference or subtle clues, contrasting with explicit, verbatim declaration.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过语境推论、线索或征候间接传达含意，区别于直截了当的明确声明。
groups.nuance_en: imply: naturally entailing or indicating a conclusion without stating it (silence / reply / assumption) · hint: offering a slight, covert, or gentle pointer (possibility / answer / intention) · insinuate: stealthily introducing an unpleasant, derogatory, or sinister suspicion (nepotism / corruption / doubt) · intimate: gently and delicately communicating in a discreet or formal manner (wishes / intentions / approval) · bespeak: serving as external, tangible evidence that reveals a quality (character / elegance / confidence)
groups.nuance_zh: imply: 逻辑上必然暗含或言下之意指示 (silence / reply / assumption) · hint: 提供微小、隐晦的提示或暗示 (possibility / answer / intention) · insinuate: 拐弯抹角地含沙射影、渗透恶意猜疑 (nepotism / corruption / doubt) · intimate: 委婉、正式且私下地透露心意 (wishes / intentions / approval) · bespeak: 作为外在征象显著彰显出某种特质 (character / elegance / confidence)

groups.name: Take Action on a Matter · 处理与应对事务 (Deal with, Handle, Address)
groups.tip: 动手处理推进事宜

items.def_zh: 处理，应付，解决（deal with）；做买卖，经营；发牌；给予（打击）
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To take action to solve a problem or handle a situation. 2. (+ in/with) To buy and sell goods or do business. 3. To distribute playing cards to players. 4. To deliver or administer (a blow, shock, or punishment).
items.ex_en: Our customer support team must deal swiftly with every incoming user complaint.
items.ex_zh: 我们的客户支持团队必须迅速处理收到的每一单用户投诉。

items.def_en: (formal/business) To take official action on, process, or execute a request, plan, or matter.
items.ex_en: The compliance department will action your formal request within three working days.
items.ex_zh: 合规部门将在三个工作日内处理并执行您的正式申请。

items.def_en: to give attention to and begin to deal with an issue, problem, or query
items.ex_en: The city council convened an urgent meeting to address the worsening housing crisis.
items.ex_zh: 市议会召开紧急会议，设法应对日益恶化的住房危机。

items.def_en: to manage, deal with, or be responsible for handling a situation or task
items.ex_en: Only experienced technicians are qualified to handle these delicate laboratory instruments properly.
items.ex_zh: 只有经验丰富的技术人员才有资格妥善处置这些精密的实验室仪器。

items.def_en: to deal with business, practical tasks, or someone's specific needs
items.ex_en: I must attend to an urgent matter before I leave the office.
items.ex_zh: 我离开办公室前必须先处理一件紧急事务。

items.def_en: to attend to or make certain that a required task is carried out
items.ex_en: Don't worry about the catering for the party; I'll see to it.
items.ex_zh: 别担心聚会的餐饮问题，我会负责照料妥当的。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to take suitable action in order to solve a problem or complete a task
items.ex_en: The newly hired security officer knows how to deal with rowdy bar patrons.
items.ex_zh: 新聘用的安保人员懂得如何应付那些吵闹不休的酒吧顾客。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to deal with, organize, or take necessary measures regarding a situation
items.ex_en: I need to see about the broken air conditioner before summer starts.
items.ex_zh: 我得在夏天来临前着手处理修空调的事。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to organize, resolve, or successfully handle a problem or matter
items.ex_en: We must sort out these scheduling conflicts before sending the final meeting invites.
items.ex_zh: 在发送最终会议邀请之前，我们必须妥善解决这些日程冲突。

items.def_zh: 处理，应付；做生意；发牌（deal 的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of deal; took action to solve a problem, did business, or distributed cards.
items.ex_en: The senior manager dealt with the complicated supplier contract very effectively yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 高级经理昨天非常高效地处理了那份复杂的供应商合同。

groups.summary_en: Verbs denoting taking decisive administrative, managerial, or practical measures to resolve a problem, request, or situation.
groups.summary_zh: 针对问题、请求或既定事务采取行动予以处理或解决。
groups.desc_en: Denotes taking practical responsibility and initiating concrete procedures to resolve a task or situation, contrasting with passive acknowledgment or mere strategic contemplation.
groups.desc_zh: 指对事务承担起实际责任并着手进行流程处置，区别于消极知晓或纯理论探讨。
groups.nuance_en: deal with: broad engagement to manage, resolve, or cope with a matter (problem / customer / reality) · handle: dexterously managing, controlling, or operating a delicate situation (crisis / complaint / machinery) · address: focusing direct intellectual or operational effort onto a specific issue (concern / question / imbalance) · action: formally executing or processing an operational task (request / item / recommendation) · attend to: giving dedicated care, service, or administrative focus to (needs / visitor / duties)
groups.nuance_zh: deal with: 广泛介入以应对、打交道或解决事务 (problem / customer / reality) · handle: 熟练操纵、掌控敏感棘手的人或局势 (crisis / complaint / machinery) · address: 集中精力直接探讨或对准治理核心问题 (concern / question / imbalance) · action: 正式将建议或任务付诸行政执行 (request / item / recommendation) · attend to: 专心照料、接待或按序处理业务 (needs / visitor / duties)

groups.name: Theft & Burglary · 偷盗与侵入行窃 (Steal, Burgle, Rob)
groups.tip: 从暗偷到明火执仗

items.def_en: [I/T] to steal things of little value, typically in small quantities repeatedly
items.ex_en: Dishonest warehouse workers would regularly pilfer small electronic components from the assembly line.
items.ex_zh: 不诚实的仓库工人经常从装配线上顺手牵羊偷拿小型电子元件。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to take or steal something, often casually or without permission
items.ex_en: Someone managed to walk off with my expensive umbrella while I visited the restroom.
items.ex_zh: 我去洗手间的时候，有人顺手牵羊拿走了我昂贵的雨伞。

items.def_en: [I/T] to take another person's property without permission or legal right and without intention of returning it
items.ex_en: A masked intruder managed to steal valuable diamond jewelry from the display case.
items.ex_zh: 一名蒙面入侵者成功从陈列柜中偷盗了昂贵的钻石珠宝。

items.def_en: to secretly take something of minor value in a casual or sneaky manner
items.ex_en: The sneaky boy tried to filch a few shiny coins from his uncle's desk.
items.ex_zh: 那个鬼鬼祟祟的男孩试图从他叔叔的书桌上顺走几枚光亮的硬币。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to steal something and hurry away with it
items.ex_en: Thieves broke into the gallery and made off with three priceless paintings.
items.ex_zh: 盗贼闯入画廊，盗走了三幅无价的名画。

items.def_en: to enter a building illegally and by force, especially in order to steal
items.ex_en: Thieves attempted to break in through the rear basement window late last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚深夜，盗贼企图破开后地下室的窗户入室行窃。

items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British) To enter a building illegally in order to steal property from it.
items.ex_en: Masked intruders broke a downstairs window to burgle the empty suburban residence.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面歹徒打破楼下的窗户，潜入这栋空无一人的郊区住宅行窃。

items.def_en: 1. (chiefly North American) To enter a building illegally in order to steal property from it.
items.ex_en: Prowlers managed to burglarize three suburban homes while the owners were on vacation.
items.ex_zh: 在房主外出度假期间，潜行小偷成功入室洗劫了三户郊区住宅。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to rob someone or a place using violence or threats with a weapon
items.ex_en: Two armed men tried to hold up the convenience store late last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚深夜，两名持枪男子企图持械抢劫那家便利店。

items.def_en: (+ of) to take property unlawfully from a person or place by force or threat of force
items.ex_en: The desperate thief decided to rob the elderly traveler of her expensive purse.
items.ex_zh: 绝望的盗贼决定强行夺取那位年长旅客昂贵的手提包。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the illicit, non-consensual taking of another party's property, scaling in intensity from stealthy theft without force to trespassing break-ins and violent confrontation.
groups.summary_zh: 指非法侵占他人财产，从隐秘盗窃递增至破门入室行窃乃至暴力抢夺。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the unlawful, clandestine or forcible appropriation of another's property, differentiated along lines of entry trespass, scale, and stealth.
groups.desc_zh: 指非法、秘密或强行侵占他人财产的行为，依非法侵入、金额体量及隐秘程度呈现级差，区别于合法的没收或借用。
groups.nuance_en: steal: general unlawful taking of another's property without consent (wallet / jewelry / thunder) · burgle: unlawful breaking and entering a premises specifically to commit theft (house / office / safe) · pilfer: repeatedly stealing items of petty value or small quantities (stationery / food / petty cash) · filch: stealthily and swiftly snatching something of minor consequence (keys / cookie / purse) · walk off with: brazenly or opportunistically pocketing and leaving with an item (trophy / prize / phone)
groups.nuance_zh: steal: 最核心的偷窃、非法剥夺所有权 (wallet / jewelry / thunder) · burgle: 破门入室或潜入建筑进行盗窃 (house / office / safe) · pilfer: 顺手牵羊、零星偷拿小额财物 (stationery / food / petty cash) · filch: 动作敏捷、神不知鬼不觉地摸走小物件 (keys / cookie / purse) · walk off with: 公然顺走、据为己有或顺手带走 (trophy / prize / phone)

groups.name: Thermal Liquid Cooking · 沸水烹煮与热油煎炸 (Boil, Bubble, Fry)
groups.tip: 厨房烹饪与受热油炸场景

items.def_en: 1. To cook food in hot oil or fat. 2. (informal) To burn or be burned by excessive heat or sunlight.
items.ex_en: Forget sunscreen at this scorching beach and your bare skin will certainly fry.
items.ex_zh: 在这烈日炎炎的海滩上要是忘了涂防晒霜，你的皮肤肯定会被晒伤。
items.ex2_en: The chef decided to fry the fresh fish fillets in hot olive oil.
items.ex2_zh: 厨师决定在热橄榄油中煎新鲜的鱼柳。

items.def_zh: 起泡，沸腾冒泡；（情感）翻腾，洋溢
items.def_en: 1. To produce or emit bubbles, especially when heated or boiling. 2. To be full of a particular feeling or quality.
items.ex_en: The rich tomato sauce began to bubble gently inside the cast-iron skillet.
items.ex_zh: 浓郁的番茄酱在铸铁平底锅里开始轻轻地冒泡沸腾。

items.def_zh: 煮沸，烧开；（液体）沸腾；暴怒，怒火中烧
items.def_en: 1. To heat a liquid until it bubbles and turns to gas, or to cook food in boiling water. 2. To be very angry.
items.ex_en: You need to boil the fresh tap water thoroughly before drinking it.
items.ex_zh: 在饮用之前，你需要把新鲜的自来水彻底烧开。
items.ex2_en: The soup on the stove began to boil vigorously after several quiet minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 炉子上的汤在平静了几分钟后开始剧烈沸腾。

items.def_en: to cook food quickly in a small amount of hot oil or fat
items.ex_en: Heat some butter and sauté the sliced mushrooms until they turn golden brown.
items.ex_zh: 加热少许黄油，将切片的蘑菇翻炒至表面呈金黄色。

items.def_en: to boil and spill out over the edges of a pot or container
items.ex_en: If you do not lower the stove heat, the warm milk will boil over.
items.ex_zh: 如果你不把炉火调小，温热的牛奶就会煮溢出锅。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce a cooking liquid or food by continuous heating and boiling
items.ex_en: You should boil down the savory broth until it thickens into a rich glaze.
items.ex_zh: 你应该将鲜美的肉汤熬浓收汁，直到它浓稠成一层发亮的芡汁。
items.ex2_en: The sweet apple cider will boil down into a dark syrup over low heat.
items.ex2_zh: 甜苹果酒在小火下会熬浓成深色糖浆。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cook or heat food in a pan using hot fat or oil
items.ex_en: Let's fry up some leftover rice and vegetables for a quick lunch.
items.ex_zh: 我们用剩下的米饭和蔬菜炒个饭当快餐吧。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cook gently in liquid kept just below or barely at the boiling point
items.ex_en: Leave the spicy vegetable curry to simmer gently on the stove for an hour.
items.ex_zh: 把香辣蔬菜咖喱放在炉子上用文火慢煨一个小时。
items.ex2_en: The seasoned beef stew simmered quietly on the back burner for two hours.
items.ex2_zh: 调味好的牛肉炖菜在后炉头上静静慢炖了两个小时。

items.def_zh: 水煮；汆（在微沸温水中煮）
items.def_en: to cook food gently in simmering water or another liquid
items.ex_en: The chef prefers to poach fresh eggs in gently simmering water with vinegar.
items.ex_zh: 主厨喜欢在加了醋的微沸温水中水煮新鲜鸡蛋。

items.def_en: to bubble and churn violently under intense heat
items.ex_en: Hot bubbling oil began to seethe violently in the deep fryer at peak heat.
items.ex_zh: 油炸锅达到最高温时，滚烫的热油开始剧烈翻腾沸腾。

groups.summary_en: Food or liquids are subjected to direct high heat, cooking through bubbling liquids, rapid boiling, or sizzling oil in a pan or pot.
groups.summary_zh: 指利用沸水翻滚或热油煎炸等液态高热介质进行熟化加热的烹饪场景。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the thermal transformation of food using liquid or fat media across various boiling and searing thresholds, contrasting with dry-heat roasting or baking.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用水相或油脂热介质在不同沸腾/煎灼阈值下加热食物，区别于干热烘烤或炙烤。
groups.nuance_en: boil: cooking in liquid sustained at or above its rapid bubbling point (potatoes / eggs / water) · simmer: cooking gently in liquid just below the boiling point with tiny occasional bubbles (soup / sauce / stew) · fry: cooking in hot oil or fat over medium to high heat (fish / eggs / chips) · sauté: quickly frying small pieces of food in a minimal film of fat over high heat (mushrooms / onions / garlic) · bubble: gurgling and producing vapor pockets while cooking or boiling (broth / stew / cauldron)
groups.nuance_zh: boil: 在沸水滚腾中剧烈烹煮 (potatoes / eggs / water) · simmer: 微沸文火慢炖，偶冒细小气泡 (soup / sauce / stew) · fry: 在热油或脂肪中煎炸 (fish / eggs / chips) · sauté: 旺火少油快速煸炒嫩煎 (mushrooms / onions / garlic) · bubble: 汤汁受热咕嘟冒泡地沸动 (broth / stew / cauldron)

groups.name: Threaten & Intimidate · 威吓与慑服
groups.tip: 仗势欺人恐吓弱小者

items.def_en: to state one's intention to take hostile action against someone in retribution
items.ex_en: The blackmailer continued to threaten the executive with leaking confidential corporate documents.
items.ex_zh: 敲诈者继续恐吓这名高管，威胁要泄露公司的机密文件。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to use threats, intimidation, or pressure to force someone to comply
items.ex_en: She had to lean heavily on her family during those tough months.
items.ex_zh: 在那段艰难的岁月里，她不得不极度依赖家人的支持。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to bully, intimidate, or give rude orders to someone
items.ex_en: Don't let them push you around; you have rights as a tenant.
items.ex_zh: 别让他们摆布你；作为租客你也是有权利的。

items.def_zh: 严密监视威逼；凌驾威吓
items.def_en: (+ sb) to stand close to someone in an intimidating way to force them to act
items.ex_en: The manager liked to stand over junior clerks until they finished their paperwork.
items.ex_zh: 经理喜欢威逼式地站在初级职员身旁，直到他们把文件做完。

items.def_en: to intimidate someone with aggressive, bullying language or domineering facial expressions
items.ex_en: The aggressive prosecutor attempted to browbeat the nervous witness into changing her testimony.
items.ex_zh: 咄咄逼人的检察官企图以严词喝斥来威逼紧张的证人改变口供。

items.def_zh: 恐吓，威胁，欺侮；横行霸道
items.def_en: To frighten, hurt, or threaten a smaller or weaker person, or force someone into doing something by using intimidation.
items.ex_en: Older kids in the neighborhood used to bully younger children for their lunch money.
items.ex_zh: 附近大一点的孩子过去常常恐吓勒索小孩子的午餐费。

items.def_en: To frighten or subdue someone into doing what one wants, especially through threats or a show of power.
items.ex_en: The proud rebels refused to be cowed by the tyrant's ruthless display of power.
items.ex_zh: 骄傲的叛逆者拒绝被暴君展示的残酷权力所吓倒。

items.def_en: To frighten or threaten someone, usually in order to persuade them to do what you want.
items.ex_en: The corrupt official tried to intimidate the journalists into dropping their sensitive investigation.
items.ex_zh: 那个腐败官员企图恐吓记者，迫使他们放弃敏感的调查。

items.def_en: to subdue or restrain someone by inspiring overwhelming respect or fear
items.ex_en: The humble delegates were visibly overawed by the majestic grandeur of the ancient palace.
items.ex_zh: 谦卑的代表们显然被古老宫殿雄伟庄严的威势震慑住了。

items.def_en: to severely frighten someone over time using systematic threats, violence, or brutality
items.ex_en: Armed gangs continued to terrorize the local villagers with nightly raids and violent threats.
items.ex_zh: 武装团伙继续通过夜间袭击和暴力威胁使当地村民陷入恐惧。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe using force, threats, or domineering demeanor to frighten someone into submission or compliance. They scale upward from persistent verbal/physical bullying to paralyzing psychological intimidation that breaks another's spirit.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过恐吓、威胁或强势举动压制他人，迫使其屈服或胆怯。
groups.desc_en: Denotes coercing or subduing another's will through displays of impending harm, superior power, or psychological oppression, contrasting with rational persuasion.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过明示将遭惩害、实力悬殊或心理重压迫使对方屈服，区别于理性的劝说或论辩。
groups.nuance_en: threaten: expressing an explicit or implicit intent to inflict harm or misfortune (witness / sanctions / violence) · intimidate: generating overwhelming fear, awe, or inferiority to force compliance (jury / opponent / competitor) · bully: systematically tormenting or persecuting a weaker individual (classmate / subordinate / peer) · browbeat: haranguing and badgering someone insolently into submission (witness / suspect / employee) · cow: thoroughly subduing into timid passivity through daunting fear (populace / workers / dissidents)
groups.nuance_zh: threaten: 扬言施加伤害、预告不利后果以示威慑 (witness / sanctions / violence) · intimidate: 凭借威势令人敬畏自卑、不敢妄动 (jury / opponent / competitor) · bully: 恃强凌弱、霸凌欺侮弱小 (classmate / subordinate / peer) · browbeat: 盛气凌人地厉声呵斥、威逼就范 (witness / suspect / employee) · cow: 以压倒性恐吓彻底慑服，使之畏葸不前 (populace / workers / dissidents)

groups.name: Throw & Loft · 投掷与高抛 (Lob, Pitch, Hurl)
groups.tip: 大力击球凌空高飞

items.def_en: [I/T] to throw something lightly, casually, or easily with an underarm motion
items.ex_en: He decided to toss the car keys lightly across the table to his brother.
items.ex_zh: 他随手把车钥匙轻轻扔过桌子递给他的兄弟。

items.def_en: to throw something in a casual, careless, or offhand manner
items.ex_en: Just chuck your coat onto the sofa and come into the warm kitchen.
items.ex_zh: 随便把外套往沙发上一扔，快进暖和的厨房来吧。

items.def_zh: 高抛，把（球）击成高弧线；投掷
items.def_en: To throw, hit, or kick a ball high into the air in a slow, curved arc.
items.ex_en: The midfielder managed to lob the ball over the advancing goalkeeper into the net.
items.ex_zh: 中场球员巧妙地将球高抛挑过出击的门将，飞入球网。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to throw or fling something away forcefully
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to toss or throw something casually or discard it by throwing
items.ex_en: Don't chuck out those magazines because my sister wants to read them later.
items.ex_zh: 别把那些杂志扔掉，因为我妹妹待会儿还想看。

items.def_zh: 投掷，抛，（棒球中）投球；搭（帐篷），扎（营）；竭力推销；向前倾跌；颠簸
items.def_en: 1. To throw or toss something, especially a ball in baseball; 2. to set up a tent or camp; 3. to promote an idea or product.
items.ex_en: The ace pitcher prepared to pitch the baseball with incredible speed and spin.
items.ex_zh: 王牌投手准备以惊人的速度和旋转投出棒球。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to throw something outwards with sudden violence or force
items.ex_en: In a fit of fury, she started to fling out old letters onto the lawn.
items.ex_zh: 在一阵狂怒之下，她开始将旧信件狠狠甩到草坪上。

items.def_zh: 把（球）高高击向空中；将（画作）挂得过高
items.def_en: (especially in sports) To hit, kick, or throw a ball high into the air.
items.ex_en: The nervous batter managed to sky the ball straight up toward the cloudless afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的击球手失误把球高高击向了晴空万里的午后天空。

items.def_zh: 猛投，用力掷；厉声说出，大声叫骂（侮辱等）
items.def_en: To throw something with great force or violence; to utter insults or accusations vehemently.
items.ex_en: Angry demonstrators began to hurl heavy cobblestones at the retreating line of riot police.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的示威者开始向后撤的防暴警察队列猛投沉重的鹅卵石。

items.def_en: to throw something violently, recklessly, or with significant force
items.ex_en: He was so furious that he would fling the heavy phone across the room.
items.ex_zh: 他愤怒至极，把沉重的电话狠狠摔到了房间另一头。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey throwing an object through the air with a particular trajectory, speed, or targeted mechanical delivery (e.g., high gentle arcs vs. forceful aggressive heaves).
groups.summary_zh: 指依据特定的抛物线、速度或姿态将物体掷出或打向空中。
groups.desc_en: Denotes projecting a projectile through the air along a high, calculated, or relaxed trajectory, contrasting with flat-trajectory shooting, hard horizontal hurling, or simple dropping.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过空中有弧度的抛物线、轻缓或有控制地向上抛投物体，区别于平直射击、猛力贯击或垂直脱手坠落。
groups.nuance_en: toss: casual, light, upward throwing with an easy motion (coin / salad / ball) · lob: lofting high into the air in a steep arc over an obstacle (grenade / ball / artillery) · pitch: deliberately aiming and throwing towards a target or batsman (baseball / tent / hay) · chuck: careless, informal, or dismissive pitching aside (stone / keys / rubbish) · sky: striking or propelling a ball steeply and almost vertically into the heavens (ball / drive / shot)
groups.nuance_zh: toss: 随手轻抛、往上颠投 (coin / salad / ball) · lob: 越过障碍的高弧度高吊、慢速抛送 (grenade / ball / artillery) · pitch: 定向瞄准投掷，或特定角度用力掷出 (baseball / tent / hay) · chuck: 口语随意抛甩、漫不经心丢弃 (stone / keys / rubbish) · sky: 将球高高击向或抛入云霄 (ball / drive / shot)

groups.name: Trim & Shave · 修剪与刮削 (Surface Material Removal)
groups.tip: 刀具修削刮去多余

items.def_en: to make neat or tidy by clipping, cutting away irregular parts
items.ex_en: The careful gardener used sharp shears to trim the messy hedge along the walkway.
items.ex_zh: 细心的园丁用锋利的剪刀修剪了步道旁杂乱的树篱。

items.def_en: to peel or cut away the outer skin or edges of an object with a knife
items.ex_en: The chef instructed the apprentice to pare the thick rind from the golden citrus.
items.ex_zh: 主厨吩咐学徒用刀削去金黄柑橘上厚厚的外皮。

items.def_en: (carpentry / engineering) To cut away a sharp right-angled edge of wood, stone, or metal to make a sloping bevel.
items.ex_en: The artisan used a sharp drawknife to chamfer the hard timber edges with grace.
items.ex_zh: 工匠用锋利的刮刀优雅地将坚硬木料的直角边削成斜角。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to trim, pare, or prune plants and bushes to reduce their size
items.ex_en: You should cut back the overgrown rose bushes before the harsh winter weather arrives.
items.ex_zh: 你应该在严冬来临之前将过度生长的玫瑰灌木修剪修短。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut away outer edges or surfaces gradually with a blade
items.ex_en: The carpenter began to pare down the wooden plank until it fit the doorway.
items.ex_zh: 木匠开始用刀片削减木板外缘，直到它契合门框。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove a thin surface layer or hair by shaving or paring
items.ex_en: The woodworker had to shave off a thin sliver of timber to make it fit.
items.ex_zh: 木工不得不刨掉木料表面薄薄的一层，使其能够严丝合缝。

items.def_en: to cut off hair or thin slivers of material from a surface with a razor or plane
items.ex_en: He used a sharp hand plane to shave uneven ridges off the wooden table.
items.ex_zh: 他用锋利的手刨从木桌表面刮去不平的凸起。

items.def_en: To shave, cut, or slice closely with a razor.
items.ex_en: The barber used a straight blade to razor the sensitive skin along his neck.
items.ex_zh: 理发师用折叠剃刀紧贴着修刮他颈部的敏感皮肤。

items.def_zh: 割（草、谷物等）；大量杀死，撂倒（mow down）
items.def_en: 1. To cut down grass or crops using a machine or scythe. 2. ('mow down') To kill or knock down people in large numbers.
items.ex_en: My grandfather prefers to mow the sprawling green lawn every single Saturday morning without fail.
items.ex_zh: 我祖父偏爱在每个周六早晨雷打不动地修剪那片广阔的绿草坪。

items.def_en: to cut wool or fleece from an animal, or clip off roughly with large shears
items.ex_en: The seasoned farmers will shear the flock of sheep before the hot summer begins.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的农夫们将在炎夏来临之前给这群绵羊剪羊毛。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate shaving, cutting back, or paring away outer surface layers, edges, or foliage using edged tools or blades to smooth or shorten them.
groups.summary_zh: 使用刀片或工具剃除、削平、修短表面材料、草木或边缘。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the subtractive reduction or planar smoothing of an outer layer or edge using a sharp blade, contrasting with shearing severance or blunt fracturing.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用锋利刃具对工件外皮、边缘实施微量切削、平整或修齐，区别于粗暴断裂或整体截断。
groups.nuance_en: trim: clipping or pruning outer fringes to neaten or size down (beard / hedge / budget) · pare: peeling or slicing off thin outermost skins or incrementally slashing away (apple / nails / costs) · shave: scraping or cutting very close to a surface to make it smooth (beard / wood / seconds) · chamfer: cutting away a sharp right-angled edge to produce a symmetrical bevel (beam / timber / stone) · cut back: systematically reducing scale or volume by excise (expenditure / workforce / vines)
groups.nuance_zh: trim: 剪齐边角、修剪边缘以使其规整 (beard / hedge / budget) · pare: 削皮、层层刨削或逐步大幅缩减 (apple / nails / costs) · shave: 贴紧表面刮净削薄，或微幅压减 (beard / wood / seconds) · chamfer: 倒角、把硬直边角削切出斜面 (beam / timber / stone) · cut back: 计划性削减规模、精简多余部分 (expenditure / workforce / vines)

groups.name: Undo Fasteners & Open Wrapping · 解开与旋开 (Unfasten, Untie, Unzip)
groups.tip: 解开扣子、螺丝等束缚

items.def_en: (+ sth) to unfasten and remove a piece of clothing or accessory
items.ex_en: He stepped inside the warm house and proceeded to take off his heavy overcoat.
items.ex_zh: 他走入温暖的屋内，随之解开扣子脱下了厚重的大衣。

items.def_en: to unfasten a buckle or an item secured with a buckle
items.ex_en: The weary driver leaned back and waited to unbuckle her tight seatbelt at last.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的司机向后靠去，终于伸手解开了系得很紧的安全带。
items.ex2_en: The worn leather harness unbuckled suddenly under the horse's immense pulling weight.
items.ex2_zh: 磨损的皮马具在马巨大的拉力下突然解开了扣子。

items.def_en: to open something fastened with a zipper
items.ex_en: She had to unzip her heavy winter parka as soon as she entered school.
items.ex_zh: 她一走进学校就不得不拉开厚重的冬季派克大衣的拉链。
items.ex2_en: Her canvas backpack unzipped unexpectedly, spilling notebooks and pencils across the hallway floor.
items.ex2_zh: 她的帆布背包意外拉开了拉链，把笔记本和铅笔散落了一地。

items.def_en: to undo a knot, string, ribbon, or shoe lace, or free something secured by a knot
items.ex_en: The boy paused to untie the tight knot securing his dirty running shoes today.
items.ex_zh: 男孩停下脚步，解开系紧他脏旧跑鞋的死结。
items.ex2_en: His loose shoelaces untied automatically while he was jogging across the park path.
items.ex2_zh: 他在公园小路上慢跑时，松垮的鞋带自行解开了。

items.def_en: To remove the paper, cloth, or other covering from a parcel, gift, or food item.
items.ex_en: The excited child could hardly wait to unwrap the bright birthday present from grandma.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的孩子迫不及待地想拆开奶奶送来的鲜艳生日礼物包装。
items.ex2_en: The delicate flower petals unwrapped slowly under the warm morning sunlight today.
items.ex2_zh: 娇嫩的花瓣今天在温暖的晨光中缓缓舒展开来。

items.def_zh: 旋开，拧开，旋松（螺丝或瓶盖等）
items.def_en: To loosen or remove something (such as a screw, lid, or bulb) by twisting or turning it.
items.ex_en: He gripped the glass jar firmly to unscrew the tight lid with great effort.
items.ex_zh: 他紧紧握住玻璃罐，使出浑身解数去拧开紧闭的盖子。
items.ex2_en: The rusted metal bolt unscrewed easily after he applied lubricating oil overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 在他敷上润滑油过夜后，生锈的金属螺栓很容易就旋开了。

items.def_en: To undo the buttons of an item of clothing.
items.ex_en: He decided to unbutton the top collar of his shirt in the stifling heat.
items.ex_zh: 在令人窒息的闷热中，他决定解开衬衫领口最上面的纽扣。
items.ex2_en: The silk vest unbuttoned easily as she moved across the dressing room floor.
items.ex2_zh: 当她穿过更衣室地板走动时，丝绸背心的扣子轻易解开了。

items.def_en: to undo or open something that is fixed closed, such as a belt, latch, or buckle
items.ex_en: Passengers were strictly advised not to unfasten their safety restraints until the light ceased.
items.ex_zh: 乘客被严格告诫在指示灯熄灭之前切勿解开安全约束装置。
items.ex2_en: The old window latch unfastened suddenly during the violent gusts of mountain wind.
items.ex2_zh: 老旧的窗栓在猛烈的山风阵风中突然解开了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to strip or rip away outer wrapping, packaging, or binding
items.ex_en: She began to tear off the brown protective tape wrapped tightly around the parcel.
items.ex_zh: 她动手撕掉包裹外紧紧缠绕着的棕色防护胶带。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to tear open a parcel, envelope, or wrapped package forcefully
items.ex_en: He could not contain his excitement and proceeded to rip open the acceptance letter.
items.ex_zh: 他抑制不住激动的心情，一把扯开了那封录取信。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe physically releasing, loosening, or reversing a mechanical fastening, wrapping, or interlocking mechanism to open an item or free a bound object.
groups.summary_zh: 指解开纽扣、旋开螺丝或拆除包裹等逆向物理拆卸、松脱行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes reversing a mechanical fastening or wrapped closure to release, expose, or open an object, contrasting with tearing apart or destructive opening.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过反转机械咬合装置或解开包覆物以使其松脱开启，区别于破坏性撕开或整体砸开。
groups.nuance_en: unfasten: releasing any generic latch, catch, or securing bond (seatbelt / coat / lock) · untie: loosening and undoing knots, bows, or cords (knot / shoelaces / ribbon) · unzip: opening a slide fastener by pulling its slider (jacket / bag / fly) · unbuckle: releasing a buckle and strap mechanism (belt / harness / shoes) · unbutton: disengaging buttons from their buttonholes (shirt / jacket / collar) · unscrew: rotating threaded hardware counter to loosen it (cap / lid / bolt)
groups.nuance_zh: unfasten: 统称解开各种扣具、松开紧固件 (seatbelt / coat / lock) · untie: 解开绳结、带子或系带 (knot / shoelaces / ribbon) · unzip: 拉开拉链 (jacket / bag / fly) · unbuckle: 扣带脱扣、解开带扣 (belt / harness / shoes) · unbutton: 解开纽扣 (shirt / jacket / collar) · unscrew: 旋开螺纹盖或卸下螺丝 (cap / lid / bolt)

groups.name: Urge to Incite · 催促、煽动与鼓动 (Urge, Agitate, Incite)
groups.tip: 呼喝吆喝以催赶驱动前行

items.def_en: (+ on) to encourage or stimulate someone to act or achieve something
items.ex_en: The cheers of the passionate crowd seemed to spur on the exhausted marathon runner.
items.ex_zh: 热烈人群的欢呼声似乎激励着筋疲力尽的马拉松跑者奋力向前。

items.def_zh: （吆喝着）催马前进，赶牲口；催促，鼓动（常作 gee up）
items.def_en: (also 'gee up') To urge a horse to move faster or turn in a particular direction; to encourage someone to put more effort into something.
items.ex_en: The coach tried to gee up the sluggish players before the critical second half.
items.ex_zh: 教练在关键的下半场开始前努力给懒散的球员们鼓劲打气。

items.def_zh: 怂恿；挑唆（做蠢事或险事）
items.def_en: to encourage someone to do something foolish or risky
items.ex_en: His reckless friends began to egg on the young boy to jump across the chasm.
items.ex_zh: 他那些鲁莽的朋友开始挑唆那个年轻小伙跳过那道深沟。

items.def_zh: 鼓动，煽动；使焦虑，使不安；搅动，摇动
items.def_en: 1. (+ for/against) To argue strongly and campaign publicly for or against political or social change. 2. To make someone feel anxious, nervous, or upset. 3. To stir or shake a liquid briskly.
items.ex_en: Radical activists took to the streets to agitate for urgent structural and economic reforms.
items.ex_zh: 激进活动家走上街头，为紧急的结构和经济改革进行公开鼓动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to deliberately provoke, instigate, or foment trouble or agitation
items.ex_en: The mischievous rabble-rouser sought to stir up religious hatred among the otherwise peaceful townsfolk.
items.ex_zh: 那个心怀不轨的煽动者企图在原本和平的镇民中挑起宗教仇恨。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to deliberately excite or provoke strong emotions, agitation, or collective action
items.ex_en: The charismatic politician attempted to whip up populist fury with an inflammatory closing speech.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有魅力的政客试图用一段极具煽动性的收尾演讲激起民粹怒火。

items.def_en: 1. (+ to/to do) To encourage or stir up people to act in a violent, unlawful, or aggressive way.
items.ex_en: He was arrested for trying to incite vulnerable youths to commit severe public violence.
items.ex_zh: 他因涉嫌挑唆脆弱的年轻人去实施严重的公共暴力行为而被捕。

items.def_en: to intentionally bring about or provoke a specific negative action or event
items.ex_en: The corrupt union boss secretly sought to instigate an unlawful strike against the company.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败的工会头目暗中策划煽动针对该公司的非法罢工。

items.def_en: to instigate or foster rebellion, discord, or violent unrest
items.ex_en: Foreign operatives worked tirelessly underground to foment civil rebellion against the newly elected government.
items.ex_zh: 外国特工在地下不遗余力地运作，以煽动反抗新当选政府的国内叛乱。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to provoke or urge people aggressively into conflict or violence against a target
items.ex_en: The demagogue used radio broadcasts to incite against minority groups across the unstable province.
items.ex_zh: 那个煽动者利用电台广播在动荡的省份内鼓动民众敌对少数群体。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve an instigator communicating passionately to impel people to action, scaling in intensity from cheerful spurring and persuasion to public agitation and inflammatory incitement to violence.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过言论驱使他人采取行动，从催促鼓劲升级至政治动员与暴力煽动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes galvanizing, nudging, or deliberately fueling human passions or disruptive actions, contrasting with benign guidance or mere advice.
groups.desc_zh: 指激励促动他人行为，尤指挑动暴乱情绪或唆使违规之举，区别于温和的劝勉或中性的建言。
groups.nuance_en: urge: earnest, pressing exhortation to take recommended action (caution / reform / patience) · incite: actively provoking or stirring people into violent or illegal rebellion (riot / violence / hatred) · instigate: intentionally initiating and orchestrating a scheme or conflict from behind the scenes (inquiry / plot / rebellion) · egg on: goading and cheering someone into reckless or mischievous behavior (friend / fight / rival) · stir up: deliberately churning up dormant strife, unrest, or sentiments (trouble / resentment / debate) · whip up: skillfully inflaming crowd emotion or hysteria to high intensity (enthusiasm / frenzy / support)
groups.nuance_zh: urge: 恳切极力催促、敦促 (caution / reform / patience) · incite: 煽动、挑起暴乱或非法激烈行径 (riot / violence / hatred) · instigate: 幕后策划唆使并策动事件/争端 (inquiry / plot / rebellion) · egg on: 煽风点火、怂恿某人做出鲁莽之举 (friend / fight / rival) · stir up: 故意搅起风波、挑动压抑的怨恨 (trouble / resentment / debate) · whip up: 极力激起、煽动起狂热情绪或支持 (enthusiasm / frenzy / support)

groups.name: Violent Attack & Aggression · 突袭、重创与反击 (Assail, Blindside, Maul)
groups.tip: 以多种方式发起猛攻

items.def_en: to suddenly attack an enemy or rival from a concealed position
items.ex_en: The guerrilla fighters waited patiently to ambush the enemy convoy inside the dark canyon.
items.ex_zh: 游击队战士在黑暗峡谷深处耐心埋伏，以突袭敌方的车队。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to attack someone suddenly and ferociously
items.ex_en: The ravenous wolves seemed ready to fall on the wounded deer in the snow.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的狼群似乎已准备好猛扑向雪地里那只受伤的鹿。

items.def_en: to attack someone suddenly and violently, often as a group
items.ex_en: Masked highwaymen emerged from the shadowy forest to set upon the lone, defenseless traveller.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面绿林强盗从阴暗的森林中窜出，围攻那个孤立无援的旅人。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to attack someone with severe physical violence or ferocious aggression
items.ex_en: The drunken brawler suddenly lunged forward to tear into the unsuspecting patron with fury.
items.ex_zh: 那个喝醉的闹事者突然向前猛扑，怒气冲冲地殴打毫无防备的顾客。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack someone suddenly and aggressively without warning
items.ex_en: Nobody expected the docile family hound to turn on its master without warning today.
items.ex_zh: 没人料到那只温顺的家犬今天竟会毫无预警地反扑攻击它的主人。

items.def_en: To attack an enemy or competitor in response to an attack by them.
items.ex_en: The defensive battalion rallied its surviving armor to counterattack the advancing hostile vanguard decisively.
items.ex_zh: 防御营重整残存的装甲部队，果断反击步步逼近的敌军前锋。

items.def_zh: 从防备较弱的一侧袭击；使措手不及，使遭受突如其来的打击
items.def_en: To attack or hit someone unexpectedly from a direction where they cannot see, or surprise someone with an unforeseen difficulty.
items.ex_en: A heavy tackle from the unguarded flank managed to blindside the star quarterback instantly.
items.ex_zh: 来自未设防侧翼的沉重擒抱瞬间从盲区狠狠撞翻了明星四分卫。

items.def_zh: 猛烈攻击，袭击；质问，抨击；困扰
items.def_en: 1. To attack someone violently or physically. 2. To criticize strongly or be troubled persistently by something.
items.ex_en: Fierce howling squalls continued to assail the lonely stone fortress throughout the freezing night.
items.ex_zh: 呼啸的猛烈风暴在冰冷的黑夜中持续猛烈袭击着孤零零的石头要塞。

items.def_en: to attack violently and cause severe wounds, or criticize mercilessly
items.ex_en: The escaped guard dog broke through the fence to savage the poor delivery boy.
items.ex_zh: 逃脱的看门犬冲破栅栏，残暴地撕咬起那个可怜的送货男孩。

items.def_zh: 撕咬伤，抓伤；粗暴对待；严厉抨击
items.def_en: 1. (of an animal or person) To wound or tear someone severely by scratching, biting, or rough handling. 2. To criticize or treat someone or something severely.
items.ex_en: A wild grizzly bear managed to maul the unwary camper near the remote stream.
items.ex_zh: 一只野生灰熊在偏僻的小溪附近把粗心大意的露营者严重抓伤抓破。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe aggressive physical assaults or fierce metaphorical offensives characterized by sudden ambush, crippling damage, or retaliatory strikes against an opponent.
groups.summary_zh: 指以突袭、猛烈痛击或反攻的方式实施肉体打击或舆论围攻。
groups.desc_en: Denotes sudden, explosive, and aggressive physical onslaughts directed at an adversary, contrasting with formal, measured warfare maneuvers or defensive warding.
groups.desc_zh: 指突发性、爆发式的猛烈肉体或言语扑击与侵袭，区别于按部就班的正规阵地战或防守格挡。
groups.nuance_en: assail: violently attacking with physical force or a relentless torrent of criticism (victim / ears / doubts) · ambush: launching an unexpected onslaught from a concealed, waiting position (patrol / convoy / prey) · blindside: hitting unexpectedly from an unmonitored blind angle (quarterback / company / unsuspecting victim) · set upon: suddenly and collaboratively attacking in a swarm (traveler / stranger / intruder) · tear into: savagely tearing, ripping, or furiously dressing down someone (meat / opponent / rival) · counterattack: answering an offensive with an immediate strike of one's own (enemy / critics / position)
groups.nuance_zh: assail: 猛烈扑打侵袭，或铺天盖地受到攻击 (victim / ears / doubts) · ambush: 设伏伏击、隐蔽埋伏后突袭 (patrol / convoy / prey) · blindside: 从视线盲区出其不意地予以重创 (quarterback / company / unsuspecting victim) · set upon: 群起而攻之、猛扑围殴 (traveler / stranger / intruder) · tear into: 撕咬狂咬，或劈头盖脸痛斥 (meat / opponent / rival) · counterattack: 遭受攻击后立即发起防守反击 (enemy / critics / position)

groups.name: Voyage & Itinerate · 游历与远行 (Travel, Tour, Journey)
groups.tip: 长途漫游与出行

items.def_en: 1. To make a journey, typically over a distance or to different places. 2. To move or journey along a route.
items.ex_en: She saved all her money so she could travel across Europe after graduating college.
items.ex_zh: 她把所有的钱都攒了下来，以便大学毕业后周游欧洲各地。

items.def_zh: 周游，游历，观光；巡回演出（或比赛）
items.def_en: To make a tour of a place or area, often for sightseeing, performance, or campaigning.
items.ex_en: The rock band announced ambitious plans to tour major arenas across North America next.
items.ex_zh: 这支摇滚乐队宣布了巡回演出北美各大主流体育馆的宏伟计划。

items.def_en: To undertake a journey or travel somewhere, especially over a long distance.
items.ex_en: The brave pilgrim chose to journey across barren deserts toward the sacred holy mountain.
items.ex_zh: 勇敢的朝圣者选择漫游跋涉穿过荒芜沙漠，奔赴神圣的名山。

items.def_en: to begin a journey or expedition towards a distant destination
items.ex_en: The mountaineering expedition will set off for the base camp before the sun rises.
items.ex_zh: 登山探险队将在太阳升起之前动身远行，前往大本营。

items.def_en: to depart and begin travelling towards a specific destination or trip
items.ex_en: We should head out early to avoid the morning traffic.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该早点出发，避开早高峰。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to travel across or briefly visit places as part of a longer itinerary
items.ex_en: We plan to pass through several historic mountain villages during our trip to Italy.
items.ex_zh: 我们打算在意大利旅途中途经并游历几个历史悠久的山村。

items.def_en: To make a long, arduous journey, typically on foot across difficult terrain
items.ex_en: The determined hikers had to trek across muddy alpine paths for twelve exhausting hours.
items.ex_zh: 意志坚定的徒步者们不得不沿着泥泞的高山小道艰难跋涉了十二个小时。

items.def_en: To go on a long journey, typically by sea or into unknown regions
items.ex_en: Ancient mariners dared to voyage into uncharted ocean waters in search of the new.
items.ex_zh: 古代水手敢于远航驶入未知的海洋深处，以探寻崭新的天地。

items.def_en: [I/T] To travel unsystematically over a wide area without a fixed itinerary
items.ex_en: Bison used to roam across the vast open grasslands of the great American plains.
items.ex_zh: 美洲野牛过去常常漫步漫游在广袤的美洲大草原上。

items.def_en: To visit places of interest as a tourist
items.ex_en: We hired a knowledgeable local guide to sightsee around the ancient Roman ruins today.
items.ex_zh: 我们今天聘请了一位博学的当地向导，在古罗马废墟周围观光游览。

groups.summary_en: A person makes a journey between distant places, whether for recreation, broad exploration, sightseeing itineraries, or purposeful relocation across vast expanses.
groups.summary_zh: 长途旅行、巡回游览或跋涉探索异地。
groups.desc_en: Denotes extended, deliberate spatial transit across diverse geographical terrains or regions, contrasting with local daily commuting or mere stationary strolling.
groups.desc_zh: 指长距离、带特定目的或宏大尺度的地理空间位移与巡游，区别于日常通勤或原地漫步散步。
groups.nuance_en: travel: generalized movement from one distant place to another across regions (world / light / road) · journey: completing an arduous, long-distance trek from start to terminus (overland / south / desert) · voyage: undertaking a prolonged, hazardous ocean or space crossing (Atlantic / cosmos / unknown) · tour: itinerant circuit travel involving visiting multiple consecutive sites (country / museum / facilities) · trek: arduous, grueling pedestrian expedition across rugged terrain (Himalayas / wilderness / jungle)
groups.nuance_zh: travel: 最广义的远行、出行或旅行 (world / light / road) · journey: 强调路途漫长、过程艰险的长途跋涉 (overland / south / desert) · voyage: 航海或太空长途巡航远征 (Atlantic / cosmos / unknown) · tour: 巡回视察、巡游或按固定路线参访 (country / museum / facilities) · trek: 穿越险恶荒野的徒步跋涉 (Himalayas / wilderness / jungle)

groups.name: Wangle & Swindle · 巧取与诈骗 (Finagle, Wangle, Bamboozle)
groups.tip: 耍手腕巧妙诱骗他人获利

items.def_en: (+ sb into sth/doing sth) Persuade sb to do sth or give sth up by deceit or trickery
items.ex_en: The slick salesman conned my elderly uncle into buying a worthless warranty.
items.ex_zh: 那个油腔滑调的推销员哄骗我上了年纪的叔叔买了一份毫无用处的保修单。

items.def_en: (+ sb out of sth) Trick or cheat sb in order to deprive them of money or possessions
items.ex_en: The corrupt accountant diddled the small business out of thousands of dollars.
items.ex_zh: 那个贪腐的会计骗取了这家小企业数千美元的钱财。

items.def_en: Fool or cheat someone, often by baffling them with misleading talk or complex pretexts
items.ex_en: He bamboozled customers with confusing jargon to sell them unnecessary insurance policies.
items.ex_zh: 他用令人费解的行话蒙骗顾客，向他们推销不必要的保险单。

items.def_en: Deceive or trick someone deliberately into believing something false or acting foolishly
items.ex_en: The deceitful landlord hoodwinked the new tenants into signing an illegal lease.
items.ex_zh: 那个诡计多端的房东诱骗新房客签下了一份非法租约。

items.def_zh: 骗取，耍手腕弄到；欺骗，耍手段
items.def_en: 1. (+ out of) (North American informal) To obtain or arrange something through clever, devious, or dishonest methods.
items.ex_en: She finagled a free hotel upgrade out of the tired front desk clerk.
items.ex_zh: 她耍手腕让疲惫的前台接待员给她免费升级了酒店房间。

items.def_zh: 设法弄到，用计谋获得；耍花招搞定
items.def_en: 1. (+ out of) (informal) To obtain something desired through clever persuasion, manipulation, or trickery.
items.ex_en: He wangled an extra week off out of his unsuspecting boss yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 他昨天耍花招从毫不知情的老板那里设法多弄到了一周假期。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Cheat sb by charging too much money or stealing from them
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_en: Swindle or defraud someone out of money or property through a calculated, dishonest scheme
items.ex_en: The bogus investment firm scammed dozens of retirees out of their savings.
items.ex_zh: 那家虚假投资公司设局诈骗了数十名退休人员的积蓄。

items.def_en: Cheat or cheat out of what is due, especially by dodging payments or swindling
items.ex_en: The contractor bilked the city government out of substantial infrastructure development funds.
items.ex_zh: 该承包商骗取了市政府巨额的基础设施建设资金。

items.def_en: 1. (North American humorous slang) To trick, cheat, or hoax someone.
items.ex_en: I think that crafty dealer hornswoggled me into purchasing a total lemon.
items.ex_zh: 我觉得那个狡猾的经销商忽悠我买下了一辆彻底的劣质车。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe obtaining something or manipulating people through devious maneuvering, clever trickery, cajolery, or outright deception. Nuances span colloquial clever schematics to folksy, colorful conning.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过耍弄手段、花言巧语或弄虚作假来设法获取利益或愚弄他人。
groups.desc_en: Denotes obtaining an illicit gain or advantage through crafty manipulation, deceitful pretense, or fraudulent schemes, contrasting with honest negotiation or forceful robbery.
groups.desc_zh: 指凭借精巧算计、虚假伪装或欺诈话术谋取不义利益，区别于诚信交易或明火执仗的强索。
groups.nuance_en: swindle: systematically defrauding a victim out of money or property through deceit (investor / fortune / public) · bamboozle: utterly confusing, tricking, or flummoxing someone into capitulation (audience / tourist / opponents) · hoodwink: pulling the wool over someone's eyes through clever deception (public / authorities / voters) · finagle: getting or achieving something through devious, shady maneuvering (invitation / visa / deal) · wangle: cleverly manipulating connections or conditions to wheedle an advantage (ticket / promotion / day off) · rip off: blatantly overcharging, defrauding, or copying without credit (consumer / customer / design)
groups.nuance_zh: swindle: 系统性设局骗取钱财、诈骗财产 (investor / fortune / public) · bamboozle: 耍把戏把人彻底蒙骗耍弄、绕晕 (audience / tourist / opponents) · hoodwink: 蒙蔽、欺瞒他人耳目使其上当 (public / authorities / voters) · finagle: 施展钻营手段、耍滑头巧取 (invitation / visa / deal) · wangle: 托关系、钻空子搞到手 (ticket / promotion / day off) · rip off: 宰客、漫天要价或赤裸裸抄袭侵吞 (consumer / customer / design)

groups.name: Worry & Fret · 担忧与焦虑不安 (Fret, Perturb, Agitate)
groups.tip: 内心发愁焦虑而烦躁难安

items.def_en: [I/T] to feel or cause to feel anxious or troubled about actual or potential problems
items.ex_en: Her persistent chest pains began to worry the entire family immensely.
items.ex_zh: 她持续不断的胸痛开始让全家人感到无比担忧。

items.def_zh: 发愁，烦躁，焦虑不安；侵蚀，磨损
items.def_en: 1. To worry constantly and be unhappy or anxious about something; 2. to wear away or erode.
items.ex_en: It does no good to fret constantly over mistakes you cannot change.
items.ex_zh: 为你无法改变的错误整日焦虑发愁毫无益处。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Worry constantly or become visibly agitated over something
items.ex_en: She spent the whole evening fretting about her upcoming university entrance interview.
items.ex_zh: 她整整一个晚上都在为即将到来的大学面试焦虑不安。

items.def_zh: （为小事）瞎操心，大惊小怪，烦恼；瞎忙
items.def_en: To worry excessively or pay too much anxious attention to small or unimportant details.
items.ex_en: Stop fussing over minor schedule changes and focus on the main presentation.
items.ex_zh: 别再为微小的日程变动瞎操心了，把注意力放在主讲报告上。

items.def_zh: 使焦虑，使心烦意乱，使不安；扰乱
items.def_en: (formal) To make someone feel worried, anxious, or unsettled.
items.ex_en: The unexpected decline in quarterly corporate earnings perturbed the board of directors.
items.ex_zh: 季度企业盈利的意外下滑令董事会成员深感忧虑。

items.def_zh: 使不安，使忧虑，使心神不定
items.def_en: (formal) To make someone feel worried, anxious, or uneasy.
items.ex_en: The mysterious late-night footsteps overhead disquieted everyone inside the old house.
items.ex_zh: 楼上深夜传来的神秘脚步声让老屋里的每个人都感到心神不宁。

items.def_zh: 折磨；让（某人）内心焦虑不安
items.def_en: (+ sb) Cause sb persistent mental distress, anxiety, or guilt over time
items.ex_en: The unresolved guilt continued to eat away at him for years.
items.ex_zh: 那份未解的内疚感多年来持续折磨着他的内心。

items.def_zh: 对……过分担忧；对……念念不忘
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Worry or think about sth incessantly to an unhealthy degree
items.ex_en: He tends to obsess over minor typographical errors in his published articles.
items.ex_zh: 他往往会对自己已发表文章中的微小排印错误过分纠结。

items.def_zh: 使心烦意乱，使严重焦虑
items.def_en: to make someone intensely nervous, troubled, or mentally stirred up
items.ex_en: The sudden sounding of the air raid sirens agitated the already anxious populace.
items.ex_zh: 防空警报的猝然响起让本就焦虑的民众陷入极度惶恐。

items.def_zh: 使慌乱，使失去镇定自信
items.def_en: to deprive someone of courage, resolve, or composure through anxiety
items.ex_en: The harsh glare from the interrogation lamps unnerved the young suspect.
items.ex_zh: 审讯灯刺眼的强光彻底打破了年轻嫌疑人的心理防线。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame articulate internal mental distress or anxiety, spanning from petty outward fussing and continuous brooding to profound internal agitation and deep disquiet.
groups.summary_zh: 表达由内心的挂虑、烦乱逐渐升级至深层心绪不宁与极度焦虑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes experiencing an anxious, churning internal emotional perturbation over prospective troubles, contrasting with sudden acute panic or serene detachment.
groups.desc_zh: 指因预想的困扰而陷入内心反复翻腾、焦躁不安的持续情绪折磨，区别于突发恐慌或坦然处之。
groups.nuance_en: worry: persistent mental distress over real or imagined hardships (health / money / future) · fret: restless, visibly irritable and agitated anxious gnawing (safety / delay / details) · fuss: disproportionate, nervous bustling and overreacting to trivia (clothes / arrangements / food) · perturb: unsettling someone's inner calm or equilibrium deeply (mind / officials / composure) · obsess over: pathologically fixing one's thoughts exclusively on a singular anxiety (weight / perfection / mistake)
groups.nuance_zh: worry: 对未知困难持续忧虑、担忧挂念 (health / money / future) · fret: 烦躁不安地在心头反复磨蚀、发愁焦灼 (safety / delay / details) · fuss: 为细枝末节小题大做地瞎操心、瞎忙活 (clothes / arrangements / food) · perturb: 使平静的内心或稳态发生深度动荡不安 (mind / officials / composure) · obsess over: 走火入魔般对某事过度思虑沉溺 (weight / perfection / mistake)

groups.name: Wrap & Enfold · 紧密包覆与护裹 (Cocoon, Jacket, Cere)
groups.tip: 如作茧或套外衣般层层裹覆

items.def_zh: 替（某人）掖好被子；把……塞入裹紧
items.def_en: (+ sb) Make sb comfortable in bed by snugly folding sheets or blankets around them
items.ex_en: Every night, the loving mother tucked in her children and read stories.
items.ex_zh: 每天晚上，慈爱的母亲都会为孩子们掖好被子并讲故事。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Cover or enfold sth completely in paper, cloth, or warm garments
items.ex_en: Let's wrap up this meeting so everyone can catch their flights.
items.ex_zh: 我们结束这次会议吧，这样大家都能赶上航班。

items.def_en: 1. To cover or enclose something with a protective casing or jacket.
items.ex_en: Workers jacketed the exposed metal pipes with thick fiberglass to prevent freezing.
items.ex_zh: 工人们用厚玻璃纤维给裸露的金属管道包上护套以防冻结。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Wrap sb or oneself tightly and warmly in clothing or blankets
items.ex_en: Be sure to bundle up before heading out into the freezing storm.
items.ex_zh: 走入刺骨的风雪之前，一定要把自己裹得暖暖和和的。
items.ex2_en: The mother bundled up the shivering toddler in a thick woolen blanket.
items.ex2_zh: 母亲用厚毛毯把瑟瑟发抖的幼童裹得严严实实。

items.def_zh: 紧紧包裹；庇护，使免受外界影响
items.def_en: 1. (+ in/from) To wrap or surround someone completely in warm, protective layers, or shield them from harsh realities.
items.ex_en: She cocooned the fragile infant in soft fleece against the icy wind.
items.ex_zh: 她用柔软的摇粒绒将脆弱的婴儿紧紧裹住以抵御寒风。

items.def_zh: 裹厚保暖或裹住以消声
items.def_en: (+ in/up) to wrap or swathe someone or something warmly or to deaden sound
items.ex_en: He muffled himself in a thick wool scarf to brave the blizzard.
items.ex_zh: 他用一条厚厚的羊毛围巾把自己裹得严严实实以冒雪前行。

items.def_en: 1. (archaic) To wrap a dead body in waxed burial cloth.
items.ex_en: Ancient priests ceremented and cered the fallen monarch before placing him within.
items.ex_zh: 古代祭司在将驾崩的君主安放进去前，用蜡布将其遗体包裹严实。

items.def_en: to wrap someone (especially a baby) tightly in cloth or blankets
items.ex_en: The nurse gently swaddled the newborn baby in a warm cotton blanket.
items.ex_zh: 护士轻柔地用温暖的棉毯把新生儿紧紧包裹起来。

items.def_zh: 温柔或密实地拥抱覆裹
items.def_en: to surround, cover, or wrap someone or something completely
items.ex_en: A thick blanket of winter mist gently enfolded the sleeping valley.
items.ex_zh: 一层厚重的冬雾温柔地笼罩覆裹着沉睡的山谷。

items.def_en: (+ in/with) to encase or cover something in a protective layer
items.ex_en: The tall towers were sheathed in gleaming panels of tinted reflective glass.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的塔楼外层被覆裹上了一块块光芒闪烁的深色反光玻璃。

groups.summary_en: An entity covers or winds material snugly around an object, forming an intimate, protective, or sealing layer reminiscent of biological skins, casings, or swaddling cloths.
groups.summary_zh: 以护套、丝茧或包膜紧密服帖地覆裹以防损或隔绝。
groups.desc_en: Denotes snugly and completely encasing an entity within soft, protective, or insulating layers, contrasting with loosely covering, binding with chains, or simple coating.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用柔软、防护性或保温包裹层将其紧密层层护裹，区别于松垮铺盖、硬性锁绑或单纯涂覆。
groups.nuance_en: wrap: enveloping completely within a flexible sheet or covering (gift / blanket / sandwich) · swaddle: wrapping an infant securely and snugly in cloths to restrict movement (baby / newborn / limbs) · cocoon: insulating within an all-enveloping, secure, cozy barrier (warmth / silence / child) · muffle: wrapping to deaden sound or protect against biting cold (throat / scarf / sound) · bundle up: dressing someone thickly in copious warm outerwear (kids / traveler / self) · jacket: encasing an object with an exterior protective protective sleeve (pipe / book / cable)
groups.nuance_zh: wrap: 用柔性材料全面包卷、包裹起来 (gift / blanket / sandwich) · swaddle: 用襁褓将婴儿紧紧包裹 (baby / newborn / limbs) · cocoon: 如蚕茧般将人全方位隔绝包裹进安全温馨中 (warmth / silence / child) · muffle: 用围巾包裹御寒，或包覆以消音减振 (throat / scarf / sound) · bundle up: 严严实实穿裹上重重防寒冬衣 (kids / traveler / self) · jacket: 给管道或电缆等套上外层护套/绝缘保护层 (pipe / book / cable)

groups.name: Wrinkle & Puckering · 起皱与褶皱 (Crease, Wrinkle, Crumple)
groups.tip: 揉搓受压形成细密褶皱

items.def_en: (+ sth) Form or cause to form thin, shallow wrinkles or ridges
items.ex_en: He crinkled up his nose in distaste upon smelling the sour milk.
items.ex_zh: 一闻到变酸的牛奶，他就嫌弃地皱起了鼻子。

items.def_en: To form small lines or folds in skin, fabric, or paper; to cause something to have wrinkles.
items.ex_en: Strong summer sunshine caused him to wrinkle his brow in a deep squint.
items.ex_zh: 夏日的烈日让他眯起双眼，额头紧紧皱起了纹路。

items.def_en: To make or develop folds, lines, or wrinkles in cloth, paper, or skin.
items.ex_en: Sitting for hours in the car will crease your freshly pressed linen trousers.
items.ex_zh: 在车里坐上几个小时会把你刚烫平的亚麻长裤坐出褶子。
items.ex2_en: Pure cotton shirts crease easily whenever you pack them tightly into luggage.
items.ex2_zh: 纯棉衬衫只要紧紧塞进行李箱就很容易起皱。

items.def_en: to draw together into small folds or ridges, especially lips or stitching
items.ex_en: The harsh taste of the raw lemon caused her to pucker involuntarily.
items.ex_zh: 生柠檬刺鼻的酸味让她不由自主地紧缩噘起了嘴巴。
items.ex2_en: The seamstress puckered the delicate silk fabric along the narrow waistline precisely.
items.ex2_zh: 女裁缝沿着狭窄的腰线精确地将精致的丝绸面料打上细褶。

items.def_en: (especially of paper or fabric) To pucker, wrinkle, or contract unevenly into folds.
items.ex_en: The wet watercolor paper began to cockle unevenly across its broad surface.
items.ex_zh: 浸湿的水彩纸表面大面积地开始不规则地起皱拱起。

items.def_zh: 使弄皱；弄乱（衣物或毛发）
items.def_en: to make something such as cloth or hair untidy and full of creases
items.ex_en: He carelessly rumpled his silk shirt by stuffing it into the gym bag.
items.ex_zh: 他把真丝衬衫胡乱塞进健身包，弄得满是褶皱。
items.ex2_en: The soft velvet bedsheets rumpled noticeably after the restless dog jumped on them.
items.ex2_zh: 躁动的狗跳上去后，柔软的天鹅绒床单明显起了褶皱。

items.def_en: to form fine, delicate creases or lines on skin, foil, or paper
items.ex_en: The thin foil wrapper crinkled loudly under the weight of his hand.
items.ex_zh: 薄薄的锡箔包装纸在他的手掌压迫下发出了细碎的起皱声。
items.ex2_en: She crinkled the crisp sheet of parchment paper before wrapping the sandwich.
items.ex2_zh: 她在包裹三明治之前揉皱了那张脆羊皮纸。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Become full of lines or wrinkles, or cause fabric or skin to do so
items.ex_en: These cheap cotton trousers always crease up after just a short walk.
items.ex_zh: 这些廉价的棉裤往往只要稍微走上几步就会起满折痕。
items.ex2_en: Careless folding will crease up your fine silk dress during long overseas flights.
items.ex2_zh: 粗心的折叠会在长途国际航班中弄皱你精美的丝绸连衣裙。

items.def_zh: （使嘴唇或织物）噘起；收拢起皱
items.def_en: (+ sth) Contract into small folds or ridges, especially the lips
items.ex_en: She puckered up in preparation for a humorous photo with her friends.
items.ex_zh: 她噘起嘴巴，准备和朋友们拍一张搞怪的照片。
items.ex2_en: Sour green apples always pucker up your mouth with their sharp acidic taste.
items.ex2_zh: 酸青苹果总是以其强烈的酸味让你的嘴唇缩拢起来。

items.def_en: to crush into irregular creases, or to collapse into folds
items.ex_en: Frustrated by writer's block, he crumpled the draft sheet into a ball.
items.ex_zh: 因文思枯竭而倍感沮丧的他把草稿纸揉搓挤压成了一团。
items.ex2_en: The flimsy cardboard box crumpled completely under the weight of the heavy books.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的纸板箱在沉重书籍的重压下完全压瘪了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe pliable surfaces—such as fabric, skin, or paper—forming unintentional lines, ridges, or furrowed puckers under pressure, dampness, or facial movement.
groups.summary_zh: 指织物、纸张或皮肤等柔性表面受挤压或收缩而起皱、起纹。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves deforming a flat, smooth, or flexible surface into irregular folds, ridges, or gathers through compression, drying, or muscle contraction, differing from tearing or breaking by preserving physical continuity.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式体现为平整柔韧的表面因受压、干燥或肌肉收缩而形成不规则褶皱或起伏，与撕裂或破损的区别在于其保持了材料的物理连续性。
groups.nuance_en: wrinkle: creates fine, natural ridges or folds through aging or contracting (brow / skin / linen) · crease: produces sharp, distinct, often linear fold lines (trousers / paper / forehead) · pucker: gathers or draws tightly inward into tight folds (lips / seam / fabric) · rumple: dishevels or messes up into untidy, disordered creases (sheets / hair / clothing) · crinkle: forms many delicate, shallow, crackling wrinkles (paper / eyes / cellophane)
groups.nuance_zh: wrinkle: 自然收缩或老化形成的细密褶皱 (brow / skin / linen) · crease: 压制或挤折出的明显线状折痕 (trousers / paper / forehead) · pucker: 沿边缘向内收拢聚缩 (lips / seam / fabric) · rumple: 揉搓折腾导致的凌乱不整褶痕 (sheets / hair / clothing) · crinkle: 形成微细松脆的浅纹或轻微卷缩 (paper / eyes / cellophane)

groups.name: Abandon & Relinquish · 放弃与抛弃 (Renounce Claims, Duties, or Bonds)
groups.tip: 彻底抛弃誓约或遗弃亲朋

items.def_zh: 自愿放弃（权利、索赔要求）
items.def_en: to officially and voluntarily give up a legal right, claim, or entitlement
items.ex_en: The company decided to waive its legal right to appeal the arbitration decision.
items.ex_zh: 该公司决定自愿放弃就仲裁裁决提起上诉的法定权利。

items.def_zh: 交出，被迫放弃（权力、职位、财产）
items.def_en: to unwillingly or formally give up control, possession, or a right to someone else
items.ex_en: The defeated commander was forced to relinquish absolute authority over the occupied territories.
items.ex_zh: 战败的指挥官被迫交出了对占领区域的绝对控制权。

items.def_zh: 放弃（权利、所有权或职责）
items.def_en: (+ sth) Renounce or surrender a claim, right, responsibility, or possession
items.ex_en: He reluctantly gave up his long-standing claim to the ancestral estate.
items.ex_zh: 他不情愿地放弃了自己对祖传庄园长期保有的索求权。

items.def_en: to leave behind someone or something completely and with no intention of returning
items.ex_en: Desperate refugees abandoned their heavy luggage beside the blocked mountain border crossing.
items.ex_zh: 绝望的难民将沉重的行李尽数遗弃在受阻的山区边境关卡旁。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Formally give up a legal right or property by signing a document
items.ex_en: He inadvertently signed away the copyright to his debut novel.
items.ex_zh: 他不慎签字放弃了自己处女作小说的版权。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Deliberately reject, forsake, or refuse to help someone or an obligation
items.ex_en: He turned his back on his parental responsibilities after moving abroad.
items.ex_zh: 移居国外后，他决然背弃了自己应尽的做父母的责任。

items.def_zh: 断绝关系，公开放弃（名位、信念）
items.def_en: to state publicly that you no longer have a connection with, believe in, or claim something
items.ex_en: The disgraced prince formally renounced all succession rights to the royal throne.
items.ex_zh: 声名狼藉的王子正式公开发表声明，放弃对王位的一切继承权。

items.def_zh: 抛弃，遗弃，彻底放弃（forsake的过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past participle of forsake; abandoned, deserted, or renounced.
items.ex_en: The lonely outpost stood completely forsaken amid the howling Arctic blizzards.
items.ex_zh: 那座孤独的哨所孤零零地被彻底遗弃在呼啸的北极暴风雪中。

items.def_zh: 遗弃，抛弃；断念，彻底放弃
items.def_en: 1. (formal or literary) To abandon someone who depends on you, or give up a habit, belief, or claim.
items.ex_en: He vowed never to forsake his lifelong principles for quick financial gain.
items.ex_zh: 他立誓决不会为了换取眼前的经济利益而背弃自己终生恪守的原则。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote letting go of possessions, claims, familial loyalties, or solemn responsibilities. They scale in moral and emotional gravity from formal relinquishment to deliberate, cold-hearted betrayal and total desertion.
groups.summary_zh: 按情感决绝度与责任背弃程度，放弃权利、职责或遗弃至亲。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves formally or voluntarily ceding ownership, rights, claims, or duties, contrasting with mere physical loss by entailing an intentional act of yielding or desisting.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式体现为主动或正式放弃法定所有权、权利、主张或职责，与单纯的丢失不同，它强调出自主观意志的割舍或退让。
groups.nuance_en: waive: voluntarily forgo a legitimate right, claim, or rule (fee / immunity / rights) · relinquish: surrender possession, power, or control with reluctance (power / control / custody) · renounce: formally or solemnly disown, repudiate, or give up (title / citizenship / claim) · give up: general cessation of effort, ownership, or pursuit (smoking / hope / fight) · abandon: completely desert or cease maintaining interest or care (project / claim / vessel)
groups.nuance_zh: waive: 声明主动放弃合法权利或免收豁免 (fee / immunity / rights) · relinquish: 勉强移交或让出控制权与所有权 (power / control / custody) · renounce: 庄严正式地声称断绝或放弃身份主张 (title / citizenship / claim) · give up: 普适性地停止努力、习惯或保有 (smoking / hope / fight) · abandon: 彻底丢下、终止维护或不再过问 (project / claim / vessel)

groups.name: Abandon Relationships · 遗弃与背弃 (Abandon, Desert, Forsake)
groups.tip: 背弃职责或狠心舍弃

items.def_en: (+ sth) Deliberately abandon a difficult relationship or responsibility instead of dealing with it
items.ex_en: He walked away from the negotiations when the terms became unreasonable.
items.ex_zh: 当条款变得不合理时，他果断退出了谈判。

items.def_zh: 甩下；突然背弃（伴侣或家庭）
items.def_en: to suddenly leave a partner, spouse, or family, ending the relationship
items.ex_en: He walked out on his family without leaving any explanation.
items.ex_zh: 他没有任何解释就抛弃了家人一走了之。

items.def_zh: 抛弃；遗弃（不再需要的人）
items.def_en: (+ sb) Discard or abandon someone completely because they are no longer wanted
items.ex_en: The ruthless warlord cast aside his former loyal retainers without remorse.
items.ex_zh: 那位残暴的军阀毫无悔意地彻底抛弃了昔日效忠于他的家臣。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Suddenly abandon a partner, spouse, or family in an irresponsible way
items.ex_en: He ran out on his wife and two young children without leaving a penny.
items.ex_zh: 他抛弃了妻子和两个年幼的孩子，甚至一分钱都没留下。

items.def_zh: 抛弃；遗弃（依附者或家庭）
