items.def_en: to run away suddenly and rapidly out of control or in panic
items.ex_en: The startled stallion suddenly bolted, throwing its inexperienced rider onto the dirt.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的种马突然狂奔脱缰，将缺乏经验的骑手摔在泥地上。

items.def_zh: 猛冲，急奔；猛击，猛掷；使（希望、梦想等）破灭
items.def_en: 1. To run or move somewhere very quickly. 2. To strike or throw something violently against a surface. 3. To destroy someone's hopes, dreams, or expectations.
items.ex_en: She had to dash to the pharmacy before it closed for lunch.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不急奔去药房，免得赶上它午间关门。

items.def_zh: 飞奔，疾驰；在……上留条纹，布满条纹；裸奔
items.def_en: 1. To move very fast in a specified direction. 2. To mark with stripes or streaks.
items.ex_en: The sports car streaked along the open coastal road into the sunset.
items.ex_zh: 跑车沿着开阔的沿海公路疾驰，迎着落日飞奔。

items.def_en: to run at maximum possible speed for a short distance
items.ex_en: The athlete managed to sprint past his rival in the final stretch.
items.ex_zh: 该运动员在最后的直道上全力冲刺，超越了对手。

items.def_en: (+ along/down) to move or run with reckless, violent speed
items.ex_en: Motorbikes tear down our quiet residential street late at night, making noise.
items.ex_zh: 深夜里摩托车在我们安静的居住区街道上狂奔飞驰，制造噪音。

groups.summary_en: An agent suddenly bursts into rapid, high-intensity running across a distance, characterized by abrupt acceleration and rushing velocity.
groups.summary_zh: 突然发力、高速冲刺或迅猛奔跑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an abrupt, high-speed burst of foot flight or sudden escape, contrasting with steady running or endurance jogging by its explosive suddenness.
groups.desc_zh: 指突发性全力冲刺、疾奔或惊慌逃窜，区别于匀速跑步或长跑，强调爆发力与猝不及防的疾驰。
groups.nuance_en: sprint: run at full maximum speed over a short distance (finish line / for the bus / 100 meters) · bolt: break away and flee suddenly in panic or evasion (horse / door / prisoner) · dash: make a quick, energetic rush or run for a short duration (to safety / across the street / into the rain) · streak: flash past at immense velocity, leaving a blur (across the sky / naked / along the track)
groups.nuance_zh: sprint: 短距离拼尽全力全速冲刺 (finish line / for the bus / 100 meters) · bolt: 受惊或伺机猛然夺路而逃 (horse / door / prisoner) · dash: 猛冲一小段路、疾奔 (to safety / across the street / into the rain) · streak: 极速飞驰而过只留下一道虚影 (across the sky / naked / along the track)

groups.name: Dawdle & Delay · 拖延与磨蹭 (Piddle, Temporize, Stall)
groups.tip: 游手好闲虚度时间慢吞吞

items.def_en: waste time doing unimportant or trivial things instead of taking action
items.ex_en: Stop messing around on your phone and finish your homework before dinner.
items.ex_zh: 别再磨蹭摆弄手机了，晚饭前把作业做完。

items.def_en: to waste time through aimless indecision or loitering
items.ex_en: Do not dilly-dally at the bus stop or we will be late.
items.ex_zh: 别在公交车站磨蹭耽搁了，否则我们要迟到了。

items.def_zh: 磨蹭，虚度光阴（piddle around/away）；撒尿
items.def_en: 1. (informal) to waste time on trivial matters; dawdle (often followed by around or away). 2. (informal or euphemistic) to urinate.
items.ex_en: Stop piddling around with old receipts and tackle the real accounting problem.
items.ex_zh: 别再为旧收据磨蹭浪费时间了，去解决真正的会计问题吧。

items.def_zh: 故意拖长；拖延（时间或进程）
items.def_en: (+ sth) prolong an event, process, or discussion unnecessarily
items.ex_en: There is no need to drag out the dispute any longer.
items.ex_zh: 没有必要再故意拖延这场争端了。

items.def_en: to deliberately delay taking action so as to gain time to think or prepare
items.ex_en: The defense attorney tried to play for time until new evidence arrived.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师试图故意拖延时间，直到新的证据送达。

items.def_zh: 设法拖延以争取（时间等）
items.def_en: (+ sth) deliberately delay taking action in order to gain an advantage or more time
items.ex_en: The diplomat began to stall for time while awaiting instructions from headquarters.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官在等待总部的指示时开始设法拖延时间。

items.def_en: [I/T] to intentionally delay or play for time in order to gain an advantage
items.ex_en: The suspect tried to stall during the interrogation by asking irrelevant questions.
items.ex_zh: 嫌疑人在审讯过程中提出无关痛痒的问题，企图拖延时间。
items.ex2_en: The defense attorney tried to stall the legal proceedings with repeated objections.
items.ex2_zh: 辩护律师试图通过不断提出异议来拖延诉讼程序。

items.def_en: to habitually or intentionally delay doing something that should be done
items.ex_en: Students who habitually procrastinate often suffer from severe stress before final exams.
items.ex_zh: 习惯性拖延的学生在期末考试前往往会承受巨大的压力。

items.def_zh: 拖延时间以待时机，搪塞；顺应潮流，妥协
items.def_en: (formal) to delay making a decision or taking action in order to gain time.
items.ex_en: The board preferred to temporize rather than face an immediate hostile takeover.
items.ex_zh: 董事会宁愿拖延时间以待时机，也不愿立即面对敌意收购。

groups.summary_en: A person deliberately or carelessly avoids action or postpones a definitive outcome through time-wasting, trifles, or diplomatic stalling maneuvers. Nuances range from petty foot-dragging to calculated strategic delay in negotiation.
groups.summary_zh: 无所事事地瞎磨蹭，或为争取时间而策略性地拖延表态。
groups.desc_en: Involves wasting time, dithering aimlessly, or deliberately manufacturing delays to postpone an inevitable action, contrasting with prompt execution or constructive planning.
groups.desc_zh: 指无所事事地磨蹭、游移不定或故意拖延阻挠以推迟决断，区别于高效执行或有建设性的筹划。
groups.nuance_en: procrastinate: systematically delay tasks out of aversion or habit (on taxes / homework / decisions) · stall: deliberately play for time or obstruct progress (negotiations / for time / engine) · dilly-dally: waste time through indecisiveness or trivial idling (over choices / on the way) · mess around: spend time aimlessly fiddling without serious purpose (with gadgets / at work / all afternoon)
groups.nuance_zh: procrastinate: 因拖延症或逃避心理一再延宕正事 (on taxes / homework / decisions) · stall: 故意拖延时间以找借口或设障 (negotiations / for time / engine) · dilly-dally: 优柔寡断磨洋工、虚掷光阴 (over choices / on the way) · mess around: 游手好闲、无目的地瞎胡闹或瞎摆弄 (with gadgets / at work / all afternoon)

groups.name: Debilitate & Incapacitate · 虚弱与致残 (Weaken, Debilitate, Incapacitate)
groups.tip: 使力量或机能逐渐丧失

items.def_en: [I/T] to make or become less strong, powerful, or effective physically or structurally
items.ex_en: Repeated flooding will severely weaken the foundation of this old stone bridge.
items.ex_zh: 反复的洪水会严重削弱这座古老石桥的地基结构。
items.ex2_en: The patient's pulse gradually weakened as the dangerous fever spiked overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 随着夜间危险的高烧飙升，病人的脉搏逐渐微弱下去。

items.def_en: to make someone or something extremely weak, frail, and devoid of vitality
items.ex_en: Months of severe malnutrition enfeeble the prisoners until they can barely stand.
items.ex_zh: 数月严重的营养不良使囚犯极度虚弱，甚至几乎无法站立。

items.def_zh: 逐渐消耗，慢慢剥夺（力量或元气）
items.def_en: (+ sth) gradually drain or weaken someone's energy, strength, or resolve
items.ex_en: Continuous setbacks sap away the young entrepreneur's original enthusiasm and creative drive.
items.ex_zh: 接连的挫折慢慢消磨掉了这位年轻创业者最初的热情与干劲。

items.def_zh: 逐渐削弱（体力、抵抗力或意志）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) gradually weaken someone's physical strength, endurance, or resistance
items.ex_en: Persistent negotiations finally wore down the opposition's resistance.
items.ex_zh: 旷日持久的谈判最终瓦解了反对派的抵抗意志。
items.ex2_en: The rubber soles will wear down quickly from running on rough asphalt.
items.ex2_zh: 在粗糙的沥青路面上跑步会导致橡胶鞋底迅速磨损变薄。

items.def_zh: 击倒；使（因伤病而）卧床不起
items.def_en: (+ sb) force someone to take to bed or incapacitate them through illness or injury
items.ex_en: A severe bout of winter flu laid low half of our staff.
items.ex_zh: 一场严重的冬季流感让我们半数员工卧床不起。

items.def_en: to damage someone's body or an organization so severely that normal function is destroyed
items.ex_en: The sudden economic sanctions threaten to cripple the small country's banking system.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的经济制裁可能会彻底瘫痪并严重削弱该小国的银行体系。

items.def_zh: 使虚弱，使衰弱；削弱（机构、经济等）
items.def_en: To make a person, body, or organization very weak and unable to function normally.
items.ex_en: Chronic illness can debilitate patients and prevent them from pursuing normal careers.
items.ex_zh: 慢性疾病会使患者身体极度虚弱，无法从事正常的工作。

items.def_zh: 使丧失能力；使不能正常运转；剥夺……的合法资格
items.def_en: To deprive someone of the physical or mental ability or legal capacity to do something or function normally.
items.ex_en: A severe spinal injury could incapacitate the worker for many long months.
items.ex_zh: 严重的脊柱损伤可能使该工人丧失行动能力长达数月之久。

items.def_zh: 使瘫痪，使丧失行动能力
items.def_en: to cause a person or system to become completely unable to move or operate
items.ex_en: Heavy snowstorms can easily paralyze public transportation throughout the entire metropolitan area.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雪极易使整个大都市区的公共交通完全陷入瘫痪。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the progressive impairment of physical strength, health, or operational capability. They range from rendering someone moderately weak or fragile to completely neutralizing their ability to function, move, or fight back.
groups.summary_zh: 使身体机能或运作能力逐渐受损乃至完全瘫痪。
groups.desc_en: Describes the progressive erosion or catastrophic removal of physical strength, operational capability, or systemic vitality, contrasting with sudden destruction by undermining functional integrity.
groups.desc_zh: 指身体机能、运作能力或系统元气被渐进削蚀或彻底剥夺瘫痪，区别于直接摧毁，强调削弱与致残。
groups.nuance_en: weaken: reduce strength, firmness, or resolving power (resolve / immune system / support) · debilitate: severely undermine vitality or functional strength over time (disease / stroke / economy) · incapacitate: make completely unable to function, act, or work (driver / soldier / by injury) · cripple: inflict devastating physical impairment or functional paralysis (economy / industry / victim)
groups.nuance_zh: weaken: 削弱力量、决心或抵抗力 (resolve / immune system / support) · debilitate: 使身体、体制陷入长期深度虚弱 (disease / stroke / economy) · incapacitate: 使丧失行动能力、无法正常履职 (driver / soldier / by injury) · cripple: 使重度致残或导致系统运转彻底瘫痪 (economy / industry / victim)

groups.name: Deceive & Dissemble · 欺瞒与掩饰伪装 (Dissemble, Dissimulate, Mask)
groups.tip: 掩饰真情故意隐瞒欺诈

items.def_en: to adopt an artificial manner of speech, demeanor, or posture to impress or mislead
items.ex_en: He affected an air of indifference to hide his deep inner anxiety.
items.ex_zh: 他佯装出一副无所谓的模样，以掩饰内心深处的焦虑。

items.def_en: to hide a feeling, smell, fact, or intention so that others do not notice it
items.ex_en: She forced a warm smile to mask her growing disappointment and sadness.
items.ex_zh: 她挤出温暖的微笑，以掩饰自己内心日益加深的失望与悲伤。

items.def_zh: 掩盖，掩饰（真相、错误或真实情感）
items.def_en: (+ sth) conceal facts, bad actions, or true feelings behind an untruthful appearance
items.ex_en: Corrupt officials conspired to cover up the scandal from the inquisitive press.
items.ex_zh: 腐败官员合谋向追查到底的媒体掩盖这桩丑闻的真相。

items.def_zh: 避重就轻地掩饰；掩饰带过
items.def_en: (+ sth) deliberately avoid dealing with unpleasant or dishonest truths by treating them lightly
items.ex_en: The manager chose to gloss over financial irregularities during the annual meeting.
items.ex_zh: 经理在年会上选择对财务违规问题避重就轻、轻描淡写地掩饰过去。

items.def_zh: 掩饰，粉饰（分歧、裂痕或缺陷）
items.def_en: (+ sth) hide or disguise flaws, disagreements, or deceit beneath a superficial show of unity
items.ex_en: The joint statement merely papered over deep disagreements between the two leaders.
items.ex_zh: 这份联合声明只是粉饰了两位领导人之间的深刻分歧。

items.def_en: (+ in) to disguise, hide, or cover something unpleasant or secret
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime sought to cloak its aggressive military actions in diplomacy.
items.ex_zh: 该专制政权试图以外交辞令为其侵略性的军事行动披上伪装。

items.def_en: to pretend to have a particular feeling, condition, or illness
items.ex_en: The schoolboy decided to feign illness so he could skip soccer practice.
items.ex_zh: 那个男生决定装病，以便能够逃避足球训练。

items.def_zh: 掩饰，掩盖（真实情感或意图）；假装
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To hide your true feelings, intentions, or motives behind a false appearance.
items.ex_en: An honest leader does not dissemble when addressing serious national crises directly.
items.ex_zh: 一位正直的领导人在直接面对国家严重危机时绝不掩饰隐瞒真相。

items.def_zh: 掩饰，隐瞒（真实感情或意图）；假装
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To hide your real feelings, thoughts, or intentions by pretending.
items.ex_en: The experienced spy learned to dissimulate effortlessly in hostile political environments.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的间谍学会了在险恶的政治环境中毫不费力地伪装掩饰真实意图。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify dishonest communication achieved by hiding one's actual feelings, intentions, or character behind a false, deceptive exterior.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过掩盖真实意图、情绪或真相，戴上面具以混淆视听的欺瞒方式。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame describe disguising true intentions, emotions, or flaws beneath a misleading exterior, contrasting with active lying by emphasizing concealment and cosmetic pretense rather than outright fabrication.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架涉及在误导性表象下隐藏真实意图、情绪或缺陷，与直接说谎不同，它强调的是遮蔽掩饰与表面伪装而非凭空捏造。
groups.nuance_en: dissemble: deliberately conceal true motives or feelings under a false appearance (intentions / feelings) · feign: actively fabricate a false physical or emotional state (illness / ignorance / interest) · mask: cover up an underlying quality or condition so it goes unnoticed (pain / symptoms / scent) · gloss over: treat serious defects superficially to minimize their importance (flaws / differences / mistakes) · cloak: wrap something in an obscuring metaphorical shroud (motives / operations / identity)
groups.nuance_zh: dissemble: 伪装掩饰真实意图或情感 (intentions / feelings) · feign: 假装或装出某种生理/心理状态 (illness / ignorance / interest) · mask: 遮蔽掩盖使内在特质不被察觉 (pain / symptoms / scent) · gloss over: 掩饰带过缺陷以大事化小 (flaws / differences / mistakes) · cloak: 笼罩隐匿行动或真实身份 (motives / operations / identity)

groups.name: Deceive & Dupe Informally · 戏弄与扯谎欺骗 (Fool, Dupe, Bullshit)
groups.tip: 把对方当傻子戏弄与耍弄

items.def_en: to deceive someone playfully or jokingly as a jest
items.ex_en: Do not take him seriously; he is only kidding about moving away.
items.ex_zh: 别当真，他只是开玩笑说要搬走逗你呢。

items.def_en: (+ sb) tease someone by attempting to make them believe something untrue
items.ex_en: He told me he won the lottery, but he was having me on.
items.ex_zh: 他告诉我他中了大奖，其实只是在拿我开涮逗乐。

items.def_zh: 误导，哄骗（使抱有虚假期望）
items.def_en: (+ sb) mislead someone into believing something false, especially about one's intentions
items.ex_en: She never intended to marry him and was only leading him on.
items.ex_zh: 她从未打算嫁给他，只是在虚情假意地哄骗他。

items.def_zh: 忽悠，假意敷衍吊人胃口
items.def_en: to deceive someone over time by giving false hope or insincere promises
items.ex_en: He kept stringing her along for months with empty promises of a promotion.
items.ex_zh: 他用升职的空头支票忽悠了她好几个月。

items.def_en: (+ sb) successfully deceive or dupe someone into believing a falsehood
items.ex_en: The elderly couple was easily taken in by the charming rogue's dishonest sales pitch.
items.ex_zh: 这对老夫妇很容易就被那个迷人骗子的虚假推销蒙骗了。

items.def_zh: 愚弄，欺骗；干傻事，开玩笑（fool around）
items.def_en: 1. To trick, deceive, or make a dupe of someone. 2. To behave in a silly or playful way.
items.ex_en: You cannot fool me with that ridiculous excuse again, because I know the truth.
items.ex_zh: 你别想再用那个荒谬的借口来愚弄我，因为我知道真相。

items.def_en: 1. (informal, taboo) To say things that are untrue or exaggerated in order to deceive, impress, or mislead someone.
items.ex_en: Stop trying to bullshit me about your sales numbers, because I saw the report.
items.ex_zh: 别再拿你的销售数据忽悠我了，我已经看过报告了。

items.def_zh: 欺骗，愚弄（使其上当受骗）
items.def_en: (+ into) to deceive someone easily into doing or believing something foolish
items.ex_en: The corrupt broker duped dozens of investors into buying worthless, bankrupt shares.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败的经纪人诱骗了数十位投资者购买毫无价值的破产股票。

items.def_en: (+ into) to confuse and deceive someone deliberately, often through trickery
items.ex_en: Smooth-talking salespeople often bamboozle naive buyers into signing expensive, unnecessary long-term contracts.
items.ex_zh: 油嘴滑舌的销售人员经常哄骗天真的买家签署昂贵且不必要的长期合同。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe informally misleading, tricking, or feeding someone false narratives to make them believe an untruth, ranging from playful teasing to cynical fabrication.
groups.summary_zh: 非正式地愚弄、哄骗或胡扯以使人信以为真。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote deceiving someone informally through playful trickery, bluster, or manipulative delays, contrasting with malicious fraud by emphasizing gullibility and interpersonal gamesmanship.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指通过打趣、吹嘘或拖延手段在人际间戏弄或蒙骗他人，与恶性诈骗不同，它更侧重利用他人的轻信进行捉弄或言语忽悠。
groups.nuance_en: dupe: trick an unsuspecting person into acting as an unwitting tool (investors / public / victim) · string along: deceptively encourage someone with false hopes over time (suitor / client / investors) · take in: successfully deceive someone into believing a falsehood (marks / buyers / audience) · kid: tease or banter through harmless untruths (friend / brother) · bullshit: blatantly bluff or talk nonsense to mislead or impress (boss / interviewer / way out)
groups.nuance_zh: dupe: 欺骗使之成为盲目的工具或冤大头 (investors / public / victim) · string along: 长期吊着某人以虚假希望拖延 (suitor / client / investors) · take in: 蒙骗使人信以为真 (marks / buyers / audience) · kid: 开玩笑式的善意戏弄或说笑 (friend / brother) · bullshit: 胡吹瞎扯以蒙混过关或忽悠 (boss / interviewer / way out)

groups.name: Deceive & Swindle · 欺诈与诈取 (Swindle, Bilk, Gyp)
groups.tip: 通过不当手段骗取财物

items.def_en: (+ out of) to act dishonestly to gain an unfair advantage or take somebody's money
items.ex_en: The corrupt business partner cheated the young founder out of his entire company.
items.ex_zh: 那个腐败的商业伙伴骗走了年轻创始人手中的全部公司股权。

items.def_en: (+ into/out of) to trick somebody into doing something or giving away money after gaining their trust
items.ex_en: The slick fraudster conned the vulnerable widow into signing over her family home.
items.ex_zh: 那个圆滑的骗子诱骗脆弱的寡妇把祖宅签字过户。

items.def_en: (+ sb) cheat someone by charging them too much money or stealing from them
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_en: (+ sb + sth) trick someone into giving away money or possessions through deception
items.ex_en: A ruthless fraudster conned the gullible tourist out of five hundred precious dollars.
items.ex_zh: 一名无情的骗子骗走了轻信的游客五百美元宝贵钱财。

items.def_en: (+ sb + sth) obtain money or possessions dishonestly from someone by fraudulent means
items.ex_en: The dishonest financial manager swindled the vulnerable elderly woman out of her savings.
items.ex_zh: 那名不诚实的财务经理诈取了那位体弱多病的老妇人的全部积蓄。

items.def_en: (+ of) to unfairly obtain an exorbitant amount of money from somebody through trickery or overcharging
items.ex_en: Corrupt shady taxi drivers frequently fleece foreign tourists of their hard-earned travel money.
items.ex_zh: 不良出租车司机经常敲诈外国游客辛苦赚来的旅行钱款。

items.def_en: (+ out of) to cheat somebody out of money or property using fraudulent schemes
items.ex_en: The fraudulent scheme swindled hundreds of desperate small business owners out of money.
items.ex_zh: 该欺诈计划骗取了数百名陷入困境的小企业主的金钱。

items.def_en: 1. (+ out of) (informal, sometimes offensive) To cheat or swindle someone out of money or fair value.
items.ex_en: A dishonest street vendor gypped the naive backpacker out of fifty foreign dollars.
items.ex_zh: 一名不诚实的街头小贩骗取了那个天真的背包客五十块外币。

items.def_en: 1. (+ out of) To cheat someone out of money owed to them, or to avoid paying a bill.
items.ex_en: The rogue contractor bilked several elderly homeowners out of substantial renovation deposits.
items.ex_zh: 那名不良承包商骗取了数位老年房主大笔的装修定金。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate cheating, tricking, or defrauding an individual or entity out of money, goods, or rights through deceitful schemes or bad-faith transactions.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过虚假交易、花招或违约手段骗取他人钱财或应得之物。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote illicitly divesting a victim of money, goods, or rights through fraudulent schemes or overcharging, contrasting with forceful theft by relying on craftiness, breach of trust, or unequal transactions.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指通过欺诈手段、信任违背或高额索价非法占有他人财物，与暴力盗窃不同，它依赖心机骗局、信用背叛或不当获利。
groups.nuance_en: swindle: deprive someone of money or property through elaborate dishonest schemes (investors / company / fortune) · fleece: excessively overcharge or systematically strip of assets (tourists / marks / fortune) · rip off: blatantly overcharge or cheat in a transaction (customers / tourists) · con: win trust to cheat someone out of assets (victims / mark / way into) · gyp: cheat, shortchange, or swindle in a petty trade (buyer / customer)
groups.nuance_zh: swindle: 设骗局诈取巨额钱财或资产 (investors / company / fortune) · fleece: 漫天要价或彻底掏空财产 (tourists / marks / fortune) · rip off: 宰客、漫天索价或明目张胆蒙骗 (customers / tourists) · con: 骗取信任以套取财物 (victims / mark / way into) · gyp: 在小额交易中克扣或敲诈 (buyer / customer)

groups.name: Declaim & Intone · 歌咏与诵念 (Chant, Intone, Recite)
groups.tip: 有节奏地诵念经文或诗歌

items.def_en: (+ sth) to declaim or intone words in a dull, flat, and monotonous voice
items.ex_en: The tired clerk droned out the standard safety regulations without any emotion.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的办事员毫无感情地用单调的语调念出标准的守则。

items.def_en: [I/T] Sing or hum in a soft, low, intimate, and soothing voice
items.ex_en: The young mother crooned a tender lullaby to soothe her crying baby.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的母亲轻柔地吟唱着温柔的摇篮曲以安抚哭泣的婴儿。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to recite or declaim a long list, poem, or memorized piece of text quickly and easily
items.ex_en: The brilliant young student reeled off all the historical dates without pausing.
items.ex_zh: 那个聪明的小学生一口气流畅地背出了所有历史日期，中途毫无停顿。

items.def_zh: 吟诵，念唱（经文等）；反复呼喊，齐声喊唱
items.def_en: 1. To sing or recite a religious prayer or liturgical text on a monotone or simple melody. 2. To repeat a word, phrase, or slogan rhythmically together with a crowd.
items.ex_en: The devoted monks chant their ancient morning prayers in the quiet chapel.
items.ex_zh: 虔诚的僧侣们在寂静的小礼拜堂里吟诵古老的晨祷。

items.def_en: 1. To sing cheerful Christmas carols or songs of joy, especially in groups outdoors.
items.ex_en: Joyful townsfolk gathered to carol beneath the brightly decorated Christmas tree outside.
items.ex_zh: 欢乐的镇民们聚集在室外装饰一新的圣诞树下唱颂歌。

items.def_zh: 背诵，朗诵；逐一列举，详述
items.def_en: 1. To say a poem, speech, or passage aloud from memory before an audience. 2. To list or describe a series of facts, complaints, or items one by one.
items.ex_en: The distinguished scholar recited the classic poem with extraordinary passion and grace.
items.ex_zh: 这位尊贵的学者极其投入且优雅地朗诵了这首经典诗篇。

items.def_en: [T/I] Say or recite text with little rise and fall of the pitch of the voice, chant-like
items.ex_en: The solemn priest intoned the traditional Latin prayers over the silent congregation.
items.ex_zh: 庄重的神父向沉默的会众低沉而平缓地吟诵起传统的拉丁文祷词。

items.def_en: [I/T] Chant or sing sacred liturgical text or scripture according to musical notations
items.ex_en: The learned rabbi cantillated the sacred scriptural verses with deep spiritual reverence.
items.ex_zh: 学识渊博的拉比怀着深切的崇敬按传统韵律诵唱神圣经文。

items.def_en: [I/T] Utter words, rhetoric, or poetry aloud in an impassioned, formal, oratorical manner
items.ex_en: The experienced orator declaimed his fiery speech before the spellbound political audience.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的演说家在屏息聆听的政治受众面前慷慨陈词。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the vocal delivery of memorized, sacred, poetic, or ritual text using musical, rhythmic, or stylized cadence. Register moves from celebratory song-bursts to liturgical droning or formal rhetorical declamation.
groups.summary_zh: 指以抑扬顿挫的语调、唱诵或富有节奏感的声调背诵、念经或歌咏。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote uttering words with rhythmic, sustained musicality or ritualistic formal cadence, contrasting with ordinary conversational speaking through heightened, formulaic, or stylized acoustic delivery.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指以仪式化韵律、持续声调或歌咏形式发声诵读，与日常交谈不同，它具有程式化、音乐性或仪式性的声音特质。
groups.nuance_en: intone: utter with little rise and fall of pitch in a solemn liturgical manner (prayer / blessing / chant) · chant: rhythmically sing or shout repetitive cadences (slogan / mantra / psalm) · recite: repeat memorized verse or prose aloud in formal performance (poem / verse / lines) · croon: hum or sing softly in a low, soothing, sentimental tone (lullaby / ballad / baby) · reel off: utter a long list or sequence rapidly and effortlessly from memory (facts / names / statistics)
groups.nuance_zh: intone: 庄重而单调地慢声吟诵 (prayer / blessing / chant) · chant: 节奏齐整地反复唱咏或呼喊口号 (slogan / mantra / psalm) · recite: 凭记忆当众正式背诵 (poem / verse / lines) · croon: 轻柔低回地哼唱或抚慰 (lullaby / ballad / baby) · reel off: 不假思索地快速报出一连串内容 (facts / names / statistics)

groups.name: Decommission & Invalidate · 退役与使作废 (Decommission, Nullify, Invalidate)
groups.tip: 法律条约宣布作废或器械退役

items.def_en: to permanently withdraw machinery, ships, or aircraft from active service
items.ex_en: The commercial airline decided to retire its oldest fleet of passenger jets.
items.ex_zh: 该商业航空公司决定让旗下服役时间最长的一批客机退役。

items.def_zh: 退役；解除戒备；撤出服役
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) withdraw from active service, operational readiness, or an official post
items.ex_en: The CEO decided to stand down after the company's financial scandal was exposed.
items.ex_zh: 公司财务丑闻曝光后，首席执行官决定引咎辞职。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) officially revoke the accreditation, legal standing, or operational validity of someone or a document
items.ex_en: The disciplinary committee voted to strike off the fraudulent physician from register.
items.ex_zh: 纪律委员会经投票决定将该行骗的医生从行医名册中除名。

items.def_zh: 逐步淘汰；逐步停用退役
items.def_en: (+ sth) gradually withdraw something from operational use over a period of time
items.ex_en: The military intends to phase out diesel utility vehicles over several years.
items.ex_zh: 军方打算在数年之内逐步停用淘汰柴油多用途车辆。

items.def_en: to cancel the legal validity of a transaction, instrument, or contract
items.ex_en: The municipal judge decided to void the unlawful commercial lease agreement completely.
items.ex_zh: 地方法官决定彻底宣布这份非法的商业租赁协议作废。

items.def_en: to make an argument, document, ticket, or legal agreement officially no longer valid
items.ex_en: A missing signature from the principal borrower will invalidate the loan agreement.
items.ex_zh: 缺少主要借款人的签字将使整份贷款协议完全失效。

items.def_zh: 使无效，废弃，取消；使失去作用，使抵消
items.def_en: 1. to make an agreement, law, or result legally void and ineffective 2. to cause something to lose its value, effect, or power
items.ex_en: The court's sudden ruling will nullify all previous clauses of the partnership.
items.ex_zh: 法院的突如其来的裁决将使合伙协议的所有先前条款归于无效。

items.def_zh: 使退役，停用（军舰、武器或核设施等）
items.def_en: to officially withdraw a ship, aircraft, nuclear power plant, or weapons system from active service
items.ex_en: The national authority decided to decommission the aging nuclear power plant safely.
items.ex_zh: 国家主管部门决定对这座老化的核电站实施安全停用退役。

items.def_zh: 封存备用；封存（装备/工厂）
items.def_en: to take equipment, ships, or industrial facilities out of active operation while preserving them in storage
items.ex_en: The manufacturing company decided to mothball the costly assembly plant until profits rebounded.
items.ex_zh: 这家制造公司决定将昂贵的装配厂封存备用，直至利润回升。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame emphasize ending the operational lifecycle or functional validity of tangible assets, facilities, weapons, or legal documents, rendering them void or decommissioned.
groups.summary_zh: 使设施、装备退役停用，或使证件、文书失去效力。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote officially retiring equipment or legally stripping an agreement or status of binding validity, contrasting with physical destruction by focusing on institutional, legal, or lifecycle termination.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指通过官方程序让设备退役或从法律上剥夺契约效力，与物理摧毁不同，它侧重体制、法理或生命周期的正式终结。
groups.nuance_en: decommission: formally withdraw equipment or infrastructure from active service (reactor / warship / plant) · nullify: render legally void or rob something of its practical effect (law / contract / effect) · invalidate: destroy the legal standing or logical cogency of something (ballots / claims / findings) · phase out: gradually discontinue the production or use of something over stages (subsidies / chemicals / fleet) · retire: withdraw an asset or person permanently from regular operational use (aircraft / debt / jersey)
groups.nuance_zh: decommission: 正式退役或停运核电设施/军舰等大型重器 (reactor / warship / plant) · nullify: 依法宣布无效或彻底抵消效力 (law / contract / effect) · invalidate: 使票据/论点/契约丧失法定效力或真理性 (ballots / claims / findings) · phase out: 分步骤循序渐进地淘汰废除 (subsidies / chemicals / fleet) · retire: 使设备退出服役或资产彻底退役 (aircraft / debt / jersey)

groups.name: Deepen & Escalate · 加深与加剧 (Deepen, Intensify, Escalate)
groups.tip: 程度层层加深，矛盾冲突激化

items.def_en: [I/T] to make an emotion, tension, or quality become sharper, stronger, or more perceptible
items.ex_en: The sudden border clash served to heighten political tensions between both nations.
items.ex_zh: 突发的边境冲突加剧了两国之间的政治紧张局势。
items.ex2_en: Public panic heightened noticeably as conflicting rumors spread across local social channels.
items.ex2_zh: 随着矛盾的谣言在当地社交渠道上传播，公众恐慌明显加剧。

items.def_en: become more intense, aggressive, or exciting
items.ex_en: The fiery political debate began to heat up as controversial topics emerged.
items.ex_zh: 随着争议性话题的浮现，激烈的政治辩论开始白热化。
items.ex2_en: The chef carefully heated up the thick tomato sauce before serving dinner.
items.ex2_zh: 厨师在上晚餐前仔细地把浓稠的番茄酱加热。

items.def_en: To become deeper, more serious, or more intense; to make something deeper or more intense.
items.ex_en: The sudden unexpected policy changes served only to deepen the existing economic crisis.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的意外政策调整只会加剧现有的经济危机。
items.ex2_en: Her deep sadness deepened further when she heard the tragic family news.
items.ex2_zh: 当听到悲惨的家庭消息时，她内心的悲伤进一步加深了。

items.def_zh: 突然加剧；（争端、暴乱）骤然爆发
items.def_en: suddenly intensify or become violent, especially of an argument, crisis, or disease
items.ex_en: Old ethnic rivalries flared up unexpectedly after the controversial municipal election ended.
items.ex_zh: 在争议性的市政选举结束后，昔日的族群对立情绪突然爆发。

items.def_en: (+ sth) increase the intensity, speed, or scope of an activity or effort
items.ex_en: The hospital had to step up security measures following the recent incident.
items.ex_zh: 在最近的事件发生后，医院不得不加强安保措施。

items.def_en: 1. To become, or make something become, greater, worse, or more serious.
items.ex_en: Diplomats worked tirelessly to prevent the hostile military border standoff from escalating.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们不知疲倦地开展工作，以防边境军事对峙局势进一步恶化升级。
items.ex2_en: Reckless military threats could easily escalate the regional dispute into open warfare.
items.ex2_zh: 鲁莽的军事威胁极易使地区争端升级为公开战争。

items.def_en: 1. To become, or make something become, stronger, more serious, or more extreme.
items.ex_en: The regional authorities intensified security measures following several unexpected urban security breaches.
items.ex_zh: 在接连发生几次意外的城市安全防线破绽后，地区当局加强了安保措施。
items.ex2_en: The fierce tropical storm intensified rapidly as it approached the coastline overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的热带风暴在夜间接近海岸线时迅速增强。

items.def_en: to make a bad situation, problem, pain, or injury significantly worse and more severe
items.ex_en: His blunt and aggressive remarks will only aggravate the tense diplomatic dispute.
items.ex_zh: 他直率且具攻击性的言辞只会加剧原本就紧张的外交争端。

items.def_en: to sharply aggravate an already critical problem, conflict, or adverse condition
items.ex_en: Severe water shortages will severely exacerbate the difficult humanitarian crisis in drought regions.
items.ex_zh: 严重的水资源短缺将使干旱地区的艰难人道主义危机严重恶化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate an increase in degree, severity, emotional depth, or destructive magnitude of an ongoing condition, dispute, or state.
groups.summary_zh: 指程度、矛盾、危机或情感在深度与烈度上的持续升级与加剧。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote an increase in the magnitude, gravity, or friction of a conflict, emotion, or crisis, contrasting with neutral expansion by emphasizing heightened friction, peril, or volatile momentum.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指冲突、情绪或危机在程度、烈度或摩擦上的加剧升级，与中性的扩大不同，它带有摩擦加深、危机迫近或动荡升级的意味。
groups.nuance_en: escalate: rapidly spiral upward in scale, scope, or severity (conflict / violence / tensions) · deepen: grow more profound, grave, or entrenched over time (crisis / recession / rift) · intensify: make or become sharper, more acute, or more concentrated (efforts / scrutiny / heat) · heighten: elevate perceived sensitivity, drama, or awareness (anxiety / awareness / drama) · aggravate: exacerbate an already unfavorable wound, grievance, or situation (problem / condition / tension)
groups.nuance_zh: escalate: 局势或冲突呈螺旋式升级失控 (conflict / violence / tensions) · deepen: 危机、衰退或裂痕向纵深加剧恶化 (crisis / recession / rift) · intensify: 集中加码、增强力度或白热化 (efforts / scrutiny / heat) · heighten: 拔高紧张情绪、警惕感或戏剧性 (anxiety / awareness / drama) · aggravate: 刺激旧伤恶化或使既存矛盾变本加厉 (problem / condition / tension)

groups.name: Deeply Read & Pore Over · 凝神研读与细勘 (Pore, Scrutinize, Peruse)
groups.tip: 集中精力致力于特定方向

items.def_en: (+ sth) read a piece of writing carefully from start to finish to scrutinize or check details
items.ex_en: Make sure you read through the contract thoroughly before signing it.
items.ex_zh: 签字之前，务必把合同从头到尾仔细通读一遍。

items.raw_cluster: 专注与致力于 Focus & Specialize
items.def_zh: 专门从事，专攻，专门研究；使专门化
items.def_en: (British English: specialise; US: specialize) (+ in) to focus on a particular subject, skill, or line of work.
items.ex_en: Several brilliant young lawyers chose to specialise in international intellectual property law.
items.ex_zh: 几位优秀的年轻律师选择专门从事国际知识产权法领域的业务。

items.def_en: to read or examine something very carefully and thoroughly
items.ex_en: The corporate lawyer will peruse every contractual clause before signing the agreement.
items.ex_zh: 公司律师在签署该协议之前将细读每一项合同条款。

items.def_zh: 梳理；彻底搜寻（文献或记录）
items.def_en: to search through a body of records or writing exhaustively for specific information
items.ex_en: Federal investigators had to comb through millions of complex financial records carefully.
items.ex_zh: 联邦调查人员不得不仔细梳理数以百万计的复杂财务记录。

items.def_zh: 费劲且深入地研读（大量资料）
items.def_en: (+ sth) read laboriously and systematically through a large quantity of text or data
items.ex_en: The exhausted graduate student had to plow through heavy stacks of research.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的研究生不得不费劲地研读成堆沉重枯燥的研究文献。

items.def_zh: 凝神研读；仔细端详审阅
items.def_en: (+ sth) examine, read, or study a text or map with intense, focused attention
items.ex_en: Historians spent days to pore over ancient faded manuscripts inside the archive.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们在档案馆里花了好几天凝神研读古老褪色的手稿。

items.def_zh: 费力通读；艰难地读完（大量枯燥资料）
items.def_en: to spend a lot of time and effort reading through dense, long, or difficult documents
items.ex_en: I had to wade through dozens of dense legal briefs last night.
items.ex_zh: 我昨晚不得不艰难地读完数十份晦涩冗长的法律文书。

items.def_zh: 仔细阅读，仔细研读，钻研；审视
items.def_en: (also 'pore over') To read or study a book, document, or map very carefully and intently.
items.ex_en: The lead detective continued to pore over faded case files late tonight.
items.ex_zh: 首席刑警今夜很晚仍在继续仔细研读那些褪色的案件卷宗。

items.def_en: to examine a text, document, or object with great care and critical attention
items.ex_en: Independent regulatory auditors will scrutinize all corporate transactions to prevent widespread corruption.
items.ex_zh: 独立监管审计人员将仔细审查所有的企业交易以防普遍腐败。

groups.summary_en: An agent directs intense, sustained cognitive focus toward texts, documents, records, or technical details, examining every word or figure meticulously. Verbs emphasize the physical and mental intensity of scrutinizing written materials.
groups.summary_zh: 聚精会神、一丝不苟地研读或细查文本与资料。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote sustained, meticulous textual reading and deep study, contrasting with casual skimming or basic literacy by stressing arduous intellectual concentration and forensic textual scrutiny.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指耗费大量心力、极为缜密地研读文本与文献，与泛读或略读不同，它强调极高的智力专注度与穷微析微的研究态度。
groups.nuance_en: pore over: examine written materials with sustained, focused intensity (documents / manuscripts / maps) · peruse: read thoroughly with attentiveness or discerning care (contract / report / fine print) · comb through: search methodically through dense text to locate specific evidence (archives / records / data) · wade through: laboriously struggle through tedious, voluminous reading matter (reports / jargon / paperwork) · plow through: forcefully push through heavy reading materials by sheer persistence (novel / files / pages)
groups.nuance_zh: pore over: 凝神潜心细细研读考证 (documents / manuscripts / maps) · peruse: 极仔细且辨别性地审阅阅读 (contract / report / fine print) · comb through: 梳理排查密集文献以寻觅线索 (archives / records / data) · wade through: 极其吃力地跋涉于枯燥冗长的书卷中 (reports / jargon / paperwork) · plow through: 凭毅力啃完厚重的阅读材料 (novel / files / pages)

groups.name: Delay & Postpone · 推迟与拖延 (Postpone, Put off, Procrastinate)
groups.tip: 主观拖沓或客观延后日程

items.def_en: (+ sth) reschedule an event or deadline to a later date or time
items.ex_en: The project managers decided to push back the final delivery deadline again.
items.ex_zh: 项目经理们决定再次将最终交付的截止日期顺延推迟。

items.def_en: to postpone doing something or holding an event, often out of aversion
items.ex_en: We should not put off our difficult medical checkups out of fear.
items.ex_zh: 我们绝不能因为恐惧而拖延那些让人难受的身体检查。

items.def_en: to arrange for an event or action to happen at a later time than originally planned
items.ex_en: The executive committee voted to postpone the annual conference until early November.
items.ex_zh: 执行委员会经投票决定将年度会议推迟至十一月上旬举行。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) delay taking action or postpone doing something until a later time
items.ex_en: The cautious board chose to hold off on major corporate acquisitions today.
items.ex_zh: 谨慎的董事会今天决定暂缓推进那些重大的企业并购行动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) postpone consideration or settlement of a matter until a future date
items.ex_en: Parliament agreed to hold over the controversial housing reform bill until spring.
items.ex_zh: 议会同意将该项颇具争议的住房改革法案延期至春季再行审议。

items.def_zh: 延期，推迟；耽搁，延误；拖延
items.def_en: 1. To postpone something or cause it to happen at a later time. 2. To slow down or make someone or something late; to procrastinate.
items.ex_en: Severe winter blizzards will inevitably delay the departure of all regional flights.
items.ex_zh: 严重的冬季暴风雪将不可避免地耽搁所有支线航班的起飞。

items.def_en: to officially withhold action or delay an event until a later date
items.ex_en: The senior academic board decided to defer final judgment on the matter.
items.ex_zh: 资深学术委员会决定将对该事项的最终裁决延后做出。

items.def_en: To delay doing something that you ought to do, usually because you do not want to do it or find it boring.
items.ex_en: Chronic students frequently procrastinate instead of completing their assigned term papers promptly.
items.ex_zh: 有拖延习惯的学生经常拖延不决，而不是及时完成布置的学期论文。

items.def_en: to waste time through aimless indecision or slow action
items.ex_en: Do not dilly-dally when completing your important university scholarship applications this week.
items.ex_zh: 本周在填写重要的高校奖学金申请材料时，千万不要磨蹭拖拉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe rescheduling events to a later time or habitually deferring action due to reluctance or disorganization.
groups.summary_zh: 指主动推迟安排或因拖沓习性而迟迟不采取行动。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote intentionally moving a scheduled event, decision, or action into a later timeframe, contrasting with accidental tardiness by highlighting conscious temporal reassignment or avoidance.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指主动将既定日程、决定或行动推迟至后续时间窗口，与被动迟到不同，它强调有意识的时间重排、暂缓或拖拉延宕。
groups.nuance_en: postpone: formally arrange for a planned event to occur at a later date (game / meeting / election) · defer: willingly yield or put off an action/decision out of strategic priority or respect (decision / judgment / payment) · push back: reschedule a deadline or launch further into the future (deadline / launch / start date) · put off: delay doing something, often due to reluctance or aversion (task / visit / chores) · procrastinate: habitually and irrationally stall on necessary duties (duties / studying / paperwork)
groups.nuance_zh: postpone: 正式将活动延期至特定后续日期 (game / meeting / election) · defer: 出于战略考量或顺从尊重而缓办推后 (decision / judgment / payment) · push back: 将截止期或项目上线时间向后顺延 (deadline / launch / start date) · put off: 因畏难或厌恶情绪而推宕拖延 (task / visit / chores) · procrastinate: 习惯性拖延正事或逃避义务 (duties / studying / paperwork)

groups.name: Delegate & Devolve · 授权与下放 (Reassigning Authority & Governance)
groups.tip: 上级下放权力或委托外包

items.def_zh: 向下级传达/下放（权力、指令、任务）
items.def_en: (+ sth) transfer tasks, decisions, or authority down through a hierarchy
items.ex_en: Senior corporate managers gradually pass down complex operational decisions to regional directors.
items.ex_zh: 企业高管逐步将复杂的运营决策权向下下放给各大区域总监。

items.def_zh: 委派；把（权力/任务）委托给
items.def_en: [I/T] to entrust a task, responsibility, or authority to another person or subordinate
items.ex_en: The busy chief executive likes to delegate mundane administrative duties to assistants.
items.ex_zh: 这位繁忙的首席执行官喜欢把日常琐碎的行政职责委派给助手。

items.def_en: to appoint someone as a deputy or authorized representative to perform an official duty
items.ex_en: The foreign minister will depute a trusted ambassador to sign the treaty.
items.ex_zh: 外交部长将指派一名值得信任的大使代表其签署该条约。

items.def_zh: 外包；把（工作或职责）分派出去
items.def_en: (+ sth) subcontract or delegate work or responsibilities to an outside or lower party
items.ex_en: The overloaded creative studio decided to farm out all complex website coding.
items.ex_zh: 不堪重负的创意工作室决定把所有复杂的网站代码编写工作外包出去。

items.def_zh: 移交；下放（权力、控制权或职责）
items.def_en: (+ sth) transfer authority, control, or official responsibility to someone else
items.ex_en: The retiring mayor will hand over administrative authority to his elected successor.
items.ex_zh: 即将卸任的市长将把行政管理权正式移交给新当选的继任者。

items.def_zh: 外包，把（工作或业务）转包给外部公司
items.def_en: (+ to) To arrange for goods or services to be produced or provided by an outside supplier rather than within the organization.
items.ex_en: Many large software firms outsource their customer service operations to foreign providers.
items.ex_zh: 许多大型软件公司将客户服务业务转包给国外的服务提供商。

items.def_zh: 下放（权力、职责等）；移交；退化
items.def_en: (+ to/upon) To transfer power, authority, or responsibility from a central organization or government to a local or lower level.
items.ex_en: The national parliament will devolve substantial fiscal governance powers to regional assemblies.
items.ex_zh: 国家议会将把可观的财政管辖权力下放给各个地方议会。

items.def_zh: 下放权力，使非集权化；分散（机构或职能）
items.def_en: To transfer authority, functions, or administrative power from a single central body to regional or local units.
items.ex_en: The health agency aims to decentralize administrative control across municipal healthcare clinics.
items.ex_zh: 卫生机构旨在将行政管理权下放并分散到各个市镇医疗诊所。
items.ex2_en: The corporate management decentralized steadily over several years across regional international branches.
items.ex2_zh: 该企业的管理架构历经数年在各区域国际分部间稳步实现分权。

items.def_en: [I/T] to hire an outside firm or individual to perform part of a larger contract or obligation
items.ex_en: The primary infrastructure contractor plans to subcontract all electrical wiring to specialists.
items.ex_zh: 主要的基础设施承包商计划将所有的电气布线工程分包给专业团队。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the institutional transfer of responsibilities, decision-making powers, operational tasks, or legal authority from a centralized entity to lower tiers or outside parties. They differ in whether power moves downward within an hierarchy, outwards geographically, or to external third-party contractors.
groups.summary_zh: 将职权、工作或管理权从中心机构下放或转包外派。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote transferring administrative responsibilities, decision-making powers, or operational functions from a central authority to lower, local, or external agents, contrasting with simple assigning by altering the structure of governance.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指将管理权责或业务功能从中央权威机构向地方或下级转移，与简单的派发任务不同，它重塑了管辖权与权力架构。
groups.nuance_en: devolve: transfer constitutional or administrative governance downward to regional bodies (power / authority / responsibility) · delegate: entrust a specific mandate or duty to a subordinate while retaining ultimate accountability (tasks / authority / duties) · decentralize: redistribute administrative control away from a single focal point (administration / operations / network) · outsource: contract an internal operational process out to external vendors (services / manufacturing / IT) · depute: appoint someone as a surrogate proxy to act on one's behalf (subordinate / officer / agent)
groups.nuance_zh: devolve: 将中央政务权力下放至地方实体 (power / authority / responsibility) · delegate: 授权下属处理特定事务但保留最终责任 (tasks / authority / duties) · decentralize: 实行权力去中心化或分散行政管理 (administration / operations / network) · outsource: 将业务外包给外部专业机构 (services / manufacturing / IT) · depute: 指派代理人代表自己行使特权 (subordinate / officer / agent)

groups.name: Delve & Peruse · 探究与细读 (Peruse, Delve, Scrutinize)
groups.tip: 钻研深掘其内在奥秘

items.def_en: To read something again, especially in order to understand it better or appreciate it.
items.ex_en: I decided to reread the final chapter to fully understand the author's subtle argument.
items.ex_zh: 我决定重读最后一章，以充分理解作者微妙的论点。

items.def_zh: 潜心探寻；深掘细查（档案、文献）
items.def_en: (+ sth) search deeply and persistently through books, archives, or facts
items.ex_en: The historian spent several months burrowing into municipal archives to verify the forgotten treaty.
items.ex_zh: 这位历史学家花了数月时间深掘市政档案，以核实那份被遗忘的条约。

items.def_en: to read or examine something carefully and attentively
items.ex_en: The senior partners will peruse the revised merger contract before the closing session tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 高级合伙人将在明天闭会前仔细审阅修改后的合并合同。

items.def_zh: 深挖，深入探究（背景、资料）
items.def_en: (+ sth) investigate or examine information deeply and thoroughly
items.ex_en: Reporters started to dig into the candidate's financial history right after the announcement.
items.ex_zh: 候选人刚一宣布参选，记者们便开始深挖其财务背景。

items.def_zh: 深层剖析，向下深入钻研（数据、细节）
items.def_en: examine detailed data or records meticulously to reveal underlying facts
items.ex_en: Our analysts must drill down into the quarterly sales data to explain this anomaly.
items.ex_zh: 我们的分析师必须深入剖析季度销售数据，以解释这一异常现象。

items.def_en: to study or read something with deep concentration and sustained focus
items.ex_en: She sat quietly in the library to pore over ancient manuscripts until nightfall.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐在图书馆里，凝神研读古代手稿，直到夜幕降临。

items.def_zh: 探究，钻研，深入查考；翻找，翻寻
items.def_en: 1. (delve into) To investigate, research, or examine something deeply and thoroughly. 2. (delve into/in) To reach into a container to search for something.
items.ex_en: The investigative committee will delve into the root causes of the sudden bridge collapse.
items.ex_zh: 调查委员会将深入探究大桥突然坍塌的根本原因。

items.def_zh: 仔细推敲，仔细审视（字句或细节）
items.def_en: to examine a text, document, or object with extremely close and critical scrutiny
items.ex_en: Immigration officers continue to scrutinize every passport under ultraviolet light for subtle alterations.
items.ex_zh: 移民官员继续在紫外线下仔细审视每本护照，以发现细微的篡改痕迹。

items.def_en: to examine deeply to fully understand an obscure meaning or profound subject
items.ex_en: Philosophers have long sought to plumb the depths of human consciousness and moral duty.
items.ex_zh: 哲学家们长期以来一直试图探求人类意识和道德责任的精义。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe examining, reading, or researching texts and data with intense thoroughness and intellectual depth to uncover hidden or exact details.
groups.summary_zh: 指带着极高的专注度，深入探究、详尽审阅或反复研读文本与资料。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote deeply investigating, probing into concealed data, or examining subject matter with analytical rigor, contrasting with superficial observation by striving to penetrate below the surface.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指对深层或隐蔽信息进行纵深探查、钻研与细致解构，与浮于表面的观察不同，它强调由表及里的穿透性与实证性。
groups.nuance_en: delve: probe deeply into hidden history, origins, or complex subjects (past / history / archives) · drill down: systematically navigate down into finer layers of granular data (details / numbers / metrics) · scrutinize: subject every facet of an object or proposal to critical, forensic examination (finances / record / text) · burrow into: dig tenaciously beneath the surface to uncover buried details (records / files / research) · dig into: actively unpack and explore an issue or dataset with vigor (issues / data / background)
groups.nuance_zh: delve: 深入挖掘历史、根源或隐晦主题 (past / history / archives) · drill down: 逐层下钻分析更精细的数据或细节 (details / numbers / metrics) · scrutinize: 用放大镜般极其严苛地审视挑剔 (finances / record / text) · burrow into: 如打洞般深钻档案探查究竟 (records / files / research) · dig into: 兴致勃勃且扎实地深挖探求问题 (issues / data / background)

groups.name: Deprive & Divest · 剥夺与剥除 (Deprive, Divest, Strip)
groups.tip: 剥除财产或剥离权益

items.def_en: (+ of) to officially and forcefully take away an honor, rank, privilege, or property from someone
items.ex_en: The sports federation voted to strip the athlete of his gold medal immediately.
items.ex_zh: 体育联合会投票决定立即剥夺该运动员的金牌。

items.def_en: (+ of) to unfairly or violently deny someone something desirable, rightful, or beneficial
items.ex_en: Years of chronic illness had robbed him of his youthful vigor and optimism.
items.ex_zh: 多年的慢性疾病剥夺了他年轻时的活力与乐观。

items.def_zh: 剥夺（亲人、希望等珍贵事物）
items.def_en: (+ of) to deprive someone cruelly or devastatingly of a loved one or intangible vital possession
items.ex_en: The prolonged, brutal siege bereaved the aging scholar of his entire immediate family.
items.ex_zh: 那场漫长而惨烈的围城彻底夺去了这位老学者所有的直系亲人。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth of sth) deliberately take away property, rights, or an official title from someone
items.ex_en: The tribunal chose to strip the corrupt general of his title and privileges.
items.ex_zh: 特别法庭决定剥夺这位腐败将军的军衔与特权。

items.def_en: (+ sb of sth) unfairly or deceitfully prevent someone from getting or keeping something rightfully theirs
items.ex_en: Dishonest financial advisers managed to cheat the elderly widow out of her life savings.
items.ex_zh: 不诚实的财务顾问竟骗取了那位年迈寡妇一生的积蓄。

items.def_en: (+ sb of sth) unfairly deprive someone of something they ought to have had
items.ex_en: His crooked business partner managed to do him out of his fair share.
items.ex_zh: 他那个心术不正的合伙人耍花招剥夺了他应得的份额。

items.def_en: (deprive someone/something of something) To take something away from someone, or prevent them from having or enjoying something important or necessary.
items.ex_en: Solitary confinement tends to deprive prisoners of sensory stimulation and normal human contact.
items.ex_zh: 单独监禁往往会剥夺犯人的感官刺激和正常的人际接触。

items.def_zh: 剥夺，夺去（权力、财产等）；使脱去（衣物）；变卖，出售（资产）
items.def_en: 1. (divest someone/something of something) To strip someone of power, rights, or possessions. 2. To strip someone of clothing. 3. To sell off an investment, business asset, or subsidiary.
items.ex_en: The high court acted swiftly to divest the rogue administrator of all authority.
items.ex_zh: 高等法院迅速采取行动，剥夺了该失职行政官员的所有权力。

items.def_en: (+ of) to oust or officially force someone out of possession of their land, home, or goods
items.ex_en: The imperial government sought to dispossess native villagers of their ancestral farming lands.
items.ex_zh: 帝国政府企图强行剥夺当地村民祖传的耕地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate dispossessing someone of rights, status, property, or privileges, typically following the syntactic pattern 'verb someone of something'. They differ primarily in register, ranging from common legal/moral denial (deprive) to formal organizational or judicial stripping (divest, strip).
groups.summary_zh: 依法律、权威或强力夺取某人的权利、身份或财产。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote divesting someone or something of essential rights, titles, property, or protective coverings, contrasting with ordinary taking by emphasizing severe loss, disempowerment, or bare exposure.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指剥夺他人的基本权利、头衔、财产或剥除其防护性外表，与一般拿走不同，它具有实质性的削弱、剥夺与暴露意味。
groups.nuance_en: deprive: prevent someone from having necessary rights, resources, or necessities (citizens / sleep / liberty) · strip: forcibly and humiliatingly take away rank, titles, or outer coverings (rank / titles / assets) · divest: legally or strategically dispose of assets, shares, or authority (assets / shares / holdings) · rob: unfairly take away a valuable intangible quality or opportunity (dignity / opportunity / youth) · bereave: ruthlessly leave desolate through death or profound loss (family / parents / widow)
groups.nuance_zh: deprive: 剥夺基本生存权利、自由或必需品 (citizens / sleep / liberty) · strip: 屈辱性地强行剥夺官阶、头衔或外壳 (rank / titles / assets) · divest: 依战略或法理剥离出售股权与资产 (assets / shares / holdings) · rob: 夺去本该属于某人的尊严、青春或机遇 (dignity / opportunity / youth) · bereave: 因死亡而使某人沦于丧亲剧痛 (family / parents / widow)

groups.name: Derail & Disrupt Balance · 扰乱平衡与搅扰 (Mess, Unbalance, Derail)
groups.tip: 打破既有秩序使事物陷入紊乱

items.def_en: (mess sth up) to disrupt or spoil a plan, arrangement, or balanced state
items.ex_en: One minor misunderstanding could completely mess up our delicate travel schedule for next week.
items.ex_zh: 一个小小的误会就可能彻底打乱我们下周精密的旅行计划。

items.def_en: (+ sth) disrupt or cause disorder in a plan, mechanism, or smooth operation
items.ex_en: A single faulty sensor managed to foul up the entire automated assembly line.
items.ex_zh: 仅一个故障传感器就彻底搞砸了整条自动化装配线的运作。

items.def_en: (+ sth) bungle or throw an arrangement into confusion and disarray
items.ex_en: Careless clerical errors threatened to screw up the firm's carefully coordinated tax filing.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的文书错误可能会把公司精心协调的纳税申报彻底搞砸。

items.def_zh: 打乱，使心烦意乱或失衡
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) upset the composure, timing, or normal functioning of someone or something
items.ex_en: Unexpected delays on the subway can easily throw off the speaker's morning rehearsal.
items.ex_zh: 地铁突发的延误很容易打乱演讲者早晨的排练节奏。

items.def_zh: 弄乱，搞砸；胡闹，瞎摆弄；聚餐
items.def_en: 1. (often mess up) To make something untidy or dirty; to spoil or ruin something. 2. (mess with / around) To handle carelessly or meddle. 3. To take meals together in a military mess.
items.ex_en: Please don't touch these neatly sorted files or you will mess them all.
items.ex_zh: 请不要碰这些分类整理好的文件，否则你会全给弄乱。

items.def_zh: 使失去平衡；使心神错乱，扰乱
items.def_en: 1. To cause someone or something to lose physical balance or stability. 2. To upset someone's mental or emotional stability.
items.ex_en: Sudden sharp gusts of wind threatened to unbalance the tightrope walker completely.
items.ex_zh: 突然刮起的阵阵狂风眼看就要彻底打破走钢丝者的平衡。

items.def_en: to disturb the composure or balance of someone, making them feel unsettled
items.ex_en: The defense attorney's pointed questions seemed to disconcert the confident prosecution witness.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师针锋相对的提问似乎扰乱了那位自信的控方证人的心神。

items.def_en: to obstruct and throw a process, plan, or negotiation completely off its normal course
items.ex_en: Stubborn disagreements over intellectual property could derail the fragile international peace talks.
items.ex_zh: 知识产权方面的顽固分歧可能会使脆弱的国际和谈彻底出轨。
items.ex2_en: The passenger train derailed suddenly on the icy tracks outside the station.
items.ex2_zh: 客运列车在车站外结冰的轨道上突然脱轨了。

items.def_en: to throw a structure, system, or mental balance thoroughly out of joint
items.ex_en: Witnessing the sudden disaster threatened to unhinge his already fragile mental state.
items.ex_zh: 亲眼目睹这场突如其来的灾难，可能使他本就脆弱的精神彻底失常。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe upsetting the physical equilibrium, established routine, or smoothly operating plan of someone or something, throwing it off-kilter.
groups.summary_zh: 打破原有的平衡、节律或稳定运作，使人或机制陷入紊乱失衡。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote disrupting the stability, coherence, or trajectory of an established process or mental equilibrium, contrasting with static error by underscoring kinetic deviation, confusion, or breakdown.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指破坏既定进程、系统稳定或心智平衡，与静态犯错不同，它强调动态轨道的偏离、打乱节奏与失衡溃败。
groups.nuance_en: derail: abruptly knock a structured process, talk, or plan off its track (negotiations / talks / career) · unbalance: perturb physical, systemic, or emotional equilibrium (rival / economy / mind) · disconcert: unsettle composure and cause sudden self-conscious confusion (audience / opponent / composure) · throw off: disrupt a delicate rhythm, calculation, or concentration (timing / balance / schedule) · mess up: botch or introduce chaos into an otherwise orderly arrangement (plans / life / timing)
groups.nuance_zh: derail: 使既定谈判、计划或事业出轨脱节 (negotiations / talks / career) · unbalance: 打破系统平衡、竞争均势或内心稳态 (rival / economy / mind) · disconcert: 使某人突然失措、局促或不安 (audience / opponent / composure) · throw off: 打乱精细节拍、计算或作息平衡 (timing / balance / schedule) · mess up: 把井然有序的规划搞砸或弄乱 (plans / life / timing)

groups.name: Derive & Conclude Logically · 逻辑推导与得出结论 (Conclude, Derive, Infer)
groups.tip: 依逻辑前提出结论

items.def_en: [I/T] to understand or infer something from information received or observed
items.ex_en: From her nervous tone, I gather that negotiations are not proceeding very well.
items.ex_zh: 从她紧张的语气中，我推知谈判进展得不太顺利。
items.ex2_en: Dark storm clouds gathered rapidly over the jagged mountain peaks this afternoon.
items.ex2_zh: 今天下午，厚厚的乌云在崎岖的山峰上空迅速聚集。

items.def_zh: 推断出，得出结论；（使）结束，终止；达成，缔结
items.def_en: 1. to decide or form an opinion after considering all the facts or information. 2. to bring something to an end, or to come to an end. 3. to arrange or agree on a formal agreement or deal
items.ex_en: After evaluating the forensic evidence, investigators conclude that the blaze was set deliberately.
items.ex_zh: 在评估了法医物证之后，调查人员断定这场大火系故意纵火。

items.def_zh: 推导出，推断；源于，起源于；获得，取得
items.def_en: 1. to deduce or trace something from an underlying source, principle, or premise. 2. (derive from) to come or originate from something. 3. to obtain or get something from something else
items.ex_en: Theoretical physicists frequently derive complex cosmological models from fundamental symmetry principles.
items.ex_zh: 理论物理学家经常从基本的对称原理推导出复杂的宇宙学模型。

items.def_en: (+ sth) arrive at a logical deduction or solution through mental effort and analysis
items.ex_en: Scientists are trying to figure out why the virus mutated so rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们正试图弄明白这种病毒为何变异得如此之快。

items.def_en: (+ sth) deduce or determine something mathematically or systematically from premises
items.ex_en: The math student tried to work out the elusive formula before the exam.
items.ex_zh: 这个数学系学生试图在考试前推导出那个难以捉摸的公式。

items.def_en: (+ sth) deduce a complete truth or narrative by systematically connecting separate facts and clues
items.ex_en: Detectives worked patiently to piece together the sequence of events before the robbery.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们耐心地综合推断抢劫发生前的事件经过。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ from) to reach an opinion or conclusion from evidence and indirect facts
items.ex_en: Historians can infer significant societal shifts directly from preserved ancient municipal tax registers.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家可以直接从保存完好的古代市政税收登记册中推断出重大社会变革。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ from) to estimate or project trends into an unknown area based on existing facts
items.ex_en: Economists must extrapolate future consumer demand carefully from these preliminary regional survey results.
items.ex_zh: 经济学家必须根据这些初步的区域调查结果审慎推测未来的消费需求。

items.def_en: [I/T] to deduce something to be probable despite lack of certain confirmation
items.ex_en: Without direct eyewitness testimony, prosecutors could only surmise the suspect's original escape route.
items.ex_zh: 在缺乏直接目击者证词的情况下，检方只能凭蛛丝马迹推测嫌疑人最初的逃跑路线。

groups.summary_en: This frame denotes arriving at an understanding, truth, or logical deduction based on premises, evidence, or systematic calculation. Verbs range from general logical conclusions to step-by-step mathematical or formal derivation.
groups.summary_zh: 指依据前提、数据或事实进行逻辑演绎，推断出必然或合乎理据的结论。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote extracting a logical conclusion or principle through systematic reasoning, observation, or synthesis of clues, contrasting with blind guessing through reliance on inferential evidence.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指基于观察证据、线索综合或逻辑法则提炼出确定结论，与凭空猜测不同，它依托严密的证据链与推导过程。
groups.nuance_en: infer: deduce unstated facts logically from premises or indirect evidence (meaning / intent / motive) · derive: trace or mathematically/conceptually extract a formula, meaning, or benefit from an origin (formula / conclusion / pleasure) · conclude: arrive at a settled analytical judgment after evaluating evidence (investigation / debate / chapter) · extrapolate: project known trends or data points into uncharted scenarios (trends / results / future) · piece together: reconstruct a coherent narrative by gathering scattered fragments (puzzle / truth / events)
groups.nuance_zh: infer: 根据间接证据或弦外之音进行逻辑推断 (meaning / intent / motive) · derive: 理论推导或从渊源中提炼公式/内涵 (formula / conclusion / pleasure) · conclude: 在全面权衡证据后得出定论 (investigation / debate / chapter) · extrapolate: 以已知数据外推预测未知趋势 (trends / results / future) · piece together: 将零散碎片拼凑拼合出事件全貌 (puzzle / truth / events)

groups.name: Designate & Denominate · 称呼与命名 (Call, Name, Term)
groups.tip: 指名道姓赋予特定称呼

items.def_zh: 称呼，给……命名；呼唤，召唤；打电话
items.def_en: 1. To give a specified name, title, or description to someone or something. 2. To speak in a loud voice to attract attention; to summon. 3. To telephone someone.
items.ex_en: Most of her close colleagues still call her by her familiar childhood nickname.
items.ex_zh: 她的大多数亲密同事仍然用她那熟悉的童年绰号称呼她。

items.def_zh: 命名，称呼；提名，任命；列举
items.def_en: 1. To give a name to a person, place, or thing. 2. To nominate or appoint someone to a role or position. 3. To mention or identify by name.
items.ex_en: The board of directors voted unanimously to name him as the new chief.
items.ex_zh: 董事会一致投票任命他为新任首席执行官。

items.def_zh: 把……称为，用特定的词语表达
items.def_en: 1. To give a particular name, title, or label to someone or something.
items.ex_en: Sociologists often term this persistent urban phenomenon as modern community fragmentation.
items.ex_zh: 社会学家常把这种持续存在的城市现象称为现代社区割裂。

items.def_en: (+ as) to assign a characterization or classification to someone or something
items.ex_en: Critics unfairly label any unorthodox political proposal as hopelessly radical or unworkable.
items.ex_zh: 批评家们不公地将任何非传统政治主张都贴上无可救药的激进或不可行标签。

items.def_en: to officially assign a specific name, status, or identity to something
items.ex_en: The city council plans to designate this wetland zone as a protected reserve.
items.ex_zh: 市议会计划将该湿地区域正式定名为受保护的自然保护区。

items.def_zh: (+ sb/sth + as sth) 把……称作；把……命名为
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth + as sth) to mention or name someone or something by a particular term or descriptor
items.ex_en: Local residents frequently refer to this narrow, winding alleyway as the Devil's Path.
items.ex_zh: 当地居民经常把这条狭窄弯曲的小巷称作“魔鬼之路”。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth + after sb/sth) to give someone or something the same name as another person or thing
items.ex_en: She was named after her grandmother, who had passed away the year before.
items.ex_zh: 她是用她祖母的名字命名的，祖母在前一年去世了。

items.def_en: to give an informal, descriptive name, title, or nickname to someone or something
items.ex_en: Music enthusiasts quickly dub the talented young prodigy the next Mozart.
items.ex_zh: 音乐爱好者们很快把这位才华横溢的神童称为“下一位莫扎特”。

items.def_en: to name a person at baptism, or formally name an object such as a ship
items.ex_en: Dignitaries gathered beside the stormy harbor to christen the navy's newest guided-missile destroyer.
items.ex_zh: 要员们齐聚在风暴肆虐的港口边，为海军最新的导弹驱逐舰举行正式命名洗礼。

groups.summary_en: A speaker or community applies an identifier, label, or specific descriptor to an entity, spanning common verbal identification to formal technical and ceremonial naming.
groups.summary_zh: 指称、给事物起名或以特定学术、正式术语界定称谓。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote assigning a specific verbal identifier, title, or descriptive classification to an entity, contrasting with basic reference by enacting a formal, nominative, or reputational identity.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指为客体赋予正式称谓、头衔或定性归类标签，与普通提及不同，它行使的是名分界定、命名或定调功能。
groups.nuance_en: designate: formally assign a status, title, or boundary to something (area / successor / representative) · dub: bestow an informal, honorary, or descriptive nickname upon someone (king / hero / phenomenon) · term: categorize or characterize something using a specific technical or conceptual phrase (behavior / process / condition) · label: classify someone or something with a simplistic, often restrictive descriptor (extremist / failure / product) · name: give a definitive proper identity or nominate formally to an office (child / successor / ship)
groups.nuance_zh: designate: 正式划定范围、指定继承人或指派官职 (area / successor / representative) · dub: 授予非正式绰号、雅号或赋予称号 (king / hero / phenomenon) · term: 用特定术语或概念名之 (behavior / process / condition) · label: 贴上简化甚至带偏见的标签定性 (extremist / failure / product) · name: 赋予专有名词命名，或正式提名 (child / successor / ship)

groups.name: Desire & Crave · 渴望与渴求 (Long, Covet, Yearn)
groups.tip: 苦苦思慕企求满足强烈心愿

items.def_zh: 热望、期盼（常带怅惘之情）
items.def_en: (+ for/to do) to want something very much, especially when it is distant or difficult to obtain
items.ex_en: Exiled dissidents long for the day they can return safely to their homeland.
items.ex_zh: 流亡异见人士热望有朝一日能够平安返回祖国。

items.def_en: (+ sth) have a restless and impatient urge to experience or obtain something
items.ex_en: After weeks of indoor desk work, the eager mountaineer was itching for adventure.
items.ex_zh: 在室内案头工作数周后，这位热切的登山者按捺不住对探险的渴望。

items.def_zh: 向往、渴望（常指不切实际的念头）
items.def_en: (+ after/for) to possess a persistent, uneasy desire for something not readily attainable
items.ex_en: Retired professionals often hanker after the hectic pace and prestige of corporate life.
items.ex_zh: 退休的专业人员常常渴望重温企业生活那种忙碌节奏与声望。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) experience an intense, aching desire for someone or something unattainable
items.ex_en: Trapped in the desolate borderlands, the weary soldier began to pine for home.
items.ex_zh: 困在荒凉的边境，疲惫的士兵开始深切思念家乡。

items.def_zh: 极度渴求、渴望（如饥似渴）
items.def_en: (+ for/after) to have a deep, gnawing spiritual or physical desire
items.ex_en: Persecuted scholars often hunger for intellectual freedom and basic recognition in tyrannical regimes.
items.ex_zh: 受到迫害的学者在专制政权下往往极度渴求学术自由与基本的认可。

items.def_zh: 热望、强烈渴求（食物、毒瘾或关注）
items.def_en: to feel an overpowering physical or psychological compulsion for something
items.ex_en: Exhausted after the marathon, she began to crave cool water and salty snacks.
items.ex_zh: 马拉松跑完精疲力竭后，她开始强烈渴望凉水和咸味小吃。

items.def_en: To feel a strong, deep, and often wistful desire or longing for someone or something.
items.ex_en: Throughout his prolonged exile, the solitary artist would constantly yearn for his native mountains.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的流亡岁月中，这位孤独的艺术家时常深切思慕故乡的群山。

items.def_zh: 垂涎，贪图，渴望（尤指他人之物）
items.def_en: To want very much to have something, especially something that belongs to someone else.
items.ex_en: Ambitious courtiers quietly covet the prime minister's growing influence over foreign imperial policy.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的廷臣暗中觊觎首相在帝国对外政策上日益增长的影响力。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) pursue or crave something with desperate, breathless eagerness
items.ex_en: Ruthless warlords pant after supreme dominion over the newly discovered fertile valley.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的军阀们迫切追逐对新发现的这片肥沃山谷的最高统治权。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this intensity scale express longing or urgent desire for something, graduated from gentle yearning or wistful dreaming up to intense craving or illicit lusting for what belongs to another.
groups.summary_zh: 表示对某物、人或状态的渴望，程度由低到高逐级递增。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote intensely longing for an object, state, or person, contrasting with mild preference by evoking acute emotional hunger, sensory compulsion, or aching lack.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指对人、物或状态产生极度渴望与思念，与温和的偏好不同，它包含生理饥渴感、心绪焦灼或因匮乏而引起的隐痛。
groups.nuance_en: crave: experience a compulsive physical or psychological appetite (attention / food / drugs) · yearn: feel a deep, poignant, and melancholic longing for something unattainable (peace / homeland / touch) · covet: enviously and illicitly desire what rightfully belongs to another (wealth / position / accolades) · pine for: physically or emotionally languish from unrequited longing or homesickness (lover / home / past) · long: endure a persistent, heartfelt desire to bridge distance or absence (reunion / break / freedom)
groups.nuance_zh: crave: 产生生理瘾性或神经驱使般的强烈饥渴 (attention / food / drugs) · yearn: 怀抱深切凄美且带感伤的长久神往 (peace / homeland / touch) · covet: 觊觎垂涎属于他人的名利或权位 (wealth / position / accolades) · pine for: 因苦恋、思乡而形销骨立、郁郁寡欢 (lover / home / past) · long: 历经时空隔绝而由衷盼望 (reunion / break / freedom)

groups.name: Detain & Imprison · 羁押与监禁 (Detain, Remand, Incarcerate)
groups.tip: 司法机关扣押或关押限制

items.def_en: to put someone in a jail or correctional facility
items.ex_en: The district court decided to jail the repeat offender for eighteen months.
items.ex_zh: 地区法院裁定将该屡犯者关进监狱服刑十八个月。

items.def_en: to put someone in a police cell or prison and secure them there
items.ex_en: Guards will lock up violent suspects immediately to ensure safety within the precinct.
items.ex_zh: 警卫将立即关押暴力嫌疑人，以确保分局内部的安全。

items.def_en: (+ sb) send someone formally to prison or a secure mental institution
items.ex_en: The tough judge decided to put away the violent burglar for ten years.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的法官决定将那名暴力入室盗窃犯关进监狱十年。

items.def_en: (+ sb) confine someone securely away from society in a prison, ward, or cell
items.ex_en: Authorities decided to shut away the dangerous spy in a remote maximum-security cell.
items.ex_zh: 当局决定将这个危险的间谍隔离关押在偏远的最高戒备牢房中。

items.def_en: (+ sb) keep someone in legal custody pending a future hearing or trial
items.ex_en: The magistrate agreed to hold over the accused felon pending next week's hearing.
items.ex_zh: 地方法官同意延期羁押这名重罪被告，直至下周开庭。

items.def_en: 1. To officially keep someone in custody or confinement, especially for questioning. 2. To delay someone or keep them from proceeding.
items.ex_en: Border patrol officers may detain suspicious travelers for further interrogation and luggage inspection.
items.ex_zh: 边境巡逻官员可扣押可疑旅客以进行进一步审讯和行李检查。

items.def_zh: 拘留；软禁（政治犯或交战国侨民）
items.def_en: to put someone in prison or a detention camp, typically during wartime or for political reasons, without a trial
items.ex_en: Hostile authorities chose to intern enemy aliens without formal trial during wartime crises.
items.ex_zh: 战时危机期间，敌对当局选择在未经正式审判的情况下拘留敌国侨民。

items.def_en: (law) To send an accused person back into custody or release them on bail while awaiting trial or further court proceedings.
items.ex_en: The presiding judge chose to remand the murder suspect without bail until trial.
items.ex_zh: 主审法官决定将这名谋杀嫌疑犯还押候审，不得保释。

items.def_en: to put someone in prison or keep them confined under formal penal authority
items.ex_en: Authoritarian regimes frequently incarcerate outspoken political journalists within high-security military prisons.
items.ex_zh: 专制政权经常把敢言的政治记者监禁在高度戒备的军事监狱中。

groups.summary_en: Judicial or law-enforcement authorities legally deprive an individual of liberty, holding them in custody, on trial remand, or in formal penal confinement. Terms range from short-term procedural holding to formal, prolonged incarceration.
groups.summary_zh: 执法或司法机关依法剥夺人身自由，实施拘留、还押或监禁。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote depriving a person of their physical liberty through state sanction, legal containment, or punitive confinement, contrasting with kidnapping by occurring under legalistic or institutional authority.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指行使国家强制力或司法程序剥夺他人人身自由，与非法绑架不同，它具备司法性、惩戒性或制度化监禁的特质。
groups.nuance_en: detain: temporarily hold someone in custody during an inquiry or border transit (suspect / travelers / protesters) · remand: send an accused person back into custody pending trial or further hearing (suspect / prisoner / case) · intern: confine enemy citizens or political dissidents without criminal trial during wartime (civilians / rebels / nationals) · incarcerate: lock someone inside a penal institution following criminal sentencing (offenders / criminals / convicts) · jail: confine an offender to a municipal lockup or prison (culprit / driver / rioters)
groups.nuance_zh: detain: 在边检或调查阶段暂时性扣留羁押 (suspect / travelers / protesters) · remand: 司法还押候审或发回羁押所 (suspect / prisoner / case) · intern: 在战乱时无需审判而拘禁敌国侨民或政见者 (civilians / rebels / nationals) · incarcerate: 经判决后正式将罪犯关入监狱监禁 (offenders / criminals / convicts) · jail: 投案入狱或收押入拘留所 (culprit / driver / rioters)

groups.name: Develop & Evolve · 生长与演变进化 (Develop, Grown, Industrialize)
groups.tip: 事物由小到大演进蜕变

items.def_en: develop into a fuller, broader, or more elaborate form over time
items.ex_en: The modest pilot initiative will slowly open out into an expansive nationwide program.
items.ex_zh: 这一低调的试点倡议将逐渐拓展演进为一项覆盖全国的宏大项目。
items.ex2_en: The visionary architect opened out the narrow interior into a spacious atrium.
items.ex2_zh: 这位有远见的建筑师将狭窄的内部空间改造成开阔的中庭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) develop and mature gradually into a larger, more advanced state or role
items.ex_en: The promising rookie will eventually grow into an authoritative leader for our team.
items.ex_zh: 这位前途光明的新秀终将成长为我们团队颇具威信的领袖。

items.def_en: (+ sth) undergo a developmental transition to become something qualitatively different or advanced
items.ex_en: Over centuries, the sleepy fishing settlement managed to turn into a bustling metropolis.
items.ex_zh: 历经数百年，这个沉睡的渔村成功演变成为一座繁华的大都市。
items.ex2_en: Intense summer heat can quickly turn fresh dairy milk into sour curds.
items.ex2_zh: 夏季酷暑很快就会将新鲜牛奶变成酸奶酪凝块。

items.def_zh: 发展；进化；成长；开发；逐渐形成；患（病）
items.def_en: To grow, mature, or evolve over time; to create, expand, or acquire something gradually.
items.ex_en: Researchers strive to develop effective antiviral therapies to combat newly emerging respiratory pathogens.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员正努力开发有效的抗病毒疗法，以应对新出现的心源性及呼吸道病原体。
items.ex2_en: The delicate embryo develops rapidly during the crucial initial weeks of gestation.
items.ex2_zh: 娇嫩的胚胎在妊娠关键的最初几周内发育迅速。

items.def_zh: 推进；向前演进取得进展
items.def_en: [I/T] to make progress or move to a higher stage of development
items.ex_en: The research team aims to advance scientific knowledge through extensive clinical trials.
items.ex_zh: 该研究团队旨在通过广泛的临床试验推进科学认知的发展。
items.ex2_en: The allied infantry troops advanced steadily across the snowy valley toward dawn.
items.ex2_zh: 盟军步兵部队在拂晓前沿着白雪覆盖的山谷稳步推进。

items.def_en: [I/T] to reach full physical, mental, or structural development
items.ex_en: The seedlings will mature over several weeks before they can be safely harvested.
items.ex_zh: 幼苗将在数周内发育完全，随后便可安全收获。
items.ex2_en: Experienced winemakers mature exceptional red vintages inside toasted oak barrels for years.
items.ex2_zh: 经验丰富的酿酒师会将上等红葡萄酒放在烘烤过的橡木桶中陈酿数年。

items.def_en: To develop large-scale industries and modern manufacturing in a country, region, or economy.
items.ex_en: The government launched ambitious reforms to rapidly industrialize the rural northern provinces.
items.ex_zh: 政府启动了雄心勃勃的改革，以使北部农业省份迅速实现工业化。
items.ex2_en: The isolated coastal region industrialized rapidly after the new railway was built.
items.ex2_zh: 新铁路建成后，偏远沿海地区迅速实现了工业化。

items.def_zh: 演化；渐进演变为高阶形式
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ into/from) to develop gradually into a more complex or better-adapted state
items.ex_en: The simple prototype quickly evolved into an indispensable tool for modern data analysis.
items.ex_zh: 这个简单的原型迅速演变成为现代数据分析中不可或缺的工具。
items.ex2_en: Creative screenwriters constantly evolve compelling cinematic characters over multiple serialized TV seasons.
items.ex2_zh: 有创造力的编剧在多季连载电视剧中不断演进塑造引人入胜的电影角色。

items.def_en: to begin to grow, sprout, or develop rapidly and luxuriantly
items.ex_en: A vibrant digital economy began to burgeon across the coastal technology hubs.
items.ex_zh: 充满活力的数字经济开始在沿海各科技枢纽中蓬勃兴起。

groups.summary_en: An entity or society advances over time from an embryonic or basic state to a sophisticated, mature, or technologically organized condition.
groups.summary_zh: 事物或社会系统历经自然滋长、演进及工业化进阶。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote progressive systemic growth, structural maturation, or adaptive advancement over time, contrasting with sudden creation by tracking gradual, organic, or societal phases of transformation.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指事物在时间维度上经历渐进的系统成长、结构成熟或演进升级，与突兀创造不同，它循着有机规律逐步跃迁。
groups.nuance_en: evolve: develop adaptively by incremental stages into a more complex form (species / language / strategy) · mature: grow into full functionality, ripeness, or peak developmental capacity (market / individual / brain) · industrialize: transform an agrarian economic infrastructure into heavy mechanized industry (nation / economy / region) · develop: bring latent capabilities, ideas, or land into structured realization (skills / plot / property) · advance: march forward in technological, scientific, or strategic capability (civilization / agenda / science)
groups.nuance_zh: evolve: 经演化与适应演变成更高阶结构 (species / language / strategy) · mature: 趋于完全成熟、稳固或巅峰状态 (market / individual / brain) · industrialize: 推动经济实体经历工业化转型 (nation / economy / region) · develop: 促使潜在能力、地块或技术渐次成形 (skills / plot / property) · advance: 在科技、文明或战略位阶上向前挺进 (civilization / agenda / science)

groups.name: Die & Perish · 死亡与消亡 (Die, Perish, Expire)
groups.tip: 从自然死亡到惨烈消亡

items.def_en: to breathe one's last breath and pass away
items.ex_en: Surrounded by his sorrowful family, the elderly monarch gently expired at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 在悲痛的家人环绕下，年迈的君王于黎明时分安详辞世。

items.def_en: cease to live (used as a gentle or polite euphemism for dying)
items.ex_en: Her beloved grandmother passed away quietly in her sleep late last Tuesday night.
items.ex_zh: 她挚爱的祖母在上周二深夜于睡梦中安详离世。

items.def_en: die and depart from biological life
items.ex_en: The revered village elder passed on after battling a persistent chronic illness.
items.ex_zh: 那位备受尊敬的村庄长者在与顽固的慢性病抗争后逝世。

items.def_en: (formal or law) To die.
items.ex_en: The legal contract terminated immediately after the sole surviving business partner deceased.
items.ex_zh: 在仅存的那位合伙人身亡后，该法律合同随即终止。

items.def_en: (+ to) to die from the effects of a disease, injury, or extreme hardship
items.ex_en: The patient tragically succumbed to severe complications following the prolonged surgical procedure.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的手术后，该患者不幸因严重的并发症不治身亡。

items.def_en: (formal or law) To die before someone else.
items.ex_en: Tragically, the eldest son predeceased his parents following an unforeseen vehicle collision.
items.ex_zh: 不幸的是，长子在一场意外的车祸后先于双亲亡故。

items.def_zh: 死，死亡；凋谢；消亡，平息；渴望
items.def_en: 1. To stop living and become dead. 2. To fade away or disappear gradually; stop functioning.
items.ex_en: Without adequate water and natural sunlight, the delicate indoor plants will die.
items.ex_zh: 若是缺乏充足的水分与自然阳光，这些娇嫩的室内植物便会枯死。

items.def_zh: 丧生，猝死，毁灭；（橡胶、食物等）老化变质，腐烂
items.def_en: 1. (formal or literary) To die, especially in an accident, disaster, or harsh conditions. 2. (of materials or food) To decay, rot, or lose quality.
items.ex_en: Thousands of vulnerable refugees perished during the brutal winter across the desolate plateau.
items.ex_zh: 在荒凉的高原上，数千名脆弱的难民在严酷的寒冬中丧生。

items.def_en: die suddenly and unexpectedly
items.ex_en: The marathon runner suddenly dropped dead from acute heart failure near the finish.
items.ex_zh: 那名马拉松选手在终点线附近因突发急性心力衰竭猝死。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the cessation of physical biological life, ranging from ordinary death to formal legal passing and violent, untimely destruction.
groups.summary_zh: 指生命机能终止，涵盖中性去世、法言辞世直至暴烈遇难或消亡。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote the irreversible cessation of biological life, contrasting with transient injury or dormancy by signaling absolute mortality, often differentiated by register, agency, or pathos.
groups.desc_zh: 该框架指有机体生命的不可逆终结，与暂时休克或负伤不同，它标志着生理生命的绝对灭绝，依语体庄重度与宿命感而有所区分。
groups.nuance_en: perish: die violently, untimely, or en masse in harsh conditions or disasters (crew / livestock / millions) · succumb: yield fatally after a prolonged defense against illness or injury (illness / injuries / infection) · expire: reach biological cessation of life with an exhaled final breath (patient / monarch / term) · pass away: gently refer to death using respectful euphemistic decorum (grandfather / friend / elder) · die: cease all vital biological functions completely and irreversibly (natural causes / thirst / cancer)
groups.nuance_zh: perish: 遇难、因恶劣环境横死或大量罹难消亡 (crew / livestock / millions) · succumb: 在久病不愈或重伤负隅抵抗后力竭殒命 (illness / injuries / infection) · expire: 咽下最后一口气或寿终正寝 (patient / monarch / term) · pass away: 带有敬意或哀思的委婉辞世 (grandfather / friend / elder) · die: 停止生命体征的中性生理死亡 (natural causes / thirst / cancer)

groups.name: Directed Strike & Deflective Impact · 偏转击打与定向击球 (Bat, Backhand, Shank)
groups.tip: 球棒打、反手击等不同打法
