items.def_en: [I/T] to ward off or deflect an incoming blow, weapon, or thrust with a counter-movement
items.ex_en: With an effortless flick of his blade, the swordsman parried the lethal thrust.
items.ex_zh: 剑客信手一挥剑刃，便架开了那致命的一刺。

items.def_zh: （高尔夫中）用杆颈击（球），斜向击偏（球）；用自制尖刀刺伤
items.def_en: 1. (golf) To strike a ball with the heel of the club so that it flies sharply sideways. 2. (slang) To slash or stab someone with a makeshift knife.
items.ex_en: He nervously shanked the ball straight into the dense trees off the fairway.
items.ex_zh: 他紧张地用杆颈把球击偏，球径直飞进了球道旁的密林中。

items.def_en: (+ sth) strike and deflect a projectile or object away with a quick blow
items.ex_en: The minister batted away questions regarding the leaked report.
items.ex_zh: 部长轻易避开了关于泄露报告的提问。

items.def_en: (+ sth) deflect or parry an incoming blow or object using an implement or forearm
items.ex_en: The quick guard raised his forearm just in time to fend off the strike.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的守卫及时抬起前臂，挡开了袭来的这一击。

items.def_en: (+ sth) strike a delivered ball or projectile back in the direction it came
items.ex_en: The agile tennis player hit back the fierce serve with incredible precision.
items.ex_zh: 那位身手矫健的网球选手以惊人的精准度回击了那记凶猛的发球。

items.def_zh: 用球棒击球；击打，拍打；眨（眼）
items.def_en: 1. To hit a ball with a bat, or take a turn at batting in baseball or cricket. 2. To hit or strike something lightly and quickly with a hand or paw. 3. To open and close one's eyes quickly (especially in 'bat an eyelid').
items.ex_en: The playful cat gently batted the colorful yarn across the carpeted living room.
items.ex_zh: 调皮的猫咪在铺着地毯的客厅里轻轻拍打着彩色的毛线球。

items.def_en: to hit a target with a sharp, quick, sweeping blow using an open hand or flat implement
items.ex_en: She grabbed a rolled magazine to swat the annoying fly hovering near her.
items.ex_zh: 她抓起一本卷起来的杂志，猛拍那只在她身旁盘旋的讨厌苍蝇。

items.def_zh: 用反手击（球）；反手击打，掌掴
items.def_en: 1. (sports) To hit a ball with a backhand stroke. 2. To strike someone with the back of the hand.
items.ex_en: She smoothly backhanded the speeding tennis ball deep into the opponent's corner.
items.ex_zh: 她流畅地反手击球，将飞速而来的网球打入对手场地深处底角。

items.def_en: to strike someone or something sharply with a flat surface, producing a loud cracking sound
items.ex_en: He smacked the wooden desk with his flat palm to restore immediate silence.
items.ex_zh: 他用手掌重重拍打木桌，以立刻恢复现场的安静。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify physical strikes delivered to a projectile or object using an implement or hand technique, differentiated by biomechanical motion, intended deflection angle, or erratic execution.
groups.summary_zh: 指使用手、拍或工具施加的特殊姿势击打或偏转击球动作。
groups.desc_en: Striking or deflecting an incoming object, attack, or question away from its trajectory, contrasting with stationary blocking or straight absorption.
groups.desc_zh: 通过击打或挥拂使来袭物、攻击或诘问偏离原定轨迹，区别于单纯静止的格挡或承受。
groups.nuance_en: parry: skillful deflection of an incoming blow or query (thrust / question / blow) · bat away: dismissive or casual swatting aside (inquiry / microphone / concern) · swat: brisk, crushing strike at an annoying nuisance (fly / hand / ball) · shank: misdirected, clumsy glancing strike in sports (kick / shot / ball) · backhand: crisp strike delivered with the back of the hand (volley / compliment / slap)
groups.nuance_zh: parry: 巧妙化解或格开来袭攻势 (thrust / question / blow) · bat away: 漫不经心或不屑地随手拂开 (inquiry / microphone / concern) · swat: 迅猛拍击讨嫌之物 (fly / hand / ball) · shank: 球类击打失误导致的严重偏向 (kick / shot / ball) · backhand: 反手抽击或反手击打 (volley / compliment / slap)

groups.name: Directives & Authoritative Demands · 命令与强制要求 (Require, Order, Command)
groups.tip: 上对下发号施令与强制要求

items.def_en: (+ to do) to command, instruct, or invite someone with personal authority
items.ex_en: The king bid his loyal heralds to summon the nobles across the realm.
items.ex_zh: 国王吩咐他忠诚的传令官去召集王国各地的贵族。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 明确要求；正式呼吁
items.def_en: (+ sth) to publicly or authoritatively demand that something happen or be provided
items.ex_en: The opposition party leader publicly called for an independent investigation into election fraud.
items.ex_zh: 反对党领袖公开呼吁对选举舞弊行为展开独立调查。

items.def_en: 1. To demand or order something authoritatively or by rule. 2. To need something for a particular purpose.
items.ex_en: Federal regulations require all commercial airlines to conduct mandatory safety inspections regularly.
items.ex_zh: 联邦法规强制要求所有商业航空公司必须定期进行安全检查。

items.def_en: (+ to do / on) to instruct, urge, or prescribe authoritatively with moral or legal force
items.ex_en: The wise judge enjoined both conflicting parties to maintain strict professional confidentiality.
items.ex_zh: 明智的法官责成产生冲突的双方务必严守职业保密义务。

items.def_zh: (+ sth) 强制规定；正式下达（命令或规则）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to authoritatively state a mandatory rule, principle, or instruction to be obeyed
items.ex_en: The government has laid down strict safety guidelines for the industry.
items.ex_zh: 政府为该行业制定了严格的安全指南。

items.def_zh: 命令，指示；订购，点餐；组织，整理
items.def_en: 1. To give instructions to or direct somebody to do something with authority. 2. To request or purchase goods or services.
items.ex_en: The commanding officer ordered his troops to withdraw immediately behind defensive barricades.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官命令他的部队立即撤退至防御路障之后。

items.def_zh: 命令，指示；指挥，统率；博得，赢得；俯瞰
items.def_en: 1. To give an authoritative order to someone. 2. To have control or charge of; to deserve and receive respect or attention.
items.ex_en: The captain commanded the disciplined crew to prepare the deck for incoming storms.
items.ex_zh: 船长命令训练有素的船员们做好准备，以应对即将来临的风暴。

items.def_en: to make something compulsory by official, statutory, or judicial authority
items.ex_en: The new municipal statute mandates routine structural inspections for all older residential towers.
items.ex_zh: 新颁布的市政法规强制要求对所有老旧住宅高楼进行常规结构检查。

items.def_en: to order or issue a legally binding decree with absolute, sovereign authority
items.ex_en: The imperial council decreed that strict curfews would govern the entire occupied territory.
items.ex_zh: 帝国委员会正式颁布法令，要求整个被占领区实行严格宵禁。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express an agent exercising formal or institutional authority to obligate someone to perform an action, differing in peremptory force.
groups.summary_zh: 体现施令者凭借权威或规范强制要求下属履行的层层升级指令。
groups.desc_en: Authoritatively laying down obligatory actions backed by legitimate or institutional power, differing from mere requesting or gentle advising.
groups.desc_zh: 依凭制度权力或绝对权威强制推行某项作为，区别于一般的请求或温和建议。
groups.nuance_en: command: supreme personal or military authority (troops / respect / obedience) · order: explicit direct instruction backed by sanctions (evacuation / inquiry / retreat) · mandate: formal legal or institutional requirement (vaccination / reporting / reforms) · enjoin: solemn legal prohibition or moral urging (conduct / party / silence) · require: systemic or conditional necessity (documentation / permit / attendance)
groups.nuance_zh: command: 统帅层级发出的绝对号令 (troops / respect / obedience) · order: 具威慑力的直接指令 (evacuation / inquiry / retreat) · mandate: 法律或制度层面的强制规定义务 (vaccination / reporting / reforms) · enjoin: 司法禁令式裁定或严肃训诫 (conduct / party / silence) · require: 客观条件或规程上的必然要求 (documentation / permit / attendance)

groups.name: Disappoint to Deject · 失望、沮丧与消沉 (Disappoint, Depress, Deject)
groups.tip: 期望落空并伴随情绪低落与无力感

items.def_en: to fail to support or help someone as they had hoped or expected
items.ex_en: The inexperienced lawyer let down his desperate client by missing crucial court deadlines.
items.ex_zh: 这名缺乏经验的律师错过了关键的庭审期限，辜负了他那急切的当事人。

items.def_en: (+ sb) cause someone to lose their cheerfulness, feeling disappointed or depressed
items.ex_en: Hearing endless pessimistic economic forecasts always manages to bring the entire office down.
items.ex_zh: 听到没完没了的悲观经济预测，总是会让整个办公室的人情绪低落。

items.def_en: 1. To fail to satisfy the hopes, wishes, or expectations of someone.
items.ex_en: The heavily delayed sequel will inevitably disappoint millions of eager franchise fans.
items.ex_zh: 这部严重拖延的续集将不可避免地让数百万热切期待的系列粉丝感到失望。

items.raw_cluster: 使沮丧与使消沉 Depress & Deject
items.def_zh: 使沮丧，使消沉；使萧条；按压
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel sad, gloomy, or downhearted. 2. To reduce economic activity or trade. 3. To press something down.
items.ex_en: The dreary gray skies and persistent chilly drizzle began to depress the campers.
items.ex_zh: 阴沉沉的灰暗天空和持续的刺骨细雨开始让露营者们感到沮丧消沉。

items.def_en: to cause someone to lose determination, confidence, or enthusiasm
items.ex_en: Repeated rejections from prestigious publishers did not dishearten the young determined novelist.
items.ex_zh: 来自著名出版商的屡次拒绝并没有让这位坚定执着的年轻小说家灰心。

items.def_en: (+ sb) cause someone to feel dispirited, despondent, or dejected
items.ex_en: The terrible news of their financial failure cast down the entire household.
items.ex_zh: 他们财务失败的糟糕消息使得全家人都陷入了消沉沮丧之中。

items.def_en: (+ sb) burden someone emotionally, causing lingering sadness or depression
items.ex_en: She felt weighed down by domestic responsibilities and work pressures.
items.ex_zh: 她感到家庭责任和工作压力压得自己喘不过气来。

items.def_zh: 瓦解斗志；严重挫伤士气
items.def_en: to destroy someone's confidence, enthusiasm, or will to persevere
items.ex_en: Constant supply shortages completely demoralized the frontline troops during the harsh campaign.
items.ex_zh: 持续的补给短缺彻底挫伤了前线部队在这场艰苦战役中的士气。

items.def_en: to make gloomy, dispirited, or downcast in spirit
items.ex_en: The unexpected loss dejected the aspiring athlete for several painful consecutive days.
items.ex_zh: 这场意料之外的失败让这名雄心勃勃的运动员垂头丧气了好几天。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe external outcomes, events, or circumstances causing someone to experience sinking spirits, ranging from mild failure to meet expectations to deep, dispiriting melancholy.
groups.summary_zh: 描述外在变故使人情绪滑落，从期望落空到深层挫败与消沉。
groups.desc_en: Subjecting someone to progressive emotional sinking, from dashed expectations down to total loss of spirit, unlike acute shock or grief.
groups.desc_zh: 使人的情绪从期待落空一路沉沦至斗志尽丧，区别于突发性的惊骇或剧痛。
groups.nuance_en: disappoint: failing to fulfill an explicit hope or standard (expectations / fans / hopes) · dishearten: chipping away at someone's resolve or confidence (news / defeat / loss) · demoralize: destroying fighting spirit, discipline, or inner morale (troops / workforce / team) · depress: casting an enduring emotional gloom over the mind (spirits / mood / outlook) · weigh down: oppressing the spirit with ongoing burdens (conscience / worries / soul)
groups.nuance_zh: disappoint: 期望未能如愿以偿 (expectations / fans / hopes) · dishearten: 打击信心并削弱做事心劲 (news / defeat / loss) · demoralize: 瓦解斗志、纪律或团队士气 (troops / workforce / team) · depress: 使情绪陷入深沉沉闷状态 (spirits / mood / outlook) · weigh down: 持续的心理负担压迫精神 (conscience / worries / soul)

groups.name: Discard as Rubbish · 弃置与作废 (Discard, Junk, Scrap)
groups.tip: 当作废品丢弃不要

items.def_zh: 报废；取消；把…作为废品扔掉
items.def_en: to cancel, abandon, or break up something as no longer useful or practical
items.ex_en: The transport agency decided to scrap the aging train fleet due to costs.
items.ex_zh: 交通管理局决定将老旧的火车车队报废，因为成本过高。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to get rid of something that is no longer wanted or needed
items.ex_en: You shouldn't throw away such a wonderful job opportunity.
items.ex_zh: 你不应该白白浪费这么好的工作机会。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to discard something useless or unwanted as trash
items.ex_en: The judge threw out the lawsuit due to lack of evidence.
items.ex_zh: 法官因证据不足驳回了该起诉讼。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to get rid of or abandon someone or something regarded as useless
items.ex_en: The greedy emperor quickly cast aside his former allies once power was secured.
items.ex_zh: 一旦皇权稳固，那位贪婪的皇帝便迅速将过去的盟友弃置一旁。

items.def_en: to throw something away casually into the trash
items.ex_en: He casually tossed the crumpled aluminum can into the nearest recycling bin.
items.ex_zh: 他随手把揉瘪的铝罐扔进了最近的垃圾回收桶。

items.def_en: (+ out/away) to casually throw something away as rubbish (informal)
items.ex_en: We should chuck out all these broken plastic chairs before the garage sale.
items.ex_zh: 在车库大甩卖前，我们应该把这些破损的塑料椅子全扔掉。

items.def_en: to get rid of or abandon something or someone abruptly (informal)
items.ex_en: She chose to ditch her old gasoline car in favor of an electric.
items.ex_zh: 她选择弃用自己的旧燃油车，换成了一辆电动汽车。

items.def_zh: 丢弃，抛弃，把……当作废物扔掉；放弃（计划等）
items.def_en: (informal) to throw away or discard something old or worthless; to abandon a plan or idea.
items.ex_en: The design team reluctantly junked the flawed prototypes after weeks of testing.
items.ex_zh: 经过数周的测试，设计团队无奈将这些有缺陷的原型当作废物抛弃。

items.def_en: to throw away or get rid of something that is no longer useful or wanted.
items.ex_en: Please discard all outdated laboratory chemicals in accordance with federal safety protocols.
items.ex_zh: 请按照联邦安全规程将所有过期的实验室化学品妥善丢弃。

groups.summary_en: An agent deliberately rids themselves of an unwanted, damaged, or useless physical object, project, or concept by casting it away or writing it off as worthless. Verbs range from neutral standard usage ('discard') to pragmatic commercial or colloquial dismissal ('scrap', 'chuck', 'ditch').
groups.summary_zh: 将废旧、无用或不再需要的事物视作垃圾处理或作废。
groups.desc_en: Permanently abandoning or discarding an entity as useless, worn out, or an impediment, contrasting with storing away or temporary setting aside.
groups.desc_zh: 将毫无价值、陈旧破损或成为累赘的物件彻底抛弃或注销，区别于封存或暂时搁置。
groups.nuance_en: scrap: formally cancel or break up for parts (plans / project / vessel) · junk: throw away as cheap worthless rubbish (car / old furniture / ideas) · ditch: abruptly desert or get rid of an inconvenient burden (partner / car / baggage) · toss: throw away casually without deliberation (draft / wrapping / letter) · cast aside: deliberately reject what was once valued (inhibitions / principles / friends)
groups.nuance_zh: scrap: 废止企划或将整物报废拆解 (plans / project / vessel) · junk: 当作破烂廉价丢弃 (car / old furniture / ideas) · ditch: 突兀摆脱甩掉包袱累赘 (partner / car / baggage) · toss: 随手轻巧地丢入废纸篓 (draft / wrapping / letter) · cast aside: 决然抛弃原先重视之物 (inhibitions / principles / friends)

groups.name: Disorganize & Jumble · 搅乱与搞混 (Muddle, Disarray, Jumble)
groups.tip: 搅浑打乱使毫无头绪

items.def_en: to mix things together in a confused, untidy way so their order is lost
items.ex_en: The playful puppy jumbled the neat stack of newly filed tax receipts.
items.ex_zh: 活泼的小狗把刚刚归档整理好的一整叠税票给弄乱了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to throw an arrangement, room, or schedule into untidy disarray
items.ex_en: The sudden system crash completely messed up my carefully organized project files.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的系统崩溃彻底搞乱了我精心整理的项目文件。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to jumble together or confuse the order or identity of things
items.ex_en: The harried receptionist managed to mix up the delicate medical sample labels.
items.ex_zh: 手忙脚乱的接待员不慎把精密医学样本的标签给搞混了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to arrange things in a confused, disordered, or nonsensical manner
items.ex_en: He accidentally muddled up the final exam papers during the hectic afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 在忙乱的午后，他不小心把期末试卷弄得杂乱无章。

items.def_en: to mix up thoughts, signals, or the proper order of things so they become unintelligible
items.ex_en: A sudden power surge scrambled the sensitive radar signals across the control room.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的电涌打乱了控制室内的精密雷达信号，使其无法辨识。

items.def_en: to throw someone's hair, clothes, or appearance into untidy disorder
items.ex_en: Violent gusts of coastal wind swiftly disheveled her elegant hair and coat.
items.ex_zh: 猛烈的沿海强风迅速吹乱了她优雅的发型和大衣。

items.def_en: 1. To arrange things in a confused, disordered way, or confuse one thing with another. 2. To make someone confused and unable to think clearly.
items.ex_en: The careless clerk managed to muddle the chronological order of our contracts.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的办事员不慎弄乱了我们合同的时间先后顺序。

items.def_en: (formal) To throw something into a state of disorder or confusion.
items.ex_en: The sudden audit disarrayed the administrative staff's carefully managed archival system.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的审计工作打乱了行政人员精心管理的档案系统。

items.def_en: to throw an orderly system, arrangement, or mind into severe disorder
items.ex_en: The immense, relentless trauma threatened to permanently derange her delicate psychological balance.
items.ex_zh: 巨大且持续的创伤恐将彻底扰乱她那脆弱的心理平衡。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe throwing a systematic arrangement, schedule, or mental clarity into a state of untidy disorder, confusion, or entangling disarray.
groups.summary_zh: 将原本有序的事物、条理或思维搅乱，使其陷入混杂与无序状态。
groups.desc_en: Disarranging individual elements into a confused, intertwined, or messy state, contrasting with total systemic destruction.
groups.desc_zh: 使原本规整的各个细部要素交织混乱、毫无章法，区别于整个系统的彻底摧毁。
groups.nuance_en: jumble: haphazardly mixing heterogeneous items together (clothes / ideas / words) · muddle: confusing thoughts, facts, or sequences into incoherence (affairs / thinking / names) · scramble: panicky or rapid shuffling of order or signals (eggs / brains / signal) · dishevel: ruffling hair or garments into untidiness (hair / clothes / appearance) · mix up: mistakenly swapping or confusing distinct entities (dates / directions / identities)
groups.nuance_zh: jumble: 多样杂物杂乱无序地混在一起 (clothes / ideas / words) · muddle: 搞乱思维条理、事实或脉络 (affairs / thinking / names) · scramble: 仓促混乱地打乱顺序或信号 (eggs / brains / signal) · dishevel: 扯乱衣物或弄乱发型 (hair / clothes / appearance) · mix up: 混淆两件截然不同的事物 (dates / directions / identities)

groups.name: Disorganize & Throw into Chaos · 扰乱秩序与致乱 (Disorganize, Disrupt, Derange)
groups.tip: 打乱正常秩序与心智

items.def_en: (+ sth) to severely disrupt or cause functional chaos in a plan or mechanical system
items.ex_en: A single misplaced decimal point fouled up the entire financial projection model.
items.ex_zh: 一个放错位置的小数点搞砸了整套财务预测模型。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to throw an orderly plan or situation into complete disarray
items.ex_en: His reckless, last-minute intervention completely screwed up our carefully planned schedule.
items.ex_zh: 他在最后一刻鲁莽的插手把我们精心策划的日程搞得一团糟。

items.def_en: to interrupt the normal progress, continuity, or operation of an activity or system
items.ex_en: Protesting workers blocked key transit intersections to disrupt morning commuter train services.
items.ex_zh: 抗议的工人们封锁了主要交通路口，扰乱了早间通勤列车的正常运行。

items.def_en: To disrupt the order, arrangement, or smooth functioning of a system, plan, or organization.
items.ex_en: Frequent contradictory directives from upper management thoroughly disorganized the ongoing construction project.
items.ex_zh: 管理层频繁下达的矛盾指令彻底打乱了正在进行的施工项目秩序。

items.def_zh: 使杂乱无章，使陷入混乱
items.def_en: to throw into complete disorder, confusion, or lack of proper arrangement
items.ex_en: The violent tactical skirmish quickly disarrayed the defending regiment's initial formation.
items.ex_zh: 激烈的战术小规模冲突迅速打乱了守军团队最初的防御阵形。

items.def_zh: 弄得翻天覆地；使彻底大乱
items.def_en: (+ sth) to cause utter confusion, total disorder, or radical disruption in a system or life
items.ex_en: The sudden arrival of noisy quadruplets turned their quiet life upside down.
items.ex_zh: 吵闹的四胞胎的突然降临让两人原本平静的生活彻底大乱。

items.raw_cluster: 扰乱与使狂乱 Disrupt & Derange
items.def_zh: 使精神错乱，使发狂；扰乱，弄乱
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive) To make someone unable to think or act normally, or make someone mentally ill. 2. To disturb the proper order or function of something.
items.ex_en: Severe sleep deprivation began to derange the exhausted soldier's cognitive faculties.
items.ex_zh: 严重的睡眠匮乏开始扰乱那名疲惫士兵的正常认知功能。

items.def_en: to overturn or transform an established system or situation completely
items.ex_en: The innovative digital platform threatens to upend the traditional retail banking industry.
items.ex_zh: 这一创新的数字平台正威胁要彻底颠覆传统的零售银行业格局。

items.def_zh: 使瘫痪，使陷入完全停滞
items.def_en: to cause a system, organization, or function to stop operating entirely
items.ex_en: The nationwide transportation strike threatened to paralyze all major industrial logistics operations.
items.ex_zh: 全国范围的交通罢工恐将使所有主要的工业物流运作彻底瘫痪。

groups.summary_en: Pertains to shattering the structural order, operational schedule, or functional coherence of a system, plan, or organization. Verbs escalate from minor procedural disorder ('disorganize') to active interruption ('disrupt') and total functional derangement ('derange', 'wreak havoc').
groups.summary_zh: 指破坏既定组织、运作体系或秩序，从打乱条理升级为瓦解瘫痪。
groups.desc_en: Severely breaking down the operational continuity and systemic stability of an organization or situation, unlike minor superficial cluttering.
groups.desc_zh: 破坏整体系统运转、打断既定秩序使其陷入瘫痪，区别于局部表层的凌乱。
groups.nuance_en: disrupt: sharply interrupting a functioning process or routine (traffic / supply chain / meeting) · disorganize: destroying structured methodology or arrangement (regiment / plan / workflow) · upend: turning established reality completely on its head (assumptions / market / lives) · derange: throwing mental or mechanical balance into madness (mind / system / machinery) · foul up: thoroughly botching and snarling an operation (schedule / paperwork / operation)
groups.nuance_zh: disrupt: 强力介入打断既定流程或服务运转 (traffic / supply chain / meeting) · disorganize: 破坏既有编制秩序与组织机能 (regiment / plan / workflow) · upend: 彻底颠覆颠倒现状或既有格局 (assumptions / market / lives) · derange: 扰乱理智或精密平衡使其失序 (mind / system / machinery) · foul up: 因拙劣失误而把局面搞砸弄乱 (schedule / paperwork / operation)

groups.name: Disparage & Defame · 贬损与诋毁 (Disparage, Discredit, Vilify)
groups.tip: 打上不良标签并败坏对方名誉

items.def_en: to speak of someone or something in a derogatory or dismissive manner
items.ex_en: Critics often disparage the amateur artist's minimalist style as crude and unrefined.
items.ex_zh: 批评家们常常贬低这位业余艺术家的极简主义风格，称其粗糙拙劣。

items.def_en: to unfairly attack the character, importance, or reputation of someone
items.ex_en: Political opponents tried to denigrate her substantial academic and legislative achievements.
items.ex_zh: 政治对手们试图抹黑她在学术与立法方面所取得的实质成就。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to criticize, belittle, or humiliate someone to make them feel insignificant
items.ex_en: He constantly put down his colleagues in meetings to hide his own deep insecurities.
items.ex_zh: 他在会议上不断贬低同事，以掩盖自己内心深深的不安全感。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to disparage or speak slightingly and unfavorably of someone or something
items.ex_en: Stop running down your brother's achievements whenever our relatives come over to visit.
items.ex_zh: 每当亲戚过来拜访时，别总是贬低你弟弟取得的成就。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to aggressively undermine or attack a person's standing, reputation, or character
items.ex_en: The old factory was torn down to make way for a modern shopping mall.
items.ex_zh: 那座旧工厂被拆除，以便改建现代化的购物中心。

items.def_zh: 败坏……的名誉，使丧失信誉；使怀疑，证实……不可信
items.def_en: 1. To damage someone's reputation so that people no longer respect or trust them. 2. To cause an idea, opinion, or report to seem false or unreliable.
items.ex_en: The shocking revelation served to utterly discredit the senator's long-standing claims of financial integrity.
items.ex_zh: 这一令人震惊的真相彻底败坏了那位参议员一直自诩廉洁的声誉。

items.def_zh: 给……带来耻辱，使蒙受污名，污名化
items.def_en: To treat or label someone or something unfairly as shameful, disgraced, or worthy of severe disapproval.
items.ex_en: Society often stigmatizes individuals who openly seek clinical help for severe mental illnesses.
items.ex_zh: 社会往往会对那些为严重心理疾病公开寻求临床治疗的人施加污名。

items.def_en: to deliberately damage someone's good reputation by making false and malicious statements
items.ex_en: The malicious tabloid article deliberately defamed the actress by inventing scandalous fabricated affairs.
items.ex_zh: 该八卦小报刊发恶意文章捏造荒唐绯闻，蓄意诽谤这位女演员的名誉。

items.def_en: to speak or write about someone in an extremely abusive or harshly disparaging manner
items.ex_en: Partisan media outlets relentlessly vilified the ambassador throughout the intense international dispute.
items.ex_zh: 在整场激烈的国际争端中，党派媒体对这位大使进行了无休止的肆意诋毁。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe verbal or communicative acts aimed at damaging a person's reputation or credibility, escalating from sneering detraction to toxic public demonization.
groups.summary_zh: 通过言论由浅入深地攻击他人声誉、可信度或道德品行，从轻视非议直至恶毒污名化。
groups.desc_en: Damaging the repute, merit, or standing of a target through belittling or defamatory expression, distinct from fair critique.
groups.desc_zh: 通过贬抑性言辞或中伤手段摧毁目标的声誉与价值，区别于理性的客观批评。
groups.nuance_en: disparage: speaking slightingly of achievements or worth (efforts / achievements / abilities) · denigrate: unfairly diminishing character or vital significance (reputation / role / contributions) · defame: harming public reputation with false malicious statements (character / company / official) · discredit: destroying confidence in validity or trustworthiness (source / theory / testimony) · vilify: subjecting to vicious, abusive public smear (opponents / minority / critics)
groups.nuance_zh: disparage: 轻视贬低成就或努力的实际价值 (efforts / achievements / abilities) · denigrate: 恶意抹杀其重要性或诋毁人格 (reputation / role / contributions) · defame: 以虚妄言辞公开中伤并败坏名誉 (character / company / official) · discredit: 削弱理论或言论证据的可信度 (source / theory / testimony) · vilify: 极尽恶毒之词进行妖魔化谩骂 (opponents / minority / critics)

groups.name: Displacement & Ouster by Force · 移位与驱离 (Shoo, Dislodge, Displace)
groups.tip: 外力迫使其脱离原位

items.def_en: to make an animal or person go away by waving your hands or making a 'shoo' sound.
items.ex_en: She shooed the stray cat off the porch before entering her front door.
items.ex_zh: 走进前门前，她挥手把走廊上的流浪猫赶跑了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to forcefully or summarily eject someone from a room, institution, or position
items.ex_en: He was kicked out of the university for repeatedly cheating on exams.
items.ex_zh: 他因多次考试作弊被大学开除。

items.def_en: to use leverage to force something out of a wedged position
items.ex_en: He grabbed a rusty screwdriver to carefully pry out the stubborn nail head.
items.ex_zh: 他拿起一把生锈的螺丝刀，小心翼翼地撬出那个顽固的钉头。

items.def_zh: 迫使移位，迫使离开家园
items.def_en: to force something or someone out of its usual or proper position
items.ex_en: The catastrophic earthquake displaced thousands of vulnerable families from their devastated coastal villages.
items.ex_zh: 那场灾难性地震迫使成千上万脆弱的家庭背井离乡，离开被毁的沿海村庄。

items.def_zh: 强行移出，从固定位置挪动；驱逐，逐出
items.def_en: 1. to force or knock something out of its fixed position. 2. to force someone to leave a place or position of power.
items.ex_en: The falling boulder dislodged several large stones from the crumbling ancient stone wall.
items.ex_zh: 滚落的巨石把几块大石头从摇摇欲坠的古老石墙上撞落下来。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to compel people, animals, or rivals to depart by force or pressure
items.ex_en: Aggressive price cuts by mega-retailers are driving small shops out of business.
items.ex_zh: 大型零售商的激进降价正在将许多小店铺挤垮倒闭。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to compel someone to leave a post, office, or geographic location
items.ex_en: Aggressive boardroom politics successfully forced out the founding director after months of conflict.
items.ex_zh: 经过数月的冲突，激烈的董事会政治斗争成功将创始董事排挤出局。

items.def_zh: 驱逐，逐出（官职、职位或领土）
items.def_en: (+ from) to drive out or expel someone from a position of authority or place
items.ex_en: Rebel forces moved swiftly to oust the authoritarian military dictator from supreme power.
items.ex_zh: 叛军迅速采取行动，将这位独裁军事独裁者逐出最高权力中枢。

items.def_zh: 使落马，颠覆并剥夺其席位
items.def_en: to cause to fall from a horse or saddle; to depose from political office
items.ex_en: The surprising election results finally unseated the incumbent governor after three consecutive terms.
items.ex_zh: 出人意料的选举结果最终颠覆了这位连任三届的现任州长。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote removing an entity from a fixed resting position, vantage point, or presence, varying in manner from trivial waving gestures to forceful mechanical unseating or political/military ouster.
groups.summary_zh: 通过挥赶、外力撞击或强力干预将人或物体自固定位置移开驱逐。
groups.desc_en: Forcibly removing an entity or person from an established, entrenched, or rightful position, contrasting with voluntary departure.
groups.desc_zh: 采取外力强行将人或事物自牢固居留之地驱逐或移位，区别于自愿离去。
groups.nuance_en: oust: politically or legally expelling someone from power or office (leader / dictator / rival) · dislodge: shifting something firmly stuck or entrenched (rock / enemy / clot) · displace: forcing populations or original elements out of their native place (residents / workers / air) · drive out: compelling departure through hostile sustained force (invaders / competitors / demons) · pry out: extracting with leverage and stubborn effort (secret / nail / confession)
groups.nuance_zh: oust: 借助政治法权或竞争将人罢黜出局 (leader / dictator / rival) · dislodge: 撼动并移开卡紧、卡死或固守之物 (rock / enemy / clot) · displace: 迫使居民背井离乡或取代原位 (residents / workers / air) · drive out: 运用敌意或压倒性力量彻底驱离 (invaders / competitors / demons) · pry out: 费力撬出紧固之物或套出隐秘 (secret / nail / confession)

groups.name: Disseminate & Broadcast · 传播与散布 (Propagate, Disseminate, Circulate)
groups.tip: 将消息、言论或思想广泛散播

items.def_zh: 散布，大肆宣扬，谣传（常用于 noise abroad/about）
items.def_en: (chiefly passive, 'be noised abroad/about') To talk about or spread news, rumors, or information widely.
items.ex_en: It was noised abroad that the king was quietly assembling a vast army.
items.ex_zh: 四下都在谣传，国王正在悄悄集结一支庞大的军队。

items.def_en: make something publicly known to a large audience
items.ex_en: You really do not need to broadcast every personal grievance across social media.
items.ex_zh: 你真的没必要把所有的个人委屈都在社交媒体上大肆宣扬。
items.ex2_en: The controversial presidential interview broadcasted live to millions of viewers across continents.
items.ex2_zh: 那场备受争议的总统采访向大洲各地数百万观众进行了现场直播。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to issue, release, or publish information, statements, or news broadly
items.ex_en: The press office put out a formal statement clarifying the new environmental regulations.
items.ex_zh: 新闻办公室发布了一份正式声明，对新的环保法规做出澄清说明。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to distribute or share news or material from person to person
items.ex_en: Please pass around this internal memorandum so every team member can review it.
items.ex_zh: 请把这份内部备忘录传阅一下，以便每位团队成员都能查看。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to transmit or distribute announcements, invitations, or messages widely
items.ex_en: The department will send out formal invitations for the annual gala next Friday.
items.ex_zh: 该部门将于下周五向所有人广泛寄发年度庆典的正式邀请函。

items.def_en: pass or be passed from person to person or place to place
items.ex_en: Shocking rumors about unexpected executive resignations began to circulate widely within the firm.
items.ex_zh: 关于高管意外辞职的惊人传闻开始在公司内部广泛流传。
items.ex2_en: The central bank circulated commemorative silver coins to mark the historic centenary.
items.ex2_zh: 中央银行发行了纪念银币，以纪念这一具有历史意义的百年庆典。

items.def_zh: 传播，宣传（思想、理论或信息）；繁殖，增殖；（声、光等）传导，传播
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To spread an idea, belief, or information widely among many people. 2. (biology) To reproduce or breed plants or animals. 3. (physics) To move or transmit through a medium, as waves or light.
items.ex_en: Philosophers used academic treatises to propagate revolutionary ideals across early modern European societies.
items.ex_zh: 哲学家们通过学术论文在早期现代欧洲社会中广泛传播革命理想。
items.ex2_en: The viral infection propagated quickly throughout the crowded school during the winter.
items.ex2_zh: 冬季期间，病毒感染在拥挤的学校中迅速传播开来。

items.def_en: spread information, knowledge, or ideas widely to many people
items.ex_en: The research organization aims to disseminate critical scientific knowledge across developing agricultural regions.
items.ex_zh: 该研究机构旨在将关键的科学知识广泛传播到发展中农业地区。

items.def_en: promote or make widely known an idea, law, or cause
items.ex_en: The interim council promulgated sweeping constitutional reforms designed to safeguard basic democratic rights.
items.ex_zh: 过渡委员会颁布了全面的宪法改革法案，旨在维护基本民主权利。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the systematic distribution and broadcasting of information, doctrines, or news across a wide population.
groups.summary_zh: 广泛公开散播、宣传理念、学说或使消息四散流传。
groups.desc_en: Spreading informational, ideological, or biological matter outward to a wide, expansive audience, unlike keeping within closed confines.
groups.desc_zh: 将信息、意识形态或生物要素广泛播撒、散布给大众，区别于局限内部流转。
groups.nuance_en: disseminate: systematically distributing knowledge or findings for absorption (information / findings / ideas) · broadcast: widely announcing across airwaves or indiscriminately (news / secret / seeds) · circulate: keeping materials moving continuously through a network (rumors / memo / currency) · propagate: actively breeding, replicating, or breeding doctrine (faith / lies / plants) · noise: indiscreetly blabbing or publicizing abroad (rumor / news / fame)
groups.nuance_zh: disseminate: 系统化地散播学术知识或核心信息 (information / findings / ideas) · broadcast: 借由媒介公开播报或不加掩饰地宣扬 (news / secret / seeds) · circulate: 使文件、传闻在特定网络内循环流转 (rumors / memo / currency) · propagate: 积极使信仰、学说或物种繁殖流传 (faith / lies / plants) · noise: 大肆张扬或走漏风声传遍四方 (rumor / news / fame)

groups.name: Dissent & Challenge Arguments · 持异议与抗辩质疑 (Dissent, Challenge, Dispute)
groups.tip: 持不同政见或公开发表反驳意见

items.def_en: to openly question the authority, accuracy, or rightness of something
items.ex_en: Defense attorneys will formally challenge the admissibility of the prosecution's wiretap evidence tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师明天将对控方窃听证据的准入性正式提出质疑。

items.def_en: to formally assert that a decision, statement, or result is wrong or invalid
items.ex_en: Opposition party leaders vowed to vigorously contest the official election results in court.
items.ex_zh: 反对党领袖誓言要在法庭上对官方选举结果进行坚决抗辩。

items.def_en: [I/T] to question the truth, correctness, or legality of a statement or claim
items.ex_en: Labor representatives vehemently disputed the company's misleading assertions regarding overall workplace safety compliance.
items.ex_zh: 工会代表对该公司关于总体职场安全达标的误导性说法提出了强烈异议。

items.def_zh: 大胆反对；公开发表异议
items.def_en: (+ against sth) to publicly voice strong disagreement or protest against an injustice or policy
items.ex_en: Activists took to the streets to speak out against human rights abuses.
items.ex_zh: 活动人士走上街头，大声疾呼反对侵犯人权的行为。

items.def_en: (+ with sb/sth) to disagree strongly with and challenge a statement or stance
items.ex_en: Senior economists took issue with the administration's optimistic assumptions regarding future interest rates.
items.ex_zh: 资深经济学家对政府关于未来利率的乐观假设提出了强烈异议。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to reply insolently or challenge assertions defensively
items.ex_en: Don't answer back when your teacher is giving you advice.
items.ex_zh: 老师给你提建议时不要顶嘴。

items.def_zh: 持异议，不同意，提出反对意见
items.def_en: (+ from) To express strong disagreement with an official opinion, policy, or decision.
items.ex_en: Two appellate judges dissented from the majority ruling regarding new commercial regulations.
items.ex_zh: 两位上诉法官对关于新商业规章的多数裁决持强烈反对意见。

items.def_zh: 反驳，驳斥；证明……属虚假，驳倒
items.def_en: To prove that a statement, theory, or accusation is false or incorrect.
items.ex_en: Scientists presented compelling empirical data to conclusively refute the opposing team's outdated hypothesis.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们提出了极具说服力的实证数据，无可辩驳地驳倒了对方过时的假设。

items.def_en: (+ at/to) to express quiet disagreement, doubts, or reluctance to accept a suggestion
items.ex_en: The conservative board members demurred at the proposal to double foreign investment.
items.ex_zh: 保守派董事会成员对将对外投资额翻倍的提议提出了异议并面露迟疑。

groups.summary_en: A speaker or faction explicitly voices disagreement, questions the validity of an official stance, or presents reasoned objections against prevailing positions.
groups.summary_zh: 表达异议、对抗既定结论并就论点展开抗辩质疑。
groups.desc_en: Articulating explicit disagreement or resistance against an established claim, ruling, or prevailing view, unlike passive compliance.
groups.desc_zh: 针对既定裁决、正统论述或主流观点提出明确质疑与抗争，区别于顺从接受。
groups.nuance_en: contest: formally battling the validity of an official outcome (election / will / verdict) · challenge: questioning the legitimacy, truth, or supremacy of a position (authority / assumption / dogma) · dispute: actively quarreling over or debating the truth of a claim (facts / boundary / ownership) · dissent: withholding philosophical assent from an orthodoxy (from majority / from doctrine / views) · refute: proving an assertion decisively to be false (allegation / thesis / claim)
groups.nuance_zh: contest: 循正规程序对裁定或竞选结果提出诉讼争端 (election / will / verdict) · challenge: 对既定权威、教条或预设立场发出质询挑战 (authority / assumption / dogma) · dispute: 就事实真伪、边界权属展开激烈争辩 (facts / boundary / ownership) · dissent: 坚持异议，拒绝赞同多数或官方论调 (from majority / from doctrine / views) · refute: 列举真凭实据确凿驳倒错误论调 (allegation / thesis / claim)

groups.name: Distract & Plague · 干扰与困扰 (Disturb, Bother, Torment, Obsess)
groups.tip: 分神受扰乃至持续纠缠

items.def_en: to annoy, worry, or cause mild mental concern to someone
items.ex_en: Does the relentless sound of nearby traffic bother your concentration while studying?
items.ex_zh: 附近持续不断的车流噪音会在你学习时扰乱你的注意力吗？

items.def_zh: 分散（注意力），使分心；使困扰，使心烦意乱
items.def_en: 1. to take someone's attention away from what they are doing or thinking about 2. to confuse, disturb, or agitate someone emotionally
items.ex_en: Pop-up notifications frequently distract him from completing his important programming tasks efficiently.
items.ex_zh: 弹窗通知频繁分散他的注意力，使他无法高效完成重要的编程任务。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause persistent, nagging worry or pain to someone
items.ex_en: A persistent feeling of guilt continued to gnaw at his conscience throughout.
items.ex_zh: 一种挥之不去的内疚感始终在蚕食和折磨着他的良心。

items.def_zh: 萦绕在心头，持续困扰；（鬼魂等）出没于，常去
items.def_en: 1. to cause repeated anxiety, guilt, or sadness to someone over a long period 2. (of a ghost) to appear repeatedly in a place
items.ex_en: Terrifying memories of the near-fatal car crash continue to haunt her everyday thoughts.
items.ex_zh: 那场九死一生的车祸带来的恐怖记忆，至今仍萦绕在她每日的思绪中。

items.def_en: to preoccupy or fill the mind of someone continually to an abnormal degree
items.ex_en: Unfounded anxieties about potential future failures completely obsess his waking mind every day.
items.ex_zh: 关于未来可能失败的无端焦虑，每天都完全占据并折磨着他的心神。
items.ex2_en: Conspiracy theorists constantly obsess about secret government cabals hidden from the public.
items.ex2_zh: 阴谋论者整天痴迷于向公众隐瞒的秘密政府阴谋集团。

items.def_zh: 不断折磨，侵蚀（某人的心神或情绪）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to persistently distress or trouble someone over a long period
items.ex_en: The unresolved guilt continued to eat away at him for years.
items.ex_zh: 那份未解的内疚感多年来持续折磨着他的内心。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to cause continuous anxiety, worry, or distress to someone's mind
items.ex_en: Dire thoughts about increasing household debt began to prey heavily on his mind.
items.ex_zh: 关于家庭债务不断增加的可怕念头，开始沉重地折磨着他的心神。

items.def_en: to afflict persistently with trouble, doubts, or physical discomfort
items.ex_en: Crippling doubts about personal competence plague the talented young artist before each exhibition.
items.ex_zh: 对自身能力的极度自我怀疑，在每次画展前都会不断折磨这位才华横溢的年轻艺术家。

items.def_en: to inflict severe, relentless mental or emotional anguish upon someone
items.ex_en: Unbearable grief over losing his beloved spouse tormented the elderly widower day and night.
items.ex_zh: 痛失挚爱的极度悲伤日夜折磨着这位年迈的鳏夫，让他痛苦不堪。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers mental disturbances and cognitive disruption caused by unwanted thoughts, memories, or external stimuli. Intensity escalates from brief loss of focus ('distract') to recurrent unsettling thoughts ('haunt') and relentless mental suffering ('plague', 'torment').
groups.summary_zh: 思维受外界或心事干扰，从一时分心升至持续缠绕、痛苦折磨。
groups.desc_en: Subjecting the mind or body to persistent, unrelenting psychological or physical affliction, far exceeding minor momentary irritations.
groups.desc_zh: 对心智或肉体进行持续性、无休止的心理折磨或困扰，远甚于暂时的轻微烦恼。
groups.nuance_en: plague: continually inflicting widespread or long-term affliction (industry / conscience / injuries) · haunt: recurring unbidden in memory like a ghost (memories / thoughts / house) · obsess: monopolizing thoughts to an unhealthy, compulsive degree (fears / detail / image) · gnaw at: relentlessly eroding peace of mind from inside (conscience / doubts / guilt) · bother: mildly inconveniencing or perturbing comfort (neighbor / noise / eyes)
groups.nuance_zh: plague: 如瘟疫般长年累月困扰或折磨 (industry / conscience / injuries) · haunt: 阴魂不散地盘桓在记忆脑海中 (memories / thoughts / house) · obsess: 强迫性地彻底占据心神 (fears / detail / image) · gnaw at: 愧疚怀疑如虫咬般由内噬咬内心 (conscience / doubts / guilt) · bother: 产生轻度烦扰或生理不适 (neighbor / noise / eyes)

groups.name: Draft & Sketch · 起草与构拟 (Draft, Sketch, Outline)
groups.tip: 拟定草案草拟初步蓝图

items.def_zh: 起草，拟订；草绘，绘制；征召入伍；选拔
items.def_en: 1. To write the preliminary version of a document, speech, or plan. 2. To draw or design a preliminary sketch. 3. To recruit someone for compulsory military service or professional sports.
items.ex_en: The legal team worked through the night to draft a comprehensive settlement contract.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队彻夜工作，拟定了一份内容详尽的和解协议草案。

items.def_en: to give the main facts, points, or general structure of a project or document
items.ex_en: The project manager clearly outlined the primary objectives for the upcoming quarterly campaign.
items.ex_zh: 项目经理清晰地概述了即将开展的季度营销活动的主要目标。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ out) to make a quick, rough drawing or outline of something without full details
items.ex_en: She sketched the old wooden bridge on rough parchment paper using charcoal pencils.
items.ex_zh: 她用炭笔在粗糙的羊皮纸上勾勒出了那座古老木桥的轮廓。

items.def_en: to sketch, mark, or plan something out in rough, general form
items.ex_en: We must block out our strategic priorities before organizing the individual project schedules.
items.ex_zh: 在安排具体的项目进度之前，我们必须大致规划出战略优先事项。

items.def_en: to prepare and write out a formal document, contract, or plan
items.ex_en: The legal team drew up a comprehensive contract for the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队为此次收购拟定了一份详尽的合同。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to produce a preliminary design, outline, or draft of something without detailing
items.ex_en: The lead architect roughed out an initial floorplan during our lunch meeting yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 首席建筑师在昨天午餐会期间勾画出了一份初步的平面图轮廓。

items.def_zh: 简要勾画，概述（轮廓或计划）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to give a brief or general description or preliminary drawing of something
items.ex_en: The director sketched out the upcoming scene to help the confused actors understand.
items.ex_zh: 导演简要概述了下一场戏的构想，以帮助困惑的演员们理解。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to plan or arrange the details of something thoroughly in advance
items.ex_en: The committee met to map out a clear strategy for the next five years.
items.ex_zh: 委员会开会为接下来的五年详细制定了清晰的战略规划。

items.def_en: (chiefly British English spelling of draft) 1. To write a preliminary version of a document, contract, or plan. 2. To draw or sketch a plan or design.
items.ex_en: The junior solicitor was instructed to draught the intricate land conveyance agreement properly.
items.ex_zh: 初级事务律师受命妥善起草那份复杂的土地转让协议。

groups.summary_en: Creators compose the preliminary, non-final version of a text, design, or visual work, advancing along the workflow from rough spatial/conceptual layout ('sketch', 'outline') to formulated working versions ('draft', 'block out').
groups.summary_zh: 制作文本、规划或艺术品的初期雏形，涵盖构想提纲、粗略勾勒直至写出初稿。
groups.desc_en: Constructing the preliminary, structural schema of a text, plan, or visual design before full rendering, contrasting with final polishing.
groups.desc_zh: 在全面落笔成型前搭建文本、构想或形体雏形，区别于成稿后的精雕细琢。
groups.nuance_en: draft: formulating the first structured written version of a formal document (bill / contract / speech) · sketch: rapidly capturing the visual outlines or fundamental traits (drawing / character / scene) · outline: enumerating the logical hierarchy or main points (argument / chapters / policy) · draw up: formally drafting and compiling legal or bureaucratic pacts (treaty / guidelines / list) · map out: strategically planning every phase of a future path (route / career / strategy)
groups.nuance_zh: draft: 起草正式文稿的第一版框架 (bill / contract / speech) · sketch: 快速勾勒视觉轮廓或速写要点 (drawing / character / scene) · outline: 列出逻辑提纲与结构纲要 (argument / chapters / policy) · draw up: 拟定并编纂正规法律文件或规章 (treaty / guidelines / list) · map out: 周全规划后续各阶段路线演进 (route / career / strategy)

groups.name: Drain & Exhaust · 排空与耗尽 (Deplete, Drain, Exhaust)
groups.tip: 资源或液体逐渐流失直至枯竭

items.def_zh: 倒空，排空（容器中的物品或液体）
items.def_en: [I/T] to remove the contents of a container so that nothing is left inside
items.ex_en: He completely emptied the heavy wooden crate before carrying it down the stairs.
items.ex_zh: 在把沉重的木箱搬下楼梯之前，他把里面的东西全倒空了。
items.ex2_en: The crowded theater emptied rapidly once the final film credits began rolling.
items.ex2_zh: 片尾字幕一开始滚动，拥挤的电影院很快就空了。

items.def_zh: 耗尽（电量或能量）；使减弱
items.def_en: to lose power or gradually deplete resources, or to cause something to do so
items.ex_en: My phone battery tends to run down extremely fast in cold weather environments.
items.ex_zh: 在严寒的天气环境下，我的手机电量往往耗尽得极快。

items.def_zh: 使排干，抽光；（液体）流尽，排空；耗尽，使精疲力竭
items.def_en: 1. To make liquid flow away from something, or to empty of liquid. 2. To completely use up someone's energy, time, or resources.
items.ex_en: Endless administrative arguments gradually drained all of her creative energy this past week.
items.ex_zh: 过去这周，没完没了的行政争执渐渐耗尽了她所有的创作精力。
items.ex2_en: The bathtub water drained slowly through the hair-clogged metal pipe in minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 浴缸里的水几分钟内通过被毛发堵塞的金属管道缓缓排空了。

items.def_zh: 削弱，暗中逐渐消耗（精力、信心）
items.def_en: to gradually weaken or destroy someone's strength, vitality, or confidence
items.ex_en: Prolonged illness and chronic pain slowly sapped his determination to finish the race.
items.ex_zh: 长期的病痛和慢性折磨逐渐消耗掉了他跑完比赛的坚强决心。

items.def_zh: 大量削减，消耗（资源、储备）
items.def_en: to reduce the amount or supply of something considerably
items.ex_en: Intensive agricultural cultivation without fallow periods can rapidly deplete vital soil nutrients over time.
items.ex_zh: 缺乏休耕的集约化农业耕作随着时间推移会迅速消耗土壤中的关键养分。

items.def_en: to completely exhaust physical or mental energy through prolonged overwork or stress
items.ex_en: Working eighty hours weekly without vacations will eventually burn out any dedicated employee.
items.ex_zh: 每周工作八十个小时且不休假，最终会把任何敬业的员工都彻底累垮。

items.def_en: to consume the whole of an available resource until none remains
items.ex_en: We used up all the flour baking cookies this morning.
items.ex_zh: 今天早上烤饼干把我们所有的面粉都用光了。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to exhaust all the financial or material resources of someone or something
items.ex_en: The corrupt financial advisor completely bled dry the trust funds of vulnerable clients.
items.ex_zh: 那位贪腐的财务顾问彻底榨干了弱势客户信托基金中的所有资金。

items.def_zh: 耗尽，用光；使筋疲力尽；详尽探讨
items.def_en: 1. To use up a supply of something completely. 2. To make someone extremely tired or weary. 3. To discuss or treat a subject thoroughly.
items.ex_en: The marathon trek across the mountainous desert terrain exhausted their remaining water rations completely.
items.ex_zh: 穿越多山沙漠地区的漫长跋涉彻底消耗掉了他们仅存的水源配给。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the progressive or total withdrawal of liquid, energy, or resources until nothing useful remains, arranged from gradual emptying to complete depletion.
groups.summary_zh: 指逐步抽空液体或消耗体力、精力与资源，直至完全见底或枯竭的过程。
groups.desc_en: Progressively emptying or drawing off vital reserves until nothing of value remains, unlike momentary, non-exhaustive consumption.
groups.desc_zh: 持续抽干储备资源或生命活力直至枯竭，区别于非消耗性或暂时的使用。
groups.nuance_en: drain: drawing off liquid, wealth, or energy steadily to an empty state (resources / swamp / battery) · sap: gradually undermining and eating away strength or vitality (energy / confidence / strength) · deplete: severely reducing the quantitative volume of available stocks (supplies / ozone / reserves) · bleed dry: extortionately or ruthlessly extracting all financial lifeblood (coffers / victim / company) · exhaust: using up an entire fund of strength or possibility (patience / fuel / options)
groups.nuance_zh: drain: 持续排干资金、能量或液体至见底 (resources / swamp / battery) · sap: 如暗中掘根般逐步暗损生机体力 (energy / confidence / strength) · deplete: 大幅削减物资库存或可用量 (supplies / ozone / reserves) · bleed dry: 榨干搜刮一切资财与生机 (coffers / victim / company) · exhaust: 用尽全部力气、耐心或可能性 (patience / fuel / options)

groups.name: Drink & Sip · 慢品与啜饮方式 (Sip, Slurp, Savor)
groups.tip: 啜饮吸吮带有声响地喝

items.def_en: [I/T] to drink by taking just a small mouthful at a time
items.ex_en: She sat comfortably by the warm fire and sipped her steaming herbal tea.
items.ex_zh: 她惬意地坐在温暖的炉火旁，小口啜饮着热气腾腾的花草茶。

items.def_zh: 饮红葡萄酒（尤指波尔多红葡萄酒）
items.def_en: 1. (dated) To drink claret (red Bordeaux wine).
items.ex_en: The wealthy aristocrats clareted abundantly late into the night at their grand manor.
items.ex_zh: 富有的贵族们在豪华庄园里尽情畅饮红葡萄酒，直至深夜。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to swallow all of a liquid drink in continuous gulps
items.ex_en: Thirsty after his workout, he drank down the large glass of iced water.
items.ex_zh: 锻炼后口渴难耐，他端起那大杯冰水一饮而尽。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to swallow an alcoholic drink rapidly and effortlessly
items.ex_en: After finishing his stressful shift, he knocked back two shots of cheap whiskey.
items.ex_zh: 结束了压力巨大的一班工作后，他痛饮了两小杯廉价威士忌。

items.def_en: [I/T] to draw liquid into the mouth by creating suction with the lips and tongue
items.ex_en: The child sucked the delicious sweet syrup noisily through a bright plastic straw.
items.ex_zh: 那个孩子用一根鲜艳的塑料吸管大声吸吮着美味甜腻的糖浆。

items.def_zh: 出声地喝，咕嘟咕嘟地喝；出声地吃
items.def_en: 1. To drink or eat something noisily with a sucking sound.
items.ex_en: He casually slurped his hot chicken noodle soup despite the quiet library surroundings.
items.ex_zh: 尽管图书馆周围很安静，他还是吧唧吧唧地大声喝着热鸡汤面。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to drink an alcoholic beverage quickly in one or a few gulps
items.ex_en: Before heading out onto the dance floor, she quickly tossed back a tequila.
items.ex_zh: 在走向舞池之前，她一仰脖子迅速喝光了一杯龙舌兰酒。

items.def_en: to drink an alcoholic beverage heartily and with relish
items.ex_en: The boisterous sailors quaffed frothy ale and sang cheerful sea shanties all night.
items.ex_zh: 喧闹的水手们畅饮着泡沫翻滚的麦芽酒，整夜唱着欢快的船夫号子。

items.def_en: [I/T] to drink deeply or in large gulps directly from a container
items.ex_en: He paused beside the trail to swig cold water from his metal canteen.
items.ex_zh: 他在小道旁停下脚步，仰头痛饮了一大口铁水壶里的凉水。

groups.summary_en: An agent consumes liquid orally according to specific acoustic manners, rates of intake, or sensory appreciation.
groups.summary_zh: 通过啜饮、出声吮吸或细细品尝来饮用液体。
groups.desc_en: Consuming liquid beverages according to deliberate, culturally distinct micro-manners and tempos, unlike basic utilitarian hydration.
groups.desc_zh: 依特定文化场景、节奏与动作幅度饮下流质，区别于基本的机械补水。
groups.nuance_en: sip: drinking in tiny, delicate taste-conscious amounts (tea / wine / coffee) · slurp: drinking loudly with an audible sucking sound (noodles / soup / tea) · knock back: rapidly downing an alcoholic shot in a single gulp (shot / beer / whiskey) · quaff: enthusiastically drinking large copious drafts with relish (ale / wine / cider) · suck: drawing liquid into the mouth through a narrow opening or straw (juice / thumb / straw)
groups.nuance_zh: sip: 极小口地啜饮品味 (tea / wine / coffee) · slurp: 呼噜呼噜作响地吸食汤水 (noodles / soup / tea) · knock back: 豪爽一仰脖干掉烈酒 (shot / beer / whiskey) · quaff: 痛饮畅酌大口麦酒 (ale / wine / cider) · suck: 藉吸管或窄口用力吮吸 (juice / thumb / straw)

groups.name: Dull & Attenuate · 钝化与减退 (Blunt, Shallow, Dull)
groups.tip: 程度变浅或威力减退

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce or moderate the level, intensity, or aggressiveness of something
items.ex_en: The aggressive politician was firmly advised to dial back his inflammatory campaign rhetoric.
items.ex_zh: 这位激进的政客被严正建议收敛并削弱其煽动性的竞选言论。

items.def_en: To become or make less deep, intense, or profound.
items.ex_en: As peace returned to the province, ancient tribal animosities finally began to shallow.
items.ex_zh: 随着和平重新降临该省，古老的部落敌意终于开始逐渐减弱淡化。
items.ex2_en: Drought conditions shallowed the wide mountain river until boats could not pass.
items.ex2_zh: 干旱使宽阔的山间河流变浅，以致船只无法通过。

items.def_zh: 变迟钝，削弱（感官或锋刃）
items.def_en: [I/T] to make or become less sharp, bright, severe, or keen
items.ex_en: Chronic fatigue and constant distractions can dull the sharpest analytical intellect over time.
items.ex_zh: 长期的疲劳和不断的干扰久而久之会削弱哪怕最敏锐的分析头脑。
items.ex2_en: The sharp surgeon's scalpel dulled gradually after hours of delicate surgical procedures.
items.ex2_zh: 经过数小时精细的手术操作后，外科医生的锋利柳叶刀逐渐变钝了。

items.def_en: to play down or deliberately make something appear less serious, severe, or intense
items.ex_en: The corporate spokesperson tried to soft-pedal the catastrophic nature of the data breach.
items.ex_zh: 企业发言人试图低调处理这次数据泄露事件的严重灾难性影响。

items.def_zh: 抑制，平息，减弱（感情、兴奋等）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to reduce the strength, intensity, or enthusiasm of an emotion or situation
items.ex_en: The government took urgent steps to damp down market panic over rising inflation.
items.ex_zh: 政府采取紧急措施，以平息市场对通胀上升的恐慌情绪。

items.def_zh: 使缓和，削弱（语气、色彩或尖锐感）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make something less intense, forceful, harsh, or bright
items.ex_en: The editor advised the young journalist to tone down his aggressive language.
items.ex_zh: 主编建议这位年轻记者缓和其咄咄逼人的语言风格。

items.def_en: 1. To make a feeling, sound, or reaction weaker or less intense. 2. To make the point or edge of something less sharp.
items.ex_en: The strong painkillers helped to blunt the sharp agony in his broken arm.
items.ex_zh: 强效止痛药有助于缓解他断臂处的剧烈锐痛。
items.ex2_en: His sharp senses blunted noticeably as advanced old age took its toll.
items.ex2_zh: 随着步入高龄，他敏锐的感官明显迟钝了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make something weaker, thinner, or less effective in force or value
items.ex_en: Thick concrete walls attenuate the radio signals passing through the modern laboratory.
items.ex_zh: 厚重的混凝土墙削弱了穿过这间现代实验室的无线电信号。
items.ex2_en: The wireless signal attenuates significantly when traveling through dense mountain forests.
items.ex2_zh: 无线信号穿过茂密的山林时会明显衰减。

items.def_en: to make a sound, physical sensation, or feeling less intense or completely numb
items.ex_en: Dense acoustic foam was installed throughout the studio to deaden unwanted background noise.
items.ex_zh: 录音室通体安装了高密度吸音泡沫，以减弱多余的背景噪音。

items.def_zh: 抑制，减弱，浇灭（热情、需求或势头）
items.def_en: To make feelings, enthusiasm, demand, or an effect less strong or intense.
items.ex_en: Rising borrowing costs have begun to dampen consumer demand across the housing market.
items.ex_zh: 不断上升的借贷成本已开始抑制整个房地产市场的消费需求。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to reducing the sharpness, depth, intensity, or acute quality of physical edges, feelings, senses, or arguments. The agent or process blunts a tip or diminishes the vividness or profoundness of an effect.
groups.summary_zh: 使锋芒、深度、感觉或效果变得迟钝浅薄。
groups.desc_en: Reducing the sharpness, intensity, or aggressive force of a sensory stimulus, emotion, or impact, contrasting with sudden extinction.
groups.desc_zh: 削减刺激、情绪、冲击力或锋刃的锐度与强度，区别于骤然彻底熄灭。
groups.nuance_en: blunt: deadening a sharp physical edge or dulling the force of an impact (knife / impact / criticism) · dull: eroding the vividness, pain, or intellectual keenness (pain / senses / sheen) · tone down: deliberately softening inflammatory language or brazen colors (rhetoric / colors / language) · damp down: suppressing or smothering rising emotional or physical flames (fires / speculation / excitement) · attenuate: progressively thinning down the strength or density of a signal (signal / effect / virus)
groups.nuance_zh: blunt: 磨钝锋刃或削弱撞击抨击的杀伤力 (knife / impact / criticism) · dull: 使光泽、感官知觉或隐痛变得迟钝麻木 (pain / senses / sheen) · tone down: 主动收敛言辞锋芒或淡化刺眼色调 (rhetoric / colors / language) · damp down: 压制或浇灭蠢动的舆情、火苗或亢奋 (fires / speculation / excitement) · attenuate: 逐渐减弱稀释波形信号或效价 (signal / effect / virus)

groups.name: Dynamic Leaping & Bouncing · 腾跃与跳跃 (Leap, Spring, Bounce)
groups.tip: 弹性蓄力腾空而起

items.def_en: to spring or rebound back quickly after striking a surface
items.ex_en: The rubber ball struck the stone pavement and bounced back into his hand.
items.ex_zh: 橡胶球砸在石板路上，弹回到了他的手中。

items.def_en: to move abruptly into an erect or elevated position with a springing leap
items.ex_en: The children jump up with great excitement whenever their grandfather visits them.
items.ex_zh: 每当祖父来访，孩子们总是兴奋得猛然跳起来。

items.def_zh: 上下急跳，欢跳；跳吉格舞
items.def_en: to move up and down with quick jerky motions; to dance a lively jig
items.ex_en: The lively puppet seemed to jig across the stage on thin invisible strings.
items.ex_zh: 那个活泼的木偶似乎在隐形细线的牵引下在舞台上上下欢跳。

items.def_en: to skip, hop, or leap about in a playful, lively manner
items.ex_en: Young lambs caper across the green meadow under the warm morning sun.
items.ex_zh: 温煦的晨光下，幼小的羊羔在绿意盎然的草地上雀跃嬉戏。

items.def_en: to jump or bound upward suddenly with energetic force
items.ex_en: The guard dogs leap up against the high fence whenever strangers approach.
items.ex_zh: 每当陌生人靠近时，看门狗都会霍然跳起扑向高栅栏。

items.def_en: to move suddenly and rapidly upwards or forwards from a stationary position
items.ex_en: The hidden tiger prepares to spring upon the unsuspecting deer from the bushes.
items.ex_zh: 潜伏的老虎准备从灌木丛中敏捷跃向那只毫无防备的鹿。

items.def_en: to walk or run with long, energetic, and bouncing leaping steps
items.ex_en: The excited puppies bound across the open field to greet their returning master.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的小狗大步腾跃着穿过开阔的田野，迎接归来的主人。

items.def_en: [I/T] to jump over something in a single movement, often using one's hands for support
items.ex_en: The athletic youth managed to vault the garden fence in a single motion.
items.ex_zh: 那个矫健的青年单手一撑，一跃翻过了花园的栅栏。

items.def_zh: （随摇滚乐等）狂暴跳跃冲撞，跳莫什舞
items.def_en: (informal) to dance wildly and aggressively by jumping around and crashing into others at a rock concert
items.ex_en: Hundreds of energetic fans began to mosh wildly in front of the stage.
items.ex_zh: 数百名精力充沛的乐迷开始在舞台前狂暴地推挤跳跃。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame capture energetic, spring-like vertical or propulsion movements off the ground, varying by rhythm, kinetic energy, and bodily control.
groups.summary_zh: 指脱离地面发力弹跳、腾空跃起或狂躁跳跃的运动方式。
groups.desc_en: Propelling the body into the air through dynamic leg springing, with distinct vectors and emotional flavors, unlike earthbound walking.
groups.desc_zh: 通过腿部蓄力迸发腾跃于空中，具有鲜明的动力方向与情绪色彩，区别于贴地行走。
groups.nuance_en: vault: leaping over an obstacle while propping oneself on hands or a pole (fence / horse / wall) · bound: leaping forward with long, springy, rhythmic strides (steps / strides / deer) · spring: suddenly releasing dynamic coil to leap from a crouch (trap / feet / surprise) · caper: skipping and gamboling about playfully without purpose (about / dance / joy) · bounce back: elastically rebounding from a surface or recovering from adversity (ball / market / defeat)
groups.nuance_zh: vault: 借助双手一撑或撑杆飞越屏障 (fence / horse / wall) · bound: 大步流星、轻快富有弹性地向前腾跃 (steps / strides / deer) · spring: 如弹簧般从伏地姿态突然弹起跳出 (trap / feet / surprise) · caper: 雀跃欢跳、滑稽戏耍 (about / dance / joy) · bounce back: 触地弹回或在挫折后迅速复原 (ball / market / defeat)

groups.name: Eat & Ingest · 吞咽与摄入 (Ingest, Imbibe, Swallow)
groups.tip: 体内摄取流质或固体食物

items.def_en: to eat, drink, or ingest edible matter (formal/scientific register)
items.ex_en: Adult pandas consume large quantities of fresh bamboo shoots during the spring season.
items.ex_zh: 成年大熊猫在春季会食用大量的鲜竹笋。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽地咽下；大口吞下
items.def_en: (+ sth) to swallow food or drink greedily, hastily, or in large mouthfuls
items.ex_en: He had to gulp down his hot coffee before running for the train.
items.ex_zh: 在赶火车之前，他不得不大口咽下滚烫的咖啡。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to swallow food rapidly without properly chewing it
items.ex_en: Late for work, he had to bolt down his breakfast within five minutes.
items.ex_zh: 上班要迟到了，他不得不在五分钟内囫囵吞下早餐。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to manage to swallow something unpalatable with difficulty or reluctance
items.ex_en: The sick child managed to choke down the bitter liquid medicine with difficulty.
items.ex_zh: 生病的孩子费了好大劲才勉强咽下苦涩的药水。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cause food, drink, or medicine to pass down the throat into the stomach
items.ex_en: You should swallow the antibiotic pill whole with a large glass of water.
items.ex_zh: 你应该配一大杯水将这粒抗生素药丸整颗吞下。

items.def_en: to take food, liquid, or other substance into the body by swallowing or absorbing it
items.ex_en: Certain marine organisms ingest microscopic plastic fragments drift within oceanic currents.
items.ex_zh: 某些海洋生物摄入了在洋流中漂浮的微塑料碎片。

items.def_en: [I/T] to swallow food or drink quickly and noisily in large mouthfuls
items.ex_en: Thirsty after the race, the runner took a deep gulp of cold water.
items.ex_zh: 赛后口渴难耐，这位跑步选手大口吞咽着凉水。

items.def_zh: 饮，喝（尤指酒）；吸收，汲取（知识、思想等）
items.def_en: 1. (formal or humorous) To drink something, especially alcohol. 2. To absorb or take in ideas, knowledge, or information.
items.ex_en: The guests gathered in the drawing room to imbibe fine vintage wines.
items.ex_zh: 客人们聚在客厅里，细细品饮上好的陈年佳酿。

items.def_zh: 咕嘟咕嘟大口喝；（液体倒出时）发出咕嘟声
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To drink something quickly and noisily in large gulps. 2. (of liquid) To pour or flow with a hollow gurgling sound.
items.ex_en: He tipped the bottle and began to glug the cold soda greedily.
items.ex_zh: 他倾斜瓶子，贪婪地咕嘟咕嘟大口喝起冰凉的汽水。

groups.summary_en: An organism takes food, drink, or substances into the body by swallowing, absorbing, or drinking down liquids.
groups.summary_zh: 通过口腔或生理器官摄入营养、吞咽液体或食物。
groups.desc_en: Drawing food or substances down the esophagus into the stomach, spanning ravenous wolfing to clinical intake, contrasting with plain chewing.
groups.desc_zh: 将固体或液体经食道吞咽送入体内，涵盖狼吞虎咽至医学摄入，区别于纯粹咀嚼。
groups.nuance_en: swallow: executing the physiological muscular action of clearing the throat (pill / pride / food) · bolt down: eating greedily and hurriedly without chewing (meal / lunch / burger) · gulp down: swallowing large gulps of drink or food voraciously (water / coffee / panic) · ingest: introducing material into the digestive tract in biological contexts (toxins / food / particles) · choke down: swallowing unpalatable food or bitter feelings with physical difficulty (medicine / tears / food)
groups.nuance_zh: swallow: 完成喉部肌肉的吞咽动作或忍气吞声 (pill / pride / food) · bolt down: 未经细嚼便囫囵吞下饭菜 (meal / lunch / burger) · gulp down: 狼吞虎咽地大口灌咽流食 (water / coffee / panic) · ingest: 生物医学语境下的消化道摄入 (toxins / food / particles) · choke down: 艰难下咽难吃之物或强咽泪水 (medicine / tears / food)

groups.name: Edit & Elide · 删减与校订 (Emend, Elide, Expunge)
groups.tip: 对文本字句进行删节与校订

items.def_en: to edit, shorten, or alter a manuscript with an editor's corrections and deletions
items.ex_en: The strict editor chose to blue-pencil several overly sentimental paragraphs in the draft.
items.ex_zh: 严谨的编辑决定用蓝铅笔删改手稿中几段过于感伤的文字。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to draw a line through written text or errors to remove or invalidate them
items.ex_en: Please cross out the incorrect date and write the valid one beside it.
items.ex_zh: 请划掉错误的日期，并在旁边写上有效日期。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to delete or cancel words or sections from an authored draft or legal document
items.ex_en: The lawyers agreed to strike out the contested clause from the final contract.
items.ex_zh: 律师们同意从最终合同中划掉这一存争议的条款。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove a part, word, or passage from a written text, recording, or broadcast
items.ex_en: He decided to cut out caffeine completely to improve his sleep.
items.ex_zh: 为了改善睡眠，他决定彻底戒掉咖啡因。

items.def_en: (+ from) to cut out words, sentences, or paragraphs cleanly from a manuscript
items.ex_en: The author decided to excise three verbose scenes from the final draft.
items.ex_zh: 作者决定从最终手稿中删去三个冗长的场景。

items.def_zh: 隐去；涂黑屏蔽（敏感信息）
items.def_en: to obscure or remove confidential information from a published legal or official document
items.ex_en: The court ordered officials to redact personal identification numbers from the public file.
items.ex_zh: 法院命令官员隐去公开档案中的个人身份识别号码。

items.def_en: (+ from) to strike out, obliterate, or wipe clean specific text, names, or recorded entries
items.ex_en: The judge ordered the clerk to expunge the improper remark from official records.
items.ex_zh: 法官命令书记员从官方记录中抹除那句不当言论。

items.def_en: (formal) To correct or improve a text, especially a scholarly or literary work.
items.ex_en: Scholars worked diligently to emend corrupt lines in the ancient Greek manuscript.
items.ex_zh: 学者们孜孜不倦地校订古希腊手稿中讹误的诗行。

items.def_zh: 省略（元音、音节或词）；忽略，略去；合并
items.def_en: 1. To omit a sound or syllable when speaking. 2. (formal) To omit, leave out, or merge things together.
items.ex_en: Casual speakers often elide unstressed syllables when talking at a rapid pace.
items.ex_zh: 人们在日常快速交谈时，往往会略去非重读音节。

groups.summary_en: An editor, scholar, or speaker removes errors, redundant vowels/sounds, or objectionable passages from an authored text, speech, or manuscript.
groups.summary_zh: 在文本或语音中剔除错误、音节、赘句或敏感字句。
groups.desc_en: Removing or correcting portions of a text or record to conform to truth, policy, or censorship, contrasting with whole document creation.
groups.desc_zh: 剔除、修润文本或记录中的特定字句以符合真实性、法规或审查，区别于全篇创作。
groups.nuance_en: emend: scholarly correcting textual corruptions or errors (text / manuscript / passage) · redact: blacking out or editing sensitive content before publication (document / names / report) · excise: surgically cutting out an entire passage or section (scene / cancer / paragraph) · expunge: totally eradicating and wiping a stain or record from existence (record / memory / name) · strike out: drawing a pen through written words to delete them (clause / sentence / line)
groups.nuance_zh: emend: 校勘纠正古籍或手稿中的讹误文字 (text / manuscript / passage) · redact: 公开前对涉密敏感信息进行脱密涂黑或编校 (document / names / report) · excise: 如外科手术般生硬切除整段内容或镜头 (scene / cancer / paragraph) · expunge: 从档案记忆中永久抹消、注销劣迹 (record / memory / name) · strike out: 在写错的词句上划线抹除 (clause / sentence / line)

groups.name: Embrace & Caress · 拥抱与亲昵 (Enfold, Nuzzle, Cuddle)
groups.tip: 用鼻子蹭或爱抚紧拥

items.def_en: to lie, sit, or curl up closely and comfortably against another person or thing
items.ex_en: The tired twins love to cuddle up together on the soft sofa.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的双胞胎喜欢在柔软的沙发上紧紧依偎在一起。

items.def_zh: 蜷缩（身体以取暖或亲昵）
items.def_en: to draw one's body into a snug, rounded position close to someone or comfortable bedding
items.ex_en: She likes to curl up with a blanket and read mystery novels.
items.ex_zh: 她喜欢裹着毛毯蜷缩着身子读悬疑小说。

items.def_en: to settle into a warm, comfortable, and affectionate position close to someone
items.ex_en: The children snuggle up to their mother as she reads a bedtime story.
items.ex_zh: 当母亲读睡前故事时，孩子们依偎在她身旁。

items.def_en: to hold someone close in an affectionate manner, often in bed or on a couch
items.ex_en: The mother sat on the rocking chair to cuddle her crying newborn baby.
items.ex_zh: 母亲坐在摇椅上，轻柔地搂抱着哭泣的新生儿。

items.def_en: (+ against/in) to settle down warmly, comfortably, and affectionately close to someone
items.ex_en: The shy child loved to nestle against her grandmother during cold winter evenings.
items.ex_zh: 在寒冷的冬夜，这个害羞的孩子喜欢蜷靠在祖母怀里。
items.ex2_en: The mother gently nestled the sleeping baby into the soft woolen blanket.
items.ex2_zh: 母亲轻轻地把熟睡的婴儿安放在柔软的羊毛毯中。

items.def_zh: 依偎；紧贴着取暖或爱抚
items.def_en: (+ up/against) to move into a warm, comfortable position close to someone else
items.ex_en: The chilled hiker tried to snuggle deeper into the warm down sleeping bag.
items.ex_zh: 受冻的徒步者试图往温暖的羽绒睡袋里再钻紧一些。

items.def_en: To rub or press gently against someone or something with the nose or face in an affectionate way.
items.ex_en: The gentle horse lowered its head to nuzzle against the girl's shoulder.
items.ex_zh: 温顺的马低下头，亲昵地蹭着女孩的肩膀。

items.def_en: (literary) To hold someone closely in one's arms; to surround, enclose, or cover completely.
items.ex_en: Gently, the mother reached out to enfold her weeping daughter in her arms.
items.ex_zh: 母亲温柔地伸出手，将啜泣的女儿紧紧拥入怀中。

items.def_en: to hold someone tightly in one's arms or embrace
items.ex_en: He rushed forward to clasp his beloved sister in a desperate, loving embrace.
items.ex_zh: 他冲上前去，深情而紧迫地将心爱的妹妹搂在怀里。

groups.summary_en: An agent expresses tenderness, affection, or protective warmth through bodily contact such as wrapping arms around or rubbing gently against another person or animal. Nuances emphasize protective sheltering versus intimate physical snugness.
groups.summary_zh: 以环抱、偎依或轻蹭肢体表达温情、依恋或保护欲。
groups.desc_en: Denotes drawing someone or oneself into close, tender bodily contact for mutual warmth or affection, contrasting with purely physical gripping or casual touching.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过身体蜷缩或贴合提供温暖与亲昵慰藉，区别于单纯的手部握持或无情感的身体碰触。
groups.nuance_en: cuddle: hold close tenderly in one's arms (child / baby / partner) · snuggle: settle into a warm, comfortable position against someone (blanket / bed / partner) · nestle: settle snugly into a sheltered, protective spot (head / valley / hills) · nuzzle: rub gently with the nose or face (neck / shoulder / cheek) · enfold: surround and envelop completely in an embrace (arms / cloak / darkness)
groups.nuance_zh: cuddle: 臂弯中温柔地拥抱依偎 (child / baby / partner) · snuggle: 紧贴他人或被褥以求温暖舒适 (blanket / bed / partner) · nestle: 依偎于受庇护的安全舒适处 (head / valley / hills) · nuzzle: 用鼻子或脸颊轻蹭亲昵 (neck / shoulder / cheek) · enfold: 张开双臂或物体完全包裹环抱 (arms / cloak / darkness)

groups.name: Emotionally Uplifting & Inspiring · 鼓舞与振奋 (Buoy, Uplift, Galvanize)
groups.tip: 唤起精神力量重拾向上斗志

items.def_en: to fill someone with the urge or ability to do or feel something uplifting
items.ex_en: Her courage continues to inspire many young athletes to pursue their ambitious dreams.
items.ex_zh: 她的勇气继续激励着许多年轻运动员去追逐远大的梦想。

items.def_en: to make someone feel more hopeful, cheerful, or confident
items.ex_en: The sudden news of renewed financial support heartens the weary hospital staff.
items.ex_zh: 重获资金支持的突发喜讯使疲惫的医护人员备受振奋。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to elevate someone's emotional state, spirits, or optimism
items.ex_en: Her encouraging message really lifted him up when he was feeling down.
items.ex_zh: 在他情绪低落时，她鼓励的话语确实让他振作了起来。

items.def_en: to become or make someone feel significantly happier, more hopeful, and encouraged
items.ex_en: A bouquet of fresh roses was sent to cheer up the sick patient.
items.ex_zh: 一束新鲜的玫瑰被送去让生病的患者振作起来。
items.ex2_en: The despondent team cheered up immediately after hearing the encouraging news.
items.ex2_zh: 听到令人鼓舞的消息后，沮丧的队员们立刻振作了起来。

items.def_zh: 激发……的极大热情，使斗志昂扬
items.def_en: (+ sb) to fill someone with intense enthusiasm, passion, or excitement
items.ex_en: The coach's speech fired up the team before the final match.
items.ex_zh: 决赛前，教练的演讲彻底点燃了全队的斗志。

items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel happier, more hopeful, or morally and spiritually inspired. 2. To raise or lift something physically.
items.ex_en: The stirring patriotic melody served to uplift the weary spirits of the soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 这首感人肺腑的爱国旋律鼓舞了战士们疲惫的精神。

items.def_zh: 鼓励，鼓舞（buoy up）；使浮起，使漂浮
items.def_en: (also 'buoy up') To make someone feel more cheerful, confident, or optimistic.
items.ex_en: The cheerful letters from his family helped to buoy his spirits during deployment.
items.ex_zh: 家人们寄来的欢快信件在服役期间鼓舞了他的斗志。

items.def_en: to make someone feel exceptionally happy, excited, and energetic
items.ex_en: The breathtaking view from the alpine summit never failed to exhilarate mountain climbers.
items.ex_zh: 高山之巅摄人心魄的美景总能令登山者们极度振奋。

items.def_zh: 激励，激起行动；电镀（锌）；通电刺激
items.def_en: 1. (+ into) To shock or excite someone into taking rapid, energetic action. 2. To coat iron or steel with a protective layer of zinc.
items.ex_en: The unexpected crisis served to galvanize local volunteers into immediate, organized action.
items.ex_zh: 这场突如其来的危机激励当地志愿者立即采取了有组织的行动。

groups.summary_en: An external factor, speech, or sentiment elevates someone's spirits, instills hope, or suddenly electrifies people into purposeful enthusiasm and action.
groups.summary_zh: 指提振精神、化解消沉或通过激昂号召使人备受鼓舞振作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes actively raising morale, spirits, or psychological vitality, contrasting with passive comforting or plain soothing.
groups.desc_zh: 指激发活力、振奋精神或重燃希望的主动情绪提升，区别于消极被动的安抚或单纯平复情绪。
groups.nuance_en: buoy: keep spirits floating amidst hardship (spirits / confidence / hopes) · uplift: morally or spiritually elevate to a noble plane (soul / mood / community) · inspire: stimulate creative or heroic action (confidence / followers / generation) · exhilarate: thrill with intense joy or sensory rush (crowd / skier / senses) · fire up: kindle sudden, aggressive enthusiasm (crowd / team / base)
groups.nuance_zh: buoy: 在困境中支撑士气使其不致沉沦 (spirits / confidence / hopes) · uplift: 在精神或道德层面上提升感召 (soul / mood / community) · inspire: 激发创造灵感或崇高行动力 (confidence / followers / generation) · exhilarate: 赋予极度的兴奋与感官愉悦 (crowd / skier / senses) · fire up: 点燃激越狂热的斗志与干劲 (crowd / team / base)

groups.name: Empirically Measure & Quantify · 实测度量与量化测定 (Measure, Quantify, Triangulate)
groups.tip: 逐一清点或推导数据

items.def_zh: 测定出（速度、时间等数值）
items.def_en: (+ at sth) to register or record a specific time, speed, or quantitative measurement
items.ex_en: His modified sports car can clock in at incredible speeds along the track.
items.ex_zh: 他的改装跑车在赛道上测定出的最高时速惊人。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to take a precise amount of something by measuring its volume, length, or mass
items.ex_en: The chef carefully measured out the spices for the recipe.
items.ex_zh: 大厨仔细称量出食谱所需的香料。

items.def_zh: 数数，清点，计算；算入，包括；重要，有价值
items.def_en: 1. To calculate the total number of people or things, or to recite numbers in order. 2. To include someone or something, or be considered as valid. 3. To be important or have value.
items.ex_en: The cashier must count the bills carefully before locking them inside the safe.
items.ex_zh: 出纳员在将钞票锁进保险箱前必须仔细清点。

items.def_zh: 估量尺寸；评估大小规格
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to inspect or gauge the physical proportions, capacity, or dimensions of something
items.ex_en: The two boxers paced around the ring, sizing each other up.
items.ex_zh: 两位拳手在拳台上踱步，审视打量着对方。

items.def_zh: 测量，度量；有……长（或宽、重等）；衡量，估量
items.def_en: 1. To determine the size, amount, degree, or length of something using a standard unit or instrument. 2. To have a particular size, dimension, or quantity. 3. To assess or evaluate the importance, effect, or value of something.
items.ex_en: The carpenter used a wooden ruler to measure the width of the board.
items.ex_zh: 木匠用木尺测量了这块木板的宽度。

items.def_en: to measure the magnitude, amount, or physical dimensions of something using an instrument
items.ex_en: Engineers use precision instruments to gauge the internal pressure of the gas cylinder.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们使用精密仪器来测量气瓶的内部压力。

items.def_zh: 量化，以数量表示，测定……的数量
items.def_en: 1. To measure or express the amount, size, or degree of something in numbers.
items.ex_en: Economists struggled to quantify the financial damage caused by the severe coastal hurricane.
items.ex_zh: 经济学家们难以量化这场严重沿海飓风所造成的经济损失。

items.def_zh: 作三角测量；将……划分成三角形
items.def_en: 1. (surveying / navigation) To determine a location or distance by using trigonometry and measuring angles from known points. 2. To divide an area into triangles.
items.ex_en: Surveyors used three distant mountain peaks to triangulate the explorer's true position.
items.ex_zh: 测量员利用三座遥远的山峰对探险者的真实位置作三角测量。

items.def_en: to mark units of measurement on an instrument or adjust it precisely against a standard
items.ex_en: Technicians must calibrate the sensitive laboratory barometer before recording any atmospheric readings.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员在记录大气读数前必须校准这台灵敏的实验室气压计。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this cognitive frame involve applying physical standards, geometric methods, or quantitative frameworks to empirically ascertain the precise dimensions, coordinates, or magnitude of something.
groups.summary_zh: 指借助工具或几何方法测定物体的物理尺寸、空间方位或将其数值化。
groups.desc_en: Denotes determining physical dimensions, extents, or numerical limits via empirical instruments or spatial methods, contrasting with subjective guessing.
groups.desc_zh: 指借助仪器、标尺或几何方法对物理量进行实测与量化，区别于主观揣测或粗略估算。
groups.nuance_en: measure: determine physical dimensions against a standard (distance / temperature / success) · gauge: assess extent or capacity using an indicator (depth / pressure / public mood) · quantify: express qualitative phenomena as precise numbers (impact / risk / emissions) · triangulate: pinpoint an unknown location from multiple fixed bearings (position / location / sources) · size up: scrutinize and empirically evaluate dimensions or capability (opponent / situation / room)
groups.nuance_zh: measure: 对照标准尺度测定物理量或成效 (distance / temperature / success) · gauge: 利用仪表或参照物判定度数或状态 (depth / pressure / public mood) · quantify: 将定性事物转化为精确数值 (impact / risk / emissions) · triangulate: 利用多点交汇法精准测定坐标 (position / location / sources) · size up: 审视并评估其体量或实力 (opponent / situation / room)

groups.name: Enclose & Confine Animals · 围圈与圈禁 (Corral, Kennel, Coop up)
groups.tip: 将动物关入犬舍或围栏内

items.def_zh: 关入马厩，在马厩喂养（马匹）
items.def_en: To put or keep horses or livestock in a stable
items.ex_en: The ranch workers always stable the riding horses before the heavy winter snowfall.
items.ex_zh: 牧场工人们总是在冬季大雪来临之前把骑乘马匹赶入马厩。

items.def_en: (+ in/up) To shut or hold animals inside a pen or small enclosed space
items.ex_en: In winter, shepherds pen their sheep safely within the sturdy stone enclosure.
items.ex_zh: 冬天，牧羊人将羊群安全地圈禁在坚固的石围栏内。

items.def_en: To confine animals or fowl in a coop or tightly restricted space
items.ex_en: Farmers should not coop up these energetic chickens inside small dark wooden sheds.
items.ex_zh: 农户们不应该把这些好动的鸡关在昏暗狭窄的木棚里。

items.def_en: (+ sb/animal) to enclose or confine an animal or group of animals within a fenced pen or bounded area
items.ex_en: The farmer worked quickly to pen in the frightened cattle before nightfall.
items.ex_zh: 农夫在日落前迅速行动，将受惊的牛群圈入围栏中。

items.def_zh: 将（宠物、动物）关入牢笼或棚舍内锁好
items.def_en: (+ animal) to confine an animal securely inside a cage, kennel, or building and lock the door
items.ex_en: The zookeepers must lock up the dangerous predatory animals before visitors can enter.
items.ex_zh: 在游客进入之前，动物园管理员必须把凶猛的食肉动物锁好。

items.def_en: (+ animals) to gather and capture livestock into a corral or tight enclosure
items.ex_en: The weary cowboys worked through dusk to corral in the scattered stray cattle.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的牛仔们顶着暮色劳作，把分散的走失牛群围拢关进畜栏。

items.def_en: To confine or lock an animal inside a barred cage
items.ex_en: It is cruel to cage a wild bird that longs for open skies.
items.ex_zh: 将一只向往辽阔天空的野鸟关进笼子是残忍的。

items.def_zh: 关入犬舍，把（狗）养在狗窝里
items.def_en: To put, house, or keep a dog in a kennel.
items.ex_en: We had to kennel the family dog while we traveled abroad on vacation.
items.ex_zh: 当我们出国度假时，不得不把家里的狗送去犬舍寄养。

items.def_zh: 把（牲畜）赶入畜栏；围捕，集中（人群或物品）
items.def_en: 1. To gather and confine livestock in a corral. 2. To collect, gather, or enclose a group of people or things.
items.ex_en: Mounted ranchers rode swiftly across the canyon to corral the unruly wild horses.
items.ex_zh: 骑马的牧民们飞驰过峡谷，把难以驯服的野马赶入畜栏。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this agricultural and domestic frame involve gathering, enclosing, and penning up livestock, pets, or working animals into designated pens, cages, or structures. Nuances reflect the specific type of enclosure and species involved.
groups.summary_zh: 指将牲畜、宠物等动物约束或聚拢在特定围栏、窝舍或笼舍中。
groups.desc_en: Denotes restricting animals (or people, pejoratively) within cramped or purpose-built domestic enclosures, contrasting with general incarceration of criminals.
groups.desc_zh: 指将动物（或贬义指人）约束在特定围栏或逼仄空间内，区别于针对罪犯的法律拘禁。
groups.nuance_en: corral: round up and herd into an open enclosure (horses / cattle / stray voters) · pen: restrict inside a fenced or small enclosure (sheep / livestock / pigs) · coop up: confine frustratingly in cramped, restricted quarters (chickens / children / family) · kennel: lodge a dog in an individual shelter (dogs / pets / hounds) · cage: lock securely behind metal bars or wire mesh (birds / wild animals / beast)
groups.nuance_zh: corral: 驱赶并围拢进露天畜栏中 (horses / cattle / stray voters) · pen: 关入带栅栏的圈栏中约束 (sheep / livestock / pigs) · coop up: 憋闷地局限在狭窄逼仄之处 (chickens / children / family) · kennel: 将犬类收拢寄养入犬舍 (dogs / pets / hounds) · cage: 用金属笼牢固囚禁猛禽猛兽 (birds / wild animals / beast)

groups.name: Endure & Persist · 持续与维持 (Continue, Last, Persist)
groups.tip: 状态延续或持久保持

items.def_zh: 持续，维持；够用，经受得住
items.def_en: To continue to exist, happen, or remain functional for a period of time.
items.ex_en: These heavy leather boots should last for several years with proper daily care.
items.ex_zh: 如果日常保养得当，这双厚实的皮靴应该能穿好几年。

items.def_en: To keep existing, happening, or doing something without stopping, or to resume after an interruption.
