items.ex_en: Despite the heavy rain, the dedicated athletes decided to continue their outdoor practice.
items.ex_zh: 尽管下着大雨，敬业的运动员们仍决定继续他们的户外训练。
items.ex2_en: The university decided to continue its popular community lecture series next semester.
items.ex2_zh: 该大学决定在下学期继续开展其深受欢迎的社区讲座系列。

items.def_en: to stay in the same place, condition, or state without changing
items.ex_en: Despite several leadership changes, the core principles of the company remain unchanged.
items.ex_zh: 尽管经历了数次领导层变动，公司的核心原则依然保持不变。

items.def_en: to continue to happen, exist, or operate without stopping
items.ex_en: We simply cannot let this terrible noise go on any longer.
items.ex_zh: 我们绝不能再让这种可怕的噪音继续下去了。

items.def_en: to persist or continue uninterrupted over an extended period
items.ex_en: Despite facing severe financial difficulties, they decided to carry on with the project.
items.ex_zh: 尽管面临严重的财务困难，他们还是决定把项目继续做下去。

items.def_zh: 维持；坚持；维持足够时间
items.def_en: to last or remain usable, durable, or resilient against depletion or adverse pressure
items.ex_en: Our emergency food supplies should hold out until the rescue team arrives.
items.ex_zh: 我们的应急食物储备应该能撑到救援队赶来。

items.def_en: to continue to exist across a long period, especially amid hardship
items.ex_en: These ancient stone monuments have endured centuries of harsh weather and neglect.
items.ex_zh: 这些古老的石质纪念碑历经了几个世纪的恶劣天气与荒废仍得以留存。

items.def_zh: 持续存在，维持；坚持不懈，执意
items.def_en: 1. To continue to exist or occur for a long time despite opposition or difficulty. 2. To stubbornly keep doing something.
items.ex_en: Doubts regarding the viability of the proposed economic policy persist among analysts.
items.ex_zh: 分析人士对这项拟定经济政策可行性的疑虑依然存在。

items.def_en: to continue unchanged; to endure or remain lasting
items.ex_en: Her profound devotion to truth and justice shall abide throughout the ages.
items.ex_zh: 她对真理与正义的深切奉献将历久弥笃，万古长存。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe a state, process, or event remaining in existence over time, ranging from neutral uninterrupted progression (continue), span of durability (last), to stubborn continuation against obstacles (persist, endure).
groups.summary_zh: 某状态或过程在时间上不断延伸、持久存续或顶住阻碍坚持。
groups.desc_en: Denotes unbroken continuation across an expanse of time, especially in resisting depletion, wear, or adversity, contrasting with momentary staying or fleeting stillness.
groups.desc_zh: 指在时间跨度中保持不间断、不消亡，尤指经受住损耗或考验，区别于短暂停留或静止。
groups.nuance_en: last: survive or remain usable across a duration (battery / supply / marriage) · endure: withstand severe hardship or prolonged wear without breaking (pain / hardship / legacy) · persist: stubbornly continue despite opposition or decay (symptoms / doubts / inflation) · hold out: maintain resistance against overwhelming pressure (garrison / supplies / hope) · carry on: forge ahead with an activity despite disruption (tradition / work / conversation)
groups.nuance_zh: last: 维持可用或存续一定时长 (battery / supply / marriage) · endure: 经受严苛苦难或岁月磨损而坚挺不衰 (pain / hardship / legacy) · persist: 顶着阻碍、反对或消退力顽强存续 (symptoms / doubts / inflation) · hold out: 在重压或匮乏下坚守不屈 (garrison / supplies / hope) · carry on: 排除干扰继续推进日常行动 (tradition / work / conversation)

groups.name: Endure Severe Mental Anguish · 极度痛苦与煎熬 (Agonize, Anguish, Suffer)
groups.tip: 身心备受剧烈痛苦与煎熬

items.def_en: [I/T] to experience physical or severe mental pain, distress, or hardship
items.ex_en: She suffered unimaginable heartbreak after the sudden loss of her young daughter.
items.ex_zh: 在幼女骤然离世后，她承受了难以想象的悲痛心碎。

items.def_zh: 使心力交瘁；极度折磨（某人）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause severe and persistent mental anguish, guilt, or distress to someone
items.ex_en: The enthusiastic audience ate up every single joke the comedian delivered.
items.ex_zh: 热情的观众全盘接受并享受着脱口秀演员讲出的每一个笑话。

items.def_zh: 使极度悲痛；使备受煎熬
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause intense, wrenching emotional pain and anguish to someone
items.ex_en: The civil war threatens to tear the entire country apart.
items.ex_zh: 内战有让整个国家分崩离析的危险。

items.def_zh: （因极度悲痛或难过而）哽咽，情绪激动失语
items.def_en: to become overwhelmed with deep grief, sadness, or emotion so that one cannot speak easily
items.ex_en: The grieving father began to choke up as he recounted the accident.
items.ex_zh: 那位悲伤的父亲在回忆起事故经过时，喉咙开始哽咽失语。

items.def_zh: 感到极度悲痛，伤心欲绝
items.def_en: (+ over/for) to feel intense, deep sorrow or distress, especially over a bereavement
items.ex_en: The entire tight-knit community gathered to grieve for the fallen young officer.
items.ex_zh: 整个关系紧密的社区聚集在一起，为殉职的年轻警官沉痛哀悼。

items.def_en: [I/T] to express deep sorrow, regret, or mourning over an agonizing situation
items.ex_en: The displaced citizens bitterly lamented the destruction of their historic ancestral town.
items.ex_zh: 流离失所的市民们对他们历史悠久的祖传小镇惨遭毁损深感哀叹。

items.def_en: to cause someone severe mental or physical suffering; or reflexively to afflict oneself with guilt or worry
items.ex_en: Guilt over his past betrayals continued to torment him throughout his retirement.
items.ex_zh: 对自己昔日背叛行为的负罪感，在他的整个退休岁月中不断折磨着他。

items.def_zh: 感到极度痛苦，痛苦煎熬；使极度痛苦
items.def_en: To suffer extreme physical or mental pain, grief, or distress, or cause someone deep agony.
items.ex_en: She anguished in profound silence over the grim fate awaiting her people.
items.ex_zh: 面对族人即将遭遇的凄惨命运，她在无尽的沉寂中备受痛苦煎熬。
items.ex2_en: The terrible news of the tragic accident anguished the entire tight-knit community.
items.ex2_zh: 惨烈事故的噩耗让整个紧密团结的社区陷入极大痛苦。

items.def_zh: 感到极度痛苦，苦苦思索，焦虑煎熬
items.def_en: (+ over/about) To spend a long time worrying intensely or suffering extreme anxiety over a difficult problem or decision.
items.ex_en: He spent several sleepless nights agonizing over whether to accept the job.
items.ex_zh: 他连续好几天彻夜难眠，苦苦思索是否该接受那份工作。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote experiencing extreme, wrenching emotional pain or tortuous mental worry, often over a grave loss or an agonizing decision. While 'agonize' focuses on protracted internal struggle or obsessive worry, 'anguish' and 'grieve' highlight deep, visceral distress.
groups.summary_zh: 表达内心经历极度痛苦、精神折磨或揪心煎熬的心理状态。
groups.desc_en: Denotes suffering acute, tearing psychological or spiritual pain, contrasting with mild sadness or purely physical injury.
groups.desc_zh: 指内心遭受剧烈的精神撕裂、折磨或心理煎熬，区别于普通轻度悲伤或单纯肉体疼痛。
groups.nuance_en: agonize: undergo protracted, desperate mental writhing (over a decision / loss / fate) · torment: cause or suffer persistent, relentless psychic persecution (guilt / memories / jealousy) · eat up: inwardly consume someone through corroding emotion (jealousy / anxiety / grief) · grieve: experience deep, mournful sorrow over death or loss (loss / death / widow) · tear apart: violently rupture emotional equilibrium (family / heart / grief)
groups.nuance_zh: agonize: 因抉择或厄运而陷入极度痛苦的内心煎熬 (over a decision / loss / fate) · torment: 遭受持续无情的精神折磨与摧残 (guilt / memories / jealousy) · eat up: 负面情绪如毒素般从内部蚀蚀心灵 (jealousy / anxiety / grief) · grieve: 因死别或重大丧失而深切哀痛 (loss / death / widow) · tear apart: 剧烈撕裂情感平衡与心灵平静 (family / heart / grief)

groups.name: Entrust & Consign · 委托与托付
groups.tip: 将财物事务托付他人代管

items.def_en: (+ to) to place someone or something safely into another's care, trust, or keeping
items.ex_en: The court decided to commit the orphaned child to the grandmother's care.
items.ex_zh: 法院裁定将这名孤儿托付给其祖母照料。

items.def_en: (+ sth to sb) to transfer responsibility, care, or custody of someone or something to another party
items.ex_en: The departing manager will hand over control of the department next Monday.
items.ex_zh: 离任的经理将于下周一移交该部门的管辖权。

items.def_zh: 签署转让；把……正式托付/交割
items.def_en: (+ sth to sb) to legally consign or transfer ownership, rights, or care of something to another person
items.ex_en: He formally agreed to sign over the family estate to his daughter.
items.ex_zh: 他正式同意签署协议，将家族庄园的所有权转让给女儿。

items.def_en: (+ sth to sb) to entrust or give something to another person to take charge of
items.ex_en: Please pass on these confidential documents to the incoming project director immediately.
items.ex_zh: 请立即将这些机密文件转交给新任项目总监保管。

items.def_en: (+ to) to formalize the delivery of someone or something into the hands or protection of another
items.ex_en: The dying leader chose to commend his loyal followers to God's grace.
items.ex_zh: 垂危的领袖选择将他忠诚的追随者托付给上帝的恩典。

items.def_en: To give someone the responsibility for doing something, or to put something valuable in their care.
items.ex_en: The board decided to entrust the complex reorganization plan to an expert.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定将复杂的重组计划委托给一位专家负责。

items.def_en: (+ to) to entrust something valuable or precious to someone for safekeeping
items.ex_en: The elderly collector confided his rarest ancient manuscript to the museum archives.
items.ex_zh: 那位年迈的收藏家将自己最珍罕的古代手稿托付给博物馆档案馆保管。

items.def_zh: 委托托运，把……交付代销；使陷入，置于（不良境地）
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To send or deliver goods to someone, especially for sale or custody. 2. (+ to) To put someone or something into an unpleasant place, condition, or situation.
items.ex_en: The local artisan consign her handmade pottery to an upscale boutique downtown.
items.ex_zh: 这位当地手艺人把她的手工陶器交付给市中心的一家高档精品店代销。

items.def_en: (variant spelling of entrust) To make someone responsible for doing something or caring for something valuable.
items.ex_en: The sovereign did intrust the sacred crown jewels unto the loyal duke.
items.ex_zh: 君主将神圣的王冠珠宝托付给了那位忠诚的公爵。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe handing over a valuable possession, delicate duty, or person to someone else's care or authority, relying on their responsibility. 'Entrust' highlights mutual trust and responsibility, whereas 'consign' often implies surrendering custody or transferring to a final, sometimes undesirable state.
groups.summary_zh: 强调将要事、重物或责任交予他人保管、照管或处置。
groups.desc_en: Denotes relinquishing control or care of something valuable to another party under trust, mandate, or permanent transfer, contrasting with casual lending or forceful handing over.
groups.desc_zh: 指基于信托、法定义务或终极处理将贵重人事物移交给受托方，区别于随意借出或强迫转交。
groups.nuance_en: entrust: place something precious into another's responsible care (child / task / future) · commit: deliver formally into custody or a repository (body to the earth / memory / patient) · consign: deliver over to an unwelcome fate, storage, or commercial agent (goods / manuscript to the flames / fate) · confide: impart a secret or cherishable reliance in private trust (secrets / worries / hopes) · commend: formally recommend or commit into safe keeping (spirit to God / work / soul)
groups.nuance_zh: entrust: 将重托或心爱之人托付给可信之人 (child / task / future) · commit: 正式将对象交付归宿、收治机构或遗忘中 (body to the earth / memory / patient) · consign: 移交保管、寄售或打入不良终局 (goods / manuscript to the flames / fate) · confide: 信任地倾吐秘密或寄托隐秘心事 (secrets / worries / hopes) · commend: 郑重保荐或将灵魂托付予神圣庇护 (spirit to God / work / soul)

groups.name: Enumerate & Assess Commercial Price · 计点数额与核定价格 (Count, Score, Price)
groups.tip: 数值清点得分与费用核算场景

items.def_zh: 数，清点；总计，共计；给……编号；把……归类为
items.def_en: 1. To count or determine the number of. 2. To amount to a particular number in total. 3. To give a number to each item in a series.
items.ex_en: The rare bird species currently numbers fewer than fifty individuals in captivity.
items.ex_zh: 这种稀有鸟类目前在圈养环境下的总数不足五十只。

items.def_zh: 价钱为，需花费；使付出（代价），使失去；估算……的成本
items.def_en: 1. To have a specified price or need a specific amount of money to buy. 2. To cause someone to lose or sacrifice something. 3. To estimate the price or production cost of something.
items.ex_en: This luxury imported car will cost you an absolute fortune in maintenance.
items.ex_zh: 买这辆豪华进口车光是后期保养就会花费你一大笔钱。

items.def_zh: 给……定价，标价；询问……的价格
items.def_en: 1. To determine or mark the price of something for sale. 2. To find out or compare the price of something.
items.ex_en: The clerk will price all the new merchandise before putting it out.
items.ex_zh: 店员会在把所有新商品摆上货架前给它们标上价格。

items.def_en: to assess and decide how much monetary worth an item or asset holds
items.ex_en: The certified appraiser valued the antique diamond necklace at twenty thousand dollars.
items.ex_zh: 特许估价师将这条古董钻石项链核定价值为两万美元。

items.def_zh: 得分，进球；记分，给……打分；为……谱曲；在……上刻划
items.def_en: 1. To win or gain points, goals, or runs in a game, sport, or test. 2. To keep a record of points in a match, or assign a grade to work. 3. To write or arrange music for instruments.
items.ex_en: The star striker managed to score twice during the final championship match.
items.ex_zh: 这位明星前锋在最终的总决赛中成功打入两球。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to add up figures, items, or scores to calculate the final total
items.ex_en: Let me tot up the dinner receipts before we split the bill.
items.ex_zh: 在我们分摊账单前，让我先把晚餐收据的金额合计一下。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to calculate the total number, cost, or score by enumerating each unit
items.ex_en: The cashier began to tally up the day's sales receipts after closing.
items.ex_zh: 打烊后，收银员开始清点核对当天的销售额明细。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to increase the retail price of goods above their original cost
items.ex_en: Retailers routinely mark up prices significantly right before the major holiday rush.
items.ex_zh: 零售商通常会在重大节日采购潮前大幅抬高商品零售价。

items.def_en: [I/T] to calculate and record a running score, count, or total of items
items.ex_en: Election officials worked through the night to tally every single paper ballot.
items.ex_zh: 选举官员们通宵达旦地工作，以累计清点每一张纸质选票。
items.ex2_en: The latest sales figures tally perfectly with our projected quarterly revenue estimates.
items.ex2_zh: 最新的销售数据与我们预期的季度收入完全吻合。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scenario frame center on enumerating individual units, tracking scored tallies, or calculating and fixing the monetary charge or value assigned to goods and services.
groups.summary_zh: 指盘点记录数额、记分以及估算和拟定商品或服务的收费价格。
groups.desc_en: Denotes determining financial amounts or unit points through structured commercial calculation or pricing, contrasting with rough non-financial estimation.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过结构化的商业计核对物品进行点数算账或厘定货币价值，区别于非财务的粗略估计。
groups.nuance_en: price: assign a retail or commercial selling rate to an item (goods / ticket / stock) · cost: calculate the expenditure required to execute something (project / repairs / option) · value: appraise professional worth or monetary equity (property / company / assets) · tally up: calculate a cumulative sum or running score (votes / bill / expenses) · mark up: raise the resale price above original wholesale cost (goods / price / wholesale)
groups.nuance_zh: price: 为商品核定零售标价或商业售价 (goods / ticket / stock) · cost: 核算完成某项目所需支出的成本 (project / repairs / option) · value: 由专业视角评估资产的市场公允价值 (property / company / assets) · tally up: 逐笔累计并清点总数或比分 (votes / bill / expenses) · mark up: 在批发进价基础上加价销售 (goods / price / wholesale)

groups.name: Equip & Outfit for Service · 装备与配备 (Equip, Outfit, Accoutre)
groups.tip: 为特定人员配备器械

items.def_en: to supply someone with all the specific clothes or equipment needed for an activity
items.ex_en: They need to kit out the team with proper winter mountaineering gear.
items.ex_zh: 他们需要为这支队伍配齐适宜的冬季登山装备。

items.def_en: (+ with) to supply a place or person with what is needed, especially fittings or equipment
items.ex_en: The institution shall furnish the research laboratory with the most advanced instruments.
items.ex_zh: 该机构应当为该研究实验室配备最先进的仪器设备。

items.def_zh: 配备；装置设备（房间、船只等）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth with sth) to supply a person, vehicle, or room with all the necessary equipment, fixtures, or fittings
items.ex_en: The laboratory was fitted out with the latest analytical instruments.
items.ex_zh: 该实验室配备了最先进的分析仪器。

items.def_en: (+ for sth) to put on specialized gear or prepare equipment in readiness for a task or operation
items.ex_en: The young soldiers had to gear up quickly for the midnight drill.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的士兵们不得不迅速配齐装备，准备参加午夜演习。

items.def_zh: 为……配备特种装备；穿戴整齐装备
items.def_en: (+ sb with sth) to dress or equip someone with specialized gear, clothes, or tools for a specific task
items.ex_en: We must rig out the field workers with heavy waterproof safety suits.
items.ex_zh: 我们必须为现场工人配备厚实的防水分体安全服。

items.def_en: to provide someone or something with the necessary equipment, clothes, or supplies for a particular purpose
items.ex_en: The charity helped outfit local rescue volunteers with protective clothing and boots.
items.ex_zh: 该慈善机构帮助为当地救援志愿者配备了防护服和长靴。

items.def_zh: 配备，装备；使具备（能力、素质等）
items.def_en: 1. to provide someone or something with the necessary tools, equipment, or items. 2. to prepare someone mentally or practically with needed skills or qualities
items.ex_en: The training course will equip new recruits with vital emergency survival skills.
items.ex_zh: 该培训课程将使新招募人员具备关键的应急生存技能。

items.def_zh: 给……装配帆具或特种装备
items.def_en: (+ out/with) to fit a boat or piece of machinery with necessary sails or gear
items.ex_en: The old fisherman spent the whole afternoon rigging the boat for squid.
items.ex_zh: 那位老渔民花了一整个下午给船只装配捕鱿专用帆具与设备。

items.def_zh: 给……穿戴特殊装备或佩饰
items.def_en: (+ in/with) to clothe or equip someone in a noticeable, military, or historical fashion
items.ex_en: The ceremonial royal guard was accoutred in gleaming polished breastplates and sabers.
items.ex_zh: 皇家仪仗队身着擦得锃亮的胸甲，佩戴着锃亮军刀，装束格外醒目。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers providing a person, group, or vessel with specialized tools, gear, supplies, or uniforms necessary for a specific task, voyage, or occupation. Differences lie in whether the focus is on functional tools, comprehensive outfitting, or ceremonial gear.
groups.summary_zh: 指为特定任务、远征或职能配齐必要的装备、服饰或工具设施。
groups.desc_en: Denotes systematically providing all necessary physical gear, tools, or furnishings needed for a specific mission or operation, contrasting with merely giving an isolated item.
groups.desc_zh: 指为执行特定任务或运行体系化提供成套工具、装备或设施，区别于零碎赠与单一物件。
groups.nuance_en: equip: supply with necessary functional tools or abilities (soldiers / kitchen / laboratory) · outfit: provide complete clothing, apparel, or field kit (expedition / team / vessel) · fit out: customize an interior or vessel with specialized equipment (ship / office / workshop) · furnish: provide living or working quarters with furniture and appliances (apartment / room / house) · kit out: thoroughly dress or supply with standardized gear (hiking team / squad / gym)
groups.nuance_zh: equip: 配备完成专业功能所必需的工具或技能 (soldiers / kitchen / laboratory) · outfit: 全套配齐远征或特殊活动所需的行头与外设 (expedition / team / vessel) · fit out: 专门针对船舱或室内进行量身改装与装配 (ship / office / workshop) · furnish: 为起居或办公场所配置成套家具陈设 (apartment / room / house) · kit out: 为团队或个人装备全套标准行装 (hiking team / squad / gym)

groups.name: Erotic Caressing & Making Out · 亲昵爱抚与接吻 (Pet, Neck, Smooch)
groups.tip: 通过接吻与抚弄表达亲昵

items.def_en: (+ to sb) to curl up closely and affectionately against another person for physical warmth or intimacy
items.ex_en: She decided to snuggle up to her boyfriend under the warm blanket.
items.ex_zh: 她决定在温暖的毛毯下紧紧依偎在男朋友身边取暖。

items.def_zh: 抚弄，抚摩；（亲昵地）抚弄爱抚；宠爱
items.def_en: 1. to touch or stroke an animal or person gently and lovingly. 2. to kiss and touch someone intimately in a sexual way.
items.ex_en: The affectionate couple sat on the secluded bench, kissing and petting intimately.
items.ex_zh: 那对恩爱的情侣坐在僻静的长凳上，亲昵地接吻抚弄着彼此。

items.def_en: (+ with) to kiss and cuddle amorously in an affectionate, often public way
items.ex_en: The newlyweds were seen canoodling affectionately in the corner of the cafe.
items.ex_zh: 有人看到这对新婚夫妇在咖啡馆的角落里亲昵地搂抱接吻。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ with) to kiss and hold someone affectionately or passionately
items.ex_en: They continued to smooch passionately under the dim streetlight after the movie.
items.ex_zh: 电影结束后，他们继续在昏暗的街灯下热情拥吻。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) to engage in casual sexual touching, petting, or kissing
items.ex_en: She caught her teenage brother fooling around with his date upstairs.
items.ex_zh: 她撞见她那十几岁的弟弟正在楼上和约会对象亲昵搞暧昧。

items.def_en: to engage in passionate kissing, embracing, and sexual petting with someone
items.ex_en: The teenage couple went behind the bleachers to make out after class.
items.ex_zh: 那对学生情侣下课后跑到看台后面激烈地接吻亲热。

items.def_en: (informal) to kiss and caress passionately.
items.ex_en: They hid in the back row of the dark theater to neck.
items.ex_zh: 他们躲在昏暗的电影院后排激情拥吻爱抚。

items.def_en: to stroke or touch someone in a loving, gentle, or sexually intimate manner
items.ex_en: He continued to gently fondle her soft hair as she fell asleep.
items.ex_zh: 在她入睡时，他继续温柔地抚摸着她柔软的秀发。

items.def_zh: 热烈接吻，搂抱接吻（英式俚语）
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ with) to kiss someone passionately for a prolonged period
items.ex_en: I saw them snogging passionately behind the crowded club after midnight.
items.ex_zh: 半夜过后，我看到他们在拥挤的俱乐部后面火热地搂抱接吻。

groups.summary_en: Describes amorous, physical intimacy between romantic partners without intercourse. 'Pet' implies intimate stroking or fondling, 'neck' specifies prolonged passionate kissing and embracing around the neck, while additions cover casual or intense kissing and snuggling.
groups.summary_zh: 情侣间接吻、拥抱、抚摩等非交垢性肢体亲昵行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes engaging in explicit physical romantic, sensual, or sexually playful caresses and kissing, contrasting with platonic or formal physical contact.
groups.desc_zh: 指具有明确浪漫与性吸引意图的情色抚摩、接吻或调情，区别于柏拉图式的温暖拥抱或礼节碰触。
groups.nuance_en: smooch: kiss and cuddle warmly and affectionately (sweetheart / lips / cheek) · neck: engage in prolonged, passionate kissing and neck-caressing (in cars / lover / partner) · make out: indulge in extended romantic kissing and heavy petting (teenagers / partner / couple) · canoodle: cuddle, kiss, and touch playfully in a cozy spot (in public / corner / lover) · fondle: caress sexually or sensually with the hands (lover / body / hair)
groups.nuance_zh: smooch: 热情依偎并发出响声地亲吻 (sweetheart / lips / cheek) · neck: 长时间热吻并抚弄颈项部位 (in cars / lover / partner) · make out: 包含激烈深吻与深入爱抚的亲热 (teenagers / partner / couple) · canoodle: 在私密角落亲昵调情抚爱 (in public / corner / lover) · fondle: 带着性欲或感官快感抚弄躯体 (lover / body / hair)

groups.name: Evacuation & Departure · 离开与腾出 (Exit, Vacate, Clear out)
groups.tip: 离开原处腾出空间或退场

items.def_en: (formal) to leave or abandon a place, tenancy, or property
items.ex_en: The tenant was legally required to quit the premises before the month ended.
items.ex_zh: 租户被依法要求在月底之前搬离并腾退该物业。

items.def_zh: 离开，走出去，退出；（戏剧）退场
items.def_en: 1. to go out of or leave a place, building, or vehicle. 2. to leave the stage (used as a stage direction). 3. to stop using a computer program.
items.ex_en: Passengers must remain seated until the aircraft comes to a complete halt.
items.ex_zh: 在飞机完全停稳之前，乘客切勿离开座位走向出口。

items.def_en: to leave a place completely and take one's belongings away
items.ex_en: The furious landlord ordered the rowdy tenants to clear out immediately.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的房东命令那些吵闹的房客立刻带上东西彻底搬走。

items.def_zh: 迁出；搬离（住所或办公地）
items.def_en: (+ of sth) to permanently stop living in or occupying a house, room, or building and remove one's belongings
items.ex_en: His landlord gave him thirty days to move out.
items.ex_zh: 房东限他三十天之内搬走。

items.def_en: to retreat rapidly or evacuate an area urgently when under danger or threat
items.ex_en: When artillery shells began landing nearby, the troops had to bug out.
items.ex_zh: 当炮弹开始在附近爆炸时，部队不得不紧急仓促撤退。

items.def_zh: 撤出；撤离（人员、军队或驻地）
items.def_en: (+ of sth) to withdraw or evacuate people or military forces from an area or premise
items.ex_en: The multinational corporation decided to pull out of the unprofitable market.
items.ex_zh: 该跨国公司决定退出这一无利可图的市场。

items.def_en: [I/T] to leave or remove people from a dangerous place to a safer location
items.ex_en: Authorities ordered coastal residents to evacuate the area ahead of the hurricane.
items.ex_zh: 当局在飓风来临之前命令沿海居民从危险区紧急疏散。

items.def_zh: 腾出，空出（房间、住所等）；辞去，离任（职位）
items.def_en: 1. to leave a building, room, or seat so that it becomes empty and available for someone else. 2. to leave a job or position so that it is vacant.
items.ex_en: All departing guests must vacate their hotel rooms by eleven in the morning.
items.ex_zh: 所有离店的宾客必须在上午十一点前腾空并离开酒店客房。

items.def_en: to leave suddenly or secretly, typically shifting location with one's possessions
items.ex_en: The indebted swindler quietly decamped from the hotel before the bill arrived.
items.ex_zh: 负债累累的骗子在账单送达之前悄悄拔营潜逃出了酒店。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scenario frame describe departing from, clearing out of, or relinquishing physical spaces, rooms, or properties. They range from neutral everyday exits to formal legal surrender of premises or urgent evacuation.
groups.summary_zh: 主动离开、腾退居所或因租约、安全原因撤离建筑物与场地。
groups.desc_en: Denotes leaving a geographical area or premises empty by withdrawing people or belongings, especially in a systematic or urgent manner, contrasting with casually walking away.
groups.desc_zh: 指系统性、紧迫性地从某地撤离人员或清空财物以腾出空间，区别于随意的离开或单人走开。
groups.nuance_en: evacuate: systematically withdraw personnel from danger or disaster (civilians / city / wounded) · vacate: formally leave a room or property completely unoccupied (premises / room / seat) · clear out: abruptly pack up and abandon an area or room (closet / apartment / squatters) · pull out: withdraw an organized force or commitment from an area (troops / investors / fleet) · bug out: make a hasty, panicked retreat under threat (soldiers / camp / personnel)
groups.nuance_zh: evacuate: 因灾难或威胁系统化撤离人员 (civilians / city / wounded) · vacate: 法定或正式搬离以腾出空房、席位 (premises / room / seat) · clear out: 迅速清空杂物或驱逐占用者腾空场地 (closet / apartment / squatters) · pull out: 组织化力量或资金成体系撤离 (troops / investors / fleet) · bug out: 临危慌乱、紧急拔营溃退 (soldiers / camp / personnel)

groups.name: Evade & Circumvent · 规避与规拒 (Shun, Circumvent, Bypass)
groups.tip: 刻意回避人际或规避冲突

items.def_en: (+ sth) To successfully avoid dealing with a rule, restriction, or difficulty by finding an indirect way
items.ex_en: The clever accountant found a legal loophole to get around the new tax.
items.ex_zh: 这位精明的会计找到了一个法律漏洞，巧妙规避了新税种。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) To deliberately avoid a person, place, or situation that could cause problems
items.ex_en: Prudent investors should steer clear of highly speculative and unregulated crypto markets.
items.ex_zh: 谨慎的投资者应当刻意避开投机性强且缺乏监管的加密货币市场。

items.def_en: to pass around the edge of something or avoid addressing a sensitive topic directly
items.ex_en: The diplomatic spokesman carefully skirted the awkward question about rising nuclear tensions.
items.ex_zh: 发言人小心翼翼地绕开了关于核局势日益紧张的尴尬问题。

items.def_en: to avoid an obstacle, standard channel, or bureaucratic procedure by taking an alternative route
items.ex_en: The team decided to bypass cumbersome bureaucratic channels to expedite the urgent relief.
items.ex_zh: 该团队决定绕过繁琐的官僚程序以加快紧急救援进程。

items.def_en: to avoid dealing with an issue or question in an evasive manner
items.ex_en: The candidate skillfully sidestepped the thorny issue regarding higher corporate tax rates.
items.ex_zh: 该候选人巧妙地回避了关于提高企业所得税税率的棘手议题。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To avoid doing something you should do by using clever excuses or deceit
items.ex_en: He always manages to wriggle out of doing the weekly household chores.
items.ex_zh: 他总是能耍花招找借口逃避做每周例行的家务杂活。

items.def_zh: 规避，巧妙避开（规则、限制等）；绕行
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To find a clever or indirect way around a rule, obstacle, or restriction. 2. To bypass or go around.
items.ex_en: Large multinational corporations often structure their operations to circumvent burdensome domestic regulations.
items.ex_zh: 跨国大企业往往通过调整运营架构来巧妙规避繁苛的国内法规。

items.def_en: (formal) to deliberately avoid or abstain from something on principle or habit
items.ex_en: A true ascetic chooses to eschew all worldly luxuries and sensual desires.
items.ex_zh: 真正的苦行僧会基于戒律刻意摈绝一切尘世奢华与感官欲望。

items.def_en: 1. To deliberately avoid someone or something out of dislike, fear, or moral disapproval.
items.ex_en: After the scandal, former associates began to deliberately shun him in public.
items.ex_zh: 丑闻爆发后，昔日的生意伙伴们开始在公众场合刻意回避冷落他。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express deliberately steering clear of social contact, rules, moral duties, or legal constraints through active avoidance, clever maneuvering, or social ostracism.
groups.summary_zh: 通过巧妙钻营或刻意回避，绕过法规约束、义务或社交对象。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately dodging an obstacle, obligation, or controversial topic by maneuver or avoidance, contrasting with confronting it head-on.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过技巧、策略或回避动作绕开障碍、义务或敏感议题，区别于迎头正视或直接对抗。
groups.nuance_en: circumvent: cleverly find a loophole to bypass legal or structural hurdles (regulations / sanctions / system) · bypass: go around an obstacle entirely via an alternative route (procedure / blockage / town) · sidestep: dodge an awkward issue or question by lateral deflection (question / issue / problem) · steer clear of: prudently keep a safe distance from hazards (scandal / traps / trouble) · eschew: deliberately abstain from or shun on principle (violence / publicity / meat)
groups.nuance_zh: circumvent: 巧妙钻空子规避法律、禁令或制度障碍 (regulations / sanctions / system) · bypass: 另辟蹊径绕过瓶颈、正规程序或堵塞点 (procedure / blockage / town) · sidestep: 灵巧向侧方避让敏感棘手的质疑 (question / issue / problem) · steer clear of: 审慎地与危险、丑闻保持安全距离 (scandal / traps / trouble) · eschew: 基于道德原则或戒律主动戒绝、避开 (violence / publicity / meat)

groups.name: Evade Truth & Gloss Over · 遮掩软化与含糊其辞 (Sugarcoat, Equivocate)
groups.tip: 闪烁其词含糊推诿以规避正面回答

items.def_en: to treat an unpleasant fact or fault lightly or evasively to minimize attention to it
items.ex_en: The corporate report attempted to gloss over the catastrophic losses of last quarter.
items.ex_zh: 该企业报告企图对上一季度出现的灾难性亏损轻描淡写地掩盖过去。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To make problems, disagreements, or mistakes seem less serious than they really are
items.ex_en: The manager tried to smooth over the dispute between the two senior engineers.
items.ex_zh: 经理试图息事宁人，调解两位高级工程师之间的争执。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To discuss a topic vaguely or obliquely instead of addressing the core issue directly
items.ex_en: Instead of answering my question, the spokesperson continued to talk around the issue.
items.ex_zh: 发言人没有回答我的问题，而是一直在实质问题上绕弯子。

items.def_zh: 套话防卫，含糊其词防担责
items.def_en: to avoid giving a direct answer or committing oneself by using qualifying language
items.ex_en: The politician began to hedge when reporters pressed him about future tax increases.
items.ex_zh: 当记者追问未来的增税计划时，那位政客开始含糊其词以防担责。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To hide or conceal unpleasant facts, mistakes, or illegal activities from public view
items.ex_en: The administration attempted to cover up the environmental scandal before the upcoming election.
items.ex_zh: 该届政府企图在即将举行的大选前掩盖这起环境丑闻。

items.def_zh: 粉饰，美化（使更易接受）；给……裹上糖衣
items.def_en: 1. To make unpleasant news, facts, or criticism seem more appealing or acceptable than they really are. 2. To coat pills or food with sugar.
items.ex_en: There is no point trying to sugarcoat the bad news for the investors.
items.ex_zh: 向投资者粉饰这则坏消息毫无意义。

items.raw_cluster: 模棱两可与推诿 Prevaricate & Equivocate
items.def_zh: 含糊其辞，闪烁其词，支支吾吾
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To speak deliberately in an ambiguous or evasive way to avoid telling the full truth or committing oneself.
items.ex_en: The witness continued to equivocate under oath, frustrating both the judge and prosecutors.
items.ex_zh: 该证人在宣誓后仍闪烁其词，令法官和检察官都十分恼火。

items.def_en: to deliberately conceal misconduct, defects, or scandals to make things appear acceptable
items.ex_en: The inquiry was dismissed by critics as an attempt to whitewash corporate negligence.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士斥责这起调查不过是企图粉饰企业疏忽的掩口之举。

items.def_en: to avoid telling the truth by speaking evasively or shifting the subject
items.ex_en: He chose to prevaricate rather than admit that his department made a mistake.
items.ex_zh: 他选择支吾搪塞，而不愿承认自己的部门犯了错误。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame emphasize the rhetorical manner of avoiding the harsh or plain truth, either by softening unpalatable realities or speaking ambiguously to dodge commitment.
groups.summary_zh: 修饰粉饰不快现实，或含糊其辞以逃避真相。
groups.desc_en: Denotes obscuring unpleasant truths or controversial faults by using euphemisms, evasive language, or superficial cover-ups, contrasting with outright denial or honest transparency.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过委婉修辞、模糊其辞或表面粉饰掩盖令人不悦的真相与过失，区别于全盘否认或公开透明。
groups.nuance_en: gloss over: treat serious defects or faults superficially to minimize them (flaws / mistakes / problem) · sugarcoat: make a harsh, bitter reality seem palatable (bad news / pills / criticism) · whitewash: cover up crimes or gross wrongdoing with a deceptive veneer (scandal / report / atrocities) · equivocate: use ambiguous language intentionally to conceal the truth (politician / responses / witness) · hedge: qualify statements cautiously to avoid committing oneself (bets / statements / answer)
groups.nuance_zh: gloss over: 浮光掠影带过严重缺点以大事化小 (flaws / mistakes / problem) · sugarcoat: 用甜蜜外包装饰刺耳真相或坏消息 (bad news / pills / criticism) · whitewash: 出于政治或公关目的掩盖罪行与丑闻 (scandal / report / atrocities) · equivocate: 故意使用含混模棱之词避开实质真相 (politician / responses / witness) · hedge: 谨小慎微地附加保留条件以避免立旗 (bets / statements / answer)

groups.name: Examine & Audit · 审查与核查
groups.tip: 官方查对账目与明细数据

items.def_en: to test or examine people or things to verify suitability or weed out undesirables
items.ex_en: Security officers screen all cargo thoroughly before loading it onto the commercial airplane.
items.ex_zh: 安检人员在将所有货物装上商用飞机前都会进行彻底筛查。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To examine or inspect something carefully line by line or detail by detail
items.ex_en: Let us go over the contract details once more before signing the document.
items.ex_zh: 在签署文件之前，让我们把合同细节再仔细核对一遍。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To inspect something thoroughly to make sure everything is correct or in good condition
items.ex_en: Always check over your essay for grammatical slips before submitting.
items.ex_zh: 提交文章前，务必仔细检查一遍是否有语法疏漏。

items.def_zh: 浏览核对，仔细翻阅审查
items.def_en: (+ sth) To examine a collection of things or pages in a document to find information or check details
items.ex_en: I need to look through these financial reports to verify last month's figures.
items.ex_zh: 我需要翻阅审查这些财务报表，以核实上个月的数据。

items.def_zh: 审计，查账；旁听（大学课程）
items.def_en: 1. To officially examine and verify the financial accounts or records of an organization. 2. (North American) To attend a university course without receiving academic credit.
items.ex_en: Independent regulators arrived yesterday to audit the bank's annual overseas transactions.
items.ex_zh: 独立监管人员昨天抵达，正式审计该银行的年度海外交易。

items.def_zh: 对……进行人口普查（或官方统计调查）
items.def_en: To conduct an official census or systematic survey of a population or group.
items.ex_en: Field researchers will census the remote island population during the coming autumn months.
items.ex_zh: 实地调查人员将在接下来的秋季对该偏远岛屿的人口进行官方普查。

items.def_zh: 审查，审核（资格、背景或材料）；（兽医）诊疗（动物）
items.def_en: 1. To examine someone's past background, qualifications, or a document carefully to check suitability and accuracy. 2. To examine or treat an animal medically.
items.ex_en: The committee spent weeks trying to vet the candidates for the judicial appointment.
items.ex_zh: 委员会花了数周时间严格审查司法职位候选人的背景资格。

items.def_en: to look at something carefully in order to check its condition or compliance with standards
items.ex_en: Officials arrived early this morning to inspect the structural integrity of the bridge.
items.ex_zh: 官员们今早早早赶来，视察大桥的结构完整性。

items.def_en: to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly with a critical eye
items.ex_en: The defense attorney began to scrutinize every piece of forensic evidence presented today.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师开始以严苛的眼光彻底核验今天呈堂的每一件法医物证。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe systematically inspecting, evaluating, or counting records, qualifications, or individuals to ensure compliance, authenticity, or complete demographic data. 'Audit' focuses on financial/procedural verification, 'vet' on character/suitability assessment, and 'scrutinize' on rigorous line-by-line inspection.
groups.summary_zh: 系统性核实账目、资质、背景或数据，确保合规与准确。
groups.desc_en: Denotes methodically scrutinizing an entity, process, or person against official criteria to uncover flaws, fraud, or qualifications, contrasting with casual looking.
groups.desc_zh: 指对照官方规范或既定标准，对对象进行系统性穿透式检视与审查，区别于日常浏览或走马观花。
groups.nuance_en: audit: conduct an official, exhaustive financial inspection (accounts / books / records) · vet: investigate a person's background thoroughly for suitability (candidates / appointees / credentials) · inspect: closely view facilities or goods for compliance and defects (factory / equipment / premises) · screen: filter individuals or items to weed out threats or unfit elements (passengers / applicants / calls) · check over: review document or gear carefully for minor mistakes (work / manuscript / car)
groups.nuance_zh: audit: 开展官方严苛的财务账目审计 (accounts / books / records) · vet: 严密调查候选人政治或道德背景资质 (candidates / appointees / credentials) · inspect: 亲临实地排查设施完好度或合规隐患 (factory / equipment / premises) · screen: 依照门槛过滤筛除不合格者或危险源 (passengers / applicants / calls) · check over: 仔细核对文稿或部件以消除疏漏 (work / manuscript / car)

groups.name: Excavate & Hollow Out · 挖掘与开凿 (Hollow, Trench, Scoop)
groups.tip: 掘土挖沟以开凿空间

items.def_en: (+ sth) To remove material from something with a curved movement or tool, leaving a hollow
items.ex_en: She used a large spoon to scoop out the pumpkin seeds before baking.
items.ex_zh: 烘烤前，她用一把大勺子舀出了南瓜子。

items.def_zh: 舀出，挖空（凹形物体掏空）
items.def_en: (+ out) to hollow out a space or remove soft earth by or as if by using a scoop
items.ex_en: The workers had to scoop out the soft earth to create a trench.
items.ex_zh: 工人们必须掏出松软的泥土，挖出一个凹槽。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To make a space inside something solid by removing material from the interior
items.ex_en: Skilled artisans carefully hollow out the tree trunks to build traditional wooden canoes.
items.ex_zh: 熟练的工匠小心翼翼地掏空树干，以制作传统的独木舟。
items.ex2_en: The ancient limestone cliff hollowed out gradually after centuries of persistent sea erosion.
items.ex2_zh: 经历几个世纪持续的海水侵蚀后，古老的石灰岩悬崖逐渐凹陷成空洞。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ through/into) to dig a passage through or under the ground or an obstacle
items.ex_en: Escaped convicts managed to tunnel under the prison walls using rudimentary metal spoons.
items.ex_zh: 逃犯们用简陋的金属勺子在监狱围墙下凿穿了一条通道。

items.def_en: To dig or carve out the inside of something so that it becomes empty or hollow.
items.ex_en: The sculptor learned to hollow the stone block to reduce its final weight.
items.ex_zh: 这位雕塑家学会了凿空石料内部，以减轻其最终重量。
items.ex2_en: The center of the rotten tree trunk hollowed over decades of decay.
items.ex2_zh: 腐烂树干的中心在数十年的腐朽过程中逐渐中空。

items.def_en: To dig a long, narrow channel or ditch in the ground, especially for defense or drainage.
items.ex_en: Exhausted soldiers began to trench the frozen earth against the approaching enemy artillery.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的士兵们开始在冻土上挖掘战壕，以抵御逼近的敌军炮火。

items.def_zh: 凿出，挖空（形成凹槽或深坑）
items.def_en: (+ out) to make a deep hole or groove in a surface using a sharp tool or heavy force
items.ex_en: The runaway tire managed to gouge a nasty furrow right across the lawn.
items.ex_zh: 滚脱的轮胎在草坪上硬生生凿出了一道触目惊心的深沟。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To cut, carve, or dig a deep groove or hole into a surface with force
items.ex_en: The vandal used a sharp screwdriver to gouge out deep marks along the vehicle.
items.ex_zh: 破坏分子用一把锋利的螺丝刀在车身一侧狠狠抠出了深痕。

items.def_zh: 挖掘，发掘（系统性开挖成坑）
items.def_en: [I/T] to make a large hole or cavity in the ground systematically, especially for construction or archaeology
items.ex_en: Archaeologists plan to excavate the ancient burial site throughout the upcoming dry season.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家计划在即将到来的整个旱季中对该古墓遗址进行系统性发掘。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the spatial carving, gouging, or digging out of earth, rock, or solid mass to create channels, depressions, or hollowed-out cavities. They emphasize shaping or removing material to form specific voids rather than merely collecting loose earth.
groups.summary_zh: 通过掘土、凿穴或开槽等方式在物体或地面挖出空腔。
groups.desc_en: Denotes removing interior material to create a cavity, trench, or passage into solid earth or substance, contrasting with shaving a surface or flattening.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过挖除内部实体物质形成凹陷、孔洞、壕沟或通道，区别于表面刨平和压实。
groups.nuance_en: hollow out: remove the entire inner mass to leave an empty shell (tree trunk / pumpkin / rock) · scoop out: dig out soft material with a curved, spoon-like motion (melon / ice cream / flesh) · gouge out: violently dig out deep grooves or holes with a sharp tool (eyes / grooves / rock) · trench: cut deep, linear drainage or defensive ditches into the ground (field / soil / positions) · tunnel: burrow an underground horizontal conduit through earth (mountain / earth / wall)
groups.nuance_zh: hollow out: 掏空内部物质使其成为中空壳体 (tree trunk / pumpkin / rock) · scoop out: 以勺状弧度动作挖出柔软内馅或泥土 (melon / ice cream / flesh) · gouge out: 用尖锐工具粗暴挖出深坑或眼窝 (eyes / grooves / rock) · trench: 在地面开挖线性壕沟或防御堑壕 (field / soil / positions) · tunnel: 穿山凿地开拓水平地下通道 (mountain / earth / wall)

groups.name: Execution & Kill by Specific Method · 定刑处决与特种处死 (Behead, Crucify, Smother)
groups.tip: 剥夺生命，涵盖行刑与屠戮

items.def_en: execute someone by suspending them by the neck with a rope
items.ex_en: The authorities decided to hang the convicted traitor in the central prison yard.
items.ex_zh: 当局决定在中央监狱的大院内将那名定罪的叛徒绞刑处死。

items.def_en: kill someone by depriving them of oxygen
items.ex_en: Dense smoke from the chemical warehouse fire threatened to asphyxiate trapped factory workers.
items.ex_zh: 化学仓库大火产生的浓烟随时可能使被困的工厂工人窒息致死。
items.ex2_en: Several trapped miners unfortunately asphyxiated before the emergency rescue team could arrive.
items.ex2_zh: 几名被困矿工不幸在紧急救援队赶到前窒息身亡。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to kill or asphyxiate someone by blocking or squeezing their windpipe
items.ex_en: The attacker tried to choke off his victim during the violent midnight struggle.
items.ex_zh: 在午夜那场激烈的搏斗中，袭击者企图死死掐住受害者的喉管将其闷死。

items.def_zh: 使窒息致死，闷死；闷熄（火）；扼杀，抑制；厚厚覆盖
items.def_en: 1. To kill someone by covering their face so they cannot breathe. 2. To extinguish a fire by cutting off air. 3. To suppress or stifle an emotion or action. 4. (+ with/in) To cover something thickly.
items.ex_en: The intruder attempted to smother the sleeping guard with a thick feather pillow.
items.ex_zh: 入侵者试图用厚厚的羽绒枕头将熟睡的警卫闷死。

items.def_en: execute someone using a guillotine
items.ex_en: Revolutionaries prepared to guillotine the captured aristocrats before a large, cheering crowd.
items.ex_zh: 革命者准备在欢呼雀跃的大群民众面前，用断头台处决被俘的贵族。

items.def_en: execute or kill someone by a massive electric shock
items.ex_en: The state decided to electrocute the serial killer following years of appeals.
items.ex_zh: 经过多年的上诉，该州决定对这名连环杀手执行电刑处死。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to kill someone by hanging them by the neck with a rope
items.ex_en: The angry vigilantes threatened to string up the horse thief without a trial.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的治安维持队员威胁要不经审讯就将偷马贼吊死。

items.def_en: 1. To execute or kill someone by cutting off their head.
items.ex_en: The ruthless warlord ordered his executioners to behead the captured enemy commander.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的军阀命令刽子手将俘获的敌军指挥官斩首示众。

items.def_zh: 将……钉在十字架上处死；严厉批评，严惩
items.def_en: 1. (historical) To execute someone by nailing or tying them to a wooden cross. 2. (informal) To criticize or punish someone severely.
items.ex_en: The hostile tabloid media will crucify the mayor for this minor administrative blunder.
items.ex_zh: 怀有敌意的小报媒体会因这次微小的行政失误而把市长骂得狗血淋头。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate specific physical methods used to kill or legally execute someone, distinguishing each act by the anatomical or mechanical means applied—such as cutting off the head, nailing to a cross, or cutting off air supply.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过特定器械、解剖部位或既定规程处死或处决受刑者。
groups.desc_en: Denotes killing an individual according to a specific physical method, sentence, or lethal mechanism, contrasting with generic, unstylized murder.
groups.desc_zh: 指按照特定机械、窒息或斩首方式处决个体，区别于无特定手法的泛指杀戮。
groups.nuance_en: behead: sever the head from the body using an axe or blade (monarch / captive / traitor) · guillotine: execute mechanistically using a falling heavy angled blade (aristocrats / king / criminal) · hang: kill by suspending by the neck with a noose (condemned man / prisoner / spy) · electrocute: kill by passing a lethal electric current through the body (inmate / convict / criminal) · smother: kill by physically covering the mouth and nose to block air (baby / victim with a pillow / fire)
groups.nuance_zh: behead: 使用刀斧斩首处决 (monarch / captive / traitor) · guillotine: 使用落刀断头台机械化斩首 (aristocrats / king / criminal) · hang: 用绞索套颈悬吊施以绞刑 (condemned man / prisoner / spy) · electrocute: 导入致命电流电殛致死 (inmate / convict / criminal) · smother: 用物捂住口鼻窒息致死 (baby / victim with a pillow / fire)

groups.name: Extrajudicial Execution & Wholesale Slaughter · 灭绝性屠杀与私刑处决 (Lynch, Massacre)
groups.tip: 从个体杀戮到集体屠杀

items.def_en: to kill, destroy, or severely wipe out a large proportion of a population
items.ex_en: The prolonged drought threatened to decimate the livestock population across the entire region.
items.ex_zh: 长期的干旱恐将重创并大批灭杀整个地区的牲畜群。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to hang someone, especially as an act of extrajudicial execution or lynching
items.ex_en: A lawless mob gathered outside the jailhouse, determined to string up the suspect.
items.ex_zh: 一伙目无法纪的暴民聚集在看守所外，决意将嫌疑人私刑绞死。

items.def_zh: 像宰杀牲畜般屠杀；滥杀
items.def_en: to kill people in large numbers in a cruel, violent, and unsparing manner
items.ex_en: Marauders burst through the gates and began to slaughter innocent townspeople without hesitation.
items.ex_zh: 劫掠者冲破大门，毫不犹豫地开始大肆屠杀无辜的镇民。

items.def_en: to kill violently, brutally, and indiscriminately, treating victims like livestock
items.ex_en: The ruthless invaders chose to butcher innocent civilians inside the barricaded village chapel.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的侵略者竟在紧闭的乡村礼拜堂内野蛮屠戮无辜平民。

items.def_zh: （用机枪等）成批扫射杀死，残酷大屠杀
items.def_en: (+ sb) to kill large numbers of people quickly and mercilessly, especially with gunfire
items.ex_en: Machine-gun nests began to mow down advancing infantrymen across the muddy battlefield.
items.ex_zh: 机枪火力点开始在泥泞的战场上疯狂扫射、成批击毙冲锋的步兵。

items.def_zh: 消灭，彻底摧毁，歼灭（群体或人口）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to completely destroy, kill, or eradicate a whole population or group
items.ex_en: Famine and deadly disease threatened to wipe out the small isolated mountain community.
items.ex_zh: 饥荒与致命疾病恐将彻底灭绝这个与世隔绝的山区小聚落。

items.def_en: 1. To kill a large number of people or animals in a cruel or violent way. 2. (informal) To defeat someone thoroughly in a game or contest.
items.ex_en: Invading forces proceeded to massacre hundreds of defenseless villagers inside the ancient shrine.
items.ex_zh: 入侵部队随后在古老的神殿内残杀屠戮了数百名毫无防备的村民。

items.def_zh: 处以私刑（通常指处死、绞死）
items.def_en: (of a mob) To put someone to death by violence, especially hanging, without legal authorization or trial.
items.ex_en: A violent racist mob gathered late that night to lynch the young captive.
items.ex_zh: 当晚深夜，一伙暴虐的种族主义暴民聚集起来，准备将年轻的俘虏私刑处死。

items.def_en: to deliberately destroy a whole population or group of living beings utterly
items.ex_en: The fascist regime planned to exterminate entire ethnic communities across occupied territories.
items.ex_zh: 法西斯政权企图在被占领土上彻底灭绝整个族群。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict the deliberate, violent killing of multiple people or targeted individuals without due process, escalating from unlawful collective execution to indiscriminate, industrial-scale extermination.
groups.summary_zh: 非法处决或针对特定人群的大规模残暴屠戮，具有极高的血腥与残酷程度。
groups.desc_en: Denotes killing defenseless individuals or vast populations through lawless mob violence, war-crime butchery, or mass liquidation, contrasting with individualized legal execution.
groups.desc_zh: 指暴民私刑或军队以灭绝性、残暴性手段成批屠戮无抵抗者，区别于单体的合法审判死刑。
groups.nuance_en: lynch: murder by an extralegal mob without due process (victim / suspect / prisoner) · massacre: indiscriminately slaughter vast numbers of defenseless victims (civilians / villagers / garrison) · slaughter: brutally butcher humans like livestock on a horrific scale (crowd / innocent people / herd) · mow down: kill in mass rapid succession using automatic gunfire (troops / civilians / enemies) · wipe out: totally annihilate a population or settlement from existence (village / army / enemy)
groups.nuance_zh: lynch: 暴民脱离法律程序的私刑处死 (victim / suspect / prisoner) · massacre: 针对手无寸铁群体的大规模无差别屠杀 (civilians / villagers / garrison) · slaughter: 如宰杀牲口般大面积血腥屠戮人类 (crowd / innocent people / herd) · mow down: 用机枪等密集火力如割草般大片扫射杀死 (troops / civilians / enemies) · wipe out: 将敌军或定居点成建制连根抹杀拔除 (village / army / enemy)

groups.name: Fade Away & Cease to Exist · 消失与消散 (Evanesce, Dissipate, Vanish)
groups.tip: 如轻烟雾气般逐渐化为乌有

items.def_zh: 逐渐消失、变得微弱或模糊
items.def_en: (+ away) to lose strength, loudness, or visibility slowly until no longer perceptible
items.ex_en: The distant church bells began to fade as we drove through the valley.
items.ex_zh: 当我们驾车穿过山谷时，远处的教堂钟声逐渐变得微弱模糊。
items.ex2_en: Continuous exposure to direct sunlight will fade the bright fabric over time.
items.ex2_zh: 长时间暴露在直射阳光下会随着时间的推移使鲜艳的织物褪色。

items.def_zh: （如雪融化般）悄然散去、逐渐消失
items.def_en: to disappear gradually or unobtrusively, like ice turning to water
items.ex_en: All lingering hostility seemed to melt away after their candid and heartfelt conversation.
items.ex_zh: 在坦诚而由衷的长谈之后，所有挥之不去的敌意似乎都悄然散去了。

items.def_en: to slowly disappear, become weaker, or cease to be visible or audible
items.ex_en: The final notes of the beautiful cello melody slowly began to fade away.
items.ex_zh: 那首优美的大提琴曲的最后音符开始慢慢消退直至不见。

items.def_en: to gradually become quieter or weaker until it stops existing altogether
items.ex_en: The applause gradually died away as the speaker began to talk.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者开口讲话时，掌声渐渐消失了。

items.def_zh: 逐渐减少直至消失，慢慢止歇
items.def_en: to gradually dwindle, weaken, or come to an end
items.ex_en: The passionate protests began to peter out once the cold winter rains arrived.
items.ex_zh: 寒冬的雨季一旦到来，激烈的抗议活动便开始逐渐止歇。

items.def_zh: 突然或完全消失、不见踪影
items.def_en: to disappear suddenly, completely, or in a way that cannot be explained
items.ex_en: The mysterious courier seemed to vanish into thin air among the crowded alleys.
items.ex_zh: 那名神秘的信使似乎在拥挤的巷弄间凭空消失得无影无踪。

items.def_zh: （使烟、雾、云气等）逐渐消散、散去
items.def_en: [I/T] to gradually disappear or scatter completely, or cause gas, vapor, or tension to do so
items.ex_en: Warm morning sunlight quickly caused the thick mountain mist to dissipate completely.
items.ex_zh: 温暖的晨光迅速让浓重的山雾彻底消散殆尽。
items.ex2_en: The tense atmosphere in the meeting room dissipated after the CEO smiled.
items.ex2_zh: 首席执行官露出了微笑，会议室里紧张的气氛随之消散。

items.def_zh: （使）非物质化，（使）化为乌有，消失
items.def_en: To cease to have physical form, or to cause something to vanish into thin air.
items.ex_en: In the optical illusion, the solid statue seemed to dematerialize before our eyes.
items.ex_zh: 在视错觉下，那座坚固的雕像仿佛在我们眼前化为乌有。
items.ex2_en: The science-fiction villain used a laser device to dematerialize the solid vault door.
items.ex2_zh: 科幻反派使用激光装置将坚固的金库大门分解消失。

items.def_zh: 逐渐消失，消散，化为乌有
items.def_en: To fade away or disappear gradually like mist, smoke, or a memory.
items.ex_en: Childhood memories often evanesce like morning dew beneath the relentless passage of time.
items.ex_zh: 童年记忆往往在无情岁月的流逝下，如朝露般渐渐化为乌有。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe entities or phenomena gradually or completely disappearing from sight, physical form, or existence. 'Evanesce' and 'dematerialize' represent literary or science-focused registers, while verbs like 'dissipate' and 'vanish' capture everyday and physical dispersal.
groups.summary_zh: 描述实体或现象由显转隐、形体散失或彻底化为乌有的过程。
groups.desc_en: Denotes gradually losing substance, intensity, or visibility until nothing remains, contrasting with sudden destruction or abrupt termination.
groups.desc_zh: 指实体、光影、声响或势头在时空中逐渐衰减、消散直至虚无，区别于猝然毁坏或截然中断。
groups.nuance_en: fade: gradually lose color, brightness, or sharpness (light / color / memories) · dissipate: cause clouds, vapor, or tension to break up and disperse into nothing (smoke / mist / anger) · vanish: disappear completely and mysteriously from sight (magician / trace / species) · peter out: gradually dwindle to a trickling halt (stream / interest / campaign) · melt away: dissolve softly and imperceptibly until gone (crowd / doubts / snow)
groups.nuance_zh: fade: 颜色、光线或记忆逐渐黯淡消退 (light / color / memories) · dissipate: 云雾、气体或情绪碎片化向四周消散 (smoke / mist / anger) · vanish: 踪迹或人影彻底、神秘地从视野凭空隐匿 (magician / trace / species) · peter out: 势头或水流细化衰减直至彻底枯竭 (stream / interest / campaign) · melt away: 如冰雪融化般不知不觉消弭化解 (crowd / doubts / snow)

groups.name: Fail to Retain or Notice · 遗忘与疏漏 (Forget, Overlook, Omit)
groups.tip: 因疏忽而未注意到或遗失

items.def_en: to be forgotten or overlooked, especially temporarily
items.ex_en: I meant to call you earlier, but the urgent task completely slipped my mind.
items.ex_zh: 我本想早点给你打电话，但这项紧急任务被我忘得一干二净。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to fail to include or inadvertently omit someone or something
items.ex_en: Be careful not to leave out any important details from your experimental report.
items.ex_zh: 小心不要在你的实验报告中遗漏任何重要细节。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to ignore, overlook, or fail to notice or consider someone or something
items.ex_en: The hiring committee chose to pass over several qualified internal candidates this year.
items.ex_zh: 聘用委员会今年决定对几位符合资格的内部候选人置之不理。

items.def_zh: 心不在焉而不去注意，不予理睬
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to stop listening to, noticing, or paying attention to one's surroundings or what is being said
items.ex_en: Tired of the endless bickering, he began to tune out his colleagues completely.
items.ex_zh: 厌倦了无休止的争吵，他索性对同事们的话充耳不闻、心不在焉。

items.def_zh: 漏掉，遗漏；未注意到；错过；未击中；想念
items.def_en: 1. To fail to notice, hear, or include something. 2. To fail to hit, reach, or catch. 3. To feel sad because someone or something is absent.
items.ex_en: The copy editor was shocked to miss several obvious typos on the cover.
items.ex_zh: 文字编辑惊讶地发现自己竟然漏掉了封面上几处显而易见的拼写错误。

items.def_en: to fail to notice, see, or consider something inadvertently
items.ex_en: It is dangerously easy to overlook subtle accounting discrepancies in such vast spreadsheets.
items.ex_zh: 在如此庞大的电子表格中，人们极容易疏忽漏看微小的会计差错。

items.def_en: to leave out or exclude someone or something, either by mistake or intention
items.ex_en: The editor decided to omit unnecessary background details from the final published article.
items.ex_zh: 编辑决定在最终发表的文章中省去不必要的背景细节。

items.def_en: 1. To fail to remember a fact, event, or name. 2. To leave something behind by mistake or omit to do something.
items.ex_en: Do not forget to lock the laboratory doors before you leave tonight, please.
items.ex_zh: 今晚离开之前，请千万不要忘记锁好实验室的大门。

items.def_zh: 刻意忘掉，抛弃（旧习惯或旧观念）
items.def_en: To make a deliberate effort to forget or discard a habit, skill, or false belief.
items.ex_en: Senior drivers must unlearn bad habits when transitioning to modern electric vehicles safely.
items.ex_zh: 资深驾驶员在平稳过渡到现代电动汽车时，必须刻意改掉以往的旧习惯。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote a cognitive lapse where an agent fails to recall stored information or inadvertently neglects to notice, include, or perform something.
groups.summary_zh: 指记忆失效未能忆起，或认知疏忽导致遗漏未办。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive or attentional failure causing information, duties, or perceptual details to escape awareness, contrasting with deliberate rejection or intentional discarding.
groups.desc_zh: 因认知或注意力缺漏导致信息、职责或细节未被保留或觉察，与蓄意剔除或主动丢弃不同。
groups.nuance_en: forget: general failure of memory retention (name / appointment / password) · overlook: fail to notice or consider, often through haste (detail / flaw / warning) · omit: leave unmentioned or excluded, intentionally or not (step / detail / clause) · slip one's mind: momentary or accidental cognitive lapse (errand / birthday) · pass over: intentionally or accidentally disregard someone/something for promotion or attention (candidate / objection)
groups.nuance_zh: forget: 普遍意义上的记忆遗忘 (name / appointment / password) · overlook: 粗心或匆忙中未予留心、视而不见 (detail / flaw / warning) · omit: 遗漏未列入或跳过 (step / detail / clause) · slip one's mind: 偶然或转瞬即逝的淡忘 (errand / birthday) · pass over: 忽略或跨过某人某事不予提拔或关注 (candidate / objection)

groups.name: Fatigue & Physical Depletion · 疲乏与劳累 (Weary, Fag, Fatigue)
groups.tip: 体力从微困走向精疲力竭

items.def_en: [I/T] to lose energy or cause someone to feel in need of rest
items.ex_en: The long, steep mountain hike caused the older tourist to tire noticeably fast.
items.ex_zh: 漫长而陡峭的山路攀登让那位上了年纪的游客明显感到疲惫不堪。
items.ex2_en: Lifting heavy crates all morning will tire even the strongest warehouse worker.
items.ex2_zh: 搬运一整个早晨的沉重箱子会让最强壮的仓库工人也感到疲惫。

items.def_zh: 使极度疲劳；使心力交瘁
items.def_en: to cause severe physical or mental exhaustion through prolonged strain
items.ex_en: Relentless night vigils and agonizing sorrow conspired to fatigue the grieving queen completely.
items.ex_zh: 连夜的守夜与噬心的悲痛交织，使这位痛失亲人的王后心力交瘁。
items.ex2_en: The elite marathon runners began to fatigue visibly during the final grueling miles.
items.ex2_zh: 在最后艰苦的几英里中，精英马拉松跑者们明显开始显现疲态。

items.def_zh: 使体力消耗殆尽，使虚弱疲惫
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone to become weak, fatigued, or physically depleted from overwork
items.ex_en: Working continuous sixteen-hour shifts will eventually run down even the strongest young workers.
items.ex_zh: 连续上十六个小时的轮班，即便是最健壮的年轻工人也会体力透支垮掉。

items.def_en: to exhaust someone's physical stamina completely
items.ex_en: The long, uphill hike completely tired the children out.
items.ex_zh: 漫长而费力的徒步爬坡把孩子们累得筋疲力竭。

items.def_zh: 使疲惫不堪，使筋疲力尽
items.def_en: (+ sb) to thoroughly tire someone out or exhaust their energy
items.ex_en: A full afternoon playing soccer in the park will tucker out energetic toddlers.
items.ex_zh: 在公园踢整整一个下午的足球，会让精力充沛的幼童筋疲力尽。

items.def_zh: （使）疲倦，（使）劳累；（使）厌烦，失去耐心
items.def_en: 1. (formal or literary) To make someone feel very tired, or to become tired. 2. (+ of) To lose patience or interest in something.
items.ex_en: Endless bureaucratic delays began to weary the patient petitioners seeking official land permits.
items.ex_zh: 无休止的官僚拖延开始让那些寻求官方土地许可的耐心请愿者感到心力交瘁。
items.ex2_en: The elderly travelers wearied quickly after climbing hundreds of steep stone steps.
items.ex2_zh: 年迈的旅行者在爬完几百级陡峭的石阶后很快就感到疲倦了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to exhaust oneself or someone completely through prolonged hard work and exertion
items.ex_en: Working twelve hours every day will quickly burn out even the most energetic staff.
items.ex_zh: 每天工作十二个小时很快就会让即使精力最充沛的员工累垮。

items.def_zh: 使人疲惫不堪；耗尽精力
items.def_en: to make someone thoroughly exhausted from prolonged work or exertion
items.ex_en: Running after toddlers all afternoon completely wore me out.
items.ex_zh: 整个下午跟在幼儿屁股后面跑让我筋疲力尽。

items.def_zh: 使筋疲力竭（常作 fag out）；苦干，辛劳工作
items.def_en: 1. (British dated, often fag out) To exhaust someone with hard work, or to tire oneself out. 2. To work hard and tirelessly.
items.ex_en: Carrying those heavy sacks of coal across the yard completely fagged him out.
items.ex_zh: 把那些沉重的煤袋搬过院子彻底把他累垮了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this scale describe the progressive onset of bodily tiredness from physical labor or prolonged exertion, progressing from mild fatigue to grueling overwork.
groups.summary_zh: 描述由体力劳作或持久消耗引发的身体倦怠与劳损程度递增。
groups.desc_en: Progressive drain or total exhaustion of vital physical/mental energy through sustained exertion, contrasting with mere transient idleness or acute illness.
groups.desc_zh: 因持续消耗而导致的生理或心理精力衰竭，与短暂停顿或急性疾病有别。
groups.nuance_en: tire: gradual onset of physical or mental fatigue (eyes / muscles) · fatigue: deep, systemic, often pathological exhaustion (crew / soldiers) · wear out: render totally depleted through prolonged friction or exertion (shoes / patience / body) · burn out: complete collapse of mental and physical energy from chronic stress (employee / nurse / student) · tucker out: informal, complete physical draining after lively effort (child / puppy)
groups.nuance_zh: tire: 逐渐感到困乏或劳累 (eyes / muscles) · fatigue: 深度且系统的体力或意志衰竭 (crew / soldiers) · wear out: 经久消耗磨损至枯竭 (shoes / patience / body) · burn out: 长期压力下身心彻底崩溃衰竭 (employee / nurse / student) · tucker out: (口语) 嬉闹折腾后精疲力竭 (child / puppy)

groups.name: Feast Sumptuously & Make Merry · 设宴享乐与畅饮 (Banquet, Feast, Spree)
groups.tip: 宴席聚餐与畅快大嚼大饮

items.def_en: to eat a lavish or excessive amount of food greedily and indulgently
items.ex_en: We stayed up late on Friday night to watch movies and pig out.
items.ex_zh: 我们周五晚上熬夜看电影，胡吃海喝了一顿。

items.def_zh: 大快朵颐，开怀痛饮美食
items.def_en: to begin eagerly eating a hearty or sumptuous meal
items.ex_en: As soon as the roast chicken arrived, everyone grabbed a plate and tucked in.
items.ex_zh: 烤鸡一端上桌，大家就拿起盘子大快朵颐起来。

items.def_zh: 纵情享乐，狂欢畅饮，过奢华快乐的生活
items.def_en: to enjoy oneself extravagantly and festively without restraint
items.ex_en: They spent the entire weekend living it up at a luxury resort in Monaco.
items.ex_zh: 他们在摩纳哥的一家豪华度假村纵情享乐度过了整个周末。

items.def_zh: 尽情享用盛宴，大吃大喝
items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to eat large amounts of delicious food and drink with great pleasure in celebration
items.ex_en: The victorious warriors feasted upon roasted meats and sweet wine until the dawn broke.
items.ex_zh: 得胜的勇士们尽情享用烤肉与美酒，狂欢直至破晓。

items.def_zh: 设宴款待；痛饮饱餐，参加宴会
items.def_en: 1. To feast or eat richly and luxuriously at a banquet. 2. To entertain someone with a lavish formal feast.
items.ex_en: The ambassador banqueted foreign dignitaries in the grand ballroom with remarkable imperial elegance.
items.ex_zh: 大使在宽敞的宴会厅中以非凡的皇室排场设宴款待外国政要。

items.def_en: (+ on) to indulge in an excessive, uncontrolled spree of eating, drinking, or revelry
items.ex_en: After finishing his strict diet, he began to binge on chocolate and pastries.
items.ex_zh: 结束严格的节食后，他开始放纵大吃巧克力和糕点。

items.def_en: (informal) To indulge in an uncontrolled bout of drinking, partying, or spending.
items.ex_en: They went downtown to spree all night after receiving their annual holiday bonuses.
items.ex_zh: 领到年终奖金后，他们去市中心通宵狂欢痛饮了一番。

items.def_en: to honor or entertain someone lavishly with public celebrations or a festive meal
items.ex_en: The university planned to fete the Nobel laureate with a grand evening gala.
items.ex_zh: 大学计划举办一场盛大的晚间庆典来设宴表彰这位诺贝尔奖得主。

items.def_zh: 以盛宴款待，用美食招待
items.def_en: (+ with) to entertain lavishly with choice food and drink
items.ex_en: The generous host regaled his weary travelers with vintage wines and delicate venison.
items.ex_zh: 慷慨的主人用陈年佳酿和精致鹿肉盛情款待了疲惫的旅人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate participating in or hosting lavish, abundant meals accompanied by celebratory merrymaking, drinking, or spending. 'Banquet' and 'feast' highlight the indulgence in magnificent food and drink, while 'spree' focuses on going on an extravagant celebratory binge.
groups.summary_zh: 指举办或参与盛大奢华的宴饮、饕餮大餐及放纵享乐活动。
groups.desc_en: Indulging lavishly in eating, drinking, and celebratory revelry, contrasting with ordinary daily dining or solitary sustenance.
groups.desc_zh: 极度奢华地享受饮食与狂欢作乐，不同于普通就餐或日常充饥。
groups.nuance_en: feast: partake abundantly of rich food in celebration (eyes / banquet / harvest) · banquet: attend or hold an elaborate formal ceremonial meal (dignitaries / guests) · pig out: informal, gluttonous overeating without decorum (junk food / pizza) · spree: indulge recklessly in an uninhibited period of pleasure (drinking / shopping) · fete: honor someone with lavish public festivities (hero / laureate)
groups.nuance_zh: feast: 尽情享用丰盛美馔或饱览胜景 (eyes / banquet / harvest) · banquet: 正式出席或举办盛大国宴、盛宴 (dignitaries / guests) · pig out: (口语) 放肆暴饮暴食毫无吃相 (junk food / pizza) · spree: 肆意纵情狂欢或挥霍 (drinking / shopping) · fete: 设宴或举办庆典隆重款待某人 (hero / laureate)

groups.name: Fight & Scuffle · 打斗与肉搏 (Roughhouse, Tussle, Brawl)
groups.tip: 身体近距离扭打推搡与肉搏

items.def_zh: 摆出打斗架势，迎面交锋
items.def_en: to adopt a fighting stance or prepare to grapple or brawl with an opponent
items.ex_en: The two angry drivers squared off in the parking lot after the collision.
items.ex_zh: 相撞后，两名愤怒的司机在停车场摆出了打斗架势。

items.def_en: to engage in a short, disorganized, and confused physical fight
items.ex_en: Rival fans began to scuffle in the corridor before police separated them quickly.
items.ex_zh: 对立的球迷在走廊里扭打起来，随后被警察迅速拉开。

items.def_zh: 胡闹扭打，嬉闹打斗；粗暴对待
items.def_en: (informal) To play or fight in a rough, boisterous, or noisy way; to handle someone roughly.
items.ex_en: The boys were warned not to roughhouse in the living room near antiques.
items.ex_zh: 男孩们被警告不要在客厅古董旁边嬉闹打斗。

items.def_zh: 与假想敌作拳击训练；虚与委蛇，闪烁其词
items.def_en: 1. To practice boxing punches and footwork in the air against an imaginary opponent. 2. To avoid directly confronting an issue or opponent; fence.
items.ex_en: The prizefighter began to shadowbox before the mirror to perfect his defensive stance.
items.ex_zh: 拳击手在镜子前对着假想敌进行拳击训练，以完善他的防守姿势。

items.def_en: to engage in a physical fight, scuffle, or boxing match
items.ex_en: The referee stepped in immediately when both boxers started to mix it up.
items.ex_zh: 两名拳手一开始激烈互殴，裁判便立刻介入制止。

items.def_en: (+ with) to engage in a close, hand-to-hand fight or struggle without weapons
items.ex_en: The guard rushed forward to grapple with the intruder on the wet grass.
items.ex_zh: 警卫冲上前去，在湿漉漉的草地上与入侵者肉搏扭打。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) To fight, wrestle, or scuffle closely; to engage in a vigorous struggle or contest.
items.ex_en: Two dogs tussled over a large bone in the middle of the yard.
items.ex_zh: 两只狗在院子中央为了一根大骨头激烈争抢扭打。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack someone physically with great force and violence
items.ex_en: Without warning, the enraged bouncer laid into the trespasser with heavy punches.
items.ex_zh: 毫无预警地，被激怒的保镖挥起重拳向闯入者猛打过去。

items.def_en: to fight noisily and roughly in a public or crowded place
items.ex_en: Drunken patrons began to brawl outside the crowded tavern just after midnight struck.
items.ex_zh: 刚过午夜，醉酒的顾客就在拥挤的酒馆外聚众斗殴起来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict close physical confrontation, violent grappling, or boisterous physical combat between individuals. They contrast along lines of playful rowdiness ('roughhouse'), disorderly skirmishes ('tussle'), non-contact training ('shadowbox'), and chaotic, violent melee fighting ('brawl', 'grapple').
groups.summary_zh: 指近身肉搏、相互扭打拉扯或喧闹的打斗冲突。
groups.desc_en: Engaging in hands-on, uncoordinated physical combat or rough contact, contrasting with regulated formal martial competition or standoff missile warfare.
groups.desc_zh: 进行近身、无序的肢体扭打与肉搏，区别于规范的擂台竞技或远距离交火。
groups.nuance_en: scuffle: short, disorganized, low-intensity tussle (police / protesters) · roughhouse: rowdy, playful, but harsh physical horseplay (kids / siblings) · brawl: noisy, public, violent physical melee (bar / patrons) · grapple: seize and struggle hand-to-hand in close quarters (opponent / intruder) · lay into: launch a furious physical or verbal assault (attacker / critic)
groups.nuance_zh: scuffle: 短暂且混乱的肢体小冲突 (police / protesters) · roughhouse: 粗野嬉闹、打闹推搡 (kids / siblings) · brawl: 喧闹混乱的公共斗殴 (bar / patrons) · grapple: 贴身紧抓并极力缠斗 (opponent / intruder) · lay into: 猛烈扑打或痛骂攻讦 (attacker / critic)

groups.name: Fit Out & Furnish with Fixtures · 装设特定构件与马具装备
groups.tip: 板条组装拼合完整架构

items.def_zh: 装配，装备，为……提供固定装置
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to equip or furnish a structure, room, or mount with necessary fittings or equipment
items.ex_en: The laboratory was fitted out with the latest analytical instruments.
items.ex_zh: 该实验室配备了最先进的分析仪器。

items.def_zh: 装配齐备，给……装备构件或用具
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to supply or furnish someone or something with all the required gear or fittings
items.ex_en: They completely kitted out the camper van with solar panels and camping gear.
items.ex_zh: 他们给露营车全面装配了太阳能电池板和野营装备。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to put a saddle on a horse or other riding animal
items.ex_en: The rancher hurried to saddle up his best mare before the storm hit.
items.ex_zh: 农场主赶在暴风雨来临之前给最好的母马套上了马鞍。

items.def_zh: 给（墙壁或天花板）镶嵌护墙板
items.def_en: to fit or cover a wall, ceiling, or door with flat wooden or composite panels
items.ex_en: Carpenters panelled the dining room with polished cherry wood to match the furniture.
items.ex_zh: 木工们用抛光的樱桃木给餐厅镶上护墙板，以搭配家具。

items.def_zh: 给（马等）装上鞍；使承担，使承受（重担或债务等）
items.def_en: 1. To put a saddle on a horse or other animal. 2. (saddle someone with) To burden someone with an unwanted responsibility or debt.
items.ex_en: He went outside early to saddle the brown pony for his young daughter.
items.ex_zh: 他一大早就出去为小女儿把那匹棕色矮马备上马鞍。

items.def_en: To provide, fit, or construct something using slats (thin strips of wood, metal, etc.).
items.ex_en: The carpenter carefully slatted the garden gate to ensure proper airflow and privacy.
items.ex_zh: 木匠精心用板条制作了花园大门，以确保通风和隐私。

items.def_en: to fit walls or ceilings with thin strips of wood to support plaster
items.ex_en: Old artisans lathed the interior walls before spreading the thick coat of plaster.
items.ex_zh: 老工匠们先给内墙钉上木条板，然后再抹上厚厚的灰泥。

items.def_zh: 给（室内墙下半部）装设壁板
items.def_en: to line the lower part of interior walls with timber paneling
items.ex_en: Rich oak wainscoted the grand dining hall, lending an air of ancient dignity.
items.ex_zh: 名贵的橡木给宏伟的宴会厅下部镶了壁板，平添了几分古朴庄严的气息。

items.def_en: to put a bridle on a horse or other riding animal
items.ex_en: The stable master bridled the spirited stallion before leading him onto the path.
items.ex_zh: 马厩主管给这匹桀骜不驯的公马套上辔头，然后牵它走上小径。

groups.summary_en: Denotes outfitting an animal or physical structure with specific structural members, boards, or riding gear (e.g., placing slats on blinds/fences or fitting a mount with a saddle).
groups.summary_zh: 为结构安装板条部件，或为坐骑备鞍装配专业马具构件。
groups.desc_en: Equipping an object, space, or animal with specialized structural parts, panels, or working gear, contrasting with mere non-structural furnishing or casual placement.
groups.desc_zh: 为空间、器物或牲畜装配特定结构性部件、板材或功能性索具，不同于普通软装摆设。
groups.nuance_en: fit out: fully supply a space/vessel with specialized equipment (ship / shop / studio) · kit out: furnish a person or unit with complete uniform/gear (team / soldier) · saddle up: equip a mount with harness and saddle for riding (horse / pony) · panel: cover structural walls with wood or prefabricated sheets (room / wall / ceiling) · wainscot: line the lower half of interior walls with paneling (hallway / study)
groups.nuance_zh: fit out: 为船舶、店铺配置专门装备与设施 (ship / shop / studio) · kit out: 为人员或团队配齐成套行头与装备 (team / soldier) · saddle up: 为坐骑备好马鞍并准备骑乘 (horse / pony) · panel: 用板材镶嵌装饰墙体或天花板 (room / wall / ceiling) · wainscot: 在墙体下半截铺设护墙板 (hallway / study)

groups.name: Fixation & Addiction · 迷恋与沉溺成瘾 (Addict, Obsess)
groups.tip: 从放任爱好到深陷其中无法自拔

items.def_en: to dominate the thoughts and attention of someone to the exclusion of other things
items.ex_en: Thoughts of the impending trial began to preoccupy her mind night and day.
items.ex_zh: 对即将到来的审判的忧虑日夜占据着她的全部思绪。

items.def_zh: 被深深吸引，疯狂爱上/迷恋上
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to become strongly and infatuatedly attracted to someone or something
items.ex_en: He completely fell for the charming artist the moment they met at gallery.
items.ex_zh: 他们在画廊相见的那一刻，他就彻底疯狂迷恋上了那位迷人的艺术家。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to develop an unhealthy, obsessive focus or attachment towards someone or something
items.ex_en: The young scholar began to fixate upon minor historical details during his research.
items.ex_zh: 这位青年学者在研究过程中开始过分痴迷于微小的历史细节。
items.ex2_en: Child psychologists caution that violent video games can fixate young impressionable minds.
items.ex2_zh: 儿童心理学家警告说，暴力视频游戏可能会使心智尚未成熟的年轻人产生执念。

items.def_en: (+ with) to inspire an intense, foolish, and unreasoning passion in someone
items.ex_en: Her dazzling beauty never failed to infatuate every young nobleman in the court.
items.ex_zh: 她耀眼的美貌总能让宫廷里的每一位年轻贵族神魂颠倒。

items.def_zh: 迷恋上，从……中获得极大快感沉溺其中
items.def_en: (+ sth) to find something intensely exciting or derive an obsessive thrill or pleasure from it
items.ex_en: Some thrill seekers genuinely get off on dangerous stunts and high-speed driving.
items.ex_zh: 一些寻求刺激的人确实能从危险特技和超速驾驶中获得极大的快感。

items.def_en: (+ sb on sth) to cause someone to become addicted to or compulsively preoccupied with something
items.ex_en: The new mobile game hooked millions of players on its daily battle challenges.
items.ex_zh: 这款新手机游戏凭借其每日对战挑战让数百万玩家沉溺上瘾。

items.def_en: 1. To cause someone or oneself to become dependent on or devoted to a drug, substance, or activity.
items.ex_en: Unregulated gambling can easily addict vulnerable individuals to severe cycles of financial ruin.
items.ex_zh: 不受监管的赌博很容易使意志薄弱者沉溺其中，陷入严重的财务破产恶性循环。

items.def_zh: 使痴迷，使着迷；念念不忘，牵挂（obsess about/over）
items.def_en: 1. To occupy the mind of someone continually and excessively. 2. (+ about/over) To think or worry about something constantly.
items.ex_en: She continued to obsess over minor grammatical errors in her published novel.
items.ex_zh: 她依然对自己已出版小说中的微小语法错误念念不忘。
items.ex2_en: Fears of financial failure continued to obsess the young entrepreneur night and day.
items.ex2_zh: 对财务失败的恐惧夜以继日地萦绕在这位年轻创业者的心头。

items.def_zh: 束缚，奴役（使被恶习欲望所控）
items.def_en: (+ to) to cause someone to lose all autonomy and be completely dominated by a habit or desire
items.ex_en: Unchecked greed will gradually enslave a person to destructive materialistic desires.
items.ex_zh: 放任不管的贪欲会逐渐使一个人沦为毁灭性物质欲望的奴隶。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express degrees of psychological and emotional fixation, moving from persistent preoccupation to complete compulsive, uncontrollable dependence.
groups.summary_zh: 从持续思绪萦绕到彻底形成强迫性依恋成瘾。
groups.desc_en: An involuntary mental or physical bondage where attention or compulsive desire is captured by a focal object, contrasting with moderate interest or rational dedication.
groups.desc_zh: 心智或欲望被特定客体完全捕获并形成强制性沉溺，不同于适度兴趣或理性投入。
groups.nuance_en: obsess: involuntary, continual mental domination by an intrusive thought (detail / safety / ex) · fixate: direct pathologically rigid and exclusive attention toward one target (target / problem / idea) · addict: cause physiological or habitual dependence on a substance/activity (gamer / consumer / user) · infatuate: inspire foolish, irrational, short-lived passion (lover / crowd) · preoccupy: engross one's thoughts to the exclusion of other concerns (mind / thoughts)
groups.nuance_zh: obsess: 念头强迫性盘踞心头令其不得安宁 (detail / safety / ex) · fixate: 病态固着于单一目标无法转移 (target / problem / idea) · addict: 使在生理或心理上产生上瘾成瘾 (gamer / consumer / user) · infatuate: 使产生盲目痴狂的短暂迷恋 (lover / crowd) · preoccupy: 占据全副心神导致无暇他顾 (mind / thoughts)

groups.name: Flatten & Level · 找平与压平 (Flatten, Level, Grade)
groups.tip: 使表面平整消除凹凸

items.def_en: [I/T] to make or become even, horizontal, or smooth over a wider surface
items.ex_en: The steep mountain trail finally flattened out into a wide green meadow.
items.ex_zh: 陡峭的山路终于展平，延伸成一片宽阔的绿草甸。
items.ex2_en: The workers used a heavy roller to flatten out the bumpy new asphalt.
items.ex2_zh: 工人们用重型压路机压平了凹凸不平的新沥青路面。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a surface smooth and flat by removing wrinkles, bumps, or irregularities
items.ex_en: She carefully ironed out every stubborn crease on the silk tablecloth before dinner.
items.ex_zh: 开饭前，她仔细烫平了丝绸桌布上的每一道顽固褶皱。

items.def_zh: 使变平整，使成水平面；平稳
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a surface flat, smooth, and even, or to become flat
items.ex_en: Workers leveled out the gravel driveway before laying down the final asphalt layer.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在铺设最后的沥青层之前把碎石车道整平了。
items.ex2_en: The fluctuating stock market finally leveled out after months of intense economic volatility.
items.ex2_zh: 经过数月剧烈的经济波动，动荡的股市终于趋于平稳。

items.def_en: to level out a surface of land or earth with machinery to prepare for building or roadwork
items.ex_en: Heavy bulldozers graded the construction site to prepare it for building the highway.
items.ex_zh: 重型推土机平整了施工场地，为修建高速公路做好准备。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to flatten or make something smooth and uniform using a roller or heavy cylinder
items.ex_en: The baker rolled out the buttery dough into a uniform rectangular sheet.
items.ex_zh: 面包师用滚筒把黄油面团碾成均匀平整的长方形薄片。

items.def_zh: （使）平整，（使）平坦；（使）相等，（使）平均
items.def_en: 1. to make a surface flat, smooth, or level 2. to make amounts, scores, or conditions equal or balanced
items.ex_en: The gardener used a rake to even the soil before planting seeds.
items.ex_zh: 园丁在播种前用耙子将泥土整平。
items.ex2_en: The score evened dramatically in the final seconds of the thrilling basketball championship.
items.ex2_zh: 在扣人心弦的篮球决赛的最后几秒，比分戏剧性地被扳平了。

items.def_zh: 弄平，压平；夷平，彻底摧毁；使平等；瞄准，对准
items.def_en: 1. to make a surface flat, smooth, or horizontal 2. to destroy or knock down a building or structure completely 3. to aim a weapon or accusation directly at someone
items.ex_en: They leveled the ground thoroughly before pouring concrete for the new garage foundation.
items.ex_zh: 他们为新车库地基浇筑混凝土前，把地面彻底弄平整了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make something flat or flatter by pressing, rolling, or hitting it
items.ex_en: Use a heavy wooden mallet to flatten the chicken breasts before frying them.
items.ex_zh: 在煎鸡胸肉之前，用重木槌将其压平。
items.ex2_en: The dough flattened easily under the pressure of the heavy marble rolling pin.
items.ex2_zh: 在厚重的大理石擀面杖的压力下，面团很容易就变平了。

items.def_en: to level or compact a ground surface using a heavy roller
items.ex_en: The maintenance crew rollered the damaged cricket pitch after the heavy rainfall stopped.
items.ex_zh: 大雨停止后，养护人员用滚筒压平了受损的板球场地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe mechanically reducing surface irregularities, humps, or slopes to make ground or physical planes uniform and horizontal. Actions range from gentle grading to heavy compression.
groups.summary_zh: 通过机械刮削或强力压制使地表或物体表面平整、均匀。
groups.desc_en: Removing bumps, slants, or wrinkles to produce a uniform planar surface, contrasting with cutting down mass or inflating.
groups.desc_zh: 通过压平、铲除或抹匀去除凹凸与褶皱以获得平整表面，区别于削切体积或充气平整。
groups.nuance_en: flatten: make planar or reduce in thickness by pressure (curve / landscape / dough) · level: bring a surface into a horizontal or uniform plane (ground / field / playing field) · grade: mechanically smooth earth to an engineered slope or flat plane (road / slope / soil) · iron out: smooth creases physically, or resolve minor difficulties metaphorically (crease / wrinkle / difference) · roll out: spread flat and thin using a roller (dough / turf / carpet)
groups.nuance_zh: flatten: 施压使其变扁或变平 (curve / landscape / dough) · level: 铲平凸起使之呈统一水平面 (ground / field / playing field) · grade: 工程上平整地基或修整坡度 (road / slope / soil) · iron out: 熨平皱褶，比喻消除细微分歧 (crease / wrinkle / difference) · roll out: 用辊碾平展开 (dough / turf / carpet)

groups.name: Flirt & Entice · 挑逗与引诱 (Flirt, Lure, Coquet)
groups.tip: 轻佻言行挑逗吸引对方注意

items.def_en: (+ sb) to make romantic or sexual overtures to someone
items.ex_en: He tried to hit on the pretty bartender, but she completely ignored him.
items.ex_zh: 他试图向漂亮的调酒师搭讪挑逗，但对方完全没理他。

items.def_zh: 调情，打情骂俏；不严肃地考虑，玩弄
items.def_en: 1. To behave playfully toward someone you are attracted to, without serious intentions. 2. (flirt with) To consider or toy with an idea or possibility briefly.
items.ex_en: She liked to flirt with handsome strangers while waiting at the hotel bar.
items.ex_zh: 在酒店酒吧等候时，她喜欢和英俊的陌生人打情骂俏。

items.def_zh: 卖弄风情，虚情假意地挑逗
items.def_en: (+ with) to behave flirtatiously without sincere affection, often in a playful or teasing manner
items.ex_en: She loved to coquet with young officers at the ball using her lace fan.
items.ex_zh: 在舞会上，她喜欢用蕾丝折扇与年轻军官们玩弄风情、虚意示好。

items.def_zh: 吸引，诱使进入（圈套或行动）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to entice, lure, or entrap someone into a particular course of action or involvement
items.ex_en: The cunning sales pitch was designed to draw in unsuspecting first-time investors.
items.ex_zh: 那番巧妙的说辞旨在诱使毫无防备的初次投资者涉足其中。

items.def_zh: 诱导，挑逗引诱（给人虚假期望）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to encourage someone to expect a romantic relationship or outcome, usually falsely or deceitfully
items.ex_en: It was cruel of him to lead her on when he never loved her.
items.ex_zh: 他根本不爱她却一直挑逗引诱给她希望，这太残忍了。

items.def_en: To persuade or tempt someone to go somewhere or do something by offering them something attractive.
items.ex_en: They placed fragrant bait inside the wooden trap to lure the hungry raccoons.
items.ex_zh: 他们在木制陷阱里放置了香喷喷的诱饵，以引诱饥饿的浣熊。

items.def_zh: 诱使，引诱（通常伴有利益或吸引力）
items.def_en: to attract or tempt someone by offering pleasure, reward, or advantage
