items.ex_en: Economists often postulate on the fundamental rational behavior of market participants.
items.ex_zh: 经济学家经常基于市场参与者的基本理性行为做出理论假设。

items.def_zh: 假定，假设；提出（观点、理论）
items.def_en: to suggest or accept that something is true, especially as the basis for a theory or argument
items.ex_en: Modern sociologists posit that rapid urbanization drastically alters traditional family structures.
items.ex_zh: 现代社会学家假定，快速的城市化从根本上改变了传统家庭结构。

items.def_zh: 使基于，使以…为前提；断定，断言
items.def_en: 1. (usually be predicated on/upon) to base an idea, action, or statement on a particular assumption or fact. 2. to state or assert that something has a particular quality or property
items.ex_en: The prosecution's entire argument was predicated upon questionable testimony from an unreliable witness.
items.ex_zh: 检方的全部论据都建立在一个不可靠证人可疑的证词之上。

items.def_en: to suggest or assume the existence, fact, or truth of something as a basis for reasoning
items.ex_en: Ancient mathematicians would postulate basic truths before constructing their complex geometric proofs.
items.ex_zh: 古代数学家在构建复杂的几何证明之前，都会先假定基本公理。

items.def_zh: 使公理化，定为不证自明的公理
items.def_en: to reduce to or formulate into fundamental self-evident axioms
items.ex_en: Theoretical physicists attempt to axiomize the fundamental laws governing the quantum universe.
items.ex_zh: 理论物理学家试图将支配量子宇宙的基本规律公理化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve laying down a hypothesis, premise, or axiomatic assumption as the theoretical basis for an argument or theory. They differ along an intensity scale from tentative conjecture to fundamental structural axiom.
groups.summary_zh: 指设定理论假设、公理或将某命题作为论证前提，强度由初步推断递增至基石确立。
groups.desc_en: Covers laying down theoretical axioms, starting assumptions, or speculative frameworks that serve as the foundation for deductive reasoning, contrasting with ungrounded 'guess' through epistemological rigor.
groups.desc_zh: 指在认识论中确立理论公理、基础前设或推论框架，与随意的“猜测”不同，强调作为逻辑推导根基的建构性与假定性。
groups.nuance_en: hypothesize: proposing a tentative, empirically testable explanation (cause / mechanism / outcome) · postulate: demanding the acceptance of a fundamental premise without proof to build theory (axiom / existence / theory) · posit: putting forward a concept or factual claim as a firm basis for argument (correlation / idea / framework) · predicate: basing an assertion or system wholly upon a prior founding condition (policy / claim / argument) · presuppose: logically requiring an unstated antecedent condition to be valid (truth / innocence / existence)
groups.nuance_zh: hypothesize: 提出供实证检验的假说性解释 (cause / mechanism / outcome) · postulate: 要求承认无需自明的基本公理以推展理论体系 (axiom / existence / theory) · posit: 确立某一事实主张作为论辩基石 (correlation / idea / framework) · predicate: 使论断或政策全盘基于某一先决前提 (policy / claim / argument) · presuppose: 在逻辑上预设、假定某一隐蔽前设成立 (truth / innocence / existence)

groups.name: Idealize & Fantasize · 理想化设想与空想 (Fantasize, Glamorize, Glamourize)
groups.tip: 赋予过分美好的想象滤镜

items.def_zh: （dream的过去式及过去分词）梦见；梦想，幻想
items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British) Past tense and past participle of dream: to experience thoughts or images while asleep, or to imagine something desired.
items.ex_en: As a boy in Manchester, he often dreamt of becoming a renowned concert pianist.
items.ex_zh: 小时候在曼彻斯特，他经常梦想成为一名著名的音乐会钢琴家。

items.def_en: 1. (+ about) To spend time thinking pleasant, imaginative thoughts about things you wish would happen while awake.
items.ex_en: Bored during the lecture, she began to daydream about escaping to tropical beaches.
items.ex_zh: 听讲座感到无聊时，她开始做白日梦，幻想逃去热带海滩。

items.def_en: entertain daydreamy, extravagant, and impractical fantasies
items.ex_en: Instead of seeking honest employment, the idle youth preferred to build castles in the air.
items.ex_zh: 这个游手好闲的青年不肯去找份正经工作，反倒宁愿想入非非。

items.def_en: (+ sth) unrealistically desire that an unpleasant reality simply cease to exist
items.ex_en: The minister knew that citizens could not simply wish away the deepening financial crisis.
items.ex_zh: 这位部长深知，公民不可能仅凭空幻想就能化解日趋恶化的金融危机。

items.def_en: 1. To imagine or view something as a future possibility or desirable outcome.
items.ex_en: Urban planners envisage a carbon-neutral city center within the next two decades.
items.ex_zh: 城市规划者设想在未来二十年内打造一个碳中和的市中心。

items.def_en: (+ about) to indulge in elaborate daydreams about desirable but unlikely events
items.ex_en: He would regularly fantasize about inheriting a fortune and traveling the world indefinitely.
items.ex_zh: 他经常沉溺于继承巨额财富并无限期环游世界的空想之中。

items.raw_cluster: 理想化与美化 Idealize & Romanticize
items.def_zh: 把……理想化，将……想象得十全十美
items.def_en: 1. To regard or represent someone or something as far better or more perfect than they really are.
items.ex_en: Biographers often caution readers not to idealize historical figures beyond human reality.
items.ex_zh: 传记作者常告诫读者，切勿将历史人物脱离人性现实地过分理想化。

items.raw_cluster: 理想化与美化 Idealize & Romanticize
items.def_zh: （使）浪漫化，把……想象得富有传奇色彩（或过于美妙）
items.def_en: 1. To talk or think about something in a way that makes it seem more exciting, heroic, or attractive than it really is.
items.ex_en: Hollywood films frequently romanticize the perilous, lonely lifestyle of outlaw gangsters.
items.ex_zh: 好莱坞电影经常将法外狂徒凶险孤独的生活方式浪漫化。

items.def_zh: 将……美化，使显得光鲜迷人
items.def_en: to portray or think of something as more attractive and exciting than it really is
items.ex_en: Media outlets should never glamorize dangerous illicit street racing to impress impressionable youths.
items.ex_zh: 媒体绝不应美化危险的非法街头飙车，来吸引缺乏判断力的年轻人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote cognitive processes where someone projects exaggeratedly desirable, unrealistic, or romanticized scenarios rather than objectively projecting feasibility.
groups.summary_zh: 带有主观滤镜地空想或构想，将事物想象得比实际更完美、浪漫或脱离现实。
groups.desc_en: Reflects viewing reality through wishful, utopian, or glamorizing lenses that filter out flaws, differing from pragmatic 'plan' through subjective embellishment or escapist detachment.
groups.desc_zh: 反映透过一厢情愿、乌托邦或美化滤镜打量现实并过滤缺陷，与实事求是的“规划”不同，带有主观粉饰或逃避现实的脱离感。
groups.nuance_en: idealize: projecting perfection onto an entity while blinding oneself to real defects (past / partner / leader) · romanticize: infusing mundane, harsh, or gritty reality with heroic or sentimental allure (poverty / struggle / war) · fantasize: indulging in vivid, unrealistic daydream scenarios detached from reality (wealth / escape / success) · daydream: drifting into idle, unfocused reverie while awake (future / possibilities / scene) · envisage: conceiving a structured, forward-looking mental vision of possible events (growth / plan / future)
groups.nuance_zh: idealize: 投射完美光环，彻底美化对象并无视缺陷 (past / partner / leader) · romanticize: 将苦难、战争等残酷现实染上英雄或浪漫色彩 (poverty / struggle / war) · fantasize: 沉溺于脱离现实的狂野白日梦 (wealth / escape / success) · daydream: 在白昼间游离出神、漫无边际地空想 (future / possibilities / scene) · envisage: 展望并设想未来可能实现的良性愿景 (growth / plan / future)

groups.name: Identify & Recognize · 识别与辨认 (Distinguish, Discern, Spot)
groups.tip: 辨明特征认出对象

items.def_en: to see, notice, or identify someone or something, often when they are hard to perceive
items.ex_en: The vigilant ranger managed to spot a camouflaged sniper among the dense trees.
items.ex_zh: 警惕的巡警在茂密的树林中认出了一名经过伪装的狙击手。

items.def_zh: 识别，认出，辨认；查明，确定；认同，感同身受
items.def_en: 1. To recognize someone or something and state or prove who or what they are. 2. To find or discover the identity or presence of something. 3. (+ with) To feel that you understand and share the feelings or experiences of someone.
items.ex_en: Forensic experts worked meticulously to identify the unknown remains recovered from the site.
items.ex_zh: 法医专家严谨细致地工作，以查明从现场收敛的无名遗骸身份。

items.def_zh: 认出，辨出；承认，认可；表彰，赏识
items.def_en: 1. To identify someone or something because you have seen, heard, or experienced them before. 2. To accept, acknowledge, or realize the existence or truth of something. 3. To officially acknowledge or praise someone for their achievements or service.
items.ex_en: Even across the crowded terminal, she could easily recognize her brother's distinctive gait.
items.ex_zh: 即便隔着拥挤的航站楼，她也能一眼认出弟弟那独特的步态。

items.def_en: to recognize the difference between two people or things, or discern something with the senses
items.ex_en: Trained perfumers can distinguish subtle floral undertones that an untrained nose completely misses.
items.ex_zh: 训练有素的调香师能辨别出未经训练的鼻子完全错过的微妙花香。

items.def_en: to recognize and select a specific person or thing from a group
items.ex_en: The victim was able to pick out the attacker from a lineup of suspects.
items.ex_zh: 受害者能够从一排嫌疑人中指认出袭击者。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Discern or distinguish someone or something with difficulty through sensory input
items.ex_en: Through the heavy fog, the lookout could barely make out the distant shoreline.
items.ex_zh: 透过浓重的迷雾，瞭望员只能勉强辨认出远处的海岸线。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Identify or choose someone or something distinctively from a larger group
items.ex_en: It is unfair to single out one player when the whole team performed poorly.
items.ex_zh: 在全队表现都很差的情况下，单单挑出一名球员来责备是不公平的。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Recognize the difference between two or more similar people or things
items.ex_en: The twins look so similar that even their teachers can hardly tell them apart.
items.ex_zh: 这对双胞胎长得太像了，连他们的老师都很难分清。

items.def_en: to perceive, recognize, or distinguish something with difficulty or keen intellect
items.ex_en: An experienced collector can quickly discern an authentic antique from a clever replica.
items.ex_zh: 一位经验丰富的收藏家能迅速辨清真正的古董与高仿复制品。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe cognitively matching sensory input against previous familiarity to determine identity, class, or individual distinctiveness.
groups.summary_zh: 指调取既有认知经验对所见所闻进行辨析，确认其具体身份或类别属性。
groups.desc_en: Captures cognitive operations that detect sensory signals, isolate unique identities, or match targets against existing memory traces, distinguishing itself from general 'see' through analytical discernment.
groups.desc_zh: 捕捉感官搜寻、特征比对并将目标与已知认知印记进行匹配的辨析过程，与泛泛的“看”不同，强调细微辨识与确认判断。
groups.nuance_en: identify: establishing exact identity or naming an observed entity definitively (victim / cause / species) · recognize: acknowledging someone or something known previously from stored memory (face / voice / handwriting) · spot: noticing and locating a faint, concealed, or fleeting target visually (flaw / trend / bird) · distinguish: separating an entity from its surrounding environment or cohort by differentiating features (features / twins / right from wrong) · make out: discerning an indistinct or obscure target with perceptual difficulty (shape / writing / figure)
groups.nuance_zh: identify: 查明并确认确切身份、名称或根源 (victim / cause / species) · recognize: 从记忆库存中辨认出曾结识的面孔或声音 (face / voice / handwriting) · spot: 敏锐搜寻并察觉微小、隐藏或转瞬即逝的目标 (flaw / trend / bird) · distinguish: 依据特征差异将混淆对象或实体分清辨明 (features / twins / right from wrong) · make out: 极度吃力地看清或听出模糊不明的对象 (shape / writing / figure)

groups.name: Imitate & Emulate · 模仿与效法 (Mimic, Ape, Emulate)
groups.tip: 照葫芦画瓢地模仿学样

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Mimic someone or something humorously or satirically to ridicule them
items.ex_en: The comedy troupe loved to send up self-important politicians during their weekly broadcasts.
items.ex_zh: 这个喜剧剧团喜欢在每周播出的节目中滑稽戏弄自命不凡的政客。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Mimic someone's voice, accent, or mannerisms for entertainment or humor
items.ex_en: The comedian can take off the prime minister's nasal accent with astonishing accuracy.
items.ex_zh: 这位喜剧演员能以惊人的准确度模仿首相那带着鼻音的腔调。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Represent or imitate actions, scenes, or characters through performance
items.ex_en: Drama students gathered on the lawn to act out dramatic scenes from classic tragedies.
items.ex_zh: 戏剧系的学生们聚集在草坪上，模仿表演经典悲剧中的戏剧性场景。

items.def_en: to imitate somebody or something unkindly in order to make them look ridiculous
items.ex_en: Cruel schoolyard bullies loved to mock the stuttering child during morning recess.
items.ex_zh: 课间休息时，残酷的校园恶霸们总喜欢嘲讽性地模仿那个结巴的孩子。

items.def_en: to deliberately copy the style of a person, artist, or work in an exaggerated, comic way
items.ex_en: The clever satirist chose to parody Victorian melodrama in his latest comedic novel.
items.ex_zh: 这位聪明的讽刺作家在最新的喜剧小说中戏仿了维多利亚时期的通俗剧风格。

items.def_en: 1. To copy the way someone speaks, moves, or behaves, especially to entertain or ridicule. 2. To resemble or imitate something closely.
items.ex_en: The parrot could skillfully mimic the telephone ring, constantly confusing the elderly homeowner.
items.ex_zh: 那只鹦鹉能逼真地模仿电话铃声，总是把那位上了年纪的房主搞糊涂。

items.def_en: 1. To copy someone's behavior, style, or speech, especially clumsily or uncritically.
items.ex_en: Amateur painters often merely ape the stylistic quirks of great Renaissance masters.
items.ex_zh: 业余画家往往只是在笨拙地盲目模仿文艺复兴大师们的风格技巧。

items.def_en: to copy the speech, gestures, or actions of somebody, often naturally or as a model
items.ex_en: Young children naturally imitate the speech patterns and mannerisms of their primary caregivers.
items.ex_zh: 幼儿会自然而然地模仿他们主要抚养人的说话方式和言行举止。

items.def_en: to try to equal or excel somebody, especially by admiring and copying their achievements
items.ex_en: The young scholar strove earnestly to emulate the moral virtues of her mentor.
items.ex_zh: 这位青年学者竭力效法导师的高尚品德，以期与之比肩。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote copying another person's speech, gestures, behavior, or style, differentiating between admiring emulation, literal copying, and mocking caricature.
groups.summary_zh: 指模仿、仿效或滑稽模仿他人的言谈举止或行为风格。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses copying the behaviors, aesthetics, or gestures of another—spanning satirical, derogatory caricature to faithful creative replication—contrasting with spontaneous 'act' by existing as a derivative copy.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖复制模仿他人的行为、风骨或举止（从尖刻的滑稽模仿到忠实的效法），与自发的“行动”不同，其本质具有派生复制性。
groups.nuance_en: imitate: copying actions, manners, or styling as a model or learning device (accent / master / behavior) · mimic: reproducing vocal nuances or mannerisms with precise, uncanny fidelity (voice / gestures / birdsong) · ape: clumsily, mindlessly, or pretentiously copying superior manners (aristocracy / culture / elite) · mock: imitating derisively in order to scorn, demean, or ridicule (accent / gait / plea) · parody: exaggerating stylistic quirks comically in literature or art (style / song / genre)
groups.nuance_zh: imitate: 以特定对象为样板照搬学习其外表或言行 (accent / master / behavior) · mimic: 惟妙惟肖、活灵活现地模仿发音或习惯小动作 (voice / gestures / birdsong) · ape: 拙劣、东施效颦或附庸风雅地机械抄袭 (aristocracy / culture / elite) · mock: 恶意学样以示取笑、奚落与嘲讽 (accent / gait / plea) · parody: 夸张抓取原作风格与怪癖进行戏仿与讽刺重构 (style / song / genre)

groups.name: Impart & Inculcate · 传授与灌输 (Instill, Inculcate, Impart)
groups.tip: 循序渐进地传授思想观点

items.def_en: (+ sth to sb) to give or impart knowledge, skills, or advice to the next person or generation
items.ex_en: Elders gathered each winter to pass on ancient oral traditions to the youth.
items.ex_zh: 长辈们每年冬天聚在一起，将古老的口头传统传授给年轻人。

items.def_en: (+ into/with) fill or soak someone or something with a particular quality or spirit
items.ex_en: The charismatic coach sought to infuse unyielding confidence into his demoralized team.
items.ex_zh: 这位极具魅力的教练试图将坚定不移的信心注入士气低落的队伍中。

items.def_zh: 传授，告知，传达；赋予，增添
items.def_en: (+ to) 1. to pass information, knowledge, or wisdom to others. 2. to give a particular quality or taste to something.
items.ex_en: The venerable professor dedicated his life to impart profound wisdom to eager students.
items.ex_zh: 这位德高望重的教授倾注一生，向求知若渴的学生传授博大智慧。

items.def_zh: 逐步灌输，传授（思想、原则等）；滴注
items.def_en: 1. (+ in/into) To gradually put a feeling, idea, or principle into someone's mind so that it becomes firmly established. 2. (medical) To put a liquid into something drop by drop.
items.ex_en: Good parents endeavor to instill enduring principles of empathy into their growing children.
items.ex_zh: 优秀的父母致力于向成长中的孩子逐步灌输恒久的同理心原则。

items.def_en: (+ with) inspire or permeate someone with a feeling, value, or quality
items.ex_en: The maestro managed to imbue the orchestra's performance with deep emotional melancholy.
items.ex_zh: 指挥家成功地让管弦乐队的演奏浸染上浓郁深沉的情感忧伤。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to teach something to someone through rigorous, continuous repetition
items.ex_en: Military instructors work relentlessly to drill discipline into every fresh squad of recruits.
items.ex_zh: 军事教官夜以继日地通过反复操练，把纪律强行灌输给每一批新兵。

items.def_en: (+ sth into sb) to instill an idea, principle, or fact in someone by constant repetition
items.ex_en: Our strict arithmetic teacher tried to drum multiplication tables into our heads daily.
items.ex_zh: 我们严厉的算术老师每天都试图把乘法表硬生生地反复灌输进我们脑子里。

items.def_en: (+ into) instruct someone in something by rigid, repetitive exercise or discipline
items.ex_en: The academy continues to drill strict safety regulations into new recruits each term.
items.ex_zh: 该学院每个学期都继续通过反复机械训导，将严格的安全规程灌输给新学员。

items.def_en: (+ in/into) instill an attitude, idea, or habit by persistent instruction
items.ex_en: The school curriculum aims to inculcate democratic values into impressionable young minds.
items.ex_zh: 该校课程旨在通过谆谆教诲将民主价值观深植于年轻人的心灵中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote passing knowledge, qualities, or principles to someone, ranging from generous sharing to deep, repetitive cognitive conditioning.
groups.summary_zh: 将知识、品质或信念传递、逐步灌输给他人并使其内化。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately transmitting knowledge, values, or qualities into someone's mind or character, contrasting with neutral 'teach' through sustained gradual absorption, pervasive saturation, or coercive repetition.
groups.desc_zh: 指将知识、价值观或特质刻意植入受众心智或品格中，区别于普通中性的“教授/告知”，强调潜移默化的渗透浸染或高压强制的重复灌输。
groups.nuance_en: impart: bestow knowledge or a subtle quality authoritatively (wisdom / flavor / information) · instill: gradually introduce a guiding principle or feeling drop by drop (values / discipline / confidence) · imbue: deeply saturate someone or something with a pervasive spirit or quality (spirit / mind / culture) · inculcate: impress persistently through earnest, repeated teaching (principles / habits / virtues) · drum into: forcibly hammer into someone by relentless drilling (facts / rules / dates)
groups.nuance_zh: impart: 郑重传授知识或赋予某种微妙质感 (wisdom / flavor / information) · instill: 润物无声般逐渐灌输思想或准则 (values / discipline / confidence) · imbue: 使通体浸润、深深浸染某种精神或特质 (spirit / mind / culture) · inculcate: 循循善诱、反复向人谆谆灌输品格信念 (principles / habits / virtues) · drum into: 强行、机械地将信息死记硬背敲入脑中 (facts / rules / dates)

groups.name: Improvise & Cobble Together · 即兴创制与临时拼凑 (Improvise, Extemporize, Cobble)
groups.tip: 未加准备当场构思创造

items.def_en: to make or assemble something quickly and roughly from whatever parts are available
items.ex_en: We managed to cobble together a temporary soundstage using discarded timber and tarps.
items.ex_zh: 我们用废弃的木料和防水布胡乱拼凑出了一个临时舞台。

items.def_en: (+ sth) quickly find, gather, or prepare something, especially food or resources, at short notice
items.ex_en: When unexpected guests arrived, she rushed inside to rustle up some hot supper.
items.ex_zh: 当意想不到的客人登门时，她急忙赶进厨房张罗弄了些热腾腾的晚饭。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make up lines, words, or actions on the spot in a performance or speech
items.ex_en: When the prompter failed, the comedian had to ad-lib the entire opening monologue.
items.ex_zh: 当提词器发生故障时，这位喜剧演员不得不即兴发挥说完全部开场白。

items.def_en: (+ sth) construct or assemble something roughly and hurriedly using whatever materials are available
items.ex_en: The workers managed to knock together a functional shelter before the storm struck.
items.ex_zh: 工人们赶在暴风雨来袭前匆匆搭起了一座能避雨的简易庇护所。

items.def_en: (+ sth) make, assemble, or arrange something hastily without much care or planning
items.ex_en: With little time to prepare, the committee could only throw together a hasty proposal.
items.ex_zh: 由于几乎没有准备时间，委员会只能草草拼凑出一份仓促的提案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) produce or prepare something very quickly, especially a meal or improvised solution
items.ex_en: She managed to whip up a delicious pasta dinner in just fifteen minutes.
items.ex_zh: 她只用了短短十五分钟就匆匆做成了一顿美味的意大利面晚餐。

items.def_en: [I/T] to speak, perform, or compose music without any prior preparation or script
items.ex_en: The brilliant orator could extemporize convincingly on complex geopolitical topics without any notes.
items.ex_zh: 这位卓越的演说家能在没有任何讲稿的情况下，就复杂的先当地缘政治议题侃侃而谈。

items.raw_cluster: 即兴创作与发挥 Improvise & Extemporize
items.def_zh: 即兴创作，即兴表演；临时凑合，临时做
items.def_en: 1. (variant spelling of improvise) To perform or create spontaneously without preparation, or make something from whatever is at hand.
items.ex_en: Stranded in the wilderness, the campers had to improvize a sturdy stretcher from branches.
items.ex_zh: 被困在荒野中，露营者们不得不临时用树枝凑合做出一副结实的担架。

items.def_zh: 临时拼凑应急装置，权宜搭建
items.def_en: to build or repair something in a makeshift way using whatever materials are accessible
items.ex_en: The stranded mechanic had to jury-rig a broken fuel line with copper wire.
items.ex_zh: 抛锚的修理工不得不用铜线权宜搭建修补破损的燃油管。

groups.summary_en: A creator devises, performs, or constructs something spontaneously without prior preparation, often utilizing whatever rudimentary materials or ideas are at hand.
groups.summary_zh: 无事先准备、随手利用现有材料或灵感临时创制或拼凑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes hastily inventing, composing, or assembling something without preparation using whatever materials or words are at hand, contrasting with planned 'construct' or rehearsed 'perform'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在毫无准备或缺乏正规材料的情况下就地取材、仓促拼凑或即兴创作，区别于预先规划的“构建”或排练过的“表演”。
groups.nuance_en: improvise: invent or create spur-of-the-moment solutions or performance without preparation (speech / melody / solution) · extemporize: deliver a speech or musical piece fluently without notes (solos / remarks / address) · cobble together: quickly assemble a makeshift functional whole from ill-fitting scraps (coalition / agreement / prototype) · whip up: quickly and effortlessly produce food or enthusiasm as if by magic (meal / dessert / excitement) · throw together: crudely and hastily assemble with minimal care (outfit / meal / report)
groups.nuance_zh: improvise: 毫无预备、根据现场情境即兴发挥或因陋就简解决 (speech / melody / solution) · extemporize: 不看讲稿或乐谱即席口若悬河地演讲或演奏 (solos / remarks / address) · cobble together: 粗制滥造地将零碎杂乱材料临时拼凑成形 (coalition / agreement / prototype) · whip up: 娴熟而迅速地张罗出饭菜或煽动起情绪 (meal / dessert / excitement) · throw together: 极度匆忙潦草地拼凑或搭配 (outfit / meal / report)

groups.name: Incarcerate & Confine · 监禁与拘押 (Imprison, Incarcerate, Confine)
groups.tip: 剥夺人身自由强制关押

items.def_en: To put or confine someone in prison or jail.
items.ex_en: The corrupt magistrate decided to jail the notorious fraudster for three long years.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的地方法官决定将臭名昭著的诈骗犯关进监狱三年。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to put someone in a prison, jail, or secure psychiatric facility
items.ex_en: Authorities had to lock up the violent offender in a maximum security facility.
items.ex_zh: 当局不得不将这名暴力罪犯关押在最高戒备设施中。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to confine someone securely in a place where they have little contact with others
items.ex_en: Her cruel family resolved to shut away the troubled girl in an attic.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的家人决定把这个受困扰的女孩关在阁楼里，与外界隔绝。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to confine a person or animal in a tight, restricted space
items.ex_en: They pen up the aggressive guard dogs in that tiny shed every morning.
items.ex_zh: 他们每天早上都把凶猛的看门狗圈禁在那个小棚屋里。

items.def_en: (+ to) to keep someone closed in a place, such as a cell or room, preventing departure
items.ex_en: The strict disciplinary code allowed officers to confine the rebellious inmate to solitary.
items.ex_zh: 严格的纪律条例允许警官将叛逆的囚犯禁闭在单独囚室中。

items.def_en: to officially keep someone in custody or prevent them from leaving
items.ex_en: Customs officials may lawfully detain any suspicious traveler for prolonged questioning upon entry.
items.ex_zh: 海关官员在入境时可依法拘留任何可疑旅客以进行长时间盘问。

items.def_en: to put someone in prison, or keep someone in a place they cannot escape from
items.ex_en: The military tribunal sentenced the defecting commander to imprison him without parole.
items.ex_zh: 军事法庭判处监禁这名叛变指挥官，且不得假释。

items.def_zh: 关押，监禁（法律正式用语）
items.def_en: (formal) to confine or imprison someone by legal or penal process
items.ex_en: The federal court decided to incarcerate the white-collar criminal in a penitentiary.
items.ex_zh: 联邦法院裁定将这面白领罪犯关押进监狱。

items.def_zh: 关押，把……关在狭小空间（pen 的过去式及过去分词，常作 pent up）
items.def_en: (archaic or literary, past tense and past participle of pen) To confine or shut up closely in a small space.
items.ex_en: For months the captive bird remained pent within the gilded iron cage.
items.ex_zh: 数月以来，这只被俘获的鸟儿一直被关在那镀金的铁笼之中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to detaining an individual or animal by judicial authority or physical restraint, restricting them to a prison, cell, or enclosed space. 'Jail' is direct and everyday, whereas 'incarcerate' is formal and judicial, and 'pent' (often archaic or participial as 'pent up') highlights close enclosure.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过司法制裁或物理禁锢手段将人限制于牢狱或狭小封闭空间内。
groups.desc_en: Denotes depriving a person or creature of physical liberty by locking them within restricted legal, carceral, or physical confines, contrasting with simple 'hold' or 'restrain'.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过司法制裁或物理禁锢剥夺人身自由，将其关押封闭在特定受限空间内，区别于单纯暂时的“控制”或“约束”。
groups.nuance_en: imprison: deprive of liberty legally by placing in a penal institution (offenders / dissidents / criminals) · incarcerate: formal, institutional lockup emphasizing total systemic custody (inmates / felons / convicts) · confine: restrict physically to a bounded space or room (patients / prisoners / movements) · detain: hold someone in official custody temporarily pending investigation (suspects / travelers / asylum-seekers) · lock up: colloquial, absolute physical confinement behind barred doors (criminals / valuables / suspects)
groups.nuance_zh: imprison: 依法判处入狱关押剥夺自由 (offenders / dissidents / criminals) · incarcerate: 正式且制度化的高墙监禁，强调失去自由的绝对状态 (inmates / felons / convicts) · confine: 物理性限制在狭小空间或特定处所内不得外出 (patients / prisoners / movements) · detain: 执法部门在调查或起诉前实施官方拘留、留置 (suspects / travelers / asylum-seekers) · lock up: 口语化强调上锁关入牢房或密室 (criminals / valuables / suspects)

groups.name: Indecisive Hesitation & Vacillation · 优柔寡断与摇摆不定 (Hesitate, Dither, Vacillate)
groups.tip: 摇摆不定迟迟难下决断

items.def_en: to intentionally delay doing or deciding something due to uncertainty
items.ex_en: Let's hold off on signing the contract until the market conditions improve slightly.
items.ex_zh: 咱们先别忙着签合同，等市场行情稍微好转再说。

items.def_en: 1. (+ about/over) To pause before doing or saying something because of uncertainty, doubt, or nervousness.
items.ex_en: Do not hesitate over accepting the offer, as opportunities like this vanish quickly.
items.ex_zh: 不要对接受这份工作犹豫不决，因为这样的机会稍纵即逝。

items.def_zh: 犹豫不决，畏首畏尾，回避决断；蹑手蹑脚地走
items.def_en: (also 'pussyfoot around') To act or speak with extreme hesitation or caution so as to avoid taking a firm stand or making a commitment.
items.ex_en: Stop pussyfooting around the issue and tell us your final decision right now.
items.ex_zh: 别再就这个问题畏首畏尾了，现在就告诉我们你的最终决定。

items.def_en: to waver repeatedly between two choices or opinions without deciding
items.ex_en: He went back and forth between the two lucrative offers before finally deciding.
items.ex_zh: 在最终做出决定之前，他在两份诱人的录用通知之间来回摇摆。

items.def_en: to hesitate and spend a long time deciding before making a choice or giving an answer
items.ex_en: The manager continued to hum and haw instead of approving the urgent budget.
items.ex_zh: 经理吞吞吐吐、犹豫不决，迟迟不肯批准那笔紧急预算。

items.def_en: to become unsteady or show indecision between choices
items.ex_en: The diplomat began to waver between upholding national duty and preserving personal honor.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官开始在履行国家职责与维护个人声誉之间摇摆不定。

items.def_zh: 犹豫不决，摇摆不定；发抖，慌乱
items.def_en: 1. (+ over/about) To hesitate, vacillate, and waste time because you cannot make up your mind.
items.ex_en: She spent the whole afternoon dithering over which evening gown to purchase.
items.ex_zh: 她整个下午都在为买哪件晚礼服而犹豫不决、浪费时间。

items.def_en: (+ between) to waver repeatedly between different opinions or courses of action
items.ex_en: Ministers vacillate between enforcing strict quarantine regulations and reopening the national economy.
items.ex_zh: 部长们在执行严格的隔离规定与重启国家经济之间摇摆不定。

items.def_en: to fail to act and waste time through continual indecision
items.ex_en: If you continue to shilly-shally, the entire venture will slip through our fingers.
items.ex_zh: 如果你继续这么优柔寡断地磨蹭，整个项目机会就会溜走。

groups.summary_en: An agent delays making a choice, changes their mind repeatedly, or engages in timid evasion due to uncertainty, conflicting feelings, or lack of resolve.
groups.summary_zh: 指因拿不定主意、畏缩或反复权衡而踌躇不前、摇摆推诿。
groups.desc_en: Denotes lingering in unresolved psychological hesitation and shifting between competing choices instead of acting, contrasting with purposeful 'ponder' or final 'refuse'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在多个选项间反复摇摆、心神不定而迟迟无法做出决断，区别于深思熟虑的“斟酌”或明确坚决的“拒绝”。
groups.nuance_en: hesitate: momentarily pause before action due to doubt or reluctance (response / second / decision) · vacillate: repeatedly swing between mutually contradictory opinions or courses (positions / policies / loyalties) · dither: waste time fussing indecisively without purpose (about details / endlessly / over choices) · waver: show sudden unsteady flickering in resolve or conviction (resolve / faith / commitment) · hum and haw: verbally stall and hem and haw to evade committing (politicians / witnesses / spokespersons)
groups.nuance_zh: hesitate: 因心存疑虑或顾忌而出现短暂的迟疑或停顿 (response / second / decision) · vacillate: 在截然相反的立场、主张间大幅度左右摇摆 (positions / policies / loyalties) · dither: 焦虑琐碎、六神无主地瞎耽误工夫且拿不定主意 (about details / endlessly / over choices) · waver: 原本坚定的决心、信念出现动摇不稳的苗头 (resolve / faith / commitment) · hum and haw: 吞吞吐吐、支支吾吾地推脱拖延表态 (politicians / witnesses / spokespersons)

groups.name: Inflict Harm & Abuse · 苛待与虐待 (Wrong, Mistreat, Abuse)
groups.tip: 不公对待直至残暴虐待

items.def_en: (+ sb) to bully, intimidate, or mistreat someone unfairly
items.ex_en: Don't let them push you around; you have rights as a tenant.
items.ex_zh: 别让他们摆布你；作为租客你也是有权利的。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to treat someone with physical violence to intimidate or harm them
items.ex_en: Two masked thugs tried to rough up the witness outside the courtroom yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 昨天两个蒙面暴徒试图在法庭外对证人动粗施暴。

items.def_en: To treat someone unfairly or unjustly.
items.ex_en: The upright minister vowed never to wrong innocent citizens for political expediency.
items.ex_zh: 这位正直的部长誓决不为了政治便利而冤枉无辜百姓。

items.def_en: To treat a person or animal in a cruel, unfair, or bad way.
items.ex_en: Local authorities intervened when the cruel owner began to mistreat his domestic animals.
items.ex_zh: 当这个残忍的主人开始虐待家畜时，地方当局介入了。

items.def_en: to treat a person or animal cruelly, roughly, or violently
items.ex_en: The international convention prohibits wardens who deliberately maltreat prisoners of war during captivity.
items.ex_zh: 国际公约严禁看守在战俘被拘禁期间对其蓄意虐待。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to hurt someone severely by repeatedly hitting or kicking them
items.ex_en: Don't beat yourself up over an honest mistake.
items.ex_zh: 不要因为一次无心之失而过度自责。

items.def_en: to treat someone with repeated cruelty, violence, or exploitation
items.ex_en: The tyrannical landlord continued to abuse vulnerable tenants through intimidation and illegal fines.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的房东继续通过恐吓和非法罚款来虐待弱势租户。

items.def_en: to deliberately single someone out for cruel or unjust treatment
items.ex_en: Corrupt senior supervisors routinely victimize junior employees who dare challenge company misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的高级主管经常打击迫害敢于质疑公司不端行为的初级员工。

items.def_en: to treat someone with extreme savage violence and cruelty
items.ex_en: Merciless guards would brutalize defenseless captives inside the squalid internment camp daily.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的警卫每天都在肮脏的集中营里野蛮残害手无寸铁的被囚者。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe subjecting a person or animal to unjust, cruel, or damaging behavior, scaling from moral injustice and neglectful mistreatment to violent, dehumanizing abuse.
groups.summary_zh: 按侵犯严重程度递增描述对人或动物的不公对待、虐待与摧残。
groups.desc_en: Denotes intentionally subjecting someone or something to physical violence, systemic cruelty, or wrongful harm, contrasting with accidental 'injure' or minor 'displease'.
groups.desc_zh: 指故意对人或动物施加肉体暴力、系统性残酷虐待或不公正侵害，区别于无意的“伤害”或轻微的“怠慢”。
groups.nuance_en: abuse: inflict sustained physical, psychological, or sexual mistreatment (power / children / victims) · maltreat: treat physically roughly or cruelly out of neglect or brutality (prisoners / animals / patients) · victimize: target maliciously to make someone suffer unfairly (whistleblowers / minorities / targets) · rough up: physically assault someone to intimidate or bully (suspects / debtors / rivals) · wrong: commit an ethical or legal injustice against someone (innocents / partners / friends)
groups.nuance_zh: abuse: 长期、系统性地滥用控制力进行身心虐待或侵害 (power / children / victims) · maltreat: 粗暴、残忍地虐待或怠慢照顾对象 (prisoners / animals / patients) · victimize: 针对性地将其当做受害者予以迫害、欺侮或做替罪羊 (whistleblowers / minorities / targets) · rough up: 动用拳脚进行肉体恐吓或毒打教训 (suspects / debtors / rivals) · wrong: 在道德或法律上予以不公正对待、委屈冤枉 (innocents / partners / friends)

groups.name: Inflict Psychological Torment · 精神折磨与创伤 (Torment, Torture, Traumatize)
groups.tip: 从轻微刺痛升级为深重心理创伤

items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause progressive, continuous mental distress or torment to someone over time
items.ex_en: The unresolved guilt continued to eat away at him for years.
items.ex_zh: 那份未解的内疚感多年来持续折磨着他的内心。

items.def_zh: 使焦虑不安，使悲伤痛苦；使苦恼
items.def_en: To make someone feel very upset, sorrowful, or anxious; to cause emotional suffering to.
items.ex_en: The sudden cancellation of the vital subsidy will deeply distress low-income families.
items.ex_zh: 突然取消这项关键补贴将使低收入家庭深感忧虑与痛苦。

items.def_en: to cause great anguish, or to suffer extreme emotional turmoil
items.ex_en: Heartbreaking images from the disaster zone continue to agonize millions of viewers worldwide.
items.ex_zh: 来自灾区的心碎画面继续使全球数百万观众备受情感煎熬。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to severely disturb or damage someone psychologically or emotionally
items.ex_en: Those toxic years in that cult really mess up anyone who joins them.
items.ex_zh: 在那邪教里度过的有毒岁月确实会搞垮任何加入者的心理。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone profound psychological anguish, emotional pain, or distress
items.ex_en: The civil war threatens to tear the entire country apart.
items.ex_zh: 内战有让整个国家分崩离析的危险。

items.def_en: to cause intense, deliberate mental or physical anguish
items.ex_en: Unanswered questions about his daughter's mysterious disappearance torture the grieving father daily.
items.ex_zh: 关于女儿神秘失踪的无解疑云每天都在折磨着这位悲痛的父亲。

items.def_en: to cause severe, persistent physical or mental anguish to someone
items.ex_en: Haunting memories of battlefield atrocities continue to torment the decorated veteran in retirement.
items.ex_zh: 战场暴行的梦魇般回忆在退伍后继续折磨着这位战功卓著的老兵。

items.def_en: to leave a permanent mark of emotional suffering on someone's psyche
items.ex_en: Such severe childhood emotional neglect can scar an impressionable individual for life.
items.ex_zh: 这种严重的童年情感忽视会给易受影响的人留下终身的心灵创伤。

items.def_zh: 使受精神创伤；使受外伤
items.def_en: To shock and upset someone severely, leading to lasting psychological or emotional damage; to cause physical injury to.
items.ex_en: The violent home invasion threatened to traumatize the terrified young siblings permanently.
items.ex_zh: 那场暴力的入室抢劫极可能会给惊恐年幼的兄妹俩造成永久精神创伤。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote causing severe mental suffering, distress, or lasting psychic injury to a person, escalating from persistent emotional agitation to debilitating, life-altering trauma.
groups.summary_zh: 指对他人心理或精神造成持久煎熬、痛苦折磨乃至深重创伤。
groups.desc_en: Denotes subjecting the psyche to severe, lingering, or debilitating mental anguish, contrasting with temporary external 'upset' or mild 'annoy'.
groups.desc_zh: 指对人的精神世界施加深重、持久且极具摧毁性的痛苦折磨，区别于短暂浅表的外界“打扰”或轻微“烦心”。
groups.nuance_en: torment: afflict repeatedly with relentless mental distress or painful reminders (memories / thoughts / doubts) · torture: subject to acute, agonizing internal anguish akin to physical racking (soul / guilt / dilemma) · scar: leave an indelible emotional trauma that permanently alters someone (psyche / childhood / survivor) · eat away at: progressively and silently corrode someone's peace of mind (guilt / suspicion / secret) · distress: cause acute sorrow, deep anxiety, or financial/mental strain (family / mind / relatives)
groups.nuance_zh: torment: 没完没了的纠结或痛苦回忆如影随形般折磨内心 (memories / thoughts / doubts) · torture: 内心犹如受酷刑般剧烈煎熬与撕扯 (soul / guilt / dilemma) · scar: 留下永难愈合的心灵创伤，彻底改变人格 (psyche / childhood / survivor) · eat away at: 负罪感或疑虑像蠹虫般日复一日慢慢蚀咬心神 (guilt / suspicion / secret) · distress: 带来剧烈的悲伤、极度揪心或痛苦忧惧 (family / mind / relatives)

groups.name: Inform on & Betray an Associate · 告密与告发 (Inform, Rat out, Grass up)
groups.tip: 暗中揭发秘密或出卖同伴

items.def_en: to inform on an associate or expose someone's misdeeds to an authority figure
items.ex_en: The nervous informant decided to rat out his fellow gang members yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 那个紧张的线人昨天决定出卖告发他的帮派同伙。

items.def_en: to inform on a criminal associate to the police
items.ex_en: The frightened burglar agreed to grass up his accomplice to avoid prison.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的窃贼为了免受牢狱之灾，同意向警方告发其同伙。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to betray and report someone to the police or authorities
items.ex_en: Driven by guilty conscience, the thief decided to turn in his accomplice.
items.ex_zh: 出于内疚，这个盗贼决定向警方检举他的同伙。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to report someone's bad behavior or misdeed to an authority figure such as a teacher or parent
items.ex_en: Tommy threatened to tell on his older brother for sneaking extra sweets.
items.ex_zh: 汤米威胁说要向家长告发哥哥偷偷多拿糖果的事情。

items.def_zh: 揭发；告密（违法犯罪行为）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to bring an associate's wrongdoing or illicit activities to light by informing the public or authorities
items.ex_en: The brave accountant chose to blow the whistle on the company's fraudulent practices.
items.ex_zh: 勇敢的会计师选择公开揭发公司内部的欺诈违法行径。

items.def_en: (informal, dated) to inform on or betray an accomplice or friend
items.ex_en: Under intense police interrogation, the nervous rookie driver began to peach on everyone.
items.ex_zh: 在警方严厉审讯下，紧张的新手司机开始向警方出卖告密所有人。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on) to inform on someone, especially regarding minor or petty infractions
items.ex_en: No one in the classroom would snitch on Billy for the prank.
items.ex_zh: 教室里没有任何人愿意打小报告告发比利的恶作剧。

items.def_en: (+ on) to betray a secret or inform to the authorities under pressure
items.ex_en: Detectives expected the timid getaway driver to squeal on the mob boss.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们指望那个胆小的逃跑司机能够供出幕后的黑帮头目。

items.def_zh: 告密，打小报告；闲聊，说闲话
items.def_en: 1. (especially of a child) to report another person's wrongdoings to someone in authority. 2. to gossip or chatter idly.
items.ex_en: Little Sarah ran straight to the teacher to tattle about the stolen crayons.
items.ex_zh: 小萨拉径直跑去老师那里打小报告，说蜡笔被人偷拿了。

groups.summary_en: A person secretly discloses incriminating information about an accomplice, peer, or group member to police, teachers, or rivals, violating solidarity.
groups.summary_zh: 背弃同伴向警方或权威秘密告密、出卖或揭发违规行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes breaching loyalty or solidarity by disclosing incriminating secrets about one's associates to authorities, contrasting with open 'accuse' or neutral 'report'.
groups.desc_zh: 指背弃信任与同盟关系，向官方或当权者秘密告发同伙的不法行为或劣迹，区别于公开“指控”或中性“汇报”。
groups.nuance_en: rat out: disloyally betray an associate to save oneself or gain favor (accomplices / friends / partners) · grass up: British slang for informing on a comrade to the police (gang / mates / thieves) · turn in: surrender a lawbreaker or oneself to the police (suspect / fugitive / brother) · snitch: petulantly or sneakily report petty wrongdoing or peers to authorities (classmates / coworkers / inmates) · blow the whistle on: disclose systemic corruption or illegal conduct to the public/authorities for ethical reasons (organization / fraud / cover-up)
groups.nuance_zh: rat out: 为保全自己或贪图利益而背信弃义地出卖同伙 (accomplices / friends / partners) · grass up: 英俚，向警察告密、出卖黑帮同伙或兄弟 (gang / mates / thieves) · turn in: 将在逃嫌犯、同谋甚至亲属扭送或举报归案 (suspect / fugitive / brother) · snitch: 告小状，出于鸡毛蒜皮或私利向长官打小报告 (classmates / coworkers / inmates) · blow the whistle on: 出于正义感向监管部门或公众吹哨揭发内部系统性腐败 (organization / fraud / cover-up)

groups.name: Informal Bargaining & Huddling · 讨价还价与私下商谈 (Dicker, Haggle, Chaffer)
groups.tip: 双方商讨条件或讨价还价

items.def_en: (+ with) to hold an informal meeting or conference to discuss a problem or plan
items.ex_en: The marketing executives decided to powwow with the creative team before launching.
items.ex_zh: 市场主管们决定在产品发布前与创意团队举行一次非正式会商。

items.def_en: (+ with/about) to bargain or haggle repeatedly, especially over petty merchandise
items.ex_en: Townspeople would gather near the marketplace to chaffer about trinkets and fabric.
items.ex_zh: 小镇居民常聚集在集市旁，就小饰品和布料讨价还价、闲扯交谈。

items.def_zh: 反复商议达成；艰难敲定
items.def_en: (+ sth) to reach an agreement or deal after protracted, vigorous discussion and bargaining
items.ex_en: Envoys worked through midnight to hammer out a lasting bilateral peace treaty.
items.ex_zh: 特使们工作到深夜，终于反复磋商敲定了一份持久的双边和平条约。

items.def_zh: 深入讨论解决；反复协商
items.def_en: (+ sth) to talk about a problem or disputed details extensively until a resolution is reached
items.ex_en: The partners scheduled an emergency retreat to hash out their strategic differences.
items.ex_zh: 合伙人们安排了一次紧急闭门会议，以深入讨论并解决他们的战略分歧。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to persuade someone through haggling to reduce a price
items.ex_en: The old factory was knocked down to make way for a modern shopping center.
items.ex_zh: 旧工厂被拆除，为一座现代化的购物中心腾出了空间。

items.def_en: (+ over/about) to argue persistently over the cost of something or petty details before reaching an agreement
items.ex_en: Bargain hunters usually haggle over prices at the crowded open-air weekend market.
items.ex_zh: 淘便宜货的顾客通常会在拥挤的周末露天市场上反复讨价还价。

items.def_zh: 空谈，扯皮，漫长费时的交涉
items.def_en: (+ with) to talk idly, profusely, or engage in lengthy, time-wasting negotiations
items.ex_en: We spent hours palavering with foreign suppliers without reaching any firm binding agreement.
items.ex_zh: 我们同外国供应商扯皮交涉了数小时，却未达成任何实质性协议。

items.def_en: 1. (+ over/with) (North American informal) To bargain or haggle persistently over the price, terms, or conditions of a deal.
items.ex_en: He drove to the used car lot to dicker over the price.
items.ex_zh: 他开车去了二手车销售点，就汽车价格反复讨价还价。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (informal) To have a casual, private chat or discussion.
items.ex_en: The coach stepped aside to confab with his top assistant during halftime.
items.ex_zh: 教练在半场休息时走到一边，同他的首席助教私下商量。

groups.summary_en: Parties engage in protracted, often petty or informal discussions over terms, prices, or minor details, ranging from street-market haggling to backroom confabs.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重非正式或琐碎细节的讨价还价、私下商谈与扯皮。
groups.desc_en: Denotes informal, tenacious, back-and-forth verbal bartering or closed-door deliberative bargaining to strike a deal, contrasting with formal legal 'negotiate' or rigid 'demand'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在非正式、纠缠拉锯式的口舌交涉或闭门磋商中反复砍价摸底以达成协议，区别于正式法律层面的“谈判”或单方面“索要”。
groups.nuance_en: haggle: persistently dispute over petty terms or price to drive it down (price / terms / flea market) · dicker: folksy back-and-forth petty bargaining over minor adjustments (details / trades / terms) · hash out: resolve intricate differences through lengthy, candid discussion (differences / compromise / treaty) · hammer out: forge an agreement through arduous, determined negotiations (deal / pact / solution) · powwow: gather informally to confer, consult, or strategize (leaders / team / executives)
groups.nuance_zh: haggle: 在小恩小惠或买卖价格上死缠烂打、反复讨价还价 (price / terms / flea market) · dicker: 乡土俚俗味，针对次要条款或旧物交易细致磨叽 (details / trades / terms) · hash out: 敞开天窗说亮话，通过深入细致的长谈厘清分歧 (differences / compromise / treaty) · hammer out: 历经艰难交涉、千锤百炼终于敲定协议 (deal / pact / solution) · powwow: 私下关起门来聚首研商、开对策碰头会 (leaders / team / executives)

groups.name: Ingest Rapidly & Noisily · 狼吞虎咽与咯吱咀嚼 (Crunch, Scarf, Gobble)
groups.tip: 门齿臼齿咀嚼咬碎食物

items.def_en: [I/T] to munch or chew audibly and vigorously
items.ex_en: The hungry horse began to chump the fresh, crisp carrots with gusto.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的马儿开始津津有味地咯吱咯吱大嚼新鲜清脆的胡萝卜。

items.def_zh: 咯吱咯吱地咬嚼；嘎吱作响；（大量）处理（数据）
items.def_en: 1. to bite, chew, or crush food noisily with the teeth. 2. (informal) to process large amounts of information or numbers.
items.ex_en: Moviegoers crunch tasty buttered popcorn while watching the dramatic action scenes unfold.
items.ex_zh: 看电影的人边看着戏剧性的动作场面上演，边嘎吱嘎吱嚼着黄油爆米花。

items.def_en: (+ sth) swallow food hurriedly without chewing it properly
items.ex_en: Rushing out the door, he had to bolt down his morning coffee.
items.ex_zh: 匆忙出门之际，他只得急匆匆地将早晨的咖啡一饮而尽。

items.def_en: (+ sth) eat something rapidly, hungrily, and noisily
items.ex_en: The starving teenagers quickly gobble up the entire stack of hot pancakes.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的青少年们迅速狼吞虎咽地吃光了整叠热煎饼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) swallow food or drink greedily and noisily in large mouthfuls
items.ex_en: Exhausted runners gulp down cold mineral water immediately after crossing the finish line.
items.ex_zh: 精疲力竭的跑者们冲过终点线后立刻大口大口吞下冰凉的矿泉水。

items.def_en: (+ sth) eat food very quickly and greedily
items.ex_en: He will scarf down three double cheeseburgers whenever he misses regular lunch.
items.ex_zh: 每当错过正餐午饭时，他都会狼吞虎咽地塞下三个双层芝士堡。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽，大口吞食（常与 down 或 up 连用）
items.def_en: (slang, chiefly North American) to eat or swallow food greedily and quickly (often with 'down' or 'up')
items.ex_en: The hungry hikers scarf delicious campfire sausages as soon as night falls.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的徒步者们一到夜幕降临就大口吞食美味的营火香肠。

items.def_en: (+ down/up) to swallow food hurriedly and greedily in large chunks
items.ex_en: Don't gobble your dinner so fast or you will get indigestion soon.
items.ex_zh: 别吃晚饭吃得那么狼吞虎咽，否则你很快就会消化不良的。

items.def_en: (+ down) to eat ravenously and quickly like a hungry animal
items.ex_en: The ravenous boy began to wolf down the warm apple pie greedily.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的孩子开始像饿狼一样贪婪地吞咽那块温热的苹果派。

groups.summary_en: An eater consumes solid or crunchy nourishment either by chewing audibly and crispily or by ravenously gulping down food with greedy speed.
groups.summary_zh: 发出清脆碎裂声用力咀嚼，或贪婪而飞快地吞咽食物。
groups.desc_en: Denotes consuming food with voracious speed, greedy urgency, or audible crunching, contrasting with civilized, measured 'eat' or slow 'chew'.
groups.desc_zh: 指狼吞虎咽、迫不及待或发出咯吱咯吱声响地急速吞咽食物，区别于文明克制的“进食”或细嚼慢咽的“咀嚼”。
groups.nuance_en: gobble up: devour rapidly and greedily in large, hurried mouthfuls (food / resources / market) · scarf down: informally inhale food with extreme hunger and speed (lunch / burger / pizza) · bolt down: swallow food hastily almost without chewing (breakfast / meal / food) · gulp down: swallow liquids or soft food quickly in loud gulps (water / pills / drink) · crunch: crush hard or crisp food loudly between the teeth (apple / crisps / gravel)
groups.nuance_zh: gobble up: 贪婪地大口吞咽一扫而空，或快速吞并资源 (food / resources / market) · scarf down: 口语中极度饥饿时风卷残云般狂吃 (lunch / burger / pizza) · bolt down: 匆忙间囫囵吞枣，几乎不嚼就咽下肚 (breakfast / meal / food) · gulp down: 喉咙发出咕咚声大口仰脖吞饮液体或药丸 (water / pills / drink) · crunch: 牙齿用力碾碎硬脆食物时发出清脆咯吱声 (apple / crisps / gravel)

groups.name: Inhabit & Dwell Continuously · 定居与长久栖息 (Inhabit, Populate, Reside)
groups.tip: 人口或生物栖息于某地

items.def_en: to live in, work in, or fill a building, area, or room
items.ex_en: Prominent international diplomatic delegations occupy several floors of this secure downtown skyscraper.
items.ex_zh: 著名国际外交代表团占用了这座市中心安保摩天大楼的若干楼层。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to inhabit a particular building, area, or habitat as one's continuous residence
items.ex_en: They are looking for a reliable live-in nanny for their twins.
items.ex_zh: 他们正在为双胞胎物色一位可靠的住家保姆。

items.def_en: to establish a permanent home and continuous, stable residence in a particular place
items.ex_en: The newlyweds decided to settle down in a quiet seaside town eventually.
items.ex_zh: 这对新婚夫妇最终决定在一座宁静的海滨小镇定居安家。
items.ex2_en: The strict kindergarten teacher quickly settled down the excited children before story time.
items.ex2_zh: 在讲故事时间之前，严格的幼儿园老师很快让兴奋的孩子们安静了下来。

items.def_en: to continue residing or dwelling in a place after others have departed
items.ex_en: She decided to stay on at the university to pursue a master's degree.
items.ex_zh: 她决定继续留在大学攻读硕士学位。

items.def_en: (+ in/at) to have one's permanent home in a specified place
items.ex_en: Distinguished university professors often reside in the picturesque historical district across town.
items.ex_zh: 著名大学教授们通常定居于城区另一端风景如画的古老历史街区。

items.def_zh: 承租定居；作为房客居住
items.def_en: to occupy land or property as a tenant or resident
items.ex_en: Generations of hardworking tenant farmers tenant the sprawling countryside manor under contract.
items.ex_zh: 世代辛勤的佃农依合同承租并居住在这座广袤的乡村庄园领地上。

items.def_en: (+ in) to live or stay permanently in a particular place
items.ex_en: Ethereal forest spirits were whispered to dwell deep within the whispering ancient pines.
items.ex_zh: 私语相传，空灵的林中仙灵世世代代栖息在低语古松林深处。

items.def_zh: 居住于，栖息于；构成……的人口；（计算机）填充（数据等）
items.def_en: 1. To live in an area and form its population; to inhabit. 2. (computing) To fill data or information into a database, spreadsheet, or form.
items.ex_en: Hardy indigenous communities continue to populate the harsh, frostbitten northern tundra landscapes.
items.ex_zh: 顽强的原住民群体继续居住栖息于严寒苦寒的北方苔原地区。

items.def_en: To live or reside in a particular place, habitat, or region.
items.ex_en: Rare migratory waterbirds inhabit the tranquil coastal marshlands during the cold winter months.
items.ex_zh: 珍稀候鸟在寒冷的冬季月份栖息栖居在这片宁静的沿海湿地之中。

groups.summary_en: Living beings live in, occupy, or colonize a territory, building, or habitat as their established place of residence.
groups.summary_zh: 指人类或动植物在某一地理环境或空间中长期居住、栖息。
groups.desc_en: Denotes establishing a lasting, continuous residential presence in a geographical space or dwelling, contrasting with temporary 'visit' or fleeting 'stay'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在某地理区域或居所内建立起长久、稳定的定居与栖息状态，区别于短暂停留的“造访”或客居式的“借宿”。
groups.nuance_en: reside: dwell permanently or legally in a designated domicile (abroad / in a mansion / legally) · dwell: literarily or archaic living in a place or state of contemplation (in caves / in the forest / among people) · inhabit: live in, populate, or occupy an environment as an organism or people (region / island / planet) · populate: supply a territory with human or biological residents (continent / cities / database) · settle down: transition into a stable, permanent domestic life in a community (in the countryside / marry / suburbs)
groups.nuance_zh: reside: 正式且具法律意义的长久定居或居留 (abroad / in a mansion / legally) · dwell: 文学色彩浓厚地长居于某处，或引申为盘桓沉溺 (in caves / in the forest / among people) · inhabit: 生物或族群把特定环境当做自然家园栖息其中 (region / island / planet) · populate: 繁衍并填充某地区使其具备常住人口 (continent / cities / database) · settle down: 告别漂泊，安家落户过上安定的家庭生活 (in the countryside / marry / suburbs)

groups.name: Inquire & Interrogate · 打探与质问 (Quiz, Debrief, Interrogate)
groups.tip: 从一般询问升级至严密审讯

items.def_en: (+ sb) to question someone indirectly to discover their opinions or intentions
items.ex_en: The manager quietly sounded out a few team members before unveiling the restructuring plan.
items.ex_zh: 经理在公布重组方案之前，私下试探了几名团队成员的口风。

items.def_en: (+ for) to try persistently to elicit information or secrets from someone
items.ex_en: The nosy reporter tried to pump him for details about the secret merger.
items.ex_zh: 那个好管闲事的记者试图向他盘问有关秘密合并案的细节。

items.def_en: (+ sb for sth) to question someone persistently or slyly to obtain secret or private information
items.ex_en: She slyly bought him drinks to pump him for private corporate data.
items.ex_zh: 她狡猾地请他喝酒，企图套取公司的机密数据。

items.def_en: (+ about/on) To question someone closely to get information or test their knowledge.
items.ex_en: The manager decided to quiz each applicant closely on their relevant past experience.
items.ex_zh: 经理决定就相关的过往经验对每位应聘者进行仔细查问。

items.def_zh: 详细询问，向（刚完成任务者）盘问情况并听取汇报
items.def_en: To question someone thoroughly about a completed mission or task in order to obtain detailed information.
items.ex_en: Senior officers will thoroughly debrief the reconnaissance pilots immediately after their return.
items.ex_zh: 侦察机飞行员一返回，高级官员就将立即向他们详细盘问任务情况。

items.def_en: (+ sb about sth) to question someone aggressively and relentlessly to extract information
items.ex_en: The detectives continued to grill the prime suspect about his missing whereabouts.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们继续就主要嫌疑人失踪期间的去向对其进行严厉盘问。

items.def_en: to subject someone to intense, unrelenting questioning and pressure
items.ex_en: Her suspicious parents began to grill her the moment she walked inside.
items.ex_zh: 她起疑的父母在她一进门时就开始严厉盘问她。

items.def_en: to question a witness closely and aggressively to test the veracity of their testimony
items.ex_en: The defense attorney rose to cross-examine the prosecution's key eyewitness about the incident.
items.ex_zh: 辩方律师起身严密盘问控方的关键目击证人有关该事件的情况。

items.def_en: To question a person closely, aggressively, or formally, especially a suspect or prisoner.
items.ex_en: Military police brought in the captured insurgent to interrogate him at length.
items.ex_zh: 宪兵带进了被俘的叛乱分子，准备对其进行长时间的正式审问。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe questioning a person to extract information, ranging from casual probing or structured testing to systematic, high-pressure interrogation. Intensity escalates from brief questioning ('quiz') to professional intelligence extraction ('debrief') and aggressive adversarial grilling ('interrogate', 'grill').
groups.summary_zh: 指通过提问获取信息，从简短测问递进至严密审讯质逼。
groups.desc_en: Denotes systematically probing, questioning, or grilling someone to extract closely held facts, contrasting with casual 'ask' or voluntary 'converse'.
groups.desc_zh: 指采取追问、盘问、打探等手段系统性榨取受访者隐匿的信息，区别于寻常中性的“询问”或自发的“交谈”。
groups.nuance_en: interrogate: subject to formal, authoritative, often coercive adversarial questioning (suspects / prisoners / witnesses) · grill: relentlessly bombard someone with aggressive, uncomfortable questions (politician / suspect / witness) · cross-examine: rigorously test a witness's claims under adversarial forensic scrutiny (witness / defendant / expert) · debrief: interrogate an operative or traveler post-mission to glean actionable intel (astronauts / pilots / soldiers) · sound out: discreetly probe someone's thoughts or inclinations in advance (colleagues / views / intentions)
groups.nuance_zh: interrogate: 官方以居高临下的威势展开正式审讯或连续盘问 (suspects / prisoners / witnesses) · grill: 像架在火上烤一样，咄咄逼人地连环追问刁难 (politician / suspect / witness) · cross-examine: 法庭式的对抗性反诘交叉盘问，揪住漏洞不放 (witness / defendant / expert) · debrief: 任务结束后系统听取当事人汇报以提取详实情报 (astronauts / pilots / soldiers) · sound out: 不露声色地旁敲侧击试探意向或口风 (colleagues / views / intentions)

groups.name: Insert & Intersperse · 填入与插入 (Interpolate, Grout, Wedge, Stuff)
groups.tip: 插入内部或嵌进缝隙

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fold or press the edges of something into a neat, secure position or narrow opening
items.ex_en: Make sure you tuck in your clean shirt before entering the interview room.
items.ex_zh: 进入面试室之前，务必把干净的衬衫下摆掖好。

items.def_en: to fill a hole or gap tightly with suitable material
items.ex_en: He used a piece of dense clay to plug the leaking pipe.
items.ex_zh: 他用一块致密的黏土紧紧堵住了漏水的管道。

items.def_en: (+ in/into) to push or fold edges into a safe, neat, or hidden position
items.ex_en: She decided to tuck the folded emergency cash into her secret jacket pocket.
items.ex_zh: 她决定把折好的应急现金塞进夹克的隐秘口袋里。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to manage to insert or fit someone or something into a very confined gap or tight space
items.ex_en: We managed to squeeze in another small suitcase into the overflowing car boot.
items.ex_zh: 我们设法把另一个小手提箱硬塞进了堆得满满的后备箱里。

items.def_en: (+ into/between) to fix or force something tightly into a narrow space
items.ex_en: He used a heavy timber to wedge the swinging door into place.
items.ex_zh: 他用一根沉重的木料把摇晃的门牢牢卡在原位。

items.def_en: (+ into) to force or squeeze a large amount into a tight space
items.ex_en: She had to cram dozens of thick textbooks into her tiny school locker.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不把几十本厚厚的教科书硬塞进她狭小的储物柜里。

items.def_en: to fill the gaps between tiles, bricks, or stones with grout
items.ex_en: The mason will carefully grout the narrow joints between the bathroom tiles.
items.ex_zh: 泥瓦匠将仔细地用填缝剂填塞浴室瓷砖之间的狭窄缝隙。

items.def_zh: 插入，添加（语句或内容）；（数学）内插
items.def_en: 1. to insert extra words, remarks, or material into a text or conversation 2. (mathematics) to calculate or estimate a value between two known values
items.ex_en: The cautious editor chose to interpolate several clarifying explanatory lines into the manuscript.
items.ex_zh: 谨慎的编辑选择在手稿中插入几行澄清性的解释文字。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to push or stuff a large amount of material into an already tight space
items.ex_en: He desperately tried to cram in one more bundle into the bulging trunk.
items.ex_zh: 他拼命想在鼓鼓囊囊的行李箱里再硬塞进一个包裹。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe physical or textual insertion into an existing matrix, text, or gap. Manner distinctions reflect whether material is squeezed into seams (grouting), wedged tightly (stuffing/plugging), or inserted into sequences (interpolating).
groups.summary_zh: 通过塞、嵌、填或穿插等具体手法将外物置入空隙或原有序列中。
groups.desc_en: Denotes placing an element tightly into an existing space, gap, or continuous body of text, contrasting with simple 'put' or loose 'add'.
groups.desc_zh: 指将某物严丝合缝、硬塞或见缝插针地填入既有缝隙、空间或连续文本中，区别于随意的“放置”或平铺直叙的“添加”。
groups.nuance_en: wedge: force tightly into a narrow space to jam or secure (door / between cushions / wood) · cram: pack forcefully into an already overflowing or restricted container (luggage / crowds / schedule) · interpolate: insert new or alien material into an existing text or data series (passages / values / words) · tuck: fold or stow neatly and snugly into an unobtrusive place (shirt / away money / behind ear) · squeeze in: manage with difficulty to insert into tight physical or temporal room (appointment / meeting / between cars)
groups.nuance_zh: wedge: 运用楔入动作硬挤进狭小缝隙并卡牢 (door / between cushions / wood) · cram: 不顾空间局限强行塞满、挤塞得水泄不通 (luggage / crowds / schedule) · interpolate: 在已有手稿或数据序列中篡入、插补文本或数值 (passages / values / words) · tuck: 妥帖舒展地将边角掖入、塞进隐蔽角落 (shirt / away money / behind ear) · squeeze in: 在逼仄的空间或排得满满的日程中硬挤出位置 (appointment / meeting / between cars)

groups.name: Insinuating & Creeping Motion · 蠕动与潜入 (Worm, Sneak, Insinuate)
groups.tip: 放低身段悄悄移动

items.def_en: to advance into a space very quietly and slowly to avoid being seen or heard
items.ex_en: Cold drafts began to creep in through the tiny gaps beneath the doorframe.
items.ex_zh: 冷风开始悄悄从门框下方的细小缝隙中潜入室内。

items.def_en: to enter a place quietly, deceitfully, and stealthily so as to avoid detection
items.ex_en: The curious boy tried to sneak in through the unlocked back kitchen window.
items.ex_zh: 那个好奇的男孩试图从厨房没锁的后窗悄悄溜进去。

items.def_en: to move slowly, carefully, or gradually in a particular direction
items.ex_en: The cat began to edge cautiously toward the open door without a sound.
items.ex_zh: 猫咪开始悄无声息地小心翼翼向敞开的门边挪动。
items.ex2_en: The skilled driver edged his massive vehicle carefully through the narrow stone alley.
items.ex2_zh: 技术娴熟的司机小心翼翼地把他的庞大车辆缓缓开过狭窄的石板巷。

items.def_zh: 潜行，偷偷地走；私带，偷偷放；告密
items.def_en: 1. To move quietly and stealthily so as to avoid being seen or heard. 2. To take, bring, or put something secretly. 3. (British informal) To tell an authority figure about someone's bad behavior.
items.ex_en: He decided to sneak into the auditorium while the lights were completely dimmed.
items.ex_zh: 他决定趁灯光完全熄灭时偷偷潜入礼堂。

items.def_zh: 蠕行，爬行前进；钻营（worm one's way into）；给（动物）驱虫
items.def_en: 1. To move slowly forward by wriggling, crawling, or twisting the body. 2. ('worm one's way into/out of') To insinuate or maneuver oneself subtly. 3. To treat an animal to expel parasitic worms.
items.ex_en: The trapped explorer had to slowly worm through the dangerously narrow rock crevice.
items.ex_zh: 被困的探险者不得不慢慢蠕动着爬过危险狭窄的岩石缝隙。

items.def_zh: 潜行，偷偷走（sneak的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. (chiefly North American informal) Past tense and past participle of sneak; to move stealthily, or to smuggle something quietly.
items.ex_en: The mischievous kids snuck past the strict guard without making a single sound.
items.ex_zh: 淘气的孩子们一声不响地从严厉的警卫身边偷偷溜了过去。

items.def_en: to move along by twisting and turning the body through a narrow space
items.ex_en: The tiny puppy managed to wriggle through the narrow iron fence bars.
items.ex_zh: 小狗设法扭动着身子钻过了狭窄的铁栅栏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to move slowly, twisting and wriggling, into a tight or restricted space
items.ex_en: The nimble ferret could easily worm into the smallest burrow underground.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的雪貂能轻而易举地蠕动钻进地下最小的洞穴里。

items.def_en: (+ oneself into) to maneuver oneself gradually into a favorable or tight position
items.ex_en: The ambitious courtier tried to insinuate himself into the monarch's inner council.
items.ex_zh: 那个野心勃勃的朝臣试图巧妙地钻进君主的内廷重臣圈子。

groups.summary_en: An agent advances gradually into a restricted, tight, or forbidden space, often using subtle wriggling motions or deceptive stealth to avoid notice.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过蠕动、钻营或极隐秘手段慢慢潜入或钻进狭小隐秘空间。
groups.desc_en: Denotes entering or moving through a space with stealthy, supple, serpentine, or evasive progression to avoid detection, contrasting with open 'enter' or straightforward 'walk'.
groups.desc_zh: 指像游蛇蠕动或暗中潜行般，以隐秘、扭动或渐进的姿态悄然钻入某处以避人耳目，区别于堂皇大方的“进入”或直线的“步行”。
groups.nuance_en: sneak: move furtively and silently to avoid seeing or hearing (in / past guards / out) · creep: advance slowly, close to the ground, almost imperceptibly (shadows / silence / in) · worm into: deviously insinuate oneself into someone's favor or a restricted domain (confidence / inner circle / heart) · wriggle: twist and turn the body with quick squirming motions to advance (out of grasp / through hole / free) · edge: advance gradually, sideways, and cautiously step by step (forward / closer / along the cliff)
groups.nuance_zh: sneak: 鬼鬼祟祟、蹑手蹑脚地溜过防线以防被发觉 (in / past guards / out) · creep: 贴近地面、无声无息且慢动作般潜行爬入 (shadows / silence / in) · worm into: 像蛀虫般工于心计地钻营潜入圈子或博得信任 (confidence / inner circle / heart) · wriggle: 像泥鳅般通过扭动身躯钻过狭洞或挣脱束缚 (out of grasp / through hole / free) · edge: 侧着身子一步一挪、极其谨慎小幅度挪动 (forward / closer / along the cliff)

groups.name: Inspire & Motivate · 激励与鼓舞 (Inspiring Action & Confidence)
groups.tip: 给予他人前行动力与信心

items.def_en: 1. To give support, confidence, or hope to someone. 2. To stimulate, foster, or promote the development of something.
items.ex_en: Her encouraging mentors continue to encourage her artistic pursuits with helpful advice.
items.ex_zh: 循循善诱的导师们不断以有益的建议鼓励她追求艺术。

items.def_en: to fill someone with the urge, creative ambition, or conviction to achieve something
items.ex_en: His selfless devotion would inspire generations of young volunteers to serve humanity.
items.ex_zh: 他无私的奉献将激励一代又一代的年轻志愿者为人类服务。

items.def_zh: 激励，激发；成为……的动机，促使
items.def_en: 1. To inspire or give someone enthusiasm and determination to do something. 2. To provide a reason or motive for an action.
items.ex_en: Strong financial bonuses rarely motivate employees to maintain genuine long-term creativity.
items.ex_zh: 丰厚的财务奖金很少能激励员工保持真正持久的创造力。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to strongly motivate, encourage, or urge someone to keep going or do better
items.ex_en: Loud cheers from the passionate crowd helped spur on the exhausted marathon runner.
items.ex_zh: 热情观众的响亮欢呼声激励着筋疲力尽的马拉松选手继续向前。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to fill someone with high energy, enthusiasm, or passionate motivation
items.ex_en: The coach's speech fired up the team before the final match.
items.ex_zh: 决赛前，教练的演讲彻底点燃了全队的斗志。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to urge or encourage someone persistently to take bold or risky action
items.ex_en: His reckless friends began to egg him on to make the dangerous jump.
items.ex_zh: 他不计后果的朋友们开始怂恿他去进行那次危险的跳跃。

items.def_en: (+ on) to urge a person forward to greater exertion or immediate action
items.ex_en: Fierce market competition will spur the engineering team toward faster technological innovation.
items.ex_zh: 激烈的市场竞争将鞭策工程团队加快技术创新步伐。

items.def_en: to give someone the courage or confidence to do something daring
items.ex_en: Early battlefield successes would embolden the rebel forces to attack the main capital.
items.ex_zh: 早期的战役胜利让叛军壮起胆量去进攻主首都。

items.def_en: to make someone feel more hopeful, cheerful, or confident
items.ex_en: The sudden positive news from home served to hearten the weary travelers.
items.ex_zh: 来自家乡的突如其来的好消息令疲惫的旅行者们为之振作。

groups.summary_en: An influencer instills spirit, purpose, hope, or willpower into another person to prompt productive action or bolster emotional resilience.
groups.summary_zh: 通过言语或精神榜样赋予他人信心与行动驱动力，促使其克服困难奋发有为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes infusing someone with creative vitality, courage, or internal drive to act boldly, contrasting with mere 'ask' or physical 'push'.
groups.desc_zh: 指赋予当事人内在精神力量、创造性灵感或勇气，驱使其迸发行动激情，区别于机械的“要求”或外界单纯的“推搡”。
groups.nuance_en: inspire: fill someone with uplifting creative or spiritual exaltation (artists / confidence / loyalty) · motivate: provide a compelling reason or internal catalyst to achieve goals (employees / students / change) · embolden: impart brave confidence to take perilous or audacious steps (rebels / critics / actions) · spur on: stimulate forward like applying spurs to a horse (runners / innovation / recovery) · fire up: electrify emotionally with enthusiastic zeal and passion (crowd / team / base)
groups.nuance_zh: inspire: 点燃灵感火花或在精神上给人以崇高的感召与启迪 (artists / confidence / loyalty) · motivate: 激发内在心理动机与行动意愿以达成特定目标 (employees / students / change) · embolden: 壮人胆气，使人敢于冒风险采取大胆举动 (rebels / critics / actions) · spur on: 如同策马扬鞭般鞭策、激励加速冲刺 (runners / innovation / recovery) · fire up: 煽动点燃群体极度亢奋激昂的热血与斗志 (crowd / team / base)

groups.name: Insult & Slander · 侮辱与诽谤 (Slander, Malign, Vilify)
groups.tip: 公然羞辱或恶意捏造抹黑

items.def_en: speak to or treat someone with intentional disrespect or scornful abuse
items.ex_en: You should never insult a loyal customer with such dismissive and rude behavior.
items.ex_zh: 你绝不应该用如此傲慢无礼的行为去侮辱一位忠实顾客。

items.def_en: speak of someone or something in a slighting, depreciative way
items.ex_en: He tends to disparage any unconventional ideas that differ from his own views.
items.ex_zh: 他往往会贬损任何与自己观点相左的非常规想法。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to insult, humiliate, or belittle someone, especially publicly
items.ex_en: The cruel supervisor would constantly put down junior workers in front of everyone.
items.ex_zh: 那个苛刻的主管经常当着众人的面贬低并羞辱初级员工。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to disparage, criticize, or denigrate someone's reputation repeatedly
items.ex_en: Envious colleagues always tried to run down her remarkable professional achievements behind her.
items.ex_zh: 嫉妒的同事们总是在背后诋毁她卓越的专业成就。

items.def_en: make damaging and defamatory false oral statements about someone
items.ex_en: The corrupt politician was formally accused of attempting to slander his honest rival.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败政客被正式指控企图口头诽谤其正直的竞争对手。

items.def_en: (formal, often passive) To insult or offend someone openly, deliberately, and to their face.
items.ex_en: His arrogant refusal to shake hands seemed calculated to affront the visiting dignitary.
items.ex_zh: 他傲慢地拒绝握手，似乎蓄意要当面冒犯来访的贵宾。

items.def_en: (formal) To speak or write about someone in an abusive and unfairly critical way so as to damage their reputation.
items.ex_en: The biased tabloid newspaper continued to vilify the activist throughout the campaign.
items.ex_zh: 那家带有偏见的八卦小报在整个竞选活动期间持续恶意中伤该活动人士。

items.def_en: (formal) To say or write false, harmful, and unfair things about someone.
items.ex_en: Dishonest competitors attempted to malign the company's integrity by spreading malicious rumors.
items.ex_zh: 不诚实的竞争对手企图通过散布恶毒谣言来中伤该公司的信誉。

items.def_en: deliberately harm the good reputation of someone through libel or slander
items.ex_en: The disgraced executive threatened legal action if they continued to defame his character.
items.ex_zh: 这名名誉扫地的高管威胁说，如果他们继续破坏他的名誉，就将诉诸法律。

groups.summary_en: An agent speaks ill of someone or directly attacks their honor, scaling from overt offensive disrespect to venomous public character assassination.
groups.summary_zh: 言语攻击、恶意中伤或损害他人名誉，程度由当面冒犯递增至恶毒诋毁。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately debasing someone's honor, character, or social esteem through spoken or written vitriol, contrasting with constructive 'criticize' or light 'tease'.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过口诛笔伐故意践踏贬损他人的尊严、名誉或人品，区别于善意的“批评”或无伤大雅的“揶揄”。
groups.nuance_en: insult: openly affront someone's dignity with offensive words or actions (intelligence / honor / host) · slander: defame maliciously with false spoken statements damaging reputation (character / reputation / competitor) · vilify: defame harshly in public discourse to turn someone into a despised villain (critics / press / opponents) · malign: spread damaging, untruthful rumors with ill-will (intentions / motives / name) · disparage: belittle someone or their achievements as unworthy of regard (efforts / accomplishments / merits)
groups.nuance_zh: insult: 当面以侮辱性言行冒犯并刺伤他人自尊 (intelligence / honor / host) · slander: 口头散布颠倒黑白的伪证诽谤败坏名声 (character / reputation / competitor) · vilify: 在舆论中恶毒丑化、将某人妖魔化为千夫所指 (critics / press / opponents) · malign: 心怀恶意地中伤诋毁他人的真实意图与名节 (intentions / motives / name) · disparage: 居高临下地轻蔑贬低对方成就的价值 (efforts / accomplishments / merits)

groups.name: Integrate & Desegregate · 整合与融入 (Systemic Socio-Political Inclusivity)
groups.tip: 消除隔离并重新融入群体

items.def_en: (+ into) to include a constituent group or element as a functional part of a unified body
items.ex_en: The progressive constitution sought to incorporate marginalized regional communities into national affairs.
items.ex_zh: 这部进步宪法力求将边缘化的地区群体纳入国家事务之中。

items.def_en: (+ into/with) to combine different ethnic or social factions into full, equal participation
items.ex_en: The innovative initiative aims to integrate diverse immigrant communities into municipal leadership roles.
items.ex_zh: 该创新举措旨在使多元化的移民群体融入市政领导层。
items.ex2_en: The exchange students integrated remarkably well into the local school community this semester.
items.ex2_zh: 本学期，这些交换生非常出色地融入了当地学校社区。

items.def_zh: 使主流化；使融入正规体制
items.def_en: to place formerly isolated or special-needs individuals into conventional educational or social environments
items.ex_en: The educational board works hard to mainstream special needs students into regular classes.
items.ex_zh: 教育委员会努力使有特殊需求的学生融入正规班级体制。

items.def_en: to fit naturally into a community or environment without looking different
items.ex_en: The shy newcomer quickly learned local customs to blend in with his neighbors.
items.ex_zh: 害羞的新来者很快学会了当地习俗，以便自然地融入邻里之间。

items.def_en: to feel or be accepted as a natural member of a social group or society
items.ex_en: It took several uneasy months for the quiet transfer student to fit in.
items.ex_zh: 那个沉默寡言的转学生花了几个忐忑不安的月份才真正融入集体。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to integrate or include someone within an existing group, system, or organization
items.ex_en: The committee made active efforts to bring in regional representatives from outlying districts.
items.ex_zh: 委员会积极采取举措，将偏远地区的代表吸纳进组织体制中。

items.def_en: (+ into) to absorb a group into the prevailing culture, adopting its customs and attitudes
items.ex_en: The new immigrant families worked tirelessly to assimilate into the surrounding suburban culture.
items.ex_zh: 这些新移民家庭不知疲倦地努力融入周边的郊区主流文化中。
items.ex2_en: The ancient empire gradually assimilated neighboring nomadic tribes through trade and intermarriage.
items.ex2_zh: 古帝国通过贸易和通婚逐渐同化了邻近的游牧部落。

items.def_en: 1. (+ into) To help someone return to normal society or a group, or to combine again into a unified whole.
items.ex_en: The extensive vocational program assists ex-convicts to reintegrate into productive civilian life smoothly.
items.ex_zh: 该广泛的职业培训项目协助刑满释放人员顺利重新融入充实的平民生活。
items.ex2_en: The injured soldier reintegrated successfully into civilian society after completing his rehabilitation program.
items.ex2_zh: 受伤的士兵在完成康复计划后成功重新融入了平民社会。

items.def_zh: 废止种族隔离，实现融合
items.def_en: 1. To end the legal or social separation of different racial or religious groups in schools or public places.
items.ex_en: The Supreme Court mandated all southern school districts to desegregate their classrooms.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院责令所有南方学区在班级中废止种族隔离以实现融合。
items.ex2_en: Public transportation systems in the region desegregated peacefully after sustained nonviolent civil protests.
items.ex2_zh: 在持续的非暴力民权抗议之后，该地区的公共交通系统和平实现了取消种族隔离。

groups.summary_en: Institutional authorities or communities incorporate previously segregated, marginalized, or excluded groups into the mainstream social, institutional, or educational fabric. Verbs contrast legal desegregation with interpersonal cultural adaptation.
groups.summary_zh: 在社会结构或体制中消除隔离、接纳吸收特定群体。
groups.desc_en: Denotes bringing disparate demographic, cultural, or structural elements into a unified, harmonious, and equal whole, contrasting with 'segregate' or superficial 'join'.
groups.desc_zh: 指将不同人群、文化或系统构件平权、有机地融汇为一个和谐统一的有机整体，区别于“隔离分立”或貌合神离的“挂靠”。
groups.nuance_en: integrate: combine distinct groups into an egalitarian, unified social structure (schools / communities / systems) · assimilate: absorb a minority culturally until distinct identity blends away (immigrants / customs / culture) · mainstream: incorporate specialized or marginal individuals/practices into prevailing norms (students / practices / ideas) · incorporate: take in and unite into a preexisting bodily structure or plan (feedback / elements / company) · blend in: adjust oneself to match the surroundings and avoid standing out (crowd / environment / colors)
groups.nuance_zh: integrate: 打破壁垒，将不同族群或模块平等有机融入完整系统 (schools / communities / systems) · assimilate: 强势同化吸收，使弱势群体的特质消弭于主流之中 (immigrants / customs / culture) · mainstream: 将边缘弱势群体或非主流理念纳入正轨主流运作 (students / practices / ideas) · incorporate: 将新要素吸纳为既有体系不可分割的组成部分 (feedback / elements / company) · blend in: 顺应环境调整自身姿态，彻底混入背景不露锋芒 (crowd / environment / colors)

groups.name: Interfere & Meddle Deviously · 乱动与不正当篡改 (Monkey, Tamper, Meddle)
groups.tip: 动手操纵把玩或胡乱摆弄拆改

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fiddle with or alter a mechanism carelessly or without authorization
items.ex_en: Do not fool with the complex settings on that delicate laboratory instrument.
items.ex_zh: 别去瞎捣鼓那台精密实验室仪器上的复杂设置。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to tinker with or tamper with something without serious intent or qualification
items.ex_en: Amateurs should not play around with the delicate safety wiring inside the panel.
items.ex_zh: 外行人不应该胡乱摆弄配电箱内部精密的安防电线。

items.def_en: (+ with) to make minor, often amateurish or experimental changes to something
items.ex_en: My grandfather loves to tinker with broken mechanical clocks in his spare time.
items.ex_zh: 我祖父喜欢在闲暇时间瞎琢磨修补那些坏掉的机械钟表。

items.def_zh: 胡乱摆弄，瞎捣弄；胡闹，瞎搞
items.def_en: (+ with/around) To play or tamper with something carelessly, foolishly, or without permission.
items.ex_en: I strictly warned the apprentice not to monkey with the high-voltage electrical panel.
items.ex_zh: 我严厉警告学徒不要胡乱摆弄高压配电箱。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to meddle with or alter something inappropriately, causing problems
items.ex_en: Please do not mess with the delicate temperature controls on this machine.
items.ex_zh: 请不要擅自乱动这台机器上精密的温度控制器。

items.def_en: (+ with/in) to try to change or influence things that are not your responsibility or concern
items.ex_en: You have no right to meddle in private business that concerns nobody else.
items.ex_zh: 你无权插手那些与他人毫不相干的私人事务。

items.def_zh: 熟练操作，摆弄；操纵，摆布（人或局势）；篡改（数据等）
items.def_en: 1. To control, move, or operate something skillfully with the hands. 2. To influence or control someone or something in a clever or dishonest way.
items.ex_en: Unethical accountants managed to manipulate the financial records to hide their massive losses.
items.ex_zh: 不道德的会计师设法篡改了财务记录，以掩盖其巨额亏损。

items.def_en: (+ with) to interfere with or damage something secretly, unauthorizedly, or illegally
items.ex_en: It is a severe federal crime to tamper with evidence during a trial.
items.ex_zh: 在审判过程中非法篡改证据是一项严重的联邦罪行。

items.def_en: to dishonestly alter, falsify, or adulterate something in order to deceive
items.ex_en: The rogue technician attempted to doctor the laboratory test results before publication.
items.ex_zh: 那个不端的技术员企图在发表前伪造并篡改实验室检测结果。

groups.summary_en: An actor inappropriately, mischievously, or deceitfully meddles with a mechanism, document, or system without authority. The scale ranges from clumsy informal tinkering ('monkey with') to unauthorized illicit alteration ('tamper with') and calculated fraudulent manipulation ('manipulate').
groups.summary_zh: 擅自乱动、瞎摆弄或不正当地篡改机构或数据。
groups.desc_en: Denotes illicitly, ineptly, or intrusive fiddling with a mechanism or situation without authorization, risking damage or corruption, contrasting with proper 'repair' or lawful 'adjust'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在未经授权、缺乏专业能力的情况下对机械、系统或他人事务进行不正当的摆弄篡改或越界插手，区别于合法的“调试”或正规的“维修”。
groups.nuance_en: tamper: make unauthorized, illicit, and harmful alterations (evidence / brakes / election) · meddle: intrusive and unwelcome interference in affairs that are not one's own (affairs / private lives / politics) · tinker: make amateurish, experimental adjustments to a mechanism without expertise (engine / code / clock) · monkey: carelessly and irresponsibly fool around with delicate objects (controls / equipment / locks) · manipulate: control or alter artfully and deceptively for selfish advantage (markets / data / people)
groups.nuance_zh: tamper: 非法篡改、破坏关键物证或重要安全机制 (evidence / brakes / election) · meddle: 狗拿耗子式横插一杠，对无关己事的他人事务妄加干预 (affairs / private lives / politics) · tinker: 业余爱好者修修补补式的尝试性摆弄调试 (engine / code / clock) · monkey: 毛手毛脚地乱摆弄精密仪器或开关导致故障 (controls / equipment / locks) · manipulate: 居心叵测、暗箱操作以操控数据、市场或人质 (markets / data / people)

groups.name: Invert & Upend · 翻转与倒置 (Upend, Invert, Overturn)
groups.tip: 倒置底朝天或颠倒上下

items.def_en: (+ sth) to turn over quickly so that the opposite side is facing up
items.ex_en: Flip the steak over after two minutes to ensure it cooks evenly.
items.ex_zh: 两分钟后将牛排翻个面，以确保受热均匀。
items.ex2_en: The speeding race car lost traction and flipped over into the muddy ditch.
items.ex2_zh: 超速的赛车失去牵引力，翻倒进了泥泞的沟渠中。

items.def_en: [I/T] To tilt or cause to lean over so that one end lifts up
items.ex_en: You need to tip up the wheelbarrow to empty out the wet gravel.
items.ex_zh: 你需要把独轮手推车翻起倾斜，倒出里面的湿碎石。
items.ex2_en: The unsteady wooden stool tipped up when the heavy suitcase was placed on it.
items.ex2_zh: 把沉重的行李箱放上去时，那张摇晃的木凳翘了起来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to reverse the position of something so that the top becomes the bottom
items.ex_en: Carefully turn over the golden pancake once bubbles begin forming on top.
items.ex_zh: 一旦表面开始冒泡，就小心地把金黄色的煎饼翻转过来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to overturn or cause something to lose balance and fall upside down or on its side
items.ex_en: The careless elbow movement threatened to tip over the hot cup of coffee.
items.ex_zh: 那个不小心的胳膊肘动作差点打翻了那杯热咖啡。
items.ex2_en: The fragile ceramic vase tipped over and smashed loudly on the hardwood floor.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的陶瓷花瓶倾倒在硬木地板上，摔得粉碎。

items.def_en: [I/T] To turn completely over or upside down, especially by accident or force
items.ex_en: Violent storm gusts can easily overturn light sailing boats in the open bay.
items.ex_zh: 猛烈的暴风阵风很容易在开阔海湾中将轻型帆船彻底吹翻。
items.ex2_en: The overloaded rowboat overturned suddenly in the middle of the deep turbulent river.
items.ex2_zh: 超载的划艇在汹涌深邃的河中央突然翻了过来。

items.def_en: To turn something upside down or reverse its normal position, order, or condition
items.ex_en: Carefully invert the mold to release the delicate pastry without cracking its surface.
items.ex_zh: 小心地将模具倒置，以便倒出精致的点心而不弄裂其表面。

items.def_en: (medicine / technical) To turn something, such as an organ or body part, inside out.
items.ex_en: The surgeon used fine micro-forceps to evert the eyelid during the delicate procedure.
items.ex_zh: 手术过程中，外科医生使用精细的微型镊子将眼睑外翻。
