items.def_en: [I/T] To overturn or cause a boat or ship to flip over in the water
items.ex_en: A freak wave struck the fishing vessel broadside and caused it to capsize.
items.ex_zh: 一股反常的巨浪侧向击中了这艘渔船，导致其倾覆。
items.ex2_en: Fierce gale winds capsized the small wooden fishing boat in the open ocean.
items.ex2_zh: 猛烈的狂风在远海将那艘小型木制渔船掀翻了。

items.def_zh: （使）颠倒，（使）倒放；彻底颠覆，打乱
items.def_en: 1. To turn something upside down or set it on end. 2. To disrupt, overturn, or throw into disorder.
items.ex_en: The sudden bankruptcy threatened to upend years of careful planning by the board.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的破产危机可能会彻底打乱董事会多年的周密规划。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify physically turning an object upside down, inside out, or reversing its physical orientation. 'Evert' is a technical/anatomical term for turning outward or inside out, whereas 'upend' stresses setting or turning an object on its end or turning it top-to-bottom.
groups.summary_zh: 将物体颠倒放置、上下翻转或自内向外翻开。
groups.desc_en: Denotes reversing the spatial orientation of an object so its top becomes bottom or inside becomes out, contrasting with horizontal 'rotate' or lateral 'shift'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在立体空间中将物体彻底翻转、颠倒，使其上下或内外朝向发生逆转，区别于平面上的“旋转”或侧向的“平移”。
groups.nuance_en: invert: reverse the customary order, top-to-bottom posture, or polarity (pyramid / image / order) · upend: knock over so as to stand on end or throw completely into chaos (cart / industry / lives) · overturn: turn upside down through physical force or legally invalidate (car / boat / ruling) · capsize: turn a water vessel completely upside down in water (boat / yacht / kayak) · evert: turn an anatomical or flexible structure inside out (eyelid / foot / tissue)
groups.nuance_zh: invert: 使上下结构、主次顺序或电荷极性彻底逆转颠倒 (pyramid / image / order) · upend: 将立置之物整个掀翻底朝天，引申为颠覆行业秩序 (cart / industry / lives) · overturn: 物理上将车船翻个底朝天，或司法上推翻前判决 (car / boat / ruling) · capsize: 舟船因失衡在水中彻底倾覆覆灭 (boat / yacht / kayak) · evert: 医学上将眼睑等柔韧组织由内向外反转外翻 (eyelid / foot / tissue)

groups.name: Involuntary Physical Startle · 生理退缩与畏缩 (Flinch, Recoil, Cringe)
groups.tip: 本能受惊畏惧而向后缩身

items.def_en: to make a slight grimace or momentary movement out of sudden pain or distress
items.ex_en: He could not help but wince when the antiseptic touched the raw wound.
items.ex_zh: 消毒药水触碰到鲜红的伤口时，他忍不住痛得龇牙咧嘴。

items.def_en: to pull back one's body or hand instinctively away from an unpleasant stimulus or danger
items.ex_en: She drew back in surprise when the dog suddenly barked.
items.ex_zh: 那只狗突然叫了一声，她吃惊地往后退缩了一下。

items.def_en: to bend one's body down in fear or apprehension; cower
items.ex_en: The terrified captive began to cringe as the interrogator raised his heavy hand.
items.ex_zh: 当审讯者举起沉重的手掌时，受惊的俘虏吓得蜷缩起来。

items.def_en: to move backwards reflexively out of fear, pain, or revulsion
items.ex_en: She could not help but shrink back from the venomous snake coiled before her.
items.ex_zh: 面对眼前盘曲的毒蛇，她忍不住本能地向后退缩。

items.def_en: to jerk or leap backward suddenly in surprise, shock, or alarm
items.ex_en: He started back in horror upon discovering the lifeless body in the shadowed hallway.
items.ex_zh: 在阴暗的走廊里发现那具毫无生气的尸体时，他惊骇地猝然倒退。

items.def_zh: 畏缩，退缩；（枪炮等）后坐，反冲
items.def_en: 1. To move back suddenly in fear, shock, or disgust. 2. (of a gun) To kick backward rapidly upon being fired.
items.ex_en: She recoiled in disgust at the rancid smell rising from the stagnant pool.
items.ex_zh: 闻到死水池中散发出的刺鼻腐臭，她厌恶地往后退去。

items.def_en: (+ at/from) To make a sudden, small movement backward in pain, fear, or shock, or avoid facing something unpleasant.
items.ex_en: The veteran officer did not flinch even when faced with immediate physical peril.
items.ex_zh: 即便面临迫在眉睫的人身危险，这位老警官也未曾退避半分。

items.def_en: to draw back in fear or lose heart in the face of danger
items.ex_en: Even the fiercest warriors quailed when the monstrous dragon emerged from the mist.
items.ex_zh: 当巨大的恶龙从迷雾中现身时，即便是最勇猛的战士也吓得畏缩不前。

items.def_en: to crouch down or shrink away in fear and helplessness
items.ex_en: The frightened puppy cowered beneath the kitchen table during the violent thunderstorm.
items.ex_zh: 狂风暴雨中，受惊的小狗害怕地蜷缩在厨房餐桌底下。

groups.summary_en: A person reacts physically and instinctively by pulling back or tensing up in response to sudden pain, disgust, shock, or physical threat. Verbs describe reflexive somatic defensive movements.
groups.summary_zh: 因剧痛、恐惧或恶心而产生的本能、突发性躯体后退或缩身反应。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an immediate, involuntary somatic retreat or contraction triggered by sudden pain, shock, or fear, contrasting with deliberate tactical retreats.
groups.desc_zh: 指由突发疼痛、惊吓或恐惧引发的本能、非自主性身体缩回或抽搐，区别于有意识的战术撤退。
groups.nuance_en: wince: brief facial contraction from sharp pain (pain / memory / criticism) · flinch: momentary physical retreat from impending impact (blow / question / scrutiny) · recoil: violent spring-back or visceral revulsion (horror / disgust / snake) · cringe: servile or embarrassed shrinking (embarrassment / dread / master) · quail: internal loss of courage and shrinking back (prospect / threat / tyrant)
groups.nuance_zh: wince: 因剧痛或难堪而面部瞬间抽搐 (pain / memory / criticism) · flinch: 面对即将到来的冲击本能后缩 (blow / question / scrutiny) · recoil: 强烈的反冲或极度生理厌恶后退 (horror / disgust / snake) · cringe: 卑躬屈膝或极度尴尬时的蜷缩 (embarrassment / dread / master) · quail: 畏惧退缩且胆气尽失 (prospect / threat / tyrant)

groups.name: Isolate & Quarantine · 隔离与孤立 (Isolate, Quarantine, Segregate)
groups.tip: 制度性分立或疫情防疫隔离

items.def_en: to separate someone or something physically or socially from others
items.ex_en: Authorities decided to isolate the infected patients to curb the pathogen's rapid spread.
items.ex_zh: 当局决定隔离受感染的病患，以遏制病原体的迅速蔓延。

items.def_en: to stop people from getting into an area by surrounding it with a rope, police, or barrier
items.ex_en: Police moved quickly to cordon off the intersection following the major traffic collision.
items.ex_zh: 重大交通事故发生后，警方迅速拉起警戒线封锁了十字路口。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) isolate someone or something completely from access, contact, or outside communication
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: (+ sb) confine or isolate someone securely away from the general public
items.ex_en: The court ordered that the dangerous felon be locked away for public safety.
items.ex_zh: 法院下令将这名危险重犯长期监禁，以保障公众安全。

items.def_en: (+ sb) keep someone in confinement or seclusion away from other people
items.ex_en: Grieving deeply, the recluse chose to shut himself away from the modern world.
items.ex_zh: 深陷悲痛中的隐士选择闭门绝俗，远离现代社会。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) separate or isolate a person, group, or area by enclosing it completely
items.ex_en: Part of the courtyard was walled off to create a private garden.
items.ex_zh: 院子的一部分被砌墙隔开，改造成了一个私人花园。

items.def_en: 1. To isolate a person, animal, or ship for a period of time to prevent the spread of infectious disease.
items.ex_en: Port authorities will quarantine incoming vessels to inspect the crew for infectious fever.
items.ex_zh: 港口当局将对入境船只实施检疫隔离，以检查船员是否感染传染性热病。

items.def_zh: 使免受隔绝；使隔绝影响
items.def_en: to protect someone or something from unpleasant experiences or external influences
items.ex_en: Generations of immense wealth served to insulate the dynasty from harsh economic realities.
items.ex_zh: 几代人积累的巨额财富使这个家族与严酷的经济现实隔绝开来。

items.def_zh: 隔离，使分开；对……实行种族隔离
items.def_en: 1. (+ from) To separate one group of people or things from another, especially because of race, sex, or religion.
items.ex_en: The tyrannical regime sought to segregate minority populations from public life entirely.
items.ex_zh: 专制政权企图将少数群体与公共生活完全隔离开来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe separating people, groups, or entities from others according to institutional policies, disease prevention, or social division.
groups.summary_zh: 因防疫、社会区隔或制度政策而将人或群体分离孤立。
groups.desc_en: Involves physically or socially severing an entity from its surrounding environment to prevent contagion, harm, or interaction, unlike mere solitary retreat.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过物理或社会手段将某实体与外界隔断以防污染、伤害或互动，区别于单纯的独处或隐退。
groups.nuance_en: isolate: generic detachment from context or contact (patient / variable / community) · quarantine: medical or security confinement to halt contagion (outbreak / traveler / ship) · cordon off: police or military physical barricading (crime scene / area / street) · wall off: rigid spatial or psychological barricading (territory / emotion / slum) · insulate: protective buffering against external shocks (economy / shock / pressure)
groups.nuance_zh: isolate: 最通用的脱离接触或分离 (patient / variable / community) · quarantine: 医疗或安全上的强制检疫隔离 (outbreak / traveler / ship) · cordon off: 警力或军方设置警戒线封锁 (crime scene / area / street) · wall off: 筑墙式空间或心理硬性隔绝 (territory / emotion / slum) · insulate: 缓冲式防护以隔绝外部冲击 (economy / shock / pressure)

groups.name: Jar & Agitate Mental Peace · 震扰心神与不适 (Disturb, Jar, Unsettle)
groups.tip: 打破内心平静，产生焦虑烦躁

items.raw_cluster: 扰乱与使不安 Disturb & Agitate
items.def_zh: 打扰，扰乱；使不安，使心烦意乱
items.def_en: 1. To make someone feel worried, anxious, or upset. 2. To interrupt someone or break the peace and order of something.
items.ex_en: These alarming reports of corruption greatly disturb the peace of mind of investors.
items.ex_zh: 这些令人担忧的腐败报道让投资者心神不宁。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to shock, distress, or disturb someone's mental calm significantly
items.ex_en: The new CEO plans to shake up the entire management structure.
items.ex_zh: 新任首席执行官计划对整个管理架构进行大洗牌。

items.def_zh: 激起（烦躁、不安等负面情绪）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to agitate or evoke turbulent, uneasy feelings within someone
items.ex_en: The eerie sound of howling wind would always stir up deep childhood fears.
items.ex_zh: 阴森呼啸的风声总是会激起他童年深处的恐惧。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to upset someone's composure or unsettle their peace of mind
items.ex_en: That unexpected interrogation really rattled up the usually composed defense attorney.
items.ex_zh: 那场意料之外的盘问彻底打乱了向来从容的辩护律师的心神。

items.def_zh: 刺激，使烦躁不适；震撼，颠簸；发出刺耳声
items.def_en: 1. (+ on) To have an unpleasant, annoying, or harsh effect on someone's nerves, feelings, or senses. 2. To shake or jolt forcefully.
items.ex_en: The harsh screech of metal brakes began to jar on everyone's frayed nerves.
items.ex_zh: 刺耳的金属刹车声开始刺激着每个人紧绷的神经。

items.def_en: to make someone feel anxious, insecure, or troubled in mind
items.ex_en: Her mysterious disappearance continues to unsettle the residents of this peaceful mountain town.
items.ex_zh: 她的离奇失踪继续令这个宁静山镇的居民感到心神不宁。

items.def_en: to stir up intense anxiety, nervous excitement, or emotional distress in someone
items.ex_en: The impending threat of war served to agitate the already panicked citizenry.
items.ex_zh: 迫在眉睫的战争威胁让本就惊慌的民众愈发焦躁不安。

items.def_en: to upset the smoothness or composure of someone; discompose
items.ex_en: A single sharp insult was enough to ruffle his normally calm demeanor.
items.ex_zh: 一句刻薄的侮辱便足以打乱他平日沉着冷静的风度。

items.def_en: to make someone worried, uneasy, or emotionally troubled
items.ex_en: The strange whispers heard throughout the darkened manor continued to disquiet her soul.
items.ex_zh: 在漆黑庄园各处传来的奇怪耳语持续让她感到焦虑不安。

groups.summary_en: Depicts external sensory inputs, shocks, or sudden events breaking someone's mental peace, composure, or concentration. The effect ranges from an abrupt clash with sensibilities ('jar') to lingering inner unease ('unsettle', 'disquiet').
groups.summary_zh: 指外界声响、反差或冲击打破内心宁静，引起突兀不安或焦虑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an unexpected friction or disruption that breaks mental equilibrium or aesthetic harmony, contrasting with long-term systemic torment.
groups.desc_zh: 指突发性摩擦或震扰打破心理平衡或协调状态，区别于长期系统的折磨。
groups.nuance_en: jar: harsh sensory or cognitive clash (nerve / ear / sensibility) · unsettle: destabilize composure or certainty (news / stomach / composure) · agitate: stir into anxious, turbulent motion (mind / crowd / market) · ruffle: disturb smooth surface or gentle pride (feather / pride / calm) · rattle: shake confidence through sudden stress (confidence / opponent / nerve)
groups.nuance_zh: jar: 刺耳或冲突的不协调震感 (nerve / ear / sensibility) · unsettle: 动摇镇定、确信或平静 (news / stomach / composure) · agitate: 激起焦虑不安与情绪翻腾 (mind / crowd / market) · ruffle: 扰乱微弱平静或微损自尊 (feather / pride / calm) · rattle: 突发施压使人慌乱失措 (confidence / opponent / nerve)

groups.name: Keep Company Disreputably · 厮混与依附 (Consort, Stooge)
groups.tip: 从日常社交结识到充当附庸傀儡

items.def_en: (+ with) (informal) to spend time together casually as close companions, often dubious
items.ex_en: He wasted his youth choosing to pal around with notorious neighborhood thieves.
items.ex_zh: 他虚度青春，选择跟附近臭名昭著的窃贼混在一起。

items.def_zh: （常指与不三不四的人）厮混在一起
items.def_en: (+ with sb) to spend time socially with disreputable or questionable company
items.ex_en: We used to hang out at the local coffee shop after school.
items.ex_zh: 我们过去放学后常在那家街角咖啡馆闲逛。

items.def_en: (+ with sb) to spend time or socialize casually with undesirable companions
items.ex_en: His parents warned him not to knock about with those delinquent street youths.
items.ex_zh: 父母警告他不要再跟街头那些不三不四的小混混混在一起。

items.def_zh: 充当傀儡，充当走狗；当衬托人，充当配角
items.def_en: 1. (+ for) (informal) To act as a pawn or subordinate tool for someone else. 2. To serve as a comic foil or straight man in a theatrical act.
items.ex_en: The politician refused to stooge for corrupt corporate lobbyists behind closed doors.
items.ex_zh: 这位政治家拒绝在幕后充当腐败企业说客的傀儡走狗。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to associate or keep company regularly with a disreputable group
items.ex_en: Ever since he started to run with that petty gang, trouble followed him.
items.ex_zh: 自从他和那个小团伙混在一起后，麻烦就一直跟着他。

items.def_zh: 亲善来往；（与敌对或违规方）私交
items.def_en: (+ with) to associate in an improper, familiar way, especially with an enemy or underlings
items.ex_en: Officers were strictly court-martialed if caught attempting to fraternize with enemy soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 军官若被发现企图与敌方士兵私相交往，将受到军法严惩。

items.def_zh: 厮混，结交（不良之徒）；符合，相称
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (disapproving) To spend a lot of time keeping company with someone disapproved of. 2. (+ with) (formal) To agree or harmonize with something.
items.ex_en: The prince was repeatedly rebuked for choosing to consort with disreputable gamblers.
items.ex_zh: 这位王子因常常与声名狼藉的赌徒厮混而屡遭训诫。

items.def_en: (+ with) to mix socially with people of higher social status in a familiar way
items.ex_en: The eager young climber loved to hobnob with local high-society figures at galas.
items.ex_zh: 那个急于往上爬的年轻人喜欢在晚宴上逢迎走动，攀附当地名流。

items.def_en: (+ with) to cooperate secretly or deceitfully with others for illicit ends
items.ex_en: The corrupt inspectors were found to collude with suppliers to alter test results.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的质检员被发现与供应商串通篡改检测结果。

groups.summary_en: These intransitive verbs denote socializing or associating with undesirable, suspicious, or illicit individuals, often carrying disapproval or implying sycophantic subservience. 'Consort' carries formal legal/moral disapproval, while 'stooge' highlights acting as an underling or compliant puppet.
groups.summary_zh: 强调与不良分子厮混、沆瀣一气或充当谄媚帮凶。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on sustained, socially questionable or opportunistically intimate association, distinct from standard neutral socializing.
groups.desc_zh: 指与可疑、声名狼藉者长期厮混或出于投机目的进行不当依附交际，区别于正常社交。
groups.nuance_en: consort: illicit or officially forbidden association (criminal / enemy / spy) · fraternize: inappropriate boundary-crossing intimacy (enemy / troops / staff) · hobnob: social climbing mix with elites (elite / celebrity / brass) · stooge: subordinate acting as a subservient pawn (boss / dictator / regime) · run with: informal chronic involvement with a dubious circle (gang / crowd / pack)
groups.nuance_zh: consort: 与违法或遭禁者不当勾结 (criminal / enemy / spy) · fraternize: 违规与敌方或下属越界亲善 (enemy / troops / staff) · hobnob: 趋炎附势地与上流权贵混迹 (elite / celebrity / brass) · stooge: 充当傀儡随从摇旗呐喊 (boss / dictator / regime) · run with: 与不良团伙或圈子厮混 (gang / crowd / pack)

groups.name: Kiss & Embrace by Manner · 亲吻与搂抱 (Kiss, Buss, Smooch)
groups.tip: 亲昵肢体接触表达爱意

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on) to kiss someone quickly and lightly, often on the cheek
items.ex_en: She leaned in to peck him lightly on the cheek before running outside.
items.ex_zh: 她凑上前匆匆轻吻了他的脸颊，随后便跑到了外面。

items.def_en: to draw close to another person affectionately in an embrace
items.ex_en: The exhausted children loved to cuddle up together beneath the heavy woolen blanket.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的孩子们喜欢紧挨着依偎在厚厚的羊毛毯下。

items.def_en: [I/T] (formal or humorous) to kiss
items.ex_en: In the moonlight, the enamored lovers leaned closely forward to tenderly osculate.
items.ex_zh: 在月光下，坠入爱河的恋人深情靠拢，温柔相吻。

items.def_en: (old-fashioned or humorous) To kiss someone.
items.ex_en: The gallant gentleman paused to buss the blushing maiden upon her rosy cheek.
items.ex_zh: 风度翩翩的绅士停下脚步，亲吻了那羞红面颊的少女。

items.def_en: (informal) To kiss and cuddle someone intimately or affectionately.
items.ex_en: Couples lingered under the dim streetlights to smooch before heading back home.
items.ex_zh: 小情侣们在昏暗的路灯下流连，搂抱亲吻后才各自回家。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to kiss and fondle someone passionately over a period of time
items.ex_en: The reckless teenager spent the evening hiding in the car to neck with Sarah.
items.ex_zh: 那个放肆的少年整个晚上都躲在汽车里与莎拉亲热接吻。

items.def_en: 1. To touch someone or something with your lips as a sign of affection, greeting, or respect. 2. (literary) To touch lightly or gently.
items.ex_en: Gentle morning breezes seemed to kiss the fragrant blossoms along the garden wall.
items.ex_zh: 清晨柔和的微风仿佛轻拂着花园围墙旁芬芳的花朵。

items.def_en: (+ with) to engage in prolonged, passionate kissing and caressing
items.ex_en: They snuck off into the empty hallway to make out during the party.
items.ex_zh: 他们趁着聚会溜进空无一人的走廊，激烈地亲热接吻。

items.def_en: [I/T] (informal, chiefly British) to kiss someone passionately for a long time
items.ex_en: The young pair went behind the cinema to snog in the cold dark.
items.ex_zh: 这对年轻情侣跑到电影院后头，在寒冷的夜色中热吻。

groups.summary_en: Individuals touch lips or embrace affectionately, varying from casual peck-like kisses to prolonged romantic smooching or necking.
groups.summary_zh: 用嘴唇触碰或亲密搂抱，从随意的轻触到缠绵激情的拥吻。
groups.desc_en: Depicts physical mouth contact and intimate embraces differentiated by erotic intensity, social protocol, or playful manner, beyond neutral greeting.
groups.desc_zh: 按情欲烈度、社交礼节或戏谑风格细分唇部接触与亲昵搂抱，区别于中性问候。
groups.nuance_en: peck: quick, chaste tap with lips (cheek / forehead / mother) · buss: hearty, noisy, often rustic kiss (cheek / lips / hand) · osculate: formal or mock-clinical kissing (lips / forehead / icon) · smooch: prolonged, affectionate, casual kissing (partner / date / screen) · neck with: intense prolonged kissing and petting (partner / boyfriend / sweetheart)
groups.nuance_zh: peck: 敷衍或纯真的轻触啄吻 (cheek / forehead / mother) · buss: 响亮粗粝、常带乡土气的亲吻 (cheek / lips / hand) · osculate: 庄重或戏谑学术风格的接吻 (lips / forehead / icon) · smooch: 亲昵且漫长的温情相拥亲吻 (partner / date / screen) · neck with: 激情的长时间搂抱接吻亲抚 (partner / boyfriend / sweetheart)

groups.name: Labor & Toil · 劳作与苦干 (Labor, Toil, Busy)
groups.tip: 付出辛勤体力奔波劳碌

items.def_zh: 使忙于，忙着做（busy oneself with/in）
items.def_en: 1. (busy oneself) To occupy oneself with something; to keep busy doing something.
items.ex_en: The clerk began to busy himself with arranging the disordered piles of documents.
items.ex_zh: 店员开始忙着整理那一堆堆杂乱无章的文件。

items.def_zh: 辛勤劳作，苦干；艰难前行；尽力争取
items.def_en: 1. To work hard, especially doing difficult physical work.
items.ex_en: For decades, the devoted researchers labor in search of an effective cancer treatment.
items.ex_zh: 几十年来，专注的研究人员辛勤苦干，寻求有效的癌症治疗方案。

items.def_en: (+ away/at) to work extremely hard and continuously for long hours under arduous conditions
items.ex_en: Penniless miners toil deep underground beneath stifling heat and constant danger of collapse.
items.ex_zh: 身无分文的矿工在闷热难耐且随时可能坍塌的极深地下苦干。

items.def_zh: 做苦工，像奴隶般辛苦劳作
items.def_en: to work extremely hard and continuously for little reward or relief
items.ex_en: She had to slave away in the restaurant kitchen for minimum wage.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不在餐馆后厨做苦工，拿着微薄的最低工资。

items.def_en: to persevere exhaustingly at a strenuous, monotonous task
items.ex_en: He continued to slog away at his overdue thesis late into the night.
items.ex_zh: 深夜里，他依然在埋头死磕自己那篇逾期的毕业论文。

items.def_en: to work relentlessly and laboriously over a prolonged period
items.ex_en: Generations of weary tenant farmers toil away under the unforgiving summer sun.
items.ex_zh: 几代疲惫的佃农在无情的炎炎烈日下不知疲倦地辛勤耕耘。

items.def_en: (+ away/through) to work hard and steadily at a tiring, tedious, and grueling task
items.ex_en: We had to slog through hundreds of confusing audit spreadsheets before morning.
items.ex_zh: 我们在天亮前必须硬着头皮啃完数百张杂乱的审计报表。

items.def_zh: 做苦工，做乏味繁重的工作
items.def_en: to perform menial, unpleasant, dull, or servile labor over extended periods
items.ex_en: The young apprentice was forced to drudge for years without ever learning true craft.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的学徒被迫常年干粗笨杂活，却从未学到真正的技艺。

items.def_en: (+ away/for) to work exceedingly hard like a slave, often with little rest or reward
items.ex_en: I will not slave all weekend just to fix your careless administrative errors.
items.ex_zh: 我绝不会整个周末当牛做马，只为了替你低级的管理失误买单。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe expending continuous bodily or mental effort in difficult, exhausting work, ranging from remaining actively occupied to agonizing over-exertion.
groups.summary_zh: 指付出繁重体力或脑力进行的持续艰辛劳作，从操持忙碌到精疲力竭。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the exhausting, arduous, or servile physical and mental exertion required to complete work, far surpassing neutral task performance.
groups.desc_zh: 强调劳作过程中的极度耗竭、苦累或奴役性付出，远超中性工作的范畴。
groups.nuance_en: toil: prolonged, physically draining labor (fields / vineyards / mine) · slog: slow, heavy, grueling perseverance (book / mud / homework) · drudge: thankless, monotonous, menial routine (kitchen / office / factory) · slave away: exploited or self-sacrificing relentless work (stove / desk / master) · labor: broad, purposeful heavy exertion (loom / vineyard / mine)
groups.nuance_zh: toil: 长期透支体力的重体力劳作 (fields / vineyards / mine) · slog: 漫长枯燥、泥潭般的硬挺硬熬 (book / mud / homework) · drudge: 枯燥乏味且低贱的苦役杂役 (kitchen / office / factory) · slave away: 奴隶般受剥削或自我压榨式苦干 (stove / desk / master) · labor: 广泛而庄重的艰辛劳作 (loom / vineyard / mine)

groups.name: Laborious Incremental Motion · 挪动与费力推进 (Budge, Chug, Inch)
groups.tip: 改变位置或挪动细微距离

items.def_en: [I/T] to move or advance slowly and gradually in a particular direction
items.ex_en: The nervous driver began to edge cautiously past the narrow mountain precipice.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的司机开始小心翼翼地徐徐驶过狭窄险峻的悬崖。
items.ex2_en: The anxious captain edged the massive cruise ship into the narrow shipping canal.
items.ex2_zh: 焦虑的船长小心翼翼地把庞大的游轮缓缓开入狭窄的运河航道。

items.def_zh: 缓慢移动，艰难地一步步挪动
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ along/towards) to move or cause to move very slowly and carefully in small stages
items.ex_en: The heavily loaded carriage had to inch across the fragile wooden bridge.
items.ex_zh: 重载马车只得在脆弱的木桥上极其缓慢地一步步挪动。
items.ex2_en: The nervous mechanic inched the heavy turbine component into its steel mounting bracket.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的机械师小心翼翼地将沉重的涡轮部件缓缓推进钢制安装架。

items.def_zh: 缓慢匀速前行，吃力运转
items.def_en: to make slow but steady progress, often like an engine working evenly
items.ex_en: Despite supply shortages, the local assembly plant managed to chug along reliably.
items.ex_zh: 尽管物资短缺，当地的装配厂依然设法吃力而稳定地运转着。

items.def_zh: 缓慢爬行，极其费力地挪动
items.def_en: to move forward at an excruciatingly slow, dragging pace
items.ex_en: Traffic began to creep along the icy highway under blinding winter blizzard conditions.
items.ex_zh: 在令人目眩的冬日暴风雪中，车辆开始在结冰的高速公路上龟速爬行。

items.def_zh: 步履沉重地前行，艰难跋涉
items.def_en: to walk or advance slowly and heavily with great effort
items.ex_en: Weary pilgrims continue to plod along the muddy track toward the distant monastery.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的朝圣者继续在泥泞小道上步履沉重地朝远处的修道院跋涉。

items.def_en: to progress in tiny, reluctant increments against resistance
items.ex_en: Rush-hour commuters had to crawl along the bridge amid dense morning fog.
items.ex_zh: 早高峰的通勤族不得不在浓密的晨雾中在桥上龟速挪动。

items.def_zh: 缓缓行进，蹑手蹑脚移动
items.def_en: to move slowly, quietly, or cautiously so as not to be noticed
items.ex_en: The shadow seemed to creep silently along the wall without making any sound.
items.ex_zh: 那道黑影似乎悄无声息地沿着墙壁缓缓移动，没有发出一丝声响。

items.def_zh: 微微移动；（使）挪动；（使）改变主意
items.def_en: 1. (usually in negative sentences) To move slightly, or to make something move slightly. 2. To change your opinion, or to persuade someone to change their mind.
items.ex_en: Despite pulling with all our collective might, the rusty boulder refused to budge.
items.ex_zh: 尽管我们用尽了全身力气去拉，那块生满青苔的巨石依然纹丝未动。
items.ex2_en: Three strong mechanics could not budge the heavy iron safe from the floor.
items.ex2_zh: 三名强壮的机械工也无法将沉重的铁保险柜从地板上挪动分毫。

items.def_zh: 咔嚓咔嚓地缓慢移动；发出咔嚓声；（一口气）咕嘟咕嘟喝下
items.def_en: 1. To move slowly while making a regular, muffled engine sound. 2. (informal) To drink all of a beverage quickly without pausing.
items.ex_en: The ancient steam train began to chug slowly up the steep incline.
items.ex_zh: 古老的蒸汽火车发出咔嚓咔嚓的声响，缓缓开上陡峭的斜坡。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame capture difficult, slow, or begrudging motion, either in tiny increments against resistance (budge/inch) or as steady, rhythmic, mechanical chugging across distance.
groups.summary_zh: 在阻力下极其缓慢、吃力地微移或伴随轰鸣有节奏地缓慢行进。
groups.desc_en: Describes motion achieved only through minute, painstaking increments against severe resistance or inertia, contrasting with fluid, unimpeded movement.
groups.desc_zh: 指克服巨大阻力或惰性、以极小幅度吃力推进的运动，区别于顺畅自由的前进。
groups.nuance_en: inch: minute, careful fractional advance (forward / way / margin) · edge: cautious, lateral, or stealthy progression (closer / out / along) · budge: minimal initial movement from a fixed state, usually negative (rock / mind / scale) · plod along: heavy-footed, weary, uninspired momentum (process / progress / path) · chug along: steady, mechanical, rhythmic, unhurried advance (economy / train / project)
groups.nuance_zh: inch: 极其微小、步步为营的寸进 (forward / way / margin) · edge: 谨慎侧向移动或微弱挤入 (closer / out / along) · budge: 撼动原本固着的状态（多用于否定） (rock / mind / scale) · plod along: 步履沉重、缺乏生气的缓慢前行 (process / progress / path) · chug along: 机械式单调运转、不紧不慢前行 (economy / train / project)

groups.name: Lean & Tilt · 倾斜与倚靠 (Lean, Tilt, Slant)
groups.tip: 重心歪斜或向支撑物倾倒

items.def_en: to incline one's upper body backwards against a resting support
items.ex_en: Exhausted from the hike, he chose to lean back against the tree trunk.
items.ex_zh: 徒步后筋疲力尽的他选择向后靠在树干上休息。

items.def_en: to bend or incline one's body sideways or downwards away from a vertical stance
items.ex_en: She had to lean over the balcony railing to catch a better view.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不探出身子越过阳台栏杆，以便看得更清楚一些。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to slope or cause to incline away from an upright position
items.ex_en: A sudden gust of wind threatened to tilt over the tall garden ladder.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的狂风眼看就要将花园里高耸的梯子吹得斜倒。
items.ex2_en: The tall bookshelf tilted over alarmingly during the brief but intense morning earthquake.
items.ex2_zh: 在清晨短暂却强烈的地震中，高大的书架令人心惊地倾斜倒下。

items.def_zh: 倾斜，使成角度移动；调整……的角度；钓鱼；谋取
items.def_en: 1. To move, proceed, or lean at an angle; to place or turn something at an angle. 2. (+ for) To try to obtain something indirectly or fish with a hook and line.
items.ex_en: The photographer angled the mirror slightly to catch the fading afternoon light.
items.ex_zh: 摄影师将镜子微微倾斜，以捕捉渐暗的午后光线。
items.ex2_en: The narrow hiking trail angled sharply upward toward the high rocky mountain peak.
items.ex2_zh: 狭窄的徒步小径急剧向上倾斜，通向高耸的多石山峰。

items.def_zh: 倾斜；倚靠，靠在……上；使倾斜
items.def_en: 1. To slope or bend away from an upright position. 2. To rest against a wall or other support, or place something in this resting position.
items.ex_en: He leaned his heavy wooden ladder against the sturdy brick wall.
items.ex_zh: 他把沉重的木梯靠在坚固的砖墙上。
items.ex2_en: The leaning tower tilted visibly and leant toward the southern horizon over centuries.
items.ex2_zh: 几个世纪以来，这座斜塔明显倾斜并向南侧的地平线歪靠。

items.def_en: [I/T] move or cause to move into a sloping position with one end higher than the other
items.ex_en: Carefully tilt the flask to pour the liquid without disturbing the sediment.
items.ex_zh: 小心倾斜烧瓶倒入液体，切勿搅动沉淀物。
items.ex2_en: The damaged boat tilted dangerously to one side after striking the hidden reef.
items.ex2_zh: 受损的船只撞上暗礁后危险地向一侧倾斜。

items.def_en: [I/T] slope or lie in an oblique direction rather than straight vertical or horizontal
items.ex_en: Golden rays of sunlight slant through the dusty blinds every morning.
items.ex_zh: 每天清晨，金色的阳光都会透过布满灰尘的百叶窗斜射进来。
items.ex2_en: The careful architect slanted the glass roof panels to maximize solar energy absorption.
items.ex2_zh: 细心的建筑师将玻璃屋顶面板倾斜安装，以最大化太阳能吸收。

items.def_zh: 倾斜；倚靠（lean的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (chiefly British English) Past tense and past participle of lean; to incline or rest against a support.
items.ex_en: She leant against the cold stone railing, watching the river flow below.
items.ex_zh: 她倚靠在冰冷的石栏杆上，注视着下方流淌的河水。
items.ex2_en: The tired traveler leant his heavy backpack against the wooden bench to rest.
items.ex2_zh: 疲惫的旅行者把沉重的背包靠在木椅上歇息。

items.def_en: [I/T] overbalance or cause to tilt to the point of spilling or falling over
items.ex_en: A sudden violent gust tipped the canoe over into the freezing river.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的狂风把独木舟掀翻在冰冷的河水中。
items.ex2_en: The unsteady pile of books tipped and fell onto the floor with a loud crash.
items.ex2_zh: 摇摇欲坠的书堆翻倒在地板上，发出沉闷的撞击声。

groups.summary_en: A body or physical object deviates from a strict vertical or horizontal orientation, or rests against a supporting surface for balance.
groups.summary_zh: 身体或物体偏离垂直/水平轴线发生倾侧，或倚靠在支撑面上。
groups.desc_en: Specifies deviation from a vertical or horizontal axis, or the physical resting of weight against a support, distinguishing dynamic bias from static symmetry.
groups.desc_zh: 指偏离垂直/水平轴线，或将重力倚靠在支撑物上，区别于静态的对称对齐。
groups.nuance_en: lean: rest weight against support or incline body (wall / fence / forward) · tilt: deliberate or accidental pivot away from level (head / table / balance) · slant: fixed diagonal orientation or perspective (roof / ray / coverage) · angle: manipulate posture or path obliquely (wheel / trajectory / camera)
groups.nuance_zh: lean: 将身体重心倚靠支撑物或倾身 (wall / fence / forward) · tilt: 绕枢轴倾斜翘起或失去水平 (head / table / balance) · slant: 呈现固定的倾斜斜面或具倾斜视角 (roof / ray / coverage) · angle: 斜向调整角度或走位 (wheel / trajectory / camera)

groups.name: Learn & Master · 学习与掌握 (Skill Acquisition & Role Preparation)
groups.tip: 钻研领会新知并彻底掌握技能

items.def_en: to gain comprehensive, expert control, understanding, or proficiency in a subject or craft
items.ex_en: It took him several arduous years to completely master the classical guitar.
items.ex_zh: 他花了数年艰苦努力才彻底掌握古典吉他。

items.def_en: (+ on) to refresh and improve one's previous knowledge or proficiency in a dormant skill
items.ex_en: I need to brush up on my conversational Spanish before our Madrid trip.
items.ex_zh: 在去马德里旅行之前，我得把荒废的西班牙语口语重新温习一下。

items.def_en: (+ on) to study a specific topic thoroughly and quickly in order to prepare
items.ex_en: She spent the entire weekend boning up on corporate tax regulations.
items.ex_zh: 她整个周末都在突击恶补企业税收法规。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to acquire a skill or piece of knowledge through practice or observation
items.ex_en: Business usually picks up in the spring, and sales figures improve rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 生意通常在春季好转，销售额也会迅速回升。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) to study a subject intensively in order to master it
items.ex_en: Mark stayed up late swotting up on European history before tomorrow's exam.
items.ex_zh: 为了明天的考试，马克熬夜苦读突击欧洲历史。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) to learn a large amount of factual material quickly for immediate application
items.ex_en: He desperately tried to mug up on local trivia before the quiz show.
items.ex_zh: 在问答节目开播前，他拼命死记硬背当地的冷知识。

items.def_en: to make knowledge, rules, or values an inherent part of one's own subconscious behavior
items.ex_en: New trainees must internalize safety regulations until they become instinctive habits.
items.ex_zh: 新员工必须内化安全规程，直至其化为本能习惯。

items.def_zh: 充当（某角色的）替角；学习（某人的角色或工作）以备接替
items.def_en: To learn another actor's part in a play so as to be able to replace them if necessary; to study another's work to act as a substitute.
items.ex_en: The young actor was chosen to understudy the lead role on Broadway.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻演员被选定为百老汇该剧主角的替角。

items.def_en: To learn something again, especially after forgetting it or after an injury.
items.ex_en: After the severe stroke, he had to relearn how to walk independently.
items.ex_zh: 严重中风后，他不得不重新学习如何独立行走。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe acquiring competence, internalized knowledge, or specific operational skills to the point of proficient execution or role mastery.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过练习、复习或跟班排练以获得专门技能或角色胜任力。
groups.desc_en: Centers on the acquisition, rapid assimilation, or specialized absorption of knowledge and operational competence, distinct from abstract intellectual contemplation.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重于知识技能的获取、速成或内化掌握，区别于抽象的纯理论思考。
groups.nuance_en: master: achieve authoritative complete command (language / craft / art) · internalize: absorb values or rules into deep subconscious (norms / values / belief) · bone up: rapid intensive cramming before an assessment (facts / history / exam) · pick up: effortless, informal experiential absorption (habit / accent / skill) · understudy: rehearse specifically to substitute for another (lead / role / actor)
groups.nuance_zh: master: 彻底融会贯通并精通掌握 (language / craft / art) · internalize: 将规范或观念内化于心 (norms / values / belief) · bone up: 临阵突击恶补知识事实 (facts / history / exam) · pick up: 潜移默化、非正式耳濡目染习得 (habit / accent / skill) · understudy: 作为候补专门跟班研习角色 (lead / role / actor)

groups.name: Legal Prohibition & Rejection · 取缔与否决 (Veto, Outlaw, Ban)
groups.tip: 行使公权力否决或取缔非法

items.def_zh: 不予准许，宣布（某事物）无效
items.def_en: to refuse to allow something, typically by finding that it breaches legal or official rules
items.ex_en: The electoral commission decided to disallow several ballots that lacked official signatures.
items.ex_zh: 选举委员会决定认定几张缺少官方签名的选票无效。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) to take strict official action to suppress, restrict, or prohibit an illegal activity
items.ex_en: City authorities have vowed to clamp down on unlicensed street vendors.
items.ex_zh: 市政当局誓言要严厉打击无照街头摊贩。

items.def_zh: 判决无效，推翻（法令、法规）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to officially reject, nullify, or veto a legal rule or statute as invalid
items.ex_en: The Supreme Court voted to strike down the controversial state law.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院投票推翻了这项有争议的州法律。

items.def_en: to decide or declare officially that something is not allowed
items.ex_en: The municipal council plans to ban single-use plastic bags next spring.
items.ex_zh: 市议会计划明年春季明令禁止使用一次性塑料袋。

items.def_zh: 正式宣布……为非法，明令取缔
items.def_en: to prohibit or forbid something formally and officially by law
items.ex_en: The new statute strictly proscribes the sale of unregistered firearms nationwide.
items.ex_zh: 新法规在全国范围内明令禁止销售未登记的枪支。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to suppress or eradicate an unwanted practice or activity completely using decisive authority
items.ex_en: The administration introduced strict measures to stamp out corruption within local agencies.
items.ex_zh: 政府出台了严厉措施，以彻底铲除地方机构内部的腐败现象。

items.def_zh: 宣布……为非法，取缔；剥夺……的法律保护
items.def_en: 1. to make an activity, organization, or practice illegal by law. 2. (historical) to deprive someone of legal protection.
items.ex_en: The government enacted legislation to outlaw the trade of endangered animal parts.
items.ex_zh: 政府颁布立法，宣布濒危动物部位交易为非法。

items.def_zh: 否决，行使否决权；拒绝批准
items.def_en: to use official authority to reject a bill, proposal, or decision, preventing it from taking effect.
items.ex_en: The president decided to veto the controversial tax bill passed by Congress.
items.ex_zh: 总统决定否决国会通过的这项有争议的税收法案。

items.def_zh: 撤销，废止（法律判决或裁决）
items.def_en: to officially reject or declare invalid, especially an official ruling or conviction
items.ex_en: The appellate judges agreed to quash his previous conviction due to misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 上诉法官一致同意因程序不当而撤销对他此前的定罪判决。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the exercise of institutional or executive power to reject a measure or permanently prohibit an activity by statute. They range from formal executive negation of a bill to total legal interdiction and criminalization.
groups.summary_zh: 运用宪法或法定行政权力正式否决法案或依法取缔违法活动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the formal, authoritative suppression, invalidation, or interdiction of practices or laws, contrasting with informal discouragement.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过权威或司法手段对行为或法令进行正式取缔、废止或封杀，区别于非正式劝阻。
groups.nuance_en: outlaw: render an entire activity or category illegal (weapon / practice / group) · ban: general authoritative interdiction or bar (export / book / protest) · veto: constitutional or executive refusal to enact (bill / resolution / measure) · proscribe: formally prohibit as dangerous or unlawful (doctrine / organization / text) · strike down: judicial invalidation of a statute (law / statute / mandate)
groups.nuance_zh: outlaw: 立法将某种行为或组织定为非法 (weapon / practice / group) · ban: 行政或权威命令明令禁止 (export / book / protest) · veto: 行使宪法或高阶权力一票否决 (bill / resolution / measure) · proscribe: 官方宣布某事物危险并予以严禁 (doctrine / organization / text) · strike down: 司法机关裁定违宪并予废止 (law / statute / mandate)

groups.name: Leisurely Strolling & Ambling · 漫步与闲逛 (Saunter, Mosey, Amble)
groups.tip: 无特定目的悠闲漫步游荡

items.def_zh: 随处闲逛，漫无目的地踱步
items.def_en: to amble along without urgency or destination
items.ex_en: They had hours to spare, so they drifted along the quiet boulevard.
items.ex_zh: 他们有多余的时间，于是在安静的林荫大道上随处闲逛。

items.def_en: to walk slowly and in a relaxed manner, enjoying the passage
items.ex_en: Couples often stroll along the riverbank while enjoying the warm summer breeze.
items.ex_zh: 情侣们常在河畔悠然踱步，享受温暖的夏日微风。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to walk slowly and casually around an area without a definite purpose
items.ex_en: Tourists love to wander around the old market, admiring colorful local crafts.
items.ex_zh: 游客们喜欢在老市场里信步闲逛，欣赏五彩斑斓的当地手工艺品。

items.def_en: 1. (+ along/over/into) (informal) To walk or stroll in a slow, relaxed, and unhurried manner.
items.ex_en: Let's mosey over to the diner and grab some hot black coffee.
items.ex_zh: 咱们慢慢溜达去小餐馆喝杯热黑咖啡吧。

items.def_en: to walk in a leisurely way for pleasure or exercise
items.ex_en: The elderly couple loves to stroll through the botanical garden every evening.
items.ex_zh: 这对老夫妇喜欢每天傍晚在植物园里悠闲漫步。

items.def_en: to walk slowly and without a clear direction, turning often
items.ex_en: We meandered along the narrow cobblestone alleyways without checking any maps.
items.ex_zh: 我们在狭窄的鹅卵石小巷中漫步穿行，完全没看地图。

items.def_en: to walk at a slow, relaxed, and easy pace
items.ex_en: The horses ambled along the dusty country trail under the afternoon sun.
items.ex_zh: 马匹在午后阳光下的尘土飞扬的乡间小道上缓步前行。

items.def_en: 1. (+ along/into/past) To walk in a slow, relaxed, confident, and unhurried way.
items.ex_en: He sauntered into the meeting room looking completely relaxed and unbothered.
items.ex_zh: 他步履从容地走进会议室，显得十分放松且毫不在意。

items.def_zh: 闲荡，闲逛；白吃白拿，乞讨（mooch off）
items.def_en: 1. (+ around/about) (chiefly British informal) To walk, stroll, or loiter around lazily with no clear purpose. 2. (+ off) (chiefly North American informal) To ask for and obtain something from someone without paying for it.
items.ex_en: The teenagers had nothing to do, so they mooched around the mall.
items.ex_zh: 这些少年无事可做，便在商场里无所事事地闲逛。

groups.summary_en: An agent walks in an unhurried, relaxed, or casual manner without urgency, often enjoying the surroundings or drifting without a strict destination.
groups.summary_zh: 指从容不迫、步调缓慢、漫无目的或轻松惬意的步行方式。
groups.desc_en: Specifies unhurried, aimless, or relaxed locomotion undertaken for pleasure or idle passage, rather than purposeful point-to-point transit.
groups.desc_zh: 指以休闲消遣或闲散消磨为目的、无确定目的地的慢速步行，区别于有明确导向的赶路。
groups.nuance_en: saunter: slow, confident, swaggering leisure walk (in / down street / park) · amble: relaxed, unhurried, gentle, pacing gait (along / horse / lane) · stroll: pleasant, social, conventional walk for enjoyment (promenade / grounds / garden) · meander: circuitous wandering following winding paths (path / river / through) · mosey: casual, unhurried drifting with colloquial nonchalance (along / over / home)
groups.nuance_zh: saunter: 慢悠悠、自信甚至略带自得的神气闲逛 (in / down street / park) · amble: 步伐舒缓平顺的从容漫步 (along / horse / lane) · stroll: 传统的散心休闲漫步 (promenade / grounds / garden) · meander: 蜿蜒曲折、漫无边际地信步而行 (path / river / through) · mosey: 懒散随性、口语化的慢慢晃荡 (along / over / home)

groups.name: Leverage Advantage · 借势获益与巧用 (Benefit, Capitalize, Exploit)
groups.tip: 从中获取利益与好处

items.def_zh: 得益，受益；有益于，使受益
items.def_en: 1. (+ from) To get an advantage or benefit from something. 2. To be useful or helpful to someone.
items.ex_en: Local retailers will greatly benefit from the surge in summer tourism traffic.
items.ex_zh: 当地零售商将从夏季旅游客流的激增中极大受益。

items.def_en: (+ from/by) to gain an advantage or benefit from a situation
items.ex_en: Clever investors often profit from temporary fluctuations in the international currency markets.
items.ex_zh: 精明的投资者往往能从国际货币市场的暂时波动中获利。

items.def_en: to utilize a situation or resource fully and strategically, often selfishly
items.ex_en: The corporation sought to exploit emerging digital channels to expand market reach.
items.ex_zh: 该企业试图充分利用新兴的数字渠道来扩大市场覆盖面。

items.def_en: (+ on) to take opportunist advantage of an event or situation for financial gain
items.ex_en: Opportunistic scalpers cashed in on the immense demand for reunion concert tickets.
items.ex_zh: 投机的黄牛借着重组演唱会门票的巨大需求大赚了一笔。

items.def_zh: 利用，依仗（声誉或优势）获利
items.def_en: (+ sth) to exploit a reputation, connection, or advantage for personal benefit
items.ex_en: He managed to secure funding by trading on his family's influential name.
items.ex_zh: 他仗着家族的显赫名望设法获取了资金。

items.def_zh: 利用（他人的弱点或特定局势）谋利
items.def_en: (+ sth) to exploit circumstances, fears, or weaknesses to gain an advantage
items.ex_en: The advertisement subtly played on consumer anxieties about aging to boost sales.
items.ex_zh: 该广告巧妙利用消费者对衰老的焦虑来促进销售。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to use an existing achievement or advantageous position as a base for further success
items.ex_en: The startup plans to build on its initial success by targeting foreign markets.
items.ex_zh: 这家初创公司计划以此前的成功为基础，进军海外市场。

items.def_en: to use something to maximum advantage to achieve a desired outcome
items.ex_en: The company decided to leverage strategic partnerships to accelerate global product distribution.
items.ex_zh: 该公司决定借力战略合作伙伴关系，加速全球产品分销。

items.def_zh: 利用，从中牟利（capitalize on）；将……大写；使资本化
items.def_en: 1. (capitalize on) To take advantage of something; to turn something to your advantage. 2. To write or print a word using a capital letter. 3. To provide a company or business with capital.
items.ex_en: The savvy retailer capitalized on the sudden trend by stocking themed merchandise.
items.ex_zh: 精明的零售商趁着这股突如其来的潮流进购了主题商品以牟利。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe actors turning circumstances, situations, or existing resources to their strategic advantage, ranging from passive reception of good to aggressive opportunistic leveraging.
groups.summary_zh: 指利用局势、机会或既有条件为自身谋取实质利益与优势。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on converting an existing resource, asset, or strategic opening into practical gain, distinguishing active opportunism from passive entitlement.
groups.desc_zh: 强调主动将既有优势、资产或破局点转化为切实现实收益，区别于被动坐享其成。
groups.nuance_en: leverage: apply strategic pressure via assets to maximize outcome (asset / brand / position) · capitalize: seize a timely opportunity for advantage (mistake / trend / success) · exploit: fully drain utility or take unfair advantage (resource / vulnerability / weakness) · cash in: monetize or opportunistically cash out on value (fame / trend / stock) · trade on: selfishly use reputation or connection as collateral (name / reputation / connection)
groups.nuance_zh: leverage: 撬动关键杠杆以放大收益 (asset / brand / position) · capitalize: 敏锐抓住稍纵即逝的良机借势谋利 (mistake / trend / success) · exploit: 榨取资源潜能或剥削利用薄弱点 (resource / vulnerability / weakness) · cash in: 趁势兑现变现或捞取好处 (fame / trend / stock) · trade on: 自私地透支名誉或关系谋求便利 (name / reputation / connection)

groups.name: Limit & Restrict Scope · 限制与划定界限 (Limit, Circumscribe, Delimit)
groups.tip: 划定界限以防逾矩

items.def_en: To keep something within a particular amount, size, or level, or prevent it from increasing.
items.ex_en: Doctors advised the elderly patient to strictly limit his daily salt intake.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议这位老年患者严格限制每日食盐摄入量。

items.def_en: (+ to) to put a hard limit on the amount, size, or freedom of action permitted
items.ex_en: Access to the server room is strictly restricted to authorized network engineers.
items.ex_zh: 进入服务器机房的权限严格受限于获得授权的网络工程师。

items.def_zh: 限制，约束（自由或活动范围）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) restrict sb's freedom, movement, or range of choices
items.ex_en: Excessive bureaucracy continues to hem in the company's ability to innovate freely.
items.ex_zh: 繁复的官僚体制持续束缚着该公司的自由创新能力。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) enclose or restrict sb's actions within narrow operational boundaries
items.ex_en: He felt fenced in by the rigid schedule and monotonous daily routine.
items.ex_zh: 他感到自己被死板的日程安排和单调的日常生活死死束缚住了。

items.def_zh: 困住；严密限制（使其无回旋余地）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) prevent sb from acting freely by severely limiting their available options
items.ex_en: My car was boxed in by two huge delivery trucks, and I couldn't pull out.
items.ex_zh: 我的车被两辆大卡车死死卡在中间，根本开不出来。

items.def_en: to severely limit or force a course of action through strict external conditions
items.ex_en: Severe budgetary deficits heavily constrain the municipal council's infrastructure development plans.
items.ex_zh: 严重的财政赤字严重限制了市议会的基础设施发展计划。

items.def_en: to reduce in extent or quantity, imposing a cutoff before natural completion
items.ex_en: Severe weather conditions forced the airline to curtail several scheduled international flights.
items.ex_zh: 恶劣的天气条件迫使该航空公司削减了数趟原定的国际航班。

items.def_zh: 限制，约束（自由或权力）；在……周围画线
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To restrict someone's power, rights, or freedom within strict boundaries. 2. (geometry) To draw a line around a shape.
items.ex_en: The new constitution sought to circumscribe the sweeping executive powers of presidents.
items.ex_zh: 新宪法试图对总统庞大的行政权力加以严格限制。

items.def_zh: 划定界限，界定，阐明……的范围
items.def_en: (formal) To determine, mark, or set the exact limits or boundaries of something.
items.ex_en: Surveyors were deployed to accurately delimit the international border through the mountains.
items.ex_zh: 测量员被派去精确划定穿过山区的国际边界线。

groups.summary_en: Verbs concerning the establishment of finite legal, physical, or operational boundaries that prevent expansion beyond set parameters.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过划定界限、设立参数或制度规范来约束范围与规模。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes establishing boundaries, borders, or structural impediments that confine freedom of action, distinguishing containment from outright prohibition.
groups.desc_zh: 强调通过划定边界、范围或设置结构性障碍收紧行动自由，区别于全盘禁止。
groups.nuance_en: circumscribe: define precise legal, conceptual, or geometric limits (power / role / freedom) · curtail: abruptly reduce duration, extent, or privilege (spending / rights / trip) · hem in: physically or strategically surround and restrict choices (forces / options / town) · box in: trap into a corner leaving no room to maneuver (opponent / policy / strategy) · constrain: compel restriction via external necessity or pressure (growth / supply / budget)
groups.nuance_zh: circumscribe: 精确划定权限、范围或概念边界 (power / role / freedom) · curtail: 削减、截断既有的权利或开支 (spending / rights / trip) · hem in: 重重包围使之丧失回旋余地 (forces / options / town) · box in: 逼入死角使其无计可施 (opponent / policy / strategy) · constrain: 受到外在条件或匮乏的强力拘束 (growth / supply / budget)

groups.name: Lobby & Solicit · 游说与劝诱 (Lobby, Induce, Canvass)
groups.tip: 施加影响促使其赞同

items.def_zh: 做…的思想工作；试图说服
items.def_en: (+ sb) try continuously to influence or persuade sb to agree to sth
items.ex_en: I have been working on my boss to approve the remote project.
items.ex_zh: 我一直在做老板的思想工作，想让他批准这个远程项目。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ for) to systematically solicit votes, subscriptions, or opinions from people in a district
items.ex_en: Volunteers went door to door to canvass for the environmental initiative candidates.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们挨家挨户走访，为环保倡议候选人游说拉票。

items.def_en: (+ into) to persuade someone to do something through persistent flattery or false promises
items.ex_en: She managed to cajole her reluctant brother into lending her his car.
items.ex_zh: 她好说歹说，终于哄劝不情愿的哥哥把车借给了她。

items.def_zh: 招揽；极力游说争取（支持或选票）
items.def_en: (+ sth) try energetically to solicit or obtain political support, votes, or business
items.ex_en: The campaign manager worked tirelessly to drum up support among younger voters.
items.ex_zh: 竞选经理不知疲倦地工作，极力在年轻选民中争取支持。

items.def_zh: 向…施压；施加压力以说服
items.def_en: (+ sb) put heavy pressure on sb in order to influence or persuade them
items.ex_en: She had to lean heavily on her family during those tough months.
items.ex_zh: 在那段艰难的岁月里，她不得不极度依赖家人的支持。

items.def_zh: 劝诱，诱使；引起，导致；催产
items.def_en: 1. To persuade or influence someone to do something. 2. To cause something to happen or exist. 3. To make a woman start labor by giving her medicine.
items.ex_en: They offered substantial tax breaks to induce foreign firms to invest locally.
items.ex_zh: 他们提供大幅税收优惠，以诱导外资企业在当地投资。

items.def_en: To try to persuade a politician, government, or other official to support or oppose a change in the law.
items.ex_en: Tech firms lobby lawmakers intensely to ease restrictions on artificial intelligence research.
items.ex_zh: 科技公司极力游说立法者，要求放宽对人工智能研发的限制。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ for) to ask someone for money, help, votes, or political support in a direct, earnest manner
items.ex_en: The charitable foundation launched a national campaign to solicit donations for refugees.
items.ex_zh: 该慈善基金会发起了一项全国性活动，为难民征集捐款。

items.def_en: (+ into) to exert sustained political, social, or coercive pressure on someone to force compliance
items.ex_en: Aggressive trade groups attempted to pressurize ministers into dropping the proposed tariff.
items.ex_zh: 激进的行业团体试图向部长们施压，迫使其放弃拟议中的关税。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict deliberate political or strategic efforts to influence legislators, voters, or decision-makers into supporting a policy or making a concession. They differ by mechanism: formal legislative pressure (lobby), offering incentives (induce), or systematic door-to-door solicitation (canvass).
groups.summary_zh: 施加政治压力或以利益诱导对决策者进行游说劝诱。
groups.desc_en: Covers concerted communication aimed at influencing decisions, securing votes, or extracting support, contrasting with disinterested information sharing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过有组织或有技巧的沟通来施压、拉拢、劝导以求改变决策或争取支持，区别于客观信息共享。
groups.nuance_en: lobby: organized influence exerted on public officials (lawmaker / government / bill) · solicit: directly appeal for aid, funds, or business (funds / opinion / business) · canvass: systematic door-to-door solicitation of votes or data (voter / district / opinion) · cajole: persuade through persistent gentle flattery and coaxing (friend / support / favor) · lean on: exert coercive social or physical pressure (witness / debtor / partner)
groups.nuance_zh: lobby: 针对官员或政策制定者的组织化游说 (lawmaker / government / bill) · solicit: 直截了当地征求、恳求资金或业务 (funds / opinion / business) · canvass: 逐门逐户走访拉票或调查民意 (voter / district / opinion) · cajole: 甜言蜜语劝诱哄骗 (friend / support / favor) · lean on: 施加逼迫性压力迫使屈服 (witness / debtor / partner)

groups.name: Logistical Transfer & Material Relocation · 物资调运与转运 (Redeploy, Wheelbarrow, Transship)
groups.tip: 人员或货物的调派、搬运转移

items.def_zh: 用车辆运走（大量物资或物品）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) take or transport goods or materials away using a vehicle or heavy carrier
items.ex_en: Sanitation trucks arrived at dawn to cart off the piles of debris.
items.ex_zh: 环卫卡车在黎明时分赶到，运走了成堆的瓦砾碎屑。

items.def_zh: 摆渡运输；往返运送（物资）到对岸
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) transport goods or people across water or a divide in repeated trips
items.ex_en: Small boats were used to ferry essential supplies across the swollen river.
items.ex_zh: 人们使用小型船只将必需物资往返摆渡运送过暴涨的河水。

items.def_zh: 拖运走；重载转运（物资或废物）
items.def_en: (+ sth) transport heavy loads or bulky materials away by vehicle
items.ex_en: Contractors brought heavy flatbeds to haul away the crushed concrete blocks efficiently.
items.ex_zh: 承包商调来重型平板卡车，高效地将破碎的混凝土块拖运走。

items.def_en: to pull or transport large quantities of heavy goods over distance by truck or rail
items.ex_en: Long freight trains haul massive quantities of coal across the rugged mountains.
items.ex_zh: 长途货运列车穿越崎岖山脉，重载拖运大宗煤炭物资。

items.def_en: to transport people or goods by boat, aircraft, or vehicle regularly over a short route
items.ex_en: Small chartered aircraft ferry medical workers between the remote northern Arctic villages.
items.ex_zh: 小型包机在偏远的北部北极村落之间往返运送医务人员。

items.def_en: (+ off/away) to transport something heavy or cumbersome in or on a cart or small vehicle
items.ex_en: Volunteers helped cart heavy bags of rice to the disaster relief center.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们帮忙用推车把沉重的大米袋运送到救灾中心。

items.def_en: 1. To transport materials or goods in a wheelbarrow.
items.ex_en: The gardener wheelbarrowed fresh compost across the yard to the flower beds.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用手推车把新鲜堆肥运过院子，送到花坛里。

items.def_zh: 重新调配，重新部署，转岗
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) To move troops, employees, or resources to a different location or task.
items.ex_en: The peacekeeping mission decided to redeploy specialized forces to the troubled region.
items.ex_zh: 维和特派团决定将专业部队重新部署到动荡地区。

items.def_en: to transfer cargo or passengers from one ship, train, or vehicle to another during transit
items.ex_en: The logistics firm needs to transship the containers from trains to cargo ships.
items.ex_zh: 物流公司需要将集装箱从火车转运到货船上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail moving goods, equipment, or assets between distinct locations, vessels, or strategic positions using specialized transport methods or logistical coordination.
groups.summary_zh: 使用特定工具或通过后勤调度将人员、物资或设备从一处转运至另一处。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to the physical conveying, distribution, or reallocation of bulk goods, supplies, or forces from one station to another, beyond mere personal travel.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及物料、大宗货品或兵力从一处向另一处的组织化转运与配置调度，区别于单纯个体出行。
groups.nuance_en: redeploy: reallocate resources or forces to a new strategic post (troops / assets / capital) · ferry: shuttle passengers or goods repeatedly across a gap (refugee / supply / vehicle) · haul: transport heavy, cumbersome loads over distance (timber / cargo / freight) · cart off: casually or roughly haul away in a vehicle (debris / suspect / trash) · wheelbarrow: transport modest bulk using a single-wheeled barrow (dirt / brick / manure)
groups.nuance_zh: redeploy: 将物资或部队战术性重新部署调遣 (troops / assets / capital) · ferry: 穿梭往返摆渡人员或物资 (refugee / supply / vehicle) · haul: 长距离拖运重载、笨重货物 (timber / cargo / freight) · cart off: 用车将杂物或人员押运运走 (debris / suspect / trash) · wheelbarrow: 用独轮车推运泥沙等粗重物料 (dirt / brick / manure)

groups.name: Lowering Bodily Posture · 屈膝屈身姿势 (Squat, Crouch, Kneel)
groups.tip: 弯折膝盖蹲下或坐定

items.def_en: bend one's knees and lower the body close to the ground
items.ex_en: The photographer had to crouch down to capture the small child at eye level.
items.ex_zh: 摄影师不得不蹲下身子，以便在与儿童视线平齐的高度拍摄。

items.def_zh: 趴下；俯下身子（紧贴地面）
items.def_en: lower one's body quickly to a crouching, kneeling, or prone posture
items.ex_en: When the explosions began, soldiers shouted at everyone to drop down immediately.
items.ex_zh: 爆炸声响起时，士兵们大喊着让所有人立刻趴倒在地。

items.def_en: lower oneself slowly onto the knees or into a deeply sunken, resting posture
items.ex_en: Exhausted by the long march, the weary traveler began to sink down onto his knees.
items.ex_zh: 长途跋涉后疲惫不堪，这位疲倦的旅人缓缓跪倒在地。

items.def_en: 1. (+ down) To go down onto one or both knees on the ground, often in prayer or respect.
items.ex_en: The faithful worshippers kneel before the altar in silent prayer every Sunday morning.
items.ex_zh: 每周日清晨，虔诚的信徒们都会在祭坛前屈膝默祷。

items.def_en: to bend the knees and bring the body close to the ground, often to hide or prepare to spring
items.ex_en: The hunter remained crouched behind the dense bushes, waiting for the deer to approach.
items.ex_zh: 猎人蜷伏在茂密的灌木丛后，静候鹿群靠近。

items.def_en: to squat down low on one's heels, often to stay warm or seek shelter
items.ex_en: We had to hunker down beside the camp stove to escape the bitter wind.
items.ex_zh: 我们只得盘蹲在野营炉旁，以躲避刺骨的寒风。

items.def_zh: 蹲下，蹲坐；擅自占用（房屋或土地）
items.def_en: 1. To bend your knees and sit close to the ground balancing on your feet. 2. To live in an unoccupied building or on land without permission.
items.ex_en: The gardener preferred to squat beside the flowerbeds rather than use a low stool.
items.ex_zh: 园丁更喜欢直接蹲坐在花坛旁，而不是坐矮凳。

items.def_zh: 屈膝（尤指单膝跪地以示敬意）
items.def_en: to bend one knee briefly touching the ground, especially in worship or reverence
items.ex_en: Devout visitors genuflect briefly toward the altar before taking their seats in the cathedral.
items.ex_zh: 虔诚的访客在大教堂就座前，都会面向圣坛行单膝下跪礼。

items.def_en: to lie or crawl on the ground face downwards, especially in abject fear or servility
items.ex_en: The captured thief began to grovel in the mud, begging desperately for mercy.
items.ex_zh: 被擒获的窃贼在泥地里卑躬屈膝地匍匐着，绝望地乞求宽恕。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe lowering one's center of gravity close to the ground by bending the knees, hips, or legs, differing in whether weight rests on the knees, the balls of the feet, or directly on the ground.
groups.summary_zh: 通过屈膝、弯腿降低身体重心或贴近地面的姿态动作。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on lowering the body's center of gravity through bending the legs and torso, contrasting with upright standing or prone lying.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过屈膝弯腰降低身体重心的具体体态姿势，区别于直立站立或水平俯卧。
groups.nuance_en: squat: balance on balls of feet with knees fully bent (floor / weight / heel) · crouch: bend low with limbs close to torso for cover or spring (bush / corner / shadow) · kneel: support body weight on one or both knees (altar / prayer / ground) · genuflect: briefly bend one knee in religious or submissive reverence (altar / presence / tradition) · hunker down: crouch low compactly to take shelter or endure a storm (shelter / storm / trench)
groups.nuance_zh: squat: 完全深蹲、双膝屈曲脚跟着地 (floor / weight / heel) · crouch: 弓身蜷缩以隐蔽身体或准备跃起 (bush / corner / shadow) · kneel: 双膝或单膝着地承重 (altar / prayer / ground) · genuflect: 单膝微屈下跪以示崇敬或屈服 (altar / presence / tradition) · hunker down: 蹲伏缩成一团以避风雨或潜心硬熬 (shelter / storm / trench)

groups.name: Lunge & Pounce · 猛冲与扑击 (Lunge, Pounce, Swoop)
groups.tip: 突然发力向前猛扑冲刺

items.def_en: (+ at/on/upon) to leap suddenly and quickly toward a person or target
items.ex_en: The leopard coiled its muscles and sprang at the unsuspecting gazelle without warning.
items.ex_zh: 金钱豹收紧肌肉，毫无预兆地跃起扑向毫无防备的瞪羚。

items.def_en: plunge forward or downward abruptly toward a target
items.ex_en: Seeing the scuffle break out, the security guard dived in to separate the fighters.
items.ex_zh: 见扭打发生，安保人员猛扑进去将打架的双方拉开。

items.def_zh: 奋身扑向；猛冲向前探扑
items.def_en: (+ for/at) to lunge or plunge one's body forward and downward to seize or intercept
items.ex_en: The agile goalkeeper dived for the ball just before it crossed the goal line.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的守门员在球越过门线前奋身扑了过去。

items.def_en: (+ down on/upon) to move rapidly downward through the air to attack or snatch something
items.ex_en: The hungry hawk swooped down on the field mouse scurrying through the tall grass.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的鹰俯冲向下，扑向在长草丛中疾跑的田鼠。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) attack or leap forward aggressively at sb
items.ex_en: The guard dog flew at the intruder before he could reach the backdoor.
items.ex_zh: 闯入者还没走到后门，看门狗就猛扑了上去。

items.def_en: fly or plunge swiftly downward through the air to attack or seize prey
items.ex_en: An eagle suddenly swooped down to snatch a trout from the rushing river.
items.ex_zh: 一只老鹰猛然俯冲而下，从奔腾的河流中抓起了一条鳟鱼。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ at) to rush forward aggressively and forcefully at someone or something in attack
items.ex_en: The enraged rhinoceros lowered its horn and charged directly at the tourist vehicle.
items.ex_zh: 被激怒的犀牛低下尖角，径直向游客的车辆发起猛冲。

items.def_en: To make a sudden forward movement or attack towards someone or something.
items.ex_en: The fencer stepped forward quickly and lunged at her opponent's chest.
items.ex_zh: 击剑手快步上前，向对手的胸部刺出了猛烈一击。

items.def_zh: 猛扑，扑抓；急忙抓住（机会、错误等）
items.def_en: To jump quickly to catch or attack something; to seize eagerly upon a mistake or opportunity.
items.ex_en: The young kitten coiled its hind legs to pounce upon the drifting yarn ball.
items.ex_zh: 小猫蜷紧后腿，猛扑向滚动着的毛线球。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses sudden, explosive forward or downward bodily leaps targeted at an opponent, prey, or objective, graded from an extended forward thrust to sudden predatory airborne leaps.
groups.summary_zh: 指身体突然爆发性向前直刺、前冲扑跃或猛扑捕捉目标。
groups.desc_en: Depicts a sudden, explosive forward or downward attack launch toward an objective, contrasting with gradual approach or defensive warding.
groups.desc_zh: 指朝目标发起爆发性向前或自上而下的突刺与扑击，区别于渐进接近或防守格挡。
groups.nuance_en: lunge: sudden linear thrust forward with weapon or body (forward / attacker / sword) · pounce: rapid leap downward to trap prey or seize error (prey / mistake / opportunity) · swoop down: rapid, curved downward aerial descent to strike (hawk / police / predator) · charge: full-speed, heavy, head-on frontal rush (enemy / line / defense) · dive: steep, rapid, headlong plunge through air or water (cover / deep / ball)
groups.nuance_zh: lunge: 持械或探身发起的直线突刺与猛扑 (forward / attacker / sword) · pounce: 腾空下扑捕获猎物或猛抓漏洞 (prey / mistake / opportunity) · swoop down: 居高临下、俯冲掠击 (hawk / police / predator) · charge: 正面高速集团冲锋或猛冲撞击 (enemy / line / defense) · dive: 迎面飞身扑救或猛烈下潜 (cover / deep / ball)

groups.name: Malfunction & Sabotage · 故障失灵与毁坏击沉 (Conk, Scupper, Peter Out)
groups.tip: 系统发生故障或计划遭毁

items.def_en: stop functioning properly due to a mechanical or technical fault
items.ex_en: Our delivery truck broke down on the highway during rush hour this morning.
items.ex_zh: 今天早高峰期间，我们的送货卡车在公路上抛锚了。
items.ex2_en: The chemistry lab technician used a special enzyme to break down the compound.
items.ex2_zh: 化学实验室技术员使用一种特殊的酶来分解该化合物。

items.def_en: (informal) of an engine, machine, or appliance, to suddenly stop working
items.ex_en: The old air conditioner finally conked out right in the middle of a heatwave.
items.ex_zh: 那台老旧的空调偏偏在一波热浪来袭时彻底坏掉了。

items.def_en: of a machine or body part, to break down, stop functioning, or fail completely
items.ex_en: After hours of climbing the steep ridge, his bad knee finally gave out.
items.ex_zh: 在攀爬陡峭的山脊数小时后，他那条有伤的膝盖终于吃不消了。

items.def_zh: （机器、器官等）坏掉，彻底停止运转
items.def_en: suddenly stop working or break down permanently
items.ex_en: It's five o'clock—let's pack up and go home.
items.ex_zh: 已经五点了——咱们收拾收拾回家吧。

items.def_zh: （机器等）出故障，坏掉（常作 conk out）；击打（头部）
items.def_en: 1. (informal, often conk out) (of a machine or engine) To break down and stop working suddenly. 2. (informal) To hit someone on the head.
items.ex_en: Our lawnmower engine sputtered loudly twice and then conked completely.
items.ex_zh: 我们的割草机引擎大声突突了两下，然后就彻底熄火坏掉了。

items.def_en: fail, malfunction, or quit working suddenly
items.ex_en: My cheap laptop crapped out just as I was saving the final assignment.
items.ex_zh: 我那台廉价的笔记本电脑偏偏在我保存期末作业时突然报废了。

items.def_zh: 彻底破坏，破坏（计划、协议）
items.def_en: to deliberately destroy, ruin, or bring about the failure of a policy, proposal, or plan
items.ex_en: The opposition party managed to torpedo the controversial bill before it reached a vote.
items.ex_zh: 反对党在争议法案付诸表决前，成功将其彻底破坏阻截。

items.def_zh: 使（计划等）破产，挫败；使（船）沉没
items.def_en: 1. (British informal) to deliberately ruin, wreck, or prevent a plan or opportunity from succeeding. 2. to deliberately sink a ship, especially one's own.
items.ex_en: A sudden transit strike threatened to scupper our holiday travel plans completely.
items.ex_zh: 一场突如其来的交通罢工眼看就要彻底搅黄我们的度假计划。

items.def_en: to spoil or completely destroy a system, relationship, or design
items.ex_en: A series of careless accounting mistakes wrecked their fragile business partnership.
items.ex_zh: 一连串粗心的做账失误彻底破坏了他们脆弱的商业合作关系。

groups.summary_en: Verbs describe mechanical systems or undertakings breaking down, suddenly quitting, or being deliberately ruined and thwarted. They range from an engine or machine abruptly dying to a plan being completely sunk or scuppered.
groups.summary_zh: 机械突发故障停摆，或计划、企图被彻底破坏扼杀。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses both mechanical/bodily cessation of function due to wear and deliberate external wreckage or scuttling of plans, beyond normal wear-and-tear.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖机械或身体因耗竭而彻底罢工，以及人为蓄意击沉破坏计划，区别于正常老化损耗。
groups.nuance_en: conk out: sudden, colloquial breakdown of engine or exhausted person (engine / heart / fan) · give out: complete structural or biological exhaustion (knee / voice / engine) · pack up: British colloquial term for an appliance quitting function (gearbox / battery / body) · scupper: deliberately sink or ruin an enterprise or plan (deal / plan / career) · torpedo: violently blast and destroy a negotiation or policy (treaty / bill / chances)
groups.nuance_zh: conk out: 引擎或体力突然彻底歇菜停摆 (engine / heart / fan) · give out: 结构承受力或机能消耗殆尽而崩溃 (knee / voice / engine) · pack up: (英俚) 机器零件报销停转 (gearbox / battery / body) · scupper: 蓄意击沉、破坏计划使其泡汤 (deal / plan / career) · torpedo: 如鱼雷般彻底轰碎击垮谈判或方案 (treaty / bill / chances)

groups.name: Manifest & Reveal · 显露与表露
groups.tip: 将隐蔽之物公开展现出来

items.def_zh: 显露，展示；表现出，流露；表明，证明；演示，说明
items.def_en: 1. To allow something to be seen, or become visible. 2. To reveal or make a feeling, quality, or attitude apparent. 3. To demonstrate, prove, or explain how to do something.
items.ex_en: The calm diplomat refused to show any sign of irritation during the tense debate.
items.ex_zh: 这位从容的外交官在紧张的辩论中拒绝流露出哪怕一丝恼怒。
items.ex2_en: Her genuine happiness showed clearly in her bright smile across the crowded room.
items.ex2_zh: 在拥挤的房间里，她明媚的笑容清晰地展现出了她由衷的喜悦。

items.def_zh: 泄露，显露（真实情感或秘密）
items.def_en: (+ sth) inadvertently reveal or betray a concealed feeling, secret, or intention
items.ex_en: His twitching eyebrow inadvertently gave away his true anxiety to the interrogator.
items.ex_zh: 他微微抽搐的眉毛无意中向审讯人员泄露了他内心的真实焦虑。

items.def_zh: （品质、情感）明显流露，显现出来
items.def_en: become clearly visible or easily observable through one's actions or demeanor
items.ex_en: Despite her nervousness, her deep knowledge of the subject shone through.
items.ex_zh: 尽管她有些紧张，但她扎实的专业素养依然表露无遗。

items.def_en: be visible or detectable beneath an outward surface or pretense
items.ex_en: Her deep-seated resentment began to show through her polite and polished facade.
items.ex_zh: 她内心深处的怨恨开始从她礼貌得体的表象下透显出来。

items.def_en: to reveal an emotion, weakness, or intention unintentionally
items.ex_en: A brief tremor in her steady voice betrayed the intense fear she felt.
items.ex_zh: 她平稳嗓音中一瞬间的颤抖，暴露了她内心深处的极度恐惧。

items.def_en: to demonstrate or reveal a quality or feeling clearly through outward actions or signs
items.ex_en: Chronic workplace stress can often manifest as severe physical fatigue and headaches.
items.ex_zh: 长期的职场压力往往会表现为严重的身体疲劳和头痛。

items.def_zh: 显露，展示；表明（show 的古旧拼写）
items.def_en: (archaic spelling of show) To allow to be seen, display, or demonstrate.
items.ex_en: The ancient scriptures shew that mercy hath ever been prized above sacrifice.
items.ex_zh: 古老的经卷表明，怜悯自古以来皆比祭祀更为尊贵。
items.ex2_en: His deep inner devotion shewed plainly in every humble deed he performed daily.
items.ex2_zh: 他内心的虔诚在他日常所做的每件谦卑善行中显露无疑。

items.def_zh: 表现出，显露，流露（情感、品质等）
items.def_en: (formal) To show or reveal a particular feeling, quality, or attitude clearly.
items.ex_en: The young candidate evinced great maturity and poise throughout the challenging interview.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的候选人在整个具有挑战性的面试中表现出了极大的成熟与沉着。

items.def_en: to indicate or be a clear sign of a particular state, attribute, or character
items.ex_en: His quiet confidence and meticulous speech bespeak an exceptionally privileged upbringing.
items.ex_zh: 他沉静的自信和严谨的言谈显示出他极其优渥的成长环境。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate making an internal feeling, mental trait, or invisible quality observable through visible behavior, actions, or outward signs. 'Show' is universal, 'manifest' signifies clear outward evidence, and 'evince' is a formal term for indicating the presence of a disposition or emotion.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过神情、举止或外在迹象流露并展现内在品质或情感。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame describe internal states, latent qualities, or concealed truths becoming perceptible through outward signs, contrasting with active verbal declaration by focusing on visible symptom or involuntary leak.
groups.desc_zh: 本框架动词描述内在状态、潜质或隐匿真相通过外在表象呈现，与直接的言辞声明不同，侧重于外露症状或无意识泄漏。
groups.nuance_en: show: neutral baseline of making visible (emotion / symptoms / signs) · manifest: formal emergence into tangible reality (symptoms / discontent / destiny) · evince: formal subtle indication of a trait or state (interest / competence / surprise) · betray: involuntary leakage of a concealed truth (nervousness / origin / weakness) · shine through: inherent excellence radiating despite obstacles (talent / character / sincerity)
groups.nuance_zh: show: 中性显露基准词 (emotion / symptoms / signs) · manifest: 正式用词，显性呈现或外化为实质 (symptoms / discontent / destiny) · evince: 雅词，细微流露特定特质或情绪 (interest / competence / surprise) · betray: 不自觉走漏隐秘真相 (nervousness / origin / weakness) · shine through: 穿透障碍自然流露出的美好特质 (talent / character / sincerity)

groups.name: Mark or Discolor with Spots · 斑点与污迹标记 (Speckle, Smudge, Fleck)
groups.tip: 涂抹污渍使表面不洁

items.def_en: to mark or cover thoroughly with numerous small spots
items.ex_en: Golden sunbeams filtered down to bespeckle the forest floor with dancing spots of light.
items.ex_zh: 金色阳光穿透林叶，使林间地面布满了跳跃的斑驳光影。

items.def_zh: 使沾上墨水或污渍；弄脏
items.def_en: to mark or stain something with a spot of ink or liquid
items.ex_en: A leaking fountain pen managed to blot the official contract with dark stains.
items.ex_zh: 漏水的钢笔在正式合同上留下了斑斑黑墨污渍。

items.def_zh: 弄脏，涂污，使模糊；（墨水、妆容等）被擦模糊
items.def_en: 1. To make a dirty mark or blur wet ink or makeup by rubbing it accidentally.
items.ex_en: Be careful not to smudge the damp ink while signing your name.
items.ex_zh: 签名时当心别把尚未干透的墨水给蹭模糊了。
items.ex2_en: Freshly printed ink smudges easily if you touch it before drying.
items.ex2_zh: 刚印出来的墨水如果在变干前触碰就很容易弄花。

items.def_zh: 使布满斑点，弄上斑点；点缀
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (often passive) To mark or cover a surface with many small spots or patches.
items.ex_en: The artist loved to speckle his canvases with tiny splashes of bright white paint.
items.ex_zh: 这位艺术家喜欢用零星细碎的亮白色油彩来点缀画布。

items.def_zh: 使布满斑点，使有斑驳；点缀
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) (usually passive) To mark or sprinkle a surface with small spots or patches of color.
items.ex_en: Early morning frost had begun to fleck the dark stone courtyard with icy crystals.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的寒霜已然将深色的石砌庭院点缀上一层晶莹的冰花。

items.def_zh: 涂抹掉，用墨水或污迹覆盖
items.def_en: (+ sth) to obscure or cover writing or a surface with ink or spots
items.ex_en: He deliberately used thick black ink to blot out the sensitive financial figures.
items.ex_zh: 他故意用浓稠的黑墨汁将那些敏感的财务数字涂抹遮盖掉。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to spread a greasy, dirty, or sticky substance messily across a surface
items.ex_en: The toddler managed to smear grease all over the freshly cleaned dining table.
items.ex_zh: 蹒跚学步的孩子弄得刚擦干净的餐桌上涂满了油腻污痕。

items.def_zh: 涂污，胡乱擦抹留下污渍
items.def_en: to spread an oily, greasy, or wet substance across a surface accidentally or messily
items.ex_en: Wet paint began to smear across his sleeve when he leaned against the wall.
items.ex_zh: 当他靠在墙上时，未干的油漆在他的袖子上蹭出了一大片污渍。

items.def_en: to cover with small drops or specks of liquid splashed onto a surface
items.ex_en: Passing trucks spattered the clean storefront windows with murky road mud.
items.ex_zh: 疾驰而过的卡车把污浊的路面泥浆溅满了洁净的沿街窗户。
items.ex2_en: Hot grease spatters violently when wet vegetables hit the frying pan.
items.ex2_zh: 湿蔬菜倒入煎锅时，热油会猛烈地飞溅。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote marking, discoloring, or marring a surface by dispersing small spots, droplets, or smeared blemishes across it. They vary by whether the mark is a diffused smear (smudge) or discrete speck-like particles (speckle, fleck, dab).
groups.summary_zh: 指在物体表面留下斑点、污痕或细碎微粒以致外观受损或显现斑驳。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame denote altering or sullying a surface by scattering discrete spots or spreading messy films, differing from thorough uniform painting or coating by their irregular, localized, and often accidental application.
groups.desc_zh: 本框架动词指在物体表面散布斑点或擦涂污渍，与均匀全面的涂装不同，侧重不规则、局部性且常具意外性的印记覆盖。
groups.nuance_en: speckle: scatter small discrete dots across a surface (freckles / stars / bird eggs) · fleck: mark with tiny random particles or flakes (paint / foam / light) · smudge: blur or dirty via friction or wiping (makeup / ink / glass) · smear: spread a thick or greasy substance messily (butter / blood / mud) · blot: absorb liquid or taint with an ink drop (ink / tears / reputation)
groups.nuance_zh: speckle: 点状疏散分布 (freckles / stars / bird eggs) · fleck: 零星微小碎片或光斑点缀 (paint / foam / light) · smudge: 擦拭蹭蹭导致的模糊污痕 (makeup / ink / glass) · smear: 涂抹黏稠油腻物造成的拖拽污迹 (butter / blood / mud) · blot: 墨水等液体滴落污染或吸干印记 (ink / tears / reputation)

groups.name: Mastermind & Detail Plans · 统筹操盘与蓝图谋划
groups.tip: 运筹帷幄绘制行动蓝图

items.def_en: (+ sth) draw up the basic outline or structural blueprint of a plan
items.ex_en: Let us rough out the primary goals before drafting the comprehensive proposal.
items.ex_zh: 在我们起草详尽方案之前，先草拟出核心目标的大纲构架吧。

items.def_zh: 通盘考虑；缜密推敲（计划或后果）
items.def_en: (+ sth) carefully consider all aspects and potential consequences of a complex plan
items.ex_en: They clearly hadn't thought the consequences through before acting.
items.ex_zh: 他们行动前显然没有把后果通盘考虑清楚。

items.def_en: (+ sth) devise or formulate the detailed particulars of a comprehensive scheme
items.ex_en: The research committee met to work out the precise details of the clinical trial.
items.ex_zh: 研究委员会齐聚一堂，详尽制定了这项临床试验的具体细节。

items.def_zh: 详尽拟定并规划（策略或方案）
items.def_en: to plan the details of an operation or project very carefully and systematically
items.ex_en: The committee met to map out a clear strategy for the next five years.
items.ex_zh: 委员会开会为接下来的五年详细制定了清晰的战略规划。

items.def_zh: 详细规划制定（未来进程或路线）
items.def_en: to map out a precise sequence of steps or a definitive plan of action
items.ex_en: The executive committee gathered to chart the company's expansion strategy for the next decade.
items.ex_zh: 执行委员会聚在一起，详细规划制定公司未来十年的扩张战略。

items.def_zh: 为……绘制蓝图；详细规划，制订计划
items.def_en: To draw up a detailed plan, design, or scheme for a project or course of action.
items.ex_en: Urban planners worked diligently to blueprint a sustainable public transport network for the metropolis.
items.ex_zh: 城市规划人员勤勉工作，为该大都市详细绘制了可持续公共交通网络的蓝图。

items.def_zh: 巧妙策划谋定（局面或结果）
items.def_en: to arrange for something complex to happen by clever and manipulative planning
items.ex_en: The clever diplomat engineered a peaceful resolution between the two rival factions.
items.ex_zh: 这位机敏的外交家巧妙谋划，在敌对两派之间促成了和平解决方案。

items.def_en: To plan and direct an elaborate, complex, or secret project, campaign, or crime.
items.ex_en: Detectives believed a corrupt insider had masterminded the daring multi-million museum heist.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们相信，是一名内部腐败人员暗中谋划了这起数百万美元的博物馆大胆劫案。

items.def_zh: 精心策划并统筹调度（行动或事态）
items.def_en: to organize or arrange a complex situation or sequence of actions secretly or meticulously
items.ex_en: The campaign manager orchestrated a nationwide series of rallies to drum up voter enthusiasm.
items.ex_zh: 竞选经理精心策划并统筹调度了全国范围的巡回集会，以激发选民热情。

groups.summary_en: Focuses on high-level cognitive engineering where an architect designs intricate plans in granular detail, or orchestrates an entire complex campaign from behind the scenes.
groups.summary_zh: 以总设计师或幕后操盘手身份周密拟定实施蓝图并统领全局。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame detail the deliberate mental formulation, structural organization, and strategic execution of complex enterprises, contrasting with spontaneous action through their emphasis on foresight, drafting, and systematic control.
groups.desc_zh: 本框架动词描述对复杂事业进行深思熟虑的构思、体系架构与战略谋划，与自发随机行动相对，强调预见性、图纸化与全盘统筹。
groups.nuance_en: rough out: draft preliminary unfinished contours (ideas / sketches / plot) · map out: chart a comprehensive step-by-step itinerary or plan (strategy / career / journey) · blueprint: design rigorous structural specifications (reforms / organization / policy) · engineer: cleverly manipulate or orchestrate behind the scenes (coup / consensus / comeback) · mastermind: direct and coordinate a complex scheme as its central brain (plot / heist / campaign)
groups.nuance_zh: rough out: 勾勒初步未成形草案 (ideas / sketches / plot) · map out: 绘制详尽的分步执行路线 (strategy / career / journey) · blueprint: 拟定严谨规范的蓝图框架 (reforms / organization / policy) · engineer: 幕后巧妙设计、操纵促成 (coup / consensus / comeback) · mastermind: 作为核心大脑操盘复杂计划 (plot / heist / campaign)

groups.name: Masticate & Bite · 撕咬与咀嚼 (Bite, Nibble, Gnash)
groups.tip: 牙齿咬碎与研磨食物

items.def_zh: 细咬，啃，小口咬；（对提议）表示微弱兴趣
items.def_en: 1. (+ at) To eat something by taking very small, gentle bites. 2. (+ at) To show cautious or slight interest in an offer or idea.
items.ex_en: She sat quietly on the bench to nibble at a crisp almond biscuit.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐在长椅上，小口啃咬着一块香脆的杏仁饼干。

items.def_en: (+ sth) bite and grind sth repeatedly between the teeth
items.ex_en: The anxious student would constantly chew on the cap of his ballpoint pen.
items.ex_zh: 那个焦虑的学生总是不停地咬着自己圆珠笔的笔帽。

items.def_en: [I/T] to crush food repeatedly with the teeth before swallowing
items.ex_en: Parents always remind young children to chew their food thoroughly before swallowing.
items.ex_zh: 父母总是提醒幼小的孩子们在吞咽前要把食物充分嚼碎。

items.def_en: [I/T] to chew continuously, especially tobacco
items.ex_en: The elderly rancher sat on the porch and chawed tobacco in quiet contentment.
items.ex_zh: 年迈的牧场主坐在走廊上，悠然自得地持续咀嚼着烟草。

items.def_en: (+ sth) pierce the surface of food or an object with the teeth
items.ex_en: He couldn't resist pausing to bite into the warm, freshly baked apple pie.
items.ex_zh: 他忍不住停下脚步，一口咬进了热气腾腾、新鲜出炉的苹果派里。

items.def_en: (+ sth) bite or chew persistently at sth with the front teeth
items.ex_en: A starving puppy continued to gnaw at the discarded bone behind the restaurant.
items.ex_zh: 一只饥饿的小狗在餐馆后门不断啃咬着那根被丢弃的骨头。

items.def_zh: 咬，撕咬；叮，蜇；咬住；产生不良影响，起作用
items.def_en: 1. To use teeth to cut into, pierce, or grip something. 2. To have a sharp, unpleasant, or serious effect.
items.ex_en: The stray dog threatened to bite anyone who attempted to touch its food bowl.
items.ex_zh: 那只流浪狗凶相毕露，作势要咬任何试图触碰其食盆的人。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on) to chew or bite noisily and vigorously
items.ex_en: The hungry horse began to chomp vigorously on a fresh bundle of hay.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的马儿开始大口咀嚼起一捆新鲜的干草。

items.def_en: To grind or strike your teeth together, especially in extreme anger, frustration, or pain.
items.ex_en: He could only gnash his teeth in bitter frustration at the unfair verdict.
items.ex_zh: 面对那不公的裁决，他只能在极度苦涩和沮丧中咬牙切齿。

groups.summary_en: These verbs describe using teeth or jaws to grip, sever, or grind food or express aggression. Nuances range from delicate, tentative small pecks to sharp piercing cuts and grinding clenches of fury.
groups.summary_zh: 强调使用牙齿对物体进行的轻啄、咬穿、咀嚼或磨切动作。
groups.desc_en: Verbs in this frame depict applying teeth or jaws to grasp, divide, or crush matter, moving beyond generic eating to foreground the mechanical manner, duration, and predatory or nervous intent of the oral action.
groups.desc_zh: 本框架动词指利用牙齿或上下颚咬合、碾碎或截断物质，脱离普通进食范畴，聚焦咬合的机械方式、持续时间及掠食或焦虑动机。
