items.ex_zh: 理发师使用保湿定型啫喱将那年轻人的乱发抹平理顺。

items.def_en: to bring unruly curls, cowlicks, or hair into a neat, manageable state
items.ex_en: A light layer of argan oil helped tame her wild, frizzy curls.
items.ex_zh: 薄薄一层摩洛哥坚果油帮助理顺了她那头蓬乱不羁的卷发。

items.def_zh: 理顺，理齐，弄平整；弄直，变直；整顿，清理
items.def_en: 1. to make something straight, tidy, or aligned, or to become straight 2. to resolve or clear up a problem, confusion, or misunderstanding
items.ex_en: She paused before the mirror to straighten her crooked collar and neat lapels.
items.ex_zh: 她在镜子前停下脚步，理齐歪斜的衣领和整洁的翻领。
items.ex2_en: His bent posture straightened immediately as the drill sergeant entered the barracks.
items.ex2_zh: 当训练军士走进营房时，他原本弯着的腰立刻挺直了。

items.def_en: [I/T] (of birds or people) to clean and arrange feathers or tidy one's appearance meticulously
items.ex_en: The solitary swan paused to preen its snow-white feathers on the calm lake.
items.ex_zh: 那只孤独的天鹅在平静的湖面上停歇，梳理自己雪白的羽毛。

items.def_zh: 用油或水把（头发）梳得服帖
items.def_en: to flatten and smooth down hair neatly using water, gel, or oil
items.ex_en: He quickly splashed tap water to slick down his messy morning cowlick.
items.ex_zh: 他飞快地捧起自来水，把早晨翘起的那撮杂乱头发按压服帖。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify deliberate grooming or tactile manipulation to align fibers, hair, plumage, or garments neatly into place, often using moisture, pomade, or careful brushing.
groups.summary_zh: 梳理毛发、羽毛或衣着，使其整齐顺滑、不杂乱。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves restoring surface order, neatness, and directionality to fibers, hair, or attire, contrasting with mechanical flattening by focusing on cosmetic tidying, alignment, and self-grooming.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指对毛发、织物或外表进行方向理顺与饰容整理，与机械性压平不同，聚焦于体表毛发、衣物的顺整、梳理与自修容貌。
groups.nuance_en: slick: flatten and coat with liquid for a glossy finish (hair / mane) · straighten: align and remove tangles or curvature (posture / hair / tie) · preen: trim, clean, and dress plumage or personal appearance (feathers / appearance / self) · spruce up: briskly tidy and refresh overall appearance (room / wardrobe / image) · tame: bring unruly strands or textures under control (curls / cowlick)
groups.nuance_zh: slick: 用油膏或水梳理抹平并赋予光泽 (hair / mane) · straighten: 理直、消除卷曲或摆正姿态 (posture / hair / tie) · preen: 整理羽毛或自满地修饰外表 (feathers / appearance / self) · spruce up: 快速收拾打扮以显利落精神 (room / wardrobe / image) · tame: 抚平驯服杂乱乱翘的毛发 (curls / cowlick)

groups.name: Smooth & Flatten · 抚平与熨平 (Smooth, Iron, Plane)
groups.tip: 压平凸起褶皱令表面光洁

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make or become level, flat, or free of uneven bumps
items.ex_en: Use a heavy rolling pin to flatten out the chilled pastry dough.
items.ex_zh: 用沉重的擀面杖将冷藏过的油酥面团压平。
items.ex2_en: The rocky mountain trail gradually flattens out near the peaceful valley floor.
items.ex2_zh: 岩石嶙峋的山路在靠近宁静谷底的地方逐渐变得平缓。

items.def_en: to eliminate wrinkles, folds, or bumps by pressing softly with the hands or an instrument
items.ex_en: She used both hands to smooth out the wrinkles on the tablecloth.
items.ex_zh: 她用双手抚平桌布上的褶皱。

items.def_zh: 抚平，使平整，使光滑；消除（障碍），使顺利
items.def_en: 1. to make a surface flat, level, or smooth, especially by pressing or rubbing 2. to make a process or situation easier by removing difficulties
items.ex_en: The mason used a trowel to smooth the wet surface of the fresh cement.
items.ex_zh: 泥瓦匠用抹刀将新水泥潮湿的表面抹平整。
items.ex2_en: The rough wooden surface smoothed nicely after several rounds of careful sanding.
items.ex2_zh: 经过几轮细致的打磨后，粗糙的木质表面变得光滑了。

items.def_en: to make a surface, texture, or situation smoother, flatter, or more even
items.ex_en: Regularly applying this thick cream will gradually smoothen the rough skin on your elbows.
items.ex_zh: 经常涂抹这种厚重的面霜会逐渐使你手肘上的粗糙皮肤变得光滑。
items.ex2_en: The dry skin on her hands smoothened quickly with regular moisturizer application.
items.ex2_zh: 经常涂抹保湿霜后，她手上干燥的皮肤迅速变得光滑了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove creases from fabric or clothing by pressing with a hot iron
items.ex_en: I need to iron out the creases in my cotton shirt before the interview.
items.ex_zh: 面试前我得把棉质衬衫上的褶皱熨平。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a wooden or painted surface completely smooth by rubbing it with sandpaper
items.ex_en: He had to sand down the old desk completely before applying the new varnish.
items.ex_zh: 在涂新清漆之前，他必须把旧书桌彻底砂光磨平。

items.def_en: [I/T] to remove creases from fabric by applying pressure with a heated iron
items.ex_en: She spent the morning ironing linen napkins to prepare for the dinner party.
items.ex_zh: 她花了一个上午熨烫亚麻餐巾，为晚宴做准备。

items.def_en: to shave thin layers off wood to make the surface level and silky
items.ex_en: The carpenter carefully planed the edge of the swollen door so it would shut.
items.ex_zh: 木匠仔细地刨平了发胀的门边，好让门能关上。

items.def_en: to polish or smooth wood or metal surfaces by rubbing with sandpaper
items.ex_en: You should sand the wooden banister thoroughly until there are no splinters remaining.
items.ex_zh: 你应该彻底打磨木制栏杆，直到没有任何毛刺为止。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote removing surface roughness, creases, or minor bumps to create a sleek, silky, or uniform texture, typically using gentle manual strokes, tools, or heat.
groups.summary_zh: 用手工抚摩、熨烫或细木工工具消除折皱与粗糙表面。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves removing physical wrinkles, ridges, or conceptual friction to create an even, planar surface, contrasting with general reduction by targeting spatial asperities through pressure, heat, or abrasion.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指通过施压、热力或研磨消除物理皱褶、凸凹或抽象摩擦以呈现平整界面，与一般缩减不同，专指针对表面不平整的机械性铲平与抹光。
groups.nuance_en: smooth: eliminate irregularities or wrinkles by gentle touch or stroke (fabric / surface / brow) · iron out: resolve wrinkles or figuratively settle discrepancies (creases / differences / wrinkles) · plane: shave wood to a flat uniform grade with a bladed tool (timber / board) · sand down: abrade surface coarseness using an abrasive medium (wood / tabletop / primer) · flatten out: press or spread something level across a plane (wrinkles / curve / dough)
groups.nuance_zh: smooth: 抚平、抹去褶皱或表面粗糙 (fabric / surface / brow) · iron out: 熨平布料皱痕或比喻消除分歧障碍 (creases / differences / wrinkles) · plane: 用刨刀削平木料表面 (timber / board) · sand down: 用砂纸磨平表面毛刺 (wood / tabletop / primer) · flatten out: 压平、展平成水平状 (wrinkles / curve / dough)

groups.name: Soil & Besmirch · 玷污与弄脏 (Blot, Tarnish, Befoul)
groups.tip: 沾染污渍油垢，损毁清白整洁

items.def_en: (+ sth) make something dirty or muddy
items.ex_en: The playful dogs managed to muck up the clean rug with wet garden soil.
items.ex_zh: 淘气的狗狗们用潮湿的花园泥巴把干净的地毯弄得脏兮兮的。

items.def_en: (+ sth) dirty or blur a surface with streaks or smudges
items.ex_en: The toddlers always smudge up the glass sliding doors with their sticky little fingers.
items.ex_zh: 幼儿们总是用黏糊糊的小手把玻璃移门蹭得到处都是污迹。

items.def_en: [T/I] Make or become dirty on the surface, especially with earth, mud, or excrement
items.ex_en: Heavy autumn rains quickly soiled the soldiers' clean uniforms with thick, stubborn mud.
items.ex_zh: 秋季的暴雨很快用厚重顽固的泥浆弄脏了士兵们干净的制服。
items.ex2_en: Her delicate white silk blouse soils very easily in dusty outdoor environments.
items.ex2_zh: 在多尘的户外环境中，她精致的白丝绸衬衫极易弄脏。

items.def_zh: 弄脏，染上污渍；玷污（名誉等）；（用吸水纸）吸干；（blot out）遮蔽，抹去
items.def_en: 1. To spot, stain, or spatter something with liquid or ink; to tarnish someone's character or reputation. 2. To dry wet ink or liquid by pressing absorbent paper against it. 3. ('blot out') To obscure from sight or completely wipe from memory.
items.ex_en: A sudden leak from the fountain pen blotted the crisp parchment with dark ink.
items.ex_zh: 钢笔突然漏水，在崭新的羊皮纸上染上了黑墨渍。

items.def_en: [T/I] Cause dirty marks or smears on a surface, obscuring clarity
items.ex_en: Be careful not to smudge the freshly painted wooden frame with your greasy thumbs.
items.ex_zh: 小心别用油腻的大拇指把刚刷好油漆的木框蹭上污迹。
items.ex2_en: Wet ink smudges easily if you turn the page without drying it.
items.ex2_zh: 如果没有晾干就翻页，未干的墨水很容易被蹭花弄脏。

items.def_zh: （使）失去光泽，变暗淡；玷污，损害（名誉）
items.def_en: 1. To lose brightness or shine through exposure to air or moisture, or cause metal to discolor. 2. To damage, spoil, or stain someone's good reputation.
items.ex_en: Damp salty air from the coast will rapidly tarnish any unprotected silver cutlery.
items.ex_zh: 来自海边的潮湿含盐空气会迅速让任何未经保护的银质餐具失去光泽。
items.ex2_en: Polished silver forks will tarnish quickly if stored inside humid basement cabinets.
items.ex2_zh: 如果存放在潮湿的地下室橱柜里，擦亮的银叉很快就会失去光泽。

items.def_zh: 弄脏，弄污；施肥于；（muck up）搞砸，弄乱；（muck out）清理（牲口棚）
items.def_en: 1. To make something dirty or muddy; to spread manure on soil. 2. ('muck up') (informal) To spoil, ruin, or make a mess of something. 3. ('muck out') To clean manure from a stable or animal enclosure.
items.ex_en: Don't muck your clean boots by walking straight across that muddy vegetable patch.
items.ex_zh: 别直接穿过那片泥泞的菜地把干净的靴子弄脏。

items.def_en: Damage someone's good name, honor, or reputation; soil or tarnish integrity
items.ex_en: Malicious political rivals sought to besmirch the minister's honorable reputation with unfounded rumors.
items.ex_zh: 怀有恶意的政治对手企图用毫无根据的谣言来玷污这位部长的良好声誉。

items.def_en: Make foul, dirty, or filthy with offensive matter; defile morally
items.ex_en: Industrial waste continued to befoul the pristine mountain streams with toxic chemical sludge.
items.ex_zh: 工业废料继续用有毒的化学污泥污染着原本清澈原始的山间溪流。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame cover the physical dirtying, staining, or discoloring of a surface, alongside the figurative degradation of an individual's honor, reputation, or purity. Nuances scale from surface smudges to severe corrosive or reputational spoiling.
groups.summary_zh: 指弄脏、留下斑印或玷污使表面变暗，引申为损害声誉或纯洁性。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves degrading the cleanliness, luster, or purity of a surface or reputation through contact with grime or moral contagion, contrasting with physical damage by emphasizing foul discoloration and loss of honor.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指因污秽接触或道德玷染导致物理表面或抽象名誉失去洁净、光泽与纯正，与物理破坏不同，强调发黑、斑渍化及名节受损。
groups.nuance_en: soil: make dirty on the physical surface or morally degrade (linen / hands / name) · tarnish: dull the bright luster of metal or discolor reputation (silver / reputation / image) · besmirch: cast persistent moral aspersion or stain on honor (reputation / character / honor) · blot: spot with ink/liquid or create an indelible blemish (record / copybook / escutcheon) · smudge: blur or smear by rubbing with greasy dirt (lens / makeup / glass)
groups.nuance_zh: soil: 弄脏衣物表面或在道德上蒙垢 (linen / hands / name) · tarnish: 使金属失去光泽或使声誉蒙尘 (silver / reputation / image) · besmirch: 诽谤诋毁以玷污名誉品格 (reputation / character / honor) · blot: 墨渍弄脏或留下不可磨灭的污点 (record / copybook / escutcheon) · smudge: 因蹭擦油脂污垢而留下污痕模糊物面 (lens / makeup / glass)

groups.name: Soothe & Console · 安抚与慰藉 (Comfort, Console, Soothe)
groups.tip: 平复痛苦焦虑，给予心理温存

items.def_en: To make someone feel calmer and less worried, unhappy, or upset; to console.
items.ex_en: She gently wrapped an arm around her sister to comfort her after the bad news.
items.ex_zh: 得知坏消息后，她轻轻搂住妹妹的肩膀以抚慰她。

items.def_en: (+ sb) make someone feel more peaceful, tranquil, or less distressed
items.ex_en: The teacher spoke softly to calm down the frantic children after the fire alarm.
items.ex_zh: 火警响起后，老师轻声说话让慌乱的孩子们平静下来。
items.ex2_en: The upset crowd calmed down after the speaker addressed their main concerns.
items.ex2_zh: 演讲者回应了他们的主要关切后，不安的人群平静了下来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) relieve or ease pain, worry, or tension through gentle care
items.ex_en: Her tender melodic singing seemed to soothe away all his lingering exhaustion and sorrow.
items.ex_zh: 她温柔悠扬的歌声似乎抚平了他心头挥之不去的疲惫与忧伤。

items.def_en: To give comfort or sympathy to someone who is unhappy, disappointed, or grieving.
items.ex_en: Neighbors gathered to console the grieving widow after the sudden loss of her husband.
items.ex_zh: 丈夫猝逝后，邻居们聚集在一起慰藉悲痛万分的遗孀。

items.def_zh: 使放心，打消……的疑虑或恐惧
items.def_en: to say or do something that removes the doubts, fears, or anxieties of someone
items.ex_en: The doctor spoke with confidence to reassure the nervous parents about the routine procedure.
items.ex_zh: 医生自信地开口，打消了这对紧张父母关于常规手术的顾虑。

items.def_zh: 抚慰，使平静；缓解（疼痛或焦虑）
items.def_en: to gently calm a person, their feelings, or to reduce bodily pain and irritation
items.ex_en: She applied a fragrant aloe lotion to soothe the stinging sunburn on her shoulders.
items.ex_zh: 她涂抹了芬芳的芦荟乳液，以缓解肩膀上刺痛的晒伤。

items.def_zh: 抚慰，在忧伤中慰藉（文雅）
items.def_en: (formal/literary) to give comfort, consolation, or relief to someone in distress or disappointment
items.ex_en: He solaced the lonely traveler with warm bread and tales of better days ahead.
items.ex_zh: 他用热面包和对未来美好时光的讲述，慰藉了那位孤独的旅人。

items.def_zh: 抚慰，平复（负罪感、受挫的自尊等）；涂药膏于
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To soothe or ease guilt, wounded pride, or hurt feelings. 2. (dated) To apply a healing ointment to a wound.
items.ex_en: A generous charitable donation could scarcely salve his guilty conscience after betraying his partner.
items.ex_zh: 在背叛合伙人后，一笔慷慨的慈善捐款也难以抚平他内心的负罪感。

items.def_zh: 减轻，缓解，平息（担忧、恐惧或疑虑）
items.def_en: (formal) To calm or reduce fear, worry, suspicion, or pain.
items.ex_en: The mayor held an emergency briefing to allay growing public fears regarding the flood.
items.ex_zh: 市长举行了紧急简报会，以平息公众对洪灾日益加剧的恐慌。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame focus on relieving another person's sorrow, grief, physical distress, or anxious apprehension through sympathy, warmth, and reassuring presence. Unlike political placating, these actions target pain and emotional woundedness rather than aggressive wrath.
groups.summary_zh: 缓解他人的悲伤、痛苦、创伤或忧惧，给予温情与抚慰。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves applying emotional warmth, reassurance, or tranquilizing influence to alleviate grief, pain, or psychic distress, contrasting with practical problem-solving by emphasizing affective restoration and empathetic easement.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指运用情感温情、宽慰或平抑力量以纾解悲恸、创痛或精神焦虑，与实际解决问题不同，强调情感心理层面的镇抚、陪伴与温存修复。
groups.nuance_en: comfort: impart strength, hope, and relief from sorrow (child / grieving / widow) · console: offer compassionate solace specifically in bereavement or defeat (mourner / loser / family) · soothe: pacify irritation, physical pain, or acute agitation (nerves / burn / throat) · solace: deeply mitigate sadness through mental peace or quiet companionship (solitude / heart / mind) · reassure: dispel doubts and fears by restoring confidence (fears / doubts / investor)
groups.nuance_zh: comfort: 给予关怀鼓励以抚平悲伤痛苦 (child / grieving / widow) · console: 专指在丧亲或受挫时予以哀悼慰藉 (mourner / loser / family) · soothe: 平息生理刺痛、神经紧绷或激化情绪 (nerves / burn / throat) · solace: 给予深层精神慰藉以排遣孤寂沉痛 (solitude / heart / mind) · reassure: 消除疑虑恐惧以重树安全感 (fears / doubts / investor)

groups.name: Speak & Articulate · 发声与语音吐字 (Utter, Aspirate, Mispronounce)
groups.tip: 开口发音与言辞表达

items.def_en: (+ sth) articulate distinct letter sounds or syllables one by one to form a word
items.ex_en: The manager quietly sounded out a few team members before unveiling the restructuring plan.
items.ex_zh: 经理在公布重组方案之前，私下试探了几名团队成员的口风。

items.def_zh: 发出某词或字母的标准读音
items.def_en: [I/T] to make the sound of a word or letter in a particular way
items.ex_en: Few foreign students can pronounce that difficult French vowel sound with complete accuracy.
items.ex_zh: 很少有外国学生能完全准确地发出那个难读的法语元音。

items.def_en: 1. To make a sound with your voice; to say something.
items.ex_en: The stunned witness could barely utter a single word to the questioning detectives.
items.ex_zh: 惊魂未定的目击者面对侦探的讯问几乎说不出一个字来。

items.def_zh: 送气发音，以送气音读出；抽吸（体液等）
items.def_en: 1. (phonetics) To pronounce a sound with an audible breath release. 2. (medicine) To draw fluid or gas out of a body cavity.
items.ex_en: Native English speakers routinely aspirate voiceless stops at the beginning of stressed syllables.
items.ex_zh: 讲英语的母语者通常在重读音节开头的清塞音上送气发音。

items.def_en: 1. To pronounce a word or name incorrectly.
items.ex_en: The nervous host managed to mispronounce the guest speaker's distinguished foreign surname.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的主持人不小心把特邀嘉宾那显赫的外国姓氏给读错了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) articulate or utter words abruptly or with difficulty
items.ex_en: Just spit out the truth already instead of keeping us all in suspense!
items.ex_zh: 快把真相吐出来吧，别再让我们大家吊着一颗心了！

items.def_zh: 声带发声或将想法说出
items.def_en: [I/T] to utter sounds or words using the vocal cords
items.ex_en: The pre-verbal infant began to vocalize distinct rhythmic syllables while playing with wooden blocks.
items.ex_zh: 尚未学会说话的婴儿在玩积木时开始发出清晰且有节奏的声音。

items.def_zh: 清晰连贯地表达音节或话语
items.def_en: [I/T] to pronounce distinct syllables clearly or express thoughts smoothly
items.ex_en: The brilliant debater could articulate complex ethical principles with remarkable clarity and poise.
items.ex_zh: 这位才华横溢的辩手能够沉着、极为清晰地阐明复杂的伦理原则。

items.def_en: [I/T] to pronounce words, syllables, or sounds distinctly and clearly
items.ex_en: The voice coach instructed the actor to enunciate every final consonant with precision.
items.ex_zh: 台词教练指导这位演员极其精准地吐出每一个词尾辅音。

groups.summary_en: A speaker employs the vocal apparatus to form phonemes, release breath, or pronounce verbal tokens, emphasizing physical phonetic mechanics.
groups.summary_zh: 通过发音器官调控气流与音节，侧重语音与吐字机制。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema centers on the biomechanical and phonetic production of vocal sounds and recognizable speech tokens, contrasting with communicative discourse (talk/say) by focusing purely on acoustic utterance, phonation, and phonetic clarity.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式聚焦于人类发音器官发声与音素形成的生物力学过程，与言语交际（talk/say）不同，纯粹着眼于发声、咬字发音及音韵清晰度。
groups.nuance_en: utter: emit any audible sound or vocal expression, even minimally (word / cry / sound) · articulate: speak syllables with distinct phonetic clarity and precision (vowels / thoughts / sounds) · pronounce: produce the phonetic realization of a word correctly (syllables / word / name) · aspirate: pronounce with an audible accompanying puff of breath (consonant / vowel / stop) · vocalize: generate raw vocal tone or voice a non-lexical acoustic response (tune / feelings / cry)
groups.nuance_zh: utter: 发出任何可听见的字词或微弱声音 (word / cry / sound) · articulate: 咬字清晰、发音准确地吐字 (vowels / thoughts / sounds) · pronounce: 按照标准音标念出词句 (syllables / word / name) · aspirate: 发音时伴随呼气声或送气 (consonant / vowel / stop) · vocalize: 产生声带发声或将感受以语音形式哼唱发出 (tune / feelings / cry)

groups.name: Speculate & Conecture · 猜想与推测 (Conjecture, Surmise, Presuppose)
groups.tip: 凭直觉或模糊线索猜测

items.def_en: 1. To estimate or form an opinion about something without having enough facts. 2. (informal) To think, suppose, or believe.
items.ex_en: I guess we might as well grab some dinner before the movie starts tonight.
items.ex_zh: 我猜我们不妨在今晚电影开场前随便吃点晚饭。

items.def_en: make a guess or conjecture despite lacking complete information
items.ex_en: Without consulting the official balance sheet, the auditor refused to hazard a guess.
items.ex_zh: 在没有查阅正式资产负债表之前，审计师拒绝进行盲目推测。

items.def_en: (+ sth) form an opinion or expectation based on conjecture
items.ex_en: I reckon on good weather tomorrow, so we should plan for the beach trip.
items.ex_zh: 我估计明天天气不错，所以我们该规划一下去海滩的行程。

items.def_en: [T/I] to form an opinion or supposition about something without sufficient evidence
items.ex_en: Ancient astronomers could only conjecture about the unseen planetary surfaces through crude telescopes.
items.ex_zh: 古代天文学家只能通过粗糙的望远镜对看不见的行星表面进行推测。

items.def_en: to put forward an explanation or hypothesis as a basis for argument
items.ex_en: Philosophers posit that subjective experience cannot be fully explained by simple neurological mechanisms.
items.ex_zh: 哲学家们假设，主观体验无法完全用简单的神经机制来解释。

items.def_en: to suggest or accept something as a basic fact or truth for reasoning
items.ex_en: Modern physicists postulate the existence of dark matter to balance mathematical cosmic equations.
items.ex_zh: 现代物理学家假定暗物质的存在，以平衡宇宙学的数学方程式。

items.def_en: [T/I] to put forward a tentative assumption in order to draw out and test its consequences
items.ex_en: Epidemiologists hypothesize that the new variant possesses a substantially higher transmission rate.
items.ex_zh: 流行病学家提出假说，认为这种新变种具有明显更高的传播率。

items.def_en: (formal) To guess or infer that something is true based on incomplete evidence.
items.ex_en: From the abandoned car, detectives could only surmise that the driver left abruptly.
items.ex_zh: 根据那辆被遗弃的汽车，侦探们只能推测司机是匆忙离开的。

items.def_zh: 预先假定，假定；以……为先决条件
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To assume or accept something as true before having proof. 2. (formal) To require something to exist or be true as a necessary prior condition.
items.ex_en: This revolutionary socio-economic model must presuppose an equitable distribution of shared natural resources.
items.ex_zh: 这一开创性的社会经济模型必须预先假定自然资源能够得到公平分配。

groups.summary_en: Cognizers form beliefs or hypotheses based on incomplete evidence, underlying assumptions, or intuition. The verbs differ in register and epistemic grounding, from informal everyday guesses to formal, deductive premises.
groups.summary_zh: 基于不充分证据或先入为主的前提出发，形成假定或猜想。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves projecting hypotheses, intuitive leaps, or intellectual estimations on incomplete evidence, contrasting with grounded deduction by highlighting probabilistic intuition, provisional modeling, and epistemic uncertainty.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指在缺乏确凿证据下凭借直觉飞跃或思维建模进行试探性推演，与实证演绎不同，强调认知前提的不确定性与假设性推断。
groups.nuance_en: conjecture: form an opinion based on flimsy or circumstantial signs (intentions / motives / origin) · surmise: infer intuitively from tenuous clues without definitive proof (outcome / truth / reason) · postulate: stipulate a foundational proposition as the basis for reasoning (existence / axiom / theory) · hypothesize: advance a structured, testable proposal to explain phenomena (relationship / mechanism / model) · guess: hazard an offhand or intuitive judgment with little certainty (answer / weight / age)
groups.nuance_zh: conjecture: 根据蛛丝马迹或薄弱证据推测 (intentions / motives / origin) · surmise: 凭直觉神会从端倪中揣度 (outcome / truth / reason) · postulate: 假定某一先验前提作为理论逻辑基石 (existence / axiom / theory) · hypothesize: 提出具系统性、可检验的科学假说 (relationship / mechanism / model) · guess: 凭粗浅直觉进行缺乏依据的瞎猜或估测 (answer / weight / age)

groups.name: Speed & Greed in Eating · 贪婪大嚼与狼吞虎咽 (Overeat, Snarf)
groups.tip: 无节制地过量塞满食物

items.def_en: Eat food enthusiastically and heartily
items.ex_en: The hungry teenagers couldn't wait to sit down and chow down on pizza.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的青少年们迫不及待地坐下来，大快朵颐地吃起披萨。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Finish eating all the food quickly and completely
items.ex_en: He polished off the entire pizza in less than ten minutes.
items.ex_zh: 他不到十分钟就把整张披萨吃得一干二净。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ up/down) to eat hurriedly and noisily in large mouthfuls
items.ex_en: The starved stray dog began to gobble meat chunks straight from the bowl.
items.ex_zh: 那只快饿瘪的流浪狗开始大口吞食碗里的肉块。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Eat something very fast in big, eager bites
items.ex_en: The greedy seagulls swooped down to gobble up every discarded chip along the pier.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的海鸥俯冲下来，大口吞光了码头上所有被遗弃的薯条。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Eat food very quickly and greedily
items.ex_en: He managed to scarf down two loaded burritos in less than three minutes flat.
items.ex_zh: 他在短短三分钟内就狼吞虎咽地吃下了两个馅料满满的卷饼。

items.def_en: to eat food extremely quickly and greedily without chewing properly
items.ex_en: Late for practice, Mark proceeded to wolf down his cold breakfast sandwich hurriedly.
items.ex_zh: 训练要迟到了，马克匆匆忙忙地狼吞虎咽吃完了冰冷的的早餐三明治。

items.def_en: to eat something rapidly, voraciously, and greedily
items.ex_en: The famished hikers scoffed three large bowls of piping hot noodles within minutes.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的徒步旅行者们几分钟内就风卷残云般吃光了三碗热气腾腾的面条。

items.raw_cluster: 暴食与过量饮食 Binge & Overeat
items.def_en: To eat more food than is healthy or than your body needs.
items.ex_en: People tend to overeat rich comfort food during festive holidays and regret it later.
items.ex_zh: 人们在节日期间往往会暴饮暴食高热量食物，事后又追悔莫及。

items.def_en: (informal) To eat or drink something quickly and greedily.
items.ex_en: My teenage brother can snarf an entire carton of chocolate ice cream effortlessly.
items.ex_zh: 我十几岁的弟弟能不费吹灰之力狼吞虎咽地吃掉整整一盒巧克力冰淇淋。

groups.summary_en: Scale measuring the speed and voracity with which food is consumed, moving from simple excessive intake to rapid, noisy, gluttonous gobbling.
groups.summary_zh: 体现从普通的进食过量升级到贪婪、疾速、狼吞虎咽地大嚼吞食。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema denotes ingesting food with voracious speed, unmannered greed, and complete abandon, contrasting with standard dining by emphasizing animalistic haste, huge mouthfuls, and rapid plate-clearing.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指以饥不择食的狂暴速度与贪婪姿态吞咽食物，与常规进食不同，突出大口吞食、不修餐桌礼仪与风卷残云般的吞噬感。
groups.nuance_en: wolf down: consume rapidly in massive, minimally chewed bites like a predator (meal / sandwich / dinner) · gobble: gulp down food swiftly and noisily with ravenous greed (food / breakfast / portion) · scarf down: voraciously and messily devour large amounts at top speed (pizza / burger / fries) · scoff: aggressively and swiftly pack food into one's mouth (pie / lunch / treats) · polish off: thoroughly finish off all remnants on a plate or dish (pie / leftovers / bottle)
groups.nuance_zh: wolf down: 如饿狼般大块吞咽、不加细嚼 (meal / sandwich / dinner) · gobble: 贪婪且发出声响地狼吞虎咽 (food / breakfast / portion) · scarf down: 极其迅速地风卷残云消灭食物 (pizza / burger / fries) · scoff: 贪得无厌地大口猛吃 (pie / lunch / treats) · polish off: 彻底扫光盘中或桌上的残羹剩饭 (pie / leftovers / bottle)

groups.name: Spin & Orbit · 旋转与公转 (Orb, Wheel, Revolve)
groups.tip: 像轮子般打转回旋

items.def_en: (+ sth) travel or orbit in a circular path around a central body
items.ex_en: Several hungry vultures began to circle around the decaying carcass in the dusty canyon.
items.ex_zh: 几只饥饿的秃鹫开始在尘土飞扬的峡谷中围绕着腐尸盘旋。

items.def_en: move in a wide circle or curve through the air or space
items.ex_en: Flocks of startled swallows wheel around the church steeple before descending into trees.
items.ex_zh: 成群受惊的燕子在教堂尖顶上空作环形转动，随后落入树丛。
items.ex2_en: The pilot wheeled the small aircraft around toward the illuminated mountain runway.
items.ex2_zh: 飞行员调转小型飞机，朝向灯火通明的山间跑道飞去。

items.def_en: [I/T] To move completely around something in a circular path
items.ex_en: The reconnaissance aircraft continued to circle the disputed border zone for three hours.
items.ex_zh: 侦察机在争议边境地区上空持续盘旋了三个小时。

items.def_zh: 绕轨道运行；使成球形，成圆形
items.def_en: (poetic) To move in a circular orbit, or to encircle or form into a sphere.
items.ex_en: Pale distant moons orb through the boundless void of the silent nocturnal heavens.
items.ex_zh: 苍白的远方明月在寂静夜空的无垠虚无中绕着轨道缓缓运行。

items.def_en: 1. To turn or move quickly in a circle or curve, as birds in flight or people pivoting. 2. To push or move something that has wheels.
items.ex_en: Dozens of gulls wheel over the harbor waters, searching intently for schooling fish.
items.ex_zh: 数十只海鸥在港湾水域上空盘旋打转，专心寻找成群的鱼类。
items.ex2_en: The nurse wheeled the injured patient into the clean emergency operating room.
items.ex2_zh: 护士推着受伤的病人进入了整洁的急诊手术室。

items.def_en: [I/T] To move around a central celestial body or object in an elliptical or circular path
items.ex_en: Numerous weather satellites orbit the Earth at altitudes exceeding several hundred kilometers daily.
items.ex_zh: 许多气象卫星每天都在数百公里以上的高度沿着轨道环绕地球运行。

items.def_en: [I/T] To move in a circle around an axis or center point
items.ex_en: The industrial turbine blades rotate continuously to generate electricity for the coastal city.
items.ex_zh: 工业涡轮机叶片持续自转，为这座沿海城市提供源源不断的电力。
items.ex2_en: The farmer regularly rotates crops across different fields to preserve soil nutrients.
items.ex2_zh: 农民定期在不同田地轮作农作物，以保持土壤养分。

items.def_zh: 旋转，转动；围绕……旋转；以……为中心
items.def_en: 1. To move in a circle or orbit around a central point or axis. 2. (+ around) To have someone or something as the main subject or focus.
items.ex_en: Our terrestrial planets revolve around the central sun in fixed, nearly circular elliptical orbits.
items.ex_zh: 我们的类地行星在固定的、接近圆形的椭圆轨道上围绕中央太阳公转。
items.ex2_en: The engine revolving the heavy carousel runs on powerful quiet electric motors.
items.ex2_zh: 带动重型旋转木马运转的发动机依靠强劲静音的电动机驱动。

items.def_en: To move rapidly in a circle or spiral around an axis
items.ex_en: High-speed laboratory centrifuges gyrate rapidly to separate biological particles from blood plasma samples.
items.ex_zh: 实验室高速离心机剧烈回旋，从血浆样本中分离生物微粒。

groups.summary_en: An entity executes circular, rotational, or orbital motion either around an external central body or in a wide circular trajectory.
groups.summary_zh: 围绕中心轴或天体进行环形旋转、公转或绕圈回旋。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves curved or rotational movement around a central axis or celestial body, contrasting with rectilinear transit by tracing circular trajectories, rotational spins, or gravitionally governed closed loops.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指围绕自身中心轴或外部引力中心作弧形或回旋式运动，与直线位移不同，强调回旋轨迹、自转轴心或受引力约束的天体闭合轨道运行。
groups.nuance_en: rotate: turn around an internal axis or pivot (wheel / tires / earth) · revolve: move in a circular or elliptical orbital course around an external focal point (planets / sun / cylinder) · orbit: trace a continuous gravitationally locked curved path around a primary body (satellite / moon / earth) · wheel: sweep through an arc or change heading rapidly in a curve (flock / birds / chariot) · circle: travel in a flat ring-shaped boundary around a point (prey / runway / target)
groups.nuance_zh: rotate: 绕物体自身的内部轴心自转 (wheel / tires / earth) · revolve: 绕外部中心天体或枢轴公转/周期性回转 (planets / sun / cylinder) · orbit: 沿受引力约束的轨道环绕主天体运行 (satellite / moon / earth) · wheel: 飞禽、马车或队伍大幅度作弧线盘旋或转向 (flock / birds / chariot) · circle: 沿平圆周轨迹在空中或地表绕圈盘旋 (prey / runway / target)

groups.name: Split & Divide · 分裂与分割 (Split, Divide, Cleave)
groups.tip: 整体裂解分成多份

items.def_en: to move or cause things to move slightly apart, creating a space between them
items.ex_en: The dense crowd began to part, allowing the emergency paramedics to rush through.
items.ex_zh: 拥挤的人群开始向两边分开，让急救医务人员得以穿过。
items.ex2_en: He gently parted the green vines to peek into the secret courtyard.
items.ex2_zh: 他轻轻拨开绿色藤蔓，向秘密院子里窥视。

items.def_en: to divide or fork cleanly into two separate branches or paths
items.ex_en: The rugged forest trail will bifurcate into two rocky tracks after that wooden bridge.
items.ex_zh: 那座木桥之后，崎岖的林间小道将一分为二，变成两条布满岩石的岔路。
items.ex2_en: The highway department will bifurcate the congested road to ease morning traffic.
items.ex2_zh: 公路部门将把拥挤的道路分流成两条支路，以缓解早高峰交通。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to divide an area, asset, or entity into several smaller parts among different parties
items.ex_en: Aggressive investors decided to carve up the struggling airline into smaller, profitable entities.
items.ex_zh: 激进的投资者决定将这家陷入困境的航空公司瓜分成数个规模更小但盈利的实体。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to divide or break something into smaller parts or distinct groups
items.ex_en: After years of growing apart, the couple decided to split up peacefully.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了多年的隔阂后，这对夫妇决定和平分手。
items.ex2_en: The teacher decided to split up the talkative students into different groups.
items.ex2_zh: 老师决定把爱说话的学生们分开分配到不同的小组。

items.def_zh: （使）分裂，（使）裂开；分开，分担；分享；断绝关系，分手
items.def_en: 1. To break, divide, or split into two or more parts. 2. To share or divide something between two or more people. 3. (informal) To end a relationship or leave.
items.ex_en: Let's split the dinner bill equally so nobody has to pay too much.
items.ex_zh: 咱们把晚餐账单平摊了吧，这样谁也不用掏太多钱。
items.ex2_en: The dried oak branch split loudly under the heavy weight of snow.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的橡树枝在沉重的积雪压迫下啪的一声裂开了。

items.def_zh: （使）分开，（使）分裂；分配，分摊；（使）产生分歧；除以
items.def_en: 1. To separate into two or more parts, or cause something to separate. 2. To share out or distribute. 3. To cause disagreement among people. 4. (mathematics) To calculate how many times one number contains another.
items.ex_en: The teacher decided to divide the large class into three smaller study groups.
items.ex_zh: 老师决定把这个大班级分成三个较小的学习小组。
items.ex2_en: The quiet river divides into two smaller streams near the mountain foothills.
items.ex2_zh: 这条静谧的河流在山脚下分流成了两条较小的溪流。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to separate or cause something to separate completely into pieces
items.ex_en: The violent tremors caused the dry concrete pavement to crack and break apart.
items.ex_zh: 剧烈的震颤导致干燥的水泥路面开裂并彻底碎成几块。
items.ex2_en: Intense ocean waves easily broke apart the fragile wooden fishing boat overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 狂暴的海浪在夜间轻易地将脆弱的木制渔船打得粉碎。

items.def_en: (+ along/through) to split or sever something firmly and cleanly, often along a natural grain
items.ex_en: With one mighty stroke, the woodsman's axe cleaved cleanly through the frozen log.
items.ex_zh: 樵夫挥斧猛力一劈，干净利落地劈开了那根冻硬的原木。
items.ex2_en: The sharp chisel cleaved the polished marble slab straight down the center.
items.ex2_zh: 锋利的凿子将打磨好的大理石板从正中间笔直劈开。

items.def_en: to break violently apart or sever completely, especially an abstract bond or unified entity
items.ex_en: Decades of bitter political strife threatened to sunder the once peaceful nation.
items.ex_zh: 数十载痛苦的政治纷争恐将强行撕裂这个曾经和平的国度。
items.ex2_en: The fragile alliance between the two neighboring kingdoms threatened to sunder.
items.ex2_zh: 两个邻国之间脆弱的同盟面临破裂的危险。

groups.summary_en: An agent separates a unified physical whole, group, or continuum into two or more parts, or a whole naturally fractures along seams under stress.
groups.summary_zh: 沿纹理、外力或界限将整体破裂、切开或划分成若干部分。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves severing a unified entity into detached components, factions, or bifurcated pathways, contrasting with general destruction by focusing on cleavage along structural seams, planes, or ideological axes.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指将一个连续完整的实体沿结构缝隙、受力面或思想界线割裂为相互分离的部分或派系，与彻底毁坏不同，强调裂解与结构分流。
groups.nuance_en: cleave: split forcefully along a natural grain or structural plane (rock / wood / bone) · bifurcate: fork or separate into two distinct diverging branches (stream / path / trachea) · divide: separate into measured parts, portions, or mutually exclusive groups (spoils / country / class) · split: rupture, tear apart, or crack lengthwise under stress (faction / seam / atom) · carve up: aggressively dismember and parcel out territory or assets (territory / empire / pie)
groups.nuance_zh: cleave: 沿天然纹理或解理面大力劈开 (rock / wood / bone) · bifurcate: 一分为二地向两个分支分流或岔开 (stream / path / trachea) · divide: 按度量或比例均分、划界或分类 (spoils / country / class) · split: 沿纵向应力缝破裂或使派系阵营撕裂分裂 (faction / seam / atom) · carve up: 瓜分、肆意宰割领土或资产份额 (territory / empire / pie)

groups.name: Spoil & Decompose · 变质与腐坏 (Spoil, Decay, Rot)
groups.tip: 事物受损毁坏或品质败坏

items.def_en: Become rotten, stale, or sour so as to be unfit for consumption
items.ex_en: If you leave the fresh milk out in this heat, it will go bad.
items.ex_zh: 如果把鲜奶留在这种闷热的环境里，它就会变质。

items.def_en: Decompose into basic organic constituents through natural chemical decay
items.ex_en: Fallen leaves gradually break down into rich organic compost during the winter months.
items.ex_zh: 落叶在冬季几个月里会逐渐自然分解成肥沃的有机堆肥。
items.ex2_en: Microscopic bacteria help break down organic household waste into nutrient-rich garden soil.
items.ex2_zh: 微小的细菌有助于将家庭有机废弃物分解成富含养分的园艺土壤。

items.def_en: Become stale or begin to decompose and spoil (chiefly British)
items.ex_en: Sniff the opened carton first, because this cream might go off very quickly.
items.ex_zh: 先闻闻打开的纸盒，因为这种奶油可能很快就会变酸变坏。

items.def_zh: 变质，腐败；损坏，破坏；宠坏，溺爱
items.def_en: 1. (of food) To become bad or unfit to eat; to cause to decay. 2. To ruin or diminish the quality, value, or pleasure of something. 3. To overindulge a child.
items.ex_en: The raw chicken will spoil quickly unless kept strictly inside the refrigerator.
items.ex_zh: 生鸡肉如果不严格存放在冰箱里很快就会变质腐坏。
items.ex2_en: Leaving the milk out in hot weather will definitely spoil it quickly.
items.ex2_zh: 大热天把牛奶留在外面肯定会很快让它变质。

items.def_en: [I/T] to undergo gradual structural decomposition by natural biological or chemical causes
items.ex_en: The fallen timber began to decay naturally under the damp forest canopy.
items.ex_zh: 倒下的树木在潮湿的森林树冠下开始自然腐烂。
items.ex2_en: Excessive moisture and voracious insects can rapidly decay the strongest timber structures.
items.ex2_zh: 过量的湿气与贪吃的昆虫会迅速腐蚀最坚固的木结构。

items.def_zh: 变质，腐败；损坏，破坏；宠坏（spoil的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of spoil; to become decayed, ruined, or overindulged.
items.ex_en: The unrefrigerated meat had completely spoilt before we could cook dinner last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚还没等我们做晚饭，未冷藏的肉就已经彻底变质了。
items.ex2_en: The unbearable summer heat had completely spoilt the fresh milk overnight.
items.ex2_zh: 难耐的酷暑一夜之间彻底让新鲜牛奶变质了。

items.def_en: Gradually decay and disintegrate completely through biological breakdown
items.ex_en: The abandoned wooden pier was left to slowly rot away in the water.
items.ex_zh: 那座废弃的木制码头被遗弃在水中，慢慢完全烂掉了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to decompose through bacterial or fungal action, turning soft, foul, and unusable
items.ex_en: Left in the damp basement, the heavy wooden crates began to soften and rot.
items.ex_zh: 留在潮湿地下室里的大木箱开始发软腐烂。
items.ex2_en: Persistent dampness and fungi can rapidly rot exposed wooden window frames outdoors.
items.ex2_zh: 持续的潮湿和真菌会迅速让室外裸露的木制窗框腐烂。

items.def_en: [I/T] to rot and decay with the production of a foul, repulsive odor
items.ex_en: The carcasses began to putrefy beneath the blazing sun, emitting a foul stench.
items.ex_zh: 尸骸在烈日下开始彻底腐败，散发出一股恶臭。
items.ex2_en: The sweltering heat and bacteria quickly putrefied the fish inside the container.
items.ex2_zh: 闷热的暑气和细菌迅速使容器内的死鱼腐烂发臭。

groups.summary_en: This intensity-graded frame traces organic matter losing freshness, decomposing, and deteriorating until ruined. Intensity progresses from functional unfitness or souring ('spoil') to structural bacterial breakdown ('decay') and total offensive putrefaction ('rot', 'putrefy').
groups.summary_zh: 按由轻至重梯度，描述有机物由失去鲜度变质到彻底腐烂崩解的过程。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the biological or organic breakdown of matter under fungal, bacterial, or environmental decay, contrasting with mechanical wear by emphasizing putrefaction, rank odor, and loss of edible/structural integrity.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指有机质在微生物、霉菌或环境作用下经历生物学分解腐烂，与物理磨损不同，强调腐败发臭、丧失食用性与结构溃烂。
groups.nuance_en: spoil: become sour, inedible, or ruined for consumption (milk / meat / food) · decay: undergo slow biochemical decomposition and structural deterioration (teeth / corpse / timber) · rot: putrefy, decompose foully, and turn soft or necrotic (fruit / wood / carcass) · go off: turn sour, foul, or biologically unsafe through age (fish / milk / produce) · break down: decompose chemically or biochemically into simpler organic constituents (tissue / waste / matter)
groups.nuance_zh: spoil: 食品变质、酸败以致不可食用 (milk / meat / food) · decay: 缓慢生物化学性分解破坏与组织败坏 (teeth / corpse / timber) · rot: 发生恶臭液化或深度腐烂 (fruit / wood / carcass) · go off: 因超时存放而发酸、发臭或变味 (fish / milk / produce) · break down: 有机物发生生化降解并化为简单组分 (tissue / waste / matter)

groups.name: Sport & Game Plays · 竞技战术执行 (Score, Defend, Play Cards)
groups.tip: 体育场上博弈较量与争夺胜负

items.def_zh: 出王牌胜过；出将牌打败
items.def_en: To play a trump card on a trick, defeating other suits
items.ex_en: She decided to trump the opponent's king of diamonds with a low spade.
items.ex_zh: 她决定用一张较小的黑桃王牌来吃掉对手的方块K。

items.def_en: To physically intercept and bring down an opponent carrying the ball
items.ex_en: The agile defender rushed forward to tackle the charging fullback near the goal.
items.ex_zh: 灵活的后卫向前冲刺，在球门附近擒抱扑倒了冲锋的全卫。

items.def_zh: （体育比赛中）贴身紧逼防守（某人）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to mark or defend closely against an opposing player in team sports
items.ex_en: Coach shouted from the sidelines for everyone to man up on defense.
items.ex_zh: 教练在场边大喊，要求每个人在防守时都贴身紧逼防守。

items.def_zh: 从后场组织倒脚推进（足球）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to pass the ball systematically forward starting from the defensive zone or goalkeeper
items.ex_en: Modern football teams prefer to play out carefully from their own defensive penalty area.
items.ex_zh: 现代足球队倾向于从自家的防守禁区谨慎地倒脚推进。
items.ex2_en: The veteran defender expertly played out the ball to the unmarked midfielder.
items.ex2_zh: 这名老练的防守球员熟练地将球从后场倒给了无人盯防的中场。

items.def_zh: 触杀（棒球中持球触碰跑垒员出局）
items.def_en: (+ sb) to touch a baserunner with the ball or the glove holding the ball to put them out in baseball
items.ex_en: The quick shortstop lunged forward to tag out the runner sliding into second base.
items.ex_zh: 机敏的游击手向前猛扑，触杀了滑向二垒的跑垒员。

items.def_en: To complete a hole or golf course in the designated standard number of strokes
items.ex_en: With an effortless swing across the fairway, the champion managed to par the hole.
items.ex_zh: 冠军在球道上轻松挥杆，成功在这一洞击出了标准杆。

items.def_zh: （美式足球或橄榄球中）打全卫位置
items.def_en: 1. (sports) To play as a fullback in American football or rugby.
items.ex_en: Throughout his college career, the athlete was chosen to fullback for the varsity squad.
items.ex_zh: 在整个大学生涯中，这名运动员都被选定为校队司职全卫。

items.def_zh: （桥牌等纸牌游戏中）出王牌杀牌
items.def_en: 1. (card games) To trump, or play a trump card when unable to follow suit in bridge or whist.
items.ex_en: Lacking any heart in her hand, the declarer chose to ruff the trick.
items.ex_zh: 手中没有任何红桃的定约人选择出王牌杀牌拿下了这一墩。

items.def_zh: （高尔夫球中）打出超过标准杆一杆的成绩
items.def_en: 1. (golf) To score one stroke more than par on a hole.
items.ex_en: A sudden gust swept his ball into the rough, forcing him to bogey.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的强风将球刮入深草区，迫使他打出超标准杆一杆。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this domain represent technical game actions and scoring events within regulated competitive sports and games. They specify sport-specific maneuvers such as playing cards of a trump suit, recording golf scores, or executing designated tactical roles.
groups.summary_zh: 指竞技体育或纸牌等规则博弈中执行的具体战术与技术动作。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema denotes the rule-bound, tactical execution of specific sports or tabletop maneuvers to neutralize an opponent, score points, or control play, contrasting with general play by demanding precise codified athletic or strategic steps.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指在竞技体育或桌游规则限定下，为压制对手、得分或控盘而执行的具体攻防技战术动作，与泛泛玩耍不同，具有高度程式化的竞技规则性。
groups.nuance_en: tackle: physically seize and force an opponent to the turf to halt progress (player / runner / opponent) · trump: override or beat another card with an established superior suit (suit / card / bid) · ruff: play a trump card on a trick led in a plain suit (trick / lead) · tag out: eliminate a baserunner by touching them with the ball or gloved ball (runner / player) · par: complete a golf hole or course in the predetermined benchmark strokes (hole / course)
groups.nuance_zh: tackle: 擒抱摔倒带球奔跑的对手以阻遏进攻 (player / runner / opponent) · trump: 打出王牌以盖过其他花色纸牌 (suit / card / bid) · ruff: 桥牌中在副牌轮次以将牌垫将获胜 (trick / lead) · tag out: 棒垒球中持球触碰离垒跑垒员使其出局 (runner / player) · par: 高尔夫以标准杆数完成球洞或赛程 (hole / course)

groups.name: Sprout & Flourish · 植物萌发生长 (Sprout, Bloom, Flourish)
groups.tip: 从含苞绽放到枝繁叶茂

items.def_en: to begin to grow and produce new leaves, shoots, or buds
items.ex_en: After two days of rain, tiny green leaves began to sprout from the branches.
items.ex_zh: 经过两天的雨水滋润，细小的绿叶开始从枝头抽芽。
items.ex2_en: Frequent gentle rains will sprout the freshly sown seeds throughout the garden.
items.ex2_zh: 频繁的细雨会让花园里新播下的种子发芽。

items.def_en: to begin to grow and push up from the soil or a seed
items.ex_en: Delicate green seedlings began to sprout up eagerly from the damp garden soil.
items.ex_zh: 娇嫩的绿色幼苗争先恐后地从潮湿的花园土壤中破土长出。

items.def_en: To produce, develop, or begin to open into buds.
items.ex_en: The rose bushes started to bud nicely as the mild spring weather arrived.
items.ex_zh: 随着温和的春季来临，玫瑰灌木丛开始吐出喜人的花蕾。

items.def_en: to grow upwards very quickly and vigorously
items.ex_en: After the warm weekend downpour, the tall sunflowers seemed to shoot up overnight.
items.ex_zh: 周末一场温暖的大雨过后，高大的向日葵似乎一夜之间就蹿高了。

items.def_zh: 开花；繁荣，成熟，达到盛期
items.def_en: 1. To produce blooms or blossom. 2. To reach full development or peak prosperity.
items.ex_en: These delicate orchids generally flower best in humid and dimly lit greenhouse environments.
items.ex_zh: 这些娇嫩的兰花通常在潮湿且光线较暗的温室环境中开花最好。

items.def_en: to produce flowers, especially on fruit trees, or to flourish vibrantly
items.ex_en: The cherry trees blossom magnificently along the riverbank every year in early spring.
items.ex_zh: 每年早春，河畔的樱花树都会绚丽盛开。

items.def_en: (+ blossom/flower) to suddenly produce an abundance of flowers or blooms
items.ex_en: After the spring warmth arrived, the orchard suddenly burst into brilliant pink blossom.
items.ex_zh: 春日暖意降临后，果园突然繁花盛开，展现出一片绚丽的粉色。

items.def_en: to grow vigorously and healthily under optimal conditions
items.ex_en: The rare alpine ferns flourish vigorously within this temperate and protected mountain microclimate.
items.ex_zh: 稀有的高山蕨类植物在这种温和且受保护的小气候中繁茂生长。

items.def_en: to grow exceptionally well and energetically in a favorable environment
items.ex_en: Native shrubs thrive remarkably well even in the poor, dry rocky soil here.
items.ex_zh: 本土灌木即使在当地贫瘠干燥的岩石土壤中也能茁壮成长。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the sequential biological progression of plant life, tracking the manner of growth from early emergence and budding to fully flowering and thriving vitality.
groups.summary_zh: 描述植物从萌芽、抽枝、开花到枝繁叶茂的各阶段生长方式。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the biological emergence, growth, and vibrant blossoming of plant life, metaphorically extended to rapid flourishing, contrasting with inorganic enlargement by centering on vital organic genesis.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指植物生命的萌发抽芽、展叶盛开及生机勃勃的绽放，并可隐喻式拓展至繁荣昌盛，与无机扩增不同，强调植物生发与生机跃动。
groups.nuance_en: sprout: emit initial green shoots or germinate from seed (seeds / leaves / potatoes) · bud: produce nascent embryonic shoots or unopened flowers (roses / trees / branches) · blossom: open into full floral bloom, indicating peak vitality (orchard / cherry / talent) · flower: produce flowers or reach the apex of cultural/historical development (plant / civilization / art) · flourish: thrive vigorously in a supportive environment (business / plants / community)
groups.nuance_zh: sprout: 破土抽芽、萌发最初的新芽 (seeds / leaves / potatoes) · bud: 形成花蕾或生出萌芽 (roses / trees / branches) · blossom: 果树等全盛怒放或才华全面展露 (orchard / cherry / talent) · flower: 植物开花或文明艺术臻于全盛极境 (plant / civilization / art) · flourish: 在适宜滋养的环境中繁茂兴盛 (business / plants / community)

groups.name: Squirm & Wriggle · 蠕动与辗转扭动 (Squirm, Wriggle, Writhe)
groups.tip: 局促不安地扭动身躯

items.def_en: to twist and fidget one's body restlessly or uncomfortably
items.ex_en: The restless toddler began to squirm around impatiently in his stiff wooden highchair.
items.ex_zh: 那个坐立不安的幼儿在坚硬的木制高脚椅上不耐烦地扭来扭去。

items.def_en: to free oneself or escape from a confined space by twisting and writhing the body
items.ex_en: The small puppy managed to wriggle out through a narrow gap under the gate.
items.ex_zh: 小狗设法从大门下的一道狭缝中扭动身躯钻了出来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to turn or contort the body or a part of it into a different position
items.ex_en: He had to twist his body awkwardly to squeeze past the narrow hallway.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不别扭地转动身体，以挤过狭窄的走廊。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move with small, quick, irregular movements from side to side or up and down
items.ex_en: The nervous boy began to wiggle his toes inside his tight new shoes.
items.ex_zh: 那个紧张的男孩开始在紧绷的新鞋子里微小地动了动脚趾。
items.ex2_en: The nervous puppy's tiny black nose began to wiggle with intense excitement.
items.ex2_zh: 那只紧张的小狗的黑色小鼻子兴奋地微微抽动起来。

items.def_zh: （因尴尬、紧张或疼痛而）扭动身体，蠕动；感到局促不安
items.def_en: To twist and wriggle the body from side to side because of discomfort, nervousness, or embarrassment.
items.ex_en: The boy started to squirm uncomfortably under his strict headmaster's stern, penetrating gaze.
items.ex_zh: 在严厉校长逼人的目光注视下，男孩开始不安地局促扭动身子。

items.def_zh: 扭动，蠕动；蠕动着穿过；巧妙避开，摆脱 (wriggle out of)
items.def_en: 1. To twist and turn the body with quick, small movements; 2. (wriggle out of) to cleverly avoid a duty or problem.
items.ex_en: The slippery little fish managed to wriggle free from the boy's wet grasp.
items.ex_zh: 那条滑溜的小鱼设法扭动身体，从男孩湿漉漉的掌握中脱身。

items.raw_cluster: 不安乱动与微动 Fidget & Squirm
items.def_zh: 坐立不安，烦躁地动来动去；摆弄，玩弄 (fidget with)
items.def_en: To make small, restless movements with the hands or feet, especially from nervousness, impatience, or boredom.
items.ex_en: Nervous applicants often fidget uncontrollably with their pens during a stressful job interview.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的求职者在压力巨大的求职面试中往往会忍不住坐立不安地摆弄钢笔。

items.def_zh: 辗转折腾；剧烈抽动打滚
items.def_en: to move one's body wildly, violently, or convulsively from side to side
items.ex_en: The patient began to thrash about violently on the bed during the nightmare.
items.ex_zh: 病人在噩梦发作时开始在床上剧烈地辗转折腾翻滚。

items.def_zh: （因剧痛或不适而）翻滚，扭动身躯；深感痛苦
items.def_en: To twist and turn the body violently, especially because of severe pain or discomfort.
items.ex_en: The stricken gladiator fell to the dust, left to writhe in agony.
items.ex_zh: 负伤的角斗士倒在尘土中，痛苦万状地抽搐翻滚。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict continuous serpentine, twisting, or restless bodily movements, distinguishing between nervous discomfort, snakelike locomotion, and agony-induced contortions.
groups.summary_zh: 描述因紧张、局促、滑动或剧痛而产生的身躯辗转扭动动作。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema denotes twisting, writhing, or convoluted bodily motions triggered by physical discomfort, constraint, or emotional embarrassment, contrasting with purposeful locomotion by emphasizing trapped, involuntary sinuous contortion.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指身体因肉体剧痛、空间束缚或内心情感尴尬所引发的蛇形辗转扭动，与自主位移不同，强调脱逃受阻时被动或痉挛性的曲折扭摆。
groups.nuance_en: writhe: contort or twist the entire body violently in severe agony or torment (pain / agony / torment) · squirm: twist or contort the torso nervously from embarrassment or physical restraint (embarrassment / seat / grasp) · wriggle: make quick small snake-like twisting movements to advance or escape (toes / through / escape) · fidget: move restlessly and make small nervous adjustments out of boredom or unease (fingers / hands / nervously) · thrash about: fling one's limbs violently and haphazardly in distress (limbs / water / bed)
groups.nuance_zh: writhe: 因极度剧痛或酷刑而在地上剧烈扭搐翻滚 (pain / agony / torment) · squirm: 因尴尬羞愧或受束缚而在原地局促扭身 (embarrassment / seat / grasp) · wriggle: 像蠕虫般做小幅度扭摆以挤过狭缝或逃脱 (toes / through / escape) · fidget: 因无聊、焦虑而手上脚下不安分地小动作频频 (fingers / hands / nervously) · thrash about: 在挣扎困顿中四肢胡乱剧烈拍打扑腾 (limbs / water / bed)

groups.name: Stab & Spear with Pointed Weapon · 刺扎与穿刺 (Stab, Spear, Transfix)
groups.tip: 用尖锐武器穿透与刺扎

items.def_en: (of an animal) To butt, stab, or pierce someone or something with a horn.
items.ex_en: The enraged ram lowered its head, threatening to horn any trespassing stranger.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的公羊低下了头，威胁着要用角顶穿任何擅闯的陌生人。

items.def_en: to force a sharp point into or through a surface
items.ex_en: The sharp thorn managed to pierce cleanly through the thick leather gardening glove.
items.ex_zh: 锋利的刺刺透了厚厚的皮革园艺手套。

items.def_en: (+ sb) pierce someone through the body using a sword, spear, or blade
items.ex_en: In the duel, the villain threatened to run through his opponent without mercy.
items.ex_zh: 在决斗中，那个恶棍威胁要毫不留情地用剑刺穿对手的身体。

items.def_en: (+ sth into sth) push a pointed weapon forcibly into someone's body
items.ex_en: The assassin attempted to thrust the dagger deep into the guard's unguarded back.
items.ex_zh: 刺客试图将匕首狠狠刺入那名卫兵毫无防备的后背。

items.def_en: To push a knife or other sharp, pointed object into someone or something.
items.ex_en: The robber pulled out a sharp hunting knife and threatened to stab anyone.
items.ex_zh: 劫匪掏出一把锋利的猎刀，威胁要刺伤任何人。

items.def_en: To push a spear or other pointed object through something, or catch something with it.
items.ex_en: The tribal fisherman used a long barbed pole to spear a large salmon.
items.ex_zh: 部落渔民用一根长长的倒钩长矛刺中了一条大三文鱼。

items.def_en: to pierce or wound deeply with a horn or tusk
items.ex_en: The furious bull managed to gore the reckless matador in the open arena.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的公牛在露天竞技场上用角挑刺重创了卤莽的斗牛士。

items.def_en: to pierce completely through a body with a sharp stake or point
items.ex_en: The ancient defenders would impale executed traitors upon tall wooden stakes outside walls.
items.ex_zh: 古代守军会将处决的叛徒用木桩刺穿高高挂在城墙之外。

items.def_en: to pierce through with a weapon so as to pin firmly in position
items.ex_en: A lethal iron bolt shot from the shadows to transfix the beast cleanly.
items.ex_zh: 一记致命的铁弩箭从阴影中射出，把那头野兽硬生生刺透钉在原地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs denoting a direct, forceful thrusting attack with a pointed implement, weapon, or natural horn into an opponent's body, causing puncture wounds through penetration.
groups.summary_zh: 指用尖刺状武器或角刺入、戳穿肉体的攻击方式。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves driving a pointed, bladed, or horned implement deeply into or through an animate target, contrasting with blunt trauma by focusing on focal penetration, impalement, and puncture wounds.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指用尖锐、带刃或带角的锋利器物深刺入或贯穿生物靶体，与钝器击打不同，强调压强极高的点状贯入、穿透与深部刺伤。
groups.nuance_en: stab: plunge a pointed thrusting weapon like a knife straight into flesh (victim / back / chest) · pierce: puncture or penetrate cleanly through a membrane, flesh, or skin (ears / skin / armor) · spear: thrust into and catch using a long pole weapon with a pointed tip (fish / target / boar) · gore: pierce or tear flesh deeply with animal horns or tusks (bull / matador / victim) · impale: drive a sharp stake completely through a body, transfixing it (stake / body / victim)
groups.nuance_zh: stab: 用匕首、短刃等尖刺武器猛捅刺入躯体 (victim / back / chest) · pierce: 刺破、扎穿皮肤、耳膜或装甲界面 (ears / skin / armor) · spear: 用长矛或标枪扎刺猎物 (fish / target / boar) · gore: 兽角或獠牙挑刺、挑破血肉 (bull / matador / victim) · impale: 用尖桩自下而上或完全贯穿钉住身躯 (stake / body / victim)

groups.name: Station & Billet · 安置与派驻 (Station, Billet, Quarter)
groups.tip: 安排入驻场所收治

items.def_en: To assign someone to a particular place or post; to position oneself or someone at a specific spot.
items.ex_en: The commanding officer chose to station vigilant sentries along the exposed northern border.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官决定在毫无遮蔽的北部边境沿线派驻警惕的哨兵。

items.def_zh: 提供床铺（或宿处），收留就寝；固定于基座，把……栽入土中；与……发生性关系
items.def_en: 1. To provide someone with a bed or sleeping accommodation. 2. To place or fix firmly in a foundation or in the ground. 3. (informal) To have sexual intercourse with someone.
items.ex_en: The small mountain innkeeper was willing to bed travelers stranded by the storm.
items.ex_zh: 那位山中小客栈的老板愿意收留因暴风雨而滞留的旅客就寝。

items.def_zh: 为……配备工作人员，在……任职
items.def_en: To provide an organization, facility, or event with workers or personnel; to serve as staff for.
items.ex_en: The local hospital needed more registered nurses to staff the busy emergency department.
items.ex_zh: 当地医院需要更多注册护士来为繁忙的急诊部配备人员。

items.def_zh: 为（驻军或人员）提供营房寄居
items.def_en: to provide housing or lodgings for military troops or attendants
items.ex_en: The commander ordered the governor to quarter two hundred soldiers inside the fortress.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官下令要塞总督为要塞内的两百名士兵安排驻宿营房。

items.def_zh: 安排外宿；分派到民居驻扎
items.def_en: (+ sb) assign military personnel to stay in private homes or scattered lodgings
items.ex_en: During wartime, authorities decided to billet out displaced recruits among the local villagers.
items.ex_zh: 在战时，当局决定将流散的新兵分派到当地村民的民居中驻扎。

items.def_en: (+ sb at sth) assign personnel or soldiers to a particular post or location
items.ex_en: Troops were stationed at the border to monitor the fragile ceasefire.
items.ex_zh: 军队被部署在边境，以监视脆弱的停火状态。

items.def_zh: 派兵驻守，防守（据点或要塞）
items.def_en: to assign a military garrison to defend a fortified place, town, or base
items.ex_en: The king dispatched several infantry battalions to garrison the strategic frontier fort indefinitely.
items.ex_zh: 国王派遣了数个步兵营无限期驻守这座具有战略意义的边境要塞。

items.def_en: To admit or send someone to a hospital for medical treatment or observation.
items.ex_en: Severe respiratory complications forced doctors to hospitalize the elderly patient for closer monitoring.
items.ex_zh: 严重的呼吸系统并发症迫使医生将这位老年患者收治住院以便密切监测。

items.def_zh: 安排宿营，向民居寄宿安排（军人）
items.def_en: to assign soldiers temporary civilian lodging or quarters, typically using 'on' or 'with'
items.ex_en: The army sought permission to billet weary infantrymen on local farmers during winter.
items.ex_zh: 入冬时节，军方请求获准将疲惫的步兵安排在当地农户家中寄宿。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this institutional frame describe formally assigning, housing, accommodating, or deploying personnel (soldiers, healthcare patients, corporate staff) to specific physical quarters, duty posts, or custodial facilities. The nuances distinguish military post assignment (station, quarter, billet) from administrative staffing and institutional admissions (hospitalize).
groups.summary_zh: 指派、驻防或集中安置人员（军人、职员或病患）至指定营所与设施。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves assigning and lodging military personnel or institutional operatives at specific strategic locations or residential quarters, contrasting with informal resting by highlighting authorized deployment, logistic billeting, and garrisons.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式指依据官方命令将武装力量或机构人员正式部署、落位驻扎于特定要塞或民舍营房，与非正式留宿不同，强调体制化调遣与后勤驻留。
groups.nuance_en: station: assign military personnel to a specific post or strategic outpost (troops / guards / detachment) · garrison: secure a town, fort, or border with a permanent defensive force (town / fort / border) · quarter: provide formal lodging and sustenance for military forces (soldiers / troops / regiments) · billet: lodge soldiers temporarily in civilian houses or non-military buildings (soldiers / recruits / guests) · hospitalize: place and keep a patient in a medical facility for care (patient / injured / casualties)
groups.nuance_zh: station: 将官兵派驻落位于指定据点或岗位 (troops / guards / detachment) · garrison: 派兵驻防要塞、城镇以保卫边界 (town / fort / border) · quarter: 正式向成建制部队配给住所营房 (soldiers / troops / regiments) · billet: 临时将兵员征用落宿于民舍村落 (soldiers / recruits / guests) · hospitalize: 将伤病员收治并留驻于医疗院所 (patient / injured / casualties)

groups.name: Stealthy Skulking & Lurking · 潜伏与匿影潜行 (Skulk, Slink, Lurk)
groups.tip: 鬼鬼祟祟、无声无息地移动

items.def_zh: 溜走，潜行，鬼鬼祟祟地走；（动物）早产
items.def_en: 1. (+ away/off/around) To walk or move quietly and stealthily, especially out of fear, guilt, or shame. 2. (of livestock) To give birth to prematurely.
items.ex_en: The guilty dog would slink into the kitchen corner whenever scolded by owners.
items.ex_zh: 每当被主人训斥时，那只心虚的狗就会偷偷溜进厨房角落。

items.def_en: 1. (+ up to/along/past) To walk or move slowly, shyly, or secretly, often sideways, trying not to attract attention.
items.ex_en: The hesitant guest tried to sidle past the noisy crowd toward the door.
items.ex_zh: 那位犹豫不决的客人试图悄悄侧身穿过嘈杂的人群走向门口。

items.def_zh: 蹑手蹑脚潜行；鬼鬼祟祟走动
items.def_en: to move quietly and stealthily about, trying to avoid detection
items.ex_en: A masked intruder was seen to creep around the dark garden after midnight.
items.ex_zh: 午夜过后，有人看到一名蒙面闯入者在漆黑的花园里蹑手蹑脚地潜行。

items.def_zh: 鬼鬼祟祟潜伏；暗中窥视徘徊
items.def_en: to lurk or move covertly and suspiciously in an area
items.ex_en: Suspicious figures began to skulk around the deserted parking garage late last night.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚深夜，可疑的身影开始在空荡荡的地下车库里鬼鬼祟祟地徘徊窥视。

items.def_zh: 鬼鬼祟祟溜走；怯生生躲开
items.def_en: to leave a place quietly and stealthily, especially out of fear, guilt, or shame
items.ex_en: Caught red-handed stealing apples, the frightened boy tried to slink away quietly.
items.ex_zh: 偷苹果被当场抓获后，那个受惊的男孩试图怯生生地悄悄溜走。

items.def_en: to move about in a secretive, suspicious manner
items.ex_en: The suspicious reporter continued to sneak around private corporate headquarters seeking secret documents.
items.ex_zh: 那位形迹可疑的记者继续在企业私人总部周围暗中转悠，搜寻机密文件。

items.def_en: to wait or move furtively in a hidden place, often with sinister intent
items.ex_en: Dangers often lurk quietly within the darkest alleys of this neglected industrial district.
items.ex_zh: 危险往往在这片被人遗弃的工业区最阴暗的小巷里悄然潜伏。

items.def_zh: 潜行，偷偷溜走，躲躲闪闪
items.def_en: 1. (+ around/about) To move around or hide secretly in shadows, especially with sinister or cowardly intent.
items.ex_en: Shady conspirators were rumored to skulk along the misty riverbank under moonlight.
items.ex_zh: 据传，居心不良的密谋者曾在月光下躲躲闪闪地沿着薄雾笼罩的河岸潜行。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move around stealthily and restlessly in search of prey or opportunity
items.ex_en: The leopard continued to prowl along the perimeter fence in search of prey.
items.ex_zh: 这只豹子继续沿着外围围栏悄然潜行，搜寻猎物。

groups.summary_en: An agent moves stealthily, sideways, or keeps out of sight, typically motivated by guilt, cowardice, fear, or sinister intent.
groups.summary_zh: 指因心虚、怯懦或心怀不轨而鬼鬼祟祟地潜行、躲闪或潜伏。
groups.desc_en: Denotes secretive, furtive physical movement or stationary concealment driven by guilt, cowardice, or predatory intent, contrasting with neutral walking or overt waiting.
groups.desc_zh: 指因愧疚、畏怯或不轨企图而鬼祟潜行或隐匿窥伺，区别于中性的走动或公开的等待。
groups.nuance_en: slink: move smoothly and guiltily close to the ground (away / off / through the shadows) · skulk: loiter furtively with predatory or evasive intent (in the shadows / around the corridor) · lurk: remain hidden waiting to ambush or spy (beneath the surface / in dark alleys) · sidle: walk with discreet, oblique indirectness (up to / over to) · sneak: move quietly and illicitly to evade detection (into the room / out of the house)
groups.nuance_zh: slink: 愧疚、羞怯或鬼祟地贴地潜行 (away / off / through the shadows) · skulk: 怀揣不良企图或畏罪潜伏游荡 (in the shadows / around the corridor) · lurk: 伏匿伺机突袭或窥视 (beneath the surface / in dark alleys) · sidle: 侧身小心翼翼凑近 (up to / over to) · sneak: 规避视线地偷偷溜走 (into the room / out of the house)

groups.name: Strand & Immobilize · 滞留与受困 (Maroon, Bog down, Strand)
groups.tip: 陷入泥沼难以拔出动弹

items.def_en: to cause a ship to run aground, or forbid aircraft/pilots from flying
items.ex_en: Dense morning fog forced aviation authorities to ground all regional passenger flights.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的浓雾迫使民航部门停飞所有支线客运航班。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) sink into mud and become unable to move, or become severely impeded
items.ex_en: Don't let petty arguments bog down our progress on this important project.
items.ex_zh: 别让琐碎的争执使我们在这一重大项目上的进展陷入停滞。
items.ex2_en: Heavy army trucks began to bog down in the thick mud.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的军用卡车开始陷在厚厚的泥淖中动弹不得。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) sink deeply into wet or muddy ground so that progress stops
items.ex_en: The ancient wagon began to mire down into the sodden marshland path.
items.ex_zh: 那辆古旧的四轮马车开始深深陷进湿透的沼泽小径中。
items.ex2_en: Endless procedural bureaucracy threatens to mire down our crucial reform initiative indefinitely.
items.ex2_zh: 无休止的繁文缛节可能会无限期地阻碍我们关键的改革倡议。

items.def_en: to leave someone in a helpless situation or place without transport, funds, or escape
items.ex_en: The sudden transit strike threatens to strand hundreds of commuters downtown tonight.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的公交罢工可能导致数百名通勤者今晚滞留市中心。

items.def_zh: 使困于受阻处，使受困孤立；放逐（某人）到荒岛上
items.def_en: 1. (usually passive, 'be marooned') To leave someone trapped and isolated in an inaccessible or deserted place with no way to escape.
items.ex_en: Fierce blizzards will easily maroon travelers in remote mountain passes without shelter.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的暴风雪很容易让没有避难所的旅客困在偏远的山口孤立无援。

items.def_zh: 陷入泥沼，受阻停滞；使陷入泥沼，使停滞不前
items.def_en: (also 'bog down') To become stuck or cause something to become stuck in mud or wet ground; to become delayed and unable to make progress.
items.ex_en: Heavy rains threatened to bog the supply trucks in the churned mud.
items.ex_zh: 暴雨眼看就要让补给卡车深陷在翻起的烂泥之中。
items.ex2_en: Heavy construction vehicles easily bog in the saturated ground after storms.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨过后，重型施工车辆很容易陷在湿透的泥地里。

items.def_zh: 使陷于泥沼，使缠身受阻
items.def_en: to cause something to sink in deep mud, or entangle someone heavily in difficulties
items.ex_en: Unending bureaucratic delays will mire the ambitious environmental reform in endless disputes.
items.ex_zh: 无休止的官僚延误将使这项雄心勃勃的环保改革陷入无休止的纷争泥沼。

items.def_zh: 陷入泥沼，受阻停滞（bog的过去式及过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past tense and past participle of bog; stuck in wet ground or stalled and unable to make progress ('bogged down').
items.ex_en: Negotiations became bogged in minor procedural disputes for nearly two whole weeks.
items.ex_zh: 谈判因细小的程序性争议而受阻停滞了将近整整两周。
items.ex2_en: Endless administrative red tape completely bogged the entire infrastructure project for months.
items.ex2_zh: 无休止的繁文缛节使整个基础设施项目彻底停滞了数月。

items.def_en: to catch an entity or person in a confined space, snare, or inescapable circumstance
items.ex_en: Corrupt syndicates often entrap desperate laborers through fraudulent recruitment contracts and debt.
items.ex_zh: 腐败犯罪集团往往通过欺诈性招工合同和债务使走投无路的劳工陷入圈套。

groups.summary_en: A traveler, vehicle, or project becomes physically trapped, stranded in a remote location, or hopelessly impeded by difficult terrain or adverse conditions. Verbs contrast physical sinking into soft mud/mire (bog, mire) with abandonment in desolate places (maroon, strand).
groups.summary_zh: 陷入泥沼难以脱身，或被遗弃偏远险境受困。
groups.desc_en: Denotes being involuntarily trapped, immobilized, or cut off from movement due to physical terrain or logistical failure, contrasting with deliberate delays or voluntary stays.
groups.desc_zh: 指因恶劣地形或后勤中断而被困无法动弹或滞留隔绝，区别于主动停留或轻微延误。
groups.nuance_en: strand: leave helpless and isolated far from transport (passengers / travelers / vehicles) · maroon: abandon ashore or in complete isolation with slim hope of rescue (sailors / survivors) · bog down: entrap in sticky ground, stalling progress (tanks / negotiations / reform) · mire: sink into deep mud or intractable entanglements (infantry / in bureaucracy / in debt) · ground: force an aircraft or ship onto land, halting travel (fleet / flights / vessels)
groups.nuance_zh: strand: 使流落孤立境地或被困途中 (passengers / travelers / vehicles) · maroon: 遗弃于荒僻绝地或孤岛 (sailors / survivors) · bog down: 陷入泥潭导致进退两难 (tanks / negotiations / reform) · mire: 深陷烂泥或棘手泥淖 (infantry / in bureaucracy / in debt) · ground: 迫使飞机停飞或船只搁浅 (fleet / flights / vessels)

groups.name: Strategic Avoidance & Circumvention · 策略规避与避开 (Sidestep, Eschew, Circumvent)
groups.tip: 巧妙躲避正面锋芒

items.def_en: (+ from sth) to deliberately avoid doing or facing something through hesitation or nervousness
items.ex_en: Responsible leaders never shy away from difficult discussions during severe corporate crises.
items.ex_zh: 负责任的领导者在严峻的企业危机期间绝不会回避艰难的讨论。

items.def_zh: 绕开（问题）；避重就轻地回避
items.def_en: (+ sth) to avoid dealing with or addressing an awkward issue or topic directly
items.ex_en: The politician tried to skirt around sensitive questions about recent campaign funding.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客试图避重就轻地绕开有关近期竞选资金的敏感问题。

items.def_en: to avoid discussing or dealing directly with a controversial topic or problem
items.ex_en: The spokesperson skillfully managed to skirt the controversial topic during yesterday's briefing.
items.ex_zh: 新闻发言人在昨天的简报会上巧妙地避开了对这一争议话题的讨论。

items.def_en: to avoid dealing with a rule, process, or hierarchy by going around it
items.ex_en: Senior administrators found a legal loophole to by-pass standard committee review protocols.
items.ex_zh: 高级管理人员找到了一个法律漏洞，借此绕过了标准的委员会审查程序。

items.def_zh: 绕开；避开（某人或棘手问题）
items.def_en: (+ of sb/sth) to deliberately avoid or keep away from a person, hazard, or sensitive topic
items.ex_en: Inexperienced investors are strongly advised to steer clear of volatile offshore assets.
items.ex_zh: 强烈建议缺乏经验的投资者远离波动剧烈的离岸资产。

items.def_en: to cleverly find a way around an obstacle, regulation, or difficulty
items.ex_en: Smugglers designed clever shipping routes to circumvent strict regional trade export embargoes.
items.ex_zh: 走私者设计了巧妙的航运路线以规避严格的地区贸易出口禁令。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To deliberately avoid or abstain from something out of principle or caution.
items.ex_en: Principled diplomats must eschew partisan interests to preserve long-term international peace accords.
items.ex_zh: 恪守原则的外交官必须摈弃党派利益，以维护长期的国际和平协议。

items.def_zh: 横跨一步躲开；回避，巧妙避开（问题或责任）
items.def_en: 1. To step quickly to one side to avoid someone or something. 2. To cleverly evade or avoid dealing with a difficult question or problem.
items.ex_en: The CEO managed to sidestep inquiries regarding upcoming layoffs during the meeting.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官在会议期间巧妙回避了关于即将裁员的质询。

items.def_en: to consistently and deliberately avoid a person, practice, or situation out of caution or distaste
items.ex_en: Ascetic monks deliberately shun modern conveniences to cultivate quiet spiritual contemplation daily.
items.ex_zh: 苦行僧深居简出，刻意远离现代便利设施，以每日潜修清静的心灵沉思。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to deliberately shunning, bypassing, or avoiding an issue, duty, or practice through strategic calculation, policy, or principled restraint rather than rapid physical movement.
groups.summary_zh: 出于原则、策略或审慎考量，刻意回避、绕开某事或不良行为。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the calculated, tactful, or illicit evasion of obstacles, duties, or confrontations, contrasting with plain retreat or involuntary escaping.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过智谋、规避手段或迂回走位巧妙避开阻碍或责任，区别于单纯逃跑或被动脱逃。
groups.nuance_en: circumvent: bypass formal rules or barriers via ingenuity (regulations / sanctions / security) · sidestep: evade a tricky issue by shifting focus deftly (questions / controversy / challenges) · eschew: deliberately and habitually abstain from on moral or pragmatic grounds (violence / publicity / meat) · skirt: move along the outer edge to avoid confronting directly (the issue / danger / regulations) · steer clear: actively maintain a safe distance from a hazard (trouble / conflict / gossip)
groups.nuance_zh: circumvent: 钻空子绕过繁文缛节或禁令 (regulations / sanctions / security) · sidestep: 灵巧回避棘手问题 (questions / controversy / challenges) · eschew: 出于原则或审慎有意戒绝 (violence / publicity / meat) · skirt: 擦着边缘掠过以避开要害 (the issue / danger / regulations) · steer clear: 刻意与麻烦保持距离 (trouble / conflict / gossip)

groups.name: Strategic Orchestration & Intricate Engineering · 策划运作与精密编排 (Choreograph, Contrive)
groups.tip: 运筹帷幄，预先构思蓝图

items.def_en: to skillfully and artfully bring about a complex or tricky event
items.ex_en: Operatives worked quietly to engineer a decisive shift in foreign electoral policy.
items.ex_zh: 特工人员暗中活动，巧妙促成了外国选举政策的决定性转变。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to invent, concoct, or devise an elaborate plan, scheme, or story
items.ex_en: He had to cook up an excuse for being late to the morning briefing.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不编造一个早会迟到的借口。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to produce a creative idea, complex plan, or solution through thought
items.ex_en: He had to think up a plausible excuse for arriving two hours late.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不编出一个合理的借口来解释迟到两个小时的原因。

items.def_zh: 凭空构想出；策划出（奇想或复杂计划）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to invent or plan something that is very creative, unusual, or improbable
items.ex_en: Marketing interns can dream up wild promotional stunts to attract younger consumers.
items.ex_zh: 营销实习生能够凭空构想出各种狂野的促销绝招来吸引年轻消费者。

items.def_zh: 构想出；发明（精巧计划或装置）
items.def_en: to invent a plan, method, or system with careful thought and ingenuity
items.ex_en: Engineers worked overtime to devise an ingenious water filtration system for refugees.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们加班加点，为难民构想出一套巧妙的水过滤系统。

items.def_en: to plan and direct an elaborate undertaking, complex scheme, or conspiracy from behind the scenes
items.ex_en: Detectives suspect international criminals helped mastermind the daring diamond museum heist downtown.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们怀疑国际罪犯在幕后策划了市中心这起大胆的钻石博物馆劫案。

items.def_zh: 精心策划；密谋操纵（全局）
items.def_en: to arrange, plan, or coordinate the elements of an intricate situation to produce a desired effect
items.ex_en: Rebel commanders attempted to orchestrate a coordinated uprising across several neighboring provinces.
items.ex_zh: 叛军指挥官企图在邻近的数个省份精心策划一场协同起义。

items.def_zh: 精心策划，细致安排；编排（舞蹈等动作）
items.def_en: 1. To plan and coordinate a complex event, situation, or operation carefully. 2. To design and arrange the steps and movements for a dance or performance.
items.ex_en: Campaign managers worked tirelessly to choreograph every moment of the candidate's convention.
items.ex_zh: 竞选经理们不辞辛劳地精心编排候选人大会上的每一个时刻。

items.def_zh: 谋划，巧妙策划；设法做到，巧计促成；发明，设计
items.def_en: 1. To cleverly plan, devise, or invent something. 2. To manage to do or bring about something despite difficulties.
items.ex_en: The captive managed to contrive an ingenious escape route despite continuous surveillance.
items.ex_zh: 尽管受到持续监视，那名俘虏还是设法策划出一条巧妙的逃生路线。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe designing and pulling together complex schemes, maneuvers, or staged actions with elaborate precision, often to produce a calculated, prearranged outcome.
groups.summary_zh: 通过精巧策划与严密编排，推动复杂事件或预谋方案按预期执行。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the sophisticated, deliberate design and harmonization of complex schemes or multi-party actions, contrasting with spontaneous execution or haphazard planning.
groups.desc_zh: 指对复杂事件或多方力量进行深思熟虑的精密谋划与协同编排，区别于即兴发挥或随性安排。
groups.nuance_en: orchestrate: harmonize diverse elements for maximum collective impact (campaign / coup / revival) · choreograph: plan elaborate sequences down to the micro-detail (transition / moves / protest) · mastermind: act as the intellectual architect behind a covert or grand plot (robbery / plot / scheme) · engineer: cleverly manipulate conditions to deliver a specific outcome (deal / downfall / consensus) · devise: invent an inventive method, plan, or system from scratch (strategy / plan / trap)
groups.nuance_zh: orchestrate: 统筹整合各方以精心策划 (campaign / coup / revival) · choreograph: 精确编排各环节细枝末节 (transition / moves / protest) · mastermind: 作为幕后主脑策划大案要案 (robbery / plot / scheme) · engineer: 施展手腕暗中促成结果 (deal / downfall / consensus) · devise: 从无到有设计出精巧方案 (strategy / plan / trap)

groups.name: Strike & Hack with Bladed Weapon · 兵刃刺斩 (Bayonet, Tomahawk, Pike)
groups.tip: 冷兵器刺穿与劈砍伤

items.def_zh: （野猪、大象等）用长牙刺戳；用长牙掘
items.def_en: To stab, gore, or dig something with long tusks.
items.ex_en: The enraged wild boar turned fiercely to tusk its wounded hunter.
items.ex_zh: 被激怒的野猪猛然转身，用长牙狠刺受伤的猎人。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) cut or wound severely with violent blows from a bladed weapon
items.ex_en: Marauders used heavy broadswords to chop up enemy defensive barricades and sentries.
items.ex_zh: 掠夺者使用沉重的阔剑乱砍敌人的防御路障并斩伤哨兵。

items.def_en: strike repeatedly and roughly with an axe, cleaver, or heavy blade
items.ex_en: Exhausted pioneers had to hack away dense jungle growth with heavy machetes.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的拓荒者不得不挥舞重型大砍刀猛劈茂密的丛林植被。

items.def_en: to strike or hack forcefully using a heavy butcher blade
items.ex_en: The butcher swung downwards to cleaver the tough mutton into uniform joints.
items.ex_zh: 屠夫挥刀猛剁，将韧硬的羊肉劈砍成均等的肉块。

items.def_en: to pierce or assault violently using a short stabbing blade
items.ex_en: The assassin emerged from shadowy alleyways to dagger the unsuspecting noble guard.
items.ex_zh: 刺客从阴暗的巷弄中现身，用匕首猛刺毫无防备的贵族侍卫。

items.def_en: to thrust or pierce through with a long spear or pike
items.ex_en: Infantry advanced steadily in tight formation to pike down advancing cavalry lines.
items.ex_zh: 步兵以紧密阵型稳步推进，用长矛刺击冲锋的骑兵阵列。

items.def_en: To stab or kill someone with a bayonet.
items.ex_en: Trench soldiers charged across the muddy field to bayonet enemy defensive positions.
items.ex_zh: 战壕士兵冲过泥泞的阵地，用刺刀刺杀敌方防御阵地内的守军。

items.def_en: to strike, cut, or kill with a heavy curved cavalry sword
items.ex_en: Cavalry riders galloped furiously to saber fleeing infantrymen across the wide meadow.
items.ex_zh: 骑兵呼啸奔驰，挥舞军刀砍杀穿过广阔草地溃逃的步兵。

items.def_zh: 用（北美印第安）战斧砍杀
items.def_en: To strike, cut, or kill someone with a tomahawk.
items.ex_en: Frontier raiders moved stealthily through moonlit forests to tomahawk unsuspecting colonial outposts.
items.ex_zh: 边境袭击者悄然穿过月光笼罩的森林，用战斧砍杀毫无防备的殖民哨所人员。

groups.summary_en: Denominal combat verbs where the instrument itself defines the violent thrusting, gouging, or hacking attack inflicted on an enemy (e.g., using a fixed rifle-blade, thrown axe, or animal tusk).
groups.summary_zh: 指借由特定兵刃（刺刀、战斧）或獠牙施加的刺杀与劈击动作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes aggressive, close-quarters physical violence inflicted with specific edged or pointed weaponry, contrasting with blunt trauma or firearm discharge.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用特定冷兵器进行的近战砍杀、刺扎或劈削，区别于钝器击打或热兵器射击。
groups.nuance_en: bayonet: stab or thrust using a rifle-mounted blade (infantry / prisoners / sentries) · hack away: chop repeatedly with crude, brutal strokes (at vines / at flesh / at armor) · saber: cut down or wound with a heavy cavalry sword (enemy / riders / fleeing troops) · pike: impale or strike using a long spear (charging cavalry / spearmen) · cleaver: chop or cleave heavily as with a butcher's knife (carcass / bone / meat)
groups.nuance_zh: bayonet: 用枪刺近战刺杀 (infantry / prisoners / sentries) · hack away: 挥舞利器胡乱猛砍 (at vines / at flesh / at armor) · saber: 用马刀挥砍斩击 (enemy / riders / fleeing troops) · pike: 用长枪戳刺穿透 (charging cavalry / spearmen) · cleaver: 如屠夫般用重刃大砍 (carcass / bone / meat)

groups.name: Strip & Peel Surface · 剥壳与脱皮 (Decorticate, Hull, Pare)
groups.tip: 解调分离特定信号成分

items.def_en: (+ sth) to gradually remove the outer layer or skin of something using a sharp tool
items.ex_en: Chefs must carefully pare away bruised rind before slicing fresh winter melons.
items.ex_zh: 厨师在切新鲜冬瓜前，必须仔细削去碰伤的外皮。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove an outer skin, rind, or covering by pulling it away
items.ex_en: Kids love to peel off sticky citrus rinds after lunch every day.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们每天午饭后都喜欢剥掉黏糊糊的柑橘皮。
items.ex2_en: The weathered paint will gradually peel off the damp exterior garage wall.
items.ex2_zh: 风化变质的油漆会逐渐从潮湿的车库外墙上剥落。

items.def_zh: 给（谷物、果实）脱壳或去蒂
items.def_en: to remove the outer husk, pod, or calyx from grains, beans, or fruit
items.ex_en: Workers use specialized mechanical drums to hull dry coffee beans every harvest.
items.ex_zh: 每年收获季，工人们都会使用专用的机械转筒给干燥的咖啡豆脱壳。

items.def_en: to remove the leafy husk of corn or open the shell of oysters and clams
items.ex_en: Volunteers gathered at community tables to shuck freshly harvested ears of sweetcorn.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们聚在社区桌前，剥去刚采收的甜玉米苞叶。

items.def_zh: 剥去；剥下（外皮、壳或保护层）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove an outer layer, skin, bark, or covering from something
items.ex_en: Carpenters use sharp flat chisels to strip off old blistered wood varnish.
items.ex_zh: 木工用锋利的平凿剥去起泡的旧木器清漆层。

items.def_en: to strip or scrape the protective outer bark from a tree or log
items.ex_en: Foresters must bark felled timber promptly before fungal rot damages precious heartwood.
items.ex_zh: 林业人员必须在真菌腐蚀珍贵心材前，及时剥去砍伐原木的树皮。

items.def_zh: 剥去（树皮、外壳等）；剥除（器官或组织的）被膜（或皮质）
items.def_en: (botany, medicine) To remove the bark, husk, or outer cortex from a plant or body organ.
items.ex_en: Skilled surgeons gently decorticate dense fibrous pleural tissue during delicate thoracic procedures.
items.ex_zh: 在精细的胸腔手术中，熟练的外科医生轻轻剥除增厚的纤维胸膜组织。

items.def_en: (telecommunications) To extract the original modulating information signal from a carrier wave.
items.ex_en: The circuit contains specialized analog components designed to demodulate high-frequency carrier signals.
items.ex_zh: 该电路包含专用于对高频载波信号进行检波解调的模拟元件。

items.def_en: to strip off the skin or hide of an animal or person completely and brutally
items.ex_en: Cruel tyrants ordered palace executioners to publicly flay condemned political conspirators alive.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的君主命令宫廷刽子手当众将定罪的政治阴谋家活活剥皮。

groups.summary_en: An agent strips, pares, or strips away the outer shell, bark, rind, or protective membrane from biological specimens, grains, or organs.
groups.summary_zh: 机械或人工剥除外皮、谷壳、树皮或组织外膜。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the mechanical or manual peeling away of an external natural rind, skin, or bark, contrasting with deep dissection or chemical erosion.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过机械或人工手段将表层果皮、树皮或外壳剥除削去，区别于深层解剖或化学腐蚀。
groups.nuance_en: pare: trim the thin outer skin or edge of something meticulously (apple / rind / nails) · peel off: strip away an outer layer, skin, or protective coating (skin / bark / sticker) · hull: remove outer shell, husks, or calyx of seeds or berries (strawberries / peas / corn) · decorticate: strip the bark or cortex surgically/industrially (brain / tree / seed) · bark: strip outer bark from a tree trunk or scrape skin roughly (tree / shins / knuckles)
groups.nuance_zh: pare: 精细削去薄外皮或边缘 (apple / rind / nails) · peel off: 撕下剥离表皮或涂层 (skin / bark / sticker) · hull: 去除种籽的外壳或草莓果蒂 (strawberries / peas / corn) · decorticate: 工业剥皮或外科剥离皮层 (brain / tree / seed) · bark: 剥除树皮或擦破大片皮肉 (tree / shins / knuckles)

groups.name: Strip Husk & Detach Layer · 剥离与脱壳 (Husk, Shuck, Ablate)
groups.tip: 剥除果壳或外层表皮

items.def_en: to come off or cause to come off in small thin pieces or layers
items.ex_en: Dry weather caused old exterior wall plaster to crack and flake off.
