items.ex_en: Plant roots absorb crucial moisture and dissolved minerals through their semipermeable cellular membranes.
items.ex_zh: 植物根系通过其半透细胞膜逐渐吸收关键的水分与溶解矿物质。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To take in liquid or moisture completely into porous material or organic tissue
items.ex_en: Dry cellulose sponges rapidly soak up liquid spills from porous polished marble surfaces.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的纤维素海绵能迅速将多孔抛光大理石表面溢出的液体完全吸净。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To absorb moisture or nutrients readily and completely into the body or cells
items.ex_en: We stood silently at the summit, drinking in the magnificent view.
items.ex_zh: 我们静静地站在山顶上，尽情饱览那壮丽的景色。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To pull fluids, air, or essential nutrients inward into bodily tissues
items.ex_en: Deep root networks draw in underground moisture efficiently during prolonged periods of drought.
items.ex_zh: 深密的根系网络在长期干旱期间能够高效地摄取地下深处的水分。

items.def_en: To absorb food or nourishment into the body tissues after digestion
items.ex_en: Intestinal walls assimilate essential nutrients directly into the bloodstream during the digestive process.
items.ex_zh: 肠壁在消化过程中将必需的营养成分直接吸收并同化输送至血液之中。
items.ex2_en: Nutrients assimilate more efficiently into the bloodstream after light physical exercise.
items.ex2_zh: 轻微运动后，营养物质会更有效地被血液吸收。

items.def_en: (Physiological/Botanical) To take in fluid or moisture into organic structures by absorption
items.ex_en: Dry seeds imbibe water rapidly during germination, swelling to twice their original size.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的种子在萌发期间迅速吸水，膨胀至原先的两倍大。

items.def_en: (biology/medicine) to absorb something again, especially a fluid or substance back into tissues or the bloodstream
items.ex_en: The delicate renal tubules reabsorb vital nutrients into the circulating bloodstream with quiet perfection.
items.ex_zh: 纤细的肾小管以静谧的精妙机制，将重要营养素重吸收进循环的血液之中。

items.def_zh: 再吸收，重新吸收（骨质或组织）
items.def_en: (biology/medicine) to break down and absorb bone or tissue back into the body
items.ex_en: Specialized osteoclasts resorb damaged bone matrix to allow newer, healthier tissue to flourish.
items.ex_zh: 特化的破骨细胞重吸收受损的骨基质，好让更健康的新生组织繁衍生长。

groups.summary_en: Biological tissue, cells, or bodily substances take in fluids, nutrients, or broken-down organic material. 'Resorb' and 'reabsorb' specifically detail the physiological uptake of substances previously secreted or bone/tissue matrix degradation, whereas 'absorb' describes general uptake.
groups.summary_zh: 生物组织、细胞对液体、营养物质或自体降解产物的摄取与吸收。
groups.desc_en: Denotes drawing liquid, energy, or chemical substances across a membrane into an internal system, contrasting with expelling or repelling.
groups.desc_zh: 指机体或物质将流体、能量或分子内聚吞并至内部系统，区别于排泄或抵挡外推。
groups.nuance_en: absorb: general drawing in and retaining of moisture or impact (liquids / shocks / heat) · soak up: greedily taking in large quantities like a sponge (sun / liquid / atmosphere) · imbibe: drinking in liquids or taking in ideas culturally (alcohol / culture / wisdom) · assimilate: digesting and integrating substances or concepts into a body (nutrients / ideas) · resorb: physiological reabsorption of bodily tissues or fluids (bone / blood / cysts)
groups.nuance_zh: absorb: 广义的汲取、吸收液体或吸收冲击震荡 (liquids / shocks / heat) · soak up: 像海绵般贪婪大体量地吸饱 (sun / liquid / atmosphere) · imbibe: 饮入液体，或浸染文化思想 (alcohol / culture / wisdom) · assimilate: 消化吸收营养或同化文化观念 (nutrients / ideas) · resorb: 生理学上病理组织或骨质的再吸收溶化 (bone / blood / cysts)

groups.name: Accuse & Challenge Validity · 归咎与质疑 (Impute, Impugn, Asperse)
groups.tip: 将过错归咎于他人并加以指控

items.def_en: to accuse or incriminate someone by attributing guilt or criminal wrongdoing to them
items.ex_en: The prosecutor produced telephone records that tended to inculpate the defendant in the conspiracy.
items.ex_zh: 检察官出示了电话记录，这些记录意在指控该被告参与了共谋。

items.def_en: to charge someone with a crime or expose them to an accusation
items.ex_en: The forged documents were deliberately planted to criminate the innocent finance director.
items.ex_zh: 伪造的文件被故意栽赃，用以控告这位无辜的财务主管有罪。

items.def_en: to attack someone's reputation or integrity with false or malicious charges
items.ex_en: Envious rivals sought to asperse her virtuous character with malicious, whispered falsehoods.
items.ex_zh: 心怀嫉妒的对手企图以恶毒的窃窃流言中伤她高洁的品格。

items.def_zh: 向（某人名誉）投以怀疑；归咎
items.def_en: (cast aspersion/doubt on sb/sth) Cause people to doubt the honesty, integrity, or character of sb
items.ex_en: His erratic testimony only served to cast serious doubt on his professional integrity.
items.ex_zh: 他飘忽不定的证词只让人对他的职业操守产生了严重怀疑。

items.def_en: (+ sth on sb) Blame sb for a crime or mistake, especially unfairly
items.ex_en: Don't try to pin the blame on me for your own sloppy accounting mistakes.
items.ex_zh: 别想把你那马虎算错账的过失归咎到我头上。

items.def_en: to formally call someone before a court to answer an indictment, or to publicly accuse them of a fault
items.ex_en: The magistrate will arraign the corrupt official tomorrow on multiple counts of bribery.
items.ex_zh: 地方治安法官将于明天就多项受贿罪名正式传讯这位贪官。

items.def_zh: 归咎于，把……归罪于；把……归因于
items.def_en: (formal) ('impute something to') To claim that someone is responsible for a fault or crime; to attribute a quality or characteristic to someone.
items.ex_en: It is unjust to impute selfish motives to a purely benevolent community initiative.
items.ex_zh: 将自私的动机归咎于一项纯粹出于善意的社区举措是不公正的。

items.def_zh: 指责，抨击，质疑（……的真实性或诚实性）
items.def_en: (formal) To challenge or attack the truth, honesty, or integrity of a motive, character, or statement.
items.ex_en: The defense attorney tried to impugn the witness's integrity during a fierce cross-examination.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师在激烈的交叉盘问中试图质疑该证人的诚信。

groups.summary_en: A speaker formally attributes a fault, crime, or unworthy motive to someone, or challenges and attacks the integrity and credibility of their character or statements. Register is decidedly formal, rhetorical, and legalistic.
groups.summary_zh: 在言论中向某人归咎责任或质疑、诋毁其人品与诚信。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formally or rhetorically assigning blame, wrongdoing, or false motives to someone, contrasting with neutral attribution by carrying an adversarial intent to damage credibility or establish guilt.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过正式指控或言语攻击将过失、罪责或虚妄动机归咎于对方，区别于中性归因，带有损害其公信力或确立罪责的对抗色彩。
groups.nuance_en: impugn: directly challenge the honesty, integrity, or validity of something (integrity / motives / validity) · impute: ascribe an undesirable action or motive to a person (motives / blame / guilt) · asperse: maliciously slander or defame a person's reputation (reputation / character) · arraign: formally charge before a court or severely censure publicly (defendant / policies) · pin on: informally shift or fix blame onto a scapegoat (blame / crime / rap)
groups.nuance_zh: impugn: 质疑攻击真实性或人格 (integrity / motives / validity) · impute: 将不良意图或过失归咎于人 (motives / blame / guilt) · asperse: 诽谤中伤名誉 (reputation / character) · arraign: 传讯提审或公开谴责 (defendant / policies) · pin on: 口语中栽赃甩锅 (blame / crime / rap)

groups.name: Acknowledge & Confess · 承认与坦白 (Admit, Acknowledge, Confess)
groups.tip: 从勉强认可到主动供认罪错

items.def_en: to accept or admit that something exists or that a factual situation is true
items.ex_en: The board must formally acknowledge the structural failures outlined in the auditor's report.
items.ex_zh: 董事会必须正式认可审计报告中所列出的结构性缺陷。

items.def_en: (+ to) to admit that you have done something wrong, usually something minor (informal)
items.ex_en: You might as well fess up to breaking Mom's favourite porcelain vase.
items.ex_zh: 你最好还是坦白承认打碎了妈妈最喜爱的瓷花瓶吧。

items.def_zh: 敞开心扉；坦率道出心事
items.def_en: (+ to sb) Speak honestly and openly about your feelings or secret experiences
items.ex_en: He finally decided to open up to his closest friend about his grief.
items.ex_zh: 他终于决定向自己最亲密的朋友敞开心扉，倾诉内心的悲痛。

items.def_en: (+ to sth/to doing sth) Admit that you have done something wrong, shameful, or embarrassing
items.ex_en: No one would own up to breaking the window, so the whole class was kept after school.
items.ex_zh: 没有人愿意承认打破了窗户，所以全班都被罚放学后留堂。

items.def_zh: 承认，供认；准许进入；接收（入院等）
items.def_en: 1. To agree or acknowledge, often unwillingly, that something is true or that you have done something wrong. 2. To allow someone to enter a place or join an institution.
items.ex_en: The junior analyst had to admit that her forecast was entirely based on guesswork.
items.ex_zh: 初级分析师不得不承认她的预测完全建立在推测之上。

items.def_en: 1. To admit, especially formally or to police, that you have done something bad, illegal, or embarrassing. 2. To tell God or a priest about your sins.
items.ex_en: Under intense questioning, the suspect chose to confess his involvement in the payroll heist.
items.ex_zh: 在严厉盘问下，嫌疑人选择供认自己参与了这起工资款抢劫案。

items.def_en: [I/T] to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true or that you have lost an argument
items.ex_en: The incumbent had to concede defeat after trailing by twenty thousand uncounted ballots.
items.ex_zh: 在落后两万张未计选票后，现任官员不得不认输。

items.def_en: (+ with/about) to tell the full truth about something you have kept secret
items.ex_en: The director finally decided to come clean about the company's hidden operational debts.
items.ex_zh: 董事最终决定全盘托出公司隐瞒的运营债务。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe acknowledging that something is true or that one is responsible for an error or wrongdoing, ranging from reluctant concessions to deep, contrite unburdening.
groups.summary_zh: 承认某事属实或承认自身过错，从勉强认可递进至痛切招供坦白。
groups.desc_en: Denotes conceding the truth of a fact, fault, or secret often previously withheld, differing from simple stating by overcoming internal hesitation or external resistance.
groups.desc_zh: 指承认此前隐瞒或抵赖的事实、过错或秘密，区别于陈述客观事实，包含克服心理抗拒或打破否认的动态过程。
groups.nuance_en: admit: yield to the truth of an unwelcome fact or fault (mistake / defeat / guilt) · confess: disclose sins, crimes, or deep-seated secrets with moral gravity (sins / crimes / feelings) · concede: reluctantly grant the validity of an opponent's point or victory (point / defeat / election) · acknowledge: openly recognize the reality, existence, or receipt of something (reality / contribution / receipt) · own up: fully accept personal responsibility for a wrongdoing (mistake / fault)
groups.nuance_zh: admit: 不情愿地承认过失或事实 (mistake / defeat / guilt) · confess: 坦白罪恶或内心隐秘 (sins / crimes / feelings) · concede: 退让承认对方论点或落败 (point / defeat / election) · acknowledge: 正式公开认可存在或接受事实 (reality / contribution / receipt) · own up: 勇于承担个人过错责任 (mistake / fault)

groups.name: Administer & Direct Governance · 治理与统领管理 (Administer, Conduct, Captain)
groups.tip: 指引前行并主持日常运转

items.def_zh: 组织，实施，主持；指挥（乐团）；带领，引导；传导（热、电）
items.def_en: 1. to organize and perform a particular activity; to manage or direct. 2. to direct the performance of musicians or an orchestra. 3. to lead or guide someone somewhere. 4. to transmit heat, electricity, or sound.
items.ex_en: An independent ethics committee will conduct a thorough investigation into the alleged misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 一个独立的伦理委员会将对指控的不当行为展开彻底调查。

items.def_zh: 统领，担任……的队长（或船长、机长）
items.def_en: to act as the leader or captain of a sports team, ship, or aircraft.
items.ex_en: The veteran midfielder was chosen to captain the national football team this season.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的中场球员本赛季被选为国家足球队的队长。

items.def_en: [I/T] to officially conduct the policy, actions, and affairs of a state or organization
items.ex_en: Strict constitutional guidelines govern the daily operations and emergency powers of the cabinet.
items.ex_zh: 严格的宪法准则制约并治理着内阁的日常运作与紧急权力。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to assume formal control, command, or administration of an organization or jurisdiction
items.ex_en: The new commissioner will take over administration of the police department next Monday.
items.ex_zh: 新任专员将于下周一接管警政部门的管理权。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to be in official charge of or lead a situation, organization, or period of governance
items.ex_en: The elder statesman was asked to preside over the newly established transitional authority.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深政治家受邀主持统领新成立的过渡权力机构。

items.def_zh: 管理，掌管；执行，实施；给予，施用（药物等）
items.def_en: 1. to manage and organize the affairs of a business, government, or institution. 2. to implement or enforce a law, test, or justice. 3. to give or provide medicine, treatment, or aid to someone.
items.ex_en: Trained civil servants administer the public health programs across all nineteen regional districts.
items.ex_zh: 训练有素的公务员在全省十九个行政辖区内管理并推行公共卫生项目。

items.def_en: (+ over) to hold the position of authority in meetings or governance frameworks
items.ex_en: The chief justice will preside over the contentious parliamentary debate regarding electoral reform.
items.ex_zh: 首席大法官将主持这场关于选举改革、争议颇大的议会辩论。

items.def_en: to direct, pilot, or act as chief leader of an enterprise or organization
items.ex_en: She was appointed to helm the struggling technology firm through its complex restructuring.
items.ex_zh: 她被任命统领这家陷入困境的科技公司度过复杂的重组期。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate exercising formal executive direction, stewardship, or organizational command over public affairs, institutions, maritime crews, or projects.
groups.summary_zh: 指行使公职行政管理、统领机构组织或指挥团队项目。
groups.desc_en: Denotes exercising executive authority, organizational control, and steering over an institution or endeavor, contrasting with passive supervision by embodying hands-on governance and command.
groups.desc_zh: 指对组织或事业行使行政权力、领导权与统筹治理，区别于被动监视，强调实质性的统领调度与执掌方向。
groups.nuance_en: administer: manage the practical execution and operation of legal or organizational affairs (justice / fund / medicine) · govern: wield sovereign regulatory control and policy-making over a body (country / institution / conduct) · preside over: occupy the authoritative head seat during a meeting or epoch of change (meeting / court / transition) · helm: steer and direct the overall vision of an organization (company / project / initiative) · conduct: organize and lead the execution of a specific structured activity (investigation / symphony / business)
groups.nuance_zh: administer: 执行管理具体政务或机构事务 (justice / fund / medicine) · govern: 统筹治理并制定监管规范 (country / institution / conduct) · preside over: 主持会议或掌管时代过渡 (meeting / court / transition) · helm: 掌舵执掌机构方向 (company / project / initiative) · conduct: 组织操办具体活动或调查 (investigation / symphony / business)

groups.name: Admit & Re-admit · 准入与接纳 (Admit, Enroll, Matriculate)
groups.tip: 重新批准进入或再次接纳

items.def_zh: 准许进入，接纳入学/住院
items.def_en: to allow someone to enter an institution, school, or hospital as an official member or patient
items.ex_en: The prestigious academy will admit only forty prospective musicians for the autumn semester.
items.ex_zh: 这所声誉卓著的学院秋季学期仅接纳四十名未来的音乐家入学。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to accept someone as an admitted member, student, or hospital patient
items.ex_en: The overcrowded clinic could no longer take in any more emergency fever patients.
items.ex_zh: 人满为患的诊所再也无法收治更多的急诊发热患者了。

items.def_en: (+ sb/for sth) to officially enroll or admit someone into an organization, course, or institution
items.ex_en: The academy decided to sign up thirty eager young recruits for flight training.
items.ex_zh: 学院决定为三十名热切的年轻新学员办理飞行训练的注册入会。
items.ex2_en: Dozens of ambitious volunteers signed up for the weekend environmental cleanup project.
items.ex2_zh: 数十名积极的志愿者报名参加了周末的环境清理项目。

items.def_en: to restore someone to a previous official position, membership, or rank
items.ex_en: The arbitration panel voted unanimously to reinstate the wrongfully discharged senior union representative.
items.ex_zh: 仲裁委员会一致投票决定恢复这名被不当解雇的高级工会代表的职位。

items.def_en: [I/T] to officially register someone as a member or student in an institution
items.ex_en: The vocational college hopes to enroll hundreds of qualified apprentices before September begins.
items.ex_zh: 这所职业学院希望在九月来临之前招收数百名合格的学徒注册入学。
items.ex2_en: Many eager foreign students will enroll in the advanced language course this fall.
items.ex2_zh: 今年秋季，许多热切的外国留学生将注册高级语言课程。

items.def_zh: 录取入学，准予注册入大学（正式语体）
items.def_en: [I/T] to formally admit or be admitted as a student into a university or college
items.ex_en: Gifted scholars will matriculate into the university after completing their rigorous entrance examinations.
items.ex_zh: 有才华的学者在完成严苛的入学考试后将被正式录取进入该大学就读。
items.ex2_en: The prestigious university decided to matriculate fifty outstanding foreign applicants this autumn.
items.ex2_zh: 这所知名大学决定在今年秋天录取五十名优秀的外国申请者。

items.def_zh: 重新准许进入，重新接纳（readmit 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of readmit: to allow someone to enter, join, or be admitted to a place or institution again.
items.ex_en: The recovering patient was readmitted to the intensive care unit after developing complications.
items.ex_zh: 这名处于恢复期的病人在出现并发症后被重新收治进入重症监护病房。

items.def_zh: 重新接纳，准许…重新加入
items.def_en: to allow someone to enter a school, hospital, country, or organization again
items.ex_en: The disciplinary committee decided not to readmit the expelled student for another term.
items.ex_zh: 纪律委员会决定下学期不再重新接纳那名被开除的学生入学。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve granting an individual official membership, entrance, or re-entry into an institution, school, hospital, or organization.
groups.summary_zh: 指机构或组织在制度上批准某人进入、恢复学籍或接纳为正式成员。
groups.desc_en: Denotes granting formal entry or membership into an institution or institutional status, distinct from generic welcoming by adhering to institutional criteria and registration procedures.
groups.desc_zh: 指依规准予进入机构或取得制度化成员资格，区别于一般迎接入门，强调符合标准程序与资格认证。
groups.nuance_en: admit: grant entrance or access based on qualification or eligibility (patient / student / visitor) · enroll: officially register someone into a course, school, or organization (student / member / voter) · matriculate: formally enroll as a degree-seeking candidate at a college or university (student / freshman) · readmit: grant entry back to a person or entity after exclusion or discharge (patient / member / state) · take in: absorb or shelter someone into a home or establishment (stranger / lodger / stray)
groups.nuance_zh: admit: 准予进入或符合资格接纳 (patient / student / visitor) · enroll: 正式注册登记为成员或学员 (student / member / voter) · matriculate: 注册为高校学位候选人 (student / freshman) · readmit: 重新接纳或准予重返 (patient / member / state) · take in: 收容寄宿或吸纳接纳 (stranger / lodger / stray)

groups.name: Advance & Exalt Status · 提拔与擢升 (Promote, Elevate, Aggrandize)
groups.tip: 提拔地位官职上升

items.def_en: [I/T] to help someone move forward in career or social status
items.ex_en: Securing that lucrative corporate contract helped advance her standing within the competitive firm.
items.ex_zh: 赢得那份利润丰厚的商业合同有助于推进她在竞争激烈的公司里的地位。
items.ex2_en: Talented junior diplomats can advance rapidly through the bureaucratic hierarchy.
items.ex2_zh: 才华横溢的初级外交官可以在官僚体系中迅速晋升。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to advance in rank, corporate hierarchy, or social standing
items.ex_en: Hardworking employees who meet ambitious performance targets usually move up within two years.
items.ex_zh: 完成雄心勃勃业绩目标的勤奋员工通常会在两年内获得晋升。
items.ex2_en: The board decided to move up promising young managers to senior leadership roles.
items.ex2_zh: 董事会决定将有前途的年轻经理提拔至高级领导岗位。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to elevate someone abruptly to a higher rank, position, or classification
items.ex_en: They decided to bump up the creative copywriter to associate creative director overnight.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定连夜将这位富有创意的文案破格提拔为副创意总监。

items.def_zh: 提拔，晋升；促进，推进；推销，宣传
items.def_en: 1. to raise someone to a higher rank, position, or status. 2. to encourage the development or progress of something. 3. to advertise or publicize something to increase sales
items.ex_en: The regional board voted to promote the talented young researcher to laboratory director.
items.ex_zh: 地区委员会投票决定提拔这位才华横溢的年轻研究员为实验室主管。

items.def_en: (+ to) to raise someone to a higher or more important rank, dignity, or position
items.ex_en: His exemplary diplomatic service helped elevate him to the high rank of ambassador.
items.ex_zh: 他典范般的外交功绩使他被提升到了大使的高级职位。

items.def_en: to elevate someone to the rank of nobility or endow with noble qualities
items.ex_en: Selfless devotion to the vulnerable will surely ennoble the human spirit beyond earthly riches.
items.ex_zh: 对弱势群体的无私奉献必将升华人类的心灵品格，使其超越世俗财富。

items.def_en: to raise someone to a very high level of power, status, or praise
items.ex_en: The grateful monarch chose to exalt the valiant commander above all court dignitaries.
items.ex_zh: 心怀感激的君王选择擢升英勇的指挥官，使其地位凌驾于所有朝臣之上。

items.def_zh: 提升…的地位（或权力、财富）；吹捧，夸大
items.def_en: 1. to increase the power, wealth, status, or importance of someone or something. 2. to praise or portray something as greater than it really is
items.ex_en: The ambitious monarch used foreign wars solely to aggrandize his realm and authority.
items.ex_zh: 这位野心勃勃的君主利用对外战争仅仅是为了扩张疆土并提升自身权力。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures upward mobility in social, corporate, or political rank. Verbs scale from regular organizational promotion, to dignified spiritual/social elevation, culminating in excessive aggrandizement of power and prestige.
groups.summary_zh: 指在阶级、官阶或权力声望上向上提拔、擢升，乃至极度扩充势力地位。
groups.desc_en: Denotes raising an individual to a higher rank, post, dignity, or prestige, contrasting with basic vertical lifting by operating within hierarchical, social, or spiritual ladders.
groups.desc_zh: 指在等级制、社会阶层或威望梯次上擢升提拔个体，区别于物理上的托起，强调地位、尊严或权势的跃升。
groups.nuance_en: promote: raise to a higher job rank, position, or tier (employee / officer / cause) · elevate: raise to a superior intellectual, moral, or social standing (status / discourse / rank) · exalt: glorify, revere, or praise to an supreme degree (leader / virtue / hero) · ennoble: bestow noble rank on, or lend moral dignity to (commoner / spirit / struggle) · aggrandize: augment power, wealth, or stature, often grasping or excessive (wealth / power / reputation)
groups.nuance_zh: promote: 职级或序列晋升 (employee / officer / cause) · elevate: 抬高社会或精神层次 (status / discourse / rank) · exalt: 崇敬捧高或赞美至极 (leader / virtue / hero) · ennoble: 封爵或赋予高尚品格 (commoner / spirit / struggle) · aggrandize: 扩张壮大权势或声望 (wealth / power / reputation)

groups.name: Affix & Append Linguistic Elements · 添加与附加 (Prefix, Suffix, Affix)
groups.tip: 在词干前后添加词缀成分

items.def_en: (+ to) to casually or arbitrarily attach an extra item or amendment to an existing text
items.ex_en: Don't just tack on an irrelevant concluding clause to that carefully worded contract.
items.ex_zh: 别把一条风马牛不相及的附则草率地硬塞在那份措辞严密的合同末尾。

items.def_en: to add an extra statement, postscript, or section immediately at the end of a text
items.ex_en: The author chose to subjoin a brief explanatory poem to his final chapter.
items.ex_zh: 作者选择在最后一章末尾附录一首简短的解说诗作为补充。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to append or attach an extra word, clause, or detail to the end of a text or remark
items.ex_en: The editor advised me not to tag on another sentence after the punchline.
items.ex_zh: 编辑建议我不要在妙语之后又赘加一句废话。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to attach or affix text, a clause, or notes as an addition to a document
items.ex_en: Counsel agreed to append several newly discovered emails to the official court affidavit.
items.ex_zh: 律师同意将几封新发现的电子邮件追加附于正式法庭宣誓书之后。

items.def_zh: 在……前添加（前缀、词冠等）；加前缀于
items.def_en: (+ to/with) To add a word, title, or letter at the beginning of another word or number.
items.ex_en: You must prefix each invoice code with the two-letter designation for your regional office.
items.ex_zh: 你必须在每个发票代码前加上代表你所在地区办事处的两个字母前缀。

items.def_en: (+ to) to attach a linguistic affix to a root, or physically attach an addition to a document
items.ex_en: Scholars often affix grammatical markers to ancient root words to denote past tense.
items.ex_zh: 学者们经常在古老词根上添加语法标记以表示过去时态。

items.def_en: (+ to) (linguistics) To attach a group of letters to the end of a word to form a new word or inflection.
items.ex_en: Linguists often suffix archaic case endings to substantive stems to trace syntactic evolution.
items.ex_zh: 语言学家常常在名词词干后加古体格位后缀，以探寻句法演化历程。

items.def_en: (+ to) (formal) To add a piece of writing, signature, or document to the end of an official text.
items.ex_en: The clerk will append the revised treaty text to the primary legislative docket.
items.ex_zh: 书记官将把修改后的条约文本附于主要立法卷宗的末尾。

groups.summary_en: A writer, speaker, or legal drafter attaches an element—such as a morpheme, note, codicil, or supplementary clause—to a root word, base document, or text. Verbs differentiate by exact structural positioning (prefixing to the front, suffixing/appending to the tail).
groups.summary_zh: 在词基或文本首尾增添词缀、注释或附件。
groups.desc_en: Denotes attaching or joining a linguistic or structural component to a core base, contrasting with generic physical attachment by focusing on morphological or textual composition.
groups.desc_zh: 指在核心词干或正文结构前后加缀构词或补充成分，区别于物理粘贴，聚焦形态学与文本层面的增补修饰。
groups.nuance_en: prefix: attach an element to the beginning of a word or stem (morpheme / title / name) · suffix: attach a formative element to the end of a word (ending / particle / word) · affix: linguistically fasten a bound morpheme to a base (morpheme / formative) · append: add a supplementary text or clause at the end of a document (appendix / clause / note) · tack on: casually or inappropriately attach an extra item (rider / amendment / fee)
groups.nuance_zh: prefix: 置于词首作前缀 (morpheme / title / name) · suffix: 置于词尾作后缀 (ending / particle / word) · affix: 附着词缀于词根 (morpheme / formative) · append: 文档末尾追加补充材料 (appendix / clause / note) · tack on: 随意或生硬附加上去 (rider / amendment / fee)

groups.name: Affix & Fasten Lightly or Temporarily · 连接与固定 (Affix, Tack, Pin)
groups.tip: 将两物接合固定在一起

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fasten or attach something to another object with a clip
items.ex_en: Please clip on your visitor badge before entering the restricted pharmaceutical manufacturing laboratory.
items.ex_zh: 在进入制药受限生产车间之前，请夹好您的访客证。
items.ex2_en: The microphone clips on easily to your collar without causing any fabric damage.
items.ex2_zh: 这个麦克风可以轻松夹在你的衣领上，不会损坏任何织物。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to attach or fasten a notice, picture, or cloth to a surface using pins
items.ex_en: The warden told the secretary to pin up the revised schedule immediately outside.
items.ex_zh: 管理员让秘书立刻把修改后的日程表用大头针钉在门外墙上。

items.def_zh: 用平头钉钉上；粗略固定
items.def_en: (+ sth) to fix or attach something lightly or temporarily with small nails or tacks
items.ex_en: He managed to tack on the torn canvas strip using two rusted nails.
items.ex_zh: 他用两枚生锈的钉子把那条扯破的帆布勉强钉了上去。

items.def_en: to fasten items together or onto a backing with a mechanical clamp or clip
items.ex_en: Remember to clip the loose vouchers to the invoice before submitting the envelope.
items.ex_zh: 在提交信封之前，记得用夹子把散落的凭证固定在发票上。

items.def_en: to fasten or attach one object to another using a thin pointed piece of metal
items.ex_en: She used a silver brooch to pin the fragile corsage onto her lapel.
items.ex_zh: 她用一枚银别针把那枚娇嫩的胸花别在自己的衣领上。

items.def_zh: 用平头钉（图钉）钉住；粗缝；额外附加上
items.def_en: 1. To fasten or attach something with small nails (tacks) or temporary stitches. 2. (tack on) To add something extra as an afterthought.
items.ex_en: The tailor used silk thread to tack the delicate lace along the hem.
items.ex_zh: 裁缝用丝线将精美的蕾丝花边粗缝固定在裙摆边缘。

items.def_en: to secure sheets of paper or materials together using small metal wire staples
items.ex_en: You should staple these signed medical consent forms to the main patient chart.
items.ex_zh: 你应该用订书钉把这些签署过的医疗知情同意书订在主病历上。

items.def_en: (formal) To stick, attach, or fasten one thing securely to another.
items.ex_en: Applicants must affix a recent passport photo firmly to the upper application corner.
items.ex_zh: 申请人必须将近期护照照片牢固地贴在申请表的右上角。

groups.summary_en: Handlers fasten, adhere, or anchor one item onto another surface, ranging from temporary, light pin-like attachment to formal physical bonding.
groups.summary_zh: 将一物附加、钉合或粘贴于另一物体表面，含轻度固定与胶黏。
groups.desc_en: Denotes fastening objects using light, removable, or puncturing hardware, distinguishing itself from heavy, permanent bonding (welding, gluing) by prioritizing reversibility and minimal damage.
groups.desc_zh: 指运用轻型、可拆卸或刺穿式五金配件固定物体，区别于焊接、胶合等强力永久结合，强调临时性与易拆卸。
groups.nuance_en: pin: fasten or pierce through with a sharp slender pin (badge / brooch / notice) · tack: fix lightly with small, flat-headed nails or loose stitches (carpet / poster / hem) · clip: hold together firmly using a spring or clasping pressure (paper / coupon / wire) · staple: bind together securely with a thin wire bent through the layers (document / papers / booklet) · affix: formally stick or fasten a label or stamp to a surface (stamp / seal / label)
groups.nuance_zh: pin: 用别针刺穿固定 (badge / brooch / notice) · tack: 用图钉或粗缝轻巧暂订 (carpet / poster / hem) · clip: 用夹子弹性夹紧 (paper / coupon / wire) · staple: 用订书针折弯装订 (document / papers / booklet) · affix: 正式张贴附上印章标签 (stamp / seal / label)

groups.name: Aim & Direct · 对准与瞄准 (Aim, Square, Sight)
groups.tip: 调整朝向位置使其归正

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ at/toward) To direct a finger, object, or weapon in a specific direction
items.ex_en: Never point that loaded hunting rifle directly at anyone, even during routine maintenance.
items.ex_zh: 即便在日常保养期间，也绝不要把那支上了膛的猎枪直接对准任何人。

items.def_zh: 平端对准，把（武器）平举指向
items.def_en: (+ at) To bring a weapon or finger horizontally in direct aim at someone
items.ex_en: The sentry level his carbine at the shadowy figure creeping across the perimeter.
items.ex_zh: 哨兵平端起卡宾枪，对准了那个潜行穿过防线周界的黑影。

items.def_zh: 对准，瞄准（枪炮、镜头、目光）
items.def_en: (+ on/at) To point or direct a weapon, camera, or light steadily at a target
items.ex_en: The nervous cameraman kept the spotlight trained on the podium throughout the speech.
items.ex_zh: 在整个演讲过程中，紧张的摄像师一直将聚光灯稳稳对准讲台。

items.def_zh: 调正，使对齐（成直角或平正）；使挺直（双肩）；使一致，与……相符；结清（账目）
items.def_en: 1. To adjust or align something so that it is level, straight, or at right angles. 2. To pull back and straighten one's shoulders. 3. To make things agree or fit together, or to be consistent with something. 4. To settle or clear a debt or bill.
items.ex_en: The drill sergeant ordered the recruit to square his slouching shoulders without delay.
items.ex_zh: 训练教官命令新兵立刻把耷拉着的双肩挺直端正。
items.ex2_en: His broad shoulders squared noticeably as he walked confidently onto the stage.
items.ex2_zh: 当他自信地走上舞台时，他宽阔的肩膀明显挺得笔直。

items.def_zh: 瞄准，对准；力求，旨在；针对
items.def_en: 1. To point a weapon, camera, or hit directly at someone or something. 2. (+ to do / at) To intend or strive to achieve a particular goal. 3. (+ at) To direct a remark, product, or action toward a specific audience.
items.ex_en: The archer drew her bowstring taut and aimed directly at the red bullseye.
items.ex_zh: 射手把弓弦拉得紧绷，直接瞄准了红色的靶心。

items.def_en: To aim a weapon or optical device using sights or visual cues
items.ex_en: The surveyor used the calibrated theodolite to sight along the distant boundary marker.
items.ex_zh: 测量员利用校准后的经纬仪，通过瞄准器对准远处的界标进行观测。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to direct a sight, weapon, or instrument precisely onto a specific target
items.ex_en: The radar operator managed to zero in on the unidentified aircraft within seconds.
items.ex_zh: 雷达操作员在数秒之内便成功锁定了那架不明飞行物。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to align a sight, barrel, or implement straight towards a target
items.ex_en: The sniper carefully lined up his rifle sight with the distant target.
items.ex_zh: 狙击手小心地将步枪瞄准镜对齐远处的靶标。
items.ex2_en: The laser sight lined up perfectly with the red mark on the wall.
items.ex2_zh: 激光瞄准器与墙上的红色标记完美对齐。

groups.summary_en: In this physical manipulation and spatial orientation frame, an agent points an implement, weapon, or body directly toward a target or makes perpendicular adjustments. While 'aim' is the dominant everyday verb for lining up sights or trajectory, specialized verbs denote mechanical or geometric squaring.
groups.summary_zh: 指将身体、工具、武器或视线精准指向特定目标或调整为垂直对正。
groups.desc_en: Denotes orienting a weapon, sensor, or optical line of sight along a precise vector toward an intended target, contrasting with generalized turning by requiring pinpoint directional calibration.
groups.desc_zh: 指将武器、镜头或视线沿特定矢量精准指向目标，区别于一般的转向，强调几何校准与弹道对准。
groups.nuance_en: aim: point a weapon or effort toward an intended target or objective (gun / camera / blow) · sight: inspect or take precise aim through an optical viewfinder or crosshair (target / rifle / land) · train: bring a heavy weapon or camera to bear continuously on a moving subject (artillery / lens / spotlight) · level: point a firearm horizontally and directly at a target (gun / rifle / pistol) · zero in on: adjust focus or aim with increasing precision onto a mark (target / location / issue)
groups.nuance_zh: aim: 操纵武器或精力指向标的 (gun / camera / blow) · sight: 透过准星目镜瞄准观测 (target / rifle / land) · train: 调动重火器或镜头持续对准 (artillery / lens / spotlight) · level: 举枪平端指对 (gun / rifle / pistol) · zero in on: 逐步收拢精度锁定目标 (target / location / issue)

groups.name: Alter Trajectory & Channel Away · 偏转与改道 (Deflect, Divert, Reroute)
groups.tip: 受阻反弹或主动改变方向

items.def_zh: 使改走新路线，为……重新规划路径
items.def_en: to send vehicles, flights, or data by a completely different route
items.ex_en: Flooding forced officials to reroute traffic away from the damaged highway.
items.ex_zh: 洪水迫使官员为受损公路周边的车辆重新规划行车路线。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to deflect or turn aside an approaching blow, danger, or unwanted intrusion
items.ex_en: She raised both arms to ward off the falling roof debris.
items.ex_zh: 她举起双臂挡开掉落的屋顶瓦砾。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to intercept and force someone or something to change direction
items.ex_en: Rangers rode ahead to head off the stampeding herd before the ravine.
items.ex_zh: 护林员策马赶到前方，在峡谷前拦截受惊狂奔的畜群使其改道。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to defend against or push away an approaching attacker or object
items.ex_en: The guard raised his baton to fend off the violent intruder.
items.ex_zh: 警卫举起警棍推开并抵挡凶猛的入侵者。

items.def_zh: 使改道，转移（车流、水流或注意力）
items.def_en: (+ from/to) to turn aside traffic, water, attention, or a course from its established path
items.ex_en: Engineers dug a wide canal to divert rising floodwaters into the lake.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们挖掘了一条宽阔的水渠，将暴涨的洪水引流到湖泊中。

items.def_zh: （使）偏斜，（使）偏转；转移（注意力、批评等）
items.def_en: 1. To change direction after hitting something, or cause something to do this. 2. To divert or redirect attention, criticism, or blame.
items.ex_en: The armored shield deflected the incoming projectile away from the personnel.
items.ex_zh: 装甲防护盾使射来的弹丸偏转方向，保护了人员安全。
items.ex2_en: The fast tennis ball deflected off the net and landed out of bounds.
items.ex2_zh: 快速飞行的网球碰到球网发生偏转，落在了界外。

items.def_zh: 使改道，使改变方向；转移（精力、资源等）；改寄（邮件）
items.def_en: 1. To send someone or something in a different direction or toward a new goal. 2. To arrange for mail or digital traffic to be sent to a new address.
items.ex_en: The post office will redirect all your letters to your new address.
items.ex_zh: 邮局会将你所有的信件改寄到你的新住址。

items.def_zh: 使转变方向，将……转移到支线或无关分支上
items.def_en: to divert someone or something from the main track, plan, or subject onto a tangent
items.ex_en: A sudden irrelevant phone call sidetracked the team from their core objective.
items.ex_zh: 一通突如其来且无关紧要的电话使团队偏离了核心目标。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this trajectory-altering frame express changing the heading, trajectory, or designated path of an approaching object, fluid, traffic, or resource. Deflect focuses on immediate angular ricochet upon collision or physical defense, divert emphasizes channeling a moving flow or attention off its original line, and redirect/reroute specify an administrative or deliberate systematic change of destination.
groups.summary_zh: 指改变运动中物体、流体或流向的既定路径，使其偏离原本航向或转向新终点。
groups.desc_en: Denotes changing the trajectory, flow, or attention of an approaching object, force, or resource away from its original path, contrasting with stopping it outright by preserving momentum in a new direction.
groups.desc_zh: 指使迎面而来的人事物、资源或力量偏离原有轨道，区别于直接使其停摆，强调维持动量并转嫁其流向。
groups.nuance_en: deflect: cause an oncoming projectile or blow to glance off obliquely (blow / bullet / criticism) · divert: intentionally re-channel a flow, attention, or resource toward an alternative course (traffic / funds / attention) · reroute: alter an established travel or network route (traffic / flight / pipeline) · sidetrack: push a discussion or train of thought away from its primary purpose (issue / conversation / debate) · head off: intercept someone or something early to prevent progress on that path (crisis / confrontation / group)
groups.nuance_zh: deflect: 弹开偏转迎面击打或指责 (blow / bullet / criticism) · divert: 将人流物料或注意力分流引开 (traffic / funds / attention) · reroute: 变更既定运输通信管线走向 (traffic / flight / pipeline) · sidetrack: 使议题或思路由主线跑偏 (issue / conversation / debate) · head off: 提前拦截阻断去路以化解危机 (crisis / confrontation / group)

groups.name: Ambush & Waylay by Manner · 伏击与阻截 (Waylay, Bushwhack, Ambush)
groups.tip: 埋伏在暗处出其不意发起袭击

items.def_en: to obstruct or seize someone or something moving from one place to another before they reach their destination
items.ex_en: Fighter jets were scrambled to intercept the unidentified aircraft over the border.
items.ex_zh: 战斗机紧急升空，在边界上空拦截不明飞行器。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to conceal oneself in ambush to launch a surprise attack on an unsuspecting target
items.ex_en: Bandits lay in wait for the merchant convoy in the narrow pass.
items.ex_zh: 强盗们在狭窄的山口处设伏，等待商队经过。

items.def_en: to lure or trick someone into a dangerous trap or compromising situation
items.ex_en: Undercover agents conspired to entrap the corrupt official during the exchange.
items.ex_zh: 卧底探员合力设计，在交易时诱使该贪官落入圈套。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to attack someone suddenly by leaping out or taking them entirely by surprise
items.ex_en: Two masked men jumped on him from the dark alley behind.
items.ex_zh: 两名蒙面男子从身后黑暗的巷子里猛扑出来袭击了他。

items.def_en: to make a surprise attack on someone from a concealed position
items.ex_en: Rebel fighters planned to ambush the military convoy along the mountain road.
items.ex_zh: 叛军计划在山路上埋伏突袭军方车队。

items.def_zh: 埋伏袭击，拦截（waylay 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of waylay; to have waited in hiding to attack, intercept, or accost someone.
items.ex_en: The weary messenger was waylaid by highwaymen in the depths of night.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的信使在深夜遭到拦路强盗的伏击。

items.def_zh: 伏击，突袭；在丛林中开路
items.def_en: (especially North American) 1. To attack or ambush someone from a hidden place. 2. To cut one's way through thick woods or bush.
items.ex_en: Guerrillas managed to bushwhack the patrol unit deep in the dense forest.
items.ex_zh: 游击队在茂密的森林深处成功伏击了巡逻小队。

items.def_zh: 伏击，埋伏袭击；半路拦截（以便交谈或抢劫）
items.def_en: To stop, intercept, or attack someone unexpectedly from a hidden place.
items.ex_en: The robber intended to waylay solitary travelers on the desolate road.
items.ex_zh: 强盗打算在这条荒凉的道路上半路拦截独行的旅客。

groups.summary_en: Attackers lie in concealed waiting to surprise, intercept, or violently strike an unsuspecting traveler or military force.
groups.summary_zh: 潜伏在暗处出其不意地截击、袭击或拦截毫无防备的行者与敌军。
groups.desc_en: Denotes surprising, intercepting, or detaining a target from concealment along a transit route, contrasting with open assault by relying on concealment, surprise, and suddenness.
groups.desc_zh: 指隐蔽在行进路线两侧设伏，对目标实施突袭或阻截，区别于公开交火，强调伪装匿迹与出其不意。
groups.nuance_en: ambush: launch a surprise tactical assault from concealed cover (patrol / convoy / enemy) · waylay: wait in hiding to intercept, detain, or rob someone en route (traveler / messenger / minister) · bushwhack: ambush stealthily from dense wild bush, often lawlessly (guerrillas / troops / travelers) · intercept: cut across the path to seize or prevent passage of an entity (missile / communication / courier) · lie in wait for: remain concealed patiently while awaiting the arrival of prey or foe (victim / target / prey)
groups.nuance_zh: ambush: 隐蔽隐蔽处实施战术伏击 (patrol / convoy / enemy) · waylay: 半路伏击拦路打劫或强留纠缠 (traveler / messenger / minister) · bushwhack: 丛林中设伏放冷枪 (guerrillas / troops / travelers) · intercept: 途中横向穿插截击 (missile / communication / courier) · lie in wait for: 屏息潜伏静候猎物 (victim / target / prey)

groups.name: Amorphous Amassing · 堆积与积聚 (Heap, Mound, Bank)
groups.tip: 集中堆放成堆或丘

items.def_en: to pile snow, earth, or coal into a high ridge or protective sloping mass
items.ex_en: Snowplows banked huge piles of snow along the sides of the street.
items.ex_zh: 扫雪车把大堆大堆的积雪堆积在街道两侧成堤。
items.ex2_en: Dry snow banked high against the roadside during the fierce blizzard.
items.ex2_zh: 在猛烈的暴风雪中，干雪在路旁堆积成了高高的雪堆。

items.def_en: to draw earth or loose material up around plants into an elevated mound
items.ex_en: The gardener hilled rich soil around the base of the tomato plants.
items.ex_zh: 园丁将肥沃的土壤培在番茄植株的根部堆成土墩。

items.def_en: to collect or accumulate loose items into an amorphous mass
items.ex_en: Fallen autumn leaves pile up against the wooden garden fence each morning.
items.ex_zh: 每天清晨，飘落的秋叶都会在花园木栅栏边堆积起来。
items.ex2_en: Volunteers pile up dry timber in the center of the village square.
items.ex2_zh: 志愿者们将干木材堆在村庄广场中央。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to put things into a large, messy, or rounded mound
items.ex_en: Workers heaped up broken bricks beside the half-demolished brick wall.
items.ex_zh: 工人们把碎砖头在那面被拆了一半的砖墙旁堆成大堆。
items.ex2_en: Dry fallen leaves heap up in the corners of the courtyard every autumn.
items.ex2_zh: 每年秋天，干燥的落叶都会在院子的角落里堆积起来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to arrange objects or allow items to accumulate in tall piles
items.ex_en: Unanswered invoices began to stack up on her office desk this week.
items.ex_zh: 本周未处理的发票开始在她办公室的桌上高高堆叠起来。
items.ex2_en: Warehouse clerks stack up heavy cardboard boxes near the loading dock every morning.
items.ex2_zh: 仓库管理员每天早晨在装货码头附近把沉重的纸箱叠放起来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to form loose earth, snow, or clouds into a steep ridge or mound
items.ex_en: Dark storm clouds were banking up on the horizon.
items.ex_zh: 地平线上暴风雨前的乌云正在层层堆积。
items.ex2_en: Strong coastal winds bank up huge drifts of sand against the seawall.
items.ex2_zh: 强劲的海风将大堆的沙子堆积在海堤前。

items.def_zh: 堆积，堆放；大量给予（赞扬、批评等）；装满
items.def_en: 1. To arrange things in a large, untidy pile. 2. (+ on/upon) To give someone a great deal of praise, criticism, etc. 3. (+ with) To fill something with a large amount of things.
items.ex_en: He heaped dried firewood beside the stone fireplace for the cold night.
items.ex_zh: 他在石制壁炉旁堆了许多干柴，以备度过寒冷的夜晚。

items.def_zh: 堆成土堆（或土墩），堆积；筑堤防卫
items.def_en: (often mound up) To pile earth, snow, or other material into a rounded heap or bank.
items.ex_en: They mounded fresh earth around the newly planted fruit saplings.
items.ex_zh: 他们在新栽的果树幼苗周围堆起了一圈新土。

groups.summary_en: An agent gathers or piles loose material into a rounded, voluminous, or sprawling mass without strict alignment. The verbs differ primarily in register, typical substances (earth, snow, dishes), and the contour of the resulting mass.
groups.summary_zh: 将松散物质大体堆聚成隆起的团块或土丘状，不强调整齐度。
groups.desc_en: Denotes gathering materials into an irregular, loose, or rounded elevated accumulation, contrasting with orderly stacking by yielding an unstratified, amorphous bulk.
groups.desc_zh: 指将松散物料聚拢堆叠成不规则、隆起的团块，区别于规整层叠的码放，呈现无固定边界的粗放堆垒。
groups.nuance_en: heap: pile things up loosely, carelessly, or abundantly (rubbish / blankets / praise) · mound: build or pack up earth or matter into a rounded hillock (earth / snow / rice) · bank: form a protective, elevated sloped ridge of snow, earth, or cloud (snow / embers / earth) · pile up: continuously collect or amass to form an increasing mass (debris / work / debt) · stack up: arrange items in an orderly vertical column (boxes / plates / firewood)
groups.nuance_zh: heap: 杂乱或大量堆聚 (rubbish / blankets / praise) · mound: 堆筑成圆顶小丘 (earth / snow / rice) · bank: 聚起倾斜的长堤或雪堆 (snow / embers / earth) · pile up: 不断堆积累加 (debris / work / debt) · stack up: 整齐层层叠码 (boxes / plates / firewood)

groups.name: Anticipatory Projection & Mind's-Eye Imaging · 预见瞻望与意象具化 (Envision, Foresee)
groups.tip: 在脑海中描摹未来图景

items.def_en: to think about and plan for future events or prospective conditions
items.ex_en: A visionary leader must look ahead and anticipate upcoming market shifts.
items.ex_zh: 有远见的领导者必须展望未来，预判即将到来的市场变革。

items.def_en: to imagine or expect beforehand that an event will happen and mentally prepare for it
items.ex_en: We anticipate a surge in customer inquiries after the product launch today.
items.ex_zh: 我们预料今天产品发布后客户咨询量将会激增。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to create a vivid mental picture or idea of something in one's mind
items.ex_en: The old photograph conjured up vivid memories of his childhood seaside town.
items.ex_zh: 那张老照片在他脑海中唤起了关于童年海滨小镇的鲜活记忆。

items.def_en: to predict or calculate future developments based on analysis or projective modeling
items.ex_en: Meteorologists forecast severe thunderstorms across the northern valleys by this evening.
items.ex_zh: 气象学家预测今晚北部山谷地区将出现强雷雨。

items.def_en: to imagine or form a mental picture of something that might happen or exist in the future
items.ex_en: The architect envisions a sustainable community powered entirely by solar energy.
items.ex_zh: 这位建筑师设想建设一个完全由太阳能供电的可持续社区。

items.def_en: To know, realize, or predict beforehand that something will happen.
items.ex_en: No one could foresee the economic disruption caused by the sudden conflict.
items.ex_zh: 没有人能够预见这场突发冲突所引发的经济混乱。

items.def_zh: 想象，设想（在脑海中勾勒画面）；使形象化，使显现
items.def_en: 1. (British English spelling of visualize) To form a mental image or picture of something. 2. To make something visible.
items.ex_en: He closed his eyes to visualise every stage of the surgical procedure.
items.ex_zh: 他闭上双眼，在脑海中勾勒出手术步骤的每一个阶段。

items.def_en: to have a presentiment of or act as a foreshadowing warning of an impending future event
items.ex_en: Those ominous storm clouds presage a bitter winter over the mountain pass.
items.ex_zh: 那些不祥的暴风阴云预示着山口将迎来一个严酷的冬天。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe deliberately projecting oneself into future scenarios or mentally modeling prospective states of affairs, picturing upcoming events or possibilities with concrete clarity.
groups.summary_zh: 在脑海中对未来情境或可能性进行推演构想、心象具象化及预先察觉。
groups.desc_en: Denotes projecting prospective scenarios or mentally generating visual representations before they materialize, contrasting with abstract deduction through vivid imagination and intuitive foresight.
groups.desc_zh: 指在事态成真之前构想未来情景或在脑海中生成直观表象，区别于抽象逻辑推演，依赖具象想象与直觉预见。
groups.nuance_en: envision: imagine or form a mental picture of future possibilities (future / society / success) · foresee: know or realize beforehand through prescience or situational trends (problems / danger / consequences) · visualize: form a concrete visual image of something in the mind's eye (results / scene / success) · anticipate: foresee and act early in preparation for an eventuality (needs / move / backlash) · conjure up: evoke a vivid mental image or memory out of nothing (image / memory / impression)
groups.nuance_zh: envision: 展望勾勒未来蓝图 (future / society / success) · foresee: 基于趋势预见到后果危局 (problems / danger / consequences) · visualize: 脑海具象化成像呈现 (results / scene / success) · anticipate: 预判并提前有所准备 (needs / move / backlash) · conjure up: 凭空唤起逼真意象或记忆 (image / memory / impression)

groups.name: Appreciate & Value · 赏识与珍视 (Appreciate, Value, Prize)
groups.tip: 认可价值并给予真诚赏识与感激

items.def_en: to consider someone or something to be important, useful, or of great worth
items.ex_en: The firm genuinely values team members who demonstrate integrity and initiative.
items.ex_zh: 该企业由衷看重表现出诚实与主动性的团队成员。

items.def_zh: 赞赏，欣赏，珍视；感激；理解，体谅；增值
items.def_en: 1. To recognize the good qualities or value of someone or something. 2. To be grateful for something. 3. To fully understand or realize a situation. 4. To increase in value over time.
items.ex_en: We sincerely appreciate your prompt assistance during this difficult administrative transition.
items.ex_zh: 我们由衷感激您在这次艰难的行政过渡期给予的及时协助。
items.ex2_en: Residential property values will appreciate steadily in this desirable suburban neighborhood.
items.ex2_zh: 在这个理想的郊区社区，住宅地产的价值将稳步升值。

items.def_zh: 珍视，高度重视；撬动，撬开
items.def_en: 1. To value or esteem someone or something highly. 2. (usually UK) To force open or move something using leverage (pry).
items.ex_en: Scholars prize ancient manuscripts for their exceptional historical and linguistic value.
items.ex_zh: 学者们极为珍视古手稿，因其具有非凡的历史与语言价值。

items.def_en: to hold someone or something dear and treat them with great care and devotion
items.ex_en: She treasures the golden locket that belonged to her beloved grandmother.
items.ex_zh: 她珍藏着那枚曾经属于她挚爱祖母的黄金小盒坠子。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to consider something to be very important, valuable, or significant
items.ex_en: The conservative board sets great store by traditional business etiquette and protocol.
items.ex_zh: 保守的董事会非常看重传统的商业礼仪与规程。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to admire, respect, and hold someone in high esteem
items.ex_en: Young athletes around the world look up to her as an inspirational leader.
items.ex_zh: 全世界的年轻运动员都视她为鼓舞人心的榜样并敬佩她。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to have a very favourable opinion of someone or something
items.ex_en: Senior executives think highly of her innovative approach to crisis management.
items.ex_zh: 高级管理层对她在危机处理中的创新方法评价极高。

items.def_en: to keep an idea, hope, or love deeply and tenderly in one's heart over time
items.ex_en: He still cherishes the quiet hope that peace will soon prevail.
items.ex_zh: 他心中依然珍藏着和平很快就会到来的宁静希望。

groups.summary_en: Experiencers recognize the worth, qualities, or usefulness of an object, person, or relationship, varying from cognitive gratitude and evaluation ('appreciate', 'value') to treating something as an irreplaceable treasure ('prize', 'treasure', 'cherish').
groups.summary_zh: 感知并认可某人某物的价值与品质，从知晓感激延伸至格外看重与深情呵护珍视。
groups.desc_en: Denotes holding an entity in high cognitive, emotional, or monetary esteem, contrasting with simple liking by recognizing its intrinsic worth, rarity, or irreplacibility.
groups.desc_zh: 指在认知、情感或价值上给予高度重视，区别于泛泛的喜欢，强调对其内在价值、稀缺性或不可替代性的深切认同。
groups.nuance_en: value: attach significant worth, utility, or importance to something (opinion / friendship / time) · appreciate: fully recognize and grasp the worth, subtlety, or gratitude due to something (art / support / nuance) · prize: rate exceptionally high for its rarity, virtue, or excellence (freedom / possession / specimen) · treasure: guard and hold dear with profound emotional reverence (memories / keepsake / heirloom) · cherish: nurture, hold lovingly in mind, and protect with warmth (hope / dream / family)
groups.nuance_zh: value: 评估并重视实用或内在价值 (opinion / friendship / time) · appreciate: 领会鉴赏美感或心怀感激 (art / support / nuance) · prize: 因珍稀卓越而视若珍宝 (freedom / possession / specimen) · treasure: 奉若至宝般悉心珍藏 (memories / keepsake / heirloom) · cherish: 怀揣珍视并爱护 (hope / dream / family)

groups.name: Approach & Near · 接近与靠近 (Approach, Near, Close in)
groups.tip: 缩短空间距离

items.def_en: to come or go near to someone or something in distance or time
items.ex_en: Shadows lengthened across the quiet valley as twilight neared the village.
items.ex_zh: 随着暮色临近村庄，阴影在宁静的山谷中逐渐拉长。
items.ex2_en: The weary travelers smiled as their destination neared with every passing hour.
items.ex2_zh: 疲惫的旅行者微笑着，因为目的地随着时间的流逝越来越近了。

items.def_zh: 靠近，接近；着手处理；找…商量
items.def_en: 1. to come near or nearer to someone or something in distance, time, or quality. 2. to deal with a situation or problem. 3. to speak to someone about a matter or request
items.ex_en: A heavy passenger train approached the dimly lit platform at midnight.
items.ex_zh: 一列沉重的客运列车在午夜驶近了灯光昏暗的站台。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move forward towards someone or something in a purposeful manner
items.ex_en: The infantry units advanced cautiously toward the enemy trench under artillery cover.
items.ex_zh: 步兵分队在火炮掩护下小心翼翼地向敌方战壕推进。
items.ex2_en: The experienced chess player advanced his knight into an aggressive attacking position.
items.ex2_zh: 这位经验丰富的棋手将他的骑士推进到具有攻击性的位置。

items.def_en: (+ on/around) to move steadily closer to surround or corner a target
items.ex_en: Police squads began to close in on the fugitive’s abandoned hideout.
items.ex_zh: 警方小组开始向逃犯废弃的藏匿据点步步逼近合围。

items.def_en: to approach or come closer in space or time (formal or literary)
items.ex_en: The travelers rested as the darkness drew near across the silent woods.
items.ex_zh: 随着夜幕在寂静的林间移近，旅人们停下脚步歇息。

items.def_zh: 快速逼近，气势汹汹地逼近
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to approach someone or something rapidly, threateningly, or with great momentum
items.ex_en: The hurricane was bearing down on the coastal towns at terrifying speed.
items.ex_zh: 飓风以可怕的速度向沿海城镇逼近。

items.def_zh: 悄悄靠近，不知不觉临近
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to move slowly, stealthily, or imperceptibly closer to someone or something
items.ex_en: Tiredness seemed to creep up on her as soon as the sun went down.
items.ex_zh: 太阳一下山，疲惫感仿佛就不知不觉袭上了她的心头。

items.def_zh: 汇聚靠近，从不同方向聚集接近
items.def_en: (+ on) to move toward the same point from different directions
items.ex_en: Thousands of passionate fans converged on the national stadium for the final.
items.ex_zh: 成千上万热情的球迷从四面八方向国家体育场汇聚赶来观看决赛。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate physical or temporal movement toward an entity or threshold, decreasing the distance separating them.
groups.summary_zh: 指在空间位置或时间跨度上朝着目标靠拢，持续缩短彼此距离。
groups.desc_en: Denotes shortening spatial or temporal distance toward a target or threshold, contrasting with generalized transit by centering on the reduction of the remaining gap.
groups.desc_zh: 指缩短与目标或临界点之间的空间或时间间距，区别于普通行进，核心聚焦于剩余间隙的递减与迫近。
groups.nuance_en: approach: move physically or temporally closer toward a destination or state (city / deadline / threshold) · near: draw proximate in distance or time as a continuous process (shore / completion / end) · close in: advance menacingly or decisively to surround and capture (police / enemy / darkness) · bear down on: approach rapidly and intimidatingly from a position of momentum or weight (storm / vessel / defender) · creep up on: approach stealthily and gradually without being noticed (victim / behind / age)
groups.nuance_zh: approach: 向目标或阶段性界限靠拢 (city / deadline / threshold) · near: 逐步临近或步入尾声 (shore / completion / end) · close in: 步步逼近形成合围之势 (police / enemy / darkness) · bear down on: 带着压迫感疾速逼近 (storm / vessel / defender) · creep up on: 悄无声息地逐步贴近 (victim / behind / age)

groups.name: Arduously Journey on Foot · 跋涉与重步慢行 (Trek, Tramp)
groups.tip: 艰难费力或长途行进跋涉

items.def_zh: （赶着狗拉雪橇）在雪地上跋涉，赶狗拉雪橇；捣碎，捣烂
items.def_en: 1. To travel over snow with a dogsled, directing the dogs with voice commands. 2. To crush or mash food into a thick, soft mass.
items.ex_en: The seasoned driver mushed his team across the frozen Alaskan tundra.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的驭手赶着他的雪橇犬队跋涉穿过阿拉斯加冰冻的苔原。

items.def_zh: 长途徒步穿过；重步行经
items.def_en: (+ sth) to walk heavily and firmly across a wide area or difficult land
items.ex_en: Hikers tramp across the muddy moors despite the persistent autumn drizzle.
items.ex_zh: 尽管秋雨淅淅沥沥，徒步者们仍重步行经泥泞的荒原。

items.def_zh: 步履沉重地前行；缓慢跋涉
items.def_en: to walk slowly with heavy steps, especially because of tiredness or difficult ground
items.ex_en: Weary miners trudged along the dirt track after a grueling night shift.
items.ex_zh: 经过艰苦的夜班后，疲惫的矿工们步履沉重地走在泥土小路上。

items.def_en: (+ across/through) to undertake a long, strenuous journey on foot
items.ex_en: The expedition planned to trek across the scorching dunes for three weeks.
items.ex_zh: 探险队计划在灼热的沙丘上长途跋涉三周时间。

items.def_zh: （长途或艰难地）跋涉，重步行走；踩，践踏
items.def_en: 1. (+ through/across) To walk with heavy, steady steps over a long distance or across rough ground. 2. To step heavily on something; trample.
items.ex_en: The weary soldiers had to tramp across muddy terrain for hours.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的士兵们不得不踩着重步在泥泞的地带中跋涉数小时。

items.def_zh: 步履沉重地走；吃力前行
items.def_en: (+ through/along) to walk slowly with heavy steps because you are exhausted or carrying a burden
items.ex_en: Exhausted porters trudged through the deep winter drifts carrying heavy supplies.
items.ex_zh: 筋疲力竭的搬运工背负着沉重的补给品，在冬日的深雪堆中吃力前行。

items.def_zh: 艰难跋涉通过；费力地走过
items.def_en: (+ sth) to walk slowly and with great effort through mud, snow, or harsh terrain
items.ex_en: Rescuers had to slog through thick swamp mud to locate the wreckage.
items.ex_zh: 救援人员不得不艰难跋涉穿过厚重的沼泽泥淖以寻找残骸。

items.def_zh: 艰难跋涉；深一脚浅一脚地走
items.def_en: (+ through/along) to walk with heavy, slow steps, especially through mud or harsh terrain
items.ex_en: We had to slog through ankle-deep marshland to reach the shoreline camp.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不深一脚浅一脚地跋涉过齐踝深的湿地，才到达湖畔营地。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures demanding, exhausting, or heavily paced overland travel on foot across rugged distances or harsh conditions. 'Tramp' emphasizes heavy, determined footsteps over long stretches, while 'mush' specifically denotes driving or traveling arduously with a dogsled across snow.
groups.summary_zh: 指在恶劣地形或长途路途中迈着沉重步伐、艰辛用力的徒步前行。
groups.desc_en: Denotes walking laboriously over difficult terrain or long distances, contrasting with light stepping by capturing the heavy, exhausting physical toll on feet and legs.
groups.desc_zh: 指在恶劣地形或长途行进中迈出沉重疲惫的步伐，区别于轻快行走，强调脚步的沉重滞碍与体能消耗。
groups.nuance_en: trudge: walk slowly with heavy, weary, dragged steps through mud or snow (snow / mud / path) · trek: undertake an arduous, protracted journey on foot across wilderness (mountains / desert / wilderness) · slog: toil through thick, sticky, or resistant ground with dogged persistence (mud / swamp / terrain) · tramp: walk heavily and steadily over long distances across the countryside (roads / hills / woods) · mush: drive a dog sled through snow, or push heavily through harsh tundra (snow / dogs / tundra)
groups.nuance_zh: trudge: 踏着泥雪拖着沉重疲惫步履前行 (snow / mud / path) · trek: 翻山越岭式长途跋涉 (mountains / desert / wilderness) · slog: 在泥泞阻力中硬着头皮艰难深涉 (mud / swamp / terrain) · tramp: 迈着稳重重步在旷野远行 (roads / hills / woods) · mush: 赶雪橇或在极地雪地重步推进 (snow / dogs / tundra)

groups.name: Ascend & Elevate · 上升与抬升 (Rise, Ascend, Elevate)
groups.tip: 由低向高的运动

items.def_en: (informal) To raise or increase the amount, price, or level of something.
items.ex_en: The local utility company decided to up energy prices again this winter.
items.ex_zh: 当地公用事业公司决定今年冬天再次提高能源价格。

items.def_en: to lift or move something to a higher position, level, or rank
items.ex_en: The dock crane will raise the shipping container onto the waiting vessel.
items.ex_zh: 码头起重机将把集装箱吊起装上等待的货船。

items.def_zh: 上升，升起；上涨，增加；站立，起立
items.def_en: 1. To move upwards or ascend. 2. To increase in amount, level, or value. 3. To stand up from a sitting or lying position.
items.ex_en: Black plumes of smoke began to rise above the distant horizon.
items.ex_zh: 黑色的滚滚浓烟开始在遥远的地平线上升起。

items.def_en: to raise someone or something to a higher position or level using physical effort
items.ex_en: The movers carefully lifted the heavy piano onto the transport truck.
items.ex_zh: 搬运工人小心翼翼地把沉重的钢琴抬上了运输卡车。
items.ex2_en: Heavy morning fog began to lift slowly as the warm sun emerged.
items.ex2_zh: 随着温暖的太阳升起，晨间浓雾开始慢慢散去。

items.def_en: to move vertically upwards from a lower to a higher position
items.ex_en: Bright hot air balloons go up quietly into the clear morning sky.
items.ex_zh: 鲜艳的热气球静静地升入清澈的清晨天空。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to elevate or raise something to a higher physical level
items.ex_en: Her encouraging message really lifted him up when he was feeling down.
items.ex_zh: 在他情绪低落时，她鼓励的话语确实让他振作了起来。

items.def_en: to raise someone or something to a higher physical, moral, or official position
items.ex_en: The hydraulic platform will elevate the technicians to the high ceiling lights.
items.ex_zh: 液压升降台将把技术人员抬升到高处的天花板灯具旁。

items.def_en: to move upward or travel towards the top of something; formal equivalent of rise
items.ex_en: The mountaineers prepared to ascend the steep icy summit at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 登山者们准备在拂晓时分攀登陡峭险峻的冰峰。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate vertical movement from a lower location or status to a higher one, either intransitively (ascending) or transitively (raising/lifting).
groups.summary_zh: 自下而上地垂直移动、升起，或施力将某物抬高。
groups.desc_en: Denotes upward motion through space, altitude, or numerical measurement, contrasting with horizontal movement by aligning along the vertical gravity axis.
groups.desc_zh: 指沿垂直重力轴在空间高度或数值量度上由低向高的运动，区别于水平位移，核心在于垂直方位的攀升。
groups.nuance_en: rise: move upward autonomously or naturally without external hoisting (sun / smoke / prices) · ascend: formal or graceful climbing to a summit, throne, or higher air (stairs / throne / mountain) · lift: exert physical force to pick something up off a surface (fog / weight / lid) · raise: actively cause something to become higher or more upright (hand / flag / salary) · elevate: formally hoist or dignify both physically and systematically (feet / tone / position)
groups.nuance_zh: rise: 自主自然升腾或上升 (sun / smoke / prices) · ascend: 正式登上高台、宝座或攀向高处 (stairs / throne / mountain) · lift: 施力提起离开基座 (fog / weight / lid) · raise: 主动抬高使其耸立或调高 (hand / flag / salary) · elevate: 机械性举升或结构化提拔 (feet / tone / position)

groups.name: Ascend by Hand & Foot · 攀登与攀爬 (Scale, Clamber, Shin)
groups.tip: 手脚并用向上攀登

items.def_en: (+ sth) to move or climb up steep, rugged terrain hurriedly using both hands and feet
items.ex_en: The lost hikers had to scramble up the steep and rocky ravine.
items.ex_zh: 迷路的徒步旅行者不得不手脚并用爬上陡峭多石的峡谷。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to climb quickly up a pole, tree, or vertical structure using one's arms and legs
items.ex_en: The agile boy could shin up the wooden flagpole in seconds.
items.ex_zh: 那个身手敏捷的男孩几秒钟之内就能顺着木旗杆爬上去。

items.def_zh: 攀登，登上；骑上；增加；发起，组织；安装，固定
items.def_en: 1. To climb up, ascend, or get onto a horse, bicycle, or platform; 2. to increase gradually in amount or intensity; 3. to organize or initiate an activity; to fix firmly in place.
items.ex_en: The cavalry officer swiftly mounted his horse and drew his gleaming sword.
items.ex_zh: 骑兵军官迅速骑上他的马，拔出了闪亮的佩剑。

items.def_en: 1. (often shin up/down) To climb quickly up or down a pole, tree, or rope using one's arms and legs.
items.ex_en: The mischievous boy loved to shin up the courtyard trees after school.
items.ex_zh: 这个调皮的男孩放学后喜欢手脚并用顺着院子里的树往上爬。

items.def_en: (+ up/over) to climb quickly but awkwardly with hands and feet over rough ground
items.ex_en: The children had to scramble up the rugged rocky bank together.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们只得一起手脚并用吃力地爬上崎岖多石的河岸。

items.def_en: 1. To climb mountains as a sport or expedition.
items.ex_en: Experienced athletes often mountaineer in the Swiss Alps during summer seasons.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的运动员常常在夏季前往瑞士阿尔卑斯山进行登山运动。

items.def_en: (+ up/onto) to climb with difficulty and effort, typically using both hands and feet
items.ex_en: The exhausted hikers had to clamber onto the slippery ledge to escape the rising tide.
items.ex_zh: 筋疲力尽的徒步者不得不手脚并用爬上湿滑的岩架，以躲避上涨的潮水。

items.def_en: to climb up or over a very steep or high surface such as a wall or cliff
items.ex_en: Without safety ropes, the daring climber managed to scale the sheer granite cliff within hours.
items.ex_zh: 在没有安全绳的情况下，那位大胆的攀登者在数小时内成功攀上了陡峭的花岗岩悬崖。

groups.summary_en: Verbs specifying the physical manner of moving upward across steep, vertical, or rugged obstacles using hands, feet, specialized gear, or bodily grip.
groups.summary_zh: 强调手脚并用、攀援贴附或借助器械沿陡峭表面向上攀爬的动作方式。
groups.desc_en: Denotes ascending steep or vertical surfaces by actively engaging both hands and feet, contrasting with casual walking by necessitating whole-body grip, balance, and traction.
groups.desc_zh: 指四肢并用在陡峭或垂直立面上向上攀登，区别于平地踏步，需要手抓脚踩维持附着力与身体平衡。
groups.nuance_en: scale: successfully climb up and over a very steep, sheer barrier or precipice (wall / cliff / height) · clamber: climb clumsily or with effort using both hands and feet over rough obstacles (rocks / bank / ledge) · scramble: move hurriedly and awkwardly over steep rough terrain on hands and knees (slope / ridge / rocks) · shin: climb up or down a smooth vertical pole or thin trunk gripping with shins and arms (tree / pole / mast) · mount: set foot upon and climb stairs, a steed, or an elevated platform (horse / platform / stage)
groups.nuance_zh: scale: 翻越攀爬绝壁或险隘高墙 (wall / cliff / height) · clamber: 四肢并用费力笨拙攀上 (rocks / bank / ledge) · scramble: 手脚并用手爬脚蹬越过碎石陡坡 (slope / ridge / rocks) · shin: 抱紧树干或细杆蹭着爬 (tree / pole / mast) · mount: 踏上登梯、跨上马背或站上平台 (horse / platform / stage)

groups.name: Ask & Inquire · 询问与打听 (Seeking Information or Answers)
groups.tip: 开口打听消息或提出疑问

items.def_zh: 询问，打听；请求，要求；邀请
items.def_en: 1. To put a question to someone in order to get information or an answer. 2. To request something or make a request of someone. 3. To invite someone somewhere.
items.ex_en: You should ask the front desk clerk for directions before heading into the historic district.
items.ex_zh: 在前往历史街区之前，你应该向前台文员询问路线。

items.def_en: (+ on/about) to ask someone a series of formal or probing questions to obtain detailed answers
items.ex_en: Detectives spent hours questioning the primary suspect about his precise whereabouts on Friday night.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们花了数小时盘问这名主要嫌疑人周五晚上的确切行踪。

items.def_en: to ask several people in order to get information, advice, or help
items.ex_en: I will ask around the neighborhood to see if anyone found a stray black cat.
items.ex_zh: 我会在社区附近四处打听，看看是否有人捡到了一只走失的黑猫。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to seek official or systematic information about a matter
items.ex_en: An independent judicial commission was appointed to inquire into the allegations of systemic police corruption.
items.ex_zh: 一个独立的司法委员会受命深入调查有关警察系统性腐败的指控。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to ask questions or examine facts to make sure someone or something is correct or safe
items.ex_en: My supervisor dropped by unexpectedly to check up on our progress.
items.ex_zh: 主管出乎意料地过来查看我们的项目进度。

items.def_en: (+ whether/if) to ask a question, especially to clarify or express doubt about a fact
items.ex_en: Several board members queried whether the projected revenue figures were based on realistic assumptions.
items.ex_zh: 几位董事会成员发问质疑预计的收入数据是否基于切合实际的假设。

items.def_en: to ask someone for information; to investigate or look into something
items.ex_en: The journalist visited the town hall to inquire about the newly proposed environmental zoning regulations.
items.ex_zh: 记者前往市政厅，打听新提议的环境分区规章。

items.def_en: to ask a suspect or prisoner systematic, rigorous questions closely and aggressively
items.ex_en: Intelligence officers continued to interrogate the captured operative in a secure, undisclosed military facility.
items.ex_zh: 情报官员在一个保密的未公开军事设施内继续审讯被俘特工。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this communicative frame denote an agent posing questions to an interlocutor to obtain facts, clarification, or guidance, differing primarily by formal versus conversational register.
groups.summary_zh: 为获取信息、答复或指导而向对方提出疑问或进行询问打听。
groups.desc_en: Denotes seeking information, answers, or clarification from interlocutors, contrasting with declaration by positioning the speaker as an information recipient probing for knowledge.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动向对话方索取信息、解答或澄清疑点，区别于陈述宣告，言者处于信息接收端并发起探测探询。
groups.nuance_en: ask: put a straightforward question or request to someone (question / permission / price) · inquire: formally solicit information or investigate circumstances (condition / health / details) · question: probe beliefs, actions, or veracity with skepticism (motives / suspect / decision) · query: raise an explicit doubt, formal objection, or computational lookup (database / bill / validity) · interrogate: systematically and aggressively cross-examine someone under formal authority (prisoner / witness / suspect)
groups.nuance_zh: ask: 最日常直接的提问发问 (question / permission / price) · inquire: 正式探问详情或查问 (condition / health / details) · question: 抱持怀疑质问或查考 (motives / suspect / decision) · query: 提出明确质疑或数据库查询 (database / bill / validity) · interrogate: 官方机构严厉连续审讯 (prisoner / witness / suspect)

groups.name: Assert Political Hegemony · 殖民与支配 (Dominate, Colonize)
groups.tip: 对群体施加绝对权力支配

items.def_zh: 统治，支配，控制；占主导地位
items.def_en: 1. To have control, power, or authority over someone or something. 2. To be the most prominent or important feature of something.
items.ex_en: A handful of multinational corporations completely dominate the domestic telecommunications industry in this region.
items.ex_zh: 少数跨国公司完全支配了该地区的国内电信行业。

items.def_en: to reduce a country or people to the status of a dependent satellite or client
items.ex_en: The expansionist empire sought to vassalize its smaller neighboring states through economic coercion and threats.
items.ex_zh: 这个扩张主义帝国企图通过经济胁迫和威胁使周边较小的邻国沦为附庸。

items.def_en: to subject another region, polity, or market to imperial or geopolitical hegemony
items.ex_en: The superpower utilized military pacts and currency controls to hegemonize international maritime trade routes.
items.ex_zh: 该超级大国利用军事条约和货币管制来掌控国际海上贸易航线的霸权。

items.def_zh: 称霸；对…耀武扬威地统治
items.def_en: (+ sb) to act in a superior, domineering manner towards others; exercise autocratic sway over
items.ex_en: He loved to lord over the junior interns and assign them menial chores.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢对低年级实习生发号施令，分派给他们琐碎粗重的杂务。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to exercise sovereign authority, power, or dominance over a territory or people
items.ex_en: The benevolent monarch continued to rule over the prosperous realm for more than four decades.
items.ex_zh: 这位仁慈的君主统治了这个繁荣的王国四十余年。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to prevent a group or population from advancing or rebelling through oppressive control
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime deployed paramilitary units to hold down rebellious factions in the provinces.
items.ex_zh: 专制政权部署准军事部队，以压制各省的叛乱派系。

items.def_zh: 在……开拓殖民地，使殖民地化；（生物）大量繁殖于，占领
items.def_en: 1. To send settlers to an area to establish political control over it. 2. (biology) (of plants or animals) To establish itself and spread in a new area.
items.ex_en: Weeds and creeping ivy steadily colonized the crumbling stone courtyard of the abandoned monastery.
items.ex_zh: 杂草与蔓生常春藤渐渐占据了这座废弃修道院坍塌的石砌庭院。

items.def_en: to bring a territory, people, or group under complete political control by force
items.ex_en: The invading army moved ruthlessly across the plains to subjugate the fierce indigenous tribes.
items.ex_zh: 侵略军无情地横扫平原，武力征服了凶悍的本土部落。

groups.summary_en: These transitive verbs denote asserting pervasive political, territorial, or structural control over a nation, community, or demographic group. 'Dominate' focuses on exercising overwhelming sway or mastery, while 'colonize' focuses on settling and establishing institutional hegemony over indigenous lands.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过强权对领地、国家或族群实行制度性支配与统治。
groups.desc_en: To impose geopolitical or hierarchical supremacy over a territory or population, distinct from mere administrative governance by its inherently asymmetric, coercive, and subjugating nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指对某一领土或群体强加地缘政治或层级制压迫性统治，与普通行政管辖不同，它强调不对称的强制性与臣服依附。
groups.nuance_en: dominate: exert overarching mastery or control (market / region / opponent) · colonize: establish demographic settlement and political exploitation (territory / island / people) · subjugate: bring under total subservient control by force (population / rebel / nation) · vassalize: reduce an autonomous entity to a tributary subordinate (kingdom / state / neighbor) · lord over: behave in an arrogant, domineering manner toward inferiors (subordinate / peer / household)
groups.nuance_zh: dominate: 施加压倒性控制或主导地位 (market / region / opponent) · colonize: 通过定居与政治盘剥建立殖民统治 (territory / island / people) · subjugate: 以武力彻底镇压并使之臣服 (population / rebel / nation) · vassalize: 使自主实体沦为纳贡附庸 (kingdom / state / neighbor) · lord over: 摆出傲慢姿态作威作福 (subordinate / peer / household)

groups.name: Asserting & Claiming Positions · 声明与立论 (Assert, Contend, Profess)
groups.tip: 明确宣告观点或立场

items.def_en: to state that something is the case, typically without providing definitive proof
items.ex_en: The company's advertisements boldly claim that their herbal supplement can cure common chronic ailments.
items.ex_zh: 该公司的广告大胆声称，他们的草本补充剂能够治愈常见的慢性疾病。

items.def_zh: 坚持认为，固执己见地宣称
items.def_en: to assert consistently and persistently in the face of doubt or opposition
items.ex_en: Despite mounting empirical counterevidence, the defense attorney maintained that his client was utterly innocent.
items.ex_zh: 尽管相反的经验证据不断增多，辩护律师仍坚持认为他的当事人是完全无辜的。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to state an opinion, argument, or proposition for consideration or debate
items.ex_en: The committee decided to put forward a bold proposal to reform public transportation funding.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定提出一项改革公共交通资金支持的大胆提议以供讨论。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to firmly adhere to or maintain the truth of a claim or assertion despite challenges
items.ex_en: I will stand by my decision regardless of public criticism.
items.ex_zh: 无论外界如何批评，我都会坚持自己的决定。

items.def_zh: 断言，明确坚称；维护，坚持（权利或权威）
items.def_en: 1. To state clearly and firmly that something is true. 2. To behave in a way that expresses your rights, authority, or confidence.
items.ex_en: During the tense meeting, the diplomat took care to assert his nation's sovereign territorial rights.
items.ex_zh: 在紧张的会议期间，这位外交官坚决维护了自己国家的主权领土权利。

items.def_zh: 坚决主张，声称；竞争，争夺；搏斗，应付
items.def_en: 1. To state or argue something strongly as an opinion or fact. 2. To compete against someone in order to gain something. 3. (+ with) To struggle or deal with difficulties.
items.ex_en: Leading climate scientists contend that drastic emissions cuts are necessary to prevent catastrophic global warming.
items.ex_zh: 顶尖气候科学家坚决主张，必须大幅削减排放以防止灾难性的全球变暖。

items.def_en: to state something emphatically and positively as a confirmed truth
items.ex_en: The witness took the stand to affirm that she had indeed seen the incident happen.
items.ex_zh: 证人走上证人席，坚称自己确实目睹了那起事件的发生。

items.def_zh: 声称，自称（常指虚假地）；公开承认，表明（信仰或情感）
items.def_en: 1. To claim or assert something, especially falsely. 2. To openly state or declare a belief, feeling, or religion.
items.ex_en: He professed profound loyalty to the reformist cause while secretly funneling party funds abroad.
items.ex_zh: 他公开宣称深切效忠于改革事业，暗地里却将政党资金转移至国外。

groups.summary_en: A speaker declares a proposition, personal stance, or controversial belief with conviction. Verbs distinguish between making emphatic factual claims (assert), maintaining an argument against opposition (contend), and openly avowing an inner conviction or identity (profess).
groups.summary_zh: 坚定阐述立场、论点或宣称某项事实/信仰，语体偏向书面与正规辨析。
groups.desc_en: To put forward a statement or belief with formal conviction, differing from ordinary speaking by its deliberate posture of intellectual or legal defense against dispute.
groups.desc_zh: 指以正式、坚定的姿态提出陈述或主张，与普通表达不同，它带有应对质疑、确立立场的辩护性与声明性。
groups.nuance_en: assert: state positively and emphatically without needing prior proof (right / innocence / authority) · contend: maintain a position in argumentative dispute (point / theory / view) · claim: declare ownership or truth, often vulnerable to skepticism (damages / responsibility / innocence) · affirm: validate or reassert a solemn truth or prior judgment (decision / loyalty / faith) · profess: openly declare a belief, feeling, or allegiance, sometimes insincerely (ignorance / faith / loyalty)
groups.nuance_zh: assert: 坚定强硬地断言自身权利或事实 (right / innocence / authority) · contend: 在辩论争论中力主某一观点 (point / theory / view) · claim: 声称拥有或属实，常待证实 (damages / responsibility / innocence) · affirm: 庄严确认或重申既有判断与信念 (decision / loyalty / faith) · profess: 公开表白信念或态度，有时带有虚饰意味 (ignorance / faith / loyalty)

groups.name: Assess & Evaluate · 评估与量化评价 (Assigning Comparative Quality or Ranking)
groups.tip: 考量品质并给出评级

items.def_en: (+ sth) to evaluate and mark someone or their performance based on criteria or numerical ranking
items.ex_en: The strict panel will score off each candidate strictly based on their presentation delivery skills.
items.ex_zh: 严格的评审团将完全根据候选人的演讲表达技巧来对其打分评估。

items.def_en: 1. To estimate or assess the monetary worth, quality, or importance of something. 2. To regard something as important or valuable; cherish.
items.ex_en: Certified antique appraisers met this afternoon to value the rare nineteenth-century diamond necklace accurately.
items.ex_zh: 持证古董评估师今天下午会面，以准确评估那条罕见的十九世纪钻石项链的价值。

items.def_en: to evaluate an answer, performance, or asset by assigning numerical points
items.ex_en: Senior examiners will score the final chemistry essays using a rigorous, standardized evaluation rubric.
items.ex_zh: 资深考官将使用严格的标准化评分细则对期末化学论文进行评分。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to carefully examine and evaluate a person or situation before forming a judgement
items.ex_en: The two boxers paced around the ring, sizing each other up.
items.ex_zh: 两位拳手在拳台上踱步，审视打量着对方。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to consider and assess the relative merits, qualities, or drawbacks of something
items.ex_en: Before accepting the overseas position, she carefully weighed up the financial perks against personal disruption.
items.ex_zh: 在接受这份海外职位之前，她仔细权衡了丰厚的经济待遇与个人生活被打乱的得失。

items.def_zh: 评估，评价，定级；值得，应得；被认为，被评价
items.def_en: 1. To assign a standard, value, or ranking to someone or something. 2. To be considered or have a certain ranking or value. 3. To deserve or warrant something.
items.ex_en: Most international travel magazines rate this five-star seaside resort as the finest in Europe.
items.ex_zh: 大多数国际旅游杂志将这家五星级海滨度假村评为欧洲最佳。

items.def_en: to evaluate and classify according to predetermined quality levels or score bands
items.ex_en: Inspectors grade the organic timber shipments according to their density, grain uniformity, and moisture content.
items.ex_zh: 检验员根据有机木材的密度、纹理均匀度和含水量对其进行质量定级。

items.def_en: (+ among/as) to give someone or something a specific position in a graded hierarchy
items.ex_en: Global university leagues consistently rank this prestigious institution among the top ten in the world.
items.ex_zh: 全球大学排行榜一贯将这所顶尖学府列入世界前十名之列。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve judging an entity's standing, quality, or merit along a qualitative or numerical scale, ranging from subjective appreciation to calibrated grading.
groups.summary_zh: 依据一定标准或尺度对对象的优劣等级进行定级、打分或评价。
groups.desc_en: To estimate worth, merit, or performance by systematically matching an entity against comparative criteria, distinct from mere intuition by its calculative or hierarchical nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据比照标准系统测定对象的价值、优劣或绩效，与单纯凭直觉判断不同，它强调量化核算或层级定位。
groups.nuance_en: rate: assign a relative value or score on a recognized scale (performance / service / hotel) · grade: classify systematically into formal quality tiers (exam / beef / timber) · rank: place in sequential, competitive hierarchical order (player / university / candidate) · value: appraise intrinsic or monetary worth (property / asset / collection) · size up: intuitively inspect and assess potential or strength (opponent / situation / newcomer)
groups.nuance_zh: rate: 在既定尺度或等级上打分评估 (performance / service / hotel) · grade: 按质量与规格分门别类或评分 (exam / beef / timber) · rank: 按竞争位次排出先后顺位 (player / university / candidate) · value: 评估内在价值或资产市价 (property / asset / collection) · size up: 审视并直觉研判对手或形势 (opponent / situation / newcomer)

groups.name: Assign & Allocate · 分派与配给 (Assign, Allocate, Task)
groups.tip: 向上呈递任务或分配具体职责

items.def_en: (+ sth) to delegate or assign work or duties to external contractors or subordinates
items.ex_en: The small design firm had to farm out the complex coding tasks to freelancers.
items.ex_zh: 这家小型设计公司不得不将复杂的编程工作外包给自由职业者。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to distribute or allocate tasks, penalties, or resources to individuals
items.ex_en: The floor manager will hand out individual assignments before the morning factory shift begins.
items.ex_zh: 车间主管将在早班工厂开工前给每个人分派具体的生产任务。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ to) to entrust a task, responsibility, or authority to a subordinate
items.ex_en: Effective senior executives know how to delegate operational responsibilities to trusted department heads.
items.ex_zh: 高效的高级管理人员深谙如何向值得信赖的部门主管下放日常运营职责。

items.def_en: (+ to/for) to officially distribute resources, funds, or tasks for a specific purpose
items.ex_en: The municipal council agreed to allocate additional emergency funding for rebuilding the flood-damaged bridge.
items.ex_zh: 市议会同意拨出额外的专项应急资金，用于重建被洪水冲毁的桥梁。

items.def_en: (+ to) to give a specific share of time, money, or work to someone as their due
items.ex_en: The conference organizers will allot twenty minutes to each featured speaker for question time.
items.ex_zh: 会议组织者将给每位特邀演讲者分摊二十分钟的提问互动时间。
