items.ex_en: The carpentry crew will frame the two-story house before the heavy rains begin.
items.ex_zh: 木工队将在大雨来临之前把这栋双层房屋的木骨架搭建好。

items.def_en: (+ sth) construct or erect a building, fence, scaffolding, or upright structure
items.ex_en: The contractors managed to put up the protective wooden fence in two days.
items.ex_zh: 承包商在两天内便搭建起了这道防护木栅栏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) assemble and place structural components in their upright operational position
items.ex_en: Workers worked diligently to set up the steel scaffolding around the entire facade.
items.ex_zh: 工人们加紧施工，把钢制脚手架架设在整面外墙周围。
items.ex2_en: The folding exhibition tents set up easily without requiring any specialized tools.
items.ex2_zh: 这种折叠展览帐篷无需任何专用工具即可轻松搭建。

items.def_en: (+ sth) assemble structural or prefabricated framework elements to form a complete unit
items.ex_en: They carefully piece together the prefabricated timber frame according to the structural blueprint.
items.ex_zh: 他们严格按照结构图纸，仔细地将预制木框架拼装起来。

items.def_en: to fit together the separate component parts of a structure
items.ex_en: Engineers arrived on site to assemble the modular components of the transmission tower.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们赶到现场，开始组装输电铁塔的各模块构件。
items.ex2_en: The modular furniture components assemble easily with only a simple screwdriver.
items.ex2_zh: 这些模块化家具部件只需一把普通的螺丝刀就能轻松组装。

items.def_en: 1. To build or construct a structure, building, or monument. 2. To raise something to a vertical position; to establish a system or idea.
items.ex_en: The civic council voted to erect a bronze monument in the public plaza.
items.ex_zh: 市议会投票决定在公共广场上竖立一座青铜纪念碑。

items.def_zh: 用桁架构固，以构架支撑
items.def_en: to support or strengthen a roof or bridge with a framework of beams
items.ex_en: Specialist contractors had to truss the weak timber bridge with heavy steel beams.
items.ex_zh: 专业施工队必须用重型钢梁来做桁架，以加固脆弱的木桥。

items.def_en: (construction) To furnish or fit a roof with rafters.
items.ex_en: The builders plan to rafter the barn using sturdy beams of local pine.
items.ex_zh: 建筑工人们计划采用坚固的当地松木梁为谷仓装配屋椽。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to raising upright structures, assembling architectural frameworks, or fitting structural supports into place.
groups.summary_zh: 指竖立柱梁、搭建骨架及安装建筑结构构件。
groups.desc_en: Specifies raising vertical structures, assembling structural timbers, or fitting components into an upright architectural framework, contrasting with flat manufacturing.
groups.desc_zh: 指将构件拼装成立体架构、立起竖直结构或架设梁架，不同于平面的制造或散件加工。
groups.nuance_en: erect: raise upright or build a substantial vertical structure (monument / crane / tent) · assemble: put together manufactured components into a complete unit (parts / machinery / furniture) · frame: construct the supporting skeleton of a building or object (house / roof / wall) · rafter: fit or furnish a roof with sloping support beams (ceiling / roof / barn) · put up: quickly raise or construct a temporary structure (scaffolding / fence / shelter)
groups.nuance_zh: erect: 坚直竖立或立起大型建筑物 (monument / crane / tent) · assemble: 拼装预制零部件 (parts / machinery / furniture) · frame: 搭建主骨架或框构 (house / roof / wall) · rafter: 安装椽木架设屋顶 (ceiling / roof / barn) · put up: 快速搭设或立起结构 (scaffolding / fence / shelter)

groups.name: Burn & Overheat · 灼烧与过热 (Thermal Stress to Combustion)
groups.tip: 高温烈火炙烤，表皮碳化焦黑

items.def_en: (+ sth) Become hot or make something significantly hotter
items.ex_en: Running intensive programs will quickly heat up the laptop casing during hot afternoons.
items.ex_zh: 在炎热的午后运行高负荷程序很快会让笔记本外壳变得滚烫。
items.ex2_en: Cold leftover soup will heat up quickly in the microwave within two minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 冰凉的剩汤在微波炉中两分钟内就会迅速热起来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to burn superficially or slightly, especially so as to singe hair, feathers, or cloth
items.ex_en: A stray flying ember managed to singe the frayed hem of her jeans.
items.ex_zh: 飞溅出的火星轻轻烧焦了她牛仔裤的毛边。

items.def_en: to burn or scorch the surface of something with sudden, intense heat
items.ex_en: The sudden blast of fiery exhaust threatened to sear the worker's exposed skin.
items.ex_zh: 突然喷出的炽热废气几乎要灼伤工人裸露在外的皮肤。

items.def_zh: （使）烧焦，（使）焦黑；炙烤；（使植物）枯焦
items.def_en: 1. To burn and discolor the surface of something with intense heat, or to become burned on the surface. 2. (of the sun or drought) To dry up or wither vegetation.
items.ex_en: Intense summer heat began to scorch the dry grass across the open lawn.
items.ex_zh: 夏日的酷暑开始将开阔草坪上的干草晒得焦黄枯萎。
items.ex2_en: Dry pine needles scorch quickly under intense direct sunlight during hot summer afternoons.
items.ex2_zh: 在炎热的夏日午后，干燥的松针在强烈的直射阳光下很快就会烧焦。

items.def_en: Become extremely hot or develop a high fever
items.ex_en: Touch his forehead immediately; the poor kid is burning up with high fever.
items.ex_zh: 快摸摸他的额头，这可怜的孩子正发着高烧，浑身滚烫。

items.def_en: [I/T] to partially burn or reduce to black carbon or charcoal
items.ex_en: The intense bonfire flames rapidly began to char the logs into brittle blackness.
items.ex_zh: 篝火炽烈的火焰很快就将原木烤成了焦黑的炭状。
items.ex2_en: Thin wooden sticks char quickly when held over an open cooking fire.
items.ex2_zh: 细木棍放在露天炊火上烤时很快就会炭化变黑。

items.def_zh: （使）过热，变得过热；（使经济等）过热
items.def_en: 1. To become excessively hot, or make an engine, machine, or system too hot. 2. (economics) (of an economy) To expand at an unsustainably fast rate, or cause it to do so.
items.ex_en: The old tractor engine began to overheat after hours of uninterrupted plowing work.
items.ex_zh: 连续耕作数小时后，这台老旧拖拉机的发动机开始过热了。
items.ex2_en: Careless drivers often overheat car engines by ignoring dashboard temperature warnings.
items.ex2_zh: 粗心的司机常常因忽视仪表盘上的温度警报而使汽车引擎过热。

items.def_en: to burn something completely until reduced entirely to ashes
items.ex_en: Industrial facilities must safely incinerate all hazardous medical waste at exceptionally high temperatures.
items.ex_zh: 工业设施必须在极高温度下安全焚化所有危险医疗废物。

groups.summary_en: An object, surface, or organism absorbs excessive heat, moving from functional overheating and localized superficial singing/scorching to deep thermal destruction and charring.
groups.summary_zh: 物体受热温度过高，由热负荷超标演进到表面灼伤焦黑直至焚毁。
groups.desc_en: Traces the continuum of thermal damage from surface marking and heating beyond safe limits to complete destructive consumption by fire.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖从表面灼伤、温度超限到彻底被烈火焚为灰烬的渐进式热损伤过程。
groups.nuance_en: sear: burn or scorch the exterior surface intensely and rapidly (meat / flesh / skin) · scorch: discolor, dry, or damage the surface with brief heat (fabric / earth / lawn) · singe: burn superficial ends, edges, or fuzz slightly (hair / feathers / eyebrows) · char: blacken and reduce partially to carbon by heat (wood / remains / timber) · incinerate: destroy completely by burning to ashes (waste / garbage / bodies)
groups.nuance_zh: sear: 瞬间高温骤灼表层 (meat / flesh / skin) · scorch: 烤焦、炙烤表面留下灼斑 (fabric / earth / lawn) · singe: 燎焦表层绒毛或纤端 (hair / feathers / eyebrows) · char: 烧焦碳化 (wood / remains / timber) · incinerate: 彻底焚化焚毁 (waste / garbage / bodies)

groups.name: Bury & Entomb · 安葬与埋葬 (Funerary Interring & Consignment)
groups.tip: 将逝者入棺或迁墓下葬

items.def_en: to place a dead body into a grave or the ground, often during a funeral
items.ex_en: Grieving family members gathered quietly to bury the beloved patriarch in local soil.
items.ex_zh: 悲痛的家属们静静聚在一起，将敬爱的家族长辈安葬在乡土之中。

items.def_en: (formal/literary) to commit a body to the earth by burial
items.ex_en: At dusk, solemn mourners gathered to inhume the fallen hero in sanctified ground.
items.ex_zh: 薄暮时分，神情庄重的哀悼者们齐聚一堂，将阵亡英雄入土安葬于圣地。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Bury a deceased person in a grave
items.ex_en: The townsfolk quietly came together to lay away their oldest and dearest resident.
items.ex_zh: 小镇居民悄然聚首，为镇上最年长也最受爱戴的故人送终安葬。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Bury someone with solemn funeral rites
items.ex_en: Dignitaries from around the nation assembled to lay the former premier to rest.
items.ex_zh: 来自全国各地的显要人物齐聚一堂，郑重安葬了这位前总理。

items.def_en: to formally deposit a corpse in a grave or tomb with funeral rites
items.ex_en: The archbishop arrived to inter the departed cardinal within the cathedral's stone vault.
items.ex_zh: 大主教亲临现场，主持将离世红衣主教下葬于大教堂石墓的庄严仪式。

items.def_en: To place a dead body into a coffin.
items.ex_en: The undertaker wept softly as he prepared to coffin his lifelong childhood companion.
items.ex_zh: 殡仪师在准备将自己一生的童年挚友装殓入棺时不禁低声啜泣。

items.def_en: to place a dead body in a crypt, mausoleum, or solid tomb
items.ex_en: Monks conducted sacred midnight rites to entomb the ancient abbot within the crypt.
items.ex_zh: 僧侣们举行神圣的午夜仪式，将年迈的修道院院长入葬于地宫墓穴。

items.def_en: To bury a dead body or remains in the ground again, especially in a different location.
items.ex_en: Authorities chose to rebury the excavated historic soldiers with appropriate military honors.
items.ex_zh: 当局决定以恰当的军礼重新安葬出土的历史士兵遗骸。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the ritualistic or physical placement of a deceased human or animal corpse into a grave, coffin, tomb, or the earth.
groups.summary_zh: 将逝者遗体放入棺木、墓穴或地下安葬的殡葬行为与场景。
groups.desc_en: Addresses the sacred, ritualistic, or permanent physical concealment of human remains within the earth or a vault, contrasting with unceremonious dumping.
groups.desc_zh: 指依照礼俗将遗体永久安置、埋葬于地下或墓穴的安灵仪式，不同于草率丢弃。
groups.nuance_en: bury: general act of placing a dead body into the ground (corpse / victim / deceased) · inter: formally deposit a dead body into a grave with ritual solemnity (remains / body / ashes) · entomb: seal a body inside a tomb, vault, or crypt (pharaoh / crypt / vault) · inhume: deposit a body in the earth (formal/anthropological) (bones / body / remains) · lay to rest: euphemistic and reverent consigning to the grave (hero / patriarch / leader)
groups.nuance_zh: bury: 放入地下掩埋入土 (corpse / victim / deceased) · inter: 庄重肃穆地正式入葬 (remains / body / ashes) · entomb: 封入陵墓、墓室或石棺 (pharaoh / crypt / vault) · inhume: 遗体土葬 (bones / body / remains) · lay to rest: 委以长眠或安息的委婉祭葬 (hero / patriarch / leader)

groups.name: Calibrate & Fine-Tune · 仪器校准与细微调整 (Calibrate, Tweak, Fine-tune)
groups.tip: 精细调校参数至合规状态

items.def_en: 1. To make small, fine adjustments to a machine, system, or plan to improve it. 2. To twist, pinch, or pull something with a sudden jerk.
items.ex_en: The technician decided to tweak the audio filters to remove that annoying buzz.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员决定微调音频滤波器，以消除那恼人的嗡嗡声。

items.def_en: (+ sth) calibrate a sensitive scale or measuring instrument to a precise baseline of zero
items.ex_en: Remember to zero out the analytical balance before placing any chemical sample down.
items.ex_zh: 在放上任何化学样品之前，切记先将分析天平校准清零。

items.def_zh: 微调（飞行平衡、电路或设置）
items.def_en: to make minor adjustments to controls, sails, or balance mechanisms
items.ex_en: The pilot reached down smoothly to trim the elevator controls for level flight.
items.ex_zh: 飞行员平稳地下推操纵，微调升降舵配平以保持平飞。

items.def_en: (+ sth) adjust parameters or controls precisely to achieve optimal calibration or focus
items.ex_en: The guitarist spent several minutes trying to dial in the perfect overdrive tone.
items.ex_zh: 吉他手花了数分钟调试旋钮，试图校准出最完美的过载音色。

items.def_en: (+ sth) adjust a mechanism, wheel, or instrument so that it aligns accurately and symmetrically
items.ex_en: The mechanic used a specialized wrench to true up the wobbly bicycle wheel.
items.ex_zh: 机械师用专用扳手校正了那只晃动的自行车轮圈。

items.def_en: to make very small adjustments to a system or setting to achieve best performance
items.ex_en: Scientists must fine-tune the cooling algorithm to achieve optimum superconducting performance levels.
items.ex_zh: 科学家们必须微调冷却算法，以实现最佳的超导性能。

items.def_zh: 校准，标定；精确调节，仔细评估
items.def_en: 1. To check, mark, or adjust a measuring device so that it gives accurate readings. 2. To carefully assess or adapt something to a particular standard.
items.ex_en: The astronomer paused to calibrate the ancient brass astrolabe against the polar star.
items.ex_zh: 天文学家停下脚步，参照北极星校准那具古老的黄铜星盘。

items.def_en: (+ in/out) to adjust an instrument or sight to read zero or align precisely on target
items.ex_en: He went to the shooting range early to zero his precision rifle scope.
items.ex_zh: 他大清早就去靶场，为自己的精准步枪瞄准镜归零校准。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to adjusting mechanisms, parameters, or sensitive measuring instruments to conform to a standard or achieve optimal operational accuracy. They span from informal minor tweaks to standardized scientific calibration.
groups.summary_zh: 针对仪器、系统或参数进行微小修正或标准标定，以达到精确状态。
groups.desc_en: Highlights exacting, minute mechanical or systemic adjustments against an absolute standard or optimal threshold, contrasting with broad revision.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据绝对基准或最佳工况对系统、仪器进行极微小而精密的调校，不同于粗放修改。
groups.nuance_en: calibrate: adjust against a known measurement standard to ensure accuracy (instrument / sensor / scale) · fine-tune: make tiny delicate changes to optimize performance (engine / balance / parameters) · tweak: apply slight practical twists or modifications (settings / design / code) · zero out: adjust a scale or gauge to read zero at base level (balance / scale / counter) · true up: correct physical alignment or squareness of a mechanical part (wheel / frame / axle)
groups.nuance_zh: calibrate: 依据标准器进行计量标定与校准 (instrument / sensor / scale) · fine-tune: 针对性能做精细微调 (engine / balance / parameters) · tweak: 针对细节稍作调弄修改 (settings / design / code) · zero out: 仪器回零或清零校正 (balance / scale / counter) · true up: 机械平直度或圆度校正 (wheel / frame / axle)

groups.name: Capitalize & Provide Finance · 融资与注资 (Finance, Capitalize, Underwrite)
groups.tip: 注入资金支持项目

items.def_zh: 为……提供资金，出资；贷款购买
items.def_en: To provide the money needed to pay for something such as a project, business, or large purchase.
items.ex_en: International consortiums agreed to finance the construction of the deep-water cargo port.
items.ex_zh: 国际财团已达成协议，为深水货运港口的建设提供资金。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) rescue an enterprise or institution from financial collapse by injecting funds
items.ex_en: Taxpayers were outraged when the treasury decided to bail out reckless mortgage lenders.
items.ex_zh: 当财政部决定向鲁莽的按揭贷款机构提供紧急救助资金时，纳税人被激怒了。

items.def_en: (+ sth into sth) supply large amounts of investment capital or funding into an enterprise
items.ex_en: Venture funds continue to pump money into promising biomedical startups across the continent.
items.ex_zh: 风险投资基金继续向遍布欧洲大陆的前沿生物医药初创企业注资。

items.def_zh: 对（财务/资本结构）进行资金支撑
items.def_en: (+ sth) strengthen a precarious balance sheet or venture by supplying financial backing
items.ex_en: The parent firm stepped in to shore up the struggling branch's depleted capital.
items.ex_zh: 母公司及时介入，以资金支持苦苦支撑的分支机构枯竭的资本。

items.def_en: to pay part of the cost of something via public funds or organizational assistance
items.ex_en: The regional government agreed to subsidize clean energy initiatives for low-income rural households.
items.ex_zh: 地区政府同意动用公共资金补贴低收入农村家庭的清洁能源项目。

items.def_en: to provide a large permanent sum of money for a school, hospital, or chair
items.ex_en: The wealthy alumnus arranged to endow a permanent research chair in quantum physics.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有的校友出资为量子物理系设立了一个永久性特聘教授教席基金。

items.def_zh: 包销；承销；为…提供经济担保
items.def_en: to accept financial responsibility for a commercial project or issue of securities
items.ex_en: Reputable investment syndicates gathered to underwrite the sovereign bond issue despite geopolitical turmoil.
items.ex_zh: 尽管地缘政局动荡，声誉卓著的投资财团依然聚首为该国债发行提供承销担保。

items.def_zh: 为……提供资金；利用（capitalise on）；大写
items.def_en: 1. To supply a business with the necessary funds or capital. 2. (capitalise on) To use a situation to your own advantage. 3. To write or print in capital letters.
items.ex_en: Shareholders gathered yesterday to adequately capitalise the newly formed clean-technology venture.
items.ex_zh: 股东们昨日开会，为这家新成立的清洁技术合资企业注足了资本。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate institutional, corporate, or financial acts of providing capital, balance-sheet backing, or structural funding to establish or maintain a venture.
groups.summary_zh: 为企业、项目或交易提供资本金、资金安排或承销金融担保。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on injecting equity, absorbing risk, or providing monetary foundations to establish or rescue an entity, contrasting with regular payment or purchasing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过注资、认购股权或风险兜底来为实体提供长期资金支撑或危机解救，区别于日常支付。
groups.nuance_en: capitalise: provide a business with capital sum or convert earnings into equity (startup / enterprise / venture) · finance: provide overall funds for a large undertaking or purchase (project / operation / deficit) · underwrite: guarantee financial backing and assume risk (loan / insurance / IPO) · bail out: rescue financially from imminent insolvency (bank / airline / economy) · subsidize: support financially through government grants to keep costs low (industry / farming / housing)
groups.nuance_zh: capitalise: 提供股本启动资金或资本化 (startup / enterprise / venture) · finance: 为大型项目或赤字统筹融资 (project / operation / deficit) · underwrite: 承销并担保承担财务风险 (loan / insurance / IPO) · bail out: 紧急注资纾困破产危机 (bank / airline / economy) · subsidize: 发放财政补贴维持运营 (industry / farming / housing)

groups.name: Capture & Seize Power · 强占与篡夺 (Forcibly Take Control or Territory)
groups.tip: 武力夺取领土或控制权

items.def_en: to succeed in taking control of a place, city, or enemy position by military force
items.ex_en: Infantry units fought all night to capture the strategic coastal fortress by dawn.
items.ex_zh: 步兵部队彻夜激战，终于在黎明前攻占了这座具有战略意义的沿海要塞。

items.def_en: to take control of an area, power, or weapon suddenly by using physical force
items.ex_en: Rebel commanders moved swiftly to seize the provincial radio broadcast building by force.
items.ex_zh: 叛军指挥官迅速采取行动，以武力夺取了省广播大楼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Assume control of a territory, organization, or political power, often forcefully
items.ex_en: The military junta managed to take over the capital city during midnight operations.
items.ex_zh: 军政府在午夜行动中成功夺取了首都的控制权。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Forcibly take power, authority, or control from someone after a struggle
items.ex_en: The rebellious prince sought to wrest away the royal scepter from his father.
items.ex_zh: 叛逆的王子企图从父亲手中强行夺走象征王权的权杖。

items.def_zh: 攻占，夺回（失地等）；重新拿回；重拍；重考
items.def_en: 1. To take control of a place or position again by force. 2. To take an exam or photograph again.
items.ex_en: Allied divisions launched a fierce counteroffensive to retake the lost border outpost.
items.ex_zh: 盟军师团发起猛烈反攻，以重新夺回沦陷的边境前哨。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To take someone's power, throne, or position illegally or by force.
items.ex_en: The ambitious general plotted secretly to usurp the sovereign throne and dissolve parliament.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的将军暗中密谋篡夺君主王位并解散议会。

items.def_zh: 费力夺取，强行攫取（控制权）
items.def_en: (+ from) to forcefully extract control, power, or authority away from someone against resistance
items.ex_en: The insurgent faction struggled bitterly to wrest control from the entrenched military leadership.
items.ex_zh: 叛军派系艰苦奋战，试图从根深蒂固的军方领导层手中夺取控制权。

items.def_zh: 强征，霸占（设备、场所用于军事）
items.def_en: to officially take possession or control of something, especially for military or emergency use
items.ex_en: The retreating army moved swiftly to commandeer civilian cargo vessels for emergency transit.
items.ex_zh: 撤退的军队迅速行动，强行征用了民用货轮用于紧急转运。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict the forceful or unlawful taking of sovereign power, high office, or fortified positions. 'Usurp' stresses taking supreme authority wrongfully without legal right, whereas 'retake' focuses on recapturing territory or strongholds previously lost.
groups.summary_zh: 通过武力或非法手段夺取权力、王位或收复阵地地盘。
groups.desc_en: Covers acquiring sovereignty, leadership, or resources by sudden unconstitutional or violent force against opposition, contrasting with consensual transfer.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过突发暴力、政变或强取豪夺从对手手中夺取政权、主导权或资源，区别于和平移交。
groups.nuance_en: usurp: wrongfully seize a throne, power, or authority without legal right (throne / authority / power) · seize: take forcible possession suddenly and decisively (power / control / assets) · wrest: pull or extract power or control with violent effort (control / leadership / initiative) · commandeer: officially seize property for military or urgent public use (vehicle / building / vessel) · take over: assume managerial or sovereign control, forcefully or procedurally (company / regime / operations)
groups.nuance_zh: usurp: 篡夺王位、权力或合法职权 (throne / authority / power) · seize: 强力突袭查扣或夺取 (power / control / assets) · wrest: 竭力从敌手处硬生生夺出 (control / leadership / initiative) · commandeer: 征用或强占民用物资作军用 (vehicle / building / vessel) · take over: 接收并接管控制权 (company / regime / operations)

groups.name: Care & Minister to · 照料与看护 (Tend, Nurse, Minister)
groups.tip: 悉心护理与日常照料

items.def_en: to look after someone who is ill, very old, or young by attending to their needs
items.ex_en: She returned home every evening to care for her ailing and bedridden grandmother.
items.ex_zh: 她每天晚上都回家照料卧病在床且身体虚弱的祖母。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) take care of someone or something, attending to their health, comfort, or safety
items.ex_en: His aunt volunteered to look after the lively twin boys during their vacation.
items.ex_zh: 在假期期间，他的姑姑主动承担起看顾这对活泼双胞胎男孩的责任。

items.def_zh: 照料，看护，照管；往往会，倾向于
items.def_en: 1. To care for or look after someone or something. 2. To regularly or frequently behave in a particular way or be likely to do something.
items.ex_en: Dedicated volunteers visit the hospice daily to tend to the frailest hospice patients.
items.ex_zh: 热心的志愿者每天造访临终关怀医院，悉心照看那些最虚弱的病患。

items.def_en: to take care of a child or dependent animal as a guardian for a period
items.ex_en: The charitable couple decided to foster several neglected rescue dogs until loving adoption.
items.ex_zh: 这对富有善心的夫妇决定收容寄养数只被忽视的救援犬，直至有人领养。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) give delicate, sustained care to a sick person or weak entity to help them recover
items.ex_en: He carefully nursed the fragile startup along until it became profitable.
items.ex_zh: 他悉心扶持这家脆弱的初创公司，直至其实现盈利。

items.def_en: (+ sb) provide attentive personal service to someone, especially an invalid or elderly person
items.ex_en: Devoted nurses continued to wait on the paralyzed patient with patience and kindness.
items.ex_zh: 尽职尽责的护士们始终耐心友善地服侍着这位瘫痪的病人。

items.def_en: (+ to) to tend to someone's physical, medical, or emotional needs with devotion
items.ex_en: Volunteers stepped forward to minister to the wounded survivors sheltering inside the chapel.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们走上前去，细心照料在小教堂里避难的受伤幸存者。

items.def_zh: 护理，看护，照料（病人或伤员）；给……喂奶，哺乳；悉心调养，怀抱（情绪或想法）
items.def_en: 1. To care for a sick or injured person. 2. To feed a baby with milk from the breast. 3. To hold or nurture a feeling, idea, or injury carefully.
items.ex_en: The medic stayed up all night to nurse the injured young soldier.
items.ex_zh: 军医整夜未眠，悉心照料看护那名受伤的年轻士兵。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve providing dedicated personal, medical, or maternal care to an invalid, sick person, or dependent living being over time.
groups.summary_zh: 针对患病、受伤或体弱者提供贴身看护、治疗与日常照料的关怀行为。
groups.desc_en: Expresses ongoing devotion to satisfying the bodily, health, or spiritual needs of the vulnerable, contrasting with detached supervision.
groups.desc_zh: 强调持续悉心满足老弱病幼的生理、健康或精神照护需求，不同于抽离式的业务监管。
groups.nuance_en: nurse: care for sick, injured, or infant people through convalescence (patient / invalid / wound) · tend: watch over, attend to, and manage domestic or living things (flock / garden / wounded) · minister to: attend to the deeper emotional, spiritual, or comfort needs of others (needs / sick / dying) · foster: rear and care for a child without blood relation, or nurture growth (child / talent / growth) · care for: provide steady practical assistance and emotional affection (elderly / sick / children)
groups.nuance_zh: nurse: 悉心看护照料病患以助康复 (patient / invalid / wound) · tend: 照看与抚弄照料 (flock / garden / wounded) · minister to: 关切服侍精神或生死重大需求 (needs / sick / dying) · foster: 寄养扶育或培植成长 (child / talent / growth) · care for: 承担生活上的长期照料责任 (elderly / sick / children)

groups.name: Catch & Seize · 接拿与截捕 (Catch, Field, Intercept)
groups.tip: 在运动中拦截并接稳飞球

items.def_en: (+ sth) Make a sudden attempt to seize or take hold of a moving or static object
items.ex_en: He grabbed at the handrail as the train lurched forward.
items.ex_zh: 列车猛然前冲时，他一把抓住了扶手。

items.def_zh: 接球，防守（接防飞球）；巧妙应对（提问或批评）；派出（参赛队伍或候选人）
items.def_en: 1. To catch, intercept, or stop and throw the ball in sports like baseball or cricket. 2. To deal with or answer questions, criticisms, or telephone calls skillfully. 3. To put a sports team or candidate into a competition.
items.ex_en: The agile shortstop raced backward gracefully to field the high pop fly.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的游击手从容后退，稳稳接住了那个高飞球。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Seize or grab an airborne or moving object rapidly and abruptly
items.ex_en: She managed to snatch up the falling glassware before it struck the tiles.
items.ex_zh: 她眼疾手快，赶在下落的玻璃器皿砸向地砖前一把抓住了它。

items.def_zh: 接住，拦截；抓住，捕获；赶上（车辆等）；染上（疾病）
items.def_en: 1. To stop and hold something moving through the air with your hands. 2. To capture an animal or person. 3. To reach in time to board a vehicle.
items.ex_en: He reached out his bare hands to catch the flying ball with ease.
items.ex_zh: 他伸出双手，轻而易举地接住了飞来的球。

items.def_zh: 中途拦截，截击（飞行中的球或投掷物）
items.def_en: to catch or receive a ball or projectile before it reaches its destination
items.ex_en: The alert defender sprinted ahead to intercept the opponent's intended pass to goal.
items.ex_zh: 机警的防守队员快速前插，截断了对手传向球门的传球。

items.def_en: to catch suddenly or unexpectedly (informal)
items.ex_en: The quick outfielder managed to nab the screaming fly ball along the fence.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的外野手紧贴围栏，一把逮住了那个呼啸而来的飞球。

items.def_zh: 拢住，兜住（四处乱滚或四散的物品）
items.def_en: to gather together or trap loose, moving objects with one's hands
items.ex_en: She had to corral the scattering marbles before they rolled under the heavy sofa.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不赶在四散的弹珠滚进笨重的沙发底之前将它们一一拢住。

items.def_en: to catch or seize something quickly, suddenly, and forcefully
items.ex_en: The goalie managed to snatch the ricocheted ball straight out of thin air.
items.ex_zh: 守门员一把从半空中猛地抓住了折射弹回的皮球。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe intercepting and taking hold of an airborne, rolling, or moving object, ranging from routine grasping in sports to aggressive snatching.
groups.summary_zh: 指在半空中或地面上出手截留、截获或抓住处于运动中的物体。
groups.desc_en: Denotes arresting the trajectory of a moving object or securing a fleeing quarry mid-motion, contrasting with picking up a stationary item.
groups.desc_zh: 指在半空中拦截、迎击飞来之物或在移动中捕获逃脱者，不同于拾取静止物品。
groups.nuance_en: catch: intercept and hold a moving object or person (ball / fish / thief) · intercept: stop, seize, or interrupt the path of something before arrival (pass / missile / communications) · snatch: seize hastily, suddenly, and often surreptitiously (purse / weapon / opportunity) · field: catch or stop a ball and return it into play (ball / grounder / questions) · nab: capture or arrest a perpetrator suddenly in the act (suspect / criminal / thief)
groups.nuance_zh: catch: 接住飞来物或擒获目标 (ball / fish / thief) · intercept: 半途拦截阻截 (pass / missile / communications) · snatch: 猝不及防下手夺取 (purse / weapon / opportunity) · field: 接球并迅速处理回传 (ball / grounder / questions) · nab: 当场逮住或抓获嫌犯 (suspect / criminal / thief)

groups.name: Catch Fire & Blaze · 点燃与引燃 (Ignite, Flare, Blaze)
groups.tip: 引火生热点起火苗

items.def_en: [T/I] to start a fire by setting light to fuel, or to begin burning gently
items.ex_en: The wanderer knelt beside the hearth to kindle a gentle fire from pine needles.
items.ex_zh: 行者跪在壁炉旁，用松针点燃了一簇温和的火苗。
items.ex2_en: Dry autumn leaves kindle easily from the smallest spark in breezy weather.
items.ex2_zh: 在有微风的天气里，干燥的秋叶即使遇上极小的火星也极易起火。

items.def_en: begin to burn with flames
items.ex_en: The dry curtains might catch on fire if placed too near the heater.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的窗帘若是离取暖器太近，很可能会着火。

items.def_en: suddenly burn more brightly or intensely
items.ex_en: Dry pine needles caused the campfire to flare up with unexpected ferocity.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的松针使营火骤然蹿出火苗，猛烈燃烧起来。

items.def_en: suddenly ignite and start burning violently
items.ex_en: The damaged racing car suddenly spun off the track and burst into flames.
items.ex_zh: 受损的赛车突然偏离赛道，瞬间燃起了熊熊大火。

items.def_en: to burn with a powerful, extremely bright, and hot flame
items.ex_en: Bonfires blazed brightly across the hillside throughout the chilly autumn night.
items.ex_zh: 整片山坡上的营火在清冷的秋夜里熊熊燃烧，放出耀眼的光芒。

items.def_zh: （火焰）突然烧旺，闪亮；（愤怒、暴力等）爆发；（使）张开，（使）呈喇叭形展开
items.def_en: 1. (often + up) To burn suddenly with a bright, unsteady flame. 2. (often + up) (of anger, violence, or illness) To suddenly erupt or become worse. 3. To widen gradually at the bottom, or make something widen.
items.ex_en: A sudden gust of wind made the dying embers flare into bright life.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的狂风使即将熄灭的余烬骤然闪亮，重新烧旺。
items.ex2_en: The sudden draft flared the campfire, scattering bright sparks into the darkness.
items.ex2_zh: 突然刮来的一阵风吹旺了营火，把明亮的火花散入黑暗中。

items.def_zh: 点燃，引发；着火，起火；激起，引发（冲突、热情等）
items.def_en: 1. To catch fire, or make something start to burn. 2. To trigger or arouse strong feelings, controversy, or enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: Leaking fuel can instantly ignite upon contact with the hot engine manifold.
items.ex_zh: 泄漏的燃油接触到灼热的发动机歧管可能会瞬间起火。
items.ex2_en: A stray electrical spark can instantly ignite dry gasoline vapors in closed garages.
items.ex2_zh: 封闭车库中的微小电火花能瞬间引燃干燥的汽油蒸气。

items.def_en: [I/T] to catch fire and burn furiously in an extensive, destructive blaze
items.ex_en: The wooden tenements conflagrated swiftly, turning the entire district into ash.
items.ex_zh: 木质公寓楼迅猛燃为火海，将整个街区化为灰烬。
items.ex2_en: Careless handling of volatile chemicals can easily conflagrate the entire laboratory building.
items.ex2_zh: 对易挥发化学品处理不慎很容易将整个实验室大楼引燃成一片火海。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the initiation and escalating physical intensity of combustion, from the first spark of catching fire to a sudden burst or roaring flame.
groups.summary_zh: 描述物体被引燃起火到突然迸发强光或剧烈燃烧的物理强度进程。
groups.desc_en: Traces the spontaneous transition from initial combustion to roaring, uncontrolled fire, contrasting with the smoldering of embers.
groups.desc_zh: 体现从初起受燃起火到烈焰熊熊奔腾的突发爆发过程，不同于微火阴燃或余烬残热。
groups.nuance_en: ignite: cause to catch fire or begin combustion chemically (fuel / spark / mixture) · kindle: light a fire through tinder or awaken fiery passion (bonfire / flame / enthusiasm) · flare up: suddenly erupt with intense, brilliant, brief flames (fire / rebellion / tempers) · blaze: burn with great, sustained brightness and heat (furnace / sun / inferno) · conflagrate: catch fire and erupt into a massive, destructive inferno (city / woodland / building)
groups.nuance_zh: ignite: 物理点燃或化学引燃 (fuel / spark / mixture) · kindle: 借引火物点火或激发热情 (bonfire / flame / enthusiasm) · flare up: 烈火或情绪骤然腾起冲天 (fire / rebellion / tempers) · blaze: 熊熊烈火灿烂持久燃烧 (furnace / sun / inferno) · conflagrate: 爆发毁灭性巨型火灾 (city / woodland / building)

groups.name: Chatter & Ramble · 闲聊与信口漫谈 (Babble, Chatter, Ramble)
groups.tip: 信马由缰地随意漫谈杂扯

items.def_zh: 喋喋不休地唠叨，闲聊；（牙齿）打颤；（鸟或动物）鸣叫
items.def_en: 1. To talk quickly and continuously about unimportant things. 2. (of teeth) To knock together repeatedly from cold or fear.
items.ex_en: The nervous teenagers continued to chatter about fashion during the entire movie.
items.ex_zh: 那些紧张的青少年在整场电影期间一直喋喋不休地闲聊时尚。

items.def_zh: 漫谈，闲扯，语无伦次地说；漫步，漫游；（植物）蔓生
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/about) To talk or write for a long time in a confused, unfocused way. 2. (+ through/over) To walk for pleasure in the countryside.
items.ex_en: The tired professor began to ramble about obscure historical trivia without focus.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的教授开始漫无边际地闲扯起晦涩的历史冷知识。

items.def_zh: 胡扯，喋喋不休地说胡话
items.def_en: to talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish, excited, or incomprehensible way
items.ex_en: Delirious with high fever, the young boy started to babble incoherently.
items.ex_zh: 小男孩因高烧神志不清，开始语无伦次地胡扯乱说。

items.def_en: to talk at length about unimportant things in an idle or childish manner
items.ex_en: Idle courtiers continued to prattle about court gossip beneath the arched ceiling.
items.ex_zh: 无所事事的朝臣们在拱顶天花板下絮絮叨叨地闲扯宫廷琐事。

items.def_zh: 嗡嗡作声地长篇大论，单调啰唆
items.def_en: talk for a long time in a dull, monotonous, and boring voice
items.ex_en: Our manager proceeded to drone on about sales metrics for two hours.
items.ex_zh: 我们的经理接着用单调啰唆的语调就销售指标长篇大论了两个小时。

items.def_en: talk incessantly and boringly about trivial matters
items.ex_en: She will rabbit on about her pedigree cats unless someone stops her.
items.ex_zh: 除非有人出面打断，否则她会对自己养的纯种猫喋喋不休个没完。

items.def_en: talk at length in an aimless, confused, or disjointed manner
items.ex_en: He tended to ramble on whenever an interviewer asked an unexpected question.
items.ex_zh: 每当面试官提出意想不到的问题时，他往往会东拉西扯地信口漫谈。

items.def_zh: 单调低沉地唠叨，冗长慢谈
items.def_en: (+ on) to speak continuously and monotonously in a boring tone
items.ex_en: The exhausted speaker continued to drone about budget cuts to bored attendees.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的发言人继续用单调低沉的语调向无聊的与会者念叨预算削减。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict informal, uncontrolled speech, distinguishing rapid, incessant trivial talk from disjointed, wandering, and excessively long-winded monologues.
groups.summary_zh: 指缺乏严谨结构、琐碎或漫无边际、信口开河的言语交谈方式。
groups.desc_en: Characterizes uninterrupted, frivolous, or disorganized speech that lacks direction or substance, contrasting with coherent, purposeful discourse.
groups.desc_zh: 指缺乏实质内容、缺乏逻辑或滔滔不绝的琐碎碎念漫谈，不同于条理清晰的正式言说。
groups.nuance_en: chatter: talk rapidly and incessantly about trivial matters (monkeys / teeth / crowd) · ramble: talk or write at length aimlessly without clear point or structure (speech / speaker / writer) · babble: speak incoherently, foolishly, or like an infant (baby / brook / idiot) · prattle: talk in a childish, simple, or foolishly artless manner (children / gossip / chatterbox) · drone on: speak monotonically, flatly, and tediously at length (lecturer / speaker / professor)
groups.nuance_zh: chatter: 喋喋不休聊些鸡毛蒜皮 (monkeys / teeth / crowd) · ramble: 毫无中心信马由缰地长篇漫谈 (speech / speaker / writer) · babble: 语无伦次或如儿语般胡说 (baby / brook / idiot) · prattle: 稚气或轻浮地唠叨个不停 (children / gossip / chatterbox) · drone on: 声音平淡单调且冗长折磨人 (lecturer / speaker / professor)

groups.name: Chew Repetitively & Clamp Jaws · 咀嚼与咬磨 (Chew, Champ, Chomp)
groups.tip: 用牙齿反复嚼碎或撕咬食物

items.def_en: 1. to bite and grind food repeatedly with the teeth. 2. to think carefully about something (often with 'on' or 'over').
items.ex_en: She took a few minutes to chew on his intriguing business proposal.
items.ex_zh: 她花了几分钟时间仔细深思他那个颇具吸引力的商业提议。

items.def_zh: 咀嚼，咬碎（医学生理用词）
items.def_en: [I/T] to chew food thoroughly with teeth to reduce it to pulp
items.ex_en: Patients who cannot masticate their food properly require a specialized soft diet.
items.ex_zh: 无法充分咀嚼食物的患者需要特殊的软质流食。

items.def_en: continue chewing food or an object repetitively
items.ex_en: The happy beagle continued to chew away at his favorite rubber toy.
items.ex_zh: 那只欢快的比格犬继续不停地咬嚼着它最喜欢的橡胶玩具。

items.def_en: (+ at sth) continuously bite or nibble at something hard
items.ex_en: Hungry field mice began to gnaw away at the wooden pantry door.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的田鼠开始反复啃咬食品储藏室的木门。

items.def_zh: 格格地咬，大声咀嚼；（马）咬嚼（嚼子）
items.def_en: to chew or bite noisily, vigorously, or impatiently
items.ex_en: The restless warhorse champed at its iron bit before the morning charge.
items.ex_zh: 焦躁的战马在晨间冲锋前烦躁不安地大声咀嚼着铁嚼子。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) bite down forcefully and noisily with the jaws
items.ex_en: The starving hiker chomped down on the thick crust of sourdough bread.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的徒步旅行者使劲咬住那块厚实坚硬的酸酵母面包。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ at/on) to bite or nibble at something hard persistently with the front teeth
items.ex_en: Beavers constantly gnaw on tree branches to keep their sharp teeth trimmed.
items.ex_zh: 海狸不断啃咬树枝，以磨整它们锋利的牙齿。

items.def_zh: 格格地大口咀嚼，用力咬
items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on/at) to chew or bite with forceful, noisy jaw movements
items.ex_en: He stood by the stall and chomped noisily on a crisp apple.
items.ex_zh: 他站在摊位旁，大口咀嚼着一个清脆的苹果，发出响声。

groups.summary_en: An agent rhythmically grinds, masticates, or clamps teeth onto food or an object using continuous, forceful mandibular action.
groups.summary_zh: 上下颚持续用力开合，反复咀嚼、咬合或咀磨坚韧物件。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the mechanical, rhythmic grinding or clamping of the jaws upon an object, contrasting with quick biting (a single severance) or swallowing (ingestion without mastication).
groups.desc_zh: 指下颌对物体进行有节奏的反复机械研磨、咀嚼或重压咬合，区别于瞬间切断的咬（bite）或直接吞咽（swallow）。
groups.nuance_en: chew: baseline repetitive grinding with teeth (food / gum / cud) · masticate: formal or physiological grinding to pulp (bolus / food / solids) · gnaw: persistent nibbling erosion with incisors (bone / rope / bark) · chomp: noisy, vigorous downward biting (cigar / bit / apple) · champ: restless or impatient clamping of jaws (bit / oats / food)
groups.nuance_zh: chew: 最基准的牙齿反复咀嚼 (food / gum / cud) · masticate: 正式或生理学意义上的研磨粉碎 (bolus / food / solids) · gnaw: 用门齿持续啃咬侵蚀 (bone / rope / bark) · chomp: 吧唧嘴、用力大口咀嚼咬住 (cigar / bit / apple) · champ: 躁动、不耐烦地咬动或咀嚼 (bit / oats / food)

groups.name: Classify & Sort · 分类与分级 (Sort, Grade, Pigeonhole)
groups.tip: 按属性理清事物类别

items.def_en: (+ sth) separate things or people into distinct classes, groups, or categories based on specific criteria
items.ex_en: Volunteers helped sort out the donated clothes into distinct age categories.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们帮忙将捐赠的衣物按不同年龄段挑出并分类整理。

items.def_zh: 整理，分类；拣选；交往，协调
items.def_en: 1. To arrange things in a particular order or divide them into categories. 2. To pick out or separate from others. 3. (archaic) To associate with or suit.
items.ex_en: Clerks must sort these urgent incoming letters by their regional postal codes.
items.ex_zh: 办事员必须按照各地区的邮政编码整理拣选这些紧急来信。

items.def_zh: 将……分级，按等级分类；给……评分，批改（作业、试卷）；给（路面）平整坡度
items.def_en: 1. To arrange, classify, or sort into grades or levels. 2. To give a grade or mark to a student's work. 3. To level a road or ground to a smooth slope.
items.ex_en: Inspectors will grade the harvested timber based on density and grain quality.
items.ex_zh: 检验员将根据密度和纹理质量把采伐的木材划分等级。

items.def_en: (+ as/into) to assign items formally to a particular group or category based on shared characteristics
items.ex_en: Biologists classify this newly discovered freshwater fish as an endangered species.
items.ex_zh: 生物学家将这种新发现的淡水鱼正式归类为濒危物种。

items.def_en: (+ as/into) to place people or things into specific conceptual groups
items.ex_en: Researchers categorize these distinct social behaviors into four primary psychological types.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员将这些独特的社会行为划分为四种主要的心理类型。

items.def_en: (+ sth) examine a large collection of items or information very carefully to find or categorize what is needed
items.ex_en: Investigators had to sift through hundreds of financial documents to locate evidence.
items.ex_zh: 调查人员不得不细致筛查数百份财务文件以查找证据。

items.def_en: (+ through) to examine information or objects meticulously to separate the useful from the unneeded
items.ex_en: Historians patiently sift through ancient archives to separate verifiable facts from mythology.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家耐心地细筛古老档案，以甄别神话并筛选出可靠史实。

items.def_en: (+ as) to unfairly or rigidly classify someone or something into an overly restrictive category
items.ex_en: Critics unfairly pigeonhole the versatile performer as merely a slapstick comedian.
items.ex_zh: 批评家们刻板地将这位多才多艺的演员定性为单纯的滑稽小丑。

groups.summary_en: An agent systematically evaluates a group of items or people and assigns them to distinct categories, ranks, or tiers based on quality, size, or specific criteria.
groups.summary_zh: 依品质、规格或特征将事物或人员系统性归类、分等或排序。
groups.desc_en: Involves systematically differentiating and arranging items according to established criteria, qualitative tiers, or preconceived bins, differing from mere random separation.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据既定标准、品质层级或预设框架对事物进行系统性辨析与归纳分类，区别于无标准的随机分离（separate）。
groups.nuance_en: sort: baseline separating into ordered groups or orders (mail / laundry / rubbish) · classify: formal assignment to systematic conceptual categories (organisms / documents / data) · categorize: practical grouping under descriptive labels (expenses / risks / books) · grade: arranging into quality or proficiency ranks (eggs / lumber / students) · pigeonhole: rigidly or unfairly forcing into narrow stereotypes (candidates / genres / authors)
groups.nuance_zh: sort: 最通用的按类别理顺归整 (mail / laundry / rubbish) · classify: 正式地按科学体系或层级分类 (organisms / documents / data) · categorize: 贴标签式的实用归类 (expenses / risks / books) · grade: 按品质、大小或等级评定分级 (eggs / lumber / students) · pigeonhole: 机械刻板地生搬硬套归类 (candidates / genres / authors)

groups.name: Classify & Sort · 分类与归整 (Classify, Sort, Group, Size)
groups.tip: 按属性特征进行归并分组

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) gather or arrange people or objects into categories or sets based on shared characteristics
items.ex_en: The cataloguer will group together related artifacts from the Bronze Age.
items.ex_zh: 文物编目员会将青铜时代的相关器物归类在一起。
items.ex2_en: Excited young children group together quickly around the colorful holiday entertainer.
items.ex2_zh: 兴奋的小孩子们迅速在色彩斑斓的节日表演者身边聚拢成一团。

items.def_zh: 按大小排列（或分类）；给……上浆（或涂胶料）
items.def_en: 1. To sort, arrange, or grade according to size. 2. To treat or coat a surface with size or glue.
items.ex_en: Workers carefully size the polished gemstones before mounting them in gold rings.
items.ex_zh: 工人们在将打磨好的宝石镶入金戒前先按大小分类。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ into/by) to arrange things systematically according to their type, class, or quality
items.ex_en: Postal machinery can sort thousands of parcels every hour by destination code.
items.ex_zh: 邮政设备每小时能根据目的地编码分拣数千件包裹。

items.def_en: to pass substances or candidates through a check or sieve to separate by suitability
items.ex_en: Human resources will screen all submitted resumes to eliminate unqualified applicants.
items.ex_zh: 人力资源部门将甄别筛选所有提交的简历，以淘汰不合格的申请人。

items.def_zh: 将……降级；划分到较低等级
items.def_en: (+ sth) reduce the rank, grade, or classification of something according to quality or size
items.ex_en: The inspector decided to grade down the damaged fruit to industrial use.
items.ex_zh: 检验员决定将这些受损的水果降级为工业加工用果。

items.def_zh: 把……分组，把……归类；（使）成群，聚合
items.def_en: 1. To classify or arrange people or things into groups. 2. To gather together or form a group.
items.ex_en: The teacher will group students according to their current reading proficiency levels.
items.ex_zh: 老师将根据学生目前的阅读能力水平把他们分组。
items.ex2_en: The nervous students grouped together quietly near the examination room door.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的学生们在考场门旁静静地聚拢在一起。

items.def_en: to arrange or sort products according to their quality, size, or importance
items.ex_en: Orchard workers grade the fresh apples before packing them into wooden crates.
items.ex_zh: 果园工人们在将新鲜苹果装入木箱前先按品质分拣等级。

items.def_en: (+ as/into) to categorize objects or data into formal taxonomical groups
items.ex_en: Botanists formally classify the rare tropical specimen into an entirely new genus.
items.ex_zh: 植物学家正式将这一罕见的热带标本划归为一个全新的属。

groups.summary_en: An agent systematically evaluates, separates, and arranges objects or data into organized categories, batches, or graduated scales based on physical traits (such as size, shape, or type).
groups.summary_zh: 按照规格尺寸、品质或属性等特征，将杂乱物品或数据有序地归类、挑选分档。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes organizing assorted entities by assembling like items together or filtering them by dimension/quality, distinct from abstract cataloguing.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重将杂乱实体按物理规格、品质或亲和度聚拢归整或分选过滤，区别于抽象的编目建档。
groups.nuance_en: group: assembling related entities into coherent clusters (students / items / symptoms) · size: physically sorting by dimensional measurements (timber / gravel / garments) · screen: filtering out unsuitable items via evaluation or testing (candidates / calls / blood) · grade: evaluating and assigning to qualitative echelons (produce / diamonds / meat) · classify: grouping under categorical frameworks (records / artifacts / taxa)
groups.nuance_zh: group: 将具亲和性的实体归聚成组 (students / items / symptoms) · size: 依据物理尺寸测量筛选分号 (timber / gravel / garments) · screen: 设卡排查以筛除不合格者 (candidates / calls / blood) · grade: 评估并按优劣分档定级 (produce / diamonds / meat) · classify: 纳入类别框架体系处理 (records / artifacts / taxa)

groups.name: Cleanse & Cull · 剔除与剥离残渣 (Weed, Flesh, Cull)
groups.tip: 剥掉表层或剔除多余无用部分

items.def_en: to remove or eliminate inferior, unwanted, or harmful members from a group
items.ex_en: The rigorous training program is designed to weed out unsuitable military recruits.
items.ex_zh: 严苛的训练项目旨在清除并淘汰不合格的新兵。

items.def_en: 1. (weed out) To remove unwanted or inferior people or things from a group. 2. To remove wild and unwanted plants from the ground or a garden.
items.ex_en: The selection committee must weed inferior submissions before publishing the final shortlist.
items.ex_zh: 选拔委员会在公布最终候选名单之前必须剔除较差的作品。

items.def_zh: 刮除（生皮上的）肉；充实，丰富（常与 out 连用）
items.def_en: 1. To remove adhering meat and fat from the underside of a skin or hide. 2. (flesh something out) To add more details or information to something to make it fuller.
items.ex_en: The tanner used a curved scraper to flesh the cowhide meticulously.
items.ex_zh: 制革工用一把弧形刮刀细致地刮除牛皮上的残肉与脂肪。

items.def_en: (+ away/down) to trim off an outer layer, skin, or excess surface material with a knife
items.ex_en: The chef used a sharp knife to pare away the bruised rind.
items.ex_zh: 厨师用一把锋利的刀削去受损碰伤的外皮。

items.def_zh: 剥除；剔除（残渣或无用部分）
items.def_en: (+ sth) separate and eliminate unwanted parts or impurities from an overall collection or substance
items.ex_en: Engineers worked diligently to strip out toxic impurities from the chemical compound.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们勤勉工作，从化合物中剥除并剔除有害杂质。

items.def_en: to pick out and eliminate weak, excess, or defective individuals from a population
items.ex_en: Rangers must cull diseased deer each winter to prevent forest-wide ecological collapse.
items.ex_zh: 护林员每年冬季必须剔除患病的鹿，以防止森林生态崩溃。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ off/away) to remove an unwanted surface substance or residue by drawing a hard edge across it
items.ex_en: He had to scrape stubborn barnacles away from the boat hull.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不从船体上刮除顽固附着的藤壶残渣。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) find and completely eliminate unwanted, inferior, or harmful elements
items.ex_en: The audit team was hired to root out systemic corporate embezzlement.
items.ex_zh: 审计小组受聘彻底根除并肃清公司内部的系统性挪用公款行为。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe manual, chemical, or selective processing to remove unwanted matter, residual flesh, impurities, or inferior elements from an organic substrate, collection, or hide.
groups.summary_zh: 从机体或群体中清理剔除残渣、赘肉或杂质。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on purging unwanted, defective, or surplus elements from a collective body to purify or optimize the remainder, differing from mere destructive trimming.
groups.desc_zh: 指从群体或整体中辨识并彻底剔除残次、杂质或多余成分以净化或优化主体，区别于普通的单纯裁剪或削减。
groups.nuance_en: weed out: systematically eliminating undesirable members or flaws (incompetents / errors / applicants) · cull: selecting and removing surplus or inferior stock from a population (herd / flock / collection) · pare: shaving down outer excess or cutting away unwanted material (costs / budget / nails) · root out: vigorously searching out and eradicating hidden evils (corruption / heresy / nests) · strip out: removing specific internal components or clutter completely (assets / costs / fittings)
groups.nuance_zh: weed out: 汰劣留良，系统性剔除杂质或不合格者 (incompetents / errors / applicants) · cull: 为控制数量或质量而选择性淘汰扑杀 (herd / flock / collection) · pare: 削减边沿多余部分或压缩冗余 (costs / budget / nails) · root out: 斩草除根式彻底挖除隐患 (corruption / heresy / nests) · strip out: 剥离、剔除特定内部核心构成 (assets / costs / fittings)

groups.name: Climb Clumsily or Mount Up · 爬上与吃力登攀 (Clamber, Scramble, Mount)
groups.tip: 手脚并用攀爬或跨骑登上

items.def_en: to climb up onto a horse, bicycle, or elevated platform
items.ex_en: The knight managed to mount his warhorse despite wearing heavy plate armour.
items.ex_zh: 尽管身着沉重的板甲，骑士还是设法骑上了战马。

items.def_en: (+ onto/to sth) climb up an incline, structure, or vehicle with difficulty, using hands and feet
items.ex_en: The children had to clamber up onto the high rocks carefully.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们只得手脚并用、小心翼翼地吃力爬上高高的岩石。

items.def_zh: 手脚并用攀上；快速爬上
items.def_en: (+ sth) move quickly and with awkward effort up a steep slope or rough surface
items.ex_en: Hikers had to scramble up the scree-covered ridge before dusk fell.
items.ex_zh: 徒步者们必须在黄昏降临前手脚并用快速爬上铺满碎石的山脊。

items.def_en: (+ up/onto) to climb or move hurriedly or clumsily over rough ground using both hands and feet
items.ex_en: The frightened goat began to scramble up the steep gravel embankment.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的山羊开始仓促攀登陡峭的碎石路堤。

items.def_en: To climb or move awkwardly and with difficulty, using your hands and feet.
items.ex_en: Tourists had to clamber over fallen logs along the overgrown forest trail.
items.ex_zh: 游客们不得不手脚并用吃力地翻过杂草丛生的林间倒木。

items.def_zh: 重新登上，再骑上（马或自行车）；重新安装，重装（底座、展品等）
items.def_en: 1. To get back onto a horse, bicycle, or other mount after getting off. 2. To fix or attach something again onto a frame, base, or support.
items.ex_en: After catching his breath, the fallen cyclist proceeded to remount his bike.
items.ex_zh: 在缓过气来之后，摔倒的骑手重新跨上了自行车。

items.def_en: (+ up) to climb quickly up a tree or pole using your arms and legs
items.ex_en: The daring boy managed to shin up the tall telephone pole quickly.
items.ex_zh: 那个胆大的男孩迅速手脚并用抱爬上了高高的电线杆。

items.def_en: to climb to the top of a high, steep wall, cliff, or obstacle
items.ex_en: Elite mountaineers prepared their equipment to scale the vertical granite cliff.
items.ex_zh: 精英登山队员准备好装备，准备攀登陡峭的花岗岩悬崖。

groups.summary_en: An agent moves upward or ascends onto an elevated object, surface, or mount, especially by using hands and feet or with physical exertion. 'Clamber' focuses on awkward, clumsy scrambling upward, whereas 'mount' denotes getting onto an animal, vehicle, or platform.
groups.summary_zh: 费力攀爬、手脚并用登上或跨骑上高处。
groups.desc_en: Depicts physically elevating oneself onto or over an obstacle using awkward, strenuous, or hands-and-feet effort, contrasting with effortless ascending or walking upstairs.
groups.desc_zh: 强调借助手脚并用、吃力挣扎或笨拙攀爬的姿势登临高处或越过障碍，区别于轻松平稳的登高或拾级而上（ascend/walk up）。
groups.nuance_en: scramble: frantic, hurried clambering using hands and feet over rough terrain (rocks / slope / embankment) · clamber: awkward, clumsy, and laborious climbing over obstacles (wall / carriage / wreckage) · mount: formal or deliberate stepping up onto an elevated platform or beast (horse / podium / bicycle) · scale: conquering and surmounting steep vertical barriers (heights / wall / peak) · shin: gripping with shins and arms to climb a narrow vertical column (tree / pole / drainpipe)
groups.nuance_zh: scramble: 手脚并用、仓促敏捷地在险峻地形攀爬 (rocks / slope / embankment) · clamber: 吃力笨拙、姿态不雅地攀爬阻碍物 (wall / carriage / wreckage) · mount: 庄重或有意识地跨上、登上坐骑或高台 (horse / podium / bicycle) · scale: 征服、翻越陡峭险峻的垂直高墙绝壁 (heights / wall / peak) · shin: 紧抱圆柱体顺势倒换四肢向上爬 (tree / pole / drainpipe)

groups.name: Cling & Cuddle · 紧抱与依偎 (Cling, Cuddle, Snuggle)
groups.tip: 紧紧抓附依附不脱手

items.def_en: (+ to/with sb) hold someone close or lie snugly together for warmth or affection
items.ex_en: The exhausted toddler wanted to cuddle up with her grandmother after dinner.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的幼儿晚饭后想依偎在祖母怀里取暖。

items.def_en: (+ to/with sb) settle into a warm, comfortable position close to someone
items.ex_en: The sisters would snuggle up together under the thick duvet every evening.
items.ex_zh: 每天晚上，两姐妹都会在厚厚的被子下紧贴蜷坐在一起。

items.def_en: 1. (+ up) To hold someone or an animal closely and affectionately in your arms, or to curl up comfortably together.
items.ex_en: The frightened puppy began to cuddle close to its mother for safety.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的小狗开始依偎紧贴着母亲寻求安全感。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ against/into) to rest warmly and closely against someone or something
items.ex_en: The sleepy child nestled her tired face against her father's broad shoulder.
items.ex_zh: 昏昏欲睡的孩子将疲倦的脸庞紧紧依偎在父亲宽厚的肩膀上。
items.ex2_en: The sleepy child nestled against her warm mother during the chilly winter evening.
items.ex2_zh: 在寒冷的冬夜里，瞌睡的孩子依偎在她温暖的母亲身旁。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ up/into) to settle into a warm, comfortable position close to someone or something
items.ex_en: The kitten liked to snuggle into the pile of fresh warm laundry.
items.ex_zh: 小猫喜欢舒适地蜷缩依偎在刚洗好、暖烘烘的衣物堆里。

items.def_en: (+ to sb/sth) hold on tightly to someone or something for physical security or support
items.ex_en: The scared sailor had to cling on tightly to the slippery mast.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的水手不得不死死抓住湿滑的桅杆以保安全。

items.def_zh: 挤在一起；蜷缩缩成一团
items.def_en: to crowd close together, often for warmth or protection
items.ex_en: Shivering refugees had to huddle together against the biting winter gale.
items.ex_zh: 发抖的难民们不得不挤在一起以抵御刺骨的冬日寒风。
items.ex2_en: The shepherd huddled his shivering sheep tightly together inside the protective barn.
items.ex2_zh: 牧羊人把瑟瑟发抖的羊群紧紧聚集在具有保护作用的谷仓内。

items.def_zh: 紧紧抓住，抓牢；黏着，附着；依恋，坚持
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) To hold onto someone or something very tightly, or to stick closely to a surface. 2. (+ to) To refuse to give up an old belief, hope, or habit.
items.ex_en: Damp fabric tended to cling tightly to the athlete during heavy downpours.
items.ex_zh: 在暴雨倾盆中，湿漉漉的布料紧紧贴在运动员的身上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe bodily postures of holding someone or something close out of affection, comfort, fear, or a desire for physical security.
groups.summary_zh: 出于依恋、寻求温暖或安全感而紧密贴近或拥抱。
groups.desc_en: Describes drawing tight to an object or living being for protection, warmth, or intimacy, contrasting with mere touching, grappling, or trapping.
groups.desc_zh: 指为寻求安全感、温暖或亲密而紧紧贴近、抱合或依偎，区别于单纯的接触、缠斗或禁锢。
groups.nuance_en: cling: holding fast tenaciously due to fear, attachment, or physical cohesion (hope / clothes / mother) · cuddle: holding affectionately in one's arms for mutual warmth (baby / partner / puppy) · snuggle: curling into a cozy, warm, and compact position against someone or something (duvet / blanket / sibling) · nestle: settling snugly and protectedly into a sheltered nook (valley / cottage / cheek) · huddle: crowding close together defensively against cold or danger (crowd / players / sheep)
groups.nuance_zh: cling: 出于恐惧、不舍或附着力而死死抓住不放 (hope / clothes / mother) · cuddle: 充满爱意地拥入怀中取暖爱抚 (baby / partner / puppy) · snuggle: 舒适缱绻地蜷缩依偎在身旁或被窝里 (duvet / blanket / sibling) · nestle: 安详地半隐半偎在庇护所或柔软角落 (valley / cottage / cheek) · huddle: 因寒冷或恐惧而防卫性地蜷缩挤作一团 (crowd / players / sheep)

groups.name: Clot & Congeal · 凝结与增稠 (Thicken, Coagulate, Clot)
groups.tip: 流体聚集成块，由稀变稠变硬

items.def_en: become more viscous or make a liquid denser and semi-solid
items.ex_en: Allow the savory gravy to simmer until it begins to thicken up.
items.ex_zh: 让美味的肉汁文火微沸，直至开始变稠。
items.ex2_en: The talented chef added cornstarch to thicken up the simmering beef stew.
items.ex2_zh: 这位才华横溢的大厨加入了玉米淀粉，以使微沸的炖牛肉汤汁变稠。

items.def_en: form into thick semi-solid clots
items.ex_en: Without regular flushing, residual slurry will quickly clot up the entire pipe.
items.ex_zh: 如果不定期冲洗，残留的泥浆很快就会凝结成块堵塞整根管道。
items.ex2_en: Old engine oil will clot up if stored in freezing temperatures outside.
items.ex2_zh: 旧机油如果在室外冰冻的温度下储存就会结块变稠。

items.def_en: turn into or assume a jelly-like, congealed consistency
items.ex_en: The gelatin mixture will jell up nicely after chilling in the refrigerator.
items.ex_zh: 明胶混合液在冰箱冷藏后会很好地凝成果冻状。
items.ex2_en: Chilling the fruit puree will jell up the mixture into a firm dessert.
items.ex2_zh: 将果泥冷藏会使混合物凝结成一种紧实的甜点。

items.def_en: to form soft, solid lumps from a liquid, or cause blood, cream, etc. to thicken into lumps
items.ex_en: The cut bled freely at first, but the blood soon began to clot naturally.
items.ex_zh: 伤口起初流血不止，但血液很快就开始自然凝结了。
items.ex2_en: Special medical agents clot the blood rapidly to prevent life-threatening surgical bleeding.
items.ex2_zh: 特殊的医用药剂可以使血液迅速凝固，以防止危及生命的手术出血。

items.def_zh: （使）变浓，（使）变稠，（使）变厚；（情节等）变得复杂
items.def_en: 1. to become thicker, denser, or heavier, or make something thicker. 2. to become more complex or intense.
items.ex_en: Add two spoons of cornstarch while stirring constantly until the rich gravy begins to thicken.
items.ex_zh: 加入两勺玉米淀粉并不断搅拌，直到浓稠的肉汁开始变厚。
items.ex2_en: The chef added cold butter to thicken the rich mushroom cream sauce.
items.ex2_zh: 厨师加入了冷黄油，使浓郁的蘑菇奶油酱汁变得更加浓稠。

items.def_en: to separate into curds or lumps, typically as milk turns sour or sauce breaks
items.ex_en: Never add lemon juice to hot milk, or the liquid will curdle immediately.
items.ex_zh: 千万不要在热牛奶里加柠檬汁，否则液体会立刻凝成乳块。
items.ex2_en: Adding excessive vinegar will curdle the warm fresh milk in the bowl.
items.ex2_zh: 加入过量的醋会使碗中温热的鲜牛奶结块变酸。

items.def_en: to solidify or become viscous and jelly-like, especially on cooling
items.ex_en: The residual fat from the roast beef began to congeal into a pale jelly.
items.ex_zh: 烤牛肉渗出的残留油脂开始凝结成一层浅色的胶状物。
items.ex2_en: Cold weather will quickly congeal the melted grease on the frying pan.
items.ex2_zh: 寒冷的天气会使煎锅上融化的油脂迅速凝固。

items.def_en: to change from a fluid into a thickened, curdlike mass, especially by chemical or heat action
items.ex_en: The application of mild heat caused the egg proteins in the mixture to coagulate.
items.ex_zh: 施加微热使混合物中的蛋清蛋白质凝结成块。
items.ex2_en: Warm milk will coagulate naturally once acidic lemon juice is introduced.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦加入酸性柠檬汁，温牛奶就会自然凝固。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe fluid substances (especially blood, milk, or culinary liquids) undergoing a colloidal transformation into a semi-solid or gelatinous consistency. They contrast along register and physiological vs. culinary contexts.
groups.summary_zh: 描述液体（尤指血液、胶体或乳液）聚集、稠化并形成半固态块状。
groups.desc_en: Marks the phase transition of a fluid becoming viscous, semi-solid, or gummy through chemical or physical processes, distinct from freezing solid into ice.
groups.desc_zh: 指液体通过化学或物理反应变稠、转为半固体或结块的相变过程，区别于单纯降温结冰（freeze）。
groups.nuance_en: thicken: general increase in viscosity or body of a liquid (sauce / soup / mixture) · coagulate: physiological or biochemical transformation into a solid jelly (blood / protein / latex) · clot: aggregating into localized semi-solid lumps or obstructing flow (blood / milk / cream) · congeal: solidifying or setting into a jellylike mass as temperature drops (fat / grease / blood) · curdle: separating into sour curds and watery whey (milk / cream / sauce)
groups.nuance_zh: thicken: 最通用的液体稠度或浓度增加 (sauce / soup / mixture) · coagulate: 生理或生化上的整体凝结成胶状 (blood / protein / latex) · clot: 局部积聚抱团成血块或乳块堵塞流动 (blood / milk / cream) · congeal: 尤指随温度下降油脂等固化发硬 (fat / grease / blood) · curdle: 变酸变质而析出水乳分离的凝块 (milk / cream / sauce)

groups.name: Coax & Wheedle · 劝诱与哄劝 (Coax, Cajole, Wheedle)
groups.tip: 用甜言蜜语讨好哄劝或激发他人行动

items.def_en: (+ sb into doing sth) persuade someone gently or skillfully to do something
items.ex_en: My brother managed to talk me into lending him my car for the weekend.
items.ex_zh: 我哥哥设法说服了我，让我在周末把车借给他开。

items.def_en: To persuade someone gently and patiently to do something; to manipulate something carefully into a desired position.
items.ex_en: The nurse patiently coaxed the frightened little girl into swallowing her liquid medicine.
items.ex_zh: 护士耐心地哄着那个受惊的小女孩把药水喝了下去。

items.def_en: (+ sb) be exceptionally nice or flatter someone to persuade them to do what you want
items.ex_en: She tried to butter up her manager before asking for a substantial pay raise.
items.ex_zh: 在提出大幅加薪的要求之前，她极力巴结讨好自己的经理。

items.def_en: to coax or entice someone with sweet talk, mild compliments, or subtle flattery
items.ex_en: The courtier sought to blandish the young monarch with flattering compliments and soft promises.
items.ex_zh: 侍臣试图用阿谀奉承和轻柔的许诺来讨好年轻的君王。

items.def_en: To persuade someone to do something by making promises or using flattery.
items.ex_en: The diplomat skillfully cajoled the reluctant delegates into signing the interim peace accord.
items.ex_zh: 外交官巧妙地劝诱勉强的代表们签署了临时和平协议。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ into/out of) to obtain something or persuade someone through continuous flattering words
items.ex_en: The shrewd lobbyist tried to wheedle sensitive commercial details out of the junior minister.
items.ex_zh: 那名老练的说客试图用甜言蜜语从初级部长口中套出敏感的商业细节。

items.def_zh: 激励，激起，促使迅速行动；镀锌
items.def_en: 1. To shock or stimulate someone into taking action. 2. To cover metal with a protective layer of zinc.
items.ex_en: The unexpected electoral defeat served to galvanise the opposition party into immediate radical reform.
items.ex_zh: 意料之外的选举失利促使反对党迅速行动起来进行彻底改革。

items.def_en: (+ into) to entice or lure someone cleverly into doing something via artful deception or charm
items.ex_en: He managed to inveigle his wealthy acquaintance into financing his risky business venture.
items.ex_zh: 他设法诱使他那位富有的熟人为他风险极高的商业投资提供资金。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe using gentle persistence, flattery, soothing tones, or artful blandishments to persuade someone to do something they are initially hesitant to do.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过甜言蜜语、奉承诱导或温和软磨硬泡来劝诱就范。
groups.desc_en: Signifies inducing someone to do something through gentle persuasion, flattery, persistence, or seductive artifice, distinct from blunt commanding or forceful ordering.
groups.desc_zh: 指运用温柔劝导、甜言蜜语、软磨硬泡或诱导技巧打动对方，区别于直白的下令或粗暴要求。
groups.nuance_en: coax: patiently and gently persuading or manipulating someone/something into a state (child / confession / engine) · cajole: persistent teasing flattery and honeyed words to overcome reluctance (voters / boss / donor) · wheedle: whining, ingratiating entreaty to extract a favor (money / permission / favor) · inveigle: cunningly and deceitfully luring someone into a trap or agreement (investors / heiress / stranger) · butter up: shamelessly flattering beforehand to soften someone for a request (client / supervisor / in-laws)
groups.nuance_zh: coax: 耐心温和、循循善诱地引导或调试 (child / confession / engine) · cajole: 用连哄带捧的好话磨人以克服对方顾虑 (voters / boss / donor) · wheedle: 谄媚讨好、死缠烂打地央求索取 (money / permission / favor) · inveigle: 设套巧妙诱骗使其在不知不觉中就范 (investors / heiress / stranger) · butter up: 预先大拍马屁以便顺理成章提出要求 (client / supervisor / in-laws)

groups.name: Coerce & Constrain Action · 施压与强力迫使 (Pressure, Necessitate, Compel)
groups.tip: 施加外力强使服从

items.def_en: (+ sb) treat someone unfairly by making unreasonable demands on their time or service
items.ex_en: She felt constantly put upon because her colleagues always dumped their tedious chores onto her.
items.ex_zh: 她感到总被苛待苛求，因为同事们总是把琐碎乏味的杂事推给她。

items.raw_cluster: 使遭受与迫使 Subject & Expose
items.def_zh: 使遭受，使承受；使服从，使隶属
items.def_en: to make someone or something experience, suffer, or be affected by something unpleasant; bring under control
items.ex_en: The laboratory subjected the experimental alloy to extreme temperatures to test its overall durability.
items.ex_zh: 实验室使该实验合金经受极端温度，以测试其整体耐用性。

items.def_en: (+ into) to rush or coerce someone into doing something without fair consideration
items.ex_en: The committee tried to railroad the local residents into accepting the controversial highway project.
items.ex_zh: 委员会试图仓促逼迫当地居民接受这项备受争议的公路项目。

items.def_en: (formal) to make something necessary or unavoidable; require
items.ex_en: Unforeseen structural damage in the foundation will necessitate extensive and costly structural repairs.
items.ex_zh: 地基中未预见到的结构性损坏将迫使进行昂贵且全面的结构修复。

items.def_en: (+ sb) exert strong pressure or intimidation on someone to compel them to comply
items.ex_en: She had to lean heavily on her family during those tough months.
items.ex_zh: 在那段艰难的岁月里，她不得不极度依赖家人的支持。

items.def_en: To persuade or force someone to do something by making them feel anxious or obliged.
items.ex_en: Senior executives continued to pressure the lead scientist to approve the questionable safety report.
items.ex_zh: 高管们继续对首席科学家施压，迫使其批准那份存疑的安全报告。

items.def_en: to make someone do something by using legal authority, irresistible power, or circumstance
items.ex_en: The court issued an injunction to compel the defaulting tenant to surrender the keys.
items.ex_zh: 法院下达了一项禁令，强行要求违约租户交出钥匙。

items.def_en: (+ into) to force an unwilling person to do something by using threats or manipulation
items.ex_en: The corrupt officer attempted to coerce the vulnerable witness into signing a false confession.
items.ex_zh: 那名腐败警官企图胁迫处于弱势的证人签署一份虚假的供词。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate applying psychological, legal, circumstantial, or physical duress upon an agent to dictate or enforce their compliance.
groups.summary_zh: 通过心理、形势、法律或外力压制手段，促使或逼迫当事人屈服服从。
groups.desc_en: Captures the application of overpowering external pressure, leverage, or absolute necessity to compel an unwilling agent, contrasting with voluntary acquiescence.
groups.desc_zh: 指施加压倒性的外部压力、权力杠杆或客观必然性强迫当事人遵从，区别于自愿同意或温和商议。
groups.nuance_en: compel: inexorably driving someone by overwhelming moral, legal, or physical force (submission / obedience / testimony) · coerce: enforcing compliance through intimidation, threats, or brute force (confession / compliance / cooperation) · pressure: exerting persistent psychological, social, or economic strain (government / peers / witness) · railroad: rushing someone unfairly into a decision without due process (bill / suspect / defendant) · lean on: applying targeted informal intimidation or leverage to force cooperation (informant / witness / debtor)
groups.nuance_zh: compel: 道德、法律或客观必然性强力驱使不得不为 (submission / obedience / testimony) · coerce: 运用恐吓、威胁或武力强行逼迫就范 (confession / compliance / cooperation) · pressure: 持续施加心理、社会或经济层面的高压 (government / peers / witness) · railroad: 剥夺抗辩权、粗暴仓促地强行定罪或推行 (bill / suspect / defendant) · lean on: 暗中施压施暴或敲打以逼其合作 (informant / witness / debtor)

groups.name: Collide & Ram · 猛撞与冲击 (Bump, Ram, Butt)
groups.tip: 轻微磕碰颠簸的物理碰撞

items.def_zh: 碰撞，撞上；颠簸前行；碰伤
items.def_en: 1. to hit or knock against something accidentally, usually with light force. 2. to travel along in an uneven, bouncing way.
items.ex_en: I accidentally bumped my head against the open cupboard door while cleaning up.
items.ex_zh: 打扫卫生时，我不小心把头磕在了开着的橱柜门上。

items.def_en: [I/T] to push, poke, or butt gently with the head or a tool
items.ex_en: The playful young goat began to bunt its small head against the wooden gate.
items.ex_zh: 调皮的小山羊开始用它的小脑袋轻轻顶撞那扇木门。

items.def_en: [I/T] to hit or push someone or something with the head or horns
items.ex_en: The enraged ram lowered its horns and prepared to butt the aggressive trespasser.
items.ex_zh: 那只被激怒的公羊压低了角，准备猛冲顶撞那个具侵略性的闯入者。

items.def_en: (+ sth) collide violently and uncontrollably with a person, vehicle, or barrier
items.ex_en: The speeding pickup lost traction and plowed into the solid concrete security barrier.
items.ex_zh: 超速行驶的皮卡失去了抓地力，猛撞在坚固的混凝土安全护栏上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) strike something suddenly and with immense momentum
items.ex_en: The runaway delivery van skidded on the wet asphalt and slammed into a lamp post.
items.ex_zh: 那辆失控的送货面包车在湿滑的沥青路面上打滑，重重撞上了路灯柱。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ into) to violently crash or drive forcefully into someone or something
items.ex_en: The high-speed pursuit ended when the stolen car smashed into a brick retaining wall.
items.ex_zh: 高速追逐在失窃车辆猛撞上一堵砖石挡土墙后宣告结束。
items.ex2_en: The angry protester smashed the heavy brick into the shop display window.
items.ex2_zh: 愤怒的抗议者将沉重的砖头砸向了商店的陈列橱窗。

items.def_en: 1. to hit or drive into something with heavy force. 2. to push or force something into a place firmly.
items.ex_en: The heavy armored vehicle was ordered to ram the fortified perimeter gate at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 那辆重型装甲车奉命在黎明时分猛力撞击加固的外围大门。

items.def_en: (+ sth) crash into something with violent destructive force
items.ex_en: A disoriented driver failed to brake in time and smashed into the parked cruiser.
items.ex_zh: 一名神志恍惚的司机未能及时刹车，轰然撞上了停着的巡逻警车。

groups.summary_en: A vehicle, person, or object strikes another forcibly. Verbs contrast light or incidental accidental bumping with deliberate, heavy, head-on battering designed to smash through obstacles.
groups.summary_zh: 以力撞击目标，从轻微磕碰过渡到故意猛冲撞击。
groups.desc_en: Denotes violent, sudden physical impact where a moving body strikes another with substantial mass or momentum, differing from light touching or controlled brushing.
groups.desc_zh: 指运动实体携带巨大质量或动量对另一物体施加剧烈、突发性的物理撞击，区别于轻触或受控摩擦。
groups.nuance_en: bump: light, inadvertent, or low-speed collision without severe destruction (car / head / elbow) · ram: intentionally and forcefully striking head-on with heavy mass (gate / wall / ship) · butt: striking with the head or horns (goat / opponent / door) · smash into: crashing into a barrier at high speed with shattering violence (tree / wall / storefront) · plow into: hurtling uncontrollably and deeply through obstacles (crowd / barricade / snowbank)
groups.nuance_zh: bump: 低速、轻微或无意间的碰撞颠簸 (car / head / elbow) · ram: 用重物故意迎面猛烈撞击击溃 (gate / wall / ship) · butt: 用头顶或角向前猛顶撞 (goat / opponent / door) · smash into: 高速猛烈撞向障碍物致使其粉碎 (tree / wall / storefront) · plow into: 势不可挡、失控般深深犁入冲散障碍 (crowd / barricade / snowbank)

groups.name: Come or Bring to a Standstill · 停顿与停滞 (Halt, Stall, Arrest)
groups.tip: 运动中断戛然而止

items.def_en: to stop or bring to a standstill the progress, motion, or spread of something
items.ex_en: Prompt international intervention helped to arrest the alarming spread of the infectious respiratory disease.
items.ex_zh: 及时的国际干预有助于遏制这种传染性呼吸道疾病令人担忧的蔓延。

items.def_en: (of a vehicle or moving person) to come to a halt
items.ex_en: The black limousine pulled up smoothly outside the entrance of the luxury downtown hotel.
items.ex_zh: 那辆黑色加长轿车平稳地停在了市中心豪华酒店的入口外。

items.def_en: to slow down gradually and then stop completely due to friction or breakdown
items.ex_en: Production across the manufacturing plant ground to a halt following the catastrophic power outage.
items.ex_zh: 灾难性的断电发生后，整个制造工厂的生产陷入了彻底停顿。

items.def_en: cease moving forward or stop operating
items.ex_en: All naval operations came to a halt during the unprecedented severe tropical storm.
items.ex_zh: 在这场前所未有的特大热带风暴期间，所有海军行动都停止了。

items.def_en: (of an engine or machine) suddenly break down, stall, or stop working
items.ex_en: My vintage car engine unexpectedly conked out right in the middle of evening traffic.
items.ex_zh: 我那辆老式汽车的发动机在晚高峰车流正中突然熄火停转了。

items.def_en: (of a vehicle) slow down and come to a complete stop at a particular place
items.ex_en: The legal team drew up a comprehensive contract for the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队为此次收购拟定了一份详尽的合同。

items.def_en: To stop moving or progressing, or to make someone or something stop.
items.ex_en: The government ordered all construction work to halt until safety inspections were thoroughly conducted.
items.ex_zh: 政府下令所有施工作业全部暂停，直到全面完成安全检查。
items.ex2_en: The traffic police officer raised his hand to halt the oncoming vehicles.
items.ex2_zh: 交警举起手，拦停了迎面驶来的车辆。

items.def_zh: （使发动机等）熄火，抛锚；（使进程）停顿，拖延；拖延，支吾
items.def_en: 1. (of an engine or vehicle) To stop suddenly, or cause to stop suddenly. 2. To stop or cause a process to stop making progress. 3. To deliberately delay doing something or answering.
items.ex_en: The rookie driver panicked at the steep incline and accidentally stalled the manual car.
items.ex_zh: 新手司机在陡坡上惊慌失措，不小心让这辆手动挡汽车熄火了。
items.ex2_en: The old truck engine stalled suddenly on the steep mountain road.
items.ex2_zh: 那辆老卡车的引擎在陡峭的山路上突然熄火了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe an agent bringing an ongoing motion, progress, or engine to a sudden or temporary stop, or a moving entity/process stopping of its own accord. While 'halt' denotes a decisive or formal stop, 'stall' emphasizes involuntary loss of momentum or intentional delay.
groups.summary_zh: 描述行进、行动或运转进程突然或暂时中断、停顿。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the deceleration, mechanical failure, or deliberate halting that brings motion or progress to an absolute standstill, contrasting with merely slowing down.
groups.desc_zh: 指因制动、机械故障或外力干预导致运动或进程彻底停顿或陷于停滞，区别于单纯的减速缓冲。
groups.nuance_en: halt: abrupt or definitive stopping of movement or operations (troops / production / advance) · stall: temporary arrest due to mechanical failure, loss of lift, or delaying tactics (engine / negotiations / car) · arrest: forceful seizure that stops a biological, physical, or social process (development / decline / heart) · pull up: bringing a moving vehicle or steed to a controlled stop (car / horse / taxi) · conk out: colloquial sudden breakdown or expiration from exhaustion (engine / battery / machine)
groups.nuance_zh: halt: 明确、果断地下令停止或行动戛然而止 (troops / production / advance) · stall: 机械失速熄火、拖延使进程陷入停顿 (engine / negotiations / car) · arrest: 强力遏制、阻断生理或发展进程 (development / decline / heart) · pull up: 驾驶员或骑手有控制地带住缰绳或刹停车辆 (car / horse / taxi) · conk out: (口语) 机械突然彻底罢工坏掉或体力耗尽 (engine / battery / machine)

groups.name: Command & Marshal · 统率与节制 (Direct, General, Marshal)
groups.tip: 发号施令指引方向

items.def_en: to steer, lead, or direct an organization, project, or crew
items.ex_en: She was chosen to helm the multinational corporation through its critical restructuring phase.
items.ex_zh: 她被选定掌舵这家跨国公司，引领其度过关键的重组阶段。

items.def_en: be the person who makes the critical decisions and directs what should be done
items.ex_en: Everyone in the office knows that the senior partner still calls the shots here.
items.ex_zh: 办公室里的每个人都知道，高级合伙人仍然在这里发号施令并掌控大局。

items.def_en: (+ sth) take control or operational command of an organization, operation, or group
items.ex_en: The seasoned commander arrived at dawn to take over the ongoing rescue operation.
items.ex_zh: 那位经验丰富的指挥官于黎明抵达，接管了正在进行的救援行动。

items.def_zh: 指挥，统率，指导；命令，指示；导演（戏剧、电影等）；指引（方向）
items.def_en: 1. To control, manage, or lead someone or something with authority. 2. To give an authoritative instruction or command to someone. 3. To be in charge of making a film, play, or show.
items.ex_en: The seasoned general arrived at headquarters to direct the complex troop movements personally.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的老将抵达总部，亲自统率调度复杂的部队调动。

items.def_en: to gather together and organize people, troops, or resources in an orderly way for action
items.ex_en: The strategic command managed to marshal adequate logistical supplies ahead of the winter offensive.
items.ex_zh: 战略指挥部在冬季攻势发起前成功统筹调度了充足的后勤物资。

items.def_zh: 统率，指挥（军队等）；担任统帅
items.def_en: To act as a general; to command, lead, or direct military forces.
items.ex_en: The decorated veteran was appointed to general the entire multinational peacekeeping force abroad.
items.ex_zh: 这位战功赫赫的老将获任统率海外的整支多国维和部队。

items.def_en: to act as the energetic front-line leader of a campaign, offensive, or initiative
items.ex_en: The prominent environmental scientist was selected to spearhead the nationwide carbon reduction initiative.
items.ex_zh: 那位著名的环境科学家被选定带头领导全国范围的减碳倡议行动。

items.def_en: to take control of resources, vehicles, or leadership authority arbitrarily for operational needs
items.ex_en: Emergency military authorities had to commandeer private four-wheel-drive vehicles to navigate flooded rural roads.
items.ex_zh: 紧急军事当局不得不征用私人的四驱车辆以在被洪水淹没的乡村道路上通行。

groups.summary_en: A superior leader or military commander exercises high-level tactical oversight, marshaling personnel, resources, and movements toward a concerted strategic objective. Nuances span operational direction to grand battlefield generalship.
groups.summary_zh: 以统帅或指挥官身份全局调度兵力、部署资源并掌控行动全局。
groups.desc_en: Represents the exercise of supreme authority to strategically orchestrate, steer, and deploy troops, agents, or assets, distinct from frontline physical fighting.
groups.desc_zh: 指运用统御权威对军队、资源或行动进行战略统筹、指派与调度，区别于一线的冲锋陷阵。
groups.nuance_en: direct: overseeing, guiding, and giving authoritative instructions to operations (campaign / traffic / enterprise) · marshal: gathering, arranging, and deploying dispersed forces or resources methodically (evidence / forces / arguments) · helm: actively steering and leading an organization as captain (ship / project / company) · spearhead: taking the lead at the cutting edge of an initiative (assault / reform / offensive) · commandeer: authoritatively seizing private resources for military or urgent use (vehicle / building / supplies)
groups.nuance_zh: direct: 指导、统率并向运作下发权威指令 (campaign / traffic / enterprise) · marshal: 将分散的兵力、论据或资源井然有序地聚拢调度 (evidence / forces / arguments) · helm: 居于掌舵统领地位驾驭局势 (ship / project / company) · spearhead: 一马当先带头冲锋或发起先锋倡议 (assault / reform / offensive) · commandeer: 依战时或紧急特权强行征用 (vehicle / building / supplies)

groups.name: Compile & Catalogue · 编纂与编目 (Compile, Index, Tabulate)
groups.tip: 编年记载与编目建档

items.def_en: to make an index for a book or list of items, or enter something systematically into an index
items.ex_en: The professional editor took three whole weeks to index the comprehensive reference manual.
items.ex_zh: 专业编辑整整花了三周时间为这部详尽的参考手册编排索引。

items.def_en: (+ sth) prepare and write out a formal document, catalog, list, or plan
items.ex_en: The legal team drew up a comprehensive contract for the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队为此次收购拟定了一份详尽的合同。

items.def_en: to make a complete, detailed list of goods, assets, or possessions
items.ex_en: Auditors arrived at the regional depot to inventory all stored high-value telecommunications hardware.
items.ex_zh: 审计人员抵达区域仓库，对所有入库的高价值电信硬件进行了全面清点盘存。

items.def_en: to produce a book, list, or report by assembling information gathered from many sources
items.ex_en: The research assistant spent months compiling data from various historical government archives worldwide.
items.ex_zh: 研究助理花了数月时间汇编整理来自世界各地不同历史政府档案的数据。

items.def_zh: 将……载入编年史，按时间顺序详细记录
items.def_en: To record a series of events in writing in the order in which they happened.
items.ex_en: The historian devoted his life to chronicle the tumultuous decline of the ancient empire.
items.ex_zh: 这位历史学家毕生致力于按编年顺序详细记录那个古代帝国的动荡衰亡。

items.def_zh: 将……编入目录，为……编制目录；系统记录，列举
items.def_en: To list, classify, and record items systematically in a catalogue.
items.ex_en: The chief curator began to catalogue the newly acquired rare manuscripts systematically.
items.ex_zh: 首席馆长开始系统地将新购得的珍贵手稿编入藏品目录中。

items.def_zh: 将……编入目录，为……编制目录；系统记录，列举
items.def_en: To list, classify, and record items systematically in a catalog.
items.ex_en: The botanical team worked diligently to catalog all endangered plant species found within the reserve.
items.ex_zh: 植物学团队辛勤工作，为保护区内发现的所有濒危植物物种编制了系统目录。

items.def_en: to arrange data or facts in tabular form or columns
items.ex_en: The research team will tabulate the clinical survey results into clear statistical columns.
items.ex_zh: 研究小组将把临床调查结果制成清晰的统计数据表格。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the systematic gathering, ordering, and listing of historical events, archival records, or inventory items into structured compendia or formal registries.
groups.summary_zh: 指将历史事件、档案或文献条目按序搜集、整理编排成册或建档编目。
groups.desc_en: Involves collecting, structuring, and systematically recording disparate documents, data, or items into an authoritative inventory or unified work, differing from composing original creative text.
groups.desc_zh: 指把分散的文献、数据或实物搜集、梳理并系统登记为规整目录或编纂成果，区别于原创性构思与创作。
groups.nuance_en: compile: collecting and assembling material from diverse sources into a whole (data / report / anthology) · catalogue: systematically listing items with descriptive details (holdings / artifacts / exhibits) · index: generating an alphabetical or thematic lookup register for quick retrieval (book / database / files) · tabulate: arranging raw quantitative or categorical data into ordered tables (results / figures / votes) · chronicle: recording historical events sequentially in chronological order (history / reign / expedition)
groups.nuance_zh: compile: 广罗散件并汇总整编成册 (data / report / anthology) · catalogue: 详尽且具说明性地分门别类编目登记 (holdings / artifacts / exhibits) · index: 提炼编制便于检索的主题或字母索引 (book / database / files) · tabulate: 将杂乱原始数据排列成矩阵图表 (results / figures / votes) · chronicle: 忠实按编年体顺序顺次记述史实 (history / reign / expedition)

groups.name: Condense & Recapitulate · 概括与提炼总结 (Summarize, Recapitulate, Sum up)
groups.tip: 归纳核心要点并做整体收尾

items.def_en: 1. To state or express the main points of something concisely (often used as 'sum up'). 2. To calculate the total of.
items.ex_en: In a brief final sentence, the speaker sum the entire debate with absolute clarity.
