groups.nuance_en: beg: ask earnestly or humiliatingly for food, mercy, or favor (pardon / mercy / bread) · plead: offer desperate, impassioned emotional or legal appeals (guilty / ignorance / for help) · implore: call upon someone with tearful, urgent distress (mercy / judge / help) · beseech: urge or entreat with profound humility and devotion (aid / king / lord) · supplicate: pray or appeal from a kneeling, lowly posture (deity / ruler / forgiveness)
groups.nuance_zh: beg: 屈尊哀告或祈求怜悯施舍 (pardon / mercy / bread) · plead: 苦苦恳求或在法庭上极力辩解 (guilty / ignorance / for help) · implore: 痛切甚至涕泪俱下地急迫哀求 (mercy / judge / help) · beseech: 极尽虔诚与卑微地请求 (aid / king / lord) · supplicate: 伏地长跪向神明或权贵叩拜乞恩 (deity / ruler / forgiveness)

groups.name: Despise & Disdain · 鄙视与蔑视 (Despise, Disdain, Scorn)
groups.tip: 居高临下瞧不起与冷笑鄙薄

items.def_en: to regard someone as socially, intellectually, or morally inferior
items.ex_en: She never looks down on anyone just because they come from a humble background.
items.ex_zh: 她绝不会仅仅因为别人出身平凡而看不起对方。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) regard someone or something as inferior, worthless, or contemptible
items.ex_en: Arrogant aristocrats often look down upon hard-working laborers in the city streets.
items.ex_zh: 傲慢的贵族往往看不起城市街头辛勤劳作的工人。

items.def_en: (+ sth/sb) reject or show overt disdain for something as being beneath one's dignity
items.ex_en: The snobbish critic will turn up his nose at any modest independent production.
items.ex_zh: 那位势利的评论家对任何小成本独立制作都嗤之以鼻。

items.def_en: to express a low opinion of someone or something; to belittle
items.ex_en: It is petty and unprofessional to disparage your predecessor during public conferences.
items.ex_zh: 在公开会议上贬低你的前任既狭隘又显得不专业。

items.def_en: To dislike and look down on someone or something with strong contempt.
items.ex_en: Honest merchants despise deceitful practices that exploit vulnerable and uninformed elderly customers.
items.ex_zh: 诚信的商人鄙视那些利用弱势且不知情的老年客户的欺诈行为。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To regard or treat someone or something with contempt as unworthy of respect. 2. To refuse or reject something because of feeling superior.
items.ex_en: The proud noble seemed to disdain all forms of common manual labor.
items.ex_zh: 这位心高气傲的贵族似乎不屑于参与任何普通的体力劳动。

items.def_zh: 鄙视，轻蔑；不屑接受，摒弃
items.def_en: 1. To feel or show contempt and disdain for someone or something. 2. To reject or refuse something with contempt.
items.ex_en: The austere scholar chose to scorn worldly accolades and lucrative commercial offers.
items.ex_zh: 这位严谨的学者断然摒弃世俗的名誉和诱人的商业邀约。

items.def_zh: 傲慢地摒弃；轻蔑地拒绝
items.def_en: to reject with contempt or disdain, especially an offer, person, or overture
items.ex_en: The reclusive poet chose to spurn every flattering invitation from the royal court.
items.ex_zh: 这位隐居的诗人断然拒绝了王室发来的每一封奉承的请帖。

groups.summary_en: Verbs signifying an attitude of extreme disregard, viewing a target as worthless, despicable, or far beneath one's dignity and standards.
groups.summary_zh: 表示将某人或某物视为无价值、低下或不值一顾的蔑视态度。
groups.desc_en: Denotes viewing or treating someone or something as beneath one's dignity or completely unworthy of respect, unlike neutral rejection or objective criticism which evaluates utility or truth.
groups.desc_zh: 指将人或事物视为低人一等或毫无尊严价值的傲慢排斥，区别于客观批判或中性的拒绝选拔。
groups.nuance_en: despise: deep moral contempt or revulsion (cowardice / hypocrisy) · disdain: aloof sense of superiority and refusal to stoop (offer / small talk) · scorn: vocal, derisive rejection of worthlessness (advise / overtures) · spurn: contemptuous, overt refusal of an advance (advances / plea / offer)
groups.nuance_zh: despise: 发自内心的道德鄙夷与厌弃 (cowardice / hypocrisy) · disdain: 自持清高而不屑一顾 (offer / small talk) · scorn: 嘲弄蔑视且公然嗤之以鼻 (advise / overtures) · spurn: 傲慢轻蔑地断然回绝 (advances / plea / offer)

groups.name: Deter & Ward off · 威慑防范与阻止侵扰 (Deter, Dissuade, Ward off)
groups.tip: 预先防范或威慑以避灾害

items.def_zh: 挡住，防住，避开（危险、厄运）
items.def_en: to prevent someone or something bad from affecting, damaging, or reaching one
items.ex_en: Doctors advise getting vaccinated early to ward off severe seasonal respiratory infections.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议尽早接种疫苗，以防范严重的季节性呼吸道感染。

items.def_en: to scare away potential intruders or threats by displaying formidable force
items.ex_en: The loud automated alarm managed to frighten off intruders before police arrived.
items.ex_zh: 刺耳的自动警报器在警察赶到之前成功吓跑了入侵者。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) deter an intruder, attacker, or competitor by intimidating them
items.ex_en: Aggressive guard dogs patrolling the perimeter will scare off potential trespassers effectively.
items.ex_zh: 在周界巡逻的凶猛护卫犬能有效吓退潜在的非法入侵者。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) resist or delay an impending attack, threat, or adversary
items.ex_en: Our exhausted squad managed to hold off the enemy advance until dawn.
items.ex_zh: 我们精疲力竭的小队设法抵挡住了敌军的推进，直至破晓。

items.def_en: (+ sth) prevent an impending problem or attack from developing or arriving
items.ex_en: Emergency economic measures were taken to head off a major banking collapse.
items.ex_zh: 有关方面采取了紧急经济措施，以阻止一场重大的银行崩溃。

items.def_zh: 威慑，吓住；阻止，使打消念头
items.def_en: 1. (+ from) To make someone decide not to do something by making them realize the difficulties or bad consequences.
items.ex_en: Harsh penalties and constant surveillance can deter drivers from exceeding speed limits.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的处罚和持续的监控能威慑司机，使其不敢超速行驶。

items.def_zh: 避开，延缓，推迟（坏事）；击穿，敲破
items.def_en: (also 'stave off') To temporarily prevent or delay something bad from happening.
items.ex_en: The central bank introduced subsidies to stave off an impending economic recession.
items.ex_zh: 央行推出了补贴措施，以延缓即将来临的经济衰退。

items.def_en: (+ from) to persuade someone not to take a particular harmful or unwise course of action
items.ex_en: Mentors tried to dissuade the ambitious youth from pursuing that reckless course.
items.ex_zh: 导师们试图劝阻这位雄心勃勃的年轻人不要采取那项鲁莽的举动。

items.def_en: To temporarily avert or delay an imminent bad outcome or disaster.
items.ex_en: Emergency international loans helped stave off the impending collapse of the national currency.
items.ex_zh: 紧急国际贷款帮助暂时化解了本国货币即将面临的崩盘危机。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame focus on preventing an impending harm, attack, or undesirable action, either by intimidating the actor with punitive consequences or by proactively deflecting the threat.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过惩罚威慑阻止不良企图，或主动筑起防线避开、延缓危险侵害。
groups.desc_en: Denotes proactively preventing an unwanted agent or event from intruding or occurring through intimidation or preventive resistance, contrasting with reactive defense or passive avoidance.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过震慑、威压或预防性阻击使威胁不敢逼近或无法发生，区别于威胁到来后的被动防御或消极回避。
groups.nuance_en: deter: discourage an action through fear of consequences (aggression / criminals) · ward off: deflect or keep at bay an impending threat (infection / blow / evil) · dissuade: talk someone out of a contemplated course (friend / client) · stave off: temporarily hold back an inevitable crisis (bankruptcy / collapse)
groups.nuance_zh: deter: 凭威慑后果令其知难而退 (aggression / criminals) · ward off: 设防抵挡并击退逼近的灾祸 (infection / blow / evil) · dissuade: 劝阻规劝放弃打算 (friend / client) · stave off: 极力延缓化解迫在眉睫的危机 (bankruptcy / collapse)

groups.name: Deteriorate & Decay · 恶化与衰败 (Decline in Quality or Condition)
groups.tip: 局势日趋恶化更为严重

items.def_en: to gradually become less, worse, or lower in quality or strength
items.ex_en: Without substantial investment, the public health sector will inevitably decline further.
items.ex_zh: 若缺乏巨额投资，公共卫生部门势必会进一步衰退。

items.def_en: gradually deteriorate in quality, health, or overall condition
items.ex_en: His physical health started to go downhill rapidly after he ceased exercising.
items.ex_zh: 在他停止锻炼之后，他的身体健康状况便开始迅速走下坡路。

items.def_en: To become worse, or to make something become worse, more severe, or more difficult.
items.ex_en: Continued drought conditions will only worsen the severe food shortages across the region.
items.ex_zh: 持续的旱情只会让整个地区本就严重的粮食短缺进一步恶化。
items.ex2_en: Patient symptoms worsened overnight despite intensive antibiotic treatment in the hospital.
items.ex2_zh: 尽管在医院接受了强化的抗生素治疗，病人的症状在一夜之间仍恶化了。

items.def_en: lose structural integrity, health, or functional order progressively
items.ex_en: Under intense psychological stress, his mental stamina began to break down completely.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大的心理压力之下，他的精神意志开始彻底瓦解。
items.ex2_en: Specialized stomach bacteria break down fibrous plant materials into digestible nutrients.
items.ex2_zh: 专门的肠胃细菌将纤维植物物质分解为易消化的营养素。

items.def_en: disintegrate or decay into pieces through age, wear, or neglect
items.ex_en: The historic wooden chapel began to fall apart after decades of neglect.
items.ex_zh: 经过数十年的荒废，这座历史悠久的木质小礼拜堂已破败不堪。

items.def_en: [I/T] to be destroyed gradually by natural processes, or decline in health and vigor
items.ex_en: Without proper maintenance, the grand ancient timber structures will slowly decay.
items.ex_zh: 若无妥善维护，这些宏伟的古老木构建筑将逐渐腐朽损坏。
items.ex2_en: Fungal infections can decay fallen logs into rich organic garden soil.
items.ex2_zh: 真菌感染可以使倒下的原木腐烂成肥沃的有机花园土壤。

items.def_en: To become progressively worse in quality, condition, or value over time.
items.ex_en: Doctors observed her physical condition deteriorate rapidly throughout the harsh cold winter.
items.ex_zh: 医生们观察到在严酷寒冬期间，她的身体状况迅速恶化。

items.def_en: (+ into) to pass into an inferior, weaker, or less desirable state
items.ex_en: The peaceful neighborhood demonstration could easily degenerate into violent clashes with police.
items.ex_zh: 该社区原本和平的抗议活动极易蜕化为与警方的暴力冲突。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses entities undergoing progressive loss of quality, strength, health, or structural integrity. 'Worsen' covers any general downward trend, whereas 'decay' and 'degenerate' signify advanced biological or moral breakdown.
groups.summary_zh: 描述事物质量、健康或状态逐步走低乃至崩坏。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the progressive, entropy-driven loss of physical integrity, functional health, or moral quality, contrasting with sudden destruction or static deficiency.
groups.desc_zh: 指物理结构、机能健康或道德品质发生渐进式、不可逆的退化与崩解，区别于瞬间突发毁损或静态的不足。
groups.nuance_en: deteriorate: steady progressive worsening of state (health / relations) · decay: organic decomposition or institutional rotting (teeth / society) · degenerate: moral or genetic decline into an inferior form (condition / debate) · fall apart: structural collapse into non-functionality (system / marriage)
groups.nuance_zh: deteriorate: 状态或质量的持续渐进恶化 (health / relations) · decay: 有机物腐烂或制度从内部衰亡 (teeth / society) · degenerate: 堕落退化至低下劣质的境地 (condition / debate) · fall apart: 结构解体支离破碎走向瘫痪 (system / marriage)

groups.name: Develop & Evolve · 发展与演进 (Progress, Evolve, Mature)
groups.tip: 事物逐步向前迈进与深化拓展

items.def_en: [I/T] to grow or cause to grow into a more advanced, complete, or elaborate state
items.ex_en: The research team hopes to develop new renewable energy solutions next year.
items.ex_zh: 研究团队希望在明年研发出新的可再生能源解决方案。
items.ex2_en: Healthy seedlings develop rapidly into sturdy bushes with sufficient sunlight exposure.
items.ex2_zh: 在充足的阳光照射下，健康的幼苗会迅速长成茁壮的灌木。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move forward in position, development, or technological maturity
items.ex_en: Technological innovations consistently advance the efficiency of modern manufacturing assembly lines.
items.ex_zh: 技术创新不断推进现代制造装配线的生产效率。
items.ex2_en: The rebel army advanced slowly toward the fortified border post yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 叛军昨天缓慢地向筑有防御工事的边境哨所挺进。

items.def_en: To develop, advance, or improve gradually over time.
items.ex_en: Construction of the long highway will progress steadily despite the adverse weather.
items.ex_zh: 尽管天气恶劣，这条长途公路的建设仍将稳步推进。

items.def_zh: 逐渐演变，逐步发展；（生物）进化
items.def_en: To develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complex form; to undergo biological evolution.
items.ex_en: Primitive tribal rituals would gradually evolve into complex religious and cultural systems.
items.ex_zh: 原始的部落仪式逐渐演变成为复杂的宗教与文化体系。
items.ex2_en: The forward-thinking company evolved its business model to meet modern consumer demands.
items.ex2_zh: 这家具有前瞻性的公司发展了其商业模式以满足现代消费者的需求。

items.def_en: [I/T] to become fully developed or reach a sophisticated, stable state
items.ex_en: With patience and testing, the experimental operating software will mature into a viable product.
items.ex_zh: 通过耐心打磨与测试，这款实验性操作系统将成熟为一款可行的产品。
items.ex2_en: Careful oak barrel aging matures the young red wine into perfection.
items.ex2_zh: 精细的橡木桶陈酿使这款年轻的红葡萄酒趋于完美成熟。

items.def_en: (+ sth) gradually develop or mature into a larger, more advanced state
items.ex_en: The modest family venture could eventually grow into a multinational commercial powerhouse.
items.ex_zh: 这家规模不大的家族企业最终可能会逐步成长为跨国商业巨头。

items.def_zh: 顺利成型；显现良好发展势头
items.def_en: develop or progress in a promising, structured, or mature manner
items.ex_en: The new business model is beginning to shape up quite nicely.
items.ex_zh: 这种新的商业模式正开始展现出相当良好的成型势头。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) help someone or something to develop, improve, or make progress
items.ex_en: The veteran trainer worked hard to bring along the inexperienced young athletes.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的教练努力培养那些缺乏实战经验的年轻运动员。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe entities advancing through natural, historical, or planned stages toward a more complex, advanced, or complete state. 'Progress' emphasizes forward linear motion or improvement, while 'evolve' highlights gradual adaptation and structural transformation over time.
groups.summary_zh: 描述事物按阶段向前推进、深化或逐步演化为更成熟高级形态的过程。
groups.desc_en: Denotes positive, teleological maturation, refinement, and expansion of complexity over time, unlike mere quantitative increase or random alteration.
groups.desc_zh: 指事物历经时间淬炼由低级向高级、复杂及成熟形态演进的积极过程，区别于单纯的数量增加或随意的变化。
groups.nuance_en: develop: structured emergence and expansion into maturity (skill / economy) · evolve: gradual adaptive transformation through stages (species / strategy) · mature: ripening to full biological or emotional capacity (talent / market) · advance: forward motion along a benchmarked continuum (technology / knowledge)
groups.nuance_zh: develop: 结构性深化并扩展成熟 (skill / economy) · evolve: 经由阶段性适应演进转化 (species / strategy) · mature: 达致完全成熟充盈状态 (talent / market) · advance: 沿既定标尺向前推进行进 (technology / knowledge)

groups.name: Dirty & Stain · 弄脏与沾污 (Dirty, Smut, Soil, Befoul)
groups.tip: 沾染尘垢或留下顽固污迹

items.def_en: (+ sth) make something dirty, untidy, or soiled
items.ex_en: The muddy children managed to mess up the clean living room carpet.
items.ex_zh: 浑身是泥的孩子们把干净的客厅地毯弄得又脏又乱。

items.def_en: to make something physically unclean, particularly with dirt, mud, or waste
items.ex_en: Take off your muddy boots lest you soil the newly cleaned marble floors.
items.ex_zh: 脱掉沾满泥巴的靴子，以免弄脏刚擦洗干净的大理石地面。
items.ex2_en: White linen trousers soil quickly on dusty country walking trails.
items.ex2_zh: 白色亚麻长裤在尘土飞扬的乡村步道上很容易弄脏。

items.def_zh: 弄脏，熏黑；（谷物等）感染黑穗病
items.def_en: To mark or stain something with soot or dirt; (of crops) to infect or become infected with smut disease.
items.ex_en: Dense factory chimneys smut the evening sky with continuous plumes of soot.
items.ex_zh: 密集的工厂烟囱喷涌出连绵的黑烟，熏黑了傍晚的天空。
items.ex2_en: The ripening wheat ears smutted rapidly after the humid summer rainfall.
items.ex2_zh: 潮湿的夏雨过后，正在成熟的麦穗迅速感染了黑穗病。

items.def_en: (+ sth) cover or spoil something with dirt, mud, or grime
items.ex_en: Don't run across that wet garden patch or you'll muck up your shoes.
items.ex_zh: 别跑过那块潮湿的菜地，否则会把你的鞋子搞脏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) cover or dirty a surface with greasy, sticky, or smudged marks
items.ex_en: Careless painters managed to smear up the glass windows with sticky grease.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的油漆工把黏稠的油垢抹得满玻璃窗都是。

items.def_en: To make something dirty or unclean.
items.ex_en: The children's dirty paws will dirty the freshly painted hallway wall.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们脏兮兮的爪子会弄脏刚刷好油漆的走廊墙壁。

items.def_en: to blacken or cover deeply with ingrained dirt or grime
items.ex_en: Heavy coal dust continued to begrime the faces of the weary underground miners.
items.ex_zh: 浓重的煤尘不断蒙黑那些疲惫不堪的井下矿工的脸膛。

items.def_en: to make something foul, filthy, or offensively impure
items.ex_en: Industrial runoff continues to befoul the pristine waters of the ancient river valley.
items.ex_zh: 工业污水不断污染着这条古老河谷原始纯净的水域。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate transferring grime, soot, or pollution onto a clean surface, varying from mild smudging to heavy, vile contamination.
groups.summary_zh: 指使物体表面沾上灰尘、黑垢或遭受严重污损。
groups.desc_en: Denotes contaminating or defacing a surface with grime, filth, or foreign substances, contrasting with damaging the structural integrity itself.
groups.desc_zh: 指用污垢、污秽或异物涂抹玷污表层使其肮脏失洁，区别于破坏结构本体的功能性损坏。
groups.nuance_en: soil: make dirty on the surface through contact (hands / reputation) · begrime: encrust deeply with soot or ingrained grime (face / walls) · befoul: morally or foully pollute with offensive matter (water / air / nest) · mess up: untidy, taint, or spoil visually (clothes / room)
groups.nuance_zh: soil: 表面沾染污渍或名誉受损 (hands / reputation) · begrime: 彻底被煤烟灰垢浸染积垢 (face / walls) · befoul: 恶臭秽物污染或道德玷污 (water / air / nest) · mess up: 弄乱搞脏致外观狼藉 (clothes / room)

groups.name: Discuss & Deliberate Together · 商讨与研商 (Discuss, Confer, Deliberate)
groups.tip: 各抒己见共同探讨议题

items.def_en: To talk about something with other people in order to exchange opinions or reach a decision; to examine a topic in speech or writing.
items.ex_en: The committee met yesterday afternoon to discuss possible revisions to the company policy.
items.ex_zh: 委员会昨天下午开会讨论了对公司政策的可能修订。

items.def_en: (+ with) to discuss something with someone in order to seek their advice or consent
items.ex_en: The prime minister will consult with senior military advisors before announcing his final decision.
items.ex_zh: 首相在宣布最终决定之前将与高级军事顾问进行磋商。

items.def_zh: 和谈；会谈（特指敌对双方）
items.def_en: (+ with) to hold formal discussions with an opponent or opposing side to discuss terms
items.ex_en: The rebel commander sent an emissary across the lines to parley with the general.
items.ex_zh: 叛军指挥官派出一名使者跨越火线与将军谈判。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to discuss a problem, plan, or situation thoroughly with someone
items.ex_en: We need to sit down and talk over the details before signing the contract.
items.ex_zh: 在签署合同之前，我们需要坐下来详细商讨各个细节。

items.def_zh: 深入讨论以解决（分歧或细节）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to discuss something in detail until an agreement, solution, or decision is reached
items.ex_en: We stayed up all night to hash out the final details of the contract.
items.ex_zh: 我们熬了一整夜，终于把合同的最终细节敲定了。

items.def_zh: 非正式地讨论或探讨（想法、计划）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to discuss an idea, plan, or suggestion informally or casually
items.ex_en: Let us kick around some marketing ideas over lunch before next week's formal presentation.
items.ex_zh: 我们下周正式汇报前，先趁午餐时间随便聊聊几个营销想法吧。

items.def_en: (+ on/about) to discuss something thoroughly and formally before taking a critical decision or verdict
items.ex_en: The jurors deliberated for twelve hours before finally reaching a unanimous guilty verdict.
items.ex_zh: 陪审团仔细审议了十二个小时，最终达成了有罪的一致裁决。

items.def_zh: 商讨，协商；授予，赋予（奖项、学位、权利等）
items.def_en: 1. To discuss something with someone in order to exchange opinions or reach a decision. 2. To formally grant or give an honor, degree, title, or right to someone.
items.ex_en: The board members asked for ten minutes to confer before signing the agreement.
items.ex_zh: 董事会成员要求给他们十分钟商量一下，然后再签署协议。

groups.summary_en: Two or more interlocutors exchange views, evaluate alternatives, and pool advice to reach a shared understanding, resolution, or verdict. Verbs distinguish informal conversation from formal consultation and institutional deliberation.
groups.summary_zh: 双方或多方交流意见、磋商权衡，以谋求共识或决议。
groups.desc_en: Denotes collective verbal exchange focused on weighing alternatives and solving problems collaboratively, contrasting with unilateral exposition or hostile arguing.
groups.desc_zh: 指多方围绕特定议题共同推敲、权衡利弊以求达成共识，区别于单向宣讲或敌对争吵。
groups.nuance_en: deliberate: formally and carefully weigh options before deciding (jury / committee) · confer: consult each other to align viewpoints (diplomats / doctors) · hash out: resolve contentious details through intense debate (contract / differences) · consult: seek expert counsel or reference (specialist / lawyer)
groups.nuance_zh: deliberate: 正式审慎权衡后定夺 (jury / committee) · confer: 交换意见以协调共商 (diplomats / doctors) · hash out: 深入透彻交锋以达成妥协 (contract / differences) · consult: 就专业事项求教或征询 (specialist / lawyer)

groups.name: Disembark from a Vehicle · 下车与离载具 (Disembark, Alight, Detrain)
groups.tip: 指乘客从交通工具上下车或着陆

items.def_en: [I/T] to exit a bus, curb, or carriage by taking a downward step
items.ex_en: He glanced at his watch as he stepped off the morning commuter bus.
items.ex_zh: 他走下早班通勤公交车时看了一眼手表。

items.def_en: [I/T] to exit or cause passengers to leave a train
items.ex_en: All passengers must detrain immediately due to an unexpected obstruction on the track.
items.ex_zh: 由于铁轨上突发障碍物，所有乘客必须立即下车。
items.ex2_en: The military transport officer detrained the weary soldiers at midnight.
items.ex2_zh: 军事运输官在半夜让疲惫的士兵们下了火车。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to leave a bus, train, aircraft, or large vehicle
items.ex_en: Remember to take all your belongings before you get off the subway train.
items.ex_zh: 从地铁列车下来之前，请记得带齐所有个人物品。

items.def_en: (+ of sth) to leave or exit a car, taxi, or small enclosed vehicle
items.ex_en: She paid the cab driver and told the children to get out carefully.
items.ex_zh: 她给出租车司机付了钱，并叮嘱孩子们小心下车。

items.def_en: (+ from) to step down or get off a train, bus, or other transport (formal)
items.ex_en: The elderly gentleman waited patiently to alight from the first-class railway carriage.
items.ex_zh: 那位老绅士耐心地等待着从头等火车车厢走下来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to leave a ship, aircraft, or other large vehicle after a journey
items.ex_en: Cruise passengers were granted permission to disembark shortly after the ship had docked.
items.ex_zh: 游轮靠岸后不久，乘客们便获准下船。
items.ex2_en: The charter airline disembarked all international passengers after customs clearance.
items.ex2_zh: 包机航空公司在海关清关后让所有国际旅客下机。

items.def_en: (especially NAmE) to get off an airplane after it has landed.
items.ex_en: Passengers seated in rows twenty through thirty may now prepare to deplane.
items.ex_zh: 坐在第二十排至第三十排的乘客现在可以准备下机了。

items.def_zh: 下船，下飞机，登陆；卸下（货物、乘客）；剥去（树皮）
items.def_en: 1. to leave or remove passengers or goods from a ship or aircraft; to disembark. 2. to strip the bark from a tree trunk.
items.ex_en: The infantry unit received strict orders to debark upon reaching the northern coast.
items.ex_zh: 步兵部队接到严格命令，一到达北部海岸便立即登陆下船。
items.ex2_en: The naval transport debarked three hundred armed marines onto the beach.
items.ex2_zh: 海军运输舰将三百名全副武装的海军陆战队员送上海滩登岸。

groups.summary_en: Passengers or crew exit a conveyance (aircraft, ship, train, bus, or vehicle). Verbs vary primarily by the specific type of transport involved ('deplane' for planes, 'detrain' for trains, 'disembark' general/maritime, 'alight' formal public transit).
groups.summary_zh: 乘客或机组人员从船只、飞机、火车或车辆中走出离开。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the physical act of exiting a conveyance at a stopping point, contrasting with starting transit or boarding.
groups.desc_zh: 指人员在停靠点离开或踏下载具的物理行为，区别于上车或运输在途状态。
groups.nuance_en: disembark: formal departure from a ship, aircraft, or vessel (passengers / troops) · alight: formal or deliberate stepping down from vehicle (train / carriage) · detrain: specifically step out of a train (passengers / division) · deplane: specifically exit an airplane (travelers / crew)
groups.nuance_zh: disembark: 乘客或军队正式离开船舶、飞行器 (passengers / troops) · alight: 优雅或审慎地步下车轿 (train / carriage) · detrain: 特指步下或疏散出火车 (passengers / division) · deplane: 特指走出机舱离开飞机 (travelers / crew)

groups.name: Disentangle & Strip Apart · 拆解与解构解脱 (Disengage, Disentangle, Cannibalize)
groups.tip: 解开机械联锁或脱离挂钩

items.def_en: (+ sth) to disentangle or separate tangled strands, items, or confused elements
items.ex_en: It took me over an hour to sort out the tangled headphone cords.
items.ex_zh: 我花了一个多小时才把缠成一团的耳机线理顺。

items.def_zh: 解开；拆散（编织物或缠结）
items.def_en: [I/T] to undo or become undone from a tangled, woven, or knitted state
items.ex_en: Be careful pulling that loose thread, or the entire sleeve will unravel completely.
items.ex_zh: 拽那根线头时小心点，否则整只袖子都会拆散脱线。
items.ex2_en: The patient tailor unraveled the tangled wool yarn into neat balls.
items.ex2_zh: 耐心的裁缝把缠结的毛线拆开并缠成整齐的线球。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to completely dismantle or demolish a structure, engine, or assembly
items.ex_en: The old factory was torn down to make way for a modern shopping mall.
items.ex_zh: 那座旧工厂被拆除，以便改建现代化的购物中心。

items.def_en: to take a machine, apparatus, or structure to pieces systematically
items.ex_en: Specialized engineers were hired to dismantle the aging nuclear reactor with extreme care.
items.ex_zh: 聘请了专业工程师极其小心地拆除这座老化的核反应堆。

items.def_zh: （使机械等）脱开，脱离啮合；使脱离，摆脱束缚；（军队）撤出战斗
items.def_en: 1. To separate or release a clutch, lock, or mechanism; to become detached. 2. To withdraw or free oneself or troops from a conflict or situation.
items.ex_en: Depress the foot pedal firmly to disengage the clutch before shifting the gear.
items.ex_zh: 在换挡之前用力踩下脚踏板以使离合器脱开。
items.ex2_en: The safety locking gear disengages automatically when air pressure drops suddenly.
items.ex2_zh: 当气压突然下降时，安全锁定装置会自动脱开断开。

items.def_zh: 解开，理顺（缠结物）；使摆脱，脱离（纠葛）
items.def_en: To separate things that have become twisted or knotted together; to free oneself or someone from an entangled situation.
items.ex_en: The diplomat worked tirelessly to disentangle the country from the escalating foreign conflict.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官不知疲倦地工作，以使国家摆脱不断升级的外国冲突。

items.def_en: to dismantle a machine, vehicle, or structure completely down to its basic core
items.ex_en: The mechanics will strip down the racing motorcycle to inspect every single part.
items.ex_zh: 技工们将彻底拆卸这辆赛车摩托，以检查每一个零部件。

items.def_zh: 拆用（旧机器等）的零部件来修理其他机器；分流，蚕食（现有产品）的销量
items.def_en: 1. To take parts from one machine, vehicle, or device to repair another. 2. To reduce sales of an existing product by introducing a similar new one.
items.ex_en: We had to cannibalize two damaged tractors to keep the third one running.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不拆用两台受损拖拉机的零件，才让第三台保持运转。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict the deliberate decoupling, extraction, or salvage-dismantling of mechanical parts, interwoven threads, or linked systems to free them or repurpose their components.
groups.summary_zh: 解开缠结、脱开机械锁合或拆除部件以作挪用。
groups.desc_en: Denotes separating tangled or assembled components to restore autonomy or salvage elements, contrasting with destructive crushing or chaotic breaking.
groups.desc_zh: 指将缠绕、嵌合或装配的组件分离开来以解脱束缚或利旧回收，区别于暴力的砸碎或混沌破坏。
groups.nuance_en: disentangle: free from snarled confusion or complication (wires / finances) · disengage: uncouple or withdraw from contact (gears / troops) · strip down: dismantle to bare essentials for inspection (engine / argument) · cannibalize: salvage parts from one unit to repair another (fleet / equipment)
groups.nuance_zh: disentangle: 从错综复杂的缠绕中理清解脱 (wires / finances) · disengage: 解除机械啮合或脱离战阵接触 (gears / troops) · strip down: 剥解拆卸至最简核心以检修 (engine / argument) · cannibalize: 拆用报废装备部件拼修新机 (fleet / equipment)

groups.name: Disguise & Cover Up · 伪装与粉饰 (Masquerade, Whitewash, Camouflage)
groups.tip: 戴上面具化装潜入，乔装假冒特定身份

items.def_en: deliberately avoid dealing with flaws, mistakes, or difficult issues
items.ex_en: The spokesperson attempted to gloss over the glaring budget deficits during the briefing.
items.ex_zh: 发言人在通报会上试图对显眼的预算赤字轻描淡写带过。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to take action to prevent illicit, embarrassing, or wrongful deeds from becoming known
items.ex_en: The corrupt mayor hired private investigators to help cover up his fraudulent activities.
items.ex_zh: 这位腐败的市长雇佣了私家侦探来协助掩盖他的欺诈行径。

items.def_en: conceal disagreements or defects superficially rather than resolving them
items.ex_en: The joint statement merely papered over deep disagreements between the two leaders.
items.ex_zh: 这份联合声明只是粉饰了两位领导人之间的深刻分歧。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth as sb/sth) to fraudulently represent someone or something as something genuine or superior
items.ex_en: The swindler attempted to pass off cheap brass jewelry as genuine antique gold.
items.ex_zh: 那个骗子企图把廉价黄铜首饰冒充成真正的古董黄金。

items.def_en: conceal someone's real character, intentions, or true nature with a false exterior
items.ex_en: He put on a friendly smile to camouflage his underlying resentment toward them.
items.ex_zh: 他露出一副友善的笑容，以掩饰自己心底对他们的怨恨。

items.def_zh: 伪装，冒充，假扮（masquerade as）；参加化装舞会
items.def_en: (also 'masquerade as') To pretend to be someone or something else in order to deceive people.
items.ex_en: The con artist managed to masquerade as an elite neurosurgeon for several months.
items.ex_zh: 那个骗子假扮成顶尖神经外科医生，竟然瞒骗了数月之久。

items.def_zh: 掩饰，粉饰（罪过、丑闻等）；粉刷（墙壁等）；（体育比赛中）完封，让对手一分未得
items.def_en: 1. To conceal or downplay mistakes, faults, or scandals in order to protect an image or reputation. 2. To paint a wall or surface with whitewash. 3. (sports) To defeat an opponent completely without allowing them to score.
items.ex_en: The administration was accused of trying to whitewash the serious safety inspection failures.
items.ex_zh: 管理层被指责试图粉饰重大的安全检查失职。

items.def_zh: 隐瞒，掩饰真实情感/意图
items.def_en: disguise or conceal one's real motives, feelings, or beliefs through deception
items.ex_en: An experienced spy knows exactly when to speak truth and when to dissemble.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的间谍非常清楚何时讲真话，何时该掩饰真情。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe deceptive actions taken to mask true identity, faults, or illicit behavior behind a benign, respectable facade.
groups.summary_zh: 以虚假身份伪装、或粉饰遮盖罪责以掩人耳目。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deceptive concealment through superficial masking or false external presentation, contrasting with outright denial or honest transparency.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过表层粉饰、掩盖或假象隐匿瑕疵与真相，区别于断然否认或坦荡透明。
groups.nuance_en: camouflage: conceal by blending into the environment (tanks / intent) · whitewash: cover up crimes or flaws under a virtuous pretext (record / corruption) · paper over: superficially patch up cracks or disputes (differences / cracks) · masquerade: pretend to be someone or something else falsely (as expert / identity)
groups.nuance_zh: camouflage: 融入背景伪装隐蔽 (tanks / intent) · whitewash: 粉饰美化劣迹以掩盖罪责 (record / corruption) · paper over: 敷衍弥缝分歧裂痕 (differences / cracks) · masquerade: 冒充并戴上假面具行事 (as expert / identity)

groups.name: Dislike to Revulsion · 厌恶与反感反胃 (Dislike, Distaste, Disgust, Loathe)
groups.tip: 从轻微反感递进为生理级作呕排斥

items.def_en: To feel that you do not like someone or something.
items.ex_en: Many people genuinely dislike the taste of bitter melon despite its health benefits.
items.ex_zh: 尽管苦瓜对健康有益，许多人还是真心不喜欢它的味道。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone to feel intense distaste, disinterest, or disgust
items.ex_en: His arrogant attitude and constant bragging really turn off everyone he meets.
items.ex_zh: 他傲慢的举止和不停的吹嘘真让每一个遇到他的人感到反感。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to disgust or sicken someone severely with something repulsive
items.ex_en: The gruesome medical pictures in the textbook totally grossed out the young students.
items.ex_zh: 教科书里令人毛骨悚然的医学图片彻底把年轻学生们恶心到了。

items.def_en: To cause someone to feel extreme dislike, revulsion, or strong disapproval.
items.ex_en: The blatant dishonesty displayed by the politician will surely disgust many ordinary voters.
items.ex_zh: 政客表现出的公然虚伪肯定会让许多普通选民感到强烈反感。

items.def_en: to feel intense hatred, disgust, or complete unwillingness to endure something
items.ex_en: I loathe waking up early on cold winter mornings to clear the driveway.
items.ex_zh: 我极其讨厌在寒冷的冬日清晨早起清理车道。

items.def_en: to hate something very much, especially on strong moral grounds
items.ex_en: Civilized societies must abhor any form of cruelty against defenseless human beings.
items.ex_zh: 文明社会必须对任何针对毫无防备之人的残酷行径深恶痛绝。

items.def_en: to make someone feel physically sick, horrified, or deeply repelled
items.ex_en: The stench emanating from the rotting garbage was enough to revolt anyone nearby.
items.ex_zh: 腐烂垃圾散发出的恶臭足以让附近的任何人都感到反胃作呕。

items.def_en: to cause someone to feel shock, disgust, and physical nausea
items.ex_en: The horrific details of the gruesome crime will sicken anyone who reads them.
items.ex_zh: 这桩可怕罪行的骇人细节会让任何读到的人都感到触目惊心、恶心反胃。
items.ex2_en: Many elderly patients sickened rapidly during the severe winter flu outbreak.
items.ex2_zh: 在严酷的冬季流感爆发期间，许多老年患者迅速患病发作。

groups.summary_en: An experiencer harbors an aversion toward a stimulus, progressing in visceral intensity from mild disinclination to physical revulsion and outright detestation.
groups.summary_zh: 从轻微反感不快逐渐递增至极度恶心乃至深恶痛绝。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an emotional to visceral revulsion against an object, ranging from simple distaste to nausea-inducing abhorrence, contrasting with mild disinterest.
groups.desc_zh: 指对客体产生的从轻度反感到直达生理作呕的强烈排斥与憎恶，区别于中性的不感兴趣或客观批判。
groups.nuance_en: loathe: intense enduring hatred and contempt (liars / chores) · abhor: moral revulsion with shuddering aversion (violence / cruelty) · disgust: sickening distaste triggered by foulness (hypocrisy / sight) · revolt: provoke visceral nausea or rebellion in sensibility (stomach / conscience)
groups.nuance_zh: loathe: 根深蒂固且轻蔑至极的厌恶 (liars / chores) · abhor: 发自道德良知的惊悚痛恨 (violence / cruelty) · disgust: 令人反胃作呕的极度厌恶 (hypocrisy / sight) · revolt: 激起胃部生理或道德层面的强烈反感 (stomach / conscience)

groups.name: Dismantle & Disjoint · 拆解与分脱 (Take Apart Component by Component)
groups.tip: 使关节或连接处脱开

items.def_en: (+ sth) to separate something composite into its simpler components or individual parts
items.ex_en: Our biology teacher showed us how enzymes break down complex food molecules efficiently.
items.ex_zh: 我们的生物老师向我们展示了酶是如何高效分解复杂食物分子的。
items.ex2_en: Plastic bags do not break down naturally in ordinary landfill sites.
items.ex2_zh: 塑料袋在普通垃圾填埋场中不会自然分解。

items.def_en: to separate an object into the smaller parts from which it is made
items.ex_en: The curious little boy liked to take apart old clocks to see inside.
items.ex_zh: 那个好奇的小男孩喜欢把旧钟表拆开，看看里面的结构。

items.def_zh: 拆线，拆散（缝线或错综结构）
items.def_en: to undo the stitches of needlework or carefully disentangle a complex construct
items.ex_en: She used a sharp seam ripper to carefully unpick the flawed embroidery stitches.
items.ex_zh: 她用锋利的拆线器小心翼翼地拆掉了织错的刺绣针脚。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to separate an assembled mechanism or object into its constituent pieces
items.ex_en: The technician had to pull apart the casing to examine the damaged circuitry.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员不得不拆开外壳以检查受损的电路。

items.def_zh: 彻底拆卸（至裸架或基本零件）
items.def_en: to completely dismantle an engine or vehicle to clean, inspect, or repair it
items.ex_en: Over the weekend, Mark decided to strip down his car engine completely for repairs.
items.ex_zh: 周末，马克决定彻底拆卸汽车发动机进行维修。

items.def_zh: 拆除，拆卸（机械、结构或组织）
items.def_en: to take a machine or structure to pieces piece by piece
items.ex_en: The demolition crew will dismantle the old suspension bridge using heavy cranes tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 拆迁队明天将使用重型起重机拆卸这座旧吊桥。

items.def_zh: 肢解，切断关节；使脱节，使脱臼
items.def_en: To take something apart at the joints; to disconnect, disrupt, or separate the components of something.
items.ex_en: The master butcher demonstrated how to cleanly disjoint the roasted carcass with precision.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的屠夫演示了如何精准利落地顺着关节切开烤禽。

items.def_en: To take a machine, structure, or piece of equipment apart into its separate pieces.
items.ex_en: You must disassemble the flat-pack furniture carefully before attempting to move houses.
items.ex_zh: 在搬家之前，你必须小心地将平板组装家具拆卸开。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote separating an assembled structure, mechanism, or articulated body into its individual constituents, ranging from orderly breakdown to structural articulation separation.
groups.summary_zh: 把组合结构、机械或带关节躯体逐步分拆卸解，侧重机械性或解剖性操作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes systematically breaking an assembled whole into individual pieces in an orderly fashion, contrasting with irreversible destructive smashing.
groups.desc_zh: 指按照构造机理有条理地将整体拆解为独立零件，区别于不可逆的暴力砸毁。
groups.nuance_en: dismantle: systematically take down a structure or organization (rig / empire) · disassemble: mechanically uncouple manufactured parts in reverse order (engine / rifle) · pull apart: separate forcibly or examine piece by piece (bread / argument) · disjoint: sever joints or destroy systematic coherence (bones / structure)
groups.nuance_zh: dismantle: 系统性拆除复杂工程设施或组织架构 (rig / empire) · disassemble: 严格依逆序拆卸机械组件 (engine / rifle) · pull apart: 掰开剥离或逐块深究剖析 (bread / argument) · disjoint: 肢解脱臼关节或断裂逻辑连贯性 (bones / structure)

groups.name: Display & Exhibit · 陈列与展出
groups.tip: 摆出事物供人观看欣赏

items.def_zh: 以……为特色展出；重点展示
items.def_en: to make something a prominent or special attraction in an exhibition or presentation
items.ex_en: The autumn gallery exhibition will feature rare landscape paintings by renowned modern masters.
items.ex_zh: 秋季美术展将重点展出著名现代大师罕见的风景画作品。

items.def_zh: 陈列，展出；显露，表现；（屏幕上）显示
items.def_en: 1. To put something in a place where people can see it easily. 2. To show a particular feeling, quality, or skill clearly. 3. (of an electronic device) To show words, pictures, or data on a screen.
items.ex_en: The local museum will display newly discovered artifacts from the ancient Roman tomb.
items.ex_zh: 当地博物馆将展出古罗马古墓中新出土的珍贵文物。

items.def_zh: 展出，陈列，展览；表现出，显露（品质、迹象等）
items.def_en: 1. To display something publicly in an exhibition, museum, or gallery. 2. (formal) To clearly show a particular quality, feeling, or symptom.
items.ex_en: Several emerging contemporary artists will exhibit their innovative sculptures at the city gallery.
items.ex_zh: 几位新兴当代艺术家将在城市画廊展出他们富有创意的雕塑作品。

items.def_en: to display something proudly or ostentatiously so that it attracts widespread notice
items.ex_en: He loved to parade his expensive new sports car down the main boulevard.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢开着昂贵的新跑车在主干道上招摇过市、大肆炫耀。

items.def_en: to exhibit the best qualities or features of something prominently to an audience
items.ex_en: The annual trade expo provides a great platform to showcase innovative green technologies.
items.ex_zh: 一年一度的贸易博览会为展示创新的绿色技术提供了绝佳平台。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to arrange or display things attractively for people to see or inspect
items.ex_en: The baker took great care to set out fresh pastries in the window.
items.ex_zh: 面包师非常用心地把新鲜出炉的糕点摆放在橱窗里展示。

items.def_zh: 摆出；陈列（供人观赏或使用）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to place items in an open or designated area so that they are visible and accessible
items.ex_en: Staff members put out colorful brochures and informative flyers for the prospective students.
items.ex_zh: 工作人员摆出了色彩鲜艳的宣传册和内容丰富的传单供未来的学生取阅。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to display something proudly or conspicuously to attract admiration
items.ex_en: She could not resist the urge to show off her sparkling diamond ring.
items.ex_zh: 她忍不住想炫耀一下自己闪闪发光的钻戒。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate placing physical items, artworks, or merchandise out in the open or in a gallery/store so that people can view or inspect them. 'Display' emphasizes attractive visual arrangement, whereas 'exhibit' denotes formal presentation in a public exhibition, museum, or fair.
groups.summary_zh: 指将展品、商品或艺术品有意识地陈列供公众观览。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately placing objects or qualities in prominent public view to attract admiration or inspection, contrasting with concealing or casually storing.
groups.desc_zh: 指刻意将物品或特质置于公众视野醒目处供人观摩、欣赏或检视，区别于隐匿或日常随意摆放。
groups.nuance_en: exhibit: present formally for public or legal inspection (paintings / evidence) · showcase: highlight premier strengths or talent attractively (talent / portfolio) · display: arrange openly so as to be seen clearly (wares / emotions) · parade: ostentatiously flaunt for vanity or intimidation (wealth / military power)
groups.nuance_zh: exhibit: 正式公开展出或出示法定物证 (paintings / evidence) · showcase: 重点聚焦展示拔尖才能与精品 (talent / portfolio) · display: 陈列显露以便清晰观瞻 (wares / emotions) · parade: 炫耀式招摇过市或大肆展示 (wealth / military power)

groups.name: Dissemble & Misrepresent · 掩饰与隐瞒 (Feign, Belie, Fib)
groups.tip: 掩饰真实真相并编造假象

items.def_en: (+ that / sb to be sth) to falsely assert, imply, or pretend that something is the case
items.ex_en: He tried to make out that he was an expert in international finance.
items.ex_zh: 他极力假装自己是国际金融领域的专家。

items.def_en: to behave insincerely or pretend to feel an emotion that is not genuine
items.ex_en: Stop trying to play act concern when we all know you do not care.
items.ex_zh: 别再假装关心了，我们都知道你根本不在乎。

items.def_en: to give a false or misleading account of the nature of something
items.ex_en: The defense attorney argued that the media coverage had blatantly misrepresented the defendant.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师辩称媒体报道公然歪曲了被告的形象。

items.def_en: (formal) To pretend to have a particular feeling, illness, or condition.
items.ex_en: He decided to feign a severe headache in order to avoid the dinner.
items.ex_zh: 他决定假装剧烈头痛，以此逃避那场晚宴。

items.def_zh: 掩饰，掩盖；证明……不真实，与……不符
items.def_en: (formal) 1. To give a false impression of something; to disguise or contradict. 2. To show that something is false or incorrect.
items.ex_en: Her calm and cheerful demeanor seemed to belie the deep sorrow inside her.
items.ex_zh: 她平静而愉悦的举止似乎掩盖了内心深处的悲伤。

items.def_en: (informal) To tell a small, harmless lie.
items.ex_en: The little girl confessed that she had fibbed about finishing her daily chores.
items.ex_zh: 小女孩坦白承认自己在完成日常家务的事情上撒了小谎。

items.def_en: [I/T] to conceal one's true motives, thoughts, or feelings under a false appearance
items.ex_en: A seasoned politician often learns how to dissemble when answering hostile interview questions.
items.ex_zh: 经验老道的政客通常深谙在面对怀有敌意的采访提问时如何掩饰真意。

items.def_en: [I/T] to hide one's real feelings, character, or intentions by pretense
items.ex_en: Unable to dissimulate his intense disgust, he quickly turned his head away awkwardly.
items.ex_zh: 由于无法掩饰内心的极度反感，他尴尬地迅速把头扭向了一边。

groups.summary_en: An agent deliberately obscures the truth or presents a false impression, spanning petty untruths, pretended states, and external appearances that contradict internal reality.
groups.summary_zh: 故意隐匿真相或展现虚假表象，涵盖撒小谎、假装状态以及表里相悖。
groups.desc_en: Denotes veiling real feelings, identity, or truths behind deceptive pretense, contrasting with transparent sincerity or plain error.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过虚假表象、做作或伪装刻意掩盖真情实感与真相，区别于真诚坦率或无意犯错。
groups.nuance_en: dissemble: conceal genuine motives or feelings behind a false facade (feelings / intent) · feign: invent an excuse or simulate an affliction (illness / ignorance) · belie: give a contradictorily false impression of inner reality (age / reputation) · dissimulate: actively hide intentions through crafty pretense (motives / character)
groups.nuance_zh: dissemble: 伪装掩饰真实意图或情绪 (feelings / intent) · feign: 佯装生病、无知或装出某种神情 (illness / ignorance) · belie: 表象与实质不符而遮蔽真实情况 (age / reputation) · dissimulate: 狡诈地暗中隐瞒图谋 (motives / character)

groups.name: Dissipate Resources Recklessly · 挥霍与耗尽 (Waste, Squander, Fritter away)
groups.tip: 毫无节制肆意挥霍

items.def_en: to waste time, money, or effort gradually on trivial or useless things
items.ex_en: He managed to fritter away his entire substantial inheritance on gambling within months.
items.ex_zh: 他在几个月内就把大笔可观的遗产全在赌博中挥霍殆尽了。

items.def_zh: 白白浪费；糟蹋（机会、金钱）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to fail to make good use of an asset, opportunity, or advantage; squander
items.ex_en: You shouldn't throw away such a wonderful job opportunity.
items.ex_zh: 你不应该白白浪费这么好的工作机会。

items.def_zh: 浪费，挥霍，滥用；（使）消瘦，衰弱；破坏，使荒芜
items.def_en: 1. To use more of something than is necessary, or to use it carelessly or uselessly. 2. (often 'waste away') To gradually become thin and weak, especially from illness. 3. (slang) To kill or destroy.
items.ex_en: Do not waste your hard-earned savings on cheap gadgets you will never use.
items.ex_zh: 别把你辛辛苦苦攒下的积蓄浪费在那些你永远用不上的廉价小玩意上。

items.def_en: (informal) to spend a large amount of money recklessly and quickly
items.ex_en: He blew his entire monthly paycheck in one wild weekend at the casino.
items.ex_zh: 他在赌场的疯狂周末里把整整一个月的薪水全挥霍光了。

items.def_zh: 快速挥霍耗尽（巨额钱财或资源）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to spend or use up large amounts of money or resources very quickly and carelessly
items.ex_en: The startup burned through five million dollars of venture capital in six months.
items.ex_zh: 该初创公司在六个月内就烧光了五百万美元的风险投资。

items.def_en: to foolishly scatter, exhaust, or waste away wealth, energy, or resources
items.ex_en: The reckless heir dissipated his ancestral fortune on high-stakes gambling in Monte Carlo.
items.ex_zh: 这位挥霍无度的继承人在蒙特卡洛的豪赌中耗尽了祖传的家产。
items.ex2_en: The dense morning fog dissipated quickly as sunlight warmed the valley.
items.ex2_zh: 随着阳光温暖山谷，晨间浓雾迅速消散了。

items.def_en: To waste money, time, or opportunity in a foolish or careless manner.
items.ex_en: The administration squandered a rare legislative opportunity by delaying essential economic reforms.
items.ex_zh: 该届政府因推迟关键的经济改革而白白错失了难得的立法契机。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to waste or squander money, time, or an opportunity completely and foolishly
items.ex_en: He pissed away his entire severance package on expensive designer clothes and parties.
items.ex_zh: 他把全部的遣散费都愚蠢地挥霍在了昂贵的名牌服装和聚会上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the careless, irresponsible, or lavish expenditure of finite resources (money, time, talents) such that they are depleted without yield, scaling from mere unproductivity to ruinous dissipation.
groups.summary_zh: 按程度递增描述对金钱、时间等宝贵资源的浪费、挥霍直至耗尽。
groups.desc_en: Denotes heedlessly and irreversibly exhausting finite assets through wanton indulgence, contrasting with prudent investment or gradual attrition.
groups.desc_zh: 指由于肆无忌惮、放纵挥霍而使有限资源不可逆地消耗殆尽，区别于稳健投资或渐进损耗。
groups.nuance_en: squander: foolishly lose precious, unrecoverable resources (fortune / talent) · fritter away: disperse aimlessly in small, wasteful amounts (time / savings) · burn through: consume assets with alarming speed (cash / capital) · dissipate: cause energy, wealth, or cloud to scatter and vanish (wealth / energy)
groups.nuance_zh: squander: 愚蠢挥霍大宗资产或荒废宝贵机遇 (fortune / talent) · fritter away: 零敲碎打地虚度或慢慢散尽 (time / savings) · burn through: 惊人极速地烧穿耗尽资金 (cash / capital) · dissipate: 放荡挥霍使精力财富烟消云散 (wealth / energy)

groups.name: Divide & Segment · 分割与细分 (Subdivide, Partition, Polarize)
groups.tip: 按结构或界限细分切离

items.def_en: [I/T] to divide something into separate, well-defined sections or groups
items.ex_en: The marketing department segmented the consumer database according to income and purchasing habits.
items.ex_zh: 市场部根据收入水平和购买习惯将消费者数据库进行了细分。
items.ex2_en: The developing insect embryo segments naturally within forty-eight hours of incubation.
items.ex2_zh: 发育中的昆虫胚胎在孵化四十八小时内会自然分节。

items.def_en: To divide something into smaller parts or sections.
items.ex_en: The developer chose to subdivide the historic estate into six separate residential lots.
items.ex_zh: 开发商决定将这座具有历史意义的庄园细分成六处独立的住宅地块。
items.ex2_en: The large biological cells subdivide continuously into smaller identical units.
items.ex2_zh: 这些大生物细胞不断细分成更小的相同单元。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to separate or divide an area or whole into smaller distinct sections
items.ex_en: Police sectioned off the street with tape while detectives examined the crime scene.
items.ex_zh: 当刑警勘查犯罪现场时，警方用警戒线将整条街道隔离开来。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to divide or separate into distinct smaller parts, groups, or segments
items.ex_en: After years of growing apart, the couple decided to split up peacefully.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了多年的隔阂后，这对夫妇决定和平分手。
items.ex2_en: The teacher decided to split up the talkative students into different groups.
items.ex2_zh: 老师决定把爱说话的学生们分开分配到不同的小组。

items.def_en: to divide a room, surface, or country into separate parts using walls or borders
items.ex_en: Postwar treaties partitioned the former empire into several unstable, ethnically divided nation-states.
items.ex_zh: 战后条约将前帝国分割为数个动荡且存在民族分歧的民族国家。

items.def_en: to divide into separate distinct categories, compartments, or mental sections
items.ex_en: She learned to compartmentalize her intense grief in order to remain effective at work.
items.ex_zh: 她学会将深切的悲痛封存隔开，以便在工作中保持高效。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to divide an area, company, or resource into smaller portions, often aggressively or unfairly
items.ex_en: Greedy executives quickly carved up the failing tech startup among their preferred shell companies.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的高管们迅速将这家濒临倒闭的科技初创公司瓜分给各自青睐的空壳公司。

items.def_en: 1. To divide people, opinions, or groups into two completely opposing extremes. 2. (physics) To cause light waves to oscillate in one direction.
items.ex_en: The controversial immigration policy threatens to polarize voters along deep ideological lines.
items.ex_zh: 这项饱受争议的移民政策可能会使选民沿着深刻的意识形态界线走向两极分化。
items.ex2_en: Public opinion polarized sharply following the controversial court ruling this week.
items.ex2_zh: 本周极具争议的法庭裁决出台后，公众舆论急剧两极分化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote partitioning an existing whole into smaller constituent parts, categories, or ideological extremes, altering its internal structural cohesion.
groups.summary_zh: 将一个现有整体在结构、地域或观念层面上予以切割、隔断或极化细分。
groups.desc_en: Denotes dividing a continuous space, market, or entity into distinct sectors or opposing factions, contrasting with unorganized scattering or blending.
groups.desc_zh: 指依特定标准将连续整体划分为若干清晰区块、门类或截然对立的两极，区别于散乱分割或混合揉杂。
groups.nuance_en: partition: set up physical or legal boundaries separating parts (room / country) · segment: divide into targeted, measurable slices (market / audience) · compartmentalize: separate psychologically or organizationally into isolated units (thoughts / life) · polarize: drive into sharply contrasting, hostile extremes (opinions / electorate)
groups.nuance_zh: partition: 设墙或划界割据领土与空间 (room / country) · segment: 按属性细分市场客群与数据 (market / audience) · compartmentalize: 心理或体制上刻意割裂隔离 (thoughts / life) · polarize: 撕裂分化为势不两立的两极 (opinions / electorate)

groups.name: Drink Heavily & Make Merry · 痛饮狂欢 (Carouse, Wassail, Revel)
groups.tip: 开怀畅饮彻夜狂欢庆祝

items.def_en: [I/T] to drink intoxicating liquor habitually or repeatedly, often in a social setting
items.ex_en: The aging scholar would tipple spiced sherry in the dim parlor every evening.
items.ex_zh: 那位年迈的学者每晚都会在昏暗的起居室里小酌几杯加香雪莉酒。

items.def_en: to drink a large quantity of alcohol in a lively or unrestrained social setting
items.ex_en: The whole crew went downtown to booze up after finishing their grueling shift.
items.ex_zh: 全组人在结束了令人筋疲力竭的轮班后，进城去痛饮狂欢了一番。

items.def_en: to enjoy oneself in an extravagant, boisterous, and unrestrained manner
items.ex_en: They decided to live it up in Vegas for their tenth wedding anniversary.
items.ex_zh: 他们决定在拉斯维加斯尽情狂欢，庆祝结婚十周年。

items.def_en: (informal) to drink alcohol heavily, especially in the company of others
items.ex_en: The rowdy tourists spent their entire vacation boozing beside the all-inclusive resort pool.
items.ex_zh: 那些吵闹的游客在全包度假村的泳池边痛饮了一整个假期。

items.def_en: (+ in) to take part in noisy, lively festivities or indulge deeply in merrymaking
items.ex_en: The victorious villagers reveled deep into the night beneath the harvest moon.
items.ex_zh: 获胜的村民在满月之下纵情狂欢，直至深夜。

items.def_en: [I/T] (formal or humorous) to drink alcohol, especially in a convivial atmosphere
items.ex_en: The distinguished guests imbibed vintage champagne while discussing state affairs at the gala.
items.ex_zh: 贵宾们在晚会上边品饮陈年香槟，边讨论国家大事。

items.def_en: (literary) To drink alcohol and celebrate noisily and unrestrainedly with a group of people.
items.ex_en: Drunken sailors continued to carouse noisily in the tavern until the dawn broke.
items.ex_zh: 喝得酩酊大醉的水手们一直在酒馆里喧闹狂饮，直到破晓。

items.def_zh: 痛饮狂欢；行酒祝愿，为……干杯
items.def_en: (historical or literary) To drink plentifully and celebrate noisily, especially during festive winter gatherings.
items.ex_en: Merry villagers gathered to wassail through the snowy orchard on Twelfth Night.
items.ex_zh: 欢乐的村民们在主显节前夕齐聚，穿过白雪皑皑的果园痛饮祝祷。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe engaging in boisterous, noisy, and often drunken celebration or merrymaking, typically in social gatherings. 'Carouse' and 'wassail' carry literary or archaic overtones of lively, alcohol-fueled festivities.
groups.summary_zh: 指在社交聚会中开怀畅饮、纵酒喧闹与狂欢作乐的情景。
groups.desc_en: Denotes noisy, indulgent, and communal consumption of alcohol accompanied by boisterous revelry, contrasting with solitary or modest drinking.
groups.desc_zh: 指众人喧闹放纵地痛饮烈酒并尽情狂欢寻乐，区别于独酌品酒或克制的小酌。
groups.nuance_en: carouse: drink lavish amounts noisily and rowdily (all night / with mates) · revel: indulge in exuberant celebrations and merrymaking (in victory / festivities) · booze: drink alcohol heavily or habitually (binge / heavily) · wassail: engage in old-fashioned festive communal drinking (revelers / night)
groups.nuance_zh: carouse: 通宵达旦喧嚣聚饮狂欢 (all night / with mates) · revel: 沉浸于狂喜快意中畅饮作乐 (in victory / festivities) · booze: 酗酒买醉狂饮 (binge / heavily) · wassail: 传统民俗式痛饮祝酒狂欢 (revelers / night)

groups.name: Electoral Campaigning & Politicking · 竞选拉票与政治运作 (Campaign, Politick, Stump)
groups.tip: 参与政治竞选与权力角逐

items.def_zh: 参与竞选，从事竞选活动
items.def_en: (+ for/against) to run a series of planned activities to win an election
items.ex_en: The veteran senator campaigned vigorously for healthcare reform throughout the battleground state.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深参议员在整个摇摆州为医疗改革开展了积极的竞选活动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to campaign and compete as a candidate to win an elected public office
items.ex_en: She announced her ambitious plan to run for mayor in the upcoming election.
items.ex_zh: 她宣布了雄心勃勃的计划，准备参加即将举行的市长竞选。

items.def_zh: 作为候选人竞选（议员等职位）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to compete as an official candidate in an election (chiefly British)
items.ex_en: The school management will not stand for any form of bullying on campus.
items.ex_zh: 学校管理层绝不容忍校园内出现任何形式的霸凌行为。

items.def_zh: 巡回演说拉票，在各地助选
items.def_en: [I/T] to travel around an area making political campaign speeches
items.ex_en: The charismatic candidate spent October stumping across the rust belt for union support.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有魅力的候选人整个十月都在铁锈地带巡回演说，以争取工会支持。

items.def_zh: 游说拉票，挨门挨户走访拉选票
items.def_en: [I/T] to visit voters directly to solicit votes or determine political support
items.ex_en: Volunteers canvassed every neighborhood to identify undecided voters before the crucial primary vote.
items.ex_zh: 在关键的初选之前，志愿者走访了每个街区以确定犹豫不决的选民。

items.def_zh: 进行政治活动，拉选票；搞权术活动
items.def_en: (chiefly US) To engage in political activities, campaigns, or strategic maneuvering for advantage.
items.ex_en: The mayor spent the entire fundraiser politicking with influential business leaders and donors.
items.ex_zh: 市长在整个筹款活动中都在与有影响力的商界领袖和捐助者进行政治拉拢。

items.def_zh: 巡回造势，在乡镇穿梭竞选
items.def_en: [I/T] to travel rapidly through rural areas making brief political appearances
items.ex_en: The young governor barnstormed through rural counties to rally working-class populist support.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻的州长穿梭于各个乡村县开展巡回造势，以凝聚工薪阶层的民粹支持。

items.def_zh: （在各地作短暂停留）进行巡回竞选演说
items.def_en: (chiefly US politics) To travel rapidly through small towns making brief campaign appearances or speeches.
items.ex_en: The president whistlestopped through small Midwestern towns during his historic reelection bid.
items.ex_zh: 总统在历史性的连任竞选期间，在中西部各小镇作了短暂停留的巡回演说。

groups.summary_en: Candidates and political operatives engage in public and backroom activities to win votes, gain influence, or secure public office. Verbs range from formal broad-scale campaigning to grassroots whistle-stop touring and self-interested political maneuvering.
groups.summary_zh: 候选人或政客为争取选民支持、赢得公职而进行的竞选游说与政治运作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes pursuing elective public office via grassroots travel, public speaking, and political networking, contrasting with administrative governing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过巡回演讲、深入基层拉票等运作争取选票入职公职，区别于日常施政或幕后行政管理。
groups.nuance_en: stump: tour rural or regional districts giving repetitive speeches (district / state) · canvass: solicit votes and gauge sentiment door-to-door (voters / neighborhood) · barnstorm: conduct rapid, high-energy tours across regions (country / Midwest) · politick: engage in behind-the-scenes partisan scheming (colleagues / convention)
groups.nuance_zh: stump: 巡回下基层发表大选拉票演说 (district / state) · canvass: 挨家挨户走访拉票调查民意 (voters / neighborhood) · barnstorm: 跨大区旋风式强力竞选巡演 (country / Midwest) · politick: 搞政客式钻营拉拢与幕后运作 (colleagues / convention)

groups.name: Emerge & Loom Obscurely · 显露与隐现 (Loom, Hulk, Silhouette)
groups.tip: 事物在视野中浮现或逼近

items.def_zh: 投影遮蔽；显出隐约暗影
items.def_en: cast a dark silhouette over, or appear faintly like a dark outline
items.ex_en: Tall pines shadowed the narrow dirt path as the twilight slowly faded away.
items.ex_zh: 随着暮色渐渐褪去，高大的松树在狭窄的土路上投下了一片昏暗的阴影。

items.def_en: (usually passive) To cast someone or something as a dark shape against a lighter background.
items.ex_en: The solitary guard tower was silhouetted sharply against the glowing crimson sunset.
items.ex_zh: 孤零零的岗楼在血红色的晚霞映衬下显现出清晰的轮廓。

items.def_en: to appear or loom as a large, indistinct mass
items.ex_en: A massive freighter began to bulk out through the swirling maritime morning fog.
items.ex_zh: 一艘巨大的货轮在弥漫翻腾的海上晨雾中隐约凸显出来。

items.def_en: to be easily noticeable or visually prominent against a surrounding background
items.ex_en: Her innovative approach made her application stand out from hundreds of others.
items.ex_zh: 她创新的方法使她的申请在数百人中脱颖而出。

items.def_en: (+ over/above) stand or rise to a conspicuous, imposing height
items.ex_en: Ancient volcanic peaks tower majestically above the fertile green valleys below them.
items.ex_zh: 古老的火山峰巍然耸立在下方肥沃的翠绿山谷之上。

items.def_zh: 赫然耸现，隐隐显现；逼近
items.def_en: 1. (+ over/ahead) To appear as a large, often frightening or indistinct shape. 2. (of an unpleasant event) To seem likely to happen soon.
items.ex_en: Severe budget deficits loom over the upcoming negotiations regarding national public infrastructure.
items.ex_zh: 严重的财政赤字赫然笼罩着即将举行的国家公共基础设施谈判。

items.def_zh: 庞然耸立，巍然显现；笨重地移动
items.def_en: 1. (+ over) To loom or appear massive, heavy, and imposing. 2. To move in a heavy or clumsy manner.
items.ex_en: The abandoned iron foundry hulked ominously beside the dark, heavily polluted canal.
items.ex_zh: 那座废弃的炼铁厂在昏暗且严重污染的运河边庞然耸立，显得阴森可怕。

items.def_en: cast a large, dark shadow over something, making it loom darkly
items.ex_en: Towering corporate skyscrapers overshadow the historic brick houses lining the waterfront avenue.
items.ex_zh: 耸立的企业摩天大楼遮蔽了滨水大道旁的历史红砖民居。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe large, shadowy, or threatening shapes becoming visible or standing out against a contrasting background. They emphasize visual manner—ranging from projecting a dark outline to towering menacingly through mist or darkness.
groups.summary_zh: 指庞大或阴暗的轮廓隐约显现、赫然耸立或背光勾勒。
groups.desc_en: Denotes appearing indistinctly as a massive, dark, or ominous silhouette that dwarfs its surroundings, contrasting with crisp illumination or minute appearance.
groups.desc_zh: 指在朦胧暗影中凸显出庞大、沉重或令人心生敬畏恐慌的巨大轮廓，区别于清晰明朗的显现或细小的外表。
groups.nuance_en: loom: appear vaguely in immense, threatening form (disaster / mountain) · hulk: stand or sit as an inert, bulky, heavy mass (wreck / shadow) · silhouette: project as a dark outline against a bright background (figure / skyline) · tower: rise vertically to an astonishing, dominating height (cliff / building)
groups.nuance_zh: loom: 阴森庞大地隐隐逼近或悬挂于前 (disaster / mountain) · hulk: 笨重粗大如废墟般庞然矗立 (wreck / shadow) · silhouette: 在逆光亮色背景下显现沉黑轮廓 (figure / skyline) · tower: 拔地而起巍峨耸峙远超周边 (cliff / building)

groups.name: Empathize & Commiserate · 同情与体恤怜悯 (Pity, Sympathize, Commiserate)
groups.tip: 对他人不幸心生哀怜并感同身受

items.def_en: (+ sb) to feel sympathy and compassion for someone in a difficult or painful situation
items.ex_en: I truly feel for the displaced families who lost everything in the flood.
items.ex_zh: 我由衷地同情那些在洪水中失去了一切的流离失所的家庭。

items.def_zh: 为……深感悲痛；为……心如刀绞
items.def_en: (+ sb) to feel intense sorrow, empathy, or pity for someone suffering
items.ex_en: My heart bleeds for the innocent children trapped inside the besieged city.
items.ex_zh: 我为被困在围城中的无辜孩子们深感心痛。

items.def_en: To feel sorrow, sympathy, or compassion for someone in an unfortunate or suffering condition.
items.ex_en: She could not help but pity the destitute beggar shivering in the cold.
items.ex_zh: 她不禁怜悯起那个在严寒中瑟瑟发抖的赤贫乞丐。

items.def_en: (formal or archaic) To feel deep pity or compassion for someone suffering misfortune.
items.ex_en: The benevolent magistrate compassionated the starving peasants and lowered their onerous grain taxes.
items.ex_zh: 这位仁慈的地方官怜悯饥饿的农夫，减免了他们沉重的粮食税负。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To feel or express compassion and sorrow for someone's suffering or misfortune. 2. (+ with) To agree with, support, or approve of an opinion or cause.
items.ex_en: Local authorities sympathized with the striking workers but refused to renegotiate wages immediately.
items.ex_zh: 地方当局同情罢工工人的处境，但拒绝立即重新就薪资展开谈判。

items.def_en: (+ with) to understand and directly experience the feelings and experiences of another
items.ex_en: Therapists must strive to empathize with their clients without adopting their emotional baggage.
items.ex_zh: 治疗师必须努力与患者产生共鸣，同时又不背负对方的情感包袱。

items.def_en: (+ with) to express deep sympathy or shared sorrow for someone's misfortune
items.ex_en: Colleagues gathered after the board meeting to commiserate with the demoted department director.
items.ex_zh: 董事会会议结束后，同事们聚在一起慰问那位被降职的部门主任。

items.def_en: (+ with) (formal) to express sympathy to someone who is grieving a loss
items.ex_en: Diplomats arrived at the embassy to condole with the grieving ambassador's family.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们抵达大使馆，向悲痛的大使家属致以慰问与哀悼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express affective concern, shared suffering, or sorrow for another's distress, ranging from superior pity to egalitarian empathy and shared grief.
groups.summary_zh: 指对他人的苦难或不幸心怀关切，包括居高临下的怜悯与感同身受的共情。
groups.desc_en: Cognitively sharing or outwardly acknowledging another person's distress, moving from detached sorrow to intimate emotional resonance, unlike plain intellectual understanding.
groups.desc_zh: 认知并分担或对外表达他人的痛苦与困境，从疏离的怜悯递进至深刻的情感共鸣，区别于纯粹理性的理解。
groups.nuance_en: pity: condescending or detached sorrow for another's misfortune (victim / plight) · sympathize: conscious emotional alignment and support (mourner / views) · empathize: deep visceral projection into another's feelings (patient / perspective) · commiserate: mutual verbal sharing of grief or grievance (colleague / loser) · condole: formal expression of sympathy upon bereavement (family / widow)
groups.nuance_zh: pity: 带有俯视感或疏离感的怜悯惋惜 (victim / plight) · sympathize: 理智同理与情感声援 (mourner / views) · empathize: 设身处地的深层共情沉浸 (patient / perspective) · commiserate: 相互吐槽或分担忧愁 (colleague / loser) · condole: 对丧亲家属的正式吊唁慰问 (family / widow)

groups.name: Emphasize & Accentuate · 强调与突显 (Stress, Highlight, Accentuate)
groups.tip: 特别突出重点以引起重视

items.def_zh: 强调，着重；重读；给……施加压力
items.def_en: 1. To emphasize or give special importance to a fact, point, or idea. 2. To place emphasis or stress on a word or syllable. 3. To subject something to mechanical or mental stress.
items.ex_en: The chief executive stressed the absolute necessity of rigorous quality control measures.
items.ex_zh: 首席执行官强调了采取严格质量控制措施的绝对必要性。

items.def_en: draw special attention to an important fact, issue, or detail
items.ex_en: The final audit highlighted substantial accounting discrepancies within the overseas branch offices.
items.ex_zh: 最终审计着重指出了海外分公司内部存在的重大账目出入。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to make a particular quality, feature, or contrast more prominent or noticeable
items.ex_en: The subtle lighting design brings out the delicate textures of the marble sculpture.
items.ex_zh: 巧妙的灯光设计突显了大理石雕塑细腻的纹理质感。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to draw clear attention to something or make its importance evident
items.ex_en: The crisis pointed up the urgent need for structural reform.
items.ex_zh: 这场危机凸显了进行结构性改革的紧迫性。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to emphasize or exaggerate the value or importance of something
items.ex_en: The defense attorney played up her client's spotless military record before the jury.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师在陪审团面前大肆宣扬其当事人毫无瑕疵的服役记录。

items.def_en: give special importance or prominence to something in speaking or writing
items.ex_en: The keynote speaker emphasized that technological innovation alone cannot solve climate change.
items.ex_zh: 主旨发言人强调，仅靠技术创新无法解决气候变化问题。

items.def_en: make a feature, fact, or feeling more noticeable or prominent
items.ex_en: Her tailored black suit serves to accentuate her tall and athletic physical build.
items.ex_zh: 她那身剪裁合体的黑色西装突显出了她高挑而健美的体魄。

items.def_zh: 过分强调，过分着重；使过度紧张，使承受过大压力
items.def_en: 1. To place too much emphasis on something. 2. To subject someone or something to excessive strain or stress.
items.ex_en: Parents should not overstress academic performance at the expense of a child's happiness.
items.ex_zh: 父母不应该以牺牲孩子的快乐为代价而过分强调学业成绩。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on giving cognitive, verbal, or rhetorical prominence to a fact, point, or principle to ensure listeners recognize its critical importance. Verbs vary from standard communicational emphasis to excessive or disproportionate focus.
groups.summary_zh: 在言语或论述中着重强调某事实或观点，突出其重要性。
groups.desc_en: Directing focal attention to a specific feature to make it stand out from its background, unlike merely stating or noticing it.
groups.desc_zh: 将焦点注意力定向导流至特定特征使其从背景中凸显，区别于平铺直叙地陈述或被动注意。
groups.nuance_en: stress: putting firm cognitive or rhetorical weight on an essential point (importance / need) · highlight: drawing visual or topical attention to a prominent feature (discrepancy / achievements) · accentuate: naturally sharpening or exaggerating existing contours (contrast / divide) · emphasize: broad deliberate prioritization of an idea (role / value) · play up: strategically amplifying or hyping a favorable aspect (success / credentials)
groups.nuance_zh: stress: 施加认知或修辞上的重音与强调 (importance / need) · highlight: 标定高光以吸引视觉或话题焦点 (discrepancy / achievements) · accentuate: 强化或凸显既有轮廓与反差 (contrast / divide) · emphasize: 审慎且有意识地赋予主导地位 (role / value) · play up: 策略性夸大或渲染正面亮点 (success / credentials)

groups.name: Enact & Decree · 颁布法令与司法裁决 (Enact, Promulgate, Decree)
groups.tip: 立法机构颁布法令或政策

items.def_zh: 宣布，作出（正式判决或裁定）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to deliver or announce a formal legal verdict or judicial decision officially
items.ex_en: The supreme court handed down a historic ruling regarding digital privacy rights yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院昨天就数字隐私权作出了一项具有历史意义的裁定。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to state officially and firmly that something must be done or obeyed as a rule or principle
items.ex_en: The government has laid down strict safety guidelines for the industry.
items.ex_zh: 政府为该行业制定了严格的安全指南。

items.def_zh: 颁布，制定（法律）；扮演，演出；发生，实行
items.def_en: 1. To make a proposal or bill into a law. 2. To perform a story, play, or role.
items.ex_en: Parliament will enact stringent consumer protection laws before the current session officially concludes.
items.ex_zh: 议会将在本次会议正式结束前颁布严格的消费者保护法。

items.def_zh: 颁布，发布命令；判决，裁定
items.def_en: 1. To officially order, judge, or decide something by decree.
items.ex_en: The monarch decreed that all political prisoners should receive an immediate royal pardon.
items.ex_zh: 君主颁布法令，要求对所有政治犯立即给予王室赦免。

items.def_zh: 命定，以法律或权威规定
items.def_en: to order or decree officially by virtue of superior authority or fate
items.ex_en: Ancient tradition ordained that only elder priests could enter the inner sacred temple.
items.ex_zh: 古老的传统规定，唯有年长的祭司才被准许进入内侧圣殿。

items.def_zh: 制定法律，通过立法规定
items.def_en: [I/T] to make or pass laws, especially concerning a particular issue
items.ex_en: Lawmakers must legislate responsibly against artificial intelligence misuse to protect public election integrity.
items.ex_zh: 立法者必须负责任地通过立法防范人工智能滥用，以维护公众选举的公正。

items.def_zh: 正式公布，颁布（法律、教义）
items.def_en: to formally proclaim or make known a law or decree to the public
items.ex_en: The interim council promulgated the new constitutional framework during a nationwide broadcast.
items.ex_zh: 过渡委员会在一次全国广播讲话中正式公布了新宪法框架。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a formal judgment or decision about a legal problem or disputed matter
items.ex_en: An independent international tribunal was appointed to adjudicate the complex maritime border dispute.
items.ex_zh: 一个独立的国际法庭受命裁决这起复杂的海洋划界争端。

groups.summary_en: Authorities, legislative bodies, or sovereigns formally establish laws, issue official orders, or hand down binding judicial judgments upon a state or community.
groups.summary_zh: 立法机构或掌权者正式颁布法律、发布政令或裁决。
groups.desc_en: Formally exercising sovereign, legislative, or judicial authority to institute binding legal realities, unlike informally setting rules or negotiating.
groups.desc_zh: 正式行使主权、立法或司法权威以确立具有强制约束力的法律事实，区别于非正式立规或协商约定。
groups.nuance_en: enact: passing a bill into official statutory law (legislation / reforms) · decree: unilaterally ordering by sovereign prerogative (ban / state of emergency) · ordain: appointing or establishing by divine or supreme authority (priesthood / fate) · legislate: deliberating and establishing general legal codes (standards / protections) · adjudicate: settling a legal dispute by judicial authority (claim / dispute)
groups.nuance_zh: enact: 议会表决并正式通过颁布成文法 (legislation / reforms) · decree: 凭借最高主权单方面发布具有拘束力的政令 (ban / state of emergency) · ordain: 依神权或终极权威注定或任命 (priesthood / fate) · legislate: 通过立法程序创设整体规则 (standards / protections) · adjudicate: 司法机关对争议作出裁决审处 (claim / dispute)

groups.name: Encircle & Wreathe · 环绕与缠圈 (Wreathe, Entwine, Enlace)
groups.tip: 线绳藤蔓互相缠绕交错

items.def_en: (+ sth) to curve or wind around something forming a loose circle or ring
items.ex_en: The delicate gold chain loops around her neck twice before clasping behind.
items.ex_zh: 精致的金链在她颈间缠绕了两圈，随后在后方扣合。
items.ex2_en: The careful electrician looped the copper wire around the grounding terminal.
items.ex2_zh: 细心的电工把铜线绕在了接地端子上。

items.def_en: To wind around or enfold closely, as with a band or ribbon
items.ex_en: Silken ribbons enlace the marble pillars throughout the grand illuminated ballroom.
items.ex_zh: 丝带缠绕着灯火辉煌的宏伟宴会厅中的每一根大理石柱。

items.def_en: To form a circle around something; surround completely
items.ex_en: Heavily armed federal agents encircle the perimeter of the abandoned warehouse building.
items.ex_zh: 全副武装的联邦特工包围了这座废弃仓库建筑的周边外围。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to twist, coil, or wrap continuously around a central object
items.ex_en: Wild clematis vines wind around the rusty garden trellis in dense layers.
items.ex_zh: 野生的铁线莲藤蔓层层叠叠地缠绕在生锈的花园棚架上。
items.ex2_en: The gardener wound flexible support tape around the leaning sapling stem.
items.ex2_zh: 园丁将柔性支撑胶带缠绕在倾斜的幼苗树干上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to fold or encircle closely around an object or body part
items.ex_en: She wrapped a warm woolen scarf around her neck against the chill.
items.ex_zh: 她用一条温暖的羊毛围巾裹住脖子以抵御严寒。
items.ex2_en: A thick layer of morning mist wrapped around the mountain peak.
items.ex2_zh: 一层厚厚的晨雾笼罩缠绕在山峰周围。

items.def_en: To adorn or encircle with or as if with a garland or wreath
items.ex_en: Local villagers garland the ancient stone altar with fresh jasmine blossoms every spring.
items.ex_zh: 每年春天，当地村民都会用新鲜的茉莉花环装饰那座古老的石祭坛。

items.def_en: (+ with/around) To twist or wind things closely together or around something else.
items.ex_en: Ancient oak boughs entwine above the forest trail, creating a natural vaulted ceiling.
items.ex_zh: 古老的橡树枝在林间小道上方交织盘绕，形成了一座天然的拱顶。
items.ex2_en: The florist entwined delicate ivy branches around the wedding arch pillars.
items.ex2_zh: 花艺师把精致的常春藤枝条缠绕在婚礼拱门的柱子上。

items.def_zh: 盘绕，环绕，笼罩；编成花环
items.def_en: (+ in/with) (literary, often passive) To encircle, surround, or cover something with or as if with a wreath (such as mist, smoke, or flowers).
items.ex_en: The snow-capped mountain crest was wreathed in thick, swirling morning mists.
items.ex_zh: 白雪覆盖的山顶被厚重翻滚的晨雾重重笼罩。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe winding, curling, or draping something around an object in a decorative, continuous, or enveloping loop or crown. 'Wreathe' centers on encircling or crowning like a garland, whereas 'entwine' denotes winding lovingly or decoratively around something.
groups.summary_zh: 如花环或藤蔓般围绕、环抱或紧贴盘绕于物体周围。
groups.desc_en: Forming an encircling or intertwining boundary around an object with flexible, decorative, or sinuous elements, unlike rigid mechanical boxing.
groups.desc_zh: 以柔性、装饰性或蜿蜒盘旋的元素构成环抱或交织的环带，区别于刚性的机械式围挡。
groups.nuance_en: encircle: forming an unbroken circular boundary around something (island / campfire) · wreathe: curling around in decorative coils or clouds (head / smoke) · entwine: twisting closely together in mutual spiraling (threads / vines) · enlace: intricately interlacing or binding as with ribbons (limbs / ribbons) · garland: adorning ceremoniously with floral rings (statue / winner)
groups.nuance_zh: encircle: 呈环状无缝围成一周 (island / campfire) · wreathe: 如花环或烟雾般盘旋环绕 (head / smoke) · entwine: 相互缠绕绞结在一起 (threads / vines) · enlace: 错综交织或如带状缠结 (limbs / ribbons) · garland: 以花环或彩带进行节庆式环绕装点 (statue / winner)

groups.name: Enclose & Belt · 环绕与带状包围 (Environ, Girdle, Gird)
groups.tip: 环形包夹周遭围拢

items.def_en: to encircle or surround something with a strip or continuous ring
items.ex_en: Dozens of colorful flowerbeds belt the outer lawns of the university campus.
items.ex_zh: 数十个五彩斑斓的花坛如带般环绕着大学校园的外侧草坪。

items.def_en: (formal/literary) to encircle completely as if with a ring
items.ex_en: Towering basalt sea cliffs enring the mysterious forgotten island on all sides.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的玄武岩海蚀崖从四面如套环般完全环绕着这座神秘的荒岛。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to surround or enclose an area with a fence or boundary structure
items.ex_en: The rancher worked all afternoon to fence in the expanding horse pasture.
items.ex_zh: 牧场主忙碌了整个下午，用栅栏将扩建的马匹牧场围了起来。

items.def_zh: 严密包围；围住使无法脱身
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround someone or something tightly so that movement is restricted
items.ex_en: Heavy police barricades hemmed in the protesters along the crowded downtown boulevard.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的警察路障将抗议者严密包围在拥挤的市中心林荫大道上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to enclose or isolate an area with walls or barriers
items.ex_en: Part of the courtyard was walled off to create a private garden.
items.ex_zh: 院子的一部分被砌墙隔开，改造成了一个私人花园。

items.def_en: 1. (literary or archaic) To surround, encircle, or enclose completely.
items.ex_en: High protective stone ramparts environ the ancient fortress against hostile foreign invasions.
items.ex_zh: 高耸防护的石质壁垒环抱围绕着这座古老的要塞，以御外敌入侵。

items.def_zh: 围绕，环绕；用带状物束紧；环剥（树皮）
items.def_en: 1. (literary) To surround or encircle something like a belt. 2. To cut a ring of bark from around the trunk of a tree.
items.ex_en: Ancient stone walls girdle the quiet medieval town against northern winter winds.
items.ex_zh: 古老的石墙如带般环绕着这座中世纪小镇，抵御着北方的冬风。

items.def_en: to encircle or secure with a belt or band; to enclose defensively
items.ex_en: Towering ramparts gird the sanctuary to repel invaders during times of siege.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的城墙环绕防护着圣所，以在围城时期抵御入侵者。

groups.summary_en: Physical objects, environmental features, or protective bands encircle a central area like a belt or perimeter wall. While 'environ' belongs to high-register geographic or environmental setting and 'girdle' evokes a circular band cinching or binding an area, related formal verbs denote structural, defensive, or anatomical belting.
groups.summary_zh: 指地貌、带状物或防护结构如腰带般紧密围绕或束缚某物。
groups.desc_en: Establishing a continuous perimeter around an area to contain, secure, or demarcate it, unlike open-ended bordering.
groups.desc_zh: 沿区域外沿建立闭合环带以实施阻隔、封控或界定，区别于单侧无封口的接壤边界。
groups.nuance_en: girdle: encircling like a wide belt or physical boundary (city / equator) · gird: binding or surrounding for defensive readiness (loins / fortress) · hem in: confining tightly to restrict outward movement (refugees / traffic) · fence in: enclosing physically or socially with barriers (pasture / cattle) · environ: encompassing as an ambient natural or social surroundings (forest / suburbs)
groups.nuance_zh: girdle: 宛如带状地貌或束带般环抱周匝 (city / equator) · gird: 束紧或构筑防御性包围环 (loins / fortress) · hem in: 紧迫逼仄地围困以阻绝外逃 (refugees / traffic) · fence in: 用栅栏或屏障在物理上圈围禁锢 (pasture / cattle) · environ: 自然或社会性地环绕环抱 (forest / suburbs)

groups.name: Engrave & Inscribe into Surfaces · 雕刻与铭刻 (Engrave, Inscribe, Etch)
groups.tip: 把文字或图案深刻表面

items.def_en: (+ sth) to create a shape, design, or inscription by cutting away a hard material
items.ex_en: The sculptor carefully carved out a delicate floral motif from the marble block.
items.ex_zh: 雕刻师从这块大理石中精心雕刻出了一道精致的花卉图案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cut, form, or inscribe deeply into stone, metal, or wood using a chisel
items.ex_en: The mason chiseled out the fallen king's epitaph upon the granite monument.
items.ex_zh: 石匠在花岗岩纪念碑上凿出了那位陨落国王的墓志铭。

items.def_en: [I/T] to produce a shape or inscription by cutting away material from wood or stone
items.ex_en: The craftsman carved delicate geometric patterns directly onto the oak headboard.
items.ex_zh: 工匠直接在橡木床头板上刻出了精致的几何图案。

items.def_en: 1. (+ on/with) To cut words, pictures, or patterns into a hard surface such as stone, metal, or wood. 2. (often passive) To impress deeply on the mind or memory.
items.ex_en: The jeweler will engrave your initials on the inside of the gold ring.
items.ex_zh: 珠宝商会把您名字的首字母铭刻在这枚金戒指的内圈。

items.def_en: 1. to press or stamp a mark or design onto a surface. 2. to fix an idea, memory, or feeling firmly in someone's mind.
items.ex_en: Heavy metal stamps imprint the official seal upon every authentic certificate issued.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的金属印章在每份发放的正规证书上压印出官方标志。

items.def_zh: 蚀刻，雕刻；深深印在，使铭记
items.def_en: 1. to cut lines or designs into metal, glass, or stone using acid or a sharp tool. 2. to make a strong, clear, or unforgettable impression on someone's mind.
items.ex_en: The artisan etched a detailed coastal landscape onto the dark glass panel.
items.ex_zh: 工匠在这块深色玻璃板上蚀刻出了一幅细致的海岸风景。

items.def_en: to cut precisely into a hard surface with a sharp tool to form letters or designs
items.ex_en: Calligraphers incised ancient religious verses into the smooth slate tablets.
items.ex_zh: 书法家们将古老的宗教经文细致雕刻进光滑的石板之中。

items.def_en: to carve or cut stone, wood, or metal into shapes using a chisel
items.ex_en: He chiseled a deep groove into the stone sill to drain rainwater.
items.ex_zh: 他在石质窗台上凿出一条深槽以排出积攒的雨水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify cutting, biting with acid, or incising words, designs, or memories deeply into a hard medium so that the mark remains permanent and prominent.
groups.summary_zh: 指用刀刻、酸蚀等方式在坚硬表面或心底留下永久的印记或文字。
groups.desc_en: Cutting, incising, or biting deeply into a hard substrate to leave permanent graphic marks, unlike surface painting or temporary printing.
groups.desc_zh: 通过切削、刻划或化学咬蚀在硬质基底上留下永久性图文印记，区别于表层的喷涂或易损印制。
groups.nuance_en: carve: shaping or gouging material three-dimensionally with blade tools (wood / statue) · engrave: precision-cutting linear text or designs into hard plates (tombstone / plaque) · etch: eroding fine lines chemically or using acid/lasers (glass / circuit) · chisel: hacking or sculpting stone/wood with brute percussive strikes (marble / block) · incise: making clean, sharp surgical or decorative cuts into a surface (grooves / line)
groups.nuance_zh: carve: 以刀具立体切削或镂空构型 (wood / statue) · engrave: 在硬质金属或石材上精密镌刻铭文 (tombstone / plaque) · etch: 利用酸液腐蚀或激光蚀刻出纤细线条 (glass / circuit) · chisel: 用凿具施加冲击力凿削石木 (marble / block) · incise: 利刃划出规整锐利的凹纹或切口 (grooves / line)

groups.name: Entertain & Amuse · 娱乐与愉悦 (Provide Enjoyment / Amusement)
groups.tip: 逗人开心并带来轻松快乐的心境

items.def_zh: 使欢乐，使娱乐；招待，款待；抱有，考虑（想法、希望等）
items.def_en: 1. To interest and amuse someone. 2. To invite people as guests and provide food and drink for them. 3. To consider or hold a thought, idea, or feeling in your mind.
items.ex_en: The traveling magician entertained the audience with clever card tricks for hours.
items.ex_zh: 巡回魔术师用巧妙的扑克把戏逗乐了观众整整几个小时。

items.def_zh: 使高兴，使愉悦；以……为乐，感到高兴
items.def_en: 1. To give someone great pleasure or satisfaction. 2. (delight in) To take great pleasure in doing something.
items.ex_en: Her witty storytelling delighted the banquet guests throughout the long evening.
items.ex_zh: 她风趣诙谐的讲述在漫长的晚宴上给客人们带来了极大愉悦。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to make someone laugh suddenly and uncontrollably with amusement
