items.ex_en: Her impression of the boss made everyone in the room crack up.
items.ex_zh: 她模仿老板的样子让屋里的所有人都笑得前仰后合。
items.ex2_en: The reckless driver managed to crack up his father's expensive luxury car.
items.ex2_zh: 那个鲁莽的司机把他父亲昂贵的豪华轿车给撞毁了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to make someone feel happier, entertained, and more cheerful
items.ex_en: A warm bowl of soup helped cheer up the exhausted hikers considerably.
items.ex_zh: 一碗热汤极大地让疲惫不堪的徒步者们振作快活了起来。
items.ex2_en: The gloomy little boy cheered up immediately upon seeing his birthday gifts.
items.ex2_zh: 那个闷闷不乐的小男孩一看到生日礼物，立刻高兴了起来。

items.def_en: to cause sb to laugh, smile, or feel pleasantly entertained
items.ex_en: His ridiculous costume amused everyone who attended the office charity luncheon.
items.ex_zh: 他滑稽滑头的装扮逗乐了所有参加办公室慈善午餐的人。

items.def_en: to pleasantly distract or entertain sb away from care or routine work
items.ex_en: A brief stroll in the garden diverted his mind from demanding work duties.
items.ex_zh: 在花园里散步片刻让他得以解闷，暂时摆脱了繁重的工作职责。

items.def_zh: 以吸引力取悦/消磨（时光）
items.def_en: to charm, delight, or enchant sb, often helping time pass pleasantly
items.ex_en: The bard beguiled the weary travelers with romantic tales of forgotten realms.
items.ex_zh: 吟游诗人用被遗忘国度的浪漫故事消磨着疲惫旅人的时光。

items.def_en: (+ with) to entertain sb lavishly with stories, jokes, or fine food and drink
items.ex_en: Uncle Arthur regaled us with thrilling stories from his years in Africa.
items.ex_zh: 亚瑟叔叔用他在非洲那些年遇到的惊险故事把我们逗得十分开心。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to providing pleasurable diversion, laughter, or intellectual enjoyment to an audience or individual, ranging from general hospitality to evoking genuine mirth or charm.
groups.summary_zh: 提供消遣、引人发笑或取悦他人，强调营造欢愉与娱乐体验。
groups.desc_en: Pleasantly occupying someone's attention through humor, spectacle, or hospitality, unlike merely pacifying or informing them.
groups.desc_zh: 通过幽默、展演或周全款待令人心生欢悦并转移注意力，区别于机械安抚或单向传达信息。
groups.nuance_en: entertain: providing hospitality, shows, or varied diversions for guests (guests / crowd) · amuse: provoking mild laughter, smiles, or playful interest (children / reader) · delight: causing keen sensory or intellectual pleasure (audience / senses) · beguile: charming or enchanting, sometimes with a mesmerizing or deceptive tinge (traveler / hours) · regale: lavishing someone with tales, jokes, or rich feasts (crowd / listener)
groups.nuance_zh: entertain: 组织节目、待客或展演以长时取悦宾客 (guests / crowd) · amuse: 逗乐或唤起轻松有趣的注意 (children / reader) · delight: 赋予极其敏锐的感官或心智愉悦 (audience / senses) · beguile: 以迷人魅力或幻象令人浑然忘忧 (traveler / hours) · regale: 滔滔不绝讲述逸事或盛情款待 (crowd / listener)

groups.name: Erosion & Destabilization · 动摇与瓦解 (Erode, Undermine, Destabilize)
groups.tip: 破坏平衡态势，使系统陷入混乱

items.def_en: To gradually diminish or cause something to diminish in size or integrity through friction, erosion, or prolonged stress
items.ex_en: Continuous foot traffic can wear away the polished stone steps over decades.
items.ex_zh: 数十年间持续不断的行人人流会逐渐磨损这些光洁的石阶。
items.ex2_en: The soft rubber soles wore away gradually on rough gravel paths.
items.ex2_zh: 柔软的橡胶鞋底在粗糙的碎石路上逐渐磨损了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to wear away or diminish the strength, power, or stability of something slowly over time
items.ex_en: Unchecked corruption will gradually erode public trust in our judicial system.
items.ex_zh: 若不加制止，腐败将随着时间推移逐步削弱公众对司法体制的信任。
items.ex2_en: Coastal limestone cliffs erode slowly against relentless violent winter ocean waves.
items.ex2_zh: 沿海的石灰岩悬崖在无休止的冬日狂浪拍打下缓慢侵蚀。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To gradually diminish, weaken, or undermine power, stability, or confidence in small increments
items.ex_en: Rising utility costs continue to chip away at our monthly savings cushion.
items.ex_zh: 不断上涨的公用事业费用正持续一点点蚕食我们的每月储蓄储备。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To gradually damage, erode, or weaken a physical structure or abstract foundation over time
items.ex_en: The unresolved guilt continued to eat away at him for years.
items.ex_zh: 那份未解的内疚感多年来持续折磨着他的内心。

items.def_en: to weaken or ruin a system, authority, or foundation gradually or insidiously from below
items.ex_en: Spreading false rumors will undermine the fragile credibility of our management team.
items.ex_zh: 散布虚假谣言会暗中动摇我们管理团队本就脆弱的公信力。

items.def_zh: 颠覆；暗中破坏（政权、原则）
items.def_en: to undermine the power and authority of an established system or institution from within
items.ex_en: Rebel officers plotted to subvert the constitutional government from within its ranks.
items.ex_zh: 叛乱军官密谋从内部颠覆这个立宪政府的统治与权威。

items.def_zh: 破坏……的稳定，动摇，使陷入混乱
items.def_en: To make a system, government, or economy unstable and likely to fail or collapse.
items.ex_en: The sudden currency collapse threatens to destabilize the entire regional economy.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的货币崩溃面临动摇整个地区经济稳定的大危机。
items.ex2_en: The shaky government coalition destabilized rapidly under intense public scrutiny yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 在昨天公众的严密审视下，摇摇欲坠的执政联盟迅速瓦解动摇了。

items.def_zh: 使脱轨；使严重失衡紊乱
items.def_en: to throw a system, operation, or person into total disorder and instability
items.ex_en: The sudden supply shock threatened to unhinge the fragile international trade network.
items.ex_zh: 突发的供应冲击有可能使脆弱的国际贸易网络陷入严重混乱失衡。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures intentional or gradual actions that compromise the balance, structure, or security of a system, institution, or physical foundation, ranging from imperceptible wear to outright subversion.
groups.summary_zh: 通过逐渐侵蚀、暗中破坏或颠覆机制，使原本稳固的体系或结构陷入动荡与瓦解。
groups.desc_en: Progressively wearing away the physical, political, or cognitive foundations of a system, unlike instant demolition.
groups.desc_zh: 循序渐进地侵蚀物理、政治或认知基础直至整体瓦解，区别于瞬间的暴力拆除或摧毁。
groups.nuance_en: erode: wearing away material or abstract standing by friction or gradual process (coastline / confidence) · undermine: secretly or subtly weakening structural foundations from below (authority / credibility) · destabilize: upsetting equilibrium and making an entity volatile (regime / market) · chip away at: incrementally breaking down a large obstacle piece by piece (lead / margin) · unhinge: violently throwing a mind or complex structure off balance (sanity / mind)
groups.nuance_zh: erode: 经年累月受冲刷磨蚀而逐渐退化 (coastline / confidence) · undermine: 从底部或内部暗中掏空基石 (authority / credibility) · destabilize: 打破原有力量平衡令其动荡飘摇 (regime / market) · chip away at: 蚕食式一点一滴削弱庞然大物 (lead / margin) · unhinge: 使心智或复杂机制骤然脱轨失常 (sanity / mind)

groups.name: Erupt & Gush Forwards · 喷射、倒出与倾泻 (Gush, Disgorge, Effuse)
groups.tip: 液体或物体大量涌出、喷出

items.def_en: To flow, rush, or emerge rapidly and abundantly from an enclosure or container
items.ex_en: She poured out her troubles to her best friend over coffee.
items.ex_zh: 她一边喝咖啡一边向闺蜜倾诉自己的烦恼。
items.ex2_en: Tearful grievances poured out uncontrollably as she confronted her estranged family members.
items.ex2_zh: 当她面对疏远的家人时，满腹委屈泪如雨下地倾泻而出。

items.def_en: To gush or shoot forward suddenly and forcefully from an opening
items.ex_en: A stream of scalding water spurt out through the ruptured radiator cap.
items.ex_zh: 一股滚烫的热水突然从破损的水箱盖裂口处猛烈喷出。
items.ex2_en: The punctured garden hose spurted out cold water across the lawn.
items.ex2_zh: 被刺破的花园水管将冷水喷射到了草坪各处。

items.def_en: (+ from/out) to flow out suddenly and in large volumes with considerable momentum
items.ex_en: Black oil began to gush from the fractured pipeline beneath the bay.
items.ex_zh: 黑色原油开始从海湾下方破裂的输油管道中大量喷涌而出。
items.ex2_en: The deep underground fissure gushed boiling muddy water into the valley.
items.ex2_zh: 地下深处的裂缝向山谷中喷涌出滚烫的泥水。

items.def_en: To eject, discharge, or expel contents violently or copiously outward
items.ex_en: Faulty exhaust vents spew out foul smog into the nearby residential courtyard.
items.ex_zh: 故障的排气口向附近的住宅院落里大量喷射出难闻的烟雾。
items.ex2_en: Thick grey smoke spewed out continuously from the damaged industrial boiler.
items.ex2_zh: 受损的工业锅炉不断喷出滚滚浓烟。

items.def_en: [I/T] to expel large quantities of something rapidly, violently, and often unpleasantly
items.ex_en: The active volcano continues to spew noxious ash over surrounding farming communities.
items.ex_zh: 这座活火山持续向周围的农业村落喷出大量有害的火山灰。
items.ex2_en: Scalding volcanic gases spewed from deep fissures in the barren ground.
items.ex2_zh: 滚烫的火山气体从贫瘠地面的深裂缝中喷涌而出。

items.def_en: [I/T] to send out or emerge in a rapid and vigorous stream, jet, or surge
items.ex_en: Pressurized water spouted high into the air from the broken street hydrant.
items.ex_zh: 承压的水流从街头破裂的消防栓中向空中猛烈喷射而出。
items.ex2_en: The damaged water main spouted icy muddy water into the street.
items.ex2_zh: 受损的主水管将冰冷浑浊的水喷射到了街道上。

items.def_zh: （大量）涌出，喷出，吐出；被迫交出（非法所得）
items.def_en: 1. To pour or discharge liquid, gas, or contents out quickly and in large quantities; (of a vehicle or building) to empty out people. 2. To surrender or give back money or goods obtained illegally.
items.ex_en: The overloaded ferry disgorged hundreds of anxious passengers onto the damp wharf.
items.ex_zh: 超载的渡轮将数百名焦急的乘客如潮水般吐卸在潮湿的码头上。

items.def_zh: 涌出，流出，泻出；倾泻（情感等）
items.def_en: To pour out or flow out freely; to express emotions or thoughts with unrestrained enthusiasm.
items.ex_en: The wounded soldier effused dark blood onto the muddy trench floor.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的士兵将暗红的鲜血不断倾泻在泥泞的战壕地面上。
items.ex2_en: Bright yellow sparks effused copiously from the molten iron furnace opening.
items.ex2_zh: 明黄色的火星从熔铁炉口大量溢出。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict the sudden, forceful, or copious expulsion of liquids, crowds, or interior contents outward from an enclosed space or receptacle.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重液体或内含物从封闭空间内突然、猛烈或大体量向外喷涌倒出。
groups.desc_en: Discharging fluids, matter, or speech with violent velocity or overwhelming volume, unlike steady trickling or controlled pouring.
groups.desc_zh: 以爆裂般的高速或不可遏止的巨大体量向外宣泄流体、物质或言辞，区别于平稳滴流或受控倾倒。
groups.nuance_en: gush: pouring out suddenly and copiously under pressure (oil / blood) · spew: ejecting foul, molten, or chaotic matter violently and indiscriminately (lava / toxic fumes) · spout: discharging in a forceful, focused jet or stream (water / rhetoric) · disgorge: emptying contents rapidly or unwillingly from an enclosed space (passengers / floodwaters) · effuse: flowing out unrestrainedly, often used of warmth or sentiments (light / praise)
groups.nuance_zh: gush: 承压剧烈且大量地奔涌喷射 (oil / blood) · spew: 狂暴且无规律地吐出脏污或熔浆杂物 (lava / toxic fumes) · spout: 呈管束状集中向外强力喷涌 (water / rhetoric) · disgorge: 空间受迫吐出或一次性倾泻容纳物 (passengers / floodwaters) · effuse: 充沛、不受限地散溢流淌或热情倾诉 (light / praise)

groups.name: Establish & Codify · 确立与建制 (Institute, Institutionalize, Enact)
groups.tip: 设立机构推行成制

items.def_en: to set up an organization, system, or set of rules on a firm or permanent basis
items.ex_en: The coalition government aims to establish clear regulatory guidelines for digital currencies.
items.ex_zh: 联合政府旨在为数字货币建立起一套明确的监管规范制度。

items.def_zh: 建立，制定；实行，开创；提起（诉讼）
items.def_en: 1. to introduce, establish, or initiate a system, policy, or practice. 2. to start or initiate a legal proceeding.
items.ex_en: The university decided to institute stricter safety protocols across all research laboratories.
items.ex_zh: 该大学决定在所有科研实验室中正式实行更为严格的安全规程。

items.def_zh: 引进，实施（新法律或制度）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to introduce and enact a new law, system, or administrative regulation
items.ex_en: Parliament plans to bring in tough environmental standards for automobile manufacturers.
items.ex_zh: 议会计划针对汽车制造商出台并实施严苛的环境新规。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to include a formal provision, clause, or restriction expressly within a codified legal document
items.ex_en: Lawmakers managed to write in specific protections for freelance workers before passage.
items.ex_zh: 立法者赶在法案通过前将针对自由职业者的特定保护条款明文列入其中。

items.def_en: to make a proposal or bill into official law through a legislature
items.ex_en: The legislature voted to enact sweeping reforms across the primary healthcare network.
items.ex_zh: 立法机关投票正式通过了针对基层医疗网络的全面改革法案。

items.def_zh: 使处于牢固地位；牢固确立
items.def_en: to establish an attitude, habit, or position so firmly that change is very difficult
items.ex_en: Decades of political patronage only served to entrench corrupt bureaucratic practices firmly.
items.ex_zh: 数十年的政治恩庇只会让腐败的官僚陋习在体制内彻底根深蒂固。

items.def_zh: 使制度化，使成惯例；把……送入收容机构（如疗养院、精神病院）
items.def_en: 1. to establish a practice, custom, or norm as an accepted and permanent part of an organization or society. 2. to place someone in a long-term care institution such as a hospital or psychiatric facility.
items.ex_en: The ministry sought to institutionalize annual audits for all public health agencies.
items.ex_zh: 该部委试图让所有公共卫生机构的年度审计制度化并成为惯例。

items.def_zh: 编纂（法典）；将…条理化/法典化
items.def_en: to arrange laws, rules, or principles into a systematic official code
items.ex_en: Legal scholars gathered for months to codify regional maritime trade regulations systematically.
items.ex_zh: 法学学者们汇聚数月，旨在系统地将区域海事贸易法规编纂成法典。

groups.summary_en: Authorities, societies, or organizations formally set up, enact, or deeply embed laws, customs, or administrative practices into an enduring official structure. Verbs range from inaugurating a system to embedding it irrevocably into cultural or legal norms.
groups.summary_zh: 正式创立制度、颁布法律，或将其深度融入体制系统。
groups.desc_en: Imparting formal, enduring, and systematic status to practices or principles through authoritative codification, unlike keeping ad-hoc traditions.
groups.desc_zh: 通过权威法制化程序赋予惯例或准则以正规、持久且体系化的制度地位，区别于临时约定或非正式俗成。
groups.nuance_en: institute: formally initiating and putting a system into operation (inquiry / reforms) · codify: compiling unwritten norms or scattered rules into an authoritative code (laws / principles) · institutionalize: embedding a practice permanently into societal or organizational structures (corruption / racism) · entrench: establishing a power or privilege so firmly that change is difficult (privilege / positions) · enact: legally voting and ratifying policies into force (statute / measures)
groups.nuance_zh: institute: 正式立项开创并推行体系运作 (inquiry / reforms) · codify: 将零散习惯法或原则法典化、条理化 (laws / principles) · institutionalize: 使特定行为模式深深固化为体制常态 (corruption / racism) · entrench: 构筑坚固防线使特权或理念盘根错节 (privilege / positions) · enact: 依法通过并赋予其法理效力 (statute / measures)

groups.name: Establish & Found Entities · 创立与设立组织 (Establish, Found, Institute)
groups.tip: 奠定根基确立组织制度

items.def_zh: 创立，创建，建立；把……建立在（某基础上）
items.def_en: 1. to establish an organization, institution, or city. 2. (be founded on/upon) to base something on a particular principle, idea, or fact
items.ex_en: Pioneering researchers helped found the nation's premier astronomical institute in 1952.
items.ex_zh: 先驱研究者们于1952年协助创立了该国最顶尖的天文研究所。

items.def_zh: 建立，设立，创办；确立，证实
items.def_en: 1. to start or set up an organization, company, or system on a firm basis. 2. to achieve widespread acceptance or recognition; to prove or ascertain
items.ex_en: The tech veteran hopes to establish a research facility in his hometown.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深技术专家希望在家乡设立并创办一家研发机构。

items.def_zh: 制定，设立，开创（制度/规程）
items.def_en: to introduce or officially establish an organization, system, rule, or inquiry
items.ex_en: The board decided to institute an independent review committee regarding financial misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定正式设立一个独立审查委员会来调查财务不端行为。

items.def_en: to legally register a business enterprise as an official corporate entity
items.ex_en: The entrepreneurs worked with legal counsel to incorporate their logistics company.
items.ex_zh: 创业者们与法律顾问合作，正式注册成立了他们的物流法人公司。

items.def_zh: 创立，建立（企业、机构、组织）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to establish, found, or formally organize a company, institution, or system
items.ex_en: Two local activists helped set up a regional wildlife rescue organization.
items.ex_zh: 两位当地活动家协助创办并建立了一家地区野生动物救助组织。
items.ex2_en: The new community dental clinic set up within three busy weeks.
items.ex2_zh: 新的社区牙科诊所在忙碌的三周之内就建立了起来。

items.def_zh: 开创；创办（商业或实体组织）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to begin, launch, and establish a new business venture or operational entity
items.ex_en: Young software engineers gathered in the garage to start up a consultancy.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的软件工程师们聚集在车库里开创了一家咨询服务实体。
items.ex2_en: The computer system starts up automatically every morning at eight o'clock.
items.ex2_zh: 电脑系统每天早晨八点钟都会自动启动。

items.def_zh: 正式设立，组建（委员会/法定机构）
items.def_en: to establish or set up an official body, tribunal, or authority in legal form
items.ex_en: The treaty authorized member nations to constitute a joint arbitration panel immediately.
items.ex_zh: 该条约授权各成员国立即依法正式组建一个联合仲裁庭。

items.def_zh: 自力更生创办，白手起家；[计] 引导，自举
items.def_en: 1. to start or build a business or project using only one's own limited resources without external help. 2. (computing) to boot or load a program into a computer using a smaller initial program
items.ex_en: With zero venture funding, the team managed to bootstrap their software business.
items.ex_zh: 在毫无风险投资的情况下，该团队完全自力更生创办起软件业务。

groups.summary_en: Verbs describing the deliberate act of creating, formalizing, and placing an enduring organization, system, school, or corporate enterprise on a firm footing.
groups.summary_zh: 正式创立、设立并稳固推行组织、机构、制度或企业。
groups.desc_en: Originating, organizing, and bringing an ongoing corporate or institutional entity into lawful existence, unlike merely starting an activity.
groups.desc_zh: 构想、组织并使具有持续运作能力的法人或机构实体在法律和实际上成立，区别于单纯开展单项活动。
groups.nuance_en: found: establishing an institution with initial capital, philosophy, or charter (university / dynasty) · establish: setting an organization or company on a firm, lasting basis (network / headquarters) · incorporate: legally constituting an enterprise as a distinct corporate body (business / company) · set up: practical assembling and launching of an enterprise or apparatus (shop / committee) · bootstrap: starting a business from scratch relying strictly on self-generated funds (startup / enterprise)
groups.nuance_zh: found: 奠定资本、愿景或章程而奠基创立 (university / dynasty) · establish: 构筑坚实根基以使组织长久立足 (network / headquarters) · incorporate: 依法完成注册取得独立法人资格 (business / company) · set up: 筹备搭建硬件与团队以启动营运 (shop / committee) · bootstrap: 白手起家、依靠自有原始积累滚动创设 (startup / enterprise)

groups.name: Even Surface Coating · 涂覆、裹覆与抹匀 (Coat, Butter, Spread)
groups.tip: 将油脂或涂料均匀抹在表面

items.def_en: (+ sth) To apply an ointment, cream, or substance onto a surface and rub until it forms an even layer or absorbs
items.ex_en: Gently rub in the moisturizing balm until the dry skin absorbs it.
items.ex_zh: 轻轻把保湿霜涂抹抹匀，直到干燥的皮肤完全将其吸收进去。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To apply a substance evenly and smoothly across an entire surface
items.ex_en: The search team spread out across the forest to look for the missing hikers.
items.ex_zh: 搜救队在森林中分散开来寻找失踪的徒步旅行者。
items.ex2_en: The gardener spread out fresh wood mulch evenly across the flowerbeds.
items.ex2_zh: 园丁把新鲜的木屑均匀地铺撒在各个花坛上。

items.def_en: [I/T] to apply a substance across a flat surface in an even, continuous layer
items.ex_en: She used a wide spatula to spread strawberry jam across the toast.
items.ex_zh: 她用宽刮刀把草莓果酱均匀地摊平涂抹在烤面包片上。
items.ex2_en: Soft cream cheese spreads smoothly across warm toasted bagels every morning.
items.ex2_zh: 软质奶油奶酪每天早晨都能顺滑地涂抹在烤热的百吉饼上。

items.def_zh: 涂黄油于；讨好，奉承（butter up）
items.def_en: 1. To spread butter on something. 2. (in 'butter up') To flatter someone to gain an advantage.
items.ex_en: The chef demonstrated how to butter the baking sheets before pouring batter.
items.ex_zh: 主厨示范了在倒入面糊之前如何将黄油涂抹在烤盘上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To spread or coat a thick, generous layer of a substance over a surface
items.ex_en: Beachgoers slather on thick sunblock before heading toward the crowded sunny shore.
items.ex_zh: 去海滩的人在走向阳光充足、人头攒动的海岸前厚厚涂抹上防晒霜。

items.def_zh: 给……涂上一层，覆上；穿上外套
items.def_en: To cover the surface of something with a thin layer of a substance.
items.ex_en: The factory workers coat each steel chassis with rust-resistant epoxy paint.
items.ex_zh: 工厂工人们在每个钢制底盘上均匀涂覆上一层防锈环氧漆。

items.def_en: to cover with a thin, shiny liquid or culinary mixture that hardens smoothly
items.ex_en: The pastry chef gently glazed each warm bun with sweet sugar syrup.
items.ex_zh: 面点师在每个温热的小圆面包上轻轻刷涂上一层甜糖浆上光。
items.ex2_en: The wet highway glazed over with black ice during subzero temperatures.
items.ex2_zh: 潮湿的公路在零度以下的低温中结上了一层光滑的薄冰。

items.def_en: to apply a protective, glossy coat of resinous liquid over wood or metal
items.ex_en: Woodworkers varnish the antique walnut dining table to protect its rich grain.
items.ex_zh: 木匠们为这张胡桃木古董餐桌刷上清漆，以保护其深邃的纹理。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote providing a functional, culinary, or protective layer uniformly across a surface (e.g., buttering toast, coating metal or food uniformly).
groups.summary_zh: 指在物体表层均匀覆盖或涂抹一层功能性、保护性或食用性涂层。
groups.desc_en: Applying a layer of viscous or fluid substance across a surface to cover, protect, or finish it, unlike spot-staining or soaking.
groups.desc_zh: 在基底表面均匀施加一层黏性或流质物质以达成覆盖、保护或饰面效果，区别于局部的浸染或渗泡。
groups.nuance_en: spread: distributing a substance across a surface in an even layer (jam / butter) · coat: covering entirely with an exterior protective or finishing layer (paint / chocolate) · slather on: applying an extravagantly thick, messy layer (sunscreen / lotion) · glaze: brushing with a thin glossy coat that shines or hardens (pottery / pastry) · varnish: finishing wood or resin with a hard, clear protective seal (table / floor)
groups.nuance_zh: spread: 延展开来使介质形成平整薄层 (jam / butter) · coat: 全面包覆上一层外护层或外膜 (paint / chocolate) · slather on: 厚重甚至过量地大坨涂抹 (sunscreen / lotion) · glaze: 刷涂一层透光发亮的晶状或糖色光泽 (pottery / pastry) · varnish: 为木器等封上一层坚硬透明的罩光漆 (table / floor)

groups.name: Exact Reproduction & Duplication · 复制与复印 (Duplicate, Replicate, Facsimile)
groups.tip: 精准再造或仿制原型

items.def_en: (+ sth) To print or duplicate multiple copies of a document using a machine
items.ex_en: The assistant will quickly run off fifty copies of the financial agenda.
items.ex_zh: 助理会迅速印制出五十份这份财务议程的复印件。

items.def_en: to reproduce written or typed documents using a stencil duplicator
items.ex_en: School clerks used to mimeograph exam papers for hundreds of waiting students.
items.ex_zh: 学校办事员过去常常为数百名等待的学生油印考试试卷。

items.def_en: to produce a photographic copy of printed matter using a photocopier
items.ex_en: Please photocopy both sides of your official identity card for our records.
items.ex_zh: 请复印您官方身份证件的正面和反面以供我们存档备案。

items.def_zh: 精准复制，摹仿；传真发送
items.def_en: To make an exact copy or reproduction of something; to transmit by fax.
items.ex_en: Specialized presses facsimile ancient illuminated manuscripts for museum archives worldwide.
items.ex_zh: 专业印刷机为全球博物馆档案精准复制古代泥金手抄本。

items.def_zh: 大量生产，机械地粗制滥造出
items.def_en: (+ sth) To produce large quantities of identical items or copies quickly and mechanically
items.ex_en: The sweatshop continues to churn out cheap identical plastic novelties around clock.
items.ex_zh: 这家血汗工厂日夜不停地大批量机械粗制出廉价且雷同的塑料小玩意。

items.def_en: to make an exact genetic or functional biological/digital copy of an original
items.ex_en: Bioengineers successfully cloned the rare fern to prevent its permanent ecological extinction.
items.ex_zh: 生物工程师成功克隆了这种珍稀蕨类植物，以避免其永久性生态灭绝。

items.def_zh: 复制，仿制；重复（实验等以验证结果）；（使）自我复制
items.def_en: 1. To copy, reproduce, or repeat something precisely, such as an experiment or design. 2. (biology) To make an exact copy of itself.
items.ex_en: Independent scientists attempted to replicate the unusual laboratory findings under identical conditions.
items.ex_zh: 独立科学家们尝试在完全相同的条件下精确复现这一不同寻常的实验结果。
items.ex2_en: Single-celled pathogens replicate rapidly within warm human blood vessels under stress.
items.ex2_zh: 单细胞病原体在受压的温暖人体血管内迅速复制繁衍。

items.def_zh: 复制，复印；重复，做同样的事
items.def_en: 1. To make an exact copy of something. 2. To do something again, especially unnecessarily.
items.ex_en: Do not duplicate administrative procedures when filing your annual corporate tax return.
items.ex_zh: 在申报年度企业所得税时，不要进行重复繁琐的行政流程。

groups.summary_en: An agent reproduces an original artifact, document, or scientific result to create an identical copy. Verbs emphasize precise physical cloning, documentary reproduction, or methodological repetition.
groups.summary_zh: 精准仿制原型、复制文献或重现实验结果，强调毫厘不爽的复制性。
groups.desc_en: Creating a functionally or physically identical facsimile of an original item, unlike inspired reimagination or analog approximation.
groups.desc_zh: 制作在物理、内容或功能上与原型完全一致的副本，区别于带有二度创作的模仿或模糊近似。
groups.nuance_en: duplicate: producing an exact second copy identical to the primary item (key / document) · replicate: scientifically or precisely reproducing an original process or outcome (experiment / study) · photocopy: capturing and reproducing a printed document electrostatically (page / report) · clone: creating a genetically or architecturally identical twin (cell / device) · churn out: mass-producing identical copies rapidly and unthinkingly (copies / pamphlets)
groups.nuance_zh: duplicate: 精确翻模或复印出与原件无异的副本 (key / document) · replicate: 严格依照实验或机制再现同样结果 (experiment / study) · photocopy: 通过静电光学照相技术纸质复印 (page / report) · clone: 基因或底层架构级别的一对一克隆复制 (cell / device) · churn out: 机械化、流水线式粗糙批量产出副本 (copies / pamphlets)

groups.name: Examine & Scrutinize · 深入检查与细致审视 (Examine, Inspect, Scrutinize)
groups.tip: 仔细核查检验细枝末节

items.def_zh: 仔细检查，审查；体检；考核，考查
items.def_en: 1. To inspect closely in order to determine the condition or nature of something. 2. To test someone's knowledge, skill, or qualifications.
items.ex_en: The customs officer will carefully examine every piece of international cargo today.
items.ex_zh: 海关官员今天将仔细审查检查每一件运抵的国际货物。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To examine or inspect something methodically or critically to assess its quality or detect errors
items.ex_en: The senior editor agreed to look over the manuscript for typographical errors.
items.ex_zh: 资深编辑同意过目一下这份手稿，以仔细检查排版印刷错误。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To scrutinize, inspect, or study something with intense and sustained focus
items.ex_en: Historians pore over fragile parchment scrolls under specialized museum illumination.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们在博物馆专用照明下极为专注地仔细研读易损的羊皮纸卷轴。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To examine details, documents, or objects carefully and systematically
items.ex_en: Let us go over the terms of the contract once more before signing it.
items.ex_zh: 在签署之前，让我们再仔细核对一遍合同的条款。

items.def_en: to officially examine accounts, records, or procedures for accuracy
items.ex_en: Independent accountants were hired to audit the firm's financial records thoroughly.
items.ex_zh: 独立会计师受聘对该公司的财务记录进行彻底审计。

items.def_en: to investigate someone's past background or an item's fitness before approving
items.ex_en: The committee will vet each candidate's background before making any final recommendations.
items.ex_zh: 委员会将在提出最终推荐人选之前审查每位候选人的背景。

items.def_en: To look at something closely and critically to check its condition or detect errors.
items.ex_en: Safety officials arrived this morning to inspect the factory's structural integrity.
items.ex_zh: 安全官员今早抵达，以视察工厂的结构完整性。

items.def_en: to examine someone or something extremely thoroughly and critically
items.ex_en: Regulators will scrutinize every detail of the proposed corporate merger very thoroughly.
items.ex_zh: 监管机构将极其彻底地严密审查该企业合并案的每一个细节。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe visual or cognitive inspection where an agent systematically checks an object, document, or subject for flaws, truth, or details. Nuances differentiate general testing from rigorous, critical probing.
groups.summary_zh: 指为查找缺陷、核实真相或评估状况而系统性地观察与审查。
groups.desc_en: Directing critical, methodical perception to investigate an entity's internal integrity, truth, or details, unlike casual glance.
groups.desc_zh: 运用批判性、方法论式的敏锐感知探测实体的内部完整性、真实度或细节，区别于走马观花式的泛览。
groups.nuance_en: examine: testing or checking conditions systematically to diagnose or evaluate (patient / evidence) · inspect: making an official visual check for compliance or defects (vehicle / site) · scrutinize: peering intensely and skeptically into the finest details (data / motives) · audit: formally and quantitatively verifying financial accounts or systems (records / accounts) · vet: rigorously screening an individual's background or credentials (candidate / dossier)
groups.nuance_zh: examine: 系统化检视与诊断以评估状态 (patient / evidence) · inspect: 官方按规章对缺陷或合规性进行实地查验 (vehicle / site) · scrutinize: 带着怀疑眼光巨细靡遗地剖析审视 (data / motives) · audit: 依财务与内控制度严格核准审计 (records / accounts) · vet: 全面审查背景资格与政治底细 (candidate / dossier)

groups.name: Exceed Moderation & Overdo · 过度与过火 (Overdo, Overreach, Overindulge)
groups.tip: 行为举止或表述超出合理限度

items.def_en: (usually be/get carried away) To lose self-control or moderation due to excessive enthusiasm or excitement
items.ex_en: He got carried away by the excitement and made promises he could not keep.
items.ex_zh: 他一时兴奋冲昏了头脑，许下了无法兑现的承诺。

items.def_en: [I/T] to have too much of something enjoyable, especially food, drink, or leisure
items.ex_en: Guests were warned not to overindulge in rich food during the banquet.
items.ex_zh: 客人们被提醒在宴会期间切勿过度贪食油腻食物。
items.ex2_en: The wealthy grandparents overindulged their youngest grandson with expensive electronic toys.
items.ex2_zh: 富有的祖父母用昂贵的电子玩具过分溺爱了他们最小的孙子。

items.def_en: To act without restraint, moderation, or proportion in doing, saying, or spending
items.ex_en: You don't need to go overboard spending money on expensive decorations.
items.ex_zh: 你没必要走极端花这么多钱买昂贵的装饰品。

items.def_zh: 大吃大喝；过度暴饮暴食
items.def_en: To overindulge excessively in eating food beyond moderation
items.ex_en: We stayed up late and pigged out on pizza and ice cream.
items.ex_zh: 我们熬夜狂欢，大吃披萨和冰淇淋。

items.def_zh: 把……做得过分；夸大；使过度劳累；煮（烤）得过久
items.def_en: 1. To do something to an excessive degree, or exaggerate. 2. To cook food for too long.
items.ex_en: Be careful not to overdo the garlic or it will ruin the sauce.
items.ex_zh: 注意大蒜不要放得太过量，否则会毁了这道酱汁。

items.def_zh: 自不量力，做过头而受挫
items.def_en: to defeat one's own purpose by attempting too much or overextending oneself
items.ex_en: The ambitious general overreached in his campaign and suffered a catastrophic defeat.
items.ex_zh: 这位野心勃勃的将军在战役中冒进过头，结果遭遇惨败。

items.def_zh: 把……做得过火；夸大（overdo的过去分词）
items.def_en: To do something to an excessive degree, or exaggerate (past participle of overdo).
items.ex_en: His constant flattery felt distinctly overdone and quickly annoyed everyone in the room.
items.ex_zh: 他不断的奉承显得明显过火，很快就惹恼了房间里的所有人。

items.def_en: to demand too much physical, mental, or financial effort from someone or something
items.ex_en: Working twelve hours a day will severely overtax your physical strength.
items.ex_zh: 每天工作十二小时会使你的体力严重超负荷。

groups.summary_en: Agents carry an action, effort, or behavior beyond proper or safe limits, leading to exhaustion, failure, or excessive indulgence.
groups.summary_zh: 行为或努力超出适度界限，导致精力耗尽、弄巧成拙或过度放纵。
groups.desc_en: Trespassing past the threshold of balance, health, or prudence into unsustainable excess, unlike staying safely within bounds.
groups.desc_zh: 越过理性、节制或生理负荷的适度底线而陷入过火失衡，区别于恪守本分的适可而止。
groups.nuance_en: overdo: exaggerating an action or working beyond sensible limits (exercise / role) · overreach: failing or collapsing by aggressively overextending one's power or capacity (authority / ambitions) · overindulge: yielding excessively to pleasure, appetite, or whims (alcohol / children) · go overboard: reacting or expending resources with uncontrolled, ridiculous extravagance (spending / reactions) · overtax: exhausting a system's energy, strength, or tolerance (resources / patience)
groups.nuance_zh: overdo: 矫枉过正、用力过猛或用力超出合理范围 (exercise / role) · overreach: 盲目扩权弄巧成拙、因野心冒进而遭反噬 (authority / ambitions) · overindulge: 毫无节制地纵情享乐或溺爱放任 (alcohol / children) · go overboard: 举止过度夸张、用力过度到不合情理 (spending / reactions) · overtax: 使资源、耐力或承载力不堪重负 (resources / patience)

groups.name: Excite & Thrill · 激动与振奋 (Arousal & Exhilaration)
groups.tip: 由情绪雀跃递进为极致狂喜刺激

items.def_en: to cause strong feelings of enthusiasm, eagerness, or agitation
items.ex_en: The news of the discovery excited great interest among the scientific community.
items.ex_zh: 这项发现的消息在科学界引起了极大的兴趣。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To make someone intensely excited, stimulated, or full of anticipation
items.ex_en: The loud music was intended to hype up the crowd before the concert.
items.ex_zh: 喧闹的音乐旨在音乐会开始前煽动起人群的狂热情绪。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To fill someone with high energy, enthusiasm, and exhilaration
items.ex_en: The upbeat music was intended to pump up the crowd before the game.
items.ex_zh: 欢快的音乐旨在赛前点燃观众的热情。

items.def_zh: 热情称赞，兴奋地说；使充满热情，使极为激动
items.def_en: 1. (+ about/over) To express great excitement or enthusiasm about something. 2. To make someone feel full of enthusiasm and excitement.
items.ex_en: The critics enthused over the young director's remarkable new motion picture.
items.ex_zh: 影评人们对这位年轻导演的新电影赞不绝口。

items.def_en: (+ sb) To arouse intense enthusiasm, passion, or excitement in someone
items.ex_en: The coach's speech fired up the team before the final match.
items.ex_zh: 决赛前，教练的演讲彻底点燃了全队的斗志。

items.def_zh: 使极为激动，使狂喜；感到兴奋，震颤
items.def_en: 1. To cause someone to feel a sudden wave of intense excitement, pleasure, or emotion. 2. To feel a sudden surge of excitement or pleasure.
items.ex_en: The sudden victory thrilled millions of dedicated football fans across the nation.
items.ex_zh: 这场突如其来的胜利让全国数百万忠实的足球迷狂喜不已。
items.ex2_en: The excited audience thrilled at the famous singer's sudden surprise appearance.
items.ex2_zh: 激动的观众为这位著名歌手的突然意外亮相而感到震撼兴奋。

items.def_zh: 使极度兴奋；使震撼激昂
items.def_en: to fill someone with sudden, intense, tingling shock and excitement
items.ex_en: Her breathtaking performance electrified the entire audience in the packed theater hall.
items.ex_zh: 她令人屏息的精彩表演让座无虚席的剧场观众为之震撼沸腾。

items.def_zh: 使狂喜陶醉；使欣喜若狂
items.def_en: to exhilarate someone emotionally beyond normal self-possession
items.ex_en: The dizzying taste of triumph intoxicated the young champion beyond all reason.
items.ex_zh: 胜利带来的眩晕快感让这位年轻的冠军彻底陶醉，近乎失去理智。

groups.summary_en: An external stimulus or internal feeling triggers progressive states of high positive emotional arousal, nervous animation, electric joy, or breathless exhilaration.
groups.summary_zh: 刺激引发正向兴奋感与充沛活力，从热忱洋溢到极度激昂狂喜。
groups.desc_en: Physiologically or emotionally arousing someone to an intense state of anticipation, joy, or passion, unlike maintaining tranquil calm.
groups.desc_zh: 在生理或神经层面唤醒极其强烈的亢奋、期待或狂喜状态，区别于维持内心的沉静冷寂。
groups.nuance_en: excite: triggering general heightened arousal, curiosity, or restless agitation (crowd / neurons) · thrill: sending a sudden shiver of intense pleasure or adventure through someone (spectator / fan) · electrify: stunning a group into sudden, breathless, high-voltage enthusiasm (audience / stadium) · pump up: intentionally building aggressive confidence and adrenaline (team / athlete) · fire up: igniting passionate enthusiasm or moral drive (base / supporters)
groups.nuance_zh: excite: 激活神经系统，引发躁动与强烈好奇 (crowd / neurons) · thrill: 带来骤然袭来、通体战栗的冒险狂喜 (spectator / fan) · electrify: 宛如触电般让全场瞬间屏息震撼 (audience / stadium) · pump up: 刻意注入肾上腺素以调动冲劲 (team / athlete) · fire up: 点燃情绪火苗以激起义愤或昂扬斗志 (base / supporters)

groups.name: Exert Sustained Effort · 竭力争取与奋斗 (Strive, Endeavor, Struggle)
groups.tip: 全力以赴克服困难达成目标

items.def_en: (+ for/to do) to make strenuous or determined efforts in the face of difficulties or opposition
items.ex_en: Many low-income families struggle to pay for basic necessities like healthcare.
items.ex_zh: 许多低收入家庭为了支付医疗保健等基本必需品而艰难挣扎。

items.def_en: (+ for/to do) to work hard and persistently toward a difficult objective
items.ex_en: The dedicated research team laboured tirelessly to discover a viable medical cure.
items.ex_zh: 这个敬业的研究团队不知疲倦地苦干，力求发现一种可行的治疗方法。

items.def_en: (+ for/after/to do) to exert oneself to the utmost to reach or achieve something
items.ex_en: He strained with all his might to push the heavy boulder away.
items.ex_zh: 他使劲全力试图将那块沉重的巨石推开。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To exert sustained, determined effort and struggle toward achieving an ambition or standard
items.ex_en: Our dedicated faculty will continually strive for academic excellence across all disciplines.
items.ex_zh: 我们敬业的教职员工将持续为所有学科的卓越学术水平而奋力追求。

items.def_en: To work or labour incessantly and arduously over a prolonged period
items.ex_en: She slaved away in the hot kitchen all afternoon preparing dinner.
items.ex_zh: 她整个下午都在闷热的厨房里拼命苦干准备晚饭。

items.def_en: (+ at sth) To work persistently and doggedly at a difficult task without giving up
items.ex_en: He continued to plug away at the difficult math problem until bedtime.
items.ex_zh: 他坚持不懈地埋头攻克那道数学难题，直到就寝时间。

items.def_en: 1. (+ for/against/to do) To make a great, determined effort to achieve something difficult.
items.ex_en: We must always strive to maintain the highest ethical standards in journalism.
items.ex_zh: 我们必须始终努力保持新闻业最高的道德标准。

items.def_en: 1. (+ to do) (formal, British English spelling of endeavor) To make an earnest effort to achieve something.
items.ex_en: The ambassadors shall endeavour to reach a peaceful resolution to the conflict.
items.ex_zh: 大使们应当竭力寻求和平解决冲突的方案。

groups.summary_en: An agent exerts persistent, principled effort against obstacles or long odds to attain an ambitious goal or uphold a standard. While 'strive' suggests continuous, aspirational exertion and 'endeavour' denotes formal or conscientious undertaking, related verbs highlight arduous struggle or laborious toil toward an objective.
groups.summary_zh: 指为实现目标或克服障碍而持续付出艰苦努力、奋力拼搏。
groups.desc_en: Applying continuous physical, intellectual, or moral force over an extended period to overcome obstacles, unlike effortless ease or brief attempts.
groups.desc_zh: 在漫长周期内持续施加肉体、智力或意志力量以抗击阻力，区别于轻而易举或浅尝辄止。
groups.nuance_en: strive: passionately and purposefully reaching upward toward a lofty target (excellence / perfection) · struggle: laboring against heavy, painful resistance or impending failure (adversity / survival) · endeavour: undertaking an earnest, sustained effort in serious endeavors (mission / quest) · labour: enduring heavy, exhausting, repetitive exertion (fields / hours) · slave away: working subordinately and relentlessly under oppressive conditions (kitchen / desk)
groups.nuance_zh: strive: 向上追求卓越或崇高理想的锐意进取 (excellence / perfection) · struggle: 面对沉重逆境或存亡绝境的抗争挣扎 (adversity / survival) · endeavour: 带着郑重责任感持之以恒地尝试推进 (mission / quest) · labour: 承受耗尽体力的繁重劳作 (fields / hours) · slave away: 在压榨或严苛环境下不知疲倦地当牛做马 (kitchen / desk)

groups.name: Fall Behind in Progress · 滞后与脱节 (Lag, Straggle, Trail)
groups.tip: 行进速度缓慢掉在队尾

items.def_en: to stay behind or proceed slowly when others are moving forward
items.ex_en: Do not linger behind while the rest of the tour group advances.
items.ex_zh: 旅行团的其他成员往前走时，你不要拖拉留在后面。

items.def_en: To move backward or gradually lose ground behind competitors or travelling companions
items.ex_en: The troops were ordered to fall back to fortified positions.
items.ex_zh: 部队接到命令，撤退到坚固的防御阵地。

items.def_en: [I/T] to follow behind or be losing in a competition or procession
items.ex_en: Our local football team trailed by two goals at the final whistle.
items.ex_zh: 终场哨声响起时，我们本地的足球队以两球落后。

items.def_zh: 滞后，落后；给（水管、水箱等）加保温层
items.def_en: 1. (+ behind) To move, develop, or happen more slowly than others. 2. (chiefly British) To wrap pipes or water tanks with insulating material.
items.ex_en: Production levels began to lag behind schedule due to severe material shortages.
items.ex_zh: 由于严重的材料短缺，生产进度开始滞后。

items.def_zh: 掉队，落后；散乱地蔓延（或移动）
items.def_en: (+ behind/along) To move slowly and fall behind others; to grow or spread untidily.
items.ex_en: The tired hikers began to straggle far behind the experienced lead guide.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的徒步者们开始稀稀落落地掉队，落在经验丰富的领队身后。

items.def_en: To fail to keep pace and fall to a position behind others in a line or competition
items.ex_en: The injured runner slowly began to drop behind the other marathon competitors.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的跑步选手慢慢开始落后于其他马拉松参赛者。

items.def_en: to fail to keep up with the pace, schedule, or progress of others
items.ex_en: If you miss several classes, you will quickly fall behind in school.
items.ex_zh: 如果你缺席几堂课，你在学业上很快就会落后。

items.def_en: To move, progress, or develop more slowly than others, creating a noticeable gap
items.ex_en: Rural school districts often lag behind urban centers in technological resources.
items.ex_zh: 乡村学区在技术资源方面往往落后于城市中心。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe moving or progressing more slowly than others in a line, group, or competitive benchmark, scaling from a gradual gap in pace to disorganized, total dispersion behind.
groups.summary_zh: 按滞后与脱节程度递增描述在行进、竞争或进度上落于人后。
groups.desc_en: Moving or developing at a pace slower than a benchmark or group, steadily falling to the rear, unlike keeping stride or leading.
groups.desc_zh: 行动或演进节奏滞后于参照基准或群体、持续向后位脱节，区别于并驾齐驱或领跑前沿。
groups.nuance_en: lag: moving or developing too slowly relative to competitors or schedule (economy / recovery) · trail: following visibly behind a leader or winning pack (opponent / rival) · straggle: wandering or wandering behind in a loose, disordered, and sluggish manner (hikers / troops) · fall behind: gradually failing to sustain an established pace or benchmark (payments / rivals) · linger: dawdling or deliberately staying behind when others move on (doorway / memory)
groups.nuance_zh: lag: 相较于既定日程或竞品存在明显的滞后时差 (economy / recovery) · trail: 在序列上亦步亦趋地落后于前方领跑者 (opponent / rival) · straggle: 步调散漫、队伍涣散地落于队尾后方 (hikers / troops) · fall behind: 渐次掉队、无力维系既有进度基准 (payments / rivals) · linger: 依依不舍或慢条斯理地在原地徘徊逗留 (doorway / memory)

groups.name: Fall Ill & Suffer Ailment · 染病与受疾患困扰 (Sicken, Ail, Languish)
groups.tip: 身体染病并承受生理痛苦

items.def_en: (+ from) to experience physical illness, pain, or continuous debility
items.ex_en: Many elderly patients suffer from persistent joint inflammation during cold damp winters.
items.ex_zh: 许多老年患者在阴冷潮湿的冬季备受顽固性关节炎的折磨。

items.def_en: to suddenly or gradually become sick
items.ex_en: The foreign minister took ill suddenly during an official banquet in London.
items.ex_zh: 外交部长在伦敦的一次官方宴会期间突然染病。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To begin to suffer from a specific illness or ailment, typically not life-threatening
items.ex_en: I think I'm coming down with the flu because my throat hurts.
items.ex_zh: 我想我是感冒了，因为我嗓子疼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To become sick or contract an ailment that causes physical deterioration
items.ex_en: Several village children fell ill with severe measles early this past spring.
items.ex_zh: 去年早春，村里的几个孩子因出严重的麻疹而病倒。

items.def_en: (+ sth) To become severely incapacitated or die as a result of an illness or disease
items.ex_en: The elderly poet tragically succumbed to pneumonia after a long winter illness.
items.ex_zh: 这位老诗人在经历漫长的冬日病痛后，不幸因肺炎逝世。

items.def_zh: 生病，患病；使厌恶，使恶心，使作呕
items.def_en: 1. To become ill or start to develop a disease. 2. To make someone feel deeply disgusted, shocked, or physically ill.
items.ex_en: The young soldier began to sicken shortly after drinking the contaminated river water.
items.ex_zh: 那名年轻士兵在饮用了受污染的河水后不久便开始患病。
items.ex2_en: The graphic battlefield photographs sickened sensitive gallery visitors within mere seconds.
items.ex2_zh: 那些逼真的战场照片在几秒钟内就让敏感的画廊参观者感到恶心不适。

items.def_zh: 患病，受病痛折磨；使困扰，使苦恼
items.def_en: 1. To suffer from illness, pain, or distress. 2. To cause trouble, affliction, or pain to someone.
items.ex_en: The physician could not fathom what strange distemper did ail the king.
items.ex_zh: 御医无法参透究竟是何种离奇的疾疫在折磨着国王。

items.def_en: to become weak, feeble, or deteriorate due to illness or prolonged distress
items.ex_en: The wounded knight was left to languish in the dark, cold dungeon.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的骑士只能在阴暗寒冷的城堡地牢中日渐衰弱憔悴。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe falling ill, deteriorating in physical vitality, or suffering prolonged chronic distress. They range from formal or literary descriptions of decline to standard medical onset.
groups.summary_zh: 描述患病、身体渐衰或长期受慢性疾患困扰的身体状态。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves an organism transitioning into an incapacitated physical state or enduring prolonged bodily distress, contrasting with traumatic physical injury by emphasizing internal pathological onset and systemic decline.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式呈现有机体转入病理失能状态或持续遭受身体病痛折磨，与外力造成的物理创伤相比，强调内在病理发作与全身性衰竭衰竭过程。
groups.nuance_en: come down with: abrupt onset of mild-to-moderate infectious illness (flu / cold / fever) · sicken: rapid onset or revulsion leading to illness (illness / stomach) · ail: chronic persistent distress often affecting older or vulnerable subjects (patient / heart) · succumb to: fatal or overwhelming capitulation to disease (injuries / illness / infection) · languish: prolonged debilitating decline without recovery (prison / illness / bed)
groups.nuance_zh: come down with: 突发性染上中轻度传染病 (flu / cold / fever) · sicken: 突发患病或作呕致病 (illness / stomach) · ail: 慢性持续性的疾痛困扰 (patient / heart) · succumb to: 最终不敌病魔而倒下或病逝 (injuries / illness / infection) · languish: 缠绵病榻且日渐衰弱衰竭 (prison / illness / bed)

groups.name: Favor & Prefer · 偏爱与青睐 (Prefer, Favor, Fancy)
groups.tip: 在对比选择中表现出的特殊倾向

items.def_en: To like one thing, person, or option better than another.
items.ex_en: Many people prefer reading physical books to using digital electronic screens.
items.ex_zh: 许多人比起看电子屏幕，更喜欢阅读纸质书。

items.def_zh: 偏爱，青睐；有利于；赞同，支持
items.def_en: 1. To treat with partiality or prefer one person or thing over another. 2. To approve of, support, or be advantageous to.
items.ex_en: Parents should never favor one child over another when settling family disputes.
items.ex_zh: 父母在调解家庭纷争时不应偏爱其中一个孩子。

items.def_en: accord special importance, superiority, or structural priority to one thing over another
items.ex_en: The new legislation seems to privilege corporate interests over individual worker rights.
items.ex_zh: 这项新法规似乎把企业的利益置于单个工人的权利之上予以优先对待。

items.def_en: feel a casual or sudden attraction or liking toward someone or something
items.ex_en: Do you fancy going for a quick drink after work tonight?
items.ex_zh: 你今晚下班后想去喝一杯吗？

items.def_en: show an emerging or tentative preference for a particular view or candidate
items.ex_en: Most independent voters currently lean toward supporting the newly proposed tax reform.
items.ex_zh: 大多数独立选民目前倾向于支持这项新提出的税制改革。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to choose or treat one person or thing differently from others, especially to show special favor
items.ex_en: It is unfair to single out one player when the whole team performed poorly.
items.ex_zh: 在全队表现都很差的情况下，单单挑出一名球员来责备是不公平的。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to choose one particular option rather than others after consideration
items.ex_en: After weighing both offers, she decided to opt for the smaller firm.
items.ex_zh: 在权衡了两份录用通知后，她决定选择那家规模较小的公司。

items.def_zh: 逐渐喜欢上；对…产生好感
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to start to like or appreciate someone or something more
items.ex_en: The cautious committee members gradually began to warm to his innovative plan.
items.ex_zh: 谨慎的委员会成员们逐渐开始对他的创新方案产生好感。

groups.summary_en: A person evaluates alternatives and singles out one option, person, or taste with greater liking, partiality, or bias.
groups.summary_zh: 权衡不同选择时表现出主观倾向，更倾向于喜爱、支持某人某事。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves asymmetrical cognitive or practical tilting toward one option over alternatives, contrasting with neutral choosing by highlighting subjective partiality, structural privilege, or emotional bias.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式呈现相较于其他选项在认知或行动上产生不对称倾斜，与中立的选择相比，更凸显主观偏心、结构性优待或情绪青睐。
groups.nuance_en: prefer: general comparative cognitive choice (option / alternative / tea) · favor: active partiality or institutional advantage (candidate / policy / approach) · privilege: structural or systemic elevation above peers (group / perspective / class) · fancy: spontaneous personal or whimsical liking (idea / chance / runner) · lean toward: tentative shifting inclination (compromise / candidate / view)
groups.nuance_zh: prefer: 普遍的比较性偏好 (option / alternative / tea) · favor: 主动的偏袒或制度性青睐 (candidate / policy / approach) · privilege: 结构性、特权化的优待 (group / perspective / class) · fancy: 随性或一时的青睐喜欢 (idea / chance / runner) · lean toward: 初步或试探性的立场倾斜 (compromise / candidate / view)

groups.name: Find & Detect · 发现与察觉 (Discover, Detect, Spot)
groups.tip: 通过感官获知客观存在

items.def_zh: 找到，发现；发觉，感到；裁决
items.def_en: 1. To discover someone or something by searching or by chance. 2. To perceive, realize, or experience something. 3. (law) To make a legal judgment or verdict.
items.ex_en: I was surprised to find my lost keys sitting on the counter.
items.ex_zh: 我很惊讶地发现我丢失的钥匙正放在柜台上。

items.def_en: to see, notice, or identify sb/sth, especially sth that is hard to see
items.ex_en: I managed to spot him standing across the crowded busy train platform.
items.ex_zh: 我设法在拥挤繁忙的火车站台对面认出了他。

items.def_en: to become aware of, find, or uncover sth unexpected, hidden, or previously unknown
items.ex_en: Archaeologists were amazed to discover ancient golden artifacts buried beneath the sand.
items.ex_zh: 考古学家们惊喜地发现埋在沙土之下的古代黄金文物。

items.def_en: To notice, discover, or identify the presence or existence of something, especially something subtle.
items.ex_en: Sensitive monitoring equipment can detect trace amounts of toxic gas immediately.
items.ex_zh: 灵敏的监测设备能够立即察觉到微量的有毒气体。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to recognize or distinguish someone or something among a group of things or people
items.ex_en: The victim was able to pick out the attacker from a lineup of suspects.
items.ex_zh: 受害者能够从一排嫌疑人中指认出袭击者。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to manage to see, hear, or recognize someone or something with difficulty
items.ex_en: Through the dense fog, we could barely make out the distant lighthouse.
items.ex_zh: 透过浓重的大雾，我们勉强辨认出远处的灯塔。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to discover or uncover something after investigation or searching
items.ex_en: The exhaustive investigation failed to turn up any credible evidence of fraud.
items.ex_zh: 详尽的调查并未能查出任何可靠的欺诈证据。
items.ex2_en: Valuable clues will surely turn up during our routine background search.
items.ex2_zh: 在我们常规的背景调查中肯定会出现有价值的线索。

items.def_en: to perceive, recognize, or distinguish sth with difficulty using sight or intellect
items.ex_en: It was difficult to discern any difference between the two counterfeit paintings.
items.ex_zh: 很难辨别出这两幅伪造画作之间有任何差别。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this perception frame denote discovering the existence, presence, or identity of an object, anomaly, or clue. 'Find' serves as the broad, neutral outcome verb, whereas 'detect' emphasizes sensory perception, technical measurement, or noticing subtle, hidden signals.
groups.summary_zh: 通过感官观察、检验或搜寻察觉并确定隐蔽或既有事物的存在。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves active or incidental sensory acquisition of previously hidden, obscure, or unlocated stimuli, contrasting with static looking by highlighting the epistemic transition from unawareness to identification.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式呈现主动或偶然通过感官捕获隐匿、模糊或未定位的刺激物，与静态的观看相比，凸显从未察觉到完成辨识的认知转变。
groups.nuance_en: discover: bringing previously unknown facts or sites to light (truth / evidence / talent) · detect: picking up faint, concealed, or minute signals (anomaly / odor / cancer) · spot: visually identifying something despite distance or clutter (mistake / trend / predator) · discern: cognitively or perceptually untangling subtle features (difference / shape / pattern) · turn up: unearthing something elusive through search or chance (clue / lead / document)
groups.nuance_zh: discover: 揭示先前未知的真相或事物 (truth / evidence / talent) · detect: 察觉隐秘、微弱或细微的物理信号 (anomaly / odor / cancer) · spot: 在杂乱或远距离中眼尖发现 (mistake / trend / predator) · discern: 辨别或看清细微差异与轮廓 (difference / shape / pattern) · turn up: 经过查找或碰巧翻找出来 (clue / lead / document)

groups.name: Fine-Tune Physical & Visual Settings · 校零与微调间距 (Zero, Kern, Calibrate)
groups.tip: 精细调校参数或对齐位置

items.def_zh: 微调，精确校准（仪器、参数或机械）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make precise adjustments or calibrations to an instrument, setting, or mechanism
items.ex_en: He took several minutes to dial in the suspension settings on his bike.
items.ex_zh: 他花了几分钟微调校准自行车上的避震参数。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to adjust a measuring instrument or scale so that it reads zero at the baseline
items.ex_en: Remember to zero out the electronic scale before weighing the chemical powder.
items.ex_zh: 称量化学粉末之前，切记将电子秤调零校准。

items.def_zh: 将（仪器、仪表等）调零，归零；瞄准，校准（武器）
items.def_en: 1. to adjust an instrument or measuring device so that it reads zero 2. to aim or calibrate a weapon precisely at a target
items.ex_en: The technician had to zero the pressure gauge before conducting the experiment.
items.ex_zh: 技术员在进行实验之前必须先把压力计调零。

items.def_en: to adjust components into correct spatial or mechanical orientation relative to one another
items.ex_en: Mechanics must carefully align the front wheels to prevent uneven tire wear.
items.ex_zh: 机械师必须仔细校准前轮以防止轮胎磨损不均。
items.ex2_en: The two mechanical gears did not align properly inside the housing.
items.ex2_zh: 这两个机械齿轮在外壳内部没有对齐好。

items.def_en: to adjust a balance or scale to deduct the weight of an empty container
items.ex_en: The alchemist would tare the heavy vessel ere weighing the rare powders.
items.ex_zh: 炼金术士在称量稀有粉末之前，必先扣除沉重容器的皮重。

items.def_en: to adjust the horizontal spacing between characters or letters in typography
items.ex_en: The printer must kern the bold headline lest clumsy gaps mar the page.
items.ex_zh: 排字匠须细心调整标题粗体字的字距，以免粗糙的空隙有损版面美观。

items.def_en: to bring an object or wheel into exact alignment, level, or circular symmetry
items.ex_en: The craftsman used a spoke wrench to true the bicycle's bent wheel.
items.ex_zh: 工匠用辐条扳手将自行车变形的车轮校正复圆。

items.def_en: to adjust a measuring instrument against an established standard
items.ex_en: The astronomer did carefully calibrate the brass astrolabe against the fixed stars.
items.ex_zh: 天文学家对照恒星之位，极为精细地校准了那尊黄铜星盘。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe making precise, technical, micro-level adjustments to instruments, typography, or spatial machinery to establish baselines, alignment, or balanced proportionality.
groups.summary_zh: 对仪表、排版或机械参数进行技术性微调与校零。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves minute mechanical, geometric, or digital recalibration to bring an instrument or layout into strict baseline conformity, contrasting with crude modification through its reliance on precise micro-tolerances.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及对机械、几何或数字布局进行极其微小的校准以达到严苛基准，与粗放调整相比，强调基于精密微小公差的合规归位。
groups.nuance_en: calibrate: systematically aligning measuring apparatus to certified standards (instrument / sensor / model) · zero: resetting an indicator precisely to the initial baseline (gauge / counter / scale) · tare: offsetting receptacle weight to isolate contents (scale / balance) · kern: adjusting proportional spacing between adjacent characters (font / typography / letters) · true: bringing a mechanical part into perfect axial or planar alignment (wheel / surface / edge)
groups.nuance_zh: calibrate: 系统性参照标准校准仪器 (instrument / sensor / model) · zero: 精确归零仪表示数 (gauge / counter / scale) · tare: 去皮重以测量净重 (scale / balance) · kern: 微调印刷相邻字符的字偶距 (font / typography / letters) · true: 校平或校正轴线至完全对齐 (wheel / surface / edge)

groups.name: Flamboyant & Affective Walking · 昂首阔步与招摇走动 (Sashay, Flounce)
groups.tip: 招摇、大摇大摆或优雅地走动

items.def_zh: 大摇大摆走动；招摇过市
items.def_en: to walk about in a prominent or showy way to attract attention or show off
items.ex_en: He loves to parade around the office in his expensive new designer suit.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢穿着昂贵的新名牌西装在办公室里大摇大摆地走动。

items.def_zh: 忿然走开；趾高气扬地离去
items.def_en: to walk away in a stiff, angry, or haughty manner
items.ex_en: Furious at the sudden decision, the manager decided to stalk off silently.
items.ex_zh: 经理对这个突如其来的决定感到愤怒，忿然拂袖而去。

items.def_zh: 大模大样地走进来；轻率擅入
items.def_en: to enter a place boldly, casually, or presumptuously without permission or apprehension
items.ex_en: He had the nerve to waltz in late without even offering an apology.
items.ex_zh: 他竟然有胆量迟到还大模大样地走进来，连句道歉都没有。

items.def_zh: 大摇大摆地走；趾高气扬地走
items.def_en: to walk with a proud, erect, pompous, or arrogant gait
items.ex_en: The wealthy peacock began to strut across the courtyard before the assembled guests.
items.ex_zh: 那只华丽的孔雀开始在聚集的宾客面前趾高气扬地走过院子。

items.def_en: to walk or bounce about in an energetic, proud, or self-important manner
items.ex_en: She began to prance around the living room in her brand-new designer dress.
items.ex_zh: 她穿着那件崭新的名牌连衣裙在客厅里欢跃奔走。

items.def_zh: 趾高气扬地大步走，怒气冲冲地阔步走
items.def_en: To walk or leave with exaggerated, angry, or impatient movements in order to draw attention to oneself.
items.ex_en: After the bitter argument, she managed to flounce out of the conference room.
items.ex_zh: 激烈争吵之后，她怒气冲冲地阔步走出了会议室。

items.def_zh: 大摇大摆地走，摇曳而行，招摇走动
items.def_en: To walk in an easy, confident, and noticeable way, often with an exaggerated swaying of the hips.
items.ex_en: The model began to sashay across the platform, turning heads in the crowd.
items.ex_zh: 模特摇曳生姿地走过展台，引得人群纷纷侧目。

items.def_zh: 大模大样地走；步态傲慢
items.def_en: to walk in an aggressive, boastful, or excessively confident way
items.ex_en: The local bully would swagger down the street as if he owned it.
items.ex_zh: 那个街头恶霸大模大样地走在街上，仿佛整条街都是他的。

groups.summary_en: Verbs denoting deliberate, stylized, or expressive walking meant to show off, assert confidence, or register dramatic emotional petulance.
groups.summary_zh: 以夸张、摇曳或带着强烈情绪的姿态昂首阔步、招摇走动。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves stylistically exaggerated, theatrical locomotion meant to project arrogance, dramatic mood, or deliberate visibility, contrasting with neutral walking by foregrounding physical posturing and social spectacle.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式表现为高度夸张、具有戏剧性姿态的位移走动，旨在传达傲慢、情绪宣泄或刻意博取眼球，与普通行走相比，强调肢体姿态与社交表演性。
groups.nuance_en: strut: stiff, puffed-up walking to broadcast dominance or vanity (catwalk / stage / plumage) · swagger: arrogant, swinging gait signaling aggressive self-confidence (attitude / gait / style) · flounce: jerky, impatient walk expressing petulance or dramatic indignation (exit / room / hallway) · sashay: fluid, exaggeratedly glamorous side-to-side gliding (aisle / stage / runway) · prance: bouncy, springy, attention-seeking steps (horse / performer / child)
groups.nuance_zh: strut: 昂首挺胸、趾高气昂的炫耀步伐 (catwalk / stage / plumage) · swagger: 摆臂晃体、盛气凌人的派头大步 (attitude / gait / style) · flounce: 甩手顿足、带有愠怒戏剧性的一摔而走 (exit / room / hallway) · sashay: 摇曳生姿、引人注目的滑步款款而行 (aisle / stage / runway) · prance: 轻快蹦跳、雀跃招摇地走动 (horse / performer / child)

groups.name: Flatter & Ingratiate · 奉承与逢迎 (Flatter, Fawn, Ingratiate)
groups.tip: 用甜言蜜语讨好他人

items.def_en: (informal) to be very nice or flatter someone because you want them to do something for you
items.ex_en: Don't try to butter up the boss just to get an early promotion.
items.ex_zh: 别为了早点升职就去给老板抹蜜奉承。

items.def_zh: 对……说甜言蜜语，奉承；加蜜使变甜
items.def_en: 1. (often honey up to) To speak flatteringly or cajolingly to someone. 2. To sweeten with or as if with honey.
items.ex_en: He attempted to honey up to the wealthy heiress all evening long.
items.ex_zh: 他整晚都试图对那位富家女继承人说甜言蜜语以讨其欢心。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to try to become friendly or ingratiate oneself with someone for selfish reasons
items.ex_en: The ambitious intern tried to cozy up to the director during the party.
items.ex_zh: 那个野心勃勃的实习生在聚会上极力巴结拉拢部门总监。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to flatter or behave deferentially toward someone to win their support
items.ex_en: He was always playing up to the boss in hopes of getting a promotion.
items.ex_zh: 他总是巴结老板，希望能获得升职。

items.def_zh: 奉承，阿谀，巴结；使感到荣幸；（衣服、发型等）使显得更好看
items.def_en: 1. To praise someone excessively or insincerely, especially to gain an advantage. 2. To make someone feel pleased, honored, or proud. 3. To make someone look more attractive than they usually do.
items.ex_en: The insincere salesman tried to flatter her in hopes of closing the sale.
items.ex_zh: 那个虚伪的推销员试图奉承她，希望能促成这笔交易。

items.def_en: (+ oneself with) to make someone like you, especially deliberately and insincerely
items.ex_en: The ambitious diplomat sought to ingratiate himself with the high-ranking foreign minister.
items.ex_zh: 那位野心勃勃的外交官试图讨好这位位高权重的外交部长。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to flatter or try to please someone in authority in order to gain an advantage
items.ex_en: He spent most of his time trying to suck up to the supervisor.
items.ex_zh: 他把大部分时间都花在阿谀奉承主管上了。

items.def_en: (+ on/over) to praise someone and be excessively polite to them to gain their favor
items.ex_en: The sycophantic aides would constantly fawn over their demanding supervisor during every meeting.
items.ex_zh: 那些阿谀奉承的助手在每次会议上都不断讨好他们苛刻的主管。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe praising or behaving subserviently toward someone, typically in an insincere manner aimed at gaining favor, advantage, or approval.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过虚假夸赞、卑躬屈膝或刻意讨好他人以获取私利或好感。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves manipulative interpersonal smoothing through praise, servility, or feigned affection to secure personal advantage, contrasting with genuine complimenting by highlighting instrumental, self-serving duplicity.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式体现为通过恭维、奴颜卑膝或假意亲昵来进行功利性人际润滑以牟利，与真诚赞赏相比，强调工具化和自私自利的虚伪企图。
groups.nuance_en: flatter: insincerely praising someone's vanity for social reward (boss / ego / vanity) · fawn: displaying subservient, groveling devotion toward power (master / official / superior) · ingratiate: deliberately weaving oneself into someone's favor through charm or service (oneself / favor / family) · suck up to: vulgar, transparent subservience to authority (teacher / boss / management) · butter up: lavishly softening up an authority before making a request (client / parent / supervisor)
groups.nuance_zh: flatter: 虚伪迎合他人虚荣心以求好感 (boss / ego / vanity) · fawn: 卑躬屈膝、摇尾乞怜般讨好权贵 (master / official / superior) · ingratiate: 刻意讨好逢迎使自己得宠 (oneself / favor / family) · suck up to: 露骨谄媚、拍马屁 (teacher / boss / management) · butter up: 求人办事时大灌迷魂汤 (client / parent / supervisor)

groups.name: Flush & Wash Down · 冲洗与高压洗涤 (Hose down, Power-wash, Flush)
groups.tip: 用水管冲洗去除污物

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove residue or soap from a surface with clean running water
items.ex_en: Please rinse down the tiled patio after scrubbing away all the grime.
items.ex_zh: 刷掉所有污垢后，请把铺了瓷砖的露台冲淋干净。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to clean a large surface thoroughly using a strong flow of water
items.ex_en: He washed down the spicy tacos with a cold glass of lemonade.
items.ex_zh: 他喝了一大口冰柠檬水，咽下了辛辣的墨西哥卷饼。

items.def_en: to wash, spray, or water something using a flexible hose
items.ex_en: The gardener used cold water to hose the dusty driveway after noon.
items.ex_zh: 园丁在午后用冷水冲洗了满是灰尘的车道。

items.def_zh: 撇去……的浮渣（或浮沫）；起浮沫，长浮渣
items.def_en: to remove scum or foam from the surface of a liquid, or to become covered with scum
items.ex_en: The cook paused to scum the surface of the simmering broth slowly.
items.ex_zh: 厨师停下动作，缓缓撇去慢炖肉汤表面的浮沫。
items.ex2_en: Stagnant pond water will scum quickly under the hot summer sun.
items.ex2_zh: 死水池塘在夏日烈日下很快就会浮起一层浮渣。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to clean an enclosed space, container, or system by running a liquid through it
items.ex_en: The mechanic had to flush out the radiator to remove old coolant.
items.ex_zh: 修理工不得不冲洗干净散热器以排除旧冷却液。

items.def_en: to wash or clean something thoroughly using a stream of water from a hose
items.ex_en: He took a moment to hose down the muddy truck after work.
items.ex_zh: 下班后，他抽空用软管把满是泥泞的卡车彻底冲洗了一番。

items.def_en: to cleanse or clear out a space by causing a rapid flow of water through it
items.ex_en: They had to flush the pipes thoroughly to remove the trapped sediment.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须彻底放水冲刷管道，以清除滞留的沉积物。
items.ex2_en: Fresh water continued to flush through the drain for several minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 清水继续在下水道中冲洗流淌了好几分钟。

items.def_en: to clean surfaces using a mechanical sprayer that delivers high-pressure water
items.ex_en: We hired a contractor to power-wash the moss off the stone patio.
items.ex_zh: 我们请了一名承包商用高压水枪冲洗掉石质露台上的青苔。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote cleaning, dislodging, or clearing dirt and contaminants from surfaces using a pressurized or directed stream of liquid. They emphasize the dynamic fluid mechanism rather than generic wiping or scrubbing.
groups.summary_zh: 强调运用定向水流或加压液体喷射来冲刷、清理表面污垢。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves clearing accumulated detritus, dirt, or liquid by directing a forceful, voluminous stream of fluid, contrasting with soaking or scrubbing by highlighting pressurized hydraulic removal.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及通过高压、大量的定向水流强力冲散并排走沉积物、污垢或液体，与浸泡或擦洗相比，强调水力冲击与强效排浊机制。
groups.nuance_en: flush: rapidly purging an interior or conduit with a sudden gush (toilet / pipe / toxin) · hose down: spraying an expansive surface using a flexible hose (driveway / deck / vehicle) · power-wash: blasting deep-seated grime away using mechanical high pressure (patio / siding / pavement) · rinse down: gently carrying away superficial residue with flowing liquid (wall / equipment / sink) · wash down: thoroughly sluicing dirt off an upright or broad structure (deck / wall / floor)
groups.nuance_zh: flush: 借急涌水流排空管道或内部 (toilet / pipe / toxin) · hose down: 用软管水流大范围冲洗表面 (driveway / deck / vehicle) · power-wash: 用机械高压水枪强力剥离顽固污渍 (patio / siding / pavement) · rinse down: 用水流轻轻冲走表层残渣 (wall / equipment / sink) · wash down: 彻底冲刷立面或宽敞地板 (deck / wall / floor)

groups.name: Foam & Bubble · 发泡与起沫 (Effervesce, Froth, Lather)
groups.tip: 液体翻腾产生气泡泡沫

items.def_en: to produce hissing bubbles vigorously on the surface of a liquid
items.ex_en: The baking soda made the vinegar fizz up instantly in the glass.
items.ex_zh: 小苏打让杯中的醋立刻起泡并发出嘶嘶声。

items.def_en: to produce or fill with a mass of small bubbles or froth
items.ex_en: The turbulent waves began to foam up against the dark jagged rocks.
items.ex_zh: 汹涌的波浪开始在漆黑嶙峋的岩石上泛起白沫。
items.ex2_en: Whisk the chilled egg whites vigorously to foam up the mixture.
items.ex2_zh: 用力搅拌冷藏的蛋白以使混合物起泡。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to produce a thick soap froth, or cover something with lather
items.ex_en: You need to lather up the bar of soap before washing thoroughly.
items.ex_zh: 在彻底清洗之前，你得先把肥皂揉出泡沫。
items.ex2_en: This natural herbal soap will lather up richly in warm water.
items.ex2_zh: 这款天然草本肥皂在温水中会起丰富的泡沫。

items.def_en: to make a continuous hissing sound while producing small gas bubbles
items.ex_en: The cold soda started to fizz the moment she opened the can.
items.ex_zh: 她一打开易拉罐，冰镇汽水就开始嘶嘶冒泡。

items.def_en: To form or produce a mass of small soap bubbles; to spread lather on someone or something.
items.ex_en: The barber proceeded to lather the customer's jaw with warm shaving cream.
items.ex_zh: 理发师接着用温热的剃须膏在顾客的下巴上涂抹泡沫。
items.ex2_en: The mild shampoo refused to lather well in the hard water.
items.ex2_zh: 这种温和的洗发水在硬水中不容易起泡沫。

items.def_en: to produce or become covered with a dense layer of small bubbles
items.ex_en: The dark stout began to foam as it filled the pint glass.
items.ex_zh: 深色黑啤倒入品脱杯时开始大量冒出泡沫。

items.def_en: [I/T] to produce or cause to produce a thick mass of small bubbles on a liquid surface
items.ex_en: The barista used warm milk to froth the surface of the latte.
items.ex_zh: 咖啡师用温牛奶在拿铁表面打出浓密的奶泡。
items.ex2_en: The sparkling cider began to froth vigorously inside the chilled glass.
items.ex2_zh: 起泡苹果酒在冰镇玻璃杯中开始剧烈地冒起泡沫。

items.def_zh: 起泡，冒气泡；活跃，兴高采烈
items.def_en: 1. To produce small bubbles of gas and make a hissing sound. 2. To show high spirits, enthusiasm, or liveliness.
items.ex_en: The vintage champagne began to effervesce vigorously inside the tall crystal flutes.
items.ex_zh: 那瓶陈年香槟在细长的高脚水晶杯中欢快地冒着气泡。

groups.summary_en: This physical change-of-state frame specifies liquids generating, trapping, or discharging masses of gas bubbles or soapy foam. Manner varies by physical trigger: soapy agitation ('lather'), chemical gas release ('effervesce'), vigorous physical churning ('froth'), or agitated liquid eruption ('fizz').
groups.summary_zh: 指液体因化学反应、机械剧烈搅动或皂化作用而产生气泡或泡沫。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the vigorous mechanical or chemical creation of a frothy, gas-suspended bubble matrix on or within a liquid, contrasting with flat boiling by emphasizing cellular surface froth and bubbly aeration.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式展现通过机械搅拌或化学反应在液体表层或内部剧烈形成气液相交的泡沫基质，与平稳沸腾相比，强调蜂窝状表层泡沬化与充气翻滚。
groups.nuance_en: foam: generating a dense, thick mass of small persistent bubbles (soap / sea / mouth) · froth: whipping or churning liquid into a creamy, airy surface scum (milk / beer / coffee) · lather: producing thick suds through friction with soap and water (soap / shampoo / shave) · effervesce: spontaneously releasing fine, hissing gas bubbles through chemical reaction (champagne / tablet / beverage) · fizz: making a sharp hissing sound while releasing brisk micro-bubbles (soda / tonic / drink)
groups.nuance_zh: foam: 产生致密绵长的大量小气泡 (soap / sea / mouth) · froth: 搅打翻滚出的轻盈奶沫或白沫 (milk / beer / coffee) · lather: 皂液经摩擦揉搓出的浓密泡沫 (soap / shampoo / shave) · effervesce: 化学反应自发析出细密嘶嘶气泡 (champagne / tablet / beverage) · fizz: 碳酸液体释放细碎气泡伴随滋滋声 (soda / tonic / drink)

groups.name: Foot the Bill & Bankroll · 出资与全面包办 (Fund, Bankroll, Foot the Bill)
groups.tip: 出资赞助提供财力

items.def_en: to pay the costs of an event, athlete, or broadcast in return for publicity
items.ex_en: A global sportswear company agreed to sponsor the upcoming international marathon race.
items.ex_zh: 一家全球运动服饰公司同意赞助即将举行的一场国际马拉松赛事。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to produce or pay money unwillingly under pressure
items.ex_en: The reluctant tenant had to cough up three months of back rent.
items.ex_zh: 那个不情愿的租客不得不勉强掏出拖欠了三个月的租金。

items.def_en: [I/T] (foot the bill for sth) to pay for something, especially when it is expensive or should be paid by others
items.ex_en: The company agreed to foot the bill for their luxurious client dinner.
items.ex_zh: 公司同意为他们招待客户的奢华晚宴买单。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to pay out a large sum of money, often reluctantly
items.ex_en: I had to fork out five hundred dollars for sudden car repairs.
items.ex_zh: 我不得不为突如其来的汽车维修掏了五百美元腰包。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to spend or pay a substantial amount of money, usually begrudgingly
items.ex_en: Parents often shell out thousands of dollars for their children's private tutoring.
items.ex_zh: 父母们常常为孩子的课外辅导大把掏出数千美元。

items.def_en: To provide money for an event, project, organization, or activity.
items.ex_en: The government decided to fund the renewable energy research project this year.
items.ex_zh: 政府决定在今年为该可再生能源研究项目提供资金。

items.def_zh: 资助；向…提供赌本/启动资金
items.def_en: to provide someone with money to start a venture or contest
items.ex_en: The wealthy patron chose to stake the young entrepreneur in his venture.
items.ex_zh: 那位富有的资助人决定向这位年轻创业者的企业提供启动资金。

items.def_en: (informal) To support a person, organization, or project by giving them large amounts of money.
items.ex_en: A mysterious billionaire agreed to bankroll the independent filmmaker's ambitious project.
items.ex_zh: 一位神秘的亿万富翁同意出资支持这位独立电影人的宏大项目。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame emphasize the specific manner of covering costs—from straightforward allocation of money to lavishly underwriting or begrudgingly paying the entire tab.
groups.summary_zh: 以特定方式买单、全面包办开支或全额资助某项开销。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves assuming the comprehensive, often begrudged or high-risk financial burden of an enterprise or liability, contrasting with mere transactional purchasing by highlighting complete underwriting or reluctant expenditure.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式体现为承担企业或赔付责任中全面、高风险甚至不情愿的资金包办，与普通交易支付相比，强调全盘兜底注资或无奈解囊掏腰包。
groups.nuance_en: bankroll: fully underwriting an expensive project or entity with deep capital (campaign / film / venture) · foot the bill: bearing the entire ultimate financial cost, often reluctantly (expenses / dinner / damages) · fund: officially providing institutional financial backing (research / program / project) · shell out: reluctantly parting with substantial cash out of pocket (money / fortunes / sum) · stake: risking seed capital on a venture or competitor (startup / gambler / venture)
groups.nuance_zh: bankroll: 凭借雄厚资本全面包办资助大型项目 (campaign / film / venture) · foot the bill: 为最终全部开销买单兜底（多含勉强） (expenses / dinner / damages) · fund: 官方或机构正式提供项目资金 (research / program / project) · shell out: 不情愿地掏出大笔腰包支出 (money / fortunes / sum) · stake: 冒风险为初创企业或人押注注资 (startup / gambler / venture)

groups.name: Forced Packing & Cramming · 硬塞与挤满 (Stuff, Jam, Cram)
groups.tip: 硬挤入狭小缝隙直至填满

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to force a large number of people or things into a limited space
items.ex_en: He decided to pack in his office job to travel the world.
items.ex_zh: 他决定辞去办公室的工作去环游世界。

items.def_en: (+ into/with) to force people or things into a space that is almost too small for them
items.ex_en: Commuters tried to cram into the subway train during the morning rush.
items.ex_zh: 早高峰期间，通勤者们拼命往地铁车厢里挤。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to push people or things forcefully into a small or tight enclosure
items.ex_en: The handlers had to cram into the small cage three reluctant sheep.
items.ex_zh: 工作人员不得不把三只不情愿的羊硬塞进狭窄的笼子里。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to force an object tightly into a narrow space so that it cannot move
items.ex_en: He managed to wedge into the tiny corner shelf another heavy dictionary.
items.ex_zh: 他设法将另一本厚重的词典死死塞入角落那个狭窄的隔架。

items.def_zh: 硬塞，塞满；挤进；（使）卡住，使故障；干扰（广播信号）
items.def_en: 1. To push or wedge something forcefully into a tight space, or crowd into a space until full. 2. To become stuck or make a machine become stuck and unable to move. 3. To block or disrupt electronic communications or signals.
items.ex_en: Dozens of eager shoppers began to jam the narrow aisles of the store.
items.ex_zh: 数十名热切的顾客开始挤满了商店狭窄的过道。
items.ex2_en: Excited holiday shoppers will jam into the mall before the doors open.
items.ex2_zh: 兴奋的节日购物者在商场开门前就会涌入进去。

items.def_zh: 把……塞进，填塞；给（食物）填馅；吃撑，狼吞虎咽
items.def_en: 1. To push or force something tightly or carelessly into a space or container. 2. To fill the inside of food with a mixture before cooking. 3. (stuff oneself) To eat a very large amount of food.
items.ex_en: She had to stuff several thick sweaters into her already overflowing suitcase.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不把几件厚毛衣硬塞进已经装得满满当当的行李箱里。

items.def_en: (+ in/into) to fix or force something tightly into a narrow space so that it cannot move
items.ex_en: He managed to wedge the heavy wooden block firmly under the doorframe.
items.ex_zh: 他设法将那块沉重的木块牢牢卡紧塞在门框底下。

items.def_en: (+ into/down) to force something into place with heavy, violent downward or inward thrusts
items.ex_en: The worker used a pole to ram the dry soil down firmly.
items.ex_zh: 工人用一根长杆将干燥的泥土用力往下猛夯结实。

groups.summary_en: An agent forces items or people into a limited space beyond its easy capacity, using physical pressure. The intensity scales with the degree of force applied and whether the objects are compressed, wedged immovably, or tightly jammed.
groups.summary_zh: 用力施加压力，将人或物强行塞入、卡入或挤入狭小受限的空间中。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the application of physical compressive force to drive items into a space already exceeding its comfortable capacity, contrasting with orderly packing through mechanical jamming and spatial coercion.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及施加物理压缩外力，将物品强行压入已远超正常容量的狭窄空间，与有序收纳相比，凸显机械性强塞与空间硬挤压。
groups.nuance_en: cram: forcefully packing people or objects into an overcrowded space (schedule / suitcase / passengers) · stuff: loosely or haphazardly filling a cavity to bursting (turkey / pocket / bag) · jam: wedging objects so tightly together that movement stops (crowd / lock / gears) · ram: forcefully driving an object deep into a tight gap with momentum (rod / cargo / vehicle) · wedge: tightly securing something into a narrow crevice by force (door / gap / foot)
groups.nuance_zh: cram: 强行将人员或物品硬塞进拥挤空间 (schedule / suitcase / passengers) · stuff: 随意或胡乱塞满凹陷软物至鼓胀 (turkey / pocket / bag) · jam: 挤紧卡死致使无法动弹 (crowd / lock / gears) · ram: 借冲力强力撞塞进狭窄夹缝 (rod / cargo / vehicle) · wedge: 紧紧嵌进狭窄缝隙以卡位 (door / gap / foot)

groups.name: Fortify Resolve · 严阵以待与心理武装 (Brace, Steel, Nerve)
groups.tip: 心理防线建立、咬紧牙关直面困难

items.def_en: to prepare oneself physically or mentally for an impending confrontation or exertion
items.ex_en: The campaign team must gear up for the grueling final week ahead.
items.ex_zh: 竞选团队必须整装待发，迎接接下来极其艰难的最后一周。

items.def_zh: 做好心理准备；迎接（冲击/考验）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to prepare oneself mentally or physically for something difficult or unpleasant
items.ex_en: Residents along the coast must brace for the severe incoming tropical hurricane.
items.ex_zh: 沿海居民必须做好充分准备，以迎接即将来袭的强烈热带飓风。

items.def_zh: 使下定决心，使坚强（以面对困难，尤指 steel oneself）；钢化，给……包上钢
items.def_en: (steel oneself) To prepare yourself mentally to do something difficult or unpleasant.
items.ex_en: He had to steel his weary mind against the harsh impending criticism.
items.ex_zh: 他必须使自己疲惫的心灵坚强起来，以面对即将到来的严厉批评。

items.def_zh: 鼓起勇气，使振作精神（尤指 nerve oneself）
items.def_en: (nerve oneself) To brace or encourage oneself to face something difficult or dangerous.
items.ex_en: She took a deep breath to nerve herself for the dangerous ascent.
items.ex_zh: 她深吸了一口气，鼓起勇气准备迎接危险的攀登。

items.def_en: (+ oneself / for) to prepare oneself physically or mentally for an unpleasant shock or blow
items.ex_en: Passengers were instructed to brace themselves against the sudden turbulence during flight.
items.ex_zh: 乘客们接到指示，在飞行途中遭遇突发气流时要稳住身体做好防备。

items.def_zh: 硬起心肠；使变得冷酷坚强
items.def_en: (+ oneself / one's heart) to make oneself emotionally unyielding or insensitive to hardship or pity
items.ex_en: The veteran officer had to harden his heart against their desperate pleas.
items.ex_zh: 这位老军官不得不硬起心肠，无视他们绝望的哀求。
items.ex2_en: His heart seemed to harden as the bitter war dragged on endlessly.
items.ex2_zh: 随着惨烈的战争无休止地拖延，他的心似乎硬了起来。

items.def_en: to make oneself calm and determined before an ordeal or confrontation
items.ex_en: She had to steel herself before entering the room to confront him.
items.ex_zh: 在走进房间当面质问他之前，她不得不下定决心硬起头皮。

items.def_zh: 咬紧牙关准备；严阵以待
items.def_en: (+ oneself / loins) to summon up resolution and inner strength to face a challenge
items.ex_en: The ancient warriors began to gird themselves for the bloody battle ahead.
items.ex_zh: 古老的战士们开始严阵以待，准备迎接即将到来的血腥决战。

groups.summary_en: An agent deliberately steels their own mind, nerves, or body in order to withstand an impending shock, ordeal, or painful confrontation. These verbs typically take reflexive pronouns or nouns denoting courage/resolve as their direct objects.
groups.summary_zh: 主体主动调整或强化心理与神经，以应对即将到来的痛苦或冲击。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves mobilizing psychological willpower and physiological tension to withstand an imminent shock, trauma, or trial, contrasting with passive waiting by emphasizing proactive mental armoring.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及调动心理意志与生理紧张感以抵御即将来临的冲击、创伤或考验，与被动等待相比，强调积极的主观心理武装与全身戒备。
groups.nuance_en: brace: mechanically anchoring posture or expectations against violent impact (impact / shock / disaster) · steel: forging cold, unyielding internal emotional resilience against hardship (resolve / nerve / oneself) · nerve: mustering immediate acute courage to perform a daunting act (oneself / challenge) · gird: proactively outfitting oneself with psychological armor for struggle (loins / oneself / battle) · harden: rendering sensibility calloused and impervious to pain or sympathy (heart / attitude / stance)
groups.nuance_zh: brace: 身体或心理紧绷以承受正面冲击 (impact / shock / disaster) · steel: 铁心硬性磨砺意志以迎战困境 (resolve / nerve / oneself) · nerve: 鼓足勇气准备执行令人发怵之事 (oneself / challenge) · gird: 心理严阵以待整装待发 (loins / oneself / battle) · harden: 使内心变得麻木冷硬以杜绝软弱 (heart / attitude / stance)

groups.name: Frighten & Spook · 惊吓与惊扰 (Frighten Suddenly or Unease)
groups.tip: 突遭惊吓令人毛骨悚然

items.def_en: to make someone feel worried, fearful, or suddenly anxious about danger
items.ex_en: The sudden dip in quarterly sales began to alarm the senior executives.
items.ex_zh: 季度销售额的骤降开始让高级管理层感到恐慌与不安。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to cause a person or animal to leave or stay away by frightening them
items.ex_en: The loud barking dog managed to scare off the prowler last night.
items.ex_zh: 那只大声狂吠的狗昨晚成功吓退了图谋不轨的潜入者。

items.def_zh: 使毛骨悚然；令人害怕不安
items.def_en: (+ sb) to cause someone to feel uneasy, nervous, or frightened
items.ex_en: The way that abandoned house looks at dusk really creeps me out.
items.ex_zh: 那栋废弃房屋在黄昏时的模样真让我心里发毛。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to startle or unnerve someone with sudden fright or suspense
