items.ex_en: The strange noises coming from the attic began to spook out everyone.
items.ex_zh: 阁楼上传来的诡异声响开始把大家吓得毛骨悚然。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make someone feel frightened, worried, or anxious
items.ex_en: The unexpected flash of thunder managed to scare the sleeping child awake.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的雷鸣闪电吓醒了正在熟睡的孩子。
items.ex2_en: Skittish stray animals scare easily when strangers approach them without warning.
items.ex2_zh: 胆小的流浪动物在陌生人毫无预警地靠近时很容易受惊。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make someone feel sudden fear or panic
items.ex_en: The eerie silence of the dark forest began to frighten the hikers.
items.ex_zh: 幽暗森林里阴森的寂静开始让徒步旅行者们感到惊恐。

items.def_en: To surprise or frighten someone suddenly, often causing a sudden physical reaction or flinch.
items.ex_en: The sudden slam of the back door managed to startle the cat.
items.ex_zh: 后门突然砰的一声关上，着实把猫吓了一大跳。

items.def_zh: 惊吓，使惊恐不安；受惊，惊慌
items.def_en: (informal) To frighten a person or animal suddenly so that they panic, or to become startled and afraid.
items.ex_en: The sudden loud motorcycle roar managed to spook the nervous young horse.
items.ex_zh: 摩托车突然发出的巨大轰鸣声惊吓到了那匹神经紧张的小马。
items.ex2_en: Skittish deer will spook easily when hunters step on dry twigs.
items.ex2_zh: 当猎人踩到干树枝时，胆小的鹿很容易受惊。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe causing a person or animal to experience sudden alarm, panic, or skittish apprehension. Register varies from everyday 'scare' to sudden 'startle' and the nervous skittishness implied by 'spook'.
groups.summary_zh: 指突发性使人或动物受惊、恐慌或神经高度紧绷。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the abrupt or lingering breach of emotional equilibrium caused by sudden shock, impending threat, or eerie uncertainty, contrasting with general unpleasurableness by triggering defensive fear or reflexive flight.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式展现因突发惊骇、潜在威胁或诡异未知而瞬间或持续打破情绪稳态，与普通不悦相比，突出触发防御性恐惧或应激惊逃反应。
groups.nuance_en: startle: shocking someone with a sudden, momentary involuntary jolt (victim / horse / sleeper) · frighten: evoking acute standard fear and anticipation of harm (child / animal / crowd) · spook: unsettling nervous skittishness leading to erratic avoidance (market / horse / investor) · alarm: triggering widespread rational apprehension over serious danger (public / community / resident) · creep out: evoking a slow, uncanny visceral revulsion or unease (stranger / vibe / look)
groups.nuance_zh: startle: 突发性使人猛然一惊 (victim / horse / sleeper) · frighten: 引起强烈的常规恐惧与惊恐 (child / animal / crowd) · spook: 惊扰神经使之惊疑不定、仓皇退避 (market / horse / investor) · alarm: 因严峻威胁引发群体性警觉恐慌 (public / community / resident) · creep out: 引起毛骨悚然、诡异发毛的恶心感 (stranger / vibe / look)

groups.name: Garble & Obfuscate · 混乱失真与蓄意晦涩 (Garble, Obfuscate)
groups.tip: 故意混淆视听使事实晦涩难懂

items.def_zh: 使模糊，混淆（判断或真相）
items.def_en: to make an issue, fact, or judgment less clear, transparent, or objective
items.ex_en: Personal bias should not cloud your professional judgment during the audit process.
items.ex_zh: 在审计过程中，个人偏见不应当混淆你的专业判断。
items.ex2_en: His troubled eyes began to cloud as painful memories surfaced again.
items.ex2_zh: 随着痛苦的回忆再次浮现，他忧伤的双眼开始变得迷蒙。

items.def_zh: 搅混；把（事实/情况）搞混乱
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make an issue, argument, or situation confusing and unclear
items.ex_en: His vague remarks will only muddy up the already complicated contract negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 他含糊其辞的话语只会把本就复杂的合同谈判搞得一团糟。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cause an issue, meaning, or fact to become obscure or ambiguous
items.ex_en: Unfounded rumors served to cloud over the true facts of the incident.
items.ex_zh: 毫无根据的谣言蒙蔽了该起事件的客观真相。
items.ex2_en: The legal issues cloud over whenever contradictory evidence is presented.
items.ex2_zh: 每当提出相互矛盾的证据时，法律问题就会变得模糊不清。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to confuse elements of a message or story so that it becomes garbled
items.ex_en: The tired witness began to mix up the timeline of that afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的目击者开始把那天下午的时间线彻底搞混了。

items.def_zh: 伪造，篡改（使记录或陈述失实）
items.def_en: to alter information, accounts, or records deliberately so as to mislead
items.ex_en: The accountant conspired to falsify the official financial records to conceal losses.
items.ex_zh: 该会计合谋篡改官方财务记录以隐瞒亏损。

items.def_zh: 弄混，混淆（使思路或信息杂乱）
items.def_en: to confuse or jumble a message, issue, or arrangement so it becomes unclear
items.ex_en: Careless clerical errors served to muddle the clear intentions of the agreement.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的文书错误混淆了该协议本该明确的意图。

items.def_zh: 歪曲，曲解；混淆，使（信息、话语等）杂乱不清
items.def_en: 1. To confuse, distort, or scramble a message, text, or signal so that it becomes unclear or misleading.
items.ex_en: The poor radio connection managed to garble the dispatcher's urgent broadcasted instructions.
items.ex_zh: 恶劣的无线电信号干扰了调度员紧急播报的指示，使其杂乱不清。

items.def_zh: 故意混淆，使晦涩难懂，使困惑
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To deliberately make a message, issue, or fact obscure, confusing, and hard to understand.
items.ex_en: The corrupt politician attempted to obfuscate the real issues behind empty rhetoric.
items.ex_zh: 那个腐败的政客企图用空洞的说辞来故意混淆真正的实质问题。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe making messages, communications, or facts incomprehensible or distorted, whether through accidental transmission errors and confusion or deliberate intellectual muddying.
groups.summary_zh: 使讯息或事实扭曲失真、语焉不详或晦涩难懂。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves distorting, scrambling, or obscuring structural coherence so that an originally clear signal or fact becomes unintelligible, contrasting with overt lying by prioritizing informational corruption and deliberate murkiness.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及歪曲、打乱或掩盖信息的结构连贯性，致使原本清晰的信号或事实变得无法辨识，与直接说谎相比，强调信息失真降解与蓄意晦涩混淆。
groups.nuance_en: garble: accidentally or mechanically corrupting a transmission into incoherence (message / signal / speech) · obfuscate: deliberately making meaning opaque, convoluted, or hard to parse (issue / fact / language) · muddle: mixing up distinct elements through intellectual confusion (thought / mind / sequence) · muddy: clouding a previously clear situation with extraneous noise (waters / debate / issue) · falsify: purposefully altering records or evidence to mislead (data / document / result)
groups.nuance_zh: garble: 机械传输或表达错乱致信息面目全非 (message / signal / speech) · obfuscate: 蓄意用生涩复杂表述将事实彻底搅浑 (issue / fact / language) · muddle: 脑子糊涂把不同元素混为一谈 (thought / mind / sequence) · muddy: 搅浑浑水使原本清晰的辩题失焦 (waters / debate / issue) · falsify: 伪造篡改数据以达到欺瞒目的 (data / document / result)

groups.name: Generate Commercial Return · 取得收益与入账 (Earn, Gross, Net)
groups.tip: 凭付出辛劳赚取酬劳

items.def_en: (+ sth) to yield or produce a certain amount of income or profit
items.ex_en: The newly opened downtown branch should bring in substantial monthly profits for the firm.
items.ex_zh: 这家新开的市中心分店应该会为公司带来可观的月利润。

items.def_en: to produce or generate a financial return, dividend, or profit
items.ex_en: These municipal bonds typically yield a reliable annual return for long-term investors.
items.ex_zh: 这些市政债券通常能为长期投资者带来可靠的年收益。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to earn or attract a specified amount of money or revenue
items.ex_en: The charity concert managed to pull in over twenty thousand dollars in donations.
items.ex_zh: 这场慈善音乐会成功吸引了超过两万美元的捐款。

items.def_en: to gain an amount of profit beyond all expenses and deductions
items.ex_en: After paying all production costs, we hope to clear five thousand dollars tonight.
items.ex_zh: 扣除所有制作成本后，我们希望今晚能净赚五千美元。
items.ex2_en: The massive bank check should clear within two regular business days.
items.ex2_zh: 那张巨额银行支票应该会在两个正常工作日内核算结清。

items.def_zh: 挣得，赚取；赢得，博得；应得
items.def_en: 1. To receive money as payment for work done. 2. To get something that you deserve through your efforts, qualities, or skills.
items.ex_en: Through months of diligent freelance work, she managed to earn a steady income.
items.ex_zh: 通过数月勤奋的自由职业工作，她成功获得了稳定的收入。

items.def_en: to earn or produce an amount as clear profit after all tax, costs, and expenses
items.ex_en: Selling the property enabled the family to net a substantial profit after taxes.
items.ex_zh: 出售该房产使这家人在扣除税费后净赚了一大笔利润。

items.def_en: To earn a particular total amount of money before taxes and other costs are deducted.
items.ex_en: The blockbuster movie is projected to gross two hundred million dollars domestically.
items.ex_zh: 这部卖座大片预计将在国内取得两亿美元的总票房收入。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to earn or take in large amounts of money easily or quickly
items.ex_en: The trendy boutique has been raking in massive cash since the summer holiday.
items.ex_zh: 自从暑假以来，这家时尚精品店一直在大把赚取巨额现金。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe specific commercial or accounting manners of realizing monetary proceeds from labor, investment, or enterprise, distinguishing pre-expense totals, post-expense surpluses, and baseline earnings.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过劳动、经营或扣除成本等特定方式获取并核算财务收益。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves the conversion of commercial activity, capital investment, or enterprise into measurable financial intake, contrasting with simple receiving by defining specific stages of accounting realization (gross vs net).
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式体现为通过商业运作、资本投放或经营活动将价值变现为可量化的财务入账，与单纯收钱相比，界定了特定核算阶段的实现（如毛利与净利）。
groups.nuance_en: gross: generating total revenue prior to any deductions (revenue / profit / box office) · net: realizing final profit strictly after all operational costs are subtracted (amount / gain / margin) · earn: receiving rightful compensation or return through labor or interest (wage / living / dividend) · yield: generating productive or agricultural financial return on investment (return / interest / crop) · rake in: raking up huge, lucrative sums of money rapidly (cash / fortunes / millions)
groups.nuance_zh: gross: 扣减成本前的总营收入账 (revenue / profit / box office) · net: 严密扣除所有税费成本后的纯赚净得 (amount / gain / margin) · earn: 凭借劳动、经营或利息应得收入 (wage / living / dividend) · yield: 资产投资生息或产出利润收益 (return / interest / crop) · rake in: 迅速疯狂捞取大笔暴利 (cash / fortunes / millions)

groups.name: Guarantee & Assure · 保证与担保 (Assure, Warrant, Guarantee)
groups.tip: 打消对方疑虑并提供确定承诺

items.def_en: to promise formally that certain conditions will be met, often offering restitution if not
items.ex_en: The manufacturer promised to guarantee complete customer satisfaction or issue a prompt refund.
items.ex_zh: 制造商承诺保证客户完全满意，否则将立即退款。

items.def_zh: 向……保证，使确信；确保，使确定发生；（英）给……投保（人寿险）
items.def_en: 1. To tell someone positively that something is true or will happen, so as to remove doubt. 2. To make something certain to happen. 3. (British English) To insure someone's life.
items.ex_en: The project director sought to assure anxious shareholders that the schedule remained realistic.
items.ex_zh: 项目主管试图向焦虑的股东保证工期进度依然切合实际。

items.def_zh: 保证，担保；使有必要，证明……合理
items.def_en: 1. To guarantee or state with confidence that something is true, safe, or reliable. 2. To make a particular action or state seem necessary, reasonable, or justified.
items.ex_en: The sellers expressly warrant that the vehicle remains completely free of mechanical defects.
items.ex_zh: 卖方明确担保该车辆绝无任何机械故障缺陷。

items.def_en: to state officially and formally that something is true, accurate, or meeting standard specifications
items.ex_en: Independent inspectors arrived on site to certify that the installation met safety standards.
items.ex_zh: 独立检查员抵达现场，以正式核实该设施符合安全标准。

items.def_en: to formally and solemnly promise to do, give, or uphold something
items.ex_en: The newly elected governor chose to pledge steadfast allegiance to the national constitution.
items.ex_zh: 新当选的州长郑重承诺坚定恪守国家宪法。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) assert or confirm with certainty the good character, truth, or reliability of someone or something
items.ex_en: Several former colleagues gladly agreed to vouch for his exceptional professional integrity today.
items.ex_zh: 几位前同事今天欣然同意为他卓越的职业操守作保。

items.def_en: (+ sth) guarantee the quality, truth, or reliability of a product, claim, or promise
items.ex_en: We fully stand behind the durability and reliable performance of every appliance sold.
items.ex_zh: 我们对售出的每台电器的耐用性及可靠性能承担全面质量保证。

items.def_en: (+ sth) declare with complete confidence that something is reliable and effective
items.ex_en: My grandmother swears by a cup of hot lemon water for any cold.
items.ex_zh: 我祖母坚信喝一杯热柠檬水能治任何感冒。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame center on speech acts that commit the speaker to the truth, quality, or certainty of an outcome, relieving doubts or accepting formal liability.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过语言或法律文书做出确凿承诺，打消对方疑虑或对品质承担责任。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves pledging personal, legal, or authoritative reputation to eliminate epistemic doubt and underwrite future performance, contrasting with mere assertion by assuming direct liability for failure.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及押注个人声誉、法律效力或权威信誉以消除对方认知疑虑，并为未来履约全盘兜底，与普通宣称相比，包含对失信的主动担责承诺。
groups.nuance_en: guarantee: legally or formally promising a specific outcome or replacement (safety / loan / success) · assure: psychologically dispelling another person's doubts or fears (client / ally / public) · warrant: legally justifying an action or affirming product condition (investigation / quality / arrest) · vouch for: staking personal credibility on someone's integrity or ability (character / reliability / integrity) · pledge: solemnly binding oneself to an overarching duty or donation (allegiance / support / fund)
groups.nuance_zh: guarantee: 具有法定或形式效力地包修、包退或包保结果 (safety / loan / success) · assure: 打消他人疑虑，向其拍胸脯打包票 (client / ally / public) · warrant: 使行动具有正当性，或在质保条款中作担保 (investigation / quality / arrest) · vouch for: 以个人信誉为他人品行或可靠性作保 (character / reliability / integrity) · pledge: 庄严宣誓承诺承担大额捐款或重责 (allegiance / support / fund)

groups.name: Harsh & Low Animal Vocalizations · 动物粗粝啼鸣 (Croak, Caw, Squawk)
groups.tip: 喉头发声与沙哑低鸣的发音方式

items.def_en: (of pigs or large animals) to make a low, rough, throaty sound
items.ex_en: The heavy sow began to grunt contentedly while devouring the fresh vegetable scraps.
items.ex_zh: 这头大母猪在吞食新鲜菜屑时满意地打起粗重的呼噜来。

items.def_zh: （羊等）咩咩叫；微弱地抱怨，抽抽搭搭地说
items.def_en: 1. To make the wavering cry of a sheep, goat, or calf. 2. (disapproving) To complain or speak in a weak, high, trembling voice.
items.ex_en: A lost lamb began to bleat pitifully across the misty hillside for protection.
items.ex_zh: 一只迷途的羔羊在薄雾笼罩的山坡上可怜地咩咩叫着寻求庇护。

items.raw_cluster: 动物叫声 Animal Sound & Cry
items.def_zh: （母鸡）咯咯叫；发出啧啧声（表示同情或不赞成）
items.def_en: 1. (of a hen) To make a short, low, characteristic sound. 2. (+ over/at) To make a clicking sound with the tongue to express disapproval, sympathy, or fussy concern.
items.ex_en: The broody hen continued to cluck softly while guarding her clutch of eggs.
items.ex_zh: 孵蛋的母鸡一边守护着窝里的蛋，一边继续轻柔地咯咯叫着。

items.def_en: (of wild geese or swans) to make a loud, resonant call in flight or warning
items.ex_en: A wedge of migrating geese began to honk loudly across the autumn sky.
items.ex_zh: 一队排成人字形南飞的秋雁在长空之上高声鸣叫。

items.def_zh: （青蛙或乌鸦）呱呱叫；用沙哑的声音说话；（俚）死
items.def_en: 1. To make a deep, rough sound like a frog or crow; to speak with a low, hoarse voice. 2. (slang) To die.
items.ex_en: A solitary bullfrog started to croak rhythmically from beneath the shadowed lily pads.
items.ex_zh: 一只孤单的牛蛙在睡莲阴影下方有节奏地呱呱叫了起来。

items.def_zh: （鸟类）发出粗厉刺耳的叫声；大声抱怨，抗议
items.def_en: 1. (of a bird) To make a loud, harsh, shrill noise. 2. (informal) To complain noisily or indignantly.
items.ex_en: The startled parrot began to squawk loudly when the cat approached the cage.
items.ex_zh: 当猫靠近笼子时，受惊的鹦鹉开始发出粗厉刺耳的尖叫。

items.def_en: (of a crow, rook, or raven) To make its loud, harsh, characteristic cry.
items.ex_en: A black crow perched upon the dead branch and let out another caw.
items.ex_zh: 一只黑乌鸦落在枯枝上，又发出了一声粗厉的哇哇叫。

items.def_en: (of an owl, raptor, or bird) to emit a harsh, loud, piercing cry
items.ex_en: A solitary barn owl let out a piercing screech across the dark woods.
items.ex_zh: 一只孤零零的仓鸮在漆黑的树林里发出了一声穿透夜空的厉鸣。

groups.summary_en: Verbs denoting low, grating, harsh, or throaty vocalizations characteristic of specific creatures such as corvids, amphibians, and barnyard fowl.
groups.summary_zh: 描述乌鸦、青蛙或家禽等发出粗粝、低沉或嘶哑鸣叫的声音特征。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves animals emitting rough, guttural, low-frequency, or unmelodious non-harmonic acoustic cries, contrasting with melodious birdsong through its percussive, raspy, or abrasive phonation.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式表现为动物喉部发出粗粝、低频或难听杂乱的非谐音啼鸣，与悦耳的啁啾鸣禽相比，凸显其摩擦音、钝浊感与刺耳嘶哑特征。
groups.nuance_en: croak: low, gravelly, raspy noise typical of anurans or ravens (frog / raven / voice) · squawk: loud, harsh, abrasive screech of startled birds (parrot / seagull / bird) · caw: sharp, flat, guttural shout characteristic of corvids (crow / raven / rook) · honk: resonant, brassy blare emitted by waterfowl (goose / horn / swan) · grunt: deep, short guttural grunt of ungulates (pig / boar / seal)
groups.nuance_zh: croak: 蛙类或渡鸦发出的低沉沙哑粗粝声 (frog / raven / voice) · squawk: 鹦鹉或鸟禽受惊时爆出的刺耳粗叫 (parrot / seagull / bird) · caw: 乌鸦等鸦科发出的刺耳单调啼鸣 (crow / raven / rook) · honk: 雁鹅等发出的浑厚如铜喇叭的嘎嘎声 (goose / horn / swan) · grunt: 猪或野兽喉咙深处的短促哼叫 (pig / boar / seal)

groups.name: Heal Tissue & Cure Disease · 医治与使康复 (Cure, Heal, Remedy)
groups.tip: 疾病得到根治与创口愈合

items.def_en: (+ with/for) to give medical care or attention to an illness or injured person
items.ex_en: Paramedics worked quickly under difficult conditions to treat the injured passenger for shock.
items.ex_zh: 医护人员在恶劣条件下迅速开展救治，为受伤的乘客缓解休克症状。

items.def_zh: （使）愈合，（使）治愈；调解，平息（争吵、分歧）
items.def_en: 1. To become healthy again, or make an injury, wound, or sick person healthy. 2. To resolve or put an end to an unpleasant situation or disagreement.
items.ex_en: With proper rest and clean dressings, the deep laceration should heal completely soon.
items.ex_zh: 只要充分休息并保持敷料清洁，这个深伤口很快就会彻底愈合。
items.ex2_en: The herbal ointment helped heal the severe burn within two weeks.
items.ex2_zh: 这种草药膏在两周内治愈了严重的烧伤。

items.def_zh: 治愈，治好；矫正，消除（问题）；腌制，加工处理（肉、鱼等）
items.def_en: 1. To make an ill person healthy again, or treat a disease successfully. 2. To solve a problem or put an end to bad behavior. 3. To preserve meat, fish, or other food by drying, salting, or smoking.
items.ex_en: Modern antibiotic courses can reliably cure this bacterial infection within two short weeks.
items.ex_zh: 现代抗生素疗程能在短短两周内切实治愈这种细菌感染。
items.ex2_en: The patient began to cure naturally once the fever broke completely.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦高烧彻底退去，病人体内就开始自然痊愈。

items.def_en: become covered with healthy new skin or scar tissue
items.ex_en: Apply this antibacterial ointment to help the blister heal over quickly.
items.ex_zh: 涂抹这种抗菌药膏有助于水泡快速结痂愈合。

items.def_en: become completely healthy and whole again, especially of a wound or injury
items.ex_en: The cut on his knee took nearly three weeks to heal up completely.
items.ex_zh: 他膝盖上的伤口花了将近三周才完全愈合。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) give quick or temporary medical treatment to an injured person or wound
items.ex_en: The field medic worked swiftly to patch up the wounded soldier before transport.
items.ex_zh: 战地医务兵在转运前迅速处理了那名负伤士兵的伤口。

items.def_en: to treat, correct, or provide an effective counteractant for a disease or bodily defect
items.ex_en: Doctors prescribed targeted therapy to remedy the patient's severe chronic respiratory deficiency.
items.ex_zh: 医生开具了靶向疗法，以纠正并医治患者严重的慢性呼吸功能缺陷。

items.def_en: (+ from) to recover health, energy, or strength gradually after illness or injury
items.ex_en: He retired to the quiet countryside to recuperate from his exhausting cardiac surgery.
items.ex_zh: 他隐退到静谧的乡间，以调养并从消耗巨大的心脏手术中康复。

groups.summary_en: A medical practitioner, therapeutic intervention, or natural biological process restores a diseased organism or damaged tissue back to healthy functioning. 'Heal' centers on the organic closing of wounds and restoration of whole tissue, whereas 'cure' targets the eradication of a specific medical pathology, disease, or infection.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过医药干预或肌体自我修复使伤口愈合、消除疾病并恢复健康。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves organic cellular restoration of injured tissue or the systemic eradication of disease, contrasting with mere cosmetic patching by aiming for the structural and functional reintegration of health.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式展现受损组织的有机细胞级修复或病灶的彻底根除，与表层的暂时应付相比，强调身心健康结构与机能的重组与根本性复原。
groups.nuance_en: cure: completely eradicating a pathological illness or condition (disease / patient / infection) · heal: organically re-knitting biological tissue or resolving emotional trauma (wound / bone / breach) · remedy: counteracting, correcting, or alleviating a systemic defect (situation / deficiency / injustice) · treat: applying medical or pharmaceutical interventions to manage disease (patient / symptom / infection) · recuperate: regaining baseline physical strength after exhaustive illness (strength / energy / patient)
groups.nuance_zh: cure: 彻底药到病除根治疾病 (disease / patient / infection) · heal: 肉体组织创伤自然愈合或精神抚平 (wound / bone / breach) · remedy: 补救系统缺陷或纠正不良状况 (situation / deficiency / injustice) · treat: 施加医学手段针对性治疗调理 (patient / symptom / infection) · recuperate: 病后或重创后休养以重聚体能 (strength / energy / patient)

groups.name: Heat & Thermal Prep · 加热与升温 (Warm, Heat, Preheat)
groups.tip: 施加热量使温度升高

items.def_en: (+ sth) Become hot or make food, a liquid, or an enclosure hotter
items.ex_en: Please heat up the remaining beef stew before the guests arrive for dinner.
items.ex_zh: 请在客人们抵达享用晚餐之前把剩下的炖牛肉加热好。
items.ex2_en: The small metal room began to heat up in the afternoon.
items.ex2_zh: 那个小铁皮房在下午开始变热了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to heat food that has grown cold, or to gradually increase temperature
items.ex_en: She placed the leftover soup in the microwave oven to warm up gently.
items.ex_zh: 她把剩下的汤放进微波炉里慢慢加热至热透。
items.ex2_en: She decided to warm up the savory chicken soup for lunch.
items.ex2_zh: 她决定把美味的鸡汤热一下当午饭。

items.def_zh: （使）变暖，（使）温暖；加热（食物等，常与up连用）
items.def_en: 1. To become warm or warmer, or to make someone or something warm or warmer.
items.ex_en: The morning sun quickly began to warm the chilly mountain cabin during dawn.
items.ex_zh: 清晨破晓时分，朝阳很快便温暖了寒冷的山间小屋。
items.ex2_en: The chilly room will warm comfortably once we light the fireplace.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦我们点燃壁炉，寒冷的房间就会变得温暖舒适。

items.def_en: 1. To heat an oven, pan, or appliance to a particular temperature before using it.
items.ex_en: You should preheat the baking oven to four hundred degrees before rolling dough.
items.ex_zh: 在擀面团之前，你应该先把烤箱预热到四百度。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Heat a liquid until it boils vigorously
items.ex_en: The cook placed a kettle on the stove to boil up fresh water.
items.ex_zh: 厨师把水壶放在炉子上，打算把新鲜的水加热至沸腾。
items.ex2_en: The rich soup will boil up quickly over the roaring fire.
items.ex2_zh: 浓汤在旺火上很快就会沸腾起来。

items.def_en: 1. To make something hot or warm, or to become hot or warm.
items.ex_en: Carefully heat the delicate mixture over low flame until small bubbles appear steadily.
items.ex_zh: 用文火小心加热这份精细的混合液，直到细密的气泡平稳冒出。
items.ex2_en: The thick copper pan will heat quickly over the gas flame.
items.ex2_zh: 厚铜锅在瓦斯火焰上很快就会受热升温。

items.def_en: to make food or a liquid hot again after it has cooled down
items.ex_en: You can easily reheat the leftover pasta in the microwave for your lunch.
items.ex_zh: 你可以很方便地用微波炉重新加热剩下的意面当作午餐。

items.def_en: to heat a liquid (especially milk) until it is just below its boiling point
items.ex_en: Carefully scald the fresh milk before whisking it into the delicate custard mixture.
items.ex_zh: 在把鲜奶搅入精致的卡仕达蛋糊之前，先小心将其加热至微沸状态。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe transferring thermal energy to bring an object, liquid, or enclosure from a lower temperature to a desired higher temperature.
groups.summary_zh: 指对物体、食物或空间进行加温，使其由凉变热或达到预设温度。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive schema involves transferring thermal energy to elevate an object's temperature to a desired threshold for culinary, physical, or comfort utility, contrasting with spontaneous burning by emphasizing controlled, goal-oriented thermal conditioning.
groups.desc_zh: 认知图式涉及通过热能传导使物体温度上升至满足烹饪、物理加工或舒适度所需的特定阈值，与自燃或烧毁相比，强调温控性与目标导向的加热调适。
groups.nuance_en: heat: generally elevating kinetic thermal energy of a mass (water / oven / metal) · warm: moderately and gently raising temperature to comfortable levels (hands / milk / soup) · preheat: bringing an appliance or material to a set temperature beforehand (oven / skillet / engine) · reheat: warming previously cooked food that has gone cold (leftovers / soup / coffee) · scald: heating a liquid to just below boiling or burning tissue with steam (milk / skin / surface)
groups.nuance_zh: heat: 普遍提高介质的热能温度 (water / oven / metal) · warm: 温和地升温至适体或微温状态 (hands / milk / soup) · preheat: 事先将仪器或器具空烧预热至指定温度 (oven / skillet / engine) · reheat: 将冷却的剩菜残羹再次加热 (leftovers / soup / coffee) · scald: 加热液体至微沸边沿或滚烫烫伤 (milk / skin / surface)

groups.name: Heel, Capsize & Invert · 倾斜与翻覆 (Heel, Capsize, Turtle)
groups.tip: 重心偏移或底朝天

items.def_zh: （船只因偏载或进水而）持续侧倾
items.def_en: of a ship: to lean steadily to one side, especially because of cargo shift or flooding
items.ex_en: The stricken cargo vessel began to list dangerously toward her damaged starboard side.
items.ex_zh: 那艘受损的货轮开始危险地向遭到破坏的右舷一侧持续倾侧。

items.def_zh: （船只等）倾斜，倾侧；使倾斜；紧随，尾随
items.def_en: (especially of a boat or ship) To lean over or tilt to one side; to cause to lean over.
items.ex_en: A ferocious gust of wind caused the sleek racing yacht to heel sharply.
items.ex_zh: 一阵狂暴的突风使那艘流线型的竞速游艇剧烈地倾斜向一侧。
items.ex2_en: Sudden violent crosswinds can heel the tall sailboat dangerously to port.
items.ex2_zh: 突如其来的强烈侧风会使高大的帆船危险地向左舷倾斜。

items.def_en: fall or cause something to tilt over onto its side or upside down
items.ex_en: The overloaded rowboat began to tip over into the icy river water suddenly.
items.ex_zh: 那艘超载的划艇突然开始侧向翻倒进冰冷的河水中。
items.ex2_en: The playful puppy managed to tip over the heavy plastic trashcan.
items.ex2_zh: 淘气的小狗把沉重的塑料垃圾桶给碰倒了。

items.def_zh: （船只或车辆）翻覆，底朝天翻转；捕龟
items.def_en: (especially of a boat or vehicle) To turn completely upside down; capsize.
items.ex_en: The reckless speeder hit the slick curb and caused the vehicle to turtle.
items.ex_zh: 那辆鲁莽超速的车撞上了湿滑的路缘石，导致整辆车底朝天翻了过去。

items.def_en: to capsize onto its side or back; of a person, to fall over suddenly
items.ex_en: Overcome by the stifling warehouse heat, the exhausted worker seemed about to keel over.
items.ex_zh: 由于难以忍受仓库中窒息的酷热，那位筋疲力尽的工人似乎马上要栽倒在地。

items.def_en: turn completely upside down or onto its side, especially of a boat or vehicle
items.ex_en: The racing catamaran caught a sudden rogue wave and began to roll over.
items.ex_zh: 那艘竞速双体船遭遇了一阵突如其来的狂浪，开始倾侧颠覆。

items.def_en: capsize or invert so that the underside is facing upward
items.ex_en: A sudden heavy swell caused the light wooden dinghy to turn over completely.
items.ex_zh: 一阵突如其来的巨浪导致那艘轻便的小木艇彻底翻扣了过去。

items.def_en: of a boat: to overturn completely in the water, or to cause one to do so
items.ex_en: Fierce ocean squalls threatened to capsize the fragile sailboat far from the shore.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的海上飑风眼看就要将那艘远离海岸的脆弱帆船彻底掀翻。
items.ex2_en: The small fishing boat might capsize if large rogue waves hit.
items.ex2_zh: 如果遭遇巨大的异常涌浪，这艘小渔船可能会倾覆。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this nautical and physical motion frame describe watercraft or upright bodies tilting progressively from upright trim to complete upside-down inversion. Nuances range from temporary lateral leaning caused by wind (heel, list) to dynamic flipping (capsize) and full 180-degree hull inversion (turtle, keel over).
groups.summary_zh: 描述船只或物体受风浪或外力发生侧倾乃至完全倒扣翻沉的动态过程。
groups.desc_en: Denotes lateral tilting, destabilization, or complete inversion of floating vessels, vehicles, or bodies, contrasting with simple falling by emphasizing a pivot along an axis until equilibrium is lost.
groups.desc_zh: 指船体、车辆或躯体沿轴线发生横向倾斜、失衡乃至彻底翻覆，与单纯跌倒（fall）的区别在于强调失去平衡并倒扣反转的力学轴向运动。
groups.nuance_en: list: static, ongoing tilt caused by uneven weight (ship / vessel) · heel: dynamic lean under external force like wind or waves (sailboat / yacht) · capsize: overturning entirely in water (boat / canoe) · turtle: flipping upside down until the hull or roof stays inverted (dinghy / car) · keel over: collapsing sideways suddenly from weakness or shock (person / patient)
groups.nuance_zh: list: 因配载不均导致的静止持续倾斜 (ship / vessel) · heel: 在风浪外力作用下的动态侧倾 (sailboat / yacht) · capsize: 水上彻底底朝天翻沉 (boat / canoe) · turtle: 翻转至完全倒扣状态 (dinghy / car) · keel over: 因虚弱猝然向侧方倒地 (person / patient)

groups.name: Hesitate & Scruple over Details · 疑义与据理力争 (Demur, Stickle, Scruple)
groups.tip: 为细枝末节据理力争僵持不下

items.def_zh: 犹豫，迟疑（因吃惊或疑虑而裹足不前）
items.def_en: (+ at) to hesitate or be reluctant to accept or do something because of scruples or difficulty
items.ex_en: Principled auditors might boggle at the questionable accounting methods discovered in the ledger.
items.ex_zh: 有原则的审计人员可能会对账簿中发现的存疑做账手段感到犹豫不决。

items.def_en: (+ sth) raise petty, unnecessary objections or quibbles over minor details
items.ex_en: Hypercritical reviewers will invariably cavil at minor formatting choices in this lengthy report.
items.ex_zh: 吹毛求疵的审稿人总会在这份长篇报告里对微不足道的排版格式挑剔一番。

items.def_zh: 顾忌，起疑虑（通常用于否定句）
items.def_en: (+ to do sth) to hesitate to do something because one thinks it may be morally wrong
items.ex_en: He did not scruple to disclose confidential records to advance his own career.
items.ex_zh: 为了提升自己的仕途，他毫不顾忌地公开了绝密档案。

items.def_zh: 提出异议，抗辩，表示反对或迟疑
items.def_en: (+ at/to) to express disagreement, hesitation, or polite objection to something.
items.ex_en: Polite board members did not openly demur at the ambitious corporate reorganization scheme.
items.ex_zh: 彬彬有礼的董事会成员并未对这项野心勃勃的企业重组方案公然提出异议。

items.def_zh: 对……犹豫畏缩；对……表示异议
items.def_en: (+ sth) hesitate or refuse to proceed because of scruples, difficulty, or reluctance
items.ex_en: Several cautious committee members chose to balk at approving the extremely costly project.
items.ex_zh: 几位谨小慎微的委员会成员对批准这项极其昂贵的工程表示犹豫畏缩。

items.def_zh: 因顾虑而犹豫；因良心不安而止步
items.def_en: (+ sth) hesitate to do something because of moral doubts or principled scruples
items.ex_en: The upright politician would stick at accepting bribes disguised as harmless campaign donations.
items.ex_zh: 这位刚正不阿的政客因良心所致，绝不肯收受伪装成无害竞选捐赠的贿赂。

items.def_en: (+ about/over) to raise trivial or irritating objections to avoid addressing the main issue
items.ex_en: Lawyers continued to quibble over tiny semantic distinctions instead of settling the contract.
items.ex_zh: 律师们继续为微小的语义差别吹毛求疵，而不是抓紧敲定合同。

items.def_zh: （为微不足道的细节）据理力争，吹毛求疵，固执己见
items.def_en: (+ for/about/over) to argue stubbornly or insist pedantically on minor points or rules.
items.ex_en: Pedantic peddlers often stickle over every single trivial penny during minor roadside transactions.
items.ex_zh: 小气市侩在路边做小买卖时，常常为区区一分小钱而固执地斤斤计较。

groups.summary_en: Refers to raising objections or showing reluctance over ethical principles, rules, or minor terms rather than entering open conflict. 'Demur' signals polite, principled hesitation, while 'stickle' marks rigid, stubborn insistence on exact details.
groups.summary_zh: 出于原则或细则提出疑义、犹豫不决或固执坚持争端。
groups.desc_en: Denotes pausing, disputing, or refusing compliance based on moral reservations, fastidiousness, or petty technicalities, contrasting with generic hesitation by locating resistance in conscience or pedantic objection.
groups.desc_zh: 指因良心道德顾虑或拘泥于细微枝节而犹豫、提出异议或拒不依从，与一般迟疑（hesitate）的区别在于阻力源自道德顾忌或挑剔细节。
groups.nuance_en: demur: politely raise polite doubt or reluctance (proposal / suggestion) · scruple: hesitate out of moral or ethical conscience (lie / cheat) · balk at: refuse abruptly out of reluctance or difficulty (price / compromise) · quibble: dispute trivial technicalities to evade agreement (details / wording) · stickle: insist stubbornly on punctilious points (protocol / terms)
groups.nuance_zh: demur: 委婉礼貌地提出异议或迟疑 (proposal / suggestion) · scruple: 出于良心道德而顾忌退缩 (lie / cheat) · balk at: 面对阻力或高昂代价断然畏缩止步 (price / compromise) · quibble: 纠缠琐碎枝节以回避核心 (details / wording) · stickle: 固执己见地死扣细则与规矩 (protocol / terms)

groups.name: High-Heat Cooking & Overheating · 顶热炙烤与火候过度 (Broil, Overcook, Scorch)
groups.tip: 明火烧烤或过度烹煮

items.def_en: [I/T] to ruin food completely by cooking it for too long or at too high a temperature
items.ex_en: If you neglect the simmering skillet, you will surely burn the delicate garlic.
items.ex_zh: 如果你疏忽了文火煎锅，肯定会把娇嫩的大蒜完全烧糊。
items.ex2_en: The sweet buttery garlic will burn quickly if the heat is too high.
items.ex2_zh: 如果火太大，香甜的黄油大蒜很快就会糊掉。

items.def_en: to cook food on a heavy flat hot surface or iron plate with high heat
items.ex_en: The short-order cook proceeded to griddle several beef patties over the sizzling iron plate.
items.ex_zh: 快餐厨师随后在嘶嘶作响的铁板上烙烤了几块牛肉饼。

items.def_en: (+ sth) be ruined or destroyed by excessive heat, or burn food completely
items.ex_en: Don't forget the toast on high heat, or it will completely burn up.
items.ex_zh: 别开大火就把吐司不管了，否则它会被彻底烧成焦炭。

items.def_zh: （因过度受热）变干硬；烘干过度
items.def_en: (+ sth) lose all moisture and become hard through prolonged or excessive cooking heat
items.ex_en: Prolonged baking at elevated temperatures will inevitably dry out the delicate roasted chicken.
items.ex_zh: 在过高的温度下烘烤过久，必然会导致鲜嫩的烤鸡变得干硬无汁。
items.ex2_en: The tender roast beef will dry out if left in the oven.
items.ex2_zh: 如果留在烤箱里，鲜嫩的烤牛肉就会风干变柴。

items.def_en: (+ sth) become or make the surface of food pleasantly dry and firm using high direct heat
items.ex_en: Broil the seasoned chicken skin for two minutes to crisp up the edges.
items.ex_zh: 把调味鸡皮炙烤两分钟，好让边缘变得香脆诱人。
items.ex2_en: The seasoned potato slices will crisp up beautifully under high heat.
items.ex2_zh: 调味过的土豆片在高温下会变得非常香脆。

items.def_en: [T/I] to burn the surface of food slightly or unintentionally by excessive direct heat
items.ex_en: Keep stirring the custard constantly so that you do not scorch the bottom.
items.ex_zh: 不断搅动蛋奶糊，这样才不至于把锅底烧焦。
items.ex2_en: The delicate cotton fabric will scorch easily under an excessively hot iron.
items.ex2_zh: 娇贵的棉织物在过热的熨斗下很容易被烤焦。

items.def_zh: （在烤架或烤箱上火下）烤，炙烤；（天气等）酷热，烘烤
items.def_en: 1. (chiefly NAmE) To cook food by direct heat under an oven element or over charcoal (equivalent to BrE 'grill'). 2. To make or become extremely hot under the sun or high heat.
items.ex_en: Adjust the oven setting to broil the seasoned flank steak over intense heat.
items.ex_zh: 调整烤箱设置，用强烈的上火炙烤那块腌制好的牛侧腹牛排。
items.ex2_en: The marinated pork ribs will broil quickly on the upper rack.
items.ex2_zh: 腌制好的猪排在烤箱上层会很快烤好。

items.def_zh: 把……煮得过久，过度烹饪；煮得过久
items.def_en: To cook food for too long so that it becomes dry, burnt, or spoiled.
items.ex_en: Take care not to overcook the tender salmon fillets in the hot oven.
items.ex_zh: 小心别把烤箱里那几块鲜嫩的三文鱼柳烹煮过久了。
items.ex2_en: Tender seafood will overcook rapidly if you leave it in boiling broth.
items.ex2_zh: 如果你把鲜嫩的海鲜留在滚烫的肉汤里，它很快就会煮过头。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame contrast aggressive direct overhead radiant cooking with cooking food too long or at excessive heat, leading to degradation of texture or burnt results.
groups.summary_zh: 采用上方强直射热源炙烤，或因加热失当、过火导致食物烧焦烹坏的情境。
groups.desc_en: Denotes applying extreme direct thermal radiation or heat that risks or results in charring, drying, and structural degradation, contrasting with plain cooking by foregrounding intense radiative heat and over-processing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过强烈的直接热辐射炙烤，乃至导致焦糊、脱水或质地损坏，与常规烹饪的区别在于极高温度下的炙烤及过热毁损风险。
groups.nuance_en: broil: cook under intense, direct top-down dry heat (steak / ribs) · griddle: cook flat with heavy surface heat (pancake / burger) · scorch: singe or burn superficially by excessive heat (fabric / sauce) · overcook: expose too long to heat, ruining texture or flavor (vegetables / meat) · dry out: deplete moisture completely through heat (roast / bread)
groups.nuance_zh: broil: 用高强度直火顶热炙烤 (steak / ribs) · griddle: 在平底铁板上高温煎烙 (pancake / burger) · scorch: 表面轻微灼焦或烧焦发黑 (fabric / sauce) · overcook: 烹调时间过长毁损口感风味 (vegetables / meat) · dry out: 过度受热导致水分彻底流失 (roast / bread)

groups.name: Impair & Debilitate · 阻碍损毁与致残瘫痪 (Queer, Cripple, Hamstring)
groups.tip: 从轻微受损到彻底致残

items.def_en: (informal, dated) to spoil or ruin a plan or someone's chances of success.
items.ex_en: The unexpected arrival of the building inspector threatened to queer our secret renovation.
items.ex_zh: 建筑检查员的意外到访眼看就要搞砸我们的秘密翻修计划。

items.def_en: to severely restrict the efficiency, freedom of action, or operation of someone or something
items.ex_en: Chronic budget reductions continue to hamstring the agency's ability to enforce basic regulations.
items.ex_zh: 长期的预算削减持续削弱该机构执行基本法规的能力。

items.def_en: slow down gradually until completely stopping or becoming incapacitated
items.ex_en: Due to severe winter storms, the city's transit network will soon grind to a halt.
items.ex_zh: 由于严重的冬季风暴，整个城市的交通网络很快将陷入停滞状态。

items.def_zh: 使失去战斗力；使丧失功能
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) injure, damage, or impair someone or something so that they cannot function or participate
items.ex_en: A severe knee injury threatens to put the star striker out of action.
items.ex_zh: 一次严重的膝伤眼看就要让这位明星前锋无法上场参赛。

items.def_en: (+ sth) stop a machine, system, or organization from operating, often rendering it completely non-functional
items.ex_en: A massive cyberattack shut down the entire hospital network for several hours yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 一场大规模的网络攻击昨天使整家医院的网络系统瘫痪了数小时。
items.ex2_en: The old factory will shut down permanently at the end of December.
items.ex2_zh: 这家老工厂将在十二月底永久停工关闭。

items.def_zh: 严重破坏，削弱；使致残，使残疾
items.def_en: 1. to seriously damage an organization, economy, or system so it can no longer operate properly. 2. (dated, offensive) to injure someone so that they are permanently unable to walk or use their limbs properly.
items.ex_en: The prolonged transport strike could cripple the nation's fragile manufacturing economy.
items.ex_zh: 旷日持久的交通罢工可能会严重削弱该国脆弱的制造业经济。

items.def_zh: 使瘫痪；使完全停止运转
items.def_en: to cause a person, system, or organization to become completely unable to act or function
items.ex_en: Heavy blizzard conditions completely paralyzed commuter train services across the metropolitan area.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雪肆虐导致整个大都市区的通勤列车服务完全瘫痪。

items.def_zh: 使无能力，使伤残丧失工作能力
items.def_en: to prevent someone or something from functioning normally, as by injury, illness, or damage
items.ex_en: A sudden knee injury incapacitated the chief engineer just before construction began.
items.ex_zh: 就在工程开工前，膝盖的意外受伤使总工程师丧失了正常工作能力。

groups.summary_en: An agent, condition, or event impairs an operation, person, or organization so severely that it loses its operational capacity. Nuances scale from spoiling or compromising a process to utterly incapacitating or paralyzing functionality.
groups.summary_zh: 破坏运作或致残机体，使其丧失正常机能与行动力。
groups.desc_en: Denotes damaging, disabling, or structurally neutralizing a system, person, or operation, contrasting with passive weakening by emphasizing functional immobilization and loss of effective agency.
groups.desc_zh: 指对系统、肢体或运转机制进行破坏、阻碍或使其瘫痪，与一般消弱（weaken）的区别在于强调彻底剥夺其行动机能与运作能力。
groups.nuance_en: hamstring: severely handicap efficiency or leverage beforehand (reform / effort / economy) · cripple: inflict devastating, lasting functional damage (industry / infrastructure / economy) · paralyze: freeze into total immobility or indecision (traffic / government / sector) · incapacitate: render physically or legally unable to function (worker / driver / soldier) · queer: disrupt and ruin the prospect of success (deal / pitch / chances)
groups.nuance_zh: hamstring: 预先束缚手脚以重挫运作效率 (reform / effort / economy) · cripple: 造成破坏性且持久的机能残障 (industry / infrastructure / economy) · paralyze: 使系统完全停摆或陷入僵滞 (traffic / government / sector) · incapacitate: 使身体或法律层面丧失行为能力 (worker / driver / soldier) · queer: 捣乱破坏使全盘计划泡汤 (deal / pitch / chances)

groups.name: Indirect Communication & Implication · 委婉暗示与示意 (Hint, Intimate)
groups.tip: 不直说而委婉隐晦暗示

items.def_en: to express or indicate indirectly without explicitly stating
items.ex_en: The manager's cautious remarks imply that major budget reductions are approaching.
items.ex_zh: 经理谨慎的言辞暗示着重大的预算削减即将到来。

items.def_en: To suggest or indicate something indirectly.
items.ex_en: She did not mention leaving, but her quiet behavior hinted as much.
items.ex_zh: 她虽未言明去意，但沉默的举止已透露出了这一点。

items.def_en: (+ sth) suggest or allude to something indirectly rather than stating it plainly
items.ex_en: The latest government report hinted at significant regulatory changes next year.
items.ex_zh: 最新的政府报告暗示了明年可能迎来重大监管变革。

items.def_en: (+ sth) mention or allude to a subject briefly or indirectly in passing
items.ex_en: The speaker only touched on the budget deficit without providing any concrete solutions.
items.ex_zh: 发言人只是简略提到了财政赤字，并未给出任何具体解决方案。

items.def_en: (+ sth) intend or convey a subtle meaning indirectly; imply
items.ex_en: I honestly had no clue what he was getting at during lunch.
items.ex_zh: 说实话，午餐时我根本没弄懂他到底在暗指什么。

items.def_en: 1. To communicate or make something known indirectly; to hint. 2. To state or announce officially.
items.ex_en: The board chairman intimated that several senior directors would soon step down.
items.ex_zh: 董事会主席委婉透露，几位资深董事不久后将会辞职。

items.def_en: (+ to) to mention or refer to something in an indirect, passing manner
items.ex_en: The speaker subtly alluded to ongoing legal disputes without giving any details.
items.ex_zh: 发言人含蓄地提及了正在进行的法律纠纷，未透露任何细节。

items.def_zh: 含沙射影；暗指（常含贬义）
items.def_en: to suggest or hint at something unpleasant in an indirect and unpleasant way
items.ex_en: He dared to insinuate that my recent promotion was entirely unearned.
items.ex_zh: 他竟然含沙射影，暗示我最近的晋升完全是名不副实。

groups.summary_en: Verbs describing communicative acts where the speaker conveys meaning subtly, obliquely, or delicately rather than stating it plainly.
groups.summary_zh: 指不直接言明，而是通过微妙言辞、含蓄提示或眼神委婉传达意图。
groups.desc_en: Denotes conveying meaning covertly, subtly, or through associational cues, contrasting with explicit assertion by relying on the recipient's inferential deduction.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过含蓄迂回的线索或隐语传递意图，与明确陈述（state explicitly）的区别在于依赖接收方的联想与推论。
groups.nuance_en: hint: provide a faint, deliberate clue (intentions / possibility) · imply: logically entangle an unstated consequence or premise (guilt / meaning) · intimate: communicate delicate or personal knowledge subtly (desire / resignation) · insinuate: sneak in a sly, usually derogatory or malicious suggestion (corruption / incompetence) · allude: refer to something obliquely without direct mention (past / crisis)
groups.nuance_zh: hint: 故意给出微弱线索以暗示 (intentions / possibility) · imply: 逻辑上蕴涵未明言的结论 (guilt / meaning) · intimate: 私下委婉含蓄地透露意向 (desire / resignation) · insinuate: 拐弯抹角地影射负面或恶意内容 (corruption / incompetence) · allude: 暗讽或借典故旁敲侧击 (past / crisis)

groups.name: Induct & Invest Clergy/Rulers · 授职与就职 (Enthrone, Invest, Ordain)
groups.tip: 授予神职、王权或官方职务

items.def_zh: 正式授予（职位、权力或长袍）
items.def_en: (+ with) to formally confer a rank, office, or insignia of power upon someone
items.ex_en: The chancellor was invested with supreme authority during the historic convocation ceremony.
items.ex_zh: 在历史性的全体大会上，校长被正式授予了最高权力。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to officially induct someone into public office through a formal oath
items.ex_en: The new president will be sworn in on January 20th.
items.ex_zh: 新总统将于1月20日宣誓就职。

items.def_zh: 授予圣职；封立（牧师、神父）
items.def_en: to officially confer holy orders on someone, appointing them as a priest, minister, or rabbi
items.ex_en: The bishop will ordain three new priests at the cathedral this Sunday.
items.ex_zh: 主教将于本周日在主教座堂为三位新神父授予圣职。

items.def_en: to introduce someone into an official public position with a formal ceremony
items.ex_en: Parliament will inaugurate the newly elected president in a formal ceremony tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 议会将于明天举行正式典礼，为新当选的总统举行就职仪式。

items.def_zh: 使正式就任；吸收（入职/入会）
items.def_en: (+ into) to formally admit someone into a post, holy office, or organization
items.ex_en: The academy inducted the distinguished composer into its prestigious fellowship last night.
items.ex_zh: 该学院昨晚正式吸纳这位著名作曲家为其尊贵的会士。

items.def_en: to dedicate someone formally and religiously to a divine service or to the office of bishop
items.ex_en: The archbishop gathered the clergy to consecrate the newly chosen provincial bishop.
items.ex_zh: 大主教召集全体神职人员，为新当选的教区主教祝圣。

items.def_zh: 授予（某人）神职；给……穿僧袍（或长袍）
items.def_en: 1. To invest someone with clerical office or priestly robes. 2. To clothe in a frock.
items.ex_en: The abbot prepared to frock the humble novice before the ancient altar.
items.ex_zh: 古老的祭坛前，修道院院长准备为这位谦逊的见习修士披上僧袍。

items.def_zh: 使登基，使即位；使就主教职；尊崇
items.def_en: To formally place a monarch or high-ranking religious leader on a throne in an official ceremony.
items.ex_en: They will enthrone the new archbishop during an ancient cathedral liturgical ceremony.
items.ex_zh: 他们将在庄严的主教座堂礼拜仪式中为新大主教举行登基就任礼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote ceremonial, institutional installations of religious or civic dignitaries into official office or holy orders. They involve formal rites such as dressing in vestments, seating upon a bishop's or monarch's chair, or conferring official powers.
groups.summary_zh: 通过庄严宗教或世俗仪式为神职人员、主教或统治者授予圣职与职权。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formally, ritually, or ecclesiastically bestowing sacred or executive authority upon an individual, contrasting with secular appointment by emphasizing solemn ceremonial initiation and sanctification.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过宗教或神圣庄严的仪式授予特定圣职、王权或最高领袖权位，与普通世俗任职（appoint）相比突显神圣性与礼仪性就职。
groups.nuance_en: ordain: invest with holy orders through sacramental rites (priest / minister) · consecrate: solemnly dedicate to a divine purpose or high sacred office (bishop / sanctuary) · invest: formally endow with official robes, insignia, and authority (ruler / sovereign) · enthrone: solemnly place on a throne to inaugurate reign (monarch / bishop) · swear in: administer an official oath of office (president / judge)
groups.nuance_zh: ordain: 经圣礼按立授予神职 (priest / minister) · consecrate: 祝圣封立为高级神职或专用场所 (bishop / sanctuary) · invest: 授予法衣、权标并赋予权威 (ruler / sovereign) · enthrone: 举行加冕登基大典 (monarch / bishop) · swear in: 主持法定宣誓就职仪式 (president / judge)

groups.name: Indulgent & Satiating Overconsumption · 纵欲暴食与饱胀进食 (Binge, Gorge)
groups.tip: 放任食欲毫无节制大吃大喝

items.def_en: (+ on sth) eat heartily, enthusiastically, and voraciously
items.ex_en: The hungry teenagers happily chowed down on pizza after their soccer tournament.
items.ex_zh: 足球比赛结束后，饥肠辘辘的青少年们高兴地大口吃着披萨。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) eat enough food until one is completely full
items.ex_en: Do not fill up on bread before the main dinner arrives, kids.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们，在主菜上桌之前，可千万别拿面包填饱了肚子。
items.ex2_en: The attendant had to fill up each car before the long journey.
items.ex2_zh: 服务员必须在长途旅行前给每辆车加满油。

items.def_en: (+ on) to indulge in eating an extraordinarily large amount of food greedily
items.ex_en: We stayed up late to watch movies and pig out on snacks.
items.ex_zh: 我们熬夜看电影，胡吃海塞了一大堆零食。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽至撑饱；大吃特吃
items.def_en: (+ with sth) eat a very large amount of food until uncomfortably full
items.ex_en: The children stuffed themselves with sweet pastries until their bellies visibly ached.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们大吃甜糕点，直吃到肚子明显作痛才肯罢休。

items.def_en: (+ oneself) to eat so much food that one feels completely, uncomfortably full
items.ex_en: I stuffed myself at the buffet and could barely walk back home.
items.ex_zh: 我在自助餐厅吃得太撑，几乎走不回去了。

items.raw_cluster: 暴饮暴食与放纵 Binge & Indulge
items.def_zh: 大吃大喝，暴食；狂欢放纵
items.def_en: To indulge excessively in food, alcohol, or another activity in a short period.
items.ex_en: Stressed college students frequently binge on junk food during stressful final exams.
items.ex_zh: 面临巨大压力的大学生在期末考试期间经常暴饮暴食垃圾食品。

items.def_zh: 狼吞虎咽，大吃大嚼；塞饱
items.def_en: To eat a large amount of food greedily and until completely full.
items.ex_en: The hungry hikers gorged on roasted potatoes around the blazing campfire.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的徒步旅行者围着熊熊的篝火狼吞虎咽地吃着烤土豆。

items.def_en: to feed or supply someone (especially oneself) with food to full excess
items.ex_en: The greedy nobles glutted themselves with rich delicacies throughout the banquet.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的贵族们在整场宴会中尽情享用珍馐佳肴，直吃得过饱。

groups.summary_en: Scale measuring the degree of uncontrolled, excessive food consumption to full bodily repletion and gluttonous stuffing.
groups.summary_zh: 反映从无节制的放纵暴食到将胃填满、吃到撑胀的程度递增。
groups.desc_en: Denotes excessive, unrestrained, and hedonistic food or drink consumption beyond natural satiety, contrasting with normal feeding by highlighting compulsive indulgence and bloated excess.
groups.desc_zh: 指超出正常饱腹界限的放纵、狂暴式暴饮暴食，与正常进食的区别在于放纵食欲、失控填塞及由此导致的饱胀。
groups.nuance_en: binge: indulge in an uncontrolled, compulsive eating bout (snack / dessert) · gorge: stuff oneself greedily to maximal physical capacity (meat / banquet) · glut: overwhelm or satiate to unpleasant excess (appetite / market) · pig out: eat enormous quantities untidily and gluttonously (junk food / pizza) · stuff: fill to uncomfortable tightness (oneself / belly)
groups.nuance_zh: binge: 失控且病态地阵发性暴饮暴食 (snack / dessert) · gorge: 狼吞虎咽塞入最大胃容量 (meat / banquet) · glut: 过量充斥以致生厌 (appetite / market) · pig out: 不顾吃相地放肆大嚼暴食 (junk food / pizza) · stuff: 把肚子塞得紧绷发胀 (oneself / belly)

groups.name: Informal & Improvised Musical Performance · 随性即兴演奏 (Vamp, Busk, Jam)
groups.tip: 不拘一格的即兴表演与演奏

items.def_zh: 随意弹拨；漫不经心地试音奏乐
items.def_en: to improvise or play an instrument in a casual, aimless way
items.ex_en: He sat on the porch, idly noodling on his acoustic guitar.
items.ex_zh: 他坐在门廊上，漫不经心地随手弹拨着原声吉他。

items.def_zh: 随性伴奏；跟着即兴演奏
items.def_en: to play music informally and spontaneously along with other musicians or a recording
items.ex_en: The bassist started to jam along with the upbeat brass section.
items.ex_zh: 贝斯手开始跟着欢快跳跃的铜管乐声随性即兴伴奏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to play an improvised musical variation or series of notes based on an existing theme
items.ex_en: The saxophonist began to riff on the classic jazz melody with flair.
items.ex_zh: 萨克斯手技艺出众，开始在那段经典爵士旋律的基础上即兴变奏。

items.def_en: to play improvised music casually with other musicians
items.ex_en: The local indie musicians meet weekly in the garage to jam together.
items.ex_zh: 这群当地的独立音乐人每周都会在车库碰头一起即兴合奏。
items.ex2_en: Desperate commuters jam the subway entrances during peak morning rush hours.
items.ex2_zh: 在早高峰时段，绝望的通勤者挤满了地铁入口。

items.raw_cluster: 即兴创作与演奏 Improvise & Vamp
items.def_zh: 即兴伴奏，弹奏反复过渡乐节；拼凑，捏造（vamp up）；勾引（男子）
items.def_en: 1. (music) To improvise a simple, repeating musical accompaniment. 2. ('vamp up') To patch up, refurbish, or invent hastily. 3. (informal) To act flirtatiously or seductively toward someone.
items.ex_en: The pianist had to vamp softly until the lead singer stepped onstage.
items.ex_zh: 钢琴师不得不弹奏轻柔的反复过渡乐节，直到主唱登台。

items.def_en: [I/T] to sweep the fingers lightly across the strings of an instrument
items.ex_en: She closed her eyes and lightly strummed the delicate ukulele strings.
items.ex_zh: 她闭上双眼，轻柔地扫弄着尤克里里那纤细的琴弦。

items.def_en: 1. To play music, sing, or perform in a public place in order to earn money from passersby.
items.ex_en: Street performers often busk near the crowded subway station during rush hour.
items.ex_zh: 街头艺人经常在高峰时段拥挤的地铁站附近卖艺演奏。

items.def_zh: 轻快奏出（高音），轻柔鸣啭；引诱，哄骗
items.def_en: 1. To play or sing light, high-pitched, piping or warbling musical notes. 2. (dialect) To coax or wheedle.
items.ex_en: A cheerful shepherd began to tweedle a jaunty tune upon his pipe.
items.ex_zh: 欢快的牧羊人用风笛轻快地奏出了一支活泼的调子。

groups.summary_en: Musicians play instruments or sing in an informal, improvised, or public street context, often repeating basic chord patterns, busking for tips, or casually noodling on an instrument.
groups.summary_zh: 指在街头卖艺、即兴伴奏或随意摆弄乐器的非正式演奏方式。
groups.desc_en: Denotes spontaneous, casual, or public musical performance without rigid notation, contrasting with rehearsed concert playing by highlighting improvisation, jamming, and street-level execution.
groups.desc_zh: 指脱离严格乐谱、随性即兴或在街头公共场所演奏，与正规排练演奏（rehearse/perform）的区别在于其自发即兴感与非正式场景。
groups.nuance_en: jam: improvise freely together with other musicians (musicians / band) · busk: perform in public streets or squares for voluntary tips (commuters / crowd) · riff on: spontaneously develop variations on a theme (melody / motif) · vamp: play a simple repeating harmonic accompaniment while waiting (chords / progression) · noodle: casually wander over an instrument without formal direction (guitar / keys)
groups.nuance_zh: jam: 与乐手们非正式即兴合奏切磋 (musicians / band) · busk: 在街头或地铁即兴卖艺募赏 (commuters / crowd) · riff on: 基于某段旋律动机随性变奏发挥 (melody / motif) · vamp: 重复简单的过渡和弦以填补空白 (chords / progression) · noodle: 漫不经心地随手乱弹拨弄琴弦 (guitar / keys)

groups.name: Infraction Penalization & Criminalization · 处罚与定罪 (Ticket, Penalize, Criminalize)
groups.tip: 从明令禁止上升到定罪惩治

items.def_en: to summon someone to court or issue an official ticket for a minor infraction
items.ex_en: The patrol officer cited the careless driver for exceeding the speed limit.
items.ex_zh: 巡警对那名超速驾驶的粗心司机开出了违规处罚单。

items.def_en: to compel someone to pay an amount of money as an official punishment for breaking a law or rule
items.ex_en: The city council fined the restaurant heavily for severe sanitary code violations.
items.ex_zh: 市议会对那家严重违反卫生条例的餐馆处以高额罚款。

items.def_zh: 对……开违规罚单；为……购票（或售票）
items.def_en: 1. to issue an official notice of a traffic offense or other fine to someone. 2. to provide someone or something with a ticket.
items.ex_en: The traffic warden ticketed three illegally parked vehicles along the downtown avenue.
items.ex_zh: 交通管理员对市中心大道上非法停放的三辆车开了罚单。

items.def_en: to impose a penalty or sanction on someone for breaking a rule, law, or agreement
items.ex_en: Referees will penalize any aggressive player who violates established safety protocols.
items.ex_zh: 裁判将对任何违反既定安全规则的攻击性球员予以惩处。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to punish or penalize someone severely for an infraction or offense
items.ex_en: The supervisor will come down on anyone caught falsifying their attendance records.
items.ex_zh: 主管将严惩任何被抓到伪造考勤记录的人。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to enforce laws or penalties rigorously against offenders or unlawful acts
items.ex_en: The police announced a new campaign to crack down on reckless driving.
items.ex_zh: 警方宣布开展一项新行动，严厉打击危险驾驶行为。

items.def_en: [I/T] to conduct legal proceedings against someone in respect of a criminal charge
items.ex_en: The state decided to prosecute the fraudulent contractor for corporate embezzlement.
items.ex_zh: 州政府决定以职务侵占罪对那个涉嫌欺诈的承包商提起公诉。

items.def_zh: 定……为违法行为，使定罪；把……当作罪犯对待
items.def_en: 1. to make an action or activity illegal by law. 2. to treat someone or a group as criminals.
items.ex_en: Human rights advocates argue that governments should not criminalize peaceful public protests.
items.ex_zh: 人权倡导者主张，政府不应将和平的公众抗议定为违法行为。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to law enforcement and statutory measures applied to wrongful conduct, progressing from minor administrative citations to severe statutory penalization and the formal classification of acts as crimes.
groups.summary_zh: 针对违章或违法行为施加处罚，从行政罚款升级为刑事定罪。
groups.desc_en: Denotes enforcing regulatory compliance or state sanction against illicit conduct, contrasting with private reprimand by exercising codified legal or pecuniary retribution.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据法规对违规或违法行为施加惩戒、罚金或定罪，与普通训诫的区别在于国家或行政权力的成文法制裁。
groups.nuance_en: ticket: issue a formal citation for a minor infraction (driver / speeder) · fine: impose a mandatory financial penalty (offender / company) · penalize: handicap or punish under specific rules or law (breach / violation) · criminalize: turn a previously unlegislated act into a punishable crime (behavior / protest) · crack down on: enforce aggressive, concerted suppressive action (crime / dissent)
groups.nuance_zh: ticket: 为轻微违规行为开具行政罚单 (driver / speeder) · fine: 依法裁决处以金钱罚款 (offender / company) · penalize: 按规则或法律施加扣分、受罚或惩处 (breach / violation) · criminalize: 通过立法将某种行为定性为犯罪 (behavior / protest) · crack down on: 采取严厉的高压整肃打击 (crime / dissent)

groups.name: Infuse & Permeate · 灌注与渗透 (Thorough Fluidic Infiltration)
groups.tip: 液体或物质完全渗透灌注

items.def_en: (+ sth) to penetrate deeply into the substance of a material by liquid absorption
items.ex_en: Rainwater began to soak into the parched earth after months of drought.
items.ex_zh: 干旱数月后，雨水开始深深渗透进龟裂干涸的泥土中。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to slowly flow, spread, or diffuse throughout a porous medium
items.ex_en: Oily liquid seeped through the thick canvas bag onto the workshop floor.
items.ex_zh: 油性液体慢慢渗穿了厚帆布袋，滴落到了车间的地板上。

items.def_en: (+ with/into) to introduce or soak a quality or essence thoroughly into a medium
items.ex_en: The chef infused the olive oil with crushed garlic and fresh rosemary.
items.ex_zh: 厨师在橄榄油中浸入压碎的大蒜与新鲜迷迭香以萃取香气。

items.def_en: [I/T] to spread throughout and pervade every part of an area or material
items.ex_en: A rich aroma of freshly brewed coffee permeated the entire quiet morning bakery.
items.ex_zh: 浓郁的新煮咖啡香气弥漫在清晨宁静的面包店每一个角落。

items.def_en: (+ with) to saturate or inspire completely with a feeling, value, or quality
items.ex_en: Her visionary writings imbue young generations with profound hope and boundless courage.
items.ex_zh: 她那富有远见卓识的著作令年轻一代充满了深切希望与无限勇气。

items.def_en: to spread over or through something with light, color, or moisture
items.ex_en: Golden evening light suffused the ancient stone chapel through the rose window.
items.ex_zh: 金黄色的傍晚霞光穿过玫瑰花窗，洒满了整座古老的石砌小教堂。

items.def_zh: 相互渗透，互相贯通；穿透
items.def_en: (formal) To penetrate, permeate, or diffuse into each other; to spread through and blend together.
items.ex_en: Ancient cultural traditions and modern innovations interpenetrate harmoniously in the vibrant metropolis.
items.ex_zh: 古老的文化传统与现代的创新在这座充满活力的都市中交相渗透、融为一体。
items.ex2_en: Fresh artistic perspectives interpenetrate traditional painting methods across this latest gallery exhibition.
items.ex2_zh: 在这场最新的画廊展览中，崭新的艺术视角融入了传统绘画技法。

items.def_zh: 灌注（液体、血液于器官等）；充满，洒遍
items.def_en: 1. (medicine) To pass fluid, especially blood, through the vessels of an organ or tissue. 2. (literary) To suffuse or spread liquid, light, or color over something.
items.ex_en: Pale twilight began to perfuse the shadowy forest with an ethereal glow.
items.ex_zh: 苍白的薄暮开始在幽暗的森林中弥漫开来，笼罩着空灵的光晕。

groups.summary_en: A fluid, gas, quality, or substance deeply spreads, diffuses, and saturates throughout every part of a matrix or medium. 'Perfuse' and 'interpenetrate' denote specialized and reciprocal diffusion respectively.
groups.summary_zh: 液体、气味或无形质感彻底扩散并浸润充满整个空间或结构内部。
groups.desc_en: Denotes liquid, gas, or abstract qualities thoroughly saturating and penetrating every pore or part of an entity, contrasting with mere surface coating by pervasive internal absorption.
groups.desc_zh: 指液体、气体或抽象精神品质从内部彻底渗透、充盈并浸润每一处细微结构，与表面附着（coat）的区别在于深度的全方位浸染。
groups.nuance_en: infuse: instill a spirit, quality, or steeped flavor into a substance (flavor / confidence) · permeate: spread diffuse particles through porous barriers or culture (smell / ideology / water) · imbue: deeply saturate temperament, mind, or identity with qualities (culture / spirit / values) · suffuse: spread gradually across or throughout like light or flush (light / color / warmth) · perfuse: bathe or force fluid through anatomical tissue (tissues / organ)
groups.nuance_zh: infuse: 注入品格、精神力量或经浸泡提取风味 (flavor / confidence) · permeate: 弥散穿透多孔介质或深入社会肌理 (smell / ideology / water) · imbue: 将某种精神气质深层熏陶浸染于内心 (culture / spirit / values) · suffuse: 如光线、红晕般渐渐弥漫洋溢 (light / color / warmth) · perfuse: 医学上使液体贯注经由器官组织 (tissues / organ)

groups.name: Ingest & Consume · 进食与吞咽 (Eat, Devour, Gobble)
groups.tip: 口咽摄入食物的动作

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on/at) To take small, tentative bites of food slowly
items.ex_en: The shy rabbit sat calmly in the garden and nibbled on lettuce.
items.ex_zh: 那只害羞的兔子平静地坐在花园里，小口啃吃着生菜叶。

items.def_en: (+ sth) consume all of the food that has been served or prepared
items.ex_en: The enthusiastic audience ate up every single joke the comedian delivered.
items.ex_zh: 热情的观众全盘接受并享受着脱口秀演员讲出的每一个笑话。

items.def_en: (+ on sth) eat food greedily or enthusiastically
items.ex_en: The hungry construction workers chowed down on thick beef burgers at noon.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的建筑工人们在正午尽情大吃着厚实的牛肉汉堡。

items.def_en: (+ sth) start eating food enthusiastically and with gusto
items.ex_en: The famished tourists happily tucked into a hearty plate of pasta.
items.ex_zh: 饥肠辘辘的游客们高兴地大快朵颐，享受丰盛的意面。

items.def_en: 1. To put food into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it. 2. (+ away/into) To destroy or wear away gradually.
items.ex_en: The doctor advised the recovering patient to eat more fresh organic vegetables.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议正在康复中的病人多吃新鲜的有机蔬菜。

items.def_en: To consume food very quickly and eagerly, chewing very little
items.ex_en: The hurried student wolfed down a quick sandwich before the morning lecture.
items.ex_zh: 匆忙的学生在早课开始前狼吞虎咽地咽下了一个三明治。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ up/down) To eat food hurriedly and noisily, swallowing large pieces
items.ex_en: He was so starving that he quickly gobbled down the sweet pie.
items.ex_zh: 他饿极了，三下五除二就狼吞虎咽地吃光了那块甜馅饼。

items.def_en: To eat all of something greedily, rapidly, and voraciously
items.ex_en: The hungry beast devoured the fresh meat in a matter of seconds.
items.ex_zh: 那只饥饿的野兽几秒钟之内就将新鲜的肉块吞食殆尽。

groups.summary_en: An agent consumes solid food through the mouth by chewing and swallowing. Manners range from basic routine ingestion ('eat') to ravenous, aggressive consumption ('devour') or rapid, noisy gulping ('gobble', 'wolf down').
groups.summary_zh: 通过口腔咀嚼并吞下食物的动作，涵盖从常规进食到狼吞虎咽的粗鲁吃相。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the physical taking of nourishment into the alimentary tract, differentiated by velocity, voracity, and physical decorum from generic nutrient intake.
groups.desc_zh: 指将食物摄入消化道的生理动作，依据进食速度、贪婪程度及仪态从普通摄取营养中分化出来。
groups.nuance_en: nibble: take tiny, tentative, repeated small bites (cheese / biscuit) · devour: consume ravenously and destructively with speed (meal / prey) · wolf down: swallow huge portions rapidly without proper chewing (food / sandwich) · gobble: swallow hastily and noisily in large chunks (turkey / dinner) · chow down: eat heartily and enthusiastically in casual contexts (barbecue / feast)
groups.nuance_zh: nibble: 细嚼慢咽地小口微咬微啃 (cheese / biscuit) · devour: 如饥似渴、毁灭性地吞食殆尽 (meal / prey) · wolf down: 狼吞虎咽、不及咀嚼便大口咽下 (food / sandwich) · gobble: 粗鲁喧闹地大块吞咽 (turkey / dinner) · chow down: 随性开怀大吃 (barbecue / feast)

groups.name: Inspect & Scrutinize · 检查与细审 (Examine, Inspect, Scrutinize)
groups.tip: 严密审视细究各个细节

items.def_en: to examine something to see if it is correct, safe, or satisfactory
items.ex_en: Please check the engine oil level carefully before starting your long journey.
items.ex_zh: 在开始长途旅行前，请仔细检查一下机油油位。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) examine or inspect someone or something to ascertain accuracy, state, or safety
items.ex_en: We need to check out of the hotel by noon, but let's check out the local market first.
items.ex_zh: 我们需要在中午前结账退房，不过先去看看当地的集市吧。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) inspect or examine someone or something quickly to assess condition or quality
items.ex_en: The editor promised to look over the draft report before lunchtime today.
items.ex_zh: 编辑答应在今天午饭前大致过目浏览一下这份报告草稿。

items.def_en: to look at something carefully, especially to check that it is in good condition or complies with rules
items.ex_en: A certified safety officer will inspect the factory equipment tomorrow morning.
items.ex_zh: 持证安全官员将于明天上午正式视察这批工厂设备。

items.def_en: (+ sth) examine, review, or inspect something in detail for errors or quality
items.ex_en: The auditor spent hours going over the complex financial accounts for errors.
items.ex_zh: 审计员花了数小时仔细核查那些复杂的财务账目以寻找错误。

items.def_en: to look at or consider a person or thing carefully and thoroughly in order to learn more about them
items.ex_en: Medical researchers examined the tissue samples thoroughly under a high-powered microscope.
items.ex_zh: 医学研究人员在高倍显微镜下极其仔细地审查了这些组织样本。

items.def_en: to look at, read, or study something with intense concentration over an extended time
items.ex_en: Historians spent many weeks poring over fragile ancient manuscripts in the archive.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们在档案馆里耗费数周时间，专心致志地细读脆弱的古代手稿。

items.def_zh: 仔细审查，细看，严密审视
items.def_en: To examine or inspect someone or something very closely and thoroughly.
items.ex_en: Financial regulators closely scrutinized the suspicious bank transactions for possible money laundering.
items.ex_zh: 金融监管机构严密审视了这些可疑的银行交易，以排查潜在的洗钱行为。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe visually or analytically examining something with increasing degrees of critical thoroughness, moving from routine inspection to rigorous, unrelenting scrutiny for defects or hidden details.
groups.summary_zh: 指对事物进行由浅入深的细致检查、审视或严密核验。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately surveying, dissecting, or evaluating an object or situation with critical focus to detect flaws or verify status, contrasting with casual looking through methodical scrutiny.
groups.desc_zh: 指带着批判性审视目的，对目标进行细致勘察、解构与核验以探寻瑕疵，与漫不经心的看（look）相比具有严谨的方法性与专注度。
groups.nuance_en: inspect: critically examine against official standards or for defects (equipment / vehicle / factory) · scrutinize: subject to minute, relentless critical analysis (record / contract / detail) · examine: systematically test, observe, or evaluate composition and health (patient / specimen / evidence) · pore over: read or study with sustained, intense closeness (document / map / manuscript) · check: quickly confirm correctness, condition, or presence (tires / list / status)
groups.nuance_zh: inspect: 依据官方标准严格视察与验查瑕疵 (equipment / vehicle / factory) · scrutinize: 严苛、巨细靡遗地剖析审视 (record / contract / detail) · examine: 系统性检查体检、检测或评估证据 (patient / specimen / evidence) · pore over: 聚精会神、极度贴近地埋头研读 (document / map / manuscript) · check: 快速核实无误、清点或确认状态 (tires / list / status)

groups.name: Install & Invest · 任命与就职 (Ordain, Inaugurate, Install)
groups.tip: 官职委派与仪式性就职履新

items.def_en: (+ with/in) to formally endow someone with legal rights, power, or official insignia
items.ex_en: The constitution invests the supreme court with the power to interpret laws.
items.ex_zh: 宪法正式赋予最高法院解释法律的至高权力。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to formally admit someone into public office through an official oath
items.ex_en: The new president will be sworn in on January 20th.
items.ex_zh: 新总统将于1月20日宣誓就职。

items.def_zh: 开启，引进（新时代、新任期）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to mark the formal beginning of a new period, regime, or leadership
items.ex_en: The signing of the landmark treaty will usher in a peaceful era.
items.ex_zh: 这一具有里程碑意义的条约签署将开启一个和平的新纪元。

items.def_en: (+ as/in) to formally place someone in an official position or rank with an appropriate ceremony
items.ex_en: The university will formally install Professor Clark as the new chancellor next month.
items.ex_zh: 该大学将于下个月正式为克拉克教授举行新校长就职典礼。

items.def_zh: 授予圣职，任命为神职人员；注定，规定
items.def_en: 1. To officially appoint or consecrate someone as a priest or religious minister. 2. (formal) (of God, fate, or authority) To decide or decree something beforehand.
items.ex_en: The bishop will formally ordain several young ministers at the cathedral tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 主教明天将在大教堂正式为几位年轻牧师授予圣职。

items.def_zh: 为……举行就职典礼，使正式就任；开创，使正式开始；为……举行落成（或开幕）典礼
items.def_en: 1. To introduce someone into an official position with a formal ceremony. 2. To officially begin or initiate something new or important.
items.ex_en: Officials will inaugurate the new governor during a grand ceremony at noon.
items.ex_zh: 官员们将于正午在盛大的典礼上为新州长举行就职仪式。

items.def_zh: 授予圣职，任命；整顿，安排
items.def_en: (rare or archaic) To ordain someone to a religious office; to order or arrange.
items.ex_en: The council gathered to ordinate several worthy scholars to the holy order.
items.ex_zh: 参事会齐聚一堂，为几位德高望重的学者授予圣职。

items.def_en: (+ into) to formally introduce someone into a new position, office, or exclusive organization
items.ex_en: The society will induct three prominent scientists into its distinguished ranks tonight.
items.ex_zh: 该学会今晚将正式接纳三位杰出的科学家为其显赫成员。

groups.summary_en: An authority or institutional body formally confers an official office, sacred status, or public mandate onto a person through an established ceremony.
groups.summary_zh: 权威机构通过既定仪式正式授予当事人公职、圣职或法定权力。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formally seating, inaugurating, or placing an official, ruler, or cleric into an enduring seat of institutional authority, contrasting with informal placement through ceremonial protocol.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过既定礼仪流程将官员、统治者或神职人员正式安置于体制性的权位之上，与普通放置（place）相比强调制度权威的确立。
groups.nuance_en: install: formally seat someone in an office or bishopric (rector / president / officer) · inaugurate: mark the formal commencement of a high official tenure or era (president / governor / era) · induct: formally admit a member into an exclusive organization or hall (honoree / hall of fame) · swear in: initiate office through solemn constitutional oath (magistrate / minister) · invest: ceremonially endow with robe and symbols of high rank (dignitary / knight)
groups.nuance_zh: install: 举行就职式正式迎入职位或主教席位 (rector / president / officer) · inaugurate: 举行典礼开启国家元首任期或划时代纪元 (president / governor / era) · induct: 正式接纳进入精英组织、名人堂 (honoree / hall of fame) · swear in: 通过庄严宪法宣誓使之就任 (magistrate / minister) · invest: 授予官服印信确立高阶权位 (dignitary / knight)

groups.name: Intend & Resolve · 意图与决意 (Intend, Resolve, Mean)
groups.tip: 确立行动意图与内在意志

items.def_zh: 立志，决意；用意志力驱动；遗赠（财产）
items.def_en: 1. To intend, desire, or determine something by a deliberate exercise of willpower. 2. To try to make something happen simply by thinking about it. 3. To leave something to someone in a will.
items.ex_en: She could not simply will the agonizing headache to vanish from her mind.
items.ex_zh: 她无法仅仅用意志力就让那折磨人的头痛从脑海中消失。

items.def_zh: 想要，愿意（will 的过去式，表意愿或决心）；将，会（表假设或推测）；过去常常（表习惯）
items.def_en: 1. Used as the past form of 'will' to express intention, willingness, or determination. 2. Used to express conditional outcomes, polite requests, or past habits.
items.ex_en: Despite repeated warnings from his doctors, he would not abandon his reckless lifestyle.
items.ex_zh: 尽管医生一再警告，他仍不愿放弃放纵不羁的生活方式。

items.def_en: (formal) to have as an intentional aim or firmly planned resolution
items.ex_en: The dedicated committee purposed to complete the comprehensive reform before next spring.
items.ex_zh: 尽责的委员会决意在明年春天之前完成这项全面改革。

items.def_zh: 打算，企图；意味着（mean 的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of mean: intended, had in mind, or signified.
items.ex_en: She meant to finish the financial report before leaving the office yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 她昨天本打算在离开办公室之前完成那份财务报告。

items.def_en: [I/T] to have in mind as a purpose, plan, or objective to be achieved
items.ex_en: We intend to expand our international operations significantly over the next two years.
items.ex_zh: 我们打算在未来两年内大幅拓展我们的跨国业务。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a firm and formal decision to do something
items.ex_en: The board resolved to pursue legal action against the rogue former director.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决意对那位胡作非为的前董事采取法律行动。

items.def_en: (+ to do sth) to begin an undertaking with a clear intention or determined purpose
items.ex_en: The young scientist set out to prove her hypothesis through rigorous experimentation.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻的科学家着手通过严谨的实验来证实她的假设。

items.def_en: (+ doing sth) to plan or resolve firmly to achieve a particular result
items.ex_en: The new government policy is aimed at reducing youth unemployment.
items.ex_zh: 政府出台的新政策旨在降低青年失业率。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame center on a conscious mental purpose, purposefulness, or fixed determination to bring about a particular future outcome. They range from basic aim ('mean') to volitional force ('will') and formal, deliberate intent ('purpose', 'resolve').
groups.summary_zh: 指主体在内心形成特定目标、意图或达成某事的坚定决意。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formulating an active, goal-directed mental determination toward a future course of action, contrasting with passive wishing by committing internal agency and will.
groups.desc_zh: 指在心智中形成导向未来行动的明确目标或决意，与单纯空想（wish）的区别在于投入了主体意志与内在决断。
groups.nuance_en: intend: have in mind as a purposeful objective or plan (to go / harm / change) · resolve: reach a firm, unshakeable decision to persist (issue / conflict / dispute) · purpose: deliberately fix the will upon a serious, considered aim (action / deed) · set out: embark with a clear, conscious destination or goal in mind (career / journey / objectives) · aim at: orient calculated strategies specifically toward a target (target / audience / milestone)
groups.nuance_zh: intend: 心中存有明确打算或企图 (to go / harm / change) · resolve: 下定不可动摇的坚决意志 (issue / conflict / dispute) · purpose: 庄重立志并将意志定位于明确目标 (action / deed) · set out: 带着既定意图动身或着手创业 (career / journey / objectives) · aim at: 针对预定靶标采取针对性举措 (target / audience / milestone)

groups.name: Interlink & Coalesce · 联结互通与汇聚结块 (Interconnect, Conglomerate)
groups.tip: 彼此相通，交织成更大网络

items.def_en: (+ with sb/sth) connect, join, or combine together to form an integrated system or alliance
items.ex_en: The two railway networks are scheduled to link up by the end of next year.
items.ex_zh: 这两条铁路网计划于明年年底实现连通。
items.ex2_en: Engineers linked up the two separate optical fibers across the mountain gorge.
items.ex2_zh: 工程师们将穿过山峡的两条独立光纤连接了起来。

items.def_en: (+ with sth) join, coordinate, or be closely interconnected with another system or entity
items.ex_en: Our marketing campaign will tie in directly with the nationwide product release.
items.ex_zh: 我们的营销活动将与全国范围的产品发布直接紧密结合。

items.def_en: to join or become joined together by weaving or blending
items.ex_en: Ancient legends and recorded facts interlace throughout this comprehensive historical account.
items.ex_zh: 古老的传说与记载的史实在整部详尽的记述中交织融合。
items.ex2_en: The skilled weaver decided to interlace colorful silk ribbons into the tapestry.
items.ex2_zh: 技艺娴熟的织工决定将彩色丝带交织编入挂毯中。

items.def_en: join together with others to form a single united group or coalition
items.ex_en: Local shopkeepers decided to band together to resist the corporate developer's plans.
items.ex_zh: 当地店主决定联合起来，共同抵制这家企业开发商的计划。

items.def_en: (formal) To gather, cluster, or combine distinct parts or organizations into a single coherent mass or entity.
items.ex_en: Smaller regional firms often conglomerate to withstand fierce competition from market giants.
items.ex_zh: 较小的地区性公司往往聚合成综合性大实体，以抵御市场巨头的激烈竞争。
items.ex2_en: The visionary investor helped conglomerate three struggling tech startups into one enterprise.
items.ex2_zh: 这位有远见的投资者帮助将三家苦苦挣扎的科技初创公司合并为一家企业。

items.def_en: To connect with one another, or to connect two or more things, so that they form an integrated system.
items.ex_en: Highways and rail networks interconnect across the sprawling industrial region efficiently.
items.ex_zh: 公路与铁路网络在这片广阔的工业区内高效地相互连接。
items.ex2_en: Engineers plan to interconnect all peripheral regional power stations next year.
items.ex2_zh: 工程师计划在明年将所有周边区域发电站相互连接起来。

items.def_en: to come together to form one larger group, substance, or mass
items.ex_en: Disparate activist factions began to coalesce into a powerful and unified movement.
items.ex_zh: 不同的抗议派系开始汇合成一股强大而统一的运动力量。

items.def_en: to collect or form into a mass or group
items.ex_en: Cosmic dust particles slowly agglomerate under gravitational pull to form celestial bodies.
items.ex_zh: 宇宙尘埃颗粒在引力作用下缓慢聚集，形成天体。
items.ex2_en: Intense mechanical pressure helped agglomerate loose metallic powders into solid blocks.
items.ex2_zh: 强大的机械压力促使松散的金属粉末聚集烧结成坚硬的实心块。

groups.summary_en: Distinct elements, organizations, or networks link mutually or gather into a cohesive mass or cluster. Manner ranges from systematic mutual linkage to dense physical or corporate agglomeration.
groups.summary_zh: 多元实体相互贯通网络化，或凝聚聚拢成块的演化方式。
groups.desc_en: Denotes separate entities, organizations, or structures joining, weaving, or massing together to create an integrated or conglomerate whole, contrasting with solitary addition through systemic interpenetration.
groups.desc_zh: 指多个分离的个体、结构或实体通过互联、编织或聚结形成一个一体化或块状的整体，与单向添加（add）相比强调彼此间的网络化与聚合。
groups.nuance_en: interconnect: establish two-way pathways or structural links between systems (networks / devices) · coalesce: merge disparate factions or particles into a single fluid entity (factions / ideas / droplets) · conglomerate: mass together diverse parts into a collective lump or corporate empire (firms / assets) · agglomerate: collect loosely clustered items into a dense mass (particles / industries) · interlace: weave strands across each other in reciprocal patterns (threads / fingers)
groups.nuance_zh: interconnect: 在各系统间建立双向互通链接 (networks / devices) · coalesce: 使各自分散的派系或液滴融合为一个有机整体 (factions / ideas / droplets) · conglomerate: 将不同产业或实体拼拢聚合成集团巨头 (firms / assets) · agglomerate: 使松散的团块杂乱堆积聚集 (particles / industries) · interlace: 使各线条股线相互交叠编织 (threads / fingers)

groups.name: Intertwine & Convolute · 盘绕与交织 (Intertwine, Convolute, Involve)
groups.tip: 互相盘绕缠结呈复杂曲折

items.def_en: (+ sth) encircle or coil repeatedly around a central core or object
items.ex_en: Thick ivy tendrils wind around the stone pillars of the ancient chapel.
items.ex_zh: 茂密的常春藤卷须缠绕在古老小教堂的石柱上。
items.ex2_en: She chose to wind delicate satin ribbons around the gift box.
items.ex2_zh: 她选择将精致的缎带缠绕在礼品盒上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) twist, coil, or encircle tightly around something else
items.ex_en: She wrapped a warm woolen scarf around her neck against the chill.
items.ex_zh: 她用一条温暖的羊毛围巾裹住脖子以抵御严寒。
items.ex2_en: A thick layer of morning mist wrapped around the mountain peak.
items.ex2_zh: 一层厚厚的晨雾笼罩缠绕在山峰周围。

items.def_en: [I/T] To wind or turn things around each other into a spiral or complex shape
items.ex_en: He watched the mechanic twist several copper wires into a single cable.
items.ex_zh: 他看着机械师把几根铜线扭转缠绕成一根电缆。

items.def_en: [I/T] To wind into rings, loops, or a spiral shape
items.ex_en: The sailor began to coil the heavy mooring rope on the deck.
items.ex_zh: 水手开始把甲板上沉重的系泊缆绳盘绕成圈。
items.ex2_en: The venomous garden snake began to coil tightly around the branch.
items.ex2_zh: 那条有毒的花园蛇开始紧紧盘绕在树枝上。

items.def_en: [I/T] To wind or spiral around something, or twist two things together
items.ex_en: Sweet honeysuckle blossoms twine gently through the weathered wooden fence.
items.ex_zh: 芬芳的忍冬花枝温婉地盘绕穿过风化斑驳的木栅栏。
items.ex2_en: The patient florist will twine thin floral wire around the delicate bouquet.
items.ex2_zh: 耐心的花艺师会把细花艺铁丝缠绕在精致的花束上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) coil or interweave two or more flexible strands around each other
items.ex_en: The artisan will twist together several colorful threads to make a sturdy cord.
items.ex_zh: 工匠将几根彩色丝线扭结在一起，制成一条结实的绳索。

items.def_en: (+ with) To twist or wind two or more things closely together, or to be closely connected.
items.ex_en: Their distinct cultural traditions intertwine beautifully in this historic border city.
items.ex_zh: 他们各自独特的文化传统在这座历史悠久的边境城市完美交织。
items.ex2_en: The artisan began to intertwine silver and gold wires into a ring.
items.ex2_zh: 工匠开始将金丝和银丝缠绕在一起编成一枚戒指。

items.def_zh: （使）卷绕，（使）盘旋缠绕；使复杂化
items.def_en: To twist, coil, or fold intricately together; to make something complex or difficult to follow.
items.ex_en: The legal team managed to convolute a simple dispute into years of litigation.
items.ex_zh: 该法律团队硬是把一场简单的纠纷盘绕复杂化为长达数年的诉讼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame emphasize twisting elements together into an intricate, twisted, or convoluted physical or abstract configuration. 'Convolute' stresses extreme twisting or complicating until clarity is lost, while 'intertwine' focuses on mutual, reciprocally coiled physical or conceptual relationships.
groups.summary_zh: 相互盘绕扭结，形成极其复杂、盘错或晦涩的形态。
groups.desc_en: Denotes twisting, looping, or winding strands, bodies, or concepts around one another into complex, spiraling, or knotty entanglements, contrasting with linear straightness through continuous tortuous wrapping.
groups.desc_zh: 指线股、躯体或概念相互盘绕、缠裹及螺旋交织，与直线展开（straighten）的区别在于其复杂的缠绕与错综曲折。
