items.def_en: (+ sth on sth) to sprinkle a powdery or granular substance over a surface by shaking a container
items.ex_en: You can shake on some crushed red pepper to give the pasta extra heat.
items.ex_zh: 你可以晃动调料瓶在意大利面上撒些碎辣椒，让它更辛辣入味。

items.def_en: (+ with) to cover a surface lightly with a fine powder or sugar
items.ex_en: Before serving, lightly dust the chocolate truffles with fine cocoa powder for presentation.
items.ex_zh: 上桌前，在巧克力松露上轻撒一层细腻的可可粉以供点缀。

items.def_en: 1. (dated) To scatter or cover a floor or ground with straw or similar material.
items.ex_en: The stable hands straw the cold stone floor to keep the horses warm tonight.
items.ex_zh: 马夫们在冰冷的石地上铺撒稻草，好让马匹今夜保持暖和。

items.def_en: 1. (+ on/over/with) To scatter small drops of liquid or tiny pieces of powder or sugar lightly over a surface.
items.ex_en: Sprinkle coarse sea salt over the warm focaccia just before taking it outside.
items.ex_zh: 端出去之前，在热气腾腾的佛卡夏面包上撒上粗海盐。

items.def_en: to throw or drop things in different directions so they cover an area irregularly
items.ex_en: Wind gusts scatter dry autumn leaves across the empty driveway every single afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 每天下午，阵阵秋风都会将干燥的落叶散落到空旷的车道各处。
items.ex2_en: The frightened flock of wild birds scattered quickly in every single direction.
items.ex2_zh: 受惊的野鸟群迅速朝着各个方向四散飞去。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) to scatter things haphazardly over an area so as to cover it
items.ex_en: Fallen cherry blossoms strew the quiet stone pathway with delicate, pale pink petals.
items.ex_zh: 飘落的樱花在幽静的石径上撒满了娇嫩的淡粉色花瓣。

groups.summary_en: An agent manually scatters, drops, or spreads loose substances, grains, or liquid drops loosely across a surface. Verbs vary by the fineness of the matter distributed and whether the action is light, deliberate, or decorative.
groups.summary_zh: 将松散细小碎屑、粉末或水滴分散撒在表面上。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on releasing loose, dry, or granular materials irregularly across an expansive area or surface, contrasting with grouped piling or uniform painting.
groups.desc_zh: 指将松散、干燥或颗粒状物资零散播撒在广阔平面上，不同于集中堆叠或均匀涂抹。
groups.nuance_en: scatter: randomly fling or disperse entities in multiple directions (seeds / ashes / papers) · sprinkle: cast small sparse droplets or granules gently over a target (sugar / lawn / rain) · strew: spread a layer of loose items untidily over a floor or ground (flowers / debris / litter) · dust: cover with a fine, powdery, powdery layer (flour / cocoa / surface) · drizzle: pour fine droplets or a thin liquid stream unevenly (olive oil / honey / rain)
groups.nuance_zh: scatter: 随意朝各个方向抛散、播散散落 (seeds / ashes / papers) · sprinkle: 稀疏、轻柔地点撒微小颗粒或水滴 (sugar / lawn / rain) · strew: 凌乱地铺散、撒落在地面或平面上 (flowers / debris / litter) · dust: 轻撒一层极细的干粉 (flour / cocoa / surface) · drizzle: 淋下细密液滴或丝状细流 (olive oil / honey / rain)

groups.name: Scatter & Sprinkle · 撒落与喷洒 (Sprinkle, Scatter, Spritz)
groups.tip: 向表面扑撒粉末或细碎物

items.def_en: (+ sth on sth) to apply a liquid mist or fine spray onto a receiving surface
items.ex_en: Remember to spray on the cleaning solution evenly across the kitchen glass table.
items.ex_zh: 记得将清洁液均匀地喷洒在厨房的玻璃桌面上。

items.def_en: (+ sth on sth) to drop tiny drops of liquid or light particles gently over a surface
items.ex_en: The baker likes to sprinkle on powdered cinnamon before putting buns into ovens.
items.ex_zh: 面包师喜欢在把小圆面包放进烤箱之前撒上肉桂粉。

items.def_en: to cover lightly with a powdered substance such as flour or sugar
items.ex_en: Dust the rolled pastry dough lightly with flour so it does not stick.
items.ex_zh: 在擀好的油酥面团上轻轻撒上一层薄面粉，以免粘连。

items.def_en: [I/T] to drop small drops or particles scatteringly over a surface
items.ex_en: She paused to sprinkle water over the delicate potted ferns on the balcony.
items.ex_zh: 她停下脚步，在阳台娇嫩的盆栽蕨类植物上洒了些水。

items.def_en: To powder or treat something, especially the skin, with talcum powder.
items.ex_en: After drying off completely, talc your feet to keep them cool and dry.
items.ex_zh: 彻底擦干后，在双脚上扑些滑石粉，以保持凉爽干燥。

items.def_en: To spray a quick, fine mist of liquid onto someone or something.
items.ex_en: Spritz some cold mineral water onto your tired face to instantly feel refreshed.
items.ex_zh: 往疲倦的脸上喷点冷矿泉水，瞬间就能感觉神清气爽。

items.def_en: [I/T] to throw or drop things in different directions so they fall over a wide area
items.ex_en: Children run across the lawn to scatter bread crumbs for the hungry pigeons.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们跑过草坪，撒下面包屑喂食饥饿的鸽子。
items.ex2_en: The crowd scattered quickly across the public park when the heavy thunderstorm began.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨开始时，公园里的人群迅速四散开来。

items.def_en: to scatter things untidily over a surface or place
items.ex_en: Wild roses strew the crumbling castle courtyard with fragrant, velvety crimson petals.
items.ex_zh: 野玫瑰在残破的城堡庭院中散落下一片片芬芳而天鹅绒般的深红花瓣。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe distributing fine powders, droplets, or particulate substances lightly over a receiving surface. 'Spritz' designates applying a fine liquid mist via a nozzle, while 'talc' specifically means dusting with talcum powder.
groups.summary_zh: 指将微细颗粒、粉末或细雾分散挥洒在目标受体表面。
groups.desc_en: Centers on dispersing fine liquid mists or light particulate powders over an object for conditioning, seasoning, or hygiene, contrasting with heavy pouring.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重于向目标物体表面喷洒细密水雾或撒落轻质粉末以起调理、调味或清洁作用，区别于大倾角倒出。
groups.nuance_en: spritz: spray a brief, fine burst of liquid via a nozzle (perfume / face / water) · spray on: apply a pressurized liquid layer onto a surface (sunscreen / paint / repellent) · sprinkle on: lightly drop granular condiments or drops on food or objects (cheese / herbs / salt) · dust: tap a powdery film over baking or cosmetics (powder / sugar / fingerprints) · talc: apply cosmetic dry talcum powder to absorb moisture (body / skin / gloves)
groups.nuance_zh: spritz: 用喷嘴短促喷出一阵轻巧的水雾或气雾 (perfume / face / water) · spray on: 喷涂、施加一层雾化液体 (sunscreen / paint / repellent) · sprinkle on: 往某物表面点缀轻撒颗粒调味料或水珠 (cheese / herbs / salt) · dust: 轻扑或拍上一层粉状物 (powder / sugar / fingerprints) · talc: 涂抹滑石粉以保持干爽 (body / skin / gloves)

groups.name: Scurry & Scuttle · 窜逃与小跑 (Scurry, Scuttle, Scamper)
groups.tip: 小步慌乱快速逃窜

items.def_zh: 急促小跑离开；仓皇溜走
items.def_en: depart hastily with brisk, short, hurried steps
items.ex_en: The frightened mice scurry off beneath the floorboards whenever the kitchen light flickers.
items.ex_zh: 每当厨房灯光闪烁，受惊的小老鼠就会仓皇溜入地板下面。

items.def_en: to run with quick, light steps, especially in a playful or hurried way
items.ex_en: Playful puppies scamper across the wet grass, chasing after an old rubber ball.
items.ex_zh: 顽皮的小狗在湿漉漉的草地上欢快地小跑，追逐着一只旧橡胶球。

items.def_en: move away suddenly and very rapidly in a sudden dash
items.ex_en: The startled deer dart off into the dense pine forest within a second.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的鹿在转瞬间便疾奔窜入了茂密的松林之中。

items.def_en: flee quickly with rapid, agitated steps like a frightened small animal
items.ex_en: Tiny crabs scuttle away toward deep burrows as footsteps approach the sandy shore.
items.ex_zh: 脚步声临近沙滩时，小螃蟹们便仓皇逃窜回深处的洞穴。

items.def_zh: 碎步疾跑，仓促逃窜；凿沉（船只）；破坏，破坏（计划）
items.def_en: 1. To run with quick, hurried steps, like a crab or mouse. 2. To deliberately sink a ship by opening valves or making holes in its hull. 3. To deliberately spoil or ruin a plan or proposal.
items.ex_en: Startled by the loud noise, several spiders scuttle rapidly across the stone floor.
items.ex_zh: 被巨响惊扰后，几只蜘蛛仓促地在石板地面上碎步疾跑。

items.def_zh: 碎步急跑，疾走；仓促奔跑
items.def_en: (+ away/along/around) To move quickly with short, rapid steps, especially in haste or fear.
items.ex_en: Panicked shoppers scurry around the department store trying to grab the final discounts.
items.ex_zh: 恐慌的顾客在百货商店里仓促奔跑，争相抢购最后的折扣商品。

items.def_en: to move lightly and quickly or hurriedly along a surface
items.ex_en: Dry autumn leaves skitter across the pavement whenever sudden icy wind blows hard.
items.ex_zh: 每当冷冽的强风刮起，干燥的秋叶便轻快地掠过人行道。

items.def_en: to move suddenly and rapidly in a particular direction
items.ex_en: Golden fish dart through the tangled aquatic weeds whenever shadows cross the pond.
items.ex_zh: 每当池塘泛起阴影，金鱼便猛地穿梭窜过交错的水草。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict moving briskly with short, hurried, agitated steps, typical of rodents, insects, or startled individuals darting away in fear or urgency.
groups.summary_zh: 指带着惶恐或急迫心情，以碎步敏捷仓促逃窜或快跑的动作。
groups.desc_en: Captures rapid, agile, short-paced evasion or darting movements typical of small rodents, insects, or agitated creatures, unlike heavy running or formal marching.
groups.desc_zh: 特指如小动物或昆虫般短促、迅捷、轻巧地慌乱小跑或窜逃，不同于沉重的奔跑或规整的行进。
groups.nuance_en: scurry: hurry along with hurried, agitated, brisk footsteps (mice / clerks / feet) · scuttle: move with short, rapid steps close to the ground in panic (crab / beetle / away) · scamper: run playfully and lightly like a small child or animal (squirrel / puppy / kids) · skitter: skim or glide lightly and rapidly over a surface (leaves / bugs / across) · dart: move suddenly and rapidly in a sharp, evasive trajectory (shadow / eyes / room)
groups.nuance_zh: scurry: 慌张焦虑、迈着急促碎步跑动 (mice / clerks / feet) · scuttle: 贴地仓皇逃窜、横冲直撞 (crab / beetle / away) · scamper: 欢快蹦跳、顽皮敏捷地小跑 (squirrel / puppy / kids) · skitter: 在表面轻巧滑行、飞快擦过 (leaves / bugs / across) · dart: 犹如离弦之箭般突兀闪躲或猛冲 (shadow / eyes / room)

groups.name: Seize & Hold Hostage · 绑架与劫持 (Kidnap, Abduct)
groups.tip: 暴力劫持人质勒索或带走

items.def_en: 1. To take someone away illegally by force, usually in order to demand money for their release.
items.ex_en: Armed militants conspired to kidnap the foreign diplomat for an exorbitant ransom demand.
items.ex_zh: 武装分子密谋绑架该国驻外外交官以索要巨额赎金。

items.def_en: (+ sb) abduct or carry someone away illicitly by force or stealth
items.ex_en: Thieves broke into the gallery and made off with three priceless paintings.
items.ex_zh: 盗贼闯入画廊，盗走了三幅无价的名画。

items.def_en: (+ sb) abduct or seize someone and take them away abruptly and swiftly
items.ex_en: Masked assailants burst inside the compound to whisk away the oil tycoon's daughter.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面袭击者冲进大院，迅速将石油大亨的女儿强行劫走。

items.def_en: (+ sb) carry or transport someone away forcibly against their will
items.ex_en: Rebel forces arrived in black trucks to cart off the town mayor forcibly.
items.ex_zh: 叛军乘黑色卡车赶来，强行押走了镇长。

items.def_en: (informal) to suddenly and forcibly take someone away or kidnap them
items.ex_en: Gunmen tried to snatch the visiting foreign executive right outside his luxury hotel.
items.ex_zh: 持枪歹徒企图就在豪华酒店门外强行掳走来访的外国高管。

items.def_en: 1. To take someone away illegally by force or deception; to kidnap.
items.ex_en: The court proved that the defendant plotted to abduct the heiress for money.
items.ex_zh: 法院证实该被告密谋绑架这位女继承人以索取钱财。

items.def_zh: 劫持（交通工具及其人员）
items.def_en: to seize control of a vehicle, aircraft, or its occupants by force in transit
items.ex_en: Armed skyjackers attempted to hijack the commercial airliner shortly after midnight flight departure.
items.ex_zh: 武装劫机分子在午夜航班起飞不久后企图劫持该客机。

items.def_en: to take arbitrary or military control of a vehicle or building by coercion
items.ex_en: Military officials intervened to commandeer the civilian vessel for urgent coastal evacuation operations.
items.ex_zh: 军方官员出面干预，强行征用该民用船只用于紧急沿海撤离行动。

groups.summary_en: These transitive verbs describe taking a person away unlawfully and by force or deception. 'Kidnap' strongly collocates with ransom demands and illicit detention, while 'abduct' is the formal and legal term for unlawfully carrying someone off.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过暴力或欺骗手段非法掳走并扣押人员。
groups.desc_en: Involves unlawfully and forcibly seizing persons or transport conveyances against their will, distinguished from legal arrest or simple property theft.
groups.desc_zh: 指违背当事人意愿，通过暴力或胁迫手段强行掠夺、扣留人身或劫持交通载具，区别于合法逮捕或普通盗窃。
groups.nuance_en: kidnap: unlawfully capture and detain a person, typically demanding ransom (heir / diplomat / hostage) · abduct: seize someone covertly or forcefully by trickery or force (child / victim / alien) · hijack: seize control of a vehicle in transit by threat or violence (plane / bus / broadcast) · commandeer: confiscate a vehicle or building, often claiming emergency authority (car / boat / building) · snatch: aggressively grab and spirit away someone in an instant (baby / purse / off the street)
groups.nuance_zh: kidnap: 绑架扣为人质以索要赎金 (heir / diplomat / hostage) · abduct: 诱拐、强行带走或劫持人身 (child / victim / alien) · hijack: 中途以暴力或胁迫手段劫持运行中的载具 (plane / bus / broadcast) · commandeer: 强征或强行占用车辆/设施 (car / boat / building) · snatch: 猝不及防地当街抢夺或强拉拐走 (baby / purse / off the street)

groups.name: Share Sorrow & Commiserate · 同情与体恤 (Empathize, Condole, Commiserate)
groups.tip: 感同身受分担他人苦痛

items.def_en: To feel genuine compassion or sympathy for someone enduring distress
items.ex_en: I truly feel for those refugees who lost their homes during severe winter.
items.ex_zh: 我真心心疼那些在严冬中失去家园的难民。

items.def_zh: 向……表示同情慰问；主动关怀
items.def_en: (+ sb) offer sympathy, support, or condolences to someone experiencing grief
items.ex_en: Neighbors decided to reach out to the grieving widow with warm home-cooked meals.
items.ex_zh: 邻居们决定向悲痛的遗孀表达慰问关怀，并送去热乎的家常菜。

items.def_en: (+ with) To feel and express sadness, pity, or compassionate understanding for someone
items.ex_en: Many colleagues gathered to sympathize with Mark following his sudden and tragic loss.
items.ex_zh: 在马克遭受突如其来的悲惨变故后，许多同事聚在一起安慰同情他。

items.def_zh: 有同感，产生共鸣，感同身受
items.def_en: (+ with) To understand and share the feelings, thoughts, or attitudes of another person.
items.ex_en: Therapists must genuinely empathize with their patients to build strong bonds of trust.
items.ex_zh: 治疗师必须真正与患者产生共鸣，才能建立牢固的信任关系。

items.def_en: (+ with) To express sympathy, sorrow, or shared grievances for someone's misfortune
items.ex_en: The managers met privately to commiserate with the team over the contract cancellation.
items.ex_zh: 经理们私下碰头，就合同被取消一事与团队共同表达遗憾与同情。

items.def_en: (+ with) To express sympathy, sorrow, or condolences to someone experiencing grief or misfortune.
items.ex_en: Dozens of dignitaries arrived at the estate to condole with the bereaved family.
items.ex_zh: 数十位显贵抵达庄园，向痛失亲人的家属表示深切吊唁与慰问。

items.def_en: (+ sb) feel immense sorrow, sympathy, and emotional pain for another's distress
items.ex_en: My soul aches for the young orphans wandering alone through the war ruins.
items.ex_zh: 看到年幼的孤儿在战争废墟中孑然徘徊，我的内心无比痛惜怜悯。

items.def_en: (+ sb) feel profound and intense grief or sympathy on behalf of someone suffering
items.ex_en: Her tender heart seemed to bleed for every starving child across the land.
items.ex_zh: 这片土地上每一个挨饿的孩子，都让她温柔的心为之淌血绞痛。

groups.summary_en: An agent expresses heartfelt sorrow, shared distress, or emotional alignment with another person who is suffering. Nuances range from intellectual emotional resonance ('empathize') to formal verbal condolences ('condole') and mutual lamenting ('commiserate').
groups.summary_zh: 针对他人遭遇的痛苦、不幸表达感同身受的悲伤、体恤或慰问。
groups.desc_en: Represents recognizing, entering into, or formally expressing shared grief and compassionate sorrow for another’s suffering, contrasting with indifferent analysis.
groups.desc_zh: 指感同身受地体察、介入并向承受苦难者正式表达哀思与同情，区别于冷眼旁观或理性剖析。
groups.nuance_en: sympathize: feel pity, sorrow, or intellectual agreement for someone's plight (victim / position / family) · empathize: mentally identify and share another's exact feelings from their viewpoint (struggle / pain / patient) · commiserate: verbally exchange mutual sympathy or lament setbacks together (loser / colleague / fate) · condole: formally express condolences upon a death or bereavement (widow / loss / family) · bleed for: suffer profound, visceral heartache on another's behalf (innocent / victim / heart)
groups.nuance_zh: sympathize: 对受难者的不幸表达关切、怜悯或赞同 (victim / position / family) · empathize: 真正换位思考、共情对方的内心体验 (struggle / pain / patient) · commiserate: 共同分担痛楚、互诉悲苦或抱怨失败 (loser / colleague / fate) · condole: 在丧事中正式致哀慰问 (widow / loss / family) · bleed for: 极为刻骨铭心、撕心裂肺地心疼 (innocent / victim / heart)

groups.name: Shave & Depilate · 剃刮与除毛修容 (Shave, Scrape, Shear)
groups.tip: 修剪毛发剃胡打理仪容

items.def_en: to cut small amounts off hair or beard to keep it neat without removing completely
items.ex_en: He visits the local barber every two weeks to trim his unruly beard.
items.ex_zh: 他每两周去一次当地理发店，修剪一下杂乱的胡须。

items.def_en: (+ sth) remove hair completely from the skin using a razor
items.ex_en: He decided to shave off his thick beard completely for the job interview.
items.ex_zh: 为了参加求职面试，他决定把浓密的胡须彻底刮除。

items.def_zh: 剃（须），刮（毛）；刨平，刮掉薄层；略微削减
items.def_en: 1. To cut hair from the face or body very close to the skin using a razor. 2. To cut or scrape thin slices from a surface. 3. To reduce something slightly.
items.ex_en: James stands before the bathroom mirror to shave carefully with fresh warm foam.
items.ex_zh: 詹姆斯站在浴室镜子前，用温热的新鲜泡沫仔细剃须。

items.def_en: (+ sth) remove stubble, hair, or a top surface layer using a firm scraping blade
items.ex_en: Use a warm razor to scrape off stubborn stubble from your jaw line.
items.ex_zh: 用温热的剃刀将下颌线上顽固的胡茬刮除干净。

items.def_en: (+ sth) cut hair, wool, or fleece completely away close to the skin
items.ex_en: The veterinarian had to shear off the dog's matted fur before treating wounds.
items.ex_zh: 兽医在处理伤口前不得不将狗狗纠结成团的毛发全部剪除。

items.def_en: to remove hair, skin, or surface layers by drawing a hard edge firmly across
items.ex_en: The esthetician used a sterile surgical blade to gently scrape peach fuzz away.
items.ex_zh: 美容师使用无菌手术刀片轻轻刮除面部的细小绒毛。

items.def_en: (archaic) Past participle of shave; to remove hair closely with a razor.
items.ex_en: With shaven crown, the ascetic monk entered the mountain temple in solemn silence.
items.ex_zh: 苦修僧剃净头顶，在庄严肃穆的沉寂中步入山寺。

items.def_en: to cut the wool or hair completely off an animal or person using shears
items.ex_en: Farmers gather every spring to shear thick fleece from hundreds of mature sheep.
items.ex_zh: 每年春天，农夫们都会聚在一起为数百只成年绵羊剪取厚厚的羊毛。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve removing hair, stubble, or thin outer surfaces from the body using a bladed or abrasive instrument. The frame emphasizes closeness to the skin, mechanical cutting, or smooth finishing.
groups.summary_zh: 使用刀片或机械工具紧贴表皮刮剃毛发或平整修容。
groups.desc_en: Describes mechanical shearing, scraping, or close-cutting to remove hair, wool, or thin surface layers, contrasting with deep chopping or blunt tearing.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用刮刃或剪具贴近表皮将毛发、羊毛或薄表层切除刮净，区别于深度的劈砍或撕扯。
groups.nuance_en: shave: slice off hair at skin level using a sharp blade (beard / head / legs) · scrape: mechanically draw a hard edge across to dislodge outer crusts (paint / rust / hide) · shear: clip wool or hair comprehensively using heavy shears (sheep / fleece / hedges) · trim: cut away uneven tips or surplus edges to neaten (hair / beard / edges) · shave off: slice away thin slivers or small numerical amounts (fraction / seconds / wood)
groups.nuance_zh: shave: 用锋利刀片贴皮剃除毛发 (beard / head / legs) · scrape: 用坚硬边缘紧刮以剥除表皮或垢层 (paint / rust / hide) · shear: 用大剪刀大面积剪除羊毛或修整 (sheep / fleece / hedges) · trim: 剪去碎屑、发尾以修饰齐整 (hair / beard / edges) · shave off: 削去微薄表层或微量缩减 (fraction / seconds / wood)

groups.name: Slander, Smear & Defame · 诋毁与诽谤 (Denigrate, Defame, Vilify)
groups.tip: 从言语贬低演进到公然抹黑

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Criticize someone or something unfairly and damage their reputation
items.ex_en: It is totally unfair to run down your former coworkers behind their backs.
items.ex_zh: 在背后恶意诋毁贬低你的前同事是极其不公道的。

items.def_en: to publish a false statement that is damaging to a person's reputation
items.ex_en: The tabloid was sued for millions after attempting to libel the honest judge.
items.ex_zh: 该小报在企图发文诽谤那位正直的法官后被索赔数百万美元。

items.def_en: to make a false and damaging spoken statement about someone
items.ex_en: He threatened legal action if his opponent continued to slander him on air.
items.ex_zh: 他扬言如果对手继续在广播节目中口头诽谤他，就将采取法律手段。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Make damaging, insulting remarks that impugn someone's character or standing
items.ex_en: Desperate political rivals constantly cast slurs on his integrity during the election campaign.
items.ex_zh: 走投无路的政治对手在竞选期间不断对他的正直品格横加中伤诽谤。

items.def_en: to damage someone's reputation by making false accusations or malicious leaks
items.ex_en: Competitors launched an aggressive campaign to smear the rising startup's clean corporate reputation.
items.ex_zh: 竞争对手发起了一场猛烈的舆论攻势，抹黑这家新兴初创公司清白的声誉。

items.def_en: to unfairly criticize someone or something and suggest they have little value or importance; to defame
items.ex_en: Bitter rivals attempted to denigrate the young scientist's revolutionary discoveries in academic journals.
items.ex_zh: 怀恨在心的对手试图在学术期刊上贬低这位年轻科学家的颠覆性发现。

items.def_en: to damage the good reputation of someone by making false or malicious statements
items.ex_en: The false accusations were deliberately designed to defame the renowned surgeon's good name.
items.ex_zh: 这些虚假指控是蓄意设计的，旨在败坏这位著名外科医生的声誉。

items.def_en: to speak or write about someone in an abusively disparaging manner
items.ex_en: Partisan bloggers relentlessly vilify anyone who disagrees with their extreme political dogmas online.
items.ex_zh: 党派博主在网上无情地辱骂和极力中伤任何反对其极端政治教条的人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe making malicious, damaging, or disparaging statements about someone's reputation or character. They scale from belittling and unfair criticism to legally actionable false statements and virulent, public character assassination.
groups.summary_zh: 恶意贬低、破坏名誉乃至蓄意中伤诽谤。
groups.desc_en: Actions of publicly attacking or damaging someone's reputation through false, malicious, or derogatory statements, contrasting with objective criticism or mere insult by focusing on the erosion of social esteem and standing.
groups.desc_zh: 通过虚假、恶意或贬损性言辞公开破坏他人名誉与社会声望的行为，与客观批评或普通侮辱相比，侧重于对名誉地位的毁损。
groups.nuance_en: slander: make false spoken defamatory statements (reputation / rival) · libel: publish permanent defamatory falsehoods (author / publisher / newspaper) · smear: spread damaging innuendo to tarnish character (candidate / opponent / witness) · denigrate: unfairly belittle the value or importance of someone (achievements / character) · defame: legally harm a good name through malicious false claims (company / official) · vilify: aggressively speak ill of someone in abusive public language (whistleblower / minority)
groups.nuance_zh: slander: 口头捏造诽谤 (reputation / rival) · libel: 以书面或永久形式造谣中伤 (author / publisher / newspaper) · smear: 抹黑、用污名诋毁人格 (candidate / opponent / witness) · denigrate: 贬抑、贬低价值或名誉 (achievements / character) · defame: 法律层面损害名誉 (company / official) · vilify: 痛骂、公然极度丑化 (whistleblower / minority)

groups.name: Slow & Outdoor Cooking · 慢炖与户外炙烤 (Stew, Barbecue, Simmer)
groups.tip: 火烤炭炙等烹饪手艺

items.def_en: to cook a large piece of meat slowly with vegetables in a covered pot
items.ex_en: Grandmother loves to pot-roast seasoned beef with root vegetables on cold winter afternoons.
items.ex_zh: 祖母喜欢在寒冷的冬日下午，将调好味的牛肉和根茎蔬菜放在砂锅里慢烤煨炖。

items.def_en: Boil gently until reduced in volume or cooked thoroughly
items.ex_en: Turn down the gas flame and let the rich gravy simmer down slowly.
items.ex_zh: 关小瓦斯火苗，让浓郁的肉汁慢慢文火煨浓收汁。
items.ex2_en: The skilled cook must simmer down the vegetable stock to enrich its flavor.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的厨师必须用文火煮浓蔬菜汤以增加其风味。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Reduce in liquid volume or cause food to reduce through gentle, prolonged cooking
items.ex_en: You need to cook down those crushed ripe tomatoes until sauce thickens nicely.
items.ex_zh: 你需要将压碎的熟番茄慢熬收汁，直到酱汁变得浓稠可口。
items.ex2_en: The sweet berry mixture will cook down into a delicious thick fruit jam.
items.ex2_zh: 甜浆果混合物会慢煮浓缩成美味浓稠的果酱。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Cook meat or vegetables slowly in liquid until very soft and tender
items.ex_en: The chef decided to stew down tough cabbage leaves with fragrant pork broth.
items.ex_zh: 大厨决定用香浓的猪肉高汤将粗韧的卷心菜慢炖至软烂。
items.ex2_en: Tough cuts of beef stew down slowly until tender inside the ceramic pot.
items.ex2_zh: 坚硬的牛肉块在砂锅里慢慢炖至软烂多汁。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cook food on a metal grate directly over hot coals or open flames
items.ex_en: Let's fire up the charcoal pit and grill some juicy marinated steaks outside.
items.ex_zh: 咱们把炭火生起来，到外面的铁架上烤几块多汁的腌牛排吧。

items.def_en: To cook food on a barbecue, over an open fire or heated coals outdoors.
items.ex_en: We usually barbecue spicy chicken wings on the patio during warm summer evenings.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖的夏夜，我们通常会在庭院烤架上炭烤香辣鸡翅。

items.def_zh: 炖，焖，煨（用慢火水煮）；焦虑，生闷气
items.def_en: 1. To cook food slowly in liquid in a closed pot or pan. 2. (+ over/about) (informal) To worry, fret, or brood over something for a long time.
items.ex_en: Do not sit there and stew about that minor setback all night long.
items.ex_zh: 别整晚干坐在那儿为那个小小的挫折生闷气发愁了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cook liquid gently just below the boiling point over an extended duration
items.ex_en: Allow the spicy broth to simmer quietly over very low heat for hours.
items.ex_zh: 让这锅香辣高汤用极微小的火温火慢炖几个小时。
items.ex2_en: She let the delicious onion stew simmer slowly over the small flame.
items.ex2_zh: 她让美味的洋葱炖菜在小火上慢慢煨煮。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent extended cooking scenarios, specifically outdoor grilling over coals/smokers or prolonged slow liquid boiling in a pot.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及长时间低温炖煮或在炭火/烤架上烟熏炙烤的料理场景。
groups.desc_en: Thermal food preparation characterized either by prolonged low-heat moisture reduction or high-heat outdoor radiant grilling, contrasting with rapid indoor boiling or baking by emphasizing specialized slow tenderness or smoky charring.
groups.desc_zh: 以长时间慢火慢煨收汁或户外明火辐射炙烤为特征的烹饪方式，与快速水煮或普通烘烤相比，侧重于食材熟成软烂或烟熏焦香。
groups.nuance_en: simmer: cook gently in liquid just below boiling point (sauce / soup / stew) · stew: cook slowly in closed liquid for prolonged tenderizing (meat / vegetables) · barbecue: roast or smoke slowly over low indirect outdoor heat or coals (ribs / brisket / pork) · grill: cook quickly over direct high radiant heat (steak / burger / vegetables) · pot-roast: braise large tough cuts with vegetables in a covered pot (beef / chuck) · cook down: reduce liquid volume through sustained gentle boiling (stock / sauce)
groups.nuance_zh: simmer: 文火慢煨 (sauce / soup / stew) · stew: 焖炖使其软烂 (meat / vegetables) · barbecue: 户外烟熏慢烤 (ribs / brisket / pork) · grill: 明火高温直烤 (steak / burger / vegetables) · pot-roast: 焖烤整块大肉 (beef / chuck) · cook down: 慢炖收汁濃縮 (stock / sauce)

groups.name: Smell & Exude Odor · 散发恶臭 (Emit Foul Smells with Varying Intensity)
groups.tip: 臭气熏天令人掩鼻退避

items.def_en: (informal, chiefly BrE) to have an unpleasant or stale smell
items.ex_en: Open the kitchen window immediately because those leftover boiled eggs really pong.
items.ex_zh: 快把厨房窗户打开，那些剩下的水煮蛋真的很臭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Smell strongly and unpleasant of a particular substance
items.ex_en: His heavy wool coat reeked of cheap cigars and damp cellar air.
items.ex_zh: 他厚重的羊毛大衣散发着廉价雪茄和潮湿地下室的难闻气味。

items.def_en: (informal) to smell very foul or offensively pungent
items.ex_en: After two weeks without electricity, the apartment refrigerator was starting to hum.
items.ex_zh: 断电两周后，公寓里的冰箱开始臭气熏天了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Fill an enclosed place with an extremely unpleasant, foul smell
items.ex_en: Burning that leftover garlic toast will completely stink out the entire staff breakroom.
items.ex_zh: 把剩下的蒜蓉吐司烤焦会让整个员工休息室都充斥着恶臭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Cause an entire room or area to smell very bad
items.ex_en: Please don't microwave your leftover fish here and stink up the whole office.
items.ex_zh: 请不要在这里用微波炉热剩鱼，把整个办公室搞得臭气熏天。

items.def_zh: 散发恶臭，发臭；极糟，令人讨厌
items.def_en: 1. To have an extremely unpleasant smell. 2. (informal) To be very bad, unfair, or unpleasant.
items.ex_en: The whole unfair grading process stinks and deserves a formal student protest.
items.ex_zh: 这整个不公平的评分流程简直糟糕透顶，理应受到学生的正式抗议。

items.def_zh: 散发强烈刺鼻臭味（常指酒气、汗臭或烟味）
items.def_en: (+ of) to emit an extremely strong, pervasive, and offensive odor
items.ex_en: The drunken sailor reeked of stale whiskey and sweat after the long voyage.
items.ex_zh: 经过长途航行后，那个醉醺醺的水手浑身散发着难闻的宿醉酒气和汗臭。

items.def_zh: 散发恶臭，发臭（stink的过去式）
items.def_en: 1. Past tense of stink; smelled extremely bad.
items.ex_en: The unwashed hockey gear stank so badly that nobody entered the locker room.
items.ex_zh: 没洗的冰球护具发出一股冲天恶臭，以至于没人敢进更衣室。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this olfactory frame indicate emanating foul, pungent, or offensive airborne scents. They scale from faint or standard unpleasant odors to unbearable, suffocating emanations that overpower an entire vicinity.
groups.summary_zh: 按气味浓烈与难闻程度，散发从隐约异味到刺鼻恶臭。
groups.desc_en: Emitting or being saturated with noxious, stale, or intensely unpleasant airborne scents, contrasting with neutral olfactory emission or sweet fragrance by focusing on sensory repulsion and pervasive contamination.
groups.desc_zh: 散发或浸透令人极度厌恶、发臭或刺鼻的气味，与中性气味散发或芳香相比，强调刺鼻难闻与空气弥漫的污染感。
groups.nuance_en: stink: emit a sharp, foul, and offensive odor (garbage / feet / breath) · reek: emit a pervasive, heavy, and often chemical or stale stench (alcohol / tobacco / sweat) · pong: emit an irritating bad smell in informal British usage (cheese / socks) · hum: give off a distinct, rising stench detectable at a distance (drain / bin) · stink out: fill an entire enclosed space with overwhelming foul odor (room / house)
groups.nuance_zh: stink: 发出明显恶臭 (garbage / feet / breath) · reek: 散发浓烈刺鼻陈腐臭味 (alcohol / tobacco / sweat) · pong: 发臭（英式口语） (cheese / socks) · hum: 恶臭熏天、远闻即感 (drain / bin) · stink out: 恶臭熏透整个封闭空间 (room / house)

groups.name: Sniff & Scent · 闻嗅与寻味感知 (Sniff, Snuff, Scent)
groups.tip: 耸起鼻子嗅探隐约气味

items.def_en: to perceive the odor of something using the olfactory sense
items.ex_en: Can you smell the distinct aroma of roasted coffee beans drifting upstairs?
items.ex_zh: 你能闻到飘到楼上的那股浓郁的烤咖啡豆香气吗？

items.def_zh: 到处闻嗅；探头探脑地打探
items.def_en: (+ sth) Explore an area by sniffing scents, or pry inquisitively into affairs
items.ex_en: The hound began to sniff around the damp garden shed for food scraps.
items.ex_zh: 猎犬开始在潮湿的花园棚子周围到处闻嗅，寻找残羹剩饭。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Discover or detect something by smelling it, or figuratively track down through investigation
items.ex_en: Trained police dogs can easily sniff out concealed narcotics hidden inside travel luggage.
items.ex_zh: 受过训练的警犬能轻易嗅出藏在旅行行李中的违禁毒品。

items.def_zh: 嗅出，闻到；发觉，察觉；使充满香味
items.def_en: 1. To smell or detect the presence of something by its odor. 2. To add a pleasant perfume or fragrance to something.
items.ex_en: The alert deer scented the approaching predator long before it came into view.
items.ex_zh: 警惕的鹿早在捕食者进入视线之前就嗅到了它的气息。

items.def_zh: 闻，嗅；抽鼻子；嗤之以鼻，轻蔑地对待
items.def_en: 1. (+ at) To breathe air in noisily through the nose to smell something or clear the nasal passage. 2. ('sniff at') To show disapproval, contempt, or lack of interest.
items.ex_en: He paused to sniff at the carton of milk before pouring his cereal.
items.ex_zh: 他在倒麦片前停下来，闻了闻那盒牛奶。

items.def_en: to sniff noisily at something or inhale deeply to catch a trace scent
items.ex_en: The curious terrier snuffed the crisp winter air to catch the fox scent.
items.ex_zh: 好奇的㹴犬对着清冽的冬日空气用力抽吸鼻子，捕捉狐狸的气味。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Detect or find something by scent or through shrewd enquiry
items.ex_en: The investigative reporter managed to nose out the council's hidden financial scandal.
items.ex_zh: 这位调查记者设法打探出了市议会隐瞒的财务丑闻。

items.def_en: to probe or root around inquisitively while sniffing
items.ex_en: The inquisitive pig snooted around the damp undergrowth looking for buried truffles.
items.ex_zh: 那头好奇的猪用鼻子拱着潮湿的下层灌木丛到处嗅闻，寻找埋藏的松露。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve actively taking air in through the nose to identify an odor or detecting a quarry's airborne smell, ranging from quick audible inhalations to instinctual predatory detection.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过鼻子主动吸气以闻辨气味，或动物凭借气味感知追踪目标。
groups.desc_en: Actively drawing air through the nasal passage to detect, trace, or evaluate chemical odors, contrasting with passive smelling by foregrounding intentional sensory exploration and detective inquiry.
groups.desc_zh: 主动通过鼻腔吸气以探查、追踪或辨别气味，与被动闻到气味相比，强调主观的嗅探探索与寻味甄别。
groups.nuance_en: sniff: draw air audibly through the nose to identify a smell (perfume / food / air) · scent: detect or track subtle airborne odors, typically by an animal (prey / danger / trail) · snuff: inhale deeply or noisily into the nostrils (breeze / powder) · sniff out: discover hidden things through investigation or acute scent (truffles / contraband / scandal) · nose out: detect and track down by persistent searching (clue / story / truth)
groups.nuance_zh: sniff: 抽动鼻子闻嗅 (perfume / food / air) · scent: 凭气味察觉或追踪 (prey / danger / trail) · snuff: 耸鼻深嗅 (breeze / powder) · sniff out: 嗅探找出隐秘事物 (truffles / contraband / scandal) · nose out: 探听发掘出隐匿线索 (clue / story / truth)

groups.name: Snub & Disdain · 冷落与轻慢 (Snub, Slight, Cold-shoulder)
groups.tip: 社交场上的当面冷落与漫不经心

items.def_en: to insult someone by treating them without proper respect or attention
items.ex_en: The hostess felt slighted when the guest of honor ignored her polite greeting.
items.ex_zh: 当主宾无视她礼貌的问候时，女主人感到受到了怠慢。

items.def_zh: 轻慢，怠慢，轻浮对待（trifle with）；虚度（光阴）
items.def_en: (trifle with) to treat someone or something without seriousness or respect; to waste time frivolously
items.ex_en: A wise diplomat does not trifle with sacred national traditions during delicate negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 精明的明智外交官在微妙的谈判期间绝不会轻慢神圣的国家传统。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Deliberately ignore someone or fail to attend a planned meeting with them
items.ex_en: He chose to blow off our scheduled strategy lunch without any advance warning.
items.ex_zh: 他没有任何事先通知，就故意爽约了我们安排好的战略午餐会。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Rudely ignore, dismiss, or refuse to listen to someone
items.ex_en: He tried to brush off the criticism as petty jealousy.
items.ex_zh: 他试图对这些批评不予理会，将其归咎于小人的嫉妒。

items.def_en: to intentionally ignore or be unfriendly toward someone
items.ex_en: After their bitter argument, she chose to cold-shoulder him at the department dinner.
items.ex_zh: 激烈的争吵之后，她在部门晚宴上故意冷落他。

items.def_en: 1. to insult someone deliberately by ignoring them or treating them with cold disrespect. 2. to extinguish a cigarette by pressing the end against something.
items.ex_en: She deliberately snubbed her former business partner by turning away in public.
items.ex_zh: 她在公众场合故意转过身去，冷落了她以前的商业合伙人。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Make someone feel unwelcome and exclude them through hostile coldness or social silence
items.ex_en: Cliquish team members deliberately froze out the new analyst from private social events.
items.ex_zh: 抱团的团队成员故意在私下社交活动中排挤这位新入职的分析师。

items.def_en: to reject an offer, approach, or gesture in an abrupt or ungracious manner
items.ex_en: The company firmly rebuffed the competitor's hostile takeover proposal earlier this morning.
items.ex_zh: 该公司今天清晨断然回绝了竞争对手的敌意收购提议。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe treating an interlocutor with deliberate coldness, disrespect, or dismissal of their social status. 'Snub' focuses on overt social rebuff, whereas 'trifle' focuses on treating someone or their feelings dismissively without proper seriousness.
groups.summary_zh: 指以冷淡、傲慢或敷衍的态度故意轻视、羞辱或排斥他人。
groups.desc_en: Deliberately ignoring, dismissing, or treating someone with calculated coldness and contempt, contrasting with accidental oversight or polite refusal by signaling social devaluation and intentional disrespect.
groups.desc_zh: 故意忽视、轻慢或以刻意冷淡的态度对待他人，与无意疏忽或礼貌拒绝相比，带有明确的社会排斥与蔑视意味。
groups.nuance_en: snub: rebuff or ignore haughtily and deliberately in a social context (invitation / colleague / guest) · slight: treat someone disrespectfully by failing to show proper courtesy (host / ally / friend) · cold-shoulder: deliberately display chilly indifference toward someone (newcomer / former friend) · freeze out: systematically exclude someone from a group or activity (rival / partner / competitor) · rebuff: reject an overture or request bluntly and abruptly (advances / offer / appeal)
groups.nuance_zh: snub: 傲慢怠慢或冷落 (invitation / colleague / guest) · slight: 轻视怠慢礼节 (host / ally / friend) · cold-shoulder: 刻意冷遇态度冷漠 (newcomer / former friend) · freeze out: 联合排挤使孤立 (rival / partner / competitor) · rebuff: 严词回绝或碰钉子 (advances / offer / appeal)

groups.name: Social Intercourse & Professional Interaction · 交往与对话 (Converse, Network, Commune)
groups.tip: 人际互动中沟通并拓展人脉

items.def_zh: 建立工作关系网，拓展人脉；把……连成网络
items.def_en: 1. to interact with others to exchange information and develop professional contacts. 2. to connect computers or systems together.
items.ex_en: Young entrepreneurs attend local conferences mainly to network with seasoned venture capitalists.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的创业者参加本地会议主要为了与经验丰富的风险投资人建立人脉。

items.def_zh: 接洽，沟通协作（业务或跨领域交流）
items.def_en: (+ with) to communicate and coordinate closely with another person or group, especially in business
items.ex_en: Our technical project lead regularly interfaces with regional client representatives on software issues.
items.ex_zh: 我们的技术项目负责人定期就软件问题与区域客户代表进行接洽沟通。

items.def_en: Make an effort to communicate or establish contact with someone, especially for help or business
items.ex_en: The university counselor encouraged stressed students to reach out for professional mental support.
items.ex_zh: 大学辅导员鼓励压力过大的学生主动联络以寻求专业的心理支持。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Spend time interacting socially with people
items.ex_en: The quiet novelist rarely mixed with high society figures during the summer festival.
items.ex_zh: 在夏季节日期间，这位寡言的小说家极少与上流社会人士交际往来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Establish working communication and exchange information between groups or organizations
items.ex_en: Our safety officer will liaise with local emergency personnel during the scheduled drill.
items.ex_zh: 在预定的演习期间，我们的安全官将与当地应急人员进行联络对接。

items.def_en: (+ upon/on) to speak or converse authoritatively or formally on a topic
items.ex_en: The visiting scholar discoursed upon medieval political philosophy before an attentive university audience.
items.ex_zh: 客座学者在聚精会神的高校听众面前就中世纪政治哲学作了正式论述。

items.def_en: (+ with) to engage in conversation with someone.
items.ex_en: Diplomats retired to the quiet library to converse privately about the treaty terms.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们退到安静的图书馆，私下商讨条约条款。

items.def_en: (+ with) to share deep, intimate feelings or thoughts with someone or nature without reserve
items.ex_en: The weary poet walked deep into the ancient forest to commune with nature.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的诗人走向古老森林的深处，与大自然进行心灵的沟通。

groups.summary_en: Encompasses purposeful social and communicative engagement. Verbs vary from standard verbal interaction ('converse') and career-oriented contact building ('network') to deep intellectual or spiritual sharing ('commune', 'interface').
groups.summary_zh: 强调人际对话交流、建立社交往来或专业联络的场景。
groups.desc_en: Engaging in interpersonal contact across formal, organizational, or deeply personal registers to exchange information or establish rapport, contrasting with casual talking by emphasizing purpose, alignment, and relational dynamics.
groups.desc_zh: 在职场、社交或深度心灵层面进行人际交往以传递信息或建立纽带，与随性闲聊相比，侧重沟通的目的性、协作对接与情感交融。
groups.nuance_en: network: interact with others to cultivate professional contacts and opportunities (clients / peers / alumni) · interface: connect and coordinate directly with another person or unit (team / department / stakeholders) · liaise with: serve as an official channel between distinct groups (police / committee / embassy) · converse: engage in serious, structured spoken conversation (scholar / stranger / partner) · commune: share deep, intimate, often nonverbal thoughts or feelings (nature / spirit / soul)
groups.nuance_zh: network: 建立扩展人脉网络 (clients / peers / alumni) · interface: 对接协调沟通 (team / department / stakeholders) · liaise with: 担任联络人沟通协调 (police / committee / embassy) · converse: 进行正式深入交谈 (scholar / stranger / partner) · commune: 深度心灵交融感应 (nature / spirit / soul)

groups.name: Spatial Contiguity & Bordering · 毗连与接壤 (Border, Adjoin, Abut)
groups.tip: 空间界限相交相靠

items.def_zh: 与……接壤，毗邻；给……镶边；近似，接近 (border on)
items.def_en: 1. (+ on) To be next to or share a boundary with a country, area, or property. 2. To form an edge along something. 3. (+ on) To come close to or be almost the same as something.
items.ex_en: Rows of tall cypress trees gracefully border the historic vineyard's southern perimeter.
items.ex_zh: 成排的高大柏树优美地环绕着这座历史悠久的葡萄园南侧边界。

items.def_en: 1. To be located next to or live near someone or something.
items.ex_en: Our tranquil suburban community neighbors a vast ecological bird sanctuary along the river.
items.ex_zh: 我们宁静的郊区社区紧邻沿河的大型生态鸟类保护区。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Share a boundary with a particular place or territory
items.ex_en: This peaceful mountain province directly borders on three separate sovereign nations.
items.ex_zh: 这个和平的山区省份直接与三个独立的主权国家接壤。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Touch or meet something closely at its boundary or edge
items.ex_en: The newly built wooden fence butts up against our neighbor's concrete driveway.
items.ex_zh: 新修的木栅栏紧邻并顶靠着邻居家混凝土车道的边缘。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Adjoin or lead directly into a neighboring space or area
items.ex_en: The elegant French dining doors open onto a sunlit stone courtyard garden.
items.ex_zh: 优雅的法式餐厅双开门直通阳光明媚的石砌庭院花园。

items.def_zh: 位于……的侧翼；侧面与……相邻
items.def_en: to be situated at the side or along the edge of someone or something
items.ex_en: Majestic marble statues gracefully flank the grand central entrance to the museum.
items.ex_zh: 庄严的大理石雕像典雅地矗立在博物馆宏伟的正门两侧。

items.def_en: to be next to and joined with a building, room, or plot of land
items.ex_en: A modern glass sunroom adjoins the rustic stone kitchen of the manor.
items.ex_zh: 一间现代化的玻璃日光浴室与庄园质朴的石砌厨房紧密毗连。

items.def_zh: 紧邻，邻接（尤指边界直接碰合）
items.def_en: (+ on/against) to touch along a border or have a common boundary with another property
items.ex_en: The private residential estate abuts against a protected national forest along its ridge.
items.ex_zh: 这处私人住宅庄园沿山脊与受保护的国家森林直接接壤。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this spatial frame assert that two distinct geographical areas, parcels of real estate, or physical objects share a common perimeter or touch directly at the margin. They range from everyday geographical statements (border, neighbor) to formal, legal, and architectural descriptions (adjoin, abut, flank).
groups.summary_zh: 指地域、地产或实体在地理空间上互相相邻、边缘接壤或直接相触。
groups.desc_en: Existing in immediate physical, geographic, or architectural contact with an adjacent entity without intervening space, contrasting with loose proximity ('near') by denoting touching boundaries.
groups.desc_zh: 在物理、地理或空间结构上与相邻实体紧密相接且无中间间隔，与普通的“靠近”相比，强调边界的直接触碰或接壤。
groups.nuance_en: adjoin: be immediately next to and joined with a space or building (room / property / garden) · abut: terminate directly against a boundary or structure with physical contact (pier / wall / pavement) · border: form or run along an edge of a region or territory (country / lake / forest) · flank: be situated directly on the side or sides of something (entrance / general / road) · butt up against: push or touch squarely right up to an edge (fence / building / beam)
groups.nuance_zh: adjoin: 紧邻并相连 (room / property / garden) · abut: 毗邻顶触 (pier / wall / pavement) · border: 沿边缘接壤 (country / lake / forest) · flank: 位于两侧护卫或夹峙 (entrance / general / road) · butt up against: 紧挨顶触边缘 (fence / building / beam)

groups.name: Speak & Talk · 说话与交谈 (Verbal Utterance and Conversational Exchange)
groups.tip: 开口发声进行语言交流表达

items.def_zh: 说话，交谈；演说，发言；讲（某种语言）
items.def_en: 1. to say words, talk, or have a conversation with someone 2. to make a speech to an audience 3. to be able to communicate in a particular language
items.ex_en: The foreign minister will speak to reporters regarding the newly signed trade pact.
items.ex_zh: 外交部长将就新签署的贸易协定向记者们发表讲话。

items.def_en: (+ with/to) to talk in a friendly, informal, and relaxed manner about non-serious matters
items.ex_en: We sat on the front porch to chat about our upcoming summer vacations.
items.ex_zh: 我们坐在前廊上闲聊即将到来的暑假。

items.def_zh: 说话，交谈；讲（speak 的过去分词）
items.def_en: the past participle of speak
items.ex_en: Those harsh, unthinking words were spoken in haste and caused unnecessary hurt.
items.ex_zh: 那些严厉而欠考虑的话是在仓促之中说出的，造成了不必要的伤害。

items.def_en: Speak more loudly, or state an opinion openly without hesitation
items.ex_en: You need to speak up during staff meetings if you disagree with decisions.
items.ex_zh: 如果你不同意决定，就需要在员工会议上大胆畅所欲言。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Discuss a problem or situation thoroughly with someone
items.ex_en: We need to sit down and talk over the details before signing the contract.
items.ex_zh: 在签署合同之前，我们需要坐下来详细商讨各个细节。

items.def_zh: 公开表达意见；挺身表态
items.def_en: Publicly express one's views or objections candidly and firmly
items.ex_en: Activists took to the streets to speak out against human rights abuses.
items.ex_zh: 活动人士走上街头，大声疾呼反对侵犯人权的行为。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to speak or write authoritatively and at length upon a scholarly subject
items.ex_en: The distinguished professor discoursed on Victorian literary theory before a packed lecture hall.
items.ex_zh: 那位著名教授在座无虚席的演讲厅里深入论述了维多利亚时期的文学理论。

items.def_en: (+ with) to engage in a formal, thoughtful, or prolonged conversation with someone
items.ex_en: The visiting prime minister conversed with the foreign ambassador on bilateral energy policies.
items.ex_zh: 来访的总理就双边能源政策与外国大使进行了正式交谈。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this baseline frame denote the vocal delivery of words or an interactive verbal exchange between individuals, spanning spontaneous chatter to formal addresses.
groups.summary_zh: 用声音说出言语，或与他人展开双向口头交流与谈话。
groups.desc_en: Employing voiced language to convey information, express opinions, or maintain reciprocal spoken engagement, contrasting with non-verbal messaging or formal writing through oral communication.
groups.desc_zh: 使用有声语言传递信息、表达观点或进行口头交互，与非语言表达或书面形式相比，强调口语声带发声与言语互动。
groups.nuance_en: speak: articulate words or address an audience orally (language / truth / crowd) · chat: converse in an informal, easy, and lighthearted manner (friend / neighbor / colleague) · speak up: talk louder or boldly voice an opinion against injustice (meeting / class / rights) · speak out: publicly declare beliefs or condemn wrongdoing (abuse / injustice / policy) · discourse: talk extensively and systematically about a topic (philosophy / theology / politics)
groups.nuance_zh: speak: 开口说话、发表演说 (language / truth / crowd) · chat: 轻松闲聊叙旧 (friend / neighbor / colleague) · speak up: 大声说出、为正义发声 (meeting / class / rights) · speak out: 挺身公开抨击 (abuse / injustice / policy) · discourse: 系统性长篇论述交谈 (philosophy / theology / politics)

groups.name: Specialized Cavity Stuffing · 填膛与烹饪填塞 (Farce, Pouch, Stuff)
groups.tip: 打包入袋或装入容器

items.def_en: (+ with) to fill the inside of poultry, meat, or vegetables with seasoned breadcrumbs, herbs, etc.
items.ex_en: She expertly stuffed the holiday turkey with seasoned herbs and stale sourdough breadcrumbs.
items.ex_zh: 她熟练地将调味香草和酸面包屑填入节日火鸡中。

items.def_en: (+ with) to fill or line a receptacle or garment with soft protective material
items.ex_en: The shipping clerk padded the fragile ceramic vase with dense bubble wrap.
items.ex_zh: 发货员用致密的气泡垫填充衬垫易碎的陶瓷花瓶。

items.def_en: to plug or fill a cavity or bore with a soft compressible wad
items.ex_en: Carefully wadding the musket barrel with cloth ensured the black powder remained stable.
items.ex_zh: 用软布将滑膛枪管紧密塞满塞实，能确保黑火药保持稳固。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Fill a space, receptacle, or cavity completely and tightly
items.ex_en: He decided to pack in his office job to travel the world.
items.ex_zh: 他决定辞去办公室的工作去环游世界。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Force a great deal of material or things into a confined space or cavity
items.ex_en: She tried to cram too many thick sweaters into her small leather carry-on.
items.ex_zh: 她试图把太多厚毛衣硬塞进她的小皮质随身行李箱里。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Fill or line a hollow cavity or shape with soft padding material
items.ex_en: The theatrical costumer padded out the lightweight dummy with batting for extra fullness.
items.ex_zh: 戏剧服装师用棉絮将轻质人体模型填塞衬垫得更加饱满。

items.def_zh: 装入小袋（或囊袋）中；（使）鼓起成袋状
items.def_en: 1. To put something into a small bag or pouch. 2. To bulge outward like a pouch, or cause something to do so.
items.ex_en: The hamster pouched seeds inside its expandable cheeks before scurrying across the cage.
items.ex_zh: 仓鼠在笼子里穿梭前，把种子装进了鼓鼓的腮囊里。
items.ex2_en: His heavy trousers pouched awkwardly around his knees after hours of hiking.
items.ex2_zh: 徒步几小时后，他沉重的裤子在膝盖处尴尬地鼓了起来。

items.def_zh: 在（肉、禽等）中塞入填料；填塞
items.def_en: (cooking, archaic) To stuff meat, poultry, or vegetables with a seasoned filling before cooking.
items.ex_en: The royal chef chose to farce the tender pigeon with savory wild mushrooms.
items.ex_zh: 御厨选择用风味浓郁的野生蘑菇作为填料塞入鲜嫩的鸽肉中。

groups.summary_en: An agent fills an enclosed cavity or flexible container (such as meat, poultry, or a small receptacle) with a specific compound, mixture, or stuffing. Verbs differ by technical domain (culinary arts vs. storage) and register.
groups.summary_zh: 在食材内膛或囊袋状容器内填塞配料或充填物，具明确专业场景。
groups.desc_en: Inserting, packing, or forcing soft, seasoned, or protective filling into an internal hollow space or food cavity, contrasting with simple covering by emphasizing internal expansion and cavity occupancy.
groups.desc_zh: 将柔软、调味或防护性填充物压入或塞入内部空腔或食材腹腔中，与表面覆盖相比，强调内部容积的饱满填塞与膨胀。
groups.nuance_en: stuff: pack tightly or fill the hollow cavity of food or containers (turkey / cushion / pocket) · farce: stuff seasoned minced meat or forcemeat into culinary cavities (poultry / vegetables / fish) · pad: fill with soft material for cushioning, shape, or comfort (jacket / bra / seat) · cram into: force an excessive amount of matter violently into a tight space (suitcase / locker / mouth) · pouch: enclose or form into a pouch-like cavity for packing (dough / fabric / fold)
groups.nuance_zh: stuff: 填塞充盈腔体 (turkey / cushion / pocket) · farce: 烹饪填馅塞肉 (poultry / vegetables / fish) · pad: 加垫料防震定型 (jacket / bra / seat) · cram into: 强行硬塞塞满 (suitcase / locker / mouth) · pouch: 缝纳囊袋状填入 (dough / fabric / fold)

groups.name: Spot & Scar Surface · 斑驳与麻点污损 (Splotch, Pockmark)
groups.tip: 破坏表面留下瑕疵或污斑

items.def_en: (+ with) to mark or speckle a surface with tiny specks or dots of color
items.ex_en: Tiny glistening gold sparkles fleck the smooth green surface of the polished stone.
items.ex_zh: 微小闪亮的金色斑点点缀在抛光石材光滑的绿色表面上。

items.def_zh: 弄脏；在表面留下划痕斑点
items.def_en: (+ sth) to damage, dirty, or disfigure the surface of something with scratches, blemishes, or spots
items.ex_en: Heavy work boots can easily mark up the newly polished oak dance floor.
items.ex_zh: 厚重的工装靴很容易在刚抛光的橡木舞池地板上留下划痕和划印。

items.def_zh: 使有斑驳花纹（如斑驳光影）
items.def_en: (+ with) to mark with rounded spots or patches of light and shade
items.ex_en: Afternoon sunlight filtered through high canopy leaves to dapple the mossy garden bench.
items.ex_zh: 午后的阳光穿透高耸的树冠，在长满青苔的花园长椅上投下斑驳光影。

items.def_zh: 磨损；擦破表面留下痕迹
items.def_en: (+ sth) to make marks, scrapes, or rough patches on the surface of an object by scraping or rubbing
items.ex_en: Playing basketball on asphalt will quickly scuff up your brand-new leather sneakers.
items.ex_zh: 在沥青地面上打篮球会很快磨损擦花你崭新的真皮运动鞋表面。
items.ex2_en: Cheap plastic phone cases tend to scuff up quickly in everyday pockets.
items.ex2_zh: 廉价的塑料手机壳在日常口袋里很容易迅速磨花磨损。

items.def_en: to spot, stain, or disfigure with ink, paint, or a heavy blemish
items.ex_en: A leaky fountain pen managed to blot the parchment with permanent black ink.
items.ex_zh: 漏水的钢笔在羊皮纸上留下了擦不掉的黑墨水污渍。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To mark or cover a surface with large, irregular spots or stains of color or liquid.
items.ex_en: Careless painters accidentally splotched the pale wooden floor with bright crimson oil paint.
items.ex_zh: 粗心的油漆工不小心把鲜艳的深红色油漆洒在浅色木地板上，留下一片片污迹。

items.def_zh: 使留下麻子，在……上留下坑洼（或凹痕）
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To mark, scar, or pit a surface or skin with small hollow scars or craters.
items.ex_en: Years of severe untreated acne had pockmarked his forehead and upper cheeks noticeably.
items.ex_zh: 多年严重的未治疗痤疮在他的前额和上脸颊留下了明显的凹坑麻痕。

items.def_zh: 使凹陷，使表面留下坑洼
items.def_en: (+ with) to mark or indent a surface with hollows, craters, or small depressions
items.ex_en: Ancient corrosive acid rain had pitted the outdoor limestone monument over several decades.
items.ex_zh: 数十年来，具有腐蚀性的酸雨使这座室外石灰岩纪念碑表面布满了坑洼凹痕。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe defacing, marking, or blemishing a surface through localized spots, irregular blotches, or pitted depressions.
groups.summary_zh: 在表面留下斑块、瘢痕、点状凹陷等局部瑕疵损害。
groups.desc_en: Disfiguring, speckling, or damaging a continuous surface with scattered spots, indentations, or blemishes, contrasting with uniform coloring or clean destruction by creating uneven, textured imperfection.
groups.desc_zh: 用零星斑点、凹坑或瑕疵破坏或污染原本平整的外观表面，与均匀染色或彻底毁灭相比，强调局部的斑驳不平与肌理损伤。
groups.nuance_en: pockmark: pit or scar a surface with small circular hollow depressions (face / wall / lawn) · pit: form tiny holes or hollow scars from corrosion or disease (metal / skin / stone) · dapple: mark with small variegated spots or patches of light and shade (sunlight / coat / skin) · fleck: mark or streak with tiny scattered specks (paint / tweed / dust) · splotch: disfigure with large, irregular, messy stains or blotches (ink / sauce / canvas)
groups.nuance_zh: pockmark: 留下麻点凹坑瘢痕 (face / wall / lawn) · pit: 形成点状微小蚀坑 (metal / skin / stone) · dapple: 形成斑驳光影斑点 (sunlight / coat / skin) · fleck: 点缀细小微斑微粒 (paint / tweed / dust) · splotch: 溅上不规则大块污渍 (ink / sauce / canvas)

groups.name: Spurt & Gush · 喷射与涌出 (Spurt, Gush, Jet)
groups.tip: 液体受压大股喷涌而出

items.def_en: [I/T] to force a thin stream of liquid through a narrow opening
items.ex_en: The leaky valve squirted a thin stream of pressurized hydraulic fluid across the garage.
items.ex_zh: 漏损的阀门将一股高压液压油细流喷射到了车库另一端。
items.ex2_en: Warm water squirted forcefully from the garden hose directly onto the driveway.
items.ex2_zh: 温水从花园软管中强劲地喷射出来，直冲到车道上。

items.def_en: to flow or pour out suddenly in very large quantities
items.ex_en: Cold mountain spring water gushed continuously over the slippery rocks after spring thaw.
items.ex_zh: 春季解冻后，冰凉的山泉水持续不断地在大片湿滑岩石上涌出。
items.ex2_en: The broken municipal pipe gushed gallons of water onto the city street.
items.ex2_zh: 破裂的市政管道将大量的水喷涌到城市街道上。

items.def_en: to surge out rapidly in very large quantities
items.ex_en: Gallons of muddy river water gushed out from the fractured concrete retaining wall.
items.ex_zh: 数加仑泥泞的河水从开裂的混凝土挡土墙中大股倾泻涌出。

items.def_en: to discharge or emerge suddenly and with great force
items.ex_en: A bright spark shot out from the roaring fireplace onto the woven rug.
items.ex_zh: 一颗明亮的火星从熊熊燃烧的壁炉中疾射而出，落在了编织地毯上。
items.ex2_en: The volcano can shoot out deadly clouds of ash during an active eruption.
items.ex2_zh: 火山在剧烈喷发时会喷射出致命的火山灰云。

items.def_en: to flow or burst out suddenly in a rapid stream from a confined space
items.ex_en: Crimson red sauce spurted out forcefully when the pressurized jar finally popped open.
items.ex_zh: 当带压力的密封罐终于弹开时，深红色的酱汁猛然喷了出来。
items.ex2_en: The violent geyser spurted out scalding mineral water high into the morning air.
items.ex2_zh: 猛烈的间歇泉将滚烫的矿泉水高高喷向清晨的空中。

items.def_en: to spurt out in a rapid, forceful stream under high pressure
items.ex_en: Pressurized water began to jet through the tiny crack in the cooling pipe.
items.ex_zh: 承压水开始从冷却管的细小裂缝中疾冲喷出。
items.ex2_en: The modern fire apparatus can jet streams of water across incredible distances.
items.ex2_zh: 现代消防设备可以将水流强劲地喷射到极远的距离。

items.def_zh: 喷出，喷射，涌出；突然加速，冲刺
items.def_en: 1. When liquid or flame spurts, it shoots out suddenly in a strong stream. 2. To increase speed or effort suddenly.
items.ex_en: Cold oil began to spurt from the broken hose across the garage floor.
items.ex_zh: 冰冷的机油从破损的软管中喷涌而出，溅落了满地。
items.ex2_en: The broken garden sprinkler began to spurt water across the freshly paved driveway.
items.ex2_zh: 坏掉的花园喷头开始把水喷洒在刚铺好的车道上。

items.def_en: 1. When hot water, steam, or liquid geysers, it spouts forcefully upward into the air.
items.ex_en: Scalding water began to geyser furiously from the ruptured geothermal pipe downtown.
items.ex_zh: 滚烫的开水从市中心破裂的地热管道中猛烈喷涌上天。

groups.summary_en: A liquid issues forth forcibly and rapidly from a narrow orifice or pressurized source. Verbs are differentiated by fluid volume, steadiness, and the kinetic violence of the discharge.
groups.summary_zh: 液体受压自孔道或源头猛烈、大量涌出，按喷射力度、流速及持续性排序。
groups.desc_en: Forcing liquid or gas out through an aperture or ruptured surface under high dynamic pressure, contrasting with passive leaking or trickling by virtue of kinetic propulsion and volume velocity.
groups.desc_zh: 在强劲动压作用下将液体或气体从孔隙或破口中强力喷发喷射，与缓慢渗漏或滴淌相比，强调高压喷发力与喷射速度。
groups.nuance_en: spurt: shoot out abruptly in an intermittent, forceful stream (blood / water / fuel) · gush: flow out copiously, rapidly, and abundantly under release (oil / tears / fountain) · squirt: force out liquid through a narrow orifice in a thin rapid jet (ink / juice / hose) · jet: propel outward continuously with great velocity and directional force (steam / fuel / water) · geyser: erupt violently and skyward like a natural thermal spout (mud / water / steam)
groups.nuance_zh: spurt: 阵发性喷涌射出 (blood / water / fuel) · gush: 奔腾涌出、大量狂泻 (oil / tears / fountain) · squirt: 细流哧出射出 (ink / juice / hose) · jet: 高速定向喷流 (steam / fuel / water) · geyser: 柱状如间歇泉般冲天喷发 (mud / water / steam)

groups.name: Stage & Present · 排演与搬上舞台 (Stage, Dramatize, Mount)
groups.tip: 筹办搬上舞台呈现演出

items.def_en: to manage and oversee the financial and managerial aspects of staging a play or film
items.ex_en: She agreed to produce the independent documentary after reviewing the director's initial budget.
items.ex_zh: 在审阅了导演的初步预算后，她同意出资监制这部独立纪录片。

items.def_zh: 上演，把……搬上舞台；举行，组织（活动、抗议等）
items.def_en: 1. To organize and present a play, show, or performance on stage. 2. To organize and carry out an event, protest, or action.
items.ex_en: The local theatre company plans to stage a fresh adaptation of Hamlet.
items.ex_zh: 当地剧团计划在今年春天把改编版《哈姆雷特》搬上舞台。

items.def_en: to organize, produce, and put on a play, exhibition, or performance
items.ex_en: The university drama society will mount an ambitious new production of Macbeth.
items.ex_zh: 大学话剧社将筹备上演一部雄心勃勃的全新《麦克白》。

items.def_en: to produce and present a play, concert, or theatrical show
items.ex_en: The drama department decided to put on a classic Broadway musical this semester.
items.ex_zh: 戏剧系决定在本学期排演一部经典的百老汇音乐剧。

items.def_zh: 用动作把…表演出来；搬演
items.def_en: (+ sth) to perform a story, scene, or event using actions and dialogue
items.ex_en: The drama students will act out a tense interrogation scene for class.
items.ex_zh: 戏剧系学生将在课堂上把一段紧张的审讯场景生动地表演出来。

items.def_en: (+ for sth) to audition or compete for a role in a theatrical production or film
items.ex_en: Dozens of hopeful young actors arrived to try out for the lead role.
items.ex_zh: 数十位满怀希望的年轻演员赶来参加主角的选角试演。

items.def_en: [I/T] to practice a play, piece of music, or dance for public performance
items.ex_en: The cast met early each morning to rehearse the complex ballroom dance sequence.
items.ex_zh: 演员阵容每天清晨集合，排练复杂的舞厅跳舞桥段。

items.def_zh: 将……改编为戏剧（或影视剧）；夸张，把……戏剧化
items.def_en: 1. To adapt a story, novel, or real event into a play, film, or TV drama. 2. To make an event or situation seem much more exciting, dramatic, or serious than it really is.
items.ex_en: The network hired an acclaimed playwright to dramatize the historic espionage trial.
items.ex_zh: 电视台聘请了一位著名编剧将那场历史性的间谍审判改编为电视剧。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the creative and logistical act of adapting, organizing, and physically producing a performance or text for a theatrical audience.
groups.summary_zh: 指将文本、剧本或事件编排制作并在舞台、荧幕上呈现给观众的演艺行为。
groups.desc_en: Organizing, rehearsing, and physically mounting a dramatic or artistic work for live performance, contrasting with merely writing text or acting privately by encompassing collective public realization.
groups.desc_zh: 对戏剧或艺术作品进行组织、排演并最终搬上舞台公开演出，与单纯案头创作或私人试演相比，侧重现场的舞台立体呈现与公演运作。
groups.nuance_en: stage: adapt and physically produce a performance on a platform (play / opera / coup) · mount: finance, organize, and present an elaborate production or exhibition (production / show / exhibit) · put on: present or organize an entertainment for an audience (concert / play / exhibition) · dramatize: adapt a written work into theatrical form for drama (novel / incident / biography) · rehearse: practice systematically in preparation for public performance (scene / speech / dance)
groups.nuance_zh: stage: 搬上舞台演出 (play / opera / coup) · mount: 策划制作展演 (production / show / exhibit) · put on: 举办上演演出 (concert / play / exhibition) · dramatize: 将作品改编为戏剧 (novel / incident / biography) · rehearse: 排练演练 (scene / speech / dance)

groups.name: Stand & Upright · 站立与起立 (Stand, Rise, Upright)
groups.tip: 双腿直立或由坐而起

items.def_en: to rise from a sitting, lying, or kneeling position to an upright stance
items.ex_en: He paused to catch his breath before managing to get up from the sofa.
items.ex_zh: 他停下来喘口气，随后才设法从沙发上站起身来。

items.def_en: to rise from a sitting or lying position onto one's feet
items.ex_en: Everyone was asked to stand up when the chief judge entered the room.
items.ex_zh: 首席法官步入法庭时，所有人起立致敬。

items.def_zh: 站立，直立；立起；位于；经受，容忍
items.def_en: 1. To be on your feet in an upright position, or to rise to this position. 2. To be located or positioned in a particular place. 3. (usually in negative) To endure, withstand, or tolerate something unpleasant.
items.ex_en: My legs were so stiff that I couldn't even stand for two minutes.
items.ex_zh: 我的腿太僵硬了，连两分钟都站不住。

items.def_zh: （stand 的过去式和过去分词）站立，直立；位于；容忍
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of stand: to be in an upright position on one's feet; to be situated; to endure or tolerate.
items.ex_en: She stood quietly beside the window, watching the heavy rain soak the garden.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地伫立在窗边，看着大雨打湿了花园。

items.def_en: to stand erect from a low or seated posture
items.ex_en: The citizens rose up against the corrupt military regime.
items.ex_zh: 市民们揭竿而起，反抗腐败的军事政权。

items.def_en: to bring one's torso into an erect vertical posture
items.ex_en: Straighten up and pull your shoulders back before you walk into the interview.
items.ex_zh: 走进面试室前，挺直身子站好，把肩膀往后展一展。
items.ex2_en: Please straighten up the messy living room before our dinner guests finally arrive.
items.ex2_zh: 在晚餐客人最终到达之前，请先把凌乱的客厅收拾整齐。

items.def_en: (formal) to stand up from a kneeling, sitting, or lying position
items.ex_en: The audience was requested to rise as the national anthem began to play.
items.ex_zh: 国歌奏响之际，全场观众被要求肃立。

items.def_en: to restore or raise something to an erect vertical position
items.ex_en: The crew worked together to upright the heavy wooden wardrobe against the wall.
items.ex_zh: 队员们齐心协力将沉重的木制大衣柜重新竖立在墙边。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote assuming, maintaining, or returning to a vertical, upright posture on one's feet from a recumbent or seated position.
groups.summary_zh: 指双脚着地维持垂直挺立状态，或从坐卧体位转为站立姿势。
groups.desc_en: Maintaining or moving into an upright vertical posture supported primarily by the feet, contrasting with sitting or reclining by establishing vertical physical presence and readiness.
groups.desc_zh: 保持或转变为双脚支撑的竖直挺拔姿态，与静坐或平卧相比，侧重展现纵向直立的空间体态与起身动作。
groups.nuance_en: stand: maintain an erect, motionless vertical posture on one's feet (guard / line / corner) · rise: move upward from a sitting, kneeling, or lying position (seat / table / bed) · stand up: actively shift the body into a full vertical standing posture (chair / audience / crowd) · get up: rise from bed or recover from a fallen position (morning / floor / sofa) · straighten up: extend the spine vertically after crouching or bending (back / posture)
groups.nuance_zh: stand: 站立站着 (guard / line / corner) · rise: 起立升起 (seat / table / bed) · stand up: 站起身来 (chair / audience / crowd) · get up: 起床起身 (morning / floor / sofa) · straighten up: 挺直腰背站正 (back / posture)

groups.name: Start & Embark · 启程与开拔起动 (Embark, Restart, Commence)
groups.tip: 着手开展或登程出发

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to begin a journey or start an enterprise with a specific aim
items.ex_en: The researchers set out on an ambitious expedition across the frozen Antarctic interior.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员动身踏上穿越冰封南极内陆的宏大征程。

items.def_en: to leave the ground or begin to become rapidly active and successful
items.ex_en: The flight was finally cleared to take off despite the gathering storm clouds.
items.ex_zh: 尽管暴风雨云正在积聚，该航班最终获准顺利起飞。

items.def_en: to begin a journey or major expedition
items.ex_en: The expedition planned to set off at dawn before the desert heat peaked.
items.ex_zh: 探险队计划在拂晓前沙漠高温到达顶点前动身启程。

items.def_en: to begin a journey, event, or sequence of actions
items.ex_en: We should start off early tomorrow if we want to avoid the traffic.
items.ex_zh: 如果我们想避开交通高峰，明天一成就得尽早起步出发。
items.ex2_en: The lively brass marching band started off the vibrant annual summer town parade.
items.ex2_zh: 欢快的铜管军乐队拉开了小镇一年一度充满活力的夏季游行序幕。

items.def_zh: 向新方向出发；独立开拓
items.def_en: to start moving purposefully in a specific direction or embark on an independent venture
items.ex_en: After five years at the firm, he decided to strike out on his own.
items.ex_zh: 在公司工作五年后，他决定自立门户、独立开拓属于自己的事业。

items.def_en: [I/T] to begin or start an undertaking, ritual, or formal activity
items.ex_en: The graduation ceremony will commence promptly at ten o'clock in the main auditorium.
items.ex_zh: 毕业典礼将于上午十点整在主礼堂正式开始。
items.ex2_en: The company will commence construction on the new office building next spring season.
items.ex2_zh: 该公司将于明年春季正式开展新办公楼的建设工程。

items.def_zh: 着手，开始（常与 on/upon 连用）；上船（或飞机）
items.def_en: 1. (embark on/upon) To start a new project, venture, or course of action. 2. To board a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.
items.ex_en: The young entrepreneur prepared to embark upon a high-risk venture in renewable energy.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻的创业者准备着手开展一项高风险的可再生能源新事业。
items.ex2_en: The nervous crew embarked the anxious passengers onto the waiting ocean ferry.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的乘务员引导焦急的乘客登上等待中的远洋渡轮。

items.def_zh: 重新开始；重新启动（设备、系统等）
items.def_en: To begin again, or to cause something such as a machine, system, or activity to start again after stopping.
items.ex_en: The technician advised the user to restart the computer after updating the software.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员建议用户在更新软件后重新启动电脑。
items.ex2_en: The stalled economic recovery will hopefully restart after new trade deals take effect.
items.ex2_zh: 在新的贸易协定生效后，停滞的经济复苏有望重新启动。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the initiation of major journeys, ventures, or restarting an activity after an interruption.
groups.summary_zh: 指开启旅途、启动企业事业项目或中断后重新开动。
groups.desc_en: Setting forth on a journey, expedition, or new substantial undertaking, contrasting with generic initiation ('begin') by emphasizing physical departure, travel, or venture launch.
groups.desc_zh: 踏上旅途、远征或启动重大开拓性事业，与普通的“开始”相比，强调空间开拔、启程出发与冒险征程的起步。
groups.nuance_en: embark: board a vessel or enter upon a new major enterprise (ship / voyage / venture) · set out: begin a physical journey or attempt to achieve a specific goal (journey / trail / career) · set off: start a journey or trigger a chain of events (trek / trip / alarm) · take off: leave the ground in flight or depart suddenly (plane / rocket / career) · strike out: venture boldly in a new or independent direction (wilderness / path / future)
groups.nuance_zh: embark: 乘船启航或投身新事业 (ship / voyage / venture) · set out: 启程动身或立志着手 (journey / trail / career) · set off: 动身出发 (trek / trip / alarm) · take off: 起飞腾飞或遽然离去 (plane / rocket / career) · strike out: 另辟蹊径大胆闯荡 (wilderness / path / future)

groups.name: Steer & Navigate Craft · 驾驭与操舵领航 (Conn, Steer, Helm)
groups.tip: 操控车辆船只或导航前行

items.def_zh: 引航；驾驶（航向精细操纵）
items.def_en: to steer or guide a ship or aircraft through hazardous waters or air routes
items.ex_en: An experienced local captain arrived to pilot the cargo vessel through the reef.
items.ex_zh: 一位经验丰富的地方船长赶来引航，操纵货轮穿过暗礁区。

items.def_en: (+ from sth) to guide or direct the movement of a vessel or vehicle away from something
items.ex_en: The captain ordered the helmsman to steer away from the jagged coral reef.
items.ex_zh: 船长命令舵手操舵转向，驶离犬牙交错的珊瑚礁。
items.ex2_en: The autonomous patrol ship steered away toward the calmer open ocean waters.
items.ex2_zh: 自主巡逻船转向驶向了更加平静的开阔公海海域。

items.def_en: to reverse the engines of a vessel in order to back up or stop forward headway
items.ex_en: The captain ordered the crew to back down the ferry into the dock.
items.ex_zh: 船长命令船员倒舵退车，将轮渡缓缓倒进码头泊位。

items.def_en: [I/T] to guide or control the direction of a vessel, vehicle, or aircraft
items.ex_en: The captain had to steer the fishing vessel through dangerously choppy harbor waters.
items.ex_zh: 船长不得不掌舵操纵渔船穿过港湾内汹涌危险的风浪。
items.ex2_en: The massive freight vessel steered smoothly into the busy international trading port.
items.ex2_zh: 庞大的货轮平稳地驶入了繁忙的国际贸易港口。

items.def_en: [I/T] to direct and manage the charted course of a ship, aircraft, or vehicle
items.ex_en: The seasoned captain had to navigate the cargo vessel through dense coastal fog.
items.ex_zh: 这位经验丰富的船长必须驾驶货轮穿过沿海弥漫的浓雾。

items.def_en: to steer a ship or boat by operating the helm or rudder
items.ex_en: The seasoned skipper agreed to helm the racing yacht through the difficult channel.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的老船长答应操舵领航，驾着参赛帆船穿过这道险要的水道。

items.def_zh: 指挥操舵，掌舵（操纵船只或潜水艇的航向）
items.def_en: 1. (nautical) To direct the steering and navigation of a ship or submarine.
items.ex_en: The veteran commander took the bridge to conn the nuclear submarine through straits.
items.ex_zh: 老练的指挥官登上舰桥，亲自指挥操舵让核潜艇穿越海峡。

items.def_zh: 骑摩托车，乘摩托车旅行
items.def_en: 1. To ride or travel on a motorcycle.
items.ex_en: They planned to motorbike through the scenic mountain pass over the holiday weekend.
items.ex_zh: 他们计划在周末假期骑摩托车穿越风景优美的山口旅行。

groups.summary_en: An operator directly directs the course, speed, or steering of a vessel, vehicle, or craft. Technical maritime terms like 'conn' denote issuing tactical steering orders from the bridge, whereas broader navigation verbs encompass the physical handling of the helm.
groups.summary_zh: 在舰船或载具上操舵、下达航向指令并掌控行驶动态。
groups.desc_en: Directing and controlling the heading, course, or mechanical locomotion of a ship, aircraft, or vehicle, contrasting with passive riding by emphasizing active trajectory guidance and helm control.
groups.desc_zh: 操控指示船舶、航空器或载具的航向、路线或行进，与被动搭乘相比，强调主动操舵领航与轨迹掌控。
groups.nuance_en: steer: guide the physical heading of a vehicle using a wheel or rudder (car / boat / course) · helm: act as the steersman or direct the overarching leadership of a vessel (ship / project / company) · navigate: plan and follow a geographical route over water, air, or land (channel / globe / waters) · pilot: guide an aircraft in flight or navigate a ship through tricky channels (plane / vessel / tanker) · conn: direct the steering of a naval vessel from the control station (ship / bridge)
groups.nuance_zh: steer: 操舵掌轮控制方向 (car / boat / course) · helm: 掌舵主导把舵 (ship / project / company) · navigate: 领航导航航行 (channel / globe / waters) · pilot: 驾驶飞行或引航领江 (plane / vessel / tanker) · conn: 在舰桥指挥操舰 (ship / bridge)

groups.name: Sting & Tingle · 刺痛与触感微刺 (Tickle, Prickle, Tingle)
groups.tip: 针扎微刺伴随酥麻之感

items.def_en: to experience an uncomfortable, irritating sensation on the skin prompting scratching
items.ex_en: The rough wool sweater made his sensitive neck itch terribly all morning long.
items.ex_zh: 那件粗羊毛毛衣让他敏感的脖子整个早晨都奇痒无比。

items.def_zh: 胳肢，挠痒；使发痒，使发轻微刺痒；逗乐，使高兴
items.def_en: 1. To touch someone lightly in a way that causes laughter or a tingling sensation. 2. To feel or cause a slight itching or tickling sensation. 3. (informal) To amuse or please someone.
items.ex_en: A loose thread inside his woolen scarf continued to tickle his throat annoying.
items.ex_zh: 羊毛围巾里一根散落的线头总是不停地使他的喉咙发痒。

items.def_en: (+ with) to experience a slight, prickly, stinging sensation caused by cold, emotion, or friction
items.ex_en: Her cheeks began to tingle with the biting mountain wind as she stepped outside.
items.ex_zh: 当她走到户外时，凛冽的山风吹得她的脸颊隐隐发麻微痛。

items.def_zh: 感到刺痛（或微痛、发麻）；刺，扎；使感到刺痛
items.def_en: To feel or cause a tingling, stinging, or prickling sensation on the skin.
items.ex_en: The coarse fabric made the tender skin along his collarbones prickle with discomfort.
items.ex_zh: 粗糙的布料让他锁骨处娇嫩的皮肤感到一阵阵刺痛不适。
items.ex2_en: The rough woolen sweater prickled his neck skin throughout the winter morning.
items.ex2_zh: 整个冬天的早晨，粗糙的羊毛衫一直扎得他脖子上的皮肤发痒刺痛。

items.def_en: to feel intense heat or a stinging, burning sensation on the skin
items.ex_en: My exposed neck began to burn up after hours in the direct sun.
items.ex_zh: 在烈日下暴晒几个小时后，我裸露的脖子开始发烫刺痛。

items.def_zh: （皮疹、疼痛等）突然发作；阵发刺痛
items.def_en: to suddenly become inflamed, painful, or intensely irritated on the skin
items.ex_en: His chronic eczema tends to flare up whenever the weather turns cold and dry.
items.ex_zh: 每当天候变冷干燥时，他的慢性湿疹就往往会突然发作红痛。

items.def_en: to feel a sharp, clean, stinging wound pain, such as from an antiseptic or slap
items.ex_en: The scrape on his bare knee began to smart when the disinfectant touched it.
items.ex_zh: 当消毒剂碰到他裸露膝盖上的擦伤时，伤口火辣辣地抽痛起来。

items.def_en: to feel or cause a sharp, burning, localized pain on the skin or eyes
items.ex_en: The strong salt spray began to sting his open cuts and irritated eyes.
items.ex_zh: 强烈飞溅的盐沫水开始刺痛他暴露的伤口和发炎的双眼。

groups.summary_en: A localized skin area or bodily surface experiences or produces a faint, irritating, light, or prickling sensory stimulation.
groups.summary_zh: 身体表面因微弱刺激而产生发痒、微刺或阵阵麻痛感。
groups.desc_en: Experiencing or inflicting a localized, prickling, or sharp superficial cutaneous sensation, contrasting with deep visceral pain or broad numbness by foregrounding sharp, vibrant nerve stimulation.
groups.desc_zh: 皮肤表面经历或引发局部发痒、微刺或锐利的神经针刺感，与深度内脏疼痛或麻木相比，强调表层敏锐而振颤的刺痒反应。
groups.nuance_en: sting: produce a sharp, momentary burning or prickling wound (bee / disinfectant / cold) · smart: cause a stinging, lingering superficial sharp pain (eyes / skin / wound) · prickle: produce tingling sensations like multiple tiny needles (spine / skin / scalp) · tingle: experience a vibrating, slight stinging or warm thrill (fingers / nerves / skin) · tickle: stimulate nerve endings lightly to provoke twitching or laughter (throat / nose / rib)
groups.nuance_zh: sting: 刺痛蛰痛 (bee / disinfectant / cold) · smart: 剧烈火辣辣作痛 (eyes / skin / wound) · prickle: 针扎般刺痒 (spine / skin / scalp) · tingle: 麻刺发麻感 (fingers / nerves / skin) · tickle: 瘙痒、发痒逗痒 (throat / nose / rib)

groups.name: Stovetop Oil & Pan Cooking · 煎炒与焖煸 (Sauté, Braise, Sear)
groups.tip: 运用烘炖等手法烹制食材

items.def_en: [I/T] to fry food in a shallow pan with a moderate layer of oil or fat
items.ex_en: She heated olive oil in a skillet to pan-fry the seasoned sea bass.
items.ex_zh: 她在平底锅里加热橄榄油，油煎调味好的海鲈鱼。

items.def_en: [I/T] to cook sliced food quickly in a small amount of very hot oil while tossing continuously
items.ex_en: He heated the seasoned wok to stir-fry crisp vegetables in very hot oil.
items.ex_zh: 他将烧热的炒锅架起，在滚烫的油里大火快炒爽脆的蔬菜。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cook or heat food in a pan using hot oil or fat
items.ex_en: Let's fry up some leftover rice and vegetables for a quick lunch.
items.ex_zh: 我们用剩下的米饭和蔬菜炒个饭当快餐吧。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to simmer food or sauce in a pan so that its liquid evaporates and reduces
items.ex_en: Allow the crushed tomatoes to cook down until the sauce becomes thick and rich.
items.ex_zh: 让压碎的西红柿在锅中煨缩，直到酱汁变得浓稠醇厚。
items.ex2_en: The simmering fruit sauce must cook down over low heat for twenty minutes.
items.ex2_zh: 慢炖的水果酱汁必须在小火上浓缩煮熬二十分钟。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to quickly fry food in a little hot fat over high heat
items.ex_en: Let's sauté up some fresh mushrooms with garlic and butter for dinner tonight.
items.ex_zh: 咱们今晚用蒜和黄油煸炒一些新鲜蘑菇来当下饭菜吧。

items.def_en: to fry the surface of meat briefly at high heat to lock in juices and create color
items.ex_en: The chef placed the marbled steak in smoking oil to sear each side.
items.ex_zh: 大厨把雪花牛排放在冒烟的热油中，高温灼烙每一面以锁住肉汁。

items.def_zh: 焖，炖（先煎炒后加少量汤汁盖紧锅慢煮）
items.def_en: To fry food lightly in fat and then cook it slowly with liquid in a covered pan or pot.
items.ex_en: The recipe instructed her to braise the tough beef ribs in seasoned stock.
items.ex_zh: 菜谱指导她将耐嚼的牛肋排在调味高汤里加盖慢火焖炖。

items.def_zh: 嫩煎，短时间煸炒（在少量热油中快速翻炒）
items.def_en: To fry pieces of food quickly in a small amount of hot fat or oil.
items.ex_en: The recipe instructed him to saute diced onions in butter until soft and translucent.
items.ex_zh: 食谱指导他把洋葱丁放入黄油中短时间煸炒至绵软半透明。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame characterize stovetop culinary techniques using hot fat, pans, and controlled moisture, moving from high-heat frying to combination slow-braising.
groups.summary_zh: 炉灶锅底油煎、快炒与先煎后慢火焖煮的常用专业烹调料理技法。
groups.desc_en: Cooking food in a hot pan or skillet using conductive heat, oil, or minimal simmering liquids, contrasting with deep-frying or dry baking by concentrating on pan agitation, crusting, or shallow reduction.
groups.desc_zh: 利用平底锅或炒锅以油脂传导热或少许汤汁烹调食材，与纯油炸或烤箱干烤相比，强调锅具煎烙、爆炒或慢煸软化。
groups.nuance_en: sauté: fry quickly in a small amount of hot oil or fat over high heat while tossing (vegetables / onions / mushrooms) · sear: scorch the surface quickly at intense temperature to lock juices or create crust (steak / tuna / roast) · braise: fry lightly and then stew slowly in a closed vessel with liquid (beef / ribs / pork) · stir-fry: fry pieces of food rapidly over very high heat in a wok while stirring continuously (noodles / chicken / vegetables) · pan-fry: fry food in a shallow pan with moderate oil over medium heat (fish / cutlet / dumpling)
groups.nuance_zh: sauté: 热油快煸嫩炒 (vegetables / onions / mushrooms) · sear: 高温瞬间炙烤锁汁 (steak / tuna / roast) · braise: 煎封后慢火焖煸 (beef / ribs / pork) · stir-fry: 旺火爆炒翻炒 (noodles / chicken / vegetables) · pan-fry: 平底锅浅油慢煎 (fish / cutlet / dumpling)

groups.name: Strangle & Throttle · 掐扼与窒息 (Strangle, Throttle, Choke)
groups.tip: 卡掐咽喉阻断呼吸致人窒息

items.def_en: [I/T] to make someone unable to breathe normally by squeezing the throat or blocking the windpipe
items.ex_en: The dense black smoke threatened to choke the trapped firefighters inside the stairwell.
items.ex_zh: 浓密的黑烟眼看就要呛住困在楼梯间内的消防队员，使他们窒息。
items.ex2_en: The young toddler began to choke during lunch on a large grape.
items.ex2_zh: 那名幼童在吃午饭时被一颗大葡萄卡住喉咙开始窒息。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to cut off someone's air supply by squeezing or compressing their throat
items.ex_en: The bouncer managed to choke off the unruly patron before security arrived.
items.ex_zh: 保安赶来之前，门卫一把勒住这名闹事顾客的颈部使其无法呼喊反抗。

items.def_zh: 掐晕；锁喉使其窒息昏迷
items.def_en: (+ sb) to render someone unconscious by constricting their neck and cutting off air or blood flow
items.ex_en: The martial artist used a precise rear naked choke to choke out his opponent.
items.ex_zh: 武术家使用精准的裸绞动作，直接将对手锁喉致其窒息晕厥。

items.def_zh: 掐死，勒死，使窒息；扼杀，抑制；节流，调节（引擎节气门）
items.def_en: 1. To choke or strangle someone by squeezing their throat tightly. 2. To suppress, choke back, or prevent the development of something. 3. To control the speed or flow of an engine with a throttle.
items.ex_en: The enraged attacker tried to throttle the guard before being overpowered by bystanders.
items.ex_zh: 暴怒的袭击者企图死死掐住守卫的脖子，随后被路人合力制服。

items.def_en: to kill or render unconscious by covering the face to cut off air supply
items.ex_en: The intruder attempted to smother the sleeping witness using a thick feather pillow.
items.ex_zh: 闯入者企图用厚重的羽绒枕头捂住熟睡证人的口鼻致其窒息。

items.def_en: to cause someone to lose consciousness or die through deprivation of oxygen
items.ex_en: The buildup of toxic carbon monoxide threatened to asphyxiate the trapped miners overnight.
items.ex_zh: 有毒一氧化碳的积聚眼看就会在一夜之间让受困矿工窒息死亡。
items.ex2_en: The patient slowly asphyxiated as fluid filled both of his damaged lungs.
items.ex2_zh: 随着液体充满受损的双肺，患者慢慢陷入了窒息。

items.def_zh: 扼死，勒死，掐死；压制，扼杀
items.def_en: 1. To kill or harm someone by squeezing their throat tightly so they cannot breathe. 2. To prevent something from growing, developing, or continuing.
items.ex_en: Detectives determined that the suspect had used a heavy leather belt to strangle him.
