items.ex_zh: 侦探们查明，嫌疑人当时是用一条厚重皮带死死勒死了他。

items.def_en: to kill someone by strangling them with a wire, cord, or metal collar
items.ex_en: The assassin used a thin steel wire to garrotte the corrupt general silently.
items.ex_zh: 刺客用细钢丝悄无声息地将那个腐败的将军绞死。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the hostile act of gripping, compressing, or blocking someone's throat or windpipe to obstruct breathing or blood flow. Intensity spans from brief windpipe obstruction to lethal, sustained strangulation.
groups.summary_zh: 用手、绳索或物体勒紧或卡阻喉部使之窒息。
groups.desc_en: Killing, injuring, or subduing a living being by compressing the neck or airway to prevent respiration, contrasting with general poisoning or piercing by focusing on mechanical windpipe/vascular constriction.
groups.desc_zh: 通过压迫颈部、呼吸道或喉头阻断通气来致死、制服或造成窒息，与毒杀或刺杀相比，强调机械性扼闭气管或静脉血管。
groups.nuance_en: strangle: compress the neck tightly with hands or cord to kill or choke (victim / enemy / scream) · throttle: attack the throat by squeezing the windpipe forcibly (intruder / neck / growth) · choke: block the airway internally or externally so breath is cut off (dust / fumes / smoke) · asphyxiate: cause suffocation and death by depriving the body of oxygen (gas / carbon monoxide / fumes) · smother: kill or extinguish by covering the face or cutting off air supply (infant / flames / cries) · garrotte: strangle someone using a wire, cord, or specialized collar device (guard / victim / target)
groups.nuance_zh: strangle: 勒死掐死 (victim / enemy / scream) · throttle: 扼死掐喉 (intruder / neck / growth) · choke: 气管噎塞窒息 (dust / fumes / smoke) · asphyxiate: 缺氧致窒息死亡 (gas / carbon monoxide / fumes) · smother: 捂闷致窒息、压制 (infant / flames / cries) · garrotte: 钢丝绞喉勒杀 (guard / victim / target)

groups.name: Strew & Litter · 散落与乱撒 (Scatter Objects Carelessly over a Flat Area)
groups.tip: 零散抛撒随意落在各处

items.def_en: to scatter seeds broadly over the ground by hand rather than planting in furrows
items.ex_en: The traditional farmer preferred to broadcast rye seeds across the prepared open field.
items.ex_zh: 这位传统农夫喜欢在平整好的开阔田野上用手均匀地撒播黑麦种子。
items.ex2_en: The seeds broadcast evenly across the open hillside field beneath the wind.
items.ex2_zh: 种子在风的吹拂下均匀地散落播撒在开阔的山坡田野上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to leave objects lying untidily in various places
items.ex_en: He tended to leave around his wet towels on the shared bathroom floor.
items.ex_zh: 他总是习惯把用过的湿毛巾随处乱扔在共用浴室的地板上。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to drop or throw objects untidily all over an area
items.ex_en: The reckless toddler loved to scatter about colourful plastic building blocks across the rug.
items.ex_zh: 这个调皮的小幼儿喜欢把五颜六色的塑料积木胡乱扔得满地毯都是。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to disperse objects broadly over a flat surface
items.ex_en: The search team spread out across the forest to look for the missing hikers.
items.ex_zh: 搜救队在森林中分散开来寻找失踪的徒步旅行者。
items.ex2_en: The gardener spread out fresh wood mulch evenly across the flowerbeds.
items.ex2_zh: 园丁把新鲜的木屑均匀地铺撒在各个花坛上。

items.def_en: [I/T] to throw or drop a quantity of small things loosely in all directions over an area
items.ex_en: The gardener began to scatter wildflower seeds across the freshly cleared hillside plot.
items.ex_zh: 园丁开始将野花种子抛撒在刚清理出来的向阳山坡地上。
items.ex2_en: A flock of startled sparrows will scatter across the park upon hearing noise.
items.ex2_zh: 一群受惊的麻雀一听到响动就会在公园各处四散飞走。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with/among) To scatter or place things at intervals among other things to add variety.
items.ex_en: The landscaper chose to intersperse purple lavender among the rows of dwarf shrubs.
items.ex_zh: 景观设计师选择在成行的矮灌木之间穿插点缀几丛紫色薰衣草。

items.def_zh: 乱丢杂物于，使乱七八糟地布满
items.def_en: to leave things lying scattered around untidily on a surface
items.ex_en: Irresponsible campers continued to litter the pristine mountain trails with discarded plastic bottles.
items.ex_zh: 不负责任的露营者继续用废弃塑料瓶乱扔乱丢，弄脏了原始山道。

items.def_zh: 散播，撒满，遍布（strew的过去分词）
items.def_en: 1. Past participle of strew; scattered or covered untidily across a surface.
items.ex_en: Dry autumn leaves were strewn untidily across the flagstones of the deserted courtyard.
items.ex_zh: 干枯的秋叶凌乱地撒满了荒废庭院里的石板路。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this spatial frame depict scattering or distributing physical things untidily, haphazardly, or at wide intervals across a floor or ground surface. 'Strew' covers broad loose dispersion, while 'intersperse' deliberately distributes elements amidst others.
groups.summary_zh: 杂乱、随意地将碎物抛撒、散落并布满于地面或表面。
groups.desc_en: Denotes dispersing discrete items loosely or untidily across an area, contrasting with orderly distributing or systematic placing by emphasizing haphazard dispersal and visual clutter.
groups.desc_zh: 指将零散物件随意、杂乱地抛撒或散落于某平面，与有序的“分发、布置”相对，强调无序散布与视觉凌乱。
groups.nuance_en: scatter: randomly throw or distribute in various directions (seeds / ashes / papers) · strew: spread loosely over an entire surface to cover it untidily (petals / debris / flowers) · litter: clutter a space with discarded rubbish or mess (trash / streets / beaches) · intersperse: scatter things at varied intervals among other things (anecdotes / commentary / illustrations)
groups.nuance_zh: scatter: 向各方向随意撒播或散开 (seeds / ashes / papers) · strew: 散落铺满表面造成凌乱感 (petals / debris / flowers) · litter: 丢弃垃圾等杂物弄脏空间 (trash / streets / beaches) · intersperse: 在他物之间穿插点缀散置 (anecdotes / commentary / illustrations)

groups.name: Stride & Clomp · 阔步与重步迈进 (Stride, Stalk, Clomp)
groups.tip: 大步流星重步踏地前行

items.def_en: to walk slowly and heavily with effort, as if exhausted
items.ex_en: Exhausted after hiking, the tired travelers continued to plod along the muddy road.
items.ex_zh: 徒步后筋疲力竭的旅人们只得继续沿着泥泞的道路沉重缓慢地跋涉。

items.def_en: to walk into a room or place with firm, resolute, rhythmic steps
items.ex_en: The manager marched in and demanded an immediate explanation from the startled staff.
items.ex_zh: 经理大踏步走进来，要求受惊的员工立刻作出解释。

items.def_en: to depart by walking away with long, purposeful steps
items.ex_en: Without offering an apology, he strided off toward the waiting car outside.
items.ex_zh: 他没有道歉，便大步走开朝外面等候的汽车走去。

items.def_zh: 昂首阔步，傲慢或愤怒地大步走
items.def_en: to walk with stiff, haughty, or menacing long strides
items.ex_en: Insulted by the decision, the diplomat stalked out of the negotiation chamber.
items.ex_zh: 受到该决定的冒犯，这位外交官愤怒而傲慢地大步走出了谈判室。

items.def_zh: 大步走，阔步行进（stride的过去式）
items.def_en: 1. Past tense of stride; walked with long, purposeful steps.
items.ex_en: The solitary traveler strode across the windswept moor beneath a darkening winter sky.
items.ex_zh: 在日渐昏暗的冬日苍穹下，孤独的行者大步穿越风声呼啸的荒原。

items.def_zh: 脚步沉重地走，沉重地践踏
items.def_en: 1. (+ around/up/down) To walk with heavy, loud, clumsy steps.
items.ex_en: Stop clomping around upstairs in those muddy boots while the baby sleeps.
items.ex_zh: 趁着孩子还在睡觉，别再穿着那双泥靴在楼上沉重地走来走去了。

items.def_en: to walk away with heavy, angry, deliberate footsteps
items.ex_en: After losing the argument, Liam stomped off and slammed his bedroom door.
items.ex_zh: 吵输之后，莉安忿然顿足离去，砰地摔上了卧室的门。

items.def_en: to walk with very heavy, deliberate, and loud steps to convey anger
items.ex_en: The furious child stomped down the hallway, refusing to eat his vegetables.
items.ex_zh: 怒气冲冲的孩子重重地顿着脚穿过走廊，拒绝吃蔬菜。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame indicate deliberate walking styles marked either by long, purposeful, confident steps or heavy, noisy, lumbering footfalls against the ground.
groups.summary_zh: 指迈大步果断前行，或脚步沉重笨拙、发出巨响的行进步态。
groups.desc_en: Specifies forceful, purposeful, or emotionally charged locomotive gaits, contrasting with neutral 'walking' by foregrounding gait weight, stride length, and emotive posture (anger, confidence, or heaviness).
groups.desc_zh: 指带有鲜明情绪、力量感或特定目的性的迈步动作，与中性的“行走”相对，突出步伐的长短、沉重度以及傲慢、愤怒等身态表征。
groups.nuance_en: stride: walk with long, decisive, and confident steps (room / stage / platform) · stalk: walk stiffly, haughtily, or menacingly (corridor / grounds / hall) · stomp: tread heavily and noisily to show irritation or fury (feet / stairs / floor) · clomp: walk with a loud, clumsy, heavy-shod clatter (boots / hooves / shoes) · plod: walk slowly and heavily with immense sustained effort (mud / snow / path)
groups.nuance_zh: stride: 迈大步自信而果断地走 (room / stage / platform) · stalk: 昂首阔步或愤怒阴沉地昂然行走 (corridor / grounds / hall) · stomp: 跺着脚愤愤重踏而行 (feet / stairs / floor) · clomp: 穿重鞋发出粗重笨拙的踏步声 (boots / hooves / shoes) · plod: 步履沉重迟缓地艰难跋涉 (mud / snow / path)

groups.name: Strip of Vital Attribute · 剥夺特质与脱除生物机能 (Defoliate, Unsex, Desensitize)
groups.tip: 脱落附着物或剥除特质

items.def_zh: 使裸露，剥除植被或覆盖物
items.def_en: (+ of) to strip a landscape, tree, or surface of its covering, vegetation, or foliage
items.ex_en: Intensive logging operations have completely denuded the steep hillside of its ancient forest.
items.ex_zh: 密集的采伐作业彻底剥除了陡峭山坡上原有的古老森林植被。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to completely drain someone or something of vitality, resources, or essential strength
items.ex_en: Years of corrupt leadership have bled the small town dry of financial resources.
items.ex_zh: 多年的腐败领导彻底榨干了这座小镇的财政资源。

items.def_zh: 剥夺；脱除（特质、尊严或生机）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth of sth) to deprive someone or something of a vital property, attribute, or dignity
items.ex_en: The harsh tribunal stripped the disgraced officer of his rank and military honors.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的法庭剥夺了这名身败名裂的军官的军衔和军旅荣誉。

items.def_en: to strip a person of human attributes, individuality, or basic dignities
items.ex_en: Cruel prison conditions seek to dehumanize inmates and destroy their sense of dignity.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的监狱环境意在剥夺囚犯的人性并摧毁他们的尊严感。

items.def_en: to deprive a male of sexual vitality or virility, or to weaken a system of its potency
items.ex_en: The proposed amendments would utterly emasculate the agency's power to enforce regulations.
items.ex_zh: 拟议中的修正案将彻底削弱该机构执行法规的效力。

items.def_en: To strip trees or bushes of their leaves, especially by using chemicals, or to shed leaves.
items.ex_en: Military aircraft sprayed toxic chemicals over the jungle to defoliate the dense canopy.
items.ex_zh: 军用飞机在丛林上空喷洒有毒化学品，以剥除茂密的树冠枝叶。
items.ex2_en: The deciduous apple trees naturally defoliate when cold autumn weather arrives.
items.ex2_zh: 当寒冷的秋季天气到来时，落叶苹果树会自然脱落叶子。

items.def_zh: 剥夺……的性别特质；阉割，剥夺……的性功能
items.def_en: 1. (archaic or literary) To deprive someone of the qualities, emotions, or roles considered characteristic of their sex. 2. To castrate or sterilize.
items.ex_en: The ruthless queen prayed to dark spirits to unsex her of all remorse.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的王后向黑暗神灵祈求，剥除自己所有柔弱与悔恨的特质。

items.def_en: to surgically remove the testicles or reproductive organs, depriving an organism of sexual reproductive function
items.ex_en: The veterinarian will castrate the young male horse before training begins next month.
items.ex_zh: 兽医将在下个月开始训练前为这匹幼年公马做阉割手术。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the radical transformation of an organism, landscape, or identity by systematically stripping away essential natural attributes such as leaves, sexual identity, or vitality, often through artificial or destructive means.
groups.summary_zh: 剥夺生命体原生的自然机能、叶片或性别特质。
groups.desc_en: Involves forcibly divesting an entity of an essential, defining, or biological attribute, contrasting with benign subtraction by signifying irreversible degradation, neutralization, or barrenness.
groups.desc_zh: 指强行剥夺实体赖以成立的核心特征、活力或生物机能，与普通的“移除、拿走”相对，强调不可逆的削弱、残损或去人性化。
groups.nuance_en: strip of: officially or forcibly deprive of rights, rank, or assets (titles / dignity / citizenship) · emasculate: weaken severely or deprive of masculine virility and power (authority / legislation / confidence) · dehumanize: strip of human qualities, individuality, or compassion (prisoners / victims / workers) · denude: bare a natural surface by stripping vegetative or protective cover (land / hillsides / trees) · defoliate: strip foliage specifically from plants or trees (crops / forests / jungle)
groups.nuance_zh: strip of: 强制剥夺头衔、权利或尊严 (titles / dignity / citizenship) · emasculate: 阉割、严重削弱权威或男子气概 (authority / legislation / confidence) · dehumanize: 剥夺人性使非人化 (prisoners / victims / workers) · denude: 剥光植被或表层覆盖物使之光秃 (land / hillsides / trees) · defoliate: 施药破坏或脱除植物叶片 (crops / forests / jungle)

groups.name: Structural Failure & Inward Fall · 倒塌与塌陷 (Collapse, Cave in, Subside)
groups.tip: 结构失去支撑下陷或坍塌

items.def_en: of ground or a foundation: to sink downward to a lower level
items.ex_en: Extensive underground mining caused the foundation of the old church to subside rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 大面积的地下采矿导致这座老教堂的地基迅速沉降。

items.def_zh: （结构、支撑物）断裂垮塌，支撑不住
items.def_en: of a structure or surface: to break, yield, or buckle suddenly under weight or force
items.ex_en: The rotten wooden floorboards gave way beneath the weight of the heavy machinery.
items.ex_zh: 腐烂的木地板在重型机械的分量下轰然断裂塌陷。

items.def_zh: 塌陷，塌落；使凹陷；（向压力）屈服，让步 (cave in)
items.def_en: To collapse or cause to fall inwards (often cave in); to give in to pressure or demands.
items.ex_en: The abandoned shed's roof caved after heavy winter snow accumulated on top.
items.ex_zh: 废弃棚屋的屋顶在厚重的冬雪积压下向内塌陷了。
items.ex2_en: The heavy mining equipment could cave the unstable underground tunnel walls inwards.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的采矿设备可能会使不稳定的地下隧道墙壁向内坍塌。

items.def_en: of a roof, ceiling, or excavation: to collapse inward toward the center
items.ex_en: Rescue crews rushed to the site when the mine shaft suddenly caved in.
items.ex_zh: 矿井突然向内坍塌时，救援人员迅速赶往了现场。

items.def_en: to collapse or buckle completely under sudden weight, force, or pressure
items.ex_en: The flimsy scaffolding crumpled up completely when struck by the moving excavator.
items.ex_zh: 脆弱的脚手架在被移动的挖掘机撞击后彻底垮塌了。
items.ex2_en: The frustrated writer crumples up another sheet of paper into a tight ball.
items.ex2_zh: 沮丧的作家把另一张稿纸揉成了一个紧实的纸团。

items.def_en: to collapse inward or downward, especially of a roof, ceiling, or ground
items.ex_en: During the intense storm, the decayed ceiling of the library fell in.
items.ex_zh: 在暴风雨肆虐期间，图书馆腐朽的天花板向内塌落了。

items.def_zh: 倒塌，塌陷；崩溃，瓦解；（因病累）倒下；使倒塌；折叠
items.def_en: 1. To fall down suddenly due to loss of support; to completely fail or break down. 2. To cause something to fall down or fold up.
items.ex_en: Faulty engineering caused the multi-story apartment building to collapse into rubble.
items.ex_zh: 工程缺陷导致那栋多层公寓楼轰然倒塌为一堆瓦砾。
items.ex2_en: The demolition crew used controlled explosives to collapse the abandoned concrete factory building.
items.ex2_zh: 拆除队使用定向炸药炸毁塌了那座废弃的水泥工厂厂房。

items.def_zh: （结构或人）受压瘫倒，严重变形压塌
items.def_en: to suddenly collapse inward or buckle under intense pressure or force
items.ex_en: The car hood crumpled upon severe impact with the concrete barrier.
items.ex_zh: 轿车引擎盖在与混凝土护栏猛烈撞击后受压严重变形压塌。
items.ex2_en: She angrily crumpled the rejected job application into a tight paper ball.
items.ex2_zh: 她愤怒地把被拒绝的求职申请表揉成了一个紧实的纸团。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe physical structures, roofs, or ground surfaces giving way inward, downward, or completely under weight, pressure, or loss of support. The distinction lies in whether the failure is a downward buckling (cave in, subside) or a total catastrophic disintegration (collapse, crumple).
groups.summary_zh: 描述建筑物、地表或结构因承重或外力而向内下陷或轰然倒塌。
groups.desc_en: Articulates total loss of internal structural integrity resulting in inward, downward buckling under gravity, contrasting with external demolition by emphasizing inherent mechanical failure.
groups.desc_zh: 指结构因失去内部支撑力而在重力作用下向内凹陷或瓦解坍塌，与外部破坏性的“拆毁”相对，强调本体结构的内向崩溃与陷落。
groups.nuance_en: collapse: completely break down and fall abruptly inward or down (building / bridge / economy) · cave in: buckle inward from the top or sides under overhead weight (roof / tunnel / ceiling) · subside: sink gradually downward to a lower level (ground / foundation / floodwaters) · crumple: compress suddenly into compact folds or writhing heap under impact (car / fender / body)
groups.nuance_zh: collapse: 失去支撑骤然向内整体坍塌 (building / bridge / economy) · cave in: 顶部或侧面因受重压向内凹陷塌方 (roof / tunnel / ceiling) · subside: 结构或地表逐渐下陷沉降 (ground / foundation / floodwaters) · crumple: 因撞击皱缩变形扭曲成一团 (car / fender / body)

groups.name: Subsidize & Fund · 资助与赞助 (Finance, Fund, Underwrite)
groups.tip: 提供财力支持与补贴

items.def_en: to provide the money needed for a particular project, institution, or activity
items.ex_en: The municipal council agreed to fund the construction of a new public park.
items.ex_zh: 市政委员会同意为建设一座新的公共公园提供资金。

items.def_en: to provide the capital, credit, or funds necessary to pay for something
items.ex_en: Private investors stepped forward to finance the development of the innovative solar project.
items.ex_zh: 私人投资者挺身而出，为该创新太阳能项目的研发提供资金支持。

items.def_zh: 赞助，资助；主办，发起；倡议（法案等）
items.def_en: to support an event, activity, or person by providing money or goods; officially organize or propose something
items.ex_en: Several global corporations agreed to sponsor the upcoming international environmental conference.
items.ex_zh: 数家全球跨国企业同意赞助即将召开的国际环境大会。

items.def_zh: 紧急注资救助；经济援助
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to provide financial aid to rescue an organization or individual from collapse
items.ex_en: The wealthy benefactor offered to bail out the failing community arts center.
items.ex_zh: 那位富有的恩人提出注资拯救陷入困境的社区艺术中心。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to supply or pay a sum of money required to support something
items.ex_en: Local businesses agreed to stump up the necessary cash for the festival parade.
items.ex_zh: 当地商家同意掏出举办节日游行所需的必要款项。

items.def_en: to pay part of the cost of something to keep prices low or encourage it to happen; give a subsidy to
items.ex_en: The government will subsidize public transit fares to encourage greener urban commuting.
items.ex_zh: 政府将资助公共交通票价，以鼓励更环保的城市通勤方式。

items.def_en: to provide a large permanent sum of money for an institution, school, or scholarship
items.ex_en: The wealthy alumna decided to endow a prestigious chair in modern literature.
items.ex_zh: 那位富有的女校友决定捐赠设立一个现代文学的特聘讲座教授席位。

items.def_en: to accept financial responsibility for something, agreeing to pay any costs if it fails or loses money
items.ex_en: Wealthy patrons offered to underwrite the immense costs of the exploratory ocean voyage.
items.ex_zh: 富有的资助人表示愿意承保这次远洋勘探航行的巨额费用。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate providing monetary backing, institutional subsidies, or commercial underwriting to support an individual, project, arts event, or enterprise.
groups.summary_zh: 指提供资金、政府财政补贴或商业赞助以支持项目、活动或实体的运作。
groups.desc_en: Centers on providing capital assistance to maintain operations, offset costs, or initiate projects, contrasting with commercial investing by foregrounding non-repayable or protective financial sponsorship.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过拨款、援助等方式提供财力支持以弥补成本或维持运作，与商业“投资”相对，强调兜底性、补贴性或赞助性的资金注入。
groups.nuance_en: fund: provide necessary money for a designated undertaking (project / research / initiative) · subsidize: pay part of the production cost to keep consumer prices low (farmers / transport / industry) · finance: provide large-scale commercial credit or structured capital (acquisition / expansion / deficit) · underwrite: guarantee financial liability or insure against loss (offering / loan / risk) · bail out: rescue financially from imminent insolvency (bank / airline / economy)
groups.nuance_zh: fund: 为特定项目拨付专项款项 (project / research / initiative) · subsidize: 发放财政补贴以平抑成本 (farmers / transport / industry) · finance: 提供大宗商业筹资或信用信贷 (acquisition / expansion / deficit) · underwrite: 承销证券或包揽亏损兜底担保 (offering / loan / risk) · bail out: 紧急注资挽救濒临破产者 (bank / airline / economy)

groups.name: Supervise & Oversee · 监督与监管 (Oversee, Supervise, Monitor)
groups.tip: 居于上位严密督查与把控

items.def_en: to enforce regulations, standards, or agreements in an organization, industry, or group
items.ex_en: Independent inspectors arrived to police the safety standards across chemical manufacturing plants.
items.ex_zh: 独立质检员进驻化工厂，以监督管理各项安全标准的执行。

items.def_en: to observe, record, and check the progress or quality of an activity over a period of time
items.ex_en: Researchers continuously monitor the water quality of the river for hazardous pollutants.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员持续监测该河流的水质，排查有害污染物。

items.def_en: [I/T] (formal) to take responsible managerial care and direction of an organization or enterprise
items.ex_en: The chief engineer was chosen to superintend the construction of the new suspension bridge.
items.ex_zh: 总工程师获选督导这座新悬索桥的全面施工管理。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to guard, protect, and closely supervise someone or something
items.ex_en: She asked her neighbor to watch over the children while she ran an errand.
items.ex_zh: 她外出办事时请邻居照看一下孩子们。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to monitor someone or something carefully and continuously
items.ex_en: The detective hired an assistant to keep tabs on the suspect's daily routines.
items.ex_zh: 侦探雇了一名助手来密切监视嫌疑人的日常行踪。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to investigate or inspect someone to verify they are acting properly or performing duties
items.ex_en: My supervisor dropped by unexpectedly to check up on our progress.
items.ex_zh: 主管出乎意料地过来查看我们的项目进度。

items.def_en: [I/T] to watch and direct someone or an activity to make sure that work is done correctly and safely
items.ex_en: An experienced chemist will supervise the graduate students during their laboratory experiments.
items.ex_zh: 一名资深化学家将在研究生进行实验室实验期间指导并监督他们。

items.def_en: To watch and manage an operation, project, or workforce to ensure it is done properly.
items.ex_en: A committee was formed to oversee the allocation of emergency disaster relief funds.
items.ex_zh: 专门成立了一个委员会来监督应急抗灾救援资金的分配。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe exercising administrative, operational, or regulatory authority by watching over workers, projects, or compliance to ensure standards are met. 'Oversee' emphasizes overarching managerial responsibility, while 'supervise' and 'police' involve closer, hands-on administrative scrutiny.
groups.summary_zh: 行使管理职能以监督人员、项目或法规执行，确保合规与正常运转。
groups.desc_en: Involves maintaining managerial surveillance, accountability, or regulatory oversight over processes and personnel, contrasting with passive 'watching' through vested responsibility and corrective authority.
groups.desc_zh: 指凭借法定职责或管理权限，对人或工作流程实施监视、督导与控制，与普通的“看管”相对，强调管理责任与纠偏权力。
groups.nuance_en: oversee: supervise a complex project or team with ultimate executive responsibility (operations / construction / transition) · supervise: directly manage and direct personnel executing specific tasks (staff / trainees / exams) · monitor: continuously observe and record data to detect variances or compliance (progress / emissions / heart rate) · police: enforce regulatory standards and law observance through inspection (industry / borders / compliance)
groups.nuance_zh: oversee: 统筹把控复杂项目的宏观运行 (operations / construction / transition) · supervise: 在现场直接督导、管理人员操作 (staff / trainees / exams) · monitor: 持续监测数据与状态以及时发现异常 (progress / emissions / heart rate) · police: 巡查监督规章与行业纪律的执行 (industry / borders / compliance)

groups.name: Suppress & Disenfranchise · 镇压与剥夺政治权利 (Quash, Subjugate, Disenfranchise)
groups.tip: 以强权平定骚乱并剥夺选民权利

items.def_en: to forcibly put an end to protests, rebellion, or dissenting speech
items.ex_en: Riot police used tear gas to suppress the escalating street demonstration outside parliament.
items.ex_zh: 防暴警察使用催泪瓦斯镇压了议会外不断升级的街头抗议活动。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to exert strict administrative or physical control to suppress an activity or group
items.ex_en: Authorities plan to clamp down on unlicensed vendors operating around the central square.
items.ex_zh: 有关部门计划严厉限制并取缔在中心广场周边经营的无照摊贩。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to take strong, severe measures to enforce laws or suppress opposition
items.ex_en: The police announced a new campaign to crack down on reckless driving.
items.ex_zh: 警方宣布开展一项新行动，严厉打击危险驾驶行为。

items.def_en: 1. To violently put down or suppress a rebellion, rumor, or opposition. 2. (law) To officially declare a court decision or legal procedure invalid.
items.ex_en: The military commander deployed heavy troops to quash the armed rebellion swiftly.
items.ex_zh: 军事指挥官调集重兵，迅速平息了这场武装叛乱。

items.def_zh: 剥夺……的选举权（或公民权）
items.def_en: To deprive someone of the right to vote or take away their civil liberties and representation.
items.ex_en: Restrictive voting laws will disenfranchise thousands of low-income citizens across the state.
items.ex_zh: 限制性的选举法律将剥夺该州数以千计低收入公民的投票权。

items.def_en: to defeat and gain total political and military dominance over a population
items.ex_en: The ruthless empire sought to subjugate neighbouring nations through continuous military conquests.
items.ex_zh: 残暴的帝国企图通过接连不断的军事征服彻底奴役周边邻国。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to eradicate or suppress rebellion, crime, or dissent completely by forceful means
items.ex_en: Health officials launched a nationwide campaign to stamp out the infectious livestock disease.
items.ex_zh: 卫生官员发起了一场全国性的专项行动，以彻底扑灭该牲畜传染病。

items.def_en: to destroy opposition or uprisings completely and ruthlessly by force
items.ex_en: The dictator ordered the armored division to crush all domestic political opposition.
items.ex_zh: 独裁者命令装甲师彻底粉碎国内所有的政治反对势力。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe state or institutional authorities forcibly crushing political dissent, rebellion, or fundamental civic rights, progressing from stripping legal privileges to absolute, violent subjugation.
groups.summary_zh: 指官方或统治力量镇压反叛势力并剥夺民众政治权利或自由。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the authoritarian use of state or institutional force to crush dissent and abrogate civil standing, contrasting with lawful governing by highlighting coercive subjugation and silencing.
groups.desc_zh: 指运用政权或体制强力扑灭异见、剥夺公民政治权利，与合法的“管制”相对，强调专制强制力、屈服感与政治剥夺。
groups.nuance_en: suppress: forcibly put an end to protests, information, or impulses (rebellion / speech / evidence) · crush: utterly destroy resistance by overwhelming, brutal force (uprising / dissent / opposition) · quash: officially and decisively extinguish an insurrection or legal ruling (rebellion / rumor / conviction) · disenfranchise: deprive of the legal right to vote or marginalize from civic power (voters / minorities / populations) · subjugate: bring a people or territory under total domination and servitude (nation / tribes / population)
groups.nuance_zh: suppress: 强行压制、遏制反叛或言论 (rebellion / speech / evidence) · crush: 以摧枯拉朽的暴力彻底粉碎抵抗 (uprising / dissent / opposition) · quash: 坚决平息叛乱或司法上宣布无效撤销 (rebellion / rumor / conviction) · disenfranchise: 剥夺选举权或公民政治参与资格 (voters / minorities / populations) · subjugate: 征服奴役某族群或国家 (nation / tribes / population)

groups.name: Surface Coating & Cladding · 铺覆饰面与碎石 (Wallpaper, Gravel, Pave)
groups.tip: 在表面铺设贴附面层

items.def_en: to cover a wall or ceiling with flat panels of wood or decorative material
items.ex_en: Craftsmen arrived to panel the executive boardroom walls with fine polished mahogany.
items.ex_zh: 工匠们前来用精美的抛光红木板装潢执行会议室的墙面。

items.def_en: to surface a roadway with compacted layers of small broken stone and tar
items.ex_en: The regional council decided to macadamize the dusty carriage roads between villages.
items.ex_zh: 地区议会决定用碎石铺平村庄之间尘土飞扬的马车道。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cover a natural or prepared ground surface completely with a hard paving layer
items.ex_en: Developers plan to pave over the historic garden to create additional parking spaces.
items.ex_zh: 开发商计划铺砌覆盖掉这座历史悠久的花园，以新建额外的停车位。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to coat or finish a surface entirely with a layer of gravel
items.ex_en: The workers will gravel over the muddy farm path before winter storms arrive.
items.ex_zh: 工人们将在冬季风暴来临前用碎石铺满泥泞的农场小路。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cover a wall surface with wallpaper
items.ex_en: The joint statement merely papered over deep disagreements between the two leaders.
items.ex_zh: 这份联合声明只是粉饰了两位领导人之间的深刻分歧。

items.def_zh: 铺砌（用石块、沥青等铺设路面）
items.def_en: to cover an area of ground or road with concrete, stones, or bricks
items.ex_en: The municipal crew began to pave the old pedestrian alleyway with stone cobbles.
items.ex_zh: 市政施工队开始用鹅卵石铺设这条古老的步行巷道。

items.def_en: To cover the walls of a room with decorative wallpaper.
items.ex_en: We hired a painter to wallpaper the guest bedroom with floral patterns.
items.ex_zh: 我们请了一名粉刷工，给客卧糊上带花卉图案的壁纸。

items.def_zh: 铺碎石于，用沙砾铺设；使困惑，使为难
items.def_en: 1. To cover a path, driveway, or road with gravel. 2. (dated) To confuse or puzzle someone completely.
items.ex_en: The landscaping crew will gravel the winding driveway leading up to the house.
items.ex_zh: 绿化施工队将在这条通向房屋的蜿蜒车道上铺设碎石。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this finishing and infrastructure frame designate dressing structural surfaces—whether interior walls or outdoor walkways—with a uniform decorative or aggregate layer such as wallpaper or loose gravel.
groups.summary_zh: 指在墙面或路面上铺敷装饰壁纸、碎石或硬化面层。
groups.desc_en: Covers applying an engineered, durable top layer or finish over a base substrate, contrasting with mere 'painting' through structural cladding, tiling, or surfacing with rigid materials.
groups.desc_zh: 指在建筑或地面基底上铺筑硬质材料或贴附饰面层，与普通的“涂抹、遮盖”相对，强调结构性附着、硬化与饰面施工。
groups.nuance_en: pave: cover ground with stone, brick, or concrete to create a firm surface (road / courtyard / driveway) · panel: fit a wall or ceiling with discrete sheets of wood or architectural material (walls / ceiling / room) · wallpaper: apply decorative paper sheets onto interior walls (room / bedroom / flat) · gravel: surface a track or driveway with loose crushed rock (path / road / driveway)
groups.nuance_zh: pave: 用砖石、沥青或混凝土硬化铺路 (road / courtyard / driveway) · panel: 镶装木板、护墙板装饰墙面 (walls / ceiling / room) · wallpaper: 裱糊壁纸以装饰内墙 (room / bedroom / flat) · gravel: 用碎石子铺垫路面或通道 (path / road / driveway)

groups.name: Surround & Hem In · 环绕与合围 (Encircle, Compass, Ring)
groups.tip: 从所有侧面包抄环绕

items.def_en: to form a circle around something or someone
items.ex_en: Majestic pine trees ring the crystal waters of the remote mountain lake.
items.ex_zh: 雄伟的松树成环形围绕着偏远高山湖泊的清澈湖水。

items.def_en: to be positioned all around someone or something so as to enclose them
items.ex_en: Dense forests and steep rocky cliffs surround the ancient medieval castle completely.
items.ex_zh: 茂密的森林和陡峭的岩壁完全包围了这座古老的中世纪城堡。

items.def_en: to surround someone or something closely so that they cannot move or escape freely
items.ex_en: Tall concrete walls and barbed wire hem in the occupants on every side.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的混凝土围墙和带刺铁丝网从四面八方将里面的人严密禁锢。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to move nearer from surrounding positions so as to trap someone or something
items.ex_en: Law enforcement officers quietly closed in on the hideout from surrounding rooftops.
items.ex_zh: 执法人员从周围的屋顶悄然向藏匿点合围逼近。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround someone or something completely so that movement or escape is impossible
items.ex_en: My car was boxed in by two huge delivery trucks, and I couldn't pull out.
items.ex_zh: 我的车被两辆大卡车死死卡在中间，根本开不出来。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to surround an area or target with barriers, enclosing it on all sides
items.ex_en: The farmer worked all afternoon to fence in the vast sheep pasture.
items.ex_zh: 农夫忙活了整个下午，用栅栏围住了那片广袤的羊群牧场。

items.def_zh: 包围，环绕；达到，实现；图谋
items.def_en: 1. (literary or archaic) To surround or encircle completely. 2. (formal or archaic) To achieve or accomplish a purpose. 3. (archaic) To plot or scheme.
items.ex_en: Dark towering clouds compass the lonely watchtower as the severe thunderstorm approaches.
items.ex_zh: 狂暴的雷雨逼近之际，乌黑翻腾的阴云将孤独的瞭望塔团团环绕。

items.def_en: 1. To surround someone or something completely in a circle.
items.ex_en: A protective stone moat and high ramparts encircle the historic imperial palace.
items.ex_zh: 一条防护性的石头护城河与高耸的堡垒环绕着这座历史悠久的皇宫。

groups.summary_en: Entities or topological features arrange themselves along the entire perimeter of a target, closing off boundaries or forming an unbroken perimeter. Verbs differ primarily in register and spatial nuance, from literary and archaic spatial bounding (compass) to geometric positioning (encircle) and defensive confinement (ring, hem in).
groups.summary_zh: 指事物或群落沿周边排列形成闭合圈，将其环绕或圈禁在内。
groups.desc_en: Depicts forming a continuous enclosing boundary around a target to trap, isolate, or restrict egress, contrasting with passive 'bordering' by asserting containment, siege, or encirclement.
groups.desc_zh: 指在目标周围形成闭合圈以实施围堵、孤立或切断退路，与静态的“毗邻、边缘”相对，强调合围、封锁与压迫性束缚。
groups.nuance_en: surround: extend all the way around something on every side (building / city / enemy) · encircle: form a distinct physical or tactical circle enclosing a target (troops / island / waist) · hem in: trap within tight, constricting limits preventing escape (forces / vehicles / fleet) · ring: enclose with an unbroken circular border or cordon (trees / police / stadium) · box in: restrict movement completely on all sides as if in a crate (car / opponent / defender)
groups.nuance_zh: surround: 从各侧面完整包围、环抱 (building / city / enemy) · encircle: 形成闭合圈战术包围或环绕 (troops / island / waist) · hem in: 紧紧合围困于狭小空间使其无法动弹 (forces / vehicles / fleet) · ring: 呈环状警戒线式密闭围护 (trees / police / stadium) · box in: 四面卡位封堵去路如置箱中 (car / opponent / defender)

groups.name: Sway & Lose Balance Drunkenly · 摇晃与步履踉跄 (Reel, Stagger)
groups.tip: 步履不稳左右摇摆晃动

items.def_en: to move unsteadily from side to side showing poor physical equilibrium
items.ex_en: The exhausted toddler began to wobble unsteadily across the thick wool rug.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦不堪的幼童迈着不稳的脚步，东倒西歪地走过厚厚的羊毛地毯。
items.ex2_en: Strong autumn winds will wobble the fragile decorative wooden fence along the lawn.
items.ex2_zh: 强烈的秋风会使草坪边脆弱的木制装饰栅栏摇晃不定。

items.def_zh: 摇摇欲坠地走；颤巍巍走动
items.def_en: to move with weak, unsteady, trembling steps as if about to fall
items.ex_en: The fragile elderly man tottered down the steep stairs with a wooden cane.
items.ex_zh: 那位虚弱的老人拄着木拐杖，颤巍巍地走下了陡峭的台阶。

items.def_en: to step backward unsteadily and sway from shock, dizziness, or a blow
items.ex_en: Struck by the sudden impact, the boxer reeled back against the elastic ropes.
items.ex_zh: 受到猛烈一击后，拳击手摇晃着踉跄后退，撞在了弹性围绳上。

items.def_zh: 踉跄独行；摇摇晃晃前行
items.def_en: to walk forward with clumsy, unsteady, wobbling steps
items.ex_en: The weary hiker stumbled along the dark mountain trail toward the distant light.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的徒步者摇摇晃晃地在黑暗的山间小路上独行，朝远处的亮光走去。

items.def_en: to walk or move unsteadily in an irregular, zigzagging course like a drunkard
items.ex_en: After leaving the tavern, the drunken patron began to weave around the crowded sidewalk.
items.ex_zh: 离开酒馆后，那位醉汉在拥挤的人行道上醉步蹒跚地摇晃行进。

items.def_zh: 摇晃，踉跄，蹒跚；感到眩晕，发昏；卷，绕
items.def_en: 1. To stagger or move unsteadily as if about to fall, or to feel dizzy and overwhelmed. 2. To wind something onto a reel.
items.ex_en: Dizzied by the sudden blow, the injured fighter reeled across the wooden ring.
items.ex_zh: 被突然的一击打得头晕目眩，受伤的拳手在木质拳台内踉跄摇晃。

items.def_zh: 摇晃，蹒跚，踉跄；使震动，使大吃一惊；错开，交错安排
items.def_en: 1. To walk or move unsteadily as if about to fall. 2. To shock or astonish someone deeply. 3. To arrange things so they happen at different times.
items.ex_en: Weak from severe dehydration, the lost traveler staggered toward the desert oasis.
items.ex_zh: 由于严重脱水而虚弱不堪，迷路的行者蹒跚着朝沙漠绿洲走去。

items.def_zh: 猛然前倾颠簸；歪斜晃动
items.def_en: to make an abrupt, uncontrolled, and unsteady movement forward or sideways
items.ex_en: The drunk man lurched toward the counter, nearly knocking over a bar stool.
items.ex_zh: 那个醉汉猛然歪斜着晃向吧台，差点撞倒了一张高脚凳。

groups.summary_en: This frame involves uncoordinated, swinging steps caused by dizziness, severe intoxication, physical blows, or intense shock. 'Stagger' highlights unsteadiness with sudden stumbling steps to keep from falling, while 'reel' accents spinning disorientation and swaying wildly backward or sideways.
groups.summary_zh: 指因眩晕、受击或醉酒而失去平衡，身体剧烈晃动、步履不稳。
groups.desc_en: Describes unsteady, erratic bodily equilibrium involving drunken or dazed stumbling, contrasting with smooth directional movement by highlighting vestibular disruption and impending falls.
groups.desc_zh: 指因眩晕、醉酒或重击导致前庭失衡而产生的虚浮、歪斜步伐，与平稳行走相对，强调身体摇摇欲坠的失衡态。
groups.nuance_en: stagger: walk unsteadily with wide, clumsy strides as if about to fall (drunkenly / blind / forward) · reel: lurch backward or sideways dizzily from a blow or shock (backward / shock / blow) · lurch: make an abrupt, uncontrolled rolling pitch or sudden staggering jerk (forward / corridor / deck) · totter: walk with feeble, shaky, trembling steps like a frail elder or infant (steps / heels / legs) · wobble: move with uneven, trembling side-to-side oscillations (knees / wheels / legs)
groups.nuance_zh: stagger: 步履蹒跚、踉踉跄跄似要摔倒 (drunkenly / blind / forward) · reel: 受打击后眩晕退缩、摇晃站立不稳 (backward / shock / blow) · lurch: 猛然失去平衡向一侧歪斜倾晃 (forward / corridor / deck) · totter: 步态虚浮颤巍地蹒跚小步走 (steps / heels / legs) · wobble: 左右摇摆晃动、颤颤巍巍 (knees / wheels / legs)

groups.name: Swerve & Veer · 突然偏转与改变方向 (Change Direction Abruptly)
groups.tip: 行进中突然拐弯或偏离

items.def_en: [I/T] to turn or move smoothly or suddenly in a new direction
items.ex_en: The driver swung the wheel hard to enter the narrow side alley.
items.ex_zh: 司机猛打方向盘，使车子急转弯拐进了狭窄的侧巷。
items.ex2_en: The rusty iron gate swung shut loudly when the cold wind blew.
items.ex2_zh: 当冷风吹过时，生锈的铁门砰的一声猛然关上了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to suddenly move or cause to move at an angle from a straight path
items.ex_en: The speeding sports car skewed wildly across the slick road before stopping.
items.ex_zh: 那辆超速跑车在湿滑的路面上猛烈斜向打滑，随后停了下来。
items.ex2_en: Biased survey questions can skew the statistical results of the sociological study.
items.ex2_zh: 带有偏见的调查问题会歪曲这项社会学研究的统计结果。

items.def_zh: 急转避让；突然偏转方向
items.def_en: to make a sudden, sharp directional shift away from someone or something
items.ex_en: The running back cut away sharply to evade the charging linebacker.
items.ex_zh: 跑卫突然敏捷地急转避让，躲过了冲撞过来的线卫。

items.def_en: to turn aside abruptly and sharply, especially to avoid a collision
items.ex_en: The cyclist swerved away just in time to avoid the opening car door.
items.ex_zh: 骑车人及时急拐避开，才没有撞上突然打开的车门。

items.def_en: to change direction abruptly and turn away from an original path
items.ex_en: The delivery van veered off the main road onto a rough gravel track.
items.ex_zh: 那辆送货车突然偏离主干道，拐上了一条崎岖的碎石小径。

items.def_en: (+ away/off) To suddenly change course or turn away sharply, especially in order to avoid an obstacle.
items.ex_en: The frightened warship sheered off into the mist to avoid the hidden reef.
items.ex_zh: 惊慌的战舰急转偏离航向驶入迷雾，以避开暗礁。

items.def_en: to change direction suddenly, especially when moving at speed
items.ex_en: The motorcycle veered violently to the left to miss an oncoming truck.
items.ex_zh: 摩托车猛地向左急转弯，避开了一辆迎面驶来的卡车。

items.def_zh: 急转弯，突然转向；背离，偏离；使急转
items.def_en: To change direction abruptly, especially while moving fast to avoid hitting something; to cause a vehicle to turn aside.
items.ex_en: She swerved into the opposite lane to avoid hitting a stray deer.
items.ex_zh: 她猛打方向盘切入对向车道，以避免撞上一只迷途的鹿。
items.ex2_en: The quick driver swerved the steering wheel sharply to avoid the pedestrian.
items.ex2_zh: 敏捷的司机猛打方向盘以避开横穿马路的行人。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe a moving vehicle, person, or object abruptly deviating from a straight path, often to avoid an obstacle or under sudden external force. While 'veer' suggests a sharp shift in course, 'swerve' emphasizes an evasive, often jerky turn.
groups.summary_zh: 指移动物体或人突然变向或急转，多为躲避障碍。
groups.desc_en: Signifies a rapid, abrupt angular departure from an established heading, contrasting with continuous gradual 'turning' by emphasizing suddenness, evasion, or sudden shift in trajectory.
groups.desc_zh: 指行驶或前进轨迹发生突然、剧烈的锐角变向，与平缓自然的“拐弯”相对，强调应对突发状况时的急转、偏离或规避。
groups.nuance_en: swerve: turn aside sharply and abruptly, often to avoid an obstacle (traffic / road / car) · veer: shift course or direction gradually or sharply due to force or whim (off course / wind / conversation) · sheer: swerve suddenly away from a course, especially a nautical or aerial path (away / clear / off) · skew: distort or suddenly bias away from an aligned trajectory or balance (data / perspective / results)
groups.nuance_zh: swerve: 骤然猛打方向以闪避障碍 (traffic / road / car) · veer: 改变航向或谈话风向发生急转偏离 (off course / wind / conversation) · sheer: （航行中）猛然急转偏航躲开危险 (away / clear / off) · skew: 歪斜偏离原定基准线或产生偏倚 (data / perspective / results)

groups.name: Swing & Sway · 摆动与波动 (Oscillate, Ripple, Sway)
groups.tip: 如涟漪般起伏泛起波纹

items.def_en: Move rhythmically and continuously from one side to the other
items.ex_en: The tall pine branches began to sway back and forth in the wind.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的松树枝条开始在风中富有节奏地来回摇曳。

items.def_en: Move or pivot around a central point in a smooth, sweeping curve
items.ex_en: The crane operator swung around the heavy steel beam toward the waiting workers.
items.ex_zh: 起重机操作员将沉重的钢梁摆转过去，送向等候的工人们。
items.ex2_en: The security camera swung around automatically to film the suspicious dark alleyway.
items.ex2_zh: 监控摄像头自动旋转转向，对准拍摄可疑的黑暗小巷。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move slowly from side to side or backward and forward, typically rooted at the base
items.ex_en: The heavy stalks of wheat swayed gently under the warm summer breeze.
items.ex_zh: 沉甸甸的麦穗在温暖的夏日微风中轻轻摇摆。
items.ex2_en: Emotional political speeches can easily sway undecided voters during an intense election.
items.ex2_zh: 充满激情的政治演说在激烈选举中很容易左右动摇摇摆选民。

items.def_zh: 起微波，起涟漪；如波浪般翻滚；（在…中）扩散，传开
items.def_en: 1. to move in small waves, or to cause the surface of something to do this. 2. to spread gradually through a person, group, or place like a wave
items.ex_en: A subtle shudder rippled across the tranquil surface of the mountain lake.
items.ex_zh: 一阵微弱的震颤如波浪般在高山湖泊宁静的水面上荡漾开来。
items.ex2_en: A sudden morning breeze rippled the calm surface of the mountain lake.
items.ex2_zh: 清晨突如其来的微风吹拂着平静的高山湖面泛起阵阵涟漪。

items.def_en: to move with a continuous smooth, wavelike motion
items.ex_en: The golden grasslands undulated gracefully beneath the sweeping gusts of morning wind.
items.ex_zh: 金色的草原在清晨阵阵长风的吹拂下呈优美的波浪形起伏。
items.ex2_en: The rhythmic electronic beat undulated the cheering crowd during the music festival.
items.ex2_zh: 有节奏的电子节拍让音乐节上欢呼的人群如波浪般起伏晃动。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move back and forth or in an arc while suspended from an axis or pivot point
items.ex_en: An ornate pendulum clock swung silently against the dimly lit parlor wall.
items.ex_zh: 一座华丽的钟摆钟在光线昏暗的客厅墙上静静地左右摆动。
items.ex2_en: The athletic gymnast swung his muscular body across the parallel bars effortlessly.
items.ex2_zh: 体格健壮的体操运动员毫不费力地在双杠上摆动着身躯。

items.def_en: to rise and fall irregularly in number, level, or physical position
items.ex_en: The patient's blood pressure began to fluctuate unpredictably throughout the night.
items.ex_zh: 整夜之间，患者的血压开始出现不可预测的剧烈上下波动。

items.def_zh: 摆动，振荡；（在两种观点、情感之间）摇摆不定
items.def_en: 1. to move repeatedly from one position to another and back again at a regular speed. 2. to keep changing between two extreme opinions, moods, or states
items.ex_en: The metal needle oscillated between positive and negative readings on the gauge.
items.ex_zh: 仪表上的金属指针在正负读数之间有规律地往复摆动。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote continuous, wave-like, or back-and-forth physical motion around a pivot or across a surface. While 'oscillate' denotes periodic pendulum-like or electronic alternation, 'ripple' captures outward spreading surface undulations.
groups.summary_zh: 指物体绕定点往复摆动或沿表面呈波浪状起伏扩散。
groups.desc_en: Embodies rhythmic, periodic back-and-forth or wave-like kinetic cycles, contrasting with static rest or unidirectional flow by emphasizing alternating oscillation around an axis.
groups.desc_zh: 指绕轴心或基线进行的周期性往复摆动或波状运动，与静止或单向流动相对，强调往返交替的摇曳与波动。
groups.nuance_en: swing: move back and forth while suspended from an axis (pendulum / arms / gate) · sway: lean rhythmically from side to side without fixed pivot (trees / hips / crowd) · oscillate: vary systematically back and forth between two limits or states (pendulum / prices / needle) · fluctuate: rise and fall irregularly without stable rhythm (temperatures / rates / moods) · undulate: move with smooth, rolling, wave-like crests and troughs (hills / surface / grass)
groups.nuance_zh: swing: 悬垂或固定于一点的前后弧形摆动 (pendulum / arms / gate) · sway: 底座固定或直立物的整体节律性左右摇晃 (trees / hips / crowd) · oscillate: 在两个极限状态或数值间机械摆动 (pendulum / prices / needle) · fluctuate: 指标或情绪无规则地上下剧烈波动 (temperatures / rates / moods) · undulate: 像波浪起伏般呈平滑波状起伏 (hills / surface / grass)

groups.name: Systemic & Spatial Relocation · 移位与转置 (Translocate, Relocate, Reposition)
groups.tip: 改变空间位置或方向挪动

items.def_en: (chess) to make a special move shifting the king two squares toward a rook and placing that rook on the square the king has just crossed.
items.ex_en: Anticipating the coming attack, the grandmaster quietly castled to secure his king.
items.ex_zh: 预料到即将到来的猛攻，这位国际象棋特级大师悄然王车易位以护卫国王。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Move objects or personnel around to different positions or configurations
items.ex_en: We had to shift around several heavy desks to accommodate new team members.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不挪动几张沉重的办公桌，以便容纳新团队成员。
items.ex2_en: The furniture shifted around during the rough voyage across the stormy sea.
items.ex2_zh: 在穿越风暴海域的颠簸航行中，家具四处挪动。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) Change position or relocate slightly to make space or reconfigure
items.ex_en: Could you move over a bit so another person can sit down?
items.ex_zh: 你能稍微往旁边挪一下腾点空间，好让另一个人坐下吗？
items.ex2_en: Please move the chair over to make room for our guest.
items.ex2_zh: 请把椅子挪过去一点，给我们的客人腾出空间。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move to a new place or establish something in a new location
items.ex_en: The pharmaceutical corporation decided to relocate its headquarters to a smaller city.
items.ex_zh: 这家制药公司决定将其总部迁移到一个规模较小的城市。
items.ex2_en: Many tech startups relocated to smaller towns to avoid high city taxes.
items.ex2_zh: 许多科技初创公司搬迁到小城镇以避开高昂的城市税收。

items.def_en: to change the physical position or strategic orientation of something
items.ex_en: The artillery commander ordered the unit to reposition the cannons before dawn.
items.ex_zh: 炮兵指挥官命令该部队在拂晓前重新调整大炮的阵位。

items.def_en: to cause two or more things to change places with each other
items.ex_en: The editor accidentally transposed two paragraphs during the late stages of production.
items.ex_zh: 编辑在制作后期不小心将两个段落互换了位置。

items.def_en: to assign troops, resources, or workers to a new position or task
items.ex_en: The general chose to redeploy reserve battalions along the vulnerable northern border.
items.ex_zh: 将军选择将预备营重新部署在脆弱的北部边境沿线。

items.def_zh: 使移位，迁移（动植物等）；发生易位
items.def_en: (biology, ecology) to move or be moved from one place to another, especially of plants, animals, or genetic material.
items.ex_en: Conservationists worked tirelessly to translocate the endangered rhinos to a safer sanctuary.
items.ex_zh: 环保人士不知疲倦地工作，将濒危犀牛迁移至更安全的保护区。
items.ex2_en: Rare native plants translocated successfully to the neighboring island over several decades.
items.ex2_zh: 数十年来，稀有本土植物成功迁移并定居于邻近岛屿。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent deliberate, systematic movement or positional exchange of objects, elements, or personnel from one place or configuration to another, often within a formal, scientific, or rule-governed system.
groups.summary_zh: 在规则系统、科学语境或组织内部进行有序的空间转置与重新定位。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the strategic or structural realignment of assets, personnel, or elements to new coordinates, contrasting with casual 'moving' by highlighting systemic coordination or revised deployment.
groups.desc_zh: 指在系统或空间架构内对人员、设施或要素进行有目的的重新编排与移位，与日常的“搬动”相对，强调系统性与战略重构。
groups.nuance_en: relocate: move an entire enterprise, home, or institution to a new location (headquarters / plant / family) · reposition: adjust the stance, market posture, or spatial alignment of an entity (brand / troops / patient) · transpose: swap the relative places or order of two things (digits / words / letters) · redeploy: transfer military forces or organizational resources to a new task (troops / capital / assets) · translocate: shift biological molecules or elements from one site to another (proteins / gene / population)
groups.nuance_zh: relocate: 整体搬迁机构、企业或家庭驻地 (headquarters / plant / family) · reposition: 调整定位、阵位或市场姿态 (brand / troops / patient) · transpose: 颠倒或置换两者的相对位置与顺序 (digits / words / letters) · redeploy: 重新调配部署军队、资金等资源 (troops / capital / assets) · translocate: （生物学）使染色体片段或物质发生转位 (proteins / gene / population)

groups.name: Tactical Assault & Direct Fire · 进攻与交火 (Enfilade, Counterstrike, Engage)
groups.tip: 战场上的主动突击与炮火交锋

items.def_en: to open fire on or begin fighting an enemy unit or aircraft
items.ex_en: The destroyer received immediate authorization to engage the incoming hostile aircraft.
items.ex_zh: 该驱逐舰获得了立即向来袭敌机开火交战的授权。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to begin shooting heavily with firearms or artillery at a target
items.ex_en: The squad hidden in the tree line suddenly opened up on us.
items.ex_zh: 潜伏在树林线中的小队突然向我们猛烈开火。

items.def_en: to return gunfire in response to an attack
items.ex_en: The spokesperson fired back at critics with recent economic data.
items.ex_zh: 发言人用最新的经济数据迅速回击了批评者。

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to adjust aim or projectile fire directly onto an enemy position
items.ex_en: The sniper slowly zeroed in on the enemy radio operator across town.
items.ex_zh: 狙击手慢慢校准瞄准镜，锁定了穿过城镇的敌军无线电操作员。

items.def_en: to attack an enemy position continuously with large guns or bombs
items.ex_en: Heavy artillery batteries bombarded the fortified bunker complex for three continuous days.
items.ex_zh: 重炮部队连续三天不断炮击那座加固的地堡设施群。

items.def_en: to attack ground targets repeatedly with machine-gun fire from low-flying aircraft
items.ex_en: Fighter jets swooped down low to strafe retreating enemy armored convoys.
items.ex_zh: 战斗机低空俯冲而下，反复扫射撤退中的敌军装甲车队。

items.def_en: To launch an attack in response to an enemy's assault; retaliate with military force.
items.ex_en: Allied forces prepared to counterstrike after enduring weeks of unrelenting missile attacks.
items.ex_zh: 盟军在承受了数周无情的导弹袭击后，准备发起强力反击。

items.def_zh: （以纵射火力）射击，向……实施纵射
items.def_en: (military) To direct gunfire along the entire length of an enemy trench, line of troops, or position.
items.ex_en: From the flanking ridge, machine gunners enfiladed the exposed enemy trenchline.
items.ex_zh: 机枪手从侧翼的山脊上居高临下，对暴露无遗的敌方战壕实施纵射。

groups.summary_en: Combatants initiate or retaliate with coordinated military force or projectile fire targeting opposing positions, ranging from retaliatory strikes to sweeping gunfire angles.
groups.summary_zh: 作战双方发起战术突击、还击或火力扫射，侧重交战与射击动作。
groups.desc_en: Captures initiating offensive kinetic contact, heavy ordnance delivery, or direct firing upon hostile forces, contrasting with defensive maneuvering by emphasizing deliberate lethality and tactical assault.
groups.desc_zh: 指以重火力对敌对目标主动实施压制性打击或近距离接敌交火，与防守机动相对，强调战术突击、倾泻弹药与直接杀伤。
groups.nuance_en: engage: enter into active combat or close tactical contact with an enemy (targets / enemy / force) · bombard: attack continuously with heavy artillery shells, bombs, or missiles (fort / city / coastline) · strafe: attack ground targets with continuous low-flying aircraft machine gunfire (column / convoy / troops) · counterstrike: launch a retaliatory offensive immediately following an attack (positions / bases / forces) · enfilade: rake a hostile line with swept gunfire along its entire longitudinal length (flank / trench / position)
groups.nuance_zh: engage: 与敌军正式接战或锁定目标交火 (targets / enemy / force) · bombard: 实施高密度的密集炮轰或轰炸 (fort / city / coastline) · strafe: 战机超低空扫射地面部队 (column / convoy / troops) · counterstrike: 遭袭后实施快速反击作战 (positions / bases / forces) · enfilade: 沿敌阵地侧翼进行纵射扫射 (flank / trench / position)

groups.name: Tactical Deception & Swindling · 虚招与诈取 (Feint, Diddle, Outmaneuver)
groups.tip: 运用假动作或诡计蒙蔽对手

items.def_en: (+ sb + into sth/doing sth) Persuade or trick someone into doing something through deceit
items.ex_en: The fraudulent broker conned my uncle into liquidating his entire pension.
items.ex_zh: 那个诈骗经纪人诱骗我叔叔将全部养老金变现。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Cheat someone financially by charging too much or swindling them
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_zh: 诱骗，欺蒙（以巧妙手段惑人）
items.def_en: (+ into) to charm, divert, or mislead someone strategically or deceitfully
items.ex_en: The cunning spy beguiled the young diplomat into revealing state secrets.
items.ex_zh: 狡猾的间谍巧施诱骗，蒙蔽了那位年轻外交官以获取国家机密。

items.def_en: 1. (+ at) To make a deceptive movement or pretended attack to distract or mislead an opponent.
items.ex_en: The boxer feinted to the left before landing an unexpected right hook.
items.ex_zh: 拳击手先向左虚晃一枪，随后出其不意地打出一记右勾拳。

items.def_en: 1. (+ out of) (informal) To cheat or swindle someone, especially out of money. 2. ('diddle around') To waste time doing silly or useless things.
items.ex_en: The shady mechanic diddled her out of three hundred dollars for repairs.
items.ex_zh: 那个不良修理工通过维修欺诈骗取了她三百美元。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Dishonestly arrange circumstances so that someone is framed or deceived
items.ex_en: The corrupt officer stitched up an innocent bystander to close the case.
items.ex_zh: 那个腐败警官设计陷害了一名无辜的旁观者以迅速结案。

items.def_en: (+ out of/into) to trick someone into giving money or property by winning their confidence
items.ex_en: He conned several elderly investors out of their life savings through fraud.
items.ex_zh: 他通过欺诈手段从几位老年投资者那里骗取了毕生积蓄。

items.def_zh: 欺诈，行骗（法律层面谋利）
items.def_en: (+ of) to illegally obtain money or property from someone through deliberate deception
items.ex_en: The corrupt executive was prosecuted for attempting to defraud the company's shareholders.
items.ex_zh: 这名腐败的高管因企图欺诈公司股东而遭到起诉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to misleading an adversary or counterparty through deceptive maneuvers, fraudulent tricks, or deliberate misdirection to gain an unfair advantage or swindle them.
groups.summary_zh: 通过战术佯攻或欺诈手段迷惑对手以谋取利益。
groups.desc_en: Denotes outwitting or bilking a mark through psychological manipulation, feigned intent, or fraudulent tricks, contrasting with honest competition or outright theft through deceptive artifice.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过虚假声势、心理圈套或诈术骗取钱财或取得战术优势，与正当竞争或明抢相对，强调欺诈手法与计谋诱导。
groups.nuance_en: defraud: illegally obtain money or property by deliberate deception (investors / revenue / bank) · con: swindle a victim through gaining trust and deceitful pitches (tourists / marks / buyers) · feint: make a distracting mock attack or deceptive body movement (left / jab / attack) · beguile: charm, enchant, or mislead someone subtly into compliance (audience / victims / prey) · rip off: blatantly overcharge or cheat someone out of money (consumers / tourists / patrons)
groups.nuance_zh: defraud: 经由精心构陷在法律上欺诈财物 (investors / revenue / bank) · con: 利用建立信任的方式行骗诱导 (tourists / marks / buyers) · feint: 做出佯攻以声东击西 (left / jab / attack) · beguile: 巧言令色蛊惑引诱或蒙蔽 (audience / victims / prey) · rip off: 敲竹杠或宰客以获取暴利 (consumers / tourists / patrons)

groups.name: Tailor & Condition to Specs · 驯化与定制调适 (Condition, Individualize, Tailor)
groups.tip: 按需调整以适应环境

items.def_en: (+ sth) Design, modify, or tailor something to suit a specific purpose or group
items.ex_en: This new coding curriculum is specifically geared toward high school beginners.
items.ex_zh: 这门新的编程课程专门针对高中初学者进行了调整定制。

items.def_en: to adapt or make something specifically suited for a particular person or need
items.ex_en: We can tailor the training program to meet your company's operational needs.
items.ex_zh: 我们可以量身定制该培训计划，以满足贵公司的运营需求。

items.def_en: to modify something to suit a particular individual or task
items.ex_en: The mechanic can customize this standard motorcycle to fit your riding style.
items.ex_zh: 机械师可以按需改装这辆标准摩托车，以契合你的骑行习惯。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Adapt or condition something precisely to meet individual requirements
items.ex_en: The personal trainer tailored the exercise regime to her specific physical limitations.
items.ex_zh: 私人教练针对她特殊的身体局限，量身定制了锻炼方案。

items.def_zh: 训练，使适应，使习惯于；调节，改善（发质、皮肤或空气等的状态）
items.def_en: 1. to train or accustom a person or animal to behave or think in a particular way 2. to improve the condition of hair, skin, air, or other materials
items.ex_en: Rigorous military training conditions recruits to remain calm under extreme combat pressure.
items.ex_zh: 严苛的军事训练训练新兵在极端的战斗压力下保持冷静。

items.def_en: to make someone or something accustomed to a particular condition through exposure
items.ex_en: Repeated exposure gradually habituated the laboratory rats to the loud sudden noises.
items.ex_zh: 反复的暴露逐渐使实验室大鼠适应了突然出现的巨大噪音。

items.def_zh: 使个性化，使适应个别需要；赋予……个人特色
items.def_en: to modify or adapt something to suit the special needs or character of a particular individual
items.ex_en: The specialized clinic seeks to individualize treatment plans for every cancer patient.
items.ex_zh: 这家专科诊所致力于为每位癌症患者提供个性化的治疗方案。

items.def_en: to adapt or become accustomed to a new climate or environment
items.ex_en: Mountaineers rested for two days at base camp to acclimate properly.
items.ex_zh: 登山者在大本营休整了两天，以便充分适应高空气候。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote modifying, training, or customizing an organism, mind, product, or process so that it fits a distinct physiological state, individual recipient, or contextual requirement.
groups.summary_zh: 通过训练、驯化或定制使之适应特定个体或机能状态。
groups.desc_en: Refers to intentionally reshaping, modifying, or training an entity to fit specific physiological, environmental, or personal requirements, contrasting with generic processing by stressing calibrated optimization.
groups.desc_zh: 指为适应特定受众需求、环境或规格，对事物进行定制剪裁或通过训练促成适应，与泛化的加工相对，强调量身定做与定向驯化。
groups.nuance_en: tailor: adapt or modify something precisely for a particular purpose or person (approach / message / policy) · customize: build or alter according to individual personal specifications (software / settings / car) · condition: train a person or animal to behave in a specified way through habit (reflexes / muscles / behavior) · acclimate: adapt physiologically or psychologically to a new climate or environment (body / recruits / plants) · individualize: adapt instructions or care specifically to single persons (treatment / instruction / care)
groups.nuance_zh: tailor: 为契合特定目标量身裁衣式调整 (approach / message / policy) · customize: 依据客户规格个性化定制产品 (software / settings / car) · condition: 通过反复训练或刺激形成条件反射 (reflexes / muscles / behavior) · acclimate: 逐步服水土、适应新环境气候 (body / recruits / plants) · individualize: 针对个体差异实施个性化施教或治疗 (treatment / instruction / care)

groups.name: Taint & Desecrate · 玷污与亵渎 (Sully, Defile, Desecrate)
groups.tip: 由纯洁被玷污升级到亵渎神圣

items.def_en: to contaminate or affect something slightly with an undesirable quality
items.ex_en: The ongoing bribery scandal tainted the minister's otherwise spotless political reputation.
items.ex_zh: 持续发酵的受贿丑闻给这位部长原本无可挑剔的政治声誉染上了污点。

items.def_en: to corrupt the moral purity or physical cleanliness of something
items.ex_en: Greed and unchecked ambition can completely pollute a person's moral compass.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪和不受约束的野心会彻底玷污一个人的道德准则。

items.def_en: to damage the purity, integrity, or reputation of something previously clean
items.ex_en: Unfounded rumors threatened to sully the family's ancient, honorable lineage forever.
items.ex_zh: 毫无根据的谣言大有永久玷污该家族古老而尊贵血统之势。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Spoil, corrupt, or make something dirty or impure
items.ex_en: One dishonest employee managed to foul up the team's entire hard reputation.
items.ex_zh: 一名不诚实的员工搞糟了团队好不容易建立起来的声誉。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Degrade, sully, or bring disgrace to someone's name or reputation (as in dragging through the mud)
items.ex_en: Political rivals tried to drag her respected name through the mud online.
items.ex_zh: 政治对手企图在网络上抹黑并玷污她受人尊敬的名声。

items.def_zh: 玷污，亵渎，糟蹋；（狭路中）以纵队前进
items.def_en: 1. To spoil, pollute, or treat something pure or sacred with great disrespect. 2. (of troops) To march in a narrow line or single file.
items.ex_en: The invading vandals defiled the sacred temple by smashing centuries-old ancestral relics.
items.ex_zh: 入侵的破坏者砸碎了数百年历史的祖先遗物，亵渎了这座神圣的寺庙。

items.def_en: to treat something sacred with irreverence, disrespect, or abuse
items.ex_en: Trespassers profaned the ancient cathedral by spray-painting crude obscenities on altar stones.
items.ex_zh: 侵入者在祭坛石上喷涂粗俗秽语，亵渎了这座古老的大教堂。

items.def_zh: 亵渎，玷污，糟蹋（圣物或圣地）
items.def_en: To damage or treat a sacred place, grave, or holy object with deliberate disrespect.
items.ex_en: Hooligans desecrated several sacred graves in the historic cemetery last midnight.
items.ex_zh: 昨晚半夜，不良分子亵渎并破坏了那座历史公墓里的几处圣墓。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures moral corruption and sacrilege, scaling from marring purity or reputation to outright physical or ritual desecration of sacred, inviolable sites or objects.
groups.summary_zh: 从玷污名誉洁白递进到严重污损、亵渎神圣场所与宗教圣物。
groups.desc_en: Depicts corrupting moral purity, sacred value, or pristine integrity through profane violation or pollution, contrasting with physical damage by highlighting symbolic and moral defilement.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过玷污、亵渎或不洁行为破坏事物在道德、精神或神圣层面的纯洁性，与物理损坏相对，强调象征性与道德性的玷辱。
groups.nuance_en: desecrate: violate the sanctity of a sacred place, object, or grave (graves / temple / altar) · profane: treat sacred things with irreverence, contempt, or vulgarity (sanctuary / religion / rites) · defile: ruin the purity or sanctity of something revered or clean (temple / reputation / purity) · sully: tarnish an untarnished moral reputation or clean state (reputation / name / honor) · taint: contaminate subtly with an undesirable, rotten, or corrupt quality (evidence / food / legacy)
groups.nuance_zh: desecrate: 粗暴践踏、亵渎宗教圣物或陵墓 (graves / temple / altar) · profane: 亵渎神圣事物、视圣物为粗俗 (sanctuary / religion / rites) · defile: 彻底污损名节、圣洁或纯真 (temple / reputation / purity) · sully: 玷污本来无可挑剔的名誉或纯洁 (reputation / name / honor) · taint: 掺入微量腐败、有害成分以致变质 (evidence / food / legacy)

groups.name: Take into Custody · 缉捕与拘押 (Arrest, Collar, Detain)
groups.tip: 执法机关依法剥夺人身自由

items.def_zh: 逮捕，拘留；遏制，阻止；吸引（注意）
items.def_en: 1. To seize someone by legal authority and take them into custody. 2. To stop or slow down a process or development. 3. (formal) To attract and hold someone's attention.
items.ex_en: Authorities moved swiftly to arrest the fugitive before he boarded the flight.
items.ex_zh: 当局迅速行动，在这名逃犯登机之前将其依法逮捕。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Arrest someone or take them to a police station for questioning
items.ex_en: The detectives hauled in two prime suspects for intensive preliminary questioning.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们带走了两名主要嫌疑人到警局接受密集的初步审讯。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Apprehend someone and take them into custody
items.ex_en: Business usually picks up in the spring, and sales figures improve rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 生意通常在春季好转，销售额也会迅速回升。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Place someone in a prison, cell, or secure psychiatric facility
items.ex_en: The court decided to lock up the serial robber for fifteen years.
items.ex_zh: 法院决定将那名连环抢劫犯关押入狱十五年。

items.def_zh: 逮捕，捉拿；拦截（某人与之说话）
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To catch and arrest a suspect or criminal. 2. (informal) To stop someone and make them listen or talk to you.
items.ex_en: Undercover patrol officers collared the pickpocket as he tried to escape.
items.ex_zh: 便衣巡警在那名扒手试图逃窜时当场将其捉拿归案。

items.def_en: to officially keep someone in custody or delay their departure for questioning
items.ex_en: Border guards detained the traveler after detecting suspicious irregularities in his passport.
items.ex_zh: 边防警卫在发现护照存在可疑违规问题后，扣留了这名旅客。

items.def_en: (formal) to catch and arrest a suspect or fugitive
items.ex_en: Federal marshals managed to apprehend the escaped felon hiding near the border.
items.ex_zh: 联邦执法官成功缉拿了躲藏在边境附近的在逃重罪犯。

items.def_en: (informal) to catch someone doing something wrong and seize them suddenly
items.ex_en: Store security nabbed the petty shoplifter just outside the sliding glass doors.
items.ex_zh: 商场安保在自动玻璃门外当场逮住了那个小偷小摸的窃贼。

groups.summary_en: This scenario describes law enforcement or legal authorities seizing a suspect and placing them in custody. 'Collar' is informal police slang for catching or apprehending a wrongdoer, whereas 'arrest' denotes the full legal act of taking someone into official custody under warrant or suspicion.
groups.summary_zh: 司法执法人员发现嫌疑人并依法抓扣、收押之刑事执法场景。
groups.desc_en: Designates the lawful or coercive apprehension and physical deprivation of liberty of a suspect, contrasting with voluntary accompaniment by emphasizing authoritative seizure and detention.
groups.desc_zh: 指执法机构运用强制力剥夺嫌疑人人身自由并将其扣押，与普通的“拦阻”相对，强调法定拘捕程序与失去人身自由。
groups.nuance_en: arrest: seize formally under legal authority and take into official custody (suspect / criminal / protester) · detain: hold someone in official custody or delay their departure temporarily (suspects / travelers / cargo) · apprehend: catch and formally arrest an offender or fugitive after pursuit (fugitive / felon / criminal) · collar: informal capture or catching of a criminal red-handed (thief / suspect / crook) · lock up: imprison or secure behind bars safely (felon / inmate / criminal)
groups.nuance_zh: arrest: 依据法律程序正式予以逮捕归案 (suspect / criminal / protester) · detain: 依法暂扣、扣留或拘留 (suspects / travelers / cargo) · apprehend: 经过追捕将逃亡罪犯缉捕归案 (fugitive / felon / criminal) · collar: 抓获现行犯、“逮住”小偷 (thief / suspect / crook) · lock up: 关进牢房予以监禁关押 (felon / inmate / criminal)

groups.name: Tear & Rip · 撕裂与扯碎 (Tear, Rip, Shred)
groups.tip: 用力扯破或撕成碎块

items.def_en: (+ sth) Tear paper, fabric, or other fibrous material into small pieces
items.ex_en: He was so furious that he threatened to rip up the partnership agreement.
items.ex_zh: 他非常愤怒，甚至威胁要撕毁合伙协议。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Pull something flexible or fibrous into several ragged parts
items.ex_en: He tore up the draft agreement in frustration and walked out of the room.
items.ex_zh: 他沮丧地撕毁了协议草案，甩门而去。

items.def_en: 1. To pull or be pulled apart or into pieces by force. 2. To run or move somewhere very quickly.
items.ex_en: He tore open the urgent parcel without waiting for a pair of scissors.
items.ex_zh: 他等不及拿剪刀，急匆匆地一把撕开了那个紧急包裹。

items.def_en: [I/T] to tear something quickly and suddenly with substantial force
items.ex_en: A jagged metal shard ripped through his jacket sleeve during the collision.
items.ex_zh: 碰撞中，一块参差不齐的金属碎片猛力扯破了他的夹克袖子。
items.ex2_en: He ripped the envelope open with great urgency to read the letter.
items.ex2_zh: 他急切地撕开信封阅读里面的信件。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Pull something violently into separate ragged pieces
items.ex_en: The civil war threatens to tear the entire country apart.
items.ex_zh: 内战有让整个国家分崩离析的危险。

items.def_en: to cut or tear something into thin, narrow strips or fine fragments
items.ex_en: The clerk shredded the classified memos to protect the agency's secrets.
items.ex_zh: 职员将机密备忘录碎成细条纸屑，以保护机构的秘密。

items.def_en: to cut or tear skin or flesh deeply and jaggedly
items.ex_en: The jagged metal shard from the wreckage managed to lacerate his forearm quite deeply.
items.ex_zh: 残骸中锋利的金属碎片深深割裂了他的前臂。

items.def_en: to tear something apart violently into pieces with raw emotional or physical fury
items.ex_en: In a sudden paroxysm of grief, she threatened to rend her finest silken robes.
items.ex_zh: 在突如其来的悲恸中，她撕扯起自己最华贵的丝袍。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail pulling something flexible, fibrous, or organic apart by force into separate ragged pieces. 'Tear' is the general verb of division, while 'rip' implies sudden violence and speed, and 'shred' entails reducing material to many thin strips.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过强力将布帛、纸张或肌肉等纤维柔性组织暴力扯断或撕碎。
groups.desc_en: Denotes pulling something apart by tensile or shearing force so that structural integrity is destroyed, unlike clean cutting with a blade or brittle breaking.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过拉扯或剪切应力将物体扯破撕碎、破坏其结构完整性，区别于利刃的规整切割或脆性断裂。
groups.nuance_en: tear: basic pulling apart into pieces (paper / fabric / ligament) · rip: forceful, rough, or sound-producing tearing (seam / envelope / page) · shred: reducing into narrow strips or fragments (documents / cabbage / evidence) · lacerate: jaggedly tearing flesh or deep tissue (skin / muscle / flesh) · rend: literary, violent, or sorrowful wrenching apart (garment / heart / veil)
groups.nuance_zh: tear: 基础的受力撕开或扯破 (paper / fabric / ligament) · rip: 粗暴、迅猛或伴有响声的撕裂 (seam / envelope / page) · shred: 细密切碎或撕成条状/碎片 (documents / cabbage / evidence) · lacerate: 撕扯致伤口呈锯齿状开裂 (skin / muscle / flesh) · rend: 书面或文学色彩的剧烈扯碎或撕裂心扉 (garment / heart / veil)

groups.name: Thermal Rekindling & Heating · 重新加热与复燃 (Reheat, Reignite, Rekindle)
groups.tip: 施加热量再次升温或点燃

items.def_en: [I/T] to heat food, an engine, or a space until it reaches a suitable temperature
items.ex_en: Please warm up the leftover soup on the stove before everyone sits down.
items.ex_zh: 大家坐下前，请把炉子上的剩汤热一下。
items.ex2_en: The chilly room will warm up quickly once the central heating starts.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦中央供暖启动，寒冷的房间很快就会暖和起来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to light a flame, burner, or cigarette again after it has gone out
items.ex_en: The gust blew out his candle, so he knelt down to relight it.
items.ex_zh: 阵风吹熄了蜡烛，于是他跪下重新点燃它。
items.ex2_en: The dying campfire relit suddenly when a strong breeze swept through camp.
items.ex2_zh: 当一阵强风掠过营地时，快要熄灭的篝火突然复燃了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Make something warm or hot again, or become warm again
items.ex_en: He set the kettle on the stove to heat up water for morning tea.
items.ex_zh: 他把水壶放在炉子上烧热晨茶所需的水。
items.ex2_en: The midday air heated up rapidly under the scorching desert sun yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 昨天在沙漠灼热的阳光下，正午的气温迅速升高。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Ignite a flame, boiler, or furnace anew
items.ex_en: The coach's speech fired up the team before the final match.
items.ex_zh: 决赛前，教练的演讲彻底点燃了全队的斗志。

items.def_zh: 突然复燃；猛烈燃烧起来
items.def_en: Suddenly burst into flame again after dying down
items.ex_en: The smoldering charcoal suddenly began to flare up under the stiff autumn breeze.
items.ex_zh: 闷烧的木炭在强劲的秋风下突然又猛烈燃烧起来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to relight a dying fire, ember, or flame, or catch fire again
items.ex_en: The wanderer gently blew upon the ashes to rekindle the dying hearth fire.
items.ex_zh: 流浪者轻轻对着灰烬吹气，以重新点燃垂熄的炉火。
items.ex2_en: Old childhood memories rekindled in her mind during the quiet train ride.
items.ex2_zh: 在安静的火车旅途中，童年的旧日回忆在她心中重新唤起。

items.def_en: To heat food, liquid, or an object again until it is hot.
items.ex_en: You can easily reheat the pasta in the microwave for two quick minutes.
items.ex_zh: 你可以把意面放进微波炉里迅速重新加热两分钟。

items.def_zh: （使）重新点燃；使再次燃起，重燃（情绪、冲突或希望）
items.def_en: To catch fire again or make something catch fire again; to revive strong feelings, debates, or conflicts.
items.ex_en: The controversial editorial threatened to reignite intense public debate over judicial reform.
items.ex_zh: 这篇颇具争议的社论可能会重新引发公众对司法改革的激烈辩论。
items.ex2_en: Long-dormant passions reignited within him as he returned to his old craft.
items.ex2_zh: 当他重操旧业时，体内沉睡已久的热情再度燃起。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on reviving warmth, fire, or heat in an object, substance, or flame that had cooled or gone out. Verbs typically denote either warming something back up or striking combustion anew.
groups.summary_zh: 使冷却的物体再次受热，或使熄灭的火焰与燃烧重新引燃。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on restoring thermal energy, combustion, or figurative passion that had cooled or died down, contrasting with initial heating or brand-new ignition.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重于使已经冷却、暗淡或熄灭的温度、火焰或激情重新升高或复燃，区别于首次加热或全新的点火。
groups.nuance_en: reheat: returning previously cooked food to a warm temperature (soup / leftovers / coffee) · reignite: causing dormant fire or intense emotion to catch again (passion / debate / conflict) · rekindle: gently reviving fading embers, feelings, or ties (romance / friendship / hope) · flare up: sudden, volatile bursting into flame or unrest (violence / infection / temper)
groups.nuance_zh: reheat: 将已冷却的熟食重新加热至适温 (soup / leftovers / coffee) · reignite: 使处于休眠状态的烈火或激烈情绪重燃 (passion / debate / conflict) · rekindle: 细致温和地重新点燃余烬、唤醒旧情或希望 (romance / friendship / hope) · flare up: 突然且不可控地复燃或剧烈爆发 (violence / infection / temper)

groups.name: Thick & Lavish Application · 厚涂与重裹 (Slather, Daub, Rosin)
groups.tip: 厚厚涂抹油脂或树脂覆层

items.def_en: [I/T] to spread an oily, greasy, or sticky substance over an expanse
items.ex_en: The mechanic had to smear thick black grease all over the squeaking gears.
items.ex_zh: 技工不得不将厚厚的黑润滑脂涂满嘎吱作响的齿轮。

items.def_en: To rub or coat something (especially the bow of a stringed instrument) with rosin.
items.ex_en: The maestro would diligently rosin his horsehair bow before beginning the somber concerto.
items.ex_zh: 大师在开始演奏那首忧郁的协奏曲前，仔细地给马尾琴弓擦上松香。

items.def_en: (+ sth + on/over sth) Spread a thick, wet layer of substance heavily over a surface
items.ex_en: She had to plaster on another wet layer of clay across the cracked surface.
items.ex_zh: 她只得在开裂的表面上重重抹上一层厚厚的湿黏土。

items.def_en: [I/T] to spread a thick, sticky substance crudely, heavily, or unevenly on a surface
items.ex_en: The children began to daub wet mud crudely across the clean wooden fence.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们开始胡乱把湿泥巴涂抹在干净的木栅栏上。

items.def_en: (+ sth + on/onto sth) Smear or apply cosmetics, mud, or paste in a very thick layer
items.ex_en: She tends to cake on foundation whenever she prepares for an evening party.
items.ex_zh: 每当筹备晚宴时，她总喜欢把粉底涂得极厚。

items.def_en: (+ sth + on/onto sth) Apply a thick, generous, viscous layer of substance to a surface
items.ex_en: Be sure to slather on sunscreen generously before you head out to play.
items.ex_zh: 出去玩之前，一定要在身上厚厚地涂上一层防晒霜。

items.def_en: (+ on/with) to apply a thick layer of a paste-like substance over a wide area
items.ex_en: They had to plaster the damaged facade with a thick coat of protective stucco.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须在受损的外墙上大面积抹上一层厚厚的保护性粉刷灰浆。

items.def_zh: 厚厚地涂，大量涂抹；大量使用
items.def_en: To spread or apply something thickly or in very generous quantities.
items.ex_en: He would always slather rich butter onto his freshly toasted bread every morning.
items.ex_zh: 每天早晨，他总会在刚烤好的面包上厚厚涂上一层浓郁的黄油。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to applying viscous materials, oils, or resins onto a surface in thick, heavy, or specialized layers (such as spreading paste thickly or rubbing rosin on bowstrings).
groups.summary_zh: 指在物体表面极其厚实、大面积或针对性地抹上膏体、树脂等粘稠介质。
groups.desc_en: Involves spreading or heaping a viscous, paste-like substance in heavy, generous layers over a surface, unlike light spraying or fine coating.
groups.desc_zh: 指在物体表面极其厚实、大面积地涂抹或堆积粘稠膏状物质，区别于轻微的喷涂或薄层的精细涂层。
groups.nuance_en: slather: applying lavishly, generously, and thickly (sunscreen / butter / sauce) · daub: smearing crudely, clumsily, or patchily (mud / paint / ointment) · plaster: coating heavily so as to cover completely or stiffen (walls / mud / hair) · cake on: drying or hardening into a thick crusted layer (mud / makeup / grime)
groups.nuance_zh: slather: 极其大方、慷慨且厚厚地涂抹 (sunscreen / butter / sauce) · daub: 粗糙、拙劣或不规整地点涂抹抹 (mud / paint / ointment) · plaster: 大量厚敷以完全覆盖或形成硬壳 (walls / mud / hair) · cake on: 膏泥结块、硬化成厚厚硬壳 (mud / makeup / grime)

groups.name: Tinker & Mend · 捣鼓与修理 (Tinker, Fettle, Mend)
groups.tip: 摆弄修补恢复正常功能

items.def_en: to cover a hole or repair a defect by fastening a piece of material over it
items.ex_en: The hermit sought coarse cloth to patch the worn mantle of his youth.
items.ex_zh: 隐士找来粗布，修补他年轻时穿旧的斗篷。

items.def_en: to touch, adjust, or tinker with something repeatedly, often aimlessly or while trying to fix it
items.ex_en: Stop trying to fiddle with that broken radio before you ruin it completely.
items.ex_zh: 别再胡乱摆弄那台坏收音机了，免得彻底弄坏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Repair something temporarily or roughly with available materials
items.ex_en: He used spare wire and duct tape to patch up the broken fence.
items.ex_zh: 他用备用铁丝和绝缘胶带马虎地修补好了破损的栅栏。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Make small experimental changes or improvised adjustments to a machine or device
items.ex_en: He spent all afternoon trying to tinker with the lawnmower in his garage.
items.ex_zh: 他整个下午都在车库里捣鼓修理那台割草机。

items.def_en: (+ sth) Improve or repair a surface or object by making small additions or corrections
items.ex_en: She spent a few minutes touching up her makeup before the live broadcast.
items.ex_zh: 在直播开始前，她花了几分钟补了补妆。

items.def_en: [I/T] to repair something that is broken, torn, or damaged so that it can be used again
items.ex_en: She sat quietly under the lamp to mend her son's frayed school uniform.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐在灯下，缝补儿子磨损的校服。
items.ex2_en: His broken leg began to mend nicely after weeks of complete rest.
items.ex2_zh: 经过几周的充分休息，他骨折的腿开始良好愈合。

items.def_zh: 修补，摆弄，瞎捣鼓（tinker with）；做补锅匠
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To make small, experimental adjustments or repairs to a machine, system, or plan. 2. (historical) To work as a traveling tinker mending metal household items.
items.ex_en: He loves to tinker with old mechanical watches during his spare weekend hours.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢在周末闲暇时瞎捣鼓那些老旧的机械表。

items.def_zh: 修补，修理；（冶金/铸造）修整（铸件边缘），修炉
items.def_en: 1. (dialect) To mend, repair, or put something in good condition. 2. (engineering) To trim the rough edges from a metal casting or piece of pottery.
items.ex_en: The elderly blacksmith stepped outside to fettle the rusted blades of the scythe.
items.ex_zh: 老铁匠走到屋外，着手修整长柄镰刀上生锈的刃口。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote hands-on physical fixing, patching, or adjusting of broken household items, tools, garments, or machinery, often involving improvised or artisanal skill.
groups.summary_zh: 指动手修整、补缀衣物器具，或摆弄调试机械部件以使其恢复正常运转。
groups.desc_en: Involves making informal, small-scale adjustments, repairs, or improvements to a device or state, distinct from standardized industrial manufacturing or professional overhaul.
groups.desc_zh: 指对机械构件或事物进行非正式的、局部的捣鼓、修补或微调，区别于标准化工业制造或彻底专业大修。
groups.nuance_en: tinker: casually or inexpertly experimenting with parts (engine / watch / gadget) · mend: restoring a broken or torn item to usable condition (clothes / fences / net) · patch up: hastily or temporarily repairing damage (relationship / leak / tire) · fettle: putting into good working order or trimming cast edges (engine / casting / machinery)
groups.nuance_zh: tinker: 随意摸索尝试、小打小闹地摆弄修整 (engine / watch / gadget) · mend: 将破损破裂之物修复至可用状态 (clothes / fences / net) · patch up: 仓促或打补丁式地临时修补 (relationship / leak / tire) · fettle: 精细调校使处于良好运转状态，或清理铸件毛边 (engine / casting / machinery)

groups.name: Tolerate & Endure · 承受与苦熬 (Bear, Stand, Endure)
groups.tip: 默默担待乃至长期熬过痛苦折磨

items.def_en: accept or endure someone or something unpleasant or annoying without complaining
items.ex_en: The manager refused to tolerate loud or rude behavior inside the quiet office.
items.ex_zh: 经理绝不容忍安静的办公室内出现大声喧哗或粗鲁的行为。

items.def_zh: 容忍，忍受（不快的人或事）
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) to tolerate or accept an unpleasant person or situation without complaining
items.ex_en: I can't put up with his constant complaining any longer.
items.ex_zh: 我再也无法容忍他没完没了的抱怨了。

items.def_zh: 经受；忍受（常用于否定句或疑问句）
items.def_en: endure or tolerate an unpleasant situation or person without breaking down
items.ex_en: I honestly cannot stand his constant whining about the smallest daily inconveniences.
items.ex_zh: 我真受不了他总是为了日常中最微不足道的小事抱怨连连。

items.def_en: to persevere or endure through adversity or severe pressure without giving up
items.ex_en: Hang on a second, let me grab a pen to write that down.
items.ex_zh: 稍等一下，我拿支笔把它记下来。

items.def_zh: 忍耐到底，熬过（困难局面）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to continue doing something difficult, tedious, or unpleasant until the end
items.ex_en: Despite the grueling schedule, she resolved to stick out the remainder of the term.
items.ex_zh: 尽管日程艰辛，她还是下定决心熬过这学期剩下的日子。

items.def_zh: 忍受，承受；承担，负起；带有，具有；生育，结出（果实）
items.def_en: 1. To accept, tolerate, or endure a painful, unpleasant, or difficult situation. 2. To carry or support a weight or responsibility. 3. To give birth to a child, or produce flowers or fruit.
items.ex_en: He could no longer bear the agonizing physical pain in his broken leg.
items.ex_zh: 他再也无法忍受断腿处传来的剧烈阵痛。

items.def_zh: 坚持挺过，熬过（艰难境遇）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to endure a difficult, painful, or adverse situation with determination until it passes
items.ex_en: They had no choice but to tough out the brutal winter without power.
items.ex_zh: 在断电的情况下，他们别无选择，只能咬牙熬过这个严冬。

items.def_en: [I/T] suffer something difficult, painful, or unpleasant patiently over a long period
items.ex_en: The refugees had to endure bitter cold during their long trek northward.
