items.def_en: to arrange things in a straight line or in correct relative positions
items.ex_en: The mechanic will align the steering column with the newly replaced front wheels.
items.ex_zh: 机械师将把转向柱与新更换的前轮校准在一条直线上。
items.ex2_en: The planets will align perfectly in the night sky later this month.
items.ex2_zh: 本月晚些时候，行星将在夜空中完美排成一线。

items.def_en: to bring an object, wheel, or frame into accurate alignment, shape, or level
items.ex_en: The wheelwright used gentle hammer strokes to true the buckled steel rim.
items.ex_zh: 修车匠用锤子轻轻敲击，以校正变形的钢质轮辋。

items.def_zh: 使并列，把……放在近处；使贴合
items.def_en: To place something side by side or next to another, or bring two surfaces into contact.
items.ex_en: The surgeon will appose the severed edges of the incision with fine sutures.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生将用细缝合线把切口分离的两端贴合对齐。

items.def_zh: 校准，准直；使（光线、粒子束等）平行
items.def_en: 1. To make rays of light or particles travel strictly parallel to each other. 2. To align the optical axis of an instrument accurately.
items.ex_en: The laboratory technician used specialized convex lenses to collimate the laser beam.
items.ex_zh: 实验室技术人员使用特制的凸透镜使激光束完全准直平行。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the spatial manipulation of physical parts, optical beams, or biological surfaces to bring them into parallel pathways, exact contact, or geometric correspondence.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过几何或机械调节，使表面平行贴合、光束平行准直或构件位置精确对称。
groups.desc_en: Refers to the rigorous spatial orientation of components to achieve exact collinearity, coplanarity, or direct contact, differing from messy grouping by geometric precision.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过几何级校准使构件达到严格的共线、平行或贴合，区别于随意摆放，强调高精度对准。
groups.nuance_en: align: adjust components to lie precisely along a true line (wheels / text / policy) · collimate: make parallel, especially rays of light or optical axes (beam / lens / telescope) · appose: place side-by-side or in close physical contact (edges / lips / flaps) · true: bring an object into exact mechanical squareness or balance (wheel / surface / edge)
groups.nuance_zh: align: 使各部件在一条基准线上精准排齐 (wheels / text / policy) · collimate: 使光束或光学透镜光轴严格准直平行 (beam / lens / telescope) · appose: 将两边缘紧密贴合、贴并 (edges / lips / flaps) · true: 机械校正使其平整或对称平衡 (wheel / surface / edge)

groups.name: Analyze & Deconstruct · 分解与剖析 (Analyze, Deconstruct, Dissect)
groups.tip: 审视细节探求根由

items.def_zh: 分析，剖析；分解（物质成分）
items.def_en: 1. To examine something methodically and in detail in order to explain or interpret it. 2. (chemistry) To separate a substance into its constituent parts to determine its composition.
items.ex_en: The scholar sought to analyze the hidden metaphysical themes within the poet's verse.
items.ex_zh: 这位学者试图深入剖析诗人诗句中隐藏的形而上学主题。

items.def_en: (+ into) to separate complex information or figures into smaller, more comprehensible units
items.ex_en: Let us break down the annual expenditure into concise, manageable monthly budget categories.
items.ex_zh: 让我们将年度支出细分成简明易管的各月预算类别进行分析。
items.ex2_en: The complex machinery broke down completely under the strain of continuous operations.
items.ex2_zh: 在连续运转的重压下，复杂的机械设备彻底瘫痪了。

items.def_zh: 挑剔剖析；逐项细拆分析
items.def_en: (+ sth) to examine or criticize a text, argument, or plan thoroughly piece by piece
items.ex_en: Hostile reviewers immediately began to pick apart the flawed methodology in her proposal.
items.ex_zh: 心存敌意的审稿人立刻开始逐项挑剔剖析她方案中的缺陷方法论。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to separate a complex structure, argument, or theory into its constituent elements
items.ex_en: The professor proceeded to take apart the economic model, exposing its underlying flaws.
items.ex_zh: 教授着手拆分分析这一经济模型，揭示其潜在的缺陷。

items.def_en: to examine, criticize, or analyze something piece by piece with minute precision
items.ex_en: The investigative journalist meticulously chose to dissect every clause of the disputed contract.
items.ex_zh: 调查记者细致入微地逐条深入剖析那份有争议的合同条款。

items.def_en: to analyze a sentence, string of code, or message into its component parts to grasp the exact meaning
items.ex_en: Linguists meticulously parse ancient inscriptions to uncover subtleties of grammatical structure and meaning.
items.ex_zh: 语言学家对古代铭文进行严密的语法解析，以探寻其语法结构和含义的精妙之处。

items.def_en: to break down a concept, narrative, or text into basic parts to expose underlying assumptions
items.ex_en: Philosophers continue to deconstruct traditional moral frameworks to expose historical cultural biases.
items.ex_zh: 哲学家们继续解构传统的道德框架，以揭示其中暗含的历史文化偏见。

groups.summary_en: An analyst breaks down a complex problem, text, or dataset into its constituent elements to understand its underlying structure, logic, or meaning.
groups.summary_zh: 将复杂事物、文本或系统拆解为构成要素以深入理解其结构与机理。
groups.desc_en: Treats an intellectual or physical whole as a composite to be partitioned into constitutive elements for scrutiny, differing from vague contemplation by systematic dissection.
groups.desc_zh: 将思想或物理整体系统拆解为其构成要素以探究机理，区别于泛泛思考，强调条分缕析与结构解构。
groups.nuance_en: dissect: cut open or examine minutely part by part (cadaver / argument / text) · parse: resolve a sentence or data into syntactic components (sentence / code / data) · deconstruct: expose underlying contradictions and assumptions in a structure (myth / text / theory) · analyze: examine components methodically to determine nature or function (sample / trend / problem)
groups.nuance_zh: dissect: 细致解剖或逐段严苛剖析 (cadaver / argument / text) · parse: 对语句或数据流进行句法/结构拆析 (sentence / code / data) · deconstruct: 解构文本或理论以暴露内在假定与矛盾 (myth / text / theory) · analyze: 系统化分解并探究各成分属性与功能 (sample / trend / problem)

groups.name: Apologize & Beg Pardon · 致歉与乞宥
groups.tip: 表示歉意、乞求原谅与宽恕

items.def_en: To forgive someone for a fault or minor mistake, or to justify an action.
items.ex_en: Please excuse my tardiness, as unexpected highway congestion delayed my morning commute.
items.ex_zh: 请原谅我的迟到，早晨路上突发的交通拥堵耽误了我的通勤。

items.def_en: (+ to/for) To tell someone that you are sorry for having done something wrong or causing trouble.
items.ex_en: The airline manager publicly stepped forward to apologize for the extensive holiday cancellations.
items.ex_zh: 航空公司经理公开出面，为假期期间大规模的航班取消表示道歉。

items.def_en: stop feeling angry or resentful toward someone for an offense or mistake
items.ex_en: She found it remarkably difficult to forgive his repeated breaches of confidentiality.
items.ex_zh: 她发现自己极难原谅他一再违反保密协议的行为。

items.def_zh: 推托；请求免予责任或活动
items.def_en: to ask to be excused from an obligation, arrangement, or promise with an apology
items.ex_en: He called late in the afternoon to beg off from tonight's dinner party.
items.ex_zh: 他傍晚时分打来电话，推托说今晚的晚宴无法参加了。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to compensate or atone for an offense, fault, or omission
items.ex_en: He worked overtime all weekend to make up for the lost hours.
items.ex_zh: 他整个周末都在加班，以弥补损失的工时。

items.def_en: forgive or excuse a person for a mistake, breach of manners, or fault
items.ex_en: The governor chose to pardon the reformed prisoner following decades of exemplary behavior.
items.ex_zh: 在服刑人员展现出数十年模范表现后，州长决定予以赦免。

items.def_en: (+ for) make amends or reparation for a wrong, transgression, or error
items.ex_en: The fallen politician sought to atone for past transgressions through sustained community service.
items.ex_zh: 落马政客试图通过长期的社区服务来弥补过去的过失。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey expressions of regret, contrition, or admitting an error, as well as the immediate transactional plea to release oneself or another from fault or offense.
groups.summary_zh: 表达悔意、承认过失以及请求他人宽恕或原谅的言语交际行为。
groups.desc_en: Covers the relational acts of admitting fault, seeking remission, or releasing grievance, moving beyond casual regret toward moral reconciliation or liability mitigation.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖承认过失、乞求宽宥或免除怨恨的人际互动，区别于空洞悔憾，强调道德层面的和解与责任免除。
groups.nuance_en: apologize: express explicit verbal regret for a fault or offense (to client / profusely / for error) · pardon: officially excuse a crime or release an offender from penalty (convict / prisoner / crime) · excuse: overlook or forgive a minor lapse, or justify it (behavior / absence / lapse) · atone: make tangible amends or reparation for a wrongdoing (for sin / crime / neglect)
groups.nuance_zh: apologize: 就过失明确用言语表达歉意 (to client / profusely / for error) · pardon: 具有官方或尊长地位特赦过错、免予追究 (convict / prisoner / crime) · excuse: 原谅小毛病或为违规找免责理由 (behavior / absence / lapse) · atone: 付出实际行动或受苦以弥补罪愆 (for sin / crime / neglect)

groups.name: Appoint & Delegate · 委任与指派 (Appoint, Delegate, Reassign, Subcontract)
groups.tip: 组织人事任命与业务层层转包

items.def_en: to formally choose someone to hold a particular position or perform an official task
items.ex_en: The shareholders voted to appoint a veteran auditor to oversee the restructuring process.
items.ex_zh: 股东们投票决定任命一位资深审计师来监督重组过程。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to delegate or transfer decisions, responsibilities, or authority to a subordinate
items.ex_en: The department head decided to hand down key budgetary decisions to regional coordinators.
items.ex_zh: 部门负责人决定将关键的预算决策权下放给各区域协调员。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to delegate, subcontract, or assign tasks or work to an external party
items.ex_en: To meet tight deadlines, the studio decided to farm out several animation sequences.
items.ex_zh: 为了赶上紧张的交期，工作室决定将几个动画片段外包出去。

items.def_en: (+ sth to sb) to officially transfer legal ownership, rights, or authority to someone else by signing a document
items.ex_en: The elderly patriarch agreed to sign over legal custody of the family estate.
items.ex_zh: 年迈的家族长辈同意签字转让家族庄园的合法管辖权。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ to) to entrust a task, responsibility, or authority to another person
items.ex_en: Senior executives must learn to delegate critical operational responsibilities to trusted department heads.
items.ex_zh: 高管必须学会将重要的运营职责委派给值得信任的部门主管。

items.def_zh: 重新指派，重调（工作、职位等）；重新分配
items.def_en: To give someone a different job, role, or location, or to assign a task or resource to someone else.
items.ex_en: The director decided to reassign the lead engineer to the overseas infrastructure initiative.
items.ex_zh: 主管决定将首席工程师重新调派到海外基础设施项目中。

items.def_en: To pay an outside person or organization to do part of a larger job that you have agreed to do.
items.ex_en: The primary contractor decided to subcontract the structural electrical wiring to local specialists.
items.ex_zh: 主承包商决定将建筑电气布线工程分包给当地的专业公司。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this administrative frame describe delegating responsibilities, redistributing roles, or allocating tasks and portions of work downward or to third parties.
groups.summary_zh: 指在组织架构内委派职务、下放权力或将部分业务分包转移。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the institutional transfer of roles, duties, or tasks from a higher authority to a subordinate or external party, differing from simple asking by jurisdictional transfer.
groups.desc_zh: 指职权或任务自上而下或向外转嫁的制度化分派，区别于简单的打招呼帮忙，强调权责的转移。
groups.nuance_en: delegate: entrust authority or task to a deputy or subordinate (authority / task / responsibility) · appoint: officially assign a person to an office or position (judge / committee / minister) · subcontract: farm out portions of a main contract to outside vendors (work / project / manufacture) · reassign: transfer an employee or resource to a different duty (officer / personnel / role)
groups.nuance_zh: delegate: 授权或委派下属代行职责 (authority / task / responsibility) · appoint: 官方正式任命某人担任官职 (judge / committee / minister) · subcontract: 将总包工程的部分业务分包转包 (work / project / manufacture) · reassign: 将人员或任务重新调配改派 (officer / personnel / role)

groups.name: Aver & Proclaim · 断言与宣告 (Authoritative Public Declaration)
groups.tip: 郑重断言并向公众公开宣告

items.def_en: (+ sth) to proclaim or state something publicly and officially
items.ex_en: The town council chose to give out the new water rationing guidelines yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 镇议会昨天正式公布了最新的定量限水指南。

items.def_en: to state clearly, officially, and emphatically for the public record
items.ex_en: The electoral commission will officially declare the verified results before international observers tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 选举委员会明天将在国际观察员面前正式宣布核实后的结果。

items.def_en: to express an idea or doctrine clearly and authoritatively
items.ex_en: The foreign minister will enunciate the new diplomatic doctrine before the general assembly.
items.ex_zh: 外交部长将在联合国大会上正式阐明新的外交方针。

items.def_en: to announce officially and publicly in a formal or ceremonial manner
items.ex_en: The sovereign chose to proclaim a national holiday to commemorate the historic victory.
items.ex_zh: 君主决定正式宣布设立国家假日以纪念这场历史性的胜利。

items.def_en: to make known an official law, decree, or doctrine publicly and officially
items.ex_en: The legislative council intends to promulgate strict environmental protection regulations later this month.
items.ex_zh: 立法委员会打算在本月晚些时候正式颁布严格的环境保护法规。

items.def_en: 1. (+ that) (formal / law) To state or assert firmly and positively that something is the case.
items.ex_en: The defense attorney did aver that the accused party remained entirely blameless.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师郑重声明，被告方完全是清白无辜的。

items.def_en: 1. (formal / archaic) To announce, proclaim, or make known publicly or solemnly.
items.ex_en: Solemn brass trumpets did annunciate the grand ceremonial entrance of the victorious monarch.
items.ex_zh: 肃穆的铜号宣告着凯旋君主的庄严入场。

groups.summary_en: An authority or institutional speaker announces a definitive truth or formal finding categorically and solemnly. Nuances range from sworn evidential assertions to ceremonial public proclamations.
groups.summary_zh: 以庄重、权威或官方口吻作出的定论性宣告与明断。
groups.desc_en: Involves making formal, emphatic, and legally or socially binding affirmations before an audience, distinguishing itself from casual speech by solemn finality and legal authority.
groups.desc_zh: 在公众或法权面前作出郑重、排他且具约束力的断言宣告，区别于日常说话，强调庄严权威性与公开性。
groups.nuance_en: proclaim: announce officially and publicly with fanfare or authority (independence / state of emergency / victory) · promulgate: put a law or dogma into effect by official declaration (law / edict / doctrine) · aver: declare positively and with deep conviction as fact (innocence / truth / right) · declare: state openly, formally, and explicitly (war / bankruptcy / allegiance)
groups.nuance_zh: proclaim: 官方以隆重形式公开宣告 (independence / state of emergency / victory) · promulgate: 依法颁布并推行法令戒条 (law / edict / doctrine) · aver: 确凿断言、一口咬定其真实性 (innocence / truth / right) · declare: 正式声明立场、破产或宣战 (war / bankruptcy / allegiance)

groups.name: Bid & Offer · 竞标与出价 (Bid, Outbid, Underbid)
groups.tip: 在交易竞价中出资竞争

items.def_en: (+ for sth / + sth) submit a formal tender, offer, or bid for a contract or item
items.ex_en: Several foreign engineering firms decided to put in for the subway construction tender.
items.ex_zh: 几家外国工程公司决定就地铁建设项目提出投标。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ on/for) to offer a price for something, especially at an auction
items.ex_en: The wealthy connoisseur did bid five hundred golden guineas for the rare folio.
items.ex_zh: 那位富有的鉴赏家在拍卖会上为那本珍本出价五百金基尼。

items.def_en: [I/T] to submit an updated or secondary bid in an auction
items.ex_en: The investment fund chose to rebid after their initial acquisition offer was rejected.
items.ex_zh: 投资资金在最初的收购报价被拒绝后决定重新出价竞标。

items.def_zh: 出价低于（竞争对手）；竞标开价过低；（桥牌）叫牌过低
items.def_en: 1. To offer to do work or supply goods for a lower price than a competitor. 2. (bridge) To bid less than one's hand of cards justifies.
items.ex_en: The domestic supplier managed to underbid all foreign rivals to win the procurement.
items.ex_zh: 这家国内供应商通过报出低于所有外国对手的价格赢得了采购合同。

items.def_en: (+ sth) raise the price of an item at an auction by offering successive higher amounts
items.ex_en: Aggressive collectors continued to bid up the price of the rare post-impressionist painting.
items.ex_zh: 狂热的收藏家们不断抬高这幅罕见后印象派画作的拍卖价格。

items.def_en: To offer to pay a higher price than another bidder or competitor, especially at an auction.
items.ex_en: A private collector managed to outbid the museum for the rare medieval tapestry.
items.ex_zh: 一名私人收藏家以更高的出价击败博物馆，拍下了那幅罕见的中世纪挂毯。

items.def_en: [I/T] to make a bid higher than the value of something or higher than intended
items.ex_en: Inexperienced traders frequently overbid during initial public auctions due to sheer speculative excitement.
items.ex_zh: 没有经验的交易员在首次公开拍卖中常因单纯的投机兴奋而开价过高。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail offering specific monetary amounts in an auction, tender, or contract setting, differentiating by bidding higher, lower, or beating a competitor's price.
groups.summary_zh: 指在拍卖或招投标中提出报价，尤指高于或低于对手价格的竞价方式。
groups.desc_en: Refers to formal monetary offers in an auction, tender, or procurement setting to secure a contract or lot, contrasting with everyday shopping by its competitive pricing mechanism.
groups.desc_zh: 指在拍卖或招投标中为争夺合同或标的物提出的竞价行为，区别于明码标价的买卖，强调竞价机制。
groups.nuance_en: bid: formally offer a stated sum for purchase or contract (auction / tender / contract) · outbid: offer a higher price than a rival bidder to win (competitor / rival / collector) · underbid: offer a lower price than competitors or true value (project / rival / estimate) · rebid: submit a revised or subsequent bid during a process (contract / hand / project)
groups.nuance_zh: bid: 在拍卖或竞标中正式递交出价 (auction / tender / contract) · outbid: 叫出高于对手的价格压倒对方 (competitor / rival / collector) · underbid: 报出低于对手或低于实际成本的低价 (project / rival / estimate) · rebid: 在新一轮竞投中重新递交修改报价 (contract / hand / project)

groups.name: Bid & Outbid · 报价与叫牌竞争 (Lowball, Outcall, Outbid)
groups.tip: 拍卖交易中估价出价与压价

items.def_en: bid higher than the true value of an asset or beyond one's hand strength
items.ex_en: Excited buyers often overbid for historic properties, paying far beyond fair market worth.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的买家往往会对历史建筑出价过高，支付远超公允市场价值的金额。

items.def_en: (+ sth) aggressively force the acceptable price or offer to a lower level in negotiations
items.ex_en: Fierce market competition has driven down smartphone prices significantly.
items.ex_zh: 激烈的市场竞争大幅拉低了智能手机的价格。

items.def_en: (+ with sth) put forward an initial offer or contributing sum in a competitive arrangement
items.ex_en: If we all pitch in, we can finish clearing the yard in an hour.
items.ex_zh: 如果我们大家齐心协力，一个小时就能把院子清理干净。

items.def_en: offer a higher price than another bidder at an auction or sale
items.ex_en: She was determined to outbid every rival buyer to secure the prime real estate.
items.ex_zh: 她下定决心要出价高于每一个竞争买家，拿下这处黄金地段房产。

items.def_zh: 虚报低价，报极低价；给……极低的报价
items.def_en: (informal) To offer an intentionally or deceptively low estimate, bid, or price to someone in a negotiation.
items.ex_en: The unscrupulous contractor tried to lowball the renovation estimate to win our business.
items.ex_zh: 那个无良承包商试图虚报极低的装修报价以拿下我们的业务。

items.def_zh: （桥牌或纸牌游戏中）叫牌胜过，出价高过
items.def_en: (card games) To make a higher bid than another player.
items.ex_en: With quiet resolve, the veteran bridge master did outcall his rival's ambitious hand.
items.ex_zh: 这位资深的桥牌大师不动声色，以更高的叫牌压制了对手激进的牌势。

items.def_zh: 出价低于竞争对手（或叫牌偏低）
items.def_en: submit a lower bid than a competitor, or bid lower than justified in bridge
items.ex_en: The consortium decided to underbid the competition to ensure securing the long-term infrastructure contract.
items.ex_zh: 该财团决定报出低于竞争对手的价格，以确保拿下这项长期基建合同。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame represent strategic communication in negotiations, bridge, or auctions, specifically offering, undercutting, or overcalling terms and prices.
groups.summary_zh: 在谈判、拍卖或牌局中出价、压低要价或以高叫牌压制对手。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on strategic pricing dynamics designed to either undercut, outshine, or manipulate an adversarial negotiation or auction, differing from neutral bidding by tactical aggression.
groups.desc_zh: 聚焦于在博弈性谈判或竞拍中采用压低、抬高或压制手段的价格战术，区别于中性出价，强调竞争攻防策略。
groups.nuance_en: lowball: propose an unrealistically low offer to exploit or anchor a deal (offer / buyer / estimate) · outbid: overcome an opponent by tendering a superior price (rival / opponent / developer) · drive down: aggressively force market prices or valuations downward (prices / costs / wages) · pitch in: contribute resources or funds alongside others collaboratively (money / effort / share)
groups.nuance_zh: lowball: 报出极度不合常理的超低价以试探或压榨对方 (offer / buyer / estimate) · outbid: 出价高于所有竞争者以击败对手 (rival / opponent / developer) · drive down: 施压强行压低市场价格或成本 (prices / costs / wages) · pitch in: 多人齐心出钱或出力共同促成 (money / effort / share)

groups.name: Bleed & Hemorrhage · 出血与流血 (Bleed, Hemorrhage)
groups.tip: 普通渗血到大出血的加剧

items.def_en: to slowly seep out through small tears or a cut in tiny amounts
items.ex_en: Dark venous blood began to ooze slowly from the jagged cut on his forearm.
items.ex_zh: 暗色的静脉血开始从他前臂参差不齐的伤口中缓缓渗出。
items.ex2_en: The old pine tree oozed sticky golden resin from a small crack.
items.ex2_zh: 老松树从小裂缝中渗出粘稠的金黄色树脂。

items.def_en: slowly ooze or flow out through vascular tissue or a dressing
items.ex_en: Fresh droplets of blood began to seep out through the loosely applied gauze dressing.
items.ex_zh: 新鲜的血珠开始透过包扎较松的纱布敷料缓缓渗出。

items.def_en: to flow or pass slowly through a bandage, tissue, or wound
items.ex_en: Blood continued to seep into the sterile surgical dressing despite the applied pressure.
items.ex_zh: 尽管施加了压力，血液仍不断浸渗到无菌手术敷料中。

items.def_zh: 流血，出血；榨取（钱财）；（颜料等）渗开
items.def_en: 1. to lose blood from the body, or cause someone to lose blood. 2. to extort money from someone. 3. to spread or run into an adjacent area (of dye or ink).
items.ex_en: The deep gash continued to bleed persistently until the paramedic applied direct pressure.
items.ex_zh: 在急救人员进行直接按压之前，那道深伤口一直在持续流血。

items.def_zh: 大出血，严重失血；（资金、人员等）巨额流失
items.def_en: 1. to bleed heavily and dangerously from a ruptured blood vessel. 2. to lose a large amount of money, personnel, or resources rapidly.
items.ex_en: Trauma surgeons worked desperately before the injured patient began to hemorrhage uncontrollably inside.
items.ex_zh: 创伤外科医生在受伤病人腹腔开始不可控地大出血之前拼命展开抢救。

items.def_en: die or lose consciousness as a result of catastrophic, uncontrolled blood loss
items.ex_en: Without immediate combat tourniquets, wounded soldiers can quickly bleed out from arterial wounds.
items.ex_zh: 若不立即使用战术止血带，受伤士兵可能会因动脉破裂迅速大量失血致死。

items.def_zh: 放血，因大量失血而休克或致死
items.def_en: [I/T] to drain or lose all or most blood, causing death or near-death
items.ex_en: The wounded gladiator did slowly exsanguinate upon the bloodstained sand of the arena.
items.ex_zh: 负伤的角斗士在竞技场血染的沙地上因失血过多而濒临死亡。
items.ex2_en: A severe puncture wound quickly exsanguinated the injured animal in the wilderness.
items.ex2_zh: 严重的刺伤使野外受伤的动物迅速失血过多而亡。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote losing blood internally or externally from damaged vascular tissue, escalating from minor weeping to catastrophic, uncontrollable blood loss (often extended to rapid loss of money or resources).
groups.summary_zh: 描述身体组织创伤性流血或失血，从微量渗血递增至大量喷涌与失控大出血。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the discharge or loss of vital blood or fluid from a vessel or system, graded by rate and volume from a sluggish percolation to fatal drainage, contrasting with generic fluid leakage by its vital, circulatory, or depleting consequence.
groups.desc_zh: 指生命血液或内部流体自脉管或系统逸失的过程，依渗出速率与失血量呈级数递进，与一般“液体泄漏”的区别在于其关涉生命力、血液循环或灾难性的枯竭。
groups.nuance_en: ooze: viscous, sluggish emission through small pores or cracks (blood / pus / sap) · bleed: baseline discharge of blood from vascular injury (wound / cut / nose) · hemorrhage: rapid, massive, and uncontrolled loss of blood or assets (internal blood / cash / talent) · bleed out: fatal total exsanguination from uncontained trauma (casualty / victim / artery) · exsanguinate: clinical or forensic complete drainage of blood (carcass / body / patient)
groups.nuance_zh: ooze: 黏稠、缓慢地自裂隙或微孔渗出 (blood / pus / sap) · bleed: 血管破损后的基准流血 (wound / cut / nose) · hemorrhage: 快速、海量且失控的急剧大出血或资产流失 (internal blood / cash / talent) · bleed out: 未受遏制直至失血致死的全过程 (casualty / victim / artery) · exsanguinate: 临床或法医术语中的彻底抽干血液 (carcass / body / patient)

groups.name: Breathe & Respiring · 呼吸与叹纳 (Inhale, Exhale, Respire)
groups.tip: 维持生命的自主呼吸与呼气

items.def_en: To draw air into the lungs
items.ex_en: Breathe in deeply through your nose and hold it for three seconds.
items.ex_zh: 用鼻子深吸一口气，屏住三秒钟。

items.def_en: To expel air from the lungs
items.ex_en: Relax your shoulders and breathe out slowly through your mouth.
items.ex_zh: 放松肩膀，通过嘴巴缓缓呼气。

items.def_en: To emit a long, audible breath expressing relief, fatigue, or sadness
items.ex_en: She sat back in her chair and sighed with immense relief after the exam.
items.ex_zh: 考试结束后，她靠在椅子上，长长地舒了一口气。

items.def_en: To draw air or vapor into the lungs
items.ex_en: Just step outside for a second and inhale the cool night air.
items.ex_zh: 赶紧到外面呆一秒，吸两口夜晚的凉爽空气。

items.def_en: (formal/technical) To engage in the physiological process of respiration
items.ex_en: In the damp gloom of the cavern, the slumbering beast continued to respire rhythmically.
items.ex_zh: 在洞穴潮湿的幽暗中，那头沉睡的巨兽依旧有节奏地呼吸着。

items.def_en: To breathe out air or vapor from the lungs
items.ex_en: The yoga instructor told the class to exhale slowly through their mouths.
items.ex_zh: 瑜伽教练让全班学员用嘴缓缓呼气。

items.def_zh: 呼吸，呼出；轻声低语，吐露
items.def_en: 1. To take air into the lungs and expel it again. 2. To whisper or say something very softly.
items.ex_en: He leaned close to her ear to breathe a desperate, solemn promise.
items.ex_zh: 他贴近她的耳边，轻声吐露出一句绝望而庄重的誓言。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers the vital respiratory mechanics of drawing air into the lungs and expelling it, as well as modifying airflow into deep sighs or barely audible breaths.
groups.summary_zh: 指肺部吸入与排出气体的生理机制，以及伴随情绪的深呼吸与叹息。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the physiological ventilation of lungs or respiratory organs, differing from non-biological air flow by its somatic rhythm and affective or metabolic agency.
groups.desc_zh: 指肺部或呼吸器官的生理通气活动，与非生物性的“气流流动”不同，它具有躯体节律性以及代谢或情绪表达功能。
groups.nuance_en: breathe: baseline act of drawing and expelling air (air / oxygen / deeply) · inhale: deliberate or physiological drawing inward of air or vapor (fumes / breath / smoke) · exhale: expelling breath outward from lungs (air / vapor / smoke) · sigh: audible, prolonged exhalation conveying relief, grief, or fatigue (sigh / relief / grief) · respire: technical or biological cellular/organ exchange of gases (tissues / organisms / skin)
groups.nuance_zh: breathe: 呼气与吸气的基准生理动作 (air / oxygen / deeply) · inhale: 刻意或生理性地吸入气体或烟汽 (fumes / breath / smoke) · exhale: 将肺中气体呼出体外 (air / vapor / smoke) · sigh: 发出声响的长吁慢叹，表达释怀、悲伤或倦怠 (sigh / relief / grief) · respire: 细胞或生物体气体交换的专门生物学术语 (tissues / organisms / skin)

groups.name: Bribe & Suborn · 贿赂与收买 (Grease, Bribe, Suborn)
groups.tip: 以金钱利益腐蚀公职或证人

items.def_zh: 打点，塞钱疏通（尤指grease sb's palm）
items.def_en: (informal, esp. 'grease someone's palm') to covertly give money to an official to facilitate smooth processing
items.ex_en: The contractor tried to grease the inspector's palm to overlook several safety violations.
items.ex_zh: 承包商企图暗中塞钱打点检查员，好让他对几处安全违规视而不见。

items.def_en: to give illegal hush money or kickbacks to someone to ensure silence or secure compliance
items.ex_en: The corrupt developer paid off city officials to expedite the disputed permit.
items.ex_zh: 这名黑心开发商向市政官员行贿，以加快有争议的许可证审批。

items.def_en: (+ sb) settle matters with someone, often illicitly or through covert financial satisfaction
items.ex_en: He promised to square away the disgruntled clerk with an envelope of cash.
items.ex_zh: 他答应拿一封厚厚的现金暗中摆平那个心怀不满的办事员。

items.def_en: to pay someone off in order to stop them from causing trouble, revealing secrets, or prosecuting
items.ex_en: They attempted to buy off the primary witness with a large sum of cash.
items.ex_zh: 他们试图用巨额现金收买主要证人。

items.def_zh: 用金钱私下打通；收买摆平
items.def_en: (+ sb) arrange or improperly pacify an official or witness through illicit inducement
items.ex_en: The crooked manager knew how to fix up inspectors before each surprise audit.
items.ex_zh: 那个心术不正的经理深谙如何在每次突击审计前私下打通检查员。

items.def_en: To illegally give money or gifts to someone, especially in authority, to persuade them to do something for you.
items.ex_en: The suspect attempted to bribe the border guard with a thick wad of bills.
items.ex_zh: 嫌疑人企图用一厚叠钞票贿赂边境警卫。

items.def_zh: 收买，唆使（某人做违法之事，尤指作伪证）
items.def_en: (formal / law) To secretly bribe or persuade someone to commit an unlawful act, especially to commit perjury in court.
items.ex_en: The defense attorney was accused of attempting to suborn a key prosecution witness.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师被指控企图收买控方的关键证人作伪证。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote corruptly inducing someone to act dishonestly, breach duty, or commit perjury using money, illicit favors, or covert payments, differentiated by stealth, formality, and illicit purpose.
groups.summary_zh: 通过金钱利益或不正当好处拉拢腐蚀他人，以诱使其违背公职职责或作伪证。
groups.desc_en: Denotes illicitly corrupting or securing favorable action from someone through illicit material inducements, distinct from legitimate compensation or negotiation by its moral illegality and perversion of duty.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过非法物质利益诱使或收买当事人以牟取私利，与合法的“报酬”或“商业协商”区别在于其背弃公职准则的腐败性与违法性。
groups.nuance_en: grease: covert lubricating payoff to expedite bureaucratic action (palms / skids / wheels) · bribe: baseline illicit transfer of money/favors to subvert duty (officials / judges / inspectors) · buy off: paying an adversary or potential whistleblower to drop opposition or silence charges (protesters / critics / witnesses) · suborn: inducing a witness to commit perjury or unlawful acts by deceit or cash (witnesses / perjury / jury)
groups.nuance_zh: grease: 隐蔽打点以润滑官僚阻力、加速通融 (palms / skids / wheels) · bribe: 破坏职务公正的基准行贿行为 (officials / judges / inspectors) · buy off: 通过出资买通对手或知情者以平息反对或封口 (protesters / critics / witnesses) · suborn: 诱使或收买证人作伪证或从事非法勾当 (witnesses / perjury / jury)

groups.name: Butcher & Core Meat/Carcass · 剥皮与剔膛 (Skin, Bone, Core)
groups.tip: 除去外表层或剥离内里

items.def_en: to remove the bones from a piece of meat or fish to produce boneless cuts
items.ex_en: The chef demonstrated how to fillet fresh salmon with a single swift motion.
items.ex_zh: 主厨示范了如何一刀麻利地将新鲜三文鱼剔骨切片。

items.def_en: 1. To remove the skin from an animal or fruit. 2. To injure the skin on a part of your body by scraping it.
items.ex_en: The butcher used a razor-sharp knife to carefully skin the deer carcass.
items.ex_zh: 屠夫用一把锋利的刀小心翼翼地剥掉鹿尸的皮。

items.def_zh: 去（水果等）的果心，掏出……的核心
items.def_en: To remove the core or seeds from fruit such as apples.
items.ex_en: Be sure to peel and core the crisp apples before slicing them up.
items.ex_zh: 切片前，务必先将这些脆苹果削皮并掏出果心。

items.def_en: To remove the bones from meat or fish before cooking.
items.ex_en: You need to bone the chicken breasts completely before wrapping them in pastry.
items.ex_zh: 在将鸡胸肉裹入面皮之前，需要彻底剔去骨头。

items.def_en: to extract and remove all internal skeletal bones from meat or poultry
items.ex_en: She spent the afternoon learning how to debone a whole roast duck efficiently.
items.ex_zh: 她花了一个下午学习如何利落地将一整只烤鸭剔骨。

items.def_en: to remove the stomach and internal organs from an animal or fish before cooking
items.ex_en: The fisherman showed his son how to gut the fresh trout by the riverbank.
items.ex_zh: 渔夫在河岸边向儿子示范如何掏空新鲜鳟鱼的内脏。

items.def_en: to formally or surgically disembowel a body or carcass by removing all entrails
items.ex_en: The pathologist had to completely eviscerate the cadaver during the thorough postmortem examination.
items.ex_zh: 病理学家在进行详尽的尸检时，必须切除尸体的全部内脏。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve butchering or deeply hollowing an animal carcass or firm food item by removing anatomical structural elements such as hides, bones, or central fibrous cores.
groups.summary_zh: 指屠宰或食材预处理中剥除毛皮、剔除骨骼或挖去中心硬芯/内脏。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the anatomical preparatory dressing of a carcass, fish, or produce by surgically stripping off external coverings or excising internal organs/cores, contrasting with rough chopping by its structural dissection.
groups.desc_zh: 指对肉身胴体、鱼鲜或果蔬进行的解构性初加工，即剥除外皮、剔去骨骼或掏空脏腑/内核，与粗鲁的“剁砍”区别在于其顺应解剖结构的剖分性。
groups.nuance_en: skin: stripping the outer pelt or dermal layer from a carcass (carcass / animal / deer) · bone: stripping meat away from the skeleton or removing bones (meat / chicken / fish) · gut: rapid, coarse disembowelment of a slaughtered body or building (fish / deer / building) · eviscerate: thorough, surgical removal of internal viscera (carcass / organs / entrails) · core: excising the central seed-bearing column of fruit (apples / pears / cabbage)
groups.nuance_zh: skin: 剥除胴体的毛皮或表皮层 (carcass / animal / deer) · bone: 从骨架上剔除骨头或脱骨 (meat / chicken / fish) · gut: 快速、粗暴地掏空猎物内脏或清空建筑物内部 (fish / deer / building) · eviscerate: 彻底且具外科/屠宰规范地摘除内脏 (carcass / organs / entrails) · core: 剜除果实中心含有硬籽的核部 (apples / pears / cabbage)

groups.name: Capture & Stage Production · 录影与补拍制作 (Record, Film, Reshoot)
groups.tip: 提前录下声音图像备用

items.def_en: [I/T] record moving pictures using a video camera or motion-picture equipment
items.ex_en: The independent crew arrived downtown at dawn to film the opening car chase.
items.ex_zh: 独立摄制组破晓时分抵达市中心，拍摄开场的追车镜头。

items.def_en: record audio or video on magnetic tape or digital media
items.ex_en: The journalist decided to tape the entire interview to guarantee complete accuracy.
items.ex_zh: 记者决定将整个采访过程录音，以确保完全准确无误。

items.def_en: (+ sth) record a track, audio line, or foundational take in a production studio
items.ex_en: The government has laid down strict safety guidelines for the industry.
items.ex_zh: 政府为该行业制定了严格的安全指南。

items.def_en: (+ sth) record new audiovisual material over an existing recorded tape or take
items.ex_en: He accidentally managed to tape over his sister's wedding video with football highlights.
items.ex_zh: 他不小心用足球集锦把姐姐的婚礼录像给覆盖重录了。

items.def_en: record a performance, scene, or event onto videotape or video media
items.ex_en: Security guards set up hidden equipment to videotape every unauthorized visitor entering.
items.ex_zh: 保安架设了隐蔽设备，给进入的每一位未经许可的访客录像。

items.def_zh: 预先录制，预先录音（或录像）
items.def_en: To record sound, television programs, or other material in advance before broadcasting or using it.
items.ex_en: The radio station opted to prerecord the holiday broadcast a week in advance.
items.ex_zh: 广播电台选择提前一周预先录制节日特别节目。

items.def_zh: 重拍，补拍（电影镜头或照片）
items.def_en: To film a scene or photograph something again, often to improve or correct it.
items.ex_en: The perfectionist director forced the exhausted actors to reshoot the dramatic scene.
items.ex_zh: 追求完美的导演强迫精疲力竭的演员们重拍那场戏剧性的戏码。

groups.summary_en: This operational domain captures technical actions in audio-visual and film production pipelines where performances or scenes are captured, prepared in advance, or recaptured due to technical or narrative necessity.
groups.summary_zh: 影视与音频制作中对画面或声音进行的录制、预先准备或重新拍摄。
groups.desc_en: Denotes capturing audiovisual content onto physical or digital storage media, differing from mere observation or live viewing by its mechanical inscription and reproductive permanence.
groups.desc_zh: 指将视听素材记录并固化到物理或数字介质上的制作工序，与单纯的“目击观看”区别在于其机械写入与可重放的留存属性。
groups.nuance_en: film: capturing motion pictures photographically or cinematically (scene / movie / documentary) · tape: recording audiovisual material onto magnetic tape or casual electronic tracks (show / interview / event) · prerecord: recording material in advance prior to scheduled transmission or playback (broadcast / segment / music) · reshoot: re-recording a scene to fix flaws or alter artistic direction (scene / take / sequence)
groups.nuance_zh: film: 以胶片感或电影级手法拍摄动态影像 (scene / movie / documentary) · tape: 以磁带或常规电子设备录制音视频 (show / interview / event) · prerecord: 在正式播出或上映前预先录制备用 (broadcast / segment / music) · reshoot: 为弥补瑕疵或调整调度而重新补拍 (scene / take / sequence)

groups.name: Castrate & Sterilize · 绝育与去势 (Neuter, Geld, Spay)
groups.tip: 切除生殖器官以绝育或驯服

items.def_en: To castrate a male domestic fowl to improve the quality of its flesh
items.ex_en: The traditional farmer sought to caponize the young roosters for the royal banquet.
items.ex_zh: 传统农夫试图阉割那些年轻的公鸡，以备王室宴席之需。

items.def_zh: 为（动物）做绝育手术；使失去效力（或力量）
items.def_en: 1. To surgically remove the reproductive organs of an animal so that it cannot produce offspring. 2. To make something harmless or ineffective.
items.ex_en: The shelter advises all prospective owners to neuter their adopted cats promptly.
items.ex_zh: 收容所建议所有领养者及时为领养的猫咪做绝育手术。

items.def_en: To render an animal or human permanently incapable of producing offspring
items.ex_en: The state formerly sanctioned coercive measures to sterilize individuals deemed mentally unfit.
items.ex_zh: 该国过去曾批准采取强制手段，对被认为心智不健全者施行绝育手术。

items.def_zh: 阉割，给……去势；使丧失力量（或效果），削弱
items.def_en: 1. To remove the testicles of a male animal or person. 2. To deprive something of its power, vigor, or effectiveness.
items.ex_en: The veterinarian arrived at dawn to castrate several young bulls on the ranch.
items.ex_zh: 兽医清晨赶到牧场，给几头年轻的小公牛做去势手术。

items.def_zh: 阉割，给（雄性动物，尤指公马）去势；剥夺……的活力
items.def_en: To castrate a male animal, especially a horse; to deprive something of vitality or strength.
items.ex_en: The master ordered the stable hands to geld the unruly young stallion immediately.
items.ex_zh: 马主命令马厩杂工立即将这匹桀骜不驯的年轻公马阉割。

items.def_zh: 切除（雌性动物的）卵巢，为（雌性动物）做绝育手术
items.def_en: To surgically remove the ovaries of a female animal so that it cannot produce young.
items.ex_en: The clinic offers a low-cost service to spay stray female dogs regularly.
items.ex_zh: 该诊所定期提供低成本服务，为流浪母犬切除卵巢。

items.def_en: To deprive a male animal or human of male reproductive organs
items.ex_en: Ancient ritualistic codes permitted high priests to surgically emasculate captured enemy warriors.
items.ex_zh: 古老的宗教仪式法令允许大祭司通过外科手段阉割被俘的敌方武士。

groups.summary_en: Veterinary and biological agents surgically remove or disable reproductive organs in animals or humans to eliminate fertility or suppress sex drive.
groups.summary_zh: 通过外科手术切除或灭活生殖腺，使机体丧失生育能力。
groups.desc_en: Denotes surgically rendering an organism permanently incapable of biological reproduction, differing from temporary contraception by its irreversible anatomical ablation.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过外科手术切除生殖器官以使其永久丧失生育能力，与“可逆避孕”区别在于其不可逆的解剖学切除性。
groups.nuance_en: castrate: removing the male testicles of animals or humans (male / bull / criminal) · neuter: generic desexing of domestic companion animals regardless of sex (pets / dogs / cats) · spay: surgical excision of the ovaries and uterus of a female animal (female dog / cat / heifer) · geld: castrating an adult male horse or livestock for pacification (horse / stallion / colt) · sterilize: broad clinical rendering infertile of any organism or medical instrument (patient / population / animals)
groups.nuance_zh: castrate: 摘除雄性动物或人类的睾丸 (male / bull / criminal) · neuter: 对家养宠物进行中性化的去势绝育统称 (pets / dogs / cats) · spay: 手术摘除雌性动物的卵巢与子宫 (female dog / cat / heifer) · geld: 阉割成年公马或牲畜以去性烈、便驭服 (horse / stallion / colt) · sterilize: 广义的临床使个体丧失生育力或器具灭菌 (patient / population / animals)

groups.name: Casual Party Circulation & Mixing · 穿梭应酬与随性社交 (Mingle, Socialize, Hobnob)
groups.tip: 在宴会社交圈中走动攀谈

items.def_en: associate or converse freely with others in a social gathering
items.ex_en: Despite her natural shyness, she managed to mix in at the dinner party.
items.ex_zh: 尽管生性害羞，她还是在晚宴上成功融入了社交圈。
items.ex2_en: Gently mix in the dark chocolate chips after beating the cake batter.
items.ex2_zh: 打匀蛋糕糊后，轻轻拌入黑巧克力碎粒。

items.def_en: spend time socializing casually and familiarly with others
items.ex_en: He spent the entire weekend palled around with foreign delegates at the resort.
items.ex_zh: 整个周末他都和外国代表在度假村里结伴交往、厮混应酬。

items.def_zh: 在社交场合走动应酬，交际；（使）混合，融合
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) to move around and chat with people socially at an event. 2. (+ with) to mix or combine together.
items.ex_en: The friendly host encouraged all the newly arrived guests to mingle freely.
items.ex_zh: 热情的房东鼓励所有新到的客人们自由走动应酬。
items.ex2_en: The bartender mingled fresh fruit juices with sparkling water to make punch.
items.ex2_zh: 调酒师将新鲜果汁与苏打水混合在一起制作宾治饮品。

items.def_zh: 社交，交际，联谊；使适应社会生活，使社会化
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) to spend time enjoying oneself socially with other people. 2. to train someone to behave in ways that are acceptable in their society.
items.ex_en: She enjoys attending weekend charity events to socialize with fellow community leaders.
items.ex_zh: 她喜欢参加周末慈善活动，与其他社区领袖联谊交际。

items.def_en: (+ with) to meet and spend time with famous or important people in social contexts
items.ex_en: At the film festival, aspiring young actors rub shoulders with celebrated industry legends.
items.ex_zh: 在电影节上，满怀抱负的年轻演员得以与大名鼎鼎的业界传奇并肩交往。

items.def_zh: 亲热交际，与（名流等）过从甚密
items.def_en: (+ with) to mix socially, especially with people of higher social status
items.ex_en: He frequently attends exclusive charity galas to hobnob with the city's wealthy elite.
items.ex_zh: 他经常出席高档慈善晚会，与本市的名流富豪过从甚密。

items.def_en: [I/T] (+ with) to talk informally with others, especially to gain an advantage or make connections
items.ex_en: The ambitious junior executive tried to schmooze with the board members during cocktails.
items.ex_zh: 雄心勃勃的初级主管在鸡尾酒会上试图与董事会成员套近乎。

groups.summary_en: Characterizes the manner in which people move freely among others at a gathering, making small talk and building cordial ties. 'Socialize' is standard behavioral integration, 'mingle' highlights moving smoothly from group to group, and 'hobnob' implies familiar association with elite or influential figures.
groups.summary_zh: 在社交场合中周旋走动、与各方搭话应酬的动态姿态。
groups.desc_en: Denotes fluid, self-propelled movement among different social actors in an informal gathering, contrasting with formal diplomatic audiences by its casual, transactional, or egalitarian intermingling.
groups.desc_zh: 指在社交聚会中流转于不同人群之间展开非正式攀谈，与拘谨严肃的“正式会见”区别在于其随意、穿梭与建立社交联系的流动性。
groups.nuance_en: mingle: moving fluidly among guests at an event to strike up diverse conversations (guests / crowd / partygoers) · socialize: participating broadly in communal interactions for leisure (colleagues / neighbors / friends) · hobnob: associating intimately or conspicuously with higher-status elites (celebrities / royalty / politicians) · schmooze: conversational networking aimed at ingratiating oneself for personal or career gain (clients / agents / donors)
groups.nuance_zh: mingle: 在人群中穿梭流转，与不同宾客搭话结识 (guests / crowd / partygoers) · socialize: 广泛参与社交活动以休闲联谊 (colleagues / neighbors / friends) · hobnob: 与名流高层显赫人物亲密往来、攀附交际 (celebrities / royalty / politicians) · schmooze: 带着功利或自肥目的的套近乎、热络社交 (clients / agents / donors)

groups.name: Catalyze & Precipitate · 催化与加速促成 (Catalyze, Precipitate, Spark)
groups.tip: 充当催化剂以加速转变

items.def_en: (+ sth) to cause something to happen or bring a major change into being
items.ex_en: The widespread adoption of AI is likely to bring about major changes in the job market.
items.ex_zh: 人工智能的广泛应用可能会给就业市场带来重大变革。

items.def_en: to ignite or cause the sudden beginning of a process or reaction
items.ex_en: The sudden tax hike sparked fierce outrage across the entire working-class community.
items.ex_zh: 突然的税率上调在整个工薪阶层社区引发了强烈愤慨。

items.def_en: to cause a process, development, or rate of change to happen faster
items.ex_en: Strategic investments in digital infrastructure will accelerate economic growth across the country.
items.ex_zh: 对数字基础设施的战略投资将加速全国的经济增长。

items.def_en: 1. (chemistry) To speed up a chemical reaction by acting as a catalyst. 2. To cause an important event or change to happen or start.
items.ex_en: Her impassioned speech served to catalyze an epochal uprising against the tyranny.
items.ex_zh: 她慷慨激昂的演说催化了一场反抗暴政的划时代起义。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to precipitate a sudden chain of events, a series of actions, or a crisis
items.ex_en: A single reckless comment set off a furious diplomatic crisis between both nations.
items.ex_zh: 一句鲁莽的言论在两国之间激起了一场激烈的外交危机。

items.def_zh: 诱发，触发（剧烈动荡或冲突）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to suddenly precipitate a violent, rapid, or dramatic reaction
items.ex_en: The sudden announcement of price hikes touched off violent protests across the capital.
items.ex_zh: 突然宣布的涨价消息在首都全城引发了暴力抗议。

items.def_zh: 陡然引致，加速促成（突发事件）
items.def_en: to make an event or crisis happen suddenly, unexpectedly, or prematurely
items.ex_en: The minister's sudden resignation precipitated a severe political crisis within the ruling coalition.
items.ex_zh: 部长的突然辞职在执政联盟内部陡然引致了一场严重的政治危机。

groups.summary_en: This frame refers to agents, events, or substances that cause an action, transformation, or reaction to happen much more rapidly without themselves being depleted. 'Catalyze' stresses structural or chemical-like acceleration of change, whereas 'precipitate' focuses on abruptly bringing about an outcome.
groups.summary_zh: 充当催化剂或引线，加速、激发某重大事态或转变的发生。
groups.desc_en: Denotes setting off, accelerating, or abruptly bringing about a dramatic chain of consequences or crisis, differing from slow evolutionary development by its ignition-like speed and structural trigger effect.
groups.desc_zh: 指诱发、加速或突发性地促成戏剧性事件或危机连锁反应，与缓慢的“渐变发展”区别在于其导火索式的点火速度与结构性促动机制。
groups.nuance_en: catalyze: accelerating a transformative social, chemical, or intellectual shift without being consumed (change / movement / transformation) · precipitate: abruptly causing a crisis or unforeseen catastrophe to happen prematurely (crisis / collapse / conflict) · spark: instantly igniting an intense, widespread emotional or physical upheaval (protest / riot / debate) · set off: triggering a cascading chain reaction or explosive episode (alarm / explosion / wave)
groups.nuance_zh: catalyze: 催化并大幅加速变革进程而自身不被损耗 (change / movement / transformation) · precipitate: 促使危机或突发灾难骤然降临、仓促激化 (crisis / collapse / conflict) · spark: 像火星般瞬间点燃轩然大波或激烈抗争 (protest / riot / debate) · set off: 触动引爆装置从而引发连锁反应或爆发 (alarm / explosion / wave)

groups.name: Cavil & Petty Faultfinding · 吹毛求疵与琐屑挑剔 (Niggle, Nitpick, Cavil)
groups.tip: 吹毛求疵抓住无关痛痒微瑕挑刺

items.def_zh: 吹毛求疵，挑剔细节；使烦恼，纠缠
items.def_en: 1. (+ over/about) to criticize or argue about small, unimportant details. 2. to cause slight, persistent worry or irritation to someone.
items.ex_en: Stop niggling about tiny font sizes when the main report needs major revisions.
items.ex_zh: 主报告还需要大改呢，别再死扣那些微不足道的字号细节了。

items.def_en: (+ sb) repeatedly criticize someone about petty or insignificant matters
items.ex_en: His hypercritical boss constantly picks at his formatting rather than evaluating his ideas.
items.ex_zh: 他那吹毛求疵的老板总是挑剔他的排版，而不是评估他的创意。

items.def_en: (+ sth) focus attention obsessively on small flaws or minor errors
items.ex_en: The meticulous proofreader zeroed in on two minor typos in the draft report.
items.ex_zh: 那位细致入微的校对员死咬着草案报告中的两处微小笔误不放。

items.def_en: (+ at/about) to make unnecessary complaints or petty criticisms about negligible points
items.ex_en: The haughty reviewer caviled at the author's subtle stylistic choices throughout the novel.
items.ex_zh: 傲慢的评论家对作者贯穿全书的微妙文风选择吹毛求疵。

items.def_zh: 吹毛求疵，挑剔微小的毛病
items.def_en: (+ over/about) to look for and criticize small, unimportant mistakes in something.
items.ex_en: Please don't nitpick over punctuation marks when the draft is merely preliminary.
items.ex_zh: 这只是初稿，请别在标点符号这样的小地方吹毛求疵。

items.def_zh: 为细枝末节争拗，搬弄琐碎规条
items.def_en: to quibble over petty details or use shady, trivial tricks in an argument
items.ex_en: The cynical lawyer chose to pettifog over obscure procedural technicalities for hours on end.
items.ex_zh: 那个心怀鬼胎的律师一连几个小时搬弄晦涩的程序琐规进行争拗。

items.def_en: (+ at/about) to complain continually about trivial matters in an annoying way
items.ex_en: The dissatisfied client continued to carp about insignificant delays throughout the entire project.
items.ex_zh: 在整个项目过程中，那位不满意的客户不断对无关紧要的延误唠叨抱怨。

groups.summary_en: Focuses on the irritating manner of finding fault in microscopic, irrelevant particulars while ignoring substantial merit. Verbs differ in whether they emphasize irritating fussiness ('niggle'), obsessive inspection ('nitpick'), or frivolous argumentative objections ('cavil').
groups.summary_zh: 关注挑剔微不足道的细节瑕疵，小题大做地挑刺争拗。
groups.desc_en: Denotes persistently raising trivial, pedantic, or annoying objections to minor details, differing from constructive evaluation by its obstructionist, petty, and hyper-critical posture.
groups.desc_zh: 指在枝微末节上持续提出琐碎、教条或令人反感的责难，与建设性的“客观评审”区别在于其偏执狭隘与挑剔捣乱的心态。
groups.nuance_en: cavil: raising frivolous and unnecessary objections to fine points of an argument (details / rules / terms) · nitpick: fussy, microscopic searching for trivial imperfections (grammar / wording / layout) · niggle: persistently worrying, nagging, or irritating over tiny unresolved details (worries / doubts / issues) · carp: constant, querulous finding fault in a bitter, unconstructive tone (complaints / critic / spouse)
groups.nuance_zh: cavil: 就微末细枝无端辩驳、吹毛求疵 (details / rules / terms) · nitpick: 显微镜式挑剔无关痛痒的字句排版瑕疵 (grammar / wording / layout) · niggle: 纠缠于微小顾虑或使人烦扰不休 (worries / doubts / issues) · carp: 喋喋不休、尖酸怨艾地挑错抱怨 (complaints / critic / spouse)

groups.name: Celebrate & Revel · 欣喜与狂欢 (Rejoice, Revel, Carouse)
groups.tip: 举杯欢庆沉浸在极度喜悦中

items.def_en: to mark a happy event or milestone with enjoyable public or social festivities
items.ex_en: The entire town gathered in the plaza to celebrate the hard-won championship victory.
items.ex_zh: 全镇居民聚集在广场上，共同庆祝这来之不易的锦标赛胜利。

items.def_en: to enjoy oneself socially by drinking, laughing, and celebrating cheerfully
items.ex_en: The villagers gathered beneath the midsummer moon to drink cider and make merry.
items.ex_zh: 村民们聚集在仲夏的月色下，畅饮苹果酒，欢宴作乐。

items.def_en: continue celebrating or reveling rowdily
items.ex_en: Even after the music stopped at midnight, they decided to party on at Mark's apartment.
items.ex_zh: 尽管午夜时分音乐已经停了，他们还是决定去马克家继续嗨。

items.def_en: spend time enjoying oneself extravagantly and enthusiastically
items.ex_en: After landing the major bonus, the young executives decided to live it up.
items.ex_zh: 拿到巨额奖金后，年轻的高管们决定尽情狂欢寻乐一番。

items.def_en: 1. (+ at/over/in) To feel or show great happiness about something.
items.ex_en: The victorious soldiers rejoiced over the sudden arrival of long-awaited, glorious peace.
items.ex_zh: 获胜的士兵们为久违的光荣和平的突降而欢欣庆贺。

items.def_zh: 狂欢作乐，纵情庆祝；陶醉于，沉醉于（revel in）
items.def_en: 1. To celebrate, dance, or drink in a noisy, lively way. 2. ('revel in') To get great pleasure, satisfaction, or delight from something.
items.ex_en: The boisterous crowd continued to revel until the morning sun crested the horizon.
items.ex_zh: 喧闹的人群纵情庆祝，狂欢作乐，直到旭日跃出地平线。

items.def_en: to drink alcohol heavily, party loudly, and revel in a rowdy, uncontrolled manner
items.ex_en: The rowdy sailors went ashore to carouse until dawn in the tavern.
items.ex_zh: 喧闹的水手们上岸在酒馆里痛饮狂欢，纵酒作乐直到天明。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame mark an escalation from internal, elevated happiness to loud, hedonistic public merrymaking and abandoned, rowdy partying.
groups.summary_zh: 指由心怀极大欢悦逐步升级为喧闹、放纵乃至醉饮的狂欢庆贺。
groups.desc_en: Denotes engaging in jubilant festive celebration or riotous sensory gratification, differing from calm inner happiness by its overt, demonstrative, and often uninhibited public display.
groups.desc_zh: 指沉浸于欢欣庆祝或放浪形骸的感官享乐之中，与内敛平静的“欣喜”区别在于其外显性、仪式狂欢感及行为上的不加节制。
groups.nuance_en: celebrate: marking an honor, achievement, or milestone with commemorative festivities (victory / anniversary / success) · rejoice: expressing profound, uplifting spiritual or moral exultation (heart / triumph / news) · revel: taking unrestrained, visceral delight in a hedonistic atmosphere (luxury / victory / freedom) · carouse: indulging in rowdy, loud, alcohol-fueled partying late into the night (drinkers / sailors / partygoers)
groups.nuance_zh: celebrate: 通过庆典或聚会仪式性地庆贺胜利、里程碑 (victory / anniversary / success) · rejoice: 表达发自内心的深沉欣喜、感恩或崇高欢愉 (heart / triumph / news) · revel: 沉湎纵情于感官狂欢或陶醉于某项成就 (luxury / victory / freedom) · carouse: 聚众豪饮、夜夜笙歌的喧嚣狂饮寻欢 (drinkers / sailors / partygoers)

groups.name: Chaff & Heckle · 讥嘲与起哄 (Twit, Heckle, Chaff)
groups.tip: 用言辞挖苦、嘲笑或起哄

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) tease or mock someone in a playful or slightly mocking way
items.ex_en: The comedians frequently poke fun at arrogant politicians during their late-night talk show.
items.ex_zh: 喜剧演员经常在他们的深夜脱口秀节目中打趣傲慢的政客。

items.def_en: to poke fun at someone in a friendly, informal manner
items.ex_en: His teammates continued to rib him good-naturedly about his terrible new haircut.
items.ex_zh: 队友们善意地拿他糟糕的新发型不停地开玩笑取乐。

items.def_en: 1. (dated or informal) To tease, mock, or playfully reproach someone about a fault or mistake.
items.ex_en: His older brother loved to twit him playfully about his clumsy cooking mistakes.
items.ex_zh: 他哥哥总喜欢拿他笨拙的下厨糗事戏弄嘲笑他。

items.def_en: to tease someone in a lighthearted, good-natured way
items.ex_en: The old scholar loved to chaff his devoted students about their youthful vanities.
items.ex_zh: 那位老学者喜欢打趣他忠实的门生们身上那些年轻人的虚荣心。

items.def_en: to deliberately annoy someone by persistent petty teasing or critical prodding
items.ex_en: He knew exactly which painful topic to needle his sister about during dinner.
items.ex_zh: 他深知在晚餐时提起哪件痛处能故意数落挤兑他妹妹。

items.def_en: (+ sb) silence or drown out a speaker by shouting or heckling loudly
items.ex_en: The angry crowd shouted down the politician before he could finish his opening remarks.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的群众大声起哄，让那位政客开场白还没说完就无法继续了。

items.def_zh: 起哄，喝倒彩，打断（演讲者等）；梳理（麻等）
items.def_en: 1. To interrupt a public speaker or performer with loud, aggressive, or mocking comments. 2. To dress or comb flax or hemp.
items.ex_en: Angry protestors attempted to heckle the visiting politician throughout his entire opening address.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的抗议者在来访政客的整个开幕演讲中不断大声起哄喝倒彩。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe teasing someone either through mild, nagging reminders of faults, persistent lighthearted ribbing, or disruptive public interruptions during an address.
groups.summary_zh: 以戏弄揭短、揶揄取笑或公开起哄打断的方式促狭质难。
groups.desc_en: Denotes targeting a speaker or performer with provocative verbal mockery or interruptions, differing from friendly praise by its aggressive, disruptive, or teasingly destabilizing nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指以嘲弄话语或骚扰性插话针对发言者/表演者，与善意的“赞扬应和”区别在于其具有挑衅性、打乱节奏或戏弄拆台的属性。
groups.nuance_en: chaff: good-naturedly bantering or teasing without venom (comrades / friends / colleagues) · rib: playful, good-humored elbow-poking teasing about personal quirks (brother / buddy / teammate) · needle: persistently and slyly provoking someone to needle a reaction (rival / opponent / boss) · heckle: aggressively shouting taunts and interruptions to disrupt a public speaker (speaker / politician / comic) · shout down: overwhelming a speaker's voice through sheer collective shouting volume (speaker / opposition / dissenters)
groups.nuance_zh: chaff: 善意打趣、无伤大雅地插科打诨 (comrades / friends / colleagues) · rib: 拿亲近之人的习性或失误善意取笑揶揄 (brother / buddy / teammate) · needle: 蓄意且狡黠地用言语挑衅以激怒对方 (rival / opponent / boss) · heckle: 在公共集会中公开发难喝倒彩以打断发言 (speaker / politician / comic) · shout down: 凭借集体的声浪压制并淹没发言者的声音 (speaker / opposition / dissenters)

groups.name: Cheat & Exploit · 侵吞与剥削 (Short, Profiteer, Gouge)
groups.tip: 短斤少两不法克扣

items.def_en: to give less change than is due, or to treat someone unfairly by withholding full value
items.ex_en: The dishonest street vendor tried to shortchange unsuspecting tourists on their change yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 那个奸诈的街头小贩昨天企图给毫无戒心的游客少找零钱。

items.def_zh: 克扣，少给（钱物或找零）；使短路；（金融）卖空，做空
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To cheat someone by giving them less than the full amount of money, goods, or change owed. 2. To cause or undergo an electrical short circuit. 3. (finance) To sell a security or commodity short.
items.ex_en: The crooked cashier tried to short the hurried customer by twenty whole dollars.
items.ex_zh: 那个心术不正的收银员企图克扣那个匆忙的顾客整整二十美元找零。

items.def_en: (+ sb) cheat someone by charging them too much money for something
items.ex_en: Unsuspecting tourists are often ripped off by unlicensed taxi operators.
items.ex_zh: 毫无防备的游客经常被无照出租车司机敲竹杠。

items.def_en: to deprive someone of money or property by fraud, extortion, or exorbitant fees
items.ex_en: The shady mechanic managed to fleece naive car owners with exorbitant repair fees.
items.ex_zh: 那个黑心汽修工用离谱的修理费敲了天真车主们的竹杠。

items.def_zh: 敲诈；哄抬价格漫天要价
items.def_en: to overcharge someone grossly, especially in a monopoly or emergency situation
items.ex_en: Gas stations began to gouge desperate drivers right after the hurricane struck the coast.
items.ex_zh: 飓风袭击沿海地区后，加油站立刻开始向走投无路的司机漫天要价。

items.def_en: (disapproving) To make an unfair or excessive profit, especially by charging exorbitant prices during a shortage, crisis, or war.
items.ex_en: Unscrupulous merchants attempted to profiteer from the acute shortage of essential medical supplies.
items.ex_zh: 不法商贩企图趁关键医疗物资严重短缺之际牟取暴利。

items.def_en: to take property or money from someone by deliberate deception or illegal artifice
items.ex_en: The rogue accountant conspired to defraud elderly clients out of their retirement savings.
items.ex_zh: 那名不法会计密谋诈骗老年客户的退休积蓄。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote illicitly withholding what is owed, making unfair commercial gains, or extracting exorbitant sums from vulnerable parties during transactions.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过少给应付款项、哄抬价格或不正当交易手段侵吞利益与剥削他人。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deliberately swindling, depriving, or taking predatory economic advantage of a weaker counterparty, differing from fair trade by its sharp deception or coercive extortion.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过欺诈手段或利用对方弱势地位攫取不当暴利，与正当的“商业溢价”区别在于其欺瞒性、侵吞性与掠夺性压榨。
groups.nuance_en: shortchange: unfairly giving less change, value, or attention than is rightfully owed (customers / students / public) · gouge: extortionately overcharging during shortages or captive markets (consumers / prices / renters) · rip off: blatantly overcharging or defrauding a vulnerable buyer (tourists / victims / customers) · fleece: systematically stripping a naive mark of their money or valuables (investors / marks / tourists) · profiteer: exploiting public emergencies or scarcity to reap exorbitant unethical margins (war / crisis / pandemic)
groups.nuance_zh: shortchange: 故意少给零钱，或在质量、待遇上予以克扣 (customers / students / public) · gouge: 趁灾难或垄断之危疯狂哄抬物价、索取暴利 (consumers / prices / renters) · rip off: 明目张胆地狠宰或通过劣质冒充敲诈买家 (tourists / victims / customers) · fleece: 像剪羊毛般系统性侵吞敲骨吸髓、榨干受害者钱财 (investors / marks / tourists) · profiteer: 借战乱、疫情或物资匮乏之机大发不义国难财 (war / crisis / pandemic)

groups.name: Chisel, Flake & Hew Material · 凿削与刻裂削打 (Hewn, Knap, Striate)
groups.tip: 砍削石木原料以雕琢成器

items.def_en: [I/T] to cut or break small fragments off the edge or surface of hard material
items.ex_en: The mason used a hammer to chip small fragments off the granite slab.
items.ex_zh: 石匠用铁锤从花岗岩石板边缘敲下细小的碎块。
items.ex2_en: The delicate ceramic mug chipped when it hit the edge of the sink.
items.ex2_zh: 精致的陶瓷杯撞到水槽边缘时磕掉了一小块。

items.def_en: to cut or press a long, narrow furrow into a surface
items.ex_en: The carpenter used a special plane to groove the wooden panels for assembly.
items.ex_zh: 木匠用专门的刨子在木板上压出凹槽以便组装。

items.def_zh: 使有条纹，加条痕（或沟槽）
items.def_en: to mark a surface with fine stripes, grooves, or parallel lines.
items.ex_en: Centuries of glacial movement had begun to striate the ancient mountain bedrock.
items.ex_zh: 数个世纪的冰川运动在古老山脉的基岩上磨出斑斑条痕。

items.def_en: (+ at sth) gradually break small pieces off a hard material by striking it
items.ex_en: Sculptors slowly chip away at the marble block to reveal the figure beneath.
items.ex_zh: 雕刻家在整块大理石上慢慢敲凿，使下面的雕像显现出来。

items.def_zh: 敲琢（打制燧石等石器）；敲碎
items.def_en: to shape flint or stone into tools or building blocks by striking off flakes.
items.ex_en: The ancient craftsman sat quietly to knap raw flint into razor-sharp hunting arrowheads.
items.ex_zh: 远古工匠静坐着敲琢天然燧石，将其打制成锋利的猎箭箭镞。

items.def_en: (+ sth) carve, shape, or cut something out of stone or timber by heavy cutting strokes
items.ex_en: Hermits laboured for decades to hew out sacred chapels from the sheer cliff.
items.ex_zh: 隐士们辛劳数十年，在陡峭的悬崖峭壁上凿刻出神圣的礼拜堂。

items.def_en: to shape or chop heavy wood or stone by forceful blows of an ax or chisel
items.ex_en: Pioneers wielded broad axes to hew sturdy oak logs for their frontier cabins.
items.ex_zh: 开拓者们挥舞宽刃斧劈砍坚硬的橡木原木，用来搭建边境小木屋。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote rough-shaping, fracturing, or grooving rigid raw materials (such as stone, flint, or timber) by blunt-force chipping, cleaving, or scoring with fine parallel furrows.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过击打、劈凿或削划使石材木料成形或形成条纹肌理。
groups.desc_en: Denotes subtractively shaping, splitting, or incising rigid mineral or woody material via struck edged tools, contrasting with soft molding by its brittle fracturing and forceful reduction.
groups.desc_zh: 指借助刃具施加外力以击打、碎裂或刻凿硬质矿石或木材，与“泥塑铸模”区别在于其利用材质脆断特性的减材加工力学。
groups.nuance_en: chip: dislodging small flakes or fragments from an edge by sharp light impact (stone / paint / flint) · knap: flaking brittle stone like flint with controlled percussion into sharp tools (flint / stone / arrowhead) · hew: forcefully felling, dressing, or roughing out heavy timber or stone using an ax or adze (timber / stone / logs) · striate: marking a hard surface with fine parallel structural grooves or scratches (rock / surface / metal)
groups.nuance_zh: chip: 经轻巧叩击从边缘崩碎或削下细小碎屑 (stone / paint / flint) · knap: 运用受控敲击法打制燧石等硬脆石料以制成刃器 (flint / stone / arrowhead) · hew: 用斧、锛重力砍劈原木或粗加工石料 (timber / stone / logs) · striate: 在硬质表面刻画出平行条纹或细密凹槽 (rock / surface / metal)

groups.name: Claim & Assert · 声称与坚持 (Allege, Claim, Insist, Assert)
groups.tip: 从单方断言到法理定罪性声称

items.def_en: to state that something is true, typically without providing proof
items.ex_en: The suspect continued to claim that he was sleeping when the robbery occurred.
items.ex_zh: 嫌疑人坚称案发时他正在睡觉，却未提供任何证据。

items.def_zh: 坚持（说法/声明），忠于原主张
items.def_en: (+ sth) maintain the truth or validity of an assertion without wavering
items.ex_en: I will stand by my decision regardless of public criticism.
items.ex_zh: 无论外界如何批评，我都会坚持自己的决定。

items.def_en: to continue to argue or insist that something is true against skepticism or opposition
items.ex_en: Defense counsel continued to maintain that their client acted strictly in self-defense.
items.ex_zh: 辩方律师顶住外界质疑，坚称其当事人完全属于正当防卫。

items.def_zh: （未提出充分证据而）声称，断言，指控
items.def_en: To state that someone has done something wrong or illegal, especially without having yet proved it.
items.ex_en: Prosecutors allege that the former executive embezzled millions in corporate development funds.
items.ex_zh: 检方指控这位前高管侵吞了数百万公司的发展资金。

items.def_en: (+ sth) assert emphatically or solemnly that something is true
items.ex_en: The key witness was entirely willing to swear to the driver's reckless behavior.
items.ex_zh: 关键证人完全愿意发誓证实该司机存在危险驾驶行为。

items.def_zh: 坚持说，硬说；坚决要求，坚持主张
items.def_en: 1. To state firmly and clearly that something is true, especially when others disagree. 2. (+ on) To demand that something happen, refusing to accept any opposition.
items.ex_en: The manager chose to insist that all employees attend the emergency morning briefing.
items.ex_zh: 经理坚决要求所有员工都必须参加紧急早会。

items.def_en: to state a fact or belief firmly, positively, and forcefully
items.ex_en: The spokesperson chose to assert that the company followed all environmental safety standards.
items.ex_zh: 发言人坚定声明，公司严格遵守了所有环境安全标准。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote stating that something is true, ranging from making formal unproven accusations to forceful, unyielding declarations of personal belief or fact.
groups.summary_zh: 指陈述某事属实，从无实据的指称逐步升级至坚定强硬的断言。
groups.desc_en: Denotes putting forward a factual proposition as true in the face of possible doubt or contestation, differing from an undisputed report by the speaker's loaded burden of proof.
groups.desc_zh: 指在面临潜在质疑或缺乏确证的情况下，坚称某事实主张属实，与中立的“陈述报道”区别在于其言说者背负的举证责任与断言张力。
groups.nuance_en: claim: asserting an unproven fact or rightful ownership subject to validation (responsibility / damages / title) · assert: stating a proposition positively, confidently, and forcefully (innocence / authority / rights) · allege: stating a wrongdoing without conclusive proof, typically in legal contexts (fraud / corruption / misconduct) · insist: demanding or declaring stubbornly despite opposition or contrary belief (innocence / terms / truth)
groups.nuance_zh: claim: 声明某项未经最终证实的权利或事实主张 (responsibility / damages / title) · assert: 笃定、自信且有力地宣称某论断或行使权利 (innocence / authority / rights) · allege: 在司法语境下指控某人不端，但尚未坐实定罪 (fraud / corruption / misconduct) · insist: 面对怀疑、异议仍顽固坚称或执意要求 (innocence / terms / truth)

groups.name: Compile & Index · 汇编与编目索引 (Compile, Index)
groups.tip: 收集汇总资料编排成册

items.def_en: 1. To create an alphabetical index for a book, document, or collection. 2. To list or record something in an index.
items.ex_en: The university archivist worked diligently to index thousands of historical town records.
items.ex_zh: 大学档案员勤勉工作，为数千份城镇历史档案编制索引。

items.def_zh: 汇编；整理汇集（资料、清单等）
items.def_en: (+ sth) assemble or compile information, documents, or data into a unified list or document
items.ex_en: Analysts had to put together a comprehensive market report within two days.
items.ex_zh: 分析师们必须在两天之内汇编出一份全面的市场报告。

items.def_zh: 拟定；起草编制（清单、文件或表格）
items.def_en: (+ sth) prepare and write out a systematic list, document, or plan
items.ex_en: The legal team drew up a comprehensive contract for the acquisition.
items.ex_zh: 法律团队为此次收购拟定了一份详尽的合同。

items.def_en: 1. To collect information from various sources and arrange it into a book, list, or report. 2. (computing) To translate source code into machine code.
items.ex_en: The research team spent months trying to compile regional demographic data into reports.
items.ex_zh: 研究小组花了数月时间将区域人口统计数据汇编成报告。

items.def_en: to list, classify, and systematically describe items in a catalog
items.ex_en: Librarians worked around the clock to catalog newly acquired rare manuscript collections.
items.ex_zh: 图书管理员夜以继日地将新入藏的珍贵手稿逐一编入目录。

items.def_zh: 核对整理，校勘（各源数据）
items.def_en: to collect, compare, and assemble information or pages in their proper order
items.ex_en: The clerk had to collate hundreds of scattered survey responses before final review.
items.ex_zh: 在最终审查前，办事员必须将数百份零散的问卷结果核对整理成序。

items.def_en: to arrange information, figures, or data into systematic columns and rows
items.ex_en: Statisticians began to tabulate election results into neat columns for public display.
items.ex_zh: 统计人员开始将选举结果制成整齐的表格以便向公众公布。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to organizing, structuring, and systematizing collected information, documents, or data into comprehensive reference formats or searchable catalogs.
groups.summary_zh: 搜集并系统化编排信息成册、清单或检索目录。
groups.desc_en: Denotes gathering disparate documentary items, data, or materials and systematically organizing them into a unified catalog or directory, contrasting with authoring original content by its aggregating and structural curation.
groups.desc_zh: 指将零散的文献、数据或条目搜集起来，并系统性地梳理编排成集册或索引，与创作新内容的“撰写”区别在于其汇聚与结构化整理属性。
groups.nuance_en: compile: collecting information from multiple existing sources into an orderly compendium (dossier / report / statistics) · index: providing an alphabetical or thematic pointer system for rapid retrieval of records (book / documents / archives) · catalog: systematically listing and detailing an inventory of items according to a scheme (collection / artifacts / library) · collate: assembling and critically comparing pages or datasets in proper logical sequence (data / evidence / manuscripts)
groups.nuance_zh: compile: 从多方来源搜集信息汇编成完整的数据集或报告 (dossier / report / statistics) · index: 为文献或数据建立字母表或主题检索索引系统 (book / documents / archives) · catalog: 依据既定分类体系将馆藏或存货逐一登记录目 (collection / artifacts / library) · collate: 仔细校勘、排序并对照多份文稿或数据序列 (data / evidence / manuscripts)

groups.name: Confiscate & Expropriate by Authority · 官方征用与没收 (Confiscate, Seize, Impound)
groups.tip: 权威机构依法或强行充公

items.def_en: to take possession of property, contraband, or assets by official warrant or legal force
items.ex_en: Customs agents obtained an official court warrant to seize the smuggled goods.
items.ex_zh: 海关官员取得了法院正式搜查令，依法扣押了这批走私货物。

items.def_en: to officially take private property away from someone as a penalty or legal measure
items.ex_en: Border guards will confiscate any undeclared agricultural products found inside passenger luggage.
items.ex_zh: 边检人员将依法没收在旅客行李中查获的任何未申报农产品。

items.def_en: to take legal custody of an object or vehicle until a fine is paid or case resolved
items.ex_en: Traffic police decided to impound the stolen vehicle until ownership was resolved.
items.ex_zh: 在产权问题解决之前，交警决定扣留这辆被盗车辆。

items.def_zh: 征用（战时或紧急官方调配）
items.def_en: to formally demand and take over supplies, buildings, or vehicles for official or military use
items.ex_en: The military council voted to requisition private transport vehicles during the national emergency.
items.ex_zh: 军事委员会投票决定在国家紧急状态期间征用民用运输车辆。

items.def_zh: 征用，强占（车辆、建筑物等用于军事或官方用途）
items.def_en: to officially take possession or control of private property, vehicles, or buildings, especially for military or emergency use
items.ex_en: Retreating soldiers decided to commandeer private civilian trucks to carry their wounded companions.
items.ex_zh: 撤退的士兵决定强行征用平民卡车来运送负伤的同伴。

items.def_zh: 剥夺（财产、土地等），强夺；逐出
items.def_en: (formal) to deprive someone of land, property, or possessions
items.ex_en: Corrupt landlords conspired to dispossess hundreds of impoverished farmers of their ancestral fields.
items.ex_zh: 不良地主密谋剥夺数百名贫苦农民祖辈相传的田地。

items.def_zh: 征用，没收（私有财产供公用）
items.def_en: (of a government or authority) to officially take away private property or land for public use
items.ex_en: The city council voted to expropriate several riverside plots for new highway construction.
items.ex_zh: 市议会投票决定征用数个临河地块用于建设新公路。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe an authority, government, military, or legal entity seizing private property, land, or resources, either for public/state use or as a punitive forfeiture.
groups.summary_zh: 指官方或司法机构依职权征调、强制接管或没收私人财产。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an authoritative, sovereign, or militarized entity taking physical custody of private property under color of law or state emergency, differing from mere theft by its official procedural justification.
groups.desc_zh: 指执法部门、主权机关或军事当局依据法律法令或紧急征召权，强制接管或扣押私有财产，与非法“盗窃”区别在于其具有公权力外衣与程序正当性主张。
groups.nuance_en: seize: suddenly taking physical or legal control of contraband or assets by official force (contraband / drugs / assets) · confiscate: appropriating private property as a punitive legal penalty for public forfeiture (weapons / goods / property) · impound: placing vehicles or records in secure legal custody pending fine payment or trial (vehicles / car / documents) · requisition: officially demanding property or supplies for state, military, or public use (vehicles / buildings / supplies) · expropriate: taking private land or assets for eminent domain or public infrastructure (land / estates / property)
groups.nuance_zh: seize: 官方凭借强制力突击查封、扣押违禁品或资产 (contraband / drugs / assets) · confiscate: 作为惩罚性法律手段依法没收私有物品归公 (weapons / goods / property) · impound: 将违规车辆或物证暂扣至指定车场或库房待处 (vehicles / car / documents) · requisition: 军政机关因战时或公共紧急事态强制征调物资 (vehicles / buildings / supplies) · expropriate: 政府基于公共利益征收征用私人土地或不动产 (land / estates / property)

groups.name: Connect & Relate in Mind · 关联与联想 (Associate, Relate, Link)
groups.tip: 将不同事物联系在一起

items.def_en: (+ to/with) to make, see, or state a connection between two things
items.ex_en: Researchers repeatedly link high sugar intake to increased risks of chronic disease.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员多次将高糖摄入与慢性病风险升高联系在一起。

items.def_zh: 使联系，把……联系起来；与……有关，涉及；叙述，讲述；理解并产生共鸣
items.def_en: 1. To show or make a connection between two or more things; (relate to) to be connected with. 2. To tell or narrate a story or facts. 3. (relate to) To understand and feel sympathy for someone.
items.ex_en: The introductory chapter seeks to relate economic conditions directly to shifting social unrest.
items.ex_zh: 导论章节试图将当时的经济状况与日益加剧的社会动荡直接联系起来。

items.def_zh: 把……联系在一起，联想；结合，结交，交往
items.def_en: 1. To connect someone or something in one's mind with someone or something else. 2. (associate with) To spend time with someone or have a relationship with them.
items.ex_en: Most people instinctively associate the smell of pine trees with cold winter holidays.
items.ex_zh: 大多数人本能地把松树的气味与寒冷的冬季节日联系起来。

items.def_en: (+ with) to realize or show that a relationship exists between people or things
items.ex_en: Detectives struggle to connect the two seemingly unrelated robberies across separate city districts.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们努力把不同城区发生的两起看似无关的抢劫案联系起来。
items.ex2_en: The quiet country road connects directly with the bustling interstate highway ahead.
items.ex2_zh: 这条宁静的乡村道路直接与前方繁华的州际公路相连。

items.def_zh: 将……与……在脑海中联系起来
items.def_en: (+ sth to sth) mentally associate or link one idea, person, or thing with another
items.ex_en: Voters still tie the former governor to the municipal corruption scandals.
items.ex_zh: 选民们依然在脑海中把前州长与那起市政腐败丑闻联系在一起。

items.def_en: (+ sth) perceive or establish a conceptual or logical connection between things
items.ex_en: The two railway networks are scheduled to link up by the end of next year.
items.ex_zh: 这两条铁路网计划于明年年底实现连通。
items.ex2_en: Engineers linked up the two separate optical fibers across the mountain gorge.
items.ex2_zh: 工程师们将穿过山峡的两条独立光纤连接了起来。

items.def_zh: 相互关联，显示互相关系
items.def_en: [I/T] to bring into or have a mutual or reciprocal relationship
items.ex_en: Subsequent studies failed to correlate elevated blood pressure with occasional caffeine consumption.
items.ex_zh: 随后的研究未能证明高血压与偶发性咖啡因摄入之间存在相互关联。
items.ex2_en: High exercise levels correlate strongly with improved cardiovascular health in most adults.
items.ex2_zh: 对大多数成年人而言，高运动量与心血管健康的改善密切相关。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote an agent mentally drawing a bridge or seeing an inherent relationship between two concepts, entities, or occurrences. 'Relate' points to identifying a logical connection, whereas 'associate' often operates via perceptual or imaginative connection.
groups.summary_zh: 在心智或逻辑上将两个或多个对象联系、联想在一起。
groups.desc_en: Denotes forming or establishing a cognitive or structural correspondence between two mental ideas or phenomena, differing from physical binding by its epistemic or conceptual nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指在两个概念、事物或现象之间建立心智上的联想或逻辑因果纽带，与物理上的“捆绑连接”区别在于其认知与概念关联属性。
groups.nuance_en: associate: mentally connecting an idea, trait, or memory with another entity (name / color / risk) · connect: recognizing a logical link or empirical bridge between two disparate events (events / dots / clues) · correlate: establishing an interdependent statistical or empirical relationship between variables (variables / factors / data) · link: identifying an evidential causal nexus or pipeline between phenomena (smoking / gene / crime)
groups.nuance_zh: associate: 在心智或记忆中将两件事物自发联想在一起 (name / color / risk) · connect: 识破、理清不同离散线索或事件间的内在逻辑 (events / dots / clues) · correlate: 建立两组变量或数据之间互为消长的统计学相关性 (variables / factors / data) · link: 明确指出两者之间客观存在的因果或纽带关系 (smoking / gene / crime)

groups.name: Constitute & Compose · 构成与组成 (Make up, Comprise, Form)
groups.tip: 由部分组装成整体

items.def_zh: 由……组成，由……构成；在于，存在于
items.def_en: 1. (consist of) To be composed or formed of. 2. (consist in) To have something as an essential feature or basis.
items.ex_en: True happiness does not consist in the sheer accumulation of material wealth.
items.ex_zh: 真正的幸福并不在于物质财富的单纯积累。

items.def_en: to be made up of particular parts, or to constitute a whole
items.ex_en: Ten elected delegates and several technical advisors comprise the national advisory committee.
items.ex_zh: 全国咨询委员会由十名民选代表和数位技术顾问组成。

items.def_zh: 组成，构成（常用于被动 be composed of）
items.def_en: (chiefly passive) to be formed from specific elements, substances, or members
items.ex_en: The investigative panel is composed of leading scientists and respected former judges.
items.ex_zh: 调查小组由顶尖科学家和受人尊敬的前法官共同组成。

items.def_en: to combine together to form an entire group, amount, or whole
items.ex_en: Women and young adults make up the vast majority of our volunteer workforce.
items.ex_zh: 妇女和年轻群体构成了我们志愿者队伍的绝大部分。

items.def_en: (+ sth) be formed from or composed of specified parts or elements
items.ex_en: The simple breakfast tray would typically consist of warm porridge, boiled eggs, and tea.
items.ex_zh: 简单的早餐盘通常由热粥、水煮蛋和清茶组成。

items.def_en: (+ sth) combine together to form or constitute a whole
items.ex_en: These disparate minor offenses add up to a serious breach of official regulations.
items.ex_zh: 这些零散的轻微违规行为组合起来便构成了对官方条例的严重违反。

items.def_zh: 构成，组成；被视为，算作；设立，任命
items.def_en: 1. To combine to form a whole; to make up. 2. To be equivalent to or considered as something. 3. To establish or appoint officially.
items.ex_en: Seven independent sovereign nations constitute the newly formed regional trade alliance.
items.ex_zh: 七个独立主权国家构成了这个新建立的区域贸易联盟。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express mereological relationships where parts form a unified whole or a whole is composed of individual elements. Syntactic framing dictates whether parts serve as the subject (make up, form, constitute) or the whole serves as the subject (consist of, comprise).
groups.summary_zh: 表达部分与整体的构成关系，涵盖由部分组成整体或整体包含部分。
groups.desc_en: Denotes serving as the elemental components that structurally make up a whole, or reciprocally, encompassing those parts, differing from dynamic assembly by its stative, defining ontology.
groups.desc_zh: 指各要素在结构上构成一个整体，或整体包容涵盖这些部分，与动作性的“物理装配”区别在于其静态的界定性与本体论包含关系。
groups.nuance_en: constitute: legally, technically, or quantitatively forming the essential essence or whole of something (majority / crime / element) · comprise: encompassing or including parts within a designated whole entity (chapters / states / members) · compose: parts combining together to collectively form a cohesive structure (team / council / music) · make up: flexibly forming the components or percentage share of an aggregated body (workforce / population / deficit)
groups.nuance_zh: constitute: 在法律、定性或数量上充当构成实质或主体 (majority / crime / element) · comprise: 整体由内向外地包含、涵括若干明确组成部分 (chapters / states / members) · compose: 多种部分或要素聚合构筑成有机整体 (team / council / music) · make up: 各部分拼组、构成某总体的具体比例或份额 (workforce / population / deficit)

groups.name: Continuous Inundation & Heavy Fire · 炮火轰击与密集袭击 (Bombard, Barrage, Shell)
groups.tip: 炮火密集倾泻连番猛烈轰击

items.def_en: to fire heavy explosive shells at a fortress, city, or position continuously
items.ex_en: Hostile forces continued to shell the isolated garrison base throughout the freezing night.
items.ex_zh: 敌军在严寒的夜晚持续炮击那座孤立的驻军基地。

items.def_en: (+ sb) attack someone forcefully and relentlessly with blows or harsh criticism
items.ex_en: The furious coach began to lay into his team for their sloppy defending.
items.ex_zh: 暴怒的教练因队员防守松散而开始对他们痛骂一通。

items.def_zh: 如雨点般倾泻于；密集猛烈袭击
items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) fall upon or strike a target in an overwhelming, continuous shower of blows, fire, or criticism
items.ex_en: Scathing public criticism began to rain down on the government after the scandal broke.
items.ex_zh: 丑闻曝光之后，严厉的公众指责如雨点般向政府倾泻而来。

items.def_zh: 以密集炮火轰击；连珠炮似地攻击（质问、投诉等）
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To attack heavily with an overwhelming burst of artillery fire or missiles. 2. (+ with) To bombard someone with a continuous stream of questions, criticisms, or complaints.
items.ex_en: Furious reporters continued to barrage the press secretary with hostile questions regarding corruption.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的记者们连珠炮似地就腐败问题向新闻秘书提出尖锐质问。

items.def_zh: 炮击，轰炸；连番轰炸（提问、投诉等）；用粒子轰击
items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To attack a place continuously with bombs, shells, or missiles. 2. (+ with) To direct a relentless flood of questions, criticisms, or information at someone. 3. (physics) To direct high-energy particles at a substance.
items.ex_en: Disgruntled consumers began to bombard customer service representatives with angry telephone calls today.
items.ex_zh: 不满的消费者今天开始连番拨打愤怒的投诉电话轰炸客服代表。

items.def_en: to strike repeatedly with fists, missiles, or heavy blows
items.ex_en: Violent hailstones continued to pummel the exposed vehicle roofs along the rural highway.
items.ex_zh: 猛烈的冰雹接连重击着乡村公路上暴露在外的汽车车顶。

items.def_en: to attack or strike with sudden, intense, and destructive force, like a blitzkrieg
