items.ex_en: The gale-force winds caused the flimsy bedroom window panes to rattle through the night.
items.ex_zh: 强劲的大风让卧室那扇脆弱的窗玻璃整夜格格作响。
items.ex2_en: The nervous child rattled the metal doorknob repeatedly trying to escape the room.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的孩子反复摇晃金属门把手，发出声响，试图逃出房间。

items.def_en: To shake continuously with very small, rapid movements, or to cause something to do so.
items.ex_en: The powerful bass speakers made the glass coffee table vibrate across the wooden floor.
items.ex_zh: 强劲的低音扬声器使木地板上的玻璃茶几微微震颤起来。
items.ex2_en: The violin strings vibrate rapidly whenever the musician pulls the bow across them.
items.ex2_zh: 每当音乐家拉动琴弓掠过琴弦时，小提琴琴弦就会快速振动。

items.def_en: to shake slightly and quickly, typically from cold or momentary dread
items.ex_en: The fragile autumn leaves seemed to shiver beneath the touch of the icy frost.
items.ex_zh: 脆弱的秋叶在刺骨寒霜的抚触下仿佛微微打颤。
items.ex2_en: The sudden loud crack of thunder shivered the frightened little puppy into hiding.
items.ex2_zh: 突如其来的一声炸雷吓得受惊的小狗浑身发抖，躲了起来。

items.def_en: [I/T] to move unsteadily from side to side because of lack of balance
items.ex_en: The unbalanced front wheel caused the entire steering column to wobble during the drive.
items.ex_zh: 失衡的前轮导致整个转向柱在行驶过程中不停地摇摆晃动。
items.ex2_en: A loose screw wobbled the front wheel whenever the bicycle gained speed.
items.ex2_zh: 只要自行车一加速，一颗松动的螺丝就会让前轮晃动。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to move or cause sth to move rapidly back and forth with agitating motion
items.ex_en: The turbulent storm began to shake about the small fishing vessel with frightening force.
items.ex_zh: 狂暴的风暴以骇人的力量开始猛烈晃动这艘小渔船。
items.ex2_en: The wooden crates shook about violently in the cargo hold during the storm.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨期间，木箱在货舱里剧烈地晃荡。

items.def_en: [I/T] to hit or shake something with a sudden, harsh, painful impact
items.ex_en: The unexpected blow to his left shoulder did jar his arm with severe pain.
items.ex_zh: 左肩承受的突如其来的一记重击，震得他的整条手臂剧烈生疼。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail the acoustic, mechanical, or impact-driven manner of oscillatory motion. 'Vibrate' emphasizes rapid high-frequency pulses, 'rattle' involves loose objects knocking with clattering sound, and 'jar' highlights a harsh, jarring shock.
groups.summary_zh: 着眼于机械高频震动、撞击震撼或伴随杂音的特定摇动方式。
groups.desc_en: Depicts rapid, repetitive back-and-forth oscillations or jarring collisions producing sound and disturbance, contrasting with single impacts or smooth movements.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘快速、反复的微细往复振动或伴随杂音的震击颤动，区别于单次的猛击或平滑连续的位移。
groups.nuance_en: vibrate: oscillate rapidly with continuous microscopic or mechanical pulses (phone / vocal cords / machine) · rattle: shake with a clattering, loose noise or severely unnerve someone (window / saber / composure) · jar: strike a discordant, shaking blow to physical or mental stability (nerves / teeth / sensibility) · shiver: tremble finely from cold, fear, or intense resonance (body / sail / glass) · shake about: violently agitate in multiple erratic directions (contents / fluid / passenger)
groups.nuance_zh: vibrate: 高频微幅震动或共鸣 (phone / vocal cords / machine) · rattle: 伴随喀哒乱响的松脱晃动，或令某人心慌意乱 (window / saber / composure) · jar: 产生剧烈震颤感或使神经感知受刺耳震动 (nerves / teeth / sensibility) · shiver: 因寒冷、恐惧或共振而发生细碎颤抖 (body / sail / glass) · shake about: 在容器或封闭空间内被剧烈杂乱摇晃 (contents / fluid / passenger)

groups.name: Wake & Awaken · 苏醒与唤醒 (Wake, Awake, Awaken)
groups.tip: 由睡梦中清醒或叫醒

items.def_en: [I/T] To stop sleeping and become conscious of one's surroundings
items.ex_en: The alarm didn't go off, so I didn't wake up until eight.
items.ex_zh: 闹钟没响，所以我直到八点才醒。
items.ex2_en: The gentle morning sunshine woke up the campers sleeping inside their tents.
items.ex2_zh: 清晨柔和的阳光唤醒了在帐篷里熟睡的露营者。

items.def_en: To emerge from sleep, or to cause someone to stop sleeping.
items.ex_en: The piercing morning alarm went off loudly enough to wake everyone in the household.
items.ex_zh: 刺耳的晨间闹钟大声响起，足以吵醒屋子里的所有人。
items.ex2_en: She woke early every morning to enjoy the peaceful stillness of dawn.
items.ex2_zh: 她每天清晨醒来，享受黎明时分的宁静祥和。

items.def_en: (formal or literary) To stop sleeping, or cause someone to stop sleeping; to awaken or rouse.
items.ex_en: She did awake at dawn to the gentle rustling of leaves outside her window.
items.ex_zh: 黎明时分，她在窗外树叶的轻柔沙沙声中醒来。
items.ex2_en: The sound of distant thunder awakes the nervous watchdog in the yard.
items.ex2_zh: 远处的雷声惊醒了院子里神经紧绷的看门狗。

items.def_en: to regain consciousness after sleep or fainting
items.ex_en: After fainting in the crowded subway car, the passenger began to slowly come to.
items.ex_zh: 在拥挤的地铁车厢中晕厥后，那位乘客开始慢慢苏醒过来。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to awaken someone from sleep or a state of complete inactivity
items.ex_en: The trumpet blast served to rouse up the slumbering garrison for the sudden siege.
items.ex_zh: 号角的鸣响唤醒了沉睡中的驻军，以应对突如其来的围攻。

items.def_en: [I/T] To arouse from sleep, or stimulate an emotion, memory, or faculty
items.ex_en: The scent of wild lavender would awaken fond memories of his distant childhood home.
items.ex_zh: 野生薰衣草的香气总能唤醒他对遥远童年故居的深情记忆。
items.ex2_en: The town awakened slowly as warm sunlight broke through the morning fog.
items.ex2_zh: 随着温暖的阳光穿透晨雾，小镇缓缓苏醒过来。

items.def_en: [I/T] To bring out of state of sleep, unconsciousness, or inactivity by active effort
items.ex_en: No amount of loud knocking could rouse the exhausted sentry from his deep sleep.
items.ex_zh: 再响亮的敲击声也无法将筋疲力尽的哨兵从沉睡中叫醒。

groups.summary_en: Living beings emerge from sleep, unconsciousness, or spiritual dormancy, progressing from simple physiological rousing to deep moral or intellectual awakening.
groups.summary_zh: 从睡眠或麻木昏睡中醒转，由生理醒来渐至意识觉醒。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the physiological or metaphorical transition from sleep, numbness, or dormancy into conscious alertness and activity, unlike continuous vigilance or initial inception.
groups.desc_zh: 指从睡眠、麻木或蛰伏潜伏状态转变为清醒机敏的生理或心理过程，区别于持续的警惕或事物的最初创生。
groups.nuance_en: wake: transition spontaneously out of natural sleep (sleeper / dawn / consciousness) · awaken: stir profound dormant emotions, memories, or realizations (conscience / interest / memory) · rouse: stir someone vigorously out of deep sleep, stupor, or apathy (crowd / dreamer / suspicion) · come to: regain normal consciousness after fainting or anesthesia (patient / senses / victim) · awake: formal poetic emergence into wakefulness (mind / soul / nation)
groups.nuance_zh: wake: 从自然生理睡眠中睁眼苏醒 (sleeper / dawn / consciousness) · awaken: 唤醒沉睡的情感、记忆或道德意识 (conscience / interest / memory) · rouse: 强力惊醒熟睡者或激荡沉沦麻木的心神 (crowd / dreamer / suspicion) · come to: 昏厥、麻醉或休克后苏醒恢复知觉 (patient / senses / victim) · awake: 文雅或庄重地表达醒来与意识萌动 (mind / soul / nation)

groups.name: Walk Clumsily & Shufflingly · 笨拙拖步与蹒跚挪动 (Bumble, Shamble)
groups.tip: 脚步不稳摇晃拖沓的走姿

items.def_en: to walk with heavy, slow, shuffling steps
items.ex_en: Tired commuters had to plod along the snowy sidewalk after the heavy winter blizzard.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雪过后，疲惫的通勤者只得在积雪的人行道上挪行。

items.def_en: (+ along/away) to walk by dragging one's feet along the ground without lifting them fully
items.ex_en: The weary patient would shuffle along the hospital corridor using a lightweight metal walker.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的病人借助轻便的金属助行架，在医院走廊里拖着脚慢吞吞地走。

items.def_zh: 踉跄，摇晃慢行；笨手笨脚地做；含糊结巴地说
items.def_en: 1. (+ around/along) To move awkwardly, clumsily, or unsteadily. 2. To act or work in a confused, incompetent way. 3. To speak indistinctly or stammer.
items.ex_en: He watched the sleepy puppy bumble around the living room and bump into chairs.
items.ex_zh: 他看着昏昏欲睡的小狗在客厅里笨拙地踉跄晃荡，撞到了椅子上。

items.def_en: 1. (+ along/into) To walk slowly and awkwardly without lifting your feet properly, as if tired or weak.
items.ex_en: The exhausted survivors did shamble into the refugee encampment after their long, grueling march.
items.ex_zh: 经过漫长而艰苦的跋涉，筋疲力尽的幸存者们步履蹒跚地走进了难民营。

items.def_en: to walk or move ahead clumsily, awkwardly, or unsteadily
items.ex_en: Without a flashlight, the hikers had to stumble along the uneven forest trail blindly.
items.ex_zh: 没有手电筒，徒步者们只得在崎岖不平的林间小道上跌跌撞撞地前行。

items.def_zh: 磕磕绊绊地盲目走；跌跌撞撞
items.def_en: (+ into/around) to move clumsily or blindly as if unable to see or control oneself
items.ex_en: In the pitch darkness, he started to blunder into heavy furniture across the room.
items.ex_zh: 在漆黑一片中，他开始在房间里磕磕绊绊地盲目乱撞到沉重的家具。

items.def_zh: 沉重缓慢地走；笨拙前行
items.def_en: (+ along/on) to walk slowly and heavily without grace or agility
items.ex_en: The weary pack mules continued to plod on through the muddy mountain pass relentlessly.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的骡队继续迈着沉重的步伐，在泥泞的山口中步履维艰地前行。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail moving with awkward, clumsy, or slow dragging strides, typically showing physical lethargy, confusion, or lack of coordination. 'Shamble' specifically captures dragging the feet in an awkward, shuffling gait, while 'bumble' emphasizes clumsy, blundering movements through space.
groups.summary_zh: 指动作迟缓拖沓、拖着脚步或跌跌撞撞的笨拙走动姿态。
groups.desc_en: Describes gait patterns marked by clumsiness, fatigue, lack of foot-clearance, or disorientation, contrasting with purposeful, brisk, or graceful locomotion.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘因疲乏、体型笨拙或重心不稳而拖脚挪步、磕绊前行的运动样态，区别于利落、优雅或具方向性的行进。
groups.nuance_en: plod: trudge with heavy, slow, and mechanically determined steps (feet / traveler / donkey) · shuffle: walk without fully lifting the feet, dragging soles against the floor (feet / feet along / slippers) · shamble: move with an awkward, ungainly, loose-jointed shuffle (figure / gait / creature) · stumble along: progress clumsily while repeatedly tripping or losing balance (path / dark / life) · bumble: proceed erratically and ineptly while making blundering moves (speaker / novice / bureaucracy)
groups.nuance_zh: plod: 步伐沉重迟缓、机械而吃力地跋涉 (feet / traveler / donkey) · shuffle: 拖着鞋底不离地、沙沙挪动地擦地而行 (feet / feet along / slippers) · shamble: 关节松散、步履蹒跚拖沓地无序挪步 (figure / gait / creature) · stumble along: 踉踉跄跄、频频磕绊地艰难摸索 (path / dark / life) · bumble: 笨头笨脑、跌跌撞撞或漏洞百出地瞎摸索 (speaker / novice / bureaucracy)

groups.name: Warn & Advise of Danger · 告诫与预警 (Warn, Caution, Admonish)
groups.tip: 预先提醒注意可能的危险

items.def_en: to inform someone in advance of a possible danger, problem, or unpleasant situation
items.ex_en: Road signs along the steep descent warn drivers of frequent rockslides during rainstorms.
items.ex_zh: 陡坡路段的指示牌警告司机暴雨期间常有落石发生。

items.def_en: (+ to) to warn someone of a potential problem, hazard, or new development so they are prepared
items.ex_en: The weather forecast sought to alert residents to the incoming dangerous winter storm system.
items.ex_zh: 天气预报旨在提醒居民注意即将到来的危险冬季风暴系统。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to give secret or advance warning to sb about impending danger or police action
items.ex_en: An anonymous insider managed to tip off the investigative journalists before the raid occurred.
items.ex_zh: 一名匿名知情人设法在突击搜查发生前向调查记者通风报信。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to order or advise sb strongly to stay away or not get involved in danger
items.ex_en: The guard fired a shot into the air to warn off intruders.
items.ex_zh: 警卫朝天开了一枪以警告入侵者离开。

items.def_en: to warn or advise someone carefully about a danger, risk, or mistake
items.ex_en: Senior financial advisors caution investors against making speculative moves during periods of market instability.
items.ex_zh: 资深财务顾问告诫投资者在市场动荡期间切勿进行投机性操作。

items.def_en: (+ against/to) to advise or urge someone earnestly, warning them firmly of an error or danger
items.ex_en: The judge felt compelled to admonish the young defendant against further violations of probation.
items.ex_zh: 法官感到有必要严肃力诫这名年轻被告切勿再度违反缓刑规定。

items.def_en: to warn someone specifically before a dangerous or unwelcome event occurs
items.ex_en: Meteorologists were able to forewarn coastal communities of the powerful hurricane hours ahead.
items.ex_zh: 气象学家得以提前数小时向沿海社区预警强飓风的来袭。

groups.summary_en: An authority or peer alerts someone in advance about impending danger, negative consequences, or unacceptable conduct, urging care or avoidance.
groups.summary_zh: 提前就潜在危险、不良后果或不当行为向当事人发出提醒与警示。
groups.desc_en: Involves giving advance notice of imminent peril, adverse consequences, or regulatory censure, contrasting with mere educational instruction or post-hoc critique.
groups.desc_zh: 指就迫在眉睫的危险、不良后果或规章惩戒发出先期警示，区别于一般知识讲授或事后批评归因。
groups.nuance_en: warn: notify unequivocally of imminent danger or serious consequences (public / driver / investor) · caution: advise prudent restraint or carefulness to avoid pitfalls (driver / patient / consumer) · admonish: reprove mildly while urging moral or practical correction (child / disciple / offender) · alert: abruptly notify someone to assume active defensive vigilance (troops / authorities / public) · forewarn: provide early strategic intel well before an event unfolds (ally / team / leader) · tip off: provide confidential or inside advance warning secretly (police / insider / accomplice)
groups.nuance_zh: warn: 正式且明确告诫即将来临的危险或后果 (public / driver / investor) · caution: 规劝保持审慎以防踩坑或触规 (driver / patient / consumer) · admonish: 带有道德戒勉意味地温和劝诫责备 (child / disciple / offender) · alert: 促使进入高度戒备与应变警戒状态 (troops / authorities / public) · forewarn: 提前预先通知使其早做防备 (ally / team / leader) · tip off: 秘密通风报信或透露内幕消息 (police / insider / accomplice)

groups.name: Waste Away & Wither · 衰竭与消沉 (Wither, Languish, Collapse)
groups.tip: 体能衰竭垮掉或身心萎靡不振

items.def_en: to gradually lose physical strength, energy, or endurance
items.ex_en: Near the final miles of the marathon, several runners began to flag down physically.
items.ex_zh: 在马拉松最后的几英里处，好几名选手的体力开始明显下降衰退。

items.def_zh: 枯萎消沉；渐渐虚脱衰竭
items.def_en: to become progressively weak, enervated, or exhausted, losing physical vitality
items.ex_en: Deprived of hope and solitary in her cell, she felt her spirit wilt away.
items.ex_zh: 在牢房里孤立无援且失去了希望，她感到自己的生机与心智正慢慢枯萎消沉。

items.def_en: to lose vigor, strength, or fresh vitality gradually
items.ex_en: Without fresh investment and talent, the local arts scene began to wither.
items.ex_zh: 由于缺乏新的投资和人才，当地的艺术圈开始逐渐萎缩。
items.ex2_en: Prolonged neglect can wither promising cultural initiatives in any developing city.
items.ex2_zh: 长期的忽视会使任何发展中城市里大有希望的文化项目萎缩。

items.def_en: 1. (informal, often crock up) To collapse or break down due to illness, fatigue, or injury. 2. (informal) To injure or incapacitate someone.
items.ex_en: Running two back-to-back marathons completely crocked his knees for the entire season.
items.ex_zh: 连续跑了两场马拉松彻底搞垮了他的膝盖，让他整个赛季都无法参赛。

items.def_zh: 衰弱，憔悴；受煎熬，长期陷于困境
items.def_en: (+ in) 1. To grow weak, feeble, or listless. 2. To be forced to stay in an unpleasant situation or place for a long time.
items.ex_en: The innocent prisoner continued to languish in a damp cell without trial.
items.ex_zh: 无辜的囚犯未经审判，继续在阴暗潮湿的牢房中备受煎熬。

items.def_en: to gradually become very thin, frail, and weak from illness or neglect
items.ex_en: Without proper treatment, the patient began to waste away rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 若不接受适当治疗，患者便会迅速衰弱消瘦。

items.def_en: to suddenly fall down unconscious or utterly break down in health
items.ex_en: Exhausted from the relentless heat, the marathon runner collapsed near the finish line.
items.ex_zh: 马拉松选手因酷热难耐精疲力竭，在终点线附近虚脱倒地。
items.ex2_en: The economic crisis collapsed several prominent commercial banks in just one week.
items.ex2_zh: 经济危机在短短一周内搞垮了几家知名商业银行。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the progressive physical wasting, moral enervation, or sudden failure of bodily vitality, scaling from chronic debilitation and dispirited fading to total sudden physical breakdown.
groups.summary_zh: 按生命力丧失程度递增描述机体日渐衰弱、消沉乃至轰然垮掉。
groups.desc_en: Portrays progressive systemic exhaustion, physical shriveling, or prolonged decay under neglect, confinement, or disease, contrasting with sudden catastrophic collapse.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘在疾病、幽禁或忽视下机体与生机逐步枯槁、萎缩消沉的慢性衰竭过程，区别于瞬间的断裂与毁灭。
groups.nuance_en: wither: dry up, shrink, and lose vitality entirely (leaf / reputation / hope) · languish: suffer prolonged debility in miserable neglect or confinement (prison / illness / neglect) · waste away: gradually lose all body mass and strength through disease (body / patient / invalid) · wilt away: droop limply from extreme heat, exhaustion, or discouragement (flower / spirit / confidence) · collapse: abruptly break down structurally or physically fall in a heap (building / patient / economy)
groups.nuance_zh: wither: 彻底干枯萎缩或光环丧失殆尽 (leaf / reputation / hope) · languish: 在被遗忘、受囚禁或恶劣环境中受煎熬式消沉 (prison / illness / neglect) · waste away: 因病痛或饥谨致身体机能慢性枯槁瘦弱 (body / patient / invalid) · wilt away: 因缺水、乏力或打击而无精打采地蔫垂 (flower / spirit / confidence) · collapse: 发生突发性彻底垮塌崩溃 (building / patient / economy)

groups.name: Weave & Braid · 编织与交错 (Weave, Braid, Plait)
groups.tip: 多股线缕穿插编成辫状

items.def_en: (+ sth) to interweave strands of hair or fiber together into plaits or braids
items.ex_en: She carefully braided up her daughter's unruly curls before the ballet performance.
items.ex_zh: 在芭蕾舞演出前，她细心地将女儿蓬乱的卷发编结整齐。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to introduce or incorporate threads or strands into an existing woven arrangement
items.ex_en: The artisan decided to weave in silver threads to accentuate the tapestry pattern.
items.ex_zh: 手工艺人决定织入银线，以突出挂毯的图案。

items.def_en: [I/T] To form fabric or structure by interlacing threads or flexible strands at right angles
items.ex_en: Traditional craftsmen weave durable baskets using flexible willow twigs and dried rushes.
items.ex_zh: 传统手艺人用柔韧的柳条和干灯心草编织结实耐用的篮子。

items.def_en: To interweave three or more strands of hair, ribbon, or wire together
items.ex_en: The stylist will braid colorful ribbons through the dancer's hair for the parade.
items.ex_zh: 造型师将把彩色丝带编入舞者的头发中以参加游行。

items.def_en: 1. (chiefly British) To weave three or more strands of hair, straw, or rope together into a braid. 2. To form material into pleats.
items.ex_en: She sat quietly on the porch to plait the dry straw into hats.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐在门廊上，将干麦秆编成草帽。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To weave, cross, or blend threads, branches, or elements over and under each other.
items.ex_en: The master gardener decided to interlace flexible branches to form a natural arbor.
items.ex_zh: 园艺大师决定将柔韧的树枝相互交织，构筑一座天然凉亭。
items.ex2_en: Tall willow branches interlace naturally to create a shady canopy over paths.
items.ex2_zh: 高大的柳树枝条自然地交织在一起，在小径上形成林荫。

items.def_en: [I/T] To weave or blend together tightly and complexly, whether physically or metaphorically
items.ex_en: Ancient legends interweave mortal destinies with the capricious whims of forgotten gods.
items.ex_zh: 古老的传说将凡人的命运与被遗忘神祇的反常心意紧密交织在一起。
items.ex2_en: Different musical themes interweave gracefully throughout the composer's final symphony.
items.ex2_zh: 不同的音乐主题优美地交织在这位作曲家最后的交响曲中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict interlacing flexible strands, threads, fibers, or hair into a cohesive fabric, rope, or patterned arrangement. 'Plait' and 'braid' center on overlapping three or more strands into a band, while 'weave' and 'interlace' cover broader crossing-over structures.
groups.summary_zh: 将线股、毛发或柔性材料交错穿插编织成网状或辫状。
groups.desc_en: Involves interlacing, entwining, or blending flexible strands, storylines, or elements into a unified, complex fabric, distinct from merely attaching or stacking parts.
groups.desc_zh: 指将柔软线缆、发丝、线索或意象彼此交织、编结或融合成结构紧密的复杂整体，区别于简单的堆叠或端头连接。
groups.nuance_en: weave: interlace threads on a loom or seamlessly blend complex story strands (cloth / narrative / spell) · braid: plait three or more strands of hair or fiber diagonally into a rope (hair / cord / rug) · plait: fold flexible sections flatly over one another in a disciplined pattern (hair / straw / ribbon) · interlace: cross or link multiple linear elements intimately together (fingers / branches / threads) · interweave: closely merge disparate themes, cultures, or materials (themes / traditions / fabrics)
groups.nuance_zh: weave: 在织机上经纬交错穿梭，或密织复杂情节与织锦 (cloth / narrative / spell) · braid: 将三股及以上发丝或纤维斜向绞编成辫 (hair / cord / rug) · plait: 将平整柔软的条状物有层次地叠编 (hair / straw / ribbon) · interlace: 肢体骨节或线性元素交叠相扣 (fingers / branches / threads) · interweave: 将异质的题材、文化或纹理深层交融 (themes / traditions / fabrics)

groups.name: Wring & Twist · 拧绞与扭捏 (Wring, Twist)
groups.tip: 旋转拧转纤维挤绞出水分

items.def_en: to bend or turn something around forcibly with a rotating motion
items.ex_en: He had to twist the rusty valve firmly to shut off the water.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不用力转动生锈的阀门以关闭水流。

items.def_zh: 拧，绞，拧干；扭，勒；勒索，强行取得
items.def_en: 1. To twist and squeeze something tightly to extract liquid from it. 2. To clasp and twist one's hands in distress. 3. To obtain something with difficulty or by force.
items.ex_en: Anxious about the test results, she began to wring her hands in silence.
items.ex_zh: 因担心检测结果，她开始焦急地在沉默中绞着双手。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to remove or separate something by rotating and twisting it with force
items.ex_en: The bottle has a child-proof cap that is difficult to twist off.
items.ex_zh: 这个瓶子装有儿童安全瓶盖，很难直接拧开。

items.def_zh: 把（衣物等）拧干，绞出（水分）
items.def_en: (+ sth) to squeeze and twist something wet forcefully with hands to extract liquid
items.ex_en: Please wring out your soaked jacket before hanging it inside the cabin.
items.ex_zh: 把湿透的夹克挂进小屋之前，请先将水分拧干。

items.def_en: to pull or twist something suddenly and violently with great force
items.ex_en: The thief managed to wrench the handbag from the tourist's shoulder and fled.
items.ex_zh: 小偷猛地从游客肩上扯下皮包后逃之夭夭。

items.def_en: to pull or twist something forcefully away from someone's grip
items.ex_en: The rebel commander sought to wrest control of the garrison from loyalist forces.
items.ex_zh: 叛军指挥官企图从效忠派军队手中强行夺取要塞的控制权。

items.def_zh: 拧，绞，拧干（wring的过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: Past tense and past participle of wring; twisted tightly or squeezed liquid out.
items.ex_en: She wrung the heavy woolen towel thoroughly before hanging it on the line.
items.ex_zh: 她把厚重的羊毛毛巾彻底拧干后晾在了绳子上。

groups.summary_en: An agent applies opposing torsional force to compress, twist, or extract liquid from a flexible material or body part. Intensity moves from rhythmic squeezing to forceful twisting that causes structural strain or pain.
groups.summary_zh: 双手施加反向扭力，通过绞拧挤出液体或致使部位受扭受压。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the forceful application of rotational, torsional, or shearing stress to deform, extract liquid from, or wrench away an object, distinct from straight tensile pulling.
groups.desc_zh: 强调施加旋转扭转应力以使其发生形变、拧出汁水或暴力拧夺脱离，区别于纯粹的直线拉扯或平推。
groups.nuance_en: twist: rotate ends in opposite directions or wind off course (ankle / cap / wire) · wring: compress by severe twisting to extract liquid, or suffer intense anguish (cloth / neck / hands) · wrench: violently pull and twist with sudden levering torque (joint / door / weapon) · wrest: seize away by vigorous struggling, twisting, or legal maneuvering (control / power / weapon) · wring out: thoroughly squeeze out moisture or extract concessions under duress (water / confession / concession)
groups.nuance_zh: twist: 反向扭转两端、拧开或使其扭曲变形 (ankle / cap / wire) · wring: 拧绞以榨干水分，或因极度焦虑而搓揉双手 (cloth / neck / hands) · wrench: 伴随杠杆式扭力猛然拧拽或使关节扭伤 (joint / door / weapon) · wrest: 拼力扭打抢夺或通过博弈硬夺控制权 (control / power / weapon) · wring out: 拧干拧尽液体，或施压榨取妥协口供 (water / confession / concession)

groups.name: Abandon & Desert · 抛弃与遗弃 (Desert, Forsake, Jettison)
groups.tip: 主动放弃权利或所有物

items.def_en: To discard or ignore someone or something because they are no longer useful or interesting
items.ex_en: The ruthless prince cast aside loyal allies once his throne was secure.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的王子一旦王位稳固，便将忠诚的盟友弃置一旁。

items.def_en: To get rid of or part company with someone or something quickly and without ceremony
items.ex_en: The suspect decided to ditch the stolen getaway car in a dark alley.
items.ex_zh: 嫌疑人决定将偷来的逃跑车辆扔在一条黑暗的小巷里。

items.def_zh: 放弃（权利、主张）；抛弃，遗弃
items.def_en: 1. To give up a claim, right, or belief completely. 2. To leave someone or something behind, often permanently or with no intention of returning.
items.ex_en: Rising floodwaters forced the villagers to abandon their homes and evacuate immediately.
items.ex_zh: 不断上涨的洪水迫使村民们抛弃家园，立即撤离。

items.def_en: To leave someone or a military post without permission and with no intention of returning
items.ex_en: The panicked soldier chose to desert his unit during the midnight artillery barrage.
items.ex_zh: 惊慌失措的士兵在午夜炮击期间擅自脱离部队潜逃。

items.def_en: To abandon someone you have a moral duty to, or permanently give up a cherished way of life
items.ex_en: The ascetic knight vowed to forsake all worldly pleasures for spiritual enlightenment.
items.ex_zh: 这位苦修骑士誓言断绝一切尘世享乐，以求精神上的领悟。

items.def_en: To discard unwanted cargo from a craft, or get rid of plans and ideas abruptly
items.ex_en: Facing severe financial deficits, the board chose to jettison the expansion project.
items.ex_zh: 面对严重的财务赤字，董事会决定断然放弃扩张计划。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures completely turning one's back on dependents, possessions, or long-held commitments, leaving them behind to fend for themselves or discarding them entirely.
groups.summary_zh: 指彻底撇下、背弃或扔掉人、物或使命，使其自生自灭。
groups.desc_en: Signifies breaking ties of duty, affection, or utility to permanently leave behind people, property, or causes, contrasting with strategic temporary withdrawal.
groups.desc_zh: 指割裂道义、情感或功用纽带，将人、物或事业彻底弃置不顾，区别于战术性的暂时撤出或留有后路的撤退。
groups.nuance_en: abandon: completely surrender control, care, or loyalty to someone or something (ship / family / plan) · desert: unlawfully or treachously walk away from military post or moral duty (post / spouse / army) · forsake: renouncingly leave behind long-held beloved attachments, allies, or habits (allies / homeland / ways) · jettison: cast cargo overboard to lighten load, or discard obsolete ideas (cargo / policy / ballast) · ditch: informally and unceremoniously get rid of an inconvenient burden (car / friend / plan)
groups.nuance_zh: abandon: 彻底撒手放弃所有权、看护职责或原有计划 (ship / family / plan) · desert: 背信弃义或触犯刑律地开小差、遗弃阵地或配偶 (post / spouse / army) · forsake: 决绝告别昔日誓盟、故土、至亲或嗜好 (allies / homeland / ways) · jettison: 为减负断尾求生而抛弃压舱物或抛弃废策 (cargo / policy / ballast) · ditch: 不留情面、随手甩掉麻烦的拖累或伙伴 (car / friend / plan)

groups.name: Abolish & Annul · 废除与废黜 (Repeal, Annul, Overturn)
groups.tip: 彻底废除陈旧陋习或法令

items.def_en: To officially cause a statute or legislative act to lose its legal force by legislative action
items.ex_en: Parliament voted overwhelmingly to repeal the controversial tax statute passed last year.
items.ex_zh: 议会以压倒性多数投票废止了去年通过的那项极具争议的税收法令。

items.def_en: To reverse, vacate, or override a prior judicial ruling, legal precedent, or official outcome
items.ex_en: The appellate court took decisive action to overturn the erroneous prior verdict.
items.ex_zh: 上诉法院采取果断行动，推翻了之前错误的判决。
items.ex2_en: The controversial legal precedent overturned unexpectedly after public outcry intensified nationwide.
items.ex2_zh: 随着全国抗议加剧，那项备受争议的判例意外被推翻了。

items.def_en: To officially declare an indictment, legal verdict, or subpoena legally invalid and set it aside
items.ex_en: The high court moved to quash the indictment citing flawed evidence collection.
items.ex_zh: 高等法院以证据收集存在瑕疵为由，裁定撤销该起诉书。

items.def_zh: 宣告无效（婚姻、合约、判决）
items.def_en: To declare a contract, marriage, law, or election officially null and void as if it never existed
items.ex_en: The high court acted decisively to annul the fraudulent commercial agreement yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 高等法院昨日果断采取行动，宣告该欺诈性商业协议自始无效。

items.def_zh: 废除，废止（法律、制度或习俗）
items.def_en: To officially end a law, system, practice, or institution.
items.ex_en: The reformist government pledged to abolish archaic labor practices across all industries.
items.ex_zh: 改革派政府承诺在所有行业废除陈旧的劳工制度。

items.def_en: To officially end, revoke, or evade an authoritative agreement, treaty, or formal duty
items.ex_en: The rogue regime decided to abrogate the international arms treaty unilaterally.
items.ex_zh: 该流氓政权决定单方面废除国际军控条约。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this high-intensity institutional frame designate formally and permanently dismantling laws, long-standing practices, judicial decisions, or historic institutions.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过权威、法律或政府机构彻底推翻、废除法令与体制。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the authoritative, institutional, or judicial nullification and elimination of a law, custom, verdict, or structure, contrasting with informal non-compliance.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过权威、宪典或司法力量使法律、惯例、判决或既定建制彻底失效废止，区别于非正式的怠于遵行。
groups.nuance_en: abolish: completely eradicate an institutional system, practice, or tax by law (slavery / monarchy / tax) · repeal: officially revoke a legislative statute by subsequent legislative action (law / act / tariff) · annul: declare an agreement, marriage, or election void ab initio (marriage / contract / election) · quash: judicially crush or suppress a ruling, rebellion, or subpoena (indictment / rebellion / rumor) · overturn: invalidate and reverse a previous legal precedent or verdict (ruling / verdict / decision) · abrogate: solemnly repeal or repudiate a treaty, sovereign right, or compact (treaty / agreement / right)
groups.nuance_zh: abolish: 依法彻底铲除既有的社会制度、习俗或税目 (slavery / monarchy / tax) · repeal: 由立法机关经法定程序撤销废除法令条文 (law / act / tariff) · annul: 依法宣告契约、婚姻或选举自始无效 (marriage / contract / election) · quash: 司法上驳回起诉、镇压叛乱或平息流言 (indictment / rebellion / rumor) · overturn: 推翻并逆转下级法院的判决或司法先例 (ruling / verdict / decision) · abrogate: 废止并撕毁跨国条约、君权或法定协定 (treaty / agreement / right)

groups.name: Abrade & Roughen · 粗糙与打磨糙化 (Rough, Scuff, Coarsen, Chafe)
groups.tip: 表面经磨蚀变得糙硬不平

items.def_en: To intentionally or accidentally mark and scratch up a surface to reduce slickness
items.ex_en: He used coarse sandpaper to scuff up the glossy surface before painting.
items.ex_zh: 他在上漆前用粗砂纸打磨光滑表面以增加粗糙度。
items.ex2_en: The hardwood floor scuffed up easily under the dancers' heavy wooden shoes.
items.ex2_zh: 在舞者沉重的木鞋踩踏下，硬木地板很容易磨损了。

items.raw_cluster: 使粗糙与变粗 Rough & Coarsen
items.def_zh: 使粗糙，打毛；粗暴对待；草拟
items.def_en: 1. To make a surface uneven, coarse, or textured. 2. ('rough up') To treat someone violently.
items.ex_en: Workers will rough the smooth concrete foundation so the mortar adheres properly.
items.ex_zh: 工人们将把光滑的混凝土基底打毛，以便砂浆牢固附着。

items.def_en: To scrape, scratch, or roughen the surface of shoes, furniture, or floors through friction
items.ex_en: The child tended to scuff the polished toes of his leather shoes.
items.ex_zh: 这孩子老是蹭磨他那双擦得锃亮的皮鞋鞋尖。
items.ex2_en: Cheap leather shoes scuff quickly when walking across uneven gravel roads.
items.ex2_zh: 在崎岖不平的碎石路上行走时，廉价皮鞋很快就会磨损。

items.def_en: To scrape or wear away the smooth surface or skin of something through rigorous friction
items.ex_en: Fierce desert gales slowly abrade the ancient stone monuments over centuries.
items.ex_zh: 几个世纪以来，猛烈的沙漠狂风慢慢磨蚀着古老的石碑。

items.def_en: To cause a texture, skin, or fabric to become rough, hard, or harsh to the touch
items.ex_en: Years of harsh manual labor in the fields began to coarsen her skin.
items.ex_zh: 多年在田间繁重的体力劳作逐渐使她的皮肤变得粗糙。
items.ex2_en: Her delicate skin coarsened after weeks of exposure to dry desert winds.
items.ex2_zh: 在干燥的沙漠风沙中暴露数周后，她细腻的皮肤变粗糙了。

items.def_en: To make something sore or wear its surface rough by repetitive friction and rubbing
items.ex_en: Stiff new hiking boots will chafe your ankles during a long mountain trek.
items.ex_zh: 在漫长的山地徒步中，硬挺的新登山靴会磨伤你的脚踝。
items.ex2_en: Sensitive skin chafes easily against coarse fabric during intense athletic training.
items.ex2_zh: 在高强度体能训练中，敏感的皮肤摩擦粗糙面料很容易发红擦伤。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate modifying the texture of a surface to make it coarse, uneven, or abrasive, whether intentionally (e.g., to prepare for adhesion) or through wear, friction, and elemental exposure.
groups.summary_zh: 通过摩擦、擦刮或物理加工使光滑表面变糙、起毛或出现划痕磨损。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to rubbing, scratching, or treating a surface mechanically to make it harsh, scraped, or friction-ready, contrasting with gentle polishing or fine smoothing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过机械刮擦、磨蚀或刻意打磨使平滑表面变得粗涩、起毛或磨损破损，区别于精细的抛光抚平或洁净养护。
groups.nuance_en: abrade: wear down or scrape away surface material by sustained abrasive friction (rock / skin / metal) · chafe: make skin or fabric sore and worn by repetitive rubbing friction (skin / collar / restraint) · scuff: scrape surface finish slightly by brushing against rough obstacles (shoes / floor / surface) · rough: deliberately distress or texture a smooth face to increase mechanical grip (surface / stone / edges) · coarsen: cause texture, voice, or sensibilities to become harsh and unrefined (skin / hands / tone)
groups.nuance_zh: abrade: 因持续磨蚀磨料导致表层擦伤或损耗剥离 (rock / skin / metal) · chafe: 摩擦生热导致皮肤红肿破损或织物磨损 (skin / collar / restraint) · scuff: 刮蹭磕碰使光洁鞋面或地板留下擦痕 (shoes / floor / surface) · rough: 故意将平整基底打毛粗化以增强抓力 (surface / stone / edges) · coarsen: 使质地、手足皮肤或声音嗓音变得粗砺 (skin / hands / tone)

groups.name: Abscond & Bolt · 潜逃与逃逸 (Abscond, Decamp, Skip)
groups.tip: 迅速逃离危险或避开抓捕

items.def_en: To make a rapid, evasive escape from a difficult or threatening predicament rather than face it
items.ex_en: When police sirens echoed down the alley, the shoplifters chose to cut and run.
items.ex_zh: 当警笛声在巷子里回荡时，顺手牵羊的小贼们拔腿就溜。

items.def_zh: 溜走；不告而别（逃避账单或责任）
items.def_en: (+ on) To leave hurriedly or secretly, especially to avoid paying a bill or fulfilling a duty
items.ex_en: The irresponsible tenant decided to skip out on three months of unpaid rent.
items.ex_zh: 那个不负责任的房客决定溜之大吉，赖掉三个月未付的房租。

items.def_zh: 逃跑（尤指为赖债而潜逃）
items.def_en: (archaic) To run away secretly to avoid paying gambling or financial debts.
items.ex_en: Having lost a fortune at hazard, the disgraced nobleman chose to levant abroad.
items.ex_zh: 在骰子赌局中输光家产后，名誉扫地的贵族决定潜逃海外赖债。

items.def_en: To leave a place suddenly, secretly, or unexpectedly, often to escape an unwelcome obligation
items.ex_en: The fraudulent promoters chose to decamp overnight before angry investors could intervene.
items.ex_zh: 诈骗发起人在愤怒的投资者介入前，连夜秘密撤走潜逃。

items.def_en: To suddenly dash away out of control or in panic to evade detention or danger
items.ex_en: The frightened horse managed to bolt from the barn into open fields.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的马匹从马厩中脱逃，一路狂奔至开阔的田野中。

items.def_en: To escape secretly and hide, especially after stealing money or to evade the law
items.ex_en: The corrupt accountant managed to abscond with millions in stolen company funds.
items.ex_zh: 这名腐败的会计携数百万挪用的公司资金成功潜逃。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe running away secretly, abruptly, or furtively, almost always to evade debt, prosecution, capture, or obligations. They convey illicit stealth, hurried flight, or breaking parole.
groups.summary_zh: 强调为逃避债务、惩罚或抓捕而秘密、仓促地潜逃。
groups.desc_en: Actors depart precipitously and illicitly to evade detection, debts, or custody, contrasting with standard 'departing' through stealth, suddenness, and evasion of accountability.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者为了躲避追责、债务或拘禁而仓促且非法地脱身，与普通'离开'相比带有强烈的潜逃、隐秘与规避法律/道德责任色彩。
groups.nuance_en: cut and run: panic-driven sudden abandonment (position / investment) · skip out: informal evasion of debt or duty (hotel bill / rent) · decamp: sudden departure often taking baggage or funds (with the cash / from the camp) · bolt: explosive instinctive physical flight (horse / suspect) · abscond: formal covert flight specifically with stolen assets or from custody (with the funds / prisoner)
groups.nuance_zh: cut and run: 恐慌驱使下的急遽抛弃或脱身 (position / investment) · skip out: 口语化溜走以逃避账单或职责 (hotel bill / rent) · decamp: 卷席携资而逃或悄然撤走 (with the cash / from the camp) · bolt: 突发性本能冲刺狂奔 (horse / suspect) · abscond: 携款潜逃或脱逃监禁的正式法律用词 (with the funds / prisoner)

groups.name: Absent & Avoid · 缺席与回避 (Withdraw, Stay Away, Skive)
groups.tip: 有意不参加或避开

items.def_en: (+ of) Leave abruptly or evade an obligation or engagement
items.ex_en: She tried to duck out of the tedious departmental budget meeting early.
items.ex_zh: 她试图从沉闷的部门预算会议上提早溜走。

items.def_en: (+ from) Not go to a place where you are expected or intended to be
items.ex_en: Doctors advised the recovering patient to stay away from stressful work environments.
items.ex_zh: 医生建议正在康复的患者避开压力繁重的工作环境。

items.def_en: Fail to attend a class, meeting, or scheduled duty intentionally
items.ex_en: He decided to skip the mandatory training session to finish his urgent report.
items.ex_zh: 他决定缺席强制性培训会议，以便完成紧急报告。

items.def_en: (also 'absent oneself') To stay away from a place or event where you are expected to be.
items.ex_en: The diplomat chose to absent himself from the contentious plenary debate entirely.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官选择完全缺席那场争议不断的全体辩论。

items.def_en: Stay away from school or duties without permission
items.ex_en: Unsupervised teenagers would frequently truant to spend their afternoons at the mall.
items.ex_zh: 缺乏管教的青少年经常逃学，把下午的时间打发在商场里。

items.def_en: Avoid or neglect a duty, responsibility, or effort out of laziness or fear
items.ex_en: A reliable team member will never shirk essential duties during a critical deadline.
items.ex_zh: 可靠的团队成员绝不会在紧要关头逃避核心职责。

groups.summary_en: Denotes deliberately or improperly avoiding a duty, gathering, or workplace, absenting oneself from an expected presence.
groups.summary_zh: 指擅自缺席本应参加的场合、逃避义务或故意不到场。
groups.desc_en: Actors deliberately fail to appear or withhold presence from an expected obligation, differing from passive 'non-attendance' through purposeful dereliction or evasive intent.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者蓄意在应履行的义务场合缺席或回避，与单纯的'不在场'相比，具有故意脱逃、擅离职守或推诿避事的意图。
groups.nuance_en: duck out: informal discreet slip away from a commitment (meeting / early) · stay away: deliberate non-involvement or physical distance (from trouble / from work) · skip: casual omission of an scheduled event (class / lunch) · absent: formal deliberate removal of oneself (oneself from duty / oneself from the chamber) · truant: illicit unexcused absence from school or role (school / duties) · shirk: ethically culpable evasion of labor or responsibility (responsibility / duties)
groups.nuance_zh: duck out: 溜走以避开未尽的义务或会议 (meeting / early) · stay away: 刻意保持距离以求不卷入 (from trouble / from work) · skip: 随意跳过既定安排 (class / lunch) · absent: 正式用语中自发缺席或离场 (oneself from duty / oneself from the chamber) · truant: 旷课或擅离职守 (school / duties) · shirk: 逃避该承担的繁重责任或劳役 (responsibility / duties)

groups.name: Accelerate & Expedite · 促进与加速 (Expedite, Accelerate, Quicken)
groups.tip: 扫除流程障碍，加快运行节奏

items.def_en: Move or progress at a faster rate, or make something happen more rapidly
items.ex_en: The project manager hired extra freelancers to speed up the development process.
items.ex_zh: 项目经理聘请了额外的自由职业者以加快开发进度。

items.def_en: Cause an event or outcome to occur sooner than expected
items.ex_en: Unforeseen political scandals served to hasten the sudden downfall of the regime.
items.ex_zh: 意料之外的政治丑闻加速了该政权的轰然倒台。
items.ex2_en: Her pulse hastened as she approached the stage to deliver the speech.
items.ex2_zh: 当她走近舞台准备发表演讲时，脉搏不由得加速了。

items.def_en: Make or become faster, more active, or more alert
items.ex_en: Footsteps behind her caused her pulse to quicken in the dim alleyway.
items.ex_zh: 昏暗小巷中身后传来的脚步声使她的脉搏骤然加快。

items.def_en: Increase the speed of a process, event, or vehicle; cause to happen sooner
items.ex_en: Favorable economic policies will accelerate growth across renewable energy sectors this decade.
items.ex_zh: 有利的经济政策将在未来十年加速可再生能源领域的增长。

items.def_en: (formal) to make a process, delivery, or action happen faster and more efficiently
items.ex_en: Paying an additional service fee will expedite customs clearance for international shipments.
items.ex_zh: 支付额外服务费将加快国际货物的清关流程。

items.def_zh: 促发；猛烈促成（危机或剧变）
items.def_en: Cause an undesirable event or crisis to happen suddenly, unexpectedly, or prematurely
items.ex_en: The sudden currency devaluation threatened to precipitate a catastrophic nationwide banking collapse.
items.ex_zh: 货币的突然贬值极有可能骤然引发全国性的银行业灾难性崩溃。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate speeding up the progress, movement, or completion of an action, process, or legal transaction.
groups.summary_zh: 指人为干预或外力介入，使过程、审批或速度显著提速增效。
groups.desc_en: Agents reduce elapsed time or drive processes forward toward culmination, advancing beyond mere 'moving faster' by systematically clearing bottlenecks or compressing developmental schedules.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者缩短时间周期或强力推进进程走向终点，与单纯的'加快速度'相比，强调系统性打通堵点、压缩进程或催化提前发生。
groups.nuance_en: speed up: generic velocity increase (production / heartbeat) · quicken: organic or sensory briskness (pulse / pace) · hasten: purposeful swiftness to avoid delay or disaster (departure / demise) · accelerate: steady geometric or mechanical growth (growth / vehicle) · expedite: administrative unblocking to ease throughput (delivery / process) · precipitate: rash or violent premature triggering (crisis / downfall)
groups.nuance_zh: speed up: 最通用的提高速度 (production / heartbeat) · quicken: 偏机体本能或感官节奏的加快 (pulse / pace) · hasten: 为防延误或抢时间而急行催促 (departure / demise) · accelerate: 呈机械或速率规律的稳步提速 (growth / vehicle) · expedite: 官方行政上的扫清阻碍以加速推进 (delivery / process) · precipitate: 骤然促成或过早引爆危机 (crisis / downfall)

groups.name: Accompany & Escort · 陪伴与护送 (Convoy, Chaperone, Tag Along)
groups.tip: 陪同在旁或随行护送

items.def_en: (+ with) To accompany someone, especially without being explicitly invited or needed
items.ex_en: Do you mind if my little brother tags along with us to the cinema?
items.ex_zh: 你介意我弟弟跟着我们一起去看电影吗？

items.def_en: to travel or go somewhere with someone as a companion or escort; to happen or exist at the same time as something
items.ex_en: Two armed security officers will accompany the visiting ambassador to the summit.
items.ex_zh: 两名武装安全官员将陪同来访的大使前往峰会现场。

items.def_en: To politely guide, lead, or conduct someone to their proper seat or destination
items.ex_en: Courteous flight attendants will usher VIP guests directly into the first-class cabin.
items.ex_zh: 彬彬有礼的乘务员将引导贵宾直接进入头等舱。

items.def_en: To accompany someone socially to ensure proper behavior and welfare, usually a young person
items.ex_en: Several responsible teachers volunteered to chaperone the teenagers during the weekend excursion.
items.ex_zh: 几位负责任的老师自愿在周末远足期间陪同并监护这些青少年。

items.def_en: To travel with someone in order to guide, protect, or supervise them
items.ex_en: State police cars were assigned to escort the foreign dignitary through town.
items.ex_zh: 州警车奉命护送外国政要穿过市区。

items.def_en: To accompany ships, vehicles, or travelers as an armed escort for safety
items.ex_en: Naval destroyers were deployed to convoy merchant vessels through perilous pirate waters.
items.ex_zh: 海军驱逐舰被部署前往危险的海盗水域为商船护航。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers traveling in company with another entity, spanning formal protective escorts, social guidance, and casual joint travel.
groups.summary_zh: 指与他人结伴同行，涵括礼节陪伴、保卫护送及跟随照管。
groups.desc_en: One entity travels alongside another to provide guidance, protection, surveillance, or deference, surpassing plain 'co-presence' through structural asymmetry or protective duty.
groups.desc_zh: 随行者为了指引、保护、监督或礼节而与主体同行，超越了普通的'结伴'，蕴含监护、守卫或非对等的从属关系。
groups.nuance_en: tag along: informal and passive following without strong mandate (with friends / on a trip) · accompany: neutral formal accompaniment (soloist / dignitary) · usher: guiding transit to a designated station (guests / era) · chaperone: protective moral supervision of minors (group / prom) · escort: defensive, honorific, or custodial guarding (convoy / prisoner) · convoy: armed collective protection of transport vehicles (merchant ships / supplies)
groups.nuance_zh: tag along: 非受邀或无特定职责地尾随跟从 (with friends / on a trip) · accompany: 中性正式的相伴同行或伴奏 (soloist / dignitary) · usher: 礼貌引路至指定席位或开启新纪元 (guests / era) · chaperone: 对青少年的监管与风纪看护 (group / prom) · escort: 具有防护、礼仪或押解性质的护卫 (convoy / prisoner) · convoy: 军事武装护送车队或船队 (merchant ships / supplies)

groups.name: Acquire Knowledge & Master · 研习与习得 (Acquire, Master, Absorb)
groups.tip: 从初学者到彻底掌握

items.def_en: Acquire a skill, language, or piece of knowledge casually without formal instruction
items.ex_en: Business usually picks up in the spring, and sales figures improve rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 生意通常在春季好转，销售额也会迅速回升。

items.def_zh: 学习，研习；得知，获悉（learn 的英式过去式和过去分词）
items.def_en: (chiefly British English) A past tense and past participle form of learn: to gain knowledge or skill through study, practice, or experience.
items.ex_en: She learnt the fundamental rules of classical composition during her university days.
items.ex_zh: 她在大学期间习得了古典作曲的基本法则。

items.def_en: Gain knowledge, an ability, or a skill through continuous effort or experience
items.ex_en: Students must acquire practical lab expertise before conducting advanced independent medical research.
items.ex_zh: 学生在开展高级独立医学研究前，必须先习得实际的实验技能。

items.def_en: Take in and fully understand information, ideas, or complex facts
items.ex_en: The bright intern managed to absorb the complex regulatory framework within days.
items.ex_zh: 这位聪明的实习生在几天之内就消化理解了复杂的监管框架。

items.def_en: Attain a firm or comprehensive understanding of a concept or subject
items.ex_en: Novice programmers often struggle to grasp advanced algorithms without sufficient practice.
items.ex_zh: 初学者若缺乏足够练习，往往难以充分领会高级算法。

items.def_en: Acquire complete knowledge of or proficiency in an art, subject, or technique
items.ex_en: It takes decades of relentless discipline to master traditional Japanese sword craftsmanship.
items.ex_zh: 需要数十载坚持不懈的磨砺才能彻底精通传统日本刀剑锻造工艺。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses the process of gaining knowledge, comprehension, or skill through cognitive exertion or experience. Verbs range from broad acquisition to effortless internal absorption and total command.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过认知努力或经历吸收知识与技能，涵盖从初步领会到精通掌握的程度。
groups.desc_en: Cognitive subjects assimilate informational structures from basic internalization to definitive command, going beyond simple 'knowing' into progressive internalization and skill integration.
groups.desc_zh: 认知主体对知识或技能进行吸收与建构，不同于被动的'知晓'，展现从偶得、内化到全面掌控的进阶式认知过程。
groups.nuance_en: pick up: casual incidental absorption (language / habits) · acquire: gradual deliberate accretion of complex assets (skills / reputation) · absorb: deep frictionless conceptual intake (information / culture) · grasp: intellectual comprehension of essential mechanics (concept / significance) · master: attaining complete virtuoso command (technique / craft)
groups.nuance_zh: pick up: 潜移默化或耳濡目染地偶得 (language / habits) · acquire: 长期稳步习得复杂技能或资本 (skills / reputation) · absorb: 如海绵般深度吸收信息或文化 (information / culture) · grasp: 顿悟领会核心机理与主旨 (concept / significance) · master: 达到炉火纯青的熟练掌控 (technique / craft)

groups.name: Adapt & Accommodate · 适应与顺应 (Adjust, Conform, Reconcile)
groups.tip: 调整自身以配合他人需求

items.def_en: To change your behavior, expectations, or ideas so as to fit a new situation or environment
items.ex_en: Immigrants must adjust their daily expectations when settling into a vastly different culture.
items.ex_zh: 移民在融入截然不同的文化环境时，必须调整日常预期以适应新生活。
items.ex2_en: Her vision adjusted gradually to the dim light inside the ancient cave.
items.ex2_zh: 她的视线逐渐适应了古老洞穴内昏暗的光线。

items.def_en: To gradually modify behavior, structure, or methods to suit different conditions or purposes
items.ex_en: Animals must constantly adapt their hunting strategies to survive changing climate conditions.
items.ex_zh: 动物必须不断调整捕食策略以适应不断变化的气候条件并生存下去。

items.def_zh: 顺从，赞同（他人意愿或计划）
items.def_en: To accept, agree with, or adapt to someone else's plan, idea, or suggestion without resistance
items.ex_en: I decided to fall in with their holiday plans instead of arguing.
items.ex_zh: 我决定顺从他们的度假计划，不再争论。

items.def_zh: 使顺应，使适应；迎合；容纳；向……提供便利
items.def_en: 1. To adjust, adapt, or change behavior to fit new conditions or satisfy needs. 2. To provide space, shelter, or lodging for someone.
items.ex_en: The policy was modified to accommodate the needs of low-income families.
items.ex_zh: 该政策进行了修改，以迎合低收入家庭的需求。

items.def_en: (+ to/with) To behave according to the usual standards, rules, or expectations of a group
items.ex_en: All employees must conform to the strict safety regulations of the plant.
items.ex_zh: 所有员工都必须遵从工厂严格的安全规程。

items.def_en: (reconcile oneself to) To accept an unpleasant situation or compromise that cannot be changed
items.ex_en: She had to reconcile herself to the fact that her career was over.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不甘心接受自己职业生涯已经结束的事实。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to modifying one's behavior, ideas, or policies to fit changing circumstances, rules, or the needs of others. They range from mutual compromise to unidirectional compliance.
groups.summary_zh: 调整自身行为或安排以符合外部变化或他人需求。
groups.desc_en: An entity alters internal parameters or behavior to fit external boundary conditions, moving beyond 'changing' to focus on harmonization and relational equilibrium.
groups.desc_zh: 主体调整自身内在参数或行为以迎合外部约束条件，不同于一般的'改变'，重在契合环境或化解冲突以达平衡。
groups.nuance_en: adjust: pragmatic calibration to fine-tune fit (mirror / expectations) · adapt: systemic evolution to survive new environments (to climate / strategy) · accommodate: generous modification to fit another's needs (wishes / guest) · conform: alignment with established societal or technical norms (to standards / to rules) · reconcile: resolving ideological or affective discord (differences / accounts)
groups.nuance_zh: adjust: 实用性的微调或校准 (mirror / expectations) · adapt: 演化或系统性重塑以适应新生态 (to climate / strategy) · accommodate: 迁就或顾及他者需求的顺应 (wishes / guest) · conform: 遵从社会规范或技术规格 (to standards / to rules) · reconcile: 调和观念分歧或账目矛盾 (differences / accounts)

groups.name: Address & Confront · 处理与应对 (Address, Confront, Grapple with)
groups.tip: 直面并着手解决问题

items.def_en: To give attention to or deal with a matter or problem directly
items.ex_en: The committee met yesterday to address the growing issue of housing shortages.
items.ex_zh: 委员会昨天召开会议，以着手解决日益严重的住房短缺问题。

items.def_en: To take vigorous action to reduce, stop, or defeat an undesirable problem
items.ex_en: The government launched new initiatives to combat illicit drug trafficking nationwide.
items.ex_zh: 政府启动了新举措，以在全国范围内打击非法毒品贩运。

items.def_zh: 着手处理，应对（难题）；阻截，扑倒，抢断（对手）
items.def_en: 1. To make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem or situation. 2. (sports) To intercept, stop, or knock down an opposing player.
items.ex_en: Our team must tackle the most urgent technical bottlenecks by next Monday.
items.ex_zh: 我们团队必须在下周一前着手解决最紧迫的技术瓶颈。

items.def_en: To face and deal with a difficult situation or opponent bravely or directly
items.ex_en: We must boldly confront these financial difficulties before they overwhelm the company.
items.ex_zh: 在这些财务困难压垮公司之前，我们必须勇敢正视它们。

items.def_en: To struggle hard to deal with or solve a difficult problem
items.ex_en: Economists continue to grapple with the underlying causes of persistent global inflation.
items.ex_zh: 经济学家们继续努力设法应对持续性全球通胀的根本原因。

items.def_en: To accept a difficult challenge, duty, or fight against an opponent
items.ex_en: She was eager to take on the daunting responsibility of chief executive.
items.ex_zh: 她渴望承担起执行首席执行官这一艰巨职责。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe taking determined, head-on action to manage, solve, or confront difficult challenges, crises, or systemic problems.
groups.summary_zh: 指主动、果断地正视并设法化解棘手困难、危机或复杂问题。
groups.desc_en: Agents directly face, engage, or dismantle a systemic crisis or adversary, differing from mere 'talking about' through resolute confrontation and active engagement.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者直面并着手解决棘手危机、难题或对手，与泛泛的'提及'截然不同，包含正面交锋与实际干预。
groups.nuance_en: address: diplomatic or programmatic focus on a topic (issue / challenge) · combat: active aggressive containment of a menace (crime / disease) · tackle: energetic physical or pragmatic dismantling of a knotty issue (problem / crisis) · confront: stark, uncompromising exposure of an unpleasant reality (accuser / dilemma) · grapple with: protracted mental or physical wrestling with intractable friction (existential dread / paradox) · take on: bold assumption of a formidable adversary or challenge (incumbent / risk)
groups.nuance_zh: address: 官方或方案层面系统性着手处理 (issue / challenge) · combat: 极富斗志地迎战并遏制公害 (crime / disease) · tackle: 劲头十足地正面破解硬骨头 (problem / crisis) · confront: 毫不退缩地直面指责或严酷现实 (accuser / dilemma) · grapple with: 陷入与错综复杂困境的长期缠斗 (existential dread / paradox) · take on: 勇挑重担或向强敌发起挑战 (incumbent / risk)

groups.name: Address & Greet · 致辞与向……进言 (Salute, Pitch, Speak To)
groups.tip: 面对特定受众发表演讲致辞

items.def_zh: 向……演说，致辞；设法解决，处理；称呼
items.def_en: 1. To make a formal speech to a group of people. 2. To direct attention and effort toward dealing with a problem or issue.
items.ex_en: The prime minister will address the conference tomorrow on economic revitalization strategies.
items.ex_zh: 首相明天将向大会发表演说，阐述经济复兴战略。

items.def_en: (+ to) To present an idea, proposal, or speech aimed directly at persuading a target listener
items.ex_en: The startup founders will pitch their business concept to prominent venture capitalists.
items.ex_zh: 初创公司创始人将向知名风险投资人推销他们的商业理念。

items.def_en: To communicate directly with a gathering, or speak publicly addressing a designated body
items.ex_en: The ambassador rose to speak to the assembly regarding regional peace accords.
items.ex_zh: 大使起身向大会致辞，阐述区域和平协定。

items.def_en: To call out to attract someone's attention or greet them enthusiastically from a distance
items.ex_en: The captain hailed the approaching vessel through a megaphone across the harbor.
items.ex_zh: 船长隔着海港用扩音器向靠近的船只大声致意。

items.def_en: To honor or formally greet an assembly or distinguished individual with respectful words
items.ex_en: We salute the courageous firefighters who risked their lives during the crisis.
items.ex_zh: 我们向危机中冒着生命危险的英勇消防员致敬。

items.def_en: To approach and speak to someone boldly, abruptly, or aggressively
items.ex_en: A disheveled stranger accosted him outside the station demanding spare change angrily.
items.ex_zh: 一名衣衫不整的陌生人在车站外唐突上前搭话，愤怒地索要零钱。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict directing a formal utterance, greetings, or tailored message specifically toward a designated person, crowd, or assembly.
groups.summary_zh: 指正式面向特定受众开口发话、致词或进言阐述。
groups.desc_en: A speaker directs intentional linguistic or physical signals toward an interlocutor to initiate interaction, differing from general 'talking' through overt targeting, framing, or solicitation.
groups.desc_zh: 说话者向特定目标定向投射言辞或敬意以开启交流，超越了普通的'谈话'，强调受众指向性、策略推介或突发拦阻。
groups.nuance_en: address: deliver formal speech or direct attention to an entity (audience / council) · pitch: strategic presentation to sell an idea or service (client / proposal) · hail: loud distance-bridging call or enthusiastic praise (cab / hero) · salute: formal honorific military or ceremonial tribute (flag / bravery) · accost: aggressive uninvited approach that borders on harassment (stranger / celebrity)
groups.nuance_zh: address: 向特定受众做正式演讲或阐释进言 (audience / council) · pitch: 为促成合作或投资而精准推介 (client / proposal) · hail: 远距离招手呼唤或高调颂扬 (cab / hero) · salute: 军礼式致敬或庄严致意 (flag / bravery) · accost: 唐突、不请自来甚至带胁迫感的半路拦阻 (stranger / celebrity)

groups.name: Admit & Acknowledge · 承认与招认 (Acknowledge, Admit, Confess)
groups.tip: 从被动认错到正式坦承事实

items.def_en: To admit or confess to having done something wrong, especially something minor or mischievous
items.ex_en: He finally decided to fess up about breaking his roommate's expensive laptop.
items.ex_zh: 他终于决定坦白交待摔坏室友昂贵笔记本电脑的事。

items.def_zh: 承认，供认（常指勉强或因证据确凿）
items.def_en: To agree, often reluctantly or under pressure, that something is true or that one has done something wrong
items.ex_en: He was forced to admit that his initial calculations were completely wrong.
items.ex_zh: 他被迫承认自己最初的计算完全错误。

items.def_zh: 坦白认错，对过失承担责任
items.def_en: (+ to) To admit responsibility for an error, misconduct, or unpleasant fact
items.ex_en: No one would own up to breaking the window, so the whole class was kept after school.
items.ex_zh: 没有人愿意承认打破了窗户，所以全班都被罚放学后留堂。

items.def_zh: 承认（属实）；告知收到；向……致谢
items.def_en: 1. To accept, admit, or recognize the truth or existence of something. 2. To confirm receipt of a letter or message. 3. To express gratitude for assistance or work done.
items.ex_en: The ministry failed to acknowledge receipt of our formal complaint for weeks.
items.ex_zh: 该部门连续数周都未告知收到我们的正式申诉。

items.def_en: (+ about/with) To finally tell the whole truth about something previously concealed or lied about
items.ex_en: The politician finally decided to come clean about his secret offshore accounts.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客终于决定就其隐秘的海外账户全盘托出。

items.def_zh: 坦白，供认（过错、罪行或秘密）
items.def_en: To admit formally or openly that one has committed a crime, sin, or embarrassing fault
items.ex_en: The suspect formally confessed to the burglary under interrogation by senior detectives.
items.ex_zh: 在高级侦探的审讯下，嫌疑人正式供认了盗窃罪行。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe explicitly accepting the truth, reality, or responsibility of a situation or fault, ranging from matter-of-fact recognition to guilt-driven confession.
groups.summary_zh: 从客观认可事实到主动招认过失或罪责的表态行为。
groups.desc_en: Actors surrender concealment of a fault, liability, or taboo fact under internal or external pressure, moving past 'stating' into the realm of conceded vulnerability.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者在内外压力下放弃隐瞒，低头认可自身过错或不可告人的事实，不同于客观'陈述'，体现被迫承认或卸下心理负担。
groups.nuance_en: fess up: informal candid concession of a minor blunder (to mistake / to cheating) · admit: grudging concession of an undeniable fact or flaw (defeat / guilt) · own up: taking full moral accountability for misbehavior (to the crime / to error) · acknowledge: polite or formal validation of an existing reality (receipt / defeat) · come clean: thorough cathartic unburdening after deceit (about the affair / with the police) · confess: solemn institutional or juridical admission of sin or guilt (sins / crime)
groups.nuance_zh: fess up: 口语化地坦白小错 (to mistake / to cheating) · admit: 勉强认输或被动承认事实 (defeat / guilt) · own up: 勇于担责认账 (to the crime / to error) · acknowledge: 礼节性或正式层面确认事实的存在 (receipt / defeat) · come clean: 彻底交代底细以求洗心革面 (about the affair / with the police) · confess: 庄重悔罪或具有司法效力的供述 (sins / crime)

groups.name: Adopt & Embrace · 接纳与采纳 (Embrace, Espouse, Buy into)
groups.tip: 欣然接受建议或收养为家庭成员

items.def_en: To accept or support an idea, philosophy, or premise, agreeing to align with it
items.ex_en: I refused to buy into their absurd conspiracy theory about the election.
items.ex_zh: 我绝不相信他们关于选举的荒谬阴谋论。

items.def_en: To accept or start using a proposed idea, method, challenge, or career path
items.ex_en: Several schools decided to take up the novel curriculum proposed by experts.
items.ex_zh: 几所学校决定采纳专家提议的新型课程体系。

items.def_zh: 采纳，采用；收养，领养；正式通过（动议、提案）
items.def_en: 1. To choose to take up or follow an idea, method, or policy. 2. To legally take another's child as one's own. 3. To formally accept or approve a proposal.
items.ex_en: The council voted unanimously to adopt the proposed regulations on environmental protection.
items.ex_zh: 委员会一致投票通过并正式采纳提议的环境保护规章。

items.def_en: To absorb, integrate, and incorporate people, concepts, or customs into a larger group
items.ex_en: The community strives to assimilate foreign customs while preserving its original heritage.
items.ex_zh: 该社区在保留原有传统的同时，努力吸收接纳外来习俗。
items.ex2_en: New immigrant families assimilate naturally into local neighborhoods within a few generations.
items.ex2_zh: 新移民家庭在几代之内就会自然地融入当地社区。

items.def_en: To accept, support, or take up an idea, belief, or lifestyle readily and enthusiastically
items.ex_en: Forward-thinking enterprises readily embrace technological innovations to boost overall operational efficiency.
items.ex_zh: 具有前瞻性的企业欣然采纳技术创新，以提升整体运营效率。

items.def_en: To actively support, champion, or adhere to a cause, doctrine, or belief system
items.ex_en: The candidate has consistently espoused progressive political doctrines throughout her entire career.
items.ex_zh: 这位候选人在整个职业生涯中始终坚定信奉并拥护进步政治主张。

groups.summary_en: Focuses on welcoming, officially choosing, or enthusiastically taking up beliefs, policies, practices, or outsiders. 'Adopt' centers on institutional or conscious selection, while 'embrace' highlights emotional and enthusiastic acceptance.
groups.summary_zh: 指主动接纳外来者，或欣然采纳新的观念、制度与方针。
groups.desc_en: Agents willingly accept, integrate, or champion an ideological framework or paradigm, distinguishing from basic 'choosing' by deep personal allegiance and programmatic deployment.
groups.desc_zh: 主体由表及里地接受、融入并践行某种理念或体系，不仅是表面的'挑选'，更包含理念认同、信念皈依与身体力行。
groups.nuance_en: buy into: informal credulous acceptance of a premise (narrative / myth) · take up: beginning practice of an activity or cause (hobby / cause) · adopt: legally or formally choosing a method or child (policy / child) · assimilate: melting down distinctives to absorb into a matrix (culture / immigrants) · embrace: impassioned warm acceptance of a concept (diversity / future) · espouse: public ideological allegiance and championship (cause / doctrine)
groups.nuance_zh: buy into: 盲从或接受某种说法与假设 (narrative / myth) · take up: 开始涉足某活动或致力于某事业 (hobby / cause) · adopt: 正式采纳某项政策或合法收养 (policy / child) · assimilate: 同化吸收融入整体 (culture / immigrants) · embrace: 热情拥抱接纳新生事物或理念 (diversity / future) · espouse: 公开拥护并宣扬某种学说或主义 (cause / doctrine)

groups.name: Affirm & Assert · 断言与确认声明 (Assert, Maintain, Attest)
groups.tip: 坚定确切地陈述事实或立场

items.def_en: To keep stating strongly that something is true, despite opposition or doubt
items.ex_en: The defendant maintains that he was nowhere near the scene of crime.
items.ex_zh: 被告坚称事发时自己根本不在犯罪现场附近。

items.def_en: To affirm or assert something positively, often guaranteeing its authenticity
items.ex_en: The scholar did avouch the authenticity of the ancient royal charter signed.
items.ex_zh: 这位学者确证了那份附有签署的古老皇家特许状的真实性。

items.def_en: To state a fact or belief firmly, positively, and with strong conviction
items.ex_en: She asserted her constitutional right to speak openly before the congressional inquiry.
items.ex_zh: 她在国会质询前坚决主张自己公开发言的宪法权利。

items.def_zh: 断言，坚定声明；证实，确认
items.def_en: To state clearly and firmly that something is true or valid.
items.ex_en: The high court affirmed the validity of the contentious international trade contract.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院正式确认了这份引发争议的国际贸易合同的有效性。

items.def_en: To provide or act as clear proof that something exists or is true
items.ex_en: Multiple eyewitnesses attest to the extraordinary bravery displayed by the young officer.
items.ex_zh: 多名目击者证实了这名年轻军官所展现出的非凡勇气。

items.def_en: To state or assert firmly and formally that something is indeed true
items.ex_en: The witness did aver that the signature on the deed was genuine.
items.ex_zh: 证人坚称地契上的签名确属真实无误。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers communicative acts where a speaker solemnly, confidently, or legally states that a fact is undoubtedly true. 'Assert' emphasizes forceful confidence, 'affirm' suggests formal validation or confirmation, and 'attest' implies bearing witness or furnishing proof.
groups.summary_zh: 指正式、坚定且确凿地宣称、证实或陈述某事为真。
groups.desc_en: Speakers declare truth with epistemic weight and certitude, differing from 'saying' through heightened speaker commitment, juridical gravity, and readiness to defend the claim.
groups.desc_zh: 宣示者对陈述内容的真实性赋予高可信度担保，不同于普通的'说话'，体现坚守立场、司法作证或不容置疑的断言。
groups.nuance_en: maintain: steadfast persistence in an assertion despite pushback (innocence / position) · assert: confident, authoritative declaration of stance or prerogative (authority / innocence) · affirm: solemn, positive reaffirmation of foundational truths (loyalty / belief) · attest: evidentiary witness-bearing to prove validity (to the truth / to character) · aver: formal, confident verification without doubt (competence / facts)
groups.nuance_zh: maintain: 顶住反驳与质疑执着坚称 (innocence / position) · assert: 自信强势地断言或主张权力 (authority / innocence) · affirm: 庄严确证既定立场或信仰 (loyalty / belief) · attest: 具有证据力地出面证实或作证 (to the truth / to character) · aver: 极有分量地正式确证某事实非虚 (competence / facts)

groups.name: Afford & Provide · 负担与提供 (Furnish, Yield, Supply)
groups.tip: 具备财力并供应所需

items.def_en: To make available or supply something that someone needs or desires.
items.ex_en: The relief agency will provide clean water and emergency shelter to victims.
items.ex_zh: 救援机构将向灾民提供干净饮用水和应急避难所。

items.def_en: To provide a sufficient amount of goods, materials, or energy for practical use.
items.ex_en: Local reservoirs supply fresh drinking water to hundreds of surrounding rural communities.
items.ex_zh: 当地水库向周边数百个农村社区供应新鲜饮用水。

items.def_zh: 买得起，担负得起；提供，给予
items.def_en: 1. To have enough money, time, or resources to be able to buy or do something. 2. (formal) To provide or supply something.
items.ex_en: The towering balcony affords a magnificent panoramic view across the entire city.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的阳台提供了俯瞰整座城市的绝佳全景。

items.def_en: To produce, supply, or generate a result, profit, or natural resource.
items.ex_en: These long-term capital investments should yield substantial financial returns for shareholders eventually.
items.ex_zh: 这些长期资本投资最终应当能为股东产生丰厚的财务回报。

items.def_en: To manage to find, supply, or produce money, resources, or an answer when required.
items.ex_en: They struggled desperately to come up with the cash for the deposit.
items.ex_zh: 他们竭尽全力设法凑齐那笔购房定金。

items.def_en: (+ with) To provide or supply someone with what is needed, useful, or necessary.
items.ex_en: The whistleblower agreed to furnish investigators with confidential internal emails and records.
items.ex_zh: 告密者同意向调查人员提供绝密的内部电子邮件和记录。

groups.summary_en: This frame spans two linked senses: possessing sufficient monetary or temporal resources to absorb an expenditure, and formally conferring or yielding a distinct benefit, opportunity, or protection to others.
groups.summary_zh: 指经济或时间上能承受支出，或引申为正式提供、赋予某种条件。
groups.desc_en: Entities yield, generate, or deliver resources necessary to meet capacity, differing from plain 'giving' by emphasizing resource enablement, output yield, or fiscal tolerance.
groups.desc_zh: 主体输出、产出或提供支撑所需之资源，与普通'给与'相比，凸显出经济承受力、产能产出或赋能支持。
groups.nuance_en: provide: general delivery of essentials or support (care / shelter) · supply: systematic stocking of consumed logistics (goods / electricity) · afford: carrying the financial or strategic consequence (cost / luxury) · yield: producing organic or investment output under pressure (harvest / returns) · come up with: resourceful generation of elusive requirements (money / solution) · furnish: equipping an environment with functional necessities (apartment / evidence)
groups.nuance_zh: provide: 最基础地提供生活保障或条件 (care / shelter) · supply: 物资或能源的规模化补给与供应 (goods / electricity) · afford: 具备承担经济消耗或代价的能力 (cost / luxury) · yield: 生产、投资或受压后产出效益 (harvest / returns) · come up with: 费尽心力设法筹措出解法或款项 (money / solution) · furnish: 装备房屋家具或在法庭上提供关键佐证 (apartment / evidence)

groups.name: Age & Obsolete · 老化与废弃 (Date, Superannuate, Outmode)
groups.tip: 年岁渐长过时陈旧终遭淘汰

items.def_en: Show signs of age or obsolescence, or reveal the specific past era when something was made
items.ex_en: Those oversized shoulder pads really date the jacket to the early eighties.
items.ex_zh: 那些超大垫肩真是一眼显出这件夹克出自八十年代初。

items.def_en: Gradually stop using, producing, or operating something obsolete in stages
items.ex_en: The automaker plans to phase out fossil fuel vehicles within five years.
items.ex_zh: 该汽车制造商计划在五年内逐步淘汰燃油汽车。

items.def_zh: 因年老废弃；使退休淘汰
items.def_en: Retire someone with a pension or declare an old object or machine obsolete from long service
items.ex_en: The railway department decided to superannuate the decaying fleet of steam engines.
items.ex_zh: 铁路部门决定将这批老旧废弃的蒸汽机车作退役淘汰处理。

items.def_en: (formal) To make something obsolete, outmoded, or old-fashioned.
items.ex_en: Rapid advancements in modern artificial intelligence threaten to antiquate traditional software systems.
items.ex_zh: 现代人工智能的飞速发展势必使传统软件系统趋于过时废弃。

items.def_en: Cause something to become out of date or no longer fashionable or usable
items.ex_en: Digital streaming services rapidly outmoded conventional compact discs within a few years.
items.ex_zh: 数字流媒体服务在短短几年内迅速使传统的CD光盘落伍过时。

items.def_en: Take the place of a person or thing previously in authority or use, making it obsolete
items.ex_en: Modern automated assembly lines have superseded traditional manual labor across the factory.
items.ex_zh: 现代自动化装配线已经取代了全工厂传统的体力劳动。

groups.summary_en: Addresses the process of rendering something old-fashioned, outdated, or superseded by new technology and modern standards.
groups.summary_zh: 指技术、制度或事物随时间推移或新事物诞生而过时、老化或被淘汰。
groups.desc_en: Objects, ideas, or workers lose functional currency due to temporal decay or technological displacement, contrasting with generic 'getting old' through systemic obsolescence and decommissioning.
groups.desc_zh: 客体或人员因时光流逝或技术更迭而丧失现代适用性，不同于中性的'变老'，侧重于系统性落伍、功能淘汰与更替弃用。
groups.nuance_en: date: reveal chronological origin through telltale marks (style / fossil) · phase out: planned progressive decommissioning of a line (subsidy / technology) · superannuate: retire someone or something due to old age or tenure (official / engine) · antiquate: render stylistically or functionally archaic (equipment / view) · outmode: make unusable through technological innovation (machinery / technique) · supersede: replace and displace an older standard completely (treaty / version)
groups.nuance_zh: date: 显露时代痕迹而显老旧或判定年代 (style / fossil) · phase out: 计划周密的分期逐步淘汰 (subsidy / technology) · superannuate: 因年事已高或服役超期而安排退役 (official / engine) · antiquate: 使之在风格或功能上沦为古旧 (equipment / view) · outmode: 被新潮流或新技术挤压至过时 (machinery / technique) · supersede: 全面替代并废除旧有标准或规范 (treaty / version)

groups.name: Aggravate & Worsen · 加剧与恶化 (Exacerbate, Compound, Intensify)
groups.tip: 不良状况多重叠加而愈发严重

items.def_en: To make an existing illness, injury, or unpleasant situation worse
items.ex_en: Strenuous physical exercise will only aggravate your severe lower back muscle strain.
items.ex_zh: 剧烈体育运动只会加重你严重的腰部肌肉拉伤。

items.def_en: To become more serious, severe, or acute, especially of crises or conflicts
items.ex_en: Fierce ethnic tensions continue to deepen as peace negotiations stall once again.
items.ex_zh: 随着和平谈判再度停滞，激烈的民族矛盾仍在继续深化。
items.ex2_en: Continuous military drills deepen anxiety among residents living near the disputed border.
items.ex2_zh: 持续的军事演习加深了争议边界附近居民的焦虑。

items.def_en: To become worse, or to make something worse than it was before
items.ex_en: Unfavorable economic policies will inevitably worsen living standards for many low-wage workers.
items.ex_zh: 不利的经济政策必将恶化许多低薪工人的生活水准。
items.ex2_en: Patient health conditions worsened rapidly after the dangerous bacterial infection spread unchecked.
items.ex2_zh: 由于危险的细菌感染肆虐失控，病人的身体状况急剧恶化。

items.def_zh: 使加重，使恶化；混合，化合
items.def_en: 1. To make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse. 2. To combine two or more parts or substances to form a whole.
items.ex_en: Severe logistic disruptions compound the acute shortages of food throughout the province.
items.ex_zh: 严重的物流中断使全省急剧的粮食短缺问题进一步恶化。

items.def_en: To make or become significantly greater, more serious, or more intense
items.ex_en: Border disputes could rapidly escalate into a full-scale armed conflict between nations.
items.ex_zh: 边界争端可能迅速升级为两国之间的全面武装冲突。
items.ex2_en: Provocative political statements escalate diplomatic friction between neighboring countries needlessly.
items.ex2_zh: 挑衅性的政治言论不必要地升级了邻国之间的外交摩擦。

items.def_zh: 使恶化；加重（痛苦、危机等）
items.def_en: To make a bad situation, disease, or problem much worse or more severe
items.ex_en: Heavy industrial emissions exacerbate respiratory illnesses among residents living in urban areas.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的工业废气排放加重了生活在城市区域居民的呼吸系统疾病。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe making an already difficult, painful, or negative situation substantially worse by adding new complications or increasing severity.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过叠加问题或提升严重性，使既有的不良局面、痛苦或矛盾进一步恶化。
groups.desc_en: Internal friction or external hazards intensify an already negative state, differing from simple 'increasing' by tracking descent into critical dysfunction or peril.
groups.desc_zh: 负面状态受到内外部破坏性因子的作用而步步恶化，不同于一般'增加'，强调朝危急、失控或不可逆的溃败方向加剧。
groups.nuance_en: aggravate: increasing frustration or irritating an injury (injury / problem) · deepen: expanding emotional or existential severity (crisis / depression) · worsen: overall progressive deterioration of conditions (weather / patient) · compound: multiplying negative factors into compounding complexity (errors / misery) · escalate: spiraling into open confrontation or higher stakes (conflict / war) · exacerbate: acute sharp worsening of an already fraught problem (inequality / asthma)
groups.nuance_zh: aggravate: 惹恼他人或刺激伤痛使其恶化 (injury / problem) · deepen: 程度向纵深下陷或情绪加重 (crisis / depression) · worsen: 整体态势不可逆地每况愈下 (weather / patient) · compound: 负面因素雪上加霜地交织叠加 (errors / misery) · escalate: 摩擦升级为不可控的激烈冲突 (conflict / war) · exacerbate: 对本就恶劣的病情或矛盾形成剧烈火上浇油 (inequality / asthma)

groups.name: Agree & Accede · 赞同与允诺 (Assent, Concur, Yield)
groups.tip: 从日常赞同到正式应允同意

items.def_en: (+ in/to) To accept or agree to something passively, without arguing or showing active enthusiasm
items.ex_en: The manager chose to acquiesce in the board's contentious restructuring plan quietly.
items.ex_zh: 经理选择默许董事会颇具争议的重组方案，并未多言。

items.def_en: (+ to) To give permission for something to happen, or agree formally to do something
items.ex_en: The patient must formally consent to the surgical procedure in written form.
items.ex_zh: 患者必须以书面形式正式同意接受该外科手术程序。

items.def_en: (+ with) To share someone's opinion or agree with an official decision
items.ex_en: Several prominent economists concur with the central bank's controversial monetary policy decision.
items.ex_zh: 数位著名经济学家赞同央行颇具争议的货币政策决定。

items.def_en: (+ to) To express formal or official agreement to a suggestion, proposal, or request
items.ex_en: The committee gave unanimous assent to the proposed revisions of the charter.
items.ex_zh: 委员会一致赞同提议的章程修订案。

items.def_zh: 同意，应允；就任，登基；正式加入
items.def_en: 1. (+ to) (formal) To agree to a request, demand, or proposal. 2. (+ to) To take up a high office, title, or the throne. 3. (+ to) To formally become a member of an organization or sign a treaty.
items.ex_en: The authorities refused to accede to the unreasonable demands of the hijackers.
items.ex_zh: 当局拒绝答应劫持者提出的不合理要求。

items.def_en: (+ to) To reluctantly agree to a demand or request after initially refusing or resisting
items.ex_en: After hours of relentless negotiation, management finally had to give in.
items.ex_zh: 经过数小时不休止的谈判，管理层最终不得不妥协让步。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey formal or reluctant agreement to a request, proposal, or dominant opinion. Nuances range from dignified yielding to formal diplomatic consensus or passive acquiescence.
groups.summary_zh: 表示在经过考量、请求或压力后正式赞成、顺从或允诺他人主张。
groups.desc_en: Parties converge in judgment or yield to another's demands, moving past casual 'okaying' across a continuum ranging from reluctant surrender to harmonious concord.
groups.desc_zh: 各方达成意见一致或向对方立场屈服，跳脱了随意的'应允'，形成从被动妥协到主动和谐共识的广谱梯度。
groups.nuance_en: acquiesce: passive silent submission without protest (in defeat / to the demand) · consent: legally autonomous authorization (to surgery / of the governed) · concur: intellectual unity of judgment or timing (with the findings / opinion) · assent: formal reasoned endorsement of an opinion (to proposal / to treaty) · accede: diplomatic yielding to repeated demands or treaties (to throne / to request) · give in: exhausted collapse of resistance against pressure (to temptation / to demands)
groups.nuance_zh: acquiesce: 虽不情愿但默不作声地顺从接受 (in defeat / to the demand) · consent: 具法律自主权的知情同意或许可 (to surgery / of the governed) · concur: 智识判断上的契合共鸣或同时发生 (with the findings / opinion) · assent: 对提议深思熟虑后的正式赞成 (to proposal / to treaty) · accede: 外交层面的妥协签约或登基即位 (to throne / to request) · give in: 在持久施压下彻底放弃抵抗而屈服 (to temptation / to demands)

groups.name: Alternative & Secondary Employment · 兼职与自主从业 (Freelance, Moonlight, Side-hustle)
groups.tip: 从事自由职业或夜间兼职

items.def_en: to work as a temporary employee, typically in an office setting
items.ex_en: She had to temp as a receptionist while searching for permanent work.
items.ex_zh: 她在寻找固定工作期间，不得不做前台临时工。

items.def_zh: 转包兼职；作为替工工作
items.def_en: (+ sth) to subcontract work or work as an outside substitute contractor
items.ex_en: The overloaded marketing firm decided to sub out the website design project.
items.ex_zh: 工作过量的营销公司决定将网站设计项目转包兼职出去。
items.ex2_en: Experienced electricians sub out frequently for larger commercial development projects downtown.
items.ex2_zh: 经验丰富的电工经常接分包工程，参与市中心的大型商业开发项目。

items.def_en: to do separate pieces of work or odd jobs for various employers
items.ex_en: He managed to job as an independent translator for various publishing houses.
items.ex_zh: 他设法作为独立翻译为多家出版社承揽零星小活。

items.def_zh: 从事自由职业，做自由兼职
items.def_en: to work independently for various clients rather than being employed full-time by a single employer.
items.ex_en: He decided to freelance as a graphic designer rather than seek employment.
items.ex_zh: 他决定从事平面设计自由职业，而不是去求职应聘。

items.def_zh: 兼职，打第二份工（尤指夜间或瞒着雇主兼职）
items.def_en: (informal) to work at a second job, often at night and without the main employer's knowledge.
items.ex_en: He had to moonlight as a taxi driver to clear his debts.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不兼职开出租车来还清名下的债务。

items.def_en: to undertake secondary work or a side business to earn extra income
items.ex_en: She managed to side-hustle as a private tutor to earn extra cash.
items.ex_zh: 她设法搞副业兼职做私人家教，以挣些外快。

groups.summary_en: Depicts working outside regular, single-employer full-time contracts. 'Freelance' denotes operating as an independent contractor for various clients, while 'moonlight' explicitly involves holding a secondary, often covert night or weekend job alongside a primary one.
groups.summary_zh: 脱离传统单一全职劳动关系的自由接单或秘密兼职副业。
groups.desc_en: Workers operate outside standard primary payrolls through piecemeal, nocturnal, or autonomous enterprise, distinguishing from plain 'working' through flexibility, informal risk, or secondary timing.
groups.desc_zh: 劳工脱离传统全职长聘框架，从事零星、夜间或自主副业，与普通'工作'相比，突出灵活用工、二次变现与独立兼职属性。
groups.nuance_en: temp: short-term interim clerical coverage (at agency / for summer) · sub out: contracting parcelled jobs to external vendors (component / construction) · freelance: autonomous sell-off of creative or technical work (writer / designer) · moonlight: illicit or secretive secondary evening job (as cabbie / as bartender) · side-hustle: entrepreneurial secondary revenue generation (vintage sales / podcast)
groups.nuance_zh: temp: 从事短期临时代班派遣劳务 (at agency / for summer) · sub out: 将分项业务外包转包 (component / construction) · freelance: 自由职业接单创作或咨询 (writer / designer) · moonlight: 背着主业悄悄利用夜间兼职打工 (as cabbie / as bartender) · side-hustle: 个人主导的副业创新创收 (vintage sales / podcast)

groups.name: Ameliorate & Alleviate · 好转与纾解 (Ameliorate, Alleviate, Mitigate)
groups.tip: 由差变好或使境况有所改善

items.def_en: To make pain, tension, or hardship less severe or gradually decrease
items.ex_en: The doctor prescribed effective painkillers to ease the intense post-surgery discomfort.
items.ex_zh: 医生开具了有效的止痛药，以缓解术后的剧烈不适。
items.ex2_en: The tension eased noticeably once the peace agreement was officially signed yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 昨天和平协议正式签署后，紧张局势明显缓和了下来。

items.def_en: To reduce the harshness, severity, or harmful effects of something
items.ex_en: Prompt emergency measures helped mitigate the devastating impacts of the sudden flash flood.
items.ex_zh: 及时的应急措施有助于缓解突发山洪造成的破坏性影响。

items.def_en: To make suffering, deficiency, or severe problems less intense or severe
items.ex_en: The government introduced new subsidies to alleviate the suffering of drought-stricken farmers.
items.ex_zh: 政府出台了新的补贴措施，以减轻遭受旱灾的农民的痛苦。

items.def_en: To make a bad, unpleasant, or painful situation better and more tolerable
items.ex_en: International humanitarian aid helped ameliorate the harsh living conditions in the refugee camps.
items.ex_zh: 国际人道主义援助有助于改善难民营内艰苦的生活条件。
items.ex2_en: Working conditions ameliorated significantly after employees formed an independent labor union.
items.ex2_zh: 员工成立独立工会后，工作环境得到了显著改善。

items.def_en: 1. To make or become better; to improve.
items.ex_en: Targeted social investments can substantially meliorate the economic prospects of impoverished rural communities.
items.ex_zh: 有针对性的社会投资能够大幅改善贫困乡村社区的经济前景。
