items.ex2_en: Patient symptoms meliorated steadily under the innovative new experimental medical therapy.
items.ex2_zh: 在创新的实验性新疗法下，病人的症状稳步好转。

items.def_en: To cause a failing situation, business, or economy to become successful and healthy again
items.ex_en: The newly appointed chief executive managed to turn around the struggling tech enterprise.
items.ex_zh: 新任命的首席执行官成功扭转了这家陷入困境的科技公司的颓势。
items.ex2_en: The company's financial fortunes turned around remarkably after launching the innovative product.
items.ex2_zh: 推出这款创新产品后，该公司的财务状况显著好转。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on transforming bad, distressing, or substandard conditions into more tolerable, humane, or positive states.
groups.summary_zh: 指改善恶劣现状、减轻痛苦困境或使情势好转。
groups.desc_en: Agents reduce systemic suffering or reverse decline to foster recovery, going beyond basic 'improving' by operating squarely on distress, deficits, or structural failure.
groups.desc_zh: 行动者缓解苦难或逆转衰颓局面，与泛泛的'改善'不同，专门针对痛苦、短板或系统性恶化进行干预与纾解救赎。
groups.nuance_en: ease: lowering friction, tension, or local pain (tension / burden) · mitigate: reducing structural severity or impact of hazards (damage / risk) · alleviate: taking off the physical or economic weight of misery (poverty / symptoms) · ameliorate: institutional refinement of substandard social states (conditions / poverty) · turn around: complete 180-degree reversal of failing fortunes (economy / company)
groups.nuance_zh: ease: 舒缓身心痛楚或松绑严苛紧张状态 (tension / burden) · mitigate: 减轻自然或战略危害的破坏烈度 (damage / risk) · alleviate: 显著纾解贫困或病痛之重压 (poverty / symptoms) · ameliorate: 对落后恶劣的社会环境进行制度性改良 (conditions / poverty) · turn around: 使颓败的企业或经济彻底扭亏为盈实现大逆转 (economy / company)

groups.name: Anchor & Ground · 固定与扎根 (Ground, Anchor, Root)
groups.tip: 将底部固牢立定防止倾倒

items.def_en: To attach or secure one thing firmly to another so that it will not come loose
items.ex_en: Workers must securely fasten the heavy steel cables to the concrete pillars.
items.ex_zh: 工人们必须将粗重钢缆牢固地固定在混凝土柱上。
items.ex2_en: The heavy wooden gate fastens securely with a sturdy iron latch mechanism.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的木门依靠结实的铁插销装置牢牢扣合。

items.def_zh: 使稳固，牢固确立；使停飞；使搁浅；罚（孩子）不准出门
items.def_en: 1. To base something firmly on facts, principles, or solid ground. 2. To prevent an aircraft or pilot from flying. 3. To cause a boat or ship to run aground. 4. To punish a child by forbidding them to go out.
items.ex_en: Aviation authorities decided to ground all passenger flights due to the incoming hurricane.
items.ex_zh: 由于飓风即将来临，航空当局决定让所有客运航班停飞。

items.def_en: To fix something firmly in position so that it cannot move, or establish a firm psychological or moral basis
items.ex_en: The captain carefully navigated into the protected bay to anchor for the night.
items.ex_zh: 船长小心翼翼地驶入受庇护的海湾抛锚过夜。
items.ex2_en: The engineering team anchored the tall communications tower firmly into solid bedrock.
items.ex2_zh: 工程队将高耸的通信塔牢牢固定在坚硬的基岩中。

items.def_en: To tie a boat or vehicle securely with ropes or an anchor to the shore or ground
items.ex_en: The sailors worked quickly to moor the luxury yacht securely to the pier.
items.ex_zh: 水手们迅速行动，将豪华游艇牢牢系泊在码头上。
items.ex2_en: Dozens of colorful fishing boats moor quietly along the coastal harbor docks.
items.ex2_zh: 数十艘色彩斑斓的渔船静静地停泊在沿海港口码头旁。

items.def_en: (+ in) To fix something firmly into a place, tradition, or origin so it develops deep ties
items.ex_en: His peculiar storytelling style is deeply rooted in ancient local folk traditions.
items.ex_zh: 他独特的讲故事风格深深植根于古老的地方民间传统。
items.ex2_en: Cacti root quickly in porous desert soil despite severe moisture deficits.
items.ex2_zh: 尽管严重缺乏水分，仙人掌仍能在多孔的沙漠土壤中迅速扎根。

items.def_en: To fix an object or concept firmly and deeply into a surrounding mass or solid context
items.ex_en: The developers managed to embed the advanced security protocol directly into the system.
items.ex_zh: 开发人员成功将高级安全协议直接嵌入到系统之中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe securing an entity firmly to a foundation, bedrock, or fixed physical substrate to prevent drift or displacement. Figuratively, they describe basing arguments, principles, or individuals deeply in concrete realities and cultural roots.
groups.summary_zh: 指将物体或理念深植、固定于稳固基底以防漂移晃荡。
groups.desc_en: An entity is structurally bound to a substrate to prevent dislocation, differing from simple 'attaching' through profound physical stability, mooring, or conceptual foundationalism.
groups.desc_zh: 将物体或理念深植并固定于基底以防位移或动摇，不同于表层的'连接'，强调力学稳固、抗风浪锚定或思想扎根。
groups.nuance_en: fasten: mechanical interlocking of parts (seatbelt / latch) · ground: providing theoretical grounding or electrical safety (theory in reality / aircraft) · anchor: holding against hydrodynamic or volatile drift (ship / hope) · moor: securing floating vessels to docks via hawsers (vessel / boat) · root: biological or deep psychic embedding into origins (in culture / tradition) · embed: inserting deeply into a dense enveloping matrix (sensor / journalist)
groups.nuance_zh: fasten: 机械式的扣紧或固定连接 (seatbelt / latch) · ground: 使理论立足现实，或将飞行器停飞/电路接地 (theory in reality / aircraft) · anchor: 下锚使之在风浪动荡中保持定力 (ship / hope) · moor: 缆绳系泊固定船只 (vessel / boat) · root: 盘根错节般深植于历史文化或传统根基 (in culture / tradition) · embed: 深度内嵌于密闭基体或组织中 (sensor / journalist)

groups.name: Animal Bleats & Yelps · 羊啼与犬吠 (Baa, Bleat, Yelp)
groups.tip: 禽兽虫鸟发出的叫声鸣响

items.def_en: 1. When a sheep or lamb baas, it makes its characteristic bleating cry.
items.ex_en: A lost lamb began to baa softly as darkness fell over the hillside.
items.ex_zh: 夜幕降临山坡，一只走失的羊羔开始轻声咩咩叫。

items.def_en: 1. When a small dog or puppy yips, it lets out short, sharp, high-pitched barks.
items.ex_en: The excited terrier puppy began to yip whenever someone walked past the door.
items.ex_zh: 每当有人走过门前，那只兴奋的梗犬幼犬就会短促尖叫。

items.def_en: to make the typical wavering cry of a sheep or goat
items.ex_en: A frightened goat began to bleat loudly when the storm clouds suddenly gathered.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨云骤然聚集时，一只受惊的山羊开始大声哀鸣。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to utter a sudden, sharp, high-pitched cry of pain, distress, or excitement
items.ex_en: The injured stray hound gave a sudden yelp out when touched on its paw.
items.ex_zh: 那只受伤的流浪猎犬爪子被碰触时，突然痛得尖叫了一声。

items.def_en: to bark continuously with sharp, annoying, high-pitched snaps
items.ex_en: The neighbor's tiny Chihuahua would yap incessantly whenever a postal carrier approached.
items.ex_zh: 每当邮递员走近，邻居家的小吉娃娃就会烦人地狂吠不止。

items.def_en: to give a sudden, short, high-pitched cry of pain or alarm
items.ex_en: The puppy let out a sharp yelp after accidentally stepping on a thorn.
items.ex_zh: 小狗不小心踩到荆棘后，发出了一声刺耳的尖叫。

groups.summary_en: Animals such as sheep, goats, or canines utter brief, species-typical cries communicating distress, demand, pain, or social calls. Verbs denote distinct timbres ranging from dull bleating to sharp, high-pitched yelping.
groups.summary_zh: 羊或犬科动物发出短促高亢的叫声，用于呼叫同伴、发出惊叫或表达伤痛。
groups.desc_en: Emitting high-pitched, sharp, or plaintive vocal sounds characteristic of specific animals (especially sheep and canines), contrasting with deep roars or human articulate speech.
groups.desc_zh: 发出羊类、犬类等动物特有的尖锐、短促或哀怨鸣叫，与低沉咆哮或人类清晰的话语相对立。
groups.nuance_en: baa: natural bleat of a sheep (sheep / lamb) · bleat: plaintive sheep cry or whiny human complaint (sheep / goat / complaint) · yelp: sudden, sharp cry of pain or alarm (dog / puppy / pain) · yelp out: sudden vocal eruption under distress (cry / scream / agony) · yap: shrill, repetitive, irritating barking or chattering (terrier / dog / jaws) · yip: short, high-pitched excited squeak or bark (puppy / coyote)
groups.nuance_zh: baa: 羊类本能的咩咩叫 (sheep / lamb) · bleat: 羊的哀鸣或人类软弱的抱怨 (sheep / goat / complaint) · yelp: 突发尖利的痛呼或惊叫 (dog / puppy / pain) · yelp out: 痛苦中脱口而出的尖叫 (cry / scream / agony) · yap: 尖锐刺耳、连珠炮式的吠叫或唠叨 (terrier / dog / jaws) · yip: 幼犬兴奋短促的轻吠 (puppy / coyote)

groups.name: Announce & Proclaim · 宣告与公布 (Proclaim, Declare, Broadcast)
groups.tip: 从日常通知到庄严正式宣告

items.def_en: To make something known publicly and officially; to declare or broadcast information.
items.ex_en: The university board will officially announce the appointment of the new president tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 大学董事会将于明天正式公布新校长的任命。

items.def_en: To announce something clearly, firmly, and publicly
items.ex_en: The foreign minister stepped forward to declare the sovereign nation's strict neutrality.
items.ex_zh: 外交部长走上前去，郑重声明该主权国家的中立立场。

items.def_en: To tell a piece of news to a lot of people; disseminate information widely
items.ex_en: Please do not broadcast our confidential travel plans to the whole office.
items.ex_zh: 请不要把我们的保密出行计划到处宣扬给整个办公室的人。
items.ex2_en: The shocking corporate scandal broadcasted rapidly through local radio stations this morning.
items.ex2_zh: 这起令人震惊的企业丑闻今天早上迅速在当地广播电台传开。

items.def_en: To state something officially, ceremonially, or with authority
items.ex_en: The presiding judge will officially pronounce sentence on the convicted fraudster this afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 主审法官将于今天下午正式对这名定罪的诈骗犯宣判。

items.def_en: To announce or signal that something important or good is about to happen
items.ex_en: The breakthrough clinical trial was widely heralded as the dawn of a cure.
items.ex_zh: 这项突破性的临床试验被广泛预告为治愈希望的曙光。

items.def_en: To state something officially, publicly, and emphatically, often with legal authority
items.ex_en: The governor stepped forward to proclaim a state of emergency across the region.
items.ex_zh: 州长走上前去，庄严宣布该地区进入紧急状态。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the communicative act of transmitting official declarations, solemn statements, or important news openly and authoritatively to the public.
groups.summary_zh: 公开、权威且正式地向公众宣告或广播消息。
groups.desc_en: Formally and openly declaring information to a broad audience, distinguished from private whispering or casual chatting by its public authority, performative force, or ceremonial gravity.
groups.desc_zh: 面向公众正式、公开地发布信息，以其公共权威、施事效力或仪式庄重感区别于私下低语或随性闲聊。
groups.nuance_en: announce: standard formal disclosure of new facts (decision / engagement / arrival) · declare: authoritative or emphatic statement of reality or intent (independence / war / state of emergency) · proclaim: official, public, often solemn promulgation (republic / amnesty / victory) · pronounce: authoritative or formal verdict/judgment (dead / sentence / guilty) · broadcast: wide dissemination across media or loud dissemination of secrets (news / interview / secret) · herald: signaling or joyfully presaging the arrival of a new era or achievement (arrival / dawn / breakthrough)
groups.nuance_zh: announce: 标准公开宣布事实 (decision / engagement / arrival) · declare: 权威或强硬地宣称现实与意向 (independence / war / state of emergency) · proclaim: 庄严昭告天下 (republic / amnesty / victory) · pronounce: 具有法理效力的宣判或定性 (dead / sentence / guilty) · broadcast: 通过媒介大范围广播或张扬 (news / interview / secret) · herald: 预示新时代或成就的来临 (arrival / dawn / breakthrough)

groups.name: Answer & Reply · 问答与答复 (Answer, Reply, Retort)
groups.tip: 对疑问作出应答与正式回复

items.def_zh: 回答，答复；响应，应对；符合，适应
items.def_en: 1. To say, write, or do something in return to a question, letter, or call. 2. To match, correspond to, or satisfy a need or description.
items.ex_en: The secretary took less than two minutes to answer the client's urgent inquiry.
items.ex_zh: 秘书花了不到两分钟就回复了客户的紧急询问。

items.def_zh: 回答，答复；做出回应，反击
items.def_en: 1. To say, write, or do something as an answer to what someone has said, asked, or done.
items.ex_en: The ambassador took several days to formulate and reply to the foreign inquiry.
items.ex_zh: 大使花了好几天时间起草并答复了外国的质询。

items.def_en: [I/T] to send a written letter or message in answer to one received
items.ex_en: I sent her a long email last week, but she hasn't written back yet.
items.ex_zh: 我上周给她发了一封长邮件，但她还没给我回信。

items.def_en: (informal) to send a reply or communication back to an inquirer
items.ex_en: I sent an email last week, but she hasn't replied back yet.
items.ex_zh: 我上周发了邮件，但她还没回复。

items.def_en: (+ sb) to reply or answer, often impudently or argumentatively, to a speaker
items.ex_en: Don't answer back when your teacher is giving you advice.
items.ex_zh: 老师给你提建议时不要顶嘴。

items.def_en: to reply insolently or disrespectfully to someone in authority
items.ex_en: The rebellious teenager was grounded for daring to talk back to his teacher.
items.ex_zh: 这名叛逆的青少年因胆敢顶撞老师而被罚禁足。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this core question-and-answer dialogue frame center specifically on supplying a verbal or written statement to satisfy a question, letter, summons, or direct inquiry.
groups.summary_zh: 针对收到的提问、信函、传唤或呼叫给出直接回答或书面答复。
groups.desc_en: Responding verbally or textually to an antecedent inquiry or provocation, contrasting with initiating a dialogue or staying silent.
groups.desc_zh: 对先前的提问、言论或挑衅做出言语或书面回应，与发起对话或保持沉默相对立。
groups.nuance_en: answer: neutral, broad response to a question or challenge (question / door / phone) · reply: formal or direct response to an assertion or message (letter / email / inquiry) · write back: epistolary response via writing (letter / note) · reply back: redundant/informal responsive communication (message / email) · answer back: rude, defiant response to authority (parent / teacher / superior) · talk back: rebellious oral retorts challenging discipline (parent / boss)
groups.nuance_zh: answer: 中性广泛的回答或应答 (question / door / phone) · reply: 正式、直接的书面或口头答复 (letter / email / inquiry) · write back: 专门指写信或书面回复 (letter / note) · reply back: 口语口吻的回信或复讯 (message / email) · answer back: 顶嘴、反驳权威 (parent / teacher / superior) · talk back: 叛逆性的顶撞或不服管教 (parent / boss)

groups.name: Apply & Exert · 运用与施加 (Exert, Wield, Exercise)
groups.tip: 施加力量或运用能力

items.def_en: to bring a physical force, law, or rule into direct practical contact or use
items.ex_en: The technician had to apply continuous pressure to the valve to stop leaks.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员必须对阀门施加持续的压力以阻止泄漏。
items.ex2_en: The same basic safety rules apply equally to all factory machine operators.
items.ex2_zh: 同样的基本安全规则同等地适用于所有工厂机械操作员。

items.def_en: to make use of one's rights, skills, discretion, or patience
items.ex_en: Citizens must actively exercise their constitutional right to vote in the upcoming election.
items.ex_zh: 公民必须在即将举行的大选中积极行使其宪法赋予的投票权。

items.def_en: to put resources, arguments, or capabilities into action effectively
items.ex_en: The defense attorney will deploy several expert witnesses to establish an airtight alibi.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师将调动数名专家证人以确立无懈可击的不在场证明。

items.def_en: to apply force, influence, or resources firmly to solve an issue or affect an outcome
items.ex_en: Diplomats worked tirelessly to bring international pressure to bear on the rogue regime.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们不知疲倦地工作，对该流氓政权施加国际压力。

items.def_en: to hold and use effectively power, influence, or authority
items.ex_en: The media mogul continues to wield immense political influence across the entire nation.
items.ex_zh: 这位传媒大亨继续在全国范围内施加巨大的政治影响力。

items.def_zh: 施加（影响、压力等），运用（力量）；竭力，努力
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/over) To use power, influence, or physical force to achieve an effect. 2. ('exert oneself') To make a strong physical or mental effort.
items.ex_en: Powerful lobby groups frequently exert undue influence over environmental policy decisions.
items.ex_zh: 实力强大的游说团体常常对环境政策决策施加不当影响。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate bringing force, pressure, authority, or specialized capabilities to bear on someone or something to produce a desired outcome.
groups.summary_zh: 指主动施加压力、动用权力或发挥某种能力以达到目的。
groups.desc_en: Putting an intangible capacity, power, or instrument into active, purposeful physical or psychological operation, contrasting with passive possession or idle restraint.
groups.desc_zh: 将无形的能力、权力或手段付诸积极、有目的的实际运作，与被动持有或闲置克制相对立。
groups.nuance_en: apply: purposeful, practical implementation of a rule or force (pressure / rule / logic) · exert: vigorous expenditure of strength, influence, or effort (pressure / influence / authority) · wield: confident handling of vast power, influence, or a weapon (power / influence / weapon) · exercise: regular, legitimate manifestation of rights or faculties (right / discretion / caution) · deploy: strategic positioning and mobilization of resources or tactics (resources / tactics / force) · bring to bear: channeling diverse pressures or arguments onto a single target (pressure / influence / resources)
groups.nuance_zh: apply: 实用性地落实规则或外力 (pressure / rule / logic) · exert: 费力施加自身力量或影响 (pressure / influence / authority) · wield: 熟练执掌并运用大权或武器 (power / influence / weapon) · exercise: 依法或依理行使权利与机能 (right / discretion / caution) · deploy: 战略性调配与部署资源策略 (resources / tactics / force) · bring to bear: 集中施加多方压力或论据以破局 (pressure / influence / resources)

groups.name: Apportion & Ration · 分发与配给 (Allot, Ration, Parcel)
groups.tip: 按份拆分发放到人

items.def_en: To divide food or resources into servings or shares and distribute them
items.ex_en: Volunteers helped portion out warm meals to displaced families at the shelter.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们在庇护所协助把热餐按份分发给流离失所的家庭。

items.def_en: (also 'portion out') To divide something into parts or servings and distribute them.
items.ex_en: The chef took great care to portion the expensive caviar among eight guests.
items.ex_zh: 大厨非常细心地将昂贵的鱼子酱分成八份分给客人们。

items.def_en: To assign a specific amount, share, or time to someone for a particular purpose
items.ex_en: The committee decided to allot additional funds for regional renewable energy research initiatives.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定为区域可再生能源研究项目拨发额外资金。

items.def_en: To divide and distribute parts of something among people according to a plan or proportion
items.ex_en: The council must fairly apportion the maintenance costs among all commercial property owners.
items.ex_zh: 市政委员会必须在所有商业业主之间合理分摊维护费用。

items.def_en: To distribute or administer something, especially punishment, rewards, or harsh treatment
items.ex_en: The merciless magistrate chose to mete out the harshest penalty permitted by law.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的法官决定给予法律所允许的最严厉的惩罚。

items.def_en: To limit the amount of a scarce commodity that someone is allowed to have
items.ex_en: During the severe drought, authorities had to strictly ration domestic water usage.
items.ex_zh: 在严重干旱期间，当局不得不严格限量配给生活用水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame center on dividing a limited pool of resources, tasks, or provisions into measured, calculated shares among recipients. They highlight fairness, scarcity, or systematic allocation.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重将有限资源、份额或定量配额精准、有计划地分给各个对象。
groups.desc_en: Dividing and distributing limited resources or punitive consequences according to a scheme, rule, or constraint, contrasting with haphazard sharing or wholesale dumping.
groups.desc_zh: 根据特定方案、规则或限度，分割并分配有限资源或惩处，与随意分享或整批抛售相对立。
groups.nuance_en: allot: designating a predetermined share or slot to a specific recipient (time / funds / quota) · apportion: dividing proportionally according to justice, ratio, or liability (costs / blame / seats) · ration: strictly limiting consumption during scarcity (food / water / fuel) · mete out: solemn, authoritative dispensing of punishment or harsh treatment (punishment / justice / penalty) · portion out: physical division into discrete meal-sized or task-sized servings (food / soup / rations) · portion: assigning shares of a whole (estate / territory / goods)
groups.nuance_zh: allot: 按预定配额拨给份额或时间 (time / funds / quota) · apportion: 按比例或责任分摊与划分 (costs / blame / seats) · ration: 资源匮乏时的定量配给限制 (food / water / fuel) · mete out: 权威性地施加惩罚或报应 (punishment / justice / penalty) · portion out: 动手分成一份份的份量 (food / soup / rations) · portion: 将整体分块划拨 (estate / territory / goods)

groups.name: Apprehend & Collar · 逮捕与擒获 (Apprehend, Collar, Nab)
groups.tip: 警方突然出击当场捉拿归案

items.def_en: To bring a suspect into a police station or court for questioning or custody
items.ex_en: Detectives decided to haul in the primary suspect for intense overnight questioning.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们决定拘押传讯主要嫌疑人进行通宵突审。

items.def_en: (informal) To arrest someone and take them to a police station
items.ex_en: The local patrol officers managed to run in two suspects after the brawl.
items.ex_zh: 斗殴发生后，当地巡警成功将两名嫌疑人拘捕带回警局。

items.def_en: (informal) To arrest someone or raid a place for illegal activity
items.ex_en: Federal agents arrived before dawn to bust the illegal gambling den downtown.
items.ex_zh: 联邦特工在黎明前赶到，突击查抄了市中心的非法赌场。
items.ex2_en: The counterfeit ring busted completely after federal investigators intercepted the shipments.
items.ex2_zh: 在联邦调查人员截获货物后，该制假团伙彻底垮台被查抄。

items.def_en: (informal) To capture or arrest someone, especially by surprising them or catching them red-handed
items.ex_en: Undercover security officers moved quickly to collar the pickpocket in the crowded subway.
items.ex_zh: 便衣安保人员迅速行动，在拥挤的地铁里当场逮住了扒手。

items.def_en: To catch and arrest someone who has committed a crime, especially after a search
items.ex_en: Federal marshals launched a coordinated operation to apprehend the fugitive across state borders.
items.ex_zh: 联邦法警展开联合行动，跨越州界拘捕了这名逃犯。

items.def_zh: 捉拿，当场逮捕；一把抓取，夺得
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To catch and arrest a criminal, especially unexpectedly. 2. (informal) To take, grab, or get something quickly.
items.ex_en: Patrol officers were able to nab the burglar just as he fled through the window.
items.ex_zh: 巡警在窃贼刚从窗户逃出时就一把将他逮住。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to taking a suspect or criminal into custody by seizing them directly, ranging from colloquial catchphrases to formal law enforcement procedures.
groups.summary_zh: 指警方或执法力量依法或当场拘捕、擒获嫌疑人。
groups.desc_en: Physically seizing, intercepting, or detaining a suspect or wrongdoer, colored by varying degrees of slangy informality, surprise, or legal formality compared to generic capture.
groups.desc_zh: 对嫌疑人或违法者进行人身控制、抓捕或拘留，相较于宽泛的捕捉，带有不同程度的口语俗称、突击性或法律程序意味。
groups.nuance_en: apprehend: formal legal seizure of a suspect by law enforcement (suspect / fugitive / criminal) · collar: physical or unexpected street-level seizure of an offender (thief / suspect / culprit) · nab: quick, opportunistic capture in the act (pickpocket / thief / crook) · bust: organized police raid or crackdown involving arrest (drug dealer / gang / ring) · haul in: forcibly bringing a suspect into a police station (suspect / witness) · run in: colloquial taking into custody for an infraction (drifter / offender)
groups.nuance_zh: apprehend: 警方法律意义上的正式捉拿归案 (suspect / fugitive / criminal) · collar: 扭住衣领般当街拿下或逮住 (thief / suspect / culprit) · nab: 眼疾手快抓获现行犯 (pickpocket / thief / crook) · bust: 突击搜查并一网打尽 (drug dealer / gang / ring) · haul in: 强行将嫌疑人带回警局 (suspect / witness) · run in: 口语中因小过将人拘解带走 (drifter / offender)

groups.name: Approve & Ratify · 批准与认可 (Ratify, Endorse, Sanction)
groups.tip: 官方立法确认并正式批准

items.def_en: To give official legal power or formal permission for someone to do something
items.ex_en: The board of directors met early to authorize funding for the new facility.
items.ex_zh: 董事会早早召开会议，正式核准为新设施提供资金。

items.def_zh: 不加审查地照批，走过场批准
items.def_en: To approve an official measure or decision routinely and mechanically without critical scrutiny
items.ex_en: The compliant committee was criticized for choosing to rubber-stamp the controversial building project.
items.ex_zh: 顺从的委员会因不加审查地走过场批准该争议建筑项目而饱受批评。

items.def_en: To give formal and final approval or confirmation to a project, expense, or decision
items.ex_en: The finance director finally agreed to sign off on the substantial marketing budget.
items.ex_zh: 财务总监最终同意签字核准这笔数额巨大的营销预算。

items.def_en: To give official, binding permission or formal legal approval for an action
items.ex_en: The ethics board will not sanction clinical trials without proper written patient consent.
items.ex_zh: 伦理委员会不会正式批准没有适当书面患者知情同意的临床试验。

items.def_en: To express public, authoritative approval and support for a proposal, candidate, or plan
items.ex_en: Prominent labor unions gathered to officially endorse the progressive candidate for mayor.
items.ex_zh: 各大知名工会齐聚一堂，公开表态支持并背书这位进步派市长候选人。

items.def_zh: 正式批准，签署生效（条约、协议等）
items.def_en: To make an agreement, treaty, or amendment officially valid by signing or voting for it.
items.ex_en: The senate voted overwhelmingly to ratify the landmark international climate agreement.
items.ex_zh: 参议院以压倒性多数投票批准了这项具有里程碑意义的国际气候协定。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on formal acts of giving legal, legislative, or institutional authority and binding assent to treaties, agreements, or appointments.
groups.summary_zh: 强调机关或法权层面赋予公约、法案或提案法律效力。
groups.desc_en: Formally confirming, legitimizing, or giving institutional assent to a decision, treaty, or action, contrasting with spontaneous personal agreement or unofficial toleration.
groups.desc_zh: 对某项决定、条约或行为进行正式确认、赋予合法性或制度化许可，与自发的个人赞同或非官方默许相对立。
groups.nuance_en: authorize: conferring official legal permission or power to act (payment / search / expenditure) · sanction: giving authoritative blessing, or alternatively legal penalization (operation / conduct / intervention) · endorse: public, reputational approval or support (candidate / proposal / product) · ratify: formal legislative or constitutional confirmation of a treaty or law (treaty / amendment / agreement) · sign off on: practical, bureaucratic final approval of a project (plan / budget / design) · rubber-stamp: approving thoughtlessly and automatically without scrutiny (decision / legislation / measure)
groups.nuance_zh: authorize: 官方授权给予合法执行权 (payment / search / expenditure) · sanction: 给予权威性认可与批准 (operation / conduct / intervention) · endorse: 以个人或机构名誉公开背书支持 (candidate / proposal / product) · ratify: 立法或条约层面的正式批准生效 (treaty / amendment / agreement) · sign off on: 官僚流程中签字放行 (plan / budget / design) · rubber-stamp: 不加核查闭眼盖章式审批 (decision / legislation / measure)

groups.name: Arbitrate & Preside Competitions · 裁判与执法裁断 (Judge, Referee, Adjudicate)
groups.tip: 法官或裁判依法决断

items.def_zh: 裁判，裁决，评定；审理，判决；判断，评价
items.def_en: 1. To decide the result of a competition, contest, or show as a judge. 2. (law) To formally try a legal case or hear someone in a court of law. 3. To form an opinion or conclusion about someone or something.
items.ex_en: Celebrity chefs were specially invited to judge the prestigious national baking competition.
items.ex_zh: 名厨们受特邀担任这项著名的全国烘焙大赛的裁判。

items.def_zh: 当裁判，为……担任裁判；审阅，评审（学术论文等）
items.def_en: 1. To act as the official referee in a sports match to ensure the rules are obeyed. 2. (academic) To evaluate and review a scholarly article or book before publication.
items.ex_en: A veteran official was selected to referee the contentious championship football match.
items.ex_zh: 一名资深裁判被选定执法这场充满争议的足球冠军决赛。

items.def_zh: 为……当裁判，当裁判；仲裁，公断
items.def_en: 1. To act as the official judge enforcing the rules in sports such as baseball, tennis, or cricket; to arbitrate or decide a dispute.
items.ex_en: She was chosen to umpire the highly anticipated men's tennis final on Sunday.
items.ex_zh: 她被选定担任周日备受瞩目的男子网球决赛的主裁判。

items.def_zh: 担任裁判；主持赛事/仪式
items.def_en: (+ at/in) to act as an official in charge of a sports match or formal proceeding
items.ex_en: The senior diplomat was requested to officiate at the international peace treaty signing.
items.ex_zh: 资深外交官受邀主持了这项国际和平条约的签署仪式。

items.def_zh: 判决，裁决，裁定；担任（赛事等的）评判
items.def_en: 1. (+ on/between) To act as a judge in a competition, dispute, or legal case and make a formal decision.
items.ex_en: A panel of independent arbitrators was formed to adjudicate on the maritime dispute.
items.ex_zh: 一个独立仲裁小组被组建起来对这起海事争端作出裁决。

items.def_en: [I/T] to officially judge and settle a dispute between two dissenting parties
items.ex_en: An independent labor mediator was invited to arbitrate the bitter wage dispute.
items.ex_zh: 一位独立劳工调解员受邀就激烈的工资争议进行仲裁。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this institutional frame describe serving as an official arbiter, applying formal rules to evaluate contestants, oversee sporting matches, or deliver binding legal or administrative verdicts.
groups.summary_zh: 指官方裁决人员依规主持竞赛评判、体育执法或作出正式裁定。
groups.desc_en: Serving as an impartial authority to interpret rules, maintain order, and resolve disputes in competitive sports or legal proceedings, contrasting with mere spectatorship or biased advocacy.
groups.desc_zh: 作为中立权威，在体育竞技或法律程序中解释规则、维持秩序并裁定争端，与单纯观赛或偏袒辩护相对立。
groups.nuance_en: judge: evaluating merit and delivering decisions in contests or courts (contest / competition / case) · referee: supervising continuous-motion field sports to enforce rules (match / soccer / fight) · umpire: making localized, definitive calls in set-play sports (baseball / tennis / cricket) · officiate: presiding ceremonially or administratively over a game or rite (ceremony / game / funeral) · adjudicate: formal legal settlement of contested claims (claim / dispute / bankruptcy) · arbitrate: legally binding dispute resolution between two conflicting parties (dispute / grievance / settlement)
groups.nuance_zh: judge: 在比赛或法庭上依据标准评判断案 (contest / competition / case) · referee: 场上移动执法高流动性球赛 (match / soccer / fight) · umpire: 在固定回合制球赛中作出判定 (baseball / tennis / cricket) · officiate: 正式主持赛事或典礼活动 (ceremony / game / funeral) · adjudicate: 司法或行政上审判定夺争议 (claim / dispute / bankruptcy) · arbitrate: 仲裁化解劳资或双方利益争端 (dispute / grievance / settlement)

groups.name: Archive & Record · 存档与记录 (Chronicle, Document, Log, Catalog)
groups.tip: 将历史资料收录建档保存

items.def_en: To record the details of an event or process formally in writing or media
items.ex_en: Historians worked painstakingly to document the oral testimonies of wartime survivors.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家们艰苦卓绝地工作，以文献形式记录战时幸存者的口述证言。

items.def_en: To enter systematic facts, times, or events into an official record or register
items.ex_en: Air traffic controllers must immediately log every unusual radar discrepancy in detail.
items.ex_zh: 空中交通管制员必须立即将每起异常雷达偏差详细载入日志。

items.def_en: To place or store historical records, documents, or electronic data in an archive.
items.ex_en: The university library began a major project to archive rare historical manuscripts digitally.
items.ex_zh: 大学图书馆启动了一个大型项目，将珍贵的历史手稿进行数字化归档。

items.def_en: To put documents or records into an orderly collection or storage system for later use
items.ex_en: She filed away the advice for future reference.
items.ex_zh: 她把这条建议记在心里，以备日后参考。

items.def_en: To record a series of events in a detailed, factual, and chronological way
items.ex_en: The detailed memoirs chronicle the arduous journey of early polar explorers.
items.ex_zh: 这些详尽的回忆录按时间顺序记述了早期极地探险家的艰辛旅程。

items.def_en: To make a complete, classified, and descriptive list of items or materials
items.ex_en: Curators took several months to catalog thousands of ancient artifacts in the collection.
items.ex_zh: 策展人们花了数月时间为馆藏的数千件古代文物编制分类目录。

groups.summary_en: This scenario involves systematically preserving information, historical artifacts, or governance transactions for perpetuity and retrievability. Actions emphasize authenticity, structure, and formal documentation.
groups.summary_zh: 指按规范对历史数据、文件或事项进行系统建档、编目与长期保存。
groups.desc_en: Systematically collecting, preserving, and organizing factual records, documents, or artifacts for long-term preservation and retrieval, contrasting with immediate casual notation or discarding.
groups.desc_zh: 系统性收集、保存和整理事实记录、文献或档案，以备长期留存和检索，与随手便条或随手丢弃相对立。
groups.nuance_en: document: providing detailed empirical evidence and written proof (process / case / abuses) · log: keeping a continuous chronological record of events or metrics (hours / miles / calls) · archive: depositing records into secure long-term historical storage (data / records / correspondence) · file away: systematically stowing documents into classified folders (papers / report / receipt) · chronicle: recording historical events in literary, chronological narrative form (history / rise / voyage) · catalog: creating an organized, indexed inventory of items (collection / books / exhibits)
groups.nuance_zh: document: 用书面证据翔实记录以供证实 (process / case / abuses) · log: 按时间顺序流水账式登记运行数据 (hours / miles / calls) · archive: 封存移交历史档案库长期保管 (data / records / correspondence) · file away: 归类入档存放于文件夹中 (papers / report / receipt) · chronicle: 编年体叙事记录历史沿革 (history / rise / voyage) · catalog: 编制系统化的条目目录或清单 (collection / books / exhibits)

groups.name: Arise & Emerge · 出现与产生 (Arise, Emerge, Crop up)
groups.tip: 问题或现象逐渐浮现

items.def_en: to become evident or visible after having been hidden or dormant
items.ex_en: Disturbing financial irregularities began to surface after an independent audit was launched.
items.ex_zh: 独立审计启动之后，令人不安的财务违规问题开始浮出水面。

items.def_en: to become apparent, prominent, or known through inquiry or gradual revelation
items.ex_en: Startling evidence began to emerge during the extensive investigation by congressional researchers.
items.ex_zh: 在国会研究员的广泛调查过程中，令人震惊的证据逐渐显露出来。

items.def_zh: 出现，浮现；发生，产生；起身
items.def_en: 1. to begin to exist, emerge, or become noticeable. 2. to get up or stand up.
items.ex_en: Unforeseen logistical challenges may arise when entering new overseas retail markets.
items.ex_zh: 在开拓新的海外零售市场时，可能会出现不可预见的物流挑战。

items.def_en: to appear, occur, or come to light unexpectedly or inconveniently
items.ex_en: Several urgent technical issues unexpectedly cropped up during the software rollout yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 昨天在软件上线发布期间，意外地突然冒出了几个紧急技术故障。

items.def_en: to arise, occur, or be brought into consideration unexpectedly or naturally
items.ex_en: The sensitive topic of employee compensation will certainly come up during tomorrow's meeting.
items.ex_zh: 员工薪酬这一敏感议题肯定会在明天的会议上被提及讨论。

items.def_en: to appear, develop, or emerge suddenly and in noticeable numbers
items.ex_en: Trendy cafes began to spring up across the historic district this year.
items.ex_zh: 今年，时髦的咖啡馆开始在历史街区各处涌现。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame signify intangible matters (problems, questions, opportunities, or disputes) coming into existence, coming to notice, or developing out of a preceding situation. 'Arose' is the simple past of arise.
groups.summary_zh: 特指抽象事物（如问题、机遇、争执等）产生、浮现或显露出来。
groups.desc_en: Transitioning from invisibility, latency, or non-existence into active visibility or recognition, contrasting with remaining static, hidden, or intentionally produced.
groups.desc_zh: 从隐匿、潜伏或无到有地转变为显现、发生或被察觉，与保持静止、隐藏或有意制造相对立。
groups.nuance_en: arise: originating naturally as a result of circumstances or problems (questions / complications / opportunities) · emerge: gradually breaking out from obscurity, darkness, or confinement (leader / economy / truth) · surface: coming to the noticeable upper layer after lying dormant or submerged (allegations / rumors / issues) · crop up: appearing unexpectedly or sporadically to cause distraction (problems / errors / weeds) · spring up: rapidly and prolifically bursting into existence (buildings / businesses / doubts) · come up: arising casually in conversation or scheduling (issue / topic / trial)
groups.nuance_zh: arise: 顺理成章或由局势派生出问题 (questions / complications / opportunities) · emerge: 从隐匿或困境中逐步崭露头角 (leader / economy / truth) · surface: 沉寂已久后浮出水面为人所知 (allegations / rumors / issues) · crop up: 意外、零星冒出来添乱 (problems / errors / weeds) · spring up: 雨后春笋般迅速拔地而起 (buildings / businesses / doubts) · come up: 随口被提及或事项临近 (issue / topic / trial)

groups.name: Arm & Equip · 武装与配备 (Arm, Equip, Weaponize)
groups.tip: 配置武器设备充实战力

items.def_en: To supply someone or oneself with weapons or equipment needed for defense or attack
items.ex_en: The government decided to arm local guards to protect the remote border.
items.ex_zh: 政府决定为当地警卫配备武器，以保卫偏远的边境。

items.def_en: To provide someone or an organization with a complete set of clothes, armor, or specialized equipment
items.ex_en: They managed to outfit the entire research expedition with advanced polar gear.
items.ex_zh: 他们设法为整支科考队配备了先进的极地装备。

items.def_en: To provide a person, group, or vehicle with the necessary tools, machinery, or gear for a specific purpose
items.ex_en: The charity worked tirelessly to equip regional clinics with modern medical devices.
items.ex_zh: 该慈善机构孜孜不倦地工作，为地区诊所配备现代医疗设备。

items.def_en: To supply a ship, vehicle, or facility with essential machinery, weapons, or supplies
items.ex_en: The laboratory was fitted out with the latest analytical instruments.
items.ex_zh: 该实验室配备了最先进的分析仪器。

items.def_en: To equip or adapt an area, civilian police force, or resource for military purposes
items.ex_en: Critics argued that the state should not militarize municipal police departments.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士认为，国家不应将市政警察部门军事化。

items.def_zh: 将…改造为武器；使武器化
items.def_en: 1. To adapt or develop something (such as a technology, chemical agent, or issue) into a weapon to attack or gain advantage.
items.ex_en: Hostile actors attempted to weaponize sensitive private data during the campaign.
items.ex_zh: 敌对势力企图在竞选期间将敏感的私人数据武器化。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe supplying individuals, military units, or devices with weapons, tactical gear, or offensive capability. While 'equip' broadly covers necessary operational gear, 'arm' and 'weaponize' focus specifically on offensive or combative readiness.
groups.summary_zh: 指为人员或组织配备武器装备或使某物具备攻击性功能。
groups.desc_en: Providing an agent, group, or object with the technical apparatus, weapons, or specialized gear necessary for functional capability or combat readiness, contrasting with stripping bare or leaving unprepared.
groups.desc_zh: 为个体、团体或载具提供执行任务或战备所需的专业器械、武器或装备，与剥夺装备或毫无准备相对立。
groups.nuance_en: arm: supplying offensive or defensive weaponry and lethal capability (rebels / soldiers / police) · equip: outfitting with functional tools, machinery, or technical skills (lab / team / vehicle) · outfit: supplying complete sets of specialized clothing or gear for a venture (expedition / squad / crew) · fit out: furnishing a ship, building, or room with essential fittings (vessel / workshop / kitchen) · militarize: infusing civilian institutions or zones with military arms and tactics (police / border / zone) · weaponize: converting an ordinary tool, concept, or disease into an offensive instrument of destruction (information / pathogens / rhetoric)
groups.nuance_zh: arm: 配备致命武器或攻防军备 (rebels / soldiers / police) · equip: 配备专业功能工具、机器或技能 (lab / team / vehicle) · outfit: 全套行头配置以执行特定出征任务 (expedition / squad / crew) · fit out: 内部装或按规格装修设备 (vessel / workshop / kitchen) · militarize: 将民用组织或区域军事化 (police / border / zone) · weaponize: 将寻常工具、概念或病原体武器化 (information / pathogens / rhetoric)

groups.name: Arrest & Apprehend · 拘捕与缉拿 (Apprehend, Arrest, Detain)
groups.tip: 执法人员缉拿控制犯罪嫌疑人

items.def_en: To seize someone by legal authority and take them into custody on suspicion of a crime
items.ex_en: Authorities moved swiftly to arrest the corporate officer on suspicion of fraud.
items.ex_zh: 当局迅速行动，以涉嫌诈欺逮捕了该企业高管。

items.def_en: To catch a fleeing suspect or enemy through pursuit or force
items.ex_en: Federal agents worked alongside local deputies to capture the escaping felon.
items.ex_zh: 联邦特工与当地副警长联手抓获了那名在逃重罪犯。

items.def_en: (informal) To raid or catch someone in the act of committing a crime and arrest them
items.ex_en: Undercover officers managed to bust the smugglers right at the docks.
items.ex_zh: 便衣警察成功在码头当场查获了那些走私犯。
items.ex2_en: The notorious cartel busted suddenly following coordinated police raids across the province.
items.ex2_zh: 在全省协调一致的警方突袭后，这个恶名昭彰的贩毒集团轰然覆灭。

items.def_en: To take a suspect into custody for questioning or arrest
items.ex_en: Business usually picks up in the spring, and sales figures improve rapidly.
items.ex_zh: 生意通常在春季好转，销售额也会迅速回升。

items.def_en: To keep someone in official custody, preventing them from leaving
items.ex_en: Border officials have legal authority to detain undocumented travelers for questioning.
items.ex_zh: 边境官员拥有依法拘留无证旅客进行讯问的权力。

items.def_en: 1. (formal / law) To catch and arrest someone suspected of a crime. 2. (formal) To understand or perceive something.
items.ex_en: The fugitive was apprehended near the border after a prolonged manhunt.
items.ex_zh: 经过长时间的搜捕，这名逃犯在边境附近被捕。

groups.summary_en: This legal and policing frame denotes taking a suspect, offender, or fugitive into custody by lawful authority, depriving them of liberty for investigation or trial.
groups.summary_zh: 指执法机关依法抓捕、羁押或剥夺嫌疑人的人身自由。
groups.desc_en: Depriving an individual of freedom under legal or coercive authority on suspicion of an offense, contrasting with merely questioning, monitoring, or releasing.
groups.desc_zh: 依法或以强制权力因犯罪嫌疑剥夺某人的人身自由，与单纯盘问、监视或释放相对立。
groups.nuance_en: arrest: statutory seizure and formal booking of a person under the law (suspect / demonstrator / thief) · detain: holding someone temporarily in custody without necessarily charging immediately (passenger / suspect / alien) · apprehend: law-enforcement location and custody-taking of a fugitive or suspect (felon / suspect / runaway) · capture: seizing an elusive target or enemy by force or pursuit (fugitive / soldier / prey) · bust: aggressively raiding and capturing lawbreakers (dealer / ring / suspect) · pick up: informally taking someone in for questioning or minor detention (suspect / hitchhiker / witness)
groups.nuance_zh: arrest: 法律程序上的正式批捕拘捕 (suspect / demonstrator / thief) · detain: 短暂扣留盘查而不一定立即立案 (passenger / suspect / alien) · apprehend: 缉捕、扣押在逃人员归案 (felon / suspect / runaway) · capture: 经追捕强行擒获逃犯或敌军 (fugitive / soldier / prey) · bust: 扫荡突击捕获违规犯罪分子 (dealer / ring / suspect) · pick up: 便衣或随警带回局里协助调查 (suspect / hitchhiker / witness)

groups.name: Ascend & Reach the Peak · 上升与攀达顶峰 (Rise, Ascend, Crest)
groups.tip: 由低处向高处升起或登顶

items.def_en: to climb up onto a higher surface, platform, or incline
items.ex_en: The conductor took a deep breath before mounting the wooden podium.
items.ex_zh: 指挥家深吸了一口气，然后登上了木质指挥台。

items.def_en: 1. to climb up, go up, or rise to a higher position. 2. to rise to a higher rank or position of authority.
items.ex_en: She watched the majestic hot air balloon slowly ascend into heaven.
items.ex_zh: 她注视着那只雄伟的热气球缓缓升入苍穹。

items.def_en: to climb up a steep surface such as a rock face, mountain, or high wall
items.ex_en: Two brave mountaineers managed to scale the sheer granite cliff face.
items.ex_zh: 两名勇敢的登山者成功攀越了那座陡峭的花岗岩峭壁。

items.def_zh: 攀上……顶端；到达顶峰（或最高点）
items.def_en: to reach the top of a hill, mountain, or wave, or reach the highest level or point.
items.ex_en: The weary riders watched twilight descend as they crested the hill.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的骑手们登上山顶，目睹暮色降临。

items.def_en: to reach the top of a mountain, cliff, or steep climb
items.ex_en: We were completely exhausted by the time we topped out yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 昨天当我们终于攀至顶端时，整个人已经精疲力竭了。

items.def_en: [I/T] to successfully reach the peak of a high mountain
items.ex_en: Only experienced climbers should attempt to summit this dangerous icy mountain.
items.ex_zh: 只有经验丰富的登山者才应尝试登上这座危险的冰山顶峰。

groups.summary_en: An entity moves upward along a gradient, slope, or vertical axis, culminating in reaching the absolute highest point. Verbs scale in intensity from gentle or standard upward progress ('ascend') to arduous clambering and finally topping the summit ('crest', 'crown').
groups.summary_zh: 沿着斜坡或高度向上攀登，直至到达顶峰或最高点。
groups.desc_en: Moving progressively upward through degrees of height, intensity, or elevation until reaching the supreme apex, contrasting with steady-state leveling or descent.
groups.desc_zh: 沿高度、烈度或位阶逐步向上推进直至登顶，与保持平稳或下行相对立。
groups.nuance_en: ascend: formal upward spatial climb or elevation to power (throne / mountain / stairs) · mount: climbing onto a higher surface or steadily intensifying (horse / podium / pressure) · scale: climbing up steep or sheer heights with effort (wall / cliff / heights) · crest: reaching and traversing the top ridge of a physical wave or hill (hill / wave / ridge) · top out: hitting the absolute upper ceiling or peak limit (market / earnings / peak) · summit: reaching the highest peak of a mountain or career (Everest / mountain / career)
groups.nuance_zh: ascend: 庄重向上攀升或登上帝位 (throne / mountain / stairs) · mount: 跨上较高表面或压力逐步聚积 (horse / podium / pressure) · scale: 费力攀越陡峭垂直立面 (wall / cliff / heights) · crest: 冲上并越过浪尖或山脊线 (hill / wave / ridge) · top out: 触顶并停止增长封顶 (market / earnings / peak) · summit: 成功征服极峰或抵达巅峰 (Everest / mountain / career)

groups.name: Ascend & Scale · 上升与攀登 (Ascend, Clamber, Scramble)
groups.tip: 沿坡度或垂直方向攀爬上升

items.def_en: To rise, move upward, or climb toward a higher point or level
items.ex_en: The royal delegation began to ascend the grand marble staircase slowly.
items.ex_zh: 皇家代表团开始缓慢地登上宏伟的大理石阶梯。

items.def_en: To climb quickly up a pole, rope, or tree by grasping with arms and legs
items.ex_en: The mischievous boy decided to shinny up the flagpole on dare.
items.ex_zh: 那个淘气的男孩在激将之下蹭着爬上了旗杆。

items.def_en: To climb up or over a steep surface such as a wall or cliff
items.ex_en: Commando units were trained to scale fortress walls in total silence.
items.ex_zh: 突击队员接受过在绝对寂静中攀爬要塞城墙的训练。

items.def_en: To move upward on a slope, steep surface, or vertical object using feet and usually hands; to go up gradually in altitude, amount, or level.
items.ex_en: Hikers must climb a steep, winding path to reach the sanctuary.
items.ex_zh: 徒步旅行者必须沿着一条陡峭曲折的小路攀登才能到达庇护所。

items.def_en: To climb hastily over rough, steep, or rocky ground using hands and feet
items.ex_en: The hikers had to scramble over loose boulders near the summit.
items.ex_zh: 徒步者们不得不手脚并用攀爬山顶附近松动的巨石。

items.def_en: To climb or move with difficulty or awkwardness, using both hands and feet
items.ex_en: He had to clamber over slippery rocks to reach safety.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不吃力地爬过湿滑的岩石以到达安全地带。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe upward physical movement, especially effortful negotiation of vertical or steep terrain using limbs or mechanical momentum. They range from formal upward progression to hurried, awkward scrambles.
groups.summary_zh: 强调借助肢体攀爬陡峭地形或向上移行的动作方式。
groups.desc_en: Physically climbing or negotiating vertical or rugged inclines using bodily exertion, limbs, or technique, contrasting with effortless gliding, riding, or walking on flat terrain.
groups.desc_zh: 运用肢体力量或攀登技术在陡坡或垂直面上克服重力向上，与平地轻松行走或乘坐机械上升相对立。
groups.nuance_en: climb: generic, deliberate upward movement using legs and hands (tree / ladder / mountain) · ascend: formal, steady upward motion (stairs / slope / heights) · scale: overcoming sheer vertical barriers with skill or gear (wall / cliff / facade) · scramble: rough, awkward ascent over loose terrain using hands and feet (rocks / slope / scree) · clamber: clumsy, ungainly, effortful climbing over obstacles (over rocks / out of ditch / aboard) · shinny up: climbing a slender pole or trunk by gripping with arms and shins (tree / pole / post)
groups.nuance_zh: climb: 泛指手脚并用的向上攀登 (tree / ladder / mountain) · ascend: 稳步平缓的向上移动 (stairs / slope / heights) · scale: 攻克垂直高耸障碍物 (wall / cliff / facade) · scramble: 在乱石堆或陡坡手足并用乱攀 (rocks / slope / scree) · clamber: 吃力笨拙地爬越障碍物 (over rocks / out of ditch / aboard) · shinny up: 夹树干或杆子贴身蹭爬 (tree / pole / post)

groups.name: Attest & Testify · 证实与作证 (Attest, Testify, Vouch, Witness)
groups.tip: 出具证据证实或立誓作证

items.def_en: To see an event personally, or formally sign a legal document to confirm its authenticity
items.ex_en: An independent notary was summoned to witness the signing of wills.
items.ex_zh: 一名独立公证人被召集前来见证遗嘱的签署。

items.def_en: (+ to) To serve as explicit evidence or testimony that proves a fact or state of affairs
items.ex_en: These crumbling monuments bear witness to the empire's forgotten architectural glory.
items.ex_zh: 这些风化的遗迹见证了该帝国早已被遗忘的建筑辉煌。

items.def_en: To state emphatically or under oath that something is definitely true or accurate
items.ex_en: The storekeeper was prepared to swear to the suspect's identity.
items.ex_zh: 店主准备在宣誓下确认嫌疑人的身份。

items.def_en: (+ to) To make a formal statement of truth in court or provide clear proof of something
items.ex_en: The key informant agreed to testify against the corrupt local politician.
items.ex_zh: 关键举报人同意出庭作证指控这位腐败的地方政客。

items.def_en: (formal) To confirm, show, or prove that something is true, genuine, or correct, often by giving evidence.
items.ex_en: Several ancient manuscripts attest to the historic truth of this battle.
items.ex_zh: 几份古代手稿证实了这场战役的历史真实性。

items.def_en: (+ for) To assert personal confidence in someone's integrity, character, or the truth of a claim
items.ex_en: Her former manager was more than willing to vouch for her.
items.ex_zh: 她的前经理非常愿意为她的品行作保。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to providing formal or direct evidence that confirms the truth, existence, or authenticity of something, typically grounded in personal knowledge or official authority.
groups.summary_zh: 基于个人见闻或权威出具证据，正式证实某事属实或有效。
groups.desc_en: Confirming the authenticity, existence, or veracity of a claim based on direct personal knowledge, legal oath, or definitive evidence, contrasting with hearsay, speculation, or denial.
groups.desc_zh: 基于直接目击、法律誓约或确凿证据证实事物的真实性，与道听途说、主观臆测或否认相对立。
groups.nuance_en: testify: making a solemn legal declaration under oath in court (court / trial / hearing) · attest: serving as certified, official confirmation of a fact or quality (skills / truth / validity) · vouch: putting one's personal credibility on the line to guarantee someone or something (character / integrity / veracity) · witness: observing an event firsthand or signing an official instrument (accident / signature / will) · bear witness: serving as a historic, moral, or spiritual testament to an event (faith / history / courage) · swear to: pledging solemn personal certainty about an assertion (truth / fact / statement)
groups.nuance_zh: testify: 在法庭出庭宣誓作证 (court / trial / hearing) · attest: 官方或第三方正式证明有效性 (skills / truth / validity) · vouch: 押上个人信誉为他人人品担保 (character / integrity / veracity) · witness: 亲眼目睹案发或见证签字 (accident / signature / will) · bear witness: 历史或道德层面上见证并作证 (faith / history / courage) · swear to: 赌咒发誓确认其千真万确 (truth / fact / statement)

groups.name: Attribute & Ascribe · 归因与归功 (Attribute, Ascribe, Impute)
groups.tip: 追溯缘由肯定功劳

items.def_zh: 归功于，把…归于；信任，相信；把（钱）存入账户
items.def_en: 1. to attribute something to someone or believe that they are responsible for an achievement 2. to believe or trust someone or something 3. to add an amount of money to someone's bank account
items.ex_en: Historians largely credit the bold young commander with winning the siege.
items.ex_zh: 历史学家大多将攻城战的胜利归功于那位英勇的年轻指挥官。

items.def_en: To say or believe that something is the result of a particular situation, event, or person's action
items.ex_en: Medical researchers attribute the sudden outbreak to contaminated local water supplies.
items.ex_zh: 医学研究人员将这次疫情的突然爆发归因于当地受污染的水源。

items.def_en: To consider that something is caused by something else, especially as a useful lesson or experience
items.ex_en: Let us just chalk our awkward first performance up to experience.
items.ex_zh: 我们就把第一次糟糕的演出当作吸取经验吧。

items.def_en: To explain something by identifying a single main cause, such as luck or human failing
items.ex_en: The seasoned pilot chose to put the incident down to turbulence.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的飞行员决定将这一事件归因于气流颠簸。

items.def_en: To consider that something is caused by a particular person, event, or condition
items.ex_en: Philosophers often ascribe deep profound motives to ordinary human actions.
items.ex_zh: 哲学家们常常将深奥的动机归属于普通的人类行为。

items.def_en: To claim that someone is guilty of an undesirable action or possesses a particular quality
items.ex_en: It is unjust to impute selfish and malicious intentions to him.
items.ex_zh: 将自私恶毒的企图归咎于他是很不公正的。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on identifying the source, cause, or authorship of an action, achievement, or condition. Nuances range from acknowledging laudable contributions to assigning blame or inferring causal links.
groups.summary_zh: 指将原因、功劳、作品归属于特定对象或渊源。
groups.desc_en: Mentally mapping a quality, origin, causation, or responsibility back to its perceived source or creator, contrasting with treating an outcome as uncaused or completely generic.
groups.desc_zh: 在认知上将结果、性质、成就或罪责溯源至其来源或始作俑者，与视为凭空发生或无关相对立。
groups.nuance_en: attribute: objectively linking an outcome, quote, or effect to an agent or cause (success / quote / paintings) · ascribe: attributing an intangible quality, motive, or authorship to a source (motive / meaning / origins) · credit: positively acknowledging someone as the benefactor or creator of success (achievement / victory / discovery) · impute: ascribing an undesirable motive, fault, or guilt to someone (motive / blame / guilt) · chalk up to: informally explaining an outcome as caused by a specific factor (inexperience / bad luck / fatigue) · put down to: attributing a problem, error, or trait to an underlying factor (stress / age / misunderstanding)
groups.nuance_zh: attribute: 客观将成果、引言或事件归因于某人某事 (success / quote / paintings) · ascribe: 归属抽象动机、寓意或源头 (motive / meaning / origins) · credit: 褒奖地归功于某人的功劳 (achievement / victory / discovery) · impute: 将不良动机或罪责归咎于人 (motive / blame / guilt) · chalk up to: 口语中归结为运气、失误等外部因素 (inexperience / bad luck / fatigue) · put down to: 将负面表现归因为特定内因 (stress / age / misunderstanding)

groups.name: Avoid & Steer Clear · 避开与远离 (Shun, Steer Clear, Bypass)
groups.tip: 位移以躲避碰触

items.def_en: To pass along the edge of something, or avoid dealing directly with a delicate subject
items.ex_en: The politician tried to skirt the controversial questions about recent tax hikes.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客试图回避关于近期增税的争议性问题。

items.def_en: To go around a place, obstruction, or formal hurdle rather than going through it
items.ex_en: A new ring road was built to bypass heavy downtown congestion.
items.ex_zh: 修建了一条新的环路以绕过市中心的严重拥堵。

items.def_en: (+ of) To keep entirely away from someone, something dangerous, or an awkward topic
items.ex_en: Cautious investors should definitely steer clear of volatile and unregulated assets.
items.ex_zh: 谨慎的投资者绝对应该远离高波动且不受监管的资产。

items.def_en: To take proactive action to prevent an impending danger, injury, or misfortune from affecting you
items.ex_en: She drank warm lemon tea daily to ward off autumn colds.
items.ex_zh: 她每天喝热柠檬茶以防止秋季感冒。

items.def_en: 1. To stay away from someone or keep out of the path of something. 2. To prevent something bad or undesirable from happening.
items.ex_en: Drivers were officially advised to avoid the coastal motorway during floods.
items.ex_zh: 官方建议司机在洪水期间避开沿海高速公路。

items.def_en: To persistently and deliberately avoid, reject, or keep away from someone or something
items.ex_en: The solitary writer chose to shun publicity and live entirely secluded.
items.ex_zh: 这位深居简出的作家选择避开公众关注，过着完全幽居的生活。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers staying away from people, objects, topics, or hazards deliberately to prevent contact, risk, or conflict. It highlights preventative spatial distancing or intentional social aversion.
groups.summary_zh: 主动保持空间或社交距离，防范风险、接触或冲突。
groups.desc_en: Intentionally keeping one's path, conduct, or presence at a safe distance from hazards, confrontations, or unwanted persons, contrasting with direct engagement or collision.
groups.desc_zh: 有意在路线、举止或接触上与危险、冲突或排斥对象保持安全间距，与迎头相撞或直接接触相对立。
groups.nuance_en: avoid: generic effort to stay away from harm, individuals, or actions (mistakes / collision / trouble) · shun: deliberately, systematically ostracizing or rejecting someone/something (publicity / meat / society) · steer clear: actively navigating away from perceived danger or nuisance (trouble / area / conflict) · bypass: circumventing a physical obstruction, rule, or hierarchy (city / committee / regulations) · skirt: moving along the perimeter to evade touching a sensitive core (edge / issue / controversy) · ward off: taking proactive measures to deflect an impending threat (danger / evil / infection)
groups.nuance_zh: avoid: 泛指避开麻烦、碰撞或人事物 (mistakes / collision / trouble) · shun: 道德或生活习惯上刻意彻底避开或排斥 (publicity / meat / society) · steer clear: 掌舵般谨慎绕开危险区域或事端 (trouble / area / conflict) · bypass: 绕过物理堵塞、正规程序或层级 (city / committee / regulations) · skirt: 沿边缘打转以回避核心争端 (edge / issue / controversy) · ward off: 采取主动招架抵御来袭的灾殃 (danger / evil / infection)

groups.name: Ban & Prohibit · 禁止与取缔 (Forbid, Outlaw, Disallow)
groups.tip: 严格划定红线遏制行动

items.def_en: To state clearly that someone is not allowed to do something
items.ex_en: Strict safety regulations explicitly forbid laboratory workers from dining inside labs.
items.ex_zh: 严格的安全规程明确禁止实验人员在实验室内部用餐。

items.def_zh: 阻止；正式封阻（进入或参加）
items.def_en: (+ from) To officially prevent someone from entering a place, doing something, or participating
items.ex_en: Regulatory authorities moved swiftly to bar the disgraced executive from management.
items.ex_zh: 监管机构迅速采取行动，禁止这名名誉扫界的高管参与管理。

items.def_en: 1. To forbid or prohibit something officially, or ban someone from doing something.
items.ex_en: The city council voted decisively to ban single-use plastic bags.
items.ex_zh: 市议会果断投票决定禁止使用一次性塑料袋。

items.def_en: To formally, legally, or officially make an action or practice forbidden
items.ex_en: Federal workplace regulations strictly prohibit smoking inside all government office buildings.
items.ex_zh: 联邦工作场所法规严禁在所有政府办公楼内吸烟。

items.def_en: To pass a law that renders an activity, group, or object completely illegal
items.ex_en: The legislature voted decisively to outlaw hazardous chemical dumps near rivers.
items.ex_zh: 立法机构果断投票，宣布在河流附近倾倒危险化学品为非法。

items.def_zh: 正式下令禁止；截击禁运
items.def_en: To authoritatively or militarily forbid or intercept trade, movement, or prohibited activities
items.ex_en: Naval forces moved decisively to interdict illicit arms shipments at sea.
items.ex_zh: 海军部队果断出击，在海上截击非法武器运输船只。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses formal enactments of legal or institutional barriers that forbid certain actions, goods, or rights altogether, ranging from mild disallowance to statutory criminalization.
groups.summary_zh: 通过法规、条令或官方权威彻底取缔或全面禁止某种行为或事物。
groups.desc_en: Using institutional, statutory, or parental authority to forbid an action, object, or trade from occurring, contrasting with granting permission or tacit deregulation.
groups.desc_zh: 依托制度、法律或家长权威发布禁令，彻底剥夺某项行为或交易的许可，与给予授权或放任默许相对立。
groups.nuance_en: ban: imposing a high-profile, total official prohibition on a practice or good (smoking / weapons / exports) · prohibit: strictly, formally disallowing by codified regulation or statute (entry / sale / discrimination) · forbid: personal or imperative prohibition issued by authority or religion (child / marriage / entry) · outlaw: declaring a practice or entity illegal and stripping legal protection (organization / weapon / practice) · bar: physically or procedurally blocking an individual or group from entry or participation (entry / lawyer / candidate) · interdict: military or juridical interception and prohibition of contraband or transit (arms / drugs / shipping)
groups.nuance_zh: ban: 社会性全面封禁某种行径或物品 (smoking / weapons / exports) · prohibit: 依明文规章法律予以严禁 (entry / sale / discrimination) · forbid: 家长、权威或戒律直接发令禁止 (child / marriage / entry) · outlaw: 定性为违法并剥夺合法存续地位 (organization / weapon / practice) · bar: 在门槛上把关拒之门外 (entry / lawyer / candidate) · interdict: 军事或司法层面的截断拦截与禁运 (arms / drugs / shipping)

groups.name: Bargain & Haggle · 讨价还价与磋商 (Bargain, Dicker, Chaffer)
groups.tip: 商讨交易价格并互不相让

items.def_en: To persuade a seller to reduce the price of an item
items.ex_en: The old factory was knocked down to make way for a modern shopping center.
items.ex_zh: 旧工厂被拆除，为一座现代化的购物中心腾出了空间。

items.def_en: To compel a seller to accept a substantially lower price
items.ex_en: He managed to beat down the antique merchant by twenty dollars.
items.ex_zh: 他设法把古董商人的开价狠压了二十美元。

items.def_en: To bargain or haggle back and forth in an argumentative or protracted way
items.ex_en: Old traders gathered along dusty lanes to chaffer over handmade rugs.
items.ex_zh: 老商贩们聚集在尘土飞扬的小巷里，漫天还盘争论手工地毯的价钱。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) To negotiate the terms and conditions of a transaction or agreement
items.ex_en: Union leaders met with management yesterday to bargain over employee wages.
items.ex_zh: 工会领袖昨天与管理层会面，就员工薪资展开谈判。

items.def_en: To argue back and forth, especially about the price of something or the terms of an agreement, in order to get a better deal.
items.ex_en: Tourists love to haggle with street vendors over souvenir ceramic plates.
items.ex_zh: 游客们喜欢就纪念品瓷盘的价钱同街头摊贩讨价还价。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) To engage in petty bargaining or dispute over minor terms
items.ex_en: They wasted entire afternoons trying to dicker over trivial contract details.
items.ex_zh: 他们浪费了整整几个下午，试图就微不足道的合同细节反复扯皮。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe informal or contentious discussions over prices, terms, or conditions, typically involving back-and-forth concessions.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及在买卖或协议中反复交涉以压低价格或争取有利条件的动作。
groups.desc_en: Involves transactional dispute and reciprocal compromise over price or terms, contrasting with unilateral pricing or formal, detached negotiation.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及在交易中就价格或条款反复推拉磋商与互作妥协，区别于单方面统一定价或正规脱离市井气的书面谈判。
groups.nuance_en: bargain: standard negotiation of mutually acceptable terms (price / contract / deal) · haggle: petty, persistent disputing over small amounts (price / souvenir / flea market) · dicker: informal, indecisive bartering or wrangling (terms / trade / price) · chaffer: traditional or marketplace bickering (wares / goods / price) · beat down: aggressively force a seller to lower terms (price / seller / quote) · knock down: persuade to reduce a cost, or strike off an auction lot (price / estimate / hammer)
groups.nuance_zh: bargain: 就条件或价格进行常规磋商谈判 (price / contract / deal) · haggle: 为小利或细节喋喋不休地杀价讨价 (price / souvenir / flea market) · dicker: 口语中磨磨蹭蹭的折冲与反复商讨 (terms / trade / price) · chaffer: 传统集市中喧嚣拉锯的叫卖砍价 (wares / goods / price) · beat down: 强力迫使对方压低价格 (price / seller / quote) · knock down: 成功砍掉价格，或拍卖落槌成交 (price / estimate / hammer)

groups.name: Beat It & Clear Out · 溜走与拔腿开溜 (Vamoose, Scram, Skedaddle)
groups.tip: 快速离去、溜走或撤离特定场景

items.def_en: to depart immediately, most often used as an imperative to get lost
items.ex_en: The annoyed security guard yelled at the noisy teenagers to beat it.
items.ex_zh: 恼怒的保安大声呵斥吵闹的青少年赶紧滚蛋。

items.def_en: to go away immediately, usually spoken angrily to disperse unwanted bystanders
items.ex_en: The angry groundskeeper shouted at the trespassers to clear off immediately.
items.ex_zh: 愤怒的场地管理员大声呵斥入侵者立刻滚开。

items.def_en: to leave in a rush, especially in order to escape chase or punishment
items.ex_en: The burglar made off as soon as the burglar alarm went off.
items.ex_zh: 防盗警报一响，窃贼就仓皇逃窜了。

items.def_en: to run away or retreat hurriedly and spontaneously
items.ex_en: The startled rabbits decided to skedaddle as soon as we approached.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的兔子一看到我们靠近就赶紧溜走了。

items.def_en: to leave a place immediately and quickly, frequently used as a blunt command
items.ex_en: The grumpy shopkeeper ordered the unruly kids to scram right now.
items.ex_zh: 脾气暴躁的店主命令那些不守规矩的孩子立刻滚蛋。

items.def_en: (informal) to depart or run away quickly
items.ex_en: As soon as the siren sounded, the street gamblers decided to vamoose.
items.ex_zh: 警报一响，街头赌徒们便立刻溜之大吉。

groups.summary_en: This informal and slang-rich motion frame describes leaving a place with extreme haste, abruptness, or evasiveness—often when ordered to disperse or when escaping detection. Verbs carry punchy, colloquial energy.
groups.summary_zh: 指匆忙、突然或逃避性地离开某地；多用于口语开溜或轰赶。
groups.desc_en: Denotes an abrupt, urgent, or secretive departure from a scene to escape notice, confrontation, or duty, unlike neutral leaving or orderly retreats.
groups.desc_zh: 指为躲避注意、冲突或职责而突然、匆忙或慌不择路地离开现场，区别于中性的离去或有秩序的撤退。
groups.nuance_en: beat it: blunt, slangy imperative or sudden flight (imperative / scene / police) · scram: urgent hasty departure to avoid trouble (scene / intruder / police) · vamoose: colloquial, swift vanishing from a location (kid / thief / troublemaker) · skedaddle: humorous, scrambled running away in panic (crowd / children / soldiers) · make off: stealthy escape, often with stolen goods (loot / money / thief) · clear off: abrupt departure under orders or brusque dispersal (loiterer / trespasser / street)
groups.nuance_zh: beat it: 粗鲁生硬地喝令滚蛋或拔腿就跑 (imperative / scene / police) · scram: 唯恐惹祸上身而急速开溜 (scene / intruder / police) · vamoose: 俚语中俏皮或迅速地溜之大吉 (kid / thief / troublemaker) · skedaddle: 略带诙谐的抱头鼠窜或落荒而逃 (crowd / children / soldiers) · make off: 携赃或暗中悄然逃离现场 (loot / money / thief) · clear off: 遭驱赶时悻悻离去或勒令走开 (loiterer / trespasser / street)

groups.name: Beget & Engender · 生育与滋生创造 (Beget, Engender, Sire)
groups.tip: 血脉延续，繁衍生息后代

items.def_en: To physically deliver offspring, or metaphorically produce a groundbreaking idea or movement
items.ex_en: The underground cultural renaissance helped give birth to modern punk music.
items.ex_zh: 这场地下文化复兴运动催生了现代朋克音乐。

items.def_en: To produce or cause something new, prolific, or numerous to develop rapidly
items.ex_en: The runaway success of the mobile game will spawn countless imitators.
items.ex_zh: 这款手机游戏的巨大成功势必会催生无数模仿者。

items.def_en: To become the male parent of an animal or child
items.ex_en: The prized stallion was chosen by the royal stable to sire champions.
items.ex_zh: 皇家马厩选拔了这匹名贵种马去繁育冠军后代。

items.def_en: To cause, produce, or bring about a feeling, situation, or condition
items.ex_en: Unclear government guidelines only served to engender deep public confusion and distrust.
items.ex_zh: 含糊不清的政府指导方针只会滋生公众深深的困惑与不信任。

items.def_zh: 生育，繁衍；引起，导致（beget的过去分词）
items.def_en: (archaic or formal) Past participle of beget: to father children; to bring into existence or cause.
items.ex_en: Hatred and continuous deception have only begotten profound misery for generations.
items.ex_zh: 仇恨和持续的欺骗只会给世世代代造成深重的苦难。

items.def_en: To produce young or reproduce sexually through biological procreation
items.ex_en: Most migratory bird species return annually to their native habitats to procreate.
items.ex_zh: 大多数候鸟每年都会返回故土栖息地进行繁衍生殖。

groups.summary_en: Encompasses generative acts bringing new life or abstract conditions into existence, ranging from paternal lineage and biological procreation to giving rise to complex systemic consequences.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖生物繁衍孕育生命，以及催生出抽象事件或后果的过程。
groups.desc_en: Signifies initiating biological lineage or giving foundational rise to abstract consequences, contrasting with general creation or mechanical manufacturing.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过生物繁衍确立血统或在抽象层面上成为事物的直接源头根基，区别于一般的人工制造或机械产出。
groups.nuance_en: beget: archaic paternal siring, or inexorably generating outcomes (violence / child / distrust) · sire: act as the biological male progenitor, esp. livestock (colt / champion / offspring) · engender: give birth to abstract conditions or emotions (mistrust / controversy / debate) · spawn: produce prolifically or generate unwanted offshoots (clones / movement / offspring) · procreate: formal biological reproduction of the species (offspring / human / species) · give birth to: literal maternal delivery, or metaphorically originating an era (child / movement / idea)
groups.nuance_zh: beget: 带有古旧与经卷色彩的父系繁衍，或必然引致后患 (violence / child / distrust) · sire: （尤指牲畜）作为父本配种传宗 (colt / champion / offspring) · engender: 滋生或催生某种抽象的社会情绪与后果 (mistrust / controversy / debate) · spawn: 大量产卵，或贬义滋生不良产物与派系 (clones / movement / offspring) · procreate: 正式的种族生物繁衍行为 (offspring / human / species) · give birth to: 母亲分娩，或比喻孕育出崭新时代与思想 (child / movement / idea)

groups.name: Believe & Trust · 相信与信任 (Believe, Trust, Buy into)
groups.tip: 从主观相信到托付信任

items.def_en: 1. To accept something as true, genuine, or real. 2. (+ in) To have trust or confidence in someone or something.
items.ex_en: Many honest citizens still believe that true justice will prevail eventually.
items.ex_zh: 许多正直的公民仍然相信真正的正义终将取得胜利。

items.def_en: To accept something as true or plausible despite initial doubt
items.ex_en: Nobody was willing to credit his bizarre explanation for being absent.
items.ex_zh: 没有人愿意相信他那套离奇的缺席解释。

items.def_zh: 轻信，盲目接受（谎言或借口）
items.def_en: To accept an improbable story, claim, or excuse without questioning it
items.ex_en: The naive tourists tended to swallow every wild claim made by the fraudulent guide.
items.ex_zh: 天真的游客们往往会盲目轻信那个骗子导游编造的荒唐说法。

items.def_en: To completely believe in or accept an idea, explanation, or philosophy, sometimes uncritically
items.ex_en: I simply refuse to buy into his bizarre conspiracy theories about the secret society.
items.ex_zh: 我绝不买账他那些关于秘密社团的古怪阴谋论。

items.def_en: To believe that someone is honest, dependable, or sincere and will not harm you
items.ex_en: She could not trust anyone who repeatedly broke promises without showing any sincere remorse.
items.ex_zh: 她无法信任任何屡次违背诺言却毫无悔意的人。

items.def_en: (+ in) To trust someone completely by sharing secret or intimate feelings and thoughts
items.ex_en: He chose to confide in his mentor regarding his deep ethical concerns about the project.
items.ex_zh: 关于他对该项目的深层伦理担忧，他选择向导师倾诉。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express epistemic commitment, accepting propositions as true, or placing personal reliance in someone's integrity. Differences span from intellectual assent to uncritical acceptance and deep faith.
groups.summary_zh: 表示认知上的确信、信任或轻信，涵盖从理性认同到全盘接纳。
groups.desc_en: Denotes accepting propositions as true or placing psychological reliance in persons or ideas, unlike factual knowing or verified certainty.
groups.desc_zh: 指在认知上接纳某一命题为真，或在心理上对人与理念寄予托付依赖，区别于经实证的确定性知晓。
groups.nuance_en: believe: accept factual truth or maintain conviction (story / theory / promise) · trust: place reliance on integrity, reliability, or safety (friend / institution / instincts) · credit: formally or provisionally attach belief to a claim (account / rumor / explanation) · swallow: gullibly accept an improbable claim without scrutiny (lie / myth / story) · buy into: invest belief and commitment in an ideology or concept (narrative / vision / culture) · confide: impart private secrets relying on another's discretion (secret / trust / fear)
groups.nuance_zh: believe: 认定事实为真或持有信念 (story / theory / promise) · trust: 托付信任，信赖对方的操守或可靠性 (friend / institution / instincts) · credit: 予以置信，对某说法给予初步采信 (account / rumor / explanation) · swallow: 不假思索地轻信谎言或全盘吞下 (lie / myth / story) · buy into: 认同并买账某套说辞或理念 (narrative / vision / culture) · confide: 出于信任倾吐私密心声 (secret / trust / fear)

groups.name: Bestow & Endow · 赠予与赋予 (Confer, Bestow, Grant)
groups.tip: 正式或慷慨地赋予资源

items.def_en: To officially give or allow someone something that they have asked for or deserve, such as permission, rights, or funds
items.ex_en: The municipal authority refused to grant permission for the commercial development near the nature reserve.
items.ex_zh: 市政当局拒绝准予在自然保护区附近进行商业开发的许可。

items.def_en: To endow or present someone with a desirable attribute, talent, or material gift
items.ex_en: Nature seemed to gift the young violinist with extraordinary technical precision and innate emotional depth.
items.ex_zh: 上天似乎赋予了这位年轻小提琴手非凡的精准技巧与天生的情感深度。

items.def_en: (+ in/with) To confer legal power, authority, or rights officially upon someone
items.ex_en: The constitutional amendment will vest complete executive authority in the newly established commission.
items.ex_zh: 该宪法修正案将把完整的行政权力正式赋予新设立的委员会。

items.def_zh: 赋予，天生具有；资助，向……捐赠
items.def_en: 1. ('be endowed with') To naturally possess a good quality, talent, or feature. 2. To give a large sum of money to establish or provide an ongoing income for a school, hospital, or organization.
items.ex_en: She was fortunate to be endowed with rare musical talent and incredible perseverance.
items.ex_zh: 她十分幸运，天生具备罕见的音乐才华与惊人的毅力。

items.def_en: (+ upon/on) To officially grant an honor, degree, title, or right to someone
items.ex_en: The university senate voted to confer an honorary doctorate on the celebrated human rights advocate.
items.ex_zh: 大学评议会投票决定授予那位著名的民权倡导者荣誉博士学位。

items.def_en: (+ upon/on) To present an honor, right, or gift to someone, emphasizing generosity or dignity
items.ex_en: The sovereign chose to bestow the highest order of chivalry on the retired general.
items.ex_zh: 君主决定将最高级别的骑士勋章赐予那位退役将军。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the formal, gracious, or providential transfer of intangible gifts, honors, privileges, or natural abilities, typically from a superior authority or nature itself to a recipient.
groups.summary_zh: 上位者、机构或大自然庄重赋予、赐予或授给某人荣誉、权利与天赋。
groups.desc_en: Involves an asymmetric transfer of authority, honor, privilege, or natural talent from a higher power or benefactor, contrasting with commercial selling or casual gifting.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及上位者、赐予者或自然法则对权威、荣耀、特权或资质的单向赋予，区别于对等商业交易或随意的赠送礼物。
groups.nuance_en: bestow: present formally or graciously as an honor (award / blessing / favor) · confer: grant an honor, degree, or consultative authority officially (title / degree / legitimacy) · endow: equip with a permanent fund, property, or natural talent (institution / talent / beauty) · grant: officially concede or permit a legal right or request (permission / visa / pardon) · vest: legally settle absolute authority or property rights into a holder (power / authority / control) · gift: present voluntarily, often legally or informally without consideration (shares / property / house)
groups.nuance_zh: bestow: 郑重或施恩般赐予荣誉、福泽 (award / blessing / favor) · confer: 官方或机构正式授予学衔、头衔或特权 (title / degree / legitimacy) · endow: 为机构捐赠基金，或天生赋予非凡资质 (institution / talent / beauty) · grant: 官方核准、准予法定权利或诉求 (permission / visa / pardon) · vest: 依法将权力或产权完全归属于某主体 (power / authority / control) · gift: 无偿赠与或在法律意义上过户财产 (shares / property / house)

groups.name: Bid & Tender · 出价与投标 (Bid, Tender, Quote)
groups.tip: 拍卖或竞标中提议价格

items.def_en: To state the exact price at which one is willing to provide a product or service
items.ex_en: The contractor agreed to quote an exact price for the complete renovation of the basement.
items.ex_zh: 承包商同意就地下室的彻底翻新工程给出一个确切的报价。

items.def_zh: 出价，喊价；投标，竞标；努力争取
items.def_en: 1. To offer a particular price for something, especially at an auction or for a commercial contract. 2. (bid for/to do) To make an effort or attempt to achieve something.
items.ex_en: Ambitious suitors gathered at dawn to bid for the ancestral lands of the fallen duke.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的买家们黎明时分聚集在一起，竞标竞购那位落魄公爵的祖传领地。

items.def_en: (+ a bid/tender) To submit an official commercial proposal or bid for consideration
items.ex_en: Three rival engineering firms decided to put in a bid for the bridge construction project.
items.ex_zh: 三家互为竞争对手的工程公司决定为该桥梁建设项目递交标书。

items.def_en: To make a formal written offer to supply goods or execute work at a specified rate
items.ex_en: The consortium decided to tender for the supply of clean water to the remote district.
items.ex_zh: 该财团决定正式投标向偏远地区供应清洁饮用水的项目。

items.def_en: To submit an offer higher than another buyer in an auction or competitive sale
items.ex_en: A private collector managed to outbid all rivals during the high-stakes contemporary art auction.
items.ex_zh: 在竞争激烈的当代艺术品拍卖会上，一位私人收藏家出价高于所有对手。

items.def_en: To submit a lower estimate or bid than a rival contractor in order to win business
items.ex_en: The rival builder managed to underbid our proposal by cutting crucial labor costs drastically.
items.ex_zh: 竞争对手建筑商通过大幅削减关键人工成本，报出了比我们更低的中标价。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures commercial interactions where parties submit formal, competitive price proposals or procurement offers to secure contracts, acquisitions, or auction lots. The communication is generally binding, structured, and comparative.
groups.summary_zh: 在拍卖、竞标或商业洽谈中正式提交报价或供标方案。
groups.desc_en: Signifies proposing formal commercial terms, costs, or commitments in a competitive market environment, unlike informal price estimation or retail shopping.
groups.desc_zh: 指在竞争性市场或招投标流程中正式提交报价、发包或承揽意愿，区别于非正式估价或普通零售选购。
groups.nuance_en: bid: offer a specific price competitively at auction or contract (project / auction / takeover) · tender: formally submit a structured offer or payment for a procurement (contract / resignation / bid) · quote: state an estimated price for potential services (fee / estimate / rate) · outbid: offer a higher price than a rival to secure a prize (rival / competitor / collector) · underbid: offer a lower price than a competitor or underestimate costs (rival / contract / project) · put in: informally lodge or submit an offer or claim (bid / claim / application)
groups.nuance_zh: bid: 在竞标或拍卖中正式报出竞争性价格 (project / auction / takeover) · tender: 依规范流程递交投标书或正式提交辞呈/款项 (contract / resignation / bid) · quote: 营业方针对特定服务开出估算报价 (fee / estimate / rate) · outbid: 出价高于竞争对手以夺得标的物 (rival / competitor / collector) · underbid: 出价低于对手，或低估预算竞价 (rival / contract / project) · put in: 口语中提交报价、申请或索赔 (bid / claim / application)

groups.name: Bleach & Whiten · 漂白与褪色 (Whiten, Decolor, Fade)
groups.tip: 化学漂白剥离表面色泽

items.def_en: To lose brightness, color, or vibrancy gradually, especially over time or from exposure to light
items.ex_en: Bright summer curtains will slowly fade if exposed to relentless afternoon sunlight for months.
items.ex_zh: 明亮的夏日窗帘若连续数月暴露在强烈的午后阳光下，便会慢慢褪色。
items.ex2_en: Harsh detergent fades bright cotton fabrics after just a few hot washes.
items.ex2_zh: 强效洗衣剂只需几次热水清洗就会使鲜艳的棉质衣物褪色。

items.def_en: To remove the natural or artificial color from a chemical compound, liquid, or fabric
items.ex_en: The alchemist attempted to decolorize the dark tincture using fine charcoal powder and heat.
items.ex_zh: 炼金术士试图用活性炭粉末和加热法使那深色的药剂脱色。

items.def_en: 1. To make cloth, hair, or paper white or much lighter using chemicals or sunlight.
items.ex_en: She used concentrated lemon juice and bright sunshine to bleach the stained linen tablecloths.
items.ex_zh: 她利用浓缩柠檬汁和明媚的阳光来漂白那些染有污渍的亚麻桌布。
items.ex2_en: The wooden deck bleached rapidly under the unrelenting desert sun each summer.
items.ex2_zh: 每年夏天，木甲板在无情的沙漠烈日照晒下迅速泛白。

items.def_en: To make hair, fabric, or skin lighter or paler in tone
items.ex_en: A small amount of peroxide will gradually lighten your hair over several gentle applications.
items.ex_zh: 少量的双氧水经过几次温和使用后，会逐渐使你的发色变浅。
items.ex2_en: Her dark hair lightened noticeably after spending long sunny afternoons outdoors.
items.ex2_zh: 在户外度过漫长阳光明媚的午后，她乌黑的头发明显变浅了。

items.def_en: To make something white or lighter in color, or to become white
items.ex_en: Regular use of this specialized abrasive paste helps whiten coffee stains on enamel surfaces.
items.ex_zh: 定期使用这种专用研磨膏有助于使牙釉质表面的咖啡污渍变白。
items.ex2_en: Ancient limestone cliffs whiten spectacularly whenever harsh winter frost coats their surfaces.
items.ex2_zh: 每当严冬白霜覆盖其表层，古老的石灰岩悬崖就显得格外雪白。

items.def_zh: 使发白；（因惊吓等）褪去血色
items.def_en: To strip of color, or to become pale, through shock, fear, or chemical/culinary treatment
items.ex_en: Sudden mortal terror caused the young sentry's weathered face to blanch beneath the moonlight.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的致命恐惧令年轻哨兵那饱经风霜的脸庞在月光下褪尽血色。
items.ex2_en: The sudden horrifying news blanched her face with sheer disbelief and panic.
items.ex2_zh: 突如其来的可怕消息吓得她脸色煞白，满是难以置信与惊恐。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers processes where color is drained, chemically extracted, or naturally stripped away by sunlight and exposure, transforming surfaces into white, pale, or faded tones.
groups.summary_zh: 指经化学处理、日晒或氧化导致颜色褪去、泛白或变浅。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the chemical, solar, or biological reduction of color and vividness toward whiteness or paleness, unlike intentional color transformation through dye or paint.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过化学作用、光照或生理反应使颜色与光泽减退、趋向苍白或褪色，区别于使用颜料的主动着色涂覆。
groups.nuance_en: bleach: whiten drastically via chemical agents or harsh sun (fabric / hair / coral) · whiten: make or become brighter and lighter in tone (teeth / smile / sheets) · fade: gradually lose color, vibrancy, or distinctness over time (sun / jeans / memory) · decolorize: artificially strip pigment through chemical treatment (solution / oil / substance) · blanch: lose color suddenly through shock, or scald food to pale it (face / fear / almonds) · lighten: reduce darkness or heavy saturation generally (skin / shade / hair)
