groups.desc_en: Demonstrating exact structural, quantitative, or semantic congruence between two sets of data or realities, contrasting with mere approximation or variance.
groups.desc_zh: 两套数据、事实或陈述在结构、数量或意义上表现出严密一致，与粗略相近或出现分歧相对。
groups.nuance_en: tally: compute to an identical score or matched numerical records (votes / figures / accounts) · correspond: show a parallel or equivalent relationship across systems (letters / descriptions / categories) · square: reconcile harmoniously with principles or existing evidence (facts / claims / conscience) · align: bring into directional or philosophical uniformity (interests / strategies / values) · check out: confirm as genuine or accurate upon verification (story / alibi / credentials) · coincide: occur at the identical point in time, space, or opinion (interests / views / dates)
groups.nuance_zh: tally: 数据与记录吻合相符 (votes / figures / accounts) · correspond: 对应一致或语义相符 (letters / descriptions / categories) · square: 与既有事实或原则合拍无矛盾 (facts / claims / conscience) · align: 利益、取向或立场对齐一致 (interests / strategies / values) · check out: 经核查属实无讹 (story / alibi / credentials) · coincide: 时间、意见等巧合或重叠一致 (interests / views / dates)

groups.name: Measure & Estimate · 估算与计量 (Gauge, Appraise, Assess)
groups.tip: 估量价值与规模大小

items.def_en: To form a judgment or calculation about the approximate value, size, or cost of something.
items.ex_en: Contractors estimate that repairing the historic stone bridge will take nearly five months.
items.ex_zh: 承包商估计修复这座历史悠久的石桥大约需要五个月时间。

items.def_en: To calculate or judge the nature, value, price, or significance of an asset or problem
items.ex_en: Certified evaluators visited the estate to assess the taxable value of the private art collection.
items.ex_zh: 认证评估师拜访了该庄园，以评定这批私人艺术藏品的应税价值。

items.def_en: To make a reasoned judgment or measurement about a quantity, situation, or person's mood
items.ex_en: The experienced captain looked up at the darkening sky to gauge the impending storm.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的船长抬头凝视着暗下来的天空，以估量即将来临的风暴。

items.def_en: To calculate or state an amount or value that is nearly but not completely exact
items.ex_en: Scientists approximate the age of these fossil remains at roughly three million years.
items.ex_zh: 科学家估算这些化石遗骸的年代大约距今三百万年。

items.def_en: To estimate an amount, size, or distance visually without using instruments
items.ex_en: The veteran carpenter could eyeball the timber dimensions without using a tape measure.
items.ex_zh: 那位经验丰富的老木匠不用卷尺也能凭眼力目测出木材的尺寸。

items.def_en: To examine someone or something to evaluate their value, quality, or condition formally
items.ex_en: Independent insurance experts arrived promptly to appraise the storm damage on the commercial building.
items.ex_zh: 独立的保险专家迅速赶到现场，对商业大楼遭受的风暴损失进行正式评估。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses mental or instrumental computations used to determine the magnitude, value, duration, or likelihood of something without precise definitive calculation.
groups.summary_zh: 通过经验、感官或初步数据对数量、价值或规模进行预估与测算。
groups.desc_en: Forming an approximate, qualitative, or analytical judgment of value, size, or impact in the absence of exact instruments, contrasting with strict scientific calibration.
groups.desc_zh: 在缺乏精确仪器的情况下，对数值、规模或价值进行定性或粗略的专业判断，与严格物理校准相对。
groups.nuance_en: estimate: project a calculated approximation of cost or quantity (costs / losses / population) · assess: evaluate the nature, condition, and risk of a situation analytically (impact / damage / performance) · gauge: read clues or reactions to determine magnitude or intent (mood / reaction / distance) · appraise: determine monetary worth or official quality (property / talent / assets) · approximate: come close to an exact figure or reality without precision (figure / number / trajectory) · eyeball: estimate casually by unassisted sight (measurements / distance / proportions)
groups.nuance_zh: estimate: 估算费用、数据或数量 (costs / losses / population) · assess: 系统评估损益、风险或状况 (impact / damage / performance) · gauge: 观察蛛丝马迹以揣摩测量 (mood / reaction / distance) · appraise: 官方或专业估价鉴定 (property / talent / assets) · approximate: 粗略估算或无限接近 (figure / number / trajectory) · eyeball: 凭肉眼目测估计 (measurements / distance / proportions)

groups.name: Mediate & Intercede · 调解与求情 (Intervene, Arbitrate, Plead)
groups.tip: 从中斡旋化解双方矛盾争端

items.def_en: To become involved in a conflict or difficult situation to help resolve it or prevent problems.
items.ex_en: The government had to step in to prevent the bank from collapsing.
items.ex_zh: 政府不得不出手干预，以防止该银行倒闭。

items.def_en: (+ with/for) To make an urgent, emotional, and humble request on behalf of someone.
items.ex_en: Desperate villagers went directly to the magistrate to plead for lower grain taxes.
items.ex_zh: 走投无路的村民们直接面见地方官，为降低粮食税而苦苦恳求。

items.def_en: To intentionally become involved in a difficult situation in order to improve it or prevent it from worsening.
items.ex_en: The security team had to intervene before the heated dispute became physically violent.
items.ex_zh: 在激烈的争吵升级为肢体暴力前，安保团队不得不出面干预。

items.def_en: To try to end a disagreement between two or more people or groups by acting as a neutral go-between.
items.ex_en: A seasoned diplomat was assigned to mediate the long-standing maritime boundary dispute peacefully.
items.ex_zh: 一名经验丰富的外交官被指派从中斡旋，以和平调解长期的海上边界争端。

items.def_en: To speak to someone in authority on behalf of another person to settle a dispute or ask for mercy.
items.ex_en: The community priest agreed to intercede with the harsh judge on the boy's behalf.
items.ex_zh: 社区神父同意代表这个男孩向严苛的法官求情斡旋。

items.def_en: To officially judge and settle a dispute between two opposing parties after hearing both sides.
items.ex_en: A retired judge was officially appointed to arbitrate the bitter intellectual property dispute.
items.ex_zh: 一位退休法官被正式任命为仲裁员，公断这起激烈的知识产权纠纷。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe stepping into a conflict or crisis on behalf of another party or to reconcile opposing sides. While 'intercede' emphasizes pleading for mercy or favor, verbs like 'mediate' and 'arbitrate' focus on neutral dispute resolution, and 'intervene' denotes decisive involvement.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及介入纠纷调解或代人求情，强调居中撮合或施加影响。
groups.desc_en: Inserting oneself between conflicting parties to reconcile differences, facilitate resolution, or plead on behalf of another, contrasting with partisan fighting or neutral detachment.
groups.desc_zh: 介入冲突双方之间以调解矛盾、促成和解或代为求情，与卷入派系搏斗或漠然置之相对。
groups.nuance_en: mediate: act as an impartial facilitator to help parties reach agreement (dispute / peace / talks) · arbitrate: act with formal authority to deliver a binding resolution (claim / dispute / grievance) · intercede: plead or intervene affectionately on someone else's behalf (on behalf of / with authority) · intervene: enter an evolving crisis to alter its course or halt escalation (crisis / conflict / market) · step in: take initiative to help or resolve when existing efforts stall (negotiations / breach / dispute) · plead: make an emotional, urgent appeal (case / cause / leniency)
groups.nuance_zh: mediate: 作为中立第三方促成和解 (dispute / peace / talks) · arbitrate: 行使权威或仲裁权裁定 (claim / dispute / grievance) · intercede: 为他人代为求情或说项 (on behalf of / with authority) · intervene: 介入事态以扭转走向 (crisis / conflict / market) · step in: 主动介入顶上或化解僵局 (negotiations / breach / dispute) · plead: 恳切央求或抗辩 (case / cause / leniency)

groups.name: Meet & Encounter · 遭遇与邂逅 (Encounter, Run into, Come up against)
groups.tip: 偶遇或正面交锋遭遇

items.def_en: To encounter someone unexpectedly when going about your day
items.ex_en: I did not expect to bump into my high school tutor at the grocery.
items.ex_zh: 我真没想到会在杂货店意外撞见我高中的家教老师。

items.def_en: To discover or meet someone or something purely by chance
items.ex_en: Researchers rarely come across such intact archaeological specimens in this remote mountainous region.
items.ex_zh: 研究人员在这一偏远山区很少能偶然碰到如此保存完好的考古标本。

items.def_zh: 偶然碰见，邂逅；遭遇（困难）
items.def_en: To meet someone by chance, or experience unexpected difficulties
items.ex_en: I did not expect to run into my former college roommate at the airport terminal.
items.ex_zh: 我真没想到会在机场航站楼偶然碰见我大学时的室友。

items.def_en: 1. To experience or come up against something difficult, unpleasant, or dangerous. 2. To meet someone unexpectedly.
items.ex_en: Expedition members encounter severe blizzards whenever they ascend above the high mountain pass.
items.ex_zh: 探险队员每当攀登至高山隘口之上时，总会遭遇狂暴的风雪。

items.def_zh: 遭遇，面对（严重阻碍或反对）
items.def_en: To be faced with serious opposition, an adversary, or a formidable obstacle
items.ex_en: The aggressive reform bill will come up against severe opposition from traditional trade unions.
items.ex_zh: 这项激进的改革法案必将面临来自传统工会的强烈反对。

items.def_en: To face an unpleasant or challenging situation, fact, or person directly
items.ex_en: Corporate managers must directly confront the uncomfortable realities of their declining market share.
items.ex_zh: 企业管理者必须直面他们市场份额不断下滑这一令人难堪的现实。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on coming into contact with individuals or adverse situations, predominantly unexpectedly or without prior design. Key contrasts distinguish stumbling upon an old acquaintance from facing formidable obstacles or enemies.
groups.summary_zh: 指偶然邂逅某人，或在行进与办事中迎面遭遇困难、阻碍与对抗。
groups.desc_en: Coming face-to-face with a person, difficulty, or obstacle without prior arrangement or control, contrasting with planned appointments or voluntary visits.
groups.desc_zh: 未经预先安排而意外与人、困难或障碍迎面相撞，与预约会面或主动探访相对。
groups.nuance_en: encounter: unexpectedly meet someone or experience an unfamiliar obstacle (resistance / stranger / problems) · run into: casually and by chance meet a familiar person, or collide with trouble (friend / trouble / snag) · bump into: lighthearted accidental personal run-in (acquaintance / colleague / neighbor) · come across: find or chance upon something or someone while seeking or browsing (evidence / article / relics) · come up against: run headlong into severe institutional or circumstantial resistance (opposition / barrier / wall) · confront: meet a challenger or hostile reality face-to-face (enemy / problem / crisis)
groups.nuance_zh: encounter: 意外遭遇障碍或偶遇陌生人 (resistance / stranger / problems) · run into: 偶然撞见熟人或遭遇阻碍 (friend / trouble / snag) · bump into: 轻松偶然地邂逅或碰到熟人 (acquaintance / colleague / neighbor) · come across: 无意中翻出、发现或结识 (evidence / article / relics) · come up against: 迎面撞上强硬阻力或体制高墙 (opposition / barrier / wall) · confront: 正面对峙或勇敢面对挑战 (enemy / problem / crisis)

groups.name: Mellow & Soften · 缓和与熟化 (Soften, Subdue, Season)
groups.tip: 褪去青涩尖锐，变得温和醇厚

items.def_en: To mature or make someone or something experienced and fit over an extended period
items.ex_en: Years of competitive matches will gradually season the young rookie into a resilient leader.
items.ex_zh: 多年的竞技比赛磨炼终将使这位年轻的新人成长为一名坚韧的领袖。

items.def_en: To become or make less severe, harsh, or rigid in attitude, tone, or appearance
items.ex_en: Hearing the child's sincere apology helped soften the teacher's unusually stern expression.
items.ex_zh: 听到孩子真诚的道歉，老师那异常严厉的神情渐渐缓和了下来。
items.ex2_en: Her hardened facial features softened noticeably when she finally saw her smiling child.
items.ex2_zh: 当她终于看到微笑的孩子时，她紧绷的面容明显柔和了下来。

items.def_en: 1. To become softer, richer, or calmer with age or experience.
items.ex_en: This robust red wine will slowly mellow into a silky vintage after several years.
items.ex_zh: 这款浓郁的红葡萄酒在窖藏数年后，口感会慢慢变得醇和顺滑。
items.ex2_en: Decades of quiet countryside living mellowed the retired general's once fiery temper.
items.ex2_zh: 数十年平静的乡村生活使这位退役将军曾经火爆的脾气变得温和。

items.def_en: To develop fully and acquire a richer, more rounded quality or flavor over time
items.ex_en: These green orchard pears will ripen nicely if left on the kitchen counter.
items.ex_zh: 如果放在厨房台面上，这些果园采摘的青梨会很好地成熟变甜。
items.ex2_en: Warm summer sunshine and frequent rains ripen the sweet grapes across the valley.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖的夏日阳光和频繁的降雨让整个山谷中甘甜的葡萄熟透了。

items.def_en: To make something less extreme or harsh, usually by balancing it with another quality
items.ex_en: The wise judge sought to temper strict justice with genuine compassion for the offender.
items.ex_zh: 明智的法官试图用对罪犯的由衷仁慈来缓和严苛的正义。

items.def_en: To soften the tone, light, or intensity of something, making it calmer and less striking
items.ex_en: The interior designer used heavy linen curtains to subdue the blinding midday desert sunlight.
items.ex_zh: 室内设计师选用厚实的亚麻窗帘，使正午耀眼的沙漠阳光变得柔和。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe individuals, substances, or flavors losing their harshness, sharpness, or aggression over time, becoming gentle, rich, and balanced through maturation or experience.
groups.summary_zh: 描绘性情、风味或事物随岁月历练褪去锋芒、趋于温和醇厚的熟化过程。
groups.desc_en: Alleviating harshness, sharpness, or intensity over time to achieve a balanced, palatable, or cooperative state, contrasting with abrupt cessation or intensification.
groups.desc_zh: 随时间推移缓和严苛、锋芒或烈度以达到圆融温和的状态，与骤然停止或剧烈升级相对。
groups.nuance_en: mellow: soften harshness or edge through maturity and passage of time (flavor / personality / wine) · temper: moderate an extreme impulse with a balancing counterweight (justice / enthusiasm / metal) · soften: reduce physical hardness or rhetorical impact (blow / stance / tone) · ripen: mature naturally to optimal fullness and flavor (fruit / conditions / talent) · subdue: tone down vividness or bring an unruly force under calm control (emotions / colors / opposition) · season: condition and stabilize through exposure to environment and use (timber / cast iron / players)
groups.nuance_zh: mellow: 因岁月沉淀而褪去锋芒、变得圆润 (flavor / personality / wine) · temper: 以调和物中和过激锐气 (justice / enthusiasm / metal) · soften: 减轻冲力、硬度或缓和语气 (blow / stance / tone) · ripen: 自然熟透至最佳状态 (fruit / conditions / talent) · subdue: 压制暴烈情绪或柔和色彩明度 (emotions / colors / opposition) · season: 历经风雨以历练稳固 (timber / cast iron / players)

groups.name: Melt & Liquefy · 融化与液化 (Melt, Liquefy, Thaw, Deliquesce)
groups.tip: 受热相变由固转液

items.def_en: change from a solid, frozen state to a liquid state by absorbing heat
items.ex_en: The thick winter ice began to melt rapidly under the warm morning sun.
items.ex_zh: 在温暖的朝阳下，厚厚的冬冰开始迅速融化成水。
items.ex2_en: The talented pastry chef gently melted rich dark chocolate over simmering water.
items.ex2_zh: 天才糕点师在微沸的水上轻轻融化了浓郁的黑巧克力。

items.def_en: become liquid by absorbing moisture directly from the ambient atmosphere
items.ex_en: Left exposed to the humid night air, the mineral salts slowly began to deliquesce.
items.ex_zh: 暴露在潮湿的夜间空气中，矿物盐慢慢开始潮解自融。

items.def_en: incorporate solid particles into a liquid solute until an even liquid solution forms
items.ex_en: Stir the mixture gently until the sugar crystals completely dissolve in warm water.
items.ex_zh: 轻轻搅拌混合物，直到糖晶体完全溶解在温水中。
items.ex2_en: Hot boiling water will dissolve the dense salt crystals within a few seconds.
items.ex2_zh: 沸腾的热水会在几秒钟内溶解密集的盐结晶。

items.def_en: join or liquefy components together using intense heat
items.ex_en: The intense heat of the blast furnace caused the metal alloys to fuse together.
items.ex_zh: 鼓风炉的高温使金属合金熔合在一起。
items.ex2_en: The skilled welder used an electric arc to fuse the broken steel plates.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的焊工使用电弧将断裂的钢板熔接在一起。

items.def_en: pass from a frozen to a liquid or unfrozen state as the temperature rises
items.ex_en: The frozen lake will gradually thaw as the warm spring temperatures finally arrive.
items.ex_zh: 随着温暖春意的终降临，结冰的湖面将逐渐解冻。
items.ex2_en: The chef left the frozen poultry at room temperature to thaw it completely.
items.ex2_zh: 大厨将冷冻家禽置于室温下，以便将其完全解冻。

items.def_en: to become liquid, or to turn a solid or gas into a liquid by heating, pressure, or condensation
items.ex_en: Engineers cooled and pressurized the natural gas to liquefy it for safe transport.
items.ex_zh: 工程师对天然气进行冷却加压使其液化，以便安全运输。
items.ex2_en: Solid paraffin wax will liquefy quickly when exposed to direct open flame heat.
items.ex2_zh: 固体石蜡在接触直接明火的热量时会迅速液化。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses thermodynamic and physical phase transitions where solids or compressed gases convert into liquids through heat, pressure changes, or ambient exposure. It also extends metaphorically to softening of resolve or sentiment.
groups.summary_zh: 指固态物质或气体在受热、受压或受潮后转变为液相的相变过程。
groups.desc_en: Transforming from a solid to a liquid state through thermal energy or solvent action, contrasting with freezing or simple breakage.
groups.desc_zh: 通过热能或溶剂作用使物质从固态转化为液态，与凝固或单纯机械破损相对。
groups.nuance_en: melt: turn from solid to liquid via heat, or metaphorically dissolve away (ice / butter / heart) · thaw: unfreeze from a frozen or rigid state, warming gradually (meat / relations / snow) · liquefy: undergo conversion into liquid under heat or pressure (gas / solids / fat) · dissolve: disintegrate uniformly into a solvent solution (sugar / salt / partnership) · fuse: melt together and blend into a unified whole through intense heat (metals / elements / style) · deliquesce: melt away spontaneously by absorbing atmospheric moisture (chemical / flesh / structure)
groups.nuance_zh: melt: 受热融化或感化消融 (ice / butter / heart) · thaw: 解冻、消融僵局 (meat / relations / snow) · liquefy: 施加温压使物质液化 (gas / solids / fat) · dissolve: 溶入溶剂完全化解 (sugar / salt / partnership) · fuse: 熔融结合为一体 (metals / elements / style) · deliquesce: 潮解或自溶消解 (chemical / flesh / structure)

groups.name: Mesmerize & Transfix · 蛊惑与催眠 (Hypnotize, Mesmerize, Entranced, Captivate)
groups.tip: 心神被牢牢摄取与迷住

items.def_en: attract and hold the interest and affection of someone completely through irresistible charm
items.ex_en: Her natural grace and radiant smile never failed to captivate everyone she met.
items.ex_zh: 她优雅的气质和灿烂的笑容总能深深迷住遇到的每一个人。

items.def_en: hold the complete attention of someone as if by an irresistible hypnotic spell
items.ex_en: The flickering flames of the campfire seemed to mesmerize the weary travelers.
items.ex_zh: 营火摇曳的火光似乎催眠般吸引着疲惫的旅人们。

items.def_en: fill someone with wonder and delight, putting them into an altered, dreamlike state
items.ex_en: The haunting strains of the nocturnal symphony never failed to entrance the poet.
items.ex_zh: 夜曲那萦绕心头的旋律总能令这位诗人为之出神入迷。

items.def_en: hold someone's rapt attention completely, as if under an enchanted trance
items.ex_en: The ancient storyteller could easily spellbind the entire audience with eerie legends.
items.ex_zh: 这位古老的故事讲述者能轻易用诡异的传说镇住全场听众。

items.def_en: to put someone into a state of hypnosis; to fascinate or charm someone so completely that they cannot look away or think clearly
items.ex_en: The rhythmic ticking of the antique clock seemed to gently hypnotize the sleepless patient.
items.ex_zh: 老式钟表有节奏的滴答声似乎能让失眠的患者慢慢进入催眠状态。

items.def_en: cause someone to become completely motionless with astonishment, awe, or horror
items.ex_en: The sudden sight of the monstrous shadow seemed to transfix the terrified guard.
items.ex_zh: 突然出现的巨大阴影吓得心惊胆战的守卫瞬间呆立在原地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote capturing a person's conscious attention so completely that they enter a trance-like, receptive, or frozen state. The effect can be clinical hypnosis or an irresistible psychological state induced by fascination, beauty, or charisma.
groups.summary_zh: 指以超常魅力或催眠手段使人完全着迷、注意力停滞如入迷宫的心理状态。
groups.desc_en: Holding someone's attention so entirely that will, movement, or critical thought is temporarily paralyzed, contrasting with mild entertainment or fleeting interest.
groups.desc_zh: 完全摄取某人的注意力致使其行动、意志或批判力暂时停顿，与普通娱乐或短暂兴趣相对。
groups.nuance_en: transfix: freeze someone motionless with shock, awe, or terror (audience / onlooker / victim) · mesmerize: hold in an almost hypnotic trance of sheer aesthetic or dramatic fascination (crowd / gaze / viewers) · spellbind: entrance completely as if by a magical recitation or performance (audience / children / listeners) · captivate: charm and hold affection or interest irresistibly (heart / mind / audience) · hypnotize: induce a compliant trance, literally or through monotonous rhythm (patient / viewer / room) · entrance: fill with profound delight and otherworldly absorption (spectators / public / readers)
groups.nuance_zh: transfix: 震慑惊呆而定在原地不动 (audience / onlooker / victim) · mesmerize: 极具魅惑力地使人入迷恍惚 (crowd / gaze / viewers) · spellbind: 如中魔咒般全神贯注 (audience / children / listeners) · captivate: 勾摄住心魂与极高好感 (heart / mind / audience) · hypnotize: 催眠或使其失去自主抗拒力 (patient / viewer / room) · entrance: 令人心醉神迷、恍若置身仙境 (spectators / public / readers)

groups.name: Military Occupation & Conquest · 占领与据守 (Capture, Garrison, Take over)
groups.tip: 以武力占据领地或掌控要冲

items.def_en: To assume dominant control, command, or ownership over a physical area or organization
items.ex_en: Rebel forces moved swiftly to take over the local broadcasting station at dawn.
items.ex_zh: 叛军在黎明时分迅速行动，强占了当地的广播电台。

items.def_zh: （武力）占领；占用（空间或时间）；使忙碌
items.def_en: 1. To enter and take control of a country, town, or area by military force. 2. To fill, exist in, or use a space, area, or period of time. 3. To keep someone busy or occupied.
items.ex_en: Hostile troops advanced across the border to forcibly occupy the strategic industrial region.
items.ex_zh: 敌军越过边境，武力占领了该战略工业区。

items.def_en: To station soldiers in a town or fort to defend and retain sovereign control of it
items.ex_en: The commander ordered fresh infantry battalions to garrison the vulnerable border fortress.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官命令新的步兵营派兵驻守易受攻击的边境要塞。

items.def_en: To gain control of an enemy town, outpost, or position by armed combat or tactical maneuver
items.ex_en: Allied forces launched a nocturnal assault to capture the heavily fortified coastal outpost.
items.ex_zh: 盟军发起夜袭，攻占了戒备森严的沿海前哨基地。

items.def_en: To take hold of a strategic location or seat of power suddenly and aggressively
items.ex_en: The insurgent soldiers planned to seize the presidential palace in a dawn raid.
items.ex_zh: 叛军士兵计划在拂晓突袭中夺取总统府。

items.def_en: To incorporate a territory or province into an existing political state, usually by force
items.ex_en: The expanding empire sought to annex the neighboring province through sheer military dominance.
items.ex_zh: 扩张中的帝国企图凭借单纯的军事优势吞并邻省。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers martial or authoritative acts of seizing control of a territory, installation, or building and maintaining control over it. Frequent collocates include territory, capital, stronghold, and base.
groups.summary_zh: 指凭借武力或控制力夺取并驻守领土、要塞或设施。
groups.desc_en: Taking and maintaining sovereign or strategic physical control over territory or positions through armed strength, contrasting with peaceful treaty or commercial tenancy.
groups.desc_zh: 通过武装力量夺取并保持对战略要地或领土的控制权，与和平条约或民事承租相对。
groups.nuance_en: occupy: move into and hold military administrative control over hostile or foreign land (territory / city / zone) · capture: take possession of a hostile position or force by combat (city / stronghold / flag) · seize: suddenly and forcefully grab control of power or strategic assets (power / capital / weapons) · annex: formally and unilaterally incorporate conquered land into one's own state (territory / province / region) · garrison: station military troops in a location to defend and hold it (town / fort / border) · take over: usurp operational or sovereign control completely (government / country / base)
groups.nuance_zh: occupy: 武力进驻并实施军事占领 (territory / city / zone) · capture: 激战后攻克夺取 (city / stronghold / flag) · seize: 猝然以武力抢夺接管 (power / capital / weapons) · annex: 强行吞并划入己方版图 (territory / province / region) · garrison: 派兵驻防守备 (town / fort / border) · take over: 全面接管控制权 (government / country / base)

groups.name: Misguide & Deceive · 误导与引向歧途 (Mislead, Deceive, Delude)
groups.tip: 从引向歧途到蓄意诓骗

items.def_en: To cause someone to make a mistake, form an erroneous judgment, or wander from moral conduct
items.ex_en: Corrupt advisors conspired to lead the young monarch astray from his official duties.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的顾问们密谋引诱年轻的君主偏离其官方职责。

items.def_en: To cause someone to believe something that is not true by giving false information or leaving out key facts
items.ex_en: The false statistics were deliberately designed to mislead the public about inflation rates.
items.ex_zh: 这些虚假统计数据旨在就通胀率对公众产生误导。

items.def_zh: 误导，错误引导；寄错，指错方向
items.def_en: 1. To guide, direct, or channel someone or something into the wrong course or target. 2. To put the wrong address on a letter or parcel.
items.ex_en: The defense attorney tried to misdirect the jury’s attention toward irrelevant personal details.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师试图将陪审团的注意力错误引导至无关的个人细节上。

items.def_en: To deceive or trick someone, often by disguise, pretense, or cunning manipulation
items.ex_en: The fraudulent salesman managed to hoodwink several elderly residents out of their savings.
items.ex_zh: 那名骗子推销员设法蒙混欺骗了几位老年居民的积蓄。

items.def_en: To deliberately make someone believe something false in order to gain an advantage
items.ex_en: The disgraced accountant used forged documents to deceive internal auditors during the review.
items.ex_zh: 身败名裂的会计在审查期间使用伪造文件来欺骗内部审计师。

items.def_en: To deceive someone into holding an irrational, false, or foolish belief
items.ex_en: He continued to delude himself that his failing startup would suddenly become profitable.
items.ex_zh: 他继续哄骗自己，幻想濒临倒闭的创业公司会突然实现盈利。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe causing someone to follow a false path, adopt incorrect assumptions, or succumb to deliberate deception. They range from diversionary steering to outright intentional falsehood.
groups.summary_zh: 指将人引向错误方向、传达虚假认知或进行蓄意欺骗与误导。
groups.desc_en: Directing someone away from the truth or proper conduct, whether by deliberate trickery or insidious distortion, contrasting with candid guidance or simple error.
groups.desc_zh: 无论是蓄意欺骗还是隐秘诱导，引诱他人偏离真相或正道，与坦诚引导或无心失误相对。
groups.nuance_en: mislead: give a false impression or inaccurate information that causes error (investors / public / court) · deceive: deliberately practice fraud or hide truth to gain advantage (partner / enemy / consumers) · delude: cause someone (often oneself) to persist in a false and foolish belief (oneself / followers / public) · hoodwink: dupe someone by deceptive sleight of hand or trickery (authorities / voters / buyers) · lead astray: coax or corrupt morally into a bad course of action (youth / followers / disciple) · misdirect: intentionally divert attention or movement toward the wrong target (focus / anger / funds)
groups.nuance_zh: mislead: 释放错误信息导致判断走偏 (investors / public / court) · deceive: 蓄意瞒骗行诈 (partner / enemy / consumers) · delude: 使沉溺于虚妄迷梦或自欺 (oneself / followers / public) · hoodwink: 用障眼法蒙骗糊弄 (authorities / voters / buyers) · lead astray: 诱入歧途致使道德滑坡 (youth / followers / disciple) · misdirect: 故意转移视线或导向错处 (focus / anger / funds)

groups.name: Misinterpret & Misjudge · 误解与曲解 (Misinterpret, Distort, Misread)
groups.tip: 歪曲解读原意酿成偏差

items.def_en: To fail to understand someone or something correctly
items.ex_en: Due to poor translation, the foreign delegates began to misunderstand the core proposal.
items.ex_zh: 由于糟糕的翻译，外国代表们开始误解核心提案。

items.def_en: To understand or explain the meaning of something incorrectly
items.ex_en: Critics often misinterpret his ambiguous paintings as cynical attacks on modern society.
items.ex_zh: 评论家经常曲解他模棱两可的画作，将其视为对现代社会的愤世嫉俗抨击。

items.def_en: To understand the intent or signs of a situation, person, or text incorrectly
items.ex_en: The diplomatic team completely misread the political signals emanating from the neighboring capital.
items.ex_zh: 外交团队彻底误判了来自邻国首都释放出的政治信号。

items.def_en: To alter or misrepresent the true meaning of someone's words or actions unfairly
items.ex_en: Tabloid reporters deliberately twist my candid remarks to generate sensationalist headlines.
items.ex_zh: 小报记者故意歪曲我坦率的言论以制造轰动性的头条新闻。

items.def_en: To interpret or understand words, actions, or motives incorrectly.
items.ex_en: The jury must be careful not to misconstrue the defendant’s silence as guilt.
items.ex_zh: 陪审团必须小心，不要将被告的沉默曲解为认罪。

items.def_en: To change facts, ideas, or statements so that they give a false or misleading impression
items.ex_en: Partisan media outlets deliberately distort historical facts to suit their current political narrative.
items.ex_zh: 党派媒体故意扭曲历史事实，以迎合其当下的政治叙事。
items.ex2_en: The acoustic vocal tone distorted unpleasantly whenever the singer shouted into the microphone.
items.ex2_zh: 每当歌手对着麦克风大喊时，原声声调就会发生难听的失真。

groups.summary_en: This cognitive frame involves interpreting statements, actions, or evidence incorrectly, either through honest perceptual error or deliberate, tendentious distortion. Verbs highlight failure to grasp intent or the twisting of original meaning.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖因误读、判断失误或刻意曲解而未能正确领会事实原意的动词。
groups.desc_en: Assigning an erroneous, warped, or malicious meaning to a statement, sign, or situation, contrasting with accurate decoding or fair listening.
groups.desc_zh: 对陈述、信号或情况作出错误、扭曲或恶意的解读，与准确解码或客观倾听相对。
groups.nuance_en: misinterpret: draw an erroneous meaning or conclusion from data or language (silence / results / data) · misconstrue: interpret motives or statements in an unfavorable or wrong light (motives / remarks / intentions) · misread: wrongly decipher subtle cues or texts through carelessness (signals / situation / public mood) · distort: warp the original shape, truth, or balance of facts (truth / facts / perspective) · twist: purposefully contort words to suit a biased narrative (words / meaning / testimony) · misunderstand: fail completely to grasp the correct intended idea (concept / point / instructions)
groups.nuance_zh: misinterpret: 对数据或话语理解有误 (silence / results / data) · misconstrue: 恶毒或错误地曲解动机 (motives / remarks / intentions) · misread: 看走眼、误读局势隐性信号 (signals / situation / public mood) · distort: 歪曲事实真貌 (truth / facts / perspective) · twist: 刻意断章取义扭曲话柄 (words / meaning / testimony) · misunderstand: 根本未领会原意 (concept / point / instructions)

groups.name: Mismanage & Botch · 笨拙处理与处置不当 (Mismanage, Botch, Bungle)
groups.tip: 操持应对日常治理

items.def_zh: 处理不当，管理不善；粗暴对待，乱翻乱搬
items.def_en: 1. To manage or deal with a situation, task, or responsibility clumsily, carelessly, or incompetently. 2. To handle something roughly or clumsily.
items.ex_en: The interim director would completely mishandle the sensitive public relations crisis.
items.ex_zh: 这位临时总监在处理极其敏感的公关危机时举措严重不当。

items.def_en: To handle something badly or make a serious mistake that ruins a plan
items.ex_en: One minor technical glitch could mess up the whole launch schedule today.
items.ex_zh: 今天一个微小的技术失误就可能搞砸整个发射日程。

items.def_en: To handle a delicate problem or situation awkwardly or indecisively
items.ex_en: The rookie diplomat continued to fumble every critical question regarding the trade dispute.
items.ex_zh: 这位新手外交官在应对有关贸易争端的每一个关键问题时依然显得笨拙不堪。

items.def_en: To organize or manage an organization or affair badly or incompetently
items.ex_en: Corrupt executives managed to grossly mismanage the pension fund over several decades.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的高管在数十年间将该养老基金管理得一塌糊涂。

items.def_en: To spoil something by doing it badly, clumsily, or carelessly
items.ex_en: Inexperienced mechanics are bound to botch the repair on such an intricate engine.
items.ex_zh: 毫无经验的修理工肯定会把这种复杂发动机的维修工作彻底搞砸。

items.def_en: To carry out a task clumsily or incompetently, leading to embarrassing failure
items.ex_en: The nervous agents managed to bungle what should have been a straightforward sting.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的探员们竟然把原本轻而易举的诱捕行动彻底办砸了。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on handling a delicate situation, project, or task in an incompetent, clumsy, or negligent manner that creates chaos or failure.
groups.summary_zh: 指因无能、疏忽或笨拙而错误处置事务，导致局面恶化或搞砸。
groups.desc_en: Ruining an undertaking or task through sheer incompetence, clumsiness, or poor judgment, contrasting with unavoidable external failure.
groups.desc_zh: 由于无能、笨拙或失策而将本可办好的事情搞砸，与不可抗力导致的失败相对。
groups.nuance_en: bungle: ruin an operation through gross clumsiness and ineptitude (investigation / heist / job) · botch: execute a specific task so poorly that the outcome is ruined (attempt / surgery / execution) · mismanage: govern, direct, or administrate resources incompetently (funds / economy / crisis) · mishandle: deal with a sensitive case or delicate object tactlessly (crisis / case / diplomacy) · fumble: drop the ball literally or lose momentum clumsily (ball / opportunity / response) · mess up: spoil an opportunity or make a chaotic mess (chance / life / plans)
groups.nuance_zh: bungle: 笨头笨脑地彻底搞砸行动 (investigation / heist / job) · botch: 手艺或执行拙劣导致一团糟 (attempt / surgery / execution) · mismanage: 管理不善、治理无方 (funds / economy / crisis) · mishandle: 处置危机或物料不当 (crisis / case / diplomacy) · fumble: 笨拙地抓不住机会或慌乱失手 (ball / opportunity / response) · mess up: 把事情或好局搞得一团乱 (chance / life / plans)

groups.name: Mistreat & Torment · 虐待与苛待 (Maltreat, Mistreat, Abuse, Torment)
groups.tip: 残忍对待或给予身心摧残

items.def_en: treat someone or an animal cruelly or carelessly, causing unnecessary suffering
items.ex_en: Strict municipal regulations penalize any owner who dares to ill-treat domestic animals.
items.ex_zh: 严格的市政法规惩处任何胆敢虐待家养动物的主人。

items.def_en: treat a person or animal badly, cruelly, or unfairly over time
items.ex_en: The cruel master continued to mistreat his exhausted laborers without any remorse.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的雇主继续苛待他那些疲惫不堪的劳工，毫无悔意。

items.def_en: inflict severe physical, verbal, or emotional harm on someone within one's care or custody
items.ex_en: Authorities intervened quickly when the guardian began to physically abuse the foster child.
items.ex_zh: 当监护人开始对寄养儿童实施身体虐待时，有关部门迅速介入。

items.def_en: subject someone repeatedly to excruciating mental agony or persistent physical distress
items.ex_en: Unbearable memories of the battlefield continued to torment the retired veteran every night.
items.ex_zh: 不堪回首的战场记忆每晚都在折磨着这位退伍老兵。

items.def_en: (formal) to treat a person or animal cruelly, violently, or unkindly
items.ex_en: International humanitarian laws explicitly prohibit soldiers to maltreat detained prisoners of war.
items.ex_zh: 国际人道法明确禁止士兵虐待被扣押的战俘。

items.def_en: treat with extreme, savage physical violence that dehumanizes the victim
items.ex_en: Ruthless prison guards would frequently brutalize defenseless inmates during unlawful nightly interrogations.
items.ex_zh: 残忍的狱警经常在非法的夜间审讯中野蛮伤害手无寸铁的囚犯。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on inflicting cruel, physically violent, or psychological suffering upon persons or animals who are under one's power. It highlights the sustained, malevolent, and abusive nature of the conduct across interpersonal, domestic, and institutional contexts.
groups.summary_zh: 指对人或动物进行身体伤害、言语侮辱或精神折磨等残酷苛待行为。
groups.desc_en: Inflicting cruel, harmful, or degrading treatment upon a dependent or vulnerable entity over time, contrasting with proper care or fair punishment.
groups.desc_zh: 对处于弱势或从属地位的个体施加长期残忍、有害或侮辱性的折磨，与妥善照管或公正惩罚相对。
groups.nuance_en: abuse: exploit power to cause physical, emotional, or sexual harm (power / child / substance) · mistreat: treat unkindly, unfairly, or improperly (prisoners / animals / workers) · torment: cause severe, persistent mental anguish or physical pain (soul / captive / minds) · brutalize: desensitize to cruelty or subject to savage bodily violence (inmates / population / victims) · maltreat: treat roughly and brutally, often leaving physical marks (patients / captives / subordinates) · ill-treat: treat in an uncharitable, neglectful, or harsh manner (elderly / minority / animals)
groups.nuance_zh: abuse: 滥用权力施加身心侵害 (power / child / substance) · mistreat: 苛待虐待、不公对待 (prisoners / animals / workers) · torment: 长期从精神或身体上折磨煎熬 (soul / captive / minds) · brutalize: 施以野蛮兽性摧残 (inmates / population / victims) · maltreat: 粗暴残虐对待 (patients / captives / subordinates) · ill-treat: 刻薄冷酷慢待 (elderly / minority / animals)

groups.name: Moisten & Hydrate · 湿润与补水 (Moisten, Dampen, Wet)
groups.tip: 补充水分保持滋润状态

items.def_en: To cover, saturate, or touch something with water or other liquid
items.ex_en: The sudden rain shower managed to completely wet my newly ironed cotton shirt.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的阵雨把新熨好的纯棉衬衫彻底浇湿了。

items.def_en: To increase the level of moisture or water vapor in air or an enclosure
items.ex_en: Museum curators regularly humidify the preservation vaults to protect delicate ancient scrolls.
items.ex_zh: 博物馆馆长定期对保存库进行加湿，以保护娇贵脆弱的古代卷轴。

items.def_en: 1. To supply or absorb water to maintain adequate moisture in the body, skin, or other substances. 2. (chemistry) To combine chemically with water.
items.ex_en: Athletes should drink plenty of fluids to properly hydrate their bodies during marathons.
items.ex_zh: 运动员在马拉松比赛中应饮用充足的液体来为身体补水。
items.ex2_en: Dry garden soil hydrates quickly once steady rainfall begins falling over the lawn.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦草坪上开始持续降雨，干燥的花园土壤很快就会吸收水分。

items.def_en: To moisten lightly with liquid without thoroughly soaking
items.ex_en: You should dampen the cloth slightly before wiping dust off the polished furniture.
items.ex_zh: 在擦拭光面家具上的灰尘之前，你应该先把抹布稍微润湿。

items.def_en: To apply an oily or moist substance to reduce friction and dryness
items.ex_en: Engineers regularly lubricate the mechanical joints to minimize unnecessary friction and wear.
items.ex_zh: 工程师定期润滑机械关节，以最大限度减少不必要的摩擦和磨损。

items.def_en: To make something slightly wet, supple, or damp
items.ex_en: Apply a mild ointment to moisten your dry skin after washing your hands.
items.ex_zh: 洗手后涂抹温和的药膏以润湿干燥的皮肤。
items.ex2_en: Her pale cheeks moistened softly with warm tears of profound relief and joy.
items.ex2_zh: 她苍白的面颊被如释重负和喜悦的温热泪水轻轻打湿。

groups.summary_en: Covers adding water, liquid, or moisture to skin, body tissues, or dry objects to prevent dehydration and soften them.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过补充水分或喷洒液体使物体、皮肤等保持润泽或湿润。
groups.desc_en: Adding a controlled, moderate amount of moisture or liquid to a dry surface or organism, contrasting with soaking or drenching completely.
groups.desc_zh: 向干燥表面或有机体施加适度、受控的水分，与彻底浸透或大水冲淋相对。
groups.nuance_en: moisten: make slightly wet or damp to enhance flexibility or comfort (lips / clay / sponge) · dampen: wet lightly or take off dryness, often cooling or subduing (cloth / hair / spirits) · hydrate: supply water internally or at a cellular level to maintain physiological balance (skin / body / cells) · humidify: increase moisture vapor specifically in surrounding air (room / air / chamber) · lubricate: apply fluid to reduce mechanical friction (engine / joints / machinery) · wet: apply water or liquid broadly to an object (surface / bed / whistle)
groups.nuance_zh: moisten: 微润表面以改善干燥柔韧度 (lips / clay / sponge) · dampen: 轻微沾湿或打湿 (cloth / hair / spirits) · hydrate: 细胞或机体深层补充水分 (skin / body / cells) · humidify: 提高环境空气中的湿度 (room / air / chamber) · lubricate: 注入润滑液减小机械摩擦 (engine / joints / machinery) · wet: 弄湿、使带水 (surface / bed / whistle)

groups.name: Moisten & Soak · 浸润与浸泡 (Dampen, Wet, Bedew)
groups.tip: 水分沾染使其潮湿

items.def_en: To cover, saturate, or touch something with water or other liquid
items.ex_en: The morning downpour managed to thoroughly wet our canvas tents and sleeping gear.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的大雨把我们的帆布帐篷和睡眠装备彻底弄湿了。

items.def_en: To increase the level of moisture or water vapor in air or an enclosed space
items.ex_en: High-tech sensors work continuously to humidify the sterile air inside the greenhouse.
items.ex_zh: 高科技传感器持续运转，为温室内的无菌空气增加湿度。

items.def_en: To wet or sprinkle a surface lightly with drops of liquid or dew
items.ex_en: Early morning mist descended silently to bedew the petals of the wild roses.
items.ex_zh: 清晨的薄雾悄然降临，如露水般润湿了野玫瑰的花瓣。

items.def_en: To clean or moisten an area lightly using a wet sponge
items.ex_en: The nurse gently began to sponge down the feverish child with cool water.
items.ex_zh: 护士开始用凉水轻轻地用海绵擦洗发烧的孩子以使其凉爽。

items.def_en: To make something slightly wet or humid
items.ex_en: Please dampen the clean paper towel before attempting to wipe the glass tabletop.
items.ex_zh: 擦拭玻璃桌面之前，请先将干净的纸巾微微弄湿。

items.def_en: to make something slightly wet, or to become slightly wet
items.ex_en: The surgeon asked the assistant to moisten the sterile gauze with saline solution.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生要求助手用生理盐水润湿无菌纱布。
items.ex2_en: The dry sponge moistened immediately upon contact with the warm soapy water.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的海绵一接触温热的肥皂水就立刻湿润了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe applying a controlled or mild amount of liquid to a surface or substance to eliminate dryness without totally drenching it.
groups.summary_zh: 指施加适量液体使物体表面或内部微湿、解燥，但未达到湿透程度。
groups.desc_en: Applying or infusing liquid onto a surface or substance to alter its moisture level, contrasting with total submersion or destructive saturation.
groups.desc_zh: 通过施加或渗入液体改变物体湿润度，区别于整机淹没或破坏性浸透。
groups.nuance_en: wet: generic application of liquid (whistle / surface) · moisten: slight wetting to soften or condition (lips / sponge / soil) · dampen: slight wetting or suppressing dryness (cloth / hair) · humidify: increasing airborne moisture vapor (air / room) · bedew: delicate condensation or natural droplet coverage (grass / cheeks) · sponge down: localized cleaning or cooling with moist absorbent tool (counter / patient)
groups.nuance_zh: wet: 泛指弄湿或沾水 (whistle / surface) · moisten: 微量浸润以软化或调理 (lips / sponge / soil) · dampen: 稍加打湿或微湿抑干 (cloth / hair) · humidify: 提高空气中的水汽湿度 (air / room) · bedew: 凝露般轻覆水滴 (grass / cheeks) · sponge down: 用湿海绵擦拭降温或清洁 (counter / patient)

groups.name: Monopolize & Selfish Usurpation · 独占与自私侵吞 (Hog, Monopolize, Corner)
groups.tip: 贪婪独占不与他人分享

items.def_en: To acquire enough of a commodity or market share to control its commercial supply and price
items.ex_en: The wealthy cartel attempted to corner the global market for rare industrial minerals.
items.ex_zh: 富有的卡特尔企图垄断稀有工业矿产的全球市场。

items.def_en: To take possession of something, often without right or permission, for one's exclusive use
items.ex_en: The corrupt official attempted to secretly appropriate company funds for personal real estate.
items.ex_zh: 该腐败官员企图秘密将公司资金据为己有以购置个人房产。

items.def_en: To selfishly hold on to or consume an item rather than sharing it with peers
items.ex_en: Do not bogart that shared bowl of buttered popcorn while we watch movies.
items.ex_zh: 我们看电影时，别一个人霸着那碗共享的黄油爆米花不放。

items.def_en: To obtain exclusive possession or complete control of an asset, conversation, or market
items.ex_en: The vocal critic tried to monopolize the entire panel discussion with lengthy diatribes.
items.ex_zh: 那位言辞激烈的批评家试图用冗长的抨击独占整个小组讨论的时间。

items.def_en: (informal) to take or use more than your share of something selfishly so that others cannot use it
items.ex_en: My older brother always likes to hog the bathroom mirror every single morning.
items.ex_zh: 我哥哥每天早上总是喜欢霸占着浴室的镜子不放。

items.def_en: To seize and hold power, position, or rights wrongfully and forcefully
items.ex_en: The ambitious military general plotted covertly to usurp royal power from the crown.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的军事将领暗中密谋从王室手中篡夺权力。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote taking, holding, or consuming disproportionate control or ownership of shared resources, space, or opportunities out of self-interest. They highlight exclusive appropriation that denies fair access to others.
groups.summary_zh: 指自私或专横地侵占、独揽共享资源、空间或话语权，排斥他人分享。
groups.desc_en: Taking exclusive possession or control of a resource selfishly or illegitimately, contrasting with shared utilization or lawful acquisition.
groups.desc_zh: 出于自私或非正当手段对资源进行独占与侵吞，区别于公平共享或合法取得。
groups.nuance_en: hog: greedily keeping more than one's fair share (lane / bathroom / ball) · monopolize: totally dominating access to exclude others (conversation / market / attention) · corner: strategically securing total market control (market / supply) · usurp: illegitimately seizing power or authority (throne / power / authority) · appropriate: taking possession without permission, often officially or covertly (funds / land / culture) · bogart: selfishly holding onto a shared item without passing it (joint / mic)
groups.nuance_zh: hog: 贪婪独霸超过自己应得份额 (lane / bathroom / ball) · monopolize: 全面垄断以排除他人参与 (conversation / market / attention) · corner: 策略性囤积操纵市场 (market / supply) · usurp: 篡夺非法掌控权力或职能 (throne / power / authority) · appropriate: 未经许可据为己有或侵吞 (funds / land / culture) · bogart: 自私霸占本应轮换之物 (joint / mic)

groups.name: Mouth & Mutter · 口型发音与机械含糊言说 (Mutter, Lip, Murmur)
groups.tip: 从动嘴发声到组织语言表达

items.def_en: To shape words silently with the lips without phonating any audible sound.
items.ex_en: She stood backstage to silently lip the song's opening lyrics to him.
items.ex_zh: 她站在后台，无声地冲他动着嘴唇念出歌曲的开篇歌词。

items.def_zh: 说出，用言辞表达；用口型不出声地说；口是心非地说
items.def_en: 1. To express or utter words, especially pompously or insincerely. 2. To form words with the lips without making any sound.
items.ex_en: The cynical politician would merely mouth empty platitudes without offering any real solutions.
items.ex_zh: 那位虚伪的政客只会口是心非地说些空洞的陈词滥调，而不提供任何真正的解决方案。

items.def_en: To utter words indistinctly so that others struggle to understand them.
items.ex_en: The frightened witness began to mumble incoherent excuses during the tense court interrogation.
items.ex_zh: 在紧张的法庭质询中，吓坏了的证人开始含糊其辞地念叨不连贯的借口。

items.def_en: To speak in a low, unclear voice with near-closed lips, often in complaint.
items.ex_en: Disgruntled employees continued to mutter dark complaints about the sudden pay reductions today.
items.ex_zh: 心怀不满的员工们今天继续低声含糊抱怨突如其来的降薪。

items.def_en: To repeat words without understanding them or with no genuine personal thought.
items.ex_en: He would just blindly parrot slogans he heard online without understanding their implications.
items.ex_zh: 他只会盲目地鹦鹉学舌般重复网上听来的口号，根本不明白其中的含义。

items.def_zh: 喋喋不休，假大空地说出
items.def_en: To speak or utter opinions pompously, repetitively, and in great quantities.
items.ex_en: The arrogant professor started to spout tedious philosophical theories at the dinner party.
items.ex_zh: 傲慢的教授在晚宴上开始喋喋不休地大谈乏味的哲学理论。
items.ex2_en: Warm mineral water spouted high into the crisp morning air from the geyser.
items.ex2_zh: 温热的矿泉水从间歇泉中喷涌而出，高高地喷入清晨清爽的空气中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail non-standard speech production—either articulating words silently with the lips, chanting insincere platitudes, or muttering indistinctly under breath.
groups.summary_zh: 无声对口型、敷衍假意言说，或闭唇低声嘟哝含混发音的言语形态。
groups.desc_en: Articulating words indistinctly, mechanically, or without genuine engagement, contrasting with clear, expressive, and authentic speech.
groups.desc_zh: 含糊、机械或言不由衷地发音言说，区别于清晰、生动且真诚的表达。
groups.nuance_en: mouth: silently forming words with lips or insincerely reciting phrases (words / platitudes / lyrics) · mutter: speaking in low, barely audible tones expressing complaint (threats / under one's breath / complaints) · mumble: articulating words indistinctly due to low volume or sluggish articulation (apology / excuse / words) · lip: shaping words soundlessly or speaking impudently (lyrics / response) · parrot: mindlessly repeating without comprehension (slogans / party line / phrases) · spout: glibly and profusely discharging words or jargon (nonsense / rhetoric / claptrap)
groups.nuance_zh: mouth: 仅动嘴型不出声或言不由衷背诵 (words / platitudes / lyrics) · mutter: 低沉含混地喃喃抱怨 (threats / under one's breath / complaints) · mumble: 吐字不清、咕哝难辨 (apology / excuse / words) · lip: 默念对口型或顶撞回嘴 (lyrics / response) · parrot: 机械盲目跟读复述 (slogans / party line / phrases) · spout: 滔滔不绝喷出空洞高论 (nonsense / rhetoric / claptrap)

groups.name: Move Gently & Inch Along · 轻移与挪动 (Edge, Inch, Nudge, Worm)
groups.tip: 谨慎缓慢地一点点向前挪

items.def_zh: 轻移，小心缓慢地挪动；减轻，缓和
items.def_en: 1. To move gently, carefully, and slowly into or out of a position. 2. To become less severe, or make something less difficult or painful.
items.ex_en: She carefully eased the heavy wooden cabinet through the narrow doorway without a scratch.
items.ex_zh: 她小心翼翼地把笨重的木柜挪过狭窄的门道，丝毫没有刮碰。
items.ex2_en: The severe economic sanctions eased gradually after both nations signed the bilateral treaty.
items.ex2_zh: 在两国签署双边条约后，严厉的经济制裁逐渐有所缓解。

items.def_zh: 侧身缓缓移动；逐步挪动
items.def_en: to move slowly and carefully, often sideways or by tiny degrees
items.ex_en: The nervous driver edged his car forward into the crowded intersection inch by inch.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的司机把车一点点缓缓往前挪，开进了拥挤的十字路口。
items.ex2_en: The cautious cat edged silently along the narrow brick ledge above the courtyard.
items.ex2_zh: 警惕的猫咪沿着院子上方狭窄的砖砌窗台悄悄地慢慢挪动。

items.def_en: to move or make something move very slowly and in very small increments
items.ex_en: The rescue crew inched the fallen beam away from the trapped hiker very cautiously.
items.ex_zh: 救援人员极其谨慎地把倒下的横梁一点点从受困的登山者身上移开。
items.ex2_en: The determined mountain climber inched steadily toward the freezing rocky summit all morning.
items.ex2_zh: 坚定的登山者整个上午都在缓慢而平稳地向冰冷的岩石顶峰挪动。

items.def_en: to push someone or something gently, gradually coaxing them into a specific position
items.ex_en: He nudged the heavy crate into the corner with his boot to clear space.
items.ex_zh: 他用靴子轻轻将沉重的木箱推入角落，以腾出空间。

items.def_en: to move oneself slowly and cautiously through a crowded or restricted gap
items.ex_en: We managed to worm our way through the dense concert crowd toward the stage.
items.ex_zh: 我们设法在拥挤的音乐会人群中挤出一条路，挪到了舞台前。

items.def_en: to move smoothly and quickly or wriggle with a slight swaying motion through a narrow space
items.ex_en: The caver shimmied through the narrow rock fissure with only inches to spare.
items.ex_zh: 洞穴探险者扭动身体，紧贴着岩壁滑步钻过了狭窄的石缝。

groups.summary_en: Refers to moving oneself or an object gradually, carefully, and slowly in order to avoid damage, detection, or physical strain. These verbs emphasize cautious navigation through tight physical spaces or delicate situations.
groups.summary_zh: 强调以极其谨慎、微小且缓慢的动作轻挪入位或避开阻碍。
groups.desc_en: Advancing in tiny, cautious, or lateral increments through tight or sensitive spaces, contrasting with brisk, open movement.
groups.desc_zh: 在狭窄或敏感空间内极小幅、谨慎或侧身蠕动挪移，区别于快速开阔的行进。
groups.nuance_en: inch: progressing forward by microscopic increments (forward / closer / toward the exit) · edge: moving cautiously or sideways into position (nearer / away / toward the door) · ease: guiding something gently and smoothly into place (car / tension / into a chair) · nudge: gently prodding into motion or position (elbow / price / forward) · shimmy: vibrating or wiggling side-to-side through a tight space (through / into jeans / up a pole) · worm one's way: insinuating oneself patiently into a confined space or favor (into confidence / through crowd)
groups.nuance_zh: inch: 极微小幅度寸步挪动 (forward / closer / toward the exit) · edge: 侧身或试探性小心蹭移 (nearer / away / toward the door) · ease: 缓缓、稳妥地顺入或挪移 (car / tension / into a chair) · nudge: 轻轻推动或微调位移 (elbow / price / forward) · shimmy: 扭动或侧向晃动穿过窄缝 (through / into jeans / up a pole) · worm one's way: 蠕动钻进狭处或钻营逢迎 (into confidence / through crowd)

groups.name: Murmur & Coo · 呢喃与温声软语 (Whisper, Purr, Breathe)
groups.tip: 柔和轻声倾诉或甜蜜呢喃

items.def_en: To utter words very softly and with warmth into someone's ear
items.ex_en: He leaned close to her ear and breathed a quiet promise into the darkness.
items.ex_zh: 他俯身凑近她的耳畔，在黑暗中轻柔地吐露了一句誓言。

items.def_en: To speak very quietly, using breath rather than the vocal cords
items.ex_en: The librarian whispered the instructions to us so she would not disturb the readers.
items.ex_zh: 图书管理员压低声音向我们耳语指示，以免打扰到读者。

items.raw_cluster: 轻声细语与呢喃 Murmur & Coo
items.def_zh: 轻柔低语，温柔地说；（鸽子等）咕咕叫
items.def_en: 1. To speak in a soft, gentle, and loving voice. 2. (of a dove or pigeon) To make a soft low murmur.
items.ex_en: The mother cooed sweet reassurances to her sleepy baby until he drifted off.
items.ex_zh: 母亲用轻柔宠溺的声音低语安慰着困倦的婴儿，直到他沉沉睡去。

items.def_en: To say something in a soft, low, barely audible voice
items.ex_en: She murmured a faint prayer before stepping out onto the brightly lit stage.
items.ex_zh: 在走上灯火通明的舞台之前，她低声轻吟了一句祷告。

items.def_en: To speak quietly and in a low voice that is difficult to hear clearly
items.ex_en: He muttered an angry complaint under his breath as he washed the dirty dishes.
items.ex_zh: 洗脏盘子时，他在嘴里低声嘀咕着愤怒的抱怨。

items.def_zh: 娇声而言；猫般轻柔发声
items.def_en: To speak in a smooth, quiet, pleasantly seductive tone
items.ex_en: She purred a flirtatious compliment across the candlelit table, catching him completely off guard.
items.ex_zh: 隔着烛光餐桌，她娇声说了一句挑逗的赞美，让他措手不及。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses vocalizations delivered in a hushed, gentle, affectionate, or soothing register, typically conveying intimacy, tenderness, or comforting reassurance.
groups.summary_zh: 指用极为轻柔、深情或娇嗔的低音细语，传达温存与安抚。
groups.desc_en: Producing low, soft, intimate vocalizations characterized by tenderness or secrecy, contrasting with loud, projected declarations.
groups.desc_zh: 发出低沉、柔和、亲昵的喉音或轻语，带有温存或隐秘感，区别于高声宣讲。
groups.nuance_en: whisper: speaking without vocal cord vibration for confidentiality (secrets / in one's ear / sweet nothings) · murmur: low, continuous, subdued sound of indistinct speech or affection (approval / sweet nothings / assent) · coo: speaking with gentle, high-pitched dove-like affection (words / over baby / softly) · purr: speaking in a throaty, seductive, or contented low tone (satisfaction / voice / compliments) · breathe: uttering very softly as an exhale (sigh / words / vow)
groups.nuance_zh: whisper: 压低声带的耳语或说悄悄话 (secrets / in one's ear / sweet nothings) · murmur: 低缓含混的私语或咕哝表达 (approval / sweet nothings / assent) · coo: 宛如鸽鸣般娇柔温存地呢喃 (words / over baby / softly) · purr: 喉底发出娇媚或惬意的低语 (satisfaction / voice / compliments) · breathe: 如吐气般极为轻柔地倾诉 (sigh / words / vow)

groups.name: Muzzle & Silence · 压制与封口 (Gag, Silence, Stifle)
groups.tip: 给言论戴上口套强行压制

items.def_en: To tell or signal someone to be quiet, often by saying 'shh'
items.ex_en: The usher shushed the noisy teenagers as soon as the opening scene began.
items.ex_zh: 开场一演，引座员就立刻对吵闹的少年们做出嘘声手势示意安静。

items.def_en: To stop talking, making noise, or shouting, especially when ordered to do so
items.ex_en: The exhausted teacher ordered the rowdy class to pipe down and finish reading.
items.ex_zh: 筋疲力尽的老师命令吵闹的班级安静下来，把书读完。

items.def_zh: 扼杀；压抑；阻止（言论或表达）
items.def_en: To suppress, quell, or smother an utterance, opinion, or impulse before it can fully form
items.ex_en: The regime tried to stifle internal dissent before any public demonstrations could materialize.
items.ex_zh: 该政权试图在任何公众抗议形成之前扼杀内部异见。

items.def_en: To stop someone from expressing their views, criticisms, or opposition
items.ex_en: The administration used restrictive contracts to silence whistleblowers within the corporate ranks.
items.ex_zh: 管理层利用限制性合同压制公司内部告密者的声音。

items.def_en: To prevent someone from speaking freely or disseminating information, often via legal orders or force
items.ex_en: A strict court injunction effectively gagged the press from reporting on the ongoing investigation.
items.ex_zh: 一项严格的法庭禁令有效地封堵了媒体对正在进行的调查的报道。

items.def_zh: 钳制，剥夺…发表言论的自由；给（动物）戴口套
items.def_en: 1. To prevent a person, group, or the media from expressing opinions freely. 2. To put a muzzle over the nose and mouth of an animal.
items.ex_en: The new censorship laws were clearly designed to muzzle independent journalists across the country.
items.ex_zh: 新的审查法案显然旨在钳制全国各地独立记者的言论自由。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe coercive interventions aimed at preventing speech, public dissent, whistleblowing, or free expression by force or political suppression.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重于运用权势、法律或暴力手段强行封堵言论、压制发声。
groups.desc_en: Suppressing vocal output, free expression, or dissent through coercion or physical blockage, contrasting with rational persuasion.
groups.desc_zh: 通过外力压制、物理封堵或权威施压强行制止发声，区别于理性说服。
groups.nuance_en: silence: systematically extinguishing sound, debate, or critics (critics / opposition / guns) · muzzle: legally, politically, or physically preventing free expression (press / watchdog / dissent) · gag: applying a physical restraint or legal order to prevent speech (witnesses / press / media) · stifle: choking off sound, reaction, or impulse before full emergence (laughter / yawns / dissent) · shush: urgently demanding quiet, often verbally (crowd / children / audience) · pipe down: informal cessation of loud, annoying talk (noise / talkers)
groups.nuance_zh: silence: 全面压制使之失声或平息 (critics / opposition / guns) · muzzle: 通过法规或强制手段剥夺言论权 (press / watchdog / dissent) · gag: 下达禁令或封口使不得作证泄密 (witnesses / press / media) · stifle: 遏制、掐灭刚萌生的声音或反应 (laughter / yawns / dissent) · shush: 嘘声示意安静 (crowd / children / audience) · pipe down: 俚俗地闭嘴或降低噪音 (noise / talkers)

groups.name: Object & Protest · 反对与抗议 (Object, Dissent, Kick Against)
groups.tip: 从提出异议到公开抗议反对

items.def_en: (+ to) To state that you do not approve of or agree with a plan, decision, or situation.
items.ex_en: Several board members objected to the sudden merger proposal during the annual executive meeting.
items.ex_zh: 几位董事会成员在年度高管会议上对这项突如其来的合并提案提出了异议。

items.def_en: To show anger, resistance, or defiance toward rules or constraints that limit you.
items.ex_en: The rebellious young poet constantly kicked against the suffocating traditions of his aristocratic family.
items.ex_zh: 这位叛逆的年轻诗人不断反抗着他贵族家庭令人窒息的传统。

items.def_en: (+ against) To declare one's opposition or criticism openly and publicly.
items.ex_en: Activists took to the streets to speak out against human rights abuses.
items.ex_zh: 活动人士走上街头，大声疾呼反对侵犯人权的行为。

items.def_zh: 持异议，公开表达不赞同
items.def_en: (+ from) To publicly disagree with an official opinion, decision, or doctrine.
items.ex_en: Two senior justices dissented from the majority opinion in yesterday's landmark supreme court ruling.
items.ex_zh: 在昨天最高法院的里程碑式裁决中，有两名资深法官对多数意见持有异议。

items.def_en: To express passionate, vehement condemnation or objection to an injustice.
items.ex_en: The human rights committee cried out against the unlawful detention of peaceful activists.
items.ex_zh: 人权委员会对非法拘留和平活动人士的行为提出了强烈谴责。

items.def_zh: 抗议，反对；坚决声明，力辩
items.def_en: 1. To express strong disagreement, disapproval, or objection, especially publicly. 2. (+ that) To state or declare something firmly and emphatically, especially when others doubt it.
items.ex_en: Thousands of citizens protested against the proposed tax hikes outside the parliament building yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 昨天成千上万的市民在议会大厦外抗议拟议的增税方案。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote expressing strong, overt disapproval or resistance against decisions, rules, or authority, ranging from formal procedural opposition to vocal public resistance.
groups.summary_zh: 表达对决定或权威的明确反对与抗议，从程序性异议到强烈声讨。
groups.desc_en: Formally or forcefully declaring disagreement or resistance against an established rule, claim, or injustice, contrasting with compliant acceptance.
groups.desc_zh: 对既定规则、主张或不公提出正式或强烈的反对与抗议，区别于顺从接纳。
groups.nuance_en: object: raising a formal, procedural, or moral counter-argument (proposal / plan / to the court) · protest: vocalizing strong collective or individual indignation (decision / policy / injustice) · dissent: withholding consent from an orthodoxy or majority ruling (ruling / dogma / opinion) · speak out: bravely voicing opposition publicly (against abuse / injustice / corruption) · cry out against: lamenting or denouncing an outrage with intense emotion (injustice / cruelty / atrocity) · kick against: stubbornly resisting an inescapable authority or constraint (pricks / rules / authority)
groups.nuance_zh: object: 提出程序性、法理或道义反对 (proposal / plan / to the court) · protest: 公开强烈抗议不公或决议 (decision / policy / injustice) · dissent: 持不同政见或违背主流裁决 (ruling / dogma / opinion) · speak out: 挺身而出大声疾呼 (against abuse / injustice / corruption) · cry out against: 悲愤声讨或痛斥暴行 (injustice / cruelty / atrocity) · kick against: 徒劳或顽固地抗拒管束 (pricks / rules / authority)

groups.name: Oblige & Behoove · 应当与道义责任 (Ought, Behoove, Incumb)
groups.tip: 基于道义或规则的要求

items.def_en: To be convenient, acceptable, or morally and socially fitting for someone
items.ex_en: Such rude and dismissive behavior does not suit a diplomat representing our nation abroad.
items.ex_zh: 这种粗鲁无礼的举止绝不符合代表国家驻外的外交官身份。

items.def_zh: 应该，应当（基于道义、职责或常理）
items.def_en: (modal verb, usually followed by 'to') Used to indicate duty, moral obligation, or what is advisable or expected.
items.ex_en: Citizens ought to respect the fundamental rights and personal dignity of their fellow neighbors.
items.ex_zh: 公民理应当尊重其街坊邻里的基本权利和个人尊严。

items.def_zh: 归属于；落到……头上（指职责）
items.def_en: To fall as a duty, responsibility, or necessity upon someone
items.ex_en: The difficult responsibility will now devolve on the deputy director in the director's absence.
items.ex_zh: 在主管缺席期间，这项艰巨的职责现在将落到副主管的头上。

items.def_en: To bind legally or morally to a specified course of action
items.ex_en: The contractual agreement obliges both parties to disclose all relevant financial records immediately.
items.ex_zh: 合同协议要求双方必须立即披露所有相关的财务记录。

items.def_en: To be suitable or appropriate for a particular status, occasion, or role
items.ex_en: The grand banquet was organized with a quiet elegance that befitted a royal celebration.
items.ex_zh: 这场盛大的国宴以一种契合皇室庆典的静谧高雅规格举办。

items.def_zh: 对……而言有必要/理所应当
items.def_en: To be incumbent upon, fitting, or necessary as a duty or responsibility (used impersonally, e.g., 'it behooves someone to')
items.ex_en: It behooves every senior researcher to verify all experimental data before publishing the paper.
items.ex_zh: 每位资深研究员在发表论文前，都有必要认真核实所有实验数据。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express moral obligation, propriety, logical necessity, or normative expectation. They range from modal assertions of duty to impersonal, formal expressions denoting that an action is becoming or required of a person in a particular role.
groups.summary_zh: 表达道义义务、合宜性或社会与职务上的理所应当。
groups.desc_en: Expressing normative, moral, or situational duty imposed by decorum, status, or natural propriety, contrasting with explicit statutory compulsion.
groups.desc_zh: 由身份、体面或道义情理所决定的应有作为与责任，区别于单纯法定强迫。
groups.nuance_en: behoove: demanding action as fitting to one's interest, moral duty, or dignity (us / society / government) · befit: matching natural status, occasion, or character (station / king / occasion) · oblige: binding someone by legal force, moral duty, or gratitude (guests / conscience / duty) · ought: indicating ideal moral expectation or probability (duty / respect / justice) · devolve on: transferring or falling upon as an ultimate duty (heir / successor / deputy)
groups.nuance_zh: behoove: 基于理应、体统或利益有义务 (us / society / government) · befit: 适宜匹配身份或场合 (station / king / occasion) · oblige: 迫于道义、人情或职责必须为之 (guests / conscience / duty) · ought: 表达道义应当或合理预期 (duty / respect / justice) · devolve on: 职责或担子自然落到某人身上 (heir / successor / deputy)

groups.name: Obscure & Mask · 遮蔽与隐匿 (Conceal, Veil, Shroud)
groups.tip: 遮掩秘密使其隐没不见

items.def_en: To disguise or hide a feeling, sound, smell, or fact behind another layer
items.ex_en: He put on a broad, confident smile to mask his deep internal anxiety.
items.ex_zh: 他露出了爽朗自信的微笑，以掩饰自己内心深处的焦虑。

items.def_en: To separate or shelter an area from public view using a screen or barrier
items.ex_en: The hospital staff quickly screened off the intensive care bed with tall curtains.
items.ex_zh: 医院的工作人员迅速用高大的帘布将重症监护病床隔开以防外人窥探。

items.def_en: To prevent something from being seen, known, or discovered
items.ex_en: The company intentionally concealed critical audit findings from regulatory inspectors during the review.
items.ex_zh: 该公司在审查期间故意向监管督察员隐瞒了关键的审计结果。

items.def_zh: 遮掩，遮蔽；使模糊，使费解
items.def_en: to cover something or block it from view; to make something difficult to see, hear, or understand
items.ex_en: Thick autumn fog rose from the valley and obscured the road ahead completely.
items.ex_zh: 深秋浓重的山谷迷雾升腾而起，完全遮蔽了前方的道路。

items.def_en: To cover something with a layer or mask so as to hide it partly from view
items.ex_en: A delicate layer of mist veiled the distant mountain peaks at dawn today.
items.ex_zh: 今天黎明时分，一层微妙的薄雾隐隐遮蔽了远处的山峰。

items.def_en: (+ in) To cover or envelop something completely so that it cannot be seen or identified clearly
items.ex_en: The ancient ruins were shrouded in mystery long after the archaeological excavation ended.
items.ex_zh: 考古发掘结束很久之后，这座古代遗址仍然笼罩在神秘之中。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on blocking lines of sight or cognitive perception through physical coverings, darkness, or deliberate obfuscation.
groups.summary_zh: 通过实体覆盖物、黑暗或迷局阻隔视线，使之模糊或难以辨识。
groups.desc_en: Placing a visual, physical, or cognitive barrier over something to prevent detection, contrasting with unveiling or clarifying.
groups.desc_zh: 设置视线、物理或认知屏障以遮蔽隐藏，区别于揭开或澄清。
groups.nuance_en: conceal: deliberately keeping something secret or out of sight (weapons / identity / feelings) · obscure: making something indistinct, dim, or hard to comprehend (meaning / view / details) · mask: adopting a deceptive outer appearance to disguise what lies beneath (pain / symptoms / intentions) · veil: covering with a thin layer of secrecy or cloth (face / truth / threat) · shroud: enveloping completely in heavy gloom or mystery (mystery / mist / secrecy) · screen off: erecting a physical partition to block line of sight (area / bed / view)
groups.nuance_zh: conceal: 刻意隐匿不被发现 (weapons / identity / feelings) · obscure: 使视线模糊或使意义晦涩 (meaning / view / details) · mask: 戴上伪装以掩盖底层真相 (pain / symptoms / intentions) · veil: 如罩薄纱般含蓄隐约遮掩 (face / truth / threat) · shroud: 如裹尸布般重重包裹或笼罩于谜团 (mystery / mist / secrecy) · screen off: 设立隔断以挡住视线 (area / bed / view)

groups.name: Observe & Scrutinize · 观察与审视 (Observe, Watch, Scrutinize)
groups.tip: 集中精力长久持续注视

items.def_en: To watch someone or something carefully, ensuring safety or guarding against wrongdoing
items.ex_en: Could you please keep an eye on my luggage while I buy lunch?
items.ex_zh: 我去买午饭的时候，你能帮我照看一下行李吗？

items.def_en: To look at someone or something for a period of time, paying close attention to developments
items.ex_en: We watched the migrating birds cross the evening sky until they disappeared completely.
items.ex_zh: 我们注视着候鸟飞过傍晚的天空，直到它们彻底消失在视野中。

items.def_en: To keep track of and observe the progress or quality of something systematically over time
items.ex_en: Nurses closely monitored the patient's heart rate throughout the night for unexpected changes.
items.ex_zh: 护士们整夜严密监测病人的心率，以防出现意外变化。

items.def_zh: 观察，注视；注意到；遵守（规则、习俗等）；评论
items.def_en: 1. To watch someone or something carefully. 2. To notice or perceive something. 3. To obey a rule, law, or custom. 4. To make a formal remark or comment.
items.ex_en: The scientific team observed several rare behavioral patterns in the newly discovered species.
items.ex_zh: 科考队在这个新发现的物种身上观察到了几种罕见的行为模式。

items.def_en: To look closely or intently at someone or something, often assessing them directly
items.ex_en: The security guard carefully eyeballed every single visitor before letting them through the gate.
items.ex_zh: 保安在放行之前，仔细打量了进门的每一个访客。

items.def_en: To inspect, examine, or look at someone or something very closely and critically
items.ex_en: Tax auditors will scrutinize every corporate expense report submitted during the past three years.
items.ex_zh: 税务审计员将严格审查过去三年提交的每一份企业报销报告。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey focused, sustained visual monitoring and perceptual tracking of an entity over time, either for scientific collection, vigilance, or analytical assessment.
groups.summary_zh: 指对目标进行持续、专注的视觉监测、审视或追踪。
groups.desc_en: Applying directed sensory and analytical attention over time to monitor behavior or detect flaws, contrasting with mere casual glancing.
groups.desc_zh: 带有明确目的持续施加感官与分析性注视，区别于漫不经心的瞥视。
groups.nuance_en: watch: looking attentively at dynamic actions unfolding over time (game / steps / screen) · observe: systematically recording empirical facts or customs without interference (behavior / phenomenon / rules) · scrutinize: examining every microscopic detail with critical suspicion (documents / evidence / motives) · monitor: continuously tracking progress or metrics against a baseline (patient / election / performance) · keep an eye on: maintaining protective or wary oversight (children / luggage / developments) · eyeball: assessing informally and directly with one's naked eyes (target / rival / distance)
groups.nuance_zh: watch: 留心注视动态事件演变 (game / steps / screen) · observe: 客观、系统性地观察记录 (behavior / phenomenon / rules) · scrutinize: 挑剔且透彻地审视细节 (documents / evidence / motives) · monitor: 依据指标持续监控追踪 (patient / election / performance) · keep an eye on: 照看警戒以防差池 (children / luggage / developments) · eyeball: 用肉眼直接估量打量 (target / rival / distance)

groups.name: Occupy & Colonize · 侵占与殖民 (Colonize, Settle, Subjugate)
groups.tip: 强行占领并建立殖民

items.def_en: Establish a community or colony in a new area, often displacing original inhabitants
items.ex_en: Thousands of European immigrants settled the fertile river valley throughout the nineteenth century.
items.ex_zh: 十九世纪期间，数千名欧洲移民在这片肥沃的河谷定居殖民。

items.def_en: Take and maintain military control and presence in a foreign territory
items.ex_en: Hostile military forces occupied the strategic border province after a prolonged artillery campaign.
items.ex_zh: 敌对军事力量在长期的炮击作战之后占领了该战略边境省份。

items.def_en: Supply a territory or region with human inhabitants or settlers
items.ex_en: The royal decree aimed to populate the newly conquered borderlands with veteran soldiers.
items.ex_zh: 皇家法令旨在用退伍老兵去充实并落户新征服的边境土地。

items.def_en: Take control of an area or country and formally incorporate it into one's own territory
items.ex_en: The imperial government officially annexed the neighboring territory following the successful winter offensive.
items.ex_zh: 帝国政府在成功的冬季攻势后，正式吞并了邻近领土。

items.def_en: Bring a people or region completely under domination and political control by force
items.ex_en: The empire used overwhelming military might to subjugate rebellious tribes across the province.
items.ex_zh: 该帝国利用压倒性的军事力量征服了全省各地叛乱的部落。

items.def_zh: 使殖民地化，开拓殖民地；（动植物）大批繁殖于，聚居于
items.def_en: to establish political control over an area and send settlers there; (of plants or animals) to populate a new habitat
items.ex_en: British forces colonised vast territories across the globe during the nineteenth century era.
items.ex_zh: 十九世纪期间，英国军队在全球范围内开拓建立了广袤的殖民地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote settling, occupying, or establishing political and territorial control over foreign regions or indigenous populations.
groups.summary_zh: 指国家或群体在领土上定居、占领并建立外来政治控制统治。
groups.desc_en: Establishing territorial dominance, habitation, or sovereign control over another region or population by force or settlement, contrasting with equal coexistence.
groups.desc_zh: 通过武力或定居对另一领土或群体确立统治占领与主权，区别于平等共存。
groups.nuance_en: occupy: taking military or physical possession of an area (territory / building / zone) · colonise: settling among and establishing political-economic control over an indigenous area (land / territory / island) · settle: establishing permanent residential communities in a region (frontier / area / land) · annex: formally incorporating external territory into an existing sovereign state (territory / province / region) · subjugate: bringing a population entirely under armed dominion and servitude (population / nation / rebels) · populate: providing human inhabitants to fill a territory (region / continent / world)
groups.nuance_zh: occupy: 军事或物理占领控制 (territory / building / zone) · colonise: 移民定居并施加宗主统辖 (land / territory / island) · settle: 开拓建立永久居民点 (frontier / area / land) · annex: 吞并领土并入版图 (territory / province / region) · subjugate: 武力征服使之彻底臣服 (population / nation / rebels) · populate: 繁衍迁徙以充实人口 (region / continent / world)

groups.name: Offer & Tender · 给予与正式递交 (Tender, Proffer, Present)
groups.tip: 主动呈递或赋予他人

items.def_en: To formally give, submit, or hand over something to somebody at a ceremony or official encounter
items.ex_en: The ambassador presented her official credentials to the head of state during the ceremony.
items.ex_zh: 大使在仪式上向国家元首正式呈递了国书。

items.def_en: (chiefly UK) To submit a motion, proposal, or document formally for discussion at a meeting
items.ex_en: The member of parliament tabled a crucial amendment to the environmental bill yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 该议员昨天正式就这项环保法案提交了一份关键的修正提案。

items.def_en: To offer or impart a gesture such as hospitality, an invitation, or formal sympathy
items.ex_en: The university president extended a warm welcome to all international scholars at dinner.
items.ex_zh: 大学校长在晚宴上向所有国际学者表达了热烈的欢迎。
items.ex2_en: The scenic coastal hiking trail extends along the rocky cliffs for twenty miles.
items.ex2_zh: 这条风景优美的沿海远足步道沿着岩石悬崖延伸了二十英里。

items.def_en: To submit an official document, letter of resignation, or piece of work to an authority
items.ex_en: Employees must hand in their signed safety evaluation forms before the weekend begins.
items.ex_zh: 员工必须在周末到来之前上交签字确认的安全评估表格。

items.def_zh: 正式提出，呈递；投标；（法官等）裁定给予
items.def_en: 1. (formal) To offer or present something formally for acceptance. 2. (business) To make a formal offer to supply goods or do a job at a stated price.
items.ex_en: The minister formally tendered his immediate resignation following the severe public finance scandal.
items.ex_zh: 在严重的公共财政丑闻曝光后，部长正式呈递了立即生效的辞呈。

items.def_zh: 提供；端上；提出（建议/辞呈）
items.def_en: To hold out something to someone for acceptance, or to put forward advice or explanations courteously
items.ex_en: He graciously proffered a helpful explanation when the confused client asked for guidance.
items.ex_zh: 当困惑的客户寻求指导时，他彬彬有礼地提出了解释说明。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this formal transaction frame involve offering, presenting, or proffering an asset, payment, bid, or resignation for someone else's formal evaluation or acceptance. They emphasize formal protocol, deference, or contractual procedures.
groups.summary_zh: 指按照正式程序或以庄重态度呈递、提出财物、辞呈或建议以供接纳。
groups.desc_en: Formally extending a tangible item, proposal, or resignation for another party's consideration or acceptance, contrasting with unilateral imposition.
groups.desc_zh: 庄重、正式地递交物品、方案或辞呈以供对方考虑接纳，区别于单方强加。
groups.nuance_en: tender: formally submitting an official document, bid, or payment (resignation / bid / apology) · proffer: deferentially holding out an object, advice, or greeting (hand / advice / assistance) · present: ceremonially exhibiting or bestowing something (award / credentials / petition) · table: placing an idea or motion formally on the agenda (motion / bill / amendment) · extend: reaching outward to bestow a courtesy or offer (invitation / welcome / olive branch) · hand in: physically delivering an expected document up an authority hierarchy (resignation / notice / homework)
groups.nuance_zh: tender: 依正式程序提交款项、辞呈或标书 (resignation / bid / apology) · proffer: 恭敬伸出递送好意或物什 (hand / advice / assistance) · present: 庄重陈列呈递或授予 (award / credentials / petition) · table: 将方案提案摆上桌面审议 (motion / bill / amendment) · extend: 伸展给予礼节、善意或邀请 (invitation / welcome / olive branch) · hand in: 向上级或机构提交归还公文作业 (resignation / notice / homework)

groups.name: Official Scheduling & Allocation · 预定日程与指派敲定 (Slate, Timetable, Earmark)
groups.tip: 列入候选名单或既定日程

items.def_en: To arrange or plan that an event will take place at a particular designated time
items.ex_en: The committee scheduled the final project review for next Wednesday morning at ten.
items.ex_zh: 委员会将最终的项目审查安排在下周三上午十点举行。

items.def_en: To officially choose someone or something to hold a specific office or purpose
items.ex_en: The director designated two experienced engineers to oversee the installation of the network.
items.ex_zh: 主管指派了两位经验丰富的工程师来监督该网络系统的安装。

items.def_en: To make a tentative, provisional arrangement for a meeting or appointment
items.ex_en: Let's pencil in a quick follow-up meeting for next Tuesday afternoon just in case.
items.ex_zh: 我们先把简短的后续跟进会议暂定在下周二下午，以防万一。

items.def_en: To plan and set the definitive time and schedule of an operation or project
items.ex_en: The logistics team carefully timetabled every single flight to prevent severe airport runway congestion.
items.ex_zh: 物流团队周密排定了每个航班的时间表，以防止机场跑道严重拥堵。

items.def_zh: 预定，指定，把……列入计划；严厉批评
items.def_en: 1. (often passive, chiefly North American) to schedule, plan, or designate someone or something for a particular event or role. 2. (chiefly British) to criticize severely
items.ex_en: The city council has slated the historic downtown theater for demolition next autumn.
items.ex_zh: 市议会已预定于明年秋季拆除这座具有历史意义的市中心剧院。

items.def_en: (+ for) To designate or set aside funds, resources, or items for a specific predetermined purpose
items.ex_en: The state legislature earmarked twenty million dollars specifically for urban school infrastructure improvements.
items.ex_zh: 州立法机构专门划拨了两千万美元资金，专项用于改善城市学校基础设施。

groups.summary_en: This administrative frame denotes formally scheduling events, earmarking resources, or nominating candidates for future duties and roles. The verbs emphasize structured institutional planning, programmed arrangements, and prospective appointments.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重官方、行政或组织层面上对时间表、项目安排、资金用途或候选人的正式预订指派。
groups.desc_en: Assigning planned events, resources, or roles to explicit timeframes or operational buckets, contrasting with random ad-hoc execution.
groups.desc_zh: 将计划事项、资源或角色预排入明确的时间表或专项配置，区别于随机临时处置。
groups.nuance_en: schedule: setting an event to occur at a specific calendar date and time (meeting / flight / appointment) · slate: nominating or organizing someone/something for an upcoming milestone (release / trial / candidate) · earmark: designating funds or resources strictly for a predetermined purpose (funds / budget / land) · timetable: laying out a structured sequential schedule of activities (departure / reforms / events) · pencil in: tentatively reserving a preliminary date subject to change (date / lunch / meeting) · designate: officially assigning a title, purpose, or agent to a specific role (area / successor / site)
groups.nuance_zh: schedule: 编排指定具体日程与时间 (meeting / flight / appointment) · slate: 预定在某期推出或拟定候选 (release / trial / candidate) · earmark: 拨划留作特定专项用途 (funds / budget / land) · timetable: 制定分阶段的详细进度时刻表 (departure / reforms / events) · pencil in: 暂定草拟日期以便后续调整 (date / lunch / meeting) · designate: 正式指派特定代号、用途或人选 (area / successor / site)

groups.name: Operate & Run · 运转与操纵 (Operate, Run, Pilot)
groups.tip: 操控机械并保持其正常运转

items.def_en: to operate, handle, or manipulate a tool, machine, or lever
items.ex_en: The veteran mechanic carefully worked the emergency release lever to free the jam.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的机械师小心地扳动紧急释放手柄以排除卡阻。

items.def_en: to cause a machine to function or to manage the daily business of an organization
items.ex_en: They run the backup generator whenever the city suffers a sudden power outage.
items.ex_zh: 每当全城突发停电时，他们就会开动备用发电机。
items.ex2_en: The silent electric motor runs smoothly without generating any noticeable vibration or heat.
items.ex2_zh: 静音电动机运转平稳，不会产生任何明显的振动或热量。

items.def_zh: 运转，运行；操作，操控；经营；动手术
items.def_en: 1. To work, function, or control a machine or system. 2. To manage or run a business or organization. 3. (+ on) To perform surgery.
items.ex_en: Only certified technicians are authorized to operate this specialized medical imaging equipment safely.
items.ex_zh: 只有持证技术人员才有权安全操作这台专用的医学成像设备。
items.ex2_en: The automated banking network operates reliably throughout weekends and major holiday periods.
items.ex2_zh: 自动银行网络在周末和重大节假日期间均能稳定运行。

items.def_en: to manage, control, or operate a machine or vehicle with skill
items.ex_en: The test pilot handled the high-speed jet with exceptional precision and effortless control.
items.ex_zh: 试飞员以非凡的精准度和游刃有余的操控驾驭着这架高速喷气机。

items.def_zh: 驾驶；操纵（飞行器或船只）
items.def_en: to operate the controls of an aircraft, vessel, or complex vehicle
items.ex_en: She successfully piloted the massive cargo vessel through the narrow, treacherous river canal.
items.ex_zh: 她成功驾驶着那艘巨型货轮穿过了狭窄且危险的运河河道。

items.def_en: to direct and steer the course of an aircraft, ship, or vehicular system
items.ex_en: The experienced captain navigated the ship safely through the violent storm towards harbor.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的船长驾驶轮船安全穿过狂风暴雨，驶向港口。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame focus on an agent actively controlling, directing, or driving the mechanisms of machinery, vehicles, equipment, or business organizations.
groups.summary_zh: 指主体主动操纵设备、驾驶交通工具或掌管企业业务运营。
