items.def_en: To sew over the edge of one or two pieces of cloth to reinforce and bind the seam
items.ex_en: The tailor used silk thread to overlock the raw hemline of the dress.
items.ex_zh: 裁缝用丝线给连衣裙未收口的底边进行了锁边。

items.def_en: To join or decorate materials with needle and thread in continuous patterns
items.ex_en: Grandmother taught the children how to stitch delicate patterns onto cotton linen.
items.ex_zh: 祖母教孩子们如何在棉麻布上针缝出精致的图案。

items.def_zh: 缝合，用接缝连接；使出现裂纹（或皱纹）
items.def_en: 1. To join two edges of cloth, leather, or metal together with a seam. 2. To mark with lines or wrinkles.
items.ex_en: The leatherworker must seam these two thick hide sections together by hand.
items.ex_zh: 皮具工人必须手工将这两块厚厚的皮革部件缝合在一起。

items.def_en: To stitch together layers of fabric with a soft padding in between
items.ex_en: Artisans meticulously quilt the heavy winter blankets using traditional geometric stitching patterns.
items.ex_zh: 手艺人们运用传统的几何针法细致地缝制厚重的冬被。

items.def_en: To fold back and sew down the edge of a piece of cloth to prevent fraying
items.ex_en: She sat down quietly to hem the long curtains before hanging them.
items.ex_zh: 她静静地坐下来，先给长窗帘卷边，然后再把它们挂起来。

items.def_en: To sew pieces of cloth together with long, loose temporary stitches before final sewing
items.ex_en: The dressmaker decided to baste the delicate sleeves before machine stitching them.
items.ex_zh: 裁缝决定在用缝纫机车缝之前，先用针线把娇贵的袖子疏缝定位。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this tailoring and textile frame pertain to uniting pieces of fabric, leather, or sheet metal along their edges with continuous stitch lines or structural joins.
groups.summary_zh: 裁缝与装配场景，指沿织物、皮革或金属边缘缝合拼接形成接缝。
groups.desc_en: Specifies techniques of fastening textiles or edges together with needle and thread, contrasting with generic 'joining' or 'gluing' through fiber-specific structural stitching.
groups.desc_zh: 特指用针线将织物或边沿拼接缝合的工艺手法，与通用的'连接'或'胶合'不同，强调基于纤维的结构性车缝。
groups.nuance_en: stitch: basic continuous puncture and looping of thread (wound / fabric) · seam: joining two edges along a structural line (trousers / panels) · hem: folding and securing an outer raw edge (skirt / curtain) · overlock: reinforcing edges to prevent fraying (knitwear / seams) · baste: loose temporary tacking stitches (garment / quilt) · quilt: stitching layers together with padding (blanket / jacket)
groups.nuance_zh: stitch: 针线穿引缝合的基础动作 (wound / fabric) · seam: 沿缝合线拼接两片布料边缘 (trousers / panels) · hem: 折叠并缝固外边缘以防散边 (skirt / curtain) · overlock: 包缝/拷边防止布边抽丝 (knitwear / seams) · baste: 定型用的临时假缝 (garment / quilt) · quilt: 夹层绗缝固定棉絮 (blanket / jacket)

groups.name: Search & Probe · 探寻与摸索 (Fumble, Grope, Scrabble)
groups.tip: 摸索探试以获知内情

items.def_zh: 摸索寻找，探听；捕鱼，钓鱼
items.def_en: 1. (+ for/in) To try to find something by feeling around; to try to get information, compliments, or attention indirectly. 2. To catch or try to catch fish.
items.ex_en: He continued to fish in his deep coat pockets for the car keys.
items.ex_zh: 他继续在深邃的大衣口袋里摸索寻找车钥匙。

items.def_en: To search clumsily or awkwardly for something using one's fingers in a pocket, bag, or dark space
items.ex_en: She fumbled frantically in her handbag trying to locate the ringing mobile phone.
items.ex_zh: 她在手提包里慌乱地摸找，试图找出正在响铃的手机。

items.def_en: To search thoroughly through a collection of things by turning them over and moving them aside
items.ex_en: He had to root around in the messy drawer to find spare batteries.
items.ex_zh: 他不得不在杂乱的抽屉里到处翻寻，以找到备用电池。

items.def_en: To feel about blindly, hesitantly, or uncertainly with one's hands in search of something
items.ex_en: The lost traveler had to grope along the damp cave wall in darkness.
items.ex_zh: 迷路的旅行者不得不在黑暗中沿着潮湿的洞壁盲目摸索。

items.def_en: To scratch or grope around frantically and hurriedly with one's fingers to locate something
items.ex_en: Frantic passengers scrabbled through the debris to recover their dropped identification papers.
items.ex_zh: 慌乱的乘客在废墟瓦砾中扒寻，试图找回掉落的身份证件。

items.def_en: To search relentlessly until hidden items, elusive facts, or secrets are discovered
items.ex_en: Investigative journalists managed to ferret out the truth behind the clandestine transactions.
items.ex_zh: 调查记者们设法查获了这桩秘密交易背后的真相。

groups.summary_en: Refers to searching blindly, tactilely, or indirectly for an object or information without direct line of sight. 'Fish' highlights reaching into a receptacle or angling for an outcome, whereas 'grope' and 'fumble' emphasize uncoordinated or vision-impaired touch.
groups.summary_zh: 指在盲视或受限环境下凭触觉、试探摸索搜寻目标。
groups.desc_en: Denotes searching in an unguided, clumsy, or tactilely constrained manner, contrasting with systematic 'investigating' or open visual 'looking' through physical rummaging under low visibility.
groups.desc_zh: 指在视线受阻或狭小混乱空间内凭触觉笨拙、盲目地掏摸探寻，与系统性的'调查'或直观的'寻找'不同。
groups.nuance_en: grope: blind feeling about with outstretched hands (dark / wall) · fumble: clumsy, uncoordinated tactile searching (keys / pocket) · scrabble: frantic scratching or scrambling motion (dirt / pebbles) · root around: invasive digging and rummaging through cluttered items (drawer / purse) · ferret out: persistent unearthing of hidden information or items (secret / truth) · fish: reaching into a deep enclosure blindly (pocket / bag)
groups.nuance_zh: grope: 黑暗中盲目摸索 (dark / wall) · fumble: 笨拙失调地乱摸 (keys / pocket) · scrabble: 慌乱地抓挠扒拉 (dirt / pebbles) · root around: 在杂物中翻箱倒柜搜寻 (drawer / purse) · ferret out: 坚持不懈地搜寻出隐秘之物 (secret / truth) · fish: 把手伸入深处盲掏 (pocket / bag)

groups.name: Secure Custodial Release · 司法保释与暂释 (Parole, Remand, Spring)
groups.tip: 保释出狱或从束缚中解脱

items.def_zh: （非正式）捞人；助人越狱或迅速保释出狱
items.def_en: (informal) To help someone escape from jail or arrange for their sudden, successful release from custody
items.ex_en: A skilled defense lawyer managed to spring the suspect before midnight yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 一位老练的辩护律师昨晚午夜前设法把嫌疑人捞了出来。

items.def_zh: 保释出狱；（引申）施以财务救援
items.def_en: To secure the release of an arrested suspect by providing financial security to the court
items.ex_en: Her wealthy uncle agreed to bail out the reckless youth after his arrest.
items.ex_zh: 那位鲁莽的青年被捕后，他富有的叔叔同意出钱保释他。

items.def_zh: 释放；撤案释放（羁押人员）
items.def_en: To give official permission to an inmate or suspect to leave custody because charges are dropped or completed
items.ex_en: The magistrate decided to discharge the detained suspect due to lack of evidence.
items.ex_zh: 鉴于证据不足，地方法官决定撤案释放这名被拘留的嫌疑人。

items.def_zh: 保释（某人）；（用容器）舀水（出船舱）
items.def_en: (also 'bail out') To pay money to secure the temporary release of an accused person from custody before trial.
items.ex_en: The family gathered enough funds to bail the young man out of custody.
items.ex_zh: 这家人凑齐了足够的资金，将那名年轻男子保释出狱。

items.def_en: To officially forgive a crime and release someone from legal penalties or confinement
items.ex_en: The president decided to pardon the elderly whistleblower after decades of peaceful advocacy.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了数十年的和平呼吁后，总统决定赦免这位年迈的举报人。

items.def_en: To grant a prisoner early release from prison on the condition of good behavior under supervision
items.ex_en: The state board decided to parole the reformed offender after eight long years.
items.ex_zh: 经过漫长的八年，州假释委员会决定假释这名已经改过自新的罪犯。

groups.summary_en: This legal and custodial frame covers securing the release of an incarcerated, detained, or arrested person, often conditioned upon financial guarantees, supervision, or covert intervention. Terms vary from formal statutory procedures to informal prison slang.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及通过保释金、假释等司法程序或外部干预使羁押人员重获自由。
groups.desc_en: Encapsulates lawful or illicit release of an individual from penal or judicial confinement, contrasting with general 'freeing' or 'rescuing' by operating within legal procedures or extralegal jailbreaks.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖将人从刑事或司法羁押中通过程序合法释放或非法劫狱的场景，不同于通泛的'解救'，具有强烈的司法/监禁语境。
groups.nuance_en: bail: secure release before trial via monetary pledge (suspect / prisoner) · parole: conditional early release based on good behavior (inmate / convict) · pardon: executive absolution extinguishing penal consequences (offender / prisoner) · discharge: formal release upon completion of terms or dismissal (inmate / defendant) · spring: informal or illicit extraction from custody (jail / inmate)
groups.nuance_zh: bail: 缴纳保释金换取审前暂释 (suspect / prisoner) · parole: 服刑期间因良好表现获假释 (inmate / convict) · pardon: 行政长官特赦或免罪 (offender / prisoner) · discharge: 期满或诉讼终止后的正式释放 (inmate / defendant) · spring: 俚语中助人越狱或捞人脱罪 (jail / inmate)

groups.name: Seduce & Charm · 勾引与诱惑 (Seduce, Captivate, Bewitch)
groups.tip: 以甜言蜜语或魅力诱人入局

items.def_en: To please and attract someone by being pleasant, engaging, or courteous
items.ex_en: His pleasant demeanor and polite manners never failed to charm new clients.
items.ex_zh: 他宜人的举止和彬彬有礼的态度总能迷住新客户。

items.def_en: 1. To persuade someone to have sexual relations with you. 2. (+ into) To tempt or attract someone into doing something unwise or wrong.
items.ex_en: Clever marketing campaigns can easily seduce vulnerable shoppers into buying unnecessary luxury items.
items.ex_zh: 巧妙的营销活动很容易诱使缺乏抵抗力的消费者购买不必要的奢侈品。

items.def_en: To attract and hold someone's full attention or affection through exceptional charm or beauty
items.ex_en: Her mesmerizing vocal performance managed to captivate the entire concert hall audience.
items.ex_zh: 她那令人着迷的歌唱表演彻底吸引住了整个音乐厅的观众。

items.def_en: To powerfully attract or charm someone by an alluring appearance, charm, or offer
items.ex_en: Untold promises of imperial wealth allure daring explorers into the perilous wilderness.
items.ex_zh: 帝皇财富的无尽诱惑吸引着无畏的探险家们深入险象环生的荒野。

items.def_en: To fascinate, enchant, or captivate someone so strongly that they seem under a spell
items.ex_en: Her ethereal voice seemed to bewitch every traveler who wandered into the misty forest.
items.ex_zh: 她那空灵的嗓音似乎迷住了每一个漫步走进迷雾森林的旅人。

items.def_en: To charm, enchant, or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or insidious way
items.ex_en: The sorceress used false promises to beguile the young prince into surrendering his crown.
items.ex_zh: 女巫用虚假的诺言蛊惑了年轻的王子，使他交出了王冠。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on enticing someone into romance, physical intimacy, or unwise compromises through powerful charisma, flattering blandishments, or sensual allure. Nuances stretch from passionate attraction to cynical manipulation.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重以魅力、甜言蜜语或感官诱惑促使他人动情或做出违背原则之事。
groups.desc_en: Involves exercising an irresistible, often manipulative or erotic attraction over someone, going beyond pleasant 'pleasing' into overcoming resistance and clouding rational judgment.
groups.desc_zh: 施加难以抗拒、常带诱导性或情欲色彩的吸引力，超越普通的'讨喜'，强调瓦解对方理智与抵抗意志。
groups.nuance_en: seduce: enticement into sexual compliance or moral straying (lover / follower) · captivate: holding unyielding attention through sheer beauty or brilliance (audience / imagination) · bewitch: casting an almost magical, irrational enchantment (onlooker / soul) · charm: winning over via pleasing manners or personality (stranger / crowd) · allure: enticing by offering elusive promises or glamour (investor / prospect) · beguile: charming through deception or delightful diversion (victim / crowd)
groups.nuance_zh: seduce: 色诱或诱导违背原则 (lover / follower) · captivate: 凭魅力彻底抓牢注意力 (audience / imagination) · bewitch: 施加如着魔般的非理性迷惑 (onlooker / soul) · charm: 用讨喜的举止言谈博得好感 (stranger / crowd) · allure: 用诱惑力吸引诱导 (investor / prospect) · beguile: 巧妙蒙蔽或以趣事使人入迷 (victim / crowd)

groups.name: Seize & Snatch · 夺取与抢夺 (Grab, Snatch, Wrest)
groups.tip: 伸手迅猛夺走物品

items.def_en: To steal or seize something swiftly and casually, often when no one is watching
items.ex_en: Someone managed to swipe my unguarded phone while I was ordering coffee this morning.
items.ex_zh: 今天早上我点咖啡时，有人顺手牵羊偷走了我无人看管的手机。

items.def_en: To buy or obtain something eagerly and immediately as soon as it becomes available
items.ex_en: All front-row concert tickets were snapped up within seconds of going on sale.
items.ex_zh: 演唱会前排门票在开售几秒钟内便被一抢而空。

items.def_en: To take hold of something suddenly, roughly, or eagerly with one's hand
items.ex_en: Just grab your coat quickly so we do not miss the last evening train.
items.ex_zh: 赶紧抓上你的外套，这样我们才不会错过今晚的末班火车。

items.def_en: To take hold of something suddenly and firmly, often using official authority or force
items.ex_en: Federal agents moved swiftly to seize the illicit cargo before the cargo ship docked.
items.ex_zh: 联邦执法人员在该货轮靠岸前迅速行动，依法查封了违禁货物。

items.def_zh: 猛抢，一把夺过；抓紧时间做（如抢先获胜、抓紧休息）；绑架
items.def_en: 1. To take or grab something quickly, suddenly, or roughly. 2. To quickly seize a victory or opportunity, or get a brief period of rest. 3. (informal) To kidnap someone.
items.ex_en: The agile thief managed to snatch her diamond necklace and vanish into the crowd.
items.ex_zh: 那名敏捷的小偷一把抢走她的钻石项链，随即消失在人群中。

items.def_en: To forcibly pull or extract something from someone's grip or control with great effort
items.ex_en: The rebel commander sought to wrest political control from the failing monarch's hands.
items.ex_zh: 叛军指挥官企图从日薄西山的君主手中强行夺取政权。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to taking possession of an object or advantage abruptly, roughly, or by rapid opportunistic action. While some denote quick physical clutching, others emphasize forceful extraction or competitive usurpation.
groups.summary_zh: 强调以猝不及防、粗暴或投机的方式迅速夺取物品或控制权。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the sudden, forceful appropriation of physical or abstract objects, contrasting with consensual 'taking' or orderly 'receiving' through speed, aggression, and lack of consent.
groups.desc_zh: 指以猝不及防的暴力或速度强行占有物体或权利，与平和的'拿取'或'接收'相对，强调突发性与强制性。
groups.nuance_en: seize: forceful, decisive taking under legal power or brute force (assets / weapon) · snatch: sudden, quick jerk of taking before prevention (purse / victory) · grab: hurried, rough grasping with a hand (coat / opportunity) · wrest: wrenching away with violent twisting effort (control / power) · snap up: eagerly buying or taking scarce items instantly (tickets / bargains) · swipe: surreptitious filching or sweeping theft (wallet / candy)
groups.nuance_zh: seize: 依法强制查封或用力猛力夺取 (assets / weapon) · snatch: 猝不及防地飞手夺取 (purse / victory) · grab: 匆忙而粗鲁地一把抓住 (coat / opportunity) · wrest: 费力扭扯夺去控制权 (control / power) · snap up: 疯抢紧俏货品 (tickets / bargains) · swipe: 顺手牵羊顺走 (wallet / candy)

groups.name: Sell & Auction · 抽奖式与竞价拍卖销售 (Raffle, Auction, Liquidate)
groups.tip: 通过公开竞价或摸彩出售

items.def_en: To group goods into lots for sale by auction
items.ex_en: The auction house will lot the deceased collector's antique furniture for tomorrow's major sale.
items.ex_zh: 拍卖行将把已故收藏家的古董家具分批编组，供明日的大型拍卖会竞拍。

items.def_en: To sell something to the highest bidder at a public auction event
items.ex_en: The bankrupt company plans to auction off its fleet of luxury cars next week.
items.ex_zh: 这家破产公司计划下周将其拥有的豪华车队全数拍卖掉。

items.def_en: (+ to) To declare an item sold at auction by striking the gavel
items.ex_en: The old factory was knocked down to make way for a modern shopping center.
items.ex_zh: 旧工厂被拆除，为一座现代化的购物中心腾出了空间。

items.def_en: To bargain or haggle back and forth publicly regarding prices in a sale
items.ex_en: Merchants spent hours chaffering over woven silks in the bustling medieval market square.
items.ex_zh: 商人们在熙攘的中世纪集市广场上，为了几匹丝绸讨价还价数小时之久。

items.def_zh: 以抽奖方式送出或售出
items.def_en: To sell tickets to many buyers and distribute the item as a prize to the drawn winner
items.ex_en: The local charity decided to raffle off a signed guitar to raise emergency relief funds.
items.ex_zh: 当地慈善机构决定以抽奖方式送出一把签名吉他，以筹集紧急救灾资金。

items.def_zh: 拿……抽奖出售，以摸彩方式卖出
items.def_en: (also 'raffle off') To offer an item as a prize in a raffle, selling numbered tickets to determine the winner.
items.ex_en: The volunteer group will raffle two round-trip flight tickets during the annual spring gala.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者团体将在年度春季晚会上以摸彩售券方式送出两张往返机票。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers structured, public disposal mechanisms where goods are sold through competitive open bidding or randomized lot-drawing (raffles/lotteries), commonly seen in fund-raising, estate clearing, or clearance events.
groups.summary_zh: 通过公开竞拍或抽奖券机制转让、处置财物或奖品。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to structured, competitive, or chance-based mechanisms for commercial disposal, contrasting with fixed-price retail selling through competitive bidding or lottery mechanics.
groups.desc_zh: 通过结构化的竞价或射幸（抽彩）机制实现财产转让，与普通的标价零售相对，侧重竞标或凭运气销售。
groups.nuance_en: auction off: selling to the highest bidder in an open public sale (estate / art) · knock down: hammer striking to finalize an auction sale (painting / lot) · raffle off: distributing an item by selling numbered lottery tickets (car / hamper) · lot: grouping items into discrete batches for sale (antiques / shares) · chaffer: protracted haggling over price terms (goods / bargain)
groups.nuance_zh: auction off: 在公开竞价中价高者得卖出 (estate / art) · knock down: 拍卖师落槌成交 (painting / lot) · raffle off: 售彩抽奖式转让货品 (car / hamper) · lot: 把物品分批打包供竞拍 (antiques / shares) · chaffer: 琐碎地讨价还价 (goods / bargain)

groups.name: Sell & Vend · 出售与倒手 (Resell, Flip, Offload)
groups.tip: 面向公众转卖或向外兜售

items.def_en: To transfer ownership or clear out an asset by sale or formal settlement
items.ex_en: The board resolved to dispose of non-core properties to reduce the corporation's heavy debt.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定转让出清非核心资产，以减轻公司的沉重债务。

items.def_zh: 以旧折价换新；折价转让
items.def_en: To give a used product as partial payment when purchasing a replacement model
items.ex_en: I traded in my old sedan for a hybrid SUV.
items.ex_zh: 我把旧轿车折价置换了一辆混动SUV。

items.def_zh: 快买快卖；翻转倒卖（房产等）
items.def_en: To buy an asset, improve or hold it briefly, and quickly resell it for a quick profit
items.ex_en: Investors purchased the rundown apartment building, renovated it quickly, and flipped it for profit.
items.ex_zh: 投资者买下了那栋破旧的公寓楼，迅速翻修后转手倒卖以获取利润。
items.ex2_en: The speeding sports car suddenly flipped upside down after hitting the curb.
items.ex2_zh: 超速行驶的跑车撞到路缘石后突然翻了个底朝天。

items.def_en: To sell something, often fast, cheap, or by persuasive touting
items.ex_en: Desperate street vendors tried to flog counterfeit designer watches to passing tourists near the station.
items.ex_zh: 车站附近走投无路的街头小贩试图向路过的游客兜售仿冒名牌手表。

items.def_zh: 转售，倒手卖出，转手出售
items.def_en: To sell something that you previously purchased, especially for a profit.
items.ex_en: Scalpers often buy concert tickets in bulk and resell them online at inflated prices.
items.ex_zh: 黄牛经常大量购入演唱会门票，然后在网上以高价转手卖出。

items.def_en: To sell or dispose of surplus, unwanted, or risky goods or shares to another party
items.ex_en: The fund manager acted quickly to offload volatile tech stocks during the market downturn.
items.ex_zh: 在市场低迷期间，基金经理迅速行动，甩卖了波动剧烈的科技股。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame detail transferring previously purchased or held commodities, assets, or property to a downstream buyer, frequently driven by financial turnover, liquidation, secondary markets, or arbitrage.
groups.summary_zh: 转售、倒卖或处理已持有的商品、资产以回笼资金或获利。
groups.desc_en: Denotes disposing of, liquidating, or rapidly reselling secondary goods for quick liquidity or profit, contrasting with original primary-market 'selling' through opportunistic or unwanted turnover.
groups.desc_zh: 指处置二手、过剩或投机性商品以迅速变现或脱手，区别于源头正规零售，强调倒买倒卖或清仓处理。
groups.nuance_en: flip: buying and swiftly reselling for rapid capital gain (house / tickets) · resell: selling goods previously bought (merchandise / domain) · offload: dumping unwanted or burdensome stock or liabilities (inventory / assets) · flog: aggressively or cheaply selling off goods (wares / vehicle) · dispose of: getting rid of surplus or obsolete assets definitively (property / surplus) · trade in: surrendering a used item in part-payment for a new one (car / phone)
groups.nuance_zh: flip: 低买快卖赚取差价 (house / tickets) · resell: 倒手转售既得物品 (merchandise / domain) · offload: 甩卖积压或包袱资产 (inventory / assets) · flog: 兜售或廉价叫卖 (wares / vehicle) · dispose of: 最终处分或剥离闲置财产 (property / surplus) · trade in: 以旧换新折抵货款 (car / phone)

groups.name: Send & Dispatch · 发送与派遣 (Dispatch, Route, Forward)
groups.tip: 寄送物品或派发人员

items.def_en: To distribute or post large quantities of invitations, circulars, or signals
items.ex_en: The committee will send out formal invitations to all community members early next week.
items.ex_zh: 委员会将于下周初向所有社区成员散发正式邀请函。

items.def_en: To send commercial merchandise or cargo by postal service, freight, or sea
items.ex_en: The warehouse will ship your ordered electronics directly to your designated delivery address tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 仓库将于明天把您订购的电子产品直接寄送到您指定的收货地址。

items.def_en: To re-send or redirect mail, emails, or packages to a subsequent recipient
items.ex_en: Please forward the confidential financial report to the external auditor for immediate review.
items.ex_zh: 请将这份机密财务报告转发给外部审计师进行即时审查。

items.def_en: To send something along a planned pathway or course
items.ex_en: The logistics network will route incoming emergency supplies through regional hubs to maximize efficiency.
items.ex_zh: 物流网络将按既定路线经由区域枢纽分发运抵的应急物资，以最大化效率。

items.def_zh: 发送，寄出；派遣，打发；促使，使处于某种状态
items.def_en: 1. To arrange for something to be carried, delivered, or transmitted to a place. 2. To cause or order someone to go somewhere. 3. To cause someone or something to move or be in a particular state.
items.ex_en: I will send the finalized contractual agreement to your corporate email address this afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 我今天下午会把最终确定的合同协议发送到您的企业邮箱。

items.def_en: To send off someone or something promptly to a specific destination for a specific purpose
items.ex_en: The commander decided to dispatch two elite battalions to reinforce the vulnerable border outpost.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官决定调遣两个精锐营去增援脆弱的边境哨所。

groups.summary_en: Involves causing goods, messages, or personnel to be transported or delivered to an intended destination. Highlights differences in promptness, routing, and formality.
groups.summary_zh: 安排人员、物品或信息送达或派往指定地点。
groups.desc_en: Involves mobilizing, routing, and transmitting physical packages or formal communications to a designated destination, differing from mere 'giving' through logistical mediation and directed transit.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及通过物流或通信网络将货品或公文定向发往目的地，区别于普通的'交递'，突出物流路径与程序化派送。
groups.nuance_en: send: generic causative movement toward a recipient (message / parcel) · dispatch: prompt sending of agents, troops, or crucial mail for a task (courier / forces) · forward: redirecting received items to a subsequent destination (email / address) · route: directing traffic or consignments through a specific path (shipment / pipeline) · ship: transporting goods via commercial freight channels (cargo / product) · send out: circulating broadly or emitting from a hub (invitations / signals)
groups.nuance_zh: send: 最基础的向外寄送 (message / parcel) · dispatch: 迅速调遣人员或特快派送公文 (courier / forces) · forward: 将收到的邮件/信函转寄下家 (email / address) · route: 规划路径发送 (shipment / pipeline) · ship: 借助商业货运长途发运 (cargo / product) · send out: 批量散发或中枢发出 (invitations / signals)

groups.name: Sensory Overwhelm & Impairment · 感觉剥夺与感官损害 (Deafen, Blind, Stun)
groups.tip: 震聋耳朵等造成感官功能受损

items.def_en: To deprive a part of the body of sensation or make someone unable to feel physical sensations
items.ex_en: The harsh winter wind threatened to numb my exposed fingers within minutes of walking.
items.ex_zh: 凛冽的冬风吹得厉害，刚走几分钟就快要把我露在外面的手指冻麻木了。

items.def_en: To make someone unable to think clearly or react properly due to shock, blow, or glare
items.ex_en: The unexpected explosion caused enough concussive force to daze the guards at the gate.
items.ex_zh: 意外的爆炸产生了巨大的震波，使大门口的守卫瞬间发懵发恍。

items.def_en: To knock unconscious or semi-conscious, or overwhelm sensory faculties with shock or sound
items.ex_en: A sudden heavy blow across the helmet managed to stun the defending boxer completely.
items.ex_zh: 头盔上猝不及防的一记重击直接将防守的拳击手彻底打晕了。

items.def_en: To cause someone to lose their sight permanently, or temporarily through an intense flash of light
items.ex_en: The powerful camera flash seemed to blind him momentarily in the darkened lecture hall.
items.ex_zh: 在昏暗的演讲厅里，强烈的照相机闪光灯似乎瞬间让他眩目致盲。

items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To make someone unable to hear, either permanently or temporarily, due to an extremely loud noise.
items.ex_en: The continuous roaring of factory engines threatened to deafen the unprotected assembly line workers.
items.ex_zh: 工厂发动机持续不断的轰鸣声可能会震聋没有防护措施的流水线工人。

items.def_en: To cause a person or body part to completely lose the ability to move or feel
items.ex_en: The rare neurotoxin can paralyze respiratory muscles within hours if left entirely untreated.
items.ex_zh: 如果完全不予治疗，这种罕见的神经毒素可在数小时内使呼吸肌瘫痪。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on verbs denoting the temporary or permanent disabling of bodily senses or cognitive faculties through intense physical stimuli. They emphasize sensory shock ranging from transient daze to lasting physical incapacity.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过强烈的外部刺激造成感官功能受损、麻木或暂时丧失知觉。
groups.desc_en: Denotes extreme physical or psychological overload that disables faculties, differing from mere 'tiring' or 'distracting' by acute sensory deprivation or cognitive neutralization.
groups.desc_zh: 指强烈物理冲击或心理震荡使机体感官或意识暂时丧失机能，与普通的'疲倦'或'分心'相对，强调感官瘫痪或麻痹。
groups.nuance_en: deafen: overpowering hearing with excessive acoustic volume (explosion / noise) · blind: neutralizing vision via intense glare or injury (headlights / sand) · stun: rendering semiconscious or mentally paralyzed through sudden impact (blow / news) · daze: inducing bewildered, unsteady confusion (punch / shock) · numb: extinguishing sensation or emotional response (cold / grief) · paralyze: immobilizing motor or operational capability entirely (fear / venom)
groups.nuance_zh: deafen: 震耳欲聋破坏听觉 (explosion / noise) · blind: 强光眩目或刺瞎视觉 (headlights / sand) · stun: 猛击或惊讯使人神志发蒙 (blow / news) · daze: 击晕或使神志恍惚 (punch / shock) · numb: 物理致麻或情感麻木 (cold / grief) · paralyze: 致使肢体或运作完全瘫痪 (fear / venom)

groups.name: Serve & Dole Out · 盛出与施舍式分发 (Dish out, Spoon, Dole out)
groups.tip: 盛饭布菜式逐一分派

items.def_en: To provide food or drink to someone at a meal or table
items.ex_en: The waiters began to serve hot pumpkin soup to the guests at every table.
items.ex_zh: 侍者们开始向每张桌子旁的客人们端上热气腾腾的南瓜汤。

items.def_zh: 盛（饭菜），分发（食物）；（dish out）分发，分派（建议、惩罚等）
items.def_en: 1. (usually 'dish up / dish out') To serve or distribute food into dishes or onto plates. 2. ('dish out') To distribute or dispense something freely, such as advice, criticism, or punishment.
items.ex_en: She grabbed a ladle and began to dish hearty beef stew onto our plates.
items.ex_zh: 她拿起汤勺，开始往我们的盘子里盛丰盛的炖牛肉。

items.def_en: To distribute something, such as food or criticism, freely and often generously or indiscriminately
items.ex_en: The outspoken critic is always ready to dish out harsh assessments of modern architecture.
items.ex_zh: 这位直言不讳的评论家总是毫不吝啬地对现代建筑大加苛评。

items.def_en: To distribute something, usually money, food, or assistance, in small measured amounts
items.ex_en: The besieged garrison had to dole out their remaining grain supplies in meager rations.
items.ex_zh: 被围困的守军不得不将剩余的粮食微量分发，配给极其微薄。

items.def_en: To transfer food from a container to plates using a large spoon
items.ex_en: The chef helped spoon out the fragrant rice into individual serving bowls for dinner.
items.ex_zh: 厨师帮忙用大勺将香喷喷的米饭分盛到各个晚餐碗中。

items.def_en: To give things to each person in a group by hand
items.ex_en: Volunteers arrived early to hand out warm woolen blankets to homeless people downtown.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们早早赶来，向市中心的无家可归者分发温暖的羊毛毯。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict the physical, everyday act of distributing food onto plates, or colloquially distributing criticism, information, or handouts broadly and sometimes haphazardly.
groups.summary_zh: 指将食物盛到盘中分发，或引申为施舍、随意大量分发（常含口语色彩）。
groups.desc_en: Refers to portioning out food, punishments, or resources from a central reservoir, differing from neutral 'distributing' through explicit manual dishing or hierarchical paternalistic allocation.
groups.desc_zh: 指从中心容器中盛出或以家长式施舍态度分发饭食、财物或惩罚，区别于中立的'分发'，强调分舀动作或居高临下的分配。
groups.nuance_en: dish out: liberally or casually distributing portions, criticism, or punishment (advice / penalties) · dole out: measured, parsimonious distribution of meager supplies (rations / aid) · serve: formally offering food or drink to a diner (meal / wine) · spoon out: manual transfer using a concaved utensil (soup / sauce) · hand out: free direct distribution to an assembled crowd (leaflets / food)
groups.nuance_zh: dish out: 随性盛出或大肆给予批评/惩罚 (advice / penalties) · dole out: 节制且带施舍性质地微量配发 (rations / aid) · serve: 正式为客人端上餐饮 (meal / wine) · spoon out: 用勺子分舀流质 (soup / sauce) · hand out: 当面免费派发 (leaflets / food)

groups.name: Serve & Tend · 侍候与接待 (Wait on, Tend, Cater)
groups.tip: 担任侍应生端盘服务宾客

items.def_en: To serve food and drink to someone at a table, or attend to someone's personal needs
items.ex_en: Dedicated flight attendants continue to wait on first-class passengers throughout the long flight.
items.ex_zh: 尽职尽责的空乘人员在整个漫长的飞行过程中悉心服侍头等舱乘客。

items.def_en: To care for or manage something attentive to customer needs, especially in 'tend bar'
items.ex_en: He earned extra tuition money working night shifts to tend bar at a pub.
items.ex_zh: 他在一家酒吧上夜班调酒看台，以此赚取额外的学费。

items.def_en: To provide food and beverage services for events, or supply what is needed and wanted
items.ex_en: The local restaurant was contracted to cater the annual company gala this Saturday evening.
items.ex_zh: 这家当地餐馆获签合同，为本周六晚上的公司年度庆典承办酒席。

items.def_zh: 当女侍应生，当女服务员
items.def_en: To work as a waitress serving food and drinks in a restaurant or café.
items.ex_en: She decided to waitress at a seaside café during summer vacation to save money.
items.ex_zh: 她决定暑假期间在一家海滨咖啡馆当女服务员以攒钱。

items.def_en: To prepare and serve alcoholic drinks behind a bar in an establishment
items.ex_en: The hotel hired experienced staff who know how to bartend during busy festive banquets.
items.ex_zh: 这家酒店雇用了经验丰富、懂得在繁忙节日宴会期间熟练调酒的员工。

items.def_en: (+ to) To attend to someone's needs, health, comfort, or spiritual welfare
items.ex_en: Devoted nurses remained by the bedside to minister to the wounded soldiers throughout the night.
items.ex_zh: 尽职的护士们整夜守在病床边，细心照料受伤的士兵。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers attending to the physical needs of patrons or masters by serving food, drinks, or hospitality. Verbs emphasize institutional service or attentive personal pampering.
groups.summary_zh: 指在餐饮、旅宿或家庭环境中提供侍餐、照料与殷勤服务。
groups.desc_en: Involves attentive commercial or domestic attendance to personal needs and dining comforts, contrasting with transactional 'working' through direct hospitality servitude.
groups.desc_zh: 指在商业或私人家政场景中对客人的饮食与生活需求进行贴身照料与伺候，与通泛的'劳动'不同，强调款待与服侍。
groups.nuance_en: wait on: attending directly to someone's personal requests or dining orders (table / master) · tend: looking after the operational state of people or facilities (bar / sheep) · cater: supplying tailored culinary or logistical services to an event (banquet / wedding) · bartend: preparing drinks and managing tavern counters (pub / lounge) · minister: attending devotedly to spiritual or physical distress (needs / sick)
groups.nuance_zh: wait on: 端茶递水伺候用餐或需求 (table / master) · tend: 照看吧台或照护特定对象 (bar / sheep) · cater: 为宴会提供订制餐饮或迎合需求 (banquet / wedding) · bartend: 担任酒保调酒服务 (pub / lounge) · minister: 关切并照料疾苦或精神需求 (needs / sick)

groups.name: Servile Subservience & Deference · 卑屈俯首与奴颜屈从 (Kowtow, Truckle, Grovel)
groups.tip: 面对强权卑躬屈膝并服从

items.def_en: (+ before/to) To cower servilely and fawn obsequiously upon a superior
items.ex_en: The cowardly courtier would always cringe before the tyrannical ruler to protect his privileged position.
items.ex_zh: 那个懦弱的朝臣总是对暴虐的统治者卑躬屈膝，以保全自己的特权地位。

items.def_en: (+ to) To show extreme reverence, subservience, or uncritical submission to a master
items.ex_en: The captive subjects refused to bow down to the arrogant tyrant despite impending execution.
items.ex_zh: 尽管面临处决，被俘虏的臣民们仍拒绝向傲慢的暴君下跪屈服。

items.def_en: (+ to) To submit obsequiously and yield meekly to another's will
items.ex_en: A proud statesman should never truckle to foreign dictators merely to avoid political conflict.
items.ex_zh: 一位有尊严的政治家绝不该为了避免政治冲突而对外国独裁者俯首帖耳。

items.def_en: (+ to/before) To act in an obsequious or degrading manner to obtain forgiveness or favor
items.ex_en: He despised having to grovel before his ruthless landlord merely to request a lease extension.
items.ex_zh: 他极度鄙视自己为了请求延长租约而不得不向冷酷的房东低三下四。

items.def_zh: 卑躬屈膝，唯命是从；磕头
items.def_en: (+ to) (disapproving) to show excessive deference or submission to someone in power; (historical) to kneel and touch the ground with the forehead in worship or submission
items.ex_en: The corrupt official was prepared to kowtow to anyone who held superior political clout.
items.ex_zh: 这个贪官时刻准备着向任何拥有更大政治权势的人唯命是从、卑躬屈膝。

items.def_en: To behave sycophantically toward someone influential in hopes of personal advancement
items.ex_en: He tried to bootlick the managing director constantly in hopes of securing a quick promotion.
items.ex_zh: 他一味地向常务董事阿谀奉承，希望能迅速获得晋升。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe excessive, groveling, or humiliating subservience shown to a dominant person or power. They highlight extreme willingness to sacrifice self-respect or autonomy in order to curry favor or avoid punishment.
groups.summary_zh: 强调丧失自尊、讨好权贵的极度卑躬屈膝、盲从逢迎或奴隶式的屈服。
groups.desc_en: Expresses excessive, degrading deference or self-abasement to placate authority, contrasting with noble 'respecting' or professional 'obeying' through total forfeiture of dignity.
groups.desc_zh: 指为讨好权贵而极度自我贬低、卑躬屈膝的顺从行为，与体面的'尊重'或正常的'服从'相对，强调丧失尊严与奴颜媚骨。
groups.nuance_en: kowtow: humiliating subservience by yielding entirely to superior demands (regime / boss) · grovel: abject crawling or pleading for mercy or favor (feet / pardon) · truckle: yielding meekly under authority or bullying (demands / pressure) · cringe: involuntary or cowardly recoiling in fear and deference (master / blow) · bootlick: sycophantically flattering for cynical personal gain (superiors / officials) · bow down: ritualistic or total submission to higher power (idol / conqueror)
groups.nuance_zh: kowtow: 毫无底线地叩头屈从 (regime / boss) · grovel: 匍匐摇尾祈求宽恕 (feet / pardon) · truckle: 屈服于压力软弱顺从 (demands / pressure) · cringe: 畏怯退缩的奴才态 (master / blow) · bootlick: 阿谀奉承、舔权逢迎 (superiors / officials) · bow down: 彻底跪拜臣服 (idol / conqueror)

groups.name: Severing & Cleaving · 砍断与断绝 (Sever, Cleave, Sundering)
groups.tip: 彻底切断斩断使分离

items.def_en: To remove by cutting, or to completely interrupt access, supply lines, or personal contact
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: To chop or slice away a protruding part, branch, or limb with a single decisive stroke
items.ex_en: The gardener used heavy shears to lop off the withered branches from the oak.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用大剪刀咔嚓一下剁掉了橡树上的枯枝。

items.def_zh: 切断，割断；断绝（联系、关系）
items.def_en: 1. To cut completely through something so it separates into two parts. 2. To break off or completely end a relationship, connection, or diplomatic tie.
items.ex_en: The embattled nation decided to sever diplomatic ties with its hostile neighboring state yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 深陷困境的国家昨日决定断绝与其敌对邻国的外交关系。

items.def_en: To split or sever something cleanly and powerfully along a natural grain or plane with a heavy blade
items.ex_en: With one mighty swing of his battleaxe, the warrior managed to cleave the wooden shield.
items.ex_zh: 勇士挥起战斧奋力一劈，将木盾瞬间劈成了两半。
items.ex2_en: Dry pine logs cleave easily along their straight grain under the heavy axe.
items.ex2_zh: 干燥的松木原木在沉重的斧头下顺着笔直的纹理极易被劈开。

items.def_en: To surgically cut off a limb or digit, or figuratively lop off an essential component
items.ex_en: Surgeons were forced to amputate the crushed limb to prevent severe infection from spreading.
items.ex_zh: 为了防止严重感染扩散，外科医生不得不截除了那条被碾碎的肢体。

items.def_en: To forcefully tear or drive apart into separate pieces or divided factions
items.ex_en: A bitter ideological dispute threatened to sunder the ancient brotherhood into two warring camps.
items.ex_zh: 一场激烈的意识形态纷争眼看就要将这个古老的手足盟会撕裂为两个交战阵营。
items.ex2_en: The ancient political empire sundered into multiple small rival states after civil war.
items.ex2_zh: 内战之后，这个古老的政治帝国分裂成了多个相互敌对的弱小城邦。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote forceful, complete separation of a physical object into distinct parts with an edged tool or overwhelming force, frequently extended to absolute, irreversible termination of relationships, ties, or communications.
groups.summary_zh: 强调以利刃或猛力彻底斩断实体，或决绝切断关系、纽带与联系。
groups.desc_en: Involves the violent, permanent bisection or detachment of connected anatomical or structural bodies, differing from precise 'trimming' or 'cutting' through irreversible rupture.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过重力或锐器将相连的肢体或结构彻底、永久地斩断劈开，与轻微的'修剪'或普通'切割'相对，强调决绝与撕裂。
groups.nuance_en: sever: cutting completely through a limb, bond, or connection (ties / artery) · cleave: forcefully splitting along a grain or fissure with a heavy blade (skull / rock) · lop off: quickly and roughly chopping away a protruding part (branch / ear) · amputate: surgically removing an extremity by medical procedure (limb / leg) · sunder: violently tearing apart unified entities into fragments (alliances / kingdom) · cut off: interrupting continuity or physically isolating (retreat / supplies)
groups.nuance_zh: sever: 彻底切断纽带或肢体 (ties / artery) · cleave: 沿纹理劈开硬物 (skull / rock) · lop off: 随手咔嚓砍掉突出部分 (branch / ear) · amputate: 临床外科截肢 (limb / leg) · sunder: 暴力撕裂联合体 (alliances / kingdom) · cut off: 截断供给或退路 (retreat / supplies)

groups.name: Shed & Cast Off · 蜕变与脱落 (Slough, Shed, Moult, Cast off)
groups.tip: 自然脱去死皮或旧层

items.def_en: come off in strips or flakes from a surface, or strip away an outer layer
items.ex_en: After days under the harsh desert sun, sunburned skin began to peel off his shoulders.
items.ex_zh: 在沙漠烈日下暴晒数天后，他肩膀上被晒伤的皮肤开始大片脱皮。
items.ex2_en: The painter used a scraper to peel off old cracked paint from walls.
items.ex2_zh: 油漆工用刮刀把墙上开裂的旧油漆剥落下来。

items.def_en: lose or cast off hair, skin, leaves, or clothes naturally or intentionally
items.ex_en: Deciduous trees will shed their golden leaves as cold autumn temperatures begin to arrive.
items.ex_zh: 随着寒冷秋意的降临，落叶乔木纷纷褪落它们金黄色的树叶。

items.def_en: shed or remove the surface dead cells from skin in scales or flakes
items.ex_en: Dermatologists advise using a gentle facial scrub weekly to exfoliate dead surface cells safely.
items.ex_zh: 皮肤科医生建议每周使用温和的面部磨砂膏，以安全地去除表皮角质。
items.ex2_en: Flaky sunburned skin exfoliated naturally after several days of applying soothing aloe lotion.
items.ex2_zh: 涂抹了几天舒缓芦荟乳液后，脱皮晒伤的皮肤自然剥落了。

items.def_en: shed feathers, hair, or an outer cuticle periodically to make way for new growth
items.ex_en: Many avian species will moult their worn flight feathers before undertaking their long autumn migration.
items.ex_zh: 许多鸟类在开启漫长的秋季迁徙之前，都会蜕换掉磨损的飞羽。

items.def_en: rid oneself of something burdensome or shed an old protective layer
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: (often slough off) to shed dead skin or an outer layer naturally, or to get rid of something unwanted or unpleasant
items.ex_en: The patient's burned skin will gradually slough as new healthy tissue forms underneath.
items.ex_zh: 随着下方新生健康组织的形成，患者被烧伤的表皮将逐渐脱落。
items.ex2_en: The gentle chemical serum will slough dead cells without causing any skin irritation.
items.ex2_zh: 这种温和的化学精华液会脱落死皮细胞，而不会引起任何皮肤刺激。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe natural, biological shedding or intentional detachment of an outer layer—such as reptile skin, animal coats, dead human tissue, or outgrown beliefs. They denote shedding a husk to emerge renewed.
groups.summary_zh: 指表皮、毛发等自然蜕落，或引申为摆脱多余沉重旧物之状态改变。
groups.desc_en: Describes the organic or deliberate discarding of worn-out outer coverings, coatings, or burdens, differing from 'losing' or 'dropping' by natural exfoliation and cyclical renewal.
groups.desc_zh: 描述生物或机体周期性、有机地脱落老旧外层或卸除外物负担，不同于意外'遗失'，强调自然蜕皮与更新。
groups.nuance_en: shed: naturally dropping outer coats, moisture, or pounds (skin / leaves / tears) · slough: dead tissue or habit casting off progressively (skin / habits) · moult: periodic shedding of feathers, hair, or exoskeleton (feathers / coat) · exfoliate: peeling off outer layer in small scales or flakes (skin / rock) · cast off: intentionally discarding outworn burdens or anchors (chains / doubts) · peel off: removing a thin adherent surface layer (coating / sunburn)
groups.nuance_zh: shed: 自然掉毛、蜕皮或卸去重负 (skin / leaves / tears) · slough: 腐肉脱落或改掉恶习 (skin / habits) · moult: 鸟兽周期性换毛褪羽 (feathers / coat) · exfoliate: 表皮呈片状角质剥落 (skin / rock) · cast off: 坚决摆脱羁绊或枷锁 (chains / doubts) · peel off: 揭除附着表层 (coating / sunburn)

groups.name: Shelter & Hole Up · 隐蔽与据守 (Take Cover, Hole Up, Hunker Down)
groups.tip: 躲入地堡掩体以防遭受打击

items.def_en: To get behind or under a protective barrier to shield oneself from incoming danger
items.ex_en: Soldiers shouted for everyone to take cover immediately behind the thick concrete barrier.
items.ex_zh: 士兵们大声呼喊，让所有人立即隐蔽在厚实的水泥掩体后面。

items.def_en: To stay hidden or secluded in a safe, concealed place over a prolonged period
items.ex_en: The notorious fugitive managed to hole up inside an abandoned mountain cabin for weeks.
items.ex_zh: 这名臭名昭著的逃犯成功在深山的一间废弃木屋里藏匿了数周之久。

items.def_zh: 蹲守潜伏；原地避险待命
items.def_en: To settle in a safe, sheltered place and prepare to wait out an ongoing danger or storm
items.ex_en: Coastal residents decided to hunker down inside reinforced shelters until the raging hurricane passed.
items.ex_zh: 沿海居民决定在加固的避难所内原地蹲守避险，直到狂暴的飓风过去。

items.def_en: To dig defensive trenches and fortify one's position to resist assault
items.ex_en: The infantry unit dug in along the crest of the hill to withstand artillery.
items.ex_zh: 步兵分队沿着山脊掘壕据守，以抵御敌方的炮火袭击。

items.def_zh: 躲入地堡（掩体）；使（球）击入沙坑
items.def_en: (also 'bunker down') To take shelter in a safe, fortified place to protect oneself from an attack or disaster.
items.ex_en: Frightened villagers rushed to bunker down beneath the stone church as air sirens wailed.
items.ex_zh: 防空警报凄厉拉响，惊恐的村民们纷纷涌入石质教堂下方躲入掩体。

items.def_zh: 构筑壕沟据守；使固守防线
items.def_en: To establish oneself or troops firmly in defensive trenches or fortified positions
items.ex_en: The defending battalion worked through the stormy night to entrench their positions along the perimeter.
items.ex_zh: 防守营顶着风雨连夜构筑壕沟，沿着外围阵地严防固守。

groups.summary_en: This frame involves seeking refuge or holing up in fortified, entrenched, or safe locations to withstand an external threat, storm, or attack.
groups.summary_zh: 躲入坚固、封闭或安全据点以躲避外部危险、攻击或灾难。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to seeking fortified or concealed refuge to endure imminent danger or adversity, contrasting with active 'attacking' or open 'fleeing' through defensive immobility.
groups.desc_zh: 指进入坚固掩体或隐蔽所保持静止，以抵御恶劣环境或致命威胁，与主动'反击'或露天'逃窜'相对，侧重隐蔽据守。
groups.nuance_en: hole up: hiding away in a remote or confined sanctuary (cabin / outlaw) · hunker down: crouching low and stubbornly staying put during a crisis (storm / negotiations) · take cover: quickly sheltering behind protection from active fire or debris (bombing / rain) · bunker: retreating into heavily fortified deep defense (shelter / compound) · entrench: establishing well-fortified defensive positions or fixed beliefs (positions / troops) · dig in: preparing stubbornly for a prolonged siege (positions / heels)
groups.nuance_zh: hole up: 躲入封闭僻静处藏匿 (cabin / outlaw) · hunker down: 蹲伏据守以捱过危机 (storm / negotiations) · take cover: 规避战火或飞石就地隐蔽 (bombing / rain) · bunker: 撤入坚固掩体深处 (shelter / compound) · entrench: 挖掘壕沟固守或固执己见 (positions / troops) · dig in: 顽固坚守阵地准备持久消耗 (positions / heels)

groups.name: Shiver & Tremble · 战栗与发抖 (Shiver, Tremble, Quiver)
groups.tip: 因寒冷恐惧产生的肢体抖动

items.def_en: (+ with/from) To shake slightly and uncontrollably because you are cold, frightened, or excited.
items.ex_en: The shivering stray puppy began to shiver uncontrollably from the biting midnight frost.
items.ex_zh: 那只受冻的流浪小狗在午夜刺骨的寒霜中忍不住瑟瑟发抖。
items.ex2_en: The sudden loud explosion shivered the glass windows of nearby downtown shops.
items.ex2_zh: 突如其来的剧烈爆炸震碎了附近市区商店的玻璃窗。

items.def_en: to shake with a slight, rapid, often delicate movement from emotion or tension
items.ex_en: Her delicate lips began to quiver with unspoken sorrow upon hearing the tragic news.
items.ex_zh: 听到那个悲惨的噩耗，她纤柔的嘴唇因难以言表的悲伤而微微颤动。

items.def_en: (+ sb) Cause someone to tremble or feel deeply shocked and agitated
items.ex_en: The new CEO plans to shake up the entire management structure.
items.ex_zh: 新任首席执行官计划对整个管理架构进行大洗牌。

items.def_zh: 颤抖，战栗，发抖；摇晃，晃动
items.def_en: (+ with/at) To shake slightly and uncontrollably because you are cold, frightened, or emotionally excited; to shake slightly (of the ground or leaves).
items.ex_en: Her hands began to tremble with cold as the icy wind picked up.
items.ex_zh: 随着刺骨的寒风刮起，她的双手冷得发抖。

items.def_zh: （因恐惧、寒冷等）不寒而栗，战栗，发抖；（机器等）剧烈震颤
items.def_en: (+ at/with) To shake suddenly and violently because of fear, cold, or disgust; (of a vehicle or machine) to shake violently.
items.ex_en: He shuddered at the dreadful memory of the near-fatal car crash.
items.ex_zh: 想到那场险些丧命的车祸，他不禁不寒而栗。

items.def_en: to shake violently or continuously, especially from sheer terror or overwhelming shock
items.ex_en: The captured soldiers quaked before the merciless tyrant awaiting their sentence.
items.ex_zh: 被俘的士兵们在冷酷的暴君面前战栗，等待判决。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote involuntary, rapid, fine oscillatory movements of the body caused by cold, fear, weakness, excitement, or profound emotional shock. 'Shiver' is predominantly thermal, 'tremble' spans cold, terror, and physical frailty, while 'shudder' signals an intense, convulsive spasm.
groups.summary_zh: 指身体因寒冷、恐惧、虚弱或震骇而产生的不自主颤动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes involuntary oscillating bodily vibrations triggered by cold, fear, or profound excitement, differing from deliberate 'shaking' or mechanical 'vibrating' through physiological autonomic response.
groups.desc_zh: 指因寒冷、恐惧或剧烈情感诱发的不可自主控制的身体细微颤动，不同于外力'摇动'，属于自主神经应激反应。
groups.nuance_en: shiver: brief tremors caused typically by cold or sudden dread (cold / spine) · tremble: sustained quivering from strong emotion, weakness, or fear (hands / lips) · quiver: rapid, light vibration indicating suppressed intensity (voice / leaves) · shudder: sudden violent whole-body convulsion from revulsion or horror (horror / thought) · quake: deep, heavy trembling under violent instability (earth / boots) · shake up: emotionally unnerving someone deeply (confidence / team)
groups.nuance_zh: shiver: 因寒战或突来战栗打哆嗦 (cold / spine) · tremble: 情绪激动或衰弱导致持续颤抖 (hands / lips) · quiver: 压抑情感时的轻微颤动 (voice / leaves) · shudder: 因极度厌恶或恐惧而全身猛烈一颤 (horror / thought) · quake: 惊恐万状或天崩地裂般震颤 (earth / boots) · shake up: 心理上深受震动扰乱 (confidence / team)

groups.name: Shoulder & Bear · 承担与背负 (Shoulder, Bear, Assume)
groups.tip: 主动挑起重担或负责

items.def_en: To bravely endure, support, or carry a heavy burden, sorrow, cost, or responsibility
items.ex_en: The eldest brother had to bear the financial burden of the family.
items.ex_zh: 作为长兄，他不得不独自承担家庭的经济负担。

items.def_en: To take on a position, power, or responsibility formally and officially
items.ex_en: She will officially assume the duties of prime minister starting next Monday.
items.ex_zh: 她将于下周一正式履行首相职务。

items.def_zh: 担负，承担（责任、费用等）；用肩推挤
items.def_en: 1. To accept or take on responsibility, blame, or burden. 2. To push or move past someone using your shoulders.
items.ex_en: The young manager chose to shoulder the responsibility for the failed product launch.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的经理选择为这次失败的产品发布承担责任。

items.def_en: To take in or pay for costs, losses, or shocks without letting them cause breakdown elsewhere
items.ex_en: The local government agreed to absorb the unforeseen costs of the repairs.
items.ex_zh: 当地政府同意承担维修中产生的意外费用。

items.def_en: To accept a new challenge, heavy duty, or commitment of personal effort
items.ex_en: She decided to take on the daunting task of reorganizing the department.
items.ex_zh: 她决定接下重组该部门这项艰巨的任务。

items.def_en: To accept the blame or responsibility for something that goes wrong, especially when others are at fault
items.ex_en: The junior clerk had to carry the can for his boss's mistake.
items.ex_zh: 初级文员不得不替他老板的过失背黑锅。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey accepting, sustaining, or managing heavy obligations, psychological burdens, fiscal debts, or moral liability over time.
groups.summary_zh: 表示自愿接纳或不得不支撑起重任、罪责与经济压力。
groups.desc_en: Involves accepting, carrying, and enduring the weight of liabilities, costs, or ethical blame, differing from voluntary 'embracing' through the somatic metaphor of carrying an onerous load.
groups.desc_zh: 借用肉体挑担负重的意象，指接受并承受债务、责任或过失的重压，区别于欣然'接受'，强调负重与承载。
groups.nuance_en: shoulder: deliberately carrying heavy burdens or blame upon oneself (responsibility / cost) · bear: withstanding grueling hardship, costs, or pain over time (burden / loss) · assume: taking on formal duties, risks, or titles (office / risk) · absorb: soaking up impacts, debts, or shocks internally (losses / shocks) · carry the can: taking the full blame unfairly for collective failures (mess / fault) · take on: agreeing to handle a challenging commitment (task / client)
groups.nuance_zh: shoulder: 挺身挑起重任或过责 (responsibility / cost) · bear: 长期忍受苦难、损失或重负 (burden / loss) · assume: 依职权履新承担风险与责任 (office / risk) · absorb: 自行消化吸收损失或冲击 (losses / shocks) · carry the can: 替集体过失背黑锅 (mess / fault) · take on: 承揽接手棘手任务 (task / client)

groups.name: Shroud & Cloak · 笼罩与裹覆 (Shroud, Cloak, Enfold)
groups.tip: 覆于表面以遮蔽或保护

items.def_en: To cover someone or something securely in paper, cloth, or warm garments
items.ex_en: Let's wrap up this meeting so everyone can catch their flights.
items.ex_zh: 我们结束这次会议吧，这样大家都能赶上航班。

items.def_en: To dress in or cover with a mantle, or to hide and conceal something intentionally
items.ex_en: Dense autumn fog rose to cloak the entire valley in complete obscurity.
items.ex_zh: 浓密的秋雾升起，遮蔽了整座山谷。

items.def_zh: 覆盖，罩住；（脸上）泛起红晕
items.def_en: 1. (literary) To cover or envelop a surface like a cloak. 2. (literary) (of a blush) To spread over the face.
items.ex_en: Fresh, untrodden snow mantled the quiet hillside beneath the pale moonlight.
items.ex_zh: 未被踩踏的新雪在苍白的月色下覆盖着寂静的山坡。

items.def_en: To wrap, bind, or swaddle someone or something completely in bands of fabric or fog
items.ex_en: Choking layers of grey smog swathes the sprawling city every dry winter.
items.ex_zh: 每个干燥的冬天，令人窒息的灰暗雾霾都会笼罩这座庞大的城市。

items.def_en: To surround, wrap, or clasp closely within drapery, arms, or darkness
items.ex_en: The darkness of the ancient forest enfolds the solitary traveler in silence.
items.ex_zh: 古老森林的浓黑将这名孤身旅人无声地包围起来。

items.def_en: To cover, envelop, or obscure from view as if with a funerary cloth or dense mist
items.ex_en: Heavy grey mist shrouds the jagged peaks of the forgotten mountain range.
items.ex_zh: 沉重的灰雾笼罩着这座被遗忘的山脉犬牙交错的山峰。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame depict physically or metaphorically enveloping an object or person tightly within a covering, garment, or layer of fog/darkness, emphasizing enclosure, concealment, or solemn protection.
groups.summary_zh: 指像斗篷或帷幔般紧紧包裹、遮蔽或笼罩。
groups.desc_en: Denotes completely enveloping, wrapping, or veiling an entity in a protective or obscuring covering, contrasting with simple covering ('cover') by emphasizing obscurity, enclosure, or atmospheric mystery.
groups.desc_zh: 指用织物、遮蔽物或气象完全包裹或笼罩某物，与一般的“遮盖 (cover)”相比，强调隐匿性、全封闭包覆或神秘肃穆的氛围感。
groups.nuance_en: shroud: to obscure or screen from sight, often somberly (mystery / body / mountain) · cloak: to deliberately conceal or mask the true nature (intentions / secrecy / darkness) · swathe: to wrap entirely in overlapping bands or layers (bandage / mist / fabric) · enfold: to lovingly or gently wrap around within (arms / darkness / embrace) · mantle: to blanket with a thick spreading layer (snow / dusk / smoke)
groups.nuance_zh: shroud: 笼罩隐蔽，常带阴郁神秘感 (mystery / body / mountain) · cloak: 刻意伪装或遮掩真相 (intentions / secrecy / darkness) · swathe: 用层层布幔或带状物缠裹裹严 (bandage / mist / fabric) · enfold: 慈爱或温柔地拥入怀中包覆 (arms / darkness / embrace) · mantle: 厚厚地覆盖蔓延 (snow / dusk / smoke)

groups.name: Sideline & Marginalize · 边缘化与排挤 (Sideline, Marginalize, Shunt Aside)
groups.tip: 将对手冷落排挤到边缘地带

items.def_en: To take up so much space, attention, or resource that someone or something else is pushed aside
items.ex_en: Heavy government borrowing threatened to crowd out private investment in local industries.
items.ex_zh: 政府的大举借贷可能会排挤当地工业领域的私人投资。

items.def_en: To push someone out of a position, job, or opportunity through aggressive competition
items.ex_en: The ruthless newcomer managed to elbow out his rival for the promotion.
items.ex_zh: 那个手段狠辣的新人设法挤掉了竞争对手，赢得了晋升。

items.def_en: To move someone to a less prominent or unimportant post to avoid dealing with them directly
items.ex_en: The outspoken director was swiftly shunted aside to a harmless advisory committee.
items.ex_zh: 这位心直口快的总监迅速被边缘化，调到了无足轻重的顾问委员会。

items.raw_cluster: 排挤与边缘化 Marginalize & Sideline
items.def_zh: 使边缘化，排挤；使退出比赛（因伤等）
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To prevent someone from participating in an activity or playing a major role; to marginalize. 2. To remove a player from a team or game, especially due to injury.
items.ex_en: A sudden knee injury sidelined the star striker for the championship match.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的膝伤让这名主力前锋无法参加冠军决赛。

items.def_en: To treat a person, group, or concept as insignificant or peripheral to society or power
items.ex_en: The proposed economic policy risks marginalizing low-income families even further.
items.ex_zh: 拟议中的经济政策可能会让低收入家庭更加被社会边缘化。

items.def_en: To deliberately prevent someone from being involved in a group by being cold or uncooperative
items.ex_en: The senior partners tried to freeze out the new associate during meetings.
items.ex_zh: 高级合伙人们在会议期间试图孤立并排挤那位新来的律师。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses manipulative or political actions that diminish a person or group's influence by pushing them away from decision-making or public attention without formal dismissal.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过政治或组织手段将人排挤出核心决策圈、置于边缘位置。
groups.desc_en: Involves actively pushing an individual, group, or issue out of the center of power, attention, or activity to a periphery, contrasting with neutral omission by stressing aggressive or systematic displacement.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动将人、团体或议题排挤出权力、决策或注意力的中心，与中性的“忽略”相比，强调具有竞争性、排他性或体制性的边缘化推挤。
groups.nuance_en: sideline: to remove from active participation or play (rival / minister / issue) · marginalize: to push socially or politically to an inconsequential status (minority / community / voice) · elbow out: to aggressively or ruthlessly shove aside for space (competitor / incumbent / peer) · crowd out: to displace by taking up finite space, capital, or attention (investment / competitors / private sector) · freeze out: to exclude coldly through concerted social or economic hostility (partner / newcomer / dissenter)
groups.nuance_zh: sideline: 排除在关键行动或赛场之外 (rival / minister / issue) · marginalize: 在社会或政治上使边缘化、无权化 (minority / community / voice) · elbow out: 用手肘硬挤掉、粗暴排挤 (competitor / incumbent / peer) · crowd out: 因占据有限资源或空间而挤出 (investment / competitors / private sector) · freeze out: 通过冷漠或联合抵制冷落排挤 (partner / newcomer / dissenter)

groups.name: Sift & Winnow · 筛选与扬弃 (Sift, Cull, Riddle)
groups.tip: 迎风扬谷吹去糠秕留谷粒

items.def_en: To examine a collection of things carefully to organize them or remove unwanted items
items.ex_en: She spent hours sorting through boxes of old family photographs.
items.ex_zh: 她花了数小时翻检那几箱老家庭照片。

items.def_en: (+ from) To divide distinct components or isolate one material from another
items.ex_en: The specialized machine will separate the pure grain from the outer husks.
items.ex_zh: 这台专用机器会将纯净的谷粒与外层的稻壳分离。
items.ex2_en: The heavy oil and fresh water separated naturally inside the glass container.
items.ex2_zh: 稠密的油和清水在玻璃容器内自然分层分开了。

items.def_en: (often + through) To pass a substance through a sieve, or examine a mass of data closely to isolate essentials
items.ex_en: Detectives spent countless hours to sift through thousands of confidential surveillance files.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们花费了无数个小时，仔细查阅了成千上万份机密监控文件。

items.def_en: To separate large pieces from fine earth, sand, or gravel using a coarse mesh riddle
items.ex_en: The laborers riddles coarse river gravel to prepare fine construction sand.
items.ex_zh: 劳工们用粗筛筛分粗河卵石，以制备细致的建筑沙。

items.def_zh: 扬去（谷糠），簸（谷）；筛选，甄别挑出
items.def_en: To blow air through grain to separate chaff from seeds, or to narrow down a group by removing less desirable elements.
items.ex_en: Traditional farmers winnow wheat by tossing it high into the autumn breeze.
items.ex_zh: 传统农夫将小麦高高抛向秋风中以扬去谷糠。

items.def_en: To reduce population size by removing inferior animals, or select specific items from a pool
items.ex_en: Wildlife rangers were forced to cull the overpopulated deer herd this winter.
items.ex_zh: 野生动物巡护员今年冬天被迫对数量过剩的鹿群进行选择性猎捕。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses separating finer particles from coarse chaff physically, or figuratively refining a large volume of choices, evidence, or people to extract only the most valuable remnants.
groups.summary_zh: 指物理上的过筛除杂，或比喻性地细致剔除糟粕以保留精粹。
groups.desc_en: Denotes systematically passing a mixture through a separation process to isolate valuable or desired elements from debris, contrasting with casual picking by emphasizing fine-grained analysis or elimination.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过分级、筛选或去劣存优的方法把混乱混合物分解，与随意的“挑选”相比，强调细致审查、层层过滤或淘汰机制。
groups.nuance_en: sift: to pass through a sieve or thoroughly examine details for truth (evidence / records / flour) · winnow: to separate the useful from the useless by blowing or filtering (applicants / field / options) · cull: to select and remove inferior, excess, or doomed items (herd / population / data) · riddle: to screen coarse gravel or penetrate with holes/flaws (gravel / bullets / errors) · sort through: to methodically inspect an unorganized heap (papers / belongings / emails)
groups.nuance_zh: sift: 细致筛查、详加推敲 (evidence / records / flour) · winnow: 汰劣留良、层层甄别 (applicants / field / options) · cull: 剔除残弱、选择性杀灭或剔除 (herd / population / data) · riddle: 用粗筛网过滤或使布满孔洞缺陷 (gravel / bullets / errors) · sort through: 在翻找中逐一理清分类 (papers / belongings / emails)

groups.name: Sign & Execute Agreements · 签署与订立 (Sign, Ink, Ratify, Enter Into)
groups.tip: 签署协议达成正式合约

items.def_en: To write one's name on a document or contract to make it official or legally binding
items.ex_en: Both parties gathered in the boardroom to sign the five-year lease.
items.ex_zh: 双方在会议室齐聚，正式签署了为期五年的租赁合同。

items.def_zh: 正式签署并生效（法律文件）
items.def_en: To complete all legal formalities required to make a contract or deed valid, especially by signing
items.ex_en: The attorneys will execute the property deed once all signatures are gathered.
items.ex_zh: 在收齐所有签名后，律师们将使该房产契约正式签署生效。

items.def_en: To give official approval to an agreement, plan, or document by signing or formally agreeing
items.ex_en: The finance director refused to sign off on the extravagant travel expenses.
items.ex_zh: 财务总监拒绝在那份开销过大的差旅费报销单上签字批准。

items.def_en: To formally bind oneself to a contract, agreement, or institutional partnership
items.ex_en: Both nations decided to enter into a comprehensive bilateral trade partnership agreement.
items.ex_zh: 两国决定正式缔结一项全面的双边贸易伙伴关系协议。

items.def_zh: 正式签署（合同或协议）；给……涂墨水
items.def_en: 1. (informal) To sign a formal contract or agreement. 2. To apply ink to a surface or printing block.
items.ex_en: The superstar finally inked a lucrative sponsorship deal with the sportswear company.
items.ex_zh: 这位巨星终于与那家运动服装公司正式签下了一份丰厚的代言合同。

items.def_en: To make a formal agreement, treaty, or amendment officially valid by giving government or organizational sanction
items.ex_en: The national parliament voted overwhelmingly to ratify the landmark international peace treaty.
items.ex_zh: 国家议会以压倒性多数投票批准了这项里程碑式的国际和平条约。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe formalizing legally binding pacts, commercial deals, or official documents by signature or procedural execution. They range from neutral administrative actions to journalistic idioms and high-level diplomatic ratification.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖签署、达成及核准具约束力契约或协议的动词与短语，兼具商务与外交色彩。
groups.desc_en: Denotes formally finalizing and legally binding a contract, treaty, or formal pact, contrasting with informal agreement by stressing binding legal rituals and commitments.
groups.desc_zh: 指正式签署、缔结并使条约或商业合同发生法律效力，与一般的“口头同意”相比，强调法定约束力与程序完备性。
groups.nuance_en: sign: general affixing of a signature to create an agreement (contract / lease / agreement) · execute: to perform all formalities necessary to render a contract legally binding (deed / document / contract) · ink: journalistic term for finalizing and signing a deal (deal / contract / pact) · ratify: to formally sanction or confirm through a governing authority (treaty / amendment / convention) · enter into: to formally initiate and commit to a mutual relationship (agreement / partnership / negotiations)
groups.nuance_zh: sign: 普遍的签字画押以成立协议 (contract / lease / agreement) · execute: 完成所有法定签署程序使合同生效 (deed / document / contract) · ink: 新闻用语，敲定并签署协议 (deal / contract / pact) · ratify: 由立法机关或权力机构正式批准追认 (treaty / amendment / convention) · enter into: 正式订立并加入契约/关系 (agreement / partnership / negotiations)

groups.name: Sign & Validate · 签署与草签 (Endorse, Countersign, Ink)
groups.tip: 在文件上署名或签署姓名首字母

items.def_en: To write one's name on a formal document to authenticate it or express agreement
items.ex_en: Please sign your name on the dotted line at the bottom.
items.ex_zh: 请在底部的虚线上签上您的名字。

items.def_zh: 草签，在……上签署姓名首字母
items.def_en: To mark, sign, or approve a document with the first letters of one's names.
items.ex_en: The client must initial each amended clause on every contract page.
items.ex_zh: 客户必须在合同每一页的各项修改条款旁草签姓名首字母。

items.def_en: To add a secondary signature to a document previously signed by another party to confirm authenticity
items.ex_en: The bank manager must countersign the check before funds can be released.
items.ex_zh: 在发放资金之前，银行经理必须在此支票上会同副署。

items.def_en: To give official written approval or final authorization to a plan or document
items.ex_en: The city council needs to sign off on the architectural master plan.
items.ex_zh: 市议会需要对该建筑总体规划方案签字批准。

items.def_en: To sign the back of a check or legal paper, or formally give public approval to a policy
items.ex_en: The committee voted unanimously to endorse the senator's progressive tax reform proposal.
items.ex_zh: 委员会一致投票公开支持参议员提出的累进税改革方案。

items.def_en: (informal/journalistic) To formally sign and execute a deal, contract, or treaty
items.ex_en: The studio managed to ink a multimillion-dollar distribution deal this morning.
items.ex_zh: 该制片厂今天上午成功签署了一份价值数百万美元的发行协议。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate adding signatures, marks, or initials to official instruments, contracts, or draft treaties to indicate review, formal consent, or legal validity.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过在文件上草签、签署或批注来确认审阅并赋予正式效力。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the specific procedural action of marking, signing, or counter-signing a document to authenticate, endorse, or approve it, contrasting with broad agreement by focusing on the validating mark itself.
groups.desc_zh: 指在文件上做标记、草签、副署或背书以证明其真实性或予以核准的程序性动作，着眼于核验标记的行为本身。
groups.nuance_en: initial: to mark with initials for provisional approval or page confirmation (clause / document / changes) · countersign: to add a secondary signature confirming validity (passport / cheque / order) · endorse: to sign the back of a negotiable instrument or formally approve (cheque / policy / candidate) · sign off on: to grant explicit final managerial or technical approval (budget / design / project) · ink: to put ink to paper to ratify a specific instrument (pact / extension / accord)
groups.nuance_zh: initial: 签署姓名首字母以草签或逐页确认 (clause / document / changes) · countersign: 会签、副署以复合验证真实性 (passport / cheque / order) · endorse: 票据背书或公开背书支持 (cheque / policy / candidate) · sign off on: 领导或专家审查后签字放行认可 (budget / design / project) · ink: 落笔成文式签署 (pact / extension / accord)

groups.name: Silence & Hush · 制止作声与使安静 (Silence, Hush, Muzzle)
groups.tip: 发出嘘声示意安静以制止喧哗

items.def_en: To cause a person, crowd, or controversy to calm down and become quiet
items.ex_en: The speaker raised her hand to quiet the increasingly restless crowd.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者举起手，让愈发骚动的群众安静下来。
items.ex2_en: The noisy classroom quieted immediately when the strict principal stepped into the room.
items.ex2_zh: 严厉的校长一走进房间，吵闹的教室立刻安静了下来。

items.def_en: To make someone quiet, calm, or cease making sounds, often gently
items.ex_en: The mother gently hushed her crying infant with a tender lullaby.
items.ex_zh: 母亲用一首轻柔的摇篮曲温柔地哄安静了啼哭的婴儿。
items.ex2_en: The noisy theater hushed instantly as the main lights dimmed for showtime.
items.ex2_zh: 演出即将开始主灯熄灭时，喧闹的剧院瞬间安静了下来。

items.raw_cluster: 制止与使沉默 Silence & Hush
items.def_zh: （发嘘声）让……安静，使噤声；发出嘘声
items.def_en: To tell someone to be quiet, especially by saying 'shush' or making a similar sound.
items.ex_en: The librarian quickly shushed the noisy students studying in the reading room.
items.ex_zh: 图书管理员赶紧发声让阅览室里喧闹的学生安静下来。

items.def_en: To stop talking or become quieter, often in response to an order
items.ex_en: The teacher told the unruly boys to pipe down during class.
items.ex_zh: 老师厉声让那些不服管教的男生在上课时闭嘴安静。

items.def_en: To prevent someone from speaking, shouting, expressing opinions, or making noise
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime tried to silence all critical voices in the press.
items.ex_zh: 该专制政权企图压制新闻界的所有批评声音。

items.def_en: To prevent an individual or press from speaking or publishing freely
items.ex_en: The newly passed law effectively muzzles independent journalists investigating government corruption.
items.ex_zh: 新通过的法律实际上封锁了调查政府腐败的独立记者的言论。

groups.summary_en: Addresses suppressing vocal noise, speech, or dissent. Stretches from gentle conversational soothing to institutional suppression, gagging, or political muzzling.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过发声规劝、安抚或强硬手段制止发声、压制异议使其安静。
groups.desc_en: Denotes compelling or inducing quiet by suppressing sound, speech, or dissent, contrasting with spontaneous quietness by highlighting an imposed, external cessation of noise.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过施加外力或指令迫使他人闭嘴或环境安静，与自发的“沉默”相比，强调施加控制、压制异见或平息杂音。
groups.nuance_en: silence: to forcibly or completely extinguish speech, sound, or opposition (critics / guns / opposition) · hush: to soothe or quieten with gentle restraint or secrecy (crowd / scandal / baby) · muzzle: to gag or suppress freedom of expression through power (press / watchdog / whistleblowers) · shush: to tell someone to be quiet, usually with a 'sh' sound (child / audience / talker) · quiet: to calm, abate, or lower the level of disturbance (nerves / rumors / room)
groups.nuance_zh: silence: 彻底压制、使消音或封口 (critics / guns / opposition) · hush: 安抚使之肃静或刻意掩盖丑闻 (crowd / scandal / baby) · muzzle: 给……戴上口套、强行剥夺言论自由 (press / watchdog / whistleblowers) · shush: 嘘声制止喧哗 (child / audience / talker) · quiet: 使平静、压低喧闹或疑虑 (nerves / rumors / room)

groups.name: Simplify & Clarify · 简化与澄清 (Simplify, Distill, Clarify, Demystify)
groups.tip: 剔除繁复使其清晰明了

items.def_zh: 剔除冗余，剥离至最简形式
items.def_en: To remove all non-essential parts, features, or elaborations so that only the fundamental core remains
items.ex_en: The developer chose to strip down the software to its essential code.
items.ex_zh: 开发者选择将该软件剥离冗余，仅保留其核心代码。

items.def_zh: 通俗化，降低门槛（常带贬义）
items.def_en: To simplify academic or intellectual material to an exaggerated degree so anyone can grasp it, often losing nuance
items.ex_en: Critics argued the network chose to dumb down the documentary for ratings.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士认为，电视台为了收视率故意将这部纪录片通俗庸俗化。
items.ex2_en: College textbooks inevitably dumb down when commercial publishers prioritize mass appeal over depth.
items.ex2_zh: 当商业出版商将大众吸引力置于深度之上时，大学教科书不可避免地走向浅薄化。

items.def_en: To make a statement, idea, or situation clearer and easier to understand by removing ambiguity
items.ex_en: The spokesperson held a press conference to clarify their misunderstood official policy.
items.ex_zh: 发言人召开了新闻发布会，以澄清他们那项被误解的官方政策。

items.def_en: 1. To make something easier to understand, use, or do by removing unnecessary complexity.
items.ex_en: We must simplify the application process to help older citizens participate easily.
items.ex_zh: 我们必须简化申请流程，以帮助老年人更轻松地参与。
items.ex2_en: The complex registration rules simplify considerably once you create an online portal account.
items.ex2_zh: 一旦你创建了在线门户账号，繁琐的注册规则就会大大简化。

items.def_en: To extract the most essential points or core ideas from a vast amount of information
items.ex_en: She managed to distill the complex research into a clear ten-minute presentation.
items.ex_zh: 她成功地将复杂的研究成果提炼为一场清晰的十分钟报告。

items.def_zh: 去神秘化，深入浅出地解释
items.def_en: To make a difficult or obscure subject clear, comprehensible, and easily understood by ordinary people
items.ex_en: His popular lecture series aimed to demystify quantum physics for everyday audiences.
items.ex_zh: 他广受欢迎的系列讲座旨在为大众深入浅出地普及量子物理学。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate rendering complex concepts, texts, or procedures intelligible and clear by stripping away jargon, redundant steps, and ambiguity. They operate mainly on intellectual, rhetorical, or administrative content.
groups.summary_zh: 去除多余修饰、繁杂细节或模糊隐晦，使内容清晰易懂、易于执行。
groups.desc_en: Denotes stripping away extraneous complexity, jargon, or confusion to reveal essential meaning or structure, contrasting with mere abbreviation by emphasizing cognitive clarity.
groups.desc_zh: 指剥离非核心的复杂修饰、行话或混杂成分以彰显本质，与单纯的“缩略”相比，强调提升理解度与认知清晰度。
groups.nuance_en: simplify: to make less complex or easier to do/understand (process / language / procedure) · clarify: to free from confusion, ambiguity, or impurities (position / meaning / thought) · distill: to extract the quintessential core ideas from a vast volume (essence / wisdom / findings) · demystify: to make a complex, esoteric topic intelligible to ordinary people (process / science / finance) · dumb down: to oversimplify at the expense of intellectual rigor (curriculum / content / news)
groups.nuance_zh: simplify: 化繁为简、降低操作或理解门槛 (process / language / procedure) · clarify: 澄清歧义、使条理分明 (position / meaning / thought) · distill: 提炼去粗、萃取思想精髓 (essence / wisdom / findings) · demystify: 破除神秘感、使通俗易懂 (process / science / finance) · dumb down: 贬义的过度低智化、削弱专业性 (curriculum / content / news)

groups.name: Sit & Settle · 坐下与就座 (Sit, Seat, Perch)
groups.tip: 弯膝落座与安坐指定位置

items.def_zh: 靠坐下；舒适地靠着坐好
items.def_en: To relax and make yourself comfortable by leaning back in a deep chair
items.ex_en: He settled back into the armchair and closed his eyes for a quick nap.
items.ex_zh: 他舒服地靠在扶手椅上，闭上双眼打了个盹。

items.def_zh: 坐，就座；使就座；坐落于；担任（委员会、法庭等成员）
items.def_en: 1. To rest one's body with the weight supported by the buttocks rather than the feet. 2. To cause someone to sit down; seat. 3. To be located or situated. 4. To serve as a member of an official committee, council, or court.
items.ex_en: The weary traveler sat by the roadside to rest his aching feet.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的旅人坐在路边，想歇歇酸痛的双脚。

items.def_en: To guide someone to a chair or provide official sitting accommodation for people
items.ex_en: The polite usher offered to seat the late arrivals in the back.
items.ex_zh: 彬彬有礼的引座员主动引导迟到者在后排就座。

items.def_zh: 使安坐；使舒舒服服坐好
items.def_en: (ensconce oneself) To position oneself comfortably, safely, and securely in a chair or cozy corner
items.ex_en: He ensconced himself in a plush leather armchair beside the roaring fireplace.
items.ex_zh: 他舒舒服服地窝在熊熊燃烧的壁炉旁那张厚实的皮扶手椅里。

items.def_en: To sit down suddenly, heavily, and clumsily onto a seat
items.ex_en: After a grueling shift, she plumped down heavily on the old sofa.
items.ex_zh: 经过一段疲惫的值班后，她猛然一屁股倒坐在旧沙发上。

items.def_en: (+ on) To sit on the edge of something narrow or elevated, often precariously
items.ex_en: The fearless cat loved to perch on the narrow balcony railing outside.
items.ex_zh: 那只胆大的猫喜欢高高栖坐在室外狭窄的阳台栏杆边缘。
items.ex2_en: She perched her heavy sunglasses securely on top of her curly brown hair.
items.ex2_zh: 她把沉重的太阳镜稳稳地架在自己卷曲的棕发上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe assuming or placing someone in a seated posture with body weight supported by the buttocks and thighs. Distinctions turn on formal seating, informal dropping down, high precarious balance, or sinking comfortably into cushions.
groups.summary_zh: 指人就座、坐下，或让某人安置于坐席上。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the manner of placing one's body into a seated posture or nestling into a resting spot, contrasting with the generic static state ('sit') by highlighting posture, comfort, or precarious balance.
groups.desc_zh: 指采取坐姿或落座于某处的具体动态与姿态，与静态的“坐着”相比，强调就座时的体态舒适度、陷入感或平衡状态。
groups.nuance_en: sit: default action of resting weight on buttocks/thighs (chair / desk / bench) · seat: to formally place or provide accommodation for sitting (guests / delegates / audience) · perch: to sit lightly, narrowly, or precarically on an edge or high spot (stool / edge / branch) · ensconce: to establish oneself firmly and comfortably in a secure spot (armchair / corner / sofa) · settle back: to sink back comfortably into a seat for relaxation (cushions / seat / armchair)
groups.nuance_zh: sit: 最基础的中性就座动作 (chair / desk / bench) · seat: 正式引领就座或容纳就座 (guests / delegates / audience) · perch: 窄窄地高踞、栖坐于边缘 (stool / edge / branch) · ensconce: 舒适安稳地窝在/深坐于某处 (armchair / corner / sofa) · settle back: 惬意地向后倚靠就座 (cushions / seat / armchair)

groups.name: Skip & Bypass · 跳过与绕过 (Omit, Sidestep, Bypass)
groups.tip: 略过既定步骤或直接绕开

items.def_en: To ignore or disregard someone or something, especially in favor of another
items.ex_en: The board decided to pass over the qualified insider for outside talent.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决定忽略那位资历出众的内部员工，转而选用外部人才。

items.def_en: To spend too little time, money, or effort on something essential, effectively cutting corners
items.ex_en: You should never skimp on safety equipment when undertaking hazardous construction work.
items.ex_zh: 在进行高危建筑施工时，绝不能在安全设备上克扣应付。

items.def_zh: 略过，跳过；避开，缺席；蹦跳着走
items.def_en: 1. To pass over or omit an item, step, or stage, moving directly to the next. 2. (informal) To not attend an event, meeting, or class that you should attend. 3. To move forward with light, springy steps, hopping on each foot in turn.
items.ex_en: Due to time limits, we will skip the introductory slides this morning.
items.ex_zh: 由于时间有限，我们今早将直接略过介绍性的幻灯片。

items.def_en: To advance ahead out of proper turn or omit intervening stages in a sequence
items.ex_en: Impatient drivers frequently jump the slow queue at the busy highway junction.
items.ex_zh: 不耐烦的司机经常在繁忙的公路交叉口违规插队越过慢车。

items.def_en: To avoid or circumvent an obstacle, regulation, or official procedure by taking an alternative route
items.ex_en: They created an automated tool to bypass the cumbersome internal approval system.
items.ex_zh: 他们开发了一个自动化工具来规避繁琐的内部审批流程。

items.def_en: To avoid dealing directly with an issue, question, or obligation by subtle evasion
items.ex_en: The politician tried to sidestep the thorny question about recent tax increases.
items.ex_zh: 政客试图回避有关近期税收上涨的棘手问题。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe deliberately omitting, passing over, or navigating around an established step, rule, or obstacle. While 'skip' emphasizes leaving out an item in a sequence, 'bypass' and 'sidestep' highlight evading formal procedures or direct confrontations.
groups.summary_zh: 指有意跳过步骤、规避规则或绕开既定障碍的动作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes intentionally or pragmatically omitting, avoiding, or charting a path around an intermediate stage, rule, or obstacle, contrasting with unintentional absence by stressing deliberate evasion or jumping forward.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动或权宜性地忽略、绕开中间步骤、规则或障碍，与无意的“遗漏”相比，强调刻意跳过、越级推进或规避阻碍。
groups.nuance_en: skip: to omit a step, item, or meal intentionally or lightly (chapter / meal / step) · bypass: to go around an obstacle, formal channel, or town to save time (bureaucracy / surgery / town) · sidestep: to adroitly evade a difficult issue, question, or responsibility (question / challenge / trap) · pass over: to disregard or omit from consideration, especially promotion (candidate / detail / text) · skimp on: to scrimp or provide inadequate effort/resources to something (details / quality / training)
groups.nuance_zh: skip: 径直跳过某一步骤或项 (chapter / meal / step) · bypass: 绕过正式渠道、障碍或拥堵路段 (bureaucracy / surgery / town) · sidestep: 灵巧地回避棘手问题或责任 (question / challenge / trap) · pass over: 忽略、置之不理或晋升时跳过 (candidate / detail / text) · skimp on: 在……上克扣省事、敷衍了事 (details / quality / training)

groups.name: Slashing & Lacerating · 刀割与砍削 (Slash, Gash, Slit)
groups.tip: 用利刃挥舞劈砍斩削切口

items.def_en: To cut smoothly or forcefully through something with a sharp edge
items.ex_en: The sharp surgical knife can slice through the heavy canvas with ease.
items.ex_zh: 这柄锋利的手术刀能够轻而易举地切穿厚重的帆布。

items.def_en: To cut or tear violently along an edge so that the interior is exposed
items.ex_en: He used a jagged key to rip open the tightly taped parcel.
items.ex_zh: 他用一把凹凸不平的钥匙暴力划开了被胶带缠得严严实实的包裹。

items.def_en:
1. to cut or hit violently with a sweeping stroke of a knife, sword, or other sharp blade
2. to reduce prices, costs, or jobs drastically
items.ex_en: The masked burglar used a razor to slash the priceless canvas painting.
items.ex_zh: 蒙面窃贼用剃刀猛烈划破了那幅价值连城的帆布油画。

items.def_en: To make a long, straight, narrow cut in something, often with a clean blade
items.ex_en: She carefully slit the envelope using a thin brass letter opener today.
items.ex_zh: 今天她用一把轻薄的黄铜开信刀小心地切开了信封。

items.def_en: To make a long, deep, violent cut into someone's flesh or a surface
items.ex_en: The falling sheet of glass gashed a deep wound across his forearm.
items.ex_zh: 坠落的玻璃碎片在他的前臂上砍开了一道深深的伤口。

items.def_en: To cut or tear skin or flesh roughly and deeply
items.ex_en: The flying shards of jagged glass lacerated the surgeon's hands and forearms.
items.ex_zh: 飞溅的尖锐玻璃碎片割破了外科医生的双手和前臂。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses making long, rapid, sweeping cuts into tissue or material with a sharp, swift edge, producing deep lacerations.
groups.summary_zh: 用锋利刀刃以挥掠之势划开、割破或造成深长裂口。
groups.desc_en: Denotes cutting or tearing flesh, fabric, or surfaces with violent, sharp, or sweeping blade strokes, contrasting with neat severing ('cut/slice') by stressing jagged edges, sweeping force, or deep wounding.
groups.desc_zh: 指用锋利刃具或暴力进行大跨度挥砍、划割或撕裂，与平整齐整的“切开”相比，强调伤口深长、撕裂性创伤或迅猛的攻击性动作。
groups.nuance_en: slash: to make wide, violent, sweeping cuts (throat / budget / tires) · slit: to make a straight, narrow, clean incision (throat / envelope / seam) · gash: to inflict a deep, long, gaping wound (leg / forehead / arm) · lacerate: to tear or mangle flesh jaggedly (skin / tissue / heart) · rip open: to tear open with sudden, tearing physical force (packet / wound / seam)
groups.nuance_zh: slash: 挥刃猛砍、大幅削减 (throat / budget / tires) · slit: 细长利落地切开细口 (throat / envelope / seam) · gash: 划出又深又宽的豁口 (leg / forehead / arm) · lacerate: 撕裂成锯齿状创口、摧残 (skin / tissue / heart) · rip open: 暴力撕扯开 (packet / wound / seam)

groups.name: Slay & Slaughter · 杀戮与处死 (Slay, Murder, Execute)
groups.tip: 剥夺生命的不同手段方式

items.def_en: (informal) To murder or eliminate someone purposefully, especially in criminal contexts
items.ex_en: The crime boss ordered his loyal henchmen to bump off the informant.
items.ex_zh: 那个犯罪头目命令忠诚的心腹除掉那名线人。

items.def_zh: 杀死，致死；终结，破坏；使痛苦不堪
items.def_en: 1. To cause the death of a person, animal, or plant. 2. To stop, destroy, or put an end to something.
items.ex_en: The sudden frost killed all the delicate seedlings in the garden overnight.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的严霜一夜之间冻死了花园里所有娇嫩的幼苗。

items.def_en: To put someone to death lawfully as an official punishment for a capital crime
items.ex_en: The state executed the convicted murderer by lethal injection early this morning.
items.ex_zh: 州政府于今天清晨通过注射死刑处决了这名被定罪的杀人犯。
