items.def_en: To remove the inside or core of an object or earth bank to create an empty cavity
items.ex_en: Water currents gradually hollowed out a massive limestone cavern beneath the cliff face.
items.ex_zh: 水流在悬崖下逐渐淘空，形成了一个巨大的石灰岩洞穴。
items.ex2_en: The ancient oak trunk hollowed out completely over centuries of natural insect decay.
items.ex2_zh: 经过几个世纪自然的昆虫侵蚀，古老橡树的树干彻底空心化了。

items.def_en: To dig a hole or continuous passage into or under something, typically using claws, hands, or repetitive scraping
items.ex_en: Terrified rabbits burrowed deep beneath the thorny hedge to escape prowling foxes.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的野兔在多刺的树篱下深挖洞穴，以躲避四处徘徊的狐狸。

groups.summary_en: Pertains to excavating a continuous passage through earth, rock, or other solid obstacles. 'Tunnel' implies excavating a path underground, 'bore' focuses on drilling a cylindrical cavity, and 'burrow' denotes an animal-like digging inwards.
groups.summary_zh: 指穿透岩石、泥土或障碍物向深处钻凿或掘出通道。
groups.desc_en: Penetrating, excavating, or carving continuous passages through solid geological or structural barriers, differing from superficial digging by establishing enclosed subterranean conduits.
groups.desc_zh: 在坚固地质或结构体中向内穿透挖掘出贯通通道，区别于表层挖掘，强调形成封闭的地下或内部管道。
groups.nuance_en: tunnel: constructing an underground transit corridor (mountain / hill / bedrock) · bore: cutting cylindrical holes with rotary mechanical force (hole / cylinder / tunnel) · burrow: small animals or agents digging into soil for shelter (earth / ground / holes) · mine: excavating mineral deposits or destabilizing fortifications (coal / seam / tunnel) · hollow out: removing interior mass to form a cavity (log / cliff / stone)
groups.nuance_zh: tunnel: 开凿供通行的地下通道 (mountain / hill / bedrock) · bore: 机械旋转钻削出圆柱孔洞 (hole / cylinder / tunnel) · burrow: 小型动物或主体掘土筑穴以藏身 (earth / ground / holes) · mine: 采掘矿脉或暗挖坑道破坏工事 (coal / seam / tunnel) · hollow out: 掏空内部体量形成空腔 (log / cliff / stone)

groups.name: Underestimate & Belittle · 轻视与低估 (Underestimate, Undervalue, Belittle, Minimize)
groups.tip: 主观评估远低于实际

items.def_en: to treat or portray an issue, problem, or accomplishment as being insignificant
items.ex_en: The company spokesperson tried to minimize the security breach during the press conference.
items.ex_zh: 公司发言人在新闻发布会上试图淡化这次安全漏洞。

items.def_en: to fail to guess the true scale, strength, or difficulty of an adversary, task, or quantity
items.ex_en: Never underestimate your opponent's ability to recover quickly from an early tactical setback.
items.ex_zh: 永远不要低估对手从早期战术挫折中迅速恢复的能力。

items.def_en: To fail to recognize the full importance, value, or ability of someone or something.
items.ex_en: Critics underrate her strategic contributions simply because she prefers working behind the scenes.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士仅仅因为她喜欢幕后工作就低估了她的战略贡献。

items.def_en: to rate the worth, importance, or contributions of someone or something below their true merit
items.ex_en: Traditional firms often undervalue the immense impact of junior employees' creative digital ideas.
items.ex_zh: 传统公司往往低估初级员工富有创意的数字化构想所带来的巨大影响。

items.def_en: to fail to give full credit to or estimate someone's true capability accurately
items.ex_en: Do not sell yourself short during the interview; highlight your impressive leadership accomplishments.
items.ex_zh: 面试时不要看轻自己；大胆突出你令人瞩目的领导成就。

items.def_en: to make someone or their actions seem small, trivial, or unimportant
items.ex_en: The harsh supervisor constantly belittled his subordinates' hard work in front of colleagues.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的主管经常在同事面前贬低部属的辛勤付出。

groups.summary_en: Centers on judging someone or something to be less capable, valuable, severe, or important than they actually are. It contrasts miscalculating capability with deliberately diminishing significance.
groups.summary_zh: 指在认知上低估其能力、价值或有意淡化其重要性与严重性。
groups.desc_en: Evaluating someone or something below true merit, strength, or significance, distinct from objective miscalculation by carrying dismissive or condescending appraisal.
groups.desc_zh: 主观上低估目标实力、价值或严重性，区别于中立的测算失误，带有轻视、贬损或自大判断的倾向。
groups.nuance_en: underestimate: misjudging capability or threat downwards (strength / resolve / costs) · belittle: actively deprecating worth to make trivial (achievements / efforts / concerns) · undervalue: pricing or esteeming assets below intrinsic merit (stock / currency / contribution) · minimize: rhetorically downplaying gravity or impact (damage / role / risk) · sell short: failing to recognize latent potential due to bias (talent / abilities / partner)
groups.nuance_zh: underestimate: 算低对手实力或潜在威胁 (strength / resolve / costs) · belittle: 刻意贬低贬损他人价值或成就 (achievements / efforts / concerns) · undervalue: 估值偏低或不予足够重视 (stock / currency / contribution) · minimize: 话语上蓄意将严重性缩至最小 (damage / role / risk) · sell short: 因偏见而错判或看轻潜在能力 (talent / abilities / partner)

groups.name: Underestimate & Undervalue · 低估与轻视 (Belittle, Underrate, Downplay)
groups.tip: 评价偏低并带有轻蔑不屑色彩

items.def_en: To guess an amount, difficulty, or capacity to be smaller or less than it actually is
items.ex_en: Contractors underestimated the total construction costs due to sudden raw material price hikes.
items.ex_zh: 由于原材料价格突然暴涨，承包商低估了总建设成本。

items.def_en: To fail to recognize how good, powerful, or important someone or something really is
items.ex_en: Pundits underrate the veteran boxer's stamina ahead of this grueling championship rematch.
items.ex_zh: 在这场艰苦的冠军复赛之前，专家们低估了这位老将拳手的耐力。

items.def_en: To deliberately make something seem less important, serious, or urgent than it is
items.ex_en: Officials downplayed public health risks despite emerging evidence of widespread local contamination.
items.ex_zh: 尽管有新证据表明当地出现了大范围污染，官员们还是淡化了公共卫生风险。

items.def_zh: 低估……的价值（或重要性），轻视，看轻；对……估价过低
items.def_en: 1. To fail to appreciate the true worth, importance, or qualities of someone or something. 2. To rate or estimate the financial value of an asset too low.
items.ex_en: Many contemporary collectors undervalue rare antique textiles because modern synthetic fabrics dominate.
items.ex_zh: 由于现代合成织物占据主导，许多当代收藏家低估了珍稀古代纺织品的价值。

items.def_en: To fail to present or appreciate someone or something with the praise and respect they deserve
items.ex_en: You sell yourself short by refusing to apply for that senior executive position.
items.ex_zh: 你拒绝申请那个高管职位，简直是小看了自己的能力。

items.def_en: To treat someone or their achievements as small, unimportant, or worthless
items.ex_en: He cruelly belittled her artistic talents whenever she showed him her new paintings.
items.ex_zh: 每当她向他展示新画作时，他总是无情地贬低她的艺术才能。

groups.summary_en: Encompasses cognitive assessments or communicative acts that minimize the actual worth, competence, or significance of someone or something. Nuances vary between flawed appraisal and dismissive contempt.
groups.summary_zh: 表示在认知或言论中低估、轻慢其价值或能力，具贬低色彩。
groups.desc_en: Cognitively or socially discounting importance, excellence, or market worth, contrasting with outright rejection by acknowledging existence while severely reducing perceived stature.
groups.desc_zh: 在认知或社会评价上削减对象的重要性或价值，区别于全盘否定，承认知晓但大幅压低其地位或分量。
groups.nuance_en: underrate: assigning insufficient appraisal compared to true capability (player / movie / talent) · downplay: purposefully diminishing perceived public importance (significance / severity / scandal) · undervalue: failing to appreciate economic or moral worth (currency / labor / asset) · underestimate: quantitatively or tactically misjudging magnitude (enemy / time / difficulty) · belittle: verbally disparaging with condescension (opponent / work / contribution)
groups.nuance_zh: underrate: 评价过低，未给予应有认可 (player / movie / talent) · downplay: 刻意淡化公众眼中的重要性或严重程度 (significance / severity / scandal) · undervalue: 经济或道义上未充分体现其价值 (currency / labor / asset) · underestimate: 战术或数量上算小规模或难度 (enemy / time / difficulty) · belittle: 居高临下地出言贬损 (opponent / work / contribution)

groups.name: Understate & Downplay · 轻描淡写与贬低 (Minimize, Soft-pedal, Gloss over)
groups.tip: 故意淡化严重性或压低评价

items.def_zh: 弱化处理；采取缓和调门
items.def_en: To treat or present a problem less firmly or with restrained emphasis
items.ex_en: The politician tried to soft-pedal tax hikes to avoid angering anxious suburban voters.
items.ex_zh: 该政客试图弱化增税议题，以免激怒焦虑的郊区选民。

items.raw_cluster: 轻描淡写与贬低 Understate & Downplay
items.def_zh: 淡化……的重要性，轻描淡写；表演低调含蓄
items.def_en: 1. To make something seem less important, serious, or dramatic than it really is. 2. To act a role with understatement and restraint.
items.ex_en: The diplomat underplayed the severe border skirmish to preserve fragile regional peace talks.
items.ex_zh: 这位外交官对严重的边境冲突轻描淡写，以维持脆弱的地区和谈。

items.def_en: To reject or dismiss a serious concern, question, or criticism impatiently
items.ex_en: He tried to brush off the criticism as petty jealousy.
items.ex_zh: 他试图对这些批评不予理会，将其归咎于小人的嫉妒。

items.def_en: To treat a mistake or unpleasant fact as negligible by mentioning it only briefly
items.ex_en: The annual report glossed over significant quarterly losses with vague optimistic corporate slogans.
items.ex_zh: 该年度报告用空洞乐观的企业口号对巨额季度亏损敷衍带过。

items.def_en: To treat or describe something as being of very little importance or magnitude
items.ex_en: The doctor tried to minimize the patient's anxiety before the minor surgical procedure.
items.ex_zh: 在进行小型手术之前，医生尽量减轻患者的焦虑。

items.def_en: To make something appear less important, serious, or urgent than it really is
items.ex_en: The administration downplayed the inflation figures to ease rising panic in financial markets.
items.ex_zh: 政府淡化了通胀数据，以缓解金融市场上不断蔓延的恐慌情绪。

groups.summary_en: This frame denotes deliberately minimizing the severity, importance, scale, or impact of an issue in discourse, often to soothe concern, deflect scrutiny, or avert blame.
groups.summary_zh: 指刻意淡化事态严重性、重要性或负面影响，避重就轻。
groups.desc_en: Rhetorically framing an issue, error, or danger as negligible to blunt alarm or accountability, differing from outright lying by selective softening and omission.
groups.desc_zh: 通过修辞将问题、过失或危机描述为微不足道以化解恐慌或问责，区别于直接撒谎，侧重选择性淡化和粉饰。
groups.nuance_en: downplay: intentional public minimization of severity (crisis / rift / impact) · gloss over: evading awkward truths by superficial mention (details / mistakes / flaws) · soft-pedal: deliberately reducing emphasis to placate (rhetoric / policy / demands) · brush off: dismissively swatting aside concerns as irrelevant (complaints / warning / advice) · minimize: systematically reducing attributed scale or guilt (losses / culpability / risk)
groups.nuance_zh: downplay: 刻意对公众淡化严重程度 (crisis / rift / impact) · gloss over: 轻描淡写一笔带过尴尬缺陷 (details / mistakes / flaws) · soft-pedal: 软化调门或诉求以安抚对手 (rhetoric / policy / demands) · brush off: 漫不经心地拂开或不予理会 (complaints / warning / advice) · minimize: 系统性压低事件规模或责任 (losses / culpability / risk)

groups.name: Undo & Unfasten · 解开与松绑 (Untie, Loosen, Unravel)
groups.tip: 解开绳结松开扣件

items.def_en: To release someone or something from ropes, bonds, or fetters
items.ex_en: The mysterious knight gently unbound the captive maiden from the cold dungeon chains.
items.ex_zh: 神秘骑士温柔地为地牢中被俘的少女解开了冰冷的锁链。

items.def_zh: 解开，解松（纽扣、绳结等）；撤销，废止；破坏，毁掉
items.def_en: 1. To unfasten, untie, or loosen a button, knot, or package. 2. To cancel or reverse the effect of a previous action. 3. To ruin or destroy someone or something.
items.ex_en: She sat beside the fire and carefully undid the ribbon on the gift.
items.ex_zh: 她坐在壁炉旁，小心翼翼地解开了礼物上的丝带。

items.def_en: To make something less tight, firmly fixed, or compact
items.ex_en: The mechanic loosened the rusty bolts before replacing the worn vehicle brake pads.
items.ex_zh: 机械师在更换磨损的车载刹车片前拧松了生锈的螺栓。
items.ex2_en: The tight screws loosened gradually under the constant vibration of the factory machine.
items.ex2_zh: 在工厂机器持续不断的震动下，拧紧的螺丝逐渐松脱了。

items.def_zh: 拆散，解开（织物、缠结的线绳）
items.def_en: To cause threads or fibers that are woven or tangled to come apart
items.ex_en: The kitten playfully unraveled the large ball of red knitting wool across carpet.
items.ex_zh: 小猫调皮地将地毯上的大红色毛线球拆弄得散落一地。
items.ex2_en: The knitted woolen sweater unraveled quickly when its loose thread caught on a nail.
items.ex2_zh: 当毛衣松开的线头挂在钉子上时，这件针织羊毛衫迅速脱线散开了。

items.def_en: To undo a knot, ribbon, or the string or laces fastening something
items.ex_en: He quickly untied the tight knot securing the wooden boat to the dock.
items.ex_zh: 他飞快地解开了将木船固定在码头上的紧绳结。
items.ex2_en: The intricate sailor's knot untied easily once you pushed the central rope loop.
items.ex2_zh: 只要推动中间的绳圈，这个复杂的水手结就能轻而易举地解开。

items.def_zh: 解开，打开（扣件、安全带等）
items.def_en: To open or loosen a buckle, latch, zip, or other fastening mechanism
items.ex_en: Passengers must not unfasten their safety belts until the aircraft comes to rest.
items.ex_zh: 在飞机完全停稳之前，乘客切勿解开安全带。
items.ex2_en: Her leather sandals unfastened unexpectedly while she walked across the cobblestone street courtyard.
items.ex2_zh: 当她穿过鹅卵石街道的庭院时，她的皮凉鞋扣带意外松脱了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to releasing, opening, or loosening physical attachments such as knots, buttons, laces, or bindings. They range from simple mechanical release to untangling intricate fastenings.
groups.summary_zh: 解开、松开或解脱绳结、纽扣、包装等物理固定物。
groups.desc_en: Reversing physical bonds, knots, or fasteners to restore components to a free state, differing from destructive tearing by orderly mechanical release.
groups.desc_zh: 解除物理绑扎、结扣或紧固件以恢复自由状态，区别于破坏性撕扯，侧重有序的机械脱扣或解构。
groups.nuance_en: undo: general reversal of ties, buttons, or binds (knot / button / zipper) · unfasten: releasing mechanical locking mechanisms (seatbelt / clasp / latch) · untie: specifically loosening knotted cords or laces (rope / shoes / bow) · loosen: reducing tension without fully disconnecting (grip / collar / bolt) · unravel: separating wound or woven strands, often unintentionally (threads / knitting / mystery)
groups.nuance_zh: undo: 泛指解开、脱开纽扣或系带 (knot / button / zipper) · unfasten: 解开带扣、搭扣等机械固件 (seatbelt / clasp / latch) · untie: 特指解开打结的绳索鞋带 (rope / shoes / bow) · loosen: 调松间隙或张力但未完全脱离 (grip / collar / bolt) · unravel: 拆解或自行散开线股编织物 (threads / knitting / mystery)

groups.name: Unlawful Incursion & Encroachment · 非法侵入与蚕食越界 (Trespass, Encroach, Infringe)
groups.tip: 未经允许强行踏入私人领地

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To encroach upon or violate a legal right, covenant, or agreement
items.ex_en: The new municipal ordinance may infringe on citizens' constitutional right to peaceful assembly.
items.ex_zh: 这项新的市政条例可能会侵犯公民和平集会的宪法权利。

items.def_zh: 非法侵入，擅入（私人领地）；冒犯，侵害
items.def_en: (+ on/upon) to enter someone's land or property without permission; to intrude on someone's rights or privacy
items.ex_en: Warning signs clearly stated that anyone who trespassed on the private estate faced prosecution.
items.ex_zh: 警示牌明确指出，任何非法侵入私人庄园者都将面临起诉。

items.def_zh: 偷猎；越界非法捕捞/窃取
items.def_en: To trespass on another's property to take game or fish, or to illicitly appropriate resources
items.ex_en: Armed gangs frequently poach endangered black rhinos inside the strictly protected national park.
items.ex_zh: 武装团伙频繁在受到严格保护的国家公园内偷猎濒危黑犀牛。

items.def_en: (+ on/into) To enter a place or situation where one is unwelcome or has no right to be
items.ex_en: Paparazzi tried to intrude upon the mourning family during the private memorial service.
items.ex_zh: 在私人追悼会期间，狗仔队试图打扰处于哀痛中的家属。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To intrude gradually and stealthily beyond acceptable or legal boundaries
items.ex_en: Urban developers continually encroach upon delicate wetland ecosystems surrounding the sprawling coastal city.
items.ex_zh: 城市开发商不断蚕食着这座沿海扩张城市周围脆弱的湿地生态系统。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To have an unwanted or detrimental effect on another person's rights or sphere
items.ex_en: The proposed noisy development project will impinge directly upon the residents' daily tranquility.
items.ex_zh: 拟建的高噪音开发项目将直接妨碍居民日常生活的宁静。

groups.summary_en: This legal and territorial frame covers entering someone's real property without authorization or gradually violating another person's rights, domains, or boundaries. Verbs range from explicit unauthorized entry to incremental overreach.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及未经许可进入私人领地，或对他人合法权益、边界进行非法侵占或蚕食。
groups.desc_en: Gradual, covert, or illegitimate boundary violations trespassing onto another's territorial, legal, or moral domain, contrasting with open assault by stealthy intrusion.
groups.desc_zh: 渐进式、隐蔽或非法的越界行为，侵入他人的领土、权益或权利范围，区别于公开攻击，侧重蚕食与逾矩。
groups.nuance_en: trespass: unlawful entry onto private land or personal bounds (property / land / privacy) · encroach: creeping, incremental usurpation of space or rights (territory / liberties / shoreline) · infringe: legally violating codified patents, copyrights, or terms (copyright / patent / rights) · poach: illegally harvesting game or illicitly luring talent (game / clients / staff) · impinge: exerting restrictive collision or intrusion on autonomy (freedom / sovereignty / rights)
groups.nuance_zh: trespass: 非法踏入私人地产或隐私边界 (property / land / privacy) · encroach: 悄无声息地逐步蚕食地盘或权限 (territory / liberties / shoreline) · infringe: 法律层面侵犯专利、版权或权益 (copyright / patent / rights) · poach: 非法盗猎野生动物或非法挖角 (game / clients / staff) · impinge: 碰撞挤压并损害他人自主权 (freedom / sovereignty / rights)

groups.name: Unseal & Open · 解封与破启 (Unseal, Uncap, Pry open, Break open)
groups.tip: 拆除封条并打开容器

items.def_en: To open a sealed or locked container by applying physical force
items.ex_en: Burglars used heavy crowbars to break open the metal cash register after midnight.
items.ex_zh: 夜半过后，窃贼用沉重的撬棍破开了金属收银机。
items.ex2_en: The brittle wooden crate broke open upon impact with the concrete warehouse floor.
items.ex2_zh: 脆弱的木箱撞击到水泥仓库地面后当场摔裂散开。

items.def_en: To remove the protective cap or lid from a bottle, pen, or device
items.ex_en: The professor uncapped his vintage fountain pen to sign the historic academic charter.
items.ex_zh: 教授拔开老式钢笔的笔帽，签署了这份具有历史意义的学术宪章。

items.def_en: To force open a tight lid, sealed crate, or door using a lever or tool
items.ex_en: Detectives managed to pry open the jammed wooden drawer using a pocket knife.
items.ex_zh: 侦探们用一把小折刀设法撬开了卡住的木抽屉。

items.def_en: To open a sealed envelope, package, or wrapper quickly and forcefully by tearing it
items.ex_en: The excited child ripped open the birthday parcel without reading the attached card.
items.ex_zh: 兴奋的孩子连附带的贺卡都顾不上看，就撕开了生日包裹。

items.def_en: To remove an obstructive stopper, bung, or plug sealing an opening or pipe
items.ex_en: She unplugged the drainage hole to let dirty water drain from the tub.
items.ex_zh: 她拔掉了排水孔的塞子，让浴缸里的脏水流尽。

items.def_en: To break the seal of a letter, container, or document to open it.
items.ex_en: The magistrate solemnly unsealed the official royal decree before the assembled town council.
items.ex_zh: 地方法官在聚集的镇议会成员面前庄严地启封了皇家法令。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers physically removing, cutting, or breaking an adhesive, wax, or mechanical seal that keeps a container, envelope, or entrance shut, permitting access to its contents.
groups.summary_zh: 破除密封胶、封泥或外层封闭结构，打开包装或信件。
groups.desc_en: Breaching, tearing, or prying open an airtight, sealed, or secured barrier, contrasting with routine opening by requiring deliberate disruption of an integrity seal.
groups.desc_zh: 破坏、揭除或撬开密封、加封或受阻的屏障，区别于普通开门窗，强调打破原本完好的防损闭锁结构。
groups.nuance_en: unseal: breaking an official wax, plastic, or airtight seal (envelope / container / tomb) · pry open: leveraging mechanical force against stubborn seals (crate / door / lid) · rip open: tearing violently through pliable packaging (package / letter / wrapper) · uncap: removing a protective screw-on or press-on lid (bottle / pen / lens) · break open: using sudden force to fracture a sealed container (safe / shell / pinata)
groups.nuance_zh: unseal: 启封官方封条、蜡封或气密密封 (envelope / container / tomb) · pry open: 借助杠杆力撬开咬合牢固的盖子 (crate / door / lid) · rip open: 暴力撕扯包装材料 (package / letter / wrapper) · uncap: 旋开或拔开笔盖、瓶盖等防护帽 (bottle / pen / lens) · break open: 施加外力砸破砸开封闭容器 (safe / shell / pinata)

groups.name: Untie & Unleash · 解开与爆发式释放 (Unleash, Unloose, Let loose, Vent)
groups.tip: 解开禁锢爆发释放而出

items.def_en: To free someone or something from physical restraint; release strong emotions or actions without restraint
items.ex_en: The coach finally let loose his bottled frustration after another terrible defensive error.
items.ex_zh: 又一次糟糕的防守失误后，教练终于彻底宣泄出压抑已久的挫败感。

items.def_zh: 触发；引起（连锁反应/爆发现象）
items.def_en: To cause an intense, violent, or sudden reaction, process, or series of events to start immediately
items.ex_en: The sudden economic sanctions triggered a catastrophic collapse of the country's national currency.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的经济制裁引发了该国货币灾难性的崩溃。

items.def_en: (+ on) To express a strong negative emotion, such as anger or frustration, openly and forcefully
items.ex_en: He unfairly vented his workplace frustrations on his supportive partner after arriving home.
items.ex_zh: 到家后，他不理智地把工作中的挫败感发泄到了支持他的伴侣身上。

items.def_zh: 释放，发泄，解除约束使爆发；解开（系绳、皮带）
items.def_en: 1. To release a powerful force, emotion, or effect suddenly and often destructively. 2. To remove a leash from a dog or animal.
items.ex_en: The fierce tropical typhoon unleashed devastating winds across the vulnerable coastal fishing villages.
items.ex_zh: 凶猛的热带台风向脆弱的沿海渔村倾泻出极具破坏性的狂风。

items.def_en: To loosen, untie, or set free from a bond, leash, or confining grip
items.ex_en: The shepherd gently unloosed the frightened hound from its tangled leather leash.
items.ex_zh: 牧羊人轻轻解开受惊猎犬身上缠绕的皮绳，放其自由。

items.def_en: To free someone or something from chains, bonds, or severe limitations
items.ex_en: The revolution aimed to unchain oppressed citizens from centuries of tyrannical monarchical rule.
items.ex_zh: 这场革命旨在把受压迫的民众从数百年专制君主统治的枷锁中解放出来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this dynamic frame describe removing physical or psychological restraints, allowing pent-up fury, wild power, weapons, or destructive forces to burst forth without inhibition.
groups.summary_zh: 挣脱束缚或解除拘禁，使积蓄的力量、情感或破坏力猛烈迸发。
groups.desc_en: Releasing volatile pent-up energy, fierce emotions, or ferocious actors from confinement, contrasting with calm letting-go by sudden explosive fury.
groups.desc_zh: 解开拘束，将积压的狂暴能量、激烈情绪或凶猛力量爆发式释放，区别于平静松手，具有宣泄破坏性。
groups.nuance_en: unleash: unchaining powerful, destructive forces or campaigns (fury / war / hounds) · vent: discharging accumulated emotional steam or gaseous pressure (anger / frustration / spleen) · let loose: abruptly freeing bounded violence, laughter, or cries (screams / arrows / dogs) · unchain: setting free from literal or systemic fetters (prisoners / economy / imagination) · trigger: initiating a sudden chain reaction of dormant forces (avalanche / panic / crisis)
groups.nuance_zh: unleash: 解开猛兽锁链，释放狂暴破坏力 (fury / war / hounds) · vent: 释放胸中积压的怒气或怨气 (anger / frustration / spleen) · let loose: 突发性释放受控的暴力、喊叫或猛兽 (screams / arrows / dogs) · unchain: 斩断字面或制度性枷锁重获自由 (prisoners / economy / imagination) · trigger: 扣动扳机引发休眠力量的连锁爆发 (avalanche / panic / crisis)

groups.name: Urge & Exhort · 敦促与力劝 (Urge, Exhort, Press)
groups.tip: 由一般催促上升至恳切告诫

items.def_en: To encourage or push someone strongly to do something foolish or risky
items.ex_en: Mischievous older boys egged him on to jump across the dangerously wide ditch.
items.ex_zh: 淘气的年长男孩们怂恿他跳过那条危险的宽水沟。

items.def_en: To urge someone gently but seriously to do what is right
items.ex_en: The headmaster solemnly admonished students to exhibit integrity during the upcoming final examinations.
items.ex_zh: 校长庄重告诫学生们在即将到来的期末考试中保持诚信。

items.def_en: To try hard to persuade or compel someone to do something
items.ex_en: Diplomats pressed the warring factions to sign a permanent ceasefire agreement without delay.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们敦促交战各方毫不拖延地签署永久停火协议。

items.def_zh: 敦促，催促；力劝，大力主张
items.def_en: To advise or try hard to persuade someone to do something.
items.ex_en: Health authorities strongly urge all vulnerable citizens to receive their annual influenza vaccinations.
items.ex_zh: 卫生当局强烈力劝所有易感人群接种年度流感疫苗。

items.def_en: To provoke or annoy someone into action by persistent prodding
items.ex_en: His constant teasing was designed to goad her into an angry response.
items.ex_zh: 他不断的戏弄旨在激怒她，促使她做出愤怒的反应。

items.def_en: To strongly encourage or urge someone to do something through earnest speech
items.ex_en: The prime minister continued to exhort citizens to remain calm during the crisis.
items.ex_zh: 首相在危机期间继续告诫民众保持冷静。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe exerting moral, persuasive, or vocal force on someone to prompt immediate action or compliance, ranging from earnest advice to persistent badgering.
groups.summary_zh: 表示以热切的言辞、劝告或道义力量催促、力劝他人采取行动。
groups.desc_en: Exerting persistent psychological, moral, or authoritative pressure on an agent to initiate prompt action, differing from neutral advice by imperative urgency.
groups.desc_zh: 对主体施加心理、道德或权威压力以促其立即行动，区别于中立建议，带有迫切督促与催促色彩。
groups.nuance_en: urge: earnest, pressing recommendation of a critical path (caution / restraint / reforms) · exhort: impassioned, moralizing persuasion to duty (flock / troops / followers) · press: applying persistent, uncomfortable leverage (government / debtor / claims) · goad: irritating or provoking someone into hasty reaction (opponent / crowd / pride) · egg on: colloquially inciting reckless or misbehaved acts (comrades / peer / troublemakers)
groups.nuance_zh: urge: 极力主张并恳请采取必要举措 (caution / restraint / reforms) · exhort: 激情饱满且带有道德劝诫的训谕 (flock / troops / followers) · press: 施加持续令人难堪的压力逼其就范 (government / debtor / claims) · goad: 用尖锐言语刺激挑衅使其激愤行动 (opponent / crowd / pride) · egg on: 口语中怂恿煽动做出鲁莽过激之举 (comrades / peer / troublemakers)

groups.name: Usurp & Arrogate · 侵占与僭取 (Arrogate, Usurp, Appropriate)
groups.tip: 擅自越权霸占不法利益

items.def_en: Take something, especially public money or land, for one's own use without permission
items.ex_en: The corrupt official was accused of attempting to appropriate public funds for private renovations.
items.ex_zh: 这名贪官被指控企图将公共资金据为己有来进行私人房屋翻修。

items.def_en: Officially take possession or control of something by force or authority, especially for military or emergency use
items.ex_en: Soldiers had authority to commandeer civilian vehicles during the unexpected border emergency.
items.ex_zh: 在突发边境紧急情况期间，士兵有权强征民用车辆。

items.def_zh: 先发制人取得；抢先占有
items.def_en: Acquire or claim something before others can do so, preventing them from accessing it
items.ex_en: The tech giant moved quickly to preempt any rival bids for the promising startup.
items.ex_zh: 该科技巨头迅速采取行动，先发制人抢先收购了这家前景光明的初创公司。

items.def_zh: 篡夺；非法侵占（权力、王位）
items.def_en: Take a position of power, throne, or authority illegally or by force
items.ex_en: The ambitious general conspired secretly with foreign allies to usurp the royal throne.
items.ex_zh: 野心勃勃的将军与外国盟友暗中勾结，企图篡夺王位。

items.def_en: Officially take away private property from its owner, often without fair compensation
items.ex_en: The revolutionary government resolved to expropriate large agricultural estates without providing any compensation.
items.ex_zh: 革命政府决定没收大型农业庄园，且不提供任何补偿。

items.def_zh: 妄取，僭取，擅自霸占（arrogate to oneself）
items.def_en: (formal) to claim, take, or seize power, authority, or rights for oneself without justification
items.ex_en: The unelected council member attempted to arrogate executive authority to himself without legal basis.
items.ex_zh: 这名未经选举产生的议员企图在毫无法律依据的情况下将行政权力僭取到自己手中。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe seizing, claiming, or assuming rights, powers, or privileges without legitimate authority or legal justification.
groups.summary_zh: 指未经授权、非法或专横地侵占权力、特权或他人财产。
groups.desc_en: Seizing, claiming, or expropriating authority, property, or privileges without legitimate entitlement, contrasting with legal acquisition by brazen unilateral overreach.
groups.desc_zh: 在毫无合法授权的情况下强行侵占或僭取权力、财产与特权，区别于正当获取，具有单方面擅权性质。
groups.nuance_en: usurp: illegally seizing sovereign throne or constitutional office (throne / power / authority) · arrogate: presumptuously claiming rights or powers not belonging to one (privilege / responsibility / right) · commandeer: taking arbitrary possession of private goods for emergency use (vehicle / building / ship) · expropriate: state authority dispossessing private property, often forcibly (land / assets / property) · appropriate: improperly taking possession of funds or culture for private use (funds / culture / ideas)
groups.nuance_zh: usurp: 篡夺王位、宪法职权或主权 (throne / power / authority) · arrogate: 专横狂妄地擅自揽取特权或裁量权 (privilege / responsibility / right) · commandeer: 战时或紧急状态下强行征用民物 (vehicle / building / ship) · expropriate: 政府公权力强制没收征收私产 (land / assets / property) · appropriate: 私自挪用侵吞公款或挪用文化符号 (funds / culture / ideas)

groups.name: Vaunt & Preen · 骄傲与炫示自夸 (Pride, Boast, Preen)
groups.tip: 内心自豪与言行张扬吹嘘的展现

items.def_en: ('pride oneself on') To feel very pleased and proud of a quality, skill, or achievement.
items.ex_en: Our boutique hotel has always prided itself on providing exceptional and attentive customer service.
items.ex_zh: 我们的精品酒店一直以提供卓越而周到的客户服务自豪。

items.def_en: To speak with excessive pride or self-satisfaction about one's achievements or possessions
items.ex_en: He could not resist the urge to boast about his extensive real estate portfolio.
items.ex_zh: 他忍不住吹嘘自己规模庞大的房地产资产。

items.def_zh: 得意地嚷嚷；幸灾乐祸地夸口
items.def_en: (+ about/over) To express gleeful triumph or boast noisily over a rival's defeat
items.ex_en: She could not resist the urge to crow over her rival's sudden defeat.
items.ex_zh: 她忍不住为对手的突然落败而幸灾乐祸地得意嚷嚷。

items.def_en: To talk ostentatiously and excessively about what one has done or owns
items.ex_en: He loves to brag about his fancy watch whenever new guests arrive.
items.ex_zh: 每当有新客人来，他就喜欢炫耀吹嘘自己的名贵手表。

items.def_zh: 得意扬扬；顾影自怜；自鸣得意
items.def_en: To congratulate oneself or display obvious vanity and complacency about one's appearance or skill
items.ex_en: The newly promoted director continued to preen about his sudden professional triumph.
items.ex_zh: 新升任的主管继续对他职业生涯的突然胜利表现得自鸣得意。

items.def_en: (+ over) To show malicious or smug pleasure at one's own success or another person's misfortune
items.ex_en: It is bad sportsmanship to gloat over your defeated opponent after winning.
items.ex_zh: 获胜后对战败的对手幸灾乐祸是缺乏体育精神的。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey experiencing, displaying, or advertising excessive satisfaction in one's personal achievements, possessions, or qualities. While 'pride' highlights inner self-worth, 'boast' and 'brag' manifest as vocal swagger.
groups.summary_zh: 指为自身才干、功绩或外貌感到荣耀自得，并向他人夸示炫耀。
groups.desc_en: Displaying self-satisfaction, status, or triumph with conspicuous ostentation to evoke admiration or envy, differing from humble pride by aggressive public vanity.
groups.desc_zh: 大肆炫耀自身成就、地位或胜利以招引艳羡或震慑对手，区别于谦抑的自豪，带有外显虚荣与挑衅意味。
groups.nuance_en: boast: overtly publicizing possession of enviable assets or skills (wealth / record / prowess) · brag: vulgar, persistent self-praise in conversation (exploits / victory / money) · gloat: relishing malice over an opponent's misfortune (triumph / defeat / misery) · preen: complacently grooming oneself or basking in adulation (feathers / vanity / self-regard) · crow: exulting loudly and gratingly over small triumphs (victory / success / results)
groups.nuance_zh: boast: 夸耀所拥有的显赫资产、纪录或能力 (wealth / record / prowess) · brag: 口头粗俗且频繁地自吹自擂 (exploits / victory / money) · gloat: 幸灾乐祸地对败者洋洋自得 (triumph / defeat / misery) · preen: 顾盼自雄、打扮自恋以求受人瞩目 (feathers / vanity / self-regard) · crow: 像公鸡啼叫般刺耳得瑟自己的小胜 (victory / success / results)

groups.name: Ventilate & Aerate · 通风与充气 (Air, Ventilate, Oxygenate)
groups.tip: 使空气流通或通入气体

items.def_zh: 开窗透气；彻底晾晒散味
items.def_en: [I/T] to expose a room or clothing thoroughly to fresh air so as to remove dampness or odors
items.ex_en: Open all the windows for a few hours to air out the freshly painted living room.
items.ex_zh: 把所有窗户打开几个小时，给刚粉刷完的客厅通通风散味。
items.ex2_en: The musty guest bedroom will air out quickly with the windows wide open.
items.ex2_zh: 窗户大开后，这间有发霉气味的客房很快就会通风散味。

items.def_en: (+ sth) to clear or freshen an enclosed space or filter by forcing fresh air through it
items.ex_en: We used compressed air to blow out the dust clogging the engine filter.
items.ex_zh: 我们用压缩空气吹透滤网，清除了堵塞发动机的灰尘。

items.def_zh: 使通风，晾晒；公开表达，发表
items.def_en: 1. To expose a room, clothing, etc. to fresh air or heat so that it becomes dry or fresh. 2. To express your opinions or complaints publicly.
items.ex_en: Open the bedroom windows wide to air the stuffy room before bedtime.
items.ex_zh: 睡前把卧室窗户大开，让闷热的房间通通风。
items.ex2_en: The damp winter blankets must air outside in the warm sunshine all afternoon.
items.ex2_zh: 潮湿的冬毯必须在温暖的阳光下晾晒整个下午。

items.def_zh: 使室内或封闭空间通风；为患者进行机械通气
items.def_en: to cause fresh air to circulate freely through a room or building, or to provide medical respiration
items.ex_en: Architects installed modern ducts to properly ventilate the crowded underground facility.
items.ex_zh: 建筑师安装了现代管道，以使拥挤的地下设施保持良好通风。

items.def_zh: 使充气，通气；使暴露于空气中
items.def_en: To introduce air or gas into soil, water, or another substance to make it fresher, lighter, or richer in oxygen.
items.ex_en: Gardeners must regularly aerate the compacted soil to ensure healthy root growth.
items.ex_zh: 园丁必须定期给板结的土壤通气，以确保根系健康生长。

items.def_zh: 给（血液、水体等）充氧，使与氧气结合
items.def_en: to supply, treat, or enrich a substance (such as blood or water) with oxygen
items.ex_en: The modern medical machine works continuously to oxygenate the patient's blood during surgery.
items.ex_zh: 这台先进的医疗设备在手术过程中持续运行，为患者的血液充氧。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to introducing fresh air, oxygen, or gas into a space, liquid, or soil to freshen, dry, or sustain biological and chemical processes. Nuances range from passive airing to active mechanical ventilation and chemical oxygenation.
groups.summary_zh: 指通入新鲜空气、氧气或气体以通风、干燥或充氧。
groups.desc_en: Introducing fresh air, oxygen, or gas flow through an enclosed space, liquid, or system, contrasting with natural draft by deliberate circulation or purification.
groups.desc_zh: 使新鲜空气、氧气或气流穿过密闭空间、液体或系统，区别于被动漏风，侧重主动循环换气或加氧净化。
groups.nuance_en: ventilate: circulating air through rooms or mechanical systems (room / mine / lungs) · air: freshening enclosed spaces or damp fabrics (room / sheets / grievances) · aerate: charging liquids or soil with circulating gas (soil / wine / blood) · oxygenate: biochemically or chemically infusing with oxygen (blood / tissue / water) · air out: thoroughly purging lingering odors from an enclosure (closet / bedroom / car)
groups.nuance_zh: ventilate: 机械或建筑性组织气流换气 (room / mine / lungs) · air: 开窗晾透以祛除室内或织物潮腐气 (room / sheets / grievances) · aerate: 充气使土壤疏松或令液体饱含气体 (soil / wine / blood) · oxygenate: 在生化或化学上注入足量氧气 (blood / tissue / water) · air out: 彻底敞开通风以散净积郁异味 (closet / bedroom / car)

groups.name: Verbal Enumeration & Recitation · 逐一列举与数说 (Enumerate, Recite, Reel off)
groups.tip: 逐条清点罗列细目，详尽说明各项细节

items.def_en: To recite or count off items or grievances in sequence, often checking them off mentally or on fingers
items.ex_en: She began to tick off her manager's annoying habits on her fingers.
items.ex_zh: 她开始掰着手指数落经理那些令人讨厌的习惯。

items.def_en: To give a full, precise, and itemized spoken or written account of something
items.ex_en: The extensive quarterly report will detail all financial transactions completed this year.
items.ex_zh: 这份详尽的季度报告将详细列出今年完成的所有金融交易。

items.def_en: To narrate a series of events, experiences, or facts in clear, sequential detail
items.ex_en: The elderly veteran began to recount his harrowing wartime experiences to the captive audience.
items.ex_zh: 这位老兵开始向入神的听众详细叙述他痛苦的战时经历。

items.def_en: 1. (formal) To name or list items, reasons, or details one by one in order.
items.ex_en: The official report sought to enumerate every single flaw discovered during the inspection.
items.ex_zh: 官方报告试图逐一列出检查中发现的每一个缺陷。

items.def_zh: 一气呵成地念出；滔滔不绝地背出
items.def_en: To recite a rapid, unbroken sequence of facts, names, or numbers effortlessly from memory
items.ex_en: The talented young student could effortlessly reel off the names of every world capital.
items.ex_zh: 这位天才小学者能毫不费力地一气背出世界上所有首都的名字。

items.def_zh: 讲得一清二楚；逐一详明
items.def_en: To explain something point by point in full, unmistakable, step-by-step clarity
items.ex_en: You don't need to spell out every detail; we get the general idea.
items.ex_zh: 你不需要把每个细节都阐释得那么细，我们明白大意。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe verbally detailing, recounting, or ticking through a succession of reasons, grievances, points, or achievements one after another in spoken discourse or rhetorical presentation.
groups.summary_zh: 指在言谈或论述中一五一十、逐条道出事实、理由或论点。
groups.desc_en: Uttering, citing, or accounting for items in an ordered sequence one by one, contrasting with vague summarizing by exhaustive, granular disclosure.
groups.desc_zh: 按顺序将项目一一道来、数算或引述，区别于模糊的笼统概括，强调巨细靡遗、条分缕析的详尽呈现。
groups.nuance_en: enumerate: formal, numbered listing of distinct items (grievances / rights / reasons) · reel off: rapid, effortless verbal delivery of a long list (facts / names / stats) · tick off: checking off items sequentially, sometimes with annoyance (sins / demands / complaints) · spell out: articulating terms explicitly and without ambiguity (details / terms / strategy) · recount: narrating events chronologically from memory (adventures / history / deeds)
groups.nuance_zh: enumerate: 正式逐条数算或列出 (grievances / rights / reasons) · reel off: 一口气连珠炮般熟练报出一长串 (facts / names / stats) · tick off: 逐项核对勾除，有时带愠怒之色 (sins / demands / complaints) · spell out: 掰开了揉碎了条分缕析地讲明 (details / terms / strategy) · recount: 凭记忆按时序详述往事或经历 (adventures / history / deeds)

groups.name: Vindicate & Defend Legitimacy · 辩护与证成 (Vindicate, Defend, Uphold, Champion)
groups.tip: 摆出合理论据为行为开脱辩明

items.def_en: to speak, write, or argue in support of someone or something against hostile criticism
items.ex_en: The experienced attorney stood up to defend her client against the baseless accusations.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的律师站出来为她的委托人辩护，反驳毫无根据的指控。

items.def_en: To provide a good reason for something or prove that an action or belief is reasonable.
items.ex_en: The minister struggled to justify the controversial decision to increase public transit fares.
items.ex_zh: 部长极力证明提高公共交通票价这一争议性决定的正当性。

items.def_en: to support, defend, or fight for a person, right, or opinion being unfairly targeted
items.ex_en: True friends will always stick up for you when others spread cruel gossip.
items.ex_zh: 当别人散播恶毒谣言时，真正的朋友总会站出来为你说话。

items.def_en: to confirm, support, or maintain a decision, principle, or stance as correct and sound
items.ex_en: The supreme judicial court voted to uphold the original ruling made last spring.
items.ex_zh: 最高司法法院投票决定维持去年春天作出的原始判决。

items.def_en: to clear someone of blame or prove an argument or action to have been fully warranted
items.ex_en: Newly discovered forensic evidence will ultimately vindicate the wrongfully imprisoned investigator.
items.ex_zh: 新发现的法医证据最终将证明这位被冤入狱的调查员无罪。

items.def_en: to supply solid evidence or reasoning to demonstrate that a claim or argument is true
items.ex_en: The lead researcher failed to substantiate his extraordinary claim with verifiable data.
items.ex_zh: 首席研究员未能用可验证的数据来证实他那非同寻常的主张。

groups.summary_en: Focuses on arguing for the correctness, legitimacy, or validity of an action, stance, or person against accusation or criticism. It emphasizes rational and moral argumentation.
groups.summary_zh: 指提供法理、道义或事实依据，为某立场或行为正名辩白。
groups.desc_en: Establishing the justice, truth, or rightful standing of an accused person, principle, or act against challenge, differing from mere advocacy by successful exoneration.
groups.desc_zh: 在遭受质疑或攻击后确立当事人、原则或行为的正当与真实性，区别于单纯口头声援，强调洗刷与证成。
groups.nuance_en: vindicate: clearing name or doctrine through subsequent vindicating proof (reputation / judgment / innocence) · defend: repelling active criticism or legal indictment (rights / honor / policy) · uphold: judicially or ethically affirming valid standards (verdict / constitution / tradition) · justify: offering valid normative reasons for past actions (actions / expense / conduct) · substantiate: verifying factual truth with empirical evidence (claims / charges / theory)
groups.nuance_zh: vindicate: 借事实或证据洗刷污名并证成正确性 (reputation / judgment / innocence) · defend: 抵御外界指控并护卫正当性 (rights / honor / policy) · uphold: 司法或道义上维持、确认既有原则 (verdict / constitution / tradition) · justify: 阐明过往行为具有合理性与依据 (actions / expense / conduct) · substantiate: 出示真凭实据坐实指控或理论 (claims / charges / theory)

groups.name: Violate & Infringe · 侵犯与违犯 (Infringe, Violate, Encroach)
groups.tip: 越界侵蚀他人合法权益与法规

items.def_en: Invade someone's sphere of interest or hurt their feelings by overstepping boundaries
items.ex_en: You should be careful not to tread on his authority during the meeting.
items.ex_zh: 在会议期间，你应该小心不要侵犯他的职权。

items.def_en: Gradually intrude upon or infringe on someone's property, rights, or personal time
items.ex_en: Excessive overtime demands began to encroach on the personal time of the employees.
items.ex_zh: 过度的加班要求开始逐渐侵蚀员工的个人时间。

items.def_zh: 侵犯（权利、隐私等，infringe on/upon）；违犯，触犯（法律、条约）
items.def_en: 1. (infringe on/upon) to limit, encroach on, or violate someone's legal rights, freedom, or privacy. 2. to break or violate a law, rule, or contract.
items.ex_en: Critics argued that the new surveillance measures would infringe on fundamental civil liberties.
items.ex_zh: 批评人士指出，新的监控措施将侵犯基本的公民自由。

items.def_en: Go beyond the acceptable limits of a law, rule, or moral standard
items.ex_en: Corrupt state officials who deliberately transgress the law must face severe criminal penalties.
items.ex_zh: 故意违犯法律的腐败官员必须面临严厉的刑事处罚。

items.def_en: Directly break or fail to respect a law, agreement, principle, or someone's privacy
items.ex_en: Unauthorized drone surveillance operations directly violate international maritime laws and sovereignty agreements.
items.ex_zh: 未经授权的无人机监视行动直接违反了国际海洋法和主权协定。

items.def_zh: 撕毁；违反（契约、保密协议）
items.def_en: Fail to observe the terms of a legal agreement, contract, or code of conduct
items.ex_en: Disclosing proprietary corporate data will seriously breach your legally binding employment contract.
items.ex_zh: 泄露公司专有数据将严重违反具有法律约束力的雇佣合同。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to breaching, undermining, or stepping over legal limits, constitutional rights, contracts, or boundaries.
groups.summary_zh: 指逾越界限、破坏条约法例或侵蚀侵犯他人的正当权利与领地。
groups.desc_en: Breaching, overstepping, or dishonoring laws, boundaries, treaties, or sovereign rights, differing from civil disagreement by aggressive non-compliance.
groups.desc_zh: 以具有侵害性或违逆性的行为逾越法律、边境、公约或主权，区别于一般分歧，具有非正义的违犯性。
groups.nuance_en: violate: brazen desecration or disruption of fundamental rights (sovereignty / truce / privacy) · breach: snapping contractual, security, or ethical boundaries (contract / security / protocol) · infringe: legally trespassing upon intellectual or defined liberties (patent / copyright / rules) · transgress: crossing moral, social, or religious boundaries (limits / moral laws / borders) · encroach on: slowly usurping perimeter rights or space (prerogative / wetlands / autonomy)
groups.nuance_zh: violate: 粗暴践踏主权、休战协议或基本人权 (sovereignty / truce / privacy) · breach: 撕裂、击穿合同信任或安全防线 (contract / security / protocol) · infringe: 法律意义上侵蚀专利或既定自由 (patent / copyright / rules) · transgress: 逾越道德、风俗或宗教禁忌底线 (limits / moral laws / borders) · encroach on: 蚕食占领管辖外空间或特权 (prerogative / wetlands / autonomy)

groups.name: Violent Shudder & Mechanical Vibration · 剧烈颠簸与机械震颤 (Judder, Shudder, Rattle)
groups.tip: 机械或物体剧烈颠簸与颤动

items.def_zh: 格格作响地振动；使嘎嘎作响
items.def_en: To make or cause to make a rapid succession of short, sharp knocking sounds while shaking
items.ex_en: Fierce gale-force winds began to rattle the loose metal shutters on the cottage.
items.ex_zh: 狂风开始吹得小屋松动的金属百叶窗格格作响。
items.ex2_en: The loose windowpanes began to rattle violently during the sudden midnight thunderstorm.
items.ex2_zh: 在半夜突如其来的雷暴中，松动的窗玻璃开始剧烈晃荡作响。

items.def_en: To move or cause to move continuously and rapidly back and forth
items.ex_en: Heavy freight trucks cause the old wooden floorboards to vibrate with tremendous force.
items.ex_zh: 重型货车使得旧木地板剧烈地震动起来。
items.ex2_en: The cellular phone continued to vibrate noisily against the polished wooden desk.
items.ex2_zh: 手机在光滑的木书桌上不停地嗡嗡震动。

items.def_en: To rattle noisily and violently while moving or shaking
items.ex_en: Cheap metal plates began to clatter loudly across the cafeteria during the tremor.
items.ex_zh: 在震动中，廉价的金属盘子在食堂里乒乒乓乓地响个不停。
items.ex2_en: The hurried waiter clattered dirty dishes loudly as he cleared the table.
items.ex2_zh: 匆忙的服务员在收拾餐桌时把脏盘子弄得叮当乱响。

items.def_en: To shake violently and momentarily, typically from cold, horror, or mechanical strain
items.ex_en: The massive locomotive engine seemed to shudder under the immense mechanical strain.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的机车引擎在巨大的机械负荷下剧烈震颤起来。

items.def_en: To shake or sway abnormally with a rhythmic rocking motion, especially of a vehicle's wheels or frame
items.ex_en: The front wheels began to shimmy violently once the vehicle reached highway speeds.
items.ex_zh: 车辆一旦达到高速公路行驶速度，前轮就开始剧烈晃动。

items.def_en: (especially of a vehicle or machine) to shake and vibrate violently and noisily
items.ex_en: The old washing machine started to judder violently during its final spin cycle.
items.ex_zh: 旧洗衣机在最后一次脱水过程中开始剧烈震颤颠簸。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe intense, jerky, or noisy physical vibration and shaking, typical of malfunctioning machinery, vehicles, or profound physical shock. They contrast sharply with gentle quivering by emphasizing mechanical violent oscillation or audible rattling.
groups.summary_zh: 描述机械失灵、车辆颠簸或机体遭受强烈冲击时的剧烈震颤与杂音抖动。
groups.desc_en: Subjecting an entity or mechanism to violent, shuddering, or uncoordinated mechanical oscillations, differing from gentle harmonic vibration by harsh, jarring instability.
groups.desc_zh: 使机械装置或机体遭受剧烈、不协调的颠簸、震颤或抖动，区别于平滑谐振，体现出刺耳失控的机械颠簸感。
groups.nuance_en: judder: heavy, violent low-frequency mechanical jerking (brakes / engine / airframe) · shudder: convulsive full-body or structural trembling from shock (ship / locomotive / frame) · rattle: rapid succession of short, sharp impact clatters (windows / loose bolts / carriage) · vibrate: high-frequency rhythmic oscillating motion (needle / membrane / motor) · clatter: noisy discordant clashing of hard moving parts (dishes / tracks / mechanism)
groups.nuance_zh: judder: 刹车或机械过载时沉重剧烈的低频抽搐跳动 (brakes / engine / airframe) · shudder: 受到剧烈冲击时全身或大型结构痉挛震荡 (ship / locomotive / frame) · rattle: 紧固件松动所致持续急促的嗒嗒撞击碰撞 (windows / loose bolts / carriage) · vibrate: 规律、高频的往复物理微震 (needle / membrane / motor) · clatter: 坚硬物件相互磕碰发出的嘈杂哐啷声 (dishes / tracks / mechanism)

groups.name: Visit & Frequent · 探访与造访 (Haunt, Patronize, Drop by)
groups.tip: 往来特定场所探望

items.def_en: To visit a particular place often or regularly.
items.ex_en: Distinguished scholars and artists often frequent this quiet historical library in the capital.
items.ex_zh: 杰出的学者和艺术家经常光顾首都这座幽静的古老图书馆。

items.def_en: To make an informal, unannounced, or brief visit to a person or place
items.ex_en: Why don't you drop by my office for coffee this afternoon?
items.ex_zh: 今天下午你顺道来我办公室喝杯咖啡如何？

items.def_en: To visit a place briefly, often to run a quick errand or say hello
items.ex_en: I need to pop into the grocery store to grab some fresh milk.
items.ex_zh: 我需要顺便去一下杂货店买点新鲜牛奶。

items.def_en: To pay a formal or deliberate short visit to someone at their home or office
items.ex_en: The foreign ambassador decided to call on the foreign minister yesterday afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 外国大使昨天下午决定正式造访外交部长。

items.def_en: To visit a particular place repeatedly and persistently, becoming a familiar presence there
items.ex_en: Homeless stray cats regularly haunt the narrow alleyways behind the bustling fish market.
items.ex_zh: 无家可归的流浪猫经常出没在熙熙攘攘的鱼市后面的狭窄小巷里。

items.def_en: To visit a restaurant, shop, or establishment regularly as a paying customer
items.ex_en: Affluent local residents regularly patronize this independent organic grocery store in the city.
items.ex_zh: 富裕的当地居民经常光顾市内这家独立的有机杂货店。

groups.summary_en: Covers visiting physical locations or individuals, especially with repeated regularity or informality. 'Frequent' implies habitual visitation, 'patronize' highlights recurring customer presence, and 'drop by' captures brief informal visits.
groups.summary_zh: 指经常出入某处场所或非正式地上门拜访巡视。
groups.desc_en: Presenting oneself as a caller, patron, or habitual visitor at a location or to a person, contrasting with long-term residence by bounded temporary stays.
groups.desc_zh: 作为到访者、顾客或常客造访某地或拜访某人，区别于长期定居，属于有时限的短期驻足或定期往来。
groups.nuance_en: frequent: repeatedly visiting a commercial or public establishment (cafe / theater / pub) · patronize: regularly buying from a business, or acting condescendingly (shops / restaurants / arts) · haunt: perpetually lingering at a favorite hangout or past scene (library / clubs / memories) · call on: paying an intentional, respectful, or formal social visit (client / neighbour / minister) · drop by: informal, spontaneous brief visit without an appointment (office / house / apartment)
groups.nuance_zh: frequent: 频繁穿梭光顾某公共或商业场所 (cafe / theater / pub) · patronize: 成为商家老主顾经常光顾惠顾 (shops / restaurants / arts) · haunt: 魂牵梦萦或长年流连盘桓于旧地 (library / clubs / memories) · call on: 正式、礼节性地上门登门拜会 (client / neighbour / minister) · drop by: 不经预约顺道短暂停留的非正式串门 (office / house / apartment)

groups.name: Visual Detection & Noticing · 察觉与发现 (Spot, Catch Sight Of, Detect)
groups.tip: 视线扫过捕捉特定目标

items.def_en: To suddenly see someone or something, often briefly or unexpectedly
items.ex_en: She suddenly managed to catch sight of her former professor in the crowd.
items.ex_zh: 她突然在人群中瞥见了自己以前的教授。

items.def_en: To manage to see or identify something with difficulty
items.ex_en: Through the dense fog, he could barely make out the distant coastal lighthouse.
items.ex_zh: 穿过浓雾，他勉强辨认出远处的海岸灯塔。

items.def_en: To see someone or something for a brief moment, often incompletely
items.ex_en: Fans stood in the pouring rain just to glimpse the arriving movie star.
items.ex_zh: 影迷们站在倾盆大雨中，只为能隐约瞥见抵达的电影明星一眼。

items.def_en: To pick out or focus visual attention on one particular person or thing among many
items.ex_en: It is unfair to single out one player when the whole team performed poorly.
items.ex_zh: 在全队表现都很差的情况下，单单挑出一名球员来责备是不公平的。

items.def_en: To see, detect, or recognize someone or something, especially with difficulty or after careful searching.
items.ex_en: Sharp-eyed rangers were the first to spot the elusive snow leopard yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 目光敏锐的护林员昨天率先发现了那只神出鬼没的雪豹。

items.def_zh: 看到；发现（远处的微小或隐蔽目标）
items.def_en: To manage to see something, especially after looking for a long time or at a great distance
items.ex_en: Lookouts were finally able to sight enemy warships on the hazy morning horizon.
items.ex_zh: 瞭望员终于在清晨朦胧的地平线上看到了敌方战舰。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe visually picking out, identifying, or noticing someone or something, especially when obscured, distant, or embedded in a crowded background.
groups.summary_zh: 强调在纷杂或隐蔽环境中敏锐地发现、认出或捕捉到目标。
groups.desc_en: Involves successfully isolating or distinguishing a visual target from a background or under difficult conditions, unlike passive 'see' or sustained 'watch'.
groups.desc_zh: 强调在复杂背景或视线受阻等不利条件下成功捕捉、辨识出特定目标，而非被动的'see'或持续注视的'watch'。
groups.nuance_en: spot: successfully detect among distractors (target / error / trend) · glimpse: catch a momentary, partial view (figure / face / silhouette) · make out: discern with perceptual difficulty (shape / writing / landmark) · sight: visually locate, especially after searching (shore / bird / submarine) · catch sight of: suddenly notice unexpectedly (movement / stranger / friend)
groups.nuance_zh: spot: 在杂乱背景中精准发现或认出 (target / error / trend) · glimpse: 短暂瞥见、浮光掠影 (figure / face / silhouette) · make out: 极度费力地辨认出轮廓或细节 (shape / writing / landmark) · sight: （历经搜寻后）首次观测到 (shore / bird / submarine) · catch sight of: 突然无意间捕捉到视线 (movement / stranger / friend)

groups.name: Vocal Sighs & Murmurs · 叹息与呻吟 (Sigh, Groan, Moan)
groups.tip: 以叹气呻吟声表达身心痛楚

items.def_en: Emit a long, audible breath expressing sadness, relief, tiredness, or longing
items.ex_en: Exhausted after the long journey, she could only sigh with profound relief.
items.ex_zh: 长途跋涉后精疲力竭的她只能深感释然地叹了口气。

items.def_en: Make a series of low, feeble, fretful sounds expressive of fear, pain, or unhappiness
items.ex_en: The frightened little puppy began to whimper softly in the cold, dark room.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的小狗在阴冷黑暗的房间里低声呜咽起来。

items.def_zh: 发出“啊”的声音（表示赞叹、欣喜或痛苦等）
items.def_en: To make a prolonged 'aah' sound, expressing pleasure, relief, admiration, or pain.
items.ex_en: She stepped into the warm therapeutic bath and let out a satisfied aah.
items.ex_zh: 她迈入温热的理疗浴池，发出一声满意的“啊”的赞叹。

items.def_en: Make a prolonged, low sound expressing physical suffering, sexual pleasure, or discontent
items.ex_en: The injured hiker began to moan softly while waiting for rescue teams.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的徒步旅行者在等待救援队时低声痛苦地呻吟。

items.def_en: Inhale suddenly and audibly with an open mouth, typically due to shock, pain, or breathlessness
items.ex_en: Onlookers let out an audible gasp when the reckless acrobat suddenly slipped.
items.ex_zh: 当鲁莽的杂技演员突然脚滑时，围观的人群发出一阵倒吸凉气的声音。

items.def_en: Make a deep, inarticulate sound conveying pain, despair, or intense disapproval
items.ex_en: Students began to groan aloud when the strict professor assigned more tedious homework.
items.ex_zh: 当严厉的教授布置更多乏味的作业时，学生们开始大声发牢骚。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote involuntary or semi-voluntary non-verbal vocalizations that express physical sensations or deep emotional states such as relief, pleasure, sorrow, or physical discomfort.
groups.summary_zh: 表示因疼痛、解脱、愉悦或忧伤而发出的叹息、呻吟等非语言人声。
groups.desc_en: Denotes involuntary or expressive non-verbal vocalizations of physical discomfort, emotional relief, or distress, contrasting with deliberate articulated 'speak'.
groups.desc_zh: 指表达身体不适、情感释放或痛苦时发出的非言语叹息或低吟，区别于清晰有意的'speak'。
groups.nuance_en: sigh: release audible breath from relief or weary resignation (relief / despair / boredom) · groan: deep inarticulate sound of pain or dismay (pain / displeasure / effort) · moan: low prolonged sound of suffering or sensual pleasure (agony / pleasure / sorrow) · gasp: sharp intake of breath from shock or exertion (shock / air / surprise) · whimper: low feeble cry of fear or pain (child / dog / pain)
groups.nuance_zh: sigh: 呼出长气以表释怀或疲惫无奈 (relief / despair / boredom) · groan: 表达痛苦或懊恼的低沉呻吟 (pain / displeasure / effort) · moan: 拖长音调的哀鸣或欢愉呻吟 (agony / pleasure / sorrow) · gasp: 震惊或缺氧时倒吸凉气 (shock / air / surprise) · whimper: 恐惧或孱弱时断断续续的呜咽 (child / dog / pain)

groups.name: Volunteer & Offer · 自愿奉献与主动提供 (Volunteer, Offer, Step Forward)
groups.tip: 主动提供帮助或服务

items.def_en: to state one's willingness to give assistance, take action, or present something
items.ex_en: The kind neighbor decided to offer immediate financial assistance to the struggling family.
items.ex_zh: 好心的邻居决定立即向这个陷入困境的家庭提供经济援助。

items.def_zh: 自愿做，主动提供；自愿服役
items.def_en: 1. to offer to do something without being forced or paid 2. to offer information, opinions, or assistance willingly 3. to enlist for military or social service willingly
items.ex_en: Several experienced local retired nurses offered to volunteer at the temporary health clinic.
items.ex_zh: 几位经验丰富的当地退休护士主动提出去临时诊所做志愿服务。

items.def_en: to present oneself willingly to help, take on responsibility, or provide testimony
items.ex_en: The brave eyewitness decided to step forward and provide crucial testimony in court.
items.ex_zh: 勇敢的目击证人决定挺身而出，在法庭上提供关键证词。

items.def_zh: 投入协作，自愿助一臂之力
items.def_en: to join enthusiastically with others to help accomplish a shared task
items.ex_en: If we all pitch in, we can finish clearing the yard in an hour.
items.ex_zh: 如果我们大家齐心协力，一个小时就能把院子清理干净。

items.def_zh: 举手自荐，自愿接下任务
items.def_en: to signify that one is willing to volunteer for an assignment or duty
items.ex_en: Who is going to put their hand up to organize the office party?
items.ex_zh: 谁愿意举手自荐来组织这次办公室聚会？

items.def_zh: 主动呈递，提出（建议/帮助）
items.def_en: to hold out or put forward something graciously for someone to accept
items.ex_en: The seasoned diplomat chose to proffer a polite compromise to break the impasse.
items.ex_zh: 经验丰富的外交官选择主动提出一个礼貌的妥协方案以打破僵局。

groups.summary_en: Involves spontaneously, willingly, and freely offering one's services, time, aid, or information without compulsion, command, or monetary demand.
groups.summary_zh: 指不求回报、无外界强迫下自告奋勇承担任务或主动提供帮助与信息。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on uncoerced, proactive personal initiative to provide services, aid, or resources without compulsion, contrasting with formal or obligatory 'assign'.
groups.desc_zh: 强调不受强迫、出于主观意愿的主动提议、请缨或贡献，区别于被动接受安排或法定的'assign'。
groups.nuance_en: volunteer: freely undertake a task without obligation (service / time / information) · offer: formally present for acceptance or rejection (assistance / help / apology) · step forward: proactively identify oneself to help or take responsibility (witness / volunteer / candidate) · pitch in: join collectively to assist in a shared task (effort / money / chores) · proffer: tender delicately or ceremoniously (advice / handshake / resignation)
groups.nuance_zh: volunteer: 自觉自愿承担任务或提供 (service / time / information) · offer: 主动提出供对方选择接纳与否 (assistance / help / apology) · step forward: 挺身而出、主动站出来承担 (witness / volunteer / candidate) · pitch in: 众人齐心协力投入支援 (effort / money / chores) · proffer: 郑重或谦逊地递上、提出 (advice / handshake / resignation)

groups.name: Vomit & Puke · 呕吐与反胃 (Vomit, Puke, Throw up)
groups.tip: 恶心反胃将胃内容物吐出

items.def_en: (informal British) To vomit or bring up one's stomach contents
items.ex_en: He drank far too much sour cider and had to chuck up outside.
items.ex_zh: 他喝了太多发酸的苹果酒，只得在外面吐了起来。

items.def_en: To expel food and digestive fluids involuntarily through the mouth
items.ex_en: The investigation threw up some unexpected problems for the company.
items.ex_zh: 调查给公司暴露出了一些意想不到的问题。

items.def_en: To eject matter forcefully from the stomach through the mouth
items.ex_en: Severe food poisoning caused the distressed patient to vomit repeatedly throughout the night.
items.ex_zh: 严重的食物中毒导致痛苦的患者整夜不停地呕吐。

items.def_en: (informal) To vomit or bring up contents from the stomach.
items.ex_en: He drank too much cheap tequila last night and started to puke everywhere.
items.ex_zh: 他昨晚廉价龙舌兰喝得太多，开始到处呕吐起来。

items.def_en: (informal) To vomit or disgorge the contents of one's stomach
items.ex_en: The dizzy carnival ride made several kids barf their lunch onto the grass.
items.ex_zh: 令人头晕的游乐场设施让几个孩子把午饭都吐到了草地上。

items.def_en: To make strong, involuntary muscular spasms as if about to vomit
items.ex_en: Smelling the rotten meat in the cellar caused his stomach to violently heave.
items.ex_zh: 闻到地窖里腐肉的气味，他的胃部剧烈干呕起来。

groups.summary_en: Verbs here designate the involuntary, forceful physical ejection of stomach contents through the mouth due to nausea, sickness, or intoxicants. The frame spans clinical terms to casual colloquial expressions.
groups.summary_zh: 指因恶心或疾病通过口腔剧烈排空胃中内容物。
groups.desc_en: Describes the biological or physical ejection of stomach contents via the mouth, varying primarily in register from clinical to informal and colloquial.
groups.desc_zh: 指胃部内容物经食道口部猛烈倒流排出的生理动作，主要通过临床、口语与俚语的语域风格区分。
groups.nuance_en: vomit: clinical and standard ejection of stomach contents (blood / food / bile) · throw up: common colloquial equivalent for emesis (dinner / meal / guts) · puke: blunt, informal emesis (beer / guts / bile) · barf: highly informal, colloquial regurgitation (breakfast / lunch / drink) · heave: make violent dry or wet retching motions (chest / stomach / guts)
groups.nuance_zh: vomit: 临床或书面正式的呕吐 (blood / food / bile) · throw up: 通俗日常的吐出、呕吐 (dinner / meal / guts) · puke: 粗俗直白的口语呕吐 (beer / guts / bile) · barf: 俚语化的翻胃吐酒或食物 (breakfast / lunch / drink) · heave: 剧烈的干呕或伴随痉挛的恶心 (chest / stomach / guts)

groups.name: Vomit & Regurgitate · 呕吐与反胃 (Throw Up, Regurgitate, Spew)
groups.tip: 胃部食物倒流剧烈反胃

items.def_en: To bring swallowed food up again to the mouth
items.ex_en: The baby began to regurgitate sour milk all over her father's new shirt.
items.ex_zh: 婴儿开始把发酸的奶水反流得父亲的新衬衫到处都是。

items.def_en: To eject matter from the stomach through the mouth; vomit
items.ex_en: The investigation threw up some unexpected problems for the company.
items.ex_zh: 调查给公司暴露出了一些意想不到的问题。

items.def_en: (informal) To vomit
items.ex_en: She rushed toward the dirty bathroom stall just in time to puke violently.
items.ex_zh: 她及时冲进肮脏的卫生间隔间，剧烈地吐了起来。

items.def_en: To make the sound or movement of vomiting; retch
items.ex_en: Overcome by terrible nausea, the exhausted sailor could only heave over the railing.
items.ex_zh: 极度恶心的疲惫水手只能趴在栏杆上不停地干呕。

items.def_en: To discharge the contents of the stomach up through the mouth, especially because of illness.
items.ex_en: Patients suffering from acute food poisoning frequently vomit and experience severe dehydration.
items.ex_zh: 遭受急性食物中毒的患者常常呕吐并伴有严重脱水。

items.def_en: To vomit copiously and forcefully
items.ex_en: After taking the bad pill, he began to spew vile bile endlessly.
items.ex_zh: 服下变质的药丸后，他开始止不住地狂吐胆汁。
items.ex2_en: Hot molten lava began to spew continuously from the rumbling volcanic crater.
items.ex2_zh: 滚烫的熔岩开始从隆隆作响的火山口不断喷涌而出。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers the physiological act of forcefully expelling the contents of the stomach through the mouth, ranging from clinical and formal terms to vivid, everyday conversational idioms.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖将胃内容物经口剧烈排出的生理动作，包含日常口语与医学书面表达。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses both biological emesis and metaphorical violent expulsion or passive reflux of substance or words, contrasting with gradual 'leak' or 'drain'.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖反刍反胃的生理排出，以及向外剧烈喷吐、言语机械复述等隐喻动作，区别于平缓的'leak'或'drain'。
groups.nuance_en: regurgitate: bring swallowed food back up, or mechanically repeat information (food / facts / ideology) · spew: forcefully and profusely eject liquid or vitriol (lava / toxic waste / abuse) · vomit: medically or violently discharge gastric contents (blood / poison / meal) · throw up: colloquially eject gut contents (undigested food / contents / hands) · heave: produce convulsive upward spasms of retching (stomach / dry heaves / chest)
groups.nuance_zh: regurgitate: 生理反刍，或机械不经思考地复述 (food / facts / ideology) · spew: 猛烈喷射溢出，或喷薄恶语 (lava / toxic waste / abuse) · vomit: 胃内容物的剧烈喷出 (blood / poison / meal) · throw up: 常见的翻胃呕吐 (undigested food / contents / hands) · heave: 伴随剧烈痉挛的作呕或耸动 (stomach / dry heaves / chest)

groups.name: Vote & Poll · 投票与表决 (Poll, Cast, Refer)
groups.tip: 政治选举中投出选票

items.def_en: To formally express a choice or opinion in an election, referendum, or meeting
items.ex_en: Citizens will vote on the proposed tax reform during the upcoming national referendum.
items.ex_zh: 公民将在即将举行的全民公决中就拟议的税改方案进行投票。

items.def_en: To register a vote or ballot formally in an election
items.ex_en: Electors solemnly gathered at dawn to cast their fateful ballots for the republic.
items.ex_zh: 选民们拂晓时庄严集会，为共和国投下决定命运的选票。

items.def_en: (parliamentary) To separate into distinct groups to register formal 'ayes' and 'noes' votes
items.ex_en: The Speaker rang the bell, ordering the members of parliament to divide.
items.ex_zh: 议长摇响铃铛，命令议员们分列两边进行表决。
items.ex2_en: The party whips divided the voting members quickly across the parliamentary chamber.
items.ex2_zh: 党鞭迅速将议会大厅内的投票议员分成两方。

items.def_en: To survey opinions systematically or to receive a specified number of votes in an election
items.ex_en: The independent candidate managed to poll surprisingly well in the rural conservative districts.
items.ex_zh: 这位独立候选人在保守的乡村选区获得了出人意料的高得票率。

items.def_en: To vote or ask people to vote secretly on an issue or candidate.
items.ex_en: Union leaders decided to ballot their members secretly before initiating a nationwide strike.
items.ex_zh: 工会领导决定在发起全国性罢工之前对会员进行无记名投票表决。

items.def_en: To solicit votes, subscriptions, or opinions directly from individuals across an electorate
items.ex_en: Volunteers went door-to-door across the neighborhood to canvass for the environmental candidate.
items.ex_zh: 志愿者们走街串巷挨家挨户游说，为环保候选人拉票。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses formal procedures where participants register their preference, cast ballots, or poll a population to reach a collective political or civic decision.
groups.summary_zh: 公民或成员通过投递选票、民调等程序进行集体表决。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to structured collective decision-making or opinion-gathering procedures within civic, political, or organizational contexts, unlike informal 'choose'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在政治、社团或集体决策程序中按章程表决或民意测验，区别于随意的私人'choose'。
groups.nuance_en: vote: formally express a choice in an election or debate (resolution / candidate / budget) · cast: formally deposit or register a ballot (ballot / vote / lot) · poll: survey the opinions or count the votes of a group (voters / electorate / public) · ballot: conduct a secret vote or record of voting (members / delegates / union) · canvass: systematically solicit votes or determine opinions (constituency / neighborhood / voters)
groups.nuance_zh: vote: 正式投票表决支持或反对 (resolution / candidate / budget) · cast: 庄重投下或行使选票 (ballot / vote / lot) · poll: 对群体进行民调、统计得票 (voters / electorate / public) · ballot: 进行无记名投票表决 (members / delegates / union) · canvass: 逐户游说、系统性拉票或探寻意向 (constituency / neighborhood / voters)

groups.name: Wait & Await · 等待与守候 (Await, Bide, Linger)
groups.tip: 静止期待后续的发生

items.def_en: To stay where one is or delay action until a particular time or event occurs.
items.ex_en: Please wait here quietly until the doctor is ready to see the patient.
items.ex_zh: 请在此安静等候，直到医生准备好接诊病人。

items.def_en: To spend time waiting or wandering idly in an area without clear purpose
items.ex_en: Bored teenagers often hang around the convenience store after school with nothing to do.
items.ex_zh: 无聊的青少年放学后常常无所事事地在便利店附近闲逛游荡。

items.def_en: To wait for a short period, especially during an interruption or on telephone calls
items.ex_en: Please hold on for a moment while I transfer your call to billing.
items.ex_zh: 请稍候片刻，我这就把您的电话转接到计费部门。

items.def_en: To wait expectantly for someone or something, or to be in store for someone
items.ex_en: Diplomats anxiously await the official communiqué regarding the conclusion of bilateral trade negotiations.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们焦急地等待有关双边贸易谈判结束的正式公报。

items.def_en: To stay in a place longer than necessary, reluctant to depart
items.ex_en: The guests continued to linger in the courtyard long after the party ended.
items.ex_zh: 聚会结束很久之后，客人们仍然在院子里徘徊不肯离去。

items.def_en: (one's time) To wait patiently for a favorable opportunity before taking decisive action
items.ex_en: The exiled prince resolved to bide his time until the tyrant's grip weakened.
items.ex_zh: 流亡的王子决定静候时机，直至暴君的统治力量削弱。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers remaining in a place or postponing an action until an anticipated person, time, or event arrives, ranging from neutral staying put to expectant or patient endurance.
groups.summary_zh: 指停留某处、推迟行动以期盼或守候人、事、时机到来。
groups.desc_en: Denotes staying in a state of suspended activity or patience expecting a future event or arrival, differing from purposeless 'stop' or permanent 'stay'.
groups.desc_zh: 指在预期特定事件或人物到来之前保持暂停、耐心等待的状态，区别于无目标的'stop'或永久驻留的'stay'。
groups.nuance_en: wait: general suspension of action pending an occurrence (turn / results / arrival) · await: formally or expectantly anticipate a definite outcome (decision / verdict / fate) · bide: patiently mark time, typically for a favorable chance (time / moment / chance) · linger: stay longer than necessary or expected (doubts / scent / doorstep) · hang around: wait idly and aimlessly in a vicinity (corner / lobby / backstage)
groups.nuance_zh: wait: 最通用的静候或耽搁 (turn / results / arrival) · await: 书面庄重地静候确定的判决或结果 (decision / verdict / fate) · bide: 隐忍等待最有利的时机 (time / moment / chance) · linger: 迟迟不去、逗留徘徊 (doubts / scent / doorstep) · hang around: 无所事事地在附近闲逛磨蹭 (corner / lobby / backstage)

groups.name: Waive & Forgo · 弃权与自愿放弃 (Forgo, Forfeit, Cede)
groups.tip: 自愿放弃索赔或特权

items.def_en: To officially surrender your legal rights, property, or title by signing a document
items.ex_en: He inadvertently signed away the copyright to his debut novel.
items.ex_zh: 他不慎签字放弃了自己处女作小说的版权。

items.def_zh: 放弃（权利、要求等）；免除，不强求遵守
items.def_en: 1. To officially and voluntarily give up a legal right, claim, or rule, or decide not to insist on a requirement.
items.ex_en: The applicant agreed to waive all claims to future royalties from the patent.
items.ex_zh: 申请人同意正式放弃对该专利未来所有特许权使用费的索赔权。

items.def_en: To lose the right to have or do something because you broke a rule, contract, or law
items.ex_en: Tenants who violate the lease terms will automatically forfeit their initial security deposit.
items.ex_zh: 违反租赁条款的租户将自动丧失其初始押金。

items.def_en: To formally give up possession of territory, authority, or rights to another country or entity
items.ex_en: Following the war, the defeated empire was forced to cede several strategic provinces.
items.ex_zh: 战争结束后，战败的帝国被迫割让了数个战略省份。

items.def_en: To decide not to have, do, or enjoy something pleasant or advantageous
items.ex_en: To pay for college tuition, he decided to forgo buying a new car.
items.ex_zh: 为了支付大学学费，他决定放弃购买新车。

items.def_en: To yield possession, control, or a right to someone else under pressure or obligation
items.ex_en: Under intense regulatory scrutiny, the firm was ordered to surrender its operating license.
items.ex_zh: 在严密监管下，该企业被迫交出了其经营许可证。

groups.summary_en: This frame highlights voluntarily relinquishing an entitlement, privilege, claim, or requirement, usually in a formal, legal, or gracious concession.
groups.summary_zh: 指自愿、正式地放弃自身合法权益、索赔权或应得待遇。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the deliberate, voluntary surrender or relinquishment of a right, privilege, claim, or opportunity, unlike involuntary 'lose' or 'drop'.
groups.desc_zh: 强调自觉、自愿地放弃或割让合法权利、索赔要求、特权或良机，区别于被动遗失的'lose'或丢弃的'drop'。
groups.nuance_en: waive: legally or officially give up a claim or requirement (fee / right / immunity) · forgo: voluntarily do without a pleasure or advantage (privilege / opportunity / salary) · forfeit: lose or surrender as a penalty for wrongdoing (deposit / license / title) · cede: formally yield territory or authority under pressure (territory / power / control) · surrender: deliver up possession or control, often reluctantly (weapon / autonomy / custody)
groups.nuance_zh: waive: 法律或程序上主动豁免、放弃权益 (fee / right / immunity) · forgo: 自制地克制、主动舍弃享乐或好处 (privilege / opportunity / salary) · forfeit: 因违规、受罚而丧失或被没收 (deposit / license / title) · cede: （常在条约或压力下）正式割让领土或权限 (territory / power / control) · surrender: 迫于形势缴械投降或交出主权 (weapon / autonomy / custody)

groups.name: Warn & Alert · 告诫与示警 (Warn, Alert, Forewarn)
groups.tip: 从寻常提醒升级为拉响警报

items.def_en: (+ against/about) To advise someone to be careful or prudent to avoid a mistake or risk
items.ex_en: Financial advisors caution clients against investing their life savings in volatile crypto markets.
items.ex_zh: 财务顾问告诫客户，切忌将一生的积蓄投资于动荡的加密市场。

items.def_zh: 预先走漏风声；向……通风报信
items.def_en: To provide confidential advance warning or confidential hints about impending events
items.ex_en: An anonymous insider managed to tip off detectives before the suspects fled town.
items.ex_zh: 一名匿名知情人设法在嫌疑人逃离小镇前向侦探通风报信。

items.def_en: (+ about/of) To tell someone in advance about impending danger, harm, or unpleasant consequences
items.ex_en: Meteorologists warn residents about the imminent danger of flash floods along the coast.
items.ex_zh: 气象学家警告沿海居民防范即将发生山洪暴发的危险。

items.def_zh: 向……报警，使警觉，使注意到
items.def_en: (+ to) To warn someone of a potential danger or problem, or make them aware of a fact.
items.ex_en: Automated security monitors alert technicians to unexpected spikes in server temperature immediately.
items.ex_zh: 自动化监控系统会立即向技术人员报警提示服务器温度的异常升高。

items.def_zh: 预先警告，先发制人通报
items.def_en: To warn or notify someone in advance about a coming risk or eventuality
items.ex_en: Scouts rushed back to forewarn the garrison of the enemy's covert nighttime advance.
items.ex_zh: 侦察兵火速赶回，就敌人夜间秘密推进的情况预先警告守军。

items.def_en: To cause sudden anxiety or make someone acutely aware of danger
items.ex_en: The sudden drop in engine pressure began to alarm the young co-pilot.
items.ex_zh: 发动机压力的突然下降让年轻的副驾驶感到惊慌不安。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on alerting agents to imminent hazard, danger, or trouble so they can take protective or preventative measures. It scales from routine cautions to urgent, high-intensity emergency alarms.
groups.summary_zh: 指就潜在危险或突发危机向对方发出预警和告诫。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on providing communicative signals or notices about impending danger or negative outcomes so the recipient can take heed, unlike simply 'inform'.
groups.desc_zh: 强调在危险、风险或危机发生前发出预警或告诫以促使戒备，区别于中立客观陈述的'inform'。
groups.nuance_en: warn: give explicit notice of impending harm or consequences (danger / public / risk) · alert: abruptly call attention to an immediate hazard or critical situation (authorities / staff / population) · caution: advise prudence or mild restraint against potential errors (investor / driver / suspect) · forewarn: provide advance notice well before an eventual contingency (crew / consumers / ally) · tip off: provide confidential inside advance warning (police / rival / investigator)
groups.nuance_zh: warn: 就潜在危险或严重后果发出正式警告 (danger / public / risk) · alert: 使迅速警觉并进入戒备状态以应对紧急事态 (authorities / staff / population) · caution: 规劝小心谨慎、提醒避免失误 (investor / driver / suspect) · forewarn: 提早预先打招呼或防范 (crew / consumers / ally) · tip off: 私下通风报信、提供内幕警示 (police / rival / investigator)

groups.name: Waterproof & Seal · 保护与加固 (Waterproof, Seal, Weatherize)
groups.tip: 筑起防线，抵御外界侵蚀损伤

items.def_en: Cover with a thin protective layer of plastic, metal, or wood joined by adhesive
items.ex_en: They laminate the reference cards with heavy plastic to ensure they remain waterproof.
items.ex_zh: 他们用厚塑料膜覆膜参考卡，以确保其防水耐用。

items.def_en: Close an opening or cover a surface tightly with a protective coating to prevent fluid or air passage
items.ex_en: Workers seal the cracks around the outer frame using high-grade silicone protective sealant.
items.ex_zh: 工人们使用高级硅酮保护性密封胶封闭外框周围的裂缝。

items.def_en: Make a structure, surface, or material stronger by adding extra support or substance
items.ex_en: Engineers reinforce the concrete foundation with steel rods to withstand seismic ground tremors.
items.ex_zh: 工程师用钢筋加固混凝土基础，以抵御地震引起的地表震颤。

items.def_en: to treat fabric, a surface, or an object so that water cannot penetrate it
items.ex_en: You must waterproof your hiking boots with wax spray before entering swampy terrain.
items.ex_zh: 进入沼泽地带之前，你必须用蜡喷雾给登山靴做防水处理。

items.def_zh: 使耐风雨；作抗候防护处理
items.def_en: Modify or treat a building or item to protect it from extreme weather or cold temperatures
items.ex_en: Contractors weatherize old suburban homes by installing thick insulation and sturdy storm windows.
items.ex_zh: 承包商通过安装厚绝缘层和坚固防风窗来为郊区老宅做抗候处理。

items.def_en: Fill cracks, seams, or joints with a waterproof material to prevent leakage
items.ex_en: Be sure to caulk the bathroom tiles properly to prevent chronic water leakage.
items.ex_zh: 务必将浴室瓷砖缝隙仔细填实，以防止长期渗漏水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe applying physical barriers, chemical coatings, or treatments to surfaces to protect them from environmental elements.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过涂层、密封或结构改性，使物体具备防渗、防水及耐环境侵袭能力。
groups.desc_en: Involves physically treating surfaces, edges, or structures with impermeable barriers to block environmental intrusion, unlike merely 'cover' or 'paint'.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过物理屏障、涂层或填缝手段处理构件表面，以抵御水气或外界风化侵蚀，区别于单纯表面美化的'paint'或遮盖的'cover'。
groups.nuance_en: waterproof: treat materials to prevent any penetration of water (fabric / basement / boot) · seal: securely close joints or pores against air or liquid escape (envelope / leak / container) · weatherize: adapt or insulate a building against extreme climatic elements (home / window / structure) · caulk: fill and close seams or cracks with waterproof compound (tub / boat / seam) · laminate: overlay and fuse with protective plastic or resin layers (document / floor / surface)
groups.nuance_zh: waterproof: 施加防水处理以彻底阻绝水分渗漏 (fabric / basement / boot) · seal: 封堵缝隙、封闭孔口以防介质泄漏 (envelope / leak / container) · weatherize: 为房屋抵御恶劣严寒或风雨作防风保暖改造 (home / window / structure) · caulk: 使用填缝剂密封接缝裂缝 (tub / boat / seam) · laminate: 压膜、覆膜以加固或防损 (document / floor / surface)

groups.name: Weave & Coil · 编织与卷绕 (Entwine, Braid, Wind)
groups.tip: 纺织缝缀紧密相连

items.def_en: To wrap something flexible repeatedly around an object or center point
items.ex_en: Carefully wind the thick electrical extension cord around the plastic storage wheel.
items.ex_zh: 把粗长的电源延长线小心地缠绕在塑料储线轮上。
items.ex2_en: The narrow mountain trail winds gently through the dense pine forest ahead.
items.ex2_zh: 狭窄的山径在前方茂密的松林间缓缓蜿蜒。

items.def_en: To wind or arrange a flexible material into continuous circular or spiral loops
items.ex_en: The gardener began to coil the long rubber hose after watering the lawn.
items.ex_zh: 浇完草坪后，园丁开始将长长的橡胶水管盘绕成圈。
items.ex2_en: The venomous snake coiled tightly around the branch before striking its prey.
items.ex2_zh: 毒蛇在袭击猎物前紧紧盘绕在树枝上。

items.def_en: To weave three or more strands of hair, rope, or fabric over and under each other
items.ex_en: She helped braid the colorful ribbons into her younger sister's long hair.
items.ex_zh: 她帮忙把彩带编织进妹妹长长的辫子里。

items.def_en: To twist or wind two or more things closely around each other
items.ex_en: Gnarled ivy vines entwine the crumbling stone columns of the abandoned hillside chapel.
items.ex_zh: 粗糙的常春藤藤蔓紧紧盘绕着荒废山顶小教堂剥落的石柱。
items.ex2_en: The romantic lovers' fingers entwine tenderly while walking along the quiet beach.
items.ex2_zh: 恋人们漫步在宁静的海滩上，手指温柔地缠绕在一起。

items.def_en: To join three or more pieces of hair, straw, or ribbon by intertwining them diagonally
items.ex_en: Villagers gather together every harvest evening to plait dry golden straw into hats.
items.ex_zh: 村民们每个丰收之夜聚在一起，把金黄的干麦秆编成草帽。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) To weave threads together, or blend two stories, themes, or elements closely together.
items.ex_en: Ancient folklore and personal memories interweave throughout the poet's hauntingly lyrical verses.
items.ex_zh: 古老的民间传说与个人回忆在诗人凄美的抒情诗句中紧密交织。
items.ex2_en: The skillful author expertly interweaves different narrative threads into a compelling novel.
items.ex2_zh: 这位技艺精湛的作家熟练地将不同的叙事线索交织成一部扣人心弦的小说。

groups.summary_en: This frame describes physically interlacing, winding, or twisting multiple strands, fibers, or narrative elements so that they wrap around or pass through each other in an integrated structure.
groups.summary_zh: 将多股线材、纤维或抽象叙事元素相互交缠、盘绕成复合结构。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to intertwining, winding, or spiraling flexible strands or bodies around an axis or into an intricate fabric, unlike planar 'fold' or 'straighten'.
groups.desc_zh: 指将柔软的线缆、躯体或条状物沿轴线盘绕或多股交错编织，区别于平面的'fold'或平直的'straighten'。
groups.nuance_en: braid: interweave three or more strands systematically into a flat or round strip (hair / rope / cord) · coil: wind flexible material into concentric rings or spirals (rope / snake / wire) · wind: encircle or wrap repeatedly around a core (thread / watch / bandage) · entwine: twist or interlace closely together around something (vines / fingers / lovers) · plait: weave hair, straw, or fabric strands symmetrically (hair / ribbon / dough)
groups.nuance_zh: braid: 将三股及以上材料交叉编成辫状 (hair / rope / cord) · coil: 将柔性物体盘卷成圈或螺旋形 (rope / snake / wire) · wind: 缠绕、紧紧卷在物体周围 (thread / watch / bandage) · entwine: 相互缠绕、盘根错节交织在一起 (vines / fingers / lovers) · plait: （尤指英式）按股编排发辫或草编 (hair / ribbon / dough)

groups.name: Weave & Knit · 结网与织构 (Spin, Mesh, Enmesh)
groups.tip: 交织经纬结成网络结构

items.def_en: To draw out and twist natural fibers, or produce fine silk threads to form a web or cocoon
items.ex_en: Patient spiders spin intricate silken webs between the damp bushes every chilly morning.
items.ex_zh: 耐心的蜘蛛每个寒冷的清晨都在潮湿的灌木丛间吐丝结网。
items.ex2_en: Delicate silk threads spin smoothly from the cocoon under the warm mist.
items.ex2_zh: 细腻的蚕丝在温热的水雾下从蚕茧中顺畅地抽纺出来。
