groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe a visceral reaction of extreme distaste, physical revulsion, or moral sickness caused by something repulsive. Nuances contrast physical gagging and nausea with deep-seated aesthetic or ethical abhorrence.
groups.summary_zh: 引发本能的生理作呕感或强烈的道德与审美厌恶。
groups.desc_en: Evoking an intense, visceral aversion or physical-psychological recoil, contrasting with mere intellectual disagreement or mild dislike.
groups.desc_zh: 引发本能的生理排斥、胃部反胃或心理上的强烈厌恶退避，区别于理性的观点不合或轻微反感。
groups.nuance_en: disgust: standard moral or sensory outrage and revulsion (behavior / sight) · repel: drive backward through intense distaste or natural opposition (stench / advance) · revolt: stir stomach-turning rebellion and deep moral indignation (conscience / cruelty) · nauseate: trigger physical or visceral sickness and loathing (smell / hypocrisy) · turn off: informal extinguishment of attraction or interest (audience / consumer)
groups.nuance_zh: disgust: 感官或道德上触发的标准反感与作呕 (behavior / sight) · repel: 产生令人避之不及、排斥退缩的强烈厌恶 (stench / advance) · revolt: 令人胃部翻江倒海或引发深层良知反叛 (conscience / cruelty) · nauseate: 引起生理性恶心作呕或深恶痛绝 (smell / hypocrisy) · turn off: 口语中指彻底败坏胃口、扫兴或丧失性趣/兴趣 (audience / consumer)

groups.name: Disinfect & Sanitize · 消毒与水质净化 (Disinfect, Sanitize, Chlorinate)
groups.tip: 物理化学手段，除去杂质病原

items.def_zh: 使无菌；消灭全部微生物
items.def_en: To make something completely clean by destroying all bacteria and other microorganisms on it
items.ex_en: The surgeon used high-pressure steam to sterilize all surgical instruments before the operation.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生在手术前使用高压蒸汽对所有手术器械进行了灭菌消毒。

items.def_en: To clean something using chemicals in order to kill bacteria and pathogens
items.ex_en: Nurses regularly disinfect the hospital countertops using powerful antimicrobial solutions to prevent infections.
items.ex_zh: 护士们定期使用强效抗菌溶液给医院台面消毒，以防止感染。

items.def_zh: 对……进行卫生消毒；使清洁卫生
items.def_en: To make something completely clean and free of bacteria, especially by using heat or chemicals
items.ex_en: Food processing plants must thoroughly sanitize their preparation surfaces between every production cycle.
items.ex_zh: 食品加工厂在每个生产周期之间必须对加工台面进行彻底卫生消毒。

items.def_zh: 用氯消毒，给……加氯处理；使氯化
items.def_en: To treat or disinfect water or another substance with chlorine.
items.ex_en: Municipal engineers carefully chlorinate the municipal water supply to safeguard the public from pathogens.
items.ex_zh: 市政工程师仔细地对城市供水加氯消毒，以保护公众免受病原体侵害。

items.def_zh: 清除污染；消除毒害物质
items.def_en: To remove dangerous substances such as chemicals, poisons, or radiation from a place, object, or person
items.ex_en: Specialized hazmat crews worked around the clock to decontaminate the toxic chemical spill.
items.ex_zh: 专业危险品处理人员夜以继日地工作，以清除剧毒化学品泄漏造成的污染。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers deliberate chemical or thermal treatments applied to water, surfaces, or instruments to destroy harmful microorganisms and pathogens. It emphasizes hygiene, sanitation, and safety.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过化学药剂或物理手段进行消杀、消毒与灭菌处理。
groups.desc_en: Eliminating, neutralizing, or reducing microbiological pathogens and toxins on inanimate or living substrates, differing from cosmetic washing or gross dirt removal.
groups.desc_zh: 杀灭、中和或降低无生命表面或环境中的病原微生物与毒物，区别于普通的表面洗涤或污垢清除。
groups.nuance_en: sterilize: completely eradicate all viable microbial life forms (instruments / needles) · disinfect: destroy vegetative pathogenic microorganisms on surfaces (surfaces / wounds) · sanitize: reduce bacterial counts to public health safety levels (kitchen / utensils) · decontaminate: purge hazardous radiological, chemical, or biological agents (area / suit) · chlorinate: treat water supplies specifically using chlorine chemicals (pool / water supply)
groups.nuance_zh: sterilize: 彻底杀灭包括芽孢在内的一切活体微生物 (instruments / needles) · disinfect: 杀灭物体表面或局部机体的致病性无芽孢微生物 (surfaces / wounds) · sanitize: 将细菌数量降低至符合公共卫生安全标准的水平 (kitchen / utensils) · decontaminate: 清除核、化、生等危险污染物或放射性沉降 (area / suit) · chlorinate: 特指通过加氯化学手段净化消毒水体 (pool / water supply)

groups.name: Disinherit & Expropriate · 剥夺继承权与没收 (Disinherit, Confiscate, Forfeit)
groups.tip: 剥夺继承权或合法权益

items.def_zh: 断绝继承权；断绝经济资助
items.def_en: Prevent someone from receiving an inheritance or financial support, typically out of anger
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: Officially take private property away by legal authority as a penalty or protective measure
items.ex_en: Customs officials have legal authority to confiscate undeclared luxury goods entering the country.
items.ex_zh: 海关官员有法定权力没收入境的未申报奢侈品。

items.def_zh: 断绝关系；否认有任何瓜葛
items.def_en: Refuse to acknowledge someone as one's child or family member, revoking all claims and rights
items.ex_en: His furious father threatened to disown him permanently after his latest criminal arrest.
items.ex_zh: 在他最近一次犯罪被捕后，愤怒的父亲扬言要同他彻底断绝关系。

items.def_en: (formal) Take away private property for public use or state ownership, sometimes without consent
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime moved swiftly to expropriate privately held farmland without fair compensation.
items.ex_zh: 该专制政权迅速采取行动，无偿征用了私有农田。

items.def_en: To legally prevent someone from inheriting your money or property.
items.ex_en: The billionaire altered his testament to disinherit his reckless eldest son entirely.
items.ex_zh: 这位亿万富翁修改了遗嘱，彻底剥夺了鲁莽长子的继承权。

groups.summary_en: This legal and familial governance frame encompasses officially barring a rightful beneficiary from an estate, or seizing private assets through judicial decree or authoritarian sanction.
groups.summary_zh: 涉及在法律或家族层面剥夺继承资格或强行没收财产。
groups.desc_en: Legally, socially, or authoritatively stripping an individual or entity of inheritance, property, or entitlement, contrasting with fair market acquisition or voluntary gift.
groups.desc_zh: 通过法律、社会关系或公权力强行剥夺他人的继承权、财产或既有权益，区别于公平市场交易或自愿赠与。
groups.nuance_en: disinherit: formally revoke an heir's right to an estate (son / heir) · cut off: severance of familial financial support or testamentary favor (daughter / family) · disown: total familial repudiation accompanied by loss of inheritance (child / relative) · expropriate: sovereign or state seizure of private property for public use (land / assets) · confiscate: punitive or lawful seizure of illicit or contested goods (contraband / weapons)
groups.nuance_zh: disinherit: 依法立遗嘱剥夺法定继承人的财产继承权 (son / heir) · cut off: 家族长辈切断经济资助或遗嘱受惠资格 (daughter / family) · disown: 绝裂亲属关系并剥夺其一切家族身份与利益 (child / relative) · expropriate: 国家或公权力依据征收权强制征用私产 (land / assets) · confiscate: 司法或行政机关因违法行为罚没、没收财物 (contraband / weapons)

groups.name: Dislocate & Luxate · 脱臼与骨骼错位 (Dislocate, Luxate, Put Out)
groups.tip: 关节或部件脱离原本位置

items.def_zh: 使（关节、骨头）脱臼或扭伤
items.def_en: To displace a joint or bone from its normal position through sudden physical strain
items.ex_en: The rugby player put out his right shoulder during a violent tackle yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 这名橄榄球运动员昨天在一次激烈的冲撞中弄脱了右肩关节。

items.def_en: (formal or medical) To dislocate an anatomical joint completely
items.ex_en: Severe impact during the collision was sufficient to luxate the driver's left hip.
items.ex_zh: 碰撞时的剧烈冲击足以使驾驶员的左髋关节完全脱位。

items.def_en: (medical) To undergo or cause partial dislocation of a joint without complete separation
items.ex_en: The gymnast felt her shoulder joint subluxate momentarily before sliding back into position.
items.ex_zh: 体操运动员感到自己的肩关节瞬间发生半脱位，随后又滑回原位。
items.ex2_en: The violent impact subluxated the athlete's shoulder joint during the championship rugby match.
items.ex2_zh: 在橄榄球锦标赛中，剧烈的撞击导致运动员的肩关节发生了半脱位。

items.def_en: (informal) To dislodge suddenly from its joint or socket, or to cause a joint to pop free
items.ex_en: She just popped out to the post office to mail a parcel.
items.ex_zh: 她刚出去去邮局寄个包裹，一会儿就回来。

items.def_zh: 使脱臼，使关节移位；使混乱，扰乱
items.def_en: 1. To force a bone out of its normal position in a joint. 2. To disrupt or throw an established system, schedule, or organization into disorder.
items.ex_en: The awkward fall caused the young athlete to dislocate his elbow during practice.
items.ex_zh: 笨拙的摔倒导致这名年轻运动员在训练中手肘脱臼。

groups.summary_en: This medical and anatomical frame describes forcing a bone or joint out of its normal anatomical socket or contiguous relation. Collocations almost exclusively focus on shoulders, hips, fingers, and spinal vertebrae.
groups.summary_zh: 指关节因外力或扭伤离开正常解剖位置而脱臼或错缝。
groups.desc_en: Forcing an anatomical joint or bone out of its normal structural articulation, contrasting with fractures, simple sprains, or muscle tears.
groups.desc_zh: 外力强行使骨骼关节脱离其正常的解剖对位结构，区别于骨折、轻度扭伤或肌肉拉伤。
groups.nuance_en: dislocate: displacement of bones forming a joint out of normal position (shoulder / hip) · luxate: formal clinical term for complete joint displacement (patella / tooth) · subluxate: partial or incomplete displacement of a joint (vertebra / joint) · pop out: colloquial description of a sudden, painful displacement (knee / shoulder) · put out: everyday vernacular for wrenching a joint or back out of alignment (back / neck)
groups.nuance_zh: dislocate: 关节脱位、脱臼的标准医学与日常表述 (shoulder / hip) · luxate: 描述关节完全脱位的正式临床解剖术语 (patella / tooth) · subluxate: 关节轻度错位或不完全半脱位 (vertebra / joint) · pop out: 俚语化描述关节突发滑出或弹出的脱臼 (knee / shoulder) · put out: 日常口语中指因拉扯用力不当致使骨骼关节错位 (back / neck)

groups.name: Dislodge & Displace · 移位与强行挪离 (Displace, Dislodge, Uproot)
groups.tip: 迫使其离开原有位置

items.def_zh: 迫使离开原位（或家园）；取代，替代；排开（水）
items.def_en: 1. To force people or animals to leave their home or usual environment. 2. To take the place or position of someone or something; to move something from its usual place.
items.ex_en: The violent civil war threatened to displace hundreds of thousands of innocent villagers.
items.ex_zh: 惨烈的内战恐将迫使数十万无辜村民流离失所。

items.def_en: To move or cause something stuck or stubborn to move even slightly
items.ex_en: Despite our combined pushing efforts, the heavy oak wardrobe would not budge.
items.ex_zh: 尽管我们合力推挤，那座沉重的橡木衣柜却纹丝不动。
items.ex2_en: The persistent mover finally budged the stubborn refrigerator across the narrow hallway.
items.ex2_zh: 坚持不懈的搬运工终于把那台卡住的冰箱在狭窄的走廊里挪动了一点。

items.def_zh: 将……连根拔起；迫使离开家园
items.def_en: To pull something out of the ground by its roots, or force someone to leave their secure lifelong home
items.ex_en: The impending highway construction will inevitably uproot dozens of families from their village.
items.ex_zh: 即将开工的公路建设势必会迫使该村的数十户家庭迁离家园。

items.def_zh: 逐出；用力移开（卡住之物）
items.def_en: To forcibly knock, pry, or remove something or someone from a fixed, stuck, or secure position
items.ex_en: The mechanic used a heavy steel pry bar to dislodge the rusted bolt.
items.ex_zh: 修理工用一根沉重的钢制撬棍撬下了那颗生锈的螺栓。

items.def_en: To dislodge someone from a saddle, vehicle seat, or settled physical stance
items.ex_en: A sudden violent buck from the wild stallion threatened to unseat the rider.
items.ex_zh: 野公马猛然剧烈一颠，差点把骑手掀落马下。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers moving an object, substance, or person out of a settled, fixed, or established position by physical force, pressure, or upheaval. It contrasts dislodging an impacted object with large-scale demographic displacement.
groups.summary_zh: 指施加外力将固着物挪开，或使人及群体被迫脱离原有安居位置。
groups.desc_en: Forcibly removing, shifting, or expelling an object, person, or population from a fixed, seated, or established position, contrasting with voluntary relocation or simple motion.
groups.desc_zh: 通过外力将物体、人或群体从原有的固定、锚定或既定位置强行撬动、驱离或取代，区别于自愿搬迁或单纯位移。
groups.nuance_en: dislodge: knock or pry loose an embedded or stuck item (boulder / debris) · displace: compel removal or usurp the spatial/functional position of something (residents / volume) · unseat: abruptly depose an incumbent from office or saddle (politician / rider) · uproot: violently tear out by the roots or eradicate settled life (tree / communities) · budge: achieve minimal movement against stubborn resistance, usually negated (weight / stance)
groups.nuance_zh: dislodge: 撬动或震松原本嵌死、卡住的物体 (boulder / debris) · displace: 强行使群体背井离乡或在空间/功能上取代原有位置 (residents / volume) · unseat: 突然将某人从公职罢免或从马背/座位上颠下 (politician / rider) · uproot: 连根拔起或彻底拔除定居的生活根基 (tree / communities) · budge: 在顽固阻力下发生微小挪动（多用于否定句） (weight / stance)

groups.name: Dismantle & Deconstruct · 拆解与解构 (Dismantle, Disassemble, Take apart)
groups.tip: 逐一拆除结构使其崩解

items.def_en: To separate an object into the pieces from which it was made
items.ex_en: Curious about its inner workings, the boy decided to take apart the clock.
items.ex_zh: 出于对内部运作的好奇，男孩决定把时钟拆开来看个究竟。

items.def_en: To take a machine, piece of furniture, or mechanism apart into separate components
items.ex_en: The technician had to carefully disassemble the complex machine to identify the fault.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员必须小心翼翼地拆卸这台复杂的机器以查明故障。

items.def_en: To dismantle an engine or vehicle down to its bare parts for repair or inspection
items.ex_en: The mechanics had to strip down the racecar engine to diagnose the pressure loss.
items.ex_zh: 机械师们不得不把赛车引擎彻底拆解至骨架，以排查压力下降的原因。

items.def_zh: 拆卸，拆开；逐步废除，取消
items.def_en: 1. To take a machine or structure apart into separate pieces. 2. To gradually end or dismantle a system, organization, or agreement.
items.ex_en: The new administration plans to systematically dismantle the corrupt regulatory framework over time.
items.ex_zh: 新一届政府计划随着时间推移逐步废除腐败的监管体系。

items.def_en: To break down a complex system, theory, or structure into constituent elements to understand or expose it
items.ex_en: The literary professor helped students deconstruct the underlying philosophical themes of the novel.
items.ex_zh: 文学教授帮助学生解构了这部小说潜在的哲学主题。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame specify systematically taking an apparatus, physical structure, or institutional framework apart piece by piece, reversing its assembly.
groups.summary_zh: 指按部就班地将机械、结构或体系拆卸成各个组件或彻底解体。
groups.desc_en: Systematically taking apart an assembled structure, machine, or conceptual paradigm piece by piece, contrasting with random destruction or smash-and-break demolition.
groups.desc_zh: 有步骤、系统地将机械装置、工程结构或理论范式逐层分拆瓦解，区别于杂乱无章的砸毁或暴力破坏。
groups.nuance_en: disassemble: methodically reverse assembly into functional parts (engine / firearm) · take apart: plain, accessible dismantling of a mechanism (watch / toy) · strip down: reduce a machine to bare components by peeling external layers (car / bike) · dismantle: systematically terminate and tear down a large apparatus or organization (scaffolding / regime) · deconstruct: critically expose the underlying assumptions of a text or concept (theory / narrative)
groups.nuance_zh: disassemble: 逆向系统性拆卸机械设备至各功能零部件 (engine / firearm) · take apart: 最通用的口语化分拆、拆开物件 (watch / toy) · strip down: 剥离外围零件直达骨架底层的彻底拆解 (car / bike) · dismantle: 系统性拆除大型工程结构或废除体制网络 (scaffolding / regime) · deconstruct: 哲学或批评层面对文本、理论范式的解构剖析 (theory / narrative)

groups.name: Dismember & Mutilate · 肢解与残害 (Dismember, Mutilate, Hack Apart)
groups.tip: 刀具割断，肢解形体结构

items.def_en: Methodically cut up a dead body, plant, or tissue to examine its anatomical structure
items.ex_en: Medical students are required to dissect human cadavers to study muscular anatomical structures.
items.ex_zh: 医学生被要求解剖人体标本，以研究肌肉解剖结构。

items.def_en: Chop violently and repeatedly so as to cut someone or something into separate pieces
items.ex_en: The woodsman used a heavy axe to hack apart the fallen tree trunks.
items.ex_zh: 伐木工用一把沉重的斧头将倒下的树干乱刀劈碎。

items.def_en: Inflict severe, disfiguring damage on the body of someone or an animal
items.ex_en: The barbaric poachers chose to mutilate the rhino before stealing its precious horns.
items.ex_zh: 野蛮的盗猎者在盗取珍贵犀牛角之前将其躯体残忍摧残。

items.def_zh: 肢解，割断手足；分裂，瓜分（国家等）
items.def_en: To cut, tear, or pull off the limbs of a person or animal, or divide a country, territory, or organization into separate parts.
items.ex_en: The serial killer attempted to dismember the corpse to hinder the police investigation.
items.ex_zh: 连环杀手企图肢解尸体以阻挠警方的调查。

items.def_en: Violently rip or shred a body apart into separate limbs
items.ex_en: The vicious pack of wild dogs threatened to tear the trapped deer limb from limb.
items.ex_zh: 凶残的野狗群恐将把那只受困的鹿大卸八块。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote violently tearing, cutting, or hacking a living body or carcass into pieces, or systematically dividing an entity limb by limb. They emphasize severe destructive force and bodily fragmentation.
groups.summary_zh: 强调对肢体进行暴力撕扯、砍斫碎解或肢解分割的动作。
groups.desc_en: Inflicting extreme physical butchery by severing limbs, carving bodies, or violently degrading bodily integrity, contrasting with clean killing or simple surgical cutting.
groups.desc_zh: 通过截断肢体、乱刀砍割或毁灭肉身完整性施加极其残酷的摧残，区别于利落的处决或规范的外科手术。
groups.nuance_en: dismember: systematically sever the limbs from a body (corpse / victim) · mutilate: grievously disfigure or permanently ruin an essential anatomical part (body / remains) · hack apart: chop savagely and clumsily with heavy edged weapons (carcass / torso) · tear limb from limb: hyper-violent, beastly or furious ripping apart (prey / captive) · dissect: careful anatomical separation for scientific study (specimen / cadaver)
groups.nuance_zh: dismember: 切断、肢解尸体或活体的四肢躯干 (corpse / victim) · mutilate: 严重残害并毁损身体重要部位及容貌 (body / remains) · hack apart: 使用重刃利器野蛮且粗暴地乱砍乱剁 (carcass / torso) · tear limb from limb: 极其残暴野兽般地生撕活裂肢体 (prey / captive) · dissect: 为解剖学研究而实施的细致解剖与组织分离 (specimen / cadaver)

groups.name: Dismiss & Terminate · 解聘与革职 (Fire, Sack, Oust)
groups.tip: 解除任职或开除出局

items.def_en: To remove someone decisively from their job, often for unsatisfactory performance
items.ex_en: The boss decided to fire him on the spot for blatant insubordination today.
items.ex_zh: 老板今天因他公然顶撞而决定当场把他开除。
items.ex2_en: The old combustion engine fired instantly upon turning the rusty ignition key yesterday.
items.ex2_zh: 昨天一转动生锈的点火钥匙，这台老式内燃机立刻点火发动了。

items.def_zh: 免职，解雇，开除；对……不予理会，驳回；解散
items.def_en: 1. To remove someone from a job, position, or organization. 2. To decide that something is not important enough to consider. 3. To allow or tell people to leave.
items.ex_en: The firm reserves the absolute right to dismiss any employee caught leaking data.
items.ex_zh: 公司保留解雇任何被发现泄露数据之雇员的绝对权力。

items.def_en: To dismiss an employee from their post abruptly or harshly
items.ex_en: The company decided to sack the senior accountant following allegations of serious fraud.
items.ex_zh: 在爆出严重欺诈指控后，公司决定把高级会计师炒鱿鱼。

items.def_zh: 终止（雇佣关系），解约解聘
items.def_en: To end an employee's contract or position formally and legally
items.ex_en: Management decided to terminate his employment contract immediately due to persistent gross misconduct.
items.ex_zh: 由于持续严重的渎职行为，管理层决定立即终止他的劳动合同。
items.ex2_en: The high-speed rail line will terminate conveniently at the newly built airport station.
items.ex2_zh: 这条高速铁路线将便捷地终到于新建成的机场车站。

items.def_en: To force someone out of a position of authority, responsibility, or office
items.ex_en: Shareholders gathered enough proxy votes to oust the disgraced chief executive from office.
items.ex_zh: 股东们筹集了足够的委托投票权，将这位名誉扫地的首席执行官罢免赶下台。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame mark the authoritative and permanent severance of an individual's employment or administrative post. Connotations range from polite contractual termination to punitive and unceremonious firing.
groups.summary_zh: 雇主或权威机构永久性解除某人职务、解雇或罢免。
groups.desc_en: Authoritatively expelling an employee, official, or leader from their post or employment, differing from voluntary retirement, consensual leave, or contract expiration.
groups.desc_zh: 依职权或强力将员工、官员或领导人免职、解雇或驱逐出既有岗位，区别于自愿辞职、协议离职或合同期满卸任。
groups.nuance_en: dismiss: formal, administrative release from an official appointment (employee / minister) · fire: direct, commonplace termination, usually for performance or cause (worker / staff) · sack: predominantly British colloquial, blunt firing (manager / coach) · terminate: cold, bureaucratic or corporate ending of an employment contract (employment / contract) · oust: politically or forcefully force someone out of power or seat (dictator / CEO)
groups.nuance_zh: dismiss: 正式、公事公办地解聘或免去职务 (employee / minister) · fire: 最普遍直接的因故解雇、炒鱿鱼 (worker / staff) · sack: 英式常用口语，直截了当地踢出团队或解职 (manager / coach) · terminate: 冰冷官僚的企业人事用语，终止雇佣合同 (employment / contract) · oust: 政治政变或权力斗争中强行驱逐、赶下台 (dictator / CEO)

groups.name: Disown & Disavow · 划清界限与断绝 (Disassociate, Disavow, Repudiate)
groups.tip: 明确断绝联系或划清界线

items.def_en: To behave in a way that shows you are not involved with or do not agree with someone or something
items.ex_en: The politician tried to distance himself from his former ally's controversial racial remarks.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客试图与前盟友引发争议的种族主义言论撇清干系。

items.def_zh: 划清界限，声明脱离关系；使分离，使脱离联系
items.def_en: 1. (disassociate oneself from) To state clearly that you are not connected with or responsible for someone or something.
items.ex_en: The university moved quickly to disassociate itself from the disgraced professor's fraudulent research.
items.ex_zh: 该大学迅速采取行动，声明与那位身败名裂的教授的造假研究划清界限。

items.def_zh: 断绝（亲子等）关系；否认归属
items.def_en: To refuse to acknowledge or maintain a relationship with a family member or associate
items.ex_en: She decided to disown her manipulative brother after years of deceit and financial exploitation.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了多年的欺骗和经济盘剥后，她决定与善于操纵人的哥哥断绝关系。

items.def_en: To deny any responsibility or support for something previously said, done, or endorsed
items.ex_en: The foreign ministry issued a statement to disavow the rogue operative's covert actions.
items.ex_zh: 外交部发表声明，否认与那名擅自行动的特工的秘密活动有任何牵连。

items.def_zh: 断绝关系；驳斥并拒绝承认
items.def_en: To refuse to accept, acknowledge, or be associated with someone or something
items.ex_en: The leader was quick to repudiate the extremist ideology promoted by rogue factions.
items.ex_zh: 该领导人迅速驳斥并拒绝承认由流氓派系鼓吹的极端主义意识形态。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe public or formal actions taken by individuals or organizations to cut ties, deny connection, or renounce responsibility for someone else's actions, statements, or beliefs.
groups.summary_zh: 指公开发声明或采取行动，断绝与某人或某事的牵连并否认责任。
groups.desc_en: Deliberately establishing distance and severing connection from an affiliated entity, deed, or controversial statement to protect reputation, contrasting with passive neglect.
groups.desc_zh: 为保全声誉或原则，蓄意与某关联方、争议行为或不当言论划清界限并切断纽带，区别于被动的忽视。
groups.nuance_en: distance oneself from: strategically move away from a problematic tie (comments / scandal) · disassociate: formally or mentally break an association or connection (group / remarks) · disavow: deny responsibility, authorization, or knowledge of an act (statement / agent) · disown: cut off all familial, personal, or property ties entirely (child / heritage) · repudiate: forcefully reject, dispute the validity of, or refuse to obey (debt / treaty)
groups.nuance_zh: distance oneself from: 为免受牵连而在策略上拉开距离 (comments / scandal) · disassociate: 正式声明断绝关系或在认知上解绑 (group / remarks) · disavow: 拒不承认与某行为或言论有牵连、否认授权 (statement / agent) · disown: 绝裂亲缘关系并断绝道义与财产承认 (child / heritage) · repudiate: 坚决拒斥并拒绝履行条约、债务或承认效力 (debt / treaty)

groups.name: Disown & Repudiate · 断绝关系与拒不承认 (Repudiate, Renounce, Disavow)
groups.tip: 决绝宣布断绝亲情或师承关系

items.def_en: To get rid of or abandon someone or something completely and without remorse
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: To deny publicly any knowledge of, connection with, or responsibility for someone or something
items.ex_en: The corporation acted promptly to publicly disavow any connection with the corrupt lobbyist.
items.ex_zh: 该企业迅速采取行动，公开否认与那个腐败的说客有任何瓜葛。

items.def_en: To state formally and publicly that you will no longer have, support, or claim something
items.ex_en: The former revolutionary decided to formally renounce violence as a tool for political reform.
items.ex_zh: 这位前革命者决定正式宣布放弃将暴力作为政治改革的手段。

items.def_zh: 断绝关系，否认与……有关系；声明脱离
items.def_en: To decide that you no longer want to be associated with or responsible for someone or something.
items.ex_en: His wealthy family threatened to disown him if he married the penniless artist.
items.ex_zh: 他富有的家人威胁说，如果他娶那个身无分文的艺术家就与他断绝关系。

items.def_en: To reject strongly and formally as having no authority, truth, or binding power
items.ex_en: The prime minister publicly repudiated the controversial statements made by his deputy.
items.ex_zh: 首相公开声明断然拒绝接受其副手发表的争议言论。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve a formal, severe, or public refusal to accept, acknowledge, or maintain a relationship with a person, claim, or heritage. While 'disown' usually involves family or kin, 'repudiate' rejects validity, and 'disavow' denies association or responsibility.
groups.summary_zh: 指公开、坚决且决绝地断绝关系、推卸责任或拒不承认。
groups.desc_en: Unequivocally casting aside, disclaiming, or renouncing a cherished relationship, fundamental belief, or formal allegiance with severe finality, contrasting with temporary suspension.
groups.desc_zh: 彻底、不可逆地抛弃、否认或弃绝曾经的血亲关系、核心信仰或从属誓言，区别于暂时的冷落或搁置。
groups.nuance_en: repudiate: emphatically reject as false, invalid, or having no claim (doctrine / accusation) · renounce: formally surrender or relinquish a right, title, or former faith (citizenship / claim) · disown: explicitly cast off kinship and refusal to recognize lineage (son / family) · disavow: explicitly deny ownership of or prior association with something (alliance / actions) · cast off: throw aside an unwanted person, restraint, or garment as baggage (lover / shackles)
groups.nuance_zh: repudiate: 义正言辞地全盘拒斥、否决其效力或真伪 (doctrine / accusation) · renounce: 正式通告放弃头衔、国籍、权利或先前信仰 (citizenship / claim) · disown: 决绝地断绝骨肉亲情与家族血缘认同 (son / family) · disavow: 明确声称对此前所做所为不予承认或毫无瓜葛 (alliance / actions) · cast off: 如抛弃赘物般甩掉不受欢迎的人、旧束缚 (lover / shackles)

groups.name: Disparage & Slur · 贬损与蔑称 (Trash-talk, Put down, Diss)
groups.tip: 从轻浮取笑升级到公开言语羞辱挑衅

items.def_en: To demean, humiliate, or belittle someone in front of others
items.ex_en: The manager liked to put down his assistants in front of important clients.
items.ex_zh: 那位经理喜欢在重要客户面前贬低自己的助理以使他们难堪。

items.def_en: To use disparaging or insolent talk against an opponent to demoralize them
items.ex_en: The boxers continued to trash-talk each other until the opening bell finally rang.
items.ex_zh: 拳击手们互相恶语挑衅，直到开场铃声终于响起。

items.def_en: (informal) To speak disrespectfully to or criticize someone in an insulting or dismissive manner.
items.ex_en: He released a bitter track to diss his former bandmates after the breakup.
items.ex_zh: 乐队解散后，他发行了一首尖酸的歌曲来嘲弄贬低前队友。

items.def_en: To represent something or someone as being of little value or worth
items.ex_en: Critics unfairly disparaged her substantial contribution to the groundbreaking scientific research.
items.ex_zh: 批评家们不公正地贬低了她对这项突破性科研成果的重大贡献。

items.def_en: To criticize someone severely and unkindly, often behind their back
items.ex_en: She always badmouths her coworkers whenever the supervisor steps out of the office.
items.ex_zh: 主管一走出办公室，她就总是背地里说同事的坏话。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses colloquial, hostile, or insolent verbal denigration meant to diminish someone's status, respect, or competence in an informal or aggressive context.
groups.summary_zh: 指在口语或冲突中用轻蔑、侮辱性言语贬损、驳斥他人。
groups.desc_en: Demeaning, mocking, or derogating someone's worth, skills, or character using dismissive, insulting language, contrasting with constructive critique.
groups.desc_zh: 使用贬损、蔑视或侮辱性的言辞贬低他人的价值、能力或品格，区别于建设性的批评或客观讨论。
groups.nuance_en: disparage: formally belittle, undervalue, or depreciate the merits of (achievements / skills) · put down: deflate someone's self-esteem by cutting verbal belittlement (colleague / partner) · diss: urban slang for slighting, disrespecting, or dissing someone publicly (rival / artist) · trash-talk: aggressive psychological boast-and-insult banter (opponent / player) · badmouth: speak spitefully and critically behind someone's back (boss / neighbor)
groups.nuance_zh: disparage: 正式语体中贬低、贬损功绩或才干的价值 (achievements / skills) · put down: 通过刻薄话当面挫败他人自尊 (colleague / partner) · diss: 俚语中无礼轻蔑、公开挑衅或羞辱 (rival / artist) · trash-talk: 竞技场上旨在击溃心理防线的叫嚣与垃圾话 (opponent / player) · badmouth: 在背地里恶意中伤、讲坏话 (boss / neighbor)

groups.name: Dispatch & Send Forth · 派遣与发配 (Send off, Deploy, Detach)
groups.tip: 调派人马物资出发

items.def_zh: 委派或派选（人员去执行某项任务）
items.def_en: To assign a particular officer, soldier, or subordinate officially to execute a specific duty
items.ex_en: The captain detailed two experienced officers to secure the perimeter around the building.
items.ex_zh: 队长委派了两名经验丰富的警官去守卫大楼周围的警戒线。

items.def_zh: 部署或调派（军队、警力或资源）
items.def_en: To move troops, personnel, or equipment into position ready for immediate operational action
items.ex_en: The government decided to deploy emergency medical teams to the flood-stricken region.
items.ex_zh: 政府决定向遭受洪灾的地区调派应急医疗小组。

items.def_en: To send someone on a mission or transport an item by mail or courier to its recipient
items.ex_en: I need to send off these signed contracts before the post office closes.
items.ex_zh: 我需要在邮局关门前把这些签好的合同寄送出去。

items.def_zh: 派遣，调遣；发出（信件等）；迅速处理；杀死
items.def_en: 1. To send someone or something quickly to a particular destination for a specific purpose. 2. (formal) To deal with a task promptly; to kill a person or animal.
items.ex_en: The embassy dispatched a special envoy to negotiate the immediate release of hostages.
items.ex_zh: 大使馆迅速调遣了一名特使，以前去协商立即释放人质的事宜。

items.def_zh: 分遣或抽调（兵力或人员执行特别任务）
items.def_en: To send away a group of soldiers, ships, or workers from the main body for a special assignment
items.ex_en: The commander detached a small naval unit to patrol the northern shipping lanes.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官抽调了一支小型海军部队去巡逻北部航道。
items.ex2_en: The modular cargo pod detached smoothly from the delivery transport vehicle on arrival.
items.ex2_zh: 模块化货舱在抵达后顺利脱离了运输车辆。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote sending agents, military units, vehicles, or urgent consignments purposefully and expeditiously to a designated location.
groups.summary_zh: 为特定任务或目的调遣人员、部队或车辆前往指定地点。
groups.desc_en: Officially sending personnel, units, or consignments on a designated mission with purpose and speed, contrasting with casual wandering or private travel.
groups.desc_zh: 依官方命令、任务分派或紧急指令快速派遣人员、部队或专件前往特定目的地，区别于私人出行或闲逛。
groups.nuance_en: dispatch: prompt, official transmission of envoys, troops, or couriers (courier / forces) · deploy: strategical positioning of forces or resources ready for action (troops / assets) · detail: assign an individual or small unit to a temporary, specialized duty (officer / squad) · detach: separate a unit from a parent body for independent mission (battalion / escort) · send off: informally bid farewell or physically forward someone away (delegation / parcel)
groups.nuance_zh: dispatch: 带有权威与紧急色彩地派发特使、部队或急件 (courier / forces) · deploy: 为执行战备或战术任务而战略性展开与调派 (troops / assets) · detail: 抽调特定人员或小分队临时执行特种勤务 (officer / squad) · detach: 从母建制部队中独立分离出一支队伍执行外派 (battalion / escort) · send off: 送别或将人员/包裹发运送出 (delegation / parcel)

groups.name: Dispatch Electronic Documents · 传真与专递发件 (Fax, Wire, Telecopy)
groups.tip: 通过传真或电讯手段收发信函

items.def_en: To send a message, instruction, or funds electronically using a telegraphic network
items.ex_en: The company agreed to wire the emergency funds to our foreign account today.
items.ex_zh: 公司同意今天把应急资金电汇到我们的海外账户。

items.def_en: To send a message by submarine telegraph cable or telegram
items.ex_en: The ambassador quickly cabled the latest peace proposal back to London headquarters.
items.ex_zh: 大使迅速通过海底电报将最新的和平方案发回伦敦总部。

items.def_en: To transmit a facsimile of a document over a telephone or digital line
items.ex_en: Please telecopy the certified legal documents to our Zurich branch without delay.
items.ex_zh: 请毫不拖延地将经认证的法律文件传真发送给我们苏黎世的分行。

items.def_en: To send off a message, fax, or email quickly and abruptly
items.ex_en: Infuriated by the decision, he fired off an angry email to the manager.
items.ex_zh: 他对这个决定大为光火，立即给经理匆忙发了一封措辞愤怒的邮件。

items.def_en: To send a document electronically using a fax machine.
items.ex_en: Our office can fax the signed lease agreement to your agency this afternoon.
items.ex_zh: 我们办公室今天下午可以把签好的租赁协议传真给你们中介。

groups.summary_en: Verbs referring to transmitting specific documents, records, or urgent telegraphic communications via dedicated telecommunication machines or services.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过专用电信设备或网络即时发送文档、电报或票据。
groups.desc_en: Transmitting printed matter, textual data, or formal messages across distance via telecommunication lines and wire networks, contrasting with physically carrying postal paper.
groups.desc_zh: 借助电信线路、电报网络或传真技术远程即时发送文本文书或专递讯息，区别于传统的物理邮政投递。
groups.nuance_en: fax: transmit a facsimile copy of a printed document via telephone line (document / contract) · telecopy: older technical/corporate synonym for faxing documents (memo / page) · wire: transmit funds or urgency text via commercial electric telegraph/interbank (money / message) · cable: transmit messages overseas via undersea submarine cable (instructions / news) · fire off: rapidly, aggressively, or casually shoot off a message (email / memo)
groups.nuance_zh: fax: 经由电话线路传送打印文书的图文传真 (document / contract) · telecopy: 企业及技术语境中对传真文件的早期正式称呼 (memo / page) · wire: 经由电报网络发电报或通过银行系统电汇 (money / message) · cable: 经由跨洋海底电缆向海外拍发外交或商业电报 (instructions / news) · fire off: 快速、连珠炮式或冲动地发送邮件或讯息 (email / memo)

groups.name: Display & Flaunt · 显摆与炫耀 (Flaunt, Show off, Brandish)
groups.tip: 张扬显摆财富才华，招摇过市博眼球

items.def_en: To display abilities, possessions, or status conspicuously to elicit praise or attention
items.ex_en: He bought an expensive sports car just to show off to his neighbors.
items.ex_zh: 他买了一辆昂贵的跑车，纯粹是为了向邻居们炫耀。

items.def_en: To display money, jewellery, or status symbols conspicuously to impress others
items.ex_en: The lottery winner liked to flash thick wads of cash at local clubs.
items.ex_zh: 那个彩票大奖得主喜欢在当地俱乐部里显摆大把大把的钞票。
items.ex2_en: Bright bolts of lightning flashed dramatically across the pitch-black midnight thunderstorm sky.
items.ex2_zh: 明亮的闪电在漆黑一片的午夜雷暴天空中耀眼地闪烁。

items.def_en: To exhibit or display something proudly and publicly so that everyone notices
items.ex_en: She constantly parades her luxury designer handbags whenever she attends social gatherings.
items.ex_zh: 每当参加社交聚会时，她总是在众人面前大肆炫耀自己的名牌手袋。

items.def_en: 1. To show off your wealth, beauty, or possessions proudly and openly so others admire or envy you.
items.ex_en: He loved to flaunt his immense inherited wealth before his struggling colleagues.
items.ex_zh: 他喜欢在苦苦打拼的同事面前公开炫耀自己继承的巨额财富。

items.def_zh: 炫耀性出示，挥舞（权柄或凭据）
items.def_en: To display or wave something aggressively or ostentatiously as a threat or show of power
items.ex_en: The tyrant brandished his sovereign authority to silence any hint of political dissent.
items.ex_zh: 暴君大肆挥舞着君主权威，以压制任何政治异见的苗头。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on ostentatious visual or verbal displays of wealth, assets, or power executed deliberately to provoke envy, admiration, or intimidation.
groups.summary_zh: 刻意高调展示财富、特权或实力以引人注目、艳羡或施加威慑。
groups.desc_en: To exhibit possessions, advantages, or weapons ostentatiously or aggressively to elicit envy, awe, or intimidation, unlike neutral showing or presenting.
groups.desc_zh: 带有炫耀、招摇或恐吓意图地高调展示财富、优势或武器，区别于中性的展示或呈现。
groups.nuance_en: show off: boastful display to draw admiration (skills / wealth) · flash: brief, ostentatious exposure (cash / jewelry / smile) · parade: proud, protracted public exhibition (trophies / virtues) · flaunt: brazen, shameless display defying modesty (wealth / body / rules) · brandish: aggressive, menacing display (weapon / authority / document)
groups.nuance_zh: show off: 爱慕虚荣地招摇卖弄 (skills / wealth) · flash: 瞬间炫耀性地亮出 (cash / jewelry / smile) · parade: 招摇过市般游街示众 (trophies / virtues) · flaunt: 肆无忌惮地炫耀并挑衅公序良俗 (wealth / body / rules) · brandish: 挥舞或亮出以示威吓 (weapon / authority / document)

groups.name: Display & Flaunt · 炫耀与炫示 (Flaunt, Flash, Parade)
groups.tip: 从客观展示升级为刻意夸耀

items.def_zh: 得意地穿戴，炫耀，夸示；玩耍，嬉戏
items.def_en: 1. to wear or display something proudly or conspicuously. 2. (archaic) to play or amuse oneself.
items.ex_en: The young actor arrived at the gala sporting a flashy velvet tuxedo.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻演员得意地穿着一身亮眼的丝绒礼服来到了晚会现场。

items.def_en: to show something expensive, impressive, or eye-catching briefly and ostentatiously
items.ex_en: He unbuttoned his cuff specifically to flash his diamond-encrusted gold watch.
items.ex_zh: 他特意解开袖扣，好亮出他那块镶满钻石的金表。
items.ex2_en: A brilliant warning light flashed continuously upon the industrial machine's operational dashboard.
items.ex2_zh: 一盏明亮的警示灯在该工业设备的操控仪表盘上持续闪烁。

items.def_en: to display something proudly or conspicuously before an audience so as to gain attention
items.ex_en: The proud collector loved to parade his rare antique cars during town festivals.
items.ex_zh: 这位骄傲的收藏家喜欢在小镇节日期间大肆卖弄展示他的罕见古董车。

items.def_en: to deliberately display something one has or can do in order to impress others
items.ex_en: The boy performed backflips on the lawn just to show off his agility.
items.ex_zh: 那个男孩在草坪上空翻，只为了卖弄自己敏捷的身手。

items.def_en: to display something ostentatiously, boldly, or insolently in order to provoke envy or admiration
items.ex_en: Influencers often flaunt lavish lifestyle habits that their young followers cannot realistically afford.
items.ex_zh: 网红们经常招摇显摆奢华的生活方式，而他们年轻的粉丝根本负担不起。

groups.summary_en: These verbs denote conspicuously wearing, displaying, or calling attention to clothes, possessions, or achievements in order to attract admiration, envy, or status.
groups.summary_zh: 强调带着自豪、招摇或炫耀的意味展示服饰、财物或特质。
groups.desc_en: An intensity scale of conspicuous self-presentation, ranging from playfully wearing a noticeable item to shamelessly rubbing an advantage in others' faces.
groups.desc_zh: 从带有些许自豪感的随性穿戴展示，层层升级到毫无顾忌、公然招摇的炫示强度梯队。
groups.nuance_en: sport: visibly and casually wear or exhibit (beard / badge / style) · flash: ostentatiously gleam or momentarily reveal (cash / diamond / credentials) · parade: deliberately strut or exhibit at length (achievements / wealth) · show off: actively posture to elicit praise (new car / talents) · flaunt: aggressively and brazenly display to provoke or impress (privilege / wealth)
groups.nuance_zh: sport: 略带自豪地穿戴展现 (beard / badge / style) · flash: 显摆性地闪现亮出 (cash / diamond / credentials) · parade: 招摇过市地高调展示 (achievements / wealth) · show off: 卖力表现以博取赞许 (new car / talents) · flaunt: 嚣张跋扈地炫耀示威 (privilege / wealth)

groups.name: Disqualify & Invalidate · 取消资格与使不合格 (Disqualify, Invalidate, Incapacitate)
groups.tip: 判定不符规范，剥夺参与资格

items.def_en: To officially decide that someone or something is ineligible or no longer considered
items.ex_en: His recent shoulder injury might rule out his participation in the championship tournament.
items.ex_zh: 他最近的肩伤可能会彻底排除他参加锦标赛的资格。

items.def_en: To officially declare someone ineligible to participate in a competition or hold an office
items.ex_en: The committee decided to disqualify the runner after detecting prohibited performance-enhancing drugs.
items.ex_zh: 检测出违禁兴奋剂后，委员会决定剥夺该赛跑选手的参赛资格。

items.def_zh: 使不合格，使不相宜，剥夺……的资格
items.def_en: To make someone or something unsuitable, incapable, or unqualified for a specific purpose or role.
items.ex_en: Severe visual impairment will necessarily unfit an applicant for commercial pilot duties.
items.ex_zh: 严重的视力损伤必然会使申请人丧失担任商业飞行员的资格。

items.def_en: To deprive a contract, claim, or standing of official legal effectiveness or soundness
items.ex_en: Failing to sign the document properly will completely invalidate the insurance policy.
items.ex_zh: 未能合规签署该文件将使整份保险单完全作废。

items.def_en: To render someone unable to function or legally unqualified due to injury or illness
items.ex_en: A sudden stroke incapacitated the senior executive, forcing him to step down immediately.
items.ex_zh: 突发中风让这位高管丧失了工作能力，迫使他立即辞职。

groups.summary_en: Involves legally, procedurally, or physically stripping someone of their eligibility, legitimacy, or fitness to perform an official role or contest.
groups.summary_zh: 通过法律、规则或身心状态使人失去任职或比赛资格。
groups.desc_en: To render a person or thing formally or inherently ineligible, powerless, or legally void, unlike temporary suspension or mere criticism.
groups.desc_zh: 因资格不符、程序瑕疵或能力丧失而在法律、规则或实质上剥夺其有效性，区别于暂时的停职或单纯的批评。
groups.nuance_en: rule out: dismiss as an option during evaluation (possibility / candidate) · disqualify: declare officially ineligible by violation or defect (athlete / bidder) · unfit: render substantively unsuitable or inadequate (soldier / applicant) · invalidate: nullify the legal or factual force (contract / election / theory) · incapacitate: strip of physical or mental power to function (illness / injury / debtor)
groups.nuance_zh: rule out: 排除可能性或人选 (possibility / candidate) · disqualify: 因违规或缺陷取消法定资格 (athlete / bidder) · unfit: 使在体质或实质上不合格 (soldier / applicant) · invalidate: 使法律效力或事实依据作废 (contract / election / theory) · incapacitate: 使丧失生理或法定行为能力 (illness / injury / debtor)

groups.name: Disrupt & Derail · 扰乱与破坏 (Derail, Upset, Discommode)
groups.tip: 从横加干预到打破秩序

items.def_en: to throw plans, arrangements, or an equilibrium into unexpected confusion or disorder
items.ex_en: The surprise train cancellation completely upset our carefully prepared holiday travel schedule.
items.ex_zh: 列车突然取消彻底打乱了我们精心准备的度假行程安排。

items.def_en: to interrupt or cause problems that prevent an event, system, or process from continuing normally.
items.ex_en: The ongoing power outages severely disrupt production across the entire manufacturing sector.
items.ex_zh: 持续的停电严重扰乱了整个制造业部门的正常生产。

items.def_en: to successfully oppose or block someone's efforts, plans, or ambitions from succeeding
items.ex_en: Vigilant border guards successfully thwarted an ambitious plan to smuggle rare artifacts.
items.ex_zh: 机警的边防警卫成功挫败了一项走私珍贵文物的宏大图谋。

items.def_zh: 使脱轨；阻碍破坏（计划/谈判）
items.def_en: to cause a plan, project, or negotiation to fail, veer off course, or collapse suddenly
items.ex_en: A dispute over patent rights threatens to derail the historic multi-billion merger.
items.ex_zh: 专利权的争议有可能阻碍并破坏这场数十亿美元的历史性并购。
items.ex2_en: The speeding passenger train derailed violently along the treacherous icy mountain curve.
items.ex2_zh: 飞驰的客运列车在危险结冰的山道弯道处剧烈脱轨。

items.def_en: to overturn or thoroughly destabilize an established system, assumption, or state of affairs
items.ex_en: The revolutionary invention will completely upend established theories within global climate science.
items.ex_zh: 这项革命性的发明将彻底颠覆全球气候科学界的既有理论。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe throwing a structured process, schedule, system, or organization into disorder or breakdown by active interference or sudden interference.
groups.summary_zh: 强调强行打断、阻挠或破坏既有秩序与进程，造成混乱或中断。
groups.desc_en: An intensity escalation of disordering an established process, escalating from minor inconvenience to total, catastrophic derailment.
groups.desc_zh: 对既定秩序或进程破坏烈度的递增，从轻微打乱、造成混乱直到彻底颠覆和摧毁。
groups.nuance_en: upset: perturb an equilibrium or schedule (stomach / plans / balance) · disrupt: throw a continuous system into disorder (traffic / supply chain) · thwart: actively block a purpose from succeeding (plot / ambition / bid) · derail: cause a process to veer into total collapse (negotiations / career) · upend: overturn an entire established order or status quo (industry / assumptions / life)
groups.nuance_zh: upset: 扰乱原有的平衡或计划 (stomach / plans / balance) · disrupt: 破坏连续系统的正常运转 (traffic / supply chain) · thwart: 设卡阻挠使企图落空 (plot / ambition / bid) · derail: 使进程脱轨并陷入瘫痪 (negotiations / career) · upend: 彻底倾覆既定格局或认知 (industry / assumptions / life)

groups.name: Disrupt & Interrupt · 打扰与中断 (Disrupt, Intrude, Break up)
groups.tip: 中途插手干预直至进程被打断

items.def_en: To interrupt someone who is speaking or disrupt an ongoing discussion
items.ex_en: Please do not break in while the committee chairman is delivering his report.
items.ex_zh: 在委员会主席作报告时，请大家不要随便插话打岔。

items.def_en: To stop someone while they are speaking or break a connection prematurely
items.ex_en: Heavy snow cut off several remote villages for days.
items.ex_zh: 大雪将几个偏远村庄阻隔了数天之久。

items.def_en: 1. To say or do something that makes someone stop speaking or doing an activity. 2. To stop a continuous process or flow temporarily.
items.ex_en: A persistent cough caused the speaker to interrupt his lecture several times.
items.ex_zh: 一阵持续不断的咳嗽导致演讲者多次被迫打断他的讲座。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To enter or interrupt without invitation or permission, disturbing privacy or activity
items.ex_en: Reporters must not intrude upon the grieving family during this difficult time.
items.ex_zh: 在这个艰难的时刻，记者们绝不能去侵扰悲痛中的家人。

items.def_en: To throw into disorder, radically break the continuity of, or stop a normal process
items.ex_en: Noisy protestors attempted to disrupt the international economic summit during opening remarks.
items.ex_zh: 喧闹的抗议者企图在开幕致辞期间破坏国际经济峰会的正常进行。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe breaking the ongoing continuity of an action, process, or event, causing temporary delay, disorder, or termination.
groups.summary_zh: 指介入进行中的事务或状态，造成中断、紊乱或阻碍。
groups.desc_en: An intensity spectrum of breaking into someone's ongoing activity or speech, moving from conversational interjection to invasive system disruption.
groups.desc_zh: 强行切入他人正在进行的话语或行动的强度梯队，从礼貌插话过渡到粗暴侵入与系统性打断。
groups.nuance_en: break in: interrupt a conversation or activity suddenly (conversation / thought) · cut off: abruptly sever someone's speech or connection (speaker / caller / supply) · interrupt: break continuity midway through an act (speech / silence / journey) · intrude: enter unwelcome into a private sphere (privacy / grief / thoughts) · disrupt: cause widespread turmoil that halts ongoing functioning (meeting / service)
groups.nuance_zh: break in: 突兀插话或打断 (conversation / thought) · cut off: 强行截断对方的话语或通路 (speaker / caller / supply) · interrupt: 中途打断连续性活动 (speech / silence / journey) · intrude: 违逆意愿擅自闯入私密空间 (privacy / grief / thoughts) · disrupt: 制造大范围混乱使进程瘫痪 (meeting / service)

groups.name: Disseminate & Broadcast · 广泛传播与散播 (Disseminate, Diffuse, Propagate)
groups.tip: 如播撒种子般广泛散播信息

items.def_en: To tell a lot of people news or information, especially when it may not be true
items.ex_en: Malicious gossips put about a false rumor regarding the company's impending bankruptcy.
items.ex_zh: 恶意造谣者四处散布有关公司即将破产的不实谣言。

items.def_en: To send or pass information, reports, or materials from person to person
items.ex_en: The secretary will circulate the finalized meeting minutes to all board members.
items.ex_zh: 秘书将把定稿的会议纪要分发给所有的董事会成员传阅。
items.ex2_en: Warm air circulated steadily through the central ventilation vents inside the modern building.
items.ex2_zh: 温暖的空气在现代大厦内部的中央通风口中稳定循环。

items.def_en: To spread an idea, belief, or theory widely among many people
items.ex_en: Political zealots utilized social platforms to propagate their extreme ideological views nationwide.
items.ex_zh: 政治狂热分子利用社交平台在全国范围内宣传他们极端的意识形态观点。
items.ex2_en: The revolutionary social movement propagated rapidly across neighboring regions within a single year.
items.ex2_zh: 这场革命性的社会运动在短短一年内迅速传播扩展到了邻近地区。

items.def_en: To spread information, customs, or influence widely into surrounding areas
items.ex_en: Trade routes helped diffuse advanced technological innovations throughout medieval European civilizations.
items.ex_zh: 贸易通道助力将先进的科技创新广泛扩散到整个中世纪欧洲文明中。
items.ex2_en: The rich scent of roasted coffee beans diffused rapidly throughout the quiet bakery.
items.ex2_zh: 浓郁的烘焙咖啡豆香味在安静的面包店里迅速弥漫开来。

items.def_zh: 传播，散播，分发（信息、知识等）
items.def_en: (formal) To spread information, knowledge, ideas, or news widely among many people.
items.ex_en: The university health center works tirelessly to disseminate vital disease prevention guidelines.
items.ex_zh: 大学健康中心不知疲倦地工作，以广泛传播关键的疾病预防指南。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers dispersing information, doctrines, findings, or seeds to a wide audience or across an expansive territory, often systematically.
groups.summary_zh: 指系统性、广泛地向公众散播信息、学说或观念。
groups.desc_en: To scatter information, rumors, or doctrines across a population or territory, distinguished by channel, velocity, and communicative intent.
groups.desc_zh: 将信息、谣言或思想学说向群体或空间推播发散，侧重传播渠道、速率与受众广度，区别于定点传达。
groups.nuance_en: put about: maliciously or loosely spread rumors (rumor / story) · circulate: pass around freely within a network (newsletter / memo / petition) · propagate: systematically breed and advance ideas or biological traits (doctrine / faith / plant) · diffuse: passively disperse evenly through a medium (heat / ideas / culture) · disseminate: widely and authoritatively broadcast seeds of knowledge (research / information / findings)
groups.nuance_zh: put about: 私下散布流言蜚语 (rumor / story) · circulate: 在闭环或网络中流转传阅 (newsletter / memo / petition) · propagate: 体系化繁育、宣传或延展 (doctrine / faith / plant) · diffuse: 均匀发散渗透入环境 (heat / ideas / culture) · disseminate: 广度播撒知识与研究成果 (research / information / findings)

groups.name: Dissipate & Disperse · 消散与驱散 (Dissipate, Disperse, Scatter)
groups.tip: 雾气或力量逐渐消散消失

items.def_en: To become bright and free of fog, clouds, or obstruction, or cause this clearance
items.ex_en: The dense morning fog began to clear once the wind picked up.
items.ex_zh: 风势一起来，清晨那片浓厚的迷雾就开始逐渐消散了。
items.ex2_en: Ground crews cleared fallen tree branches from the icy runway before the flight landed.
items.ex2_zh: 在航班降落前，地勤人员清理了结冰跑道上掉落的树枝。

items.def_en: To disperse and disappear as the sun warms the atmosphere (used especially of fog or mist)
items.ex_en: The morning mist should burn off rapidly once the bright sun rises.
items.ex_zh: 一旦明亮的太阳升起，晨雾应该很快就会经日晒而散去。
items.ex2_en: The hot afternoon sun quickly burned off the dense fog hanging over the valley.
items.ex2_zh: 午后火热的太阳迅速驱散蒸发了笼罩在山谷上方的浓雾。

items.def_en: To move or make people, particles, or animals move apart quickly in various directions
items.ex_en: Loud thunderclaps made the startled pigeons scatter instantly across the wide square.
items.ex_zh: 响亮的雷声让受惊的鸽群瞬间四散在开阔的广场上。
items.ex2_en: A sudden gust of wind scattered the dry leaves across the lawn.
items.ex2_zh: 一阵突如其来的狂风把枯叶吹散在草坪上。

items.def_en: To cause a group, smoke, or cloud to scatter in different directions and clear
items.ex_en: Riot police deployed water cannons to disperse the hostile crowd outside parliament.
items.ex_zh: 防暴警察动用水炮驱散了议会大厦外充满敌意的聚集人群。
items.ex2_en: The thick morning fog will disperse as the warm sun rises.
items.ex2_zh: 随着温暖的太阳升起，清晨的浓雾将会消散。

items.def_zh: （使烟、云、感情等）消散，消除；挥霍，浪费
items.def_en: 1. to gradually fade away, scatter, and disappear, or to cause something to do so 2. to waste time, energy, or money foolishly
items.ex_en: The intense heat from midday sun caused the lingering fog to dissipate.
items.ex_zh: 正午阳光的酷热使弥漫未散的薄雾逐渐消散得无影无踪。
items.ex2_en: Gentle ocean breezes quickly dissipated the unpleasant odor from the harbor.
items.ex2_zh: 温和的海风迅速吹散了港口难闻的气味。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on the manner of disappearance through breaking up, spreading thin, or scattering across a wide space (such as fog, clouds, crowds, or tension), leaving nothing concentrated.
groups.summary_zh: 着重指通过由聚变散、向外扩散稀释而使实体或气氛归于无形。
groups.desc_en: The physical disintegration or thinning out of a concentrated mass until it dissolves, distinct from moving as a coherent whole.
groups.desc_zh: 原本聚集的实体或能量在空间中逐渐稀释、分散直至化为乌有，区别于整体转移或机械移动。
groups.nuance_en: clear: become transparent or free of obstruction (smoke / sky / mist) · burn off: vanish under the heat of the sun (fog / haze) · scatter: send or flee in random directions (crowd / seeds / ashes) · disperse: break up an assembly or concentration systematically (protesters / cloud / chemical) · dissipate: dissolve gradually into nothingness (energy / tension / fortune)
groups.nuance_zh: clear: 障碍物退散而恢复清澈明朗 (smoke / sky / mist) · burn off: 受日照烘烤而蒸发消散 (fog / haze) · scatter: 杂乱无章地向四处溃散或抛撒 (crowd / seeds / ashes) · disperse: 驱散聚合人群或稀释密集浓度 (protesters / cloud / chemical) · dissipate: 逐渐飘散消耗直至完全归零 (energy / tension / fortune)

groups.name: Dissuade & Deter · 劝阻与设法打消 (Dissuade, Deter, Discourage)
groups.tip: 循循善诱给出建议，力劝打消原定念头

items.def_en: Convince someone through earnest discussion not to do something they planned
items.ex_en: His worried mother tried earnestly to talk him out of dropping out.
items.ex_zh: 他担忧的母亲诚挚地试图说服他放弃退学的念头。

items.def_en: (+ from) To persuade someone not to do something.
items.ex_en: Security advisors managed to dissuade the president from visiting the volatile combat zone.
items.ex_zh: 安全顾问们设法劝阻了总统，使其打消前往动荡交战区的念头。

items.def_en: (formal) Strongly urge someone against foolish conduct or towards duty
items.ex_en: The judge exhorted the young offender against continuing a reckless criminal lifestyle.
items.ex_zh: 法官竭力规劝那名年轻罪犯，警告他切勿再过这种鲁莽的犯罪生活。

items.def_en: Tell someone explicitly to stay away from a person, place, or dangerous activity
items.ex_en: The guard fired a shot into the air to warn off intruders.
items.ex_zh: 警卫朝天开了一枪以警告入侵者离开。

items.def_en: (+ from) Prevent someone from doing something by making them fearful of the consequences
items.ex_en: Harsh financial penalties are designed to deter corporations from dumping hazardous chemical waste.
items.ex_zh: 严厉的经济处罚旨在威慑各大企业，防止它们倾倒危险化学废物。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on targeted interpersonal verbal communication intended to talk someone out of an intended action, course of conduct, or risky plan by offering reasons and warnings.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重以语言说理或指出不良后果，促使对方打消念头。
groups.desc_en: An intensity scale of discouraging an agent from an intended action, progressing from gentle verbal persuasion to fear-inducing structural barriers.
groups.desc_zh: 劝阻或阻吓他人行动的强度阶梯，从温和的说理劝导升级为利用恐惧和威慑手段迫使其放弃。
groups.nuance_en: talk out of: persuade away through reasoned dialogue (decision / resigning) · dissuade: advise against by appealing to reason or consequences (client / friend) · exhort: urgently urge or admonish away from vice or danger (masses / disciples) · warn off: sternly caution to stay away from hazard or boundary (intruders / investors) · deter: prevent action by instilling fear of severe retribution or cost (criminals / aggression / attacks)
groups.nuance_zh: talk out of: 通过谈话摆明利害说服其打消念头 (decision / resigning) · dissuade: 从后果角度循循劝阻 (client / friend) · exhort: 恳切告诫甚至警示 (masses / disciples) · warn off: 严正警告使其知难而退 (intruders / investors) · deter: 以严惩或巨大代价使其心生恐惧不敢妄动 (criminals / aggression / attacks)

groups.name: Distract & Sidetrack · 分心与转移 (Distract, Deflect, Divert)
groups.tip: 偏移正题或将注意力强行引开

items.def_en: To take someone's attention away from what they are trying to do or focus on
items.ex_en: Loud traffic noises outside frequently distract students from focusing on their complex exam.
items.ex_zh: 窗外嘈杂的交通噪音经常分散学生们的注意力，使他们难以专注于复杂的考试。

items.def_en: To cause someone or something to change direction or turn their attention elsewhere
items.ex_en: Police officers had to divert northbound traffic onto secondary roads after the accident.
items.ex_zh: 事故发生后，警官们不得不将北行车流转移引导至次级公路上。

items.def_en: To redirect criticism, questions, or attention away from oneself to someone or something else
items.ex_en: The clever politician easily deflected uncomfortable questions about his questionable campaign contributions.
items.ex_zh: 这位精明的政客轻而易举地转移了有关其可疑竞选捐款的尖锐提问。
items.ex2_en: The stray bullet deflected off the thick armor without penetrating it.
items.ex2_zh: 流弹击中厚装甲后发生偏转，未能穿透。

items.def_zh: 使分心，使偏离正题；转变话题
items.def_en: 1. (often passive) To distract someone from their main topic, goal, or task onto something less important.
items.ex_en: Minor procedural debates threatened to sidetrack the committee from its core investigative duties.
items.ex_zh: 细枝末节的程序性争论有可能使委员会偏离其核心的调查任务。

items.def_en: To make someone believe something false or behave improperly, leading them away from the right path
items.ex_en: Corrupt associates deliberately led the impressionable heir astray into illegal gambling rings.
items.ex_zh: 心术不正的同伙蓄意引诱这名缺乏主见的继承人走入歧途，卷入非法赌博圈。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve drawing a person's attention, thoughts, or momentum away from their central objective or focus. They emphasize cognitive interruption, avoidance, or derailment.
groups.summary_zh: 指引开注意力、打断核心思路或使目标与讨论偏离正轨。
groups.desc_en: Mechanisms that draw attention, resources, or motion away from an intended target or correct path, differing in agency and trajectory.
groups.desc_zh: 通过不同手法将注意力、路线或能量自既定靶心调离，侧重偏离方向与诱导机制。
groups.nuance_en: distract: shatter focus by sensory intrusion (driver / attention / audience) · divert: intentionally rechannel a flow or mental focus (traffic / attention / funds) · deflect: bounce an incoming force or criticism away (criticism / missile / blow) · sidetrack: draw into an irrelevant secondary tangent (discussion / investigation) · lead astray: misguide toward moral error or confusion (youth / inquiry)
groups.nuance_zh: distract: 因感官刺激使专注力涣散 (driver / attention / audience) · divert: 有意识地将水流、资金或注意力引向他处 (traffic / attention / funds) · deflect: 使来袭的外力或批评偏转弹开 (criticism / missile / blow) · sidetrack: 扯入无关紧要的旁枝末节 (discussion / investigation) · lead astray: 诱入歧途或导致认知走偏 (youth / inquiry)

groups.name: Diverge & Deviate · 分岔与偏离 (Deviate, Stray, Veer)
groups.tip: 由同一道路分道扬镳

items.def_en: To wander away from the correct place, route, or subject unintentionally
items.ex_en: The lecturer warned the students not to stray from the designated topic.
items.ex_zh: 讲师告诫学生们在讨论时不要无意偏离指定的讲题。

items.def_zh: 岔开，分叉；产生分歧，偏离
items.def_en: 1. (of roads, paths, lines, etc.) To separate and go in different directions; branch off. 2. (of opinions, trends, etc.) To differ, disagree, or develop in different directions.
items.ex_en: Their political opinions began to diverge sharply after the contentious national election.
items.ex_zh: 在引发争议的全国大选之后，他们的政治观点开始产生尖锐的分歧。

items.def_en: (+ from) To act differently from standard practice, an original plan, or expectations
items.ex_en: The research team decided not to depart from standard testing protocols this time.
items.ex_zh: 研究小组决定这一次绝不偏离标准试验规程。

items.def_en: To depart from an established course, standard, rule, or acceptable behavior
items.ex_en: Pilots must never deviate from authorized flight corridors during severe winter storms.
items.ex_zh: 在严冬暴风雪期间，飞行员绝不能擅自偏离核准的飞行航线。

items.def_en: To change direction or course suddenly and sharply
items.ex_en: The speeding vehicle suddenly veered into oncoming traffic to avoid hitting the animal.
items.ex_zh: 超速行驶的车辆突然猛转向迎面驶来的车流，以避免撞到动物。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express moving apart from a common physical course or departing from a standard, norm, or topic. They emphasize separation of trajectory, divergence of opinions, or drifting off track.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重路线的分离散开，或行动、观点偏离既定轨道与标准。
groups.desc_en: The manner in which a moving entity, path, or standard drifts away from an established baseline, tracking, or convention.
groups.desc_zh: 实体运动、行进轨迹或标准规范偏离既定基准线的具体方式，区别于彻底掉头或静止中断。
groups.nuance_en: stray: wander aimlessly or unconsciously off course (path / sheep / topic) · diverge: split into separate, increasingly distant directions (paths / opinions / branches) · depart: deliberately set aside customary practice (tradition / protocol / norm) · deviate: bend away from an accepted standard or statistical norm (norm / standard / course) · veer: make a sudden, sharp, uncontrolled change in direction (car / wind / policy)
groups.nuance_zh: stray: 无意识漫步走失或脱离正轨 (path / sheep / topic) · diverge: 从同一点分道扬镳且距离渐远 (paths / opinions / branches) · depart: 主动打破或背离既定成规 (tradition / protocol / norm) · deviate: 偏离既定标准或统计正态 (norm / standard / course) · veer: 突然且不可控地猛烈转向 (car / wind / policy)

groups.name: Diverge & Dissent · 异议与意见分歧 (Dissent, Differ, Conflict)
groups.tip: 从意见不合升级为公开放抗

items.def_en: (+ with/from/on) To hold an unlike opinion or distinct view on a matter
items.ex_en: The chief economist strongly differed with fellow board members on monetary policy.
items.ex_zh: 首席经济学家在货币政策上与其他董事会成员意见严重相左。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) To enter into a serious dispute or breach in friendship due to an argument
items.ex_en: The two business partners fell out over how to divide their company's unexpected profits.
items.ex_zh: 这两位商业合伙人因如何分配公司这笔意外利润而彻底闹翻了。

items.def_zh: 不同意，持异议；不一致，不符；（食物等对身体）不适宜
items.def_en: 1. (+ with/on/about) To have a different opinion or fail to agree with someone. 2. To not match or correspond. 3. (+ with) (of food or climate) To cause someone slight physical discomfort.
items.ex_en: Several committee members strongly disagree with the chairman on the proposed policy changes.
items.ex_zh: 几位委员会成员就拟议的政策变动与主席持强烈异议。

items.def_en: (+ from) To refuse to agree with an official opinion, established dogma, or common consensus
items.ex_en: Two senior justices dissented from the majority ruling in the landmark constitutional case.
items.ex_zh: 在这一具有里程碑意义的宪法案件中，两名资深大法官对多数判决表示反对。

items.def_en: (+ with/over) To hold beliefs, ideas, or interests that collide directly and incompatibly
items.ex_en: His conservative principles clash sharply with the progressive values promoted by his colleagues.
items.ex_zh: 他的保守原则与同事们所倡导的激进价值观发生了尖锐冲突。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe expressing or sustaining divergence in perspective, belief, or reasoning. Contrasts delineate mild intellectual difference from formal legal or political defiance against a consensus.
groups.summary_zh: 对既有观点、主张或共识表达分歧、不一致或异议。
groups.desc_en: An intensity spectrum of intellectual and personal conflict, scaling from subtle variance of opinion to explosive, irreconcilable confrontation.
groups.desc_zh: 人际或思想矛盾的激烈度进阶，从细微的分歧逐步演化为公开异议直至针锋相对的激烈交火。
groups.nuance_en: differ: hold distinct perspectives or qualities without animosity (opinions / tastes) · disagree: express explicit non-concurrence (statement / proposal) · fall out: enter into bitter personal estrangement after dispute (friends / partners) · dissent: formally refuse to conform with official orthodoxy (judge / party / faction) · clash: collide with volatile, hostile incompatibility (cultures / personalities / troops)
groups.nuance_zh: differ: 见解或特质各不相同且不带敌意 (opinions / tastes) · disagree: 明确表达不赞同或意见不合 (statement / proposal) · fall out: 因争吵闹翻而反目成仇 (friends / partners) · dissent: 官方或体制内正式提出异议 (judge / party / faction) · clash: 针锋相对地爆发正面交锋 (cultures / personalities / troops)

groups.name: Divert & Deflect · 偏转与转向 (Deflect, Siphon, Redirect)
groups.tip: 受阻或引导改变航向

items.def_en: Send traffic, resources, or communications via a different route
items.ex_en: Authorities had to reroute heavy traffic through narrow residential streets during construction.
items.ex_zh: 施工期间，有关部门不得不将繁忙的车流改道引至狭窄的居民区街道。

items.def_en: Gradually divert money or resources from one intended source into another
items.ex_en: Corrupt officials managed to siphon off millions from the international flood relief fund.
items.ex_zh: 腐败官员设法从国际抗洪救灾基金中抽走了数百万资金。

items.def_zh: 使转向，使改道；转移（注意力等）；娱乐
items.def_en: 1. To make someone or something change direction or follow a different route. 2. To redirect resources or attention for a different purpose. 3. (formal) To entertain or amuse someone.
items.ex_en: The government decided to divert crucial development funds toward emergency healthcare infrastructure.
items.ex_zh: 政府决定将至关重要的发展资金转用于应急医疗基础设施。

items.def_zh: 偏斜；使转向；转移（视线/批评）
items.def_en: Cause an incoming projectile or accusation to bounce off and change direction
items.ex_en: The politician tried to deflect harsh criticism by blaming previous administrative failures.
items.ex_zh: 这位政客试图通过归咎于前任政府的失误来转移严厉的批评。
items.ex2_en: The heavy tennis ball deflected sharply off the edge of the net.
items.ex2_zh: 沉重的网球擦到球网边缘后急剧偏转。

items.def_zh: 挡开（武器）；巧妙避开（质问）
items.def_en: Ward off an incoming blow or skillfully deflect a difficult question
items.ex_en: The prime minister managed to parry hostile questions about the controversial new tax.
items.ex_zh: 首相巧妙地避开了关于这项有争议的新税种的敌意质问。

groups.summary_en: Describes deliberately forcing an object, projectile, person, or resource to change its path or orientation. This includes physical ricochets and the intentional rerouting of traffic, rivers, attention, or funds.
groups.summary_zh: 指主动改变物体行进方向，或调转目光、话题、资源流向。
groups.desc_en: Tactical maneuvers to intercept and alter the heading or destination of a fluid, object, or threat, unlike stopping it dead.
groups.desc_zh: 截击并改变流体、物体或外来威胁的运动路线，侧重调整轨迹而非硬性逼停。
groups.nuance_en: reroute: systematically map to a different itinerary (traffic / flight / call) · siphon off: secretly drain or embezzle a portion of a flow (funds / fuel / resources) · divert: channel away to an alternative course or outlet (river / flight / resources) · deflect: bounce aside an incoming trajectory on impact (bullet / blow / blame) · parry: artfully ward off an attack or awkward question (thrust / question / blow)
groups.nuance_zh: reroute: 官方或体系性地重新规划路线 (traffic / flight / call) · siphon off: 暗中抽取、分流侵吞 (funds / fuel / resources) · divert: 将水流或资源引向替代分支 (river / flight / resources) · deflect: 借力反弹改变来袭物体或指责的轨迹 (bullet / blow / blame) · parry: 灵巧招架避开物理攻势或尴尬盘问 (thrust / question / blow)

groups.name: Divert & Transform · 转向与内倾 (Internalize, Invert, Deflect)
groups.tip: 改变原有流向，转向内在或别处

items.def_zh: 使内向，使转向内在；使内弯，内陷
items.def_en: To turn one's thoughts, feelings, or interests inward; to fold or turn inward.
items.ex_en: Prolonged solitary confinement will inevitably introvert an inmate's thoughts and emotional responses.
items.ex_zh: 长期的单独监禁不可避免地会使囚犯的思想和情感反应内缩封闭。

items.def_en: To reorient one's thoughts, affections, or edges toward the interior rather than external reality
items.ex_en: In his grief, the reclusive poet turned inward, completely shunning the outside world.
items.ex_zh: 悲痛之中，这位隐世诗人转向内心世界，彻底避开了外界。

items.def_en: To turn something inside out, upside down, or completely reverse its directional order
items.ex_en: The sudden economic crisis threatened to invert the established hierarchy of social classes.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的经济危机有可能彻底颠倒既有的社会阶层秩序。

items.def_en: To cause something to alter its direct course or veer away toward a diverted track
items.ex_en: The strong magnetic field can deflect high-energy particles along a curved pathway.
items.ex_zh: 强磁场可以使高能粒子沿弯曲轨道发生偏转。
items.ex2_en: The spacecraft deflected slightly from its planned trajectory due to gravitational pull.
items.ex2_zh: 由于引力作用，航天器略微偏离了预定轨道。

items.def_en: To absorb and integrate thoughts, attitudes, or conflicts inward into one's psyche
items.ex_en: Children often internalize societal values before they learn how to evaluate them critically.
items.ex_zh: 儿童往往在学会批判性评估社会价值观之前，就已经将其内化于心。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame involve reorienting momentum, mental energy, or structure away from an outward path into an inward, reversed, or redirected trajectory. They bridge psychological introspection with geometric turning inward.
groups.summary_zh: 指将注意力、能量、结构从外向引向内部倾斜、折返或转向逆位。
groups.desc_en: Psychological and structural transformation where energies, attitudes, or structures are redirected inward or completely flipped.
groups.desc_zh: 心理动力或物理结构将其能量指向内部化或彻底颠倒变换，区别于向外宣泄或线性平移。
groups.nuance_en: turn inward: retreat into private psychological self-reflection (mind / thoughts / community) · introvert: direct psychological libido toward the internal world (personality / energy) · invert: flip upside down or reverse the established order (pyramid / values / relation) · deflect: shift external psychic pressure away onto another (guilt / anxiety) · internalize: incorporate external values or pain deeply into the self (values / guilt / oppression)
groups.nuance_zh: turn inward: 闭关自守或退缩回内心反思 (mind / thoughts / community) · introvert: 心理层面将精力引向内在潜意识 (personality / energy) · invert: 颠倒物理朝向或倒置价值序列 (pyramid / values / relation) · deflect: 转移心理压力或转嫁指责 (guilt / anxiety) · internalize: 将外在价值观或苦痛深度内化进自身系统 (values / guilt / oppression)

groups.name: Divination & Occult Foreseeing · 占卜与通灵预测 (Divine, Augur, Douse)
groups.tip: 借助占卜或异象提前窥见未来

items.def_zh: （用寻龙尺等）探寻水源或矿脉
items.def_en: To search for underground water or minerals using a handheld rod or pendulum
items.ex_en: The local farmer used a hazel branch to dowse for underground water.
items.ex_zh: 当地农夫用一根榛木枝探寻地下水源。

items.def_en: To discover hidden knowledge or future events by supernatural means or intuitive perception
items.ex_en: Ancient priests claimed they could divine the gods' intentions through celestial alignments.
items.ex_zh: 古代祭司声称他们能够通过天象排列来探知神明的意图。

items.def_en: To practice the art of foretelling the future without relying on empirical data
items.ex_en: Wandering mystics would soothsay future calamities for gullible villagers in exchange for food.
items.ex_zh: 流浪的玄学家会为轻信的村民预言未来的灾难，以此换取食物。

items.def_en: To predict or foresee an outcome by interpreting natural omens or signs
items.ex_en: Ancient seers claimed the flights of migratory birds could augur a king's victory.
items.ex_zh: 古代预言家声称候鸟的飞行轨迹能够预兆国王的胜利。

items.def_zh: （通过水晶球等）占卜预知未来，凝视窥探未来
items.def_en: to attempt to foresee the future or reveal distant events by gazing into a reflective object such as a crystal ball or mirror
items.ex_en: The cloaked sorceress began to scry the deep shadows within her obsidian mirror.
items.ex_zh: 披着斗篷的女巫开始凝视黑曜石镜子深处的阴影以窥探未来。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers methods of gaining insight into the future or uncovering hidden truths via occult, intuitive, or ritualistic practices rather than rational analysis.
groups.summary_zh: 通过通灵、巫术或直觉超自然手段占卜未来或探查隐秘。
groups.desc_en: Esoteric, ritualistic practices designed to uncover hidden resources or predict the future through supernatural attunement, not rational deduction.
groups.desc_zh: 借助神秘仪式、灵感应或巫术媒介勘探隐蔽资源或断定未来吉凶，区别于基于常识的科学推演。
groups.nuance_en: dowse: locate subterranean water or minerals via dowsing rod (water / minerals / ley lines) · divine: intuit or foretell through mystical insight or omen (future / intentions / truth) · soothsay: claim the ability to predict upcoming events (prophecy / fate) · augur: read signs and omens to portend success or failure (success / doom / future) · scry: peer into a reflective medium to receive visions (crystal / mirror / water)
groups.nuance_zh: dowse: 借助寻龙尺/探杆勘测地下水源或矿藏 (water / minerals / ley lines) · divine: 借助通灵感应占卜吉凶或直觉洞察 (future / intentions / truth) · soothsay: 预言世事与宿命 (prophecy / fate) · augur: 观物候星象以预兆成败 (success / doom / future) · scry: 凝视水晶球或水面等反射媒介通灵凝视 (crystal / mirror / water)

groups.name: Dodge & Duck · 躲避与低头 (Dodge, Evade, Weave)
groups.tip: 迅速闪身或低头避开撞击

items.def_en: To sneak away or extricate oneself discreetly from a commitment or gathering
items.ex_en: He made up a lame excuse to duck out of the boring meeting.
items.ex_zh: 他编造了一个蹩脚的借口，偷偷溜出了那个无聊的会议。

items.def_en: To step laterally away from an approaching threat, blow, or obstacle
items.ex_en: The agile boxer managed to sidestep the powerful right hook just in time.
items.ex_zh: 动作敏捷的拳击手及时侧步避开了那记强有力的右勾拳。

items.def_zh: 低头躲避，缩头避开；迅速躲避；浸入水中
items.def_en: 1. To lower your head or body quickly to avoid being seen or hit. 2. (informal) To avoid or dodge a duty, question, or responsibility. 3. To submerge or push briefly underwater.
items.ex_en: She had to duck quickly to avoid being struck by the flying ball.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不迅速低头，以免被飞来的球击中。

items.def_en: To move quickly aside or out of the way to avoid a blow, missile, or encounter
items.ex_en: The fugitive had to dodge between moving cars to escape the pursuing police.
items.ex_zh: 逃犯不得不在行驶的车辆间闪避穿梭以摆脱追赶的警察。

items.def_en: To make rapid zig-zagging directional shifts with the upper body to evade blows
items.ex_en: The nimble fighter continued to weave under incoming punches during the final round.
items.ex_zh: 在最后一个回合中，敏捷的拳手不断左右闪避来袭的拳头。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures rapid evasive bodily adjustments made to escape impending physical impacts, detection, or inconvenient duties. Verbs contrast swift lowering of the torso ('ducking') with lateral shifts ('dodging') and strategic maneuvers.
groups.summary_zh: 指迅速低头或侧身避开来袭物、视线或责任的敏捷闪避动作。
groups.desc_en: Kinematic evasion tactics of the body or mind to elude sudden physical blows, traps, or unwanted social obligations.
groups.desc_zh: 身体或心智采取的躲闪机动，用以规避来袭的击打、障碍或强加的社交职责，区别于逃跑。
groups.nuance_en: duck: drop head or body down swiftly (head / punch / blow) · duck out of: slip away sneakily from an obligation (responsibility / meeting) · dodge: sidestep swiftly to evade a moving hazard or inquiry (bullet / traffic / tax / question) · sidestep: elegantly circumvent a prickly issue (controversy / question / regulation) · weave: thread evasively through obstacles with winding motion (through traffic / defenders)
groups.nuance_zh: duck: 猛然压低头部或身体下潜 (head / punch / blow) · duck out of: 悄悄溜走以逃避差事 (responsibility / meeting) · dodge: 敏捷侧跳闪避来物或刁难问题 (bullet / traffic / tax / question) · sidestep: 巧妙绕过或架空争议焦点 (controversy / question / regulation) · weave: 蛇形穿梭穿过层层障碍 (through traffic / defenders)

groups.name: Domineer & Patronize · 盛气凌人与作威作福 (Boss around, Bully, Trample)
groups.tip: 居高临下施加统辖

items.def_en: To continually tell someone what to do in an unpleasant and domineering way
items.ex_en: Stop trying to boss everyone around like you own the entire department.
items.ex_zh: 别再像整个部门都是你的一样，对所有人颐指气使了。

items.def_zh: 称王称霸，作威作福；册封为贵族
items.def_en: 1. (lord it over) To act in a superior, arrogant, or domineering way toward someone. 2. To make someone a lord.
items.ex_en: He loved to lord it over his younger coworkers whenever the manager left.
items.ex_zh: 每当经理离开时，他总喜欢对年轻的同事们作威作福。

items.def_zh: 以恩赐态度对待，居高临下看人
items.def_en: To speak to or treat someone in a way that seems kind but clearly betrays a feeling of superiority
items.ex_en: Senior executives must not patronize junior staff when addressing their legitimate workplace concerns.
items.ex_zh: 高管在回应初级员工合理的职场关切时，绝不可流露出居高临下的态度。

items.def_en: To treat someone in a domineering, harassing, or intimidating manner
items.ex_en: The brutal schoolmaster would constantly bullyrag the weaker students until they wept openly.
items.ex_zh: 冷酷的教书先生经常威逼恐吓体弱的学生，直逼得他们当众哭泣。

items.def_en: To act without any care for someone else's feelings, rights, or opinions
items.ex_en: The greedy developer rode roughshod over the objections raised by local residents.
items.ex_zh: 贪婪的开发商横行霸道，对当地居民提出的反对意见全然不顾。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame convey exercising authority in an arrogant, overbearing, or haughty manner, treating subordinates as inferiors and micromanaging them aggressively.
groups.summary_zh: 以高高在上、跋扈蛮横的姿态压制或差遣他人。
groups.desc_en: An intensity climb in authoritarian interpersonal oppression, escalating from petty nagging to unbridled, tyrannical subjugation.
groups.desc_zh: 人际交往中专横跋扈、凌驾于人烈度的递增，从好为人师、呼来喝去恶化为残酷践踏人权与尊严。
groups.nuance_en: patronize: treat condescendingly with an air of superior benevolence (client / audience) · boss around: annoyingly issue peremptory orders to subordinates (staff / siblings) · bullyrag: intimidate and harangue overbearingly (witness / junior) · lord: act arrogantly superior over someone (over peers / over family) · ride roughshod over: tyrannically crush rules, rights, or feelings without mercy (rights / objections / opposition)
groups.nuance_zh: patronize: 居高临下地假装宽宏关照 (client / audience) · boss around: 好发号施令地呼来喝去 (staff / siblings) · bullyrag: 盛气凌人地恐吓训斥 (witness / junior) · lord: 作威作福地居高临下支配 (over peers / over family) · ride roughshod over: 肆意践踏他人权利或规章 (rights / objections / opposition)

groups.name: Don & Wear · 穿戴与着身 (Don, Slip On, Throw On)
groups.tip: 把衣履护具穿戴于身躯上

items.def_en: Wear or display an item of clothing, jewelry, or haircut conspicuously and with pride
items.ex_en: The young musician arrived at the awards ceremony sporting a vintage leather jacket.
items.ex_zh: 这位年轻的音乐家身穿一件复古皮夹克，神气十足地来到了颁奖典礼。

items.def_en: Put on a piece of clothing, armor, or an accessory, especially with some formality or purpose
items.ex_en: The surgeon will don sterile protective garments before entering the specialized operating theater.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生进入专用手术室前，将穿戴好无菌防护服。

items.def_zh: 穿，戴；蓄（发、须）（wear的过去分词）
items.def_en: (past participle of wear) To have clothing, jewellery, or an accessory on one's body.
items.ex_en: The queen had worn an exquisite diamond necklace to the royal banquet.
items.ex_zh: 王后佩戴着一条精致的钻石项链出席了皇家宴会。

items.def_en: Put on a garment or footwear quickly, easily, and without fuss
items.ex_en: She will slip on a light cardigan before heading outside into the evening.
items.ex_zh: 在步入暮色的室外之前，她会轻松套上一件薄开衫。

items.def_en: Put on clothes hastily and without worrying much about appearance
items.ex_en: I just threw on an old sweater and hurried out the door.
items.ex_zh: 我胡乱套上一件旧毛衣就急匆匆地冲出了门。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on the transitional and durative acts of placing clothes, shoes, or accessories onto the body. It ranges from deliberate dressing to quick, casual slipping on of apparel.
groups.summary_zh: 涵盖把衣服、配饰穿戴上身以及穿著的状态。
groups.desc_en: Distinct scenarios and registers of clothing oneself, spanning formal ceremonial dressing, casual throwing-on, to proud public wear.
groups.desc_zh: 穿戴服饰的不同语域与行为场景，涵盖正式仪式感披挂、仓促随性套上以及自信的穿戴展示。
groups.nuance_en: throw on: dress hastily and casually without care (coat / clothes / shirt) · slip on: easily glide into a simple garment (shoes / jacket / robe) · don: formally or deliberately put on attire (uniform / mantle / armor) · sport: wear openly and self-confidently for visual effect (hat / suit / tie) · worn: actively have clothing upon the body continuously (shoes / garments / coat)
groups.nuance_zh: throw on: 随手套上匆忙披身 (coat / clothes / shirt) · slip on: 顺手轻松滑穿上身 (shoes / jacket / robe) · don: 庄重或郑重其事地穿戴上 (uniform / mantle / armor) · sport: 得意或自信地穿戴展示 (hat / suit / tie) · worn: 处于持续着身的状态 (shoes / garments / coat)

groups.name: Donate & Philanthropic Giving · 捐赠与施予 (Donate, Bestow, Contribute)
groups.tip: 出于善意无偿奉献

items.def_en: (+ to) To give money, goods, or resources alongside others toward a common fund or cause
items.ex_en: Generous benefactors contribute significant funds to the international disaster relief effort every year.
items.ex_zh: 慷慨的捐助者每年都向国际救灾工作捐献巨额资金。

items.def_zh: 捐赠，捐献（财物、器官或血液）
items.def_en: 1. To give money, food, clothes, blood, or organs to help a person or organization.
items.ex_en: The wealthy philanthropist plans to donate half of his vast fortune to charity.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有的慈善家计划将他庞大财产的一半捐赠给慈善机构。

items.def_en: To contribute a small amount of money or help toward a shared gift, fund, or endeavor
items.ex_en: All the team members decided to chip in twenty dollars for Sarah's gift.
items.ex_zh: 所有团队成员都决定凑二十美元为莎拉买礼物。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon) To present something valuable or honorable as a gift or conferment
items.ex_en: The prestigious university decided to bestow an honorary doctorate upon the legendary scientist.
items.ex_zh: 这所知名大学决定授予这位传奇科学家荣誉博士学位。

items.def_en: To leave money or personal property to someone or an institution in a will
items.ex_en: The wealthy aristocrat decided to bequeath his valuable art collection to the gallery.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有的贵族决定通过遗嘱将他珍贵的艺术收藏品捐赠给美术馆。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate transferring funds, goods, blood, or resources to a charity, institution, or needy party without expecting compensation. The action is driven by altruism, civic duty, or institutional philanthropy.
groups.summary_zh: 向慈善机构、组织或弱者无偿赠与资金、物品或资源。
groups.desc_en: Altruistic alienation of personal assets for public benefit, distinct according to institutional formality, testamentary transfer, or pooling.
groups.desc_zh: 无偿让渡私人资产以资助公共或慈善事业，因体制正规性、遗嘱继承或众人凑份子而场景各异。
groups.nuance_en: chip in: informally contribute small amounts to a shared sum (money / advice) · contribute: furnish resources or effort to a common fund or cause (funds / articles / time) · donate: officially give assets to a charity or public cause (blood / organs / millions) · bestow: confer a prestigious gift or honor ceremoniously upon a recipient (title / favor / blessing) · bequeath: legally leave assets to successors via testament (estate / fortune / legacy)
