items.ex_en: The strong tavern liquor threatened to inebriate the foreign visitors completely before midnight.
items.ex_zh: 小酒馆里的烈酒大有在午夜前就将外国访客彻底灌醉之势。

items.def_en: To confuse or stupify someone's mind, typically with alcohol
items.ex_en: Too many rounds of cheap grain liquor will easily befuddle a man's mind.
items.ex_zh: 几轮廉价烈酒下肚，很容易就会把一个人的神志灌得迷迷糊糊。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures physiological and psychological states caused by alcohol or psychoactive substances, ranging from light euphoria to incapacitating stupor.
groups.summary_zh: 指酒精或麻醉物质导致头晕目眩、兴奋或醉倒的生理状态。
groups.desc_en: Describes the physical effect of ethanol or drugs impairing motor control and mental faculty, contrasting with returning to a clear-headed state.
groups.desc_zh: 指酒精或药物等物质麻痹中枢神经导致感官失调与中毒，区别于清醒生理过程。
groups.nuance_en: intoxicate: formal biological induction of alcohol or drug poisoning (driver / guest / system) · inebriate: literary or clinical rendering into drunkenness (crowd / patrons) · befuddle: impairing cognitive faculty and coherence through drink (mind / faculties) · slosh: slang for rendering heavily, sloppily drunk (patron / drinker) · sober up: clearing the mind and metabolizing alcohol back to baseline (driver / reveler)
groups.nuance_zh: intoxicate: 医学与法医层面的酒精麻醉与体内致醉 (driver / guest / system) · inebriate: 文雅或书面语中指使酩酊大醉 (crowd / patrons) · befuddle: 酒精麻痹大脑使其昏头昏脑 (mind / faculties) · slosh: 俗语指喝得烂醉如泥 (patron / drinker) · sober up: 酒醒并恢复清醒认知 (driver / reveler)

groups.name: Introduce & Preface · 开篇与前置说明 (Preface, Foreword, Preamble)
groups.tip: 通过写序引出全书正题

items.def_en: To provide an opening statement or initial presentation to orient an audience
items.ex_en: The speaker took a moment to introduce the fundamental themes of the lecture.
items.ex_zh: 演讲者花了一点时间来介绍本次讲座的基本主题。

items.def_en: To introduce a speech, document, or statement with an introductory explanation
items.ex_en: The minister preambled his official announcement with a brief summary of current progress.
items.ex_zh: 部长在发表正式声明前，先简要概述了当前的进展作为开场白。

items.def_en: (+ to) To serve as an introduction or preparation for the main topic
items.ex_en: The historical overview served to lead in to the main discussion on policy reform.
items.ex_zh: 这段历史概述为接下来关于政策改革的主要讨论作了铺垫。

items.def_en: To start a book, performance, or speech with a particular remark or piece
items.ex_en: The keynote speaker decided to open with a humorous personal anecdote to engage everyone.
items.ex_zh: 主讲人决定以一段幽默的个人轶事作为开篇，以吸引大家的注意。

items.def_zh: 为……作序；以……作为开场白（或前奏）
items.def_en: (+ with) To introduce a book, speech, or action with an opening statement or preliminary event.
items.ex_en: He chose to preface his remarks with a heartfelt acknowledgment of his team's effort.
items.ex_zh: 他决定在发言前，先由衷致谢团队所付出的努力作为开场白。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this discourse-framing frame refer to providing introductory remarks, preambles, or background commentary that precede the main text or speech.
groups.summary_zh: 在正文、演说或行动之前作开篇介绍或铺垫说明。
groups.desc_en: Refers to uttering or setting down preliminary material to contextualize what follows, contrasting with diving immediately into the substantive core.
groups.desc_zh: 指在正文或正题之前引入铺垫性说明，区别于开门见山直奔核心实体内容。
groups.nuance_en: preface: providing an authorial explanation before a formal work or comment (remarks / book / speech) · introduce: presenting a new topic, speaker, or concept systematically (subject / speaker / topic) · open with: launching a performance or text with a specific opening act (quote / song / joke) · lead in: serving as a transitional, smooth ramp toward the main topic (main topic / discussion) · preamble: constructing a formal or constitutional prefatory rationale (treaty / declaration)
groups.nuance_zh: preface: 声明动机或在正题前加开场白 (remarks / book / speech) · introduce: 正式引入并呈现新话题或新概念 (subject / speaker / topic) · open with: 演出或文章以某元素作为开端起笔 (quote / song / joke) · lead in: 铺垫并顺畅引向正题 (main topic / discussion) · preamble: 撰写正式公约或法案的前言序文 (treaty / declaration)

groups.name: Introduce & Present · 介绍与引荐 (Present, Acquaint, Usher in)
groups.tip: 引荐新人或向公众展示展示

items.def_en: To formally introduce someone to another person or bring someone forward before an audience
items.ex_en: Allow me to present our guest of honor to the assembled distinguished members tonight.
items.ex_zh: 请允许我向今晚在座的各位尊贵成员引荐我们的主宾。

items.def_zh: 介绍，引荐；引进，推行；提出（议案等）；作为……的开端
items.def_en: 1. To tell someone another person's name when they meet for the first time. 2. To bring something into use or existence for the first time. 3. To formally present a bill, idea, or proposal for discussion.
items.ex_en: Let me introduce our new colleague to everyone before we begin the morning meeting.
items.ex_zh: 在早会开始前，让我向大家介绍一下我们的新同事。

items.def_en: To introduce a proposal, argument, or candidate for formal consideration or attention
items.ex_en: The committee decided to bring forward a revised proposal during the afternoon session.
items.ex_zh: 委员会决定在下午的会议上正式提出一项经修订的提案供审议。

items.def_en: To mark or signal the beginning of a new period, reform, or momentous era
items.ex_en: The breakthrough treaty promised to usher in an unprecedented era of economic cooperation.
items.ex_zh: 这项突破性条约有望开启一个前所未有的经济合作时代。

items.def_en: To make someone familiar with a person, fact, or situation through formal disclosure
items.ex_en: The director arranged a formal briefing to acquaint the board with the new regulations.
items.ex_zh: 董事安排了一次正式通报会，让董事会熟悉各项新规定。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this interpersonal and ceremonial frame involve acquainting individuals with each other or formally bringing an audience into contact with a person, work, or new concept. They span basic social introductions to formal ceremonial presentations.
groups.summary_zh: 在社交或正式场合将某人、事物引荐介绍给他人认识。
groups.desc_en: Involves bringing a person, innovation, or ceremonial display into social awareness or public view, contrasting with keeping something secret or withholding access.
groups.desc_zh: 指将人、事物或新纪元郑重推向社会认知或公众视野，区别于深藏不露或隐蔽搁置。
groups.nuance_en: introduce: making people known to each other or launching an innovation (guest / bill / concept) · present: offering formally for inspection, audience, or honor (award / candidate / findings) · usher in: marking the grand opening of a new historical epoch or trend (era / age / change) · acquaint: familiarizing a person with facts or another individual (oneself with / audience) · bring forward: proposing an idea or candidate for active consideration (proposal / motion / witness)
groups.nuance_zh: introduce: 彼此相识引见或推行新事物 (guest / bill / concept) · present: 庄重呈递、引荐展示以备检阅评判 (award / candidate / findings) · usher in: 迎入并开启全新时代或变革 (era / age / change) · acquaint: 使熟悉某人或告知详情 (oneself with / audience) · bring forward: 提出议案或提请人选考虑 (proposal / motion / witness)

groups.name: Intrude & Force Entry · 闯入与鲁莽侵入 (Barge, Burst, Muscle in)
groups.tip: 粗暴莽撞地冲入空间

items.def_en: To interrupt a conversation or meddle in someone else's affairs rudely without invitation
items.ex_en: I wish he wouldn't constantly butt in while we are discussing sensitive financial matters.
items.ex_zh: 我真希望在我们商讨敏感的财务问题时，他别老是插嘴。

items.def_en: (+ on/upon/into) To enter a place or join an activity where one is not invited, wanted, or expected
items.ex_en: Reporters repeatedly tried to intrude upon the grieving family during the private memorial service.
items.ex_zh: 在私人追悼会期间，记者们屡次试图侵扰这个悲痛的家庭。

items.def_en: To enter a room or building suddenly, loudly, and with great physical force
items.ex_en: Armed officers burst into the abandoned warehouse before the suspects could destroy any evidence.
items.ex_zh: 武装警察猛冲进废弃仓库，嫌疑人甚至来不及销毁任何证据。

items.def_en: (+ on) To force one's way into an organization, enterprise, or conversation by aggressive pressure
items.ex_en: A rival corporation tried to muscle in on their lucrative territory within weeks.
items.ex_zh: 几周之内，一家竞争对手便试图强行插足他们利润丰厚的业务地盘。

items.def_zh: 闯入，猛冲，乱撞；用驳船运送
items.def_en: 1. (+ into/past/through) To move clumsily and forcefully, intruding rudely into a place or bumping into people. 2. To transport goods by barge.
items.ex_en: He rudely barged into the private meeting room without even bothering to knock first.
items.ex_zh: 他连门都懒得敲，就蛮横无理地冲进了私人会议室。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures forceful, impolite, or clumsy bodily incursions into physical spaces or social situations without invitation. Nuances distinguish kinetic momentum from calculated social entitlement.
groups.summary_zh: 未获许可而粗暴、莽撞地闯入空间或介入他人谈话。
groups.desc_en: Describes pushing past physical or boundary thresholds violently or aggressively uninvited, contrasting with polite, sanctioned entry.
groups.desc_zh: 指无视界限与礼节，粗暴强行冲入或非法侵入他人空间，区别于礼貌受邀获准进入。
groups.nuance_en: intrude: infringing upon privacy or sovereign territory uninvited (privacy / property / space) · barge: clumsily or aggressively bursting into a room without knocking (room / office / door) · burst into: sudden, high-velocity entry driven by impulse (room / tears / flames) · muscle in: aggressively forcing one's way into an existing venture or market (territory / racket / market) · butt in: pushy personal intrusion into ongoing interaction (affairs / queue)
groups.nuance_zh: intrude: 侵扰隐私、专属领地或宁静 (privacy / property / space) · barge: 不敲门笨拙横冲直撞闯入 (room / office / door) · burst into: 势头迅猛地冲进房间或情绪爆发 (room / tears / flames) · muscle in: 倚仗势力强行插足地盘或市场 (territory / racket / market) · butt in: 蛮横插手他人地界或插队 (affairs / queue)

groups.name: Invigorate & Energize · 振奋与赋能 (Energize, Galvanize, Revitalize)
groups.tip: 为身体注入精力，精神大振

items.def_en: To make someone or something much more lively, spirited, colorful, or energetic
items.ex_en: A splash of vibrant paint will definitely pep up this dull and dreary living room.
items.ex_zh: 涂上一抹鲜艳的油漆肯定能让这间单调沉闷的客厅焕发活力。

items.def_en: To supply someone or something with enthusiasm, physical energy, or operational drive
items.ex_en: The passionate keynote address seemed to energize the entire staff for the project ahead.
items.ex_zh: 那场激昂的主旨演讲似乎为全体员工注入了应对后续项目的活力。

items.def_en: To imbue something languishing or depleted with new life, vigor, strength, or success
items.ex_en: Targeted public investments helped revitalize the once neglected historic district of the capital.
items.ex_zh: 有针对性的公共投资帮助首都这一曾被忽视的历史街区重获新生。

items.def_en: To shock or stimulate people into sudden, vigorous, purposeful excitement and rapid action
items.ex_en: The shocking investigative report served to galvanize the citizens into demanding immediate legislative reforms.
items.ex_zh: 这篇令人震惊的调查报道激励了市民立即采取行动，要求立法改革。

items.def_zh: 使精力充沛，使振奋；刺激，激励
items.def_en: 1. To give someone fresh energy, strength, and vitality; to stimulate or revitalize.
items.ex_en: A brisk walk through the cool mountain air will thoroughly invigorate your tired body.
items.ex_zh: 在清凉的山间空气中快步走上一程，能彻底让你疲惫的身体恢复充沛活力。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers imparting freshness, stamina, electrical dynamism, or biological vitality to a tired person, mind, or stagnant institution. 'Invigorate' evokes crisp physical rejuvenation, 'energize' conveys active operational power, and 'galvanize' indicates shocking into sudden motion.
groups.summary_zh: 指赋予活力、生机或精神力量，使疲乏或迟滞之物振奋重燃。
groups.desc_en: Refers to infusing fresh vitality, physical strength, or rapid momentum into an exhausted or stagnant system, contrasting with draining energy or leaving dormant.
groups.desc_zh: 指为疲惫或停滞的机体/系统注入强劲活力或激活动能，区别于耗竭生机或听任委靡。
groups.nuance_en: energize: charging with active operational power and drive (base / team / campaign) · invigorate: imparting brisk, healthy freshness and vitality (economy / body / debate) · revitalize: restoring dying life, solvency, or vigor to full health (neighborhood / company / culture) · galvanize: shocking into sudden, urgent collective action (public / community / coalition) · pep up: injecting quick, lively spark to cheer up spirits (performance / party / troops)
groups.nuance_zh: energize: 赋予充沛能量与驱动力 (base / team / campaign) · invigorate: 注入清新生机使身心精神焕发 (economy / body / debate) · revitalize: 使濒死衰败之物彻底复兴重焕生机 (neighborhood / company / culture) · galvanize: 如电击般强烈震惊并激发集体行动 (public / community / coalition) · pep up: 注入快节奏活力使其打起精神 (performance / party / troops)

groups.name: Invite & Bid · 邀请与招引 (Summon, Bid, Ask over)
groups.tip: 礼貌邀人参加活动或上门

items.def_zh: 邀请，约请；招致，诱发；征求
items.def_en: 1. To politely or formally ask someone to come somewhere or do something. 2. To act in a way that makes something unpleasant likely to happen. 3. To solicit or request suggestions, questions, or applications.
items.ex_en: The university planned to invite several world-renowned scientists to its annual research symposium.
items.ex_zh: 该大学计划邀请几位世界知名的科学家出席其年度科研研讨会。

items.def_en: To invite, summon, or order someone to attend or do something (literary or formal)
items.ex_en: The king did bid the weary traveler to sit and partake of the royal banquet.
items.ex_zh: 国王吩咐这位疲惫的旅人入座，共享御宴。

items.def_en: To invite someone to come to your home for a meal, drink, or social visit
items.ex_en: We should ask over the new neighbors for dinner sometime this coming weekend.
items.ex_zh: 我们应该在这个周末找个时间邀请新邻居来家里吃顿饭。

items.def_en: To entertain someone as a guest in one's home
items.ex_en: We're planning to have our neighbors over for drinks this weekend.
items.ex_zh: 我们打算周末请邻居来家里喝一杯。

items.def_en: To officially or authoritatively demand someone's presence
items.ex_en: The parliamentary committee decided to summon the chief executive for further formal questioning.
items.ex_zh: 议会委员会决定正式传唤该首席执行官接受进一步质询。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on requesting someone's presence, participation, or response, ranging from friendly social invitations to authoritative or ritualistic summons.
groups.summary_zh: 指请求或邀请某人出席、参与活动或前来作客。
groups.desc_en: Involves extending a formal or social summons requesting someone's presence, contrasting with commanding by force or banishing.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动向他人发出正式邀约或社交招请以使其光临，区别于强权押解或放逐排挤。
groups.nuance_en: invite: the standard polite request asking for attendance or participation (guest / comment / scrutiny) · bid: archaic or literary formal summoning or urging (farewell / guest / welcome) · ask over: informal, hospitable solicitation to visit one's home (neighbors / friends / folks) · have over: hosting someone as a domestic guest (company / family / colleagues) · summon: authoritative or legal command ordering someone to appear (witness / council / courage)
groups.nuance_zh: invite: 标准礼貌邀请出席或征求意见 (guest / comment / scrutiny) · bid: 书面或古雅的致意、招请或吩咐 (farewell / guest / welcome) · ask over: 口语中热情请人来家里串门 (neighbors / friends / folks) · have over: 接待某人在家中做客 (company / family / colleagues) · summon: 带有法律或权威强制力的传唤召见 (witness / council / courage)

groups.name: Invoke & Appeal to Authority · 援引与诉诸 (Invoke, Cite, Adduce)
groups.tip: 援引法条权威或呼吁求援

items.def_en: To refer to a book, article, law, or precedent as an authority or proof in an argument
items.ex_en: The lawyer was able to cite a relevant judicial precedent to support her client's claim.
items.ex_zh: 律师得以援引一项相关的司法判例来支持其当事人的主张。

items.def_zh: 退而诉诸，求助于（法律或权利）
items.def_en: To resort to an authority, statute, or reserve resource when other arguments or means have failed
items.ex_en: If my freelance business doesn't take off, I have some savings to fall back on.
items.ex_zh: 如果我的自由职业做不起来，我还有一些积蓄可以支撑。

items.def_en: To offer an example, reason, or piece of evidence as proof or justification in a formal argument
items.ex_en: The prosecutor failed to adduce sufficient compelling evidence to prove the defendant's guilt.
items.ex_zh: 检察官未能举出充分且有说服力的证据来证实被告有罪。

items.def_en: To formally appeal to or demand that someone or an authority take action or provide testimony
items.ex_en: Human rights organizations call upon the international community to enforce stricter sanctions immediately.
items.ex_zh: 人权组织呼吁国际社会立即实施更为严格的制裁。

items.def_en: 1. To cite a law, rule, or principle to justify an action or support an argument. 2. To appeal to a deity, spirit, or higher authority for help or protection. 3. To evoke or bring a feeling or image to mind.
items.ex_en: The government decided to invoke emergency powers to maintain public order during the crisis.
items.ex_zh: 政府决定援引紧急权力，以在危机期间维护公共秩序。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to calling upon an established law, authoritative precedent, constitutional right, or supernatural entity to legitimize a course of action or justify a contentious stance.
groups.summary_zh: 指引用法律法规、权威先例或崇高力量为自身行为辩护或立论。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on calling upon an authoritative precedent, law, or deity to substantiate a claim or legitimize action, contrasting with relying solely on naked personal assertion.
groups.desc_zh: 指引述法规、权威先例或诉诸神明为自身主张提供合法性依托，区别于仅凭个人空口断言。
groups.nuance_en: invoke: calling upon a law, right, deity, or spirit for protection or justification (clause / power / spirit) · cite: explicitly naming a text, author, or statistic as evidence (precedent / case / study) · adduce: formally bringing forward proofs or reasons in an argument (evidence / reason / instance) · call upon: appealing formally to an institution or person to act (government / allies / people) · fall back on: resorting to an underlying fallback measure when others fail (excuse / savings / precedent)
groups.nuance_zh: invoke: 诉诸神灵、援引法条或行使法定权利以求护佑证实 (clause / power / spirit) · cite: 精确列举文献、案例或数据作为论据 (precedent / case / study) · adduce: 严谨提出证言证据以支持争辩 (evidence / reason / instance) · call upon: 正式号召或呼吁某方付诸行动 (government / allies / people) · fall back on: 别无选择时退而求助于后手支撑 (excuse / savings / precedent)

groups.name: Involuntary Muscle Jerks · 抽动与肌肉震颤 (Twitch, Spasm, Tic)
groups.tip: 肌肉局部的细微不受控抽搐

items.def_en: 1. To make a sudden, brief, involuntary movement, or cause a body part to do so. 2. To pull or jerk something with a quick, sharp movement.
items.ex_en: His left eyelid began to twitch uncontrollably after working long hours under stress.
items.ex_zh: 在压力下长时间工作后，他的左眼皮开始不受控制地抽动。
items.ex2_en: The nervous horse twitched its sensitive ears toward the sudden rustling in the bushes.
items.ex2_zh: 紧张的马儿将敏感的耳朵朝向灌木丛中突然传来的沙沙声抽动了一下。

items.def_en: To exhibit a recurrent, involuntary muscular contraction, typically of the face
items.ex_en: A solitary muscle near his clenched jaw continued to tic in the pale moonlight.
items.ex_zh: 在苍白的月光下，他紧咬的下颌旁有一块肌肉仍在不停抽动。

items.def_en: To make rapid, light, irregular movements, such as a flickering eyelid or racing pulse
items.ex_en: Her eyelids began to flutter softly as she slowly drifted out of deep unconsciousness.
items.ex_zh: 随着她慢慢从深度昏迷中苏醒，眼睑开始微微颤动。
items.ex2_en: The startled songbird fluttered its colorful wings before darting into the dense canopy.
items.ex2_zh: 受惊的鸣禽振动着色彩斑斓的双翼，随后一头扎进了茂密的树冠中。

items.def_en: To shake or vibrate with a slight, rapid, and barely perceptible motion
items.ex_en: Her pale lips seemed to quiver with suppressed emotion as she spoke his name.
items.ex_zh: 当念出他的名字时，她苍白的嘴唇似乎因压抑着情绪而微微颤抖。

items.def_en: To undergo a sudden, involuntary, and often painful contraction of a muscle or muscle group
items.ex_en: The runner collapsed when his calf muscle began to violently spasm near the finish.
items.ex_zh: 快到终点时，跑者的小腿肌肉剧烈痉挛，随即倒在地上。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe sudden, brief, involuntary muscle contractions or small jerking movements. They range from tiny, repetitive eyelid flickers to sharp, localized bodily spasms.
groups.summary_zh: 描述身体局部肌肉微小、短暂且不由自主的抽搐、跳动或颤动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes sudden, brief, involuntary contractions of muscular fibers, contrasting with smooth, deliberate, coordinated motor actions.
groups.desc_zh: 指肌纤维发生的短暂、不由自主的突发性抽搐或微颤，区别于平稳自主协调的运动。
groups.nuance_en: twitch: brief, sharp, jerky contraction of a specific muscle (eyelid / muscle / lip) · spasm: sudden, painful involuntary prolonged muscle cramp (muscle / back / chest) · tic: habitual, repetitive involuntary neural twitch (facial / nervous) · flutter: light, rapid, unsteady fluttering motion (eyelashes / heart / pulse) · quiver: rapid, delicate trembling from chill, tension, or fear (lip / chin / voice)
groups.nuance_zh: twitch: 局部单次短促痉挛性抽动 (eyelid / muscle / lip) · spasm: 突发阵发性剧痛抽搐或肌肉痉挛 (muscle / back / chest) · tic: 神经质、习惯性反复抽动的面容动作 (facial / nervous) · flutter: 睫毛或心房轻微急促的扇动或悸动 (eyelashes / heart / pulse) · quiver: 因寒冷、恐惧而产生的细碎震颤 (lip / chin / voice)

groups.name: Involve & Entangle · 卷入与牵连 (Enmesh, Entangle, Implicate)
groups.tip: 深陷纷争或复杂事端之中

items.def_en: (+ in) To show or suggest that someone is involved in an illegal or morally reprehensible act
items.ex_en: Leaked financial documents directly implicate several senior executives in the massive bribery scandal.
items.ex_zh: 泄露的财务文件直接证实数名高管卷入了这起巨额贿赂丑闻。

items.def_en: (+ in/with) To cause someone or something to become caught in a confusing or compromising difficulty
items.ex_en: He warned his daughter never to entangle herself in dubious online investment schemes.
items.ex_zh: 他告诫女儿切莫让自己卷入可疑的网络投资骗局之中。

items.def_zh: 使卷入，使陷入（纷争或困境）；牵连
items.def_en: (+ in/with) (often passive) To involve someone deeply in an argument, conflict, or difficult situation.
items.ex_en: The neutral nation was determined not to embroil itself in the regional military conflict.
items.ex_zh: 这个中立国下定决心，绝不让自己卷入这场地区军事冲突之中。

items.def_en: (+ in) (usually passive) To involve someone deeply in a messy, intractable problem or controversy
items.ex_en: The ambitious municipal project became hopelessly mired in bureaucratic delays and intense controversy.
items.ex_zh: 这项雄心勃勃的市政工程无可救药地深陷于官僚拖延与激烈争议的泥潭之中。

items.def_en: (+ in) To entangle someone thoroughly in a complex net of troubles, conflicts, or deceit
items.ex_en: He found his family increasingly enmeshed in a perilous web of political intrigue.
items.ex_zh: 他发现自己的家族正愈发深陷于政治阴谋的凶险罗网之中。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on drawing or ensnaring someone deeply into a complicated, compromising dispute, crime, or hostile situation from which extraction is difficult.
groups.summary_zh: 指将人深陷于纷争、丑闻或困境中，难以脱身。
groups.desc_en: Depicts pulling an entity into a sticky, complicated, or compromising web of trouble or crime, contrasting with keeping clean detachment.
groups.desc_zh: 指将人或实体卷入复杂难解、自拔不得的麻烦或罪责泥潭，区别于洁身自好与明确切割。
groups.nuance_en: implicate: showing connection to a crime or compromising wrongdoing (suspect / official / scandal) · embroil: dragging into fierce, chaotic strife or discord (nation / politician / conflict) · entangle: snaring inextricably in complicated problems or relationships (finances / limbs / affairs) · enmesh: ensnaring thoroughly in a metaphorical web or trap (bureaucracy / network / system) · mire: sinking deeply into paralyzing mud, debt, or scandal (debt / controversy / scandal)
groups.nuance_zh: implicate: 举证牵扯进犯罪或不端丑闻 (suspect / official / scandal) · embroil: 拖入纷乱的战祸或白热化纠纷 (nation / politician / conflict) · entangle: 像绳索般错综复杂地纠缠绊住 (finances / limbs / affairs) · enmesh: 如罗网深陷于体制或网状困境 (bureaucracy / network / system) · mire: 深深陷入泥淖而难以自拔 (debt / controversy / scandal)

groups.name: Irrigate & Cleanse · 冲洗与洁身 (Rinse, Flush, Syringe)
groups.tip: 用水流清洗清洁身体部位

items.def_en: Wash lightly with clean liquid, especially to remove soap, dirt, or debris from skin or mouth
items.ex_en: You must rinse the soap residue off your face with cool, clean water.
items.ex_zh: 你必须用干净的凉水把脸上的肥皂残留物漂洗干净。

items.def_zh: 灌洗，冲洗（尤指阴道等身体腔道）
items.def_en: To wash or flush a body cavity (especially the vagina) with a stream of water or a cleansing solution.
items.ex_en: Doctors generally advise patients not to douche regularly because it disrupts natural flora.
items.ex_zh: 医生通常建议患者不要经常灌洗，因为这会破坏正常的菌群平衡。

items.def_en: Cleanse or empty something by causing a strong surge of water or liquid to flow through it
items.ex_en: Use plenty of water to flush the remaining toxic chemicals down the laboratory drain.
items.ex_zh: 用大量的水将实验室管道内残留的有毒化学物质冲刷干净。
items.ex2_en: Her pale cheeks flushed crimson with sudden embarrassment when everyone looked at her.
items.ex2_zh: 当所有人都望向她时，她苍白的脸颊因突如其来的尴尬而涨得通红。

items.def_zh: 用注射器冲洗（耳道/伤口等）
items.def_en: Cleanse or flush out an orifice (such as an ear) using a specialized syringe
items.ex_en: The specialist will gently syringe your ear canal to remove the impacted wax.
items.ex_zh: 专科医生会用注射器轻柔地冲洗你的耳道，以清除积结的耳垢。

items.def_en: Wash out a body cavity, organ, or wound with a controlled continuous stream of water or saline
items.ex_en: The trauma surgeon used sterile saline to thoroughly irrigate the deep laceration.
items.ex_zh: 创伤外科医生使用无菌生理盐水彻底冲洗了那道较深的撕裂伤口。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to washing, purging, or rinsing bodily cavities, passages, or skin surfaces with targeted streams of water or medicinal solutions to ensure cleanliness or medical hygiene.
groups.summary_zh: 用水流或药液对身体孔道、创口或表面进行定向冲洗洁治。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the cleansing, clearing, or medical washing of a cavity, surface, or bodily passage via a directed stream of liquid, distinguishing it from general bathing or static soaking.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过定向液流对体腔、创口或表面进行冲刷、清洁或医疗冲洗，区别于一般的浸泡或静态沐浴。
groups.nuance_en: rinse: quick removal of soap or residue using clean water (mouth / hair / dishes) · flush: sudden forceful purge of a passage or system (toilet / pipes / wound) · irrigate: continuous therapeutic or agricultural flooding (wound / eye / field) · syringe: instrument-directed jet washing of a delicate cavity (ear / canal) · douche: internal liquid cleansing of a body cavity (vagina)
groups.nuance_zh: rinse: 用清水快速冲掉泡沫或残留物 (mouth / hair / dishes) · flush: 大水或强水流冲击清空管道 (toilet / pipes / wound) · irrigate: 持续性医疗冲洗或灌溉 (wound / eye / field) · syringe: 用注射器/注水管定向冲洗娇嫩孔道 (ear / canal) · douche: 专用液体灌洗体腔 (vagina)

groups.name: Isolate & Sequester · 司法隔离与依法扣押 (Isolate, Quarantine, Impound)
groups.tip: 扣押财产或强行隔绝陪审团

items.def_en: to separate someone or something physically or socially from others
items.ex_en: Health authorities decided to isolate the infected individuals until all lab results returned.
items.ex_zh: 卫生部门决定在所有化验结果出来之前将感染者隔离起来。

items.def_en: to enclose or seal off an area with a barrier or police tape to prevent access
items.ex_en: Police officers moved quickly to cordon off the crime scene from curious onlookers.
items.ex_zh: 警官们迅速拉起警戒线，将案发现场与好奇的围观群众隔离开来。

items.def_en: to isolate a person, animal, or ship to prevent the spread of infectious disease
items.ex_en: Officials were instructed to quarantine the imported livestock to prevent the disease from spreading.
items.ex_zh: 官员们接到指示，对进口牲畜进行检疫隔离，以防疾病蔓延。

items.def_en: to seize and hold legal custody of property, documents, or vehicles by law
items.ex_en: Authorities have the right to impound any vehicle parked unlawfully near the embassy.
items.ex_zh: 当局有权依法扣押任何在大使馆附近非法停放的车辆。

items.def_zh: 使隔绝，使隔离（陪审团等）；扣押，没收（财产）
items.def_en: (formal/law) to isolate a jury from outside influence during a trial; to legally seize property until a debt or dispute is settled
items.ex_en: The judge chose to sequester the jury throughout the duration of the sensational murder trial.
items.ex_zh: 在这起轰动一时的谋杀案审理期间，法官选择让陪审团全程与外界隔离。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to officially separating people or properties from outside contact, whether sequestering a jury, quarantining for public health, or impounding assets.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过法律或官方行政手段将人员隔绝外界或扣押财产。
groups.desc_en: Involves the formal, legally sanctioned, or safety-driven segregation of individuals, assets, or juries to prevent contamination, bias, or escape, differing from voluntary solitude or casual physical separation.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据司法、防疫或安全指令对人员、财产或陪审团实施强制性隔离、扣押或封锁，区别于自发的独处或普通的物理隔开。
groups.nuance_en: isolate: separate to stop transmission or contact (patient / virus / suspect) · cordon off: establish a physical barrier to restrict access (crime scene / area / street) · quarantine: compulsory detention due to suspected infectious disease (traveler / ship / animal) · impound: legal seizure and retention of physical property (vehicle / vessel / documents) · sequester: judicial isolation of persons or confiscation of assets (jury / property / funds)
groups.nuance_zh: isolate: 防疫或防干扰的物理/社会隔离 (patient / virus / suspect) · cordon off: 用警戒线封锁特定区域 (crime scene / area / street) · quarantine: 涉疫强制检疫隔离 (traveler / ship / animal) · impound: 依法扣押车辆或财物 (vehicle / vessel / documents) · sequester: 司法隔离陪审团或依法冻结查封财产 (jury / property / funds)

groups.name: Issue, Republish & Put Out · 重印与发行 (Reissue, Put out, Print)
groups.tip: 排版印刷与公开发行

items.def_en: To prepare and officially issue a book, journal, or piece of music for general sale
items.ex_en: The university press will publish his comprehensive historical monograph early next spring.
items.ex_zh: 大学出版社将于明年早春正式出版他这部详尽的史学专著。

items.def_en: To produce and make available a publication, statement, or creative release to the public
items.ex_en: The research institute plans to put out a detailed statistical report next Monday.
items.ex_zh: 该研究所计划于下周一公开发布一份详尽的统计报告。

items.def_en: To launch and publish a new product, literary title, or commercial run
items.ex_en: The company intends to bring out a revolutionary new smartphone before the holidays.
items.ex_zh: 该公司打算在假期前推出一款具有革命性的新款智能手机。

items.def_en: To print a new supply of copies of a book, article, or photograph without making major changes.
items.ex_en: The publisher had to reprint ten thousand additional copies due to unexpected customer demand.
items.ex_zh: 由于顾客需求出人意料地旺盛，出版商不得不加印一万册。

items.def_en: To print and distribute a new edition or version of a book, recording, or document
items.ex_en: The record label decided to reissue the legendary band's classic debut album on vinyl.
items.ex_zh: 唱片公司决定以黑胶唱片形式重新发行这支传奇乐队经典的处女作专辑。

groups.summary_en: Focuses on the commercial publishing workflow of manufacturing new runs, alternate editions, or fresh printings of existing literary or visual works. Collocates include edition, hardback, run, and serial.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重书籍、刊物等作品的重新发行、加印或换版出版。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on the public dissemination, manufacturing, or subsequent re-release of printed or media material to a market, unlike private authorial composition or internal distribution.
groups.desc_zh: 强调出版物或音像作品面向公众市场的正式印发、推出或改版重印，区别于案头创作或内部传阅。
groups.nuance_en: publish: formal public commercial release of a text or work (book / findings / journal) · put out: produce and issue to the public (statement / album / newsletter) · bring out: launch a new edition or product commercially (novel / collection / record) · reprint: print additional copies without major text changes (bestseller / article) · reissue: release an updated, revised, or renewed edition after lapse (album / classic / catalog)
groups.nuance_zh: publish: 正式出版或向公众公开发布 (book / findings / journal) · put out: 制作并对外发布 (statement / album / newsletter) · bring out: 商业性推出新书或新专辑 (novel / collection / record) · reprint: 原版加印或再版印刷 (bestseller / article) · reissue: 重新改版发行或绝版重发 (album / classic / catalog)

groups.name: Itch & Tingle · 感官麻痒与刺痛 (Itch, Tingle, Prickle)
groups.tip: 表皮神经刺痛与微痒

items.def_zh: 起鸡皮疙瘩；感觉有虫爬般发痒
items.def_en: To experience an eerie, creep-like tingling sensation on your skin caused by disgust or chills
items.ex_en: Just watching those repulsive insects on the wall made my skin crawl with disgust.
items.ex_zh: 仅仅看着墙上那些恶心的昆虫，就让我厌恶得浑身起鸡皮疙瘩。

items.def_en: 1. To have an uncomfortable feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch. 2. (+ for/to do) (informal) To feel a strong, impatient desire to do something.
items.ex_en: The wool sweater caused his neck to itch intensely throughout the entire morning.
items.ex_zh: 整整一个上午，那件羊毛衫都扎得他的脖子奇痒难耐。

items.def_en: To experience a slight stinging, prickling, or throbbing sensation on the skin or body part
items.ex_en: A curious chill made the back of her delicate neck tingle with anticipation.
items.ex_zh: 一股奇异的凉意使她娇嫩的后颈泛起一阵充满期待的刺麻感。

items.def_en: To feel as though tiny sharp needles or pins are stinging the skin
items.ex_en: Cold fear began to prickle along his arms as heavy footsteps approached the door.
items.ex_zh: 随着沉重的脚步声逼近门口，一股冷冽的恐惧感如针刺般传遍他的双臂。
items.ex2_en: Dry winter wool garments prickled his sensitive skin throughout the entire long flight.
items.ex2_zh: 在整场漫长的飞行中，干燥的冬装羊毛衣料一直扎得他敏感的皮肤隐隐作痛。

items.def_zh: 刺痛；感到阵阵火辣灼痛
items.def_en: To produce a sharp, stinging superficial pain, as from a scrape, cut, or harsh liquid
items.ex_en: The antiseptic applied to his fresh wound caused his tender skin to smart fiercely.
items.ex_zh: 涂在新鲜伤口上的消毒剂让娇嫩的皮肤感到一阵阵剧烈的火辣刺痛。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on mild to moderate superficial somatosensory sensations on the skin, such as prickling, tingling, or itching sensations that provoke an impulse to scratch.
groups.summary_zh: 指皮肤表层产生的轻微刺痒、蚁走感、发麻或引起搔抓冲动的躯体知觉。
groups.desc_en: Depicts localized cutaneous or somatic paresthesias characterized by prickling, irritation, or sharp minor discomfort, unlike deep visceral aches or muscular soreness.
groups.desc_zh: 描述皮肤表层或感官神经引起的刺痒、麻木或微小锐痛，区别于深层内脏痛或肌肉酸痛。
groups.nuance_en: itch: irritating sensation evoking a desire to scratch (skin / scalp / bite) · tingle: pleasant or unpleasant mild prickling vibratory sensation (spine / fingers / anticipation) · prickle: sharp, tiny stinging sensation like miniature needles (skin / neck / eyes) · crawl: creeping sensation as if insects were moving on skin (flesh / skin) · smart: stinging, sharp superficial burning pain (eyes / cut / slap)
groups.nuance_zh: itch: 引发抓挠欲望的皮肤发痒 (skin / scalp / bite) · tingle: 轻微麻刺或颤栗感 (spine / fingers / anticipation) · prickle: 如针扎般的微小扎刺感 (skin / neck / eyes) · crawl: 如蚁爬行的发毛起鸡皮感 (flesh / skin) · smart: 伤口受刺激引起的灼痛刺痛 (eyes / cut / slap)

groups.name: Jettison & Cast off · 抛弃与断然丢弃 (Jettison, Scrap, Ditch)
groups.tip: 抛下重物或弃置无用之物

items.def_en: Get rid of someone or something that you no longer want, need, or accept
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: Get rid of unwanted waste or possessions carelessly, or abruptly end a relationship with someone
items.ex_en: Irresponsible contractors continued to dump industrial waste secretly into the pristine mountain stream.
items.ex_zh: 不负责任的承包商继续偷偷将工业废料随意倾倒进清澈的山间溪流中。

items.def_zh: 报废；取消；把……当废物丢弃
items.def_en: Discard or abandon an idea, plan, or piece of machinery as useless or obsolete
items.ex_en: The transport authority decided to scrap the outdated trains after years of frequent breakdowns.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了数年频繁的故障后，交通管理局决定将那些过时的列车报废。

items.def_en: (informal) Get rid of, abandon, or stop using someone or something that is no longer desired
items.ex_en: She wisely decided to ditch her old habits and embrace a healthier lifestyle instead.
items.ex_zh: 她明智地决定摒弃旧习惯，转而拥抱一种更加健康的生活方式。

items.def_zh: 抛弃，丢弃（重物以减负）；放弃（无用计划等）
items.def_en: 1. To throw goods, cargo, or fuel overboard from a ship or aircraft to make it lighter in an emergency. 2. To get rid of an unwanted idea, plan, or person.
items.ex_en: The cargo pilot had to jettison excess fuel over the ocean during an emergency.
items.ex_zh: 在遭遇紧急情况时，货机飞行员不得不将多余的燃油倾倒在海洋上空以减负。

groups.summary_en: Pertains to abruptly shedding, discarding, or dropping objects, cargo, plans, or unwanted ties to lighten a load, eliminate burdens, or clear space rapidly.
groups.summary_zh: 强调为减负、断舍离或应对危机而断然抛弃物品或计划。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the decisive, often abrupt or unceremonious abandonment of dead weight, obsolete assets, or relationships to unburden oneself, contrasted with orderly disposal or careful relinquishment.
groups.desc_zh: 强调为减负、止损或脱身而断然、粗暴地抛弃包袱、报废资产或甩掉关系，区别于有序处理或审慎放弃。
groups.nuance_en: jettison: discard cargo or burdens decisively to survive or streamline (cargo / fuel / plans) · cast off: untie or discard what binds or clothes (ropes / inhibitions / coats) · dump: callously or abruptly discard in bulk (toxic waste / partner / shares) · scrap: discard as useless or obsolete material (project / old ships / policy) · ditch: informally abandon or escape from an unwanted burden or companion (car / boyfriend / school)
groups.nuance_zh: jettison: 紧急或断然抛弃以减轻负担 (cargo / fuel / plans) · cast off: 解开缆绳或摆脱旧有束缚 (ropes / inhibitions / coats) · dump: 粗暴倾倒废弃物或甩掉伴侣/抛售股票 (toxic waste / partner / shares) · scrap: 报废拆解或废弃无用计划 (project / old ships / policy) · ditch: 俚语中果断甩掉累赘、翘课或弃车 (car / boyfriend / school)

groups.name: Jinx & Bad-mouth · 致厄与招晦气 (Jinx, Hoodoo, Put the hex on, Blight)
groups.tip: 施加晦气让其遭殃

items.def_en: To bring persistent bad luck, misfortune, or jinxes to a sports team, individual, or project
items.ex_en: Fans wondered if an ancient curse continued to hoodoo their luckless baseball team.
items.ex_zh: 球迷们纳闷是否是一记古老的诅咒在持续给这支倒霉的棒球队带来厄运。

items.def_en: To put a decisive stop to an activity or squelch someone's plans and good fortune entirely
items.ex_en: Torrential rain quickly put the kibosh on our grand outdoor wedding plans yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 昨天倾盆而下的大雨迅速让我们盛大的户外婚礼计划彻底告吹。

items.def_en: To ruin, spoil, or severely damage the prospects, happiness, or health of something
items.ex_en: A sudden scandal threatened to permanently blight his promising future in public service.
items.ex_zh: 一场突如其来的丑闻极有可能永远摧残他在公职领域本充满希望的前途。

items.def_en: To bring bad luck or misfortune to someone or something.
items.ex_en: Don't celebrate our victory yet, or you might jinx the entire tournament.
items.ex_zh: 先别急着庆祝胜利，否则你可能会给整场锦标赛招来霉运。

items.def_en: To deliberately or fatefully wreck a plan, opportunity, or chance of success
items.ex_en: A sudden torrential downpour completely scuppered our weekend plans for a beach barbecue.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的倾盆大雨彻底让我们周末的海滩烧烤计划泡了汤。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to bringing bad luck, superstitious misfortune, or disastrous outcomes upon an endeavor or person, often by speaking prematurely or acting carelessly.
groups.summary_zh: 以乌鸦嘴、触霉头或迷信力量带来晦气，使计划或事物败坏遭殃。
groups.desc_en: Refers to the supernatural or perceived casting of bad luck upon an endeavor, or abruptly spoiling someone’s chances, contrasting with physical sabotage or rational criticism.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过招致厄运、带来晦气或莫名阻挠使事物功败垂成，区别于物理破坏或合理的理性批评。
groups.nuance_en: jinx: bring bad luck or superstition-fueled failure upon (team / chances / project) · hoodoo: bring persistent uncanny misfortune or voodoo-like bad luck to (player / expedition) · put the kibosh on: decisively bring a sudden halt or ruin to (plans / deal / career) · blight: spoil, impair, or wither hopes or development deeply (prospects / crops / reputation) · scupper: deliberately or fatefully wreck an ambition or enterprise (deal / chances / bid)
groups.nuance_zh: jinx: 乌鸦嘴或带来霉运 (team / chances / project) · hoodoo: 招致长期的邪门厄运 (player / expedition) · put the kibosh on: 俚语彻底搞砸或紧急叫停 (plans / deal / career) · blight: 摧残或留下挥之不去的阴影 (prospects / crops / reputation) · scupper: 毁掉或断送大好机会 (deal / chances / bid)

groups.name: Joke & Tease · 开玩笑与调侃 (Joke, Jest, Kid)
groups.tip: 以轻松诙谐之语活跃气氛

items.def_en: To deceive playfully as a joke; tease or banter
items.ex_en: Don't get upset about that silly remark, because I was only kidding around.
items.ex_zh: 别为那句傻话生气，我刚才只是在闹着玩开玩笑呢。

items.def_en: To tell jokes or say something humorous rather than serious.
items.ex_en: The colleagues liked to joke about the terrible coffee served in the breakroom.
items.ex_zh: 同事们喜欢拿休息室里难喝的咖啡互相说笑逗乐。

items.def_en: To exchange lighthearted, playful, and teasing remarks
items.ex_en: The two old friends paused to banter good-naturedly before starting the morning meeting.
items.ex_zh: 这两位老朋友在晨会开始前停下来，相互风趣地打趣逗乐。

items.def_en: To make a witty or sarcastic remark quickly
items.ex_en: The minister paused to quip about the unreliability of modern weather forecasting technology.
items.ex_zh: 部长停顿了一下，就现代天气预报技术的不可靠性说了句俏皮话。

items.def_en: To speak in a playful, humorous, or teasing way
items.ex_en: He dared not jest in the presence of the somber, unyielding monarch.
items.ex_zh: 面对神情阴郁且固执专断的君王，他丝毫不敢戏谑说笑。

groups.summary_en: Verbs here signify speaking in a playful, lighthearted, or teasing manner rather than in earnest, often to provoke laughter or defuse tension.
groups.summary_zh: 以戏谑、非严肃的方式言语，说笑或打趣调侃。
groups.desc_en: Centers on lighthearted, playful, and non-serious verbal engagement meant to amuse rather than inform or deceive, distinct from earnest conversation or malicious mockery.
groups.desc_zh: 聚焦于打趣、说笑等非严肃性口头互动，旨在逗乐调侃而非传递事实或恶意讽刺，区别于正经交谈或恶语相向。
groups.nuance_en: joke: speak or act non-seriously to provoke laughter (with friends / about age) · kid: playfully tease or pretend falsehood in jest (younger brother / about money) · jest: archaic or formal wit and light mockery (with courtiers / in earnest) · quip: make a witty, pithy, spontaneous retort (to reporters / about politics) · banter: engage in friendly, good-humored reciprocal repartee (with colleagues / playfully)
groups.nuance_zh: joke: 讲笑话或开玩笑以逗乐 (with friends / about age) · kid: 善意开玩笑或半真半假逗弄 (younger brother / about money) · jest: 文雅或古风式的打趣说笑 (with courtiers / in earnest) · quip: 针对特定语境敏捷俏皮地插话回怼 (to reporters / about politics) · banter: 双方互开玩笑、轻松逗趣 (with colleagues / playfully)

groups.name: Judge & Adjudicate · 裁决与依法认定 (Adjudge, Rule, Deem)
groups.tip: 基于规则与法律做出权威判定

items.def_en: To make an authoritative legal decision or declaration on a point of law
items.ex_en: The judge will rule on the admissibility of the contested evidence tomorrow morning.
items.ex_zh: 法官将于明天上午就争议证据是否具有可采性作出裁决。

items.def_en: To consider, judge, or declare in an official or legal evaluation
items.ex_en: The regulatory committee will deem the merger unlawful under existing antitrust statutes.
items.ex_zh: 监管委员会将根据现行反垄断法规认定该合并案违法。

items.def_en: To state an official decision, opinion, or judgment formally or publicly
items.ex_en: The appellate court will pronounce judgment on the high-profile constitutional dispute tomorrow.
items.ex_zh: 上诉法院将于明日就这起备受瞩目的宪法争议正式宣布裁决。

items.def_en: To act as a judge or give an official judgment in a formal dispute
items.ex_en: An independent tribunal was appointed to adjudicate the protracted cross-border contract dispute.
items.ex_zh: 已任命一个独立仲裁庭来裁决这起旷日持久的跨境合同纠纷。

items.def_en: (formal / law) to declare, decide, or judge officially that someone or something is a certain way
items.ex_en: The tribunal will adjudge the company liable for the extensive coastal pollution damage.
items.ex_zh: 法庭将裁决该公司对大面积海岸污染损害承担法律责任。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe authoritative cognitive evaluations made by courts, arbitrators, or officials to determine legal status or culpability. They denote issuing a binding formal finding rather than pronouncing a punitive sentence.
groups.summary_zh: 指法官、仲裁者等权威依据事实和法律对性质或地位作出正式裁断。
groups.desc_en: Signifies authoritative, formal, or official legal evaluation and binding determination of a status or dispute, unlike private subjective opinion or casual assessment.
groups.desc_zh: 指具有法定权威或仲裁权的主体对争议、性质或状态做出正式且具约束力的裁定，区别于私下的主观意见或随意评价。
groups.nuance_en: rule: issue an authoritative judicial or official decree (on evidence / in favor of / against) · deem: formal administrative or cognitive determination of status (unfit / necessary / complete) · adjudicate: sit as a formal tribunal to resolve a dispute (claim / dispute / bankruptcy) · adjudge: declare judicially after hearing evidence (guilty / bankrupt / insane) · pronounce: declare officially or ex cathedra (judgment / sentence / dead)
groups.nuance_zh: rule: 法官或仲裁方做出正式裁定 (on evidence / in favor of / against) · deem: 法律或官方层面正式认定/视作 (unfit / necessary / complete) · adjudicate: 审判并裁决复杂争议 (claim / dispute / bankruptcy) · adjudge: 经司法程序判决某人处于某种状态 (guilty / bankrupt / insane) · pronounce: 郑重宣告或宣判结论 (judgment / sentence / dead)

groups.name: Judge & Convict · 审判与定罪 (Find guilty, Sentence, Adjudicate)
groups.tip: 法庭审理并依法判定有罪

items.def_en: To state officially in court that someone will receive a particular punishment
items.ex_en: The presiding magistrate decided to sentence the convicted embezzler to seven years imprisonment.
items.ex_zh: 主审法官决定判处该被定罪的贪污犯七年有期徒刑。

items.def_zh: 判决……有罪，定罪；证明……有错
items.def_en: To officially declare or find someone guilty of a criminal offense in a court of law.
items.ex_en: The jury took only two hours to convict the defendant of fraud.
items.ex_zh: 陪审团仅用了两个小时就判定被告犯有诈骗罪。

items.def_en: To officially pronounce a harsh punishment or death penalty upon a convicted criminal
items.ex_en: The military tribunal chose to condemn the notorious traitor to death by firing squad.
items.ex_zh: 军事法庭最终决定判处臭名昭著的叛国者枪决死刑。

items.def_en: To reach a judicial verdict establishing that a defendant committed an offense
items.ex_en: The unanimous jury voted to find the defendant guilty of first-degree felony charges.
items.ex_zh: 全体陪审员一致表决裁定被告所涉一级重罪指控成立。

items.def_en: To pronounce judicially or rule formally that someone is guilty or liable
items.ex_en: The high court will adjudge the rogue financial firm guilty of corporate fraud.
items.ex_zh: 高等法院将依法裁定这家失范的金融公司犯有企业欺诈罪。

groups.summary_en: This legal frame focuses on formal judicial outcomes where an accused person is officially adjudicated, found guilty of a crime, and assigned legal penalty.
groups.summary_zh: 法庭经审判正式判定当事人有罪并施加刑罚。
groups.desc_en: Covers the formal judicial conclusion of criminal culpability and subsequent imposition of penal sanctions, setting it apart from mere accusation, investigation, or civil liability.
groups.desc_zh: 指刑事审判中确定被告有罪并依法量刑惩处，区别于前端的指控调查或民事侵权裁量。
groups.nuance_en: convict: formally declare guilty of a criminal offense by verdict (felon / fraudster / traitor) · sentence: impose a specified penal sanction upon a convict (to prison / to death / to community service) · condemn: express total judicial doom or extreme moral censorship (to death / criminal / actions) · find guilty: formal jury or judicial verdict of culpability (defendant / on all counts) · adjudge: legally determine liability or criminal status (in contempt / liable)
groups.nuance_zh: convict: 陪审团或法庭正式定罪 (felon / fraudster / traitor) · sentence: 依法判处特定刑罚 (to prison / to death / to community service) · condemn: 宣告判处极刑或强烈道德谴责 (to death / criminal / actions) · find guilty: 庭审认定有罪结论 (defendant / on all counts) · adjudge: 司法裁定具有违法状态或刑事责任 (in contempt / liable)

groups.name: Jurisdictional Division & Districting · 划分管区与选区 (District, Redistrict, Gerrymander)
groups.tip: 按地域划分行政片区

items.def_en: 1. To divide an area or city into administrative, legislative, or school districts.
items.ex_en: City planners decided to district the northern sector into exclusive residential zones.
items.ex_zh: 城市规划人员决定将北部区域划分为独立的专门居住区。

items.def_en: To divide an urban municipal territory into distinct electoral or administrative wards
items.ex_en: The civic charter required the elders to ward the growing metropolis equitably.
items.ex_zh: 市政特许状要求长者们将这座不断扩张的大都市合理划分为各个行政区。

items.def_en: To redraw the political, voting, or school boundary lines of an administrative region
items.ex_en: State lawmakers gathered to redistrict the metropolitan voting boundaries before the general election.
items.ex_zh: 州立法人员齐聚一堂，准备在大选前重新划分大都会选区的边界。

items.def_en: To designate or divide an urban area into police or voting precincts
items.ex_en: The commissioner moved to precinct the newly annexed municipality into four patrol zones.
items.ex_zh: 局长着手将新并入的自治市划分为四个巡逻警区。

items.def_zh: 不正当划分（选区以谋求私利）
items.def_en: To redraw electoral district boundaries unfairly to give one political party an electoral advantage
items.ex_en: The incumbent party attempted to gerrymander suburban voting districts to secure parliamentary seats.
items.ex_zh: 执政党企图通过不正当划分郊区选区来确保议会席位。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote the legal and institutional partition of territorial entities into official districts for voting, schooling, policing, or civic governance, emphasizing borders defined by state authority.
groups.summary_zh: 指官方或公权力依行政、司法、学区或选举需要划分管理辖区。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the geometric and political delineation of geographic territory into administrative or voting units, contrasting with organic settlement boundaries or military conquest.
groups.desc_zh: 指为行政管理或选举目的在地理区域上划分政治边界与选区，区别于自然聚落边界或军事占领分界。
groups.nuance_en: district: divide a region into administrative sectors (city / territory / zone) · redistrict: redraw electoral or administrative boundaries after census (state / boundaries / county) · gerrymander: manipulate boundary lines unfairly for partisan electoral gain (electoral map / voting district / congressional seats) · ward: divide into local municipal voting divisions (borough / city / town) · precinct: partition an urban area for policing or local ballot counting (neighborhood / city)
groups.nuance_zh: district: 划分一般行政或司法管区 (city / territory / zone) · redistrict: 依人口普查重新重组选区边界 (state / boundaries / county) · gerrymander: 为党派私利恶意操弄重划选区 (electoral map / voting district / congressional seats) · ward: 划分为市级选举区或市政坊 (borough / city / town) · precinct: 划定警区或基层投票选区 (neighborhood / city)

groups.name: Kibitz & Meddle · 插嘴与瞎出主意 (Butt in, Chime in, Meddle)
groups.tip: 从旁多嘴出谋或横加干预

items.def_en: To join into a conversation or debate, often suddenly with an agreement or opinion
items.ex_en: Feel free to chime in whenever you have a relevant suggestion to offer.
items.ex_zh: 无论何时，只要你有切题的建议，欢迎随时插话搭腔。

items.def_en: To get involved in other people's affairs where one is not wanted or needed
items.ex_en: She warned her intrusive relatives not to interfere in her private financial decisions.
items.ex_zh: 她警告那些爱管闲事的亲戚不要干涉她的私人财务决定。

items.def_en: To offer unwanted advice or critique to the person who is actually in charge
items.ex_en: Stop trying to backseat-drive the marketing campaign when Sarah is clearly running it.
items.ex_zh: 既然营销活动显然由萨拉负责，你就别再指手画脚多管闲事了。

items.def_zh: 乱插嘴，瞎提建议；指点牌局
items.def_en: To look on and offer unwanted advice or commentary, especially during a game of cards.
items.ex_en: My uncle loves to kibitz while everyone else concentrates on playing poker.
items.ex_zh: 在别人全神贯注打扑克时，我叔叔总喜欢在旁边瞎支招插嘴。

items.def_en: To rudely interrupt a conversation or meddle in someone else's affairs
items.ex_en: It was rude of him to butt in while the directors were speaking.
items.ex_zh: 在董事们谈话时冒失地横加插嘴，他这样很不礼貌。

groups.summary_en: Depicts bystanders intruding into conversations, games, or affairs with unsolicited commentary, backseat advice, or meddlesome critiques.
groups.summary_zh: 旁观者胡乱插话、评头论足或多管闲事。
groups.desc_en: Pertains to uninvited, gratuitous verbal intervention or unwanted meddling in others' activities or conversations, distinguishing it from solicited guidance or legitimate supervision.
groups.desc_zh: 指未经邀请、令人厌烦地插嘴、瞎出主意或干预他人事务，区别于受邀指导或合法监督。
groups.nuance_en: kibitz: offer unsolicited, annoying running commentary or advice as an onlooker (at cards / on politics) · butt in: interrupt a private conversation or activity rudely (on a discussion / abruptly) · chime in: join a conversation abruptly or supportively (with agreement / unexpectedly) · backseat-drive: dictate actions from a position without actual responsibility (from the passenger seat / in management) · interfere: intrude unhelpfully into affairs where one has no role (with legal process / in private matters)
groups.nuance_zh: kibitz: 旁观者讨厌地多嘴支招 (at cards / on politics) · butt in: 粗鲁生硬地横插一杠/打断谈话 (on a discussion / abruptly) · chime in: 适时附和插话或搭腔 (with agreement / unexpectedly) · backseat-drive: 事后诸葛或越俎代庖指手画脚 (from the passenger seat / in management) · interfere: 越界干涉或妨碍他人事务 (with legal process / in private matters)

groups.name: Kick & Punt · 踢蹬与脚击 (Punt, Boot, Hack)
groups.tip: 凌空抽射或脚蹬反击

items.def_en: To kick roughly or indiscriminately at an opponent's shins or feet in sports
items.ex_en: The aggressive defender began to hack at the striker's shins without hesitation.
items.ex_zh: 那名动作凶狠的防守球员毫不犹豫地开始乱踢前锋的小腿胫骨。

items.def_en: To drop a ball from the hands and kick it before it touches the ground
items.ex_en: The goalkeeper stepped up under pressure to punt the football past midfield.
items.ex_zh: 守门员顶住压力上前，凌空大脚将足球踢过了中场。

items.def_zh: 凌空踢球，反弹踢；做凌空飞踢
items.def_en: 1. (sports) To kick a ball just as it rebounds from the ground after being dropped from the hands. 2. (combat sports) To perform a dropkick on an opponent.
items.ex_en: The rugby fly-half chose to dropkick the ball cleanly through the uprights.
items.ex_zh: 橄榄球接锋选择反弹踢球，皮球利落地穿过了球门立柱。

items.def_en: To kick something or someone hard and forcefully, often sending it a long distance
items.ex_en: He managed to boot the stray football completely over the neighbors' wooden fence.
items.ex_zh: 他飞起一脚，把飞过来的足球狠狠踢过了邻居家的木栅栏。

items.def_en: To kick a ball high and far with brute force, especially in soccer
items.ex_en: Under intense defensive pressure, the defender chose to hoof the clearance upfield.
items.ex_zh: 在严密防守的重压下，后卫只得选择大脚猛抽把球解围到前场。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses forcefully striking or propelling an object or opponent using the foot or boot. It ranges from technical athletic maneuvers like dropkicking and punting to raw, forceful kicks directed at physical targets.
groups.summary_zh: 指用脚、靴子对球或目标物施加的各种击打与踢射动作。
groups.desc_en: Captures violent, targeted, or technical propulsion using the foot or boot, distinct from stomping directly downward or swinging a handheld implement.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用脚部或鞋靴进行的针对性踢打、解围或特定技术踢球，区别于向下的踩踏或器械挥击。
groups.nuance_en: punt: kick a ball dropped from hands before it touches the ground (football / into touch / away) · boot: kick forcefully and crudely (ball into the stands / door / intruder) · hack: kick haphazardly or violently at shins or ball (opponent's shins / at the turf) · dropkick: kick a ball just as it rebounds off the ground (field goal / rugby ball) · hoof: informally kick a ball high, long, and without finesse (ball clear / upfield)
groups.nuance_zh: punt: 橄榄球等凌空踢凌空抽射或脚踢解围 (football / into touch / away) · boot: 大力猛踢或用力踹 (ball into the stands / door / intruder) · hack: 粗暴乱踢或猛踢小腿 (opponent's shins / at the turf) · dropkick: 半凌空踢，球刚触地反弹时踢出 (field goal / rugby ball) · hoof: 俚语中无脑大脚开球往前踢 (ball clear / upfield)

groups.name: Kid & Rib · 戏弄与打趣 (Josh, Rib, Wind up)
groups.tip: 轻松开玩笑或善意逗弄戏谑

items.def_en: (UK informal) To tease someone by pretending something false is true
items.ex_en: Don't believe his outrageous ghost story, because he is only having you on.
items.ex_zh: 别信他那个离谱的鬼故事，他只是在拿假话逗你玩呢。

items.def_en: (informal) To say something not meant seriously, or tell playful lies to someone for amusement.
items.ex_en: I was only trying to kid you when I announced my early retirement.
items.ex_zh: 我宣布自己要提前退休，其实只是想逗你开个玩笑而已。

items.def_en: (informal) To tease or joke with someone playfully and amiably
items.ex_en: The friendly teammates frequently josh one another about their comical practice blunders.
items.ex_zh: 关系融洽的队员们经常就训练中闹出的滑稽小失误相互打趣戏弄。

items.def_en: (informal) To tease someone in an affectionate and good-natured way
items.ex_en: The older boys liked to gently rib their cousin about his new haircut.
items.ex_zh: 大男孩们喜欢善意地拿表弟的新发型跟他逗乐打趣。

items.def_en: (UK informal) To say things intentionally to mislead or tease someone as a joke
items.ex_en: Stop trying to wind up your little sister with those ridiculous alien stories.
items.ex_zh: 别再编那些荒诞的外星人故事故意诓骗逗弄你妹妹了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to verbally teasing or feeding someone playful falsehoods for amusement without malicious intent, often testing their gullibility.
groups.summary_zh: 指善意逗弄、开玩笑或拿人寻开心的动词群。
groups.desc_en: Refers to affectionate or provocative verbal teasing, good-natured deception, or testing someone's credulity, contrasting with harsh bullying or sincere deceit.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过善意的戏弄、善意欺骗或逗哏来逗弄对方，区别于恶意的欺凌或真正的诈骗。
groups.nuance_en: kid: tease lightly or state untruth playfully (little brother / about age) · rib: poke good-natured fun at someone persistently (teammate / about haircut) · josh: tease in a warm, folksy, gentle manner (friend / affably) · wind up: deliberately tease someone into becoming annoyed or agitated (brother / opponent / teacher) · have on: British informal tricking of someone into believing nonsense (colleague / gullible friend)
groups.nuance_zh: kid: 随口开玩笑或逗弄 (little brother / about age) · rib: 友好取笑或拿某事开涮 (teammate / about haircut) · josh: 亲昵随和地打趣逗乐 (friend / affably) · wind up: 英式逗弄激怒使人抓狂 (brother / opponent / teacher) · have on: 逗人玩、哄骗某人相信蠢话 (colleague / gullible friend)

groups.name: Kindle & Spark · 点燃与引燃 (Kindle, Ignite, Spark)
groups.tip: 引燃火种或点燃热情

items.def_en: To cause something to catch fire and begin to burn actively
items.ex_en: A single wayward spark was sufficient to set alight the ancient dry timber.
items.ex_zh: 仅仅一颗乱窜的火星，便足以点燃那堆干枯已久的古木。

items.def_en: To produce small electrical flashes, or cause a sudden sequence of events or feelings
items.ex_en: The sudden policy change threatens to spark widespread protests across the capital.
items.ex_zh: 这项突然出台的政策变动恐将在整个首都引发大范围的抗议浪潮。

items.def_en: 1. To start a fire burning, or to arouse strong feelings, interest, or hope in someone.
items.ex_en: Her impassioned speech managed to kindle fresh hope within the weary villagers.
items.ex_zh: 她那段充满激情的演讲成功在疲惫不堪的村民心中重新燃起了希望。
items.ex2_en: Dry pine twigs kindle instantly whenever a tiny spark lands upon their resinous needles.
items.ex2_zh: 每当微小的火星落入多脂的松针上时，干燥的松树细枝便会瞬间点着。

items.def_en: To catch fire or make something start burning; to trigger a strong reaction
items.ex_en: Intense friction between the moving metal parts could easily ignite the spilled fuel.
items.ex_zh: 运转中的金属部件间剧烈的摩擦极易引燃泄漏的燃油。
items.ex2_en: The accumulated flammable gas ignited abruptly when an electrical spark jumped between terminals.
items.ex2_zh: 当电火花在接线端之间跳跃时，积聚的易燃气体突然起火爆炸。

items.def_en: To ignite an explosive fuse, or precipitate a violent outburst or crisis
items.ex_en: The sudden announcement of price hikes touched off violent protests across the capital.
items.ex_zh: 突然宣布的涨价消息在首都全城引发了暴力抗议。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures the initial inception of ignition—starting a fire from a small spark, tinder, or match—as well as the figurative awakening of interest, hope, or romance.
groups.summary_zh: 引燃初始火花或微火，亦指激起、点燃某种强烈情感或灵感。
groups.desc_en: Describes the catalytic initiation of combustion, an emotional surge, or sudden conflict, moving from a dormant state to an active fire, unlike sustained fuel burning.
groups.desc_zh: 强调引燃火苗或突然诱发冲突、情感的初始触发机制，区别于火焰的持续燃烧过程。
groups.nuance_en: ignite: trigger combustion chemically or initiate explosive unrest (fuel / spark plug / riots) · kindle: nurture a small flame or gently arouse an emotion (fire / romance / interest) · spark: precipitate sudden action, conflict, or debate through a catalyst (protest / controversy / outrage) · touch off: trigger a massive, rapid, volatile explosion or chain reaction (crisis / explosion / rebellion) · set alight: physically apply open flame to incinerate (bonfire / candles / car)
groups.nuance_zh: ignite: 物理点燃或引爆激烈动荡 (fuel / spark plug / riots) · kindle: 生火添柴或慢慢唤起内心激情 (fire / romance / interest) · spark: 如火星般触发突发事件或辩论 (protest / controversy / outrage) · touch off: 点燃引信引爆大规模冲突危机 (crisis / explosion / rebellion) · set alight: 直接纵火或用明火点着 (bonfire / candles / car)

groups.name: Kiss & Caress · 亲吻与爱抚 (Make out, Canoodle, Neck)
groups.tip: 热烈亲吻拥吻肢体接触

items.def_en: (informal) To kiss, cuddle, and caress amorous partner intimately in a fond way
items.ex_en: The enamored young couple sat on the park bench to canoodle until twilight.
items.ex_zh: 那对热恋中的小情侣坐在公园长椅上依偎亲热，直到暮色降临。

items.def_en: (informal) To kiss someone affectionately or engage in slow, romantic kissing
items.ex_en: The newlyweds leaned across the café table to smooch tenderly before their flight.
items.ex_zh: 新婚夫妇隔着咖啡馆的餐桌探过身去，在登机前深情地亲吻依偎。

items.def_en: (informal) To engage in mutual kissing and sexual touching passionately
items.ex_en: They slipped into the empty cinema lounge to make out in the dark.
items.ex_zh: 他们悄悄溜进空荡荡的影院休息室，躲在暗处亲吻抚摸起来。

items.def_en: (informal) To kiss and fondle passionately, especially on the neck and mouth
items.ex_en: The infatuated teenagers hid behind the bleachers to neck during the halftime break.
items.ex_zh: 那对陷入热恋的青少年趁着半场休息，躲在看台后搂抱亲吻。

items.def_en: (British informal) To kiss and caress someone passionately.
items.ex_en: They managed to snog passionately beneath the flickering streetlight before heading home.
items.ex_zh: 在各自回家前，他们在闪烁的路灯下紧紧拥吻了一番。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this intimate physical frame describe passionate or affectionate kissing, fondling, and amorous embraces. They encompass romantic caressing as well as colloquial and informal idioms for making out.
groups.summary_zh: 表达情侣间的深情亲吻、拥抱爱抚或激吻亲热。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses informal, colloquial, or passionate expressions of prolonged romantic kissing and intimate tactile affection, contrasting with formal platonic salutations.
groups.desc_zh: 涵盖通俗语境下持续的热吻、爱抚与亲昵缠绵，区别于礼节性的吻手礼或纯洁贴面礼。
groups.nuance_en: make out: engage in prolonged passionate kissing and fondling (at the back of the cinema / intensely) · snog: British informal for ardent, prolonged kissing (at the party / passionately) · neck: American retro slang for deep passionate kissing above the collar (in the car / lovers) · smooch: affectionate, intimate, slow-tempo kissing (on the dancefloor / sweetly) · canoodle: fondle and cuddle amorously in a semi-public context (in the park / secretly)
groups.nuance_zh: make out: 激烈的亲热或深情热吻 (at the back of the cinema / intensely) · snog: 英式口语中的亲嘴与狂吻 (at the party / passionately) · neck: 美式俚语指搂脖颈热吻 (in the car / lovers) · smooch: 甜蜜慢节奏的温情拥吻 (on the dancefloor / sweetly) · canoodle: 依偎爱抚缠绵 (in the park / secretly)

groups.name: Kit & Outfit · 装备与整套装配 (Kit, Outfit, Rig, Equip)
groups.tip: 配齐所需器材与物资

items.def_en: (often kit out/up) to supply or equip someone or something with a complete set of clothes, tools, or gear
items.ex_en: The coach arrived early to kit the rookie players with fresh training gear.
items.ex_zh: 教练早早赶到现场，为新手队员们配齐全新的训练装备。

items.def_en: To provide someone or an organization with a complete set of equipment or clothing
items.ex_en: The charitable organization worked diligently to outfit the volunteer search crew with coats.
items.ex_zh: 该慈善机构辛勤工作，为志愿搜救队配备了防寒大衣。

items.def_en: To supply with the necessary items, tools, or skills for a specific purpose
items.ex_en: The university strives to equip every graduate with robust analytical problem-solving skills.
items.ex_zh: 该大学致力于让每位毕业生都掌握扎实的分析性解决问题技能。

items.def_en: To supply someone or something with all the necessary items or clothes
items.ex_en: The hiking club will kit out all participating members before the mountain expedition.
items.ex_zh: 登山俱乐部将在出发远征高山之前，为所有参会成员配齐装备。

items.def_en: To fit someone out with specialized clothing, gear, or operational apparatus
items.ex_en: They decided to rig out the children in matching waterproof rain gear today.
items.ex_zh: 他们今天决定给孩子们穿戴上一整套配套的防水防雨行头。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame denote supplying a person, team, or vehicle with a comprehensive set of gear, tools, or clothing necessary for an expedition, task, or sport. They focus on assembling a complete operational kit.
groups.summary_zh: 指为某人、队伍或车辆配齐执行特定任务所需的全套装备工具。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the comprehensive, systematic provisioning of persons or vessels with specialized garments, tools, or gear for an expedition or function, beyond simple dressing.
groups.desc_zh: 强调为特定任务、远征或职能全套配备专业服装、工具与装备，超越了普通的日常穿衣。
groups.nuance_en: equip: provide with necessary technical apparatus or mental tools (laboratory / troops / with skills) · outfit: furnish with complete sets of specialized clothing or mission gear (expedition / team / soldiers) · kit: supply with standardized uniform and essential items (recruits / squad / players) · kit out: thoroughly furnish someone with complete gear (adventurer / hikers / room) · rig out: dress or equip, often extravagantly or distinctively (ship / child in costume / vehicle)
groups.nuance_zh: equip: 配备专业器械、技术或能力 (laboratory / troops / with skills) · outfit: 为远征或特殊活动全套配齐装备服饰 (expedition / team / soldiers) · kit: 发放标准成套制服装备 (recruits / squad / players) · kit out: 从头到脚彻底行头齐全 (adventurer / hikers / room) · rig out: 打扮、盛装配齐或改装船只车辆 (ship / child in costume / vehicle)

groups.name: Ladle & Bail · 舀取与舀水 (Ladle out, Bail out, Dip)
groups.tip: 用勺或长柄容器盛取液体

items.def_en: (+ into/out) to lower a ladle, cup, or bucket into a liquid to scoop some up
items.ex_en: She took a wooden ladle to dip some fresh broth from the pot.
items.ex_zh: 她拿起一把木勺，探入锅中舀取了一些新鲜的热高汤。
items.ex2_en: The narrow mountain trail dips steeply into a shady valley filled with pines.
items.ex2_zh: 狭窄的山间小径陡峭地向下倾斜，没入一片长满松树的阴凉山谷中。

items.def_en: to ladle or portion freshly cooked food from pots into serving dishes ready for eating
items.ex_en: Grandmother called everyone into the dining room to dish up the hot stew.
items.ex_zh: 祖母把大家招呼进餐厅，准备将热气腾腾的炖菜盛出装盘。

items.def_en: to serve soup or liquid food from a pot into bowls using a ladle
items.ex_en: The cafeteria worker began to ladle out steaming vegetable soup to hungry students.
items.ex_zh: 食堂工作人员开始用长柄勺把热气腾腾的蔬菜汤分盛给饥肠辘辘的学生。

items.def_zh: 用长柄勺舀取，盛出；大量分发
items.def_en: 1. (+ out/into) to serve, lift, or transfer liquid or food using a ladle 2. (+ out) to give out or distribute money, praise, or gifts generously
items.ex_en: The chef paused to ladle rich gravy over the roasted slices of beef.
items.ex_zh: 主厨停下手，用长柄勺把浓郁的肉汁仔细浇在切片的烤牛肉上。

items.def_en: to remove unwanted water from a boat or container by scooping it out with a bucket or tin
items.ex_en: The stranded sailors worked frantically to bail out seawater with a plastic bucket.
items.ex_zh: 遇险的水手们用塑料桶拼命舀出船舱内的海水以防沉没。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures dipping deep-bowled vessels into liquids (such as soup, broth, water, or bilgewater) to scoop, transfer, or empty them. It contrasts measured culinary dispensing with rapid, repetitive manual bailing.
groups.summary_zh: 特指用长柄大勺或器具舀取汤汁流质，或舀出积水。
groups.desc_en: Relates to the deep scooping, transferring, or emergency removal of liquids using concave vessels or buckets, contrasted with sipping, pouring from a spout, or pumping.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用凹形器皿进行深舀、盛出或紧急舀水排涝，区别于细啜、喷嘴倾倒或机械泵水。
groups.nuance_en: ladle: scoop out liquid in generous portions using a long-handled spoon (soup / punch / stew) · ladle out: distribute liquid food or figurative largesse freely (portions / charity / praise) · bail out: scoop water vigorously from a sinking vessel to prevent drowning (boat / canoe / bilge) · dip: plunge a small vessel briefly into liquid to extract a sample (cup into water / bucket into well) · dish up: serve hot food from pots to plates ready for eating (dinner / stew / meal)
groups.nuance_zh: ladle: 用长柄勺大勺盛取汤汁 (soup / punch / stew) · ladle out: 大勺分发流食或慷慨分发资助 (portions / charity / praise) · bail out: 紧急舀出船舱积水防沉 (boat / canoe / bilge) · dip: 舀子快速探入深处盛取 (cup into water / bucket into well) · dish up: 把锅中热饭热菜盛盘上桌 (dinner / stew / meal)

groups.name: Lampoon & Satirize · 戏拟与戏谑 (Lampoon, Caricature, Burlesque)
groups.tip: 恶意嘲弄与讽刺挖苦他人

items.def_en: To deliberately copy the style of someone or something in an exaggerated, comic way
items.ex_en: The comedy troupe chose to parody the melodramatic acting style of silent cinema.
items.ex_zh: 喜剧剧团选择恶搞模仿默片时期夸张煽情的表演风格。

items.def_zh: 嘲弄，戏弄，挖苦；用牵索固定
items.def_en: 1. To make fun of or ridicule someone. 2. To secure or steady something with a guy-rope.
items.ex_en: The older students began to guy the nervous freshman about his formal attire.
items.ex_zh: 高年级学生开始拿那名紧张的新生身上过于正式的着装打趣挖苦。

items.def_en: To parody something through ludicrous, exaggerated, grotesque imitation
items.ex_en: The satirical play sought to burlesque the pretentiousness of contemporary aristocratic high society.
items.ex_zh: 这部讽刺剧旨在用荒诞滑稽的夸张手法，嘲弄当代贵族上流社会的虚荣做作。

items.def_zh: 把…画成漫画嘲讽；夸张讽刺
items.def_en: To make a comically exaggerated or distorted representation of someone or their traits
items.ex_en: The political cartoonist loved to caricature the prime minister's distinctive prominent ears.
items.ex_zh: 这位时政漫画家酷爱把首相那双显眼的招风耳画成夸张的讽刺画。

items.def_en: To publicly criticize or make fun of someone using ridiculing satire
items.ex_en: The campus magazine dared to lampoon the administration's baffling new parking policies.
items.ex_zh: 校刊大胆发表戏谑文章，公开讽刺校方令人匪夷所思的新停车政策。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses making fun of or parodying people, public figures, or customs, often through artistic caricature, comic impersonation, or theatrical spoofing.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过夸张模仿、讽刺画或滑稽戏来调侃并讽刺特定人物或事物。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses the mocking, exaggerated, or theatrical imitation of individuals, texts, or genres to expose absurdity or folly, setting it apart from earnest homage or factual critique.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过夸张模仿、滑稽剧场化或戏拟手段对特定对象进行辛辣嘲弄或讽刺，区别于真诚致敬或写实批驳。
groups.nuance_en: lampoon: publicly ridicule or satirize sharply via writing or drama (politician / policy / elite) · caricature: distort and exaggerate prominent physical or stylistic traits (president / features / manners) · parody: closely imitate a specific work's style for comedic subversion (novel / film / song) · burlesque: grotesque, risqué, or exaggerated theatrical mockery (tradition / melodrama / opera) · guy: subject an individual to public mockery or caricature (figure / opponent / pompous official)
groups.nuance_zh: lampoon: 通过文字或剧作辛辣讽刺并揭露丑态 (politician / policy / elite) · caricature: 夸张变形特征进行漫画式嘲弄 (president / features / manners) · parody: 恶搞戏拟特定作品的风格 (novel / film / song) · burlesque: 荒诞不羁、滑稽脱俗的舞台式讽刺 (tradition / melodrama / opera) · guy: 把某人当靶子公开取笑或扮丑捉弄 (figure / opponent / pompous official)

groups.name: Land-Use Zoning & Spatial Partition · 土地规划与分区 (Zone, Parcel out, Section off)
groups.tip: 按照功能或属地分割规划

items.def_en: To separate an area or interior space into distinct enclosed parts with physical dividers or barriers
items.ex_en: Police sectioned off the street with tape while detectives examined the crime scene.
items.ex_zh: 当刑警勘查犯罪现场时，警方用警戒线将整条街道隔离开来。

items.def_zh: 将……划为特定区域，分区规划；（zone out）走神，发呆
items.def_en: 1. To divide land or an area into zones designated for specific uses or purposes. 2. (zone out) (informal) To lose concentration or become unaware of one's surroundings.
items.ex_en: City officials decided to zone the waterfront area exclusively for public commercial recreation.
items.ex_zh: 市政官员决定将滨水区专门划定为公共商业休闲功能区。

items.def_en: To change the official zoning status or permitted land usage of a designated urban area
items.ex_en: The city council voted unanimously to rezone the industrial corridor for residential development.
items.ex_zh: 市议会一致投票决定，将工业走廊重新划定为住宅开发用地。

items.def_en: To divide an expansive property, estate, or resource into distinct portions and distribute them
items.ex_en: The wealthy landowner chose to parcel out the vast rural estate among heirs.
items.ex_zh: 这位富有的土地所有者选择将庞大的乡间地产分片分配给各个继承人。

items.def_en: To divide a room, structure, or territory into distinct separate sections by erecting walls or boundaries
items.ex_en: The architect suggested we partition the spacious open gallery into three private studios.
items.ex_zh: 建筑师建议我们用隔断将宽敞的开放式展厅隔成三间独立的画室。

groups.summary_en: This frame refers to partitioning continuous urban, rural, or interior space into bounded parcels designated for specific usages (residential, commercial, industrial) or controlled occupancy.
groups.summary_zh: 指依用途规划土地功能区，或在空间上拉设界线以划分特定使用区域。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the deliberate division and regulatory designation of land or interior space into distinct functional sectors, differing from general 'dividing' by its basis in planning laws, legal parcels, or physical containment boundaries.
groups.desc_zh: 指依据规划法规、地权或物理隔断对土地及内部空间进行功能性划界与分配，区别于普通的“分割/划分”，强调法定管制与结构化区块布局。
groups.nuance_en: zone: legally designate land for specific urban uses (district / land / area) · rezone: alter the statutory land-use classification (property / parcel / tract) · parcel out: divide land or resources into smaller distributive shares (land / acreage / estate) · section off: physically cordon or partition an interior area (room / area / quadrant) · partition: legally or structurally divide a space or property (estate / room / country)
groups.nuance_zh: zone: 依法规划定土地功能分区 (district / land / area) · rezone: 依法变更土地规划性质 (property / parcel / tract) · parcel out: 将土地或资产分包配售成小块 (land / acreage / estate) · section off: 用隔板或绳栅隔离出特定区域 (room / area / quadrant) · partition: 通过法律或实体结构对空间进行硬性分割 (estate / room / country)

groups.name: Launch & Propel · 发射与起航 (Launch, Propel, Blast off)
groups.tip: 用力推向空中或水面

items.def_en: to shoot a bullet, rocket, or projectile from a weapon or device
items.ex_en: The rookie nervously fired a flare into the dark woods to call for help.
items.ex_zh: 那名新手紧张地向黑暗的树林里发射了一枚信号弹以呼救。
items.ex2_en: The ancient naval cannon fired unexpectedly during the annual historic battlefield reenactment demonstration.
items.ex2_zh: 在一年一度的古战场历史重演展示中，那门古老的海军加农炮意外走火了。

items.def_zh: 发射；使（船）下水；发起，开展；发行，投放（市场）
items.def_en: 1. To send a rocket, missile, or satellite into the air or into space. 2. To put a ship or boat into the water. 3. To start a major activity or introduce a new product to the market.
items.ex_en: Engineers plan to launch the weather satellite early tomorrow morning from the coastal base.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们计划明天清晨从沿海基地发射这颗气象卫星。
items.ex2_en: The newly designed space probe launches smoothly from the desert platform tomorrow morning.
items.ex2_zh: 这台新设计的太空探测器将于明天清晨从沙漠发射平台顺利发射升空。

items.def_en: (of a rocket or spacecraft) to leave the launch pad with immense propulsion
items.ex_en: The space shuttle blasted off into orbit under clear blue skies.
items.ex_zh: 航天飞机在晴朗的蓝天下点火升空进入轨道。

items.def_en: to untie mooring lines and depart from shore or dock in a boat
items.ex_en: The crew cast off at dawn and sailed into the open ocean.
items.ex_zh: 船员们在黎明时分解缆启航，驶向浩瀚的大洋。

items.def_en: to drive, push, or cause an object to move vigorously forward
items.ex_en: A specialized turbine will propel the experimental craft forward through the dense fluid.
items.ex_zh: 专用涡轮将推动这艘实验飞行器穿过高密度流体向前行驶。

groups.summary_en: Covers verbs for forcefully propelling a vessel, projectile, or craft into motion, whether sending a spacecraft into orbit, firing ordnance, or sending a boat into water.
groups.summary_zh: 指将飞行器、弹药或舰船强力送入空间、水域或轨道的动作。
groups.desc_en: Involves setting an object, vessel, or initiative into dynamic forward motion or flight using substantial propulsion or ceremonial release, contrasting with simple 'throwing' or 'starting' through its scale, technical trajectory, and formal initiation.
groups.desc_zh: 指凭借强劲推进力或正式启航仪式将航天器、船只或项目推入高速轨道或起始历程，区别于普通的“投掷”或“开始”，强调启动势能与轨道规模。
groups.nuance_en: launch: formally send into flight, water, or public operation (missile / satellite / campaign) · propel: drive forward with sustained mechanical or physical force (craft / vehicle / body) · blast off: violently ascend under rocket combustion (rocket / shuttle / spacecraft) · fire: discharge a projectile via ignition or mechanism (missile / rocket / torpedo) · cast off: untie and release a vessel from moorings to begin a voyage (lines / boat / ship)
groups.nuance_zh: launch: 正式发射、下水或发布上线 (missile / satellite / campaign) · propel: 施加持续动力向前推进驱动 (craft / vehicle / body) · blast off: 依靠火箭燃料剧烈喷气起飞升空 (rocket / shuttle / spacecraft) · fire: 点火或机械触发发射弹药 (missile / rocket / torpedo) · cast off: 解开缆绳使船只起航 (lines / boat / ship)

groups.name: Lay & Bond Masonry · 砌筑与灰浆固定 (Mortar, Grout, Point, Brick)
groups.tip: 胶结粘牢物体部件

items.def_en: To finish, repair, or point-fill the mortar joints of a brick wall with fresh mortar
items.ex_en: The mason returned this morning to point the damaged joints along the garden wall.
items.ex_zh: 泥瓦匠今天早上回来修补花园围墙上受损的灰缝。

items.def_en: (+ in) To fix or set stones, bricks, or pipes firmly in an underlying wet layer of mortar or concrete
items.ex_en: Make sure to bed each stone in fresh mortar so it stays firmly aligned.
items.ex_zh: 确保把每块石头都牢牢嵌在新鲜的水泥灰浆里，让它保持平整固定。

items.def_en: To coat an external masonry or brick wall with a protective, uniform layer of plaster or mortar
items.ex_en: The contractor was hired to render the external facade with weather-resistant waterproof plaster.
items.ex_zh: 承包商受聘使用耐候防水灰浆对建筑外立面进行抹灰。

items.def_zh: 用灰浆砌合；用迫击炮轰击
items.def_en: 1. To join bricks or stones together using mortar. 2. To attack or bombard a target with mortar shells.
items.ex_en: They had to mortar the rough fieldstones together before sunset to finish the wall.
items.ex_zh: 他们必须在日落前用灰浆把粗糙的原石砌在一起以完工墙体。

items.def_en: To fill the narrow spaces and crevices between tiles or masonry blocks with thin, hardening mortar
items.ex_en: After setting the ceramic tiles, the worker began to grout the narrow gaps carefully.
items.ex_zh: 贴好瓷砖后，工人开始仔细地用填缝剂填充狭窄的缝隙。

groups.summary_en: A specialized civil and trade construction frame dealing with joining bricks, stones, tiles, or blocks together using wet mineral binders such as mortar, grout, or cement slurry that dry into rock-hard joints.
groups.summary_zh: 指在建筑施工中用灰浆、填缝剂砌筑或填补石砖接缝的专门工艺。
groups.desc_en: Refers to technical masonry processes of bonding, embedding, and sealing stone or brick with wet binder compounds, differing from generic 'gluing' or 'building' by its specialized mineral materials and structural finishing techniques.
groups.desc_zh: 指使用砂浆、灰浆对石材或砖块进行铺砌、粘结与嵌缝密封的专业瓦作工艺，区别于普通“粘贴”或“建造”，强调矿物胶结材料与结构性修饰。
groups.nuance_en: mortar: secure masonry units together using wet mortar (bricks / blocks / stones) · bed: firmly set a stone or brick into a fresh layer of mortar (stone / block / brick) · grout: inject thin fluid mortar to fill tile joints or structural voids (tiles / joints / cavities) · point: finish or repair the exposed exterior mortar joints of a wall (joints / brickwork / stonework) · render: apply a continuous protective coat of plaster to exterior walls (wall / surface / facade)
groups.nuance_zh: mortar: 用砂浆粘结砌筑 (bricks / blocks / stones) · bed: 将石砖深稳坐浆嵌入灰层 (stone / block / brick) · grout: 灌注稀浆填充瓷砖缝或空隙 (tiles / joints / cavities) · point: 勾缝、剔补外墙接缝砂浆 (joints / brickwork / stonework) · render: 在外墙表面打底抹灰抹面 (wall / surface / facade)

groups.name: Leak & Spill Confidential Information · 泄露与走漏机密 (Leak, Spill, Blab)
groups.tip: 公开此前隐瞒或未知的信息

items.def_zh: 泄露，透露（机密信息）；（液体、气体等）渗漏，漏出
items.def_en: 1. To intentionally or accidentally disclose secret information to the public. 2. To let liquid or gas escape through a hole or crack.
items.ex_en: An anonymous official decided to leak the sensitive budget audit to the press yesterday.
items.ex_zh: 一名匿名官员昨天决定将敏感的预算审计报告透露给媒体。
items.ex2_en: Secret diplomatic correspondence leaked onto public social media platforms early this morning.
items.ex2_zh: 秘密外交信函于今天清晨被泄露到了公共社交媒体平台上。

items.def_en: (+ on) To report illegal, unethical, or wrongful activities within an organization to authorities or the public
items.ex_en: She took a major risk to blow the whistle on the company's illegal dumping.
items.ex_zh: 她冒着极大风险揭发了公司非法倾倒废物的黑幕。

items.def_en: To divulge a secret or reveal confidential plans prematurely or indiscreetly
items.ex_en: Don't let Mike know about the party, or he will definitely spill the beans.
items.ex_zh: 别让迈克知道聚会的事，否则他肯定会说漏嘴泄密。

items.def_en: To reveal confidential information or confess, especially under pressure or eagerly
items.ex_en: After two hours of questioning, the nervous suspect finally agreed to spill the details.
items.ex_zh: 经过两个小时的审问，紧张的嫌疑人终于同意把细节全盘托出。
items.ex2_en: Hot coffee spilled everywhere when the crowded commuter train jolted to a stop.
items.ex2_zh: 当拥挤的通勤列车猛然停下时，热咖啡洒得满地都是。

items.def_en: To talk indiscreetly or tell secrets through carelessness or lack of restraint
items.ex_en: He swore he would keep the secret, but he blabbed to everyone within hours.
items.ex_zh: 他发誓会保密，但没过几小时他就大嘴巴告诉了所有人。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on unauthorized, accidental, or indiscreet disclosures of classified or private information. It highlights breaches of confidentiality, careless gossip, or calculated whistleblowing.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重未经授权、不慎或故意违规走漏秘密与内部消息。
