groups.desc_en: Denotes stabilizing and training horticultural growth along artificial physical frameworks, contrasting with generic structural binding.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用人造支架对植物进行捆绑引缚与定型生长，区别于普通物体固定。
groups.nuance_en: tie up: secure stems loosely to prevent snapping (vine / tomato / shoot) · stake: drive an upright post to hold a heavy stalk (tree / tomato / plant) · lattice: interweave branches through crossed laths (vine / climber / rose) · trellis: train climbing plants along a free-standing framework (clematis / vine / runner bean) · espalier: prune and train a woody plant flat against a wall (fruit tree / apple / pear)
groups.nuance_zh: tie up: 简单绑扎以防倒伏 (vine / tomato / shoot) · stake: 打桩支撑粗重主干 (tree / tomato / plant) · lattice: 引导枝条在格栅上穿插交织 (vine / climber / rose) · trellis: 引缚攀援植物在棚架上铺展 (clematis / vine / runner bean) · espalier: 修剪引导树枝沿墙面呈扁平状生长 (fruit tree / apple / pear)

groups.name: Support & Fortify · 构筑斜撑与加固强化 (Buttress, Fortify, Strengthen)
groups.tip: 设桩支托加固结构

items.def_en: To make a material, structure, or defensive line firmer, more unyielding, and less flexible
items.ex_en: The commander ordered reinforcements to stiffen the crumbling defensive line along the river.
items.ex_zh: 指挥官下令调遣增援部队，以加固沿河摇摇欲坠的防线。
items.ex2_en: The soldiers' resolve stiffened markedly when their revered commander joined the frontlines.
items.ex2_zh: 当受到崇敬的指挥官亲临前线时，士兵们的决心明显变得坚定了。

items.def_en: To support an unstable wall or ceiling using stout wooden or metal beams
items.ex_en: Engineers hurried to shore up the unstable ceiling using heavy wooden beams.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们匆忙使用粗重的木梁支撑起不稳定的天花板。

items.def_zh: 设防加固；增强防卫能力
items.def_en: To strengthen a place against attack by building defenses, or to physically enhance resistance
items.ex_en: The garrison labored day and night to fortify the perimeter against potential bombardments.
items.ex_zh: 守军日夜劳作以加固周边阵地，抵御可能到来的炮击。

items.def_en: 1. To support or reinforce a wall with a buttress. 2. To strengthen or support an argument, belief, or system.
items.ex_en: The scholar presented rigorous archival evidence to buttress her controversial historical thesis.
items.ex_zh: 这位学者展示了翔实的档案证据，以有力支持她那备受争议的历史论题。

items.def_zh: 用皮带扎紧；为……加固准备
items.def_en: To encircle, bind, or secure with a belt or band, or to steel and reinforce someone or something for an ordeal
items.ex_en: The stoic knights quietly girded themselves for the grueling siege to come.
items.ex_zh: 坚毅的骑士们悄然整装束带，准备迎接即将到来的严酷围城战。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express the reinforcement of an exterior wall, barrier, or intellectual defense to withstand heavy strain or bombardment. 'Buttress' evokes exterior masonry supports or heavy corroboration of claims, whereas 'fortify' and 'stiffen' emphasize augmenting defensive strength.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重建造外部扶垛或注入加固力量以抵御外部冲击与负荷。
groups.desc_en: Denotes bracing, reinforcing, or structural shoring from without or within against impending physical or conceptual collapse, unlike merely adding mass.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过外部斜撑或内部固化来增强抗压抗塌能力，区别于单纯的体积增大。
groups.nuance_en: stiffen: increase structural rigidity or inner resolve (resolve / fabric / spine) · shore: prop up a leaning structure or failing system externally (wall / economy / confidence) · fortify: systematically strengthen against military or structural assault (castle / position / defense) · buttress: provide external physical or argumentative counter-thrust (wall / argument / claim) · gird: encircle tightly for physical defense or psychological readiness (loins / city / resolve)
groups.nuance_zh: stiffen: 增强刚性或硬化意志 (resolve / fabric / spine) · shore: 从外部斜撑以防倒塌或崩溃 (wall / economy / confidence) · fortify: 构筑工事全面加固防御 (castle / position / defense) · buttress: 筑起扶壁或为论点提供坚实支撑 (wall / argument / claim) · gird: 束紧缠裹以做好应战准备 (loins / city / resolve)

groups.name: Support & Fortify · 环栅圈护与桩栅设防 (Palisade, Stockade, Barricade)
groups.tip: 修筑栅栏工事设防

items.def_zh: 筑栅栏围护；用排桩设防
items.def_en: To enclose, fortify, or secure an area with an upright barrier of heavy timber posts
items.ex_en: The pioneers labored ceaselessly to stockade their vulnerable settlement against sudden wilderness attacks.
items.ex_zh: 先驱者们不休地构筑坚固木栅，以防范荒野中突然发动的袭击。

items.def_en: To completely surround or enclose a parcel of land or structure with a wooden or metal fence
items.ex_en: The rancher decided to fence in the entire pasture to protect the calves.
items.ex_zh: 牧场主决定用栅栏将整片牧场围起来，以保护牛犊。

items.def_en: To fortify, surround, or protect a location with a broad defensive embankment or earthwork wall
items.ex_en: Vast earthen mounds ramparted the ancient citadel against encroaching tribal invaders.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的土垒构筑成坚实壁垒，守护古堡抵御步步逼近的部落侵略者。

items.def_en: To build an impromptu defensive barrier across a road, entrance, or space to obstruct access
items.ex_en: Rebel fighters quickly barricaded the narrow alleyways with overturned carts and scrap metal.
items.ex_zh: 反叛分子迅速用倾覆的推车和废弃金属封锁了狭窄的巷道。

items.def_en: 1. To surround, enclose, or fortify an area with a fence of pointed stakes.
items.ex_en: The defending garrison palisaded the northern ridge with thousands of sharp timber stakes.
items.ex_zh: 守城部队用数千根尖锐的木桩在北侧山脊筑起栅栏固守。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on enclosing, defending, or barricading an perimeter by erecting stakes, timber palisades, or defensive barriers. While 'palisade' specifies planting a wall of pointed wooden stakes, kindred verbs cover surrounding enclosures with heavy logs or improvised obstacles.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过修筑木桩栅栏、路障等物理屏障实施外围设防圈护。
groups.desc_en: Denotes creating exclusionary perimeter fortifications using earthworks or stake barriers to keep intruders out, distinct from simple enclosure.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用栅桩、土垒等障碍物修筑环形防御工事以拒敌，区别于普通的圈地围栏。
groups.nuance_en: stockade: enclose securely with heavy vertical timber stakes (fort / outpost / camp) · fence in: erect a domestic barrier to contain or restrict movement (cattle / pasture / yard) · rampart: encircle with a protective earthen mound or embankment (fortress / city / defense) · barricade: hastily throw together an ad-hoc obstruction (street / entrance / door) · palisade: fortify a defensive perimeter with pointed wooden stakes (settlement / camp / perimeter)
groups.nuance_zh: stockade: 用粗木桩修筑防御性寨栏 (fort / outpost / camp) · fence in: 围起普通栅栏以防牲畜走失或限制活动 (cattle / pasture / yard) · rampart: 筑起防护性土垒或壁垒 (fortress / city / defense) · barricade: 匆忙设路障堵截通道 (street / entrance / door) · palisade: 竖立尖头木桩排栅以作防卫 (settlement / camp / perimeter)

groups.name: Support & Sustain · 作为基底与深层根植 (Underlie, Ground, Undergird)
groups.tip: 作为底层基础提供长久支撑

items.def_en: (+ in) To base an argument, belief, or method firmly on reality, empirical facts, or primary principles
items.ex_en: The professor insisted on grounding her economic theories firmly in empirical research data.
items.ex_zh: 这位教授坚持将她的经济学理论牢固地建立在实证研究数据之上。

items.def_zh: 贯穿并深刻影响；构成的基础
items.def_en: To be the essential pervading quality, principle, or underlying influence shaping a style or philosophy
items.ex_en: Profound spiritual beliefs inform every single brushstroke of the master's late paintings.
items.ex_zh: 深邃的灵性信仰贯穿并深刻影响着这位大师晚期画作的每一笔。

items.def_en: To embed or establish something deeply and immovably within a tradition, experience, or environment
items.ex_en: Her deep artistic convictions remain firmly rooted in generations of local folk traditions.
items.ex_zh: 她深厚的艺术信念依然深深扎根于数代流传的本土民间传统之中。

items.def_en: To fix something firmly in place or establish a secure, immutable foundation for ideas or values
items.ex_en: The constitution serves to anchor the nation's core legal values amidst political turmoil.
items.ex_zh: 宪法在政治动荡中发挥着锚定国家核心法律价值的基石作用。
items.ex2_en: The massive iron ship anchors securely within the sheltered deepwater harbor basin.
items.ex2_zh: 这艘巨大的铁船在有遮蔽的深水港池内牢牢地抛锚停泊。

items.def_zh: 构成……的基础，作为……的内在原因；位于……之下
items.def_en: 1. To be the basis, cause, or foundation of something. 2. To lie under or beneath something.
items.ex_en: Deep cultural misunderstandings underlie the prolonged diplomatic tensions between the two allied states.
items.ex_zh: 深刻的文化误解构成了两个同盟国之间长期外交紧张关系的内在根源。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate being the latent foundation, fundamental cause, or subterranean stratum upon which visible phenomena rest. 'Underlie' denotes existing beneath the surface as the root origin, while 'anchor' and 'ground' emphasize giving firm, immovable stability to abstract concepts.
groups.summary_zh: 充当事物底层的根基、驱动原因或支撑性基岩。
groups.desc_en: Denotes serving as the foundational, implicit, or bedrock source from which ideas or structures derive, contrasting with surface-level support.
groups.desc_zh: 强调充当最深层的根基、潜藏逻辑或本源依据，区别于表层的外在支撑。
groups.nuance_en: ground: establish firmly upon empirical facts or moral principles (theory / argument / belief) · inform: pervade and subtly shape the character of something (decision / policy / work) · root in: originate deeply and draw life from an origin (tradition / history / culture) · anchor: fasten securely to prevent drifting away (identity / currency / economy) · underlie: form the invisible, fundamental substrate beneath (assumption / tension / cause)
groups.nuance_zh: ground: 使理论或信念扎根于确凿事实 (theory / argument / belief) · inform: 贯穿并潜移默化地塑造实质 (decision / policy / work) · root in: 深植于传统或历史根基 (tradition / history / culture) · anchor: 抛锚固定以防漂移走样 (identity / currency / economy) · underlie: 构成隐秘而根本的底层逻辑 (assumption / tension / cause)

groups.name: Support & Undergird · 奠定基石与巩固支撑 (Undergird, Underpin, Bolster)
groups.tip: 从底层构筑坚固支撑

items.def_en: To make an idea, belief, structure, or policy stronger and more dependable
items.ex_en: New structural steel pillars were added to reinforce the aging bridge against collapse.
items.ex_zh: 桥梁加装了新的结构钢柱，以加固老旧桥体防止坍塌。

items.def_en: To improve something or make it stronger, more resilient, or more confident
items.ex_en: A substantial infusion of foreign capital helped bolster the country's fragile currency reserves.
items.ex_zh: 大量外资的注入帮助充实并巩固了该国脆弱的外汇储备。

items.def_en: To give support, strength, or a basic structure to something such as an argument, economy, or system
items.ex_en: Robust empirical data underpin the landmark conclusions presented in this comprehensive scientific report.
items.ex_zh: 扎实的实证数据构成了这份详尽科学报告中开创性结论的基础。

items.def_en: To provide evidence, facts, or proof that underpins the validity of a claim or theory
items.ex_en: The defense attorney failed to provide sufficient forensic evidence to substantiate his client's alibi.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师未能提供足够的法医物证来证实其委托人的不在场证明。

items.def_zh: 从底层支撑，加固，夯实（基础）
items.def_en: 1. To support, strengthen, or provide the underlying foundation for a system, theory, or structure.
items.ex_en: Shared democratic ideals undergird the long-standing strategic alliance between both partner nations.
items.ex_zh: 共同的民主理想从根本上巩固支撑了两个伙伴国之间长期的战略联盟。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe providing a deep structural, theoretical, or institutional foundation that keeps a larger system, policy, or argument stable. While 'undergird' emphasizes supplying fundamental bedrock support, synonyms like 'underpin' and 'substantiate' focus on grounding claims and structures solidly.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重为制度、理论或体系提供底层支柱与根基性支撑。
groups.desc_en: Denotes reinforcing and stabilizing an existing structure or argument from below or outside to maintain its validity, contrasting with passive existence as a base.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动从底部或外部施加支承或提供证据以巩固既有架构，区别于被动的充当根基。
groups.nuance_en: reinforce: add physical material or troops to increase load capacity (structure / concrete / troop) · bolster: prop up and boost sagging confidence or numbers (morale / confidence / share) · underpin: construct foundational support from beneath (economy / theory / system) · substantiate: furnish concrete evidence to validate an assertion (claim / allegation / theory) · undergird: form the comprehensive bedrock framework supporting an enterprise (democracy / reform / economy)
groups.nuance_zh: reinforce: 增补结构材料或兵力以强化强度 (structure / concrete / troop) · bolster: 托举提振疲软的士气或数字 (morale / confidence / share) · underpin: 从底部打基筑底以提供结构依托 (economy / theory / system) · substantiate: 提供确凿证据证实假说或指控 (claim / allegation / theory) · undergird: 为整个宏观体系奠定不可动摇的基石 (democracy / reform / economy)

groups.name: Suppress & Stifle · 压制与扼杀 (Hush, Smother, Stifle)
groups.tip: 以强力手段扼杀言论与异见

items.def_en: To prevent facts about an embarrassing, illegal, or unethical matter from becoming known
items.ex_en: The corrupt officials tried desperately to hush up the massive bribery scandal immediately.
items.ex_zh: 腐败官员们极力想要立刻掩盖这起重大的受贿丑闻。

items.def_zh: 压制，扼杀，掩盖（丑闻或异见）；掐死，扼杀（为解剖谋杀）
items.def_en: 1. (dated) To suppress, stifle, or hush up a discussion, inquiry, or scandal quietly. 2. (historical) To murder someone by suffocation in order to sell the body.
items.ex_en: Corrupt ministers conspired together to quietly burke the sensitive parliamentary bribery inquiry.
items.ex_zh: 腐败的部长们密谋串通，暗中悄悄压制了那项敏感的议会受贿调查。

items.def_en: To stop something from happening, developing, or continuing through heavy-handed control
items.ex_en: The authoritarian regime implemented harsh censorship laws to stifle political dissent completely.
items.ex_zh: 该威权政权实施严酷的审查法律，旨在彻底扼杀政治异见。

items.def_en: To extinguish or suppress a movement, scandal, or discussion completely
items.ex_en: The public relations team moved quickly to smother the growing scandal before dawn.
items.ex_zh: 公关团队在黎明前迅速采取行动，彻底平息了愈演愈烈的丑闻。

items.def_zh: 迅速制止；压制（传言/异议）
items.def_en: To put a complete and forceful stop to a rumor, protest, or opposition immediately
items.ex_en: The company president issued a statement to squelch baseless rumors regarding bankruptcy.
items.ex_zh: 公司总裁发表声明，迅速制止了有关破产的毫无依据的传言。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on deliberate, often underhanded or ruthless actions to choke off debate, kill investigations, or extinguish political dissent before it gains traction.
groups.summary_zh: 指动用手段封杀讨论、扼杀调查或悄然平息丑闻异见。
groups.desc_en: Denotes forcefully silencing, smothering, or strangling an expression, sound, or revelation at inception, contrasting with natural dying down.
groups.desc_zh: 指施加外力窒息、压低或扼杀萌芽状态下的声音、真相或反抗，区别于自发平息。
groups.nuance_en: hush up: suppress public disclosure or scandal through secrecy (scandal / affair / investigation) · burke: quietly suppress or bypass an inquiry or discussion before debate (inquiry / bill / debate) · stifle: choke off an emotional impulse or breathing mechanically (yawn / dissent / laugh) · smother: extinguish completely by covering or depriving of oxygen (flame / cry / initiative) · squelch: crush decisively with immediate, heavy-handed force (rebellion / rumor / dissent)
groups.nuance_zh: hush up: 严密封锁丑闻以防外泄 (scandal / affair / investigation) · burke: 悄无声息地阻挠或扼杀议案审议 (inquiry / bill / debate) · stifle: 强行憋住冲动或压制异议 (yawn / dissent / laugh) · smother: 严密覆盖使之窒息或熄灭 (flame / cry / initiative) · squelch: 采取雷霆手段当场彻底粉碎 (rebellion / rumor / dissent)

groups.name: Suppurate & Fester · 化脓与溃烂 (Fester, Weep, Ulcerate)
groups.tip: 伤口恶化感染排脓溃烂

items.def_en: To swell and fill with pus prior to bursting
items.ex_en: The neglected wound began to gather, forming a painful, throbbing yellow head.
items.ex_zh: 被忽视的伤口开始蓄脓，形成了一个令人作痛、突突跳动的黄色脓头。
items.ex2_en: The young girl quickly gathered fresh wild mushrooms from the damp forest.
items.ex2_zh: 小女孩迅速从潮湿的森林里采摘了新鲜的野生蘑菇。

items.def_en: To exude clear fluid, pus, or blood steadily from a surface lesion
items.ex_en: The deep surgical incision continued to weep clear fluid into the sterile dressing.
items.ex_zh: 较深的手术切口持续向无菌敷料中渗出清亮的体液。

items.def_en: To become infected and develop pus, deteriorating over time
items.ex_en: Without proper antiseptic treatment, the untreated dog bite began to swell and fester.
items.ex_zh: 由于缺乏适当的消毒处理，那处未作治疗的狗咬伤口开始红肿溃烂。

items.def_en: (formal, medicine) To form or discharge pus.
items.ex_en: The deep laceration began to suppurate, exuding thick yellow pus along the incision.
items.ex_zh: 较深的撕裂伤开始化脓，沿着切口处渗出浓稠的黄色脓液。

items.def_en: To break out in or become afflicted with an open inflammatory sore
items.ex_en: Untreated bacterial infections can cause delicate internal tissues to quickly inflame and ulcerate.
items.ex_zh: 未加治疗的细菌感染会导致脆弱的内部组织迅速发炎并形成溃疡。
items.ex2_en: Corrosive industrial chemicals ulcerate unprotected human skin upon direct physical exposure.
items.ex2_zh: 腐蚀性工业化学品在直接接触时会使未受保护的人体皮肤发生溃烂。

groups.summary_en: This biological frame captures progressive infection and tissue decay marked by inflammation, purulent discharge, and chronic rotting of untreated wounds.
groups.summary_zh: 描述伤口感染发炎、蓄积并排出脓液或软组织持续恶化腐烂的病理变化。
groups.desc_en: Denotes pathological suppurative deterioration and rotting of organic tissue or festering emotional corruption, contrasting with benign healing.
groups.desc_zh: 描述机体组织化脓坏死或情感创口持续恶化溃烂的病理过程，区别于正常的愈合生肌。
groups.nuance_en: gather: accumulate pus beneath intact skin prior to rupture (boil / abscess / infection) · weep: exude clear serum or watery pus continuously (wound / sore / eczema) · fester: generate foul rot and pus internally, breeding deep corruption (wound / resentment / grievance) · suppurate: undergo the formal physiological process of forming pus (lesion / ulcer / wound) · ulcerate: develop deep, eroding open sores that destroy surface tissue (skin / lining / tissue)
groups.nuance_zh: gather: 脓肿在破溃前于皮下聚积成脓 (boil / abscess / infection) · weep: 伤口创面不断渗出浆液或清脓 (wound / sore / eczema) · fester: 创口化脓溃烂，引申为怨恨积郁发酵 (wound / resentment / grievance) · suppurate: 产生脓液的正式病理过程 (lesion / ulcer / wound) · ulcerate: 表面组织剥蚀形成深层溃疡 (skin / lining / tissue)

groups.name: Surface Exposure & Geological Emergence · 地表露出与岩层突现 (Outcrop, Protrude, Jut)
groups.tip: 岩层或现象由地下露头显出

items.def_en: Of rock or mineral strata, to appear exposed directly at the earth's surface
items.ex_en: Thick beds of dark crystalline limestone crop out along the windswept northern cliffs.
items.ex_zh: 厚层深色结晶石灰岩在饱受风蚀的北部悬崖上直接显露出来。

items.def_en: To stick out prominently beyond the surrounding surface or main body
items.ex_en: Jagged black rocks jut out dangerously from the turbulent coastal waters at low tide.
items.ex_zh: 退潮时，嶙峋的黑色礁石从汹涌的沿海水域中危险地突伸出来。

items.def_en: To rise up and break above the surface of a liquid, ground, or surrounding cover
items.ex_en: The massive submarine surfaced silently amidst the thick fog of the early morning.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的潜艇在清晨的浓雾中无声无息地浮出了水面。

items.def_en: To stick out from or through something, becoming conspicuously visible
items.ex_en: Several broken metal rods protrude ominously through the crumbling concrete foundation wall.
items.ex_zh: 几根折断的金属杆从摇摇欲坠的混凝土基墙中危险地探出头来。

items.def_en: (geology) of a rock formation or stratum, to appear exposed above the surface of the ground
items.ex_en: Massive granite formations outcrop conspicuously across the barren crest of the desolate ridge.
items.ex_zh: 巨大的花岗岩体显眼地显露在荒凉山脊贫瘠的顶峰上。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on natural or geological features breaking through a covering plane to become visible above the ground or surrounding medium. It emphasizes physical exposure, structural protrusion, and spatial prominence.
groups.summary_zh: 强调地层、岩石或结构穿透表层、突出显露在地表或基质之上的状态与过程。
groups.desc_en: Denotes geological formations breaking through cover or projecting prominently beyond a surrounding baseline, contrasting with mere flatness.
groups.desc_zh: 指地质岩层穿透覆土露出地表或物理结构向外显著凸起，区别于平整延伸。
groups.nuance_en: crop out: appear naturally exposed at the surface without soil cover (rock / strata / seam) · jut out: stick out sharply at an angle past the general line (cliff / chin / headland) · surface: emerge into view above a liquid or covering medium (whale / submarine / secret) · protrude: push outward or bulge beyond a confining boundary (nail / bone / tongue) · outcrop: expose an underlying rock bed as an above-ground formation (granite / formation / reef)
groups.nuance_zh: crop out: 矿脉或岩层自然剥露于地表 (rock / strata / seam) · jut out: 陡峭地从轮廓线向外伸出 (cliff / chin / headland) · surface: 浮出水面或从覆盖物下露出 (whale / submarine / secret) · protrude: 凸出或顶出原有限制边缘 (nail / bone / tongue) · outcrop: 形成露出地表的基岩景观 (granite / formation / reef)

groups.name: Surge & Billow · 汹涌与翻腾 (Surge, Roll, Swell)
groups.tip: 大股巨浪或浓烟翻滚

items.def_en: To move in a circular or spiral direction like a whirlpool or curling smoke
items.ex_en: Autumn leaves eddy softly in small spiral patterns across the deserted courtyard stones.
items.ex_zh: 秋叶在空寂的庭院石板上轻柔地打着细小的漩涡飘转。

items.def_en: To arrive or move across an area in large undulating waves or banks, as fog or tide
items.ex_en: Dense ocean fog began to roll in, obscuring the entire rocky coastline within minutes.
items.ex_zh: 浓重的大海迷雾翻卷漫涌而来，几分钟内便遮蔽了整个岩石海岸。

items.def_en: To become larger, rounder, or rise up in smooth undulating mounds
items.ex_en: Towering gray ocean waves began to swell threateningly as the violent gale intensified.
items.ex_zh: 随着狂暴大风的加剧，高耸的灰色海浪开始威胁性地剧烈隆起。
items.ex2_en: Heavy seasonal rains quickly swell local rivers beyond their normal water embankments.
items.ex2_zh: 季节性的大暴雨迅速使当地河流的水位暴涨，越过了正常的堤坝。

items.def_en: 1. (of smoke, cloud, or fabric) To swell outward and roll upward in great waves or masses.
items.ex_en: Thick black plumes of acrid smoke billowed outward from the burning industrial warehouse.
items.ex_zh: 浓密刺鼻的黑色烟柱从燃烧的工业仓库中翻腾涌向天空。

items.def_en: To move forward rapidly and powerfully in a sudden wave or flow
items.ex_en: An irresistible wave of icy sea water surged forward through the breached sea wall.
items.ex_zh: 一股不可阻挡的冰冷海水势不可挡地越过决口的防波堤急剧奔涌。

groups.summary_en: This frame describes large masses—such as water, smoke, cloud, or fabric—swelling, undulating, and rolling outward in powerful or majestic waves.
groups.summary_zh: 形容烟雾、水流或布匹大片翻滚涌动、波涛起伏。
groups.desc_en: Denotes rolling, turbulent, fluid dynamic motion gathering mass and momentum, contrasting with steady laminar flow.
groups.desc_zh: 强调流体或群体如波涛般翻滚、积蓄动量并连绵涌动，区别于平稳层流。
groups.nuance_en: eddy: swirl in circular, counter-current vortices (dust / current / mist) · roll in: advance steadily and inexorably in vast waves (fog / tide / breaker) · swell: expand volumetrically and heave upward (wave / crowd / organ) · billow: puff outward in rolling, ballooning masses (smoke / sail / cloud) · surge: rush forward in a sudden, powerful, concentrated heave (crowd / wave / adrenaline)
groups.nuance_zh: eddy: 打着漩涡打转流动 (dust / current / mist) · roll in: 如巨浪般浩浩荡荡不可阻挡地推进 (fog / tide / breaker) · swell: 隆起膨胀或海浪起伏 (wave / crowd / organ) · billow: 烟云或风帆受力鼓胀翻滚 (smoke / sail / cloud) · surge: 如潮水般猛烈向前涌动 (crowd / wave / adrenaline)

groups.name: Surge & Skyrocket · 激增与暴涨 (Rocket, Soar, Surge)
groups.tip: 高高翱翔或如火箭般急升

items.def_en: To increase suddenly and powerfully in value, quantity, or intensity
items.ex_en: Consumer demand for electric vehicles surged dramatically following the implementation of green subsidies.
items.ex_zh: 实施绿色补贴后，消费者对电动汽车的需求出现了剧烈激增。

items.def_en: To grow or increase dramatically in a very short period
items.ex_en: Local property values shoot up whenever a new rapid transit station is constructed.
items.ex_zh: 每当修建新的快速公交站时，当地的地产价值便会迅猛窜升。

items.def_en: To increase or rise extremely quickly and suddenly; to move very fast.
items.ex_en: International fuel prices rocketed to record highs immediately following the unexpected military invasion.
items.ex_zh: 在突如其来的军事入侵发生后，国际燃油价格立即暴涨至历史新高。

items.def_en: To rise, increase, or ascend rapidly to a remarkably high level
items.ex_en: Global semiconductor profits continue to soar despite widespread logistical delays in overseas supply chains.
items.ex_zh: 尽管海外供应链普遍出现物流延误，全球半导体利润仍持续急剧攀升。

items.def_en: To rise extremely fast and steeply, especially of prices, costs, or demand
items.ex_en: Rental housing costs skyrocket in metropolitan areas due to persistent severe supply shortages.
items.ex_zh: 由于持续严重的房源短缺，大都市地区的住房租金急剧飞涨。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers sudden, steep upward trajectories in prices, numbers, or popularity, emphasizing explosive vertical momentum.
groups.summary_zh: 描述价格、数量或声誉极速垂直飙升、暴涨的强烈态势。
groups.desc_en: Denotes extreme, nearly vertical upward acceleration in metrics or prices, contrasting with steady linear growth.
groups.desc_zh: 指数值、价格等在短时间内呈现近乎垂直的爆炸式暴涨，区别于线性匀速增长。
groups.nuance_en: surge: swell rapidly past normal thresholds with sudden pressure (demand / price / infection) · shoot up: ascend abruptly and steeply (fuel price / crime rate / interest rate) · rocket: blast upward at tremendous, unstoppable velocity (share price / career / inflation) · soar: glide smoothly to an exceptionally lofty plateau (temperature / profit / inflation) · skyrocket: explode upward in an extreme, runaway trajectory (cost / deficit / popularity)
groups.nuance_zh: surge: 突破常规门槛的迅猛涌增 (demand / price / infection) · shoot up: 陡直陡升蹿高 (fuel price / crime rate / interest rate) · rocket: 如火箭般高速飞跃攀升 (share price / career / inflation) · soar: 盘旋高飞至极高水准 (temperature / profit / inflation) · skyrocket: 呈现失控式的爆炸性暴涨 (cost / deficit / popularity)

groups.name: Surge & Stampede · 奔涌与暴冲 (Surge, Charge, Bolt)
groups.tip: 人群或力量汹涌奔冲之势

items.def_en: To move forward with a sudden, forceful, wave-like mass motion
items.ex_en: Panicked spectators surged toward the narrow stadium exits as alarms began ringing incessantly.
items.ex_zh: 当警报声不断鸣响时，惊慌失措的观众如同浪潮般蜂拥挤向狭窄的体育场出口。

items.def_en: To rush forward aggressively in attack or headlong movement
items.ex_en: The mounted knights charged fiercely into the enemy ranks during the decisive battle.
items.ex_zh: 骑兵在决定性的战役中勇猛无畏地向敌军阵营发起了猛烈冲击。

items.def_en: To break away and run out of control suddenly due to fright
items.ex_en: Terrified by the sudden thunderclap, the young horse bolted wildly across the field.
items.ex_zh: 受到突如其来的雷声惊吓，那匹年轻的马仓皇逃窜穿过了田野。

items.def_en: To move with immense speed and violently reckless velocity
items.ex_en: A massive flaming boulder hurtled down the steep mountainside toward the helpless village below.
items.ex_zh: 一块巨大的燃烧巨石以惊人速度沿陡峭山坡向下猛冲，砸向下方无助的村庄。

items.def_en: To run wildly and suddenly together in panic, or force a herd or crowd to do so.
items.ex_en: The sudden crack of gunfire caused the terrified cattle herd to stampede blindly westward.
items.ex_zh: 突如其来的枪声使得受惊的牛群盲目地向西狂奔惊逃。
items.ex2_en: Rattlesnakes and wolves stampeded the nervous horses through the wooden fence boundary.
items.ex2_zh: 响尾蛇和狼群使受惊的马群狂奔着冲撞冲破了木制栅栏边界。

groups.summary_en: Describes masses of people, animals, or fluid forces moving forward with sudden, overwhelming velocity and uncontrolled momentum.
groups.summary_zh: 群体或狂暴力量受惊慌或冲动驱使，突发且失控地狂奔涌动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes wild, panic-driven or aggressive sudden mass flight and momentum, contrasting with orderly directional march.
groups.desc_zh: 指受到恐慌或狂暴驱动的群体或个体失去理智的疯狂冲撞奔逃，区别于有序行进。
groups.nuance_en: surge: press forward as a dense, fluid mass against a barrier (crowd / mob / demonstrator) · charge: rush straight forward with aggressive, offensive intent (bull / soldier / cavalry) · bolt: dash away suddenly in terror or panic (horse / suspect / animal) · hurtle: fly recklessly through the air or along a path at deadly speed (vehicle / debris / train) · stampede: rush headlong in an uncontrollable, trampling mob (herd / crowd / shopper)
groups.nuance_zh: surge: 密集人群如洪流般向前涌动施压 (crowd / mob / demonstrator) · charge: 带有攻击性地发起正面向前冲锋 (bull / soldier / cavalry) · bolt: 惊恐万状下突然窜逃脱缰 (horse / suspect / animal) · hurtle: 带着致命速度鲁莽飞驰或飞掷 (vehicle / debris / train) · stampede: 惊群失控踩踏式蜂拥奔逃 (herd / crowd / shopper)

groups.name: Surgical Excision & Ablation · 切除与切离 (Resect, Excise, Ablate)
groups.tip: 医学手术局部截除切离

items.def_en: To surgically remove a tumor, eyeball, or structure whole and intact from its enveloping sheath
items.ex_en: The ophthalmic surgeon operated delicately to enucleate the diseased eyeball without puncturing its capsule.
items.ex_zh: 眼科医生精细地进行手术，在不刺破其包膜的情况下完整摘除了病变眼球。

items.def_en: To remove tissue, an organ, or a tumor by surgical cutting
items.ex_en: The surgical team decided to excise the malignant tumor with wide, clear surgical margins.
items.ex_zh: 手术团队决定切除恶性肿瘤，并留出足够宽的洁净手术切缘。

items.def_en: To completely pull up, eradicate, or surgically excise an organ or malignant growth
items.ex_en: Surgeons worked for hours to completely extirpate the deep-seated cancerous tumor from the pelvic cavity.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生苦战数小时，终于将盆腔深部的恶性肿瘤彻底根除切除。

items.def_en: 1. (surgery) To surgically cut out part of an organ, bone, or diseased tissue.
items.ex_en: The specialized surgical team had to resect a diseased section of the patient's colon.
items.ex_zh: 专业的外科团队不得不切除了患者一截病变的结肠组织。

items.def_en: To surgically or thermally remove, erode, or destroy body tissue (such as heart pathways or tumors)
items.ex_en: Specialists used radiofrequency energy to ablate the abnormal heart pathway causing chronic arrhythmias.
items.ex_zh: 专家们利用射频能量消融了引起慢性心律失常的心脏异常传导通路。
items.ex2_en: Superficial glacier layers ablate naturally under the continuous exposure of warm sunlight.
items.ex2_zh: 在温暖阳光的持续照射下，表层冰川会自然消融剥蚀。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses formal clinical and surgical verbs denoting the precise operative removal of damaged, cancerous, or diseased tissue and anatomical structures from a living body.
groups.summary_zh: 专指外科手术中精确切除、剔除或消除病变组织与器官的医疗动作。
groups.desc_en: Denotes precise, specialized surgical excision or physical ablation of pathological tissue, contrasting with gross traumatic cutting.
groups.desc_zh: 指医学上对病变组织施行的精细切除、剜出或消融术，区别于粗暴的机械切割。
groups.nuance_en: enucleate: remove a whole organ or tumor cleanly without rupture (tumor / eyeball / cyst) · excise: surgically cut out tissue completely using sharp dissection (lesion / tumor / mole) · extirpate: completely eradicate a diseased organ or eradicate fully (cancer / thyroid / weed) · resect: cut away a specific functional segment of an organ (bowel / colon / lung) · ablate: vaporize, erode, or destroy tissue using energy or heat (endometrium / cornea / tumor)
groups.nuance_zh: enucleate: 完整剜出包膜内肿瘤或眼球 (tumor / eyeball / cyst) · excise: 运用锐器完整切除病灶 (lesion / tumor / mole) · extirpate: 斩草除根式彻底切除器官或根除异物 (cancer / thyroid / weed) · resect: 手术部分切除脏器节段 (bowel / colon / lung) · ablate: 运用热力、激光等能量消融摧毁组织 (endometrium / cornea / tumor)

groups.name: Surgical Puncturing & Deep Piercing · 穿刺与切开引流 (Puncture, Incise, Pierce)
groups.tip: 尖锐长枪刺破并扎入

items.def_en: Force a sharp point through or into something to create a clear opening
items.ex_en: The nurse used a sterile needle to pierce the blister and release built-up fluid.
items.ex_zh: 护士用无菌针头刺破水疱，引流出积聚的液体。

items.def_zh: 用长矛刺穿；（用手术刀）切开，刺破（脓肿等）
items.def_en: 1. To pierce or strike with a lance. 2. (medicine) To cut or prick open a boil or abscess with a small sharp surgical blade.
items.ex_en: The attending physician decided to lance the swollen boil to relieve the severe pressure.
items.ex_zh: 主治医生决定用手术刀切开肿胀的疖子，以缓解严重的压迫感。

items.def_en: Make a small hole in something with a sharp object, often causing sudden deflation or release
items.ex_en: A rusty nail managed to puncture the heavy rear tire of the loaded truck.
items.ex_zh: 一颗生锈的铁钉刺穿了满载卡车厚实的后轮胎。
items.ex2_en: The inflated party balloon punctured instantly with an extremely sharp bang sound.
items.ex2_zh: 充气的派对气球瞬间被扎破，伴随一声极其响亮的爆裂声。

items.def_en: Cut into flesh or a surface cleanly and precisely with a sharp blade
items.ex_en: The surgeon used a scalpel to incise the abdominal wall with clinical precision.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生用手术刀精准利落地切开了患者的腹壁组织。

items.def_en: Pierce completely through with a long, sharp instrument or stake
items.ex_en: The surgeon warned that the sharpened trocar could easily impale the posterior vascular wall.
items.ex_zh: 外科医生警告说，锋利的穿刺针极易刺穿后侧血管壁。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate piercing deeply into tissue or bodily swelling using a sharp instrument, especially to relieve pressure or discharge fluid. Lance focuses on surgical opening, puncture denotes making a hole, and impale highlights violent deep penetration.
groups.summary_zh: 指使用尖锐器械深度穿透、刺入或切开肿胀组织引流。
groups.desc_en: Denotes deep penetrative punctures or strategic incisive entries to drain, impale, or access cavities, contrasting with surface scratching.
groups.desc_zh: 指利用尖锐器械进行深刺、切开穿透以排脓或贯通，区别于浅表擦划裂伤。
groups.nuance_en: pierce: penetrate completely through with a pointed tip (ear / skin / armor) · lance: slit open a purulent collection to release pressure (boil / abscess / blister) · puncture: make a small, deep hole with a sharp point (lung / tire / vein) · incise: make a clean, planned cut into biological tissue (scalpel / skin / wound) · impale: pierce through the entire body with a large stake (victim / torso / prey)
groups.nuance_zh: pierce: 用尖锐物扎透贯穿 (ear / skin / armor) · lance: 用手术刀挑破切开脓疮引流 (boil / abscess / blister) · puncture: 尖物刺破形成狭深孔洞 (lung / tire / vein) · incise: 外科手术中整齐切开皮肤组织 (scalpel / skin / wound) · impale: 用尖桩从躯体穿透钉死 (victim / torso / prey)

groups.name: Surgical Removal & Alteration · 身体组织摘除与去势 (Declaw, Desex, Dock)
groups.tip: 医学手术切除身体部位

items.def_en: To surgically cut off or chemically cauterize the horns of livestock
items.ex_en: The rancher decided to dehorn the young calves before turnout to prevent herd injuries.
items.ex_zh: 牧场主决定在放牧前给小牛去角，以防牛群相互击伤。

items.def_en: To cut short an animal's tail, ears, or other anatomical extremities
items.ex_en: The veterinarian refused to dock the puppy's tail purely for cosmetic purposes.
items.ex_zh: 兽医拒绝纯粹为了美观而给小狗断尾。
items.ex2_en: The large cargo ship docked safely alongside the busy commercial loading pier.
items.ex2_zh: 这艘大型货轮在繁忙的商业装卸码头旁安全地靠泊了。

items.def_zh: 阉割；为（动物）做绝育手术
items.def_en: To surgically remove the reproductive organs of an animal
items.ex_en: Animal shelters routinely neuter stray cats before putting them up for adoption.
items.ex_zh: 动物收容所通常会在流浪猫被领养前为其进行绝育手术。

items.def_en: To surgically alter or excise an animal's vocal cords to mute or soften its bark
items.ex_en: The clinic will debark the hound to eliminate the chronic noise disturbance.
items.ex_zh: 该诊所将对猎犬实施声带切除手术，以消除长期的噪音困扰。
items.ex2_en: Bark on old oak trees debarks easily during prolonged spells of severe drought.
items.ex2_zh: 在长期严重的干旱期间，老橡树上的树皮很容易自然脱落剥开。

items.def_en: 1. (veterinary) To surgically remove the claws of an animal, especially a cat.
items.ex_en: Many veterinarians now strongly counsel owners not to declaw their indoor cats.
items.ex_zh: 如今许多兽医极力建议主人不要为家养室内猫切除爪子。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe elective or customary surgical alterations and tissue removals performed on animals or patients, such as amputating claws, docking tails, debarking, or neutering anatomical appendages.
groups.summary_zh: 多用于兽医或特定医疗场景，指切除、剥夺特定身体部位或附属结构。
groups.desc_en: Denotes intentional surgical mutilation, desexing, or anatomical alteration of animals, contrasting with general therapeutic surgery.
groups.desc_zh: 特指为了驯化、美观或绝育对动物身体结构进行的截除或改变，区别于常规治病。
groups.nuance_en: dehorn: remove the horns of livestock to prevent injury (cattle / calf / goat) · dock: truncate an animal's tail for breed standard or hygiene (tail / sheep / dog) · neuter: surgically remove reproductive organs to sterilize (pet / male / dog) · debark: surgically excise canine vocal cords to suppress barking (dog / canine / bark) · declaw: amputate the terminal phalanges to remove claws (cat / kitten / paw)
groups.nuance_zh: dehorn: 割除牲畜角质以防抵人互伤 (cattle / calf / goat) · dock: 截除动物尾巴以符合品种外观或卫生 (tail / sheep / dog) · neuter: 切除动物生殖腺进行绝育 (pet / male / dog) · debark: 切除声带使犬类失去吠叫能力 (dog / canine / bark) · declaw: 截去猫第一趾节以去爪 (cat / kitten / paw)

groups.name: Surrender & Yield · 投降与让步 (Surrender, Yield, Concede)
groups.tip: 战局不敌放弃抵抗彻底认输

items.def_en: To stop fighting or competing and accept defeat
items.ex_en: Exhausted after twelve grueling rounds, the battered boxer finally decided to give up.
items.ex_zh: 在经历了十二轮艰苦搏斗后，疲惫不堪的拳击手最终决定认输。

items.def_en: (+ arms/weapons) To surrender weapons and cease combat resistance
items.ex_en: The government has laid down strict safety guidelines for the industry.
items.ex_zh: 政府为该行业制定了严格的安全指南。

items.def_en: (+ to) To stop resisting, or give up control and possession under pressure
items.ex_en: Under intense political pressure, the governor finally yielded to the opposition's legislative demands.
items.ex_zh: 在巨大的政治压力下，州长最终向反对派的立法诉求做出了让步。

items.def_en: To admit defeat in a contest or election, or surrender an entitlement or point
items.ex_en: The senator refused to concede defeat until every mail-in ballot was counted.
items.ex_zh: 在所有邮寄选票清点完毕之前，参议员拒绝承认败选。

items.def_en: 1. To stop fighting and admit defeat, giving up resistance to an enemy. 2. To give up something or hand someone over into the control or possession of another.
items.ex_en: The besieged rebels agreed to surrender their weapons and evacuate the outpost peacefully.
items.ex_zh: 被包围的叛军同意缴械投降，和平撤出该前哨基地。

groups.summary_en: Pertains to giving up a physical fight, position, or claim to an opponent, or ceding control to another party.
groups.summary_zh: 指放下武器认输、放弃阵地或主动做出让步放弃主导权。
groups.desc_en: Denotes capitulation, acknowledging defeat, or voluntarily relinquishing control or claims under pressure, contrasting with defiant resistance.
groups.desc_zh: 指在强力施压下被迫承认失败、缴械或让渡控制权，区别于顽抗到底。
groups.nuance_en: give up: abandon an ongoing effort, habit, or resistance (smoking / fight / claim) · lay down: formally relinquish weapons to end fighting (arm / weapon / sword) · yield: submit to external force after resistance is overcome (ground / pressure / point) · concede: reluctantly acknowledge defeat or the opponent's validity (defeat / election / point) · surrender: formally capitulate and hand over custody or sovereignty (weapon / city / prisoner)
groups.nuance_zh: give up: 中途放弃努力或习性 (smoking / fight / claim) · lay down: 正式放下武器宣布停战 (arm / weapon / sword) · yield: 承受重压后被迫退让屈从 (ground / pressure / point) · concede: 勉强认输或承认对方正确 (defeat / election / point) · surrender: 正式交出武装或主权投降 (weapon / city / prisoner)

groups.name: Surveil & Keep Tabs · 监控与追踪观察 (Monitor, Surveil, Keep tabs on)
groups.tip: 严密守望并监控进程

items.def_en: To supervise an industry, community, or regulation to ensure that laws or standards are obeyed
items.ex_en: Independent regulators were established to police the newly deregulated telecommunications market.
items.ex_zh: 设立了独立监管机构，以监督管控新近放开管制的电信市场。

items.def_zh: 追踪；追踪观察（动态变化）
items.def_en: To follow the trail or observe the changing progress of someone or something continuously
items.ex_en: Public health authorities used mobile technology to track the rapid spread of the contagion.
items.ex_zh: 公共卫生部门利用移动技术追踪该传染病的快速蔓延。

items.def_en: To observe, supervise, and check the progress, quality, or condition of someone or something continuously over time.
items.ex_en: Nurses continue to monitor the patient's vital signs around the clock in the intensive care unit.
items.ex_zh: 在重症监护室里，护士们继续全天候监测患者的生命体征。

items.def_zh: 严密监视；时刻关注……的动态
items.def_en: To monitor the actions, movements, or whereabouts of someone continuously
items.ex_en: My supervisor hired an assistant to keep tabs on my ongoing field research.
items.ex_zh: 我主管雇了一名助手来时刻盯住我的实地调研动态。

items.def_en: To keep a person, place, or group under close, often clandestine, visual or electronic observation
items.ex_en: Federal agents were deployed to surveil the warehouse linked to international smuggling networks.
items.ex_zh: 联邦特工被派去暗中监视那处与国际走私网络有关的仓库。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses systematically keeping continuous or regular watch over individuals, communications, or changing situations to ensure compliance, gather intelligence, or detect deviations.
groups.summary_zh: 指为搜集情报、保证安全或督促合规而进行持续监视与复核。
groups.desc_en: Denotes ongoing, covert or regulatory observation to track activities and preempt threats, contrasting with casual glancing.
groups.desc_zh: 指对目标施加系统性、警戒性或秘密的持续追踪与观察，区别于无意注视。
groups.nuance_en: police: enforce rules and maintain order over an arena (community / industry / border) · track: trace the movement path or sequential development of a subject (shipment / suspect / progress) · monitor: continuously observe and record readings or behavior for compliance (vital sign / election / compliance) · keep tabs on: informal, vigilant tracking of someone's whereabouts (competitor / spending / movement) · surveil: subject to targeted, sophisticated espionage or visual scrutiny (suspect / premises / diplomat)
groups.nuance_zh: police: 维持秩序、监督合规与执法 (community / industry / border) · track: 循迹追踪实体位置或发展轨迹 (shipment / suspect / progress) · monitor: 持续监控并记录生理参数或规范达标情况 (vital sign / election / compliance) · keep tabs on: 非正式但时刻警惕地盯梢其动向 (competitor / spending / movement) · surveil: 运用专业技术手段进行秘密严密监视 (suspect / premises / diplomat)

groups.name: Survey & Inspect · 巡视与查勘 (Appraise, Reconnoiter, Scope out)
groups.tip: 居高临下大范围查看

items.def_en: to look at or investigate an area or situation thoroughly beforehand to find out what it is like
items.ex_en: Let us scope out the neighborhood first before we sign the rental agreement.
items.ex_zh: 在签租房协议之前，咱们先去摸清周边环境吧。

items.def_en: to look closely and formally at every part of something to assess its condition or detect defects
items.ex_en: Safety regulators arrived unannounced to inspect every pressure valve throughout the chemical plant.
items.ex_zh: 安全监管人员突击造访，仔细核查了化工厂内的每一个压力阀门。

items.def_zh: 俯瞰，审视，巡视；全面考察，通盘考虑；测量，勘测；进行民意调查
items.def_en: 1. to look at, inspect, or examine something carefully, especially from a broad perspective. 2. to investigate or poll the opinions or behavior of a group. 3. to measure and map an area of land.
items.ex_en: The engineering team must survey the coastal terrain before commencing construction on the seawall.
items.ex_zh: 在海堤破土动工之前，工程队必须全面勘测这片沿海地形。

items.def_en: to look at someone or something carefully with an eye toward judging their value, quality, or status
items.ex_en: The curator paused to critically appraise the condition of the seventeenth-century oil painting.
items.ex_zh: 馆长停下脚步，审视评估了这幅十七世纪油画的保存状况。

items.def_en: to make a military or strategic observation of an area to gain situational intelligence
items.ex_en: Special forces scouts crossed the border to reconnoiter the enemy's fortified artillery positions.
items.ex_zh: 特种侦察兵越过边界，去先行侦察敌方设防的炮兵阵地。

groups.summary_en: Verbs here denote taking an overarching, comprehensive visual sweep or systematic examination of a physical landscape, property, or situation to gather information and assess conditions.
groups.summary_zh: 指居高临下或全局性地打量、勘测、考察某一处所或全局态势。
groups.desc_en: Involves methodical visual or strategic examination of an area, person, or object to evaluate condition or gather intelligence, differing from passive 'look' or simple 'see' through deliberate evaluative purpose.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及出于评估现状或搜集情报之目的，对特定区域、对象进行有条理的实地查勘与审视，与单纯的“看”相比具有明确的评估或战术目的性。
groups.nuance_en: survey: broad overview mapping or systemic scrutiny (land / damage / public opinion) · inspect: formal rigorous checking for defects or compliance (facilities / documents / troops) · appraise: expert qualitative or financial evaluation (property / talent / options) · reconnoiter: military or tactical advance exploration of territory (enemy positions / terrain) · scope out: informal preliminary casing or sizing up (competition / venue / scene)
groups.nuance_zh: survey: 全面概查或测绘审视 (land / damage / public opinion) · inspect: 严密查验合规性或瑕疵 (facilities / documents / troops) · appraise: 专家式的价值或资质评定 (property / talent / options) · reconnoiter: 战术性或军事前哨侦察 (enemy positions / terrain) · scope out: [口]预先打探摸底 (competition / venue / scene)

groups.name: Survive & Subsist · 存活与维持生计 (Eke out, Scrape by, Get by)
groups.tip: 在艰难条件下勉强维持生命

items.def_en: (+ on) To have just enough money or resources to survive without luxury
items.ex_en: During graduate school, we had to get by on cheap ramen and student stipends.
items.ex_zh: 读研期间，我们只得靠廉价拉面和学生补贴勉强糊口。

items.def_en: To support someone temporarily through a difficult period of shortage
items.ex_en: A modest emergency loan should tide over the family until next month's paycheck.
items.ex_zh: 一笔微薄的应急贷款应能帮这家人渡过难关，撑到下个月发工资。

items.def_zh: 靠微薄收入勉强维持生活，存活；存在
items.def_en: (+ on) (formal) To manage to stay alive with very little food, money, or resources.
items.ex_en: Many impoverished villagers subsist on plain rice and wild roots during extreme droughts.
items.ex_zh: 在极度干旱期间，许多贫困村民仅靠白米和野菜勉强维生。

items.def_zh: 勉强过活；东拼西凑度日
items.def_en: To manage to live with only barely enough money, food, or resources
items.ex_en: After paying his hefty medical bills, he could barely scrape by each month.
items.ex_zh: 支付了巨额医疗费后，他每个月都过得十分拮据，东拼西凑度日。

items.def_en: To make a scarce supply last, or to earn a meager living with difficulty
items.ex_en: The elderly artisan continued to eke out a meager living by repairing antique clocks.
items.ex_zh: 这位老工匠继续靠修理老式古董钟表竭力维持着微薄的生计。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on precarious physical or economic survival under scarcity. Agents barely sustain life, relying on frugal means, frugal rations, or desperate resourcefulness.
groups.summary_zh: 表现面对资源匮乏时艰难求生、竭力维持最低生计的生活状态。
groups.desc_en: Denotes enduring hardship and maintaining basic physical or economic existence under severe constraints, contrasting with flourishing or thriving by emphasizing bare minimums.
groups.desc_zh: 指在匮乏或极端严苛的条件下维持最基本的生理存活或生计底线，与“繁荣、兴盛”相对，强调勉强维系与紧缩度日。
groups.nuance_en: subsist: barely maintain physical life through minimal nourishment or income (subsistence diet / wage / meager rations) · eke out: painstakingly supplement or stretch meager resources to survive (existence / living / livelihood) · scrape by: narrowly avoid insolvency or starvation with barely enough means (poverty line / minimum wage) · get by: manage minimally without luxury or ease (basic skills / current income) · tide over: provide temporary survival support until relief arrives (emergency loan / cash reserves)
groups.nuance_zh: subsist: 仅靠最低饮食或微薄收入勉强糊口 (subsistence diet / wage / meager rations) · eke out: 竭力拼凑、省吃俭用维持 (existence / living / livelihood) · scrape by: 勉强不至破产断炊 (poverty line / minimum wage) · get by: 尚能应付凑合过关 (basic skills / current income) · tide over: 暂时接济以渡过难关 (emergency loan / cash reserves)

groups.name: Suspect & Disbelieve · 怀疑与否定 (Suspect, Doubt, Disbelieve)
groups.tip: 从存疑到认定不可信

items.def_en: (+ sb/sth) feel doubt, curiosity, or uncertainty regarding the truth or reliability of something
items.ex_en: I've often wondered about what life would be like in another country.
items.ex_zh: 我经常琢磨如果生活在另一个国家会是什么样子。

items.def_zh: 怀疑，疑有；觉得……可疑，不信任；猜想
items.def_en: 1. To think or believe that something is likely or true, especially something bad or illicit. 2. To doubt the truth or honesty of someone or something; to distrust.
items.ex_en: Forensic investigators suspect that foul play was involved in the politician's sudden death.
items.ex_zh: 法医调查人员怀疑这位政客的离奇猝死背后涉及刑事犯罪。

items.def_en: To feel uncertain about something or consider it unlikely to be true.
items.ex_en: Economists doubt that the aggressive tax cut will generate substantial long-term growth.
items.ex_zh: 经济学家们怀疑激进的减税措施能否带来实质性的长期增长。

items.def_en: feel no confidence or trust in someone or something because you suspect bad motives
items.ex_en: Voters increasingly mistrust the candidate because of his evasive responses during the debates.
items.ex_zh: 由于该候选人在辩论中含糊其辞，选民们对他愈发不信任。

items.def_en: [I/T] feel sure that something is not true or that someone is not telling the truth
items.ex_en: Jurors chose to disbelieve the witness when phone logs contradicted his formal alibi.
items.ex_zh: 当通话记录与证人的正式不在场证明相矛盾时，陪审团选择不予采信。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures an epistemic scale regarding propositions: from a preliminary inkling or hunch that something might be true/untrue (suspect), to active uncertainty and lack of conviction (doubt), culminating in categorical rejection of truth (disbelieve).
groups.summary_zh: 从猜度可能性递进至怀疑真实性，最终达到断然不信的程度。
groups.desc_en: Reflects an escalating epistemic progression from tentative intuitive conjecture toward outright rejection of truth or credibility, differing from neutral wondering by harboring negative or wary presuppositions.
groups.desc_zh: 指认知层面上从直觉性的猜想演变为彻底拒斥其真实性与可信度的递进过程，与中性的“好奇推测”不同，带有负面设想或质疑色彩。
groups.nuance_en: wonder about: mildly reflect upon or query credibility with curiosity (motives / truth) · suspect: actively hypothesize guilt, foul play, or hidden facts (foul play / betrayal / deception) · doubt: feel cognitive uncertainty or lack of conviction (veracity / competence / outcome) · mistrust: possess deep-seated skepticism toward integrity or safety (intentions / motives / advice) · disbelieve: outright reject an assertion as false or impossible (account / report / claims)
groups.nuance_zh: wonder about: 略带好奇地探询或纳闷 (motives / truth) · suspect: 倾向于推定有疑或作恶 (foul play / betrayal / deception) · doubt: 认知上生疑、缺乏信念 (veracity / competence / outcome) · mistrust: 缺乏信任、戒心深重 (intentions / motives / advice) · disbelieve: 断然不信、否定真实性 (account / report / claims)

groups.name: Suspect & Mistrust · 猜忌与戒备不信 (Suspect, Second-guess, Skepticize)
groups.tip: 从心生怀疑到丧失信任

items.def_en: To feel uncertain about the reliability, truth, or honesty of someone or something
items.ex_en: Colleagues began to doubt her integrity when the financial discrepancies came to light.
items.ex_zh: 当财务账目漏洞被揭露后，同事们开始怀疑她的诚信。

items.def_zh: 斜视，以怀疑与不信任的目光看待
items.def_en: To regard someone or an idea with an attitude of suspicion, mistrust, or disapproval
items.ex_en: Conservative scholars looked askance at the radical new interpretations of constitutional law.
items.ex_zh: 保守派学者对这一激进的宪政法新解释投以怀疑和审视的目光。

items.def_en: To feel doubt or have an inkling about someone's integrity, guilt, or motives
items.ex_en: Detectives suspect his sudden wealth stems from unauthorized offshore insider trading activities.
items.ex_zh: 探员们怀疑他的暴富源于未经授权的海外内幕交易行径。

items.def_zh: 事后质疑，妄加猜测怀疑
items.def_en: To criticize, doubt, or anticipate someone's judgment or actions with suspicion
items.ex_en: Subordinates were afraid to act because the manager loved to second-guess every operational decision.
items.ex_zh: 下属们不敢擅动，因为经理总爱事后挑剔并质疑每一项运营决策。

items.def_en: To feel suspicious of someone or something, doubting their honesty, reliability, or safety.
items.ex_en: Foreign investors deeply mistrust the regime due to past arbitrary asset seizures.
items.ex_zh: 由于过去屡次发生任意没收资产的行径，外国投资者对该政权深怀戒心。

groups.summary_en: Centering on affective wariness, unease, and interpersonal suspicion. One harbors apprehension that someone might be deceitful, unsafe, or acting with hidden ulterior motives.
groups.summary_zh: 偏向对人或事物意图与安全性的猜疑、戒备及防范心态。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on affective suspicion, chronic vigilance, and skeptical wariness toward motives, contrasting with theoretical questioning by implying interpersonal guardedness and defensive second-guessing.
groups.desc_zh: 聚焦于人际交往中对动机的防备、多疑与审视，与纯粹的理论设问相比，侧重防御性的戒备心与挑剔审判心理。
groups.nuance_en: doubt: harbor cognitive reservation or hesitation (loyalty / credibility) · suspect: actively intuit deceit or malice (motives / foul play) · mistrust: harbor chronic wariness toward reliability or goodwill (intentions / promises / leadership) · look askance at: regard with visible disapproval, suspicion, or distaste (proposals / claims / newcomers) · second-guess: critically review or doubt past decisions or another's motives after the fact (strategy / judgment / motives)
groups.nuance_zh: doubt: 抱有疑虑与犹豫 (loyalty / credibility) · suspect: 怀疑包藏祸心或欺诈 (motives / foul play) · mistrust: 怀有长期戒备与防人之心 (intentions / promises / leadership) · look askance at: 斜眼睨视、投以怀疑与不以为然的目光 (proposals / claims / newcomers) · second-guess: 事后推敲猜忌或妄加揣测 (strategy / judgment / motives)

groups.name: Suspend & Defer · 中止与延期 (Adjourn, Recess, Prorogue)
groups.tip: 会议或审理程序暂时休会

items.def_en: To stop something temporarily from operating, continuing, or being active
items.ex_en: The transport authority decided to suspend all passenger ferry services during the typhoon.
items.ex_zh: 交通管理局决定在台风期间暂停所有客运轮渡服务。

items.def_en: To postpone an action, event, or decision until a later time
items.ex_en: The council opted to defer the zoning decision until further environmental assessments concluded.
items.ex_zh: 市议会决定推迟区划决议，直至进一步的环境评估结束。

items.def_en: To take a temporary break or pause during an official meeting, session, or court trial
items.ex_en: The trial judge announced that the court would recess for forty-five minutes.
items.ex_zh: 主审法官宣布法庭将休庭四十五分钟。
items.ex2_en: The legislative speaker recessed the heated debate until early tomorrow morning.
items.ex2_zh: 立法议长将这场激烈的辩论休会推迟到明早进行。

items.def_en: To suspend or end a meeting, trial, or legislative session with the intention of resuming it later.
items.ex_en: The presiding officer declared that the assembly would adjourn until tomorrow morning.
items.ex_zh: 主持会议的官员宣布大会休会，延期至明晨继续举行。
items.ex2_en: The committee chairperson adjourned the contentious session after reaching a critical consensus.
items.ex2_zh: 在达成关键共识后，委员会主席宣布这场充满争议的会议休会。

items.def_en: To discontinue the meetings of a parliament or legislative assembly without formally dissolving it
items.ex_en: The Prime Minister advised the monarch to prorogue the current parliamentary session early.
items.ex_zh: 首相建议君主提前中止并休止当前的议会会期。
items.ex2_en: Parliament will prorogue next Tuesday after completing the final legislative debates.
items.ex2_zh: 议会在完成最后的立法辩论后将于下周二休会。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers formal, institutional, or procedural actions taken to halt proceedings, meetings, or sessions temporarily with the intention of reconvening later.
groups.summary_zh: 指官方或会议程序中的暂停、休会或推迟重开。
groups.desc_en: Describes procedural actions that interrupt an ongoing legislative, judicial, or administrative proceeding, contrasting with outright cancellation by holding open the prospect of scheduled resumption.
groups.desc_zh: 描述立法院、司法机构或行政会议程序性的中途停止与延期，与“彻底废止”不同，保留了后续按期恢复的机制。
groups.nuance_en: suspend: officially stop temporarily or hold in abeyance (operations / rules / proceedings) · defer: put off consideration or action to a later scheduled time (decision / judgment / debate) · recess: take an official brief interval during a session (session / court / parliament) · adjourn: formally conclude a meeting or sitting with resumption scheduled later (meeting / hearing / session) · prorogue: discontinue a legislative session by royal/executive prerogative without dissolving it (parliament / assembly)
groups.nuance_zh: suspend: 正式中止或暂缓实施 (operations / rules / proceedings) · defer: 延期审议或付诸日后决定 (decision / judgment / debate) · recess: 会议期间正式休会片刻 (session / court / parliament) · adjourn: 会议或庭审正式告一段落、择期再会 (meeting / hearing / session) · prorogue: 依特权休会或停止立法会期 (parliament / assembly)

groups.name: Suspend & Prorogue · 停会与延期 (Prorogue, Adjourn, Defer)
groups.tip: 议会官方暂停或延缓会期

items.def_en: To arrange for an event, debate, or legislative session to take place at a later time than scheduled
items.ex_en: Organizers decided to postpone the annual conference until travel restrictions were lifted.
items.ex_zh: 组织者决定推迟年会，直到旅行限制解除后再择期举行。

items.def_en: To officially delay an action, decision, or hearing until a future point in time
items.ex_en: The board resolved to defer consideration of the takeover bid until next quarter.
items.ex_zh: 董事会决议将收购要约的审议推迟至下一季度。

items.def_en: To break off proceedings formally and postpone them to a later specified date
items.ex_en: The tribunal voted to adjourn the proceedings until pertinent financial documents were submitted.
items.ex_zh: 法庭投票决定休庭，延期至提交相关财务文件后再开庭。
items.ex2_en: The court adjourned until ten o'clock tomorrow morning for jury deliberations.
items.ex2_zh: 法庭休庭至明早十点以进行陪审团审议。

items.def_en: To decide not to proceed with a project, bill, or agenda item for an indefinite period
items.ex_en: The development committee agreed to shelve the costly subway expansion proposal indefinitely.
items.ex_zh: 发展委员会同意无限期搁置耗资巨大的地铁扩建提案。

items.def_en: (politics, chiefly British) To officially end a session of parliament without dissolving it, suspending meetings until the next session.
items.ex_en: The Crown announced the royal proclamation to prorogue parliament ahead of the referendum.
items.ex_zh: 王室发布了在公投前使议会休会的王家文告。
items.ex2_en: The national legislative assembly prorogued late yesterday evening amid intense public debate.
items.ex2_zh: 在公众的激烈辩论中，国民议会于昨晚深夜休会。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this constitutional and legislative frame involve formally putting off, concluding, or deferring parliamentary sessions and institutional proceedings. They emphasize executive intervention terminating a calendar period without formal dissolution.
groups.summary_zh: 指依据宪制权力中止议会会期或将议程法定延期。
groups.desc_en: Emphasizes the formal, institutional postponement or termination of institutional proceedings or plans, differing from casual stalling through formal authority or procedural shelving.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重依据法定职权或组织流程，将计划或会期予以正式延缓、搁置或结会，与随意的拖延不同，具有严格的制度约束力。
groups.nuance_en: postpone: reschedule a designated event to a future date (hearing / match / vote) · defer: submit to procedural delay out of deference or expediency (consideration / action / matter) · adjourn: terminate a current sitting until an appointed date (assembly / trial / meeting) · shelve: set aside a proposal indefinitely without formal rejection (plans / bill / project) · prorogue: terminate a parliamentary session constitutionally (parliament / legislature)
groups.nuance_zh: postpone: 重新安排至未来的某日举行 (hearing / match / vote) · defer: 因权衡或礼让而延期考虑 (consideration / action / matter) · adjourn: 宣布休会并择期重开 (assembly / trial / meeting) · shelve: 长期搁置某项提案 (plans / bill / project) · prorogue: 依宪制宣布议会休会 (parliament / legislature)

groups.name: Suspend & Recess · 休会与中止 (Adjourn, Suspend, Break off)
groups.tip: 议会法庭暂时中断或休会

items.def_en: To temporarily prevent something from continuing or being in effect
items.ex_en: International regulators moved quickly to suspend the airline's operating license over safety violations.
items.ex_zh: 针对违规安全隐患，国际监管机构迅速采取行动中止了该航空公司的运营许可证。

items.def_en: To suddenly pause or terminate discussions, relations, or proceedings
items.ex_en: The foreign minister abruptly broke off bilateral negotiations after maritime border incursions.
items.ex_zh: 在发生海上边界侵犯事件后，外长突然中断了双边谈判。
items.ex2_en: Direct communications broke off suddenly when severe winter storms damaged power lines.
items.ex2_zh: 当猛烈的冬季暴风雪损坏输电线时，直接通讯突然中断了。

items.def_en: To step down temporarily from a witness stand or pause active duties in an inquiry
items.ex_en: The CEO decided to stand down after the company's financial scandal was exposed.
items.ex_zh: 公司财务丑闻曝光后，首席执行官决定引咎辞职。

items.def_zh: 休会，休庭，暂停工作；把……嵌入壁内，使凹进
items.def_en: 1. (formal, chiefly US) To stop work or proceedings temporarily, especially of a parliament, committee, or court. 2. To set something into a wall or surface.
items.ex_en: The congressional committee voted to recess for two hours before hearing testimony.
items.ex_zh: 国会委员会表决决定在听取证词前暂停休会两小时。
items.ex2_en: The committee chair decided to recess the lengthy hearing until early next week.
items.ex2_zh: 委员会主席决定将漫长的听证会休会至下周初。

items.def_en: To temporarily end a meeting, trial, or legislative session with the intention of resuming later
items.ex_en: Unable to reach a consensus, the arbiters agreed to adjourn the dispute hearing.
items.ex_zh: 由于无法达成共识，仲裁员们同意暂时休庭并延后审理此争议。
items.ex2_en: The international climate summit adjourned early this afternoon following constructive preliminary talks.
items.ex2_zh: 在进行建设性的初步会谈后，国际气候峰会于今天下午提早休会。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this procedural frame denote pausing or breaking off an ongoing meeting, court trial, or legislative assembly for an interval, with the explicit intention of resuming later. They distinguish formal adjournments from temporary pauses.
groups.summary_zh: 指会议、审判或工作进程暂时中止或休会以待续行。
groups.desc_en: Covers situational pauses, intermissions, or unilateral cessations in institutional or operational sessions, distinguishing itself from final dissolution by preserving the status quo.
groups.desc_zh: 指在组织运作、法律庭审或军事部署中出现的阶段性歇会或中途暂停，区别于“解散”，强调维持现状以待后命。
groups.nuance_en: suspend: abruptly or officially pause an ongoing process (standing orders / operations / talks) · recess: enter an scheduled institutional break (congress / committee / tribunal) · adjourn: conclude the current sitting until a fixed next time (court / session) · break off: abruptly stop ongoing interactions or communications (negotiations / relations / engagement) · stand down: withdraw temporarily from an active operational state (troops / alerts / witness)
groups.nuance_zh: suspend: 暂时中止进行中的规程 (standing orders / operations / talks) · recess: 机构按计划短暂停会歇息 (congress / committee / tribunal) · adjourn: 正式结束本次会期 (court / session) · break off: 突然单方面中断交涉 (negotiations / relations / engagement) · stand down: 解除戒备状态或走下证人席 (troops / alerts / witness)

groups.name: Sustain & Uphold · 维持与支撑 (Sustain, Maintain, Uphold)
groups.tip: 持续供给能量维持状态

items.def_en: To continue to do something at the same brisk pace, quality, or standard
items.ex_en: The marathon leader struggled valiantly to keep up the relentless four-minute mile pace.
items.ex_zh: 马拉松领跑者奋力支撑，以期保持住四分钟一英里的强劲配速。

items.def_en: To cause something to continue at the same level, standard, or state without declining
items.ex_en: The facility relies on backup generators to maintain sterile cleanroom conditions during blackouts.
items.ex_zh: 该设施依靠备用发电机在停电期间维持无菌洁净室的状态。

items.def_zh: 维持，保持；支撑，供养；遭受，蒙受（损失、伤亡）
items.def_en: 1. To support, maintain, or nourish something over time. 2. To experience or suffer damage, injury, or loss
items.ex_en: The isolated garrison could barely sustain defensive operations without fresh ammunition supplies.
items.ex_zh: 如果没有新的弹药补给，这支孤立的驻军几乎无法维持防御行动。

items.def_en: To make something last for a longer period of time than expected
items.ex_en: The defense attorney filed multiple appeals specifically intended to prolong the litigation process.
items.ex_zh: 辩护律师提出了多项申诉，专门意在拖长整个诉讼程序。

items.def_en: To support, maintain, or defend a principle, decision, or law against challenge
items.ex_en: The Supreme Court voted unanimously to uphold the constitutionality of the landmark statute.
items.ex_zh: 最高法院一致投票支持维持该具有里程碑意义之法案的合宪性判决。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame emphasize continuously providing the energy, resources, legal backing, or effort needed to prevent an ongoing condition or level from dropping.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重持续提供力量、资源或支持以维系既有状态。
groups.desc_en: Denotes imparting continuous energy, moral commitment, or structural force to prevent collapse or degradation, differing from mere 'holding' through its endurance against ongoing strain.
groups.desc_zh: 指持续注入力量、道德承诺或资源以支撑某事物不致坍塌或衰退，与被动的“握持”相比，突出对抗消耗与重压的坚守。
groups.nuance_en: keep up: maintain continuous pace or active standard against fatigue (appearances / momentum / pace) · maintain: preserve an existing state, system, or assertion continuously (order / standards / innocence) · sustain: bear up under heavy burden or provide life-giving continuity (damage / life / growth) · prolong: artificially extend the temporal duration of something (life / agony / negotiations) · uphold: defend, validate, or legally confirm a principle or decision (ruling / tradition / constitution)
groups.nuance_zh: keep up: 咬牙保持步调或水准 (appearances / momentum / pace) · maintain: 持续维护系统、秩序或声称 (order / standards / innocence) · sustain: 承受重荷或注入维生资源 (damage / life / growth) · prolong: 在时间跨度上人为拖长或延续 (life / agony / negotiations) · uphold: 捍卫、支持或确认合法性 (ruling / tradition / constitution)

groups.name: Sway & Oscillate · 侧仰摇晃与摇曳 (Totter, Reel, Teeter, Billow)
groups.tip: 前后或左右规律摆动

items.def_zh: 摇摆，晃动；动摇，左右（看法或决定）
items.def_en: 1. To move slowly from side to side or back and forth. 2. To persuade or influence someone to change their mind or opinions.
items.ex_en: Tall birch trees began to sway rhythmically in the rising evening wind.
items.ex_zh: 高耸的桦树在渐起的晚风中开始有节奏地左右晃动。
items.ex2_en: Skillful persuasive rhetoric did not sway the stubborn jury members during deliberations.
items.ex2_zh: 在审议期间，巧妙且有说服力的言辞并未动摇固执的陪审员。

items.def_en: To quiver, sway, or flicker gently instead of remaining upright and steady
items.ex_en: The candle flame started to waver as a sudden cold draft invaded the hallway.
items.ex_zh: 随着一阵冷风灌入走廊，烛火开始颤晃不定地摇曳。

items.def_en: To sway unsteadily or move balance-wise as if on the verge of toppling over
items.ex_en: The precarious stack of porcelain plates began to teeter dangerously near the edge.
items.ex_zh: 边缘处那一摞岌岌可危的瓷盘开始危险地晃动起来，摇摇欲坠。

items.def_en: To move or stand in a feeble, unsteady manner, swaying from weakness
items.ex_en: The elderly gentleman began to totter unsteadily across the uneven cobblestone courtyard.
items.ex_zh: 老绅士步履蹒跚、颤巍巍地穿过了凹凸不平的鹅卵石庭院。

items.def_en: To walk, sway, or spin out of control due to dizziness, shock, or heavy intoxication
items.ex_en: Struck forcefully on the chin, the heavyweight boxer began to reel toward the ropes.
items.ex_zh: 下巴遭到重击后，重量级拳击手头晕目眩地踉跄着倒向边绳。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures ungrounded, rhythmic, or unsteady side-to-side tilting of tall upright structures, intoxicated individuals, or windblown foliage.
groups.summary_zh: 描绘高耸物体在风中摇曳，或人醉酒失衡时缓慢左右倾晃。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses unsteady, rhythmic, or ungrounded physical rocking and tilting indicative of lost equilibrium or yielding flexibility, contrasting with steady self-propelled movement.
groups.desc_zh: 描述身体或物体失去平稳、前后左右摆动或倾斜的状态，反映出平衡的丧失或顺风摆荡，与稳定自主的运动形成对照。
groups.nuance_en: sway: move smoothly and rhythmically side to side (trees / hips / crowd) · waver: flicker or shake erratically with indecision or fading strength (light / flame / resolve) · teeter: balance precariously on the brink of falling or tipping (edge / brink / high heels) · totter: walk or stand with feeble, shaking, unstable steps (steps / regime / empire) · reel: stagger wildly backwards or sideways from shock or dizziness (shock / blow / drunken stupor)
groups.nuance_zh: sway: 规律柔和地左右摇曳 (trees / hips / crowd) · waver: 摇曳不定、因虚弱或迟疑而晃动 (light / flame / resolve) · teeter: 在边缘摇摇欲坠、岌岌可危 (edge / brink / high heels) · totter: 踉跄蹒跚、基座动摇 (steps / regime / empire) · reel: 因打击或眩晕而步履踉跄、天旋地转 (shock / blow / drunken stupor)

groups.name: Swear & Pledge · 发誓与立誓 (Plight, Pledge, Vow)
groups.tip: 庄严起誓并订立承诺保单

items.def_en: to affirm the truth or one's intention by taking an oath, often invoking God or truth
items.ex_en: The incoming prime minister must swear an oath of allegiance before taking office.
items.ex_zh: 候任首相在就职前必须庄严宣誓效忠。

items.def_en: to formally commit oneself or one's resources to a cause, duty, or individual
items.ex_en: Wealthy industrial philanthropists pledged millions of dollars to clean energy research initiatives.
items.ex_zh: 富有的实业慈善家们立誓保证为清洁能源研究项目资助数百万美元。

items.def_en: to make a serious, deeply personal promise with sacred or solemn intent
items.ex_en: The young knight knelt silently before the altar to vow perpetual chastity.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的骑士静静地跪在祭坛前，立下终身守贞的庄严誓言。

items.def_zh: 发誓保证，立誓许婚（尤用于 plight one's troth）
items.def_en: (archaic or literary) To solemnly pledge or promise (one's faith or loyalty), especially in marriage.
items.ex_en: Under the ancient oaks, the young lovers chose to plight their troth forever.
items.ex_zh: 古老的橡树下，年轻的情侣立誓许婚，许下永恒的山盟海誓。

items.def_zh: 使自身受约束，订立死约
items.def_en: to place oneself under an unbreakable moral, legal, or verbal obligation
items.ex_en: By signing the covenant, the founding members bind themselves to mutual defense obligations.
items.ex_zh: 签署盟约即意味着创始成员国使自身受相互防务义务的严格法律约束。

groups.summary_en: Denotes making binding, grave commitments to a cause, person, or principle, ranging from formal contractual promises to sanctified oaths invoking divine or moral duty.
groups.summary_zh: 指以名誉、信仰或庄严誓词作出具有约束力与道德重量的承诺。
groups.desc_en: Signifies binding oneself to an inviolable obligation, truth, or cause by invocation of sacred witness or formal commitment, differing from informal promises through solemnity and moral jeopardy.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过神明见证或庄严承诺将自身与不可推卸的责任、誓言绑缚在一起，与日常“允诺”相比，具有极高的严肃性与背誓代价。
groups.nuance_en: swear: bind oneself under formal oath or divine invocation to tell truth or perform duty (allegiance / secrecy / oath) · vow: dedicate oneself solemnly and passionately to a religious or moral aim (poverty / vengeance / eternal love) · pledge: offer a solemn formal guarantee, often accompanied by security or public commitment (support / loyalty / funds) · plight: solemnly offer or bind one's faith or marital promise (troth / faith) · bind oneself: incur an inescapable legal or ethical duty deliberately (contract / oath)
groups.nuance_zh: swear: 郑重宣誓效忠或起誓求真 (allegiance / secrecy / oath) · vow: 立下神圣宏愿或誓言 (poverty / vengeance / eternal love) · pledge: 公开庄严质押或承诺 (support / loyalty / funds) · plight: 郑重许诺婚约或誓约 (troth / faith) · bind oneself: 使自身受法律或道德死契约束 (contract / oath)

groups.name: Sweat & Exude · 出汗与分泌 (Perspire, Exude, Secrete)
groups.tip: 腺体分泌体液或冒出汗水

items.def_zh: 出汗，流汗；渗出水汽；焦虑，担忧；努力工作
items.def_en: 1. To produce liquid through your skin because you are hot, ill, or nervous. 2. (informal) To worry or feel anxious about something. 3. To work very hard.
items.ex_en: Nervous students began to sweat profusely in the unventilated, sweltering examination hall.
items.ex_zh: 在闷热不通风的考场里，紧张的学生们开始大量出汗。

items.def_en: To flow out very slowly through small openings or cracks like a thick liquid
items.ex_en: Thick black crude oil started to ooze steadily from the ruptured pipeline seam.
items.ex_zh: 黏稠的黑色原油开始从破裂的管道焊缝中缓缓渗出。
items.ex2_en: The damaged storage barrel slowly oozed toxic chemical liquid onto the concrete.
items.ex2_zh: 受损的储存桶将有毒化学液体缓缓渗出到混凝土上。

items.def_en: (of a gland or organism) To produce and discharge a substance, such as saliva, hormones, or venom
items.ex_en: Specialized endocrine cells secrete essential hormones directly into the bloodstream during stress.
items.ex_zh: 特化的内分泌细胞在应激期间将必需的激素直接分泌到血液中。

items.def_en: To release or ooze a liquid, substance, or distinct smell slowly and steadily through pores
items.ex_en: Damaged pine bark begins to exude a thick, aromatic resin to heal itself.
items.ex_zh: 受损的松树皮开始渗出一种浓稠且芳香的树脂以自我修复。

items.def_en: To secrete sweat through the pores of the skin (more polite or medical than sweat)
items.ex_en: Patients undergoing intense physical examinations often perspire profusely despite cool room temperatures.
items.ex_zh: 尽管室内温度偏低，接受高强度体检的患者仍常常大量出汗。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the biological, physiological, or metaphorical release of fluids (like sweat, moisture, or odor) through the skin, glands, or surfaces. They span clinical secretion to visceral sweating.
groups.summary_zh: 指人体、腺体或物体表面分泌出水分、汗液或汁液。
groups.desc_en: Portrays the physiological or physical discharge of moisture or liquid through pores or surface boundaries, differing from mere leaking by involving biological exertion or organic pressure.
groups.desc_zh: 描绘水分或汁液通过毛孔、膜或组织表层被挤压或分泌排出的物理/生理过程，与机械渗漏不同，多涉及有机体的代谢或压力。
groups.nuance_en: sweat: emit saline moisture through the skin due to heat, effort, or fear (fever / palms / brow) · perspire: emit sweat (euphemistic or formal medical register) (heavily / forehead) · exude: discharge moisture, resin, or charisma steadily across a surface (sap / confidence / moisture) · ooze: slowly and viscosity-laden trickle out of a fissure (pus / mud / blood) · secrete: organically generate and release a functional substance internally or externally (hormones / enzymes / venom)
groups.nuance_zh: sweat: 因热、劳累或紧张而流汗 (fever / palms / brow) · perspire: [雅称/医学] 出汗、排汗 (heavily / forehead) · exude: 慢慢渗出汁液，或由内而外散发气质 (sap / confidence / moisture) · ooze: 稠厚液体缓慢渗流 (pus / mud / blood) · secrete: 有机体分泌生理活性物质 (hormones / enzymes / venom)

groups.name: Sweeten & Enrich Palate · 加糖与增甜 (Sweeten, Sugar, Honey)
groups.tip: 增添风味甜意，改善食物口感

items.def_en: To add sugar to food or drink to make it sweeter, or to sprinkle sugar over a surface
items.ex_en: She lightly sugared the freshly baked pastries before presenting them to guests.
items.ex_zh: 在将新鲜出炉的点心端给客人之前，她在表面轻轻撒了一层糖。

items.def_en: To sweeten food or drink with honey, or to coat with a sweet glaze
items.ex_en: He honeys his chamomile tea every evening to soothe his dry throat.
items.ex_zh: 他每天晚上都在洋甘菊茶里加点蜂蜜，以缓解喉咙干痛。

items.def_en: To make food sweeter, or figuratively to flatter someone to make them more compliant
items.ex_en: They tried to sweeten up the landlord before asking for another lease extension.
items.ex_zh: 他们在提出再次续租之前，试图讨好一下房东。

items.def_en: To preserve or coat fruit or confectionery in heavy boiling sugar or syrup
items.ex_en: The confectioner candified ripe citrus peel in heavy boiling syrup for holiday treats.
items.ex_zh: 糖果师将成熟的柑橘皮浸入浓稠沸腾的糖浆中制成蜜饯，作为节日美点。

items.def_zh: 使变甜，加糖于；使更具吸引力，使变温和；变甜
items.def_en: 1. To make food, drink, or substances sweeter by adding sugar or sweetener, or to become sweet. 2. To make a deal, offer, or condition more attractive or favorable.
items.ex_en: You can sweeten the tart blackberry sauce with a spoonful of raw sugar.
items.ex_zh: 你可以加一勺原糖来增加这道微酸黑莓酱的甜味。
items.ex2_en: Ripe summer peaches sweeten noticeably as warm sunshine bathes the orchard daily.
items.ex2_zh: 随着温暖的阳光每日洒满果园，成熟的夏桃明显变甜了。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame center on adding sucrose, honey, or artificial sweeteners to consumables to augment sweetness, mellow harsh bitterness, or metonymically make conditions more alluring or palatable.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过加糖增甘，中和苦涩滋味，亦引申为使条件更具诱惑力。
groups.desc_en: Entails the culinary or metaphorical addition of saccharine substances or agreeable traits to soften harshness or enhance sensory appeal, contrasting with baseline flavoring by focusing solely on sweetness.
groups.desc_zh: 涉及在烹饪或修辞中加入糖分或宜人元素，以中和苦涩或提升愉悦感，与泛泛的调味不同，专指增甜与软化。
groups.nuance_en: sweeten: make sweet by adding sugar or making terms more agreeable (tea / deal / pot) · sweeten up: flatter or appease someone before making a demand (boss / committee) · sugar: coat or mix directly with refined sugar (strawberries / pill) · honey: sweeten with honey or coat with excessive flattery (words / tea / tone) · candify: preserve or crystallize completely in heavy sugar (fruit / peel)
groups.nuance_zh: sweeten: 加糖变甜，或修饰条款以使人容易接受 (tea / deal / pot) · sweeten up: [口]预先讨好谄媚以图方便 (boss / committee) · sugar: 撒白糖或给苦口良药加糖衣 (strawberries / pill) · honey: 加蜂蜜增甜，或言辞极度甜言蜜语 (words / tea / tone) · candify: 制成蜜饯或使之结晶糖化 (fruit / peel)

groups.name: Swelter & Suffer Heat · 酷热难耐与受暑熬 (Swelter, Roast, Sweat it out)
groups.tip: 受暑热中暑煎熬痛苦

items.def_zh: 忍受酷热煎熬；耐着性子熬过
items.def_en: To endure a period of oppressive heat or tense waiting until it passes
items.ex_en: With the air conditioner broken, we had to sweat it out until evening.
items.ex_zh: 空调坏了，我们只得耐着性子在酷热中熬到晚上。

items.def_zh: 被晒得发烫，受干热炙烤
items.def_en: To become intensely hot and dry under direct sun or strong heat
items.ex_en: The red clay roof tiles baked relentlessly under the scorching afternoon sun.
items.ex_zh: 红色的黏土瓦在午后炙热的阳光下被烤得滚烫。
items.ex2_en: The relentless summer sun baked the dry cracked mud along the riverbank.
items.ex2_zh: 无情的夏日骄阳将河岸上干裂的泥土烤得滚烫。

items.def_zh: 闷热受熬；在湿热中受罪
items.def_en: To swelter or feel uncomfortably hot and humid, especially in an enclosed space
items.ex_en: Dozens of frustrated commuters stewed inside the stalled, unventilated subway car for hours.
items.ex_zh: 数十名沮丧的通勤者在停滞且不通风的地铁车厢里湿热难耐地熬了几个小时。

items.def_en: 1. To feel uncomfortably, oppressively hot and sweat excessively.
items.ex_en: The farmworkers sweltered in the humid midday heat while harvesting the summer corn.
items.ex_zh: 农工们在潮湿闷热的中午采收夏玉米，热得极为难受。

items.def_zh: 感到极度烘热，热得受不了
items.def_en: To feel uncomfortably and excessively hot, as if being baked in an oven
items.ex_en: We were absolutely roasting in the crowded attic without any fans or ventilation.
items.ex_zh: 我们待在没有任何风扇或通风设施的拥挤阁楼里，简直热得受不了。
items.ex2_en: The fierce desert sun roasted the unprepared travelers throughout their long hike.
items.ex2_zh: 在漫长的徒步旅行中，烈日灼烤着毫无准备的旅行者。

groups.summary_en: Verbs describing suffering from intense, oppressive heat and sweating profusely. They range from natural physiological responses to figurative expressions of baking or stewing in high temperatures.
groups.summary_zh: 描述人体遭受酷暑炙烤、闷热难耐乃至挥汗如雨的生理与主观体验。
groups.desc_en: Depicts passive physical distress and oppressive suffering under intense ambient heat and humidity, differing from active warming by emphasizing acute bodily exhaustion and trapped discomfort.
groups.desc_zh: 表现身体暴露在极端高温潮湿环境下所忍受的难熬煎熬，与舒适的取暖不同，突出窒息感、折磨感与体力耗竭。
groups.nuance_en: swelter: suffer intense, humid, airless heat helplessness (passengers / residents / heatwave) · roast: endure blistering, direct, dry heat intensely (sun / fire / kitchen) · bake: be subjected to prolonged dry, oven-like ambient heat (desert / pavement / attic) · stew: endure stifling, damp heat, often with mounting agitation (sweat / traffic) · sweat it out: endure a grueling, sweltering ordeal until the finish (fever / heatwave / waiting period)
groups.nuance_zh: swelter: 在闷热潮湿中汗流浃背、苦不堪言 (passengers / residents / heatwave) · roast: 如置火烤般受烈日炙烤 (sun / fire / kitchen) · bake: 如置烤箱般受持续干热炙烤 (desert / pavement / attic) · stew: 处于湿热难耐环境中，或急躁熬受 (sweat / traffic) · sweat it out: 熬过高温发汗或咬牙挨过难关 (fever / heatwave / waiting period)

groups.name: Swing & Whiff · 挥空与抡击 (Swing and miss, Slash, Flail)
groups.tip: 手臂或器物划出弧线挥击

items.def_zh: 挥空，未击中（球）；轻轻地吹，喷气；吸入，闻到
items.def_en: 1. (baseball) To swing at a pitch and miss completely; to strike out. 2. To blow or puff lightly; to smell or sniff slightly.
items.ex_en: The rookie swung hard at the final slider and whiffed to end the game.
items.ex_zh: 这名新秀对着最后一记滑球大力挥棒却彻底挥空，结束了比赛。

items.def_en: To move or wave an object through the air with a soft, swift hissing or whistling sound
items.ex_en: The fencing instructor swished her foil through the crisp morning air with precision.
items.ex_zh: 击剑教练在清晨清冽的空气中精准地将花剑挥舞得嗖嗖作响。
items.ex2_en: The silk curtain swished softly across the wooden floor in the breeze.
items.ex2_zh: 丝绸窗帘在微风中拂过木地板，发出沙沙的响声。

items.def_en: To make a forceful sweeping motion with a bat or arm to hit something but entirely miss contact
items.ex_en: The batter swung and missed at a deceptive fastball right over the plate.
items.ex_zh: 击球手对着正中本垒的欺骗性快速球挥棒，却完全击空。

items.def_en: To wave or swing one's arms or implements wildly, erratically, and without control
items.ex_en: The drowning swimmer flailed his arms frantically before the attentive lifeguard reached him.
items.ex_zh: 溺水者慌乱地胡乱挥舞双臂，随后警惕的救生员赶到了他身边。
items.ex2_en: Broken electrical cables flailed wildly across the flooded street during the storm.
items.ex2_zh: 暴风雨中，断裂的电缆在被水淹没的街道上狂乱地甩动。

items.def_en: To swing a blade, whip, or implement with wide, sweeping cuts through the air or across a surface
items.ex_en: The explorer slashed his heavy machete through the thick undergrowth along the trail.
items.ex_zh: 探险家挥动沉重的大砍刀，在小径旁茂密的下层灌木丛中劈开一条路。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses swinging a bat, blade, club, or limb aggressively through the air, often culminating in missing the intended target or whistling harmlessly through empty space. 'Whiff' represents the air-cutting sound of a strikeout or miss, whereas 'flail' connotes wild, uncontrolled swinging.
groups.summary_zh: 指挥动器械或手臂在空中猛抡，常伴随挥空或带起风声。
groups.desc_en: Highlights the aggressive or erratic swinging of an implement or limb that completely fails to connect with its intended target, contrasting with an effective 'hit' or 'strike'.
groups.desc_zh: 强调手持器械或肢体大力抡舞挥击却完全未能触及预定目标的动作，与有效的“击中”相对，突出力落空处与空气摩擦感。
groups.nuance_en: whiff: swing and strike only air without contact (strike three / fastball / pitch) · swing and miss: complete an intentional swing that totally bypasses the target (fastball / opportunity) · slash: deliver sweeping, violent cutting strokes through air or surface (undergrowth / budget / tires) · flail: wave or swing arms or implements wildly and erratically (limbs / arms / helpless) · swish: sweep or flick through the air with a distinct rustling or hissing sound (cane / tail / skirts)
