items.def_en: to dare to undertake a risky enterprise or put forward a tentative thought or attempt
items.ex_en: None dared venture an objection before the imperious decree of the sovereign.
items.ex_zh: 在君王专横的法令面前，无人敢提出异议。

items.def_en: to commit oneself to and begin executing a complex or demanding project or task
items.ex_en: The consortium will undertake a comprehensive feasibility study for the railway project.
items.ex_zh: 该财团将对铁路项目着手进行全面的可行性研究。

items.def_en: (+ to do) to make a strenuous and determined effort to accomplish something difficult
items.ex_en: We must endeavor to reconcile these conflicting demands before the final deadline.
items.ex_zh: 我们必须竭力在最后截止日期前调和这些冲突的诉求。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses deliberate, often tentative or demanding efforts to execute a difficult enterprise, test an idea, or probe one's limits.
groups.summary_zh: 指审慎试探、敢于承接艰巨任务或尝试未知行动。
groups.desc_en: To make a tentative, exploratory, or modest attempt at a challenging endeavor, contrasting with confident, routine execution.
groups.desc_zh: 对艰巨或不确定的事项进行摸索性、试探性或谦恭的尝试，区别于胸有成竹的按部就班。
groups.nuance_en: have a stab: make an informal or inexperienced try at a difficult task (at the puzzle / at cooking) · essay: make an earnest, measured attempt at an arduous challenge (task / leap / explanation) · venture: dare to tentatively offer or attempt something requiring audacity (opinion / remark / step) · undertake: formally agree to take upon oneself an extensive, solemn task (project / voyage / study) · endeavor: strive persistently and conscientiously toward a noble or difficult goal (to resolve / to succeed)
groups.nuance_zh: have a stab: 抱着试一试的心态做非正式尝试 (at the puzzle / at cooking) · essay: 谨慎而庄重地试图克服艰巨考验 (task / leap / explanation) · venture: 战战兢兢或试探性地抛出观点、迈出一步 (opinion / remark / step) · undertake: 郑重接下并着手承担某项宏大任务 (project / voyage / study) · endeavor: 竭尽全力、克尽厥职地朝目标努力 (to resolve / to succeed)

groups.name: Verbalize & Voice Feelings · 语言表达与说出 (Voice, Put into words, Express)
groups.tip: 将内心感受用准确言辞表述出来

items.def_en: To give verbal utterance or public expression to concerns, feelings, or objections
items.ex_en: Several residents rose to voice their concerns about the planned highway expansion.
items.ex_zh: 几位居民起身对拟建的公路扩建工程表达了担忧。

items.def_en: To show, depict, or convey a thought, opinion, or emotion using words, looks, or actions
items.ex_en: She struggled to express her profound gratitude to the doctors who saved her.
items.ex_zh: 她竭力向救她性命的医生们表达自己由衷的感激。

items.def_en: To express something complex, intangible, or deeply felt in explicit spoken or written language
items.ex_en: He found it impossible to put his overwhelming grief into words.
items.ex_zh: 他发现自己无法用言语表达那排山倒海般的悲痛。

items.def_en: To give one's opinions freely, honestly, and boldly, especially in defense or protest
items.ex_en: Activists took to the streets to speak out against human rights abuses.
items.ex_zh: 活动人士走上街头，大声疾呼反对侵犯人权的行为。

items.def_en: 1. To express thoughts, feelings, or ideas in spoken or written words.
items.ex_en: The therapist encouraged the patient to verbalize his suppressed childhood anxieties.
items.ex_zh: 心理治疗师鼓励患者用言语表达出他压抑已久的童年焦虑。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses translating internal sentiments, abstract ideas, or bodily pain into externalized spoken or written language. The focus is on finding words to make the internal intelligible.
groups.summary_zh: 将内心的感受、思绪或直觉转化成言辞表达出来。
groups.desc_en: To translate internal mental states, convictions, or grievances into spoken or written words, contrasting with non-verbal feeling or concealment.
groups.desc_zh: 将内心的思绪、立场或委屈转化宣之于文字与口语，区别于非语言宣泄或隐忍不言。
groups.nuance_en: voice: express publicly a specific concern, opinion, or objection (concerns / doubts / objections) · express: articulate feelings or ideas outwardly through words or deeds (feelings / gratitude / views) · put into words: successfully formulate elusive or deep feelings into spoken language (grief / gratitude / feelings) · speak out: declare an opinion publicly and courageously against an injustice (against injustice / on the issue) · verbalize: systematically render inner thoughts or symptoms into explicit spoken terms (emotions / thoughts / problems)
groups.nuance_zh: voice: 公开表达忧虑、异议或群众心声 (concerns / doubts / objections) · express: 将主观情绪与观念传达表露于外 (feelings / gratitude / views) · put into words: 准确将难以名状的感触提炼成言辞 (grief / gratitude / feelings) · speak out: 挺身而出、毫不避讳地公开发声抗争 (against injustice / on the issue) · verbalize: 将抽象思想或内在症状用系统语言述说 (emotions / thoughts / problems)

groups.name: Verge & Border On · 临近与濒临 (Verge, Border, Teeter)
groups.tip: 逐渐接近边缘或临界点

items.def_en: To stay close to a particular value, level, or boundary without decisively crossing it
items.ex_en: The company's stock price continues to hover around fifty dollars per share.
items.ex_zh: 该公司的股票价格继续在每股五十美元左右徘徊。

items.def_zh: 近似，濒临（某种极端状态）
items.def_en: To come very close to being an extreme state, quality, or condition
items.ex_en: His reckless driving habits border on outright madness during rush hour traffic.
items.ex_zh: 他在高峰时段鲁莽的驾驶习惯简直近乎彻底的发疯。

items.def_en: To lie along the outer edge of something or come close to touching a controversial line
items.ex_en: The controversial new policy seems to skirt the limits of constitutional law.
items.ex_zh: 这项备受争议的新政策似乎险触宪法的底线边缘。

items.def_zh: 濒临，临近；接近（某种状态）
items.def_en: (also 'verge on') To come close to or be on the brink of reaching a particular state or condition.
items.ex_en: Her persistent exhaustion began to verge on a severe chronic physical collapse.
items.ex_zh: 她持续的疲劳开始濒临严重的慢性身体崩溃。

items.def_en: To stand or balance precariously on the brink of disaster or extreme change
items.ex_en: The unstable regime continues to teeter on the brink of total collapse.
items.ex_zh: 这个不稳定的政权继续在彻底崩溃的边缘摇摇欲坠。

items.def_en: To border physically or approach very closely to a particular condition, state, or limit
items.ex_en: The reckless financial speculation began to verge on blatant fraud as debts mounted without control.
items.ex_zh: 随着债务失控攀升，这种不计后果的金融投机开始濒临明目张胆的诈骗。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame express being closely adjacent to an extreme, perilous, or decisive state, often indicating a precarious threshold before a complete transition.
groups.summary_zh: 指空间或状态上极度贴近、濒临某种临界点。
groups.desc_en: To come extremely close to an extreme, disastrous, or categorical threshold, contrasting with staying comfortably within safe bounds.
groups.desc_zh: 极其逼近某种极端境况、质变界限或危险临界点，区别于处在安全幅度之内。
groups.nuance_en: hover around: fluctuate closely nearby a specific numeric point or state (freezing / sixty percent / mark) · border on: come perilously close to an extreme or unacceptable quality (insanity / absurdity / treason) · skirt: move along the outer edge without directly crossing into it (the edge / disaster / topic) · verge: approach so near a threshold that entry is imminent (on ruin / on tears / on collapse) · teeter on: balance precariously on the brink of catastrophic failure (the brink / the edge / collapse)
groups.nuance_zh: hover around: 在特定数值或状态附近上下微幅盘旋 (freezing / sixty percent / mark) · border on: 逼近极端或不可接受的质变边缘 (insanity / absurdity / treason) · skirt: 沿边界掠过、刻意避开核心实质 (the edge / disaster / topic) · verge: 极度贴近某种濒危状态的关口 (on ruin / on tears / on collapse) · teeter on: 在灾难倾覆边缘岌岌可危地晃荡 (the brink / the edge / collapse)

groups.name: Violent Cleaving & Sundering · 强力撕裂与劈开 (Sunder, Sever, Rend)
groups.tip: 彻底切断关联使之两隔

items.def_en: Break or cause to break into numerous sharp, thin, and jagged fragments
items.ex_en: The wooden mast began to splinter violently under the hurricane's relentless force.
items.ex_zh: 在飓风无情的摧残下，木质桅杆开始剧烈裂成碎片。
items.ex2_en: The powerful explosion splintered the sturdy wooden barricades into tiny jagged pieces.
items.ex2_zh: 剧烈的爆炸将坚固的木制路障炸成了锋利细碎的碎片。

items.def_en: Divide or cut something cleanly or forcibly into distinct parts, or end a relationship abruptly
items.ex_en: The ambassador was instructed to sever all diplomatic ties with the regime.
items.ex_zh: 大使接到指令，切断与该政权的所有外交关系。

items.def_en: (literary) To split, tear, or break apart violently into two or more parts.
items.ex_en: A bitter ideological divide threatened to sunder the kingdom into warring factions.
items.ex_zh: 激烈的意识形态分歧势要将这个王国彻底撕裂成交战的派系。
items.ex2_en: The ancient rock sundered completely under the sudden, violent geological stress.
items.ex2_zh: 在突然而剧烈的地质压力下，那块古老的岩石彻底裂开了。

items.def_en: Split or sever something along a natural grain or with a sharp, heavy blow
items.ex_en: With one mighty stroke, the executioner's axe cleaved the timber in twain.
items.ex_zh: 刽子手的巨斧猛力一挥，将木料一劈两半。
items.ex2_en: The brittle limestone will cleave cleanly when struck with an iron chisel.
items.ex2_zh: 用铁凿敲击时，脆弱的石灰岩会整齐地劈开。

items.def_en: Tear something violently and brutally apart into two or more pieces
items.ex_en: Fierce sorrow seemed to rend her very soul as she wept uncontrollably.
items.ex_zh: 当她失声痛哭时，剧烈的悲伤似乎猛扯撕裂着她的灵魂。

groups.summary_en: Elevated or literary verbs describing severe, traumatic, and violent parting, splitting, or dividing of physical bodies, bonds, or territories into separate pieces.
groups.summary_zh: 多具文雅或戏剧色彩，指施加暴力使物体、肢体或关系彻底断绝、劈开。
groups.desc_en: To split, tear, or dismember an object with violent physical force or extreme trauma, contrasting with gentle incision or orderly parting.
groups.desc_zh: 施加暴烈外力将物体崩解、劈裂或强行撕断，区别于平滑切割或柔和的分离。
groups.nuance_en: splinter: break or fragment violently into thin, sharp shards (wood / bone / faction) · sever: cut completely through a connection, limb, or bond with sharp force (rope / limb / ties) · sunder: tear apart into separate pieces with cataclysmic or tragic force (kingdom / soul / bonds) · cleave: split sharply along a natural fissure or divide cleanly through (rock / wood / air) · rend: tear violently apart by pulling or ripping (garments / flesh / fabric)
groups.nuance_zh: splinter: 爆裂或崩解成尖锐细碎的碎屑 (wood / bone / faction) · sever: 利落地斩断肢体、绳索或切断关系 (rope / limb / ties) · sunder: 以灾难性巨力使整体四分五裂、生离死别 (kingdom / soul / bonds) · cleave: 沿劈理顺势劈开坚硬之物，或破空穿行 (rock / wood / air) · rend: 粗暴撕扯布帛、肌肉撕开裂口 (garments / flesh / fabric)

groups.name: Wade & Tramp · 涉水与泥行 (Wade, Splash, Slosh)
groups.tip: 在泥水水坑中踩踏前行

items.def_en: To move through liquid causing drops to fly noisily about
items.ex_en: The children laughed as they began to splash through the shallow fountain.
items.ex_zh: 孩子们笑着开始踩着浅水喷泉，水花四溅作响。
items.ex2_en: Speeding cars splash dirty puddle water all over careless pedestrians nearby.
items.ex2_zh: 疾驰的汽车把水坑里的脏水溅到了附近粗心的行人身上。

items.def_en: To walk with effort through shallow water, mud, or deep liquid
items.ex_en: We had to wade through knee-deep swamp water to reach dry land.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不吃力地蹚过齐膝深的沼泽水才到达陆地。

items.def_en: To walk barefoot in shallow water for leisure or pleasure
items.ex_en: The tourists loved to paddle barefoot along the cool edge of the surf.
items.ex_zh: 游客们喜欢赤脚沿着清凉的海浪边缘涉浅水漫步。

items.def_zh: 在水坑（或泥水）中践踏；把（黏土）捣制成胶土
items.def_en: 1. to splash, dabble, or tramp about in muddy water or shallow puddles 2. to work wet clay into a dense, watertight lining
items.ex_en: The barefoot boys continued to puddle through the muddy lane after rain.
items.ex_zh: 雨后，赤脚的男孩们继续在泥泞的小巷水坑里踩水嬉戏。

items.def_zh: 在烂泥/水中吧唧吧唧地走
items.def_en: To splash clumsily through water, slush, or mud while walking
items.ex_en: We had to slosh through freezing slush to get to the station.
items.ex_zh: 我们不得不吧唧吧唧地踩着冰冷的雪泥赶往车站。
items.ex2_en: The careless waiter sloshed hot soup all over the white tablecloth.
items.ex2_zh: 粗心的服务员把热汤洒得满白桌布都是。

groups.summary_en: Captures the act of walking or splashing through shallow water, mud, or wet substances where footing meets fluid resistance.
groups.summary_zh: 在浅水、淤泥或积水中艰难踩踏、涉行或戏水。
groups.desc_en: To walk with effort through water, mud, or thick resistant liquid that impedes normal foot movement, contrasting with free running or swimming.
groups.desc_zh: 在水流、泥泞或具阻力的液体中艰难涉足前行，区别于平地奔跑或悬浮游泳。
groups.nuance_en: splash: strike and scatter water noisily while moving (through puddles / water / waves) · wade: walk with physical effort through waist- or knee-deep resistant water or mud (across the river / through mud) · paddle: walk leisurely with bare feet in shallow water (in the sea / along the shore) · puddle: dabble or wade messily through shallow puddles of muddy water (around / in the rain) · slosh: trudge through wet, muddy, or slushy terrain with a squelching sound (through mud / across snow / in boots)
groups.nuance_zh: splash: 涉水时手脚拍击溅射起大片水花 (through puddles / water / waves) · wade: 顶着及膝深水的阻力吃力涉渡 (across the river / through mud) · paddle: 在浅滩赤足嬉水漫步 (in the sea / along the shore) · puddle: 在雨水残洼中邋遢摸索踢踏 (around / in the rain) · slosh: 在泥泞或融雪中踩着黏湿泥浆踏步 (through mud / across snow / in boots)

groups.name: Wag & Oscillate · 摆动与摇晃 (Wiggle, Swish, Wave)
groups.tip: 左右摇摆尾巴晃动

items.def_en: To move one's hand or an object back and forth repeatedly through the air
items.ex_en: The departing passengers began to wave their hands vigorously from the deck.
items.ex_zh: 离港的乘客们开始从甲板上用力挥舞双手告别。

items.def_en: To whip or jerk an animal's tail sharply from side to side
items.ex_en: The restless horse began to switch its tail against the annoying flies.
items.ex_zh: 躁动的马儿开始甩动尾巴抽打恼人的苍蝇。
items.ex2_en: The cat's tail switched nervously back and forth on the rug.
items.ex2_zh: 猫的尾巴在小地毯上不安地甩来甩去。

items.def_en: To make quick, short movements from side to side or up and down
items.ex_en: He could barely wiggle his bruised toes inside the tight hiking boot.
items.ex_zh: 在紧绷的登山靴里，他几乎无法动弹受了淤伤的脚趾。
items.ex2_en: The loose wooden floorboard wiggled whenever anyone walked across the hall.
items.ex2_zh: 每当有人走过走廊，那块松动的木地板就会晃动。

items.def_zh: 摇摆，摇动（尾巴或手指等）
items.def_en: To move rapidly back and forth or up and down, especially of an animal's tail or a finger.
items.ex_en: The friendly golden retriever began to wag its tail at the visitor.
items.ex_zh: 那只友善的金毛寻回犬开始朝来访者欢快地摇尾巴。
items.ex2_en: The dog's bushy tail wagged energetically whenever his owner walked in.
items.ex2_zh: 每当主人走进来，这只狗浓密的尾巴就会兴奋地摇晃。

items.def_en: To move or wave smoothly and quickly through the air, often with a soft hissing sound
items.ex_en: The fencing master made his rapier swish swiftly through the empty air.
items.ex_zh: 击剑大师使出刺剑，在虚空中唰地一声迅疾划过。
items.ex2_en: Her long satin skirt swished softly as she danced across the room.
items.ex2_zh: 当她穿过房间跳舞时，长长的缎面裙摆轻轻作响。

groups.summary_en: Verbs here depict quick, repeated, expressive oscillating movements of appendages, bodily extremities (tails, fingers, hips), or slender flexible tools.
groups.summary_zh: 专指尾巴、手指、枝条或肢体末端轻快且富有表现力的来回摆动。
groups.desc_en: Denotes rapid, rhythmic, or flexible back-and-forth movement of an appendage or slender object, differing from generic oscillation or swinging by its light, brisk, and often expressive or playful nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指附肢或纤细物体轻快、有节奏或灵活的来回摆动，区别于宏观的机械振荡或悬空摆动，带有轻巧、敏捷或表意的特征。
groups.nuance_en: wag: rhythmic sideways flicking, typically of a tail or finger (tail / finger / tongue) · wiggle: small, quick sinuous squirming (toes / hips / worm) · swish: swift whistling or rustling sweep through air or liquid (tail / skirt / cane) · wave: broad undulating or greeting sweep (hand / flag / branch) · switch: sharp, sudden whipping flick (tail / cane / whip)
groups.nuance_zh: wag: 节律性左右摆动，多表轻快或告诫 (tail / finger / tongue) · wiggle: 短促细微的扭动或蠕动 (toes / hips / worm) · swish: 伴随轻微破空声或沙沙声的疾扫 (tail / skirt / cane) · wave: 幅度较大的起伏挥动或招手 (hand / flag / branch) · switch: 尖锐迅疾的抽打式甩动 (tail / cane / whip)

groups.name: Wager & Gamble · 打赌与押注 (Wager, Stake, Punt)
groups.tip: 赌博押注的风险交易

items.def_en: 1. To risk money on the unknown result of an event or competition. 2. To feel confident or certain that something is true or will happen.
items.ex_en: I bet our team will secure the regional championship this coming Saturday.
items.ex_zh: 我敢说我们队会在本周六拿下地区冠军。

items.def_en: To risk money, reputation, or one's future on the success of an enterprise or the outcome of a contest
items.ex_en: The minister decided to stake his political reputation on the tax reform.
items.ex_zh: 部长决定押上自己的政治声誉来推行这项税制改革。

items.def_en: To play games of chance for money, or to take huge speculative chances in hopes of gains
items.ex_en: He chose to gamble his life savings on volatile offshore cryptocurrency markets.
items.ex_zh: 他选择孤注一掷，将一生的积蓄投进波动的离岸加密市场。

items.def_zh: （在赛马等中）下小注；冒险一试
items.def_en: (informal) To bet money on a horse, team, or venture; to take a speculative chance on an unknown
items.ex_en: I took a punt on an obscure startup and earned huge returns.
items.ex_zh: 我冒险投资了一家名不见经传的初创公司，获得了丰厚回报。

items.def_en: To risk an amount of money on a future outcome or competition, formalized under agreed odds
items.ex_en: He offered to wager a substantial sum on the champion's eventual victory.
items.ex_zh: 他提出要在卫冕冠军的最终胜利上下大笔赌注。

groups.summary_en: Involves staking money or value on an uncertain future outcome (sporting matches, dice, cards, or speculative ventures), ranging from formal bookmaking wagers to informal personal challenges.
groups.summary_zh: 以金钱或贵重物对不确定结果进行下注、博弈或立誓赌赛。
groups.desc_en: Focuses on risking material assets or reputation on an uncertain future contingency for speculative gain, contrasting with prudent commercial investing by its reliance on chance and speculative hazard.
groups.desc_zh: 指在结果未卜的情境下押上财物或声誉以博取回报，区别于审慎的商业投资，强调对机遇的投机与风险承担。
groups.nuance_en: bet: standard commitment of money or belief on an outcome (money / race / farm) · wager: formal or deliberate staking on a contest or contingency (sum / fortune / reputation) · stake: risk vital assets or status directly on a venture (career / life / capital) · gamble: take reckless, high-exposure chances (future / savings / fortune) · punt: take a casual or opportunistic speculative shot (stock / company / horse)
groups.nuance_zh: bet: 最常用的立约打赌或日常下注 (money / race / farm) · wager: 正式或深思熟虑的打赌与押注 (sum / fortune / reputation) · stake: 将核心身家或名誉置于险地 (career / life / capital) · gamble: 孤注一掷或鲁莽涉险 (future / savings / fortune) · punt: 英式口语，指带投机性质的偶尔一试或下注 (stock / company / horse)

groups.name: Wager & Gamble · 押注与博彩 (Wager, Gamble, Stake)
groups.tip: 以财物作注博取回报

items.def_en: To bet a specific amount of money or offer odds on an event.
items.ex_en: The bookmaker refused to lay odds against the undefeated local boxing champion.
items.ex_zh: 庄家拒绝为这位未尝败绩的本土拳王开出对抗盘口。

items.def_en: To risk money, one's reputation, or safety on the outcome of a contest or undertaking.
items.ex_en: The explorers were prepared to stake their very lives on the expedition.
items.ex_zh: 探险家们准备押上自己的性命去完成这次远征。

items.def_en: To play games of chance for money, or take risky actions hoping for success.
items.ex_en: Desperate investors often gamble their remaining capital on highly speculative mining stocks.
items.ex_zh: 孤注一掷的投资者往往拿剩余资金去投机性极强的矿业股上豪赌。

items.def_en: (informal/chiefly BrE) To bet money on a race or venture, or take a gamble on an opportunity.
items.ex_en: She decided to punt fifty pounds on an outsider in the race.
items.ex_zh: 她决定花五十英镑在比赛的一匹冷门马上投机一搏。

items.def_zh: 押注，打赌；下赌注于；敢说，确信
items.def_en: 1. (+ on) (formal) To bet an amount of money on the outcome of an unpredictable event or competition. 2. To say or guess with confidence that something is true.
items.ex_en: Few analysts dared to wager on the unpredictable outcome of the referendum.
items.ex_zh: 很少有分析师敢就全民公投难以预测的结果下注断言。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate placing money, assets, or status at hazard upon an uncertain contest, game of chance, or future event in hopes of winning gains.
groups.summary_zh: 在不可预测的结果或赌局中投入资金或资本博取收益。
groups.desc_en: Covers the mechanical and commercial placement of financial stakes upon gaming outcomes, contrasting with metaphorical risk-taking by focusing on the transactional hazarding of money.
groups.desc_zh: 侧重于在博彩、赛马等博弈场景中实际出资押注的交易动作，区别于隐喻性的冒险，强调资金下注的机制行为。
groups.nuance_en: lay: place a direct monetary wager against or on an event (money / odds / bet) · stake: put up funds or possessions to back an outcome (fortune / chips / thousand dollars) · wager: execute a measured gamble on an eventuality (sum / prize / estate) · punt: engage in informal, opportunistic betting (outsider / accumulator / horse) · gamble: systematically play games of chance for stakes (wages / casino / cards)
groups.nuance_zh: lay: 庄家或赌徒开出赔率、垫付下注 (money / odds / bet) · stake: 摆上筹码或重金作为赌资 (fortune / chips / thousand dollars) · wager: 订立赌约并交付赌注 (sum / prize / estate) · punt: 试探性、投机性下注 (outsider / accumulator / horse) · gamble: 沉溺或参与成体系的博彩行为 (wages / casino / cards)

groups.name: Wail & Howl · 哀号与恸哭 (Wail, Howl, Keens)
groups.tip: 由伤心落泪演变为嚎啕大哭

items.def_en: To make a sudden, loud vocalization because of intense pain, fear, or distress
items.ex_en: The injured soldier began to cry out in agony after the blast.
items.ex_zh: 爆炸过后，受伤的士兵开始在极度痛苦中痛呼哀号。

items.def_en: To utter a loud, long, mournful cry in severe pain, grief, or rage
items.ex_en: The bereaved father began to howl in uncontrollable anguish beside the casket.
items.ex_zh: 痛失亲人的父亲在棺木旁难以自抑地号叫恸哭。

items.def_zh: 恸哭，哀号，嚎啕；呼啸，发出长而尖厉的声音
items.def_en: 1. To cry out with a long, high, mournful sound of pain or grief; to utter with wailing. 2. To make a prolonged, high-pitched mournful sound.
items.ex_en: The frightened toddler started to wail loudly when left in the room.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的幼童被留在房间里时开始大声啼哭哀号。

items.def_en: To weep loudly and noisily, typically like a distraught child
items.ex_en: The spoiled boy began to bawl loudly when his toy was taken.
items.ex_zh: 玩具被拿走时，那个被惯坏的男孩开始放声大哭大闹。

items.def_en: To utter a high-pitched, piercing wail in mourning for the dead
items.ex_en: The mourners began to keen beneath the cold drizzle of the cemetery.
items.ex_zh: 送葬者在公墓冰冷的细雨中发出了凄厉的挽歌哭号。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate high-volume, vocalized outpourings of intense agony, mourning, or physical torment characterized by prolonged pitch and vocal strain.
groups.summary_zh: 指伴随高亢尖锐、长声嘶吼的极度痛苦或悲恸呼号。
groups.desc_en: Describes the emission of loud, inarticulate vocalizations driven by intense grief or agony, distinguished from ordinary weeping or shedding tears by sustained acoustic volume and auditory piercingness.
groups.desc_zh: 指因极度悲恸、剧痛而发出的高亢、持久且非语言的号哭，区别于无声落泪或普通啜泣，强调声浪的穿透力与撕裂感。
groups.nuance_en: wail: emit a high-pitched, sustained lamentation (mourner / siren / baby) · howl: produce a prolonged, animalistic, resonant cry of pain (wind / mob / agony) · keen: utter an ancient, piercing, ritualistic dirge for the dead (widow / woman / bereavement) · bawl: yell or weep loudly and unrestrainedly, often childishly (infant / child / lungs) · cry out: release a sudden, involuntary burst of vocal anguish (pain / terror / despair)
groups.nuance_zh: wail: 发出尖厉、冗长、回荡的悲号 (mourner / siren / baby) · howl: 类似野兽狂吠般沉闷深沉的痛嚎 (wind / mob / agony) · keen: 痛失亲人时具有仪式感、撕心裂肺的哀哭 (widow / woman / bereavement) · bawl: 毫无节制地放声大哭或嚎啕 (infant / child / lungs) · cry out: 突发、本能地痛呼或惨叫 (pain / terror / despair)

groups.name: Wait & Tarry · 停留与等待 (Tarry, Linger, Bide, Mark time)
groups.tip: 静止逗留或等待时机

items.def_en: Pass time doing little while waiting for a better opportunity or command to proceed
items.ex_en: The junior diplomats could only mark time while awaiting directives from headquarters.
items.ex_zh: 初级外交官们在等待总部的指令期间只能原地踏步、消极等待。

items.def_en: Stay in a place longer than necessary because one is reluctant to leave
items.ex_en: The guests continued to linger in the garden long after the reception.
items.ex_zh: 招待会结束很久之后，客人们依然在花园里徘徊逗留。

items.def_zh: 等待，等候（时机）；停留，逗留
items.def_en: (especially in 'bide one's time') To wait patiently for a good opportunity to do something.
items.ex_en: The patient strategist decided to bide his time until the enemy advanced.
items.ex_zh: 耐心的谋略家决定静待时机，直到敌人向前推进。

items.def_en: Stay longer than intended, or delay leaving or arriving somewhere
items.ex_en: The weary travelers could not tarry long in the hospitable mountain hamlet.
items.ex_zh: 疲惫的旅人们无法在这个热情好客的山村久留耽搁。

items.def_en: Wait patiently until an unpleasant or stormy event comes to an end
items.ex_en: We took shelter in the abandoned cabin to wait out the blizzard.
items.ex_zh: 我们躲在废弃的小木屋里，耐心等待暴风雪平息。

groups.summary_en: Describes remaining in a place or delaying action instead of proceeding. Nuances highlight patient strategic waiting (biding), leisurely reluctance to depart (lingering), or archaic dilly-dallying (tarrying).
groups.summary_zh: 指停留不走、延迟离开或耐心驻守等待时机成熟。
groups.desc_en: Characterizes non-hasty deferral or intentional pausing in a location or state, contrasting with punctual departure or dynamic progression by deliberate temporal dilation.
groups.desc_zh: 指在某处或某状态下从容驻足、拖延或蓄意搁置，区别于按部就班或仓促启程，体现对时间的消磨、延缓或隐忍。
groups.nuance_en: tarry: delay one's departure; stay leisurely behind (moment / traveler / stranger) · linger: stay reluctantly or persistently as if reluctant to leave (guest / scent / doubt) · bide: wait patiently and watchfully for an opportune moment (time / hour / opportunity) · mark time: pass time aimlessly while waiting for a turn of events (troops / committee / workforce) · wait out: endure the duration of a difficult condition until its end (storm / siege / recession)
groups.nuance_zh: tarry: 文雅或古风用法，迟延不前、流连耽搁 (moment / traveler / stranger) · linger: 依依不舍地徘徊，或事物久久不散 (guest / scent / doubt) · bide: 隐忍自重，静待良机 (time / hour / opportunity) · mark time: 原地踏步，消极等待转机 (troops / committee / workforce) · wait out: 耐心熬过不良局面直至终结 (storm / siege / recession)

groups.name: Wake & Rouse · 唤醒与使振奋 (Awaken, Rouse, Stir)
groups.tip: 从沉睡或昏睡中被唤醒

items.def_en: To emerge from sleep into consciousness, or to cause another person to do so
items.ex_en: The alarm didn't go off, so I didn't wake up until eight.
items.ex_zh: 闹钟没响，所以我直到八点才醒。
items.ex2_en: The gentle morning sunshine woke up the campers sleeping inside their tents.
items.ex2_zh: 清晨柔和的阳光唤醒了在帐篷里熟睡的露营者。

items.def_en: To begin to move slightly after sleep, or to provoke someone into movement or consciousness
items.ex_en: The sleeping baby began to stir as the morning sunlight touched her.
items.ex_zh: 晨光洒在熟睡的婴儿身上时，她开始微微动弹。
items.ex2_en: A sudden gust of wind stirred the dry leaves across the patio.
items.ex2_zh: 一阵突如其来的微风吹动了露台上的枯叶。

items.def_en: To stop sleeping, or to wake someone up from slumber or inactivity
items.ex_en: The gentle bird songs at dawn served to awaken the sleepy village.
items.ex_zh: 破晓时分清脆的鸟鸣声唤醒了沉睡的宁静村庄。
items.ex2_en: The elderly monk awakens quietly before the sun crests the eastern mountains.
items.ex2_zh: 这位年迈的僧人在太阳爬上东山之前静静地醒来。

items.def_en: 1. To wake someone up from sleep. 2. To make someone feel active, excited, or interested.
items.ex_en: The loud alarm failed to rouse the exhausted sentry from deep sleep.
items.ex_zh: 响亮的警报未能将精疲力竭的哨兵从沉睡中弄醒。

items.def_en: To restore to consciousness, life, or renewed strength after fainting, illness, or sleep
items.ex_en: Paramedics used cold compresses and oxygen to revive the unconscious marathon runner.
items.ex_zh: 医护人员用冷敷和供氧使失去知觉的马拉松跑者苏醒过来。
items.ex2_en: The withered indoor plants revived quickly after receiving abundant water and sunshine.
items.ex2_zh: 枯萎的室内植物在得到充足的水分和阳光后迅速恢复了生机。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate disturbing someone from sleep, stupor, or apathy, shifting an individual or group from dormancy into active physical consciousness or vigorous action.
groups.summary_zh: 指将人从睡眠、昏睡或麻木中叫醒，促使其清醒并活跃起来。
groups.desc_en: Denotes transition from dormant, unconscious, or lethargic states into alert physical or mental vitality, differing from mere beginning by re-energizing existing latent capacities.
groups.desc_zh: 指从休眠、昏迷或慵懒状态转化为机能活跃与警醒，区别于事物的全新启动，强调复苏现有的内在潜能。
groups.nuance_en: wake up: cross the threshold from physiological sleep to alertness (sleeper / morning / town) · awaken: formal or figurative awakening of emotions, memories, or consciousness (interest / conscience / curiosity) · rouse: actively shake someone out of deep torpor, apathy, or sleep (rabble / sleeper / passion) · stir: make initial slight signs of life or provoke mild motion (crowd / breeze / emotions) · revive: bring back from near-extinction, fainting, or exhaustion (patient / tradition / economy)
groups.nuance_zh: wake up: 生理意义上从睡眠中醒来 (sleeper / morning / town) · awaken: 较正式或隐喻唤醒记忆、良知或情感 (interest / conscience / curiosity) · rouse: 强力惊醒、唤醒沉睡或激起斗志 (rabble / sleeper / passion) · stir: 产生微小萌动，或引起心潮翻涌 (crowd / breeze / emotions) · revive: 使从昏死、濒危或衰竭中彻底复苏 (patient / tradition / economy)

groups.name: Ward Off & Forfend · 禳除与防范 (Forfend, Avert, Ward off)
groups.tip: 祈求避开灾祸预先阻绝

items.def_en: To take active measures to repel or defend against danger, harm, illness, or unwanted advances
items.ex_en: She took mega doses of vitamin supplements to ward off the winter flu.
items.ex_zh: 她服用了大剂量的维生素补充剂以抵御冬季流感。

items.def_en: To successfully deflect or defend oneself against an incoming blow, attack, criticism, or difficulty
items.ex_en: The spokesperson struggled to fend off sharp questions regarding the corruption scandal.
items.ex_zh: 发言人竭力挡开关于腐败丑闻的一连串尖锐盘问。

items.def_en: To delay, ward off, or prevent something harmful or unwelcome from taking effect for a period of time
items.ex_en: Emergency interest rate cuts failed to stave off the looming economic crisis.
items.ex_zh: 紧急降息未能推迟迫在眉睫的经济危机的爆发。

items.def_en: To prevent an unpleasant, dangerous, or disastrous event from happening
items.ex_en: Swift intervention by diplomatic mediators helped avert a devastating regional border war.
items.ex_zh: 外交调解员的迅速介入有助于防止一场灾难性的地区边境战争。

items.def_en: 1. (archaic or formal) To avert, ward off, or prevent something undesirable from happening.
items.ex_en: May righteous fortune forfend our besieged city from such a dreadful calamity.
items.ex_zh: 愿正直的命运庇佑，防止这般可怕的灾难降临我们被困的城池。

groups.summary_en: This frame focuses on anticipatory measures taken to protect against, drive away, or deflect an approaching danger, evil, or catastrophe.
groups.summary_zh: 在祸患来临之前主动采取行动加以避开或抵御。
groups.desc_en: Encompasses proactive defensive efforts to prevent impending harm, misfortune, or attack from landing, contrasting with passive endurance by active interceptive shielding.
groups.desc_zh: 指主动采取防御、招架或祈禳手段阻止迫在眉睫的灾祸或打击降临，区别于被动承受，强调防患于未然的化解与格挡。
groups.nuance_en: ward off: keep away danger, disease, or evil through preventative measures (evil spirits / blow / illness) · fend off: deflect or repulse a physical or aggressive attack (attackers / questions / bankruptcy) · stave off: temporarily hold off a looming crisis or scarcity (collapse / bankruptcy / disaster) · avert: prevent a catastrophe or shift eyes away from an unpleasant sight (crisis / disaster / eyes) · forfend: archaic or solemn protective shielding from impending ill (heaven / disaster / catastrophe)
groups.nuance_zh: ward off: 采取避忌或养生手段抵御疾病、灾殃或打击 (evil spirits / blow / illness) · fend off: 招架、抵挡实质性的物理攻击或追问 (attackers / questions / bankruptcy) · stave off: 延缓、勉强拖住危局或饥荒的爆发 (collapse / bankruptcy / disaster) · avert: 成功扭转局势以避开灾难，或转开视线 (crisis / disaster / eyes) · forfend: 典雅古体，祈求上苍保佑免受祸殃 (heaven / disaster / catastrophe)

groups.name: Warm Up & Limber · 热身与伸展拉伸 (Warm Up, Stretch, Limber Up)
groups.tip: 活动舒展筋骨使身体灵活

items.def_en: To extend one's limbs or body to full length in order to loosen and elongate the muscles
items.ex_en: Runners must stretch their tight hamstrings thoroughly before attempting a sprint.
items.ex_zh: 跑步者在尝试冲刺前必须彻底拉伸紧绷的腘绳肌。
items.ex2_en: The rubber waistband stretches comfortably to accommodate many different body sizes.
items.ex2_zh: 橡胶腰带具有舒适的延展性，可以适应多种不同的体型。

items.def_en: To prepare for physical activity by exercising gently to increase circulation and muscle suppleness
items.ex_en: Athletes should warm up properly before entering the pool to prevent cramps.
items.ex_zh: 运动员入水前应做好充分的热身准备以防抽筋。
items.ex2_en: She placed cold milk on the stove to warm up breakfast drinks.
items.ex2_zh: 她把冷牛奶放在炉子上加热早餐饮品。

items.def_en: To make one's muscles or body flexible and pliable by performing stretching exercises
items.ex_en: The dancers spent twenty minutes on stage to limber up before rehearsals.
items.ex_zh: 舞者们在排练前花二十分钟在台上活动舒展筋骨。
items.ex2_en: The physiotherapist used gentle massage techniques to limber up stiff shoulder joints.
items.ex2_zh: 物理治疗师用温和的按摩手法放松僵硬的肩关节。

items.def_en: To perform light exercises to relieve physical stiffness and make joints move freely
items.ex_en: He did gentle shoulder rolls to loosen up after sitting for hours.
items.ex_zh: 久坐数小时后，他轻轻转动肩膀来活动开僵硬的筋骨。
items.ex2_en: Warm baths help loosen up tense neck muscles after hard physical labor.
items.ex2_zh: 温水浴有助于在繁重的体力劳动后放松紧张的颈部肌肉。

items.def_zh: 使柔软，活动（肌肉）；做准备活动，热身
items.def_en: (also 'limber up') To do light stretching exercises to make muscles flexible and ready for physical effort.
items.ex_en: Gymnasts always limber their joints thoroughly before tackling any balance beam routine.
items.ex_zh: 体操运动员在进行平衡木套路前总是彻底活动柔软关节。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe performing gentle physical exercises, dynamic stretches, or calisthenics to loosen stiff joints, elevate heart rate, and prepare muscles for vigorous exertion. They contrast general calisthenics with targeted muscle lengthening.
groups.summary_zh: 指在剧烈运动前进行轻柔拉伸或活动，使身体舒展防伤。
groups.desc_en: Involves conditioning the body's musculature through preparatory movement to achieve elasticity and prevent injury, contrasting with heavy athletic exertion by its preparatory nature.
groups.desc_zh: 指在剧烈运动前通过针对性活动提升体温、拉伸韧带以达到柔软柔韧状态，区别于高负荷正式训练，具有过渡预备性。
groups.nuance_en: warm up: elevate cardiovascular rate and muscle temperature prior to action (engine / athlete / singer) · stretch: extend muscles and joints to improve range of motion (hamstring / body / limbs) · limber up: execute targeted flexibility routines to remove stiffness (joints / team / dancers) · loosen up: relax tight muscles or unwind tense mental states (shoulders / muscles / speaker) · limber: render muscles or wood pliable and supple (limbs / muscles / body)
groups.nuance_zh: warm up: 综合提升心率与肌肉温度以备战 (engine / athlete / singer) · stretch: 延长肌肉与肌腱以增加关节活动度 (hamstring / body / limbs) · limber up: 针对性消除僵硬、增强身体柔韧度 (joints / team / dancers) · loosen up: 放松绷紧的肌肉或缓解紧张拘束的神态 (shoulders / muscles / speaker) · limber: 使四肢或材质变得柔软易弯曲 (limbs / muscles / body)

groups.name: Warn & Admonish in Advance · 预先告诫与提醒 (Alert, Caution, Tip off)
groups.tip: 防患未然提前预警以促其警醒

items.def_en: To warn someone about possible danger, mistakes, or negative consequences
items.ex_en: The manual serves to caution operators against exceeding maximum operational pressure limits.
items.ex_zh: 操作手册旨在告诫操作人员切勿超过最大运行压力限制。

items.def_en: To give someone secret or advance information about something that is about to happen
items.ex_en: An anonymous insider decided to tip off federal agents about the tax fraud.
items.ex_zh: 一名匿名知情人士决定向联邦探员告发这起税务欺诈内情。

items.def_en: To warn someone of a dangerous or surprising situation so they can take action
items.ex_en: Sirens blared loudly across the base to alert soldiers of incoming fire.
items.ex_zh: 警报在基地各处厉声作响，提醒士兵防备来袭火力。

items.def_en: To advise or urge someone earnestly, or gently warn them not to do something
items.ex_en: The elderly judge saw fit to admonish the young defendant against further violations.
items.ex_zh: 年长的法官适时温和告诫年轻被告切莫再犯。

items.def_en: To warn someone about a possible danger, difficulty, or unpleasant event beforehand.
items.ex_en: Officials forewarned residents of severe flooding hours before the storm made landfall.
items.ex_zh: 暴风雨登陆数小时前，官员便向居民预先发出了严重洪灾的警告。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers acts of advising someone ahead of time regarding oncoming peril, hazards, or negative outcomes, varying from gentle cautions to urgent alerts.
groups.summary_zh: 就潜在危险或不利后果向当事人提前预警或严肃告诫。
groups.desc_en: Entails transmitting advance notice about imminent peril, risks, or misconduct to influence subsequent behavior, differing from informative reporting by its cautionary and preventive intent.
groups.desc_zh: 指在事发前针对危险、隐患或失当行径向当事人敲响警钟，区别于中立的事实陈述，带有诫勉、规劝与防范意味。
groups.nuance_en: caution: urge prudent behavior and deliberate care (motorist / investor / youth) · forewarn: provide explicit prior intelligence about upcoming hazard (public / traveler / consumers) · alert: summon immediate vigilance and state of readiness (authorities / public / troops) · admonish: reprove mildly while earnest-mindedly counseling against recurrence (student / disciple / wrongdoer) · tip off: secretly pass privileged intelligence about impending action (police / cartel / suspects)
groups.nuance_zh: caution: 告诫谨慎行事、提醒提防风险 (motorist / investor / youth) · forewarn: 预先获知或发出明确的祸患情报 (public / traveler / consumers) · alert: 迅速向受众拉响警报使其进入临战戒备 (authorities / public / troops) · admonish: 带有道德或长辈色彩的温和训诫与提醒 (student / disciple / wrongdoer) · tip off: 私下密报、透风报信 (police / cartel / suspects)

groups.name: Water & Irrigate Soil · 浇灌与农田供水 (Irrigate, Hydrate, Sprinkle)
groups.tip: 向土壤或植物人工浇水润泽

items.def_zh: 给……浇水，灌溉；流泪，流口水；给……供水
items.def_en: 1. to pour water on plants or the soil to help them grow; to supply land with water 2. (of eyes) to fill with tears; (of the mouth) to produce saliva
items.ex_en: Remember to water the delicate tomato seedlings every morning before the sun rises.
items.ex_zh: 记住每天清晨日出之前给娇嫩的番茄幼苗浇水。

items.def_en: To water thoroughly or wash down using a flexible hose
items.ex_en: The gardener used a long pipe to hose down the parched flowerbeds.
items.ex_zh: 园丁用一根长软管彻底冲浇了干枯的花坛。

items.def_zh: 喷淋或洒水于（草坪、花园）
items.def_en: To scatter fine drops of water lightly over a lawn, field, or flowerbed
items.ex_en: She used a fine nozzle to sprinkle fresh water across the thirsty lawn.
items.ex_zh: 她用细喷嘴将清水轻轻喷洒在干渴的草坪上。

items.def_zh: 为（土壤或植物）补充水分
items.def_en: To restore or supply an adequate amount of water to parched soil, compost, or living tissue
items.ex_en: Gardeners must hydrate dry compost thoroughly before planting any delicate summer seeds.
items.ex_zh: 园丁在播种娇嫩的夏季种子之前，必须彻底为干燥的堆肥补充水分。
items.ex2_en: Dehydrated food ingredients hydrate rapidly when submerged into boiling vegetable broth.
items.ex2_zh: 脱水食材浸泡在沸腾的蔬菜高汤中会迅速吸收水分膨胀。

items.def_en: To supply land, crops, or agricultural soil with water by means of channels, pipes, or automated systems
items.ex_en: Engineers constructed deep canals to irrigate vast fields across the arid valley.
items.ex_zh: 工程师修建了深水渠，以灌溉干旱山谷中的大片农田。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame designate applying water artificially to crops, lawns, gardens, or dry soil via canals, sprinklers, or manual pouring to support plant growth.
groups.summary_zh: 向土地、植被或农作物注水浇灌，维持水土润泽与生长。
groups.desc_en: Describes the purposeful application of water to flora, crops, or terrain to nurture life and sustain moisture, contrasting with natural rainfall through deliberate human agency.
groups.desc_zh: 指人工有计划地向作物、花草或地表输送水分以维持生长，区别于天然降水，强调人为主观供给与管护。
groups.nuance_en: water: manually or simply provide water to plants or domestic spaces (garden / flowers / lawn) · irrigate: engineer systematic channels or apparatus to supply extensive farmlands (crops / desert / fields) · sprinkle: scatter light droplets across a surface (lawn / flour / courtyard) · hose down: blast a forceful stream of water from a flexible pipe for cleaning or soaking (pavement / deck / vehicle) · hydrate: supply water internally or at a cellular level to prevent dryness (skin / cells / body)
groups.nuance_zh: water: 日常或手工给植物浇水 (garden / flowers / lawn) · irrigate: 水利工程系统化大面积灌溉农田 (crops / desert / fields) · sprinkle: 喷洒细密水花或点阵状洒水 (lawn / flour / courtyard) · hose down: 用水管冲刷地面或淋湿大片区域 (pavement / deck / vehicle) · hydrate: 细胞或肌理层面的深层补水、水化 (skin / cells / body)

groups.name: Wave & Salute · 致意与挥手招呼 (Wave, Greet, Salute)
groups.tip: 用招手、挥手等动作打招呼

items.def_en: to lower and raise your head quickly as an informal acknowledgment or greeting
items.ex_en: He gave a polite nod to the receptionist before walking toward the elevators.
items.ex_zh: 在走向电梯之前，他礼貌地向接待员点头致意。

items.def_en: to bid farewell to departing people by waving, or to dismiss someone with a dismissive hand gesture
items.ex_en: The smiling parents gathered on the platform to wave off their departing children.
items.ex_zh: 面带微笑的父母们聚集在站台上，挥手为离去的孩子们送行。

items.def_en:
1. to move your hand or arm as a greeting, farewell, or signal
2. to move loosely back and forth or flutter in the wind
items.ex_en: She stood by the platform window and began to wave at her friends.
items.ex_zh: 她站在站台窗边，开始向朋友们招手致意。

items.def_en: to greet, call out to, or wave enthusiastically to attract someone's attention from a distance
items.ex_en: The watchman hailed the incoming foreign delegates from atop the fortress walls.
items.ex_zh: 守卫从要塞城墙上高声向远道而来的外国代表致候。

items.def_en: to bring a hand to the forehead as a formal military sign of respect, or to greet someone formally
items.ex_en: The sentry straightened his posture to salute the commanding officer entering the compound.
items.ex_zh: 哨兵挺直身子，向进入大院的指挥官敬礼致意。

groups.summary_en: This frame captures interpersonal physical signs used to acknowledge, greet, or bid farewell to someone. Nuances range from casual hand-waving to formal military saluting or warm physical acknowledgment across distances.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过挥手、敬礼等动作向他人致以问候、致意或告别。
groups.desc_en: Covers physical gestures and formal bodily posturing used to acknowledge, welcome, or pay tribute to another, differing from conversational speaking by relying on visual etiquette.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过特定的身体姿态或肢体动作用于迎送、致意或表示敬重，区别于口头对话，依赖视觉礼仪传达信息。
groups.nuance_en: wave: raise and swing the hand as a sign of recognition or farewell (hand / crowd / banner) · salute: perform a crisp formal military sign of respect, or pay tribute (officer / flag / bravery) · hail: call out loudly or signal to attract attention, or acclaim enthusiastically (cab / victor / ship) · nod: incline the head slightly in curt acknowledgment or assent (head / assent / acquaintance) · wave off: brush aside or decline a gesture or person with a dismissive wave (protest / advice / rescuer)
groups.nuance_zh: wave: 挥手示意迎送、道别或引人注目 (hand / crowd / banner) · salute: 行标准军礼或隆重致敬 (officer / flag / bravery) · hail: 扬声招手叫停车辆，或热烈欢呼拥戴 (cab / victor / ship) · nod: 略微点头以示默许或简短招呼 (head / assent / acquaintance) · wave off: 挥手推却、回绝或示意退下 (protest / advice / rescuer)

groups.name: Waver & Distrust · 疑虑动摇与踌躇信任 (Waver, Hesitate, Hedge)
groups.tip: 由将信将疑到心生戒备

items.def_en: To pause before saying or doing something due to uncertainty or reluctance
items.ex_en: He seemed to hesitate for several seconds before signing the lucrative contract.
items.ex_zh: 在签署这份利润丰厚的合同前，他似乎迟疑了数秒。

items.def_zh: 闪烁其词，留退路以规避不测
items.def_en: To avoid making a definite decision or commitment out of skepticism or caution
items.ex_en: The spokesperson began to hedge when pressed for details about company spending.
items.ex_zh: 在被追问公司开支细节时，发言人开始闪烁其词以留退路。

items.raw_cluster: 怀疑与不信任 Doubt & Distrust
items.def_en: To feel that someone or something cannot be relied upon or trusted.
items.ex_en: Local merchants began to distrust foreign investors after the sudden market crash.
items.ex_zh: 在遭遇突如其来的市场崩盘后，当地商人开始对外国投资者产生戒备。

items.def_en: To become unsteady or falter in resolution, opinion, or faith
items.ex_en: The general did not waver in his commitment despite mounting political pressure.
items.ex_zh: 尽管政治压力不断增加，将军的信念却未曾动摇。

items.def_zh: 在两种选择或信任间摇摆不定
items.def_en: To alternate or waver between different opinions or actions indecisively
items.ex_en: Diplomats vacillated between imposing severe economic sanctions and pursuing peaceful dialogue.
items.ex_zh: 外交官们在施加严厉经济制裁与寻求和平对话之间摇摆不定。

groups.summary_en: Highlights the behavioral paralysis or hesitation resulting from lack of trust and chronic doubt. Because one lacks confidence in an entity or claim, one wavers and delays commitment.
groups.summary_zh: 因内心缺乏信任与坚定信念，而在决断时动摇、游移与踌躇不前。
groups.desc_en: Expresses mental fluctuation, unsteady conviction, or protective hesitation before committing, contrasting with resolute certainty through persistent oscillation between competing options.
groups.desc_zh: 指在做出决断或投注信任时内心动摇、摇摆不定或留有后路，区别于笃定与决绝，强调在多选项间的拉扯与游移。
groups.nuance_en: waver: exhibit unsteady conviction or physical tremble under pressure (resolve / loyalty / voice) · vacillate: swing indecisively back and forth between two opposing courses (opinions / politician / policy) · hesitate: pause briefly out of uncertainty or reluctance before acting (step / speaker / heart) · hedge: mitigate risk by avoiding absolute commitment or setting countervailing bets (bets / investments / language) · distrust: withhold faith and harbor active suspicion toward someone or something (intentions / promises / motive)
groups.nuance_zh: waver: 意志、决心或视线在压力下产生动摇 (resolve / loyalty / voice) · vacillate: 在两种对立的主张或路线之间反复摇摆 (opinions / politician / policy) · hesitate: 因疑虑、踌躇而在行动前短暂停顿 (step / speaker / heart) · hedge: 说话留退路、两头下注以规避风险 (bets / investments / language) · distrust: 缺乏信任，抱持主动的猜忌与提防 (intentions / promises / motive)

groups.name: Weatherproof & Protect · 防护与抵御 (Weatherproof, Waterproof, Winterize)
groups.tip: 抵御外界侵蚀提供防护

items.def_en: To coat a surface with a liquid protective substance that prevents moisture or air penetration
items.ex_en: Workers must seal the wooden deck with varnish to prevent water damage.
items.ex_zh: 工人必须用清漆密封木质甲板，以防止水分渗透侵蚀。

items.def_zh: 使作过冬准备；防冻处理
items.def_en: To adapt, insulate, or treat a building, engine, or system so that it can withstand freezing winter conditions
items.ex_en: Homeowners must winterize their outdoor plumbing systems before the first severe freeze.
items.ex_zh: 房主在初次严重霜冻来临前，必须对室外水管系统进行防冻处理。

items.def_en: To treat a metal surface with chemicals or paint so that it resists oxidation and corrosion
items.ex_en: Technicians spray a protective coating to rustproof the steel beams against corrosion.
items.ex_zh: 技术人员喷涂了一层保护涂层，以使钢梁防锈耐腐蚀。

items.def_en: To make a fabric, wall, or object impervious to water by coating or treating it with a sealant
items.ex_en: Hikers often waterproof their leather boots using a special wax before expeditions.
items.ex_zh: 远足者在探险前常用一种特殊的蜡涂层来使皮靴防水。

items.def_zh: 使防风雨，使不受风雨侵蚀
items.def_en: 1. To treat, seal, or coat a surface, building, or garment so that it resists damage from rain, wind, and cold.
items.ex_en: Builders used specialized sealant to weatherproof the external brick walls against rain.
items.ex_zh: 建筑工人使用专业密封剂对外部砖墙进行防风雨处理，以抵御雨水侵蚀。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame refer to treating, coating, or sealing physical structures, fabrics, or surfaces to make them resilient against harsh atmospheric elements like water, freezing cold, or wind. They emphasize protective material modification.
groups.summary_zh: 通过涂层、封堵等工艺改造表面或建筑，抵御风雨侵蚀或恶劣天气。
groups.desc_en: Involves applying treatments, protective barriers, or structural modifications to shield property against seasonal decay and moisture, contrasting with superficial cleaning through structural shielding.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过涂层封堵、工艺处理或结构改造以抵御恶劣气候、水汽及季节性侵蚀，区别于表面保洁，重在建立物化防护屏障。
groups.nuance_en: weatherproof: adapt materials to endure outdoor exposure and climatic wear (coat / casing / fabric) · waterproof: render an object totally impervious to water penetration (boots / watch / basement) · winterize: prepare buildings, machinery, or crops to withstand freezing winter conditions (home / pipes / camper) · rustproof: coat metal surfaces to prevent oxidation and corrosion (chassis / metal / parts) · seal: close up fissures or apertures hermetically to stop leaks (gap / envelope / deck)
groups.nuance_zh: weatherproof: 做耐候处理以经受风吹日晒 (coat / casing / fabric) · waterproof: 做深度防水处理以滴水不漏 (boots / watch / basement) · winterize: 为应对严寒与冰冻对设施做越冬维护 (home / pipes / camper) · rustproof: 在金属表面涂层以防锈蚀 (chassis / metal / parts) · seal: 封堵缝隙与孔洞以防气液渗漏 (gap / envelope / deck)

groups.name: Weave & Thread · 穿行与穿梭 (Weave, Thread, Wiggle Through)
groups.tip: 在狭窄空隙间巧妙穿针引线

items.def_en: Follow a curving, twisting, or sinuous path through terrain or spaces
items.ex_en: The scenic path winds gently through dense pine forests and rocky ravines.
items.ex_zh: 这条风景优美的小径穿过茂密的松林与岩石峡谷，蜿蜒延伸。
items.ex2_en: The climber had to wind the climbing rope tightly around his waist.
items.ex2_zh: 登山者必须将登山绳紧紧地缠绕在腰间。

items.def_en: Walk slowly and deliberately through a messy, dangerous, or obstructed area
items.ex_en: The weary travelers picked their way across the treacherous, ice-covered mountain pass.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的旅人们择路而行，小心穿过凶险结冰的山口。

items.def_en: Move by repeatedly turning and changing direction between obstacles, people, or vehicles
items.ex_en: The agile courier managed to weave through heavy traffic on his bicycle.
items.ex_zh: 敏捷的快递员骑着自行车设法在拥挤的车流中穿梭自如。

items.def_en: Squeeze or move slowly and furtively through a narrow passage or tightly packed crowd
items.ex_en: The determined reporter managed to worm through the dense crowd outside court.
items.ex_zh: 那位坚定的记者设法费力挤过法院门外拥挤的人群。

items.def_en: 1. To make one's way carefully through a crowded or narrow space. 2. To pass a thread, needle, or strip through an opening.
items.ex_en: She had to thread carefully through the packed marketplace to reach home.
items.ex_zh: 她不得不小心翼翼地穿过拥挤的集市以赶回家中。

groups.summary_en: This frame specifies navigating a path by deftly winding, swerving, and passing through crowded, confined, or obstacle-laden spaces. It highlights continuous course adjustments and agility.
groups.summary_zh: 指在拥挤、狭窄或充满障碍的空间中敏捷游移穿行。
groups.desc_en: Represents sinuous, calculated motion navigating through dense obstacles, crowds, or cramped conduits, differing from linear forward movement through continuous lateral adjustment.
groups.desc_zh: 指在密集障碍物、人群或狭小孔道中曲折、机敏地穿行绕行，区别于径直前行，强调不断变向、见缝插针的轨迹。
groups.nuance_en: weave: advance along an undulating, crisscrossing line among obstacles (traffic / crowd / paths) · thread: maneuver carefully and delicately through narrow gaps or barriers (needle / alleyways / crowd) · wind: follow a naturally twisting, curving route or channel (river / road / path) · worm through: wriggle patiently and furtively into or out of cramped spaces (tunnel / crowd / gap) · pick one's way: advance with fastidious, cautious steps over treacherous terrain (rubble / stones / swamp)
groups.nuance_zh: weave: 忽左忽右、穿针引线般在车流或人群中穿梭 (traffic / crowd / paths) · thread: 精密小心地穿过极为狭小的缝隙或巷弄 (needle / alleyways / crowd) · wind: 路线本身天然或大跨度地迂回曲折 (river / road / path) · worm through: 像蠕虫般一点点硬挤、蠕动钻透狭小空间 (tunnel / crowd / gap) · pick one's way: 在险恶难行的地面上择路审慎前行 (rubble / stones / swamp)

groups.name: Wed & Form Marital Alliances · 结为伉俪与联姻 (Wed, Espouse, Tie the knot)
groups.tip: 跨宗族或阶层通婚联合

items.def_en: (formal or literary) To marry someone; to join in matrimonial union
items.ex_en: The fair maiden agreed to wed the gallant knight upon his return.
items.ex_zh: 美丽的少女答应在英勇的骑士归来之时与他结为连理。

items.def_en: (+ with/by) To join forces or bind families/dynasties together, often through marriage
items.ex_en: The wealthy count decided to ally his noble house with the royalty.
items.ex_zh: 富有的伯爵决定通过与王室联姻来巩固自己贵族家族的势力。
items.ex2_en: The two independent political factions allied during the recent general election.
items.ex2_zh: 这两个独立的政治派别在最近的大选中联合了起来。

items.def_en: (idiomatic) To get married legally or ceremonially
items.ex_en: The happy young couple decided to tie the knot on a beach.
items.ex_zh: 这对幸福的年轻情侣决定在海滩上喜结连理。

items.def_en: (archaic or literary) To marry someone or give someone in marriage
items.ex_en: The young lord was proud to espouse the duke's eldest daughter.
items.ex_zh: 年轻的领主因能迎娶公爵的长女而深感自豪。

items.def_en: 1. (+ with) When people from different families, religions, or social groups intermarry, they marry each other.
items.ex_en: Royal dynasties frequently intermarried with distant kingdoms to solidify political truces.
items.ex_zh: 王室各朝代常常与远方王国通婚，以此巩固政治休战协议。

groups.summary_en: This frame encompasses entering into matrimonial unions, whether viewed as romantic commitments, religious solemnities, or socio-political alliances between families or tribes. It covers both solemn rites and diplomatic pairings.
groups.summary_zh: 指通过婚姻结合，尤指家族、族群间缔结婚约以达成联姻。
groups.desc_en: Denotes the formal contracting of legal matrimony or political/social unions, contrasting with informal romantic association through institutionalized, binding commitments.
groups.desc_zh: 指男女之间缔结法定婚姻，或家族、派系间通过结亲达成政治联合，区别于普通谈情说爱，具有制度化与盟约性。
groups.nuance_en: wed: formal or literary act of entering lawful matrimony (partner / heir / couple) · espouse: take up as a spouse in traditional diction, or embrace a cause (cause / bride / doctrine) · tie the knot: informal, colloquial expression for getting married (sweethearts / couple / weekend) · ally: enter into a cooperative, protective pact via union or agreement (dynasty / family / faction) · intermarry: contract marriages across disparate tribes, castes, or social groups (races / dynasties / clans)
groups.nuance_zh: wed: 正式或书面语中结为夫妻 (partner / heir / couple) · espouse: 古风指结缡娶嫁，现多比喻拥护吸纳某主义 (cause / bride / doctrine) · tie the knot: 口语化、亲切指喜结连理、扯证成家 (sweethearts / couple / weekend) · ally: 借联姻或条约与他方结成政治同盟 (dynasty / family / faction) · intermarry: 异族通婚、阶层间或家族内部相互联姻 (races / dynasties / clans)

groups.name: Wedge & Jam · 嵌塞与卡紧 (Jam, Cram, Squeeze into)
groups.tip: 楔入窄缝或用力塞紧

items.def_en: To succeed in getting oneself or an object into a very tight, crowded opening or compartment
items.ex_en: Commuters had to squeeze into the overcrowded train carriage during rush hour.
items.ex_zh: 早高峰期间，通勤者不得不硬挤进过度拥挤的火车车厢中。

items.def_en: To force a large number of people or things into a space that is too small for them
items.ex_en: Organizers had to cram dozens of excited fans into the tiny auditorium.
items.ex_zh: 组织者不得不把几十名兴奋的粉丝硬塞进狭小的礼堂里。

items.def_en: To force or squeeze someone or something into an inadequate space or schedule with great difficulty
items.ex_en: The producer managed to shoehorn three more interviews into the hectic schedule.
items.ex_zh: 制作人硬是在繁忙的日程安排中强行凑合塞进了三次采访。

items.def_en: To push, shove, or pack something into a narrow space so tightly that it becomes stuck or immovable
items.ex_en: He accidentally jammed his fingers into the narrow gap beneath the door.
items.ex_zh: 他不小心把手指紧紧卡进了门下狭窄的缝隙中。
items.ex2_en: The old office printer jammed again during a very busy morning shift.
items.ex2_zh: 旧办公室打印机在非常繁忙的早班期间又卡纸了。

items.def_en: To force, pack, or squeeze something tightly into a narrow space so that it cannot move
items.ex_en: She tried to wedge her oversized suitcase between the two bus seats.
items.ex_zh: 她试图把自己超大的行李箱塞进两个公共汽车座位之间固定住。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe forcibly pressing or packing an object or person into an extremely tight, constricted space so that movement is restricted or blocked. 'Wedge' suggests triangular taper or immobility, while 'jam' highlights obstruction, and 'cram' stresses overfilling.
groups.summary_zh: 指强行将人或物体挤压、嵌入狭窄缝隙，使其紧塞或动弹不得。
groups.desc_en: Describes forcing an object into an uncomfortably small space or becoming immovably trapped due to compression, contrasting with gentle fitting by forceful lateral containment.
groups.desc_zh: 指通过挤压强行塞入容积过小的空间，或因卡死而失去机动性，区别于正常的严丝合缝，强调外力挤逼与卡阻。
groups.nuance_en: wedge: force tightly into a narrow split, or secure by a triangular block (door / foot / between) · jam: force or pack violently so that movement is halted or blocked (gears / brakes / doorway) · cram: pack excessive numbers or bulk into limited confines (belongings / suitcases / heads) · shoehorn: forcefully fit something into an ill-suited, tight context with great effort (metaphor / scene / schedule) · squeeze into: exert compression to barely fit inside tight limits (costume / corner / schedule)
groups.nuance_zh: wedge: 楔入裂隙中卡紧，或用楔子固定 (door / foot / between) · jam: 挤死、卡壳或使机械运转受阻 (gears / brakes / doorway) · cram: 填鸭式把过多事物硬塞入有限空间 (belongings / suitcases / heads) · shoehorn: 牵强附会或生拉硬拽塞进不合适的情境 (metaphor / scene / schedule) · squeeze into: 勉强挤进紧身衣服或狭小角落 (costume / corner / schedule)

groups.name: Weep & Whimper · 哭泣与呜咽 (Sob, Weep, Whimper)
groups.tip: 断断续续抽泣抽噎流泪

items.def_en: To make low, feeble, intermittent sounds expressing fear, pain, or discontent
items.ex_en: The frightened puppy began to whimper softly in the dark underground cellar.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的小狗在黑暗的地下室里开始低声呜咽。

items.def_en: To cry and sniffle tearfully, often in a weak, fretful, or insincere manner
items.ex_en: The spoiled child began to snivel loudly after being denied sweet candy.
items.ex_zh: 被拒绝给糖后，被惯坏的孩子开始大声抽鼻涕抱怨哭诉。

items.def_zh: 啜泣，抽噎，呜咽；抽噎着说
items.def_en: To cry noisily while taking sudden, sharp, gasping breaths; to say something while weeping in this way.
items.ex_en: The devastated widow began to sob uncontrollably during the solemn memorial service.
items.ex_zh: 在庄严的追悼会上，极度悲痛的寡妇情不自禁地抽噎啜泣起来。

items.def_en: To shed tears quietly or continuously as an expression of deep sorrow or grief
items.ex_en: Grieving mourners stood silently beneath the cold rain to weep for him.
items.ex_zh: 悲痛的哀悼者们静静地伫立在冷雨中，为他流泪悲泣。

items.def_en: To lose control of one's emotions and begin weeping uncontrollably
items.ex_en: She finally began to break down in tears after hearing the news.
items.ex_zh: 听到那个消息后，她的情绪终于彻底崩溃，失声痛哭。
items.ex2_en: Soil microbes break down stubborn organic waste into rich, nutritious compost.
items.ex2_zh: 土壤微生物将难以降解的有机废物分解为肥沃营养的堆肥。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on subdued, convulsive, or quiet expressions of grief and distress, highlighting uneven breathing, low gasps, and flowing tears rather than loud outcries.
groups.summary_zh: 侧重抽噎、落泪或低声呜咽等非高声哀号的悲伤哭泣表现。
groups.desc_en: Depicts shedding tears accompanied by suppressed, broken, or convulsive respiration, contrasting with boisterous wailing by quieter, somatic sorrow and loss of emotional composure.
groups.desc_zh: 指伴随呼吸抽搐、吞声哽咽的落泪过程，区别于声震四野的号啕大哭，表现为较为内敛、身体发颤的悲伤与情绪崩溃。
groups.nuance_en: weep: shed tears quietly and copiously as a pure expression of grief (sorrow / joy / grave) · sob: cry with convulsive, shuddering gasps for breath (child / shoulders / uncontrollably) · whimper: utter feeble, plaintive, broken whining sounds of pain or fear (dog / toddler / misery) · snivel: weep tearfully while repeatedly sniffing wet mucus, often eliciting contempt (hypocrite / coward / brat) · break down: lose all psychological control and collapse into uncontrollable crying (witness / suspect / grief)
groups.nuance_zh: weep: 典雅书面语，潸然泪下或默默痛哭 (sorrow / joy / grave) · sob: 伴随身体剧烈抽动、上气不接下气的抽泣 (child / shoulders / uncontrollably) · whimper: 因害怕、无助发出的细弱呜咽声 (dog / toddler / misery) · snivel: 抽抽搭搭抹泪、鼻涕眼泪齐流的抽搭 (hypocrite / coward / brat) · break down: 心理防线彻底瓦解而失声痛哭 (witness / suspect / grief)

groups.name: Welcome & Receive · 欢迎与接纳 (Greet, Receive, Usher in)
groups.tip: 对来访者致以热情问候接待

items.def_en: To formally meet, accommodate, or react to visitors or guests upon their arrival
items.ex_en: The ambassador prepared to receive the foreign delegates at the embassy tonight.
items.ex_zh: 大使准备今晚在使馆正式接待这批外国代表。

items.def_zh: 欢迎，热情接待；乐于接受，欣然欢迎
items.def_en: 1. To greet a visitor or newcomer in a friendly or polite manner. 2. To receive or accept an idea, decision, or change gladly.
items.ex_en: The friendly hotel staff smiled warmly to welcome the exhausted international travelers.
items.ex_zh: 友善的酒店员工热情微笑，迎接疲惫的国际旅客。

items.def_en: To accept, support, or welcome an idea, person, or change with enthusiasm and open arms
items.ex_en: The board members chose to embrace the radical reforms suggested by management.
items.ex_zh: 董事会成员选择欣然接受管理层所提出的彻底改革方案。

items.def_en: To mark the beginning of or formally introduce a new person, period, or phase
items.ex_en: The groundbreaking technology promises to usher in a prosperous era of exploration.
items.ex_zh: 这项突破性技术有望开辟一个繁荣的全新探索时代。

items.def_en: To give a sign of polite recognition or welcome to someone upon meeting or arrival
items.ex_en: She stepped outside into the morning sunshine to greet her new neighbors.
items.ex_zh: 她走到室外温暖的晨光中，向新邻居们礼貌问候。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on greeting a visitor, newcomer, or new initiative with hospitality, openness, or positive acceptance. It contrasts friendly personal receptions with formal institutional hospitality.
groups.summary_zh: 以热情或礼貌的姿态迎接访客，或欣然接纳新事物。
groups.desc_en: Covers accommodating newcomers, guests, or external proposals with hospitable reception or ceremonial introduction, contrasting with defensive exclusion by openness and hospitality.
groups.desc_zh: 指以好客态度接纳访客、新来者或欣然接受新理念、新纪元，区别于冷漠排外，强调主动的开门相迎与礼节包容。
groups.nuance_en: welcome: greet arrivals with genuine warmth, or accept ideas gladly (guests / change / reform) · receive: formally host, admit, or process visitors or communications (delegates / visitors / sacrament) · greet: give an initial formal or polite salutation to an arrival (host / audience / news) · embrace: passionately adopt, accept, or physically hug someone or an ideology (culture / concept / lifestyle) · usher in: inaugurate, herald, or guide into a momentous new era or phase (era / changes / century)
groups.nuance_zh: welcome: 热情诚挚地欢迎宾客，或乐见改变 (guests / change / reform) · receive: 官方、正式地接见外宾或接待来客 (delegates / visitors / sacrament) · greet: 初见时开口问候、打招呼或映入眼帘 (host / audience / news) · embrace: 张开双臂拥抱，或全盘欣然接纳新思想 (culture / concept / lifestyle) · usher in: 引领、开创或迎来一个崭新纪元 (era / changes / century)

groups.name: Whimper & Whine · 呜咽与低泣 (Whine, Pule, Snivel)
groups.tip: 因痛苦或哀伤发出低沉呜咽

items.def_en: To cry weakly or plaintively like a baby or young animal
items.ex_en: The abandoned newborn kitten began to mewl softly in the cold alley.
items.ex_zh: 被遗弃的新生小猫在寒冷的小巷中开始微弱地啼叫。

items.def_en: 1. To make weak, low crying sounds expressing pain, fear, or unhappiness, or utter words in this manner.
items.ex_en: The injured dog lay near the porch to whimper softly in pain.
items.ex_zh: 受伤的狗趴在门廊旁，痛苦地低声呜咽着。

items.def_en: To cry and sniffle in a tearful, complaining, or self-pitying way
items.ex_en: He began to snivel self-pityingly after his supervisor criticized his sloppy report.
items.ex_zh: 在主管批评了他粗心草率的报告后，他开始自怨自艾地抽搭哭诉。

items.def_en: To cry plaintively with a thin, weak voice
items.ex_en: The starving child continued to pule faintly in the bitter winter cold.
items.ex_zh: 饥饿的孩子在刺骨的寒冬中继续微声哀啼。

items.def_en: To emit a prolonged, high-pitched cry of distress, complaint, or petulance
items.ex_en: The tired toddler started to whine relentlessly for his favorite bedtime toy.
items.ex_zh: 疲倦的幼儿开始没完没了地哀鸣哭闹，非要他心爱的睡前玩具。

groups.summary_en: Verbs in this frame describe the production of weak, plaintive, high-pitched vocal sounds that communicate fear, helplessness, pain, or childish petulance.
groups.summary_zh: 指因疼痛、恐惧或委屈而发出微弱、尖细、哀怨的呜咽或哼唧声。
groups.desc_en: Emitting subdued, plaintive, or nasal vocalizations of distress, pain, or childish dissatisfaction, contrasting with full-throated crying or standard complaining.
groups.desc_zh: 发出微弱、哀怨或带鼻音的委屈痛苦之声，区别于放声大哭或普通的言语抱怨。
groups.nuance_en: mewl: weak, kitten-like crying (infant / newborn) · whimper: low, broken sounds of fear or pain (dog / child / victim) · snivel: tearful, runny-nosed whining (complainer / brat) · pule: feeble, thin whimpering (sick child / beggar) · whine: prolonged, high-pitched nasal complaining (child / motor / dog)
groups.nuance_zh: mewl: 似猫叫般孱弱细弱的哭泣 (infant / newborn) · whimper: 恐惧或剧痛下断断续续的呜咽 (dog / child / victim) · snivel: 抽泣且涕泗横流的哀怨 (complainer / brat) · pule: 虚弱细小的低啼 (sick child / beggar) · whine: 拖长的刺耳鼻音抱怨或哀鸣 (child / motor / dog)

groups.name: Whisk & Bundle · 快速送走与敏捷转移 (Whisk, Hustle, Bundle)
groups.tip: 迅速动作或极速位移之势

items.def_zh: 紧急运送；急送（去医院等）
items.def_en: To transport someone or something somewhere with the greatest possible speed
items.ex_en: Paramedics worked quickly to rush the critical patient straight to emergency surgery.
items.ex_zh: 急救人员迅速行动，将危重病人紧急送往手术室抢救。
items.ex2_en: Panicked shoppers rushed toward the emergency exits when the loud alarm sounded.
items.ex2_zh: 响亮的警报响起时，惊慌的顾客们冲向紧急出口。

items.def_zh: 匆忙塞进；粗暴快速带走
items.def_en: (+ into/off) To push or pack someone quickly and roughly into a car, room, or vehicle
items.ex_en: Guards hurried forward to bundle the protesting suspect into the waiting van.
items.ex_zh: 警卫赶上前去，把抗议的嫌疑人粗暴匆忙地塞进等候的面包车。

items.def_zh: 推推搡搡迅速带走；催促快走
items.def_en: (+ into/out of) To cause someone to move quickly by pushing or urging them along firmly
items.ex_en: Security agents moved fast to hustle the endangered diplomat out of danger.
items.ex_zh: 安保特工动作迅速，推搡催促着受威胁的外交官脱离险境。

items.def_zh: 暗中劫走；神不知鬼不觉地运走
items.def_en: To take someone or something away rapidly, secretly, and without attracting notice
items.ex_en: Rebels managed to spirit away the captive prince during the midnight raid.
items.ex_zh: 叛军在午夜突袭中成功神不知鬼不觉地劫走了被俘的王子。

items.def_zh: 飞快带走，匆匆送走；快速挥动；搅拌
items.def_en: 1. (+ away/off/into) To move or take someone or something somewhere very quickly and suddenly. 2. (cooking) To beat eggs, cream, or other liquid rapidly.
items.ex_en: Secret service agents had to whisk the visiting dignitary away from protesters.
items.ex_zh: 特勤局特工不得不迅速将这位来访的政要从抗议者身边匆匆带走。

groups.summary_en: This frame specifies quickly and often stealthily transporting or sweeping someone or something away to safety, secrecy, or another location, with deftness and dispatch.
groups.summary_zh: 指迅速、果断甚至掩护性地把某人或物送离或转移。
groups.desc_en: Removing or transporting someone or something with abrupt, agile speed or secretive haste, contrasting with standard carrying or open vehicular transport.
groups.desc_zh: 以敏捷、迅速甚至隐秘的方式将人或物急送/转移，区别于常规搬运或公开运输。
groups.nuance_en: rush: urgent, speed-driven movement (patient / report) · bundle: unceremoniously pushing or packing someone away (suspect / children) · hustle: roughly urging or shoving forward rapidly (crowd / prisoner) · spirit away: mysteriously or surreptitiously whisking off (witness / heir) · whisk: light, lightning-fast conveyance out of sight (dignitary / dish)
groups.nuance_zh: rush: 紧急火速送往 (patient / report) · bundle: 粗暴、胡乱地塞入带走 (suspect / children) · hustle: 推搡催促着迅速转移 (crowd / prisoner) · spirit away: 神秘莫测或暗中掳走/带离 (witness / heir) · whisk: 极其轻快敏捷地带离现场 (dignitary / dish)

groups.name: Whisper & Murmur · 低语与呢喃 (Murmur, Breathe, Sussurate)
groups.tip: 压低嗓音轻声细语

items.def_zh: 低语，耳语，私语；（风、树叶等）沙沙作响
items.def_en: 1. To speak very softly using breath rather than vocal cords. 2. (literary) To make a soft, rustling sound.
items.ex_en: The gentle breeze began to whisper through the swaying branches of willow.
items.ex_zh: 微风开始在摇曳的柳树枝桠间发出沙沙低语。

items.def_zh: 沙沙作响；发出柔和低语声
items.def_en: To make a soft, rhythmic whispering or rustling sound like leaves or light waves
items.ex_en: Dry autumn leaves softly sussurate against the cobblestones in the cool night.
items.ex_zh: 干燥的秋叶在凉爽的夜色中掠过鹅卵石，发出柔和的沙沙声。

items.def_en: To utter words very softly and quietly, like a gentle exhalation
items.ex_en: She leaned close to breathe her deepest secret into his listening ear.
items.ex_zh: 她凑近跟前，将心底最深的秘密屏息轻吐进他的耳畔。

items.def_en: To say something in a very quiet, gentle voice that is soft and subdued
items.ex_en: The mother leaned down to murmur comforting words to her sleepy infant.
items.ex_zh: 母亲俯下身子，向昏昏欲睡的婴儿柔声低语着安抚的话。

items.def_en: To say something in an urgent, fierce, or threatening whisper with sibilant sounds
items.ex_en: He leaned across the table to hiss a vicious threat under breath.
items.ex_zh: 他隔着桌子探过身去，压低嗓门恶狠狠地吐出一句威胁。

groups.summary_en: Denotes speaking with low acoustic volume without full vocal cord vibration, typically for secrecy, intimacy, or discretion. Also extends poetically to gentle ambient rustles.
groups.summary_zh: 指出于保密、亲密或谨慎而极轻柔地耳语，亦比喻微弱沙沙声。
groups.desc_en: Producing faint, breathy vocal sounds at minimal volume without full vocal cord vibration, contrasting with normal audible speech.
groups.desc_zh: 用极低音量发出的带气流、声带微振的耳语微声，区别于常规发声清晰的说话。
groups.nuance_en: whisper: deliberate voiceless breath-speech for secrecy (secret / confession) · sussurate: soft rustling or whispering background sound (leaves / wind / voices) · breathe: uttering very softly as an exhale (sigh / words / pledge) · murmur: continuous, indistinct, low vocal rumbling (crowd / prayer / stream) · hiss: sibilant, hostile or urgent whisper (warning / threat)
groups.nuance_zh: whisper: 刻意压低声带的保密私语 (secret / confession) · sussurate: 如风吹树叶般柔和沙沙低语 (leaves / wind / voices) · breathe: 似吐气般极轻柔地吐露 (sigh / words / pledge) · murmur: 含混不清、持续低沉的呢喃 (crowd / prayer / stream) · hiss: 齿擦音明显、带敌意或警示的嘶声低语 (warning / threat)

groups.name: Whistle & Sound · 鸣响与发声 (Whistle, Pipe, Hiss)
groups.tip: 吹哨鸣响或发出声响

items.def_en: to speak up unexpectedly, usually in a high or shrill tone
items.ex_en: The timid intern suddenly piped up with a brilliant idea during conference.
items.ex_zh: 胆小的实习生在会议期间突然尖声插话，提出了一个绝妙的主意。

items.def_en: to make a high-pitched, shrill sound, or speak in a thin treble voice
items.ex_en: The frightened little girl piped her complaint in a shrill, quavering voice.
items.ex_zh: 受惊的小女孩用尖锐颤抖的声音尖声哭诉着。

items.def_en: to produce a continuous sharp sibilant sound resembling escaping steam
items.ex_en: Damaged pipes began to hiss loudly as boiling steam escaped the fracture.
items.ex_zh: 破损的水管随着沸腾的蒸汽从裂缝中逸出而大声发出嘶嘶声。

items.def_en: to blow a short, quick blast on a horn or whistle
items.ex_en: The impatient driver began to toot his horn at the stalled traffic.
items.ex_zh: 不耐烦的司机开始对着停滞不前的车流短促按响喇叭。
items.ex2_en: A miniature steam locomotive tooted cheerily as it rounded the botanical garden bend.
items.ex2_zh: 微型蒸汽机车绕过植物园弯道时发出欢快短促的鸣笛声。

items.def_zh: 吹口哨，鸣笛；呼啸，发尖锐声
items.def_en: 1. To make a high sound by forcing air through your lips or teeth, or by blowing a whistle. 2. To move quickly making a sharp sound like a whistle.
items.ex_en: Cold autumn winds began to whistle sharply through the cracked window panes.
items.ex_zh: 凄冷的秋风开始穿过破裂的窗玻璃，发出尖锐的呼啸声。

groups.summary_en: This frame centers on the mechanics of sound generated by forced airflow through narrow apertures, whether human lips, windpipes, or pressurized conduits. Collocations range from signalling tunes to wind howling.
groups.summary_zh: 气流经狭窄孔隙挤出所发出的尖细鸣音、嘶鸣或哨音表达。
groups.desc_en: Emitting sharp, thin, or high-pitched acoustic signals via airflow or resonance, contrasting with deep roars or resonant bells.
groups.desc_zh: 通过气流或共振发出清脆、尖厉或细高的声音，区别于低沉轰鸣或厚重钟鸣。
groups.nuance_en: pipe up: suddenly speaking in a high or shrill voice (child / critic) · pipe: emitting a thin, shrill sound (flute / bird / voice) · hiss: sharp escaping-air sound (steam / snake / radiator) · toot: short, perfunctory horn blast (horn / whistle / driver) · whistle: clear, high-pitched air-blown tone (referee / train / wind)
groups.nuance_zh: pipe up: 尖声突兀地开口发话 (child / critic) · pipe: 发出尖细清脆的管乐声或声调 (flute / bird / voice) · hiss: 尖锐气体逸出的嘶嘶声 (steam / snake / radiator) · toot: 鸣响短促的喇叭声 (horn / whistle / driver) · whistle: 吹出清澈高亢的口哨或汽笛声 (referee / train / wind)

groups.name: Whiten & Blanch · 发白与褪色 (Blanch, Pale, Bleach)
groups.tip: 失去血色或因受热发白

items.def_en: To lose color in the face, typically through fear, illness, or shock
items.ex_en: His hollow cheeks seemed to pale visibly at the grim, unexpected revelation.
items.ex_zh: 面对那冷酷而不期而至的真相，他凹陷的双颊明显变得苍白。

items.def_en: To become white or paler, or to make something white
items.ex_en: Special mineral treatments can gradually whiten aged fabric without damaging delicate fibers.
items.ex_zh: 特殊的矿物处理能逐渐使陈旧的织物变白，而不会损伤脆弱的纤维。
items.ex2_en: His pale knuckles whitened noticeably as he clenched his fists in anger.
items.ex2_zh: 当他愤怒地握紧拳头时，苍白的指关节明显发白。

items.def_en: To make or become white or lighter by chemical treatment or exposure to sunlight
items.ex_en: Harsh afternoon sunlight will rapidly bleach the brilliant dye from these curtains.
items.ex_zh: 午后强烈的阳光会很快将这些窗帘上鲜艳的染料晒褪色。
items.ex2_en: Old bones bleach naturally in the desert sun after many dry years.
items.ex2_zh: 在干旱多年后，古老的骨骼在沙漠阳光下自然变白。

items.def_en: To remove the color from a substance by chemical or thermal processing
items.ex_en: The alchemist sought an elusive compound capable to decolorize the murky solvent.
items.ex_zh: 炼金术士竭力寻找一种能够使浑浊溶剂脱色的稀世化合物。

items.def_zh: （脸色）变苍白；焯水，将（蔬菜、坚果等）汆烫
items.def_en: 1. To become pale suddenly from fear, shock, or pain. 2. (cooking) To plunge food into boiling water briefly, usually before plunging into cold water.
items.ex_en: The proud nobleman did blanch upon hearing the terrifying verdict of treason.
items.ex_zh: 那位高傲的贵族在听到叛国罪的可怕判决时，脸色骤然煞白。
items.ex2_en: The chef decided to blanch fresh spinach briefly before preparing the salad.
items.ex2_zh: 大厨决定在做沙拉之前先把新鲜菠菜焯一下水。

groups.summary_en: Verbs signifying a loss of skin color due to physical shock or terror, or chemically/physically stripping pigmentation from surfaces.
groups.summary_zh: 指因惊恐失血而面如土色，或通过物理、化学手段除去色素。
groups.desc_en: Draining or chemical removal of color resulting in a pale, stark white state, contrasting with darkening, staining, or natural aging.
groups.desc_zh: 使物体或面色脱色退彩而呈现惨白或纯白，区别于上色、发黑或自然陈化。
groups.nuance_en: pale: losing healthy facial flush from shock or illness (cheeks / complexion) · whiten: making or becoming generally white (teeth / hair / sheet) · bleach: chemically or solar stripping pigment (fabric / bones / hair) · decolorize: technical removal of colored impurities (solution / oil) · blanch: sudden total drained pallor or scalding to whiten (face / almonds / vegetables)
groups.nuance_zh: pale: 因惊吓或疾病失去血色而发白 (cheeks / complexion) · whiten: 使整体变白或自然变白 (teeth / hair / sheet) · bleach: 经化学或光照漂白褪色 (fabric / bones / hair) · decolorize: 技术性去除色素杂质 (solution / oil) · blanch: 瞬间面无血色惨白，或烹饪热烫脱皮 (face / almonds / vegetables)

groups.name: Widen & Broaden · 拓宽与延展 (Broaden, Expand, Flange)
groups.tip: 物理或视界维度的延展

items.def_zh: 向外张开；呈喇叭形张开
items.def_en: To gradually become wider at the bottom or end, like a bell or funnel
items.ex_en: The sleek glass vase begins to flare out gracefully near the rim.
items.ex_zh: 这个造型优美的玻璃花瓶在接近边缘处优雅地呈喇叭形向外张开。
items.ex2_en: The skilled tailor flared out the skirt hem using soft pleated fabric.
items.ex2_zh: 熟练的裁缝用柔软的褶皱面料将裙摆做成喇叭状张开。

items.def_en: To become wider, more spacious, or unobstructed, such as a narrow path entering a broad valley
items.ex_en: The narrow mountain trail suddenly opens out into a breathtaking alpine meadow.
items.ex_zh: 狭窄的山间小道豁然展宽，眼前呈现出一片美不胜收的高山草甸。
items.ex2_en: The workers opened out the folded banquet tables inside the large hall.
items.ex2_zh: 工人们在大厅里把折叠的宴会桌一一展开。

items.def_en: To become wider physically, or to increase the range of someone's knowledge, experience, or opinions
items.ex_en: Traveling across varied cultures will profoundly broaden a young person's global perspective.
items.ex_zh: 游历多元文化将极大地拓宽一个年轻人的全球视野。
items.ex2_en: The narrow river begins to broaden noticeably as it approaches the coastline.
items.ex2_zh: 这条狭窄的河流在接近海岸线时开始明显变宽。

items.def_en: To become larger in size, area, volume, or scope, or to make something do so
items.ex_en: The thriving tech enterprise plans to expand operations into three overseas markets.
items.ex_zh: 这家蓬勃发展的科技企业计划将业务扩张到三个海外市场。
items.ex2_en: Hot compressed gases expand rapidly to drive the heavy pistons inside engines.
items.ex2_zh: 高温压缩气体迅速膨胀，以驱动发动机内部沉重的活塞。

items.def_en: 1. To become wider, or to make something wider. 2. To increase or broaden the scope, range, or degree of something.
items.ex_en: Engineers need to widen the old canal to accommodate larger cargo barges.
items.ex_zh: 工程师们需要拓宽这条古老的运河，以容纳更大的货运驳船。
items.ex2_en: Her dark pupils widened in astonishment upon seeing the unexpected royal visitor.
items.ex2_zh: 看到意料之外的王室访客，她深色的瞳孔惊讶地放大了。

groups.summary_en: Captures increase across transverse physical dimensions (such as roadways, doorways, and gaps) as well as the metaphorical broadening of perspective, horizons, knowledge bases, and disparities.
groups.summary_zh: 指物理横向跨度、孔径的加宽，或视野、范围、差距的拓展放大。
groups.desc_en: Increasing the lateral dimension, aperture, or conceptual scope of an entity, contrasting with linear elongation or three-dimensional swelling.
groups.desc_zh: 扩大横向宽度、开孔尺寸或概念边界，区别于纵向拉长或全维膨胀。
groups.nuance_en: flare out: widening outwards bell-shaped from a narrower point (skirt / nostrils / roadway) · open out: unfolding or spreading into wide expanse (landscape / valley / view) · broaden: expanding scope, perspective, or surface width (horizons / smile / base) · expand: dimensional growth or elaboration (business / chest / territory) · widen: simple direct increase in horizontal width (road / gap / eyes)
groups.nuance_zh: flare out: 喇叭口状向外张开/扩宽 (skirt / nostrils / roadway) · open out: 豁然开朗展开延展 (landscape / valley / view) · broaden: 扩展视野、范围或横截面 (horizons / smile / base) · expand: 体积增大、业务或版图全面扩张 (business / chest / territory) · widen: 横向距离或开口的单纯加宽 (road / gap / eyes)

groups.name: Wiggle & Squirm · 扭动与蠕动 (Wiggle, Squirm, Writhe)
groups.tip: 身体小幅度扭动挣脱

items.def_en: To move, or make something move, with small, quick movements from side to side or up and down.
items.ex_en: The toddler loved to wiggle his bare toes happily in the warm sand.
items.ex_zh: 这个蹒跚学步的孩子喜欢在温暖的沙滩上开心地扭动光脚趾。
items.ex2_en: The small bait fish wiggled desperately inside the fisherman's plastic bucket.
items.ex2_zh: 那条小鱼饵在渔夫的塑料桶里拼命扭动着。

items.def_en: To twist and turn with quick, small writhing movements like a worm, often to escape or fit into a tight space
items.ex_en: The trapped puppy managed to wriggle free from the narrow iron railings.
items.ex_zh: 被困的小狗设法扭动身体，从狭窄的铁栏杆中脱身。

items.def_en: To make small, restless, continuous movements with the hands or feet because of boredom, anxiety, or impatience
items.ex_en: Nervous applicants often fidget with their pens during stressful job interviews.
items.ex_zh: 紧张的求职者在压力巨大的求职面试中往往会坐立不安地摆弄钢笔。

items.def_en: (+ into/through) To crawl or wriggle slowly and laboriously through a narrow or crowded space
items.ex_en: The brave firefighter had to worm through the collapsed basement's tiny debris.
items.ex_zh: 英勇的消防员不得不像蚯蚓般吃力地爬过倒塌地下室的狭小废墟。

items.def_zh: 局促蠕动，骨碌骨碌地动
items.def_en: To twist and move the body about from side to side, especially because of nervousness, discomfort, or embarrassment
items.ex_en: The guilty schoolboy began to squirm under the teacher's severe, steady gaze.
items.ex_zh: 在老师严厉而坚定的注视下，感到心虚的男生开始局促不安地扭动。

groups.summary_en: This frame covers subtle to restless involuntary or voluntary body movements characterized by undulating, twisting, or shifting motions, often signaling discomfort, amusement, or confinement.
groups.summary_zh: 表示躯体细碎扭转或蠕动，常伴随不安、局促或挣脱感。
groups.desc_en: Executing continuous small, twisting, or sinuous bodily movements due to confinement, restlessness, or discomfort, contrasting with rigid stillness or locomotion.
groups.desc_zh: 因受限、不安或不适而身体持续细碎扭动、蜿蜒穿行，区别于静止不动或正常行走。
groups.nuance_en: wiggle: quick, light, playful back-and-forth twitches (toes / ears / tail) · wriggle: serpentine sinuous twisting to escape or move (worm / escapee / snake) · fidget: restless, nervous micro-movements of hands/feet (child / hands / audience) · worm: slow, sneaky, insidious wriggling motion (way through / into confidence) · squirm: uncomfortable twisting from embarrassment, pain, or restraint (baby / witness / victim)
groups.nuance_zh: wiggle: 欢快、轻微的左右摆动/扭动 (toes / ears / tail) · wriggle: 蛇形般蜿蜒挣脱或穿行 (worm / escapee / snake) · fidget: 局促烦躁、坐立不安的小动作 (child / hands / audience) · worm: 缓慢钻动、钻营渗透 (way through / into confidence) · squirm: 因尴尬、痛苦或受制而扭动难安 (baby / witness / victim)

groups.name: Wince & Flinch · 龇牙与抽搐躲闪 (Wince, Grimace, Flinch, Recoil)
groups.tip: 因剧痛或恐惧不由自主龇牙缩头

items.def_zh: 龇牙咧嘴，蹙眉皱面；畏缩，退避
items.def_en: (+ at) To make a sudden, brief facial expression or involuntary movement of pain, distress, or embarrassment.
items.ex_en: He could not help but wince at the painful injection needle's prick.
items.ex_zh: 在疼痛的注射针刺入时，他忍不住咧嘴缩了一下。

items.def_en: To tremble convulsive-fashion throughout the torso from sharp revulsion or piercing pain
items.ex_en: A cold dread made her shudder violently from deep within her chest.
items.ex_zh: 一种冰冷的恐惧令她从胸膛深处剧烈地打了个寒战。
